title: OpenShift 4.x Installer is not creating worker nodes
issue: - When my OpenShift 4.x install completes it does not have any nodes for me to run workloads on. How can this be investigated?
root_cause: The installer doesn't provision worker nodes directly, like it does with master nodes. Instead, the cluster relies on the Machine API Operator, which is able to scale up and down nodes on supported platforms. If more than fifteen to twenty minutes (depending on the speed of the cluster's Internet connection) have elapsed without any workers, the Machine API Operator needs to be investigated, using the *diagnostic steps* from this article.

title: Increasing the instance size of your instances at install time for OpenShift 4.x
issue: - The size of my instances is insufficient to run all or some of the components that OpenShift starts by default.- I have core OpenShift [components OOMing](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3790861) when I install a cluster
resolution: At this time it is not possible to do at this time however the general process will be: 1. Create the Installation Configuration: `openshift-install create install-config--dir=/root/4xlarge` 1. Create the YAML Manifests: `openshift-install create manifests--dir=/root/4xlarge` 1. Update the Machine Manifests: `sed-i 's/m4.large/m4.4xlarge/g' /root/4xlarge/openshift/99_openshift-cluster-api_*.yaml` 1. Install the Cluster: `openshift-install create cluster--dir=/root/4xlarge`

title: OpenShift 4.x Pods OOMing
issue: - I recently installed an OpenShift 4.x cluster and now see pods in an OOM state. How do I debug this ~~~ openshift-kube-apiserver installer-3-ip-10-0-20-234.us-east-2.compute.internal 0/1 OOMKilled 0 22m openshift-kube-apiserver installer-5-ip-10-0-20-234.us-east-2.compute.internal 0/1 OOMKilled 0 20m openshift-kube-scheduler installer-1-ip-10-0-38-86.us-east-2.compute.internal 0/1 OOMKilled 0 27m ~~~
root_cause: OOM (Out of Memory) errors are the result of a pod or process not have enough memory (the limit usually set by hardware limitations (physical amount of RAM in a system) or cgroup limits (limiting a pod or process to only some sliver of total system RAM). In either case, more resources need to be added so that the process/pod in question can properly run and function. If increasing the resources (RAM) to a host and or cgroup only temporarily resolve the issue, you either did not provide enough resource or the resource in question may have a memory leak. WIth OpenShift should you need to [increase your instance size](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3792521) you can do so as part of the install.

title: OpenShift 4.x Install object creation order
issue: - What order should I create install object if I am not planning to simply run `openshift-install create cluster`
resolution: If you are looking to not simply run `openshift-install create cluster`, the order you need to generate materials in; is as follows: 1. **install-config** or **manifests templates** these can be run at the same time or independent of one another (and don't need to have something run before them.- In general, it is a best practice to run **install-config** then **manifests templates** however at this time we have no hard requirement on this. 1. **manifest**, this must be run after **manifests templates** and before **ignition-config**, if it's going to be run.- My 1. **ignition-config**, this must be run after **manifest**. To create a cluster with or with our pre-generating install object, run: `openshift-install create cluster` If any objects were pre-generated or generaged, and modified prior to running this (they will be picked up and used, over creating them as part of a manual input process.

title: How to install multiple Openshift cluster from a single location
issue: - How to invoke muliple invocations of openshift cluster install?- How to save install for future references?
resolution: - In order to allow users to customize their installation, the installer can be invoked multiple times. The state is stored in a hidden file in the asset directory and contains all of the intermediate artifacts. This allows the installer to pause during the installation and wait for the user to modify intermediate artifacts.- For example, you can create an install config and save it in a cluster-agnostic location: ~~~ openshift-install--dir=initial create install-config mv initial/install-config.yaml rm-rf initial ~~~- You can use the saved install-config for future clusters by copying it that install config into the asset directory and then invoking the installer: ~~~ mkdir cluster-0 cp install-config.yaml cluster-0/ openshift-install--dir=cluster-0 create cluster ~~~- Supplying a previously-generated install-config like this is explicitly part of the stable API.- You can also edit the assets in the asset directory during a single run. For example, you can adjust the cluster-version operator's configuration: ~~~ mkdir cluster-1 cp install-config.yaml cluster-1/ openshift-install--dir=cluster-1 create manifests # warning: this target is unstable "${EDITOR}" cluster-1/manifests/cvo-overrides.yaml openshift-install--dir=cluster-1 create cluster ~~~- As the unstable warning suggests, the presence of manifests and the names and content of its output is an unstable API. It is occasionally useful to make alterations like this as one-off changes, but don't expect them to work on subsequent installer releases.

title: How to apply configuration changes to cluster in Openshift 4
issue: - How to apply configuration changes to cluster in Openshift 4- How does machine-config operator works
resolution: - The `MachineConfigOperator` has "high level" knobs for some components of the cluster state; for example, SSH keys and kubelet configuration. However, there are obviously a quite large number of things one may want to configure on a system. For example, offline environments may want to specify an internal NTP pool. Another example is static network configuration. By providing a MachineConfig object containing Ignition configuration, systemd units can be provided, arbitrary files can be laid down into /etc and /var, etc. One known ergonomic issue right now for supplying files is that you must encode file contents via data: URIs. This is part of the current Ignition specification. Note also the mode is in decimal; mode 420 is octal 0644 or rw-r--r--.- This example MachineConfig object replaces /etc/chrony.conf with some custom NTP time servers. ~~~ # This example MachineConfig replaces /etc/chrony.conf apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 50-examplecorp-chrony spec: config: storage: files:- contents: source: data:,server%20clock.redhat.com%20maxdelay%200.4%20offline verification: {} filesystem: root mode: 420 path: /etc/chrony.conf ~~~- The controller will notice the new MachineConfig and generate a new "rendered" version that looks like worker-. Use oc describe machineconfigpool/worker to monitor the status of the rollout of the new rendered config to each node. ~~~ oc describe machineconfigpool/worker Name: worker Namespace: Labels: Annotations: API Version: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 Kind: MachineConfigPool Metadata: Creation Timestamp: 2019-01-22T12:58:08Z Generation: 1 Resource Version: 4072680 Self Link: /apis/machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1/machineconfigpools/worker UID: 5ddb708d-1e45-11e9-b9e1-02d3ec294f42 Spec: Machine Config Selector: Match Labels: Machineconfiguration. Openshift. Io / Role: worker Machine Selector: Match Labels: Node- Role. Kubernetes. Io / Worker: Max Unavailable: Paused: false Status: Conditions: Last Transition Time: 2019-01-22T12:58:32Z Message: Reason: Status: False Type: Degraded Last Transition Time: 2019-01-25T09:33:30Z Message: Reason: Status: False Type: Updated Last Transition Time: 2019-01-25T09:33:30Z Message: Reason: All nodes are updating to worker-f2e40991ff71bec36b3d4a8b4995af8c Status: True Type: Updating Configuration: Name: worker-f2e40991ff71bec36b3d4a8b4995af8c Source: API Version: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 Kind: MachineConfig Name: 00-worker API Version: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 Kind: MachineConfig Name: 00-worker-ssh API Version: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 Kind: MachineConfig Name: 01-worker-kubelet API Version: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 Kind: MachineConfig Name: 50-examplecorp-chrony Machine Count: 3 Observed Generation: 1 Ready Machine Count: 0 Unavailable Machine Count: 1 Updated Machine Count: 0 ~~~- Which later updated to: ~~~ Kind: MachineConfig Name: 50-examplecorp-chrony Machine Count: 3 Observed Generation: 1 Ready Machine Count: 3 Unavailable Machine Count: 0 Updated Machine Count: 3 ~~~- Note this configuration only applies to workers (see the role: worker label); currently if you want to apply to both master and workers, you must create two separate MachineConfig objects.- To test the new configuration. Ssh the worker machine and from root you can see as below: ~~~ $cat /etc/chrony.conf server clock.redhat.com maxdelay 0.4 offline ~~~

title: How to modify API configuration in Openshift 4
issue: - How to make changes for kube-API server in Openshift
resolution: - The configuration observer component is responsible for reacting on external configuration changes. For example, this allows external components (registry, etcd, etc..) to interact with the Kubernetes API server configuration (KubeAPIServerConfig custom resource).- Currently changes in following external components are being observed: 1. `host-etcd` endpoints in kube-system namespace. The observed endpoint addresses are used to configure the storageConfig.urls in Kubernetes API server configuration. ~~~ $ oc get ep-n kube-system NAME ENDPOINTS AGE host-etcd 192.0.2.1:2379,192.0.2.2:2379,192.0.2.3:2379 4d $oc edit ep host-etcd ~~~- cluster images.config.openshift.io custom resource. The observed CR resource is used to configure the imagePolicyConfig.internalRegistryHostname in Kubernetes API server configuration: ~~~ oc edit crd ~~~- cluster-config-v1 configmap in kube-system namespace. The observed configmap install-config is decoded and the networking.podCIDR and networking.serviceCIDR is extracted and used as input for admissionPluginConfig.openshift.io/RestrictedEndpointsAdmission.configuration.restrictedCIDRs and servicesSubnet ~~~ oc get cm-n kube-system ~~~

title: Difference between Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and Vertical Pod Autoscaler
issue: - What difference between `Horizontal Pod Autoscaler` and `Vertical Pod Autoscaler`?- Is **Vertical Pod Autoscaler*
supported?
resolution: - **Horizontal Pod Autoscaler** specifies how the system should automatically increase or decrease the scale of a replication controller or deployment configuration, based on metrics collected from the pods that belong to that replication controller or deployment configuration.- More information on HPA is given [here.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.6/dev_guide/pod_autoscaling.html#hpa-autoscaling)- On the other hand, **Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA)** frees the users from necessity of setting up-to-date resource requests for the containers in their pods. When configured, it will set the requests automatically based on usage and thus allow proper scheduling onto nodes so that appropriate resource amount is available for each pod. It can both down-scale pods that are over-requesting resources, and also up-scale pods that are under-requesting resources based on their usage over time.- More information on **VPA** is given [here.](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/vertical-pod-autoscaler#vertical-pod-autoscaler)- Currently **VPA** isn't supported by Red Hat.- Testing on **VPA** can be done, please check [blog.](https://blog.openshift.com/how-full-is-my-cluster-part-4-right-sizing-pods-with-vertical-pod-autoscaler/)- There are some known limitations with **VPA**, they are listed [here.](https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes-autoscaler/tree/master/vertical-pod-autoscaler#known-limitations-of-the-alpha-version)

title: Duplicated https://access.redhat.com/node/3759411/draft - Upgrades in OCP 3.10 and 3.11 causes SDN cluster network disruption
issue: - Cluster SDN network is disrupted when upgrading the master-control plane.- Upgrading OCP is causing cluster SDN network disruption.- Upgrade from 3.10.x to 3.10.y causes network disruption.- Upgrade from 3.11.x to 3.11.y causes network disruption.- Upgrade from 3.10 to 3.11 causes network disruption.
resolution: - Red Hat is working in an fix were the master control plane upgrade, will recreate the cluster SDN pods in an controlled manner.- Code will be fixed by implementing a new behavior, the SDN will only be recreated after draining the nodes, in addition the rollout of the SDN pods will be done only in the nodes upgrade phase and only as needed.- For 3.10 version, this problem is under work in Bugzilla https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1660880.- For 3.11 version, this problem is under work in Bugzilla https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1657019.
root_cause: - During the master control plane upgrade, the SDN daemonSet in the namespace openshift-sdn is changed, this triggers the SDN pods recreation across the entire cluster, causing an network disruption.

resolution: The following pages have been updated for the most recent image versions. 3.11- https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install/disconnected_install.html#disconnected-syncing-images 3.10- https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.10/install/disconnected_install.html#disconnected-syncing-images
root_cause: The listed tag is not properly up-to-date, compared to what's in the container registry. Until the process is automated, showing the current (supported/GA'd) tag the issue may reoccur where the disconnected installation tags can be several versions behind.

title: Docker is hanging, what do I need to capture to troubleshoot this further?
issue: - PLEG is not healthy: pleg was last seen active 8h2m2.2s ago; threshold is 3m0s- Running `docker ps` hangs.- Consistent issues with docker and debug logs are not showing the issue
resolution: To get an RCA we would need a Goroutine dumped and docker core. 1. Goroutine dumped to journal. ~~~ # sudo kill-SIGUSR1 $(pidof dockerd-current) # sudo kill-SIGUSR1 $(pidof docker-containerd-current) ~~~- After the above gather a sosreport, if that is not possible gather the logs and upload to case. ~~~ # sosreport OR # journalct--since "2 hours ago" > $(hostname).logs # docker info # rpm-qa docker ~~~ 1. Capture a gdb gcore from docker and containerd. To capture this you would need the 'gdb' package which will include the `gcore` command. The 'gcore' command captures a 'snapshot' of the process memory and the process remains running. ~~~ # lsof-p $(pidof dockerd-current) # gcore-o /example_path_name/dockerd_core $(pidof dockerd-current) # lsof-p $(pidof docker-containerd-current) # gcore-o /example_path_name/containerd_core $(pidof docker-containerd-current) ~~~

title: Deployments are failing and no new images are being created
issue: We had done the OpenShift upgrade recently. Everything was working fine until today morning and from this morning we are not able to deploy any images or pods successfully. Receiving the following error Failed create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = [failed to set up sandbox container "a556225bbe9ee617de6b8bd06391912ee51afc5b397fe35a759e963e8e9e570a" network for pod "provider-ui-56-d6dgl": NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod "provider-ui-56-d6dgl_digital-prod" network: failed to send CNI request: Post http://dummy/: dial unix /var/run/openshift-sdn/cni-server.sock: connect: connection refused, failed to clean up sandbox container "a556225bbe9ee617de6b8bd06391912ee51afc5b397fe35a759e963e8e9e570a" network for pod "provider-ui-56-d6dgl": NetworkPlugin cni failed to teardown pod "provider-ui-56-d6dgl_digital-prod" network: failed to send CNI request: Post http://dummy/: dial unix /var/run/openshift-sdn/cni-server.sock: connect: connection refused]
resolution: The fix should roll out with the next z-stream release. Expected results: oom-killer does not kill the process due to score being-999 and a health check is configured to check health of pod. Workaround: Making the following changes will set qosClass Guaranteed with oom-score set to 0. This is not a complete fix but it will reduce the kills of this process. ~~~ # oc project openshift-sdn # oc edit ds ovs ~~~ Change the limits to equal the request Setting the following limits: ~~~ resources: limits: cpu: 200m memory: 400Mi requests: cpu: 200m memory: 400Mi ~~~
root_cause: - Changes from 3.9 to 3.10 now has OVS running in a pod. By default the oom-score is 992 due to being in qosClass Burstable.- The leaves it open to getting killed by oom-killer.- If ovs-vswitchd gets killed the container will still be running but will stay in a bad state as no health check is configured.

title: Does openshift docker image ship with control M agent?
issue: What are your recommendation for application scheduler within openshift for apps deployed inside the PODs of the kubernetes cluster?
resolution: - Red Hat does not ship a Control M agent in our container catalog.- May be ONE exists in the community or by contacting the maintainers.- However, there are a few options available that you might find interesting. The first is the Cron Job feature of OpenShift: 3.6- https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.6/dev_guide/cron_jobs.html However, in 3.6 it is in Technology Preview only. This means we do not recommend it for production use, as in this version it is not fully tested and verified. It becomes fully supported in 3.9, so if you want to use this for production I would suggest upgrading to 3.9 to take advantage of it: 3.9- https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.9/dev_guide/cron_jobs.html For general automation and management, you may also be interested in using Ansible instead, as it is targeted toward large-scale management: https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/index.html https://docs.ansible.com/ansible-tower/

title: Elasticsearch pod crashed with OOM errors
issue: - After an upgrade, `ES` cluster seems to be unstable.- `ES` pod has had 6 restarts and has been running for the last two hours.- Few `indices` were marked as `red`.- The `ES` pod crashed with the following error ~~~ java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space Dumping heap to /elasticsearch/persistent/heapdump.hprof... Unable to create /elasticsearch/persistent/heapdump.hprof: File exists ~~~- `Kibana` pod continues to register messages such as ~~~ {"type":"log","@timestamp":"tags":["status","plugin:elasticsearch@5.6.13","info"],"pid":227,"state":"green","message":"Status changed from red to green- Kibana index ready","prevState":"red","prevMsg":"Request Timeout after 3000ms"} {"type":"log","@timestamp":"","tags":["status","ui settings","info"],"pid":227,"state":"green","message":"Status changed from red to green- Ready","prevState":"red","prevMsg":"Elasticsearch plugin is red"} {"type":"log","@timestamp":"tags":["status","plugin:elasticsearch@5.6.13","error"],"pid":227,"state":"red","message":"Status changed from green to red- Request Timeout after 3000ms","prevState":"green","prevMsg":"Kibana index ready"} {"type":"log","@timestamp":"tags":["status","ui settings","error"],"pid":227,"state":"red","message":"Status changed from green to red- Elasticsearch plugin is red","prevState":"green","prevMsg":"Ready"} ~~~
resolution: - Check how much RAM is allocated to an `ES` instance.- It's recommended to allocate at least `16Gi`, however one can set depending on the amount of workload `EFK` stack is handling.- It has been found that the `ES` instance RAM was set to `8Gi` which was quite insufficient for the `ES` cluster in order to function properly.- The moment instance RAM got increased, re-initializing `ES` cluster helped to overcome the issue.
root_cause: - `ES` deploymentconfig: ~~~- name: CLUSTER_NAME value: logging-es- name: INSTANCE_RAM value: 8Gi ~~~- `ES` instance RAM was set to `8Gi` which is quite insufficient while managing heavy workloads in the cluster.

FAILED- RETRYING: Wait for all control plane pods to become ready (59 retries left). FAILED- RETRYING: Wait for all control plane pods to become ready (58 retries left). ~~~
resolution: This issue has been resolved in OpenShift 3.11.43: and 3.10.66:. Additionally if the following log is observed in /var/log/messages.... ~~~ Unable to update cni config: No networks found in /etc/cni/net.d ~~~ Please verify atomic-openshift-node service status. It will likely be in a failed state... ~~~ systemctl status atomic-openshift-node ~~~ openshift-ansible does not contain necessary checks for a healthy atomic-openshift-node services. It will continue on until it's time to bring up api services then fail. A root cause for a failed atomic-openshift-node service is missing grpquota setting on the filesystem that will host `/var/lib/origin/openshift.local.volumes` (emptydir in OCP). Often is it not remembered, ideal or cost effective to deploy an additional vol for emptydir. This pushes emptydir up to the / filesystem. The operating system or machine image often does not get configured with grpquota option enabled for / especially when using the Red Hat Cloud Access RHEL7 AMI or Amazon Market RHEL7 AMI in AWS. Follow the [disk quotas for RHEL 7 procedure](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/6/html/storage_administration_guide/ch-disk-quotas) and enable for the / filesystem.
root_cause: This was worked by Engineering team in https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1614904 and https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1638525.

title: Only web console containers running after upgrading Openshift 3.7 to 3.9
issue: After upgrading an OpenShift cluster from 3.7 to 3.9, the cluster reports:
Only the *openshift-web-console
containers are running
The rest of the containers (registry, registry-console, router, loader) are stuck at *ContainerCreating

`oc get events` reports the pods are failing with errors like the following: ~~~ Failed create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed pulling image "satellite.server.local:5000/organization-containers-pod:v3.9.51": unknown: NotFound. ~~~

When using an internal registry, rather than Satellite or the public Red Hat image registry The error shows that the cluster cannot create new pods from the given image, but that container image shown does not exist in the Satellite registry nor on the Red Hat public registry at [registry.access.redhat.com](registry.access.redhat.com). This image should be getting synced from Satellite to a dedicated OpenShift registry, but OpenShift is pointing to an incorrect image location.
resolution: Run the following command on all nodes and verify the configuration is correct: ~~~ # grep format: /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml ~~~ Run this on only the masters in the cluster: ~~~ # grep format: /etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml ~~~ Fix any configuration options that are incorrect and restart the service(s) involved. The *atomic-openshift-master-api* / *atomic-openshift-master-controllers* and/or *atomic-openshift-node* services may need to be restarted.

title: Recovering glusterfs from failure, glusterfs is managed by heketi on a standalone VM.
issue: 'gluster volume start VOLUME' failed with a missing brick configured by heketi running on a standalone VM. A missing brick is one of the 3 way replicated glusterfs volume.
resolution: Heketi 7 running on a standalone VM is not a supported configuration. OSC deployment guide describes "Red Hat only supports Heketi inside OpenShift Container Platform in OCS." [1] [1] https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_container_storage/3.11/html/deployment_guide/chap-documentation-red_hat_gluster_storage_container_native_with_openshift_platform-identify_usecase
root_cause: Heketi 7 running on a standalone VM is not a supported configuration.

title: How to add co-located etcd hosts to existing cluster
issue: - Adding co-located etcd node to existing cluster- Adding master/compute/infra node to cluster
resolution: In two phases the new co-located etcd will be added. Here is the OpenShift installation document for details; [Adding Hosts to an Existing Cluster](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/adding_hosts_to_existing_cluster.html#replacing-existing-masters) **Phase 1: Adding new master node into the existing cluster:** Here are the 4 steps process to add new master: Step 1: Adding new master node to inventory file Example of inventory file: ~~~ [OSEv3:children] masters nodes etcd new_masters [masters] master[1:2].example.com [new_masters] master3.example.com <--- new master node where new etcd will be co-located [etcd] master[1:2].example.com [nodes] master[1:2].example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-master' node1.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-compute' node2.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-compute' infra-node1.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-infra' infra-node2.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-infra' [new_nodes] master3.example.com <--- new master node ~~~ Step 2: Run master scaleup playbook ~~~ #cd /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible #ansible-playbook-i playbooks/openshift-master/scaleup.yml e.g #ansible-playbook-i /etc/ansible/hosts playbooks/openshift-master/scaleup.yml ~~~ Step 3: Verify the installation of new master ~~~ # oc get nodes <--- you will see the new master in the output. ~~~ Step 4: Add the new master node under [masters] node group and remove node group new_masters from inventory file ~~~ [OSEv3:children] masters nodes etcd new_masters <--- remove [masters] master[1:3]].example.com <---- master3 added [new_masters] <---- remove master3.example.com <--- remove ~~~ **Phase 2: Adding the same new master as new co-located etcd:** Here are the 4 steps process to add new etcd: Step 1: Adding a new etcd into inventory file:----------------------- Example of inventory file: ~~~ [OSEv3:children] masters nodes etcd new_etcd [masters] master[1:3].example.com [etcd] master[1:2].example.com [new_etcd] master3.example.com [nodes] master[1:3].example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-master' node1.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-compute' node2.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-compute' infra-node1.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-infra' infra-node2.example.com openshift_node_group_name='node-config-infra' ~~~ Step 2: Run playbook etcd scaleup playbok: ~~~ #cd /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible #ansible-playbook-i /etc/ansible/hosts playbooks/openshift-etcd/scaleup.yml ~~~ Step 3: Verify the etcd cluster health and member list as below: On master 1- Cluster health check ~~~ # etcdctl-C \ https://etcd1.example.com:2379,https://etcd2.example.com:2379,https://etcd3.example.com:2379 \--ca-file=/etc/origin/master/master.etcd-ca.crt \--cert-file=/etc/origin/master/master.etcd-client.crt \--key-file=/etc/origin/master/master.etcd-client.key cluster-health ~~~- Cluster member list check ~~~ # etcdctl-C \ https://etcd1.example.com:2379,https://etcd2.example.com:2379,https://etcd3.example.com:2379 \--ca-file=/etc/origin/master/master.etcd-ca.crt \--cert-file=/etc/origin/master/master.etcd-client.crt \--key-file=/etc/origin/master/master.etcd-client.key member list ~~~ Step 4: Add the new new_etcd node under [etcd] node group and remove node group new_etcd from inventory file ~~~ [OSEv3:children] masters nodes etcd new_etcd <--- remove [etcd] master[1:3]].example.com <---- master3 added as new etcd [new_etcd] <---- remove master3.example.com <--- remove ~~~

title: Multiple Network Interfaces Causing OpenShift Install Errors
issue: - OpenShift install issue- nodes wont register, dnsmasq is not configured to openshift_ip, sdn connectivity issues- Physical nodes each have 2 net connections/interfaces (one 'management' interface for SSH, etc. and one 'openshift' interface)- For our ansible inventory file, all nodes have the openshift_ip set to the 'openshift' network ip corresponding to that system.- The playbook fails while trying to register the nodes. When I login to the physical systems, dnsmasq is listening on the 'management' network instead of the 'openshift' network since that is how ansible configured- node-config file also has dnsIP as 'management' instead of 'openshift'- If I manually make dnsmasq changes and atomic-openshift-node changes for the dnsIP and restart, the node will register
resolution: - First, set the public ip in the ansible hosts file to the ip address of the network you want dnsmasq and OpenShift services listening on: ~~~ openshift_public_ip=[IP ADDRESS] ~~~- Be sure to set this for each node- If this does not work, set on each host the below variable to the ip address of the correct subnet for that node: ~~~ openshift_dns_ip=[IP ADDRESS] ~~~- Setting this is usually not recommended, but this can be a workaround to properly set the dns listening addres- This is described in our [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/install_config/install/prerequisites.html#dns-config-prereq)- NOTE: After failed installs it is suggested to revert to VM snapshots from shortly before the install process, or else run the "uninstall" playbook. This is described in the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/install_config/install/advanced_install.html#installer-known-issues)- See also related [container runtime issues](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3241891)

title: After configuring router sharding on multiple routers with a empty NAMESPACE_LABELS="" variable for a particular router, causes intermediate connection loss while accessing routes.
issue: A router `dev-env-router` configured with `NAMESPACE_LABLES="env=dev"` is for serving routes with wildcard: `*os-dev.example.com` and another router say `default-infra-router` is configured with a empty `NAMESPACE_LABLES=""` for serving routes with wildcard `*os-pub.example.com`.

For the new routes created with wildcard `*os-pub.example.com` it working unstable- sometime returns page with title_Application is not available_, but routes with `os-dev.example.com` are working correctly.
Setting a `NAMESPACE_LABLES="env!=dev"` for router `default-infra-router` resolves the issue.
Why the communication breaks with empty `NAMESPACE_LABLES=""`?

title: How do I stop the OpenShift Network Operator
issue: - I have a need to stop the OpenShift Network Operator. How can this be done?
resolution: - Create the following patch: ~~~ $ cat < version-patch.yaml >- op: add > path: /spec/overrides/- > value: > kind: DaemonSet > name: cluster-network-operator > namespace: openshift-cluster-network-operator > unmanaged: true > EOF ~~~- Apply this patch to the cluster version operator, and stop the dameon set for the cluster network operator. ~~~ $ oc patch clusterversion version--type json-p "$(cat version-patch.yaml)" $ oc delete ds openshift-cluster-network-operator/cluster-network-operator ~~~
root_cause: This should not be done unless instructed by Red Hat Support. This can cause your SDN and Networking to get into a bad state, and not be tracked by the CVO.

title: How do I see the changes between two OpenShift releases
issue: - I am looking to update from OCP 4.1.z to 4.1.z+2 and I want to know the changes that have occurred between these two releases.
resolution: You can generate a complete changelog between two images, by running the following command (pointing to two different release images): ~~~ $ oc adm release info--changelog=/tmp/4.0.0-0.9_to_4.0.0-0.11_change.log quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.0.0-0.9 quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.0.0-0.11 ~~~

title: Unable to schedule new pod on master node OCP 4.x
issue: - Not able to schedule any new pod on the master after successful installation of OCP 4.x- The Master node is Ready and Schedulable True
resolution: - Remove taint from the master ~~~ # oc adm taint node node.example.com node-role.kubernetes.io/master:NoSchedule- ~~~ or- Add toleration to the deployment config for scheduling new pod on the msater node ~~~ tolerations:- key: "key1" operator: "Equal" value: "value1" effect: "NoSchedule" ~~~
root_cause: - The master node is taint with the effect `NoSchedule`- New pods that do not match the taint are not scheduled onto that node.- Existing pods on the node remain.

title: OpenShift 4.x installation fails if no AWS profile is set
issue: - When aws credentials are not set with correct profile we can see error like below: ~~~ INFO Writing AWS credentials to "/root/.aws/credentials" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html) FATAL failed to fetch Terraform Variables: failed to fetch dependency of "Terraform Variables": failed to fetch dependency of "Install Config": failed to fetch dependency of "Base Domain": failed to generate asset "Platform": open /root/.aws/credentials: file exists ~~~
resolution: - When an.aws/credentials file exists and the AWS_PROFILE env var is not set the installer prompts for credentials but then fails due to the existence of.aws/credentials.- This indicates that your.aws/credentials file doesn't have a [default] profile. Since the installer doesn't know which profile to use, it asks for the credentials. When it tries to write them to disk, it sees that the file already exists and refuses to make changes out of an abundance of caution. Unfortunately, we are a bit limited here because the logic around profiles and credentials comes from AWS's go library.- Below is an example file: ~~~ cat /root/.aws/credentials [default] aws_access_key_id = xyz aws_secret_access_key = xyz ~~~

title: How to access external peripheral devices such as 3rd part serial interface devices and/or tcp based devices

resolution: The pod will likely need some level of privilege in order to access it. You will need to use nodeSelectors or taints/tolerations in order to ensure that the workload lands on the host with the device. It is recommended to try with podman locally to see if the workload works in the container with the device mounted into the container. From there we can figure out how to match any privileges/permissions/mounts.

title: 3scale Security Best Practices
issue: - I need documentation for 3scale regarding security best practices.
resolution: There are several key areas of the 3scale API Management platform that relate to security:- Authentication It is recommended to use Red Hat Single Sign On as the authentication method for the Admin Portal, the Developer Portal, and the API service. Relevant documentation for implementing this can be found for each of these below. https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.5/html/admin_portal_guide/admin-portal-sso https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.5/html/creating_the_developer_portal/authentication#enabling_and_disabling_authentication_via_red_hat_single_sign_on https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.5/html/creating_the_developer_portal/sso https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.5/html/using_the_developer_portal/openid-connect#configure-oidc-rhsso-integration- Logging The APIcast gateway has various logging levels it can be configured for. When set to either `info` or `debug` it's possible that it may log sensitive keys such APP Keys or Oauth bearer tokens. It is recommended that production gateways be configured with an appropriate logging level to avoid this. The various logging levels can be found in the documentation below under the `APICAST_LOG_LEVEL` environment variable description. https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.5/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_environment_variables In addition, it is recommended to always avoid using query parameters to send sensitive information such as access tokens or app keys. It is recommended to always use headers instead. The reason for this is that access logs may include query parameters and leave this sensitive information on any of the servers that the request passes through. This includes, the gateway, proxies, or the API backend. This is considered industry best practice and 3scale recommends the same.- Developer portal spam protection When the developer portal is open to the public it's possible that spam bots may discover this and attempt to signup illegitimate accounts. To avoid this it is recommended that spam protection be enabled. This will enable recaptcha on the signup form and prevent spam bots from signing up. Instructions on how to enable spam protection can be found in the following article: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3498841 Work is being done to integrate these instructions into the official documentation: https://issues.jboss.org/browse/THREESCALE-1110- TLS It is recommended to always use TLS (https) in all possible scenarios with 3scale. This includes the APIcast gateway, RH SSO integration, the Admin and Developer portals and anywhere else. The reason for this is that without encryption, clients may be vulnerable to man in the middle attacks and this may result in sensitive information being leaked outside of the control of the system administrator. To achieve this, it may require adding custom certificates to the Openshift router. Please refer to the Openshift documentation for how to configure this. https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/certificate_customization.html If a custom CA is required for a RH SSO integration the 3scale zync component must be configured with the CA. Instructions on how to configure this can be found here: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3342601

title: Why the egress router pod fails to start with error "failed to configure macvlan device: invalid argument"?
issue: After upgrading the OCP cluster form OCP v3.9 to OCP v3.10, egress router pod fails to start with below error. Further upgrading to OCP v3.11 the issue still persist. ~~~ 2019-05-01T23:10:09.409096-04:00 hostname atomic-openshift-node: E0501 23:10:09.407910 49357 pod_workers.go:186] Error syncing pod bc6c7d1a-6c83-11e9-855f-00505685ec44 ("egress-router-pod-xxx_egressproject(bc6c7d1a-6c83-11e9-855f-00505685ec44)"), skipping: failed to "CreatePodSandbox" for "egress-router-pod-xxx_egressproject(bc6c7d1a-6c83-11e9-855f-00505685ec44)" with CreatePodSandboxError: "CreatePodSandbox for pod \"egress-router-pod-xxx_egressproject(bc6c7d1a-6c83-11e9-855f-00505685ec44)\" failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up sandbox container \"0c0ca900d3101e6921e295ce32b5032f41cd3b9b478ffd01232c68786f8f773b\" network for pod \"egress-router-pod-xxx\": NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod \"egress-router-pod-xxx_egressproject\" network: failed to configure macvlan device: invalid argument" ~~~
The cluster has few physical nodes and few virtual, the egress router pod fails to start on ALL physical nodes but starts up successfully on virtual nodes.
Tried rebuilding one of the node and with fresh installation of RHEL 7.6 OS and then joined it to the cluster, the issue still persists.
resolution: * Currently working on it.
root_cause: * This Bug occurs because the macvlan interface in the egress router pod's network namespace ends up getting the same ifindex number as its parent interface ("enp13s0") does in the root network namespace. (That being "4".) This confuses a bit of code in the kernel that compares ifindex numbers without also comparing network namespaces.

title: Can we use the Argo Tunnel Ingres Controller with OpenShift?
issue: We are considering to use this, [Argo Tunnel Ingres Controller](https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-tunnel/reference/kubernetes/) but wonder if it can work with OpenShift and how it would be supported?
resolution: [Argo Tunnel Ingres Controller](https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-tunnel/reference/kubernetes/) is not certified with OpenShift Container Platform and thus not supported or guaranteed to work. Customers may implement [Argo Tunnel Ingres Controller](https://developers.cloudflare.com/argo-tunnel/reference/kubernetes/) on their own, but won't receive support for it or have guarantee that updates won't break the functionality. In case of problems or other questions, Red Hat will apply [How does Red Hat handle third-party software, drivers, and/or uncertified hardware/hypervisors or guest operating systems?](https://access.redhat.com/third-party-software-support) and limit it's support accordingly.

title: OpenShift CLI: "oc" and "kubectl" have different behaviours
issue: - The command "kubectl" is a symbolic link to /usr/bin/oc, the binary file where the command "oc" is implemented. However, "oc" and "kubectl" have different behaviours when they are executed. ~~~ # which oc /usr/bin/oc # which kubectl /usr/bin/kubectl # readlink-e /usr/bin/kubectl /usr/bin/oc # oc version oc v3.11.59 kubernetes v1.11.0+d4cacc0 features: Basic-Auth GSSAPI Kerberos SPNEGO Server https://master1.local:8443 openshift v3.11.59 kubernetes v1.11.0+d4cacc0 # kubectl version Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"11+", GitVersion:"v1.11.0+d4cacc0", GitCommit:"d4cacc0", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2018-12-18T16:26:37Z", GoVersion:"go1.10.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"} Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"11+", GitVersion:"v1.11.0+d4cacc0", GitCommit:"d4cacc0", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2018-12-18T16:26:37Z", GoVersion:"go1.10.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"} ~~~
root_cause: - [As mentioned on the product documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/cli_reference/differences_oc_kubectl.html#differences-oc-kubectl-using-kubectl), oc is built on top of kubectl.- OpenShift CLI is distributed as a single binary that can act as a different tool depending on its name and/or symlinks. So if named as (or have a symlink created with the name) "oc", it will provide higher-level commands generally targeted for end-users. If renamed to "kubectl", it will provide only the functionality of a kubectl binary.- "oc" provides more functionalities than "kubectl" on OpenShift and it is the recommended command.

title: Unable to create a new Service, update an existing one or sync an Application using OIDC after upgrading Red Hat 3scale On-premises from 2.3 to 2.4
issue: No new API configurations can be stored.
The following message is shown for a second in the Admin Portal: Couldn't update the Staging Configuration
And then it stays as: There seems to be an error in your Staging Configuration. Please review, fix and re-submit.
An empty list is returned from the following URL: `/admin/api/services/{service_id}/proxy/configs/staging.json`.
The `system-sidekiq` pod logs shows the following message: Exception-- could not obtain a database connection within 5.000 seconds (waited 5.000 seconds)
After 3scale 2.4 upgrade, client ID/secret of new 3scale applications are not getting auto created or synchronized in rh-sso.
resolution: Change the value of the Environment Variable `RAILS_MAX_THREADS` to `25` in the `system-sidekiq` pod. Follow the instructions below on how to perform this change from either the Terminal (using the `oc` utility) or the OpenShift UI (Web Console). ### Terminal ### When logged into the cluster with a valid administrator account and inside the 3scale project, execute the following command: ~~~ # oc set env dc/system-sidekiq RAILS_MAX_THREADS=25 ~~~ **NOTE:** If the `system-sidekiq` pod doesn't re-deploy automatically, please run the following command: ~~~ # oc rollout latest dc/system-sidekiq ~~~ ### OpenShift UI (Web Console) ### Login to the Web Console and select the project that contains Red Hat 3scale: 1. Browse to `Applications > Deployments > system-sidekiq > Environment`. 2. Click in **Add Value** to add a new Environment Variable. 3. Choose `RAILS_MAX_THREADS` as its name and `25` as the value. 4. Click on **Save**. **NOTE:** If the `system-sidekiq` pod doesn't re-deploy automatically, please click on **Deploy** in the top right of the screen. The RFE (Request For Enhancement) [THREESCALE-2323](https://issues.jboss.org/browse/THREESCALE-2323) has been opened to include this step in the Documentation. **UPDATE (05/16/2019)** The upgrading guide [Upgrading 3scale API Management 2.3 to 2.4](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/infrastructure/upgrade23-24) has been updated and it now includes this step.
root_cause: Starting from Red Hat 3scale 2.4 On-premises, the `system-resque` pod has been removed and all its tasks are now performed by `system-sidekiq`. After upgrading from 2.3 to 2.4 On-premises, the `system-sidekiq` pod inherited the value `1` as `RAILS_MAX_THREADS`, while the recommended value is `25`. In this scenario, `system-sidekiq` is running out of slots for the database connections.

title: Openshift 4.x installer does not ask for AWS credentials during installation
issue: - Openshift installer does not ask for `access key id` and `secret access key` during installation. However installation finished without an error and cluster deployed in my AWS environment. ~~~ [user@user ocp4]$./openshift-install create cluster? SSH Public Key? Platform aws? Region ap-southeast-2? Base Domain aws.cee.redhat.com? Cluster Name arnabghosh? Pull Secret [? for help] *
resolution: Workaround: Use two different user to install two different OCP cluster from a single VM ~~~ [root@user ~]# useradd new-user [root@user ~]# su new-user [new-user@user ~]$ cd && wget https://github.com/openshift/installer/releases/download/v0.12.0/openshift-install-linux-amd64 [new-user@user ~]$ mv openshift-install-linux-amd64 openshift-install [new-user@user ~]$ chmod +x openshift-install [new-user@user ~]$ openshift-install create cluster ~~~
root_cause: When user runs openshift installer on a VM for the first time to install OCP 4.0 on AWS, it always ask for `access key id` and `secret access key`. The installer stores this credentials in `/home/user/.aws/credentials` file during first installation by a user. When the same user create a new cluster, the openshift installer takes AWS credentials from `/home/user/.aws/credentials` file instead of asking user again.

title: How can I run the 4.x install multiple times using an existing install-config
issue: - How can I run the installer with out being prompted everytime for the same information when invoking `openshift-install create cluster`
resolution: The installer can be invoked multiple times. The install-config.yaml will be used from the asset directory from which the `openshift-install` command is invoked. For example, you can create an install config and save it in a cluster-agnostic location: ~~~ openshift-install--dir=initial create install-config mv initial/install-config.yaml. rm-rf initial ~~~ You can use the saved install-config for future clusters by copying it into the asset directory and then invoking the installer: ~~~ mkdir cluster-0 cp install-config.yaml cluster-0/ openshift-install--dir=cluster-0 create cluster ~~~

title: How to customize Jenkins slave container images on OpenShift v3?
issue: A custom Jenkins slave container image with new technology stack is needed.
The custom slave container image needs to be used in a Jenkins pipeline.
resolution: 1: Creates a slave Image based on `jenkins-slave-base-rhel7` ~~~ # We are basing our builder image on openshift base-rhel7 image FROM registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/jenkins-slave-base-rhel7:v3.11 # Install the required software RUN yum-y install ant && yum-y clean all USER 1001 ~~~ 2: Builds or imports the slave container image Here is the example of building the slave container image on OpenShift: ~~~ oc new-build--strategy=docker--binary=true--name=agent-ant oc start-build agent-ant--from-file=./Dockerfile ~~~ 3: Labels the image for using as a Jenkins slave [openshift-jenkins-sync-plugin](https://github.com/openshift/jenkins-sync-plugin) uses a image labeled with "role=jenkins-slave" as a Jenkins slave container. ~~~ oc label is agent-ant "role=jenkins-slave" ~~~ 4: Creates a Jenkins pipeline for using the container image as a slave Here is a example pipeline: ~~~ kind: "BuildConfig" apiVersion: "v1" metadata: name: "ant-sample-pipeline" spec: strategy: type: JenkinsPipeline jenkinsPipelineStrategy: jenkinsfile: |- pipeline {agent {node {label 'agent-ant'}} stages {stage('version') {steps {script {sh "ant--version"}}}}} ~~~

title: Connecting APIcast on Docker to 3scale AMP on OpenShift Cluster
issue: Documentation connecting APIcast deployed on Docker to 3scale API Management instance on an OpenShift Cluster needs to be updated.
resolution: [Connect APIcast from Other Deployments](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/infrastructure/onpremises-installation#connect_apicast_from_other_deployments) shows that when connecting APIcast running on Docker to a 3scale API Management instance OpenShift Cluster, ```BACKEND_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE``` environment variable (defined in [APIcast environment variables](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale/2.2/html-single/deployment_options/#apicast_environment_variables)) must be set. This is not required when connecting to 3scale AMP Management version 2.2 or later. To deploy and connect APIcast running on Docker * [Configure the integration settings](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/deployment_options/apicast-overview#configure_the_integration_settings) to the default "3scale APIcast" (even though APIcast deployed on Docker is self managed). * [Configure your service](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/deployment_options/apicast-overview#configure_your_service). Set the value of Public Base URL to the Public address of APIcast. The message "Make sure to add the correct route. " along with the link "User Default URL" will appear in the UI. Add a route if needed. * Start APIcast as described in [Run the Docker Containerized environment gateway](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/deployment_options/apicast-docker#step_2_run_the_docker_containerized_environment_gateway). An alternate way to connect without changing the Public Base URL is: * [Configure the integration settings](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/deployment_options/apicast-overview#configure_the_integration_settings) to the default "3scale APIcast" (even though APIcast deployed on Docker is self managed). * Start APIcast as described in [Run the Docker Containerized environment gateway](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.4/html/deployment_options/apicast-docker#step_2_run_the_docker_containerized_environment_gateway) * When API call is made, set the HTTP header ```Host: ```. A Request for Feature Enhancement (RFE) has been raised to update the documentation. This RFE can be tracked in the following JIRA issue: [THREESCALE-2462](https://issues.jboss.org/browse/THREESCALE-2462])

title: [xPaaS] AMQ drainer pod does not handle expired messages
issue: - The AMQ Drainer can not ignore expired messages.- The AMQ Drainer moves expired messages to the DLQ and gets stuck with the migration of those messages.

title: Unable to list the node name on the container nameserver list
issue: - Deploying new application container does not show the `node-ip` of the node where the container is scheduled.- Is this an expected behavior or should there be any changes required to be made?
resolution: - This is indeed an expected behavior, with Openshift DNS changing to `CoreDNS` the clusterDNS ip would be used as the nameserver for application containers. ~~~ # oc exec ruby-ex-1-94krj-- cat /etc/resolv.conf search testdns.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local us-east-2.compute.internal nameserver 172.30.0.10 options ndots:5 ~~~- The service IP should resolve the internal cluster domain and for the external cluster name resolution, the service would reach the respective dns daemonset pod running on all the nodes. ~~~ #oc get svc-n openshift-dns NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE dns-default ClusterIP 172.30.0.10 53/UDP,53/TCP 29d ~~~- These pods do container the `node-ip` in their nameserver list which could then used for name resolutions. ~~~ # oc get pods-n openshift-dns NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE dns-default-f9ttn 2/2 Running 0 29d dns-default-mj2wl 2/2 Running 0 29d dns-default-q7bfl 2/2 Running 0 29d dns-default-x58r6 2/2 Running 0 29d dns-default-x6fr9 2/2 Running 0 29d dns-default-xdxsc 2/2 Running 0 29d # oc exec dns-default-mj2wl-n openshift-dns-- cat /etc/resolv.conf Defaulting container name to dns. Use 'oc describe pod/dns-default-mj2wl-n openshift-dns' to see all of the containers in this pod. search us-east-2.compute.internal nameserver 10.0.0.2 ~~~

title: How to get gid affected to a gluster volume created with heketi in OCS
issue: GID affected to a volume dynamically created in Openshift Containers Storage is not visible with heketi-cli or gluster
resolution: Dynamic provisionning using gluster storageClass Get the volumle claim bound and used by the application ~~~ # oc get pvc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE test-gluster-apps Bound pvc-c34cf01f-2a26-11e9-8ce9-525400947181 1Gi RWO glusterfs-ocs-apps 31s ~~~ The Gid effectively used is added as an annotation (pv.beta.kubernetes.io/gid) to the physical volume. Use oc describe command to get the gid ~~~ # oc describe pv pvc-c34cf01f-2a26-11e9-8ce9-525400947181 Name: pvc-c34cf01f-2a26-11e9-8ce9-525400947181 Labels: Annotations: Description=Gluster-Internal: Dynamically provisioned PV gluster.kubernetes.io/heketi-volume-id=a956e37f2782974ed0d040a4c30b1aa1 gluster.org/type=file kubernetes.io/createdby=heketi-dynamic-provisioner pv.beta.kubernetes.io/gid=2000 <--------- GID from Heketi/Gluster appears here pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller=yes pv.kubernetes.io/provisioned-by=kubernetes.io/glusterfs volume.beta.kubernetes.io/mount-options=auto_unmount StorageClass: glusterfs-ocs-apps Status: Bound Claim: storage-test/test-gluster-apps Reclaim Policy: Delete Access Modes: RWO Capacity: 1Gi Message: Source: Type: Glusterfs (a Glusterfs mount on the host that shares a pod's lifetime) EndpointsName: glusterfs-dynamic-test-gluster-apps Path: vol_a956e37f2782974ed0d040a4c30b1aa1 ReadOnly: false Events: ~~~ Here after an example with static volume and GID (manual creation with Heketi-cli) GID must be added on physical volume using pv.beta.kubernetes.io/gid annotation ~~~ # oc describe pv asb-etcd Name: asb-etcd Labels: apps=asb-etcd Annotations: Description=Ansible service broker ETCD pv.beta.kubernetes.io/gid=3000 <--------- GID from Heketi/Gluster pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller=yes StorageClass: Status: Bound Claim: openshift-ansible-service-broker/etcd Reclaim Policy: Retain Access Modes: RWO Capacity: 1Gi Message: Source: Type: Glusterfs (a Glusterfs mount on the host that shares a pod's lifetime) EndpointsName: glusterfs-static-asb-etcd-endpoints Path: vol_e953a15a065f9811d6cd0a2c49d1e6a5 ReadOnly: false Events: ~~~
root_cause: When dynamic provisioning is enable with Red Hat Openshift Container Storage, the Gid effectively used is added as an annotation (pv.beta.kubernetes.io/gid) to the physical volume. To avoid duplicated information this information is available on the physical volume only

title: Verifying certificate expiry for OpenShift 4.x installs
issue: My UPI installation fails due to certificate errors
root_cause: When deploying an OpenShift 4 environment using the UPI method, any delays between generating the ignition configuration files and actual cluster bootstrap could cause certificate expiry. As part of the UPI deployment procedure, creating ignition configuration files causes a number of TLS certificates to be created and are used by various Kubernetes components as part of the cluster bootstrap. To minimise security exposure, a number of these certificates are seeded with a 24hr expiry, this is the time in which the person deploying a cluster has to complete the cluster bootstrap process. Exceeding this time period will result in certificates expiring and a failed installed. This could be observed at either the etcd creation or cluster bootstrap stages of the installation, and may manifest in error messages such as the following: (these log files are examples from [gathered installation logs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.1/installing/installing-gather-logs.html#installation-bootstrap-gather_installing-troubleshooting)) ~~~ $ tail artifacts/journals/kubelet.log Jun 13 14:10:07 etcd-0 hyperkube[860]: E0613 14:10:07.401463 860 kubelet.go:2274] node "etcd-0" not found Jun 13 14:10:07 etcd-0 hyperkube[860]: E0613 14:10:07.502831 860 kubelet.go:2274] node "etcd-0" not found Jun 13 14:10:07 etcd-0 hyperkube[860]: E0613 14:10:07.603331 860 kubelet.go:2274] node "etcd-0" not found ~~~ ~~~ $ cat bootstrap/journals/bootkube.log-- Logs begin at Wed 2019-06-12 20:23:07 UTC, end at Wed 2019-06-12 21:08:42 UTC.-- Jun 12 20:23:33 boots-int systemd[1]: Started Bootstrap a Kubernetes cluster.... Jun 12 20:29:01 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: etcd cluster up. Killing etcd certificate signer...... Jun 12 20:29:41 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: Created "0000_00_cluster-version-operator_00_namespace.yaml" namespaces.v1./openshift-cluster-version-n... Jun 12 20:30:18 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: Pod Status:openshift-kube-apiserver/kube-apiserver DoesNotExist Jun 12 20:30:18 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: Pod Status:openshift-kube-scheduler/openshift-kube-scheduler DoesNotExist Jun 12 20:30:18 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: Pod Status:openshift-kube-controller-manager/kube-controller-manager DoesNotExist Jun 12 20:30:18 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: Pod Status:openshift-cluster-version/cluster-version-operator Pending Jun 12 20:49:08 boots-int bootkube.sh[1509]: Error: error while checking pod status: timed out waiting for the condition ~~~

title: Troubleshooting the OpenShift Container Platform 4.x: cluster-network-operator
issue: - I don't seem to have a functioning SDN with my newly created cluster, what data should I collect to investigate the issue?
root_cause: The cluster network operator is responsible for deploying the networking components. It does this in response to a special object created by the installer. From a deployment perspective, the network operator is often the *"canary in the coal mine."* It runs very early in the installation process, after the master nodes have come up but before the bootstrap control plane has been torn down. It can be indicative of more subtle installer issues, such as long delays in bringing up master nodes or apiserver communication issues. Nevertheless, it can have other bugs.

title: Uninstall and reinstallation of OCS with playbook results in heal status reporting missing volfile
issue: After running the OCS uninstall playbook and re-installing OCS heal and heal info commands report failed. Example: ~~~ sh-4.2# gluster volume heal vol_160b27f813d558545fd0aa63ba1f6a3a info vol_160b27f813d558545fd0aa63ba1f6a3a: Not able to fetch volfile from glusterd Volume heal failed. ~~~
resolution: Remove /var/lib/glusterd, /etc/glusterfs, and /var/lib/heketi directories manually from the OCS host nodes after the uninstall playbook is complete: ~~~ # rm-rf /var/lib/glusterd /etc/glusterfs /var/lib/heketi ~~~
root_cause: This is a known issue with the current version of the openshift-ansible package starting with 3.11.84-1 and newer. See the following Bugzilla link for information: [BZ#1722231](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1722231 "BZ#1722231").

title: Deferr Quay garbage collection for an unspecified length of time
issue: A bug in the Red Hat Quay's garbage collection system can cause a manifest loss in the registry. The images can still be pulled, but manifests can't be viewed in the UI.
resolution: The garbage collection needs to, immediately, be deferred until a fix is available. To defer garbage collection, the following needs to be added to Quay's config.yaml file.: ~~~ GARBAGE_COLLECTION_FREQUENCY: 15552000 STAGGER_WORKERS: false ~~~ This will disable garbage collection for 6 months. Quay will need to be restarted immediately afterwards.

title: Customizing projectRequestTemplate in Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4
issue: - How to set__projectRequestTemplate__ in `Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4`?- How to edit_master-config.yaml_ file in `Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4` to configure__projectRequestTemplate__?
resolution: In `Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 3` version it was possible to modify the_master-config.yaml_ file after which restart of the Master API service was required. From `Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4`, a lot of these master configurations are handled by separate resources. The configuration for `projectRequestTemplate` is described as part of the__projects.config.openshift.io__ Custom Resource Definition (CRD) whose description is as follows: ~~~ projectRequestTemplate: description: projectRequestTemplate is the template to use for creating projects in response to projectrequest. This must point to a template in 'openshift-config' namespace. It is optional. If it is not specified, a default template is used. ~~~ Thus, you need to create a template of the resource kind__Template__ in the__openshift-config__ project which will be referred by the project being created.

title: How to modify CIDR range for instances created during OpenShift 4.x install
issue: - How to modify the default CIDR ranges created by installer in Openshift 4.x- Installing an installer-provided infrastructure OpenShift cluster and need to change the subnet for services and pods
resolution: - In order to allow users to customize their installation, the installer can be invoked multiple times. The state is stored in a hidden file in the asset directory and contains all of the intermediate artifacts. This allows the installer to pause during the installation and wait for the user to modify intermediate artifacts.- For example, you can create an install config and save it in a cluster-agnostic location: ~~~ openshift-install--dir=initial create install-config ~~~- Modify the CIDR ranges like below: ~~~ networking: clusterNetwork:- cidr: 10.128.0.0/14 hostPrefix: 23 machineCIDR: 10.0.0.0/16 networkType: OpenShiftSDN serviceNetwork:- 172.30.0.0/16 ~~~- NOTE: This might not be available in all UPI (user-provided infrastructure) installations. Check the documentation as well for updates.

title: Quay: Migrate from LocalStorage to object storage
issue: Quay users running with the LocalStorage storage engine may desire to move to object storage to utilize Quay features such as geo-replication of images across data centers.
resolution: ### Prerequisites Stop all running Quay container(s) [Back up](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3498981) the quay database and image storage ### Identify Storage Directory Using the LocalStorage engine requires mounting over `/datastorage` dir. ~~~ $ docker ps 73a0a0ab4035 quay.io/coreos/quay:v2.9.4 "/bin/sh-c./quay-e…" 0.0.0.0:80-> 80/tcp, 0.0.0.0:443-> 443/tcp, 8443/tcp quay-container ~~~ ~~~ $ docker inspect quay-container | grep Binds-A2 "Binds": ["/etc/quay/config:/conf/stack", "/etc/quay/storage:/datastorage" ~~~ `/etc/quay/storage` is mounted over the `/datastorage` dir therefore contains image data that must be copied to object storage. ### Inspect Quay datastorage directory ~~~ $ cd /etc/quay/storage $ ls registry $ ls registry/_verify sha256 uploads ~~~ ### Recursively Upload image data to Object Storage Each supported object storage engine will have a specific tool to accomplish this task. It is very important to upload to the correct path within the object storage bucket. By default `storage_path` is set to `/datastorage/registry` therefore `/datastorage` should be appended to the bucket when uploading. #### Generic S3 Upload [s3cmd](https://s3tools.org/) is a useful tool when uploading to a S3 compatible object store: ~~~ $ s3cmd put--recursive /etc/quay/storage s3://quay-storage/datastorage ~~~ #### AWS S3 ~~~ $ aws s3 cp /etc/quay/storage s3://quaybucket/datastorage--recursive ~~~ ### Reconfigure Quay with Object Storage Engine Restart a single Quay container, navigate to the superuser panel, edit the Registry Storage settings to utilize the object storage, save the config, and restart the Quay container. ### Test Test that image data has been properly migrated to object storage by pulling containers from a variety of users/organizations. $ docker pull quay.example.com/example/helloworld
root_cause: Quay does not have a built in mechanism for migrating from LocalStorage (NFS) to object storage.

title: Cluster Console status shows API Success Rate is less than 100% in OCP 3.11
issue: In OpenShift's Cluster Console (located in project `openshift-console`), the status page for `All Projects` shows `API Request Sucess Rate` as less than 100%.
resolution: The `API Request Success Rate` status is an indicator for any HTTP request made to OpenShift's Master API. Ideally, status should be as close to 100% as possible, but this is not always feasible. Any HTTP request that doesn't reply with a `2xx` HTTP code will count as an API request failure on this indicator. Some examples: * A login attempt is made, but the user doesn't exist, or the password is wrong; * Cluster user tries to `get`, `edit` or `delete` a resource that doesn't exist; * Internal requests returning `Gateway Timeout`; * Internal requests returning `Host Not Found` DNS errors. Some of these unexpected returns are acceptable for determined scenarios, while others can mean health issues to the cluster. It's up to the cluster administrator to decide which is the *normal* rate. For example, the cluster administrator can look at the indicator's history to see if the rate is very different from previous usage history, and if it is, get details and troubleshooting to see if it's an issue for cluster health. To get requests' details, read this documentation section: [Monitoring Events and Logs: Cluster Logs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/security/monitoring.html#security-monitoring-audit-log).

title: Modifying the list of roles available via the Membership page in OpenShift 3.9 WebUI
issue: - In Resources> Membership UI page of OpenShift 3.9, we cannot see custom roles when we try to edit the membership and assign a role to a user. But when we check the "show hidden roles" field at the bottom, we can see those roles. Is there a way, we can get our custom roles while we edit without checking the "show hidden roles".- How can I view extra roles in the membership tab when adding roles to users via the WebUI?- Would it be feasible to create a duplicate 'admin_backup' of the built-in admin role, and then edit the built-in role to have the permissions we have assigned to the 'admin_n' custom role?
resolution: There is a [whitelist of roles](https://github.com/openshift/origin-web-console/blob/enterprise-3.11/app/scripts/constants.js#L184) to include if none are already included in the project. That said, it is possible to customize `MEMBERSHIP_WHITELIST` using custom scripts in the master config file that override this variable. Reference the following documentation on how to add custom scripts to the web console: [Changing the membership whitelist](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/web_console_customization.html#changing-the-membership-whitelist) [Loading custom scripts and stylesheets](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/web_console_customization.html#loading-custom-scripts-and-stylesheets) ### To show additional project roles:- Simply create a new role in that project and it should automatically appear in the drop down. ### To show additional cluster roles:- Create a WHITELIST.js file, similar to the [example in the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.9/install_config/web_console_customization.html#changing-the-membership-whitelist), including any of your custom clusterroles in the list: ~~~ window.OPENSHIFT_CONSTANTS.MEMBERSHIP_WHITELIST = ["admin", "basic-user", "edit", "system:deployer", "system:image-builder", "system:image-puller", "system:image-pusher", "view", "custom-role-1", "custom-role-2"]; ~~~- Share that file via a `https://` URL that is resolvable in your browser- Edit the configmap for the webconsole to add that url as an extension scriptURLs: ~~~ oc edit configmap webconsole-config-n openshift-web-console # This opens a editor where you can make the below change: apiVersion: v1 data: webconsole-config.yaml: | apiVersion: webconsole.config.openshift.io/v1 clusterInfo:... extensions: properties: {} scriptURLs:- https://test.example.com/whitelist.js features:... ~~~- Finally, scale the web console pod down and backup. Once the pod is up and running you should now see your additional cluster roles! ~~~ oc scale-n openshift-web-console deployment webconsole--replicas=0 oc scale-n openshift-web-console deployment webconsole--replicas=1 # Change this number to however many replicas you had previously ~~~

title: What challenges are there when installing Openshift in Hybrid Cloud environment
issue: - How can containers running on both On-premise and On-cloud models should be orchestrated by OpenShift- Would there be 2 different installations of OpenShift is required to orchestrate between these two models (on-premise and Cloud)?
resolution: - Nothing in OpenShift or Kubernetes understands multiple infrastructures or GEO segmented deployments. So to successfully deploy and operate OpenShift onto multiple infrastructures or GEO segmented environments, OpenShift either has to think it's on a single infrastructure or you, as the deployer of the software (OpenShift), need to bring that awareness and intelligence to the product (often achieved via a custom UI/Portal that uses the OpenShift API's of one or multiple clusters on the backend). In both situations a sophisticated IaaS investment is needed to make "stretch clusters" a reality.- By far the more common deployment pattern is to deploy multiple OpenShift clusters--one in each location or data center or IaaS environment (as stated above)--and then wire a northbound (UI/Portal) as well as provision a global load balancer to allow for traffic to come in via IP proximity. In most customer situations, this is what we (Red Hat) recommend since it is simpler to deploy and manage.- However as not all business requirements are the same, and sophisticated IaaS deployments and investments have been made by some customers, there are situations where it is feasible to consider a "stretch cluster," Because a "stretch cluster" or multi-site deployment topology can mean many things to different people Red Hat classifies OpenShift Container Platform multi-site deployment topology to be one of the following:- Three (3) masters on the same DC + infra and app nodes on a remote site (private or public cloud)- Three (3) masters on the same DC + infra + app nodes on a the first site + additional app nodes on a remote site (private or public cloud)- Masters and infra/app nodes splitted between N Data Centers (DCs). The value of N is often 3 (as its what we recommend), to avoid split-brain scenarios with DC loss, but in some situations can be 2 (depending on your needs for fault tolerance).- Below are the challenges that needed to be worked by the customer:- A flat network between Data Centers Defined as a single vlan or subnet that instances (systems) on the network see each other as being neighbors.- A low latency network (with less that 2ms of latency) between instances (systems) The main consideration with this requirement is tied to etcd1. All reads and writes run through a etcd cluster (cluster of 3) and that round robin trip across the 3 instances in order to reach quorum needs to be a fast trip or you risk API failures.- A high throughput network- The number of etcd instances must to be an odd number (3, 5, 7... etc) to maintain quorum. See etcd's documentation on deployments for mor details. Note: Cluster size (of OpenShift) and by proxy etcd can impact how many etcd nodes you decide to run. More instances of etcd (above what are needed for fault tolerance), are not recommended due to the replication of data that happens between instances. You can not have 2 in DC-Alpha and 1 in DC-Beta, as the loss of a DC will could cause etcd to loose and thus we (Red Hat) recommend a minimum of 3 DCs.- HA/Fault Tolerant Storage, that spans and is accessible to all instances (systems) in all Data Centers (DCs) In the case of the "registry" you also want some "object storage" solution.- Some top level service proxy or load balancer. This is to allows your application pod[s] to move anywhere in the cluster, and still be accessible or available if migrations happen. in some cases GEO awareness is an issue (to minimize latency), so this top level service proxy or load balancer, needs to be possible of handling or dealing with these requirements. ###### Customer handle federation in some way themselves. Red Hat does not support hybrid installation setup ###### Note: This is not a configuration that is tested by QE (at least, not at scale).

title: Creating a custom role with the ability to check the pods status but disallow to check the pod logs.
issue: - I want to grant a role to a user who can **view*
the pod **status*

resolution: - Create a back up of view role ~~~ $ oc get clusterrole view-o yaml > [file.yaml] ~~~- From the file taken as a backup remove the line where you see pod/logs- Also remove the following lines as well: ~~~ aggregationRule: clusterRoleSelectors:- matchLabels: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/aggregate-to-view: "true" ~~~- Create the new role by running the following: ~~~ $ oc create-f < file.yaml > ~~~- Apply that role to a user that you want to provide the access to view the status of the pod and disallow to view the logs. ~~~ $ oc adm add-cluster-role-to-user < role-name > < user-name > ~~~

title: How to configure/enable auditd on RHEL CoreOS on OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: How to configure auditd on RHEL CoreOS?
We need `auditd` running on RHEL CoreOS, how can we enable it?
resolution: `auditd` is installed and available on RHEL CoreOS, but disabled by default. In order to enable `auditd` and have it run on OpenShift Container Platform- Node(s), `MachineConfigs` can be used. ### Basic configuration changes after OpenShift Container Platform installation Basic instructions on how to manage and change certain configuration files and options on RHEL CoreOS with OpenShift Container Platform 4, can be found on [Changing Ignition Configs after installation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.1/architecture/architecture-rhcos.html#digging-into-machine-config_architecture-rhcos). It's recommended to create the additional `MachineConfig` within a `JSON` file format and apply it to OpenShift Container Platform 4, using `oc create-f ` command. The `MachineConfigs` are read in order (from *00* to *99*). Labels inside the `MachineConfigs` identify the type of Openshift Container Platform- Node each is for (`master` or `worker`). If the same file appears in multiple `MachineConfigs` files, the last one wins. So, for example, any file that appears in a *99* file would replace the same file that appeared in a *00* file. The `MachineConfigController` will roll out the change across the cluster 1 Openshift Container Platform- Node at a time (by default) and part of this process will to reboot the Openshift Container Platform- Node. All configuration changes will be picked up on the reboot and applied accordingly. More information on this process and workflow can be found on [Understanding the machine config operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.1/architecture/control-plane.html#understanding-machine-config-operator_control-plane). ### Enable auditd on RHEL CoreOS Create a file called `30-audit-worker.json` with the below content to enable `auditd.service` on all OpenShift Container Platform- Node(s). As highlighted above, to have the service enabled for all OpenShift Container Platform- Node(s) the configruation needs to be created for each `MachineConfigPool`. ~~~ {"apiVersion": "machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1", "kind": "MachineConfig", "metadata": {"labels": {"machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role": "worker"}, "name": "30-audit-worker"}, "spec": {"config": {"ignition": {"version": "2.2.0"}, "systemd": {"units": [{"name": "auditd.service", "enabled": true}]}}}} ~~~ Apply the change once ready by running `oc create-f 30-audit-worker.json`. Once successfully applied, wait for the `MachineConfigController` to pick up the change and apply it to all Openshift Container Platform- Node the label is matching.
