title: Pods run into errors because the pods are reviewed by restricted SCC even if hostmount-anyuid is specified.
issue: Pods using `hostmount-anyuid` SCC cannot start with errors. ~~~ $ oc project kube-service-catalog $ oc get pod-o wide NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE apiserver-xxxx 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 12 24m 10.128.66.202 xxxxxxxxx $ oc logs apiserver-xxxx... F0729 02:29:05.967194 1 storage_decorator.go:57] Unable to create storage backend: config (5m0s 1m0s}), err (open /etc/origin/master/master.etcd-client.crt: permission denied) ~~~

The pods are reviewed by `restricted` SCC even if `hostmount-anyuid` is specified. ~~~ $ oc get pods apiserver-xxx-o yaml... apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: annotations: openshift.io/scc: restricted... spec:... serviceAccount: service-catalog-apiserver serviceAccountName: service-catalog-apiserver $ oc get scc hostmount-anyuid-o yaml... users:- system:serviceaccount:openshift-infra:pv-recycler-controller- system:serviceaccount:kube-service-catalog:service-catalog-apiserver ~~~
resolution: Make sure that `restricted` SCC hasn't been modified and `allowHostDirVolumePlugin` keeps `false`: ~~~ $ oc get-o yaml scc restricted allowHostDirVolumePlugin: true allowHostIPC: false... ~~~ If it has been modified, it should be returned to the default value `false`: ~~~ $ oc get-o yaml scc restricted allowHostDirVolumePlugin: false allowHostIPC: false... ~~~
root_cause: The SCCs are applied to a pod in the order: 1. `restricted` SCC tries to be applied. The priorities are defined in [the securitycontextconstraints/byrestrictions.go code](https://github.com/openshift/origin/blob/release-3.11/pkg/security/apiserver/securitycontextconstraints/byrestrictions.go) 2. [If the pod uses hostPath](https://github.com/openshift/origin/blob/release-3.11/pkg/security/apiserver/securitycontextconstraints/provider.go#L238), the `restricted` SCC cannot be applied. 3. The next priority SCC, `hostmount-anyuid` is applied. If `restricted` SCC has modified to allow mounting host directories, `restricted` SCC becomes to be able to applied to a pod in the #2 process. That's why the pod is reviewed by `restricted` SCC not by `hostmount-anyuid` SCC.

title: How to use images of registry.redhat.io without sharing the Customer Portal login information to non-admin users on OpenShift?
issue: How do OpenShift non-admin users like developers use images of `registry.redhat.io`?
OpenShift non-admin users cannot use images of `registry.redhat.io` because the registry requires authentication.
Because the auth info of `registry.redhat.io` is the same as the Red Hat Customer Portal's login info, it should not be distributed to non-admin users.
resolution: The images of `registry.redhat.io` should be imported as ImageStreams in the `openshift` project to share the images in the cluster. OpenShift has the `registry.redhat.io` auth info in the`openshift` project. ~~~ # OpenShift 3.x $ oc describe secrets imagestreamsecret-n openshift Name: imagestreamsecret... Type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Data ====.dockerconfigjson: 1923 bytes # OpenShift 4.x $ oc describe secrets samples-registry-credentials-n openshift Name: samples-registry-credentials... Type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Data ====.dockerconfigjson: 2758 bytes ~~~ The images of `registry.redhat.io` can be imported using the secrets. ~~~ $ oc import-image rhel-minimal-n openshift--from=registry.redhat.io/rhel-minimal--all--reference-policy=local--confirm ~~~ The developers can use the imageStreams even if they don't know the `registry.redhat.io` auth info. ~~~ $ oc login-u user1 $ oc project user1-project $ cat < <'EOF' > sample-buildconfig.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: List items:- apiVersion: v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: rhel-minimal-base- apiVersion: v1 kind: BuildConfig metadata: name: rhel-minimal-base spec: output: to: kind: ImageStreamTag name: rhel-minimal-base:latest source: dockerfile: | FROM registry.redhat.io/rhel-minimal CMD tail-f /dev/null type: Dockerfile strategy: dockerStrategy: # refer to the ImageStream in the openshift project from: kind: ImageStreamTag name: rhel-minimal:latest namespace: openshift type: Docker triggers:- imageChange: {} type: ImageChange EOF $ oc apply-f buildconfigsample.yaml ~~~

title: Etcdctl command is not present in OpenShift 3.11. How is the etcd cluster investigated?
issue: `etcdctl` command is not present in OpenShift 3.11. How is the etcd cluster investigated? ~~~ [root@master-0 ~]# etcdctl bash: etcdctl: command not found ~~~
resolution: Use the `etcdctl3` / `etcdctl2` aliases to investigate the etcd cluster's status. There's no need to use the options to access the etcd cluster like `cert-file`, `key-file` or `ca-file`. ~~~ [root@master-0 ~]# etcdctl3 member list e852ee5907c96df6, started, master-0.etcd.example.com, https://10.74.180.64:2380, https://10.74.180.64:2379 [root@master-0 ~]# etcdctl2 cluster-health member e852ee5907c96df6 is healthy: got healthy result from https://10.74.180.64:2379 cluster is healthy ~~~
root_cause: In most cases`etcdctl` command is not installed on OpenShift 3.10 or 3.11. The `etcdctl` command would be only on the following nodes: * The master nodes of a cluster upgraded from v3.9 * The dedicated etcd nodes of v3.11/v3.10 cluster The `etcdctl3` / `etcdctl2` are aliases defined in the`/etc/profile.d/etcdctl.sh`. The aliases use the options like `cert-file`, `key-file` or `ca-file` to access to the etcd cluster. ~~~ [root@master-0 ~]# cat /etc/profile.d/etcdctl.sh #!/bin/bash # Sets up handy aliases for etcd, need etcdctl2 and etcdctl3 because # command flags are different between the two. Should work on stand # alone etcd hosts and master + etcd hosts too because we use the peer keys. etcdctl2() {cmd="ETCDCTL_API=2 etcdctl--cert-file /etc/etcd/peer.crt--key-file /etc/etcd/peer.key--ca-file /etc/etcd/ca.crt--endpoints https://`hostname`:2379 ${@}" if [[-f /usr/local/bin/master-exec]]; then /usr/local/bin/master-exec etcd etcd /bin/sh-c "$cmd" else /bin/sh-c "$cmd" fi} etcdctl3() {cmd="ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl--cert /etc/etcd/peer.crt--key /etc/etcd/peer.key--cacert /etc/etcd/ca.crt--endpoints https://`hostname`:2379 ${@}" if [[-f /usr/local/bin/master-exec]]; then /usr/local/bin/master-exec etcd etcd /bin/sh-c "$cmd" else /bin/sh-c "$cmd" fi} ~~~

title: The 'system-mysql' pod from Red Hat 3scale API Management shows the messages "Aborted connection" and "Got an error reading communication packets" on the logs
issue: The `system-mysql` pod in all of our 3scale instances is filled with error messages- mostly packet communication messages happening every 10 seconds: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.625314Z 39 [Note] Got an error reading communication packets Also aborted connection messages, happening less frequently: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.625314Z 75 [Note] Aborted connection 75 to db: 'system' user: 'root' host: '1.1.1.1' (Got an error reading communication packets)
resolution: This issue is happening because the `Liveness Probe` configured on OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) is calling `system-mysql` using a regular `TCP` connection, but not a valid `mysql` one. The probe detects the pod as up (`TCP` connection is successful), however `system-mysql` considers it an anomaly since it's not valid `mysql` connection and informs on the logs about it. Hence, although it might cause a lot of noise currently on the pod's logs, these messages are otherwise harmless and could be safely ignored if not followed by any other error messages. The Bug [THREESCALE-2293](https://issues.jboss.org/browse/THREESCALE-2293) has been created to address this issue. It's likely that the `Liveness Probe` will be changed in a future release in order to provide a real `mysql` call instead of a regular `TCP` one.
root_cause: Following below is the `Liveness Probe` from the current `system-mysql` deploymentconfig object, indicating a simple `TCP` connection to check the pod status instead of a `mysql` level one: ~~~ livenessProbe: failureThreshold: 3 initialDelaySeconds: 30 periodSeconds: 10 successThreshold: 1 tcpSocket: port: 3306 timeoutSeconds: 1 name: system-mysql ports:- containerPort: 3306 protocol: TCP ~~~

title: OpenShift Images ‘:latest’ points to older image (and security grade are lower than reality)
issue: - Some OpenShift images “:latest” tags don’t point to the ‘latest’ image or image version that Red Hat ships.- For example the jenkins master image points to a version of the image from the OpenShift 3.6 release.- These images show a security grade less than an ‘A’, so when will these images be updated?
resolution: Where multiple versions of a product exist in the same container repository (such as openshift3), the:latest tag may not always be applied to the most recent minor version of container image for a product release (for various reasons). Customers should review all tags for a given container image and reference the security grade for tags relevant to their product version. ## Reference Links:- [OpenShift Lifecycle](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift)- [Life Cycle Changes announced with 3.10 GA](https://access.redhat.com/articles/3532971) (on 2018-08-28):
root_cause: A number of container images are shipped as part of OpenShift and maintained per the OpenShift life cycle, however, may not have the:latest tag pointing to the most recent release. One such example is with the Jenkins container image, which is using the:latest tag for the 3.6 version of OpenShift, this minor release is no longer maintained and may be subject to vulnerabilities. Customers using OpenShift v3 are advised to upgrade to the latest release of OpenShift. ### More details on the Jenkins Image In the Jenkins Example, the:latest tag was intentionally pointing to the 3.6 version to address limitations in version compatibility..- [https://github.com/openshift/jenkins/pull/431](https://github.com/openshift/jenkins/pull/431) With version 3.7 Red Hat decided to pin the jenkins ‘:latest’ tag to always point to a version 3.6 jenkins image. This was necessary because all clusters prior to version 3.7 contained code designed to pull the jenkins image via the “latest” tag, however the v3.7 jenkins image was not compatible with v3.6 clusters due to embedded oc client binaries in the image which were not cross-version compatible. To avoid impacting customers running v3.6 and earlier clusters, Red Hat pinned the:latest tag so that it would continue to point to an image which could work in those clusters. Version 3.7 and newer clusters contained logic to pull version specific tags (e.g. a v3.7 cluster will pull the jenkins image via the 3.7 tag, not the:latest tag).

title: Why is the cluster monitoring config rolled back after adding alert rules on OpenShift 3.11?
issue: Why is the cluster monitoring config rolled back in the following steps? 1. Change `configmap/cluster-monitoring-config` according to [the documented steps for etcd monitoring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/prometheus_cluster_monitoring.html#configuring-etcd-monitoring_prometheus-cluster-monitoring). 2. Add some alert rules to the Alertmanager config according to [the solution for editing Alertmanager config](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3804781). 3. The `configmap/cluster-monitoring-config` changed by the step `1.` is rolled back to the default.
resolution: If the `configmap/cluster-monitoring-config` was changed from the default, the `playbooks/openshift-monitoring/config.yml` playbook cannot be used. Edit the Alertmanager rules by manual: ~~~ # Export the current Alertmanager config $ oc project openshift-monitoring $ oc extract secret/alertmanager-main--keys alertmanager.yaml--to=./ # Edit the Alertmanager config $ vim alertmanager-main.yaml... # Import the edited Alertmanager config to the cluster $ oc create secret generic alertmanager-main--from-file=alertmanager.yaml--dry-run-o yaml | oc replace-f- ~~~
root_cause: The playbook `playbooks/openshift-monitoring/config.yml` rolls back the `configmap/cluster-monitoring-config` to the default. See also [the playbook source code](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-ansible/blob/release-3.11/roles/openshift_cluster_monitoring_operator/tasks/install.yaml#L88). Modifying the `configmap/cluster-monitoring-config` using the playbook is not supported.

title: How to collect gluster FUSE client logs in Openshift Container Storage?
issue: For troubleshooting purposes, it's quite often needed to collect gluster FUSE client mount logs.
In an on-premise gluster enviroment, they are located at `/var/log/glusterfs/.log` by default.
However, when a gluster volume is used as a persistent volume in openshift, where are these logs stored?
resolution: Let's use the volume name `vol_8392ee620beb8d97d4e28ea18f669290` as an starting point for an example on how to gather this information. 1. First, check for the persistent volume name in Openshift (PV) matching this volume in the gluster side. One possible way of getting this info is by running the command: for i in $(oc get pvc--all-namespaces | awk '{print $4}' | grep-v VOLUME); do echo "PVC $i"; oc describe pv $i | grep-i path; done It'll give the PV and its associated gluster volume: ** PVC pvc-c5c9afef-292b-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00 ** ** Path: vol_8392ee620beb8d97d4e28ea18f669290 ** PVC pvc-5440cc68-2b9c-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00 Path: vol_fc6692443139b8dd60d737774ec40b5e PVC pvc-d0ff9d1f-292a-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00 Path: vol_527d36a0fa0fef4156b514518d867902 In this case, the matching PV name for the volume is `pvc-c5c9afef-292b-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00` 2. Describe the PVC contents to check its properties. In this example, the PVC name is `postgresql` [root@master-0 ~]# oc get pvc | grep pvc-c5c9afef-292b-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00 postgresql Bound pvc-c5c9afef-292b-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00 1Gi RWO glusterfs-storage 5d Describing the PVC, it shows that it's bounded to a pod in the project `my-test-project`. [root@master-0 ~]# oc describe pvc postgresql Name: postgresql Namespace: my-test-project StorageClass: glusterfs-storage Status: Bound Volume: pvc-c5c9afef-292b-11e9-a72e-fa163e6bed00 Labels: app=rails-pgsql-persistent template=rails-pgsql-persistent Annotations: openshift.io/generated-by=OpenShiftNewApp pv.kubernetes.io/bind-completed=yes pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller=yes volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner=kubernetes.io /glusterfs Finalizers: [] Capacity: 1Gi Access Modes: RWO Events: 3. Next step consists in checking which pod claims this PVC. title: After moving MySQL to an external database, creating a new Service on Red Hat 3scale API Management returns HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error)
issue:
I used `mysqldump` to get a copy of the database running in OpenShift, and after configuring the external MySQL server with the database backup, updated the secret with the Database url to point to the new server: mysql2://: @ / This appeared to work until we tried to add a service or credential, and I was getting `HTTP 500` errors (both via API calls and admin ui). I found the following message in the `system-sphinx` logs: Exception-- Mysql2::Error: The user specified as a definer ('root'@'%') does not exist: INSERT INTO `audits` (`auditable_id`, `auditable_type`, `action`, `provider_id`, `kind`, `audited_changes`, `created_at`, `version`, `request_uuid`) VALUES (12345, 'Contract', 'update', 2, 'Cinstance', '---
first_daily_traffic_at:
- 2019-09-14 00:51:59 UTC
- 2019-09-16 12:15:54 UTC
', '2019-09-17 13:34:14', 10, '1234567890')
resolution: ***Disclaimer:** Configuring an external MySQL database on Red Hat 3scale On-premises is currently not officially supported or documented and subject to [Commercially Reasonable Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/710953) only.* Use the `'root'@'%'` user as in the example below: mysql2://root: @ / Obtain the `base64` value of the endpoint defined above and edit the `URL` parameter inside the `system-database` secret to include this value as `base64`: $ echo "mysql2://root: @ / " | base64 **NOTE:** Create a new `'root'@'%'` user in the database if it doesn't exist, granting all the necessary privileges. Please also notice that it's needed to use a valid `IP address` instead of the `hostname` for the new instance.
root_cause: Some components of Red Hat 3scale API Management On-premises are hardcoded to use the `'root'@'%'` user. This issue might be addressed later once configuring an external MySQL database becomes fully supported.

title: How to restart nodes in OCP 3
issue: - How to restart the machine, virtual machine, or instance that an OpenShift node is running on
resolution: ### For OCP 3.X #### Read for: [Infrastructure nodes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/manage_nodes.html#infrastructure-nodes). #### For regular nodes and masters:- [Mark the node as unschedulable](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/manage_nodes.html#marking-nodes-as-unschedulable-or-schedulable)- This forbids any new pods from scheduling on this node. ~~~ $ oc adm manage-node--schedulable=false ~~~- [Evacuate pods from the node](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/manage_nodes.html#evacuating-pods-on-nodes)- For more options on how drain, check the documentation. ~~~ $ oc adm drain [--pod-selector=] You can use--ignore-daemonsets and set it to true to ignore daemonset-managed pods: $ oc adm drain--ignore-daemonsets=true ~~~- Stop `atomic-openshift-node` service ~~~ # systemctl stop atomic-openshift-node ~~~- [Restart the VM, instance, or physical machine](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/manage_nodes.html#rebooting-nodes) ### For OCP 3.9 and previous- Check that the processes started automatically (if they were enabled in systemd) or start them manually ~~~ # systemctl status docker # systemctl status atomic-openshift-node # systemctl start docker # systemctl start atomic-openshift-node.service # systemctl status openvswitch ~~~- [Optional but recommended] Verify the health of the docker storage on the node: ~~~ //You should have a dm.thinpooldev value in the /etc/sysconfig/docker-storage file and a docker-pool logical volume: # ssh # cat /etc/sysconfig/docker-storage DOCKER_STORAGE_OPTIONS=--storage-opt dm.fs=xfs--storage-opt dm.thinpooldev=/dev/mapper/docker--vg-docker--pool # lvs LV VG Attr LSize Pool Origin Data% Meta% Move Log Cpy%Sync Convert docker-pool rhel twi-a-t--- 9.29g 0.00 0.12 ~~~- Make the node schedulable again ~~~ # oadm manage-node--schedulable=true ~~~

title: Facing issues in adding labels to namespaces
issue: - Cannot add labels to namespaces- Adding labels gives no RBAC policy errors- I need to use the wildcard namespace matcher- I need a possibility to allow traffic from one namespace to another to reduce the efforts of remembering to add labels to each pod that is in the namespace.
resolution: - A recommendation would be to go through the published documentation highlighting how to [manage limit and quota](https://docs.openshift.com/dedicated/3/admin_guide/managing_projects.html#managing-limits-and-quota-on-project-resources) as it should be really helpful, to begin with:- Why some of the namespaces have a policy and some do not?- The reason is that `at the time of creating this article` project template was only recently added to OpenShift Dedicated environment, so it's likely you have some projects created from `before` the template went into effect.- When the template was added, it started applying those default network policies.- You can modify the project template so that every project created after you modify the template can have a label added to it where the label matches the project name.- You would just have to modify the first `object` to look like: ~~~- apiVersion: v1 kind: Project metadata: labels:- project: ${PROJECT_NAME} annotations: openshift.io/description: ${PROJECT_DESCRIPTION} openshift.io/display-name: ${PROJECT_DISPLAYNAME} openshift.io/requester: ${PROJECT_REQUESTING_USER} name: ${PROJECT_NAME} spec: {} status: {} ~~~- You can use the `project` label as the selector
root_cause: - The reasons for `pod selector networkpolicy` not working could be majorly because you have to specify the pod selector *AND* a wildcard namespace selector.- Otherwise, the pod selector only applies to the current namespace that the network policy lives in.

title: How to check ephemeral pods disk consumption

Access the compute node and change to the path of ephemeral volumes: ~~~ # cd /var/lib/origin/openshift.local.volumes/pods/ ~~~ 3. Sort the directories by occupation storage: ~~~ # du-sh | sort-h.. 188M 6ab87796-ef75-11e9-83b4-005056b98f29 261M 612a3df5-ef50-11e9-83b4-005056b98f29 369M 180e3722-eec3-11e9-83b4-005056b98f29... ~~~ 4. List all `pods` running in this compute node: ~~~ # for i in `docker ps-q` do echo === $i === docker inspect $i | grep-Ei "kubernetes.pod.uid|kubernetes.pod.name|kubernetes.pod.namespace" done ~~~ 5. Match the `UUID` with the `pod` and namespace information

title: Can't access Kibana web interface after upgrading to OpenShift 3.11
issue: - Cannot login to Kibana after upgrading to OpenShift 3.11- Cannot login to Cluster console- Logs from `kibana-proxy` container shows: ~~~~ # oc logs kibana-xxx-c kibana-proxy 2019/01/8 21:30:11 auth: unable to verify auth code with issuer: Post https://openshift.example.com:8443/oauth/token: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority 2019/01/8 21:30:12 server: authentication failed: unauthenticated ~~~~- Logs from `master-api` shows: ~~~ Encountered config error json: unknown field "masterCount" in object *config.MasterConfig, raw JSON: http: TLS handshake error from 10.10.0.51:35612: EOF http: TLS handshake error from 10.10.0.52:32848: EOF http: TLS handshake error from 10.10.0.50:45654: EOF v1beta1.servicecatalog.k8s.io failed with: Get https://172.128.0.0:443: dial tcp 172.128.0.0:443: connect: no route to host v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io failed with: Operation cannot be fulfilled on apiservices.apiregistration.k8s.io "v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again ~~~
resolution: If a custom Master API certificate was configured, then also set `openshift_additional_ca` Ansible variable[^1]. Configure the variable's value to point to the certificate used for the Master API. After configuring the `openshift_additional_ca`, run the `openshift-master/redeploy-openshift-ca.yml` playbook [^2]. You will need to redeploy the affected pods (`oc delete pod` and they will redeploy automatically). For additional details, refer to documentation on [Configurating cluster variables](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install/configuring_inventory_file.html#configuring-cluster-variables) and [Redeploying certificates](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/redeploying_certificates.html#redeploying-new-custom-ca). As the playbook also redeploys new or custom CA, it is recommended to run the [redeploy-certificates](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/redeploying_certificates.html#redeploying-all-certificates-current-ca) playbook. You can configure to redeploy only master certificates with [playbooks/openshift-master/redeploy-certificates.yml](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/redeploying_certificates.html#redeploying-master-certificates). Check the redeployed ca on the masters: ~~~ # openssl x509-noout-text-in /etc/origin/master/ca.crt ~~~
root_cause: In OpenShift 3.11, a new sidecar container (`oauth-proxy`) was introduced to Kibana that handles OAuth authentication with the Master API. If this container is not configured to trust the Master API's certificate it will not complete the OAuth process. The best way to configure this is through `openshift_additional_ca` and redeploy certificates as mentioned in resolution section.

title: Send messages through RHMI, some components receive: "no credit available"
issue: - When trying to send messages through RHMI, component receives `no credit available`.- The same happens even for `persisted messages`- This also happens for `non-persisted messages` even when consumers are available.- A `restart` of components on our side did not resolve the issue.
resolution: - At the time of the creation of this article, a `bug` in the `interconnect component` renders the router/interconnect `mesh-network` incompletely formed resulting in the discrepancy.- Open a ticket for [OpenShift Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new) so that it is picked up by the correct experts.
root_cause: - The bug states that in scenarios where there are a sufficient number of addresses in use that an inter-router `mobile address update (MAU message)` requires multiple transfer frames to deliver, it is possible for the inter-router control link to become blocked such that it will not recover.- When this happens, the neighbor relationship between the connected routers is lost due to the non-flow of `HELLO` messages.- Is the issue expected to happen for even `persisted messages`, which should be stored in case of no consumer connected? ~~~ This is the expected behavior. ~~~

title: Backup and restore fluentd buffers
issue: - Need to restore buffers saved from fluentd from `/var/log/`
resolution: - Note: this is not yet tested. Do not publish this solution. 1. Choose a node 1. Mark the node unschedulable # oc adm cordon NODENAME 1. Drain the node # oc adm drain NODENAME NOTE: This should NOT get rid of the fluentd pod, since fluentd runs as a daemonset 1. Wait for the fluentd on that node to clear out any and all buffers on the node 1. Restore the "saved" buffers to /var/log/ (or wherever you recovered them from, in case it's not there). It shouldnt matter if it was on the same host that you backed up from, so far as I can tell. 1. If/when the fluentd pod picks up these buffers, it should start sending them, and eventually clear them out. In that case, you could then: 1. Uncordon the node # oc adm uncordon NODENAME

title: How to shutdown a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform worker node
issue: Can I turn off my OCP application nodes on weekends?
resolution: **1- Shutdown procedure** 1.1- Take a [backup](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.9/day_two_guide/environment_backup.html) of application nodes 1.2- [Idling Applications](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.9/admin_guide/idling_applications.html#idling-applications-idling-applications) ~~~ $ oc idle ~~~ It is possible to idle multiple services at once with **[--resource-names-file](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.9/admin_guide/idling_applications.html#idling-applications-idling-multiple-services)** option. *The idle command is limited to a single project. For idling applications across a cluster, run the idle command for each project individually.* 1.3- Marking nodes as schedulable=false to avoid messages like node NotReady ~~~ $ oc adm manage-node node1.example.com--schedulable=false ~~~ 1.4 Shutdown the node **2- Start-up procedure** 2.1- Start machine 1.3- Marking nodes as schedulable=false to avoid messages like node NotReady ~~~ $ oc adm manage-node node1.example.com--schedulable=true ~~~ 2.2- Hit the app URL to start the pods or scale the pods manually from the desired project ~~~ $ curl ruby-ex-project1.apps.example.com ~~~ or ~~~ $ oc scale dc--replicas=N ~~~ *N = number of desired replicas.* **Don't forget [backup](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.9/day_two_guide/environment_backup.html).**
root_cause: I often get asked if it's possible to disconnect nodes from the development environment during the weekends to save money.

title: How to copy images from mirror-registry to registry into restricted environment in OCP 4.2
issue: - Uploading OCP 4.2 installation images from local filesystem to registry into restricted network- Bringing OCP 4.2 images from mirror registry to restricted environment
resolution: - There are two ways to bring all the images from mirror registry to restricted network environment **Method 1: Bringing all the images at once** ~~~ 1. Launch mirror-registry in an environment which can access internet # podman run-d--name mirror-registry-p:5000...-v /opt/registry/data:/var/lib/registry:z... docker.io/library/registry:2 2. Mirror OCP4.2 repository to the mirror-registry # oc adm-a ${LOCAL_SECRET_JSON} release mirror \... 3. Backup data directory of the mirror-registry by tar ball # cd /opt/registry # tar cvf- data | gzip-c > data.tar.gz 4. Copy the tar ball to your restricted network environment 5. Restore the backup file in the restricted network environment, and then launch a new mirror-registry there # mkdir-p /opt/registry # cd /opt/registry # tar xf data.tar.gz # podman run-d--name mirror-registry-p:5000...-v /opt/registry/data:/var/lib/registry:z... docker.io/library/registry:2 ~~~ **Method 2: Bringing all the images one by one** ~~~ 1. Launch mirror-registry in your restricted network environment 2. In an environment which can access internet, pull an image to local directory # skopeo copy docker://quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.2.1 dir:/tmp/imagedir--authfile quay.json 3. Backup the directory as tar ball, and then send it to your restricted network environment. # cd /tmp # tar cvf- imagedir | gzip-c > imagedir.tar.gz 4. Extract the tar ball, and copy it to your mirror-registry running on your restricted network environment. # cd /tmp # tar xvf imagedir.tar.gz # skopeo copy dir:/tmp/imagedir docker://: /openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.2.1--authfile local.json ~~~

title: wrong/bad image due to current search order in docker config/registries.conf
issue: - A wrong and eventually bad image can get loaded as- Images can get specified by a shortened path like `repo/image:tag`,- while multiple registries can be enabled in `registries.conf`.- This can hit any image, while it is a special security risk for OCP core/platform images.- Example- `rhgs3/rhgs-volmanager-rhel7:3.11.3-4` also exists on `docker.io`. Luckily this image is from no real harm and will log "Relax, you have only been h0nX0r3d, not hacked."
resolution: - avoid using shortened path image specification, like `repo/image:tag` in a first.- check and if needed adjust the sequence of registries in the configuration by level of trust.- to ensure that the OCP core/platform images get loaded from the Red Hat registry it is recommended to have the Red Hat registries first, like ~~~ registries = ['registry.redhat.io', 'quay.io',] ~~~- **Note**: this order can be in conflict with the solution for "[ImagePullBackOff when pulling image from docker.io private registry.](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3568231)".
root_cause: - if using a shortened path like `repo/image:tag` the image can get pulled from any of the enabled registries where the search for `repo/image:tag` give a result.- So the search order becomes from importance as the image will get loaded from first instead of the maybe desired registry later in the search order.

title: The Jenkins kubernetes plugin "dynamic pvc workspace volume" fails to create PersistentVolumeClaim on OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - We are using an external Jenkins instance with the kubernetes plugin version 1.19.2 installed.- When we try to use the "dynamic pvc workspace volume" feature, it fails to create a `PersistentVolumeClaim` with the following error: Failure executing: POST at: https://example.com/api/v1/namespaces/its-jenkins-prod/persistentvolumeclaims. Message: persistentvolumeclaims "pvc-jenkins-slave-foo-bar-rn7nb" is forbidden: cannot set blockOwnerDeletion if an ownerReference refers to a resource you can't set finalizers on: no RBAC policy matched,. Received status: Status(apiVersion=v1, code=403, details=StatusDetails(causes=[], group=null, kind=persistentvolumeclaims, name=pvc-jenkins-slave-foo-bar-rn7nb, retryAfterSeconds=null, uid=null, additionalProperties={}), kind=Status, message=persistentvolumeclaims "pvc-jenkins-slave-foo-bar-rn7nb" is forbidden: cannot set blockOwnerDeletion if an ownerReference refers to a resource you can't set finalizers on: no RBAC policy matched,, metadata=ListMeta(_continue=null, remainingItemCount=null, resourceVersion=null, selfLink=null, additionalProperties={}), reason=Forbidden, status=Failure, additionalProperties={}).
resolution: - Please create a new `ClusterRole` that enables the `ServiceAccount` to update pod finalizers. apiVersion: authorization.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: rules:- apiGroups:- "" attributeRestrictions: null resources:- pods/finalizers verbs:- update- Then assign the `ClusterRole` to the `ServiceAccount` used by the Jenkins instance. $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user system:serviceaccount::
root_cause: - OCP comes with a Jenkins version that leverages the kubernetes plugin in version 1.18.2. The "dynamic pvc workspace volume" feature is not available in this version.- Hence the Jenkins `ServiceAccount` shipped with OCP does not have the required persmissions.

title: OpenShift S2I Build Fails with "Peer's certificate issuer has been marked as not trusted by the user"
issue: - Cannot pull source from external Git repository ~~~ error: build error: fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/openshift/ruby-ex.git/': Peer's certificate issuer has been marked as not trusted by the user. ~~~- Our OpenShift install is behind a proxy which re-issues a new cert for external sites.- The S2I build image does not have the proxy CA in place, does not trust the CA, can't download source code from github.com or internal gitlab repo- Cloning or pulling source from a custom git repository and getting issuer is not recognized messages ~~~ Cloning "https://example.com/test/project.git "... error: fatal: unable to access 'https://example.com/test/project.git/': Peer's Certificate issuer is not recognized. ~~~
resolution: **This is a common situation with environments using proxies or firewalls.**- Create a [secret](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/dev_guide/builds/build_inputs.html#source-secrets-trusted-certificate-authorities) containing the CA.- Make sure of using the file name `ca.crt`, using a different name may cause the secret to not be recognizable.- [Attach](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/dev_guide/builds/build_inputs.html#source-clone-secrets) the secret to the builder service account in the project.- Attach it as a source pull secret: ~~~ $ oc set build-secret--source BUILDCONFIG SECRET ~~~- If it is necessary to have this secret in every project, there is a [separate solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2958391) for auto-attaching secrets/service accounts to projects. **If proxy or firewall is not configured in environment and still facing this issue then modify `resolv.conf` file of all VM's present in OCP environment.**- Content of `/etc/resolv.conf` before doing the modification. ~~~ # Generated by NetworkManager search cluster.local lab.example.com nameserver 10.0.0.1 ~~~- Content of `/etc/resolv.conf` after modification ~~~ # Generated by NetworkManager search cluster.local example.com nameserver 10.0.0.1 ~~~- Re deploy the application

title: Wrong port on node .kubeconfig and master-config.yaml after redeploying certificates
issue: After redeploying certificates with Ansible playbook it fails during task: *Wait for master API to come back online*.
resolution: New certificates are written to `*.kubeconfig` files in folders at `/etc/origin` and these files are created from scratch with values from ansible inventory file. All parameters in these `.kubeconfig` files are created with current values of variables or their default values.- So if you change for example variables for master API port: `openshift_master_api_port` and `openshift_master_console_port` then these variables are used inside the `.kubeconfig` files.- If you were using non-default values for installation of the cluster and then these variables are commented, then these variables are initialized to their default value and these default values are used in the `.kubeconfig` and `master-config.yaml` files.
root_cause: The master API port is changed after redeploying certificates in all `*.kubeconfig` files.

title: Unable to allocate new volumes
issue: Users are not able to allocate storage volumes to their pods.
resolution: Check settings of `timedatectl` on all nodes from a workstation that you are using to install the cluster. This issue was caused by independent Gluster storage – glusterfs nodes so the example here is bind to these nodes, but it applies to all nodes of OCP cluster. ~~~ $ ansible glusterfs-m command-a "timedatectl" $ ansible all-m command-a "timedatectl" ~~~ In the output you should see that `NTP enabled: yes`. If it is not enabled use `timedatectl set-ntp true` with ansible to correct it on all your nodes. ~~~ $ ansible glusterfs-m command-a "timedatectl set-ntp true" $ ansible all-m command-a "timedatectl set-ntp true" ~~~ If you can see in the output: `NTP synchronized: no` then please follow KCS: [timedatectl does not correctly show the actual status of NTP as synchronized](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3759171). To enable NTP on masters to ensure proper failover use the `openshift_clock_enabled=true` variable for the Ansible inventory file. ## Reference- [Day Two Operations Guide https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/day_two_guide/index.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/day_two_guide/index.html)- [NTP Synchronization https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/day_two_guide/run_once_tasks.html#day-two-guide-ntp-synchronization](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/day_two_guide/run_once_tasks.html#day-two-guide-ntp-synchronization)
root_cause: Even the fact that the time difference is a few seconds, it could impact the files leading to split-brains. So it is important to have a minimum difference in time with nodes. Especially for the gluster nodes. Virtual machines have no physical clock and can be paused at any time and started back up hours later.

title: Unable to deploy openshift-infra metrics with glusterfs-block
issue: Unable to deploy openshift-infra metrics with independent Gluster Cluster. Pods in openshift-infra are restarted all the time after deploying openshift-infra with persistent storage on glusterfs-block. The job that is creating an initial database in Casandra is failing for timeout (hawkular-metrics-schema). `WARN 2019-09-19 09:31:38,146 [main] org.hawkular.metrics.schema.Installer:run:102- Installation failed com.datastax.driver.core.exceptions.OperationTimedOutException: [hawkular-cassandra/172.30.72.229:9042] Timed out waiting for server response`
resolution: - First remove the current instance of openshift-infra with Ansible playbook: ~~~ cd /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible ansible-playbook./playbooks/openshift-metrics/config.yml-e "openshift_metrics_install_metrics=false" ~~~- To provide a longer timeout for an initial job while deploying initial database structure in Casandra it is important to change the role that is used for deploying openshift-infra namespaces. Edit the `/usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible/roles/openshift_metrics/templates/hawkular_metrics_schema_job.j2` and add the lines with definition of additional environment variables for the container. The additional variables are `CASSANDRA_CONNECTION_MAX_DELAY`, `CASSANDRA_CONNECTION_MAX_RETRIES`, `VERSION_UPDATE_DELAY`, `VERSION_UPDATE_MAX_RETRIES`. Their default value is defined in Tech Details for [Hawkular Metrics Schema Installer](https://access.redhat.com/containers/?tab=tech-details#/registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ose-metrics-schema-installer). If these variables are not defined, they are using these default variables. ~~~ apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: Job metadata: name: hawkular-metrics-schema labels: metrics-infra: hawkular-metrics name: hawkular-metrics-schema spec: template: spec: version: v1 metadata: labels: metrics-infra: hawkular-metrics #name: hawkular-metrics containers:- name: hawkular-metrics-schema image: {{openshift_metrics_schema_installer_image}} imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent env:- name: TRUSTSTORE_AUTHORITIES value: "/hawkular-metrics-certs/tls.truststore.crt" ### This are the additional parameters added to extend timeout period..- name: CASSANDRA_CONNECTION_MAX_DELAY value: "80"- name: CASSANDRA_CONNECTION_MAX_RETRIES value: "5"- name: VERSION_UPDATE_DELAY value: "50"- name: VERSION_UPDATE_MAX_RETRIES value: "10" ### volumeMounts:- mountPath: /hawkular-metrics-certs name: hawkular-metrics-certs- mountPath: /hawkular-account name: hawkular-metrics-account volumes:- name: hawkular-metrics-certs secret: secretName: hawkular-metrics-certs- name: hawkular-metrics-account secret: secretName: hawkular-metrics-account restartPolicy: OnFailure ~~~- Adding these variables is just a workaround to be able to deploy the metrics. It is still important to investigate what is the root cause of failure during deployment. It can be for example slow DNS response or another issue.- Deploy again the openshift-metrics with the Ansible playbook ~~~ cd /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible ansible-playbook./playbooks/openshift-metrics/config.yml ~~~- Check the result. After successful deployment the pods should be created, initial job executed and pods should not be restarting. ~~~ ~ root(ocp:workspaces) $ oc get pods-n openshift-infra NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE hawkular-cassandra-1-f2k22 1/1 Running 1 21h hawkular-metrics-kn5bs 1/1 Running 2 21h hawkular-metrics-schema-2htds 0/1 Completed 4 21h heapster-svjwt 1/1 Running 2 21h ~~~ 5. After deploying openshift-metrics with this additional you should more investigate what was the root cause of timeout. It can be issue with DNS for example or some other problems in your cluster infrastructure. This solution is provided as a workaround and did not solve the root cause. It is important to find why metrics were not deployed correctly with default initial values.
root_cause: In this particular issue, the timeout was caused probably by the slow response of DNS. With enough timeout the deployment was successful as well as operation.

issue: During a build using `Dockerfile` with `multi-stage` the build fails with the following message: ~~~ Cloning " @scm address>: "... Commit: (Merge pull........ error: build error: no FROM statement found ~~~
resolution: Create a `Dockerfile` starting with a `FROM` instruction.: ~~~ FROM: AS builder ARG ARG_NAME_1 ARG ARG_NAME_N........ FROM: ARG ARG_NAME_1 ARG ARG_NAME_N COPY--from=builder...... ~~~ To define a value for `ARG` instructions and use it in any instruction after a `FROM` without declaring it statically inside `Dockerfile`, specify them in the `buildconfig`: ~~~... strategy: dockerStrategy: buildArgs:- name: ARG_NAME_1 value: ARG_VALUE_1- name: ARG_NAME_N value: ARG_VALUE_N... ~~~
root_cause: Openshift 3.10 and 3.11 comes with Docker 1.13 (which does not have `multi-stage` build implemented). Trying to start a build with an `ARG` instruction will fail because, until Docker version 1.17, a `Dockerfile` **must** start with a `FROM` instruction. OpenShift build runs in a build container with a specific builder image, therefore it is not using the underlying `Docker`. The build pod detects that the `Dockerfile` is a `multi-stage` one and the `Dockerfile` is built using https://github.com/openshift/imagebuilder/ instead of a traditional `docker build`. `Imagebuilder` supports multistage builds, unlike the version of Docker that OpenShift uses. Here is some references with more details about this OpenShift and Docker `multi-stage` build:- [Clarify why multi-stage build works](https://github.com/openshift/origin/issues/21627)- [Understand how ARG and FROM interact](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#understand-how-arg-and-from-interact)

title: How to move etcd data volume in Openshift?
issue: - Procedure required to move etcd data volume in Openshift 3.11
resolution: It should be noted, that there are two commands to perform the backup with etcdctl: `backup`[^1] and `snapshot`[^2]. The snapshot method is the recommended for this use case, because data will be moved and no new node has been created. Also, it's advisable to create an external NFS share, S3 bucket, or any external storage location, to save the snapshot. [^1]: While the etcdctl backup command is used to perform the backup, etcd v3 has no concept of a backup. Instead, either take a snapshot from a live member with the etcdctl snapshot save command or copy the member/snap/db file from an etcd data directory. [^2]: The etcdctl backup command rewrites some of the metadata contained in the backup, specifically, the node ID and cluster ID, which means that in the backup, the node loses its former identity. To recreate a cluster from the backup, create a new, single-node cluster, then add the rest of the nodes to the cluster. The metadata is rewritten to prevent the new node from joining an existing cluster. ##Prerequisites:- Create VG/LV in masters nodes. For example, from bastion host could be created with ansible ad-hoc commands. It should be noted that disks must be provided before. # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-a "vgcreate etcdVG /dev/vdc" # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-a "lvcreate-n etcd_lv-l 100%FREE etcdVG" # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-a "mkfs.fstype /dev/mapper/etcdVG-etcd_lv" # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-m mount-a "path=/var/lib/etcd src=/dev/mapper/etcdVG-etcd_lv fstype=fstype state=present"- Create the backup directory. It must be present in all masters, as a shared file system, or must be replicated in all masters servers. # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-m shell-a "mkdir-p /backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/{etcd-config-{{inventory_hostname}},snapshot}"- Create directory to temporarily move the etcd pod definition. # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-m file-a "path=/root/etcd_stop/ owner=root group=root mode=644 state=directory"- Install etcd package, it's needed to restore the snapshots. # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-m yum-a "name=etcd state=present"- Copy etcd configuration of each etcd host. # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-m shell-a "cp-a /etc/etcd/ /backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/etcd-config-{{inventory_hostname}}/" ## Snapshot creation.- **To take the snapshot, It must be performed only in one master node**. For more information, please take a look at [Day Two Operations Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/3.11/html/day_two_operations_guide/day_two_environment_backup#backing-up-etcd_environment-backup).- Obtain the etcd endpoint IP address from the static pod manifest. $ export ETCD_POD_MANIFEST="/etc/origin/node/pods/etcd.yaml" $ export ETCD_EP=$(grep https ${ETCD_POD_MANIFEST} | cut-d '/'-f3)- Obtain the etcd pod name. $ oc login-u system:admin $ export ETCD_POD=$(oc get pods-n kube-system | grep-o-m 1 '\S*etcd\S*')- Take a snapshot of the etcd data in the pod and store it locally. $ oc project kube-system $ echo ${ETCD_POD} $ oc exec ${ETCD_POD}-c etcd-- /bin/bash-c "ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl \--cert /etc/etcd/peer.crt \--key /etc/etcd/peer.key \--cacert /etc/etcd/ca.crt \--endpoints $ETCD_EP \ snapshot save /var/lib/etcd/snapshot.db"- Copy the snapshot into a share location. # cp /var/lib/etcd/snapshot.db /backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/snapshot/$(date +%Y%m%d)_snapshot.db- Or copy in each master. # scp /var/lib/etcd/snapshot.db master2.lab.example.com:/backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/snapshot/$(date +%Y%m%d)_snapshot.db # scp /var/lib/etcd/snapshot.db master3.lab.example.com:/backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/snapshot/$(date +%Y%m%d)_snapshot.db ##Stop etcd and restore it from snapshot. **It should be noted that these steps must be performed on all master nodes, one at a time**.- Stop the Etcd pod. # mv /etc/origin/node/pods/etcd.yaml /root/etcd_stop/etcd.yaml- Remove /var/lib/etcd. # rm-rf /var/lib/etcd/*- Mount the new file system (VG/LV) into "/var/lib/etcd". # mount /dev/mapper/etcdVG-etcd_lv /var/lib/etcd- Restore file from snapshot. # source /etc/etcd/etcd.conf # export ETCDCTL_API=3 # ETCD_DATA_DIR=/backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/restore # etcdctl snapshot restore /backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/snapshot/$(date +%Y%m%d)_snapshot.db \--data-dir $ETCD_DATA_DIR \--name $ETCD_NAME \--initial-cluster "$ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER" \--initial-cluster-token "$ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_TOKEN" \--initial-advertise-peer-urls $ETCD_INITIAL_ADVERTISE_PEER_URLS \--skip-hash-check=true- Move files from restore dir. # cp-a /backup/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)/restore/* /var/lib/etcd/.- Restore SElinux. # restorecon-Rv /var/lib/etcd- Move back all etcd pod definition. Pods will be recreated. # ansible-i inventory.yml masters-a "mv /root/etcd_stop/etcd.yaml /etc/origin/node/pods/etcd.yaml" ## etcd checks.- Connect to a master node as root, and run. To get more information go to the article [etcd Troubleshooting](https://access.redhat.com/articles/3093761#etcd3) # source /etc/etcd/etcd.conf # export ETCDCTL_API=3 # ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS=`etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS--write-out=fields member list | awk '/ClientURL/{printf "%s%s",sep,$3; sep=","}'` # etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS--write-out=table member list # etcdctl3--endpoints=$ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS endpoint status--write-out=table # etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS endpoint health # etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS check perf
root_cause: etcd will improve its deployment performance and stability under fast disks. Usually this is not created by default.

title: How to access master and worker nodes in OpenShift 4
issue: - How to access master or worker nodes in OpenShift 4.2?- Can `SSH` be used to access master and worker nodes in OpenShift 4.2?
resolution: - You can access master and worker nodes in OpenShift 4.2 using `SSH`. The `SSH private key` that has been generated during the installation of OpenShift 4.x cluster will be used.- Please refer to the following documents for more information about generating and using `SSH key pair` while installing OpenShift 4.2: 1. [Installing OpenShift 4.2 cluster on bare metal](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.2/installing/installing_bare_metal/installing-bare-metal.html#ssh-agent-using_installing-bare-metal) 2. [Installing OpenShift 4.2 cluster on vSphere](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.2/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere.html#ssh-agent-using_installing-vsphere) 3. [Installing OpenShift 4.2 cluster quickly on AWS](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.2/installing/installing_aws/installing-aws-customizations.html#ssh-agent-using_installing-aws-customizations)- Use the `SSH private key` to access `core` user on master and worker node: # ssh-i /path/to/privatekey core@master-hostname # ssh-i /path/to/privatekey core@worker-hostname- To update SSH keys used in RHCOS hosts please refer to this solution [4510281](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4510281)

title: Clair: Force Alpine CVE data refresh
issue: Alpine CVE data incorrect or appears stall in Clair db or on Red Hat Quay.
resolution: https://github.com/quay/clair/blob/master/ext/vulnsrc/alpine/alpine.go#L77 You force the alpine updater to reindex and redownload the database by updating the keyvalue table with a previous commit. This should do it: ~~~ # UPDATE keyvalue SET value = 'a72a03d255e7572cbc4215c1a6c9b6c5917ad45f' WHERE id = 3; ~~~ Then delete the Clair pod and let it restart. Clair will on next update see that the commits do not match and will redownload the database and update it again.
root_cause: The keyvalue corresponds to the Alpine's secdb commit hash, the last commit was made on November 13th, or 21 days ago. Because the last commit on Github is the same as the one stored in the keyvalue table, update is not done, it is skipped.

title: All pod deployments are failing showing error message "invalid label value: "{{ .Release.Name }}""
issue: - New application deployments or scaling out fail with the following error message: invalid label value: "{{.Release.Name}}": a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue', or 'my_value', or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?')
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and currently working on a solution for it on [Bug 1760807](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1760807).- If you are facing the same issue, please open a support case.- As a workaround: 1- Edit the deployment configuration showing this error and remove the wrong value: # oc edit dc spec: affinity: podAntiAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:- podAffinityTerm: labelSelector: matchExpressions:- key: app.kubernetes.io/instance operator: In values:- '{{.Release.Name}}' <---------------- remove the faulty value topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname weight: 100 2- Rollout a new deployment: # oc rollout latest dc/
root_cause: - One of the application Deployment configurations is using wrong parameter value: # oc edit dc spec: affinity: podAntiAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:- podAffinityTerm: labelSelector: matchExpressions:- key: app.kubernetes.io/instance operator: In values:- '{{.Release.Name}}' <---------------- faulty value topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname weight: 100

title: missing log entries (kibana) from some pod's in several namespaces
issue: - There are missing log entries on Kibana from some pods in several namespaces- On these projects all pods have log outputs but only a part of the pods can be queried via kibana- Logs from some pods can not be found- Kibana shows only the last 5k lines from all logs
resolution: - There is a workaround for this issue- change the log rotation size on the docker configuration:- Modify docker logs size rotation. Modify the file /etc/sysconfig/docker and add to the line OPTIONS `--log-opt max-size=20m` and `--log-opt max-file=10`. You can put a bigger size if you are plenty of disk space. After this, reboot docker service, node by node- Check if fluentd is getting kill- [KCS 3303861](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3303861)- Restart fluentd pods- Check if "ls-l /var/log/*pos" are getting updated and customer is able to see the logs in kibana- Currently there is no fix for this issue- but it is getting tracked by this two Bugzillas:- [OpenShift 4.x- 1741663](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1741663)- [OpenShift 3.x-1765646](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1765646)
root_cause: - It is a problem with the docker rotation from logs based on their size

title: Build operation with Satellite subscriptions failed on RHOCP4.2
issue: The build operation using the satellite subscription based on the Docs[1] failed. Here's the test steps: + Prepare the repository file based on the Docs[1] ~~~ > You must provide or create a yum-compatible repository configuration file, > that downloads content from your Satellite instance. ~~~ Unfortunately, it does not show the example about the repository file. Usually, the repository file has the following entries: ~~~ [test-XXX] name=test-XXX baseurl = https://satellite.../content/dist/rhel/server/7/7Server/x86_64/os enabled=1 gpgcheck=0 sslverify=1 sslcacert = /etc/rhsm/ca/....-ca.pem sslclientkey = /etc/pki/entitlement/...-key.pem sslclientcert = /etc/pki/entitlement/....pem ~~~ + Prepare the following Dockerfile and some other files based on the Doc: ~~~ # cat Dockerfile FROM registry.redhat.io/rhel7:latest USER root COPY./etc-pki-entitlement /etc/pki/entitlement COPY./yum.repos.d /etc/yum.repos.d RUN rm /etc/rhsm-host && \ yum-y update && \ yum-y instalimal && \ rm-rf /etc/pki/entitlement USER 1001 ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash"] # ~~~ + Building the image will fail as follows: ~~~ # oc start-build rhel7-yum--from-dir... STEP 4: COPY./yum.repos.d /etc/yum.repos.d XXXXXXXXXX STEP 5: RUN rm /etc/rhsm-host && yum-y update && yum-y install tcpdump && rm-rf /etc/pki/entitlement Loaded plugins: ovl, product-id, search-disabled-repos, subscription-manager Error loading certificate: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/etc/pki/consumer/cert.pem' Trying other mirror. It was impossible to connect to the Red Hat servers. This could mean a connectivity issue in your environment, such as the requirement to configure a proxy, or a transparent proxy that tampers with TLS security, or an incorrect system clock. Please collect information about the specific failure that occurs in your environment, using the instructions in: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1527033 and open a ticket with Red Hat Support... ~~~ [1] https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.2/html/builds/using-red-hat-subscriptions-in-builds#running-builds-with-satellite-subscriptions
resolution: The workaround is to modify the following two entries in the repo file.- change "sslverify" value from 1 to 0- remove "sslcacert" entry Here's the modified repo file: ~~~ [test-XXX] name=test-XXX baseurl = https://satellite.../content/dist/rhel/server/7/7Server/x86_64/os enabled=1 gpgcheck=0 sslverify=0 sslclientkey = /etc/pki/entitlement/...-key.pem sslclientcert = /etc/pki/entitlement/....pem ~~~ Note: With this repository file, yum command will still output the following error. But, you can just ignore it. The build operation will work well in spite of this error message. ~~~ Error loading certificate: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/etc/pki/consumer/cert.pem' ~~~
root_cause: The Docs[1] has not enough information about the repository file.

title: openshift-samples operator does not recognize updated pull secret
issue: After updating the [global cluster pull secret](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.2/openshift_images/managing-images/using-image-pull-secrets.html#images-update-global-pull-secret_using-image-pull-secrets), the `ImageStreams` managed by the `samples` operator still use previous pull secret.
resolution: Delete all `ImageStreams` that are managed by the operator. The `ImageStreams` will be automatically recreated by the operator. `oc delete imagestream-l samples.operator.openshift.io/managed=true-n openshift` Once recreated, the updated credentials will be used.
root_cause: The `ImageStream`s continue to use stale credentials.

title: How to estimate the right size to support hive metastore for production load in OpenShift Container Platform 4 - Metering
issue: We are planning to use OpenShift Metering, and we would like to understand how to estimate the size of hive metastore to support a production workload.
resolution: There have not been any specific scale been done which makes it difficult to recommend any specific sizing for hive metastore. Up to know, 100 GB seems feasible and has shown to cope with production grade testing running for a while. But as scale testing is still in progress it will take more time until accurate information in this area become available.

title: Configuring DNS servers in  ignition files
issue: When configuring node network connections via direct ignition file modification, the nameserver is not applied to the node after ignition.
resolution: Configuring static network via ignition is not a documented process. [dracut](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/dracut.cmdline.7.html) is to be used to configure static network in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.2 and later. ~~~ coreos.inst=yes coreos.inst.install_dev=sda coreos.inst.image_url=http://test-miscweb001.vegas.com/ose/rhcos-4.2.0-x86_64-metal-bios.raw.gz coreos.inst.ignition_url=http://test-miscweb001.vegas.com/ose/nonprod2-ose42/vvnoshnd23.ign ip=172.25.40.137::172.25.40.1:255.255.255.0:::none:10.25.16.46 nameserver=10.25.16.46,10.25.16.48 ~~~__Note:__ Direct modification of ignition files is not a documented process. As such, updates to the platform may break modifications placed in the ignition file without warning. Additionally:- Modifications made via ignition may make the cluster unsupportable- Modifications made via ignition may prevent future updates from succeeding

title: How to disable sticky session for a specific route in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: How to disable sticky session for a specific route in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform.
We need to disable sticky session for a particular route in OpenShift but are unable to-do it.
resolution: - This feature request is tracked via [RHBZ #1278851](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1278851). This feature is included in OpenShift v3.5[Sticky Sessions](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.5/architecture/core_concepts/routes.html#routes-sticky-sessions).- Cluster administrators can turn off stickiness for passthrough routes separately from other connections, or turn off stickiness entirely.- By default, sticky sessions for passthrough routes are implemented using the source [load balancing strategy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.5/architecture/core_concepts/routes.html#load-balancing). The default can be changed for all passthrough routes by using the ROUTER_TCP_BALANCE_SCHEME [environment variables](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.5/architecture/core_concepts/routes.html#env-variables), and for individual routes by using the haproxy.router.openshift.io/balance [route specific annotation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.5/architecture/core_concepts/routes.html#route-specific-annotations).

title: Using docker overlay2 driver with quotas
issue: Can I please have a procedure on how to use the overlay2 driver for Docker, on Openshift 3.9, and enable qutoas on containers.
I need to set the quotas so that a single container cannot consume all the storage.
resolution: 1) Edit /`etc/sysconfig/docker-storage-setup` and add the following option: ~~~ EXTRA_STORAGE_OPTIONS="--storage-opt overlay2.size= " ~~~ where * * is the quota limit to enforce. As an example, for a quote of `5 GB` use: ~~~ EXTRA_STORAGE_OPTIONS="--storage-opt overlay2.size=5G" ~~~ 2) Restart the docker service: ~~~ systemctl restart docker ~~~

title: How to create a Openshift build from a local source code?
issue: - How to create a `build` from a local jar file?- How to create a `build` from a local directory?- How to create a `build` from a local git repository?
resolution: A `build` in OpenShift Container Platform is the process of transforming input parameters into a resulting object. Most often, builds are used to transform source code into a runnable container image. Below the steps to create a build from a source directory: As a prerequisite, you must be logged in the Openshift cluster as well as created a project. 1. Check if the `image-streams`is already imported in your repository: ~~~~ $oc get is NAME DOCKER REPO TAGS UPDATED apicurito-ui docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/apicurito-ui 1.4,1.2,1.3 camel-ose-springboot-xml docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/camel-ose-springboot-xml fis-java-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fis-java-openshift latest,1.0,2.0 fis-karaf-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fis-karaf-openshift 2.0,1.0 fuse docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse latest 40 seconds ago fuse-apicurito-generator docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse-apicurito-generator 1.2,1.3,1.4 fuse-java-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse-java-openshift latest 32 minutes ago fuse7-console docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse7-console 1.3,1.4,1.0 + 2 more... fuse7-eap-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse7-eap-openshift 1.2,1.3,1.4 + 2 more... fuse7-java-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse7-java-openshift 1.5,1.0,1.1 + 3 more... fuse7-karaf-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse7-karaf-openshift 1.0,1.1,1.2 + 2 more... jboss-fuse70-console docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/jboss-fuse70-console 1.0 jboss-fuse70-eap-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/jboss-fuse70-eap-openshift 1.0 jboss-fuse70-java-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/jboss-fuse70-java-openshift 1.0 jboss-fuse70-karaf-openshift docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/jboss-fuse70-karaf-openshift 1.0 ~~~~ 2. Create a new build specifying the `image-stream` that best suits to the application project, in this example the `fis-java-openshift`: ~~~~ $oc new-build--binary=true--image-stream=fis-java-openshift:2.0--name=fuse ~~~~ 3. Check the outputs in the terminal: ~~~~--> Found image c990278 (12 days old) in image stream "openshift/fis-java-openshift" under tag "2.0" for "fis-java-openshift:2.0" Fuse Integration Services- Java-------------------------------- Platform for building and running plain Java applications (fat-jar and flat classpath) Tags: builder, java * A source build using binary input will be created * The resulting image will be pushed to image stream tag "fuse:latest" * A binary build was created, use 'start-build--from-dir' to trigger a new build--> Creating resources with label build=fuse... buildconfig.build.openshift.io "fuse" created--> Success ~~~~ 4. Start the build where the `--from-dir` parameter must be pointing to the application project folder. Rather than relying on a project directory, it is possible to create a build from a file`--from-file= ` or from a Git or SVN working directory,`--from-repo= `. ~~~~ $oc start-build fuse--from-dir=/home/fuse-user/fuse-rest--follow ~~~~ 5. The previous command will start the build as well as downloading the maven dependencies and pushing the image. ~~~~ [INFO]------------------------------------------------------------------------ [INFO] BUILD SUCCESS [INFO]------------------------------------------------------------------------ [INFO] Total time: 01:21 min [INFO] Finished at: 2019-12-23T19:00:31Z [INFO] Final Memory: 45M/110M [INFO]------------------------------------------------------------------------ Copying Maven artifacts from /tmp/src/target to /deployments... Running: cp *.jar /deployments... done Pushing image docker-registry.default.svc:5000/fuse/fuse:latest... Pushed 5/6 layers, 84% complete Pushed 6/6 layers, 100% complete Push successful ~~~~ 6. Afterward, create a `new-app` from the previous build: ~~~ $oc new-app fuse ~~~ 7. A `DeploymentConfig` will be created and also a `Service` exposing the application internally as the output below shows: ~~~--> Found image b462947 (4 minutes old) in image stream "fuse/fuse" under tag "latest" for "fuse" temp.builder.openshift.io/fuse/fuse-1:4aeea8e2---------------------------------------------- Platform for building and running plain Java applications (fat-jar and flat classpath) Tags: builder, java * This image will be deployed in deployment config "fuse" * Port 8778/tcp will be load balanced by service "fuse" * Other containers can access this service through the hostname "fuse"--> Creating resources... deploymentconfig.apps.openshift.io "fuse" created service "fuse" created--> Success Application is not exposed. You can expose services to the outside world by executing one or more of the commands below: 'oc expose svc/fuse' Run 'oc status' to view your app. ~~~

title: Enabling a static egress IP address for External Project Traffic fails with "Error assigning Egress IP" in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: When trying to enable a static IP address for External Project Traffic (egress), the IP address is not being assigned on the nodes primary network interface as a secondary IP address.
resolution: * Static IP addresses for External Project Traffic Egress IPs are implemented as additional IP addresses on the primary network interface, and must be in the same subnet as the node’s primary IP. * As per [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/3.11/html/cluster_administration/admin-guide-manage-networking#enabling-static-ips-for-external-project-traffic), please ensure that the chosen `egressIPs` are in the same subnet as the node’s primary IP and are not configured in any Linux network configuration files, such as `ifcfg-eth0`.
root_cause: * The selected egress IP must be on the local subnet of the node hosting the egress IP's primary interface.

title: Error getting broker catalog: Get https://asb.openshift-ansible-service-broker.svc:1338/osb/v2/catalog: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

title: Red Hat CodeReady Workspaces scalability workaround on OCP 4.1/AWS
issue: The following are the issues faced while doing a hands-on workshop of CodeReady Workspaces on OpenShift Client Platform (OCP) 4.1/Amazon Web Services (AWS):- Workspace creation on CodeReady Workspaces takes a long time (around 2-3 minutes per workspace).- Workspace creation progress is serial (not parallel due to the AWS specification). Creation of attendees' workspaces takes a long time.
resolution: ## Method 1: Change `pvcStrategy` To reduce the EBS provisioning process, change the `pvcStrategy` in the CoreReady Workspaces Custom Resource (CR). Pros:- With product support- No additional storage configuration required for the OCP infrastructure Cons:- EBS can mount on only one node, so all workspaces must deploy to a single node ### Default ~~~ storage: pvcStrategy: per-workspace pvcClaimSize: 1Gi preCreateSubPaths: true ~~~ ### Share single EBS volume for all users ~~~ storage: pvcStrategy: common pvcClaimSize: 100Gi preCreateSubPaths: true ~~~ ## Method 2: Use AWS EFS To avoid the EBS provisioning bottleneck, use AWS EFS via an external provisioner. Pros:- Creation of workspaces is quicker- Scaling of nodes is possible Cons:- Without product support ## Procedure 1. Use the `nfs-client` provisioner. See [nfs-client](https://github.com/kubernetes-incubator/external-storage/tree/master/nfs-client). 2. Create a namespace for the external provisioner: ~~~ $ oc new-project nfs-client-provisioner $ NAMESPACE=`oc project-q` ~~~ 3. Create Role-based access control (RBAC) by modifying the namespace: ~~~ $ cat deploy/rbac.yaml kind: ServiceAccount apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: nfs-client-provisioner kind: ClusterRole apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: nfs-client-provisioner-runner rules:- apiGroups: [""] resources: ["persistentvolumes"] verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "delete"]- apiGroups: [""] resources: ["persistentvolumeclaims"] verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "update"]- apiGroups: ["storage.k8s.io"] resources: ["storageclasses"] verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]- apiGroups: [""] resources: ["events"] verbs: ["create", "update", "patch"] kind: ClusterRoleBinding apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: run-nfs-client-provisioner subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: nfs-client-provisioner namespace: nfs-client-provisioner roleRef: kind: ClusterRole name: nfs-client-provisioner-runner apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Role apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: leader-locking-nfs-client-provisioner rules:- apiGroups: [""] resources: ["endpoints"] verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"] kind: RoleBinding apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: leader-locking-nfs-client-provisioner subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: nfs-client-provisioner # replace with namespace where provisioner is deployed namespace: nfs-client-provisioner roleRef: kind: Role name: leader-locking-nfs-client-provisioner apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io $ oc create-f deploy/rbac.yaml $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user hostmount-anyuid system:serviceaccount:$NAMESPACE:nfs-client-provisioner ~~~ 4. Create the Elastic File System (EFS) volume from the AWS Console. To confirm the NFS Server hostname and path from the mount options: ~~~ $ sudo mount-t nfs4-o nfsvers=4.1,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,timeo=600,retrans=2,noresvport fs-c1a1d7e0.efs.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com:/ efs Caution: Security Groups setting You have to open nfs port using Security Group, check if you face "Connection Timeout" https://dev.classmethod.jp/etc/20181209-efs/ ~~~ 5. Deploy the external provisioner. Modify the NFS server and path (`env` and `volume` sections) as per your environment. ~~~ $ cat deploy/deployment.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: nfs-client-provisioner kind: Deployment apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1 metadata: name: nfs-client-provisioner spec: replicas: 1 strategy: type: Recreate template: metadata: labels: app: nfs-client-provisioner spec: serviceAccountName: nfs-client-provisioner containers:- name: nfs-client-provisioner image: quay.io/external_storage/nfs-client-provisioner:latest volumeMounts:- name: nfs-client-root mountPath: /persistentvolumes env:- name: PROVISIONER_NAME value: fuseim.pri/ifs- name: NFS_SERVER value: fs-c1a1d7e0.efs.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com- name: NFS_PATH value: / volumes:- name: nfs-client-root nfs: server: fs-c1a1d7e0.efs.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com path: / $ oc create-f deploy/deployment.yaml ~~~ 6. Test the external provisioner. ~~~ $ oc create-f deploy/test-claim.yaml-f deploy/test-pod.yaml $ oc delete-f deploy/test-pod.yaml-f deploy/test-claim.yaml ~~~ 7. Change the CR for CodeReady Workspaces cluster creation. ### Default ~~~ storage: pvcStrategy: per-workspace pvcClaimSize: 1Gi preCreateSubPaths: true ~~~ ### Use EFS volume for workspaces ~~~ storage: pvcStrategy: common pvcClaimSize: 1Gi preCreateSubPaths: true workspacePVCStorageClassName: 'managed-nfs-storage' ~~~
root_cause: - Supported dynamic provisionable volume is only AWS EBS on OCP 4.1.- CodeReady Workspaces requires `storageclass` to do user workspace dynamic provisioning.- EBS provisioning takes 2-3 minutes per user workspace and is serialized.- The time taken to complete the setup is **(2-3 minutes) x (number of users)**.

title: OpenShift 'oc' unable to inspect or pull docker images from 'registry.redhat.io'
issue: When trying to run `oc cluster up` command, the output is one of the following error messages:- Error inspecting image from `registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-control-plane:v3.11`: ~~~ # oc cluster up Getting a Docker client... Checking if image registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-control-plane:v3.11 is available... error: unexpected error inspecting image registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-control-plane:v3.11 ~~~- Error pulling docker image from `registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-cli:v3.11`: ~~~ # oc cluster up Getting a Docker client... Checking if image registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-control-plane:v3.11 is available... Pulling image registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-control-plane:v3.11 Pulled 1/5 layers, 20% complete Pulled 1/5 layers, 34% complete Pulled 2/5 layers, 48% complete Pulled 2/5 layers, 54% complete Pulled 2/5 layers, 61% complete Pulled 3/5 layers, 74% complete Pulled 3/5 layers, 79% complete Pulled 3/5 layers, 85% complete Pulled 3/5 layers, 91% complete Pulled 4/5 layers, 94% complete Pulled 4/5 layers, 98% complete Pulled 5/5 layers, 100% complete Extracting Image pull complete Pulling image registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-cli:v3.11 error: error pulling Docker image registry.redhat.io/openshift3/ose-cli:v3.11 ~~~
resolution: The `oc`command uses `docker` command in order to inspect and pull images from the registry. Therefore, it is necessary to verify if docker daemon is enabled and running. To do so, follow these two steps: 1. Check if docker daemon is enabled and running: ~~~ # systemctl is-enabled docker # systemctl is-active docker ~~~ 2. If the docker daemon is not enabled and running, enable it and run it by doing the following: ~~~ # systemctl enable docker # systemctl start docker ~~~ After confirming the docker daemon is enabled and running, login in the `registry.redhat.io` with `docker login` command, as follows: # docker login registry.redhat.io Username: rhportaluser Password: Login Succeeded Finally, run `oc` again: # oc cluster up
root_cause: Since `oc` uses docker to inspect and pull images from the `registry.redhat.io`, the docker daemon needs to be enabled and running and it is necessary to login into the registry so it is possible to pull the images.

title: Error message "Server returned HTTP response code: 401 for URL: http://localhost:8180/services/rest/server/queries/definitions/processesMonitoring..." in the kie server log file after the smart router is restarted
issue: - After deploying a process-definition KJAR to the kiesevers, we get these "Server returned HTTP response code: 401" errors for the smart router;- The following error is repeatedly logged in the smart router console log after it has been started: ERROR: Error when forwarding request to server java.io.IOException: Server returned HTTP response code: 401 for URL: http://localhost:8180/services/rest/server/queries/definitions/processesMonitoring?... Caused by: java.io.IOException: Server returned HTTP response code: 401 for URL: http://pam-mde-kieserver-1-prod-scb-...
resolution: Set `KIE_SERVER_USER` (`org.kie.server.user`) and `KIE_SERVER_PWD` (`org.kie.server.pwd`) variables in the Business Central/Controller configuration file to the same values as the `KIE_SERVER_CONTROLLER_USER` (`org.kie.server.pwd`) and `KIE_SERVER_CONTROLLER_PWD` (`org.kie.server.pwd`).
root_cause: The error logged in the smart router console/server log file, seems to be related to Business central registering default queries to Kie server (through Smart router). For this action the credentials are taken from environment variables `KIE_SERVER_USER` and `KIE_SERVER_PWD` (defined in Business central DeploymentConfig). This user needs to have correct roles defined: `kie-server`.
