title: Add privileges to developers create metrics.k8.io api resources
issue: - How to add privileges to developers create `metrics.k8.io` api resources?
resolution: - Create a custom role, which should be created by the cluster admin: ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: custom-metrics-server-devs rules:- apiGroups:- custom.metrics.k8s.io- external.metrics.k8s.io- metrics.k8s.io resources: ["*"] verbs: ["*"] ~~~ **Please note that the api groups mentioned should be created already. The above example will enable users to access all resources in all namespaces with apigroups mentioned above. You can edit the resources and verbs section as per your convenience.**- Create the cluster role: ~~~ $ oc create-f.yaml ~~~- Add that clusterrole to the user(here developers): ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user custom-metrics-server-devs developer1 ~~~

title: Is it possible to upgrade specific OCP 4 nodes?
issue: - Is it possible to upgrade specific nodes during the cluster upgrade?
resolution: - You can set the `Paused` to `true` for e.g. the worker pool to accomplish that (this has effect on the whole pool, not single nodes) ~~~ # oc edit mcp worker (change the paused to true) ~~~- Also, the MCO has a `MaxUnavailable` field for the master and worker `MachineConfigPool` that you can set to 0 to effectively stop from updating or taking any configuration changes.

title: Monitor OSD clusters where ping is not available
issue: Ping / ICMP packets, to the a cluster, are not returning an ack. OSD Clusters drop most inbound connections, including ICMP ping request. This is to limit the network attack surface area but it also limits monitoring options. This network policy **can not*
be altered.
resolution: The only available inbound connections are to the application routers. All other connection attempts will be dropped. The application routers have the following characteristics:- The IP's for the routers are dynamic. Monitoring tools should use DNS resolution..- The available ports are: 443, 80 and 6443- The protocol is HTTP(S) over TCP/IP- To receive and OK (200) status, the request must be directed at an active OpenShift Route Since ping uses ICMP it will be dropped. Only HTTP(S) traffic is allowed. So the recommendation is to monitor the cluster by sending HTTP(s) requests to the clusters' application router(s). If HTTP(s) is not available on the monitoring tool, a number of other suggestions that rely only on TCP/IP are listed in the *Diagnostic Steps* section below. The application routers' domain name(s) can be found on the_Networking_ tab of the OCM details page, under the_Default application router_ and the_Additional application router_. **Navigation**: From the [OCM Search page](https://cloud.redhat.com/openshift)-> Search for the cluster Name/Id-> Click the cluster name-> Click the Networking tab If an `OK (200)` response is required, an active application route (Openshift: `oc get route object`) must be used in the HTTP requests. If an incorrect name is used:- a `Service Unavailable (503)` may be returned, which may be acceptable as it indicates the cluster is up and routable.- Or a `DNS error` error may be returned, if the router domain name was used. **For example:** If the application router is `https://apps.myCluster.c9f9.p1.openshiftapps.com`, then monitoring:- `https://apps.myCluster.c9f9.p1.openshiftapps.com`- Will return a_DNS_ error as the name is not resolvable.- `https://no-route.apps.myCluster.c9f9.p1.openshiftapps.com`- Will return a_Service Unavailable (503)_ error as the OpenShift route does not exist.- `https://my-route.apps.myCluster.c9f9.p1.openshiftapps.com`- Will return a_OK (200)_, if the OpenShift route exists. This can be confirmed with the OC command `oc get route-n myNamespace` in the application project/namespace. **VPN Notes**: Since a VPN connection is a private connection, ensure that any traffic, monitoring the VPN, traverses one of the application routers that is marked with *Make router private*. More details can be found by reading [??Title??URL??](https://ddd)

title: Set container log limits when Docker is filling up /var/lib/docker with large log files.
issue: - How do I set log limits for container logs.- Docker is configured to use a thin pool logical volume for storage but is still filling up `/var/lib/docker`.- Running `docker info` shows plenty of data space available but my root file system is filling up with most space taken up in `/var/lib/docker`.- With OpenShift 3 I am seeing that docker is filling up space on `/var/lib/docker`.
resolution: - Container logs by default are not configured to be rotated or limited to a max size by docker. A log file can grow so large that it fills up the disk space if the container runs for long enough and generate enough logs. See [Docker Logging Documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/admin/logging/overview/) for more information on what can be set.- To set log limits for containers on a host `--log-opt` can be configured with `max-size` and `max-file` so that a containers logs are rolled over when they reach a max limit and only a certain number of files are saved before being discarded. ~~~ # cat /etc/sysconfig/docker OPTIONS='--insecure-registry=172.30.0.0/16--signature-verification=false--selinux-enabled--log-opt max-size=50m--log-opt max-file=5' ~~~- Restart docker service for the changes to take effect. ~~~ # systemctl restart docker ~~~ If there is already a log file already present on the host that needs to be removed, run the following to clear its contents and reduce its size. ~~~ # cat /dev/null > /var/lib/docker/containers/CONTAINER_ID/CONTAINER_ID-json.log OR # cat /dev/null > $(docker inspect--format='{{.LogPath}}' CONTAINER_ID) ~~~ *This will remove all logs for the given container*

title: How to add custom policies with ConfigMaps in APIcast self-managed deployed with the Operator
issue: - When adding custom policies in APIcast according to the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.8/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_policies#adding_custom_policies_to_apicast_on_another_openshift_container_platform) the build fails. Is there an alternative method to add custom policies?
resolution: ### **Prerequisites**- The user must have privileges to uninstall and install the APIcast Operator.- The user must have privileges to create ConfigMaps in APIcast namespace. ###**Before starting** Adding custom policies consist of two steps:- Add the custom policies to APIcast.- Make the custom policies available in the 3scale admin-portal. 3scale uses the parameter `APICAST_REGISTRY_URL` to determine which 3scale policies to show in the UI based on the version of APIcast running. By default, `APICAST_REGISTRY_URL` is set to http://apicast-staging:8090 meaning that it pulls the policies that are stored in the apicast-staging built-in gateway. When hosting APIcast outside the OpenShift cluster the value `APICAST_REGISTRY_URL` must be set to the host of APIcast self-managed. The parameter is placed in the `system-environment` ConfigMap. However there are some scenarios where the user can’t update the system-environment ConfigMap due to lack of privileges in the 3scale deployment. In this case the alternative is to maintain the `APICAST_REGISTRY_URL` as is and update the registry with the 3scale API. Below are described the steps to add custom policies with ConfigMaps depending on whether the user can have access to the 3scale deployment to modify ConfigMaps and redeploy the related component system-app. ### **Scenario 1: system-environment ConfigMap from 3scale can be updated by the user** 1. Uninstall the Operator (this is required, otherwise any changes will be reconciled including the mounted volumes). 2. Apply the ConfigMaps with the custom policies on the Deployment object. ~~~ oc create configmap example-policy--from-file=policies/example/0.1 oc set volumes deployment/apicast-example-apicast--add--overwrite--name=example-policy \ >--mount-path=/opt/app-root/src/policies/example/0.1--source='{"configMap":{"name":"example-policy"}}' ~~~ 3. Optional: update the `APICAST_POLICY_LOAD_PATH` if you want to change the default loath path. The default load path is /opt/app-root/src/policies. You can see more information in APIcast [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.8/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_environment_variables#policy-load-path). 4. In the namespace where APIcast self-managed is deployed, create a new route that points to the APIcast service with the target port 8090. Make sure all the necessary configuration in your environment for this route to be externally accessible from the external are in place: 3scale will need to communicate with APIcast via this URL. (Route for policies image) 5. In the 3scale project, update the parameter APICAST_REGISTRY_URL in `system-environment` ConfigMap with the route configured in APIcast self managed. (APICAST_REGISTRY_URL image) 6. Redeploy system-app deployment configuration. 7. Configure the Product from the 3scale admin portal:- From Integration > Settings configure:- Deployment: APIcast self-managed- Public Base URL: the route configured for the APIcast self-managed gateway- At the bottom click "Update Product"- From Integration > Configuration:- Promote v.X to Staging APIcast- Promote v.X to Production APIcast if desirable With this solution any custom policy added in the self-managed APIcast will be available to all services since the policies for all services will be pulled from the APIcast self managed gateway. ### **Scenario 2: system-environment ConfigMap from 3scale can’t be updated by the user** When it is not possible to change the APICAST_REGISTRY_URL because the user doesn't have access to 3scale the workaround is to update the Policy Registry: 1. Uninstall the Operator (this is required, otherwise any changes will be reconciled including the mounted volumes). 2. Apply the ConfigMaps with the custom policies on the Deployment object. ~~~ oc create configmap example-policy--from-file=policies/example/0.1 oc set volumes deployment/apicast-example-apicast--add--overwrite--name=example-policy \ >--mount-path=/opt/app-root/src/policies/example/0.1--source='{"configMap":{"name":"example-policy"}}' ~~~ 3. Optional: update the APICAST_POLICY_LOAD_PATH if you want to change the default loath path. The default load path is /opt/app-root/src/policies. You can see more information in APIcast [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.8/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_environment_variables#policy-load-path). 4. Use the 3scale API endpoint_Apicast Policy Registry Create_ to create an APIcast Policy. Note that the name parameter must be the same as the name of the root folder of the policy and the version the same as the subfolder, e.g. "example/0.1"--> name = example, version = 0.1. 5. Configure the Product from the 3scale admin portal:- From Integration > Settings configure:- Deployment: APIcast self-managed- Public Base URL: the route configured for the APIcast self-managed gateway- At the bottom click "Update Product"- From Integration > Configuration:- Promote v.X to Staging APIcast- Promote v.X to Production APIcast if desirable With this method only the services configured with the self-managed APIcast will have access to the custom policies. ###**Custom policies after upgrading APIcast** There is a disadvantage when using this workaround: when updating APIcast the operator must be reinstalled and it will reconcile any changes meaning that custom policies will be removed. When upgrading the APIcast self managed the custom policies must be mounted again. The procedure to upgrade APIcast and adding custom policies would be: 1. Uninstall the Operator 2. Create ConfigMaps & volumeMounts 3. Confirm policy is in UI and works 4. Reinstall the Operator 5. Update the channel 6. Repeat steps 1- 3
root_cause: There is a known issue [THREESCALE-5515](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-5515) when building images to add custom policies.

title: Using RHACM to Deploy an Openshift Cluster on AWS to an Existing VPC
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: When using `openshift-install` to deploy an Openshift cluster on AWS I am able to specify the VPC the new cluster should be deployed to via the steps at [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/installing/installing_aws/installing-aws-vpc.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/installing/installing_aws/installing-aws-vpc.html). In RHACM's **Create a cluster*
menu I do not see an option to specify the VPC.
resolution: * From the **Create a cluster** menu on ACM you may click the toggle at the top to enable direct YAML editing which will pop out an editor from the sidebar. * Once you select an Infrastructure Provider (in this case AWS) you will see a new tab created on the YAML editor for the `install-config.yaml` file. * This YAML corresponds to the `install-config.yaml` from the openshift-install documentation. * Following the same documentation from openshift-install you may set your existing VPC under `spec.platform.aws.subnets:` and the newly deployed cluster will be deployed to that VPC.

resolution: The bootstrap machine is unable to get ignition file from S3 resource in a disconnected environment. it is unable to reach the public IP addresses for EC2 and ELB endpoints. To resolve this, it must be create a VPC endpoints for EC2, S3 and LB resources and attach it to the subnet that the clusters are using. The VPC provided to the OpenShift installer must have the endpoints named as follows:- com.amazonaws.region-1.s3- com.amazonaws.region.ec2- com.amazonaws.region.elasticloadbalancing As an example creating the endpoints follows as:- Get VPC, Subnets, Security Groups and Routes ~~~ # VPC_ID=`aws ec2 describe-vpcs | jq-r.Vpcs[].VpcId`; echo $VPC_ID # Get vpc-id # SUBNETS=`aws ec2 describe-subnets | jq-r.Subnets[].SubnetId`; echo $SUBNETS # Get subnets-id # SG=`aws ec2 describe-security-groups | jq-r.SecurityGroups[].GroupId`; echo $SG # Get Security Groups # ROUTES=`aws ec2 describe-route-tables | jq-r.RouteTables[].RouteTableId`; echo $ROUTES # Get Route Tables # REGION="eu-west-1" ~~~- Create Endpoints S3, EC2 and LoadBalancing (Those could be created from AWS Console UI as well)** ~~~ # aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint--vpc-id $VPC_ID--service-name com.amazonaws.${REGION}.s3--route-table-ids $ROUTES # aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint--vpc-id $VPC_ID--service-name com.amazonaws.${REGION}.ec2--subnet-ids $SUBNETS--security-group-ids $SG--vpc-endpoint-type Interface # aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint--vpc-id $VPC_ID--service-name com.amazonaws.${REGION}.elasticloadbalancing--subnet-ids $SUBNETS--security-group-ids $SG--vpc-endpoint-type Interface ~~~ Please note that VPC_ID, SUBNETS, SG, ROUTES must be replaced with the ID of the VPC_ID, SUBNETS, SG, ROUTES in question. Documentation references:- [VPC Requirements for AWS Private Cluster](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/installing/installing_aws/installing-aws-private.html#installation-custom-aws-vpc-requirements_installing-aws-private)- [Installing the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-install.html)- [AWS CLI Configuration and credential file settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html)

title: How to expand PVC for ES when Expanding Volumes Dynamically is not possible in OCP 4
issue: - VSphere disks are not available to be used with feature `allowVolumeExpansion`
resolution: Steps shared on [Bugzilla #1846458](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1846458), but requires validation: 1. ~~~ If so, we need to do only the following steps for extending. 1. Extend VMDK size on vSphere side 2. Login the work node where ES pod is running, and extend PV's filesystem $ mount | grep /elasticsearch-[0-9] /dev/sdb on /var/lib/kubelet/pods/7a6774c9-1dff-4d92-89cd-fb61796951ff/volumes/kubernetes.io~vsphere-volume/elasticsearch-0 type ext4 (rw,relatime,seclabel) $ sudo resize2fs /dev/sdb 3. Alter the PV/PVC accordingly ~~~ 2. ~~~ 1. Set ClusterLogging to Unmanaged state 2. Set Elasticsearch object to Unmanaged state. 3. Scale down one of ElasticSearch pods by oc scale--replicas=0 deployments elastic... 4. Delete its PVC and PV of the pod 5. Extend the volume size I. Extend VMDK size II. Attach it to one of worker node, and then run xfs_growfs III. Detach it from the node 6. Create its PVC and PV with the same names, but change the size 7. Scale up one of ElasticSearch pods by oc scale--replicas=1 deployments elastic... 8. Do Step 3 to 7 for other ElasticSearch pods. 9. Set the Elasticsearch object to Managed state. 10. Set ClusterLogging to Managed state ~~~
root_cause: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/storage/expanding-persistent-volumes.html#expanding-pvc-filesystem_expanding-persistent-volumes

resolution: - This issue has been resolved by the Red Hat Engineering team through a reported Bugzilla [BUG 1531938](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1531938)- If above error messages are getting continuously logged for a non existing role, then there is a need to upgrade to the OpenShift Cluster to the version 4.1.0 where this issue is fixed or higher than that.- Public advisory for this bug can be found [here](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2019:0758)

title: Is volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer supported in OpenShift?
resolution: - The volumeBindingMode `WaitForFirstConsumer` is a **beta** feature on Kubernetes 1.11.- This is **not supported** on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.x, as it is based on Kubernetes 1.11.- The volumeBindingMode `WaitForFirstConsumer` is a **stable** feature on Kubernetes 1.13.- It is **supported** on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x, as it is based on Kubernetes 1.13.- Find more information about `WaitForFirstConsumer` volumeBindingMode [here](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/10/11/topology-aware-volume-provisioning-in-kubernetes/).- Disclaimer: Note that the link provided above points to a web site not owned or controlled by Red Hat. Use information present here at your own discretion.*

title: What are the observed limits for kernel semaphore parameters?
issue: What are the observed limits for kernel semaphore parameters?
resolution: The following is a list of the Linux semaphore limits. The system call affected by the limit and the error that results if the limit is reached are noted in parentheses: parameter kernel variable description ceiling kernel.sem SEMMSL This is the maximum number of semaphores that can be allocated in a semaphore set. (semget(), EINVAL) 65536 (notes 1 & 2) SEMMNS This is a system-wide limit on the number of semaphores in all semaphore sets. The number of semaphores on the system is also limited by SEMMNI and SEMMSL; in fact, the default value for SEMMNS is the product of the defaults for these two limits. (semget(), ENOSPC) 2147483647 (note 3) SEMOPM This is the maximum number of operations per semop() call. (semop(), E2BIG) 1000 (note 4) SEMMNI This is a system-wide limit on the number of semaphore identifiers (in other words, semaphore sets) that can be created. (semget(), ENOSPC) 32768 * note 1: It is possible to raise SEMMSL to values larger than 65,536, and create semaphore sets up to that larger size. However, it isn’t possible to use semop() to adjust semaphores in the set beyond the 65,536th element * note 2: Because of certain limitations in the current implementation, the practical recommended upper limit on the size of a semaphore set is around 8000. * note 3: The practical ceiling for the SEMMNS limit is governed by the amount of RAM available on the system * note 4: The ceiling value for the SEMOPM limit is determined by memory allocation primitives used within the kernel. The recommended maximum is 1000. In practical usage, it is rarely useful to perform more than a few operations in a single semop() call * note 5: SEMMNI can be increased to 16777216 via the "ipcmni_extend" Kernel command line parameter on RHEL 7.8+ and 8.1+. See [On RHEL servers, changing the semaphore value fails with a message "setting key "kernel.sem": Numerical result out of range"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4968021) for more details.
root_cause: In a glance to kernel source code, one can quickly check the aforementioned limits, and the respective commentaries which depict their implementation practical limits: ipc/util.h: /* * The IPC ID contains 2 separate numbers- index and sequence number. * By default, * bits 0-14: index (32k, 15 bits) * bits 15-30: sequence number (64k, 16 bits) * * When IPCMNI extension mode is turned on, the composition changes: * bits 0-23: index (16M, 24 bits) * bits 24-30: sequence number (128, 7 bits) */ #define IPCMNI_SHIFT 15 #define IPCMNI_EXTEND_SHIFT 24 #define IPCMNI_EXTEND_MIN_CYCLE (RADIX_TREE_MAP_SIZE * RADIX_TREE_MAP_SIZE) #define IPCMNI (1 < < IPCMNI_SHIFT) #define IPCMNI_EXTEND (1 < < IPCMNI_EXTEND_SHIFT) include/uapi/linux/sem.h: #define SEMMNI 128 /* <= IPCMNI max # of semaphore identifiers */ #define SEMMSL 250 /* <= 8 000 max num of semaphores per id */ #define SEMMNS (SEMMNI*SEMMSL) /* <= INT_MAX max # of semaphores in system */ #define SEMOPM 32 /* <= 1 000 max num of ops per semop call */ #define SEMVMX 32767 /* <= 32767 semaphore maximum value */ #define SEMAEM SEMVMX /* adjust on exit max value */

title: Does OpenShift support multi-factor authentication (MFA)?
issue: - How to use `multi-factor authentication` with OpenShift?
resolution: - By default OpenShift does not have `multi-factor authentication`.- Red Hat SSO provides `multi-factor authentication` and support.- In order to have `multi-factor authentication` there must be an identity provider that support it.- You can use `Red Hat Single Sign-On` which can be deployed on OpenShift.- For more information please refer [Red Hat Single Sign-On for OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_single_sign-on_continuous_delivery/2/html/red_hat_single_sign-on_for_openshift/index) and the list of [Authentication identity providers](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/authentication/identity_providers/).

title: The nodeca daemon doesn't get installed after changing the mangementState to Removed for the image registry operator
issue: - After changing the managementState of the image registry operator the operator will strip down the storage configured for the image registry pod.- The output of oc get events will show that the **image-registry-certificates*
configmap and **serviceca*

config map mount failure errors as follows: ~~~ 5m5s Warning FailedMount pod/node-ca-7cf5s MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "serviceca": configmap "image-registry-certificates" not found 5m27s Warning FailedMount pod/node-ca-f4j4t MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "serviceca": configmap "image-registry-certificates" not found 5m28s Warning FailedMount pod/node-ca-lq4f5 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "serviceca": configmap "image-registry-certificates" not found 5m43s Warning FailedMount pod/node-ca-tlqf4 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "serviceca": configmap "image-registry-certificates" not found ~~~
resolution: Per [Bugzilla #1807471](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1807471), this is a known issue fixed at Errata [RHBA-2020:2409](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2020:2409) on OpenShift 4.5.1. ### Workaround Patch the Operator configuration object by running the following commands and enabling the `nodeca` daemon storage. ~~~ # oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io cluster--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"storage":{"emptyDir":{}}}}' # oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io cluster--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"managementState":"Managed"}}' ~~~

title: How to install and verify installation of a specific version of OpenShift Virtualization in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.6
issue: How to install and verify installation of of a specific version of OpenShift Virtualization in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.6? The install guide only gives instructions for installing the most up-to-date release and from the GUI is not really possible to pin to a specific version released in the past: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/virt/install/installing-virt-cli.html
resolution: Installation of CNV by CLI is a 2 step process. ### Subscribing to the OpenShift Virtualization catalog by using the CLI Apply the following resources: ~~~ cat < <'EOF' | oc apply-f- apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-cnv--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: kubevirt-hyperconverged-group namespace: openshift-cnv spec: targetNamespaces:- openshift-cnv--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: hco-operatorhub namespace: openshift-cnv spec: channel: stable name: kubevirt-hyperconverged source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 installPlanApproval: Manual EOF ~~~ *startingCSV* can point to an arbitrary older version, *installPlanApproval* should be set to *Manual* to prevent the cluster from automatically reaching the most up to date release. #### Verification This will create some pods in namespace `openshift-cnv`, they must all be running. The easiest way to verify this are these verification steps: Ensure that OpenShift Virtualization deployed successfully by watching the PHASE of the ClusterServiceVersion (CSV) in the openshift-cnv namespace. Run the following command: ~~~ $ watch oc get csv-n openshift-cnv ~~~ The following output displays if deployment was successful: ~~~ NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Succeeded ~~~ #### Example ~~~ [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# cat < <'EOF' | oc apply-f- apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-cnv--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: kubevirt-hyperconverged-group namespace: openshift-cnv spec: targetNamespaces:- openshift-cnv--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: hco-operatorhub namespace: openshift-cnv spec: channel: stable name: kubevirt-hyperconverged source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 installPlanApproval: Manual EOF namespace/openshift-cnv created operatorgroup.operators.coreos.com/kubevirt-hyperconverged-group created subscription.operators.coreos.com/hco-operatorhub created [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get csv-n openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Pending [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get csv-n openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Pending [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get csv-n openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 InstallReady [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get csv-n openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Installing (...) [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get csv-n openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Installing ~~~ At this point, some of the pods are still in `ContainerCreating` stage: ~~~ [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get pods-n openshift-cnv NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cdi-operator-d4b9df6c4-lmmsz 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s cluster-network-addons-operator-5fcc54c86d-p8k8c 1/1 Running 0 16s hco-operator-89ddd5f8b-ks7rn 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s hostpath-provisioner-operator-699f767767-d7tgg 1/1 Running 0 16s kubevirt-ssp-operator-575cd6b6db-6tfdm 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s node-maintenance-operator-949cf7ccd-fxtdv 1/1 Running 0 16s virt-operator-6596994466-qn2f9 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s virt-operator-6596994466-rvl24 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get pods-n openshift-cnv NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cdi-operator-d4b9df6c4-lmmsz 1/1 Running 0 3m39s cluster-network-addons-operator-5fcc54c86d-p8k8c 1/1 Running 0 3m39s hco-operator-89ddd5f8b-ks7rn 1/1 Running 0 3m39s hostpath-provisioner-operator-699f767767-d7tgg 1/1 Running 0 3m39s kubevirt-ssp-operator-575cd6b6db-6tfdm 1/1 Running 0 3m39s node-maintenance-operator-949cf7ccd-fxtdv 1/1 Running 0 3m39s virt-operator-6596994466-qn2f9 1/1 Running 0 3m39s virt-operator-6596994466-rvl24 1/1 Running 0 3m39s ~~~ Eventually, all of the above containers will show as `Running` and the csv will switch to `Succeeded`: ~~~ [root@openshift-jumpserver-0 ~]# oc get csv-n openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Succeeded ~~~ ### Deploying the OpenShift Virtualization Operator by using the CLI Create the `HyperConverged` resource: ~~~ cat < <'EOF' | oc apply-f- apiVersion: hco.kubevirt.io/v1beta1 kind: HyperConverged metadata: name: kubevirt-hyperconverged namespace: openshift-cnv spec: BareMetalPlatform: true EOF ~~~ #### Verification Now, wait for a few DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.5.0 OpenShift Virtualization 2.5.0 kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator.v2.4.2 Succeeded ~~~ * Make sure that all pods in namespace title: Control over project/namespace names in Red Hat OpenShift Container platform for non-admin users
issue: - The default projects created after the installation of `RHOCP`by the openshift installer do start with `openshift-*` or `kube-*` and non-admin users are not allowed to create the projects with these terms.- Is it possible to add specific terms similar to those that are not permitted?- Is it possible to block users from creating a project named `xyz-*`?
resolution: - There is an [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1065) filed with engineering to add this functionality in the future.- Open a support ticket with Red Hat support to get the latest status of the RFE.
root_cause: - OpenShift does not currently have the ability to restrict users from creating a blacklist of names that cannot be used by **non-admin** users for creating `projects/namespaces`.

title: [WIP] Project request template reverts the quota changes post cluster installation

title: Diskmaker pods logs error "unable to add disk-id" every 5 seconds, when OCS is deployed using LSO.
issue: Diskmaker pods logs error **unable to add disk-id*

every 5 seconds, when OCS is deployed using LSO. ~~~ E0922 16:37:40.778533 1 diskmaker.go:278] unable to add disk-id /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-123 to local disk pool: unable to find device with id /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-123 ~~~
resolution: * To avoid the error messages in the `DiskMaker` logs, one needs to create a `LocalVolume CR` for every OCS node separately and include only the available devices in the **devicePaths** section. ~~~ apiVersion: local.storage.openshift.io/v1 kind: LocalVolume metadata: name: local-block-node1 <------ Change the name for every node namespace: local-storage labels: app: ocs-storagecluster spec: nodeSelector: nodeSelectorTerms:- matchExpressions:- key: kubernetes.io/hostname <------ Change the key to be 'hostname' operator: In values:- dell-r730-009.dsal.lab.eng.rdu2.redhat.com <------ Add the hostname here storageClassDevices:- storageClassName: localblock volumeMode: Block devicePaths:- /dev/disk/by-id/ <------ Add the devices ~~~
root_cause: * While configuring OCS to use LSO, in the `LocalVolume CR`, the node selector is mentioned as **cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage**. and thus it would choose all the OCS nods. * As per the [Installation Document](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_container_storage/4.5/html-single/deploying_openshift_container_storage_using_bare_metal_infrastructure/index#creating-openshift-container-storage-cluster-on-bare-metal_rhocs) it is recommended to provide all the devices, across all nodes by their **disk-id** in the `devicePaths` section. * Because of the above configuration, the `DiskMaker` pods would try to look for all the devices mentioned in the **devicePaths** section on all the OCS nodes. * Since, the devices under **devicePaths** sections contains the `disk-id` from all nodes, it will not be able to find a devices which are not present on a specific node and hence the error is logged in `DiskMaker` logs.

title: Getting 'x509 errors' while installation when the `baseDomain` has a trailing dot(.)
issue: - The `baseDomain` has a trailing dot(.) in the file `install-config.yaml` and due to which the installation of the cluster is failing with `x509` errors.- The domain name is published by the Google Cloud DNS and the same domain name has been given to `baseDomain` filed in the `install-config.yaml` file but cluster installation is failing with the `x509` errors.
resolution: - According to this [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1853418), this issue is resolved in **OpenShift v4.6**- Find the Bugfix in this [ERRATA](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2020:4196) update.

title: AWS resource invocation does not work due to invalid Signature
issue: - We are facing the below error ~~~ SignatureDoesNotMatch The request signature we calculated does not match the signature you provided. Check your key and signing method. finger_print/1234abc/right_thumb.wsq file-others /file-others/finger_print/1234abc/right_thumb.wsq 123xyz $HOST_ID ~~~
resolution: - Probably the credentials placed here `.aws/config` are inappropriate and could not match with the actual ones stored in the AWS account.

title: Expose Prometheus alert to zabbix
issue: - Is it possible to forward the alert raised by Prometheus to Zabbix Server?- Our requirement is to forward only alerts raised by Prometheus to a centralized external Zabbix server
resolution: - Implementing alerting for an external server would require out of the box implementation.
root_cause: - Zabbix isn't part of [supported webhook receivers](https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/integrations/#alertmanager-webhook-receiver) from Prometheus

title: OpenShift API randomly returns i/o timeouts
issue: - While running build jobs using Jenkins, the OpenShift API randomly failing with i/o timeout. ~~~ error: couldn't get deployment test1: Get https://x.x.x.x:443/api/v1/namespaces/test1/replicationcontrollers/test1: dial tcp x.x.x.x:443: i/o timeout ~~~
resolution: - Check if the `drop templates` feature is enabled in the external firewall. Disabling it can help to narrow down this issue.
root_cause: - Checkpoint firewall has a feature called `drop templates` which helps accelerate firewall performance. If this feature is enabled we might face such issues.

title: Is it possible to disable audit logging from ElasticSearch in RHOCP3.11?
issue: - Is it possible to disable `audit logging` from `ElasticSearch` in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.11?
resolution: - With Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.11, option to disable `audit logs` in `ElasticSearch` at this moment isn't available.- The `audit logs` from node or from the RHOCP `api` are all logged in the `.operation indices` which ideally should not be altered, as it would need a lot many changes in `logging-fluentd configmap` and wouldn't be the supported config change.

title: How to recreate a brick from scratch in Openshift Container Storage 3.x?
issue: Sometimes, LVM thin pools might get corrupted to the point that the data stored in them is not recoverable. In such scenarios, the easiest option is to recreate the affected Gluster brick from scratch and use the remaining available replicas in the volume to synchronise the data. However, due to Openshift Container Storage architecture, the thin pool and logical volume names have to be preserved when doing such activity. Otherwise, there'll be a mismatch in between Gluster and Heketi, causing a discrepancy in the configuration.
The below procedure describes what are the needed steps to accomplish this task.
resolution: For the discussion, we'll use testvolume as an example, assuming that that the thin pool in the third brick is corrupted and cannot be recovered. Status of volume: testvolume Gluster process TCP Port RDMA Port Online Pid------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Brick 192.168.0.1:/var/lib/heketi/mount s/vg_17157017b21051f0ad760f5e313d6064/brick_19ebb7b845995c4184d3daed777f44c1/brick 49152 0 Y 332 Brick 192.168.0.2:/var/lib/heketi/mount s/vg_b3bb72b0e24322705379209f5a99b602/brick_516efa820ecad335ef7c7214c7475c22/brick 49152 0 Y 192 Brick 192.168.0.3:/var/lib/heketi/mount s/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246/brick N/A N/A N N/A Self-heal Daemon on localhost N/A N/A Y 70372 Self-heal Daemon on 192.168.0.1 N/A N/A Y 115066 Self-heal Daemon on 192.168.0.2 N/A N/A Y 79210 Self-heal Daemon on 192.168.0.3 N/A N/A Y 89883 As a prerequisite, collect the output of these commands: lvs--all--units k--reportformat=json > lvs-NODENAME-$(date-I).js vgs--all--units k--reportformat=json > vgs-NODENAME-$(date-I).json They contain required information about sizes that would be needed during the recreation. The following steps are to be applied in the Gluster pod / node where the brick has to be recreated 1. Remove the brick from the Gluster volume configuration. The required command is: gluster v remove-brick testvolume replica 2 192.168.0.3:/var/lib/heketi/mounts/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246/brick force 2. Remove the thin pool: /usr/sbin/lvm lvremove--autobackup=n-f vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 It's important to note that the LVM thin pool is named the same as the brick. 3. Nex step is thin pool recreation. The command to run is /usr/sbin/lvm lvcreate-qq--autobackup=n--poolmetadatasize--chunksize 256K--size--thin vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246--virtualsize--name brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 The values that need to be filled are the metadatasize of the pool, its size and its virtual size. Using the lvs command output collected previously, we can search for this information. grep tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 lvs-192.168.0.3-2020-10-14.js {"lv_name":"brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246", "vg_name":"vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b", "lv_attr":"Vwi-aotz--", "lv_size":"2097152,00k", "pool_lv":"tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246", "origin":"", "data_percent":"0,73", "metadata_percent":"", "move_pv":"", "mirror_log":"", "copy_percent":"", "convert_lv":""}, {"lv_name":"tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246", "vg_name":"vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b", "lv_attr":"twi-aotz--", "lv_size":"2097152,00k", "pool_lv":"", "origin":"", "data_percent":"0,73", "metadata_percent":"10,32", "move_pv":"", "mirror_log":"", "copy_percent":"", "convert_lv":""}, {"lv_name":"[tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246_tdata]", "vg_name":"vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b", "lv_attr":"Twi-ao----", "lv_size":"2097152,00k", "pool_lv":"", "origin":"", "data_percent":"", "metadata_percent":"", "move_pv":"", "mirror_log":"", "copy_percent":"", "convert_lv":""}, {"lv_name":"[tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246_tmeta]", "vg_name":"vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b", "lv_attr":"ewi-ao----", "lv_size":"12288,00k", "pool_lv":"", "origin":"", "data_percent":"", "metadata_percent":"", "move_pv":"", "mirror_log":"", "copy_percent":"", "convert_lv":""}, The sizes we're looking for are listed above: "lv_size":"2097152,00k" in the thin pool tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246_tdata ==> This is the value needed for size and virtual size parameters "lv_size":"12288,00k" in the thin pool tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246_tmeta ==> This is the value needed for the metadatasize parameter. So the complete command would be: /usr/sbin/lvm lvcreate-qq--autobackup=n--poolmetadatasize 12288K--chunksize 256K--size 2097152K--thin vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/tp_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246--virtualsize 2097152K--name brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 4. One the thin pool is available, create the file system and mount it. The mkfs parameters are standard, and do not depend on the brick size: mkfs.xfs-i size=512-n size=8192 /dev/mapper/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b-brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 ==> Note this is a hash, not a hyphen mount-o rw,inode64,noatime,nouuid /dev/mapper/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b-brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 /var/lib/heketi/mounts/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246 In this step it's assumed that the mount point exists, which should be the case, as it's a re-creation of an existing brick. mkdir /var/lib/heketi/mounts/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246/brick chown:2000 /var/lib/heketi/mounts/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/brick_b7fff45457e535d424a84b95419b0246/brick Note that no entries are added to the `/etc/fstab` file, since it's also assumed that these entries are already present, as the brick existed previously. 5. Attach the brick back, so the healing process can sync up the data from the remaining two bricks in the volume: gluster volume add-brick testvolume replica 3 192.168.0.3:/var/lib/heketi/mounts/vg_9e4c8b1a364cfa9ee5f377766f435f8b/brick

title: BuildConfigs that use "dots" in their names are producing wrong labels on resulting builds
issue: - `BuildConfig names` that include `semantic version number` i.e. `X.Y.Z` i.e has `dots` in their names (**for example: bc-33.snapshot-webservice-2**), creates builds` labels` with `truncated` like: **bc-33*

and not bc-33.snapshot-webservice-2- When BuildConfigs are created with `dot` in their names, the parameter `successfulBuildsHistoryLimit` does not honor the `integer value` passed to it and delete all builds starting with `bc-33`
root_cause: - `Dot` in `BuildConfig names` were allowed to be used in RHOCP **v3.11** but onwards **v4.4** this was removed.- **[A bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1862532)** has been filed to fix this behavior and the ERRATA will be released in **RHOCP v4.6**

title: Auto Scaling apps with Custom Metrics in Redhat OpenShift Container platform 4.x
issue: - How to Auto Scale with Custom Metric?- How to use custom metrics for HPA
resolution: - By default out of box RHOCP supports `HPA` with `CPU` and `Memory` metrics. However when application demand increases it should scale with various factors such as traffic patterns, No of requests and so.- To scale the application using a custom metric. One needs to provide the appropriate metric from the application and configure those metrics to the Prometheus-adapter.- Configuring the application metrics for monitoring.- Follow the procedure in [Enable monitoring for user-defined project](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/monitoring/enabling-monitoring-for-user-defined-projects.html#enabling-monitoring-for-user-defined-projects_enabling-monitoring-for-user-defined-projects).- Follow the procedure in [Exposing the custom application metrics for horizontal pod autoscaling](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/monitoring/exposing-custom-application-metrics-for-autoscaling.html) with a slight configuration change to configure the Prometheus in openshift-user-workload-monitoring.- Add the Promtheus endpoint in openshift-user-workload-monitoring in the deployment of prometheus-adapter ~~~---prometheus-auth-config=/etc/prometheus-config/prometheus-config.yaml <---Need to create an config map---config=/etc/adapter/config.yaml---logtostderr=true---metrics-relist-interval=1m---prometheus-url=https://prometheus-user-workload.openshift-user-workload-monitoring.svc:9091 <-------secure-port=6443 ~~~- Create a config map with the ServiceAccount to authenticate the Prometheus ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: prometheus-adapter-prometheus-config namespace: openshift-user-workload-monitoring data: prometheus-config.yaml: | apiVersion: v1 clusters:- cluster: certificate-authority: /etc/ssl/certs/service-ca.crt server: https://prometheus-user-workload.openshift-user-workload-monitoring.svc:9091 name: prometheus-user-workload contexts:- context: cluster: prometheus-user-workload user: custom-metrics-apiserver name: custom-metrics-apiserver current-context: custom-metrics-apiserver kind: Config preferences: {} users:- name: custom-metrics-apiserver user: tokenFile: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token ~~~

title: Elasticsearch pod went into CrashLoopBackOff with with 'java.io.IOException: No space left on device' in OCP 4.5
issue: `Elasticsearch` pod went into `CrashLoopBackOff` with `java.io.IOException: No space left on device`. ~~~ elasticsearch-cdm-wx1qj2o2-1-8cbb6d8f-6s6rq 1/2 CrashLoopBackOff 163 3d10h 10.152.X.Y node1 elasticsearch-cdm-wx1qj2o2-2-6dd654bbf6-6bc2b 2/2 Running 0 3d10h 10.152.X.Y node2 elasticsearch-cdm-wx1qj2o2-3-f8fbdf769-wcrz2 2/2 Running 0 3d10h 10.152.X.Y node3 ~~~

`Elasticsearch` Logs shows below message: ~~~ at org.elasticsearch.bootstrap.Elasticsearch.main(Elasticsearch.java:84) ~[elasticsearch-5.6.16.redhat-2.jar:5.6.16.redhat-2] ') error: org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.AppenderLoggingException: Error writing to stream /elasticsearch/persistent/elasticsearch/logs/elasticsearch.log org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.AppenderLoggingException: Error writing to stream /elasticsearch/persistent/elasticsearch/logs/elasticsearch.log at org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.OutputStreamManager.writeToDestination(OutputStreamManager.java:263) at org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.FileManager.writeToDestination(FileManager.java:261) at org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.rolling.RollingFileManager.writeToDestination(RollingFileManager.java:219) at org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.OutputStreamManager.flushBuffer(OutputStreamManager.java:293)... Output Ommitted... at java.lang.Thread.dispatchUncaughtException(Thread.java:1959) Caused by: java.io.IOException: No space left on device at java.io.FileOutputStream.writeBytes(Native Method) at java.io.FileOutputStream.write(FileOutputStream.java:326) at org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.OutputStreamManager.writeToDestination(OutputStreamManager.java:261)... 39 more ~~~
resolution: * This issue occurs when `Elasticsearch` becomes unable to write the `logs` to PVC due to lack of storage. * Access the node on which the `Elasticsearch` is storing the `logs`. ~~~ $ ssh core@ ~~~ * Check the directory where the `Elasticsearch` PVC is mounted. ~~~ $ df-h ~~~ * Try to delete some old log files which are occupying the space. Note: There will be two directories inside the PVC mounted directory, `indices` and `logs`. Make sure to delete the files from the `logs` directory and not from the `indices`. * Once you remove the old log files from the PVC mounted directory, `scale-down` the `elasticsearch` deployment and `scale-up` again. ~~~ $ for i in $(oc get deployment-l component=elasticsearch-o name); do oc scale $i--replicas 0; done $ oc get pods-l component=elasticsearch $ for i in $(oc get deployment-l component=elasticsearch-o name); do oc scale $i--replicas 1; done ~~~
root_cause: * `Elasticsearch` storage was full.

title: Red Hat 3scale APIcast is failing with the error message "document fails length limit"
issue: APIcast is on the `CrashLoopBackOff` state with the following message on its logs: ERROR: /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/liquid.lua:2643: document fails length limit. length limit:100000 stack traceback: /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/liquid.lua:2643: in function 'check_length' /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/liquid.lua:2243: in function 'visit' /usr/local/share/lua/5.1/liquid.lua:1975: in function 'render' /opt/app-root/src/src/apicast/cli/command/start.lua:56: in function 'nginx_config' /opt/app-root/src/src/apicast/cli/command/start.lua:157: in function 'start' /opt/app-root/src/src/apicast/cli.lua:49: in function /tmp/q75Tc0UpE6:60: in function 'file_gen' init_worker_by_lua:51: in function [C]: in function 'xpcall' init_worker_by_lua:58: in function loading staging environment configuration: /opt/app-root/src/config/staging.lua

title: Persistent Volume can't be deleted when deleting a project containing azure-file storage in OpenShift 4
issue: When deleting a project containing `azure-file` storage the `azure-storage-account-xxxxxx` `secret` is deleted before `PersistentVolume`, which prevents the `PersistentVolume` from being deleted.
resolution: There are two ways to work around this problem: 1. Kubernetes documentation suggests using `secretNamespace` in the Azure File `StorageClass` so that the secret is kept in a different `namespace` and not deleted when the project is removed. 2. Manually clean up the failed `PersistentVolume` in OpenShift and then remove all the Azure file shares that are no longer referenced by a `PersitentVolume`.
root_cause: The the `secret` with the `StorageAccount` is deleted before the `PersistentVolume` which prevents the `PersistentVolume` from being deleted.

title: Increasing  OpenShift router's timeout
issue: - The OpenShift Container Platform's router closes HTTP connections after 30s whereas the timeout set for client is 30s and the http-keep-alive value is set to 300 seconds- The external system is configured to reuse existing connections- With other products, where their router is configured with a timeout of 900s. Is possible to keep connections alive between requests for as much as 900s as well with OpenShift Container Platform?-------- Original----- original title: Route Configuration to keep connections alive on OpenShift- With a scenario using TLS termination ‘edge’ and the backend speaks plain http, the timeout is set for client to 30s and the http-keep-alive value to 300 seconds- After 30 seconds the router from OpenShift Container Platform closes the connection with Apigee, a API Frontend used on front of the cluster- From reading HAProxy documentation, this shouldn’t happen for 300s (timeout http-keep-alive) since we are between requests and thus the ‘timeout client’ isn’t relevant.- Since most (> 95%) of the traffic to go through Apigee, it is one of the few clients accessing the router at all. In this scenario (basically one client making all the requests), it is recommended to work with persistent connections in order to reduce workload on both sides. With another products, where their router is configured with a timeout of 900s – and Apigee holds a number of ~800 connections established during rush-hours.- Is possible to keep connections alive between requests for as much as 900s as well with OpenShift Container Platform?
resolution: - If many clients can connect to your service through the router, it is possible to increase the timeout by following this documentation [routes configuration](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/architecture/networking/routes.html#env-variables) Anyway, increasing this timeout too much is not recommended:- Whenever the router reloads, old HAProxy process remains attending old connections while a new haproxy process (with current configuration) starts. So, if there are many long-lasting connections, many old haproxy processes may accumulate causing RAM exhaustion and poor performance in the meanwhile.- Increasing the timeout will increase the number of open sockets handled by haproxy- If only one client will connect to the service hosted in the Openshift platform, please consider using [nodeport services](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/dev_guide/expose_service/expose_internal_ip_nodeport.html)
root_cause: - We are investigating this issue

title: Change number of shards for index template in OpenShift Container Platform 4.x - Elasticsearch
issue: How to specify the number of shards for specific indexes in OpenShift Elasticsearch
resolution: Till OpenShift 4.1 to 4.4, default indices are created in.operation, project-*,.kibana pattern, so the below process is specifically recommended and verified with clo-4.4 and Elasticsearch-4.4 operator. Here the syntax to make the changes in Elasticsearch template: Syntax ~~~ $ oc exec-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPUT https://localhost:9200/_template/-d '{"order":,"template":"[]","settings":{"index":{"number_of_shards":" ","number_of_replicas":" "}}}' ~~~ **Where:** **template-name**- Get the template name from Elasticsearch storage using following command. you can make the changes in whichever JSON template based on your requirement in the Elasticsearch storage. ~~~ $ oc exec-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca https://localhost:9200/_template | grep-i '.json' ~~~ **template-pattern**- pattern use by the template **shards_count**- number of shards count **replica_count**- number of replica **order_number**- Multiple index templates can potentially match an index, in this case, both the settings and mappings are merged into the final configuration of the index. The order of the merging can be controlled using the order parameter, with lower order being applied first, and higher orders overriding them. You can also see the currently applied templates of your elasticsearch cluster using in dir "/usr/share/elasticsearch/index_templates" inside the elasticsearch pod as: ~~~ /usr/share/elasticsearch/index_templates/common.settings.kibana.template.json /usr/share/elasticsearch/index_templates/common.settings.operations.orphaned.json /usr/share/elasticsearch/index_templates/common.settings.operations.template.json /usr/share/elasticsearch/index_templates/common.settings.project.template.json ~~~ //Example to make changes in template: ~~~ $ oc exec-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPUT https://localhost:9200/_template/common.settings.kibana.template.json-d '{"order":0,"template":".kibana*","settings":{"index":{"number_of_shards":"1","number_of_replicas":"1"}}}' $ oc exec-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPUT https://localhost:9200/_template/common.settings.project.template.json-d '{"order":0,"template":"project*","settings":{"index":{"number_of_shards":"1","number_of_replicas":"1"}}}' $ oc exec-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPUT https://localhost:9200/_template/com.redhat.viaq-openshift-operations.template.json-d '{"order":0,"template":".operations.*","settings":{"index":{"number_of_shards":"1","number_of_replicas":"1"}}}' ~~~

title: How the BUFFER_QUEUE_LIMIT work for Fluentd in OCP 4
resolution: OK back to our options to increase flush speed: Tune flush_thread_count e.g by doubling each time and flush_interval by descreasing to half If 1 is not fast enough we can tune flush_mode to immediate If the incoming rate is also high, we can tune chunk_full_threshold to value less than 0.95 make flushing more aggressive than waiting a chunk to be 95% full. I highly recommend to tune these parameters in multiples small steps and watch on Elasticsearch CPU/MEM and Health. These env vars are taken into consideration inside run.sh but the run.sh controls them based on node FS space: https://github.com/openshift/cluster-logging-operator/blob/release-4.4/files/fluentd/run.sh#L116 (edi We can tune the fluentd flushing behavior by editing the configmap, however this requires that we the ClusterLogging CR's spec.managementState field to Unmanaged to signal to the operator to not reconcile anything.- name: BUFFER_QUEUE_LIMIT value: "32"- name: BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT value: 8m- name: FILE_BUFFER_LIMIT value: 256Mi I highly recommend to tune these parameters in multiples small steps and watch on Elasticsearch CPU/MEM and Health. TW, if you increase flush threads, you should see also fluentd eating up more memory. So may track this too. BTW, just curious about a "hacky" scenario (not gng to try this but just for the sake of knowing it) where buffer files are moved to another location and copied in buffer dir again after a day. Will the logs be pushed anyway? Will it cause any corruption of data? I don't know so much to tell if this will somehow corrupt fluentd and/or the data somehow. My gut feeling that this should be ok based on the fact that fluentd's bookeeping for chunks/flushing is not persistent in any different files than the buffers. However, based on the incoming flow of logs where fluentd is using position files to know where to recover in case of disruption, I am not sure how these position "counter" affect the chunks. https://coreos.slack.com/archives/C01BNE7S171/p1602568876227900 the actual chunk size is set based on experience from earlier clusters. I don't recall why or what capped the value in the past. The current calculation determines the number of output buffers and uses that and 10% of the available disk to calculate the maximum number of buffers before you are "full". It's a classic rate problem. if more logs go in then can be pushed out they get buffered. fluent is a single threaded ruby app that benefits by applying up to 1 cpu. Assuming ES (or other destination) is sized appropriately, there is no push back there and you are limited by fluents capacity https://coreos.slack.com/archives/CB3HXM2QK/p1605723585157400?thread_ts=1605716718.154200&cid=CB3HXM2QK

title: OVA Export from RHEV 4.3 to RHEV 4.2 Fails at VM PowerON
issue: Powering on the VM, the following error is seen: ~~~ VM prtg-apac is down with error. Exit message: internal error: qemu unexpectedly closed the monitor: 2020-11-13T19:55:31.412656Z qemu-kvm:-drive file=/rhev/data-center/mnt/blockSD/1c27cac5-7007-46b5-b976-45aa47573073/images/1222ab3d-9de5-491b-96a4-65d20b7bcf37/6ac472c7-6a65-4e93-a24c-980c94962ed4,format=qcow2,if=none,id=drive-ua-1222ab3d-9de5-491b-96a4-65d20b7bcf37,serial=1222ab3d-9de5-491b-96a4-65d20b7bcf37,werror=stop,rerror=stop,cache=none,aio=native: 'serial' is deprecated, please use the corresponding option of '-device' instead 2020-11-13T19:55:31.415172Z qemu-kvm:-drive file=/rhev/data-center/mnt/blockSD/1c27cac5-7007-46b5-b976-45aa47573073/images/1222ab3d-9de5-491b-96a4-65d20b7bcf37/6ac472c7-6a65-4e93-a24c-980c94962ed4,format=qcow2,if=none,id=drive-ua-1222ab3d-9de5-491b-96a4-65d20b7bcf37,serial=1222ab3d-9de5-491b-96a4-65d20b7bcf37,werror=stop,rerror=stop,cache=none,aio=native: Image is not in qcow2 format. ~~~
resolution: - In this case, cloned the source VM to remove the multiple snapshots.- After creating a clone, then ran `Export as OVA`
root_cause: 1. The front end sends the back end a VM and an export destination. 2. The back end creates new disk (for the ova) if the destination requires, and prepares the VM source disks. 3. The back end asks VDSM to create an OVA file with the complete OVF specification and export destination. 4. VDSM runs ovirt-ova tool- creates the OVA in the destination (using qemu-img convert which may include file format conversion). 5. The back end teardowns the VM source disks. Notes: 1. Step 4 is equivalent to qemu-img convert with the collapse option set and the target format set to QCOW. 2. Only after building the OVA file we could update the OVF with the export size. 3. If possible, we’ll consider using streaming the disk data directly from the qemu chain into OVA. 4. In future openshift env we could use the ovirt-ova tool to run it as an openshift job witout depending on VDSM, or using ansible.

title: ACM 2.1 Is observability service for any managed cluster or only for OpenShift managed clusters?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.1/html/release_notes/red-hat-advanced-cluster-management-for-kubernetes-release-notes#whats-new-in-red-hat-advanced-cluster-management-for-kubernetes I'm sorry but I'm not able to completely understand if observability service is for any managed cluster or only for OpenShift managed clusters. There are several notes about this like: "Note: In Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management the metrics-collector is only supported for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x clusters. " Also in the matrix support page: https://access.redhat.com/articles/5486041 there is an observability table. My doubt is if the notes and the matrix are for RHACM without enabling observability, and after enabling it you can "monitor" any cluster, openshift or not.
resolution: Observability is a part of installation but it is not enabled automatically, therefore ACM have two "states", if observability is enabled or not. Please take a look enabling observability [1] Statement in documentation: "Note: In Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management the metrics-collector is only supported for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x clusters. " This statement is referring to the clusters where ACM is collecting metrics need to be on openshift 4.x. So for example observability will not works with 3.x openshift clusters. Statement does not mean the observability is limited to only openshift. ACM supporting (not in all cases fully) EKS,GKE, AKS too. Like you referred to support matrix for more details about support. [2] You must enable observability to have support described at [2] observability table. 1: https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.1/html-single/observing_environments/index#enabling-observability 2: https://access.redhat.com/articles/5486041

title: Running a cluster backup is failing with '*restore-etcd-pod/pod.yaml: Not found in archive'
issue: - Running a cluster backup on OpenShift is causing an error: tar: *restore-etcd-pod/pod.yaml: Not found in archive tar: Exiting with failure status due to previous errors
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and is tracking the resolution in [RHBZ#1898954](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1898954).- A possible workaround is to run the following commands to correct the modification date of the relevant directory on the OpenShift Container Platform Master Node. After executing these commands, the backup can be triggered again. $ oc debug node/master-0.example.com sh-4.2# chroot /host sh-4.4# touch $(crictl inspect $(crictl ps--name etcd$-q) | jq-r '.status.mounts |.[] | select (.containerPath=="/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources") |.hostPath')
root_cause: - The error is caused by a changed update procedure which modifies all static resources and the backup script can't detect on a reliable way which static resources should been backed up.- The backup script is checking the `static-pod-resources` by the modification date, which needs to be improved. This is currently investigated by the Engineering team under the [RHBZ#1898954](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1898954).

title: Build started failing to clone repo after OCP upgrade from 4.5 to 4.6.
issue: - Build failed with below error message: ~~~ FIPS mode initialized ssh_dispatch_run_fatal: Connection to 10.x.x.x port 22: invalid argument fatal: Could not read from remote repository. Please make sure you have the correct access rights and the repository exists. ~~~
resolution: - The external git repository should be upgraded to meet RHEL8's FIPS compliance standards.- For more details follow the article [4137741](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4137741)
root_cause: - In 4.5 the base image was ubi7 for builder and in 4.6 that is moved to ubi8 with latest RHEL8 FIPS certification.- The FIPS limits what algorithms can be used with SSH protocol and while something was fine by the RHEL6 release date, does not mean that it is allowed in the latest RHEL8 FIPS certification.

title: fluentd not sending logs to kibana with no write index is defined for alias
issue: ~~~ 2020-12-03 12:57:05 +0000 [warn]: [clo_default_output_es] failed to flush the buffer. retry_time=3 next_retry_seconds=2020-12-03 12:57:09 +0000 chunk="5b58c243b1238394171f05d1b4337d4b" error_class=Fluent::Plugin::ElasticsearchOutput::RecoverableRequestFailure error="could not push logs to Elasticsearch cluster ({:host=> \"elasticsearch.openshift-logging.svc.cluster.local\",:port=> 9200,:scheme=> \"https\",:user=> \"fluentd\",:password=> \"obfuscated\"}): [400] {\"error\":{\"root_cause\":[{\"type\":\"illegal_argument_exception\",\"reason\":\"no write index is defined for alias [infra-write]. The write index may be explicitly disabled using is_write_index=false or the alias points to multiple indices without one being designated as a write index\"}],\"type\":\"illegal_argument_exception\",\"reason\":\"no write index is defined for alias [infra-write]. The write index may be explicitly disabled using is_write_index=false or the alias points to multiple indices without one being designated as a write index\"},\"status\":400}" ~~~
resolution: Prevent this from happening by modifying the ClusterLogging object. Set the curator to delete logs. As per the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/logging/config/cluster-logging-curator.html#cluster-logging-curator-yaml_cluster-logging-curator) By default it deletes logs that are 30 days old. Edit the configmap: ~~~ $ oc edit configmap curator ~~~ Set the default to a smaller time. For example, 7 days. *Temporarily* set the curator schedule using the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/logging/config/cluster-logging-curator.html#cluster-logging-curator-schedule_cluster-logging-curator) Set it to run every hour, for example. This way, the curator will run now, to clear up some space. Once it has run, change the schedule back to its previous values.

title: Scaling up and down a deployment with SR-IOV interfaces attached to its pods, the worker node ends up running DHCP on the VFs in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.5
issue: > **Disclaimer:*

Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. When scaling up and down a deployment with SR-IOV interfaces attached to its pods, the worker node at some point ends up running DHCP on the VFs when they move back to netns 1. ~~~ [root@worker-0 ~]# ip a ls dev ens1f0v21 64: ens1f0v21: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP group default qlen 1000 link/ether brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff inet 192.168.123.174/24 brd 192.168.123.255 scope global dynamic noprefixroute ens1f0v21 valid_lft 690795sec preferred_lft 690795sec inet6... scope link noprefixroute valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever [root@worker-0 ~]# nmcli conn NAME UUID TYPE DEVICE Wired Connection 5f123cb7-3abb-477a-8c29-55fa809f19b4 ethernet ens1f0v21 Wired Connection 5f123cb7-3abb-477a-8c29-55fa809f19b4 ethernet ens1f1 Wired Connection 5f123cb7-3abb-477a-8c29-55fa809f19b4 ethernet ens7f1 ovs-if-br-ex 5090ed3a-6dca-44b6-a31c-6c6539132c23 ovs-interface br-ex Wired Connection 5f123cb7-3abb-477a-8c29-55fa809f19b4 ethernet eno2np1 Wired Connection 5f123cb7-3abb-477a-8c29-55fa809f19b4 ethernet ens7f0 br-ex 45858fce-90a1-41d6-ae89-3437bac40a76 ovs-bridge br-ex ovs-if-phys0 7fd65994-e486-4f47-a18f-0f5e6e02c235 ethernet ens1f0 ovs-port-br-ex 214c5ade-fed8-4b3c-84f7-86e11397d6bb ovs-port br-ex ovs-port-phys0 9ec1d966-97a1-4334-a3ed-0400ec39ef1a ovs-port ens1f0 ~~~ This happens in systems with a default connection in NetworkManager, e.g. for IPI installations: ~~~ [core@worker-0 ~]$ sudo cat /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/default_connection.nmconnection [connection] id=Wired Connection uuid=5f123cb7-3abb-477a-8c29-55fa809f19b4 type=ethernet multi-connect=3 permissions= [ethernet] mac-address-blacklist= [ipv4] dns-search= method=auto [ipv6] addr-gen-mode=eui64 dns-search= method=auto [proxy] ~~~ This is particularly problematic if the VFs belong to the PF of the machine network interface, as they will get an additional lease on the machine network and thus will break node networking.
resolution: This is a known bug. See: * [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1896866](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1896866) * [https://github.com/openshift/sriov-network-operator/issues/414](https://github.com/openshift/sriov-network-operator/issues/414) * [https://github.com/openshift/sriov-network-operator/pull/415](https://github.com/openshift/sriov-network-operator/pull/415) ### Workaround Push the following workaround to all SR-IOV worker nodes, either manually or via a machine config: ~~~ # cat /etc/udev/rules.d/99-test.rules ACTION=="add|change|move", ATTRS{device}=="0x154c|0x1016|0x1018|0x101c|0x1014", ENV{NM_UNMANAGED}="1" ~~~
root_cause: For further details, see: [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1896866#c19](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1896866#c19)

title: [RFE] cluster subscription automation
issue: - As git-ops-minded DevOps-Team running OpenShift 4 in a fully automated fashion, it would be nice to be able to subscribe the clusters in a fully automated fashion.- Right now, the only documented way to subscribe OpenShift 4 clusters, is to go to [https://cloud.redhat.com/openshift](https://cloud.redhat.com/openshift), choose the cluster and edit the subscription settings. This is not a feasible approach to deploy and update clusters with 100% automation.- The minimum requirement would be to able to subscribe clusters via API calls. There already is https://api.openshift.com but it is not consistently documented and the way to subscribe clusters (patching the cluster's subscription section via API) seems pretty clumsy and inconvenient.- Is the API as to whether it is semantically versioned in a consequent fashion, meaning that is possible to rely on v1 not having any breaking changes at some point.- There should be one API call would be possible to do that and contains all the information to type into the web UI at cloud.redhat.com (service level, cluster purposes and so one) and then the cluster should be subscribed.- The perfect approach would be a subscription operator running in the OpenShift cluster that has a Subscription custom resource which then can be filled with all the necessary information to correctly subscribe the cluster. This way it would also be very easy and convenient to change subscription properties like the service level and have the change correctly applied immediately.

title: Update certificates in route using oc patch command
issue: - Unable to update route certificate and key using `oc patch` CLI.- Passing certificate file path in `oc patch` command does not add the certificate content in the route definition.
resolution: 1. Export certificate file path and the route name to variables: ~~~ $ export CRT_FN= $ export KEY_FN= $ export ROUTE= ~~~ 2. Export the content from the certificate files to the respective variables. ~~~ $ export CERTIFICATE="$(awk '{printf "%s\\n", $0}' ${CRT_FN})" $ export KEY="$(awk '{printf "%s\\n", $0}' ${KEY_FN})" ~~~ 3. Execute the patch command: ~~~ $ oc patch "route/${ROUTE}"-p '{"spec":{"tls":{"certificate":"'"${CERTIFICATE}"'","key":"'"${KEY}"'"}}}' ~~~

title: Readiness probes failing with 'exec failed: container'
issue: - Readiness probes for elastic search pods failing with following messages: ~~~ 1h 3h 2 logging-es-data-master-xxxx Pod spec.containers{elasticsearch} Warning Unhealthy kubelet, node Readiness probe failed: rpc error: code = 2 desc = oci runtime error: exec failed: container_linux.go:235: starting container process caused "process_linux.go:83: executing setns process caused \"exit status 15\""... 1h 7h 2 logging-es-data-master-xxxx Pod spec.containers{elasticsearch} Warning Unhealthy kubelet, node Readiness probe failed: rpc error: code = 2 desc = oci runtime error: exec failed: cannot exec a container that has run and stopped... 1h 1h 1 logging-es-data-master-xxxx Pod spec.containers{elasticsearch} Warning Unhealthy kubelet, node Readiness probe failed: rpc error: code = 2 desc = oci runtime error: exec failed: container " " does not exist ~~~
resolution: - Restart the respective pods. Here, considering the Elasticsearch pods: 1. Scale down the pod replicas to 0: ~~~ $ for dc in `oc get dc-o=name--selector=component=es`; do oc scale $dc--replicas=0; done ~~~ 2. Ensure that all the ES pods are terminated successfully. 3. Once terminated successfully, scale up the replicas back: ~~~ $ for dc in `oc get dc-o=name--selector=component=es`; do oc scale $dc--replicas=1; done ~~~ 4. Check the pod status of newly deployed pods and events: ~~~ $ oc get events-n openshift-logging $ oc get pods-owide-n openshift-logging ~~~
root_cause: - The following messages indicate that the command cannot be executed inside the containers, and so returning unhealthy pod status: ~~~ 1h 7h 2 logging-es-data-master-xxxx Pod spec.containers{elasticsearch} Warning Unhealthy kubelet, node Readiness probe failed: rpc error: code = 2 desc = oci runtime error: exec failed: cannot exec a container that has run and stopped. ~~~- It highlights that the container has been started and stopped already, before executing a command inside the container for readiness probe check.

title: OCS deployment gets stucks due to thin storage PVCs remain in pending state indefinitely
issue: - OCS deployment is stuck and `rook-ceph-mon-a-canary` pod keep restarting- `oc get events-n openshift-storage` reporting `pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims` for ceph-mon canary pod ~~~ 25m Warning FailedScheduling pod/rook-ceph-mon-a-canary-123456890ab-ccccc error while running "VolumeBinding" filter plugin for pod "rook-ceph-mon-a-canary-123456890ab-ccccc": pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims 24m Warning FailedScheduling pod/rook-ceph-mon-a-canary-123456890ab-ccccc skip schedule deleting pod: openshift-storage/rook-ceph-mon-a-canary-123456890ab-ccccc ~~~
resolution: 1. Make sure VMware user used by the cloud provider has read permission to view vSphere/vCenter task status. 2. Forcefully redeploy the `kube-controller-manager` which will make `Pending` PVC gets in to the `Bound` State. ~~~ $ oc patch kubecontrollermanager/cluster--type merge-p "{\"spec\":{\"forceRedeploymentReason\":\"Forcing new revision with random number $RANDOM to make message unique\"}}" ~~~ **Kindly note that you need to apply above workaround for every PVC creation which is getting stuck in `Pending` state**
root_cause: The permission mentioned in **[Openshift 4.4 Installation documentation- vSphere](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere.html#installation-required-vcenter-account-privileges_installing-vsphere)** are not sufficient and also it depends on how user and role was created on vSphere.

title: Grafana and Prometheus console gives 500 Internal Error
issue: - Unable to access Grafana and Prometheus console after changing the OCP's self signed certificate to `custom certificate`.- Error thrown in the `grafana-proxy` container: ~~~ oauthproxy.go:646: error redeeming code (client:10.11.10.1:36446): Post https://external-master-vip-name:8443/oauth/token: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority oauthproxy.go:439: ErrorPage 500 Internal Error Internal Error provider.go:372: authorizer reason: no RBAC policy matched ~~~
resolution: Follow the below steps: a. Append the CA certificate signing your custom certificates to `/etc/origin/master/ca-bundle.crt`. ~~~ # cat.crt > > /etc/origin/master/ca-bundle.crt ~~~ b. Restart the master-api and master-controllers. ~~~ # /usr/local/bin/master-restart api # /usr/local/bin/master-restart controllers ~~~
root_cause: The `CA bundle` didn't have the CA certificate which signed the custom certificates.

title: Fabric8 Maven Plug-in: "The API version in the data (v1) does not match the expected API version"

title: Topology Manager fails to assign VLAN for correct SR-IOV devices
issue: - While deploying a resource-aligned pod using Topology Manager feature, VLAN is not being set on the correct SRIOV device.
resolution: **There are two workarounds:**- Disable network-resource-injector by edit the default SriovOperatorConfig CR, there is an option called Injector, set it to false will disable network-resource-injector. Disabling network-resource-injector in this case where multiple containers requesting dpdk interfaces exist in one pod is recommended.- Put the only container `dpme` that requests resource as the first container in pod spec. which will prevent injector from wrongly injecting resources.
root_cause: - This is an issue of network-resource-injector (a daemon managed by sriov operator), it automatically configure the resource limit/request according to what's defined in pod net-attach-defs.- There is a known defect in network-rsource-injector that it only injects resource in the first container which may not be expected by user.

title: Why are no ceph-mgr standby instances running in an OpenShift Container Storage 4.x cluster?
issue: - Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage installs only one (1) `ceph-mgr` Pod by default.- From my general experience with "Ceph", the number of `ceph-mgr` processes should be at least three (3) to not have a single point of failure and to have "standby" `ceph-mgr` processes running.- How to properly add additional `ceph-mgr` Pods in Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage?
root_cause: - Since the 12.x ("Luminous") Ceph release (Red Hat Ceph Storage 3.x), the `ceph-mgr` daemon is required for normal operations.- Although I/O can continue when `ceph-mgr` is down, metrics will not refresh and some metrics-related calls (e.g., `ceph df`) may block..- In a traditional deployment of Red Hat Ceph Storage, it is best practice to deploy three (3) `ceph-mgr` on different hosts for reliability.- In Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage, Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform / kubernetes is responsible for keeping the `ceph-mgr` Pod running on one of the nodes. Even if there is a short outage, that should only lead to a short interruption in metrics collection and ceph status reporting.- In Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage, **it is sufficient and by design to only have one `ceph-mgr` Pod running.**
