title: How to share PVs between pods in OCP 4
issue: - Is it possible to subdivide a big PV to be used by several smaller PVCs?- For performance reasons, a big PV was created, and need to share between pods.
resolution: It's possible to use one PVC by several pods, but it's needed to highlight the following:- All the pods need to be in the same `namespace`, because PVCs are namespaced resources.- All the pods will be able to access to all the data in the PVC. There is an example in the OCP 3 documentation. This example is for a NFS volume, but can be modified to use other shared storage types.
root_cause: A PV can be only bounded to a PVC, and it's not possible to subdivide in multiple PVC.

title: How to test basic ingress connectivity issues
issue: - Connection to exposed applications are failing and want to diagnose the issue.
resolution: When trying to determine if your route is working or not, is helpful to perform a series of basic tests to understand the problem and potentially isolate it to an specific component. For that, we're going to perform a series of curl requests to the different steps in the chain. First of all, depending of the route tls configuration we may want to use different flags for our tests or the openssl client. Please adjust the examples accordingly to your configuration. For the example commands we take into account the following:- Namespace: `test-project`- Application name: `app`- HTTP Port: `80`- HTTPS Port: `443`- Route URL (http): `app-test-project.apps.cluster.com`- Route URL (https): `app-ssl-test-project.apps.cluster.com` Please remember to store the output of all commands in case your debugging ends up opening a support case so the engineer can easily take a look. ## Testing the route directly This is the simpler of all and most probably where you have detected a problem. We're going to make calls to the exposed routes directly. This assumes the route reaches the cluster directly, which may not be the case. If you have load balancers in front of Openshift set up, check the Load Balancers section below. ### HTTP ~~~ $ curl-Lkv ttp://app-test-project.apps.cluster.com/ #... < HTTP/1.0 200 OK #... ~~~ ### HTTPS ~~~ $ curl-Lkv https://app-ssl-test-project.apps.cluster.com/ #... < HTTP/1.0 200 OK #... ~~~ Test with Openssl client as well. Keep in mind that the lines for the request must be sent manually, after the debbuging output you will have the oportunity to type our request. ~~~ GET / HTTP/1.0 Host: app-ssl-test-project.apps.cluster.com ~~~ After a trailing newline we should see the response: ~~~ $ openssl s_client-crlf-connect:443-servername #... Start Time: 1614770813 Timeout: 300 (sec) Verify return code: 19 (self signed certificate in certificate chain)--- GET / HTTP/1.0 Host: app-ssl-test-project.apps.cluster.com HTTP/1.0 200 OK content-type: text/plain content-length: 1000 #... ~~~ ## Testing a router node directly In order to confirm we're reaching the router (HAProxy) directly, we're going to make the same test but using a node IP and the port where the router is serving. Get the IP from a node and the port the router for the ingress you're testing is serving for each approrpriate case: ~~~ $ oc get svc-n openshift-ingress NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE router-internal-default ClusterIP 172.30.198.173 80/TCP,443/TCP,1936/TCP 7d23h ~~~ ### HTTP ~~~ $ curl- Lv http://:80-H "Host: app-test-project.apps.cluster.com" ~~~ ### HTTPS ~~~ $ curl-Lkv https://: 443--resolve:443:app-ssl-test-project.apps.cluster.com $ openssl s_client-connect:443-servername app-ssl-test-project.apps.cluster.com ~~~ ## Testing the service endpoint If connection to the route worked, let's try out calling the service. Keep in mind that these commands must be run from a cluster node. First get where the service is being exposed: ~~~ $ oc get svc-n test-project NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE app ClusterIP 172.30.127.203 8080/TCP 102m ~~~ Then call the service using the appropriate method for the traffic the pod is exposing: ### HTTP ~~~ $ curl-Lv http://172.30.127.203:8080 #... < HTTP/1.0 200 OK #... ~~~ ### HTTPS ~~~ $ curl-Lkv https://172.30.127.203:8080 $ openssl s_client-connect 172.30.127.203:8080 ~~~ ## Testing the pod directly First of all let's launch a debug pod for our application: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n test-project NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE app-1-build 0/1 Completed 0 107m app-5cdc5f89db-gspwp 1/1 Running 0 106m $ oc debug pod/app-5cdc5f89db-gspwp Starting pod/app-5cdc5f89db-gspwp-debug... Pod IP: 10.131.0.76 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. (app-root) sh-4.2$ ~~~ ~~~ (app-root) sh-4.2$ curl-Lv app:8080 # Or https (app-root) sh-4.2$ curl-Lkv https://app:8080 ~~~ ## Check application logs Your application logs may algo contain clues as of what could be happening underneath so it's always good to check those. ~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE app-1-build 0/1 Completed 0 3h53m app-5cdc5f89db-gspwp 1/1 Running 0 3h51m $ oc logs app-5cdc5f89db-gspwp * Running on http://0.0.0.0:8080/ (Press CTRL+C to quit) 10.128.2.1-- [03/Mar/2021 10:59:52] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200- 10.128.2.1-- [03/Mar/2021 10:59:56] "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" 404- 10.128.2.1-- [03/Mar/2021 11:00:00] "GET /status HTTP/1.1" 404- 10.128.2.1-- [03/Mar/2021 11:00:03] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200- #... ~~~ ## Load balancers TODO Statement. We can't help with outside load balancers much, only provide sane defaults for them to work.

title: How to expose the Jaeger OpenTelemetry collector for use outside the OpenShift cluster.
issue: The Jaeger Operator creates a route for the Jaeger Query, exposing it to users outside of the OpenShift cluster, using the OpenShift OAuth proxy to do the user authentication. The Jaeger Collector, however, isn't exposed as it should typically be restricted to in-cluster consumers, like the pods running your workload. In some specific cases, the Jaeger Agent might be running outside of the cluster, requiring the Collector to be exposed.
resolution: To expose the Jaeger Collector outside the cluster, create a route similar to the example below: ~~~ kind: Route apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: simplest-collector namespace: default spec: host: simplest-collector-default.apps-crc.testing to: kind: Service name: simplest-collector weight: 100 port: targetPort: https-grpc tls: termination: passthrough insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: None ~~~ Note that the collector does *not* offer any authentication other than Mutual TLS at the moment. Make sure to provision a TLS client certificate for your Jaeger Agents, using your existing tooling. Configure your Jaeger custom resource to mount the corresponding secrets in the Jaeger Agent and Collector. Configure your Jaeger Agent by setting the following flags: ```--reporter.grpc.tls.enabled=true--reporter.grpc.tls.ca=/tmp/tls/ca.pem--reporter.grpc.tls.server-name=collector.example.net--reporter.grpc.tls.cert=/tmp/tls/client.pem--reporter.grpc.tls.key=/tmp/tls/client-key.pem ``` The flag `reporter.grpc.tls.ca` should point to the CA that signed the server certificate. This will be used by the Jaeger Agent to authenticate the server. The flag `reporter.grpc.tls.server-name` should be used only if the collector's hostname does not match the CN or the hostnames lised in the server certificate. The flag `reporter.grpc.tls.cert` should point to the client certificate. The flag `reporter.grpc.tls.key` should point to the client certificate's key. Configure your Jaeger Collector by setting the following flags: ```--collector.grpc.tls.enabled=true--collector.grpc.tls.cert=/tmp/tls/server.pem--collector.grpc.tls.key=/tmp/tls/server-key.pem--collector.grpc.tls.client-ca=/tmp/tls/ca.pem ``` The flag `collector.grpc.tls.cert` should point to the server's certificate. The flag `collector.grpc.tls.key` should point to the server certificate's key. The flag `collector.grpc.tls.client-ca` should point to the CA that signed the client certificates. WARNING: Failing to configure Mutual TLS for this use case means that your Collector might be open to accept data from the public internet. The following jaeger.yaml file provides an example of all of the agent and collector settings mentioned above. ~~~ # setup an elasticsearch with `make es` apiVersion: jaegertracing.io/v1 kind: Jaeger metadata: name: simple-prod spec: strategy: production storage: type: elasticsearch options: es: server-urls: http://elasticsearch.default.svc:9200 agent: options: reporter: grpc: tls: enabled: true ca: /custom-ca/ca.pem cert: /custom-tls/client.pem key: /custom-tls/client-key.pem volumes:- name: tlsvol-agent secret: secretName: agent-tls- name: tlsvol-ca-agent secret: secretName: custom-ca volumeMounts:- name: tlsvol-agent mountPath: "/custom-tls" readOnly: true- name: tlsvol-ca-agent mountPath: "/custom-ca" readOnly: true collector: options: collector: grpc: tls: enabled: true client-ca: /custom-ca/ca.pem cert: /custom-tls/server.pem key: /custom-tls/server-key.pem volumes:- name: tlsvol-collector secret: secretName: collector-tls- name: tlsvol-ca-collector secret: secretName: custom-ca volumeMounts:- name: tlsvol-collector mountPath: "/custom-tls" readOnly: true- name: tlsvol-ca-collector mountPath: "/custom-ca" readOnly: true ~~~

title: Why am I getting "Duplicate entry 'master-<username>' for key 'UK_RU8TT6T700S9V50BU18WS5HA6'" error?
issue: I run RH-SSO on Openshift and I found "Duplicate entry 'master- ' for key 'UK_RU8TT6T700S9V50BU18WS5HA6'" error is logged. What is the issue? Example log: ~~~ [0m [0m04:30:33,009 INFO [org.keycloak.services] (ServerService Thread Pool-- 55) KC-SERVICES0006: Importing users from '/opt/eap/standalone/configuration/keycloak-add-user.json' [0m [33m04:30:33,173 WARN [org.hibernate.engine.jdbc.spi.SqlExceptionHelper] (ServerService Thread Pool-- 55) SQL Error: 1062, SQLState: 23000 [0m [31m04:30:33,173 ERROR [org.hibernate.engine.jdbc.spi.SqlExceptionHelper] (ServerService Thread Pool-- 55) Duplicate entry 'master- ' for key 'UK_RU8TT6T700S9V50BU18WS5HA6' [0m [31m04:30:33,184 ERROR [org.keycloak.services] (ServerService Thread Pool-- 55) KC-SERVICES0010: Failed to add user ' ' to realm 'master': user with username exists ~~~
root_cause: RH-SSO deployed on OpenShift by template automatically tries to add an initial user, but since the addition is tried every time when RH-SSO pod start up, from the second time and onwards, the error always occur as an user already exists in RH-SSO. See [KEYCLOAK-7563](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/KEYCLOAK-7563) for more details. You can ignore the error as it doesn't have any side effects.

title: oauth-proxy CORS problem
issue: If an oauth-proxy sidecar is used for authentication the first authentication works perfectly well. However, if a cookie refresh is due, the user sees only a blank page. When hitting the browser reload button the user is redirected to the OCP login screen again and reaches the application with all information after successful atuhentication.
resolution: Hi Tobias, thanks for your hints in the right direction. The frontend uses nginx with proxy-pass to access the backend running in the same namespace (dashboard-frontend, dashboard-backend). Here I added the following lines to the nginx.conf that is copied in the Dockerfile to the image created: ``` location / {add_header "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" *; try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html =404;} location /ocp/api/ {proxy_set_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin *; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; proxy_set_header Host $http_host; proxy_pass http://dashboard-backend:8080;} ``` I bet it will be possible to restrict the allowance further ("*" is not ideal from a security perspective) but I'm just too tired now to test further and just happy that it works now. Please close and archive this case.
root_cause: Hej Andreas, hej Madd, were you successful with changing the annotation or adding the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://oauth-openshift.apps.s01.cmpf.schwarz` directive to the dashboard server? Cheers Tobias We installed a customer web application and are using the OCP oauth-proxy as a sidecar to authenticate before reaching the frontend. This works fine when we hit the link (for example bookmark) to the application. The user is redirected to OCP login and after successful authentication redirected to the frontend. But after the cookie expires (we set this to 15 minutes for security reasons with the '--cookie-expire=15m' argument) the click to the bookmark link will then open the frontend with no dynamic information form openshift. As we see in the web-console the access is tried but denied for CORS reasons: ``` Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'https://oauth-openshift.apps.p04.cmpf.schwarz/oauth/authorize?approval_prompt=force&client_id=system%3Aserviceaccount%3Asit-dashboard%3Aproxy&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fdashboard.apps.p04.cmpf.schwarz%2Foauth%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=user%3Acheck-access+user%3Ainfo+user%3Alist-projects&state=4686a450fe7d6c6b532cd3f90618f364%3A%2Focp%2Fapi%2Fv1%2Fuser' (redirected from 'https://dashboard.apps.p04.cmpf.schwarz/ocp/api/v1/user') from origin 'https://dashboard.apps.p04.cmpf.schwarz' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource. ```

title: How to notify the difference between Local time and RTC time in timedatectl
issue: - As [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5017611](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5017611) says, In RHEL8, `timedatectl` can not be used to check 11 minutes mode is on and working or not.- Command `timedatectl` reports "System clock synchronized: yes" even if "rtcsync" is commented in /etc/chrony.conf.- In this situation, As one of workarounds,we can check if 11 minutes mode is working by monitoring Local time and RTC time ~~~ # timedatectl Local time: Tue 2020-01-21 15:45:55 JST Universal time: Tue 2020-01-21 06:45:55 UTC RTC time: Tue 2020-01-21 06:45:54 Time zone: Asia/Tokyo (JST, +0900) System clock synchronized: yes NTP service: active RTC in local TZ: no ~~~- Do we have a tool to monitor Local time and RTC time?
resolution: You can use a took like # How to use this script ~~~ # cat check_timedatectl.sh #!/bin/bash # # This tool monitors "RTC time" and "Local time". # # Author: Red Hat # License: MIT # #set-e #DEFAULT_LOG=/var/log/${0}.log PROG=$0 function show_help () {cat < < EOH Usage: $0 [Options...] Options:-s Log to syslog.-h Show this help.-d Show debug. EOH} function show_debug () {if [${debug_mode:=off} == "on"] then echo $save echo ####################### echo local_date $local_date echo local_time $local_time echo l_tz $l_tz echo rtc_date $rtc_date echo rtc_time $rtc_time echo t_zone_c $t_zone_c echo t_zone_m $t_zone_m echo s_mark $s_mark echo t_zone_t $t_zone_t echo ####################### fi} function show_timedatectl () {LANG=C timedatectl | sed 's/^[\t]*//'} function comp_parm {param_1=$1 param_2=$2 value_1=$(eval echo "$""${param_1}") value_2=$(eval echo "$""${param_2}") if [${value_1}!= ${value_2}] then mesg="[${PROG}]: Warning: detected the diffrence in timedatectl: ${param_1}=${value_1} and ${param_2}=${value_2}" output_log "$mesg" fi} function output_log () {log_message=$1 if [-n "${log_message}"] then if [${syslog_mode:=off} == "on"] then logger $log_message else echo $log_message fi fi} while getopts k:sdh OPT do case "${OPT}" in s) syslog_mode=on;; d) debug_mode=on;; h) show_help; exit 0;; \?) echo "Invalid option!"; exit 1;; esac done shift $((OPTIND- 1)) # Store the output of timedatectl save=$(show_timedatectl) # Parse the output of timedatectl local_date=$(echo $save | awk '{print $4}') local_time=$(echo $save | awk '{print $5}') l_tz=$(echo $save | awk '{print $6}') rtc_date=$(echo $save | awk '{print $16}') rtc_time=$(echo $save | awk '{print $17}') t_zone_c=$(echo $save | awk '{print $20}' | sed-e s/\(//-e s/,//) t_zone_m=$(echo $save | awk '{print $21}' | sed-e s/\(//-e s/,//) s_mark=$(echo $save | awk '{print $22}' | sed-e s/\(//-e s/,// | cut-c 1) t_zone_t=$(echo $save | awk '{print $22}' | sed-e s/\)//) show_debug # Compare Local date and RTC date comp_parm local_date rtc_date # Compare Local time and RTC time comp_parm local_time rtc_time # Compare Time zone comp_parm l_tz t_zone_m ~~~

title: "oc image mirror -f file.txt" to quay fails with "ErrCode=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM"
issue: Using `oc image mirror-f file.txt` to mirror images to a quay instance with ~117 images instance results in ~~~ http2: server sent GOAWAY and closed the connection; LastStreamID=1, ErrCode=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, debug="" ~~~
resolution: **Workaround**: To work around the issue, you can split the mirror workload in chunks of 20 images per run like this: Assuming there is a `mirror.txt` with many (> 20) images to mirror, the following command can be used to split the workload in chunks: ~~~ [shell ~]$ split mirror.txt-l 20 mirror.split. [shell ~]$ for i in mirror.split.*; do oc image mirror-a pull-secret.json-f $i; done ~~~
root_cause: * Currently the `oc` command line interface requests a token with a scope covering all repositories that are going to be mirrored. This creates a huge token, that is then injected into the request using the `Authorization:` header. The size of the header field then exceeds the typical maximum size of reverse proxies (typically 4/8k) and thus the request fails.

title: "Secure" or "SameSite" attributes cookies for the HAProxy router in OpenShift
issue: - The HAproxy version shipped in OpenShift Container Platform to expose `Route`objects does not support adding attributes like "Secure" or "SameSite" to the issued routing cookies (used to re-target pods).- Modern web browsers (e.g.: Google Chrome) are changing the default behavior for how cookies will be sent in first and third party contexts. As a result, the sticky sessions configured in HAproxy will no longer work.- Any cookies used by a site will be considered as third-party cookies when the site is displayed within the frame.- For cookies needed in a third-party context, it will be required to ensure they are marked as `SameSite=None; Secure`.
resolution: - For OCP 3.11 this was fixed on [this ERRATA](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2020:5107)- For OCP 4.x this was fixed on the version 4.6- If you are affected by this issue, please open a support case with [Red Hat support](https://access.redhat.com/support) for further assistance.- As the route needs to be annotated with the `haproxy.router.openshift.io/cookie-same-site` annotation the [official documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.6/html/networking/configuring-routes#nw-route-specific-annotations_route-configuration) needs to be checked regarding supported settings.- If you are using customized router templates in OCP 3.11 as described in our documentation section [Deploying a Customized HAProxy Router](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/3.11/html/configuring_clusters/setting-up-a-router#install-config-router-customized-haproxy), you need to update the customized template to make use of this feature.

title: Supportablity matrix for Openshift EUS and timelines
issue: - What is time line to receive updates from the EUS?- Which subscriptions are required to receive EUS updates?- What is the channel name to receive EUS updates for Openshift?
resolution: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/updating/updating-cluster-between-minor.html#understanding-upgrade-channels_updating-cluster-between-minor https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift-eus
root_cause: When OpenShift Container Platform 4.6 transitions to the EUS phase of its lifecycle the stable-4.6 channel will no longer receive subsequent z-stream updates. After you upgrade to a version that is exclusive to the EUS channel, that cluster will no longer be eligible for minor version upgrades until upgrades to the next EUS version become available. The next planned EUS version is to be 4.10 and the upgrade to that version will require a serial set of version upgrades, such as from 4.6 to 4.7 to 4.8 to 4.9 to 4.10. Additionally, you may only switch to the EUS channel when your cluster is running a supported version of OpenShift Container Platform 4.6.

title: Nessus scanners are finding TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 enabled for the Docker API on TCP ports in Openshift Container Platform 3.11
issue: Nessus scanners are finding TLSv1.0 enabled for the Docker API, for example, on port TCP/4243 (finding 104743), so it is needed to check how it is possible to disable TLSv1.0 for the Docker API, and TLSv1.1 as well. Docker was installed via the RHEL yum repository and the API needs to be available on the network for automation purposes. While we have secured the API using mutual cert authentication, the vulnerability still needs to be remedied, either via configuration, an update to a version that allows you to disable TLSv1.0 (and possibly TLSv1.1), or via risk documentation if there is no remedy available.
resolution: Docker by default does not listen on any TCP ports, so the vulnerability is not exploitable, as Docker, instead, is defaulting to a root-owned UNIX socket. This can be changed to include a TCP socket but we don't recommend it, as this exposes security concerns as any user that can access the Docker socket can, by definition of a root-full daemon, execute a privileged container and gain root access to the host. Regarding the TLS version offered on the socket; Red Hat builds the latest version of Docker with go1.10.3 which does include support for tls1.2. However, the implementation of the Docker API does not allow any options passed that will allow for changing the minimum accepted TLS version of 1.0. To allow for a MinVersion to be specified as per the Go language tls package, we'd need to implement a tls.Config structure and define MinVersion as it is done so for this ServerDefault: ~~~ // ServerDefault is a secure-enough TLS configuration for the server TLS configuration. var ServerDefault = tls.Config{// Avoid fallback to SSL protocols < TLS1.0 MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS10, PreferServerCipherSuites: true, CipherSuites: DefaultServerAcceptedCiphers,} ~~~ We apply this ServerDefault to our TLS server configuration: ~~~ // Server returns a TLS configuration meant to be used by a server. func Server(options Options) (*tls.Config, error) {tlsConfig:= ServerDefault tlsConfig.ClientAuth = options.ClientAuth tlsCert, err:= tls.LoadX509KeyPair(options.CertFile, options.KeyFile) if err!= nil {if os.IsNotExist(err) {return nil, fmt.Errorf("Could not load X509 key pair (cert: %q, key: %q): %v", options.CertFile, options.KeyFile, err)} return nil, fmt.Errorf("Error reading X509 key pair (cert: %q, key: %q): %v. Make sure the key is not encrypted.", options.CertFile, options.KeyFile, err)} tlsConfig.Certificates = []tls.Certificate{tlsCert} if options.ClientAuth > = tls.VerifyClientCertIfGiven {CAs, err:= certPool(options.CAFile) if err!= nil {return nil, err} tlsConfig.ClientCAs = CAs} return &tlsConfig, nil} ~~~ When we start the `dockerd` service, we call tlsconfig.Server, which does not allow for any specification: ~~~ func (cli *DaemonCli) start() (err error) {---- 8 <---- if cli.Config.TLS {tlsOptions:= tlsconfig.Options{CAFile: cli.Config.CommonTLSOptions.CAFile, CertFile: cli.Config.CommonTLSOptions.CertFile, KeyFile: cli.Config.CommonTLSOptions.KeyFile,} if cli.Config.TLSVerify {// server requires and verifies client's certificate tlsOptions.ClientAuth = tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert} tlsConfig, err:= tlsconfig.Server(tlsOptions) if err!= nil {return err} serverConfig.TLSConfig = tlsConfig} ~~~ And the editable "Options" structure has no way to specify or pass a MinVersion that could be picked up by the underlying tls.Config. ~~~ // Options represents the information needed to create client and server TLS configurations. type Options struct {CAFile string // If either CertFile or KeyFile is empty, Client() will not load them // preventing the client from authenticating to the server. // However, Server() requires them and will error out if they are empty. CertFile string KeyFile string // client-only option InsecureSkipVerify bool // server-only option ClientAuth tls.ClientAuthType} ~~~ This being said, it doesn't seem this is possible to do with Docker. In addition, Red Hat is moving away from utilizing or developing Docker, instead moving to other utilities such as podman, skopeo, buildah, or cri-o for Red Hat OpenShift. Docker and all of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 have entered Maintenance Phase 2 where only security updates are being considered for inclusion: ~~~ https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/errata#Maintenance_Support_2_Phase Unfortunately, adding this functionality to Docker is not something we can do at this time, so Requests for Enhancement are denied. ~~~ As an alternative, Red Hat recommends that you switch Docker to use UNIX-only sockets, and if you absolutely need your Docker service to be accessible over TCP/HTTP with TLS, you could set up an nginx proxy that would take incoming HTTPS requests, decrypt them, and forward them on to Docker's UNIX socket. With nginx, you can absolutely limit the accepted TLS versions.

title: Docker slowness issue while having low CPU usage and network I/O being healthy in Openshift Container Platform 3.11 with AWS ENA driver: troubleshooting.
issue: ENA is the Amazon Network driver and the application that is running slow is in a docker container.
resolution: The Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) is designed to improve operating system health and reduce the chances of long-term disruption because of unexpected hardware behavior and or failures. The ENA architecture keeps device or driver failures as transparent to the system as possible. This topic provides troubleshooting information for ENA. Usually, from RHEL perspective, it is possible to load the module temporarily without restarting the instance to see if it is loading correctly: ~~~ #insmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-xxxx/kernel/drivers/net/ethernet/amazon/ena/ena.ko.xz # lsmod | grep ena ~~~ If there are no errors, driver is getting loaded without any issues. Extra steps are needed to enable ENA on a amazon instance. ~~~ After doing a insmod of the driver, perform the below: # depmod (Regenerate kernel module dependency map files) # echo 'add_drivers+=" ena "' > > /etc/dracut.conf.d/ena.conf # dracut-f-v (Generate the new initrd image) # lsinitrd /boot/initramfs-xxx.el7.x86_64.img | grep ena.ko (Validate that the initramfs image contains the ena driver) ~~~ If you lose connectivity while enabling enhanced networking, the ena module might be incompatible with your instance's current running kernel. This can happen if you install the module for a specific kernel version (without dkms, or with an improperly configured dkms.conf file) and then your instance kernel is updated. If the instance kernel that is loaded at boot time does not have the ena module properly installed, your instance will not recognize the network adapter and your instance becomes unreachable. ~~~ If you enable enhanced networking for a PV instance or AMI, this can also make your instance unreachable. If your instance becomes unreachable after enabling enhanced networking with ENA, you can disable the enaSupport attribute for your instance and it will fall back to the stock network adapter. To disable enhanced networking with ENA (EBS-backed instances) From your local computer, stop the instance using the Amazon EC2 console or one of the following commands: stop-instances (AWS CLI), Stop-EC2Instance (AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell). If your instance is managed by AWS OpsWorks, you should stop the instance in the AWS OpsWorks console so that the instance state remains in sync. Important If you are using an instance store-backed instance, you can't stop the instance. Instead, proceed to To disable enhanced networking with ENA (instance store-backed instances). From your local computer, disable the enhanced networking attribute using the following command. modify-instance-attribute (AWS CLI) $ aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute--instance-id instance_id--no-ena-support From your local computer, start the instance using the Amazon EC2 console or one of the following commands: start-instances (AWS CLI), Start-EC2Instance (AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell). If your instance is managed by AWS OpsWorks, you should start the instance in the AWS OpsWorks console so that the instance state remains in sync. (Optional) Connect to your instance and try reinstalling the ena module with your current kernel version by following the steps in Enable enhanced networking with the Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) on Linux instances. To disable enhanced networking with ENA (instance store-backed instances) If your instance is an instance store-backed instance, create a new AMI as described in Create an instance store-backed Linux AMI. Be sure to disable the enhanced networking enaSupport attribute when you register the AMI. register-image (AWS CLI) $ aws ec2 register-image--no-ena-support... ~~~ The ENA device posts keep-alive events at a fixed rate (usually once every second). The ENA driver implements a watchdog mechanism, which checks for the presence of these keep-alive messages. If a message or messages are present, the watchdog is rearmed, otherwise the driver concludes that the device experienced a failure and then does the following: ~~~ Dumps its current statistics to syslog Resets the ENA device Resets the ENA driver state The above reset procedure may result in some traffic loss for a short period of time (TCP connections should be able to recover), but should not otherwise affect the user. The ENA device may also indirectly request a device reset procedure, by not sending a keep-alive notification, for example, if the ENA device reaches an unknown state after loading an irrecoverable configuration. Below is an example of the reset procedure: [18509.800135] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: Keep alive watchdog timeout. // The watchdog process initiates a reset [18509.815244] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: Trigger reset is on [18509.825589] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: tx_timeout: 0 // The driver logs the current statistics [18509.834253] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: io_suspend: 0 [18509.842674] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: io_resume: 0 [18509.850275] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: wd_expired: 1 [18509.857855] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: interface_up: 1 [18509.865415] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: interface_down: 0 [18509.873468] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: admin_q_pause: 0 [18509.881075] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: queue_0_tx_cnt: 0 [18509.888629] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: queue_0_tx_bytes: 0 [18509.895286] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: queue_0_tx_queue_stop: 0............... [18511.280972] ena 0000:00:07.0 eth1: free uncompleted tx skb qid 3 idx 0x7 // At the end of the down process, the driver discards incomplete packets. [18511.420112] [ENA_COM: ena_com_validate_version] ena device version: 0.10 //The driver begins its up process [18511.420119] [ENA_COM: ena_com_validate_version] ena controller version: 0.0.1 implementation version 1 [18511.420127] [ENA_COM: ena_com_admin_init] ena_defs: Version:[b9692e8] Build date [Wed Apr 6 09:54:21 IDT 2016] [18512.252108] ena 0000:00:07.0: Device watchdog is Enabled [18512.674877] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 46 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.674933] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 47 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.674990] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 48 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.675037] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 49 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.675085] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 50 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.675141] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 51 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.675188] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 52 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.675233] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 53 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.675279] ena 0000:00:07.0: irq 54 for MSI/MSI-X [18512.772641] [ENA_COM: ena_com_set_hash_function] Feature 10 isn't supported [18512.772647] [ENA_COM: ena_com_set_hash_ctrl] Feature 18 isn't supported [18512.775945] ena 0000:00:07.0: Device reset completed successfully // The reset process is complete ~~~

title: How to get the Router Access logs in an external Syslog server.
issue: - How to get the `Router Access logs` in an external Syslog server.
resolution: - The `Router access logs` are part of [infrastructure logs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/logging/cluster-logging.html) in cluster logging.- To get `Router Access logs`, first step is to [configure Ingress access logging](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/networking/ingress-operator.html#nw-configure-ingress-access-logging_configuring-ingress) in `OpenShift` cluster.- Then ensure that [log forwarding to external Syslog resource](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/logging/cluster-logging-external.html#cluster-logging-collector-log-forward-syslog_cluster-logging-external) is working.- Now, to get these `Router Access logs` in the external `Syslog` resource, the `syslog` section settings in `ClusterLogForwarder` should look like below: ~~~ spec: outputs:- name: mysyslog syslog: rfc: RFC5424 facility: local0 severity: debug type: syslog url: XXXX.XX.XX.XX:XXX ~~~- Ensure that a proper pipeline is created for `infrastructure logs` to be forwarded to `External Syslog` server. ~~~ pipelines:- inputRefs:- infrastructure <---------- name: logs outputRefs:- mysyslog <----------- default ~~~- Once the external `Syslog` server start getting logs as per the above settings, verify if `Router access logs` are getting captured in the below way: 1) Get Container Id of `logs` named container of router pods in `openshift-ingress` namespace. ~~~ $ oc describe pods-n openshift-ingress | grep title: Virtual Machine cannot boot on RHV with default chipset Q35
issue: - Imported Windows virtual machine with recover menu inside the guest when starting with cluster default chipset (Q35).
resolution: - Either use another chipset like 440FX and set it as a custom chipset for the VM.- Or refresh the drivers on Windows guest. First, boot the VM with SATA/IDE disk type, remove old RHV drivers, and install a new one. Once new drivers are installed, shift back to virtio type disk instead of SATA/IDE.
root_cause: - Windows OS was unable to support the old drivers on the new chipset.

title: Status of the master node is NotReady due to the error `failed to create listener: failed to listen on 0.0.0.0:8443: listen tcp4 0.0.0.0:8443: bind: address already in use`
issue: - The master node is in the NotReady state.- Docker and atomic-openshift-node services are running.
resolution: - kill-9 `Parent Process ID`- Restart master API and controller. ~~~ /usr/local/bin/master-restart api api /usr/local/bin/master-restart controllers controllers ~~~
root_cause: - Old master-API process was not exited correctly and the docker lost the reference that it is actually a container running; like a rouge container without any supervision.

title: Failure creating Fluentd Daemonset in openshift-logging.
issue: - Failure creating Fluentd Daemonset in openshift-logging.- No Fluentd pods are running in openshift-logging and Fluentd Daemonset also not found.- Cluster logging Operator pod logs shows below messages: ~~~ 2021-03-25T13:00:29.697750323Z {"component":"cluster-logging-operator","error":{"msg":"Unable to create or update collection for \"instance\": Failure creating Fluentd Daemonset DaemonSet.apps \"fluentd\" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[16].mountPath: Invalid value: \"/var/run/ocp-collector/secrets/fluentd\": must be unique"},"level":"0","message":"Error reconciling clusterlogging instance","ts":"2021-03-25T13:00:29.697660927Z"} ~~~
resolution: - Remove internal Elasticsearch's details mentioned in the spec output section in ClusterLogForwarder ~~~- name: elasticsearch <-----| secret: | name: fluentd | Remove this section type: elasticsearch | url: https://elasticsearch.openshift-logging.svc:9200 <-----| ~~~
root_cause: - In the spec output section in ClusterLogForwarder, mention only the external log forwarder details.- To put logs in internal ES or see logs in (internal) kibana, use `- default` in outputRefs section of the needed log type in pipelines. ~~~ pipelines:- inputRefs:- application name: container-logs outputRefs:- default <-------- external-log-forwarding ~~~

title: Failed to provision volume with StorageClass "thin": No VM found
issue: - Unable to create PVCs in the OCP cluster deployed on VMware vSphere using `thin` StorageClass.- Dynamic Provisioning of volumes using `thin` StorageClass is failing with `No VM found` error.- PVC stuck into Pending state and reports the following error. ~~~ Warning ProvisioningFailed persistentvolumeclaim/test-pvc1 Failed to provision volume with StorageClass "thin": No VM found ~~~
resolution: - Verify that the correct folder name is specified in the `cloud-provider-config` ConfigMap. If folder name is incorrect then edit the `cloud-provider-config` ConfigMap and mention the correct folder name. Wait for few minutes until the changes have been applied to all the cluster nodes and test the Dynamic Provisioning again. ~~~ $ oc edit cm cloud-provider-config-n openshift-config.... [Workspace] server = "xxxxx.xxxxx.xxxxx" datacenter = "xxxxx" default-datastore = "xxxxx" folder = "xxxxx" <----- Verify the folder name.... ~~~
root_cause: - In the `cloud-provider-config` ConfigMap folder name was incorrect.

title: Failed to pull the image using Imagestream
issue: - Error deploying pod using imagestream: ~~~ 1s Warning Failed pod/prometheus-thanos-0 Failed to pull image "oauth-proxy:release": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error reading manifest release in docker.io/library/oauth-proxy: errors: ~~~- Node searches the image on 'docker.io' due to default search parameters.
resolution: - There are two ways to enable imagestreams with Kubernetes resources:- Enabling imagestream resolution on a specific resource. This allows only this resource to use the imagestream name in the image field.- Enabling imagestream resolution on an imagestream. This allows all resources pointing to this imagestream to use it in the image field.- Use oc set image-lookup to enable imagestream resolution on a specific resource or imagestream resolution on an imagestream. ~~~ $ oc set image-lookup ~~~- To allow the Kubernetes deployment named mysql to use imagestreams, run the following command: ~~~ $ oc set image-lookup deploy/mysql ~~~
root_cause: - When using imagestreams with Kubernetes resources, you can only reference imagestreams that reside in the same project as the resource. The imagestream reference must consist of a single segment value, for example ruby:2.5, where ruby is the name of an imagestream that has a tag named 2.5 and resides in the same project as the resource making the reference.

title: Missing kernel-headers from Openshift node the after upgrading to 4.6
issue: - Error while building images "Your kernel headers for kernel 4.18.0-193.41.1.el8_2.x86_64 cannot be found at /lib/modules/4.18.0-193.41.1.el8_2.x86_64/build or /lib/modules/4.18.0-193.41.1.el8_2.x86_64/source"- Unable to get kernel-headers after update in the openshift node.- Third party modules which requires compilation using kernel-headers like falco/sysdig.
resolution: - Issue had been reported to Red Hat as 1888853 and it has been fixed by ERRATA in Openshift 4.6.6: [RHBA-2020:5115](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2020:5115)
root_cause: Sysdig is composed of two parts: the kernel driver, sysdig-probe, responsible for extracting system events from the kernel, and the userspace programs, sysdig and csysdig. Sysdig-probe, being a kernel module, must be compiled against the exact same kernel that is running in your host. Usually, for traditional Linux distributions, this task is easily accomplished by installing a C compiler and the headers for the running kernel. Generally, this is all automated using the dkms framework, which sysdig depends on. However, when you run sysdig inside a Docker container, you are essentially running a completely different runtime inside the container, and getting the kernel headers of the host runtime is not always an easy task. Previously, depending on the host OS, there have been two general approaches we’ve taken to solving this problem for sysdig: 1. Having the user manually install the kernel headers for the running kernel in the host and bind mount them when starting the Docker container. 2. Precompiling sysdig-probe for every possible kernel version on our side, and downloading it at runtime into the container during the bootstrap phase. For some distributions, such as CoreOS and Atomic Host, the first option is not possible, because the kernel headers are not available in the host, since it completely lacks a package manager. With this new 0.1.103 release of sysdig, we are now precompiling all the sysdig-probe kernel modules for all the kernels officially released by RHEL, Fedora, CentOS and Ubuntu. This has the following benefits: 1. It is now possible to use the sysdig Docker container on distributions that don’t ship kernel headers (such as Atomic Host). 2. For distributions that normally ship kernel headers (e.g. Ubuntu, CentOS, Fedora, … in their traditional versions), installing the kernel headers in the host is most likely not necessary anymore*, simplifying the whole sysdig installation process.

title: Allowing cluster-admin to specify the `kube-apiserver` rollout time
issue: - The kube-apiserver rollout will happen automatically when its certifications are rotated. Currently, this may happen at anytime, depending on the expiration time of certifications. The user command may fail during the kube-apiserver rollout. Especially, in case the user is running commands that take a long time, for example, when running "oc rsync" or "oc cp" to collect application data. The user would like to avoid the kube-apiserver rolling out in those times.
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and is tracking this issue in the following Feature-Request.- [RFE-1668](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1668)

title: MongoDB removed from OpenShift 4.6
resolution: - MongoDB templates removed.- All MongoDB-based samples have been replaced, deprecated, or removed.- MongoDB changed their licensing to the `Server Side Public License` [1], which Red Hat does not consider a truly free, open-source license. As a result, we can't even ship security patches without violating the license. [1] https://www.mongodb.com/licensing/server-side-public-license

title: Why users are getting 40+ character string username while setup Azure AD (Office 365) IDP with Openshift4?
issue: - After login to OpenShift web-console username is displaying 40+ character string username instead of an actual username.
resolution: - During configuration keep the IDP mapping as follows: ~~~ email: email name: name preferred_username: email ~~~
root_cause: - The `random` looking `40+ character` names are the IDP user name which is similar in the OpenShift identity resource for the user.- The reason used is `upn` is being used as the `preferred_username`.- The name field is the value that a person enters as their display name when accepting the invite to the Azure AD.

title: Is the warning mechanism for use of deprecated APIs available on OpenShift 4?
resolution: - [This feature was implemented for Kubernetes 1.20](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1693) and therefore it is available on OpenShift from version **4.7** onwards.- This mechanism throws a warning message when a deprecated API is trying to be used. Output example: ~~~ Warning: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1 ClusterRoleBinding is deprecated in v1.17+, unavailable in v1.22+; ~~~

title: Image Registry can be deactivated
issue: Can we deactivated Image Registry on OCP 4.6- Is it mandatory to use the image-registry?- In case we don´t use the image-registry, we will have any problem with Red Hat operators support?
resolution: The Image Registry Operator installs a single instance of the OpenShift Container Platform registry, and manages all registry configuration, including setting up registry storage.- Is it mandatory to use the image-registry? You can disable the internal registry by using the internal registry operator. On platforms that do not provide shareable object storage, the OpenShift Image Registry Operator bootstraps itself as *Removed*- In case we don´t use the image-registry, we will have any problem with Red Hat operators support? As long as you don't use the ImageStream API or rely on Operators that use it it should be fine.

title: Fine grain Jenkins user permissions
issue: - We wanted to give developers access only to their application job in the Jenkins. What level access we can provide?- Restrict users on Jenkins so that they can only view and run specific jobs
resolution: - To restrict users on Jenkins so that they can only view and run specific jobs Go to Manage Jenkins > Configure Global Security > Under Authorization Strategy > Select the checkbox for Project-based Matrix Authorization Strategy In the matrix, select something similar to below:- User/group Authenticated user- Read #adminuser- Administer Go to View > Pipeline > Select pipeline > Configure > Under General 1. Enable project-based security 2. Set inheritance strategy to do not inherit 3. Add the user id and the desired permissions

resolution: **Kindly contact Red Hat Ceph Storage support team for further investigation of this issue** If all PGs are `active+clean` state, kindly re-deploy the OSD daemon which is getting killed by `oom-killer`.
root_cause: The `ceph-osd` daemon consuming more than 5 GB (default memory limit for pod) of memory was primarily due to left over PGs from deleted pool. The root cause was not possible to conclude due to insufficient data for investigation of this issue.

title: Does a VMware vCenter appliance upgrade affect Openshift Container Storage?
issue: Does vCenter upgrade impact OCS storage?
What are the best practices for updating vCenter on a VMware datacenter hosting OCS nodes?
resolution: * vCenter upgrades should not affect the Running nodes. * As long as the OCS nodes are in Running state, the clients should be able to access storage. * **NOTE:** The update should not make any authentication changes or any changes to node IPs/hostnames.

title: Alertmanager pod crashes with "field hipchat_api_url not found in type config.plain".
issue: - Alertmamager pod is in crshloopbackoff with below error in the logs: ~~~ level=error ts=2021-04-10T05:11:06.426Z caller=coordinator.go:124 component=configuration msg="Loading configuration file failed" file=/etc/alertmanager/config/alertmanager.yaml err="yaml: unmarshal errors:\n line 7: field hipchat_api_url not found in type config.plain" ~~~
resolution: - As a workaround we can try editing the `alertmanager-main` secret (this is mounted as a volume by the alertmanager pod) and remove the `hipchat_api_url` line. If necessary delete crashed alertmanager pods to force the scheduler to re-create them. To do the same follow below steps, 1. First get the current alertmanager-config using below: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-monitoring get secret alertmanager-main--template='{{index.data "alertmanager.yaml"}}' |base64-d > alertmanager.yaml ~~~ 2. Remove the `hipchat_api_url` line in the alertmanager.yaml file. 3. Apply the new configuration file using below command: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-monitoring create secret generic alertmanager-main--from-file=alertmanager.yaml--dry-run-o=yaml | oc-n openshift-monitoring replace secret--filename=- ~~~ 4. Check if the pods got redeployed, if not please delete them and they should be re-created with the new config. ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n ~~~
root_cause: - There is no more support for hipchat in Alertmanager version 0.21.0- The secret used to create "/etc/alertmanager/config/alertmanager.yaml" should reflect the HipChat removal

title: Machine Config Pool apply stucked on unable to terminate POD
issue: - Applying MCP after compliance-operator scan with auto remediation stuck on failure to terminate oauth-openshift POD- Pod stuck in terminating, pod stuck in container-creating state.- When pod is created, then deleted before ready, pod is stuck terminating.- Why kubelet logs shows below message log: ~~~ kubelet_pods.go:980] Pod "console-66d476cf7c-l4ppm" is terminated, but pod cgroup sandbox has not been cleaned up. ~~~
resolution: [Bug# 1943564](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1943564) has been raised with the engineering team to understand the issue further, as MCO failed to drain the node with the pending pod. There is existing [Bug#1903228](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1903228) that engineering team is working on the fix.
root_cause: - Pod is scheduled on a node but stuck in pending State (waiting on the containerCreating state) and it never started. When the MC is getting applied to the machine, Machine config operator marked the machine as node degraded as its failed to drain that node because of this pending pod.- When pod is created, then deleted before ready, pod is stuck terminating state and its blocking the node drain while MCO is trying to apply the new machine- config.

title: Unable to provision/Install Openshift 4.7 on AWS with error "Internal error: listing instance types"
issue: - Unable to install Openshift on the AWS with below error: ~~~ Internal error: listing instance types: fetching instance types: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation. ~~~
resolution: - IAM user is required to be added with permission of "ec2:DescribeInstancetypes" which is not documented in Red Hat official Installation [doc](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/installing/installing_aws/installing-aws-account.html#installation-aws-permissions_installing-aws-account)- Red Hat Bug [1944963](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1944963) is filled to fix the documentation to include above permission.
root_cause: - For Openshift 4.7 "ec2:DescribeInstancetypes" is required to complete installation.

title: Creating Addition Users on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Nodes
issue: - Need to create additional users on nodes of a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform for performing ssh on the node
resolution: - Red Hat does not recommend performing ssh operations on the RHOCP nodes- Creation of additional users is neither recommended by Red Hat nor supported.
root_cause: - Red Hat CoreOS(RHCOS) is an `immutable Operating System` and Red Hat does not `recommend` making any `manual changes` to RHCOS. The changes are to be made through a `machine-config-operator`. The changes made through `machine-config-operator` are also limited in `support`.

title: Failed to update the logging stack from 4.5 to 4.6 due to broken catalog source
issue: - Failed to update the logging stack from 4.5 to 4.6.- Operators provided by Red Hat are not available.
resolution: - Execute the below command to re-create the catalog source ~~~ $ oc delete catalogsource redhat-operators-n openshift-marketplace ~~~
root_cause: - OLM establishes the connection through a resource called catalog source- If the cluster doesn't see any of the RedHat operators, that implies olm can't properly interact with the catalog source.

title: OpenShift behaviour when EC2 nodes are configured with EC2 auto-recovery in AWS
issue: - OCP 4.5 is deployed on AWS using IPI installation. With EC2 auto-recovery disabled and in the event an EC2 instance goes down. How would OpenShift cluster behave?- How would OpenShift behave if the underlying EC2 nodes are configured with EC2 auto-recovery enabled?
resolution: - With EC2 auto-recovery disabled and in the event an EC2 instance goes down. How would the OpenShift cluster behave? ~~~ If an EC2 instance fail then machinest can be used present in machine-config-operator project to scale up instance immediately. If cluster is deployed using IPI installation then machinesets are created by default. But, if the cluster is deployed using UPI installation then machinesets can be created manually. However, replacing a master node is little bit tricky since a couple of ETCD configuration needs to be tweaked. Machineset for master nodes are also not available in both cases of IPI and UPI installation. They have to be created manually for master nodes. ~~~- How will OpenShift behave if the underlying EC2 nodes are configured with EC2 auto-recovery enabled?- If a worker or master node fails then OpenShift will not automatically replace the node. But, you can scale down and scale up the nodes using machineset to replace a worker node. For master nodes you will have to follow couple of extra steps mentioned in the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/backup_and_restore/replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member.html#replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member).

title: Update the core set of Red Hat Single Sign-On resources for OpenShift in a disconnected environment
resolution: - Download the resources from a host with external connectivity ~~~ $ mkdir sso-templates $ cd sso-templates $ for resource in sso72-image-stream.json \ sso72-https.json \ sso72-mysql.json \ sso72-mysql-persistent.json \ sso72-postgresql.json \ sso72-postgresql-persistent.json \ sso72-x509-https.json \ sso72-x509-mysql-persistent.json \ sso72-x509-postgresql-persistent.json do wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jboss-openshift/application-templates/ose-v1.4.11/sso/${resource} done ~~~- Copy the resources to the host from where 'oc' commands are run- Update the resources using local template references: ~~~ $ cd $ for resource in sso72-image-stream.json \ sso72-https.json \ sso72-mysql.json \ sso72-mysql-persistent.json \ sso72-postgresql.json \ sso72-postgresql-persistent.json \ sso72-x509-https.json \ sso72-x509-mysql-persistent.json \ sso72-x509-postgresql-persistent.json do oc replace-n openshift--force-f./${resource} done ~~~

title: How to apply individual patches for OpenShift images based from JBoss EAP 6.4 and later
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: How do I apply individual patches?
How to use CLI patch command for a JBoss EAP image for OpenShift?
resolution: ####Summary This solution describes an approach for applying Red Hat JBoss EAP patch files to container images for OpenShift. In this solution, there is a patch file in the form of a zip archive that is incorporated into a container image using a secret that contains the patch zip file. The patch zip file is incorporated into a container image during a build step within OpenShift. Please note that this example also uses a Git repository as the source input of the OpenShift build step. An example exists at [https://github.com/luck3y/eap-patch-using-secrets-cli](https://github.com/luck3y/eap-patch-using-secrets-cli) and can be used as a reference. ####Basic instructions: * Create a secret for each patch that will be applied. The contents of each secret will be a patch file. ~~~ $ oc create secret generic jbeap-16108--from-file=jbeap-1234.zip=jbeap-1234.zip ~~~ In this command, the `--from-file` option is described as `--from-file= = `. * Update `extensions/patch-build.cli` to install the required patch(es). The project Git repository should include an [.s2i/environment](https://github.com/luck3y/eap-patch-using-secrets-cli/blob/master/.s2i/environment) file with the following contents: ~~~ CUSTOM_INSTALL_DIRECTORIES=extensions ~~~ Alternatively, the `CUSTOM_INSTALL_DIRECTORIES` environment variable may be provided as part of a `oc new-app with-e CUSTOM_INSTALL_DIRECTORIES...` command when creating a pod. The application template or existing build configuration may now be modified to refer to the secret(s) containing the patch(es) and then the application is rebuilt. See: [https://github.com/luck3y/eap-patch-using-secrets-cli/blob/master/eap71-basic-s2i-patching.json#L243](https://github.com/luck3y/eap-patch-using-secrets-cli/blob/master/eap71-basic-s2i-patching.json#L243) for the necessary build configuration change to refer to the secret during the build. This change can be made by editing and replacing the existing application template or by using the OpenShift client `oc edit bc/app-name`. * Install / replace the updated template: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift replace--force-f eap71-basic-s2i-patching.json ~~~ * Create / recreate the application pod: ~~~ $ oc new-app--template=eap71-basic-s2i-patching \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_URL="https://github.com/luck3y/eap-patch-using-secrets-cli.git" \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_REF="master" \-p CONTEXT_DIR="" \-p APPLICATION_NAME="eap-patching-demo" ~~~ Alternatively, the OpenShift buildconfig can be modified to add the needed secret in a similar way (or edit the buildconfig yaml in the OpenShift console.) ~~~ oc edit bc/eap-app-name ~~~ ####Verification At the end of the OpenShift build step, a message may be observed indicating patching was successful. For example: ~~~ Running /home/jboss/install.sh- echo 'Running /home/jboss/install.sh'- injected_dir=/tmp/src/extensions- cp-rf /tmp/src/extensions /opt/eap/extensions- echo 'Executing patch-build.cli'- /opt/eap/bin/jboss-cli.sh--file=/opt/eap/extensions/patch-build.cli Executing patch-build.cli {"outcome": "success", "result": {}} ~~~ When the application pod is created a message similar to the following example should be logged during pod deployment: ~~~ 03:19:08,195 INFO [org.jboss.as.patching] (MSC service thread 1-2) WFLYPAT0050: JBoss EAP cumulative patch ID is: jboss-eap-7.1.5.CP, one-off patches include: eap-715-jbeap-1234 ~~~ ####Additional Notes * As an alternative to using secrets, the patch file may be included in git / scm and referred to directly from install.sh, the patch would be available in the local extensions directory structure in the build pod. * Curl and maven may also be used from install.sh to fetch the file containing a patch.

title: Cluster version not found in the stable channel
issue: - Installation is failing with a similar error: ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion-oyaml | grep channel f:channel: {} channel: stable-4.7 message: 'Unable to retrieve available updates: currently reconciling cluster version 4.7.6 not found in the "stable-4.7" channel' ~~~- Even though the latest installer is GA, it does not shows up in the stable channel.
resolution: - Either patch the cluster to use the fast channel: ~~~ $ oc patch clusterversion/version-p '{"spec":{"channel":"fast-4.7"}}'--type=merge ~~~- Or wait for around two days so that the build gets promoted to the stable channel.- Also, the Red Hat Engineering team is aware of this issue and working to point [latest](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/latest/) subdirectory to the [stable](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/stable/) subdirectory.
root_cause: - At the time of writing this article, the OpenShift installer published in mirror.openshift.com points to the [latest](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/latest/) subdirectory.- Whenever, a release is rolled out officially (apart from the candidate channel), it first comes in the fast channel, however, we wait for around 48 hours before promoting it to a stable channel.- Hence till then the [latest](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/latest/) subdirectory would be pointing towards the [fast](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/fast/) subdirectory directory.- This causes the cluster to produce the following error until the latest release is in the stable channel because the cluster defaults to the stable channel: ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion-oyaml | grep channel f:channel: {} channel: stable-4.7 message: 'Unable to retrieve available updates: currently reconciling cluster version 4.7.6 not found in the "stable-4.7" channel' ~~~

title: Configure an IngressController to capture certain HTTP request and response headers
issue: - How to configure `Ingress access logging` to enable the capture of HTTP request and response headers in access logs.- In OCP 3.x, It was possible creating a router custom template and inserted the `capture request header` for XFF in the "frontend" stanza. Is this procedure supported on OCP 4.6?
resolution: - By default, when access logging is enabled, the IngressController logs the HTTP request line and response code but no headers.- Edit the IngressController's `spec.logging.access.httpCaptureHeaders` field to capture the required headers. ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: IngressController metadata: name: default namespace: openshift-ingress-operator spec: logging: access: destination: type: Container httpCaptureHeaders: request:- name: X-My-Header maxLength: 5 ~~~- The `maxLength` specifies a maximum length for the header value. If a header value exceeds this length, the value will be truncated in the log message. Note that the ingress controller may impose a separate bound on the total length of HTTP headers in a request.- For more information on IngressController API Endpoints refer to this [document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/rest_api/operator_apis/ingresscontroller-operator-openshift-io-v1.html#api-endpoints).

title: Operator Queries
issue: Do Red Hat Integration Operators support multiple versions of a product instance in the same OpenShift cluster. Specifically we are interested in the operators of- Red Hat Single Sign On- AMQ Broker- 3Scale- AMQ Streams
resolution: AMQ Broker: The version can be set explicitly or it can be set so the latest is used- see https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_amq/2020.q4/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#assembly-br-how-operator-chooses-container-images_broker-ocp 3Scale: The 3scale operator is currently Tech Preview see- https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.10/html-single/operating_3scale/index#provision-threescale-services-via-operator AMQ Streams: This appears to have a set of operators- see https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_amq/2020.q4/html-single/amq_streams_on_openshift_overview/index#overview-components_str Red Hat SSO: At time of writing this is tech preview too- see https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5129211 The operators themselves are maintained by each product team ie. the team that creates and maintains each product and they are all at differing levels of operator maturity (https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/operators/understanding/olm-what-operators-are.html see last section) Of all the operators the AMQ streams ones are probably the most mature. In streams if you want to deploy a specific AMQ Streams version, then you can download the corresponding "OpenShift Installation and Examples" package [0] and follow the documented manual procedure [1]. In the YAML files that are part of this package you can also change the image URL to set a specific version if needed (but this is not recommended). Same story applies for the AMQ broker and most of the Integration products, but for example the Registry only supports the OperatorHub. The AMQ Streams operators are GA and it is one of the most advanced integration operators (level 4 with some level 5 capabilities [2]). Changing the version not possible using the OperatorHub, where you have channels (i.e. stable, amq-streams-1.5.x, amq-streams-1.6.x, amq-streams-1.x) instead of exact versions (i.e. 1.6.2), and they always deploy the latest channel image. (This is supposed to simplify things for the average user, as you also get automatic updates for that channel by default (but this can be disabled)). title: oc logs/oc rsh/oc exec/oc debug commands fail in some pods/nodes in OCP 4: unable to upgrade connection: Unauthorized
issue: - Any or all of `oc logs` / `oc rsh` / `oc exec` / `oc debug node` commands fails: ~~~ unable to upgrade connection: Unauthorized ~~~ ~~~ error: You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials (pods/log pod_name)) ~~~- Also `oc adm must-gather` fails with error: ~~~ error: You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials (pods/log must-gather-xxxxx)) ~~~
resolution: Get the `machine-config-daemon` logs from the affected nodes: ~~~ $ mkdir node $ for node in $(oc get node-o name-l node-role.kubernetes.io/worker);do oc debug ${node}-- chroot /host bash-c 'crictl logs $(crictl ps-q--name machine-config-daemon)' > ${node}_mcd.log done $ tar-zvcf machine-config-daemon_logs.tar.gz node/ ~~~ If `oc debug node` command fails, try with: ~~~ $ mkdir node $ for node in $(oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/master-o jsonpath="{.items[*].metadata.name}");do ssh-i [ssh.key] core@${node} sudo-i-- 'crictl logs $(sudo-i crictl ps-q--name machine-config-daemon)' 2> node/${node}_mcd.log done $ tar-zvcf machine-config-daemon_logs.tar.gz node/ ~~~ As there could be different errors, it's needed to check the exact error from the log and resolve the issue. After resolving the issue in one node, could be needed to repeat with other nodes.
root_cause: Some nodes have an invalid certificate, and the `oc` command fails trying to authenticate. The Machine Config Pool is degraded, or is not able to upgrade the nodes. As it could be caused by different reasons, it's needed to check the logs to know the root cause.

title: How , why libvirt URI need to be provided at Bare metal provider
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: From 6.5.2. Creating a provider connection by using the console in [1] we see on list of params following:- Add your libvirt URI. See Connection URIs for more information. What does it mean? 1. https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.2/html-single/manage_cluster/index#creating-a-provider-connection-for-bare-metal
resolution: Please take a look in openshift documentation "Deploying installer-provisioned clusters on bare metal": Baremetal IPI (Installer-provisioned installation) [1] #### What is libvirt URI used for? As a prereq. please take a look: [2], you need to prepare: Your bare metal server login credentials, which include the libvirt URI, SSH Private Key, and a list of SSH known hosts; see Generating an SSH private key and adding it to the agent [2] Can't skip the libvirt URI for a Baremetal install through ACM- ACM uses the libvirt host you specify as the location to launch the bootstrap VM (tepmorary VM) that is needed temporarily for a Baremetal IPI installation. Libvirt URI [3], is pointing to a baremetal provisioner node. For example libvirt URI [4], generally be something like qemu+ssh://root@provisioner.cluster.example.com/system Which requires that you provide ACM with the necessary ssh private key and have the corresponding public key configured on the provisioner node. You don't have to connect to the provisioner as root as long as your target user has access to the qemu:///system instance. The known host is the known host string for the libvirt host to be used. If you have ssh manually into that libvirt host then it would be in your local known hosts file. at ~/.ssh/known_hosts 1: [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing_bare_metal_ipi/ipi-install-overview.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing_bare_metal_ipi/ipi-install-overview.html "IPI install overview") 2: [https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.2/html-single/manage_cluster/index#creating-a-provider-connection-for-bare-metal](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.2/html-single/manage_cluster/index#creating-a-provider-connection-for-bare-metal "Creating a provider connection for baremetal") 3: [https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.6/html/installing_on_bare_metal/installing-on-bare-metal#ssh-agent-using_installing-bare-metal](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.6/html/installing_on_bare_metal/installing-on-bare-metal#ssh-agent-using_installing-bare-metal "ssh agent using baremetal") 4: [https://libvirt.org/uri.html](https://libvirt.org/uri.html "libvirt URI")

title: Disconnected mirror registry upload fail with error no basic auth credentials
issue: - Why upload to the local registry is failing with following error. ~~~ error: unable to push file://openshift/release: failed to upload blob sha256:0c3f157e7f32f7f899311f6bcdba28e4eb84b31ac60d6b30240949da58bdaec3: Post "https://registry.example.com:5000/v2/openshift/release/blobs/uploads/": no basic auth credentials ~~~- How to fix the `no basic auth credentials` error while uploading the images from directory to local registry
resolution: Edit the new file auth file and add a section that describes your registry including the local registry domain name and the port: ~~~ "auths": {" ": {(1) "auth": " ", (2) "email": "you@example.com"}, (1) For, specify the registry domain name, and optionally the port, that your mirror registry uses to serve content. For example, registry.example.com or registry.example.com:5000 (2) For, specify the base64-encoded user name and password for the mirror registry. ~~~ It's mentioned in the openshift official docs for [mirroring-registry](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/installing/install_config/installing-restricted-networks-preparations.html#installation-adding-registry-pull-secret_installing-restricted-networks-preparations)
root_cause: Incorrect domain name or missing port can cause this error. So the mirror registry `domain name` and the `port` should be mentioned correctly as mentioned below. ~~~ For, specify the registry domain name, and optionally the port, that your mirror registry uses to serve content. For example, registry.example.com or registry.example.com:5000 ~~~

title: How to switch a connected OpenShift cluster to disconnected/restricted one?
issue: - If an OpenShift cluster is installed as a connected network, is there any way to switch it to a disconnected environment?
resolution: - Switch the registry- Create a mirror registry [1].- Mirror Red Hat registry [2].- Configure the registry repository mirroring within OCP [3].- Re-deploy internal registry [4]. > Note: What is not described in the documentation is that create a config map named registry-config that contains your certificate for the mirrored registry and patch the image.config.openshift.io/cluster object: ~~~ $ oc create configmap registry-config--from-file=.crt-n openshift-config $ oc patch image.config.openshift.io/cluster--patch '{"spec":{"additionalTrustedCA":{"name":"registry-config"}}}'--type=merge ~~~- Mirror OLM [5] > Note: Also what is important is to check the operators to see if they are supported in the network restricted mode [6].- Disable telemetry [7]. [1]: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/install_config/installing-restricted-networks-preparations.html#installing-restricted-networks-preparations [2]: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/install_config/installing-restricted-networks-preparations.html#installation-mirror-repository_installing-restricted-networks-preparations [3]: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-registry-mirror_image-configuration [4]: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/registry/configuring_registry_storage/configuring-registry-storage-vsphere.html [5]: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/operators/admin/olm-restricted-networks.html [6]: https://access.redhat.com/articles/4740011 [7]: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/support/remote_health_monitoring/opting-out-of-remote-health-reporting.html

title: Unable to set sysctl parameter 'net.core.netdev_max_backlog' at pod level
issue: - The parameter **net.core.netdev_max_backlog*
does not works on pod level.- Adding above parameter in the **securityContext*

section of pod's definition fails to start the pod with the following event error: ~~~ Warning FailedCreatePodSandBox 11s kubelet, NODE Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to cleanup [/var/run/netns/319844c6-af6b-49d4-8d91-a2e4268790eb /var/run/ipcns/319844c6-af6b-49d4-8d91-a2e4268790eb /var/run/utsns/319844c6-af6b-49d4-8d91-a2e4268790eb] after pinns failure exit status 1 ~~~- This is the securityContext on the pod: ~~~ securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: s0:c55,c30 sysctls:- name: net.core.netdev_max_backlog < < adding this option fails the pod to start value: "250000" ~~~
resolution: - Only sysctls that are `namespaced` can be set independently on pods. If a sysctl is not namespaced (called as`node-level` sysctls) it cannot be set within OpenShift Container Platform.- As the systcl **net.core.netdev_max_backlog** is `not namespaced` and `unsafe`, it needs to be enabled at a node-level. Follow the steps mentioned under the section **Enabling unsafe sysctls** by referring to this [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/nodes/containers/nodes-containers-sysctls.html#nodes-containers-sysctls-unsafe_nodes-containers-using)- After following the above steps deploy the application pod which will collect the values for above mentioned parameter.

title: Red Hat OpenShift Serverless pods stay in "Terminating" state for around 45 seconds approximately
root_cause: - This is an expected behaviour required by [Red Hat OpenShift Serverless](https://www.openshift.com/learn/topics/serverless) to guarantee an errorless scalability.- This may create problems if you have [resource quotas](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/applications/quotas/quotas-setting-per-project.html) configured in your project. If that is your case, it is recommended that you optimize your quotas taking into account the information described on the previous point.- At the time when this article is being written, the engineers involved in [Red Hat OpenShift Serverless](https://www.openshift.com/learn/topics/serverless) and its upstream project are trying to reduce this time (around 15 seconds less) in future releases, but it is not guaranteed that this will happen.- In case you need further guidance or information, feel free to contact [Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/support).

title: How do I print from an OpenShift container
issue: How do I print from an OpenShift container to a central print server.
resolution: 1. Install cups-client and its dependencies. They shouldn't need to install any server/daemon software, like cups or avahi-daemon or systemd. 2. Run a command like the following to print a document: lp-h If a CUPS server is running on and is configured to accept jobs from remote clients, this should work. Setting up a CUPS service to accept jobs from remote clients is explained here: How to access CUPS from remote systems in Red Hat Enterprise Linux https://access.redhat.com/solutions/35312 The container will need to allow access out to port 631 on the remote CUPS server. If that all works, they can do the following instead of using the "-h" parameter to the lp command: * set SERVER_NAME to the address of the remote server * Set the ServerName directive in /etc/cups/client.conf ~ Bryan

title: csi-rbdplugin pods are missing after upgrading OCS cluster
issue: - The `oc get pods-n openshift-storage` showing only `csi-rbdplugin-provisioner` pods but `csi-rbdplugin*` pods are missing.- PVC failing to attach with error `MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "pvc-12345678-9999-aaaa-bbbb-ccccdddd123456": kubernetes.io/csi: attacher.MountDevice failed to create newCsiDriverClient: driver name openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com not found in the list of registered CSI drivers`
resolution: Kindly backup `rook-ceph-operator-config` configmap and edit to set `ROOK_CSI_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION=true` so that operator can skip the version check for `csi-rbdplugin` pods while configuring drivers. ~~~ $ oc get cm-o yaml rook-ceph-operator-config > rook-ceph-operator-config.yaml $ oc edit cm rook-ceph-operator-config ~~~ **Add ROOK_CSI_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION: "false" under data section, wait for 5min then verify csi-rbdplugin pods are running** ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage-o wide ~~~
root_cause: The version check for CSI rbdplugin pods are failing because the ceph-CSI version of both upstream and downstream are different. We are investigating this issue internally. Kindly contact Red Hat Openshift Container Support team for more information.

title: What does the warning OUT gather logs unavailable: unexpected EOF mean when running oc adm must gather
issue: - when running `oc adm must-gather` the following message is seen ~~~ [must-gather-f778l] POD Gathering data for ns/openshift-image-registry... [must-gather-f778l] OUT gather logs unavailable: unexpected EOF ~~~
resolution: - In this context, the ` OUT gather logs unavailable: unexpected EOF` warning means that the connection to the API server used to stream the logs to the command line has been interrupted.- However this is only *a warning* that the logs of the `gather` script which is run inside the must-gather pod cannot be displayed in real time, the must-gather pod is still running on the cluster, and `oc adm must-gather` may eventually complete.- if you need to follow the activity of the must-gather pod in real time, you can start a separate `oc logs` on the must-gather pod as such:- find the namespace in which the must-gather pod is created. This will be displayed in the beginning of the `oc adm must-gather` command output: oc adm must-gather... [must-gather] OUT namespace/openshift-must-gather-zjrzw created...- find the must-gather pod inside this namespace: $ oc-n openshift-must-gather-zjrzw-o name-l app=must-gather get pods pod/must-gather-pl5nh- monitor the logs of this pod $ oc-n openshift-must-gather-zjrzw logs-f pod/must-gather-h7bht gather Wrote inspect data to must-gather. Gathering data for ns/openshift-cluster-version... Wrote inspect data to must-gather. Gathering data for ns/openshift-config... Gathering data for ns/openshift-config-managed... Gathering data for ns/openshift-authentication...
root_cause: When deploying a RHOCP cluster, this cluster has usually a load balancer in front of the API server, and this load balancer has a timer limit to drop connections when those connections are inactive. In the case of the log streaming, it can be that there is no log to display for a longer amount of time when the must-gather pod is getting data from a heavily loaded cluster. For instance when using HA Proxy, with a `timeout client` and `timeoutserver` of 1 m the realtime log display will be interrupted with the message `unexpected end of file` if the target pod does not log output at least once a minute. Note that there can be other causes of timeouts when troubleshooting oc adm must-gather, see for instance [this Solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5227051) for the error `OUT gather never finished: timed out waiting for the condition`.
