title: Cluster Logging Operator fails to install in a disconnected environment
issue: - After mirroring the Cluster Logging Operator to a disconnected registry, the CLO install fails due to not finding the image `ose-cluster-logging-operator-bundle`
resolution: This has been resolved in the following release (and the ones after):- [4.6.1](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2020:5633) The workaround, if updating to a newer release is not an option, is to this issue is to add a second filter when creating the custom mapping file for image mirroring as per [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/operators/admin/olm-restricted-networks.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/operators/admin/olm-restricted-networks.html): ~~~ for sha in $(echo "select bundlepath from operatorbundle where name like '%clusterlogging%';" | sqlite3-line $db_path | grep sha256 | cut-d ":"-f2); do grep $sha olm/$default_mapping > > $custom_mapping; done for sha in $(echo "select * from related_image where operatorbundle_name like 'clusterlogging%';" | sqlite3-line $db_path | grep sha256 | cut-d ":"-f2); do grep $sha olm/$default_mapping > > $custom_mapping; done ~~~ Then use the custom mapping file created to complete the CLO mirroring: ~~~ $ oc image mirror-a pull-secret-json-f $custom_mapping--continue-on-error=true ~~~ Note: At the time of writing there is an issue with `oc image mirror` where it does not mirror all of the sha256 images to correct this for installing CLO after running the above command: ~~~ skopeo copy--all docker://registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-logging-curator5@sha256:904e21f0eb89c3e6b7aaab78dd6a052f215f96b1d62d70e6bec2516b04651e0c docker://registry.example.com/olm-openshift4-ose-logging-curator5 skopeo copy--all docker://registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-logging-fluentd@sha256:f262f333d80b3ca40cf0fad7a4b33f8d9748724167e462c7540421e2c46e72bd docker://registry.example.com/olm-openshift4-ose-logging-fluentd skopeo copy--all docker://registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-cluster-logging-operator@sha256:c4300dd4a4d069203fb3d00822778ebc66401b88fa22523be967e717505a4020 docker://registry.example.com/olm-openshift4-ose-cluster-logging-operator ~~~
root_cause: The filter used was: ~~~ for sha in $(echo "select * from related_image where operatorbundle_name like 'clusterlogging%';" | sqlite3-line $db_path | grep sha256 | cut-d ":"-f2); do grep $sha olm/$default_mapping > > $custom_mapping; done ~~~ This filter does not included the bundle package in the `index.db` file created because it is not referenced in the `related_image` table in the `index.db` file.

title: Can I access a Virtual Machine Instance running in OpenShift Virtualization through the Terminal
issue: Can I access a virtual machine instance running in OpenShift Virtualization through the terminal?
resolution: - Ensure that the `virtctl` tool is installed using the Official Red Hat Documentation- [OCP 4.6+](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/virt/install/virt-installing-virtctl.html)- [OCP 4.5](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/virt/install/virt-installing-virtctl.html)- List the available virtual machines running on your cluster `[user@computer ~] oc get vmi-A` `NAMESPACE NAME AGE PHASE IP NODENAME` ` 1m Running 10.131.X.X XXX`- Switch to the project / namespace where the virtual machine is running `[user@computer ~] oc project `- Connect to the virtual machine console `[user@computer ~] virtctl console `- Alternatively connect to the virtual machine through VNC (**Please note:** VNC client is required) `[user@computer ~] virtctl vnc `

title: Can I create Red Hat Enterprise Linux virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: Can I create Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization?
resolution: - Download the required RHEL QCOW image from the [Red Hat website.](https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/479/)- Select Red Hat Enterprise Linux Update KVM Guest Image as the download- Set the following environment variables:- `PVC_NAME`: To set the name of the PersistentVolumeClaim created as the boot-source of the Virtual Machine- `RHEL_QCOW`: The file path to the downloaded QCOW for RHEL- `USER`: The name of the user that will be created on the RHEL Virtual Machine- `PASSWORD`: The password to log into the RHEL Virtual Machine- Upload the image to your cluster `virtctl image-upload dv ${PVC_NAME}--size=15Gi--image-path=${RHEL_QCOW}--insecure`- Create the virtual machine using the uploaded image and template in the [attachments below](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/attachments/rhel.yml) `oc process-f rhel.yaml--param=PVC_BOOT_SOURCE=${PVC_NAME}--param=RHEL_USER=${USER}--param=RHEL_PASSWORD=${PASSWORD} | oc create-f-`

title: [RFE]nginx Base Image with Prometheus Exporter
issue: Red Hat offers a supported Base Image for nginx (https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/ubi8/nginx-118). We found out that this base image does not contain the nginx-prometheus-exporter (https://github.com/nginxinc/nginx-prometheus-exporter). Since Prometheus is the default monitoring tool in OpenShift, it would be cool if Red Hat would provide a base image with the exporter already installed. At the moment, we have to extend the image by ourselves or add the official nginx-prometheus-exporter image as a side car. Both options are not very easy from an organizational point of view.
resolution: - As the nginx-prometheus-exporter package is not part of the standard RHEL distribution, it's not easy to push it into UBI.- Engineering team is considering extending the underlying services (at least for httpd/mod_status) to expose metrics in the native Prometheus format, which obviates the need for a separate scraper/exporter.- There are no plans for such metrics expose for NGINX.

title: Get names of subscribed systems under a subscription contract
issue: - How to get systems names that are subscribed under a subscription contract?- Without using Satellite, is it possible to get systems names that are subscribed under a subscription contract?
resolution: - It s possible to get the required info without using Red Hat Satellite.- This method relies on issuing API calls using the (Open API specification for RHSM-API)[https://access.redhat.com/management/api/rhsm] to get the required data as follows: 1- Login to [RHSM-API](https://access.redhat.com/management/api)![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/1_48.png) 2- Under `Manage` choose `RHSM API Tokens`:![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/2_47.png) 3- Under `Generate an offline token` click on `GENERATE TOKEN`:![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/3_33.png) 4- Copy and save the offline token:![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/4_21.png) 5- Copy and save the following script to a file, in this demo I will name the file `script.sh`: ~~~ offline_token='' contractid= accessToken=`curl-s https://sso.redhat.com/auth/realms/redhat-external/protocol/openid-connect/token-d grant_type=refresh_token-d client_id=rhsm-api-d refresh_token=$offline_token | jq--raw-output.access_token` curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer $accessToken"-X GET "https://api.access.redhat.com/management/v1/subscriptions?limit=1000"-H "accept: application/json" | jq-r--arg contractid "$contractid" '.body[] | select(.contractNumber == $contractid)' | jq-r.subscriptionNumber > /tmp/subid for subid in `cat /tmp/subid` do echo "====================================================" echo "subscription ID: $subid" subname=`curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer $accessToken"-X GET "https://api.access.redhat.com/management/v1/subscriptions"-H "accept: application/json" | jq-r--arg subid "$subid" '.body[] | select(.subscriptionNumber == $subid)' | jq-r.subscriptionName` echo "Subscription Name: $subname" systems=`curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer $accessToken"-X GET "https://api.access.redhat.com/management/v1/subscriptions/$subid/systems"-H "accept: application/json" | jq-r '.body[].systemName'` echo "Systems:" for x in $systems do echo $x done echo "====================================================" done ~~~ 6- Paste the copied offline token to the `offline_token` variable in the script, and set the desired contract ID value in the `contractid` variable as shown in the below example: ~~~ offline_token='PASTE OFFLINE TOKEN HERE' <------ contractid=PASTE CONTRACT ID HERE <------ accessToken=`curl-s https://sso.redhat.com/auth/realms/redhat-external/protocol/openid-connect/token-d grant_type=refresh_token-d client_id=rhsm-api-d refresh_token=$offline_token | jq--raw-output.access_token` curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer $accessToken"-X GET "https://api.access.redhat.com/management/v1/subscriptions?limit=1000"-H "accept: application/json" | jq-r--arg contractid "$contractid" '.body[] | select(.contractNumber == $contractid)' | jq-r.subscriptionNumber > /tmp/subid for subid in `cat /tmp/subid` do echo "====================================================" echo "subscription ID: $subid" subname=`curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer $accessToken"-X GET "https://api.access.redhat.com/management/v1/subscriptions"-H "accept: application/json" | jq-r--arg subid "$subid" '.body[] | select(.subscriptionNumber == $subid)' | jq-r.subscriptionName` echo "Subscription Name: $subname" systems=`curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer $accessToken"-X GET "https://api.access.redhat.com/management/v1/subscriptions/$subid/systems"-H "accept: application/json" | jq-r '.body[].systemName'` echo "Systems:" for x in $systems do echo $x done echo "====================================================" done ~~~ 7- Make this script an executable file: ~~~ $ chmod +x script.sh ~~~ 8- Run it: ~~~ $./script.sh ~~~ 8- Example output: ~~~ ==================================================== subscription ID: 1234567 Subscription Name: Red Hat Developer Subscription for Individuals Systems: host1.example.com host2.example.com ==================================================== ==================================================== subscription ID: 7654321 Subscription Name: 60 Day Product Trial of Red Hat OpenShift Broker/Master Infrastructure, Self-Supported (2 Core) Systems: host3.example.com ==================================================== ~~~

title: BYOK (Bring your own key) Disk Encryption Keys on Azure with a customer-managed key
issue: Is it possible to encrypt CoreOS disks on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) using the Azure Encryption at Rest with our own key?
resolution: BYOK Disk Encryption Keys on Azure at install-time is not available in 4.5/4.6. Although, by default, Red Hat supports SSE (Server Side Encryption) with platform-managed keys. However, it is possible to move nodes to using BYOK (SSE-based) on **Day 2**. + As long as the VM is powered down, you could move from a platform-managed key to a customer-managed key right from the Azure console. Since this operation is done at the infrastructure layer, it wouldn’t effect upgrades as there’s nothing that will touch the OpenShift VMs disk encryption key mechanism (with the exception of elastic compute.) + If you’re using elastic compute (MachineSets/Node Autoscaler) then any new nodes created would default to using platform-managed keys unless you modified the MachineSets. Starting with 4.6.16 support was introduced: (4.6.16+: [RHSA-2021:0308](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:0308)) that will allow you to do this. Details can be found here on how to do that: [BZ1884632](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1884632#c5)

title: Get vulnerabilities that match the non-RPM content using cve-pylib

However, the oval files contained in the Security Data API only includes RPM content. To add non-RPM content we can use a tool called cve-pylib which is able to filter the data by product and flaw impact in the Product Security namespace in Github
resolution: cve-pylib let us Retrieve customizable details about found CVEs or about specific CVE ids input on cmdline. It is based on python. For example if we need to search critical CVEs related to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) 4.x we can use: $ python rhsecapi.py--q-product 'OpenShift Container Platform 4'--q-severity=critical [NOTICE] rhsda: 3 CVEs found with search query CVE ID PUB DATE BUGZILLA SEVERITY CVSS2 CVSS3 RHSAS PKGS CVE-2020-27846 2020-12-17 1907670 critical 9.8 1 0 CVE-2020-11100 2020-04-02 1819111 critical 8.8 5 5 CVE-2017-12629 2017-10-12 1501529 critical 10.0 9.8 10 8 Passing the '-x' option also gives additional information about the flaws above. I've filtered the results a bit below to be more readable: $ python rhsecapi.py--q-product 'OpenShift Container Platform 4'--q-severity=critical-x [NOTICE] rhsda: 3 CVEs found with search query [NOTICE] rhsda: Valid Red Hat CVE results retrieved: 3 of 3 CVE-2020-11100 SEVERITY: Critical Impact DATE: 2020-04-02 BUGZILLA: 1819111 FIXED_RELEASES:... Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.11: [haproxy-0:1.8.23-3.el7] via RHSA-2020:1287 (2020-04-07) Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.4: [haproxy-0:2.0.13-3.el7] via RHSA-2020:1936 (2020-05-04)... FIX_STATES:... CVE-2020-27846 SEVERITY: Critical Impact DATE: 2020-12-17 BUGZILLA: 1907670 FIXED_RELEASES: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.7: via RHSA-2020:5633 (2021-02-24) FIX_STATES:... CVE-2017-12629 SEVERITY: Critical Impact DATE: 2017-10-12 BUGZILLA: 1501529 FIXED_RELEASES:... FIX_STATES:... Not affected: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 [openshift4/ose-logging-elasticsearch5] Not affected: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 [openshift4/ose-logging-elasticsearch6] Not affected: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 [openshift4/ose-metering-presto]... Regarding CVE-2020-27846, we actually rated this one Low impact for OCP 4. As you can see the statement for the flaw curl-s https://access.redhat.com/hydra/rest/securitydata/cve/CVE-2020-27846.json | jq '.statement'

title: Cluster deploy fails to find /etc/origin/master/ca-bundle.crt
issue: - During the upgrade from 3.11.318 to 3.11.374 it fails for: ~~~ Error loading file /etc/origin/master/ca-bundle.crt\n139943696226192:error:02001002:system library:fopen:No such file or directory ~~~

title: Container fails to start with chdir to cwd (\"/home/nonroot\") set in config.json failed: permission denied"
issue: - containers built upon the gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot image fail to start due to error ~~~ Error: container create failed: time="2021-03-18T20:30:44Z" level=error msg="container_linux.go:366: starting container process caused: chdir to cwd (\"/home/nonroot\") set in config.json failed: permission denied" ~~~
resolution: This issue is being tracked by [Bugzilla 1934177](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1934177) This issue has been fixed in the following OpenShift Container Platform releases:- 4.6.?- 4.7.? If you would like to work around the issue, you can fix the issue by updating the pod container definition to runAsUser: 65532. This should look as follows: ~~~ kind: Pod apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: foo spec: containers:- name: foo image: hasheddan/crossplane:nocreds securityContext: runAsUser: 65532 ~~~ Alternatively, you can change the working directory if the runAsUser does not match your extended version of the base image or is just not working. To change the working directory, you can add the following: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: foo spec: containers:- name: foo image: hasheddan/crossplane:nocreds workingDir: /tmp ~~~
root_cause: TL;DR: runc has a set of three operations whose order is pretty particular. For different use cases, the order can cause a container creation to perpetually EPERM. There are three operations in runc when finalizing a namespace for a container: apply capabilities, setuid/setgid for the container user, and chdir to the working directory. The order used to be setuid, apply caps, chdir. If the caps are configured in such a way, the container user is not allowed to chdir to its own working directory. https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/2086/ changed the order to: chdir, setuid, apply caps. This order is the one CNV pods are relying on to not break. However, this order leads to situations where, if the user that runs runc doesn't have access to the cwd, and attempts to chdir, runc fails with "chdir to cwd (%q) set in config.json failed...". This broke prometheus pods. Thus, https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/2712 fixes prometheus pods by making the order setuid, chdir, apply caps. However, this order breaks CNV. The runc version that applies this order is: runc-1.0.0-72.rhaos4.5.giteadfc6b.el8 and runc-1.0.0-82.rhaos4.6.git086e841.el8 (the latter will also be added to 4.7).

title: Trying to add new cluster to manage via Red Hat OpenShift GitOps

title: Unable to rollback the deployment in OpenShift Container Platform 4.x
issue: - Issue in rolling back a `deployment` to a specific `revision`.- While rolling back a deployment using the command gives the below error: ~~~ # oc rollout undo deploy/--to-revision= Error from server (NotFound): the server could not find the requested resource ~~~
resolution: - The `oc client` version should be `same` as that of the `clusterversion` or the server version. If not upgrade it to the respective version. For example: ~~~ $ oc version Client Version: 4.6.22 Server Version: 4.6.22 Kubernetes Version: v1.19.0+d46d32f ~~~
root_cause: - If your `oc client` is running on a `lower` version than the server you encounter with the above error.

title: Image push fails with "swift: Too Large Object" error
issue: - Image push to Swift backed OpenShift internal registry fails and shows `received unexpected HTTP status: 500 Internal Server Error`.- Image registry logs show 'swift: Too Large Object` error.
resolution: - Set increased quotas on the size and number of objects stored in an RHOSP Swift container.
root_cause: The Swift storage driver returns "Too Large Object" when it gets 413 from the storage [1]. According to Swift documentation [2], 413 is returned when a container quota is exceeded. [1]: https://github.com/openshift/image-registry/blob/8e0c068aef607fceffe3e179c3a9701f51c51dff/vendor/github.com/ncw/swift/swift.go#L309 [2]: https://docs.openstack.org/swift/pike/api/container_quotas.html

title: OCS 3.11 - RHGS - How to repair a gluster blockvolume iscsi disk device  - mount failed: exit status 32
issue: This is OCS 3.11 platform, in the "openshift-monitoring" namespace, there is a pod "alertmanager-main-0" in status ContainerCreating ~~~ # oc get pods-n openshift-monitoring NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE alertmanager-main-0 0/3 ContainerCreating 0 45m alertmanager-main-2 3/3 Running 0 11d ~~~ On the description of that pod we see some errors ~~~ # oc describe pod alertmanager-main-0 Name: alertmanager-main-0 Namespace: openshift-monitoring Priority: 0 PriorityClassName: Node: ocs-infra-1/10.10.10.51... Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Warning FailedAttachVolume 54m attachdetach-controller Multi-Attach error for volume "pvc-92699c76-a23c-11e9-821b-566f3ad8000a" Volume is already exclusively attached to one node and can't be attached to another Normal Scheduled 54m default-scheduler Successfully assigned openshift-monitoring/alertmanager-main-0 to ocs-infra-1 Normal SuccessfulAttachVolume 54m attachdetach-controller AttachVolume.Attach succeeded for volume "pvc-92699c76-a23c-11e9-821b-566f3ad8000a" Warning FailedMount 52m kubelet, opsinfra31.consum.red MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "pvc-92699c76-a23c-11e9-821b-566f3ad8000a": mount failed: exit status 32 Mounting command: systemd-run Mounting arguments:--description=Kubernetes transient mount for /var/lib/origin/openshift.local.volumes/plugins/kubernetes.io/iscsi/iface-default/10.10.10.4:3260-iqn.2016-12.org.gluster-block:e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32-lun-0--scope-- mount-t xfs-o defaults /dev/dm-6 /var/lib/origin/openshift.local.volumes/plugins/kubernetes.io/iscsi/iface-default/10.10.10.4:3260-iqn.2016-12.org.gluster-block:e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32-lun-0 Output: Running scope as unit run-72307.scope. mount: wrong fs type, bad option, bad superblock on /dev/mapper/mpathaa, missing codepage or helper program, or other error ~~~ There is also another event related: ~~~ 4m 15h 525 alertmanager-main-0.166ac2df9ae92f46 Pod Warning FailedMount kubelet, ocs-infra-1 (combined from similar events): Unable to mount volumes for pod "alertmanager-main-0_openshift-monitoring(00229e24-810c-11eb-9e7f-0050569935e2)": timeout expired waiting for volumes to attach or mount for pod "openshift-monitoring"/"alertmanager-main-0". list of unmounted volumes=[alertmanager-main-db]. list of unattached volumes=[alertmanager-main-db config-volume secret-alertmanager-main-tls secret-alertmanager-main-proxy alertmanager-main-token-lfx4q] ~~~ Q. What can we do to make this pod started again?
resolution: Try to repair manually the XFS filesystem on top of the blockvolume device (exported as an iscsi disk) 1) Identify the BHV and the blockvolume associated to the PV "pvc-92699c76-a23c-11e9-821b-566f3ad8000a" From the events log above, `transient mount for /var/lib/origin/openshift.local.volumes/plugins/kubernetes.io/iscsi/iface-default/10.10.10.4:3260-iqn.2016-12.org.gluster-block:e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32-lun-0` we see that the iqn for iscsi device is `iqn.2016-12.org.gluster-block:e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32` That iscsi device is served by the IP 10.10.10.4, this is the IP address of one of the gluster nodes that is servicing this blockvolume. Connect to that gluster node and get the output of command `targetcli ls`, on that we can see the following information: ~~~ | o- blockvol_5afc939e7bda90eb01fc92f9cac472ad [vol_0a96c7ee21ee6f69b726cda46990d6ab@10.10.10.2/block-store/e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32 (2.0GiB) activated] | | o- alua.......................................................... [ALUA Groups: 3] | | o- default_tg_pt_gp.............................. [ALUA state: Active/optimized] | | o- glfs_tg_pt_gp_ano......................... [ALUA state: Active/non-optimized] | | o- glfs_tg_pt_gp_ao.............................. [ALUA state: Active/optimized] | o- iqn.2016-12.org.gluster-block:e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32....... [TPGs: 3] | o- tpg1.................................................................. [disabled] | | o- acls................................................................. [ACLs: 0] | | o- luns..................................................................[LUNs: 1] | | | o- lun0.....[user/blockvol_5afc939e7bda90eb01fc92f9cac472ad (glfs_tg_pt_gp_ano)] | | o- portals........................................................... [Portals: 1] | | o- 10.10.10.4:3260......................................................... [OK] | o- tpg2.................................................................. [disabled] | | o- acls................................................................. [ACLs: 0] | | o- luns................................................................. [LUNs: 1] | | | o- lun0..... [user/blockvol_5afc939e7bda90eb01fc92f9cac472ad (glfs_tg_pt_gp_ao)] | | o- portals........................................................... [Portals: 1] | | o- 10.10.10.3:3260......................................................... [OK] | o- tpg3............................................ [gen-acls, tpg-auth, 1-way auth] | o- acls................................................................. [ACLs: 0] | o- luns................................................................. [LUNs: 1] | | o- lun0.... [user/blockvol_5afc939e7bda90eb01fc92f9cac472ad (glfs_tg_pt_gp_ano)] | o- portals........................................................... [Portals: 1] | o- 10.10.10.2:3260......................................................... [OK] ~~~ From that we find that: iscsi device `iqn.2016-12.org.gluster-block:e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32` is the blockvolume `blockvol_5afc939e7bda90eb01fc92f9cac472ad` allocated in BHV `vol_0a96c7ee21ee6f69b726cda46990d6ab` 2) On the gluster node, mount the BHV locally, ie on /mnt ~~~ [root@ocs-gluster-0 ~]# mount-t glusterfs localhost:/vol_0a96c7ee21ee6f69b726cda46990d6ab /mnt ~~~ 3) Run xfs_repair on the blockvolume device (the blockvolume is a file with name `e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32` under directory `/block-store/` on the gluster volume `vol_0a96c7ee21ee6f69b726cda46990d6ab`) ~~~ [root@ocs-gluster-0 ~]# xfs_repair /mnt/block-store/e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32 Phase 1- find and verify superblock... Cannot get host filesystem geometry. Repair may fail if there is a sector size mismatch between the image and the host filesystem. Phase 2- using internal log- zero log... ERROR: The filesystem has valuable metadata changes in a log which needs to be replayed. Mount the filesystem to replay the log, and unmount it before re-running xfs_repair. If you are unable to mount the filesystem, then use the-L option to destroy the log and attempt a repair. Note that destroying the log may cause corruption-- please attempt a mount of the filesystem before doing this. ~~~...in this particular case this command failed to repair the filesystem 4) If above command fails with above message we'll have to try again with `-L` option which could cause data loss in some cases, but there is no real alternative since the data loss likely already occurred: See Warning note on [3.5. Repairing an XFS File System](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/storage_administration_guide/xfsrepair) ~~~ [root@ocs-gluster-0 ~]# xfs_repair-L-f /mnt/block-store/e481bd6d-15f6-4d89-826b-49e9f5d71e32 Phase 1- find and verify superblock... Cannot get host filesystem geometry. Repair may fail if there is a sector size mismatch between the image and the host filesystem. Phase 2- using internal log- zero log... ALERT: The filesystem has valuable metadata changes in a log which is being destroyed because the-L option was used.- scan filesystem freespace and inode maps... sb_fdblocks 513512, counted 521704- found root inode chunk Phase 3- for each AG...- scan and clear agi unlinked lists...- process known inodes and perform inode discovery...- agno = 0- agno = 1- agno = 2- agno = 3- process newly discovered inodes... Phase 4- check for duplicate blocks...- setting up duplicate extent list...- check for inodes claiming duplicate blocks...- agno = 0- agno = 2- agno = 3- agno = 1 Phase 5- rebuild AG headers and trees...- reset superblock... Phase 6- check inode connectivity...- resetting contents of realtime bitmap and summary inodes- traversing filesystem...- traversal finished...- moving disconnected inodes to lost+found... Phase 7- verify and correct link counts... Maximum metadata LSN (47:19487) is ahead of log (1:2). Format log to cycle 50. done ~~~ Now the filesystem is repaired, and the pod was able to star successfully.
root_cause: The filesystem on top of the blockvolume was damaged and required manual action to repair it.

title: How to copy a image from test cluster to prod cluster
issue: we have configured the image registry locally by using NFS so how to download the image
resolution: 1. Expose your image registry in test-cluster, so that images can be access publicly.- Here is the ref doc[1].- Ensure you are able to pull images from test-cluster to external, you can try running below command outside of test-cluster ``` # HOST=$(oc get route default-route-n openshift-image-registry--template='{{.spec.host}}') # podman login-u $(oc whoami)-p $(oc whoami-t)--tls-verify=false $HOST ``` 2. You can use skopeo tool to copy image from test-cluster(source cluster) to prod-cluster(destination cluster).- Here we are assuming src cluster is test-cluster where images exists, dest cluster is production cluster to which images need to transfer- ``` #skopeo copy--src-creds=:--src-tls-verify=false oci: \--dest-creds=:--dest-tls-verify=false oci: ```- Once image is copied you can run oc new-app command as you mentioned in previous comment. 3. Please note that Skopeo is an Opensource tool, we are suggesting for achieving the user requirement & Red Hat is not officially supporting in any issues related Skopeo.- You can go through multiple unofficial documentations to understand working nature & syntax of skopeo. [2][3][4]

title: [WIP] How to fix a backingstore from an InvalidBackingStore condition?
issue: Backingstore is in Rejected Phase due to an `InvalidBackingStore` condition. ~~~ Spec: Pv Pool: Num Volumes: 3 Resources: Requests: Storage: 200Gi Storage Class: thin Type: pv-pool Status: Conditions: Last Heartbeat Time: 2021-03-04T08:47:50Z Last Transition Time: 2021-04-26T02:00:00Z Message: Scaling down the number of nodes is not currently supported Reason: InvalidBackingStore Status: Unknown Type: Available Last Heartbeat Time: 2021-03-04T08:47:50Z Last Transition Time: 2021-04-26T02:00:00Z ~~~
resolution: * There can be 2 scenarios that may exist. * The noobaa backingstore pods are seen as Running. * No noobaa backingstore pods might be seen Running, neither from CLI or Noobaa console. In such case, restart the `noobaa-operator` pod to re-spawn. In either cases, it is required to correct it from the noobaa-db. Follow the below steps to delete the Noobaa node entries from the db. * Take a note of the backingstore pods and its PVCs. ~~~ mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-0 [PVC: noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-noobaa-0 SC: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd] mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-1 [PVC: noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-noobaa-1 SC: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd] mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-2 [PVC: noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-noobaa-2 SC: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd] mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-48b9003e [PVC: mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pvc-48b9003e SC: thin] mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-71bd4c29 [PVC: mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-71bd4c29 SC: thin] mcg-pv-pool-bs-velero-noobaa-pod-76106c93 title: [WIP] How to recover the Noobaa backingstore from Creating Phase that happened post an OCS upgrade?
issue: The quay-registry backingstore got into Creating Phase after upgrade from OCS 4.4.2 to OCS 4.5.2. How can I restore the noobaa pods to make the backingstore and bucketclass available again? ~~~ #------------------# #- Backing Stores-# #------------------# NAME TYPE TARGET-BUCKET PHASE AGE mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry pv-pool Creating 1h57m16s noobaa-default-backing-store aws-s3 nb.1618244976752.apps.dkochuka-ocssdspnq.ceeindia.support Ready 2h23m40s #------------------# #- Bucket Classes-# #------------------# NAME PLACEMENT PHASE AGE mcg-pv-pool-bc-quay-registry {Tiers:[{Placement:Mirror BackingStores:[mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry]}]} Verifying 1h57m54s noobaa-default-bucket-class {Tiers:[{Placement: BackingStores:[noobaa-default-backing-store]}]} Ready 2h23m41s ~~~

The Backingstore Noobaa pods end up in InvalidImageName state post OCS upgrade. ~~~ Warning Failed 11m (x13 over 13m) kubelet Error: InvalidImageName Warning InspectFailed 3m40s (x49 over 13m) kubelet Failed to apply default image tag "NOOBAA_CORE_IMAGE": couldn't parse image reference "NOOBAA_CORE_IMAGE": invalid reference format: repository name must be lowercase ~~~
resolution: Follow the below steps for the BackingStores that remain in Creating Phase post upgrade. * Scale down the noobaa-operator and ocs-operator, so that the pods are not auto-created during the procedure. ~~~ $ oc scale deployment noobaa-operator--replicas=0 $ oc scale deployment ocs-operator--replicas=0 ~~~ * Tag all the old pvcs with `label: pool: `. Here "pool_name" refers to the backingstore name. ~~~ $ oc get pvc NAMESPACE NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE openshift-storage mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pvc-10b8f03c Bound pvc-a1cfbf23-69ec-4985-b216-d32883af3708 200Gi RWO thin 42m openshift-storage mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pvc-1fad25a9 Bound pvc-9f5e5f5a-2ed4-4292-a3f9-61c1bbd92f20 200Gi RWO thin 42m openshift-storage mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pvc-2ca5ef99 Bound pvc-8f9b67f1-b60c-4305-b92e-dcf66730498d 200Gi RWO thin 42m openshift-storage noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-0 Bound pvc-f350f267-84d1-4960-887b-37d1fc25ce1a 200Gi RWO ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd 251d openshift-storage noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-1 Bound pvc-afcc18c4-6a31-4402-a09c-80afec3a6022 200Gi RWO ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd 251d openshift-storage noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-2 Bound pvc-2b2ed250-c14d-40b7-ab20-5f51c070b8dd 200Gi RWO ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd 251d ~~~ *In above, the ones provisioned using `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storageclass are the older PVCs; while the ones created with `thin` storageclass are new PVCs.* Tag the older PVCs; ~~~ $ oc label pvc noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-0 pool=mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry $ oc label pvc noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-1 pool=mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry $ oc label pvc noobaastorage-mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-2 pool=mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry ~~~ * Copy the AGENT_CONFIG from an older pod, and add it to the backingstore secret. * We should be now seeing a set of 9 pods for each backingstore. ~~~ mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-0 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 214 19h mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-1 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 214 19h mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-noobaa-2 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 215 19h mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pod-0 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 2m1s mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pod-1 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 31s mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pod-2 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 18s mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pod-10b8f03c 0/1 InvalidImageName 0 18h mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pod-1fad25a9 0/1 InvalidImageName 0 18h mcg-pv-pool-bs-quay-registry-noobaa-pod-2ca5ef99 0/1 InvalidImageName 0 18h ~~~ *The CrashLoopBackOff title: Openshift Container Storage 4.X noobaa-db-0 pod in CrashLoopBackOff fails to start - Fatal Assertion 28558 at src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/wiredtiger_util.cpp 361
issue: This is a OCS 4.4 platform based on VMware, so the OCS/OCP nodes are virtual machines. One Virtual Machine (correspond to OCS storage node "ocp-storage-2") was rebooted sue to some unknown issue. After that reboot, the container inside pod `noobaa-db-0` is failing to start, from pod events: ~~~ Warning BackOff 4m12s (x84 over 22m) kubelet, ocs-storage-0 Back-off restarting failed container ~~~ The reason found was that inside that container there is a MongoDB database that fails to start again and again with the same storage error ending in ~~~ Fatal Assertion 28558 at src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/wiredtiger_util.cpp 361 aborting after fassert() failure ~~~ (see Diagnostic Steps for more detailed logs) Q. What can be done get this database up again (so that pod `noobaa-db-0` will be able to start)?
resolution: 1) Let the system to run fsck on the ceph-rbd device by making the pod `noobaa-db-0` to start on another OCS node. or 2) Manually run fsck de ceph-rbd device or 3) Restore from a previous snapshot. *Note.* Since OCS 4.6, we recommend to take regular snapshots of the PV where this database is allocated, so it could be restored at the point in time where it was collected, all changes after that point would be lost, that means so access to new objects created after that point would be lost too.
root_cause: In this particular case, it seems OCS node was probably hung between 01:43 (last logs were at 01:43:13 CET, see below) and at 9:30 when the system was restarted: "The node was NotReady, the administrator had to turn off, turn on the VM at vCenter because it was unresponsive." ~~~ # tail /var/log/vmware-vmsvc.3.log [2021-01-26T01:42:13.509Z] [warning] [guestinfo] long-name was not set in tools.conf, using empty string. [2021-01-26T01:42:13.511Z] [warning] [guestinfo] GetDiskInfo: ERROR: Partition name buffer too small [2021-01-26T01:42:13.511Z] [warning] [guestinfo] Failed to get disk info. [2021-01-26T01:42:43.510Z] [warning] [guestinfo] long-name was not set in tools.conf, using empty string. [2021-01-26T01:42:43.513Z] [warning] [guestinfo] GetDiskInfo: ERROR: Partition name buffer too small [2021-01-26T01:42:43.513Z] [warning] [guestinfo] Failed to get disk info. [2021-01-26T01:43:13.510Z] [warning] [guestinfo] long-name was not set in tools.conf, using empty string. title: Worker node not coming up in fresh baremetal UPI installation
issue: The worker node was not coming up during the fresh bare metal UPI cluster installation. ~~~ # oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master.example.com Ready master 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 master1.example.com Ready master 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 master2.example.com Ready master 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 ~~~
resolution: - Ensure that all **`pending CSR's`**are approved. ~~~ # oc get csr NAME AGE SIGNERNAME REQUESTOR CONDITION csr-ABCDEF 25m kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client-kubelet system:node:master1.ocp.optional.in Pending,Issued # oc adm certificate approve csr-ABCDEF ~~~- Wait for the second CSR to come up and then **`manually approve`** that as well.- After approving both CSR's, the worker node will come up in the **`NOT READY `** state which will eventually come up in **`READY`** state after some time. ~~~ # oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master.example.com Ready master 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 master1.example.com Ready worker 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 master2.example.com Ready worker 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 worker.example.com NotReady worker 7h v1.13.4+b626c2fe1 ~~~
root_cause: - **`Two CSR certificates need to be approved per worker node`** so that the new worker node is added to the cluster and is available for operation.

title: Kubernetes / Openshift compatible applications
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: Why were my application pods deleted and rescheduled on my Openshift Cluster? Why did my application fail or go offline for a period of time? Is my application Kubernetes compatible/compliant? What is meant by a Kubernetes resilient application? Would my application run well on OpenShift?
resolution: Openshift Container Platform is a certified implementation of Kubernetes therefore OpenShift is expected to manage applications containers as well as Kubernetes. [Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/what-is-kubernetes/#why-you-need-kubernetes-and-what-can-it-do) ~~~ Containers are a good way to bundle and run your applications. In a production environment, you need to manage the containers that run the applications and ensure that there is no downtime. For example, if a container goes down, another container needs to start. Wouldn't it be easier if this behavior was handled by a system?... Kubernetes provides you with: Service discovery and load balancing; Storage orchestration; Automated rollouts and rollbacks, Automatic bin packing; Self-healing. ~~~ From an operational perspective an application needs to be able to handle- Node failures- both planned and unplanned- Application (pod) failures- unplanned- Increases in load. Planned and unplanned For the first 2. This means the application pods can be stopped and restarted in any order so the application pods can not have a defined startup/shutdown order. If possible the cluster will send shutdown signals to the pods, but on the occasions that these signals were not received a a consistency check may also be required on startup. Note, for high availability more than 1 pod is required for each service. For the last point, handling an increase in client load, the cluster can either scale horizontally or vertically. In Kubernetes and more so in OpenShift, it easy to scale horizontally, through using additional pod replicas but this assumes the applications were architectured to scale horizontally. Scaling vertically is also possible but would require pod outages so the CPU and memory can be increased. This may or may not cause minor outages depending on how the application is architectured. Manually scaling out replicas is useful for planned load events but for unplanned load events then the Openshift feature of Horozontal Pod Autosaling would be useful. Just because an application is not fully Kubernetes compatible, it does not mean it wont run on Kubernetes, it just means some of the features mentioned in the quote above will not be compatible with the application. ### Additional resources on application design [Top 10 must-know Kubernetes design patterns](https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2020/05/11/top-10-must-know-kubernetes-design-patterns) [Introduction to Kubernetes patterns](https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/cloud-native-apps/introduction-to-kubernetes-patterns) [Container Design Patterns](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2016/06/container-design-patterns/)

title: Invalid Kafkas CustomResourceDefinition (metadata.annotations too long)
issue: - Invalid Kafkas CustomResourceDefinition when installing the cluster operator (metadata.annotations too long)
resolution: Use the following command to avoid this issue when installing the cluster operator: ~~~ oc-n $NAMESPACE create-f install/cluster-operator \--dry-run=client-o yaml | oc-n $NAMESPACE replace--force-f- ~~~
root_cause: The `kubectl apply` can only handle resources up to some size and the `oc` command line tool is base on that.

title: After reboot, reserved memory size have 4 kb or 8kb less
issue: After reboot, reserved memory size have 4 kb or 8kb less: Before reboot memory size: # cat dmesg | grep "kernel code" [0.000000] Memory: 5237848k/69206016k available (7352k kernel code, 2661536k absent, 1614252k reserved, 6278k data, 1844k init) After reboot memory size: # cat dmesg | grep "kernel code" [0.000000] Memory: 5237848k/69206016k available (7352k kernel code, 2661536k absent, 1614248k reserved, 6278k data, 1844k init)
root_cause: The different size of reserved memory may be caused by some memory pages that cannot be released in time when counting the reserved memory pages during boot progress. And this problem does not often happen, usually discovered after server restart. Restarting the server again can resolve this problem.

issue: Installation fails because get-resources.sh does not honor the no_proxy settings in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.6/4.7 with Installer Provisioned Infrastructure When looking at the logs of the `metal3-(...)` container with `oc logs-l baremetal.openshift.io/cluster-baremetal-operator=metal3-state--all-containers`, one can see: ~~~ 61cd444c-ecdd-458a-b355-9415d93e0dc5_a9a7c74b-cd65-4d95-910c-ee1e9826a0a1_2021-05-21-13-08-55.tar.gz: May 21 09:06:40 worker-3 ironic-python-agent[2659]: 2021-05-21 09:06:40.203 2659 INFO ironic_python_agent.extensions.standby [-] Image /tmp/rhcos-47.83.202103251640-0-compressed.x86_64.qcow2 written to device /dev/sda in 1.641312599182129 seconds ~~~ But then right after that: ~~~ 61cd444c-ecdd-458a-b355-9415d93e0dc5_a9a7c74b-cd65-4d95-910c-ee1e9826a0a1_2021-05-21-13-08-55.tar.gz: May 21 09:06:40 worker-3 ironic-python-agent[2659]: 2021-05-21 09:06:40.243 2659 DEBUG oslo_concurrency.processutils [-] Running cmd (subprocess): blkid-p-o value-s PTTYPE /dev/sda execute /usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/oslo_concurrency/processutils.py:377 61cd444c-ecdd-458a-b355-9415d93e0dc5_a9a7c74b-cd65-4d95-910c-ee1e9826a0a1_2021-05-21-13-08-55.tar.gz: May 21 09:06:40 worker-3 ironic-python-agent[2659]: 2021-05-21 09:06:40.292 2659 DEBUG oslo_concurrency.processutils [-] CMD "blkid-p-o value-s PTTYPE /dev/sda" returned: 2 in 0.049s execute /usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/oslo_concurrency/processutils.py:416 61cd444c-ecdd-458a-b355-9415d93e0dc5_a9a7c74b-cd65-4d95-910c-ee1e9826a0a1_2021-05-21-13-08-55.tar.gz: May 21 09:06:40 worker-3 ironic-python-agent[2659]: 2021-05-21 09:06:40.333 2659 DEBUG oslo_concurrency.processutils [-] 'blkid-p-o value-s PTTYPE /dev/sda' failed. Not Retrying. execute /usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/oslo_concurrency/processutils.py:467 61cd444c-ecdd-458a-b355-9415d93e0dc5_a9a7c74b-cd65-4d95-910c-ee1e9826a0a1_2021-05-21-13-08-55.tar.gz: May 21 09:06:40 worker-3 ironic-python-agent[2659]: 2021-05-21 09:06:40.373 2659 ERROR ironic_lib.disk_utils [-] Failed to retrieve partition table type for disk /dev/sda for node None. Error: Unexpected error while running command. ~~~ Meaning that the image is copied to the worker's disk but that lsblk then does not report any partition table: `Failed to retrieve partition table type for disk /dev/sda for node None. Error: Unexpected error while running command.`
resolution: This is a known bug: * [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1948513](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1948513) * [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1963210](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1963210) * [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1963212](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1963212) Until this is fixed, the only known supported workaround is to set up a disconnected environment for the installation and add the proxy settings only after the deployment. In this case, one can forgo the proxy settings in `install-config.yaml` and avoid this bug altogether. **Remove** the proxy settings pre-installation: * 3.6.2. Setting proxy settings within the install-config.yaml file (optional) [https://openshift-kni.github.io/baremetal-deploy/4.7/Deployment.html#ipi-install-setting-proxy-settings-within-install-config_ipi-install-configuration-files](https://openshift-kni.github.io/baremetal-deploy/4.7/Deployment.html#ipi-install-setting-proxy-settings-within-install-config_ipi-install-configuration-files) **Add** the following pre-installation: * 3.5. Creating an RHCOS images cache (optional) [https://openshift-kni.github.io/baremetal-deploy/4.7/Deployment.html#ipi-install-creating-an-rhcos-images-cache_ipi-install-installation-workflow](https://openshift-kni.github.io/baremetal-deploy/4.7/Deployment.html#ipi-install-creating-an-rhcos-images-cache_ipi-install-installation-workflow) * 3.7. Creating a disconnected registry (optional) [https://openshift-kni.github.io/baremetal-deploy/4.7/Deployment.html#ipi-install-creating-a-disconnected-registry_ipi-install-configuration-files](https://openshift-kni.github.io/baremetal-deploy/4.7/Deployment.html#ipi-install-creating-a-disconnected-registry_ipi-install-configuration-files) **After** installation, set proxy settings: * Configuring the cluster-wide proxy [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/networking/enable-cluster-wide-proxy.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/networking/enable-cluster-wide-proxy.html)

title: TopicAuthorizationException: Not authorized to access topics issue when KafkaConnect connect to Kafka
issue: When I configure my `KafkaConnect` resource to `Kafka` broker, I met the issue: ~~~ org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TopicAuthorizationException: Not authorized to access topics: [connect-cluster-offsets] ~~~
resolution: `Kafka` CR needs to define `authentication` and optionally `authorization` spec and `KafkaConnect` CR needs to reference it as well as `KafkaUser` CR. In the `KafkaUser` CR, define the `topic` and `group` ACLs.- In the `Kafka` CR, make sure below specs are defined properly. Add the `authentication` spec under the `spec.kafka.listeners` for the `tls` listener and add the `spec.kafka.authorization` spec. Here is an example to use `scram-sha-512` type: ~~~ apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 kind: Kafka metadata: name: my-cluster spec: kafka: # defines the authorization type authorization: superUsers:- my-user type: simple...... listeners:......- name: tls port: 9093 tls: true type: internal # defines the authentication type authentication: type: scram-sha-512 ~~~- In the `KafkaUser` CR, make sure the `spec.authentication` is defined properly: ~~~ apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 kind: KafkaUser metadata: name: my-connect labels: # reference the correct cluster name strimzi.io/cluster: my-cluster spec: # Use the same authentication type as Kafka CR defined authentication: type: scram-sha-512 # Use the same authorization type as Kafka CR defined authorization: type: simple acls: # Kafka Connects internal topics used to store configuration, offsets or status # For each internal topic, there are four operations: Read, Describe, Write, Create- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-configs operation: Read- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-configs operation: Describe- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-configs operation: Write- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-configs operation: Create- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-status operation: Read- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-status operation: Describe- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-status operation: Write- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-status operation: Create- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-offsets operation: Read- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-offsets operation: Write- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-offsets operation: Describe- resource: type: topic name: connect-cluster-offsets operation: Create # Additional topics and groups used by connectors # Change to match the topics used by your connectors # For the custom topic, all 4 types of operations are needed # For group, only Read is sufficient- resource: type: group name: my-group patternType: literal operation: Read- resource: type: topic name: my-topic patternType: literal operation: Read- resource: type: topic name: my-topic patternType: literal operation: Describe- resource: type: topic name: my-topic patternType: literal operation: Write- resource: type: topic name: my-topic patternType: literal operation: Create ~~~- In the `KafkaConnect` CR: ~~~ apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 kind: KafkaConnect metadata: name: my-connect annotations: # # use-connector-resources configures this KafkaConnect # # to use KafkaConnector resources to avoid # # needing to call the Connect REST API directly strimzi.io/use-connector-resources: "true" spec: version: 2.7.0 replicas: 1 # Specify the correct bootstrap name by checking bootstrap service name and correct port bootstrapServers: my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap:9093 tls: trustedCertificates:- secretName: my-cluster-cluster-ca-cert certificate: ca.crt # Use the same authentication type as Kafka CR defined authentication: type: scram-sha-512 # Reference the KafkaUser defined previously username: my-connect # KafakaUser will create a same name secret, reference this secret in secretName and retrieve the value from password key passwordSecret: secretName: my-connect password: password config: # Reference the group name defined previously group.id: my-group offset.storage.topic: connect-cluster-offsets config.storage.topic: connect-cluster-configs status.storage.topic: connect-cluster-status ~~~
root_cause: - The required `authentication` or `authorization` spec is not properly defined in `KafkaConnect` CR.- The `KafkaUser` CR does not define all 4 types of operations for the topic defined.

title: kube-scheduler, fatal error: concurrent map writes

title: Achieving (supporting) point to point OpenShift version upgrades
issue: - I have a need to upgrade from one version of OpenShift to another. This path (the point between the two versions) is not represented on the OpenShift upgrade path (directly: point to point). Is upgrading in this fashion supported?
resolution: Support for upgrades is provided from any supported version of OCP to any other (in the 4.x line) To [upgrade between any two versions](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/updating/updating-cluster-cli.html#update-upgrading-cli_updating-cluster-cli ) you can simply run the following: ~~~ oc adm upgrade--to= ~~~- **Note**: that some additional CLI options may be needed; if this path is not in the graph. - See: **--allow-explicit-upgrade=false**: *Upgrade even if the upgrade target is not listed in the available versions list.* (in the help output or man page, for more details)

title: Pods in Openshift-logging (moved to infra nodes) go in pending state after adding defaultNodeSelector.
issue: - All the new or restarted pods in [logging-stack moved to infra nodes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/logging/config/cluster-logging-moving-nodes.html) go in to pending state after [defaultNodeSelector](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/nodes/scheduling/nodes-scheduler-default.html) is added to the cluster.
resolution: - Opting in to `defaultNodeSelector` is an all-in solution. The best approach here to schedule all workload to worker nodes and openshift-logging pods to infra nodes is to apply a label to all worker nodes with the `defaultNodeSelector` and put `taints` on the infra nodes.- By [using tolerations to control cluster logging pod placement](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/logging/config/cluster-logging-tolerations.html) logging pods can be restricted to be placed on `infra nodes` only.
root_cause: - As the `defaultNodeSelector` being a [cluster-wide node selector](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/nodes/scheduling/nodes-scheduler-default.html), **cannot** be used in combination with the [node selectors in ClusterLogging](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/logging/config/cluster-logging-moving-nodes.html).- The `cluster-wide node selector` is applied by the `OpenShift APIserver` which cannot be controlled by the `Cluster Logging Operator`.

title: Manual LDAP sync with non latin characters in Openshift Container Platform.
issue: When trying to [sync LDAP groups](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/authentication/ldap-syncing.html) with the below command: ~~~ $ oc adm groups sync--sync-config={ad_sync_file.yml}--whitelist={ad_sync_whitelist_file.txt}--confirm ~~~ Group `DN's` ended up having non Latin characters in them like: ~~~ **Ö, â, ç, ğ, î, ş, û, ü*
resolution: Make sure `UTF-8` is the default locale's setting for both shell and console: ~~~ $ locale LANG=en_US.UTF-8 LC_CTYPE="en_US.UTF-8" LC_NUMERIC="en_US.UTF-8" LC_TIME="en_US.UTF-8" LC_COLLATE="en_US.UTF-8" LC_MONETARY="en_US.UTF-8" LC_MESSAGES="en_US.UTF-8" LC_PAPER="en_US.UTF-8" LC_NAME="en_US.UTF-8" LC_ADDRESS="en_US.UTF-8" LC_TELEPHONE="en_US.UTF-8" LC_MEASUREMENT="en_US.UTF-8" LC_IDENTIFICATION="en_US.UTF-8" LC_ALL= ~~~ Make sure the remote terminal being used (putty, secure crt, etc) defaults to use `UTF-8` and emulation is set to Xterm. ~~~ Terminal-> Appearance-> Character Encoding to UT-8 ~~~
root_cause: Remote terminal encoding overwrites the local encoding settings.

title: Providing a user with permissions to only deploy applications
issue: need to create a separate user that is allowed to only deploy the application.
resolution: Hello Glenn, Greetings for the day! Welcome to Red Hat Technical Support. My name is Ankit and I'll be assisting you on this case. After reviewing your attachments, I can see the system:deployer clusterrole doesn't have the access to namespace/project by default. `system:deployer` grants the right to deploy within a project and is used primarily with service accounts for automated deployments. Default configuration: ``` $ oc describe clusterrole system:deployer Name: system:deployer Labels: Annotations: openshift.io/description: Grants the right to deploy within a project. Used primarily with service accounts for automated deployments. rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate: true PolicyRule: Resources Non-Resource URLs Resource Names Verbs--------------------------------------------- pods [] [] [create get list watch] events [] [] [create list] imagestreamtags [] [] [create update] imagetags [] [] [create update] imagestreamtags.image.openshift.io [] [] [create update] imagetags.image.openshift.io [] [] [create update] replicationcontrollers [] [] [delete get list update watch] replicationcontrollers/scale [] [] [get update] pods/log [] [] [get] ``` For your requirement, you need to explicitly add the namespace resource to get the access to project. Follow the steps to create a custom clusterrole by extending the system:deployer: 1. Extract the system:deployer yaml #oc get clusterrole system:deployer-o yaml > custom-deployer.yaml 2. Modify the YAML file and add the below line in the end. ```- apiGroups:- "" resources:- namespaces verbs:- get ``` **Also make sure to change the name (let's say system:custom-deployer) and selfLink fields in the yaml. 3. Now add this role to your user/group as per the requirement. #oc policy add-role-to--n I hope this will resolve your issue.-- Regards, Ankit Sachdeva Red Hat
root_cause: `system:` clusterroles are reserved for OCP level access which can be bound to service accounts instead of users. However, it still works if you do a rolebinding with users. But this is not a recommended practice.

title: OpenShift 4.5 and 4.6: Catalog Operator pod consuming a huge amount of CPU

title: Using the cluster CA in OpenShift Pipelines
issue: How can the global cluster certificates be used within OpenShift Pipeline Tasks?
Can a custom PKI be used in OpenShift Pipeline Tasks?
resolution: * This feature is available in OpenShift Pipelines 1.4 and in clusters where [a custom PKI is configured as per the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/networking/configuring-a-custom-pki.html). * The certificate that is defined in the cluster-global `proxy/cluster` object results in the ConfigMap "config-trusted-cabundle" in a namespace: ~~~ $ oc get cm NAME DATA AGE config-service-cabundle 1 40m config-trusted-cabundle 1 40m inject-cluster-certs 0 30m kube-root-ca.crt 1 40m ~~~ * With OpenShift Pipelines 1.4, any ConfigMap named `config-trusted-cabundle` or `config-service-cabundle` is automatically mounted to `SSL_CERT_DIR` (defaults to "/etc/ssl/certs/"). The destination where this is mounted to can be changed by changing the environment variable `SSL_CERT_DIR`. * In the OpenShift Pipelines Task, the CA Bundle is then mounted under `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt`.

title: How to add additional nameservers and search domains in OCP 4.x?
issue: - Is it possible to modify the `nameservers` in `/etc/resolv.conf`?- The Domain Search List provided by DHCP does not contain all the required domains. How can we add additional?- How to update the `nameservers` used by the OpenShift 4.x cluster?- Upstream nameservers have changed and need updating in the OpenShift cluster.
resolution: - In ocp 4.6, NetworkManager uses the keyfile plugin to configure the interface of the RHCOS node, and the connections configs are in `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections`.- To update nameservers, configure the following machine-config to run the `nmcli conn modify` as a one-shot service that executes after network-online.target is up and running. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: add-additional-name-servers-on-worker-role spec: config: ignition: config: {} security: tls: {} timeouts: {} version: 3.1.0 networkd: {} passwd: {} storage: {} systemd: units:- contents: | [Unit] Description=nmcli-con-modify After=network-online.target [Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=nmcli connection modify +ipv4.dns " " #To add additional DNS servers to any previously set, use the + prefix: ExecStartPost=systemctl restart NetworkManager [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target enabled: true name: nmcli-con-modify.service osImageURL: '' ~~~- Once the file is created on the node, the object could be created on the cluster using the following command. ~~~ $ oc create-f dns.yaml ~~~- Wait until the new machine-config is detected on the pool and then using a fresh rendered-worker machine-config the changes would be applied to the worker nodes under the pool.- For the changes to take into effect a reboot is required. **Note:** MachineConfig operator can automatically reboot the node.- On the other hand, a feature NMState Operator recently implemented in 4.7 and the operator will make those changes, As [RFE-1559](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1559), Kubernetes NMState Operator is in Tech Preview in OCP 4.7: [About the Kubernetes NMState Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/networking/k8s_nmstate/k8s-nmstate-about-the-k8s-nmstate-operator.html).
root_cause: - Manually changing the configuration on RHCOS is not supported so Creating a MachineConfig would be the preferred and supported way.- `DNS-Default` pod runs on each node that loads the `/etc/resolv.conf` only when starting pod.

title: Jenkins pod fails to mount the backup data
issue: - Jenkins pod is unable to mount the existing backup data. The backup data is stored on the host machine and needs to be mounted as hostPath.- The pod is crashing with permission denied errors in the logs: ~~~ usr/local/bin/jenkins-common.sh: line 16: /var/lib/jenkins/passwd: Permission denied /usr/local/bin/jenkins-common.sh: line 17: /var/lib/jenkins/passwd: Permission denied ERROR: ld.so: object 'libnss_wrapper.so' from LD_PRELOAD cannot be preloaded: ignored. Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS:-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions-Dsun.zip.disableMemoryMapping=true mkdir: cannot create directory ‘/var/lib/jenkins/logs’: File exists /usr/libexec/s2i/run: line 307: /var/lib/jenkins/image-version: Permission denied Administrative monitors that contact the update center will remain active Detected password environment variable change, updating Jenkins configuration... config.xml sed: couldn't open temporary file /var/lib/jenkins/users/admin_17052214066449153461/sedPCC7eQ: Permission denied /usr/libexec/s2i/run: line 23: /var/lib/jenkins/password: Permission denied ~~~
resolution: - By default jenkins pod is meant to run with restricted scc considering the pods inherit the scc values from the deployment.- The pod was running with the expected scc but, on checking the pod description the following section looked different with runAsUser section ~~~ securityContext: capabilities: drop:- KILL- MKNOD- SETGID- SETUID privileged: false runAsUser: 1000080000 < < ~~~- In the above context runAsUser values was `1000080000` and the existing jenkins backup data directory was having the user ownership with id as `100002000` which was not allowing the pod to start properly.- To fix the issue, change the ownership of the backup data same as mentioned in the pod description's runAsUser section ~~~ chown-R 1000080000 ~~~
root_cause: - The issue was with the mismatch of ownership value configured on the data backup

title: Add additional keystore in existing secrets for new domain
issue: - How to add additional keystore in the existing secrets
resolution: - Create a keystore for mydomain ~~~ $/usr/lib/jvm/jre/bin/keytool-genkey-alias mydomain-keyalg RSA-keystore keystore.jks-keysize 2048 ~~~- Export the Certificate using Keystore ~~~ $/usr/lib/jvm/jre/bin/keytool-export-alias mydomain-file mydomain.crt-keystore keystore.jks $/usr/lib/jvm/jre/bin/keytool-import-trustcacerts-alias mydomain-file mydomain.crt-keystore clientkeystore.jks ~~~ Create a secret in the Cluster using created keystore.jks ~~~ $oc create secret generic rest-keystore--from-file=keystore.jks ~~~- Verify secret creation ~~~ $oc get secrets rest-keystore Opaque 1 28m $oc describe secrets rest-keystore Name: rest-keystore Namespace: default Labels: Annotations: Type: Opaque Data ==== keystore.jks: 2175 bytes ~~~- Perform the same steps for creating new keystore and certificate for new Domain mydomain1 ~~~ $/usr/lib/jvm/jre/bin/keytool-genkey-alias mydomain1-keyalg RSA-keystore keystore1.jks-keysize 2048 $/usr/lib/jvm/jre/bin/keytool-export-alias mydomain1-file mydomain1.crt-keystore keystore1.jks $/usr/lib/jvm/jre/bin/keytool-import-trustcacerts-alias mydomain1-file mydomain1.crt-keystore clientkeystore1.jks ~~~- Convert the new keystore1.jks to base64 ~~~ $openssl base64-in keystore1.jks-out test $ cat test (copy the content) ~~~- Edit the existing secret ~~~ $oc edit secret rest-keystore data: keystore.jks: (Old Entry> keystore1.jks: ~~~- Verify the secret added with new keystore ~~~ $oc get secrets | grep rest-keystore rest-keystore Opaque 2 45m $oc describe secrets rest-keystore Name: rest-keystore Namespace: default Labels: Annotations: Type: Opaque Data ==== keystore.jks: 2175 bytes keystore1.jks: 2245 bytes ~~~

title: oc kustomize error - "couldn't make loader... must be a directory to be root"
issue: - When running code with `oc kustomize.` receive the following error- it seems to be using a yaml file as a directory, however, this works in `kustomize build.`: ~~~ Error: couldn't make loader for gitlab-ci-sa.yaml: got file 'gitlab-ci-sa.yaml', but 'overlays/dev/gitlab-ci-sa.yaml' must be a directory to be a root ~~~- If running the command with `kustomize build overlays/dev` there is no issues with the current version: ~~~ {Version:kustomize/v4.1.3 GitCommit:0f614e92f72f1b938a9171b964d90b197ca8fb68 BuildDate:2021-05-21T17:30:04+01:00 GoOs:darwin GoArch:amd64} ~~~- Since kustomize is actually bundled in kubectl and oc simply acts as a wrapper around kubectl, this is a limitation from the kubernetes level.

title: Infinispan custom resource let project stuck in Terminating Phase
issue: - If a project consisting Red Hat Data Grid operator is deleted without uninstalling the operator properly, the namespace is supposed to stuck in Terminating Phase forever.- All the possible options listed over [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4165791) were tried but no luck deleting the project.- Finalizer value from the project as well as from the `Infinispan` CR could not be removed. ~~~ $ project_status message: 'Some resources are remaining: infinispans.infinispan.org has 1 resource instances' reason: SomeResourcesRemain status: "True" type: NamespaceContentRemaining- lastTransitionTime: "2021-01-06T09:10:45Z" message: 'Some content in the namespace has finalizers remaining: finalizer.infinispan.org in 1 resource instances' reason: SomeFinalizersRemain status: "True" type: NamespaceFinalizersRemaining phase: Terminating ~~~ ~~~ $ oc patch-n dev Infinispan/example-infinispan--type=merge-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":null}}' The Infinispan "example-infinispan" is invalid:
spec.security.endpointEncryption.type: Unsupported value: "": supported values: "Service", "service", "Secret", "secret", "None"
status.security.endpointEncryption.type: Unsupported value: "": supported values: "Service", "service", "Secret", "secret", "None" ~~~
resolution: - The hack should be like this: `oc edit crd infinispans.infinispan.org`then find and remove in editor this yaml snippet: ~~~ enum:- Service- service- Secret- secret- None ~~~- Two times one in the spec and one in the status.- At this point the CR infinispan should be editable in order to remove the finalizer value.
root_cause: - Infinispan CR was stuck with a finalizer which had to be removed with the help of infinispan CRD.

Check logs fore more info.""}" "{""message"":""org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.CommitFailedException: Commit cannot be completed since the group has already rebalanced and assigned the partitions to another member. title: Prometheus dropping samples/s with timestamps arriving out of order.
issue: - Receiving the alert message as below in the OCP console: ~~~ Prometheus openshift-monitoring/prometheus-k8s-0 is dropping 35.74 samples/s with timestamps arriving out of order. ~~~- The Prometheus pods shows below warnings: ~~~ 2021-02-25T10:19:22.208961998Z level=warn ts=2021-02-25T10:19:22.208Z caller=scrape.go:1372 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=openshift-multus/monitor-network/0 target=https://x.x.x.x:8443/metrics msg="Error on ingesting out-of-order samples" num_dropped=18 2021-02-25T10:19:26.183671522Z level=warn ts=2021-02-25T10:19:26.183Z caller=scrape.go:1372 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=openshift-monitoring/node-exporter/0 target=https://x.x.x.x:9100/metrics msg="Error on ingesting out-of-order samples" num_dropped=1587 ~~~
resolution: - Make sure to configure the Chrony time service by following the documentation [Configuring chrony time service](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/install_config/installing-customizing.html#installation-special-config-chrony_installing-customizing)- Synchronizing nodes of the OpenShift cluster to internal NTP servers is definitely preferred over synchronization to a random selection of public servers like `pool.ntp.org`.
root_cause: - Prometheus relies on accurate time for its TSDB and will throw errors when trying to ingest (scrape) metrics if records already exist for the target within the same time frame. This can be caused by clock skew (time drift on nodes) or duplicate targets being scraped.

title: Scale Worker-MachineSet get overridden
issue: We would like to scale the default Worker-MachineSet to a higher Number, but it always gets scaled back. Stated in https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.2/html-single/manage_cluster/index#resizing-a-cluster it should work by modifying the MachineSet. We did (directly in OpenShift trough Compute/MachineSets/) but it does not work.
resolution: In our case local cluster was deployed by hive. Hive has a Machinepool that is being constantly reconciled by the Hive operator as the MachinePool is the parent(guide) for remote MachineSets. Changing is possible by finding the MachinePool associated with the hive deployed cluster and change the value of replicas. For example: #kubectl patch machinepool cahl-vmware-worker-n cahl-vmware--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"replicas":4}}' OR directly edit the file to change the number of replicas.
root_cause: local cluster was deployed by hive. Machinepool is being constantly reconciled by the Hive operator.

title: Configure an external ElasticSearch cluster for the Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh 2.x
issue: We would like to use an external ElasticSearch cluster for the Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh version 2.x. Is there a way to configure this? We found this solution https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4600591, but only applies to version 1.0 of Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh.
resolution: If you would like to use an external ElasticSearch cluster for the Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh version 2.x you need to: 1) Install Jaeger operator standalone instead of as part of Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh [1]. 2) After you have installed the Jaeger operator you can configure it to point to an external ElasticSearch using the documentation [2]. 3) When you follow the instructions [3] to install the operators for Service Mesh v2.x omit the installation of the ElasticSearch and Jaeger operators 4) Configure your ServiceMeshControlPlane resource to use the standalone Jaeger instance rather than the one installed with Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh [4]. [1] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/jaeger/jaeger_install/rhbjaeger-installation.html [2] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/jaeger/jaeger_install/rhbjaeger-deploying.html#jaeger-config-external-es_jaeger-deploying [3] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/service_mesh/v2x/installing-ossm.html [4] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/service_mesh/v2x/ossm-observability.html#ossm-config-external-jaeger_observability

title: Grant a Service Account permission to create a project with a nodeSelector in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - Granting the `admin` role to the service account does not allow the creation of namespaces with a node selector.- The creation of a new project with a node selector is limited to the `oc adm`command.
resolution: - Create a cluster role `namespace-manager`: ~~~ $ oc create clusterrole namespace-manager--verb=create,delete,get,list,patch,update,watch--resource=namespace ~~~ Add the `namespace-manager` clusterrole to the service account: ~~~ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user namespace-manager system:serviceaccount:default:robot ~~~- Login as the service account: ~~~ $ oc serviceaccounts get-token system:serviceaccount:default:robot # token prints here $ oc login--token= ~~~ Create a new project with a--node-selector definition: ~~~ $ oc new-project dev-project \--node-selector='type=developer,region=west' ~~~
root_cause: - This restriction on the creation of projects with a nodeSelector is due to the fact that the clusterrole `admin` does not have `create` or other verbs on the `namespace` resource or `namespace/status` resource.: ~~~ oc export clusterrole admin | grep-i namespaces-C 10- patch- update- watch- apiGroups:- "" attributeRestrictions: null resources:- bindings- events- limitranges- namespaces/status- pods/log- pods/status- replicationcontrollers/status- resourcequotas- resourcequotas/status verbs:- get- list- watch- apiGroups:- "" attributeRestrictions: null resources:- namespaces verbs:- get- list- watch ~~~
