title: How to add new storage devices to swift (managed by Director)
issue: Need to add new swift device in the following environment:- RHOSP 13, 16.0, 16.1- During overcloud deployment Swift was configured to use `/srv/node/d1` as a storage device (folder on local disk).- Existing overcloud templates were customized. `SwiftRawDisks` parameter was defined to use `/dev/vdb` drive to store swift data.- `/dev/vdb` wasn't used after running deploy command. Need to finish swift data migration and delete `/srv/node/d1` from list of swift's storage devices.
resolution: This KCS is a comprehensive guide for many different use cases. Be sure to follow the procedures for the correct chapter. If there should be any question, please contact Red Hat Support. ### How to Format devices to be used by Swift Note: The content of this KCS is a candidate to be merged in Red Hat OpenStack Platform product guide, as per [this BZ](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/1882186). While that BZ is open, this KCS will temporarily host details on how format and prepare disks, to be added to Swift, as well. In order to function properly, Swift needs to manage file-systems that can handle extra attributes (e.g. `xfs`) ~~~ # mkdir /srv/node/sdx # chown root:root /srv/node/sdx # This step is incredibly important, see the note below. # fdisk /dev/sdx # partprobe # This example creates only one partition. Please adjust it to the use case of the environment.... Select (default p): p <==== Partition number (1-4, default 1): 1 <== First sector (2048-20971519, default 2048): Enter Using default value 2048 Last sector, +sectors or +size{K,M,G} (2048-20971519, default 20971519): +XXG Partition 1 of type Linux and of size XX GiB is set Save the partition table changes. Command (m for help): w <===... # mkfs-t xfs /dev/sdx # blkid ~~~ Edit `/etc/fstab` to include the above added device. Red Hat suggests to use `UUID` instead of the disk paths, in order to avoid issues on kernel updates. ~~~ UUID=" " /srv/node/sdx xfs noatime 0 2 ~~~ For more details refer to [this BZ](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1767698). Finally mount the device and adjust its permissions ~~~ # mount-a # mount | grep-w /srv/node/sdx # semanage fcontext-l | grep /srv/node/ # Confirm the current environment has the correct labeling rules in place before Swift start transferring data # chown 42445:42445 /srv/node/sdx # chmod 755 /srv/node/sdx ~~~ Please keep in mind that having `42445:42445` owning the mount point before the device is properly mounted might enable Swift to write in the root filesystem. Due to containerization, this risk is mitigated, but please make sure to have the mount point owned by `root:root` until the device is confirmed to be mounted, and to be having the correct permissions as extra precautions. Once the above steps are completed, refer to the following sections on how to update the rings and rebalance accordingly to have this new device managed by Swift. ### Setting proper permissions for new swift devices There is a hidden issue that could cause data corruption and should be addressed before taking any further steps. RHOSP director will not set proper permissions for swift drives that were added this way. As a result, you will have the following picture: ~~~ [heat-admin@controller-0 ~]$ ls-lZ /srv/node/ drwxr-xr-x. 42445 42445 system_u:object_r:var_t:s0 d1 drwxr-xr-x. root root system_u:object_r:unlabeled_t:s0 vdb ~~~ You need to reset the owner and Selinux label on all Controller and Object Storage nodes by taking the following steps on director node with active stackrc environment file:- use `nova list` command to obtain a list of IP addresses that belong to affected nodes;- run the following script on director node to obtain information about current state of your environment (please adjust IP settings): ~~~ for i in 8 11 23; do ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$i" 'sudo ls-lh /srv/node/; sudo ls-lZ /srv/node'; done ~~~- run the following script on director node to fix ownership and permissions (you may need to adjust UID/GID):- In RHOSP13 and 14 ~~~ for i in 8 11 23; do ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$i" 'sudo chown 42445:42445 /srv/node/vdb/; sudo chcon-t var_t /srv/node/vdb/'; done ~~~- In RHOSP15 and later ~~~ for i in 8 11 23; do ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$i" 'sudo chown 42445:42445 /srv/node/vdb/; sudo chcon-t container_file_t /srv/node/vdb/'; done ~~~- confirm that all Controller and Object Storage nodes have proper permissions. ### Get overcloud Swift ring files and commit changes to their undercloud copy #### Getting ring files from undercloud Undercloud's object storage stores a copy of overcloud swift ring files. This copy will be used to deploy new Object Storage nodes and replace existing Controller and Object Storage nodes. We will use this copy to modify overcloud ring files and distribute them across the nodes. Steps to get overcloud Swift rings on director node with active stackrc environment file: ~~~ $ mkdir temp && cd temp/ $ swift download overcloud-swift-rings swift-rings.tar.gz $ tar xzvf swift-rings.tar.gz $ mkdir backup && cp swift-rings.tar.gz backup/ ~~~ Swift rings files will be available in `etc/swift` folder. #### Uploading modified ring files back to undercloud object storage Undercloud needs to have up-to-date copy of overcloud ring files to properly provision new Object Storage nodes and replaced Controller and Object Storage nodes. As a result, changed ring files should be uploaded back to Undercloud Object Storage: ~~~ tar cvzf swift-rings.tar.gz etc/ swift upload overcloud-swift-rings swift-rings.tar.gz ~~~ ### Get information about current state of swift cluster Swift ring files could be viewed as configuration files that describe high-level state of Swift cluster. There should be no difference between Swift ring files obtained from undercloud object storage and the ones that are used on existing Controller and Object Storage nodes. A `swift-ring-builder` command should be used to get a human-readable information from existing ring files and to modify those files. Here are commands that will show the state of standard rings: ~~~ swift-ring-builder /etc/swift/account.builder swift-ring-builder /etc/swift/container.builder swift-ring-builder /etc/swift/object.builder ~~~ ### Changing rings `swift-ring-builder` command could be used to make various changes to ring files. Here are commands that should be used to replace Swift device:- `swift-ring-builder BUILDER_FILE rebalance` should be used to apply changes;- `swift-ring-builder BUILDER_FILE add` should be used to add `/srv/node/vdb` devices to existing rings;- `swift-ring-builder BUILDER_FILE set_weight` should be used to reduce the weight of `/srv/node/d1` devices to zero;- `swift-ring-builder BUILDER_FILE remove` should be used to remove `/srv/node/d1` devices. ### Syncing the changes Swift services were containerized in RHOSP 12. As a result, changed ring files should be delivered to containers. The problem is that configuration directories aren't mounted to swift containers directly, so containers must be restarted after new ring files are copied to proper folders. Here is a script that could be used to distribute ring files from director node to a specified Controllers and restart swift containers on those nodes: ~~~ cd etc/swift/ for j in 8 11 23; do ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" "rm *.ring.gz" for i in account.ring.gz container.ring.gz object.ring.gz; do scp $i heat-admin@192.168.24."$j":~/ ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" "sudo cp-f "$i" /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/swift/etc/swift/" ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" "sudo chown root:root /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/swift/etc/swift/"$i"" ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" "sudo restorecon /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/swift/etc/swift/"$i"" done ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" "rm *.builder" for i in account.builder container.builder object.builder; do scp $i heat-admin@192.168.24."$j":~/ ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" "cat "$i" | sudo tee /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/swift/etc/swift/"$i" > /dev/null" done ssh heat-admin@192.168.24."$j" 'for k in `sudo docker ps--format "{{.Names}}" | grep swift`; do sudo docker restart $k; done' done cd../../ ~~~ ### Rebalancing properly Don't migrate all the data at once. The cluster would not be able to handle the load generated by replicators working to move **all** the data at once. And there would be a time when all of the old data would be on the source device but the ring would point to the new target device for all replicas. Until replicators moved **all** the data to the target device, the data would be inaccessible. Ideally, split the move into 10% chunks. First put weight of 90.0 to the old, source device and 10.0 to the new, target device. Let replicators move the data. Then, do 80 and 20. Repeat until all the data is moved over. ### Putting everything together Here is a list of actions that were taken in a testing environment to migrate the data from `/srv/node/d1`: 1. Restored permissions as described in *Setting proper permissions for new swift devices section above. 2. Obtained swift ring files from Undercloud's object storage as described in *Getting ring files from undercloud* subsection above. 3. Obtained information about current state of the swift cluster as described in *Get information about current state of swift cluster* above. Node's IP addresses, device IDs and names, regions and zone numbers should be used in the following commands. 4. Added new device to rings and rebalanced: ~~~ swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder add z1-172.X.4.10:6002/vdb 100 # z1 is a zone number to use. In my case there was only one zone swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder add z1-172.X.4.15:6002/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder add z1-172.X.4.18:6002/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder add z1-172.X.4.10:6001/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder add z1-172.X.4.15:6001/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder add z1-172.X.4.18:6001/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder add z1-172.X.4.10:6000/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder add z1-172.X.4.15:6000/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder add z1-172.X.4.18:6000/vdb 100 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder rebalance swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder rebalance swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder rebalance ~~~ In this particular case `swift-ring-builder... rebalance` command printed the following warning message, so there was a need to wait for one hour AFTER SYNCING the changes (taking next step): ~~~ Reassigned 1024 (100.00%) partitions. Balance is now 33.40. Dispersion is now 0.00------------------------------------------------------------------------------- NOTE: Balance of 33.40 indicates you should push this ring, wait at least 1 hours, and rebalance/repush.------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ~~~ 5. Synced the changed ring files as described in *Syncing the changes* section above. 6. Took 1 hour break. 7. Rebalanced the rings: ~~~ swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder rebalance swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder rebalance swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder rebalance ~~~ 8. Synced the changed ring files as described in *Syncing the changes* section above. 9. Adjusted weight of original device (need to use d1 device IDs from the first step): ~~~ swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder set_weight d0 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder set_weight d1 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder set_weight d2 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder set_weight d0 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder set_weight d1 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder set_weight d2 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder set_weight d0 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder set_weight d1 0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder set_weight d2 0 ~~~ 10. Rebalanced the rings and synced the changed ring files. 11. Deleted old devices: ~~~ swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder remove d0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder remove d1 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/account.builder remove d2 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder remove d0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder remove d1 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/container.builder remove d2 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder remove d0 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder remove d1 swift-ring-builder etc/swift/object.builder remove d2 ~~~ 12. Rebalanced the rings and synced the changed ring files. 13. Uploaded changed overcloud Swift rings to Undercloud object storage as described in *Uploading modified ring files back to undercloud object storage* above. **IMPORTANT** Swift logs located at Controller and Object Storage nodes in `/var/log/containers/swift/` folder should be used to check the status of the storage after any change above.
root_cause: Red Hat OpenStack director doesn't manage existing swift rings: it only creates them during first deployment and uses existing ring files to deploy additional Controller and Object Storage nodes. As a result, it is impossible to change actual data distribution by defining `SwiftRawDisks` for existing overcloud stack.

title: All request are routed to same pod
issue: - Testing multipod deployment all request goes to same pod
resolution: Openshift is based on kubernetes. You can define wether all request remember the pod for same IP https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/ with sessionAffinity
root_cause: Openshift is configured to use sessionAffinity=clientIP which always route request from same IP to same pod.

title: How to set a predefined password for the core user in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x?
issue: How to set a predefined password for the core user in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x?
resolution: Generate a sha512 password. For example, one can use ansible to achieve this. ~~~ # subscription-manager repos--enable ansible-2.9-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms # yum install ansible-y ~~~ The following example hashes password `redhat`: ~~~ $ password=$(ansible-m debug-a msg="{{'redhat' | password_hash('sha512')}}" localhost | awk '/msg/ {print $NF}' | sed 's/^"//' | sed 's/"$//') $ echo $password $6$1CfdjqP/tslNaimn$fgtdAhWs3bH8tSLuJaOJGD/TPCuQwImRb22tADAEwZfqVn1fZjCc.3uNKD1BCckt3Lasv/9s.Va7E2Jr.NR8U1 ~~~ Now, inject the password into the master and worker nodes. In order to do so, generate the ignition files and modify them with `jq`: ~~~ $ openshift-baremetal-install create ignition-configs--dir=openshift-install (...) $ for type in master worker; do cat /root/openshift-install/${type}.ign | jq '. += {"passwd": {"users": [{"name": "core", "passwordHash": "'$(echo-n $password)'"}]}}' | tee /root/openshift-install/${type}.ign done ~~~

title: Why a VM container is going into pending state in OpenShift Container Platform 4.6?
issue: Unable to start VM in Container Native Virtualization. ~~~ Warning FailedScheduling 11m default-scheduler 0/14 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient devices.kubevirt.io/tun, 10 Insufficient devices.kubevirt.io/vhost-net, 14 Insufficient devices.kubevirt.io/kvm. ~~~
resolution: * Enable hardware assist virtualization or[Virtualization Hardware Extensions on Physical machines.](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html-single/virtualization_deployment_and_administration_guide/index#sect-Troubleshooting-Enabling_Intel_VT_x_and_AMD_V_virtualization_hardware_extensions_in_BIOS)
root_cause: * Usage of VMs as worker nodes for OpenShift Virtualization is not supported in a nested virtualization deployment.

title: --node-ip parameter not visible in kubelet.service file
issue: Not able to define specific node IP for internal communication in kubelet.service file.
resolution: In 4.6, the--node-ip is populated only if API internal VIP is set in infrastructure object. And that field is only set in vsphere IPI platforms (because it is managed by platform) but not in UPI, so this ultimately translates in the node-ip parameter never to be present on vsphere UPI. Given that it is not supported to modify the unit, this in turn means you cannot set node-ip.
root_cause: If we check at [MCO source code](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/release-4.6/templates/worker/01-worker-kubelet/vsphere/units/kubelet.service.yaml) on #L31, it will only be present in Vsphere IPI installation.

title: How to ensure that the ImagePullPolicy is set to `always` for every image in OpenShift 4
issue: In OCP 3.11 it is possible to enable the [AlwaysPullImages admission controller](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/image_policy.html#image-policy-always-pull-images). It will ensure that the `ImagePullPolicy` is set to `Always`. There is no similar content in the OCP 4 documentation.
resolution: AlwaysPullImages feature is not supported in OCP 4. A Request for Feature Enhancement (RFE) was filed to evaluate the feasibility of adding this functionality in future releases of OpenShift. For more information, or to also request this feature, please open a [support case with Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new) [^1]. [^1]:
root_cause: Currently there is no supported way to enable the AlwaysPullImages admission controller in OCP 4.x

title: Configuring custom Grafana with Prometheus from OCP/OSD
issue: - Need to configure the Grafana DataSource with OCP/OSD Prometheus.- Not able to customize shipped Grafana.- No permission to add user to your existing Prometheus secret(prometheus-k8s-htpasswd)
resolution: ## NOTE: Custom Grafana does not permit Red Hat support to assist you. ### Requirements:- A custom installation of Grafana- oc cli (you can use the webconsole(**not is covered at this sample**) if you are able to use it). ### Steps: If you have a need for a custom Grafana installation and have to connect it to the Prometheus provided by Openshift(OCP/OSD), you can follow these steps: 1- Create a Service Account ~~~ oc create sa ~~~ 2- Grant the cluster-monitoring-view cluster role to the service account created. [You must use a role that has read access to all namespaces, such as the cluster-monitoring-view](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.1/monitoring/cluster_monitoring/prometheus-alertmanager-and-grafana.html#monitoring-accessing-prometheus-alertmanager-grafana-directly_accessing-prometheus) ~~~ oc-n adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user view-z ~~~ 3- Get service account token created in the previous step ~~~ oc serviceaccounts get-token-n ~~~ 4- Get the token and use it to authenticate. 5- Update or Create the GrafanaDataSource ~~~ apiVersion: 1 datasources:- access: proxy basicAuth: false withCredentials: false isDefault: true jsonData: timeInterval: 5s tlsSkipVerify: true **httpHeaderName1: "Authorization"** name: Prometheus secureJsonData: ** httpHeaderValue1: "Bearer...eyJ..."** type: prometheus **URL: ** version: 1 ~~~ 6- restart the grafana pod.

title: WARN  [org.apache.activemq.artemis.utils.actors.OrderedExecutor] Java heap space: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
issue: - Broker runs out of memory and throws an exception while adding more messages to page store: ~~~ WARN [org.apache.activemq.artemis.utils.actors.OrderedExecutor] Java heap space: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space ~~~
root_cause: The current implementation of paging creates caches for paged messages to facilitate quick delivery of those messages. Those caches are per queue and can be as 60 MB in size per each destination. This may lead to the exhaustion of JVM heap memory if there is a large number of destinations in paged mode. For example for a broker with 1000 destinations all in page mode the cache alone can take up up to 60 GB of heap space. This has been logged as bug [ENTMQBR-5192](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ENTMQBR-5192). The only way at the moment to reduce the size of this cash is to reduce the page size ` ` and ` `.

title: How to change Jenkins Agent Maven's OpenJDK  version in Openshift Container Platform 4
issue: The `Jenkins Maven Agent` by defaults uses `OpenJDK 11`, but it is possible to customize it to use `OpenJDK 8`: ~~~ bash-4.4# mvn-version Apache Maven 3.6.2 (Red Hat 3.6.2-6) Maven home: /usr/share/maven Java version: 11.0.11, vendor: Red Hat, Inc., runtime: /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-11.0.11.0.9-2.el8_4.x86_64 Default locale: en_US, platform encoding: UTF-8 OS name: "linux", version: "5.10.25-linuxkit", arch: "amd64", family: "unix" ~~~
resolution: .- Create a `ConfigMap` to overwrite file `/etc/java/maven.conf` with the following content: ~~~ JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.8.0-openjdk ~~~.- Add the `ConfigMap` to the `OSE Jenkins Maven Agent` and set the `mountPath` to: ~~~ /etc/java/maven.conf ~~~ After starting the pod, `Maven` will use `OpenJDK 8`, which can be verified in the pod: ~~~ bash-4.4# mvn-version Apache Maven 3.6.2 (Red Hat 3.6.2-6) Maven home: /usr/share/maven Java version: 1.8.0_292, vendor: Red Hat, Inc., runtime: /usr/lib/jvm/java-1.8.0-openjdk-1.8.0.292.b10-1.el8_4.x86_64/jre Default locale: en_US, platform encoding: UTF-8 OS name: "linux", version: "5.10.25-linuxkit", arch: "amd64", family: "unix" ~~~
root_cause: By default, `Apache's Maven` installation on the `OSE/Jenkins Maven Agent` image uses the `JDK` indicated on `/etc/java/maven.conf`. Even when `OpenJDK 8` is installed, `Maven` will only use the version configured in `/etc/java/maven.conf`.

title: Brick multiplexing in Red Hat Gluster on-premise environments
issue: Brick multiplexing is only supported for OpenShift Container Storage environments as it´s indicated in [RHGS 3.5 Administration guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_gluster_storage/3.5/html-single/administration_guide/index#many-bricks-per-node-multiplex)
resolution: In the case brick multiplexing option is enabled in a Red Hat Gluster on-premise environment please follow the steps to disable it 1. In one of the nodes execute #gluster volume set all cluster.brick-multiplex off 2. Restart one by one the nodes, between each reboot check the bricks of the node rebooted are online # gluster volume status

title: How to collect ongoing performance data in ARO cluster for troubleshooting CPU throttling issues
issue: - Pods running with CPU limits and a high number of threads show CPU throttling despite the CPU limit is not hit.- The default Grafana dashboard shows CPU throttling even though CPU usage does not touch its limit.- You want to collect performance data to troubleshoot the CPU throttling issues
resolution: > **Important note:** The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted [Service Level Agreements](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/production/sla.html) and [support procedures](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/production/soc.html). Installing unsupported packages does not necessarily make a system unsupportable by Red Hat Global Support Services; however, Red Hat Global Support Services will be unable to support or debug problems with packages not shipped in standard RHEL channels. Installing packages from EPEL is done at the user's own risk.** Setup and configure a collectl debug daemonset which can be deployed to required nodes Please obtain the YAML files in the following GitHub project: https://github.com/tunacado/openshift4-debug Ensure you a logged into your cluster as a user with admin privileges. and run the following command to set up the namespace, security context constraints, and service account: ~~~ $ git clone https://github.com/robbmanes/openshift4-debug Next follow the steps outlined here to create the collectl pods deployed to each node in order to log the data we need: https://github.com/tunacado/openshift4-debug/tree/main/utilities/collectl $ cd openshift4-debug/ $ oc create-f openshift4-debug.yaml $ oc project openshift4-debug $ cd utilities/collectl/ $ oc create-f imagestream.yaml $ oc create configmap collectl-entrypoint--from-file entrypoint.sh $ oc create-f buildconfig.yaml The build for the container image should finish eventually: $ oc get build $ oc create-f daemonset.yaml Please be sure to adequately label the nodes so that the collectl daemonSet is deployed on each. $ oc label node worker-0.example.com collectl="true" ~~~ check if debug pod is running and collectl pods are deployed ~~~ $ oc get pods $ oc logs collectl-example ~~~ Once the pods have been scheduled and are executing on the nodes in question, you can `oc exec` to the pods in order to verify that they are collecting data from within the pod: ~~~ $ oc exec $COLLECTL-POD ls /var/log/collectl/ ~~~ When needed, you can copy log files out of the pod like so: ~~~ $ oc cp:/var/log/collectl/.raw.gz ~/Downloads/.raw.gz $ oc cp:/var/log/collectl/.log ~/Downloads/.log ~~~ Gathering "before" sosreport Collect a sosreport from a node immediately before running your test (We are using this to capture data under /sys/fs/cgroup). To do so, please follow the instructions provided here: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3820762 ~~~ Find which node the debug pod is running: $ oc get pods-o wide Access the node with `oc debug $NODE` and run the `toolbox` command to generate a debug container that will contain the sosreport command. $ oc debug node/ sh-4.4# chroot /host sh-4.4# toolbox # note: you may want to remove the container and start with a fresh toolbox to ensure you can oc cp the sosreport off the node [root@node ~]# sosreport-k crio.all=on-k crio.logs=on You can copy the sosreport off the node while the debug shell was still running like so: $ oc cp:/host/var/tmp/sosreport-.tar.xz ~/Downloads/sosreport-.tar.xz ~~~ Run your application test and record the relevant timestamps including start and stop. Or you can use this command to run the test pod with limits you want to test ~~~ $ oc-n openshift4-debug run limit-test--image=registry.redhat.io/ubi7-minimal--requests "cpu=50m,memory=512m"--limits "cpu=200m,memory=1G"--command-- /bin/sh-c "dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/null" ~~~ Collect CPU shares, stat, cfs_quota_us data every 30 seconds ~~~ Check the cgroup system information by opening another debug shell Finding which node the limit-test pod is running: $ oc get pods-o wide $ oc debug node/ sh-4.4# chroot /host Finding the pod name and ID via crictl: sh-4.4# crictl pods | grep limit-test Getting the path to the cgroup: sh-4.4# crictl inspectp | grep cgroupsPath sh-4.4# cd /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-burstable.slice/kubepods-burstable-podxxx.slice/ sh-4.4# while true; do date > > /tmp/.log; cat cpu.{shares,stat,cfs_quota_us} > > /tmp/.log; sleep 30; done ~~~ Gathering "after" sosreport Immediately after running your test, collect a second sosreport using the same steps as for Gathering "before" sosreport Copy the contents of /var/log/collectl inside of the `collectl` pod on the node in question and provide them to us. Collect the grafana graphs. ~~~ CPU Usage query: `sum(node_namespace_pod_container:container_cpu_usage_seconds_total:sum_rate{namespace="openshift4-debug", pod="limit-test"}) by (container)` CPU Throttling query: `sum(increase(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{namespace="openshift4-debug",pod="limit-test",container="limit-test"}[5m])) by (container) / sum(increase(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{namespace="openshift4-debug",pod="limit-test",container="limit-test"}[5m])) by (container)` ~~~

title: Monitoring operator degraded due to empty value of ca-bundle.crt
issue: - Cluster upgrade stuck with monitoring operator degraded due to empty `ca-bundle.crt` in configmap: ~~~ status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: "2021-07-12T11:26:32Z" message: 'Failed to rollout the stack. Error: running task Updating Alertmanager failed: syncing Thanos Querier trusted CA bundle ConfigMap failed: waiting for config map key "ca-bundle.crt" in openshift-monitoring/alertmanager-trusted-ca-bundle ConfigMap object failed: timed out waiting for the condition: empty value' reason: UpdatingAlertmanagerFailed status: "True" type: Degraded ~~~
resolution: 1. Verify the content of `alertmanager-trusted-ca-bundle` configmap: $ oc-n openshift-monitoring get cm alertmanager-trusted-ca-bundle-oyaml apiVersion: v1 data: ca-bundle.crt: "" < <== empty value kind: ConfigMap metadata:... name: alertmanager-trusted-ca-bundle... 2. Copy the content of `/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem` file from one of the worker nodes: $ oc debug node/ sh-4.4# chroot /host sh-4.4# scp /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem @:/ // exit from the debug pod // once copied, modify the copied file in order to align the spaces (on bastion node) $ sed-i-e 's/^/ /' $ cat // copy the complete output 3. Modify the `data.ca-bundle.crt` section of the respective configmap: $ oc-n openshift-monitoring edit cm alertmanager-trusted-ca-bundle // paste the copied content in the following manner: apiVersion: v1 data: ca-bundle.crt: | < <== do add the pipe(|) to start the block # ACCVRAIZ1-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- // save & exit

title: Corrupt Prometheus Database in OCP
issue: Pods won't start or shows a state of `CrashBackoff`
Pod logs show: caller=main.go:596 err="Opening storage failed invalid block sequence: block time ranges overlap: [mint: 1622340000000, maxt: 1622347200000, range: 2h0m0s, blocks: 369]:....
resolution: Delete the pods and let the operator restart them. $ oc delete pod/prometheus-k8s-0-n openshift-monitoring $ oc delete pod/prometheus-k8s-1-n openshift-monitoring
root_cause: The local database is corrupted. Deleting the data will only lose a short window of information, and since the local database is only stored in the transient disk space of the POD, deleting it should resolve the issue. From the [Prometheus storage documentation](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/2.28/getting_started/): > If your local storage becomes corrupted for whatever reason, the best strategy to address the problem is to shut down Prometheus then remove the entire storage directory. You can also try removing individual block directories, or the WAL directory to resolve the problem. Note that this means losing approximately two hours data per block directory. Again, Prometheus's local storage is not intended to be durable long-term storage; external solutions offer extended retention and data durability.

title: Why the "User Access Administrator" on azure is required for OpenShift 4 IPI installation?
issue: - Why the Azure Account requires the "User Access Administrator" to install the OCP 4 via IPI as [documented](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing_azure/installing-azure-account.html#installation-azure-permissions_installing-azure-account)?
resolution: The azure installer creates new identities for the cluster and therefore requires access to create new roles, and role assignments. Therefore the service principal to have at least "User Access Administrator" roles assigned in the subscription. Refer:-- Attach Administrative Role https://github.com/openshift/installer/blob/master/docs/user/azure/credentials.md#step-3-attach-administrative-role The required permissions are *not* broken down beyond the two role assignments (as documented here: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing_azure/installing-azure-account.html#installation-azure-permissions_installing-azure-account), however, here’s what those roles are used for so you have a better understanding of why they’re needed: 1. User Access Administrator: Needed to provide a managed identity to the OpenShift VM’s so they can access the Azure Cloud APIs. If you don’t enable this, the node itself won’t be able to connect to any Azure cloud resources. 2. Contributor Role of Subscription: Needed to create/manage any Azure resources (resource group, network resources, etc.) during both install (for IPI) and the (Day 2) operation of the cluster. While there may be a subset of certain permissions that aren’t needed under the Contributor role, we don’t have any plans to scope permissions beyond this high-level role assignment since contributor role is also what is required for ARO clusters. 3. (optionally) AAD Graph Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy permissions needs to be granted to the SP: This is used to mint finer grained (reduced scope) SP’s for OpenShift components requiring cloud API access. If this is not granted to the SP, then the SP is used 'as-is' and passed through to all OpenShift components requiring Cloud API access (internal registry, Machine API, Ingress, etc.) If you are concerned with providing a SP that has contributor role enabled for the subscription, then you can always look at scoping it to to just the OpenShift Resource Group. Depending on the installation method, this can be accomplished on Day 1 or Day 2: 1. Using IPI workflow with a SP scoped to the subscription for Day 1 installation then re-scope it to the RG once you know the name on Day 2. The reason it can’t be done on Day 1 is that the installer creates its own RG for the OpenShift deployment during the installation process, so there’s no way to scope the SP to this RG in advance of installation since it won’t yet exist. Additionally, there’s no way to pass in a pre-existing RG to the installer in the IPI workflow, so It’s going to require development work to support this. (https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CORS-1482) 2. Use UPI workflow to deploy to an empty (we don not support deploying to shared RG’s), user-created RG using a SP scoped to that RG. If you do want to scope the SP to a particular resource group on Day 2 for IPI or Day 1 for UPI, then you’d minimally need: Contributor role for RG, Contributor for VNet, Contributor for public DNS zone, and User Access Administrator for RG, User Access Administrator access for VNet

title: Pod runs in default project but fails in a custom project
issue: - Some pods are able to run in `default` project but failed to run in custom project due to permission errors, similar to something below. ~~~... 10-listen-on-ipv6-by-default.sh: info: can not modify /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf (read-only file system?)... 2021/07/19 13:28:16 [emerg] 1#1: mkdir() "/var/cache/nginx/client_temp" failed (13: Permission denied) nginx: [emerg] mkdir() "/var/cache/nginx/client_temp" failed (13: Permission denied) ~~~
resolution: - Create a new service account ~~~ oc create sa test ~~~- Add `anyuid` SCC to the test serviceaccount ~~~ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid-z test ~~~- Make sure to use the test sa created before to run the pod. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: my-pod spec: serviceAccountName: test ~~~
root_cause: - Pods running in `default` project do not use any `scc` to run. Therefore, the pods will run with escalated privileges if needed by [default](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4586091).- The `default` project is not intended to run custom workloads.

title: How to create Customizing banner for the web console in OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - Create logon banner for Web console- Customizing login banner for Web console
resolution: You can customize the OpenShift Container Platform web console to set a custom logo, product name, links, notifications, and command-line downloads. This is especially helpful if you need to tailor the web console to meet specific corporate or government requirement- Customizing the web console involves the following steps: 1. Use the OpenShift CLI to generate a baseline template to start from. 2. Add the template as a secret. 3. Update the OAuth Custom Resource to specify the name of the secret containing the template created previously.- Three templates relating to the login process can be customized: 1. Error page: If we want to put any banner for the Error page. 2. Login page: To put a banner for the default login page. 3. Login provider selector page: To put banner while IDP provider selection page. **Steps:-**- Prerequisites `You must have administrator privileges.` Procedure:-- First we need to check if there are already secrets created inside openshift-config project. ~~~ $ oc get secret-n openshift-config|grep-i temp login-template Opaque 1 4d17h providers-template Opaque 1 4d17h ~~~- If old secrets are available you may need to delete those for creating a new banner. ~~~ Take backup of secrets and delete the old once. $ oc get secret login-template-n openshift-config-oyaml > login-template-backup.yaml $ oc get secret providers-template-n openshift-config-oyaml > providers-template-backup.yaml $ oc delete secret login-template providers-template-n openshift-config ~~~- Run the following commands to create basic templates you can modify: ~~~ $ oc adm create-login-template > login.html $ oc adm create-provider-selection-template > providers.html $ oc adm create-error-template > errors.html ~~~ What you may have noticed by browsing the generated providers-default-template.html template file is that it is fairly generic. It does not contain any of the existing styling and UI elements that you would typically find by navigating to the OpenShift web console. This is ideal if you are interested in heavily customizing the user experience, such as adding your own organizational branding and styling scheme- Below is the example where We can extract the provider template from the existing setup by running the following command. We can take the help of this file to add customization as per requirement. ~~~ $ curl-sLk https://console-openshift-console.apps. /auth/login > providers-template.html $ vi providers-template.html < < add the customization $ cp providers-template.html providers.html ~~~- Now we need to create the secrets for those templates in which we have done the customization. ~~~ For example, here we are doing for login and provider only:- $ oc create secret generic login-template--from-file=login.html-n openshift-config $ oc create secret generic providers-template--from-file=providers.html-n openshift-config ~~~- Finally we need to edit/patch the auth.config.openshift.io cluster and Update the specification: ~~~ $ oc edit oauths cluster spec: templates: login: name: login-template providerSelection: name: providers-template ~~~

title: Prometheus not able to read etcd metrics after upgrade in OCP 3
issue: - After a cluster Openshift minor version upgrade, Prometheus is no longer able to read etcd metrics. Also, Etcd targets are shown as "DOWN" in Prometheus UI: [image=[src="images/screenshot_2019-11-06_at_11.01.45.png", alt="etcd endpoints down", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center",]]- The etcd monitoring targets are down with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`message on Prometheus GUI.
resolution: - If it doesn't exist already, create the kube-etcd-client-certs secret as described in step #9 of [this procedure](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/prometheus_cluster_monitoring.html#configuring-etcd-monitoring_prometheus-cluster-monitoring).- Add the secret to the Prometheus statefulset definition: ~~~ $ oc set volume statefulset prometheus-k8s--add--name=secret-kube-etcd-client-certs--type=secret--secret-name=kube-etcd-client-certs--mount-path=/etc/prometheus/secrets/kube-etcd-client-certs-c prometheus ~~~- Then, redeploy the Prometheus pods: ~~~ # Take note of the amount of desired replicas: $ oc get statefulset prometheus-k8s # Scale it down: $ oc scale statefulset prometheus-k8s--replicas=0 # When no promotheus pod is running, scale it back to the desired amount of replicas, I.e.: $ oc scale statefulset prometheus-k8s--replicas=2 ~~~ Wait till all the Prometheus pods are in running state, then check the etcd endpoint through the UI. They should appear as "Up": [image=[src="images/promup.png", alt="prometheus EPs up", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center",]]
root_cause: Eventually, when performing upgrades between z-releases the statefulset definition for the Prometheus pod might overwritten resetting any customization made (like [etcd monitoring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/prometheus_cluster_monitoring.html#configuring-etcd-monitoring_prometheus-cluster-monitoring). This, though, shouldn't remove the etcd object from the servicemonitor list.

title: Is it supported to change the "--allocate-node-cidrs" argument for kube-controller-manager during installation
issue: - How to enable--allocate-node-cidrs is enabled for kube-controller-manager during installation?
resolution: - Changing of such argument is not supported in the case of OpenShift-SDN and OVNKubernetes.- By default `--allocate-node-cidrs` is disabled for kube-controller-manager configurations.
root_cause: - Openshift-SDN and OVNKubernetes both do their own CIDR allocation.

title: TFTP Listener IP configuration
issue: How to configure TFTP listener IP. In server we have 2 NIC with 2 IP's, one IP with Gateway configuration (IP-A), and another IP without Gateway (IP-B). I would like to use the TFTP with IP-B, let me know how to configure the same.
resolution: Hello, Can you try as below- (I have used interface 10.44.128.123 and port 69) Method 1. Adding below in tftp.socket,---- [Socket] ListenDatagram=10.44.128.123:69---- For this either use systemctl edit as below- # systemctl edit tftp.socket Or create a file as /etc/systemd/system/tftp.socket.d/override.conf # systemctl daemon-reload # systemctl status tftp.socket ● tftp.socket- Tftp Server Activation Socket Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/tftp.socket; disabled; vendor preset: disabled) Active: active (listening) since Fri 2021-07-02 19:30:29 IST; 19s ago Listen: 10.44.128.123:69 (Datagram) < <====== CGroup: /system.slice/tftp.socket keep tftp.service as it is- # systemctl cat tftp.service # /usr/lib/systemd/system/tftp.service [Unit] Description=Tftp Server Requires=tftp.socket Documentation=man:in.tftpd [Service] ExecStart=/usr/sbin/in.tftpd-s /var/lib/tftpboot StandardInput=socket [Install] Also=tftp.socket Method 2 Here we are starting tftpd as standalone i.e. listen mode. As per man page (man tftpd) we need to add few switches as below to tftpd snip from man page------l- Run the server in standalone (listen) mode, rather than run from inetd. In listen mode, the--timeout option is ignored, and the--address option can be used to specify a specific local address or port to listen to.-a- Specify a specific address and port to listen to when called with the--listen or--foreground option. The default is to listen to the tftp port specified in /etc/services on all local addresses.--------- modified service unit (tftp.service) as below-------------------------------- [Unit] Description=Tftp Server #Requires=tftp.socket Documentation=man:in.tftpd [Service] ExecStart=/usr/sbin/in.tftpd-l-a 10.44.128.123:69-s /var/lib/tftpboot-v < <=============== #StandardInput=socket Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=true [Install] #Also=tftp.socket WantedBy=multi-user.target----------------------------------- # systemctl daemon-reload # systemctl start tftp.service testing- # ps-ef|grep-i ftp root 1523 1 0 20:41? 00:00:00 /usr/sbin/in.tftpd-l-a 10.44.128.123:69-s /var/lib/tftpboot-v # touch /var/lib/tftpboot/hello.txt # tftp 10.44.128.123 tftp> get hello.txt getting from 10.44.128.123:hello.txt to hello.txt [netascii] tftp> [root@rhel8u1-1 ~]# [root@rhel8u1-1 ~]# [root@rhel8u1-1 ~]# ll total 4-rw-------. 1 root root 1209 May 20 2020 anaconda-ks.cfg-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 0 Jul 2 20:52 hello.txt < <------------ Regards, Amey Betkiker Red Hat Global Support www.redhat.com/en/enterprise-linux-8 https://www.redhat.com/en/openshift-4 https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/management/insights

title: Coreos-installer command fails with os error during installation from RHCOS ISO image
issue: - Sometimes while running coreos-installer command on RHCOS live ISO image fails with os error message **Error: decoding and writing image**.
resolution: - The only way to resolve this issue is to download a new ISO image for live ISO installation.
root_cause: - The **os error 5** looks like the `EIO 5 Input/output error` returned by Linux syscalls.- This is a generic error and it may occur if there is an issue with downloaded RHCOS ISO image or the image is corrupt.

title: OpenShift 4.x Unable to Upgrade OS Image due to rpm-ostree status=11/SEGV
issue: When performing an upgrade from 4.4, the nodes will get stuck attempting to upgrade the osimage. You will notice:- MCD complains about osimage not matching expected image- MCD service has exit status 1- systemd reports rpm-ostree "Main process exited, code=killed, status=11/SEGV"
resolution: This issue was being tracked by:- OCP 4.5: Bugzilla [1885726](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1885726) To work around the issue you can follow these steps. **4.4** 1. Download RPM updates (NOTE: please open a Red Hat OCP case to receive these due to not available on download site) 1. Transfer RPMs to the NODE 1. SSH to node 1. Execute the following: ~~~ rpm-ostree usroverlay rpm-Uvh rpm-ostree{,-libs}-2019.6-9.el8_2.x86_64.rpm ~~~ At this point, as long as RPM update succeeds, the MCD should retry installing the target image and will automatically use the new rpm-ostree binary. If the MCD has reached a point where it is no longer attempting to update the image, you can perform the following while replacing xxxx with the logged sha value that the MCD is attempting to update to: ~~~ echo quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:xxxx > /etc/pivot/image-pullspec pivot ~~~ After confirming the pivot completed successfully, reboot the node. **4.5** 1. Download the rpm-ostree and rpm-ostree-libs RPMs from https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/290/ver=4.5/rhel---8/4.5.41/x86_64/packages. To simplify finding the RPMs, just put rpm-ostree into the filter field. 1. Transfer RPMs to the NODE 1. SSH to node 1. Execute the following: ~~~ rpm-ostree usroverlay rpm-Uvh rpm-ostree{,-libs}-2020.4-1.el8.x86_64.rpm ~~~ At this point, as long as RPM update succeeds, the MCD should retry installing the target image and will automatically use the new rpm-ostree binary. If the MCD has reached a point where it is no longer attempting to update the image, you can perform the following while replacing xxxx with the logged sha value that the MCD is attempting to update to: ~~~ echo quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:xxxx > /etc/pivot/image-pullspec pivot ~~~ After confirming the pivot completed successfully, reboot the node.

title: Support of binary protocol in openshift
issue: Support of binary protocols in OpenShift Container Platform
resolution: Ingress support limited options only. It is not like typical LoadBalancer. An Ingress Controller is configured to accept external requests and proxy them based on the configured routes. This is limited to HTTP, HTTPS using SNI, and TLS using SNI, which is sufficient for web applications and services that work over TLS with SNI. Please refer the documents below for more information on this. [1] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/networking/configuring_ingress_cluster_traffic/overview-traffic.html [2] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/networking/configuring_ingress_cluster_traffic/configuring-ingress-cluster-traffic-ingress-controller.html#nw-using-ingress-and-routes_configuring-ingress-cluster-traffic-ingress-controller [3] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/dev_guide/expose_service/index.html

title: Can a smartrouter be used without a controller (Business Central) to balance immutable KieServers?
issue: Can a smartrouter be used without a controller (Business Central) to balance immutable KieServers?
resolution: Following the steps below: 1. Generate a SSL Encryption Key and Certificate.- Generate the server.keystore (jboss / mykeystorepass): ~~~ $ keytool-genkeypair-alias jboss-keyalg RSA-keystore server.keystore-storepass mykeystorepass--dname "CN=omolinab,OU=Engineering,O=mycompany.com,L=Barcelona,S=NC,C=ES" ~~~- Certificate name: jboss- Certificate passw: mykeystorepass ~~~ $ keytool-list-keystore server.keystore $ keytool-certreq-keyalg RSA-alias jboss-keystore server.keystore-file certreq.csr $ openssl req-in certreq.csr-noout-text $ keytool-export-alias jboss-keystore server.keystore-file server.crt ~~~ 2. Create your project ~~~ $ oc project rhpam-smartrouter ~~~ 3. Creating the secrets for KIE Server, Business Central, Smartrouter and the administrative user ~~~ $ oc create secret generic kieserver-app-secret--from-file=server.keystore $ oc create secret generic businesscentral-app-secret--from-file=server.keystore $ oc create secret generic smartrouter-app-secret--from-file=server.keystore $ oc create secret generic rhpam-credentials--from-literal=KIE_ADMIN_USER=rhpamadmin--from-literal=KIE_ADMIN_PWD=admin@123 ~~~ 4. Installing the immutable monitor through the template which includes the MONITOR and SMARTROUTER: ===> MONITOR + SMARTROUTER ~~~ $ oc new-app-f rhpam79-prod-immutable-kieserver.yaml \-p APPLICATION_NAME=rhpam-immutable-s2i \-p CREDENTIALS_SECRET=rhpam-credentials \-p KIE_SERVER_HTTPS_SECRET=kieserver-app-secret \-p KIE_SERVER_HTTPS_KEYSTORE=server.keystore \-p KIE_SERVER_HTTPS_NAME=jboss \-p KIE_SERVER_HTTPS_PASSWORD=mykeystorepass \-p KIE_SERVER_CONTAINER_DEPLOYMENT=rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library=com.myspace:hello-world:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_URL=https://github.com/omolinab/hello-world.git \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_REF=main \-p MAVEN_REPO_URL=http://nexus3-nexus.192.168.42.187.nip.io/repository/maven-public/ \-p MAVEN_REPO_ID=nexus-repo \-p MAVEN_REPO_USERNAME=admin \-p MAVEN_REPO_PASSWORD=admin1234 \-p IMAGE_STREAM_NAMESPACE=rhpam-smartrouter ~~~ 5. Installing the immutable KieServer through the template which includes the IMMUTABLE KIESERVER and POSTGRESQL 10: ===> IMMUTABLE KIESERVER (S2i) + POSTGRESQL 10 ~~~ $ oc new-app-f rhpam79-prod-immutable-monitor.yaml \-p APPLICATION_NAME=rhpam-monitoring \-p CREDENTIALS_SECRET=rhpam-credentials \-p BUSINESS_CENTRAL_HTTPS_SECRET=businesscentral-app-secret \-p BUSINESS_CENTRAL_HTTPS_KEYSTORE=server.keystore \-p BUSINESS_CENTRAL_HTTPS_NAME=jboss \-p BUSINESS_CENTRAL_HTTPS_PASSWORD=mykeystorepass \-p KIE_SERVER_ROUTER_HTTPS_SECRET=smartrouter-app-secret \-p KIE_SERVER_ROUTER_HTTPS_KEYSTORE=server.keystore \-p KIE_SERVER_ROUTER_HTTPS_NAME=jboss \-p KIE_SERVER_ROUTER_HTTPS_PASSWORD=mykeystorepass \-p KIE_SERVER_CONTROLLER_OPENSHIFT_GLOBAL_DISCOVERY_ENABLED=true \-p MAVEN_REPO_URL=http://nexus3-nexus.192.168.42.187.nip.io/repository/maven-public/ \-p MAVEN_REPO_ID=nexus-repo \-p MAVEN_REPO_USERNAME=admin \-p MAVEN_REPO_PASSWORD=admin1234 \-p IMAGE_STREAM_NAMESPACE=rhpam-smartrouter ~~~ After everything is running there will be 4 pods:- 1 Business Central pod- 1 Smartrouter pod- 1 KieServer pod- 1 Postgresql pod Then the Business Central pod can be stopped and the smartrouter will be able to work without the controller. However it will be working fine for an insecure connection which is the default one: ~~~ $ curl-k http://insecure-rhpam-monitoring-smartrouter-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io/mgmt/list {"containerInfo": [{"alias": "hello-world", "containerId": "rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library", "releaseId": "com.myspace:hello-world:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT"}, {"alias": "hello-world", "containerId": "rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library", "releaseId": "com.myspace:hello-world:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT"}, {"alias": "hello-world", "containerId": "rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library", "releaseId": "com.myspace:hello-world:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT"}], "containers": [{"rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library": ["http://insecure-rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io:80/services/rest/server"]}, {"hello-world": ["http://insecure-rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io:80/services/rest/server"]}], "servers": [{"rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver": ["http://insecure-rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io:80/services/rest/server"]}]} ~~~ ~~~ $ curl-X POST-u 'rhpamadmin:admin@123' "http://insecure-rhpam-monitoring-smartrouter-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io/containers/rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library/processes/hello-world.hello-world-process/instances"-H "content-type: application/json" ~~~ So from now on, for setting up the configuration for the secure connection between the KieServer and the Smartrouter, follow the steps below: 1. Stop the KieServer and Smartrouter pods, so you will be able to change the values without the annoyed restarting of the pods while you are doing it. 2. You should modify/add the following properties: * KieServer pod ~~~ KIE_SERVER_ROUTE_NAME = rhpam-engine-kieserver <===== from insecure-rhpam-engine-kieserver KIE_SERVER_ROUTER_SERVICE = rhpam-monitoring-smartrouter <===== smartrouter service name ~~~ Note: I told you before to add the property "KIE_SERVER_USE_SECURE_ROUTE_NAME" but it is not used here * Smartrouter pod ~~~ KIE_SERVER_ROUTER_PROTOCOL = https JAVA_OPTS_APPEND =-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/etc/smartrouter-secret-volume/server.keystore-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=mykeystorepass ~~~ 3. Start the Smartrouter pod. 4. Start the KieServer pod. Finally you can check that everything whouls work as expected: ~~~ $ curl-k https://rhpam-monitoring-smartrouter-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io/mgmt/list {"containerInfo": [{"alias": "hello-world", "containerId": "rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library", "releaseId": "com.myspace:hello-world:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT"}], "containers": [{"rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library": ["https://rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io:443/services/rest/server"]}, {"hello-world": ["https://rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io:443/services/rest/server"]}], "servers": [{"rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver": ["https://rhpam-immutable-s2i-kieserver-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io:443/services/rest/server"]}]} ~~~ ~~~ $ curl-k-X POST-u 'rhpamadmin:admin@123' "https://rhpam-monitoring-smartrouter-rhpam-smartrouter.192.168.42.187.nip.io/containers/rhpam-smartrouter-kieserver-library/processes/hello-world.hello-world-process/instances"-H "content-type: application/json" ~~~

title: How to recreate OCP3 admin.kubeconfig manually
issue: - How to recreate the admin.kubeconfig manually without running the ansible redeploy certificates playbook?
resolution: - The admin.kubeconfig can be recreated easily by running the `openshift-ansible/playbooks/redeploy-certificates.yml` and it should be the preferred way to recreate the admin.kubeconfig. However, if the playbook can't be executed, the steps below show how to create the `admin.kubeconfig` manually.- The `admin.kubeconfig` is ultimate access file to connect to the cluster. It contains the user with `cluster-admin` permissions. Loosing the `admin.kubeconfig `would have serious impact on the cluster during the running any playbook, due the playbook uses the `admin.kubeconfig` to connect and execute commands in the cluster.- It needs to run as root.- Let's create the working directory: ~~~ # mkdir /root/admin-create # cd /root/admin-create ~~~- Create the private key: ~~~ # openssl genrsa-out admin.key 2048 ~~~- Create the config file for openssl containing the lines below: ~~~ # vi openssl.cnf > > [req] distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name req_extensions = v3_req prompt = no [req_distinguished_name] O=system:masters, O=system:cluster-admins CN=system:admin [v3_req] # Extensions to add to a certificate request keyUsage = digitalSignature, keyEncipherment extendedKeyUsage = clientAuth basicConstraints = critical,CA:FALSE < < ~~~- Generate the admin client certificate request: ~~~ # openssl req-new-out admin.csr-key admin.key-config openssl.cnf ~~~- Sign the certificate: ~~~ # openssl x509-req-in admin.csr-CA /etc/origin/master/ca.crt-CAkey /etc/origin/master/ca.key-CAcreateserial-out admin.crt-days 365-sha256-extfile openssl.cnf-extensions v3_req ~~~- Confirm that the client certificate is signed by correct CA: ~~~ # openssl x509-noout-subject-issuer-in /etc/origin/master/ca.crt # openssl x509-noout-issuer-subject-in admin.crt ~~~- If it is ok, check the values from the master-config.yaml: ~~~ # grep "masterURL\|masterPublicURL" /etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml ~~~- Generate the kubeconfig where "--master=" is "masterURL" and the "masterPublicURL" is "--public-master=" with all https and the port: ~~~ # oc adm create-kubeconfig--master=--public-master=--certificate-authority=/etc/origin/master/ca.crt--client-certificate=admin.crt--client-key=admin.key--kubeconfig=admin.kubeconfig ~~~- Verify that the admin kubeconfig works: ~~~ # oc get nodes--config=admin.kubeconfig # oc whoami--config=admin.kubeconfig ~~~
root_cause: - The `admin.kubeconfig` is used by the playbook when executing updates, installs and other actions on OpenShift cluster.- By default, the playbook will use `admin.kubeconfig` from the first master from the inventory file, to execute actions with `oc` cli tools.

title: Why are the paths of a gluster-block multipathed device flapping up and down?
issue: In an application pod with a gluster-block device attached, the status of the paths reported by the `multipath` command are flapping up and down: [root@host1 ~]# multipath-ll mpatho (36001405dc190add4235421f98d6a7b17) dm-82 LIO-ORG,TCMU device size=45G features='1 queue_if_no_path' hwhandler='0' wp=rw |-+- policy='round-robin 0' prio=1 status=active | `- 33:0:0:0 sdg 8:96 active ready running |-+- policy='round-robin 0' prio=1 status=enabled | `- 42:0:0:0 sdh 8:112 active ready running `-+- policy='round-robin 0' prio=1 status=enabled `- 32:0:0:0 sdi 8:128 active ready running After some time: mpatho (36001405dc190add4235421f98d6a7b17) dm-82 LIO-ORG,TCMU device size=45G features='1 queue_if_no_path' hwhandler='0' wp=rw |-+- policy='round-robin 0' prio=1 status=enabled | `- 33:0:0:0 sdg 8:96 failed ready running |-+- policy='round-robin 0' prio=0 status=enabled | `- 42:0:0:0 sdh 8:112 failed faulty running `-+- policy='round-robin 0' prio=1 status=active `- 32:0:0:0 sdi 8:128 active ready running
Why is this occurring?
resolution: * As a workaround, restart the glusted pods (converged deployment) or nodes (independent deployment) one by one, making sure the healing is complete before starting the next node. After this is done, run an `xfs_repair` in the gluster-block device, following the steps in KCS article ["How to manually repair a gluster-block filesystem used by OpenShift "](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4768681) * For a permanent fix, upgrade OCS to the latest 3.11.6 version. The steps for such task can be found in [part III of the OCS 3.11 Deployment Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_container_storage/3.11/html/deployment_guide/part-upgrade)
root_cause: The gluster-block client is getting frequent disconnections at the time of handling call_bail requests. These requests are coming because the gluster-block client is not getting a response to an inode lock operation in the default threshold stablished, which is 1800 seconds. It gets stuck at this point.

title: Downloading container images is slow from China mainland
issue: Pull Images from registry.redhat.io or quay.io is slow.
resolution: Red Hat China is working on this issue with Global IT and Engineering team for a long time. In order to mitigate the impact for our customers, here is an interim solution for customers to use before a final solution. As a workaround, you can bind registry.redhat.io to ip 184.87.234.137, which is located in HongKong, in `/etc/hosts` file. Before bind `registry.redhat.io` to `184.87.234.137`: ~~~ # podman login registry.redhat.io-u Password: Login Succeeded! [root@dell-per730-02 ~]# time podman pull registry.redhat.io/rhceph/rhceph-4-rhel8:latest Trying to pull registry.redhat.io/rhceph/rhceph-4-rhel8:latest... Getting image source signatures Copying blob 45cc8b7f2b43 done Copying blob 3b29d22d82ba done Copying blob 5f6bf015319e done Copying config 4208075b0b done Writing manifest to image destination Storing signatures 4208075b0bc4ee57f205b55c9421fad8d34716427e18c9d1091d82908355bfa9 real 1m56.944s <======================= user 0m40.693s sys 0m6.879s ~~~ After bind `registry.redhat.io` to `184.87.234.137`: ~~~ # tail-n1 /etc/hosts 184.87.234.137 registry.redhat.io # ping registry.redhat.io PING registry.redhat.io (184.87.234.137) 56(84) bytes of data. 64 bytes from registry.redhat.io (184.87.234.137): icmp_seq=1 ttl=51 time=52.3 ms 64 bytes from registry.redhat.io (184.87.234.137): icmp_seq=2 ttl=51 time=51.10 ms 64 bytes from registry.redhat.io (184.87.234.137): icmp_seq=3 ttl=51 time=51.9 ms # time podman pull registry.redhat.io/rhceph/rhceph-4-rhel8:latest Trying to pull registry.redhat.io/rhceph/rhceph-4-rhel8:latest... Getting image source signatures Copying blob 45cc8b7f2b43 done Copying blob 5f6bf015319e done Copying blob 3b29d22d82ba done Copying config 4208075b0b done Writing manifest to image destination Storing signatures 4208075b0bc4ee57f205b55c9421fad8d34716427e18c9d1091d82908355bfa9 real 0m52.980s <======================= user 0m41.296s sys 0m7.059s ~~~
root_cause: Please note that, Quay Enterprise doesn't control download speed since it links directly to its storage for image downloads. We advise users to check the network connection to the storage location. If that does not provide any insight: 1. Restart docker daemon 2. Check the output of a timed docker pull $time docker pull quay/ 3. Use a VPN. This may cause more number of hops, but lower overall latency 4. Verify that there are no DNS issues in the network If none of the suggestions helped, users may wish to try using [Squashed](https://coreos.com/blog/quayio-new-features) Image feature. Here is more [information](https://docs.quay.io/guides/squashed-images.html) on how to pull squashed images. Additionally, Quay is hosted in AWS us-east-1 region, and images are stored on S3. You can obtain CDN list from [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)

title: OSD Weight and Pod Affinity configuration in OpenShift Container Storage - Developer Preview
issue: In some instances, it might be required to assign an object storage device (OSD) to all the solid state drives (SSDs) on a host machine including a partitioned device that has a dedicated partition for the operating system. In such cases, you must reduce the load on this OSD as it shares the same physical device as the local operating system.
resolution: **Note: A support exception is required for running this solution in production because a wrong configuration can break the cluster.** **Developer preview releases are meant for customers who are willing to evaluate new products or releases of products in an early stage of product development. In this case, OCS 4.8 does not support configuring OSD weight and pod affinity in the production environment.** This is a live document to be used in various environments and configurations. If you find any mistakes or missing instructions or need any assistance, please add an [Issue](https://github.com/red-hat-storage/ocs-training/issues) or write us @ `ocs-devpreview@redhat.com`. To reduce the load on the OSD, you need to configure either one or both of the following options depending on your cluster setup and workload:- InitialWeight- controls the capacity for data placement- PrimaryAffinity- Sets the primary OSD for the placement group that serves the read load

title: vSphere machines are stuck in deleting phase if associated OpenShift node object is deleted
issue: - `vSphere` machine is stuck in `deleting` phase if associated `node` is deleted.- Below logs are observed in `machine-api-controller` pod: ~~~ 2021-07-26T18:25:35.907168430Z I0726 18:25:35.907131 1 controller.go:168] worker-1: reconciling Machine 2021-07-26T18:25:35.907168430Z I0726 18:25:35.907155 1 controller.go:208] worker-1: reconciling machine triggers delete 2021-07-26T18:25:35.911705275Z I0726 18:25:35.911684 1 controller.go:337] Could not find node from noderef, it may have already been deleted: worker-1 2021-07-26T18:25:35.911705275Z I0726 18:25:35.911700 1 actuator.go:150] worker-1: actuator deleting machine 2021-07-26T18:25:36.024206052Z I0726 18:25:36.024183 1 machine_scope.go:148] Node "worker-1" not found 2021-07-26T18:25:36.024217091Z I0726 18:25:36.024204 1 machine_scope.go:102] worker-1: patching machine 2021-07-26T18:25:36.041096582Z E0726 18:25:36.041059 1 actuator.go:57] worker-1 error: worker-1: reconciler failed to Delete machine: worker-1: Can't check node status before vm destroy: nodes "worker-1" not found 2021-07-26T18:25:36.041123410Z E0726 18:25:36.041105 1 controller.go:229] worker-1: failed to delete machine: worker-1: reconciler failed to Delete machine: worker-1: Can't check node status before vm destroy: nodes "worker-1" not found ~~~
resolution: - The issue is known to Red Hat and it is being tracked under [BZ-1977369](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1977369). **Workaround**- If the node object is not present, then delete the machine from `vSphere` directly. Note: Make sure that the VM doesn't have any disk attached apart from system disk to avoid any data loss.

title: How to apply different IP CIDR range for egress CIDR pool
issue: - Can we use a different IP CIDR range for egress IP CIDR?- Split IP range for the Egress CIDR pool.
resolution: - Yes, we can allocate multiple CIDR Ranges but they must be from the same subnet as the subnet of node’s primary IP.- Set the appropriate value for the subnet ensuring that the required set of IPs are included in that range. For example: ~~~ $ oc patch hostsubnet-p '{"egressCIDRs": ["10.0.1.X/Y","10.0.20.X/Y"]}' ~~~ **Note:**- Egress IPs are implemented as additional IP addresses on the primary network interface of the node and must be in the same subnet as the node’s primary IP. Egress IPs must not be configured in any Linux network configuration files, such as ifcfg-eth0.- CIDR network specification should be in canonical form.

title: OCP 4 node goes into NotReady state
issue: - After installing an OCP cluster, the nodes are getting into `NotReady` state frequently.- Node becomes `NotReady`.
resolution: #### Fixes- For **RHOCP 4.5**: The fix has been delivered at RHOCP 4.5.27- [Errata RHBA-2021:0033](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2021:0033)- For **RHOCP 4.6**: The fix has been delivered at RHOCP 4.6.8- [Errata RHSA-2020:5259](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2020:5259) #### Workaround SSH into the affected node and restart the `kubelet` service: ~~~ $ ssh-i core@ $ sudo systemctl restart kubelet ~~~ **Note:** Before restarting the `kubelet` service, capture the logs from the cluster for further analysis.- Gather debug information from the cluster and check the status of `kubelet` service from the affected `node`: ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather [...] $ ssh-i core@ $ sudo systemctl status kubelet ~~~ If the issue re-occurs, capture the above data and open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?intcmp=hp|a|a3|case&caseCreate=true) with Red Hat.
root_cause: One possible cause could be an vMotion of the node. Even if vMotion is supported, a vMotion of a OpenShift node could leave the node in a `NotReady` status. For more information, review [Use of VMware VMotion with OpenShift VMs](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4975241).

title: Cluster-wide entitlement certificate stops working suddenly causing errors on pods running on RHOCP4
issue: - Failed to install NVIDIA GPU driver due to following error in the logs ~~~ Errors during downloading metadata for repository 'rhel-8-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms': Status code: 403 for https://cdn.redhat.com/content/dist/rhel8/8/x86_64/appstream/os/repodata/repomd.xml (IP: 23.204.100.83) Error: Failed to download metadata for repo 'rhel-8-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms': Cannot download repomd.xml: Cannot download repodata/repomd.xml: All mirrors were tried ~~~
resolution: create "offline systems" in RHSM web: https://access.redhat.com/management/systems/create This does not upload a package profile to Errata Notifications, and so that should prevent Errata Notifications from inadvertently triggering entitlement certificate regeneration
root_cause: - Periodically there are content changes to products. When this happens, Candlepin marks affected entitlement certificates as "dirty."- Dirty certificates are (optionally) regenerated when certain requests are made to Candlepin.- Regeneration replaces old certificates with new ones, and in particular marks the old certificates as revoked.- Authorizer denies access to content via the old certificates thereafter. **Terminology** ~~~- Candlepin is the open-source entitlement engine which manages a subscriptions and entitlement certificates.- Authorizer is the internal application that grants or denies access for content based on entitlement certificates. It keeps track of what certificates have been revoked. ~~~

title: ROSA init/installation fails with the error "Failed to create user 'osdCcsAdmin': ResourceNotReady: failed waiting for successful resource state"
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Installation of ROSA cluster fails with the below error message. ~~~ [root@nc-14jul21-2fd6 ~]# rosa init I: Logged in as 'xxxxx@yourdomain.com' on 'https://api.openshift.com' I: Validating AWS credentials... I: AWS credentials are valid! I: Validating SCP policies... I: AWS SCP policies ok I: Validating AWS quota... I: AWS quota ok. If cluster installation fails, validate actual AWS resource usage against https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_getting_started/rosa-required-aws-service-quotas.html I: Ensuring cluster administrator user 'osdCcsAdmin'... time="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" level=error msg="Max retries reached waiting for stack to create" E: Failed to create user 'osdCcsAdmin': ResourceNotReady: failed waiting for successful resource state ~~~
resolution: - Check user **osdCcsAdmin** in the IAM section of the Account if above user already exist in console or with below command. ~~~ # aws iam get-user--user-name osdCcsAdmin ~~~- Check the Cloud formation stack in the account if stack has already been created.- If Cloudformation stack already exits for the Openshift installation, please delete stack and try installation. ~~~ # rosa init--delete-stack ~~~- If issue persists, please engage Red Hat support for further troubleshooting of the issue.
root_cause: - During multiple attempts of installation, stack is not removed and user required permissions are not set properly in the account.

title: Can the loglevel of Jaeger be configured in ServiceMesh 2.x?
issue: A `ServiceMeshControlPlane` with `Jaeger AllInOne` was deployed and need to configure the log level of `Jaeger`. Are the debug logs of `Jaeger` needed by `ServiceMesh` or any other components? Can the log-level parameter be set to other values?
resolution: The `log-level` parameter must be set in the `Jaeger` object: ~~~ # oc edit jaeger jaeger 5 apiVersion: jaegertracing.io/v1 6 kind: Jaeger 7 metadata: [...] 71 agent: 72 config: {} 73 options: {} 74 resources: {} 75 allInOne: 76 config: {} 77 options: 78 log-level: info <----- 79 query: 80 base-path: / 81 resources: {} ~~~ Once it is modified, it will create a new `Deployment` for `Jaeger` with the new configuration. This will not be overwritten by the operator: ~~~ NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE grafana-7b7578dc56-8xw54 2/2 Running 0 98m istio-egressgateway-bf5856bf5-gp7p9 1/1 Running 0 98m istio-ingressgateway-98f8cb66b-pk2jn 1/1 Running 0 98m istiod-basic-64bd86fc8f-bmmth 1/1 Running 0 100m jaeger-5b6b5fccc-t9m8t 2/2 Running 0 4s jaeger-5c655fc79d-wtfjk 2/2 Terminating 0 98m # oc get pod jaeger-5b6b5fccc-t9m8t-o yaml | grep log-level---log-level=info ~~~ `Jaeger` will still be able to retrieve the spans and perform the searches, however that information will not be logged in the `Jaeger` pod. With the `log-level` set to `debug` every `UDP packet` that is received by the `Jaeger Agent` is logged, as well as every batch that is sent by the `Jaeger Agent` to the `Collector`. The `Collector` also logs every batch it receives and logs every span that is stored in the permanent storage. Having the `log-level` set to `debug` is the easiest way to know that there is no problem in `Jaeger` to read the traffic spans.
root_cause: The `log-level` parameter for `Jaeger` can't be configured from the `ServiceMeshControlPlane` object, and it is set by default to `debug`. The list of parameters that can be configured in the `ServiceMeshControlPlane` can be found here: [Maistra Service Mesh custom resources](https://maistra.io/docs/ossm-custom-resources.html#ossm-cr-example_ossm-custom-resources-v2x)

title: KubePersistentVolumeFullInFourDays alert firing up even when there is enough space left on the backend storage
issue: - Alertmanager sends `KubePersistentVolumeFullInFourDays` alerts- frequently even when there is enough space left in the device.
resolution: - `KubePersistentVolumeFullInFourDays` is a prediction and as such shouldn't be a critical type of alert in the first place. Additionally, since this is a prediction and not a reflection of a current state, it is fine to silence such an alert if it is causing issues.- You can still know if disks are running out of space with `KubePersistentVolumeUsageCritical` alert.- You can silence the alert so you can disable this alert message: [Silence Alert](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4451161 "https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4451161")
root_cause: - This occurs because there is an issue with the expression which was responsible for triggering this alert which was reported as a bug and was fixed in OCP 4.x.- For more information regarding this bug: [Bugzilla #1800489](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1800489 "https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1800489")

title: Kibana users are getting empty page and unable to create index pattern.
