title: kubeconfig - oc commands: error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized) in OCP 4
issue: - Unable to run any `oc` commands using `KUBECONFIG` variable.- Unable to run any `oc` commands using the `--kubeconfig= ` option.- All `oc` commands throws the following error: ~~~ error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized) ~~~
resolution: This Solution will describe the process to sanitize a `kubeconfig` to retrieve the install format. **Please save the file once it has been sanitized, this is your emergency cluster login.** > **Note:**_Before to modify a `kubeconfig` file, always backup it_ > **Note:** If you need a quick way to access to your cluster, and the `admin` context is present in the file, update the `current-context` to point to the `admin` context and use the `kubeconfig` file as it. > **Important:** don't execute `oc login` when using the installation `kubeconfig` file, as it could change the special `system:admin` user and could break the `kubeconfig`. #### Description The `kubeconfig` file is a `YAML` formatted file, which include 5 main sections:- `clusters`: provides the list of the clusters known in the `kubeconfig`. Only 1 cluster should be present in the emergency `kubeconfig`.- `contexts`: provides the different context to connect to a cluster as a specific user.- `current-context`: is set to the current context- `preferences`: usually empty. Not required for the emergency `kubeconfig`.- `users`: provides the list of users available to connect to the cluster. Only 1 user should be defined in the emergency `kubeconfig` with certificates and not with token. #### 1/ Clean-up the contexts The `contexts` section should contains a context named `admin`. That's the only context the emergency `kubeconfig` is required to have. You can removed all other contexts. ~~~ contexts:- context: cluster: myupi46cluster user: admin name: admin ~~~ The context is just a way to match a specific user with a cluster. In this example, the context named: `admin` will use the user `admin` to connect to the cluster "`myupi46cluster`". ####2/ Clean up the clusters The `admin` context contains a user and a cluster value. In the `clusters` section remove all other clusters to keep the only one matching the context. ~~~ clusters:- cluster: certificate-authority-data: [...a_base64_encrypted_certificate_authority...] server: https://api.myupi46cluster.lab.example.com:6443 name: myupi46cluster ~~~ ####3/ Clean up the users The `admin` context contains a user and a cluster value. In the `users` section remove all other clusters to keep the only one matching the context. ~~~ users:- name: admin user: client-certificate-data: [...a_base64_encrypted_certificate...] client-key-data: [...a_base64_encrypted_key..] ~~~ > **Note:**_Please note that the admin user does not use a token, but have a certificate and a key to authenticate with the cluster_ ####4/ Set the `current-context` Once the undesired contexts, clusters and users have been removed, set the `current-context` to your remaining context. ####5/ Test and archive The `kubeconfig` can now be used to connect to the cluster, either using the `KUBECONFIG` variable ~~~ $ export KUBECONFIG=./kubeconfig $ oc get co ~~~ or using the `--kubeconfig` option ~~~ $ oc--kubeconfig=./kubeconfig get co ~~~ Once validated this `kubeconfig` file must be archived in a safe place. > **Important:** don't execute `oc login` when using the installation `kubeconfig` file, as it could change the special `system:admin` user and could break the `kubeconfig`. #### Sample of an install `kubeconfig` ~~~ clusters:- cluster: certificate-authority-data: [...a_base64_encrypted_certificate_authority...] server: https://api.myupi46cluster.lab.example.com:6443 name: myupi46cluster contexts:- context: cluster: myupi46cluster user: admin name: admin current-context: admin preferences: {} users:- name: admin user: client-certificate-data: [...a_base64_encrypted_certificate...] client-key-data: [...a_base64_encrypted_key..] ~~~ > **Note:** For lost or not working `kubeconfig` file, if the cluster is OCP 4.6+ check [How to get `system:admin` kubeconfigs on OpenShift Container Platform 4.6+](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6112601), and for OCP 4.5 or previous versions, follow the solution: [Generate a new `system:admin` kubeconfig in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5705711).
root_cause: Whenever the authentication Operator is degraded, the kube:admin user/certificates provided during the installation process should be used to connect to the cluster as an emergency process. The user & certificate are stored in a file called **kubeconfig** and it should contain only 1 cluster, context and user. But in some case, additional contexts, users and sometimes clusters are added to this file, and they may prevent the file to be used correctly for a emergency process. This KCS will explain how to sanitize the kubeconfig file to retrieve it to his original state.

title: OpenShift 4.7 UPI  Installation on GCP fails with no subnets available
issue: - The openshift installation is failing due to insufficient subnets for the cluster nodes.
resolution: - Change either the `hostPrefix` or `cidr` value in `install-config.yaml` so that there are atleast 3 subnets for the master nodes during the installation. ~~~- cidr: 100.124.124.0/16 hostPrefix: 23 ~~~
root_cause: - The combination of `cidr` and `hostPrefix` in `install-config.yaml` determines the number of subnets available for the cluster nodes to use.- For instance, the below configuration results in two logical subnets, which is not sufficient for 3 master nodes during installation and hence the installation fails. ~~~- cidr: 100.124.124.0/22 hostPrefix: 23 ~~~

title: ETCD performance troubleshooting
issue: *This guide is intended as troubleshooting guide and sums up several different KCS, articles and blogs.
Customer experience several problems like:- random timeouts in the cluster- the cluster doesn't look stable- 'oc login' doesn't work every time.- problem collecting must-gather (OCP4) due to timeouts
resolution: For best performance make sure that- you are following only official Red Hat documentation **as not everything suggested in upstream is supported**- masters (where ETCD runs) use **dedicated disk** (not shared with other nodes/workers, using dedicated SSD or LUN. For cloud environments try to pick up best region for storage) as this is most common issue.- masters have enough resources (CPU, RAM)- in the case of virtualized environment make sure CPU is not allowed to overcommit (above 100%)- network can handle enough IO and bandwidth between masters is fast enough (ps: having masters in different DCs is not recommended as you should rather use [RHCAM](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/management/advanced-cluster-management) and failover to another cluster, but in case there's no other option, network latency should be below 2ms [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/articles/3220991))
root_cause: **Slow disk** Fast disks are the most critical factor for etcd deployment performance and stability. A slow disk will increase etcd request latency and potentially hurt cluster stability. Since etcd’s consensus protocol depends on persistently storing metadata to a log, a majority of etcd cluster members must write every request down to disk. You can find several indicator of issues within ETCD logs: ~~~ mvcc: finished scheduled compaction at 241674166 (took 112.969552ms) ~~~ Since etcd keeps an exact history of its keyspace, this history should be periodically compacted to avoid performance degradation and eventual storage space exhaustion. Compacting the keyspace history drops all information about keys superseded prior to a given keyspace revision. The space used by these keys then becomes available for additional writes to the keyspace. **Compaction should be always below 100ms** and anything above means performance issues. ~~~ apply entries took too long ~~~ After a majority of etcd members agree to commit a request, each etcd server applies the request to its data store and persists the result to disk. Even with a slow mechanical disk or a virtualized network disk, such as Amazon’s EBS or Google’s PD, applying a request should normally take fewer than 50 milliseconds (and around 5ms for fast SSD/NVMe disk). If the average apply duration exceeds 100 milliseconds, etcd will warn that entries are taking too long to apply. **There should be no 'took too long' messages at all** on healthy cluster. **Important:** When looking for the took too long messages, it's needed to check the date and the amount of time in the message. For example, it's not the same ~1000 messages in 5 days for 100ms than 30k messages in just one day for 500ms or even more. ~~~ failed to send out heartbeat on time ~~~ etcd uses a leader-based consensus protocol for consistent data replication and log execution. Cluster members elect a single leader, all other members become followers. The elected leader must periodically send heartbeats to its followers to maintain its leadership. Followers infer leader failure if no heartbeats are received within an election interval and trigger an election. If a leader doesn’t send its heartbeats in time but is still running, the election is spurious and likely caused by insufficient resources. To catch these soft failures, if the leader skips two heartbeat intervals, etcd will warn it failed to send a heartbeat on time. *Usually this issue is caused by a slow disk. Before the leader sends heartbeats attached with metadata, it may need to persist the metadata to disk. The disk could be experiencing contention among etcd and other applications, or the disk is too simply slow* **CPU starvation** If monitoring of the machine’s CPU usage shows heavy utilization, there may not be enough compute capacity for etcd. Moving etcd to dedicated machine, increasing process resource isolation with cgroups, or renicing the etcd server process into a higher priority can usually solve the problem. **Slow network** can also cause this issue. If network metrics among the etcd machines shows long latencies or high drop rate, there may not be enough network capacity for etcd. Moving etcd members to a less congested network will typically solve the problem. However, if the etcd cluster is deployed across data centers, long latency between members is expected. **WARNING** Tuning the heartbeat-interval as noted in [3.4 tuning documentation](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.4/tuning/) is not supported and you should make sure your latency between DCs is less than 2ms.

title: The thanos queries is not exporting the path for getting the labels from the api in OCP 4
issue: Not possible to query to the `thanos-querier` the path `/api/v1/labels` since it's not exposed for the `kube-rbac-proxy` container.
Not able to list the `/api/v1/labels` path when querying to the `thanos-querier`.
resolution: Task [MON-1695](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MON-1695) was created to expose the path `/api/v1/labels` in the `thanos-querier`.
root_cause: The `kube-rbac-proxy` container inside the `thanos querier` only exposes the `/api/v1/query` and `/api/v1/query_range` paths, but not the `/api/v1/labels`. Then, it's not possible to list the labels.

title: Kubernetes upstream NamespaceDefaultLabelName feature availability in Openshift 4
issue: - How to select a Namespace by its Name in NetworkPolicy?- How to use K8s feature NamespaceDefaultLabelName in Openshift?
resolution: - NamespaceDefaultLabelName is in beta stage in upstream K8s and Kubernetes versions are entirely integrated inside OpenShift and hence this feature is beta on OpenShift 4.8 (based on Kubernetes 1.21) and is expected to become general-availability on OpenShift 4.9 (based on Kubernetes 1.22)- Considering it as alpha/beta product and its not document in our enterprise documentation above feature is not supported as per [this article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3452661)- Feature is expected to be GA from **Openshift 4.9**.- Internal backport RFE-2076 has been created for the above feature.
root_cause: - Kubernetes versions are entirely integrated inside OpenShift. This means that if any feature is beta on upstream Kubernetes, it is also on OpenShift consequently.- In the case of NamespaceDefaultLabelName, it is beta on Kubernetes 1.21 and is expected to become general-availability on Kubernetes 1.22 [1]. Therefore this feature is beta on OpenShift 4.8 (based on Kubernetes 1.21) and is expected to become general-availability on OpenShift 4.9 (based on Kubernetes 1.22), which is the next version to be released.

title: What data does Red Hat collect from the Openshift Container Platform 4.x?
issue: - Which data is transmitted to Red Hat?- How long will the data be stored for?- In which country is this data stored?
resolution: - Red Hat doesn't receive any cluster sensitive data or application data.- The only data received related to the cluster is informational, eg. The cluster ID, Number of nodes, Number of cores, Cluster health information eg. Alerts, Operator health, Subscription details etc.- To check what data is collected by Telemtry please click [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/virt/logging_events_monitoring/virt-openshift-cluster-monitoring.html#what-information-is-collected_virt-openshift-cluster-monitoring)- Red Hat does not collect personal data, rather it collects data that is used to detect flaws or vulnerabilities and improve the product experience.- This data is available until the cluster is running with the valid subscriptions and would generally be stored at one of the Red Hat US data centers.

title: What is the meaning of different values in " ntpq> rv assID " output ?
issue: - How to interpret `ntpq> rv assocID` output to check if NTP is synchronizing correctly or not?
resolution: ~~~ ntpq> rv 29583 assID=62236 status=9014 reach, conf, 1 event, event_reach, srcadr=192.168.23.1, srcport=123, dstadr=192.168.247.11, dstport=123, leap=00, stratum=3, precision=-6, rootdelay=218.750, rootdispersion=1381.516, refid=24.1.4.14, reach=377, unreach=0, hmode=3, pmode=4, hpoll=10, ppoll=10, flash=400 peer_dist, keyid=0, ttl=0, offset=-29.750, delay=0.316, dispersion=30.400, jitter=1.136, reftime=d1e4505b.d456f5b0 Thu, Aug 4 2011 0:55:23.829, org=d1e4c793.e477ba4b Thu, Aug 4 2011 9:24:03.892, rec=d1e4c793.ec1fc3ac Thu, Aug 4 2011 9:24:03.922, xmt=d1e4c793.ec0b133c Thu, Aug 4 2011 9:24:03.922, filtdelay= 0.32 0.40 0.33 0.45 0.42 0.42 0.33 0.38, filtoffset=-29.75-30.89-29.97-30.11-30.15-29.20-30.25-30.36, filtdisp= 15.63 31.00 46.38 61.75 77.14 92.52 107.91 123.28 ~~~- The `rv` command displays the system variables billboard, including the system status word.- The `rv assocID` command, where assocID is the association ID, displays the peer variables billboard, including the peer status word. Note that, except for explicit calendar dates, times are in milliseconds and frequencies are in parts-per-million (PPM).- The server has successfully synchronized to its sources if the `leap` peer variable has value other than 3 (11b). The client has successfully synchronized to the server when the leap system variable has value other than 3.- The `reach` peer variable is an 8-bit shift register displayed in octal format. When a valid packet is received, the rightmost bit is lit. When a packet is sent, the register is shifted left one bit with 0 replacing the rightmost bit. If the reach value is nonzero, the server is reachable; otherwise, it is unreachable. Note that, even if all servers become unreachable, the system continues to show valid time to dependent applications.- A useful indicator of miscellaneous problems is the `flash` peer variable, which shows the result of [13 sanity tests](http://www.eecis.udel.edu/~mills/ntp/html/decode.html#flash). It contains the flash status word bits, commonly called flashers, which displays the current errors for the association. These bits should be zero for a valid server.- The flash codes in the rv command output give the reason why the ntp source is rejected: ~~~ flash=400 peer_dist distance threshold exceeded flash=800 peer_loop peer synchronization loop ~~~- Refer this [article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/278043) for details on flash codes.- The three peer variables `filtdelay` `filtoffset` and `filtdisp` show the `delay` `offset` and `jitter` statistics for each of the last eight measurement rounds. These statistics and their trends are valuable performance indicators for the server, client and the network.- For instance, large fluctuations in `delay` and `jitter` suggest network congestion. Missing clock filter stages suggest packet losses in the network.- The synchronization distance, defined as one-half the delay plus the dispersion, represents the maximum error statistic.- The `jitter` represents the expected error statistic.- The maximum error and expected error calculated from the `peer` variables represents the quality metric for the server.- The maximum error and expected error calculated from the `system` variables represents the quality metric for the client.- If the root synchronization distance for any server exceeds 1.5 s, called the select threshold, the server is considered invalid.

title: How to delete stale  information from the Noobaa UI?
issue: After using the Noobaa UI for some administrative operations (deleting buckets, nodes, etc), it's possible that the deleted entities are still displayed by the interface. An example of such scenario can be found in the screenshot below.![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/photo1629967763_0.jpeg)
It's worth mentioning that the Noobaa UI is not intended for any administration activity. Please, for administration purposes, only use the Openshift UI or the `oc` command line.
The reason why these entries are listed is because they are still referred in the Noobaa database. How can they be removed, without directly using the Postgres command line?
resolution: Use the `noobaa api` command to delete these bogus entries.- The instructions to download and install the CLI can be found [at this link](https://red-hat-storage.github.io/ocs-training/training/ocs4/ocs.html#_install_the_noobaa_cli_client).- If the stale entries are Noobaa nodes, once the CLI is installed, execute the following command to delete them from the database: noobaa api node_api delete_node '{"name":"node-name"}'- Similar commands can be used to delete pools, buckets, etc.
root_cause: The Noobaa UI was used for administration purposes, when it's only intended for troubleshooting.

title: How to automatically set default resource request and limit for containers in a deployment ?
issue: - How to use `LimitRange` resource to automatically set default resource `request` and `limit` for containers inside deployments?
resolution: - It is possible to set a default value for resource `request` and `limit` for all containers in a deployment.- Someone can achieve this by creating a `LimitRange` resource inside the project.- Currently, creating a `LimitRange` using `oc` client tool is not supported.- It is important to manually write a `LimitRange` resource definition file and create the resource object in the project.- Someone can follow below steps to achieve this:- Values can be modified based on one's requirement. 1- Create a file with the below content: ~~~ apiVersion: "v1" kind: "LimitRange" metadata: name: deaful-limit spec: limits:- type: "Container" defaultRequest: cpu: "100m" memory: "100Mi" default: cpu: "200m" memory: "200Mi" ~~~ 2- Use the above file to create the `LimitRange` object with below command: ~~~ $ oc create-f default-limit.yaml-n ~~~
root_cause: - It is possible to automatically set default values for resource `request` and `limit` inside all newly created deployments in the namespace leveraging `LimitRange` resource.

title: Unable to pull images from registry.redhat.io and quay.io in RHOCP 4
issue: Unable to pull images from registry.redhat.io and quay.io getting error "unable to pull image: ErrImagePull: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error reading manifest"
resolution: Update the global pull secret using the below steps:- Before changing the pull-secret make a backup of it using the below command: ~~~ oc extract secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--to /home/user/--confirm ~~~ For downloading the pull secret login to the [URL](https://cloud.redhat.com/openshift/install/pull-secret) with the Red Hat credentials that have the OCP subscription. Note: Updating the global pull secret will cause node reboots while the Machine Config Operator (MCO) syncs the changes.- Enter the following command to update the global pull secret for the cluster: ~~~ oc set data secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--from-file=.dockerconfigjson= ~~~ For more details refer to the [Openshift documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/openshift_images/managing_images/using-image-pull-secrets.html#images-update-global-pull-secret_using-image-pull-secrets)
root_cause: Global cluster pull secret which is created at the time of OCP installation and it is having all the pull-secret like quay.io, registry.connect.redhat.com, registry.redhat.io. The global pull secret is expired then the cluster is no longer able to pull images from this registry and will get the error "unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized"

title: "Unable to authenticate the request due to an error - invalid bearer token" error on a newly installed Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x
issue: - On a newly installed Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x system on baremetal, following error is observed. ~~~ E0310 20:52:36.150503 1 authentication.go:65] Unable to authenticate the request due to an error: [invalid bearer token, Post https://172.30.0.1:443/apis/authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1/tokenreviews: dial tcp 172.30.0.1:443: connect: connection refused] ~~~- What can cause this error?
resolution: - This `IP:port` combination `172.30.0.1:443` is on the service subnet.- The error below leads to either the `iptables` rules are not in place to allow this communication or that the `apiserver` backing this call (the `Openshift apiserver`) is refusing the connection or not running/ready. ~~~ E0310 20:52:36.150503 1 authentication.go:65] Unable to authenticate the request due to an error: [invalid bearer token, Post https://172.30.0.1:443/apis/authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1/tokenreviews: dial tcp 172.30.0.1:443: connect: connection refused] ~~~- Check out if the `iptables` rules are in place or not. ~~~ [root@worker-1 ~]# iptables-save | grep 443 | grep 172.30.0.1-A KUBE-SERVICES!-s 10.128.0.0/14-d 172.30.0.1/32-p tcp-m comment--comment "default/kubernetes:https cluster IP"-m tcp--dport 443-j KUBE-MARK-MASQ-A KUBE-SERVICES-d 172.30.0.1/32-p tcp-m comment--comment "default/kubernetes:https cluster IP"-m tcp--dport 443-j KUBE-SVC-NPX46M4PTMTKRN6Y ~~~- Check [this](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/networking/openshift_sdn/configuring-kube-proxy.html) documentation to see if `iptables` are in sync or not. Contact Red Hat Technical Support team for any further clarification.
root_cause: - Missing `iptable` rules or stopped firewall may cause this.

title: Recover the RHCOS image on vSphere when machine stuck in Provisioned Phase in RHOCP 4
issue: - RHCOS image saved by IPI installer on vSphere data store was Powered Up- New machines does not load the ignition files on RHCOS image- New machines stuck in `Provisioned` Phase
resolution: #### For 4.7 and later This issue was fixed on the [latest version of OCP (4.7+)](https://github.com/openshift/installer/pull/4660), the [`RHOCP installer`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere-installer-provisioned.html#cli-installing-cli_installing-vsphere-installer-provisioned) will create a vSphere VM Template after OVF is imported. **The workaround below should be done only *when this VM Template was also modified*. Otherwise, you can restore the RHCOS VM from this template- these steps are not covered in this KCS.** #### Workaround for 4.6 and before A new OVF Template importer on vSphere should be executed to restore the base machine template.- To import the OVF template and restore VM Base image, follow the steps [on this documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere.html#installation-vsphere-machines_installing-vsphere):- Download a new RHCOS ova template on from [the official repository](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/dependencies/rhcos/4.6/);- Upload the chosen template to the same folder in vSphere manually. The procedure to import is located in step **"4. In the vSphere Client, create a template for the OVA image"** on [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere.html#installation-vsphere-machines_installing-vsphere);- Get the existing template name and delete it. The current name is defined on `ProviderSpec`: ~~~ $ oc get machines ${MACHINE_PROVISIONED_PHASE}-n openshift-machine-api-o json | jq.spec.providerSpec.value.template "ocp-stage-clusterId-rhcos" ~~~- After that, rename the new one with the same name as the previous RHCOS template. **Do not Power On this machine after ran those steps, otherwise the OVF should be imported again.**
root_cause: The RHCOS VM image, that is placed on same installation folder on vSphere data store, **should never be Powered Up** due to ignition that enable systemd services only run on the first boot (it leverages systemd presets). According with the [ignition's getting started](https://github.com/coreos/ignition/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#enabling-systemd-services): *"Ignition is not typically run more than once during a machine's lifetime in a given role, so this situation requiring manual systemd intervention does not commonly arise."*, and rerun ignition is actualy not supported- there is a [feature request to improve the troubleshoot when some stuck happens on first boot](https://github.com/coreos/ignition/issues/1214). As the ignition runs only on first boot, if the VM Image was Powered Up manually/accidentally, the ignition will run without machine config objects, then the image will become useless to create new machines. When new machine will be requested, the vSphere will provisioned the Virtual Machine, but no ignition files will be loaded on first boot, then the machine will be stayed in `Provisioned` Phase on `machine-api-controller`. One machine is in Provisioned phase [when](https://github.com/openshift/machine-api-operator/blob/release-4.6/pkg/controller/machine/controller.go#L78-L81):- Instance exists; And/OR- Machine has been given providerID/address; And/OR- Machine has NOT been given nodeRef In this case, the Machine stopped in `Provisioned` phase due no `.status.nodeRef` was assigned by `machine-api nodelink-controller`.

title: How to Scan OpenShift4 Vulnerabilities Using OpenSCAP?
issue: How to scan OpenShift4 vulnerabilities?
How to use OpenSCAP to vulnerabilities in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4?
How to perform a vulnerability scan and generate a report?
resolution: * Choosing one of the nodes that you want to scan ~~~ oc get node oc debug node/$--image=ubi7 ~~~ * Install OpenSCAP and related tools in debug pod ~~~ curl-L \ http://copr.fedoraproject.org/coprs/openscapmaint/openscap-latest/repo/epel-7/openscapmaint-openscap-latest-epel-7.repo-o \ /etc/yum.repos.d/openscapmaint-openscap-latest-epel-7.repo yum install-y openscap openscap-utils scap-security-guide wget bzip2--skip-broken ~~~ * Performing a scan with OpenShift OVAL, e.g. 4.7, we using oscap-chroot to run oscap on it in a filesystem mounted at the given path ~~~ wget https://www.redhat.com/security/data/oval/v2/RHEL8/openshift-4.7.oval.xml.bz2-O- | bzip2--decompress > ropenshift-4.7.oval.xml oscap-chroot /host/ oval eval--report vulnerability.html ropenshift-4.7.oval.xml ~~~ * Copy the scan report from another terminal before you exiting the debug pod ~~~ cp vulnerability.html /host/tmp/vulnerability.html # Find your debug pod name oc get pod NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE $ 1/1 Running 0 87s oc cp $:/host/tmp/vulnerability.html vulnerability.html ~~~ ## Notes: The RHSA OVAL definitions are available individually and as a complete package, and are updated within an hour of a new security advisory being made available on the Red Hat Customer Portal.

title: Is it possible to tweak Descheduler profiles in Openshift 4.7?
issue: - Can the descheduler profiles be modified to tweak the threshold values?- How to enable namespace filtering in OCP 4.7?
resolution: - As of now, changes in profile configurations are not supported.- The engineering team is working on implementing back some of the previously available options including [Namespace filtering](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/WRKLDS-300) and [LowNodeUtilization thresholds](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/WRKLDS-299).
root_cause: - In 4.6 and earlier, the descheduler was Tech Preview so full control was allowed over the configuration with the strategy file.- After publishing as GA, the set of options are restricted down based on the request and supportability, in the interest of cluster stability.

title: ROSA cluster installation state pending Waiting for OIDC configuration
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Creating a cluster using regular **AWS*
accounts works.- When we create and account using **STS*

switches, it hangs. does not appear to provision anything in **AWS**. ~~~ $ rosa list cluster ID NAME STATE 1n2kd3ijdkbseuvi1tpd5sbgt1uocvod migrate ready 1n7r1oi66loiju0ofhbhnvuvbf3uecrl sts-test2 pending ~~~- **Permissions*
say they are correct.- **Account*
is correct.- **Region*
is correct EXCEPT for the `OIDC URL`.- Once the **user*
has run `rosa create cluster` and it shows as `Pending: waiting for OIDC configuration`.
resolution: - Once the **user** has run `rosa create cluster` and it shows as `Pending: waiting for OIDC` they need to run: ~~~ $rosa create operator-roles--cluster ~~~ and ~~~ rosa create oidc-provider--cluster ~~~ This will set up the **roles** and **oidc** and allow the `installer` to move on.
root_cause: - It is been mentioned in the [ROSA documentation](URL "https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_getting_started_sts/rosa-sts-creating-cluster.html#rosa-sts-creating-cluster_rosa-sts-creating-cluster") that `The cluster state is Pending until the following steps are complete`.- `Step 3 and Step 4` need to be completed from the [documentation](URL "https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_getting_started_sts/rosa-sts-creating-cluster.html#rosa-sts-creating-cluster_rosa-sts-creating-cluster") in order to complete the installation successfully.

title: Openshift Pipelines (Tekton) issue when used with LimitRange
issue: - Openshift Pipelines (Tekton) behaves not as expected when used along with LimitRange in a project due to which Pipeline run fails with the below error: ~~~ failed to create task run pod "tekton-vs-limits-9a5zi1-echo-6w9nk": pods "tekton-vs-limits-9a5zi1-echo-6w9nk-pod-vxmhl" is forbidden: cpu max limit to request ratio per Container is 100, but provided ratio is 1000.000000. Maybe missing or invalid Task tekton-vs-limits/echo ~~~
resolution: - The issues with Pipelines operator when used with LimitRange is reported as bug and Engineering team is working on the same. The way in which the default request and limit values are taken will be reworked and upcoming version of the operator will provide better support to the LimitRange setting (Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines 1.6).- The issue has been captured in detail in the bugzilla [1983045](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1983045) and [1989205](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1989205).- No workaround's are available as of now other than adjusting the LimitRange setting in order to accommodate the method of ratio calculation used by Pipelines operator.
root_cause: - The cause of incorrect behavior is that Min value in LimitRange is taken instead of default request, in the calculation of Limit/Request ratio and provide a value way higher than the Max Limit/Request Ratio set, which is unexpected. This causes the init container to fail and the pipeline ends in error.

title: Operator hanging - too many replica sets preventing upgrade
issue: - Console (or other Operator) degraded due to a failed deployment unable to match desired replicas: ~~~ oc get co NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE console 4.6.40 False True False 7h28m ~~~ ~~~ openshift-console-operator pod log: 1 status.go:78] SyncLoopRefreshProgressing InProgress Working toward version 4.6.40 2021-08-13T15:05:31.638320123Z E0813 15:05:31.638150 1 status.go:78] DeploymentAvailable FailedUpdate 2 replicas ready at version 4.6.40 2021-08-13T15:05:34.230178759Z E0813 15:05:34.228554 1 status.go:78] SyncLoopRefreshProgressing InProgress Working toward version 4.6.40 2021-08-13T15:05:34.230178759Z E0813 15:05:34.228575 1 status.go:78] DeploymentAvailable FailedUpdate 2 replicas ready at version 4.6.40 2021-08-13T15:05:36.205704366Z E0813 15:05:36.204832 1 status.go:78] RouteHealthDegraded FailedGet failed to GET route (https://console-redhat.example.com/health): Get "https://console-redhat.example.com/health": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers) ~~~
resolution: - When looking at the deployment for the operator pods, observe 'revisionHistoryLimit' field and determine if you have more replicasets than the set limit. See [Diagnostic Steps]- Delete the replica-sets that are flagged as 0 desired and restart deployment if necessary: ~~~ $ oc get replicasets-n openshift-console: NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AGE console-569c876cc9 0 0 0 34d <- console-58d98dc9c5 0 0 0 14d <- console-59d7f9c6dc 0 0 0 7d <- console-69547b59c4 0 0 0 34d <- console-6bccdb5548 0 0 0 7d <- console-6cf5b647f9 1 1 1 17h console-6fc5786b5d 0 0 0 21d <- console-767f9787b5 0 0 0 21d <- console-794d46fd97 0 0 0 28d <- console-79bf8cdcd 1 0 0 17h console-7b7656697d 0 0 0 28d <- console-d46c5d96 1 1 1 17h console-dcffb5f65 0 0 0 14d <- console-fd9cf5fbd 0 0 0 41d <- downloads-595c4fcff 0 0 0 140d downloads-677479766b 0 0 0 189d downloads-6f9f7cdb56 0 0 0 191d downloads-cfb6c966 0 0 0 189d downloads-d55456f44 2 2 2 17h downloads-fcd5645f5 0 0 0 188d ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get rs-n openshift-console $ oc delete rs/console-569c876cc9-n openshift-console $ oc delete rs/console-58d98dc9c5-n openshift-console #... repeat until all 0 desired RS are removed # rollout the deployment after clearing all empty replicasets: $ oc rollout restart deployment/console-n openshift-console ~~~- Observe successful deployment of pods in operator namespace, and Cluster Operator moving to READY
root_cause: - Observe the deployment status revisionHistoryLimit that has been exceeded with number of replicasets in the namespace matching this deployment with '0 desired' status. Having more than this value in replicasets can stall a deployment.

title: Cluster upgrade getting stuck waiting on monitoring, service-ca
issue: The service-ca operator will in progressing state and monitoring operator will be in degraded state ~~~ $ oc get co NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE [..] monitoring 4.7.21 False False True 4m24s service-ca 4.7.21 True True False 11d ~~~ The service-ca pod will be in pending state: ~~~ $ oc get pod-n openshift-service-ca NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE service-ca-54b7675c-wm7wt 0/1 Pending 0 3d $ oc get pod service-ca-54b7675c-wm7wt-o yaml-n openshift-service-ca state: waiting: message: 'container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root (pod: "service-ca-54b7675c-wm7wt_openshift-service-ca(56b43a68-072d-4995-8b53-6a6e8749db1c)", container: service-ca-controller)' reason: CreateContainerConfigError ~~~
resolution: The right user type is `MustRunAsRange` ~~~ $ oc edit scc restricted runAsUser: type: MustRunAsRange < < < < < < < < ~~~ Check if service-ca pod is running ~~~ $ oc get pod-n openshift-service-ca NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE service-ca-5bd8998c8c-cmx59 1/1 Running 0 30s ~~~

title: To retrieve kube-state-metrics from application pod
issue: Trying to retreive metrics exposed by kube-state-metrics service and openshift-state-metrics service in openshift-monitoring namespace but getting 401 error
resolution: From application pod, it can be accessed using service account token Create a service account: ~~~ $ oc create sa test-sa serviceaccount/test-sa created ~~~ Create a test application deployment mapping the serivce account: ~~~ apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: test-app namespace: test spec: progressDeadlineSeconds: 600 replicas: 1 revisionHistoryLimit: 10 selector: matchLabels: app: test-app strategy: rollingUpdate: maxSurge: 1 maxUnavailable: 0 type: RollingUpdate template: metadata: labels: app: test-app name: test-app spec: containers:- name: test-app command: ["sleep", "3600"] image: quay.io/openshift-examples/toolbox imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst restartPolicy: Always schedulerName: default-scheduler securityContext: {} serviceAccount: test-sa < < < < < < < < < serviceAccountName: test-sa terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 ~~~ Give view built-in role to the service account user: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user view-z test-sa clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/view added: "test-sa" ~~~ Now try accessing from the applicaton pod: ~~~ $ oc rsh test-app-79f96c99c6-5h4xk sh-4.4$ sh-4.4$ curl-k https://kube-state-metrics.openshift-monitoring.svc:9443-H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)" Kube-State-Metrics Metrics Server Kube-State-Metrics Metrics metrics sh-4.4$ sh-4.4$ exit ~~~

title: 3scale APIManager deployed via the operator is not picking up the latest images available
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? Hi Team, According to Red Hat Catalog, the digest of images used by the 3scale operator as well as some of the API Manager components have a bad health index. For instance:- The 3scale operator uses an image corresponding to tag 1.13.0-17 published 5 months ago and graded as a D for the health index. Please see the attached screenshots: 3scaleOperator_0_70_image_digest.png and 3scaleOperator_0_70_image_tag_history.png- The 3scale API Manager system-app component uses a an image corresponding to tag 1.14-0-12 released 6 months ago and graded as a D for the health index. Please see the attached screenshots: 3scale2-10_system-app_image_digest.png and 3scale2-10_system-app_image_tag_history.png For the above image samples, there seem to be more recent images which have a better health index (A). Isn't the 3scale operator (as well as the API Manager components) supposed to fetch the latest images of the installed 3scale version if available during a fresh install (or automatically)? Can this be enforced? Euro-information are using disconnected OpenShift clusters but the Red Hat Image Catalog is mirrored through JFrog Artifactory. Unfortunately, the Ops team keeps getting bad health index alerts (Jfrog Xray) on 3scale component images. Any feedback is welcome regarding how to mitigate this issue. Thanks in advance. Jean Nyilimbibi Red Hat France Consulting Architect Where are you experiencing the behavior? What environment? VALIDATION When does the behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times? Repeatedly
resolution: Hello Jean, Thank you for contacting the Red Hat support. My name is Gustavo and I'll be assisting you on this case. We already have an internal ticket opened with engineering about this issue and can be tracked [here](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-7435). The engineering is already aware of this problem. The way it works is: The components images (backend, apicast,...) URLs are referenced in the Operator ClusterServiceVersion (an OLM concept). The operators do not reference floating tags of the images but images that contain a fixed SHA identifier. The reason for that is because that way of referencing images is required to support Network-Restricted installations. To fix this issue, each time a component image automatically changes (because of a CVE for example) a new operator OLM release would be needed (a new CSV has to be deployed so it triggers redeployment of the components with the new images). However, until very recently Red Hat (Freshmaker) did not provide any mechanism to automatically create a new CSV version each time there's an automated image change of any of its operands (backend, apicast,...) through Freshmaker. That's why we are observing the operator not using the components new images. This automation mechanism has been implemented recently in Red Hat and they plan to make use of it to try to avoid the kind of issue reported starting in **3scale 2.11**. You could overwrite the corresponding component image in the CR attribute of the APIManager but overwriting the image invalidates upgrades because overwritten images are not upgraded when an upgrade is performed. So, it's recommended to wait the next release in order to check whether this issue has been fixed. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: No Priority Class is defined in the openshift-ingress-canary daemon set
issue: - The **openshift-ingress-canary*
DaemonSet does not have a priority class defined which causes the pods to stay in a pending status.
resolution: - By default, there is no **PriorityClass** defined in the **OpenShift v4.7** but in **OpenShift v4.8**, the `system-cluster-critical` priorityClassName is defined by default.- The priority class can be updated by using these [pod priority classes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/scheduling/priority_preemption.html#admin-guide-priority-preemption-priority-class).
root_cause: - The **openshift-ingress-canary** DaemonSet will try to start a pod on a specific node and that node will have some resources available. Since no priority class is defined, this leaves the pods to stay in the pending state. Priority class helps the pod to start on the specific nodes and removes the lower priority pods.

title: Problem to configuring Viewing Cluster Logs by Using Kibana
issue: When configuring *Viewing Cluster Logs by Using Kibana*, according to https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/logging/cluster-logging-visualizer.html#cluster-logging-visualizer-kibana_cluster-logging-visualizer in the Kibana interface, after clicking **Discover**, it should appear a drop-down menu in the top-left corner with **app**, **audit**, and **infra*
options, to create the index, but nothing appears.
resolution: Include `default` in one of `outputRefs` of `ClusterLogForwarder` instance: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging edit ClusterLogForwarder instance... pipelines:- inputRefs:- audit- application- infrastructure name: rsyslog-001 outputRefs:- rsyslog-01- default < < <======= Include this line... ~~~
root_cause: A `default` clausure is necessary in one of `outputRefs` definition inside `pipelines`.

issue: We are trying to use non root account for external database in OpenShift 4.7 and 3Scale operator but it does not seem to work Using root account not considered acceptable for our mysql cluster
resolution: Hello Karri, Thank you for contacting the Red Hat support. My name is Gustavo and I'll be assisting you on this case. Please refer to the 3scale official [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.10/html/installing_3scale/configure-external-mysql-database#external-mysql-database-limitations) where points out about the MySQL database user. Although there is a `mysql2://` formatted URL that would supposedly allow for any combination of username and password, the user `'root'@'%'` should always be used otherwise the connection to the database will fail. The reason behind it is that some sections from Red Hat 3scale are still hardcoded to use the `'root'@'%'` user and it's a technical requirement at this time. > With the mysql2:// formatted URL, **you must use 'root'@'%'** or the connection to the database will fail. Using any combination of username and password is not supported since 3scale uses 'root'@'%'. I hope this information is useful for you. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: Disk attach and mount takes very long while creating  pod with multiple AzureDisks
issue: - The attach or mount is taking a very long time when multiple machines request it at the same time- AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc- ": Retriable: true, RetryAfter: 0s, HTTPStatusCode:-1, RawError: Future#WaitForCompletion: context has been cancelled: StatusCode=200-- Original Error: context deadline exceeded- Application pod has multiple AzureDisks attached to it, and while creating a pod, it take a significant amount of time for the pod to become ready.
resolution: - For pods with more than 1 AzureDisk volume, each mount takes in average of 80 to 120 Seconds, This is based on the way Azure Plugin updates the VM Config on Azure API.
root_cause: - When the pod with multiple AzureDisk volume is created, the Kube-Controller instructs the Azure Plugin to attach the Specific Azure Disks, which updates the VM config on Azure independently instead of Batch update which creates multiple disk attach operations on Azure portal.- These operations are executed sequentially which causes delay while attaching the disk to the node.

title: Is it supported to change netmasks in a running OpenShift 4 cluster?
resolution: - Changing node netmasks is considered a job outside OpenShift and therefore there is not any supportability objection in this regard. OpenShift does not require any specific netmask for its nodes either.- At the time when this KCS article is being written (latest OpenShift version is 4.7), changing service and pod netmasks is not supported.- There is a request for enhancement asking to allow netmask range extensions on later OpenShift versions. For more information, please contact [Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/support).- Reducing netmask ranges is not expected to be supported in the future.

title: Can master nodes in OpenShift be vms hosted on RHEL 8 KVM Hypervisor?
issue: - Can OpenShift master vms be hosted on RHEL 8 KVM Hypervisor or do we need RHV infra or VMware?- Is running master vms on RHEL 8 a supported deployment method?- Can the hypervisor be plain RHEL 8 KVM/libvirt for hosting the vms?
resolution: - Master nodes can be virtual machines hosted on RHEL8 KVM Hypervisor provided that masters always need to be Red Hat CoreOS systems and can be in any form. The communication should be seamless between the masters and the workers.- There should be no firewall in between and if firewall exists, all required ports should be open. The hypervisor should provide the bridged network instead of NAT network.- If there is a mixed environment, Red Hat would recommend the baremetal procedure to consider all machines as baremetal. One can't mix clouds infra with in-house infra.- For example: AWS+RHV is not possible but RHV+Baremetal+vmware is possible, only if they are considered as baremetal. The RHEL8 KVM/libvirt virtual machines can be used as masters, and in practical, having virtual machines as masters is very much used.- While choosing the deployment, one needs to make sure that the process should be baremetal. Additionally, please consider the incoming traffic as well as minimum requirements for the masters before building on RHEL8 KVM Hypervisor.- Red Hat tested RHCOS masters deployment on both RHV virtual machines as well as KVM, the only difference here would be that one need to consider these machines as baremetal since there isn't a dedicated process for KVM machines. RHV provides additional features over normal KVM offerings from RHEL8.

title: Elasticsearch in yellow state with 50% of unassigned shards
issue: The state of the elasticsearch will be in yellow and 50% of the shards will be in unassigned: ~~~ $ oc exec-c elasticsearch elasticsearch-cdm-xxxx-- es_util--query=_cat/health?v epoch timestamp cluster status node.total node.data shards pri relo init unassign pending_tasks max_task_wait_time active_shards_percent 1632251498 19:11:38 elasticsearch yellow 2 2 124 124 0 0 124 0- 50.0% ~~~ All the replica shards will be in UNASSIGNED ~~~ $ oc exec-c elasticsearch elasticsearch-cdm-xxxx-- es_util--query=_cat/shards?h=index,shard,prirep,state,unassigned.reason,node | grep UNASSIGNED [...] infra-000983 1 r UNASSIGNED INDEX_CREATED infra-000983 0 r UNASSIGNED INDEX_CREATED audit-000974 1 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT audit-000974 0 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT app-002838 1 r UNASSIGNED INDEX_CREATED app-002838 0 r UNASSIGNED INDEX_CREATED infra-000972 1 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT infra-000972 0 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT [...] infra-000986 1 r UNASSIGNED INDEX_CREATED infra-000986 0 r UNASSIGNED INDEX_CREATED infra-000971 1 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT infra-000971 0 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT audit-000971 1 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT audit-000971 0 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT audit-000973 1 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT audit-000973 0 r UNASSIGNED NODE_LEFT ~~~
resolution: The elasticsearch `cluster.routing.allocation.enable` value is set to `all` so that replica shards will get assigned. ~~~ $ oc rsh-c elasticsearch elasticsearch-cdm-xxxx # curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'-XPUT https://localhost:9200/_cluster/settings-d '{"persistent": {"cluster.routing.allocation.enable": "all"}}' GET /_cluster/health?pretty {"cluster_name": "elasticsearch", "status": "green", < < < < < < < < < < < < "timed_out": false, "number_of_nodes": 2, "number_of_data_nodes": 2, "active_primary_shards": 130, "active_shards": 260, "relocating_shards": 0, "initializing_shards": 0, "unassigned_shards": 0, < < < < < < < < < < < < < "delayed_unassigned_shards": 0, "number_of_pending_tasks": 0, "number_of_in_flight_fetch": 0, "task_max_waiting_in_queue_millis": 0, "active_shards_percent_as_number": 100.0 < < < < < < < < < <} $ oc get elasticsearch NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT elasticsearch Managed green 2 2 all ~~~ Note: It will take sometime for the shards to get assigned based on the number.

title: Instance & Handler objects missing in Service Mesh Version 2
issue: The resource for instance and handler objects are available in OSSM v1 ~~~ $ oc project istio-system-v1 Now using project "istio-system-v1" on server "https://:6443". $ oc get instances NAME AGE attributes 152m requestcount 152m requestduration 152m requestsize 152m responsesize 152m tcpbytereceived 152m tcpbytesent 152m tcpconnectionsclosed 152m tcpconnectionsopened 152m $ oc get handlers NAME AGE kubernetesenv 152m prometheus 152m ~~~ The resource for instance and handler objects are missing in OSSM v2 ~~~ $ oc project istio-system-v2 Now using project "istio-system-v2" on server "https://:6443". $ oc get instances No resources found in istio-system-v2 namespace. $ oc get handlers No resources found in istio-system-v2 namespace. ~~~
resolution: Update the SMCP `spec.telemetry.type` to `Mixer` ~~~ $ cat istio-installation.yaml apiVersion: maistra.io/v2 kind: ServiceMeshControlPlane metadata: name: basic namespace: istio-system spec: version: v2.0 telemetry: type: Mixer tracing: type: Jaeger sampling: 10000 addons: jaeger: name: jaeger install: storage: type: Memory kiali: enabled: true name: kiali grafana: enabled: true $ oc get smcp NAME READY STATUS PROFILES VERSION AGE basic 10/10 ComponentsReady ["default"] 2.0.7.1 3m51s $ oc get instances NAME AGE attributes 3m22s requestcount 2m38s requestduration 2m38s requestsize 2m39s responsesize 2m37s tcpbytereceived 2m38s tcpbytesent 2m39s tcpconnectionsclosed 2m38s tcpconnectionsopened 2m37s $ oc get handlers NAME AGE kubernetesenv 3m29s prometheus 2m45s ~~~
root_cause: Check the SMCP for the field `spec.telemetry.type`. It's `Istiod` by default. This feature is provided by `Mixer` which is deprecated in OSSM v2.0.

title: How make changes in worker node without impacting infra node
issue: - How to customize the changes in OpenShift nodes- How to segregate the node configuration for worker nodes- How to make custom configurations for nodes
resolution: To customize the OpenShift nodes configurations, We have to perform the below task 1) Create a custom MCP similar to [infra MCP.](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5034771) ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfigPool metadata: name: custom spec: machineConfigSelector: matchExpressions:- {key: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role, operator: In, values: [worker,custom]} < < < < nodeSelector: matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/custom: "" # oc create-f # oc get mcp NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE custom rendered-custom-29c0675d3542db9d0e550e26553a4683 True False False 1 1 1 0 2d1h infra rendered-infra-8d3199291936eefd126db9680226c0fc True False False 1 1 1 0 3d22h master rendered-master-051fd019d55c2cdeb178d552f01a0617 True False False 3 3 3 0 4d22h worker rendered-worker-abe7106d309a941aaf211fc3b2294d5f True False False 3 3 3 0 4d22h ~~~ 2) Now label the worker node with a custom label ~~~ # oc label node node-role.kubernetes.io/custom="" # oc get node NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ip-10-0-150-122.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready infra 3d23h v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-155-195.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready master 5d v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-163-192.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready custom,worker 4d23h v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-165-19.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready master 5d v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-190-96.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready worker 3d23h v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-208-156.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready worker 2d1h v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-215-23.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready master 5d v1.19.0+b00ba52 ip-10-0-223-121.ap-southeast-1.compute.internal Ready worker 2d1h v1.19.0+b00ba52 ~~~ 3) Now create the MC for custom mcp only ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: custom < < < name: 40-custom spec: config: ignition: version: 3.1.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:,test filesystem: root mode: 0644 path: /etc/testinfra3 #oc create-f #oc get mc|grep-i cust 40-custom 3.1.0 46h ~~~ This time MCP will apply to the node which has a custom label only. It will go to any other nodes. Solution 2:- Now for KubeletConfig config changes, You have to perform the below task 1) Label the custom mcp with key/value pair. ~~~ # oc label machineconfigpool custom custom-kubelet=small-pods # oc get mcp custom-oyaml|grep-i pod custom-kubelet: small-pods ~~~ 2) Now create KubeletConfig yaml and include key/value pair. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: KubeletConfig metadata: name: set-max-pods-1 spec: machineConfigPoolSelector: matchLabels: custom-kubelet: small-pods < < < < kubeletConfig: podsPerCore: 20 maxPods: 200 # oc create-f # oc get mc|grep-i custom 99-custom-generated-kubelet 093319e36578d1d40f02e4d8ba939dee1f536448 3.1.0 161m ~~~ 3) Now create the KubeletConfig, It will apply to do the mcp having with custom-kubelet=small-pods label and which will update the only node with having a custom label. It will go to any other nodes. Note:- Above examples are just to reference, Please do changes as per your requirement.
root_cause: If we don't create the custom mcp/mc and try to apply the changes directly on worker nodes then it will get implemented on all the other nodes which are subsets of workers.

title: OpenShift Container Platform SDN Hosted Egress IP's are not being scheduled to nodes after upgrade to 4.8
issue: A deadlock in OCP SDN egress IP management was found, causing the SDN and thus OCP internal networking to stop working as expected.
Post update to 4.8.12, Egress IP's are not scheduled to any node via automatic namespace allocation using openshift-SDN network type.

Experiencing a total loss of all egress IP addresses (previously functional in 4.7.x pre-update) across all nodes- nodes are simply not having the egress IP allocated to the internal networks, despite validating egress cidr and egress IP allocation in automatic mode
resolution: * Red Hat is aware about this issue and working on a solution via [RHBZ #2008987](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2008987) to address it in a future version of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8. * Due to the overall impact of this issue, Red Hat has decided to stop recommending updates from Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.7 to 4.8 for the time being. * Customers running already on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8 and are experiencing Egress IP problems, should review the Root Cause and Diagnostic section of this Solution or reach out to [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport). ### Workaround Reboot the `SDN` pod on the Node experiencing the problem, alternatively all `SDN` pods sequentially. This however does not fix the problem completely, and the problem (read: deadlock) might occur later on once again when the problematic condition is met.
root_cause: Egress IP deadlock in `openshift-sdn` on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform- Nodes. `openshift-sdn` pods risk deadlocking the `go-routine` managing Egress IP assignments, in certain conditions. This halts all operations on that Node for what concerns the Egress IP management, for all namespaces and Egress IPs defined on the cluster. ### Details `openshift-sdn` usually performs two main tasks, it: * writes `iptables` rules and `OVS` flows programming the network for Egress IP on every Node * health checks Egress Nodes to determine if they can continue servicing Egress traffic. The issue is triggered by the corner cases where a Node goes offline/NotReady, subsequently requiring `openshift-sdn` to re-compute the Egress IP assignment. This computation (health-checking and re-assigning Egress IPs) requires several locks on shared internal data for the program to function properly. The deadlock is triggered by an unsafe ordering of events and locking on this internal data. Given the nature of the problem and that Nodes can always go offline or NotReady. The problem is however more susceptible to occur when the cluster entropy is increased (i.e: a lot of Node/sdn-pod reboots)- which usually happens during a cluster upgrade.

title: Can CCSP entitlements be enabled for Cloud Access or Public Cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) consumption?
issue: - How to Enable **New Products*
in **Cloud Access*

while using a Certified Cloud Service Provider (CCSP) subscription?- How to use Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Gold Images in AWS with a CCSP subscription?- Why is RHEL not available in the **Enable New Products*
section of the **Cloud Access*
(for AWS or Azure) while using a CCSP subscription?
resolution: #### Cloud Access and Gold Images with CCSP- The CCSP (Certified Cloud and Service Providers[^1]) Program[^2] doesn't provide entitlements compatible with [Red Hat Cloud Access](https://access.redhat.com/public-cloud), and therefore [RHEL Gold Images for AWS EC2](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2962171) are not available.- Gold Images for AWS are available only through Cloud Access #### Public Cloud and Custom Images with CCSP- RHEL Custom Images con be built for AWS, GCP (Google Cloud Platform) or Microsoft Azure and register them as regular hosts using the Bring Your Own Subscription (BYOS) model by registering the RHEL server with the Red Hat Subscription Management (RHSM) in the Customer Portal or registering it to your Satellite Server with an Activation Key if available.- **Note:** Terms and conditions apply, verify the [CCSP Program Guide](https://connect.redhat.com/programs/certified-cloud-service-provider). [^1]: [Red Hat Certified Cloud and Service Providers](https://www.redhat.com/en/certified-cloud-and-service-providers) [^2]: [Red Hat Certified Cloud and Service Provider Program](https://connect.redhat.com/en/programs/certified-cloud-service-provider)
root_cause: The [Red Hat Certified Cloud and Service Providers](https://www.redhat.com/en/certified-cloud-and-service-providers) [Program](https://connect.redhat.com/en/programs/certified-cloud-service-provider) doesn't provide entitlements compatible with [Red Hat Cloud Access](https://access.redhat.com/public-cloud), and therefore you can't enable the products in the Customer Portal to share the Gold Images with those services.

title: Behavior of CPU manager with realtime and cpu-partitioning tuned profiles
issue: OpenShift provides the [Performance Addon Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/scalability_and_performance/cnf-performance-addon-operator-for-low-latency-nodes.html) and the [Cluster Node Tuning Operator](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-node-tuning-operator) for fine tuning your workers for low-latency applications. Unfortunately both relies on [Machine Config Operator](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator) to work. This means they won't work if your workers are RHEL based. ## Tuned profiles: realtime or cpu-partitioning If you use RHEL workers, both profiles will provide CPU isolation when configured. The major difference between them is how they achieve isolation:

[realtime profile](https://github.com/redhat-performance/tuned/blob/master/profiles/realtime/tuned.conf) will use the ["isolcpus" kernel parameter](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/performance_tuning_guide/sect-red_hat_enterprise_linux-performance_tuning_guide-cpu-configuration_suggestions#sect-Red_Hat_Enterprise_Linux-Performance_Tuning_Guide-Tuning_scheduling_policy-Isolating_CPUs).

[cpu-partitioning profile](https://github.com/redhat-performance/tuned/blob/master/profiles/cpu-partitioning/tuned.conf) will use the [systemd CPU affinity parameter](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/managing_monitoring_and_updating_the_kernel/assembly_configuring-cpu-affinity-and-numa-policies-using-systemd_managing-monitoring-and-updating-the-kernel) and the ["rcu_nocbs" kernel parameter](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux_for_real_time/7/html/tuning_guide/offloading_rcu_callbacks). ## CPU manager Since we cannot use PAO (nor NTO) with RHEL workers, we need to rely directly on [CPU Manager](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/scalability_and_performance/using-cpu-manager.html) to constraints workload to specific CPUs. The results are different depending on the type of pod and the tuned profile used: | Tuned Profile | Guaranteed Pod | Burstable Pod | |:----------|:----------|:----------| | realtime | isolated CPUs assigned, but workload running only on the first CPU **[1]*
| non-isolated CPUs assigned | | cpu-partitioning | isolated CPUs assigned | isolated and non-isolated CPUs assigned **[2]*
root_cause: **[1]** with OCP4, isolcpus will disable [CFS scheduler](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/how-to-handle-openshift-worker-nodes-resources-in-overcommitted-state) which means no scheduling of threads. That's why the workload is running only on the first isolated CPU assigned. **[2]** with OCP4, "isolated" really means "available for isolation": * interrupts, kernel processes, OS/systemd processes will always run on reserved CPUs as configured in CPU Manager ([reservedSystemCPUs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-resources-cpus.html)). * burstable pods will run on reserved CPUs and isolated CPUs **NOT** used by a guaranteed pod. This is how Kubernetes implemented CPU Manager. * guaranteed pods will be pinned to a specific set of CPUs from the isolated pool (i.e available for isolation). Please note that for OCP4: * reserved + isolated CPUs must equals all the CPUs on the server. * reserved CPUs should be large enough to accommodate the kernel and its OS. * a guaranteed pod will have the CPUs dedicated to itself after 5 to 10 seconds (configurable) but setting it too low will put higher load on the node. * total of allocatable CPUs of a node = capacity- reserved.

title: RHOCP 4.x cluster goes down due to tainted master/s
issue: - Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.7 cluster and API server went down as all `master nodes` were tainted with `NoExecute` ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes elasticsearch=node:NoExecute ~~~- `oc` utility not working hence not able to remove tainted by below commands. ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes elasticsearch=NoExecute- ~~~ OR ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes elasticsearch- ~~~
resolution: - Connect to one of the `master node` terminal by `ssh`.- Find out the `kubeconfig` file and `export` it. ~~~ $ cd /var/lib/kubelet/ $ ls $ export KUBECONFIG=kubeconfig ~~~- With ` kubeadmin` password, try to login from the `master node` itself by executing below commands and perform `taint` action. ~~~ $ oc login-u kubeadmin-p "password" https://:6443 $ oc adm taint nodes elasticsearch=NoExecute- ~~~- It will work out and `taint` will be removed and the cluster will become `healthy` again.
root_cause: - After `tainted`, all the `nodes` including `master` with `NoExecute` effect it works like below and caused the issue.- New `pods` that do not match the `taint` cannot be scheduled onto that `node`.- Existing `pods` on the `node` that do not have matching toleration are removed.

title: A security scan reports a DNS poisoning vulnerability for dnsmasq
issue: Unauthenticated dynamic DNS updates reported in a security scan
resolution: Dnsmasq does not support dynamic DNS updates as described in RFC 2136. This is a false positive.
root_cause: Attempting to perform a dynamic update against dnsmasq does not return an error, but dnsmasq does not provide this feature. Updates will not result in any actual changes to DNS.

title: How to reset the SELinux policy on an RHCOS node in OCP
issue: - SELinux **policy changes*
(adding or changing policy modules) are not supported on Red Hat CoreOS nodes in an OpenShift cluster.- Changing SELinux **booleans*
is supported following this solution: [4910611](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4910611)
resolution: 1. Copy the default SELinux policy over the modified configuration: ~~~ $ rsync-av /usr/etc/selinux/ /etc/selinux/ ~~~ 2. Check that there are no more changes or additions to the policy: ~~~ $ ostree admin config-diff | grep 'selinux/' ~~~ 3. Delete any entries marked with 'A' (example): ~~~ $ ostree admin config-diff | grep 'selinux/'... A selinux/targeted/policy/policy.30... $ sudo rm /etc/selinux/targeted/policy/policy.30 ~~~- The output from the previous command should now be empty: ~~~ $ ostree admin config-diff | grep 'selinux/' ~~~ 4. Reboot
root_cause: rpm-ostree does not support rebuilding the SELinux policy with custom admin changes during updates. This issue is tracked upstream in: [rpm-ostree#27](https://github.com/coreos/rpm-ostree/issues/27)

XXX YY ZZ:ZZ:ZZ [1]: Failed to start Generate console-login-helper-messages issue snippet. ~~~

title: Configuring least privileged restricted and hostaccess SCC policy in a project/namespace on RHOCP 4
issue: - Configuring an `SCC` policy with least-privileged access.- From several microservices out of which 90% can be deployed using `restricted` SCC and 10% of them need `hostaccess` SCC, and don't want 90% of microservices to latch to `hostaccess` SCC.
resolution: - Can deploy 90% of them using `restricted` that is by default SCC will be allocated in OCP projects.- For 10% of them whoever needs `hostaccess` SCC can be achieved by assign SCC to service account. For example: `1).` Create a service account for using with 10% of microservices. ~~~ $ oc create serviceaccount tenpercent ~~~ `2).` Associate the policy to the service account. ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user hostaccess-z tenpercent ~~~ `3).` Patch/edit application YAML to use the desired service account. ~~~ $ oc patch dc/myAppNeedsRoot--patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName": "tenpercent"}}}}' ~~~- For syntax validation refer [Offical Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/authentication/managing-security-context-constraints.html).

title: Custom wildcard certificates for APIcast on Red Hat 3scale 2.5 and Openshift 3.11
issue: Create a custom wildcard certificate for every application that will be managed by 3scale.

Secure wildcard routes for 3scale are not configured correctly. Showing up as insecure in browser. OCP cluster certificates OCP domain = ocp.mydomain.com OCP apps domain = *.apps.ocp.mydomain.com 3scale wildcard domain = *.apim.apps.ocp.mydomain.com
resolution: There are 2 options to solve this issue. * OCP Router Add a `SAN (Subject Alternative Name)` to the default certificate used in the OCP router. The certificate will still be issued for `*.apps.ocp.mydomain.com`, but it will contain a `SAN` to `*.apim.apps.ocp.mydomain.com`. * 3scale Router Generate and include a new certificate for `*.apim.apps.ocp.mydomain.com`in the 3scale `wildcard` route following the `Secured Routes` section in the [OpenShift 3.11 Routes Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/architecture/networking/routes.html#secured-routes). For later version of 3scale and OCP 4, see [Custom certificates for APIcast on Red Hat 3scale 2.6 or later](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6462591)
root_cause: Certificates for wildcard routes don't work recursively. Hence, a certificate for `*.apps.ocp.mydomain.com` will only validate `example1.apps.ocp.mydomain.com` and `example2.apps.ocp.mydomain.com`, but not `example1.apim.apps.ocp.mydomain.com` and `example2.apim.apps.ocp.mydomain.com`.

title: How to use and confirm SMTP AUTH with DIGEST-MD5 CRAM-MD5 on Postfix.
issue: Can we use SMTP AUTH with DIGEST-MD5 CRAM-MD5 on Postfix? If we can use it, how can we check if DIGEST-MD5 or CRAM-MD5 is working?
resolution:
### How to configure smtp auth with postfix 1) install cyrus-sasl-md5 ~~~ # yum install cyrus-sasl-md5 ~~~ 2) /etc/sasl2/smtpd.conf の設定を以下に変更 (Before) ~~~ pwcheck_method: saslauthd mech_list: plain login ~~~ (After) ~~~ pwcheck_method: auxprop mech_list: plain login DIGEST-MD5 CRAM-MD5 ~~~ 3) creat a user by saslpasswd2 ~~~ # saslpasswd2-u Hostname(FQDN)-c Usrename ~~~ You can check the user by sasldblistusers2 ~~~ # sasldblistusers2 ~~~ 4) change the permission of /etc/sasldb2 which was created by creating the user to postfix ~~~ # ls-tlrt /etc/sasldb2-rw-r-----. 1 root root 12288 Nov 1 10:46 /etc/sasldb2 # chmod postfix /etc/sasldb2 # ls-tlr /etc/sasldb2-rw-r-----. 1 postfix root 12288 Nov 1 10:46 /etc/sasldb2 ~~~ 5) Configure smtp auth in Postfix. /etc/postfix/main.cf e.g. ~~~: smtpd_sasl_auth_enable = yes smtpd_sasl_local_domain = $myhostname smtpd_relay_restrictions = permit_mynetworks,permit_sasl_authenticated,reject_unauth_destination ~~~ 7) restart postfix ~~~ # systemctl restart postfix ~~~ ### How to confirm if DIGEST-MD5,CRAM-MD5,PLAIN can work on postfix Here, we can show how to confirm CRAM-MD5, PLAIN. title: After Reinstalling RHACM local-cluster Shows Detaching Status
resolution: Manually clean the `managedcluster` and `manifestworks` for the `local-clusters` namespace:- Edit the `managedclusters` and remove the finalizers that are listed: ~~~ $ kubectl edit managedclusters local-cluster Delete the items in finalizers field and save the file. ~~~- Edit `manifestworks`and remove the finalizers that are listed: ~~~ $ kubectl edit manifestworks local-cluster-klusterlet-n local-cluster Delete the items in finalizers field and save the file. $kubectl edit manifestworks local-cluster-klusterlet-crds-n local-cluster Delete the items in finalizers field and save the file. ~~~- `MultiClusterHub`will stand up a new local-cluster on its next reconcile.
root_cause: - Red Hat is tracking this issue in [BZ-2016025](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2016025)

title: Why are Openshift Container Storage Nodes Observing 'Disk Pressure' Events When a Soseport is Being Collected?
issue: Nodes hosting Gluster pods in Openshift Container Storage, are facing `Disk pressure`events, leading to pod evictions: 15s 15s 1 glusterfs-pod1 Pod Warning Evicted kubelet, node1.example.cm The node had condition: [DiskPressure]. 14s 14s 1 glusterfs-pod1 Pod Warning Evicted kubelet, node1.example.com The node had condition: [DiskPressure].
At the same time, a `sosreport`with the `--all-logs`option was being collected.
Why is the node facing disk pressure for the collection of a sosreport? How to avoid these events?
resolution: * Use the variable `--tmp-dir`to set an alternate location to `/var/tmp`for the sosreport collection. Choose a directory with sufficient space. * Alternatively, provide the requested logs as a separate tarball.
root_cause: By default, the sosreport utility stores the collected information at `/var/tmp` folder. If the sosreport stored is big (as it might happen when all the logs are collected), this file system might get full. This will cause Openshift monitoring to trigger a `disk pressure`event on this node and consequently, the hosted gluster pod will evict.

title: Pull image using OpenShift ImageRegistry default route
issue: - Pulling image using OpenShift image-registry default route. ~~~ Warning Failed 3m44s kubelet Failed to pull image "default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.. /image/xxxx:xx": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = error pinging docker registry default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps..: Get "https://default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.. /v2/": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority Warning Failed 3m44s kubelet Error: ErrImagePull ~~~
resolution: - Add the image registry default route to insecureRegistries: ~~~ $ oc edit image.config.openshift.io/cluster... spec: registrySources: insecureRegistries:- default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps..... ~~~- This will trigger an MCP rollout which will modify `/etc/containers/registries.conf` on all the nodes and append the following: ~~~ [[registry]] prefix = "" location = "default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.. " insecure = true ~~~
root_cause: - The issue is due to the self-signed Ingress certificate which is used by the ingress controller and the ingress certificate CA is not identified by the node.

title: Enable Windows Machine Config Operator in existing cluster.
issue: - Windows workload failed to run in existing cluster.- Enable hybrid networking in existing cluster.
resolution: - Windows workload can only be enabled in a cluster where the networking type is set to OVNKubernetes and Hybrid Networking is enabled.- OVNKubernetes networking can be changed after cluster installation.- Hybrid Networking can only enabled during the installation and cannot be modified post installation.- If the existing cluster is not enabled with Hybrid networking, Windows workload cannot be enabled.
root_cause: - For WindowsMachineConfigOperator(WMCO), OVNKubernetes and Hybrid Networking is prime requirement as per [Prerequisites](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/windows_containers/enabling-windows-container-workloads.html#installing-wmco-using-cli_enabling-windows-container-workloads) and [Configure OVN Kubernetes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/networking/ovn_kubernetes_network_provider/configuring-hybrid-networking.html#configuring-hybrid-ovnkubernetes_configuring-hybrid-networking)

title: Is there a way to update a package version in  Red Hat base image?
issue: - The latest UBI8/Python 3.8 base image has sqlite package version 'sqlite-3.26.0-13.el8.x86_64'.- Is there an option that Red Hat updates the base image to a newer sqlite version?- Is there a recommended way to update sqlite? It seems not to be available with yum.
resolution: - In most situations Red Hat do not ship the very latest of any given package/component. We pick known good, stable releases then package, test and ship them to our Enterprise customers.- Our container images are based on RHEL. So, if something is not in RHEL (like an updated version of sqlite) then it's impossible for it to be in our container images.- If you can't find a newer version of a package in yum, it's not likely to exist. There is no chance of any newer version. You could take the base image and maybe pull the source and compile it into the image, but that's not supported from Red Hat.

title: How can we download helm safely?
issue: - OpenShift command-line tools (oc/helm) are available in the same mirror registry [URL](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/stable/).- oc command line tool has a checksum file that has been encrypted by Red Hat GPG key. But, helm checksum file is not encrypted.
root_cause: - It seems that OCP is taking the extra precaution. But, it is definitely not a Red Hat standard to sign the SHA file. Take a look at all clients present in this [URL](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/).- For example: [rosa](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/rosa/1.1.3/). It's SHA file is not encrypted by Red Hat GPG key.- Red Hat do sign the Binaries for mac and windows and have already filed a request for feature enhancement for signing and notarizing helm binary which has been completed. So, its safe to download helm.
