title: iavf/i40evf reset triggers kernel BUG at drivers/pci/msi.c:357
issue: - Kernel panic with the following messages: ~~~ [2102.281242] iavf 0000:12:0b.0: Hardware reset detected [2106.717332] iavf 0000:12:0b.6: Reset never finished (0) [2106.722641]------------[cut here]------------ [2106.727282] kernel BUG at drivers/pci/msi.c:357! ~~~- The back trace of panic task: ~~~ crash> bt PID: 1051 TASK: ffff88f53647a0e0 CPU: 54 COMMAND: "kworker/54:1" #0 [ffff88f532ccfa20] machine_kexec at ffffffff81c65b24 #1 [ffff88f532ccfa80]__crash_kexec at ffffffff81d22342 #2 [ffff88f532ccfb50] crash_kexec at ffffffff81d22430 #3 [ffff88f532ccfb68] oops_end at ffffffff82385798 #4 [ffff88f532ccfb90] die at ffffffff81c30a7b #5 [ffff88f532ccfbc0] do_trap at ffffffff82384ee0 #6 [ffff88f532ccfc10] do_invalid_op at ffffffff81c2d2a4 #7 [ffff88f532ccfcc0] invalid_op at ffffffff8239122e [exception RIP: free_msi_irqs+0x188] RIP: ffffffff81ff1118 RSP: ffff88f532ccfd70 RFLAGS: 00010282 RAX: ffff88f534b8a900 RBX: 0000000000000000 RCX: ffff88f534b8a900 RDX: ffff88f534b8a900 RSI: 0000000000000000 RDI: 0000000000000000 RBP: ffff88f532ccfd98 R8: 0000000000000002 R9: ffff88f532ccfcfc R10: 000000000000005e R11: ffff88ca54996a00 R12: ffff88f519aa8840 R13: ffff88b7262ed870 R14: ffff88b7262ed000 R15: ffff88ca66112910 ORIG_RAX: ffffffffffffffff CS: 0010 SS: 0018 #8 [ffff88f532ccfda0] pci_disable_msix at ffffffff81ff25bd #9 [ffff88f532ccfdb8] iavf_reset_interrupt_capability at ffffffffc08eba53 [iavf] #10 [ffff88f532ccfdd0] iavf_reset_task at ffffffffc08ecb57 [iavf] #11 [ffff88f532ccfe20] process_one_work at ffffffff81cbe21f #12 [ffff88f532ccfe68] worker_thread at ffffffff81cbf336 #13 [ffff88f532ccfec8] kthread at ffffffff81cc61f1 #14 [ffff88f532ccff50] ret_from_fork_nospec_begin at ffffffff8238dd1d ~~~
resolution: Update to RHEL 8.4.z package `kernel-4.18.0-305.17.1.el8_4` ([Errata RHSA-2021:3447](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:3447)) or later. Update to RHEL 8.5 package `kernel-4.18.0-348.el8` ([Errata RHSA-2021:4356](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:4356)) or later. Update to the relevant RHOSP version when available. #### Workaround- RHEL 8.2 (RHOSP 16.1) and earlier **Including RHEL 7 (RHOSP 13, RHOSP 10)** Update to third-party drivers of the following versions or later: * `i40e` v2.17.4 * `iavf` v4.3.9 Those drivers might come from Intel's SourceForge or from the hardware vendor.
root_cause: This was investigated in RHEL 7 (OSP 13) under **Red Hat Private Bug 1838908- iavf/i40evf reset triggers kernel BUG at drivers/pci/msi.c:357**. This error was incredibly difficult to troubleshoot, and was not possible to reproduce in Red Hat or Intel labs. It involved a very long collaboration between the Red Hat driver maintainer, the Intel partner developer team, and affected customers. That work resulted in the following upstream patches in the `iavf` driver which repair this error: * [iavf: fix locking of critical sections](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/netdev/net-next.git/commit/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf?id=226d528512cfac890a1619aea4301f3dd314fe60) * [iavf: do not override the adapter state in the watchdog task](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/netdev/net-next.git/commit/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf?id=22c8fd71d3a5e6fe584ccc2c1e8760e5baefd5aa) Unfortunately, by the time the fix was found, the required changes to the driver were deemed too invasive to perform so late in the RHEL 7 lifecycle. It is not possible to both repair this issue and confidently maintain other existing stability of the `iavf` driver. It is also not possible to repair in RHOSP 13, which is built on top of RHEL 7. The above fixes were tracked for RHEL 8.5 with **Red Hat Private Bug 1975245- ice/iavf driver stop responding** and included in development package `kernel-4.18.0-332.el8` and later. This was also tracked for RHEL 8.4.z with **Red Hat Private Bug 1997534- ice/iavf driver stop responding [rhel-8.4.0.z]** and included in package `kernel-4.18.0-305.17.1.el8_4` and later. An `i40e` driver update is also necessary, which was performed in RHEL 8.4 during a regular `i40e` driver update on **Red Hat Private Bug 1838733** included in development package `kernel-4.18.0-290.el8` and later. Despite intensive work between Intel's driver team and Red Hat, it was not possible to quantify the precise `i40e` patches which repair this issue on the PF, so the earliest this issue can be repaired is RHEL 8.4. There is also separate RHEL 8 (OSP 16) z-stream tracking bug **Red Hat Private Bug 1908964- [i40e] iavf/i40evf reset triggers kernel BUG at drivers/pci/msi.c:357**. Further stability is offered by additional patches from Intel: * [iavf: Fix kernel BUG in free_msi_irqs](https://patchwork.ozlabs.org/project/intel-wired-lan/patch/20211022083014.4416-1-mateusz.palczewski@intel.com/) * [iavf: Add helper function to go from pci_dev to adapter](https://patchwork.ozlabs.org/project/intel-wired-lan/patch/20210915064123.69945-1-karen.sornek@intel.com/) * [iavf: Combine init and watchdog state machines](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/netdev/net-next.git/commit/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf?id=898ef1cb1cb24040c3e89263e02c605af70c776a) * [iavf: Add__IAVF_INIT_FAILED state](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/netdev/net-next.git/commit/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf?id=59756ad6948be91d66867ce458083b820c59b8ba) * [iavf: Refactor iavf state machine tracking](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/netdev/net-next.git/commit/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf?id=45eebd62999d37d13568723524b99d828e0ce22c) These are currently hoped to be included in RHEL 8.6.

title: Master node not getting provisioned baremetal IPI installation
issue: - Failed to boot Master node in BareMetal IPI.- Master node not getting provisioned baremetal IPI installation and installer exits with the below mentioned code. ~~~ level=error msg=Error: could not contact Ironic API: timeout reached level=error level=error msg= on../../tmp/openshift-install-204534070/masters/main.tf line 1, in resource "ironic_node_v1" "openshift-master-host": level=error msg= 1: resource "ironic_node_v1" "openshift-master-host" {~~~
resolution: There could be multiple reasons for this error. Below diagnostic steps were performed for successful installation: 1. Bootstrap was up and running successful but master nodes are not getting powered on initially. 2. On checking on the ILO, we saw that the network boot was not enabled on the boot order which was a listed prerequisite for provisioner network interfaces. This way, the bootstrap was be able to power on the machines and boot them in PXE to install rhcos on it. 3. There were three logs that were helpful in finding the solution, Ironic-inspector, Ironic-conductor and Ironic-api. 4. Bootmode was also not set in install-config file used for installation. Option "bootMode: legacy" needs to be set in install-config to boot the nodes in legacy mode.
root_cause: - Network boot was not enabled on ILO- Bootmode not set in install-config, can be set as described in [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/installing/installing_bare_metal_ipi/ipi-install-prerequisites.html#node-requirements_ipi-install-prerequisites)- To deploy an OpenShift Container Platform cluster with managed Secure Boot, you must set the bootMode value to UEFISecureBoot in the install-config.yaml file.- Download speed very slow due to image is not getting downloaded within time and connected timed out. As the installer download around 1Gb images, a slow internet connection could lead to timeout situation.

title: FAQ on the Private-link ROSA clusters
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - How will the access to the Private Link ROSA cluster work?
resolution: The following are the frequently asked questions.- What is the list of URL's need to be whitelisted for the private link ROSA cluster? ~~~ The documentation [1] highlights the URL's that are required to be whitelisted. ~~~ [1] [PrivateLink firewall prerequisites](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_getting_started/rosa-aws-prereqs.html#osd-aws-privatelink-firewall-prerequisites)- Is it necessary to allow port 80? Is it possible to open just port 443? ~~~ Yes, we need to open both ports 80 and 443. You can try to only enable 443, but this has not been tested and verified by Red Hat. ~~~- How are these SSH keys managed in terms of usage, rotation, storage, etc? ~~~ SSH is not used for PrivateLink control plane connectivity. All control plane communication is over HTTPS. ~~~- Is the IP allow-list controlled by the customer/tenant? Where is this set in the PrivateLink cluster? ~~~ The IP allow-list is managed by the SREP team and is only to gain access to our central configuration management server (Openshift Hive) for control plane access. For PrivateLink clusters, there is a private network between the Hive server and the target OSD/ROSA cluster. ~~~- If the BYOCAdminAccess role is removed to deny SRE access to AWS accounts, will it impact any SLA? Can it use more limited policies? ~~~- It is recommended not to remove BYOCAAdminAccess as this is the account used to request cloud provider access. Red Hat SRE does not access AWS accounts in the course of routine Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS operations. For emergency troubleshooting purposes, the SREs have well-defined and auditable procedures to access cloud infrastructure accounts. ~~~- When and how frequently Red Hat SRE team access the console? ~~~- The SRE doesn't access the customer console as there's no IDP for the SRE, instead, the SRE access the APIs via backplane permissions with the pod created. Connections to the SRE support pod are permitted only from a secured Red Hat network. ~~~

title: unable to sync storage configuration: exactly one storage type should be configured at the same time
issue: Image Registry Operator is reporting the following error: Unable to apply resources: unable to sync storage configuration: exactly one storage type should be configured at the same time, got 2: [EmptyDir PVC] or [Empty s3]
resolution: * The Image Registry Operator storage section of the configuration should have only one storage definition. So it should look like this: oc get configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io-o yaml.... storage: emptyDir: {} And not like this: storage: emptyDir: {} pvc: claim: image-registry-storage
root_cause: * The Image Registry Operator currently only supports one storage definition in the configuration.

title: How to query Elasticsearch from Kibana Dev Tools?
issue: - How to fetch `elasticsearch` data from `kibana` UI?- How to list `indices` and its metadata?- How to get a list of the keys and their mapping type?
resolution: - Login to the `Kibana` console.- Navigate to the `Dev Tools` menu.- Enter and execute queries on the console space.- Run the below query to view elasticsearch Health: ~~~ GET_cat/health?v ~~~- Run the below query to list indices: ~~~ GET_cat/indices?v ~~~- Run the below query to view indices creation date: ~~~ GET_cat/indices?h=i,creation.date,creation.date.string ~~~- Run the below query to view indices size: ~~~ GET_stats/indexing,store?pretty ~~~- Run the below query to get list of the keys and their mapping type: ~~~ GET /_mapping?pretty ~~~

title: Haproxy processes consuming high memory
issue: - Infra nodes report high memory utilization.- Alert: NodeMemoryUtilisationTooHigh- warning are seen/fired on infra nodes of ocp cluster.
resolution: - Add to the router deployment config an environment variable named RELOAD_INTERVAL and configure with an value between 10 and 15 seconds #oc env dc router RELOAD_INTERVAL=[larger then 5s]
root_cause: - By default the HAProxy reloads the configuration each 5 seconds, in order to update the routing table.- Long-lasting connections, such as WebSocket connections, combined with short HAProxy reload intervals, can cause instantiation of many HAProxy processes. These processes handle old connections, which were started before the HAProxy configuration reload.

title: Is there any option to declare a registry as insecure registry in install-config.yaml in OCP4 deployment?
issue: - Is it possible to specify a mirror as insecure in the `install-config.yaml` in OCP 4?
resolution: There isn't any dedicated option to declare any insecure registry during the installation. The list of options can be found [in the installer documentation](https://github.com/openshift/installer/blob/master/docs/user/customization.md). For disconnected installations, as per the [Mirroring images for a disconnected installation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/installing/installing-mirroring-installation-images.html) documentation, the `imageContentSources` section is generated in the output of the `oc adm release mirror` command. That section should be added to the `install-config.yaml`.
root_cause: There no options to declare an insecure registry in the `install-config.yaml` file.

issue:

tar: Removing leading `/' from hard link targets
tar: /etc/origin/master/ocp-audit.log: file changed as we read it", "stderr_lines": ["tar: Removing leading `/' from member names", "tar: Removing leading `/' from hard link targets", "tar: /etc/origin/master/ocp-audit.log: file changed as we read it"], "stdout": "/etc/origin/generated-configs/
/etc/origin/generated-configs/master-node02.example.com/
/etc/origin/generated-configs/master-node02.example.com/master.server.crt
/etc/origin/generated-configs/master-node02.example.com/master.server.key
/etc/origin/generated-configs/master-node02.example.com/openshift-master.crt
/etc/origin/generated-configs/master-node02.example.com/openshift-master.key
/etc/origin/generated-configs/master-node02.example.com/ca.crt
... ~~~
resolution: This is caused by a file in the target directory being updated in the middle of the playbook run. Most commonly this is an audit log or other log. In the case of an audit log, the suggestion is to temporarily or permanently move the audit log file location to another directory different than `var/origin/master`. 1. Update the `master-config.yaml` file on each master, changing: auditFilePath: "/var/log/origin/ocp-audit.log" 2. Update your inventory file, the variables: `openshift_master_audit_config` and `openshift_master_audit_policyfile` (if applicable) 3. Restart the master services one by one: $ master-restart api api $ master-restart controllers controllers 4. Re-run the playbook 5. Once the playbook is done and we confirm the certs are updated, you can either leave the new audit location or revert it back to the original

title: NooBaa's default backingstore 'noobaa-default-backing-store' is stuck in 'Creating' state in an OCS 4.X cluster
issue: NooBaa's default backingstore 'noobaa-default-backing-store' is stuck in 'Creating' state in an OCS 4.X cluster
resolution: * The following steps should be performed to fix the issue 1. Obtain the secret credentials from `noobaa-aws-cloud-creds-secret`: ~~~ # oc get noobaa-aws-cloud-creds-secret-o yaml-- Locate the aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key fields and decode them from base64 with the following commands # echo-n {aws_access_key_id} | base64-d # echo-n {aws_secret_access_key} | base64-d ~~~ 2. Preform an RPC call with the noobaa cli: ~~~ noobaa api account_api update_external_connection '{"identity": {your_decode_access_key}, "secret": {your_decode_secret_key}, "name": "noobaa-default-backing-store"}' ~~~ 3. Verify the command completed successfully and the backing store status returned to Ready.
root_cause: * An update to the `noobaa-aws-cloud-creds-secret` secret credentials can cause this issue. * The issue is being tracked in [BZ #1992090](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1992090)

title: OCP4 - Prometheus can't scrape metrics from openshift-network-diagnostics namespace.
issue: Prometheus logs return an error for `openshift-network-diagnostics` namespace: ~~~ level=warn ts=2021-11-04T08:05:44.022232114Z caller=operator.go:1697 component=prometheusoperator msg="skipping servicemonitor" error="it accesses file system via bearer token file which Prometheus specification prohibits" servicemonitor=openshift-network-diagnostics/network-check-source namespace=openshift-user-workload-monitoring prometheus=user-workload ~~~
resolution: It is fixed in `OCP 4.9` [in the following bug fix](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:3759). There are no backports so it is needed to upgrade to 4.9 and onwards or apply the workaround. Possible workaround is to add the following label to the `openshift-network-diagnostics` namespace: ~~~ metadata: labels: openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true" ~~~ And ensuring the current RBAC is not modified: ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-network-diagnostics rules:- apiGroups:- "" resources:- services- endpoints- pods verbs:- get- list- watch apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-network-diagnostics roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Role name: prometheus-k8s subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-monitoring ~~~
root_cause: As per the [bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1986061), the label and RBAC has been modified to have it created by scratch once the cluster is upgraded to 4.9.0 and onwards.

title: Elasticsearch node in CrashLoopBackOff state because of duplicate index/alias with backend ceph storage
issue: **elasticserach*
pod is going into **crashloopbackoff*
state because of duplicate index/alias
resolution: 1. Get the node name where the problematic elasticsearch pod is running. $ oc get pod-o wide 2. Connect to the node using below command $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host 3. Find out the mount point associated with **elsaticsearch** ceph PV. $ df-h | grep 4. Navigate to the path where the **elasticserach ceph PV** is mounted. $ cd 5. Navigate to the indices path inside that folder. $ cd elasticsearch/data/nodes/0/indices/ 6. Find the indices directory with UUID in the elasticsearch error log and move it to a diff directory. $ mv../../../../backup/ 7. Restart **elasticserach** with the below command. $ oc scale deployment/--replicas=0 $ oc scale deployment/--replicas=1 8. Verify if the elasticserach pod comes up successfully. $ oc get pods
root_cause: * Invalid metadata inside **elasticsearch** pod would make it think that the index is still present while it was deleted actually.

title: PVC error: dial tcp: lookup heketi-storage.gluster.svc on 10.x.x.x:53: no such host
issue: - When attempting to provision a Persistent Volume Claim in a namespace, you receive error messages like the following below ~~~ Failed to provision volume with StorageClass "glusterfs-storage": failed to create volume: failed to create volume: Post http://heketi-storage.gluster.svc:8080/volumes: dial tcp: lookup heketi-storage.gluster.svc on 10.x.x.x:53: no such host ~~~
resolution: - Ensure that all your master nodes are online and READY.- name service resolution for services occurs on the master nodes. A downed node (or if in the process of removing a master node) the node isn't fully removed from the cluster entirely, this service will still attempt to complete on the degraded master.- The best solution is to resolve any issues you have with your master nodes and ensure they are all available, or, if in the process of removing a master node, [complete the steps to remove the node](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/assembly_replace-master-host.html#deprecating-master-host_replace-master-host) so it will no longer be queried.
root_cause: - Service lookup occurs on the master host nodes.- If your master nodes are not fully READY, a downed node will be unable to complete the lookup and will fail to discover the service properly during PVC creation request.- You may see that this issue appears if any of your masters are not available or are down/rebooting for maintenance.

title: How to manage Add-ons using the command-line interface?
issue: - How to find `add-ons` using the command-line interface?- How to view `add-ons` using the command-line interface?- How to install `add-ons` using the command-line interface?- How to delete `add-ons` using the command-line interface?
resolution: `Add-ons` can be managed using the command-line interface. ### Finding an add-on service- To determine availability specific to your organization, run the following command: ~~~ # ocm get $(ocm whoami | jq-r.organization.href)/quota_summary--parameter search="resource_type='addon'" ~~~- This will return a list similar to the following: ~~~ {"kind": "QuotaSummaryList", "page": 1, "size": 1, "total": 1, "items": [{"kind": "QuotaSummary", "href": "/api/accounts_mgmt/v1/organizations/ /quota_summary", "organization_id": " ", "resource_name": "dbaOperatorAddon", "resource_type": "addon", "byoc": false, "availability_zone_type": "", "allowed": 15, "reserved": 0}]} ~~~- In this example, up to 15 resources of the `dbaOperatorAddOn` type are available ("allowed": 15).- Since no `add-ons` are currently installed the reserved amount is equal to 0. ### Viewing existing add-on service- To view a list of the existing `add-on` installations in your cluster: ~~~ # ocm get /api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/ /addons ~~~- You can find your_cluster ID_ in the URL bar in your web browser: "_https://cloud.redhat.com/openshift/details/CLUSTER-ID_"- To get the description of an `add-on`: ~~~ # ocm get /api/clusters_mgmt/v1/addons/ocs-converged | jq.description# "Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation Managed Service provides hyperconverged storage for applications within an OpenShift cluster." ~~~- To get the documentation link: ~~~ # ocm get /api/clusters_mgmt/v1/addons/ocs-converged | jq.docs_link "https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation_managed_service/1.1/html/getting_started_with_red_hat_openshift_data_foundation_managed_service/index" ~~~ ### Installing add-on service- To install an `add-on`, you can post the_add-on ID_ to the same endpoint: ~~~ # echo '{"addon": {"id": "dba-operator"}}' | ocm post /api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/ /addons ~~~- The_add-on ID_ can be found in the complete list of `add-ons` in the `OpenShift Cluster Manager database`. View this list by running: ~~~ # ocm get /api/clusters_mgmt/v1/addons ~~~- This will yield a list similar to the following: ~~~ {"kind": "AddOnList", "page": 1, "size": 1, "total": 1, "items": [{"kind": "AddOn", "href": "/api/clusters_mgmt/v1/addons/dba-operator", "id": "dba-operator", "name": "DBA Operator", "description": "Kubernetes Operator that orchestrates relational database schema migrations", "label": "api.openshift.com/addon-dba-operator", "icon: " ", "enabled": true, "resource_name": "dbaOperatorAddon", "resource_cost": 1}]} ~~~- In addition to the_add-on ID_, this list provides information on the resource cost of the `add-ons`. In this example, the `DBA Operator add-on` has a resource cost of 1.- Depending on the type of `add-on` the resource cost could be 0 if it requires no quota, or any other value between 0 and 1. ### Deleting add-on service- To delete the `add-on service` from your cluster through the `OCM CLI`, enter the following command: ~~~ # ocm delete api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/ /addons/ ~~~

title: Kube-apiserver CO degraded due to failed conditional check (ConfigObservationDegraded)
issue: - The kube-apiserver CO is degraded: ~~~ $ oc get co kube-apiserver NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE kube-apiserver 4.8.x True False True 30h =========================================================== Conditions: Last Transition Time: 2021-08-25T04:24:23Z Message: ConfigObservationDegraded: configmaps openshift-etcd/etcd-endpoints: no etcd endpoint addresses found Reason: ConfigObservation_Error Status: True Type: Degraded ~~~- The kube-apiserver-operator pod logs throws the following error, in spite of the fact that `etcd-endpoints` config map is well populated with the master node IPs. ~~~ E0830 04:06:28.282295 1 base_controller.go:266] ConfigObserver reconciliation failed: configmaps openshift-etcd/etcd-endpoints: no etcd endpoint addresses found ~~~
resolution: Ensure that the cluster nodes are not assigned with IPv6 addresses that start with the prefix `2001:db8:`. From the [source code](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-kube-apiserver-operator/blob/d6a60b2c18806d69dcf27228aacb830a699126f3/pkg/operator/configobservation/etcdendpoints/observe_etcd_endpoints.go#L72), it is evident that the `kube-apiserver-operator` does not consider IP addresses with the prefix `2001:db8:` and `192.0.2.`, as those IPs are meant to be used in documentation and example source code. **Current remediation is to deploy a new cluster with another network for the master IP addresses.** The error is still under investigation and is being worked on internally with the Engineering team via [BZ-2000521](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2000521). The efforts involve making the encountered error message more concise. Along with that, the etcd engineering team is also working on the [BZ-2004081](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2004081) that addresses not using the above-mentioned range as they are series of [IANA reserved IP ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserved_IP_addresses). The usage of such IP addresses will result in the failure of the etcd-operator, cluster installation.

title: OCP4: CVE-2021-44228 affecting Elasticsearch (Red Hat OpenShift Logging)
issue: - Red Hat OpenShift Logging mitigation for [CVE-2021-44228](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-44228) in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4
resolution: The vulnerability is already fixed in the following OpenShift Logging releases:- Openshift Logging 5.0.10 as part of [errata RHSA-2021:5137](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:5137).- Openshift Logging 5.1.5 as part of [errata RHSA-2021:5128](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:5128).- Openshift Logging 5.2.4 as part of [errata RHSA-2021:5127](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:5127).- Openshift Logging 5.3.1 as part of [errata RHSA-2021:5129](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:5129). #### Workaround There is a workaround if upgrading is not yet possible. > **Important:** If you follow the optional step 8, then please ensure that you revert the Openshift Logging and/or the Elasticsearch operator `managementState` back to `managed` state to upgrade to a version including the fix. > **Note:** This workaround takes ElasticSearch for Openshift Logging stack as an example, but the workaround can be applied the same way on Elasticsearch deployed using the official Red Hat ElasticSearch Operator. 1. Change to project where Logging stack deployed (by default `openshift-logging` project): ~~~ $ oc project openshift-logging ~~~ 2. Find the Elasticsearch `replicasets` deployed for passing later to `oc set env` command: ~~~ $ oc get rs-l component=elasticsearch NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AGE elasticsearch-cdm-ba9c6evk-1-796f6cfdbc 1 1 1 16d elasticsearch-cdm-ba9c6evk-2-7959d4d857 1 1 1 16d elasticsearch-cdm-ba9c6evk-3-5f9c5d668c 1 1 1 17d ~~~ 3. Set environment variable `ES_JAVA_OPTS` in the Elasticsearch container for system property `log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups` to `true`: ~~~ $ oc set env-c elasticsearch replicaset/ ES_JAVA_OPTS="-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true" ~~~ 3.1. You can confirm this by: ~~~ $ oc set env-c elasticsearch rs-l component=elasticsearch--list | grep ES_JAVA_OPTS ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true ~~~ 4. Scale down the Elasticsearch `ReplicaSet` so new ES pod is spawned afterwards: ~~~ $ oc scale replicaset/--replicas=0 ~~~ 5. Check new ES pod has been spawned automatically after scaling down `ReplicaSet` to `0` (there is no need to scale up as that would be done automatically): ~~~ $ oc get pods-l component=elasticsearch NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE elasticsearch-cdm-ba9c6evk-1-796f6cfdbc-4dqc6 2/2 Running 0 27m elasticsearch-cdm-ba9c6evk-2-7959d4d857-z5km9 2/2 Running 0 2d9h elasticsearch-cdm-ba9c6evk-3-5f9c5d668c-cr8lj 2/2 Running 0 2d9h $ oc set env-c elasticsearch pods-l component=elasticsearch--list | grep ES_JAVA_OPTS ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true ~~~ 6. `oc exec` into the newly-spawned ES pod to check Java command-line arguments passed correctly including `-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true`: ~~~ $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- grep-a log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups /proc/1/cmdline ~~~ `-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true` should be visible in above output. 7. Repeat steps 3 to 6 for each Elasticsearch `ReplicaSet` one at a time slowly to allow ES pods respawn while maintaining ES cluster quorum: 8. (Optional) To avoid the OpenShift Logging operator and Elasticsearch operator to rewrite changes while the fix is still being worked on, you can set it to `unmanaged`: ~~~ $ oc edit clusterlogging/instance [...] spec: [...] managementState: Unmanaged [...] $ oc edit elasticsearch/elasticsearch [...] spec: [...] managementState: Unmanaged [...] ~~~ And confirm it by checking: ~~~ $ oc get clusterlogging NAME MANAGEMENT STATE instance Unmanaged $ oc get elasticsearch NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT elasticsearch Unmanaged green 3 3 all ~~~ * (Optional) After the changes above the procedure can be done at the deployment level instead of `ReplicaSets` as explained in steps 2 to 5: ~~~ $ oc patch deployment/--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"paused": false}}' $ oc set env deployment/-c elasticsearch ES_JAVA_OPTS="-Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true" ~~~ This will create new `ReplicaSets` automatically and pods with the environment defined. After that steps 5 to 7 can be executed. This method does not need to be done if following steps 2 to 5.
root_cause: [CVE-2021-44228](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-44228) [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2030932)

title: Logged in users are seeing cluster-roles without any privilege
issue: When a user logged into OCP cluster (For any type of identity provider LDAP, HTPasswd) able to see cluster roles even though they don't have any role assigned.
resolution: For users to interact with the OpenShift Container Platform, they must first authenticate to the cluster. The authentication layer identifies the user associated with requests to the OpenShift Container Platform API. The authorization layer then uses information about the requesting user to determine if the request is allowed. As an administrator, you can configure authentication for the OpenShift Container Platform. Any user with proper credentials in Red Hat Openshift Container Platform with successful authentication, by default part of system:authenticated group. Other groups are system:authenticated:oauth, they are automatically associated with all users authenticated with an OAuth access token, and system:unauthenticated they are automatically associated with all unauthenticated users. Following documentation can be referred for more understanding [Users and Groups for 3.xx] (https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/architecture/additional_concepts/authentication.html) [Understanding authentication for 4.xx] (https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/authentication/understanding-authentication.html)
root_cause: Any user with proper credentials in Red Hat Openshift Container Platform with successful authentication, by default part of system:authenticated group. When a user is a part of "system:authenticated" group, by default all role/clusterrole bindings belongs to "system:authenticated" group will be allocated to the user as well

title: Is it possible to modify `/etc/resolv.conf` at pod level?
issue: - How to change the search domain resolution order in `/etc/resolv.conf`?- Is it possible to modify the contents of `/etc/resolv.conf`?- How can we resolve the desired domain first instead of sequentially appending the search domain from the `/etc/resolv.conf` file of pod?
resolution: - No. It is not possible to change the search domain resolution order of the `/etc/resolv.conf` file at the pod level.- If any changes are done, we may lose the internal cluster DNS resolution. **Hence, modifying it for a particular scenario is not recommended.**- However, if we want to resolve the desired domain instead of sequentially appending the search domain from the `/etc/resolv.conf` file of pod, we can append `.` at the end of the *hostname*. `eg: access.redhat.com.` ~~~ sh-4.2$ dig redhat.com. +showsearch; < <> > DiG 9.11.4-P2-RedHat-9.11.4-26.P2.el7_9.8 < <> > redhat.com. +showsearch;; global options: +cmd;; Got answer:;;-> > HEADER < <- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 45274;; flags: qr aa rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 4, ADDITIONAL: 5;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 512;; QUESTION SECTION:;redhat.com. IN A;; ANSWER SECTION: redhat.com. 292 IN A 10.4.204.55 <--------------------------------------------------- [Absolute Hostname];; AUTHORITY SECTION: redhat.com. 292 IN NS ns01.intranet.prod.int.phx2.redhat.com. redhat.com. 292 IN NS ns02.intranet.prod.int.phx2.redhat.com. redhat.com. 292 IN NS ns02.intranet.prod.int.rdu2.redhat.com. redhat.com. 292 IN NS ns01.intranet.prod.int.rdu2.redhat.com.;; ADDITIONAL SECTION: ns01.intranet.prod.int.phx2.redhat.com. 292 IN A 10.5.30.45 ns02.intranet.prod.int.phx2.redhat.com. 292 IN A 10.5.30.46 ns01.intranet.prod.int.rdu2.redhat.com. 292 IN A 10.11.5.3 ns02.intranet.prod.int.rdu2.redhat.com. 292 IN A 10.11.5.4;; Query time: 0 msec;; SERVER: 172.30.0.10#53(172.30.0.10);; WHEN: Thu Dec 30 07:59:46 UTC 2021;; MSG SIZE rcvd: 241 ~~~
root_cause: - In every application pod, `/etc/resolv.conf` file is present which includes the following contents: ~~~ search ns1.svc.cluster-domain.example my.dns.search.suffix nameserver 1.2.3.4 options ndots:5 ~~~ where,- `search` holds the entry of domain names that are appended sequentially at end of the incomplete `Hostname`.- `nameserver` holds the `svc` IP address of the `openshift-dns` project.- `ndots` is to identify the dots present in the `Hostname` to check if it is FQDN or not.- If the `Hostname` has less `.` than the `ndots` mentioned in the `/etc/resolv.conf`, then the search domain is appended to make it FQDN and further send out for resolution. If the first, search domain returns `NXDomain`, then the next search domain from `search` is appended and again send out for resolution. ~~~ sh-4.2$ dig redhat.com +showsearch; < <> > DiG 9.11.4-P2-RedHat-9.11.4-26.P2.el7_9.8 < <> > redhat.com +showsearch;; global options: +cmd;; Got answer:;; WARNING:.local is reserved for Multicast DNS;; You are currently testing what happens when an mDNS query is leaked to DNS;;-> > HEADER < <- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 25874;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 512;; QUESTION SECTION:;redhat.com.kuard.svc.cluster.local. title: Image registry pulls incorrect digest when mirroring enabled
issue: - The internal openshift image registry is proxying to an incorrect digest for all openshift image streams when mirroring is enabled.- In a cluster with image mirroring configured, when a pod is created with image as `image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift/cli:latest` (example), the pod fails due to ImagePullBackOff. ~~~ 25m Normal Pulling pod/ldap-group-sync Pulling image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift/cli" 25m Warning Failed pod/ldap-group-sync Failed to pull image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift/cli": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error parsing image configuration: Error fetching blob: invalid status code from registry 500 (Internal Server Error) 25m Warning Failed pod/ldap-group-sync Error: ErrImagePull 22m Normal BackOff pod/ldap-group-sync Back-off pulling image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift/cli" 25m Warning Failed pod/ldap-group-sync Error: ImagePullBackOff ~~~ ~~~ 2021-09-24T10:55:41.872730246Z time="2021-09-24T10:55:41.872606439Z" level=error msg="response completed with error" err.code=unknown err.detail="Get \"https://mirror-registry/mirror/blobs/sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f\": unauthorized: Not Authorized." err.message="unknown error" go.version=go1.16.6 http.request.host="image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000" http.request.id=c5e9175e-2b9c-4559-8c6e-0755e3306210 http.request.method=GET http.request.remoteaddr="10.x.x.x:1000" http.request.uri="/v2/openshift/cli/blobs/sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f" http.request.useragent="cri-o/1.21.2-15.rhaos4.8.gitcdc4f56.el8 go/go1.16.6 os/linux arch/amd64" http.response.contenttype="application/json; charset=utf-8" http.response.duration=889.386496ms http.response.status=500 http.response.written=275 openshift.auth.user="system:serviceaccount:ldap-sync:ldap-group-syncer" vars.digest="sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f" vars.name=openshift/cli 2021-09-24T10:55:41.872781776Z time="2021-09-24T10:55:41.872738525Z" level=info msg=response go.version=go1.16.6 http.request.host="image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000" http.request.id=d5db8919-e7d9-40cd-bf29-5dbad08b0e6e http.request.method=GET http.request.remoteaddr="240.0.2.1:38736" http.request.uri="/v2/openshift/cli/blobs/sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f" http.request.useragent="cri-o/1.21.2-15.rhaos4.8.gitcdc4f56.el8 go/go1.16.6 os/linux arch/amd64" http.response.contenttype="application/json; charset=utf-8" http.response.duration=889.558678ms http.response.status=500 http.response.written=275 2021-09-24T10:55:42.002776272Z time="2021-09-24T10:55:42.002690679Z" level=error msg="Background mirroring failed: error committing to storage: Get \"https://mirror-registry/mirror/blobs/sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f\": unauthorized: Not Authorized." go.version=go1.16.6 http.request.host="image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000" http.request.id=c5e9175e-2b9c-4559-8c6e-0755e3306210 http.request.method=GET http.request.remoteaddr="10.x.x.x:1000" http.request.uri="/v2/openshift/cli/blobs/sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f" http.request.useragent="cri-o/1.21.2-15.rhaos4.8.gitcdc4f56.el8 go/go1.16.6 os/linux arch/amd64" openshift.auth.user="system:serviceaccount:ldap-sync:ldap-group-syncer" vars.digest="sha256:84c9f2afcca866cd0246d0df94f38ec3512bfe83fa5fa772204cc636490c1e5f" vars.name=openshift/cli ~~~
resolution: - The issue has been identified as a bug and is being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under [BZ #2009788](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2009788)
root_cause: - The client gets an error when it tried to pull the blob sha256:84c9...5f. This is not an image digest, it's a blob digest (images consist of blobs). It gets an error because the image registry fails to proxy it from the mirror registry: ~~~ level=error msg="response completed with error" err.code=unknown err.detail="Get \"https:// /blobs/sha256:84c9 5f\": unauthorized: Not Authorized." err.message="unknown error" ~~~- This is because the registry's implementation of ICSP in 4.8 does not support authorization. The problem should be fixed in 4.9.- The fix has also been backported to 4.8.18.

title: OpenShift health check not working with HTTPS scheme or mutual auth
issue: - Unable to successfully configure `livenessProbe` over HTTPS port. The setup uses mutual authentication. The documentation is not clear on how to configure this setup.- Sample `livenessProbe` snippet used in the deployment: ~~~~ livenessProbe: httpGet: path: /healthz port: 8443 scheme: HTTPS initialDelaySeconds: 120 timeoutSeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 10 successThreshold: 1 failureThreshold: 3 ~~~~- Fails with the following message: ~~~~ Liveness probe failed: Get https://10.x.x.103:8082/healthz: EOF ~~~~- After this, pods go into a `CrashLoopBackOff` state.
resolution: - Instead of using the HTTP check, use a [custom command.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/dev_guide/application_health.html#container-health-checks-using-probes)- See Container Execution Checks section. Inside the health check script, include a curl command that points to a valid mutual auth certificate: ~~~~ # curl-k--cert /path/to/cert.pem:my-password https://localhost:8443/healthz ~~~~

title: The data is not in the destination PVs after migrating with MTC in OCP
issue: The cluster applications were migrated but the data is not there.
The MTC replicates the `PVs` but they are empty.
After using the `MTC`, the migrated applications do not have any previous data.
The migration process ends **successfully*
in a few minutes, not taking enough time to copy all the information.
resolution: Use the `File system copy method` and `Direct volume migration` for the migration process. Please refer to the docs below to get further information about the mentioned options: * [File system copy method](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.9/html-single/migrating_from_version_3_to_4#file-system-copy-method_about-mtc-3-4) * [Direct volume migration](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.9/html-single/migrating_from_version_3_to_4#direct-volume-migration-and-direct-image-migration_about-mtc-3-4) If the environment is still impacted by this issue using `File system copy method` and `Direct volume migration`, please open a support case at https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true
root_cause: The `Snapshot copy method` is only supported when using either `AWS`, `GCP`, or `Azure` as backend storage. Also, the same storageclass must be used when opting for the `Snapshot copy method`, it is not possible when using OCS, because there's a change from `Gluster` to `Ceph` in the product, making changes on the storageclass in use. The limitations of the `Snapshot copy method` can be checked in further detail in [our documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.9/html-single/migrating_from_version_3_to_4#snapshot-copy-method_about-mtc-3-4).

title: Audit logs of the debug node without chroot /host in Openshift 4.x
issue: - For auditing purpose, would like to know where the audit logs of the debug node without running chroot /host get stored.- In general, would like to audit which users do what in debug node without running chroot /host
resolution: - At the time of this writing, there is no mechanism currently that will log audit events at this level.- On the other hand, the system-level audit will turn on only after executing chroot /host on the debug pod.- OpenShift's built-in audit mechanism is created such that it only allows logging events at the apiserver layer.- Currently, we don't have any mechanism available yet which will audit commands executed in a container without chroot /host.- This can be only achieved if all containers base image has some kind of auditing mechanism enabled which would send that data to a central logging system, but that's out of scope for now.- Bugzilla: [1943768](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1943768)
root_cause: - There is no mechanism currently that will log audit events at this level.

title: OpenShift Builds Fail with “The unauthenticated git protocol on port 9418 is no longer supported”
issue: OpenShift Builds fail to clone source code from GitHub when the source URI starts with the `git://` protocol (`git://github.com/…`). This may also occur with other source code repositories that are powered by git and do not support this protocol.
resolution: - Use the HTTPS protocol to clone source code, with a URI that starts with `https://` (`https://github.com/…`). Private repositories may require a basic authentication [source clone secret](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/cicd/builds/creating-build-inputs.html#builds-source-secret-basic-auth_creating-build-inputs).- Use the SSH protocol to clone source code. This can be done with a URI that starts with `ssh://` (`ssh://git@github.com/…`), or with the SCP-style URI syntax (`git@github.com:...`). Cloning with SSH may require an SSH key to be provided as a [source clone secret](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/cicd/builds/creating-build-inputs.html#builds-source-secret-ssh-key-auth_creating-build-inputs).
root_cause: **Disclaimer:** *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* On September 1, 2021, GitHub [announced](https://github.blog/2021-09-01-improving-git-protocol-security-github/) that they are removing support for the unauthenticated git protocol. title: Does ROSA support configuring log forwarding to Loki?
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - In the `ROSA` environment, Is it possible/recommended to step up log forwarding to `Loki`.- Is there any official documentation that mentions the integration of `Loki` with `ROSA` clusters.
resolution: - OpenShift Log forwarding to `Loki` can be enabled in the OpenShift Container Platform as mentioned in the [official documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/logging/cluster-logging-external.html#cluster-logging-collector-log-forward-loki_cluster-logging-external)- The above can be configured for the ROSA environment as well. This implies the above configurations issue will not be handled by the `Managed services` facility that Red Hat provides.- For any specific use-case to integrate Loki with the ROSA environment, Contact [Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport/) for all technical questions or issues and raise a `separate ticket` with the OCP team for the issue occurrence.- The above integration is not mentioned in the official [ROSA documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/logging/rosa-install-logging.html) as this configuration is not recommended and hence does not qualify to receive support from the [Red Hat Managed Service](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/openshift/what-are-red-hat-openshift-managed-services) **Note**: The only log forwarding supported by `Red Hat Managed service` is `AWS CloudWatch`.

title: How can developers publish, configure and deploy their API-Product in an automated way.
issue: - I found the following 3 solutions in the documentation on how developer can publish API and I have a few question to help identify which solution best fits our use case- [Toolbox CLI](https://github.com/3scale/3scale_toolbox)- Allows the developer to import APIs by OAS/Swagger, create application-plans, configure the settings and deploy the proxy-config. ##and can be used with the image quay.io/redhat/3scale-toolbox.- [Service Discovery from Openshift to 3scale](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html-single/admin_portal_guide/index#service_discovery_from_openshift_to_3scale) When Service Discovery is configured, 3scale scans for_discoverable API services that are running in the same OpenShift cluster_ and automatically imports the associated API definitions into 3scale Developers add annotations to their service objects (discovery.3scale.net/*) which are then scanned and used to import the API into 3scale.-_Does the service discovery also works in a multi Openshift cluster environment, where the 3scale is not deployed in the same cluster as the API Services?_- [3scale Operator Application Capabilities](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.8/html/operating_3scale/provision-threescale-services-via-operator)- Feature is currently in Technology Preview. When is it available with production support? What are the prerequisites to use it?- Does it work in a multi cluster environment? Are there other features available?
resolution: There only features currently available to enable developers publishm configure and deploy their API products are as follows: ####Toolbox The supported method to install toolbox is described in our documentation: [4.1. Installing the toolbox](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/the-threescale-toolbox#installing-the-toolbox ""). ####Service Discovery from Openshift to 3scale Service discovery ony helps to import an API which will be configured in 3scale as API Backend and Product, as well as a 3scale Active Doc. It doesn't provide the same features as toolbox i.e. it doesn't have the additional features such as creating application plans, applications, copy services, etc. It does not work in a multi cluster OpenShift cluster environment i.e. where the 3scale is not deployed in the same cluster as the API Services This explained in the documentation [here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html-single/admin_portal_guide/index#service-discovery-concept_service-discovery ""):_When Service Discovery is configured, 3scale scans for discoverable API services that are **running in the same** OpenShift cluster and automatically imports the associated API definitions into 3scale._ Also note when using the Service Discovery feature in 3scale there are only 2 fields to fill, name & namespace. ####3scale Operator Application Capabilities As at the time of this writing, 3Scale v 2.11, there is no release update yet on when the Operator capabilities will be fully supported, they are still being worked on. Also check out the [updated documentation for 3scale 2.11 and general prerequisites](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/provision-threescale-services-via-operator "").. Please follow this JiRA [THREESCALE-3486](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-3486 "") and related issues linked to see the status of the 3scale Operator Application Capabilities. The capabilities make HTTP requests to the 3scale API, it should work from other clusters. However there are some limitations, i.e. when a proxy is used: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-7761

title: oc import-image command fails with  "Import failed (NotFound)" error
issue: The import of an image using the `oc import-image` command fails with error `Import failed (NotFound)` although the image exists and can be pulled: ~~~ error: tag xxxxxxx failed: dockerimage.image.openshift.io "192.168.1.1:443/mytest/hello- world:xxxxxxx" not found imagestream.image.openshift.io/hello-world imported with errors ~~~ ~~~! error: Import failed (NotFound): dockerimage.image.openshift.io "192.168.1.1:443/mytest/hello-world:latest" not found ~~~
Trying to import an OCI image with `oc import-image` command fails with `Import failed (NotFound)`.
resolution: The support for OCI images was included in OCP 4.7 as per the release notes: [Open Container Initiative images support](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/release_notes/ocp-4-7-release-notes.html#ocp-4-7-registry-oci-support). Please, check that the cluster version and the `oc` binary version is 4.7 or newer using the `oc version` command. If the `oc` binary version and also the cluster version is 4.7 or newer, follow the steps in the Diagnostic Steps section to check that the image exists in the registry. There are other similar issues that are related to configuration: * `Import failed (Unauthorized)`: refer to [Allowing pods to reference images from other secured registries](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/openshift_images/managing_images/using-image-pull-secrets.html#images-allow-pods-to-reference-images-from-secure-registries_using-image-pull-secrets) to create and use pull secrets. * `Import failed (InternalError):... x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`: refer to [Image configuration resources](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/openshift_images/image-configuration.html) to configure additional trust bundles. ####Workaround for OCP 4.6 If you are using `buildah` to build and push the image, make sure the image is built with the `docker` format: ~~~ $ buildah bud--format=docker-t 192.168.1.1:443/mytest/hello-world:latest. $ buildah push 192.168.1.1:443/mytest/hello-world:latest ~~~
root_cause: Buildah uses the OCI format as the default format for building and publishing images (see [buildah documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/building_running_and_managing_containers/building-container-images-with-buildah_building-running-and-managing-containers) to learn more about buildah). For OCP 4.6 and older, the `openshift-apiserver` that handles the `oc import-image` command in the backend requires the image to be pushed in the `docker` format and can not handle the OCI image format.

title: Network plugin is not ready: CNI config uninitialized
issue: network not ready: NetworkReady=false reason:NetworkPluginNotReady message:docker: network plugin is not ready: cni config uninitialized
resolution: Check nmcli conn show CONNECTION and ensure that ipv4 dns servers are set. If they are not set you will need to set them. Example: Add new nameservers: "Check nmcli conn show CONNECTION and ensure that IPv4 DNS servers are set. If they are not set, they will need to be set. To do so, follow these four steps: Example: 1. Run `nmcli` command to add new `nameservers`: ~~~ # nmcli con mod eth0 ipv4.dns "8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4" ~~~ 2. Append nameservers: ~~~ # nmcli con mod my-con-em1 +ipv4.dns "8.8.8.8" ~~~ 3. To apply changes after a modified connection using `nmcli`, activate again the connection by entering the following command: ~~~ # nmcli con up con-name ~~~ 4. Finally, the `/etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-origin-dns.sh` script runs in a `NetworkManager` shell where the variable is set based on what is set in `NetworkManager` for the connections, so to run it independently will not work. To trigger the script manually, restart the `NetworkManager` service: ~~~ # systemctl restart NetworkManager ~~~
root_cause: There is no /etc/origin/node/resolv.conf file. This file should be created by a NetworkManager dispatcher script on the host: F0408 20:14:55.772387 8335 start_node.go:176] could not start DNS, unable to read config file: open /etc/origin/node/resolv.conf: no such file or directory This file should be created by a NetworkManager dispatcher script on the host: /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-origin-dns.sh

title: How to use dynamic parameter with `Jenkinsfile` pipeline

title: [RHOCP 4.x] How to allow routes to claim different paths of the same hostname across namespaces?
issue: - How to allow **routes*
to claim different paths of the same hostname across namespaces?
resolution: - **routeAdmission** defines a policy for handling new route claims, such as allowing or denying claims across namespaces.- Add the below parameters in the Ingress controller instance: ~~~ $oc edit Ingresscontroller default-n openshift-ingress-operator spec: replicas: 2 routeAdmission: namespaceOwnership: InterNamespaceAllowed ~~~- **namespaceOwnership** describes how hostname claims across namespaces should be handled. The default is Strict.- **InterNamespaceAllowed** allows routes to claim different paths of the same hostname across namespaces.- Create a **route** in one of the projects as mentioned below: ~~~ $ oc expose svc httpd--name=test1--hostname=test.com-n test [quicklab@upi-0 ~]$ oc get route-n test NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD test1 test.com httpd 8080-tcp None ~~~- Create another **route** with the same hostname as mentioned above with a different path in another namespace: ~~~ $ oc expose svc httpd--name=test1--hostname=test.com--path=/v2-n test-1 ~~~- Check **route** status: ~~~ [quicklab@upi-0 ~]$ oc get route-n test-1 NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD test1 test.com /v2 httpd 8080-tcp None ~~~
root_cause: - The default value for **spec.routeAdmission. namespaceOwnership** is **Strict**.- **Strict** does not allow routes to claim the same hostname across namespaces.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] How to gather connectivity status between Pods & Services using must-gather?
issue: - How to gather connectivity status between **Pods*
& **Services*
running in different namespaces using **must-gather**?
resolution: - For the **OVN** cluster use the below command to connectivity status between pods running in different namespaces: ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **ovn_pod_to_pod_connectivity**: This script checks pod2pod connectivity on an OVN cluster. By default, this script spins up two pods (a client and a server) in the openshift-network-tools-* namespace.- Also optionally supply the script with a pair of source and destination names. These can either be the source and destination node names on which the debug pods should be scheduled or they can be existing pod names (format:) to run the connectivity test. ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **ovn_pod_to_svc_connectivity**: This script checks pod2svc connectivity on an OVN cluster. By default, this script spins up a pod (a client) and a service (a backing-server pod and a clusterIP:port svc) in the openshift-network-tools-* namespace.- Also optionally supply the script with a pair of source and destination names. These can either be the source and destination node names on which the debug pods should be scheduled or they can be existing pod (format:) and service names (format:) to run the connectivity test. ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_svc_connectivity ` $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_svc_connectivity ` ~~~- For the **openshiftSDN** cluster use the below command to connectivity status between pods in different namespace: ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- sdn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **sdn_pod_to_pod_connectivity**: This script checks pod2pod connectivity on a SDN cluster. By default, this script spins up two pods (a client and a server) in the openshift-network-tools-* namespace.- Also optionally supply the script with a pair of source and destination names. These can either be the source and destination node names on which the debug pods should be scheduled or they can be existing pod names (format:) to run the connectivity test. ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- sdn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **sdn_pod_to_svc_connectivity**: This script checks pod2svc connectivity on a SDN cluster. By default, this script spins up a pod (a client) and a service (a backing-server pod and a clusterIP:port svc) in the openshift-network-tools-* namespace.- Also optionally supply the script with a pair of source and destination names. These can either be the source and destination node names on which the debug pods should be scheduled or they can be existing pod (format:) and service names (format:) to run the connectivity test. ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- sdn_pod_to_svc_connectivity ` $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- sdn_pod_to_svc_connectivity ` ~~~

Returning attributes are [userPassword]. Binary attributes are []. 06:55:11,546 DEBUG [org.wildfly.security] (default task-4) Found entry [CN=test.user,OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com]. 06:55:11,552 DEBUG [org.wildfly.security] (default task-4) Context [javax.naming.ldap.InitialLdapContext@40154c99] was closed. resolution: - Create additional IngressController as follows. ~~~ $ oc create-f- < 80/TCP,443/TCP,1936/TCP 168m router-nodeport-data-ingress-controller NodePort 172.30.x.x 10.0.x.x 80:31589/TCP,443:30361/TCP 168m ~~~- Testing a connectivity to a test httpd web server ~~~ $ curl-vs http://httpd.apps.test.example.com:31589/ * Trying 10.0.x.x:31589... * Connected to httpd.apps.test.example.com (10.0.x.x) port 31589 (#0) > GET / HTTP/1.1 > Host: httpd.apps.test.example.com:31589 > User-Agent: curl/7.71.1 > Accept: */* > * Mark bundle as not supporting multiuse < HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden < Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2021 09:05:40 GMT < Server: Apache/2.4.37 (Red Hat Enterprise Linux) OpenSSL/1.1.1g < Last-Modified: Thu, 12 Nov 2020 16:02:45 GMT < ETag: "1181-5b3eb0ae4b340" < Accept-Ranges: bytes < Content-Length: 4481 < Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 < Set-Cookie: be9900b185ba26c07f97a77443ad0113=4db1afac395b0462bca66445e879534f; path=/; HttpOnly < Test Page for the HTTP Server on Red Hat Enterprise Linux <--- Httpd Test page is provided, 403 status is expected on this test page(403 is no problem). ~~~- In this way when a request goes through an external ip/port and behind the scene, the request is redirected to the HAProxy instance listening on a node port.

title: Minor version update recommendations for Red Hat Openshift 3.11
issue: Correct bugs and fix in update process of minor version in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform can be optimized following a check list
resolution: 1. Update `yum` repositories in all nodes: ~~~ rhel-7-server-rpms rhel-7-server-extras-rpms rhel-7-server-ose-3.11-rpms rhel-7-server-ansible-2.9-rpms ~~~ 2. Make VM snapshot of master nodes. 3. Authenticate with `ssh` to bastion node and identify installation inventory file. Edit inventory file, put the correct version value to the properties below: ~~~ openshift_pkg_version=-3.11.xx openshift_image_tag=v3.11.xx ~~~ 4. Execute authentication in master nodes with `system:admin` user. If there is external procedure to authenticate like `crontab`, disable it. ~~~ # Authentication command from bastion node $ ansible-i masters-m shell-a "oc login-u system:admin" # Check if authentication were successful $ ansible-i masters-m shell-a "oc whoami" ~~~ 5. Upgrade master nodes. 6. Upgrade `openshift-ansible` packages for administration console and API Server: ~~~ $ subscription-manager refresh $ yum update openshift-ansible-y $ ansible-i masters-m shell-a "subscription-manager refresh; $ yum update openshift-ansible-y" ~~~ 7. Upgrade packages for administration console and API Server: ~~~ $ cd /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible $ ansible-playbook-i playbooks/byo/openshift-cluster/upgrades/v3_11/upgrade_control_plane.yml ~~~ **IMPORTANT:** Reboot master nodes one at time, wait for READY state on node rebooted before proceeding to the next master node. ~~~ # Check node state, if you have the oc client on bastion node, just login to Openshift on command line and execute: $ oc get nodes ~~~ *OBS:* If master node fail to start, execute rollback of snapshots made before starting step 5, and try again. 8. Update worker nodes. 9. Edit inventory file, commenting all nodes not to be upgraded. By doing this, it is possible to chose nodes for update to avoid indisponibility. ~~~ $ ansible-i nodes-m shell-a "subscription-manager refresh; yum update openshift-ansible-y" ~~~ 10. Upgrade control plane ~~~ cd /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible $ ansible-playbook-i playbooks/byo/openshift-cluster/upgrades/v3_11/upgrade_control_plane.yml ~~~ 11. Validate Upgrade: 11.1 Deploy application 11.2 Test service pods 11.3 Test App routes 11.4 Check Grafana dashboard 11.5 Check Kibana data 11.6 Check Prometheus data 11.7 Check metrics 11.8 Check applications
root_cause: Monitoring tools can find vulnerabilities in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform after health check routine execution. These vulnerabilities might have been already fixed in a group of patches. That why is important to keep the cluster updated.

title: Why does my NetworkPolicy not work for the default project on Openshift 3?
issue: - Correctly created `NetworkPolicy` does not allow traffic from the `project`/`namespace` default as requested.- Workload is not reachable by `Routes`.
resolution: Set an unique `netid` for your `NetNamespace`: ~~~ $ oc patch netnamespace proxy-test-p '{"netid":42}' ~~~
root_cause: The `router` pods are located by default in the `project` default and the `NetNamespace` default has the `netid 0`. Assigning the `netid 0` to another `NetNamespace` will cause that the `NetworkPolicy` will not be applied correctly. Creating a `NetNamespace` without an `netid` will result a `NetNamespace` with `netid 0`.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] Unable to convert Ingress object to OCP Route.

object to OCP **Route**.- The **Ingress*

object is defined similarly to the following: ~~~ apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Ingress name: web-test spec: ingressClassName: contour rules:- host: foo.bar.com http: paths:- backend: serviceName: web-svc servicePort: 80 path: / ~~~- After creating the Ingress object the Route is not created.

title: Local Volume Storage Operator resize in OpenShift 4
issue: - The `Local Storage Operator` does not allow dynamic resizing of the volumes it creates.
resolution: **Note:** This resolution has a few caveats that are worthy to mention:- There is a possibility to lose data if the `Retain` policy in the `storageClass` isn't configured, make sure to backup the data as necessary.- The `PersistenVolume` object would still be showing the old size, but this won't affect functionality or constraint the storage size for the `pod`.- There is an open [[RFE] Enable volume resizing for local storage PVs](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1915732) working on this issue. #### Patch the PV to `Retain` policy ~~~ # oc patch pv/--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy": "Retain"}}' ~~~ #### Steps to resize 1. Expand the vmdk disk in VMware. 2. Spawn a debug `pod` in the target node: ~~~ # oc debug-t node/ ~~~ 3. Change the root directory to the `/host` directory: ~~~ # chroot /host ~~~ 4. Check the disks: ~~~ # lsblk ~~~ 5. Select the disk the just expanded in VMware and rescan it: ~~~ # echo 1 > /sys/class/block/$disk/device/rescan ~~~ 6. Check again the disks and notice the change in size: ~~~ # lsblk ~~~ 7. Now check your filesystem type: ~~~ # df-hT /dev/$DISK /dev/nvme0n1p2 ext4 976M 189M 721M 21% /boot <---[1] ~~~ [1]:Second column value 8. Depending on the filesystem type in the disk follow different expand methods. ### 8.1. xfs filesystem- Find the path where the disk is mounted: ~~~ # lsblk | grep $DISK NAME MAJ:MIN RM SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINT sr0 11:0 1 492K 0 rom vda 253:0 0 40G 0 disk └─vda1 253:1 0 40G 0 part / <--- # xfs_growfs /dev/${disk from previous command} ~~~ ### 8.2. ext4 filesystem- Unmount the disk from the system: ~~~ # umount /dev/$DISK ~~~- Expand using `resize2fs`: ~~~ # resize2fs /dev/$DISK ~~~ As a final step, check after finishing that the block has the desired size: ~~~ # df-hT /dev/$DISK ~~~
root_cause: The Local Volume Storage Operator doesn't support dynamic resizing of the volumes.

title: Install openshift-serverless operator without console.

resolution: To install the OpenShift-serverless operator in the same namespace as the webconsole- run the commands below after logging into your cluster with `oc login`- create namespace (NOTE: `oc new-project` will not allow namespaces starting with 'openshift-') ~~~ cat < < EOF | oc apply-f- apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-serverless labels: openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true" EOF ~~~- create operatorgroup ~~~ cat < < EOF | oc apply-f- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: openshift-serverless-operatorgroup namespace: openshift-serverless EOF ~~~- create subscription ~~~ cat < < EOF | oc apply-f- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: serverless-operator namespace: openshift-serverless spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Automatic name: serverless-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace EOF ~~~

title: How to restart Elasticsearch index management cronjobs?
issue: - How to manually restart the `index management` `cronjobs` of `elasticsearch`?
resolution: - `Index management` `cronjobs` run periodically to roll over the index and delete old data.- If the job runs successfully then the pod status will show "Completed" and if it fails, the status would be "Error".- Normally, if a job fails, it will automatically try and run another one. In case this does not happen and there are huge indices leading to disk pressure, they can be manually restarted.- Here are the steps to manually restart `Elasticsearch` `Index management` `cronjobs`: 1. Collect the current status of the cronjob: ~~~ $ oc get cronjob-L indexManagement-n openshift-logging ~~~ 2. Delete the cronjob one by one. The operator will recreate the job. ~~~ $ oc delete cronjob elasticsearch-im-app $ oc delete cronjob elasticsearch-im-audit $ oc delete cronjob elasticsearch-im-infra ~~~ 3. After 15- 20mins. Run the following command to see the completed pods: ~~~ $ oc get cronjob-L indexManagement-n openshift-logging ~~~

title: Are the OCP containers based on RHEL 8.4 are vulnerable to CVE-2019-18218, CVE-2021-35942, CVE-2021-27645, cve-2021-33574, CVE-2021-20232, CVE-2021-20231, cve-2021-3580 ?
issue: - The packages ` nettle`, `file-libs`, `glibc`, `gnutls` which can be found in Openshift containers based on RHEL 8.4 seems to have vulnerability.
resolution: - The observation regarding fixed RHEL packages in version 8.5 are correct. That what you described can be also tracked in the Container Health Index (CHI) on the Container Catalog page. For example, when you take a look at the openshift4/ose-etcd or openshift4/ose-openshift-apiserver-rhel8 (mentioned in your message) images on the Container Catalog and check the Security tab, you will see a list of CVEs what will be fixed when the particular fixed packages will be consumed from the original repositories (like RHEL). See: https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/openshift4/ose-etcd/5cdb4d425a13467289f5538d?container-tabs=security https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/openshift4/ose-openshift-apiserver-rhel8/5f748d2231efe7552d0d1d6a?container-tabs=security As you can see in the CHI, all CVEs are LOW or MODERATE impact vulnerabilities. That's why the main CHI for all OCP 4.9 images is still A. To get more details about CHI please see: https://access.redhat.com/articles/2803031?extIdCarryOver=true&sc_cid=701f2000001Css5AAC The fixed RHEL packages will be consumed in the next OCP releases. That, how fast fixes are delivered in the products depends on many factors (vulnerability severity, product lifecycle, and so on). To read more about how fixes are delivered to products please read An Open Approach To Vulnerability Management document available at https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/red-hats-open-approach-vulnerability-management (especially section Mitigating Vulnerabilities). In short, it's not known yet when the fixed RHEL packages (related to these LOW/MODERATE impact CVEs) will be delivered to OpenShift Container Platform. Those OCP images which are built based on the newest UBI8.5 image have already fixed versions of RHEL packages, see for example: https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/openshift-logging/elasticsearch-rhel8-operator/5fd118c5af03b18dd4ff3fc1?container-tabs=security Those OCP images where these CVEs are not addressed yet will consume fixed RHEL packages in the next releases (it could be next y-stream release).
root_cause: - A Qualys scan report showed below erratas: ~~~ https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:4374 https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:4358 https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:4451 ~~~- The associated CVEs: ~~~ https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2019-18218 https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2021-35942 https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2021-27645 https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-33574 https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2021-20232 https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2021-20231 https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-3580 ~~~
