title: Upgrading from 4.9 to 4.10 with RHEL 7 workers
issue: - What support state is my cluster in if I update from 4.9 to 4.10 with RHEL 7 workers, and haven't yet replaced them with RHEL 8 workers?
resolution: You deployment is supported, but it should be noted that your upgrade to 4.11 will be blocked by the Kube-apiserver operator being placed into and `Upgradeable=False` condition. This is caused whenever there are Kubelets younger than the denoted sku delta (versioning) that is supported.
root_cause: Upgrading with RHEL workers, starts with a [cluster upgrade](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/updating/updating-cluster-rhel-compute.html#rhel-compute-updating-min[…]ting-cluster-rhel-compute). Post the completion of this step, the worker nodes remain as they were prior to the upgrade (running 4.Y-1.Z openshift components). Due to the supported version sku in [kuberneties](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/)/[openshift](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/architecture/control-plane.html#control-plane-and-node-host-compatibility), running in this configuration is supported.

title: shopt -s xpg_echo is not propagated anymore in subshell
issue: - When switching the bash option `xpg_echo` with `shopt`, a new script does not inherit of the setting.- For example: ~~~ $ cat a.sh: shopt-s xpg_echo echo "\t 1st test"./b.sh $ cat b.sh echo "\t 2nd test" ~~~- The output is: ~~~ 1st test \t 2nd test ~~~ => in second script, *\t
is not interpreted as tabulation.- In RHEL 7, the *echo
of *\t
from second script is interpreted (if we add `shopt-p xpg_echo`, we ca see the value of the option): ~~~ 1st test shopt-s xpg_echo 2nd test ~~~
resolution: - You can see in `Root Cause` section that in RHEL8, the bash option are reset when a subshell is launched.- Thus, you have to reset the option to the required value in second script or not execute a second shell, but *source* it: ~~~ $ cat a.sh: shopt-s xpg_echo echo "\t 1st test"../b.sh ~~~ => thus the script will be executed in same shell, and options will not be reset.
root_cause: - If we look at the code, for *RHEL 7* and *8*, when a subshell is executed, we are going through: ~~~ initialize_subshell ()... /* Reset the values of the shell flags and options. */ reset_shell_flags (); reset_shell_options (); > > > > > reset_shopt_options (); < < < < < ~~~- `reset_shopt_options` is defined in `shopt.def`:- RHEL7, bash 4.2: ~~~ /* Reset the options managed by `shopt' to the values they would have at shell startup. */ void reset_shopt_options () {allow_null_glob_expansion = glob_dot_filenames = 0; cdable_vars = mail_warning = 0; no_exit_on_failed_exec = print_shift_error = 0; check_hashed_filenames = cdspelling = expand_aliases = check_window_size = 0; source_uses_path = promptvars = 1; #if defined (EXTENDED_GLOB) extended_glob = 0; #endif #if defined (HISTORY) literal_history = force_append_history = 0; command_oriented_history = 1; #endif #if defined (READLINE) hist_verify = history_reediting = 0; perform_hostname_completion = 1; #endif shopt_login_shell = login_shell;} ~~~ => `xpg_echo` is untouched.- in RHEL 8, bash 4.4: ~~~ /* Reset the options managed by `shopt' to the values they would have at shell startup. Variables from shopt_vars. */ void reset_shopt_options () {autocd = cdable_vars = cdspelling = 0; check_hashed_filenames = CHECKHASH_DEFAULT; check_window_size = CHECKWINSIZE_DEFAULT; allow_null_glob_expansion = glob_dot_filenames = 0; no_exit_on_failed_exec = 0; expand_aliases = 0; extended_quote = 1; fail_glob_expansion = 0; glob_asciirange = GLOBASCII_DEFAULT; glob_star = 0; gnu_error_format = 0; hup_on_exit = 0; inherit_errexit = 0; interactive_comments = 1; lastpipe_opt = 0; mail_warning = 0; glob_ignore_case = match_ignore_case = 0; print_shift_error = 0; source_uses_path = promptvars = 1; #if defined (JOB_CONTROL) check_jobs_at_exit = 0; #endif #if defined (EXTENDED_GLOB) extended_glob = EXTGLOB_DEFAULT; #endif #if defined (HISTORY) literal_history = 0; force_append_history = 0; command_oriented_history = 1; #endif #if defined (READLINE) complete_fullquote = 1; force_fignore = 1; hist_verify = history_reediting = 0; perform_hostname_completion = 1; if DIRCOMPLETE_EXPAND_DEFAULT dircomplete_expand = 1; else dircomplete_expand = 0; #endif dircomplete_spelling = 0; no_empty_command_completion = 0; #endif #if defined (PROGRAMMABLE_COMPLETION) prog_completion_enabled = 1; #endif #if defined (DEFAULT_ECHO_TO_XPG) || defined (STRICT_POSIX) xpg_echo = 1; #else xpg_echo = 0; #endif /* DEFAULT_ECHO_TO_XPG */ shopt_login_shell = login_shell;} ~~~ => in RHEL8, `xpg_echo` is reset.- It' the same for other options, for example *direxpand*.- To see it, you can add `shopt-p xpg_echo` in scripts.

title: Not all alerts have namespace label included in Openshift 4
issue: - Alert sent via webhook do not provide `namespace` label.- How can be forced to include a namespace label in the body of an alert?- Default alerts in Openshift are not following the same style.
resolution: **Disclaimer:** *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Red Hat is working against a [style guide](https://github.com/openshift/enhancements/blob/master/enhancements/monitoring/alerting-consistency.md#style-guide) for Openshift alerts to have a compliant style in all the components. Following the bugs for each component tracking the process:- [Bug 2010354](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010354) (Kube Scheduler).- [Bug 2010663](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010663) (OVN).- [Bug 2010365](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010365) (Cluster Version Operator).- [Bug 2010352](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010352) (Kube Controller Manager).- [Bug 2010358](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010358) (Cluster Autoscaler).- [Bug 2010359](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010359) (Cloud Controller Manager).- [Bug 2010347](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010347) (Image Registry).- [Bug 2010364](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010364) (Samples).- [Bug 2010376](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010376) (Routing).- [Bug 2012065](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2012065) (Etcd).- [Bug 2010375](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010375) (OLM).- [Bug 2010341](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010341) (Cloud Credential Operator).- [Bug 2010361](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010361) (SDN).- [Bug 2010345](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2010345) (DNS).- [LOG-1823](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-1823) (Cluster Logging Operator). #### Workaround A possible workaround is to duplicate the wanted `PrometheusRule` to add the missing information and silence the original `PrometheusRule`.
root_cause: Not all Openshift components follow the same style guide while creating `alert rules`. title: How to enable header capture on OpenShift 3 routers
issue: - Configuring log format on `HAProxy` is not sending headers.- How to configure `HAProxy` to capture headers.- Headers are not visible in the `rsyslog` logs.
resolution: This solution is valid only for `OCP 3.11`, the solution for `OCP 4` is [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6283571) and [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5634771) [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4629361). Edit the template following the documentation [Using a ConfigMap to Replace the Router Configuration Template](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/router/customized_haproxy_router.html#using-configmap-replace-template), specifying the header name that should be captured. Using the following syntax: ~~~ capture request header len ~~~ And then, following the steps [Viewing Logs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/router.html#viewing-logs). ### Step by step example 1. Take a copy of the template from one of the `router` pods: $ oc exec-n default cat haproxy-config.template > haproxy-config.template 2. Edit the template to add the `capture` instruction, like the following: $ cat haproxy-config.template [...] frontend public capture request header Host len 20 capture request header test len 20 [...] 3. Create the configmap with the new template: $ oc create configmap customrouter--from-file=haproxy-config.template-n default 4. Modify the `router` `DeploymentConfig` to mount the configmap: $ oc set volume dc/router--add--overwrite--name=config-volume--mount-path=/var/lib/haproxy/conf/custom--source='{"configMap": {"name": "customrouter"}}'-n default 5. Set the `TEMPLATE_FILE` environment variable in the `router` `DeploymentConfig` to use the new template: $ oc set env dc/router TEMPLATE_FILE=/var/lib/haproxy/conf/custom/haproxy-config.template-n default 6. Set `ROUTER_SYSLOG_FORMAT` and `ROUTER_SYSLOG_ADDRESS` variables: $ oc set env dc/router ROUTER_SYSLOG_ADDRESS=10.131.2.38:6514 ROUTER_LOG_LEVEL=debug ROUTER_SYSLOG_FORMAT="%[capture.req.hdr(0)]:%ci:%cp[%tr]:headers:\ {%hrl}\ {%hsl}"-n default **Note:** `%hrl` and `%hsl` are the "captured request headers" and "captured response headers" variables for `HAProxy`. [How to change log format](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3250781).
root_cause: HTTP headers are not captured by default.

title: TLS handshake error in OpenShift API logs
issue: - Lot of TLS errors can be observed in logs of API server (but also in ETCD and other components communicating with API). ~~~ 2020/02/14 19:43:32 http: TLS handshake error from:: EOF ~~~
resolution: **Generic**- Note that this could be INFO level log although the message says error. In the "Ixxxx" part- Letter *I* means INFO. If it's a harmless INFO log, it can be ignored.- Letter *W* means WARNING.- Letter *E* means ERROR.- It can be ignored on VMWare platform.- Whenever the NSX-T load balancer does a health check to the API server it does on port 8443 and we see this TLS Handshake error.- This is expected behavior.- Enterprise PKS creates a monitor that checks on port 8443.- This monitor rejects NCP’s certificate.- This is related to the way Enterprise configures the api-server. *Kube-apiserver* is listening on *localhost:8080* and *:8443*.- It cannot use the tcp/http health monitor to query *localhost:8080/healthz* since this is not accessible externally.- Kubernetes is expecting connections to port 8443 to be use TLS.- Although a TLS connection is not established, a TCP connection is established successfully, allowing the TCP health monitor to function.- There is no functional impact related to the failed TLS connections. **Network related**- It may be related to DNS issues or load balancer.- It's likely a TCP health check by the frontend load balancer.- Double-check if the from IP matches load balancer IP.- Configure the load balancer to use a TLS connection for health check instead of the plain TCP connection, so this non-TLS connection error will no longer appear.- Load balancer documentation should be consulted for more details. **Certificate related**- If certificates were updated on 3.11, redeploy them as in [3.11 install metrics cert](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6083841)- Provider specific: could be due to too many Certificate Authorities (CAs) being included in configurtion/secret, see [TLS errors with mod_auth_mellon provider](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4618811)- Certificate related issues: see [x509: certificate signed by unknown authority](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3693251) **Additional links** [ServiceUnavailable](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5480661) [openshift-authentication shows TLS handshake error with bad certificate or unknown certificate](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5635881) [TLS handshake fails due to large packets discarded for Openshift 4 on Azure](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5252831) [client related TLS issues](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5635881) [API errors](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3266571)

title: Why ingress traffic for openshift deployed in Azure clould is highly imbalanced?
issue: Ingress traffic for the cluster deployed in Azure cloud (IPI) isn't balancing ingress traffic properly between the router pods. One router is always serving more request than others.
resolution: * With the release of **openshift 4.10.3**, OVN support `local` endpoint with `ExternalTrafficPolicy`. Without this patch, the traffic is highly imbalanced by OVN and as a result of that, even though the traffic is well balanced by top level load balancer, it doesn't results in balancing at ingress level. * With **openshift 4.9**, release of [z-stream bug 2060542](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2060542) will change the `ExternalTrafficPolicy` to cluster if it detect the deployment is over the cloud. * **Workaround,** If required, user can modify ingress svc and point the ETP to `cluster`. As the operator yet doesn't monitor this resource, it won't override the settings.
root_cause: * [OVN before 4.10](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1903408) doesn't support ETP (ExternalTrafficPolicy) to local. * As a workaround user can modify ingress service and point ETP to cluster. With cluster the traffic will be balanced between router pods. * **NOTE:-** as ETP cluster add additional hope by geneve the traffic to other host, it might degrade the performance as compare to local.

title: [RHACS / StackRox] : Amazon ECR Private Repository integration with RHACS Central UI
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - How to integrate `Amazon ECR` private repository with `RHACS Central UI`?- `Amazon ECR integration` with `RHACS central UI` is failing error: `images, view d| caused by: invalid character ' <' looking for beginning of value: invalid arguments: invalid arguments`.
resolution: Here are the steps to integrate the `Amazon ECR` private repository with `RHACS Central UI`.- **Step 1**: Create a private repository with `Amazon ECR` at the AWS console. The name of the repository would be in a format like this: `.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com/ /:TAG` ~~~ For example XXXXXXXXXXXXX.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prometheus/node-exporter:latest (URI for repository) ~~~- **Step 2**: Then login to the `Amazon ECR` private registry and push the images into `.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com/ /:TAG` as follows: ~~~ # aws ecr get-login-password--region | podman login--username AWS--password-stdin.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com # docker push.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com/ /:TAG //Image should be tagged before push. ~~~- **Step 3**: Run the following command to get the registry-ID: ~~~ # aws ecr describe-repositories--region ~~~- **Step 4**: Now go to the `Central UI > > Platform Configuration > > Integrations > > Amazon ECR > > New Integration` and here fill the following details: ~~~ Integration name: Registry ID: Endpoint: `api.ecr..amazonaws.com` Region: # Here `Use container IAM role` must be unchecked so that `ACCESS KEY ID` and `SECRET ACCESS KEY` can be entered for IAM users. # Fill in the `ACCESS KEY ID` and `SECRET ACCESS KEY` for IAM users and then run the test and save the details. ~~~- **Step 5**. Now after the above integration run the following commands to scan the images with: ~~~ # roxctl image scan--image.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com/ /:TAG--token-file--insecure-skip-tls-verify-e $ROX_CENTRAL_ENDPOINT # roxctl image check--image.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com/ /:TAG--token-file--insecure-skip-tls-verify-e $ROX_CENTRAL_ENDPOINT ~~~- **Note**: In the above command token file is important as access credentials for the `roxctl` CLI. This file can be passed in the above command as option `--token-file `. The token is generated in `RHACS Central UI`. At `Central UI` fill the details `Token Name` and choose the `Role: Admin`, then save the token into a file or export the variable $ROX_API_TOKEN. Follow the steps to generate the token at `Central UI`: ~~~ `Central UI > > Platform Configuration > > Integrations > > Authentication Tokens > > API Token > > Generate Token > Fill Details > Click on Generate` ~~~
root_cause: - Using wrong `Endpoint:.dkr.ecr..amazonaws.com` during `Amazon ECR` integration. It should be `api.ecr..amazonaws.com`.

title: How to configure Openshift Distributed Tracing Platform Agent as Daemonset in a non Multitenant Installation?
issue: - How do I configure Openshift Distributed Tracing Platform Agent as `DaemonSet` in a non Multitenant Installation?
resolution: 1. When the ODTP Agent is running as `DaemonSet`, the Pods need to access host ports, but that is not possible in OpenShift by default, so there is a need to create a new Security Context Constraint (SCC) that will allow the Pods to bind in an host port, as follows: ~~~ kind: SecurityContextConstraints apiVersion: security.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: daemonset-with-hostport annotations: kubernetes.io/description: 'Allows DaemonSets to bind to a well-known host port' runAsUser: type: RunAsAny seLinuxContext: type: RunAsAny allowHostPorts: true ~~~ 2. Create a new Service Account inside the namespace where the Jaeger will be used: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: odtp-agent-daemonset namespace: ~~~ 3. Apply the SCC to the `Service Account` created in the previous step: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user daemonset-with-hostport-z odtp-agent-daemonset-n ~~~ 4. Create, or modify an existent, Jaeger in the Openshift Distributed Platform Operator inside the namespace used before, as follows: ~~~ apiVersion: jaegertracing.io/v1 kind: Jaeger metadata: name: namespace:... spec:... agent:... serviceAccount: odtp-agent-daemonset strategy: DaemonSet... ~~~ 5. Validate if the pods were created correctly: ~~~ $ oc get daemonset-n NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE NODE SELECTOR AGE jaeger-all-in-one-inmemory-agent-daemonset 3 3 3 3 3 5d23h $ oc get pods-n-o wide NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE READINESS GATES jaeger-all-in-one-inmemory-agent-daemonset-7f8br 1/1 Running 0 5d22h 10.131.0.50 ip-10-0-217-105.sa-east- 1.compute.internal jaeger-all-in-one-inmemory-agent-daemonset-fvtvw 1/1 Running 0 5d22h 10.129.3.236 ip-10-0-145-96.sa-east-1.compute.internal jaeger-all-in-one-inmemory-agent-daemonset-zmr6p 1/1 Running 0 5d22h 10.128.2.101 ip-10-0-160-65.sa-east-1.compute.internal jaeger-all-in-one-inmemory-ff546454d-r477p 2/2 Running 0 5d23h 10.128.2.99 ip-10-0-160-65.sa-east-1.compute.internal ~~~ By default, the Pods will execute only in the worker nodes.

title: How to disable default Satellite repositories in ubi8-minimal image in a disconnected environment?
issue: - When trying to build an image based upon the ubi8/ubi-minimal image in a disconnected environment, we have our own satellite server. title: Can users with the default "self-provisioner" cluster role create projects from Red Hat GitOps Operator?
resolution: - At the time when this is being written, this is not possible. There are some workarounds like creating the project via the command line and then synchronize it by following the steps below: 1. Create the project by executing the command `oc new-project`. 2. Copy the `Project` and `rolebindings.authorization.openshift.io` objects created to the Git repository. 3. [Start synchronizing from Red Hat GitOps Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/cicd/gitops/configuring-an-openshift-cluster-by-deploying-an-application-with-cluster-configurations.html#synchronizing-your-application-application-with-your-git-repository_configuring-an-openshift-cluster-by-deploying-an-application-with-cluster-configurations).- The following request for enhancement suggests a way to solve this by binding `admin` roles in `Projects` to users who have created them:- [RFE-2522: Allow users with limited privileges to create OpenShift projects directly from GitOps Operator](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-2522).- To take advantage of this in case it is implemented, cluster administrators would need to give users `create project` permission. The default `self-provisioner` role does not grant it.
root_cause: - Find a detailed explanation on the own description of [RFE-2522](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-2522).- Find details about `self-provisioner` cluster role, `ProjectRequest` objects and their relation with `Projects` on this link: [Differences between "Project" and "ProjectRequest" objects on OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6616071).

title: Fuse 7 : MongoDB driver 4.x to connect to MongoDB 4.4 and 5.x
issue: - MongoDB is supported in Fuse through the Camel component camel-mongo that uses MongoDB Java driver that are limited to version 3.12. To connect to newer versions of MongoDB, starting from 4.4 to MongoDB 5.x, a 4.x java driver is required. Please integrate these new versions of MongoDB java driver in the future releases of Fuse.
resolution: - Fuse 7.x will not upgrade to Camel 3, as this would be an incompatible upgrade in a minor release that breaks existing applications. There are no plans for a Fuse 8 release. However as you already know we already offer support for Camel 3 with Camel Extensions for Quarkus and Camel K (OpenShift only). We also plan to offer support for Camel 3 on Spring Boot 2 later this year (around summer time frame) but we will not call it Fuse 8, rather something like "Camel on Spring Boot" or similar. There are some more details in KCS https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6342381. Our engineering department already reviewed the feature request raised in ENTESB-18707. An upgrade of the MongoDB driver inside the camel-mongodb component of Fuse 7 won't be possible, the mongo client has significantly changed in version 4. The only possible option would to introduce a new camel-mondodb4 component in Fuse 7, but even that may not be easily possible. You mentioned that you cannot move to Camel Quarkus for this project. I would like to check if your project could wait for the release of Camel 3 on Spring Boot later this summer? Fuse 7.11 is currently planned for June of this year. The release of Camel 3 on Spring Boot may follow somewhat close thereafter. Exact dates however are still undefined. Camel 3 on Spring Boot will support camel-mongodb and will use a MongoDB driver of version 4.x.

title: Operator mirroring for disconnected install in OpenShift 4 ignores the operator index image
issue: - After mirroring a selection of four operators for a disconnected install they consume a lot of disk space. The operators were mirrored using the following commands to a local mirror registry: ~~~ opm index prune \-f registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 \-p kubernetes-nmstate-operator,local-storage-operator,elasticsearch-operator,cluster-logging \-t local-registry:8443/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 oc adm catalog mirror-a./pullsecret.json--insecure \ local-registry:8443/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 \ local-registry:8443 \--index-filter-by-os='linux/amd64' info: Mirroring completed in 2h28m41.06s (4.634MB/s) ~~~ After the mirroring was complete, the mirror was using over 70GiB of disk space.
resolution: It is very important to follow all the steps from the [official Red Hat Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.8/html-single/operators/index#olm-restricted-networks): ~~~ # export LOCAL_REGISTRY=local-registry.example.com:5000 # podman login $LOCAL_REGISTRY Login Succeeded! # podman login registry.redhat.io Login Succeeded! # opm index prune \-f registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 \-p kubernetes-nmstate-operator,local-storage-operator,elasticsearch-operator,cluster-logging \-t $LOCAL_REGISTRY/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 INFO[0000] pruning the index packages="[kubernetes-nmstate-operator local-storage-operator elasticsearch-operator cluster-logging]" INFO[0000] Pulling previous image registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 to get metadata packages="[kubernetes-nmstate-operator local-storage-operator elasticsearch-operator cluster-logging]" [...] INFO[0223] Generating dockerfile packages="[kubernetes-nmstate-operator local-storage-operator elasticsearch-operator cluster-logging]" INFO[0223] writing dockerfile: index.Dockerfile800645084 packages="[kubernetes-nmstate-operator local-storage-operator elasticsearch-operator cluster-logging]" INFO[0223] running podman build packages="[kubernetes-nmstate-operator local-storage-operator elasticsearch-operator cluster-logging]" INFO[0223] [podman build--format docker-f index.Dockerfile800645084-t $LOCAL_REGISTRY/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8.] packages="[kubernetes-nmstate-operator local-storage-operator elasticsearch-operator cluster-logging]" ~~~ Please, note that the previous command **creates the operator index image in the local system, not in the local registry**. In order for the index to be available it must be pushed to the local registry: ~~~ # podman push $LOCAL_REGISTRY/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 # oc adm catalog mirror \-a $LOCAL_SECRET_JSON \ $LOCAL_REGISTRY/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.8 $LOCAL_REGISTRY/olm-mirror \--index-filter-by-os='linux/amd64' [...] stats: shared=28 unique=285 size=7.441GiB ratio=0.86 [...] ~~~ Without the pruned index image, the complete catalog would be mirrored. With the pruned index image, in this case with only 4 operators, the space used was around 7,4GiB.
root_cause: The step `podman push...` was being skipped, and because of this, the wrong index image was being used to mirror.

title: Does Red Hat support the use of Fuse/AMQ on Docker, or provide Docker images?
resolution: Red Hat will support Fuse and A-MQ in Docker containers that the customer has provided with a working, properly provisioned operating system and a supported JVM. Red Hat does not (yet) provide pre-assembled Docker images, except as provided for OpenShift; any that you might find on the Docker Hub or elsewhere, even if created by Red Hat engineers, are not maintained by Red Hat Support. The scope of support is that we will try to investigate problems in, and advise on the usage and configuration of, Fuse and A-MQ when they are run on Docker, to a commercially reasonable extent, as we do for other virtualization platforms. We cannot guarantee that all features will work in all Docker installations-- there are simply too many factors over which we have no control. In general, though, we will not be able to give detailed instructions for "containerizing" Fuse or AMQ. Moreover, the Fuse/A-MQ support team won't be able to fix problems in A-MQ that arise specifically from peculiarities in Docker, most commonly its networking system. We assume that a customer who wants to use Docker has sufficient expertise with this platform to be able to handle problems of this sort. Nor will we be able to advise on Docker configuration itself; to get support specific to Docker you would need to have an OpenShift support contract. In practice, many Red Hat engineers do use Fuse and A-MQ on Docker, and find few problems. However, we typically aren't running production loads, or production security configurations; so we can't be certain that our experience will extend to a production installation. Naturally, we recommend that customers who want to use Fuse/A-MQ in a Docker environment use OpenShift, for which Red Hat provides fully supported images.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] How to configure ingress controller to use `NodePortService` endpoint publishing strategy?
issue: - Is it possible to configure the ingress controller to use the `NodePortService` endpoint publishing strategy for the bare metal installation?
resolution: To configure the default ingress controller to use the `NodePortService` endpoint publishing strategy follow the below steps:- Delete the default ingress controller and then recreate it using the following YAML ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: IngressController metadata: name: default namespace: openshift-ingress-operator spec: endpointPublishingStrategy: type: NodePortService logging: {} replicas: 2 ~~~- After this step, the ingress controller will be recreated and a random node port is assigned to it that can be viewed using the below command: ~~~ $ oc describe svc/router-nodeport-default-n openshift-ingress. ~~~ Note that the web console access will be broken since the port was changed.- Edit the service and set the chosen service port to avoid external load balancer reconfiguration each time the cluster is reinstalled. This port must be higher than 30000. ~~~ $ oc edit svc/router-nodeport-default-n openshift-ingress ~~~- Reconfigure the external load balancer to match the port set to the service.- Monitor the cluster for some time and wait for the cluster to stabilize.- To read more about `NodePortService` endpoint publishing strategy, kindly refer to the following [OpenShift documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/networking/ingress-operator.html#nw-ingress-controller-endpoint-publishing-strategies_configuring-ingress) For any issues or any technical questions kindly contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport).

title: [RHOCP 4.x] The option "--dry-run=server" makes permanent changes to secrets and configmaps
issue: - Using the option `--dry-run=server` makes permanent changes to configmaps and secrets in the OpenShift cluster- When using `--dry-run=server` as an argument, the changes were made persistently and the config map data gets modified as below. Similar behaviour is observed when used with secrets. ~~~ $ oc set data cm/cm-testing--from-literal=name=def--dry-run=server configmap/cm-testing data updated (server dry run) $ oc get cm cm-testing-oyaml apiVersion: v1 data: name: def > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The data changes persistently kind: ConfigMap metadata: creationTimestamp: "2021-12-16T02:55:19Z" name: cm-testing namespace: testnamespace resourceVersion: "4975721" uid: 0f0a1052-059d-49f2-95e8-e8fad775161b ~~~

The issue has been identified as a bug in various versions of OpenShift and is being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under separate Bugzilla's as mentioned below.- For OCP v4.9, this issue is tracked under [BZ #2038930](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2038930)- For OCP v4.8, this issue is tracked under [BZ #2038931](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2038931)- For OCP v4.7, this issue is tracked under [BZ #2035393](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2035393)- At present, the fix is released for the OpenShift v4.9.18 and v4.8.31. title: Is gp3 storage type is not available for ebs csi driver and k8/ebs drivers?
issue: - Is gp3 storage type is not available for ebs csi driver and k8/ebs drivers?- What are the steps for adding gp3 storage type in the cluster?- How to update the gp2 type to gp3 without affecting any of the existing PVs?
resolution: - This is a known [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=2049872) which would be fixed in the OCP v4.11. **Workaround:**- It is recommended to include all privileges from: https://github.com/openshift/cluster-storage-operator/pull/263/files ~~~ RELEASE_IMAGE=quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.10.4-x86_64 mkdir-p credrequests oc adm release extract \--credentials-requests--cloud=aws \--to=credrequests/ $RELEASE_IMAGE ~~~- It can be extracted and patched, the credrequest for subsequent processing with ccoctl to generate the role dfn. $ patch credrequests/0000_50_cluster-storage-operator_03_credentials_request_aws.yaml ~~~ AWS_ACCOUNT="123" OIDC_ARN="arn:aws:iam::${AWS_ACCOUNT}:oidc-provider/fff" OIDC_NAME=ocp-oidc PERM_BOUNDARY="arn:aws:iam::${AWS_ACCOUNT}:policy/optional" ccoctl aws create-iam-roles \--name=$OIDC_NAME \--region=us-west-2 \--credentials-requests-dir=credrequests \--identity-provider-arn="$OIDC_ARN" \--permissions-boundary-arn "$PERM_BOUNDARY" \--output-dir cco \--dry-run ~~~- It would be better to look at cco.
root_cause: - The OCP / the CSI driver does not have permission to use the referenced KMS key. In that case, AWS cloud API CreateDisk call returns a valid volume ID, and only after that does it realize that it does not have access to the encryption key and silently deletes the volume.

title: What is the cluster name in case of setup load balancer for port 1936 in RHOCP 4.x ?
issue: - Is ocp4 a cluster-name in frontend stats of HA Proxy configuration for port 1936?
resolution: - HA Proxy configuration for port 1936 ~~~ frontend stats bind *:1936 mode http log global maxconn 10 stats enable stats hide-version stats refresh 30s stats show-node stats show-desc Stats for ocp4 cluster (1) stats auth admin:ocp4 (2) stats uri /stats ~~~- (1) In this example, the cluster name is ocp4: "stats show-desc Stats for ocp4 cluster"- After you login, you will be able to see this line on console "Stats for ocp4 cluster". You can edit this to anything, and you will be able to see that edited line on console.- (2) Here we are mentioning username and password to check HA Proxy Statistics Report: "stats auth admin:ocp4"- You can mention any username/passowrd here: "stats auth: "- We set up this HAProxy frontend for OCP cluster to check HA Proxy Statistics Report.- This is not a mandatory change, this is optional.- If you do not want to set/check frontend stats, you can skip this part.- With HA Proxy Statistics Report, you can check all active or down resources on your cluster, like, ocp_machine_config_server_frontend/backend, k8s_api_frontend/backend, ocp_http_ingress_frontend/backend, ocp_https_ingress_frontend/backend, etc.- By updating static information, we bind it with 1936 port. title: How to scale down Bare Metal IPI RHOCP 4.x cluster ?
issue: - How to scale down `Bare Metal` nodes deployed via `RHOCP` `IPI` installation?- `Bare Metal` node is joining the cluster even after removal.
resolution: - List the `machines` and `machinesets` in the cluster: ~~~ $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api $ oc get machinesets-n openshift-machine-api ~~~- Set the annotation on the `machine` which needs to be deleted: ~~~ $ oc annotate machine/-n openshift-machine-api machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-delete-machine="true" ~~~- Cordon and drain the `node` that which needs to be deleted: ~~~ $ oc adm cordon $ oc adm drain ~~~- Scale the `machineset` associated with the respective `machine`: ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=2 machineset-n openshift-machine-api ~~~- List and delete the related `bmh` resource after scaling down the `machineset`: ~~~ $ oc get bmh-n openshift-machine-api $ oc delete bmh/-n openshift-machine-api ~~~- Although the `node` object is now deleted from the cluster, it can still rejoin the cluster after reboot or if the kubelet service is restarted. To permanently delete the `node` and all its data, [decommissioning of node](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/84663) is must or use below command to destroy the disk at software level: ~~~ $ nohup shred-n 25-f-z /dev/[HDD] // Replace "[HDD]" by disk name ~~~

title: Are RHPAM/RHDM affected by CVE-2022-22965, CVE-2022-22950, CVE-2022-22963?
issue: Are RHPAM/RHDM 7 affected by CVE-2022-22965, CVE-2022-22950, CVE-2022-22963?
resolution: Following there is the information for each of the CVEs: ============== [CVE-2022-22965](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-22965) ============== An unprivileged user could exploit these flaws to incur in a Root Code Execution flaw on a vulnerable system using Spring components. It seems that the Spring4Shell RCE (Remote Code Execution) exploitation needs OpenJDK9 or later. If using earlier OpenJDK versions, the attack will not be carried out. As you are running Java 11, it is affected. RHDM 7-> spring-webmvc "Affected" Our engineering team is evaluating the affected product and the needed fixes. ============== [CVE-2022-22963](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-22963) ============== No description is available for this CVE. OpenShift Serverless-> spring-cloud-function "Affected" RHDM 7-> Not affected Regarding the CVEs CVE-2022-22965 and CVE-2022-22963, RHAPM/RHDM products are affected, but not vulnerable. SpringBoot with RHPAM/RHDM is supported, however Spring Cloud is not included/supported so the only CVE that should affect RHPAM/RHDM is the one related to Spring Web MVC (CVE-2022-22965) component but even in this case Spring is supported both for Kie Server and Kogito only via SpringBoot executable jar and any SpringBoot application is NOT vulnerable to the exploit when it is deployed as a Spring Boot executable jar. More on above is that CVE can be exploited ONLY on Java 9+ version runtime environments. RHPAM/RHDM products deliverables contains references to Spring ONLY in Maven sources pom.xml files or in Maven Offliner Manifest file to the affected spring web mvc jar artifacts. Our engineering team is doing the upgrades to fixed Spring jars in all source branches in any case, but as a patch for just released RHPAM/RHDM 7.12.1 we ONLY will provide the fixed Maven Offliner Manifest file with the upgraded versions for Spring Boot and Spring Framework. ============== [CVE-2022-22950](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-22950) ============== No description is available for this CVE. RHDM 7-> spring-expression "Under investigation" "Under investigation" doesn't necessarily mean that the product is affected by this vulnerability. It only means that our Analysis Team is still working on determining whether the product is affected and how it is affected. Regarding the CVE CVE-2022-22950, it is still under investigation.

title: Certain indices of Cluster Logging in OpenShift Container Platform 4 don't comply with the redundancyPolicy set
issue: The `redundancyPolicy` is set to `MultipleRedundancy` to have some fault tolerance and therefore the possibility to lose some `elasticsearch` members. But it seems that certain indices don't apply the value set in `redundancyPolicy`. $ es_util--query="_cat/indices?pretty&v" | grep-v audit | grep-v app | grep-v infra health status index uuid pri rep docs.count docs.deleted store.size pri.store.size green open.kibana_111578566_user1_1 VB-xTC0qSeCR6T6DSSHW6g 1 1 1 0 7.4kb 3.7kb green open.kibana_1 Cm9Hr9p1T-2G-S4Nvv54Eg 1 1 0 0 522b 261b green open.security YtJCu7FNSB-_e8AYABnrWA 1 1 6 2 61.9kb 30.9kb green open.kibana_111578567_user2_1 VU8UDs3gTrS--S2l-PKx9A 1 1 1 0 7.4kb 3.7kb
resolution: * This is expected behavior. Only the `app*`, `infra*` and `audit*` indices apply the setting configured in the `redundancyPolicy`. * The `.security` index is created and maintained directly by `elasticsearch` and therefore can not be considered by the `redundancyPolicy` as `elasticsearch` will internally make sure that this index is available and working. * The `.kibana*` indices are created and managed by `Kibana` and therefore also out of scope of the `redundancyPolicy`. Here `Kibana` will take care about the management of these indexes and apply the required replica count to make sure it works in potential failure scenarios.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] How to allow ingress network traffic when Network Policies are configured
issue: - Is it possible to apply network policy to ingress router traffic in OpenShift?- Network policies don't allow external traffic from the router when the endpoint publishing strategy is `HostNetwork`.
resolution: - In OCP v4.5 and before, when the Ingress Controller is configured to use the `HostNetwork` endpoint publishing strategy, there is no supported way to apply network policy so that ingress traffic is allowed and all other traffic is denied.- As a consequence, since bare-metal installation uses `HostNetwork` as endpointPublishingStrategy, it was not possible to specifically allow traffic from ingress. The issue has already been raised for feature enhancement and is being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under [RFE-SDN-1340](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SDN-1340).- After this RFE got resolved for RHOCP v4.8, and later backported to older versions, the `network.openshift.io/policy-group: ingress` label is given by default if the endpoint publishing strategy is `HostNetwork`, in order to allow the incoming connections from different pods while using the network policy. The changes were also merged in the official [OpenShift documentation for Network Policy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/networking/network_policy/about-network-policy.html) ~~~ apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: allow-from-openshift-ingress spec: ingress:- from:- namespaceSelector: matchLabels: network.openshift.io/policy-group: ingress podSelector: {} policyTypes:- Ingress ~~~
root_cause: When the operator deploys a product, there needs to be some way to allow for traffic from the routers to reach services in that namespace. As a workaround, the way to achieve this is by allowing traffic from the namespace having the label "network.openshift.io/policy-group: ingress". Initially, the `network.openshift.io/policy-group: ingress` label is not given by default if the endpoint publishing strategy is `HostNetwork`. The definition of that network policy should allow for access from all pods in that namespace, and as the router pods run on the host network means that the network policy object is not fulfilling its contract and the workaround here is to label the default namespace.

title: Unable to install OpenShift Container Platform on bare metal using /dev/disk symbolic link
issue: Unable to install OpenShift Container Platform 4.5.22 on bare metal with `coreos.inst.install_dev=/dev/disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-7`.
resolution: The `coreos-installer` in 4.5 should work correctly with `/dev/disk` symlinks. Note that in 4.5 and earlier, the value passed to `coreos.inst.install_dev=` must not be prefixed with `/dev`. So it should pass `coreos.inst.install_dev=disk/by-path/pci-0000:00:17.0-ata-7` in the kernel arguments.

title: A new build triggers itself and runs in a loop
issue: - A newly created `BuildConfig` triggers itself and runs in a loop to create new images.- While creating a new `BuildConfig`, it does not throw an error for the identical input and output `imagestream`.
resolution: - The workaround is to use non-identical input and output `imagestream` for the `BuildConfig` object.- This issue has been tracked in the [Bug 2073917]. [Bug 2073917]: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2073917
root_cause: - The `imageChange` trigger is enabled by default on `BuildConfig` which results in starting a new build when it finishes.

issue: When upgrading from OpenShift Container Platform 4.7 to 4.8.5, one of the Master Nodes is stuck in the "NotReady" state.

title: Drivers and Firmware update on CoreOS Node.
issue: a hardware requirement that certain adapter firmware needs to be updated using in-band firmware tools. We need to move to the latest drivers and firmware of hardware where CoreOS is running.
resolution: For the drivers the is an option in the Technology preview that is the Driver Toolkit [1], otherwise the old approach of entitled image [2]. In the documentation linked you can see all the details. Regarding the Firmware, if it is something that must be executed from the OS you can perhaps explore the approach of creating a privileged Daemonset as the following example: ~~~ $ oc create sa fw-installer $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user-z fw-installer privileged $ cat < < EOF |oc create-f- apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: my-script data: my_script.sh: | #!/bin/sh echo "This is my script"--- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: DaemonSet metadata: name: fw-daemonset spec: selector: matchLabels: app: fw-daemonset template: metadata: creationTimestamp: null labels: app: fw-daemonset spec: serviceAccount: fw-installer serviceAccountName: fw-installer hostNetwork: true containers:- name: installer image:: args:- /bin/bash--c- | echo "do something" /tmp/my_script.sh imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent lifecycle: preStop: exec: command:- /bin/bash--c- echo "Finishing on node ${K8S_NODE}" securityContext: privileged: true volumeMounts:- mountPath: /host name: host- mountPath: /tmp/my_script.sh name: add-iptables subPath: my_script.sh resources: requests: cpu: 10m memory: 300Mi env:- name: K8S_NODE valueFrom: fieldRef: apiVersion: v1 fieldPath: spec.nodeName volumes:- name: host hostPath: path: / type: ''- name: my-script configMap: defaultMode: 365 name: my-script tolerations:- effect: NoExecute operator: Exists- effect: NoSchedule operator: Exists EOF ~~~ Preparing in advance the required image with the needed software inside. But please take the above just as a mere example. Or eventual if can be applied to your case and you need to add a firmware blob on the machine this last documentation can help [3]. [1] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/scalability_and_performance/psap-driver-toolkit.html

title: "Input Signal Out of Range" message on screen while booting RHCOS
issue: - At the time of RHCOS installation, the monitor shows an `Input Signal Out of Range` message.
resolution: - Boot the RHCOS image.- Press the `TAB` key to interrupt the boot process and edit the kernel parameters.- Append the below at the end of the kernel parameters and hit the `Enter` key. ~~~ nomodeset vga=ask ~~~- Wait for the list of available resolutions to show up.- Enter the corresponding number to the required resolution.- Press the `Enter` key to set the resolution and boot.
root_cause: - Some monitor does not support the default resolution that has been set with the RHCOS. It does require manual selection to work properly.

title: How to make two default storagecalsses in OCS
issue: How to create two default storage classes: one for rbd and one for noobaa
resolution: - One can implement a webhook that sets pvc.spec.storageClassName for newly created PVCs using any site-specific rules for object store you want.- Since it's not possible to disable our admission plugin for the default storage class, when building the admission webhook, you need to make sure there is no storage class with "our" default annotation and it won't do anything.- You can write your own admission control plugin. The upstream documentation that will help you with this task is https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/- I want to highlight that Red Hat will not be able to provide support for this admission plugin since it will not be developed by us.

title: How to enable HTTP2 with HTTPS access for applications in Red Hat Openshift Service Mesh without HTTPS termination at IngressGateway
issue: - How to enable `HTTP2 `communication between ingressgateway and application pods using `HTTPS`.- How to access application in Openshift Service Mesh using `HTTP2`.
resolution: - Enable `http2` at ingress level ~~~ oc-n openshift-ingress-operator annotate ingresscontrollers/ ingress.operator.openshift.io/default-enable-http2=true ~~~- Edit the `Service Mesh Control Plane` object to accept `https` connections on a particular port. ~~~ spec: gateways: ingress: service: ports:- name: http port: 80 protocol: TCP targetPort: 8080- name: https port: 443 protocol: TCP targetPort: 8443 ~~~- Create a `secret` to hold the certificates for `https` termination at ingress gateway. ~~~ oc create-n istio-system secret tls creds--key=sample.example.com.key--cert=sample.example.com.crt ~~~- Configure `Gateway` to allow traffic into servicemesh and listen for HTTPS requests which will terminate at `ingressgateway`. Note that the `credentialName` parameter takes the name of the secret containing the certs. ~~~ kind: Gateway metadata: name: test spec: selector: app: istio-ingressgateway servers:- port: number: 443 protocol: HTTPS name: https hosts:- 'sample.example.com' tls: mode: SIMPLE credentialName: creds ~~~- Create a `VirtualService` to configure routing for the traffic. Here http matching rules are specified since the traffic from ingressgateway is plain `http2`. ~~~ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 kind: VirtualService metadata: name: test-route spec: gateways:- test hosts:- "sample.example.com" http:- match:- uri: prefix: / route:- destination: host: mysite.myproject.svc.cluster.local port: number: 8080 ~~~- Create a `DestinationRule` to re-encrypt the traffic using https that is being sent to the destination pods.- The Upgrade Policy instructs Service Mesh to use `HTTP/2` instead of the default `HTTP/1.1` ~~~ kind: DestinationRule metadata: name: drtest spec: host: myapp.myproject.svc.cluster.local trafficPolicy: portLevelSettings:- port: number: 4443 tls: mode: SIMPLE connectionPool: http: h2UpgradePolicy: UPGRADE ~~~- Make sure that the service port `name` of the application has the name `http2` otherwise you will get the following error. ~~~ upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection termination ~~~- Test by issuing a curl command and checking the logs of the application. ~~~ curl-k-http2-prior-knowledge https://sample.example.com--resolve sample.example.com:443: ~~~- **NOTE:** For UPI installations, it is assumed that the http2 feature is enabled on the LoadBalancer.

title: Restricted-csi SCC being applied to system pods causing them to crash
issue: - Our pods are crashing with permissions issues and noticed they are running with the `restricted-csi` SCC instead of the expected `privileged` ~~~ $ oc get $PODNAME-o yaml > pod1.yaml $ oc get $PODNAME-o yaml > pod2.yaml $ diff-y pod1.yaml pod2.yaml... openshift.io/scc: restricted-csi | openshift.io/scc: privileged... securityContext: securityContext: capabilities: < drop: <- KILL <- MKNOD <- SETGID <- SETUID < privileged: true privileged: true runAsUser: 1000400000 < ~~~
resolution: There are two options to work around this issue: ### Option 1- Change group or user Assign a more specific user or group to the application. OpenShift will try to assign a more restrictive SCC to the pod, so using a more restrictive SCC like restricted-csi, which is applicable to all users (`system:authenticated`), results in the incorrect SCC being applied.- For example, in this case the below is assigned in the pod definition: groups:- system:authenticated- To resolve this issue please remove the group `system:authenticated` and instead use a group with a more reduced scope, as this group will apply to cluster components. ### Option 2- Remove restricted-csi SCC Delete the `restricted-csi` SCC to prevent it from applying to applications which require privileged access. ~~~ $ oc delete scc/restricted-csi ~~~ This SCC is added by Dynatrace; see the Root Cause section for full details.
root_cause: The `restricted-csi` SCC is not a default SCC, but is instead added by the Dynatrace utility. See the [Dynatrace documentation](https://www.dynatrace.com/support/help/setup-and-configuration/setup-on-container-platforms/openshift/configure-security-context-constraint) SCCs are defined at the global scope and are associated with individual users and groups within the cluster. When a Pod is create without an SCC definition, it is assigned an SCC based on the current context for the creation and the privileges of the associated ServiceAccount/User creating the Pod. The SCC selection algorithm is as follows: 1) Highest priority first, nil is considered a 0 priority 2) If priorities are equal, the SCCs will be sorted from most restrictive to least restrictive 3) If both priorities and restrictions are equal the SCCs will be sorted by name As the created `restricted-csi` is associated with all users (`system:authenticated`) which includes the Istio SerivceAccounts. The created SCC has the same priority as the `privileged` SCC, the SCCs are priorities from most-restrictive to least restrictive. This results with the `restricted-csi` SCC being selected for the Pod. Note that this selection only happens when the Pod is created and is not changed while the Pod is running. This is why the Pods within the same DaemonSet have different SCC values.

title: Does Red Hat Support Apicurio Studio?
issue: I wish to formally request that Red Hat consider bringing the community sponsored product Apicurio Studio [https://www.apicur.io/studio/](https://www.apicur.io/studio/) into the “fold” as an “enterprise solution” or similar so that official Red Hat support can be provided for it. The functionality offered by AS seems a natural fit for a company that states the importance of APIs as being critical for businesses in the modern world. The ability for development teams to brainstorm API designs in a collaborative fashion and to integrate their work with GitLab or another SCM for a single source of the truth seems to me to be invaluable and, I believe, works well within the other Red Hat offerings (3scale and OCP).

Currently I have installed AS on our 3.11 cluster. It works for the most part—the only issue I have is that integration with our local GitLab server does not appear to work and I am not sure whether I can raise a community support call or not. So I am in a dilemma right now, which would not be the case if AS was officially supported by RH rather than merely sponsored.
When does Red Hat plan to officially support Apicurio studio
resolution: ###DO NOT PUBLISH- Share content with customers who are interested While there is a supported version of this project included in [Red Hat Integration](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_fuse/7.10/html/designing_apis/apidesigner-overview ""), that version runs only on Openshift and it is a cut down version with less features ###Red Hat Roadmap Now Apicurio contains two main projects: Service registry and API Designer. * **OpenShift Service Registry**: The [GA release](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/openshift/openshift-service-registry "") was announced the 2nd week of April 2022 It is a managed service offered together with `Red Hat OpenShift Streams for Apache Kafka` and `Openshift API Management`. Starting a trial is pretty straight forward. See [https://red.ht/TryKafka](https://red.ht/TryKafka "") for more information * **API Designer:** Red Hat is also working on a managed SaaS version of Studio with the name `Openshift API Designer`. This will be integrated with our other managed services such as `Openshift Service Registry` and support OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Avro, Json Schema, etc creation. We are working towards a public preview at the end of Q2/early Q3 2022. It is at an early stage ###Getting Support The project is hosted and free to use here [https://studio.apicur.io/](https://studio.apicur.io/ ""), but it is not supported by Red Hat, there are no SLAs, and it is purely a volunteer managed instance. If you are using the upstream version, you can create an upstream request/issue around the challenges you face. We will be changing the way Studio is integrated with other systems such as Git and make it easier to integrate. Regardless, it has been used by tens of thousands of developers so far for creating APIs.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] How to gather connectivity status between Pods & Services using must-gather?
issue: - How to gather connectivity status between **Pods*
& **Services*
running in different namespaces using **must-gather**?
resolution: - For the **OVN** cluster use the below command to connectivity status between pods running in different namespaces: ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **ovn_pod_to_pod_connectivity**: This script checks pod2pod connectivity on an OVN cluster. By default, this script spins up two pods (a client and a server) in the openshift-network-tools-* namespace.- Also optionally supply the script with a pair of source and destination names. These can either be the source and destination node names on which the debug pods should be scheduled or they can be existing pod names (format:) to run the connectivity test. ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **ovn_pod_to_svc_connectivity**: This script checks pod2svc connectivity on an OVN cluster. By default, this script spins up a pod (a client) and a service (a backing-server pod and a clusterIP:port svc) in the openshift-network-tools-* namespace.- Also optionally supply the script with a pair of source and destination names. These can either be the source and destination node names on which the debug pods should be scheduled or they can be existing pod (format:) and service names (format:) to run the connectivity test. ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_svc_connectivity ` $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- ovn_pod_to_svc_connectivity ` ~~~- For the **openshiftSDN** cluster use the below command to connectivity status between pods in different namespace: ~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=quay.io/openshift/origin-network-tools:latest-- sdn_pod_to_pod_connectivity ~~~- **sdn_pod_to_pod_connectivity**: This script checks pod2pod connectivity on a SDN cluster. state.- Sdn pod shows below events: ~~~ Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Warning Failed 69m (x402 over 41d) kubelet, compute-2 (combined from similar events): Error: context deadline exceeded Warning Failed 5m28s (x30942 over 43d) kubelet, compute-2 Error: context deadline exceeded ~~~- Creating pods fails with FailedCreatePodSandbox with these errors shown in the events or service logs: ~~~ Warning FailedCreatePodSandBox 65m kubelet, compute-2 Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create pod network sandbox k8s_completion-branch-deployment-76b77f96cc-4hv65_passport-qa_a6de14a6-cec6-433c-8704-03f9ff0b50b2_0(2c0b75ae7b2d2f57fcb7dc0ed7577cc723a4a02c5c5ec4850aafa8723c597a96): [passport-qa/completion-branch-deployment-76b77f96cc-4hv65:openshift-sdn]: error adding container to network "openshift-sdn": failed to send CNI request: Post "http://dummy/": dial unix /var/run/openshift-sdn/cniserver/socket: connect: connection refused ~~~
resolution: - Cordon and drain node on which sdn pod is in CreateContainerError. ~~~ $ oc adm cordon $ oc adm drain ~~~- Restart crio and kubelet service on the node using ssh. ~~~ $sudo systemctl restart crio $sudo systemctl restart kubelet ~~~- Mark the node as schedulable when done. ~~~ $ oc adm uncordon ~~~

title: Ingress network policy can be overruled by egress network policy on another pod
issue: - Network policies with type Egress are not behaving as described in [https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/) in an Openshift 4 cluster, using OVN. In Openshift 3 using Calico, they behave as described.- Citation: "For a connection from a source pod to a destination pod to be allowed, both the egress policy on the source pod and the ingress policy on the destination pod need to allow the connection. If either side does not allow the connection, it will not happen."- Using policies with type ingress to deny traffic to sensitive pods, and use policies with type egress to limit the number of pods that are allowed to connect back to the internet.- Security Implications In a multitenant cluster, tenants are unable to deny traffic to their pods when another namespace applies a network policy with type egress. We use an egress policy in the case where pods need to connect to external sources. When such a pod is compromised, it can easily be used as a staging platform to attack all pods in the cluster, regardless of their ingress network policies.
resolution: - This issue is now fixed by errata in:- OCP 4.10.8+- OCP 4.9.27+- OCP 4.8.36+- OCP 4.7.47+

resolution: The config that inadvertently causes this problem is the 'Hint' setting in the spec: ~~~ rootDeviceHints:... rotational: false ~~~ As a workaround, remove that rotational setting from the install-config. title: How do I increase the kernel log ring buffer size?
issue: How do I increase the kernel log ring buffer size?
Why are boot messages missing from the logs?
A lot of boot messages are missing from the logs.
The `dmesg` file does not contain all the log messages from boot.
I need to troubleshoot the boot process but some of the boot messages are missing.
resolution: Increase the kernel log buffer, either permanently for every boot, or temporarily just for that boot. ### Permanent Change #### RHEL8 and later Use `grub2-editenv` command to modify the kernel command line. Refer: [How do I permanently modify the kernel command line in RHEL 8 or 9?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6383141) #### RHEL7 Edit the `/etc/default/grub` file and add `log_buf_len=8M` to the end of the `GRUB_CMDLINE_DEFAULT` line. For example, if the current default line reads: ~~~ GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="rd.lvm.lv=vg_root/lv_root" ~~~ Change the line so it reads: ~~~ GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="rd.lvm.lv=vg_root/lv_root log_buf_len=8M" ~~~ Rebuild the GRUB configuration used at boot time with the command: ~~~ grub2-mkconfig-o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg ~~~ Reboot the system #### RHEL 6 and RHEL 5 Edit the `/boot/grub/grub.conf` file and add `log_buf_len=8M` to the end of the GRUB kernel line. For example, if the current kernel line is: ~~~ kernel /vmlinuz-2.6.32-696.el6.x86_64 ro root=/dev/mapper/vg_root-lv_root ~~~ Change the line so it reads: ~~~ kernel /vmlinuz-2.6.32-696.el6.x86_64 ro root=/dev/mapper/vg_root-lv_root log_buf_len=8M ~~~ Reboot the system. ### Temporary Change When booting the system, stop the boot process on the GRUB kernel selection screen by pressing an arrow key up or down. * Press **e** to edit the boot entry * Use up and down arrows to select the kernel line with the `vmlinuz` file on it #### RHEL 7 * Press **End** to place the cursor on the end of that line * Add `log_buf_len=8M` to the end of the kernel line, as shown in the examples above * Press **Ctrl+x** to boot with the edited boot entry #### RHEL 6 and RHEL 5 * Press **e** again to edit the kernel line * Add `log_buf_len=8M` to the end of the kernel line, as shown in the examples above * Press **Enter** to temporarily save the changes * Press **b** to boot with the edited boot entry
root_cause: To avoid losing boot messages, the kernel log buffer must be a large enough size to contain all the boot messages up until the point the system is able to write the log to permanent storage. This is especially true if additional logging is enabled; for example by removing `quiet` from the boot line or setting `log_level=debug`- or you have a large number of storage devices. If the kernel log buffer is not large enough, the oldest messages during boot will be lost, overwritten by the latest messages. For example, the following knowledgebase solutions show specific cases where a recommendation to increase the `log_buf_len` is present: * [udevd worker unexpectedly returned with status 0x0100](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/206493) * [How to add debug messages to the boot process in Red Hat Enterprise Linux](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/67253) * [Server with many LUNs/paths crashes while booting/rescanning for LUNs](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1507193) * [Boot takes a long time with multipath SAN storage containing many paths and partitions on the LUNs](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/61496) While there is no specific recommended minimum that would be applicable to all configurations, a reasonable practical amount for most configurations is 8M in size. Typically this is a small fraction of total physical memory on modern enterprise hardware. As such, the additional memory should not adversely affect system operations, while the additional ring buffer memory often enhances supportability if or when an issue related to boot time happens or within a vmcore at crash time as well under other circumstances. By default, the log ring buffer size is set in the conf variable `CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT`. To check the default size: ~~~ # grep CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT /boot/config* CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT=20 # RHEL 7 and later CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT=19 # RHEL 6 (2.6.32) CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT=18 # RHEL 5 (2.6.18) ~~~ The `CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT` specifies the 2^N default size of the log ring buffer (1 < <`CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT`): * `20`: 2^20 = 1024KB (RHEL 7 and later default log ring buffer size) * `19`: 2^19 = 512KB (RHEL 6 default log ring buffer size) * `18`: 2^18 = 256KB (RHEL 5 default log ring buffer size) The default size of `log_buf_len` for `RHEL7 and later` is `~1048576` bytes. Details explained in [How much is the default log_buf_len size?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3081011) This default kernel configuration variable is set during compilation, and cannot be changed without recompiling the kernel (which is not supported). Overriding the default value requires changing the GRUB boot menu and rebooting. The buffer size may be increased by using the `log_buf_len` kernel boot parameter either for one boot by editing the boot menu at boot time, or permanently by changing the appropriate GRUB configuration file on disk. The `log_buf_len` kernel parameter is described within the [kernel-parameters.txt](https://access.redhat.com/articles/10476) file: ~~~ log_buf_len=n Sets the size of the printk ring buffer, in bytes. Format: {n | nk | nM} n must be a power of two. The default size is set in the kernel config file. ~~~

title: How to use self-extracting installer scripts for OpenShift Nodes provided by Red Hat Support
issue: When troubleshooting issues with OpenShift, the Red Hat's Support Teams may provide patched versions of applications that run on the Red Hat Core OS Nodes with in the cluster. This patched software will contain custom code in an attempt to resolve the issues and are bundled into a self-extracting installer that is provided through the case. How do I use this installer to test the patches?
resolution: 1) Download the self-extracting installer script from the Customer Portal case. In this example, the script will be called `kernel-installer.sh`. 2) Copy the installer script onto the affected Red Hat CoreOS Nodes. This can be achieved by using `ssh` if port 22 is accessible on the Nodes. If port 22 is blocked, the `oc cp` tool can be used to copy the installer onto the Nodes through the OpenShift APIServer. 2a) Copying the installer script using `ssh`. **NOTE** this requires access to port 22 on the individual Nodes which is not available with all installation types: ~~~ scp-i./kernel-installer.sh:/home/core/kernel-installer.sh ~~~ 2b) Copying the installer script using `oc cp` tool.- Open two terminals that have access to the cluster.- In Terminal1, run `oc debug nodes/ ` to create a debug Pod of the desired Node. This will output the name of the created Pod to standard out.- In Terminal2, run `oc cp:/host/home/core/ ` to copy the file to the desired Node. For example, copying the `kernel-installer.sh` will be possible with the following command: `oc cp kernel-installer.sh:/host/home/core/kernel-installer.sh` 3) Once the installer script has been successfully copied, the installer script can be used to deploy the patched software.- Run a debug Pod on the desired Node, chroot onto the Host and run the script similar to the following: ~~~ oc debug nodes/ # chroot /host # cd /home/core #./kernel-installer.sh WARNING: This command will extract and install new kernel and assorted debug packages. IF YOU DO NOT WANT TO DO THIS ABORT NOW Otherwise, it will install. Press ENTER to continue. [+] installing debug code for BugXXX /tmp/output_dir ~ [+] running rpm-ostree override replace rpm-ostree override replace kernel-XXXX.x86_64.rpm kernel-core-XXXX.el8_4.bz2018930.x86_64.rpm... Added: kernel-XXXX.x86_64.rpm kernel-core-XXXX.el8_4.bz2018930.x86_64.rpm Run “systemctl reboot” to start a reboot [+] Installed. Please reboot and run verification steps." ~~~- Restart the Node to pivot ostree: ~~~ # systemctl reboot ~~~ 4) To rollback the changes at any time, the following commands can be used: ~~~ # rpm-ostree reset ~~~ To test this patched software, the installer must be copied on to the Nodes.

title: Unable to create Kiali pod for serviceMesh settup

resolution: Run the below commands * Remove the Istio-system project note: If your project stuck in "Terminating", then follow the "" from KCS to remove it. * Recreate the "istio-system" project again and try to run the below command once project is created. $ oc get kiali-n istio-system NAME AGE kiali 119d Remove this Kiali custom resource using the below command $ oc patch-n istio-system kialis.kiali.io/kiali--type=merge-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":null}}' Verify if Kiali is removed $ oc get kiali-n istio-system No resources found in istio-system namespace Check if there are any crds avaibale in istio-system project using the below command $ oc get crds-o name | grep '.*\.istio\.io' Remove the above crds using the below commands $ oc patch crd/-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge Example: $oc patch crd/authorizationpolicies.security.istio.io-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge $oc patch crd/destinationrules.networking.istio.io-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge $oc patch crd/envoyfilters.networking.istio.io-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge $oc patch crd/gateways.networking.istio.io-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge
root_cause: * If Kiali objects do not removed completely during uninstall and it will not allow installing the Kiali pod again during next ServiceMesh installation.

issue: In the RHV Manager Portal, the Upload Image feature fails with 'Test Connection' or 'Choose File" Engine Reports: EVENT_ID: UPLOAD_IMAGE_NETWORK_ERROR(1,062), Unable to upload image to disk 5b0d250d-62e2-45a1-9860-7be425a99f52 due to a network error. Ensure ovirt-engine's CA certificate is registered as a trusted CA in the browser. The certificate can be fetched from https://10.10.88.15/ovirt-engine/services/pki-resource?resource=ca-certificate&format=X509-PEM-CA
resolution: [1] Check DNS Server record entry for the RHV Manager FQDN [2] Check to see if the DNS entry matches the hostname for the RHV Manager ~~~ # nmcli general hostname ~~~ [3] If the FQDN in the DNS does not match the RHV Manager hostname, change the hostnamen: ~~~ # nmcli general hostname my-server ~~~ [4] Since the engine hostname was specified incorrectly during the deployment, the tool below will need to be used to change the engine name in the engine database and certifications. [oVirt Engine Rename Tool](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_virtualization/4.4/html/administration_guide/chap-utilities_rhv_backup_restore#sect-The_oVirt_Engine_Rename_Tool) [5] Since the engine has been renamed make sure the correct certification from the engine is downloaded to the workstation. This is typically the engine's ca.pem, which is linked to the apacahe-ca.pem. Navigate to https:// < < engine_fqdn > > ovirt-engine/services/pki-resource?resource=ca-certificate&format=X509-PEM-CA- chrome://settings/certificates- Authorities tab- Import is below Authorities tab on right- Select all 3 trust settings- Look for org- < < engine_domain_fqdn > >. < < number > >- Expand < < engine_domain_fqdn > > to see the < < engine_fqdn > > certificate underneath. Verify certificate and trust settings are enabled. [6] Test Upload
root_cause: When the RHV deployment was performed, engine-fqdn.local was used when the DNS record for the engine domain was engine-fqdn.example.com. Performing 'nslookup' would not have found issue because the IP will validate the DNS record and allow the RHV Manager to be accessed in the browser regardless the engine hostname.

title: `local-pv-xxx` going to Terminating state
issue: `local-pv-xxx` are going to Terminating state. ~~~ # oc get pv|grep local|grep Terminating local-pv-2b8e3ddb 1490Gi RWO Delete Terminating openshift-storage/ocs-deviceset-localblock-1-data-19bsn7r localblock 91d ~~~
resolution: To prevent this in future follow below steps for all local pv's- Remove `ownerReference` from the PV. Run below command: ~~~ # oc patch pv local-pv-xxx-p '{"metadata": {"ownerReferences":null}}' ~~~- The issue is tracked in [Bug 2061447](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2061447)
root_cause: - Local Storage Operator added ownerReference to the PV's it created which is causing the issue. When the node gets deleted, the garbage collector issues a delete request for the PV. But since the PV is still bound to a PVC, it stays "Terminating" until the PVC is deleted. ~~~ ownerReferences:- apiVersion: v1 kind: Node name: uid: ~~~- The original intent of this was "if we're deleting the node, we don't need to keep the local storage PV for it" but clearly that causes issues when combined with MachineHealthChecks.

title: OpenShift UPI installation - how to add AWS instance’s name using AWS CLI cloudformation
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Following the Red Hat AWS OpenShift UPI installation documentation. The AWS console does not show Instance’s name- Why AWS console does not show Instance name after AWS OpenShift CLI installation
resolution: - Following the Red Hat documentation to deploy OpenShift on AWS via the CLI, you will be using `cloudformation` templates yaml files and parameters json files.- When creating AWS Instances (Master and worker nodes) You need to modify both files, to add a new key/value being the instance's name.- The InstanceName variable in parameters defined the value referred in the resource section as InstanceName.- See the snapshot below of what needs to be done Example- CloudFormation template for worker machines ~~~ AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09 Description: Template for OpenShift Cluster Node Launch (EC2 worker instance) Parameters: InstanceName: Default: workerx Type: String......... Resources: Worker0: Type: AWS::EC2::Instance Properties: Tags:- Key:!Join ["", ["kubernetes.io/cluster/",!Ref InfrastructureName]] Value: "shared"- Key: Name Value:!Ref "InstanceName" ~~~ Example- JSON file that contains the parameter values that the CloudFormation template requires ~~~ [.........}, {"ParameterKey": "InstanceName", "ParameterValue": "worker2"}] ~~~
root_cause: - By default, the `cloudformation`'s template used to deploy the OpenShift on AWS does not have a parameter to set the AWS EC2 Instance's name

title: Custom SCC incorrectly assigned to pods instead of the expected SCC due to higher priority
issue: - Why the custom SCC `test-scc` is being prioritized on OpenShift ADP restic pods instead of the SCC `velero-privileged`?- The recently created Security Context Constraint (SCC) has a higher priority than the SCC required by the pod.
resolution: - Change the SCC priorities so that `test-scc` have a lower priority than `velero-privileged`. That can be achieved by changing the key `priority: ` while editing the SCCs.- Other possibility is to create another SCC with the same privileges as `velero-privileged`, but the priority set to 1-9 (in the example below, 5 was used).- Once either of the options above is done, you can remove the pod and it should recreate with the correct SCC.- Example SCC yaml: ~~~ allowHostDirVolumePlugin: true allowHostIPC: true allowHostNetwork: true allowHostPID: true allowHostPorts: true allowPrivilegeEscalation: true allowPrivilegedContainer: true allowedCapabilities:- '*' allowedUnsafeSysctls:- '*' apiVersion: security.openshift.io/v1 defaultAddCapabilities: null fsGroup: type: RunAsAny groups:- test kind: SecurityContextConstraints metadata: name: velero-privileged-pitc priority: 5 readOnlyRootFilesystem: false requiredDropCapabilities: null runAsUser: type: RunAsAny seLinuxContext: type: RunAsAny seccompProfiles:- '*' supplementalGroups: type: RunAsAny users:- system:admin- system:serviceaccount:openshift-adp:velero volumes: ~~~
root_cause: - Both SCCs have the same priority (nil/null/0).- `oadp-operator` [GitHub page](https://github.com/openshift/oadp-operator/blob/6f4315e3e5725b3893cc1bcbfa34bfbc36f1e629/controllers/velero.go#L334) shows that the SCC priority is set to `nil`, which is the same priority set to `test-scc`.- Any unset value is considered a 0 priority.
