title: ExtremelyHighIndividualControlPlaneCPU alert troubleshooting in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: `ExtremelyHighIndividualControlPlaneCPU` alert is firing in the cluster CPU utilization on a single control plane node is very high, more CPU pressure is likely to cause a failover; increase available CPU. Extreme CPU pressure can cause slow serialization and poor performance from the kube-apiserver and etcd. When this happens, there is a risk of clients seeing non-responsive API requests which are issued again causing even more CPU pressure. It can also cause failing liveness probes due to slow etcd responsiveness on the backend. If one kube-apiserver fails under this condition, chances are you will experience a cascade as the remaining kube-apiservers are also under-provisioned. To fix this, increase the CPU and memory on your control plane nodes.
resolution: Extreme CPU pressure can cause slow serialization and poor performance from the kube-apiserver and etcd. When this happens, there is a risk of clients seeing non-responsive API requests which are issued again causing even more CPU pressure. It can also cause failing liveness probes due to slow etcd responsiveness on the backend. If one kube-apiserver fails under this condition, chances are you will experience a cascade as the remaining kube-apiservers are also under-provisioned. To fix this, increase the CPU and memory on your control plane nodes. if this needs to be reported, then capture the following dataset, and raise a new support case attaching the dataset-- must-gather- audit logs- dump of prometheus data- How to gather the audit logs of the cluster: ~~~ oc adm must-gather-- /usr/bin/gather_audit_logs ~~~ How to take a dump of the cluster prometheus data: ~~~ #!/usr/bin/env bash function queue() {local TARGET="${1}" shift local LIVE LIVE="$(jobs | wc-l)" while [["${LIVE}"-ge 45]]; do sleep 1 LIVE="$(jobs | wc-l)" done echo "${@}" if [[-n "${FILTER:-}"]]; then "${@}" | "${FILTER}" > "${TARGET}" & else "${@}" > "${TARGET}" & fi} ARTIFACT_DIR=$PWD mkdir-p $ARTIFACT_DIR/metrics echo "Snapshotting prometheus (may take 15s)..." queue ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/metrics/prometheus.tar.gz oc--insecure-skip-tls-verify exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-- tar cvzf--C /prometheus. FILTER=gzip queue ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/metrics/prometheus-target-metadata.json.gz oc--insecure-skip-tls-verify exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-- /bin/bash-c "curl-G http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets/metadata--data-urlencode 'match_target={instance!=\"\"}'" ~~~
root_cause: This alert is triggered when there is a sustained high CPU utilization on a single control plane node. The urgency of this alert is determined by how long the node is sustaining high CPU usage:- Critical- when CPU usage on an individual control plane node is greater than 90% for more than 1h.- Warning- when CPU usage on an individual control plane node is greater than 90% for more than 5m. This alert is triggered when CPU utilization across all three control plane nodes is higher than two control plane nodes can sustain; a single control plane node outage may cause a cascading failure; increase available CPU. The urgency of this alert is determined by how long CPU utilization across all three control plane nodes is higher than two control plane nodes can sustain.- Warning- when CPU utilization across all three control plane nodes is higher than two control plane nodes can sustain for more than 10m

title: ISCSI mount times out with multiple initiators in OCP 4
issue: `iSCSI` `PV's` could not be mounted with a "failed to get any path for iscsi disk" error: ~~~ Warning FailedMount 5s (x10 over 17m) kubelet MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume "volumename": failed to get any path for iscsi disk, last err seen: Timed out waiting for device at path /dev/disk/by-path/initiator:lun after 30s ~~~
The `pod` using that `volume` is stuck in `ContainerCreating` status.
The `LUN` can be mounted without any issue on the `worker` `node` manually with the same `initiator` and its credentials.
resolution: > ***Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Only one session with an `initiator` can be opened against an `iSCSI target` per `worker` `node`. This issue can be fixed by using the same `initiator` for all the connections to the same `target`. All the `PVs` in a ǹode` using the same `target` must` be using the same `initiatorName`. If the `target` is protected by `chap` password authentication, it is possible to use a ``SecretReference`` as detailed [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.19/#secretreference-v1-core) to inject the `chap` authentication into the `PV`.
root_cause: This issue is caused by multiple `PVs` with different `initiators` for the same `target` trying to be mounted on the same `worker` `node`. Only one session per `node` and per `target` is possible because is the `worker` itself who establishes the connection. This causes that no new sessions are created on the `node` if there's already an `initiatorName` in use for the `target portal`.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] Keepalived virtual router ID clashes when there are multiple cluster on same network
issue: - Is it possible deploy multiple OCP4.x cluster on **Same Network**?- What are the potential risks if there are multiple clusters on same network?- How to configure custom VRID in keepalived.conf during the IPI Installation?- How to specify VRIDs in keepalived.conf post successful OCP deployment?
resolution: - It is not possible to specify custom VRID when doing IPI installation on vSphere.- Modifying VRIDs post successful OCP deployment is not recommended as the VRID is based on the cluster name.- To overcome from such issues avoid deploying multiple clusters on same network.
root_cause: - Keepalived virtual router ID clashes when there are multiple clusters on same network.- The installer generates VRID using the cluster-name, but with the expectation that networks are segmented already and so no conflicts will occur.

title: Can't find update edge for OpenShift 4.8 to 4.9
issue: When trying to update Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) from 4.8 to 4.9 the OpenShift Console and Update Graph do not show any available update path.
Why are updates from OpenShift Container Platform 4.8 to OpenShift Container Platform 4.9 blocked?
resolution: * Up to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform [4.9.28](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:1245) update recommendation for updates from Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8 to 4.9 were removed due to the root cause described below. * With Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform [4.9.28](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:1245) upgrade recommendation for upgrades from Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8 to 4.9 have been restored and are available again, the same way as they used to be available before the upgrade recommendation was removed. * For more details about available upgrade recommendation, consult [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Update Graph](https://access.redhat.com/labs/ocpupgradegraph/update_channel). * While the upgrade recommendations were removed due the potential issue, the released versions themselves always remained supported. For question related to updates from OCP 4.8 to 4.9, contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport).
root_cause: * There are indications of a potential data inconsistency issue introduced in `etcd 3.5`. * OCP 4.9 and 4.10 both utilize `etcd 3.5` while OCP 4.8 and earlier use earlier versions of `etcd` that do not exhibit this issue. * The Solution [Potential etcd data inconsistency issue in OCP 4.9 and 4.10](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6849521) provides information for administrators of clusters running OCP 4.9 and 4.10.

title: Cannot see logs on all pods and cannot rsh to pod if there are nodes NotReady
issue: - `oc logs`, `oc rsh` and `oc exec` to a pod don't work although the pod runs fine.- There are nodes in `NotReady` status- The error messages in "Diagnostic Steps" section are shown (this is important, because if these errors are not shown, this solution doesn't apply)
resolution: Workaround is to either make sure that all the nodes are ready (by fixing whatever problems they may have) or delete the NotReady node objects (they can be re-added if needed once the issue is fully fixed). A definitive fix is being worked at [BZ#2034883](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2034883), so if you hit this issue, please open a support case with Red Hat for proper tracking.
root_cause: This issue happens while there is a renewal of the `kubelet-to-kube-apiserver-ca` and the kube-apiserver pods are re-deployed so they start using it. The `kubelet-to-kube-apiserver-ca` signs the client certificate used by kube-apiserver to access the kubelet port 10250, which is required for some operations like the ones backing `oc logs`, `oc rsh` and `oc exec` commands. When this process works normally, it works like this:- Cluster kube-apiserver operator generates the new CA and populates it to the `kube-apiserver-to-kubelet-client-ca` configmap of `openshift-kube-apiserver-operator` project.- Machine config operator reads that configmap and updates `spec.kubeAPIServerServingCAData` field of `controllerconfig/machine-config-controller` object- That makes machine config controller (a component of machine config operator) modify some of the base machineconfigs.- Once those machineconfigs are modified, the CA starts being rolled out to the nodes (in recent versions, this doesn't require a reboot).- Some time after that, cluster kube-apiserver operator deploys a new revision of the kube-apiserver that uses client certificates signed by the new CA to contact the kubelet port. However, this process may block if:- There are not ready nodes- A change in the `machine-config-daemon` daemonset is being rolled out by the machine config operator and that rollout is stuck due to the not ready nodes. The reason is that machine config operator fully blocks on the daemonset rollout forever, because it cannot finish (due to not ready nodes) and doesn't perform other tasks, like reconciling the `spec.kubeAPIServerServingCAData` field of `controllerconfig/machine-config-controller` object as per steps above. This, ultimately blocks the `kubelet-to-kube-apiserver-ca` deployment to the nodes, so when the kube-apiserver starts using it, kubelets don't acknowledge the CA used by kube-apiserver and reject the connections to the kubelet ports, making the commands that require this connections fail. This issue has only been observed so far when a change in the `machine-config-daemon` daemonset is blocked due to not ready nodes, but it is potentially possible that this issue also manifests due to other resources blocked for other reasons as long as the machine config operator is stuck waiting on them and not performing the `kubeAPIServerServingCAData` reconciliation.

title: [AMQ Interconnect] How to externalize the the vhost policies in a separate configmap ?
issue: - How to externalize the the **`vhost`*

policies in a `configmap`?- Interconnect Router Pods are not connecting to one another in the same Namespace and the startup Script is throwing errors: Waiting for IP address... Traceback (most recent call last): File "/opt/interconnect/bin/auto_mesh.py", line 246, in get_config(sys.argv[1]).append_connectors(connectors) File "/opt/interconnect/bin/auto_mesh.py", line 190, in append_connectors properties = self.get_inter_router_properties() File "/opt/interconnect/bin/auto_mesh.py", line 179, in get_inter_router_properties entities = SimpleParser(self.filename).parse() File "/opt/interconnect/bin/auto_mesh.py", line 112, in parse e = self.parse_entity() File "/opt/interconnect/bin/auto_mesh.py", line 119, in parse_entity properties = self.parse_properties() File "/opt/interconnect/bin/auto_mesh.py", line 133, in parse_properties raise Exception("Could not parse properties: %s" % self.lines[-1]) Exception: Could not parse properties:} Error configuring automesh: Could not parse properties:}
resolution: 1. Provide PolicyDir in the policy section (all the files in the /opt/router/policy will be loaded from the volume Mounts of the configMap): policy {enableVhostPolicy: true enableVhostNamePatterns: true defaultVhost: $default policyDir: /opt/router/policy} 2. Copy the content of the `vhost` part in the `qdrouterd.conf` to a file file `default-policy.json`. 3. Remove the `vhost` section from `qdrouterd.conf`. 4. Create another *CM* (`ConfigMap`) with the existing `policy` stuff: apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: router-policy data: default-policy.json: | [["vhost", {"hostname": "$default", "maxConnectionsPerUser": 100, "allowUnknownUser": false, "groups": {"$admin": {"users": "admin", "remoteHosts": "*", "sources": "*", "targets": "*", "allowAnonymousSender": "true", "allowDynamicSource": "true"}, "$apps": {"users": "apps", "remoteHosts": "*", "sources": "*", "targets": "*"}}}]] 5. In your template add the following `configMap` and the corresponding `VolumeMount`: volumeMounts:- mountPath: /opt/router/policy name: router-policy volumes:- configMap: defaultMode: 420 name: router-policy name: router-policy Once you deploy your router pods with the above steps, you should not see the exceptions related to auto_mesh script at the startup of the pod and also you should see the following lines: +0000 POLICY (info) Policy configured maxConnections: 65535, policyDir: '/opt/router/policy',access rules enabled: 'true', use hostname patterns: 'true' +0000 POLICY (info) Policy fallback defaultVhost is defined: '$default' The above lines shows that the policies are loaded now from the directory: `/opt/router/policy`
root_cause: **[ENTMQIC-3295](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ENTMQIC-3295)** **[KCS-6820131](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6820131)**

title: [RHACS / Stackrox] Creating an additional custom route for Central
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - How to access `Central` using a `different hostname` rather than the default one?- How to create a `custom route` with different URL for `Central`?
resolution: **OPTION 1**:- Considering `xyz.abc.com` to be a custom URL / hostname, create a `separate route` under stackrox namespace and put the value for `spec.host` as `xyz.abc.com` ~~~ spec: host: xyz.abc.com port: targetPort: https tls: termination: passthrough to: kind: Service name: central weight: 100 wildcardPolicy: None ~~~- After creating the route, the central will be accessible with a different hostname.- If custom certificates are being used for the central hostname, then make sure to update the central and sensor with additional certificates. For more details, please refer to the document for [Adding trusted certificate authorities](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/3.69/configuration/add-trusted-ca.html). Otherwise the central might crash. **OPTION 2**:- Edit the `existing route` for central to work with a `different hostname`. But it will only work if the RHACS is installed using `helm`.- If the installation is done via RHACS operator, then the operator might roll back all the changes made. In this case go for **OPTION 1**.

title: How to upgrade 3scale from a template to operator based deployment on OCP 4
issue: 3scale is installed via templates on OCP 4 and only the operator is supported. How to migrate data to an operator based deployment on the same cluster?
resolution: ### Backup/Restore procedure Refer to the guide to [migrate from a template based deployment in OCP 3 to an operator based deployment in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/migrating_3scale/migration-template-operator) it states that the recommended approach is to backup 3scale following the steps in the guide to [backup 3scale for a template based deployment](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates) and once complete then follow the guide to [restore 3scale for an operator based deployment](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html-single/operating_3scale/index#procedures-to-restore-databases). In case an error is encountered during this process please open a support case. #### Sanity check {#sanity-check} Please run the following tests as a sanity check pre-backup and post-restore: ~~~ oc set env dc/apicast-staging APICAST_LOG_LEVEL=debug ~~~- Send a valid curl request to the Public route for the `apicast-staging` pod which should include a valid path and set of credentials- The request should return an expected response from your API upstream server **Note**: Store the test request and response message so it can be used later for the post-restore sanity check. #### Backup Follow the [3scale backup/restore guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates). Pay attention to any sections that state **Template-based deployments** as during the backup phase these should be followed and **NOT**_"Operator-based deployments"_. In the section [backing up openshift secrets and configmaps](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates#backing_up_openshift_secrets_and_configmaps) ensure that any objects created manually (not included in the default template) are backed up accordingly. Specifically if there are any custom policies included via a `configmap` and `volumeMount` approach then the `configmap` needs to be backed up here. The backup procedure has been completed when reaching the end of this section. **IMPORTANT**: Any objects backed up during the above phase of this procedure (secrets & configmaps) should be done so by removing any fields that reference the namespace in which they were originally created. See the following example command: ~~~ oc get secrets system-smtp-o json | jq 'del(.metadata.creationTimestamp,.metadata.namespace,.metadata.resourceVersion,.metadata.uid)' > system-smtp.json ~~~ #### Prepare for restore There are 2 ways to manage the migration and both approaches are described below including the pros & cons of each, ultimately the decision is entirely based on the specific requirements of each environment and business/technical needs. ##### Option 1: Delete existing namespace Routes need to be migrated and `persistentVolumes` recycled so the easiest and cleanest way to prepare for the restore phase is by simply deleting the entire namespace. Once all objects have been deleted create exactly the same namespace as existed before. Follow **only** the [prerequisites](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/installing_3scale/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#deploying-threescale-using-the-operator) from this guide and once completed skip to the [Restore section](#Restore) below. ##### Option 2: Keep existing namespace for faster rollback purposes As routes need to be migrated it will be necessary to delete all the routes in the 3scale namespace and to ensure that is done correctly scale down the 2 zync pods responsible for managing the routes: ~~~ oc scale dc/zync--replicas=0 oc scale dc/zync-que--replicas=0 ~~~ Check existing routes in the project: ~~~ oc get routes-n <3scale-namespace> ~~~ Then proceed to manually delete each of these routes. Once completed repeat the last command above and ensure the output shows_"No resources found"_. Also ensure that there are enough `persistentVolumes` provisioned for another 3scale installation, the storage requirements are described in the [system requirements](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.8/html/installing_3scale/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#system-requirements-for-installing-threescale-on-openshift) section. Next, follow the [prerequisites](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/installing_3scale/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#deploying-threescale-using-the-operator) to finish preparation for the restore procedure taking care to use a different name for the new project than the previous installation and **take care** to [restore the secrets and configMaps](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates#restoring-operator-based-deployment) **before** installing the APIManager CR. Once that is complete proceed to the [Restore section](#Restore) below. ##### Pros & Cons of the 2 options ###### Option 1 Pros- Faster- Less steps/commands to execute- Less undocumented steps Cons- No easy/fast rollback option- Not an officially tested migration path ###### Option 2 Pros- Existing installation remains in place- Faster rollback procedure Cons- Many more commands/steps to execute- More resources need to be provisioned- More persistent volumes need to be provisioned- Cannot use exactly the same project name as before- Not an officially tested migration path #### Restore {#Restore} At this point there should be a new project + operator installed (for 3scale version 2.11) and any other prerequisites described in the official documentation.- Follow the [restoring system databases](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates#procedures-to-restore-databases) guide and remember to restore any custom objects such as configmaps at this point. Regardless of which option was followed to migrate the deployment as described in the previous section above the restore procedure should start [here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates#restoring-operator-based-deployment) as 3scale is now on an_"Operator-based deployment"_.- Continue to follow all steps as described in the official guide and pay particular attention to sections which state_Template-based deployments_ and **ignore** these and follow the alternate steps titled **Operator-based deployments**.- Once the restore procedure has been completed then run the [sanity check](#sanity-check). If an HTTP 403 or some other unexpected response is returned then wait for a period of up to 15 minutes to give the system time to synchronise data between the different applications inside the system. If the sanity check still doesn't pass then open a case attaching the `apicast-staging` & `backend-listener` pod logs.
root_cause: 3scale was installed on OCP 4.x via the templates instead of the supported Operator.

title: OCS 3.11 - heketi-cli fails with Error: Id not found
issue: This is OCS 3.11 and some heketi-cli commands fails: ~~~ sh-4.2# heketi-cli topology info Error: Id not found ~~~ At the same time we get run that command on the heketi pod, on heketi pod logs we see: ~~~ 2022/05/17 13:44:07 Can't collect topology info for metrics: Id not found ~~~
resolution: 1. Follow Diagnistic Steps (see below) to identify the cause of this issue. 2. Contact with Red Hat support as it may be required to edit heketi DB to get this issue solved. That will require to: 1) To stop and export heketi db using these steps: [How to export and import Heketi database in Openshift Container Storage-3.9 or newer version?](https://access.redhat.com/articles/3687641) 2) You will keep heketi down, that only means NO new PVs can be allocated during that time, although access to current existing PVs will remain. 3) Upload the heketidb to the Red Hat support case. Then Red Hat support will edit the heketi db and send it back to you. 4) Then import the new heketi database following the import steps from [How to export and import Heketi database in Openshift Container Storage-3.9 or newer version?](https://access.redhat.com/articles/3687641) This will start heketi pod and service using the new heketi db.
root_cause: It was found three unknown brick IDs in the heketi database. This is the cause of the metrics & topology "Id not found" error. This db would need to be fixed by manually editing the heketi db dump JSON file.

title: Builds failing to push an image to internal registry with x509 cert unknown authority error
issue: - Some builds keep on failing: ~~~ error: build error: Failed to push image: trying to reuse blob sha256:e756f3fdd6a378aa16205b0f75d178b7532b110e86be7659004fc6a21183226c at destination: pinging container registry image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000: Get "https://image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/v2/": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~- When a user deletes the Build Config and recreates it, everything works fine, the build succeeds and gets pushed normally. However, some later builds may fail sporadically again. (Deleting the whole build config again and copy-pasting (or using a template to deploy) the same code works for some time again)
resolution: - A [Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2095830) is being triaged with the engineering

title: Process is not terminated in pod terminal on UI when accessed.
issue: - A new /bin/sh process is created each time in UI while accessing the pod terminal.
resolution: - Manually killing the process can be used as a workaround: ~~~ $ kill-9 ~~~- It works as expected in CLI because exiting the shell kills the /bin/sh process.- A [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1979571 "Bugzilla") is raised for this issue which is fixed in OCP 4.9 details can be found in [Errata](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:3759 "Errata").

title: How to use ovs-tcpdump in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x with OVNKubernetes
issue: How to use ovs-tcpdump in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x with OVNKubernetes
resolution: ### How to run an ad-hoc ovs-tcpdump Connect to the node where `ovs-tcpdump` shall be executed: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ip-10-0-146-183.eu-west-1.compute.internal Starting pod/ip-10-0-146-183eu-west-1computeinternal-debug... To use host binaries, run `chroot /host` Pod IP: 10.0.146.183 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.2# chroot /host sh-4.4# ~~~ Get the OVS major version: ~~~ sh-4.4# ovs-vsctl get open. ovs_version "2.13.0" ~~~ Change the toolbox version to fedora: ~~~ cat < <'EOF' > /root/.toolboxrc REGISTRY=docker.io IMAGE=fedora:latest EOF ~~~ Run toolbox: ~~~ toolbox ~~~ **Note:** If the following error is encountered when starting the toolbox: ~~~ Error: cannot find the value of label: RUN in image: docker.io/fedora:latest ~~~ then see bug [Bug 2048789- broken toolbox in OCP 4.10 with non-default image](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2048789). Verify that this is really a fedora toolbox: ~~~ [root@toolbox /]# cat /etc/fedora-release Fedora release 33 (Thirty Three) ~~~ Get available OVS versions: ~~~ [root@toolbox /]# yum provides '*ovs-tcpdump' Fedora 33 openh264 (From Cisco)- x86_64 1.9 kB/s | 2.5 kB 00:01 Fedora Modular 33- x86_64 3.8 MB/s | 3.3 MB 00:00 Fedora Modular 33- x86_64- Updates 1.4 MB/s | 1.0 MB 00:00 Fedora 33- x86_64- Updates 13 MB/s | 12 MB 00:00 Fedora 33- x86_64 20 MB/s | 72 MB 00:03 openvswitch-test-2.13.0-2.fc33.noarch: Open vSwitch testing utilities Repo: fedora Matched from: Other: *ovs-tcpdump openvswitch-test-2.14.0-2.fc33.noarch: Open vSwitch testing utilities Repo: updates Matched from: Other: *ovs-tcpdump ~~~ **Note:** The version of fedora may need to be changed to get the desired version of openvswitch-test. Install the correct version of openvswitch-test: ~~~ yum install openvswitch-test-2.13.0-2.fc33.noarch-y yum install tcpdump-y ~~~ Now, run ovs-tcpdump. For example, to dump on all tunnel ports: ~~~ tunnel_ports=$(ovs-vsctl show | grep geneve-B2 | awk '/Port/ {print $NF}') echo $tunnel_ports ~~~ Pick one of the ports and run: ~~~ port=ovn-a58080-0; ovs-tcpdump-w /host/var/tmp/$port.pcap-i $port '((tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn)!= 0) or (tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) == (tcp-syn|tcp-ack)) or (tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst)!= 0))' ~~~ > One can only run a single ovs-tcpdump at the same time ### How to run a long-running tcpdump Create the `ovs-tcpdump-ds` DaemonSet. Adjust INTERFACE, FILTER_EXPRESSION, ADDITIONAL_TCPDUMP_CLI_OPTIONS as needed. `ovs-tcpdump` can only work on one interface simultaneously. ~~~ cat < <'EOF' > fedora-ovs-tcpdump-ds.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: fedora-ovs-tcpdump-scripts data: entrypoint.sh: | #!/bin/bash yum install procps-ng-y yum install iproute-y yum install tcpdump-y yum install openvswitch-test-${OVS_VERSION}-y DATE=$(date +%s) ovs-tcpdump--db-sock unix:/host//var/run/openvswitch/db.sock ${ADDITIONAL_TCPDUMP_CLI_OPTIONS}-i ${INTERFACE}-w /host/var/tmp/${INTERFACE}.${DATE}.pcap "${FILTER_EXPRESSION}"--- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: DaemonSet metadata: name: fedora-ovs-tcpdump spec: selector: matchLabels: name: fedora-ovs-tcpdump template: metadata: labels: name: fedora-ovs-tcpdump spec: nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/hostname: ip-10-0-146-183 hostNetwork: true containers:- name: fedora-ovs-tcpdump env:- name: OVS_VERSION value: "2.13.0"- name: INTERFACE value: "ovn-a58080-0"- name: FILTER_EXPRESSION value: "icmp"- name: ADDITIONAL_TCPDUMP_CLI_OPTIONS value: "-s0-Z root-C 1G-W 10" image: docker.io/fedora:33 command:- bash- /scripts/entrypoint.sh volumeMounts:- name: scripts mountPath: /scripts- name: hp mountPath: /host- name: dev mountPath: /dev securityContext: privileged: true runAsUser: 0 volumes:- name: scripts configMap: name: fedora-ovs-tcpdump-scripts- name: hp hostPath: path: /- name: dev hostPath: path: /dev EOF ~~~ ~~~ oc new-project ovs-tcpdump oc adm policy add-scc-to-user privileged-z default oc apply-f fedora-ovs-tcpdump-ds.yaml ~~~ Check the logs. Installation of dependencies will take a while. At some point, tcpdump will start and run: ~~~ oc logs-f-l name=fedora-ovs-tcpdump ~~~ Once done, delete the DaemonSet: ~~~ $ oc delete daemonset fedora-ovs-tcpdump ~~~ It's possible to copy the packet capture from the node's /var/tmp. Repeat this for all files which were created by the command: ~~~ oc debug node/my-cluster-node-- bash-c 'cat /host/var/tmp/my-tcpdump-capture-file.pcap' > /tmp/my-tcpdump-capture-file.pcap ~~~ Make sure to clean up /var/tmp afterwards and remove all packet capture files.

title: How to set umask permanently for OpenShift pods?
issue: - There is the bug 2040612 the crio umask sometimes set to 0000 where users run umask on Console or on 'oc rsh'.
resolution: - The [bug 2040612](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2040612) is working in progress.- Configuring Umask for crio.service would be a good workaround like the following. *** Workaround ***- Create a file. ~~~ # vim override.conf [Service] UMask=0021 ~~~- Encode the file content. ~~~ # cat override.conf | base64 W1NlcnZpY2VdClVNYXNrPTAwMjEK ~~~- Create a config file. ~~~ # vim 99-workers-crio-configuration.yaml apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-workers-crio-configuration spec: config: ignition: config: {} security: tls: {} timeouts: {} version: 3.2.0 networkd: {} passwd: {} storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,W1NlcnZpY2VdClVNYXNrPTAwMjEK mode: 420 overwrite: true path: /etc/systemd/system/crio.service.d/override.conf osImageURL: "" ~~~- Apply the config. ~~~ # oc apply-f 99-workers-crio-configuration.yaml ~~~

title: Logs not visible on `kibana dashboard`

title: Operator deployed through OLM deployed to different versions
issue: - While deploying Dell CSI Operator Certified to various cluster with a manual subscription, noticed different versions of the CSV. For older installations, the operator is in version 1.6.0 after approving the upgrade (or still in version 1.5.0 with waiting for approval), while for the newer installations the latest versions the operator deployed is 1.5.0 (and no further upgrade possible).- Could it be possible that the vendor released at some point temporary version 1.6.0 and then removed it and that's why we managed to upgrade our older installations. If so, why in some clusters with older installations we see version 1.5.0 and version 1.6.0 available, while in newer ones not?- There is also Dell CSI Operator community which has indeed version 1.6.0 as the latest one. Could it also be that the older installations are pointing wrongly to the community operator?
resolution: - There are specific ceiling-level versions of the Dell CSI operator that correspond to specific OpenShift versions. The certified 1.6.0 version is restricted to OpenShift versions 4.8 and 4.9 only.- There was a situation at one point where 1.6.0 was incorrectly pushed to older OperatorHubs, and was subsequently removed. Sounds like you updated during that window when 1.6.0 was available in older OperatorHubs.

title: Authorization error when backing up/restoring using OADP (Velero)
issue: When using Velero from the OADP operator, backups as well as restorations throw an authorization error: ~~~ Error backing up item" backup=$PV_NAME error="error getting volume info: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = azure.BearerAuthorizer#WithAuthorization: Failed to refresh the Token for request to https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION/resourceGroups/$RESOURCE_GROUP/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/$DISK_NAME?api-version=2019-07-01: StatusCode=400-- Original Error: adal: Refresh request failed. Status Code = '400'. Response body: {\"error\":\"unauthorized_client\",\"error_description\":\"AADSTS700016: Application with identifier '$APP_ID' was not found in the directory '$DIRECTORY_NAME'. This can happen if the application has not been installed by the administrator of the tenant or consented to by any user in the tenant. You may have sent your authentication request to the wrong tenant. ~~~
resolution: Set the correct client ID inside the `cloud-credentials-azure` `Secret`, ten redeploy Velero: 1. Extract the `cloud-credentials-azure` `Secret`: ~~~ $ oc extract-n openshift-adp secret/cloud-credentials-azure ~~~ 2. Edit the file and set the correct `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`: ~~~ $ vi cloud-credentials-azure ~~~ 3. Store the new `Secret`: ~~~ $ oc set data-n openshift-adp secret/cloud-credentials-azure--from-file=cloud=cloud-credentials-azure ~~~ 4. Delete the velero `Pod` as well as the controller 5. Wait for Velero to redeploy
root_cause: The client ID for the Service Principal doesn't match the `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` configured within Velero

title: How to Increase the log level of the Machine API Controllers
issue: - To better troubleshoot the Machine API Controller, how can the log level of the Machine API Controllers be increased?- Can the verbosity of the Machine API Controllers or their cloud actuators be changed? **NOTE: This should not be performed without the request of a Red Hat OpenShift Support Engineer and will result in the OpenShift Cluster in an unsupported state**
resolution: ### To deploy the changes: 1) Configure the Machine API Operator to no longer be managed by the Cluster Version Operator ~~~ openshift|⇒ oc edit clusterversion version... overrides:- group: apps kind: Deployment name: machine-api-operator namespace: openshift-machine-api unmanaged: true ~~~ 2) Scale down the MachineAPI Operator Deployment ~~~ openshift|⇒ oc scale deploy-n openshift-machine-api machine-api-operator--replicas 0 openshift|⇒ oc get deploy-n openshift-machine-api machine-api-operator NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE machine-api-operator 0/0 0 0 3d2h ~~~ 3) Set the `--v` option to a value between 1 to 10. 10 is the highest level of logging. * **NOTE:** There are 5 containers that all require the `--v` value to be increased.* ~~~ openshift|⇒ oc edit deploy machine-api-controllers... containers:- args:...---v=10 …- args:...---v=10 ~~~ 4) Wait for the new machine controller Pod to be deployed **NOTE: This change MUST be reverted before any cluster updates are performed** ### To roll-back the changes: 1) Scale up the Machine API Operator ~~~ openshift|⇒ oc scale deploy-n openshift-machine-api machine-api-operator--replicas 1 deployment.apps/machine-api-operator scaled openshift|⇒ oc get deploy-n openshift-machine-api machine-api-operator NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE machine-api-operator 1/1 1 1 3d2h ~~~ 2) Ensure the Cluster Version Operator is configured to manage the Machine API Operator. ~~~ openshift|⇒ oc edit clusterversion version... overrides: [] ~~~ 3) Wait for the Cluster Version Operator to reconcile the cluster objects into the expected managed state.
root_cause: The Cluster Version Operator (CVO) manages all ClusterOperator deployments within OpenShift and is responsible for ClusterOperator upgrades during an OpenShift upgrade. The CVO can be configured to exclude resources from it management list using the ClusterVersion resource. The `clusterversion.spec.overrides` list allows the ability to specify resources that are included in the OpenShift management but should be temporarily excluded for testing purposes.

title: CLI command to update AMQ Streams Operator version
issue: What's the CLI command to update AMQ Streams Operator version?
resolution: In OperatorHub, an opeartor will be version up by updating a channel. With the following command, you can update a channel by CLI. ~~~ # If necessary, please replace namespace and channel names with yours $ oc patch Subscription/amq-streams-n openshift-operators--type merge-p '{"spec":{"channel": "amq-streams-1.XXX.x"}}' ~~~ With Manual Approval, addtional commands are required too. ~~~ $ oc get installplan--all-namespaces NAME CSV APPROVAL APPROVED install-jw86l amqstreams.v1.8.0 Manual false install-rk5sk amqstreams.v1.7.3 Manual true # If necessary, please replace namespace and channel names with yours oc patch installplan install-jw86l-n openshift-operators--type merge-p '{"spec":{"approved":true}}' ~~~

title: Gracefull Shutdown of the cluster may destroy master nodes before workers
issue: - In the Openshift documentation The for loop to shutdown the cluster may destroy all the master nodes before the worker nodes
resolution: 1- Mark the control plane nodes in the cluster as unschedulable: ~~~ for node in $(oc get nodes-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do echo ${node}; oc adm cordon ${node}; done ~~~ 2- Shutdown worker nodes: [NOTE: Please make sure **Master** is not schedulable, else this command will shutdown master node also.] ~~~ for node in $(oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/worker-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do oc debug node/${node}-- chroot /host shutdown-h 1; done ~~~ 3- Wait until all the worker nodes are down: 4- Shutdown master nodes: ~~~ for node in $(oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/master-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do oc debug node/${node}-- chroot /host shutdown-h 1; done ~~~
root_cause: - The order of the node shutdown should be worker nodes and then master nodes.- Red Hat knows about this issue and it was tracked under [Bug 2076315](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2076315 "Bug 2076315")- Please contact Technical Support for more information.

title: Is it supported to use egress NetworkPolicy objects in OpenShift Container Platform
issue: Since Kubernetes 1.12, the use of the *egress
NetworkPolicy object is GA. Is it supported to use it in OpenShift?
resolution: * Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.x and up to 4.9 with [`OpenShiftSDN`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/openshift_sdn/about-openshift-sdn.html) as Software Defined Network (SDN) CNI network provider does not have support for `egress` type `NetworkPolicy`. Instead, [`EgressNetworkPolicy`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/openshift_sdn/configuring-egress-firewall.html#nw-egressnetworkpolicy-object_openshift-sdn-egress-firewall) can be used to manage outgoing traffic. * Starting with [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.10](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/release_notes/ocp-4-10-release-notes.html#ocp-4-10-openshift-sdn-netpol-egress-policies), support for `egress` policies and `ipBlock.except` was added to [`OpenShiftSDN`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/openshift_sdn/about-openshift-sdn.html). * Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 with [`OVN-Kubernetes`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/networking/ovn_kubernetes_network_provider/about-ovn-kubernetes.html) SDN CNI network provider has support for `egress` type `NetworkPolicy` and can properly apply the rules defined.

title: How to tell whether a networkpolicy rule is dropping traffic
issue: - Packets are reaching the `vxlan_sys_4789` interface on node, but cannot tell if they are reaching the pod.- We are seeing `SYN` packets but no `SYN ACK` response.- How to determine if NetworkPolicy rule is causing packets to be dropped?
resolution: If NetworkPolicy is dropping the packets, this can be seen in the openflow rules. Note the packet drops on table 80: ~~~ // Table 80: NetworkPolicy ingress rule enforcement // rules implementing NetworkPolicy and Multitenant isolation // accepted traffic is output to the port in reg2 cookie=0x0, duration=55451.644s, table=80, n_packets=1452, n_bytes=107448, priority=0 actions=drop ~~~ Where `n_packets` shows the number of dropped packets.

title: How to configure antiAffinity in AMQ-Broker 7.10
issue: While configuring anti-affinity as described in the document [link](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/ko-kr/red_hat_amq_broker/7.10/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#assembly-br-controlling-pod-placement-using-affinity-rules_broker-ocp) gets following error ~~~ Error "Invalid value: "object": spec.deploymentPlan.affinity.podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution in body must be of type array: "object"" for field "spec.deploymentPlan.affinity.podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution". ~~~
resolution: Kindly update the affinity section in the deployment plan for the broker deployment as below: ~~~ affinity: podAntiAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:- labelSelector: matchExpressions:- key: name operator: In values:- broker1 topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone ~~~ This will help to create the pod successfully **Note:** topologyKey can have values like topology.kubernetes.io/zone or kubernetes.io/hostname
root_cause: [ENTMQBR-6788](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ENTMQBR-6788) documentation jira is created for this issue.

title: Change admin password in Ansible Automation Platform Operator for OpenShift
issue: - How to change the password for the admin user after installing Ansible Automation Platform Controller in OpenShift?- The password in the secret-admin-password has been changed, but it does not work to login
resolution: - The secret stored in the `ansible-automation-platform` namespace called `-admin-password` is only used to store the password. It is not used for authentication.- To change the admin password for Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform Controller, login to the controller as admin using the password provided/created at installation.- Then, in the upper-right corner, click on the `admin` user, then `User Details`, and then click the blue `Edit` button.- Type the desired password in the `Password` and `Confirm Password` boxes and click `Save`- The password stored in the `-admin-password` secret is now invalid. The secret can be updated or deleted as it is not required for proper functioning.
root_cause: - The `-admin-password` secret is not used for authentication.- The secret is only used to store the password that was configured during installation.

title: OCS nodes of OpenShift cluster not showing in Customer Portal under subscription section
issue: - Unable to see nodes of newly deployed OCP clusters (running over RHV infrastructure, deployed with IPI installation) in Red Hat Customer Portal under Subscription section- Should OCS nodes appear in RHSM on customer portal?
resolution: - RHCOS do not have provision to register with RHSM, as it is built from image. Hence, the cluster nodes will not be displayed in Red Hat Customer Portal under Subscription section- From OpenShift 4 onward, the subscriptions are associated to a cluster as a whole and not to individual nodes. This can be seen and controlled from Red Hat OpenShift Cluster Manager (OCM). Refer below KCS article for more details:- [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6429761](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6429761)

title: How to restrict access to a custom path in a specific route in  RHOCP 4
issue: - Need to restrict access to the custom paths in a specific route based on the source ip addresses.
resolution: In this example the application is having two custom path's- test.test.app.example.com ==> route hostname- test.test.app.example.com/test ==> custom path supposed to be restricted- test.test.app.example.com/second ==> another custom path without any restriction [1] Create a route for the application ~~~ $ oc expose svc--hostname test.test.app.example.com ~~~ [2] Export the yaml of aforementioned route ~~~ $ oc get route-o yaml > route.yaml ~~~ [3] Create another route with different name from above "route.yaml" file with same hostname for custom path "/test" ~~~ apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1 kind: Route metadata: name: namespace: spec: host: test.test.app.example.com path: /test port: targetPort: to: kind: Service name: ~~~ [4] Give the access to the above route to only required ip addresses/network using the annotation haproxy.router.openshift.io/ip_whitelist ~~~ $ oc annotate route haproxy.router.openshift.io/ip_whitelist="x.x.x.x x.x.x.x" ~~~ After performing above step's the custom path "/test" will be only accessible by the whitelisted source ip's and another custom path "/second" and base url will be accessible to all.

title: Functional level issues for Jenkins deployed on RHOCP
issue: - Functionality level issues with the deployment of `Jenkins` as a containerized environment or any other way of deployment not done with the help of native `Jenkins` operator as provided by the Red Hat OperatorHub catalog.- Example:- Roles and Permission option not reflected in `Jenkins` GUI.- Plugin is not getting installed on `Jenkins`.
resolution: - Upon confirmation from Red Hat about the **issue not being within the scope of the RHOCP support**, connect to the `Jenkins` vendor or with the authorities who have helped in getting the `Jenkins` deployment done to get the relevant support as the intended integration or customization of `Jenkins` and plugins are beyond the scope of Red Hat Support.- Red Hat **does not possess any private registry or update center** for `Jenkins` plugins as **Red Hat officially does not distribute the plugins** or resources required to achieve the functionality.- It should be noted that any `Jenkins` deployment even with the certified operator is not liable to avail support for the entire component.

title: Failed to scale up worker node
issue: `Scale up of worker node` failed when trying to add the node after `deleting the node` and uninstalling it.
resolution: - Delete the worker node which failed to join the cluster. ~~~ # oc delete node ~~~- Run the [uninstall node](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install/uninstalling_cluster.html#uninstalling-nodes) playbook to remove the node.- Reboot the worker node.- Run the [node scaleup](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/manage_nodes.html#adding-cluster-hosts_manage-nodes) playbook again.
root_cause: - `Uninstall node` playbook didn't complete successfully.

title: Kube-api server pods not starting up and showing certificate errors
issue: - Openshift-kube-apiserver pods are in unhealthy status with certificate errors- Replacing API-server certificates
resolution: - Create the secret including the key and custom certificate in the 'openshift-config' namepsace
root_cause: - The openshift-kube-apiserver pods refernces the secrets from the 'openshift-config' namepsace, missing of the custom secrets in the mentioned namespace will block the openshift-kube-apiserver rollout with the new changes.- There is a more detailed documentation [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/security/certificates/api-server.html "here")

title: Restored PVC stuck in pending
issue: - While restoring a snapshoted PV with external CSI ODF, PVC gets stuck in pending status.
resolution: Bug report has been opened against this scenario under Jira [OADP-603](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OADP-603) As a workaround, patch the restored pending PVC with `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com` annotation. This will bound the PVC to its PV.

resolution: Bug report has been opened against this scenario under Jira [OADP-603](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OADP-603) As a workaround, patch the restored pending PVC with `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com` annotation. title: How to enable login success and failure logs in OpenShift 3?
issue: - How to enable login attempts, success and failure logs in OpenShift 3.11?
resolution: - Change `DEBUG_LOGLEVEL=4` in `/etc/origin/master/master.env` on all master nodes and restart the master API by the `master-restart api` command.- Refer to the procedure in the documentation section [Configuring Logging Levels](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/master_node_configuration.html#master-node-config-logging-levels) to change the log level.- The `DEBUG_LOGLEVEL=4` enables master API access logging and it includes the login logs. ~~~ basicauth.go:51] Login with provider "htpasswd_auth" failed for login "user" basicauth.go:54] Login with provider "htpasswd_auth" succeeded for login "user": &user.DefaultInfo{Name:"user", UID:"xxx-xxx-xxx-xxx", Groups:[]string(nil), Extra:map[string][]string(nil)} ~~~ There are some other login related logs in Audit logging too, see [Audit logging message examples in OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4706261) for details.
root_cause: The default is `DEBUG_LOGLEVEL=2` and it suppresses the login logs.

title: Caused by: java.nio.file.FileSystemException: /cassandra_data/commitlog/CommitLog-6-xxxxxxxx.log: No space left on device
issue: - Cassandra pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state due to space issues. ~~~ Caused by: java.nio.file.FileSystemException: /cassandra_data/commitlog/CommitLog-6-xxxxxxxx.log: No space left on device ~~~- How to remove old data from Cassandra PV?- What data can be deleted from Crassandra volume to make some space.
resolution: - Under the `commitlog` directory Cassandra stores the Commitlogs. Commitlogs are an append only log of all mutations local to a Cassandra node. Any data written to Cassandra will first be written to a commit log before being written to a memtable. This provides durability in the case of an unexpected shutdown. On startup, any mutations in the commit log will be applied to memtables.- We can delete the old `commitlog`. ~~~ $ oc rsh sh-4.2$ ls-la /cassandra_data/commitlog sh-4.2$ rm-rf /cassandra_data/commitlog/CommitLog-6-xxxxxxx.log ~~~

title: Bundle unpacking failed due to file size limit exceeded error

title: NBG 994: Intermittently delayed VM deployment times for VMs hosted on computes in AZ5
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? on an intermittent basis, instances deployed against computes in AZ5 can take between 30 mins to 1 hour to completely deploy. VMs will deploy rapidly in the other 4 AZs with no delay. Please find 2x sosreports for the RHOSP controller and a compute...note that the logs were collected after reproducing the issue for a VM with this uuid 7c13879c-f7d2-4170-9685-95068c3400e3. What is the business impact? Please also provide timeframe information. now blocking validation progress in the lab. When does the behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times? on an intermittent basis, instances deployed against computes in AZ5 can take between 30 mins to 1 hour to completely deploy. VMs will deploy rapidly in the other 4 AZs with no delay. The following observations were made:
resolution: Hi Dave! Details of the issue with the fabric leading to the behavior seen with the delayed VM instantiation is listed below: Root Cause: There were four uplinks on Rack5 that were carrying traffic during the provisioning. The ECMP load balancing was used on the QFX5110 (ToR) on per flow basis across all four links. Out of these four uplinks, one of the link had physical issue and it was dropping frames due to CRC erros on the link. So any flow that was hashed on this faulty link, gets request timeout due to loss of frames. Workaround: Disable the faulty link, which automatically shift all traffic flows on the remaining 3 links. Solution: Possible physical issue- a) Dirty fibre b) QSFP gone faulty Logs: ~~~ auto@spine001> show interfaces et-0/0/51 extensive | match errors Input errors: Errors: 392039, Drops: 0, Framing errors: 392039, Runts: 0, Policed discards: 0, L3 incompletes: 0, L2 channel errors: 0, L2 mismatch timeouts: 0, CRC/Align errors 392039 ~~~

title: KubeAPIDown alert NOT firing
issue: don't get alerts for API down in Prometheus when you scale down one master node
resolution: KubeAPIDown alert NOT firing. this is correct because, as I explained in my previous message if you scale down one master node, the API is still available because of the redundancy of master nodes. There is a load balancer in front of the master nodes which exposes only one address/endpoint for the API server, and that remains available even if one member of the control plane (3 machines) is down. For this reason you don't get alerts for API down in Prometheus.

title: How to enable debug logging istiod?
issue: - Istiod is the unified control plane responsible for configuring Envoy proxies in a cluster and sometimes need to take a look if something wrong.
resolution: - Backup the deployment of istiod-basic before make changes. ~~~ # oc get deployment istiod-basic-n istio-system-o yaml > istiod-basic.yaml ~~~- Change log output level ~~~ # oc edit deployment istiod-basic-n istio-system spec: containers:- args:- discovery---monitoringAddr=:15014---log_output_level=default:debug---domain- cluster.local---keepaliveMaxServerConnectionAge- 30m ~~~- The istiod pods will rollout with new ones with debug level.

title: Setting RWX volumes permission  in Red Hat OpenShift Dedicated
issue: - Is it possible/supported to set `VolumePermission` to `RWX` in Red Hat OpenShift Dedicated cluster environment
resolution: It is not supported to change the volume permission to `RWX` for the OSD environment. In `theory` if as a workaround, create an EFS volume in another AWS account and access it from OSD, then there are chances to mount a block volume into a `POD` and have the pod run an `NFS` server. `Note`: As the above workaround is not tried and tested in an OSD environment this use case would likely be fragile.
root_cause: AWS does not allow you to do RWX across storage blocks.

title: Cluster Logging for CloudWatch not working with ROSA  STS Clusters
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Cluster Logging for CloudWatch not working with ROSA STS Clusters.- Correct way to install ClusterLogging.- Documentation for logging (add-on) configuration is incomplete.
resolution: Currently, ROSA clusters installed using the Security Token Service (STS) workflow do not have the ability to create the long-lived IAM credentials necessary for the Logging add-on to properly authenticate with AWS CloudWatch. Refer to the [knowledge base solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6485391), which mentions Using the CloudWatch Logging add-on with ROSA STS Clusters. It states [Work Around to fix the issue with the logging-addon on ROSA STS Clusters](https://mobb.ninja/docs/rosa/sts-cluster-logging-addon/)

If the customer wants to install the full OpenShift Logging Operator in ROSA (and not forward logs to CloudWatch), they need to uninstall the Logging Add-on and install the OpenShift Logging Operator following the [Installing the logging subsystem for Red Hat OpenShift](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/logging/cluster-logging-deploying.html)

issue: - Installation of `ServiceMesh` operator failing with the message: ~~~ Failed to install Operator servicemeshoperator.v2.1.0 version 2.1.0-0. resolution: - Clean up the previous `ServiceMesh` installation and reinstall it again.- Follow the below [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/service_mesh/v2x/removing-ossm.html) to remove the `ServiceMesh` operator.- In case the deletion of `CRD` fails due to any `finalizers` present in them, remove the `finalizers` using the below command: ~~~ $ oc patch crd/servicemeshcontrolplanes.maistra.io-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge $ oc patch crd/servicemeshmemberrolls.maistra.io-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge ~~~

title: Configuring Hugepages on master nodes for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - Configuring hugepages supported on the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?- Is it possible/supported to configure Hugepages on master nodes for the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?
resolution: - It is supported to configure Hugepages on the OCP nodes, but they should be configured specifically to the compute nodes.- The main function of enabling the huge pages on the OCP environment is that the Memory is managed in blocks known as pages. On most systems, a page is `4Ki`. `1Mi` of memory is equal to `256` pages;` 1Gi` of memory is `256,000` pages, and so on. CPUs have a built-in memory management unit that manages a list of these pages in hardware. The Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) is a small hardware cache of virtual-to-physical page mappings. If the virtual address passed in a hardware instruction can be found in the TLB, the mapping can be determined quickly. If not, a TLB miss occurs, and the system falls back to slower, software-based address translation, resulting in performance issues. Since the size of the TLB is fixed, the only way to reduce the chance of a TLB miss is to increase the page size.- A huge page is a memory page that is larger than 4Ki. On x86_64 architectures, there are two common huge page sizes: 2Mi and 1Gi. Sizes vary on other architectures. Nodes must pre-allocate huge pages used in an OpenShift Container Platform cluster. There are two ways of reserving huge pages: at boot time and at run time. Reserving at boot time increases the possibility of success because the memory has not yet been significantly fragmented. The Node Tuning Operator currently supports boot time allocation of huge pages on specific nodes.- Enabling the huge pages would be useful for the worker nodes, as the worker nodes are running the application workloads.- To have more information refer [What huge pages do and how they are consumed by applications](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/scalability_and_performance/what-huge-pages-do-and-how-they-are-consumed-by-apps.html)
root_cause: - Enabling the huge pages for the master nodes would not be useful as the master nodes are not designed to run the application workloads, they have the responsibility to run the default openshift components to achieve `high availability` and to meet the `API calls/request`, maintain `etcd quorum`, etc.

title: Adding worker nodes using the on-premises Assisted Installer REST API
issue: You can add worker nodes to clusters using the Assisted Installer REST API that you deploy in your on-premises environment. **IMPORTANT: On-premises Assisted Installer REST API deployments are not supported by Red Hat.*
For more information, review our official documentation.
resolution: 1. Set the `$API_URL` variable by running the following command: $ export API_URL= where: **` `** is the Assisted Installer API URL, for example, `https://api.on-prem-example.openshift.com` 2. Set the `$CLUSTER_ID` variable and change the cluster status from `installed` to `adding-hosts` by running the following commands: 1. Optional. Get the list of Assisted Installer managed cluster IDs: $ curl-s $API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters | jq-r '.[].id' **Example output** "58cf54c9-b568-4b59-a673-5857d12dd204" "733411ad-0b47-4633-83ab-ded5fcdb7a98" "84bdd5d1-ebeb-4ebe-ad35-b5336dccf36f" "0942b997-672a-4258-a233-a1564bfc4cc7" 2. Set the `$CLUSTER_ID` variable using the Assisted Installer cluster ID for the Day 1 cluster that you want to add the worker to, for example: $ CLUSTER_ID= where: **` `** is the cluster ID from the previous step. 3. Change the cluster status to `adding-hosts` by running the following command: $ curl-X POST-s "$API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID/actions/allow-add-workers" The cluster status must have a status of `installed` before it can be changed to `adding-hosts`. 3. Set the `$INFRA_ENV_ID` variable with the ID of the Day 1 `InfraEnv` resource. You can use the ID of one of the existing hosts in the cluster, for example: $ INFRA_ENV_ID=$(curl-X GET-s "$API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" | jq-r ".hosts[0].infra_env_id") 4. Get the URL of the discovery ISO for the cluster worker node by running the following command: $ curl-s "$API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/infra-envs/$INFRA_ENV_ID" | jq-r '.download_url' **Example output** https://api.on-prem-example.openshift.com/api/assisted-images/images/41b91e72-c33e-42ee-b80f-b5c5bbf6431a?arch=x86_64&image_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJleHAiOjE2NTYwMjYzNzEsInN1YiI6IjQxYjkxZTcyLWMzM2UtNDJlZS1iODBmLWI1YzViYmY2NDMxYSJ9.1EX_VGaMNejMhrAvVRBS7PDPIQtbOOc8LtG8OukE1a4&type=minimal-iso&version=4.11 5. Download the ISO: $ curl-L-s--output rhcos-live-minimal.iso where: **` `** is the URL for the ISO from the previous step. 6. Boot the new worker host from the downloaded `rhcos-live-minimal.iso`. 7. Get the list of hosts in the cluster that are *not* installed. Keep running the following command until the new host shows up: $ curl-s "$API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" | jq-r '.hosts[] | select(.status!= "installed").id' **Example output** 2294ba03-c264-4f11-ac08-2f1bb2f8c296 8. Set the `$HOST_ID` variable for the new worker node, for example: $ HOST_ID= where: **` `** is the host ID from the previous step. 9. Check that the host is ready to install by running the following command: **NOTE:** Ensure that you copy the entire command including the complete `jq` expression. $ curl-s $API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID | jq ' def host_name($host): if (.suggested_hostname // "") == "" then if (.inventory // "") == "" then "Unknown hostname, please wait" else.inventory | fromjson |.hostname end else.suggested_hostname end; def is_notable($validation): ["failure", "pending", "error"] | any(. == $validation.status); def notable_validations($validations_info): [$validations_info // "{}" | fromjson | to_entries[].value[] | select(is_notable(.))]; {"Hosts validations": {"Hosts": [.hosts[] | select(.status!= "installed") | {"id":.id, "name": host_name(.), "status":.status, "notable_validations": notable_validations(.validations_info)}]}, "Cluster validations info": {"notable_validations": notable_validations(.validations_info)}} '-r **Example output** {"Hosts validations": {"Hosts": [{"id": "97ec378c-3568-460c-bc22-df54534ff08f", "name": "localhost.localdomain", "status": "insufficient", "notable_validations": [{"id": "ntp-synced", "status": "failure", "message": "Host couldn't synchronize with any NTP server"}, {"id": "api-domain-name-resolved-correctly", "status": "error", "message": "Parse error for domain name resolutions result"}, {"id": "api-int-domain-name-resolved-correctly", "status": "error", "message": "Parse error for domain name resolutions result"}, {"id": "apps-domain-name-resolved-correctly", "status": "error", "message": "Parse error for domain name resolutions result"}]}]}, "Cluster validations info": {"notable_validations": []}} 10. When the previous command shows that the host is ready, trigger the installation using the [/v2/infra-envs/{infra_env_id}/hosts/{host_id}/actions/install](https://api.openshift.com/?urls.primaryName=assisted-service%20service#/installer/v2InstallHost) API by running the following command: $ curl-X POST-s "$API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/infra-envs/$INFRA_ENV_ID/hosts/$HOST_ID/actions/install" 11. As the installation proceeds, the installation generates pending certificate signing requests (CSRs) for the worker node. You must approve the CSRs to complete the installation. Keep running the following API call to monitor the cluster installation: $ curl-s "$API_URL/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" | jq '{"Cluster day-2 hosts": [.hosts[] | select(.status!= "installed") | {id, requested_hostname, status, status_info, progress, status_updated_at, updated_at, infra_env_id, cluster_id, created_at}]}' **Example output** {"Cluster day-2 hosts": [{"id": "a1c52dde-3432-4f59-b2ae-0a530c851480", "requested_hostname": "control-plane-1", "status": "added-to-existing-cluster", "status_info": "Host has rebooted and no further updates will be posted. Please check console for progress and to possibly approve pending CSRs", "progress": {"current_stage": "Done", "installation_percentage": 100, "stage_started_at": "2022-07-08T10:56:20.476Z", "stage_updated_at": "2022-07-08T10:56:20.476Z"}, "status_updated_at": "2022-07-08T10:56:20.476Z", "updated_at": "2022-07-08T10:57:15.306369Z", "infra_env_id": "b74ec0c3-d5b5-4717-a866-5b6854791bd3", "cluster_id": "8f721322-419d-4eed-aa5b-61b50ea586ae", "created_at": "2022-07-06T22:54:57.161614Z"}]} 12. Please check console for progress and to possibly approve pending CSRs)","event_time":"2022-07-08T11:29:48.259Z","host_id":"9d7b3b44-1125-4ad0-9b14-76550087b445"} {"severity":"info","message":"Host: compute-0, reached installation stage Rebooting","event_time":"2022-07-08T11:29:48.261Z","host_id":"9d7b3b44-1125-4ad0-9b14-76550087b445"} 13.
