title: How is Manila CSI supported on OpenShift 4?
issue: - I have enabled Manila shares on OpenStack and would like for OpenShift to use it, but dynamic provisioning is not working.- PVC keeps in pending status when selecting the Manila CSI StorageClass for dynamic provisioning.
resolution: OpenStack Manila supports many Network Attached Storage protocols such as NFS, CIFS and CEPHFS and these can be selectively enabled in the OpenStack cloud. The manila-csi-driver-operator in OpenShift only supports using the NFS protocol. If this is not available and enabled in the underlying OpenStack cloud, the manila-csi-driver cannot be used to provision storage for OpenShift. In Red Hat OpenStack Platform 16.1, the Shared File Systems service (manila) with CephFS through NFS fully supports serving shares to OpenShift Container Platform through Manila CSI. Be aware that this solution is not intended for massive scale. Be sure to review important recommendations at [6667651](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6667651) All these limitations are being covered in BZ [2070276](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2070276) and will be added into the official documentation.

title: [RHOCP 3.11] Basic items to review prior to upgrading a Red Hat OpenShift 3.11 cluster from v3.11.374 to v3.11.634 in a disconnected network environment
issue: - What should be verified prior to an RHOCP 3.11 minor version upgrade?
resolution: 1. Review relevant documentation and upgrade procedure available in the links below:- [OpenShift Container Platform 3.11.634 bug fix and security update](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/release_notes/ocp_3_11_release_notes.html#ocp-3-11-634) list;- [Performing automated in-place cluster upgrades](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/upgrading/automated_upgrades.html). 2. Is the cluster experiencing any stability issue, degraded API response? 3. Review `etcd`:- Review the [KCS 4770281](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4770281), that explains the_Backend Performance Requirements for OpenShift etcd_.- Current `etcd` status: ~~~ # etcdctl--cert-file=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key-file=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--ca-file=/etc/etcd/ca.crt--endpoints=$ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS member list 216352d7383b4345: name=node3.unix.test peerURLs=https://10.53.13.68:2380 clientURLs=https://10.53.13.68:2379 isLeader=false 53c12e0ecc0d36gg: name=node1.unix.test peerURLs=https://10.53.13.66:2380 clientURLs=https://10.53.13.66:2379 isLeader=false de5ac43fcc40af33: name=node2.unix.test peerURLs=https://10.53.13.67:2380 clientURLs=https://10.53.13.67:2379 isLeader=true # etcdctl--cert-file=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key-file=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--ca-file=/etc/etcd/ca.crt--endpoints=$ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS cluster-health member 216352d7383b4345 is healthy: got healthy result from https://10.54.13.68:2379 member 53c12e0ecc0d36gg is healthy: got healthy result from https://10.54.13.66:2379 member de5ac43fcc40af33 is healthy: got healthy result from https://10.54.13.67:2379 cluster is healthy ~~~ 4. Check the health of the cluster `nodes`. Do they have Status=Ready?: ~~~ # oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION node1.unix.test Ready compute 299d v1.11.0+d4cacc0 node2.unix.test Ready compute 299d v1.11.0+d4cacc0 node3.unix.test Ready compute 299d v1.11.0+d4cacc0 ~~~ 5. Are there any expired certificates? ~~~ $ oc get csr No resources found. $ oc get csr-o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve error: one or more CSRs must be specified as or-f ~~~ 6. Reach out to Red Hat support:- Open a Proactive Case by following the [KCS 3521621](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3521621); and once opened:- Upload your inventory file for analysis;- Upload the `sosreport` of your nodes. 7. During the upgrade process, run the upgrade playbooks by appending the `-vvv` flag. This will ensure that there will be extra verbose logs in the event of any playbook failures: ~~~ $ ansible-playbook-i playbooks/byo/openshift-cluster/upgrades/v3_11/upgrade.yml-vvv ~~~

title: Why restoring virtual machine snapshot is failing with error "admission webhook "datavolume-validate.cdi.kubevirt.io" denied the request: Source PVC namespace/pvc not found
issue: - While restoring the VM from the snapshot, it is failing with the error below: ~~~ Error creating DataVolume restore-26026078-f3a9-4884-902b-afc50332c75c-rhel8-vm: admission webhook "datavolume-validate.cdi.kubevirt.io" denied the request: Source PVC my-vm-ns/rhel8-vm not found ~~~- This VM was cloned and the source VM was deleted from the cluster. The PVC rhel8-vm belongs to the source VM which was deleted.
resolution: - This is a known bug [Cloned VM's snapshot restore fails if the source VM disk is deleted](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2104479).- If a VM is failing to start/restore because of the above bug, follow the steps below to restore the VM:- Find the PVC name of the restored volume: ~~~ # oc get vm rhel8-vm-clone-o yaml|yq-y '.spec.dataVolumeTemplates[0].metadata.name' restore-9cdf58e7-9be7-42d1-9d83-7a4a21dff2e7-rhel8-vm ~~~- Patch the vm object and change the source volume of`DataVolumeTemplate` value to refer to the existing PVC. ~~~ oc patch vm/rhel8-vm-clone-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/dataVolumeTemplates/0/spec/source/pvc/name", "value":"restore-9cdf58e7-9be7-42d1-9d83-7a4a21dff2e7-rhel8-vm"}]'--type=json ~~~ If there are multiple disks, `dataVolumeTemplates/0/` has to be replaced with the corresponding index number in the JSON array.- Start the virtual machine.
root_cause: - [Cloned VM's snapshot restore fails if the source VM disk is deleted](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2104479).- The DataVolumeTemplate value in the VirtualMachineSnapshotContent CR refers to the persistent volume claim (PVC) of the source VM that triggers the creation of a clone datavolume from a non existing source which is stuck waiting on the source PVC to be ready. Instead, the datavolume should be created and completed right away since the target PVC for the clone is already populated (from the `volumesnapshot`).

title: Jenkins changes for OCP 4.11
issue: OpenShift 4.11 brings significant changes to the way Jenkins is delivered to users. OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) 4.11 changes some details of how the OpenShift Jenkins image and OpenShift Agent Base image are provided to customers. In particular, rather than producing these images as part of the OCP install payloads, we are producing them as separate images under the ‘ocp-tools-4’ organization at ‘registry.redhat.io’.
resolution: This article intends to illustrate how the change in the image build pipeline only adds to or improves the current consumption by those who use the OpenShift Jenkins image and OpenShift Agent Base image today. These changes in how the OpenShift Jenkins images are built also take the next step with the 4.10 announcement of shifting our recommendation to using multiple container Pod Templates with the Jenkins Kubernetes Plug-in. The ‘maven’ and ‘nodejs’ Pod Templates were deprecated in 4.10. The next step in this journey is that the OpenShift Jenkins Maven and NodeJS Agent images from the OCP payload are now deprecated, and no such analogous images are being produced by the Red Hat Developer Tools organization, specifically in the ‘ocp-tools-4’ repository over at ‘registry.redhat.io’. **What stays the same with the OpenShift Jenkins Image?** The Cluster Samples Operator still manages the ImageStream and pod templates for operating the OpenShift Jenkins images. The default behavior of the Jenkins DeploymentConfig from the Jenkins Template will be to trigger a redeployment when the following occurs: The Jenkins image that is referenced by the “2” ImageStreamTag of the “jenkins” ImageStream in the “openshift” Namespace has changed in the ImageStream YAML included in the Samples Operator payload. The deprecated “maven” and “nodejs” pod templates are still present in the default image configuration for those who have upgraded from OCP 4.10 and earlier. If you have upgraded from OCP 4.10 and earlier, the “jenkins-agent-maven” and “jenkins-agent-nodejs” ImageStreams will still exist in your cluster. See below for information on maintaining these ImageStreams yourself if desired. **What changes are there with the support matrix of the OpenShift Jenkins image?** The new ‘ocp-tools-4’ image will be supported across multiple versions of OCP. Gone are the days of waiting for Engineering to port the latest Jenkins security advisories to the 4.10 OCP image, then the 4.9 image, then the 4.8 image, etc. We’ll update the active version once, and it will be compatible regardless of what supported version of OCP 4.x you are currently using. What additions are there with the OpenShift Jenkins and AgentBase ImageStreams and ImageStreamTags? So, moving away from an OCP “in-payload ImageStream” to an ImageStream referencing non-OCP payload images allows us to define as many ImageStreamTags as we want. We have thus created a series of new ImageStreamTags to go along with the existing “2” or ”latest” ImageStreamTag present in 4.10 and earlier. These new ImageStreamTags address some requests made to us in the past around how the Jenkins-related ImageStreams are maintained. **Let’s dive into those new ImageStreamTags:** “ocp-upgrade-redeploy” This ImageStreamTag happens to correspond to the existing “2” ImageStreamTag with the “jenkins” ImageStream and the “latest” ImageStreamTag of the “jenkins-agent-base” ImageStream. This tag will employ an Image tag specific to only one SHA or image digest, where engineering will update the Samples Operator payload when changes of note to the ‘ocp-tools-4’ image are made (typically the handling of Jenkins Security Advisories). Then, if you prefer to update your Jenkins image as part of OCP upgrades, you will still have that option. “user-maintained-upgrade-redeploy” This new ImageStreamTag will use the least specific Image version indicator available. As such, unless you manually run 'oc import-image jenkins:user-maintained-upgrade-redeploy-n openshift' to tell the OCP ImageStream controller to access ‘registry.redhat.io’ and store any updated images in the OCP Internal Image Registry’s slot for that Jenkins ImageStreamTag, then your Jenkins DeploymentConfig will not trigger a redeployment. Users who have asked that Jenkins not be redeployed on their OCP upgrades, but rather only redeploy when they want it to redeploy, will want to use this ImageStreamTag in their Jenkins DeploymentConfig. “scheduled-upgrade-redeploy” This new ImageStreamTag will use the periodic importing of image stream tags feature of the OCP ImageStreams controller and check for changes in the backing image. If the image has changed (i.e., we have pushed changes due to recent Jenkins Security Advisories), OCP will trigger a redeployment of your Jenkins DeploymentConfig. Users who have wanted OCP to automatically pull in the latest changes of the OpenShift Jenkins image when they are available will now have this option and be able to redeploy their Jenkins DeploymentConfig as soon as that image is made available. How to choose between these options? Simply update the ImageStreamTag name in your DeploymentConfig’s reference to cite the ImageStreamTag you want to use. For example, to switch to the “scheduled-upgrade-redeploy” tag, from the namespace hosting your “jenkins” DeploymentConfig, execute: ~~~ oc patch dc jenkins-p '{"spec":{"triggers":[{"type":"ImageChange","imageChangeParams":{"automatic":true,"containerNames":["jenkins"],"from":{"kind":"ImageStreamTag","namespace":"openshift","name":"jenkins:scheduled-upgrade-redeploy"}}}]}}' ~~~ You can also run ‘oc edit dc/jenkins-n ’ and then change “jenkins:2” to “jenkins:scheduled-upgrade-redploy” or whichever ImageStreamTag you want to employ. **What happens with the “jenkins-agent-maven” and “jenkins-agent-nodejs” ImageStreams in the “openshift” namespace** While the associated in-payload for the OpenShift Jenkins Maven and NodeJS Agent images are deprecated in 4.11, no longer included in the OpenShift install payload, and do not have alternatives defined ‘ocp-tools-4’, the ‘jenkins-agent-maven’ and ‘jenkins-agent-nodejs’ ImageStreams will still be created and maintained by the OpenShift Samples Operator, but they will point to the 4.10 tags of the respective OpenShift Payload images stored at ‘registry.redhat.io’ **To pull any updates from ‘registry.redhat.io’ to the jenkins-agent-nodejs ImageStream:** oc import-image jenkins-agent-nodejs-n openshift **To pull any updates from ‘registry.redhat.io’ to the jenkins-agent-maven ImageStream:** oc import-image jenkins-agent-maven-n openshift

title: OpenShift Vulnerabilities
issue: Red Hat is committed to providing secure, stable Enterprise-class products. While we strive to find and remove software vulnerabilities during the productization process, we recognize that vulnerabilities in software can be routinely found at any point in the [life cycle](https://access.redhat.com/product-life-cycles/update_policies), and we are prepared to respond when they are discovered.
resolution: **You should contact Red Hat Product Security if:**- You think there might be a security vulnerability in a Red Hat product or service.- You want to provide feedback about our standards of service and performance. If you feel your security concern is not dealt with in a satisfactory manner, please contact the customer service manager at customerservice@redhat.com.- More information about reporting vulnerabilities can be found on the [Security Contacts and Procedures](https://access.redhat.com/security/team/contact) page. **You should contact Red Hat Customer Experience & Engagement if:**- You are unsure about how a known vulnerability affects a Red Hat product or service.- You wish to report an issue in a language other than English.- You require technical assistance for a security function (for example, "How do I configure my firewall?").- You need help upgrading packages due to security alerts. (Refer to ["How do I apply package updates from the Red Hat Network?"](https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258) for information on upgrading packages.)- Your issue is not security related. *Customers are responsible for the security status of their environment. For requests not covered by Red Hat Product Security or Red Hat Customer Experience & Engagement teams, including reviewing penetration testing results or other security documents, consulting services may be offered.* **My product is listed as "Under investigation" or "Affected", when will Red Hat release a fix for this vulnerability?**- "Under investigation" doesn't necessarily mean that the product is affected by this vulnerability. It only means that our Analysis Team is still working on determining whether the product is affected and how it is affected.- "Affected" means that our Analysis Team has determined that this product is affected by this vulnerability and might release a fix to address this in the near future. **What can I do if my product is listed as "Will not fix"?**- This depends mostly on the Impact of the vulnerability and the Life Cycle phase in which your product is currently in. Overall, you have the following options:- Upgrade to a supported product version that includes a fix for this vulnerability (recommended)- Apply a mitigation (if one exists)-Open a support case to request a prioritization of releasing a fix for this vulnerability

title: Network operator in Degraded state after adding a new node to the cluster.
issue: - Scaling up a new node to the OCP cluster causes the Network operator to be in Degraded state.- The daemonset pod of multus-additional-cni-plugins is in Pending state. The init container of cni-plugins contains the following logs: ~~~ 2022-07-31T04:22:31.885743582Z cp: not writing through dangling symlink '/host/opt/cni/bin/bridge' 2022-07-31T04:22:32.022704380Z cp: not writing through dangling symlink '/host/opt/cni/bin/tuning' ~~~
resolution: - The issue has already been raised with the engineering team and is being tracked under the [OCPBUGS-64](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-64) Workaround: 1) In the node with an issue check if there is are files `bridge` and `tuning` present: ~~~ $ ls-la /var/lib/cni/bin/bridge $ ls-la /var/lib/cni/bin/tuning ~~~ 2) If the files are not present then copy those from a working node to /var/lib/cni/bin.

title: ROSA/OSD cluster ownership transfer
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Account ID attached to the ROSA/OSD Cluster needs to be transferred/migrated to new Account ID.- ROSA/OSD Cluster ownership need to transfer.- Transfer of ownership of an ROSA/OSD cluster to a different user in the same or different Organization.
resolution: ROSA/OSD Cluster owner is transferred with the help of Red Hat SRE Team. Please open a Red Hat [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new) with below details:- Current cluster owner's username and organization id.- New cluster owner's username and organization id to which the Cluster needs to be transferred.- Current Account ID to which the Cluster is attached.- New Account ID to which the Cluster needs to be transferred.

title: How does service loadbalancing work in Red Hat OpenShift?
issue: - How does the service loadbalancing work?- What is the difference between "service" and "route" based loadbalancing?- What does IPtables have to do with service loadbalancing?- What does the mode "random" mean?- What does "probability" mean?- Why are there different probability values for each entry in IPtables?
resolution: #### How does service loadbalancing work? Service loadbalancing within OpenShift is achieved by using_IPtables_ rules to send traffic to the corresponding backend pods of the given service. If the service is set to use `ClusterIP` there will be one ipaddress assigned to this service, which will act as entrypoint for every request. This request will be routed based on the_IPtables_ settings to the backend pods. #### What is the difference between "service" and "route" based loadbalancing? Although both approaches seem to do the same, the way of achieving it is different. As mentioned above `services` use IPtables functionality to route incoming traffic to the backend pods. A `route` uses the OpenShift ingress loadbalancer, which by default is_HAproxy_. This way also uses the dedicated ipaddresses of all corresponding backend pods, but instead of creating IPtables rules, an HAproxy config gets created. #### What does "random" and "probability" mean in the IPtables ruleset for a service? In general there are two ways of loadbalancing available in IPtables. `random` and `nth`. **OpenShift implements the `random` approach.** As the name `random` suggests, traffic is routed to the backends by using chances or probabilities for each entry in the IPtables ruleset. Every rule is given a `probability` which defines by what chance this rule gets applied or is skipped. If a rule is skipped, the next rule in sequence gets evaluated. This process happens until the last rule in the ruleset is reached. The last rule will always be applied._This process is based on the fact, that IPtables processes the defined rules in sequence from top to bottom._ #### Why are there different probability values for each entry in IPtables? Let's give an example. We define a service which has 10 backend pods. So we could assume that the `probability` for each entry should be 1 in 10. Or in numerical value: 0.1 But lets look at an actual IPtables ruleset for 10 backend pods: ~~~ sh-4.4# iptables-S KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-t nat-N KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-d 172.30.121.145/32!-i tun0-p tcp-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp cluster IP"-m tcp--dport 8080-j KUBE-MARK-MASQ-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.10000000009-j KUBE-SEP-G26LMC3E26D3C7CR-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.11111111101-j KUBE-SEP-WUSOG4BBZSARVKGR-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.12500000000-j KUBE-SEP-SI2DTJNIUEMNJHCV-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.14285714272-j KUBE-SEP-OTQCK6RW7RX5SYYO-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.16666666651-j KUBE-SEP-A2WSOVJ5M6U7TQVP-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.20000000019-j KUBE-SEP-CWGOXLOZW5F5ALGG-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.25000000000-j KUBE-SEP-MCLPEDMW55UWLQ3N-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.33333333349-j KUBE-SEP-YXGGYY7ZD7R2ICPB-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-m statistic--mode random--probability 0.50000000000-j KUBE-SEP-GW7TWONKBEXWORRM-A KUBE-SVC-IMNPEZOJ4UIL5CAK-m comment--comment "project-101/httpd:8080-tcp"-j KUBE-SEP-LWZKPEJ2EVGVSSD4 ~~~ We see `probability` values ranging from `--probability 0.10000000009` to `--probability 0.16666666651` and the second to last even states `--probability 0.50000000000`. To understand these values we have to keep in mind, that IPtables rulesets are processed in sequence from top to bottom. So with our example of 10 backend pods, the_first_ rule should only be applied in 1 of 10 cases. Since there are 10 possible backends available. The_second_ rule already has a higher probability of being applied, since it is now a member of a group of 9 rules to possibly apply. This goes on until we reach the_second to last_ rule. If processing came all the way to this rule, there are only 2 rules left. The current and the last one. So the_second to last_ rule should be applied with a 50:50 chance. Or 0.5 probability. The_last_ rule in the ruleset has no `probability` set, since this rule has to be applied anyway.
root_cause: Some additional information regarding this kind of loadbalancing can be found here:- [Turning IPTables into a TCP load balancer for fun and profit](https://scalingo.com/blog/iptables)- [kube-proxy iptables load-balancing probability is not equal](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/37932)

title: oc login  fail with error: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
issue: - Cannot login to an OCP 4.x OCP cluster with--insecure-skip-tls-verify=true from MacOS/Windows machines
resolution: Red Hat knows about this issue and it was tracked under [Bug 1880865](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1880865). Please contact Technical Support for more information.
root_cause: - The reason of the problem is that even if the user selects the option "--insecure-skip-tls-verify=true" oc makes a first https request to the cluster and tries to validate the certificate (this validation should not happen, as per the request of the user adding the option insecure-skip-tls-verify=true and this is actually the reason for this bug report).

title: How to restore cluster  from etcd DB backup when 2 out of the 3 Master nodes are down?
issue: - At least one Master node is working and others are down- Some master nodes keeps on rebooting- Can occur after a hard shutdown or even after graceful shutdown of nodes- A leftover container on master-01 and master-03, that was shutting down the node as soon as the node started- Container was programmed to run Command:[chroot /host shutdown-h now], now it keeps on shutting down nodes- A pod is stuck and it automatically reboots nodes ## Warning- This process should be done only in presence of RedHat technical support.- This KCS is specifically for the case where at least one master node working and one of the pods automatically shutting down 2 other master nodes and there no way to turn them on.- It is not recommended to use **Command:[chroot /host shutdown-h now]*

using debug container because it can lead to similar situation. ## Logs It may take multiple reboots and tries, to collect right journalctl, and discover that there was a leftover container on master-01 and master-03, that was shutting down the node as soon as the node started. See: **Command:[chroot /host shutdown-h now]*

~~~ Mar 08 18:39:30 XX001 hyperkube[1655]: E0308 18:39:30.197365 1655 kuberuntime_manager.go:815] container &Container{Name:container-00,Image:registry.ocp.XX:5000/rhel8/support-tools:8.4-13,Command:[chroot /host shutdown-h now],Args:[],WorkingDir:,Ports:[]ContainerPort{},Env:[]EnvVar{},Resources:ResourceRequirements{Limits:ResourceList{},Requests:ResourceList{},},VolumeMounts:...... Mar 08 20:46:04 XX001 hyperkube[1694]: I0308 20:46:04.677849 1694 event.go:291] "Event occurred" object="XXX/XX001-debug" kind="Pod" apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="Created" message="Created container container-00" Mar 08 20:46:04 XX001 hyperkube[1694]: I0308 20:46:04.854458 1694 event.go:291] "Event occurred" object="XXX/XX001-debug" kind="Pod" apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="Started" message="Started container container-00" Mar 08 20:46:04 XX001 systemd[1]: Stopping libcontainer container 60284018b471c806214dbbc1a2c51f54c0a5ae9ac0334f2e3d89e11f95c18eff. Mar 08 20:46:04 XX001 systemd[1]: Removed slice machine.slice. Mar 08 20:46:04 XX001 systemd[1]: machine.slice: Consumed 224ms CPU time ~~~ In above situation, **only master-02*
was working, but it **wasn't enough*
for etcd quorum as **master-01*
and **master-03*
were **shutting down*
after **2-3 minutes**.
resolution:
Following these steps we were able to recover the environment: Step 1: Take etcd DB backup from working master node ~~~ ssh core@master-02 sudo su- mkdir backup /usr/local/bin/cluster-backup.sh--force backup/ ~~~ On the other two nodes, we stopped Kubelet, so the container won't start and shutdown the node ~~~ ssh core@master-01 & ssh core@master-03 sudo systemctl stop kubelet ~~~ Now the nodes were not shutting down anymore but no pods were running. Step 2: Disable static pods on the two failing node, and prepare them for redeployment Stop the etcd pod ~~~ sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd-pod.yaml /tmp ~~~ Wait few minutes until the pods are gone ~~~ sudo crictl ps | grep etcd | grep-v operator ~~~ Move the kubernetes-apiserver pod manifest ~~~ sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-pod.yaml /tmp ~~~ Wait few minutes until the pods are gone ~~~ sudo crictl ps | grep kube-apiserver | grep-v operator ~~~ Move the etcd directory ~~~ sudo mv /var/lib/etcd/ /tmp ~~~ Step 3: Restore etcd DB on single working node, master-02 ~~~ sudo /usr/local/bin/cluster-restore.sh backup/ ~~~ Step 4: We had working node, delete the pod from etcd DB ~~~ ssh core@master-02 sudo su- crictl exec-it /bin/bash etcdctl get /--prefix--keys-only | grep-debug etcdctl rm /kubernetes.io/pods/XXX/XX001-debug etcdctl rm /kubernetes.io/pods/XXX/XX003-debug ~~~ Step 5: Now that the pods were removed, we scaled the pods Check we have 1 node cluster ~~~ oc get pods-n openshift-etcd | grep-v etcd-quorum-guard | grep etcd ~~~ Scale to 3 nodes ~~~ oc patch etcd cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date--rfc-3339=ns)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~ Wait few minutes ~~~ oc get pods-n openshift-etcd | grep-v etcd-quorum-guard | grep etcd ~~~ Verify the etcd are same revision ~~~ oc get etcd-o=jsonpath='{range.items[0].status.conditions[?(@.type=="NodeInstallerProgressing")]}{.reason}{"
"}{.message}{"
"}' ~~~ Rollout Kubernetes API ~~~ oc patch kubeapiserver cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date--rfc-3339=ns)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~ Verify the kube-apiserver is at same revision ~~~ oc get kubeapiserver-o=jsonpath='{range.items[0].status.conditions[?(@.type=="NodeInstallerProgressing")]}{.reason}{"
"}{.message}{"
"}' ~~~ Rollout Kubernete Controller Manager ~~~ oc patch kubecontrollermanager cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date--rfc-3339=ns)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~ Verify they are at same revision ~~~ oc get kubecontrollermanager-o=jsonpath='{range.items[0].status.conditions[?(@.type=="NodeInstallerProgressing")]}{.reason}{"
"}{.message}{"
"}' ~~~ Rollout Kubernetes Scheduler ~~~ oc patch kubescheduler cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date--rfc-3339=ns)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~ Verify the nodes are at same revision ~~~ oc get kubescheduler-o=jsonpath='{range.items[0].status.conditions[?(@.type=="NodeInstallerProgressing")]}{.reason}{"
"}{.message}{"
"}' ~~~ The documentation used during these procedures: [Backing up etcd](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/backup_and_restore/control_plane_backup_and_restore/backing-up-etcd.html) and [Restoring to a previous cluster state](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/backup_and_restore/control_plane_backup_and_restore/disaster_recovery/scenario-2-restoring-cluster-state.html)
root_cause: **Command:[chroot /host shutdown-h now]** was used in a debug container, it was shutting down the nodes as soon as the nodes started.

title: Openshift - NTP clock drift or clock difference on virtualized platforms
issue: **ISSUE*

The following problems could be observed in a generic way, among the following examples:- Clock skew or clock drift- Clock difference- Node is not synchronized where following errors can be seen ~~~ Jun 01 21:12:45 node_name chronyd[1059]: Forward time jump detected! Jun 01 21:12:45 node_name chronyd[1059]: Can't synchronise: no selectable sources Jun 01 21:15:59 node_name chronyd[1059]: Selected source X.X.X.X Jun 01 21:15:59 node_name chronyd[1059]: System clock wrong by-28929.680663 seconds, adjustment started Aug 08 21:14:27 node_name chronyd[1059]: Forward time jump detected! Aug 03 08:42:30 node_name chronyd[24756]: Selected source X.X.X.X Aug 03 08:42:30 node_name chronyd[24756]: System clock wrong by 4.500188 seconds, adjustment started Aug 03 08:43:34 node_name chronyd[24756]: System clock wrong by 4.842190 seconds, adjustment started Aug 03 08:44:39 node_name chronyd[24756]: Can't synchronise: no selectable sources ~~~
resolution: Extra notes: The chrony service does not change the time The often misconception is that the chrony service is setting the time to the one given by the NTP server. This is incorrect – what actually happens is that based on the answer from the NTP server, chrony just tells the system clock to go faster or slower. For this reason, sometimes even though the time is wrong and the NTP server is working, the time does not get corrected immediately.
root_cause: There are several possible causes:- actual NTP clock difference- overloaded VM

title: Cannot upgrade RHACS operator separately if installed in openshift-operators project
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - By default, ACS operator is forced to install in **openshift-operators*

project as a [manual approval](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/operators/user/olm-installing-operators-in-namespace.html) strategy. So while upgrading, it gets bundled other operators and forces to upgrade all operators from the same project. Can this be approved independently or installed to a different project?- Why is the openshift-operators namespace enforced for ACS operator install? Or is it just a UI enforcement?
resolution: - This is the default behavior as all operators will upgrade at the same time due to subscriptions in a namespace are treated as a set. Refer this [KB article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6186961) to know more.- So try to install the operator in different namespace using cli as per this [doc](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/operators/user/olm-installing-operators-in-namespace.html#olm-installing-operator-from-operatorhub-using-cli_olm-installing-operators-in-namespace).- This issue is fixed in the RHACS 3.67.0 and now the RHACS operator will be installed in `rhacs-operator` namespace from OperatorHub.
root_cause: - This operator won't upgrade separately due to approval issues. That is, due to other operators in same namespace having manual approval strategy.- Also, option of selecting namespace (from web-console) while installing ACS operator is not editable.

title: Version job pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff state while upgrading
issue: - After initiating the upgrade, the `version` job pod created in `openshift-cluster-version` namespace is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff state, blocking the upgrade. ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-cluster-version NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cluster-version-operator-79879b4fb-8tvjb 1/1 Running 2 19d version-wsr4p-1-k22wp 0/1 Init:CrashLoopBackOff 5 1s ~~~
resolution: 1. If the cleanup container logs report errors in the `Diagnostic` section, check for the file on the node where the `version` job pod and cluster-version-operator pod are scheduled. ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-cluster-version-owide // ssh/oc debug the node $ sudo ls-ll /etc/cvo/updatepayloads/ ~~~ 2. If the file/directory reported in the errors exist on the location, remove it manually: ~~~ $ sudo cp /tmp/ $ sudo rm-rf./ // do not skip the './' while passing the directories name ~~~ 3. Once done, let the version job pod restart the containers. 4. This time, the cleanup container should be able to clean up all the files from `/etc/cvo/updatepayloads` and the version pod should be able to Complete the job and initiate the upgrade.
root_cause: - The `rm-rf` command executed by cleanup init-container confused the character `-` in the start of the directory's name as an option passed to the command. Due to this, the command fails to remove the directory.

title: Oracle System Database Requirements
issue: - Are there any CPU/Memory requirements?- Is `SYSTEM` user must always be SYSTEM or just during install/upgrade?- 2.12 install instructions reference a download of 2.11 software. Is this correct?- Documentation and downloaded files reference different Oracle client versions. Documentation references Version 19.8.0.0.0. The latest 19 version available is Version 19.16.0.0.0, can that be used?
resolution: The SYSTEM user is required. It is used during initialization and upgrade. The SYSTEM user will create the user and grant the appropriate roles and rights to the user connecting to the database. [2.12 installation instructions](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html-single/installing_3scale/index#installing-threescale-with-operator-oracle-system-database) in the list item 1 under "Procedure", the 3scale OpenShift templates are downloaded from the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/3scale/3scale-amp-openshift-templates/archive/refs/tags/3scale-2.11.1-GA.tar.gz) which links to 2.11 version. The link [GitHub repository](https://github.com/3scale/3scale-amp-openshift-templates/archive/refs/tags/3scale-2.12.0-GA.tar.gz) which points to 2.12 version should be used. Other than the following settings noted in the downloaded README file, no other settings are required. ~~~ ALTER SYSTEM SET max_string_size=extended SCOPE=SPFILE; ALTER SYSTEM SET compatible='12.2.0.1' SCOPE=SPFILE; ~~~
root_cause: Documentation on Oracle Database Integration requirements is not clear.

title: Ceph: UI showing alert "OSD osd.xx on ceph2.RedactedDomain.com deviates by more than 30% from average PG count."
issue: UI showing alert "OSD osd.xx on ceph2.RedactedDomain.com deviates by more than 30% from average PG count." OSD deviates by more than 30% from average PG count.
resolution: * The alert is only seen in the Ceph UI. * The alert triggers when the number of Placement Groups (PGs) is 30 percent lower or higher than the average number of PGs per OSD. * Using nonuniform disks sizes will cause this alert to trigger. * See the example in the Diagnostic Steps section. * In that output we can see that 3.6 TiB disk have less PGs and 9.1 TiB disks have many more PGs. * We also see that the utilization of all disks is approximately the same. * Despite the alert, the data below show a Ceph Cluster in good working order * Follow section 7.4 of the [Ceph Dashboard Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_ceph_storage/5/html-single/dashboard_guide/index#creating-a-silence-on-the-ceph-dashboard_dash) to "Create a Silence" to remove the alert from the UI. If one encounters this alert and the issue is not due to nonuniform disks (OSD) sizes, please open a Support Ticket with Rad Hat Ceph Support
root_cause: Using nonuniform disks sizes in the Ceph Cluster

title: Quay database pod crashes with pg_ctl message "the PID file "/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata/postmaster.pid" is empty
issue: - postgres database container in pod cluster-registry-quay-database-94b958748-jgxqs is not able to start- When you delete all pods (to get recreated by the Operator), these are the printed events: ~~~ 13m Normal SuccessfulCreate replicaset/cluster-registry-quay-mirror-bdcdd8788 Created pod: cluster-registry-quay-mirror-bdcdd8788-7jkq4 13m Normal Killing pod/cluster-registry-clair-app-c5768f5bc-s46dc Stopping container clair-app 13m Normal SuccessfulCreate replicaset/cluster-registry-quay-app-78b676f48 Created pod: cluster-registry-quay-app-78b676f48-c6vfx 13m Normal SuccessfulCreate replicaset/cluster-registry-clair-postgres-79d7845757 Created pod: cluster-registry-clair-postgres-79d7845757-ckrqt 13m Normal Killing pod/cluster-registry-clair-postgres-79d7845757-hgff6 Stopping container postgres ~~~- Local Quay registry in CrashLoopBackOff ~~~ 13m Warning FailedAttachVolume pod/cluster-registry-quay-database-94b958748-jgxqs Multi-Attach error for volume "pvc-04360834-9308-4bbd-b719-bf5d24017d7d" Volume is already exclusively attached to one node and can't be attached to another ~~~
resolution: Delete "/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata/postmaster.pid" pid file and wait for the whole stack to redeploy again

title: How to maintain clusters that need to be powered off for a long duration
issue: - How can be cluster be safely powered off for long duration and bring it back into use only when needed?- Is it supported to power off a running Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster for more than a month?- What is the recommended approach of maintaining a cluster which needs to be powered off for long duration and what is the recommended approach to restart such cluster/s.
resolution: - It is supported to poweroff the clusters.- The recommended approach of shutting down the cluster is documented HERE.- However, if the cluster needs to be powered off for a long duration, there is very specific procedure that needs to be followed. === 1: Check the kubelet certificate expiry on the master nodes. The kubelet certs are present in `/var/lib/kubelet/pki` directory. 2: Identify the validity of the kubelet-client and kubelet-server certificate. ~~~ $ openssl x509-in kubelet-client-current.pem-noout-enddate $ openssl x509-in kubelet-server-server.pem-noout-enddate ~~~

title: Getting insufficient permissions error to install Openshift Container Platform 4 on Google Cloud Platform?
issue: Getting the insufficient authentication error during the Openshift Container Platform 4 installation on Google Cloud Platform. ~~~ INFO Credentials loaded from gcloud CLI defaults FATAL failed to fetch Install Config: failed to fetch dependency of "Install Config": failed to fetch dependency of "Base Domain": failed to generate asset "Platform": failed to get projects: googleapi: Error 403: Request had insufficient authentication scopes. FATAL More details: FATAL Reason: insufficientPermissions, Message: Insufficient Permission ~~~
resolution: **Disclaimer:** *Please note that the sample code within this article is provided for customer benefit, but, is not supported by Red Hat. Customers can use it "as it is" or by customizing it appropriately. Red Hat does not support custom code. Please refer to the Scope of coverage (What Red Hat supports) for further details.* Make sure the service account exists: ~~~ gcloud iam service-accounts list ~~~ If the service account exists and has the service account key file, just set the environment variable with it as described in step 3. If the service account does not exist, then it must be created first. Also, if there is not a service account key file, it will be necessary to create the service account key. To do so, follow these steps below: 1. Create a service account key that will be used during installation. ~~~ gcloud iam service-accounts create SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID--description="DESCRIPTION"--display-name="DISPLAY_NAME" ~~~- Replace the following values:- *SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID*: The ID for the service account.- *DESCRIPTION*: Optional. A description of the service account.- *DISPLAY_NAME*: A service account name to display in the Cloud Console. 2. Grant service account an IAM role on project: ~~~ gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT_ID \--member="serviceAccount:SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID@PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \--role="ROLE_NAME" ~~~- Replace the following values:- *PROJECT_ID*: The project id.- *SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID*: The service account ID.- *ROLE_NAME*: A role name, such as roles/owner. **Note:** Save the key file in a safe place as this is the only time it can be downloaded. 3. Using credentials via environment variable: ~~~ export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/home/user/Downloads/service-account-file.json" ~~~ For more detailed information, see the articles [Creating a service account](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-managing-service-accounts#creating_a_service_account) and how to [generate the key file](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/production) in the GCP documentation.

The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* [OpenShift Container Platform](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/installing/installing_gcp/installing-gcp-account.html#installation-gcp-service-account_installing-gcp-account) requires a [Google Cloud Platform](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-managing-service-accounts#iam-service-accounts-create-gcloud) service account that provides authentication and authorization to access data in the Google APIs. Google Cloud Client Libraries use a library called Application Default Credentials (ADC) to automatically find the service account credentials. ADC looks for service account credentials in the following order: 1. If the environment variable GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is not set, ADC uses the service account that is attached to the resource that is running in the code. 3. If ADC cannot use any of the above credentials, an error occurs.

title: How do I install a three-node OpenShift Data Foundation compact cluster using ACM policy on RHACM connected clusters?
resolution: **Prerequisites**- A Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (RHACM) Hub cluster into which the managed clusters have been imported.- Managed clusters on which you will set up OpenShift Data Foundation.- Label the managed clusters on which you want to set up OpenShift Data Foundation. First, you need to install and configure the Local Storage Operator on the managed clusters. The Local Storage Operator will provision Persistent Volumes (PVs) using the local devices on the managed cluster. The OpenShift Data Foundation Operator uses these PVs to set up the storage cluster. 1) Log into the RHACM Hub cluster using the command-line interface. 2) Create a namespace in which to create the policies: ~~~ # oc create ns odf-policy-ns ~~~ 3) Install and configure the Local Storage Operator. Install and configure the Local Storage Operator using a policy similar to the following. title: Is Directory listings (indexing)  deactivated in OCP Web server components?
issue: - Security concerns associated- It is dangerous to leave this function turned on for the web server because it leads to information disclosure.
resolution: - Directory listing is a web server function that displays the directory contents when there is no index file in a specific website directory. It is dangerous to leave this function turned on for the web server because it leads to information disclosure.- For example, when a user requests *www.test.com* without specifying a file (such as index.html, index.php, or default.asp), the web server processes this request, returns the index file for that directory, and the browser displays the website. However, if the index file did not exist and if the directory listing was turned on, the web server would return the contents of the directory instead.- Currently, the directory listing is activated in OCP. This is a known issue and there has already been a bug (Bug id 2092303) related to this issue.

title: CRI-O container logs truncate lines after 8192 characters in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: Cri container logs truncate lines after 8192 characters in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform This can easily be reproduced. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. From the upstream documentation: [https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/node/kubelet-cri-logging.md](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/node/kubelet-cri-logging.md) ~~~ Log format The runtime should decorate each log entry with a RFC 3339Nano timestamp prefix, the stream type (i.e., "stdout" or "stderr"), the tags of the log entry, the log content that ends with a newline. The tags fields can support multiple tags, delimited by:. Currently, only one tag is defined in CRI to support multi-line log entries: partial or full. Partial (P) is used when a log entry is split into multiple lines by the runtime, and the entry has not ended yet. Full (F) indicates that the log entry is completed-- it is either a single-line entry, or this is the last line of the multiple-line entry. For example, 2016-10-06T00:17:09.669794202Z stdout F The content of the log entry 1 2016-10-06T00:17:09.669794202Z stdout P First line of log entry 2 2016-10-06T00:17:09.669794202Z stdout P Second line of the log entry 2 2016-10-06T00:17:10.113242941Z stderr F Last line of the log entry 2 With the knowledge, kubelet can parse the logs and serve them for kubectl logs requests. This meets requirement (3). Note that the format is defined deliberately simple to provide only information necessary to serve the requests. We do not intend for kubelet to host various logging plugins. It is also worth mentioning again that the scope of this proposal is restricted to stdout/stderr streams of the container, and we impose no restriction to the logging format of arbitrary container logs. ~~~ The maximum line length is hard-coded to 8192 bytes. All of the split lines have the `P` annotation as designed. The log parser should look for `P` as a partial line and continue reading till it hits the next `F` in the output to complete the line. For further details, also see: [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1866819](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1866819)

title: How to find out which config change triggered mcp rollout?

resolution: We can validate the details in the machine-configs once they get updated. Please refer to the below steps to verify.- Each time when the machine configs get updated they generate a config file called rendered. Step 2: This will give you the machine config that is applied in your cluster ~~~ $ oc get mc-o yaml | grep rendered name: rendered-master-54d16a945a6a9168503c654995c23ba8 name: rendered-worker-ebddd933a0177fb5d4bba395ff66e176 ~~~ Step 3: This will give you the old and current machine-configs available for your cluster ~~~ $ oc get mc NAME GENERATEDBYCONTROLLER a537783ea4a0cd3b4fe2a02626ab27887307ea51 3.2.0 51d rendered-master-54d16a945a6a9168503c654995c23ba8 a537783ea4a0cd3b4fe2a02626ab27887307ea51 3.2.0 51d rendered-worker-ebddd933a0177fb5d4bba395ff66e176 a537783ea4a0cd3b4fe2a02626ab27887307ea51 3.2.0 51d ~~~ Step 4: You need to append rendered yaml into the file ~~~ $ oc get mc rendered-master-54d16a945a6a9168503c654995c23ba8-o yaml > mc-file2.yaml ~~~ Similarly, you need to put the another rendered yaml into the file Step 5: You can use the `diff` command to compare both the old and the new rendered files and check what all changes have been applied within your cluster. ~~~ diff [options] File1 File2 ~~~ For example, contextual output for the `diff` of these two files `mc-file1.yaml` and `mc-file2.yaml`: ~~~ diff-c mc-file1.yaml mc-file2.yaml ~~~ ## Using unsupported tool to ease compare work **Disclaimer: Link contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content** You may use, too, the following unsupported tool written by one of the Red Hat engineers- which can ease the compare work [A tool to decode and compare the contents of MachineConfig(s) in OpenShift4.](https://github.com/AmrGanz/MachineConfigAnalyzer) Please find the steps to compare the rendered below- Step 1: You need to append rendered yaml into the file ~~~ $ oc get mc rendered-master-54d16a945a6a9168503c654995c23ba8-o yaml > mc-file2.yaml ~~~ Step 2: Then, you need to decode it by using the below command: ~~~ $./mca.sh decode mc-file2.yaml ~~~ Step 3: Similarly, you need to put the another rendered yaml into the file like `mc-file1.yaml` and decode it using Step 1 and Step 2. title: Error when configuring a port in a route to expose an APIcast service
issue: We want to configure a special port (50062) on the URL exposed in 3scale, this is communicated with APICast but when configuring it it sends us the following error: > The Route "apicast-3scale-dev" is invalid:
spec.host: Invalid value: "api-xxx-dev.xxxxxx.yy:50062": host must conform to DNS 952 subdomain conventions

spec.host: Invalid value: "api-xxx-dev.xxxxxx.yy:50062": a lowercase RFC 1123 label must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters or '-', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'my-name', or '123-abc', regex used for validation is '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?')
resolution: case for reference: 03265162 Now seeing the `route.yml` that you shared is clear to me what you're trying to achieve and where. You're trying to define a port in host spec level and it's not possible and that is why you're getting this error [1] because the `spec.host` is expecting only lower case alphanumeric characters or "-" and not a ":". I would say that you'll need to define this desired port in OCP level maybe with an Ingress (I'm not sure but maybe `Service.Type=NodePort`) so I'd suggest you to reach out your OpenShift administrator or open a case with the OpenShift team in order to have an assistance in how to configure it once it is out of scope of 3scale. [1] **host must conform to DNS 952 subdomain conventions**

issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? I need to configure one business-central pointing towrds three or two kie-servers at the same time. I want to know how this has to be implemented. What is the business impact? Please also provide timeframe information. High Availability is a must in our production environment.
resolution: Hi Buvnesh, > > I need to configure one business-central pointing towrds three or two kie-servers at the same time. I want to know how this has to be implemented. To run two or more kie server in HA environment, you should follow the instructions given in the Chapter 29. KIE Server clusters in a runtime environment [1]. I hope this helps. Finally, to better understand the severity you have selected for this case (severity 2), I would like to understand the overall business impact this is having to your production system. As the query here is configuration question I would like to better understand how this issue is affecting your users and production system as described in Red Hat Support Severity Level Definitions[2]. Best Regards, Biljana. [1] https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_process_automation_manager/7.11/html/installing_and_configuring_red_hat_process_automation_manager/clustering-ps-con_clustering-runtime-standalone#doc-wrapper [2] https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/severity It's a common supported use case where one business central is pointing to multiple kie server instances. ************************* Note Do not connect KIE Server to Business Central in high availability (HA) on premise environments. Business Central instances are not able to keep in sync with the status of each KIE Server. For example, if a KIE Server is up but not in sync, Business Central will not be able to deploy through that instance. ************************** What the statement above means is we currently don't support the kie server cluster to connect to the business central in HA setup [1] on premise environment. title: istio-ingressgateway and istio-egressgateway pods fail to start with error "failed to warm certificate: failed to generate workload certificate" in ServiceMesh 2.2
issue: After configuring a custom `CertificateAuthority` for `istiod` to use, the `ingressgateway` and `egressgateway` pods do not start.
resolution: In order to have `istiod` using a custom certificate the following steps must be followed: 1. If ServiceMesh is already deployed, it must be removed:- Remove the `ServiceMeshMemberRoll` and `ServiceMeshControlPlane`.- Remove the `namespace` where ServiceMesh was deployed. 2. Create the `namespace` again. 3. Create the secret `istio-ca-secret` with the certificates to be used. The data this secret must contain is:- ca-cert.pem: Certificate that will be used for communications between the data plane components- ca-key.pem: Key for the certificate above.- cert-chain.pem: Chain of certificates.- root-cert.pem: Certificate of the Root CA. 4. Create the `ServiceMeshControlPlane` and `ServiceMeshMemberRoll`. Then the different ServiceMesh components will use the certificate from the secret `istio-ca-secret`.
root_cause: The data in the secret `istio-ca-secret` was invalid.

title: OpenShift Service Mesh 2.x  Application retrieving "no healthy upstream" error  intermittently - 503 errors
issue: OpenShift Service Mesh 2.x Applications retrieving "no healthy upstream" error intermittently- 503 errors You could observe an issue with OpenShift Service Mesh 2.0.3 where sometimes an application is returning a 503 error with the following message: no healthy upstream. This message usually occurs when the application is still not ready, but in this case the application might be in working and the error message is intermittent. Below is an example of the ingressgateway log with an error message: ~~~~ istio-proxy 2021-06-07T08:59:30.783334Z debug envoy router [external/envoy/source/common/router/router.cc:477] [C315561][S12518526451601433981] cluster 'outbound|8000|9ecb6cc7-5cdb-358c-99b9-8ec256a44d2f|svc-6618faac-7180-3ae1-9b47-4e8979f477f6.51472e11-2b72-3e56-a2f3-14cafb44f8a5.svc.cluster.local' match for URL '/healthcheck/liveness' istio-proxy 2021-06-07T08:59:30.783351Z debug envoy upstream [external/envoy/source/common/upstream/cluster_manager_impl.cc:1235] no healthy host for HTTP connection pool istio-proxy 2021-06-07T08:59:30.783370Z debug envoy http [external/envoy/source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.cc:1479] [C315561][S12518526451601433981] Sending local reply with details no_healthy_upstream istio-proxy 2021-06-07T08:59:30.783387Z debug envoy http [external/envoy/source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.cc:1710] [C315561][S12518526451601433981] encoding headers via codec (end_stream=false): istio-ingressgateway-5d8687c6f-mgtgk istio-proxy 2021-06-21T07:39:42.433085Z debug envoy upstream [external/envoy/source/common/upstream/cluster_manager_impl.cc:1235] no healthy host for HTTP connection pool istio-ingressgateway-5d8687c6f-mgtgk istio-proxy 2021-06-21T07:39:42.433191Z debug envoy http [external/envoy/source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.cc:1479] [C550011][S16746365673666152539] Sending local reply with details no_healthy_upstream istio-ingressgateway-5d8687c6f-mgtgk istio-proxy 2021-06-21T07:39:42.433241Z debug envoy http [external/envoy/source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.cc:1710] [C550011][S16746365673666152539] encoding headers via codec (end_stream=false): istio-ingressgateway-5d8687c6f-fgncg istio-ingressgateway-5d8687c6f-mgtgkistio-proxy ':authority', '10.129.2.133:15090' istio-ingressgateway-5d8687c6f-fgncgistio-proxy istio-proxy':status', '503' ~~~~
resolution: - Generally, no_healthy_upstream occurs when the request was rejected by the router filter because there was no healthy upstream found.- As we can see the sidecar of the application never receives an http request as it can be seen in the istio-proxy logs- Workaround is to restart the istio ingressgateway pods inorder to address this error You may refer the below git link that the issue observed in istio 1.6.8 but still possibly persists on istio 1.6.14 version Service Mesh 2.0.3 is using Istio 1.6.14 [https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/29254] Red Hat is Aware of this bug / issue, we were following it on a separate internal ticket with our Software Engineering Team and this has been fixed in recent versions
root_cause: This is a bug on that specified version OSSM 2.0.3, istio 1.6.14 version Upgrading the OSSM environment to 2.06 solved the issue

title: [RHOCP 4.10] `oc image mirror` causes "error: you must specify at least one source image to pull and the destination to push to as SRC=DST or SRC DST [DST2 DST3 ...]"
issue: - When trying to upload images to the OpenShift 4.x registry by following [the official documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-installation-images.html#installing-mirroring-installation-images) the message `error: you must specify at least one source image to pull and the destination to push to as SRC=DST or SRC DST [DST2 DST3...]` is seen;- How to mirror registry in a airgapped/disconnected RHOCP 4 cluster?
resolution: 1. Compress the files in **ORIGIN_NODE** while maintaining the symlinks:- If using `tar`, please use `tar cvf`. ``` $ tar cvfz foo.tar.gz foo/ # tar stores symlinks by default ```- If you are using `zip`, please make sure to use the option `--symlinks`. ``` $ zip--symlinks-r foo.zip foo/ # the symlink option is required if using zip ``` 2. Transfer the compressed file from **ORIGIN_NODE** to **DESTINATION_NODE**- You can use `scp` or any other tool to do so 3. Decompress the files in **DESTINATION_NODE**. 4. After creating new archive including symbolic links, you should be able able to mirror images to local repository without issues: ``` [localadmin@DESTINATION_NODE pkgs]$ oc image mirror-a ${LOCAL_SECRET_JSON}--from-dir=${REMOVABLE_MEDIA_PATH}/mirror "file://openshift/release:${OCP_RELEASE}*" ${LOCAL_REGISTRY}/${LOCAL_REPOSITORY} DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/ openshift/ocp4 blobs:...(truncated) stats: shared=0 unique=334 size=11.92GiB ratio=1.00 phase 0: DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443 openshift/ocp4 blobs=334 mounts=0 manifests=162 shared=0 info: Planning completed in 1.86s uploading: DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/openshift/ocp4 sha256:90287d3a39880427d47991f749ba67202ccb1aa5b5666e7502c187296201 25.34MiB uploading: DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/openshift/ocp4 sha256:70c7094e6a83f75a8084cebff400a4f6a12b8cd34b05341576e18326 114MiB sha256:a6cb423b333f9b4fc24c729de8daa76aeb46e74812c58c57af9a9f6e1c68b9 DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/openshift/ocp4:4.10.30-x86_64-cli-artifacts sha256:67832d5db1d0b541142b85d88394952be88fea46917b98acb5999cc9f DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/openshift/ocp4:4.10.30-x86_64-ironic-hardware-inventory-recorder sha256:9103ca4875b77854084853247e6f6ea5c3fd1c105229ece29090b0923 DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/openshift/ocp4:4.10.30-x86_64-machine-config-operator....(truncated) sha256:5c5aad53893649df4ee8ebcc11432d52f2b8ea21bf7e80673d1794bc07a6e DESTINATION_NODE.redhat.lab:8443/openshift/ocp4:4.10.30-x86_64-csi-node-driver-registrar info: Mirroring completed in 1m21.24s (1.798MB/s) [localadmin@DESTINATION_NODE pkgs]$ You will find enclosed logs about manifest link report and screenshot of local registry with tags/manifest for OCP 4.10.30 ```
root_cause: - Files were transferred from **ORIGIN_NODE** to **DESTINATION_NODE** using `scp` or other tool that does not copy symbolic links across (symlinks);- The compression tool did not keep the symlinks in the final archive.

title: Should i cache Producers?
issue: Reading the Spring doc, they stated that we should use connection/session caching in order to get decent performances: ==> "The ConnectionFactory used with this template should return pooled Connections (or a single shared Connection) as well as pooled Sessions and MessageProducers. Otherwise, performance of ad-hoc JMS operations is going to suffer." The app is deployed on Openshift and will run without disruption. That means that the connections will be kept forever (or till something close/crash it). Is it acceptable from an "AMQ broker" point of view that clients keep connections open like this? What is the max cached connection it's able to handle (a scale, for example, is 1000 acceptable or is it a lower/higher level?) By what is it determined? For example, here, My component will be deployed maybe more than 20 times, targeting the same queue on the same broker. That mean that if i have a pool of 10 connections, i'll end up with 20x10xnbr pods cached connections to the same queue on the same broker. Is it acceptable? or should i better disable connection caching, loosing all it's benefits. > Is it acceptable from an "AMQ broker" point of view that clients keep connections open like this? What is the max cached connection it's able to handle (a scale, for example, is 1000 acceptable or is it a lower/higher level?) By what is it determined?
resolution: The connection objects can be accessed concurrently by multiple messaging clients irrespective of the client type (plain JMS/Spring/Camel). There is no harm in sharing a connection (caching) among multiple messaging clients, which is the recommended approach. Thus, you can keep a connection object open and share it among multiple messaging clients. Consequently, did you try running your application with fewer connections while increasing the producer count?- Producer caching:- It is fine to use the producer caching mechanism offered by the Spring or Camel APIs. Spring and Camel APIs take care of thread safety. Thus, you can cache producers using Spring/Camel APIs.- However, it is not recommended to cache a producer or a session directly using the JMS API to ensure thread safety and transaction support.

title: PVC for ocs-storagecluster-cephfs in pending state and subvolume group 'csi' does not exist
issue: PVC in pending state for the ocs-storagecluster storage class ~~~ oc get pvc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE user-home-pvc Pending ocs-storagecluster-cephfs 2d ~~~ Logs of csi-provisioner in openshift-container-storage namespace ~~~ oc logs csi-cephfsplugin-provisioner-aaaaaaaa-bbbbb-c csi-provisioner I0901 09:25:25.753590 1 event.go:282] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"PersistentVolumeClaim", Namespace:"nameofnamespace", Name:"nameofpvc", UID:"d5$3eb7d-89c6-47a3-9cb3-f8d145673517", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"21618761", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'ProvisioningFailed' failed to provision volume wit$ StorageClass "ocs-storagecluster-cephfs": rpc error: code = Internal desc = rados: ret=-2, No such file or directory: "subvolume group 'csi' does not exist" ~~~ The following ceph command launched from the rook-ceph-operator display the following: ~~~ ceph fs subvolumegroup ls ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem [] ~~~ Instead of showing the "csi" subvolumegroup: ~~~ ceph fs subvolumegroup ls ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem [{"name": "_deleting"}, {"name": "csi"}] ~~~ NOTE: The "csi" should be visible as soon as the first PVC has been created. The "_deleting" subvolumegroup might not be in your output. It is a subvolumegroup dynamically created, and this subvolumegroup is created as soon as one PVC has been deleted in ocs-storagecluster-cephfs.
resolution: Restarting the following pod in the openshift-storage namespace solve the situation: ~~~ oc delete pod-l app=csi-cephfsplugin-provisioner ~~~
root_cause: This is a expected behaviour from cephcsi if the storagecluster is deleted, csi pods should also get deleted, and when the storagecluster is recreated, new csi pods will come up and creates the subvolumegroup. Linked to the following BZ: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2124469

title: After upgrade RHACM from 2.4 to 2.5, there are some errors of serviceaccount "provider-credential" not found
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - After upgrade RHACM from 2.4 to 2.5, there are some errors: ~~~ cluster-lifecycle-sub: lastTransitionTime: '2022-09-12T20:55:34Z' message: >- pods "provider-credential-controller-66574d5bbb-" is forbidden: error looking up service account open-cluster-management/provider-credential: serviceaccount "provider-credential" not found ~~~
resolution: - Ensure the operator *multicluster engine for Kubernetes* is installed ~~~ $ oc get csv-n multicluster-engine NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE multicluster-engine.v2.1.1 multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.1.1 multicluster-engine.v2.0.2 Succeeded ~~~- Ensure *MultiClusterEngine* is **available** ~~~ $ oc describe MultiClusterEngine... Conditions: Last Transition Time: 2022-09-13T13:46:16Z Last Update Time: 2022-09-13T13:46:16Z Message: All components deployed Reason: ComponentsDeployed Status: True Type: Progressing Last Transition Time: 2022-09-13T13:47:28Z Last Update Time: 2022-09-13T13:47:28Z Reason: ComponentsAvailable Status: True Type: Available Current Version: 2.1.1 Desired Version: 2.1.1 Phase: Available ~~~- Scale down to 0 and delete any RS of older ACM versions (2.4): ~~~ $ oc get rs-n open-cluster-management--show-labels | grep 2\\.4 $ oc scale rs--replicas=0 $ oc delete rs ~~~- Disable and enable again the cluster-lifecycle component of Multiclusterhub ~~~ $ oc edit Multiclusterhub-n open-cluster-management...- enabled: false name: cluster-lifecycle ~~~ After a while, enable again: ~~~ $ oc edit Multiclusterhub-n open-cluster-management...- enabled: true name: cluster-lifecycle ~~~
root_cause: - Provider-crential is not used in RHACM 2.5, so any message related to this is because an old version pod from an old replicaset is running.- RHACM installs the operator *multicluster engine for Kubernetes*. In some environments, like disconnected environments, this installation may fail, causing failures in some ACM components.- RHACM deletes old version deployments, but old replicasets are not deleted. In some cases, the old replicasets may have not scaled down to 0, so old pods are still running. In this scenario, it's recommended to do a cleanup of old replicasets scaling down to 0 and deleting them. **NOTE**: In case you accidentally delete a new replicaset, its deployment will recreate the replicaset.

title: How to deploy an application with JBoss EAP Operator via the CLI
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How do I deploy an application with JBoss EAP Operator via the CLI?- How do I install JBoss EAP Operator with the apprual strategy set to `Manual` via the CLI? [The product docomentation Installing EAP Operator Using the CLI](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.4/html/getting_started_with_jboss_eap_for_openshift_container_platform/eap-operator-for-automating-application-deployment-on-openshift_default#installing-eap-operator-using-the-cli_default) only says if the apprval strategy is `Automatic`.
resolution: The following example is a step-by-step guide to deploying [clusterbench](https://github.com/clusterbench/clusterbench), a test application for clustering with JBoss EAP Operator. title: PersistentVolumeClaim is invalid: spec.resources.requests.storage: Forbidden: field can not be less than previous value
issue: Quay deployment using operator is not able to finish the deployment and fail in the reconciliation. ~~~ $ oc get quayregistry-n quay-enterprise CLUSTERNAME-registry-o yaml apiVersion: quay.redhat.com/v1 kind: QuayRegistry... spec:... status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: "2022-09-15T10:38:17Z" lastUpdateTime: "2022-09-15T10:38:17Z" message: 'all Kubernetes objects not created/updated successfully: PersistentVolumeClaim "CLUSTERNAME-registry-quay-database" is invalid: spec.resources.requests.storage: Forbidden: field can not be less than previous value' reason: ComponentCreationFailed status: "True" type: RolloutBlocked ~~~
resolution: The following documentation describe how to define the default size of each PVC which will be created automatically by quay during the deployment. [https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_quay/3/html/configure_red_hat_quay/operator-components-intro#operator-volume-size-overrides](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_quay/3/html/configure_red_hat_quay/operator-components-intro#operator-volume-size-overrides)
root_cause: By default Quay operator create two pvc size of 50GB for postgres and clair. Creating pvc manually for clair and/or postgres with a different size than the default 50Gi or changing the size of those two PVC outside of the QuayRegistry CRD will lead to this error in the reconciliation.

title: Maximum live time of a service account token in OpenShift Container Platform 4.11
issue: We installed a fresh Openshift 4.11 cluster. To configure cluster we use `ArgoCD` and therefore we have to add `ArgoCD` `serviceAccount` tokens to the `ArgoCD` instance of the target cluster. We create the token using `oc create token serviceaccount--duration=26280h` but are now wondering how to create `token` that never expire and how to list/inspect created `token`.
resolution: Red Hat is currently investigating that question and will update this Solution if and when more details become available. To raise questions or obtain further information, contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport).
root_cause: To align with upstream [Kubernetes having moved](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#urgent-upgrade-notes-1) the `LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration` feature gate to beta and enabling it by default, Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform now also follows this security feature and releases with the feature enabled. As a result, when creating new `serviceAccount` (SA), a service account token secret is no longer automatically generated. Previously, Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform automatically added a service account token to a secret for each new SA.

title: OVNKubernetes    EgressFirewall block API server  in OCP 4.7
issue: - After Migrating the OpenShift Cluster from OpenShift SDN cluster network provider to OVNKubernetes cluster network provider,egressfirewall blocks the traffic for the API services and it stops working.- EgressNetworkPolicy is automatically converted to EgressFirewall on SDN upgrade, but this conversion broke the apps because of the different behavior with respect to the API server between the two implementations.- This issue has also been observed in brand new cluster and can be reproduced.
resolution: **Workaround **- After adding the API servers endpoint ip subnet to the egressfirewall, the API service can be accessed.- There is a bug opened for this and Red Hat Engineering team is working on the fix in order to integrate this in the recent versions of OCP `- The current method or workaround is to allow access to host IP's in order to manually create allow rules in egress firewalls to those specific hosts, or a generic CIDR rule that encompasses the host networks.- However, we understand that manually configuring this isn't ideal as nodes can come and go, and allowing an entire CIDR may not be feasible as a user may not want pods to reach other hosts on the external network. Therefore Red Hat Engineering Team is planning to add a node selector to the egress firewall destination spec in OVN. That way a user can specify a label applied to one or more nodes and the kubernetes node IPs will be included in that rule **Note** The OpenShift SDN existing behavior will not change.- Red Hat Engineering Team is working on a fix and it will be available soon in upcoming OCP versions
root_cause: 1) When we create EgressFirewall objects with a whitelist of allowed IPs, automatically access to the API server is blocked from pods in that projects. 2) This is not the case or behavior of EgressNetworkPolicy in OpenShift SDN, where access to the API server was implicitly granted. 3) With Egress Firewall we need to manually add the IP addresses of the API server endpoints This is a bug which Red Hat Software Engineering is working on [1993841](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1993841) You can have a look on this upstream patch for more information [https://github.com/ovn-org/ovn-kubernetes/pull/3002]

title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) Calculation In Multicontainer Environment.
issue: - How to calculate current target cpu utilisation on multicontainer environment?- How Horizontal Pod Autoscaler(HPA) mechanism works in the deployment?
resolution: - The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) determines scaling by comparing the "Target CPU percentage" to the "Current CPU Percentage".- The utilization is calculated as per the cpu requests in the containers of the pods and auto scaling will happen based on the average utilization of pods in the deployment.- HPA calculates pod cpu utilisation as average of sum of cpu utilization of all the container in a pod divided by total cpu requests of the total pods. ~~~ HPA current CPU utilization % = Average of ((sum of cpu utilization on containers in a pod)/(total cpu requests))* 100 of pods ~~~- For example:- The container A is using cpu requests of 100m and container B will be having cpu requests of 50m. ~~~ Container A: requests: cpu: 100m <--- memory: 200Mi limits: cpu: 400m memory: 400Mi Container B: requests: cpu: 50m <--- memory: 100Mi limits: cpu: 200m memory: 200Mi ~~~- When the number of replicas = 1- Container A consumes 200m and container B consumes 20m.- HPA current CPU utilization percentage=((200+20)/(100+50))/1 *100 = 146 %- This value(146%) will be checked with target cpu utilization percentage value and autoscale of pods will happen.- When the number of replicas = 2- Container A1 consumes 110m,container A2 consumes 20m, container B1 consumes 10m.- HPA current CPU utilization percentage = ((110+20+10)/(100+150))/2 *100 = 46%- 46% is compared with target cpu utilization percentage and autoscale of pods will happen.- The desired number of replicas will be calculated using below formula. Please refer [Upstream Doc](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/#algorithm-details) for additional information ~~~ DesiredReplicas = ceil[currentReplicas * (currentMetricValue / desiredMetricValue)] ~~~- For example:- ~~~ Target-utilization = 80% Container A: requests: cpu: 100m <--- memory: 200Mi limits: cpu: 400m memory: 400Mi Container B: requests: cpu: 50m <--- memory: 100Mi limits: cpu: 200m memory: 200Mi ~~~- When CPU utilization is 200m in container A and 20m in container B.- Current replicas count should always be value 1 because it compares with each pod every time with target utilization- Desired metric value- target utilisation of cpu requests- Desired metric value- 80%(100+50) = 120- Desired replicas = ceil(1*(200+20)/120) = ceil (1.83) = 2- The total number of replicas is 2- When container A1 container consumes 110m container A2 consumes 20m container B1 consumes 10M.- Desired replicas = ceil(1*(110+20+10)/120) = ceil (1.16) = 2- So total number of replicas is 2.

title: Using cluster proxy settings in a debug pod
issue: No internet connectivity from debug pods in clusters in a restricted network environment Cluster proxy environment variables are not set in a debug pod.
resolution: Manually exporting variables---------------------------- 1. identify the cluster proxy settings: $ oc get proxy cluster-o yaml ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: Proxy metadata:... labels: app.kubernetes.io/instance: config-proxy name: cluster... spec: httpProxy: httpsProxy: noProxy:... ~~~ copy or note down the httpProxy, httpsProxy and noProxy values under "spec" In the debug pod, run: # export HTTP_PROXY= # export HTTPS_PROXY= # export NO_PROXY= Exporting variables set by the Machine Config Operator------------------------------------------------------ # source /etc/mco/proxy.env
root_cause: Debug pods do not inherit the HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY environment variables
