title: Cost Management SaaS
issue: [What form of separation of users is in place on the SaaS. If the service was to be compromised, what stops an attacker from then being able to compromise the rest of the platform?](#What)
[How intra as well as inter service traffic is protected using Transport Layer Security (TLS)?](#TLS)
[What security governance framework is used by RedHat on the SaaS?](#governance)
[What logging and incident management does RedHat have for the SaaS?](#log)
[How do RedHat secure their code and the security of their product?](#testing)
[How does RedHat manage supply chain security on the SaaS?](#supplychain)
[What do we need to do in order to ensure we are accessing and using the service in a secure way?](#secure)
[What is RedHat doing to ensure the security of their external interface of the SaaS from compromise?](#external)
[How does Red Hat check for privileged access onto the SaaS and how do they administer it?](#administer)
[How does Red Hat detect and respond to potential incidents on the SaaS? How does Red Hat handle the Operational Security of the platform](#operations)
resolution: - ## What form of separation of users is in place on the SaaS. If the service was to be compromised, what stops an attacker from then being able to compromise the rest of the platform? ## {#What} Security of customer data in Red Hat is a priority and every effort is made to ensure that information is not unnecessarily persisted and that it is secured using industry standard best practices. Data in the service is segregated by Red Hat account into different database schemas. The user and account data is populated by the Red Hat Single Sign-on Service and this controls the schema of data the user has access to. **Infrastructure and Architecture:-**- All customer data provided is stored within a secure data center with controlled access.- All volumes containing customer data at rest are encrypted with AES 256 bit encryption- All parts of the internal infrastructure transmit their logs to a centralized log aggregator for inspection and analysis.- Red Hat Security conducts regular architecture review of infrastructure- Data is always encrypted in transit.- All API calls for reading and writing data must be authenticated. **Maintaining Security:-**- All software is analyzed with static code analyzers and all reported issues are fixed before code is deployed into production.- Code is peer reviewed.- Development teams follow an Agile software delivery lifecycle, which means that security related defects can be addressed rapidly, and software patches are regularly released as part of our continuous delivery model.- Patches that can impact end users will be applied as soon as possible, but may necessitate end user notification and scheduling a service window in some cases.- All infrastructure software components are continuously monitored for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and proactively patched.- Penetration testing is conducted by both internal and external parties.- Access to systems that handle customer data is controlled via multi factor authentication and authorization controls. Access is granted on a need to know basis.- ## How intra as well as inter service traffic is protected using Transport Layer Security (TLS)? ## {#TLS}- All communication with Red Hat occurs over encrypted channels- leveraging Transport Layer Security (TLS) & mutual certificate authentication. All data is encrypted in transit and at rest.- Your data is encrypted in three key ways, on your host system at the point of collection; in transit across the network; and when it is at rest on Red Hat infrastructure- All communication with Red Hat occurs over encrypted channels using Transport Layer Security (TLS).- All TLS traffic with Red Hat servers is verified with a trusted certificate that is bundled with the application, ensuring that communications can not be intercepted, such as by a “man in the middle” attack.- The default communication model from client systems to Red Hat servers occurs with mutual TLS or two-way authentication using digital certificates.- All volumes containing your data at rest are encrypted with Linux Unified Key Setup (LUKS) encryption. More details are available in this Red Hat Insights- Security Information article.- ## What security governance framework is used by RedHat on the SaaS? ## {#governance}- Red Hat software is open source. Development of open source software begins with upstream open source development projects undertaken by individuals and private companies located throughout the world, which comprise a world-wide community of open source developers and contributors. While an individual or a private company, such as Red Hat, might manage an open source development project, many contributors can provide input to open source software. Due to the open collaborative nature of these projects, there is no way to fully or exclusively control these individual contributions or ensure such contributions will continue. The Red Hat Product Security Team does perform product governance and Software Development Life Cycle like functions.- All Red Hat software comes from upstream and publicly available upstream projects. These projects use an assortment of methods/tools (e.g. Gitlab) to track changes. As projects are productized, the software is pulled into dedicated Red Hat build servers and is reviewed, tested, and packaged by authorized Red Hat employees. All packaged products are signed by Red Hat signing servers prior to release to Red Hat subscribers so that authenticity of the packages can be verified.- Red Hat Product Security ensures that Red Hat produces secure, high-quality software that meets a customer's business needs. To do so, we created the Red Hat Secure Software Management Lifecycle (SSML), which directly aligns to the NIST Secure Software Development Framework [NIST SSDF SP-800-218](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-218/final). That framework articulates/aggregates commonly accepted and desired actions to effectively manage software, and establishes a core set of secure software development practices. By following these practices, Red Hat aims to reduce the number of vulnerabilities in released software, mitigate the potential impact of undetected or unaddressed vulnerabilities, and address the root causes of vulnerabilities to prevent future recurrences.- Red Hat performs SSML with scanning and testing for our source code. As our code is Open Source, customers have access to the source code to conduct any validations they require as Red Hat does not provide results.- ## What logging and incident management does RedHat have for the SaaS? ## {#log} All parts of the internal infrastructure transmit their logs to a centralized log aggregator for inspection and analysis.- ## How do RedHat secure their code and the security of their product? ## {#testing} The security of your data in Red Hat is a priority. Safeguards include measures designed so that information is not unnecessarily persisted and that data is properly protected. **OpenShift Dedicated:-**- Cost management operates on Red Hat’s own OpenShift Dedicated infrastructure. **Penetration Testing:-**- Penetration testing is conducted by both internal and external parties. **CVE & Patching:-**- All infrastructure software components are continuously monitored for known Common Vulnerability Exposures (CVEs) and proactively patched. Patches that can impact end-users will be applied as soon as possible but may necessitate end-user notification and scheduling a service window in some cases. **Restricted Data Access:-**- Access to systems that handle customer data is controlled via multi-factor authentication and strict authorization controls. Access is granted on a need to know basis and limited for required SaaS infrastructure operations. **Software-as-a-Service Delivery Lifecycle**:-- Development teams follow a SaaS delivery lifecycle, which means that security-related defects can be addressed rapidly, and software patches are regularly released as part of our continuous delivery model. **Static Application Security Testing (SAST):-**- This analyzes source code to find security vulnerabilities or weaknesses. In a typical SAST scan report for web applications, you will see vulnerabilities like SQL injections or Cross-Site Scripting. **Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST):-**- This is also known as black box testing, identifies vulnerabilities through simulated attacks on a running application. When you hear the terms "penetration testing" or "fuzz testing," it usually means DAST. Please find the detailed information on [Application analysis in the DevSecOps life cycle](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/application-analysis-devsecops-life-cycle).- ## How does RedHat manage supply chain security on the SaaS? ## {#supplychain}- Red Hat also has a Supply Chain team that guides and reviews all parts of the development, quality engineering and release environments. Version control is maintained and signed. Changes can only be made by approved people referencing approved bugs and there is an audit trail of activities.- ## What do we need to do in order to ensure we are accessing and using the service in a secure way? ## {#secure}- To use the service in a secure way you can create the source and then you can limit access to the cost management resource. For this purpose kindly refer [Product Documentation for Cost Management Service](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/cost_management_service/2022#limiting-access_configuri).- ## What is RedHat doing to ensure the security of their external interface of the SaaS from compromise? ## {#external}- Cost management is hosted on a network isolated OpenShift cluster in a VPC on AWS in the us-east region.- Data rests in associated services like AWS RDS and AWS S3 and is encrypted.- ## How does Red Hat check for privileged access onto the SaaS and how do they administer it? ## {#administer} Access to systems that handle customer data is controlled via multi factor authentication and authorization controls. Access is granted on a need to know basis.- ## How does Red Hat detect and respond to potential incidents on the SaaS? How does Red Hat handle the Operational Security of the platform? ## {#operations} Red Hat uses a broad set of tools and approaches to secure our cloud services and follows a formal Incident Management process for all incidents. Additionally, the integrity of Red Hat's processes are regularly audited and certified by third party assessors following industry-standard compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, etc.

title: How to put a Bare Metal Host into maintenance mode in RHOCP 4
issue: - Sometimes, putting a Bare Metal Host into maintenance mode is needed.
resolution: It is possible to detach the BareMetalHost from ironic to avoid unexpected reboots. To do that, two steps needs to be followed: 1. Drain the node: `oc adm drain ` 2. Detach the BareMetalHost from ironic: `oc annotate BareMetalHost baremetalhost.metal3.io/detached`
root_cause: Sometimes, there are some actions that require putting a Bare Metal Host into maintenance mode to avoid unexpected reboots caused by OpenShift. For example, when upgrading the server firmware, putting the Bare Metal Host is needed to be unmanaged by OpenShift.

title: Unable to use WWNID to add Bare Metal Host
issue: In Openshift cluster deployed using Bare Metal IPI, the nodes are managed by machine-api operator (i.e. IPI nodes). The cluster was deployed with openshift version 4.6. When creating Bare Metal Host objects WWNID is used for the rootDeviceHints fields the object enters state `deprovisioning` state, instead of `Available` ~~~ apiVersion: metal3.io/v1alpha1 kind: BareMetalHost metadata: name: Node-1 spec: online: true bootMACAddress: D6:A2:EE:80:7B:77 bmc: address: idrac-virtualmedia://10.10.10.10/redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1 disableCertificateVerification: true credentialsName: node-1-secret rootDeviceHints: wwn: "4x64cd94f0c5fd0642" ~~~
resolution: - Apply errata [RHBA-2022:6372](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:6372) by upgrading to 4.10.32- Apply errata [RHSA-2022:6287](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:6287) by upgrading to 4.11.3
root_cause: IPA uses pyudev to fetch WWNs. Without /run/udev, pyudev returns empty values for them.

title: Operator installation fails with "Bundle unpacking failed. Reason: DeadlineExceeded, and Message: Job was active longer than specified deadline"
issue: Due to a network problem, an Install Plan was not completed, leaving the upgrade unfinished.
resolution: 1) Find the corresponding job and configmap (usually named the same) in the openshift-marketplace and grep for the operator name or keyword in its contents. ~~~ oc get job-n openshift-marketplace-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].value|contains (" ")) |.metadata.name' ~~~ 2) Delete it and the corresponding `configmap`. (named the same as the job) found in the `openshift-marketplace` namespace. ~~~ oc delete job-n openshift-marketplace oc delete configmap-n openshift-marketplace ~~~ 3) Uninstall the failed operator installation using the web UI from the associated namespace. 4) Delete the `install plan`, `subscription`, and `csv` associated to the namespace. ~~~ oc delete ip-n oc delete sub-n oc delete csv-n ~~~ 5) Reinstall the operator via the web UI and the installation should complete successfully. #### CLI command alternative example: The command below will delete all jobs and configmaps related to `3scale` from the `openshift-marketplace` namespace. ~~~ for i in $(oc get job-n openshift-marketplace-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].value|contains ("3scale")) |.metadata.name'); do oc delete job $i-n openshift-marketplace; oc delete configmap $i-n openshift-marketplace; done ~~~
root_cause: The cause is not 100% known but a possible theory is the first time the operator bundle was pulled down from the marketplace, the extract job failed (probably due to an issue accessing the remote image, etc.) and corrupted the configmap. Therefore, the operator manifest was most likely corrupt. Once that happens, any repeat install attempts to use the same job and configmap to install another instance of the operator (i.e. in another namespace) will fail.

title: Yaml to push images to Openshift internal image registry
issue: Yaml to push images to Openshift internal image registry
resolution: - Create a yaml file `apache-image.yaml`. Suppose if you are taking `apache:2.4` as a reference then it will look something like this: ~~~ $ vi apache-image.yaml apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: approved-apache spec: lookupPolicy: local: false tags:- name: "2.4" from: kind: DockerImage name: bitnami/apache:2.4 referencePolicy: type: Source ~~~- Then apply this using oc apply. ~~~ $ oc apply-f apache-image.yaml ~~~- Above mentioned output is doing the same thing as done by using below command: ~~~ oc import-image approved-apache:2.4--from=bitnami/apache:2.4--confirm ~~~- Using an image stream as a source image in a build. Here’s an example of a BuildConfig which uses an image stream as a source: ~~~ kind: BuildConfig apiVersion: build.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: example-app spec: source: type: Git git: uri: 'https://github.com/sclorg/nodejs-ex.git' strategy: type: Source sourceStrategy: from: kind: ImageStreamTag name: 'nodejs-8-centos7:latest' output: to: kind: ImageStreamTag name: 'example-app:latest' triggers:- type: ConfigChange- type: ImageChange ~~~- Triggering when the source image changes. In order to tell OpenShift to keep checking an external image for changes,use the `--scheduled` tag when you use `oc import-image`. ~~~ oc import-image marsview--from=registry.marsrover.space/engine/marsview--scheduled--confirm ~~~
root_cause: - The moment that a new image is pushed to your latest tag, OpenShift will automatically trigger an update of your app using `trigger` functionality.

issue: ~~~ [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 api-v1.apps.example.io..xx.internal.example.net. A: read udp 10.x.x.x:1-> 10.x.x.10:53: i/o timeout [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 api-v1.apps.example.io..xx.internal.example.net. A: read udp 10.x.x.x:2-> 10.x.x.20:53: i/o timeout [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 example.blob.core.windows.net. AAAA: read udp 10.x.x.x:1-> 10.x.x.10:53: i/o timeout [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 example.blob.core.windows.net. AAAA: read udp 10.x.x.x:2-> 10.x.x.20:53: i/o timeout ~~~
root_cause: The pod on the node(10.x.x.2) made a resolution request to the dnsmasq service (port 53) on the node(10.x.x.20), and didn't receive a response. The "AAAA" means that it's an IPv6 request. This is an expected behavior, since ARO doesn't have IPv6 DNS support.

title: Cannot set autoupdate annotation after remove-cluster-role-from-user self-provisioner in OpenShift
issue: - Cannot set autoupdate annotation after remove-cluster-role-from-user self-provisioner in OpenShift
resolution: Apply the following manifest, it makes clusterrolebinding.rbac/self-provisioners with empty subjects and autoupdate=false annotation. ~~~ $ oc apply-f- <
root_cause: The `oc adm policy remove-cluster-role-from-group` removes ClusterRoleBinding resource itself when the target subject is empty: ~~~ $ oc get clusterrolebinding.rbac self-provisioners-o yaml # default configuration apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: annotations: rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate: "true" name: self-provisioner roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: self-provisioner subjects:- apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Group name: system:authenticated:oauth $ oc adm policy remove-cluster-role-from-group self-provisioner system:authenticated:oauth Warning: Your changes may get lost whenever a master is restarted, unless you prevent reconciliation of this rolebinding using the following command: oc annotate clusterrolebinding.rbac self-provisioners 'rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate=false'--overwrite $ oc annotate clusterrolebinding.rbac self-provisioners 'rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate=false'--overwrite Error from server (NotFound): clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "self-provisioners" not found ~~~ After rebooting masters, the self-provisioners will be recreated: ~~~ $ oc get clusterrolebinding.rbac self-provisioners NAME ROLE AGE self-provisioners ClusterRole/self-provisioner 34m ~~~ We need to keep the self-provisioners with empty subjects and autoupdate=false annotation.

title: Did not receive hashvalue for trusted CA value message in OpenShift 4
issue: - What is `Did not receive hashvalue for trusted CA value message` in OpenShift 4?
resolution: It means the ca-bundle.crt is missing for the operator. Some operators create a configmap with a label `config.openshift.io/inject-trusted-cabundle: "true"` to receive the cluster ca-bundle.crt. The `ca-bundle.crt` value will be populated by the cluster-network-operator. This message often appears during operator initial setup when the cluster-network-operator is not yet process the ConfigMap. If the message is repeating and never stops, there might be a problem with the cluster-network-operator.

title: [AMQ Broker] How to build your custom AMQ Broker image using init container image ?
issue: - How to build your custom AMQ Broker 7.8 image using init container image feature?
root_cause: The configuration of the AMQ7 Broker image can be customized using [Init container image feature](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_amq/2020.q4/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#proc-br-specifying-custom-init-container_broker-ocp). Below the procedure based on the following example:- Create the registry secret export IMG_NAME="amq-broker-init" export PROJECT=amq78 oc create secret docker-registry registry-redhat-io \--docker-server=registry.redhat.io \--docker-username=xxxxx \--docker-password=xxx \--docker-email=xxxx- Create config directory and the `post-config.sh`in order to add or customize your AMQ Broker configuration: mkdir-p config && cd config cat < <"EOF" > post-config.sh #!/bin/bash echo "############## Example Custom Script ###############" echo "## ##" echo "## This is an example configure script. ##" echo "## ##" echo "####################################################" echo "#### The config dir locates at ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR} ####" ls ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR} echo Adding a new account "test" with password "test" printf '\n' > > ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}/etc/artemis-users.properties echo "test = test" > > ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}/etc/artemis-users.properties # visitor has role 'viewer' # /etc/artemis-roles.properties echo "adding test role as viewer" printf '\n' > > "${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}"/etc/artemis-roles.properties echo "viewer = test" > > ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}/etc/artemis-roles.properties ## Add role 'viewer' to HAWTIO_ROLE so that it can login to the console sed-i "s/hawtio.role=admin/hawtio.role=admin,viewer/g" ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}/etc/artemis.profile echo "#### Custom config done. ####" EOF chmod-R 777 post-config.sh cd..- Create the `Dockerfile` in order to build your custom init image: cat < Dockerfile FROM registry.redhat.io/amq7/amq-broker-init-rhel7:0.2-13 COPY./config/ /amq/scripts/ EOF- Create a build and reference the `Dockerfile`: oc new-build--binary--name=$IMG_NAME-l app=$IMG_NAME oc patch bc/$IMG_NAME-p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"dockerStrategy":{"dockerfilePath":"Dockerfile"}}}}' oc set build-secret--pull bc/$IMG_NAME registry-redhat-io- Start the build oc start-build $IMG_NAME--from-dir=.--follow- Once the build finished, you should see similar lines at the end: Storing signatures Successfully pushed image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/amq78/amq-broker- init@sha256:1a4d5915cb783f0c9a10df27e7acbeee279ea726a3a02b08a58d02fdc1456fd8 Push successful- In the `activemqartemis` CR specify the `initImage` in `deploymentPlan` section: apiVersion: broker.amq.io/v2alpha4 kind: ActiveMQArtemis metadata: name: broker spec: deploymentPlan: size: 1 image: registry.redhat.io/amq7/amq-broker:7.8 initImage: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/amq78/amq-broker-init- In the broker logs, the following line will be generated: broker-container-init user defined CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR, copying broker-container-init amq-broker broker-container-init exposing env var CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR for custom init broker-container-init CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR value from /amq/init/config broker-container-init Exported value of CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR: /amq/init/config/amq-broker broker-container-init Finding default custom script at /amq/scripts/post-config.sh broker-container-init Found custom script /amq/scripts/post-config.sh, executing it broker-container-init /amq/scripts/post-config.sh

title: Access rook-ceph-tools pod without oc rsh.
issue: - `oc rsh` and `oc exec` to a pod don't work although the pod runs fine.
resolution: A definitive fix is being worked at [BZ#2034883], so if you hit this issue, please open a support case with Red Hat for proper tracking. A workaround would be to access the container from the using `crictl` from the node on which it is running. 1. Check in which node the rook-ceph-tools pod is running ~~~ TOOLS_HOST=$(oc-n openshift-storage get pods-owide |grep rook-ceph-tools) ~~~ 2. Login to that node using the SSH key ~~~ ssh core@$TOOLS_HOST-i ~~~ 3. Open bash session to the rook-ceph-tools pod ~~~ CONTAINER_ID=$(crictl ps|grep rook-ceph-tools|awk '{print $1}') circtl exec-it $CONTAINER_ID /bin/bash ~~~
root_cause: This issue happens when there are nodes that are in a `Not Ready` state at the time when the the `kubelet-to-kube-apiserver-ca` was renewed. The `kubelet-to-kube-apiserver-ca` signs the client certificate used by Kube APIServer to encrypt the communication with Kubelet on port 10250, which is the port used for `oc rsh` and `oc exec` commands. During the renewal process the Machince Config Operator is responsible for pushing the new client certificate to all the cluster nodes, however because there are nodes in a `Not Ready` state the new certificate is not pushed out, which breaks the communication between Kube APIServer, and Kubelet. I understand that currently oc exec, and oc rsh command do not work, and they are needed to perform to access the rook-ceph-tools pods and perform the ODF node removal procedure. You can use the below method to access the pod directly from the node its running on.

title: Openshift registry image prunning saves few space
issue: The OpenShift Cluster Registry has gotten bloated with images from CI/CD, after do standard cleanup procedure like this: ~~~ oc adm prune deployments--orphans--keep-complete=5--keep-failed=1--keep-younger-than=60m--confirm oc adm prune builds--orphans--keep-complete=5--keep-failed=1--keep-younger-than=60m--confirm oc adm prune images--keep-tag-revisions=3--keep-younger-than=60m--confirm ~~~ Only a small percentage of the space used is cleaned. Also there are few `imageStream` objects that contains hundreds or thousand of tags but only a few are used: ~~~ $ image_name="sha256:111122223333444455556666777788889999AAAABBBBCCCCDDDDEEEEFFFFGGGGH" $ oc get is-n cicd-project-o go-template='{{range $isi, $is:=.items}}{{range $ti, $tag:= $is.status.tags}}{{range $ii, $item:= $tag.items}}{{if eq $item.image "'$image_name'"}}{{$is.metadata.name}}:{{$tag.tag}} at position {{$ii}} out of {{len $tag.items}} {{end}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}' cicd-project-imagestream:tag-123456 at position 0 out of 1 cicd-project-imagestream:tag-abcdef at position 505 out of 1000 ~~~ The suggestion in [the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/admin_guide/pruning_resources.html "the documentation") is to run oc adm prune images with--keep-tag-revisions=0, is this safe?
resolution: We don't recommend to use the option "--keep-tag-revisions=0" to clean up the registry tags in big imageStreams, it basically means to delete everything and probably will delete more than you expect. Consider also that there is no automatic way to delete the tags from those `imageStreams` with huge number of tags as it is impossible to decide which one is valid or not. In cases like this a conscious manual approach is the recommended way.

title: Are ACLs with NFSv4 supported in OCP 4.8 ?
issue: - ACLs with NFSv4 was not supported with 4.6 and it's advised to use security context instead.- Can we use ACL with NFS4 when ACL is disabled on the NFS4 backend?
resolution: - NFSv4 ACLs exist at the protocol level and this is supported within the Red Hat Enterprise Linux kernel and by extension the RHCOS kernel as it is based on RHEL kernel with a different userspace construction to make it immutable. It is not recommended to install individual packages on an RHCOS node.- If there is a need to use a particular binary that is not installed at the host level, you can build a container[1] with the necessary binary and use the said container as needed. Such a case could be done with nfs4-acl-tools. That all being said,nfs4-acl-tools is used for the configuration and administration of ACLs from the NFS_client_ side and does not relate to ACL support as that exists within the kernel. It would be more prudent to configure/administrate ACLs at the storage backend versus the front.- If ACLs are not supported on the backend storage device then it is not possible to configure them on the client. If the NFS server itself does not support ACLs, where they actually exist within the filesystem, then it is not possible to configure them on the client side. [1] [How to use a different image with a toolbox and oc debug node in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4929021)

title: Migrate Azure private DNS zone in Openshift Container Platform 4
issue: - What are the steps needed to migrate Azure DNS zones from legacy to newer?
resolution: 1. List the DNS zones available for migration: ~~~ $ openshift-install migrate azure-privatedns-eligible ~~~ 2. Migrate the DNS zone: ~~~ $ openshift-install migrate azure-privatedns--resource-group=rg--zone=example.com--virtual-network-resource-group=rg--virtual-network=myvnet--link ~~~
root_cause: The following is an example for the [CPCORE-7758](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CPCORE-7758):- Not indenting the block: ~~~ line1: no spaces line2: 2 spaces line3: 4 spaces line4: 6 spaces ~~~- Indenting the block adding 2 spaces before `~~~`, the block is indented but the content is not shown with correct spaces: ~~~ line1: no spaces line2: 2 spaces line3: 4 spaces line4: 6 spaces ~~~- The expectation is to have the block indented without losing the spaces, the following is done by adding 8 spaces for each line and removing the lines with `~~~`: line1: no spaces line2: 2 spaces line3: 4 spaces line4: 6 spaces- Indenting the block adding **4** spaces before the `~~~` and before each line, the block is indented: ~~~ line1: no spaces line2: 2 spaces line3: 4 spaces line4: 6 spaces ~~~

title: Decrease in the limit of number of disks that can be attached to the node.
issue: - Decrease in the number of disks that can be attached to the node from 32 to 16.- After updating machineset from **Standard_E32as_v4*
to **Standard_E32as_v5*
there is a decrease in the number of disks that can be attached to the node on the Azure Platform.
resolution: - This is a known issue that is captured in the [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2118392) and is fixed in RH OCP 4.10.30.- The table is not updated and hence node describes returns a default value of 16.- 4.10 (or k8s 1.23) is simply not aware of these new instance types and their attach limits on the node.- This only applies to the CSI volumes and not on the in-tree azure disk, avoid using the in-tree volume plugin `kubernetes.io/azure-disk` entirely.

title: PrivateLink cluster do not have a Network tab in Hybrid Cloud Console
issue: - My cluster does not have a network tab in Hybrid Cloud Console- My Network tab is missing from the Hybrid Cloud Console- How do I add a 2nd router without a Networking tab in Hybrid Cloud Console
resolution: Private link clusters and STS clusters do not have a Networking tab in Hybrid Cloud Console by design. Additional public and private routers can be added to the cluster by adding a Custom Domain cluster resource. More details on custom domains can be found in the [ROSA documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/applications/deployments/osd-config-custom-domains-applications.html) **Note:** Altering the default router is not recommended as it could take the cluster into an UnManaged state.
root_cause: For STS clusters the Hybrid Cloud Console can not request the appropriate level of access required to perform the tasks. For PrivateLink clusters, the Networking tab is unnecessary as this tab was provided to enable cluster admins to make their standard ROSA (public) clusters private. But the cluster admins can still add or alter additional routers by [configuring additional Custom Domains](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/applications/deployments/osd-config-custom-domains-applications.html) resources. **Note:** Altering the default router is not recommended as it could take the cluster into an UnManaged state.

title: Step by step Datagrid 8 sql-cache-store in OCP 4
issue: How to set up Datagrid 8 sql-cache-store?
resolution: Step by step to set up the persistence in a cache is detailed below. To add SQL cache persistence follow the steps below, for simply adding file-store persistence, see solution [Adding persistence in a cache in RHDG 8 in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6960765) ## Preparation 1. Create a new project: `oc new-project $projectname` 2. Install the DG Operator. Can be installed either:- The SupportHub console- Or declaring a CR to the OLM, see example with latest DG Operator (8.3.8): ~~~ apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: datagrid-operator namespace: ${OPERATOR_NAMESPACE} spec: channel: 8.3.x installPlanApproval: Manual name: datagrid source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: datagrid-operator.v8.3.8 ~~~ ### Install the DB and set it up One can use the pre-loaded templates, otherwise `imagestream`, or helm charts. 1. Add the DataBase from the OCP console- given inside the project on the `Developer View` in the developer catalog 2. Wait for deployment complete and login on postgre pod terminal and login with following command: `psql-h 0.0.0.0-d sampledb-U user` 3. Create a table for `query-jdbc-store`: ~~~ CREATE TABLE_keys(_id SERIAL NOT NULL,_key VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,_value VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (_id)); ~~~ 4. Add entries to the DB table and fetch it- to test it if the entries (rows) got registered ### Set up the drivers on the DG 8 As detailed on [Supported cache stores in DG 8 in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6965413) there are two options for setting up the driver on the pods:- One options is to copy code artifacts to Data Grid clusters: by copying the code artifacts to a pod so that they are loaded into a PV/PVC, which can be fetched by the other pods. And then remove the pod.- Using Infinispan CR's `spec.dependencies.artifacts` field to make DG Operator fetch content, which can be an url with a jar that can be fetched. ### Create cluster There are two ways to set the cluster:- Via DG Operator- Via yaml declaration: ~~~- apiVersion: infinispan.org/v1 kind: Infinispan metadata: name: ${CLUSTER_NAME} namespace: ${CLUSTER_NAMESPACE} annotations: infinispan.org/monitoring: 'false' labels: type: middleware prometheus_domain: ${CLUSTER_NAME} spec: configMapName: "${CLUSTER_NAME}-custom-config" container: cpu: '2' extraJvmOpts: '-Xlog:gc*=info:file=/tmp/gc.log:time,level,tags,uptimemillis:filecount=10,filesize=1m' memory: 3Gi... dependencies: artifacts:- url: https://github.com/FranciscoMeloJr/EJBtests/blob/master/jgroups-5.0.0.Alpha6.jar?raw=true ~~~ ^ Example above has `spec.dependencies.artifacts` for fetching the DB jar. ### Create protobuf Login to the Datagrid console and click on Schemas and create a new one. There are two ways to do it:- via cli command, example: `schema--upload=example.proto example.proto`- via DG console: one can create (ie. write one) one directly on the console, given the console having a text editor ### Create cache with the proto schema above There are two ways to create the cache:- via DG console inside the DG cluster- Declare an CR via yaml. Example use the yaml to create a new cache with the protoschema setting up the persistence inside the cache: ~~~ {"distributed-cache":{"encoding": {"media-type": "application/x-protostream"}, "persistence":{"query-jdbc-store":{"dialect":"ORACLE", "shared":"true", "key-columns":"key", "queries":{"select-single":"SELECT id, key, value FROM ot.keys WHERE key =:key", "select-all":"SELECT id, key, value FROM ot.keys", "delete-single":"DELETE FROM_keys WHERE key =:key", "delete-all":"DELETE FROM ot.keys", "upsert":"INSERT INTO ot.keys(key,value) VALUES(:key,:value)", "size":"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ot.keys"}, "schema":{"message-name":"KeyOracle_value", "key-message-name": "KeyOracle_key", "package":"com.example", "embedded-key":"true"}, "connection-pool": {"connection-url": "jdbc:oracle:thin:@//oracle19c:1521/ABCPDB1", "driver": "oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver", "username": "ot", "password": "Orcl1234"}}}}} ~~~ ^ The connection-pool is where the conection-url is set, which is fetch from the first part of this solution ### SSL authentication with DB using TCPS protocol (TLS+TCP) One needs to set up the `javax.net.ssl.trustStore`'s path and `trustStorePassword` either at data-source level, or at DG JVM level. Either at datasource level OR DG JVM level. Example data source: ~~~ /path/to/store secret ~~~ Example DG JVM level- which you need to pass on the custom resource for the cluster (Infinispan CR): ~~~-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/path/to/truststore-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=.... ~~~
root_cause: The persistence is setup for each cache configuration, where one sets two main attributes- set via tags: `encoding` and the `persistence`, which has `query-jdbc-store` (dialect, shared, key-collums, and queries), `schema`, and `connection-pool`. ### SQL limitations and features For details on SQL storage see [DG 8- Persistence Chap 6.10. SQL cache stores](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.3/html/configuring_data_grid_caches/persistence#sql-cache-store_persistence). **SQL Store doesn't support expiration.** ### Supported cache stores in DG 8 in OCP 4 For details on which are the supported cache stores see [Supported cache stores in DG 8 in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6965413). ### H2 DB Also note configuring an in-memory H2 DB store is not recommend and does not add anything as feature to JDG/DG.

title: [Compliance Operator]: Compliance profile maps to which Industry compliance benchmark
issue: - How to map the compliance CIS profiles to the Industry compliance benchmark?- Which compliance profile is referred to as the Industry compliance benchmark?
resolution: - Run the following command to check the compliance profile and reference the Industry compliance benchmark: ~~~ # oc get profile.compliance-n openshift-compliance-o yaml-o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,COMPLIANCE-BENCHMARK:.title ~~~- Run the following command to review the rule and reference the Industry compliance benchmark: ~~~ # oc get rule-o yaml-o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STANDARD:.metadata.annotations.policies\\.open-cluster-management\\.io/standards,CONTROLS:.metadata.annotations.policies\\.open-cluster-management\\.io/controls,CIS-OCP:.metadata.annotations.control\\.compliance\\.openshift\\.io/CIS-OCP,NERC-CIP:.metadata.annotations.control\\.compliance\\.openshift\\.io/NERC-CIP,NIST-800-53:.metadata.annotations.control\\.compliance\\.openshift\\.io/NIST-800-53,PCI-DSS:.metadata.annotations.control\\.compliance\\.openshift\\.io/PCI-DSS ~~~- For more details refer to the [document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/security/compliance_operator/compliance-operator-supported-profiles.html).
root_cause: - Compliance Operator individually does not refer to the CIS Standard version. Details can be only seen in the `profile.compliance` object of the compliance operator.

title: [MTC] Migrating from RHOCP 3.11 to RHOCP 4.8 fails when using NFS StorageClass backed by Trident/Netapp CSI and rsync
issue: - Migration Toolkit for Containers (MTC) is failing when migrating `pvc/nfs-trident` between two OpenShift clusters:- Source cluster is v3.11 and Destination cluster is v4.8.- Failures in `rsync` operation can be seen: `rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors) (code 23)`.- This only happens when the `StorageClass` is Trident (Netapp) NFS:- NFS v3 and v4 are both affected.- Other storage (such as vmdk/VMWare) does not seem to be affected.- Other services that use Trident-based volumes (such as backup processes) work as expected.- `rsync` tries to copy a directory `.snapshot` that does not exit on Source cluster.- Other workloads using the Trident `StorageClass` are not showing incorrect behavior. This only seems to happen with MTC workloads.
resolution: - While configuring the migration steps on MTC Web UI, uncheck both "direct image migration" and "direct `pvc`";- By doing so, MTC will use `restic` instead of `rsync`.- `restic` is more container aware then `rsync` and doesn't fail on `xattr` during the copy process.- A `velero` backup is created on source cluster and restored on destination. If this do not solve the issue, please refer to the official documentation: [Migration Toolkit for Containers Troubleshooting](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/migration_toolkit_for_containers/troubleshooting-mtc.html#logs-and-debugging-tools_troubleshooting-mtc) or open a support case with Red Hat.
root_cause: - Direct migration (faster) copies all tributes like `selinux` labels, permissions etc;- `nfs` does not support certain file properties as above- during the copy `rsync` fails because of file `xattr`- The `rsync` client fails after around 20 attempts with the following error message:- `"test4 rsync-2shpt rsync 2022/10/03 21:38:04 [115] rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors) (code 23) at main.c(1189) [sender=3.1.3]"`- The error only happens when the `StorageClass` in use is backed by Trident/NetApp with either NFS 3 or 4.

title: openshift-storage project stuck in terminating state
issue: - `openshift-storage` project is stuck in terminating state
resolution: - Identify the resources which need to be deleted from the `openshift-storage` project. Check ***Diagnostic Steps***.- After the objects are identified, try deleting the resource. If that does not help, patch the resources. ~~~ $ oc patch-n /--type=merge-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":null}}' ~~~
root_cause: - Resources hold the project from deletion even if all the objects from the project are deleted.

title: [AMQ Streams] Integrating data from MQTT installation failed with Error : GET /connectors/mqtt-connector/config returned 500 (Internal Server Error): Request timed out
issue: - Integrate data from an installation that communicates via MQTT protocol using the below steps getting failed with error 500 (Internal Server Error):- Installed Kafka cluster- Deployed a kafka connect cluster- Created a custom image with came MQTT plugins- Created a kafka connector.- But the connector remains not ready with the below error:- GET /connectors/mqtt-connector/config returned 500 (Internal Server Error): Request timed out..
resolution: - Camel Kafka Connector has been only a Technology Preview stopped a time ago, [Camel-Kafka-Connector](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_integration/2020-q4/html/getting_started_with_camel_kafka_connector/introduction-to-camel-kafka-connector) and [Red Hat Technology Preview](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview). However, it has never had an MQTT sink/source connector. That connector has been always upstream only, [MQTT for upstream only](https://camel.apache.org/camel-kafka-connector/1.0.x/reference/connectors/camel-mqtt-source-kafka-source-connector.html). The supported replacement for Camel Kafka Connector MQTT can be:- [Kamelet Binding with AMQ Broker- MQTT support](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_integration/2022.q3/html-single/integrating_applications_with_kamelets/index#connecting-source-to-kafka) for a zero-code approach on Openshift- [Camel Extensions for Quarkus](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_integration/2022.q3/html/camel_extensions_for_quarkus_reference/camel-quarkus-extensions-overview), (Paho MQTT client available)- [Camel 3 on SpringBoot](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_integration/2022.q3/html/getting_started_with_camel_spring_boot/getting-started-with-camel-spring-boot_csb#camel-spring-boot-list) (shortly GA) with AMQ Broker (MQTT support)
root_cause: Kafka has never had an MQTT sink/source connector. That connector has been always upstream only.

title: Role for non-admin user to create PV
issue: - Is there any way a user can create PV with no cluster-admin or storage-admin role.
resolution: - Create a clusterrole as shown in below command. This will allow the user to create,update and list the PV at project level. ~~~ $ oc create clusterrole storage-admin-test--verb=create,update,patch,get,list,watch--resource=persistentvolumes,storageclasses ~~~- Assign the role to the non admin user using below command: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user storage-admin-test ~~~
root_cause: - The Persistent Volume (PV) is a cluster-wide resource, hence it will be created by either cluster-admin/storage-admin or a custom role can be created which can be assigned to the user.

title: Restricting Machine API IAM policy on AWS
issue: On AWS, the default Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy requested by the Machine API includes wide permissions for the `iam:PassRole` permission. It defaults to `'*'`, which allows any administrator with access to create or modify compute machine sets to assume any IAM policy when creating new machines.
resolution: To resolve this issue, administrators must use the Cloud Credential Operator in manual mode. More details about manual mode can be found in the [OpenShift Container Platform product documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/installing_aws/manually-creating-iam.html#manually-creating-iam-aws). Once you have configured your cluster to use manual mode, you can edit the AWS IAM policies created by the installation program for Machine API and restrict them to just the roles required by your cluster. The default roles created by the installation program are called `-worker-role` and `-master-role` for the worker and control plane machines respectively. 1. Find the Machine API user minted by the Cloud Credential Operator and edit the policy document attached to the user. The user will be called `-openshift-machine-api-aws- `. 2. Remove the existing `iam:PassRole` permission from the policy document. 3. Add a new statement to the policy document that allows the `iam:PassRole` for just the required roles. It will look something like below: ~~~ {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["iam:PassRole"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/-worker-role", "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/-master-role"]} ~~~ Important: Substitute the correct AWS account ID when updating the policy document.
root_cause: When creating `CredentialsRequest` custom resources, OpenShift Container Platform cannot know about the individual circumstances of a particular installation. The permissions requested are global and must apply to all clusters. As the product cannot know the names of the roles that are created by the installation program ahead of time, it must allow the Machine API to pass any role so that it can create the worker machines to complete the cluster installation.

title: oc-mirror does not generate a complete list of ICSP and catalogsources
issue: - As part of the output artifacts oc-mirror creates a list of ImageContentSourcePolicy objects to apply to the target cluster.- However, this list only contains images synced in the current run and does not provide a full list of ICSPs to apply to the cluster.- This means that one needs to merge all ICSPs from the different runs of an on-mirror sync, which is a manual and tedious task. Also if you start dropping operators / images from being synced, you have to manually remove them from your ICSPs. We are asking that oc-mirror produces after each run a full list of ImageContentSourcePolicy objects representing all available operators / images which path we have to redirect using an ICSP. This will allow us to simply apply the articats produced by oc-mirror to the disconnected clusters. The same behavior goes with the operator catalog images. You only get CatalogSource kinds for the catalog indexes produced in the particular run. If there is none, you do not get a catalog source.
resolution: [RFE-3000](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3000) has been raised. It is not resolved yet. Please open a support case with Red Hat to receive updates on this.

title: How to determine blob having large size in the image registry and which images are using the largest blob ?
issue: - Is there a way to check which image has a large disk usage on an image registry?
resolution: The resolution provides the steps to determine blob having large size in the image registry and which images are using the largest blob in the image registry. The folder */registry/docker/registry/v2* is the main repository to store the sha256 files. 1. Find the biggest Blobs (over 20MB) ~~~ $ TOKEN=$(oc whoami-t) $ Registry_POD=$(oc get pod-n openshift-image-registry | grep "^image-registry-" | awk '($3 =="Running"){print $1}' | head-1) $ URL=image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 $ oc rsh-n openshift-image-registry ${Registry_POD} $ BLOB_FOLDER=/registry/docker/registry/v2 $ SIZE=20000k $ find ${BLOB_FOLDER}-type f-name data-size +${SIZE}-exec ls-ld {} \; | awk '{print $5"/"$(NF)}' | awk-F'/' '{print $1" "$(NF-1)}' | sort 67327737 f2899b6ca6e3fb889044560a37dd31fd3a5061483175066db7ce7d6c00025fa0 78357770 0c673eb68f88b60abc0cba5ef8ddb9c256eaf627bfd49eb7e09a2369bb2e5db0 $ exit ~~~ 2. To display blob having a large size in the image registry and which images are using the largest blob ~~~ $ blob_name=f2899b6ca6e3fb889044560a37dd31fd3a5061483175066db7ce7d6c00025fa0 ~~~ 3. Create a file *test.sh* with the following content: ~~~ TOKEN=$(oc whoami-t) Registry_POD=$(oc get pod-n openshift-image-registry | grep "^image-registry-" | awk '($3 =="Running"){print $1}' | head-1) URL=image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 for repo in $(oc rsh-n openshift-image-registry ${Registry_POD} curl-k-s-H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://${URL}/v2/_catalog | jq-r '.repositories[]') do echo-e "\n===== ${repo} ====" for tag in $(oc rsh-n openshift-image-registry ${Registry_POD} curl-k-s-H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://${URL}/v2/${repo}/tags/list | jq-r '.tags[]') do echo-e "\n######### ${tag}" oc rsh-n openshift-image-registry ${Registry_POD} curl-k-s-H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://${URL}/v2/${repo}/manifests/${tag} | jq-r '.fsLayers[].blobSum' done done > /tmp/blob_list.txt ~~~ 4. Execute the file *test.sh* ~~~ chmod +x./test.sh./test.sh > /dev/null 2> &1 ~~~ 5. Search the biggest Blob ($blob_name) in the manifest file *tmp/blob_list.txt* ~~~ $ awk-v blobname=${blob_name} 'BEGIN{repo="";tag="";print "REPO|TAG|BLOB"}{if($1 == "====="){repo=$2};if($1 == "#########"){tag=$2};if($1 == "sha256:"blobname){print repo"|"tag"|sha256:"blobname}}' /tmp/blob_list.txt | column-s '|'-t REPO TAG BLOB *openshift/httpd* 2.4-el8 sha256:f2899b6ca6e3fb889044560a37dd31fd3a5061483175066db7ce7d6c00025fa0 *openshift/httpd* latest sha256:f2899b6ca6e3fb889044560a37dd31fd3a5061483175066db7ce7d6c00025fa0 *test/httpd-example* latest sha256:f2899b6ca6e3fb889044560a37dd31fd3a5061483175066db7ce7d6c00025fa0 ~~~

title: OpenShift installer failed to decode instruction
issue: - OpenShift installer CLI on M1 Macbook fails due to following errors at random stages: ~~~ DEBUG commands will detect it and remind you to do so if necessary. assertion failed [inst.has_value()]: failed to decode instruction: 0x0 (StateRecovery.cpp:355 determine_state_recovery_action_forward_branches) ~~~
resolution: - Ensure that the installer binary being used is for darwin/arm64 architecture: ~~~ $./openshift-install version ~~~- Update the GoLang runtime to the latest version, and export the following variable: ~~~ $ export 'GODEBUG="asyncpreemptoff=1"' ~~~- After exporting the variable, re-run the `openshift-install` command, and share the output with [Red Hat support](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true).
root_cause: - This issue is most likely due to Golang/Rosetta problem.- Exporting the `asyncpreemptoff`with value as `1` allows debugging the program with clearer insights.

title: tekton-resource-pruner job is failing and eventually causing KubeJobFailed alert to fire on OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: Every morning at about 08:15 UTC we are seeing the below Prometheus Alert firing because some `tekton-resource-pruner` job seems to fail. alertname = KubeJobFailed condition = true container = kube-rbac-proxy-main endpoint = https-main job = kube-state-metrics job_name = tekton-resource-pruner-lvjmq-27537600 namespace = openshift-pipelines openshift_io_alert_source = platform prometheus = openshift-monitoring/k8s service = kube-state-metrics severity = warning Annotations description = Job openshift-pipelines/tekton-resource-pruner-lvjmq-12345678 failed to complete. Removing failed job after investigation should clear this alert. runbook_url = https://github.com/openshift/runbooks/blob/master/alerts/cluster-monitoring-operator/KubeJobFailed.md summary = Job failed to complete.
`tekton-resource-pruner` job is failing and eventually causing `KubeJobFailed` alert to fire on OpenShift Container Platform 4
Automatic pruning of task run and pipeline run is failing
resolution: This problem was solved in Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines [1.8](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/cicd/pipelines/op-release-notes.html#op-release-notes-1-8_op-release-notes) and later. With Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines [1.8](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/cicd/pipelines/op-release-notes.html#op-release-notes-1-8_op-release-notes), the `pruner` passes the namespace-based configuration to the job so that all the commands run in one container in a loop. ### Workaround 1 Only run the [automatic pruning of task run and pipeline run](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/cicd/pipelines/automatic-pruning-taskrun-pipelinerun.html) on the `namespaces` containing Red Hat OpenShift Pipeline objects as by default each `namespace` on the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Cluster is considered by pruning. For this, the `annotation` `operator.tekton.dev/prune.skip` can be set to `true` on each `namespace` that shall be skipped. ### Workaround 2 Completely disable [automatic pruning of task run and pipeline run](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/cicd/pipelines/automatic-pruning-taskrun-pipelinerun.html) by removing the `pruner` section in the `TektonConfig` resource. * Run `oc edit TektonConfig config` and remove the below section: pruner: resources:- pipelinerun- taskrun keep: 100 schedule: "0 8 * * *" * This will remove the `tekton-resource-pruner` `cronjob` and thus prevent any Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines pruning activity from running.
root_cause: Too many containers running in parallel in the `tekton-resource-pruner` pod, causing some of them to timeout which consequently will cause the respective job to fail and eventually trigger a `KubeJobFailed` alert to fire.

title: Why the tcp_mem/udp_mem is different in RHEL 6 and RHEL 7 when the physical memory are same?
issue: - The Physical RAM is same, but after reinstall the RHEL 7, I found that the net.ipv4.tcp_mem and net.ipv4.udp_mem is different, which is smaller than its in RHEL 6.
resolution: - That's because the page calculation method is different, which is expected.
root_cause: - In RHEL 7, it is depended on nr_free_buffer_pages(), which will call nr_free_zone_pages(), and will cut the high watermark of pages. But the RHEL 6 will not. So the "limit" variable in RHEL 6 is larger than which in RHEL 7.

title: Configure CA for connecting the helm repo in Argo CD

SSL handshake has read 3185 bytes and written 436 bytes Verification: OK--- ~~~- Try to connect the repo in Argocd ~~~- In the Argo cd gui: Settings-> Repoistories-> CONNECT REPO USING HTTPS Name: Repository: Connection status: Passed ~~~- Please Note ~~~- The server name for the TLS cert has to be the same as the server to which you are trying to connect to. ~~~

title: [ACM] Unable to find machinepools for clusters created using CIM/ZTP
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - ACM Cluster Ui page does not machinepools for openshift clusters that were created using CIM/ZTP/Assisted-Service
resolution: - Machinepools are not supported in case of Baremetal host.- The only way in which you can scale the openshift clusters is by adding new nodes to the "Infrastructure Environment" using the discovery ISO.
root_cause: - MachinePools are a way to say you want X workers, Y infrastructure etc and toggle the replicas per MachinePool.- The controller turns MachinePools into MachineSets (using the installer API) that are sent to the managed cluster and actuated by the machine API for that cluster.- All of that assumes a lot more ability to be dynamic than bare metal clusters typically have.

title: Pods  evicted due to Memory Pressure on node in RHCOP 4
issue: - Application `pods` are getting `Evicted` during load testing: ~~~ $ oc get pod--all-namespaces | grep Evicted customer-gateway-6cd8f7b6c5-29hhg 0/2 Evicted 0 13h ocpw2 customer-gateway-6cd8f7b6c5-2bww2 0/2 Evicted 0 13h ocpw2 ~~~- Error log indicating `memory pressure` on the `node`: ~~~ default 14m Warning EvictionThresholdMet node/ocpw2.xxx.xxx.com Attempting to reclaim memory ~~~
resolution: - Set a [pod limits](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/nodes/clusters/nodes-cluster-limit-ranges.html#nodes-cluster-limit-pod-limits) that will allow specifying the minimum and maximum CPU and memory limits for all containers across a pod in a given project or [Resouce quota](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/applications/quotas/quotas-setting-per-project.html) that limit aggregate resource consumption per project.- Increase resources on the node.
root_cause: - This behavior is caused when the `pods` are getting `scheduled` to the `nodes` without any `resource limits` and consuming all available node memory. The best practice is to set quotas and limits on the node.

title: Use a custom SCC with OpenShift Pipelines
issue: Unable to use a custom SCC with OpenShift Pipelines.
resolution: - In OpenShift Piplines you can change the default service account used for executing pipelineruns and taskruns through TektonConfig CR (spec.pipeline.default-service-account).- You can have your custom service account associated with your custom scc and as a result, every pipelinerun and taskrun would use that scc for execution.- Keep in mind that the custom service account and custom scc need to be created and present in every namespace that pipelineruns and taskruns execute. One way to achieve that is to create them together with the namespace, quotas, resource limits, etc when a user requests a namespace on the platform.
root_cause: You currently can only use custom SCC by applying it to every namespace as listed above. The flowing [plan](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPPLAN-9661) has been created to change this.

title: Why can't the cluster-reader ClusterRole access all resources in a cluster?
issue: When using an account with the `cluster-reader` ClusterRole, it can not access Secrets, EgressFirewall, ServiceMonitor and many other resource types. Why is the definition of cluster-reader not: ~~~ apiVersion: authorization.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: view-all-the-things rules:- apiGroups:- '*' resources:- '*' verbs:- get- list ~~~ Is there a security reason for not doing this?
root_cause: When providing Users access to a ClusterRole with the ability to read all Resources and CustomResources in the cluster, such as seen in the `view-all-the-things` ClusterRole, this will include providing access to view the credentials that may be used for cluster-wide write permissions. For example, if the following steps were performed on the cluster, it would show the vulnerabilities created by this ClusterRole. **NOTE: DO NOT PERFORM THESE STEPS ON YOUR PRODUCTION CLUSTERS AND THEY ARE ONLY PROVIDED FOR TESTING PURPOSES.** ### Reproduction Steps: 1. Create the `view-all-the-things` ClusterRole ~~~ |⇒ oc apply-f view-all-the-things.yaml clusterrole.authorization.openshift.io/view-all-the-things created ~~~ 2. Create a new User called `view-user` in `default` Namespace. Associate the ClusterRole with the `view-user`. ~~~ |⇒ oc create sa view-user serviceaccount/view-user created |⇒ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user view-all-the-things system:serviceaccount:default:view-user clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/view-all-the-things added: "system:serviceaccount:default:view-user" |⇒ TOKEN=$(oc view-secret view-user-token-5j5wn token) |⇒ oc whoami--token="$TOKEN" system:serviceaccount:default:view-user ~~~ 3. The `view-user` can read the ClusterRoleBindings and see which Identities have access to the `cluster-admin` RBAC policies ~~~ |⇒ oc get clusterrolebinding | grep openshift-apiserver system:openshift:openshift-apiserver ClusterRole/cluster-admin 2d18h--- openshift-apiserver-sa is chosen--- ~~~ 4. The `view-user` can read the Token of these ServiceAccounts ~~~ |⇒ oc get sa-n openshift-apiserver openshift-apiserver-sa-o jsonpath='{.secrets}' [{"name":"openshift-apiserver-sa-token-wv5l2"},{"name":"openshift-apiserver-sa-dockercfg-l5w2n"}]% ~~~ 5. The developer/user with access to the `view-user` can impersonate the elevated ServiceAccount to perform actions ~~~ |⇒ TOKEN=$(oc view-secret-n openshift-apiserver openshift-apiserver-sa-token-wv5l2 token) |⇒ oc whoami--token="$TOKEN" system:serviceaccount:openshift-apiserver:openshift-apiserver-sa ~~~ 6. Additional step: The developer/user can leverage the elevated user to add the `cluster-admin` ClusterRole to the `view-user` account ~~~ |⇒ oc adm policy--token="$TOKEN" add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-admin view-user clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/cluster-admin added: "view-user" ~~~ ### Additional Notes The pre-defined ClusterRoles in OpenShift are built with security in-mind and this exploit is not possible when leveraging the existing `cluster-reader` ClusterRole. For example, `cluster-reader` does not have access to Secrets: ~~~ |⇒ oc get clusterrole cluster-reader-o yaml | grep-ie secret ~~~ Red Hat recommends ensuring that all users are only provided the minimal set of permissions that they require.

title: Diagnosing etcdInsufficientMembers alert in OpenShift Container Platform 4.
issue: Why is `etcdInsufficientMembers` alert showing up?
How should I detect potential issues when the `etcdInsufficientMembers`alert shows?
How to understand `etcdInsufficientMembers`?
root_cause: This alert fires when there are fewer instances available than are needed by etcd to be healthy. When etcd does not have a majority of instances available, the Kubernetes and OpenShift APIs will reject read and write requests and operations that preserve the health of workloads cannot be performed. This can occur when multiple control plane nodes are powered off as a false positive if it is a planned activity, or are unable to connect each other via the network. Check that all control plane nodes are powered and that network connections between each machine are functional in the host platform.

title: Install operator ,job error rejected: Running image is rejected by policy.
issue: Unable to install the operator normally
resolution: Edit the image.config.openshift.io/cluster custom resource: ~~~ oc edit images.config.openshift.io cluster... spec: additionalTrustedCA: name: cnuatocp-registry-ca externalRegistryHostnames:- default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.cnuat.ocbc.com registrySources: allowedRegistries:- registry.redhat.io # <------ add it- ulmcpapoc52.cnuat.ocbc.com:5000- registry.cnuat.ocbc.com:5000- quay.io- image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 ~~~
root_cause: customer configuration image registry settings, When the allowedRegistries parameter is defined, all registries, including the registry.redhat.io and quay.io registries and the default internal image registry, are blocked unless explicitly listed. If you use the parameter, to prevent pod failure, you must add the registry.redhat.io and quay.io registries and the internalRegistryHostname to the allowedRegistries list, as they are required by payload images within your environment. Do not add the registry.redhat.io and quay.io registries to the blockedRegistries list.

title: Etcd operator degraded after cluster updating in OCP 4
issue: Etcd operator is degraded after updating cluster with dual-stack cluster network.
EtcdCertSignerControllerDegraded error appears in etcd operator.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-1353](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-1353). For more information, please open a new support case with Red Hat Support ### Workaround Remove the secrets starting with `etcd-peer`, `etcd-serving-metrics` and `etcd-serving` in the project `openshift-etcd`: ~~~ $ for secret in $(oc get secrets-n openshift-etcd-o name | grep 'etcd-peer\|etcd-serving'); do oc delete $secret-n openshift-etcd;done ~~~ Check if the status of etcd operator is as expected: ~~~ $ oc get co etcd NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE etcd 4.9.31 True False False 27h ~~~
root_cause: The failure can come from two different reasons: * The first issue is that the IP addresses of the master nodes are not persistent and they changed after a reboot. This can happen, for example, during an upgrade. * The second issue is related to a second IP address that was configured in the master nodes after the cluster was installed.

title: Files created inside of container occupies space on coreos disk.
issue: When files are created within a container, it occupies space on the base CoreOS filesystem. Is this expected behaviour?
resolution: Yes, this is expected behaviour if the file is not inside a volume or if the volume is an `emptyDir`. This is considered [ephemeral storage](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/storage/understanding-ephemeral-storage.html). this can be limited using [limits](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/#setting-requests-and-limits-for-local-ephemeral-storage) and [quotas](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/applications/quotas/quotas-setting-per-project.html#quotas-resources-managed_quotas-setting-per-project).

title: Cluster Domain gets added to the /etc/resolv.conf of nodes
issue: - IPI installations/upgrade for version 4.11.z gets an additional search domain added to the `/etc/resolv.conf` which causes multiple issues.- Cluster Domain gets added to the `/etc/resolv.conf` of nodes
resolution: - A [bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-3936) is already raised and the same is in the Assigned state. **Workaround:**- Install the [NMState Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/networking/k8s_nmstate/k8s-nmstate-about-the-k8s-nmstate-operator.html) as a Day-2 operation.- Add the DNS section as part of the [official documentation.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/networking/k8s_nmstate/k8s-nmstate-updating-node-network-config.html#virt-example-nmstate-IP-management-dns_k8s_nmstate-updating-node-network-config)- There is no other way possible to edit the `/etc/resolv.conf` directly as it causes the `machine-config` operator to go into a `Degraded` state.
root_cause: - During installation, the file `/etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/30-resolv-prepender` is created on the `node` which looks for the DHCP configuration and applies them on the node.- This file picks the values for BaseDomain from the DHCP and puts them on the nodes. ~~~ $ grep-i domain /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/30-resolv-prepender | DOMAINS="${IP4_DOMAINS} ${IP6_DOMAINS} *.base-domain.example.com" ~~~

title: Response headers are converted to lowercase by haproxy routers
issue: ``Haproxy router return headers in lowercase irrespective of the case set up by the server or client``.
resolution: Haproxy will fix this using below option. [h1-case-adjust-bogus-server option](https://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/2.1/snapshot/configuration.html#option%20h1-case-adjust-bogus-server). Also best recommendation is to fix this on Application side to meet standard as stated in [RFC7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230) which states that there is no standard case for header names because they are case-insensitive. So applications must handle them in a case-insensitive manner. if Application do not stick to standard compliance which might lead to content smuggling attacks and must absolutely be fixed as you can see from [haproxy docs.](http://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/2.0/configuration.html#4-option%20h1-case-adjust-bogus-server) There's an open RFE regarding this already in place [RFE-1049](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1049) and we'll keep this document updated with it's progress.
root_cause: OpenShift 4.4+ use Haproxy 2.0 version currently and this results in headers being stored internally to lowercase, since HTTP/2 headers must be lowercase.This is not relevant in HTTP/1 since headers are case insensitive there. This breaks some legacy application which do not follow standard as stated in [RFC7230].(https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230) which states that there is no standard case for header names because they are case-insensitive. So applications must handle them in a case-insensitive manner.

title: Openshift operator: local storage and Data foundation are not updating
issue: - After recently upgrading OpenShift cluster, the operators are pending of upgrade with message: ~~~ message: 'error using catalog operatorhubio-catalog (in namespace openshift-marketplace): error encountered while listing bundles: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded <--- desc = context deadline exceeded' ~~~- There are some operators pending upgrade in the cluster.
resolution: After following the Diagnostic Steps to locate the problematic `catalogsource` and delete it from the environment. ~~~ $ oc delete catalogsource ~~~ After deleting the `catalogsource` the operators in the environment will finish the pending upgrades.
root_cause: There is a third party Catalog Source in the cluster that is not working properly and it's not reporting updates when required. This is causing the rest of the operators in the environment to not be able to finish upgrades succesfully.

title: [RHOCP] Maximum number of egress IPs that can be attached to a primary interface ?
issue: - Is there any limit for egress IPs that can be attached to a single physical interface for RHEL nodes in OCP?- How many IPs can be assigned to a physical interface?- Does Openshift Nodes have a maximum limit for assigning egressIPs on a single interface?
resolution: - The number of IPs that can be associated with a primary/secondary interface is dependent on the network interface which is being used, the maximum limit for IPs per interface can be checked in the vendor specification- Cloud vendors like [AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-eni.html#AvailableIpPerENI), and [Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/azure-subscription-service-limits?toc=%2Fazure%2Fvirtual-network%2Ftoc.json#azure-resource-manager-virtual-networking-limits) have restrictions for assigning a maximum number of private IPv4/IPv6 addresses per network interface- To know the maximum values of IPs that can be assigned to the network interface check specification provided by the vendor

Specific details would cover specific platforms and situations, so this alert needs to remain as a generic and basic approach based on the general scope of possibilities.

title: How to Change Master Node Hostame in RHOCP 4

title: TCP connectivity issues on haproxy balancer
issue: ``Haproxy Loadbalancers dropping connection with OpenShift master nodes resulting in nodes NotReady state``.
resolution: Increase nf_conntrack_max as per environment need. ~~~ sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max ~~~ Restart the firewalld.- RHEL 7 with firewalld: ~~~ systemctl restart firewalld.service. ~~~ RHEL with iptables: ~~~ service iptables restart ~~~

title: Some questions about Kubernetes Ingress and Openshift Ingress Controllers and Openshift Routes
issue: - Are the Ingress objects defined in Azure K8S used in Openshift?- Is running OpenShift's HAProxy Router in Azure K8s supported?- Is OpenShift Ingress Controller supported in non-OpenShift clusters?
resolution: - Are the Ingress objects defined in Azure K8S supported in Openshift? Kubernetes Ingress objects can be used in OpenShift. However, in terms of IngressController-specific annotations, these will not be the same for HAProxy and other IngressControllers.- Is running OpenShift's HAProxy Router in Azure K8s supported? Red Hat supports Routes and Kubernetes does not support Route objects. When creating Ingresses in OpenShift, a corresponding Route object is automatically created and added to the cluster. OpenShift's HAProxy Router is not yet supported fashion. in Azure K8s The subscription reason is because Red Hat doesn't support Azure K8s and it's not in the testing matrix. The technical reason is HAProxy Router depends on the Routes objects to be present. Routes depend on OpenShift-APIServer (using API aggregation and is not a CRD)/ The OpenShift APIServer depends on a tonne of CRDs from inside the OpenShift API definitions. [0] There's a chain of things that will be required to get the OpenShift Router running in Azure K8s and it's not supported / tested.- Is OpenShift Ingress Controller supported in non-OpenShift clusters? No, OpenShift IngressController cannot be used in a non-OpenShift cluster in a supported fashion. This may be technically possible, but this may require the use of OpenShift APIServer as Routes objects are provided through the use of APIAggregation and not CRDs. This is also not something that is tested and Red Hat Support Engineers are not trained or familiar on how to achieve this

title: Diagnosing IngressControllerUnavailable alert in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: Why is `IngressControllerUnavailable` alert showing up?
How should I detect potential issues when the `IngressControllerUnavailable` alert shows?
How to understand `IngressControllerUnavailable`?
root_cause: This alert fires when an ingress controller is failing to reply or is not active. It is only for pure monitoring purposes and serves as a generic alert, as there can be numerous issues related between DNS, loadbalancers and certs if using custom CA. The Ingress Operator uses the domain from the cluster Ingress configuration as the domain for the default Ingress Controller. The OpenShift API Server Operator uses the domain from the cluster Ingress configuration. This domain is also used when generating a default host for a Route resource that does not specify an explicit host.

title: Diagnosing KubeAPIDown Alert in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: Why is ‘KubeAPIDown’ alert showing up?
How should I detect potential issues when the ‘KubeAPIDown’ alert shows?
How to understand ‘KubeAPIDown’?
root_cause: The KubeAPIDown alert is triggered when all Kubernetes API servers have not been reachable by the monitoring system for more than 15 minutes. This is a critical alert. The Kubernetes API is not responding. The cluster may partially or fully non-functional. It can cause latency in the cluster that could be observed when executing "oc" commands taking several seconds to be applied. If it is only affecting one node, there would be still 2 API servers available and those would need to be able to process the rest of the queries, causing higher load average. There is a load balancer in front of the master nodes which exposes only one address/endpoint for the API server, and that remains available even if one member of the control plane (3 machines) is down. ~~~ Alert: name: KubeAPIDown expr: absent(up{job="apiserver"} == 1) for: 15m labels: severity: critical annotations: description: KubeAPI has disappeared from Prometheus target discovery. summary: Target disappeared from Prometheus target discovery ~~~ If you scale down or simply you have an issue with one master node, the API is still available because of the redundancy of master nodes.

title: Diagnose KubeNodeUnreachable Alert in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: Why is `KubeNodeUnreachable` alert showing up?
How should I detect potential issues when the `KubeNodeUnreachable` alert shows?
How to understand `KubeNodeUnreachable`?
root_cause: If a node is not reachable, due to outage or problem with the server, like substantial amount of resources being consumed, it would be needed to be checked from the node itself. If the node is not reachable through ssh or "oc debug" utility, it will be needed to rely on console access from the different providers.

title: Diagnosing KubeletDown Alert in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: Why is `KubeletDown` alert showing up?
How should I detect potential issues when the `KubeletDown` alert shows?
How to understand `KubeletDown`?
root_cause: This alert is triggered when the monitoring system has not been able to reach any of the cluster’s Kubelets for more than 15 minutes. This alert represents a critical threat to the cluster’s stability and the specific node affected. Excluding the possibility of a network issue preventing the monitoring system from scraping Kubelet metrics, multiple nodes in the cluster are likely unable to respond to configuration changes for pods and other resources, and some debugging tools are likely not functional, e.g. oc exec and oc logs, or oc debug, so you might need to perform SSH to enter in the node.

title: OVN keep loadbalancer objects after removing services in OpenShift 4
issue: - **OVN NorthBound DB*
has old LoadBalancer entries for one project.- There are no services or pods in a namespace, however, there are entries for this project in the **OVN NorthBound DB**.
resolution: - Upgrade the cluster to **OpenShift 4.10.40** at minimum the release where is fixed.- Fixed in **4.10.40**, [OCPBUGS-1674](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-1674), [RHBA-2022:7298](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:7298). ### Workaround- For releases before **OpenShift 4.10.40**, restart the **ovnkube-master** pods: ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-l app=ovnkube-master ~~~
root_cause: - There are some particular conditions when during a leadership transition in OVN, a loadbalancer creation could fail at the OVN side but still succeed at the OVS level.- The component in charge of this task is relying on the OVSDB cache for performance reasons it could not be aware of the mismatch between the 2 databases.

title: DNS service names are not resolving in RHOCP 4
issue: - Service DNS names are not able to resolve from any of the OCP nodes. ~~~ *
server can't find kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local: NXDOMAIN ~~~- Only the `image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc` service FQDN is getting resolved from OCP nodes.
root_cause: - RHOCP 4 uses CoreDNS which resolves the cluster service DNS names.- DNS names for Services do not resolve from the node host as the node itself is not configured to use CoreDNS as its name server and this is an expected behavior.- For example, the container runtime runs directly on the node host, so it cannot resolve cluster service DNS names, with the following exception.- As a special case, a process in the DNS DaemonSet's `dns-node-resolver` container adds the registry service's DNS name, `image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc`, to the node's `/etc/hosts` file so that the container runtime and kubelet can resolve the registry service's DNS name.- If a pod is configured to use the host network, or if a process runs directly on a node, it uses the name servers configured in the host node's `/etc/resolv.conf` file instead of CoreDNS instance.

title: Red Hat Openshift Container Platform installation is failing due to "error fetching network" on VMware vSphere.
issue: - Installation is failing with message `error fetching network` while using a portgroup from `Standard vSwitch` that exists in 2 esxi hosts.
resolution: - In case usage of `Standard vSwitch` provision the `ocp nodes` in same `ESXI` host.- In case usage of multiple `ESXI/ESX` hosts use `Distributed vSwitch`.
root_cause: - A `standard vSwitch` works within one `ESX/ESXi` host only. `Distributed vSwitches` allow different hosts to use the switch as long as they exist within the same host cluster.
