title: Frequent restarts of vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller
issue: - The `vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller` keeps terminating and restarting and below error is shown in the `vsphere CSI Driver Operator`: ~~~ VMwareVSphereDriverControllerServiceController reconciliation failed: Operation cannot be fulfilled on deployments.apps "vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again ~~~- After deployment the `vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller` pods are constantly getting restarted and different replicasets exist for the controller as shown below: ~~~ $ omg get pods-n openshift-cluster-csi-drivers NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller-5b4bb669f7-m6rkv 0/13 Pending 0 1h0m vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller-69997d74f-b7x8w 13/13 Running 0 1h31m vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller-69997d74f-bscnl 13/13 Running 0 1h0m vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller-7b44b896c7-7q7gs 0/13 Pending 0 1h0m ~~~
resolution: - Check if there are multiple credentials configured in `vsphere-creds` in `kube-system` namespace as shown below: ~~~ $ omg get secrets vsphere-creds-n kube-system-oyaml apiVersion: v1 data: vcenter.xxx-1.vmwarevmc.com.password: "xxx", vcenter.xxx-1.vmwarevmc.com.username: "xxx", vcenter.xxx-2.vmwarevmc.com.password: "xxx", vcenter.xxx-2.vmwarevmc.com.username: "xxx" kind: Secret ~~~- If more than one credentials are configured in `vsphere-creds` then code can arbitrarily pick one of them and hence secrets may keep changing and thereby causing deployment rollouts. Refer [Bug 2108473](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2108473).
root_cause: - When more than one credential is present in `vsphere-creds` secret then code can arbitrarily pick one of them and hence secrets may keep changing and thereby causing deployment rollouts.

title: Is python2-django-1.11.29-1.el7sat affected by CVE-2022-28346 and related CVEs?
issue: Is `python2-django-1.11.29-1.el7sat` affected by the following CVEs? [CVE-2022-28346](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-28346) [CVE-2022-28347](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-28347) [CVE-2022-23833](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-23833) [CVE-2021-45115](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-45115) [CVE-2021-45116](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-45116) `python2-django` is not mentioned on above CVE pages.
resolution: `python2-django-1.11.29-1.el7sat` is **NOT** affected by these CVEs.
root_cause: `python2-django-1.11.29-1.el7sat` specifically is not affected by any of these three vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities only affect python2-django-2.x, but Satellite 6.9 includes both: python2-django-1.x (not affected) and python2-django-2.x within python-pulp-container (which is affected by these three flaws). The exactly same logic applies for [CVE-2021-45115](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-45115), [CVE-2021-45116](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-45116). These issues do not affect `python2-django-1.11.29-1.el7sat`. [CVE-2021-45115](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-45115) and [CVE-2021-45116](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-45116) affect 2.2.x versions of python2-django.

title: How to run multi ingressControllers on the same infra node
issue: When creating another set of IngressControllers, the haproxy pod will be in pending status, the event complain not have free port for the requested pod ports
resolution: Default for on-prem installation of OpenShift, the endpointPublishingStrategy of the default ingressController is HostNetwork, which means it will only bind to the local(Infra Nodes) 80 and 443 ports, so if want to create another set of IngressControllers, the port will duplicate and new pods will be in pending status as the node could not allocate another 80 or 443 port for the new haproxy port So in order to run another set of IngressController on the same node, the new IngressController should use the NodePortService as below: ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: IngressController metadata: name: node-port-svc-ic namespace: openshift-ingress-operator spec: domain: example.com endpointPublishingStrategy: type: NodePortService routeSelector: matchLabels: type: apps nodePlacement: nodeSelector: matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: "" tolerations:- effect: NoSchedule key: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra operator: Exists ~~~
root_cause: Please check this for the endpoint publish strategy [cluster-ingress-operator](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-ingress-operator#endpoint-publishing)

title: devworkspace-webhook-server Pod is in CrashLoopBackoff after removing Web Terminal Operator
issue:
The `devworkspace-webhook-server-*` Pod is crashing after removing the Web Terminal Operator: ~~~ $ oc get pods-A | egrep-v "(Running|Completed)" NAMESPACE NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE openshift-operators devworkspace-webhook-server-699b55858b-hzgx2 1/2 CrashLoopBackOff 51 4h12m ~~~ Reviewing the logs from the failing Pod, it appears there is a missing ServiceAccount `devworkspace-controller-serviceaccount` resulting in the Pod failures: ~~~ {"level":"info","ts":1669165649.0705738,"logger":"cmd","msg":"Configuring Webhooks"} {"level":"info","ts":1669165649.0705845,"logger":"webhook.devworkspace","msg":"Configuring devworkspace webhooks"} I1123 01:07:32.321703 1 request.go:668] Waited for 3.247702157s due to client-side throttling, not priority and fairness, request: GET:https://172.30.0.1:443/apis/config.openshift.io/v1?timeout=32s {"level":"error","ts":1669165652.9785552,"logger":"cmd","msg":"Failed to create webhooks","error":"serviceaccounts "devworkspace-controller-serviceaccount" not found","stacktrace":"main.main
	/remote-source/app/webhook/main.go:115
runtime.main
	/usr/lib/golang/src/runtime/proc.go:255"} ~~~
resolution: This Pod appears to be a remnant of the Web Terminal Operator and should be removed before continuing. To ensure the Web Terminal Operator has been removed completely, follow the instructions for removal in the official [OpenShift Documentation- Removing the Web Terminal Operator and the custom resources that support it](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/web_console/odc-about-web-terminal.html#removing-the-web-terminal-operator-and-the-custom-resources-that-support-it). This will ensure that any remnant objects are completely removed from the cluster. If the Web Terminal functionality is required, ensure the complete removal steps have been achieved before attempting to re-install the operator using the Operator Lifecycle Manager. To reinstall the WebTerminal Operator, follow the instructions in the official [OpenShift Documentation- Installing the web terminal](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/web_console/odc-about-web-terminal.html#odc-installing-web-terminal_odc-about-web-terminal). If you continue to have issues with the WebTerminal Operator or other components in your cluster, please open a case with Red Hat Support and reference this article.

title: Backup and Restore of APIcast self-managed routes
issue: - What is the backup/restore procedure for the APIcast self-managed routes when following the backup/restore guide and/or the template to operator migration guide?
resolution: > **Note:** *it is important to highlight that once APIcast is configured as self-managed (via the product's "deployment" setting), the 3scale administrative users will be responsible for its management not 3scale. Also, if the wildcard domain on the new cluster's environment is different from the origin, the routes will need to be configured accordingly.* It is possible to backup/restore APIcast self-managed routes when migrating 3scale between versions or between OpenShift versions. First, on the origin cluster, the APIcast related Routes should be listed and added to a json file. In the example below, the Routes pointing to apicast-staging Service are listed. ~~~ oc get route--field-selector spec.to.name=apicast-staging-o json > self-managed-routes-staging.json ~~~ Secondly, the first step should be repeated. However, this time, listing the Routes that point to apicast-production Service. ~~~ oc get route--field-selector spec.to.name=apicast-production-o json > self-managed-routes-production.json ~~~ And, lastly, on the destination cluster, create the Routes according with the generated json file. ~~~ oc create-f self-managed-routes-.json ~~~ It is important to observe that, in case the namespaces of the destination and origin clusters don't match, the namespace information will need to be rectified on the json files, so it matches with the destination's namespace.
root_cause: It is usual, when customizing APIcast routes, to mark 3scale Products as_self-managed_. This is a known workaround to add custom metadata annotation to zync generated routes described in [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6222941). When using the aforementioned solution to customize routes, those are no longer managed by zync and, in case of a migration process or a backup/restore procedure, must be backed up and restored manually. Otherwise, the restored Backends will no longer be externally reachable.

title: How to create secret to store the TLS credentials in AMQ on openshift?
issue: - How to create secret to store the TLS credentials in AMQ on openshift?
resolution: - Create a secret to store the TLS credentials. ~~~ $ oc create secret generic my-tls-secret--from-file=broker.ks=~/broker.ks--from-file=client.ts=~/broker.ks--from-literal=keyStorePassword=--from-literal=trustStorePassword= ~~~- Link the secret to the service account that you created when installing the Operator. ~~~ $ oc secrets link sa/amq-broker-operator secret/my-tls-secret ~~~ **NOTE:- When generating a secret, OpenShift requires you to specify both a key store and a trust store. The trust store key is generically named client.ts**

title: Process instance does not rollback to previous state on unhandled exception
issue: Process instance does not rollback to previous state on unhandled exception The process instance encounters an unhandled exception. This exception does not force the process instance to return to its previous state and the process instance is in hanged state and we cannot recover it. [com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.internals.SQLServerException] (default task-2) **

SQLException:ConnectionID:3 ClientConnectionId: b2d039bc-695a-42dc-9932-bd28d3c25b7a com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerException: Cannot invoke a rollback operation when the AutoCommit mode is set to "true". Cannot invoke a rollback operation when the AutoCommit mode is set to "true". The errors reported earlier happen on different process definitions, but they have the same final result. The process instance is not rolled back and depending on were it got stuck seems that there is no way of recovering.
resolution: his configuration is our UAT environment, NOT a local development workstation. JBoss EAP 7.4.1 + PAM 7.12.1 (Openshift): JDBC Driver JRE 11 + Azure MsSQL 2019: **Failing behavior** JBoss EAP 7.4.1 + PAM 7.12.1 (Openshift): JDBC Driver JRE 8 + Azure MsSQL 2019: **Valid behavior** Furthermore, we encountered this ticket which, despite the fact that it refers to a specific configuration property of the datasource, it seems quite valid to explain the behavior we see with version 7.12.1. https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6389341 We have now downgraded JDBC 7.4.1 to the one built for JRE 8 and it has the behavior we expect as shown by the last configuration pointed out above. Hello, You have the following defined in the standalone-openshift.xml file: *************************************** ${env.PAM_DS_JDBC_URL} mssql 10 50 ${env.PAM_DS_USERNAME} ${env.PAM_DS_PASSWORD} false true 10000 *************************************** Could you please change to true and to false in the affected environment and let me know if this makes a difference? > > We have now downgraded JDBC 7.4.1 to the one built for JRE 8 and it has the behavior we expect as shown by the last configuration pointed out above. In regards to the above, did you mean JBoss EAP 7.4.1 instead? How is your RHPAM 7.12.1 installed? Are you using custom image for RHPAM? RHPAM 7.12.1 should be installed on EAP 7.4.2- see [1]. Also, what is the vendor of the Java that you are using? To check the version of EAP please go to the terminal, run the following and provide the output:./standalone.sh--version In the same way, please execute the following and provide the output: java-version Thank you, Biljana. [1] https://access.redhat.com/articles/3405381#RHPAM712 In regards to the version of the JDBC Driver- RHPAM will support the same versions as what is supported and tested in JBoss EAP. The most up-to-date information can be found in the following knowledge article: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) 7 Supported Configurations [1]. According to this article, for Microsoft SQL Server 2019 one should use Microsoft JDBC Driver 7.4.1. So, I believe that both JDBC Driver 7.4.1 JRE 8 and JDBC Driver 7.4.1 JRE 11 are supported.

title: Virtual Machines running Windows get very slow and/or write a lot of data to Storage when doing trim/discard/unmap/defragmentation operations
product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux for x86_64
issue: Running defrag command causes a high cpu load
Runs for a very long time
Causes all the data to be rewritten again instead of just trimming the drive
resolution: * The solution consists of adjusting slab size, which is represented by the discard_granularity qemu-kvm parameter. However two more pieces are needed: 1\. The virtio drivers must honour the discard_granularity setting, this is tracked in [Bug 2020998- [virtio-win] Windows 10 "Optimize drive"/Trim/Discard causes all data to be rewritten](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2020998), upcoming virtio-win for RHEL 8 and 9 will contain this. 2\. The discard_granularity must be exposed via libvirt to enable an officially supported use of the setting, this is being tracked in [Bug 2154127- [RFE] Expose discard_granularity](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2154127). After this, adjusting the value to 8MB or higher should improve the TRIM performance considerably.
root_cause: * The default slab (cluster) size reported by QEMU is 4K, while Windows volume defragmentation can be significantly improved if the slab size is 8MB or bigger.

title: How Can We  Solve  DNS Error From  Application POD in OpenShift Container Platform 4.7.x?
issue: - Error on DNS resolution from application pods while the OCP dns components are healthy- From an application pod, we cannot reach an URL,for example ~~~ https://api.test.org ~~~- DNS works properly in OCP since we can reach any other site. "dig" output from infra node where the pod resides return a peculiar DNS msg size.
resolution: - This is a know issue and we had a bug and Red Hat has given a fix in OCP 4.7.18- Upgrade to OCP version 4.7.18 or higher to that- The fix for BZ#1953097 enabled the CoreDNS bufsize plug-in with a buffer size of 1232 bytes, even though some DNS resolvers are capable of handling a maximum of only 512 bytes. As a result, some DNS resolvers were unable to receive messages from the DNS Operator
root_cause: - Dig command output in the OCP node where the affected pods running shows that the "MSG SIZE rcvd: 580" more than 512 bytes

title: [RHOCP 4.10] Mounting and writing to an NFSv3 share from an OpenShift pod results in the pod to hang
issue: - The issue happens when writing ‘large’ amounts of data using for example the `dd` command, which then causes the command to ‘hang’.
resolution: - Follow the documentation available at [RHOCP 4.10- Configuring persistent storage > Persistent storage using NFS](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/storage/persistent_storage/persistent-storage-nfs.html) to properly configure the NFS persistent storage. By following the steps there you will:- Create an object definition for the PV that will point to the path exported by the NFS server; and- Create a persistent volume claim that binds to the new PV. Later you can use the new `pvc` on your `pod` as done in [create a Pod that uses your PersistentVolumeClaim as a volume](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-persistent-volume-storage/#create-a-pod).

title: How can I add a second disk to an OpenShift machine set custom resource on vSphere?
issue: - Trying to add a second disk to a machine set custom resource on vSphere.- You want to use YAML to add a second disk to your OpenShift nodes but the [documentation only mentions diskGiB](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/machine_management/creating-infrastructure-machinesets.html#machineset-yaml-vsphere_creating-infrastructure-machinesets) and nothing about adding more than one disk.
resolution: For vSphere IPI or vSphere [UPI that uses MachineSets](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5307621), there is no support currently for adding a second disk to the MachineSet with vSphere. There is an RFE, [vSphere- MachineSet- Support of more than one disk](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1426), to give users of vSphere the ability to create machines with more than one disk and allow proper disk layout that better addresses their needs. In the meantime, the workaround is to manually add a second disk to the VM instance and continue from there using the documented procedures with the MachineConfig, see KCS article [Mounting separate disk for OpenShift 4 container storage](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4952011).

title: Unable to label custom namespaces with pod security admission annotations
issue: - After adding `pod security admission labels` to the application namespace, the changes are rolled back to the original state again. Consider below annotations as an example: ~~~ pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=baseline pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit=baseline ~~~
resolution: - It is `mandatory` to annotate the namespace with the label: `security.openshift.io/scc.podSecurityLabelSync: false` along with the other labels for the changes to be `persistent`.- By default, there is a `cluster-global configuration` which enforces the configured policies on pods and known workloads.- In order to keep SCCs working alongside restricted cluster-wide PSA level, there must be a mechanism that would `synchronize` the PSA policy level for a namespace that workload runs in, so that the workload is allowed by both SCC and PSA admissions. For that purpose, a `PSA Label Synchronization Controller` (hereinafter the Controller) shall be built.- The Controller watches changes of:- namespaces: `manual changes` to the interesting `labels` of the namespaces that were opted-in to label synchronization should be reverted- To disable pod security admission label sychronization in a namespace, set the value of the `security.openshift.io/scc.podSecurityLabelSync` label to `false`.- To enable pod security admission label sychronization in a namespace, set the value of the `security.openshift.io/scc.podSecurityLabelSync` label to `true`.- By default, namespaces `without` the `synchronization` label will be still considered for `label synchronization`.
root_cause: - Missing annotation: `security.openshift.io/scc.podSecurityLabelSync: false`.

title: Restricting Machine API IAM Policy on GCP
issue: On GCP, the default Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy requested by the Machine API includes the "Service Account User role", which allows any administrator with access to create or modify compute machine sets to assign any service account to newly created machines. The ability to assign arbitrary service accounts to newly created machines could allow users to gain additional privileges.
resolution: To resolve this issue, administrators must use the Cloud Credential Operator in manual mode. More details about manual mode can be found in the [OpenShift Container Platform product documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/installing_gcp/manually-creating-iam-gcp.html). Once you have configured your cluster to use manual mode, you can edit the GCP service account policy bindings created by the installation program for Machine API, remove the "Service Account User Role" from the Machine API Operator service account, and restrict the service account usage to just the service accounts required by your cluster. The default service accounts for machines that are created by the installation program are called `-w@.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `-m@.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for the worker and control plane machines respectively. These will be referred to as ` ` and ` ` in the commands below. The Machine API Operator service account, created by the Cloud Credential Operator, will be called `-openshift-m- @.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. This will be referred to as ` ` in the below commands. 1. Remove the project-level "Service account user role" binding from the Machine API service account by running the following command: `$ gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding--member="serviceAccount: "--role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser”` 2. Add the "Service account user role" binding for the worker service account by running the following command: `$ gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding--member="serviceAccount: "--role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser"--project= ` 3. Add the "Service account user role" binding for the control plane service account by running the following command: `$ gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding--member="serviceAccount: "--role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser"--project= ` Once completed, the Machine API Operator will only be able to create machines with the default worker and control plane service accounts. Additional service accounts can be bound using the above pattern.
root_cause: When creating `CredentialsRequest` custom resources, OpenShift Container Platform cannot know about the individual circumstances of a particular installation. The permissions requested are global and must apply to all clusters. As the product cannot know the names of the service accounts that are created by the installation program ahead of time, it must allow the Machine API to pass any service account so that it can create the worker machines to complete the cluster installation.

title: GitLab Runner Operator 1.9.0 Mutating/Validating Webhook fails with error ValidatingWebhook "vrunner.kb.io".

title: Build pods failing with error Requesting bear token: invalid status code from registry 403 (Forbidden) in RHOCP 4
issue: - Pods fail to access external private docker registry with following errors, 2022-12-09T15:45:52.733867017Z Warning: Pull failed, retrying in 5s... 2022-12-09T15:45:57.937944035Z error: build error: failed to pull image: After retrying 2 times, Pull image still failed due to error: initializing source docker://registry.example.com:5050/test/dev-self-service-v2-image:latest: Requesting bear token: invalid status code from registry 403 (Forbidden)
resolution: - Make sure the article [Whitelist registry URLs for optional third-party contents that OCP requires on your firewall](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6923621) is followed.- Verify the created pull secret from your Docker credentials are correct and linked it properly to your service account as per the documentation step [Allowing pods to reference images from other secured registries](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/openshift_images/managing_images/using-image-pull-secrets.html#images-allow-pods-to-reference-images-from-secure-registries_using-image-pull-secrets).- Ensure that there are no duplicate secrets that could conflict with the newly created secret of a docker registry.
root_cause: - Existing duplicate secrets were conflicting with the newly created secret for a docker registry, resulting in an error `Requesting bear token: invalid status code from registry 403 (Forbidden)`.

title: Kuryr-controller pod in CrashLoobBack in OpenShift 4
issue: - Kuryr controller pod is in CrashLoopBack- Kuryr controller pod stuck with error: ~~~ 2022-12-20 09:39:18.953 1 ERROR kuryr_kubernetes.handlers.logging kuryr_kubernetes.exceptions.K8sResourceNotFound: Resource not found: '{"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","m etadata":{},"status":"Failure","message":"pods \\"certified-operators-zhbk8\\" not found","reason":"NotFound","details":{"name":"certified-operators-zhbk8","kind":"pods"},"c ode":404}\n ~~~
resolution: 1. Find the **KuryrPort** associated with the pod name showed in the Error Log: ~~~ $ oc get kuryrports-A | grep certified-operators-zhbk8 certified-operators-zhbk8 a0b9629b-bcbe-436f-8036-adf47d01b6f2 rhocp-2tt9k-worker-dzd85 {"kuryr.openstack.org/nodeName":"rhocp-2tt9k-worker-dzd85"} ~~~ 2. Verify the **pod** no longer exists: ~~~ $ oc get pod-A | grep certified-operators-zhbk8 ~~~ 3. Delete the **leftover port**: ~~~ $ oc delete kuryrports certified-operators-zhbk8-n openshift-marketplace ~~~
root_cause: - **kuryr-controller** pod can go in CrashLoopBack status if a pod is deleted but the associated **kuryrports** remains leftover.

title: Assign access to non cluster admin users to create CRDs in RHOCP4
issue: - Non cluster-admin users are unable to create CRDs.- Users are getting below error for create/list actions on CRDs: ~~~ Error from server (Forbidden): customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io is forbidden: User " " cannot create resource "customresourcedefinitions" in API group "apiextensions.k8s.io" at the cluster scope ~~~
resolution: - Create a cluster-role with required permissions on CRD using below command: ~~~ $ oc create clusterrole--verb=*--resource=crd ~~~- Here users can assign any permission as per their requirement using `--verb` option, permissions such as `create`, `patch`, `get`, `list`,`delete`, `deletecollection`, `watch`, instead of `*`- Assign the above created cluster-role to the user: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user ~~~- After assigning the cluster-role to the user, users will be able to access CRD's in the cluster.- Users can also assign the created cluster-role to the group: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-group ~~~- After assigning the cluster-role to the group, all users added in the group will have permissions on CRD's in the cluster.
root_cause: - The regular users do not have cluster-admin permissions. However the CRD is a cluster-scope resource.- Hence if users are looking for a method to allow these non cluster-admin users to `create`,`get`,`list`,'delete' the cluster-scope resource (CRD), users can create a cluster-role for the same. And then assign the created cluster-role to the expected users.

title: [RHOCP4] Unable to access redis through OpenShift route

resolution: - The Redis app can be accessed by creating an svc of type nodePort or ExternalIP. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: labels: app: redis name: redis-cluster-nodePort namespace: my-ns spec: ports:- name: client port: 6379 protocol: TCP targetPort: 6379- name: gossip port: 16379 protocol: TCP targetPort: 16379 selector: app: redis-cluster sessionAffinity: None type: NodePort status: loadBalancer: {} ~~~ For HA it is recommended to use IP failover or External loadbalancer which does health checks and load balancing on nodePort.

title: [RHOCP4] PrometheusTargetMissing and GlusterDown alert on gluster-storage pod
issue: Prometheus is throwing an alert with GlusterDown for gluster-storage pod although gluster-storage pod is up and running.
resolution: - Opening port 8080 in iptable helped to resolve the issue. After opening port 8080 in iptables metrics were fetched successfully from Prometheus. ~~~ iptables-I OS_FIREWALL_ALLOW-p tcp-m state--state NEW-m tcp--dport 8080-j ACCEPT ~~~- To make sure iptable rule is persistent when iptable service is restarted enter the rule in file /etc/sysconfig/iptables. Find the chain name OS_FIREWALL_ALLOW, add the below entry, and save the file.- Find the chain name OS_FIREWALL_ALLOW, add the below entry, and save the file. ~~~-A OS_FIREWALL_ALLOW-p tcp-m state--state NEW-m tcp--dport 8080-j ACCEPT ~~~
root_cause: - Port 8080 is not allowed in iptable rules on node hence connectivity to port 8080 is not established.- Packets are dropped in iptable rules and there is a good number of drop counts in iptable for port 8080.

title: Migration of OCP cluster from one RHV cluster to a new RHV cluster
issue: - Is there a procedure to move an OCP cluster from one RHV cluster to a new one?- Can we change the RHV cluster of an OCP cluster?
resolution: - If you have a cluster with an IPI installation then you will have to install a new OpenShift cluster and migrate the workloads.- If you have installed the cluster with UPI then the installation is basically a bare metal installation. You can safely just take the image file from one side and move it to the other cluster. As long as IP stays the same it's not a problem.- To raise questions or obtain further information contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport).
root_cause: - With an IPI installation this is certainly going to cause major problems. Reason being IPI means that OCP is managing the underlying RHV environment. If it sees different IDs it may or may not start destroying stuff. You'd have to somehow update the Kubernetes objects offline, which I don't think is possible. Plus, we don't have a list of all objects you'd need to update. In essence, I don't think there is a reliable way to do this migration without the risk of major data loss.

title: Red Hat Service Mesh EgressGateway Origination with a specific Source IP Address in OpenShift 4
issue: - Can the Service Mesh send the outgoing traffic with a specific IP?- How to have outgoing traffic from the Service Mesh with a specific source IP.
resolution: 1. Create an **[Egress Router in DNS Proxy mode](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/networking/openshift_sdn/deploying-egress-router-dns-redirection.html#nw-egress-router-pod_deploying-egress-router-dns-redirection)** that enforces a specific Source Address on all incoming traffic on a specific port before sending it to the destination. 2. Create an **Istio DestinationRule** for redirecting the traffic from the Service Mesh to the specific port of the **Egress Router** so it can enforce the required Source IP Address.
root_cause: Since the Red Hat Service Mesh does not have the functionality to perform SNAT on outgoing traffic, a way to do it is to demand this operation to an Egress Router in DNS Proxy mode. With this configuration, the Service Mesh sends the traffic to the Egress Router that is configured to enforce a predefined source IP address on all incoming traffic. A complete reproduction of this use case is shown step by step in the [Article 6891491](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6891491).

title: ingresscontroller with mtls not working when user certificate issue by intermediateCA in RHOCP4
issue: - The mtls connection does not work when using an intermediateCA apart from the root CA, both with CRL defined.- When attempting to connect using a user certificate issued by the Intermediate CA it fails with an error of unknown CA. ~~~ curl--cert hello.example.com.crt--key hello.example.com.key--request GET-LIvvvk https://hello.example.com
Connected to hello.example.com (10.81.71.61) port 443 (#0)
ALPN, offering h2
ALPN, offering http/1.1
successfully set certificate verify locations:
CApath: none
(304) (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
(304) (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
(304) (IN), TLS handshake, Unknown (8):
(304) (IN), TLS handshake, Request CERT (13):
(304) (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11):
(304) (IN), TLS handshake, CERT verify (15):
(304) (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20):
(304) (OUT), TLS handshake, Certificate (11):
(304) (OUT), TLS handshake, CERT verify (15):
(304) (OUT), TLS handshake, Finished (20):
SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / AEAD-CHACHA20-POLY1305-SHA256
ALPN, server did not agree to a protocol..........
SSL certificate verify ok. > GET / HTTP/1.1 > Host: hello.example.com > User-Agent: curl/7.79.1 > Accept: */
LibreSSL SSL_read: error:1404C418:SSL routines:ST_OK:tlsv1 alert unknown ca, errno 0
Closing connection 0 curl: (56) LibreSSL SSL_read: error:1404C418:SSL routines:ST_OK:tlsv1 alert unknown ca, errno 0 ~~~
root_cause: - The intermediate certificate authority, having a certificate issued from the root has a CDP identifying the CRL as issued by the root authority.- A CRL is issued by the Intermediate Authority to identify any certificates that it issued that have now been revoked. Any certificates issued by the Intermediate Certificate Authority contain a CDP identifying the location of the CRL published by the Intermediate Certificate Authority.- The `ca-bundle.crt` data value of the "router-client-ca-default" therefore contains the certificate for both the root and the intermediate certificate authorities. The intermediate certificate authority contains the CDP so that the operator may find the CRL issued by the root authority.- In order to fully validate the chain the CRL published by the Intermediate Authority will also be needed. This can be identified by the CDP in the client certificate. The Validity of the CRL can be determined because the CRL is signed by the Intermediate authority, for which we have the certificate.- The client certificate is rejected even if no certificates in the chain are revoked. This is most likely because one of the required CRLs is missing so the chain can't be fully validated.- If a client certificate issue by the root certificate authority is used then all the required components are present i.e. certificate authority certificate and CRL, and so the client is accepted.- However client certificates should not be issued by the root authority.

YAML file can be downloaded from the OpenShift Secret tab on token’s Token Information page.- Create the authentication token secret for the OpenShift project using the YAML file: ~~~ oc create-f 1234567_myserviceaccount-secret.yaml ~~~- Configure the secret for OpenShift project using the following commands, replacing the secret name below with the name of your secret created in the previous step. ~~~ oc secrets link default 1234567-myserviceaccount-pull-secret--for=pull oc secrets link builder 1234567-myserviceaccount-pull-secret--for=pull ~~~- Import the Latest JBoss EAP for OpenShift Image Streams and Templates ~~~ #For JDK 8 image stream: for resource in \ eap73-amq-persistent-s2i.json \ eap73-amq-s2i.json \ eap73-basic-s2i.json \ eap73-https-s2i.json \ eap73-image-stream.json \ eap73-sso-s2i.json \ eap73-starter-s2i.json \ eap73-third-party-db-s2i.json \ eap73-tx-recovery-s2i.json do oc replace--force-f \ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jboss-container-images/jboss-eap-7-openshift-image/eap73/templates/${resource} done #For JDK 11 Image Stream for resource in \ eap73-openjdk11-amq-persistent-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-amq-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-basic-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-https-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-image-stream.json \ eap73-openjdk11-sso-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-starter-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-third-party-db-s2i.json \ eap73-openjdk11-tx-recovery-s2i.json do oc replace--force-f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jboss-container-images/jboss-eap-7-openshift-image/eap73/templates/${resource} done ~~~- After importing the images and templates, deploy applications to OpenShift using the template accordingly. ~~~ oc new-app--template=eap73-openjdk11-basic-s2i \-p IMAGE_STREAM_NAMESPACE=test-eap-demo \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_URL=https://github.com/jboss-developer/jboss-eap-quickstarts \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_REF=openshift \-p GALLEON_PROVISION_LAYERS=jaxrs-server \-p CONTEXT_DIR=helloworld-html5 ~~~ [Documentation link](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.3/html-single/getting_started_with_jboss_eap_for_openshift_container_platform/index#prepare_for_deployment)

title: authentication token IDs keep expiring after a short period
issue: - The authentication token IDs keep expiring after a short period of time, even is by default tokens should be valid 24 hours.
resolution: Ensure that the tokenConfig is null. ~~~ oc patch oauth cluster--type json-p '[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/tokenConfig"}]' ~~~
root_cause: It seems that the main issue can be an unidentified option: **AccessTokenInactivityTimeout**, notidec from the telemetry data. Customer never shared the MG. In the code [types.go](https://github.com/openshift/oauth-server/blob/master/vendor/github.com/openshift/api/osin/v1/types.go#L442-L464) ~~~ // TokenConfig holds the necessary configuration options for authorization and access tokens type TokenConfig struct {// authorizeTokenMaxAgeSeconds defines the maximum age of authorize tokens AuthorizeTokenMaxAgeSeconds int32 `json:"authorizeTokenMaxAgeSeconds,omitempty"` // accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds defines the maximum age of access tokens AccessTokenMaxAgeSeconds int32 `json:"accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds,omitempty"` // accessTokenInactivityTimeoutSeconds- DEPRECATED: setting this field has no effect. // +optional AccessTokenInactivityTimeoutSeconds *int32 `json:"accessTokenInactivityTimeoutSeconds,omitempty"` // accessTokenInactivityTimeout defines the token inactivity timeout // for tokens granted by any client. // The value represents the maximum amount of time that can occur between // consecutive uses of the token. Tokens become invalid if they are not // used within this temporal window. The user will need to acquire a new // token to regain access once a token times out. Takes valid time // duration string such as "5m", "1.5h" or "2h45m". The minimum allowed // value for duration is 300s (5 minutes). If the timeout is configured // per client, then that value takes precedence. If the timeout value is // not specified and the client does not override the value, then tokens // are valid until their lifetime. // +optional AccessTokenInactivityTimeout *metav1.Duration `json:"accessTokenInactivityTimeout,omitempty"`} ~~~ but it's not explained by the OC command: ~~~ [quicklab@upi-0 ~]$ oc explain oauth.spec.tokenConfig KIND: OAuth VERSION: config.openshift.io/v1 RESOURCE: tokenConfig DESCRIPTION: tokenConfig contains options for authorization and access tokens FIELDS: accessTokenInactivityTimeout accessTokenInactivityTimeout defines the token inactivity timeout for tokens granted by any client. The value represents the maximum amount of time that can occur between consecutive uses of the token. Tokens become invalid if they are not used within this temporal window. The user will need to acquire a new token to regain access once a token times out. Takes valid time duration string such as "5m", "1.5h" or "2h45m". The minimum allowed value for duration is 300s (5 minutes). If the timeout is configured per client, then that value takes precedence. If the timeout value is not specified and the client does not override the value, then tokens are valid until their lifetime. WARNING: existing tokens' timeout will not be affected (lowered) by changing this value accessTokenInactivityTimeoutSeconds accessTokenInactivityTimeoutSeconds- DEPRECATED: setting this field has no effect. accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds defines the maximum age of access tokens ~~~

title: OAuth API servers are not ready - PreconditionNotReady
issue: - authentication operator is not available and/or degraded with the message:- APIServerDeploymentAvailable: no apiserver.openshift-oauth-apiserver pods available on any node.
resolution: #### Fixed versions The issue has been fixed from the following versions: Version | Related BZ/Jira | Related Errata--- |--- |--- 4.8.2 | [BZ 1934400](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1934400) | [RHSA-2021:2438](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:2438) 4.7.29 | [BZ 1967359](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1967359) | [RHSA-2021:3303](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:3303) 4.6.46 | [BZ 1967361](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1989061) | [RHBA-2021:3643](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2021:3643) #### Workaround_for previous versions, please follow this **workaround** to get the Authentication Operator back online._ The SCC including the `defaultAllowPrivilegeEscalation: false` key/value have been identified in the Diagnostic Steps (step 4). Use `oc edit` to remove the key/value pair from the SCC: ~~~ $ KUBECONFIG=~/kubeconfig $ oc--kubeconfig=${KUBECONFIG} edit scc vulnerability-advisor-scc #Remove the `defaultAllowPrivilegeEscalation: false` line ~~~ Once all SCC configurations have been updated, refresh the `openshift-oauth-apiserver` replicaset. ~~~ $ oc patch replicaset.apps/apiserver-5bdfd49cf8-n openshift-oauth-apiserver-p '{"spec": {"replicas": 0}}'--kubeconfig=${KUBECONFIG} ~~~ This will trigger the replicaset to redeploy the PODs, as it will automatically recover the value to 3. Once the replicaset has started at least one pod, the `Authentication` operator should have recover and the command `oc login` should work. If the replicaset is still failing, please check the diagnostic steps again for any extra SCC to edit.
root_cause: The issue is related to a SecurityContextConstraint (SCC) setting the `defaultAllowPrivilegeEscalation: false` when the `openshift-oauth-apiserver` replicaset is trying to start the pods with the `privileged` option. A Bug fix has been submitted and should be released in a future release version (_current version: 4.6.19, 4.7.0_)

title: Impossible to copy files and directories to and from containers using oc cp command

Please see the example below: ~~~ $ oc get po NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE console-549fd97c48-fbfsh 1/1 Running 0 6d8h console-549fd97c48-jv8db 1/1 Running 0 6d8h downloads-7bb5c774c4-2gtk7 1/1 Running 0 26d downloads-7bb5c774c4-wbzb4 1/1 Running 0 26d ~~~ ~~~ $ oc cp downloads-7bb5c774c4-2gtk7:/usr/share/openshift/linux_amd64/oc /tmp/oc tar: Removing leading `/' from member names Dropping out copy after 0 retries error: unexpected EOF ~~~

Specify 0 to disable or any negative value for infinite retrying. The default is 0 (no retry).

title: ETCD restore process on SNO causes EtcdCertSignerControllerDegraded
issue: When following the ETCD restore documentation [Replacing an unhealthy etcd member whose etcd pod is crashlooping](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/backup_and_restore/control_plane_backup_and_restore/replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member.html#restore-replace-crashlooping-etcd-member_replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member) on a single node (SNO), the following messages can appear in the cluster-etcd-operator (CEO): ~~~ EtcdCertSignerControllerDegraded: [Operation cannot be fulfilled on secrets "etcd-peer-sno-0": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again, Operation cannot be fulfilled on secrets "etcd-serving-sno-0": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again, Operation cannot be fulfilled on secrets "etcd-serving-metrics-sno-0": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again] ~~~
resolution: _**Note:** The Openshift documentation is awaiting for modifications and will provide the right steps in a near future. This KCS is sharing the future update content._ The respective operator pod can be recreated by deleting the pod: ~~~ oc delete-n openshift-etcd-operator $(oc get pod-n openshift-etcd-operator-o name) ~~~ Since the issue can affect multiple operators, it is recommended to reboot the SNO after a successful restore operation.
root_cause: When restoring etcd on a SNO cluster to a previous snapshot, the revision number goes backwards in time. Many operators make use of cached results from the API Server and store those in memory along with the revision number. If the revision number goes backwards, the caches assume they already have the latest state and do not refresh. Updates on such cached objects can fail, as the revision numbers are not matching anymore. Restarting the pod, or the whole node, will wipe the memory caches and force to refresh from the API Server.

title: oc commands giving error "connection reset by peer" in RHOCP4
issue: - `connection reset by peer' error upon executing `oc` commands against `API calls`- Is it possible to deploy multiple OCP4.x clusters on the Same Network?- What are the potential risks if there are multiple clusters on the same network?- How to configure custom `VRID` in `keepalived.conf` during the IPI Installation?- How to specify `VRIDs` in `keepalived.conf` post successful OCP deployment? ~~~ E1017 08:01:12.150418 4006359 request.go:1011] Unexpected error when reading response body: read tcp 10.x.x.x:46164-> 192.x.x.x:6443: read: connection reset by peer error: unexpected error when reading response body. Please retry. Original error: read tcp 10.x.x.x:46164-> 192.x.x.x:6443: read: connection reset by peer ~~~
resolution: - It is not possible to specify custom `VRID` when doing IPI installation on vSphere.- Modifying `VRIDs` post successful OCP deployment is not recommended as the `VRID` is based on the cluster name.- To overcome such issues avoid deploying multiple clusters on the same network.- It is suggested to check for the `VRID` conflict using the below command before provisioning the cluster ~~~ # podman run quay.io/openshift/origin-baremetal-runtimecfg:4.7 vr-ids [CLUSTER_NAME] Example: # podman run quay.io/openshift/origin-baremetal-runtimecfg:4.7 vr-ids cnf11 ~~~- Ensure whatever cluster name is provided during the installation will generate the unique `VRIDs`.- A [documentation Bug#2051452](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2051452) is raised to make sure that the details are mentioned in the documentation which helps before installation.
root_cause: - `Keepalived` `virtual router` `ids` `clashes` only if the clusters deployed on the `same L2 domain`.- The installer generates VRID using the cluster name, but with the expectation that networks are segmented already and so no conflicts will occur.- Because of this assumption, there isn't a way to go and change the VRID without changing the underlying network.

title: Oauth Token queries
issue: - How we can control the expiration of token of the LDAP user login?- What is the maximum expiry we can set for the LDAP user login token?- By default what is the token expiry set?- Does the token regenerates on a password change for the LDAP user or token remains unchanged irrespective of the password update?- What is the token expiry set for service-accounts by default?
resolution: - How we can control the expiration of the token of the LDAP user login? You can set accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds to control the lifetime of access tokens. The default lifetime is 24 hours or 86400 seconds. This attribute cannot be negative. If set to zero, the default lifetime is used. To edit the token validity, you could give the accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds parameter with the required value: ``` $ oc edit oauth.config.openshift.io/cluster spec: tokenConfig: accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds: 172800 ``` The above example sets tokens validity to 48 hours (172800 seconds). Also, I would suggest that you take a backup before editing the file. Kindly refer to the document [2] which explains more about how to set accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds in OAuth.- What is the maximum expiry we can set for the LDAP user login token? You can set accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds to control the lifetime of access tokens. The default lifetime is 24 hours or 86400 seconds. This attribute cannot be negative. If set to zero, the default lifetime is used.- By default what is the token expiry set? By default, tokens are only valid for 24 hours. Existing sessions expire after this time elapses.- Does the token regenerates on password change for the LDAP user or token remains unchanged irrespective of the password update? Yes, token should regenerate after a password change.- What is the token expiry set for service accounts by default? As soon as a service account is created, two secrets are automatically added to it- an API token- credentials for the OpenShift Container Registry These can be seen by describing the service account: ``` $ oc describe sa robot Name: robot Namespace: project1 Labels: Annotations: Image pull secrets: robot-dockercfg-qzbhb Mountable secrets: robot-token-f4khf robot-dockercfg-qzbhb Tokens: robot-token-f4khf robot-token-z8h44 ``` The system ensures that service accounts always have an API token and registry credentials.The generated API token and registry credentials do not expire, but they can be revoked by deleting the secret. When the secret is deleted, a new one is automatically generated to take its place.

title: Restart CRI-O service on the Nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to restart CRI-O service on the nodes in RHOCP 4 cluster?
resolution: - Drain the node to schedule all running pods on another running node: ~~~ $ oc adm drain--ignore-daemonsets=true ~~~ Connect to the node using SSH: ~~~ $ ssh-i /path/to/privatekey core@ ~~~- Stop the kubelet service: ~~~ $ systemctl stop kubelet ~~~- Restart the cri-o service: ~~~ $ systemctl restart crio ~~~- Restart the kubelet service: ~~~ $ systemctl start kubelet ~~~- Check `cri-o` and `kubelet` service status if it's working: ~~~ $ systemctl status crio $ systemctl status kubelet ~~~- Once drain is successfully completed, uncordon the node: ~~~ $ oc adm uncordon ~~~

title: How to configure Open shift with RH SSO Identity Provider
issue: - How to configure Openshift console with RH SSO Identity Provider?- How to logout user from Openshift Console when integrated with RH SSO?- User is never logging out.
resolution: 1. Install RH SSO Operator following the [instructions](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_single_sign-on/7.6/html/server_installation_and_configuration_guide/operator) 2. Setup RHSSO with relam, created confidential client for OpenShift and created a ocpuser and set a credential. 3. RH SSO OIDC Identity Provider in Openshift Configuration 3.1 Create a Secret for RH SSO client-secret in Openshift Configuration namespace (Login to RH SSO console to get the client-secret.) ~~~ oc-n openshift-config create secret generic keycloak-client-secret--from- literal=clientSecret=909e58f1-d373–4af3-ab65-de073a54322a ~~~ 3.2 Get the CA cert from the OpenShift Ingress Operator namespace ~~~ oc-n openshift-ingress-operator get secret router-ca-o jsonpath="{.data.tls\.crt}" | base64-d-i > ca.crt ~~~ 3.3 Create ConfigMap for the CA cert in Openshift Configuration NameSpace ~~~ oc-n openshift-config create cm keycloak-ca--from-file=ca.crt ~~~ 3.4 Create YAML file for RH SSO Configuration ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: OAuth metadata: name: cluster spec: identityProviders:- name: keycloak mappingMethod: claim type: OpenID openID: clientID: idp-4-ocp clientSecret: name: keycloak-client-secret ca: name: keycloak-ca claims: preferredUsername:- preferred_username name:- name email:- email issuer: https://keycloak-sso-santoshi1.apps-crc.testing/auth/realms/myrealm ~~~ ~~~ oc apply-f oauth-cluster-config.yaml ~~~ 4. Try to Login to the Openshift Console, it redirects you to RH SSO login. Login with ocpuser and password which was created in RH SSO myrealm. 5. Update logoutRedirect oc edit console.config.openshift.io cluster based on [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-]platform/4.11/web_console/configuring-web-console.html) or [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4349271) 6. redirect_uri is not supported anymore with RH SSO 7.6.x [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973001) You should be able to logout using redirect_uri with backward compatibility steps mentioned in [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973001) 7. It prompts you for logout message and then logs out the user.
root_cause: - RH SSO user unable to logout from Openshift console.- https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4349271

title: Override the cluster-wide or namespace-wide default node selector
issue: A cluster has been deployed with a cluster-default nodeselector value which is not overwritten at a Namespace level

A Project/Namespace has been created with the `openshift.io/node-selector` annotation set to provide a default NodeSelector. Is there a way to override the default nodeSelector values at a Deployment / DaemonSet / Pod level?
resolution: It is not possible to override the default value set in the Namespace. Any nodeSelectors that are applied to the remaining Pods will be used in addition to the default, and not in place of this. This allows administrators to limit the scheduling of tenants by limiting placement locations on a per Namespace and cluster-wide scope. You need to prevent OpenShift project pods from being scheduled on certain nodes you can do one of the following: 1. Switch to PodNodeSelector 2. Remove the empty string from all those projects and they will use the defaultNodeSelector. Then define the defaultNodeSelector to be a label that is never associated with any of the nodes dedicated to only running specific appplications. ``` # oc patch namespace default-p \ '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"openshift.io/node-selector":"region=infra"}}}' ``` 3. Open a case with Red Hat Support Teams and a your interest in this feature can be registered.
root_cause: The `openshift.io/node-selector` annotation is applied to the Pods via an admission-controller plugin as the Pod-creation request traverses the kube-apiserver. Reviewing the code, there does not appear to be any way to work around this issue without:- Removing the annotation from the Namespace/Project- Placing the Pod into another Namespace [GitHub- openshift-kube-apiserver- nodeenv Admission Plugin](https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes/blob/5497c42cfe31180531f3fd12da260bf97bf3486f/openshift-kube-apiserver/admission/scheduler/nodeenv/admission.go/#L75-L101) ``` // If scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/node-selector is set on the pod, // do not process the pod further. if_, ok:= namespace.ObjectMeta.Annotations[kubeProjectNodeSelector]; ok {return nil} selector:= p.defaultNodeSelector if projectNodeSelector, ok:= namespace.ObjectMeta.Annotations[projectv1.ProjectNodeSelector]; ok {selector = projectNodeSelector} projectNodeSelector, err:= labelselector.Parse(selector) if err!= nil {return err}... // modify pod node selector = project node selector + current pod node selector pod.Spec.NodeSelector = labelselector.Merge(projectNodeSelector, pod.Spec.NodeSelector) < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < < ```

title: MachineConfigPool does not count Machines correctly for new MachineSet
issue: After creating a new MachineSet (MS) the MachineConfigPool (MCP) does not count the correct number of Machines within the MCP. ~~~ # TODO oc get nodes oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api-operator oc get machineconfigpool-n openshift-machine-config-operator ~~~
resolution: Reviewing the MachineConfigPool `matchineConfigSelector`, there are no changes in configuration between the `infra-log-mon`, `infra-external` and `infra-internal` MachineConfigPools. If the licensing is of concern for you, I would recommend using all the same `infra` MachineConfigPool and allocating workloads based on taints, affinities and selectors. If you require assistance with capacity planning or system design, I can refer a Red Hat Solution Architect or Consultant to discuss specific plans to rollout your applications into OpenShift. Please note that this will incur an addition cost. To avoid any excessive charges for nodes that are intended as Infrastructure nodes, please ensure they have the correct `node-role.kubernetes.io/XXX` annotations configured. This will ensure that the subscription licensing is correct. For more information on Infrastructure Nodes, please review the following article: * [Infrastructure Nodes in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5034771)
root_cause: I have reviewed the provided data and have noted that the MachineConfigPools are not unique with regards to their `machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role: ` and `node-role.kubernetes.io/infra` values. The Nodes must match exclusively a single MachineConfigPool via the labelling, however this naming pattern does not meet this requirements. For example, the `prd-6lwtw-infra-int-92zrj` Node is matches by both the the `infra-internal` and `infra-log-mon` MachineConfigPools.[0] ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Node metadata: name: prd-6lwtw-infra-int-92zrj labels: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: '' router: router_internal... ~~~ The naming convention should change from adding additional labels to making the `node-role.kubernetes.io/*` value unique. For example, replace: ~~~ node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: "" router: "router_internal" ~~~ With: ~~~ node-role.kubernetes.io/infra-internal: "" router: "router_internal" ~~~ I have provided amended MachineConfigPools and MachineSets matching this new labelling scheme for all of the provided YAMLs. This has been uploaded to the case in the most recent upload. Please apply these manifests to the cluster. These manifests will ensure that all future Machines created by the MachineSets will be labelled appropriately.

title: Containers are stuck in CreateError with 'error loading seccomp filter: errno 524' in OCP ARM64
issue: - During upgrades from 4.10 to 4.11 it can be seen error message in the `image-registry` pod: ``` Warning Failed pod/image-registry-658cd9b654-fcnrh Error: container create failed: level=error msg="runc create failed: unable to start container process: unable to init seccomp: error loading seccomp filter into kernel: error loading seccomp filter: errno 524" Warning Failed pod/image-registry-658cd9b654-fcnrh (combined from similar events): Error: container create failed: level=error msg="runc create failed: unable to start container process: unable to init seccomp: error loading seccomp filter into kernel: error loading seccomp filter: errno 524" ```- Updates may stick on a crashlooping phase. Deployment which may block further management.- Prometheus operator admission webhook's deployment fails to rollout. Cluster monitoring operator reports condition `Degraded=True` with `reason=UpdatingPrometheusOperatorFailed`- Issues can be seen at any pod using the `restricted-v2` SCC.- Issues can be seen after a successful update (e.g. at low container density in the cluster) whenever the container load increases.
resolution: This issue is known and is being worked on at [#RUN-1668](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RUN-1668) and [#OCPBUGS-2637](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-2637) ### Workaround Remove the `seccompProfiles` array from the `restricted-v2 SecurityContextConstraint`
root_cause: - This is a regression that impacts ARM64 clusters may who are updating from 4.10 to later versions, especially in conditions consisting of a huge density of containers per node (> 470), some containers can fail at creation time with this issue.- Any OCP from 4.11.0+ included a new `SecurityContextConstraint: restricted-v2`, that by default binds a `seccompProfile` to the workloads. More details can be found at [Bugzilla#2140163](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2140163#c20)

title: Control plane kubelet certificate expired
issue: - Failed login to the cluster via cli.- Kubelet certificate has expired Check the kubelet logs about `Unable to register node with API server` ~~~ Aug 16 11:34:39 master03.ocp-test.mcb.local hyperkube[13886]: I0816 11:34:39.084881 13886 kubelet_node_status.go:73] "Attempting to register node" node="master03.ocp-test.local" Aug 16 11:34:39 master03.ocp-test.mcb.local hyperkube[13886]: E0816 11:34:39.087662 13886 kubelet.go:2303] "Error getting node" err="node \"master03.ocp-test.local\" not found" Aug 16 11:34:39 master03.ocp-test.mcb.local hyperkube[13886]: E0816 11:34:39.090007 13886 kubelet_node_status.go:95] "Unable to register node with API server" err="nodes is forbidden: User \"system:anonymous\" cannot create resource \"nodes\" in API group \"\" at the cluster scope" node="master03.ocp-test.local" ~~~
resolution: From all the nodes ~~~ $ for cert in /etc/origin/node/certificates/kubelet-{client,server}-current.pem; do echo $cert; openssl x509-in $cert-noout-dates; done; $ oc get csr-oname | xargs oc adm certificate approve ~~~ Check the kube-system pod status ~~~ $ oc get po-n kube-system ~~~ ***Note: Sometimes time approving the csr, a chance of a new one will come up.*** If so, it is related with the certificate in /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-{client,server}-current.pem. Move all the certificates to a backup and approve the csr again and the master node was up and running.

title: [RHOCP 4] OSSM ServiceMeshMemberRoll  Error While Adding New Namespaces
issue: Unable to add any new project / namespaces into Service Mesh Member Role in RHOCP 4.x ~~~~ oc edit smmr-n istio-system default error: servicemeshmemberrolls.maistra.io "default" could not be patched: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "smmr.mutation.maistra.io": Post "https://maistra-admission-controller.openshift-operators.svc:443/mutate-smmr?timeout=10s": no endpoints available for service "maistra-admission-controller" You can run `oc replace-f /tmp/oc-edit-1356964637.yaml` to try this update again. ~~~~
resolution: - Get the OpenShift Service Mesh Must Gather and analyse the data for the SMCP pods, specifically istio-operator and jaeger pods ~~~~ $oc adm must-gather--image=registry.redhat.io/openshift-service-mesh/istio-must-gather-rhel8 ~~~~- Check if the Service Mesh Control Plane (smcp) status is OK and all the components are in Ready state ~~~~ oc get smcp-A NAMESPACE NAME READY STATUS PROFILES VERSION AGE istio-system basic 5/9 ComponentsNotReady ["default"] 2.0.8 173d ~~~~- Need to check the istio-operator pod and the problematic smcp pods- Fix the smcp pods that are in pending or error state in-order to address the smmr issue- Check if there are enough resources on the cluster nodes- If there are many smcp components in notReady state, the quick workaround is to restart the nodes which hold the smcp pods (specifically istio-operator pod)
root_cause: - Usually if there are some major problems on the Service Mesh Control Plane, then smmr is impacted and the problem is not with smmr itself but look for the background components or depended smcp components- Few SMCP pods are in pending state due to "failed to pull the image, i/o timeout " error- If the cluster is in disconnected environment and if you are using Mirror Registry, try to pull the image manually for the istio-operator pod and restart the pod- Notice that the pod would still not getting schedule because the cluster has a lack of resources- So restarting the cluster nodes could free up some resources and solve the issue, if needed,consider adding resources on the cluster nodes based on the future requirements

title: Wrong number of assets displayed in the project into the Business Central

title: Connection refused when connecting to a Passive mode FTP server deployed to ARO
issue: A `Connection refused` error is returned when transferring data from a passive FTP server deployed on ARO: ~~~ ftp: connect: Connection refused ~~~
The FTP server is exposed via a `LoadBalancer` service, through Azure Load Balancer (ALB)
resolution: Ensure the `.spec.externalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Local` in the `Service` definition: ~~~ $ oc patch svc/$SERVICE_NAME--type merge-p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Local"}}' service/SERVICE_NAME patched $ oc get svc/$SERVICE_NAME-o jsonpath='{.spec.externalTrafficPolicy}{"\n"}' Local ~~~ Make sure a fixed port or port range is selected as the data port for your FTP service: ~~~ $ oc get svc/SERVICE_NAME-o json | jq '.spec.ports' [{"name": "control-connection", "nodePort": 32345, "port": 12345, "protocol": "TCP", "targetPort": 12345}, {"name": "data-connection", "nodePort": 32344, "port": 12344, "protocol": "TCP", "targetPort": 12344}] ~~~
root_cause: When connecting to a passive FTP server, a control connection is established to a fixed port. When initiating a data transfer from/to a passive FTP server, a new connection is initiated to its data port. The data port can be fixed, or selected from a port range. If the new connection is not originating from the same source IP the (first) control connection is, a `Connection refused` error might be returned: ``` 220 Server ready for new user. Name (192.0.2.10:user1): user1 331 Password required for user1. Password: 230 User user1 logged in. Remote system type is UNIX. ftp> cd example-dir 250 Requested file action okay, completed. ftp> ls 227 Entering Passive Mode (192,0,2,10,4,1). ftp: connect: Connection refused ftp> bye ```

title: Mirroring all the Quay repository tags when the  latest tag is missing, results in "Last Sync Failed" error
issue: - The `mirroring` feature is enabled, but the mirroring status returns `Last Sync Failed` error and the repository has not been mirrored.- In `quay mirror pod` logs there is no error log, just these messages: ~~~ repomirrorworker stdout | 2022-06-10 10:04:35,274 [58] [INFO] [apscheduler.executors.default] Running job "RepoMirrorWorker._process_mirrors (trigger: interval[0:00:30], next run at: 2022-06-10 10:05:05 UTC)" (scheduled at 2022-06-10 10:04:35.273790+00:00) repomirrorworker stdout | 2022-06-10 10:04:35,295 [58] [INFO] [util.migrate.allocator] No candidates, marking entire block completed 1-2 repomirrorworker stdout | 2022-06-10 10:04:35,295 [58] [INFO] [util.migrate.allocator] No more work repomirrorworker stdout | 2022-06-10 10:04:35,309 [58] [INFO] [apscheduler.executors.default] Job "RepoMirrorWorker._process_mirrors (trigger: interval[0:00:30], next run at: 2022-06-10 10:05:05 UTC)" executed successfully ~~~
resolution: The issue is fixed in `Red Hat Quay 3.8.0`, released in errata [RHBA-2022:6976](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:6976). As a workaround for previous versions, in order to mirror all the tags, an existing `tag` need's to be set prior to adding the `*`, as it can be seen in the picture below:![Quay repo mirroring](https://access.redhat.com/system/files/repo_mirror.png) This way, it will use the defined tag as entry point and will mirror all the images.
root_cause: The issue has been identified, and a bug opened: [Support repo mirror of repos that don't have a latest tag](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-2179) If a `*` is set on the mirroring tags with the idea of mirroring all the `tags`, the first tag that Quay looks for is `latest` tag as default. If the `latest` tag does not exist in the repository, Quay will not find it and will stop the mirroring, but it will not show an error.

title: Empty node-sizing SYSTEM_RESERVED_ES parameter can result in kubelet not starting in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: After upgrading to RHOCP 4.11.17 or 4.10.43, nodes got stuck in `NotReady` state, showing the below `kubelet` error message: Dec 07 12:38:46 cp-node-01 hyperkube[100739]: Error: failed to run Kubelet: quantities must match the regular expression '^([+-]?[0-9.]+)([eEinumkKMGTP]*[-+]?[0-9]*)$' Dec 07 12:38:46 cp-node-01 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'. Dec 07 12:38:46 cp-node-01 systemd[1]: Failed to start Kubernetes Kubelet.
After upgrading to RHOCP 4.11.17or 4.10.43 experienced an issue whereby `/etc/node-sizing.env` on its master nodes contained an empty `SYSTEM_RESERVED_ES` value.
resolution: * This problem was resolved in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.11.25 via [RHSA-2023:0245](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0245). Please update to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.11.25 or later to prevent this issue from happening. * This problem was resolved in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.10.51 via [RHSA-2023:0561](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0561). Please update to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.10.51 or later to prevent this issue from happening. ### Workaround when encountering the issue 1. fix the `kubeletconfig` object(s) according to the [Manually allocating resources for nodes documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-resources-configuring.html#nodes-nodes-resources-configuring-setting_nodes-nodes-resources-configuring), ensure the `ephemeral-storage` option is set to a desired value. This will create a new rendered version that will be applied to the remaining nodes once the faulty one will be fixed. 2. Check the config: $ oc get kubeletconfig-o json | jq-r.spec.kubeletConfig.systemReserved 3. Set a valid value for `SYSTEM_RESERVED_ES` (with the same value as set previously) in the config file `/etc/node-sizing.env` on the affected node. 4. Afterwards, restart the `kubelet` service using `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` to get the node back into `Ready` and working state. ### Pro-active workaround when planning to update a cluster to an impacted version (_cf Environment section_) 1. Ensure that you have SSH access to your nodes 2. Disabled the compute Machine Config Pools (MCPs) to ensure that the node are not going to update right after the update is completed. $ for MCP in $(oc get mcp-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name!= "master") |.metadata.name'); do oc patch mcp/${MCP}--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'; done 3. Proceed with the update/upgrade to the desired version 4. Review the MCPs to confirm that the variable `SYSTEM_RESERVED_ES` is set. $ oc get mcp $ for MCP in $(oc get mcp-o json | jq-r '.items[].metadata.name'); do echo-e "\n===== ${MCP} ====="; RENDERED=$(oc get mcp ${MCP}-o json | jq-r.spec.configuration.name); echo "=> ${RENDERED}"; oc get mc ${RENDERED}-o json | jq-r '.spec.config.storage.files[] | select(.path == "/etc/node-sizing-enabled.env")' |sed-e "s/%0A/\n/g"-e "s/%20/ /g"-e "s/%2B/+/g"-e "s/%2F/\//g"-e "s/%3D/=/g"-e "s/%3A/:/g"-e "s/%7B/{/g"-e "s/%7D/}/g"-e "s/%5B/\[/g"-e "s/%5D/\]/g"-e "s/%22/\"/g"-e "s/%2C/,/g"-e "s/%40/@/g"-e "s/%23/#/g"-e "s/%25/%/g"-e "s/%24/$/g"-e "s/%7C/|/g"-e "s/%5C/\\\/g"-e "s/%3B/;/g"; done 5. Resume the MCPs $ for MCP in $(oc get mcp-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name!= "master") |.metadata.name'); do oc patch mcp/${MCP}--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"paused":false}}'; done
root_cause: A bug was introduced in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.10.43 and 4.11.17 when trying to fix an issue related to the `systemReserved.ephemeral-storage` in `KubeletConfig`.

title: How to update operators from CLI?
issue: - How to update the `logging stack` from CLI?- How to update an `OLM` provided operator from CLI?- Unable to update an `operator` from the web console.
resolution: The steps to update an `OLM` provided `operator` from the `command line` has been explained here with the example of updating the `logging` stack. Here are the steps:- Select a project and get a list of subscriptions in the project: ~~~ $ oc project $ oc get subscriptions ~~~- Confirm that the channel to which you want to upgrade is available. To get the available operator channel versions, replace in the command below with a package name. ~~~ $ oc get packagemanifest-o=jsonpath='{.status.channels[*].name}' ~~~- If the `approval strategy` is automatic, change it to manual: ~~~ $ oc get sub $ oc patch subscription/$subscriptionName--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"installPlanApproval":"Manual"}}' [Replace $subscriptionName with the subscription name.] ~~~- Modify the `spec` section as follows: ~~~ $ oc project openshift-operators-redhat $ oc edit sub elasticsearch-operator spec: channel: stable-5.3 <-- change this to the desired channel. I changed it to **stable-5.4** installPlanApproval: Manual name: elasticsearch-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: elasticsearch-operator.5.3.9 <-- This shows the current version ~~~- Check if the new `install-plan` got created: ~~~ $ oc get ip NAME CSV APPROVAL APPROVED install-6wn8p elasticsearch-operator.5.3.9 Manual true <---The old one install-7jzn4 elasticsearch-operator.5.4.3 Manual false <--- latest `install plan` ~~~- Approve the `update`: ~~~ $ oc patch installplan $installplanName--type json--patch '[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/approved", "value": true}]' [Replace $installplanName with the latest install-plan name. Here it was: install-7jzn4] ~~~- Check if the `update` is succeeded: ~~~ $ watch oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE elasticsearch-operator.5.4.3 OpenShift Elasticsearch Operator 5.4.3 elasticsearch-operator.5.3.9 Succeeded ~~~- Edit the `subscription` of `logging operator` as below: ~~~ $ oc project openshift-logging $ oc edit sub cluster-logging spec: channel: stable-5.4 <---- Changed to the desired channel installPlanApproval: Manual name: cluster-logging source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: cluster-logging.5.3.9 ~~~- Approve the new `install plan` ~~~ $ oc get ip NAME CSV APPROVAL APPROVED install-jllm9 cluster-logging.5.3.9 Manual true install-zv8f7 cluster-logging.5.4.3 Manual false $ oc patch installplan $installplanName--type json--patch '[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/approved", "value": true}]' [Replace $installplanName with the latest install-plan name. Here it was: install-7jzn4] ~~~- Check if the `update` is successful: ~~~ $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE cluster-logging.5.4.3 Red Hat OpenShift Logging 5.4.3 cluster-logging.5.3.9 Succeeded elasticsearch-operator.5.4.3 OpenShift Elasticsearch Operator 5.4.3 elasticsearch-operator.5.3.9 Succeeded ~~~ **Note: All pods will get restarted**- Check if they are all in running state after some time: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-logging ~~~

title: Unable to delete ROSA cluster as well add-on ODF-service
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Unable to delete ROSA cluster when add-on OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)-service.- `Error: Failed to get Managed Service: Failed to get managed service with id 1x53xx3xx275xxx3xjru6fqlnsxx73x9:: status is 500, identifier is '9', code is 'OCM-MS-9' and operation identifier is '2XXozXvo9FrWoLuYE7GBoTmXXXX': Unable to get managed service: record not found`
resolution: - The cluster created with "rosa service", so it should be deleted with the same command.- [Uninstalling Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation Managed Service consumer add-on using the Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS CLI](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation_managed_service/2022-q2/html-single/adding_the_red_hat_openshift_data_foundation_managed_service/index#proc_uninstalling-the-odf-ms-consumer-add-on-uisng-rosa-cli_deploy-models)- The procedure is:- Check services `$ rosa list services` `$ rosa delete service--id= `- Then go for deletion the cluster:- Check clusters `$ rosa list clusters` `$ rosa delete cluster--cluster=--watch`
root_cause: In ROSA, before deletion the cluster add-on services should be deleted first and then go for deletion the cluster.

title: The Ceph cluster is flapping very often in an ODF deployment.
issue: The Ceph cluster is flapping very often in an ODF cluster.
`auto_repair` getting triggered for Ceph PG's and causing the Ceph cluster to in 'HEALTH_WARN'.
root_cause: * The PG's goes into `active+clean+scrubbing+repair` state and the `Rook-Ceph` operator detects it to be node drain operation and sets the `noout` flag. * The `auto_repair` is getting triggered because of a [known bug](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/50900). * Upgrade the ODF cluster to the latest z-stream version or having Ceph v16.2.6 and above.

title: Gateway Timeout received when trying to create "app-" index-pattern in Kibana
issue: - When trying to create `app-` index pattern Kibana UI shows 504 timeout issues for new users, although these new users are authorized to access pod logs for a given namepsace- After increasing the kibana routes timeout to 300s, i.e. setting `"annotations": {"haproxy.router.openshift.io/timeout": "300s"` on kibana route, 504 timeout issue was gone but resulted in 502 errors
resolution: - Edit ES CR log retention limit to the recommended 7d max period. Logs are recommended to retain for a max period of 7 days in the default Elasticsearch instance. Please check the below info(in italics) from About Log Store documentation https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/logging/cluster-logging.html#cluster-logging-about-logstore_cluster-logging_The logging subsystem Elasticsearch instance is optimized and tested for short term storage, approximately seven days. If you want to retain your logs over a longer term, it is recommended you move the data to a third-party storage system_
root_cause: - The timeout seems to be happening because app- index pattern is querying huge chunk of data(as all application logs are currently forwarded in your ClusterLogForwarder config plus there is about 30days logs to query). The infra index pattern got created just fine because it has less data to manage and also json logging is not enabled for infrastructure.

title: Red Hat Quay could not connect to storage
issue: Quay is not running as intended. From logs: DistributedStorage- Could not connect to storage local_us. Error: The AWS access key Id you provided does not exist in our records.
resolution: Edit Quay `Config Bundle Secret` and make sure that `s3_access_key` and `s3_secret_key` keys inside `config.yaml` contains valid AWS `Access Key Id` and `Secret key`. For example: ~~~ $ oc get secret-n-o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' | base64-d DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: s3Storage:- S3Storage- host: s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com s3_access_key: ABCDEFGHIJKLMN s3_secret_key: OL3ABCDEFGHIJKLMN s3_bucket: quay_bucket storage_path: /datastorage/registry DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_DEFAULT_LOCATIONS: [] DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_PREFERENCE:- s3Storage ~~~
root_cause: The error message `The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist in our records` suggests that there is an issue with the credentials that you're using. The access key that you're using might have been deleted, or the associated `AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)` role or the user might have been deleted.

As a workaround, you can use a secondary network interface connected to your host, or switch to the OpenShift SDN default CNI provider. ~~~

title: Kafka producer got "Not Enough Replicas" when produce requests go up
issue: on a strimzi kafka cluster (3 broker) deployed on Openshift we've configured about 45 topics. On a specific topic sometimes, the produce requests go up 10k or even above, due to this the producer got the Not Enough Replicas error and we need to restart the brokers and also producer to restore normal functionality.
resolution: You have configured min.insync.replicas to 3. Thus, three broker instances must be present when the message producers publish messages to the corresponding topic. I'm afraid the exception you cited is bound to occur should there be less than three broker instances at the time of publishing messages. If this issue occurs again, please check the number of active broker instances. The other approach is to reduce the min.insync.replicas attribute to 2 should that be cited as a reasonable option.
