title: OpenShift GitOps ArgoCD deployment is intermittently deleted from OpenShift
issue: Installing the GitOps Operator to not have a 'default installation', the company has decided to create a custom ArgoCD deployment based on our requirements. ``` apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: openshift-gitops-operator namespace: openshift-operators spec: channel: gitops-1.7 config: env:- name: DISABLE_DEFAULT_ARGOCD_INSTANCE value: 'true' installPlanApproval: Manual name: openshift-gitops-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ```
resolution: An installation guide has been created by one of Red Hat's architects for how to install the upstream component while using the OpenShift GitOps Operator. https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/how-to-use-hashicorp-vault-and-argo-cd-for-gitops-on-openshift Following the guide, the ArgoCD Deployment must be configured to incorporate the valut-plugin as a generation plugin using the following snippet: ~~~ configManagementPlugins: |-- name: argocd-vault-plugin generate: command: ["argocd-vault-plugin"] args: ["generate", "./"] ~~~ Reviewing your provided ArgoCD deployment YAML this configuration appears to be missing. Can you please ensure this is applied to the ArgoCD object? Additionally, can you please provide me with a screenshot of the warning provided as I'm not sure where this is presented. (i.e. OpenShift Web Console, ArgoCD Web Console, etc) ~~~ "This resource is managed by ArgoCD ACD openshift-gitops and any modifications may be overwritten. Edit the managing resource to preserve changes." ~~~
root_cause: The changes are performed in the ArgoCD deployment in `openshift-gitops` with the same 'default' name Appears the operator is attempting to remove the 'default' argo deployment and is mistaking your custom deployment for the default.

title: FAQ related to how to secure communication within the  openshift cluster
issue: - Information required on security-related topics, specifically regarding services running within the cluster- Are there some controls customers can employ in openshift to prevent attacks from other applications running inside the cluster?
resolution: - What are the recommended practices for securing communication among microservices in the openshift cluster? How can customers prevent attacks from within the cluster? Red Hat OpenShift [Service Mesh](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/service_mesh/v2x/ossm-architecture.html) provides a platform for behavioral insight and operational control over your networked microservices in a service mesh. Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh allows you to connect, secure, and monitor microservices in your OpenShift Container Platform environment. All the requests to service mesh are handled by [mTLS](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/secure-your-microservices).*mTLS* is a protocol that applies the TLS authentication protocol in both directions, client to server and server to client. Kiali provides visibility into your service mesh by showing you the microservices in your service mesh and how they are connected. Documentation [Link](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/openshift-networking-and-cluster-access-best-practices) provides some recommendations for best practices for making clusters secure.- Is TLS communication between microservices enabled in openshift and how is this enabled? [Secure routes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/networking/routes/secured-routes.html) provide the ability to use several types of TLS termination to serve certificates to the client. By default, OpenShift does not ensure secure traffic between two or more pods but [serving certificate secrets](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/security/certificates/service-serving-certificate.html#understanding-service-serving_service-serving-certificate) can be used to ensure encrypted communication inside OpenshiftSDN.- Can certificates be defined in network policy? You can define network policies that restrict traffic to pods in the Openshift cluster. Network policies are just like RBAC which defines what can connect to the pod(Ingress) and where can this pod connect(egress). Basically, without a network policy in place, all pods in a namespace are accessible from other pods and network endpoints. To isolate one or more pods in a namespace, you can create NetworkPolicy objects in that namespace to indicate the allowed ingress and egress connections. Network policies are just for network isolation, certificates can't be used in Network policy.- How to achieve the objective of enabling TLS communication between microservices? Can this be done using third-party certificates? Yes, svc-svc communication is secured using [service signer CA signed certs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/security/certificates/service-serving-certificate.html). [Serving Certificates Secrets](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6837731) feature uses an *internal Certification Authority (CA)* to facilitate the creation of certificates for the application. Internal Certificates are internally managed and can't be replaced by third-party certificates. Public-facing certificates can be *replaced* by third-party certificates as they are frontend and not used internally.- The service-ca is an operator which generates self-signed service-serving certificates for use on OCP-managed services, however, if the customer wishes to secure a user-managed service customer will have to annotate the service resource definition, which automatically generates a [self-signed service-serving certificate](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/security/certificates/service-serving-certificate.html#add-service-certificate_service-serving-certificate) for the service. Is this understanding correct? Yes, understanding is correct. service-ca is an Operator that creates a self-signed CA when an OpenShift Container Platform cluster is deployed which is used as a signer to generate certificates for OCP *Internal Services* but for *user-managed services* to use encrypted communication customer can annotate the service resource definition to generate a *self-signed service-serving* certificate for the service as mentioned in self-signed [service-serving certificate](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/security/certificates/service-serving-certificate.html#add-service-certificate_service-serving-certificate)- In incase there is no annotation made on user-managed services, is TLS still enabled by default? By default, OpenShift does not ensure secure traffic between two or more pods. If there is no annotation made on user-managed services, traffic won't be secured. Customers can use *Serving Certificate Secrets* to ensure encrypted communication inside Openshift SDN.[KB article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6837731) explains more about this.- What is the difference between service-serving certificates and user-provided TLS certificates used in routes? Service-serving certificates are used to secure custom services for internal communication. Routes are public-facing objects and are part of the *ingress process* user-provided TLS certificates can only be used in routes as these are public-facing, not service-serving certificates.- In terms of customizable/system-managed certificates in openshift, how are TLS and mTLS configured? There are no mTLS features outside of the Openshift service mesh that is available by default.- Where in openshift is TLS/mTLS enabled? in what situations would it be a risk if TLS but not mTLS is used? Openshift service mesh provides *mTLS* features for network communication for mesh members whether they are services. The default openshift wildcard certificates provide TLS edge termination for exposed services.- Does openshift support mTLS by default for service-service communication? Is there a way to configure mTLS between services without the use of service mesh? mTLS between services requires a mesh, e.g.Openshift service mesh. It is free and requires no additional subscriptions. It is very much like a network expansion pack.- Is the understanding that [mutual-tls-auth_configuring-ingress](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/networking/ingress-operator.html#nw-mutual-tls-auth_configuring-ingress) encrypts client-to-service communication correct? Yes,customer can configure the Ingress Controller to enable mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication by setting a spec.clientTLS value. The *clientTLS* value configures the Ingress Controller to verify client certificates.

title: Restarting operator pods
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? We have detected a problem with several operators, which are frequently rebooted. title: Login failed (401 Unauthorized) using LDAP users in RHOCP 4
issue: - The `Openshift` login with `LDAP` user is failing with an invalid `username/password with error: Login failed (401 Unauthorized)`. ~~~ Login failed (401 Unauthorized) Verify you have provided correct credentials. ~~~- Unable to login to `OpenShift web console` using `LDAP credentials`.
resolution: - There could be multiple reasons for this issue. In this case `LDAP URL` in the `spec` section of `oauth` cluster resource was not correct. Verify the LDAP details using the diagnostic steps mentioned and modify them if incorrect. ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: OAuth metadata:..... spec: identityProviders:- ldap:........ url: ldaps:// <> ~~~ Note: After above modification, all the `oauth pods` will restart and `LDAP user` will be able to access the cluster.
root_cause: - The `LDAP url` not correct in `oauth` `cluster` file.

title: Openshift Gitops Operator in Unknown state in RHOCP 4
issue: - Redhat Openshift Gitops Operator shows `Unknown` state in the `Installed Operators` section of the OpenShift Console.- The `CSV` of Openshift Gitops Operator not present.- The Openshift Gitops Operator `subscription` shows `CatalogSourcesUnhealthy`.
resolution: - Delete the `job` and associated `configmap` of `gitops operator` which is in `unknown` state in `openshift-marketplace` namespace. ~~~ $ oc delete job-n openshift-marketplace $ oc delete configmap-n openshift-marketplace ~~~- After above step delete the `sub,csv,ip` of gitops operator in `openshift-operators` namespace. ~~~ $ oc get sub,csv,ip-n openshift-operators |grep-i gitops ~~~ ~~~ $ oc delete ip-n openshift-operators $ oc delete sub-n openshift-operators $ oc delete csv-n openshift-operators ~~~ Note: If any of the above is not present you can skip executing the associated command.- After deleting `sub,csv,ip`, navigate to `Operators → OperatorHub` in `webconsole` to check if `Gitops` operator uninstalled or not.- Install the operator again from the GUI using [document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/cicd/gitops/installing-openshift-gitops.html).
root_cause: - The `OLM` avoids pulling the `Operator Bundle Images` directly, Instead, `OLM` creates a job that points to the `Operator Bundle Images` and saves the Kubernetes manifests to the contents of a `configmap`. The `Openshift gitops operator` `job` has failed on the cluster, resulting in no data in `configmap` due to which `operator` went to an `Unknown` state.

title: Virtual Machine fails to start with "Unable to create tap device tap0: Invalid argument"
issue: Virtual Machine is not starting
After changing the vNIC model from virtio to e1000e the VM will not start
Virtual Machine stuck on starting after network setting change
resolution: * The recommended option is to use virtio-net, which supports multiqueue. * However, if e1000e is needed, please edit the Virtual Machine YAML and remove the networkInterfaceMultiqueue setting: ~~~ interfaces:- macAddress: '02:27:34:00:00:08' masquerade: {} model: e1000e name: default networkInterfaceMultiqueue: true <-------- remove this line or set to false ~~~
root_cause: * Changing from virtio-net to e1000e using the Web Console does not disable networkInterfaceMultiqueue * Virtual Machine fails to start if e1000e is the model and networkInterfaceMultiqueue is enabled. * This is a bug, being tracked in [Bug 2173254- networkInterfaceMultiqueue breaks VM start with e1000e](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2173254).

title: Unable to pull Image :  Error parsing image configuration: Download config.json in RHOCP 4
issue: - Unable to pull image from catalog.- Error getting while pulling an image: ~~~ "registry.connect.redhat.com/instana/instana-agent-operator-bundle@sha256:xyz": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = parsing image configuration: Download config.json digest sha256:xxy does not match expected sha256:xyy ~~~
resolution: There can be multiple reasons: 1. Check if the registry is listed in allowed registry configuration. `cat /etc/containers/registries.conf` OR 2. Clear the blob cache info.- Take a backup of the file `/var/lib/containers/storage/cache/blob-info-cache-v1.boltdb`. ~~~ cp /var/lib/containers/storage/cache/blob-info-cache-v1.boltdb /tmp/var/lib/containers/storage/cache/blob-info-cache-v1.boltdb_bkp ~~~- Remove the file from /var/lib/containers/storage/cache/blob-info-cache-v1.boltdb from the node. ~~~ rm-rf /var/lib/containers/storage/cache/blob-info-cache-v1.boltdb ~~~- Pull the image again using `podman pull` command: ~~~ podman pull: ~~~
root_cause: - The cache for the Blob info having bad or incorrect data. The cache present at `/var/lib/containers/storage/cache/blob-info-cache-v1.boltdb`.

title: Troubleshooting LDAP/AD authentication issues in OCP
issue: - What all are the preliminary checks to start with troubleshooting LDAP/AD authentication issues in OCP
resolution: - Verify that the LDAP configuration is correct. Ensure that the LDAP server address, port number, and user credentials are correct. ~~~ $ oc get oauth/cluster-oyaml ~~~- Check OCP authentication pod logs: ~~~ $ for i in `oc-n openshift-authentication get pods-o jsonpath='{range.items[*].metadata}{.name}{"\n"}{end}'`; do oc-n openshift-authentication logs $i &> $i.log; done ~~~- Check the logs of the LDAP server to see if there are any errors that may be causing the issue. Look for authentication-related errors or warnings.- Verify that the user account you are trying to log in with exists in AD and that it is enabled.- Verify that there are no issues with the network connectivity between the OCP server and the AD LDAP server. Test connectivity by pinging the LDAP server from the OCP server.- Check the firewall settings on the OCP server and the AD LDAP server to ensure that they are not blocking the communication between the two servers.

title: Is OPENSSL vulnerability(X.509 Email Address Buffer Overflow) affected in OCP 4.X
issue: - OPENSSL vulnerabilities reported through CVE-2022-3602 and CVE-2022-3786 are affected on OCP?- X.509 Email Address Buffer Overflow- OPENSSL VA
resolution: - The openssl version, which can be seen on OCP nodes would be of version OpenSSL 1.1 as OCP nodes use Red Hat CoreOS(RHCOS) and are based on RHEL 8.- The mentioned vulnerability on OpenSSL only impacts Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) version 9.- Red Hat Enterprise Linux versions 8 and below are based on OpenSSL version 1.x and are not affected by this vulnerability.- Any Red Hat product supported on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 that pulls the OpenSSL package from the RHEL channel is also unaffected. For example, layered products, such as Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (including RHEL CoreOS), Red Hat OpenStack Platform, and Red Hat Virtualization.- Hence OCP is not affected by this vulnerability For more info: [RHSB-2022-004 X.509 Email Address Buffer Overflow- OpenSSL- (CVE-2022-3602 and CVE-2022-3786)](https://access.redhat.com/security/vulnerabilities/RHSB-2022-004)

title: Unable to decode the CA pem bundle from IDP configmap.
issue: - While decoding the CA pem bundle provided through configmap in `openshift-config` namespace for trusting the IDP CA throws error: ~~~ $ oc get cm-n openshift-config-o jsonpath='{.data.ca-bundle\.crt}' openssl crl2pkcs7-nocrl-certfile /dev/stdin | openssl pkcs7-print_certs-noout-text unable to load certificate 140234456332096:error:0909006C:PEM routines:get_name:no start line:crypto/pem/pem_lib.c:745:Expecting: TRUSTED CERTIFICATE ~~~

title: Connecting to a remote server from an application pod running on OCP throws the error "SSL routines:tls_process_ske_dhe:dh key too small"
issue: - Connecting to a remote server from an application pod running on OCP throws the error "SSL routines:tls_process_ske_dhe:dh key too small"
resolution: - Use any of the below resolutions/; 1. Add some strong TLS 1.2 ciphers like "ECDHE" over weak DHE(Recommended fix): ~~~ $ openssl ciphers-tls1_2 | tr: \\n | grep-e ECDHE | grep-v CBC ~~~ 2. Update the base image of the container to use RHEL 7 UBI/RHEL 7 Based host. 3. Modify the host crypto policy in the pod(Least Recommended): ~~~ $ update-crypto-policies--set LEGACY ~~~ Use either some sort of init container or use it as a "CMD" in the docker file or at the time of image building.
root_cause: - The error is due to a cipher negotiation issue.- The remote server prefers DH (Diffie Hellman) key for the TLS negotiation using DHE Cipher with RSA(asymmetric).- Container host is RHEL 8 based and hence unlike RHEL 7 still supports the legacy crypto policies, RHEL 8 prefers a strong one.

title: Argo CD GUI not working post chnaging the TLS termination to "Reencrypt"

title: RHEL8: TCP encapsulated in UDP tunnel is dropped on vmxnet3 adapters
issue: - VXLAN on `vmxnet3` in RHEL 8.3 might cause TCP packet length to be calculated wrong in VXLAN frames.- VMware ESX drops packets coming from RHEL 8 container host machines.- After scaling the workers into the existing OpenShift cluster not all the functionality of the OpenShift SDN works.- Podman pod-to-pod connectivity is slow or reaches timeout.- [k3s on rhel 8 network/dns probleme and metrics not work #5013](https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/issues/5013) upstream k3s GitHub Issue for flannel networking
resolution: Update to RHEL 8.5 (`kernel-4.18.0-348.el8`) or later. Update to VMware ESXi 6.7P07 and 7.0U3 (7.0.3) or later. These updates include logic which disables `tx-checksum-ip-generic` for tunnels which the `vmxnet3` NIC does not support, so the end result is the same as the workaround below. ### Workaround Disable `tx-checksum-ip-generic` in VMs with `vmxnet3` adapters doing UDP tunneling: ~~~ ethtool-K DEVNAME tx-checksum-ip-generic off ~~~ This configuration can be applied persistently as described at: * [How to make NIC ethtool settings persistent (apply automatically at boot)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2127401) ### Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) See [Update or fresh installation with OpenShift Container Platform 4.7.24 or 4.8 may fail with networking issues on vSphere](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6279691)
root_cause: - RHEL 8.2 and earlier (including RHEL 7) didn't offload VXLAN checksum even with `tx-checksum-ip-generic` enabled, so this issue never affected those releases.- The patch [vmxnet3: add geneve and vxlan tunnel offload support](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/commit/?id=dacce2be3312) went into RHEL 8.3, enabling VXLAN checksum offloading for `vmxnet3` adapters. However, there were multiple problems with that commit.- Inner TCP traffic checksum was calculated incorrectly, repaired with upstream patch [vmxnet3: use correct tcp hdr length when packet is encapsulated](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/commit/?id=8a7f280f29a8) which was included in RHEL 8.4 via driver update on **Red Hat Private Bug 1868451**.- The inner offload capability is only for UDP tunnels, repaired with upstream patch [vmxnet3: fix cksum offload issues for non-udp tunnels](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/netdev/net.git/commit/?id=1dac3b1bc66dc68dbb0c9f43adac71a7d0a0331a) which was included in RHEL 8.4 via driver update on **Red Hat Private Bug 1868451**.- The underlying `vmxnet3` NIC implementation only supports VXLAN checksum offload for specific UDP ports, so checksum offload fails for tunnels using any other port. This was repaired with a RHEL-only patch supplied by VMware which disables VXLAN checksum offload when required, so checksum failures never happen. VMware advised this repair also requires a VMware update to ESXi 6.7P07 and 7.0U3 (7.0.3) or later. This was included with a driver update into RHEL 8.5 on **Private Bug 1941714- [ESXi][RHEL-8] VMXNET3 v4 causes invalid checksums of inner packets of VXLAN tunnel**.

title: Creating new statefulset causes the pods to consume all the CPU resource from the available quota
issue: - Creating a statefulset resource causes the pod to consume all the available CPU from he resource quota. ~~~ 51s Warning FailedCreate statefulset/application-test-patroni create Pod application-test-patroni-0 in StatefulSet application-test-patroni failed error: pods "application-test-patroni-0" is forbidden: exceeded quota: compute-long-running-quota, requested: limits.cpu=200m, used: limits.cpu=1950m, limited: limits.cpu=2 ~~~- Before creating the statefulset resource there is ample of space available for the desired number of replicas. However when the statefulset resource is created, it consumes all the available resources (cpu/memory) from the resource quota.
resolution: Remove the selector and label from the deployment/statefulset such that the values which are controlled by the application running inside the pods are not used in the deployment/statefulset.
root_cause: The statefulset resource had a `selector` (role: master) to match with the label on the pod that was created by this statefulset resource. This label on the pod was also being controlled by the application running inside the pod. The application while starting changed the value of the label `role` on the pod from `master` to `promoted` which caused the statefulset controller to think that it has no matching pods and it tries to create the same pod again and this keeps repeating.

title: [RHACS / StackRox] : sensor pod crashing with the panic: tls: failed to find any PEM data in key input
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - RHACS `Sensor` pod is crashing with the error: `panic: tls: failed to find any PEM data in key input`.
resolution: - Generate the new `init bundle` and download the secrets YAML as per the [document](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/3.73/installing/installing_ocp/init-bundle-ocp.html#roxctl-generate-init-bundle_init-bundle-ocp).- Delete the older `secrets` for `sensor`, `collector`, and `admission-control` and recreate the `secrets` with the new `init bundle` YAML. ~~~ # oc delete sensor-tls collector-tls admission-control-tls-n # oc create-f-n ~~~- After that, scale down and scale up the `sensor`, `collector`, and `admission-control` pods to pick the new secrets or recreate the pods: ~~~ # oc scale deploy/admission-control deploy/sensor--replicas=0-n # oc scale deploy/sensor--replicas=1-n # oc scale deploy/admission-control--replicas=3-n # oc delete pod-l app=collector-n ~~~
root_cause: - The `Key` or `certificate` in the secrets is corrupted.

title: Dev Spaces IDE fails to start with "Error provisioning workspace Kubernetes components"
issue: When specifying a DevFile for a Dev Space and specifying a `kubernetes` component, starting the IDE fails with the following error message: ~~~ 'Error provisioning workspace Kubernetes components: kubernetes/openshift components that define a URI are unsupported (component user-runtime)' ~~~
The IDE fails to start and shows the following error message: ~~~ The workspace has not received an IDE URL in the last 20 seconds. Try to re-open the workspace. ~~~
resolution: * This is a known limitation of the Dev Spaces Operator, adding a component via URI [is not supported](https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/blob/main/docs/unsupported-devfile-api.adoc). * There exists an issue in the Dev Workspace Operator v0.19.0 related to RBAC, please update to the Dev Workspace Operator v0.19.1 to resolve this known issue. * Instead of specifying a component using an `uri` field, use the `inlined` definition for the `components`: ~~~ components:- name: myk8deploy kubernetes: inlined: | apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: Job metadata: name: pi spec: template: spec: containers:- name: job image: myimage command: ["some", "command"] restartPolicy: Never ~~~

title: /bin/toolbox: failed to runlabel on image
issue: - Toolbox command fails with below error: ~~~ # toolbox.toolboxrc file detected, overriding defaults... Spawning a container 'toolbox-root' with image 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:1ab4c65112e9a54687c86567cecfa2a0aedf643d4b25714a04c4b85366ea3fae' Detected RUN label in the container image. Using that as the default... Error: cannot find the value of label: RUN in image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:1ab4c65112e9a54687c86567cecfa2a0aedf643d4b25714a04c4b85366ea3fae /usr/bin/toolbox: failed to runlabel on image 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:1ab4c65112e9a54687c86567cecfa2a0aedf643d4b25714a04c4b85366ea3fae' ~~~
resolution: - Remove `.toolboxrc ` so the default `registry.redhat.io/rhel8/support-tools' image will be used.
root_cause: - The toolbox command is using the image defined in /root/.toolboxrc file, which is `quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:1ab4c65112e9a54687c86567cecfa2a0aedf643d4b25714a04c4b85366ea3fae` instead of default `registry.redhat.io/rhel8/support-tools`.- When toolbox command is run, it will inspect the image and try to obtain Labels.run, if it fails to find any, no value is set for runlabel=, which causes this issue.

title: User with access scope to specific namespace are not able to get information of other users in RHACS
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - If a user with Access Scopes set to specific namespaces tries to drill in on a User or Group they do not get any useful information displayed. The number of roles shown is 0 and the namespace permissions doesn't show anything. ~~~ Config Management > RBAC > Users and Groups ~~~ Above doesn't work if user has access scopes which could provide useful information to security users who have been delegated to manage specific namespaces in one or more clusters.
resolution: - This is being worked by engineering team and ETA is to be fixed in RHACS v3.74.0.
root_cause: - Its possible, with appropriate permissions (READ Cluster, Deployment Group, K8sRole, K8sRoleBinding, K8sSubject,ServiceAccount, Secret), to show users & groups / service accounts and their respective roles and namespace permissions, given that the rolebinding is binding a namespaced role and the access scope includes the namespace. However, its not possible to show the permissions if the rolebinding is done to a clusterrole and the access scope only allows access to namespaces- For example, below rolebinding, which which grants permission in namespace "default" ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: test-rolebinding namespace: default roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: system:registry subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: test namespace: default ~~~- Above service-account (applicable also to user & groups) has no permissions within the namespace, although a user with access to the complete cluster can see the given permissions within the namespace.

title: Alpine-based applications intermittently fails to resolve DNS
issue: Using Alpine as a base image for containerization has become popular due to its small size and resource efficiency. However, it has been observed that using Alpine as a base image may lead to issues with DNS resolution, which can cause network connectivity problems. Alpine does not include the `GNU C library (glibc)` by default, which is a dependency for most DNS resolution libraries used in applications. Instead, it uses `musl libc`, which has a different implementation of DNS resolution that may not work properly with some applications. CoreDNS in OCP 4.11 was fixed to truncate DNS requests > `512 bytes` for non-EDNS requests. Alpine Linux, more specifically, `musl-libc` doesn't support EDNS nor DNS via TCP at this moment. Recommended reading: [Does Red Hat support alpine based container issues?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3461901)
resolution: To avoid DNS resolution issues, it is recommended to use a different base image that includes glibc, such as UBI(Red Hat Universal Base Image). All base images provided by Red Hat can be found in the [Certified Container Catalog](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/search?build_categories_list=Builder%20image&p=1&release_categories=Generally%20Available&product_listings_names=Red%20Hat%20Universal%20Base%20Image%209|Red%20Hat%20Universal%20Base%20Image%208|Red%20Hat%20Enterprise%20Linux%208|Red%20Hat%20Enterprise%20Linux%209)

issue: - How to update an Azure service principal for an OCP private cluster after it expires.- Is it possible to update Azure service principal after getting expires in a Vanilla OCP disconnected private cluster?
resolution: - In project kube-system, take backup of secret azure-credentials: ~~~ $ oc project kube-system $ oc get secret azure-credentials-o yaml > azurecred-backup.yaml ~~~- Make changes in the same secret: ~~~ $ oc edit secret azure-credentials-n kube-system apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: namespace: kube-system name: azure-credentials stringData: azure_subscription_id: azure_client_id: azure_client_secret: azure_tenant_id: azure_resource_prefix: azure_resourcegroup: azure_region: azure subscription id: The subscription ID to use for the cluster. Specify the id value in your account output. azure tenant id: The tenant ID. Specify the tenantId value in your account output. azure service principal client id: The value of the appId parameter for the service principal. azure service principal client secret: The value of the password parameter for the service principal. ~~~- Ensure azure_client_id and azure_client_secret are correct.- Encode it into base64 format and update it on "azure_client_secret: " field so it gets updated.- Get the base64 encoded value of the new client secret: ~~~ $ echo " " | base64-i ~~~- In order to verify changes, use below mentioned commands: ~~~ export azure_client_id=$(jq-r '.azure_client_id' file.yaml |base64-d) export azure_client_secret=$(jq-r '.azure_client_secret' file.yaml |base64-d) export azure_tenant_id=$(jq-r '.azure_tenant_id' file.yaml |base64-d)- Login using this credentials in Azure with what we got: az login--service-principal-u $azure_client_id \--password $azure_client_secret--tenant $azure_tenant_id ~~~

title: Pods are scheduling on same worker nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: - Openshift schedules all pods to different nodes, but noticed that some pods are scheduled on same nodes although there is resource available on the other nodes. ~~~ $oc get pods-o wide NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE READINESS GATES pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk0.xx--> scheduled on the same node pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk0.xx--> scheduled on the same node pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk1.xx pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk7.xx--> scheduled on the same node pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk7.xx--> scheduled on the same node pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk2.xx pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk1.xx pod-xxxxxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s ocpwrk7.xx--> scheduled on the same node ~~~
resolution: - Add label `topology.kubernetes.io/zone=""` to worker nodes using below command: ~~~ $oc label node topology.kubernetes.io/zone="" ~~~- https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/release_notes/ocp-4-7-release-notes.html#ocp-4-7-notable-technical-changes- Scaled down replica to zero and scaled up replica as per requirement(with having 4 worker node). Check whether pods scheduled to all the worker nodes (uniformed). ~~~ $oc scale deployment mydeployment--replicas=8 ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get pods-o wide NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE READINESS GATES mydeployment-xxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s woker0.xyz... mydeployment-xxxx 0/1 ContainerCreating 0 16s woker7.xyz ~~~
root_cause: - The default scheduler in OpenShift Container Platform 4.7 now uses `pod topology` spread constraints to control the placement of pods. Ensure that your nodes have the required labels in order for `pod replicas` to spread properly.- By default, the scheduler requires the `kubernetes.io/hostname` and `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` node labels. If nodes will not use these labels, define your own pod topology spread constraints instead of using the default constraints.- Please go through [Document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/release_notes/ocp-4-7-release-notes.html#ocp-4-7-notable-technical-changes).

title: oc edit fails when mounting a partition on /tmp with noexec option
issue: - `oc edit` fails with error: ~~~ $ oc edit error: open /tmp/oc-edit-1049179003.yaml: permission denied ~~~
resolution: `oc edit` use `vi` as its editor by default. Env variable `TMPDIR` can change the path of temporary file when running `oc edit` to another directory which mounted without `noexec` option. ~~~ # export TMPDIR=/test ~~~ Or as a workaround, we can extract the resource's yaml file and edit the file instead. ~~~ e.g. $ oc get po-o yaml > podname.yaml $ vim podname.yaml $ oc apply-f podname.yaml ~~~
root_cause: `oc edit` will create a temporary file in the `/tmp`, if mounted partition on `/tmp` with noexec, there is a permission issue.

title: Stuck messages in bridge queues
issue: We have AMQ installations on version 7.10.0 in OpenShift with two instances. We see in our test and production environment that messages flow normally over the bridge when necessary; so the bridge queues are usually empty. In our acceptance test environment however, we notice that we have accumulated messages on the bridge queue of the passive member. We currently have 1.33'' messages on the queue named '$.artemis.internal.sf.my-cluster.a6101f85-dab9-11e9-b218-0a580a8001b1'. Every time we restart the instance the number goes down a bit, but it does not continue go down when we just leave it running. The attributes of the cluster connections says that we have currently 1405207 in "Messages pending acknowledgement" and 78489 in "Messages acknowledged". The newest messages in the queue seems to be four days old (its a test environment so messages could come irregularly). What can be the reason for this? As I understand it messages should be passed to the active instance.

title: Draining node in OCP4 fails with unmount failure DeadlineExceeded.

title: Whereabouts CNI assigns IP's outside of the requested range on RHOCP 4
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this problem and [RHBZ#11067](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-11067) is opened to track this. To work around this problem, IP's from the allocatable pool must be made available either by expanding the range (in the `NetworkAttachmentDefinition`) or releasing addresses to the pool (removing pods).
root_cause: The mechanism to exclude ranges skips the entire range while looking for a suitable IP candidate. If the last address of an excluded range equals the last address of the requested allocation range an IP from the next subnet is allocated.

title: RHOAM Grafana Dashboard Clarifications
issue: - It is not clear what Grafana Dashboard is showing.- Is there a way to determine if API calls were rate limited in a specific time range?
resolution: Rate limiting is done per minute. So the [Grafana dashboard](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_api_management/1/guide/757a6ad2-8ca0-4150-b949-cbb1ee4e5969#_588cff28-ae64-4ff8-a89c-4fec1eeaaeb8) shows the requests per minute along with the quota that is based on the Subscription. The orange line is the quota. The line graph in green shows the requests per minute. If the line goes over the orange line (quota), then the requests have been rate limited. By default,the graph shows a 24 hour period. However, there is also a drop down menu that can be used to select a time range- e.g. Last 2 days, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days- or a time picker for a custom range. To see if a requests were rate limited in a time range other than last 24 hours, the drop down menu can be used to select a time range and see if the line goes over the orange quota.
root_cause: Grafana dasbboard documentation does not describe rate limiting over a custom time range.

title: How to Reduce Ceph Scrub Impact in OpenShift Data Foundations (ODF)
issue: - ODF which is backed by Red Hat Ceph Storage requires periodic scrubbing. Deep scrubs on a cluster can sometimes have a negative impact on the client's I/O. How can it be controlled?- Since object scrub is an essential part of the well-being of a Ceph cluster, is it possible to run it them during specified periods?- What are some of the methods available to reduce the impact of a deep-scrub in a Red Hat Ceph Storage cluster?
resolution: - Scrubbing is an operation synonymous with a filesystem check, done on the objects in Placement Groups, and is an important part of maintaining the data integrity within the Ceph cluster.- There are two types of scrubs, `Soft` scrub and `Deep` scrub.- A Soft scrub happens every day while a Deep scrub happens every week.- The scrub process generates a list of all objects in the PG being scrubbed, locks a chunk of objects (25 by default), and compares the copy on the primary OSD (in the acting set) with copy present on the replicas. The lock process prevents any I/O onto the corresponding object.- The `Soft` scrub checks the object size and its attributes, while the `Deep` scrub reads the data and validates the checksums to make sure the bits are indeed the same.- `Deep` scrubs are I/O intensive processes and may strain the client requests. **NOTE:** This process derives from the [Ceph: How to reduce scrub impact in a Red Hat Ceph Storage cluster](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1750243) solution. For more in-depth scrubbing configuration information, please review that solution, and apply the concepts shown in this solution to OpenShift (outlined below) to achieve additional desired settings. **SOLUTION:** 1. Capture the current OSD scrub times (beginning and ending). a. Begin Hour: ~~~ $ NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph tell osd.* config get osd_scrub_begin_hour--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring ~~~ b. End Hour: ~~~ $ NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph tell osd.* config get osd_scrub_end_hour--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring ~~~ 2. Set desired scrub time (begining and ending) utilizing a 24-hour format. **Example:**- 0- 12:00AM to 01:00AM- 1- 01:00AM to 02:00AM- 2- 02:00AM to 03:00AM.... and so on.. a. **Setting Begin Time to Midnight:** ~~~ $ NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph config set osd osd_scrub_begin_hour 0--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring ~~~ b. **Setting End Time to 6:00am:** ~~~ $ NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph config set osd osd_scrub_end_hour 6--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring ~~~
root_cause: ~~~ cluster: id: health: HEALTH_OK services: mon: 3 daemons, quorum e,h,i (age 19h) mgr: a(active, since 6w) mds: 1/1 daemons up, 1 hot standby osd: 33 osds: 33 up (since 17h), 33 in (since 17h) rgw: 1 daemon active (1 hosts, 1 zones) data: volumes: 1/1 healthy pools: 11 pools, 601 pgs objects: 7.11M objects, 12 TiB usage: 37 TiB used, 29 TiB / 66 TiB avail pgs: 600 active+clean 1 active+clean+scrubbing+deep <------------------- Deep Scrub io: client: 687 KiB/s rd, 55 MiB/s wr, 8 op/s rd, 647 op/s wr ~~~

title: HTTP endpoint returning error that project already exists
issue: - In a Dynatrace synthetic monitor- one HTTP request deletes an existing OSE project (if it exists); however, the subsequent request to create a new project with the same name fails with a 409 error `project already exists`.- Unable to create a synthetic monitor to monitor our API endpoints
resolution: - In order to introduce a delay in Dynatrace synthetic monitor to allow sufficient time for the project deletion to complete before creating a new project with the same name, use the following OpenShift endpoints: 1. `/healthz`: This endpoint can be used to check the health of the OpenShift cluster. It should respond quickly, but add a parameter to the URL to increase the delay, such as: ~~~ https:// /healthz?delay=15 ~~~ 2. `/api`: This endpoint provides a general API for OpenShift and should respond within a few seconds. Add a delay parameter to the URL, such as: ~~~ https:// /api?delay=15 ~~~- These endpoints should respond within a few seconds by default, but adding the "delay" parameter will force them to wait for the specified number of seconds before responding. **Note: Adding delays to synthetic monitor is not the best solution, and work with Dynatrace support to find a more effective solution.**
root_cause: - Request to create a new project is happening too soon after the request to delete a project.

ERROR ERROR with ovirt_disk_from_image.releaseimage[0], ERROR on main.tf line 16, in resource "ovirt_disk_from_image" "releaseimage": ERROR 16: resource "ovirt_disk_from_image" "releaseimage" {ERROR ERROR permanent_http_error: non-retryable error encountered while transferring ERROR image for disk ccd0e8d7-dfc8-4a66-8e91-2fe06f66b1c1 via HTTP request to ERROR https://test.com:54322/images/d3d0ff07-fcd8-493a-b50f-1b4dad03e6f6, ERROR giving up (permanent_http_error: unexpected client status code (416) received ERROR for image upload) ERROR ~~~
resolution: This issue was reported in the following [Bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-6486) and also cloned for 4.12.z [release](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-9923) During image upload terraform uses disk creation with size `17179869184` but `imageInitialSizeInBytes` size is set to 0 which cause RHV to use 1 GiB default in block-based storage ~~~ 2023-03-22 10:20:50,447+01 INFO [org.ovirt.engine.core.vdsbroker.irsbroker.CreateVolumeVDSCommand] (default task-4) [disk_create_nfTcG] START, CreateVolumeVDSCommand(CreateVolumeVDSCommandParameters:{storagePoolId='d8cd4722-1ce7-11ea-82e6-00163e6d65ed', ignoreFailoverLimit='false', storageDomainId='9b04d089-51ea-43f0-8138-a931052626b1', imageGroupId='cdee5899-b816-4999-858f-d701a6bb0681', imageSizeInBytes='17179869184', volumeFormat='COW', newImageId='3f577d63-9266-4d79-946c-b85be634a933', imageType='Sparse', newImageDescription='{"DiskAlias":"ocp-test-rhcos","DiskDescription":""}', imageInitialSizeInBytes='0', imageId='00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', sourceImageGroupId='00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', shouldAddBitmaps='false', legal='true', sequenceNumber='1', bitmap='null'}), log id: 276975ed ~~~ Image ticket ~~~ 2023-03-22 10:21:06,481+01 INFO [org.ovirt.engine.core.vdsbroker.vdsbroker.AddImageTicketVDSCommand] (default task-1) [image_upload_KvSiV] START, AddImageTicketVDSCommand(HostName = test.com, AddImageTicketVDSCommandParameters:{hostId='27ee2bcf-7bbc-4ebc-8101-dd9b92235d0f', ticketId='f52242e1-5514-4154-bdd0-51fd8cbf2f91', timeout='300', operations='[write]', size='2684354560', url='file:///rhev/data-center/mnt/blockSD/9b04d089-51ea-43f0-8138-a931052626b1/images/cdee5899-b816-4999-858f-d701a6bb0681/3f577d63-9266-4d79-946c-b85be634a933', filename='null', sparse='false', transferId='aae09d5f-c504-4588-88d7-c31a5e35af37', dirty='false'}), log id: 1733e8b3 ~~~ As a result, installation failed with REQUESTED_RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE code 416 ~~~ giving up (permanent_http_error: unexpected client status code (416) received ~~~ There is also possible to see the following error in the `ovirt-imageio` daemon log file ~~~ 2023-03-22 10:21:07,481 ERROR (Thread-95) [http] Client error: Requested range out of allowed range <-------------- ~~~ **As the fix for this issue was not released yet please follow the workaround bellow**- increase the `volume_utilization_chunk_mb` on **all RHV hosts** which will reflect the RHCOS disk size, start one by one Edit `/etc/vdsm/vdsm.conf` file and add the below configuration in all the hosts. ~~~ [irs] volume_utilization_chunk_mb=3072 ~~~- Disable the power management of the host and restart the vdsmd service to take the effect ~~~ systemctl restart vdsmd ~~~- Enable the power management back Once this configuration is added on all hosts try installation once again.
root_cause: The image uploads require an initial size and the engine defaults to 1Gib (2.5 GiB for 4.4 SP1) if not specified. This leads to a starting, but failing upload process when the image size is bigger than the default.

title: Setting Ulimits for files open in containers in RHOCP4: Configuring a Value higher than the default value
issue: - Unable to set a higher value than the default one for ulimits 'files open' in a container- ulimits 'files open' in containers is showing '1048576' even though the value is set higher in the crio service- Getting following error while setting nofile value to a higher value than the default, ~~~ setting rlimits for ready process caused: error setting rlimit type 7: operation not permitted ~~~
resolution: - Generate a encrypted string from required configuration for the sysctl 'fs.nr_open' parameter. Follow below command to do that. ~~~ #here the fs.nr_open limit is set to a value '267500000' which is higher than the default limit '1048576' $ cat < < EOF | base64-w0 fs.nr_open = 267500000 EOF ~~~- Below is the sample Machine Config file. Update the encrypted string obtained from above command in field.spec.config.storage.files[0].contents.source after base64, and save it to a file mc-sysctl.yaml. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: annotations: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: custom---> ## Kindly change this based on your requirement. Change this to name: 99-custom-sysctl-config ## the node label you need the Machine config to be applied upon spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,ZnMubnJfb3BlbiA9IDI2NzUwMDAwMAo= mode: 420 overwrite: true path: /etc/sysctl.d/99-sysctl.conf ~~~- Create machineConfig using file mc-sysctl.yaml. ~~~ #mc-sysctl.yaml will be applied only on custom labelled nodes. If you want apply it on any other nodes please update labels section with appropriate role. $ oc create-f mc.yaml ~~~- Once the above machine config is applied and nodes are ready, verify the node configurations as follows, ~~~ $ oc debug nodes/-- chroot /host cat /proc/sys/fs/nr_open ~~~- Generate another encrypted string from required configuration for the Crio runtime configurations. Follow below command to do that ~~~ $ cat < < EOF | base64-w0 [crio.runtime] default_ulimits = ["nofile=267500000:267500000",] EOF ~~~- Create a second machine config file, mc-crio.yaml for the application of the above encrypted data for Crio service ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: annotations: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: custom---> ## Kindly change this based on your requirement. Change this to name: 98-custom-container-runtime-crio ## the node label you applied in the machine config above spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,W2NyaW8ucnVudGltZV0KZGVmYXVsdF91bGltaXRzID0gWwoibm9maWxlPTI2NzUwMDAwMDoyNjc1MDAwMDAiLApdCg== mode: 420 overwrite: true path: /etc/crio/crio.conf.d/10-custom ~~~- Create machineConfig using file mc-crio.yaml. ~~~ #mc-sysctl.yaml will be applied only on custom labelled nodes. If you want apply it on any other nodes please update labels section with appropriate role,but keep in mind this would match the first machine config applied nodes. $ oc create-f mc-crio.yaml ~~~- Check for the MCP rollout and wait for the nodes to be in ready state. Please check the following output and confirm the data is populated, once the nodes are ready ~~~ $ oc debug nodes/-- chroot /host cat /etc/crio/crio.conf.d/10-custom $ oc debug node/-- chroot /host crio-status config | grep default_ulimits ~~~- Spin up a pod on the node and check the ulimits on the pod. ~~~ $ oc rsh $ ulimit-a $ ulimit-Hn $ ulimit-Sn ~~~
root_cause: - By default the value for /proc/sys/fs/nr_open is '1048576' and it servers as maximum upper limit for nofile, you could find more details in this [KCS article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3485471 "KCS").- Thus you need to increase the 'nr_open' limit before setting the 'nofile' to a higher value than the default.- There is a [KCS article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1479623 "KCS") which explains the maximum value that you could set for nr_open.

title: Infra nodes keep going in "Not Ready" state while using 99- -ssh-empty machine configs
issue: - After applying 99-master-ssh-empty and 99-worker-ssh-empty machine configs, one infra node goes into "Not Ready" state.
resolution: - Delete the MCs 99-worker-ssh-empty and 99-master-ssh-empty in order to recover the cluster.- Starting with RHOCP 4.12, if the cluster administrators want to block access to the cluster via SSH, it's enough to just delete the 99-worker-ssh and 99-master-ssh MCs. There is no need to use the xxx-empty MCs anymore.
root_cause: - The "user must have 1 or more sshKeys" constraint is not defined in the Ignition scheme, but defined and enforced by the MCD: ~~~ // verifyUserFields returns nil if the user Name = "core", if 1 or more SSHKeys exist for // this user and if all other fields in User are empty. // Otherwise, an error will be returned and the proposed config will not be reconcilable. // At this time we do not support non-"core" users or any changes to the "core" user // outside of SSHAuthorizedKeys. func verifyUserFields(pwdUser ign3types.PasswdUser) error {emptyUser:= ign3types.PasswdUser{} tempUser:= pwdUser if tempUser.Name == constants.CoreUserName && len(tempUser.SSHAuthorizedKeys) > = 1 {tempUser.Name = "" tempUser.SSHAuthorizedKeys = nil if!reflect.DeepEqual(emptyUser, tempUser) {return fmt.Errorf("ignition passwd user section contains unsupported changes: non-sshKey changes")} glog.Info("SSH Keys reconcilable")} else {return fmt.Errorf("ignition passwd user section contains unsupported changes: user must be core and have 1 or more sshKeys")} return nil} deleting ~~~- Creating MCs "99-master-ssh-empty" and "99-worker-ssh-empty" only works on older RHOCP versions. Now deleting the default machineconfigs "99-master-ssh" and "99-worker-ssh" is enough in order to delete any authorized ssh key from the nodes.

title: Discrepancies between OpenShift and CIS compliant settings
issue: - OCP default configurations differ from CIS Compliance Settings for Kubernetes, most specifically system file permissions.
resolution: - OpenShift CIS profiles exist and the best way to apply them is through the [Compliance Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/security/compliance_operator/compliance-operator-release-notes.html).- Manual hardening is not recommended because many system files are managed by operators, meaning changes will be reverted.
root_cause: Many CIS attributes' values on OpenShift are different from Kubernetes because the tests done on these technologies were different. It is expected for OpenShift to run on a Datacenter or other Enterprise hardware but Kubernetes is expected to run on anything.

title: Why does "/proc/swaps" show -2 as default priority when man page of swapon says -1 as default?
issue: - Why does "/proc/swaps" show-2 as default priority when man page of swapon says-1 as default? ~~~ Snippet from man page-p,--priority priority Specify the priority of the swap device. priority is a value between-1 and 32767. Higher numbers indicate higher priority. See swapon(2) for a full description of swap priorities. Add pri=value to the option field of /etc/fstab for use with swapon-a. When no priority is defined, it defaults to-1. < < <---- # cat /proc/swaps Filename Type Size Used Priority /dev/dm-1 partition 1470460 21416-2 ~~~
resolution: - This is expected behavior. By default first swap area gets priority with-2 and then-3 for next area and so on, unless anyone specifies the priority with `swapon` commandwithin the range of 0 to 32767.
root_cause: - Below is snippet from `swapon(2)` man page ~~~ Priority Each swap area has a priority, either high or low. The default priority is low. Within the low-priority areas, newer areas are even lower priority than older areas. All priorities set with swapflags are high-priority, higher than default. They may have any nonnegative value chosen by the caller. Higher numbers mean higher priority. Swap pages are allocated from areas in priority order, highest priority first. For areas with different priorities, a higher-priority area is exhausted before using a lower-priority area. If two or more areas have the same priority, and it is the highest priority available, pages are allocated on a round-robin basis between them. ~~~- Below is explanation from source code for default value of-2 for first swap area ~~~ mm/swapfile.c 63 static int least_priority =-1; < < <---- 3205 SYSCALL_DEFINE2(swapon, const char__user *, specialfile, int, swap_flags) 3206 {3207 struct swap_info_struct *p; 3208 struct filename *name; 3209 struct file *swap_file = NULL; 3210 struct address_space *mapping; 3211 int prio; 3212 int error;.... 3406 mutex_lock(&swapon_mutex); 3407 prio =-1; < < < < <------- initially the prio is set with "-1" 3408 if (swap_flags & SWAP_FLAG_PREFER) 3409 prio = 3410 (swap_flags & SWAP_FLAG_PRIO_MASK) > > SWAP_FLAG_PRIO_SHIFT; 3411 enable_swap_info(p, prio, swap_map, cluster_info, frontswap_map); 3412 3413 pr_info("Adding %uk swap on %s. Priority:%d extents:%d across:%lluk %s%s%s%s%s\n", 3414 p-> pages < <(PAGE_SHIFT-10), name-> name, p-> prio, 2570 static void enable_swap_info(struct swap_info_struct *p, int prio, 2571 unsigned char *swap_map, 2572 struct swap_cluster_info *cluster_info, 2573 unsigned long *frontswap_map) 2574 {2575 frontswap_init(p-> type, frontswap_map); 2576 spin_lock(&swap_lock); 2577 spin_lock(&p-> lock); 2578 setup_swap_info(p, prio, swap_map, cluster_info); < < <----- 2579 spin_unlock(&p-> lock);.... 2591} 2520 static void setup_swap_info(struct swap_info_struct *p, int prio, 2521 unsigned char *swap_map, 2522 struct swap_cluster_info *cluster_info) 2523 {2524 int i; 2525 2526 if (prio > = 0) < < <---- condition not satisfied 2527 p-> prio = prio; 2528 else 2529 p-> prio =--least_priority; < < <----- then p-> prio--(-1) =-2 2530 /* 2531 * the plist prio is negated because plist ordering is 2532 * low-to-high, while swap ordering is high-to-low 2533 */ 2534 p-> list.prio =-p-> prio; 2535 for_each_node(i) {2536 if (p-> prio > = 0) 2537 p-> avail_lists[i].prio =-p-> prio; 2538 else {2539 if (swap_node(p) == i) 2540 p-> avail_lists[i].prio = 1; 2541 else 2542 p-> avail_lists[i].prio =-p-> prio; 2543} 2544} 2545 p-> swap_map = swap_map; 2546 p-> cluster_info = cluster_info; 2547} ~~~- Following upstream commit has more explanation ~~~ swap: choose swap device according to numa node https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/a2468cc9bfdff6139f59ca896671e5819ff5f94a mm: fix ever-decreasing swap priority https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/78ecba081224a2db5876b6b81cfed0b78f58adc7 ~~~- But anyhow, only 32 swap areas can be created on any system, hence default priority will go towards negative number-2 to-28 and user defined priority will be from positive 0 to 32767.

title: Failed to pull image. Unauthorized to access repository.
issue: - Download the global cluster pull secret and add a new pull secret: ~~~ $ oc get secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config \--template='{{index.data ".dockerconfigjson" | base64decode}}' > $ oc registry login--registry=" " \--auth-basic=": " \--to= ~~~- Or update the global pull secret: ~~~ $ oc set data secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--from-file=.dockerconfigjson= ~~~- The following error message occurs: ~~~ Pulling image Failed to pull image: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error reading manifest latest in: unauthorized: unauthorized to access repository:, action: pull: unauthorized to access repository:, action: pull ~~~

title: potentially insufficient UIDs or GIDs available in user namespace
issue: An attempt to pull a apicurio registry image results in the following error: ~~~ Error: copying system image from manifest list: writing blob: adding layer with blob sha256:6909c107c8f93657491013e3ac95bbf54e399c75d13bf4e7994ce3565dfa82fb": ApplyLayer stdout: stderr: potentially insufficient UIDs or GIDs available in user namespace (requested 1000620000:0 for /deployments/apicurio-registry-storage-kafkasql-2.3.3.Final-redhat-00001-runner.jar): Check /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid if configured locally and run podman-system-migrate: lchown /deployments/apicurio-registry-storage-kafkasql-2.3.3.Final-redhat-00001-runner.jar: invalid argument exit status 1 ~~~
resolution: The USER instruction in a Dockerfile does not affect the ownership of the files added using ADD or COPY. As a result, the artifact added using the ADD instruction will have the ownership of the machine user where the docker build command was executed. In this particular case, the user had an extremely high UID of 1000620000, outside the range defined in /etc/subuid file.
root_cause: This is a bug [IPT-885](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/IPT-885)

title: prometheus pod failed to start  always terminate state
issue: - `prometheus-k8s-0` pod starts normally, but `prometheus-k8s-1` pod cannot start, and remains in `Terminating` status.- The same issue happens with pod `alertmanager-main-2`
resolution: * Check whether a custom prometheus instance has been deployed. If so, stop it, and then the Prometheus and Alertmanager pods will start correctly.
root_cause: The respective `prometheus-operator` pods in namespaces `openshift-monitoring` and `openshift-user-workload-monitoring` must have no influence on each other because they are in different projects. The scope of `prometheus-operator` `Deployment` is only in the current project, and other operators are similar. ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-monitoring get deploy prometheus-operator-oyaml....---prometheus-instance-namespaces=openshift-monitoring---thanos-ruler-instance-namespaces=openshift-monitoring---alertmanager-instance-namespaces=openshift-monitoring $ oc-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring get deploy prometheus-operator-oyaml...---prometheus-instance-namespaces=openshift-user-workload-monitoring---alertmanager-instance-namespaces=openshift-user-workload-monitoring---thanos-ruler-instance-namespaces=openshift-user-workload-monitoring ~~~ `prometheus-operator` controls Prometheus and Alertmanager, even without the above configuration, it will not affect each other. So the guess is that because of the `prometheus-operator` installed by the customer, these parameters may point to `openshift-monitoring`.

title: How to check recent IcM incidents for an ARO cluster
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - I have a cluster that is already "in trouble" or potentially "unsupported"- I am unable to verify the state of my ARO cluster- How do I collect IcM data?
resolution: 1. Click on Incident- Queries from the IcM home page 2. Create Query and in the Editor tab, enter **"ResourceID"** (not case sensitive here but you cannot use *Azure Red Hat OpenShift/ResourceID* directly, which is not ideal) 3. Scroll down to *Azure Red Hat OpenShift* option and select the "Azure Red Hat OpenShift/ResourceID" 4. You can leave the Operator as *==* by default, and put the Value as the *$ResourceURI* eg. **/subscriptions/xxxxx/resourceGroups/xxx/providers/Microsoft.RedHatOpenShift/OpenShiftClusters/xxx** 5. Click the **Run** icon image and you should be able to see all recent IcM tickets for this cluster if any.

issue: - Too many PODs create issues in `openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager` namespace.- Under `openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager` namespace a high number of PODs got created and stuck in a pending state. This is also causing the application pods deployed to be stuck in a pending state.- `OutOfpods` status and PODs quota limits exceeded in SNO (Single Node OpenShift).
resolution: **Red Hat** investigated this issue in bug report [2079082](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2079082) and **delivered a fix in following RHOCP versions**:- **4.9.32** through Errata [RHBA-2022:1694](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:1694).- **4.10.11** through Errata [RHBA-2022:1431](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:1431).- **4.11** already contains the committed fix in all of their images. If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. ************************** To temporarily free up the nodes from the_Pending_ and/or_ContainerCreating_ PODs is possible to delete the jobs in the `openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager` namespace, use the following command to *delete it all*: ~~~ $ oc delete jobs--all-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager ~~~
root_cause: The `collect-profiles` job should only take a few seconds to run. There are instances, such as when the pod cannot be scheduled, where the job will not complete in a reasonable amount of time. If multiple jobs are scheduled but unable to run, the number of scheduled jobs can exceed pod quota limits.

title: In Quay Geo-Replication, Storage Buckets not synced
issue: - Why do s3 buckets differ in size and number of objects?- How to figure out what is the delta between them?
root_cause: Over a period of time images in Quay registry are deleted. But within quay there is `no mechanism` as of now to make sure that an image deleted at some point in time is `100% removed` from the backing storage. Due to this, it is likely that many layers of such images are lying in the backing storage and causing inconsistencies in all backing stores data counts. `Replicationworkers` from the `backfill script` might take some time to catch up with latest tasks especially when images are constantly being pushed/new layers are being added to the registry. There is always a delay. A difference in the size of backing s3 storage is not worrysome. Unless it leads pulls failing due layer/s not being present in the table `imagestoragelocation` that the database expects it to be.

issue: - How to remove HTTP header "x-envoy-peer-metadata" for outbound connection?- How can we configure Service Mesh to not inject some HTTP header `x-envoy-peer-metadata` or limit its size?

An example config is: ~~~ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 kind: VirtualService metadata: name: direct-httpbin-through-egress-gateway spec: hosts:- myservice.example.com gateways:- istio-egressgateway- mesh http:- match:- gateways:- mesh port: 80 route:- destination: host: istio-egressgateway.istio-system.svc.cluster.local subset: httpbin port: number: 80 weight: 100- match:- gateways:- istio-egressgateway port: 80 route:- destination: host: myservice.example.com port: number: 80 weight: 100 headers: <---------------- the below 4 lines remove x-envoy-peer-metadata header from myservice.example.com request: remove:- x-envoy-peer-metadata ~~~- Test if the header is removed: ~~~ $ oc-n ossm-test rsh-c sleep $pod curl-sSL-D- myservice.example.com/get?show_env=true HTTP/1.1 200 OK server: envoy date: Tue, 25 Apr 2023 04:48:30 GMT content-type: application/json content-length: 874 access-control-allow-origin: * access-control-allow-credentials: true x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 65 {"args": {"show_env": "true"}, "headers": {"Accept": "*/*", "Content-Length": "0", "Host": "farnsworth.usersys.redhat.com", "User-Agent": "curl/7.88.1-DEV", "X-B3-Parentspanid": "9f4edd3eea0375b9", "X-B3-Sampled": "1", "X-B3-Spanid": "f8061891823bf94f", "X-B3-Traceid": "607da6a32b737de89f4edd3eea0375b9", "X-Envoy-Attempt-Count": "1", "X-Envoy-Decorator-Operation": "myservice.example.com:80/*", "X-Envoy-Internal": "true", "X-Envoy-Peer-Metadata-Id": "router~10.128.2.150~istio-egressgateway-557464f95c-xsdb9.istio-system~istio-system.svc.cluster.local", "X-Forwarded-For": "10.129.2.58", "X-Forwarded-Proto": "http", "X-Request-Id": "2c51248f-326a-939f-a73e-56739a1b9d5e"}, "origin": "10.129.2.58", "url": "http://myservice.example.com/get?show_env=true"} ~~~

title: How can I migrade 3scale 2.9 from OpenShift 3.11 to 3scale 2.13 and OpenShift 4.12?
issue: **NOTE: Please do not publish this article, it's for internal reference only!*

We are in the process of updating 3scale while migrating it from Openshift Cluster to another. Old cluster is running OS 3.11, new one is running OS 4.12. 3Scale version is to be update from 2.9.0 to 2.13.
resolution: **NOTE: Please do not publish this article, it's for internal reference only!** Unfortunately, there is no shortcut to the 3scale upgrade path (check this article: [Upgrading Red Hat 3scale API Management](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3638311)). It is not possible to skip any version in the upgrade path because the upgrade is done incrementally (check this article: [How to perform a 3scale update in a non-sequential major/minor version?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5064721)). Before upgrading to each version it is highly recommended to refer the supported configurations to keep the installation suitable to be covered by Red Hat support:- [3scale API Management 2.9](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5644621)- [3scale API Management 2.10](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6257141)- [3scale API Management 2.11](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6961867)- [3scale API Management 2.12](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6982425)- [3scale API Management 2.13](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2798521) Here is the steps to follow: 1. Do a full backup of your current 3scale installation ([3scale 2.9 documentation: 3scale backup and restore](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.9/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore)); 2. Upgrade to 3scale 2.10 ([3scale 2.10 documentation: 3scale template-based upgrade guide: from 2.9 to 2.10](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.10/html/migrating_3scale/upgrade-template)); 3. Do a full backup of your 3scale 2.10 installation ([3scale 2.10 documentation: 3scale backup and restore](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.10/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore)); 4. Upgrade to 3scale 2.11 ([3scale 2.11 documentation: Upgrading 3scale version 2.11.0 to version 2.11.1 using templates](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/migrating_3scale/upgrading-threescale-for-micro-release-using-templates)); 5. Do a full backup of your 3scale 2.11 installation ([3scale 2.11 documentation: 3scale backup and restore](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore)); 6. Upgrade to 3scale 2.12 ([3scale 2.12 documentation: Upgrading 3scale version 2.11 to version 2.12 using templates](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html/migrating_3scale/upgrade-template)) **Note**: 3scale 2.12 are not listed to be supported with OpenShift 3.11, but it is compatible. The usage of 3scale 2.12 into an OpenShift 3.11 is not supported by RedHat. 7. Do a full backup of your 3scale 2.12 installation ([3scale 2.12 documentation: 3scale backup and restore using templates](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates)); 8. Now it need to migrate the 3scale 2.12 from OpenShift 3.11 cluster to an OpenShift 4 cluster. The new cluster need to be one of the following versions: 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10 or 4.11. Install 3scale using operator based, because 3scale release 2.13 will only accept operator based installation. 9. Upgrade to 3scale 2.13 ([3scale 2.13 documentation: 3scale operator-based upgrade guide: from 2.12 to 2.13](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html/migrating_3scale/upgrade-operator)); 10. Do a full backup of your 3scale 2.13 installation ([3scale 2.13 documentation: 3scale backup and restore](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore)); 11. Upgrade your OpenShift to 4.12 Always open a Pro-Active case before doing maintenance. Check [how to submit a Proactive Case [Primary Article]](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5387111).
root_cause: **NOTE: Please do not publish this article, it's for internal reference only!** 3scale does not support the upgrade jumping from one version to another without upgrading to each major version in the path.

title: REST API healthy cache fails and cache/Data Grid cluster goes degraded
issue: Probe accessing REST API from Cluster returns DEGRADED instead of HEALTHY.
resolution: The creation of an invalid cache configuration- for example with Cross-Site when there is no Cross-site on the DG cluster (Infinispan CR) might not be stopped so after the creation the cache goes on degraded mode, and therefore the cluster goes on degraded mode. To track this, verify the `configlistener` pod- aka tattletale pod- to see the cache created and its configurations. When you do the REST API health check the status was returning as **DEGRADED**- instead of status **HEALTHY** or **HEALTHY_REBALANCING**- so the probe was failing. The chain of events: a- create an invalid cache b- the cache is created c- since it is invalid- no Cross-site- the other site is not connected d- cache goes degraded e- site goes degraded f- health validation returns **DEGRADED**
root_cause: The creation of an invalid cache, leads to a cache degraded and then a cluster degraded. For alternatives for unsetting Degraded mode, see the solution [Alternatives for unsetting DG 8 cluster from degraded mode](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6968860). REST API health request can return the following results: Status | Purpose--------- |--------- HEALTHY | all caches instances are working properly DEGRADED | One or more caches is in degraded mode. HEALTHY_REBALANCING | One or more caches is rebalancing FAILED | failed to start
