title: console-login-helper-messages-issuegen.path: Failed with result 'unit-condition-failed'
issue: - After trying to login to OCP nodes via ssh, the below message is printed on console: ~~~ Failed Units: 1 console-login-helper-messages-issuegen.path ~~~
resolution: - This issue is known to Red Hat and has been fixed. The bug has been fixed in OCP 4.10.26 update, please upgrade the affected clusters. https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2109546
root_cause: - The console-login-helper-messages-issuegen.service has these conditions to trigger ~~~ ConditionPathExistsGlob=|/run/console-login-helper-messages/issue.d/*.issue ConditionPathExistsGlob=|/etc/console-login-helper-messages/issue.d/*.issue ~~~- If there are no issues, then the condition gets propagated up to console-login-helper-messages-issuegen.path as failed. On my test system /etc/console-login-helper-messages/issue.d/*.issue is empty and /run/console-login-helper-messages/issue.d/*.issue has issues. There may be a race condition where the issues in /run/console-login-helper-messages/issue.d/*.issue have not populated yet and thus failing console-login-helper-messages-issuegen.path. console-login-helper-messages-issuegen.path doesn't restart automatically so it just remains failed.

title: Builds fail, integrated registry is not configured in OpenShift 4.x
issue: - All builds won't start- In OpenShift events, get an invalid output error: 31s Warning InvalidOutput Build Error starting build: an image stream cannot be used as build output because the integrated Docker registry is not configured- In the integrated container registry, we see these logs with a secret not found $ oc logs cluster-image-registry-operator-6d6b45bfdf-fl9mk I0221 14:32:30.227426 1 main.go:24] Cluster Image Registry Operator Version: v4.0.0-0.150.0.0-dirty I0221 14:32:30.228037 1 main.go:25] Go Version: go1.10.3 I0221 14:32:30.228046 1 main.go:26] Go OS/Arch: linux/amd64 I0221 14:32:30.278201 1 controller.go:371] waiting for informer caches to sync I0221 14:32:31.480835 1 controller.go:380] started events processor E0221 14:37:31.514363 1 controller.go:208] unable to sync: unable to apply objects: failed to create object *v1.Secret, Namespace=openshift-image-registry, Name=image-registry-private-configuration: unable to get cluster minted credentials "kube-system/installer-cloud-credentials": secrets "image-registry-private-configuration-user" not found, requeuing W0221 14:40:31.295881 1 reflector.go:272] k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:130: watch of *v1.ConfigMap ended with: too old resource version: 636035 (640932) W0221 14:42:12.289238 1 reflector.go:272] k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:130: watch of *v1.ConfigMap ended with: too old resource version: 636035 (641936) E0221 14:42:31.573087 1 controller.go:208] unable to sync: unable to apply objects: failed to create object *v1.Secret, Namespace=openshift-image-registry, Name=image-registry-private-configuration: unable to get cluster minted credentials "kube-system/installer-cloud-credentials": secrets "image-registry-private-configuration-user" not found, requeuing
resolution: - Create a YAML file for the Registry secret: $ export ACCESSKEY= < Your AWS Access Key> $ export SECRETKEY= $ oc create secret generic image-registry-private-configuration-user-n openshift-image-registry--from-literal=REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_ACCESSKEY=${ACCESSKEY}--from-literal=REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_SECRETKEY=${SECRETKEY}- Finally, the Registry CR may be missing the AWS region that it needs to connect to. Replace the below with your applicable AWS region. $ oc patch config instance-n openshift-image-registry--type merge--patch '{"spec": {"storage": {"s3": {"region":"us-east-1"}}}}'

title: Has 3scale been audited or pentested?
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? Hi, we are currently deploying 3scale on production environments. We will have some applications from third party vendors calling our APIs through the 3scale API gateway. Before everything goes live, we would like to know if 3scale has been audited from a security point of view. The APIcast gateways are the components that are the most exposed. Have they been pentested? My current setup is: 3scale 2.13 installed with the 3scale operator on OpenShift 4.10. Thank you, Mohammed What is the business impact? Please also provide timeframe information. potential business impact if no security audit or pentest has been performed for 3scale Where are you experiencing the behavior? What environment? all environments When does the behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times? Repeatedly Hi Gustavo, thank you for your answer. Do you have any information to share regarding the security hardening of the Nginx servers embedded in the APIcasts? Regards, Mohammed
resolution: Hi Mohammed, I've checked this subject and we don't have an official document that we can share externally, but got the following from our internal 3scale Security and Privacy FAQ that perhaps may clear your doubts:- Do you use automated software security testing tools, or do you do third party testing? > Yes, open source and commercial tools are used, as well as professional scanning services. > > Furthermore 3scale runtimes are based on container images which are available in the Red Hat Container Catalog (RHCC) [1]. Containers in RHCC are scanned for security vulnerabilities. This along with other container related security issues are described in more detail in the section "Understanding Containers Security issues" in RHCC Faq [2]. Containers in Red Hat Container Catalog are rated for security risks using a Container Health Index described in detail in [3] that assigns letter grades- "A" through "F". "A" is more up-to-date than "F". > > [1] https://access.redhat.com/containers [2] RHCC Faq: https://access.redhat.com/containers/#/faq [3] Container Health Index: https://access.redhat.com/articles/2803031- Are third party penetration and application security testing results available? > No, these are not made available to customers. However, customers are free to carry out their own scans. Find below some articles that might be helpful for you:- [Security Contacts and Procedures](https://access.redhat.com/security/team/contact)- [Tutorial on how to process vulnerability scans](https://access.redhat.com/articles/red_hat_vulnerability_tutorial) Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira Hi Mohammed, No we don't have any centralized documentation to share. But we do have several policies that enforces security on APIcast [1]. In addition, APIcast pods are built using RHEL8 as base image that which also has system-wide cryptographic policies [2]. [1] [Chapter 4. APIcast policies](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html-single/administering_the_api_gateway/index#apicast-policies) [2] [Chapter 4. Using system-wide cryptographic policies](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/security_hardening/using-the-system-wide-cryptographic-policies_security-hardening#doc-wrapper) Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: Reverting the commit for a deployed application using GitOps in CLI
issue: - How to use specific commits for applications using CLI- How to revert the commit to previous revisions using CLI
resolution: 'Application' object can be adjusted to set the targetRevision(commit). ~~~ $ oc get application-o yaml apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: Application metadata: name: gitops-test namespace: openshift-gitops.. spec: destination: namespace: gitops-test server: https://kubernetes.default.svc project: default source: path: app repoURL: https://gitlab.com/medolika/gitops-test.git targetRevision: HEAD # <============ syncPolicy: automated: {}.. $ git log commit 6318e1176c8b77de75d165a75dbfc7aa57572fa6 (HEAD-> main, origin/main) Author: Author Date: Tue Apr 18 13:36:17 2023 +0900 replicase changed commit ccb954c5e120a6c671bbb9a80fe8e88e02e53cec # <=== Target commit Author: Author Date: Tue Apr 18 12:59:53 2023 +0900 The first commit based on... ~~~ Patch 'spec.source.targetRevision' to a previous commit ~~~ $ oc patch application gitops-test--type='json'-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/source/targetRevision", "value":"ccb954c5e120a6c671bbb9a80fe8e88e02e53cec"}]'-n openshift-gitops ~~~ **Note that** at the time of writing this article, [Argo CD CLI](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/cicd/gitops/argo-cd-custom-resource-properties.html#command-line-tool_argo-cd-custom-resource-properties) tool is not supported and the recommended way to work with GitOps is using the web console.

title: Openshift Compliance result server pods stuck in ContainerCreating status
issue: - Scanning nodes for `CIS` compliance.- After creating a `ScanSettingBinding`, the result server pods are stuck in `ContainterCreating` status.- Result server pods are unable to mount volume
resolution: - Schedule the compliance results pods to run on worker nodes.- Create a `ScanSetting` CustomResource that specifies a `nodeSelector` for worker nodes in the `rawResultStorage` section:- Create a `.yaml` file with the custom `ScanSetting` definition: ~~~ apiVersion: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: ScanSetting metadata: name: namespace: openshift-compliance rawResultStorage: nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: "" <=== Specify nodeSelector for worker nodes pvAccessModes:- ReadWriteOnce rotation: 3 size: 1Gi tolerations:- operator: Exists roles:- worker- master scanTolerations:- operator: Exists schedule: 0 1 * * * ~~~- Create the custom `ScanSetting`: ~~~ $ oc create-f.yaml ~~~- Create a `ScanSettingBinding` that references your newly create `ScanSetting`: ~~~ apiVersion: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: ScanSettingBinding metadata: name: cis-compliance namespace: openshift-compliance profiles:- name: ocp4-cis-node kind: Profile apiGroup: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1- name: ocp4-cis kind: Profile apiGroup: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1 settingsRef: name: <=== Name of ScanSetting you created above kind: ScanSetting apiGroup: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1 ~~~- Check result server pods are now running on worker nodes: ~~~ $ oc get pods-o wide-n openshift-compliance | grep-i rs ocp4-cis-node-master-rs-6d4d5f8689-qr5qm 1/1 Running 0 31s 10.11.0.64 worker02 ocp4-cis-node-worker-rs-8f6ff6c89-2d9zc 1/1 Running 0 33s 10.8.2.29 worker03 ocp4-cis-rs-5dc9d74477-wz227 1/1 Running 0 2m10s 10.11.0.63 worker02 ~~~
root_cause: - The result server pods are scheduled on master nodes, and are trying to mount a vloume provisioned by the `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storage class- The `ODF` `csi-plugin` pods aren't running on the master nodes: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage-o wide | grep-i plugin csi-cephfsplugin-9gdvn 3/3 Running 0 69m 192.168.50.14 worker02 csi-cephfsplugin-nfbtr 3/3 Running 0 69m 192.168.50.15 worker03 csi-cephfsplugin-provisioner-7bf74694d-7z4k5 6/6 Running 0 69m 10.11.0.21 worker02 csi-cephfsplugin-provisioner-7bf74694d-vjssg 6/6 Running 1 69m 10.9.2.29 worker01 csi-cephfsplugin-vk4km 3/3 Running 0 69m 192.168.50.13 worker01 csi-rbdplugin-provisioner-7d4d6d4945-hsgfd 6/6 Running 0 69m 10.8.2.18 worker03 csi-rbdplugin-provisioner-7d4d6d4945-vrcfv 6/6 Running 2 69m 10.11.0.20 worker02 csi-rbdplugin-s6fn8 3/3 Running 0 69m 192.168.50.13 worker01 csi-rbdplugin-wmmv8 3/3 Running 0 69m 192.168.50.14 worker02 csi-rbdplugin-zblms 3/3 Running 0 69m 192.168.50.15 worker03 ~~~

title: 504 Gateway Timeout error in Kibana
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - How to resolve **504 Gateway Timeout*
error observed while accessing Kibana?- How to change the **timeout*
value of Kibana to get a response from Elasticsearch in OpenShift cluster?
resolution: Try **increasing the timeout value** between Kibana and Elasticsearch. You can change the timeout value of Kibana to get a response from Elasticsearch in OpenShift cluster by editing the Kibana deployment. Here are the steps you need to follow to update the timeout value of Kibana: 1. Log in to your OpenShift cluster from the command line using **"oc login"**. 2. Switch to the project or namespace where Kibana is deployed using the command **"oc project {project name}"**. 3. Get the name of the Kibana deployment by running the following command: **"oc get deployments"**. 4. Edit the Kibana deployment using the command: ~~~ oc edit deployment ~~~ 5. In the deployment manifest, find the **spec.containers** section for Kibana. Under this section, you will see a--elasticsearch.hosts parameter set to the URL of your Elasticsearch cluster. You need to add a **--elasticsearch.requestTimeout** parameter to this section as well, like this: ~~~ name: kibana image: docker.elastic.co/kibana/kibana:7.13.2 command:- /usr/local/bin/kibana-docker args:---elasticsearch.hosts=http://elasticsearch:9200---elasticsearch.requestTimeout=300000 <----------- ~~~ The **--elasticsearch.requestTimeout** parameter value is in **milliseconds**, and the above example sets it to **5 minutes** (300000 milliseconds). You can adjust this value as per your requirements. 6. Save the changes to the deployment manifest and exit the editor. 7. Check the status of the Kibana deployment to make sure the changes were applied correctly: ~~~ oc rollout status deployment/ ~~~ By following the above steps, you should be able to edit the timeout value of the Kibana deployment to get a response from Elasticsearch in the OpenShift cluster. If you need help from Red Hat, please open a support case with us by clicking [here](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true).
root_cause: The 504 Gateway Timeout error in Kibana typically means that Kibana was unable to receive a response from Elasticsearch within the configured timeout period. In most cases, increasing the timeout value between Kibana and Elasticsearch should resolve this issue.

title: No ARP reply in case of HAproxy vIP and EgressIP assigned to the same INFRA node
issue: - In a scenario where the HAproxy `Ingress vIP` (floating IP address associated to the OpenShift Application Domain) is assigned to the same INFRA node where also the `EgressIP`of the `openshift-gitops (ArgoCD)` is allocated, any ARP request for the `EgressIP` address (ARP request sent from the node that is hosting the HAproxy `Ingress vIP`) won't be answered at all.- As result of the behaviour above described, the authentication in openshift-gitops (ArgoCD integrated with OpenShift) will systematically fail because from the INFRA node isn't possible to resolve the EgressIP.
resolution: - The right ARP workflow is observed only if the HAproxy `Ingress vIP` is managed by three different nodes from the ones labelled as `egress-assignable`. ~~~ # oc get nodes # oc label node k8s.ovn.org/egress-assignable="" ~~~- This means that the `EgressIPs` have to be assigned to a set of nodes different from the INFRA nodes used for handle the HAproxy `Ingress vIP`.- The Red Hat engineering team is working on this issue with the target to fix it in a minor release greater than Red Hat OpenShift 4.12.
root_cause: - The behavior described in this solution is tracked in the JIRA [OCPBUGS-11180](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-11180).- At the writing time of this solution, there isn't any root cause analysis shared by the Red Hat engineering team.

title: Why CSR keep generating frequently
issue: - We have noticed that CSR generates quite a few times.
resolution: - Node certificates in OpenShift have 30 days [hardcoded](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-kube-controller-manager-operator/blob/release-4.5/bindata/v4.1.0/config/defaultconfig.yaml#L30) expiry. This means that approximately every 30 days a new CSR will be generated for new certificates that will last for one more month.- If the cluster is IPI (and for nodes created via machinesets on UPI clusters with cloud integration), the CSRs are approved automatically, so it is transparent for the user.- In the rest of the clusters, users are responsible of monitoring for new CSRs and approving. User can [create a cronJob](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6270481) for autoapproval

title: Unable to open Red Hat Gitops dashboard in RHOCP 4
issue: - Unable to open `Red Hat Gitops` dashboard due to below error: ~~~ Failed to query provider https://gitops.apps.cluster.example.com/api/dex: oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider, expected https://gitops.apps.cluster.example.com/api/dex got https://openshift-gitops-server-openshift-gitops.cluster.example2.com/api/dex ~~~
resolution: - Modify correct `dex.config` inside the `argocd` `CustomResource` using below command to fix the issue. ~~~ $ oc edit argocd-n openshift-gitops sso: dex: config: | connectors:- config:................ issuer: https://kubernetes.default.svc redirectURI: https://gitops.apps.cluster.example.com/api/dex/callback < <--------- id: openshift ~~~
root_cause: - Wrong `redirectURI` has been configured in `argocd-cm` `configmap`.

title: DG 8.5 Transcoder to convert serialized Java objects to JSON for console display
resolution: In DG 8.5 it was introduced a transcode Java objects without the need to 'deploy' the related Java class to the server this issue is considered as resolved, which is implemented on [ISPN-14765- Java serialization to JSON transcoder](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ISPN-14765).
root_cause: DG 7's console was not able to show data. The cache might contain any data and the console or CLI can not handle it. For java serialization you need i.e. the Java class available at server side and run into CNF if its not there- which is a huge performance impact for the console if every entry produce an Exception. However, [ISPN-14765- Java serialization to JSON transcoder](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ISPN-14765) implements a Java serialization to JSON transcoder- which was implemented give the Java serialization format is well-known, it is possible to interpret the serialized bytes into a JSON representation. This allows showing serialized objects from the Console/CLI/REST API.

title: Can we remove "openshift-debug-xxxxx" parent projects created by a node debug session?
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? I have a support question. The OpenShift cluster is running for a couple of years. Currently we are in a clean-up process to remove abandoned projects to keep the system lean and mean. We made an inventory of all projects on the cluster and discovered up to 24 debug projects: openshift-debug-node-4z8vj openshift-debug-node-5fhd4 openshift-debug-node-5t4ml openshift-debug-node-7dchj openshift-debug-node-8wpn5 openshift-debug-node-cc84w openshift-debug-node-cdc5m openshift-debug-node-d87sg openshift-debug-node-dhz4j openshift-debug-node-dpr2r openshift-debug-node-fxlkx openshift-debug-node-hbqkx openshift-debug-node-hcwgz openshift-debug-node-hsgs5 openshift-debug-node-m298p openshift-debug-node-mkcqp openshift-debug-node-n7c59 openshift-debug-node-qff2z openshift-debug-node-rnqth openshift-debug-node-s4qff openshift-debug-node-trbds openshift-debug-node-v6kqk openshift-debug-node-vntmz openshift-debug-node-xpgsf Question:

Are those projects related to debug sessions that we should be able to remove without issues? Is there any reason not to remove those Debug projects? Thanks in advance. What is the business impact? Please also provide timeframe information. No business impact, just proactive maintenance Hi Gustavo, Thank you for your reply. I see that the actual debug pods are deleted after the session is finished. My question is related to the parent project of the debug pod. I see many parent projects with no resources that are still in the cluster. Could it be that in this particular version the parent project of the debug pod is left behind. Thanks for your response. Ralph
resolution: Hello, Thank you for contacting the Red Hat support. My name is Gustavo and I'll be working with you on this case. The openshift debug pods are supposed to be alive only during the debug session (`oc debug node/ `) once you finish the session it is supposed to be deleted. You're running an OCP version that reached its End of Life. It's strongly recommended that you upgrade your cluster to a supported version. Refer the [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Life Cycle Policy](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift#dates) for further information. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira Hello Ralph, In theory, these parent projects should also be deleted after closing the debug session. But you can manually delete them without any problems. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: When adding a repository in Openshift Gitops, I face a proxy error even if the repository is in noProxy at Cluster-Wide Proxy
issue: - My Red Hat Openshift Container Platform (RHOCP) cluster is using a [Cluster-Wide Proxy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/enable-cluster-wide-proxy.html) with `noProxy` values in place- I'm trying to setup a git repository connection to a private git server in Red Hat Openshift GitOps using its IP because I can't use its FQDN at the moment- The CIDR containing the IP is present in the `noProxy` configuration of Cluster-Wide Proxy- I'm facing Proxy errors from the `git` client within the Openshift GitOps console, like `git` is trying to use Proxy to get to my git repository ~~~ Error: unable to access 'https:// / /.git': Received HTTP code XXX from proxy [...] after CONNECT` ~~~
resolution: - Add your git's private repository IP to the `noProxy` variable in your Cluster-Wide proxy configuration by editing this: ~~~ $ oc edit proxy/cluster-n openshift-config.cluster.local,.svc,127.0.0.1,example.com,localhost,10.12.50.0/24,10.12.50.14 <-- add the git's private repository IP here ~~~- Do not remove the already present CIDR, as other software may be using that, and the modification might introduce new issues
root_cause: - Use of CIDRs in combination with `git` and/or Openshift GitOps is not supported when used in the `noProxy` variable in Cluster-Wide Proxy- This is because `git` software uses `libcurl` for accessing HTTP resources, and `libcurl` doesn't support CIDRs when using the `NO_PROXY` environment variable- The issue is already highlighted by [cURL to NO_PROXY CIDR addresses are not working as expected](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5356961)- Please also have a look at [What values are defined in the 'noProxy' section under proxy configuration in OpenShift Container Platform 4.](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6618081)

title: Error "no route to host" found when trying to connect to an application exposed using external ip service.
issue: - When trying to connect to an application exposed using an external ip service it doesn't work.- Tests performed using curl fail with the error "no route to host" either from the same subnet or from a different subnet.- Accessing the application using the internal cluster service works correctly.
resolution: - The administrator is responsible for the configuration in the networking equipment to route the traffic correctly to Openshift nodes. This is explained also in Kubernetes [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#external-ips). Some ways to route the traffic are for example creating static arp entries in the layer3 equipment or layer2 host where the connection is being initiated pointing to the mac address of one of the Openshift nodes. Another solution is to use the [MetalLb operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/metallb/about-metallb.html) to expose services using external ips.- Adding a static arp entry in the origin host will fix the issue: ~~~ [root@bastion ~]# oc get service NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE test-external-ip LoadBalancer 172.30.167.225 192.168.1.249,192.168.1.249 8080:32545/TCP 23h [root@bastion ~]# arp-s 192.168.1.249 aa:aa:aa:01:01:01 (worker mac address). [root@bastion ~]# curl http://192.168.1.249:8080 Hello world! ~~~
root_cause: The external ip service feature only prepare the nodes to serve connections that are directed to the external ip but it doesn't actually configure the ip address in the nodes.

title: Using Simple Content Access (SCA) in a disconnected OpenShift environment
issue: - When the OpenShift is running in a disconnected environment the cluster and it's operators do not have access to Red Hat's Hybrid Cloud Console which is needed by the Insights Operator to pull entitlements from.- Therefore we want to mimic this particular part of the Insight Operator process in order for the cluster to supply the entitlements during builds.
resolution: - To run entitled builds within a single namespace, copy the entitlement keys (/etc/pki/entitlement/\*-key.pem and /etc/pki/entitlement/\*.pem) from a RHEL subscribed physical or virtual machine to a build secret following the instructions in this article: [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/cicd/builds/running-entitled-builds.html#builds-source-secrets-entitlements_running-entitled-builds](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/cicd/builds/running-entitled-builds.html#builds-source-secrets-entitlements_running-entitled-builds)- To entitle cluster wide builds using SharedSecret objects copy the files mentioned above from a subscribed RHEL host and follow the instructions described here: [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/cicd/builds/running-entitled-builds.html#builds-running-entitled-builds-with-sharedsecret-objects_running-entitled-builds](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/cicd/builds/running-entitled-builds.html#builds-running-entitled-builds-with-sharedsecret-objects_running-entitled-builds) Keep in mind that, as of this writing, the Shared Resources CSI Driver and The Build CSI Volumes used in the cluster wide resolution are both **Technology Preview** features! More information regarding **Technology Preview** features can be found in the following article: [https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview)

title: Metric for 'apiserver_request_total' does not record 403 and 401 responses
issue: - The Prometheus metric for `apiserver_request_total` does not record 403 and 401 responses
root_cause: This problem is documented in the following upstream [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86063) and can be summarized as follows: ~~~ currently authn is working as a filter handler which is executed before the individual implementation of the resource APIs. however, the apiserver_request_total metric is recorded after the execution of those filter handlers. that makes us never record any of the 401 Unauthorized bits. ~~~

title: OCP 4.13 vSphere IPI deployment fails with an error 'invalid install config: platform.vsphere.failureDomains.topology.datastore'
issue: - The OCP 4.13 vSphere IPI deployment fails with the below error: ~~~ FATAL failed to fetch Install Config: failed to generate asset "Install Config": invalid install config: platform.vsphere.failureDomains.topology.datastore: Invalid value: "OCP-PNQ-Datastore": full path of datastore must be provided in format / ~~~
resolution: - Make sure the vSphere user has access to at least two available datastores in the datacenter.

title: Creating a new VM with same name of old terminating VMI associates the VM with the incorrect VMI and virt-launcher pod
issue: After deleting virtual machine, a new virtual machine with same name connects to the old pod
Can't create VMs with the same name reliably.
resolution: * Please upgrade to OpenShift Virtualization 4.13 or later. * As a workaround in older versions: before creating a new VM with the same name as a recently deleted one, ensure the VMI and the virt-launcher pod have been deleted.
root_cause: * A new VM gets associated with an old VMI if it still exists and both VMs have the same name. * This is possible if the old VM is taking some time to shutdown. * This was a bug, tracked in [Bugzilla 2132873- VM is removed before virt-launcher pod exits, new VM with same name points to old VMI/virt-launcher pod still terminating](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2132873).

title: Some usbguard compliance rules are failing even applied remediation
issue: Enabled remediation for findings but scan results for following usbguard compliance rules shows still failing. Why remediation did not work? ~~~ # oc get ComplianceCheckResult |grep-i usbguard rhcos4-moderate-worker-configure-usbguard-auditbackend FAIL low rhcos4-moderate-worker-package-usbguard-installed PASS medium rhcos4-moderate-worker-service-usbguard-enabled FAIL medium rhcos4-moderate-worker-usbguard-allow-hid-and-hub FAIL medium ~~~
resolution: * After initial compliance scanning `configure-usbguard-auditbackend` rule is now created: ~~~ [root@skbastion deploy2]# oc get ComplianceRemediation |grep-i usbguard rhcos4-moderate-worker-configure-usbguard-auditbackend NotApplied <-- rhcos4-moderate-worker-package-usbguard-installed Applied rhcos4-moderate-worker-service-usbguard-enabled NotApplied rhcos4-moderate-worker-usbguard-allow-hid-and-hub NotApplied ~~~ * Enable remediation again for rules that having NotApplied status: ~~~ # for m in $(oc get-n openshift-compliance complianceremediation-o name |grep usbguard); do oc patch-n openshift-compliance $m-p '{"spec":{"apply":true}}'--type='merge' done ~~~ * Verify if the rules are having Applied status: ~~~ # oc get ComplianceRemediation |grep-i usbguard ~~~ * After re-scanning, check if the rules are passed properly.

title: kube-apiserver pod stuck in ContainerCreating state with error "x509: certificate is valid for kubernetes, kubernetes.default, kubernetes.default.svc, kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local, openshift, openshift.default, .. not api-int.test.redhat.com"
issue: - kube-apiserver pod stuck in ContainerCreating state.- api-int serving wrong CA signer certificate. ~~~ Warning FailedCreatePodSandBox 9m0s kubelet Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create pod network sandbox k8s_revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com_openshift-kube-apiserver_4808a675-3722-4e53-b69b-01cbebcbc52d_0(ebd6effec468cc5ca034982e571559e1884668993f854f1b6ff469edd0237f9): error adding pod openshift-kube-apiserver_revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com to CNI network "multus-cni-network": plugin type="multus" name="multus-cni-network" failed (add): Multus: [openshift-kube-apiserver/revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com/4808a675-3722-4e53-b69b-01cbebe845td]: error getting pod: Get "https://[api-int.test.redhat.com]:6443/api/v1/namespaces/openshift-kube-apiserver/pods/revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com?timeout=1m0s": x509: certificate is valid for kubernetes, kubernetes.default, kubernetes.default.svc, kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local, openshift, openshift.default, openshift.default.svc, openshift.default.svc.cluster.local, fd02::1, not api-int.test.redhat.com ~~~
resolution: 1) First check kube-apiserver pod events. ~~~ $ oc describe pod_name-n openshift-kube-apiserver Warning FailedCreatePodSandBox 9m9s kubelet Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create pod network sandbox k8s_revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com_openshift-kube-apiserver_4808a675-3722-4e53-b69b-01cbebe8c52d_0(ebd6effec468cc5ca034982e571559e1884668993f854f1b6ff469edd0237f9): error adding pod openshift-kube-apiserver_revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com to CNI network "multus-cni-network": plugin type="multus" name="multus-cni-network" failed (add): Multus: [openshift-kube-apiserver/revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com/4808a675-3722-4e53-b69b-01cbebe845td]: error getting pod: Get "https://[api-int.test.redhat.com]:6443/api/v1/namespaces/openshift-kube-apiserver/pods/revision-pruner-20-master1.test.redhat.com?timeout=1m0s": x509: certificate is valid for kubernetes, kubernetes.default, kubernetes.default.svc, kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local, openshift, openshift.default, openshift.default.svc, openshift.default.svc.cluster.local, fd02::1, not api-int.test.redhat.com ~~~ 2) Verify whether ***api-int*** serving wrong CA signed certificate with curl command: ~~~ $ curl-ksvI https://api-int.test.ocp.redhat.com:6443/version ~~~ Now verify which end point serving wrong certificate. ~~~ $ curl-ksvI https://api-int.test.ocp.redhat.com:6443/version--resolve "api-int.test.ocp.redhat.com:6443:[NODE_IP]" ~~~ From above command verify ***CN*** from ***Server certificate:*** field. It should be ***CN=kube-apiserver-lb-signer*** which will confirm expected CA signed this certificate.

title: Issue connecting to external Clair/Quay databases
issue: - I. When attempting to connect to external postgres databases for Quay and Clair, user is trying to connect to the "public" schema, but it says that is not allowed. What is missing in configuration?- II. Is it is possible to use one service account/user to access both quay and clair's database?
resolution: I. **For separate users accessing separate databases:** 1. `The problem can be solved by specifying a [search path](https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/search_path/) to the quay/clair database for service account/user`.- Command used on Quay database: ~~~ ALTER ROLE "role_name" SET search_path TO quay_username; ~~~- Command used on Clair database: ~~~ ALTER ROLE "role_name" SET search_path TO clair_username; ~~~ **Note**: This will not allow one user to access quay and clair at the same time. 2. `The problem can also be solved by adding a search_path in Quay and Clair config.yaml.`- `quay-app` pod expects database to be created in advance so quay-app-upgrade pod sets it up. Hence schemas and tables are already populated. This causes an issue with setting search_path for Quay. Solution is:- Add below lines in Quay config.yaml ~~~ DB_URI: postgresql://: @quayhostname.example.com: /quay_username?options=-csearch_path%3Dquay_username ~~~- "Reset" the Quay DB by cleaning up and restart quay-upgrade-app pod.- Configure the clair connstring to use a search_path with the below line: ~~~ indexer: connstring: host= port=5402 dbname=db_name user= password= sslmode=disable options=--search_path=clair_username ~~~ II. **For single service account/user accessing both DBs**- Yes it is possible to use one single service account/user to access both DBs. A database contains one or more named schemas, which in turn contain tables. Unlike databases, schemas are not rigidly separated: a user can access objects in any of the schemas in the database they are connected to, `if they have privileges(minimum CREATE rights)`. One would need to ensure that the tables(of quay + clair) are part of that same schema, otherwise unqualified queries wouldn't be able to find the tables. And the queries from Quay/Clair are all unqualified, as they expect the tables to be accessible from the DB connection by default.
root_cause: I. By default if one does not set a schema, it connects to the public schema. And public schema is only accessible by the `Postgres Admins`. Setting search_path helps

title: Unable to pull Couchbase images on Airgap OCP 4.x
issue: Unable to pull Couchbase operator and admission-controller images from Internal Registry when deployed via CAO. ~~~ Failed to pull image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/couchbase/operator@sha256:607effc8c063bce0346f5c422a62f6e679b5ac445eb379fc82b8d7f03f71817b": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = reading manifest sha256:607effc8c063bce0346f5c422a62f6e679b5ac445eb379fc82b8d7f03f71817b in image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/couchbase/operator: unauthorized: authentication required Failed to pull image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/couchbase/admission-controller@sha256:911dc2ce9a3dcfb7cdb6d337c3b5715c6422ba7188fc6cddd60b2ecefc198bb4": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = reading manifest sha256:911dc2ce9a3dcfb7cdb6d337c3b5715c6422ba7188fc6cddd60b2ecefc198bb4 in image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/couchbase/operator: unauthorized: authentication required ~~~
resolution: Deployments that are referencing an imagePullSecrets, we must ensure that the values specified within the secret are referencing the correct image registry and credentials to be used. ~~~ oc create secret docker-registry--docker-server=--docker-username=--docker-password=--docker-email= ~~~
root_cause: - By default, when installing Couchbase Operator using their CAO CLI, it will add a secret that references an external container image registry that could not be accessible by AirGap Openshift clusters.- Removing the section imagePullSecrets from the operator and admission-controller deployments will ensure that the image being pulled is from the Internal Registry

title: Can we add labels to the routes created by the 3scale Zync component?
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? Operator info: > threescale-2.13- 3scale-operator.v0.10.3 Configuration URLs used: > https://github.com/3scale/3scale-operator/blob/master/doc/apimanager-reference.md > https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4735331 > https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html/installing_3scale/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#deploying-apimanager-custom-resource--- Hi, we are facing a specific dificulty configuring the ApiManager resource using the 3Scale Operator. Our cluster has 3 ingress-controllers: default, dev, hom. All of them are configured with routerSelector. This configuration makes labeling the routes resources mandatory. We did not find an attribute to configure this route labels. Since the operators creates route resource, we are not sure if there is a problem when configuring manually the labels at the routers resources.--- Steps to reproduce: 1- install 3Scale Operator; 2- create an APIManager instance; 3- used the default configuration, changing the wildcard attribute; 4- operator created 5 "zync-*" routes and 1 "backend" route; 4.1.- only "backend" route is informed being managed by APIManager resource instance. The others does not inform. 5- we manually edited the routes to include the label for the routerSelector.--- The steps run sucessfully. We want to confirm: 1- Changing the route resource managed by APIManager instance could lead to future problem (resource update from the operator, erasing the labelling edit)? 2- Is there any attribute/configuration at the APIManager CRD to label de created routes at the routerSelector scope? Thank you. What is the business impact? Please also provide timeframe information. Client POC analysis.
resolution: Hi, Thank you for contacting the Red Hat support. My name is Gustavo and I'll be working with you on this case. Please allow me some time to perform some tests on my end and I'll get back to you shortly. Just answering your second question: "Is there any attribute/configuration at the APIManager CRD to label de created routes at the routerSelector scope?"- Unfortunately there isn't. The managed routes are created by `zync` component and currently there's no any spec to label routes. About the first question I need to perform some testes in my local instance to know in which cases the routes are persisted and not reconciled by zync. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira Hi, Just adding one more information to my answer for your second question: There's an [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-8507) to to support route/ingress labels i.e. ingress router sharding to be used in APICast CRD or this [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-4956) for APIManager CRD. Related to the first question, I was doing some tests on my end, and I can say that the zync routes are not reconciled in most of the cases. The labels were persisted if even I run the resync domains but not persisted if we change the Public Base URL that contains this route because the zync component will delete the old route that contains the labels and create a new one that not contains the labels. So I believe you'll be fine at least until you don't need to change the Public Base URL. Another scenario that these labels won't be persisted is in case you perform a 3scale backup/restore since the labels are inserted at OCP level and not system-db level, in this case you'll need to wait for the RFE. I hope I was able to answer your questions as you expected. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: [RHOCP 4.x ] Does Red Hat Supports  IPVS  proxy  for SVC in the upcoming OCP versions ?
issue: - OpenShift SVC is not doing close to fair load distribution.- The observed behavior is that some nodes get quite busy while other remain calm. This is not good when using HPA Although routes have improved load-balancing options, but when using non-HTTP frequently the options are limited to SVC + externalIPs.- So does Red Hat has any plans to implement IPVS? (https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/07/09/ipvs-based-in-cluster-load-balancing-deep-dive/)
resolution: Red Hat does not have any plans as far now to include IPVS in OpenShift OpenShift service works on TCP connection basis so if we keep a TCP connection open to anything like svc, which was assigned to a backend pod, it will remain open and be reused for all the request that go through that same TCP connection This is the situation for either openshift-sdn with iptables kube-proxy, for OVN-Kubernetes (with OVS-based load balancers) and it would be same even if the IPVS things had been accepted, because IPVS also works at TCP layer (the only benefits of IPVS are that the TCP connection distribution is smarter than for the iptables one but, once a connection is assigned, that connection remains pointing to the same pod). If there is new tcp connection established then the requests may be landed to your new scaling pods, Newer TCP connections have at least the chance to land in any of the pods, while older ones will just stick to the pod they were added to If the OpenShift-SDN is the current CNI (Older versions of OCP), then we would recommend migrating to OVN-K In OVN-K, the load balancing happens at OVS flows (by means of OVS groups) instead of iptables rules, which leads to better performance at scale. The selection algorithm depends on some tricky internals (a hash computed at the datapath). which can be seen as quite random from outside. More promising ways for relief would be: Add or modify the application readiness probe so that a pod that cannot accept new connections is not provided any new connection. Note that this means making readiness probe different from liveness probe, because we want the pod to not accept new connections, not to make it die while it is specifically attending the current ones. If the application requires to keep long standing TCP connections while ensuring even distribution at the HTTP request level, should consider to use a proper L7 load balancer instead of services. Concretely, host network ingress controllers now support TCP port customization since OCP 4.11 version so a dedicated ingress controller with custom ports + routes might do the needful
root_cause: This depends on multiple factors including the Cluster Enviornment, what CNI is in use and What OCP version is used currently Kubernetes / OpenShift uses readiness probes to decide when the container is available for accepting traffic. The readiness probe is used to control which pods are used as the backends for a service. A pod is considered ready when all of its containers are ready. If a pod is not ready, it is removed from service load balancers- With OpenShift-SDN, we have had massively improved iptables proxy performance- Since We are moving to OVN-K and making it as default CNI for the OCP, IPVS is not feasible

title: [RHOCP 4.x] Facing Error while Creating BGPPeer in MetalLB Operator - OCP 4.10
issue: - Unable to create BGPPeer in MetalLB Operator in OCP 4.x ~~~ Fix the following errors: Error "Invalid value: 4247584822: spec.peerASN in body should be less than or equal to 65535" for field "spec.peerASN" ~~~- Not able to create PeerBGB because the ASN value seems to be out of range
resolution: - Metallb BGP stack only support 2 bytes plain AS format, customers wanted to peer with metallb need adhere to the same format- When using 4 byte ASN (4247584822) on the Cisco Routers, but if peer cannot understand 4 byte, we can convert 4 byte to 2 byte AS which will be in decimal format (64813.54) but the issue is openshift metalb don't support. ASN fmt- we do support 2 bytes AS number as the error indicates it needs to be lesser than 65535 value- Bug is in progress with Red Hat Engineering team to support the 4 bytes [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2097701]
root_cause: - You should not create the Peer ASN values with. format in the DC gateway For example, below is what we should not have in DC gateway as it's difficult to change the DC gateway AS Peer values later ~~~ 2-Byte AS Number: 64813.54 4-Byte AS Number: 4247584822 ~~~- We are limited with what FRR BGP stack support and at the moment, it only supporting 2 bytes ASN- 2 bytes is more of legacy and doesn't support Asdot (.) format Unfortunately you will have to stick with plain AS format if you are peering with metallb

title: Create a custom cluster role specific to creating persistent volume

and assign this role to a user.

title: Is it recommended to set clusterNetwork or serviceNetwork addresses(CIDR) that overlap a part of the BMC network addresses?
issue: - iDRAC/BMC network is completely isolated from the cluster node network as a L2 network. Is it OK to use service or cluster network IP addresses(CRID) that are overlapped with some of BMC network addresses?

Even though technically it could work, there might be integrating or connecting the BMC network with other systems or services in the future which can cause complications. Red Hat does not test this configuration either.

title: Error message "unable to validate against any security context constraint" seen when mounting NFS storage in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - When mounting an NFS external storage, the following error occurs during creation of the pod: ~~~ Warning FailedCreate [...] replicaset-controller Error creating: pods " " is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constraint: [...] ~~~
resolution: - Check the namespace details for the allowed default values for supplementalGroups: ~~~ $ oc describe project... Annotations: openshift.io/description= openshift.io/display-name= openshift.io/requester=system:admin openshift.io/sa.scc.mcs=s0:c26,c5 openshift.io/sa.scc.supplemental-groups=1000660000/10000 openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range=1000660000/10000... ~~~- Then check the `securityContext` of the Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) definition ~~~ securityContext: runAsUser: 1000 runAsGroup: 1000 fsGroup: 1000 ~~~- Change the PVC to use `supplementalGroups` ~~~ securityContext: supplementalGroups: [1000660001] ~~~
root_cause: - The Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) is defining a group that is not in the allowed range of the SCC assigned to the user.- The Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) has too many constrains that do not match any default SCC.- The recommended way to handle NFS access- assuming it is not an option to change permissions on the NFS export- is to use supplemental groups see [NFS volume security](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/storage/persistent_storage/persistent-storage-nfs.html#nfs-volume-security_persistent-storage-nfs).- The OpenShift Container Platform NFS plug-in mounts the container’s NFS directory with the same POSIX ownership and permissions found on the exported NFS directory.- When a container or pod does not request a user ID under which it should be run, the effective UID depends on the SCC that emits this pod.- The `restricted` SCC is granted to all authenticated users by default (for available default SCCs refer to the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/authentication/managing-security-context-constraints.html#managing-pod-security-policies)).- Assuming there are no custom SCCs that might satisfy the pod requirements a pod should make use of the restricted SCC.- Looking at the details of the restricted SCC the following is shown: ~~~ $ oc describe scc restricted Name: restricted Priority: Access: Users: Groups: system:authenticated Settings: Allow Privileged: false Default Add Capabilities: Required Drop Capabilities: KILL,MKNOD,SYS_CHROOT,SETUID,SETGID Allowed Capabilities: Allowed Seccomp Profiles: Allowed Volume Types: configMap,downwardAPI,emptyDir,persistentVolumeClaim,projected,secret Allow Host Network: false Allow Host Ports: false Allow Host PID: false Allow Host IPC: false Read Only Root Filesystem: false Run As User Strategy: MustRunAsRange UID: UID Range Min: UID Range Max: SELinux Context Strategy: MustRunAs User: Role: Type: Level: FSGroup Strategy: MustRunAs Ranges: Supplemental Groups Strategy: RunAsAny Ranges: ~~~- The restricted SCC has the `supplementalGroups` strategy set to `RunAsAny`, meaning that any supplied `group ID` is accepted without range checking. As a result if the pod uses `supplementalGroups` for the PVC and the `restricted` SCC it passes the security check and launches successfully.- If `group ID` range checking is required for more secure access a custom SCC is preferred. A custom SCC can be created such that minimum and maximum `group IDs` are defined in a way that includes the desired ID.

title: How to force unicast mode for keepalived to workaround migration issues
issue: - After upgrades from RHOCP 4.10 to 4.11 situation where the Virtual IP for ingress or API is assigned to more than one node might occur.- Some nodes have migrated to unicast while others have not
resolution: This solution is not supported unless explicitly recommended by Red Hat Support or Red Hat Engineering in a support case 0. Refer to Diagnostic Steps section to collect the existing configuration and identify the affected nodes 1. Create the file `/etc/keepalived/monitor-user.conf` on each node that has no *unicast_peer* section with the exact one line content: ~~~ mode: unicast ~~~ 2. Wait up to 10 minutes and see if the migration happened. 3. If migration hasn't happened, stop and delete the keepalived-monitor container and wait for a new one to start up. ~~~ sh-4.4# crictl ps|grep keepalived-monitor|awk '{print $1}'| xargs-I contID sh-c 'echo contID && crictl stop contID && crictl rm contID' ~~~ 4. If the above step has not caused the configuration regeneration, try stopping keepalived pod, moving keepalived.conf away and starting it again ~~~ sh-4.4# mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/keepalived.yaml /root sh-4.4# mv /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf /root # This is for backup sh-4.4# mv /root/keepalived.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ ~~~ 5. If the step above doesn't work, please inform back in the support case open with Red Hat._NOTE_: If for some reason one desired to force the `multicast` mode, it would be also possible by specifying `multicast` in the config file from step 1. However, doing so is discouraged in most cases (and **not supported**, unless the contrary is explicitly stated).
root_cause: In RHOCP version 4.11 the default *keepalived* setting has changed from multicast to unicast mode as described in the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.11/html/release_notes/ocp-4-11-release-notes#ocp-4-11-vsphere-unicast-default). In case of certain upgrade issues, incorrect configuration might persistent on some of the nodes

title: How to configure access to RHSSO  using OpenShift Groups and Roles
issue: - How do we map the SSO groups to Openshift cluster?- Is it possible to integrate the users/groups within OpenShift with RH SSO in a way, that based on being a user within OpenShift, access to a specific realm is granted based on OpenShift group membership?- If not, it is possible to broker admin console login for RH SSO to our Azure Active Directory, just like this is possible for individual RH SSO clients?- In another way is it possible to create SSO groups, add users(AD users) to the groups, and give permission on the Openshift clusters to those SSO groups.
resolution: - In order to gain access to dedicated realms, applications need to be configured based on client scope roles, where RH-SSO has corresponding roles or groups. Redhat doesn't currently see a way to obtain OpenShift groups within RH-SSO. Unless users originate from an LDAP, Redhat considers this to be infeasible at the moment.

title: vulnerability reporting not working Successfully in RHACS
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - RHACS vulnerability reporting is configured with parameter ```Show vulnerabilities: since last successful report``` but report is generated for all vulnerabilities detected in every deployed Image on RHOCP clusters while it should be only generating from the last successful report.
resolution: - This is known to Red Hat and currently engineering team is working on this via a [bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ROX-17137).

title: How does load balancing occur when I have HPA enabled?
issue: (respondendo a Pereira, Gustavo) > Hi Tiberio, > > Thank you for contacting the Red Hat support. My name is Gustavo and I'll be working with you on this case. Can you share the documentation/steps you followed to configure the HPA? > > In addition, share the inspection of the namespace where the pods you're trying to scale resides: > > $ oc adm inspec ns/ > > Kind regards, > Gustavo Pereira Hi Gustavo. I realized that the problem was pod request config in deployment App. So I adjust this and solved it. However I have some questions about HPA: How occurs the load balancing when I have the HPA enabled? I can see someway how it's occurring during the HPA? There are some lifecycle config to do in Pods to avoid high memory consumer outdated, respecting the deployment strategy? (I mean not just to kill the pod but follow the deployment strategy when the pod will be create). Regards.
resolution: Hi Tiberio, Find below some helpful information related to HPA as you requested: 1. The HPA monitors the resource usage of the pods in a specific Deployment or ReplicationController. This monitoring is typically based on metrics such as CPU or memory utilization[1]. 2. If the resource usage exceeds or falls below the defined limits, the HPA automatically adjusts the number of pod replicas in the target Deployment or ReplicationController. 3. If the HPA determines that increased computing capacity is required due to high load, it scales up the number of pod replicas to distribute the load among them. This is achieved by horizontally scaling the number of pods based on the defined metrics [2]. 4. Openshift handles the internal load balancing between the replicas of the pods. Once more replicas are scaled, the traffic is automatically distributed among the additional pods through the associated service. To check the current status of the HPA, run the following command: > $ oc get hpa To check real-time updates of the HPA, you can run the following command: > $ watch oc get hpa or > $ oc get hpa-w More details on how to verify HPA status can be found in our documentation [3]. [1] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-autoscaling.html#nodes-pods-autoscaling-workflow-hpa_nodes-pods-autoscaling [2] https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.10/html-single/nodes/index#nodes-pods-autoscaling [3] https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-autoscaling.html#nodes-pods-autoscaling-status-viewing_nodes-pods-autoscaling Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: Migrate ElasticSearch PersistentVolumeClaim to a new vSphere datastore keeping the elasticsearch data
issue: Need to change the VMware datastore and have to migrate the elasticsearch-cdm pvc in a `ZeroRedundancy` Policy
resolution: * This resolution is only applicable with: * RHOCP 4 and elasticsearch Logging stack * When the `redundancyPolicy` is set to `ZeroRedundancy`, It means that there are no copy of the original data available in another Elasticsearch * Elasticsearch status is green, then, all shards and replicas are available. In the opposite way, some data could be get lost (indices in red status)--- **Section 1: summary** 1. update the vSphere datastore to new datastore 2. add new StorageClass 3. check the openshift-logging pvc 4. stop the openshift-logging elasticsearch-cdm 5. migrate the pvc data a. create the temp pv b. create the temp pvc c. create an application 'helper' to mount the elasticsearch-cdm and temp pvc to copy the data d. add the pvc 'elasticsearch-cdm-1' to the helper application e. add the pvc 'pvc-temp-elastic1' to the helper application f. check the helper application disks g. copy the data from 'source' to 'temp' disk h. remove the pvc 'elasticsearch-cdm-1' from the helper application i. create and add the new pvc to the 'helper' deployment j. copy the data from 'temp' to 'target' disk k. delete the 'helper' deployment l. delete the pvc 'pvc-temp-elastic1' m. add the new target disk to the 'elasticsearch-cdm-xxxx-1' deployment 6. start the openshift-logging elasticsearch-cdm 7. check the pods **Section 2: procedure** **1. update the vSphere datastore to new datastore** ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-config get cm cloud-provider-config-o yaml | grep datastore default-datastore = "current_datastore" # replace the parameter 'default-datastore' to the new datastore $ oc-n openshift-config edit cm cloud-provider-config $ oc-n openshift-config get cm cloud-provider-config-o yaml | grep datastore default-datastore = "new_datastore" ~~~ **2. add new StorageClass** ~~~ $ oc get sc NAME PROVISIONER RECLAIMPOLICY VOLUMEBINDINGMODE ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION AGE thin (default) kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume Delete Immediate false 26h thin-csi csi.vsphere.vmware.com Delete WaitForFirstConsumer true 26h $ cat < < EOF > > new-sc.yaml apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata: annotations: storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true" name: new-thin-sc parameters: datastore: new_datastore diskformat: thin provisioner: kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume reclaimPolicy: Delete volumeBindingMode: Immediate EOF $ oc create-f new-sc.yaml storageclass.storage.k8s.io/new-thin-sc created # remove the annotation 'storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class'from the 'thin' sc. $ oc annotate sc thin storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class- storageclass.storage.k8s.io/thin annotated $ oc get sc NAME PROVISIONER RECLAIMPOLICY VOLUMEBINDINGMODE ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION AGE new-thin-sc (default) kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume Delete Immediate false 4m41s thin kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume Delete Immediate false 26h thin-csi csi.vsphere.vmware.com Delete WaitForFirstConsumer true 26h ~~~ **3. check the openshift-logging pvc** ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging get pvc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE elasticsearch-elasticsearch-cdm-xxxx-1 Bound pvc-df7a4c4c-f742-42ad-bac7-111111111111 47684Mi RWO thin 19h elasticsearch-elasticsearch-cdm-xxxx-2 Bound in $(oc-n $ns get deployment-o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name--no-headers); do echo $i; oc-n $ns set volume deployment $i | grep-A1 pvc; echo ""; done cluster-logging-operator title: Using AMQ Artemis broker with replicated file system
issue: Artemis' journal directory may appear to be accumulating journal files that are not being removed promptly
root_cause: Artemis broker relies very heavily of fast storage devices to move and reclaim journal files. Some file systems where data is being replicated between two different sites may not respond fast enough to Java file method calls thus preventing the broker from reclaiming journal files leading to accumulation of journal files in journal directory and in extreme cases leading to a volume hosting broker's persistence storage running out of space.

title: How to Backup/Delete/Restore Subscriptions and Cluster Service Versions in OpenShift Data Foundations
issue: In the event, there is a need to remove/re-add Subscription (subs) or Cluster Service Versions (csv) from the `openshift-storage` namespace. The following are examples of why backing/restoring from the current subscription version could be useful:- Missing or faulty resources (configmap, InstallPlan, Secrets, Service Accounts, etc.).- More than a two-version differential between OCP/ODF.- Failed upgrades.
resolution: 1. Capture Names of Subs and CSVs: `$ oc get olm-n openshift-storage` a. If the issue was that the ODF and bundled operators are missing from OLM output, simply go to the Operator Hub and click "Install" on the ODF-Operator. If there is a current/active `storagesystem` `storagecluster` DO NOT MAKE ANY CHANGES, SIMPLY CLICK "INSTALL." Shown in the [ODF 4.9- odf-operator csv and subscription are not present](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973250) solutions article. b. If the operators are present, proceed to step 2 after reading the note below. **NOTE: Subscription and CSV names will change with each version. The name of the version will be after the slash. Example:**- The MCG Operator Sub in OLM output: `subscription.operators.coreos.com/mcg-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace`- The MCG Operator Sub name: `mcg-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace`- The NooBaa Operator (also known as MCG) CSV in OLM output: `clusterserviceversion.operators.coreos.com/mcg-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf`- The NooBaa Operator CSV name: `mcg-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf` 2. Backup of existing ODF Subscriptions (subs) and Cluster Service Versions (CSVs). **NOTE:** Only the `ocs-operator` is present in v4.8 and below. Additionally, the `csi-addons-operator` isn't present until v4.10+. ~~~ $ mkdir-p /tmp/subBackup $ oc get sub-n openshift-storage mcg-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace-o yaml > mcg-sub.out $ oc get sub-n openshift-storage ocs-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace-o yaml > ocs-operator-sub.out $ oc get sub-n openshift-storage odf-csi-addons-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace-o yaml > odf-csi-addons-operator-sub.out $ oc get sub-n openshift-storage odf-operator-o yaml > odf-operator-sub.out $ oc get csv-n openshift-storage mcg-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf-o yaml > mcg-operator-csv.out $ oc get csv-n openshift-storage ocs-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf-o yaml > ocs-operator-csv.out $ oc get csv-n openshift-storage odf-csi-addons-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf-o yaml > csi-addons-operator-csv.out $ oc get csv-n openshift-storage odf-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf-o yaml > odf-operator-csv.out $ ls csi-addons-operator-csv.out mcg-operator-csv.out mcg-sub.out ocs-operator-csv.out ocs-operator-sub.out odf-csi-addons-operator-sub.out odf-operator-csv.out odf-operator-sub.out ~~~ 3. Delete subscriptions/CSVs: ~~~ $ oc delete csv-n openshift-storage mcg-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf $ oc delete csv-n openshift-storage ocs-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf $ oc delete csv-n openshift-storage odf-csi-addons-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf $ oc delete csv-n openshift-storage odf-operator.v4.12.2-rhodf $ oc delete sub-n openshift-storage mcg-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace $ oc delete sub-n openshift-storage ocs-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplacesub.out $ oc delete sub-n openshift-storage odf-csi-addons-operator-stable-4.12-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace $ oc delete sub-n openshift-storage odf-operator ~~~ **NOTE:** Your ODF Operator in the OCP GUI Operator Hub has now been removed from "Installed Operators, and your deployments/operators along with the CSI resources are now gone. The data is still safe. 4. Re-Install Subs/CSVs: **Warning: The storagesystem, storagecluster, and namespace already exist. Do not attempt to make any changes to the existing storagesystem and underlying components, or attempt to create a new storagesystem. Simply restore the OCS/ODF subscription.** 5. If wanting to restore the same version that was removed, restore from the `odf-operator-sub.out` file. **NOTE:** Restoring the same version is good for use cases such as if there was a missing resource (configmap, serviceaccount, etc.), but not wanting to upgrade. Or, there is more than a two-version differential between OCP and ODF (e.g. OCP v4.12 and ODF v4.9). a. `$ oc create-f odf-operator-sub.out` **Note:** if wanting to upgrade to a higher version of OCS/ODF, the OCP version must be taken into consideration. In Accordance With (IAW) the [Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation(previously known as OpenShift Container Storage) Supportability and Interoperability Guide](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4731161), two points need to be taken into consideration regarding the OCP to OCS/ODF relationship:- OCP should be the same version, or one version ahead of ODF (Example: OCP v4.12 and ODF v4.12 or OCP v4.12 and ODF v4.11 are supported, OCP v4.12 and ODF v4.10 is unsupported).- Two version upgrade jumps are not supported (Example: Upgrading from ODF v4.10 directly to v4.12). With those two points in mind, restore the ODF Operator, from the Operator Hub in the OCP console GUI: b. Navigate to the OCP GUI-> Operator Hub. Search "OpenShift Data Foundations"-> Click "Install" **NOTE:** You will be brought to the "Install Operator" Page, do not make any changes to any of the fields **EXCEPT:** If there is a two-version differential between OCP and ODF, select the lowest version. For example, OCP v4.12 with ODF v4.10 would select v4.11, shown in the "Update Channel" section, as two-version jump upgrades are not supported. Once ODF Operator v4.11 is successfully installed/upgraded, the ODF v4.11 to v4.12 upgrade can be accomplished IAW the Official RHODF "Updating" product documentation. c. Select your Update Channel, and click "Install." **NOTE:** If upgrading during the restoring/reinstalling ODF Operator process, what is to be expected is that this process may take some time (approximately 10-20 min, sometimes longer depending on resources). Please be patient. Once the Deployments/Operators/CSI resources return, ODF will begin upgrading the other resources (OSDs, monitor pods, etc.) which may go through a few cycles of upgrading the same resource(s). Please do not panic or interject if you see resources terminate/re-create multiple times.
root_cause: In instances where resources such as deployments, serviceaccounts, configmaps, InstallPlans are missing/deleted, or there is an overall failure of an operator/deployment-dependent resources.

title: What's the security implications by giving "system:authenticated" access to the "csi" volume type?
issue: - How can we set up permissions for Hashicorp Vault to use the upstream secrets in the vault?- What's the security implications by giving "system:authenticated" access to the "csi" volume type?
resolution: It should be possible to modify the restricted-v2 scc to include the csi volumes, or alternatively, create a new SCC based on the restricted-v2 that includes the csi volume capability. In terms on security, adding this capability to pods it will only allow access to the csi objects provided by the CRD "secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1" through a CSI driver called "secrets-store.csi.k8s.io", and they will be mounted as regular volumes in the pods
root_cause: Mostly, because we do not provide support for this, so it's not considered when creating the defaults SCC's.

title: Changing the Index names of app and namespace for Elasticsearch.
issue: - Is it possible to change index names for Elasticsearch log-store from `app-` to pattern like `app1-env-` `app2-env-`.- Can we have different retention for different namespace.- Is there any recommended practice to control access and handle log retention policy when all logs are in the same index?
resolution: - The logs will never be in same index.- There is a policy defined in backend through which the indices are rollover and cleanup is performed.- Elasticsearch rolls over an index, moving the current index and creating a new index, when an index matches any of below conditions:- The index is older than the rollover.maxAge value in the ElasticSearch CR.- The index size is greater than 40 GB x the number of primary shards.- The index doc count is greater than 40960 KB x the number of primary shards.- The logs which are not in the form of json will be moved to `app-*` index instead of 'app-nologformat`.- Need to validate if the logs generated by application are in json format or not.- Regarding different retention for different namespaces, this can't be done with OCP 4.5+ versions as the logs are segregated into app-*, infra-* and audit-* indices and the same retention is applied to all such indices.- To apply different retention to different alias (app, infra and audit) as per the [doc](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/logging/config/cluster-logging-log-store.html#cluster-logging-elasticsearch-retention_cluster-logging-store).

title: Why do various Cluster Operator pods try to run with the SCC anyuid?
issue: - Why do various Cluster Operator pods try to run with the SCC `anyuid`?- The pod `container: cloud-credential-operator` is stuck with the `reason: CreateContainerConfigError`.
resolution: - Remove `-system:authenticated` group from the `anyuid` SCC, and then restart all the pods that are stuck due to this issue.- **NOTE**: Also note that, any modification in the system default SCCs is not recommended. It is recommended to create custom SCCs and then add the groups as required.
root_cause: - The `anyuid` SCC in the cluster has been configured with the `-system:authenticated` group.

title: How to Replace Two OSDs by One OSD per node in Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation Without Any Data Loss
issue: - The configuration consists in a 3-node OpenShift Cluster where OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) has been installed to provide storage.- Applications already deployed **need a different storage layout*

provided by ODF.- However, OpenShift resources (CPU and/or RAM) are very limited and they are not big enough to be able to add new drives to the nodes and extend the ODF cluster accordingly.- How to achieve this? Unfortunately [the ODF scale-up procedure](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.12/html/scaling_storage/index) do not currently fullfill this need.
resolution: - In order to be able to increase the overall storage provided by ODF with the current OpenShift resource limitations in terms of CPU and/or RAM, we will replace all drives currently assigned to ODF for bigger ones **without loosing any Applications data**.- The testings have been performed using the following set up: 3-node [OpenShift Compact mode](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/delivering-a-three-node-architecture-for-edge-deployments) cluster (aka Schedulable Control Plane) acting as Control Plane and Worker nodes, each node configured with: Openshift Nodes:- 16 CPUs,- 36 GiB RAM,- 3 SSD drives- /dev/sda: OS drive- /dev/sdb: 100 GiB- /dev/sdc: 100 GiB- 1 Ethernet Port- enp1s0 2 Operators have been installed in the OpenShift cluster to provide Cluster Storage:- Local Storage Operator (LSO) providing:- 1 LocalVolume- lv-for-odf- using 2 devices:- /dev/sdb- /dev/sdc- 1 StorageClass:- lv-for-odf-sc- OpenShift Data Foundation Operator (ODF):- created using LSO Storage Class:- lv-for-odf-sc- using OpenShift SDN network- providing Storage Classes:- ocs-storagecluster-rbd for Bloc PVCs- ocs-storagecluster-cephfs for File PVCs- ocs-storagecluster-rgw for Object Storage (OBCs)- In this document, two 100 GiB SSD drives will be replaced by one 200 GiB SSD drive on each OpenShift node.- *These are the steps required:*- Preparation Step:- deploying ODF Ceph Rook Tools to be able to access the internal Ceph cluster,- modify LSO LocalVolume lv-for-odf to use only 1 device (sdb) instead of the original 2 (sdb and sdc).- Loop Step:- For each OpenShift Node (N), **one at a time to avoid data loss** we will do:- Remove old OSDs Step,- Add new OSD Step.- Verification Step:- Verify that ODF associated Ceph cluster is healthy and using all new drives- Update ODF Storage Cluster with its new number of OSDs- *Here are the detailed operations associated to each step:*- Preparation Step details:- install Ceph Rook Tools following the steps described in [How to configure Ceph toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891)- access tool to interact with Ceph cluster and get Ceph status and topology ~~~ oc rsh-n openshift-storage $(oc get pods-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o name) sh-4.4$ ceph health HEALTH_OK sh-4.4$ ceph osd df tree ID CLASS WEIGHT REWEIGHT SIZE RAW USE DATA OMAP META AVAIL %USE VAR PGS STATUS TYPE NAME-1 0.58612- 600 GiB 30 GiB 30 GiB 102 KiB 197 MiB 570 GiB 5.07 1.00- root default-7 0.19537- 200 GiB 10 GiB 10 GiB 34 KiB 61 MiB 190 GiB 170 up osd.5-5 0.19537- 200 GiB 10 GiB 10 GiB 34 KiB 74 MiB 190 GiB 5.07 1.00- host master2-cls03-lab 2 ssd 0.09769 1.00000 100 GiB 6.4 GiB 6.4 GiB 25 KiB 41 MiB 94 GiB 6.43 1.27 184 up osd.2 4 ssd 0.09769 1.00000 100 GiB 3.7 GiB 3.7 GiB 9 KiB 33 MiB 96 GiB 3.72 0.73 169 up osd.4-3 0.19537- 200 GiB 10 GiB 10 GiB 34 KiB 62 MiB 190 GiB 5.07 1.00- host master3-cls03-lab 0 ssd 0.09769 1.00000 100 GiB 5.5 GiB 5.5 GiB 16 KiB 38 MiB 95 GiB 5.49 1.08 166 up osd.0 1 ssd 0.09769 1.00000 100 GiB 4.6 GiB 4.6 GiB 18 KiB 24 MiB 95 GiB 4.64 0.92 187 up osd.1 TOTAL 600 GiB 30 GiB 30 GiB 106 KiB 197 MiB only the /dev/sdb device like this: ~~~ spec: storageClassDevices:- devicePaths:- /dev/sdb fsType: ext4 storageClassName: lv-for-odf-sc volumeMode: Block ~~~- Loop Step details:- Working with OpenShift Node N, **do not go to next node until both following steps are completed successfully**:- Remove old OSDs Step details:- identify OSD PODs running on Node **N** (here Node **N** is to fully remove these OSD PODs, if the drives still exist on the Node itself, OpenShift will re-create those OSD PODs very soon after they were deleted. In order to avoid this behavior, we will physically remove those drives on Node **N** using the following commands: ~~~ ssh-i ~/.ssh/id_ecdsa_lab core@master1.cls03.lab [core@master1 ~]$ sudo-i [root@master1 ~]$ for device in sdb sdc; do echo "removing ${device}"; blockdev--flushbufs /dev/${device}; echo 1 > /sys/block/${device}/device/delete; done; lsblk NAME MAJ:MIN RM SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINT sda 8:0 0 100G 0 disk |-sda1 8:1 0 1M 0 part |-sda2 8:2 0 127M 0 part |-sda3 8:3 0 384M 0 part /boot `-sda4 8:4 0 99.5G 0 part /sysroot [root@master1 ~]$ exit [core@master1 ~]$ exit ~~~- remove any former OSD removal jobs: ~~~ oc delete-n openshift-storage job ocs-osd-removal-job job.batch "ocs-osd-removal-job" deleted ~~~- create OSD removal job associated with the OSDs to remove (here Ceph OSD 3 and Ceph OSD 5): ~~~ oc process-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal-p FAILED_OSD_IDS=3,5 FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=false |oc create-n openshift-storage-f- job.batch/ocs-osd-removal-job created ~~~- list OSD removal job: ~~~ oc get pod-l job-name-ocs-osd-removal-job-n openshift-storage NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE ocs-osd-removal-job-ps59l 0/1 Running 0 8s ~~~- As we have removed all OSDs on Node **N** (**master1**), the Ceph cluster is no longer healthy, it is in a degraded mode as all Ceph pools have currently **2** replicas instead of **3**.
