title: Virtual machine changes for Azure Red Hat Openshift after installation.
issue: - Is it possible to apply the following changes to ARO Virtual machines after installation: [1] Virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets should have encryption at host enabled [2] A vulnerability assessment solution should be enabled on your virtual machines [3] Vulnerabilities in security configuration on customer machines should be remediated
resolution: [1] Azure offers encryption at the host, this would be done by the customer by referring [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disks-enable-host-based-encryption-portal?tabs=azure-powershell) OpenShift offers disk encryption with byok and would be done by the customer by referring [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-byo) [2] Azure runs a vulnerability assessment solution by default, Customer can refer to [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/security-control-vulnerability-management#51-run-automated-vulnerability-scanning-tools) [3] Customer's VMs are patched by Microsoft, to have more information refer to documentation[https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/automatic-vm-guest-patching] ARO SRE patches all components of Openshift under the Security and Regulation Compliance, refer [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/responsibility-matrix#overview)

title: How do I calculate the number of CPU cores for a cluster
issue: - How do i calculate the number of cores for all the cluster nodes?- How do i calculate the number of cores for my worker nodes?- How do i calculate the number of cores in roder to adjust my subscription?- How do i calculate the number of used cores?
resolution: - How do i calculate the number of used cores in the cluster (result in milicore)? ~~~ oc adm top node | awk '{sum+=$2} END {print sum}' ~~~- How do i calculate the number of used cores by the worker nodes in the cluster? ~~~ oc adm top node--selector='node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=' | awk '{sum+=$2} END {print sum}' ~~~- How do i calculate the total number of cores for all the nodes in the cluster(result in cores)? ~~~ for n in $(oc get node-o name); do node_cpu=$(oc get $n-o jsonpath='{.status.capacity.cpu}'); ((tot_cpu+=node_cpu)); done; echo $tot_cpu ~~~- If you are calculating the number of cores to check the subscription, you must consider only workers cores (result in cores)? ~~~ tot_cpu=0; for n in $(oc get node--selector='node-role.kubernetes.io/worker='-o name); do node_cpu=$(oc get $n-o jsonpath='{.status.capacity.cpu}'); ((tot_cpu+=node_cpu)); done; echo $tot_cpu ~~~ Note: Ensure to exclude any infra cores from the worker cores for subscription calculation. Additional info:- [Infrastructure Nodes in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5034771)- [Self-managed Red Hat OpenShift sizing and subscription guide](https://www.redhat.com/en/resources/self-managed-openshift-sizing-subscription-guide)

title: Velero operator diverts deployment modifications
issue: The Velero operator requires additional annotations in deployments. These modifications are reverted by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO).
resolution: Modifications reverting to the default is working as designed. The only way the operator will not revert changes is by putting it into an Unmanaged state which is not recommended and will result in the OpenShift Cluster in an unsupported state.- ManagementState- Managed: The Operator updates the registry as configuration resources are updated.- Unmanaged: The Operator ignores changes to the configuration resources.- Removed: The Operator removes the registry instance
root_cause: The Cluster Version Operator (CVO) manages all ClusterOperator deployments within OpenShift and is responsible for ClusterOperator upgrades during an OpenShift upgrade.

title: How to configure IPI OpenShift 4 to redirect all the *.apps queries to the external DNS
issue: - How to get `*.apps.. ` externally resolved?- How to configure **DNS forwarding*
to redirect queries to an external DNS in an IPI Cluster?
resolution: 1. Export the `cluster domain`: ~~~ $ clusterdomain=$(oc get ingress.config.openshift.io cluster-ojsonpath='{.spec.domain}{"\n"}') ~~~ 2. Export `DNS IP` and `Port`: ~~~ $ dns=": " ~~~ 2. Update the DNS Operator by adding the zones that must be forwarded: ~~~ $ oc patch dns.operator default--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"servers":[{"forwardPlugin":{"policy":"Random", "upstreams":["'$dns'"]}, "name":"api-new", "zones":["'$clusterdomain'", "'$clusterdomain'.'$(echo $clusterdomain| cut-d '.'-f2-)'", "'$clusterdomain'.'$(echo $clusterdomain| cut-d '.'-f3-)'"]}]}}' ~~~
root_cause: - As reported in the [DNS Forwarding](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/networking/dns-operator.html#nw-dns-forward_dns-operator) documentation, using an External DNS for resolving some specific zones is a supported procedure. But in case the zone is `*.apps.. `, two more zones must be added to avoid that **dns-default** pods redirect the queries to the **infra coredns**.- These extra entries are required because, by default, the **dns-default** pods first try to resolve the fqdn by adding the entries it finds inside the `/etc/resolve.conf` file in the `search` section and only then tries to resolve the fqdn without adding anything. This means that the first queries do not match the value added inside the `dns.operator` and will be resolved by the **coredns infra**. For this reason, the extra zones must be added.

title: ODF - How to collect the logs in noobaa-db-pg-0 if it is in CLBO
issue: How to collect the logs inside the noobaa-db-pg-0 when it is in CLBO
resolution: 1. Patch the sts of noobaa-db-pg-0 ~~~ oc patch sts noobaa-db-pg--type='json'-p='[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/command", "value": ["sleep", "infinity"]}]' ~~~ 2. Once you are in the pod you can copy the content of `/var/lib/pgsql` 3. Restart the pod ~~~ oc scale sts noobaa-db-pg--replicas 0 oc scale sts noobaa-db-pg--replicas 1 ~~~

title: Pushing large images to Red Hat Quay fails with HTTP Status: 500 Internal  Server Error
issue: Pushing an image of size 14GB to Quay, but getting HTTP Status: 500 Internal Server Error: Error: writing blob: uploading layer chunked: received unexpected HTTP status: 500 Internal Server Error
resolution: Review storage performance.
root_cause: The storage engine is taking over 60 seconds to respond and send information back to Red Hat Quay.

title: Image-Registry operator degraded, storage configuration synchronization error in RHOCP
issue: - Error: The image-registry pods are unable to deploy, resulting in deployment failures.- Restarting Pods: The image-registry pods are continuously restarting, indicating instability or underlying issues.- Degraded Cluster Operator: The image-registry cluster operator is currently in a degraded state, impacting the functionality of the image registry.
resolution: To resolve the issue, follow the steps in the OpenShift documentation at the following URL to reconfigure the storage credentials for the Image Registry Operator: ``` $ oc create secret generic image-registry-private-configuration-user--from-literal=REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_ACCESSKEY=myaccesskey--from-literal=REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_SECRETKEY=mysecretkey--namespace openshift-image-registry ``` [Configuring Storage Credentials for the Registry Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/registry/configuring-registry-operator.html#registry-operator-config-resources-storage-credentials_configuring-registry-operator)
root_cause: - The errors indicate that there is a problem with the credentials used by the `openshift-image-registry` cluster operator when accessing the storage.

title: Pods are not coming up when they are created using DeploymentConfig in OpenShift 4
issue: - Creating application using `oc new-app` command doesn't start the pod.- Why is the pod not created using build?- New projects are created with no `builder` serviceaccount.- DeploymentConfig shows CURRENT 0: ~~~ $ oc get dc NAME REVISION DESIRED CURRENT TRIGGERED BY postgresql 0 1 0 config,image(postgresql:12-el8) rails-postgresql-example 0 1 0 config,image(rails-postgresql-example:latest) ~~~
resolution: Restart `openshift-controller-manager` pods: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-controller-manager delete pod-l app=openshift-controller-manager ~~~
root_cause: - Since the **DeploymentConfig** is an OpenShift Resource and it is handled by `controller-manager` pods, this issue can occur if these reside on the wrong network and are unable to talk to the rest of the cluster.- One of the actions that can trigger this issue is updating the ClusterNetwork without restarting all the nodes.

title: STF Dashboard is not accessible in Red Hat OpenShift 4
issue: - Grafana Dashboard returns **Application is not available*
error message.- SFT **grafana-deployment*

pod shows TLS errors: ~~~ $ oc logs grafana-deployment-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx oauth-proxy [..] 2023/05/26 08:52:10 server.go:3230: http: TLS handshake error from 10.0.0.1:39216: local error: tls: bad record MAC [..] ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [Grafana Dashboard returns Application is not available error message](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/STF-1379). ### Workaround {#workaround}- Restart the following two services using the exact following command: ~~~ $ oc-n service-telemetry delete svc grafana-alert grafana-service ~~~
root_cause: - The **grafana-deployment** pod uses two services, **grafana-alert** and **grafana-service**, and both use annotations to request OpenShift to generate TLS certificates.- A race condition between these services can occur since both try to create a TLS secret with the same name.- If this issue happens with the **grafana-service**, the **router-default** pods are not able to terminate the TLS Handshake because the secret mounted contains the certificates of the **grafana-alert** service.

title: How to Remove Old DES Entries from Keytabs
issue: DES encryption is quite old and keytabs that use it should be removed unless they are absolutely necessary. **NOTE**: This method can be used to remove keytab entries of any type, but for this article we will be focusing on the entries with DES encryption.
resolution: #### Prerequisite steps and information- Ensure `krb5-workstation` is installed; # yum install krb5-workstation- For example purposes, the Principal's hostname is `ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL`, the ciphers removed are `arcfour-hmac` and `des3-cbc-sha1`, and the revised keytab is named `/etc/new_krb5.keytab`. **Note**: one or more of these will likely be different and should reflect the needs of the target environment. #### Workflow 1. Run `ktutil`, a shell used to interact with and edit keytabs; # ktutil 2. Load the keytab for editing; ktutil: read_kt /etc/krb5.keytab 3. List the keytab entries to find the slot number used to identify which entry will be removed; ktutil: list-e slot KVNO Principal----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96) 2 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96) 3 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (des3-cbc-sha1) <--- 4 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (arcfour-hmac) <--- 5 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (camellia128-cts-cmac) 6 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (camellia256-cts-cmac) 4. `arcfour-hmac` and `des3-cbc-sha1` are in slots 3 and 4. Here, slot 4 and then slot 3 are deleted in that specific order to accommodate shifts in the table indexing due to entry removal. **Note**: in order to mitigate potential errors in entry removal due to shifting entries, removing keys from bottom to top is strongly recommended; ktutil: delete_entry 4 ktutil: delete_entry 3 5. Double check the revised entry list before saving the changes; ktutil: list-e slot KVNO Principal----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96) 2 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96) 3 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (camellia128-cts-cmac) 4 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (camellia256-cts-cmac) 6. Save the revisions to a new keytab; ktutil: write_kt /etc/new_krb5.keytab 7. Exit `ktutil`; ktutil: exit 8. Double check the newly created keytab for correctness; # klist-ek /etc/new_krb5.keytab Keytab name: FILE:/etc/new_krb5.keytab KVNO Principal------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96) 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96) 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (camellia128-cts-cmac) 2 host/ipa1.example.local@EXAMPLE.LOCAL (camellia256-cts-cmac)

title: Why is the Multicloud Gateway default backing store stuck in `Initializing` status?
issue: + After installing Openshift Data Foundation (ODF), the default backing store for the MultiCloud Gateway is stuck in `Initializing` status, although its phase is `Ready`. Inspecting some `oc` outputs: # oc get backingstore NAME TYPE PHASE AGE noobaa-default-backing-store aws-s3 Ready 6m58s However: # oc get backingstore noobaa-default-backing-store-o yaml | grep " modeCode:" modeCode: INITIALIZING In a typical scenario, if the backingstore is `Ready`, its mode should have transitioned to `Optimal`. + Why is this issue observed? How to fix it?
resolution: The workaround consists of manually removing the default backing store and letting the MCG operator re-create it. # oc delete backingstore noobaa-default-backing-store This could fail because of two reasons: 1. The backing store is in use (there's a bucket created). The error observed after running the above command will be similar to the following: Error from server: admission webhook "admissionwebhook.noobaa.io" denied the request: cannot complete because pool "noobaa-default-backing-store" in "IN_USE" state In this case, the created bucket will need to be removed. For removing a bucket, please review [Section 10.6 of the Multiclod Gateway Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.11/html/managing_hybrid_and_multicloud_resources/object-bucket-claim#deleting-object-bucket-claims_rhodf) or refer to the documentation of the tool used to create the bucket (`aws`, `s3cmd`, etc). 2. The backing store is the default resource of the `admin` user: Error from server: admission webhook "admissionwebhook.noobaa.io" denied the request: cannot complete because pool "noobaa-default-backing-store" in "DEFAULT_RESOURCE" state In this case, change this default resource to something else. First, list the Noobaa accounts using its CLI. Download the Noobaa CLI [by following these instructions](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.11/html/managing_hybrid_and_multicloud_resources/accessing-the-multicloud-object-gateway-with-your-applications_rhodf#accessing-the-Multicloud-object-gateway-from-the-mcg-command-line-interface_rhodf). Once the CLI is installed, list the accounts by: # noobaa api account list_accounts {} There will be two users with different backing stores: `admin@noobaa.io` with `noobaa-default-backing-store` and `operator@noobaa.io` with `system-internal-storage-pool-63ac16972bf4e40029fe3706` Then, change the default resource for the admin user by running the below command: # noobaa api account update_account_s3_access '{"email": "admin@noobaa.io", "s3_access": true, "default_resource": "system-internal-storage-pool-63ac16972bf4e40029fe3706", "allowed_buckets": {"full_permission": true}}' After that, delete the default backing store: # oc delete backingstore noobaa-default-backing-store backingstore.noobaa.io "noobaa-default-backing-store" deleted It'll be recreated. Once this is completed, return the admin default resource to `noobaa-default-backing-store` like this: # noobaa api account update_account_s3_access '{"email": "admin@noobaa.io", "s3_access": true, "default_resource": "noobaa-default-backing-store"", "allowed_buckets": {"full_permission": true}}'
root_cause: + The backing store creation failed, and it's stuck in an unrecoverable situation. + The Multicloud Gateway internal DB wasn't updated with the backingstore internal node information, and it can't continue with its init.

title: Support Elasticsearch 8 as an output in RHOCP 4
issue: - Needed to send logs to Elasticsearch 8- Not able to send logs from OCP Logging stack to Elasticsearch 8- Failing to deliver logs to Elasticsearch 8 with the error `contains an unknown parameter [_type]` ~~~ $ oc logs-n openshift-logging 2022-04-25 06:24:05 +0000 [warn]: [elasticsearch8] failed to flush the buffer. retry_time=36 next_retry_seconds=2022-04-25 06:25:02 +0000 chunk="5dd7459d6d36c1e0875d29c091e3947f" error_class=Fluent::Plugin::ElasticsearchOutput::RecoverableRequestFailure error="could not push logs to Elasticsearch cluster ({:host=> \"elasticsearch8.example.com\",:port=> 9200,:scheme=> \"https\",:user=> \"user\",:password=> \"obfuscated\"}): [400] {\"error\":{\"root_cause\":[{\"type\":\"illegal_argument_exception\",\"reason\":\"Action/metadata line [1] contains an unknown parameter [_type]\"}],\"type\":\"illegal_argument_exception\",\"reason\":\"Action/metadata line [1] contains an unknown parameter [_type]\"},\"status\":400}" ~~~
resolution: Red Hat reviewed the feature request in RFE [Support Elasticsearch 8 as an output](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-2544).- If the collector type is Fluentd, the feature was implemented in RHOL 5.6.3- If the collector type is Vector, the feature was implemented in RHOL 5.6.0 For being able to log forward to Elasticsearch 8, it needs to define in the `clusterLogForwarder` the version of the Elasticsearch as the example below: ~~~ spec: outputs:- name: es-8 type: elasticsearch elasticsearch: <--- the next two lines version: 8 ~~~ Documentation bug [OCPBUGS-7919](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-7919) was created. For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: For the vector collector, starting in 5.6.0 is supported to log forward to Elasticsearch 8 and for the fluent collector starting in RHOL 5.6.3 is supported to log forward to Elasticsearch 8. In previous versions of the mentioned, it's not supported. Elasticsearch 8 removed the mapping types leading to the error visible in the collector logs.

title: How to make image builds using ubi8-minimal with entitlements
issue: - Use entitlements and `microdnf` in builds from `ubi8-minimal` image.
resolution: > **Note:** This is one possible method to use build with entitlements in `ubi8-minimal`. Refer to the documentation for additional information: [Using Red Hat subscriptions in builds](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/cicd/builds/running-entitled-builds.html).- Download a subscription certificate and a `rhsm.conf` file. Refer to the workaround in [How to run an entitled build on an OCP 4 cluster?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4244451) for additional information.- With the subscription certificate, create a `secret` in the build `namespace`: ~~~ $ oc create secret generic etc-pki-entitlement--from-file=entitlement.pem=./xxxxxxxxxxxxx.pem--from-file=entitlement-key.pem=./xxxxxxxxxxxxx-key.pem ~~~- With the `rhsm.conf` file, create a machine config like this: ~~~ $ cat rhsm.conf | base64-w0 ~~~ ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-rhsmconf spec: config: ignition: version: 2.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,xxxxxx <---- encoded content of former step filesystem: root mode: 0644 path: /etc/rhsm/rhsm.conf ~~~- Apply the machine config and wait for it to be applied in the worker nodes: ~~~ $ oc apply-f rhsmconf.yaml ~~~- Use the following example of `buildconfig` to create an image. Notice that if `rhsm.conf` is found in the nodes, it is automatically mounted in the `pod` under `/run/secrets/rhsm` directory. So, a symbolic link has to be created to have this taken into account. In case your subscriptions include rhel, let's disable the repositories in the ubi8-minimal. ~~~ apiVersion: build.openshift.io/v1 kind: BuildConfig metadata: name: mybuild namespace: testbuild spec: failedBuildsHistoryLimit: 5 nodeSelector: null output: {} postCommit: {} resources: {} runPolicy: Serial source: dockerfile: | FROM registry.redhat.io/ubi8-minimal:latest USER root COPY./etc-pki-entitlement /etc/pki/entitlement RUN ln-s /run/secrets/rhsm /etc RUN microdnf--disablerepo=rhel-8-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms--disablerepo=rhel-8-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms install openssl secrets:- destinationDir: etc-pki-entitlement secret: name: etc-pki-entitlement type: Dockerfile strategy: dockerStrategy: {} type: Docker successfulBuildsHistoryLimit: 5 ~~~ > **Note:** in this case, the `rhsm.conf` file has been created at node level so as not to have to do this in all the namespaces where builds are done.

title: 3Scale Developer Portal behind a Reverse Proxy
issue: We want to setup our 3Scale Developer Portal behind a Apache Reverse Proxy. When we load the Rev. Proxy URL in the browser we get to the Start Page of our Developer Portal, but after Login we get Access Denied. It makes a call to the /session Endpoint and gets a 403 Forbidden. The Login works fine when we use the Openshift Route for the Developer Portal. Additional Info: The same Reverse Proxy- Developer Portal Setup is working fine on our older 3Scale Instance v2.8. We want to have the same setup now on our new 2.12 3Scale Instance. Is there anything that must be additionally configured or are we missing something?
resolution: Check for the_Origin_ header. It needs to be rewritten. Another solution could be to change the Developer Portal URL and create the route manually in OpenShift.
root_cause: Since relese 2.11 of 3scale some security checks have been added related to Cross-Origin requests and most likely the reverse proxy is not rewriting the request headers.

title: Prometheus JMX exporter incorrectly returns both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding response headers for gzip compressed response in JBoss EAP 7 image
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Prometheus JMX exporter incorrectly returns both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding response headers for gzip compressed response in JBoss EAP 7 image. However, [RFC 7230- Section 3.3.2. Content-Length](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230#section-3.3.2) (and also the latest [RFC 9112- Section 6.2. Content-Length](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9112#name-content-length)) expressly forbids returning both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding response headers in a response: ~~~ A sender MUST NOT send a Content-Length header field in any message that contains a Transfer-Encoding header field. ~~~
resolution: - This issue has been reported as [CLOUD-4182](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CLOUD-4182), which will be fixed in future releases.- The same issue has been reported in the upstream issue as, and this has been fixed by this PR- If you can configure a client that send a request to prometheus-jmx-exporter (`localhost:9799/metrics`), do not send a request with the `Accept-Encoding` request header having `gzip`.- Access MicroProfile Metrics subsystem (`localhost:9990/metrics`) instead of prometheus-jmx-exporter (`localhost:9799/metrics`).

title: How to load balance Openwire clients in AMQ 7?
issue: I have 5 Openwire Consumer in the queue connecting to AMQ 7 brokers cluster within Openshift; but checking the AMQ7 console, all consumers only connected to one broker only, even if I restarted the pods it only goes to one broker everytime. The consumers were not distributed or connected to other brokers.
resolution: There are two part of the problems: 1. How to load balance openwire clients in AMQ7? 2. What happen when messages are landed in a broker that does not have any consumers? This KCS will focus the first question: How to Load Balance Openwire Clients in AMQ7? > > Openwire uses failover mechanism to connect to a broker cluster, and when the broker failed, the client will retry to another broker on the URL list. The default of initial broker connection is random and the connection can be unevenly especially when the client are all up trying the connection but not all the brokers are up (recycling the AMQ 7 cluster), as the clients will initially connected to the broker that is available. Solution 1: To have client create a static connection to a specific broker. For example to have 3 consumers with static connection to the broker instead of using failover Say there are 3 consumers and 3 brokers: the consumer 1 will connect to broker 1 the consumer 2 will connect to broker 2 the consumer 3 will connect to broker 3 Solution 2: Use CORE client instead of Openwire, as CORE client By default, AMQ 7 cluster "message-load-balancing" is "ON_DEMAND". That means messages prefer to send to brokers that has consumers. However, in this case the "message-load-balancing" is configured to "OFF_WITH_REDISTRIBUTION", which means "disable load balancing but allow redistribution" but with "redistribution-delay" default to-1 (disable); so potential messages are stuck in broker that has no consumer.

title: OpenShift ingress mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication configuration for client certificates issued by an intermediate CAs and  with CRL configured
issue: - How to configure OpenShift ingress mutual TLS (`mTLS`) authentication for client certificates issued by an `Intermediate CA` and with Certificate Revocation List (`CRL`) configured.
resolution: - To force that OpenShift Ingress Operator downloads the `CRL` issued by the `Intermediate CA`, a dummy certificate which contains this `CRL` must be added to the `CA bundle`.- This second `CRL` is not being downloaded correctly, the `CRL` issued by the `Root CA` is duplicated.- This issue has been reported in [OCPBUGS-9464](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-9464).- The fix for [OCPBUGS-6661](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-6661) might also help to solve the current issue.- The backports to OpenShift 4.13 have been worked in the following issues. The fixes are available as of OpenShift 4.13.3 under [RHSA-2023:3537](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3537):- [mtls CRL not working when using an intermediate CA](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13964)- [CRL configmap is limited by 1MB max, not allowing for multiple public CRLS](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13967)- The backports to OpenShift 4.12 are being worked in the following issues:- [CRL configmap is limited by 1MB max, not allowing for multiple public CRLS. (4.12)](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14454)- [mtls CRL not working when using an intermediate CA (4.12)](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14455)- The backports to OpenShift 4.11 are being worked in the following issues:- [CRL configmap is limited by 1MB max, not allowing for multiple public CRLS. (4.11)](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14456)- [mtls CRL not working when using an intermediate CA (4.11)](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14457)
root_cause: - [OpenShift documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/ingress-operator.html#nw-mutual-tls-auth_configuring-ingress) describes that if the `CA` bundle configured value specifies an `X509v3 certificate revocation list (CRL)` distribution point, the Ingress Operator downloads the `CRL` and configures the Ingress Controller to acknowledge it. Requests that do not provide valid certificates are rejected.- Having the following `CA` hierarchy: `Root CA--> Intermediate CA`:- The `Intermediate CA` is issued by the `Root CA` and may have a `CRL` configured. This `CRL` contains the list of the certificates revoked by the `Root CA`- The client certificates are issued by the `Intermediate CA` and may have a `CRL` configured. This `CRL` contains the list of certificates revoked by the `Intermediate CA`.- Ingress Controller doesn't download the `CRL` issued by the `Intermediate CA` as this `CRL` is not referenced in the configured `CA bundle`.

title: [StackRox] How to upgrade RHACS 3.74 to 4.0
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - To know the exact steps to migrate RHACS `3.74` to `4.0`
resolution: Any already installed `3.y.z` operator is upgradable (via normal means) maximum up to `3.74.z` (where z is the latest available patch number) when the latest `Update` channel is selected. Further on, it will show up as `Up to date` even despite `4.y` versions are available. Users cannot install ACS `4.0` operator from the OperatorHub when `3.y.z` operator is installed. This is also expected: there's no way to have two copies of the RHACS operator on the cluster (irrespective of versions). Here's the `3.y → 4.0` simple upgrade procedure through channel change (recommended). 1. Make sure you have the latest 3.74.z operator installed. If the operator Update approval is configured to be Manual, user needs to approve all updates until they have 3.74.z version and it upgrades ACS Central and/or Secured Cluster Services (whichever is installed).This is basic operator upgrade procedure that should be already documented in ACS docs. This is needed in order to migrate from 3.74 to 4.0 (which is the safest) and not from earlier 3.y versions (which may cause problems). 2. The user needs to take Central database backup.This should be already documented in ACS docs. This is needed for the user to be able to roll back to `3.74` ACS version in case 4.0 goes sideways. 3. Open Subscription for the installed ACS Operator and find the Update channel there. Refer to screenshot `operator.png` attached 4. Click on the channel name and change it from the current value (latest or rhacs-3.74) to stable (recommended) or `rhacs-4.0` (if upgrades beyond 4.0.z are undesirable). Save the change. 5. The operator should start upgrading if the Update approval set to `Automatic`, or the user should approve the upgrade if the Update approval is set to `Manual`. 6. Once the 4.0 operator gets installed, it will upgrade existing ACS Central and Secured Cluster Services (whichever is installed) to its version after some short time. Steps 3-4 from command-line are performed with this command: ``` kubectl-n rhacs-operator patch subscriptions.operators.coreos.com rhacs-operator--type=merge--patch='{"spec": {"channel": "stable"}}' ```

issue: The Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundations Operator fails to upgrade due to the wrong source that is defined in spec. [Redhat-operators catalog fails at some point and finds itself in the staging registry](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7000167) [RHODF Planning Your Deployment Chapter 9. Disconnected environment- Product Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.13/html-single/planning_your_deployment/index#disconnected-environment_rhodf) [RHOCP Chapter 4. Administrator tasks, Section 4.9. Using Operator Lifecycle Manager on restricted networks- Product Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.9/html/operators/administrator-tasks#olm-restricted-networks) If the following resources and product documentation above does not solve your issue, edit the source in the InstallPlan to fix the issue.
resolution: 1. Backup current subscriptions/CSVs: **Example:** ~~~ $ mkdir-p /tmp/subBackup $ oc get sub-n openshift-storage odf-operator-o yaml > odf-operator-sub.out $ oc get csv-n openshift-storage odf-operator.v-rhodf-o yaml > odf-operator-csv.out ~~~ 2. If the ODF has failed the upgrade and this is a disconnected environment, ensure the ODF Operator subscription source(s) defined in spec are pointing towards `redhat-operators`. Two options (CLI or OCP GUI) will be shown below. a. **Option 1:** ~~~ $ oc edit subscription-n openshift-storage odf-operator----- spec: channel: stable-4.12 installPlanApproval: Automatic name: odf-operator source: redhat-operators <----------------------------- Ensure the source reflects redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: odf-operator.v4.12.1------ catalogSourceRef: apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: CatalogSource name: redhat-operators <------------------------- Ensure the source reflects redhat-operators namespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~ B. **Option 2:** Alternatively, navigate to the OCP Console GUI. Click on "Installed Operators"-> "OpenShift Data Foundations." Select the "Actions" dropdown, "Edit Subscription" tab, then proceed to make the changes shown above after clicking on the YAML tab.
root_cause: Previous configurations had different a different source defined in spec and in some cases needs to be manually updated. The new configuration should look as followed: ~~~ $ oc get olm-n openshift-storage------------ NAME PACKAGE SOURCE CHANNEL subscription.operators.coreos.com/mcg-operator mcg-operator redhat-operators stable-4.10 subscription.operators.coreos.com/ocs-operator ocs-operator redhat-operators stable-4.10 subscription.operators.coreos.com/odf-csi-addons-operator-stable-4.10-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace odf-csi-addons-operator redhat-operators stable-4.10 subscription.operators.coreos.com/odf-operator odf-operator redhat-operators stable-4.10 ~~~

title: Creating a Certificate Authority(CA) using NSS
issue: Creating a Certificate Authority(CA) using NSS
resolution: According to Mozilla, Network Security Services(NSS) is a set of libraries desinged to support cross platform development of Security Enabled client and server applications. Example Products that use NSS libraries: Firefox Thunderbird Netscape Browsers Evolution Gaim OpenOffice RHDS Certificate System mod_nss NSS supports certificates of below standard: sslv2 sslv3 PKCS #5 PKCS #7 PKCS #11 (Tokens) PKCS #12 (Files) S/MIME x.509 v3 RHEL5 has 2 sets of security libraries, trational packages like openssl and Mozilla's NSS. x.509,pkcs are standards used in certificates that form the PKI. nss default directory, i.e the directory to store certificates is /etc/pki/nssdb. Unlike openssl where certificates are created and stored in text files. the certificates created by nss-tools are stored in nss database. All certificates and keys are stored in berkelely database. There are 3 major files generally seen in a nss directory are: key3.db, cert8.db and secmod.db * `key3.db file contains a key used to encrypt and decrypt saved passwords` * `cert8.db contains certificates` * `secmod.db contains pathnames of pkcs#11 modules` ### Instruction for CA operations Creating Certificate and key databases. For better understanding we create the below structure of directories to store CA, server and user certificates * /etc/pki/nssdb/CA_db (for storing root CA certificates) * /etc/pki/nssdb/server_db (for storing certificates of servers) * /etc/pki/nssdb/client_db (for storing certificates of users) #### Create a new certificate database CA_db ~~~ $ cd /etc/pki/nssdb $ mkdir CA_db $ certutil-N-d CA_db ~~~ #### Create a Self signed Root CA certificate, specify the subject name ~~~ $ certutil-S-d CA_db-n "gss pnq CA"-s "CN=GSS PNQ CA,O=GSS,L=Pune,ST=Maharashtra,C=IN"-t "CT,,"-x-2 ~~~ **Explanation:**--S (caps) specifies create a individual certificate and add it to the database--d specifies the directory of the nss database (-d. specifies current directory)--n "Name of the certificate"--s "subject" of the certificate or Distinguished Name. (DN)--t "CT,," specifies that this certificate is a Trusted CA which can issue server certficates, and client certificates, ",," specifies uu i.e "CT,u,u", where u specifies certificate can be used for authentication and signing.--x use the certutil tool to generate the signature for certificate being created or added to the database rather than obtaining from separate CA.--2 specifies that add basic constraint extensions, like the certificate can be used to sign specific operations like SSL, object signing, SMIME etc. #### Extract the CA certificate from CA's cert database to a file ~~~ $ certutil-L-d CA_db-n "gss pnq CA"-a-o CA_db/rootca.crt ~~~ #### Display the contents fot the CA's Certificate database. ~~~ $ certutil-L-d./CA_db ~~~ #### Creating Certificates for Servers, For servers SSL servers or clients, Ex: OpenLDAP server using ssl (ldaps), HTTP Server using SSL (HTTPS) ~~~ $ mkdir /etc/pki/nssdb/server_db $ certutil-N-d server_db ~~~ #### Import the new CA certificate in the Server certificate's database and we mark it as trusted CA so that we can issue certificates for SSL Client and server authentication. ~~~ $ certutil-A-d server_db-n "gss pnq CA"-t "TC,,"-a-i CA_db/rootca.crt ~~~ **Explanation:**--A Add an existing certificate to a certificate database.--d server_db (directory of certificate database)--t "TC", specifies that this certificate is a Trusted CA which can issue server certficates, and client certificates, ",," specifies uu i.e "CT,u,u", where u specifies certificate can be used--a is ascii format--i input-file #### Create the server certificate request, specifying the subject name for the server certificate. We make the common name (CN) be identical to the hostname of the server. ~~~ $ certutil-R-d server_db-s "CN=dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com,O=GSS,L=Pune,ST=Maharashtra,C=IN"-a-o server_db/dhcp208-219.req-v 12 ~~~ **Explanation:**- The above generates certificate for host dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com, For better identification and understanding we specify Organization, Location, State, and Country--R Create a request file, that can be submitted to CA for signing the cert--d directory where certificate database exists--s subject of the certificate or DN--a ascii--o output file #### Sign the Certificate from CA, and issues a new certificate in ascii format ~~~ $ certutil-C-d CA_db-c "gss pnq CA"-a-i server_db/dhcp208-219.req-o server_db/dhcp208-219.crt-2-6 ~~~ #### Import (Add) the new server certificate to the server's certificate database in the server_db directory with the appropriate nickname ~~~ $ certutil-A-d server_db-n dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com-a-i server_db/dhcp208-219.crt-t ",," ~~~ #### Verify the certificate ~~~ $ certutil-V-d server_db-u V-n dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com ~~~ #### Creating certificates for Uses/Clients ~~~ $ mkdir /etc/pki/nssdb/client_db $ cd /etc/pki/nsssdb ~~~ #### Import the new CA certificate in the Server certificate's database and we mark it as trusted CA so that we can issue certificates for SSL Client and server authentication. ~~~ $ certutil-A-d server_db-n "gss pnq CA"-t "TC,,"-a-i CA_db/rootca.crt ~~~ #### Create a client certificate request, Specifying the subject name of the certificate ~~~ $ certutil-R-d client_db-s "CN=Joe Client,O=GSS,L=Pune,ST=Maharashtra,C=US"-a-o client_db/client.req-v 12 ~~~ #### Sign the certificate request by CA "gss pnq CA' ~~~ $ certutil-C-d CA_db-c "gss pnq CA"-a-i client_db/client.req-o client_db/client.crt ~~~ #### Add the certificate to the client nss database ~~~ $ certutil-A-d client_db-n "Joe Client"-a-i client_db/client.crt-t ",," ~~~ #### View the client certificate ~~~ $ certutil-L-d client_db-n "Joe Client" ~~~ #### Verifying the certificates To verify the server certificates ~~~ $ certutil-V-d server_db-u V-n dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com ~~~ To verify the client certificates ~~~ $ certutil-V-d client_db-u C-n "joe Client" ~~~ By default the certificates that have been created using the above procedure are in pkcs12 standard. To use the certificates on Applications, You would require the following 1. RooCA's Certificate (public key) 2. Server Certificate (Certificate and key). The Server's participating in SSL communication should have the certificates and key file nss-tools comes with pk12util command, pk12util is a pkcs\#12 Tool allowing to share certificates. This tool supports importing certificates and keys from pkcs \#12 files in to NSS or export them and also list certificates and keys in such files. #### Exporting the Server certifcate dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com in to a file dhcp208-219.pk12 ~~~ $ pk12util-d.-o dhcp208-219.pk12-n dhcp208-219.gsslab.pnq.redhat.com ~~~ The Above dhcp208-219.pk12 file has both the certificate and the key file encrypted. #### For Applications which require certificate and key file to be in pem format we can use Openssl command to convert the file from.p12 to pem format. ~~~ $ openssl pkcs12-clcerts-nokeys-in dhcp209-88.pk12-out dhcp209-88.pem ~~~ The above says that the standard of the input certificate is pkcs12, and export only client certificates (not CA certficates), `-nokeys` (do not output any private keys) So dhcp209-88.pem will contain only the certficate in pem format. PkCS12 certs have their private keys encrypted with pass phrase. When exporting the keys, You might want the key to be accessed without a passphrase. ~~~ $ openssl pkcs12-nocerts-in dhcp209-88.pk12-out dhcp209-88-key.pem-nodes ~~~
root_cause: - There are multiple ways with Red Hat Enterprise Linux to set up a Certificate Authority it can also be done with [openssl](/solutions/202293)

title: Is it possible to install different versions of the Ansible Automation Platform Operator in different namespaces of the same cluster?
issue: - Best way to install the `Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform operator` in two different namespaces on the same openshift cluster.- Is it possible to install `Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform operator` in two different/distinct namespaces?
resolution: - It is not possible. Whereas it can be possible to install two ` Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform operator` in the same cluster, but they must be having the same version. There can be some benefits to doing this, namely, there will be a dedicated operator pod per namespace (so separate reconciliation loop logs).- It is not advised to install separate versions of the `Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform operator` though, this is because the CRD schemas between the two versions may not be compatible, which will result in one of those operators failing during install.

title: How to allow traffic on all targets except an IP and port combination using NetworkPolicyEgressRule
issue: - `NetworkPolicyEgressRule` fails for the combination of ports and `ipBlock`/`except`.
resolution: - For example, to allow all egress communication to all targets on all ports except `10.10.xx.10:9090`, use the below. ~~~ [...] spec: egress:- to:- ipBlock: cidr: 0.0.0.0/0 except:- 10.10.xx.10/32 policyTypes:- Egress [...] ~~~ ~~~ [...] spec: egress:- ports:- endPort: 9899 port: 1 protocol: TCP- endPort: 65535 port: 9901 protocol: TCP policyTypes:- Egress [...] ~~~
root_cause: - The network policies are additive. Hence, we need to add two separate objects to achieve the requirement.- All the ports should be specified in the NetPol except the one it needs to be restricted.

title: How to delete stale objects from etcd db?
issue: - How to delete stale resources from `etcd` db?- Delete objects from the etcd db directly
resolution: - To remove any stale resource from the `etcd` db first try out to delete it with CLI: ~~~ $ oc delete ~~~- Check if any finalizers are there in the resource in the annotations section.- Try to forcefully delete it: ~~~ $ oc delete--force--grace-period=0 ~~~- If the above does not help delete if from `etcd` db by identifying the resources. Take the remote shell of the running `etcd` pod: ~~~ $ oc rsh etcd-master-0.example.com ~~~- Search for the resource. For example, a `route` in a `test_project` project is stuck in a terminating state: ~~~ # etcdctl get--prefix /--keys-only | grep test_project | grep-i route ~~~- Delete the object: ~~~ # etcdctl del /openshift.io/routes/test_project/httpd // httpd here is the name of the route. ~~~
root_cause: - Sometimes removing objects from the CLI or UI does not remove it from `etcd` db and can cause issues.

title: OpenShift Logging ClusterLogForwarder containing dots ',' or slashes '/' in the label set in structuredTypeKey are not stored in separate indices
issue: After the update of the OpenShift Logging stack to version 5.6.5 and newer log messages are not landing in the specific index set in structuredTypeKey in the `ClusterLogForwarder`
root_cause: Before the update to [OpenShift Logging 5.6.5](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/logging/cluster-logging-release-notes.html#openshift-logging-5-6-5-bug-fixes), the template definitions prevented Elasticsearch from indexing some labels and namespace_labels, causing issues with data ingestion. With this update, the fix replaces dots and slashes in labels to ensure proper ingestion, effectively resolving the issue.

title: During Openshift migration of version 3 to 4 ,AWS EC2 instance profile unable to asumme role
issue: - In the ongoing migration from OCP3 to OCP4, the EC2 instance profile ROLE has been assigned to the new EC2 Worker/compute OCP4 nodes. However, attempts to assume the role have been unsuccessful.- While migrating from version 3 to 4 of Openshift, the AWS EC2 instance profile encounters difficulty in assuming the role.
resolution: - The encountered error is associated with the need for additional capabilities to access the hostNetwork within the EC2 Instances during the migration from OCP3 to OCP4. Referring to the [OpenShift documentation] (https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/networking/understanding-networking.html), the solution involved adding "spec.hostNetwork = true" to the pods, resulting in the successful resolution of the issue. ~~~ spec.hostNetwork = true ~~~
root_cause: - Because of new capabilities added to Openshift, CIDR block is not reachable from the pod network. Pods that need access to these IP addresses must be given host network access by setting the spec.hostNetwork field in the pod spec to true.

title: Why is the error message 'WARNING: Unable to login as "OCFMON", using "sysdba" user instead' observed in the log
issue: Error message 'WARNING: Unable to login as "OCFMON", using "sysdba" user instead' is periodically getting logged into log files
resolution: in case your 'monuser' password 'monpassword' contains special characters, wrap it in single quotes ''' in order to be correctly interpreted
root_cause: The issue stems from configuring an Oracle instance within a Pacemaker cluster using a password which includes special characters and that isn't wrapped in single quotes. It results in persistent, unsuccessful login attempts by the OCFMON user. These occur each time the system schedules a monitoring operation, which not only fills up the logs but also causes the Oracle DB to record every sysdba login attempt internally. This has the potential to lead to failures in monitoring operations against a live DB, especially when the allocated space for Oracle's log directory becomes exhausted. How does the monitor operation check status of the DB? ~~~ # instance in OPEN state? instance_live() {local status=`monsql_one dbstat` //which calls runsql "connect \"$MONUSR\"/\"$MONPWD\"" $* dbstat ["$status" = OPEN] && return 0 ocf_log warn "Unable to login as \"$MONUSR\", using \"sysdba\" user instead" status=`dbasql_one dbstat` //which calls runsql "connect / as sysdba" $* dbstat if ["$status" = OPEN]; then return 0 else ocf_log info "$ORACLE_SID instance state is not OPEN (dbstat output: $status)" return 1 fi} ~~~ from instance_live() it runs runsql query and dbstat, what does runsql do? ~~~ runsql() {local conn_s="$1" shift 1 local func (echo "$conn_s" common_sql_opts for func; do $func; done) | execsql | common_sql_filter} ~~~ runsql calls execsql and sends its output to pipe for common_sql_filter ~~~ execsql() {if ["$US" = "$ORACLE_OWNER"]; then sqlplus-S /nolog else su- $ORACLE_OWNER-s /bin/sh-c ". $ORA_ENVF; sqlplus-S /nolog" fi} ~~~ sqlplus-S /nolog opens up sql prompt without establishing connection to the database yet output is sent to common sql filter, that filters away some of the stdout the prompt opening may produce ~~~ common_sql_filter() {grep-v '^Connected' | grep-v '^ENV MSG:' | grep-v 'Your password will expire in'} ~~~ afterwards the connection is established using one of the commands: ~~~ "connect \"$MONUSR\"/\"$MONPWD\"" or "connect / as sysdba" ~~~ and afterwards, dbstat is passed to the database, what does dbstat do? ~~~ dbstat() {echo 'select status from v$instance;'} ~~~ which in reality should produce the following type of output: ~~~ SQL> select STATUS from v$instance; STATUS------------ OPEN ~~~ from this we are tailing the last line = OPEN and storing it in 'status' variable. ~~~ status=`monsql_one dbstat` status=`dbasql_one dbstat` monsql_one() {monsql $* | tail-1} dbasql_one() {dbasql $* | tail-1} ~~~ and that is where we get the 'OPEN' for the IF statement from if ["$status" = OPEN]; then return 0

title: Network performance impact on OpenShift Container Platform 4 when configure IPsec with OVN-Kubernetes network plugin
issue: While evaluating `OVN-Kubernetes` we also enabled `IPsec` to secure traffic between nodes and found that once `IPsec` is enabled, we only achieve about 1/4 of the throughput vs. when `IPsec` is actually disabled. Can you please help us understand why this is (some impact is expected but not that much).

We have enabled `IPsec` encryption for `OVN` following [Configuring IPsec encryption](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/ovn_kubernetes_network_provider/configuring-ipsec-ovn.html). Afterwards, network bandwidth tests with `iperf` showed a heavy impact on the network performance.
Without ipsec: `~8Gbit/sec`
With ipsec: `~2Gbit/sec`
resolution: * When using [configuring IPsec encryption](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/ovn_kubernetes_network_provider/configuring-ipsec-ovn.html) with `OVN-Kubernetes` some network throughput degradation must be expected due to the additional overhead introduced by the traffic encryption and the fact that `IPSec` is CPU bound (meaning the CPU doing the encapsulation may become the bottleneck). * Network throughput with [configuring IPsec encryption](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/ovn_kubernetes_network_provider/configuring-ipsec-ovn.html) therefore mostly depends on the available CPU of the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node, network card offloading capabilities but as well on the MTU site applied and the datagram size being used. Tuning this according to the workload can greatly increase throughput to the extend possible. With various different application running on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4, such tuning becomes more difficult and therefore sensible defaults needs to be evaluated based on benchmark tests being done on the available Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Cluster.

title: HPE ProLiant servers crash due to fatal MCE upon shutting down Broadcom NetXreme Gigabit ethernet device running with bnxt_en driver
product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux for x86_64
issue: + HPE ProLiant servers crash due to fatal MCE upon shutting down Broadcom NetXreme Gigabit ethernet device running with bnxt_en driver ~~~ [383.929302] core: [Hardware Error]: CPU 0: Machine Check Exception: 5 Bank 6: bb80000000000e0b [383.929303] core: [Hardware Error]: RIP!INEXACT! 10: {intel_idle+0x6b/0xb0} [383.929304] core: [Hardware Error]: TSC 140d3b93d02 MISC 36000000 PPIN f5929bf1518b4cf [383.929306] core: [Hardware Error]: PROCESSOR 0:50657 TIME 1668500650 SOCKET 0 APIC 0 microcode 5003302 [383.929307] core: [Hardware Error]: Run the above through 'mcelog--ascii' [383.929307] core: [Hardware Error]: Machine check: Processor context corrupt [383.929308] Kernel panic- not syncing: Fatal machine check ~~~ + iLO Integrated Management Log (IML) may display either one or both of the following: ~~~ Uncorrectable Machine Check Exception (Processor 1, APIC ID 0x00000000,Bank 0x00000006, Status 0xBB800000'00000E0B, Address 0x00000000'00000000,Misc 0x00000000'11100000). Uncorrectable PCI Express Error Detected. Slot 3 (Segment 0x0, Bus 0x13,Device 0x0, Function 0x1). Uncorrectable Error Status: 0x100000 ~~~
resolution: HPE suggests that, to prevent this issue, you need to update to [HPE Broadcom NetXtreme-E Drivers for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 version: 1.10.2-219.0.55.0(B)](https://support.hpe.com/connect/s/softwaredetails?language=en_US&softwareId=MTX_579d5cde4cef4d108f24a326ff) or later. ### Workaround + HPE suggests that, as a workaround, disable RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) as follows: + Edit /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/90-rdma-hw-modules.rules + Comment out the line to auto load bnxt_re #ENV{ID_NET_DRIVER}=="bnxt_en", RUN{built-in}+="kmod load bnxt_re" + Save the modification, type "sync" to flash the change, and type "reboot" to reboot.
root_cause: + Unknown + Our engineering team is currently workin on one of our BZs, [BZ#2154168 – The kernel crashes when it's shutting down due to the fatal MCE caused by some possible bug in the inbox bnxt_en driver](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2154168) to identify the root cause to find out the resolution.

title: Is there any way to further lock down anonymous access except system:authenticated users
issue: - The main issue is the lack of granular access control in the current Openshift authentication and authorization model.- OIDC-authenticated users are able to log on to OCP clusters without specific authorizations, which raises security concerns and poses compliance and audit challenges.- Can "system:authenticated" users, without any additional RBAC or modifications to ClusterRoleBindings, cause harm to an Openshift cluster?- Should users in the "system:authenticated" group, without any additional RBAC, be considered a potential security risk to an Openshift cluster?
resolution: - To restrict more users we can change the Default ClusterRoleBinding system:authenticated to system:unauthenticated groups which help allows read-only access to non-sensitive information about the cluster. [+] https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#auto-reconciliation [+] https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#discovery-roles ~~~ Also, We can use change the role of `watcher` it will restrict more. # oc adm policy add-role-to-user ROLE (USER |-z SERVICEACCOUNT) [USER...] [flags] [options] ~~~- To minimal or no privileges for system:authenticated-only users. The objective is to achieve a more secure environment by restricting the actions and access available to these users. One possible solution is to utilize the "view" and "watcher" roles. By adding the "watch" role to a specific user (e.g., "testuser") using the following command: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-role-to-user watch "testuser" clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/watch added: "testuser" ~~~- Can "system:authenticated" users, without any additional RBAC or modifications to ClusterRoleBindings, cause harm to an Openshift cluster? "system:authenticated" is a special group in OpenShift that includes all authenticated users, including both human users and service accounts.- Should users in the "system:authenticated" group, without any additional RBAC, be considered a potential security risk to an Openshift cluster? By default, "system:authenticated" users have no permissions on the cluster, which means they cannot do any damage to the cluster without additional permissions or roles. However, being a member of "system:authenticated" group does not necessarily mean that a user is not a security risk. If a user's credentials are compromised, for example, an attacker could potentially use those credentials to gain access to the cluster and carry out malicious activities. It is always important to practice good security hygiene, such as using strong passwords, enabling two-factor authentication, and limiting access to only those who need it. Additionally, implementing RBAC and setting appropriate ClusterRoleBindings can help to further restrict the actions that "system:authenticated" users can perform, and reduce the potential attack surface of the cluster

title: ArgoCD keeps on deleting secret in Openshift
issue: - A secret called v4-0-config-user-idp-0-client-secret keeps getting created by OpenShift and subsequently deleted by ArgoCD, so the two are fighting over the existence of that resource.
resolution: - To prevent an object from being pruned, make below mentioned changes: ~~~ metadata: annotations: argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false ~~~- Here's an example of how it would look for a Deployment resource: ~~~ apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: annotations: argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false spec:... ~~~- Add the annotations section as a sibling to the name field in the metadata section of resource definition file.
root_cause: - Users have the ability to personalize certain aspects of the synchronization process in Argo CD for the desired state in the target cluster. Certain synchronization options can be specified as annotations in a particular resource. The majority of synchronization options are set up in the spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions attribute of the Application resource. Multiple synchronization options can be combined using the argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options annotation, with commas used to separate them and any whitespace being automatically removed.

title: openshift4/ose-jenkins-agent-base node images v4.10 not able to communicate with openshift4/ose-jenkins v4.10.0
issue: - Node is not able to connect to controller using JRE 11 by default and getting below mentioned error: ~~~ Exception in thread "main" java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: hudson/remoting/jnlp/Main has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 55.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 52.0 ~~~
resolution: - Update cluster to version 4.10.62 or above.
root_cause: - The error occurs because the Java Runtime version on the agent node is outdated compared to the one used to compile the Jenkins remoting jar file. The remoting jar file was compiled with class file version 55.0, corresponding to Java 11, which the agent node cannot recognize since it only supports class file versions up to 52.0, equivalent to Java 8.- Verified bug as mentioned in https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14279

title: Understanding the Need for a Bastion Host in RHOCP 4.
resolution: Bastion hosts play a crucial role in enhancing the security and management of OpenShift clusters. Bastion hosts are necessary components and the benefits they provide in an OpenShift environment are listed below: Importance of Bastion Hosts in OpenShift:- Security Enhancement:- Isolation: Bastion hosts isolate the master nodes from the public internet, safeguarding them from unauthorized access and potential security threats.- Simplified Management:- Convenience: Bastion hosts offer a streamlined approach to managing the master nodes. They enable administrators to execute commands, perform software updates, and restart services efficiently.- Scalability:- Cluster Expansion: As OpenShift clusters grow with additional master nodes, bastion hosts can be easily scaled out to provide secure access to the expanding infrastructure.- Conclusion:- Understanding the significance of bastion hosts in OpenShift is essential for ensuring the security and effective management of clusters. By implementing bastion hosts, organizations can bolster their OpenShift environment's resilience and mitigate potential risks.

title: Openshift 4 upgrade failes due to missing allowed registry
issue: - Samples Operator degraded because it's trying to pull an image from a forbidden registry.
resolution: 1. Check the samples operators messages ~~~ $ oc get co openshift-samples-oyaml ~~~ ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterOperator metadata: name: openshift-samples [...] status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: '2021-09-27T11:22:48Z' message: 'error creating samples: ImageStream.image.openshift.io "dotnet-runtime" is invalid: [spec.tags[5.0].from.name: Forbidden: registry "registry.access.redhat.com" # <-- Blocked Registry not allowed by whitelist: "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000", "default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.example.com", "quay.io:443", "registry.redhat.io:443", spec.tags[5.0-ubi8].from.name: Forbidden: registry "registry.access.redhat.com" not allowed by whitelist: "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000", "default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.example.com", "quay.io:443", "registry.redhat.io:443"];' reason: APIServerInvalidError status: 'True' type: Degraded ~~~ Note that the operator is degraded because its trying to pull from registry `registry.access.redhat.com` which is not in the cluster allowed registries 2. Add the missing registry to the image configuration. ~~~ $ oc patch image.config.openshift.io cluster--type=merge-p \ '{"spec": {"allowedRegistriesForImport": [{"domainName": "registry.access.redhat.com","insecure": false},{"domainName": "registry.connect.redhat.com","insecure": false}],"registrySources": {"allowedRegistries": ["registry.access.redhat.com","registry.connect.redhat.com"]}}}' ~~~ **Note: This action will cause a reboot of all cluster nodes.**
root_cause: - The tag `3.1-ubi8` in image stream `dotnet-runtime`is based on an image from registry `` which is not in the cluster's allowed list. ~~~ $ oc get is dotnet-runtime-n openshift-oyaml ~~~ ~~~ apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: dotnet-runtime namespace: openshift spec: lookupPolicy: local: false tags: [...]- from: kind: DockerImage name: registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/dotnet-31-runtime:3.1 # <-- Source Image Registry generation: 2 importPolicy: {} name: 3.1-ubi8 referencePolicy: type: Local ~~~

Clone cluster capacity git repo ~~~ cd $GOPATH/src/sigs.k8s.io git clone https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-capacity ~~~ **Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. 10. Build cluster capacity tool ~~~ $ cd cluster-capacity/ $ make ~~~ The following is the healthy builld output ~~~ which: no golangci-lint in (/home/user/go/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/sbin:/home/user/bin) GO111MODULE=auto go build-o hypercc sigs.k8s.io/cluster-capacity/cmd/hypercc ln-sf hypercc cluster-capacity ln-sf hypercc genpod ~~~ 11. Verify Cluster Capacity tool was built correctly by displaying its help menu ~~~ $ ~/goapps/src/sigs.k8s.io/cluster-capacity/cluster-capacity-h Cluster-capacity simulates an API server with initial state copied from the Kubernetes enviroment with its configuration specified in KUBECONFIG. If the--max-limits flag is not specified, pods are scheduled until the simulated API server runs out of resources. Usage: cluster-capacity--kubeconfig KUBECONFIG--podspec PODSPEC [flags] Flags:--default-config string Path to JSON or YAML file containing scheduler configuration.--exclude-nodes strings Exclude nodes to be scheduled-h,--help help for cluster-capacity--kubeconfig string Path to the kubeconfig file to use for the analysis.--max-limit int Number of instances of pod to be scheduled after which analysis stops. One of: json|yaml (Note: output is not versioned or guaranteed to be stable across releases).--podspec string Path to JSON or YAML file containing pod definition.--verbose Verbose mode ~~~ 12. title: Router pods going into CrashLoopBackOff state and restarting frequently after replacing the default ingress certificate in RHOCP 4
issue: - After replacing the default ingress certificate, the router pods are not coming up healthy: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-ingress NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE router-default-7bcb8c489b-94vjf 0/1 Running 221 19h router-default-7bcb8c489b-kvl72 0/1 Running 205 17h ~~~
resolution: - Take a fresh private key, try to create a new TLS secret, and patch the `ingresscontroller/default` as per the [Replacing the default ingress certificate](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/security/certificates/replacing-default-ingress-certificate.html).
root_cause: - The private key was mismatched with its formatting.- The private key of a `PKCS#8` certificate in PEM form, which should begin and end with `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY and END PRIVATE KEY`, respectively, are accidentally posing as a `PKCS#1` certificate, by beginning and ending with `BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY and END RSA PRIVATE KEY`.- The config check will fail and the daemon will not start, and the error message provided is misleading: `unable to load certificate chain from file`.- The problem in this particular scenario isn't to do with the wildcard certificate chain.- HaProxy router pods will have better logging in the near future to provide hints regarding the issue.

title: Unable to delete namespace in RHOCP 4
issue: - Regeneration of `crd` post deleting it successfully.- Unable to delete `apiservice` and `crd` from namespace.- Deletion of `namespace` is stuck due to present `crd` and `apiservice`. ~~~ status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: "2023-06-21T10:06:16Z" message: 'Discovery failed for some groups, 4 failing: unable to retrieve the complete list of server APIs: actions.kio.kasten.io/v1alpha1: the server is currently unable to handle the request, apps.kio.kasten.io/v1alpha1: the server is currently unable to handle the request, repositories.kio.kasten.io/v1alpha1: the server is currently unable to handle the request, vault.kio.kasten.io/v1alpha1: the server is currently unable to handle the request' ~~~
resolution: - Remove configured `finalizers` from `crd` yaml, follow below steps: ~~~ # oc edit crd k10s.apik10.kasten.io-oyaml-n kasten-io finalizers:- customresourcecleanup.apiextensions.k8s.io ~~~- Set finalizers as below and save it. ~~~ finalizers:[] ~~~- Post above changes try to delete `crd` again, if crd still present. ~~~ # oc delete crd k10s.apik10.kasten.io-n kasten-io--force ~~~
root_cause: - In the `crd k10s.apik10.kasten.io` there is configured `finalizers customresourcecleanup.apiextensions.k8s.io`. ~~~ finalizers:- customresourcecleanup.apiextensions.k8s.io ~~~

title: Noobaa backing store creation fails with message: Connect(): SecretOp not found
issue: - The noobaa bucket was not accessible from application, and we found on `noobaa-core` logs errors like: Jun-6 10:15:10.280 [WebServer/41] [L0] core.server.node_services.nodes_monitor:: noobaa-default-backing-store-noobaa-pod-a7497595-noobaa_storage-efaecb77 item has issues. reasons: node offline, storage is full (Thu Jan 01 1970 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time))- [Duplicated message. Suppressing for 30 seconds]- As data on Noobaa was not relevant it was decided to reinstall Noobaa, so deleted all noobaa resources (following an internal procedure, you can contact with Red Hat Support) to start from scratch the installation of Noobaa.- As this is a Red Hat Quay on OCP 4.11, in order to install Noobaa we are following steps: [3.2.2.1.1. Create A Standalone Object Gateway](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_quay/3.6/html/deploy_red_hat_quay_on_openshift_with_the_quay_operator/operator-preconfigure#create_a_standalone_object_gateway)- We failed to create a backing store type `pv-pool`, it remain in `Connecting` with this error 'Connect(): SecretOp not found'
resolution: - When deleting noobaa resources, make sure to delete PVs used by `noobaa-db-pg-0` and `noobaa-backingstore` pods. ~~~ # oc delete pv pv_name ~~~- In case these are local storage devices, wipe out the disk devices too, from the OCS node where the local disk is attached, run: ~~~ # sgdisk--zap-all /dev/sd ~~~ **Note.** Deploying noobaa via the CLI is NOT supported for ODF (with command: `noobaa install`), please use only supported methods.
root_cause: - The PVs used by `noobaa-db-pg-0` and `noobaa-backingstore` pods has the `RECLAIM POLICY` set to Retain: ~~~ NAME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES RECLAIM POLICY STATUS CLAIM STORAGECLASS REASON AGE db-noobaa-db-pg-0 50Gi RWO Retain Bound openshift-storage/db-noobaa-db-pg-0 noprovisioner 15m noobaa-backingstore 50Gi RWO Retain Available noprovisioner 14m ~~~- Please make sure that the PV is deleted, before redeploying

title: How to use Group Sync Operator with Azure Active Directory
issue: How to synchronize Azure Active Directory groups and users after configuring the authentication in OpenShift
resolution: To set up group synchronization from Azure AD to OCP/ARO/ROSA you must:- Define groups and assign users in Azure AD- Add the required API permissions to the app registration in Azure AD- Install the Group Sync Operator from the OpenShift Operator Hub- Create and configure a new Group Sync instance- Set a synchronization schedule- Test the synchronization process **Define groups and assign users in Azure AD** To synchronize groups and users with OpenShift they must exist in **Azure AD** **Add API Permissions to Azure AD App Registration** The `GroupSync` job requires some permissions on the **Azure AD**, for it to work, add the following entries: ~~~ Group.Read.All GroupMember.Read.All User.Read.All ~~~ **Install the Group Sync Operator from the OpenShift Operator Hub** 1. In the **OpenShift Operator Hub** find the **Group Sync Operator** 2. Install the operator in the `group-sync-operator` namespace **Create and configure a new Group Sync instance** Create a new secret named `azure-group-sync` in the `group-sync-operator` namespace. For this you will need the following values: `AZURE_TENANT_ID` `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` Using the `OpenShift CLI`, create the secret using the following format: ~~~ oc create secret generic azure-group-sync \--from-literal=AZURE_TENANT_ID= \--from-literal=AZURE_CLIENT_ID= \--from-literal=AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET= ~~~ 3. Create a new `Group Sync` instance in the `group-sync-operator` namespace: 4. Replace de default configuration with the example below, customizing the YAML to match the group names and saving the configuration: Sample YAML: ~~~ apiVersion: redhatcop.redhat.io/v1alpha1 kind: GroupSync metadata: name: azure-groupsync namespace: group-sync-operator spec: providers:- name: azure azure: credentialsSecret: name: azure-group-sync namespace: group-sync-operator groups:- admin- development- viewer prune: false schedule: '*/5 * * * *' ~~~ **Set a synchronization schedule** The **Group Sync Operator** provides a `cron` based scheduling parameter for specifying how often the users and groups should be synchronized. In the previous example, the schedule value is `“*/5 * * * *”`, syncing every five minutes. **Testing the synchronization process** Check to see if the `Group Sync` process has been completed with a `Condition: ReconcileSuccess` message.

Capture the current configuration: ~~~ $ NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph config get osd bdev_enable_discard--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring ~~~ ~~~ $ NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph config get osd bdev_async_discard--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring ~~~ **Example Output:** ~~~ $ ceph config get osd bdev_enable_discard false <--------------------- $ ceph config get osd bdev_async_discard false <--------------------- ~~~ 2. title: How does weighting work in load balancing for A/B testing
issue: The documentation states that the `weight` for a service can be "between 0 and 256". How does this correlate to the portion of requests sent to each service in the route?
root_cause: By default, a route will have one service defined under `.spec.to`. Up to 3 additional services can be defined under `.spec.alternateBackends` for a total of 4 services per route. Each service can be assigned a `weight` between 0 and 256. When the `weight` is `0`, the service does not participate in load-balancing but continues to serve existing persistent connections. When the `weight` is greater than `0`, it's value is evenly distributed amongst all the service’s endpoints so that the sum of the endpoint weights is the `service_weight`. The minimum weight for each endpoint is 1, which can lead to a situation where a service with a lot of endpoints can end up with a `service_weight` that is higher than the specified `weight`. In this case, reduce the number of endpoint pods to get the expected load balance weight. The portion of requests to each service is calculated by taking the `service_weight` described above and dividing it by the `sum_of_weights` which, as its name describes, is the sum of all the `weight` values defined for each of the services.

title: IBM Cloud Pak  works intermittently with Application Not Available message
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - `IBM Cloud Pak` works intermittently- Some of the scripts fails to load on `Chrome` browser with `503` errors- ANA (Application Not Available) error with `Chrome` browser
resolution: - Increase the `Memory Request` and `Limit` to accommodate the requirements- Optimize the `APIC NGINX` pods to use less `worker` processes so it will better fit within the `Memory Limits` already in place
root_cause: After a deep analyzing `APIC` pods was identified as pods reaching the memory resource limits. This is reported in the `APIC Pod Logs` as a `worker` killed by `Signal 9 (SIGKILL: Fast Termination of Linux Container)`. Because this `APIC` worker process was part of the `TLS Establishment` process, this fails, propagating the failure up to the `ibm-nginx-svc` pod, which records this as `Unexpected close of connection`. The `ibm-nginx-svc` then terminates the connection to the `OpenShift Router (HAProxy)` unexpectedly, which is causing `HAProxy` to mark the `backend` as unhealthy and disconnect it. Once all `ibm-ngin-svc` pods are reported as down by `HAProxy` it will return a simple `Application Not Available` for all current and future requests until it see's the `backend` has returned. Important:- The `Pods` never terminate, but the `NGINX` sub-processes are re-spawned.- The termination of the `workers` is not killing `PID 1` inside the `APIC` pods, so `OpenShift` does not show anything in it's event logs. Instead, it is being reported by `APIC NGINX Manager` through it's logs as `worker` killed by `Signal 9`- `HAProxy` is working as designed
