title: Openshift machines stuck in deleting phase OCP 4
issue: - How to delete the machines stuck in Deleting phase?- Is it possible to manually delete the machines stuck into deleting phase when the associated machineset is already deleted?- Not able to delete machines in Deleting phase with error logs: ~~~ 2021-11-16T14:44:32.188514003Z I1116 14:44:32.188483 1 controller.go:218] ocp-tst-infra-eu-west-1a-123lnk: reconciling machine triggers delete 2021-11-16T14:44:32.188514003Z I1116 14:44:32.188500 1 actuator.go:159] ocp-tst-infra-eu-west-1a-123lnk: actuator deleting machine 2021-11-16T14:44:32.189159864Z E1116 14:44:32.189140 1 actuator.go:69]ocp-tst-infra-eu-west-1a-123lnk error: ocp-tst1-c8k5c-infra-eu-west-1a-64lnk: failed to create scope for machine: failed to create aws client: region "eu-west-1a" not resolved: UnknownEndpointError: could not resolve endpoint 2021-11-16T14:44:32.189245997Z I1116 14:44:32.189234 1 actuator.go:104] ocp-tst-infra-eu-west-1a-123lnk: actuator checking if machine exists 2021-11-16T14:44:32.189352263Z I1116 14:44:32.189328 1 recorder.go:104] controller-runtime/manager/events "msg"="Warning" "message"="ocp-tst-infra-eu-west-1a-123lnk: failed to create scope for machine: failed to create aws client: region \"eu-west-1a\" not resolved: UnknownEndpointError: could not resolve endpoint\n\tpartition: \"all partitions\", service: \"ec2\", region: \"eu-west-1a\"" "object"={"kind":"Machine","namespace":"openshift-machine-api","name":"ocp-tst-infra-eu-west-1a-123lnk","uid":"ab123-c456-d7801d4b9a","apiVersion":"machine.openshift.io/v1beta1","resourceVersion":"17791341"} "reason"="FailedDelete" ~~~
resolution: Follow the Diagnostic Steps section and ensure that there are no underlying nodes or virtual machines (VM) attached to the machine(s). Once confirmed, it's safe to remove the orphaned Machine object manually by removing the Finalizers from the machine Object. Below are the steps to be followed to manually delete it: 1. Get/export raw JSON for the machine Object: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api get--raw /apis/machine.openshift.io/v1beta1/namespaces/openshift-machine-api/machines/ > tmp.json ~~~ 2. Edit the tmp.json file exported in step 1 and remove the finalizer from the raw JSON. For example: remove the highlighted Finalizer section ***"finalizers":["machine.machine.openshift.io"]*** ~~~ {"apiVersion":"machine.openshift.io/v1beta1","kind":"Machine","metadata":{"annotations":{"machine.openshift.io/instance-state":"poweredOn"},"creationTimestamp":"2021-12-06T01:15:59Z",***"finalizers":["machine.machine.openshift.io"],***"generateName":"ocp-test-a1bc2d4-worker-eu-west-1a-xyz","generation":2,"labels":{"machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-cluster":"ocp-test-a1bc2d4-worker-eu-west-1a-xyz","machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role":"worker","machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-type":"worker","machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machineset":"ocp-test-a1bc2d4-worker-eu-west-1a-xyz","machine.openshift.io/region":"","machine.openshift.io/zone":""}...}}} ~~~ 3. In one terminal, start a proxy to the API server: ~~~ $ oc proxy ~~~ 4. In another terminal run the curl command to replace the tmp.json data as follow: ~~~ $ curl-k-H "Content-Type: application/json"-X PUT--data-binary @tmp.json http://127.0.0.1:8001/apis/machine.openshift.io/v1beta1/namespaces/openshift-machine-api/machines/ <$NAME> / ~~~ 5. Stop the oc proxy started in step 3 above, by pressing control+c. 6. Lastly, to complete this, we will require to delete the machines manually in your cloud provider ~~~ $ oc delete machine/-n openshift-machine-api ~~~
root_cause: Most likely it happens due to inadequate permissions, it's unable to reach the underlying cloud provider API to check the scope of the machine and delete the machine objects.

title: How to add include and exclude tags in the ConfigMap of Kube Descheduler Operator?
issue: - What are the roles of the **exclude*
and **include*
tags in the ConfigMap?- Does the **include*
tag with a null value apply to all user-created namespaces in the cluster without the need to define specific namespaces?- Where and how to update Namespaces to be included for the Descheduler?
resolution: - To include all namespaces, leave both fields (exclude and include) empty or null.- To include specific namespaces, list them in the `include` field; to exclude specific namespaces, list them in the `exclude` field.- **IMPORTANT**- Both `include` and `exclude` fields cannot be used at the same time. **NOTE**- Directly modifying the ConfigMap for the Kubernetes Descheduler Operator is not recommended, as it is managed by the operator, and any changes made may be undone during the next reconciliation loop. It is advisable to use the appropriate methods provided by the operator for updating the inclusion of Namespaces for rescheduling.- To interact with the Descheduler Operator, utilize the KubeDescheduler custom resource. The operator will then adjust the ConfigMap accordingly based on the custom resource's specifications.- For more details follow the [document](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-kube-descheduler-operator#sample-cr). ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. title: Error: x509: certificate is not valid for any names when adding LDAP authintication to OpenShift Conatiner Platform 4
issue: Encrypting LDAP communication using TLS certificate.
resolution: Use a certificate that has the host name of the server being contacted added in the Subject Alternative Name extension of the certificate.
root_cause: Starting with [GoLang version 1.15](https://go.dev/doc/go1.15#commonname) which introduced a change that deprecated the use of the`commonName`, instead the Subject Alternative Name extension is used to lookup the host names. title: Ingress VIP are getting attached to two nodes at once
issue: - After updating cluster, Ingress, Console and Authentication cluster operator went into degraded state with error: ~~~ The "default" ingress controller reports Degraded=True: DegradedConditions: One or more other status conditions indicate a degraded state: CanaryChecksSucceeding=False (CanaryChecksRepetitiveFailures: Canary route checks for the default ingress controller are failing) clusteroperator/authentication is not available (OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable: Get "https://oauth-openshift.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch/healthz": dial tcp 10.190.1.133:443: connect: connection refused) because OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerDegraded: Get "https://oauth-openshift.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch/healthz": dial tcp 10.190.1.133:443: connect: connection refused clusteroperator/console is not available (RouteHealthAvailable: failed to GET route (https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch): Get "https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch": dial tcp 10.190.1.133:443: connect: connection refused) because RouteHealthDegraded: failed to GET route (https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch): Get "https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch": dial tcp 10.190.1.133:443: connect: connection refused ~~~- When tried running below command, output shows Ingress VIP is attached to two nodes. ~~~ $ oc get nodes-oyaml|grep ' k8s.ovn.org/host-addresses'|grep k8s.ovn.org/host-addresses: '["10.x.y.z"," ","10.x.y.z"]' k8s.ovn.org/host-addresses: '["10.x.y.z"," ","10.x.y.z"]' ~~~
resolution: The issue has been identified as a bug and was being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under OCPBUGS-14403. Below are the workaround shared by engineering team to mitigate the issue: Note: Perform below steps to mark entry of 'unicast peer' in 'keepalived.conf' file in every node in cluster.- 1.Take debug of node: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ ~~~- 2.Run below command: ~~~ sh-4.4# chroot /host ~~~- 3.Run following command, to add entry of unicast_peer in keepalived.conf file: ~~~ echo "# unicast_peer" | sudo tee-a /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf ~~~
root_cause: The problem lies with the new logic for unicast migration. It attempts to verify that all of the nodes for a given role are on the same machine-configuration, but because the current configs are same across node, that will never be true. For example, worker and infra has same currentConfig: ~~~ {{machineconfiguration.openshift.io/currentConfig: rendered-worker-e7c86212cbcb387db5e0126099ddf4c8}} {{node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ''}} {{machineconfiguration.openshift.io/currentConfig: rendered-infra-e7c86212cbcb387db5e0126099ddf4c8}} {{node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ''}} ~~~ This means the migration will never happen because all of the worker configs will never match. Somehow the infra nodes came up in unicast anyway (there's no migration in the logs) so they're no longer talking to the rest of the cluster and that's how duplicate VIPS happened. One possible workaround is to force the unicast migration on the remaining nodes. It should be possible to do this by writing a comment with the string "unicast_peer" anywhere in /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf. Normally this could cause a split-brain situation, but in this case since it's already happened it won't make things any worse.

issue: - After updating cluster, Ingress, Console and Authentication cluster operator went into degraded state with error: ~~~ The "default" ingress controller reports Degraded=True: DegradedConditions: One or more other status conditions indicate a degraded state: CanaryChecksSucceeding=False (CanaryChecksRepetitiveFailures: Canary route checks for the default ingress controller are failing) clusteroperator/console is not available (RouteHealthAvailable: failed to GET route (https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch): Get "https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch": dial tcp 10.x.y.z:443 connect: connection refused) because RouteHealthDegraded: failed to GET route (https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch): Get "https://console-openshift-console.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch": dial tcp 10.x.y.z:443: connect: connection refused clusteroperator/authentication is not available (OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerAvailable: Get "https://oauth-openshift.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch/healthz": dial tcp 10.x.y.z:443: connect: connection refused) because OAuthServerRouteEndpointAccessibleControllerDegraded: Get "https://oauth-openshift.apps.t8devocp01.dev.ocp.intern.ti8m.ch/healthz": dial tcp 10.x.y.z:443: connect: connection refused ~~~- When tried running below command, output shows Ingress VIP is attached to two nodes. ~~~ $ oc get nodes-oyaml|grep ' k8s.ovn.org/host-addresses'|grep k8s.ovn.org/host-addresses: '["10.x.y.z"," ","10.x.y.z"]' k8s.ovn.org/host-addresses: '["10.x.y.z"," ","10.x.y.z"]' ~~~
resolution: The issue has been identified as a bug and was being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under [OCPBUGS-14403](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14403) Below are the workaround shared by engineering team to mitigate the issue: **Note**: Perform below steps to mark entry of 'unicast peer' in 'keepalived.conf' file in every node in cluster.- 1.Take debug of node: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ ~~~- 2.Run below command: ~~~ sh-4.4# chroot /host ~~~- 3.Run following command, to add entry of unicast_peer in keepalived.conf file: ~~~ sh-4.4# echo "# unicast_peer" | sudo tee-a /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf ~~~
root_cause: The problem lies with the new logic for unicast migration. It attempts to verify that all of the nodes for a given role are on the same machine-configuration, but because the current configs are same across node, that will never be true. For example, worker and infra has same currentConfig: ~~~ {{machineconfiguration.openshift.io/currentConfig: rendered-worker-e7c86212cbcb387db5e0126099ddf4c8}} {{node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ''}} {{machineconfiguration.openshift.io/currentConfig: rendered-infra-e7c86212cbcb387db5e0126099ddf4c8}} {{node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ''}} ~~~ This means the migration will never happen because all of the worker configs will never match. Somehow the infra nodes came up in unicast anyway (there's no migration in the logs) so they're no longer talking to the rest of the cluster and that's how duplicate VIPS happened. One possible workaround is to force the unicast migration on the remaining nodes. It should be possible to do this by writing a comment with the string "unicast_peer" anywhere in /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf. Normally this could cause a split-brain situation, but in this case since it's already happened it won't make things any worse.

title: How to get the vCenter certificate credentials from OpenShift?
issue: - Is there any way to check where the `vCenter certificate credentials` are within `OpenShift`?- Does `vCenter Certificate` stored in `OCP`?
resolution: - To check the `vCenter certificates credentials`, run the following command and confirm within vCenter that they are still valid. ~~~ $ for data in $(oc get secret vsphere-creds-n kube-system-o json | jq-r '.data[]'); do echo $data | base64-d; echo; done ~~~- Also, `vCenter certificates` are required only by the `Installer` and all other `operator` runs as *no cert check*. Hence `OCP` doesn't contain `vCenter certificates`.

title: OpenShift console shows the deployment volume, pod volume, and the container mount as Read/Write instead of Read-only
issue: - Pod volumes defined with `spec.volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.readOnly: true` and it is shows up in the console with Permissions `Read/Write` instead of `Read-only`.
resolution: - On the [bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2093785), the engineering team confirmed that there are too many ReadOnly flags in Kubernetes. There is an upstream issue that talks about [CSI](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/70505) In-tree volume plugins (incl. NFS in this case) is a similar mess and we can't change Kubernetes API.
root_cause: - Kubelet mounts a NFS volume as read-only on the host if: either the volume is represented by a PV/PVC and `Pod.spec.volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.readOnly` is true or the volume is in-line in a Pod and `pod.spec.volumes.nfs.readOnly` is true.- Then the container runtime (CRI-O) bind-mounts the volume from the host to a container. The bind-mount is read-only if: `pod.spec.containers.volumeMounts.readOnly` is true.- If any of the three conditions is true, the container sees the volume as read-only and console should show it that way.

title: Information on Multiple Availability Zone cluster deployment in ROSA
issue: - In multi-AZs cluster deployment, when a zone fails, the nodes in that zone are recreated in the other ones working or not? (Including all resources running in that zone fail)?- Is it possible to simulate a zone failure in order to analyze the behavior of services when nodes in a specific zone fail?- nodes in failed AZ are not re-deployed on healthy AZs, it is right? Only stateless resources are redistributed on working AZs.
resolution: - A zone failure from AWS affects all virtual components, such as worker nodes, block or shared storage, and load balancers that are specific to a single availability zone. To protect against a zone failure, ROSA provides the option for clusters that are distributed across three availability zones, known as multiple availability zone clusters.- Existing stateless workloads are redistributed to unaffected zones in the event of an outage, as long as there is enough capacity.- It is not suggested to simulate Zone failure, It depends on several definitions, operational maturity, objective, ad-hoc/repetitive. Here question come how do you defines as zone failure? Also, without advanced notice SRE will attempt to resolve an exercise.- Along with this you have to ensure that, you have a machinepool per AZ otherwise you have to simulate such an exercise via VPC firewall rule by blocking the traffic to AZ.- If you have a machinepool, you can take less invasive tact of scaling down that AZ's machinepool.- There is a machinepool in a cluster, the machinepool distributes a machine into each AZ, totaling 3 machines by default you can select how many replicas of machines distribute across AZs in multiples of 3. If one AZ goes dead, the machinepool has no other AZ to distribute a machine to. Either additional replicas in the same pool or additional machinepools are necessary to get more machines (within the remaining AZs).

title: Image pull fail for disconnected environment unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized in RHOCP 4
issue: - Image pull fail due to unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized- Fail to pull image for OpenShift disconnected environment ~~~ Failed to pull image "quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:a1a049a84507f6f864da4682be92d2311ce7324c5ae29366203a179ef3475c5e": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = reading manifest sha256:a1a049a84507f6f864da4682be92d2311ce7324c5ae29366203a179ef3475c5e in quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev: unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized ~~~
resolution: - The `ImageContentSourcePolicy` named misconfigured- The ImageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP) is an important configuration in OpenShift that specifies how container images should be resolved and pulled from various image repositories. In a disconnected OpenShift cluster, where the cluster does not have direct internet access, the ImageContentSourcePolicy becomes crucial for handling image resolution and retrieval.- ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: ImageContentSourcePolicy metadata: name: example-policy < <-- unique identifier for each specific policy configuration. spec: repositoryDigestMirrors:- mirrors:- mirror.example.com/ocp4/rhel8 source: registry.example.com/rhel8- mirrors:- mirror.example.com/ocp4/oadp source: registry.example.com/oadp # Add more mirrors and sources as needed for other images ~~~- The ImageContentSourcePolicy with the specified name is used by the cluster components and applications to determine the source of container images. If the name is missing or incorrect, the cluster will not be able to locate the correct policy configuration for image resolution. As a result, attempts to pull container images will fail, causing applications and services to be unable to start or work properly.

dmesg shows the following log ``` kernel: ice 0000:XX:00.0: This device is not capable of SR-IOV ```
resolution: * In older version of ice driver, the bonding and sriov are mutual exclusive. The feature which supports to create VF on top of bonding PF has been added in the following OCP versions: * OCP 4.12.19 bug [2203217](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2203217 "") * OCP 4.13.7 bug [2209284](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2209284 "")

title: How can we persist the APIcast access/error logs?
issue: What problem/issue/behavior are you having trouble with? What do you expect to see? Hi, Previously, we made the changes you specified in the case number 03444949 to print the access log in the desired format. We can view the logs from the openshift console or with the oc-f logs command, but we could not find the log file in the container. We need log files daily in container, how can we provide this? Thanks, Regards. What is the business impact? Please also provide timeframe information. No business impact
resolution: Hi Merve, Sorry for my delay, I was testing this to share with you. Please be aware that doing this APIcast log persistence in files different other than the stdout/stderr is something out of the box and will be your responsibility managing the new files and its rotation because these files would not be managed by the application and they possible can grow up very fast depending of your traffic. So, the log rotation is entirely your responsibility. To be honest, I would leave the APIcast logs as it is and create a rotine to collect them using `oc logs` and redirecting them to external file as you want. Having said that, the procedure is the following: 1. Edit the env variables defining the path to file (use a different one other than `/opt/app-root/src/logs/`) > $ oc set env dc/apicast-staging APICAST_ACCESS_LOG_FILE=/path/to/file/access2.log APICAST_LOG_FILE=/path/to/file/error2.log 2. Create a PV and PVC where the files will be persisted. 3. Use the following command to set a volume in APIcast using the PVC you created previously (test it first with APIcast-staging): > $ oc set volume dc/apicast-staging--add--name=pvc-apicast-t pvc--claim-name=--mount-path=/path/to/file/ 4. Wait til the new APIcast is rolled out and check if the volume was mounted: > $ oc rsh dc/apicast-staging df-kh I hope that helps you. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira Hi Merve, Don't point the environment variables to the default files (`access.log` and `error.log`) as they are the standard output and have symbolic links, instead create new ones then you'll be allowed to copy them: > $ oc set env dc/apicast-staging APICAST_ACCESS_LOG_FILE=/opt/app-root/src/logs/access2.log APICAST_LOG_FILE=/opt/app-root/src/logs/error2.log This is one example from my local machine: > \# oc cp 3scale/apicast-staging-19-7vcd5:/opt/app-root/src/logs/error2.log /cases/03519664/error2.log tar: Removing leading `/' from member names Dropping out copy after 0 retries error: unexpected EOF [root@user01 03519664]# ls-lrth total 1.7M-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1.7M May 24 18:39 error2.log [root@user01 03519664]# Another thing, I would recommend that you don't simply set these environment variables pointing to files inside the pod. These files are not persistent, if your pod is redeployed you will lose them. I would recommend you to use Volume mount through ConfigMaps to persist these files. Let me know if you are able to copy the files now. Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira

title: Is it possible to manipulate the cluster through console URL and user's token
issue: Is it possible to manipulate the cluster through console URL and user's token
The cluster will only expose its Routes to the Internet via port 443, and the apiserver (aka port 6443) won't be exposed
If an attacker obtains the cluster-admin's token, is the hacker able to manipulate the cluster
resolution: * The attacker could manipulate the cluster through console endpoints by using user's token. * Here is an example to list Deployments under certain namespaces by using GET operation: ``` $ curl-X GET-H "Cookie: openshift-session-token=$(oc whoami-t)"-k $(oc whoami--show-console)/api/kubernetes/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/ /deployments ``` * Another example is to use PATCH operation to scale up a Deployment's replica number: ``` $ oc get deployment-n test-hack NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE hello-openshift 2/2 2 2 2m31s # Patch the deployment $ curl-X PATCH-d '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/replicas", "value": 3}]'-H "Referer: $(oc whoami--show-console)/k8s/ns/openshift-console/apps\~v1\~Deployment"-H "X-Csrftoken: 12345"-H "Content-Type: application/json-patch+json"-H "Cookie: openshift-session-token=$(oc whoami-t); csrf-token=12345"-k $(oc whoami--show-console)/api/kubernetes/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/test-hack/deployments/hello-openshift/scale {"kind": "Scale", "apiVersion": "autoscaling/v1", "metadata": {"name": "hello-openshift", "namespace": "test-hack", "uid": "35986f42-be73-49bc-b1a0-ae0b514158c6", "resourceVersion": "9970429", "creationTimestamp": "2023-08-08T04:01:28Z"}, "spec": {"replicas": 3}, "status": {"replicas": 2, "selector": "app=hello-openshift"}} $ oc get deployment-n test-hack NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE hello-openshift 3/3 3 3 3m45s ``` The following is an example to update the cluster channel: ``` $ curl-H "X-Csrftoken: 12345"-H "Cookie: openshift-session-token=$(oc whoami-t); csrf-token=12345"-H "Content-Type: application/json-patch+json"-X PATCH-d '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/channel", "value": "fast-4.13"}]'-k $(oc whoami--show-console)/api/kubernetes/apis/config.openshift.io/v1/clusterversions/version-H "Referer: $(oc whoami--show-console)/settings/cluster" ```
root_cause: The user's token should never be leaked even though apiserver is not publicly available. The attacker could still use console URL to manipulate the cluster. By default the user's token is 24 hours valid.

title: How do I transport container images for use in my Red Hat products in a disconnected environment?
issue: - There is an airgapped, disconnected, or otherwise secure environment which requires the use of container images provided by Red Hat.- What methods are available to provide container images to this environment from the Red Hat Container Catalog, `quay.io`, or other remote container image locations?
resolution: - There are multiple methods depending on your environment and existing infrastructure to provide container images to a disconnected environment. The following sections outline different environments and how to provide container images to disconnected systems within those environments. ## Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- As of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.9 and higher, there is the option to use a Mirror Registry which can pull container images from external sources such as the required `quay.io` endpoint and provide them to a disconnected environment.- The steps to configure a Mirror Registry are defined within the following documentation:- [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.13- Creating a Mirror Registry](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-creating-registry.html)- On Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8 and prior versions, no direct mirror registry solution exists. Instead, documentation on how to use other external registries are provided in the following documentation:- [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8- Mirroring Images for Disconnected Installation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.8/html/installing/installing-mirroring-installation-images) ## Red Hat Enterprise Linux- If there is a functional Red Hat Satellite provided within your environment, then entire repositories from remote container image registries can be synchronized to the Red Hat Satellite server and provided to connected hosts as per the following documentation:- [Red Hat Satellite- Managing Container Images](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_satellite/6.7/html/content_management_guide/managing_container_images)- For all Red Hat Enterprise Linux versions not connected directly to a satellite, a mirrored-registry approach can be used to provide container images to disconnected environments.- Note that Red Hat does not provide nor ship a container registry outside of the [Red Hat Quay](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/quay) container image registry. The following instructions and blog posts come with the disclaimer that they are not officially supported solutions from Red Hat and rely on non-Red Hat technologies in the form of third-party container image registries.- [How to implement a simple personal/private Linux container image registry for internal use](https://www.redhat.com/sysadmin/simple-container-registry)- [How to manage Linux container registries](https://www.redhat.com/sysadmin/manage-container-registries)

title: /sysroot mountpoint failed to resize automatically on new nodes during machineset scaleup
issue: - Machineset fails to scaleup after upgrading the Openshift cluster to 4.12.- New machines get stuck at `Provisioned` state after upgrading to 4.12.- New machines are not added to the cluster due to "no space left on the device" errors when pulling images during installation.
resolution: This issue is known to Red Hat and is being tracked under JIRA [OCPBUGS-15087](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-15087) There are 2 workarounds for this issue: **Workaround 1** [Recommended] Ensure that the VM template being used to provision new machines uses RHCOS version is same as that of cluster or closer to the current cluster version.- Download a version of the RHCOS image which is currently running on the cluster or closer to the current version of your cluster. Images are available [here](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/dependencies/rhcos/).- With the help of Virtualization vendor, create a VM template that uses the newer RHCOS image that you just downloaded.- Once the new VM template is created which points to the newer RHCOS version, [create a new machineset](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/machine_management/creating-infrastructure-machinesets.html) in the cluster which uses this template.- Try scaling up the new machineset. **Workaround 2** Manually resize the /sysroot filesystem with `xfs_growfs /` after the machine provisioning fails.- From the VM console, [break the root password on the problematic node using the rd.break](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1192).- Reboot the system and interrupt it again at the grub menu to append `selinux=0` at the end of `linux16` line.- Once you have finished that change, press Ctrl-x to accept the edit, and to boot using that kernel.- Then login into the node with the root user.- Once logged in with root, confirm that the filesystem size of /sysroot mountpoint `df-kh /sysroot` is very less when compared to the actual partition size `lsblk`.- Manually resize the /sysroot filesystem with `xfs_growfs /` command and confirm that the size is increased.- Reboot the machine again and this time the installation should complete as it has enough space to store images.
root_cause: In this specific case, the VM template being used was using RHCOS image 4.6.40 (from the time of installation). When running coreos-installer utility, the initial sysroot size set in RHCOS 4.6 image is only 2.8 Gib and the initial sysroot size set in RHCOS 4.12 image is 3.7 Gib. The size needed to download and store the RHCOS 4.12 is more than what is set in RHCOS 4.6 image. It gets stuck in a loop.- The podman command from `node-ip-configuration` fails as it does not have enough space on root to pull the 4.12 image.- The `rhcos-growpart` job cannot complete as it is still waiting for `node-ip-configuration` service to come up.

title: Console operator degraded unknow state with error massage "Unsupported management state  for console operator"
issue: - Below error can be seen in the console operator. ~~~ $ oc get clusteroperator/console NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE console 4.10.25 Unknown Unknown True 19h ManagementStateDegraded: Unsupported management state "" for console operator ~~~
resolution: - The console operator is in unknown state as mentioned below. ~~~ $ oc get co console-o yaml spec: {} status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: '2022-11-03T15:05:39Z' message: 'ManagementStateDegraded: Unsupported management state "" for console operator' reason: ManagementState_Unknown status: 'True' type: Degraded ~~~- Check routes for the openshift-console namespace. ~~~ $ oc get routes-n openshift-console NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD console console.apps.asa-dav-99.paas.cloud.asadavdc.be console https reencrypt/Redirect None downloads downloads-openshift-console.apps.asa-dav-99.paas.cloud.asadavdc.be downloads http edge/Redirect None $ oc get route console-n openshift-console-o json | jq.spec.host ~~~- For Example, The URL should look like this. ~~~ $ oc get routes-n openshift-console NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD console console-openshift-console.apps.ocp-sandbox.uat.svbank.com console https reencrypt/Redirect None downloads downloads-openshift-console.apps.ocp-sandbox.uat.svbank.com downloads http edge/Redirect None ~~~- Check with config map in openshift-console namespace and validate whether the consoleBaseAddress is correct or not. ~~~ $ oc get cm console-config-n openshift-console-o yaml apiVersion: v1 data: console-config.yaml: | apiVersion: console.openshift.io/v1 auth: clientID: console clientSecretFile: /var/oauth-config/clientSecret oauthEndpointCAFile: /var/oauth-serving-cert/ca-bundle.crt clusterInfo: consoleBaseAddress: https://console-openshift-console.apps.asa-dav-99.paas.cloud.asadavdc.be masterPublicURL: https://api.asa-dav-99.paas.cloud.asadavdc.be:6443 ~~~- Need to validate the "consoleBaseAddress" in this routing URL. It is associated with the default keyword "console-openshift" and any changes would cause this issue.- if you observed any change then edit the config map and make changes.- Restart openshift-console namespace pods. ~~~ $ oc delete pod--all-n openshift-console ~~~
root_cause: Incorrect routing URL in config map.

title: Elasticsearch snapshot and restore in RHOCP
issue: - How to backup and restore `Elasticsearch` index?
resolution: **Unsupported Procedure**: The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and supported procedures. The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the Operating System unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. The intent of this article is to provide information to accomplish the system's needs. 1. Check if there are any repositories, and they've already set up: $ oc-n openshift-logging exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XGET 'https://localhost:9200/_snapshot/_all?pretty=true' {} The blank response shows there're no repositories yet. 2. Create a repository, and have to do to all `Elasticsearch` pods.- First, create a directory where save the snapshot: $ oc-n openshift-logging rsh-c elasticsearch mkdir /elasticsearch/persistent/elasticsearch/es_repo 4. Change `managementState` to **Unmanaged**, and unfortunately, this operation would lead the operator unsupported by Red Hat: $ oc get Elasticsearch-A NAMESPACE NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT openshift-logging elasticsearch Managed green 3 3 all $ oc-n openshift-logging patch elasticsearch/elasticsearch--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"managementState": "Unmanaged"}}' $ oc get Elasticsearch-A NAMESPACE NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT openshift-logging elasticsearch Unmanaged green 3 3 all 5. Specify the path.repo: $ oc edit cm/elasticsearch-n openshift-logging add the following line: path.repo #.. omit.. path: data: /elasticsearch/persistent/${CLUSTER_NAME}/data logs: /elasticsearch/persistent/${CLUSTER_NAME}/logs repo: /elasticsearch/persistent/${CLUSTER_NAME}/es_repo #..omit 6. Restart the Elasticsearch. 7. Create the repository: $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPUT 'https://localhost:9200/_snapshot/es_backup?verify=false'-H "Content-Type: application/json"-d '{"type": "fs","settings": {"compress": true,"location": "/elasticsearch/persistent/elasticsearch/es_repo"}}' 8. Check the snapshot configuration: $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XGET 'https://localhost:9200/_snapshot/_all' 9. Take the snapshot for the index: $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPUT 'https://localhost:9200/_snapshot/es_backup/?wait_for_completion=true&pretty'-H "Content-Type: application/json"-d '{"indices": " ","ignore_unavailable": true,"include_global_state": false,"metadata": {"taken_by": "who","taken_because": "reason"}}' 10. Delete the older index: oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XDELETE https://localhost:9200/ Get index alias name by: $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XGET https://localhost:9200/_cat/indices?v 11. Restore the index: $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XPOST 'https://localhost:9200/_snapshot/es_backup/ /_restore' 12. Check the status of restore: $ oc exec-c elasticsearch-- curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XGET GET /_snapshot/my_backup/ 13. Remember to set `managementState` as `Managed` back when upgrading the OpenShift Container Platform cluster and `Operator`. $ oc-n openshift-logging patch elasticsearch/elasticsearch--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"managementState": "Unmanaged"}}' $ oc get Elasticsearch-A NAMESPACE NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT openshift-logging elasticsearch Managed green 3 3 all

title: Not able to expose the internal registry even after setting the default route as true
issue: - Route is not created for the OpenShift internal registry after performing steps mentioned in [the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/registry/securing-exposing-registry.html). ~~~ $ oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io/cluster--patch '{"spec":{"defaultRoute":true}}'--type=merge config.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io/cluster patched ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get route-n openshift-image-registry No resources found in openshift-image-registry namespace. ~~~
resolution: - Run the below command to change the management state of the `image-registry` to `Managed`. ~~~ $ oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io cluster--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"managementState":"Managed"}}' ~~~- Check the route in `openshift-image-registry` namespace. It should be created. ~~~ NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD default-route default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.newrutuja.lab.upshift.rdu2.redhat.com image-registry reencrypt None ~~~
root_cause: - The service, replicas and routes are managed by `image-registry` config. If it is in `Removed` state, those resources need to be created manually.- The `image-registry` should be in `Managed` state to be able to expose it using default route.

title: Cluster is not accessible due to unstability of ClusterOperator which eventually leads to high etcd disk size due to the openshift-debug-xxxx projects.

title: Security groups should only allow unrestricted incoming traffic for authorized ports
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - *AWS Security Hub
has logged a **High severity*
finding for a *security group
created by ROSA- An unrestricted inbound *security group
that allows custom ICMP traffic is being flagged as **High severity*
by the *AWS Security Hub*
resolution: - To follow
root_cause: - Because of a *security group* created by ROSA, *AWS Security Hub* will generate findings based on automated and continuous security checks against [security controls][2] and flag it as a **High severity** issue- The *security group* which has a *security group rule* that allows unrestricted inbound custom ICMP access will be detected by the AWS Security Hub. The UI appears broken for `PipelineRuns`

title: Understanding Openshift `externalTrafficPolicy: local` and  Source IP Preservation
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - What is `externalTrafficPolicy`- What are `externalTrafficPolicy` settings- How the `Local` policy helps in preserving the client's source IP
resolution: In summary:- Use `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` when you need to preserve the source IP of external clients.- Use `internalTrafficPolicy: Local` to optimize internal traffic routing to reduce hops and latency.
root_cause: `externalTrafficPolicy` is the setting associated with Openshift/Kubernetes Services, particularly for the `LoadBalancer` and `NodePort` service types. These policies determine how traffic is routed to the backend Pods and how the source IP of the client is preserved. **externalTrafficPolicy**:- Used to control the behavior of external traffic, typically originating from outside the cluster.- Options:- **Cluster (default)**: Traffic is routed to any node in the cluster, regardless of whether the node has a running Pod for the service or not. If the node does not have a Pod for the service, the traffic is then forwarded to a node that does. This can cause the client's source IP to be masked by the node's IP, but it ensures even load distribution across all nodes.- **Local**: Traffic is routed only to nodes that have running Pods for the service. If the node receiving the traffic does not have a Pod for the service, the traffic is dropped. This preserves the client's source IP but can lead to uneven load distribution if a particular node has more active connections.- When to use:- **Cluster**: When source IP preservation is not needed and even load distribution is preferred.- **Local**: When source IP preservation is crucial, such as for logging or security purposes. For example, you have a Openshift/Kubernetes cluster with 3 nodes: Node A, Node B, and Node C. You have a Service of type `LoadBalancer` or `NodePort` that exposes your application to the outside world. External traffic (from a client or user outside the cluster) comes in, and the LoadBalancer or NodePort routes this traffic to one of the nodes. Let's say it routes the traffic to Node A. Now, Node A has to decide what to do with this traffic. If `externalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Cluster` (the default), Node A will send the traffic to any node that has a running Pod for the Service, even if Node A itself doesn't have one. This might involve an extra hop, and during this process, the original source IP of the client can get masked or replaced by Node A's IP. If `externalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Local`, Node A will check if it has a running Pod for the Service. If Node A has a running Pod for the Service, it will send the traffic directly to its local Pod. Since there's no need for the traffic to be forwarded to another node, the original source IP of the client is preserved. If Node A does not have a running Pod for the Service, it will drop the traffic. This means the client's request will not be fulfilled, and they might experience this as a timeout or failed request. The key advantage of `Local` policy is the preservation of the client's source IP. This can be crucial for applications or systems that rely on the original source IP for logging, security filtering, or other purposes. However, the trade-off is that if a node does not have a Pod for the Service and it receives traffic, that traffic will be dropped. In simpler terms: With `Local` policy, external traffic is only served by local Pods on the node it initially reaches. If there's no local Pod, the request fails. This ensures the client's original IP address remains unchanged, but at the potential cost of some failed requests if traffic is not evenly distributed or if some nodes don't have Pods for the Service. How the `Local` policy helps in preserving the client's source IP: When a packet (a unit of data) is sent over a network, it has both a source IP (indicating where it came from) and a destination IP (indicating where it's going). As this packet travels through various network devices and systems, certain operations can change the original source IP. One such operation is NAT (Network Address Translation). In the context of Openshift/Kubernetes: 1. **Without NAT (Local Policy)**:- When `externalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Local`, the idea is to avoid any additional hops that would require NAT operations.- If the traffic reaches a node that has a running Pod for the service, the traffic is directly forwarded to the Pod. Since there's no need for NAT, the source IP remains unchanged.- If the traffic reaches a node that does NOT have a running Pod for the service, performing NAT to send the traffic to another node would change the source IP. To avoid this and preserve the source IP, Openshift/Kubernetes simply drops the traffic. 2. **With NAT (Cluster Policy)**:- When `externalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Cluster`, Openshift/Kubernetes is more less strict about where the traffic goes. If a node receives traffic but doesn't have a Pod for the service, it will forward (or NAT) the traffic to a node that does. This NAT operation changes the source IP to the IP of the node that did the forwarding. So, the act of dropping the traffic in the `Local` policy is not what preserves the source IP. Instead, it's the decision to avoid NAT altogether. By dropping traffic that would require NAT (i.e., traffic that arrives at a node without a local Pod), Openshift/Kubernetes ensures that only traffic that can be handled without changing the source IP is processed. This guarantees that when a packet is received by a Pod, its source IP is the original IP of the client, not the IP of a node that forwarded it. PS: **internalTrafficPolicy** (introduced in Kubernetes v1.21): This setting is similar to `externalTrafficPolicy` but used to control the behavior of internal traffic, which originates from inside the cluster. While `externalTrafficPolicy` deals with traffic coming from outside the cluster, `internalTrafficPolicy` deals with traffic originating from within the cluster itself.

title: RHACS S3 Integration Does Not Work With RHODF MCG(NooBaa) Endpoint
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Error when creating S3 integration with RHACS results in x509 errors- externalbackups/plugins/s3:... s3.go:204: Error: S3 backup error: RequestError: send request failed- Cannot backup RHACS to RHODF MCG S3 endpoint- x509: certificate is valid for api., *.apps., not.s3-openshift-storage.apps.
resolution: From ACS web interface go to `Platform Configuration` > `Integrations` > `Backup Integrations` > `Amazon S3` > `New integration`:- Set "Bucket entry" to s3-openshift-storage- Set "Object prefix" to the bucket name- Set "Endpoint" to apps.- Region can be set to "noobaa"
root_cause: The issue is related to virtual-hosted-style vs path-style access requests to buckets. The difference between the two access methods can be summarized as:- Virtual-hosted-style bucket request are accessible using a URL similar to `https://..- Path-style bucket request are similar to `https:// / `. The route for an RHOCP/RHODF S3 endpoint is typically, https://s3-openshift-storage.apps.. RHACS uses the virtual-hosted-style bucket request by prepending the bucket name to the S3 endpoint. This results in a request similar to https://.s3-openshift-storage.apps.. This results in an error reported in the central pod: `x509: certificate is valid for api., *.apps., not.s3-openshift-storage.apps. `

title: OSD Will Not Remove During Device Replacement - Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation
issue: After following the steps in the official Product Documentation-> Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation-> Version-> Replacing devices or in the [Steps to remove unwanted or failed Ceph OSD in Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation(previously known as Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5015451) solutions article the OSD device fails to remove from the Ceph OSD Tree and/or `openshift-storage` Deployments.
resolution: When following the steps outlined in the official Product Documentation-> Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation-> Version-> Replacing devices or In the [Steps to remove unwanted or failed Ceph OSD in Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation(previously known as Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5015451). If the OSD device fails to remove from Ceph OSD Tree or from the `openshift-storage` namespace deployments after the `$ oc process-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal-p FAILED_OSD_IDS=${osd_id_to_remove}-p FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=false |oc create-n openshift-storage-f-` command has been unsuccessfully issued; please proceed with the following workflow: 1. Delete the current job: ~~~ $ oc delete job-n openshift-storage ~~~ **NOTE:** If there are no active jobs, it may be easier to clean/purge all of the old jobs with: ~~~ $ oc delete job-n openshift-storage--all ~~~ 2. Revisit the documentation previously being followed and for the process template command, change the `FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL` argument to `true`. ~~~ $ oc process-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal-p FAILED_OSD_IDS=${osd_id_to_remove}-p FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=true |oc create-n openshift-storage-f- ~~~ 3. If met with the following error message (see below), this most likely is due to OCS/ODF upgrading over time and with new container arguments added in ODF v4.10+ failed to populate in the `ocs-osd-removal` template. ~~~ $ oc process-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal-p FAILED_OSD_IDS=${osd_id_to_remove} FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=true |oc create-n openshift-storage-f- error: unknown parameter name "FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL" error: no objects passed to create ~~~ 4. Inspect the `ocs-osd-removal` template and ensure the following container args are present: ~~~ $ oc get template-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal-o yaml spec: containers:- args:- ceph- osd- remove---osd-ids=${FAILED_OSD_IDS}---force-osd-removal <-------------------- ${FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL} <------------------ ~~~ 5. If it is determined that the args are not present, delete the template and allow time for re-creation. **NOTE: The ocs-operator must be scaled up for the re-creation of the template.** ~~~ $ oc delete template-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal ~~~ 6. Once the new template is created proceed back to the documentation workflow.
root_cause: If the `$ oc process-n openshift-storage ocs-osd-removal-p FAILED_OSD_IDS=${osd_id_to_remove}-p FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=false |oc create-n openshift-storage-f-` fails and the `FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=true` is needed. Or, if an old/outdated `ocs-osd-removal` template is present and needs to be updated to a current version that will correspond with ODF v4.10+ product documentation.

title: Nodes getting "connection refused: exit status 125" when podman is attempting to pull new image for upgrade on cluster utilizing proxy
issue: Cluster upgrade stuck attempting to upgrade the nodes which are getting "connection refused: exit status 125" when podman is attempting to pull new image for upgrade on cluster utilizing proxy.
resolution: The file /etc/mco/proxy.env was manually created on each node containing the proxy details: # 'EnvironmentFile=/etc/mco/proxy.env'. HTTP_PROXY=http://xxx.xx.xx.xx:xxxx HTTPS_PROXY=http://xxx.xx.xx.xx:xx NO_PROXY=[comma,separate, list,10.0.0.0/16,10.0.0.0/8,10.128.0.0/14,127.0.0.1,172.18.108.0/25,172.20.0.0/16,api-int.ocp2.example.prod,default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.ocp2.example.prod,localhost Then address the resulting mco conflict with the new file being present by utilizing # touch /run/machine-config-daemon-force from a debug pod or ssh login as root on each of the impacted nodes.
root_cause: The cause for the failure is that the cluster uses a proxy but the proxy settings had not been applied to the nodes rendering them unable to pull the new upgrade images in conjunction with an OCP cluster upgrade. The proxy variable was not exported on the nodes in /etc/mco/proxy.env

title: Error: Replica Override Conflict with HPA in Quay Registry Reconciliation
issue: - Facing issues while trying to override the replica numbers if they have HPA(horizontal pod autoscaler) enabled. Since enabling HPA it will be responsible for replica numbers. Check the Quay operator log to find the below error ~~~ $ oc logs 2023-07-24T13:30:39.378390359Z 1.6902054393783047e+09 INFO controllers.QuayRegistryStatus quay components conditions reconciled {"quayregistrystatus": "quayregistry/quay-prod-registry"} 2023-07-24T13:30:39.384104490Z 1.6902054393840888e+09 INFO controllers.QuayRegistryStatus quay components conditions reconciled {"quayregistrystatus": "quayregistry/quay-prod-registry"} 2023-07-24T13:30:47.650513194Z 1.6902054476504698e+09 INFO controllers.QuayRegistryStatus quay components conditions reconciled {"quayregistrystatus": "quayregistry/quay-prod-registry"} 2023-07-24T13:30:47.656647683Z 1.690205447656632e+09 INFO controllers.QuayRegistryStatus quay components conditions reconciled {"quayregistrystatus": "quayregistry/quay-prod-registry"} 2023-07-24T13:30:49.372947801Z 1.6902054493728511e+09 INFO controllers.QuayRegistry begin reconcile {"quayregistry": "quayregistry/quay-prod-registry"} ~~~
resolution: Identify where the replica count override is specified in the configuration for the Quay Registry component. Edit the relevant configuration file and remove any entries or values that attempt to override the replica count. Since HPA is already managing the replica counts, removing the replica count override should allow the HPA to do its job. The HPA adjusts the number of replicas based on metrics and policies you've defined and Save the changes you made to the configuration file.
root_cause: Attempt to override the replica count of a Quay Registry component while Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) is managing the replica counts which conflicts with the HPA's responsibility to adjust replica counts based on metrics and policies. This resulted in a warning and an error during the reconciliation process of the Quay Registry component.

title: How to request and pass an oauth token for REST API access in OpenShift 4
issue: - Getting HTTP `403` error when making a request to the OpenShift REST API. Example: ~~~ $ curl-s-k-X GET https://api.example.com:6443/apis/project.openshift.io/v1/projects {"kind": "Status", "apiVersion": "v1", "metadata": {}, "status": "Failure", "message": "projects.project.openshift.io is forbidden: User \"system:anonymous\" cannot list resource \"projects\" in API group \"project.openshift.io\" at the cluster scope", "reason": "Forbidden", "details": {"group": "project.openshift.io", "kind": "projects"}, "code": 403 ~~~- How to make REST API calls with `curl` to OpenShift?
resolution: - Use `oc login` to login to the OpenShift API server (set_USER_ accordingly), then use `oc whoami-t` to get an_Oauth Bearer Token_. Example: ~~~ $ oc login-u USER https://api.example.com:6443 $ TOKEN=$(oc whoami-t) ~~~ Alternatively (without previous login), use either of the following `curl` command to get an_Oauth Bearer Token_ (set_USER_,_PASSWORD_ and_OAuth-route-hostname_ accordingly): ~~~ $ oc get route-n openshift-authentication-o jsonpath='{.items[].spec.host}{"\n"}' # Get OAuth Route Hostname $ TOKEN=$(curl-s-k-i-L-X GET--user USER:PASSWORD 'https:// /oauth/authorize?response_type=token&client_id=openshift-challenging-client' | grep-oP "access_token=\K[^&]*") OR $ TOKEN=$(curl-s-k-i-L-X GET--user USER:PASSWORD 'https:// /oauth/authorize?response_type=token&client_id=openshift-challenging-client' | grep "access_token=" | awk-F'=' '{print $2}' | awk-F'&' '{print $1}' ~~~- Use the_Oauth Bearer Token_ in the HTTP requests to the OpenShift REST API. Example: ~~~ $ curl-s-k-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"-X GET https://api.example.com:6443/apis/project.openshift.io/v1/projects ~~~- In case the requests must be done as a `ServiceAccount`, run `oc serviceaccounts get-token` to obtain an_Oauth Bearer Token_ for the `ServiceAccount`. For example, for the `ServiceAccount`_FOOSERVICEACCOUNT_: ~~~ $ TOKEN=$(oc serviceaccounts get-token FOOSERVICEACCOUNT) ~~~

title: Thanos Querier high CPU and memory usage till OOM in RHOCP 4
issue: - `Thanos-querier` pods are consuming high `CPU` and `memory` until the node crashes.- Node is getting `OOM` due to high memory utilization by `thanos-querier` pods.
resolution: - The issue is known to Red Hat and is fixes have been delivered in RHOCP 4.9 and 4.10:- [Bug 2074413](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2074413) is fixed in RHOCP 4.9.31 [RHSA-2022:1356](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:1605)- [Bug 2071479](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2071479) is fixed in RHOCP 4.10.10 [RHSA-2022:1356](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:1356)- [Bug 2055305](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2055305) fixed in RHOCP 4.11.0 through ERRATA [RHSA-2022:5069](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:5069) **Workaround:**- Check if `cluster-monitoring-config` configmap exists in `openshift-monitoring` project: ~~~ $ oc get cm-n openshift-monitoring ~~~- Modify / create `cluster-monitoring-config` configmap. Below is the sample config: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: cluster-monitoring-config namespace: openshift-monitoring data: config.yaml: | thanosQuerier: resources: requests: cpu: 100m memory: 2Gi limits: cpu: 900m memory: 2Gi ~~~

title: OpenShift Container Platform Logging operator upgrade to  5.7 breaks external ELK stack
issue: - Why upgrading the Logging operator causes external ELK to ingest the logs?- Is there a change in the Logging operator which could stop ingesting?
resolution: Modify your filters to not use "viaq_index_name" field as it is removed from the Logging operator starting with the 5.4.10. One can benefit from "log_type" field in order to establish a similar filtering mechanism. ``` {... "hostname": "example.com", "log_type": "audit", <-------------------------------- this is for audit log "apiVersion": "audit.k8s.io/v1",...} ``` One another viable and comparably better approach is to use labels for the logs configured via [ClusterLogForwarder](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/logging/cluster-logging-external.html#cluster-logging-collector-log-forward-fluentd_cluster-logging-external) object, as it gives more control in terms over the fields which enables complex filtering and routing. ~~~ apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogForwarder metadata: name: instance namespace: openshift-logging spec:... pipelines:- name: forward-to-fluentd-secure inputRefs:- application- audit outputRefs:- fluentd-server-secure- default parse: json labels: clusterId: "C1234" <------------------------- labels defined here ~~~
root_cause: Logging Opeartor 5.4.10 "viaq_index_name" field is not there anymore. The versions going forward will no more have this field anymore. There is no exact ERRATA for the change. Filters using that field are not able to work as expected.

title: How to integrate Quay with openshift auth?
issue: - When trying to configure an OIDC provider with the following configuration: ~~~ OIDC Server: https://api.mgt.containerhostingplatform.nl:6443/ Client ID: system:serviceaccount:sscc-registry:quay-auth Client Secret: Service Name: OpenShift ~~~- When validating this configuration I get the following message: ~~~ Could not create provider for OpenShift. Error: oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider, expected "https://api.mgt.containerhostingplatform.nl:6443" got "https://kubernetes.default.svc" ~~~ Questions to address:- What is the right way to configure Quay to use open shift auth?- Is it possible to import/sync groups in Quay using an OIDC provider integration?- Is it possible to automatically add users to groups using an OIDC provider integration?
resolution: - We have filed a Jira case [**PROJQUAY-673**](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-673) and currently, our engineering team is still working on this issue.- We also have a PR that enhances Project Quay by seamlessly integrating it with OpenShift 3.x/4.x's OAuth service. It ensures that users logging into the OpenShift console can access Project Quay without additional setup. The integration carries over user details via OAuth token scopes, while not impacting Quay permissions. The goal is to simplify Quay deployment in OpenShift clusters, improving user experience. The PR introduces configuration changes, plans for a UI, and is undergoing validation testing. [**PR**](https://github.com/quay/quay/pull/473).- Our motivation is to simplify user access to Quay when logged into OpenShift. Users achieved token scopes from OpenShift OAuth, allowing authentication details to carry over to Quay, and they're considering automated endpoint discovery.

title: How to gather list of Pods per the amount of network traffic received
issue: - A list of pods per the amount of network traffic is needed.
resolution: - Log in to the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) web console as an admin user.- From the left navigation menu, go to **'Observe'** > **'Metrics'**.- On the resulting page, from the dropdown that mentions *'Insert metric at cursor'*, select the option *"container_network_receive_bytes_total"*. This gives a list of containers and the bytes received by the container. Click on the arrow button next to the 'Value' column to sort the results as per the number of bytes.- Refer to the screenshot attached below for a sample output. [image=[src="images/metrics_containers_bytes_received.png", alt="metrics_containers_bytes_received", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="List of pods receiving filtered per the amount of bytes they receive",]]- NOTE: There are other query options as well that can be used depending upon what suits your needs best. These query options can be found at the [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/networking/associating-secondary-interfaces-metrics-to-network-attachments.html#cnf-associating-secondary-interfaces-metrics-to-network-attachments-network-metrics-daemon_secondary-interfaces-metrics).
root_cause: - There are hundreds or thousands of pods running that were created by users/developers from different projects in an Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) cluster. Many of these pods could simply be running in the cluster consuming resources, however, may not be receiving any network traffic. Such pods are good candidates for taking necessary actions to avoid such a scenario.- There may be an audit/inspection to check the network consumption by pods.

title: In disconnected env Clair scanning is not working
issue: - Quay registry deployed on disconnected OpenShift cluster has issues with Clair. Images are getting queued during the scan. When checking the logs of the clair-app we can see the below error: ~~~ $ oc logs prod-registry-clair-app-69699f8dd6-xxxx Signature=0b680b15288f311fa2c2d682d8144b3b75becc327e31e3068a6b0dc958c7c8d9\": dial tcp 10.x.y.xyz:443: address tcp4!10.x.y.xyz:443: martian address","time":"2023-05-23T07:01:24Z","message":"error during scan"} ~~~
resolution: This is a known issue that is tracked in [PROJQUAY-5485](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-5485). While there is no workaround, the issue does not seem to occur in the latest Clair image 4.6.1. This image is part of Quay operator 3.8.7. "Upgrade the operator to 3.8.7"
root_cause: - The issue is due to incorrect use of API when configuring indexer.airgap, the handling of ports has not been done correctly. For more details please refer to this [link](https://github.com/quay/clair/issues/1689)- A Martian address is an IP address that is either a source or destination and does not exist, making it invalid and/or non-routable. When a container image is pushed to Quay, the image repository infrastructure expects a valid IP address for communication. If it's not valid, the request will be rejected by the server in such a case.

title: Pushing an image to  Quay causes : HTTP 500 Error
issue: - Facing 500 internal server errors while uploading an image to the Quay registry ~~~ $ podman push quay.example.com:latest Getting image source signatures Copying blob sha256:ce650482729922f6daf0e12a321c8252a5675cdd52314f5e4cae59abb83603de Copying blob sha256:0b9f60fbcaf14fc8608d681e205e87e93d3390da9369817ec004c35beb76f72e Copying blob sha256:c607b6f95cf71c63ebe2342bebfeec4d1641cccaf497b262258f2da8e9a1df34 Copying blob sha256:4bdc748e7c3d0576619eb1c8a9b360996cd2ee03ba7c3191ae81d6d4c232b04c Copying blob sha256:7577f7ad3cd4b84418e188e628151ce0fc2e707a2701b27d689b8e3c3e8ac14c Copying blob sha256:cbd644319450b33a8b606fcf081d49b094e7bba43b38ba7805a5d78a5502d3c5 Error: writing blob: initiating layer upload to /v2/xxxx/xxxx/blobs/uploads/ in quay.example.com-: received unexpected HTTP status: 500 Internal Server Error ~~~
resolution: Check the hostname in Quay config.yaml file using the below command. Then verify if the hostname is same across multiple data centers. If there are different hostnames change them to a single hostname. ~~~ $ oc exec-it quay-pod-name-- cat /quay-registry/conf/stack/config.yaml DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: radosGWStorage:- RadosGWStorage- hostname: s3.example.com access_key: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx secret_key: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx bucket_name: pnu-jxxxxx is_secure: true port: 443 storage_path: /quay DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_DEFAULT_LOCATIONS: [] DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_PREFERENCE:- radosGWStorage ~~~
root_cause: - The problem occurs due to two data centers with different hostnames. Different hostnames that connect to both data centers split up the multipart upload and sent them to both clusters at once which meant parts of the upload were completely split up.- NoSuchUpload error in the logs means that this upload was not initiated at all, this is because of the different hostnames in two datacenters.

title: How to avoid the conflict between native tuned daemon and NTO(Node Tuning Operator) for RHEL worker nodes in OpenShift 4?

title: Feature development of DeploymentConfigs has stopped
issue: - Requesting a new feature for DeploymentConfigs- Extending existing features for DeploymentConfigs- Migrating from DeploymentConfigs to Deployments or another alternative
resolution: We will analyze each customer situation and assist with providing a migration plan to Deployments or another alternative. To receive assistance with migration away from DeploymentConfigs, open an issue under [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS) and set the Component/s field to openshift-controller-manager/apps. We will evaluate the case and work on providing a migration solution. After migration plans are identified, we will update the list below with the known migration solutions. **Migration solutions**- case CASE: TBD
root_cause: Feature development of DeploymentConfigs has stopped. DeploymentConfigs manage ReplicationControllers. Because the development of ReplicationController has ceased, it is difficult to provide reasonable support for DeploymentConfigs without introducing potentially breaking changes. Therefore, DeploymentConfigs are now deprecated and no new features will be developed. Only security and critical bugs will be fixed. Kubernetes recommends to use a Deployment that configures a ReplicaSet. Therefore, we recommend to migrate existing DeploymentConfig workloads to use Deployments instead.

title: Ceph: Resolving MDS in Journal Replay to Crash to Fail Over loop
issue: Resolving MDS in `Journal Replay` to `Crash` to `Fail Over` loop It's possible for the MDS to fall into an infinite loop of the following:
Journal Replay (up:replay)--> Journal Replay Complete
Transition to other intermediate recovery states, some taking several minutes.
During the transition, MDS spends unexpectedly large amounts of time on some recovery processes, causing it to skip internal heartbeats.
Consequently, the MDS stops sending beacons to the monitors.
This causes the monitors to fail the MDS and replace it with one of the Standby MDS.
The new active MDS starts replaying the journal again.
Without intervention, this sequence of events will go on without ceasing.
resolution: Follow this link: https://docs.ceph.com/en/quincy/cephfs/troubleshooting/#stuck-during-recovery For OCP/OCS/ODF, one musta gotta do this: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7030599
root_cause: Design issue where the MDS can enter into the infinite loop described above due to a extremely large journal replay coupled with a large environment with many connections.

title: ImageContentSourcePolicy doesn't failover to other mirrors after a failure pulling an image
issue: - `ImageContentSourcePolicy` doesn't retry pulling an image from the next mirror when an image pull fails or gets aborted (for example due to 50x errors on the repository side or EOF while pulling image layers).
resolution: - When pulling an image using `ImageContentSourcePolicy` as part of using a mirrored registry ([Configuring image registry repository mirroring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-registry-mirror_image-configuration)), OpenShift does a lookup of the image manifest on the first mirror defined inside `.spec.repositoryDigestMirrors.mirrors[].`- When the image manifest is not found, then, it lookups for the manifest in the subsequent(s) mirrors. If all mirrors fail, the cluster tries the source repository. Once the image manifest is found, OpenShift attempts to pull the image from that mirror.- If something goes wrong while pulling an image from the mirrored registry, pulling the image will not be retried from the next mirror.- Red Hat is analysing the possibility to implement the feature as per [RFE-3991](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3991).
root_cause: - OpenShift attempts to pull `images` from subsequent mirrors defined inside `ImageContentSourcePolicy` only on any of the below cases:- Image manifest was not found on the current mirror.- The mirror is not reachable.- If the mirror is reachable, and the `image` manifest exists, then OpenShift will start pulling the `image`, but in case of failure, while the operation is in progress, it won't retry subsequent mirrors.

title: Etcd Removed Member Archive Snapthots Filling Up The Disk Causing High Disk Utilization On The Master Node.
issue: - Why etcd snapshots causing high disk Utilisation on master nodes post-upgradation of OCP cluster?
resolution: - The etcd members must be in sync on the master nodes.If its in sync,Snapshot files can be removed from the node. ~~~ $ ssh core@ $ rm-rf /sysroot/ostree/deploy/rhcos/var/lib/etcd/member-removed-archive-ddmmyyyy/snap ~~~
root_cause: - The nodes are updated and rebooted. After the reboot completes, the following events occur:- An XFS file system is created on the specified disk.- The disk mounts to /var/lib/etc.- The content from /sysroot/ostree/deploy/rhcos/var/lib/etcd syncs to /var/lib/etcd.- A restore of SELinux labels is forced for /var/lib/etcd.- The old content is not removed.

title: How to build an EAP 7 image in OCP and send to Quay?
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How do I build an EAP image in OCP and send to Quay?- How do I build an EAP image in OCP and send to an external registry?- How do I build an DG image in OCP and send to an external registry?
resolution: Below are the instructions to build an application in OCP and send it to Quay or private registry; ### Steps: 1. Create a new namespace: `$oc new-project build-example` 2. Get your config.json from your local podman: `$ cat $HOME/.docker/config.json` 3. Copy that to a file and make sure to remove other registries on the file, for security reasons* call this copy: config.json; *the passwords there are not encrypted necessarily. 4. Create a secret with that config.json: `$ oc create secret generic dockerhub--from-file=./config.json` 5. Add the secret above on the builder SA: `$ oc edit sa builder` The result will be: ~~~ kind: ServiceAccount apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: builder namespace: build-example secrets:- name: builder-dockercfg-t2685- name: dockerhub ~~~ 6. Create a buildconfig with the output for the registry you would like: ~~~ output: to: kind: DockerImage name: 'quay.io/fdemeloj1/mytime:latest' pushSecret: name: dockerhub ~~~ 7. Build the image: `$ oc start-build time` User can verify that the build will send the image to quay on the build logs: ~~~ Pushing image quay.io/fdemeloj1/mytime:latest... <--- 40 Getting image source signatures 41 Copying blob sha256:e53ae0a7a486542d2f6cae62f64823187075e6a0cc25dc9c5c72281352985857... ~~~ Therefore user can build in OCP and send to Quay's container registry- just forward the output to the outside docker registry. Here the OCP Documentation on it [OCP 4.10- Using docker credentials for private registries](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/cicd/builds/creating-build-inputs.html) ### Using nodeSelector Builds can be targeted to run on specific nodes by specifying labels in the nodeSelector field of a build configuration, where the default is `spec.nodeSelector: null`, meaning it can do the build in **any** OCP node. Default: ~~~ spec: nodeSelector: null ~~~ Example setting for one of the nodes: ~~~ ### get nodes $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION Node-10.internal Ready worker 173m v1.25.11+1485cc9 Node-11.internal Ready worker 170m v1.25.11+1485cc9... ### set label (to unset $ oc label node/ keypair- <-- minus removes) $ oc label node/Node-10.internal fdemeloj-only=true node/Node-10.internal labeled ### confirm the label: $ oc get node/ip-10-0-1-131.ec2.internal-o yaml | grep fdemeloj fdemeloj-only: "true"... ### set the buildconfig for that label: $ oc get bc-o yaml apiVersion: v1 items:- apiVersion: build.openshift.io/v1 kind: BuildConfig... spec: failedBuildsHistoryLimit: 5 nodeSelector: fdemeloj-only: "true" <------------------------- nodeSelector ### start build oc start-build $build_name... ### And confirm the assign: $ oc describe build build_name Name: build_name Namespace: namespace.... Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal Scheduled 26s default-scheduler Successfully assigned build/build_pod to Node-10.internal <-------------------- CONFIRMING THE NODE SELECTOR WORKED; ~~~ ## Issues ### Issue- input image without registry: If the input image is added on the `BuildConfig` without **any registry qualification** so the build will run through all the registries in the `/etc/containers/registries.conf` trying to find that image. In the example below the image `example-image:1.0.0` cannot be found in the registries: ~~~ Pulling image example-image:1.0.0... Resolving "example-image:1.0.0" using unqualified-search registries (/etc/containers/registries.conf) Trying to pull registry.redhat.io/example-image:1.0.0 Trying to pull registry/example-image:1.0.0 Trying to pull quay.io/example-image:1.0.0 Trying to pull docker.io/example-image:1.0.0 ~~~
root_cause: ### Build Process On the process above, the buildconfig yaml creates as output an DockerImage, which is sent from local to the remote registry without passing through a ImageStream (IS), as long as the dockerimage is able to be sent (i.e. the image is built) and the repository is accessible (via container registry details added on the builder SA) so the image will be correctly sent. For troubleshooting specific issues, verify the build logs. The common issues are access to the initial image, access to the external registry. ### Build on local (explanation of imagestream absence) The build of an image to send to an outside registry, as done above, **does not rely** on an ImageStream to be done- hence no ImageStream is required. For localbuild (OCP internal container registry) the IS (ImageStream) must be created first. For fetching from other namespaces the specific role and the rolebinding must be set correctly to be able to fetch from other namespaces. So for example for local builds, where IS and RoleBindings **are required accordingly for other namespace fetching.**

title: WIP: Slow internal networking speeds between pods on AWS
issue: Pods on specific AWS nodes take a long time or timeout when connecting to pods on other nodes over the internal network. For example, when accessing the internal image registry to pull images: ``` 2023-08-31T00:00:21.586122492Z error: failed to ping registry https://image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000: Get "https://image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/": net/http: TLS handshake timeout ``` and ```` Aug 30 09:24:13 ip-10-120-114-142 hyperkube[1589]: E0830 09:24:13.8481971589 remote_image.go:236] "PullImage from image service failed" err="rpc error: code = Unknown desc = pinging container registry image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000: Get \"https://image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/v2/\": dial tcp 172.30.111.154:5000: i/o timeout" image="image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/ / @sha256: " ```` Connection to services outside the cluster appear to be unaffected, even the external routes for internal services, such as the default external route for the internal image-registry.

title: SDN pods in CrashLoopBackOff after manual node restart during a Machine Configuration update
issue: SDN pod is in a CrashLoopBackOff state and reports the following error message in its logs: ``` F0909 00:51:33.835764 85702 cmd.go:118] Failed to start sdn: node SDN setup failed: net/ipv4/ip_forward=0, it must be set to 1 ```
resolution: 1. Perform the diagnostic section below to identify and connect to the impacted node, and confirm the issue matches the current case. 2. Update the ip_forward configuration to enable it. Note this command needs to be run as root, or using `sudo` ``` $ sudo sysctl-w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 ``` #### Example Output ``` net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1 ``` 3. Exit the SSH or debug session, then delete the failed SDN pod to expedite its restart: ``` $ oc delete pod-n openshift-sdn ``` 4. Wait for the SDN pod to be redeployed and observe that it succeeds: ``` $ watch oc get pods-n openshift-sdn ```
root_cause: While not explicitly confirmed, this issue seems to be caused by rebooting a node that was stuck in a "SchedulingDisabled" state while receiving a machine configuration update. By rebooting the node, the network configuration appears to have been corrupted and the ip_forward flag required by the OpenShift SDN pod is disabled.
