title: Can we change the passwords automatically generated by the system and which are stored in secrets?
issue: What are you experiencing? What are you expecting to happen? The passwords defined in the following secrets are too short and needs to be updated with longer and more complex passwords. We need to understand if we can change the passwords in the secrets or is there another methods to modify these passwords to sync up the client and server of these passwords.- backend-internal-api- system-database- system-event-hooks- system-seed- zync Define the value or impact to you or the business The cluster has to be NIST compliant and these passwords are currently not within compliance. Where are you experiencing this behavior? What environment? All environments When does this behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times? N/A
resolution: Hi Werner, Thank you for your patience in waiting for me to update this case. I was running some tests on my side and also discussing this issue further with my team. Some values stored in secrets are used at the time of installation of the 3scale component that uses them, most are static, so not all values in these secrets can be changed in a supported way after installing 3scale, and in some cases if you change them you can break your 3scale instance. Now, there are some secret values that are used at runtime such database usernames and passwords as well as the tokens for accessing some APIs. However, usernames & passwords for portal logins and internal APIs will often be static or configurable at creation time so if portal logins are to be updated they should be done via the portal and then the secrets updated to reflect those [1]. If the database credentials need to be updated then again it should first be completed on the **external DB** (embedded DB wouldn't be supported here) and then updated in the secrets [2]. So to summarize:- Master & Admin passwords should be updated from the portal and **then** updated in the secret (always backup the secret first!) [1]- DB usernames & passwords should be updated on the DB **then** in the secret (Only used when the databases is managed externally) [2]- All other occurrences of passwords cannot be modified, so it's not supported and/or recommended doing this [1] [How to change 3scale GUI Admin and Master Passwords](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5372011) [2] [APImanager CRD Reference: External Components](https://github.com/3scale/3scale-operator/blob/3scale-2.13-stable/doc/apimanager-reference.md#externalcomponentsspec) References: https://github.com/3scale/3scale-operator/blob/3scale-2.13-stable/doc/apimanager-reference.md?plain=1#L564-L692 ### backend-internal-api ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | password | Backend internal API password. Backend internal API is used by System | Autogenerated value | ~~~ ### system-database ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | DB_PASSWORD | Password of the non-administrative database user. Only used when the database is managed externally | Autogenerated value | | ORACLE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD | Password of Oracle's `SYSTEM` administrative user. Required and only used when system's database provided in `URL` field is an external Oracle database | N/A | ~~~ ### system-events-hook ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | PASSWORD | Shared secret to import events from backend to system | Autogenerated value | ~~~ ### system-seed ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | MASTER_PASSWORD | System's master password | Autogenerated value | | ADMIN_PASSWORD | System's admin password of the tenant created by default | Autogenerated value | ~~~ ### zync ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | ZYNC_DATABASE_PASSWORD | Database password associated to the user specified in the `DATABASE_URL` parameter | When the database is managed externally, this parameter is mandatory and must have the same value as the password part of the `DATABASE_URL` parameter in this secret. Otherwise the default value is an autogenerated value if not defined | ~~~ Kind regards, Gustavo Pereira **[Collab]** As discussed most of the content of those secrets is static. Some is used at runtime such as the database usernames and passwords as well as the tokens for accessing some APIs. However, usernames & passwords for portal logins and internal APIs will often be static or configurable at creation time so if portal logins are to be updated they should be done via the portal and then the secrets updated to reflect those. If the database credentials need to be updated then again it should first be completed on the external DB (embedded DB wouldn't be supported here) and then updated in the secrets. For the other passwords such as for the internal backend API and events hook I am not even sure where those are stored and we should state that these ones are not configurable. To summarise:- Master & Admin passwords should be updated from the portal and **then** updated in the secret (always backup the secret first!)- DB usernames & secrets should be updated on the DB **then** in the secret (only supported for external DBs)- All other occurrences of passwords cannot be modified- at least not in a supported manner- so an RFE would be required here After updating secrets a rollout of all deployments that reference those secrets should be executed. Regards, Kevin
root_cause: References:- https://github.com/3scale/3scale-operator/blob/3scale-2.13-stable/doc/apimanager-reference.md?plain=1#L564-L692- https://github.com/3scale/3scale-operator/blob/3scale-2.13-stable/doc/apimanager-reference.md#externalcomponentsspec- https://github.com/3scale/apisonator/blob/66ff467687d97e9a96a26b554fe0537a58eb5f1e/openshift/3scale_backend.conf#L22- https://github.com/3scale/apisonator/blob/66ff467687d97e9a96a26b554fe0537a58eb5f1e/docs/features.md?plain=1#L79 ### backend-internal-api ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | username | Backend internal API username. Backend internal API is used by System | `3scale_api_user` | | password | Backend internal API password. Backend internal API is used by System | Autogenerated value | ~~~ This secret defines the env var `CONFIG_INTERNAL_API_PASSWORD` in the following pods:- backend-listener- system-app- system-sidekiq ### system-database ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | URL | URL of the Porta database. Mandatory when the instance is managed externally. The format of the URL must be: `://: @ / `, where ` ` must be an already existing user in the external database with full permissions on the specified ` ` logical database and ` ` must be an already existing logical database in the external database. When the database is managed internally, the ` ` part of the URL can be set instead of an autogenerated one. In order to do that (if desired) set `URL` as the value specified in the `Default Value` column with the ` ` placeholder replaced with the desired value.| A default is only set when database is managed internally. Otherwise it is a mandatory field. When managed internally: If MySQL is used as System's database (the default behavior): `mysql2://root: @system-mysql/mysql`. If PostgreSQL is used(when `.spec.system.database.postgresql` is set): `postgresql://root: @system-postgresql/system`. | | DB_USER | Non-administrative database username. Only used when the database is managed externally | `mysql` | | DB_PASSWORD | Password of the non-administrative database user. Only used when the database is managed externally | Autogenerated value | | ORACLE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD | Password of Oracle's `SYSTEM` administrative user. Required and only used when system's database provided in `URL` field is an external Oracle database | N/A | ~~~ This secret defines the env var `MYSQL_PASSWORD` in the following pods:- system-mysql ### system-events-hook ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | URL | The URL to System's event reports endpoint, used by Backend to report its events | `http://system-master:3000/master/events/import` | | PASSWORD | Shared secret to import events from backend to system | Autogenerated value | ~~~ This secret do not defines any env var. ### system-seed ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | MASTER_USER | System's master username | `master` | | MASTER_PASSWORD | System's master password | Autogenerated value | | MASTER_ACCESS_TOKEN | System's master access token | Autogenerated value | | MASTER_DOMAIN | System's master domain name | `master` | | ADMIN_USER | System's admin user of the tenant created by default | `admin` | | ADMIN_PASSWORD | System's admin password of the tenant created by default | Autogenerated value | | ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN | System's admin access token of the tenant created by default | Autogenerated value | | TENANT_NAME | Tenant name under the root that Admin UI will be available with-admin suffix | ` ` | ~~~ This secret defines the env var `USER_PASSWORD` and `MASTER_PASSWORD` in the following pods:- system-app- system-sidekiq ### zync ~~~ | **Field** | **Description** | **Default value** | |--- |--- |--- | | DATABASE_URL | PostgreSQL database used by Zync. Only used when the database is managed externally | Format: `postgresql://: @: /zync_production`, where ` ` must be an already existing user in the external database with full permissions on the `zync_production` logical database, `zync_production` logical database must be an already existing logical database in the external database and the specified value of ` ` must be the same as the `ZYNC_DATABASE_PASSWORD` parameter in this secret. Otherwise it has a default value, which is `postgresql://zync: @zync-database:5432/zync_production` | | ZYNC_DATABASE_PASSWORD | Database password associated to the user specified in the `DATABASE_URL` parameter | When the database is managed externally, this parameter is mandatory and must have the same value as the password part of the `DATABASE_URL` parameter in this secret. Otherwise the default value is an autogenerated value if not defined | | SECRET_KEY_BASE | Zync's application key generator to encrypt communications | Autogenerated value | | ZYNC_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN | Authentication token used to authenticate System when calling Zync | Autogenerated value | ~~~ This secret defines the env var `POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD` in the following pods:- zync-database

title: Requests returning 403 errors and backend-worker is in crash loopback state in 3scale
issue: - All the requests to APICast gateway is returning 403 errors- backend-worker pod is in `Crash Loop Back-off` state- backend-redis pod shows following errors ~~~ 1:M 31 Feb 12:00:00.000

Background saving started by pid XXXXX XXXXX:C 31 Feb 12:00:00.000 # Failed opening the RDB file dump.rdb (in server root dir /var/lib/redis/data) for saving: Transport endpoint is not connected 1:M 31 Feb 12:00:00.000 # Background saving error ~~~
resolution: This error message indicates that there is an issue with the underlying backend-redis persistent volume storage. Typically this error is presented when using network file storage (i.e. NFS, Gluster) and the pod is unable to communicate with the remote file server while trying to read the `dump.rdb` file. To resolve this issue, first an investigation should be done to determine why the pod is unable to communicate with the remote file server. If you need help identifying the cause, open a support case with the Openshift Storage team for assistance. After any issues with the persistent volume have been resolved, API requests should work as expected. If the data from the storage volume was lost, refer to [Re-synchronization of backend-redis with System](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3443351)

title: How to use external NFS share directly into pod without storage class or pv
issue: - External NFS share directly into pod without storage class or pv.- Creating PV/PVC over NFS share is not going to solve the purpose.- Since the NFS is attached to the node directly there are chances of getting disconnected.
resolution: - How can external NFS be attached directly?- Using logic/code/binaries build an image with the nfs utils and client (and give the pod some escalated capabilities) to mount an nfs share within a pod on a locally mounted nfs on VM.- Note:- NFS share its completely managed from users end and RedHat don't provide support for it nor do have any documentation related OpenShift.- If user have concerns regarding the disconnection then they should use k8s native storage objects / PVs and RedHat don't recommend anything other than this for production unless its exception.

title: Issue while connecting to csi backend socket
issue: - Issue while connecting to csi socket ~~~ W0908 13:21:12.616499 1 connection.go:173] Still connecting to unix:///var/run/csi/csi.sock level=info msg="/csi.v1.Node/NodeStageVolume:: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = exceeds size limit: StagingTargetPath: max=128, size=142" ~~~
resolution: - Restart the CSI operator and the controller pods to reestablish the connection.- Reach out to the CSI vendor for finding the exact cause of the issue.

title: [RHOCP 4.x] Can a Pod be automatically restarted after a Secret is updated?
issue: - A `Secret` of an external application gets rotated regularly.- An External Secret Operator (upstream project) running on the cluster constantly checks and pull in the latest password and update the secret in OpenShift.- When the `Secret` is updated and correctly reflected in OpenShift, the required `Pods` are not restarted, requiring manual intervention.
resolution: - As of 14/Sep/23 there is no built-in/supported method to accomplish this automatically.- One possible method would be to run a bash script along the application so it can terminate the `Pod` on the `Secret` (or `ConfigMap`).- This issue is being tracked via JIRA [RFE-4655](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4655)
root_cause: - `ConfigMaps`/`Secrets` should just update dynamically when they are mounted into the `Pods` and send an inotify message to the processes that are running.- This is not applicable when they are updated by External Secret Operator (upstream project).

title: Unable to install Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform from registry.ci.openshift.org
issue: ~~~ Error: initializing source docker://registry.ci.openshift.org/ocp/release@sha256:352ad2d17474278d17853a804aa68764c719e65367078e5c89ca1cddfbf5cf2d: reading manifest sha256:352ad2d17474278d17853a804aa68764c719e65367078e5c89ca1cddfbf5cf2d in registry.ci.openshift.org/ocp/release: unauthorized: authentication required Jan 10 10:42:08 bootstrap.ocp4.example.com release-image-download.sh[2042]: Pull failed. Retrying registry.ci.openshift.org/ocp/release@sha256:352ad2d17474278d17853a804aa68764c719e65367078e5c89ca1cddfbf5cf2d... ~~~
resolution: - Check the OpenShift version. Here OpenShift version indicates that it is using CI binary. The pull secrets for CI expire, which might have to refresh periodically. ~~~ # openshift-install version openshift-install 4.x built from commit aaa978bb5d76472df23f6e9029 release image registry.ci.openshift.org/ocp/release@sha256:352ad2d17474278d17853a804aa68764c719e65367078e5c89ca1cddfbf5cf2d ~~~- Use the GA version of the installer, which uses quay.io as release image and with that use the pull secret obtained from https://console.redhat.com/openshift/install/pull-secret- GA version of OpenShift Container Platform can be found [HERE](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp)
root_cause: - Due to usage of OpenShift binaries from the https://docs.ci.openshift.org/- It is advised to use OpenShift binaries downloaded from https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp

title: /opt/amq/bin/launch.sh: line 527: /usr/bin/sed: Argument list too long
issue: The following message ~~~ Doing merge_all... /opt/amq/bin/launch.sh: line 527: /usr/bin/sed: Argument list too long Done. ~~~ gets logged during pod start
resolution: Use broker properties instead. More more details see [How to define broker's security settings separately from the ActiveMQArtemis CR's implementation](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7028652)
root_cause: The issue is caused by a very large **addressSettings** section in broker CR file. The resulting command line exceeds shell's command line limit.

title: The external URL is not reachable from the pod
issue: - The external URL hosted outside the Openshift cluster is not reachable from the pod where the same URL is reachable from the node.- The external URL is hosted using the IP address as same as the Openshift cluster network subnet.
resolution: - It is not possible to reach the external URL hosted as same as the cluster network IP address. **Any one of the below workarounds can be followed:**- Change the IP address of the external URL other than the Opeshift clusterNetwork CIDR.- Reinstall the cluster with a different clusterNetwork CIDR.- Run application POD on Hostnetwork and set a route specifically at host where application POD is running. Note that if another application POD on the Openshift cluster gets the same IP then that POD wont be accessible from node having custom route.- Host a reverse proxy within Openshift cluster so that reverse proxy can forward the traffic to the external endpoint when accessed via reverse proxy IP.
root_cause: - The issue is due to the subnet conflict. The external application is hosted on a IP address and that IP address belongs to Openshift ClusterNetwork CIDR which was set during cluster installation.- The traffic will be routed internally within the cluster as per the route configuration.

title: "mkdir: can't create directory '/consul/extra-config': Permission denied" While deploying an application

title: Setup-Job pod stuck in a terminating state and blocking the cluster upgrade
issue: - The `Setup-Job` pod is stuck in a terminating state.- As a result, the `machine config pool` prevented `cluster upgrade` by disabling scheduling on the `node` on which `job pod` is running.
resolution: - Check that is there any `mutating admission webhook` installed that mutates the `pod`after it is patched by the `job controller`.- Check all existing `mutating admission webhooks` and determine which of them is responsible for the mutation. ~~~ $ oc get mutatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io-n ~~~- Then, temporarily disable the culprit `webhook`, completing the upgrade, and re-enabling the `webhook`.- For future upgrades, the same steps need to be repeated.

title: Creating cpu/memory dumps from kube-apiserver pods in Openshift Container Platform 4.
issue: The kube-apiserver pods could be consuming specific amounts of cpu/memory, so it is needed to check which call is provoking this behavior to analyze the environment.
resolution: - Run the following script from your bastion host with access to `oc` CLI: ~~~ #!/bin/bash ## Usage: script.sh mkdir perfdata cd perfdata || exit 1 ### affected kube-apiserver pod KUBE_API_POD=$1 ### pids to kill PIDS_TO_KILL=() ### Obtaining container image CONTAINER_IMAGE=$(oc get pods-n openshift-kube-apiserver "${KUBE_API_POD}"-ojson |jq.spec.containers[0].image-r) ### Port-forward to kube-apiserver pod to query debug endpoints nohup oc port-forward-n openshift-kube-apiserver "${KUBE_API_POD}" 8888:6443 > port-forward-nohup & PIDS_TO_KILL+=($!) sleep 5 oc get--raw /debug/pprof/allocs--server https://localhost:8888 > "${KUBE_API_POD}".allocs.pprof; oc get--raw /debug/pprof/heap?debug=1--server https://localhost:8888 > "${KUBE_API_POD}".heap.pprof; oc get--raw /metrics--server https://localhost:8888 > "${KUBE_API_POD}".metrics; oc get--raw /debug/pprof/profile--server https://localhost:8888 > "${KUBE_API_POD}".profile.pprof.gz; ### Generate temporary pod to copy the binary from (with randomly suffixed name to avoid collisions) POD_NAME="copy-binary-$(tr-dc 'a-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | fold-w 10 | head-n 1)" oc run--pod-running-timeout=5m--restart=Always--command--image "${CONTAINER_IMAGE}" "${POD_NAME}" sleep infinity oc wait--for condition=Ready "pod/${POD_NAME}" 2> /dev/null oc cp--retries=10 "${POD_NAME}:/bin/kube-apiserver" "kube-apiserver" oc delete pod "${POD_NAME}" oc wait--for delete "pod/${POD_NAME}" 2> /dev/null kill-9 "${PIDS_TO_KILL[@]}" ~~~ It's also helpful to [collect audit logs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/security/audit-log-view.html) to see which users are using the pod the most.- Gather the `audit.log` for a master node on which your API server pod is running: ~~~ oc adm node-logs node--path=kube-apiserver/audit.log > audit.log ~~~- Find out which service accounts are doing the most API server queries: ~~~ jq.user.username-r audit.log | sort | uniq-c | sort-n ~~~ ~~~ Truncated output........... 2145 system:serviceaccount:openshift-apiserver:openshift-apiserver-sa 3344 system:serviceaccount:openshift-cluster-version:default 3651 system:serviceaccount:openshift-authentication-operator:authentication-operator 5851 system:serviceaccount:openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator:kube-controller-manager-operator 6090 system:serviceaccount:openshift-apiserver-operator:openshift-apiserver-operator 6498 system:serviceaccount:openshift-kube-apiserver-operator:kube-apiserver-operator 6892 system:serviceaccount:openshift-kube-scheduler-operator:openshift-kube-scheduler-operator 15509 system:serviceaccount:openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager:olm-operator-serviceaccount ~~~ With these two data points, it is possible to see which component is making most calls and what type of calls are causing the memory to fill up.

title: How we can check our DNS Cache is working or not on openshift cluster
issue: - To verify if the `dns` `cache` is working or not and requests are `served` from the `cache`.
resolution: - If `monitoring` is enabled (via the `prometheus` plugin) then the following `metrics` are exported, you can run them by going to OpenShift console--> observation--> metrics. ~~~ coredns_cache_entries{server, type, zones, view}- Total elements in the cache by cache type. coredns_cache_hits_total{server, type, zones, view}- Counter of cache hits by cache type. coredns_cache_misses_total{server, zones, view}- Counter of cache misses.- Deprecated, derive misses from cache hits/requests counters. coredns_cache_requests_total{server, zones, view}- Counter of cache requests. coredns_cache_prefetch_total{server, zones, view}- Counter of times the cache has prefetched a cached item. coredns_cache_drops_total{server, zones, view}- Counter of responses excluded from the cache due to request/response question name mismatch. coredns_cache_served_stale_total{server, zones, view}- Counter of requests served from stale cache entries. coredns_cache_evictions_total{server, type, zones, view}- Counter of cache evictions. ~~~ **Also, we can test it, by taking [tcpdump](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4569211) from a pod in the below following way:**- Take any of the `application` pod which resolves needs to resolve a `hostname` from the `nameserver`. title: cnsmgr-suspend-create-volume vmware CSI feature in Red Hat vSphere CSI Driver.
issue: - Red Hat provided `vSphere CSI driver` doesn't have `cnsmgr-suspend-create-volume` feature.
resolution: - [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3291) was created to implement this feature in Red Hat provided a `vSphere CSI driver`.- From OCP 4.13, `cnsmgr-suspend-create-volume` feature is enabled by default.
root_cause: - Red Hat `vSphere CSI driver` shipped the 2.4 version and in upstream `vSphere CSI` this feature is available from version 2.5+.

title: ARO Private cluster with Application Gateway CORS and timeout errors.
issue: Customers utilizing an `Azure ARO cluster` with `Application Gateway` configured have reported difficulties when attempting to access web applications hosted within this cluster. **Scenarios:*
**Internal Network Access (Within `Azure Vnet`):*

When users are located within the same `Azure Vnet` as the cluster, they have encountered a `403 Forbidden` response displayed on their web browser. Additionally, a `CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)` error message is also presented, indicating potential issues with requests being blocked due to cross-domain policies. **External Network Access:*

On the other hand, when users attempt to access the web application from a network outside the Azure Vnet, the browser struggles to establish a connection with the cluster, typically resulting in `dial tcp timeout` errors.

title: Unable to access  RHOCP web console in the browser
issue: Cluster web console fqdn is getting timed out in the browser even if all console pods are in running state.
resolution: Check and configure the correct route on the host from where web console is not accessible so that it can reach to cluster ingress VIP of the cluster. If the host machine is outside of OpenShift cluster then configure correct routing on the local host.

title: Operator Upgrade Stuck in Pending State on RHOCP
issue: - During upgrade of any operator via GUI or CLI, it fails with an error message. ~~~ Bundle unpacking failed. Reason: DeadlineExceeded, and Message: Job was active longer than specified deadline ~~~
resolution: - Get the names of any failing jobs and related config maps in the openshift-marketplace ~~~ $ oc get jobs,cm-n openshift-marketplace NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE job.batch/00701ef4b3edf6a31523be94fd0c9b10ef9d7ab8d7d4657b738fbb2f1cd9c9c 1/1 11s 321d job.batch/010ce5076702bc23682959e87165039edbfaafeee64a1aeb8aa3d31ba59ea18 1/1 10s 417d job.batch/038fb916ef8c0cb77e9cdd489a691800f2398670191009838e28016be45cb10 1/1 16s 300d job.batch/09d55c1d83be59138b65b5d1e1beea0926ed7d2b89ec7388dd93e72b6d89d15 0/1 6m8s 1d <..> NAME DATA AGE configmap/00701ef4b3edf6a31523be94fd0c9b10ef9d7ab8d7d4657b738fbb2f1cd9c9c 2 321d configmap/010ce5076702bc23682959e87165039edbfaafeee64a1aeb8aa3d31ba59ea18 2 417d configmap/038fb916ef8c0cb77e9cdd489a691800f2398670191009838e28016be45cb10 8 300d configmap/09d55c1d83be59138b65b5d1e1beea0926ed7d2b89ec7388dd93e72b6d89d15 6 30d <..> ~~~- Delete all the jobs not completed 0/1 ~~~ $ oc delete job.batch/09d55c1d83be59138b65b5d1e1beea0926ed7d2b89ec7388dd93e72b6d89d15-n openshift-marketplace job.batch "09d55c1d83be59138b65b5d1e1beea0926ed7d2b89ec7388dd93e72b6d89d15" deleted ~~~- Delete the corresponding config maps of the jobs not completed in openshift-marketplace ~~~ $ oc delete configmap/09d55c1d83be59138b65b5d1e1beea0926ed7d2b89ec7388dd93e72b6d89d15-n openshift-marketplace configmap "09d55c1d83be59138b65b5d1e1beea0926ed7d2b89ec7388dd93e72b6d89d15" deleted ~~~- Delete the failed install plan in the namespace found using the steps in the Diagnostic section ~~~ $ oc delete ip-n ~~~- Restart the OLM pod in openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager namespace by deleting the pod ~~~ $ oc get pod-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager |grep olm $ oc delete pod-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager ~~~- After completing all the steps, check the new install plan status to see if it can start successfully and the operator is upgraded ~~~ $ oc get sub,csv,installplan-n ~~~
root_cause: The cause is not 100% known but a possible theory is the first time the operator bundle was pulled down from the marketplace, the extract job failed (probably due to an issue accessing the remote image, etc.) and corrupted the configmap. Therefore, the operator manifest was most likely corrupt. Once that happens, any repeat install attempts to use the same job and configmap to install another instance of the operator (i.e. in another namespace) will fail.

title: Getting the authentication token for a Service Account in OpenShift
issue: - View authentication tokens for a service account- Access another or external cluster with a service account token- Automate or operate on builds, deployments, etc. in any project using a service account token
resolution: > **Note:** For OCP 4.11 and later, refer to [How to create a long lived service account token in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7025261), as the token is not stored in the cluster and cannot be recovered. 1. If the service account does not exist yet, create it: $ oc create serviceaccount ${SERVICE_ACCOUNT}-n ${NAMESPACE} 2. Get the authentication token for the service account:--- In OCP 3.11 and OCP 4.10 or lower--- $ oc sa get-token-n ${NAMESPACE} ${SERVICE_ACCOUNT} 3. If needed, test the service account token's API access: $ oc get user '~'--token=$(oc sa get-token-n ${NAMESPACE} ${SERVICE_ACCOUNT}) 4. Grant any required permissions to the service account 5. Login with the service account token: $ TOKEN=$(oc sa get-token-n ${NAMESPACE} ${SERVICE_ACCOUNT}) $ oc login--token=${TOKEN} Alternatively, create a kubeconfig using the token: $ oc-n ${NAMESPACE} sa create-kubeconfig ${SERVICE_ACCOUNT} > ${SERVICE_ACCOUNT}.kubeconfig > > **Note:** in step (5), as "oc sa" is deprecated and will be removed in future versions, we can extract the token also by getting it from the generated secret or by doing again "oc create token" and using the output.
root_cause: Service accounts have token secrets automatically associated with them so that services and processes can authenticate remotely and use them. See [Using Service Accounts in Applications](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/authentication/using-service-accounts-in-applications.html) for more information

title: After vCenter cluster migration - machines are in a Phase of Failed
issue: - After migration of vCenter- Machines are showing a `Phase of Failed`
resolution: Steps to resolve this issue: **If OpenShift version is below 4.11 then follow steps 1 to 2 otherwise skip to step 3** 1. Make a copy/backup of your existing oc binary 2. Download from this [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/290/ver=4.11/rhel---8/4.11.34/x86_64/product-software) and install the OpenShift command `oc` 4.11 or above. This should still work on your version of OpenShift which is 4.8. It can be tested by simply running basic commands to make sure there are no errors such as: ~~~ $ oc get machines-A ~~~ 3. Then for each machine run the following command (replace with the required machine name that is in a `Phase of Failed`): ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api patch--subresource status machines--type json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/status/phase", "value":"Provisioned"}]' ~~~
root_cause: **Warning** This is an unsupported procedure as per this KCS-> [Migrating OCP to another vCenter](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6509731) and although the above appears to resolve this issue- there is no certainty of the long time affects this may have.

title: Error 400 - Non UTF 8 Characters Are Being Rejected By ElasticSearch
issue: - `Elasticsearch` `current.log` show: `Invalid UTF-8 middle byte 0x6e` and are being rejected by `Elasticsearch`
resolution: Upgrade to `RHOCP Logging` version 5.4.4 or later to resolve this issue Please follow this guide [How to Upgrade Cluster Logging](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/logging/cluster-logging-upgrading.html)
root_cause: Issue was resolved in Logging 5.4 as non `UTF-8` characters where being rejected by `Elasticsearch`

title: Understanding the InstallationDisk Path in the install-config.yaml
issue: - The [Installing OpenShift](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/installing/installing_sno/install-sno-installing-sno.html) documentation may not be clear enough to describe the use of the `InstallationDisk` path within the `install-config.yaml` file.
resolution: The installation disk path can either be the `direct device` reference or the `Device ID`. Either use this method (example direct disk drive reference) `/dev/vda2` or the device id `/dev/disk/by-id/lvm-pv-uuid-SCEyrl-7M1H-7aVn-0drJ-e2d7-4mFF-RaYBbY`. title: oc adm top nodes - Allocatable and Capacity
issue: - `oc adm top node` displays and calculates memory
resolution: - The `oc adm top nodes` command by default displays memory usage as `Allocatable` not capacity.- This is by design as `Allocatable` is how `OpenShift/Kubernetes` calculates the memory on a node to know if there is enough memory for a scheduled task.- `Allocatable` on a `Kubernetes` node is defined as the amount of compute resources that are available for pods. The scheduler does not over-subscribe `Allocatable`.- If capacity needs to be shown then the `--show-capacity` can be used as follows: ~~~ $ oc adm top nodes--show-capacity ~~~

title: How to Increase the log level of the Operator Lifecycle Manager
issue: To better troubleshoot the Operator Lifecycle Manager functionality, how can the log level of the Operator be increased?
Can the verbosity of the Operator Lifecycle Manager be changed?
resolution: **WARNING**: This procedure includes marking components as unmanaged, which is not supported. Please follow it only as per Red Hat Support or Red Hat Engineering instructions. First, mark the the `olm-operator` deployment within the `openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager` namespace as unmanaged by the cluster version operator. Otherwise, cluster version operator will reconcile its own deployment, reverting the log level back to default. The way to do so is: ``` oc patch clusterversion/version--type json-p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/overrides","value":[{"kind":"Deployment","group":"apps","name":"olm-operator","namespace":"openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager","unmanaged": true}]}]' ``` Then, edit the `olm-operator` deployment within the `openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager` namespace to apply the `--debug` argument. One possible way to do so is with `oc edit`, like in the below example: ~~~ ~|⇒ oc edit-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager deploy/olm-operator spec: template: spec: containers:- args:...---debug ~~~ Once the higher log level is no longer required, the override must be removed so that cluster version operator deployment becomes managed again. It can be done like this: ``` oc patch clusterversion/version--type json-p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/overrides"}]' ``` Note that the command above will remove all the overrides configured in the Cluster Version Operator.

title: BufferOverflowError error with buffer space has too many data in RHOCP 4
issue: Getting `BufferOverflowError error="buffer space has too many data"` in OpenShift
Getting `BufferOverflowError error="buffer space has too many data"` when forwarding logs to CloudWatch
resolution: Fix the receiver performance (not a sender fluentd side, it's usually Elasticsearch, CloudWatch, etc.) if it's having a performance issue. To refresh the slow and buffer overflow situation, recreate the fluentd pod with `--grace-period=600` option. It allows the fluentd to suspend the log reading and flush the buffer data not yet sent to the receiver before exiting. This is important especially the fluentd is configured to use a [memory buffer](https://docs.fluentd.org/configuration/buffer-section#flushing-parameters) like when CloudWatch forwarding is configured. ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging delete pod collector-jvmjn--grace-period=600 ~~~
root_cause: Log generating rate is higher than log sending rate. This is usually caused by the log receiver is having performance issues or the performance of the intermediate components in the middle of the OpenShift cluster and the receiver is not good

title: Opening pod's terminal fails with "The terminal connection has closed" in OpenShift 4
issue: - When trying to access pod's terminal from the web console, it doesn't work and shows the error "The terminal connection has closed"- Trying oc rsh to any pod doesn't work either and shows an error calling a webhook: ~~~ $ oc rsh test-5f8cdbbb6f-f4hpk Error from server (InternalError): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "validate-exec.devworkspace-controller.svc": Post "https://devworkspace-webhookserver.openshift-operators.svc:443/validate?timeout=10s": no endpoints available for service "devworkspace-webhookserver" ~~~
resolution: Removing the Web terminal operator requires its dependencies to be manually removed as mentioned in the official [documentation.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/web_console/web_terminal/uninstalling-web-terminal.html) **NOTE:** These steps removes the Web Terminal Operator intentionally, therefore the lost of access to the pod is expected.
root_cause: The Web Terminal Operator creates the `mutatingwebhookconfigurations` and `validatingwebhookconfigurations` webhooks that are called each time a terminal session is open on a pod, either from CLI or the Console UI. If only the operators are removed, the webhooks are not removed and they are still called each time a terminal session is tried either from Console UI or CLI, throwing the error.

title: oauth logs increase when running a script within OpenShift
issue: When running scripts within `OpenShift` the `oauth` logs increase. However, they do not get updated or increase, if they are running outside of `OpenShift`, for example running a `Linux` script to check the `storage` of a `pod`
resolution: When a user is created using a `certificate` it uses the `kubeconfig` to hold this information and this is using a different `API server` and therefore will not be authenticated through the `oauth` operator. This method would be used if when running a `script` outside of `OpenShift` e.g. running from a `Linux` `cronjob` using the `--kubeconfig=` parameter. Whereas, if the user is using a `secret` then this will be using the `oauth` method of logging into this system and therefore it would use the `oauth` `API server`and logging. If the logging level was set to `debug` the logs would increase more so due to the amount of information it records.

title: Not able to schedule pods on new nodes

So there will be no issue with the workloads if the workloads are defined to be distributed in several nodes.
root_cause: - Labels on the nodes not correct.- New deployed nodes IP addresses are not appended in `spec.noProxy` of cluster-wide proxy.

title: Details on EAP externalization to DG pods (stream via internal svc)
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Details on EAP externalization to DG pods (stream via internal svc)
root_cause: The internal service has multiple endpoints, but it is not headless, and it will return only one pod at a time in a round-robin manner- so the DG pods are randomly chosen. When the EAP is externalizing to DG, it will fetch from the internal service the Pod IP and establish a stable connection with the pod the internal service returns. This stable connection is called a stream; To make EAP use another DG Pod, the user needs to break the connection already established, i.e. terminate the pod and create a new pod a new stream. Workflow ~~~ EAP pod pings service's host/IP service picks one of the dg pods and replies with one IP (one, not multiple) A stable connection EAP-> service-> DG pod IP is established ~~~ In summary: The internal svc service, provided by DG Operator, can have multiple endpoints- but it returns just one at time (one DG pod IP randomly chosen). EAP, when doing the externalization, will establish an EAP-> DG with the IP provided by the internal service, i.e. one DG IP. Corollary 1: When talking EAP to DG (e.g. externalization configuration- via remote-cache-container) the distribution of the cache entries will be done by the DG cluster itself. So the round-robin's service's is not to be blamed in case of uneven distribution (the internal service does not send each request a different DG Pod IP). Corollary 2: Using a headless service makes no difference on the above behavior, because for the type of the hot rod client's operation fetching the DG IP, still gets one DG IP at a time, i.e the stream between EAP and DG is established between two pods. Corollary 3: Given the EAP establishes one connection with_one_ DG IP, dropping that pod will drop the EAP connection. There will be no fail-over to other DG pods. In this matter also, max_retries property on the rod hot client can be used for fail back to. EAP pod might be stuck on the IP that doesn't exist anymore, and therefore, need to drop the EAP pod itself to re-connect. Example: Given the bug described [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7005531), i.e. the absence of the `publishNotReadyAddresses` property that causes a cluster not to be formed, each DG Pod will act separately and connect_at time_. Therefore, the only way to have a shield against a DG pod dropping affecting the service is to tunnel the connection via a load balancer's IP. It can be either the route's haproxy or service type load balancer, in a way that the client connects to this IP and not to the DG pods' IP. This may implicate losing client intelligence, however.

title: vSphere failed to create  volume. Error: auth service: no shared datastore found for block volume
issue: When creating a Persistent Volume Claim using csi-driver, the claim will stay in pending status with the following error message: ~~~ 'Warning' reason: 'ProvisioningFailed' failed to provision volume with StorageClass "csi-thin": rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to create volume. Error: auth service: no shared datastore found for block volume provisioning ~~~
resolution: In OCP 4.x, while using CSI-Drivers the vSphere username must contain the full domain name.- username@vsphere.local- DOMAIN\username ### Modifying the vSphere credentials The username and password are the base64 encoded values of the keys.password and.username in the secret vsphere-creds under namespace kube-system. ~~~ $ oc get secret vsphere-creds-n kube-system-o yaml apiVersion: v1 data: vsphere.openshift.example.com.password: dGVzdHBhc3N3b3JkCg== vsphere.openshift.example.com.username: cmVkaGF0Cg== kind: Secret metadata: name: vsphere-creds namespace: kube-system type: Opaque ~~~ The above secret indicates that the vSphere user is redhat and the vSphere user password is testpassword for server vsphere.openshift.example.com. To update the password, simply edit the secret and modify the value of keys with the new base64 encoded data. The secret can be updated using the following command: ~~~ # oc edit secret vsphere-creds-n kube-system ~~~ #### Example: 1. Before making any changes, be sure to backup the current configuration. ~~~ $ oc get secret vsphere-creds-o yaml-n kube-system > creds_backup.yaml $ oc get cm cloud-provider-config-o yaml-n openshift-config > cloud.yaml ~~~ 2. The new password will need to be base64 encoded and then added to the vsphere-creds secret. To encode the password run: ~~~ $ echo-n "redhat@vsphere.local" | base64-w0 cmVkaGF0QHZzcGhlcmUubG9jYWw= ~~~ It is important to use the above command to generate the base64 encoded passwords, otherwise "new-line" characters may be included. **Warning**: not using the option-n on the command echo may alter the resulting base64 string. 3. Make a copy of the vsphere-creds backup yaml file and update it with the newly encoded password. Then save the file and replace the vsphere-creds secret with the updated definition. ~~~ $ cp creds_backup.yaml creds.yaml $ vi creds.yaml apiVersion: v1 data: vsphere.openshift.example.com.password: dGVzdHBhc3N3b3JkCg== vsphere.openshift.example.com.username: cmVkaGF0Cg== <===== Copy your base64 encoded username here kind: Secret metadata: name: vsphere-creds namespace: kube-system type: Opaque $ oc replace-f creds.yaml ~~~ Note: In the above example vsphere.openshift.example.com refers to the hostname of the vCenter instance being used. The hostname must match the vCenter hostname found in the cloud-provider-config ConfigMap in the openshift-config namespace. 4. Finally, verify the username in the secret by decoding the base64 value. ~~~ $ oc extract secret/vsphere-creds-n kube-system--to=- ~~~ Then test the credentials by executing a storage or machine provisioning operation that requires vSphere integration in order to work. 5. If necessary, force a redeployment of the kube-controller-manager pods. ~~~ $ oc patch kubecontrollermanager cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~
root_cause: CSI-drivers components require a username with a full domain name to authenticate on vCenter.

title: Failed to install OCP with log error: The bootstrap machine is unable to resolve API and/or API-Int Server URLs
issue: - Failed to install an OCP cluster- The installation logs show the following warnings/errors ~~~ time="2023-04-12T17:17:00-04:00" level=debug msg="ssh: connect to host xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx port 22: Connection refused\r" time="2023-04-12T17:17:00-04:00" level=debug msg="Collecting info from xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx" time="2023-04-12T17:17:00-04:00" level=debug msg="lost connection" time="2023-04-12T17:17:01-04:00" level=warning msg="Unable to stat /home/kni/clusterconfigs/serial-log-bundle-20230412171632.tar.gz, skipping" time="2023-04-12T17:17:03-04:00" level=error msg="Bootstrap failed to complete: timed out waiting for the condition" time="2023-04-12T17:17:03-04:00" level=error msg="Failed to wait for bootstrapping to complete. This error usually happens when there is a problem with control plane hosts that prevents the control plane operators from creating the control plane." time="2023-04-12T17:17:03-04:00" level=warning msg="The bootstrap machine is unable to resolve API and/or API-Int Server URLs" ~~~
resolution: The error message `The bootstrap machine is unable to resolve API and/or API-Int Server URLs` indicated a few possible networking related issues for example: NTP and DNS, and DHCP. As configuring the network environment is part of the prerequisite for installing Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP), please refer to the figure in [Configuring networking](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/installing/installing_bare_metal_ipi/ipi-install-installation-workflow.html#configuring-networking_ipi-install-installation-workflow) to confirm the correct network setup, and that they satisfy the pre-install requirements. Here are some key components we suggest you to troubleshoot/verify: ####DHCP Review DHCP lease and make sure your subnet is allocating out IP addresses, DNS, NTP, timezone and router gateway IP. Test DHCP with the host to validate, it is possible that DHCP was set but the lease was not accepted. Test downloads from the test host (check if bastion host is on the "machineNetwork" subnet, and validate by reviewing DHCP leases, and can also then review its IP and MAC addresses). #### NTP Check underlying NTP, if hosts are out of sync the latency might trigger the error. ####DNS records Make sure DNS records for `api` and `api-int` were created. ####Reverse DNS Check if the reverse DNS lookup is set up properly in the `install-config.yaml` and ignition manifest. Here is an example for the configuration: ~~~ interfaces:- name: type: ethernet state: up ipv4: address:- ip: prefix-length: 24 enabled: true dns-resolver: config: server:- ~~~ For further details on testing the correct DNS name resolution and connection, we suggest using the following tools:- ping- nslookup- dig- host Further details can be found in this article: [Linux troubleshooting commands: 4 tools for DNS name resolution problems](https://www.redhat.com/sysadmin/DNS-name-resolution-troubleshooting-tools) **NOTE** Please ensure cleaning up all resources related to the previous installation before starting a new installation, please see [Reinstalling the OpenShift Container Platform cluster](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/installing/installing-troubleshooting.html#restarting-installation_installing-troubleshooting) for further details.

title: podman system prune: failed to prune image
issue: - Not possible to remove images with podman.- `podman system prune` command fails with error: ~~~ Error: failed to prune image: error reading image "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" as image: error locating item named "manifest" for image with ID "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx": file does not exist ~~~- `podman rmi` command fails with error: ~~~ ERRO[0000] error reading image "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" as image: error locating item named "manifest" for image with ID "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx": file does not exist ~~~
resolution: **WARNING:** Do not use `podman system prune` on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.12 until [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7037230](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7037230) is addressed. **Note:** change the `xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` with the digest of the image. If there is enough space in the disk, try to download again the image (refer to the Diagnostic Steps): 1. Search for the `RepoDigests` in the inspect: ~~~ [root@node_name /]# podman inspect xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx--format "RepoDigests: {{.RepoDigests}}" ~~~ 2. Download the image again (in OCP 4, use `/var/lib/kubelet/config.json` as `[authfile]`): ~~~ [root@node_name /]# podman pull--log-level debug--authfile [authfile] [IMAGE-PATH] ~~~ 3. Try to prune again: ~~~ [root@node_name /]# podman system prune-a--log-level debug ~~~ If there is no space in the disk, or the `RepoDigests` doesn't contain the path for the image: 1. Create a dummy manifest in `/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay-images/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx/manifest` like the following: ~~~ {"schemaVersion": 2, "mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json", "config": {"mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.container.image.v1+json", "size": 6060, "digest": "sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"}, "layers": []} ~~~ 2. Try to prune again: ~~~ [root@node_name /]# podman system prune-a--log-level debug ~~~ If it's still failing after trying above workarounds, it's possible to clean the crio storage of the OCP node as [KCS 5350721](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5350721).
root_cause: The manifest file of the image is corrupted or doesn't exists, and the image cannot be removed by `podman`.

title: Pods on a Data Plane Node are not able to communicate with pods in another Data Plane Node with OpenShift SDN.
issue: - Some Application and OpenShift Pods running on a Data Plane Node are not reachable from the pods running on the others Data Plane Nodes.- Pods running on a Data Plane Node have IP Address that belong to the **hostsubnet*
of another Node.
resolution: Delete the Node from the bare metal cluster following the steps below: 1. Mark the node as unschedulable: ~~~ $ oc adm cordon ~~~ 2. Drain all pods on the node: ~~~ $ oc adm drain--force=true ~~~ 3. Delete the node from the cluster: ~~~ $ oc delete node ~~~ 4. Powered down the physical hardware, turn it back on so that the node can rejoin the cluster and get a new **hostsubnet**.
root_cause: - This issue can be caused if a node's **hostsubnet** is manually deleted and then recreated by defining a subnet already used on another node.

title: MachineConfigPool stuck in degraded after applying the Gzip compression enabled file in RHOCP 4
issue: - `MachineConfigPool` stuck in degraded with the below error: ~~~ "message: 'Node worker.xx.xx.xx is reporting: "could not decode file \"/etc/chrony.conf\": could not create gzip reader: gzip: invalid header" ~~~
resolution: - Use only one **NTP** server information in the contents of `Butane` file.- Review the `Butane` file for multiple server entries and keep a single server entry: ~~~ $ cat chrony.bu variant: openshift version: 4.12.0 metadata: name: 0011-infra-chrony labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker openshift: kernel_arguments:- loglevel=7 storage: files:- path: /etc/chrony.conf mode: 0644 overwrite: true contents: inline: | server 172.x.x.x iburst <-- Proceed to remove one of the server details. server 172.x.x.x iburst driftfile /var/lib/chrony/drift makestep 1.0 3 rtcsync Logdir /var/log/chrony ~~~
root_cause: - The mentioned error will be encountered when `Machine Config Operator` tries to apply the child configuration which is compressed to the parent configuration that does not have the compression enabled.- Specifically to `Chrony.conf` configurations, `Gzip` compression is automatically applied if the `Butane` file contains two or more `NTP` server entries.

title: [RHOCP 4.12] Nodes cannot pull images from Harbor mirror registry during installation
issue: - Why bootstrap `Node` cannot pull image from Harbor mirror registry?- The certificate was added into_install-config.yaml_ under `additionalTrustBundle`.- Why the RHOCP `Node` cannot trust Harbor's certificate in_install-config.yaml_?- Adding the Harbor certificate manually at `/etc/containers/certs.d/ /har.crt` works as a workaround, but this is not ideal.
resolution: Add `additionalTrustBundlePolicy: Always` to_install-config.yaml_ to fix the issue.
root_cause: As described in the [Cluster Customization](https://github.com/openshift/installer/blob/master/docs/user/customization.md), by default the `additionalTrustBundle` is linked to the proxy component, but setting the `additionalTrustBundlePolicy` to "Always" should enforce it (including registry connection):- **additionalTrustBundle** (optional string): a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate bundle that will be added to the nodes' trusted certificate store. This trust bundle may also be used when a proxy has been configured.- **additionalTrustBundlePolicy** (optional string): determines when to add the AdditionalTrustBundle to the nodes'' trusted certificate store. "Proxyonly" is the default. The field can be set to following specified values. "Proxyonly": adds the AdditionalTrustBundle to nodes when http/https proxy is configured. "Always": always adds AdditionalTrustBundle.

title: How Does  Nameserver List Is Used For DNS resolution In RHOCP 4.
issue: - How does openshift use nameserver list for DNS resolution.
resolution: - In OpenShift, the `nameserver list` is used to configure the `DNS` resolution for applications running within the cluster. OpenShift relies on `DNS` to discover and communicate with various services and resources within the cluster. When a pod is created in OpenShift, it is assigned an IP address and a set of DNS settings, including the `nameserver list`. The `nameserver list` typically consists of one or more `IP addresses` of DNS servers that the cluster should use for DNS resolution.
root_cause: - The algorithm used is to try a nameserver, and if the times out, then it tries the next, until out of nameservers, then repeats trying all the name servers until a maximum number of timeouts/attempts are made.

title: Why are some applications failing to start after a failover in Openshift Data Foundation?
issue: Some applications (like `postgresql` or `mongoDB,` but not limited to them) might fail to start after a failover.
Sample pod output for a `mongo-db` pod: $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE mongo-6bdf878f76-rpq5x 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 7 (4m10s ago) 15m
For `Postgresql,` the error observed while starting up the pod in the secondary site is: changing permissions of '/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata': Operation not permitted
Why is this occurring? How to resolve this issue?
resolution: * This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [Bug 2081855](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2081855). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. * As a workaround, run the workload granting it `anyuid` OR `nonroot` SCC permissions and set a specific UID (`securityContext.runAsUser`) to run as in the deployment. This would ensure that the pod comes up with the same UID across clusters and hence functions as desired.- This is the standard way to run workloads needing additional SCC permissions in Openshift- This requires admin intervention on the 2 managed clusters though, to grant the non-default SCC to the service account of the deployment- This would also need to be pre-created on the 2 clusters * For further information, please review these links:- [Managing security context constraints](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/authentication/managing-security-context-constraints.html)- [RBAC overview](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/authentication/using-rbac.html)
root_cause: * The pod security context changes before and after the failover.- Before the failover (sample output): securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: 's0:c27,c19' fsGroup: 1000740000 runAsUser: 1000740000- After the failover (sample output): security context: seLinuxOptions: level: 's0:c27,c24' fsGroup: 1000750000 runAsUser: 1000750000 * Even though all files and directories are changed to mode `600` as per the pod that starts up, some operations would still fail as the UIDs across the clusters are different. Some file systems call that would fail are: `chmod`, `chown`, `setfsuid` (or calls that require that the UID of the file/directory should be the same as the calling process)

title: Image-registry POD taking too long to restart
issue: - The image-registry POD is taking several minutes to restart- There are a lot of files and/or empty folders in the registry.
resolution: - [High number of files in the image-registry](#High_files)- [High number of empty folders in the image-registry](#High_folders)- [Empty folders- Workaround](#Folders_workaround) ### High number of files in the image-registry If the number of files is high in the `image-registry`, the issue may be related to the `image-pruner` cronjob not being able to purge old images. ``` $ oc get job-n openshift-image-registry-l created-by=image-pruner NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE image-pruner-28162080 1/1 11s 5d image-pruner-28163520 1/1 11s 4d image-pruner-28164960 1/1 11s 3d image-pruner-28166400 0/1 2d 2d image-pruner-28167840 0/1 1d 1d image-pruner-28169280 0/1 6h 6h $ oc get pod-n openshift-image-registry | grep-E "^NAME|^image-pruner-[0-9]*-" NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE image-pruner-28162080-d46pj 0/1 Completed 0 5d image-pruner-28163520-rxffg 0/1 Completed 0 4d image-pruner-28164960-nwgbp 0/1 Completed 0 3d image-pruner-28166400-f6hth 0/1 Error 0 2d image-pruner-28167840-84fpj 0/1 Error 0 1d image-pruner-28169280-n2b9n 0/1 Error 0 6h ``` If the job duration is abnormally long and/or the pod status is not `completed` please review the container log and proceed as advised in the log. ``` $ oc logs-n openshift-image-registry image-pruner-28169280-n2b9n-c image-pruner | tail-10 2023-07-24T00:05:13.104414075Z attempt #5 has failed (exit code 1), going to make another attempt... 2023-07-24T00:07:45.212000737Z I0724 00:07:45.211801 51 prune.go:348] Creating image pruner with keepYoungerThan=1h0m0s, keepTagRevisions=3, pruneOverSizeLimit=, allImages=true 2023-07-24T00:07:45.317450592Z Failed to build graph! 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z The following objects have invalid references: 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z replicaset/ namespace=: init container configure: invalid image reference "https:// ": invalid reference format 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z Either fix the references or delete the objects to make the pruner proceed. 2023-07-24T00:07:45.319204744Z error: failed to build graph- no changes made ``` In this case, fixing the image in the replicaset or removing it if no longer used will allow the image-pruner to run again. Please refer to the RHOCP Documentation [Pruning objects to reclaim resources](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/applications/pruning-objects.html#pruning-images-manual_pruning-objects) for additional information about the `image-pruner`. ### High number of empty folders in the image-registry It has been identified that the pruner may leave some empty folders. The repositories folders `_layers`, `_uploads` & `_manifests` (and the related folder structure) are not cleaned up and still contains the tree structures of the image TAG hosting the links. There are currently active BUG(s) raised to address this issue: Version | Related BZ/Jira | Errata | Fixed Version |--- |--- |--- | 4.13 | Jira [OCPBUGS-17230](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-17230) | *N/A* | *N/A* | 4.12 | Jira [OCPBUGS-17230](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-17230) | *N/A* | *N/A* | ##### Empty folders- Workaround At the date of the KCS publication, there is still no fix for this issue. However, a workaround is available to clean-up the empty folders in the image-registry POD. Following on the [Hard pruning the registry](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/applications/pruning-objects.html#pruning-hard-pruning-registry_pruning-objects) documentation should remove all orphan blobs and folders.
root_cause: When using a Persistent Volume to store the images in the image-registry, if the image-pruner job is failing, the old images are not purged from the internal registry. This may lead to delays in the image-registry restart as it will scan all files stored on disk. In addition, the image-pruner may fail to delete relevant folders, even when the job has been completed.

title: My cluster has recently been upgraded to 4.13, and is showing an error with Hybrid Networking
issue: - The cluster has been upgraded to 4.13 and is displaying an error ~~~ failed to set up hybrid overlay logical switch port for: unable to setup Hybrid Subnet Logical Route Policy for node:, error: failed to add policy route 'inport == "rtos- " && ip4.dst == 10.132.0.0/14' for host " " on ovn_cluster_router, error: error in transact with ops...: 1 ovsdb operations failed ~~~
resolution: If Hybrid Networking is enabled in the cluster, **but no Windows Nodes or Pods are being ran**, then Hybrid Networking can be disabled: `oc patch networks.operator.openshift.io cluster--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"defaultNetwork":{"ovnKubernetesConfig":{"hybridOverlayConfig":null}}}}'` If Windows Nodes or Pods are being ran, open a case with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: Issue is likely related to https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13172.

title: Default GitOps ArgoCD instance allows reading resources for unprivileged users.
issue: The default instance of ArgoCD (openshift-gitops in namespace openshift-gitops) has the default role set to_role:readonly_. This is a potential security risk as any user (without any privileges) that is able to login to OCP can see all resources managed by the ArgoCD instance (secrets, network policies, routes,...). This ArgoCD instance is intended for Cluster management so there is high chance of potential misuse of sensitive data.
resolution: The behavior has been changed within the following RFE * [RFE-4034](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4034 "RFE-4034")- Default ArgoCD openshift-gitops instance's role should be set to "". and was delivered with the following ERRATA: * [RHEA-2023:5408](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHEA-2023:5408 "RHEA-2023:5408")- Product Enhancement Advisory This issue can be manually mitigated for earlier versions or for GitOps instances created by the affected operator version. ~~~ oc patch ArgoCD openshift-gitops-n openshift-gitops-p '{"spec": {"rbac": {"defaultPolicy": ""}}}'--type merge ~~~
root_cause: The default policy for openshift-gitops ArgoCD instance is set to read only.

title: is it possible to encrypt etcd data in ROSA
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: unable to encrypt etcd data in ROSA oc edit apiserver error: apiservers.config.openshift.io "cluster" could not be patched: admission webhook "regular-user-validation.managed.openshift.io" denied the request: Prevented from accessing Red Hat managed resources. This is in an effort to prevent harmful actions that may cause unintended consequences or affect the stability of the cluster. If you have any questions about this, please reach out to Red Hat support at https://access.redhat.com/support You can run `oc replace-f /tmp/oc-edit-3318946864.yaml` to try this update again.
resolution: you are getting permission errors because for ROSA the etcd encryption feature is not enabled by default and it can be enabled only at cluster installation time. Even with etcd encryption enabled, the etcd key values are accessible to anyone with access to the control plane nodes or cluster-admin privileges. By enabling etcd encryption for the key values in etcd, you will incur a performance overhead of approximately 20%. The overhead is a result of introducing this second layer of encryption, in addition to the default control plane storage encryption that encrypts the etcd volumes. Red Hat recommends that you enable etcd encryption only if you specifically require it for your use case.
root_cause: for ROSA not suppoted

title: Is ROSA instance support multi network interfaces?
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: Would like to know is ROSA instances support multiple network interface from different subnet?
resolution: as per the ROSA Service Definition [1], Single availability zone clusters require a minimum of 3 control planes, 2 infrastructure nodes, and 2 worker nodes deployed to a single availability zone. [1] https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_architecture/rosa_policy_service_definition/rosa-service-definition.html#rosa-sdpolicy-instance-types_rosa-service-definition Multiple availability zone clusters require a minimum of 3 control planes. 3 infrastructure nodes, and 3 worker nodes. Additional nodes must be purchased in multiples of three to maintain proper node distribution. All Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS clusters support a maximum of 180 worker nodes. Multiple availability zone clusters can only be deployed in regions with at least 3 availability zones. For more information, see the Regions and Availability Zones section in the AWS documentation[2]. [2] https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/ Each new Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS cluster is installed within an installer-created or preexisting Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in a single region, with the option to deploy into a single availability zone (Single-AZ) or across multiple availability zones (Multi-AZ). This provides cluster-level network and resource isolation, and enables cloud-provider VPC settings, such as VPN connections and VPC Peering. Persistent volumes (PVs) are backed by AWS Elastic Block Storage (EBS), and are specific to the availability zone in which they are provisioned. Persistent volume claims (PVCs) do not bind to a volume until the associated pod resource is assigned into a specific availability zone to prevent unschedulable pods. Availability zone-specific resources are only usable by resources in the same availability zone. In a multiple availability zone cluster, control plane nodes are distributed across availability zones and at least one worker node is required in each availability zone. As far as from the above docs, I cannot see the supportability mentioned for having instances to have multiple network interfaces from a different subnets.
root_cause: the use case would be not supported as it has not been tried and tested and there is no official documentation that mentions the use case, also we predict that if in theory, you could create an additional network, attach it to your nodes, and then configure a second interface on them. it would not persist across upgrades/node replacements. There isn't any way to specify additional network requirements for a ROSA Machine Pool, so at present, this does not appear to be possible.

title: MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume "pvc-dd0ba134-e1df-4a5b-bb24-cf7fa4029532" : volume attachment is being deleted
issue: MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume "pvc-dd0ba134-e1df-4a5b-bb24-cf7fa4029532": volume attachment is being deleted
resolution: Using the guide here: https://kb.vmware.com/s/article/85213 I was able to determine that there were PVC with attachments. When I do: ~~~ $ oc patch volumeattachments.storage.k8s.io csi-c3f67d3faec02d375fa0c59eae922be2b35b7591c85e61e35f297e8345f499aa-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge ~~~ I can then increase my deployment's replicas and the pods will run. However **I have to do this everytime**, can you suggest any reason this is? Basically the steps I am doing are: ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=0 deploymentconfig nexus-test $ oc scale--replicas=1 deploymentconfig nexus-test ~~~ at this point I get the errors about "volume attachment is being deleted" So I have to do ~~~ $ oc get volumeattachments.storage.k8s.io csi-3f9def683acb38f0d49b8ea987260609944a6638a91dcc939b27402c8ded947c csi.vsphere.vmware.com pvc-3518b011-f146-447a-9d8e-7a098c0682ac ocn-spvl402.inf.common.domain true 23h csi-c3f67d3faec02d375fa0c59eae922be2b35b7591c85e61e35f297e8345f499aa csi.vsphere.vmware.com pvc-dd0ba134-e1df-4a5b-bb24-cf7fa4029532 ocn-spvl402.inf.common.domain true 23h ~~~ and identify the PVCs that are causing the issue ~~~ $ oc get ovc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE nexus-blob-storage1 Bound pvc-dd0ba134-e1df-4a5b-bb24-cf7fa4029532 100Gi RWO vsphere-csi 45h nexus-blob-storage2 Bound pvc-3518b011-f146-447a-9d8e-7a098c0682ac 500Gi RWO vsphere-csi 45h nexus-test-blob-storage1 Bound pvc-fd8c7740-bc3f-4b9f-904e-d3b5656fc963 50Gi RWO vsphere-standard 139d nexus-test-pvc Bound pvc-abe59a7a-78d1-4189-90b7-e48ff6b43dd2 20Gi RWO vsphere-standard 139d ~~~ and then do ~~~ $ oc patch volumeattachments.storage.k8s.io csi-3f9def683acb38f0d49b8ea987260609944a6638a91dcc939b27402c8ded947c-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge $ oc patch volumeattachments.storage.k8s.io csi-c3f67d3faec02d375fa0c59eae922be2b35b7591c85e61e35f297e8345f499aa-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}'--type=merge ~~~ At this point the scale-up works This issue you're facing is a known issue specific to the [vSphere CSI driver 2.5.0](https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-vSphere-Container-Storage-Plug-in/2.5/rn/vmware-vsphere-container-storage-plugin-25-release-notes/index.html#known-issues). It's fixed with this [vSphere CSI driver fix](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/vsphere-csi-driver/pull/1879) that was released with the vSphere CSI driver 2.5.3. This CSI driver fix is included on OpenShift 4.12 and more recent releases, as can be checked [in our documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/storage/container_storage_interface/persistent-storage-csi-vsphere.html).
root_cause: ### Hypothesis We believe you might be facing a similar issue to * This [known issue](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6906821) where the vSphere snapshots are blocking the attachments. * This [VMware known issue](https://kb.vmware.com/s/article/85213) caused by nodes having the volume attached being deleted (sometimes by the autoscaler.

title: RH-SSO operator connecting to an external PostgreSQL DB over SSL
issue: - How can RH-SSO operator connect to external PostgreSQL DB over SSL?
resolution: Configure RH-SSO operator to connect to an external PostgreSQL DB as described in: [RH-SSO operator connecting to an external PostgreSQL DB](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6837971) Following updates are required to enable connection with PostgreSQL DB over SSL: **Step 1:** Edit keycloak-db-secret to include **SSLMODE**. The SSLMODE property can be set to any of the available [values](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-ssl.html) as per requirement. ~~~ kind: Secret apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: keycloak-db-secret namespace: stringData: POSTGRES_DATABASE: keycloak1 POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_ADDRESS: POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT: '5432' POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres POSTGRES_USERNAME: postgres SSLMODE: verify-ca type: Opaque ~~~ **Step 2:** In case SSLMODE setting needs to verify the Database certificate, we need to create **keycloak-db-ssl-cert-secret** containing the certificate. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: keycloak-db-ssl-cert-secret namespace: type: Opaque data: root.crt: {root.crt base64} ~~~ **Step 3:** Review standalone-openshift.xml to check sslMode configuration in KeycloakDS datasource. ~~~ verify-ca ~~~
root_cause: In order to enable connection to external PostgreSQL DB over SSL, we need to consider following configuration:- **SSLMODE** property in keycloak-db-secret ~~~ SSLMODE: Indicates whether to use TLS on the connection to the external PostgreSQL database. ~~~- **keycloak-db-ssl-cert-secret**: As per SSLMODE configuration, operator tries to look for the secret keycloak-db-ssl-cert-secret. ~~~ The secret is required only in case when operator needs to verify the Database’s certificate. When SSLMODE is enabled, the operator searches for a secret called keycloak-db-ssl-cert-secret containing the root.crt that has been used by the PostgreSQL database. ~~~

title: Is kexec_load supported in RHEL9?
issue: **Introduction:*

In the realm of Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), the landscape of Kexec/Kdump interfaces has undergone significant changes. This knowledgebase article sheds light on the evolution of these interfaces, specifically focusing on the transition from the kexec_load system call to kexec_file_load as the default interface. **Content:*

1. **Background:**- In versions prior to RHEL 7, the default interface for loading kexec/kdump kernels was the `kexec_load` system call.- With the advent of RHEL 8, there was a strategic shift towards utilizing the `kexec_file_load` interface as the default choice. 2. **Reasons for Change:**- The transition to `kexec_file_load` was motivated by the fact that a substantial portion of its code implementation resides within the Linux kernel.- In contrast, `kexec_load` primarily operates in user space.- This shift allows for enhanced manipulation of the kexec/kdump kernel loading process within the kernel itself, aligning with the preference for kernel-side operations. 3. **Default Setting:**- As of RHEL 8, `kexec_file_load` is the default interface for loading kexec/kdump kernels.- This change reflects a strategic decision to leverage the kernel's capabilities in this critical process. 4. **Availability of `kexec_load`:**- Despite the shift to `kexec_file_load`, the `kexec_load` interface is still available.- Users have the flexibility to revert to `kexec_load` if they have specific requirements or preferences. 5. **Manual Configuration:**- Users can manually configure their systems to enable the use of `kexec_load` if desired.- This manual configuration allows for a customized approach based on user needs. 6. **Support and Issue Resolution:**- While `kexec_load` is not the default, Red Hat acknowledges its presence and provides support for users employing this interface.- Issues encountered while using `kexec_load` will be addressed, although with a lower priority due to the default preference for `kexec_file_load`. **Conclusion:*

Understanding the nuances of the kexec/kdump interfaces in RHEL is crucial for users seeking optimal performance and reliability. While the default choice is `kexec_file_load`, the availability of `kexec_load` offers flexibility to users, allowing them to tailor their systems according to their specific requirements. Red Hat remains committed to supporting both interfaces, ensuring a seamless experience for users across diverse use cases.

title: How to register disconnected OpenShift Container Platform 4 cluster on console.redhat.com?

How to register it on [console.redhat.com](https://console.redhat.com) and attach a subscription to it?- How to subscribe OpenShift 4 clusters?- Newly installed OpenShift 4 cluster has a self-support subscription. How to change the subscription to a fully supported one?
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* ####Register an OCP 4 cluster via the web console To register a disconnected OCP 4 cluster on [console.redhat.com](https://console.redhat.com) the cluster profile needs to be created manually as outlined below:- Go to [console.redhat.com](https://console.redhat.com) and login with **org_admin** login credentials.- Go to the **Clusters** tab and select the three dots near **Create cluster** and click on the **Register cluster** button. Alternatively, use [this link](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/register).- Enter all the required details like `clusterID`, number of sockets, memory, etc.- After filling all the required details click on the **Register cluster**. This will create a cluster profile in disconnected mode.- After that, click on the respective cluster name in the 'Clusters' tab. Edit the Subscription Settings and attach the subscription according to the cluster configuration and environment by scrolling down to 'Subscription settings'. ####Register an OCP 4 cluster using the API (for automation) Alternatively, it's possible to register a disconnected OCP 4 cluster on [console.redhat.com](https://console.redhat.com) via the API as described below. This method allow to automate the registration:- Generate a [OpenShift Cluster Manager API Token](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/token)- Install the [Red Hat OpenShift Cluster Manager API Command Line Tools](https://github.com/openshift-online/ocm-cli/releases) for your respective platform.- Log into OpenShift Cluster Manager via the command line: $ ocm login--token="foo" $ echo $? 0- Create a `JSON` file that contain the cluster details: $ cat mycluster.json title: Is it possible to disable multus after the cluster has been installed
issue: - How to disable openshift-multus?- Is it possible to disable multus after cluster has been installed?
resolution: - It's possible to disable Multus during a new install by specifying it in the NetworkConfig. See [KCS 4850181](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4850181)- However in an already installed cluster it isn't possible and the operator will stamp out any attempt to change this field. Refer [BZ-1688212](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1688212) for more information.

title: ServiceMesh Operator Upgrade not possible: Bundle unpacking failed
issue: - While upgrading the ServiceMeshOperator from 2.1 to 2.4 but the upgrade is stuck. The Installplan fails with below error: ~~~ "Bundle unpacking failed. Reason: DeadlineExceeded, and Message: Job was active longer than specified deadline". ~~~
resolution: - Find the job and configmap (usually named the same) in the openshift-marketplace corresponding to the affected operator and grep for it: ~~~ $ oc get job-n openshift-marketplace-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].value|contains (" ")) |.metadata.name' ~~~- Delete the found job and the corresponding configmap, (named the same as the job) found in the openshift-marketplace namespace: ~~~ $ oc delete job-n openshift-marketplace $ oc delete configmap-n openshift-marketplace ~~~- Search for the failed installplan related to the operator and delete it: ~~~ $ oc delete ip ~~~-. A new job will be triggered and the upgrade should succeed.
