title: [LVM Storage] Estimate available pool size to provision PersistentVolumes
issue: - I would like to know a way to verify free space available for configured LVMS-cluster before creating a PV of a particular size which will be located there.- How to get pretended free space without over provisioning and running time-consuming commands like *`oc debug node/control-plane-- vgdisplay`*?- In our scenario, the majority of the PVs provided by the LVM Storage operator will consume most of the requested space, acting like a thick provisioned volume and I would like to know a way to calculate the free space.
resolution: To calculate the pretended free space that is available in the thin-pool, in the case each PersistentVolume act as thick provisioned instead of thin provisioned, you can use the following formula: ~~~ available size = (topolvm_thinpool_overprovisioned_available- topolvm_thinpool_size_bytes) ~~~ These metrics are already scrapped by prometheus to be consumed in the *Observe > Metrics* left-hand panel in the OpenShift console.
root_cause: The reason why you see a bigger size in the *`topolvm_thinpool_overprovisioned_available`* metric is because of the over-provisioning ratio, with a minimum of 2 in the thinPoolConfig, meaning that every byte of free storage will be reported as if it was 2 byte or multiplied by the number for the ratio.

title: Cannot find mpath devices with LocalVolumeDiscovery
issue: - LocalVolumeDiscoveryResults doesn't show devices which are of type *`mpath`*.- OCP console doesn't list multipath devices on LocalVolumeSet
resolution: LSO's `LocalVolumeSet` and `LocalVolumeDiscovery` CRs now support `mpath` device types. Upgrade to the corresponding version:- [4.14- OCPBUGS-10884](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-10884)- [4.13.z- OCPBUGS-13285](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13285)- [4.12.z- OCPBUGS-13357](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13357) **still being worked**
root_cause: Users can use this type along with any other, if LocalVolumeSet is edited manually. Current Local Storage Operator (LSO) version provides a DiscoveryResult that is not too helpful when it comes to mpath and it's not possible to tell which disks are backing the mpath device shown. For this reason, console was updated to allow either disk (or disk+partition) or mpath so users don't run into scenarios where they might attempt to reuse the same disk multiple times.

title: Tenable Nessus reports "SSL Certificate with Wrong Hostname" scanning RHOCP nodes
issue: - Nessus generate on multiple ports reports similar to the following, while scanning RHOCP from the internal network: ~~~ NODE_NAME,SSL Certificate with Wrong Hostname,9192," The identities known by Nessus are: master1.example.com.local node_name.local The Common Name in the certificate is: *.machine-approver.openshift-cluster-machine-approver.svc The Subject Alternate Names in the certificate are: *.machine-approver.openshift-cluster-machine-approver.svc *.machine-approver.openshift-cluster-machine-approver.svc.cluster.local machine-approver.openshift-cluster-machine-approver.svc machine-approver.openshift-cluster-machine-approver.svc.cluster.local ~~~
resolution: Ignore this kind of warning, scan RHOCP from the external network or tune appropriately the security scanner.
root_cause: Tenable Nessus is not aware of the way RHOCP services are accessed, so it falsely believes certificate names to be wrong. This report doesn't imply that any vulnerability is present in RHOCP. Other possible false positive are described in [solution 5280131](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5280131)

title: Envoy Proxy Sidecar Injection Failures in Service Mesh environment
issue: - The upstream version of Istio injects the sidecar by default if you have labeled the project. Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh requires you to opt in to having the sidecar automatically injected to a deployment, so labelling the project is not required. This avoids injecting a sidecar if it is not wanted (for example, in build or deploy pods).- The webhook created by Service Mesh checks the configuration of pods deploying into all projects to see if they are opting in to injection with the appropriate annotation.- What checks can be performed if no sidecar is injected into an application managed by Service Mesh?
resolution: - Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh relies on a proxy sidecar within the application’s pod to provide Service Mesh capabilities to the application.- There are options to enable automatic sidecar injection or manage injection manually.- Red Hat recommends automatic injection using the annotation with no need to label projects. This ensures that your application contains the appropriate configuration for the Service Mesh upon deployment. This method requires fewer privileges and does not conflict with other OpenShift capabilities such as builder pods.- If there is no Envoy proxy sidecar injected into an application deployed on Service Mesh, then verify the following:- Check that the project has been added to the Service Mesh Member Roll resource. Run the command and verify that the project appears in the member list. ~~~ $ oc get smmr default-n-o yaml ~~~- Check that the annotation `sidecar.istio.io/inject` has been added in the application's deployment resource and it's value is `true`, for example: ```yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: ratings-v1 namespace: bookinfo labels: app: ratings version: v1 spec: template: metadata: annotations: sidecar.istio.io/inject: 'true' ```- If above checks have been performed delete the application pod and wait for a new one being created. Sidecar injection should be triggered again. ~~~ $ oc delete ~~~
root_cause: - The upstream Istio community installation automatically injects the sidecar into pods within the projects you have labelled.- Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh does not automatically inject the sidecar to any pods, but requires you to opt in to injection using an annotation without labelling projects. This method requires fewer privileges and does not conflict with other OpenShift capabilities such as builder pods. To enable automatic injection you specify the `sidecar.istio.io/inject` annotation as described in the [Enabling automatic sidecar injection section](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/service_mesh/v2x/prepare-to-deploy-applications-ossm.html#ossm-automatic-sidecar-injection_deploying-applications-ossm).- If there is a delay/lag problem injecting the sidecar, it could be related to istio-proxy lagging in the startup phase. It could also be related with NTP/Chrony delays so make sure the nodes are in timely sync.

title: OCS / ODF 4.X - How to change the debug log level on openshift-storage pods
issue: - On this document we provide the procedure to increase or decrease the level of the debug logs on OCS pods The higher number, the more verbosity of debug logs. **NOTE.*

The recommended log level is set as default in the different components. Developers have considered the amount of logging, and deem it required information for most issues that can occur. Customers can reduce the log level if they prefer, but they need to understand that it may not be possible to troubleshoot certain problems that could occur. It may be required to increase the log level again in order to identify and address issues.
resolution: 1) **CSI** pods: The CSI log level IIRC is already configurable by updating this value in the configmap `rook-ceph-operator-config`. Since OCS 4.6 we added `CSI_LOG_LEVEL` to 5, but this can cause too much logs on csi pods, see internal [Bug 1971521- [RFE][GSS][OCS 4.7] How to reduce debug log verbosity for rook-ceph pods](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1971521#c38) If required we can decrease number of logs by reducing to level to 0 or 1 CSI_LOG_LEVEL: 1 Example: ~~~ [cloud-user@bastion ~]$ oc edit cm rook-ceph-operator-config # Please edit the object below. Lines beginning with a '#' will be ignored, # and an empty file will abort the edit. If an error occurs while saving this file will be # reopened with the relevant failures. # apiVersion: v1 data: CSI_LOG_LEVEL: "5" < < <---- change to 1 CSI_PLUGIN_TOLERATIONS: |2-... ~~~ NOTE1. The change of the `CSI_LOG_LEVEL` on the `rook-ceph-operator-config` will cause all the csi pods to be restarted. The ceph csi pods are responsible of provisioning: creating and deleting volumes, also to attach and detach to them, so a restart of any ceph csi pod should be transparent to running pods. NOTE2. On ODF 4.11 and higher, see: [How to enable Ceph client debug logs for Openshift Data Foundation CSI pods?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6999672) 2) **rook-ceph-operator** pod See: [How to enable and disable debug logs for rook-ceph-operator in an OpenShift Container Storage 4.X](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6135271) and also: [ODF 4.12 Troubleshooting OpenShift Data Foundation- 6.9. Enabling and disabling debug logs for rook-ceph-operator](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.12/html/troubleshooting_openshift_data_foundation/troubleshooting-alerts-and-errors-in-openshift-data-foundation#recovering-from-EBS-volume-detach_rhodf) 3) **RGW / rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore-a** pod 3.1) Add the following to the CM `rook-config-override` and restart the ceph-rgw pod (NOTE. This procedure is not working in OCS 4.8 and ODF 4.9...checking internally for other additional steps) ~~~ [client.rgw.ocs.storagecluster.cephobjectstore.a] debug rgw = 20/20 ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ oc edit cm rook-config-override # Please edit the object below. Lines beginning with a '#' will be ignored, # and an empty file will abort the edit. If an error occurs while saving this file will be # reopened with the relevant failures. # apiVersion: v1 data: config: |2 [client.rgw.ocs.storagecluster.cephobjectstore.a] debug rgw = 20/20 [global] bdev_flock_retry = 20... ~~~ OR 3.2) Change the debug level "on the fly", connect to the pod: ~~~ $ oc rsh rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore-a-647d5c54svs2 ~~~ Look for your "daemon file": ~~~ sh-4.4# ls-l /var/run/ceph/ total 0 srwxr-xr-x. 1 ceph ceph 0 May 16 14:28 ceph-client.rgw.ocs.storagecluster.cephobjectstore.a.1954.94344822789440.asok sh-4.4# ~~~ and set the desired value (temporarily) ~~~ sh-4.4# ceph daemon /var/run/ceph/ceph-client.rgw.ocs.storagecluster.cephobjectstore.a.1954.94344822789440.asok config set debug_rgw 5/5 {"success": ""} sh-4.4# ~~~ Confirm changes are in effect: ~~~ sh-4.4# tail-f /var/log/ceph/ceph-client.rgw.ocs.storagecluster.cephobjectstore.a.log 2022-09-27T15:45:47.906+0000 7f0919fb9700 1 failed to read header: The socket was closed due to a timeout 2022-09-27T15:45:47.906+0000 7f0919fb9700 5 failed to write response: Bad file descriptor 2022-09-27T15:45:47.906+0000 7f0919fb9700 1 ====== req done http_status=400 ====== 2022-09-27T15:45:50.263+0000 7f09918a8700 1 ====== starting new request req=0x7f0a1cc1c620 ===== 2022-09-27T15:45:50.263+0000 7f09918a8700 2 req 456854 0.000000000s initializing for trans_id = tx00000000000000006f896-0063331aae-672f2f-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore 2022-09-27T15:45:50.264+0000 7f09918a8700 2 req 456854 0.001000000s getting op 0 ~~~ Note. The default value is "debug_rgw 1/1" 4) **noobaa** pods- for **noobaa-core**: ~~~ # oc edit sts noobaa-core ~~~- for **noobaa-endpoint**: ~~~ # oc edit deployment noobaa-endpoint ~~~ Then add the following lines: ~~~- name: DEBUG_MODE value: "true"- name: CONFIG_JS_dbg_log_level value: "5" ~~~ Example, into the containers / command / env section: ~~~ containers:- command:- /noobaa_init_files/noobaa_init.sh- init_endpoint env:- name: NOOBAA_DISABLE_COMPRESSION valueFrom: configMapKeyRef: key: NOOBAA_DISABLE_COMPRESSION name: noobaa-config- name: DEBUG_MODE value: "true"- name: CONFIG_JS_dbg_log_level value: "5"- name: NOOBAA_LOG_LEVEL valueFrom: configMapKeyRef: key: NOOBAA_LOG_LEVEL name: noobaa-config ~~~ Alternatively, on the fly, for noobaa-core, noobaa-db or noobaa-endpoint you can you can inject the log level with this command: ~~~ # noobaa api redirector publish_to_cluster '{"target": "", "method_api": "debug_api", "method_name": "set_debug_level", "request_params": {"level": 5, "module": "core"}}' # noobaa api redirector publish_to_cluster '{"target": "", "method_api": "debug_api", "method_name": "set_debug_level", "request_params": {"level": 5, "module": "db"}}' # noobaa api redirector publish_to_cluster '{"target": "", "method_api": "debug_api", "method_name": "set_debug_level", "request_params": {"level": 5, "module": "endpoint"}}' ~~~ Changing it back would be using this command: ~~~ # noobaa api redirector publish_to_cluster '{"target": "", "method_api": "debug_api", "method_name": "set_debug_level", "request_params": {"level": 0, "module": "core"}}' # noobaa api redirector publish_to_cluster '{"target": "", "method_api": "debug_api", "method_name": "set_debug_level", "request_params": {"level": 0, "module": "db"}}' # noobaa api redirector publish_to_cluster '{"target": "", "method_api": "debug_api", "method_name": "set_debug_level", "request_params": {"level": 0, "module": "endpoint"}}' ~~~ 5) **MDS** pods Connect to each mds pod and run: ~~~ # oc rsh rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-a-xxxx sh-4.4# ceph daemon mds.ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-a config set debug_mds 20 {"success": ""} # oc rsh rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-b-xxxx sh-4.4# ceph daemon mds.ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-b config set debug_mds 20 {"success": ""} ~~~ OR from the ceph tool box ~~~ # ceph config set mds debug_mds 20 ~~~ OR Permanently configure debug log on ODF: ~~~- oc scale deployment ocs-operator--replicas 0- oc edit cm-n openshift-storage rook-config-override-o yaml # If the section [mds] doesn't exist, create it and put the following under: [mds] debug_mds = 20 debug_ms = 20 Example of rook-config-override: [global]... mon_pg_warn_max_object_skew = 0 mon_data_avail_warn = 15 [osd] osd_memory_target_cgroup_limit_ratio = 0.8 [mds] debug_mds = 20 debug_ms = 20- oc scale deployment ocs-operator--replicas 1 ~~~ 6) **MON** pods See [KCS 6960567 How to check increase debug logs for monitor pod](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6960567) Add `debug_mon = 20` in global section of the config map `rook-config-override` ~~~ # oc edit cm rook-config-override [global] debug_mon = 20 ~~~
root_cause: - ODF may fill up with debug logs the Elastic, which in some cases introduce an issue for customer. Part of the customers don't want ODF to consume so much space.

title: How to add custom registries to OpenShift 4?
issue: - Is it possible to add additional registry to OpenShift 4?- How to add container registry with url like " abc.com:5001" (including the port).- Is it possible to add a registry that requires a certificate in OpenShift 4?- According to the documentation for [configuring image registry settings](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-file_image-configuration), `additionalTrustedCA` is added but it failed to pull image from the registry: ~~~ Failed to pull image “abc.com:5001/namespace/rhel-luna:latest”: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = pinging docker registry returned: Get https://abc.com:5001/v2/: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~
resolution: As explained in the documentation for [adding specific registries](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-allowed_image-configuration), in order to add external registries, it is needed to add them to the `spec.registrySources.allowedRegistries` field of the `images.config.openshift.io` `cluster` resource, including the port if it is not the default one: ~~~ [...] spec: registrySources: allowedRegistries:- quay.io- abc.com:5001- registry.redhat.io- registry.access.redhat.com [...] ~~~ > **Note:** The changes in the `images.config.openshift.io` `cluster` resource will generate a new `rendered` `MachineConfig`, to modify the `/etc/containers/policy.json` in the nodes. The Machine Config operator will apply the new `rendered` `MachineConfig`. If needed, it will `drain` the nodes to apply the changes, and `uncordon` the nodes after that. If the registry requires a certificate for accesing, it is also needed to add the `spec.additionalTrustedCA.name` field, referencing a `configmap` with the required CA. The `configmap` should be similar to the following one as per the [configuring additional trust stores for image registry access](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-cas_image-configuration) documentation: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 data: abc.com..5001: |------BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- MIIFY.....pgUQs-----END CERTIFICATE----- kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: registry-ca-certs namespace: openshift-config ~~~ > **Note:** if the port is included in the registry URL, it's not possible to configure `abc.com:5001` in the `data` field of the `configmap`, and the "`:`" should be replaced with "`..`" like `abc.com..5001`.
root_cause: If the custom registry is configured in a port different than the default, and/or it requires a CA for the access, additional configuration is needed.

title: RHOCP4 Monitoring operator in degraded state as node-exporter pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff since bind address is already in use
issue: - Roll out of `monitoring` operator is stuck.- `node-exporter` pods in `openshift-monitoring` namespace are stuck in `CrashloopBackOff`.- Upgrade of the cluster is stuck.- `Monitoring` operator is degraded- Check for the `node-exporter` pod status in `openshift-monitoring` namespace. ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-monitoring | grep-i node-exporter NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE node-exporter-56gvq 0/2 CrashloopBackoff 0 57m node-exporter-76hdf 0/2 CrashloopBackoff 0 51m node-exporter-hg29k 0/2 CrashloopBackoff 0 43m node-exporter-hvd99 0/2 CrashloopBackoff 0 57m node-exporter-msr5t 0/2 CrashloopBackoff 0 43m node-exporter-s8znd 0/2 CrashloopBackoff 0 49m ~~~
resolution: - Switch to the `openshift-monitoring` namespace. ~~~ $ oc project openshift-monitoring ~~~- List the `node-exporter` pods along with the nodes on which the pods are scheduled. ~~~ $ oc get pods-owide | grep-i node-exporter ~~~- Cordon the node. ~~~ $ oc adm cordon ~~~- Drain the respective node on which the pod was scheduled. ~~~ $ oc adm drain--force--grace-period=-1--ignore-daemonsets ~~~ **(Note: Specify all other options if prompted for)**- Once drain is done, do a manual SSH to the node. ~~~ $ ssh core@ ~~~- Look for the process holding the port open `9100` and kill it. ~~~ $ sudo fuser 9100/tcp ### Verify what process is holding the port $ sudo fuser-k 9100/tcp ### Kill the process using the port ~~~ **Optional: If the pod still fails to start only then, Reboot the node and switch back to your bastion/helper Node and wait for some time. The pods should be up and running now. Check the pod status again.**- Lastly, uncordon the node. ~~~ $ oc adm uncordon node ~~~- Repeat this process for all the pods.
root_cause: The process used by the `previous` PID of the `node-exporter` pod does not `release` the pod and holds up the `port` not allowing the newly created pods to start.

title: The multus default route is lost when using the istio sidecar
issue: - The default route of the container is lost when a pod is created with additional networks and the istio sidecar together.
resolution: The istio CNI plugin will override where the default route is set in that set of multus CNI plugin. This is the intended behavior, and there are currently no plans to make any changes. ####Workaround You can manually add the istio CNI plugin as the first entry in the `k8s.v1.cni.cncf.io/networks` annotation. The istio sidecar injector will see the network is already injected, so it won't inject it. The plugin itself only modifies the iptables rules, so it shouldn't matter if it is invoked before the ipvlan plugin. ``` annotations: sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true" k8s.v1.cni.cncf.io/networks: '[{# <=========== "name": "v2-1-istio-cni" # <===========}, # <=========== {"name": "ipvlan-net", "ips": ["192.168.2.13/24"], "default-route": ["192.168.2.10"]}]' ```

title: service account name is not specified in custom clusterlogforwarders in RHOCP 4

title: OpenShift 4 upgrade failed while pulling the image from mirror registry with error x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
issue: - While pulling the image from mirror getting the below error: ~~~ Mirrors also failed: [registry.example.com:5000/ocp4/openshift4@sha256:c8ace6f0bcb5dfb174626b7d189bc9f9f7ee51394a92d209b4b01896f8bcf66e: error pinging docker registry registry.example.com:5000: Get \\\"https://registry.example.com:5000/v2/\\\": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (possibly because of \\\"crypto/rsa: verification error\\\" while trying to verify candidate authority certificate \\\"registry.example.com\\\")]): ~~~

If the mirror registry certificate is expired, the following needs to be done on the registry host: 1. The self-signed CA certificate for the registry must be put in the /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ folder. 2. The update-ca-trust extract command must then be run to have the host trust the new CA certificate. > **Note:** above steps could change depending on the registry host.
root_cause: There is an issue with the mirrored registry certificate (probably expired) and it needs to be replaced.

title: Non-default memory limits set Network Observability Operator don't persist to operator update
issue: - The `controller manager` `Pod` of the Network Observability Operator doesn't come up after upgrading the operator due to `OOM` errors.
resolution: This behavior has been reported and could be tracked through the story [NETOBSERV-1373](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/NETOBSERV-1373) ## Workaround If this error is noticed after updating the operator, then is required to increase memory limits for the new `ClusterServiceVersion` as described in [Network Observability controller manager pod runs out of memory](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/network_observability/troubleshooting-network-observability.html#controller-manager-pod-runs-out-of-memory_network-observability-troubleshooting) ``` $ oc-n netobserv patch csv network-observability-operator.[version]--type='json'-p='[{"op": "replace", "path":"/spec/install/spec/deployments/0/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory", value: "[New_Memory_limit]"}]' ```
root_cause: According to the product documentation, the memory limit for the controller manager pod is defined on the `ClusterServiceVersion` resource. It's important to note that when the operator undergoes an upgrade if there are non-default configured limits won't carry over. The upgraded operator will introduce a new `ClusterServiceVersion` and the previously set non-defaults limits will not apply.

title: How egress IPs are treated in case of an NFS mount with a PV
issue: - If we put an egress IP in a namespace and that namespace has PVC bound to a nfs PV the nfs client will use the egress IP as source IP? Or how does it work?
resolution: - All that Kubernetes does when mounting a NFS share is executing below mount command on the host.So any egress rules / labels that are used for pods are not used. ~~~ mount-t nfs-o: /var/lib/kubelet/some-pod-directory ~~~- Linux kernel then uses its own logic to route NFS traffic and choose the source network interface.

title: Alertmanger Configuration
issue: What are you experiencing? What are you expecting to happen? We are attempting to use alert management to send alerts to AWS SNS. In alert manager SNS is a default target for sending alerts however we aren't seeing it as being available in the console. Define the value or impact to you or the business This is a high value item before these clusters are brought into production. Where are you experiencing this behavior? What environment? AWS When does this behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times? NA
resolution: Given the absence of any configuration, initially I will provide you with an example detailing the steps to configure the Alertmanager in 'user-defined' projects. The default setup of Alertmanager in ROSA clusters permits alerts to be dispatched to 'Red Hat SRE' with receivers locked to default settings. To customize receivers, the OpenShift Administrator can activate a secondary AlertManager instance within the user workload monitoring namespace. Considering this, proceed with the following example steps: 1. **Create sns topic:** You must use an AWS account within your organization to follow the AWS procedures for creating the SNS topic. This process is described in: [[1]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-services-sns.html#cli-create-sns-topic) 2. **Subscribe sns topic:** To receive messages from a topic, you need to subscribe an endpoint to it. The endpoint will then start receiving messages published to that topic. [[2]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/es_es/cli/latest/userguide/cli-services-sns.html#cli-subscribe-sns-topic) 3. **Enable monitoring for user-definde projects:** As a cluster administrator, you can activate monitoring for user-defined projects by configuring `enableUserWorkload: true` field in the cluster monitoring ConfigMap object. ``` $ oc get cm cluster-monitoring-config-n openshift-monitoring-o yaml apiVersion: v1 data: config.yaml: | enableUserWorkload: true alertmanagerMain: {} prometheusK8s: {} kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: cluster-monitoring-config namespace: openshift-monitoring ``` 4. **Enable alert routing:** To use the default platform Alertmanager instance or a dedicated Alertmanager instance exclusively for user-defined projects, it is necessary to enable alert routing for these projects. This process is detailed in. [[3]](https://access.redhat.com/bounce/?externalURL=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.openshift.com%2Fcontainer-platform%2F4.11%2Fmonitoring%2Fenabling-alert-routing-for-user-defined-projects.html) ``` $ oc get cm user-workload-monitoring-config-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring-o yaml apiVersion: v1 data: config.yaml: | alertmanager: enabled: true enableAlertmanagerConfig: true kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: user-workload-monitoring-config namespace: openshift-user-workload-monitoring ``` 5. **Enable user permissions:** Users should be given the necessary permissions to configure alert routing for user-defined projects, as specified in the documentation. [[4]](https://access.redhat.com/bounce/?externalURL=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.openshift.com%2Fcontainer-platform%2F4.11%2Fmonitoring%2Fenabling-alert-routing-for-user-defined-projects.html%23granting-users-permission-to-configure-alert-routing-for-user-defined-projects_enabling-alert-routing-for-user-defined-projects) 6. **Set Up Alertmanager Configuration:** After completing the steps above, you can proceed to create the `AlertmanagerConfig` custom resource in your user-defined project. This custom resource will define your alert receivers (like email, PagerDuty, SNS, each others.) and routing rules. You can follow the example bellow to create an `AlertmanagerConfig` with an SNS receiver. Create a new namespace: custom-alert ``` oc create namespace custom-alert ``` 7. Extract the secret of the openshift-user-workload-monitoring namespace ``` $ oc extract secret/alertmanager-user-workload--to /tmp/-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring--confirm ``` remove quotes to improve the readability using the command: `sed-i 's/"//g' /tmp/alertmanager.yaml` 8. Configure your user workload monitoring settings in the /tmp/alertmanager.yaml file. ``` global: resolve_timeout: 5m receivers:- name: default- name: sns_receiver sns_configs:- api_url: 'https://sns. < >.amazonaws.com' sigv4: region: < > access_key: < > secret_key: < < Your Secret Key> > topic_arn: 'arn:aws:sns: < >: < >: < > ' route: group_by:- job group_interval: 1m group_wait: 30s receiver: sns_receiver repeat_interval: 1m routes:- match: alertname: Watchdog receiver: default- match: severity: warning receiver: sns_receiver ``` You should replace `'Your-region'` and `'AccountID'` with your AWS account information, and substitute `'Your_Topic'` with the name of the created topic 9. Update the secret in the openshift-user-workload-monitoring namespace. ``` oc set data secret/alertmanager-user-workload--from-file /tmp/alertmanager.yaml-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring ``` 10. **Create Alerting Rule:** Verify it works by creating a Prometheus Rule that will fire off an alert ``` apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: prometheus-example-rules namespace: custom-alert spec: groups:- name: example.rules rules:- alert: ExampleAlert expr: vector(1) ``` 11. Log into your OpenShift Console and switch to the Developer view. Select the **Observe** item from the menu on the left and then click **Alerts**. Make your **Project** is set to **custom-alert** By default, cluster alerts are only sent to Red Hat SRE and you cannot modify the cluster alert receivers. However you can make a copy of any of the alerts that you wish to see in your own alerting namespace which will then get picked up by the user workload alert-manager. 12. Duplicate a subset of the Cluster Monitoring Prometheus Rules ``` oc-n openshift-monitoring get prometheusrule \ cluster-monitoring-operator-prometheus-rules-o json | \ jq '.metadata.namespace = "custom-alert"' | \ kubectl create-f- ``` You should also have received an alert for the **Watchdog** alert in the e-mail subscribed for sns.

title: Prometheus pod logs gives error that serviceaccount prometheus-k8s cannot list resource pods in custom namespace
issue: - Prometheus pod logs gives below error message but the custom namespace test-abc is already deleted. ~~~ caller=klog.go:108 level=warn component=k8s_client_runtime func=Warningf msg="github.com/prometheus/prometheus/discovery/kubernetes/kubernetes.go:574: failed to list *v1.Pod: pods is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"test-abc\"" ~~~
resolution: - As per Diagnostic steps inside the podmonitor.yaml file, one can see namespaceSelector pointing to namespace test-abc. This podmonitor was created in namespace openshift-user-workload-monitoring. ~~~ namespaceSelector: matchNames:- test- test-xyz- test-abc ~~~- Edit all the podmonitors that are created and remove the entry for the deleted namespace test-abc. ~~~ $ oc project openshift-user-workload-monitoring $ oc edit podmonitor $ oc edit podmonitor $ oc edit podmonitor ~~~- Once the entries are removed, review the pod logs for prometheus pods from openshift-monitoring namespace. ~~~ $ oc project openshift-monitoring $ oc logs prometheus-k8s-0-c prometheus ~~~
root_cause: - Although the namespace test-abc is already deleted but since there are entries of the project test-abc in podmonitors, the errors were displayed in prometheus pod logs.

title: Do I need to deploy the Compliance Operator if I have the Red Hat Advanced Container Security deployed?
issue: What are you experiencing? What are you expecting to happen? We're currently using Compliance Operator and we have installed RHACS and have queries regarding profiles and best practices: 1- Clarification on 'Platform' vs. 'Node' in profile applications in the documentation – does 'Platform' imply control plane nodes? https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/security/compliance_operator/co-scans/compliance-operator-supported-profiles.html 2- Should we apply both profiles platform and a node profile to control planes? 3- How often do profile names change? 4- Are there Red Hat recommended best practices for using RHACS with Compliance Operator? 5- Does RHACS's 'Managing Compliance' section imply a need for the Compliance Operator, especially with tailored profiles? We're seeking guidance on effective integration and compliance checks differences between RHACS and Compliance Operator.- https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.3/operating/manage-compliance.html- https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.3/operating/manage-compliance-operator/compliance-operator-rhacs.html Define the value or impact to you or the business To get our clusters in compliance Where are you experiencing this behavior? What environment? NA When does this behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times? NA
resolution: Hi Sherief, Thanks for putting these questions together. 1- Clarification on 'Platform' vs. 'Node' in profile applications in the documentation – does 'Platform' imply control plane nodes? https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/security/compliance_operator/co-scans/compliance-operator-supported-profiles.html There's a note [2] at the very bottom of the table that says "Node profiles must be used with the relevant Platform profile. For more information, see Compliance Operator profile types." and then there's no link... except there is at the very bottom of the page under the "Additional Resources" section that links to this doc: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/security/compliance_operator/co-concepts/compliance-operator-understanding.html#compliance_profile_types_understanding-compliance Our docs can be confusing, sometimes. 2- Should we apply both profiles platform and a node profile to control planes? Not unless you're running user workloads on the control plane nodes, no. 3- How often do profile names change? Are you talking about "Platform" and "node" profiles, or the ones that you get when you run "oc get-n openshift-compliance profiles.compliance" (seen here, too: https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/security/compliance_operator/co-concepts/compliance-operator-understanding.html#compliance_profiles_understanding-compliance) I don't think engineering would change "platform" and "node" ever. As for the compliance profiles, I think it would be industry specific, so... not very often. 4- Are there Red Hat recommended best practices for using RHACS with Compliance Operator? I found these docs on the topic- https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.3/operating/manage-compliance-operator/compliance-operator-rhacs.html- but I don't know *why* you'd run both RHACS scanner and the Compliance Operator on the same cluster because I *think* the compliance operator is already pre-packaged with RHACS. Let me get back to you on this one. 5- Does RHACS's 'Managing Compliance' section imply a need for the Compliance Operator, especially with tailored profiles? This goes along with question 4. Let me get back to you on it. Hi Sherief, As I mentioned in slack, there are 2 sets of compliance profiles- one that comes with ACS out-of-the-box and an additional set of compliance profiles when you install the compliance operator. Ok, so the answer is in those docs- you just need to keep digging a bit in the "Additional Resources" link (again). Out-of-the-box ACS you get these profiles: CIS Benchmarks (Center for Internet Security) for Docker and Kubernetes HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) NIST Special Publication 800-190 and 800-53 (National Institute of Standards and Technology) PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) OpenSCAP (Open Security Content Automation Protocol): Available in RHACS for OpenShift Container Platform clusters when the Compliance Operator is installed and configured to provide results to RHACS Adding the Compliance Operator you get these additional profiles: ocp4-cis 94m ocp4-cis-node 94m ocp4-e8 94m ocp4-high 94m ocp4-high-node 94m ocp4-moderate 94m ocp4-moderate-node 94m ocp4-nerc-cip 94m ocp4-nerc-cip-node 94m ocp4-pci-dss 94m ocp4-pci-dss-node 94m rhcos4-e8 94m rhcos4-high 94m rhcos4-moderate 94m rhcos4-nerc-cip 94m https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/[…]iance-operator?extIdCarryOver=true&sc_cid=701f2000001OH6kAAG HTH, Dan

title: [RHOCP 4] Encountering 'Content is not allowed in prolog' message while accessing the route.
issue: Encountering the following error when a client hits an OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) route: ~~~ 20xx-11-26Txx:xx:09.8xxx781xx+xx:40 [Fatal Error]:1:1: Content is not allowed in prolog. ~~~
resolution: The error message, 'Content is not allowed in prolog,' is not generated by the HAproxy router pods running in the OCP cluster. Instead, it originates from the application itself. Therefore, it's beneficial to collaborate with the application team to address these specific concerns as they pertain to the application layer. **Troubleshooting Suggestions:** 1. **Check Application Logs:**- Examine the application logs for any entries related to the error. Look for clues pointing to the WebLogic Server or any other application-specific components. 2. **Review Application Configuration:**- Verify the XML configuration of the application, ensuring it conforms to the expected format and standards. Pay special attention to any changes or updates made recently. 3. **Inspect WebLogic Server:**- If your application is using WebLogic Server, investigate its logs for potential errors or warnings. The error may be linked to the server's configuration or the application's interaction with it. 4. **XML Parsing Length:**- Evaluate the length of XML parsing in your application. Very long parsing processes can sometimes lead to errors. Consider optimizing the XML parsing or breaking down large XML files if necessary. 5. **Application Dependencies:**- Assess any recent changes or updates to application dependencies. Incompatibility or misconfigurations in these dependencies can contribute to XML parsing issues.
root_cause: - These kinds of errors are often linked to issues within the customer's application, particularly with WebLogic Server. It highlights the need to thoroughly investigate application components when troubleshooting such issues.

Disaster recovery with stretch cluster for OpenShift Data Foundation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.13/html-single/configuring_openshift_data_foundation_disaster_recovery_for_openshift_workloads/index#introduction-to-stretch-cluster-disaster-recovery_stretch-cluster)

title: The secret vmware-vsphere-cloud-credentials is not getting synced correctly when updating secret vsphere-creds
issue: - The `secret/vmware-vsphere-cloud-credentials` in `ns/openshift-cluster-csi-drivers` is not synced correctly when updating `secret/vsphere-creds in ns/kube-system` due to which the `storage CO` is in progressing state.
resolution: - There is a [OCPBUGS-23426](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-23426) for this issue which has been fixed in OCPv4.14.5.
root_cause: - Previously, the `Cloud Credential Operator (CCO)` did not support updating the VMware vSphere root secret `vsphere-creds` in the `kube-system` namespace. This prevented the component secrets from synchronizing correctly. With this release, the CCO supports updating the vSphere root secret and resets the secret data when synchronized.

title: How to backup and restore application on RH OpenShift using OADP?
issue: - How to backup and restore applications on OpenShift using OADP?
resolution: - Following steps can be useful while working with OADP. The backup was done using the Velero CSI plugin, to backup CSI-backed PVCs. **1**. With OpenShift 4.11, installation of OADP can be done on the following cloud-provider. Install OADP Operator based on a cloud provider or respective mode.- [AWS](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/installing/installing-oadp-aws.html)- [AZURE](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/installing/installing-oadp-azure.html)- [GCP](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/installing/installing-oadp-gcp.html)- Along with this OADP can be used with:- [OpenShift Data Foundation(ODF/OCS)](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/installing/installing-oadp-ocs.html)- [Multicloud Object Gateway(MCG)](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/installing/installing-oadp-mcg.html) **2**. Creating a default Secret. To configure cloud-provider for Velero, steps to create this secret will be different, here sample output for **S3-compatible object storage**.- Create a default Secret if backup and snapshot locations use the same credentials or if there is no snapshot location required. The default name of the Secret is **cloud-credentials**. ~~~ $ cat < < EOF >./credentials-velero [default] aws_access_key_id= aws_secret_access_key= EOF #oc create secret generic cloud-credentials-n openshift-adp--from-file cloud=credentials-velero ~~~ **3**. Create **DataProtectionApplication** CR to configure **defaultPlugins, backupLocations, snapshotLocations and restic**(if enabled).- Navigate to Operators > Installed Operators > Create an instance of the DataProtectionApplication (DPA) CR **4**. Modifying VolumeSnapshotClass **DeletionPolicy** of **Retain** on the **VolumeSnapshotClass** will preserve the volume snapshot in the storage system for the lifetime of the Velero backup and will prevent the deletion of the volume snapshot- The Velero CSI plugin, to backup CSI backed PVCs, will choose the **VolumeSnapshotClass** in the cluster that has the same driver name and also has the **velero.io/csi-volumesnapshot-class: "true"** label set on it. ~~~ #oc patch volumesnapshotclass NAME--type=merge-p '{"deletionPolicy": "Retain"}' #oc label volumesnapshotclass NAME velero.io/csi-volumesnapshot-class="true" ~~~ **5**. Backup application with the below steps:- Navigate to Operators > Installed Operators Under Project openshift-adp, and click on OADP Operator. Under Provided APIs > Backup, click on Create instance- In IncludedNamespaces, add Namespace for which backup should be done.- Status of backup should show `Phase: Completed` **6**. Restore the application with the below steps:- This will be done with the application for which the OADP backup is completed.- Navigate to Operators > Installed Operators Under Project openshift-adp, and click on OADP Operator. Under Provided APIs > Restore- In IncludedNamespaces, add the Namespace for which should be restored and click the checkbox restorePVs.- Status of restore should show `Phase: Completed`.

title: Jaeger Pod frequently goes into Pending state when deploying Service Mesh on SNO in a disconnected environment
issue: - When deploying `OpenShift Service Mesh` on `SNO` in a `disconnected environment`, the `Jaeger` Pod frequently goes into `Pending state`. Specifically, when the `Jaeger Operator` recreates the `jaeger-pod` in `istio-system`(ServiceMeshControlPlane) namespace, it goes into `ImagePullBackOff`, and subsequently enters a `Pending state`.- Is there a setting that would eliminate this problem? Or is there a workaround?
resolution: - This behavior is not as expected. There is no configuration to resolve the issue.- The workaround is to `restart` the `Jaeger Operator` pods.- This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [OSSM-4109](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSSM-4109).- The bug `OSSM-4109` has been fixed in `Red Hat OpenShift Distributed Tracing 2.9.0` security update as per [Errata RHSA-2023:4986](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:4986)- For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: - The cause of `ImagePullBackOff` is that the image reference in the `oauth-proxy` container included in the `Jaeger` Pod refers to an image with the `latest` tag. ~~~ $ oc describe pod-n istio-system jaeger-6785d9fd7b-xxxxx <...> Normal Pulling 6m42s (x3 over 7m25s) kubelet Pulling image "registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-oauth-proxy:latest" Warning Failed 6m42s (x3 over 7m25s) kubelet Failed to pull image "registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-oauth-proxy:latest": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = pinging container registry registry.redhat.io: Get "https://registry.redhat.io/v2/": dial tcp: lookup registry.redhat.io on 172.110.12.31:53: server misbehaving Warning Failed 6m42s (x3 over 7m25s) kubelet Error: ErrImagePull Warning Failed 6m28s (x6 over 7m25s) kubelet Error: ImagePullBackOff Normal BackOff 2m24s (x23 over 7m25s) kubelet Back-off pulling image "registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-oauth-proxy:latest" $ oc get deployment jaeger-n istio-system-o yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: jaeger namespace: istio-system spec: template: metadata: spec: containers:- args: image: registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-oauth-proxy:latest # <------ ~~~- The `mirror registry` used in a `disconnected environment` contains images with digest values and does not have `tag` information, resulting in a failed attempt to access an `external registry` and pull the image.- However, the `oauth-proxy` in `Imagestream` references an image with a digest value, and when the `Imagestream` is used, the image pull succeeds, and the Pod is deployed. ~~~ $ oc get is-n openshift oauth-proxy-o yaml apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: oauth-proxy namespace: openshift spec: lookupPolicy: local: false tags:- annotations: null from: kind: DockerImage name: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:9c0cf8f4d56f16d74534c21a67cab0bbc524da3ef38a84116c4080bdc00e46ca # <------ generation: 5 importPolicy: scheduled: true name: v4.4 referencePolicy: type: Source ~~~- Upon startup, the `Jaeger Operator` accesses `route.openshift.io` to automatically detect platform features, but if this fails, it recognizes the platform as non-OpenShift and consequently stops using `Imagestream`, deploying the `oauth-proxy` container with a `tag` reference instead. ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-operators logs jaeger-operator-57cc46697c-xxxxx-c jaeger-operator | head-n 5 2023-05-25T05:21:11.102501612Z 1.6849920711024122e+09 INFO Versions {"os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "version": "go1.19.2", "jaeger-operator": "v1.39.0", "identity": "openshift-operators.jaeger-operator", "jaeger": "1.39.0"} 2023-05-25T05:21:11.102712914Z 1.6849920711027002e+09 INFO setup watching namespace(s) {"namespaces": ""} 2023-05-25T05:21:12.153493367Z I0525 05:21:12.153354 1 request.go:682] Waited for 1.035593138s due to client-side throttling, not priority and fairness, request: GET:https://172.30.0.1:443/apis/authorization.openshift.io/v1?timeout=32s 2023-05-25T05:21:18.906113267Z 1.684992078906025e+09 INFO controller-runtime.metrics Metrics server is starting to listen {"addr": "0.0.0.0:8383"} 2023-05-25T05:21:18.909317196Z 1.6849920789092264e+09 ERROR failed to determine the platform capabilities, auto-detected properties will remain the same until next cycle. {"error": "; Error getting resources for server group route.openshift.io: the server is currently unable to handle the request"} # <------ <...> 2023-05-25T05:21:19.007446090Z 1.6849920790074377e+09 INFO Not running on OpenShift, so won't configure OAuthProxy imagestream. ~~~- Because the `SNO` is not in a `HA` configuration, the `openshift-apiserver` does not respond while it is being recreated and initialized. This issue occurs when the initialization process of the `openshift-apiserver` and the `Jaeger Operator` overlap. ~~~ $ omc get-n openshift-apiserver pods apiserver-7fc4749f56-sw4pl-o yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod status: conditions:- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2023-05-25T05:21:09Z" status: "True" type: Initialized- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2023-05-25T05:21:19Z" # <------ It is overlap the initialization of Jaeger Operator pod status: "True" type: Ready- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2023-05-25T05:21:19Z" status: "True" type: ContainersReady- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2023-05-25T05:20:58Z" status: "True" type: PodScheduled startTime: "2023-05-25T05:20:58Z" ~~~

title: Troubleshooting "ImagePullBackOff" with "i/o timeout" in RHOCP 4
issue: - Pods are failing with the ImagePullBackOff issue.- Pod failed to start due to `error pinging docker registry dial tcp xxx.xx.xx.xxx:5000: i/o timeout`
resolution: - The "ImagePullBackOff" error with an "i/o timeout" in OpenShift pods indicates a failure to pull the container image from the specified registry. This can be caused by various factors, including network issues, authentication problems, or registry service disruptions.- Follow the diagnostic steps resolve the "ImagePullBackOff" issue.
root_cause: - The "ImagePullBackOff" with an "i/o timeout" error can be attributed to network connectivity issues, problems with the registry service, authentication failures, DNS resolution problems, insufficient disk space, misconfigured proxy settings, or registry health issues. Determining the root cause involves a systematic investigation of each potential issue and applying the appropriate resolution.

title: Unable to reattach OpenShift clusterafter certificate upgrade.
issue: - The Openshift Cluster Management Agent (klusterletaddonconfigs.agent.open-cluster-management.io) is causing problems when trying to detach or remove it from the cluster. After building a cluster, the agent cannot be detached successfully, and attempts to remove it resulted in the following Error == "ResourceError- klusterletaddonconfigs.agent.open-cluster-management.io "ocpp01" already exists."
resolution: 1. Which Custom Resource Definition (CRD) is managed by the "klusterletaddonconfigs.agent.open-cluster-management.io" in the manager cluster? Generally, the agent exists on the managed cluster and communicates with the hub cluster. Where does the agent typically reside? This “klusterletaddonconfigs.agent.open-cluster-management.io” is not an agent, it’s a configuration describing which addons we want to enable on a specific managed cluster. The klusterletaddonconfig is applied before we run the generate command. It’s a namespace-scoped resource on the hub, you can view it by the following command in this case: $ oc get klusterletaddonconfig-n ocpp01 ocpp01 It set in the managed cluster namespace and uses the same name with the managed cluster. Have you tried to delete it before reinstall a samename cluster? We can run: $ oc delete klusterletaddonconfig-n ocpp01 ocpp01 2. When building the cluster, the agent remains and continues to show in the console even after attempting to detach it? [Ref the attachment image] This path is for importing a new cluster, to reimport a detached cluster you need to go to another path. For example, in the following Clusters page, you can find the second cluster is detached, and hover the clicker on the right side of this row, you will see a dropdown list, the second item of it is “Import cluster”
root_cause: The root cause of the issue is that the OpenShift cluster's Klusterlet custom resource definition (CRD) already exists, which prevents the cluster from being imported or reattached. This could be due to incomplete detachment during a previous process or the cluster being imported before. The attempts to delete the CRD using commands have not been successful in resolving the problem.

title: How to configure subPath for  on a volume autoprovisioned for use with a new pod from the volumeClaimTemplate of a StatefulSet?
issue: - How to configure subPath for on a volume autoprovisioned for use with a new pod from the volumeClaimTemplate of a StatefulSet?
resolution: - Specify the `subPath` field within the `volumeMount` section of your container configuration in the pod template. Here’s an example YAML snippet: ~~~ apiVersion: apps kind: StatefulSet metadata: name: example-statefulset spec: serviceName: "example" replicas: 3 selector: matchLabels: app: example template: metadata: labels: app: example spec: containers: name: example-container image: nginx:latest volumeMounts: name: data-volume mountPath: /path/to/mount subPath: your/subpath volumeClaimTemplates: metadata: name: data-volume spec: accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"] resources: requests: storage: 1Gi ~~~ In this example, the `volumeMount` section in the container specification includes the `subPath` field, which allows to specify the `subpath` within the volume where the container’s mount should point to. Adjust the `mountPath` and `subPath` values according to your requirements and as per the configuration of the pod.

title: OpenShift Console configuration for OpenID Connect Logout
issue: - How to allow the OIDC token hint to be appended to the logout URL of the OpenShift console?- Issue- Getting logoutRedirect: Error- Missing parameters: id_token_hint- Invalid parameters: redirect_url
resolution: - Keycloak can not logout the user automatically and redirect to the application without the id_token_hint, this is part of the RP initiated logout specification and is a must to prevent malicious applications logging out users, as well as open redirects.- OpenShift doesn't pass the id_token_hint, there's no available method to facilitate a logout without a confirmation dialog, as any action taken could potentially result in a security vulnerability. KCS article about this topic:-- RH-SSO 7.6 error: Parameter 'redirect_uri' no longer supported. Please use 'post_logout_redirect_uri' with 'id_token_hint'[1](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973001) The absence of the id_token_hint results in the failure to use the post_logout_redirect_uri.

title: Cluster upgrade stuck with pulling image from docker.io fails
issue: - Upgrade is stuck and ods are in crashloopbackoff state with below error. ~~~ Warning Failed 65m (x7 over 155m) kubelet Failed to pull image "docker.io/netapp/trident-autosupport:23.10": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = loading manifest for target platform: reading manifest sha256:3cf7018bda3520bf3201c65930e453c0dd9e2df0781cbb4d984f11141d1941bb in docker.io/netapp/trident-autosupport: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit. You may increase the limit by authenticating and upgrading: https://www.docker.com/increase-rate-limit ~~~
resolution: - Check the service account associated to that pod ~~~ $ oc get pod-oyaml | grep-i serviceaccount ~~~- Create a secret and linked it to that service account ~~~ $ oc create secret docker-registry docker--docker-server-docker.io-- docker-username=--docker-password=-- docker-email= $ oc secrets link default docker-for-pull ~~~
root_cause: - This is a default behavior from docker.io, the registry will not allow anonymous pull more than 100 within six hours, hence we need to add a docker account to the SA which will pull the image.- Please check [How to work around Docker's new download rate limit on Red Hat OpenShift](https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2021/02/18/how-to-work-around-dockers-new-download-rate-limit-on-red-hat-openshift#docker_s_new_rate_limit) as well for more information.

title: Developer portal does not exist

title: How to run systemctl inside a pod?
issue: - I would like to run systemctl inside a pod, how to implement it?
resolution: - We can mount `/host` into the pod, and set hostPID to true to run `systemctl` inside a pod, for example: ~~~ # cat busybox.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: busybox spec: containers:- name: busybox image: busybox command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; title: A PV is not created and A PVC for the PV is pending with 'waiting for first consumer to be created before binding'.
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - The expected PV is not created when the PVC was created and the status of PVS seems to be pending with the error 'waiting for first consumer to be created before binding'. ~~~ $ oc describe pvc test-pvc-n test-project Name: test-pvc Namespace: test-project StorageClass: gp2 Status: Pending Volume: Labels: Annotations: Finalizers: [kubernetes.io/pvc-protection] Capacity: Access Modes: VolumeMode: Filesystem Used By: Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal WaitForFirstConsumer 86s (x26 over 7m15s) persistentvolume-controller waiting for first consumer to be created before binding ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get pv NAME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES RECLAIM POLICY STATUS CLAIM STORAGECLASS REASON AGE pvc-XXXXX 1Gi RWO Delete Bound openshift-monitoring/alertmanager-data-alertmanager-main-1 gp2 67d pvc-XXXXX 1Gi RWO Delete Bound openshift-monitoring/alertmanager-data-alertmanager-main-2 gp2 67d pvc-XXXXX 10Gi RWO Delete Bound openshift-monitoring/prometheus-data-prometheus-k8s-0 gp2 67d pvc-XXXXX 10Gi RWO Delete Bound openshift-monitoring/prometheus-data-prometheus-k8s-1 gp2 67d pvc-XXXXX 1Gi RWO Delete Bound openshift-monitoring/alertmanager-data-alertmanager-main-0 gp2 67d ~~~
resolution: - This is expected behaivor if the StorageClass is set the BindingMode as "WaitForFirstConsumer". If any pod(Consumer) binds the PVC, then the PV status should turn to Bound from Pending.- Please check a result when an admin/user create a test pod and make it use the PVC.
root_cause: - A cluster administrator can address this issue by specifying the WaitForFirstConsumer mode which will delay the binding and provisioning of a PersistentVolume until a Pod using the PersistentVolumeClaim is created.- Please refer to doc [Volume Binding Mode].(https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes/#volume-binding-mode)

title: Option to update haproxy-config.template in Red Hat OpenShift
issue: - Options to enable and disable access logs without restarting the router pods in Red Hat OpenShift 4.x.- In order to enable access logging, it is needed to modify the Ingress Controller object which results in the restart of the router pods.
resolution: - Red Hat OpenShift 3.11 provides environment variables and HAProxy template that could be modified.- It allows for a large degree of customization of the HAProxy routers.- Red Hat OpenShift 4.x uses the Ingress Operator to manage router configuration, so some options are no longer configurable.- The request has been raised with the Red Hat Engineering Team to include the feature in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) under [RFE-3714](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3714).- If there is a requirement for this feature, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: - The objective is to turn on/off logs as and when needed with the least interruption to router.- In Red Hat OpenShift 4.x, there is no such option to update haproxy-config.template for enabling the access log.

title: OVN South Bound(SB) database missing columns warnings in Red Hat OpenShift
issue: - Reading from OVN SB Database throws WARNING "Port_Binding table in OVN_Southbound database lacks additional_chassis column (database needs upgrade?)".- During upgrade from OCP 4.10 to 4.11, ovsdb schema change is not happening. # ovn-sbctl list port_binding | head 2022-11-26T07:40:49Z|00001|ovsdb_idl|WARN|Port_Binding table in OVN_Southbound database lacks additional_chassis column (database needs upgrade?) 2022-11-26T07:40:49Z|00002|ovsdb_idl|WARN|Port_Binding table in OVN_Southbound database lacks additional_encap column (database needs upgrade?) 2022-11-26T07:40:49Z|00003|ovsdb_idl|WARN|Port_Binding table in OVN_Southbound database lacks requested_additional_chassis column (database needs upgrade?)
resolution: - Conversion of OVN databases schemas should take place during any version change.- The request has been raised with the Red Hat Engineering Team to fix the [BUG](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-4557).- There is a [PULL](https://github.com/ovn-org/ovn-kubernetes/pull/3246/files) request for this issue as well.
root_cause: - ovn-dbchecker only compare DB and schema version before triggering a conversion, but the schema is allowed to change without version update.- When the ovsdb schema change, one is supposed to call ovsdb-tool convert to make sure the DB schema is migrated to the new schema.

title: Does dnsmasq installed on RedHat CoreOS from OpenShift 4.11 support DNSSec
issue: - Based on DNSMasq documentation [page](https://thekelleys.org.uk/dnsmasq/docs/dnsmasq-man.html) DNSMasq must be compiled with HAVE_DNSSEC enabled.- In CoreOS, the output from "dnsmasq-v ", does not show that flag.
resolution: - In OpenShift 4.11, CoreOS uses dnsmasq-2.79.DNSSec functionality has been included in dnsmasq-2.76 version.- So in OpenShift 4.11, DNSSec functionality is available.- The [Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1638703) has fixed this issue.
root_cause: - Secure DNS feature is essential and it is supported by the flag DNSSEC in dmsmasq.- So in order to avail of this feature, dnsmasq should be compiled with HAVE_DNSSEC enable.- Secure DNS functionality by dnsmasq can be verified as below.- [root@master ~]# dnsmasq--version Dnsmasq version 2.79 Copyright (c) 2000-2018 Simon Kelley Compile time options: IPv6 GNU-getopt DBus no-i18n IDN2 DHCP DHCPv6 no-Lua TFTP no-conntrack ipset auth DNSSEC loop-detect notify- Prior to dnsmsq 2.76 version, the DNSSEC feature was not available.

title: SDN Pods crash with &quot;fatal error: concurrent map read and map write&quot; resulting in &quot;failed to destroy network for pod sandbox&quot; Multus errors
issue: - In OpenShift 4.11.30, SDN pods crash due to issue with concurrent map read and write error.- It throws the error as below.- fatal error: concurrent map read and map write goroutine 159 [running]: runtime.throw({0x1f548ee?, 0x10?}) runtime/panic.go:992 +0x71 fp=0xc03b74fbc0 sp=0xc03b74fb90 pc=0x43c3f1 runtime.mapaccess1_faststr(0xc014455100?, 0x37?, {0xc03d618d80, 0x24}) runtime/map_faststr.go:22 +0x3a5 fp=0xc03b74fc28 sp=0xc03b74fbc0 pc=0x419145 github.com/openshift/sdn/pkg/network/node.(*networkPolicyPlugin).getPodIP(...) github.com/openshift/sdn/pkg/network/node/networkpolicy.go:991
resolution: - This issue has resolved in OpenShift 4.14- The [OCPBUGS-13975](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13975 " SDN Pods crash with "fatal error: concurrent map read and map write" resulting in "failed to destroy network for pod sandbox" Multus errors") fixed the issue in OpenShift 4.14
root_cause: - In the below function, the np.lock mutex is not acquired and it leads to panic.- func (np *networkPolicyPlugin) getPodIP(pod *corev1.Pod) string {if pod.Status.PodIP!= "" {return pod.Status.PodIP} // empty string will be returned if both pod.Status.PodIP and np.localPodIPs[pod.UID] are empty return np.localPodIPs[pod.UID]

title: Does bond-cni supports bonding for vfio-pci in Red Hat OpenShift
issue: - In OpenShift, bond-cni is not loading bond kernel module when vfio-pci is used.
resolution: - When the driver is on vfio, the kernel doesn't even see the devices. So there is no way for the bond-cni to create a bond.- if the device is on vfio and if it uses the DPDK to handle traffic than bond driver inside DPDK should be used.
root_cause: - By design, kernel has no visibility when the driver is on vfio. So in such cases bond-cni can not create the bond.

title: How to update LDAP bindDN password?
issue: - How to update LDAP user password?- How to update LDAP secret?
resolution: - Firstly, update the oauth_config.yaml with the updated LDAP bindDN user and the reference to the secret ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: OAuth metadata: name: cluster spec: identityProviders:- ldap: attributes: id: email: name: preferredUsername: bindDN: "cn=new_bindDN_user,ou=users,dc=example,dc=com" # Update with your new bindDN user bindPassword: name: ldap-secret-new namespace: # Update with the appropriate namespace ca: name: "" insecure: false url: " " ~~~ Make sure to replace new_bindDN_user, ou=users,dc=example,dc=com, your-namespace, and other placeholders with your actual values.- Create a secret 'new_secret.yaml' ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: ldap-secret-new type: Opaque data: password: RGFzc3dvcmQxMjM= # Base64-encoded new password, e.g., "Password123" ~~~ Replace the RGFzc3dvcmQxMjM= with the Base64-encoded value of your new password.- Apply the updated OAuth configuration and the new secret: ~~~ $ oc apply-f oauth_config.yaml $ oc apply-f new_secret.yaml ~~~ Ensure that you are in the correct namespace where you want to apply these changes In case of failures run the `oc adm must-gather` command and check the [Data-gathering in the Event must-gather Fails](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4971311).

title: How to create private/public key for service account? [-service-account-private-key-file]
issue: - Not able to create a private/public key for a service account?- How to create private/public for each service account?- How to create a key with ssh-keygen and add it into this configuration will this work?
resolution: - Private Key- Create a private key using openssl command ~~~ openssl genrsa-out private.key 3072 ~~~- Public Key- Create a public key using openssl command ~~~ openssl rsa-in private.key-pubout-out public.key ~~~- Create CSR- Create a certificate signing request(CSR) using the generated private key ~~~ openssl req-new-subj "/C=XX/ST=XXX-XX L=XXX/X=Red Hat/CN=secure-.domain.name.test"-key private.key-out web.csr ~~~- Create CRT- Generate the certificate using the key and csr ~~~ openssl x509-req-in web.csr-CA private-CA.pem-CAkey private-CA.key-CAcreateserial-out public.crt ~~~- Do I have to create priv/pub for each service account?- Please attach the existing keys, because Service accounts authenticate to the API using tokens signed by a private RSA key. The authentication layer verifies the signature using a matching public RSA key.- Private RSA key file (for token signing).- Public RSA key files (for token verification).- if I create a key with ssh-keygen and add it to this configuration will this work?- No, To know more about ssh-keygen https://www.ssh.com/academy/ssh/keygen.- OpenSSL is designed to provide a method for securing web based communication.

title: Purchasing the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform offering on Google Cloud Marketplace with on-demand only provides an evaluation support subscription with Red Hat
issue: After deploying an OpenShift cluster using the Google Cloud Marketplace images, it only has a 60-day evaluation subscription to Red Hat support.
resolution: As part of the preparation to deploy the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform offering from the Google Cloud Marketplace, you must first have a valid Red Hat account with which to log into the Red Hat Console. Using this account, you need to access Red Hat support via [this link](https://console.redhat.com/?gcp-ocp-activation) to request your OpenShift product subscription. The link will redirect to the Red Hat console to automatically request your support subscription. You will then receive a confirmation email from Red Hat on how to activate your subscription. This process, along with other details for pricing, billing and deploying the cluster, is described on the official Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform offering page on the Google Cloud Marketplace [here](https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/redhat-marketplace/red-hat-openshift-container-platform-prod) Once you have activated your Red Hat subscription, you must install your cluster using the command line tool, with an `install-config.yaml` that has been customised to specify a GCP Marketplace image to use for the clusters compute machines. Please refer to the "Using the GCP Marketplace offering" section of the "Installing a cluster on GCP with customizations" chapter of the official Red Hat OpenShift documentation [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/installing/installing_gcp/installing-gcp-customizations.html#installation-gcp-marketplace_installing-gcp-customizations) for more details on this. After installing the cluster, you can review its status via the [Red Hat Console](https://console.redhat.com) site. If the cluster is showing as using an evaluation subscription and you have obtained a valid OpenShift subscription as described above, you may need to manually attach the subscription by following [this article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6262561).
root_cause: When deploying the Google Cloud Marketplace offering of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform, it is required to request an OpenShift product subscription via a Red Hat support link.

title: Alert "openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service/openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service targets in openshift-operators namespace have been unreachable"
issue: - `TargetDown` alert is firing with below description: ~~~ X% of the openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service/openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service targets in openshift-operators namespace have been unreachable for more than 15 minutes. This may be a symptom of network connectivity issues, down nodes, or failures within these components. Assess the health of the infrastructure and nodes running these targets and then contact support. ~~~
resolution: To address this issue, kindly perform the following recommended steps.- Uninstall the `Red Hat OpenShift GitOps` operator from `openshift-operators` namespace.- OpenShift Container Platform web console **> ** Administrative view **> ** Operators **> ** Installed Operators **> ** Click the Options menu next **⋮** to the `Red Hat OpenShift GitOps` and select Uninstall Operator **> ** Click Uninstall.- Reinstall the `Red Hat OpenShift GitOps` operator within the `openshift-gitops-operator` namespace.- OpenShift Container Platform web console **> ** Administrative view **> ** Operators **> ** OperatorHub **> ** Choose `Red Hat OpenShift GitOps` from the list of available Operators, and click Install **> ** Select gitops-1.10 as the Update Channel **> ** Under Installation Mode select All namespaces on the cluster **> ** Ensure that `openshift-gitops-operator` is selected under Installed Namespace **> ** Tick a box for Enable Operator recommended cluster monitoring on this Namespace **> ** Click Install.- This process does not cause any impact. The new operator should seamlessly resume where the old one left off, as long as deletion of the operator's child resources during the uninstallation (There should be an option before hitting uninstall over the openshift web UI). For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).
root_cause: - Beginning with version `gitops-1.10`, a modification has been implemented in response to bug [GITOPS-3073](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-3073). This change involves adjusting the default installation namespace for the `Red Hat OpenShift GitOps` Operator to a dedicated namespace known as `openshift-gitops-operator`.

title: ArgoCD ApplicationSet Failed to unmarshal

In the below example `ignoreDifferences` has a incorrect field: ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: ApplicationSet spec: [..] template: metadata: name: '{{cluster}}-cluster-app' spec: ignoreDifferences: [..]- group: hive.openshift.io kind: ClusterDeployment jsonPointers:- /spec/controlPlaneConfig jsonPointers: <------------------- this is incorrect config, it should be under ignoreDifferences.group- /spec/provisioning/imageSetRef [..] ~~~ Correct Config: ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: ApplicationSet spec: [..] template: metadata: name: '{{cluster}}-cluster-app' spec: ignoreDifferences: [..]- group: hive.openshift.io kind: ClusterDeployment jsonPointers:- /spec/controlPlaneConfig- group: "*" kind: ClusterDeployment jsonPointers:- /spec/provisioning/imageSetRef [..] ~~~
root_cause: - Malformed yaml file.
