title: Troubleshooting 3scale SMTP related issues
issue: - Emails are not being sent as expected, often causing `Internal error` pop up to appear.- 3scale users invitations are not working.
resolution: Some common errors and their solutions are: 1. `SMTPAuthenticationError: Unrecognized authentication type`: indicates a wrong value provided for the `authentication` `SMTP` variable. It is sufficient to set the correct value that the `SMTP Server` is expecting to receive. 2. `Exception:SendAsDeniedException`: can appear if the `SMTP Server` provider prevents from customizing the `From:` field in outgoing emails. 3scale is configured to set the `From:` field to a `no-reply` email by default and therefore if the error appears it will be necessary to disable this option in order to successfully send emails. In order to disable the `From:` field customization in 3scale the outgoing email addresses need to be set to a value that is a verified alias for the account, i.e. the value of the `username SMTP variable` can be used. The outgoing email addresses can be customized by accessing the `Admin Portal` at `https:// /site/dns` and with the following Knowledge Solution: [Edit outgoing email addresses](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4112341 "Edit outgoing email addresses"). 3. `550 5.7.1 Unable to relay`: The sender is not authorized to send to the destination. This can be the result of per-host or per-recipient filtering and should further investigate on the `SMTP Server`'s settings. 4. `Net::SMTPSyntaxError with message 504 5.7.4 Unrecognized authentication type`: This indicates the incorrect use of values configured in `system-smtp` secret, recreate the secret with correct value, redeploy the system-app and system-sidekiq and test it. 5. `Net::ReadTimeout` exception indicates the destination SMTP server didn't respond to the request in 60 sec. Confirm the SMTP server whether it got any trouble at that time. [If you are using egress IP in OCP for 3scale project/namespace](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/openshift_sdn/assigning-egress-ips.html), then ensure that it is added into your SMTP server whitelist. Exception-- {:exception=> {:class=> Net::ReadTimeout,:message=> "Net::ReadTimeout",:backtrace=> ["/opt/rh/rh-ruby24/root/usr/share/ruby/net/protocol.rb:176:in `rbuf_fill'", "/opt/rh/rh-ruby24/root/usr/share/ruby/net/protocol.rb:154:in `readuntil'", "/opt/rh/rh-ruby24/root/usr/share/ruby/net/protocol.rb:164:in `readline'", "/opt/rh/rh-ruby24/root/usr/share/ruby/net/smtp.rb:950:in `recv_response'"]},:parameters=> {}} Other status codes and their descriptions can be found in [RFC 3463](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3463). **Note:** failures while sending emails often can cause an internal error message to appear. Events that trigger emails and eventually might end up failing are: Account Creation, User Invitation, Message Sent, Usage Alert, etc.

title: How to Clear "1 large objects found in pool" In Ceph
issue: When the `$ ceph health detail` output does not ID a PG where the large omap is located but does provide the pool name. ~~~ health: HEALTH_WARN 1 large omap objects bash-5.1$ ceph health detail [WRN] LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS: 1 large omap objects 1 large objects found in pool 'ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-metadata' ~~~
resolution: 1. For ODF users. If the rook-ceph-tools pod is not installed, follow the steps outlined in the [How to configure the Rook-Ceph Toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891) solution article. 2. ID the pool. ~~~ $ ceph health detail [WRN] LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS: 1 large omap objects 1 large objects found in pool 'ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-metadata' <---------- ~~~ 3. Take the pool name from step 2, and insert into the following for loop: ~~~ $ for i in `ceph pg ls-by-pool | tail-n +2 | head-n-2 | awk '{print $1}'`; do echo-n "$i: "; ceph pg $i query | grep num_large_omap_objects | head-1 | awk '{print $2}'; done | grep ": 1" ~~~ **Example:** ~~~ $ for i in `ceph pg ls-by-pool ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-metadata | tail-n +2 | head-n-2 | awk '{print $1}'`; do echo-n "$i: "; ceph pg $i query | grep num_large_omap_objects | head-1 | awk '{print $2}'; done | grep ": 1" ~~~ 4. Take the PG ID from the output in step 3, and initiate a deep scrub on that PG. ~~~ $ ceph osd pg deep-scrub ~~~
root_cause: In some instances, the `$ ceph health detail` output will provide the PG ID associated with the large omap. In this instance, the `$ ceph health detail` output did not reveal that information so a for loop was implemented to capture the `pgid`. Once captured, a deep scrub can be executed on that `pgid` to clear the large omap

resolution: * Upgrade to resolve the issue: The issue is resolved in RHCS 5.3z1, RHCS 6.1, and higher RHCS releases. As the issue is common in ODF environment, upgrade ODF to 4.13.6 or higher and the RHCS version will be upgraded to RHCS 6.1z3. * If possible, delete snapshots. A common issue is `snapshots` will have `clones` created. This means, at a later time, when the `snapshot` is deleted, it will become stuck in the trash folder. Because the `clone` is dependent on the `snapshot`. Once the `clone` is deleted, the `snapshot` will also be removed from the trash folder. For more information, [See the CephFS Docs:](https://docs.ceph.com/en/pacific/cephfs/) * Mute the Warning `[WRN]` If none of the above actions can be done, please follow this Documentation Link to `Mute` the Ceph Warning `[WRN]`. URL: [Troubleshooting Guide, section 1.5- Muting health alerts of a Ceph cluster](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_ceph_storage/5/html-single/troubleshooting_guide/index#muting-health-alerts-of-a-ceph-cluster_diag) After the cluster is upgraded, the action to `Mute` the Ceph Warning `[WRN]`, should be reversed. This issue can be seen transiently when a directory exceeds 100K entries and before the next `Deep Scrub` of the affected PG. One can `Deep Scrub` the PG manually: ~~~ # ceph pg deep-scrub # ceph pg deep-scrub 1.11 ~~~
root_cause: There is a code bug where directories are not split. If any directory becomes large enough, it will result in a persistent `large OMAP`. Expected behavior: For directories, there is a soft limit of 100K entries. When this limit is breached, the next `Deep Scrub` will split the directory into two directories to avoid the creation of a `large OMAP`. Buggy Behavior: `Snapshot` entries are not counted as entries. If a directory is mostly `snapshots`, it can well exceed 100K and eventually result in a persistent `large OMAP`. ### Artifacts: [Ceph Upstream Tracker #55215](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/55215) [RHCS 5.3.x Bugzilla #2164338](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2164338) [RHCS 6.1.x Bugzilla #2159294](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2159294) [RHCS 5.3.1 Errata RHSA-2023:0980- Security Advisory](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0980) [RHCS 6.1.0 Errata RHSA-2023:3623- Security Advisory](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3623)

title: Local Storage Operator (LSO) in 4.13+ is ignoring scsi-* discovery symlinks from earlier versions
issue: When using the Local Storage Operator (LSO) on a cluster, after updating to 4.13 or newer, Persistent Volumes (PVs) created on earlier versions aren't recreated after being deleted. The references haven't changed, and the symlinks on the nodes with the scsi-
path references are still in place.
resolution: There is a request back with the Red Hat engineering team to address this issue in: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-31059 To mitigate this in the interim, access the node and remove the symlink to the deleted device/PV for the LSO to re-detect the PV and allow it to be recreated.
root_cause: Changes were made in 4.13.10+ to have the LSO prefer wwid-* naming schemes: https://github.com/openshift/local-storage-operator/pull/419 This is suspected to have changed the behavior that we're seeing here

title: Why are windows pods running on Windows Server 2019 restarting very often even when they are in idle state ?
issue: Why are windows pods running on Windows Server 2019 restarting very often even when they are in idle state?
resolution: Reported issues has been fixed in the following errata OCP 4.15: Red Hat OpenShift for Windows Containers 10.15.0 [RHSA-2024:0954](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0954) OCP 4.14: Red Hat OpenShift for Windows Containers 9.0.1 [RHSA-2024:1203](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:1203) Contact Red Hat Technical support to know the latest status on the bugfixes for older releases like OCP 4.13 and OCP 4.12
root_cause: Application Deployments were configured with liveness & readiness probes. To check whether an application is healthy after being ready, Kubelet sends liveness probes at regular intervals. Interval and the frequency of liveness probes are controlled through the application deployment configuration. When there is no response for X(usually 10) consecutive liveness probes, Kubelet considers the application to be down and then restarts the pod. In-spite of no application workload, Kubelet restarts the pod at random intervals(usually after 2 hours). Restarts were initiated by kubelet and it is due to lack of response to the liveness probe. Upon investigation, it was found that the TCP reply packet from the application pod related to liveness probe never reached the Kubelet or the host layer. With respect to the trace analysis, it was noticed that the packets were re-written to a different container IP.

title: OpenShift logging pods in troubled state due to insufficient resources
issue: - Pods are in pending or failed status- Logging Pods are killed with OOMKill messages- Pods resource request is too high- Some Nodes are allocated lower resources than pod requests- Event log shows FailedScheduling message ##Logs ~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cluster-logging-operator-6d86699679-4kl8v 1/1 Running 0 2h16m elasticsearch-cdm-u461sh0x-1-5dbd579767-tjdsl 0/2 Pending 0 1h56m elasticsearch-cdm-u461sh0x-2-688597755c-xxf97 0/2 Pending 0 2h11m elasticsearch-cdm-u461sh0x-3-5578477b8b-rfk7f 0/2 Pending 0 2h11m elasticsearch-im-app-28275225-x5gwd 0/1 Failed 0 8m34s ~~~ The event logs contain messages such as: ~~~ Unknown Warning FailedScheduling pod/kibana-5c65cb49d-9rzlw 0/27 nodes are available: 21 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: reserved}, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master:}. preemption: 0/27 nodes are available: 27 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling. message: '0/27 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:}, 20 node(s) didn''t match Pod''s node affinity/selector, 3 Insufficient memory, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master:}. preemption: 0/27 nodes are available: 24 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling, 3 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.' ~~~ Collector pod are restarting because of OOMkill: ~~~ OOMKILL for pod/collector-4x7td lastState: terminated: containerID: cri-o://31408f45e597ce2f3ff609981649c7807bcc63db60fae70f8c177606534e5245 exitCode: 137 finishedAt: "2024-02-26T09:01:54Z" reason: OOMKilled startedAt: "2024-02-26T08:35:15Z" OOMKILL for pod/collector-bzwrp lastState: terminated: containerID: cri-o://b8225d801bcb7d9b34f6d1c61e33a34cc78c819d4a40b18fd4f53ef467942e56 exitCode: 137 finishedAt: "2024-02-25T15:04:23Z" reason: OOMKilled startedAt: "2024-02-22T01:51:20Z"... Output Omitted... ~~~
resolution: Check for node and pod limits to ensure that no limits are breached. For example, a node may be allocated with 32Gi of memory, while pods are requesting 64Gi. For Pods: ~~~ oc-n openshift-logging get clusterlogging instance-o yaml > clo.txt ~~~ For Nodes: ~~~ for node in `oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/infra=-oname`; do oc get $node-oyaml | grep capacity-A7; done ~~~ Review the allocated resources to the node and the limits on the pods. Increase the node resources(CPU, Memory) or decrease the pod requests/limits. Refer to this document for [Configuring CPU and memory limits for logging components](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/logging/config/cluster-logging-memory.html).
root_cause: The resource allocation on the pods exceed the resources/limits set on the nodes.

title: OpenShift cluster Upgrade stalls on machine-config-pools
issue: - OpenShift cluster upgrade (from version 4.11.12 to version 4.11.27) stall in between- Only machine-config operator is in degraded state.- All the Cluster Operator (CO) except for the Machine Config (MC) has been updated successfully
resolution: After further review, the current base for MachineConfig for worker and gpuworker role are the same. ``` $ OLD_RENDERED=rendered-worker-10e4f526fbd472390d8cafb9f46d60c5 $ NEW_RENDERED=rendered-gpuworker-10e4f526fbd472390d8cafb9f46d60c5 $ diff-NrU 5 <(oc get mc ${OLD_RENDERED}-o yaml) <(oc get mc ${NEW_RENDERED}-o yaml) ``` To use the same base of worker MC on gpuworker MCP, we can update the MCP and add "worker" as below: ``` $ oc edit mcp gpuworker ``` ``` "machineConfigSelector": {"matchExpressions": [{"key": "machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role", "operator": "In", "values": ["worker", "gpuworker"]}] ``` And remove the part ``` configuration: name: rendered-gpuworker-645d03dd672043da83f86dd14a31478a source:- apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig name: rendered-gpuworker-10e4f526fbd472390d8cafb9f46d60c5 ``` Later if you want to add any additional changes to the gpuworker only, you can create new MachineConfig such as `99-gpuworker-something` and add label to it: ``` "labels": {"machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role": "gpuworker"}, ``` It will be automatically applied to those nodes.

title: SR-IOV Network Operator subscription fails on '4.14 channel'
issue: - While installing `SR-IOV Network operator` in RHOCP 4.14 cluster using `4.14` channel getting below error: ~~~- message: 'constraints not satisfiable: no operators found in channel 4.14 of package sriov-network-operator in the catalog referenced by subscription sriov-network-operator-subscription, subscription sriov-network-operator-subscription exists' ~~~
resolution: - Use `channel: stable` in Subscription to the `SR-IOV Operator`. ~~~ $ cat < < EOF| oc create-f- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: sriov-network-operator-subscription namespace: openshift-sriov-network-operator spec: channel: stable name: sriov-network-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~- The `CSV` should be in `Succeeded` state if `SR-IOV Network Operator` is ready. To verify that run the following command. ~~~ $ oc get csv-n openshift-sriov-network-operator NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE sriov-network-operator.4.14.0-xxxxxxxxxxxx SR-IOV Network Operator 4.14.0-xxxxxxxxxxxx sriov-network- operator.4.14.0-xxxxxxxxxxxx Succeeded ~~~
root_cause: - All versions of the operator are now moved to `stable` channel. The ` ` channels are not published anymore.

title: User capabilities in CephObjectStoreUser - OpenShift Data Foundation 4.15 Developer preview
resolution: Administrator-like capabilities are provided for Ceph RADOS Gateway (RGW) users with the help of user capabilities. In OpenShift Data Foundation, you can set these capabilities with the help of `CephObjectStore` CRD so that the end users can send requests to the RGW server using the libraries like `go-ceph` similar to `radosgw-admin` commands. An example of `cephobjectstoreuser.yaml`: ~~~ apiVersion: ceph.rook.io/v1 kind: CephObjectStoreUser metadata: name: myUser namespace: openshift-storage spec: store: my-store displayName: my display name capabilities: user: “*” bucket: “*” ~~~ To create the user, use the following command in the command-line interface: ~~~ oc create-f cephobjectstoreuser.yaml ~~~ OpenShift Data Foundation supports only capabilities like users, buckets, and roles. However, Red Hat Ceph Storage supports more capabilities. For more information, see- [Ceph Object Gateway administrative API](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_ceph_storage/7/html/developer_guide/ceph-object-gateway-administrative-api)- [Add and remove admin capabilities](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_ceph_storage/7/html/object_gateway_guide/administration#usr-mgmt-add-remove-admin-capabilities-rgw)

title: How to customize Jaeger tracing collector with additional  arguments RHOCP 4
issue: - How to customize `Jaeger tracing collector` with additional `arguments` like below? ~~~ collector.otlp.grpc.tls.cert=/etc/tls-config/tls.crt collector.otlp.grpc.tls.enabled=true collector.otlp.grpc.tls.key=/etc/tls-config/tls.key ~~~
resolution: - For the `collector arguments`, use `options` parameter to add `custom` arguments: ~~~ spec: strategy: production collector: options: collector.otlp.grpc.tls.cert: /etc/tls-config/tls.crt collector.otlp.grpc.tls.enabled: true collector.otlp.grpc.tls.key: /etc/tls-config/tls.key ~~~

resolution: - To give a remedy for the `fluentd` custom stack, add the feature of `concatenation plugin`: [concatenation Plugin](https://github.com/fluent-plugins-nursery/fluent-plugin-concat). [FP]) (?.+)$/ tag k8s @label @CONCAT @type concat key message partial_key partial_flag partial_value P @type relabel @label @OUTPUT @type stdout ~~~- For Red Hat logging stack refer solution [Multiline logs in OpenShift 4 with ClusterLogForwarder API](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/logging/log_collection_forwarding/configuring-log-forwarding.html#logging-multil[…]log-forwarding)

title: How to renew or recreate a node's certificate in RHOCP4
issue: One or more nodes are not working, with a "NotReady" status;

Kubelet service log shows lots of messages: ~~~ Unable to authenticate the request due to an error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority http: TLS handshake error from 10.173.2.64:43632: no serving certificate available for the kubelet ~~~
Expired or mis-matched node certificates, but there are no Pending CSRs
How do I redeploy node certificates or do TLS bootstrapping?
resolution: > **Important:** This procedure is to renew **only one node** certificate without recreating the node and it's presupposed that the cluster as a whole is working. If multiple control plane nodes are not working due to expired certificates, please refer to the product documentation or open a support case with Red Hat for further analysis. 1. Make sure you have access to command `oc` with cluster-admin privileges: ~~~ $ oc whoami system:admin ~~~ 2. Check that there aren't Pending CSRs: ~~~ $ oc get csr | grep Pending ~~~ 3. Create a file `recover_kubeconfig.sh` in your bastion host with the contents: ~~~ #!/bin/bash set-eou pipefail # context intapi=$(oc get infrastructures.config.openshift.io cluster-o "jsonpath={.status.apiServerInternalURI}") context="$(oc config current-context)" # cluster cluster="$(oc config view-o "jsonpath={.contexts[?(@.name==\"$context\")].context.cluster}")" server="$(oc config view-o "jsonpath={.clusters[?(@.name==\"$cluster\")].cluster.server}")" # token ca_crt_data="$(oc get secret-n openshift-machine-config-operator node-bootstrapper-token-o "jsonpath={.data.ca\.crt}" | base64--decode)" namespace="$(oc get secret-n openshift-machine-config-operator node-bootstrapper-token-o "jsonpath={.data.namespace}" | base64--decode)" token="$(oc get secret-n openshift-machine-config-operator node-bootstrapper-token-o "jsonpath={.data.token}" | base64--decode)" export KUBECONFIG="$(mktemp)" oc config set-credentials "kubelet"--token="$token" > /dev/null ca_crt="$(mktemp)"; echo "$ca_crt_data" > $ca_crt oc config set-cluster $cluster--server="$intapi"--certificate-authority="$ca_crt"--embed-certs > /dev/null oc config set-context kubelet--cluster="$cluster"--user="kubelet" > /dev/null oc config use-context kubelet > /dev/null cat "$KUBECONFIG" ~~~ 4. Run the script to get a new bootstrap node certificate: ~~~ $ chmod 755 recover_kubeconfig.sh $./recover_kubeconfig.sh > kubeconfig-bootstrap ~~~ 5. SSH into the affected node, stop the `kubelet` service, and backup old node certificates: ~~~ # systemctl stop kubelet # mkdir-p /root/backup-certs # cp-a /var/lib/kubelet/pki /var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig /root/backup-certs # rm-rf /var/lib/kubelet/pki /var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig ~~~ 6. Copy the generated `kubeconfig-bootstrap` to `/etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig`: ~~~ # cp /etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig ~~~ 7. Start the `kubelet` service again: ~~~ # systemctl start kubelet ~~~ 8. Back in the bastion host, wait a few seconds, check the certificate requests and approve the node bootstrap: ~~~ $ oc get csr NAME AGE REQUESTOR CONDITION csr-jsv6z 11s system:serviceaccount:openshift-machine-config-operator:node-bootstrapper Pending $ oc adm certificate approve csr-jsv6z certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/csr-jsv6z approved ~~~ Wait a few more minutes and approve the new node certificate: ~~~ $ oc get csr NAME AGE REQUESTOR CONDITION csr-jsv6z 75s system:serviceaccount:openshift-machine-config-operator:node-bootstrapper Approved,Issued csr-smqlc 40s system:node:compute-1 Pending $ oc adm certificate approve csr-smqlc certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/csr-smqlc approved ~~~ After this, the node should go back into `Ready` state.

title: Why RHACS needs to run with privileged container escalation
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Compliance policy is getting violated as Kubernetes clusters should not allow container privilege escalation.- Why is container privilege required for RHACS secured-cluster-services to run.
root_cause: - The collector daemonset which leverages eBPF or CORE BPF requires elevated privileges on the nodes in order to bring in syscalls for process’s and network flows.- It’s configured for read only access to the node file system themselves.- Sensor also has some elevated RBAC privileges in the control plane itself because it pulls information from the Kube API and also handles enforcement of policies for things like deploy time (admission controller) and runtime.- The sensor container does not run in privileged mode, but it may come up with rbac permissions needed and why they are required.

title: Subscription Consumption Check Unavailable in Disconnected OpenShift Environment
issue: - Establish infrastructure nodes by labeling 3 worker nodes with node-role.kubernetes.io/infra="" (preserves worker role). Subsequently, deploy OpenShift components exclusively on these nodes using node selectors. This process requires verification to determine if a separate subscription is necessary for the newly created infrastructure nodes.
resolution: - However, running custom workloads on them is permitted with restrictions. Refer to documentation [1] for details on customized workloads on infrastructure nodes.- [1] Pasting the section for visibility: The following infrastructure workloads do not incur OpenShift Container Platform worker subscriptions: ======================================================================================================- Kubernetes and OpenShift Container Platform control plane services that run on masters- The default router- The integrated container image registry- The cluster metrics collection, or monitoring service, including components for monitoring user-defined projects- Cluster aggregated logging- Service brokers- Red Hat Quay- Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage- Red Hat Advanced Cluster Manager **NOTE:** Any node that runs any other container, pod, or component is a worker node that your subscription must cover.

title: Mask ConsoleLink with the help of RBAC
issue: - Can we manage manage Console link visibility with specific role?
resolution: - It is not possible to configure the visibility of console link with respect to role.
root_cause: - The visibility depends upon 2 facts like of cluster-admin role and other then cluster-admin role.- Cluster-admin role has full accessibility of the console and they can view everything.- If the user has no cluster-admin role then it will be not visible.

title: cluster autoscaler is spinning up nodes for Pending Pods which have taints preventing scheduling
issue: - When a MachineAutoscaler references a currently-zero-Machine MachineSet that includes spec.template.spec.taints, the autoscaler fails to deserialize that MachineSet, which causes it to fail to autoscale that MachineSet. The autoscaler's deserialization logic should be improved to avoid failing on the presence of taints.

title: OpenShift Virtualization (OCP-V) support in clusters with mixed Virtual Machines control planes and Bare Metal worker nodes
issue: - Is Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization (OCP-V, former CNV) supported in clusters with mixed Virtual Machines control planes and Bare Metal worker `nodes`?
resolution: - Running OpenShift Virtualization on a cluster with a mix of VMs and bare metal `nodes` is supported using UPI installation method.- Nested Virtualization is not supported (as of v4.15). Therefore, bare metal worker `nodes` are required in a supported environment.

title: Modifying the Nutanix configuration in RHOCP 4
issue: - Update the existing Nutanix credentials post installation
resolution: For an existing OCP cluster, if the Prism Central admin user login credentials changed, it is required to make these changes in the OCP cluster: 1) Before making any changes, be sure to backup the current configuration. ~~~ $ oc get secret nutanix-credentials-n openshift-machine-api > creds_machine_api.yaml $ oc get secret nutanix-credentials-n openshift-cloud-controller-manager > creds_cloud_controller.yaml ~~~ 2) Edit or Patch the secret named "nutanix-credentials” in the namespace “openshift-machine-api”, replacing the “stringData” data with: ~~~ oc edit secret nutanix-credentials-n openshift-machine-api ~~~ ~~~ stringData: credentials: | [{"type":"basic_auth","data":{"prismCentral": {"username":"PRISMCENTRAL_USERNAME","password":"PRISMCENTRAL_PASSWORD"},"prismElements":null}}] ~~~ 3) Edit or Patch the secret named "nutanix-credentials” in the namespace “openshift-cloud-controller-manager”, replacing the “stringData” data with: ~~~ oc edit secret nutanix-credentials-n openshift-cloud-controller-manager ~~~ ~~~ stringData: credentials: | [{"type":"basic_auth","data":{"prismCentral": {"username":"PRISMCENTRAL_USERNAME","password":"PRISMCENTRAL_PASSWORD"},"prismElements":null}}] ~~~ 4) If nutanix CSI driver has been deployed in the cluster and the Prism Element (PE) user credentials is changed, the corresponding secret that is used by the Nutanix StorageClass resource also need to update. Patch the secret in the namespace “openshift-cluster-csi-drivers”, replacing its “stringData” with: ~~~ stringData: key: PRISMELEMENT_ADDRESS:PRISMELEMENT_PORT:PRISMELEMENT_USERNAME:PRISMELEMENT_PASSWORD ~~~ In the above, use the actual data for the PRISMCENTRAL_USERNAME, PRISMCENTRAL_PASSWORD, PRISMELEMENT_ADDRESS, PRISMELEMENT_PORT, PRISMELEMENT_USERNAME, PRISMELEMENT_PASSWORD.

title: How to disable cephcluster read-affinity in ODF 4.13 and 4.14
issue: In ODF 4.13, read-affinity was enabled for the cephcluster: https://github.com/red-hat-storage/ocs-operator/pull/1939/commits/795a3b287a4e1c7425b36d35bb4aa81f30fc880d ~~~ Enable Read affinity for RBD and CephFS volumes¶ Ceph CSI supports mapping RBD volumes with KRBD options and mounting CephFS volumes with ceph mount options to allow serving reads from an OSD closest to the client, according to OSD locations defined in the CRUSH map and topology labels on nodes. ~~~ This is, in general, a positive feature and is enabled by default for storageclusters with internal storage. There are circumstances under which it is useful to be able to disable this behavior though. This is only for 4.13 and 4.14, as ODF 4.15 adds the ability to set this value per cephcluster in a more standard manner.
resolution: To disable this feature, please patch the 'rook-ceph-operator-config' configmap in the (default) openshift-storage namespace: ~~~ oc patch cm rook-ceph-operator-config--type merge-p '{"data":{"CSI_ENABLE_READ_AFFINITY":"false"}}'-n openshift-storage ~~~ This will trigger a redeploy of the csi-rbdplugin-* pods without the '--read-affinity=true' option removed.
root_cause: The feature was added in 4.13 with the commit noted earlier, but not an obvious way to disable it, if desired.

title: Openshift Pipelines operator upgrade stuck due to discontinued "config.operator.tekton.dev" CustomResource
issue: - Operator upgrade gets stuck with message `Components not in ready state: TektonPipeline: reconcile again and proceed`- `tektonconfig` resource not moving to state_Ready_
resolution: 1. Create a backup of your tekton resources ~~~ $ mkdir openshift-pipelines-tekton-bkp && \ cd openshift-pipelines-tekton-bkp $ oc get crd | grep tekton | grep-v operator | awk '{print $1}' | xargs-I {} bash-c "oc get {}-A-o json | tee {}.json" ~~~ 2. Generate a pipeline must-gather as additional backup ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--image quay.io/openshift-pipeline/must-gather ~~~ **Attention: This procedure will remove all tekton resources; save a backup using the above commands before continuing** 3. Delete the `config.operator.tekton.dev`_CustomResourceDefinition_. It will also delete the related `config`_CustomResource_ object ~~~ $ oc delete crd config.operator.tekton.dev ~~~ 4. Delete the `config`_CustomResource_ object of kind `tektonconfig` ~~~ $ oc delete tektonconfig config ~~~ 5. Delete the operator pod ~~~ $ oc delete pod--selector="app=openshift-pipelines-operator" \--namespace openshift-operators ~~~ 6. Check if the `config`_CustomResource_ object of kind `tektonconfig` has been created again ~~~ $ oc get tektonconfig config ~~~ 7. Check if the `tektoninstallerset` object has all required resources_Ready_ ~~~ $ oc get tektoninstallerset NAME READY REASON addon-clustertasks-xxx True addon-communityclustertasks-xxx True addon-consolecli-xxx True addon-openshift-xxx True addon-pac-xxx True addon-pipelines-xxx True addon-triggers-xxx True addon-versioned-clustertasks-1-8-xxx True pipeline-xxx True postpipeline-xxx True prepipeline-xxx True rhosp-rbac-xxx True trigger-xxx True validating-mutating-webhoook-xxx True ~~~ 8. Restore the backed up resources using `oc apply-f {file}` for each file generated in step one. They can be applied in any order, but it will resolve more quickly if triggers and other resources are created before tasks and then create pipelines last. Pipeline Runs typically don't need to be recreated. 9. If the restoration of the resources results in an error about an api, such as `Task`, not existing, then open a support case. Alternately, you can attempt to [uninstall and reinstall the operator](https://docs.openshift.com/pipelines/1.14/install_config/uninstalling-pipelines.html), but this process can take time to because of the necessity of removing all custom resources by hand, and it will require things like relinking secrets for pull and reapplying permissions to any service accounts that get deleted and recreated in the process.
root_cause: In the_Tech Preview_ versions of the OpenShift Pipelines operator, the Tekton objects were created accordingly to the object `config` of kind `config.operator.tekton.dev`. With the_General Availability_ versions, the `config.operator.tekton.dev`_CustomResourceDefinition_ has been discontinued in favor of `tektonconfig.operator.tekton.dev`. When the upgrade is performed from_Tech Preview_ of Openshift Pipelines to_General Availability_ versions, the upgrade from the object `config` of kind `config.operator.tekton.dev` to `config` of kind `tektonconfig.operator.tekton.dev` might get stuck. This problem can also occur if doing too far a jump in an upgrade. It's best to upgrade operators one version at a time rather than skipping ahead.

title: How to identify the credential that the ARO is actually using?
issue: - How to identify the credential that the ARO is actually using after update the service principals shown as below: ~~~ $ az ad app credential list--id $SP_ID--query "[].endDateTime"-o tsv 2025-11-07T05:17:23.XXXXXXXZ 2025-11-07T02:17:13.XXXXXXXZ ~~~
resolution: - **Step 1**. Check the `keyId`. ~~~ $ az ad app credential list--id $SP_ID [{"customKeyIdentifier": null, "displayName": null, "endDateTime": "2025-11-02T03:02:10.4966144Z", "hint": "syC", "keyId": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", < <---THIS "secretText": null, "startDateTime": "2023-11-02T03:02:10.4966144Z"}] ~~~- **Step 2**. Export the `azure-credentials`.(This require kubeadmin access) ~~~ $ oc extract secret/azure-credentials-n kube-system azure_region azure_resource_prefix azure_resourcegroup azure_subscription_id azure_tenant_id azure_client_id azure_client_secret ~~~- **Step 3**. Check the content of `azure_client_id`. ~~~ $ cat azure_client_id xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx ~~~- **Step 4**. Filter the `App registrations` with above `azure_client_id` in Azure Portal. If the `Secret ID` in corresponding App registration is the same as the `keyId` shown in Step 1, we could identify this is the credential cluster is using.
root_cause: - In general, *service principals must be unique per Azure RedHat OpenShift (ARO) Cluster* based on [this ARO documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-create-service-principal?pivots=aro-azurecli#create-a-service-principal-and-assign-role-based-access-control-rbac---azure-cli). However, when we run the command below to update the service principal: ~~~ $ az aro update--refresh-credentials--name MyManagedCluster--resource-group MyResourceGroup ~~~- This will generate additional credential as follows which is expected behavior. ~~~ $ az ad app credential list--id $SP_ID--query "[].endDateTime"-o tsv 2025-11-07T05:17:23.XXXXXXXZ < <---THIS 2025-11-07T02:17:13.XXXXXXXZ ~~~

title: Is On-demand Capacity Reservation possible in ARO?
issue: - Is [On-demand Capacity Reservation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/capacity-reservation-overview) possible in ARO?
resolution: - `On-demand Capacity Reservation` is not applicable for Azure Red Hat OpenShift currently. Since it would hit the `deny assignment` which is against with [Azure Red Hat OpenShift 4.0 support policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/support-policies-v4#cluster-management) shown as below: ~~~ Don't circumvent the deny assignment that is configured as part of the service, or perform administrative tasks normally prohibited by the deny assignment. ~~~- We plan to raise an RFE(Request for Enhancement) for this, but we don't have an ETA date as yet.

title: Newly created pods in service mesh fails with error "No networks found in /etc/cni/multus/net.d"
issue: The newly created pods in service mesh fails with error "No networks found in /etc/cni/multus/net.d" when `Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes` is configured for cluster.
resolution: - To fix this issue it is required to check `istio-operator pod` logs ~~~ $ oc logs istio-operator-6d87fc6c68-2qjss-n openshift-operators output: internal error occurred: admission plugin "ValidatingAdmissionWebhook" failed to complete validation in 13s ~~~- If there's any **third party operator or Community operator** webhook is causing issue then it is required to remove or disable the operator and then update the `Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh` operator.- If operator version is old and `SMCP` version should be supported and latest version.- After that restarting the failing pods would fix the issue: ~~~ $ oc delete pod ~~~- If the issue is still not resolved please open [support ticket](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/get-support?caseCreate=true).
root_cause: The newly created pods in service mesh fails with error "No networks found in /etc/cni/multus/net.d" when `Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes` is configured for cluster because of `istio-cni` daemonset not present as well as ongoing issue with `Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes` or any **third party operator or Community operator** webhook is causing issue.

title: Route throws 200 OK response in case of pass-through and re-encrypt route but 502 bad gateway for Edge route
issue: When doing curl request to an application route it throws 200 OK response in case of `Passthrough` and `Re-encrypt` route but 502 bad gateway for `Edge` route
resolution: - If application expects the traffic internally in cluster to be encrypted it is required to create `Passthrough` or `Reencrypt` route for such scenarios.- **In the`Edge` route** the `Ingress Controller` sets up an `ingress` pod to terminate `TLS` encryption before forwarding traffic to the destination pod. The route specifies the TLS certificate and key that the `ingress` pod uses for the route. The default certificate is used if the user does not explicitly provide the certificate and the TLS termination occurs at the router.- **In the`Passthrough` route** the pass-through termination is done by sending encrypted traffic straight to the destination without the router providing TLS termination and the destination pod serves certificates for the traffic at the endpoint, as such the connection's full path is encrypted.- **In the`Reencrypt` route** the traffic with TLS encryption is initially terminated at the `Ingress Controller` then the Ingress Controller decrypts the TLS-encrypted traffic. After the initial termination, the Ingress Controller re-encrypts the traffic and the re-encryption ensures end-to-end encryption, as the traffic is secured between the Ingress Controller and the backend service.
root_cause: This issue happens due to application expecting `encrypted` traffic inside the cluster as well and due to which the application requires `Passthrough` and `Reencrypt` route for encrypted traffic

title: package-server-manager pod creation is failing with PodSecurity errors in RHOCP4
issue: - package-server-manager pod creation is failing with PodSecurity error.- Observing error in deployment yaml: ~~~ deployment openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager/package-server-manager has a replica failure FailedCreate: pods "package-server-manager-xxx" is forbidden: violates PodSecurity "restricted:v1.24": unrestricted capabilities (container "package-server-manager" must not include "CHOWN", "DAC_OVERRIDE", "FOWNER" in securityContext.capabilities.add) ~~~
resolution: - Check deployment yaml for the service account: ~~~ securityContext:... serviceAccount: ~~~- Check which SCC have these securityContext.capabilities: "CHOWN", "DAC_OVERRIDE", "FOWNER": ~~~ $ oc get scc-o yaml | grep-i CHOWN $ oc get scc-o yaml | grep-i DAC_OVERRIDE $ oc get scc-o yaml | grep-i FOWNER ~~~- Confirm if the same SCC added to the service account the pod should run with: ~~~ $ oc adm policy who-can use scc ~~~- Remove the SCC from serviceaccount: ~~~ $ oc adm policy remove-scc-from-user-z ~~~- If this doesn't resolve the issue, try deleting the SCC: ~~~ $ oc delete scc ~~~- In few cases the SCC is managed by operator and the operator recreates the SCC as soon as it is deleted.- In such case, uninstall the operator from OperatorHub.
root_cause: - If serviceaccount have the SCC assigned where the SCC have some capabilities which should not be there, then the SCC prevents pods to be created.

title: How to Enable Groups Claim on Azure Active Directory for OpenID Connect
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Enable the `groups claim` on Azure Active Directory for use with Openshift OAuth OIDC provider.
resolution: **Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. 1. **Sign in to the Azure portal** Navigate to and sign in with your Azure account credentials. 2. **Navigate to Azure Active Directory** From the left-hand menu, select "Azure Active Directory". 3. **Select App registrations** Within the Azure Active Directory page, select "App registrations" from the menu. 4. **Select the relevant application** From the list of applications, select the application for which you want to enable the groups claim. 5. **Open Token Configuration** From the left-hand menu of the application page, select "Token configuration". 6. **Add groups claim** Click on the "+ Add groups claim" button. 7. **Configure groups claim** In the "Add groups claim" page:- Select the types of groups (security groups, distribution lists, etc.) you want to include in the groups claim.- Select the ID type (group ID or group name).- Select the source (user’s groups or groups assigned to the application).- Configure any advanced settings as required. 8. **Save the changes** Click on "Add" to save the changes. 9. **Create AAD client secret** ``` # create AAD client secret oc create secret generic aad-secret--from-literal=clientSecret=zCS8Q~qS8.xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxB6l5DOfcw.-n openshift-config ``` 10. **Configure Oauth OIDC on Openshift with groups claim**, e.g.: ``` apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: OAuth metadata: name: cluster spec: identityProviders:- name: HTPasswd mappingMethod: claim type: HTPasswd htpasswd: fileData: name: htpass-secret- name: AAD mappingMethod: claim type: OpenID openID: clientID: 171169eb-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-d36c6c6824d8 clientSecret: name: aad-secret extraScopes:- email- profile claims: preferredUsername:- preferred_username name:- name email:- email groups:- groups issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/64dc69e4-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-ebece1dd1408/v2.0 ``` [image=[src="images/aad-groups-claim.png", alt="AAD-Groups-Claim", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] ### The supported formats for group claims are:- **Microsoft Entra group ObjectId**: Available for all groups.- **sAMAccountName**: Available for groups synchronized from Active Directory.- **NetbiosDomain\sAMAccountName**: Available for groups synchronized from Active Directory.- **DNSDomainName\sAMAccountName**: Available for groups synchronized from Active Directory.- **On-premises group security identifier**: Available for groups synchronized from Active Directory. > **Note**: `sAMAccountName` and on-premises `GroupSID` attributes are available only on group objects synced from Active Directory. They aren’t available on groups created in Microsoft Entra ID or Office 365. Applications configured in Microsoft Entra ID to get synced on-premises group attributes get them for synced groups only. For more details, check Microsoft Document: [Configure group claims for applications by using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-fed-group-claims#important-caveats-for-this-functionality)
root_cause: By default, Azure Active Directory does not include the groups claim in tokens for OpenID Connect. This can limit the information available for authorization decisions.

title: All Node Machines are in Failed Phase in RHOCP 4
issue: - All machines are in failed state: ~~~ message: Instance not found on provider reason: InstanceMissing severity: Warning status: 'False' type: InstanceExists errorMessage: Can't find created instance. ~~~- Machine-controller container shows below error while reconciling machine: ~~~ 2024-03-05T17:31:16.057088477Z E0305 17:31:16.057052 1 controller.go:297] test-worker-0-xxxx: failed to check if machine exists: Failed to authenticate provider client: Authentication failed 2024-03-05T17:31:16.067470298Z E0305 17:31:16.067429 1 controller.go:329] "msg"="Reconciler error" "error"="Failed to authenticate provider client: Authentication failed" "controller"="machine-controller" "name"="test-worker-0-xxxx" "namespace"="openshift-machine-api" "object"={"name":"test-worker-0 xxxx","namespace":"openshift-machine-api"} "reconcileID"="002ba561-5edb-485d-9fd3-53f1db1ee407" 2024-03-05T17:31:16.067570420Z I0305 17:31:16.067509 1 controller.go:187] test-worker-1-xxxx: reconciling Machine 2024-03-05T17:31:16.073498818Z I0305 17:31:16.073472 1 utils.go:111] Cloud provider CA cert not provided, using system trust bundle 2024-03-05T17:31:16.111622576Z E0305 17:31:16.111521 1 controller.go:297] test-worker-1-xxxx: failed to check if machine exists: Failed to authenticate provider client: Authentication failed ~~~
resolution: - Check the `credentials` for `secret` inside `kube-system openstack-credentials` namespace: ~~~ $ oc get secret-n kube-system openstack-credentials NAME TYPE DATA AGE openstack-credentials Opaque 2 1d $ oc get secret-n kube-system openstack-credentials-o yaml | yq '.data' {"clouds.conf": "MjUzIGJ5dGVzIGxvbmc=", "clouds.yaml": "MzYxIGJ5dGVzIGxvbmc="} ~~~- Update the `credentials` within the `openshift-machine-api` namespace, as the controller won't initiate reconciliation due to hardcoding: ~~~ $ oc get secret openstack-cloud-credentials-n openshift-machine-api` NAME TYPE DATA AGE openstack-cloud-credentials Opaque 1 48d $ oc get secret openstack-cloud-credentials-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml | yq '.data' {"clouds.yaml": "MzYxIGJ5dGVzIGxvbmc="} **Note:** Ensure that the `credentials` within the `openshift-machine-api` namespace match those present in the `secret` mentioned above.
root_cause: - If the credentials used by the Machine-API controllers to authenticate with OpenStack are not updated or are incorrect, it can lead to failures when attempting to retrieve the status of machines managed by the controllers. Controller will not perform reconciliation as its hardcoded and hence secrets or cloud credentials inside `openshift-machine-api` namespace also needs to be updated so that cluster can access the backend storage for the registry.

title: [AMQ Streams] Zookeeper Pod is in CrashLoopBackOff with an ERROR Unable to load database on disk
issue: - Zookeeper Pod is in `CrashLoopBackOff` status with the following error: INFO Snapshot loaded in 35 ms, highest zxid is 0xd2100000004, digest is 845877382883 (org.apache.zookeeper.server.ZKDatabase) [main] ERROR Unable to load database on disk (org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeer) [main] java.io.IOException: The current epoch, d20, is older than the last zxid, 14435385081860 at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeer.loadDataBase(QuorumPeer.java:1123) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeer.start(QuorumPeer.java:1079) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain.runFromConfig(QuorumPeerMain.java:227) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain.initializeAndRun(QuorumPeerMain.java:136) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain.main(QuorumPeerMain.java:90) ERROR Unexpected exception, exiting abnormally (org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain) [main] java.lang.RuntimeException: Unable to run quorum server at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeer.loadDataBase(QuorumPeer.java:1149) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeer.start(QuorumPeer.java:1079) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain.runFromConfig(QuorumPeerMain.java:227) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain.initializeAndRun(QuorumPeerMain.java:136) at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeerMain.main(QuorumPeerMain.java:90) Caused by: java.io.IOException: The current epoch, d20, is older than the last zxid, 14435385081860 at org.apache.zookeeper.server.quorum.QuorumPeer.loadDataBase(QuorumPeer.java:1123)... 4 more
resolution: Once `Zookeeper` is not be able to read its database and encounters `IOException` due to file corruption in the `transaction logs`, it will fail to start with a `CrashLoopBackOff` in the status. In such a case, it is important to verify the status and health of all other `ZooKeeper pods` within the ensemble. Then, proceed with the process of cleaning the corrupted server's database. For instance: # oc get pod | grep zookeeper my-cluster-zookeeper-0 1/1 Running 1 31m my-cluster-zookeeper-1 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 10 (3m30s ago) 32m my-cluster-zookeeper-2 1/1 Running 4 (18m ago) 31m Run the following command for the Zookeeper pod in `CrashLoopBackOff` status: oc debug my-cluster-zookeeper-1 By running the above command, it will create a pod and the shell (TTY) of that pod will be prompted: `my-cluster-zookeeper-1-debug `. The Data volume of the pod `my-cluster-zookeeper-1` will be mounted automatically in the new debug pod. Backup the data `/var/lib/zookeeper/data` and rename `version-2`: mv /var/lib/zookeeper/data/version-2 /var/lib/zookeeper/data/old-version-2 Run `exit` command in the shell of the debug pod. The next restart of the Zookeeper pod `my-cluster-zookeeper-1 `, it will trigger the sync with other nodes of the zookeeper ensemble and it will start successfully. **NOTE:** Once the Zookeeper ensemble is recovered after applying the above procedure, please think to move/delete the folder `old-version-2` (`/var/lib/zookeeper/data/old-version-2`) from the zookeeper data. **NOTE:** The above resolution is **ONLY** applicable if only for **ONE ZK** pod is failing with that error. The two other ZK pods **MUST** be **UP** and **Running**.

title: Configure  GitOps operator to run on the infrastructure nodes in RHOCP4
issue: How to move the `Gitops` operator from the master node to the infrastructure nodes?
resolution: - The default `Argo CD` instance installed by the OpenShift `GitOps` operator as well as accompanying controllers can now be made to run on the cluster's infrastructure nodes by setting a simple configuration parameter.- To do this, the following steps should be taken:- Label the existing nodes as infrastructure using the following command: ~~~ $ oc label node node-role.kubernetes.io/infra="" ~~~- To isolate the workload scheduled on the infrastructure node, following taints can be applied: ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/infra infra=reserved:NoSchedule infra=reserved:NoExecute` ~~~- Add `runOnInfra` parameter in the GitOpsService custom resource(CR) by running the following command: ~~~ $ oc edit gitopsservice-n openshift-gitops` and adding `runOnInfra: true` to the `Spec` field: apiVersion: pipelines.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: GitopsService metadata: name: cluster spec: runOnInfra: true ~~~- Add tolerations to the GitOpsService custom resource(CR) if taints have been added to the nodes.- For example: ~~~ spec: runOnInfra: true tolerations:- effect: NoSchedule key: infra value: reserved- effect: NoExecute key: infra value: reserved ~~~

title: How to leverage ignition config overrides and extraManifests to separate partitions for /var/lib/containers
resolution:
**How to leverage ignition config overrides and extraManifests to separate partitions for /var/lib/containers** Nobody likes downtime! The need to lower the OpenShift (OCP) installation and upgrade times has led to some drastic changes in how the base operating system (OS) is being deployed. The [Lifecycle Agent](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7057298) provides functionality to address these concerns. Traditionally, the installation of Red Hat Core OS (RHCOS) has had a partition scheme resembling the following layout. This process is based on the following [documentation here.](https://github.com/openshift-kni/cnf-features-deploy/blob/master/ztp/gitops-subscriptions/argocd/DiskPartiitionContainers.md) ~~~ $ lsblk-f NAME MAJ:MIN RM SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINTS nvme0n1 259:1 0 1.8T 0 disk ├─nvme0n1p1 259:28 0 1M 0 part ├─nvme0n1p2 259:33 0 127M 0 part ├─nvme0n1p3 259:34 0 384M 0 part /boot └─nvme0n1p4 259:35 0 1.8T 0 part /var /sysroot/ostree/deploy/rhcos/var /usr /etc / /sysroot ~~~ In this container platform’s OS, there are two mount points that are of importance. The first is the location of ETCD, OpenShift’s API database: /var/lib/etcd. The second is the basis for this KCS article’s creation: /var/lib/containers (containers). **Using Butane to create the disk configurations** Butane is a tool to convert a butane config file into an ignition one. There is more information listed [here.](https://coreos.github.io/butane/getting-started/) First, create an alias to run the butane container. Next, take an example butane configuration file that uses a shared /sysroot partition or an entirely separate disk. ~~~ $ alias butane='podman run--rm--interactive--security-opt label=disable--volume "${PWD}":/pwd--workdir /pwd quay.io/coreos/butane:release' # Single Disk Configuration variant: fcos version: 1.4.0 storage: disks:- device: /dev/nvme0n1 wipe_table: true partitions:- number: 1 size_mib: 1- number: 2 size_mib: 127- number: 3 size_mib: 384- number: 4 size_mib: 309600- number: 5 label: containers filesystems:- device: /dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers format: xfs wipe_filesystem: true with_mount_unit: true path: /var/lib/containers $ butane single-disk.bu | jq. {"ignition": {"version": "3.3.0"}, "storage": {"disks": [{"device": "/dev/nvme0n1", "partitions": [{"number": 1, "sizeMiB": 1}, {"number": 2, "sizeMiB": 127}, {"number": 3, "sizeMiB": 384}, {"number": 4, "sizeMiB": 309600}, {"label": "containers", "number": 5}], "wipeTable": true}], "filesystems": [{"device": "/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers", "format": "xfs", "path": "/var/lib/containers", "wipeFilesystem": true}]}, "systemd": {"units": [{"contents": "# Generated by Butane
[Unit]
Requires=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-containers.service
After=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-containers.service

[Mount]
Where=/var/lib/containers
What=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers
Type=xfs

[Install]
RequiredBy=local-fs.target", "enabled": true, "name": "var-lib-containers.mount"}]}} ~~~ **Multiple Disk Configuration** The following example highlights the usage of multiple disks. ~~~ $ alias butane='podman run--rm--interactive--security-opt label=disable--volume "${PWD}":/pwd--workdir /pwd quay.io/coreos/butane:release' variant: fcos version: 1.4.0 storage: disks:- device: /dev/nvme1n1 wipe_table: true partitions:- number: 1 size_mib: 102400- number: 2 size_mib: 102400- number: 3 label: containers filesystems:- device: /dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers format: xfs wipe_filesystem: true with_mount_unit: true path: /var/lib/containers $ butane multi-disk.bu | jq. {"ignition": {"version": "3.3.0"}, "storage": {"disks": [{"device": "/dev/nvme1n1", "partitions": [{"number": 1, "sizeMiB": 102400}, {"number": 2, "sizeMiB": 102400}, {"label": "containers", "number": 3}], "wipeTable": true}], "filesystems": [{"device": "/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers", "format": "xfs", "path": "/var/lib/containers", "wipeFilesystem": true}]}, "systemd": {"units": [{"contents": "# Generated by Butane
[Unit]
Requires=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-containers.service
After=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-containers.service

[Mount]
Where=/var/lib/containers
What=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers
Type=xfs

[Install]
RequiredBy=local-fs.target", "enabled": true, "name": "var-lib-containers.mount"}]}} ~~~ **Applying the ignition configuration using ZTP using ignitionConfigOverride** The appropriate ignition configuration can be applied via an ignitionConfig override utilizing the site-config CR of an OpenShift deployment. This is converted to an annotation for the baremetal host CR. ~~~ $ cat zt-sno1.yaml..omitted.. nodes:- hostName: "zt-sno1.inbound.vz.bos2.lab" cpuset: "0-1,32-33" ignitionConfigOverride: '{"ignition":{"version":"3.2.0"},"storage":{"disks":[{"device":"/dev/nvme0n1","partitions":[{"number":1,"sizeMiB":1},{"number":2,"sizeMiB":127},{"number":3,"sizeMiB":384},{"number":4,"sizeMiB":309600},{"label":"containers","number":5}],"wipeTable":true}],"filesystems":[{"device":"/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers","format":"xfs","path":"/var/lib/containers","wipeFilesystem":true}]},"systemd":{"units":[{"contents":"# Generated by Butane
[Unit]
Requires=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-containers.service
After=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-containers.service

[Mount]
Where=/var/lib/containers
What=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers
Type=xfs

[Install]
RequiredBy=local-fs.target","enabled":true,"name":"var-lib-containers.mount"}]}}' ~~~ **Applying the ignition configuration using ZTP using extraManifests** Additionally, the ztp extraManifests can be used to apply machineConfig CRs during the cluster installation. Butane can be used to generate these files as well. ~~~ # storage-mc.bu variant: openshift version: 4.13.0 metadata: name: 98-var-lib-containers-partitioned labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master spec:... # same as original fcos variant ~~~ This file can be placed inside the extraManifests directory in the [site-config.](https://github.com/openshift-kni/cnf-features-deploy/blob/4930a645692a1a2de228e34c46738dc9944b4b84/ztp/gitops-subscriptions/argocd/example/siteconfig/example-sno.yaml#L28) ~~~ # Generated by Butane; do not edit apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master name: 98-var-lib-containers-partitioned spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage:..omitted....omitted.. networkType: "OVNKubernetes" additionalNTPSources:- clock.corp.redhat.com installConfigOverrides: "{"capabilities":{"baselineCapabilitySet": "None", "additionalEnabledCapabilities": ["OperatorLifecycleManager", "NodeTuning"]}}" extraManifestPath: zt-sno1/extra-manifests holdInstallation: false..omitted..-> tree. ├── extra-manifests │ ├── 05-proxy-cluster.yaml │ ├── 05-trusted-updateservice-ca.yaml │ ├── 98-var-lib-containers-partitioned.yaml │ └── enable-crun-master.yaml ├── zt-sno1-dualstack.yaml ├── zt-sno1-ipv4.yaml ├── zt-sno1-ipv6.yaml └── zt-sno1-secrets.yaml ~~~ **Verifying the configurations have been applied successfully** Now, verify the annotation has been applied to the baremetal host that belongs to the clusterdeployment and verify inside the cluster node. ~~~ $ oc-n zt-sno1 get bmh-ojson | jq '.items[].metadata.annotations["bmac.agent-install.openshift.io/ignition-config-overrides"]' "{"ignition":{"version":"3.2.0"},"storage":{"disks":[{"device":"/dev/nvme0n1","partitions":[{"number":1,"sizeMiB":1},{"number":2,"sizeMiB":127},{"number":3,"sizeMiB":384},{"number":4,"sizeMiB":309600},{"label":"containers","number":5}],"wipeTable":true}],"filesystems":[{"device":"/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers","format":"xfs","path":"/var/lib/containers","wipeFilesystem":true}]},"systemd":{"units":[{"contents":"# Generated by Butane\n[Unit]\nRequires=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\\x2dpartlabel-containers.service\nAfter=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\\x2dpartlabel-containers.service\n\n[Mount]\nWhere=/var/lib/containers\nWhat=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/containers\nType=xfs\n\n[Install]\nRequiredBy=local-fs.target","enabled":true,"name":"var-lib-containers.mount"}]}}" # After accessing the SNO node # lsblk-f NAME FSTYPE FSVER LABEL UUID FSAVAIL FSUSE% MOUNTPOINTS nvme0n1 ├─nvme0n1p1 ├─nvme0n1p2 vfat FAT16 EFI-SYSTEM 2235-17EA ├─nvme0n1p3 ext4 1.0 boot 217b28ca-6dcf-4db2-9abc-91a82f0b18b9 217M 31% /boot ├─nvme0n1p4 xfs root dc0f4558-8fee-412d-a92c-00179d65eed7 282.9G 6% /var │ /sysroot/ostree/deploy/rhcos/var │ /usr │ /etc │ / │ /sysroot └─nvme0n1p5 xfs 8c3d4a11-7698-45e3-af0f-fe8e135ca782 1.5T 2% /var/lib/containers nvme1n1 ~~~ **Conclusions** This concludes the article on disk partitioning using ignition and butane. This process could be applied to any number of partitions or labels inside the operating system. Other [OpenShift Docs](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7057298) cover the next step in the process covering [/var/lib/etcd](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/scalability_and_performance/recommended-performance-scale-practices/recommended-etcd-practices.html#move-etcd-different-disk_recommended-etcd-practices) and [/var/lib/containers.](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7057298#sharing-the-container-directory-between-ostree-stateroots-9) This later link discusses using a shared containers directory between two image-based installations and talks about performing an upgrade with the image-based upgrade (IBU) process. This concludes this solutions article.

title: Using Secret Storage CSI Driver with On Prem cluster
issue: - Is there a way to use a Secret Storage CSI Driver in an On Prem cluster.
resolution: - At the time of creating this KCS, it is not supported by Red Hat.- There are plans to release a techpreview operator to deploy the Secret Store CSI driver in 4.14, so official support for this driver should improve in future releases.- Refer [OCPSTRAT-583](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPSTRAT-583) to track support for the CSI Driver for secrets store.

title: Mount failed with mount: mount.nfs: access denied by server while mounting using Dell PowerShare storage
issue: - Getting issue while mounting the volume inside the pods: ~~~ MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "pvc-0000-0000": mount failed: exit status 32 Mounting command....Output: mount.nfs: access denied by server while mounting ~~~
resolution: Select the "Allow mount sub-directories" tick box. This will allow the pods to mount the volume.
root_cause: "Allow mount sub-directories" tick box was not selected. Due to which StorageClass could create the folder but the pod couldn't mount it as it wasn't permitted to.

title: Cluster operator monitoring unavailable and degraded with prometheus-k8s pods unable to start
issue: - monitoring cluster operator is unavailable, progressing, and degraded and prometheus-k8s-0 / prometheus-k8s-1 in the openshift-monitoring namespace will not start with the error message... ~~~ monitoring Cluster Operator error: Failed to rollout the stack. Error: updating prometheus-k8s: waiting for Prometheus object changes failed: waiting for Prometheus openshift-monitoring/k8s: expected 2 replicas, got 0 updated replicas ~~~- The prometheus-k8s-0 and prometheus-k8s-1 pod in the openshift-monitoring namespace will not start (pending or Init status) with the error messages... ~~~ Warning FailedMount pod/prometheus-k8s-0 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "secret-hub-alertmanager-router-ca": secret "hub-alertmanager-router-ca" not found Warning FailedMount pod/prometheus-k8s-0 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "secret-observability-alertmanager-accessor": secret "observability-alertmanager-accessor" not found Warning FailedMount pod/prometheus-k8s-0 (combined from similar events): Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[secret-observability-alertmanager-accessor secret-hub-alertmanager-router-ca], unattached volumes=[configmap-metrics-client-ca prometheus-k8s-db secret-kube-rbac-proxy secret-prometheus-k8s-tls prometheus-k8s-rulefiles-0 metrics-client-ca secret-prometheus-k8s-htpasswd secret-prometheus-k8s-proxy config config-out tls-assets web-config secret-grpc-tls secret-metrics-client-certs secret-observability-alertmanager-accessor secret-prometheus-k8s-thanos-sidecar-tls secret-hub-alertmanager-router-ca configmap-serving-certs-ca-bundle kube-api-access-8zf49 configmap-kubelet-serving-ca-bundle prometheus-trusted-ca-bundle secret-kube-etcd-client-certs]: timed out waiting for the condition. ~~~
resolution: 1. Make a backup of the cluster-monitoring-config configmap ~~~ $ oc get cm cluster-monitoring-config-o yaml-n openshift-monitoring > cluster-monitoring-config.yaml ~~~ 2. Then make a targeted precise edit of the cluster-monitoring-config configmap ~~~ $ oc edit cm cluster-monitoring-config-n openshift-monitoring ~~~ and delete the following section: ~~~ additionalAlertManagerConfigs:- apiVersion: v2 bearerToken: key: token name: observability-alertmanager-accessor pathPrefix: / scheme: https staticConfigs:- alertmanager-open-cluster-management-observability.apps.ocp4.example.com tlsConfig: ServerName: "" ca: key: service-ca.crt name: hub-alertmanager-router-ca insecureSkipVerify: false ~~~ 3. Confirm that the edits made were as intended via ~~~ $ oc get cm cluster-monitoring-config-o yaml-n openshift-monitoring > cluster-monitoring-config_new.yaml ~~~ 4. Force a restart of the two problematic pods. ~~~ $ oc delete pods prometheus-k8s-0 prometheus-k8s-1-n openshift-monitoring ~~~ 5. Confirm result via checking ~~~ $ oc get co monitoring Desired output should be NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE monitoring 4.x.xx True False False xxxd $ oc get pods-n openshift-monitoring | grep prometheus-k8s Desired output should be prometheus-k8s-0 6/6 Running 0 3h prometheus-k8s-1 6/6 Running 0 3h ~~~
root_cause: - The advanced cluster management observability operator (open-cluster-management-addon-observability) was previously installed and removed but the removal was incomplete and this is the resulting leftover cruft.- The prometheus-k8s-0 and prometheus-k8s-1 pods are attempting to access these secrets which are no longer present and as a result these two pods crucial to the monitoring cluster operator are not able to start.- This leaves the monitoring cluster operator in a unavailable, progressing, and degraded state.

title: HPE CSI driver attachment issues after cluster patch

resolution: Issues solved by HPE support team.
root_cause: The PVC with issues was created with an older storageclass config (hostSeesVLUN was false and is now true). This results in PVs not being exported properly, which makes it unable for the node to attach the storage to the po

title: Issues experienced: No OpenShift 4.14.x can finish installing in our environment
issue: OpenShift 4.14.x installations end up with all the worker nodes being marked as uninitialized and unschedulable- After installing with IPI the cluster the worker VMs don't have UUID configured
root_cause: It looks like OpenShift 4.14 (any minor version) ends up in this state when there are more than one network cards configured on the worker nodes. If there is more than one network card configured on the worker nodes when the platform is deployed then the platform deployment breaks. If any worker node is added after the platform is deployed with more than one network card configured then that worker node ends up in the state above (i.e. unusable).

title: How to collect Real-Time Logs from Ansible Automation Platform running on OpenShift?
issue: - Need to view real-time logs for monitoring and troubleshooting the Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) running on OpenShift.
resolution: - To view real-time logs in the Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) on the Operator, follow these steps: 1. Check if the Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) pod is running: ~~~ # oc get pods ~~~ 2. To view combined log messages, use the following command: ~~~ # oc logs pod/[POD_NAME]-f ~~~ 3. If you need logs for a specific container within the pod, use: ~~~ # oc logs pod/[POD_NAME]-c [CONTAINER_NAME]-f ~~~- The log messages will include information from various log files located at `/var/log/tower/*.log`.

title: Network traffic blocked by Network Policy are not detected by RHACS
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Network policy created in Red Hat Openshift Container Platform in specific namespaces to block attempts to connect to endpoints are not detected by RHACS.
resolution: - This feature is currently being worked upon by engineering team via RFE.
root_cause: - ACS does not see connection attempts that are blocked by NetworkPolicies yet because that happens in the CNI layer, lower than ACS currently operates.

title: How to find master leaders for Openshift control plane Operators
issue: Which node/pod is leader for kube-scheduler, ovn-kubernetes, kube-controller and/or kube-apiserver?
resolution: To list current elected leaders:- To find out the current `OVN-Kubernetes` master leader is, use this command ~~~ $ POD_NAME=$(oc get lease-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes--no-headers | awk '{print $2}') $ oc get pod-o wide-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes | grep $POD_NAME ovnkube-control-plane-xxxx 2/2 Running 0 5h3m xx.xx.xx.xx master-1 ~~~- To find out the current `kube-controller-manager` master leader is, use this command ~~~ $ oc get leases-n kube-system | grep kube-controller-manager kube-controller-manager master-1_xxxx 6h2m ~~~- To find out the current `kube-scheduler` master leader is, use this command ~~~ $ oc get lease-n openshift-kube-scheduler | grep kube-scheduler kube-scheduler master-1_xxxxx 5h3m ~~~
root_cause: Starting from version 4.13, OpenShift uses `leases` instead of `ConfigMaps` to manage leader election. See this solution to see how get the leader before 4.13- [How to find leaders/active controllers for different Openshift Operators in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3035261) References:- [use lease for leader election- OCPBUGSM-39083](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGSM-39083)- [migrate to using Lease for leader election- OCPBUGS-10361](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-10361)- [leader election migration steps](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/107454)

title: operator-catalog pod is failing with ImagePullBackOff in RHOCP 4

title: ArgoCD Upgrade Leads to Misconfigured ownerReferences in ConfigMaps

title: ACM continuously refreshes the bootstrap hub kubeconfig for all  managed cluster
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: When Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (ACM) for Kubernetes is running on an OpenShift 4.15 cluster and the cluster uses custom API server certificates with any empty line between certificates, ACM continually refreshes the bootstrap hub kubeconfig for all managed clusters. This will result in the klusterlet-agent on the managed cluster continually crashing and restarting. An example of certificates with an empty line looks like, ``` $ oc-n openshift-config get secret-o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64-d-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- MIIEVDCCAzygAwIBAgISBKr6kb9iMsZlx0YWqBy5FJt1MA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBCwUA MDIxCzAJBgNVBAYTAlVTMRYwFAYDVQQKEw1MZXQncyBFbmNyeXB0MQswCQYDVQQD EwJSMzAeFw0yNDAzMTkxNjIyMDRaFw0yNDA2MTcxNjIyMDNaMCUxIzAhBgNVBAMT GmFwaS5wZXJmMS52bXcuaWJtZnVzaW9uLmV1MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0D...... lJgt0UV8opH1tIR+Fk0N/2Dp4fbgRXncs9xJFqGtNiC8p2wpyuhALiBrV45J7eyc w1cdBhRpAAKSldcymLXg3lQ4znZHxNe9MJh7YEYSo1YlkhQPpK7XyNgU/y285c1p 7j3sLbpDsMmvSa+tV9emcGZ9BCCRWV7zbMqOhOEhYMxxxFL4jCL6VWDoqJ/0SJsI BIK/JIF/7p4=-----END CERTIFICATE----------BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- MIIFFjCCAv6gAwIBAgIRAJErCErPDBinU/bWLiWnX1owDQYJKoZIhvcNAQELBQAw TzELMAkGA1UEBhMCVVMxKTAnBgNVBAoTIEludGVybmV0IFNlY3VyaXR5IFJlc2Vh cmNoIEdyb3VwMRUwEwYDVQQDEwxJU1JHIFJvb3QgWDEwHhcNMjAwOTA0MDAwMDAw WhcNMjUwOTE1MTYwMDAwWjAyMQswCQYDVQQGEwJVUzEWMBQGA1UEChMNTGV0J3Mg...... hCExroL1+7mryIkXPeFM5TgO9r0rvZaBFOvV2z0gp35Z0+L4WPlbuEjN/lxPFin+ HlUjr8gRsI3qfJOQFy/9rKIJR0Y/8Omwt/8oTWgy1mdeHmmjk7j1nYsvC9JSQ6Zv MldlTTKB3zhThV1+XWYp6rjd5JW1zbVWEkLNxE7GJThEUG3szgBVGP7pSWTUTsqX nLRbwHOoq7hHwg==-----END CERTIFICATE----- ```
resolution: To resolve this issue, you can remove empty lines from the certificates using the following command: ``` oc-n openshift-config patch secret--patch="{\"data\": {\"tls.crt\": \"$(oc-n openshift-config get secret-o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64-d | sed '/^$/d' | base64-w0)\"}}" ```
root_cause: When ACM controller reconciles the bootstrap hub kubeconfig generated for each managed cluster, it retrieves the current Kube API server certificate and compares it with the CA certificate in the bootstrap hub kubeconfig. If they are not identical, the controller will create a new bootstrap hub kubeconfig with the latest CA certificate. Additionally, a new ServiceAccount token is created using TokenRequest API during this procedure because OpenShift 4.15 no longer creates the token secret for ServiceAccount.

title: What does JWT header is malformed message mean when reaching API services
issue: - We are getting **JWT header is malformed*
message by query hybrid console API with token based authentication
resolution: error message "JWT header is malformed" means a problem with the token. This can be a formatting error in the token, or the lack of correct RBAC permissions assigned to the service account. You have to double check if the token which generated is same as which supplied when a query ran. You have to check that the account used for API access have correct RBAC permissions assigned to. More about RBAC access at [Adding a user to a group](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_hybrid_cloud_console/1-latest/html/user_access_configuration_guide_for_role-based_access_control_rbac/assembly-rbac-procedures_user-access-configuration#adding-a-user-to-a-group_rbac-procedures "Adding a user to a group")

title: Path based route shows "HostAlreadyClaimed" even after deleting the older route
issue: - After deleting one route out of the two with the same host and path still show **"HostAlreadyClaimed"**.- After the deletion of the duplicate route, the other route shows the wrong description pointing to an unrelated existing route.
resolution: - This issue was reported in [RHBZ#1821095](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1821095) and initially fixed in the OpenShift 4.5 version.- The engineering team worked on the [RHBZ#1884421](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1884421) to backport the fix in OpenShift 3.11.501 version.- The workaround for this issue is to delete the router pod so the new pod spin up and register the routes. If [Router Sharding](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/architecture/networking/routes.html#router-sharding) is configured, the router pods managing the route on error need to be restarted.

title: Using storage provided by Dell CSI driver pods start and attachment operations seem to happen but there is no access to the PV.
issue: Customer created a new block volume from Dell CSI and created a test Pod to use it. Same behavior. Device not visible inside the Pod.
resolution: - It was explained that since there were no errors from the CSI drivers, kubelet understands that the are no issues with the volume and thus, the Pod starts.- The link to a very similar issue reported in Dell's CSM repository was shared: https://github.com/dell/csm/issues/1042- Customer added the mountPropgagation for the volumedevices-path into Dell's DaemonSet definition and tested once more successfully.- After this test, customer proceeded with the import of an image through the CDI process of OpenShift Virtualization which also worked without issues.
root_cause: - There is a general issue with Dell CSI driver that affects both Pods and VMs.- While pod starts,and some attachments operations are seems, when accessing the pods the PV is not seem.- This happens to block volumes.

title: Why do we get “See More Options” while opening the support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal?
issue: - Not able to proceed to open the support case under the portal.- Stuck at the “See More Options” button.- Error “Please address the error to proceed” while opening the support case.
resolution: To open the support case with Red Hat, please refer the following steps:- Go to [Red Hat Customer Portal](https://access.redhat.com).- Click on the ["Support Case"](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/) button from top bar.- Click on ["Get Support"](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/get-support?caseCreate=true) button on the right side. Opening the support case with Red Hat is divided in *6 stages* 1. **Get support** Please mention following details:- Account Number- Case owner details- Select the valid option or “other” And *continue*. 2. **Summarize**- Mention the *Product* & *Version* in use.- Write the short description about the problem statment.- Make sure to use less than *255 words*.- NO *special characters*(symbols or punctuation marks) in description.- If the word limit exceeds 255 words or use any special characters, an error message will pop-up **Please address the error to proceed**.![Please address the error to proceed](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/please_address_the_error_to_proceed.png)- According to the problem description, the new AI feature will share the “Live search results powered by Openshift AI” and suggest the related documents and articles which might be helpful.- If the desired resolution is not listed in the suggested articles list then you can click on "**See More Options**" blue button. OpenShift AI will share more relevant articles. If still the relevent solutions is not found, click on *continue*.- NOTE: Attachments (such as sosreport, screenshot, error files) can be added over the case. On the Top-Right side, an option to attach the attachments will be found.![Attachments](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/sosreport.png) 3. **Troubleshoot**- Recheck Product, Version & Description.- Refer the "Red Hat recommended results" and *continue*. 4. **Describe More** Share more details about the query, answer the following questions which will help Red Hat to understand the query and engineers can assist better:- *What are you experiencing? What are you expecting to happen?*- *Define the value or impact to you or the business*- *Where are you experiencing this behavior? What environment?*- *When does this behavior occur? Frequency? Repeatedly? At certain times?* NOTE: There are no words limits in it. Fill the answere and *continue*. 5. **Management** In this stage the case behaviour is defined.- Support Level- PREMIUM- STANDARD- ENTERPRISE- Severity- 1(Urgent)-Server impact to production environment.- 2(High)-Production has been severely reduced- 3(Normal)-Patial, non-critical loss of usage- 4(Low)-General usage questions or request- Contact details- Language, etc. 6. **Review** In the final stage of the process, the reviewer has the opportunity to review all the content and input of the case before it is shipped to Red Hat support delivery. If the reviewer is confirmed and ready to open the case, they can click on the *Submit* button.

title: InstallPlan fails with "updated validation is too restrictive" when multiple CRD versions are served
issue: - Upgrading the DevWorkSpace operator to a version which serves multiple CRD versions leads to error complaining about the existing custom resources even when they are migrated to use the latest CRD version.
resolution: **Workaround** The workaround, specifically for DevWorkSpace operator would be to unserve the old CRD version before approving the installplan: ~~~ $ oc patch crd devworkspacetemplates.workspace.devfile.io--type='json'-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/versions/0/served", "value": false}]' $ oc patch crd devworkspaces.workspace.devfile.io--type='json'-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/versions/0/served", "value": false}]' ~~~
root_cause: The issue is identified as a bug and is being worked upon in![OCPBUGS-31522](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-31522)
