title: "noobaa-default-backing-store" is not yet ready after OCP upgrade due to account not found xxxxxxxxx error
issue: After upgrade, noobaa-default-backing-store" is not yet ready after OCP upgrade due to account not found xxxxxxxxx error.
resolution: 1.Verify that all your nodes are in ready state 2.Scale all noobaa pods down: # oc project openshift-storage # oc scale deployment noobaa-operator--replicas=0 # oc scale deployment noobaa-endpoint--replicas=0 # oc scale sts noobaa-core--replicas=0 # oc scale sts noobaa-db-pg--replicas=0 3.Make sure all the noobaa pods have been terminated successfully: # oc get pod-n openshift-storage|grep noobaa 4.Restart all the noobaa pods: # oc scale sts noobaa-db-pg--replicas=1 # oc scale sts noobaa-core--replicas=1 # oc scale deployment noobaa-endpoint--replicas=1 # oc scale deployment noobaa-operator--replicas=1 5.Check the noobaa and the backing store status: # noobaa status # oc get BackingStore/noobaa-default-backing-store-oyaml | grep 'phase' 6. Reach out to Red Hat support team if these steps did not fix the issue for further assistance.

title: FedRAMP HCC Onboarding
issue: - How can I be onboarded into the FedRAMP Hybrid Cloud Console (HCC)- What should I consider when gaining access to the Hybrid Cloud Console?- What are the limitations IdP limitations of the Hybrid Cloud Console at this time?
resolution: To complete your onboarding into the FedRAMP environment please perform the following steps: 1. Fill out the `FedRAMP Package Access Request Form`, using the following values: a. `Name of Package Requested: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA)` b. `Package ID: FR2102031769` 2. Have the desired organizational administrator of the Hybrid Cloud Console fill out the [FedRAMP ROSA Access form](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/create/rosa/govcloud) a. Please ensure that the user making the attestation is a `US-Based Citizen` b. If unsure what to enter for Contract ID, Award ID or RFP Number from the U.S. Spending government website, enter N/A 3. Once this is submitted, you should receive a message from the Red Hat engineering team to the email address listed within the form regarding the status of your onboarding. During this time the Managed Cloud Services (MCS) Gov team will work on granting you access to their secure support channel where you will be able to open cases & dialogue securely with Red Hat engineering. 4. If you intend to integrate your IDP with Red Hat's HCC please provide the MCS Gov team with the following information: a. IdP Discovery Endpoint or Redirect Uri b. IdP client id c. IdP secret d. Email domain(s) which should enforce the IdP login flow (e.g. @department.agency.gov) e. Filter attribute (to filter on a key/value of users or groups that should be able to create/manage ROSA clusters) f. Any "essential" claims, to ensure a claim from the IdP exists on the token g. Insights: If you are requesting access to Red Hat Insights through your satellite servers, we will need to add your IP address or range of IP addresses to an `allow-list`, so please provide those details here as well. **NOTE:** *For you to establish a secure connection to the hybrid cloud console you will need to have this [Yubikey](https://www.yubico.com/product/yubikey-5c-nfc-fips/) (the nano, lightning, or other models will not suffice) as it is the only FIPS validated 2MFA supported at this time* 5. If you do NOT intend to integrate your IdP, therefore, you intend to bring your own IdP, please specify your authorization requirements so Red Hat can work with your team on a long-term solution. 6. Once this is complete, Red Hat will notify you that your HCC account has been created & to be on the lookout for an email from `fedramp-srep@openshiftusgov.com` containing your credentials. Once logged in you will be able to authenticate directly to the FedRAMP HCC using PIV/CAC using their IDP (should you employ one): a. If you have issues locating the email please look inside your `:spam` folder b. If you are unable to access the link `within 12 hours` of sending please locate the email and select “forgot password” to re-initiate the process

title: RHOAI operator deployments are failing in RHOCP 4
issue: - Red Hat OpenShift AI operator pods are not getting created and hence the dependent pods are stuck in CrashLoopBackOff state- RHOAI eployments are failing in project `redhat-ods-applications`- Observing below errors in the `redhat-ods-applications` project event: ~~~ 5m Warning FailedCreate replicaset/etcd-6d5f977bbf Error creating: pods "etcd-xxx" is forbidden: failed quota: quota-name: must specify limits.cpu for: etcd-secret-creator; limits.memory for: etcd-secret-creator; requests.cpu for: etcd-secret-creator; requests.memory for: etcd-secret-creator 3m7s Warning FailedCreate job/remove-deprecated-monitoring (combined from similar events): Error creating: pods "remove-deprecated-monitoring-xxx" is forbidden: failed quota: quota-name: must specify limits.cpu for: oc-cli; requests.cpu for: oc-cli ~~~
resolution: - Check for the quota created in project `redhat-ods-applications`: ~~~ $ oc get quota-n redhat-ods-applications ~~~- Take backup of the quota: ~~~ $ oc get quota-n redhat-ods-applications-o yaml > backup- ~~~- Delete the quota: ~~~ $ oc delete quota-n redhat-ods-applications ~~~- There can be a project requirement to have the quota in project `redhat-ods-applications` and should not be deleted.- In such cases, scale down the operator pod and add `limits.cpu`, `requests.cpu`, `limits.memory`, `requests.memory` in the `etcd` deployment yaml. ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=0 deployment data-science-pipelines-operator-controller-manager-n redhat-ods-applications ~~~ ~~~ $ oc edit deployment etcd spec:... template:... spec:... containers: resources: limits: cpu: "1" memory: 2Gi requests: cpu: 50m memory: 96Mi ~~~- However, as of now it is not possible to modify deployment as it is managed by operator.- Raised [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHOAIRFE-116) to get this feature available for RHOAI operator in RHOCP cluster.
root_cause: - The OpenShift AI pods are failing to create because of the quota present/created in the project `redhat-ods-applications`.

title: Guidelines for customizing JVM flags in Data Grid 8 images
issue: How to customize JVM flags on Data Grid 8 in OCP 4?
resolution: Please calculate the required resources (cpu, memory, storage) accordingly. Do not deploy DG production pods without adequate values and when tuning, make sure you know the implications of the changes- for heap and off-heap. Java is container aware- so it already sets MaxRAM as the memory size of the container (so total size == pod; for pods with only one container), as explained in [Setting MaxRAM on DG 8 pod](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6974858). **Highlight on fact java is container aware and non-elastic.** Percentage of RAM is currently what the image will use to set the heap and off-heap. Note that:- `/proc/cgroups` tells nothing about the number of CPUs: it brings information about mounted cgroup controllers, hierarchy id, etc. user cannot infer anything about the number of cpus from that.- lscpu is not container aware- For cgroups investigation use [jcmd $PID VM.info](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973111). ## **Core points**- First: the JVM is container aware- Second: for main DG purposes/behavior the JVM is inelastic; so JVM will use resources.limits for cpu calculations (GC threads, blocking threads, non-blocking threads).- Third: Allocate reasonable cpu resources for the container. Do not allocate a minimal value for the cpu resources.- Forth: Prefer runtime configuration rather than build configuration, i.e. avoid hard-coding values such as heap/off-heap sizes/jvm flags/jvm properties via container for example.- Fifth: Setting cpu resources requests == limits provides the pod with Garanteed Quality of Service (QoS) and it is usually more recommended in production critical deployments- [reference](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6972165).- Final: Select the adequate deployment method in OCP 4: either Operator or Helm charts. ### **JVM options** To set jvm arguments set `spec.container.extraJvmOpts`- example: ~~~ spec: container: cpu: '2' extraJvmOpts: '-Xlog:gc*=info:file=/tmp/gc.log:time,level,tags,uptimemillis:filecount=10,filesize=1m' ~~~ ### **Xmx (and Xms)** The default `JAVA_MAX_MEM_RATIO` is set from the DG 8 image (not the Operator), where it sets 50% for heap and 50% for non heap. This comes from the openjdk images- ubi7/ubi8 images, setting 50% as baseline (ubi8 will have 80% as baseline). For overwriting this behavior use Xmx, which will set the max heap- however, **do not set this value for the whole pod size/container, off-heap space must be left**. In fact do not set Xmx for more than 80% of the heap (so less than off-heap space). Make off-heap usage will cause OOME and OOME cgroups Killer. Again setting too small off-heap will result [in crashes](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6968671). Setting **Xms** can help on performance in some cases- where the JVM will ask from the kernel the memory at start-up the complete Xmx value (this is not guaranteed)- so some performance improvement can be gained depending on variable factors (gc collector, kernel, number of cpus, other processes in pod). ### Reduction memory utilization (returning to the kernel) The user can set-[ShrinkHeapInSteps](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8146436), can be user to reduce more aggressively the heap occupancy to the-XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio: meaning more aggressively than in stages. Without this flag, the default implementation requires several garbage collection cycles for this reduction (default == in steps). ~~~ ### Default behavior == return in steps $ java-XX:+PrintFlagsFinal-version | grep ShrinkHeapInSteps bool ShrinkHeapInSteps = true {product} {default} openjdk version "11.0.12" 2021-07-20 LTS OpenJDK Runtime Environment 18.9 (build 11.0.12+7-LTS) OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 18.9 (build 11.0.12+7-LTS, mixed mode, sharing) ### Not the behavior == doesn't return in steps == aggressively return $ java-XX:-ShrinkHeapInSteps-XX:+PrintFlagsFinal-version | grep ShrinkHeapInSteps bool ShrinkHeapInSteps = false {product} {command line} openjdk version "11.0.12" 2021-07-20 LTS OpenJDK Runtime Environment 18.9 (build 11.0.12+7-LTS) OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 18.9 (build 11.0.12+7-LTS, mixed mode, sharing) ~~~ ### Off-heap usage **Even though the cache entries might not be set for off-heap, the JVM will allocate and use off-heap memory** Off-heap usage includes, but it is not limited to, all kind of non-heap allocation- example:- metaspace- threads- GC collector (the collector itself)- modules loading (JDK11 and JDK 17).- shared libraries Some of those are nominally and stable, others are directly proportional to the load. And [jcmd native tracking](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5393201) can be used to track those, as well as [VM.info](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973111). Therefore, not just the off-heap caching will be occpy the off-heap and this must be accounted for- to avoid (native) OOME. ### Total RAM usage: RAM is directly proportional to number of owners- and defined as below: Aspect | Usage--------- |--------- Cluster-wide | number of owners * total cache size. Per node | (number of owners / number of nodes) * total cache size So the more owners, the more data used, however, one will lose data when a node goes down- and depending on the use case that can be acceptable if shared store or another way to reload the cache. If not, this can be deleted and lost completely. Also when not setting `MaxRAM`, the value it will be printed will be 137gb- see in_Diagnostic Steps_. ### Other suggestions:- Do not change the default 50% ratio between heap and off-heap unless a very detailed benchmark process was done knowing how much heap and off-heap usage was set- Complementary to the above, do not set Xmx for more than 80% of the heap (so less than off-heap space)- leave space for the off-heap (even if the cache is not set for off-heap).- Do not set off-heap for 80%, even if all the caches are off-heap, because of state transfers heap usage, which need a big chunk of heap. After the actual cache data, state transfers are the 2nd biggest memory user in DG. (in short bursts)- Setting less than 1 cpu is not recommended. In fact you should not deploy anything in production with less than 2/3 cpus. Lack of cpu will cause timeouts on execution of cli commands. If you have more resources, here is the time to use them.- Using 2+ cpus allows a much better usage of multi-thread collectors such as ParallelGC collector. For instance, for 1 CPU SerialGC can be the adequate option, given using ParallelGC would add extra overhead to manage the extra threads with the same CPU power.- Setting [QoS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6972165) by setting the same values of `limit` == `request` on the pods- In some cases generational collectors will have a better performance than non-generational- Avoid deprecated [type service Cache](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6972352)- Avoid deprecated flags, like using JDK 17 with UseParallelOldGC, it will return: `Unrecognized VM option 'UseParallelOldGC'` or `--illegal-access=debug`.
root_cause: To customize the jvm flags on Data Grid 8 Operator use **spec.container.extraJvmOpts**- example: ~~~- apiVersion: infinispan.org/v1 kind: Infinispan metadata: name: ${CLUSTER_NAME} namespace: ${CLUSTER_NAMESPACE} annotations: infinispan.org/monitoring: 'false' labels: type: middleware prometheus_domain: ${CLUSTER_NAME} spec: configMapName: "${CLUSTER_NAME}-custom-config" container: cpu: '2' extraJvmOpts: '-Xlog:gc*=info:file=/tmp/gc.log:time,level,tags,uptimemillis:filecount=10,filesize=1m-Dcom.redhat.fips=false-Dio.netty.allocator.type=unpooled' routerExtraJvmOpts: '-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=4M-Xlog:gc*=info:file=/tmp/gc.log:time,level,tags,uptimemillis:filecount=10,filesize=1m' ~~~ ### Default RAM usage By default the OpenJDK image sets the heap/off-heap ratio as 50/50 this means half of the container memory will be heap and half will be off-heap: ~~~ ENV \ ISPN_HOME="/opt/infinispan" \ JAVA_GC_MAX_METASPACE_SIZE="96m" \ JAVA_GC_METASPACE_SIZE="32m" \ JAVA_MAX_MEM_RATIO="50" \ <----------------------------------------- 50/50 JBOSS_IMAGE_NAME="datagrid/datagrid-8" \ JBOSS_IMAGE_VERSION="1.4" ~~~ Above is line 73 on [Red Hat Data Grid for OpenShift- Dockerfile](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/datagrid/datagrid-8-rhel8/5d53e7b4d70cc5521d20ecea?architecture=amd64&image=65a913ff8c1cb7493ff006a0&container-tabs=dockerfile). The `JAVA_MAX_MEM_RATIO` sets the Xmx, which has precedence over `MaxRAMPercentage` for example. Depending on the OpenJDK version, `JAVA_MAX_MEM_RATIO` is implemented setting Xmx directly, and later versions implement `MaxRAMPercentage`. This means, if the image is using the MaxRAMPercentage implementation user can overwrite with `MaxRAMPercentage`. If not then the image would set `Xmx` and any setting with `MaxRAMPercentage` is futile, because Xmx has precedence over `MaxRAMPercentage`. ### Notes- In terms of RSS in containers, using Xmx == Xms and XX:+AlwaysPretouch means the container will always run with an RSS > = NGb (N is the value in Gb for heap) no matter what, in particular it won't give any memory back to the OS even if it doesn't use it. It does that irrespective of the actual memory needs of the application- MaxRAM should not be used and instead setting a container limit via the deployment config and setting XX:MaxRAMPercentage=80.0 provides more elastic configuration, given it couples the deploymentconfig (runtime configuration) with the heap usage/size.- Using MaxDirectMemorySize translates to the `sun.nio.MaxDirectMemorySize` property and if not specified uses the `Xmx` setting for the upper bound. When using this flag, make sure to leave room for: metaspace+thread stack+ code cache+ direct buffers+other JVM/GC overhead. Otherwise the container will crash given the upper boundary- meaning the pod may die with wrong configurations.

title: Error when reconciling the machines after changing the cluster API from Public to Private
issue: - After changing the Control Plane API endpoint from Public to Private via [OCM](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/), the events below are observed: ~~~ 1 recorder.go:103] events "msg"="machineName-master-01: reconciler failed to Update machine: failed to update load balancers: LoadBalancerNotFound: Load balancers '[loadBalancerName]' not found\n\tstatus code: 400, request id: 6fdd164d-5eac-xxxx-xxxx-2ca3a97093be" "object"={"kind":"Machine","namespace":"openshift-machine-api","name":"machineName-master-01","uid":"ee57c940-xxxx-xxxx-af78-79c945ef70b8","apiVersion":"machine.openshift.io/v1beta1","resourceVersion":"1310317311"} "reason"="FailedUpdate" "type"="Warning" ~~~- The cluster does not finish its scheduled update when this issue is present.
resolution: - In order to fix the issue, it was necessary SRE to update the machine `specs` to remove the invalid reference as the Cloud Ingress Operator (CIO) is not able to reconcile it once the load balancer is not present anymore.
root_cause: - The root cause for this behavior could not be defined as the logs of the Cloud Ingress Operator (CIO) were lost after the pods being replaced. The assumption is, when the CIO removes the load balancer, it should also remove that load balancer from all master instances, which somehow must have failed. As the load balancer context was lost when it failed, it can not try to reconcile it again and the machines get stuck in the broken state.

title: MachineConfig daemon fails while updating from OCP 4.13 to OCP 4.14
issue: - When upgrading the cluster from 4.13.23 to 4.14.3, `machine-config` CO gets stuck due to a content mismatch error on all nodes. ~~~ Node node-xxx-xxx is reporting: "unexpected on-disk state validating against rendered-master-734521b50f69a1602a3a657419ed4971: content mismatch for file \"/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/openshift-config-user-ca-bundle.crt\"" ~~~
resolution: - This Problem was solved in OpenShift Container Platform 4.14.22 via [RHSA-2024:1891](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:1891). Please update to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.14.22 or later. **Workaround**: Append a new line in `/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/configmaps/cloud-config/ca-bundle.pem` file for the validation to pass.
root_cause: - Previously, the Machine Config Operator allowed user-provided certificate authority updates to be made without requiring a new machine config to trigger. Because the new write method for these updates was missing a newline character, it caused validation errors for the contents of the CA file on-disk and the Machine Config Daemon became degraded.

title: Accidentally deleted ROSA cluster : What Next?
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Is it possible to restore a deleted cluster in ROSA?- What can be done if a cluster has been accidentally deleted?- Can deleted clusters in ROSA be recovered, and if so, how?
resolution: Unfortunately, once a ROSA cluster has been deleted, there is no option for restoration. The deletion process is irreversible, and it results in the complete removal of the cluster and its associated data. In such cases, the recommended approach is to deploy a new ROSA cluster to address your needs and requirements effectively. ### Data Resilience and Backup Guidelines in ROSA Ensuring data integrity and resilience in Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) is of paramount importance. Application and application data backups are not a part of the Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS service. Therefore, it is critical that customers have a backup plan for their applications and application data.- Red Hat performs backup in only cluster created with IAM user credentials for all Kubernetes objects like `etcd`. No persistent volumes (PVs) are backed up in this backup schedule. For more information please visit Red Hat [official documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_architecture/rosa_policy_service_definition/rosa-service-definition.html#rosa-sdpolicy-backup-policy_rosa-service-definition:~:text=This%20is%20a%20full%20backup%20of%20all%20Kubernetes%20objects%20like%20etcd.%20No%20persistent%20volumes%20(PVs)%20are%20backed%20up%20in%20this%20backup%20schedule.).- There is no Red Hat-provided backup method available for ROSA clusters with STS. Red Hat does not commit to any Recovery Point Objective (RPO) or Recovery Time Objective (RTO). For more information please visit Red Hat [official documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_architecture/rosa_policy_service_definition/rosa-policy-responsibility-matrix.html#rosa-policy-incident_rosa-policy-responsibility-matrix:~:text=There%20is%20no,Time%20Objective%20(RTO).). Red Hat does not recommend taking `etcd` backups, rather it is encouraged to take all application and data backup. OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) can be implemented for ROSA STS clusters to backup and restore application data. The steps and procedure has been explained in Red Hat [official documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_backing_up_and_restoring_applications/backing-up-applications.html). **NOTE**: Restic is not supported in the OpenShift API for Data Protection on ROSA with AWS STS environment. Ensure the Restic service is disabled while implementing OADP. If any further questions or assistance is needed, please contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/support).

title: Azure Disk performance by region
issue: Azure Disk performance is known to vary by region.
Azure Disk performance issues manifest themselves as etcd performance issues such as leader election changes, high fsync latency durations, and API server failures.
resolution: Choosing a region with better performance will result in better cluster stability. Refer to [etcd backend performance requirements for OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4770281) for additional information about the etcd requiremets. The Azure platform is currently working on reducing storage latency by rolling out updates that improve storage performance. Microsoft region storage upgrade status: Completed | In Progress----------- |----------- US West, US West Central, France Central, Canada Central, Brazil South, Asia Southeast etc, both Norway regions | North Europe ~30% complete
root_cause: Azure disk performance has high latency. Etcd requires performance of its 99th percentile fsync latency to be sub 10 milliseconds. Here is a breakdown of fsync times using a simple test with the fio command line tool: Region | Fsync 99 | Fsync 99.99 | Fsync Avg | Fsync Max------ |-------- |----------- |--------- |--------- uaenorth | 5.59 | 20.88 | 2.46 | 37.71 eastasia | 6.42 | 18.58 | 2.60 | 44.49 southeastasia | 6.75 | 16.75 | 2.48 | 24.32 canadacentral | 6.78 | 26.75 | 3.09 | 36.58 norwayeast | 7.00 | 22.18 | 2.91 | 29.20 koreasouth | 7.07 | 21.99 | 3.24 | 31.38 southindia | 7.25 | 20.07 | 3.10 | 31.27 japaneast | 7.32 | 22.65 | 3.02 | 30.29 ukwest | 7.41 | 21.45 | 3.03 | 29.58 switzerlandnorth | 7.50 | 19.77 | 2.60 | 24.81 northcentralus | 7.55 | 20.94 | 3.07 | 28.68 westindia | 7.56 | 18.40 | 2.94 | 24.34 japanwest | 7.63 | 20.86 | 3.27 | 40.93 centralindia | 7.91 | 19.42 | 3.12 | 26.21 australiacentral | 7.95 | 19.62 | 2.83 | 22.99 germanywestcentral | 8.01 | 25.64 | 4.16 | 32.85 southcentralus | 8.15 | 20.76 | 3.19 | 27.72 westcentralus | 8.40 | 17.27 | 2.32 | 27.95 westus2 | 8.48 | 20.15 | 3.06 | 28.23 westeurope | 8.78 | 22.65 | 3.21 | 28.30 southafricanorth | 8.92 | 23.45 | 4.33 | 32.06 brazilsouth | 9.21 | 31.23 | 3.26 | 42.38 koreacentral | 9.32 | 24.96 | 4.25 | 54.67 canadaeast | 9.34 | 23.70 | 3.29 | 49.34 uksouth | 9.55 | 22.08 | 3.04 | 26.22 northeurope | 9.80 | 25.31 | 3.46 | 38.60 australiaeast | 9.83 | 28.70 | 4.07 | 56.37 eastus | 10.49 | 25.46 | 3.48 | 37.32 francecentral | 10.62 | 24.59 | 3.32 | 34.76 westus | 11.45 | 27.22 | 4.19 | 34.92 centralus | 15.18 | 59.21 | 5.14 | 112.97 > **Important:** The `fio` test is a short test executed at specific moment. It can show if the disk is fast enough to support the etcd requirements, but other loads in the disk could cause that etcd don't behaves correctly. Review also the etcd metrics to know the real etcd behavior as shown in [How to graph etcd metrics using Prometheus to gauge Etcd performance in OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5489721).

title: Size of virtual disks used by OSD's in ODF is not reducing on deleting workload from cephfs PVC's
issue: - On deleting workload from cephfs PVC's, the used space of VMware virtual disk (vmdk files) used by OSD's is not reducing.
resolution: - Performed below steps to reproduce the issue. 1. Deployed ODF cluster on VMware. Created thin storage class to provision persistent volumes for OSD. 2. Created cephfs PVC and wrote 400Gb data in it. Deleted the 400Gb data. `ceph df` is showing free space. From vpshere, checked vmdk files size. It's showing around 400 Gb consumed.- This test indicates data is not getting discarded by osd's.- Ceph uses bluestore device for managing data on ceph osd. For bluestore to discard, below two conditions should be true: 1. The OSD backing disk should support discard. The ceph code that detect this feature on the backing disk is: ~~~ bool BlkDev::support_discard() const {return get_int_property("queue/discard_granularity") > 0;} ~~~ 2. `bdev_enable_discard` should be set to true for all OSD's. This option enable/disable discards on OSD's. This option is false by default, that means by default bluestore won't send a discard/SCSI unmap to the underlying disk / storage. In addition, To enable asynchronous discard, `bdev_async_discard` should be set to true along with `bdev_enable_discard`. This option is false by default. If `bdev_enable_discard` is set to true, and `bdev_async_discard` is false, discard is synchronous (IO discard operation is only completed when the storage/disk respond that the discard operation is finished, that means from application / operating system side the delete command will be waiting for that IO to be completed) Run below commands using [Ceph CLI](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4870821) to set these variables to true: `ceph config set osd bdev_enable_discard true` `ceph config set osd bdev_async_discard true` **Note:**- Deletion of data from application side (ie # rm file) took more time when using sync discard (bdev_enable_discard=true, bdev_async_discard=false) as discard is a part of processing the delete request. Before worker thread picks next, discard must finish.- Deletion of data from application side (ie # rm file) was instantaneous when using async discard (bdev_enable_discard=true, bdev_async_discard=true). Discard is performed in a separate thread, outside worker threads. (IO discard operation is returned as completed immediately as soon as bluestore receive it (and the bluestore will process that discard operation to the storage internally) that means from application / operating system side the delete command will be completed with no delay)- Note: Async discard queue is not persistent. Restarted OSD will forget that there is something to discard.
root_cause: - OSD's by default does not discard data on doing delete operation. `bdev_enable_discard` on ceph side and `discard_granularity` property of storage disk side, control this behavior. `bdev_enable_discard` is set as false by default on OSD's.

keycloak url in the `authServerUrl` of `ActiveMQArtemisSecurity` CR, the AMQ Broker pod shows the following error: WARN [org.keycloak.adapters.KeycloakDeployment] Failed to load URLs from https://keycloak-host/auth/realms/amq-broker-realm/.well-known/openid-configuration: javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed: sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException: unable to find valid certification path to requested target
resolution: 1. Extract TLS certificates: $ oc extract secret/router-certs-default-n openshift-ingress--confirm tls.crt tls.key 2. Use `keytool` to create a **truststore** certificate file: $ keytool-import-noprompt-file tls.crt-alias "HOSTDOMAIN"-keystore truststore.jks-storepass password For instance: keytool-import-noprompt-file tls.crt-alias "*.apps.redhat.com"-keystore truststore.jks-storepass password 3. Create a `configmap` to mount the `truststore`certificate file to the AMQ Broker Pod: $ oc create configmap keycloak-truststore--from-file=truststore.jks 4. In the `activeMQArtemis` CR, add the following to mount the configmap as volume in the AMQ Broker pod: spec: version: 7.10.0 deploymentPlan: extraMounts: configMaps:- keycloak-truststore For **AMQ 7.11 and later**: 5. Add the following in order to include `truststore` to the `JAVA ARGS` using the env var `JAVA_ARGS_APPEND` and check the `truststore` at the runtime as described in the step `8`: apiVersion: broker.amq.io/v1beta1 kind: ActiveMQArtemis metadata: name: artemis-test spec: env:- name: JAVA_ARGS_APPEND value:-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/amq/extra/configmaps/keycloak-truststore/truststore.jks-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=password-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStoreType=jks For **AMQ 7.10**: You need to perform step `6` & `7` 6. Build your custom AMQ Broker image using [init container feature](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5897061), in the `post-config.sh` of the `initImage` add the following in order to include `truststore` to the `JAVA ARGS`: echo "JAVA_OPTIONS- Include truststore" printf '\n' > > "${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}"/etc/artemis.profile echo 'JAVA_ARGS="$JAVA_ARGS-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/amq/extra/configmaps/keycloak-truststore/truststore.jks-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=password-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStoreType=jks"' > > ${CONFIG_INSTANCE_DIR}/etc/artemis.profile 7. Reference the resulted image in the `initImage` section in the `activeMQArtemis` CR: metadata: name: ex-aao spec: deploymentPlan: size: 1 image: placeholder initImage: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/myamq2/amq-broker-init:latest 8. Check the `truststore` at the runtime: $ oc exec ex-aao-ss-0 'ps' 'fp1' | grep-iF truststore 1? title: One ODF mon pod crashes repeatedly

resolution: Follow this procedure deleting the mon-x PVC and forcing the operators to create a a new mon: 1. Scale down the deployments of the operators and of the mon: ``` oc project openshift-storage oc scale deployment ocs-operator rook-ceph-operator rook-ceph-mon-x--replicas=0 ``` 2. Scale up the operators: ``` oc scale deployment ocs-operator rook-ceph-operator--replicas=1 ``` 4. Archive all crashes: ``` $ oc rsh-n openshift-storage $(oc get pods-n openshift-storage-o name-l app=rook-ceph-operator) sh-4.4$ export CEPH_ARGS='-c /var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/openshift-storage.config' # ceph crash archive-all ```

resolution: Could you restart the pod, if possible in a different node, and if it fails again collect and attach a sosreport from that node? Also, a sosreport from the current node might help the troubleshooting efforts.
root_cause: It seems that the vsphere csi driver failed to create this directory in time while setting up the container, hence, when the kube-controller-manager tried to validate the configuration to attach the volume it failed with a timeout because the pre-conditions weren't met. title: Alertmanager notification failure to GChat(Google Chat) Webhook
issue: - Alertmanager is failing to send notifications to GChat Webhook.- In Alertmanager, a receiver with Google Chat Webhook endpoint specified has been created.- Even when relevant alerts are fired, they are not notified to Google Chat Webhook.- After the failure of notification, [AlertmanagerClusterFailedToSendAlerts](https://github.com/openshift/runbooks/blob/master/alerts/cluster-monitoring-operator/AlertmanagerClusterFailedToSendAlerts.md) alert was fired. The details of the alert suggested that the cause was `the endpoint is not reachable`. However, the Webhook endpoint has been confirmed to be correct.- How can we receive notifications from Alertmanager in GChat Webhook?
resolution: - GChat Webhook does not support receiving notifications from Alertmanager.- The JSON format that Alertmanager sends needs to be converted to a format that can be received by Gchat.
root_cause: - [The official documentation of Alertmanager](https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/configuration/#webhook_config) publishes the default JSON format of the payload part to notify the Webhook. The Webhook side needs to be able to receive in the default JSON format.- If the Webhook side cannot receive in the default JSON format, it is possible to receive notifications by using tools or libraries that convert to a format that can be received by each Webhook service (those tools or libraries are also listed in [official documentation of Alertmanager](https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/integrations/#alertmanager-webhook-receiver)).- GChat Webhook cannot receive in the default JSON format. Also, as tools or libraries that convert to a format that can be received are not published, there is a need to create a custom tool.

title: Failed to mount volume with wrong kind of device in OpenShift 4
issue: - `FailedMount` events with message `Unable to attach or mount volumes`, and any of the following reasons: ~~~ volume volume_name has volumeMode Block, but is specified in volumeMounts ~~~ ~~~ volume volume_name has volumeMode Filesystem, but is specified in volumeDevices ~~~
resolution: The volume is configured in the wrong field in the pod:- A `Filesystem` volume needs to be configured in the `volumeMounts` of the pod.- A `Block` volume needs to be configured in the `volumeDevices`. Configure the volume in the correct field.

title: [RHOCP 4] Encountering a 503 error on the passthrough route when the domain differs from *.apps.
issue: - Router pods are returning a `fe_no_sni` alert in the access logging. ~~~ haproxy[57]: 10.2xx.xx5.1xx:62375 [Date:Time] fe_no_sni~ openshift_default/ 0/-1/-1/-1/0 503 2660-- SC-- 126/1/0/0/0 0/0 "GET / HTTP/1.1" ~~~- Receiving a 503 error from router pods on a passthrough route when the external LoadBalancer fails to pass headers to the router pods.
resolution: - It is possible that the external load balancer is removing the Server Name Indication (SNI) information from incoming requests, which is causing the issue.- Consequently, the router pod does not receive the necessary SNI information required for accurate request routing, resulting in the 503 error message as shown below: ~~~ haproxy[37]: 10.2xx.xx5.1xx:62xxx [Date:Time] fe_no_sni~ openshift_default/ 0/-1/-1/-1/0 503 2660-- SC-- 126/1/0/0/0 0/0 "GET / HTTP/1.1" ~~~- Given that all traffic is encrypted (using HTTPS on port 443), the presence of `SNI` is vital for the router to identify the intended hostname the client is attempting to access.- To fix this, try adjusting the `LoadBalancer` settings so that it passes the necessary `SNI` information to the router pod correctly.- Another option is to turn off the feature that removes `SNI headers` in the load balancer. If you're testing unencrypted routes (HTTP on port 80), you might not face this issue since `SNI` isn't needed for `unencrypted traffic`. (avoid any stripping at the load balancer's end.).- OpenShift depends on `SNI` for `encrypted traffic` to direct it to the appropriate backend, in the absence of this header it will redirect the traffic to `fe_no_sni` which has the backend as `openshift-default/ `(means no endpoint).

title: How to add broker connection to a AMQ 7 broker in openshift environment
issue: How to add a broker connection to AMQ 7 broker running in openshift?
resolution: The easiest way would be to use broker properties in broker's CR (Custom Resource) yaml file. For example to add mirroring AMQP connection to another broker at port 61617 we can add following **AMQPConnections.** properties to broker CR yaml file under **brokerProperties:** section: ~~~ brokerProperties:- 'clusterConfigurations.my-cluster.producerWindowSize=-1'- 'addressSettings.#.redeliveryMultiplier=5'- criticalAnalyzer=true- criticalAnalyzerTimeout=6000- criticalAnalyzerCheckPeriod=-1- critical-analyzer-policy=LOG- "AMQPConnections.my-mirror.uri=tcp://localhost:61617"- "AMQPConnections.my-mirror.user=admin"- "AMQPConnections.my-mirror.password=password"- "AMQPConnections.my-mirror.connectionElements.mirror.type=MIRROR" ~~~ To verify if all the above properties have been applied to broker's configuration it is possible to use condition with the type **BrokerPropertiesApplied** to check if the broker properties were applied correctly. For example ~~~ oc get activemqartemis-o yaml > broker-properties.yaml ~~~ We can examine the broker-properties.yaml file and find the condition **BrokerPropertiesApplied** ~~~- lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-31T14:37:54Z" message: 'some properties resulted in error on ordinal 0: reasons: map[broker.properties:[{"value":"critical-analyzer-policy=LOG","reason":"No accessor method descriptor for: critical-analyzer-policy on: class org.apache.activemq.artemis.core.config.impl.FileConfiguration"}]]' reason: AppliedWithError status: "False" type: BrokerPropertiesApplied ~~~ The above shows that all properties but one **critical-analyzer-policy**, were applied correctly. The property **critical-analyzer-policy** used incorrect syntax therefore it has been discarded.

title: Setting up threshold value for kubelet garbage collection on windows nodes
issue: - Is it possible to set the threshold value for kubelet garbage collection on Windows nodes managed by the Windows machine config operator?- Does the kubelet garbage collection work on Windows nodes?
resolution: - The garbage collector works properly on Windows workers too. However, the default config for both container and image garbage collector high thresholds are at 85% which means if the volume utilization reaches this level, there is a high probability that the container garbage collector kicks in and evicts the PODs running on the node.- This feature of changing the high threshold value for the Windows node is not possible at the moment.- Please [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/) for more information on this.

title: ROSA Classic Cluster Installation May Fail When HCP Installer Role Is Selected

issue: - When deploying a cluster using AWS STS, the ROSA CLI Interactive Installer will present and incorrectly allow the user to select AWS-managed HCP IAM Roles when the ROSA Classic Roles should have been chosen.- During the installer's pre-flightchecks an error similar to this should appear. ~~~... Configure the use of IMDSv2 for ec2 instances optional/required: optional I: Using arn:aws:iam::{account-id}:role/ManagedOpenShift-HCP-ROSA-Installer-Role for the Installer role W: No ControlPlane account roles found. You will need to manually set them in the next steps or run 'rosa create account-roles' to create them first. {{? Role ARN: [? for help] (arn:aws:iam::...:role/ManagedOpenShift-HCP-ROSA-Installer-Role)}} E: Expected a valid ARN: interrupt ~~~ AND ~~~ W: More than one Installer role found? Installer role ARN: mg [Use arrows to move, type to filter,? for more help] > arn:aws:I am::........:role/somewhere/over/the/rainbow/mgahagan-stg-Installer-Role E: Expected a valid role ARN: interrupt ~~~

title: Cluster operator image-registry is not available during OpenShift 4.12 upgrade on AWS
issue: - Image Registry Operator is in degraded status with the following error. ~~~ $ oc get co | grep-i image-registry image-registry False True True 2h ~~~- Further checking the condition status of `image-registry` cluster operator. ~~~ $ oc get co image-registry-o json |jq-r '.status.conditions[]' "lastTransitionTime": "2023-09-25T18:32:37Z", "message": "Degraded: The deployment does not have available replicas", "reason": "Unavailable", "status": "True", "type": "Degraded" ~~~- Looking at the `clusterversion` status message. ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING SINCE STATUS version False True 1h46m Unable to apply 4.12.34: the cluster operator image-registry is not available ~~~
resolution: - `RegionEndpoint` is the endpoint for `S3` compatible storage services which is configured in the `imageregistry.operator` which has to be removed. This endpoint blocks the public access to `S3 bucket` for that region.- Take a backup of the `config.imageregistry` and delete the endpoint resource line as per below steps: ~~~ $ oc get config.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io/cluster-o yaml > myconfig.imageregistry.yaml $ oc edit config.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io/cluster... storage: managementState: Managed s3: bucket: xxxx-xxx-image-registry-us-east-1-xxxxxxxxxxxxx encrypt: true region: us-east-1 regionEndpoint: https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com <----- delete this line trustedCA: name: "" virtualHostedStyle: true storageManaged: true ~~~- Restart the image registry pods if the status of `image-registry clusteroperator` does not reflect. ~~~ $ oc delete pods-l docker-registry=default-n openshift-image-registry ~~~
root_cause: - `RegionEndpoint` is the endpoint for `S3` compatible storage services. It is optional and default is based on the Region that is provided in this case, which is "s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com".- As described it's optional. This field is most used in non-AWS (other providers which offers S3 Compatibility APIs to talk with their object storage services).

title: Not able to delete objects using 'oc delete'  command or from console in RHOCP 4

resolution: - Edit the object using `oc edit` command and remove the `finalizers` from it. See below example for a `ConfigMap`. ~~~ $ oc edit cm-n apiVersion: v1 data: kind: ConfigMap metadata: creationTimestamp: deletionGracePeriodSeconds: 0 deletionTimestamp: finalizers:- xyz/finalizer-------> Remove this line ~~~- After making changes as mentioned above, the `ConfigMap` will get deleted.- If the it doesn't get removed then check if the changes made were saved correctly. Run the below command to delete the it manually after that. ~~~ $ oc delete cm-n ~~~
root_cause: - `Finalizers` are namespaced keys that tell Kubernetes to wait until specific conditions are met before it fully deletes resources marked for deletion.

title: The openjdk based java pod failed in TLS cipher negotiation after the OCP 4.10 cluster upgrade.
issue: - The OpenJDK based java pod failed in TLS cipher negotiation after the `RHOCP 4.10` cluster upgrade.- The OpenJDK based java pod failed error: ` EET|HandshakeContext.java:553|Ignore disabled cipher suite: TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256`
resolution: - It is a cipher negotiation issue and the fix should be done on the server side by upgrading the cipher from `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256` to `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`.
root_cause: - The file `/etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/java.config` confirms ` TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256` is present in the running container on `Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8.24` not in `Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.10`.- FIPS-enabled algorithms and crypto work for both `RHOCP 4.8` and `RHOCP 4.10`. If there is a difference found in file `/etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/java.config` in the running container on `RHOCP 4.8` and `RHOCP 4.10` it's because the two versions use different versions of crypto policies. Note that crypto policies are version-specific so the host ones can't be used in containers.- Finally, FIPS configurations may change as the FIPS standard is tweaked regularly by NIST. In this case, specifically, the RSA key exchange method has been removed as not approved. That's why the server should allow the more modern and more secure ciphers.

title: Changes to project.config.openshift.io/cluster are not immediately effective
issue: - After updating the `project.config.openshift.io/cluster` resource to modify the default project template `.spec.projectRequestTemplate` field, OpenShift still references the previous one for a while- Creating a new project fails with `Error from server (NotFound): templates.template.openshift.io "old-project-template" not found`- Changes to `project.config.openshift.io/cluster` are not immediately reflected when creating a new project
resolution: - After updating the `projects.config.openshift.io/cluster` resource, wait for the OpenShift APIServer pods rollout to finish.- Wait for the the new APIServer pods to roll out: ~~~ $ watch oc get po-n openshift-apiserver NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE apiserver-66c7cdcf66-tdhvj 0/2 Pending 0 10s apiserver-7b74b94966-9l9s9 1/2 Terminating 0 39m apiserver-7b74b94966-h4qcx 2/2 Running 0 40m apiserver-7b74b94966-pf5zn 2/2 Running 0 42m ~~~- After the APIServer pods rollout is completed, creating a new project will succeed using the updated `.spec.projectRequestTemplate`: ~~~ $ oc get po-n openshift-apiserver NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE apiserver-66c7cdcf66-rd5vt 2/2 Running 0 1m apiserver-66c7cdcf66-tdhvj 2/2 Running 0 3m apiserver-66c7cdcf66-w6hsh 2/2 Running 0 2m $ oc new-project test Now using project "test" on server "https://ocp4.example.com:6443". <...> ~~~
root_cause: - Updating the `projects.config.openshift.io/cluster` resource rolls out a new version of the API Server deployment in the `openshift-apiserver` namespace. As project creation relies upon the API Server, the new `Project Request Template` will be effective after the rollout of the API Server is complete.- To learn more about project creation, please look at the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/applications/projects/configuring-project-creation.html#about-project-creation_configuring-project-creation).

resolution: - As of today(11/02/2023), the fix has not been released yet. It is scheduled for release in version **4.12.42**.- The bug is currently being tracked in the following Jira issue: [OCPBUGS-14241- Clusters with large numbers of CSVs can CrashLoop the NTO and block upgrades](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14241?focusedId=22363126&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels%3Acomment-tabpanel) **WORKAROUND**- Temporarily reduce the number of CSVs in the cluster as follows: ~~~ $ oc patch olmconfigs cluster--type=merge-p 'spec: {features: {disableCopiedCSVs: true}}' ~~~

title: Critical CVE-2023-46604 in AMQ 6 and AMQ 7
issue: In late October 2023, a security flaw [CVE-2023-46604](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2023-46604) was announced. It affects OpenWire protocol support in both AMQ 6 and AMQ 7 brokers.
resolution: _Remediation_ AMQ version 6.3: Please apply [Patch R20-HF1](https://access.redhat.com/jbossnetwork/restricted/listSoftware.html?product=jboss.amq.broker&downloadType=securityPatches&version=6.3.0). This patch works on both Fabric8 and stand-alone installations. It is an incremental patch on top of roll-up patch R20. Customers using releases earlier than R20 will need to upgrade to R20 first. AMQ version 7: please patch or upgrade to [7.11.4](https://access.redhat.com/jbossnetwork/restricted/listSoftware.html?downloadType=distributions&product=jboss.amq.broker&version=7.11.4). As of November 13, customers who run AMQ on OpenShift should be able to obtain new, fixed broker images. The procedure for installing the fixed image will depend on how the administrator set up the OpenShift installation. For some operator-based installations, the fix roll-out will be automatic. If you're not sure how to update your OpenShift AMQ installation, or whether it will be automatic, please contact Red Hat Technical Support to discuss this point._Background information_ This is an evolving situation; this note explains the current position, as we understand it. Red Hat will update this note as more information comes to light. More information might also be available on the [upstream news page](https://activemq.apache.org/news/cve-2023-46604). However, at this time there appears to be no straightforward mitigation for the defect, and we advise customers to patch or upgrade as soon as practicable. Patches are now available for all supported AMQ releases. The defect affects AMQ 6.x and 7.x brokers that expose an OpenWire listener, that clients can connect to. Clients do not have to be able to authenticate against the broker to exploit the defect. OpenWire is the protocol used by ActiveMQ (AMQ 6.x) JMS clients. The existence of the listener creates the problem; it does not matter whether any client normally uses it. The defect allows clients to instantiate arbitrary Java classes on the broker's class search path. If this instantiation causes code to be executed, then the defect allows unauthenticated clients to execute code on the broker. CVE-2023-46604 is rated as 'critical' because of this potential for an unauthenticated user to execute code. To exploit the defect to execute code, there must be a class on the broker's class search path that executes code when it is instantiated. Red Hat has identified such classes in AMQ 6.x. The defect will not be easy to exploit, but we are aware of ways in which it could be done. We therefore consider AMQ 6.x brokers to be at significant risk. The classes that Red Hat has identified as creating an exploit for the defect in 6.x are not used in 7.x. However, because we can not be certain that no such classes exist, and because adminstrators may have added their own JARs to the broker (e.g., JDBC drivers), we still consider 7.x to be at risk. However, we are not aware of any way to exploit the defect in 7.x, at this time. When it comes to assessing the risk, administrators should be aware that most installations do not expose their AMQ brokers to the public Internet, or to other wide-area networks that might harbour hostile agents. The likelihood of an intruder being able to interact with a public-facing system, and cause it to craft an OpenWire request that can exploit CVE-2023-46604 is exceedingly small. The biggest risk is to businesses that do, in fact, expose their brokers to networks or applications that they do not fully trust. Most AMQ installations, of all versions, on OpenShift and elsewhere, define an OpenWire connector. If the installation does not require the use of OpenWire, then the easiest mitigation is to disable the OpenWire connector completely. On AMQ 7, outside of OpenShift, this change can be made by editing `broker.xml`, and removing the OpenWire listener, or removing `OPENWIRE` as a protocol in any other listener. On OpenShift, you would need to edit the `ActiveMQArtemis` custom resource and redeploy. You could also block the OpenWire listener port using a firewall, if the listener has its own port. However, it is unlikely that disabling the OpenWire listener or port will be practicable in AMQ 6.x installations, because these installations usually use OpenWire exclusively. Similarly, it will not be practicable to disable the OpenWire listener in an AMQ 7 installation that still supports AMQ 6/ActiveMQ clients, because these are also OpenWire. A mitigation that would work for all broker versions, albeit an inconvenient one, is to insist that clients of the broker present a client certificate. If the certificate is invalid, the connection will fail before any OpenWire data gets exchanged, and this will remove the problem-- so long as the clients themselves are trustworthy. Red Hat will provide more information here, if any becomes available.

title: How to enable/disable SSL ciphers in Red Hat Quay
issue: How to enable/disable SSL ciphers in Quay?
resolution: 1. Edit Quay `config.yaml` file and define the SSL ciphers inside the `SSL_CIPHERS` configuration parameter. For example: $ cat /config.yaml | grep SSL_CIPHERS SSL_CIPHERS: ['CAMELLIA', '!3DES'] 2. Restart `quay-app.service` service: $ systemctl restart quay-app.service

title: EgressIP not working with hybrid OVN networking in RHOCP 4
issue: - Unable to setup EgressIP with hybrid OVN networking.- Pods running on Windows node are not routed through the EgressIP.
resolution: EgressIP and other advanced OVN functionalities are not expected to work on Windows workloads when hybrid networking is enabled.
root_cause: - Hybrid networking with the OVN-Kubernetes network plugin implements a VXLAN tunnel to connect the OVN infrastructure with the Windows workloads.- Windows workload traffic is not routed in the ovn_cluster_router by design.

title: Remove "server" from response headers in OpenShift Service Mesh
issue: - How to remove the response headers "server"?- Curl to a URL responds back with `"server"` response header. ~~~ HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8 content-length: 5290 server: istio-envoy date: Fri, 03 Nov 2023 14:47:52 GMT x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 479 set-cookie: fde6869b2fbef6be2c540d327634212f=cd083de152b12740b6503882acbb2d6b; path=/; HttpOnly cache-control: private ~~~
resolution: **NOTE: Configuring with EnvoyFilter is a fragile approach as it could easily break between releases.**- Configure the EnvoyFilter in the control plane namespace. ~~~ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 kind: EnvoyFilter metadata: name: removeserver spec: configPatches:- applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER match: listener: filterChain: filter: name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager patch: operation: MERGE value: typed_config: '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager server_name: ' ' ~~~ NOTE: Please check [this](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6972785) article for support of Envoy Filters with Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh.

Below, please find the versions of the (upstream) NFD Operand related to the Red Hat Node Feature Discovery Operator Version: | Node Feature Discovery Operator Version | Upstream NFD Operand Version | |-----------------------------------------|------------------------------| | v4.15 | v0.14.2 | | v4.14 | v0.13.1 | | v4.13 | v0.12.5 | | v4.12 | v0.10.1 | | v4.11 | v0.10.0 |

title: Pod stuck in ContainerCreating in a concrete node due to ovnkube-node-XXXX pod in CrashLoopBackoff in RHOCP4
issue: - `Pods` are stuck in `ContainerCreating` state in a concrete node.- The `RHOCP` Cluster Operators are degraded due to `node` being unstable or not able to deploy nodes. For example: ~~~ $ oc get co | egrep "dns|ingress|network|storage" dns 4.12.26 True True False 21d DNS "default" reports Progressing=True: "Have 8 available DNS pods, want 9." ingress 4.12.26 True True True 9d The "default" ingress controller reports Degraded=True: DegradedConditions: One or more other status conditions indicate a degraded state: DeploymentReplicasAllAvailable=False (DeploymentReplicasNotAvailable: 2/3 of replicas are available) network 4.12.26 True True True 21d DaemonSet "/openshift-ovn-kubernetes/ovnkube-node" rollout is not making progress- pod ovnkube-node-zff9z is in CrashLoopBackOff State... node-tuning 4.12.26 True True False 21d Waiting for 1/9 Profiles to be applied storage 4.12.26 True True False 15d VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRProgressing: VMwareVSphereDriverNodeServiceControllerProgressing: Waiting for DaemonSet to deploy node pods ~~~- The `ovnkube-node-XXXX` pod on the impacted node is in `CrashLoopBackoff` status.
resolution: **IMPORTANT NOTE: All the diagnostic steps in "Diagnostic Steps" section should get apply (if they don't, then this solution doesn't work)**.- Use below command to move the wrong file away on the `node`: ~~~ $ mv /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/ovs-if-br-ex* /root ~~~- Reboot the node: ~~~ $ reboot ~~~
root_cause: - During startup, the one-shot `ovs-configuration.service` systemd service unit runs a bash script that setups the required interfaces for OVN-Kubernetes. Most noticeable configuration is that it setups `br-ex` bridge (which bridges the `OVN` overlay with the physical interface) via `NetworkManager`commands.- Under some scenarios, there may be leftovers that may prevent this script from working properly. This solution explain how to clean one of these scenarios, so it is important to check "Diagnostic Steps" section to be sure if it applies.

title: CephFS MDSs are in CLBO due to rook-ceph-mgr-a being Unable to Perform Delete Ops - OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: Both MDSs enter an Error/CrashLoopBackOff state due to a failed `rook-ceph-mgr-a` delete operation. Most likely due to a database workload. ~~~ NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-a-9b68f854zbw9z 1/2 Running 5 5m30s rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-b-c7c87476b7gq6 1/2 Running 5 5m30s name: mds ready: false restartCount: 4 started: false state: waiting: message: back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=mds pod=rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-a-9b68f854zbw9z_openshift-storage(10c20d44-014b-4b62-b9e2-83df4a6d2177) reason: CrashLoopBackOff ~~~
resolution: 1. Stop the `ceph-mgr` daemon: `$ oc scale deployment-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-mgr-a--replicas=0` 2. Give ~5 minutes. Watch to see if MDS pods come back up/running. Monitor the pods with `$ oc get pods-n openshift-storage-w` 3. If the MDS pods come back up/running proceed to **Step 4**. If the MDS pods DO NOT come back up/running, try wiping the session In Accordance With (IAW) the steps outlined in the [ODF: MDS pods in CrashLoopBackOff (CLBO) and "EMetaBlob.replay" and "sessionmap" are in the traceback](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6994879). 4. Mount the Ceph File System with fuse or kernel driver- use the client.admin user. For example, steps 4 in the [OCS/ODF How to identify the PV cephfs associated to a damaged file reported by mds](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6991478) solution: ~~~ $ mkdir /mnt/cephfs $ mount-t ceph:/volumes /mnt/cephfs-o name=admin,secret=' ' ~~~ **Example:** ~~~ $ mount-t ceph 172.30.47.147:6789,172.30.152.29:6789,172.30.222.209:6789:/volumes /mnt/cephfs-o name=admin,secret='AQBadBNiOofgJhAA3umsBRuoiLi+yscG6FsRlA==' ~~~ 5. There should be directories/files in the `_deleting` directory that are stuck. `$ ls-l` the contents to view. 6. Run the following command to move the contents of `_deleting` to a new directory named `_deleting.tmp`: ~~~ $ mv /volumes/_deleting /volumes/_deleting.tmp ~~~ **Example:** ~~~ $ mv /mnt/cephfs/volumes/_deleting /mnt/cephfs/volumes/_deleting.tmp ~~~ 7. Scale up `rook-ceph-mgr-a` deployment: `$ oc scale deployment-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-mgr-a--replicas=1` **NOTE:** It may be necessary to engage Engineering on what to now do with the contents of `_deleting.tmp_.
root_cause: ~~~_deleting.tmp/b512666c-6edc-446d-85a2-4e175cb72c3b/903c95c5-a00b-47b5-b7cf-7a21d103cb6d/ directory, we can see the following: ~~~ The project named `dx` had the following contents: ~~~ backup_label.old global log pg_commit_ts pg_dynshmem pg_subtrans pg_wal pg_xact postgresql.conf <----- DATABASE WORKLOAD ~~~

title: Using JRE based image of RH-SSO instead of JDK
issue: - We are using RH-SSO installed over Openshift and looking to use RH-SSO image packaged with JRE instead of JDK. How can we achieve our requirement?
resolution: - In the upcoming RHBK 22 release of RH-SSO- the RH-SSO image will be built and packaged with `java-17-openjdk-headless` instead of `java-17-openjdk-devel`.- The [openjdk-headless](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5420581) package is the base package that includes JRE(Java Runtime Environment) and no developer tools.

title: Which pods are restarted/recreated during certificate renewal ?
issue: Which pods are restarted/recreated during renewal of cerificates?

`kube-apiserver`, `controller-manager`, `prometheus-adapter` and `route-controller-manager` pods are recreated and `kube-controller-manager- ` is restarted during certificate renewal, is this expected?
resolution: * The recreation of the `kube-apiserver `, `controller-manager`, `prometheus-adapter` and `route-controller-manager` pods as well as restart of `kube-controller-manager- ` is expected because in the first 24-hours certificates rotate after the cluster is installed, which is causing the pods to restart * Do not take an etcd backup before the first certificate rotation completes, which occurs 24 hours after installation, otherwise, the backup will contain expired certificates.
root_cause: * When installing OpenShift 4 clusters, a bootstrap certificate is created that is used on the control-plane nodes to create Certificate Signing Requests (CSRs) for kubelet client certificates (one for each kubelet) that will be used to identify each kubelet on any node. * The bootstrap certificate is only valid for 24 hours after cluster installation. After then, the `openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator` will issue a new certificate which is valid for 30 days. * The renewal process creates new certificates and CA bundles and will recreate the `kube-apiserver`, `controller-manager`, `prometheus-adapter` and `route-controller-manager` pods as well as restart `kube-controller-manager- `.

title: Unable to Install a RHOCP cluster on Red Hat Virtualization (RHV).
issue: - Cannot Deploy RHOCP version 4.14 over RHV.- Is it possible to install Red Hat Openshift container platform with version 4.14 over RHV.- Unable to Deploy cluster over RHV With latest Openshift Version release.
resolution: - Red Hat Virtualization (RHV) as a host platform for OpenShift Container Platform was deprecated and is no longer supported. This platform will be removed from OpenShift Container Platform in a future OpenShift Container Platform release.- Support for Installing RHV is deprecated as Introduced with [RHOCP 4.14](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes.html#ocp-4-14-rhv-deprecations).

title: Unable to restart kubelet service on OpenShift 4.x due to hanging process
issue: Node is in the NotReady state due to kubelet errors.
After following all the debugging present in this [article](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5873322) kubelet still will not restart.
In some cases the kubelet process could undergo an unclean shutdown as requested by systemd. In this case, systemd would believe the process to be stopped while it is not.
resolution: 1. Either connet to the node if you have SSH access or start a debug pod for the affected node **(admin access required):** ~~~ $ oc debug-t node/ ~~~ 2. Running: ~~~ $ systemctl status kubelet ~~~ Shows an inactive process. However, ~~~ $ ps-elf | grep kubelet ~~~ yields one or more results. 3. Forcefully kill the processes: ~~~ $ kill-9 ~~~ 4. Attempt a restart of the kubelet service: ~~~ $ systemctl start kubelet ~~~
root_cause: * Unclean Shutdown. * Orphaned Process.

title: Understanding OpenShift Storage Availability (as a developer)
issue: - How many storage classes does my cluster have configured for me to use (as a developer)?- What is my cluster's default storage class?
resolution: You can list your storage classes by running: ``` $ oc get storageclasss ```- **Note**: The default storage class should be denoted with `(default)`
root_cause: There are other ways to (using `oc` or `kubectl` to get/list the default storage class. These methods leverage looking up the [default storage class by looking up the `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` annotation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/change-default-storage-class/) on the storage class object[s], and using a `oc` or `kubectl` output format ([jsonpath](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubectl/jsonpath/) (in the example)) to parse out the data points you want to see. ``` $ oc get sc-o jsonpath='{.items[?(@.metadata.annotations.storageclass\.kubernetes\.io\/is-default-class)].metadata.name} ``` The same thing can also be done; by passing the output of the storage class object[s] to `jq`: ``` $ oc get sc-o json | jq '.items[] | select (.metadata.annotations."storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class")' ```

title: How to get which subscriptions are required to enable Red Hat Operators in OpenShift Container Platform 4.
issue: - To view the subscriptions required to enable Red Hat Operators in the command line.- How to understand which subscription is required for any specific operator provided by Red Hat.- Third party provider operators are not related to this use case as each subscription and method depend on the respective vendor.
resolution:
**Note: Third-party operator's subscription might not be labeled. This is depending on the third party provider vendors side as those are not provided by Red Hat.** 1. To view subscriptions required to enable operators, gather the following information: ~~~ $ oc get packagemanifests | grep "Red Hat Operators" $ oc get packagemanifests-o jsonpath='{range.items[*].status.channels[*]}{.currentCSVDesc.displayName}{": "}{.currentCSVDesc.annotations.operators\.openshift\.io/valid-subscription}{"
"}{end}'|awk '$0~/\[/ {print $0}'| grep-i $ oc get packagemanifests-o jsonpath='{range.items[*].status.channels[*]}{.currentCSVDesc.displayName}{": "}{.currentCSVDesc.annotations.operators\.openshift\.io/valid-subscription}{"
"}{end}'|awk '$0~/\[/ {print $0}'| grep-i *Example: For OpenShift Data Foundation, the subscriptions that are enabling the operator are OpenShift Platform Plus, OpenShift Data Foundation Essentials or OpenShift Data Foundation Advanced: $ oc get packagemanifests-o jsonpath='{range.items[*].status.channels[*]}{.currentCSVDesc.displayName}{": "}{.currentCSVDesc.annotations.operators\.openshift\.io/valid-subscription}{"
"}{end}'|awk '$0~/\[/ {print $0}'| grep-i "Data Foundation" OpenShift Data Foundation: ["OpenShift Platform Plus","OpenShift Data Foundation Essentials","OpenShift Data Foundation Advanced"] OpenShift Data Foundation: ["OpenShift Platform Plus","OpenShift Data Foundation Essentials","OpenShift Data Foundation Advanced"]* **OpenShift Data Foundation: ["OpenShift Platform Plus","OpenShift Data Foundation Essentials","OpenShift Data Foundation Advanced"]** ~~~ 2. To view the installed operator's subscription requirement, it is needed to list the following `ClusterServiceVersion`: ~~~ $ oc get clusterserviceversion-A $ oc get clusterserviceversion cluster-logging.v5.8.0-n openshift-operators-o json | jq '.metadata.annotations."operators.openshift.io/valid-subscription"' *Example: For the Logging Operator, it is included on OKE, OCP and OCP Plus subscriptions. $ oc get clusterserviceversion cluster-logging.v5.8.0-n openshift-operators-o json | jq '.metadata.annotations."operators.openshift.io/valid-subscription"'* **"["OpenShift Kubernetes Engine", "OpenShift Container Platform", "OpenShift Platform Plus"]"** ~~~

title: Cluster operator image-registry degraded in multiple availability zones not supported region
issue: - Cluster operator image-registry due to one of image-registry pod in pending status with following warning: ~~~ 0/9 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints (missing required label), 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/dev:}, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master:}, 5 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints. preemption: 0/9 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints, 6 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling. ~~~
resolution: **Step 1** Scale-up the machine set to create new machines which will be added to the availability set and at least 1 of them will be assigned the faultDomain of `1` resulting in one of them having the missing `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` of `1` allowing the pod to be scheduled. **Step 2** Delete the old machines to make sure that the only workers left around are part of the availabilitySet. **Step 3** Scale-down the machineset back.
root_cause: - In clusters that are Installed from OpenShift v4.10 onwards in a region with a single availability zone, the `cluster-api-azure plugin` in the machine-api controller will set one worker to have a `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` of "0" and another to "1"- This happens because the machines that are added to the machineset are automatically added to an availabilitySet.- The issue is that in clusters created prior to OpenShift v4.10, the existing nodes in the machineset haven't been deleted/recreated to be added to an availability zone. This means the only nodes that these pods can be scheduled on all have `topology.kubernetes.io/zone: 0`.

title: Pods aren't getting mounted on worker nodes due to "Unable to attach or mount volumes" error
issue: - All hpe-nfs-xxxxx-xxxx pods aren't getting mounted on worker nodes due to `Unable to attach or mount volumes` error- `df` hangs on all the worker nodes and there are defunct `mount.ntfs4` processes.
resolution: - Rebooting the affected worker node deletes all the defunct processes and thus solves the volume mount issue- As `hpe-csi-driver` is a third-party operator that is not directly supported by Red Hat, Customers are advised to raise a support case with the storage provider and discuss further about the permanent resolution of the issue.
root_cause: - Every hpe-nfs-xxxxx-xxxx pod has a PersistentVolmeClaim(PVC) configured with the storage provisioner `csi.hpe.com`. This PVC isn't able to mount correctly. It is likely that the PVC was not unmounted from the previous worker node after the hpe-nfs-xxxxx-xxxx pod got rescheduled to the affected worker node.

title: Unexpected deploymentconfig rolling update behavior with ConfigChange trigger
issue: - After a DeploymentConfig update, applied by ArgoCD, the triggered rollout terminated an unexpected number of pods- Consider the following scenario:- The value of maxReplicas is defined in the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)- Before the rollout 10 pods were active- As soon as the rollout started Openshift scaled the number of pods to 3 pod active. Therefore deleting 7 pods
resolution: - Set the `spec.ignoreDifferences` and the `RespectIgnoreDifferences=true` sync option in the ArgoCD Application manifest like in the following example: ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: Application spec: ignoreDifferences:- group: "apps" kind: "Deployment" jsonPointers:- /spec/replicas syncPolicy: syncOptions:- RespectIgnoreDifferences=true ~~~- The patch applied by ArgoCD is calculated using a 3-way-merge between the live state the desired state and the last-applied-configuration annotation- The sync option is used to enable ArgoCD to consider the configurations made in the `spec.ignoreDifferences` attribute also during the sync stage- **Note:**- If the Application is being created and no live state exists, the desired state is applied as-is- DeploymentConfig and ReplicationController are deprecated starting from OCP 4.14 and in future OCP version they will be removed
root_cause: - This is the expected behavior for DeploymentConfig with ConfigChange trigger- For Deployment objects the flow is different because the advice is to remove the replicas field from the deployment manifest- Removing the replicas field from DeploymentConfig is equal to write `replicas: 0`

title: How to check the NotReady transition for the RHOCP nodes
issue: - Sometimes a node goes into 'NotReady' state and comes back automatically to 'Ready' state but age of the node/uptime doesn't get change.
resolution: The following command can be use to display the transition times: ``` $ oc get nodes-o json | jq-r '"NODE|Ready|lastTransitionTime",(.items[] | "\(.metadata.name)|\(.status.conditions[] | select(.type == "Ready") |.status + "|" +.lastTransitionTime)")' | column-s'|'-t ``` This should provide an output like this: ``` $ oc get nodes-o json | jq-r '"NODE|Ready|lastTransitionTime",(.items[] | "\(.metadata.name)|\(.status.conditions[] | select(.type == "Ready") |.status + "|" +.lastTransitionTime)")' | column-s'|'-t NODE Ready lastTransitionTime master-0 True 2023-11-05T20:04:39Z master-1 True 2023-11-05T20:04:38Z master-2 True 2023-11-05T20:04:39Z worker-0 True 2023-11-05T20:14:13Z worker-1 True 2023-11-05T20:14:33Z worker-2 True 2023-11-05T20:14:23Z ```
root_cause: The command `oc get nodes` provides with a summary about the node, including the AGE field. But this field is based on the `.metadata.creationTimestamp` to reflect the data of creation of the node, **not the date of transitions** as shown in the command `oc get co`.

title: Unable to view machineset  resource utilization in RHOCP4
issue: - The `MachineSet` CPU & Memory utilization is not visible in `Openshift Console`.
resolution: - Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-19916](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-19916) and delivered a fix in `OCP version 4.15.0` through errata [RHSA-2023:7198](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7198). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: - The Openshift Console assumes that `Machines` managed by a `MachineSet` have a **machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machineset** label matching with `MachineSet's` name. The `MachineSet` which is not showing `CPU and Memory` utilization has a mismatched `label selector` in the `spec`, because of which, the console is unable to calculate related `Machine` utilization for `MachineSet`.

title: DG 8 URL checker
issue: How to verify DG 8 URL status working?
resolution: ### Scenarios In some cases the DG pod might not be responding to (external) requests, possible culprits are: a- the java application is not responding b- the network (as in the way to access the DG container inside Pod) is the culprit Therefore if we deploy a script that pings from within the pod inside the container to remove the network from the equate (culprit b) above. The `url_check.sh` should be deployed inside the same container (`$ oc cp url_check.sh CR-podname-id:/opt/infinispan`) and it should continue pinging, when there is an issue it will output the timestamp. ### url_check.sh Use the following script for testing DG 8 curl inside a pod (in the same DG 8 container): ~~~ $ cat ~/bin/url_check.sh #! /bin/bash set-x URL=$1 # Example: http://localhost:11223/rest/v2/cache-managers/default/health/status counter=0 while true; do rc=0 curl-s $URL-o /tmp/url.out rc=$? if [[$rc-eq 0]]; then if $(grep-vq HEALTHY /tmp/url.out); then counter=$(($counter + 1)) echo "$(date-Ins-u): $counter" > > /tmp/ping.out fi else echo "curl failed with $rc" exit 1 fi sleep 5 done ~~~ ### API return for HEALTHY The `HEALTHY` is not the desired output, given that's the return from API. And `ping.out` is what you would want to check to see the status of the pings. Example: ~~~ sh-4.4$ cat /tmp/ping.out 2023-11-08T22:49:36,119221775+00:00: 1 2023-11-08T22:49:54,366100340+00:00: 1 2023-11-08T22:49:59,379095857+00:00: 2 2023-11-08T22:50:04,393154771+00:00: 3 2023-11-08T22:50:09,405962177+00:00: 4 ~~~

title: OCP install on GCP using the shared vpc method fails
issue: - While installing an OCP 4.13 cluster on GCP using the [shared install method](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/installing_gcp/installing-gcp-shared-vpc.html), the bootstrap process in unable to reach the API and API-INT urls.- Control plane machines cannot access internet.
resolution: - Creating a cloud NAT resource in GCP host project attached to the shared VPC solves the issue.
root_cause: - Providing a public IP to the master nodes enables the successful execution of the curl command to external resources.- This observation leads to the conclusion that implementing a Cloud NAT configuration is required to facilitate internet access for the master nodes, resolving the connectivity issue effectively.

title: Enable resource limits and requests for s2i BuildConfig in RHOCP 4
issue: Setting resource limits in OpenShift BuildConfig is essential:- For resource-intensive builds.- In shared/multi-tenant environments.- Ensures stability and predictability.- Ensures compliance with namespace quotas.
resolution: By default, pods complete builds using available resources like memory and CPU, which can be restricted. Here are two methods to limit resource usage: 1. Define resource limitations in the default container limits of a project to restrict resource utilization. 2. Specify resource limits within the build configuration. In the given example, both the 'cpu' and 'memory' parameters are optional: ``` apiVersion: "v1" kind: "BuildConfig" metadata: name: "sample-build" spec: resources: limits: cpu: "100m" 1 memory: "256Mi" 2 ``` 1. CPU is measured in CPU units, where "100m" signifies 0.1 CPU units (100 * 1e-3). 2. Memory is measured in bytes, where "256Mi" represents 268435456 bytes (256 * 2 ^ 20). However, if a quota is set for the project, one of the following is necessary: 1. Define a resources section with explicit requests: ``` resources: requests: cpu: "100m" memory: "256Mi" ``` The requests object contains the resources corresponding to those in the quota. 2. Have a limit range defined in the project, where defaults from the LimitRange object apply to pods created during the build process. Failure to meet quota requirements will result in build pod creation failure, prompting a quota satisfaction failure.

title: How to tag ARO resources using Azure policy?
issue: - How to use Azure Policy to tag the resources in an ARO cluster's resource group?- How to tag ARO resources after the cluster is created?- How to define tags in ARO for grouping resources and for managing resource access and cost?- Azure policy requirements reject the resource provision operation if the Azure tags are not declared at the time of resource provision.
resolution: - The [doc](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-tag-resources) shows how to use Azure Policy to tag the resources in an ARO cluster's resource group at the time of installing a new cluster.- To tag resources in an existing cluster, find the name of the managed resource group and apply the policy to the existing managed resource group. There is no need to install a new cluster to tag resources.- The Azure policy tagging features will tag any resource that is deployed in the managed resource group. This would include any resource that supports having a tag associated with it.

title: Is it possible to configure Kafka brokers on an OpenShift cluster to connect to external Zookeeper cluster not on the OpenShift cluster
issue: - Is it possible to configure Kafka brokers on an OpenShift cluster to connect to external Zookeeper cluster not on the OpenShift cluster
resolution: - Unfortunately, "AMQ Streams on OpenShift" works on only a single OpenShift cluster, then no such zookeeper connection configuration is provided, "AMQ Streams on OpenShift" cannot connect to an "external" Zookeeper cluster.- As another workaround, instead of "AMQ Streams on OpenShift", you can also use "AMQ Streams on RHEL". In this case, however, it would not benefit from the automation features provided by the AMQ Streams operators.

title: Log forwarding to Splunk not working in logging 5.8.z in RHOCP 4
issue: - `Splunk` log forwarding not working after upgrading `OpenShift Logging Operator` to version `5.8.0`- Unable to forward logs to `Splunk`.
resolution: - To address this issue, kindly `enable TLS 1.3 support` on the TLS terminating load balancer in front of the `Splunk HEC (HTTP Event Collector) endpoint`.- `Splunk` is a third-party system and this should be configured from the `Splunk` end.
root_cause: - The problem arises while transitioning from `OpenSSL 1.1.1 to version 3.0.7`.- In the newer version, there is a default behavior change, where connections to `TLS 1.2` endpoints are rejected if they do not expose the [RFC 5746](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5746) extension.
