title: Persistent Volume Claim shared with other namespaces
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Can Persistent Volume Claim share with other namespaces?- Would like to share PVCs across multiple namespaces.
resolution: PVCs are specific to a project and are created and used by developers as a means to use a PV. PV resources on their own are not scoped to any single project; they can be shared across the entire OpenShift Container Platform cluster and claimed from any project. After a PV is bound to a PVC, that PV can not then be bound to additional PVCs. This has the effect of scoping a bound PV to a single namespace, that of the binding project [Persistent storage overview](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/storage/understanding-persistent-storage.html#persistent-storage-overview_understanding-persistent-storage) In conclusion, the approach of using PVCs (or PVs) across multiple namespaces is not supported. Instead, you can try to configure the NFS volume at pod (or deployment) level as this example: ~~~ kind: Pod apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: example-nfs namespace: example spec: volumes:- name: nfs-volume nfs: server: SERVER_IP path: / containers:- name: app image: alpine volumeMounts:- name: nfs-volume mountPath: /tmp/nfs ~~~

title: How to limit the size of a NFS volume provisioned to RHOCP?
issue: - Does expanding the file system on the Network File System (NFS) server mean that more storage space becomes available without any changes in RHOCP?- When using local NFS, what is the purpose of Persistent Volumes (PV) `spec: capacity: storage`?- What the meaning of storage parameter specifications, when the NFS server file system is defined as PV?
resolution: - Disk partitions can be used to [enforce disk quotas and size constraints](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/storage/persistent_storage/persistent-storage-nfs.html#nfs-enforcing-disk-quota_persistent-storage-nfs) while using NFS volumes.- Changes done to an NFS file system exported to a Red Hat Openshift cluster don't necessitate any alterations in RHOCP to be effective.- Neither `spec: capacity: storage` in PV nor `spec: resources: requests: storage` in Persistent Volume Claims (PVC) will limit the size of the volume provided. As PVCs can request specific [storage capacity](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/storage/understanding-persistent-storage.html#pv-capacity_understanding-persistent-storage), Red Hat Openshift has to know the size of each PV to match a PVC with the best possible PV.- The capacity value specified in the PV manifest `spec: capacity: storage` represents the requested storage capacity for the PV. In the context of using a locally exported file system from an NFS server, this value only serve as a PV description.

title: How to execute strace or ptrace inside RHOCP 4 pod
issue: - How to allow SYS_PTRACE capability.- Is it possible to execute `strace` or `ptrace` in a container?- Executing `ptrace` in a container returns: ~~~ ptrace Operation not permitted ~~~
resolution: 1. Create the Service Account: ~~~ $ oc create sa ptrace-sa-n ~~~ 2. Create the new SecurityContextConstraints allowing the `SYS_PTRACE` capability: $ cat < < EOF | oc create-f- allowHostDirVolumePlugin: false allowHostIPC: false allowHostNetwork: false allowHostPID: false allowHostPorts: false allowPrivilegeEscalation: true allowPrivilegedContainer: false allowedCapabilities:- SYS_PTRACE apiVersion: security.openshift.io/v1 defaultAddCapabilities: null fsGroup: type: MustRunAs groups: [] kind: SecurityContextConstraints metadata: name: ptrace-scc priority: null readOnlyRootFilesystem: false requiredDropCapabilities:- KILL- MKNOD- SETUID- SETGID runAsUser: type: MustRunAsRange seLinuxContext: type: MustRunAs supplementalGroups: type: RunAsAny users: [] volumes:- configMap- downwardAPI- emptyDir- ephemeral- persistentVolumeClaim- projected- secret EOF **Note:** This SCC is cloned from the restricted SCC depending on the application further configurations might be required. 3. Assign the newly created SecurityContextConstraints to the Service Account: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user ptrace-scc-z ptrace-sa-n ~~~ 4. Change the deployment to use the new Service Account and for adding the `SYS_PTRACE` capability to the container: ~~~ $ DEPLOY= $ NS= $ CONTAINER= $ CONTAINER_IMAGE= $ oc patch deploy ${DEPLOY}-n ${NS}--type merge-p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers":[{"name":"'${CONTAINER}'", "image":"'${CONTAINER_IMAGE}'", "securityContext": {"capabilities":{"add":["SYS_PTRACE"]}}}], "serviceAccount":"ptrace-sa"}}}}' ~~~ 5. *Optional:* The change is expected to trigger a new rollout, if not triggered, manually scale down/up the deployment: ~~~ $ oc scale deploy ${DEPLOY}-n ${NS}--replicas 0 $ oc scale deploy ${DEPLOY}-n ${NS}--replicas 1 ~~~
root_cause: - `SYS_PTRACE` capability is not allowed by default.- For executing `strace` or `ptrace` in a container is necessary to grant the `SYS_PTRACE` capability.

title: Does OpenShift 4 provide a time-based autoscaler?
issue: - Is any time-based autoscaler for pods available in OpenShift 4?- Users want to apply time-based autoscaling for pods through HPA.- How to apply autoscaling at specific time.- Is it possible to use the `cron` trigger from KEDA in OpenShift 4?
resolution: Openshift Container Platform provides the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) that support CPU utilization and memory utilization metrics, but no time-based option is allowed. There is a RFE created for supporting the KEDA `cron` trigger in the Custom Metrics Autoscaler (CMA): [Support cron trigger for KEDA in Custom Metrics Autoscaler](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4173). ####Workaround It is currently possible to use `cronjobs` for adjusting replicas of pods. These are examples of `cronjobs` that adjust `minReplicas` value of a HPA (note: users are responsible to configure the `cronjob` tasks): ~~~ 1. create RBAC for hpa scaling in cronjob-hpa-scaler-test namespace // create a serviceaccount for running cronjob----- apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: hpa-cron-runner namespace: conjob-hpa-scaler-test // create ClusterRole for running hpa----- kind: ClusterRole apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: namespace: cronjob-hpa-scaler-test name: hpa-cron-runner rules:- apiGroups: ["autoscaling"] resources: ["horizontalpodautoscalers"] verbs: ["patch", "get"] // role binding to service account----- kind: ClusterRoleBinding apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: hpa-cron-runner namespace: cronjob-hpa-scaler-test subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: hpa-cron-runner namespace: cronjob-hpa-scaler-test roleRef: kind: ClusterRole name: hpa-cron-runner apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io 2. Create cronjob-hpa-scale-up cronjob * OpenShift CLI Client 4.11 image https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/openshift4/ose-cli/5cd9ba3f5a13467289f4d51d?architecture=amd64&image=652951ad9be3782228dc60eb $ oc import-image openshift4/ose-cli:v4.11.0-202310131344.p0.g3470d04.assembly.stream--from=registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-cli:v4.11.0-202310131344.p0.g3470d04.assembly.stream--confirm $ oc get is NAME IMAGE REPOSITORY TAGS UPDATED ose-cli image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/cronjob-hpa-scaler-test/ose-cli v4.11.0-202310131344.p0.g3470d04.assembly.stream 3 hours ago $ oc create-f cronjob-hpa-scale-up.yaml // set minReplicas as 4 for test hpa every 2 a.m----- apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: CronJob metadata: name: hpa-scale-up spec: schedule: "0 2 * * *" concurrencyPolicy: "Replace" startingDeadlineSeconds: 200 suspend: false successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3 failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1 jobTemplate: spec: template: spec: serviceAccountName: hpa-cron-runner containers:- name: hpa-scale-up image: registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-cli // oc cli image command:- /bin/sh--c- oc patch hpa test--patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}' restartPolicy: OnFailure 3. Create cronjob-hpa-scale-down cronjob pod $oc create-f cronjob-hpa-scale-down.yaml // set minReplicas as 6 for test hpa in every 6 a.m----- apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: CronJob metadata: name: hpa-scale-down spec: schedule: "0 6 * * *" concurrencyPolicy: "Replace" startingDeadlineSeconds: 200 suspend: false successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3 failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1 jobTemplate: spec: template: spec: serviceAccountName: hpa-cron-runner containers:- name: hpa-scale-down image: registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-cli command:- /bin/sh--c- oc patch hpa test--patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}' restartPolicy: OnFailure ~~~
root_cause: Openshift Container Platform provides the [Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-autoscaling.html) which is a resource utilization-based autoscaler, but no time-based option is allowed. Refer to the [Supported metrics](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-autoscaling.html#supported-metrics) for additional information.

title: How to change project in MicroShift?
issue: - How to change project/namespace in the MicroShift?- When running "oc project default" the error is shown: ~~~ # oc project default error: unable to default to a user name: the server could not find the requested resource (get users.user.openshift.io ~) ~~~
resolution: Changing projects requires APIs `user.openshift.io` and `project.openshift.io`. MicroShift doesn't not include those APIs, therefore the OpenShift approach to changing the projects doesn't work on MicroShift. Instead, the Kubernetes approach is needed. The Kubernetes also does not include the `project.openshift.io` API, but it can change the namespace in your kubeconfig. You can change the namespace running the following command. ~~~ # oc config set-context--current--namespace=default Context "microshift" modified. ~~~ Additionally, an `alias` can be added to the machine: ~~~ # alias oc-project='oc config set-context--current--namespace ' # oc-project default Context "microshift" modified. ~~~ For checking the current namespace, admins can run `oc project`. ~~~ # oc project Using project "default" from context named "microshift" on server "https://localhost:6443". ~~~
root_cause: Due to the nature of MicroShift being lightweight, many OpenShift APIs are not included. To list all the objects and APIs in MicroShift. ~~~ # oc api-resources | grep-e "openshift.io" routes route.openshift.io/v1 true Route rangeallocations security.internal.openshift.io/v1 false RangeAllocation securitycontextconstraints scc security.openshift.io/v1 false SecurityContextConstraints ~~~ ~~~ # oc get apiservice | grep "openshift.io" v1.route.openshift.io Local True 190d v1.security.internal.openshift.io Local True 190d v1.security.openshift.io Local True 320d ~~~

title: MetalLb Operator failed to calling webhook "lb-admission-hook.tools.svc.cluster.local"
issue: - MetalLb Operator failed calling webhook "lb-admission-hook.tools.svc.cluster.local"- Upgrading the Metallb operator failed ~~~ 3h25m Warning InstallComponentFailed clusterserviceversion/metallb-operator.4.12.0-202310241244 install strategy failed: could not create service metallb-operator-controller-manager-service: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "lb-admission-hook.tools.svc.cluster.local": failed to call webhook: Post "https://lb-admission-hook.tools.svc:443/?timeout=5s": context deadline exceeded 4h30m Warning InstallComponentFailed clusterserviceversion/metallb-operator.4.12.0-202310241244 install strategy failed: service metallb-operator-webhook-server-service not safe to replace: extraneous ownerreferences found ~~~
resolution: Follow the below steps to resolve the issue. 1. Save the AddressPool configuration for recreate it: ~~~ $ oc get addresspool-n metallb-system-o yaml > addresspool.yaml ~~~ 2. Remove all the AddressPool: ~~~ $ oc delete addresspool-n metallb-system--all ~~~ 3. Remove all the MetalLB CSVs in the metallb-system namespace: ~~~ $ oc delete csv-n metallb-system metallb-operator. metallb-operator. ~~~ 4. Remove the latest created install plan related to MetalLB: ~~~ $ oc delete ip-n metallb-system ~~~ **Note:** *If the installPlanApproval of the Subscription is set to Manual, the new install plan must be approved after this action.* 5. Wait for the Operator Lifecycle Manager to complete the upgrade by monitoring with the following command, until the newly generated CSV reaches the Succeeded status: ~~~ $ watch oc get csv,ip-n metallb-system ~~~ 6. Re-create the AddressPool starting from the backup executed in step 1. ~~~ $ oc create-f ~~~

title: APIcast log timestamps are not with millisecond precision
issue: - In the APIcast access log the timestamp is of the form ([13/Aug/2021:10:00:40 +0000]). The time seems to be rounded to second values and yet the access log always prints +0000 instead of milliseconds.- How can timestamps be logged with millisecond precision for API calls that take milliseconds?- Is there a variable in the access log that can provide a timestamp with millisecond precision in human readable format?
resolution: ### Timestamp format and precision In the APIcast access logs, log statements start with a timestamp in the format ~~~ [13/Aug/2021:10:00:40 +0000] ~~~ **+0000** is not milliseconds part of the timestamp itself. It is in fact a UTC offset in the form of HHMM (hours and mins). **13/Aug/2021:10:00:40 +0000** is the value of nginx variable **$time_local**. $time_local value is the local time in Common Log Format and consists of date:time and timezone.- date:time is logged with seconds precision.- timezone is represented as an offset from UTC. in this case it is +0000 (0 hours and 0 mins offset from UTC). ### How to log millisecond precision timestamps 2 steps are required to achieve this.- [Inject a custom environment](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html/installing_3scale/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#injecting-custom-environments-with-the-threescale-operator) via the 3scale operator. This can be done by modifying the default configuration declared in the [production.lua](https://github.com/3scale/APIcast/blob/4bd6d46629f97fd93231247fa0926fa9dc040051/gateway/config/production.lua#L6) file with the following directive: `timer_resolution = 1ms;`- [Logging policy](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_policies#logging) can be used to customize the access logs. For example in [Enabling custom access log](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_policies#examples-of-the-logging-policy) example, the following variables would be the first configuration setting required: ~~~ "custom_logging": "[{{time_local}}] [{{msec}}]... rest omitted " ~~~ With both of the above steps completed the following would be logged: ~~~ [16/Aug/2021:18:27:19 +0000] [1629138439.381]... rest of log omitted " ~~~ $msec is the Epoch (Unix) time with millisecond precision. The integer part of the the $msec (162913843 in this example) is the same as 16/Aug/2021:18:27:19. And 381 is the time in milliseconds. **It is the only variable that provides the timestamp with millisecond precision in Nginx**. ### Timestamps logged with millisecond precision in human-readable format This is not possible in APIcast because it is built on top of OpenResty which is based on Nginx that does not provide such a setting. Therefore this is a limitation of the base technology and not APIcast.
root_cause: **By default** it is not possible to log timestamps in the APIcast access logs with millisecond precision. This is due to the fact APIcast is configured to resolve the clock time every 100ms. Therefore using the nginx variable `$msec` **alone** will not be enough as can be seen in the_"Diagnostic Steps"_ section. Steps on how to configure this are documented in the_"Resolution section"_ above and a request to add this to the official documentation has been opened [here](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-10380)

title: How to manage a customized catalog of operators in OpenShift disconnected environment
issue: - The user is currently running `Openshift 4.10.39` in disconnected mode and has a custom catalog of operators in `SQLite` format. They are planning to migrate to `Openshift 4.12.15` while maintaining a custom operator catalog but are facing challenges due to the deprecation of the SQLite format. They want to transition to a file-based catalog model but find the documentation insufficient. Specifically, they are seeking guidance on the methodology to create a custom catalog in the file-based mode and how to handle the large file size generated by the "opm render" command. Additionally, they inquire about integrating new operators in future updates.
resolution: - A solution would be to use `oc mirror` to create an `ImageSetConfiguration` including only a subset of your custom operators.- A set of ImageSetConfiguration file examples show the configuration for various mirroring use cases. #### Use case: Including the shortest OpenShift Container Platform update path ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: local: path: /home/user/metadata mirror: platform: channels`:- name: stable-4.12 minVersion: 4.11.37 maxVersion: 4.12.15 shortestPath: true ~~~ #### Use case: Including all versions of OpenShift Container Platform from a minimum to the latest version for multi-architecture releases ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL: example.com/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: platform: architectures:- "multi" channels:- name: stable-4.13 minVersion: 4.13.4 maxVersion: 4.13.6 ~~~ #### Use case: Including the Nutanix CSI Operator ~~~ kind: ImageSetConfiguration apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 storageConfig: registry: imageURL: mylocalregistry/ocp-mirror/openshift4 skipTLS: false mirror: platform: channels:- name: stable-4.11 type: ocp graph: true operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/certified-operator-index:v4.11 packages:- name: nutanixcsioperator channels:- name: stable additionalImages:- name: registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest ~~~

title: How to enable logging  Red Hat Tomcat images?
issue: - How to enable logging Red Hat Tomcat images?
resolution: - To reduce the disk space by default in the JBoss Web Server images there is only ConsoleHandler is enabled. **Default logging.properties:** ~~~ handlers = java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler.handlers = java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler.level = FINE java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler.formatter = org.apache.juli.OneLineFormatter ~~~ To enable the required logging add the required Handler inside the logging.properties. **Example Dockerfile:** ~~~ FROM registry.redhat.io/jboss-webserver-5/jws57-openjdk11-openshift-rhel8 USER root COPY logging.properties /opt/jws-5.7/tomcat/conf/ CMD ["/opt/jws-5.7/tomcat/bin/launch.sh"] ~~~ Get the tomcat [certified container images](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/search?gs&q=tomcat)

title: Descheduler pods OOM-killed on big clusters
issue: Descheduler pods [being killed by Out-of-Memory Killer](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5788651) on clusters and nodes with enough [allocatable memory](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6752811).
resolution: The issue was fixed for OpenShift Container Platform 4.14.0: [OCPBUGS-1995](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-1995). [The limits were removed](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-kube-descheduler-operator/pull/295/files).
root_cause: [Limits of Descheduler pods are hardcoded](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-kube-descheduler-operator/blob/release-4.13/bindata/assets/kube-descheduler/deployment.yaml#L41-L43). The problem is more likely to occur on large clusters because there is a dependency between the memory used by these pods and the size of the cluster.

title: How to check OpenShift routes skipping the Load Balancer
issue: An OpenShift route is not available.
resolution: Sometimes the external `Load Balancer` is not working correctly or is not correctly configured. To check if there is an issue with the external `Load Balancer`, the route can be checked performing the query directly to OpenShift router pods: 1- Check OpenShift ingress pods IPs: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-ingress-o wide ~~~ 2- Connect to any OpenShift pod, for example a console pod: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-console $ oc rsh-n openshift-console ~~~ 3- Check the route from the console pod by connecting to each router pod: ~~~ # curl-kvvv https://--resolve:443: ~~~ This example shows how to check the `oauth` route: ~~~ # curl-kvvv https://oauth-openshift.apps. /healthz--resolve oauth-openshift.apps.:443: ~~~
root_cause: The external Load Balancer is not correctly configured.

title: ODF stretch cluster - rook-ceph-osd-prepare pods going in to pending state, why?
issue: - osd prepare pods are going in pending state in a streched cluster. ~~~ rook-ceph-osd-prepare-49bf4b9b8d43ad3e67ef907aef0afb01-4f8f6 0/1 Pending 0 2h9m rook-ceph-osd-prepare-4d16307110ba4a096f9314bae612a7e9-vbhc9 0/1 Pending 0 2h9m rook-ceph-osd-prepare-503d3afa64d1a97f8b259285ae779f37-22tp2 0/1 Pending 0 2h9m rook-ceph-osd-prepare-5350221a610fa33dc16df6e8319577fc-fh2ck 0/1 Pending 0 2h9m ~~~
resolution: - Make sure that all storage nodes are having appropriate label and arbiter node shouldn't have the `cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage` label applied: ~~~ # oc label node arbiter_node_name cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage- ~~~
root_cause: - As per the CephCluster CR, with four storageClassDeviceSets that are intended to spread the OSDs across the two zones for OSDs.- For this topology spread constraint to be valid, it will require that only the nodes in defined zones have the node label `cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage`.- If the arbiter node also has the label `cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage` applied, the TSC will appear imbalanced because no OSDs are placed in the arbiter zone.

title: How change the coredump location in Openshift Container Platform 4
issue: - Users require the ability to change the default location and pattern of core dumps in an OpenShift environment
resolution: - To change the core dump location in OpenShift, create and apply a `MachineConfig` that alters the `kernel.core_pattern` parameter. This parameter directs core dumps to a specified pod location with a defined pattern.- Create a `MachineConfig` configuration file `99-change-core-pattern.yaml` with the content: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: name: 99-change-core-pattern labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker # or master, depending on which nodes you want to apply this to spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 # Replace with the version compatible with your OpenShift version storage: files:- path: /etc/sysctl.d/99-core-pattern.conf contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,a2VybmVsLmNvcmVfcGF0dGVybj1jb3JlLiVFLiVlLiVwLiV0 filesystem: root mode: 0420 ~~~ **Note**: The source includes a base64-encoded string for `kernel.core_pattern=core.%E.%e.%p.%t`. Change `kernel.core_pattern` variable according to your requirements. If a non-persistent directory is used, any core dumps stored there will be lost if the pod is restarted, rescheduled, or deleted. To ensure that core dumps are retained across pod restarts and lifecycle changes, configure the pods to use a persistent storage.- Apply the `MachineConfig` created ~~~ $ oc apply-f 99-change-core-pattern.yaml ~~~- When this change is implemented through a `MachineConfig`, all nodes receiving this update will automatically restart to incorporate the modification- Verify the `MachineConfig` application and node status ~~~ $ oc get machineconfigpool $ oc get nodes ~~~- After node reboots, verify the new configuration using ~~~ $ oc debug node/worker-0 $ chroot /host $ cat /etc/sysctl.d/99-core-pattern.conf kernel.core_pattern = core.%E.%e.%p.%t $ cat /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern core.%E.%e.%p.%t ~~~- Create a test scenario that generates a core dump and verify its location and naming pattern according to the new configuration ~~~ $ oc rsh $ cd /tmp; sleep 3600 & $ kill-11 %1; ls /tmp/core* total 80-rw------- 1 10008500 root 217088 Nov 14 20:41 core.!bin!busybox.sleep.28.1699994472 ~~~
root_cause: In OpenShift Container Platform, the default configuration for handling core dumps is managed by `systemd-coredump`. By default, `systemd-coredump` processes and stores core dumps using a pattern defined by the `kernel.core_pattern` parameter, which is typically set to pipe core dumps to the `systemd-coredump` binary `(|/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-coredump %P %u %g %s %t %c %h %e`) and the core files are normally located in `/var/lib/systemd/coredump`.

title: Gitlab operator is missing from OperatorHub in OpenShift 4.13

title: Error in namespaces: Expected device to be attached but was attaching for AWS m5.8xlarge and c5a.4xlarge instances in RHOCP 4
issue: - Getting below error in multiple namespaces after upgrading the cluster to 4.12.46 ~~~ oc get ev-A | grep-F "expected device to be attached but was attaching" test-ocp 4m22s Warning FailedAttachVolume pod/abc AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-xyz": rpc error: code = Internal desc = Could not attach volume "vol-abc" to node "i-123": attachment of disk "vol-456" failed, expected device to be attached but was attaching example-ocp 2m52s Warning FailedAttachVolume pod/test AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-test-example": rpc error: code = Internal desc = Could not attach volume "vol-bxy" to node "i-789": attachment of disk "vol-1212" failed, expected device to be attached but was attaching ~~~
resolution: - Currently the issue is being tracked under [JIRA](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-23260)- **Workaround**- The engineering team has suggested to drain the faulty node, wait for all volumes to get detached from it, shut it down and start it. By starting the node with no attached volumes (except for the root disk), AWS should report just the root disk as attached. After node start, CSINode object should get correct limit of attachable volumes (if not, restart the CSI driver Pod on the node once more).- To prevent this issue from repeating, please always drain nodes before shutting down / restarting them

title: OpenShift 4 installation fails because of Windows DHCP Server
issue: - Hosts obtain the `IP Address` from `DHCP` correctly.- Hosts are not able to obtain the `hostname` from `DHCP`. The logs show: ~~~ Nov 01 08:25:11 localhost.localdomain mco-hostname[1745]: waiting for non-localhost hostname to be assigned Nov 01 08:25:11 localhost.localdomain systemd[1]: Starting Wait for a non-localhost hostname... Nov 01 08:30:11 localhost.localdomain systemd[1]: node-valid-hostname.service: start operation timed out. Terminating. Nov 01 08:30:11 localhost.localdomain systemd[1]: node-valid-hostname.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=15/TERM Nov 01 08:30:11 localhost.localdomain systemd[1]: node-valid-hostname.service: Failed with result 'timeout'. Nov 01 08:30:11 localhost.localdomain systemd[1]: Failed to start Wait for a non-localhost hostname. ~~~
resolution: **Do not use** a Windows `DHCP` Server for OpenShift installations.
root_cause: A Linux `DHCP` Server can use the option `option host-name` to send a networked host with its `hostname`. The option `option host-name`, which is a standard `DHCP` option 12, is not honoured by Windows. At the time of this writing it looks like there is no way to force a Windows `DHCP` Server to use this option. In reality, a Windows `DHCP` Server performs dynamic `DNS` updates, that is, the Windows client will tell the `DHCP` Server what its `hostname` is, which is the opposite of what is needed in an OpenShift installation.

title: TuneD pods going into CrashLoopBackOff state on multi-architecture payload in RHOCP 4

title: How to create a truststore from Kafka ca certs for Apicurio Registry
product: Red Hat build of Apicurio Registry
issue: - How to create a truststore from Kafka ca certs for Apicurio Registry- When configuring Kafka storage with TLS security, a truststore file should be created in "ca.p12" of the secret of ApicurioRegistry.spec.configuration.kafkasql.security.tls.truststoreSecretName [1] https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_build_of_apicurio_registry/2.4/html/installing_and_deploying_apicurio_registry_on_openshift/installing-registry-streams-storage#registry-persistence-kafkasql-tls ~~~ apiVersion: registry.apicur.io/v1 kind: ApicurioRegistry metadata: name: example-apicurioregistry-kafkasql-tls spec: configuration: persistence: "kafkasql" kafkasql: bootstrapServers: "my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap.registry-example-kafkasql-tls.svc:9093" security: tls: keystoreSecretName: my-user truststoreSecretName: my-cluster-cluster-ca-cert ~~~
resolution: A way to create a truststore from Kafka ca certs for Apicurio Registry. The following are sample commands for your reference. Please adjust the commands according to your environment. Please note that "ca.p12" of Apicurio Registry's secret is not ca certs, but a truststore file including ca cert. On the other hand, "ca.p12" in AMQ Streams Kafka cluster secret is not a truststore, but ca cert. This could be confused. ~~~ KAFKA_CLUSTER=your-kafka-cluster-name TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD=password APICURIO_SECRET=my-cluster-cluster-ca-cert # get Cluster CA cert from AMQ Streams Kafka cluster secret in the namespace of AMQ Streams Kafka cluster oc get secret ${KAFKA_CLUSTER}-cluster-ca-cert-o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64-d > ca.crt # create truststore file with PKCS format from CA certificate $ keytool-keystore ca.p12-storepass ${TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD}-noprompt-alias ca-import-file ca.crt-storetype PKCS12 # replace ca.p12 with the truststore newly created $ oc create secret generic ${APICURIO_SECRET}--from-file=ca.p12--from-literal=ca.password=${TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD}--dry-run=client-o yaml | oc apply-f- ~~~

title: On ROSA, "TargetDown" alert is shown in "openshift-ocm-agent-operator"
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: In a ROSA cluster in the OpenShift Monitoring, a `TargetDown` alert is firing in the `openshift-ocm-agent-operator` namespace. How can this be resolved?

title: Amazon EKS requires legacy iptables
issue: Amazon EKS requires legacy iptables which is not available on RHEL 8 anymore
Using AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) with `amazon-vpc-cni-k8s` which requires the `iptables` kernel module
iptables are not working as expected with AWS EKS `vpc-cni`
We can not add `ip_tables` `iptable_nat` `iptable_mangle` modules as required by AWS EKS `vpc-cni`
[amazon-vpc-cni-k8s GitHub Issue #1847- IPAMD fails to start](https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/issues/1847)
[amazon-vpc-cni-k8s GitHub Issue #2373- AWS CNI failed to add chain rule for each CIDR in VPC with nf_tables mode](https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/issues/2373)
resolution: To our knowledge, EKS should be able to detect the underlying host firewall with the `ENABLE_NFTABLES` functionality: * [amazon-vpc-cni-k8s PR #2155- Add ENABLE_NFTABLES to VPC CNI](https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/pull/2155) * [amazon-vpc-cni-k8s PR #2402- Set iptables mode automatically and deprecate ENABLE_NFTABLES](https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/pull/2402) As Amazon's EKS is not a component supplied or supported by Red Hat, We have no control over its features nor visibility into its development process. Please refer to your AWS EKS support for assistance using this configuration option. Red Hat supply and support a fully working integrated Kubernetes distribution as the [**Red Hat Openshift Container Platform**](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/openshift/container-platform) product.
root_cause: The iptables firewall is considered deprecated as of RHEL 8. It has been replaced in the kernel by nftables, and in userspace by `iptables-nft` which translates old `iptables` commands to new `nftables` commands. This is noted in the RHEL product documentation: * [RHEL 8.0 Release Notes- Networking- nftables replaces iptables as the default network packet filtering framework](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html-single/8.0_release_notes/index#networking) * [Considerations in adopting RHEL 8- nftables replaces iptables as the default network packet filtering framework](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/considerations_in_adopting_rhel_8/networking_considerations-in-adopting-rhel-8#literal_nftables_literal_replaces_literal_iptables_literal_as_the_default_network_packet_filtering_framework) This decision follows the upstream Linux kernel and upstream netfilter project's direction to introduce `nftables` as the successor to `iptables` in 2013, shortly after the release of RHEL 7. The majority of Linux distributions have followed this direction and have removed `iptables` in favour of `nftables` and the relevant translation/migration tools. * [Upstream netfilter project- nftables](https://netfilter.org/projects/nftables/) * [Red Hat Developer Blog- What comes after 'iptables'? Its successor, of course: `nftables` (2017)](https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2016/10/28/what-comes-after-iptables-its-successor-of-course-nftables) * [Phoronix- NFTables IPTables-Replacement Queued For Linux 3.13 (2013)](https://www.phoronix.com/news/MTQ5MDU)

title: AMQ 7: deploying ActiveMQArtemisAddress: Failed to create new *v1.Secret "{...} must be no more than 63 characters"
issue: When creating a new AMQ 7 address by deploying an ActiveMQArtemisAddress custom resource, the process fails, and the operator log shows an error message saying that a Kubernetes Secret is too long.
resolution: Use a shorter name for the address.
root_cause: AMQ 7 has no specific limitation on the length of name of an address or queue. However, when AMQ 7 operator creates an address, it also creates a Secret to store information that will be used to clean up the address later, if required. Kubernetes creates a limit of 64 characters on the name of a Secret. Red Hat is not treating this as a defect that needs to be fixed, because it's relatively easy to solve the problem. and the whole mechanism of address management is under review.

title: How to configure LDAP_SUPERUSER_FILTER in Quay to allow users to be added as SuperUsers without restarting Quay pods
issue: - Adding LDAP_SUPERUSER_FILTER to allow users to be added as SuperUsers without restarting Quay pods
resolution: - LDAP_SUPERUSER_FILTER needs to be added in quay config as below: Any users from organization unit "Users" will be added as superuser in Quay. ~~~ LDAP_SUPERUSER_FILTER: (memberOf=cn=testgroup,ou=Users,dc=example,dc=com) ~~~ Member of a group will be added as superuser. ~~~ LDAP_SUPERUSER_FILTER: (groupMembership=cn=ldapSuperUser,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com) ~~~
root_cause: LDAP_SUPERUSER_FILTER: to be added with ldap filter "memberOf" as it is the subset of LDAP_USER_FILTER.

title: Red Hat Service Interconnect looks at `docker.io/library/oauth-proxy`
issue: - Red Hat Service Interconnect looks at `docker.io/library/oauth-proxy`
resolution: Upgrade to a version 1.4.3 or higher and create a new site.
root_cause: The RHSI used the `openshift/oauth-proxy` image up to version 1.4.3. It has since been replaced by `registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-oauth-proxy`. However, after upgrading Openshift from 4.9, the former image is no longer available on `docker.io`. This prevents RHSI versions prior to 1.4.3 from working properly. For more details see the KCS ["After upgrade Openshift 4.9+, Oauth-proxy unable to load OpenShift configuration: unable to retrieve authentication information for tokens: the server could not find the requested resource "](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6999861).

title: User with ACS Role without READ permission on ACCESS unable to log in
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: If your existing ACS environment has a Role that does not have `READ` permission on the `ACCESS` resource, users of your Auth Provider who are assigned only that Role will not be able to log into ACS. The login will appear to work, but the user will then be immediately redirected back to the login screen. All other users who have either `READ` permission on the `ACCESS` resources, or `WRITE` permission on the `ACCESS` resource, should not be affected.
resolution: A temporary workaround is to give affected users a Role that includes just the `READ` permission on the `ACCESS` resource, if possible. Patch release 4.3.1 of ACS, and all subsequent releases will not have this problem.
root_cause: A new feature in 4.3.0, Invite Users by Email, preloads data necessary to invite new users, and did check that the required permission existed before making an API request. This will be corrected in subsequent versions.

title: Images can not be downloaded by tags in lowercases
issue: Images can not be downloaded by tags in lowercases.
resolution: * Create tags in proper case, Quay.io is now fully case sensitive.
root_cause: * Quay.io database maintenance on November 12, 2023. * Previous Quay.io backend database was case insensitive (MySQL). * Current Quay.io database is case sensitive (Aurora PostgreSQL).

title: RH-SSO embedded PostgreSQL database pod crashing with message crashing with message: "pg_ctl: the PID file "/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata/postmaster.pid"
issue: RH-SSO embedded PostgreSQL database pod crashing with message crashing with message: *pg_ctl: the PID file "/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata/postmaster.pid*
resolution: ## 1. Architecture design: NOT using Embedded PostgreSQL database The `Embedded PostgreSQL database` shall **NOT BE USED** in *PRODUCTION MODE*. You shall always use an `external PostgreSQL database` with *PRODUCTION MODE*. When Doing architecture review, only `external PostgreSQL database` is **SUPPORTED** with *PRODUCTION MODE*. ## 2. Probable Cause `pg_ctl` fails to stop the process properly when Openshift was upgraded. This leads to */var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata/postmaster.pid* file to be left behind; except the file is now empty or corrupted. Upon redeployment, the new pod faces issues to define a valid `PID`, which sets the pod on a *crashloop*. ## 2. How to fix The way this is to connect to the pod in debug mode and remove this file. ~~~ oc debug pod # rm /var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata/postmaster.pid ~~~ Once the file has been removed, keycloak postgress pod is able to start SUCCESSFULLY. Thus Keycloak pod has also been able to start SUCCESSFULLY. ## 3. Testing An ultimate test is verifying that it is possible to connect to the RH-SSO admin console.

title: Resizing disks or change instance type on Azure IPI control plane nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to increase or reduce the disk size of control plane nodes on Azure IPI.- Can the instance type of the control plane nodes in Azure IPI can be changed?
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Here is a comprehensive example illustrating the process. In this scenario, a cluster comprises three control plane and some worker nodes. The emphasis in this example is on updating the control plane nodes. > **Note:** The recommended disk size for OpenShift control plane nodes in Azure is `1024 GB` as explained in [Why is the minimum recommended size of disk for control plane nodes 1024 GB when installing OpenShift 4 on Azure?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5970511) Smaller disks do not have enough performance for etcd, and specially for production environments. > **IMPORTANT NOTE:** this procedure relies on the `controlplanemachineset` Custom Resource, [which was introduced in OpenShift 4.12](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/release_notes/ocp-4-12-release-notes.html#ocp-4-12-mapi-control-plane-machine-sets). As explained in [Missing `controlplanemachineset` resource in IPI RHOCP 4 cluster](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7048381), the `controlplanemachineset` resource is not created by default in some combinations of OpenShift version and cloud provider (like OpenShift 4.12 and Azure). Refer to [Creating `controlplanemachineset` in OpenShift 4.12 clusters in Azure](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7060794) for additional information about creating it for Azure if there is no `controlplanemachineset` present in an OpenShift 4.12 cluster in Azure installed with IPI. ### Prerequisites- This procedure is specific for Azure IPI installations.- The `oc` client matches the OpenShift version currently running. It can be checked running `oc version`: [`oc` CLI documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/cli_reference/openshift_cli/getting-started-cli.html).- Prior to proceeding, it is essential to [take a backup of etcd](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/backup_and_restore/control_plane_backup_and_restore/backing-up-etcd.html) as a prerequisite.- Ensure there is an `Active` `controlplanemachineset` resource in the cluster, or create it as explained in [Creating controlplanemachineset in OpenShift 4.12 clusters in Azure](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7060794). ### Modify the control plane machines In the IPI installation method, alterations to the control plane nodes will be enforced by the `controlplanemachineset` resource.- List the control plane `nodes` and `machines`: ``` $ oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/master= NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master-0 Ready control-plane,master 14d v1.27.6+f67aeb3 master-1 Ready control-plane,master 14d v1.27.6+f67aeb3 master-2 Ready control-plane,master 14d v1.27.6+f67aeb3 [...] ``` ``` $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api-l machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role=master NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE master-0 Running Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 1 2d master-1 Running Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 2 2d master-2 Running Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 3 2d ```- The previous control plane nodes had a capacity of 256 gigabytes: ``` $ oc get machines-l "machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role=master"-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml | grep "diskSize" diskSizeGB: 256 diskSizeGB: 256 diskSizeGB: 256 ```- Verify the values prior to patching with the intended size specifications. ``` $ oc get controlplanemachineset cluster-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml | grep "diskSizeGB:" diskSizeGB: 1024 ```- In this example, the nodes have been updated with a disk size of 1024: ``` $ oc patch controlplanemachineset cluster-n openshift-machine-api--type merge \-p '{"spec":{"template":{"machines_v1beta1_machine_openshift_io":{"spec":{"providerSpec":{"value":{"osDisk":{"diskSizeGB":1024}}}}}}}}' controlplanemachineset.machine.openshift.io/cluster patched ``` It is also possible to change the `vmSize` with a different instance type (usually with a more performant one for the control plane). > **Note:** Some instance types may require additional features, like for example `Dsv5` family requires "Accelerated Networking". Check the requirements if new instance types are going to be used, and if it is needed to configure anything else in the `controlplanemachineset`). For the specific case of "Accelerated Networking", refer to [Accelerated Networking for Microsoft Azure VMs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/machine_management/control_plane_machine_management/cpmso-using.html#machineset-azure-accelerated-networking_cpmso-using).- After patching, it will require some time to update the node using a roll-out approach: ``` $ watch-n 10 "oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/master= && oc get co control-plane-machine-set" Every 10s: oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/master= && oc get co control-plane-machine-set NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master-2hpwl-2 Ready control-plane,master 11m v1.27.6+f67aeb3 master-fxmsn-2 Ready,SchedulingDisabled control-plane,master 103m v1.27.6+f67aeb3 master-ph4s7-0 Ready control-plane,master 58m v1.27.6+f67aeb3 master-rlch2-1 Ready control-plane,master 34m v1.27.6+f67aeb3 NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE control-plane-machine-set 4.12.31 True True False 14d Waiting for 1 old replica(s) to be removed NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY UPDATED UNAVAILABLE STATE AGE cluster 3 3 3 2 Active 17d ```- If the `vmSize` field is changed with a different instance type, it's possible to see it with the following command: ``` $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api-l machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role=master NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE master-2hpwl-2 Running Standard_D16s_v3 eastus 3 19m master-fxmsn-2 Deleting Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 3 111m master-ph4s7-0 Running Standard_D16s_v3 eastus 1 66m master-rlch2-1 Running Standard_D16s_v3 eastus 2 43m ```- The following command can be used to verify the changes: ``` $ oc get machines-l "machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role=master"-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml | grep "diskSize\|vmSize" diskSizeGB: 1024 vmSize: Standard_D16s_v3 diskSizeGB: 1024 vmSize: Standard_D16s_v3 diskSizeGB: 1024 vmSize: Standard_D16s_v3 ``` > **Important:** This procedure provides guidance on altering disk sizes or instance type to increase or decrease capacity. Exercise caution and refer to [Managing control plane machines with control plane machine sets](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/machine_management/control_plane_machine_management/cpmso-using.html) for further information and responsible implementation.
root_cause: It is possible to resize the disk size of the control plane nodes in Azure without replacing all of them using the `controlplanemachineset`, which is available starting with OpenShift 4.12. > **Note:** The recommended disk size for OpenShift control plane nodes in Azure is `1024 GB` as explained in [Why is the minimum recommended size of disk for control plane nodes 1024 GB when installing OpenShift 4 on Azure?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5970511) Smaller disks do not have enough performance for etcd, and specially for production environments.

title: Is it possible to configure gzip compression only for some routes in OpenShift 4?
issue: - How to configure gzip compression only for specific routes in OCP 4.- Can HTTP compression be enabled in OpenShift 4 Ingress only for one application?
resolution: Configuring gzip compression in OpenShift 4 can be achieved configuring the `httpCompression` field in the `IngressController` as explained in the documentation: [Using router compression](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/ingress-operator.html#nw-configuring-router-compression_configuring-ingress). To configure the compression only for some routes, it is needed to use the [Ingress Sharding](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/networking/ingress-sharding.html). For doing that, it is also needed to [avoid that the default ingresscontroller serves routes of all projects when using router sharding](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5097511).
root_cause: It is possible to configure the gzip compression only for some routes in OpenShift 4, using different `IngressControllers` and Ingress Sharding.

title: Updating Trust Policies for ROSA cluster creation after Nov-21-2023
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Error encountered during new STS cluster creation: ``` "Failed to create cluster: The support role 'ManagedOpenShift-Support-Role' trusted policy does not allow support access. Role ARN 'arn:aws:iam::644306948063:role/RH-Technical-Support-xxxxxxx' is not present in the support role's trust policy." ```- Inability to create a new STS cluster using the ROSA CLI.- Why do I need to update my trust policies?- How do I update my support role to allow new cluster creation?
resolution: **NOTE** This solution is only applicable after November 21 2023. Before creating a new cluster, **use one of the two following methods** to update the Support Role in the AWS account to have the correct trust policies. 1. **Update using ROSA CLI**:- Re-run the command: `rosa create account-roles` targeting the existing support role.- This command updates the existing Support Role’s trust policy by appending the required principal to the policy. 2. **Manual Update in AWS Console**:- Log into to AWS account’s web console.- Navigate to: IAM-> Roles.- Search for the support role (`ManagedOpenShift-Support-Role` by default).- Go to the `Trust Relationships` tab.- Add the IAM role from the error message to `.Statement.Principal.AWS`. **Validation**:- After completing either of the above methods, cluster creation should succeed.
root_cause: #### Why is this necessary?- As part of ROSA's new support flow, more granular roles are assigned to each customer organization.- This is to enhance security by ensuring that any given jump role has only short-term access to a limited number of customer accounts. #### Additional Notes- Ensure that the IAM roles and policies are correctly configured and up-to-date to avoid similar issues in the future.- Regularly review AWS and ROSA documentation for any updates in role management and policy settings.

The error `Missing port in address field` appears in collector logs.

title: Manual change in VirtualFunction MTU value causes MTU mismatch with SRIOV node Network  triggering Node drain.
issue: - Manual change in VirtualFunction MTU value causes MTU mismatch with SRIOV node Network triggering Node drain.- Why do we see below messages in sriov-network-config-daemon pod logs? ~~~ NeedUpdate(): VF 0 MTU needs update, desired=3040, current=3072 ~~~
resolution: - It is not recommended to set/change `MTU` value of `virtual functions` manually or via any other applications scripts.- All the changes should be done only via `SriovNetworkNodePolicy`.- To avoid this mismatch a temporary workaround is be to set all the manually modified VF's MTU equal to the value defined in `SriovNetworkNodePolicy`
root_cause: - In the [OCPBUGS-22337](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-22337) its explained how manual change of MTU can cause an issue.- If someone manually changed the mtu of some VFs that were previously configured with a `SriovNetworkNodePolicy` then the `SR-IOV Network Config daemon` detects these changes (via pollNicStatus which runs every 30s) and updates the status of the `SR-IOV network node state` object. However, the reconciliation loop doesn't trigger because it only does when the generation field changes. But with recent issue with etcd encryption, the kube-api server pods gets restarted. The resource version of objects were incremented due to this, including the one for the "device-plugin-config" config map. The resource version of this config map is part of the `sriov-network-node-state` spec. Due to this, the `SR-IOV Network Config daemon` started its reconciliation loop. The function OnNodeStateChange of the generic plugin detected changes in the MTU and returned "needDrain = true". And node is drained.

title: logging-loki-ruler pods are not injected with custom CA certificate defined in LokiStack in RHOCP 4
issue: - `logging-loki-ruler` pods are unable to evaluate the `AlertingRule`.- `logging-loki-ruler` pods fail to establish connection with object storage because of failed `certificate` validation ``` level=error ts=2023-11-20T19:04:56.601682008Z caller=compat.go:78 user=infrastructure rule_name=k8sallowedrepos rule_type=alerting query="(sum(count_over_time({kubernetes_namespace_name=\"openshift-logging\"} | json | openshift_labels_cluster_name=\"abc\" | kubernetes_event_reason=\"FailedCreate\" | message=~\".*denied.*\" | message=~\".*trusted-repos.*\"[10m])) > 5)" query_hash=834209125 msg="rule evaluation failed" err="failed to load chunk 'infrastructure/862880de39542850/18bedaadd36:18bee18f903:6b1e191c': failed to get s3 object: RequestError: send request failed\ncaused by: Get \"https://s3.storage.example.com:443/observability-observability/infrastructure/862880de39542850/18bedbadd36%3B18bee19f903%3A6b1e191c\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" ```- `CA certificate` defined in `LokiStack` custom resource is not injected in `logging-loki-ruler` pods.
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in:- For RHOL 5.9 in Bug report [LOG-4830](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4830) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.9.0 through errata [RHBA-2024:1591](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:1591)- For RHOL 5.8 in Bug report [LOG-4836](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4836) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.8.1 through errata [RHSA-2023:7720](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7720)- For RHOL 5.7 in Bug report [LOG-4837](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4837) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.7.9 through errata [RHBA-2023:7718](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:7718)- For RHOL 5.6 in Bug report [LOG-4838](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4838) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.6.14 through errata [RHBA-2023:7719](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:7719) If this issue still occurs, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. #### Workaround 1. Set `LokiStack` to `Unmanaged` state: ~~~ $ oc edit lokistack logging-loki-n openshift-logging----- output omitted----- managementState: Managed /// Change this to "Unmanaged"----- output omitted----- ~~~ 2. Add a new line for `args` and create a new `volume` & `volumeMount` in `logging-loki-ruler` statefulset: ~~~ $ oc edit sts logging-loki-ruler-n openshift-logging----- output omitted-------- ### Add a new line for args args:- '-target=ruler'- '-config.file=/etc/loki/config/config.yaml'- '-runtime-config.file=/etc/loki/config/runtime-config.yaml'- '-config.expand-env=true'- '-s3.http.ca-file=/etc/storage/ca/service-ca.crt' < < <==== Add this line--- ### Create a new volumeMount volumeMounts:- name: storage-tls mountPath: /etc/storage/ca--- ### Create a new volume for respective volumeMount volumes:- name: storage-tls configMap: name: custom-ca < < <==== Name of configmap in which CA certificate is present defaultMode: 420----- output omitted----- ~~~
root_cause: The Loki Operator did not mount a custom CA Bundle to the ruler pods caused failing object storage access when evaluating alerting/recording rules.

title: Install packages from PyPI Mirror fails on Data Science Pipelines in disconnected installation
issue: When running a pipeline in Data Science Pipelines that needs to install Python packages in a disconnected environment, it fails looking up on external URLs.
resolution: There are 3 possible methods to work around this issue. 1. Specify the URL of the PyPi package in the pipeline code. ~~~ preprocess_data_step = components.create_component_from_func(func=preprocess_data, base_image="registry.redhat.io/ubi8/python-39", packages_to_install=['https://pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com/packages/urllib3-2.0.7.tar.gz']) ~~~ 2. Inject an Environment Variable in the pipeline component to specify the PyPi mirror. ~~~ ingest_data_step = components.create_component_from_func(func=ingest_data, base_image="registry.redhat.io/ubi8/python-39", packages_to_install=['pandas']) … @dsl.pipeline(name="my-pipeline") def my_pipeline(): idx_url = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_INDEX_URL', value='https://pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com') ingest_and_process_task = ingest_data_step().add_env_variable(idx_url) ~~~ *Note:* For PyPi mirrors with self-signed certificates, it is required to inject an extra Environment Variable to disable trust validation in the PyPi mirror. The full example for both cases is shown below. ~~~ ingest_data_step = components.create_component_from_func(func=ingest_data, base_image="registry.redhat.io/ubi8/python-39", packages_to_install=['pandas'],) preprocess_data_step = components.create_component_from_func(func=preprocess_data, base_image="registry.redhat.io/ubi8/python-39", packages_to_install=['https://pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com/packages/urllib3-2.0.7.tar.gz']) … @dsl.pipeline(name="my-pipeline") def my_pipeline(): idx_url = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_INDEX_URL', value='https://pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com') trt_host = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_TRUSTED_HOST', value='pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com') ingest_and_process_task = ingest_data_step().add_env_variable(idx_url).add_env_variable(trt_host) preprocess_data_task = preprocess_data_step(ingest_and_process_task.output).add_env_variable(trt_host) ~~~ For PyPi mirrors with signed certificates, just replace *PIP_TRUSTED_HOST* with *PIP_CERT* environment variable containing the certificate file path. * It requires a secret containing this certificate file. The example below shows a secret with the certificate. ~~~ kind: Secret apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: pypi-mirror-secret data: ca.crt: >- ### INSERT CERTIFICATE CONTENTS HERE ### type: kubernetes.io/tls ~~~ * The secret must be mounted in the pipeline component. The example below shows a code snippet to mount a secret in the pipeline component. ~~~ idx_url = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_INDEX_URL', value_from=V1EnvVarSource(secret_key_ref=V1SecretKeySelector(key="index-url", name="pip-conf"))) pypi_cert = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_CERT', value='/certs/ca.crt') vol = V1Volume(name='pypi-certs', secret=V1SecretVolumeSource(secret_name='pypi-mirror-secret')) vol_mount = V1VolumeMount(name='pypi-certs', mount_path='/certs') ingest_and_process_task = ingest_data_step().add_env_variable(idx_url).add_env_variable(pypi_cert).add_volume_mount(vol_mount).add_volume(vol) ~~~ 3. Build a runtime image to use in the pipeline code. This solution basically involves building a new image from UBI Python image, adding the *pip.conf* file in */etc/* path, and push to a disconnected Image Registry. The example *pip.conf* file should look like this: ~~~ [global] index-url = https://artifactory-artifactory.apps.rmartine.dev.datahub.redhat.com/artifactory/api/pypi/disconnected-pypi/simple trusted-host = artifactory-artifactory.apps.rmartine.dev.datahub.redhat.com ~~~ And the Dockerfile should look like this. ~~~ FROM registry.redhat.io/ubi8/python-39 USER root ADD pip.conf /etc/ USER 1001 ~~~ ### Special case: PyPi mirrors with Authentication For PyPi mirrors that require authentication, the best option is to create a key/value secret and reference in the Environment Variable configuration in the pipeline code. The example below is the secret definition. ~~~ kind: Secret apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: pip-conf data: index-url: https://admin:password@pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com trusted-host: pypi-notebook.apps.hnalla.dev.datahub.redhat.com type: Opaque ~~~ And the pipeline code should look like this. ~~~ from kubernetes.client.models import V1EnvVar,V1EnvVarSource,V1SecretKeySelector … @dsl.pipeline(name="my-pipeline") def my_pipeline(): idx_url = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_INDEX_URL', value_from=V1EnvVarSource(secret_key_ref=V1SecretKeySelector(key="index-url", name="pip-conf"))) trt_host = V1EnvVar(name='PIP_TRUSTED_HOST', value_from=V1EnvVarSource(secret_key_ref=V1SecretKeySelector(key="trusted-host", name="pip-conf"))) ~~~
root_cause: Python *pip* command needs a special configuration for using private PyPi mirrors, which is not yet parametrized in the Data Science Pipelines installation.

title: Setting up NTP server for windows worker nodes in openshift
issue: - Is it possible to configure the NTP server for windows nodes in openshift?
resolution: - To configure a time server for a Windows instance, One can follow the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/windows-time-service/windows-time-service-tools-and-settings?tabs=config).- If the same configuration is needed to apply to all Windows nodes, it is best to create a custom image with this configuration.

title: Unable to login to OCP cluster using RH-SSO as identity provider
issue: - We have configured RH-SSO as oidc identity provider in Openshift and when we try to login using RH-SSO identity provider we are getting following error in browser ~~~ We are sorry... An internal server error has occurred ~~~- In Openshift oidc integration with RH-SSO- we are getting `An internal server error has occurred` when setting `spec.identityProviders.name` with spaces. Following NullPointerException is observed in RH-SSO server log ~~~ [org.keycloak.services.error.KeycloakErrorHandler] (default task-57) Uncaught server error: java.lang.NullPointerException at org.keycloak.keycloak-services@18.0.9.redhat-00001//org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.utils.RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri(RedirectUtils.java:143) at org.keycloak.keycloak-services@18.0.9.redhat-00001//org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.utils.RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri(RedirectUtils.java:63) at org.keycloak.keycloak-services@18.0.9.redhat-00001//org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.endpoints.AuthorizationEndpointChecker.checkRedirectUri(AuthorizationEndpointChecker.java:129) at org.keycloak.keycloak-services@18.0.9.redhat-00001//org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.endpoints.AuthorizationEndpoint.process(AuthorizationEndpoint.java:143) at org.keycloak.keycloak-services@18.0.9.redhat-00001//org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.endpoints.AuthorizationEndpoint.buildGet(AuthorizationEndpoint.java:112) at jdk.internal.reflect.GeneratedMethodAccessor984.invoke(Unknown Source) ~~~
resolution: - The RH-SSO identity provider in `Oauth` cluster configuration should have `spec.identityProviders.name`set to a name without spaces.
root_cause: - RH-SSO is unable to handle redirect uri with spaces.

title: OVN is broken and node becomes NotReady in OpenShift 4
issue: - `OVN` is broken and node becomes `NotReady`- The `ovnkube-node` pod does not come up on that node: ``` failed to start node network manager: failed to start default node network controller: error waiting for node readiness: gateway init failed to start watching services: watchResource for resource *factory.serviceForGateway. Failed addHandlerFunc: timed out waiting for the condition ```- There is a `headless service` with `internalTrafficPolicy: Local` in the cluster
resolution: The `headless service` with `internalTrafficPolicy: Local` isn't applicable and due to the way `OVN` was brought up from an unstable state was causing the issue. Please correct this service and verify if the node starts up.
root_cause: Refer to [this documentation](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/2086-service-internal-traffic-policy/README.md#proposal) for information about the field in Service `spec.internalTrafficPolicy`

title: OADP Azure storage account configuration with public access denied
issue: - Unable access storage bucket when storage account with option `default-action deny`.- `velero` pod losses access to backup storage location with error `Authorization error (403)`.
resolution: - If `Azure Storage account` is created with configuration parameter `--default-action Deny` as below, then As per [Azure official documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security?toc=%2Fazure%2Fstorage%2Fblobs%2Ftoc.json&bc=%2Fazure%2Fstorage%2Fblobs%2Fbreadcrumb%2Ftoc.json&tabs=azure-portal#change-the-default-network-access-rule) need to allow access for particular IP. ~~~ For particular storage account on Azure portal a) Navigate to Settings menu. b) Click Firewalls and virtual networks. c) For selected networks, select Allow access. d) Add rules to allow traffic from specific network. > > here add rule to allow access from this particular cluster e) To apply changes,click Save. ~~~ **Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to an external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or its entities, products, or services.
