title: OpenShift Container Platform 4 - Node reporting NotReady state related to ResourceExhausted
issue: We are often reporting `NotReady` state for Nodes, when `Tekton` `pipelines` are running. When looking at the `NotReady` Nodes, the below Events are being reported. Warning ContainerGCFailed 6m3s kubelet rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (16997306 vs. 16777216) Normal NodeNotReady 3m49s kubelet Node worker-01.example.com status is now: NodeNotReady Warning ContainerGCFailed 2s (x6 over 5m3s) kubelet rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (17002501 vs. 16777216)
OpenShift- Node are entering `NotReady` state and are reporting `rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (17166130 vs. 16777216)`.
resolution: **Disclaimer**:_Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ * Red Hat is aware about this problem and has investigated it in [OCPBUGS-17141](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-17141). * The problem is related to many `dead` container on the respective Red hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node, causing the `kubelet` to fail listing them, because they exceed the `gRPC` `MaxMessageSize` of **16 MiB** configured in the `kubelet`. * [pkg: kubelet: remote: increase grpc client default size to 16MiB](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/64672) contains information about `MaxMessageSize` configuration in the `kubelet`. * Given this problem is often related to heavy usage of OpenShift Pipelines or other CI/CD tooling, it's recommended to implement regular pruning for the associated resources, including the pods to prevent reaching the above limitation. * For OpenShift Pipelines, follow [Configuring the pruner](https://docs.openshift.com/pipelines/1.12/install_config/customizing-configurations-in-the-tektonconfig-cr.html#default-pruner-configuration_customizing-configurations-in-the-tektonconfig-cr) to setup and configure `pruning` of the associated resources. * An alternative approach would be to manually clean the `dead` containers on the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node, using an approach similar to the below example. ~~~ oc get nodes-o=name--no-headers-l node-role.kubernetes.io/ | while read-r host_; do oc debug $host-- chroot /host sh-c \ "crictl ps-a-s Exited--name '^(place-tools|place-scripts)$'-q | xargs-r crictl rm" done ~~~ You may need to replace `^(place-tools|place-scripts)$` with a different name pattern (or remove the `--name` parameter entirely) depending on which containers pile up more usually in your environment. * If containers cannot be cleaned up with `crictl` (e.g. because `crictl` starts throwing the same RPC error than the kubelet), then you have to follow the "with node reboot" procedure to clean the CRIO storage as documented in [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5350721). * Red Hat is further evaluating an alternative approach to clean `dead` containers on the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node via [RFE-4894](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4894) and [RFE-4898](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4898). * These request are still being evaluated and no decision has been taken if and how this may be addressed, which is why its strongly recommend to apply the `pruning` as documented above.
root_cause: The `MaxMessageSize` for `gRPC` in the `kubelet` is configured to 16 MiB and depending on the number of `dead` containers available on the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node, listing those may exceed the limit of 16 MiB and therefore cause the `kubelet` to fail with various different operation and hence entering `NotReady` state. Even if the `MaxMessageSize` could be increased further, a big enough number of dead containers would still be able to cause the issue.

title: ACM 2.9.0 and MCE 2.4.0 operators are temporarily not available in OperatorHub for RHOCP4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: ACM 2.9.0 and MCE 2.4.0 are temporarily unavailable due to an issue impacting upgrades to MCE 2.4.0 from prior releases of MCE.
The `ocm-controller` pods in `CrashLoopBackOff` after upgrading to ACM 2.9.0.

The `ocm-controller` crashes with error message: ~~~ E1121 18:21:15.357465 1 reflector.go:148] k8s.io/client-go@v12.0.0+incompatible/tools/cache/reflector.go:231: Failed to watch *v1beta2.ManagedClusterSetBinding: failed to list *v1beta2.ManagedClusterSetBinding: request to convert CR from an invalid group/version: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/v1beta1 ~~~

Listing `ManagedClusterSet/ManagedClusterSetBinding` shows the error: ~~~ $ oc get managedclusterset Error from server: request to convert CR from an invalid group/version: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/v1beta1 ~~~
resolution: * Bug [ACM-8723](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-8723) was created to address this issue and is ongoing. This knowledge article should be monitored for updates on restoration of ACM 2.9.0 and a MCE 2.4.1 that will contain the fix to the original issue * Fresh ACM 2.9.0 deploys are not affected. * Hold the upgrade to ACM 2.9.0 if you are currently on a previous version. * If you have already upgraded to ACM 2.9.0, a remediation is in progress and will be available as soon as possible * Due to this ongoing issue with the ACM upgrade from 2.8.x to 2.9.0 version, the ACM operator has been retracted for now. Bug [ACM-8767](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-8767) has been created to keep track of this.

title: Helm upgrades to Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security 4.2.3 fail with ImagePullBackoff
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: Helm upgrades to RHACS 4.2.3 fail
Status of the pods is `ImagePullBackoff`
Images for RHACS 4.2.3 are not yet available from the Red Hat Catalog
resolution: * Mitigation: The Helm charts were unpublished. * Customers with a stuck Helm upgrade should do one of the following: * roll back to the previous Helm revision by using `helm rollback-n 0` * upgrade to another RHACS version (for example, 4.2.2 or 4.3.0) by using `helm upgrade`
root_cause: The Helm charts for RHACS 4.2.3 were published prematurely.

title: Modifying Default Settings for Etcd Automatic Defragmentation in RHOCP
issue: - Is it feasible to modify the activation threshold for Automatic Defragmentation?- Currently, the operator triggers Automatic Defragmentation when the fragmented size reaches around 45% of the etcd database size.- Can this threshold be decreased to approximately 20%?- Seeking a way to adjust the triggering threshold for Automatic Defragmentation in the operator settings.- What is the default behaviour of Automatic Defragmentation
resolution: - Disabling automatic etcd defragmentation can be achieved by following the instructions provided in [this KCS Article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6960380).- The standard process of automatic defragmentation necessitates a minimum size threshold of 100MB and monitors fragmentation once it exceeds the 45% mark.- Modification of these configurations or values is not possible.
root_cause: - As per the default settings described [here](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/release-4.10/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go), the system checks every 11 minutes whether [(DbSize- DbSizeInUse) / DbSize] exceeds the maxFragmentedPercentage threshold (45%). If this condition is met, the etcd defragmentation process will be initiated (Well explained in this [KCS Article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7034568)).- If preferred, manual initiation of the defragmentation process is permissible, although typically, we rely on the operator to manage this task.- Changing these configurations or values is not feasible due to their hardcoded nature.- For more details:- Refer to the code for disabling auto defragmentation at [this GitHub link](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/master/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go).- Additional insights on automated defragmentation can be found [here](https://github.com/openshift/enhancements/blob/master/enhancements/etcd/automated-defrag.md?plain=1#L108-L115).- Details regarding the criteria for auto defragmentation are available [here](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/master/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L282-L291).

title: Step clone not running in OpenShift pipeline
issue: - I'm receiving `Permission denied` errors when attempting to use Tekton `git-clone` Task- I'm using a different user than the base UID
resolution: Either the UID or GID of the process needs to be changed to the default used in the container's filesystem (`65532`). For the UID, the `securityContext` within the Step must remove the `runAsUser` setting to go back to the default value: ~~~ steps: name: clone securityContext: runAsNonRoot: true runAsUser: 59247 <=== Remove this value, or set to `65532` ~~~ Alternatively, a Pod template can be used to set the `fsGroup` to `65532`, which will change the process's GID. This can be done in the TaskRun directly before applying via `oc apply-f /path/to/taskrun.yaml`: ~~~yaml apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1beta1 kind: TaskRun metadata: name: spec: taskRef: name: git-clone podTemplate: <=== Use this to set fsGroup in Pod securityContext: fsGroup: 65532 ~~~ Or, when using `tkn` to start the task, use the `--pod-template` flag to point to the template as a file: ~~~bash $ cat < < EOF > pod-template.yaml securityContext: fsGroup: 65532 EOF $ tkn task start--pod-template pod-template.yaml TaskRun started:-run-##### ~~~
root_cause: The file permissions of the default `git-clone` Tasks [provided by Tekton](https://hub.tekton.dev/tekton/task/git-clone "") use the UID and GID `65532`. When the `securityContext` sets the resulting Pod to use a different UID, the process will be unable to access the filesystem in the container, resulting in these errors.

title: How to create an address using broker properties
issue: - How to create address, ANYCAST or MULTICAST with broker properties
resolution: To create a ANYCAST address like testQueue the following property needs to be added to brokerProperties: section of the broker CR yaml file ~~~ "addressConfigurations.testQueue.queueConfigs.testQueue.routingType=ANYCAST" ~~~ In order to create a MULTICAST address like testTopic The following properties has to be added to brokerProperties: section of the broker CR yaml file: ~~~ "addressConfigurations.testTopic.COMMANDS.routingTypes=MULTICAST" ~~~ A complete example: ~~~ brokerProperties:- "addressConfigurations.testQueue.queueConfigs.testQueue.routingType=ANYCAST"- "addressConfigurations.testTopic.COMMANDS.routingTypes=MULTICAST" ~~~ The above broker properties would create two address *testQueue* and *testTopic*. With command ~~~./artemis queue stat--url tcp://$HOSTNAME:61616--user $AMQ_USER--password $AMQ_PASSWORD ~~~ excuted on the pod it is possible to display the created **ANYCAST** queue and confirm that it has been created. To confirm that a **MULTICAST** address has been created use command ~~~./artemis address show--url tcp://$HOSTNAME:61616--user $AMQ_USER--password $AMQ_PASSWORD ~~~

title: Cannot open details of migrated report configs in 4.3
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: Report configurations under Vulnerability management (1.0) are migrated to Vulnerability Management (2.0) when a user upgrades to 4.3.0. Clicking on these migrated report configurations to view its details might result the below error: [image=[src="images/error-msg_0.png", alt="error message", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", caption="error message",]] This error occurs because the affected report configuration has a report job with some missing fields that are required by VM (2.0). This issue only affects the ability to view the report config details, as the user is still able to trigger report jobs, edit, clone or delete the report configuration and receive scheduled reports.
resolution: Here is a workaround to resolve the issue 1. Clone the affected report configuration 2. Navigate to the affected report configurations and click on ‘Clone report’ from the available actions. 3. Save the cloned report configuration and then delete the original. **Note:** For report configs that are configured to include CVEs discovered since the last successful scheduled report, the first report on the cloned config will also include the older CVEs that were already reported by the original config. If you do not want the first report to include the older CVEs, then you can use the custom date setting for ‘CVEs discovered since’ while cloning. Set the custom date to the date when the last scheduled report from the original config was received. After receiving the first report with the cloned config, you can reset the ‘CVEs discovered since’ to ‘Since Last Sent Scheduled Report’. To get the time of last scheduled report of a config, you can make the following API ~~~ /v2/reports/configurations/ /history?reportParamQuery.query=Report%20Request%20Type%3ASCHEDULED&reportParamQuery.pagination.limit=10&reportParamQuery.pagination.offset=0&reportParamQuery.pagination.sortOption.field=Report%20Completion%20Time&reportParamQuery.pagination.sortOption.reversed=true ~~~
root_cause: The report migration from VM 1.0-> 2.0 created a job history for each report config from their last successful scheduled job. This job has some missing fields that are required by VM 2.0 which causes the affected report config details page to fail to render the report job history.

title: How to force the Kafka Operator to regenerate the Debezium topics
issue: - REST operations on the Debezium topic fails, returning HTTP codes other than 200. The following is seen on the strimzi-cluster-operator logs ~~~ io.strimzi.operator.cluster.operator.assembly.ConnectRestException: GET /connectors/CONNECTOR-NAME/config returned 500 (Internal Server Error): Request timed out ~~~- Messages like the following can be seen on Kafka pod's logs ~~~ org.apache.kafka.common.errors.NotEnoughReplicasException: The size of the current ISR Set(1) is insufficient to satisfy the min.isr requirement of 3 for partition [DEBEZIUM-TOPIC]-0 ~~~ Another example ~~~ org.apache.kafka.connect.errors.NotFoundException: No status found for task [DEBEZIUM-TOPIC]-0 ~~~
resolution: Let the Kafka operator recreate the KafkaConnect topics, but using the default options defined for the Kafka cluster. If other options are defined for replication, it will end on `NotEnoughReplicasException` exceptions on the Kafka logs If you are stuck in this state, you can either **A**. Only recreate the KafkaConnect topics **B**. Execute **A** but also recreate Kafka Cluster The steps for **A** are:- **A1** Stop the KafkaConnect, as depicted [here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_build_of_debezium/1.9.7/html/getting_started_with_debezium/viewing-change-events#restarting-kafka-connect-service)- **A2** Delete the KafkaConnect topics ~~~ $ oc delete kafkatopic [KAFKACONNECT-NAME]-configs $ oc delete kafkatopic [KAFKACONNECT-NAME]-offsets $ oc delete kafkatopic [KAFKACONNECT-NAME]-status ~~~- **A3** Replace or add in the KafkaConnect definition the following ~~~... config: config.storage.replication.factor:-1 offset.storage.replication.factor:-1 status.storage.replication.factor:-1 ~~~ It sets the default replication of the topics, the same ones that come on the cluster- **A4** Start the Kafka connect, as depicted [here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_build_of_debezium/1.9.7/html/getting_started_with_debezium/viewing-change-events#restarting-kafka-connect-service) The steps for **B** are:- **B1** Stopped and deleted Kafka Connector- **B2** Stopped Kafka Cluster- **B3** Deleted all Kafka-related pods- **B4** Deleted all Kafka topics- **B5** Started Kafka Cluster- **B6** Recreate the kafka connector, setting- **B7** Replace or add in the KafkaConnect definition the following ~~~... config: config.storage.replication.factor:-1 offset.storage.replication.factor:-1 status.storage.replication.factor:-1 ~~~ It sets the default replication of the topics, the same ones that come on the cluster- **B8** Start the Kafka connect, as depicted [here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_build_of_debezium/1.9.7/html/getting_started_with_debezium/viewing-change-events#restarting-kafka-connect-service).
root_cause: The KafkaConnect topics are created beforehand, or they are created by the operator with different replication options than the Kafka cluster.

title: Porting web applications with NodeJS front-ends to build with .NET 8.0 UBI images
issue: - The.NET 8.0 UBI images no longer contain NodeJS. How can I port applications with a NodeJS front-end from previous versions of the.NET UBI images to the.NET 8.0 UBI images?
resolution: The options to build a.NET 8.0 web application with a NodeJS front-end using the UBI.NET 8.0 images are:- A multi-stage build that builds the NodeJS front-end in a separate image- Performing the build in an image derived from the.NET 8.0 base image that includes NodeJS Both are valid options. This solution describes the second option because it is similar to how the build worked with previous.NET images (which included NodeJS), and it minimizes the required changes to the application. The steps are based on an OpenShift source-to-image (s2i) build of a.NET 7.0 application. Similar steps can be used for other build flows and for.NET 6.0. The initial BuildConfig of a.NET 7.0 application looks like this: ~~~... strategy: type: Source sourceStrategy: from: kind: ImageStreamTag namespace: openshift name: 'dotnet:7.0'... ~~~ The `dotnet:7.0` image in this snippet is the [.NET 7.0 UBI image](registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/dotnet-70), which includes NodeJS 18. The image is referenced through an ImageStream that was added to the `openshift` namespace. We will update the application `BuildConfig` to use an image that is based on the.NET 8.0 base image to which we add NodeJS 18. In OpenShift this derived image can be created by using a `BuildConfig` of type `Docker`. In other build flows, the Dockerfile from this `BuildConfig` may be used directly. ## Step-by-Step 1. Import the latest.NET and NodeJS image stream definitions into the project namespace: ~~~ $ oc apply-f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redhat-developer/s2i-dotnetcore/main/dotnet_imagestreams.json $ oc apply-f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sclorg/s2i-nodejs-container/master/imagestreams/nodejs-rhel.json ~~~ 2. Create a file named `dotnet-8-node-18.yaml` with the following content. This file defines the derived s2i image. ~~~ kind: ImageStream apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: dotnet-8-node-18--- kind: BuildConfig apiVersion: build.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: dotnet-8-node-18 spec: output: to: kind: ImageStreamTag name: 'dotnet-8-node-18:latest' strategy: type: Docker dockerStrategy: from: kind: ImageStreamTag name: dotnet:8.0 source: type: Dockerfile dockerfile: | FROM dotnet USER 0 ENV NODEJS_VERSION=18 RUN microdnf-y module enable nodejs:$NODEJS_VERSION && \ microdnf install-y--setopt=tsflags=nodocs--setopt=install_weak_deps=0 npm && \ microdnf clean all-y && \ rm-rf /var/cache/yum/* USER 1001 triggers:- type: ConfigChange- type: ImageChange- type: ImageChange imageChange: from: kind: ImageStreamTag name: nodejs:18-ubi8 runPolicy: Serial ~~~ In the `dotnet-8-node` `BuildConfig` there are triggers to automatically rebuild the image when either the.NET base image or the NodeJS 18 base image changes. These triggers enable you to automatically rebuild this image when either one of the base images change due to security patches. 3. Import the `dotnet-8-node-18.yaml` file: ~~~ $ oc apply-f dotnet-8-node18.yaml ~~~ 4. Update the application source-code to target.NET 8.0. 5. Change the `BuildConfig` to use the derived `dotnet-8-node18` image: ~~~ sourceStrategy: from: kind: ImageStreamTag- namespace: openshift- name: 'dotnet:7.0' + name: 'dotnet-8-node-18:latest' ~~~ The build is now performed in an image that includes both.NET 8.0 and NodeJS 18. 5. Optionally, some additional configuration might be needed for NodeJS to work well in the s2i build, such as configuration of an NPM mirror or an HTTP proxy. You can achieve this by adding an s2i assemble script in the source repository at `.s2i/bin/assemble`. The following example shows a script that performs initialization based on environment variables known by the.NET 7.0 s2i image: ~~~ #!/bin/bash set-e PATH=$HOME/node_modules/.bin:$PATH if [-n "$NPM_MIRROR"]; then echo "---> Setting npm mirror" npm config set registry "$NPM_MIRROR" fi if [-n "$HTTP_PROXY"]; then echo "---> Setting npm http proxy" npm config set proxy "$HTTP_PROXY" fi if [-n "$HTTPS_PROXY"]; then echo "---> Setting npm https proxy" npm config set https-proxy "$HTTPS_PROXY" fi if [-n "${DOTNET_NPM_TOOLS}"]; then echo "---> Installing npm tools..." pushd "$HOME" npm install ${DOTNET_NPM_TOOLS} popd fi # call base.NET assemble script $STI_SCRIPTS_PATH/assemble ~~~
root_cause: .NET 6 and.NET 7 images do have NodeJS embedded, but.NET 8 does not.

title: Are there security implication when granting system:service-account-issuer-discovery for system:unauthenticated in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: We were requested to apply the below change on our platform and we now would like to know if we may hit security implication / risk when granting the below `ClusterRole` to `system:unauthenticated`. kubectl create clusterrolebinding oidc-reviewer \--clusterrole=system:service-account-issuer-discovery \--group=system:unauthenticated
`oidc-reviewer` needs `system:unauthicated`.
Are there concerns with regards to security when granting `system:service-account-issuer-discovery` for `system:unauthenticated`?
resolution: Red Hat does not see an immediate security risk, when granting `system:service-account-issuer-discovery` `ClusterRole` to `system:unauthenticated` `Group`. Red Hat though is not planning on granting such permissions to unauthenticated users by default as Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Cluster administrators should carefully evaluate the risk of exposing those endpoints to unauthenticated users on a case by case basis, factoring in their organizational security requirements and based on a risk assessment for the specific Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Cluster.

Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ As per [KEP-1393](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/1393-oidc-discovery#proposal), it is mentioned that even though the information exposed are not sensitive, `kubernetes` will not provide a default binding to all authenticated and/or unauthenticated users. title: Agent based installation fails at RHOCP4 with "api vips is already in use" error
issue: Installation is started by booting the cluster nodes from the created iso image. Initial agent checks passes successfully. Assisted service checks all cluster nodes and reports that all nodes are ready for installation. After that Installation gets stuck and does not proceeds. Bootstrapping never starts. Cluster nodes do not present any error but "vips already in use" error is present in the bootstrap logs.
resolution: - **Option-1:** Remove the VIP addresses from the platform section of the install-config.yaml and set the the content as: ~~~ platform: none: {} ~~~- **Option-2:** Keep the content of the platform section of the install-config.yaml and disable the external load balancer service and remove the IP addresses from its hosting node.
root_cause: - When the platform section of the install-config.yaml is populated with the VIP addresses, OpenShift cluster tries to announce the IP addresses on cluster nodes as floating IPs.- Since the external load balancer is already announcing the same IP addresses, an IP conflict occurs.

title: Custom domain for ROSA cluster installation and API

title: NodeClockNotSynchronising alert for all nodes which are configured with DHCP NTP servers
issue: - All node's time is not synchronising with NTP servers offered by `DHCP` server.
resolution: - Ensure `/etc/chrony.conf` file has the below line: ~~~ sourcedir /run/chrony-dhcp ~~~- If there is existing machine config then delete it and apply with the updated `/etc/chrony.conf` file.- See the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform documentation on [configuring the chrony time service](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/install_config/installing-customizing.html)
root_cause: - The `/etc/chrony.conf` was missing the below line: ~~~ sourcedir /run/chrony-dhcp ~~~- As per man page of `chrony.conf` ~~~ sourcedir directory... The sourcedir directive is identical to the confdir directive, except the configuration files have the.sources suffix, they can only specify NTP sources (i.e. the server, pool, and peer directives), they are expected to have all lines terminated by the newline character, and they can be reloaded by the reload sources command in chronyc. It is particularly useful with dynamic sources like NTP servers received from a DHCP server, which can be written to a file specific to the network interface by a networking script. ~~~

title: Recommended version of VMware vSphere for OCP 4.14
issue: Which version of VMware vSphere is recommended for OpenShift Container Platform 4.14?
During the "[Whats Next in OpenShift 4.14](https://youtu.be/T0Je1UMqRNc)" presentations it was mentioned that certain vSphere versions are recommended, which ones are these?
resolution: * The required vSphere versions are described in the documentation: [VMware vSphere infrastructure requirements](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/installing/installing_vsphere/preparing-to-install-on-vsphere.html#installation-vsphere-infrastructure_preparing-to-install-on-vsphere) * Upgrades to OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 are prevented if OpenShift Container Platform is not running on vSphere 7.0u3L+ or 8.0u2+. This does not apply to clusters that already have CSI migration enabled or don’t use in-tree Persistent Volumes. * There exists an option to bypass and upgrade with an "admin ack" * VMware vSphere 7.0u3L+ or 8.0u2+ is NOT required on new OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 clusters
root_cause: * There are bugs present in vSphere <7.0u3L or vSphere <8.0u2

title: Restrict Access To RH-SSO Admin Console in OpenShift

resolution: 1. Create a configmap with the cli instructions(File jboss-cli.yaml) ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: jboss-cli data: sso-extensions.cli: | /subsystem=undertow/configuration=filter/expression-filter=ipAccess:add(,expression="path-prefix(/auth/admin)-> ip-access-control(acl={'10.0.0.0/24 allow'})") /subsystem=undertow/server=default-server/host=default-host/filter-ref=ipAccess:add() ~~~ 2. Run the command ~~~ oc create-f jboss-cli.yaml ~~~ 3. Update dc/sso ~~~ oc edit dc/sso ~~~ ~~~ volumeMounts:........- mountPath: /opt/eap/extensions name: jboss-cli volumes:......- configMap: defaultMode: 0755 name: jboss-cli name: jboss-cli ~~~ **NOTE** The example above restricts access to /auth/admin to IP addresses in the range 10.0.0.1 to 10.0.0.255. title: SSH not working from pod to external machine in  RHOCP 4
issue: - Passwordless SSH from pod to physical machine is not working: ~~~ $ oc rsh hello-world-nginx-76798d7f6-ncqmg / # ssh root@10.74.236.192 @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ @ WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE! @ @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ Permissions 0440 for '/root/.ssh/id_rsa' are too open. It is required that your private key files are NOT accessible by others. This private key will be ignored. Load key "/root/.ssh/id_rsa": bad permissions root@10.74.236.192's password: ~~~
resolution: - Remove the `securityContext.fsGroup` field which is affecting the file mode: ~~~ $ oc edit deploy/hello-world-nginx-o yaml securityContext: fsGroup: 0--------> Remove this line runAsGroup: 0 runAsUser: 0 ~~~- SSH to the external machine should work now: ~~~ $ oc rsh hello-world-nginx-5f767bdf75-mdg4f / # ls-l /root/.ssh/ total 4-r-------- 1 root root 2643 Nov 27 20:19 id_rsa / # ssh-o "StrictHostKeyChecking=no" root@10.74.236.192 Last login: Tue Nov 28 01:50:50 2023 from 10.74.236.79 [root@lab-user ~]# ~~~
root_cause: - The `fsGroup` field causes group permissions to change.- Applying `fsGroup` changes the permission of the `Secret` file. This is actually documented as expected in the API: ~~~ // Mode bits to use on created files by default. Must be a value between // 0 and 0777. // Directories within the path are not affected by this setting. // This might be in conflict with other options that affect the file // mode, like fsGroup, and the result can be other mode bits set. // +optional ~~~

title: FluentdNodeDown Alert Triggering after upgrading Logging Operator to version 5.8 in RHOCP4
issue: - Since the `upgrade` of RHOL operator to version `5.8`, `FluentdNodeDown` alerts are continuously triggered for all the `collector` pods but the pods are running fine.![Warning](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/attachments/screenshot_2023-11-24_at_17.41.43.png)
resolution: - Take the `backup` and `delete` the `prometheusrule` named `collector` under the `openshift-logging` namespace. ~~~ $ oc get prometheusrule collector-o yaml-n openshift-logging > pr_collector.yaml $ oc delete prometheusrule collector-n openshift-logging ~~~ **Note: These rules are managed by the operator and will be recreated, when the operator is reinstalled as per below steps so its safe to delete.**- `Delete` the `Subscription` & `CSV` for the `Logging` operator. ~~~ $ oc get csv,sub-n openshift-logging NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE clusterserviceversion.operators.coreos.com/cluster-logging.v5.8.0 Red Hat OpenShift Logging 5.8.0 Succeeded clusterserviceversion.operators.coreos.com/loki-operator.v5.8.0 Loki Operator 5.8.0 loki-operator.v5.7.7 Succeeded NAME PACKAGE SOURCE CHANNEL subscription.operators.coreos.com/cluster-logging cluster-logging redhat-operators stable-5.8 $ oc delete csv-n openshift-logging cluster-logging.v5.8.0 $ oc delete sub-n openshift-logging cluster-logging ~~~- Verify everything is `deleted`, Now `Uninstall` the `Logging` operator, Once the operator is properly `uninstalled` now `Install` the `Logging` operator again.- Once the operator is `Reinstalled`, Check the `Subscription`,`CSV`& `prometheusrule`. ~~~ $ oc get sub,csv-n openshift-logging $ oc get prometheusrule-n openshift-logging ~~~- Confirm if the alert has gone.
root_cause: Starting from RHOL version `5.8` the `prometheusrule` has changed from `FluentdNodeDown` to `CollectorNodeDown`, if the alert trigger after the upgrade to version `5.8` but it says `FluentdNodeDown` this means the operator has not been `upgraded` correctly.

title: How to configure PILOT_JWT_ENABLE_REMOTE_JWKS environment  variable for Istiod
issue: - `PILOT_JWT_ENABLE_REMOTE_JWKS` environment variable is supported for OCP 4.- Is there any patch command to apply `PILOT_JWT_ENABLE_REMOTE_JWKS` environment variable for fetching `JWKs` from `JwksUri` in `RequestAuthentication` for Istiod.

root_cause: - `RequestAuthentication` object giving error: ~~~ Failed to fetch jwt public key from issuer "https://example-xyz-test.abc-abc.com", jwks uri "http://example-xyz-auth.example-test-abc-test.svc.cluster.local:8080/.well-known/jwks.json": empty public key found in cache ~~~

title: Multiple restarts of RH-SSO pod before the pod could startup successfully
issue: - We have a template based installation of RH-SSO and when RH-SSO pod is started- it takes multiple restarts before the RH-SSO pod could startup successfully. How can we stop this behavior of RH-SSO pod?- RH-SSO pod is going into `CrashLoopBackOff` state during startup. The pod needs multiple restart to come in running status.
resolution: - Consider the RH-SSO startup time in `ReadinessProbe` and `LivenessProbe` [settings](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/applications/application-health.html) to:- Prevent probes getting scheduled even before RH-SSO startup- Allow certain number of probe failures to prevent unnecessary pod restarts- Consider inactivity duration for a probe after which the probe is timedout ~~~- `initialDelaySeconds`: The time(in seconds) after which probe will be scheduled- `timeoutSeconds`: The time(in seconds) of inactivity after which the probe is timedout and container is taken as failed. This value must be lower than periodSeconds.- `failureThreshold`: Number of times the probe is allowed to fail- `periodSeconds`: The difference(in seconds) between two probes ~~~
root_cause: - RH-SSO startup time is not considered while setting `ReadinessProbe` and `LivenessProbe` settings.- The `timeoutSeconds` is set to very low value.

title: Support OpenShift Oauth for AMQ Broker Console authentication and authorization using Fuse Console.
issue: - Support `OpenShift Oauth` for AMQ Broker Console authentication and authorization using `Fuse Console`.
resolution: The `Fuse Console` based on `Hawtio Online` allow to Monitor and Access to the AMQ Broker Console using **OAuth** on OpenShift. The ANQ Broker requires the following configuration to be set on the `activemqArtemis CR` in order to be managed by Fuse Console: ~~~ deploymentPlan: jolokiaAgentEnabled: true managementRBACEnabled: false ~~~ By disabling the management of `RBAC` at the broker level, the `RBAC` Config MUST be set at the Fuse Console level, like described in the following Documentation: [2.3. Role-based access control for the Fuse Console on OpenShift 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_fuse/7.12/html-single/managing_fuse_on_openshift/index#fuse-console-openshift4-rbac) To enable RBAC on Fuse Console (`Hawtio CR`), add the `rbac` section to the CR: ~~~ rbac: configMap: fuse-console-rbac ~~~ The configmap `fuse-console-rbac` should have the `ACL.yaml`. The default ACL.yaml is located here: [ACL.yaml](https://github.com/hawtio/hawtio-online/blob/main/docker/ACL.yaml) By adding the above configuration, it will be translated by the operator to an env var `HAWTIO_ONLINE_RBAC_ACL:/etc/hawtio/rbac/ACL.yaml`. The default ACL don't cover Artemis acl lines, add the following to that file: ~~~ org.apache.activemq.artemis: /list.*/: admin, viewer /is.*/: admin, viewer /get.*/: admin, viewer /set.*/: admin /manage.*/: admin, viewer /canInvoke.*/: admin, viewer /read.*/: admin, viewer /Start.*/: admin, viewer /Version.*/: admin, viewer /HAPolicy.*/: admin, viewer /Uptime.*/: admin, viewer /Address.*/: admin, viewer /Global.*/: admin, viewer ~~~ Fuse Console RBAC leverages the user’s verb access on a pod resource in OpenShift to determine the user’s access to a pod’s MBean operations in the Fuse Console. By default, there are two user roles for the Fuse Console: **admin** & **viewer**. **admin**: If a user can update a pod in OpenShift, then the user is conferred the admin role for the Fuse Console. The user can perform write MBean operations in the Fuse Console for the pod. **viewer**: If a user can get a pod in OpenShift, then the user is conferred the viewer role for the Fuse Console. The user can perform read-only MBean operations in the Fuse Console for the pod. To determine whether a user has the Fuse Console admin role for the pod, run the following command to see whether the `user` can update the pod on OpenShift: ~~~ oc auth can-i update pods/--as ~~~ For instance, for the following amq pod: ~~~ oc auth can-i update pods/amq-ss-0--as admin yes ~~~ If the response is `yes`, the user has the Fuse Console admin role for the pod. The user can perform **write** MBean operations in the Fuse Console for the pod. ~~~ oc auth can-i get pods/amq-ss-0--as viewer yes ~~~ If the response is `yes`, the user has the Fuse Console viewer role for the pod. The user can perform **read-only** MBean operations in the Fuse Console for the pod. Depending on the context, the Fuse Console prevents the user with the viewer role from performing a `write MBean` operation, by disabling an option or by displaying an "operation not allowed for this user" message when the user attempts a write MBean operation. For more information: [2.3. Role-based access control for the Fuse Console on OpenShift 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_fuse/7.12/html-single/managing_fuse_on_openshift/index#fuse-console-openshift4-rbac)

title: How to configure message load balancing and redistribution policy with the AMQ 7 OpenShift operator
issue: The documentation for AMQ 7 on OpenShift implies that it is possible to change message load balancing policy and redistribution delay. However, it does not explain how to do so.
resolution: Message load balancing policy can be `OFF`, `STRICT`, `ON_DEMAND`, or `OFF_WITH_REDISTRIBUTION`. These meanings are the same as [documented here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_amq_broker/7.11/html-single/configuring_amq_broker/index#assembly_br-enabling-message-redistribution_configuring). In addition, message redistribution can be enabled and, again, the settings are the same as they are outside OpenShift, and have the same meaning. However, there is at present no way to set these configuration elements using specific entries in the broker custom resource. Administrators will need to use the generic broker properties mechanism, like this in YAML: ``` apiVersion: broker.amq.io/v1beta1 kind: ActiveMQArtemis... spec: brokerProperties:- "clusterConfigurations.my-cluster.messageLoadBalancingType=OFF_WITH_REDISTRIBUTION"- "addressSettings.myaddress.redistributionDelay=1000" ``` Adminstrators should bear in mind that settings made this way are_not_ reflected in the `broker.xml` file generated by the operator.

title: Pushes/pulls from Quay fail with the ImmatureSignatureError exception found in Quay logs
issue: Pushes or pulls to Quay fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
resolution: - Check date/time on the nodes that access Quay and on the nodes where Quay is installed. For OpenShift installations, Chrony could be installed on the cluster; it will keep nodes time synced. For more information on how to install Chrony on OpenShift, please check [the following documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/installing/install_config/installing-customizing.html#installation-special-config-chrony_installing-customizing). For VM deployments, please see [NTP setup](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/6/html/deployment_guide/sect-date_and_time_configuration-command_line_configuration-network_time_protocol) for more information.
root_cause: - Docker v2 protocol assumes communication via JSON web tokens. The token authorizes a user to do a specific action on the repository, whether it be push or pull.- The JWT token contains a lot of information about the authorization provided, including specific time frames in which the token can be used. This includes the following:- `iss`: the service that issued the token- `aud`: the intended audience of the token (in Quay's case this is always Quay's server hostname)- `nbf`: the starting time when the token can be used- `iat`: the time when the token was issued (In case of Quay, `nbf` and `iat` times are the same)- `exp`: time when the token expires (in Quay's case JSON web tokens are valid for 1 hour)- `sub`: the name of the user who is doing the operation on a repository. All time stamps here are in Unix time format.- A sample JWT can be seen here: ~~~ {"iss": "quay", "aud": "QUAY_HOSTNAME", "nbf": 1699680454, "iat": 1699680454, "exp": 1699684054, "sub": "username", "access": [{"type": "repository", "name": "quay/mirror", "actions": ["push", "pull"]}], "context": {"version": 2, "entity_kind": "robot", "entity_reference": "username", "kind": "user", "user": "username", "com.apostille.roots": {"quay/mirror": "$disabled"}, "com.apostille.root": "$disabled"}} ~~~- Since JWT is a form of authorization, its validity is extensively checked by Quay, especially the timings. If access to Quay is tried from a node whose clock is behind Quay's (time delta between the client and Quay is negative), then Quay will reject access from that particular node. The same token might work from another node whose time is ahead of Quay node (positive time delta). For this kind of error, a `jwt.exceptions.ImmatureSignatureError` or `util.security.registry_jwt.InvalidBearerTokenException` will be raised in Quay's logs.

title: RHOCP 4 Cert Manager operator failed to obtain certificate
issue: cert-manager operator fails to obtain a certificate and shows an error similar to the following in its logs: ~~~ aabb-ccdd-eeffgghhiijj\", APIVersion:\"cert-manager.io/v1\", ResourceVersion:\"11223344\", FieldPath:\"\"}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'RetrieveError' Failed to obtain venafi certificate: x509: RSA key missing NULL parameters" ~~~ In the log snippet above, a Venafi `ClusterIssuer` is used. But the issue may not be limited to such type only.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in a private bug:- bug CM-232 For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: From a first analysis by the Engineering team, it appears that the Certification Authority used by the specific `ClusterIssuer` should be issuing certificates that include a NULL parameter within the digest information of the RSA signature. This is required as per [RFC 3279](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3279#section-2.3.1)

title: ImageStreams and Pods fail to pull images when Dev Portal generated secret is added in the namespace
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Image streams are not able to pull images from registry.redhat.io (I think not even from other external repos), following these steps: (1) Generate a token in the Registry Service Accounts app, and download it as an OpenShift secret YAML file (7457766-pull-secret.yml in my case). (2) Log into Developer Sandbox, and initialize the downloaded secret: ~~~ oc create-f 7457766-pull-secret.yml ~~~ ~~~ # create image stream $ oc replace--force-f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jboss-container-images/jboss-eap-openshift-templates/eap74/eap74-openjdk11-image-stream.json # inspect the created image stream $ oc describe is jboss-eap74-openjdk11-openshift...! error: Import failed (InternalError): Internal error occurred: registry.redhat.io/jboss-eap-7/eap74-openjdk11-openshift-rhel8:latest: illegal base64 data at input byte 20 6 seconds ago... ~~~ Also, I'm not able to build images anymore: ~~~ $ oc new-build-D $'FROM centos:7\nRUN yum install-y httpd' W1114 09:48:18.273102 33679 dockerimagelookup.go:297] container image remote registry lookup failed: docker.io/library/centos:7: illegal base64 data at input byte 20 error: unable to locate any images in image streams, local docker images with name "centos:7" ~~~ (3) Link the created secret with the "default" service account: ~~~ oc secrets link default 7457766-thofman-pull-secret--for=pull ~~~ Pods are not able to pull images from registty.redhat.io: ~~~ # start a rollout on some deployment config (or just try to create some new pod) $ oc rollout latest eap7-app-dc # inspect the newly created pod $ oc describe pod eap8-app-7f4d9f6b59-nwjtw... Events: Warning Failed 4m54s (x4 over 6m26s) kubelet Failed to pull image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/thofman-dev/eap8-app@sha256:7944a8c0c12f64b7ccbdb82023b5682736ecee76cba1c8081911d57f8fdfcd23": illegal base64 data at input byte 20... ~~~
resolution: There is an open bug [OCPBUGS-23245](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-23245) for the issue Workaround: To prevent this issue from happening, do not install the pull secret generated in step (1) into the namespace. There is no need to create a pull secret for access to the RH Image Registry on OCP 4.x, the access to the registry is enabled by default.
root_cause: [OCPBUGS-23245](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-23245)

title: oc command fails due to the corrupted kubeconfig​​ even though the --token option is specified
issue: - When running oc command with the `--token` option fails with the message: ~~~ $ oc--token=${TOKEN} whoami error loading config file ".kube/config": yaml: line 10: could not find expected ':' ~~~- Why does the command fail even though using token instead of kubeconfig?

title: SSL issue while accessing Service Mesh application
issue: - The below error is seen while accessing an application pod inside the service mesh. ~~~ connection_failure,TLS_error:_336130315:SSL_routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong_version_number ~~~
resolution: 1. Check the application pod YAML and make sure that the annotation `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeInboundPorts` does not have the container port, if it has then please remove it from deployment. ~~~ //Check if the annotation contains the container port $ oc get pod {pod-name}-n {namespace-name}-o yaml | grep "traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeInboundPorts" //Edit the deployment and remove the container port $ oc edit deployment {deployment-name}-n {namespace-name} ~~~ 2. A `Destination Rule` can be created as an alternative approach to disable the mtls for that particular application. ~~~ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 kind: DestinationRule metadata: name: disable-mtls spec: host: {application-svc}.{application-project}.svc.cluster.local trafficPolicy: tls: mode: DISABLE ~~~

title: 3scale TLS profiles
issue: A team carried out vulnerability tests on some URL's that exist in OpenShift 4.11, one of them belongs to a 3scale Developer Portal and has to do with the following: "_The use of obsolete and insecure communication protocols prior to TLSv1.3 was identified, which have multiple known design vulnerabilities for the implemented cipher suites, which they have different vulnerabilities such as POODLE, BEAST, SWEET32, LUCKY13 to mention some, which could allow unauthorized modification of blocks_" The team found information from OpenShift which mentions different profiles so it is necessary to know if 3scale supports the modern profile or has any problem regarding the previous points.
resolution: Since the route is managed by OpenShift, see the Red Hat article "[TLS configuration in OpenShift Container Platform](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5348961)" on how to configure the 3scale route TLS profile and apply it for 3scale routes.
root_cause: The HTTP server that provides access to the 3scale Developer Portal (and other portals) is through the OpenShift route process.

title: Console pods in CrashLoopBackOff after OCP 3.11 certificates renewal
issue: After running the OpenShift 3.11 internal certificates renewal Ansible [playbook](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/redeploying_certificates.html), the `console` pods in namespace `openshift-console` don't start, failing with `CrashLoopBackOff` error.
resolution: A **workaround** is to change the console container entrypoint from the default `/opt/bridge/bin/bridge` to `sh-c /opt/bridge/bin/bridge`. 1. In order to apply the change to all the `console` pods, the change must be applied to the related `console` deployment. ~~~ oc edit deployment-n openshift-console console ~~~ 2. The changes are to be applied at field `.spec.template.spec.containers[0]`. From: ~~~- command:- /opt/bridge/bin/bridge--public-dir=/opt/bridge/static--config=/var/console-config/console-config.yaml ~~~ to: ~~~- command:- sh--c- /opt/bridge/bin/bridge--public-dir=/opt/bridge/static--config=/var/console-config/console-config.yaml ~~~

title: Master nodes in OpenShift 4.12 hitting a "TECH PREVIEW: kTLS may not be fully supported" warning
issue: - The kernel of the affected master node in the OpenShift cluster is marked as tainted with the `TECH_PREVIEW` flag (`bit 16, auxiliary taint, # 65536`), with the following message in the kernel log buffer: ~~~ [1.312690] TECH PREVIEW: kTLS may not be fully supported. ~~~- The following output is also shown in these files from the filesystem, confirming the appearance of the kernel taint and that the kTLS module is marked as tainted: ~~~ $ cat /proc/sys/kernel/tainted 65536 $ for module in `ls-d /sys/module/*`; do echo "Module $module: `cat $module/taint`"; done... Module /sys/module/tls: X... ~~~- This issue is really important for the OpenShift CNF Certification program for partners, since there is one test, called [platform-alteration-tainted-node-kernel](https://github.com/test-network-function/cnf-certification-test/blob/main/CATALOG.md#platform-alteration-tainted-node-kernel), which checks that the CNFs are deployed in clusters where there are no kernel taints present. So, a failure in this test can imply complications in partner certification. Currently, this error can be whitelisted with the certification tool configuration, to make this test suite to pass, but this does not avoid the fact that the kernel taint is still there.- Affected OpenShift clusters run `metal3`.- This issue only appears on one of the master nodes of the OpenShift cluster, and the node is picked randomly, depending on the allocation of the `metal3` pod running in the cluster.
resolution: The issue is not present in OCP 4.13, where OCP nodes use RHEL 9, and kTLS is still `Tech-Preview`, but does not taint the kernel. Then, the solution is to upgrade the cluster to OCP 4.13 or higher, where all OCP nodes are running RHEL 9 and are not hitting the issue. If running OCP 4.12, with RHEL 8 based nodes, the issue is unavoidable.
root_cause: - For Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 8 nodes, reverting `metal3` back to RHCOS 8 is not possible. So, one solution that could be applied is to prevent the kTLS kernel module from loading. However, this makes `metal3` pods not to work properly because of the dependencies of other modules with kTLS module, then causing the nodes to move to an inconsistent state.- These are the three modules that depend on kTLS in RHEL 8, because they support kTLS offload: ~~~ $ lsmod | grep tls tls 102400 10 cxgb4,bonding,mlx5_core ~~~ In particular, the bonding module is making `metal3` pod to not work properly if disabled. Consequently, loading these modules fails without the `tls` module loadable, so blacklisting kTLS would break these drivers, thus this is unacceptable, therefore the solution above.- Under the scope of the Jira ticket [OCPBUGS-3083](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-3083), it is observable that, from the OS point of view, it is behaving as expected (i.e. running a kernel marked with an `auxiliary taint` after the use of a feature marked as `Tech-Preview`). In particular, in the cases analyzed, this warning appears fairly late in the master node’s journal logs, which suggests that the kernel and OS themselves should be fine and normally untainted as long as kTLS is not used.- In RHEL 8, `OpenSSL v1.1.1` was used. In RHEL 9, `OpenSSL` moved to `v3.0.0`. When kTLS support was [added to OpenSSL](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/14595), it was on by default and it was needed to pass specific options to turn it off. However, that was [later changed](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/13794) to be off by default [in 3.0.0-alpha15](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/a3a54179b6754fbed6d88e434baac710a83aaf80) (included in RHEL 9), and it would now have to pass an option to specifically enable it. A flag corresponding to this option was [added to Python 3.12](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/ssl.html?highlight=tls#ssl.OP_ENABLE_KTLS), but there is [no evidence](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Apsf%2Frequests%20OP_ENABLE_KTLS&type=code) that it is used by the requests library.- In the case analyzed here (`metal3` pods), the build config includes `enable-ktls` compiled in the kernel, which is what makes kTLS to be activated. This causes OpenSSL to run this syscall: ~~~ > setsockopt(5, SOL_TCP, TCP_ULP, "ktls", 4) ~~~ This will cause the kernel to do crypto work in kernel space. This syscall is what causes the kernel taint. Once it is compiled into OpenSSL, it looks like there is no way to disable it.- Given the aforementioned information, it is possible to determine that the `metal3` pod running in the OpenShift cluster causes the taint because `metal3` requires kTLS for its operation. In particular, the `metal3` pod always runs in a single master node, so that is the reason why only one master node from the OCP cluster is tainted.- The issue is triggered by the combination of OpenSSL 3.0 from the `ubi9` container base image used by `metal3` in OCP 4.12 with the kTLS kernel module from RHEL 8, which is the OS version for the OCP nodes in OCP 4.12. Under these circumstances, when compiled with kTLS support, OpenSSL indiscriminately calls `ktls_enable()` (which makes the `setsockopt()` call that triggers the kernel module to be loaded) on every socket, just in case it might be needed later. Running this on a RHEL 8 host is what taints the host.

title: MultiClusterObservability CR is unable to be configured in RHOCP4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - While `annotating` the ServiceAccount to use STS with S3 role in `MultiClusterObservability` CR, below error is firing, ~~~ Invalid value: "string": spec.advanced.store in body must be of type object: "string"" for field "spec.advanced.store" ~~~
resolution: - A Documentation bug [ACM-7945](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-7945) has been raised for the issue and is resolved in RHACM version 2.7, 2.8 and 2.9.- RHACM v2.9: [Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.9/html-single/observability/index#creating-mco-cr)- RHACM v2.8: [Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.8/html-single/observability/index#creating-mco-cr)- RHACM v2.7: [Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.7/html-single/observability/index#creating-mco-cr)
root_cause: - In the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.6/html-single/observability/index#creating-mco-cr) while adding parameters in `advanced` section, for annotating the `ServiceAccounts` to use STS with S3 role, configuration looked like below, ~~~ $ oc get spec: advanced: compact: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=$S3_ROLE store: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=$S3_ROLE rule: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=$S3_ROLE receive: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=$S3_ROLE query: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=$S3_ROLE ~~~- Whereas it is mentioned in the `documentation` that **If S3 bucket is configured to use STS tokens, annotate the service accounts to use STS with S3 role.**- For that `serviceAccountAnnotations` field should be applied in `spec.advanced.compact` section like below, ~~~ spec: advanced: compact: serviceAccountAnnotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: $S3_ROLE store: serviceAccountAnnotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: $S3_ROLE rule: serviceAccountAnnotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: $S3_ROLE receive: serviceAccountAnnotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: $S3_ROLE query: serviceAccountAnnotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: $S3_ROLE ~~~

title: How Do I Set Up Mirroring for a Clustered Broker in OpenShift?
issue: It is relatively straightforward to set up a mirror between two single-broker AMQ instances running in separate OpenShift clusters, but what if the source and target AMQ instances are clustered? A mirror needs to be between individual brokers and mirroring to a load-balanced endpoint does not appear to work. How do I accomplish mirroring when I have, for example 2 3-node clusters (one as the source and the other as the target)?
resolution: When configuring the mirror with brokerProperties, it is possible to preface each property with a *broker-N* prefix, indicating that the property should be applied to an individual broker instance, rather than to all the brokers in the cluster. So for configuring an individual mirror connection for each broker in a cluster, the syntax would look something like: ~~~ broker-0.AMQPConnections.\"target-async-mirror\".uri=tcp://{exposed URI of target broker 0} broker-1.AMQPConnections.\"target-async-mirror\".uri=tcp://{exposed URI of target broker 1} broker-2.AMQPConnections.\"target-async-mirror\".uri=tcp://{exposed URI of target broker 2} ~~~

title: A registry CA is not added/renewed into nodes when adding it as additionalTrustedCA to the image configuration in OpenShift 4
issue: - After adding a CA via the `additionalTrustedCA` in the `image.config` resource to solve the issue described in [Failed to pull image with x509: certificate signed by unknown authority error when using mirrored registries in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7035834), the CA is not added to the OpenShift 4 nodes.- Trying to [configure additional trust stores for image registry access](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/openshift_images/image-configuration.html#images-configuration-cas_image-configuration), the CA is not added to the OpenShift 4 nodes.- The `cluster-image-registry-operator` is failing with `ImagePullBackOff` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` message.
resolution: First of all it is needed to check that the `configmap` is correct, and the `image.config` resource is referencing it correctly. Another possible cause of the issue is the `cluster-image-registry-operator` `pod` not working as expected. In some cases, that `pod` could be failing when pulling the image from the registry (for example, for disconnected OpenShift 4 clusters). In that case, it will be needed to manually pull the image for that `pod`, to allow the `cluster-image-registry-operator` to work properly: 1. Check the image for the `cluster-image-registry-operator` `pod` that is failing, and the node in which that pod is failing: ~~~ $ oc get events-n openshift-image-registry | grep cluster-image-registry-operator [...] Failed to pull image "quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:xxxxxxxx [...] $ oc get pods-n openshift-image-registry-o wide | grep cluster-image-registry-operator cluster-image-registry-operator-xxxxxxxx-xxxxx 0/1 ImagePullBackOff 0 20d 10.0.0.1 [node_name] ~~~ 2. Access to the node in which the image is failing, and create a directory in `/tmp` for the certificate (using `oc debug node` could fail if the debug image needs to be downloaded for the node): ~~~ $ ssh [node_name] $ mkdir-p /tmp/certs $ cd /tmp/certs/ ~~~ 3. Create a `ca.crt` file in that directory, with the content of the registry's CA: ~~~ $ vi ca.crt-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- [...] ~~~ 4. Try to manually pull the image with `podman pull`, including the directory where the CA was added (change only the `[image_name]` in the following command): ~~~ $ sudo-i # podman pull--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json--cert-dir /tmp/certs/ [image_name] ~~~ If the image is correctly downloaded this way, the `cluster-image-registry-operator` should start working, and the CA configured in the `image.config` resource be added to all the nodes.
root_cause: There could be different reasons for the CA not being included in the `pods`, like wrong configuration of the `configmap` or the `image.config` resource, or the `cluster-image-registry-operator` `pod` not working as expected.

title: error validating data: ValidationError(AlertmanagerConfig.spec.receivers[0]): unknown field "msteamsConfigs"
issue: - How to send alerts via `Microsoft Teams` instead of email or opsgenie?- Getting error while adding `msTeamsConfig` to the `AlertmanagerConfig CRD`. ~~~ Error: UPGRADE FAILED: error validating "": error validating data: ValidationError(AlertmanagerConfig.spec.receivers[0]): unknown field "msteamsConfigs" in com.coreos.monitoring.v1beta1.AlertmanagerConfig.spec.receivers ~~~
resolution: - `MSTeamsConfig` configures notifications via `Microsoft Teams`. It requires `Alertmanager` > = [0.26.0.](https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/blob/main/Documentation/api.md#monitoring.coreos.com/v1alpha1.MSTeamsConfig).- `Alertmanager` native support for `MSteams` is scheduled for release as part of OCP 4.15 with the `Alertmanager` version > 0.26.0.- There is a workaround to [proxy set up alertmanager to send alerts to Microsoft Teams in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6954585).
root_cause: - MSTeamsConfig` configures notifications via `Microsoft Teams`. It requires `Alertmanager` > = [0.26.0.] which is scheduled for release as part of OCP 4.15.

title: keepalived auth_pass contains a predictable password
issue: - `/etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf` contains a predictable password, generated from cluster name
resolution: Predictable passwords in keepalived authentication are not a security issue because VRRP passwords are transmitted in clear text as per VRRP protocol design, so they can be found out just by performing network capture with `tcpdump` or similar. As they offer no security, using a stronger password doesn't make a difference
root_cause: **Disclaimer:**_Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ The [section 10.2 of RFC2338](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2338#section-10.2) defines that VRRP passwords are sent in clear text with the following text ~~~ The use of this authentication type means that VRRP protocol exchanges are authenticated by a simple clear text password. ~~~ i.e. this is a VRRP protocol limitation, not a keepalived limitation. The same section suggests that the use case for this "authentication" is to prevent configuration mistakes. In later [RFC3768](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3768#section-5.3.6), these authorization mechanisms were just removed and authentication fields were as "reserved" and unused, only for backwards compatibility. Rationale provided is: ~~~ Earlier version of the VRRP specification had several defined authentication types [RFC2338]. These were removed in this specification because operational experience showed that they did not provide any real security and would only cause multiple masters to be created. ~~~

title: Backend-redis crashing due to "(in server root dir /var/lib/redis/data): Input/output error"
issue: - `backend-redis`component is crashing (CrashLoopBackOff) showing in its logs this error: (in server root dir /var/lib/redis/data): Input/output
resolution: In most cases, this issue appears when `backend-redis` component tries to write to its PV assigned and there are some problems with the underlaying storage system used for that particular PV (e.g. issues regarding glusterfs). As the `backend-redis` pod is a standard redis pod, from a 3scale API Management perspective, there is not much to troubleshoot. Therefore, the troubleshooting has to focus on the storage system that provides the PV to the `backend-redis` pod. For the storage issue troubleshooting is highly likely the shift-storage team will require some of these items:- What node are the `backend-redis` pod scheduled to in the Openshift cluster?- Collect a sosreport from that node- Provide the storageclass definition for whichever PV is associated with the `backend-redis` pod data directory- Share the output of 'oc get pods-o wide-n ' **Once the storage issue is resolved**, `backend-redis` pod will be able to start normally after a new rollout by running the following command: $ oc rollout latest dc/backend-redis After `backend-redis`pod is up and running again, it may be required to also rollout its dependent components: $ oc rollout latest dc/backend-cron $ oc rollout latest dc/backend-worker
root_cause: - If there is any issue with the `backend-redis` storage volume, that can prevent `backend-redis` pod to be in a *Running* state since it will start crashing repeatedly until the problem with the underlaying redis storage volume is resolved.- When `backend-redis` is not in a 'Running' state its dependent components like `backend-cron` and `backend-worker` may fail too.

title: How to skip the validation of SSL for KServe
issue: When models are in the Minio that is using SSL with a self-signed certificate, it was not possible to create a connection without cabundle. How can I use `skip validation ssl` to pull a model from the Minio?
resolution: KServe provides a feature to bypass SSL validation; however, the Red Hat OpenShift AI UI currently lacks the capability to configure this option. Within a user namespace, there exists a Secret named storage-config that encapsulates registry information. When creating a data connection through the dashboard, this secret is automatically generated and is under the management of odh-model-controller. It's important to note that, at present, the dashboard does not provide an interface to configure the skip-validation field. Consequently, there arises a necessity to manually designate the storage-config Secret as unmanaged. Note: This workaround enables the utilization of specific functionalities and anticipates future support within the dashboard for this configuration. To configure the verify-ssl field within the storage-config Secret, follow these steps: 1. Make the Secret "storage-config" to `unmanaged` ~~~ oc label secret/storage-config opendatahub.io/managed=false--overwrite ~~~ 2. Update the credential key in the storage-config. (ex) This is an example when the key name is aws-connection-s3 ~~~ ❯ oc get secret storage-config-o yaml apiVersion: v1 data: aws-connection-s3: XXX kind: Secret metadata: labels: opendatahub.io/managed: "false" name: storage-config type: Opaque ~~~ You can add this field `{"verify_ssl": "false"}` in the aws-connection-s3 value using OpenShift console. [image=[src="images/dashboard-1.png", alt="OpenShift Console Secret Edit Page", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="editing storage-config Secret", lightbox="true"]] Data will be like this: ~~~ {"access_key_id": "XXX", "bucket": "XXX", "default_bucket": "XXX", "endpoint_url": "https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/", "region": "us-east-2", "secret_access_key": "XXX", "type": "s3", "verify_ssl": "false"} ~~~ After you update the Secret, you need to restart the runtime pod. Then it will skip the validation check of SSL.

issue: - Alert received from AWS ~~~ AWS case ID: XXXXX for Application: XXXXX- XXXXX AccountId: XXXXXX Subject: [Amazon GuardDuty Finding] DefenseEvasion:EC2/UnusualDNSResolver- Finding Severity: Medium Category: security-issue Service: service-ams-operations-report-incident TimeCreated: XXXX-XX-XXXX Details: Hello, AWS Managed Services has detected an Amazon GuardDuty finding within your managed account: This alert is about a potential security issue discovered by Amazon GuardDuty. DefenseEvasion:EC2/UnusualDNSResolver- EC2 instance i-XXXXX is communicating with an Unusual DNS Resolver 170.247.170.2 The alert summary can be found below: Description: EC2 instance i-XXXXX is communicating with an Unusual DNS Resolver 170.247.170.2. Account ID: XXXXXXXX Region: af-south-1 Created At: XXXX-XX-XXXX Severity: 5 Finding Severity: Medium ~~~
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*- The finding type `DefenseEvasion:EC2/UnusualDNSResolver` is generated by GuardDuty for an EC2 instance in AWS environment, if the instance is behaving in a way that deviates from the baseline behavior [1]. GuardDuty uses a baseline as a reference for this finding type, wherein it profiles EC2 instance's behavior. Any DNS traffic that falls outside of this baseline, will be flagged as suspicious thereby generating this finding.- The IPv4 address for `b.root-servers.net` was changed on November 27, 2023 [2]. title: Why does Clair report more container image vulnerabilities in my Quay registry after I upgrade Quay?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - After we upgraded Quay and Clair our users noticed a increase in the number of vulnerabilities reported on their container images. This is causing confusion with all our OpenShift customers and increasing the number of tickets opened with our OpenShift DevOps team.
resolution: - It is normal for Clair to report more vulnerabilities after an upgrade of Quay and Clair.- With new releases of Clair, the security scanning component of Quay, new OVAL databases may be added to the sources that Clair uses to pull vulnerability data. Additionally, many libraries and utilities that Clair uses internally are upgraded which may better identify vulnerabilities in container images.- This is discussed in the [Vulnerability reporting with Clair on Red Hat Quay](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_quay/3.8/html/vulnerability_reporting_with_clair_on_red_hat_quay/index) documentation.- To view the code that changes in each release of Clair, refer to the [Clair Release Notes](https://github.com/quay/clair/releases).
root_cause: - Clair developers add new OVAL vulnerabilty databases- Clair developers update internal libraries and utilities that are more efficient and effective at locating vulnerabilities

title: How to use MFA with oc cli ?
issue: - We have configured RH-SSO as oidc identity provider in Openshift and for `oc` cli login we are using Direct Grant of RH-SSO. How can we enable multi factor authentication in `oc` cli login?- We have RH-SSO configured as Identify Provider in Openshift. In browser a RH-SSO user can successfully log in using password and OTP, while when trying to login using same user through`oc` cli- users are getting HTTP 401. ~~~ $ oc login-u xxxxx--server=https://api-server-hostname:6443 Authentication required for https://api-server-hostname:6443(xxxx) Username: xxxxx Password: Login failed (401 Unauthorized) Verify you have provided correct credentials. ~~~
resolution: - With `oc` cli use `--web` option which enables [login](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/cli_reference/openshift_cli/getting-started-cli.html#cli-logging-in-web_cli-developer-commands) through web browser. This flag was added in [OCP 4.14](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes.html#ocp-4-14-openshift-cli).- In the web browser a user can login with MFA and redirect back to the terminal with the token.- Users can select the identity provider of their choice to login, in case there are multiple identity providers configured in the Openshift cluster.
root_cause: - `oc` cli does not has the feature to callback(or request) for second factor authentication(like OTP), instead the request fails with HTTP 401.

title: crio results in malformatted: Invalid character(s) found in prerelease \"el8_6\"  on RHEL worker nodes while upgrading ocp cluster from 4.10 to 4.11
issue: - The crio service is failing on RHEL worker nodes during cluster upgrade with the below mentioned error: ``` Error encountered when checking whether cri-o should wipe images: version constant 1.24.6-6.1.rhaos4.11.git7f73171.el8_6 malformatted: Invalid character(s) found in prerelease \"el8_6\" ```
