Please update to `cri-o-1.24.6-7.1.rhaos4.11.git7f731711.el8` and above.- As a workaround, downgrade the crio version on RHEL nodes: ``` $ dnf downgrade crio ```
root_cause: - An issue has been identified in the recently released version of the crio package within the [errata](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7481).

title: OADP  failed to restore PV using restic
issue:
- `PV` restore failed with restoring pv with `restic`. `nodeagent` pod log shows below error: ~~~ $ oc logs node-agent-xxx-n openshift-adp.... 2023-11-20T03:07:23.598346892Z time="2023-11-20T03:07:23Z" level=info msg="Run command=restore, stdout=restoring to.
, stderr=ignoring error for /aa.txt: lchown /host_pods/171b6dd7-b6db-4c6a-9caf-0b4ed3f5e79f/volumes/kubernetes.io~nfs/pvc-eb0866bb-b230-416b-85c9-97debd777b73/aa.txt: operation not permitted
Fatal: There were 1 errors

" PodVolumeRestore=openshift-adp/ controller=PodVolumeRestore logSource="/remote-source/velero/app/pkg/uploader/provider/restic.go:184" pod=nginx-example/ restore=openshift-adp/ snapshotID=0e9f0344 volumePath="/host_pods/171b6dd7-b6db-4c6a-9caf-0b4ed3f5e79f/volumes/kubernetes.io~nfs/pvc-eb0866bb-b230-416b-85c9-97debd777b73".... ~~~
resolution: - By default NFS volume shares are `root_squash` i.e. NFS directory is non-accessible to root.- With `root_squash`, `restic` will be mapped to `nfsnobody` and will not have enough permissions to perform the backup/restore. This has been documented in our MTC product as well as customers also required the use of `root_squash` and ran into some issues, [refer here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/migration-toolkit-for-containers/troubleshooting-mtc.html#restic-permission-error-when-migrating-from-nfs-storage-with-root-squash-enabled_troubleshooting-mtc). There are 2 ways to get around this issue: 1. Use supplemental groups and apply this same supplemental group to the restic daemonset (this change will need to be submitted to OADP as well to mimic MTC, which shouldn't be an issue if this is strongly desired). 2. Set `no_root_squash`.
root_cause: - Configuration at NFS server side.

title: UDP packets are subject to SNAT when Load Balancer Service is configured with session affinity timeout in Azure Cloud
issue: - Load Balancer Service with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` and session affinity timeout is used to provide external access to a UDP server- SNAT is performed on UDP packets in Azure Cloud coming from outside of the cluster trough the Load Balancer Service- Due to SNAT the original source IP is lost. Therefore, the source IP seen by microservice istance is the OVN-Kubernetes Gateway Router that has a 100.64.0.0/16 IP
resolution: - The bug has been fixed in ovn22.12-22.12.1-11.el9fdp.x86_64.rpm- The fix is available in OCP 4.13.16 and later- Every customer is encouraged to upgrade to the latest OCP 4.13 z-stream- After the upgrade the OVN logical rules of the OVN Gateway Router of the node hosting the pod will look like the following: ``` $ oc exec-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-it ovnkube-master-pgl5r-c sbdb-- ovn-sbctl lflow-list GR_azure-ipi-1-nnlqq-worker-eastus1-zs5lg | grep 192.0.2.3 | grep 192.0.2.1 table=7 (lr_in_dnat), priority=150, match=(reg9[6] == 1 && ct.new && ip4 && reg4 == 192.0.2.3 && reg8[0..15] == 10001), action=(reg0 = 192.0.2.1; flags.skip_snat_for_lb = 1; ct_lb_mark(backends=192.0.2.3:10001; skip_snat);) table=7 (lr_in_dnat), priority=120, match=(ct.new &&!ct.rel && ip4 && ip4.dst == 192.0.2.1 && udp && udp.dst == 10001), action=(flags.skip_snat_for_lb = 1; ct_lb_mark(backends=192.0.2.3:10001; skip_snat);) table=8 (lr_in_lb_aff_learn), priority=100, match=(reg9[6] == 0 && ct.new && ip4 && reg0 == 192.0.2.1 && reg9[16..31] == 10001 && ip4.dst == 192.0.2.3 && udp.dst == 10001), action=(commit_lb_aff(vip = "192.0.2.1:10001", backend = "192.0.2.3:10001", proto = udp, timeout = 300); /* drop */) ```
root_cause: - Using a Load Balancer Service configured with session affinity timeout causes the SNAT even if the service has the externalTrafficPolicy equals to Local- This is a known OVN-Kubernetes bug where the configured timeout causes the generation of three OVN logical rules. The rule with the highest priority has the flag `force_snat_for_lb`

title: Physical interface rename during upgrade from OpenShift 4.12 to 4.13 breaking bond connections
issue: - One of the physical interfaces of a LACP bonding gets renamed after upgrade from OCP 4.12 to 4.13 (Using Mellanox ConnectX-5 NICs)- Network card with two interfaces, one interface had its name changed from eno34 to eno34np1. During upgrade from RHEL 8 to RHEL 9 (4.12--> 4.13 OCP)
resolution: - This issue is being tracked in bug [OCPBUGS-17877](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-17877)- See this KCS to restore networking on nodes + pull a sosreport: [Recovering a node that has lost all networking in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7046419)- This issue has been resolved in the following versions, it is advisable to upgrade when possible to the following versions: [https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0741](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0741)- 4.13.33+ [https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0642](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0642)- 4.14.11+ [https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7198](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7198)- 4.15.0+ ================================================- If you want to move forward with `eno34np1` and `eno33np0`: Remove `/etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link` and `/etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link` and reboot to rename both interfaces automatically to the new naming schema.- If you want the old `eno33` and `eno34` back: Update the MAC address in `/etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-.link` to match the NIC MAC address and reboot to get the desired interface name for `eno34`.- After upgrading to the new version your devices will be `eno33np0` and `eno34np1` so please fix the file under `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/*.nmconnection` accordingly to reflect new interface names.- Please do not try to rename the devices as `eno33` and `eno34` because you cannot use names reserved from the kernel, you can use other names as `net0` and `net1` if you would like, but do not use reserved names, if you use them, it might work for now but unexpected behavior may occur in future releases/updates that may complicate.
root_cause: - The MAC address in `/etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link` is wrong. It has been mapped based on the bond's mac and not the permanent MAC address that was previously expected/used. ~~~ $ grep "" etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno3*.link etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link:# Generated by nmstate etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link:[Match] etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link:MACAddress=B8:xx:xx:xx:xx:D0 etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link: etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link:[Link] etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno33.link:Name=eno33 etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link:# Generated by nmstate etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link:[Match] etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link:MACAddress=B8:xx:xx:xx:xx:D0 ## <--same mac as eno33!! etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link: etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link:[Link] etc/systemd/network/98-nmstate-eno34.link:Name=eno34 ~~~ Lets look up the actual MAC address for `eno34`: ~~~ $ egrep "Slave|Permanent HW addr" proc/net/bonding/bond0 Slave Interface: eno33 Permanent HW addr: b8:xx:xx:xx:xx:d0 Slave queue ID: 0 Slave Interface: eno34np1 Permanent HW addr: b8:xx:xx:xx:xx:d1 <--- correct mac address. (does not match 98-nmstate-eno34.link) Slave queue ID: 0 ~~~- Upstream bug: [nmstate's persist-nic-names](https://github.com/nmstate/nmstate/pull/2301/commits/45a382e2723749c8955fa208cb7e40620fb80d45#diff-037c6f719babb7a702deb8727cf5b1e6f4db57014a1e2d7808ad02b0e11f5b70R101-R109)- OpenShift 4.12 was based on RHEL 8.6, OpenShift 4.13 and 4.14 are both based on RHEL 9.2, which incorporates a very large number of handling changes. [See Version map here.](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6907891)

title: Metrics not available for cert-manager operator
issue: - After [enabling monitoring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/security/cert_manager_operator/cert-manager-monitoring.html) for the `cert-manager` operator, the `metrics` are not visible under `Observe > Metrics`:![Metrics not available](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/screenshot_2023-12-04_at_11.09.15_pm.png)- certmanager-
`metrics` not available `Observe > Metrics`.
resolution: 1. [Enable monitoring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/security/cert_manager_operator/cert-manager-monitoring.html) for the `cert-manager` operator. 2. title: Is RH-SSO (or RHBK) deployed on OpenShift using an Embedded PostgreSQL database Supported ?
issue: Is the usage of an `embedded PostgreSQL database` backend supported in production when RH-SSO (or RHBK) is deployed on Openshift?
resolution: ## 1. title: DNS query still going to the old DNS server after updating /etc/resolv.conf via NMstate
issue: - After updating the DNS servers in the /etc/resolv.conf via the NMstate, the CoreDNS resolver still uses the old DNS servers- The updated DNS servers in the /etc/resolv.conf file on the CoreOS nodes is not used in the CoreDNS of OpenShift
resolution: - Restart the dns-default pods to use the updated DNS servers in the CoreDNS. ~~~ $ oc rollout restart ds/dns-default-n openshift-dns ~~~
root_cause: - The old DNS entries are cached in the CoreDNS pods, restarting the pods will clear cache and the CoreDNS will use the updated DNS servers.

title: Unable to add AD users to Quay
issue: - When adding Active Directory users to Quay, the following error occurs: ~~~ Could not link external user Email has already been used: UseremailID@domain.com ~~~
resolution: - **NOTE:** This problem is not caused by Quay. But, some common checks points could be:- Ensure that your SMTP server is correctly configured to allow relaying for the specified recipient's domain. You may need to check your SMTP server's settings and permissions.- If the SMTP server requires authentication, make sure that you are providing valid credentials (username and password) when trying to send the email.- Double-check that the recipient's email address ("user@example.com" in this case) is correct and valid. There might be a typo or an issue with the address itself.- check the SMTP configuration/logs with your SMTP admin to find more information
root_cause: - SMTP relays/forwards an email through an SMTP server to its final destination. In this case, it seems that the SMTP server is denying the relay of the email to the recipient user@example.com.

title: How to get OpenShift 4 metrics using the Thanos REST API
issue: How can I scrape OpenShift metrics from the Thanos querier REST API?
resolution: The Thanos instance deployed as part of the OpenShift Monitoring stack can be queried for cluster metrics via its REST API. To do so, first you require an authentication token for the `prometheus-k8s` service account to build a `curl` command that can be executed from within the prometheus container: ``` $ TOKEN=`oc create token prometheus-k8s-n openshift-monitoring` ``` Next define the query. The following example will query the "up" targets in the `openshift-monitoring namespace`, where pod name contains the word `thanos`: ``` $ QUERY="query=up{namespace='openshift-monitoring', pod=~'.*thanos.*'}" ``` The URL variable is the Thanos REST API: ``` $ URL="https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc:9091/api/v1/query?" ``` Finally, use the `oc exec` command to run `curl` from within the `prometheus` container to query the API: ``` $ oc-n openshift-monitoring exec-c prometheus prometheus-k8s-0-- curl-sGkX GET-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"-H \"Accept: application/json"\-H \"Content-Type: application/json"\--data-urlencode "${QUERY}" ${URL} | jq ``` The output of the above exampleis as follows: ``` {"status": "success", "data": {"resultType": "vector", "result": [{"metric": {"__name__": "up", "container": "kube-rbac-proxy-metrics", "endpoint": "metrics", "instance": "10.128.2.22:9094", "job": "thanos-querier", "namespace": "openshift-monitoring", "pod": "thanos-querier-5854cbd895-ckpvm", "prometheus": "openshift-monitoring/k8s", "service": "thanos-querier"}, "value": [1701749202.498, "1"]}, {"metric": {"__name__": "up", "container": "kube-rbac-proxy-metrics", "endpoint": "metrics", "instance": "10.129.3.117:9094", "job": "thanos-querier", "namespace": "openshift-monitoring", "pod": "thanos-querier-5854cbd895-ht2gn", "prometheus": "openshift-monitoring/k8s", "service": "thanos-querier"}, "value": [1701749202.498, "1"]}]}} ``` Adjust the `QUERY` variable as required.

title: A Method to Determine Socket Connection Duration
issue: - How do I know how long a connection has been Established?- How long has a socket remained open?
resolution: There are multiple methods to observe the duration of a socket connection in Linux. Without continuous observation of a socket over time, figuring out the time since creation of a socket can be done through inspection of the socket file descriptor. Unfortunately *Birth* is likely left blank but the *Change* (specific to kernel ctime struct) parameter of the socket can be inspected. This can be done by obtaining the **file descriptor** (integer reference to an open file) of the socket, then running a *stat* on the specified file descriptor in the */proc* directory. The *Change* time can then be compared to the current time. To obtain the file descriptor, the *ss* binary can be used with process name or ID: ~~~ # would need to be replaced by process name $ PROC= $ PID=$(pidof ${PROC}) # For more detail $ ps-lfp ${PID} ~~~ *ps parameters*- **-l**- Long format- **-f**- full-format listing- **-p**- Select by PID Run *ss*, filtering for the process name or PID with *grep*. As shown below **fd** is the file descriptor: ~~~ $ ss-nptu | grep ${PROC} tcp ESTAB 0 0 xx.xx.xx.xx:40552 xx.xx.xx.xx:80 users:(("nginx",pid=13610,fd=29)) ~~~ *ss parameters*- **-n**- Do not resolve service names- **-p**- Show process using socket- **-t**- Show TCP sockets- **-u**- Show UDP sockets The file descriptor can also be found through tools like *lsof*: ~~~ $ lsof-i tcp-a-p ${PID}-w ~~~ *lsof parameters*- **-i**- Define internet specifics-> here we define protocol as tcp- **-a**- AND options together- **-p**- Specify process ID to filter- **-w**- Ignore warnings Once the file descriptor has been identified, proceed to inspect the file descriptor of the socket through the */proc* file hierarchy: ~~~ # FD set to 29 based on the output of `ss` above $ FD=29 $ ls-l /proc/${PID}/fd/${FD} # Below command takes current date compared to Change time of file $ date +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%N"; stat-c %z /proc/${PID}/fd/${FD} ~~~ Inspect the *Change* time, and compare it to the current time. The *Change* time of a socket file descriptor is not the *Creation* of that file, but rather the timestamp of any change to inode specific data. As the file descriptor is a symbolic link to the in-memory pseudo file that makes up the socket attributes, it is unlikely this information is changing, it can be used as long as it is understood that any modification to file descriptor inode variables (uid, gid, mode,...) will cause file descriptor information to be unreliable. See [When does the system update timestamps of a file?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6079901), and [How can I see a file's creation time (crtime)?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/61571) for more details.
root_cause: In today's layer 7 networking stack, protocols like HTTP/2, websockets, mqtt, etc. have the tendency to keep sockets open. Even at a lower layer like tcp/ip, strategies like *connection pooling* will also maintain connection persistence. This can eventually increase resource utilization like CPU and Memory, leading to resource saturation. The protocols specified may be implemented through libraries and there is little thought on how they could push a system to performance degradation. The method provided is a simple means to try to obtain a understanding on which sockets may be opened for long periods of time, without having to actively monitor the sockets. One could watch (or implement a script to watch) for new connections, store the initialization time, and then continue watching until the connection is destroyed. This may not be the most desired or efficient method, and so the provided steps in this documentation will hopefully help to implement a strategy on understanding which connections remain open over time on a system.

title: Configuring ArgoCD web console session timeout
issue: I want to set configure the ArgoCD Web Console session timeout.
How do I set a limit on ArgoCD's user sessions in the web console?
resolution: ### For users authenticating directly with ArgoCD credentials Using the `extraConfig` parameter of the ArgoCD instance, the administrator can set the desired timeout for their users with the parameter `users.session.duration: `. For example, setting the timeout to 5 minutes would use the value `users.session.duration: 5m`, which we can add to the configuration using `oc edit`: ```sh $ oc edit argocd... spec: extraConfig: users.session.duration: 5m...... ``` This will have the users logout after 5 minutes of time. *NOTE: this value is set in the user's token on login, so this value will not change the expiration time of users currently logged in. Users will have to logout of the previous session before the new session duration will take effect.* This feature was enabled in OpenShift GitOps 1.6 [^1] ### For users authenticating via OpenShift Single Sign-On (SSO) It will require setting two parameters across two CRs, one for Oauth and one for the ArgoCD instance you want to add the timeout to. For the Oauth object, we just need to update the spec such that `.spec.tokenConfig.accessTokenInactivityTimeout` includes a timeout, like so: ``` $ oc edit oauth cluster... apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: OAuth metadata: name: cluster spec: tokenConfig: accessTokenInactivityTimeout: 300s... ``` The ArgoCD instance will then need to have the following `spec.sso.dex` configuration: ```sh $ oc edit argocds.argoproj.io... apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1beta1 kind: ArgoCD metadata: name:... spec: sso: dex: openShiftOAuth: true config: | expiry: idTokens: "10m" ``` This will set the timeout in ArgoCD to 10m. This can, naturally, be configured as desired; the only requirements are that the Oauth timeout **needs to be less than the ArgoCD timeout**, and that **the GitOps version is > = 1.12**. [^1]: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-1964

title: Exclude kubelet daemon is running in unconfined_t

title: When adding worker nodes to an OpenShift Baremetal cluster installed via Assisted Installer, Machines are neither created nor added to the MachineSet.
issue: - After adding worker nodes using the Add Hosts option in the Assisted Installer service, the new node doesn't have an associated BareMetalHost or Machine.
resolution: 1. Scale up MS by adding 1 more host: ~~~ $ oc get machineset-A NAMESPACE NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE openshift-machine-api ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0 2 2 2 2 3h33m ~~~ ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=3 machineset ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-n openshift-machine-api ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-master-0 Running 3h37m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-master-1 Running 3h37m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-master-2 Running 3h37m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-i9lc3 Running 173m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-x6f8d Running 173m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-hqed3 Provisioning 2m44s ~~~ 2. Create a BMH template for the new machine: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api get bmh ocpworker02-o yaml > bmh-ocpworker03.yaml ~~~- Replace "metadata.name:" and "spec.bootMACAddress:"- Add "spec.consumerRef.name" to the template, using the machine name created by MS. Note that the BMH that served as the template has a ID: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api describe bmh ocpworker02 | grep UID: UID: a7b41719-c32e-4e07-b536-d972dd7bea97 $ oc describe machine-n openshift-machine-api ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-x6f8d | grep a7b41719-c32e-4e07-b536-d972dd7bea97 Provider ID: baremetalhost:///openshift-machine-api/ocpworker02/a7b41719-c32e-4e07-b536-d972dd7bea97 ~~~- But the new BMH doesn't have one yet. 3. Create the BMH using the name of the node that was generated in MS: ~~~ $ cat bmh-ocpworker03.yaml apiVersion: metal3.io/v1alpha1 kind: BareMetalHost metadata: finalizers:- baremetalhost.metal3.io generation: 3 name: ocpworker03 <--- NAME OF THE NODE ADDED TO THE CLUSTER namespace: openshift-machine-api spec: automatedCleaningMode: metadata bmc: address: "" credentialsName: "" bootMACAddress: e5:e0:1c:e5:74:dd <--- MAC OF THE BOND PRIMARY INTERFACE bootMode: UEFI consumerRef: apiVersion: machine.openshift.io/v1beta1 kind: Machine name: ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-hqed3 <--- MACHINE NAME GENERATED IN MS namespace: openshift-machine-api customDeploy: method: install_coreos externallyProvisioned: true hardwareProfile: unknown online: true userData: name: worker-user-data-managed namespace: openshift-machine-api ~~~ When creating the BMH, a UID will be generated. Take note of it. ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api get bmh ocpworker03-o yaml | grep uid uid: 8d89becc-bd0a-4c7e-b3c4-5eec11d57b17 ~~~- Once this is done, your machine will go to "Provisioned" status. Collect the ProviderID from the machine generated by MS: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api get machine ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-hqed3-o yaml | grep providerID providerID: baremetalhost:///openshift-machine-api/ocpworker03/8d89becc-bd0a-4c7e-b3c4-5eec11d57b17 ~~~- The "spec.ProviderID" information must be included in the definition of the NODE that will be part of the MS. 4. Once the Machine and the BMH are aligned with information on who provides and who consumes, the last step is to add:- The same "spec.providerID" to the node that will be associated with the machine.- The "metadata.annotations.machine.openshift.io/machine" data containing the Machine's name. ~~~ $ oc edit node ocpworker03 machine.openshift.io/machine: openshift-machine-api/ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-hqed3 ~~~ **WARNING:** This step must be assertive, as the "spec" may become *immutable* once it has been filled in. From: ~~~ spec: {} ~~~ To: ~~~ spec: providerID: baremetalhost:///openshift-machine-api/ocpworker03/8d89becc-bd0a-4c7e-b3c4-5eec11d57b17 ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-master-0 Running 4h20m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-master-1 Running 4h20m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-master-2 Running 4h20m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-i9lc3 Running 3h37m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-x6f8d Running 3h37m ocp-ocpbm-4s5cb-worker-0-hqed3 Running 45m <--- NEW MACHINE ~~~
root_cause: The assisted installer performs baremetal provisioning through a process separate from the machine-api.

title: OpenShift upgrade to 4.13 is getting stuck with 'Child process stopped by signal 0'
issue: - Nodes are degraded after failing to run `rpm-ostree rebase` command due to `Child process stopped by signal 0` after initiating the upgrade to RHOCP 4.13 ~~~ Degraded Machine: and Degraded Reason: failed to update OS to quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:888eda510e3c80bca8a43a939880543a0789e42cc1732c442c532d4575bb9692: error running rpm-ostree rebase--experimental ostree-unverified-registry:quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:888eda510e3c80bca8a43a939880543a0789e42cc1732c442c532d4575bb9692: ESC[0mESC[31merror: ESC[0mSanity-checking final rootfs: bwrap(/usr/bin/true): Child process stopped by signal 0 ~~~
resolution: - As per the [release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/release_notes/ocp-4-13-release-notes.html) of RHOCP 4.13, support for RHCOS functionality is removed for the `IBM Power8 all models (ppc64le)`.- For other than IBM Power8 (ppc64le), need to make the cpu features compatible with x86-64-v2 instruction set. Refer to [RHEL 9 guest panic's during boot with following error "Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v2"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6833751) solution to raise the compatibility platform wise.
root_cause: - `IBM power 8` hardware is not compatible to run 4.13 RHOCP version.- For other than IBM Power8 (ppc64le), the issue may arise due to CPU features incompatibility with x86-64-v2 instruction set or higher.

title: How does Pod preemption work with equal pod priority in Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4?
issue: Some pods within the priority class were preemptied, but the others were not. How did the RHOCP determine which pods were to be preemptied?
resolution: 1. Red Hat Openshift Container Platform [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-priority.html#nodes-pods-priority-preempt-about_nodes-pods-priority) describes the way preemption works in standard situation, so when pod priority differences exist 2. After pod priority PodDistruptionBudget is being considered (in the best effort manner) 3. The comment in upstream [Github](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go#L194) explains the behaviour in a situation of equal priorities and no PDB restrictions- The algorithm tries to remove the minimum number of pods possible- Therefore a pod with high resource request / consumption is more likely to be removed when the pending pod has high resource requests
root_cause: - Node resource congestion did not allow scheduling a new pod with higher priority than existing pods- Some, but not all lower priority pods were preemptied- Investigation needed to be performed how the pods are chosen to be preemptied

title: Creating controlplanemachineset in OpenShift 4 clusters in vSphere
issue: - There is no `controlplanemachineset` resource in the OpenShift 4 cluster installed in vSphere to manage the control plane, while it is already supported since version 4.12.- How to create a `controlplanemachineset` resource in an OpenShift 4 cluster installed in vSphere?
resolution: Starting with OpenShift 4.16, the [control plane machine set Custom Resource is automatically created](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/machine_management/control_plane_machine_management/cpmso-getting-started.html#cpmso-platform-matrix_cpmso-getting-started) at installation time, and it requires manual activation of the Custom Resource for cluster upgraded from previous versions. ####Workaround for older releases As explained in [creating a control plane machine set custom resource](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/machine_management/control_plane_machine_management/cpmso-getting-started.html#cpmso-creating-cr_cpmso-getting-started), it is needed to create the main part of the `controlplanemachineset` as per the example in the documentation, and only few things needs to be changed from the template. Create a `cpms.yaml` file with the content in the example linked above, and change the following: 1. The ` ` which appears in two different places. The value for it can be obtained with the following command: ~~~ $ oc get infrastructure cluster-o jsonpath='{.status.infrastructureName}{"\n"}' ~~~ 2. The `failureDomains` configuration. For vSphere, it is needed to remove the `failureDomains` field and related config, as it is not yet supported in the `controlplanemachineset` at this moment. Refer to [ControlPlaneMachineSet cannot be created with empty `failureDomains` for OpenShift 4 in vSphere](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7038990) for additional information. 3. The `providerSpec` configuration (note that the indentation is different in the resource it is collected and the resource in which it will be placed): 3.1. Get the `providerSpec` from one of the current master machines: ~~~ $ oc get machines-l "machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machine-role=master"-n openshift-machine-api [...] $ oc get machines [master_machine_name]-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml [...] providerSpec: value: [...] status: [...] ~~~ 3.2. The same ` ` gathered in step 1 can be added to the `providerSpec.value.metadata.name` field, but it is not required for vSphere as per the documentation (and that field could be not present in the `providerSpec` from the `machine` resource): ~~~ metadata: creationTimestamp: null name: ~~~ 3.3. Ensure the indentation of the `providerSpec` is correct before putting the content in the `yaml` file. 4. Set the `spec.state` to `Inactive`: ~~~ state: Inactive ~~~ 5. If any change from the original `providerSpec` is desired, like different `diskGiB` or different `memoryMiB`, change it in the file accordingly. When the `yaml` file is created as explained above, and ensuring the indentation of the `providerSpec` inside the file is correct, create the resource from the file and check that the resource was created: ~~~ $ oc apply-f cpms.yaml [...] $ oc get controlplanemachinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY UPDATED UNAVAILABLE STATE AGE cluster 3 3 3 3 Inactive 43s ~~~ If the resource is created with no errors, it is now possible to activate it, setting the `spec.state` to `Active`: ~~~ $ oc edit controlplanemachineset cluster-n openshift-machine-api [...] state: Active [...] ~~~ It is possible to check the status of the `controlplanemachineset` and the `machines` and `nodes` while the new `machines` are being created with the following commands: ~~~ $ oc get controlplanemachinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY UPDATED UNAVAILABLE STATE AGE cluster 3 3 3 3 Active 4m9s $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api [...] $ oc get nodes [...] ~~~
root_cause: Starting with OpenShift 4.12, [control plane machine sets](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/release_notes/ocp-4-12-release-notes.html#ocp-4-12-mapi-control-plane-machine-sets) were introduced to provide management capabilities for the control plane machines. They are similar to what compute machine sets provide for compute machines. For OpenShift 4 installed in vSphere, while the `ControlPlaneMachineSets` are supported, the `controlplanemachineset` is not automatically created as explained in [supported cloud providers](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/machine_management/control_plane_machine_management/cpmso-getting-started.html#cpmso-platform-matrix_cpmso-getting-started) (the automatic creation during the installation of OpenShift 4.15 is available as a [Technology Preview feature](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview)).

title: Security implications of enabling kernel-devel and pods mounting
issue: > ***Disclaimer:*

Links contained here in to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.

The issue is related to security and potential risks associated with enabling `kernel-devel`, mounting `debugFS (/sys/kernel/debug)`, and granting extensive privileges to the `kepler` application on OpenShift.- For installation documentation of [kepler](https://sustainable-computing.io/installation/kepler/)- As a prerequisite for working on OpenShift and need to enable kernel-devel on [master](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler/blob/main/manifests/config/cluster-prereqs/51-master-kernel-devel.yaml) and [worker](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler/blob/main/manifests/config/cluster-prereqs/51-worker-kernel-devel.yaml) nodes:- Mount the [debugFS](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler/blob/main/manifests/config/exporter/patch/patch-openshift.yaml) (/sys/kernel/debug) into their kepler Pods (running as a DaemonSet):- For usage on OpenShift, kepler also requires a very powerful SecurityContextConstraints giving itself [extensive privileges](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler/blob/main/manifests/config/exporter/openshift_scc.yaml)
resolution: Mitigate the risks of enabling the kernel-devel module, mounting the debugFS filesystem, and granting Kepler extensive privileges:- To only enable the kernel-devel module on nodes that need it, use the following command: ~~~ $ sudo modprobe kernel-devel ~~~- To use a firewall to restrict access to the debugFS filesystem, use the following command: ~~~ $ sudo firewall-cmd--permanent--add-port=/sys/kernel/debug/tcp/open 8080 ~~~- To monitor the activity of Kepler pods to look for malicious activity, use the following command: ~~~ $ kubectl get pods-l app=kepler--watch ~~~- To regularly review the SCC that Kepler requires to ensure that it is only granting the necessary privileges, use the following command: ~~~ $ oc describe scc kepler ~~~ **Note:** *Consult with a security expert before enabling `kernel-devel` module, mounting `debugFS` filesystem, or granting extensive privileges to Kepler. This ensures appropriate risk mitigation for the specific environment.*
root_cause: The potential security risk arises from enabling the `kernel-devel` module and mounting the `debugFS` filesystem in pods, while also granting Kepler extensive privileges through the SecurityContextConstraints (SCC). These actions expose sensitive kernel debugging features and provide unnecessary capabilities to the application, increasing the likelihood of malicious exploitation and unauthorized access. To address the RCA, careful evaluation, strict controls, and regular auditing of privileges are necessary to mitigate security risks effectively.

title: After adding a bare metal worker node via Assisted Installer, it is not creating a bare metal host or machine
issue: - New node doesn't have an associated BareMetalHost or Machine- Lose the ability to identify which piece of hardware is which node
resolution: This is expected behavior. If you need access to the machine and bare metal resources, use the [IPI (Installer Provisioned Infrastructure) installer](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/installing/installing_bare_metal_ipi/ipi-install-overview.html).
root_cause: The intent and design of the Assisted Installer service is to quickly build and install a cluster on available hardware; the provided *Add hosts* option extends this functionality to allow for quickly adding a new Node to the cluster, but is not intended for adding the bare metal resources necessary for the cluster to control the underlying host. For a Bare Metal installer-provisioned infrastructure (IPI) cluster, the standard procedure should be followed to [establish a new BareMetalHost](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/installing_bare_metal_ipi/ipi-install-expanding-the-cluster.html ""). This will allow the cluster to create a corresponding Machine and MachineSet, which can be used to allow the machine-config operator to automatically create the new Node. This is more idiomatic to IPI clusters. If these resources are not needed, then using the *Add hosts* option is suitable for adding new nodes to the cluster. However, this may introduce asymmetry to the cluster, as nodes added this way won't have associated bare metal resources, unlike nodes from the original deployment. If the bare metal resources are not being used, however, this may not result in any functional differences.

title: RHOCP 4 AWS cloud-credentials access key is expired.
issue: - The AWS service account used when installing the cluster is expired how can the cloud credentials be updated?- OpenShift cluster operator, cloud-credential, is in a degraded state.- cloud-credential-operator error log *error syncing credentials: error determining whether a credentials update is needed: unable to read info for username*.- The `oc adm upgrade` command reports the error: *the cluster operator cloud-credential is degraded*.- How can the names of IAM service accounts be changed for Naming Compliance Conventions policies?
resolution: **Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.- If the cluster is already installed, please follow the outlined steps. 1. Make sure the aws account has the [required aws permissions](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/installing/installing-on-aws#installation-aws-permissions_upi-aws-installation-reqs). 2. Create or obtain an [access key via AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html). 3. Update aws-creds secret in kube-system namespace, below is an example using the default profile configured `~/.aws/credentials`. ~~~ $ PROFILE=default $ aws--profile ${PROFILE} sts get-caller-identity # Quick credential test $ AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(aws configure get ${PROFILE}.aws_access_key_id) $ AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(aws configure get ${PROFILE}.aws_secret_access_key) $ oc create secret generic aws-creds-n kube-system--from-literal="aws_access_key_id=${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}"--from-literal="aws_secret_access_key=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}"--dry-run-o yaml | oc replace-f- ~~~- To set the IAM account name for an as-yet-uninstalled cluster, refer to the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/installing/installing-on-aws#installation-aws-iam-user_installing-aws-account).
root_cause: - When the AWS service account in use reaches its expiration, it necessitates replacement. The same procedure can be employed to replace the IAM account for various other reasons, such as when there is a need to update credentials or address naming compliance issues.

title: Accessing external service on Service Mesh reserved port fails in RHOCP 4
issue: - After onboarding application to service-mesh unable to connect to external services on port 15001.- Connection to an IP outside the mesh on port 15001 is suddenly closed.
resolution: Create a `ServiceEntry` object like the following: ~~~ apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1 kind: ServiceEntry metadata: name: se-reserved-port spec: addresses:- 10.0.0.1 endpoints:- address: 10.0.0.1 hosts:- my.service ports:- name: tcp number: 15001 protocol: TCP targetPort: 15001 resolution: STATIC ~~~
root_cause: - Port `15001` is a reserved port for allowing traffic to passthrough the *istio-proxy* sidecar when configured.- Other ports in the range 15000-15090 are reserved for the *istio-proxy*.

title: Securing OpenShift on Azure Disk Encryption and Key Management
issue: - Enabling user-managed disk encryption and automatic key rotation in a self-managed OpenShift cluster on Azure.
resolution: To address the security concerns related to disk encryption and key management in a self-managed OpenShift cluster on Azure, several steps and considerations are necessary- User-Managed Disk Encryption- Enabling user-managed disk encryption must be configured during the initial cluster setup. This involves setting up the Azure Disk Encryption Set and referencing it in the `install-config.yaml` file. Post-installation configuration is not supported due to the integration requirements between OpenShift and Azure's encryption mechanisms.- Automatic Key Rotation- Automatic key rotation is not supported for user-managed keys with the OpenShift installer on Azure. However, a separate solution within Azure Key Vault can be implemented for automatic key rotation.- Azure Storage Classes- Utilize Azure's built-in server-side encryption (SSE) with customer-managed keys (CMK) for encrypting data within Azure Storage classes.
root_cause: - The inability to enable user-managed disk encryption post-installation and the lack of support for automatic key rotation are due to limitations in the OpenShift installer and Azure integration. These features require specific configurations that must be set during the initial setup phase.

title: Argo CD reports OutOfSync for RHACM Policy objects
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: When managing RHACM Policies using OpenShift GitOps, Argo CD reports the Policies as `OutOfSync`. RHACM copies the Policy as soon as it is created, including the tracking ID (`argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id`), which is likely the problem: ~~~ NAME SYNC STATUS HEALTH STATUS configuration-management OutOfSync Healthy ~~~
How can Argo CD annotations and labels be ignored by RHACM?
resolution: * For replicated policies to not show up at all in Argo CD, you can set `spec.copyPolicyMetadata` to `false` on the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management policy definition to disable the Argo CD tracking labels and annotations from being copied to the replicated policy: ~~~ spec: copyPolicyMetadata: false ~~~ * Please refer to the documentation for more information: [Managing policy definitions with OpenShift Container Platform GitOps (Argo CD)](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.9/html-single/gitops/index#gitops-policy-definitions)
root_cause: * RHACM copies the policy as soon as it is created into the clusters namespace, including the ArgoCD tracking ID (`argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id`). Therefore, the Argo CD controller wants to delete the resource that is managed by RHACM, because it is not stored in GIT.

title: How to delete orphan blobs by hard pruning from OCP container registry

root_cause: Pruner's inability to delete empty directories because the implementation of directories in the underlying storage is not consistent.

title: [MTV] Migration Toolkit for Virtualization changes the network interface names from RHV
issue: - After migrating the VMs from RHV the network interfaces changed from `ens3` to `enp1s0`
resolution: There needs to be a post-hook that changes the names of the network interfaces that looks something like: ~~~---- hosts: localhost connection: local tasks:- name: Set variable shell: ls /sys/class/net | grep-v lo register: network_device- name: network device output debug: var: network_device- name: Update network config file ansible.builtin.copy: dest: /home/runStartup.bash mode: 0700 content: | #!/usr/bin/bash NETWORKDEVICE=`ip-o-4 route show to default| awk '{printf $5}'` sed-i \"s/ens3/enp1s0/g\" /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ens3 cp-p /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-ens3 /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/enp1s0 nmcli con modify ens3 con-name enp1s0 ifname enp1s0 nmcli connection reload /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/enp1s0 sed-i '$d' /var/spool/crontab/root ~~~
root_cause: The VMs running on RHV had a custom emulation modification, the qemu process was using firmware based on the machine type i440fx. This was the default in older versions of RHV, but this was changed to Q35 starting in RHV 4.4. The machine type i440fx, the Virtual NIC is plugged to a PCI slot. Whereas machine type Q35 uses a PCI Express slot. These differences are described in the Red Hat Networking Guide [11.1. Naming Schemes Hierarchy](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html-single/networking_guide/index#sec-Naming_Schemes_Hierarchy).

title: When attempting to access OperatorHub getting error message " cloudcredentials.operator.openshift.io "cluster" is forbidden: User "xyz" cannot get resource "cloudcredentials" in API group "operator.openshift.io" at the cluster scope"
issue: - Unable to access `OperatorHub` from the web console- Getting permission error while accessing the `OperatorHub` from `webconsole`
resolution: - Please follow this below workaround to resolve the issue.- Create the cluster role by using below yaml. ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: cloud-credentials-access aggregationRule: clusterRoleSelectors:- matchLabels: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/cloud-credentials-access: "true" rules:- apiGroups: ["operator.openshift.io"] resources: ["cloudcredentials"] verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"] ~~~- Create the clusterrolebinding for required user by using below yaml. ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: name: cloud-credentials-access-binding roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: cloud-credentials-access subjects:- kind: User name: XYZ apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io ~~~
root_cause: - There is some clusterrole missing after updating OCP to eus-4.14 version 4.14.24.

title: NooBaa Stuck in Phase "Configuring" or "Connecting" with  "Invalid URL" IPv6 Clusters
issue: In IPv6 ODF Clusters NooBaa may enter a state of Configuring/Connecting. In some instances, Metal Load Balancer `metallb-operator` may be a contributing factor to the issue as well. This affects all ODF Clusters v4.15 and below. ~~~ status: conditions:- lastHeartbeatTime: "2024-06-04T05:28:30Z" lastTransitionTime: "2024-05-21T14:57:52Z" message: Invalid URL reason: TemporaryError status: "False" type: Available- lastHeartbeatTime: "2024-06-04T05:28:30Z" lastTransitionTime: "2024-05-21T14:57:52Z" message: Invalid URL reason: TemporaryError status: "True" type: Progressing- lastHeartbeatTime: "2024-06-03T10:45:49Z" lastTransitionTime: "2024-05-21T14:57:52Z" message: 'RPC: connection (0xc002812360) already closed ReconnectDelay:3s cancelPings:}' reason: TemporaryError status: "False" type: Available- lastHeartbeatTime: "2024-06-03T10:45:49Z" phase: Connecting kind: BackingStoreList ~~~
resolution: **Note:** The resolution below is a workaround. The workaround will disable connection to external buckets/endpoints. For disconnected environments, this may be ideal, however, for clusters needing external access, the workaround will allow the storageluster to reconcile if in a state "Phase: Progressing" long enough to upgrade to ODF v4.16 where the fix is in place. Remember to remove the parameters when upgraded to ODF v4.16. 1. Take a current backup of the storagelcuster.yaml: ~~~ $ oc get storagecluster-n openshift-storage-o yaml > storagecluster.yaml ~~~ 2. Edit or patch the storagecluster to disable LoadBalancer which will also disable external connectivity: ~~~ $ oc patch StorageCluster ocs-storagecluster--type='merge'-p '{"spec":{"multiCloudGateway":{"disableLoadBalancerService": true}}}' ~~~ 3. If this is a disconnected environment, and the configuration is desired, you can stop here. However, if needing access to external connections/buckets, upgrade to ODF v4.16. 4. Once ODF is upgraded to v4.16, remove the following parameters: ~~~ $ oc edit storagecluster-n openshift-storage multiCloudGateway: disableLoadBalancerService: true <---- ~~~
root_cause: In ODF cluster v4.15 and below using IPv6 and MetalLB installed, a bug exists where NooBaa/Backingstore may go into a state of `Phase: Connecting` or `Phase: Configuring` with a message stating `Invalid URL`. A workaround can be implemented to disable the load balancer in the `storagecluster.yaml`. For disconnected environments, this may be ideal. However, the permanent fix is in place for ODF v4.16. [Bug 2284652- [GSS] NooBaa Backingstore In Phase: "Connecting" with "Invalid URL" Blocking Upgrade from ODF v4.13 to ODF v4.14](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2284652)

title: Why is the ImagePullBackOff error received when importing an EKS klusterlet
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: Authentication to the image registery, registry.redhat.io, fails with the ImagePullBackOff error.
Various other pods have already been started.
resolution: 1. Log into the OpenShift UI. 2. Follow only **step #6** of the [1.4.3. Select the **MultiClusterHub** tab. 6. Edit the **MultiClusterHub** yaml in the **spec** section. 7. title: How to fetch the APIcast Staging and Production JSON configuration files on Red Hat 3scale 2.X On-premises?
issue: I can't find the configuration file inside 3scale in OpenShift in the path `https:// <3scale admin portal> /admin/api/nginx/spec.json`
resolution: The full `staging` and `production` JSON configuration files for all Products are located under the following URLs: * Staging: `http:// @system-master:3000/master/api/proxy/configs/staging.json` * Production: `http:// @system-master:3000/master/api/proxy/configs/production.json` In order to fetch them, you can open a shell into a pod such as `apicast-staging` and call the URLs above. Since `APICAST_ACCESS_TOKEN` is already included in `THREESCALE_PORTAL_ENDPOINT`, you can use this variable to access the configuration as in the following example: ~~~ $ oc exec dc/apicast-production-- bash-c 'curl $THREESCALE_PORTAL_ENDPOINT/production.json' > production.json ~~~ Please notice that the JSON configuration for individual Products only could be fetched in the Admin Portal through browsing into `--> Integration--> Configuration--> Configuration history` under both `Staging APIcast` and `Production APIcast`. **NOTE:** When using a `self-managed` APIcast instance not located on the same project as Red Hat 3scale 2.X On-premises, the configuration should be fetched using the [APICAST_MANAGEMENT_API](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale/2-saas/html/administering_the_api_gateway/apicast_environment_variables#management-api). After setting it to `debug` and performing the steps provided in [the documentation](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3673411), it's recommended reverting it back to `status` due to security reasons.

title: Compliance Operator reports incorrect results on Managed Services
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: Why do Compliance Operator scans on Managed Services fail checks on the hosted infrastructure?
resolution: Compliance Operator provides [profiles](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/security/compliance_operator/co-scans/compliance-operator-supported-profiles.html) for Platform and Node. Depending on the managed service, customer may not have access to the Control Plane, which is managed by Red Hat. This is true especially in Hosted Control Plane architectures, which don't advertise Platform profiles intended to scan the control plane. Only Node profiles are supported and tested for managed OpenShift clusters using Hosted Control Plane architectures. Currently, the Compliance Operator is only tested with **ROSA with Hosted Control Planes (HCP)**. Refer to the [Installing the Compliance Operator on ROSA hosted control planes (HCP) section in documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/security/compliance_operator/co-management/compliance-operator-installation.html#installing-compliance-operator-rosa_compliance-operator-installation). Red Hat Engineering continues working to establish support for the Compliance Operator in other Cloud Service offering and investigating solutions for profiles on Cloud Services that will account for rules maintained by Red Hat.

title: How to determine if my cluster is an OKD cluster or a supported Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster
issue: - I need to check if my OpenShift Cluster is a community OKD4 cluster or an enterprise Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster that can be supported by Red Hat
resolution: There are several clues that allow distinguishing between an OKD4 cluster, which only has community support, and a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster, for which Red Hat can provide enterprise-level support. Some of them are the following: ### Version and release image on cluster version At the time of writing this solution, if we check the current version and release image in clusterversion object like this: ~~~ oc get clusterversion/version-o custom-columns=VERSION:status.desired.version,RELEASE-IMAGE:status.desired.image ~~~ For a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster, we get an output similar to this: ~~~ VERSION RELEASE-IMAGE 4.7.19 quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@sha256:eafdac268e1f65053de423ba4a028e8de5133ab78e7954d76ed838bcf5f4f666 ~~~ Where:- The version just follows a simple `4.y.z` format- The release image is an sha256 digest of `quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release` For an OKD4 cluster, we get an output similar to this: ~~~ VERSION RELEASE-IMAGE 4.7.0-0.okd-2021-07-03-190901 quay.io/openshift/okd@sha256:66857f330c4b6199ce319c9b5b5ff3bd7ff3d4c75113cd3d33302216312d345f ~~~ Where:- The version contains `okd` in it and has different format.- The release image is an sha256 digest of `quay.io/openshift/okd` Note that these clues may be subject to change in the future. ### Node operating system Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform uses Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS as operating system while OKD uses Fedora CoreOS. Therefore, if running `oc get node-o wide` shows nodes having Fedora CoreOS as `OS-IMAGE`, that's a clue that the cluster is OKD, while nodes having Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS would be a clue of the cluster being a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster.
root_cause: OKD and Red Hat OpenShift Container platform have several differences, like the underlying OS (Fedora CoreOS vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS), the images used or the binaries distributed. But the main difference is that Red Hat only provides support for the enterprise Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform distribution, not for OKD.

title: Fluentd collector pod is taking long time to complete start-up and to have the metrics endpoint ready, triggering CollectorNodeDown alert to fire
issue: Since OpenShift Container Platform 4- Cluster Logging 5.8, we are observing lots of `CollectorNodeDown` alerts because of the below error. "Get \"https://x.x.x.x:24231/metrics\": dial tcp x.x.x.x:24231: connect: connection refused"

There is an increased number of `CollectorNodeDown` alerts firing when `collector` pods are restarting or new Nodes are being added to OpenShift. When checking, we found that the `metrics` endpoint is taking a long time to become available, causing the `target` to be reported as `DOWN`.

title: How to set the  OpenShift DNS Operator as "unmanaged"  and enable "force_tcp"?
issue: One of the issues when enabling `force_tcp` as a workaround would be if you see following in the CoreDNS logs: ~~~ [ERROR] plugin/errors: dns: overflowing header size ~~~
resolution: This operation is unsupported. It should be performed only in order to workaround certain bugs indicated below. Once the solution for those bugs is released, it is necessary to remove the workaround and upgrade to a version containing the fix. Bugs that this operation can workaround:- [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1949361](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1949361) ### Procedure To set the `openshift-dns-operator` as "unmanaged" and add `force_tcp` Check if there are any overrides: ~~~ # oc get-o json clusterversion version | jq.spec.overrides ~~~ Switch to the project `dns-operator` ~~~ # oc project openshift-dns-operator ~~~ Set the DNS Operator as "unmanaged", replace *"dns-operator-b797d9494"* with the appropriate pod name. ~~~ # cat < version-patch-add-override.yaml- op: add path: /spec/overrides value: []- op: add path: /spec/overrides/- value: kind: Deployment name: dns-operator group: apps namespace: openshift-dns-operator unmanaged: true EOF # oc patch clusterversion version--type json-p "$(cat version-patch-add-override.yaml)" ~~~ Scale down the `Deployment` to 0: ~~~ # oc get all # oc scale--replicas=0-n openshift-dns-operator deployment.apps/dns-operator ~~~ Change the configuration, add `force_tcp` to `Configmap`: ~~~ # oc edit configmap/dns-default-n openshift-dns-o yaml forward. /etc/resolv.conf {force_tcp policy sequential} ~~~ It will take a while but CoreDNS pods will pick up the change and start using in little time. Then verify in any CoreDNS pod, replace *"dns-default-49xmf"* pod name with the appropriate pod name. ~~~ # oc project openshift-dns # oc get pods # oc rsh dns-default-49xmf [root@dns-default-49xmf /]# cat /etc/coredns/Corefile.:5353 {errors health {lameduck 20s} ready kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {pods insecure upstream fallthrough in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa} prometheus 127.0.0.1:9153 forward. /etc/resolv.conf {force_tcp policy sequential} cache 900 reload ~~~ Note that the config file may be slightly different, depending on the cluster configuration and version. **IMPORTANT**: DNS operator replicas must be kept 0 while the workaround is applied. Otherwise, operator will revert it. ### To rollback the changes, just remove the overrides. ~~~ # cat < version-patch-remove-override.yaml- op: remove path: /spec/overrides EOF # oc patch clusterversion version--type json-p "$(cat version-patch-remove-override.yaml)" ~~~ Verify overrides has been removed: ~~~ # oc get-o json clusterversion version | jq.spec.overrides ~~~ Wait several minutes until the CVO scales up the DNS operator deployment and the operator resets the configuration to what it expects. Then check the configmap, `force_tcp` should be gone: ~~~ #oc edit configmap/dns-default-n openshift-dns-o yaml ~~~ Check operator runs with old configuration: ~~~ # oc project openshift-dns # oc rsh dns-default-49xmf bash [root@dns-default-49xmf /]# cat /etc/coredns/Corefile.:5353 {errors health {lameduck 20s} ready kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {pods insecure upstream fallthrough in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa} prometheus 127.0.0.1:9153 forward. /etc/resolv.conf {policy sequential} cache 900 reload} ~~~
root_cause: This is a valid workaround for [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1949361](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1949361) because it is triggered by too big UDP DNS responses, so forcing TCP works as a workaround.

title: Is podman-compose supported by Red Hat?
issue: - Is the `podman-compose` command supported by Red Hat?- Is `podman-compose` supported in RHEL 8?- Is `podman-compose` equivalent to `docker-compose`?- Is `podman-compose` supported in OpenShift?
resolution: - Red Hat does not ship nor support `podman-compose`.- Currently `podman-compose` is not shipped by Red Hat, and is not in the road map of the future releases. Red Hat recommends to use OpenShift Container Platform (based on kubernetes) as preferred technology for low-level container orchestration.- For local container orchestration, `podman play kube` can be used with kubernetes/OpenShift syntax to create local container orchestration deployments as described [in this blog post](https://www.redhat.com/sysadmin/podman-play-kube).

title: SimpleContentAccessNotAvailable is firing on OpenShift Container Platform 4.10 if Simple Content Access is not enabled
issue: On a cluster which has been updated from OCP 4.9 to 4.10 we see the `SimpleContentAccessNotAvailable` in state firing. How can we disable this alert as this alert spoils the user interface, even at project level.
`SimpleContentAccessNotAvailable` alert starts firing after update to OCP 4.10.
resolution: * If [Simple Content Access](https://access.redhat.com/articles/simple-content-access) (SCA) is not planned to be used with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4, the functionality can be disabled following [Disabling simple content access import](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/support/remote_health_monitoring/insights-operator-simple-access.html#insights-operator-disabling-sca_remote-health-reporting-from-restricted-network). * To enable and configure [Simple Content Access](https://access.redhat.com/articles/simple-content-access) follow [Importing simple content access certificates with Insights Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/support/remote_health_monitoring/insights-operator-simple-access.html). Once this is setup and configured the alert `SimpleContentAccessNotAvailable` will stop firing because the required certificate can be imported using the [Insights Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/operators/operator-reference.html#insights-operator_platform-operators-ref).
root_cause: Starting with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.10, [Insights Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/operators/operator-reference.html#insights-operator_platform-operators-ref) imports the [Simple Content Access](https://access.redhat.com/articles/simple-content-access) certificates from [Red Hat OpenShift Cluster Manager](https://console.redhat.com/openshift) by default.

title: ArgoCD - App Health stays in "progressing" when new install plan for a subscription is pending for installation
issue: - The ArgoCD changes the health status of app to progressing when a new install plan is found for a subscription.- The ArgoCD App health stays in progressing until the new install plan is updated. Is there any way to avoid this behaviour?
resolution: - The built-in health check for subscriptions can be overridden by adding the "resourceHealthChecks" field in argocd CR for custom health checks. ~~~ $ oc edit argocd openshift-gitops-n openshift-gitops [...] apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1beta1 kind: ArgoCD [...] spec: [...] resourceHealthChecks:- check: | health_status = {} if obj.status ~= nil then if obj.status.conditions ~= nil then numDegraded = 0 numPending = 0 msg = "" for i, condition in pairs(obj.status.conditions) do msg = msg.. i.. ": ".. condition.type.. " | ".. condition.status.. "\n" if (condition.type == "InstallPlanMissing" and condition.reason ~= "ReferencedInstallPlanNotFound") then numDegraded = numDegraded + 1 elseif (condition.type == "CatalogSourcesUnhealthy" or condition.type == "InstallPlanFailed" or condition.type == "ResolutionFailed") and condition.status == "True" then numDegraded = numDegraded + 1 end end if numDegraded == 0 and numPending == 0 then health_status.status = "Healthy" health_status.message = msg return health_status else health_status.status = "Degraded" health_status.message = msg return health_status end end end health_status.status = "Progressing" health_status.message = "An install plan for a subscription is pending installation" return health_status group: operators.coreos.com kind: Subscription [...] ~~~
root_cause: Subscription Health Checks rely on InstallPlans. Whenever a new InstallPlan is found the subscription.status field has a condition InstallPlanPending set. This causes ArgoCD App health to change the status to "Progressing".

title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) fails getting CPU consumption and reports unknown for current cpu usage : "the HPA was unable to compute the replica count" in OCP 4 with apiVersion autoscaling/v1
issue: - The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (`HPA`) metrics shows ` ` in the summary view under `TARGETS`: ~~~ $ oc get hpa NAME REFERENCE TARGETS MINPODS MAXPODS REPLICAS AGE Deployment/ /40% 1 10 1 3m23s ~~~- The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (`HPA`) metrics shows ` ` for the current usage and error messages in the conditions: ~~~ $ oc describe hpa [...] Metrics: (current / target) resource cpu on pods (as a percentage of request): / 50% [...] Conditions: Type Status Reason Message----------------------- AbleToScale True SucceededGetScale the HPA controller was able to get the target's current scale ScalingActive False FailedGetResourceMetric the HPA was unable to compute the replica count: unable to get metrics for resource cpu: no metrics returned from resource metrics API [...] ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get hpa-o yaml [...] conditions:- type: AbleToScale status: 'True' lastTransitionTime: '2020-06-30T15:05:26Z' reason: SucceededGetScale message: the HPA controller was able to get the target's current scale- type: ScalingActive status: 'False' lastTransitionTime: '2020-06-30T15:05:26Z' reason: FailedGetResourceMetric message: 'the HPA was unable to compute the replica count: missing request for cpu' [...] ~~~- The HorizontalPodAutoscaler was defined with `apiVersion: autoscaling/v1` and `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage`
resolution: > **Note:** If switching to HPA v2 does not fix the issue at hand, also consider the current version of OpenShift Container Platform. Older environments of OpenShift Container Platform were affected by the following issue that showed in conjunction with init containers: [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5972361](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5972361) > **Note:** Make sure that all containers of the pods to be scaled by `HPA` have `resource.request` configured. See [solution 5102451](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5102451). If not yet configured, configure it and wait some minutes to allow the `HPA` to get the data. When configuring the `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage` parameter with the `autoscaling/v1`, the `HPA` can't get metrics for resource CPU and the `v2` API **must** be used. See the `Root Cause` section for further details. ### Converting HPA v1 resources to HPA v2 resources- Change the `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage` parameter with the new `metrics` parameter: As the documentation for [Creating a horizontal pod autoscaler for CPU utilization](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-autoscaling.html#nodes-pods-autoscaling-creating-cpu_nodes-pods-autoscaling), create the HorizontalPodAutoscaler with the `autoscaling/v2` api version and the `metrics` parameter:- Edit the `HPA`: ~~~ $ oc edit hpa-n ~~~- Change the apiversion: from: ~~~ apiVersion: autoscaling/v1 ~~~ to: ~~~ apiVersion: autoscaling/v2 ~~~- Change the `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage` parameter with the new `metrics` parameter: from: ~~~ spec: [...] targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 50 [...] ~~~ to: ~~~ spec: [...] metrics:- type: Resource resource: name: cpu target: type: Utilization averageUtilization: 50 [...] ~~~ > **Note**: Set the `averageUtilization` to the desired value. It's also possible to configure different metrics, run `oc explain hpa.spec.metrics--api-version autoscaling/v2` for more information.
root_cause: - As the upstream documentation ([Autoscaling on multiple metrics and custom metrics](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale-walkthrough/#autoscaling-on-multiple-metrics-and-custom-metrics)): the `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage` field has been replaced with an array called `metrics`.- The api version to use as the documentation ([Creating a horizontal pod autoscaler for CPU utilization](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/pods/nodes-pods-autoscaling.html#nodes-pods-autoscaling-creating-cpu_nodes-pods-autoscaling)) is `autoscaling/v2`, and the `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage` parameter is not present.- When configuring the `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage` parameter with the `autoscaling/v1`, the `HPA` can't get metrics for resource cpu.

title: Cluster upgrade got stuck due to storage pods in openshift-cluster-storage-operator remains in pending/createcontainerconfigerror state
issue: - The cluster upgrade becomes stuck with the below error message. ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING SINCE STATUS version True True 24s Unable to apply 4.12.z: an unknown error has occurred: MultipleErrors ~~~- Status of storage cluster operator remains in the current cluster version. ~~~ $ oc get co | grep storage storage 4.x.z True False False 39d ~~~
resolution: - In a security context constraint (SCC), a priority value of 0 is the lowest possible priority. A nil priority is considered a 0, or lowest, priority. Higher-priority SCCs are moved to the front of the set when sorting.- The custom SCCs are of priority 1 which is causing the issue here. Unless there is any requirement/reason for setting priority 1 on these custom SCCs, reduce the priority to null for these custom SCCs. Generally, during upgrade pods get restarted and SCCs of the highest priority have more precedence.- Also as per the [KCS article 6970100](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970100), it is recommended in custom SCCs that the `runAsUser` type be set as `MustRunAsNonRoot`. ~~~ $ oc get scc dynatrace-activegate-o yaml::: priority: 0 readOnlyRootFilesystem: false requiredDropCapabilities:- ALL runAsUser: type: MustRunAsNonRoot seLinuxContext: type: RunAsAny seccompProfiles:- '*' supplementalGroups: type: RunAsAny users:- system:serviceaccount:dynatrace:dynatrace-dynakube-oneagent-privileged ~~~- Workaround has been included for Cluster Storage Operator which allows CSO Pod to be able to run with custom SCCs OCP 4.13 [RHSA-2023:1326](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:1326) OCP 4.12.14 [RHBA-2023:1858](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:1858)
root_cause: The cluster upgrade was blocked from progressing due to the openshift-cluster-storage-operator pods being in pending status due to using the custom SCC `dynatrace-activegate` instead of system SCCs. Generally, an openShift operator's pod should be using the system SCC, not a custom SCC. ~~~ $ oc get pod csi-snapshot-controller-operator-69fd8965df-zbxcr-n openshift-cluster-storage-operator-oyaml | grep scc openshift.io/scc: dynatrace-activegatge $ oc get pod cluster-storage-operator-66c94c594-w7tm7-n openshift-cluster-storage-operator-oyaml | grep scc openshift.io/scc: dynatrace-activegate ~~~- Normally, the storage operator pod uses the nonroot-v2 scc: ~~~ $ oc describe po/cluster-storage-operator-58dbf6b56c-tfrdw | grep scc openshift.io/scc: nonroot-v2 ~~~- Could see custom SCC is of priority 1. If the custom SCCs are of priority 1, then during the pods' restart the SCCs of the highest priority have more precedence and get misapplied to the pods. ~~~ $ oc get scc dynatrace-activegate-o yaml | grep priority priority: 1 ~~~

title: RHOCP 4 cluster upgrade stuck with the Cluster Network Operator failing to apply ovnkube-master daemonset
issue: When upgrading a RHOCP cluster that is using OVNKubernetes CNI the following error is seen during network operator upgrade: ~~~ Error while updating operator configuration: could not apply (apps/v1, Kind=DaemonSet) openshift-ovn-kubernetes/ovnkube-master: failed to apply / update (apps/v1, Kind=DaemonSet) openshift-ovn-kubernetes/ovnkube-master: DaemonSet.apps "ovnkube-master" is invalid: [spec.template.spec.containers[0].lifecycle.preStop: Required value: must specify a handler type, spec.template.spec.containers[1].lifecycle.preStop: Required value: must specify a handler type, spec.template.spec.containers[3].lifecycle.preStop: Required value: must specify a handler type] ~~~
This issue is seen only for clusters that meet the following three criteria:
the cluster is using the OVNKubernetes CNI
the cluster has previously been upgraded from 4.10-> 4.11
the cluster is updated to 4.12.41+ or 4.13.16+
The upgrade is currently not recommended for those clusters due to the fact that the upgrade will stall but with no known risk to availability.
resolution: * Fix has been included via the following erratas OCP 4.14.9 [RHSA-2024:0204](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0204) OCP 4.13.30 [RHBA-2024:0286](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:0286) OCP 4.12.48 [RHSA-2024:0485](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0485) * There are two options to resolve the issue. Follow option 1, if you already started the upgrade and it's now stuck, follow the option 2 if you want to change the settings prior to the running the upgrade. ###Option 1- Upgrade is stuck in the middle * To workaround the issue if the upgrade is already stuck please modify the `daemonset/ovnkube-master` resource in the `openshift-ovn-kubernetes` namespace by removing occurrences of `preStop` branches: ```yaml preStop: exec: command:- /bin/bash--c- | echo "$(date-Iseconds)- stopping nbdb" /usr/share/ovn/scripts/ovn-ctl stop_nb_ovsdb echo "$(date-Iseconds)- nbdb stopped" rm-f /var/run/ovn/ovnnb_db.pid ``` ```yaml preStop: exec: command:- /bin/bash--c- | echo "$(date-Iseconds)- stopping sbdb" /usr/share/ovn/scripts/ovn-ctl stop_sb_ovsdb echo "$(date-Iseconds)- sbdb stopped" rm-f /var/run/ovn/ovnsb_db.pid ``` * Please run ~~~ $ oc edit ds ovnkube-master-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ~~~ * Remove the above mentioned `preStop` hooks. * Continue the upgrade by running ~~~ oc rollout restart deployment cluster-version-operator-n openshift-cluster-version ~~~ * Wait for the update to continue. * The network operator pod in the `openshift-network-operator` namespace may need to be restarted in some cases for the update to continue. ###Option 2- Prepare the cluster before running the upgrade * It is also possible to change the DaemonSet post upgrade to not run into the situation. Please do the following * Mark the network operator as unmanaged and remove the preStop hooks for the 'sbdb' and 'nbdb' containers ~~~ oc patch Network.operator.openshift.io cluster--type='merge'-p='{"spec":{"managementState":"Unmanaged"}}' oc patch daemonset-nopenshift-ovn-kubernetes ovnkube-master--type='json'-p='[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/1/lifecycle/preStop"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/3/lifecycle/preStop"}]' ~~~ * The above will cause the network operator to update. Wait for it to rollout ~~~ oc wait co network--for='condition=PROGRESSING=False'--timeout=600s ~~~ * Once you have changed that please run your upgrade as usual. The network operator comes back to managed state after the upgrade.

title: Fail to install OCP cluster on VMware vSphere and Nutanix as apiVIP and ingressVIP are not in machine networks
issue: - While deploying OCP 4.12 cluster on VMware vSphere or Nutanix, the installer survey fails as apiVIP and ingressVIP are not in machine CIDR.- As the user could not define cidr for machineNetwork when creating install-config file interactively, it will use default value 10.0.0.0/16, so fail to create install-config.yaml when inputting apiVIP and ingressVIP outside of default machineNetwork.
resolution: - Fix has been included via the following erratas- OCP 4.14 [RHSA-2023:5006](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:5006)- OCP 4.13 [RHSA-2023:1326](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:1326)- OCP 4.12.20 [RHSA-2023:3410](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3410)- A temporary workaround at the moment is to use dummy VIP values (10.0.0.1 and 10.0.0.2) when filling the survey and then modifying generated `install-config.yaml` and manifests to change the machine network and VIPs to the desired values.- Another option is to just take the install-config.yaml sample [from the docs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere-installer-provisioned-network-customizations.html#installation-installer-provisioned-vsphere-config-yaml_installing-vsphere-installer-provisioned-network-customizations) and edit it for your environment, essentially treating this as an IPI installation with configurations.
root_cause: The install survey does not ask for the machine network value, and defaults to 10.0.0.0/16, so any VIP input that is not in that range of 10.0.0.0/16 will cause the survey to fail to generate an install-config.yaml file. The VIP has to exist within the machine network to prevent routing issues.

title: Missing EgressIP multiNIC routes causes connection issues in RHOCP 4
issue: - No default routes for the secondary NIC Egress IP routing table.- Default routes has not injected to Egress IP routing table causing secondary NIC connectivity issues.- Not able to connect to an external server using EgressIP on additional network interfaces.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being fixed in the following bugs: RHOCP Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 4.16 | OCPBUGS-22923 | **4.16.0** | [RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041) 4.15 | OCPBUGS-31501 | **4.15.10** | [RHSA-2024:1887](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:1887) 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-31854](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-31854) | **4.14.23** | [RHBA-2024:2051](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:2051)
root_cause: - EgressIP traffic on additional network interfaces exits OVN from the `ovn-k8s-mp0` of the node where the IP is assigned and is then applied an SNAT rule with iptables.- In that EgressIP node specific ip rules are created for the pods IPs to use a different ip routing table.- The bug is mostly related to incorrect routes in the routing table used for the pod traffic causing connectivity issues on the additional interfaces.
