title: etcd alert rules have not set triggering values as per etcd performance requirement
issue: - Alerts `etcdHighFsyncDurations` and `etcdHighCommitDurations` for checking if underlying storage is performing well or not for etcd have not set the values for being triggered as per backend performance requirement.
resolution: Red Hat evaluated this request in [RFE-5327](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-5327) and while it's recognized that it is a valid request, it's not expected this to be implemented in the product in the foreseeable future. This is due to other priorities for the product and not a reflection of the request itself.
root_cause: Following are two alerts i.e. `etcdHighFsyncDurations` and `etcdHighCommitDurations` for checking if underlying storage is performing well or not from `etcd` perspective. ~~~- alert: etcdHighFsyncDurations annotations: message: 'etcd cluster "{{$labels.job}}": 99th percentile fync durations are {{$value}}s on etcd instance {{$labels.instance}}.' expr: | histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~".*etcd.*"}[5m])) > 0.5 for: 10m labels: severity: warning------------------------------------------ alert: etcdHighCommitDurations annotations: message: 'etcd cluster "{{$labels.job}}": 99th percentile commit durations {{$value}}s on etcd instance {{$labels.instance}}.' expr: | histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~".*etcd.*"}[5m])) > 0.25 for: 10m labels: severity: warning ~~~ According to these alert rules, it seems the metrics values are compared and alert is getting fired at the time when `wal_fsync_duration_seconds` is going above `500ms` and `backend_commit_duration_seconds` is going above `250ms`. The values which are kept as boundary line i.e. `500ms` and `250ms` are too high as compared to `etcd` backend storage performance requirement. `Backend performance requirement`: [Reference KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4770281) ~~~ To rule out a slow disk from causing Etcd warnings, you can monitor metrics backend_commit_duration_seconds (p99 duration should be less than 25ms) and wal_fsync_duration_seconds (p99 duration should be less than 10ms) to confirm the storage is reasonably fast. ~~~

title: Failing for installing nodes in a ESX standalone in RHOCP 4
issue: Failing to create an Openshift machine in a standalone ESX Server with the panic error below: ~~~ 2022-10-18T10:25:06.331268050Z panic: reflect.Set: value of type mo.ComputeResource is not assignable to type mo.ClusterComputeResource ~~~

When trying to create a OpenShift machine in a standalone ESX server the `machine-api-controller` pod` crashes and fails with the error ` value of type mo.ComputeResource is not assignable to type mo.ClusterComputeResource`

OpenShift machines are always in `Provisioning` phase and the `machine-api-controller` pod is restarting ~~~ $ oc get pods-l k8s-app=controller-n openshift-machine-api NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE machine-api-controllers-5b5ff45b9b-22wrd 7/7 Running 19 2h9m $ oc get machines NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE example1-worker-8xwmj Provisioning 4h45m... ~~~
resolution: Red Hat evaluated this request in [RFE-3463](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3463) and while it's recognized that it is a valid request, it's not expected this to be implemented in the product in the foreseeable future. This is due to other priorities for the product and not a reflection of the request itself.
root_cause: The usage of Standalone ESX servers is not supported for installing OpenShift nodes. The supported options are documented in the [VMware vSphere infrastructure requirements](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/installing/installing_vsphere/installing-vsphere.html#installation-vsphere-infrastructure_installing-vsphere) section. The error message: ~~~ 2022-10-18T10:25:06.331268050Z panic: reflect.Set: value of type mo.ComputeResource is not assignable to type mo.ClusterComputeResource ~~~ Indicates that: * a standalone host is only a ComputeResource * Only a cluster can be casted from ComputeResource to ClusterComputeResource Then, it's expected to find a cluster, not a ComputeResource.

title: Finding Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces logs after shutdown
issue: - After a `devworkspace` is shutdown, related pods are destroyed and it's not clear where its logs are stored.
resolution: - Everything happening with the RHODS operator is logged in the `devworkspace-controller` pod.- Find the pod name by executing: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-operators-l=app.kubernetes.io/name=devworkspace-controller NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE devworkspace-controller-manager-xxxxxx-yyyyy 2/2 Running 0 17h ~~~- If a workspace was stopped on purpose, the logs would show: ~~~ {"level":"info","ts":"2024-07-11T09:28:58Z","logger":"controllers.DevWorkspace","msg":"Reconciling Workspace","Request.Namespace":"admin-devspaces","Request.Name":"golang","devworkspace_id":"workspacexyz","resolvedConfig":"workspace.progressTimeout=300s,workspace.containerSecurityContext is set"} {"level":"info","ts":"2024-07-11T09:28:58Z","logger":"controllers.DevWorkspace","msg":"Stopping workspace","Request.Namespace":"admin-devspaces","Request.Name":"golang","devworkspace_id":"workspacexyz"} ~~~- If a workspace is stopped due to inactivity, it will get the `controller.devfile.io/stopped-by: inactivity` annotation: ~~~ $ oc get devworkspaces-n admin-devspaces golang-ojsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.controller\.devfile\.io\/stopped-by}' inactivity ~~~

title: NGINX isn't balancing the request between its own worker processes
issue: - Why the connections seem to be allocated to the one worker process, especially given the context that the max open files would have been exceeded
resolution: - Reduce the `worker_connections` value to force the requests to shift to another worker- Add `reuseport` to the `listen` directive server {listen 443 reuseport;...} With the `reuseport` option enabled, there are multiple socket listeners for each IP address and port combination, one for each worker process. The kernel determines which available socket listener (and by implication, which worker) gets the connection. This can reduce lock contention between workers accepting new connections and improve performance on multicore systems. However, it can also mean that when a worker is stalled by a blocking operation, the block affects not only connections that the worker has already accepted but also connection requests that the kernel has assigned to the worker since it became blocked.
root_cause: By default, NGINX will only use another worker if the previous one reaches its maximum connection capacity.

title: How are cpuset assigned with OpenShift SNO workload partitioning?
issue: - How are cpuset assigned with OpenShift SNO workload partitioning?
resolution: When OpenShift SNO workload partitioning is enabled, most of OpenShift pods uses reserved cpuset and will not use isolated cpuset for applications. In the following example, 16 vCPUs environment, reserved cpuset is `0-3,8-11` and isolated cpuset is `4-7,12-15`. An application is deployed with Guaranteed `requests.cpu: 1` configuration so it uses a dedicated 1 vCPU, CPU ID 4. ~~~ $ oc get pod--all-namespaces--no-headers | grep Running | sed-e 's|\([^]*\)[]*\([^]*\).*|echo \1 \2\n oc-n \1 exec \2-- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset/cpuset.cpus|' | sh openshift-apiserver-operator openshift-apiserver-operator-7f6794f56f-gl44n 0-3,8-11 openshift-apiserver apiserver-85488c659f-ppbrv 0-3,8-11 openshift-authentication-operator authentication-operator-df9d6885b-m797b 0-3,8-11 (snip) openshift-cloud-credential-operator pod-identity-webhook-776d899879-kzkcm 5-7,12-15 openshift-cloud-network-config-controller cloud-network-config-controller-f4f876777-wgmjq 0-3,8-11 openshift-cluster-csi-drivers aws-ebs-csi-driver-controller-5467588db8-99x2t 5-7,12-15 openshift-cluster-csi-drivers aws-ebs-csi-driver-node-7q95d 5-7,12-15 (snip) openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator tuned-ck6xl 0-15 (snip) app-project app-1cpu-964df4d46-gh5fd 4 ~~~ Note that some of the OpenShift pods, namely the pod-identity-webhook and the csi-driver pods expected to use the reserved cpuset but runs with isolated cpuset. This is a limitation at this point, version 4.11.12. For the tuned pod, it prints different cpuset value as tuned pod mounts `/sys` from the host, so it actually prints the host cgroups. The actual tuned container cgroup is available at different path and uses reserved cpuset. The cpuset taken by applications are excluded from the other pods. In the example, the CPU ID 4 is taken by app-1cpu pod, so the CPU ID 4 is excluded from other applications cpuset. For non-Kubernetes/OpenShift workload, the systemd.cpu_affinity kernel parameter is set to the reserved cpuset by the PerformanceProfile configuration, so all other non-Kubernetes/OpenShift processes only use the reserved cpuset.

title: Using different network interfaces for OpenShift SDN/OVNKubernetes and node IP supported in OpenShift?
issue: - Using different network interfaces for OpenShift SDN/OVNKubernetes and node IP supported in OpenShift?- Node IP is overridden to use specific interface other than default gateway which is used by OVNKubernetes- Kubernetes Service ClusterIP 172.30.0.1 traffic uses OVNKubernetes network interface and not using overridden Node IP network interface
resolution: OpenShift supports single IP setup. Using different network interfaces for OpenShift SDN/OVNKubernetes and node IP is not tested nor supported by Red Hat. The [host-> service-> endpoint via another NIC will not work in local gateway mode](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-2663).

title: How to use network-kargs to deploy RHCOS Nodes with Static IPs in Openshift 4 on VMware
issue: - Is it possible to deploy a node in VMware with a Static IP in RHOCP?- How do I use network-kargs to configure Static IP addresses in VMware using OpenShift Container Platform?- Why using `guestinfo.afterburn.initrd.network-kargs` property is not affecting the node configuration?
resolution: Starting in [OpenShift Container Platform 4.6](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/release_notes/ocp-4-6-release-notes.html#ocp-4-6-static-ip-config-with-ova), Red Hat CoreOS Enterprise Linux has the ability to utilize a static network configuration and override the automatic DHCP setup. Custom networking command-line `ip=` parameter can be configured via `guestinfo.afterburn.initrd.network-kargs` property. **Note: `guestinfo.afterburn.initrd.network-kargs` property must be set on the VM before the first boot and it does not affect subsequent boots**. The full syntax of the ip= parameter is documented in [Dracut manpages.](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/dracut.cmdline.7.html) ~~~ ip=:[]:::::{none|off|dhcp|on|any|dhcp6|auto6|ibft}[:[][:]] explicit network configuration. If you want do define a IPv6 address, put it in brackets (e.g. [2001:DB8::1]). This parameter can be specified multiple times. is optional and is the address of the remote endpoint for pointopoint interfaces and it may be followed by a slash and a decimal number, encoding the network prefix length. ~~~ Utilizing the `govc` vSphere CLI you can use the following example to deploy a new node called Worker3 from the RHCOS46 Template to the raid0 Datastore with 4 vCPU, 16GB of RAM, on the 10.0.0.x-254 Network to the openshift-ctxdz folder. ~~~ WORKER_CONFIG=$(cat worker.ign | base64-w0) IPCFG="ip=10.0.0.103::10.0.0.254:255.255.255.0:worker3:ens192:off:10.0.0.1:10.0.0.2" govc vm.clone-vm=RHCOS46-ds=raid0-c=4-m=16384-net=10.0.0.x-24-folder=openshift-ctxdz-on=false worker3 govc vm.disk.change-vm worker3-size 120G govc vm.change-vm worker3-e "guestinfo.ignition.config.data.encoding=base64" govc vm.change-vm worker3-e "guestinfo.ignition.config.data=${WORKER_CONFIG}" govc vm.change-vm worker3-e "guestinfo.afterburn.initrd.network-kargs=${IPCFG}" govc vm.power-on worker3 ~~~ In this example, using the Ansible along with the vmware_guest module, you will be deploying the same node Worker3 from the RHCOS46 Template to the raid0 Datastore with 4 vCPU, 16GB of RAM, on the 10.0.0.x-254 Network to the openshift-ctxdz folder. **NOTE**- You will need to define the `workerContent` as a variable with the contents of worker.ign. ~~~- name: Create worker VMs from the template vmware_guest: hostname: vcenter.lab.int username: Administrator@vsphere.local password:... datacenter: OCP4 validate_certs: no folder: /vm/openshift-ctxdz/ name: worker3 state: PoweredOn template: RHCOS46 disk:- size_gb: 120 type: thin datastore: raid0 hardware: memory_mb: 16384 num_cpus: 4 memory_reservation_lock: True networks:- name: 10.0.0.x-254 wait_for_ip_address: no customvalues:- key: guestinfo.ignition.config.data value: "{{workerContent}}"- key: guestinfo.ignition.config.data.encoding value: base64- key: guestinfo.afterburn.initrd.network-kargs value: "ip=10.0.0.103::10.0.0.254:255.255.255.0:worker3:ens192:off:10.0.0.1:10.0.0.2" ~~~ The implementations that need IPv4 and IPv6, both parameters can be passed to the network-kargs considering the syntax standards from [Dracut manpages](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/dracut.cmdline.7.html): ~~~ ip=10.0.0.103::10.0.0.254:255.255.255.0:worker3:ens192:off:10.0.0.1:10.0.0.2 ip=[2001::2001]::[2001::2002]:[ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff::]:worker3:ens192:off:: ~~~ If you no longer have access to your Master or Worker Ignition files you can retrieve them by following [KCS: How to retrieve Master or Worker Ignition Configuration?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5504291) ##Disclaimers: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. title: Multiple defunct conmon processes on RHOCP 4 node
issue: - Why are there many defunct `conmon` processes on a RHOCP 4 node: ~~~ $ ps-ef|grep defunct|tail root 4026537 3069 0 Mar25? 00:00:00 [conmon] root 4031086 3069 0 Mar26? 00:00:00 [conmon] root 4033770 3069 0 Apr11? 00:00:00 [conmon] root 4034458 3069 0 Apr12? 00:00:00 [conmon] root 4035662 3069 0 Mar28? 00:00:00 [conmon] ~~~- Interactive sessions on a RHOCP 4 node are unreasonably slow.
resolution: Upgrade the cluster. The fix is present in the following releases: RHOCP Release | Tracking Bug | Errata--- |--- |--- 4.10.3 | [2019346](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2019346) | [RHSA-2022:0056](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:0056) 4.9.12 | [2032466](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2032466) | [RHBA-2021:5214](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2021:5214) 4.8.31 | [2049102](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2049102) | [RHBA-2022:0484](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2022:0484) ### Workaround: To mitigate the situation a workaround is to first drain the node and then either restart `crio.service` or reboot the node. 1. Drain the node as explained in the [pod evacuation procedure](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-working.html#nodes-nodes-working-evacuating_nodes-nodes-working) 2. Either restart `crio.service` **or** reboot the node:- restart `crio.service`: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ Starting pod/-debug... To use host binaries, run `chroot /host` If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.4# chroot /host sh-4.4# systemctl restart crio.service Removing debug pod... ~~~- reboot the node as explained in the [node rebooting documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-rebooting.html)
root_cause: [Bug #1952137](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1952137) is opened to investigate this root cause of this issue.

title: How to achieve Blue-Green deployment using a service in RHOCP 4 ?
issue: - [Document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/applications/deployments/route-based-deployment-strategies.html#deployments-ab-testing_route-based-deployment-strategies) covers the Blue-Green Deployment using routes and not service.- Is it possible to achieve a Blue-Green Deployment using a service?
resolution: - Create two `deployments` `blue-deployment` and `green-deployment`: ~~~ $ oc create deployment--image=: ~~~- Edit the deployments to add same label `key`: `value` to the pods: ~~~ spec:... template: metadata: creationTimestamp: null labels: app: testdeployment2 key: value... ~~~- Create one `Service` with desired `service-port` and `target-port`: ~~~ $ oc create service clusterip--tcp=: ~~~- Edit the created `service` and mention the same label: ~~~ $ oc edit service spec: selector: key: value type: ClusterIP ~~~- Check if the service has the desired Endpoints. [endpoint contains the pod IPs + port, created using both deployments] ~~~ $ oc describe svc ~~~- Check hitting the service IP if both deployments (Blue-Green) are accessible. ~~~ $ curl: ~~~

title: Updating Operators in OpenShift produces the error "etcdserver: request is too large"
issue: - When updating operators in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4, upgrade of an operator may fail with the error `queueinformer_operator.go:298] sync {"update" "myoperator/install-bundle"} failed: failed to update installplan bundle lookups: etcdserver: request is too large`.- Operator upgrades may fail to proceed and the operator will be in a degraded state.
resolution: - Two resolutions exist depending on the operator:- Reduce the size of the message being sent by the operator upgrade procedure as part of the upgrade bundle.- Increase the allowed size of the messages allowed by client requests in `etcd`.- It is preferable to decrease the message size to the client within the install bundle in the operator. This may involve reaching out to a third-party vendor or author of the operator to alter the size of the operator upgrade so it can send a request that fits within the default request size allowed by `etcd`.- Alternatively, configuration of `etcd` to increase the `MaxRequestBytes` parameter to exceed the size of the bundle the operator requires is possible, but requires the author of the operator to confirm what size request is needed to set the value appropriately.- *Insert etcd `MaxRequestBytes` increase value steps here*
root_cause: - The error `request is too large` returned from `etcd` during a request from the Operator Framework installation procedure indicates that too large of a request, usually in the form of bundled data or YAML in the operator update, is exceeding the maximum size that `etcd` allows for client requests.- The following error is returned to clients when too large of a request is sent to `etcd` as part of an operator upgrade.- (`etcd-io/etcd` Github Repository showing the error code and message)[https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/eeeb7e05b32466d13a25b3de0cbb03884319c1a9/server/etcdserver/errors/errors.go#L36]- (`etcd-io/etcd` Github Repository showing the check for client message sizes during requests)[https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/server/etcdserver/v3_server.go#L765-L767]- This request size is governed by the `MaxRequestBytes` parameter within `etcd` and is kept relatively small for performance reasons by default.- (`etcd-io/etcd` Github Repository showing the configurable `MaxRequestBytes` parameter)[https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/server/embed/config.go#L213]- As the request is too large to `etcd` from the client, either the size of the message must be lowered or this `MaxRequestBytes` parameter must be raised.

title: Prometheus-Adapter pods Not Running due to too many CRDs causing failure of Liveness Probe in RHOCP 4
issue: - Prometheus-adapter pods `Not Running` and having continuous restarts ~~~ NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE prometheus-adapter-xxxxxxxxx-xxxxx 0/1 Running 16 36m prometheus-adapter-xxxxxxxxx-xxxxx 0/1 Running 15 34m ~~~
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue:- For RHOCP 4.14 in bug report [OCPBUGS-7694](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-7694) and delivered a fix in RHOCP 4.14.0 through errata [RHSA-2023:5006](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:5006)- For RHOCP 4.13 in bug report [OCPBUGS-10895](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-10895) and delivered a fix in RHOCP 4.13.0 through errata [RHSA-2023:1326](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:1326)- For RHOCP 4.12 in bug report [OCPBUGS-11508](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-11508) and delivered a fix in RHOCP 4.12.14 through errata [RHBA-2023:1858](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:1858)- For RHOCP 4.11 in bug report [OCPBUGS-11759](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-11759) and delivered a fix in RHOCP 4.11.38 through errata [RHBA-2023:1863](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:1863) If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. #### Workaround A not very clean workaround would be to delete the liveness probe, only to have this working again.
root_cause: The `kube-apiserver` is overloaded and the `prometheus-adapter` waits for too long when discovering the existing CRDs resulting in the `Liveness` and `Readiness` probes failing to cause the restart of the pods.

title: Exploring Infrastructure and Master node migration from gp2 to gp3 in ROSA
issue: - Considering the 20% cost reduction with GP3 volumes, is it feasible to migrate infrastructure and master nodes from gp2 to gp3 in ROSA?- Can the Red Hat Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team facilitate this migration upon customer request?- Is this migration officially supported, and are there any considerations for migrating storage from gp2 to gp3 for master and infrastructure nodes?
resolution: At the present moment, the `control plane node volume migration to GP3` feature has not been released, and an internal Request for Enhancement (RFE) ticket is currently in progress. As a general practice, migration from gp2 to gp3 for infrastructure and master nodes is not currently supported, and the recommended approach would be to rebuild these nodes. For users who prefer not to wait for the completion of the RFE, an alternative option is available to install a new cluster. GP3 is now the default storage type for new clusters, offering immediate cost benefits. In exceptional cases, consideration can be given to a Support Exception Request, which involves an internal assessment and management approval. Approval is not guaranteed, and if granted, assistance with the migration may be provided by Red Hat's SRE team. If any further questions or assistance is needed, please contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/support).

title: Receiving Gateway Time-out when running a Prometheus query
issue: - When running a heavy query to get metrics out of Prometheus, like for example "`topk(20, count by (__name__, job)({__name__=~".+"}))`", which counts how many time series each metric has and gets the top `20`, the "`Gateway Time-out`" message is shown in the OpenShift web console or in the client: ~~~ requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 504 Server Error: Gateway Time-out for url: https://prometheus-k8s-openshift-monitoring.apps.xxxxx.local/api/v1/query_range?query=sum%28container_memory_rss[...] ~~~
resolution: There are different ways of approaching this:- Trying to build a query that is quicker to execute (like reducing the Time Range).- Check if the same issue happens without Persistent Storage configured, as the issue could be caused by slow storage.- Increasing the CPU cycles available to Prometheus by increasing the CPU request as per solution [How to set up the resource limit and request for Prometheus in OpenShift?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3867881).- Trying to wait longer: the "`Gateway Time-out`" message is generated by the `router` fronting Prometheus (in latest OpenShift 4 releases, the web console). The Prometheus `route` can be configured to have a higher value as `timeout` (note that a `timeout` of `5m` is already configured by default in OpenShift 4.12.43 and newer versions in the `console` `route` by [bug OCPBUGS-18951](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-18951)): ~~~ $ oc annotate route [prometheus-route_name]--overwrite haproxy.router.openshift.io/timeout=5m-n openshift-monitoring ~~~
root_cause: The Gateway Time-out is usually generated by the router as the query takes more time to execute than the `timeout` that has been configured at the `route` level. It could be also caused by the `query` `timeout`.

title: Ingress operator degraded with '0/7 nodes are available: 1 node(s) were unschedulable, 3 node(s) didn't have free ports for the requested pod ports, 3 node(s) didn't match node selector.'
issue: `Ingress` operator `degraded` with below error: ~~~ $ oc get events-n openshift-ingress LAST SEEN TYPE REASON OBJECT MESSAGE Unknown Warning FailedScheduling pod/router-default-bd5f69b8b-799xg 0/7 nodes are available: 1 node(s) were unschedulable, 3 node(s) didn't have free ports for the requested pod ports, 3 node(s) didn't match node selector. ~~~
resolution: * Check the node status. Whether all nodes are `ready` and `schedulable`. ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ip-X-YY-ZZ-85.cluster.internal Ready master 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ip-X-YY-ZZ-84.cluster.internal Ready master 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ip-X-YY-ZZ-86.cluster.internal Ready master 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ip-X-YY-ZZ-88.cluster.internal Ready worker 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ip-X-YY-ZZ-89.cluster.internal Ready worker 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ip-X-YY-ZZ-87.cluster.internal Ready worker 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ip-X-YY-ZZ-90.cluster.internal Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 26d v1.17.1+20ba474 ~~~ * Make the `SchedulingDisabled` node `schedulable`. ~~~ $ oc adm uncordon ~~~ * [Mark the master nodes schedulable](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-working.html#nodes-nodes-working-master-schedulable_nodes-nodes-working) if the `router-pod` replica is set to more than the number of `worker` nodes.
root_cause: * One of the `worker` nodes was `unschedulable`.

title: Troubleshooting pod evictions caused by DiskPressure in RHOCP 4
issue: - Build pods failing due to too less ephemeral storage.- Pods are evicted automatically after the following events are recorded: ~~~ $ oc get ev-n default 55m Warning EvictionThresholdMet node/worker0.example.com Attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage 55m Normal NodeHasDiskPressure node/worker0.example.com Node worker0.example.com status is now: NodeHasDiskPressure ~~~
resolution:
- The following metrics can be used, from the Web Console under **Observe-> Metrics**, to identify if a particular pod exhausted the available storage in a particular node: ~~~ sum by (pod) (container_fs_usage_bytes{node=" "}) ~~~ ~~~ sum by (pod) (kubelet_container_log_filesystem_used_bytes{node=" "}) ~~~- As a cluster administrator it is possible to verify how much ephemeral-storage every pod is using by running the following the cycle: oc get node-l node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=-o json| jq '.items[].metadata.name'-r | while read NODE; do printf "

===> $NODE
" && \ oc get--raw /api/v1/nodes/${NODE}/proxy/stats/summary | jq '.pods[] |. as $parent | "Namespace: " + $parent.podRef.namespace + "
" + "PodName:" + $parent.podRef.name + "
" + "UsedMB:" + ($parent."ephemeral-storage".usedBytes/1024|tostring) + "
==========="'-r; done The command used in this cycle is mentioned in the [Solution 6993297- How to monitor ephemeral storage consumption at pod level?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6993297).
root_cause: - Kubelet starts the eviction of the pods based on the following thresholds:- *imagefs.available* <15%- *memory.available* <100Mi- *nodefs.available* <10%- *nodefs.inodesFree* <5%- In an RHOCP installation without customization having the root filesystems used at 85% triggers the *imagefs.available* threshold.- The thresholds can be changed as mentioned in the online documentation: [Configuring garbage collection for containers and images](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-garbage-collection.html#nodes-nodes-garbage-collection-configuring_nodes-nodes-configuring).

resolution: #### Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 Upgrade to `kernel-4.18.0-305.el8` (the RHEL8.4GA kernel) or later, which contain fixes for this issue. These details were fixed by (private bug) 1746371. #### Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 This issue was investigated on RHEL7 but the resolution to this problem would have required extensive changes. Affected customers should upgrade to RHEL8.4GA (`kernel-4.18.0-305.el8`) or later.
root_cause: * The underlying problem is that the Linux filesystem writeback path does not support writing to filesystem pages outside of specific kernel interfaces (`write_begin`... `write_end` and `page_mkwrite` before writing) and so things like RDMA and mmap then writing to file backed pages may cause panics in the writeback path. The issue is described in detail by Jan Kara and is complex. * A patchset that addresses these problems describes the background: ~~~ commit fc1d8e7cca2daa18d2fe56b94874848adf89d7f5 Author: John Hubbard Date: Mon May 13 17:19:08 2019-0700 mm: introduce put_user_page*(), placeholder versions... Overview ======== Some kernel components (file systems, device drivers) need to access memory that is specified via process virtual address. For a long time, the API to achieve that was get_user_pages ("GUP") and its variations. However, GUP has critical limitations that have been overlooked; in particular, GUP does not interact correctly with filesystems in all situations. That means that file-backed memory + GUP is a recipe for potential problems, some of which have already occurred in the field. GUP was first introduced for Direct IO (O_DIRECT), allowing filesystem code to get the struct page behind a virtual address and to let storage hardware perform a direct copy to or from that page. This is a short-lived access pattern, and as such, the window for a concurrent writeback of GUP'd page was small enough that there were not (we think) any reported problems. Also, userspace was expected to understand and accept that Direct IO was not synchronized with memory-mapped access to that data, nor with any process address space changes such as munmap(), mremap(), etc. Over the years, more GUP uses have appeared (virtualization, device drivers, RDMA) that can keep the pages they get via GUP for a long period of time (seconds, minutes, hours, days,...). This long-term pinning makes an underlying design problem more obvious. In fact, there are a number of key problems inherent to GUP: Interactions with file systems ============================== File systems expect to be able to write back data, both to reclaim pages, and for data integrity. Allowing other hardware (NICs, GPUs, etc) to gain write access to the file memory pages means that such hardware can dirty the pages, without the filesystem being aware. This can, in some cases (depending on filesystem, filesystem options, block device, block device options, and other variables), lead to data corruption, and also to kernel bugs of the form: kernel BUG at /build/linux-fQ94TU/linux-4.4.0/fs/ext4/inode.c:1899! backtrace: ext4_writepage__writepage write_cache_pages ext4_writepages do_writepages__writeback_single_inode writeback_sb_inodes__writeback_inodes_wb wb_writeback wb_workfn process_one_work worker_thread kthread ret_from_fork...which is due to the file system asserting that there are still buffer heads attached: ({\ BUG_ON(!PagePrivate(page)); \ ((struct buffer_head *)page_private(page)); \}) Dave Chinner's description of this is very clear: "The fundamental issue is that-> page_mkwrite must be called on every write access to a clean file backed page, not just the first one. How long the GUP reference lasts is irrelevant, if the page is clean and you need to dirty it, you must call-> page_mkwrite before it is marked writeable and dirtied. Every. Time." This is just one symptom of the larger design problem: real filesystems that actually write to a backing device, do not actually support get_user_pages() being called on their pages, and letting hardware write directly to those pages--even though that pattern has been going on since about 2005 or so. The steps are to fix it are: 1) (This patch): provide put_user_page*() routines, intended to be used for releasing pages that were pinned via get_user_pages*(). 2) Convert all of the call sites for get_user_pages*(), to invoke put_user_page*(), instead of put_page(). This involves dozens of call sites, and will take some time. 3) After (2) is complete, use get_user_pages*() and put_user_page*() to implement tracking of these pages. This tracking will be separate from the existing struct page refcounting. 4) Use the tracking and identification of these pages, to implement special handling (especially in writeback paths) when the pages are backed by a filesystem. [1] https://lwn.net/Articles/774411/: "DMA and get_user_pages()" [2] https://lwn.net/Articles/753027/: "The Trouble with get_user_pages()" ~~~

title: How to install the K8sCSIPlugin for Inspur storage?
issue: - Need to use Inspur storage device as persistent storage, but no CSI by default- In [Red Hat's container image registry](https://catalog.redhat.com/search?searchType=software&type=Containerized%20application ""), there is no CSI driver provided by Inspur.
resolution: - In the newer version of ***Inspur K8sCSIPlugin***, an automatic installation method is provided, which is not Containerized applicable to the OpenShift environment. If you need to use it, please modify the script manually as follows and try it.- For manual installation, take “2.3 手动安装 K8sCSIPlugin 插件” in the document ‘文档版本 2.4、发布日期 2024-03-30’ that customers can currently obtain as an example: 1. First, since RHEL 8 and later, the system no longer provides docker software packages, so it is recommended to use Podman to perform the corresponding operations (image-related operations in the document), or install docker and related software packages by yourself. That is, pull the image, load the image, and build the image. For example: ~~~ podman load-i images/centos8.1.1911-for-csiplugin0-image podman build-t csiplugin:v2.3.0-f Dockerfile. podman save localhost/csiplugin:v2.3.0-o csiplugin-v2.3.0 <=== Because the image will be pushed directly to the internal image warehouse later, there is no need to perform this operation ~~~ 2. According to the test, the method of pull (load) images in all nodes provided in the document may still not be able to complete the installation of Kubernetes provided by the upstream community; and this method is not suitable for the OpenShift environment. Therefore, please push the corresponding CSI container image to the internal image registry, for example: ~~~ podman tag centos8.1.1911:for-csiplugin0 bastion.ocp4.example.com:5000/csi/centos8.1.1911:for-csiplugin0 podman push bastion.ocp4.example.com:5000/csi/centos8.1.1911:for-csiplugin0 ~~~ The above operations need to be performed on all SIDECAR images provided by Inspur. Then there are two ways to proceed: 2.1 Configure **ImageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP)** rules to map *k8s.gcr.io* to the image registry inside OpenShift; 2.2 Modify the settings in **csi-instorage-deploy.yaml** that generated by the script or the **gen-deploy-file.sh** script to use the image in the OpenShift internal image registry directly. Among them, there are 8 SIDECAR images in ***csi-instorage-deploy.yaml***: ~~~ # grep-n gcr.io csi-instorage-deploy.yaml 22: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-provisioner:v3.1.0 39: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-attacher:v3.4.0 54: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-snapshotter:v5.0.1 68: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/snapshot-controller:v5.0.1 81: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-resizer:v1.4.0 95: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/livenessprobe:v2.6.0 170: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-node-driver-registrar:v2.5.0 192: image: k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/livenessprobe:v2.6.0 ~~~ The above are replaced with the information in the actual internal registry, for example: ~~~ image: bastion.ocp4.example.com:5000/csi/csi-provisioner:v3.1.0 ~~~ The corresponding settings need to be modified in ***gen-deploy-file.sh***: ~~~ 814 elif version_ge $K8S_VERSION "1.21" 815 then 816 # GA版本 大于等于 1.21 + 健康检查 817 SIDECAR_CSI_PROVISIONER=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-provisioner:v3.1.0 818 SIDECAR_CSI_ATTACHER=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-attacher:v3.4.0 819 SIDECAR_CSI_SNAPSHOTTER=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-snapshotter:v5.0.1 820 SIDECAR_SNAPSHOT_CONTROLLER=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/snapshot-controller:v5.0.1 821 SIDECAR_CSI_RESIZER=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-resizer:v1.4.0 822 SIDECAR_CSI_NODE_DRIVER_REGISTRAR=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-node-driver-registrar:v2.5.0 823 SIDECAR_LIVENESSPROBE=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/livenessprobe:v2.6.0 824 SIDECAR_CSI_HEALTH_MONITOR_CONTROLLER=k8s.gcr.io/sig-storage/csi-external-health-monitor-controller:v0.5.0 ~~~ 3. In addition to the above CSI image, you also need to push the created image ***csiplugin:v2.3.0*** to the OpenShift internal image registry and make corresponding settings. The following two settings need to be modified: ~~~ # grep-n 'image: csiplugin' csi-instorage-deploy.yaml 108: image: csiplugin:v2.3.0 207: image: csiplugin:v2.3.0 ~~~ Or modify PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL in ***gen-deploy-file.sh*** to set the actual address: ~~~ # grep-n PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL./scripts/gen-deploy-file.sh 31:PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL=csiplugin:v2.3.0 <=== 53: PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL=${OPTARG} 286: image: ${PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL} 337: image: ${PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL} 477: image: ${PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL} 587: image: ${PLUGIN_DRIVER_IMAGE_URL} ~~~ 4. The highest Kubernetes version in the current documentation and the container image compatibility list provided is 1.23. The OpenShift Container Platform version released based on Kubernetes 1.23 is 4.10, which has reached the end of its lifecycle. So When using it in a new version, you need to pay attention to its compatibility. If you need a newer version or an update of the current version K8sCSIPlugin, please contact Inspur.
root_cause: - Inspur does not directly provide the corresponding Container Storage Interface (CSI) Driver for OpenShift. Therefore, when using Inspur storage in an OpenShift environment, you need to install the K8sCSIPlugin provided by Inspur for Kubernetes. However, since no corresponding compatibility matching test has been performed, the steps described in the document need to be adjusted accordingly during installation based on the actual situation.- At the same time, the container image used by K8sCSIPlugin provided by Inspur still comes from the old image registry *k8s.gcr.io*; however, it cannot be directly accessed in some regions, such as mainland China; and the method provided in the document to load the image to al master and worker nodes through the docker command is not applicable to the OpenShift environment.

resolution: Use RH-SSO 7.3.6 or later, as this issue has been fixed since [RH-SSO 7.3 Update 6](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4766821) release. You might also need to set up a maximum length of the Event detail stored in the database by updating the relevant xml configuration file (aka, `standalone.xml`, `standalone-ha.xml`, or `domain.xml`, or `standalone-openshift.xml` in case of running with RH-SSO Openshift image). This setting can be useful in case some field (e.g. `redirect_uri`) is very long. Here is an example of defining the maximum length.: ~~~ /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=eventsStore/provider=jpa/:write-attribute(name=properties.max-detail-length,value=${keycloak.eventsStore.maxDetailLength:1000}) ~~~ and which will read in the RH-SSO xml configuration file as something like this: ~~~............... ~~~ **Notes:** An alternative workaround would be to [disable Event Logging in the RH-SSO admin console](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_single_sign-on/7.3/html/server_administration_guide/auditing_and_events) by removing "LOGIN" from the list of saved types in "Events-> SavedTypes" in the admin console. It is not recommended to try modify the database field to allow for the additional length, as that can be very problematic and it isn't a supported changed. It could also have performance issues, and could also potentially corrupt the database if the structure/schema is modified in RH-SSO patch to correct another issue.
root_cause: The field "Details_JSON" in the "Event_entity" has a max of 2550 characters. There are around 173 characters of other JSON information. The rest can be used for the URL. The issue is related to upstream bug [KEYCLOAK-12473](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/KEYCLOAK-12473), and which bug fix has been backported into RH-SSO 7.3.6 as per internal jira [KEYCLOAK-11987](https://issues.jboss.org/browse/KEYCLOAK-11987).

title: Elasticsearch misses genUUID field, resulting in missing Elasticsearch pods after RHOCP upgrade
issue:
- After RHOCP upgrade, `Elasticsearch` pods disappeared as `genUUID` field went missing in `Elasticsearch` Custom Resource (CR).- `Elasticsearch operator` pod throws the error: ~~~ 2021-03-12T13:54:05.637757911Z {"level":"error","ts":1615557245.637258,"logger":"kubebuilder.controller","msg":"Reconciler error","controller":"elasticsearch-controller","request":"openshift-logging/elasticsearch","error":"Failed to reconcile Elasticsearch deployment spec: Unsupported change to UUIDs made: Previously used GenUUID "xxxxxxxx" is no longer found in Spec.Nodes","stacktrace":"github.com/go-logr/zapr.(*zapLogger).Error
	/go/src/github.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/_output/src/github.com/go-logr/zapr/zapr.go:128
sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/internal/controller.(*Controller).processNextWorkItem
	/go/src/github.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/_output/src/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/internal/controller/controller.go:217
sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/internal/controller.(*Controller).Start.func1
	/go/src/github.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/_output/src/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/internal/controller/controller.go:158
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait.JitterUntil.func1
	/go/src/github.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/_output/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/wait.go:133
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait.JitterUntil
	/go/src/github.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/_output/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/wait.go:134
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait.Until
	/go/src/github.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/_output/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/wait.go:88"} ~~~
resolution: 1. Switch to the `openshift-logging` project and get the current `elasticsearch` configuration and status ~~~ $ oc project openshift-logging $ oc get Elasticsearch elasticsearch-o yaml ~~~ 2. check the `status` section of the yaml output. It should contain the current conditions, as well as the elasticsearch deployments. There may be multiple deployments for `elasticsearch-cdm` (for **C**lient/**D**ata/**M**aster) and `elasticsearch-cd` (for **C**lient/**D**ata) with different "genUUID" postfixes: ~~~ status: cluster: activePrimaryShards: 0 activeShards: 0 initializingShards: 0 numDataNodes: 0 numNodes: 0 pendingTasks: 0 relocatingShards: 0 status: "" unassignedShards: 0 conditions:- lastTransitionTime: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ" message: Previously used GenUUID "xxxxxxxx" is no longer found in Spec.Nodes reason: Invalid Spec status: "True" type: InvalidUUID nodes:- deploymentName: elasticsearch-cdm-xxxxxxxx-1 upgradeStatus: {}- deploymentName: elasticsearch-cdm-xxxxxxxx-2 upgradeStatus: {}- deploymentName: elasticsearch-cdm-xxxxxxxx-3 upgradeStatus: {}- deploymentName: elasticsearch-cd-yyyyyyyy-1 upgradeStatus: {} ~~~ 3. Set the Elasticsearch CR to be `Unmanaged` and verify the change applied: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging patch elasticsearch/elasticsearch-p '{"spec":{"managementState": "Unmanaged"}}'--type=merge elasticsearch.logging.openshift.io/elasticsearch patched $ oc-n openshift-logging get elasticsearch/elasticsearch NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT elasticsearch Unmanaged green 1 1 all ~~~ For Example: ~~~ apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: Elasticsearch metadata: name: elasticsearch namespace: openshift-logging... spec:... managementState: Unmanaged ~~~ 4. Update the `genUUID` in the `Elasticsearch` CR, creating them if they are missing, and then save the changes. Specifically, the `genUUID` for the `elasticsearch-cdm` nodes noted earlier go into the section with the `roles` of `client`, `data` and `master`, while the `genUUID` for the `elasticsearch-cd` nodes go into the section with the `roles` of `client` and `data` only (ie no `master`). For example: ~~~ spec: nodes:- nodeCount: 3 genUUID: xxxxxxx ====> Add the genUUID for the `elasticsearch-cdn` nodes. resources: {} roles:- client- data- master storage: size: 200G storageClassName: localblock-sc- nodeCount: 2 genUUID: yyyyyyyy ====> Add the genUUID for the `elasticsearch-cd` nodes. proxyResources: {} resources: {} roles:- client- data storage: size: 900G storageClassName: gp2 redundancyPolicy: SingleRedundancy ~~~ 5. Set `Elasticsearch` CR managementState back to Managed and save the changes: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging patch elasticsearch/elasticsearch-p '{"spec":{"managementState": "Managed"}}'--type=merge elasticsearch.logging.openshift.io/elasticsearch patched $ oc-n openshift-logging get elasticsearch/elasticsearch NAME MANAGEMENT STATE HEALTH NODES DATA NODES SHARD ALLOCATION INDEX MANAGEMENT elasticsearch Managed green 1 1 all ~~~ 6. After applying above changes, the `Elasticsearch` `deployments` and `pods` should roll out successfully: ~~~ $ oc get pods-l component=elasticsearch NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE... elasticsearch-cdm-xxxxxxxx-1-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx 2/2 Running 0 43s elasticsearch-cdm-xxxxxxxx-2-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx 2/2 Running 0 22s elasticsearch-cdm-xxxxxxxx-3-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx 2/2 Running 0 23s elasticsearch-cd-yyyyyyyy-1-yyyyyyyyyy-yyyyy 2/2 Running 0 22s elasticsearch-cd-yyyyyyyy-2-yyyyyyyyyy-yyyyy 2/2 Running 0 23s... ~~~

title: Red Hat OpenJDK Java Image IO support
issue: - What happened to Java Advanced Image?- Does Red Hat support Java Image IO?
resolution: --- ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to an external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*--- Java Advanced Image (JAI) was superseded by Java Image IO (imports `javax.imageio`), which has been in every release of Red Hat OpenJDK so it is supported. As consequence, in OpenJDK JAI package has been removed. See [Oracle Advanced Imaging Api](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/advanced-imaging-api.html) > Due to the many requests for a comprehensive image I/O package the Java Image I/O API was developed. The Java Image I/O API is part of the Java TM 2 Platform, Standard Edition, version 1.4 (J2SE1.4). ### Usage of `com.sun` packages For users relying on JAI with Oracle JDK, it is not recommended the usage of `com.sun` packages, which are not public. https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/faq-sun-packages.html ### Deprecation on JDK 7 Some of the packages of `com.sun.image` were deprecated/removed already on JDK 7, for instance `com.sun.image.codec.jpeg`, see [Oracle JDK 7 Compatibility](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/compatibility.html). ### Package `jai-imageio-core` Available for RHEL 7, and never added to RHEL 8, there is `jai-imageio-core`, which contains a CVS snapshot of `jai-imageio-core` from https://jai-imageio.dev.java.net/. This package support formats (and codecs) that the core OpenJDK does not support.

title: The workspace has not received an IDE URL in the last 20 seconds
issue: - While creating/opening exiting Workspace getting error: The workspace has not received an IDE URL in the last 20 seconds. Try to re-open the workspace
resolution: Configure network policies as described in the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_dev_spaces/3.14/html-single/administration_guide/index#configuring-network-policies "documentation"). **Note**: wherever `openshift-devspaces` is mentioned in `NetworkPolicy` yaml provided in documentation replace it with project name where the `CheCluster` CustomResource is deployed.

title: Configure the Argo CD route with Reencrypt TLS termination in Red Hat OpenShift GitOps
issue: - Red Hat OpenShift GitOps Argo CD by default relies on a route with `passthrough` TLS termination and a self-signed certificate.- While having a global custom Ingress certificate in place for the ingress controller, need to make Argo CD rely on a route with `re-encrypt` TLS termination.
resolution: Red Hat OpenShift GitOps v1.13.0 uses the `reencrypt` TLS termination by default.- [RHEA-2024:4359](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHEA-2024:4359)- Product Enhancement Advisory For earlier versions, the route has to be configured manually as described in the following steps:- Configuring the Argo CD route for `reencrypt` TLS termination:- Patch the `argocd/openshift-gitops` instance to configure Argo CD route with `reencrypt` TLS termination ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-gitops patch argocd/openshift-gitops--type=merge-p='{"spec":{"server":{"route":{"enabled":true,"tls":{"insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy":"Redirect","termination":"reencrypt"}}}}}' ~~~ **Note:** This solution is for the scenario having a custom/public CA-signed certificate already configured for the ingress controller. Else, if not, the wildcard certificate served by the ingress controller remains self-signed as it is issued by ingress-CA, which results in a `Not secure` warning on the browser.

title: Why forwarding logs as JSON to Loki in RHOCP 4  is not needed?
issue: Is it needed to parse JSON logs into a structured object when forwarding them to a Loki output?
Can logs be forwarded using `parse: json` for all output types when creating a `ClusterLogForwarder`?
resolution: > **Disclaimer**:_Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ When forwarding logs to Loki, one does not need to use the option `parse: json` to be able to do queries using the JSON structured `keys:values`. For example: to search for the logs containing the JSON key `myField` with value `has-a-value` one can use the query: ``` {kubernetes_pod_name="something-something"} | json | myField="has-a-value" ``` instead of: ``` {kubernetes_pod_name="something-something", myField="has-a-value"} ``` To learn more about how to use **Log queries**, check the Loki [upstream documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/log_queries/). In addition to the above, it is not recommended to use `parse: json` when forwarding logs to Loki using a `ClusterLogForwarder`. The usage of the `parse: json` plugin for parsing JSON logs would have the consequence that more resources would be consumed by the collector to perform the actual parsing, and also would add an unnecessary overhead on the Loki server.
root_cause: In Loki it is possible to query as JSON without the need to forward the logs using `parse: json`. By following this best practice, one reduces the impact on the performance on the Loki server. The filtering is then moved to the client side, without impact on the performance. With Loki, the data is embedded as streams. Therefore the client only needs to create the query expression using the right filters. In addition, the usage of the `parse: json` plugin is equivalent to adding dynamic labels. But using dynamic labels is not recommended in Loki, because it can [reduce the performance](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/get-started/labels/bp-labels/#use-dynamic-labels-sparingly).

title: Best Practices for Monitoring Red Hat Virtualization
issue: How do we setup consistent enough monitoring architecture so that RHV environment health can be properly assessed and alerting is triggered when needed?
resolution: Currently, possible ways to monitor RHV include: **1) RHV notification service** This is the most preferable way. It can generate email or SNMP traps. This is documented in [RHV Admin Guide- Event notifications](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_virtualization/4.4/html/administration_guide/chap-event_notifications#Configuring_the_Red_Hat_Enterprise_Virtualization_Manager_to_Send_SNMP_Traps) Also, an external tool can be used to insert some alerts to the event log. For instance, an agent on a guest system may send a RestAPI request to add an entry to the event log with information about the filesystem, memory, and so on. **2) Ovirt engine RestAPI can be used to collect information about the hosts, VMS, storage domains, and so on.** Couple of examples: ~~~ https://example.com/ovirt-engine/api/vms/${VM_UUID}/statistics https://example.com/ovirt-engine/api/vms/${VM_UUID}/nics/${NIC_UUID}/statistics https://example.com/ovirt-engine/api/hosts/${HOST_UUID}/statistics https://example.com/ovirt-engine/api/hosts/${HOST_UUID}/nics/${NIC_UUID}/statistics ~~~ In the example above example.com should be replaced with URL of RHV Manager, ${VM_UUID} ${NIC_UUID} and ${HOST_UUID} with relevant UUIDs respectively. This might bring some problems if the monitoring tool is sending requests to RestAPI too often as it could cause additional load on the RHV Manager, this also depends on the environment size, should be thoroughly tested. More details on RHV RestAPI models and some examples could be found on the website of oVirt- an upstream project of RHV: [oVirt REST API documentation](http://ovirt.github.io/ovirt-engine-api-model/) Official documentation on RHV RestAPI is available here: [RHV REST API Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_virtualization/4.4/html/rest_api_guide/index) **3) SNMP on hypervisor** It does not look like we have anything specific to RHV here, so only standard RHEL SNMP data can be monitored. Might be used as an additional tool to monitor hosts. This is documented in [Deployment guide- ⁠19.7. Monitoring Performance with Net-SNMP](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/system_administrators_guide/ch-system_monitoring_tools#sect-System_Monitoring_Tools-Net-SNMP) **4) Red Hat CloudForms** CloudForms is a tool from Red Hat for managing your hybrid infrastructure, there is also a nice [overview](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/management/cloudforms) Currently, CloudForms uses metrics from RHV Data Warehouse (DWH). Just for reference, here's the link to [RHV DATA WAREHOUSE GUIDE](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_virtualization/4.4/html/data_warehouse_guide/index) **5) [WIP] oVirt Metrics Store** RHV documentation is available [on this page](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_virtualization/4.3/html-single/metrics_store_installation_guide/index) This will be the future monitoring for RHV and it will be improved in the next releases. The documentation for RHV is not ready yet so the above-mentioned oVirt documentation has to be used. There is an RFE to document the installation for RHV: [Bug 1451625- [Docs][RFE][Admin] Document how to deploy and configure Collectd and Fluentd on host and Manager machines](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1451625) This will require an OpenShift instance running in the customer's environment. If the instance is only used for the metric store then it is free for use and no additional subscriptions are required. More information is also available in [this presentation](https://www.redhat.com/files/summit/session-assets/2017/LT122010-radco.pdf).

title: Assign pod terminal access to a user/group in RHOCP 4
issue: - Non-Admin users are not able to access Pod terminal.- Need to assign pod terminal access to the user/group.- User who has `view` access on project not able to access pod terminal.- Users are not able to run `oc rsh` command in the cluster.
resolution: - By default the user with `project admin` access can access the pod terminal. Non `project admin` users can not access pod terminal.- To assign pod terminal access to users, create a custom role: ~~~ $ oc create role--verb=get,list,create--resource=pods/exec-n ~~~- Assign created custom role to the user: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-role-to-user--role-namespace=-n ~~~- To assign custom role to the group: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-role-to-group--role-namespace=-n ~~~- After assigning this custom role, the user will be able to `rsh` to the pod inside the same project.

title: StatefulSet pods not rescheduled automatically on node failure in OpenShift
issue: - StatefulSet pods not rescheduled automatically on node failure in OpenShift- StatefulSet pods not evicted automatically on node failure in OpenShift- Eviction doesn't work for StatefulSet pods in OpenShift
