title: rook-ceph-operator CreateContainerConfigError on install ODF 4.13/4.14
issue: When installing it does not succeed as the `rook-ceph-operator` is stuck in `CreateContainerConfigError` error.
resolution: Delete the `ocs-operator-config` ConfigMap in the `openshift-storage` namespace: ~~~ oc delete cm ocs-operator-config-n openshift-storage ~~~
root_cause: The `ocsinitialization` controller creates the `ocs-operator-config` ConfigMap, from which the `rook-ceph-operator` pod takes environment values for its configuration. The task of keeping it updated is on the `storagecluster` CR. But when a storagecluster CR is not there and an Install occurs, the configMap is not updated but the new `rook-ceph-operator` pod looks for the Key for configuration. So the `rook-ceph-operator` pod fails & so does the install.

title: Why new install of MicroShift reports "Node not ready" in proxy environment?
issue: *Why new install of MicroShift reports "Node not ready"?

MicroShift reports failure to pull the image "pinging container registry quay.io: Get \"https://quay.io/v2/\": EOF"" ~~~ Nov 27 11:39:37 test.net microshift[19823]: kubelet E1127 11:39:37.246567 19823 remote_runtime.go:176] "RunPodSandbox from runtime service failed" err="rpc error: code = Unknown desc = creating pod sandbox with name \"k8s_ovnkube-master-mb9gs_openshift-ovn-kubernetes_1c643722-509f-4189-aa43-af2865f19e37_0\": initializing source docker://quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:a473975a9daa31cb3d4805ea03f3e16818caecb073758d5c4982dc056c585e2a: pinging container registry quay.io: Get \"https://quay.io/v2/\": EOF" ~~~
resolution: If proxy is required to pull images from internet, then configure proxy for `crio` service. 1\. Create a drop-in for crio service 1.1 `mkdir /etc/systemd/system/crio.service.d/` 1.2 Add the following to `/etc/systemd/system/crio.service.d/00-proxy.conf` ~~~ [Service] Environment=NO_PROXY="localhost,127.0.0.1" Environment=HTTP_PROXY="http://$PROXY_USER:$PROXY_PASSWORD@$PROXY_SERVER:$PROXY_PORT/" Environment=HTTPS_PROXY="http://$PROXY_USER:$PROXY_PASSWORD@$PROXY_SERV ~~~ 2\. After adding the above drop-in, restart the crio/microshift service 2.2 systemctl daemon-reload 2.3 systemctl restart crio microshift For detailed steps, refer the [Microshift documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_build_of_microshift/4.14/html/networking/microshift-understanding-networking-settings)

title: Can Multiple PVCs Bind to One PV in OpenShift?
issue: - We have many volumes that are used by multiple servers- Are we able to create multiple persistent volume claims for one persistent volume?- If we have 6 different services that need to use an NFS share do we have to create 6 PersistentVolumes to the same back-end NFS share?
resolution: - There is a 1:1 ratio of PVs to PVCs. If one NFS share must be used by multiple servers/applications, it is necessary to create multiple PVs to point to one NFS share.- Multiple PVC can not be bound to a single PV. For each PV there should be separate PVC.- PVCs are specific to a project and are created and used by developers as a means to use a PV. PV resources on their own are not scoped to any single project; they can be shared across the entire OpenShift Container Platform cluster and claimed from any project. After a PV is bound to a PVC, that PV can not then be bound to additional PVCs. This has the effect of scoping a bound PV to a single namespace, that of the binding project.

title: Error creating: Internal error occurred: admission plugin "MutatingAdmissionWebhook" failed to complete mutation in 13s?
issue: - Pods are failed to get created with error 'Error creating: Internal error occurred: admission plugin "MutatingAdmissionWebhook" failed to complete mutation in 13s'
resolution: - If the core networking pods themselves are failing, one can just delete the webhook, let the pods come to running stats, and recreate the webhook.- As a Webhook admin, one should exclude openshift core components.- For more details please read [Improving Supportability of API webhooks](https://github.com/openshift/enhancements/blob/master/enhancements/kube-apiserver/api-webhook-supportability.md#skip-3rd-party-admission-webhooks-on-runlevel0-namespaces)- Red Hat is aware of such incidents and our documentation team is working on documenting more clarity in product page.- Check for the webhooks that are have timeout values of longer than 10s: ~~~ oc get MutatingWebhookConfiguration,validatingwebhookconfigurations-o custom-columns=KIND:.kind,NAME:.metadata.name,TIMEOUT:.webhooks[].timeoutSeconds ~~~ Modify any found to `10s` to stay below the 13s timeout value: ~~~ oc edit MutatingWebhookConfiguration/ #change the spec.timeout value to 10s and save the object ~~~- As a proactive step prior to upgrade to 4.14, you may modify any webhooks to have timeouts to 10s prior to the upgrade to prevent this problem from occurring during the upgrade.
root_cause: - Check if the api server is able to connect the webhook service.

title: Maven binary included in the certified S2I JAVA images with high severity CVEs
issue: - From scan results that an old version of the Maven binary is included in the certified S2I JAVA images and is classified with high severity CVEs.- RHACS scan found many vulnerability for image `jboss-webserver-5/jws57-openjdk8-openshift-rhel8`
resolution: - In RHACS version 4.4 with scanner V4 enabled issues disappear.
root_cause: - This is a false positive, depending on a discrepancy between vulnerabilities reported by Quay Security Scanner and RHACS.

title: The Azure AD OIDC shows User ID instead of username.
issue: - After integrating Azure AD with the on-premise cluster the OIDC shows a user ID instead of the username.
resolution: - Edit the OAuth config to add the parameter which consists of username under `preferredUsername`. ~~~ openID: claims: email:- email name:- name preferredUsername:- email < <==Add this parameter.- upn ~~~ If adding this parameter doesn't resolve the issue, you can add the following configuration as well ~~~ spec: identityProviders:- mappingMethod: claim name: AAD openID: claims: email:- email name:- name preferredUsername:- email- preferred_username extraScopes:- profile- openid- email ~~~ More information can be found here: https://cloud.redhat.com/experts/idp/group-claims/aro/ and here https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/configure-azure-ad-ui
root_cause: - The issue is with the display name of the user in OpenShift, which comes from the `name` claim in Azure AD.- This happens when the claim `name` is empty or has the wrong parameter configured.

title: Understanding OCP Insights Vulnerability Dashboard
issue: - How do I interpret the information presented on the Insights Vulnerability Dashboard? How do I know which cluster / image to remediate and upgrade?- How is this information different from the information available via RHACS vulnerability dashboard?
resolution: - [Red Hat Insights Vulnerability Dashboard](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_cluster_manager/2023/html/assessing_security_vulnerabilities_in_your_openshift_cluster_using_red_hat_insights/index) is included with Red Hat subscription. This service provides analysis for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.8+ and above. The analysis is provided for the infrastructure and images within Red Hat's Ecosystem catalog, **not** the workloads that are running within RHOCP.- [Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes](https://access.redhat.com/products/red-hat-advanced-cluster-security-for-kubernetes/) (RHACS) provides rich functionality to discover, monitor and mitigate threats and enforce security policies within your Kubernetes environment. Among its many features, the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes scanner discovers vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in container images and allows you to define policies for vulnerability management that can be applied at build, deploy and runtime. RHACS is included with [OpenShift Platform Plus](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_platform_plus/4/html/architecture/opp-architecture) or can be used via [RHACS Cloud Service](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.1/html/rhacs_cloud_service/index).- Insights Vulnerability Dashboard shows impacted Clusters of your OpenShift infrastructure and helps making upgrade decisions. It is not a comprehensive vulnerability management solution for OpenShift. If you are looking for vulnerability management for OpenShift and the workloads running on OpenShift, RHACS is the right solution for this.- Specifically, the Insights Vulnerability Dashboard shows the OpenShift clusters affected by CVEs. There are no plans to show images that are affected by the CVEs impacting the OpenShift clusters. This information will eventually be available within RHACS.

title: Disable the machine-config-operator autoreboot after a change in OCP 4
issue: - Avoid Openshift Container Platform 4.x automatically applying `MachineConfig` changes which require reboots.- Because of the autoreboot is started when the configuration has been changed by the Administrator. If the autoreboot which is unwanted at that moment, it can be paused by the Administrator.- Is it possible to pause `MachineConfigPool` to apply multiple `MachineConfigs` at one time?
resolution: Configuration changes to OpenShift hosts such as creating a new machine config for modifying the `NTP `configuration, or modifying the registry mirror(`imagecontentsourcepolicy`), `user-ca-bundle` (`configmap`), `pull-secret` (`secret`), registries, SSH keys, and `kubelet` configuration, etc., may be paused in order to prevent rolling reboots by setting the `spec.paused` field in the machineconfigpool to `true`: The paused field specifies whether or not changes to this machine config pool should be stopped, this includes generating a new `desiredMachineConfig` and update of machines. ### Pause the autoreboot via modifying `machineconfigpool` > **WARNING:** Remember that by **pausing** the MCP, **ALL config changes are paused**. This **prevents several changes required for the correct operation of the cluster**, including RHCOS updates, kernel arguments, file changes, proxy changes, crio/kubelet configuration, node/kubelet certificate rotations, etc. etc. from reaching any of the nodes. Doing so **can lead to potential problems** if other components assume that those config changes are already in place but they are not due to MCP being paused. In addition, it can cause failures in multiple `oc` commands, including but not limited to `oc debug`, `oc logs`, `oc exec`, and `oc attach`. In such cases, it is the user's responsibility to deal with that and un-pause accordingly. > > For additional information, refer to [The Consequences Of Pausing MachineConfig Pools In OpenShift's Machine Config Operator (MCO)](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/the-consequences-of-pausing-machineconfig-pools-in-openshifts-machine-config-operator-mco). The Administrator can pause the auto-reboot which is unwanted at that moment, modify `spec.paused` field to `true`. #### For master ~~~ # oc patch--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"paused":true}}' machineconfigpool/master ~~~ #### For worker ~~~ # oc patch--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"paused":true}}' machineconfigpool/worker ~~~ ### Checking the paused status Get to know whether the machine config pool is paused or unpaused, use `oc get machineconfigpool` or `oc get mcp` to check the `spec.paused` field is `true` or `false`. #### For master ~~~ # oc get machineconfigpool/master--template='{{.spec.paused}}' ~~~ #### For worker ~~~ # oc get machineconfigpool/worker--template='{{.spec.paused}}' ~~~ ### How to know when machine config pool must be unpaused MCO usually expects to be able to apply host level changes to the nodes, which in turn requires them to be rebooted. When `spec.paused` is `true`, it means that the changes are paused, i.e. not applied but just queued. If there are queued changes, it is recommended to schedule a maintenance window for a reboot as early as possible by turning `spec.paused`to `false`, so that the queued changes since last reboot will take effect. Failing to do this may result in different issues, the higher changes stay not applied the bigger the risk of issues. Once changes are applied, MCP can be paused again. Best way to check for pending changes is to run `oc get mcp-o wide`. With OCP 4.6, if there are pending changes, `UPDATED` column will be false and `UPDATING` column will be true even when no update is actually in progress due to pause. With OCP 4.7 and later, if there are pending changes,`UPDATED` column will be false and `UPDATING` column will remain false as well, and follow check will be useful. Another way to check is to see if the rendered config at MCP `spec` (the desired one) is different than the one at `status` (the current one). That can be checked like this: ~~~ $ oc get mcp-o custom-columns=NAME:metadata.name,DESIRED:spec.configuration.name,CONFIG-STATUS:status.configuration.name NAME DESIRED CURRENT master rendered-master-a373c027745838e7a7cd341a2c522d60 rendered-master-a373c027745838e7a7cd341a2c522d60 worker rendered-worker-17ca378c0ac4c57866cf65d0ee92d549 rendered-worker-535cfd38878432294695598224d899e3 ~~~ In this example, we can see that the desired spec for worker MCP is different from the current one, i.e. there are changes pending for worker MCP, while the master has curent config equal to desired one, i.e. no pending changes. ### Unpause the autoreboot via modifying `machineconfigpool` #### For master ~~~ # oc patch--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"paused":false}}' machineconfigpool/master ~~~ #### For worker ~~~ # oc patch--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"paused":false}}' machineconfigpool/worker ~~~
root_cause: OpenShift 4 is an operator-focused platform, and the Machine Config operator extends that to the operating system itself, managing updates and configuration changes to essentially everything between the `kernel` and `kubelet`. To repeat for emphasis, this operator manages updates to `systemd`, `cri-o`/`kubelet`, `kernel`, `NetworkManager`, etc. It also offers a new MachineConfig CRD that can write configuration files onto the host. For details, please refer to the Machine Config Operator Documentation. [Understanding the Machine Config Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/architecture/control-plane.html#understanding-machine-config-operator_control-plane)

title: Error authenticating "" with provider "AD": Could not retrieve a non-empty value for ID attributes for dn=""
issue: - After configuring ldap identity provider we are unable to log on to the openshift console using LDAP accounts- The `oauth-openshift` log shown an error message of `Error authenticating "user1" with provider "AD": Could not retrieve a non-empty value for ID attributes for dn="CN=xxxx,OU=xxxx,DC=xxxx,DC=xx,DC=xxx,DC=xx"`
resolution: Edit the `oauth cluster` CR by doing `oc edit oauth cluster` and make sure that on the list of attributes to use as the identity it has an attribute that exists. More details on Diagnostic Steps.
root_cause: The attribute used on `id` parameter needs a value. If none of the listed attribute have a value, authentication fails.

title: JGroups cluster transport configuration for Data Grid Server 8.x
issue: - How to configure JGroups ports for Data Grid Server without using infinispan.xml?- Which JGroups transport configuration is recommended?- What discovery protocol is recommended?- What ports are used for communication between nodes in a cluster?- Is it possible to cluster Data Grid instances running on two different hosts?
resolution: Red Hat Data Grid is mainly used in clustered configurations that balance client requests to distribute load and avoid excessive memory resource consumption from any one instance. RHDG uses JGroups technology as the underlying framework that provides clustering capabilities. JGroups provides mechanisms for cluster discovery and transport and also offers features such as failure detection through the use of additional network sockets. This article is intended to provide information that helps you understand how to tailor JGroups settings for different network environments and successfully set up RHDG clustering. #### RHDG defaults RHDG provides default JGroups stack configurations as part of the [Data Grid distribution](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.1/html/configuring_data_grid/configuring_clustering#jgroups_getting_started-configuring "Getting Started with Default Stacks"). The default stacks provide basic functionality that should work out of the box in most cases. The default TCP and UDP stacks use multicast and full port ranges for all cluster members. If it is possible to use UDP with multicast, it is recommended to use the `udp` stack because it scales better with messages sent 1-many. If it is not possible to use UDP or multicast, then you can use the `tcp` stack. However, this can negatively affect performance because messages are sent 1-1 and cause more network traffic and processing for the nodes. Change the JGroups stack that clusters use with the `-j ` or `--cluster-stack= ` arguments when starting the server or change the `infinispan.cluster.stack` attribute for the ` ` element in configuration. **Hint** The `-b` option will set the IP address of the server API (Hotrod, http, etc) and not affect the IP JGroups inner cluster communication will use, this is elected according to the JGroups configuration by default SITE_LOCAL, see [JGroups Transport](http://jgroups.org/manual4/index.html#Transport “JGroups 4.x documentation). The server start parameter `-k’ ‘--cluster-address` will set the IP address if the configuration contains the expression `jgroups.bind.address`, otherwise it must be directly set by configuration. #### Recommended approach In production the recommended way is to use the start options or properites to static settings to ensure the used IP addresses and ports are known. The settings should be fixed and use the different properties to set fixed port numbers and overwrite the port_range with “0” to not allow unexpected variations. Also the port-offset provided by `-o`, which provide to add an offset for the used ports to allow severa instances on the same machine, is not recommended for production because of opaque behavior. **Hint** Until 8.1.1 the offset affects only the RHDG API port `infinispan.bind.port` from 8.1.1 onwards it will add this offset to the `jgroups.bind.port` as well. ##### Important properties for configuration- `infinispan.cluster.stack` By default `tcp`is used, could be set with start option `-j ` or `--cluster-stack= `- `infinispan.bind.address` should be used to use the fix IP address- `infinispan.bind.port` should be used to change the public server port (11222) if necessary- `jgroups.bind.address` The interface JGroups will bind for udp and tcp (Cloud protocols are using this as well as tcp is used) It will default to SITE_LOCAL for the transport, but use 127.0.0.1 for MPING.- `jgroups.bind.port` The port JGroups will bind for udp and tcp (Cloud protocols are using this as well as tcp is used) For tcp transport it is `7800` For udp it is set to `0` which means random port election Port_range for UDP and TCP needs configuration change as not set and default to > 0- `jgroups.mcast_addr` Multicast address for discovery used by udp PING and tcp MPING- `jgroups-mcast_port` Multicast port for discovery used by udp PING and tcp MPING- `jgroups.join.timeout` Setting for a timeout for membership detection For a simple start command there is a new option, from RHDG 8.1.1 onwards the option `-P` `--properties= ` for the server start command can be sued to provide all the settings with a single configuration file. #### Cluster node detection There are different membership discovery protocols supported, especially for Cloud environments. See the [Default JGroups Stacks](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.1/html/configuring_data_grid/configuring_clustering#jgroups_getting_started-configuring), [Cluster Discovery](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.1/html/configuring_data_grid/configuring_clustering#cluster_discovery) and [Running Data Grid on OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.1/html/running_data_grid_on_openshift/) With the recommended UDP configuration JGroups will use UDP Multicast with the ` ` protocol to detect other nodes in the same sub-network, if a wider network is used or the network is restricted it multicast needs to be checked. It is highly recommended to check the multicast addresses or set `-Djgroups.mcast_addr=` and/or `-Djgroups.mcast_port=` to a different and unique address. This will prevent problems if other (default) instances are started in the same network and join a cluster by accident! Consider that all applications like EAP or RHDG which are using JGroups might connect. It would produce weird warn or error messages if different versions of JGroups are connecting as it is not ensured that the protocol will be compatible. At least a warning should be seen that messages of unknown members are discarded. The default TCP configuration will use MPING which relies on multicast as well. And will have the same restrictions as UDP transport. To switch to a static discovery ` ` should be used which will not use Multicast but needs static configuration. The following configuration for infinispan.xml will extend the default TCP configuration and change the discovery ~~~ ~~~ **Important Note:** It is important to use these parameters **{stack.combine="REPLACE" stack.position="MPING"}** while using "extends="tcp" to use TCPPING instead of MPING. Without this MPING is used from default tcp stack. Refer (documentation)[https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.3/html-single/data_grid_server_guide/index#customizing-jgroups-stacks_cluster-transport] Note that JGroups will probe the bind-port and increase the port-number, if not suppressed by port_range, if it is used by another process. This allows starting multiple instances of RHDG at the same machine. The TCPPING initial_hosts list should include all cluster members, including this one so the list is the same for all instances, to ensure best detection. If the addresses are all fixed and known the port_range should be set to "0" to not probe other instances which is unnecessary. **Hint** until 8.1.1 the `-o` start option to add a port-offset is not used for JGroups. It will remain the initial port, or increased by 1 if used as the default port_range is not “0”. From 8.1.1 onwards the port-offset is used and added to the bind_port if `jgroups.bind.port` expression is used. The port_range should be set to "0" in this case to prevent from unexpected change to the port and because of that unexpected discovery results. #### Use JGroups static port or autoincrement for 8.1.1+ To remove the port offset and use the automatic JGroups increment the transport bind_port could be set to a hard value without using the `${jgroups.bind.port}`, the `-o` parameter will then not have any effect to this and JGroups will increment the value by “1” if the port_range will allow it. Example for a static port setting ~~~ ~~~ If multiple instances are started with port_range=”0”, or the port_range is to low, for the same JGroups IP address the server will not start and fail with a FATAL message: ~~~ Caused by: java.net.BindException: no port available in range [7800.. 7800] (bind_addr=/) ~~~ #### Other used ports The FD_SOCK protocol will use a port as well to detect fast failure of a node. **Note** by default it will use a random port which might be affected by firewall permissions. To restrict the port to a known number `start_port` and `port_range` can be used to limit the used ports. ~~~..... ~~~ With the configuration above the FD_SOCK protocol is completely replaced in the default udp stack at the same place! There is a request to use a fix start port and allow th `-o` option to take effect for FD_SOCK port [ISPN-12531](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ISPN-12531) For more information the documentation [Configure Data Grid Clustering](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.1/html/configuring_data_grid/configuring_clustering) should be visited.

title: Is it supported to disable SELinux in Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS ?
issue: - Is it supported to disable SELinux in Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS (RHCOS)?
resolution: - No, it isn't supported to disable SELinux in a RHCOS node. If SELinux is ever disabled (even by accident), the node must be recreated/reinstalled.- Please refer to the [product documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/security/container_security/security-hosts-vms.html#security-hosts-vms-rhcos_security-hosts-vms) for more details.
root_cause: - SELinux is one extremely important security layer for RHCOS. Disabling it can severely increase the surface attack on the system.- Besides, when SELinux is disabled, the files are no longer labeled as expected. In a traditional RHEL system, this can be fixed by relabeling the file system, but this is not an option in RHCOS due to some of its specific internals. So if a node has SELinux disabled, it must be rebuilt.

title: Openshift-SDN - disable weak SSH cipher suites
issue: - Openshift-sdn component, specifically on port 9101, has exposed certain cipher suites that are considered weak.- The currently accepted weak ciphers- TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256 and- TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256, are not configurable, as they are hardcoded in the manifests.
resolution: - This behavior is marked as a bug and is being tracked in a JIRA.- Open a [Support Ticket](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) with Red Hat to get further updates on the issue.

title: Custom Grafana Dashboard for custom metrics
issue: - How to create custom dashboards of Grafana from custom metrics? How to use prometheus from openshift-user-workload-monitoring for the same?- How to create custom Grafana dashboards using Grafana operator available from OperatorHub?- How to create custom Grafana dashboards where default available metrics and custom metrics can be queried?- How to use Thanos querier as datasource for custom Grafana?
resolution: > **Note:** Starting with OCP 4.9 it's possible to configure remote write storage to send the Prometheus metrics to a remote system, and use that remote system with a custom Grafana. Refer to [KCS 6490491: Configure remote write in Prometheus Operator in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6490491) for additional information. > **IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER NOTES; UNSUPPORTED BY RED HAT** > > * *Red Hat does not support direct access to Prometheus externally because heavy ad-hoc queries can overload and degrade the Prometheus instance.* > > * *The following configuration does not permit Red Hat support to assist with a custom community version of Grafana nor any related doubt whenever there is a custom Grafana dashboard. The procedure documented in this article is not supported by Red Hat Support under [our support terms](https://access.redhat.com/es/support/offerings/production/soc).* ### Unsupported configuration The support for modification and customization for the OpenShift Monitoring stack is limited. More details on this can be [found in product documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/monitoring/cluster_monitoring/configuring-the-monitoring-stack.html#maintenance-and-support_configuring-monitoring). 1. **Deploy openshift-user-workload-monitoring stack** Deploy the openshift-user-workload-monitoring as described in [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/monitoring/monitoring-your-own-services.html#enabling-monitoring-of-your-own-services_monitoring-your-own-services) for monitoring application for custom metrics. 2. **Creating sample application which exposes custom metrics:**- To test custom metrics functionality, deploy the prometheus sample app as mentioned in the [documentation of monitoring your own services](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/monitoring/monitoring-your-own-services.html#deploying-a-sample-service_monitoring-your-own-services) which is exposing the custom metrics: `version`.- Also, create the `servicemonitor` for that application in the same application namespace as per the yaml definition in [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/monitoring/monitoring-your-own-services.html#setting-up-metrics-collection_monitoring-your-own-services).- Make sure that the custom metrics version can be queried from `thanos-querier` where `prometheus-user-workload` is used for scraping that particular metrics. [image=[src="images/thanos.png", title="Thons querier image where custom metrics can be queried.", alt="Thoanos console screenshot where custom metrics can be queried.", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] 3. **Deploy Grafana operator version 3.5:**- Open OpenShift webconsole and switch to `OperatorHub` section. Search for `Grafana operator provided by Red Hat` and Continue to accept the disclaimer, click `Install` button if you see **Grafana operator version as 3.5**. Then choose **openshift-user-workload-monitoring** as `Installed Namespace` and again click on `install` button.- Check if the Grafana operator gets successfully installed in Installed operator tab. [image=[src="images/grafana-3.png", title="Installed operators setion", alt="Installed operators section to check Grafana operator has successfully installed.", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] Check if the grafana-operator pod is in running state. ~~~ # oc get pods-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE grafana-operator-87f65f995-xxxxx 1/1 Running 0 83s ~~~ 4. **Create Grafana instance:**- From `Installed Operators`, select the `Grafana Operator`. For the Grafana resource, navigate to `Grafana` tab and click on `Create Grafana` button to create new Grafana instance. [image=[src="images/grafana-4.png", title="Create Grafana instance with provided APIs of Grafana operator", alt="Create Grafna instance image", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]]- Click on create by adding name for Grafana instance and after that you will see one grafana instance in the same page. [image=[src="images/grafana-5.png", title="Checking created Grafana instance ", alt="Checking created Grafana instance", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] Also, you need to check if Grafana pod is in running state or not. ~~~ # oc get pods-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE grafana-deployment-8667d4d4fc-xxxxx 1/1 Running 0 40s ~~~- Expose `grafana-service` to get access to the `Grafana` UI: ~~~ # oc expose svc/grafana-service ~~~ 5. **Create Grafana Data Source:**- Integrating `Thanos querier` as data source for custom grafana would be good idea as Thanos querier is able to query metrics from default prometheus instance from `openshift-monitoring` as well as from prometheus instance of `openshift-user-workload-monitoring`. So, it gives capability to create custom Grafana dashboard where default available metrics and custom metrics can be queried to fetch the data in Graph format.- The `grafana-serviceaccount` service account was created alongside the `Grafana instance`. It should have `cluster-monitoring-view` cluster role. ~~~ # oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-monitoring-view-z grafana-serviceaccount ~~~- The bearer token for this service account is used to authenticate access to `thanos-querier` in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace. To fetch the token: ~~~ For RHOCP 4.10 and older: # oc serviceaccounts get-token grafana-serviceaccount For RHOCP 4.11 and new: # oc create token grafana-serviceaccount ~~~- After this, create the `Grafana Data Source` instance: Create datasource.yaml file as below: ~~~ apiVersion: integreatly.org/v1alpha1 kind: GrafanaDataSource metadata: name: prometheus-grafanadatasource namespace: openshift-user-workload-monitoring spec: datasources:- access: proxy editable: true isDefault: true jsonData: httpHeaderName1: 'Authorization' timeInterval: 5s tlsSkipVerify: true name: Prometheus secureJsonData: httpHeaderValue1: 'Bearer $TOKEN' type: prometheus url: https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9091/ name: prometheus-grafanadatasource.yaml ~~~ `Note:` Replace url value with actual hostname of `thanos-querier` svc. `$TOKEN` with `grafana-serviceaccount` token fetched earlier. Create Grafana Data Source instance using datasource.yaml file in `openshift-user-workload-monitoring`. ~~~ # oc project # oc create-f datasource.yaml # oc get grafanadatasource-n NAME AGE prometheus-grafanadatasource 5s ~~~ 6. **Logging into Grafana console as default admin privileges:**- Open URL of Grafana which is exposing custom grafana instance from openshift-user-workload-monitoring. ~~~ $ oc get route-n grafana-route grafana-route-$operator-installed-project-monitoring.apps.mycluster.sample.com grafana-service 3000 edge None ~~~- Sign IN using default admin credentials extracted via below command: ~~~ # oc extract secret/grafana-admin-credentials-n ~~~ 7. **Creating custom Grafana Dashboard:**- Create dashboard using **'+'** Create option: [image=[src="images/create-dashboard.png", title="Create dashboard option", alt="Create dashboard option", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]]- Then **'Add query'** option can be selected to add metrics query. Here, custom metrics: `version` is mentioned as per custom metrics exposed by sample app. [image=[src="images/grafana-7.png", title="Adding prometheus query while creating dashboard", alt="Adding prometheus query while creating dashboard", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]]- After adding query, dashboard can be saved or multiple queries can be added. In case of classifying multiple dashboards into one category, New Folder can be created which is used to save the newly created dashboards. Below is the sample custom dashboard screenshot where both custom metrics: `version` and default available metrics: `instance:node_memory_utilisation:ratio` are added in one dashboard. [image=[src="images/my_dashboard.png", title="Sample custom Grafana dashboard screenshot", alt="Sample custom Grafana dashboard screenshot", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]]
root_cause: Red Hat does not support direct access to Prometheus externally because heavy ad-hoc queries can overload and degrade the Prometheus instance.

title: RouterCertsDegraded with x509 certificate signed by unknown authority in OpenShift 4
issue: After replacing the default ingress certificate with a custom one, the `authentication` Cluster Operator becomes degraded with the error below: ``` RouterCertsDegraded: secret/v4-0-config-system-router-certs.spec.data[apps.example.com]-n openshift-authentication: certificate could not validate route hostname oauth-openshift.apps.example.com: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ``` ``` Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"Deployment", Namespace:"openshift-authentication-operator", Name:"authentication-operator", UID:" ", APIVersion:"apps/v1", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'OperatorStatusChanged' Status for clusteroperator/authentication changed: Degraded changed from False to True ("RouterCertsDegraded: secret/v4-0-config-system-router-certs.spec.data[apps.example.com]-n openshift-authentication: certificate could not validate route hostname oauth-openshift.apps.example.com: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority") [...] ```
resolution: Any of the certificate requirements are not met, and create a new certificate that meets the requirements is required. > **Note:** if it is not possible to create a new certificate at this moment (for example, if a different department is in charge of that), it is possible to temporarily revert to the default ingress certificate generated by the Ingress operator: [How to revert to the default ingress certificate after replacing it with a custom certificate in Red Hat OpenShift Container Plattform 4?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5496551). ###Use cert-manager Operator for Red Hat OpenShift Starting from [cert-manager Operator for Red Hat OpenShift 1.13.0](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/security/cert_manager_operator/cert-manager-operator-release-notes.html#cert-manager-operator-new-features-1-13-0) (supported in OpenShift 4.13 and newer), it is now possible to manage certificates for the Ingress Controller: [Creating certificates for the Ingress Controller](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/security/cert_manager_operator/cert-manager-creating-certificate.html#cert-manager-certificate-ingress_cert-manager-creating-certificate). ###Re-create the ingress certificate manually Follow the steps from [Replacing the default ingress certificate](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/security/certificates/replacing-default-ingress-certificate.html), and in the step "*Create a secret that contains the wildcard certificate chain and key*" check that:- The root CA needs to be a **trusted root CA**.- The certificate must include the `subjectAltName` extension showing `*.apps.[clustername].[domain]`.- The certificate must include the **wildcard certificate** and the **root CA** (with the entire chain if there are intermediates: [How to check the order of certificates for certificate chain](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6109821)): ~~~ wildcard certificate (*.apps.[cluster_name].[domain]) intermediate CA (if available) root CA ~~~- The certificate doesn't contain as end of line `Control+M` or other characters.- The `custom-ca` `configmap` in `openshift-config` namespace includes the root CA certificate used to sign the wildcard certificate.
root_cause: The root CA from the new custom certificate provided is not recognized by the system.

title: OpenShift service mesh operator istio basic not starting due to authentication errors
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - After following the installation guides for OpenShift Service Mesh operator, when going to a new project to setup an Istio Service Mesh Control Plane it keeps the `istio-ingressgateway` and `istio-egressgateway` pods pending- The `istiod` pod is having the following repeating error: ~~~ 2021-11-11T16:36:47.343764Z error ads Failed to authenticate client from 10.x.x.x:34572: Authenticator ClientCertAuthenticator: no verified chain is found; Authenticator KubeJWTAuthenticator: failed to validate the JWT from cluster "Kubernetes": the service account authentication returns an error: [invalid bearer token, token audiences ["https://example.0.myregion.example.com"] is invalid for the target audiences ["istio-ca"]] 2021-11-11T16:36:47.528181Z warn serverca Authentication failed for 10.x.x.x:33410: Authenticator ClientCertAuthenticator at index 0 got error: no verified chain is found. Authenticator KubeJWTAuthenticator at index 1 got error: failed to validate the JWT from cluster "Kubernetes": the service account authentication returns an error: [invalid bearer token, token audiences ["https://example.0.myregion.example.com"] is invalid for the target audiences ["istio-ca"]]. ~~~- `istio-ingressgateway`, `istio-egressgateway` have following error logs. ~~~ 2023-03-23T20:38:17.138427Z info xdsproxy connected to upstream XDS server: istiod-basic.istio-system.svc:15012 2023-03-23T20:38:17.142877Z warn xdsproxy upstream [1006] terminated with unexpected error rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = authentication failure 2023-03-23T20:38:17.143215Z warning envoy config StreamAggregatedResources gRPC config stream closed: 16, authentication failure 2023-03-23T20:38:19.842195Z error failed scraping envoy metrics: error scraping http://localhost:15090/stats/prometheus: Get "http://localhost:15090/stats/prometheus": dial tcp [::1]:15090: connect: connection refused ~~~- When checking the resources of that deployment ("istiod-basic" `replicaset`) it expects "cacerts" and "istio-kubeconfig" to exist, but they are not autogenerated when the `SMCP` resource is created.
resolution: There may be an issue with the use of first party tokens, or third party tokens may be required (for example, in ROSA clusters). Configure `istiod` to use `ThirdParty` in the `ServiceMeshControlPlane` as: ~~~ spec: security: identity: type: ThirdParty thirdParty: audience: istio-ca ~~~ Note, if audience is unspecified, `istio-ca` will be used by default. If the above does not work, another a workaround is to use Istio Service Mesh 2.0. To track a solution for Istio 2.1 please open a support case with Red Hat Support. For more information, refer to [Installing Service Mesh on ROSA](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html-single/service_mesh/index#ossm-install-rosa_ossm-create-smcp) the Service Mesh documentation.

title: How to change the 'v4InternalSubnet' of OVN-K using Assisted Installer?
issue: - How to modify the `OVN-Kubernetes` `v4InternalSubnet` during installation in case of `Assisted Installer` or `Agent Based Installer`?- How to change the `v4InternalSubnet` CIDR during installation using Assisted Installer as there are `IP addresses` that conflict with the default internal `OVN-Kubernetes` join network?- How to change the `v4InternalSubnet` CIDR during installation using Agent-Based Installer as there are `IP addresses` that conflict with the default internal `OVN-Kubernetes` join network?
resolution: - This can be achieved by adding the custom manifests in the `Include Custom Manifests` option on the `Assisted Installer` user interface.- For Agent-based installer, create an `openshift` subdirectory within the installation directory and add the custom manifests. Additional information can be referred from the Agent-Based installer [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/installing/installing_with_agent_based_installer/installing-with-agent-based-installer.html#installing-ocp-agent-opt-manifests_installing-with-agent-based-installer).- The yaml can be as follows: ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: Network metadata: name: cluster spec: defaultNetwork: type: OVNKubernetes ovnKubernetesConfig: v4InternalSubnet: 100.65.0.0/16----> Change the range as per requirement ~~~
root_cause: - The `v4InternalSubnet` can be changed during the installation. However, using `Assisted installer` limited options are exposed on the UI and hence the custom manifests option can be used. All the supported options are mentioned in following [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/rest_api/operator_apis/network-operator-openshift-io-v1.html).

title: Why does enabling session replication trigger cascading failures in JBoss EAP 7?
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - We have a JBoss EAP 7 cluster consisting of 2 instances(instance#1, instance#2) with HttpSession replication enabled.- When `instance#2` is extremely slowdown but it does not hang completely such as Full GC loop, requests for `instance#1` also fail with the following message despite `instance#1` being healthy. Subsequent requests with the same `JSESSIONID` will fail on `instance#1`. Requests for another `JSESSIONID` will not fail. The sticky session is configured appropriately in the reverse proxy. ~~~ 14:20:34,412 ERROR [io.undertow.request] (default task-2) UT005023: Exception handling request to /echo/session: org.infinispan.util.concurrent.TimeoutException: ISPN000299: Unable to acquire lock after 15 seconds for key SessionCreationMetaDataKey(e0g8ISqq1eDOgaMxMkXu_Zq081BT6Y5-pxbzUwuW) and requestor GlobalTransaction{id=9, addr=infra1, remote=false, xid=null, internalId=-1}. Lock is held by GlobalTransaction{id=8, addr=instance1, remote=false, xid=null, internalId=-1} ~~~- Why does cascading failure occur when HttpSession replication is enabled?
resolution: - Immediately restarting the unstable JBoss EAP instance is a workaround for this issue.- If session replication is enabled, there is fundamentally no way to avoid cascading failures.- `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` helps prevent cascading failures. If `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` is enabled, the java process will automatically shutdown when `java.lang.OutOfMemory` is thrown. The terminated cluster member is immediately removed from the cluster by detecting `FD_SOCK` in jgroups without waiting for a timeout of `FD_ALL`. `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` is disabled by default in zipped/RPM JBoss EAP, but it's enabled by default in container images of JBoss EAP.- In OpenShift environments, `livenessProbe` is helpful in automatically restarting unstable instances. If not in an OpenShift environment, it is necessary to work with monitoring tools to restart unstable instances automatically.
root_cause: - If `instance#2` hangs completely or the java process on `instance#2` is shutdown, the failure detection by the jgroups protocol `FD_ALL/FD_SOCK/VERIFY_SUSPECT` works correctly. `instance#2` is removed from the cluster and does not cause such cascading failure issue.- However, if `instance#2` does not hang completely but it's **extremely slow**, it causes cascading failure. This problem is caused that after flushing the HTTP/AJP response in the first request on `instance#1`, `instance#1` waits for completion of replication to `instance#2` and waits for `remote-timeout`(10000ms by default) of web cache-container in infinispan subsystem, with holding a lock for concurrent requests for the same session id. For more information about the lock, see [JBoss EAP 7 does not process requests for a session in parallel](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2776221).- Subsequent requests for the same session will wait until exceeding `lock-timeout` (15000ms by default) because the first request (still executing replication and waiting for another node until `remote-timeout`) still holds the lock for the session and subsequent requests cannot acquire the lock.

title: Mismatch between etcd member IPs and IPs configured for etcd in RHOCP 4
issue: Our `etcd` Pods on our Master Nodes are showing errors like the following: ~~~ 2021-01-08T09:14:07.556275311+00:00 stderr F W0108 09:14:07.556103 17 clientconn.go:1223] grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect to {https://10.140.108.21:2379 0}. Err:connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 10.140.108.21:2379: connect: no route to host". Reconnecting... [..] 2021-01-08T09:17:29.499949344+00:00 stderr F 2021-01-08 09:17:29.499921 I | embed: rejected connection from "10.140.108.25:39732" (error "tls: \"10.140.108.25\" does not match any of DNSNames [\"localhost\" \"test45.ocp.example.com\" \"10.140.108.22\"] (lookup test45.ocp.example.com on 10.140.108.23:53: no such host)", ServerName "", IPAddresses ["10.140.108.22"], DNSNames ["localhost" "test45.ocp.example.com" "10.140.108.22"]) ~~~

`etcdctl` shows different IP addresses than what is shown in the environment variables of the `etcd` Pods: ~~~ sh-4.4# etcdctl member list 26f85dbd1395423d, started, test45-n9lbn-master-1, https://10.140.108.23:2380, https://10.140.108.23:2379, false 4b8987a866eac5cb, started, test45-n9lbn-master-2, https://10.140.108.21:2380, https://10.140.108.21:2379, false c3f7b96cdd81341b, started, test45-n9lbn-master-0, https://10.140.108.22:2380, https://10.140.108.22:2379, false sh-4.4# echo $ALL_ETCD_ENDPOINTS https://10.140.108.25:2379,https://10.140.108.23:2379,https://10.140.108.21:2379 ~~~
`etcd-ensure-env-vars` exits with the following message: ~~~ [root@test45-n9lbn-master-0 ~]# crictl logs 066497679b291 Expected node IP to be 10.140.108.22 got 10.140.108.25 ~~~
resolution: * You must use DHCP for the network and ensure that the DHCP server is configured to provide persistent IP addresses to the cluster machines. * When using `dhcpd` as a DHCP server, you may need to set additional options, as described in the following Solution: [Solution 5704151](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5704151) * To restore the `etcd` cluster, ensure that the machine where the IP changed receives the previous IP (in the above example, the expected IP address is `10.140.108.22`). * If you are unable to restore the correct IP address, please [follow the documentation to replace this `etcd` member](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/backup_and_restore/control_plane_backup_and_restore/replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member.html).
root_cause: * The root cause for this issue is likely that the IP addresses for the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Control-plane nodes have changed.- The `etcd-ensure-env-vars` init container is in charge of verifying that the IP address of the Control-plane node did not change after installation.- The verification is done in the following way: ~~~ if [[\"${NODE_master0_IP}\"!= \"${NODE_IP}\" && \"${NODE_master0_IP}\"!= \"[${NODE_IP}]\"]]; then # echo the error message to stderr echo \"Expected node IP to be ${NODE_IP} got ${NODE_master0_IP}\" > &2 exit 1 fi ~~~- `NODE_IP` is taken from `status.podIP` while `NODE_master0_IP` is a variable configured at installation time.

title: OpenShift Web Hook MethodNotAllowed Error
issue: - While building the web hooks in the OpenShift environment, seeing "MethodNotAllowed" error. Below is the error message: ~~~ $ curl https://openshift.example.com:443/oapi/v1/namespaces/myproject/buildconfigs/mybuildconfig/webhooks/a300e8f539aefce2/generic {"kind": "Status", "apiVersion": "v1", "metadata": {}, "status": "Failure", "message": "the server does not allow this method on the requested resource", "reason": "MethodNotAllowed", "details": {}, "code": 405} ~~~ With the configuration: ~~~ spec: triggers:- type: Generic generic: secret: a300e8f539aefce2- type: GitHub github: secret: 5a1457f04e7990fe- type: ImageChange imageChange: lastTriggeredImageID: 'registry.access.redhat.com/jboss-eap-6/eap64-openshift:1.2'- type: ConfigChange ~~~
resolution: With the generic trigger, you will want to make sure you're using the POST method, as per the [GitHub issue](https://github.com/openshift/origin/issues/7614). ~~~ curl https://openshift.example.com:443/oapi/v1/namespaces/myproject/buildconfigs/mybc/webhooks/a300e8f539aefce2/generic-X POST ~~~
root_cause: This is the response given when another HTTP code, like GET, is used to try to trigger the build.

title: How to limit the number of project per user in OCP?
issue: - The [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.6/admin_guide/managing_projects.html#limit-projects-per-user) to limit the number of project per user is not working.
How the admission plugin works?
Where we have to declare the sample yaml presented in the documentation?
resolution: #### OpenShift 4 There is an RFE to build a operator for `projectrequestlimits` admission webhook. No estimated date to release until the moment of this writing. #### OpenShift 3 The below configuration has to be specified in `/etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml` file: ~~~ admissionConfig: pluginConfig: ProjectRequestLimit: configuration: apiVersion: v1 kind: ProjectRequestLimitConfig limits:- selector: level: admin- selector: level: advanced maxProjects: 10- maxProjects: 2 ~~~ * Specify the limits as per the requirement. * For selector **level=admin**, no `maxProjects` is specified. This means that users with this label will not have a maximum of project requests. * For selector **level=advanced**, a maximum number of 10 projects will be allowed. * For every other user, who doesn't have the above labels, they can create maximum 2 projects. * Refer to the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.6/admin_guide/manage_users.html#managing-users-managing-user-and-group-labels) to set the user and group labels.

title: How to configure Red Hat OpenStack Platform to use jumbo frames
issue: -How can one configure RHEL OSP instance networks to use jumbo frames.
resolution: ### Configuration ### The [networking guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-openstack-platform/8/networking-guide/networking-guide) and the [OSP installation guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-openstack-platform/8/paged/director-installation-and-usage/e5-configuring-jumbo-frames) contain useful information. Please consult these guides as well. Prepare the overcloud with OSP Director templates. #### OSP 10 neutron MTU #### In OSP 10, configure the following in `network-environment.yaml` ~~~ parameter_defaults: (...) NeutronGlobalPhysnetMtu: 9000 ~~~ ##### Configuring individual physical networks with different MTUs or changing the MTU for overlay networks ##### Refer to the upstream documentation [https://docs.openstack.org/newton/networking-guide/config-mtu.html](https://docs.openstack.org/newton/networking-guide/config-mtu.html), specifically case 2 and case 3. The `path_mtu` and `physical_network_mtus` can be set via puppet module `/etc/puppet/modules/neutron/manifests/plugins/ml2.pp`, hence in `network-environment.yaml` one can configure as an example: ~~~ (...) parameter_defaults: (...) controllerExtraConfig: neutron::plugins::ml2::path_mtu: 5000 neutron::plugins::ml2::physical_network_mtus: ["provider2:4000", "provider3:1500"] NovaComputeExtraConfig: neutron::plugins::ml2::path_mtu: 5000 neutron::plugins::ml2::physical_network_mtus: ["provider2:4000", "provider3:1500"] (...) ~~~ An explanation of the different parameters can be found in the comments in the configuration files. global_physnet_mtu- global value to set MTU. For VLAN networks, no overhead calculation takes place. For VXLANs, 50 bytes of overhead are calculated. ~~~ # MTU of the underlying physical network. Neutron uses this value to calculate # MTU for all virtual network components. For flat and VLAN networks, neutron # uses this value without modification. For overlay networks such as VXLAN, # neutron automatically subtracts the overlay protocol overhead from this # value. Defaults to 1500, the standard value for Ethernet. (integer value) # Deprecated group/name- [ml2]/segment_mtu #global_physnet_mtu = 1500 global_physnet_mtu=9000 ~~~ `path_mtu` is used to set the MTU for tunnel networks. This value includes tunnel overhead, hence it's the value of the tunnel overhead + the payload. This allows to adjust to path MTU and overhead for tunnels specifically. Sets the MTU for all networks of type VXLAN / geneve / etc.; neutron subtracts another 50 bytes in the case of VXLAN tunnels to account for overhead: ~~~ # Maximum size of an IP packet (MTU) that can traverse the underlying physical # network infrastructure without fragmentation when using an overlay/tunnel # protocol. This option allows specifying a physical network MTU value that # differs from the default global_physnet_mtu value. (integer value) #path_mtu = 0 path_mtu = 5555 ~~~ `physical_network_mtus` is used to set the MTU of a particular VLAN network. VLAN networks do not subtract any overhead, hence the exact same value is used: ~~~ # A list of mappings of physical networks to MTU values. The format of the # mapping is:. This mapping allows specifying a physical # network MTU value that differs from the default global_physnet_mtu value. # (list value) physical_network_mtus = datacentre:3333 ~~~ #### OSP 8 neutron MTU #### In OSP 8 and 9, configure the following in `network-environment.yaml` ~~~ parameter_defaults: (...) NeutronTenantMtu: 9000 # force the advertisement of MTU 9000 to instances # this value may need adjustment depending on the tunnel type and tunnel overhead NeutronDnsmasqOptions: 'dhcp-option-force=26,9000' # note that this value may or may not be needed # look at the OSP documentation to find out more about the path_mtu parameter # and if it is needed in your environment controllerExtraConfig: neutron::plugins::ml2::path_mtu: 9000 NovaComputeExtraConfig: neutron::plugins::ml2::path_mtu: 9000 ~~~ #### OSP 9 neutron MTU #### In OSP 8 and 9, configure the following in `network-environment.yaml` ~~~ parameter_defaults: (...) NeutronTenantMtu: 9000 controllerExtraConfig: neutron::plugins::ml2::path_mtu: 9000 neutron::global_physnet_mtu: 9000 NovaComputeExtraConfig: neutron::plugins::ml2::path_mtu: 9000 neutron::global_physnet_mtu: 9000 ~~~ #### NIC templates #### Configure network configuration files according to the official guide [OSP 7 Jumbo Frames](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-US/Red_Hat_Enterprise_Linux_OpenStack_Platform/7/html/Director_Installation_and_Usage/sect-Configuring_Jumbo_Frames.html) [OSP 8 Jumbo Frames](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-openstack-platform/8/paged/director-installation-and-usage/e5-configuring-jumbo-frames) **Note:** It is recommended that the Provisioning interface, External interface, and any floating IP interfaces be left at the default MTU of 1500. Traffic which crosses into a network managed by another entity may be limited to an MTU of 1500, so connectivity problems can occur if jumbo frames are used on these networks. E.g., the following are examples for controller and compute NIC configuration ~~~ [stack@undercloud-6 templates]$ cat nic-configs/controller.yaml heat_template_version: 2015-04-30 description: > Software Config to drive os-net-config to configure VLANs for the controller role. parameters: ControlPlaneIp: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the ctlplane network type: string ExternalIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the external network type: string InternalApiIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the internal API network type: string StorageIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the storage network type: string StorageMgmtIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the storage mgmt network type: string TenantIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the tenant network type: string ManagementIpSubnet: # Only populated when including environments/network-management.yaml default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the management network type: string ExternalNetworkVlanID: default: 10 description: Vlan ID for the external network traffic. type: number InternalApiNetworkVlanID: default: 20 description: Vlan ID for the internal_api network traffic. type: number StorageNetworkVlanID: default: 30 description: Vlan ID for the storage network traffic. type: number StorageMgmtNetworkVlanID: default: 40 description: Vlan ID for the storage mgmt network traffic. type: number TenantNetworkVlanID: default: 50 description: Vlan ID for the tenant network traffic. type: number ManagementNetworkVlanID: default: 60 description: Vlan ID for the management network traffic. type: number ExternalInterfaceDefaultRoute: default: '10.0.0.1' description: default route for the external network type: string ControlPlaneSubnetCidr: # Override this via parameter_defaults default: '24' description: The subnet CIDR of the control plane network. type: string DnsServers: # Override this via parameter_defaults default: [] description: A list of DNS servers (2 max for some implementations) that will be added to resolv.conf. type: comma_delimited_list EC2MetadataIp: # Override this via parameter_defaults description: The IP address of the EC2 metadata server. type: string resources: OsNetConfigImpl: type: OS::Heat::StructuredConfig properties: group: os-apply-config config: os_net_config: network_config:- type: interface # physical eth0, provioning network name: nic1 use_dhcp: false dns_servers: {get_param: DnsServers} addresses:- ip_netmask: list_join:- '/'-- {get_param: ControlPlaneIp}- {get_param: ControlPlaneSubnetCidr} routes:- ip_netmask: 169.254.169.254/32 next_hop: {get_param: EC2MetadataIp}- type: ovs_bridge name: {get_input: bridge_name} use_dhcp: false mtu: 9000 members:- type: interface name: nic2 mtu: 9000 # force the MAC address of the bridge to this interface primary: true- type: vlan vlan_id: {get_param: ExternalNetworkVlanID} addresses:- ip_netmask: {get_param: ExternalIpSubnet} routes:- default: true next_hop: {get_param: ExternalInterfaceDefaultRoute}- type: vlan mtu: 9000 vlan_id: {get_param: InternalApiNetworkVlanID} addresses:- ip_netmask: {get_param: InternalApiIpSubnet}- type: vlan mtu: 9000 vlan_id: {get_param: StorageNetworkVlanID} addresses:- ip_netmask: {get_param: StorageIpSubnet}- type: vlan mtu: 9000 vlan_id: {get_param: StorageMgmtNetworkVlanID} addresses:- ip_netmask: {get_param: StorageMgmtIpSubnet}- type: vlan mtu: 9000 vlan_id: {get_param: TenantNetworkVlanID} addresses:- ip_netmask: {get_param: TenantIpSubnet} #- # Uncomment when including environments/network-management.yaml # type: vlan # vlan_id: {get_param: ManagementNetworkVlanID} # addresses: #- # ip_netmask: {get_param: ManagementIpSubnet} outputs: OS::stack_id: description: The OsNetConfigImpl resource. value: {get_resource: OsNetConfigImpl} ~~~ ~~~ [stack@undercloud-6 nic-configs]$ cat compute.yaml heat_template_version: 2015-04-30 description: > Software Config to drive os-net-config to configure VLANs for the compute role. parameters: ControlPlaneIp: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the ctlplane network type: string ExternalIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the external network type: string InternalApiIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the internal API network type: string StorageIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the storage network type: string StorageMgmtIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the storage mgmt network type: string TenantIpSubnet: default: '' description: IP address/subnet on the tenant network type: string ManagementIpSubnet: # title: Why the Aggregated Node Utilization report on container dashboard shows no data available?
issue: - Missing Aggregated Node Utilization metrics on container's overview dashboard.- The Overview Dashboard is not showing Node's utilization data.
resolution: There needs to be at least 30 days of data for some of dashboard reports (Aggregated Node Utilization) to be generated.
root_cause: There is no metrics available for more than 30 days due to which Aggregated Node Utilization report is blank.
