title: How Can I Customize the Look of Hawtio-Swagger-UI?
issue: The current version of swagger-ui does not seem to inherit the branding / customization capabilities of Hawtio. Is there a way to accomplish customization of swagger-ui in the current Fuse offering?
resolution: Although the Hawtio-Swagger-UI is not configured as a plugin, it is possible to customize the look and feel of the app with a little effort. Customization can be added by means of creating a WAR Overlay project and deploying the customized version alongside the existing swagger-ui, or by replacing the existing swagger-ui with the customized version.- Create a WAR overlay project with hawtio-swagger-ui as a dependency (attaching example). This will pull the existing resources included in hawtio-swagger-ui into the overlay project without having to manually copy all of the resources. Note that in the example project POM, I have specified an alternate contextual URI for deployment.- Include the customized image, css and other resources directly in the overlay project (in the example, I have copied web.xml, index.html, screen.css, and reset.css into the new project and made just a few small color changes in the screen.css and a title change in index.html)- (Recommended) Create a separate feature description for your customized Swagger UI (included in example- see features.xml file in src/main/resources) **STAND-ALONE KARAF**- (For stand-alone karaf environments) Add the feature URL to the container. Using the example WAR, the command would be: ~~~ > features:addurl mvn:com.redhat.example/swagger-ui-custom/1.0.0/xml/features ~~~- (For stand-alone karaf environment) Add the feature to the container. Using the example WAR, the command would be: ~~~ > features:install fabric-hawtio-swagger-custom ~~~ **FABRIC8 ENVIRONMENT**- (Recommended for fabric environment) After building the overlay war, create a profile and add the feature URL for the overlay project to the profile. Using the example, the command would be something like: ~~~ > fabric:profile-create swagger-ui-custom > fabric:profile-edit--repository mvn:com.redhat.example/swagger-ui-custom/1.0.0/xml/features swagger-ui-custom 1.0 ~~~- Add the feature to the profile. Using the example WAR, the command would look something like: ~~~ > fabric:profile-edit--features fabric-hawtio-swagger-custom swagger-ui-custom 1.0 ~~~- Assign the profile to a container. Using the example WAR, the command would look something like: ~~~ > fabric:container-add-profile root swagger-ui-custom ~~~ You should now be able to navigate to the customized UI by going to: http://localhost:8181/hawtio-swagger-custom/index.html (substitute host and port as needed). The above instructions will not replace the stock swagger UI application, but will run the customized version at an alternate contextual path (assuming the stock feature is loaded. In karaf stand-alone, the stock swagger-ui will not be loaded unless added or included elsewhere as a dependency). In a fabric environment, the custom UI will run alongside the stock UI. This option will shield your customizations from changes to the container when the container is patched and requires no changes to core files. You can update the overlay project dependency to take advantage of updated swagger-ui features by updating the dependency to the latest version and updating the changed resource files, as needed. If you want to replace the existing swagger-ui (Fabric environments), you may do so by editing the configuration for the hawtio profile to replace the stock hawtio-swagger feature with your custom version (**Note you may need to reaccomplish this each time the system is patched**). Example: ~~~ > profile-edit--resource io.fabric8.agent.properties hawtio 1.0 ~~~ ~~~ Profile:hawtio 1.0 L:1 C:1 # # Copyright 2005-2014 Red Hat, Inc. # # Red Hat licenses this file to you under the Apache License, version # 2.0 (the "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance # with the License. You may obtain a copy of the License at # # http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 # # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or # implied. See the License for the specific language governing # permissions and limitations under the License. # feature.war=war feature.fabric-redirect=fabric-redirect feature.fabric-hawtio=fabric-hawtio feature.hawtio-redhat-fuse-branding=hawtio-redhat-fuse-branding feature.hawtio-redhat-amq-branding=hawtio-redhat-amq-branding feature.fabric-hawtio-swagger=fabric-hawtio-swagger feature.swagger=swagger repository.hawtio=mvn\:io.hawt/hawtio-karaf/${version:hawtio}/xml/features attribute.parents=karaf bundle.pax-url-war=mvn:org.ops4j.pax.url/pax-url-war/2.4.7 ~~~ Change the configuration above to look something like: ~~~ Profile:hawtio 1.0* L:24 C:59 # # Copyright 2005-2014 Red Hat, Inc. # # Red Hat licenses this file to you under the Apache License, version # 2.0 (the "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance # with the License. You may obtain a copy of the License at # # http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 # # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or # implied. See the License for the specific language governing # permissions and limitations under the License. # feature.war=war feature.fabric-redirect=fabric-redirect feature.fabric-hawtio=fabric-hawtio feature.hawtio-redhat-fuse-branding=hawtio-redhat-fuse-branding feature.hawtio-redhat-amq-branding=hawtio-redhat-amq-branding feature.fabric-hawtio-swagger-custom=fabric-hawtio-swagger-custom feature.swagger=swagger repository.hawtio=mvn\:io.hawt/hawtio-karaf/${version:hawtio}/xml/features repository.hawtio-custom=mvn\:com.redhat.example/swagger-ui-custom/1.0.0/xml/features attribute.parents=karaf bundle.pax-url-war=mvn:org.ops4j.pax.url/pax-url-war/2.4.7 ~~~ Note that the custom feature URL for the customized WAR project has been added and the feature fabric-hawtio-swagger has been replaced with feature-fabric-hawtio-swagger-custom. Now only the custom version is loaded by the fabric hawtio profile. **Note: you may need to reaccomplish the above profile edit if a patch is applied to the environment**. Save the updated configuration using [Ctrl-Shift-S] and exit using [Ctrl-Shift-X]. The original swagger-ui is now replaced by the customized version.

title: Setup namespace specific entries in the OpenShift global pull secret
issue: - When trying to deploy an operator from a private image registry, is there a way to set a pull secret for a specific image?
resolution: - To set a pull secret for a specific image, it's possible to setup namespace specific entries in the global pull secret.- A possible way to accomplish this is to extract the current global pull secret and add the credentials for the needed additional registries: 1. `$ oc extract secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--to=-|jq '.auths|keys' > temp_dockerconfigjson` 2. `$ sed-i '/"registry.redhat.io"/a \ \ "mirror.disconnected.example.com/operators" \n \ "mirror.disconnected.example.com/catalogsources"' temp_dockerconfigjson` 3. `$ oc set data secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--from-file=.dockerconfigjson=temp_dockerconfigjson`
root_cause: - The `ImageContentSourcePolicy` object will make sure the operator images are pulled from the appropriate mirrored registry using the specific credentials.

title: Pods cannot access a shared volume with permission denied error in OpenShift 4
issue: - When running different pods that share a `PVC` one of the pods gets permission denied errors on that volume.- When running pods that share a `PVC` one of the pods set ups a different SELinux context for the files on that volume.- When running differents pods with added capabilities and they share a `PV` volume one of the pods loses access to the volume.
resolution: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform does modify the SELinux context of `Pods`. This behavior depends on the `SCC` configured. With a `SCC` set on `restricted` (or any `SCC ` with `seLinuxContext: type: MustRunAs`), a `Pod` gets its SELinux context from a namespace annotation. With a `SCC` set on `privileged`(or any `SCC` with `seLinuxContext: type: RunAsAny`), OpenShift Container Platform does not modify the SELinux context assigned and a random SELinux context is assigned when the `pod` does not request a specific one. If using the `privileged` SCC you can avoid this behaviour by manual assignation of the SELinux context in the configuration file: ~~~ [...] securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: "s0:cXX,cYY" [...] ~~~ The recommendation is to create a new `Security Context Constraints` to allow the capabilities needed but leave the `seLinuxContext` with type `MustRunAs` to get the SELinux context propagated from `Pods` namespace.
root_cause: Red Hat OpenShift Container Plaftform does modify the SELinux context of `Pods`. This behaviour depends on the `SCC` configured. With a `SCC` set on `restricted` (or any `SCC ` with `seLinuxContext: type: MustRunAs`), a `Pod` gets its SELinux context from a namespace annotation. With a `SCC` set on `privileged`(or any `SCC` with `seLinuxContext: type: RunAsAny`), OpenShift Container Platform does not modify the SELinux context is assigned when a `pod` does not require any.

title: How to use the oc-mirror plug-in to mirror operators?
issue: How to use `oc-mirror` plug-in to mirror operators.
How to find available operators using `oc-mirror`.
resolution: 1. Installing the [oc-mirror plug-in](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#installation-oc-mirror-installing-plugin_installing-mirroring-disconnected). ~~~ $ curl-O https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/stable/oc-mirror.tar.gz $ tar-xvf oc-mirror.tar.gz $ chmod +x./oc-mirror $ sudo mv./oc-mirror /usr/local/bin/ ~~~ 2. Disabling the default `OperatorHub` sources. ~~~ $ oc patch OperatorHub cluster--type json \-p '[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/disableAllDefaultSources", "value": true}]' ~~~ 3. [Get operator information](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/how-oc-mirror-will-help-you-reduce-container-management-complexity). ~~~ a. Login OperatorHub catalogs $ podman login registry.redhat.io b. Find the available catalogs for the target version. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalogs--version=4.11 Available OpenShift OperatorHub catalogs: OpenShift 4.11: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11 registry.redhat.io/redhat/certified-operator-index:v4.11 registry.redhat.io/redhat/community-operator-index:v4.11 registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-marketplace-index:v4.11 c. Find the available packages within the selected catalog. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11 > package.out $ cat package.out NAME DISPLAY NAME DEFAULT CHANNEL 3scale-operator Red Hat Integration- 3scale- Managed Application Services threescale-mas [···] d. Find channels for the selected package. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11--package=cluster-logging NAME DISPLAY NAME DEFAULT CHANNEL cluster-logging Red Hat OpenShift Logging stable PACKAGE CHANNEL HEAD cluster-logging stable cluster-logging.5.5.5 cluster-logging stable-5.3 cluster-logging.5.3.9 cluster-logging stable-5.4 cluster-logging.5.4.9 cluster-logging stable-5.5 cluster-logging.5.5.5 or $ for i in cluster-logging elasticsearch-operator; do oc-mirror list operators-- catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11--package=$i; done e. Find package versions within the selected channel. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11-- package=elasticsearch-operator--channel=stable-5.5 VERSIONS 5.5.5 ~~~ 4. [Configuring credentials](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#installation-adding-registry-pull-secret_installing-mirroring-disconnected) that allow images to be mirrored. ~~~ a. Download pull-secret(https://console.redhat.com/openshift/install/pull-secret). b. Add local Image Registry credentials to the pull-secret. $ MIRROR_REGISTRY=docker.registry.example.net:5000 $ podman login ${MIRROR_REGISTRY} $ podman login--authfile /root/pull-secret ${MIRROR_REGISTRY} c. Save the file either as ~/.docker/config.json or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json. $ cat /root/pull-secret | jq. > ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json $ cat ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json {"auths": {"cloud.openshift.com": {"auth": "xxxxxx...", "email": "you@example.com"}, "docker.registry.example.net:5000": {"auth": "xxxxxx" [···] ~~~ 5. Creating the [imageset configuration](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#oc-mirror-imageset-config-params_installing-mirroring-disconnected). **Note:** When running the `oc-mirror` plugin again, images gets [pruned](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#oc-mirror-updating-registry-about_installing-mirroring-disconnected) automatically from the target mirror registry if they are no longer included in the latest `imageset` that was generated and mirrored. ~~~ $ cat > imageset-config.yaml < < EOF apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL: ${MIRROR_REGISTRY}/mirror/metadata # <-- Do not delete or modify metadata generated by the oc-mirror plugin, use the same storage backend every time run the oc-mirror plugin for the same mirror registry. skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11 # <-- Set the Operator catalog packages:- name: cluster-logging # <-- Operator name channels: # <-- Specify channel and version- name: stable # <-- Default Channel- name: stable-5.5 # <-- Target Channel- If the expected Channel is different from the Default Channel, need to set the Target Channel after setting the Default Channel minVersion: '5.5.5' # <-- If the first field of the set value is a number, need to add ' '. maxVersion: '5.5.5'- name: elasticsearch-operator channels:- name: stable- name: stable-5.5 minVersion: '5.5.5' maxVersion: '5.5.5'- name: cincinnati-operator channels:- name: v1 minVersion: v5.0.0 maxVersion: v5.0.0- name: kubernetes-nmstate-operator channels:- name: stable- name: '4.11' minVersion: '4.11.0-202212070335' maxVersion: '4.11.0-202212070335' EOF ~~~ 6. [Mirroring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#mirroring-image-set-partial) an imageset to a mirror registry. ~~~ $ oc mirror--config=./imageset-config.yaml \ docker://${MIRROR_REGISTRY}--dest-skip-tls ··· info: Mirroring completed in 1m57.76s (40.22MB/s) Rendering catalog image "docker.registry.example.net:5000/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11" with file-based catalog Writing image mapping to oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047/mapping.txt Writing CatalogSource manifests to oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047 Writing ICSP manifests to oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047 # <-- This path is used in subsequent steps to create icsp and catalogsource ~~~ 7. Create `imageContentSourcePolicy` and `catalogsource`. ~~~ $ ls oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047 catalogSource-redhat-operator-index.yaml charts imageContentSourcePolicy.yaml mapping.txt release-signatures $ oc create-f imageContentSourcePolicy.yaml imagecontentsourcepolicy.operator.openshift.io/operator-0 created $ oc create-f catalogSource-redhat-operator-index.yaml catalogsource.operators.coreos.com/redhat-operator-index create ~~~ 8. Verify that the operator download is complete. ~~~ $ oc get catalogsource-n openshift-marketplace NAME DISPLAY TYPE PUBLISHER AGE redhat-operator-index grpc 13s $ oc get packagemanifest-n openshift-marketplace NAME CATALOG AGE cluster-logging 33s cincinnati-operator 33s elasticsearch-operator 33s kubernetes-nmstate-operator 33s ~~~ * If it is a completely disconnected environment, `storageConfig.local.path` needs to be set instead of `storageConfig.registry.imageURL` to [mirror the imageset to disk with the metadata, then mirror the imageset file on disk to a mirror](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#mirroring-image-set-full). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL: ${MIRROR_REGISTRY}/mirror/metadata ***Change it to*** apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: local: path: /home/user/metadata ~~~ **Note:** Do not delete or modify metadata generated by the `oc-mirror` plugin, use the same storage backend every time run the `oc-mirror` plugin for the same mirror registry.

title: How to configure limits for Kiali in Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh?
issue: - How to define limits for `Kiali` pod in Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh?- The configuration gets overridden by LimitRanges if the limits are defined in the ServiceMeshControlPlane resource.
resolution: - This is a workaround to update the Kiali limits by editing the Kiali custom resource: ~~~ $ oc edit kiali kiali-n [control-plane-name] ~~~- Add the following in the `spec.deployment.resources` section of *Kiali*'s CR. ~~~ spec: deployment: resources: limits: cpu: 250m memory: 450Mi ~~~- After making changes save out the configuration by entering `:wq` and wait for new `Kiali` deployment to rollout.
root_cause: - Currently the ServiceMeshControlPlane is unable to define **kiali.resources* for the `Kiali` resources.

title: Vector collector pods crash when kubernetes.label in structuredTypeKey contains "-"
issue: - After configuring kubernetes.label in `structuredTypeKey` in `ClusterLogForwarder`, `collector` pods started to crash: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-logging-l component=collector NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE collector-2pwwq 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 (6s ago) 8s collector-86xjq 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 (6s ago) 8s collector-9nx48 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 (6s ago) 8s collector-f62zl 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 (6s ago) 8s collector-mrw9h 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 (6s ago) 8s collector-vfxrw 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1 (6s ago) 8s ~~~- `Collector` pods are streaming below logs: ~~~ $ oc logs-c collector collector-vfxrw-n openshift-logging Creating the directory used for persisting Vector state /var/lib/vector Starting Vector process... 2024-05-10T16:52:39.358368Z WARN vector::config::loading: Transform "route_container_logs._unmatched" has no consumers 2024-05-10T16:52:39.489625Z ERROR vector::topology: Configuration error. error=Transform "default_add_es_index": error[E701]: call to undefined variable ┌─:17:34 │ 17│ val =.kubernetes.labels.region-name │ ^^^^^^ │ │ │ undefined variable │ did you mean "true"? │ = see language documentation at https://vrl.dev = try your code in the VRL REPL, learn more at https://vrl.dev/examples ~~~
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [LOG-5524](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-5524) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.9.4 through errata [RHSA-2024:4333](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4333). If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. ### Workaround As of now, there is no workaround available when `vector` collector is used. However, `fluentd` collector can be configured till the bug fix is released. ~~~ $ oc edit clusterlogging-n------ Output Omitted------ spec: managementState: Managed collection: type: vector < < < <===== Replace "vector" with "fluentd"------ Output Omitted------ ~~~
root_cause: Workloads that included labels with dashes would cause the collector to error while it was normalizing log entries as not used a correct syntax when the Logging Operator was generating the configuration for Vector.

title: What considerations we need to take when we migrate NetApp storage under ACM/MCE ?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - We need to migrate storage to a new Netapp machine, and for this we need guidance how to perform this operator (to move to a new Netapp PVCS)- that not cause data corruption or other problems in MCE / ACM.
resolution: For assisted you have to scale both assisted-service and assisted-image-service to 0. For this you will also need to scale down to zero the infrastructure-operator, since otherwise it would push the replicas back up) For the infrastructure-operator would also probably ensured by MCE that it is running, so you would also scale MCE down. We are still working on how this could be done. About deleting PVCs.: Strongly advised to do not delete PVCs, we can't be ensure that the data will not loose and it can be recovered except some cases. Whether you can retain and reuse the data on a PV will depend on your PV reclaim policy as well as your storage provider. Assuming the PV reclaim policy is set to "Retain" and your volume plugin supports this (as described in https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.15/html/storage/understanding-persistent-storage#reclaiming_understanding-persistent-storage) the data *shouldn't* be lost. Then you'd have to create the PVC specs in the AgentServiceConfig with a label selector to ensure they are bound to the PV you want. Even then we can't guarantee that your storage plugin won't wipe a PV when it's bound or something so I'd really try to avoid removing PVCs. In general scaling down deployment in order to perform migration is at article: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5794841 Other way to tackle this (unsupported way) is to set the operator to unmanaged state by CVO (cluster version operator). It could be MCE operator specific requirements and we don't recommend this method. A generic way is described at https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6727721 Some more details which need to be considered when scaling deployments. The ACM and MCE operator would scale back the deployments normally, so to prevent this they would need to be paused. The replicas are controlled by the installer because it owns an availability mode (high or basic) that you can set in the operator. The procedure for both operators is basically the same, you have to tell the operator to "pause" its reconciles.: For MCE: ~~~ oc annotate mce multiclusterengine pause="true" ~~~ For ACM: ~~~ oc annotate-n mch multiclusterhub mch-pause="true" ~~~ After the procedure is completed, remember to remove these annotations to allow the operators to continue their normal work. Note: When these 2 operators are paused, not all deployments can be modified right away. For example, you cannot edit the search-xyz deployment replicas until you first scale down the search operator replicas. Be aware of this since search deployments are one of the items you are looking into for this PVC migration.

title: OpenSSL backend is unavailable error in oc commands in OpenShift 4 with FIPS enabled
issue: When a cluster is installed with FIPS enabled, the `oc` command errors when used on a RHEL 8 or 9 system with FIPS enabled. The error is: ~~~ FIPS mode is enabled, but the required OpenSSL backend is unavailable ~~~
resolution: This is a known issue and has been reported to Red Hat engineering and tracked in the following bugs: Target Minor Release | Bug | Fixed Version | Errata--- |--- 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-23386](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-23386)|**4.16.0**|[RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041) 4.15 | [OCPBUGS-28204](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-28204)|WIP|WIP ### Workaround Until the fix for 4.15 is available, it should be possible to use the `oc` binary from 4.16 to connect to the cluster. Please, refer to [the `oc` binary versioning policy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/cli_reference/openshift_cli/usage-oc-kubectl.html#the-oc-binary) for additional information about the compatibility between versions.
root_cause: The `oc` binary provided is checking for an older OpenSSL version, which was part of RHEL 8. ~~~ rpm-qf /lib64/libcrypto.so.3 openssl-libs-3.0.7-24.el9.x86_64 <--- RHEL9 rpm-qf /usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1 openssl-libs-1.1.1k-9.el8_6.x86_64 <--- RHEL8 ~~~

title: How to configure Quarkus with Openshift secrets/configmap
issue: How to integrate some sensitive data in Openshift secret with a service developed in quarkus?
resolution: The configuration is described in the Quarkus [documentation](https://quarkus.io/guides/deploying-to-openshift#environment-variables-from-secret "documentation").- Add the key/value in the Secret and in the `resources/application.properties` file, add: ~~~ quarkus.openshift.env.secrets=my-secret quarkus.openshift.env.mapping.foo.from-secret=my-secret quarkus.openshift.env.mapping.foo.with-key=keyName ~~~- OR add an `application.properties` file to Secret: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: my-secret stringData: application.properties: | hello.message=Hello from Secret! ~~~ and add to `resources/application.properties`: ~~~ quarkus.openshift.app-secret=my-secret ~~~
root_cause: From the kubernetes-config extension, Quarkus allows the users Kubernetes resources and `quarkus.openshift.env.*` can be used to set attributes: ~~~ quarkus.openshift.env.configmaps=config-map quarkus.openshift.env.secrets=secret quarkus.openshift.env.mapping.KAFKA_SSL_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD.from-secret=light-es-cluster-ca-cert ~~~ This is possible given the project as the below extension, which is [Tech Preview](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6643671): ~~~ io.quarkus quarkus-kubernetes io.quarkus quarkus-kubernetes-config ~~~ The extension will create the below sections on the deployment yaml ~~~ ### for secret: envFrom:- secretRef: name: my-secret optional: false ### for configmap: envFrom:- configMapRef: name: my-config-map optional: false ~~~ Although the [Quarkus documentation](https://quarkus.io/guides/kubernetes-config) brings a possibility to disable/enable RBAC in Kubernetes, OCP 4.x comes with RBAC by default and cannot be disabled. Meaning it is not an optional feature. However, permissions don't play a role on accessing the configmap/secres when the volume is section present on the pod definition: deployment/deploymetconfig.yaml. ### Note about permissions For binary deployment (quarkus cli for example) user can add the property `quarkus.kubernetes-config.secrets.enabled=true` to get a secret. The property adds the role view-secrets and the role binding openshift-quickstart-view-secrets. However it won't allow to list secrets: ~~~ ### get does work $ oc get secret--as system:serviceaccount:anamespace:openshift-quickstart test-config-n anamespace NAME TYPE DATA AGE test-config Opaque 1 29m ### list does not works $ oc get secret--as system:serviceaccount:anamespace:openshift-quickstart-n anamespace Error from server (Forbidden): secrets is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:anamespace:openshift-quickstart" cannot list resource "secrets" in API group "" in the namespace "anamespace" ~~~

title: The holderIdentity is not visible after RHOCP upgrade
issue: - RHOCP upgraded from version 4.12 to 4.13 after which `holderIdentity` is not visible in the configmap.- The `holderIdentity` is not present for `kube-scheduler` and `ovn-kubernetes-master` configmap object in respective namespaces.
resolution: `Holder/leader` identity can be checked through the lease object in RHOCP 4.x version. $ oc get lease kube-scheduler-n openshift-kube-scheduler-o yaml apiVersion: coordination.k8s.io/v1 kind: Lease metadata: creationTimestamp: "2023-12-08T13:29:16Z" name: kube-scheduler namespace: openshift-kube-scheduler resourceVersion: "36920281" uid: a2a15844-6aca-40fa-xxx-15a0fe802fae spec: acquireTime: "2024-01-30T12:20:18.237808Z" holderIdentity: masterx.ocp4.xxxxx.com leaseDurationSeconds: 137 leaseTransitions: 19 renewTime: "2024-02-05T05:40:17.953161Z" $ oc get lease ovn-kubernetes-master-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-o yaml apiVersion: coordination.k8s.io/v1 kind: Lease metadata: creationTimestamp: "2023-12-08T17:46:53Z" name: ovn-kubernetes-master namespace: openshift-ovn-kubernetes resourceVersion: "36920115" uid: faa82d9d-9bf9-49c8-xxxx-b010b618cf04 spec: acquireTime: "2024-02-02T12:13:54.796401Z" holderIdentity: masterx.ocp4.xxxxx.com leaseDurationSeconds: 60 leaseTransitions: 88 renewTime: "2024-02-05T05:40:07.842863Z"

title: Proxied worker node fails to reach the Hosted Control Plane API on RHOCP 4
issue: - Worker nodes are unable to reach a Hosted Control Plane's API when a cluster-wide http `proxy` is configured.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this issue and it is being tracked in the following bugs: Target Minor Release | Bug | Fixed Version | Errata--- |--- 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-33237](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-33237)|**4.16.0**|[RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041) 4.15 | [OCPBUGS-33510](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-33510)|**4.15.16**|[RHBA-2024:3488](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:3488) 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-36518](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-36518)|**4.14.33**|[RHSA-2024:4479](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4479)

title: How to use same EgressIP for multiple namespaces in OpenShift 4?

title: How to SSH into nodes in OpenShift 4?
issue: - Where to find the SSH private key to access the OpenShift 4 nodes?- How to SSH into control plane and compute nodes in OpenShift 4 clusters?
resolution: Whenever possible, access to nodes without using SSH, by spawning a debug pod directly from the `oc` command line: ~~~ $ oc debug node/[node_name] ~~~ > **Important note:** By design, OpenShift 4 clusters are immutable and rely on [Operators](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/operators/understanding/olm-what-operators-are.html) to apply cluster changes. In turn, this means that accessing the underlying nodes directly by SSH is not the recommended procedure. Additionally, the nodes will be tainted as accessed. ####Workaround When it is not possible to access the nodes with `oc debug node` command, it is possible to leverage the `ssh` protocol for the same:- Generally, the "SSH keys (Public/Private)" are generated during the cluster installation.- The "Public Key" is passed inside the `install-config.yaml` manifest.- After successful cluster installation, the "Public key" is copied at path `$/home/core/.ssh/authorized_keys` or `/home/core/.ssh/authorized_keys.d` location across the nodes.- It is possible to use the generated "SSH Private key" to access the nodes as `core` user by running below command: ~~~ $ ssh-i /path/to/privatekey core@[master-hostname] $ ssh-i /path/to/privatekey core@[worker-hostname] ~~~
root_cause: By design, OpenShift 4 clusters are immutable and rely on [Operators](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/operators/understanding/olm-what-operators-are.html) to apply cluster changes. In turn, this means that accessing the underlying nodes directly by SSH is not the recommended procedure. Additionally, the nodes will be tainted as accessed.

title: How to set log_level in LokiStack in RHOCP 4
issue: Is it possible to set the `log_level` to `debug` in LokiStack?
How can the `log_level` being changed in Loki?
resolution: The next steps are for doing troubleshooting and it's needed to go through `Unmanaged` status. Read considerations about the `Unmanaged status` in the Documentation section ["Unsupported configurations"](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/logging/cluster-logging-support.html#cluster-logging-maintenance-support-list_cluster-logging-support). #### Step 1: Temporarily set LokiStack to State Unmanaged ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging patch lokistack/logging-loki-p '{"spec":{"managementState": "Unmanaged"}}'--type=merge ``` #### Step 2: Set the log_level ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging get cm logging-loki-config-o yaml | sed 's/log_level: info/log_level: debug/' | oc replace-f- ``` #### Step 3: Restart the Loki pods for taking the new `log_level` definition ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging delete pods-l app.kubernetes.io/instance=logging-loki-n openshift-logging ``` #### Step 4: Verify the pods have the `log_level: debug` ``` $ ingester=$(oc-n openshift-logging get pod-l app.kubernetes.io/component=ingester-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') $ oc-n openshift-logging rsh $ingester cat /etc/loki/config/config.yaml | grep log_level log_level: debug ``` #### Return LokiStack to State Managed When finishing the debug, set again the `LokiStack` to `Managed` ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging patch lokistack/logging-loki-p '{"spec":{"managementState": "Managed"}}'--type=merge ```
root_cause: By default, the `log_level` for the `LokiStack` is `info`: ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging get cm logging-loki-config-o json|jq-r '.data."config.yaml"' |grep log_level log_level: info ``` But, for troubleshooting purposes, it's needed to change to `log_level: debug`.

title: Why cloned VM is having same firmware UUID of source VM in OpenShift Virtualization?
issue: - A VM was cloned using `VirtualMachineClone` API. After cloning, the new VM has firmware UUID defined at `spec/template/spec/domain/firmware/uuid` in VM spec. However, there was no firmware defined in source VM spec: ~~~ # oc get vm centos-stream8-fmu26p5dwan2r5ts-o yaml |yq '.spec.template.spec.domain.firmware' null # oc get vm centos-stream8-fmu26p5dwan2r5ts-clone-o yaml |yq '.spec.template.spec.domain.firmware' uuid: 866fecb8-27d3-53e2-83ce-d011999b4096 ~~~- And this firmware was same as that of source VM, and now both source and cloned VMs have the same firmware UUID.- Because of this, cloud-init is not initiating reconfiguration of the VM since it didn't detected a instance UUID which is derived from firmware UUID: ~~~ new=True for source VM 2024-07-29 10:40:33,337- main.py[DEBUG]: [local] init will now be targeting instance id: 866fecb8-27d3-53e2-83ce-d011999b4096. new=True new=False for cloned VM 2024-07-29 10:40:35,176- main.py[DEBUG]: [net] init will now be targeting instance id: 866fecb8-27d3-53e2-83ce-d011999b4096. new=False ~~~- So the cloned VM network interface was not reconfigured with the new data. And hence, the VM booted without IP address.
resolution: - The root cause of the issue is fixed in OpenShift Virtualization 4.15 with upstream [PR 10515- Stop copying VMI spec to VM during snapshots](https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/pull/10515).- A workaround to fix the clone is to add an empty `firmware: {}` definition to `spec.template.spec.domain` of the source VM spec.
root_cause: - The `VirtualMachineClone` API was using the VMI spec to create the cloned VM spec. The VMI spec will also have the auto generated firmware UUID generated from the VM name. So when a new new VM is created using cloning, the source VM's firmware UUID is also copied to the cloned `virtualmachine` spec and this will be passed to the libvirtd. So the VM will get the source VMs firmware UUID.- Although, there is a check to remove firmware UUID from the spec during the clone, it will not work here since the source VM spec don't have firmware definition: ~~~ func generateFirmwareUUIDPatches(firmware *k6tv1.Firmware) (patches []string) {const firmwareUUIDPatch = `{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/domain/firmware/uuid", "value": ""}` if firmware == nil {<=== return nil} return []string{firmwareUUIDPatch}} ~~~- The issue is only observed while using VirtualMachineClone API and is not observed while cloning the VM from the console. This is because console started using VirtualMachineClone API only from 4.15.

title: [RHOCP 4] Enable/Disable access logs on the envoy proxy selectively in OpenShift Service Mesh
issue: - Is it possible to selectively `enable` and `disable` envoy proxy access logs in `OpenShift Service Mesh`?- Configuring `global access logging` in `OpenShift Service Mesh` leads to `enabling` logs on all the application projects that are part of `OpenShift Service Mesh`, is it possible to control which application projects should have `access logs enabled`?- Access logging is switched on as a global mesh setting, can `EnvoyFilter` or `Telemetry` switch this off on an individual workload?
resolution:
- Selective `disable` or `enable` cannot be done if enabled in `ServiceMeshControlPlane` globally, once enabled it would be a global config.- `EnvoyFilter` or `Telemetry` can be used, but [Support for Envoy Filters with Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6972785) should be reviewed.- Observations shared below when `EnvoyFilter` or `Telemetry` is used.- Enabled global `access logging` by patching `SMCP`: ~~~ $ oc patch smcp basic--type merge-n istio-system-p '{"spec":{"proxy":{"accessLogging":{"file":{"format":"[%START_TIME%] %RESPONSE_CODE% 
"}}}}}' $ oc patch smcp basic--type merge-n istio-system-p '{"spec":{"proxy":{"accessLogging":{"file":{"name":"/dev/stdout"}}}}}' servicemeshcontrolplane.maistra.io/basic patched $ oc get smcp basic-o yaml | yq ".spec.proxy" accessLogging: file: format: "[%START_TIME%] %RESPONSE_CODE% 
" <--- NOTE only 2 parameters are configured for default logging name: /dev/stdout ~~~- Check logs (default behavior): ~~~ $ oc get smmr-o wide NAME READY STATUS AGE MEMBERS default 3/3 Configured 30d ["book","bookinfo","kuard"] $ oc project kuard $ oc logs kuard-blue-697749b885-tvh4q-c istio-proxy-f...... 2023-07-31T14:02:31.867245Z info ads SDS: PUSH request for node:kuard-blue-697749b885-tvh4q.kuard resources:1 size:4.0kB resource:default [2023-07-31T14:03:06.901Z] 200 <--- as expected from step 1, only 2 parameters are returned "START_TIME, RESPONSE_CODE" [2023-07-31T14:03:08.663Z] 200 <--- ~~~- Created `EnvoyFilter` for `kuard` application(sample test application) with additional parameters defined in `envoy-filter`: ~~~ $ oc get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io NAME AGE access-log 5s $ oc get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io access-log-o json| jq '.spec.configPatches[0].patch.value.typed_config.access_log[0].typed_config.format' "[%START_TIME%] "%REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)% %PROTOCOL%" %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% %RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS% %CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS% "%UPSTREAM_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_REASON%" %BYTES_RECEIVED% %BYTES_SENT% %DURATION% %RESP(X-ENVOY-UPSTREAM-SERVICE-TIME)% "%REQ(X-FORWARDED-FOR)%" "%REQ(USER-AGENT)%" "%REQ(X-REQUEST-ID)%" "%REQ(:AUTHORITY)%" "%UPSTREAM_HOST%" %UPSTREAM_CLUSTER% %UPSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS% %DOWNSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS% %DOWNSTREAM_REMOTE_ADDRESS% %REQUESTED_SERVER_NAME% %ROUTE_NAME%
" $ oc logs kuard-blue-697749b885-tvh4q-c istio-proxy-f...... [2023-07-31T14:06:02.832Z] 200 <--- global config from step 1 appended along with below custom EnvoyFilter logs [2023-07-31T14:06:02.832Z] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200- via_upstream- "-" 0 3385 0 0 "10.74.208.77,10.128.2.2" "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/112.0.0.0 Safari/537.36" "ce9868ce-e2c0-967c-a4be-4737d9ff1dc6" "kuard.apps.cluster4111.xx.xx.xx.xx" "10.128.3.49:8080" inbound|8080|| 127.0.0.6:36935 10.128.3.49:8080 10.128.2.2:0 outbound_.80_._.kuard.kuard.svc.cluster.local default <--- envoyFilter enabled logs ~~~- Created `EnvoyFilter` to disable the logs (by sending the logs to /dev/null): ~~~ $ oc get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io NAME AGE access-log 8m40s $ oc get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io access-log-o json| jq '.spec.configPatches[0].patch.value.typed_config.access_log' [{"name": "envoy.file_access_log", "typed_config": {"@type": "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.access_loggers.file.v3.FileAccessLog", "format": "[%START_TIME%] "%REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)% %PROTOCOL%" %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% %RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS% %CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS% "%UPSTREAM_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_REASON%" %BYTES_RECEIVED% %BYTES_SENT% %DURATION% %RESP(X-ENVOY-UPSTREAM-SERVICE-TIME)% "%REQ(X-FORWARDED-FOR)%" "%REQ(USER-AGENT)%" "%REQ(X-REQUEST-ID)%" "%REQ(:AUTHORITY)%" "%UPSTREAM_HOST%" %UPSTREAM_CLUSTER% %UPSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS% %DOWNSTREAM_LOCAL_ADDRESS% %DOWNSTREAM_REMOTE_ADDRESS% %REQUESTED_SERVER_NAME% %ROUTE_NAME%
", "path": "/dev/null" <--- disable logs using envoy_filter}}] $ oc logs kuard-blue-697749b885-tvh4q-c istio-proxy-f |tail...... [2023-07-31T14:24:53.806Z] 200 [2023-07-31T14:24:53.970Z] 200 <--- [2023-07-31T14:24:55.965Z] 200 <--- envoy_filter is applied to "disable" logs hence no logs with custom envoy_filter, but the default global config from step 1 is enabled hence the logs are generated ~~~- With `Telemetry(enabling)`, adding `meshConfig` in `SMCP` (Envoy filter is deleted before this step): ~~~ $ oc get-n istio-system smcp basic-o yaml | yq '.spec.techPreview' meshConfig: extensionProviders:- envoyFileAccessLog: logFormat: text: "[%START_TIME%] %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% 
" path: /dev/stdout name: log- envoyFileAccessLog: logFormat: text: "[%START_TIME%] "%REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)% %PROTOCOL%" %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% %RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS% %CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS% 
" path: /dev/stdout <--- name: logfile <--- $ oc get-n kuard telemetries.telemetry.istio.io logging-kuard-o yaml| yq '.spec' accessLogging:- providers:- name: logfile <--- selector: matchLabels: app: kuard $ oc logs kuard-blue-697749b885-wq72m-c istio-proxy-f...... [2023-07-31T15:23:16.045Z] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200- via_upstream- <--- no default config observed only telemetry defined logs ~~~- With `Telemetry(disabling)`: ~~~ $ oc get-n istio-system smcp basic-o yaml | yq '.spec.techPreview' meshConfig: extensionProviders:- envoyFileAccessLog: logFormat: text: "[%START_TIME%] %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% 
" path: /dev/stdout name: log- envoyFileAccessLog: logFormat: text: "[%START_TIME%] "%REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)% %PROTOCOL%" %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% %RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS% %CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS% 
" path: /dev/null <--- Disable name: logfile <--- $ oc get-n kuard telemetries.telemetry.istio.io logging-kuard-o yaml| yq '.spec' accessLogging:- providers:- name: logfile <--- selector: matchLabels: app: kuard $ oc logs kuard-blue-697749b885-wq72m-c istio-proxy-f...... [2023-07-31T15:23:16.045Z] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200- via_upstream- <--- <--- ~~~- Delete `Telemetry`: ~~~ $ oc delete telemetries.telemetry.istio.io logging-kuard telemetry.telemetry.istio.io "logging-kuard" deleted $ oc logs kuard-blue-697749b885-wq72m-c istio-proxy-f...... [2023-07-31T15:23:16.045Z] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200- via_upstream- [2023-07-31T15:25:53.850Z] 200 <--- due to default config for logging [2023-07-31T15:25:54.275Z] 200 [2023-07-31T15:25:54.574Z] 200 [2023-07-31T15:25:55.023Z] 200 ~~~

title: Tekton pipelines in a cluster with Resource Quotas enabled
issue: - When you try to start a Tekton pipeline on a cluster with Resource Quotas enabled, also if you have set resources (limits and requests) for each and every task according to the Tekton documentation, pipeline doesn't start with the following error message: failed to create task run pod "xxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxx-m6twl-xxxxx-xx-xxxx": pods "xxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxx-m6twl-xxxxx-xx-xxxx" is forbidden: failed quota: "quota name": must specify limits.cpu,limits.memory,requests.cpu,requests.memory. Maybe missing or invalid Task "task name"
resolution: - Apply this object to the cluster (modify limits according to your needs) kind: LimitRange apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: limit-range namespace: limit-testing spec: limits:- type: Container default: cpu: 500m memory: 512Mi defaultRequest: cpu: 500m memory: 256Mi
root_cause: In addition to the containers created for each of the step defined in the task pipeline there may be also an initContainer created. Init Containers are outside the direct control of the author of the task and pipeline. It means that no resource requests or limits can be set on them through a stepTemplate. This is a know situation [1]. To make a pipeline work in a cluster with Resource Quota enabled it might be necessary to apply a LimitRange in the namespace/project in wich the pipeline is defined. In this way LimitRange will apply default request and limits values in case an object do not have them. (in this case initContainer) [1] [https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/a-guide-to-tekton-and-resource-quotas](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/a-guide-to-tekton-and-resource-quotas)

title: Prometheus pod logs show SIGBUS error code=0x2 in RHOCP 4
issue: - After upgrade from 4.5 to 4.6, Prometheus alerts are targeting the message "has disappeared from Prometheus target discovery".- Prometheus pods are in `CrashLoopBackOff` with a `SIGBUS error code=0x2` ~~~ unexpected fault address 0x7f63860e2000 fatal error: fault [signal SIGBUS: bus error code=0x2 addr=0x7f63860e2000 pc=0x470e08] ~~~- The Prometheus volume has run out of space. Note in some cases the below logs do not appear even when out of space condition is seen: ~~~ 2021-04-12T15:38:26.955695412Z level=error ts=2021-04-12T15:38:26.955Z caller=scrape.go:1088 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=openshift-multus/monitor-network/0 target=https://10.0.0.3:8443/metrics msg="Scrape commit failed" err="write to WAL: log samples: write /prometheus/wal/00000588: no space left on device" 2021-04-12T15:38:27.048922251Z level=error ts=2021-04-12T15:38:27.048Z caller=scrape.go:1088 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=openshift-multus/monitor-network/0 target=https://10.0.0.2:8443/metrics msg="Scrape commit failed" err="write to WAL: log samples: write /prometheus/wal/00000588: no space left on device" 2021-04-12T15:38:27.284125345Z level=error ts=2021-04-12T15:38:27.284Z caller=scrape.go:1088 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=openshift-multus/monitor-network/0 target=https://10.0.0.4:8443/metrics msg="Scrape commit failed" err="write to WAL: log samples: write /prometheus/wal/00000588: no space left on device" ~~~
resolution: Consult the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/monitoring/troubleshooting-monitoring-issues.html#determining-why-prometheus-is-consuming-disk-space_troubleshooting-monitoring-issues) to investigate why Prometheus is using up all the disk. The possible solutions are: 1. Increase the storage size 2. Reduce the [retention period](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/monitoring/configuring-the-monitoring-stack.html#modifying-retention-time-for-prometheus-metrics-data_configuring-the-monitoring-stack) for Prometheus metrics data Meanwhile it's taken a decision, it could be deleted some data from the prometheus storage to be able to start it. If the persistent volumes cannot be accessed directly: Access them by `oc rsh` into the Prometheus pods: ~~~ $ oc-n rsh-c prometheus ~~~ Or by using "oc debug": ~~~ $ oc-n rsh-c debug ~~~ For further details on deleting data manually from Prometheus, refer to this [solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7033177)
root_cause: The permanent storage used by the Prometheus pods got full.

title: OpenShift Log Aggregation - Directly querying elasticsearch
issue: - A client requirement has arisen in which directly querying the elasticsearch instance as provided by the the OpenShift log aggregation deployment.- Looking at the elasticsearch pod, I've noted that there are 3 ACL's configured system.logging.fluentd, system.logging.kibana and system.admin- For this specific requirement, read access to all indices will be required (and hence will be using the system.admin ACL).- I'd like to find out where I can find the cert and keypair for the system.admin user? I've extracted the fluent and kibana certs/key pairs from the pods directly, but unfortunately neither have sufficient privileges: ~~~ curl-XGET-k-E./cert.pem--key./key 'https://172.30.x.x:9200/_cat/count' {"error":"ForbiddenException[Attempt from null to_all indices for indices:data/read/count and User [name=system.logging.kibana, roles=[]]]","status":403} ~~~ I've also looked at the trustedstore java kestore but it does not appear to contain a key.
resolution: - There is the admin cert that is available as of 3.2 that a customer can use to manually delete or get old indices from Elasticsearch. 1. Check that you have the following secret entries "admin-key", "admin-cert", "admin-ca" in the logging-elasticsearch secret ~~~ $ oc get secret/logging-elasticsearch-o yaml ~~~ 1a. If there are not these values, you will need to rerun the logging-deployer with version at least 3.2.0 so that the deployer can generate these certificates and attach them to the secret. That process is described in the OpenShift docs[1] 2. Connect to an Elasticsearch pod that is in the cluster you are attempting to clean up from: Find a pod ~~~ $ oc get pods-l component=es $ oc get pods-l component=es-ops ~~~ Connect to pod ~~~ $ oc rsh {your_es_pod} ~~~ 2a. From within an Elasticsearch pod you can issue the following to delete an index of your choice ~~~ $ curl--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-XDELETE "https://localhost:9200/{your_index}" ~~~ NOTE: The location for--key and--cert may be different in some versions. Check the logging-es dc's secrets section for exact locations. There is further documentation described on the ES Delete[2] and Delete by query[3] API pages. [1] https://docs.openshift.org/latest/install_config/upgrading/manual_upgrades.html#manual-upgrading-efk-logging-stack [2] https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/1.5/docs-delete.html [3] https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/1.5/docs-delete-by-query.html Additional info: With delete api [1], if your indices tagged with date is more simple we can delete data that start with 2016-OR 2016-05- the first will delete all data in 2016 the second all data in may 2016. e.g; ~~~ curl-XDELETE 'http://localhost:9200/logstash-2016-05-' curl-XDELETE 'http://localhost:9200/logstash-2016-05-' ~~~ [1] https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/docs-delete.html So I will request you to upgrade to 3.2 version of Openshift Enterprise.

title: No members in a group when syncing groups in OpenShift with LDAP on IPA
issue: [OpenShift syncing groups with LDAP](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/install_config/syncing_groups_with_ldap.html#sync-ldap-rfc-2307) can find user groups but not their members when bind dn and passwords aren't specified. With `ldap_group_sync.yaml`: ~~~ url: ldap://10.0.0.0:389 insecure: true ca: my-ldap-ca-bundle.crt rfc2307:... ~~~ The `oadm groups sync` got no users: ~~~ $ oadm groups sync--sync-config=ldap_group_sync.yaml apiVersion: v1 items:- apiVersion: v1 kind: Group metadata: annotations: openshift.io/ldap.sync-time: 2016-08-02T17:26:08-0400 openshift.io/ldap.uid: cn=admins,dc=example,dc=com openshift.io/ldap.url: localhost:389 creationTimestamp: null labels: openshift.io/ldap.host: localhost name: admins users: null kind: List metadata: {} ~~~
resolution: There are two resolutions:- Specify the bind dn and its password in group sync yaml configuration. Please follow below steps.- Allow anonymous lookups of group membership following [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2205251). ### How to specify bind dn and its password In `ldap_group_sync.yaml`, add `bindDN` and `bindPassword`: ~~~ url: ldap://10.0.0.0:389 bindDN: cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com bindPassword: password insecure: true ca: my-ldap-ca-bundle.crt rfc2307:... ~~~ You will find users in the synced LDAP groups. ~~~ $ oadm groups sync--sync-config=ldap_group_sync apiVersion: v1 items:- apiVersion: v1 kind: Group metadata: annotations: openshift.io/ldap.sync-time: 2016-08-02T17:26:08-0400 openshift.io/ldap.uid: cn=admins,dc=example,dc=com openshift.io/ldap.url: localhost:389 creationTimestamp: null labels: openshift.io/ldap.host: localhost name: admins users:- admin- user1 kind: List metadata: {} ~~~
root_cause: Authentication is required for looking up group membership in IPA 4.1 and newer, which is installed in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, as described in [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2205251).

issue: - How are OpenShift images kept up-to-date?- Does the admin need to run scheduled 'docker pull' or 'yum update'? Or does an automated job update images?- How to always pull security updates in images?

title: While system boots, dracut shows 'Remounting -o '
issue: - While system boots, dracut shows 'Remounting-o '
resolution: - This is an expected behavior.
root_cause: - dracut tries to mount the root filesystem with default mount option. If /etc/fstab contains additional options which is not `default`, dracut does remount the filesystem with the options. This behavior comes from following implementation. ~~~ #!/bin/sh. /lib/dracut-lib.sh filter_rootopts() {local v v="" rootopts=$1 # strip ro and rw options local OLDIFS="$IFS" IFS=, set-- $rootopts IFS="$OLDIFS" while [$#-gt 0]; do case $1 in rw|ro);; defaults);; *) v="$v,${1}";; esac shift done rootopts=${v#,} echo $rootopts} if [-n "$root"-a-z "${root%%block:*}"]; then mount-t ${fstype:-auto}-o "$rflags" "${root#block:}" "$NEWROOT" \ && ROOTFS_MOUNTED=yes if! getarg rd_NO_FSTAB \ &&! getarg rootflags \ && [-f "$NEWROOT/etc/fstab"] \ &&! [-L "$NEWROOT/etc/fstab"]; then # if $NEWROOT/etc/fstab contains special mount options for # the root filesystem, # remount it with the proper options rootfs="auto" rootopts="defaults" while read dev mp fs opts rest; do # skip comments ["${dev%%#*}"!= "$dev"] && continue if ["$mp" = "/"]; then rootfs=$fs rootopts=$opts break fi done < "$NEWROOT/etc/fstab" rootopts=$(filter_rootopts $rootopts) if [-n "$rootopts"]; then umount $NEWROOT info "Remounting ${root#block:} with-o $rootopts,$rflags" mount-t "$rootfs"-o "$rflags","$rootopts" \ "${root#block:}" "$NEWROOT" 2> &1 | vinfo fi fi fi ~~~

title: PV in Terminating state: CheckStorageClasses failed
issue: - PV stuck in Terminating state, the Finalizer is keeping it bound.- vSphere problem detector operator shows the following logs: ~~~ datastore.go:124] CheckStorageClasses checked 6 storage classes, 1 problems found operator.go:247] CheckStorageClasses failed: StorageClass ocs-thin-sc: datastore DS_OCP4_XXX is part of DatastoreCluster_OCP4 datastore cluster ~~~- Trying to remove the impacted Disk and add it back results in an Unhealthy Ceph during rebalancing: ~~~ exec: Running command: ceph osd safe-to-destroy 2--connect-timeout=15--cluster=openshift-storage--conf=/var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/openshift-storage.config--name=client.admin--keyring=/var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/client.admin.keyring--format json--out-file /tmp/866506581 cephosd: osd.2 is NOT be ok to destroy, retrying in 1m until success ~~~

title: ROSA 4.12 clusters require user action before scheduling a minor version upgrade
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) cluster upgrading from 4.12 to 4.13 needs cluster owner action to ensure the stability of the cluster through and after the upgrade operation.- To ensure that cluster owners understand the changes occurring as part of upgrading the underlying Kubernetes to v1.26, there are acknowledgments necessary to ensure cluster owners have taken the necessary precautions.- To ensure AWS policies have been updated before enabling ROSA STS 4.12 cluster upgrades to 4.13, AWS role policy updates are part of the upgrade workflow outlined in the Resolution below.
resolution: > **Note:** For ROSA IAM (non-STS) clusters, the STS role/policy-related steps in this guide do not apply; those clusters will not have a step in the CLI workflow about ensuring policies are updated. #### Prerequisites Before starting with the upgrade to OpenShift 4.13 (which uses Kubernetes 1.26), as a significant number of deprecated APIs are removed in that version, it's necessary to review [KCS 6958394: Preparing to upgrade to OpenShift Container Platform 4.13](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6958394) to understand the changes and to verify if those changes could affect the custom applications in the cluster. #### Prepare to Upgrade ROSA STS To prepare for upgrading ROSA STS from from 4.12 to 4.13, the following tasks need to be done: 1. Upgrade to [latest/current ROSA CLI](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/rosa/). As part of the upgrade task, the ROSA CLI helps by updating STS policies with the 'auto' mode, or allowing to inspect the changes before applying them, with 'manual' mode. 2. Understand [upgrading ROSA clusters with STS](https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/upgrading/rosa-upgrading-sts.html) using ROSA CLI or the [Red Hat Cloud Console](https://console.redhat.com/openshift). 3. Prepare for an upgrade by updating the ROSA STS roles/policies to the latest. List the account roles and notice if they are grouped by the prefix in their naming scheme. Using the prefix that is relevant to the roles for the cluster (assuming logged in), the upgrade can start for each group as shown below: ~~~ $ rosa list account-roles ROLE NAME ROLE TYPE ROLE ARN OPENSHIFT VERSION customprefix-ControlPlane-Role Control plane arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/customprefix-ControlPlane-Role 4.12 customprefix-Installer-Role Installer arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/customprefix-Installer-Role 4.12 customprefix-Support-Role Support arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/customprefix-Support-Role 4.12 customprefix-Worker-Role Worker arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/customprefix-Worker-Role 4.12 ManagedOpenShift-ControlPlane-Role Control plane arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-ControlPlane-Role 4.12 ManagedOpenShift-Installer-Role Installer arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-Installer-Role 4.12 ManagedOpenShift-Support-Role Support arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-Support-Role 4.12 ManagedOpenShift-Worker-Role Worker arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-Worker-Role 4.12 $ rosa list clusters $ rosa upgrade account-roles--prefix ManagedOpenShift # $ rosa list account-roles |grep ManagedOpenShift ManagedOpenShift-ControlPlane-Role Control plane arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-ControlPlane-Role 4.13 ManagedOpenShift-Installer-Role Installer arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-Installer-Role 4.13 ManagedOpenShift-Support-Role Support arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-Support-Role 4.13 ManagedOpenShift-Worker-Role Worker arn:aws:iam::00sample0000:role/ManagedOpenShift-Worker-Role 4.13 ~~~ And now the ROSA cluster and the STS account roles are prepared for updating to 4.13 release. #### Optional: If it's wished to **continue at the CLI** to initiate the upgrade, as a cluster owner, proceed with the following step. The `upgrade cluster` function checks the preparedness for Kubernetes 1.26 API deprecation details. After these checks are done, it's offered to schedule the upgrade to the 4.13 version for the cluster. If more than one cluster, it may need to list them to determine the cluster wished to upgrade. For listing the clusters for the cluster ID and then run the upgrade command on the 4.11 cluster (the `rosa upgrade cluster` command will allow you to schedule an upgrade interactively): ~~~ $ rosa list clusters $ rosa upgrade cluster-c ~~~
root_cause: ROSA clusters upgrading from 4.12 to 4.13 need cluster owner action to ensure the stability of the cluster through and after the upgrade operation. For additional information about Kubernetes deprecated APIs, refer to:- [KCS 6958394: Preparing to upgrade to OpenShift Container Platform 4.13](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6958394)- [Kubernetes.io v1.26 Deprecated API Reference](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26) For ROSA STS Clusters, AWS STS role policies required for ROSA 4.13 must be up to date when coming from older versions.

title: ACS Collector pods stuck into CrashLoopBackOff state after upgrade to RHACS v4.4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - After RHACS cluster is upgraded to version 4.4, Collector pods are getting stuck into CrashLoopBackOff state with below error message for collector container: ~~~ Trying to open the right engine! libpman: failed to create the ringbuf map for CPU '121'. (If you get memory allocation errors try to reduce the buffer dimension) (errno: 12 | message: Cannot allocate memory) terminate called after throwing an instance of 'sinsp_exception' ~~~
resolution: - The issue has been resolved in RHACS 4.4.2 in the following update: [Important: RHACS 4.4 enhancement and security update](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:2941)- NOTE: The workaround, described in this article, must not be applied to-RT kernels.- To work around the issue, modifications to the Collector configuration are necessary, reducing the allocation of kernel ring buffers and/or resizing them. This can be achieved by adjusting the following options: 1. `Operator installation`: The operator controls Collector configuration, the SecuredCluster CR `securedclusters.platform.stackrox.io/stackrox-secured-cluster-services` has to be modified. Here is how it should look like after modification: ~~~ apiVersion: platform.stackrox.io/v1alpha1 kind: SecuredCluster spec: [...] clusterName: testing-cluster [...] # the part below has to be added overlays:- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: DaemonSet name: collector patches:- path: spec.template.spec.containers[name:collector].env[-1] value: | name: ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_CPU_PER_BUFFER value: "4"- path: spec.template.spec.containers[name:collector].env[-1] value: | name: ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_THREAD_CACHE_SIZE value: "8192"- path: spec.template.spec.containers[name:collector].env[-1] value: | name: ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_BUFFER_SIZE value: "1048576" # end of the custom part perNode: collector: [...] ~~~ 2. `Helm installation`: In this case, modify Collector DaemonSet in the secured cluster directly: ~~~ apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: DaemonSet spec: spec: containers:- name: collector env: [...]- name: ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_CPU_PER_BUFFER value: "4"- name: ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_THREAD_CACHE_SIZE value: "8192"- name: ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_BUFFER_SIZE value: "1048576" ~~~- The idea is to apply those settings, then if it doesn't help directly, continue changing those values in the following way: ~~~ Increasing ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_CPU_PER_BUFFER (it's safe so long as there are at least 4 to 8 buffers allocated in total) Decreasing ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_THREAD_CACHE_SIZE (it's safe to go as low as 1k) Decreasing ROX_COLLECTOR_SINSP_BUFFER_SIZE (but 1Mi is already a good value) ~~~
root_cause: - In ACS 4.4, the Collector component transitioned to CO-RE BPF, altering the allocation of kernel memory. Now, all memory is allocated upfront, rather than on demand as previously. The strategy involves generating one in-kernel buffer for each CPU core, so the quantity of kernel memory consumed varies based on the number of cores present on the node.

title: Deleting a DeploymentConfig does not delete the ReplicationControllers
issue: - Deleting a DeploymentConfig fails to delete corresponding Pods and ReplicationControllers- Kube-controller-manager shows errors indicating a problem with a "conversion webhook"
resolution: If the webhooks are part of an existing operator installation, the user will need to troubleshoot their failure. If there is no clear reason, the user may open a case with Red Hat Support. If the webhooks (or their operator) are no longer intended to be installed, remove the offending webhook(s) using one or both of the following commands: ~~~ oc delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration oc delete validatingwebhookconfiguration ~~~
root_cause: [Admission webhooks](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/) are a way to modify and control objects as they enter the cluster, and apply to *all* objects. If a webhook's Service and Pods are removed, but the webhook itself remains installed into the cluster, it can still potentially block new resources like Pods and Deployments from entering the cluster; the webhook cannot mutate or validate the objects without the matching service, but the cluster may expect it to. In addition, the cluster's garbage collector may have trouble removing the webhook due to the blockage it's introduced into the cluster.

title: External hosts in the 10.88.0.0/16 subnet cannot access or ssh to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform nodes or pods by default
issue: - When using Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform, the `podman` container engine utility comes present on Red Hat CoreOS nodes automatically.- If an external host within your network is on a `10.88.0.0/16` subnet, it will be unable to reach the OpenShift cluster's nodes or pods after installation.- How do I ensure that hosts within my network with an IPv4 address in the `10.88.0.0/16` range can reach my OpenShift 4 cluster?
resolution: - The following steps require deleting and recreating all `podman` containers on your OpenShift Container Platform nodes.- If you have pods/containers running within Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform, these pods will be unaffected.- Each container must be recreated after the following steps as we are changing the parameters of the default network in which they are operating on.- Change the default `podman` container network from the `10.88.0.0/16` subnet on the `cni0-podman` bridge to a differing subnet.- This requires applying a `MachineConfig` object to your cluster to ensure all nodes receive the same configuration. An example `MachineConfig` definition in YAML is provided below that changes the default `10.88.0.0/16` to `10.99.0.0/16`: ~~~ variant: openshift version: 4.12.0 metadata: name: 99-podman-default-network labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker storage: files:- path: /etc/cni/net.d/87-podman-bridge.conflist mode: 0644 overwrite: true contents: inline: | [{"name": "podman", "driver": "bridge", "network_interface": "cni-podman0", "subnets": [{"subnet": "10.99.0.0/16", "gateway": "10.99.0.1"}], "ipv6_enabled": false, "internal": false, "dns_enabled": false, "ipam_options": {"driver": "host-local"}}] ~~~- Note in the above configuration, *only* the `machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker` label is applied. You will likely need to apply this to the `machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master` labels as well for this change to occur across both master and worker nodes, as both have `podman` installed on them and active by default.- Create machine configs with [Butane](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/installing/install_config/installing-customizing.html#installation-special-config-butane_installing-customizing).- Once you have your YAML properly defined, it can be deployed with: ~~~ $ oc apply-f./99-podman-default-network.yaml ~~~- At this point, it is *best* to drain, cordon, and reboot the Red Hat CoreOS node(s) affected by this MachineConfig.- Rebooting allows for the old netfilter chains that routed traffic on the default `podman` subnet to be removed completely, and the new `podman` network upon rebooting will reflect the changes.- If rebooting immediately is not an option, a less appealing and safe option is removing the default `cni-podman0` bridge from the Red Hat CoreOS node once all containers have been removed or deleted from within `podman`.- *Do not run the following command if you have rebooted your Red Hat CoreOS nodes after the MachineConfig has applied, as it is unnecessary since the default subnet should have already been changed. ~~~ # ip link delete cni-podman0 ~~~
root_cause: - The default container network for the `podman` container network using the CNI networking backend is a `10.88.0.1/16` subnet for rootful containers.- If this subnet is in use in an environment outside of the OpenShift, then routing to and from OpenShift environments and the external `10.88.0.0/16` subnet within your larger network will by default not function properly, as a route exists to this subnet that will only ever forward traffic to the internal `podman` linux bridge. ~~~ [core@coreos-worker-01 ~]$ route-n Kernel IP routing table Destination Gateway Genmask Flags Metric Ref Use Iface 10.88.0.0 0.0.0.0 255.255.0.0 U 0 0 0 cni-podman0 ~~~- Therefore, the default bridge network for `podman` must be changed to a subnet that is *not in use* by either your network as a whole or internally within OpenShift.

title: Packet loss error while installing OpenShift using Assisted Installer on Bare-Metal
issue: - While deploying the RHOCP 4.11 version, the node status shows "alert: Insufficient Packet loss: Packet loss percentage requirement of equals 0.00% not met for connectivity between server_1 (20.00%), server_2 (30.00%)."- The installation may also fail during the host validation checks.
resolution: - The network manager configuration enables the other network interfaces connected to the server which causes assisted service to check their connectivity against their IP.- It is a known issue to the Red Hat and is being tracked in [BugZilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2105358)- **WORKAROUND**: Disabling the NIC that is unused will solve the problem.- This can be done the hard way by unplugging the cable, or the easy way via configuration when defining the cluster in [**Assisted Installer**](https://github.com/RHsyseng/telco-operations/tree/main/assisted-installer/disable-nic)- The interfaces can also be iterated through in the agent-config.yaml or install-config.yaml and set to `absent`. ~~~ interfaces:- macAddress: 00:fd:fd:fd:fd:d0 name: eno1- macAddress: 00:fd:fd:fd:fd:d1 name: eno2- macAddress: 00:fd:fd:fd:fd:d2 name: eno3- macAddress: 00:fd:fd:fd:fd:d3 networkConfig: interfaces:- name: eno1 type: ethernet state: up mac-address: 00:fd:fd:fd:fd:d0- name: eno2 type: ethernet state: up mac-address: 00:fd:fd:fd:fd:d1- name: eno3 type: unknown state: absent ~~~
root_cause: - The network manager configuration enables the other interfaces.- During the host validation checks, the assisted service performs a full mesh check testing connectivity between all interfaces on all hosts. If there are disabled, unused NICs present, these checks will fail.

title: Can I run images from different architctures under emulation on OpenShift nodes?
issue: I have a cluster with arm64 based nodes. Can I run an amd64 based image using emulation such as qemu?
resolution: Architecture emulation is not supported on OpenShift nodes, however OpenShift does support multi-architecture clusters. What this means is that you can have a mixture of different architectured compute nodes and use labels and selectors to schedule workloads based on architecture. The only limitation is that all of the control plane nodes must be of the one architecture. For more details, please refer to the official documentation for [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/) for your desired version. The "Configuing multi-architecture compute machines on an OpenShift cluster" can be found in the "Postinstallation configuration" section of the documentation.

title: How to get the size of all DeploymentConfig (dc) objects inside ETCD in RHOCP 4?
issue: - Cannot list the `DeploymentConfig` (dc) objects in ETCD?- How to list the size of all the `DeploymentConfig` objects in ETCD?
resolution: - List total number of `DeploymentConfig` objects. ~~~ $ oc rsh-n openshift-etcd (From inside container run below commands) $ etcdctl--command-timeout=20s get--prefix--keys-only /openshift.io/deploymentconfigs | sed '/^$/d' | wc-l 2 ## here output is 2, it should be different as per number of dc's ~~~- Display size consumed by each `DeploymentConfig` object. ~~~ $ for resource in $(etcdctl--command-timeout=20s get--prefix--keys-only /openshift.io/deploymentconfig); do SIZE=$(etcdctl get $resource-w protobuf | wc-c); echo "$SIZE $resource"; done | sort-n 4401 /openshift.io/deploymentconfigs/test/mysql 5033 /openshift.io/deploymentconfigs/test/cakephp-mysql-example ~~~ **Note:** This output is returned in Bytes.
root_cause: - `DeploymentConfigs` are displayed at the API endpoint at `/openshift.io/` and not at `kubernetes.io/` because they are OpenShift object.

title: How to get the size of all Replication Controller objects from ETCD  in RHOCP 4 ?
