title: BA Operator Upgrade from 7.11 to 7.12 halts in OCP 4
issue: BA Operator upgrade from 7.11 to 7.12 halts on pending state ~~~ $ oc get kieapp NAME VERSION ENVIRONMENT STATUS AGE rhpam-trial 7.11.1 rhpam-trial Deployed 26h $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE businessautomation-operator.7.11.1-3 Business Automation 7.11.1-3 businessautomation-operator.7.11.1-2 Replacing businessautomation-operator.7.12.0-1 Business Automation 7.12.0-1 businessautomation-operator.7.11.1-3 Pending <-------------------- 7.12.0-1 ~~~
resolution: BA Operator Version 7.11 to 7.12 breaks CRD compatibility preventing the upgrade depending on the KieApp Custom Resource created. In case the user is setting a spec `KieApp` that was deprecated/removed for instance `loginModule: required`, which its enumeration only accepts `optional`, this will prevent the upgrade. Example: ~~~ spec: auth: ldap: url: ldaps://myldap.example.com... referralMode: FOLLOW loginModule: required ← must be loginModule: optional not to break. ~~~ Given this incompatibility, the Operator will be in a pending upgrade state because the new CRD cannot validate the previous CRs. ### Workarounds First, change the required spec for a new one valid, e.g. loginModule: optional. And then the upgrade should work. However, if the user is in the middle do that in the middle of a pending Upgrade it won't work, so remove both Operators (replacing and pending Operators) and then re-install again. A final, more radical solution, would be to Remove the KieApp Custom Resource in case that is the problem or remove the spec that is deprecated/removed. This causes direct interruption of service on the environment, reason as follows: Although the removal of the Business Operator does not cause interruption of service, the removal of the `kieapps.app.kiegroup.org` CRD will cause the removal of the KieApp CR, which subsequently causes the removal of all pods/deployments by the KieApp.
root_cause: The upgrade makes a new KieApp CRD be installed on the cluster. So then the KieApp CRs already there must be validated before the **new CRD is installed**. This is a feature that prevents further issues. However, if the KieApp CR has an element that was removed/deprecated, the validation pre-install is halted. So the upgrade will be halted until the spec is changed. The spec `loginModule` was changed for accenting two values: [required, optional] to one [optional]. If there is an unsupported value the upgrade won't happen. Finally, about OperatorGroup (OG) and InstallPlans (IP) being used more than once, the OLM framework has some limitations/settings such as 1:N (one to many) cardinality of OG and IP for Operators, as explained on [How can Operators be updated independently from each other?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6389681). The OLM is composed of three components inside the `openshift-lifecycle-manager` namespace:- the OLM pod- the Catalog Operator (CO) pod,- the Package Server, which is an aggregated api service that serves operator metadata

title: OpenShift 3.1 running a 3.2 version router.
issue: - I need features from the 3.2 router but can not update my environment to from 3.1 to 3.2- I see the following error in the router logs: error reloading router: wait: no child processes- Router is reloading to often due to [bug 1320233- haproxy is reloaded every 10 minutes N-times for N endpoints](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1320233)- Can I get a fix in 3.1 for [Bug 1353744- Router slow in loading routes to haproxy config](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1353744)
resolution: The OpenShift 3.2 router is backwards compatible with with environments running 3.1. Meaning that the image `registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ose-haproxy-router:v3.2` can be used for the router in a 3.1 environment. ####Updating the router- To change the version of router that is being used, edit the router's the deployment configuration. ~~~ # oc edit dc/router... spec: template: spec: containers:- env:... image: registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ose-haproxy-router:v3.2 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent... ~~~- OpenShift 3.2 updated the router's role, this will also need to be updated in OpenShift 3.1. A rule needs to be added to the "system:router" role. The role will look similar the the following: ~~~ # oc edit clusterrole system:router apiVersion: v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: creationTimestamp: 2016-05-24T18:15:10Z name: system:router resourceVersion: "36" selfLink: /oapi/v1/clusterroles/system:router uid: 73eb006a-21db-11e6-8075-fa163ecd1122 rules:- apiGroups: null attributeRestrictions: null resources:- endpoints- routes verbs:- list- watch- apiGroups: null attributeRestrictions: null resources:- routes/status verbs:- update ~~~

title: Does Red Hat provide Docker-formatted container images for JBoss Fuse/A-MQ?
issue: Red Hat supports Fuse and A-MQ on OpenShift, using Docker-formatted container images. A question naturally arises whether Red Hat makes the relevant images, or others, available to customers, for other purposes.
resolution: In general, Red Hat does not support the use of Fuse or A-MQ container images for purposes other than running on OpenShift. Of course, nothing prevents customers using these images but, if faults are discovered, they may not be fixed unless they can be reproduced on OpenShift.

title: Pods are stuck in "ContainerCreating" status in OpenShift
issue: A pod gets stuck in `ContainerCreating` status and throws an event error similar to: ~~~ Failed sync Error syncing pod, skipping: failed to "StartContainer" for "POD" with RunContainerError: "runContainer: API error (500): unable to open database file ~~~
Docker storage gets full, corrupted and fails to work in expected way.
resolution: Update to docker-1.10 or later to resolve an issue where the docker daemon would become corrupt, not handle the corruption properly, and would lead to this issue. Following are the methods to manually clean the docker pool:- Set up Garbage Collection as this will remove terminated containers and images not referenced by any running pods. Removing these would also remove the metadata and logs of the containers that were deleted. For more information, refer to the [Setting up GC](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/admin_guide/garbage_collection.html "Set up GC") documentation.- With Docker 1.8 and later, there are now log-rotate capabilities. To get these to work, set options like the following in: ~~~ docker config: '/etc/sysconfig/docker' OPTIONS='--selinux-enabled--log-opt max-size=10m--log-opt max-file=7' ~~~- It's also possible to periodically prune older versions of objects from the OpenShift instance that are no longer needed. To prune those images: 1. Log in to the CLI as a user with an access token. The user must also have the cluster role system:image-pruner or greater (for example, cluster-admin); 2. [Assign a user with access token](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2317371) 3. [Prune images](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/admin_guide/pruning_resources.html#pruning-images)
root_cause: The cause of this error is when the docker pool gets filled up with the stdout logs and unused docker images with insufficient space left for the new image.

title: Session affinity in openshift 3
issue: - How sticky session handled in Openshift 3.- Do we need to create IP sticky or any layer 7 sticky between F5 LB and HAPROXY Router node?- Default router (haproxy.conf) shows that router and pods go by least connection and Cookie insert (so it's actually cookie based session sticky isn't it?)- I see connections between HAPROXY router and pods they go via least connection rule, how can I make them session sticky?- How do I edit route or haproxy.conf file to update app route to have session sticky?
resolution: - With the release of Openshift 3.2 "The HAProxy router should now obfuscate the pod IP in when using cookies for session affinity."- HAProxy was configured, in the default template, to inject a session cookie into each connection.- The session cookie was used when a client created a 2nd+ session.- If the client supplied the cookie HAProxy would be able to make sure you ended up using the same backing pod.- Before this change the contents of the cookie included information about the system (that it was OpenShift), the internal name of the service backing the Route, and even the IP address of the backing pod. Nothing was using that information. The concatenation of that information was merely a unique key for HAProxy.- After this change:- The cookies contents are a hash of all of the above information.- End users will not get any of the above, they will just get some 'random' bytes.- If you have changed the default template to disable cookies for sessions affinity then these changes have no impact.- Implementing sticky sessions is up to the underlying router configuration. The default HAProxy template implements sticky sessions using the balance source directive which balances based on the source IP.- Specific configuration for this router implementation is stored in the `haproxy-config.template` file located in the `/var/lib/haproxy/conf` directory of the router container. ~~~ # oc rsh $routerpod sh-4.2$ cat /var/lib/haproxy/conf ~~~- For further information, please read the [Routes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/architecture/networking/routes.html#routes-sticky-sessions) section of the architecture documentation

title: High memory usage by etcd in OpenShift 3.x
issue: - High memory usage by etcd- After increasing the memory on etcd nodes from 16GB-> 32GB, memory still being consumed quickly- Large number of Event resources are being generated in the cluster- Etcd cluster is unstable ~~~ [root@example ~]# free-m total used free shared buff/cache available Mem: 32013 30610 238 345 1164 796 Swap: 4095 1474 2621 [root@example ~]# systemctl restart etcd [root@example ~]# free-m total used free shared buff/cache available Mem: 32013 11235 18500 334 2278 20185 Swap: 4095 1455 2640 ~~~- Restart of etcd freed up 18GB of Mem, while about half an hour later it is back to: ~~~ [root@example ~]# free-m total used free shared buff/cache available Mem: 32013 25502 1607 369 4903 5833 Swap: 4095 1452 2643 ~~~
resolution: Etcd stores events from the OpenShift cluster in main memory. These are the same events that can be seen with: ~~~ $ oc get events--all-namespaces ~~~ These events have a default time-to-live (how long they remain in memory) of 2 hours. If etcd is using large amounts of memory and there are large numbers of events returned by the previous command, set the time-to-live to a smaller amount in `/etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml` file, as follows[1]: ~~~ kubernetesMasterConfig: apiServerArguments: event-ttl:- "30m" ~~~ This causes etcd to prune events more frequently, freeing up memory. However, a large number of events can be indicative of other problems in the cluster; repeated events in extreme numbers should be investigated further. Additionally, it should be noted that setting a shorter time-to-live can impact the ability to monitor the events in a cluster since there is a shorter period of time in which to investigate events. [1]

title: How to manage subscription of the Virtual Machine launched from Azure Marketplace
issue: - When I lauch Red Hat Enterprise Linux from Azure Marketplace, how should I register my subscription?- When I lauch Red Hat Enterprise Linux from Azure Marketplace, how can I enable additional repositories such as OpenShift and gluster.
resolution: You don't have to register subscription with subscription-manager command. When you create or delete from Azure Market Place, subscription is automatically registered and deregistered. The subscription costs according to the usage. If you want to stop VM tentative, you can deallocate VM. Deallocated VM isn't billed for Virtual Machine. As of the extra repository, such as OpenShift, gluster and so on, you can't enable these repository in On-Demand VM. On-Demand Supported Products are listed in [Microsoft Azure Certified Cloud Provider](https://access.redhat.com/ecosystem/partners/ccsp/microsoft-azure#gettingstarted). If you want to use the products not listed here and you already have the valid subscription, you should use [Cloud-Access](https://access.redhat.com/articles/ccp-azure-faq). NOTE: if you register your cloud-access subscription with subscription-manager on you On-Demand subscription VM, they would be paying twice (Microsoft Azure charge for Red Hat Enterprise Linux plus the subscription to Red Hat).
root_cause: Virtual Machines which you can launch from Azure Marketplace is On-Demand Subscription. The difference is described [here](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2041283).

Jul 11 20:55:44 knakayam-ose32-smaster forward-journal[10503]: Forwarding stdin to journald using Priority Informational and tag docker Jul 11 20:55:44 knakayam-ose32-smaster forward-journal[10503]: time="2016-07-11T20:55:44.863571209+09:00" level=warning msg="devmapper: Usage of loopback devices is strongly discouraged for production use. title: Issues Running `systemctl restart` Command to OpenShift Master Services
issue: - `atomic-openshift-master.service` fails to start or restart with error messages- OpenShift master errors in `systemctl status` or `journalctl-xe` referring to yaml issues: ~~~ Jul 19 16:51:35 master.example.com atomic-openshift-master[69659]: F0719 16:51:35.928627 69659 start_master.go:100] yaml: line 5: did not find expected key Jul 19 16:51:35 master.example.com systemd[1]: atomic-openshift-master.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=255/n/a Jul 19 16:51:35 master.example.com systemd[1]: Failed to start Atomic OpenShift Master. ~~~ ~~~ $ systemctl status atomic-openshift-master.service ● atomic-openshift-master.service- Atomic OpenShift Master Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/atomic-openshift-master.service; enabled; vendor preset: disabled) Active: failed (Result: start-limit) since Tue 2016-07-19 16:51:36 EDT; 12s ago Docs: https://github.com/openshift/origin Process: 69659 ExecStart=/usr/bin/openshift start master--config=${CONFIG_FILE} $OPTIONS (code=exited, status=255) Main PID: 69659 (code=exited, status=255) ~~~
resolution: - Error messages indicating problems with yaml are often syntax errors or missing/incorrect values in `/etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml` or other configuration files.

title: Subscription Requirements for Red Hat Single Sign-On (RH-SSO)
issue: - Does `Red Hat Single Sign-On`(Red Hat SSO or RH-SSO) require a separate subscription?- Which subscriptions do I need to use `Red Hat Single Sign-On`?- What is `JBoss Core Services Collection` and does it need additional subscription?- Do I need an OpenShift separate subscription for the RH-SSO image for OpenShift?- Does JBoss Middleware subscription alone cover support for using the RH-SSO image for OpenShift?
resolution: - `Red Hat Single Sign-On (RH-SSO)` does not have its own SKU (Stock Keeping Unit); hence one can't buy an RH-SSO subscription directly. RH-SSO is built on top of the JBoss EAP platform and leverages it extensively (JTA, JAX-RS, JPA, Infinispan, etc...).- Red Hat Single Sign-On is part of the [Red Hat JBoss Core Services Collection](https://access.redhat.com/collections/red-hat-jboss-core-services-collection), which provides components that increase the value of JBoss Middleware products by enhancing manageability, security, scalability, and interoperability.. All entitled users (customers) of JBoss Middleware products, with the exception of users (customers) exclusively entitled to JBoss Web Server, are entitled to JBoss Core Services. See the Red Hat JBoss Core Services [datasheet](https://www.redhat.com/cms/managed-files/mi-core-services-collection-datasheet-inc0403358-201606-en.pdf) and [FAQ](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2294961) for additional information.- If you already have a valid/active JBoss Middleware support contract for one of the JBoss Middleware products (i.e. JBoss EAP, Data Grid, Fuse, Process Automation Manager, or any of the [Middleware](https://www.redhat.com/en/products/middleware) bundles such as [Red Hat Runtimes](https://www.redhat.com/en/products/runtimes), [Red Hat Integration](https://www.redhat.com/en/products/integration) or [Red Hat Process Automation](https://www.redhat.com/en/products/process-automation)), then you already have support for RH-SSO as it is covered under the JBoss Core Services Collection. Each JBoss Middleware product, except JBoss Web Server, comes with support for RH-SSO automatically without any additional cost.- If you are not already a JBoss Middleware customer, then you can buy a subscription to one of the JBoss Middleware products as RH-SSO does not have its own SKU. For example, you can purchase online a subscription for [Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (JBoss EAP)](https://www.redhat.com/en/store/red-hat-jboss-enterprise-application-platform#?sku=MW0196814) or for [Red Hat Runtimes](https://www.redhat.com/en/products/runtimes), which include support for RH-SSO, or you can also contact [Red Hat Sales](https://www.redhat.com/en/contact#tab.contact-method.1) if you are interested in something more comprehensive or need more information.- The Red Hat Single Sign-On (RH-SSO) for OpenShift image from the [Red Hat Container Catalog registry](https://access.redhat.com/containers/), is only supported to run on Openshift. It is the only RH-SSO image that is productized/released, and it is an image that is designed to be used in OpenShift. A valid/active OpenShift subscription entitlement is required for receiving support on this image from Red Hat. It is not necessary to buy an additional JBoss Middleware subscription in addition to an active OpenShift subscription to receiving support for the RH-SSO for OpenShift image. However, having only a valid/active JBoss subscription entitlement (like for EAP or for the [Middleware](https://www.redhat.com/en/products/middleware) bundles) does not cover Openshift itself. Although the RH-SSO container image must be run on OpenShift, it can be used to protect any application, regardless of where it runs or whether or not it is based on Red Hat Middleware. Refer to [Red Hat OpenShift sizing and subscription guide](https://www.redhat.com/en/resources/openshift-sizing-subscription-guide) that provides a description of the subscription model for Red Hat® OpenShift Container Platform.- Red Hat does not produce any standard Docker image for RH-SSO. The source for the [RH-SSO container image](https://github.com/jboss-container-images/redhat-sso-7-image) is for building the standalone image that is only used internally as a base for the productized and supported OpenShift image. It is also based on some other intermediate images which are not released publicly either. So, for those customers that still want to use and run RH-SSO in a containerized image environment, but without having an Openshift subscription (or not willing to buy a new OpenShift subscription from Red Hat), or even perhaps not looking to run such RH-SSO image on OpenShift environment, then they will have to build their own custom container images from scratch using the [ZIP distribution of RH-SSO software downloads](https://access.redhat.com/jbossnetwork/restricted/listSoftware.html?downloadType=distributions&product=core.service.rhsso). This should also work and those customers will be supported for specific RH-SSO related issues as long as they have a valid/active JBoss Middleware support contract and that the custom container image is built with the RH-SSO software being used on a supported JVM/OS combination as per the [Red Hat Single Sign-On Supported Configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2342861). But, it is to be noted that those customers will still own the creation and maintenance of such a custom container image. Red Hat treats custom built images as `custom software` and will not provide support for the resulting images themselves, but rather support on the JBoss Middleware products included as part of the images. Refer to [How are JBoss Products supported when used in container images](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3213211) for furthermore details.

title: How to clean up elasticsearch indices when elasticsearch fills up the disk of a data store in OSP's centralized logging solution?
issue: As part of Red Hat OpenStack's tech preview, one can configure a [centralized logging architecture](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-openstack-platform/version-8/red-hat-openstack-platform-operational-tools/). After some time, elasticsearch is filling the whole disk of a data store in Red Hat OpenStack Platform's centralized logging solution. ~~~ [root@datastore ~]# sudo find /-size +100000-exec ls-la '{}' 2> /dev/null \; | sort-k 5-n| tail-n20-rw-r--r--. 1 elasticsearch elasticsearch 246367839 Jun 21 17:41 /var/lib/elasticsearch/datastore/nodes/0/indices/logstash-2016.06.21/1/index/_aa2.fdt-rw-r--r--. 1 elasticsearch elasticsearch 246937268 Jul 4 17:05 /var/lib/elasticsearch/datastore/nodes/0/indices/logstash-2016.07.04/4/index/_bbk.fdt (...) ~~~ How can one clean up the disk?
resolution: Currently the `elastic-curator` is shipped with the `OpenShift` and `Atomic` repositories, so one will have to use `virtualenv` and `pip` to cleanup indices. This will avoid conflicts with system libraries. ~~~ virtualenv elastic_cleanup ~~~ Activate the virtualenv ~~~. elastic_cleanup/bin/activate ~~~ Note a (`elastic_cleanup`) before the prompt to indicate that the virtualenv is active ~~~ (elastic_cleanup)[root@node1 ~]# ~~~ Install the `curator` ~~~ (elastic_cleanup)[root@node1 ~]# pip install elasticsearch-curator==3.5 ~~~ > Please note that of time of this writing, only curator 3.5 is supported for this solution. The syntax used to run curator 4 is significantly different (see `Diagnostic Steps`). Run the curator. Ensure ELK stack is up and running, or that elasticsearch is accepting API connections. title: dnsmasq not started after installing OpenShift Enterprise 3.2
issue: - Failed to deploy pods with `no such host: kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local`- OpenShift cannot resolve hostnames
resolution: Check dnsmasq status and start it manually when it's not up and running. ~~~ systemctl status dnsmasq systemctl start dnsmasq ~~~ In OpenShift Enterprise 3.2, it configures NetworkManager and NetworkManager starts dnsmasq. This script is located at `/etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-origin-dns.sh` and it contains `systemctl restart dnsmasq`. We don't need `systemctl enable dnsmasq`. However we sometimes see that the dnsmasq is not starting after the installation for some reason. Red Hat is trying to get steps to reproduce this issue.
root_cause: Root cause analysis is ongoing on

title: What are the openshift_master_default_subdomain or osm_default_subdomain variables used for?
issue: - I want to understand what these variables are for.- When you deploy a service it creates a URL. That URL needs to have a certain subdomain and needs to be public facing. Currently, with `osm_default_subdomain` set, the subdomain is correct, but the URL (when clicked) doesn't load.
resolution: In order to expose a service publicly, you should create a [route](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/architecture/core_concepts/routes.html) that will be a fully routable hostname.- It is usually expected that this hostname will be routable because it will be based off of the [wildcard DNS Entry](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/install_config/install/prerequisites.html#prereq-dns), which should route directly to the IP address of the node that is running the router pod. This allows the router to properly identify the traffic that is incoming, and direct it to the service, or application, that the traffic is attempting to reach (via the defined route). These variables, depending on the version of OpenShift that you are running, will allow you to change what the default hostname will be when a new route is created.- For example, if you do not change this variable and create a new application, like `my-php`, within the project `mytesting`, the default created hostname would be `my-php-mytesting.router.default.svc.cluster.local`.- But if you had used this variable during installation and set the default subdomain to `example.com`, when you create the `your-python` application, within the project `yourtesting`, the default hostname would be `your-python-yourtesting.example.com`. ######The variable was changed in Release 3.2 from `osm_default-subdomain` to `openshift_master_default_subdomain` as you can see in the [change logs](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/install_config/revhistory_install_config.html#thu-may-12-2016)
root_cause: As this is a [Cluster Variable](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/install_config/install/advanced_install.html#configuring-cluster-variables) to be used during installation, you should refer to our [documentation for the installer](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/install_config/install/advanced_install.html#configuring-cluster-variables). If you already have a working cluster, you can also follow [this guide](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2081043) to help you set it up.

title: Why 'shmall' and 'shmmax' shows very high value in RHEL 7 ?
issue: - Why 'shmall' and 'shmmax' shows very high value in RHEL 7?
resolution: - The value is coming from [kernel code](https://access.redhat.com/labs/rhcb/RHEL-7.9/kernel-3.10.0-1160.el7/sources/raw/include/uapi/linux/shm.h) ~~~ #define SHMMNI 4096 /* max num of segs system wide */ #define SHMMAX (ULONG_MAX- (1L < <24)) /* max shared seg size (bytes) */ #define SHMALL (ULONG_MAX- (1L < <24)) /* max shm system wide (pages) */ ~~~- Value of `ULONG_MAX` can be found as below: ~~~ # getconf-a |grep ULONG_MAX ULONG_MAX 18446744073709551615 ~~~- Now `lL < <24` means bit shift which is calculated as follows: ~~~ 1L < <24 means 2^24---> 16777216 ~~~- Hence actual value becomes as below: ~~~ # echo 18446744073709551615-16777216|bc 18446744073692774399 < <=----- < <=----- ~~~

title: Need more information on RHBZ #1310959
issue: We ran multiple times into ImageStramTag problems. After searching around I found the following Bugreport: BZ #1310959. The questions related to this bug are:
Is there a newer version of 3.1.X which has the fix included (so we don't need to do a major upgrade very soon)
Is the bug only in combination with Native-HA triggered (so we can run without Native-HA until the 3.2 upgrade)
Is there a better workaround or anything what can help which isn't documented publicly
resolution: * The way in which this was fixed/addressed was to introduce a massive change which prevented Red Hat from back-porting this into OpenShift 3.1.X. * It is not likely that the Native-HA configuration or routing triggered this issue but other changes with 3.1.1 or 3.1 that also came with the changes to Navive-HA. * There are currently no documented workarounds to this issue, and the recommendation is to update to Red Hat OpenShift 3.2.

title: How to connect to OpenShift instance after a deployment
issue: - After an OpenShift deployment, how to connect to master and nodes instances.- What is the password to connect to OpenShift instances after a deployment
resolution: After a successful deployment of OpenShift Enterprise made with QCI, a master and one or more nodes are running. Be default, QCI configure SSH to only accept password-less connection using SSH keys. These keys can be found in the `/usr/share/foreman/.ssh/openshift/ /` folder. A connection can be made using this syntax: ~~~ ssh-i /usr/share/foreman/.ssh/openshift/ /id_rsa root@-ose-master1.example.com ~~~ In addition to the root user, QCI also create the cloudsuite-install user.

title: Can't find Fuse Integration Services [FIS] or A-MQ xPaaS image templates in the Container Development Kit [CDK v2.0]
issue: It is not clear that the [OpenShift Enterprise xPaaS image documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/using_images/xpaas_images/index.html) does **not*

apply to the containerized OpenShift Enterprise instance delivered as a part of the [Container Development Kit](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-container-development-kit/) as discussed in section [1.3 WHAT IS INSIDE CDK](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/red-hat-container-development-kit/2.0/installation-guide/#what_is_inside_cdk). In particular, under the header [OpenShift Source-to-Image (S2I) Workflow](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/using_images/xpaas_images/fuse.html#fuse-using-application-templates) it specifies that the Fuse Integration Services image streams json file can be found on the filesystem at: ~~~ /usr/share/openshift/examples/xpaas-streams/fis-image-streams.json ~~~ However, in a CDK 2.0 installation there are no files or sub-directories contained within the /usr/share/openshift directory.
resolution: The JBoss Fuse Integration Services templates are available from the [jboss-fuse/application-templates](https://github.com/jboss-fuse/application-templates) repository which you can clone via: ~~~ git clone https://github.com/jboss-fuse/application-templates ~~~ The main JBoss Middleware templates are available from [jboss-openshift/application-templates](https://github.com/jboss-openshift/application-templates) repository which you can clone via: ~~~ git clone https://github.com/jboss-openshift/application-templates ~~~ As well, by default, there is a select, tested, list of the JBoss Middleware templates already included in the CDK. These can be found in this directory: ~~~ /opt/adb/openshift/templates/ ~~~ You should see the following list: ~~~ [vagrant@rhel-cdk share]$ ls-latrh /opt/adb/openshift/templates total 156K-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 2.5K Apr 7 09:27 wildfly-image-streams.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 12K Apr 7 09:27 nodejs-mongodb.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 7.7K Apr 7 09:27 nodejs.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 25K Apr 7 09:27 jws30-tomcat7-mysql-persistent-s2i.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 8.5K Apr 7 09:27 jboss-image-streams.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 14K Apr 7 09:27 image-streams-rhel7.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 30K Apr 7 09:27 eap64-mysql-persistent-s2i.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 12K Apr 7 09:27 eap64-basic-s2i.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 13K Apr 7 09:27 cakephp-mysql.json-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 8.5K Apr 7 09:27 cakephp.json drwxr-xr-x. 3 root root 106 Apr 8 01:53.. drwxr-xr-x. 2 root root 4.0K Apr 8 01:53. [vagrant@rhel-cdk share]$ ~~~
root_cause: Not all xPaaS templates have been tested to be delivered as a part of the CDK.

title: [Satellite 6] Openshift 3.2 repository not available on Red Hat Satellite.
issue: - Unable to load Openshift 3.2 repository on Red Hat Satellite.
resolution: 1) On customer portal confirm that Openshift subscription is added to satellite organization. 2) Make sure that manifest is in sync with the Red Hat CDN Server Satellite webUI > > Content > > Red Hat Subscriptions > > Manage Manifest > > click Refresh Manifest 3) After successful refresh, enable the required repositories Satellite webUI > > Content > > Red Hat Repositories > > Expand Red Hat Openshift Enterprise > > Expand the 3.2 repos and sync the same. For more KB articles/solutions related to Red Hat Satellite 6.x Repository Issues, please refer to the [Red Hat Satellite Consolidated Troubleshooting Article for Red Hat Satellite 6.x Repository Issues.](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6444871)

title: How to downgrade docker-1.9.1 to docker-1.8.2
issue: - How to downgrade docker-1.9.1 to docker-1.8.2- `yum update` installs unsupported docker-1.9 on OSE 3.1- Got Transaction check error when running `yum downgrade docker-1.8.2 docker-selinux-1.8.2` ~~~ Transaction check error: file /etc/sysconfig/docker from install of docker-1.8.2-10.el7.x86_64 conflicts with file from package docker-common-1.9.1-40.el7.x86_64 file /usr/bin/docker from install of docker-1.8.2-10.el7.x86_64 conflicts with file from package docker-common-1.9.1-40.el7.x86_64 ~~~
resolution: We need to use `swap` instead of `downgrade` when we have package structure change like this. ~~~ # yum swap docker-* docker-*1.8.2 # sed-i 's/--storage-opt dm.use_deferred_deletion=true//' /etc/sysconfig/docker-storage # systemctl restart docker ~~~

title: How to configure proxy in CDK for Openshift
issue: - Proxy configuration for Openshift in Red Hat CDK
resolution: **NOTE:** Some users reported the following configuration is incomplete and doesn't work. This is work in progress article.- The referenced file names in [How to work with HTTP proxies to make deployments works in Openshift 3](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1519243) are not directly available in the CDK. Instead of `/etc/sysconfig/atomic-openshift*` one has to modify this file `/etc/sysconfig/openshift_option`. In there add below settings: ~~~ HTTP_PROXY=http://USERNAME:PASSWORD@10.0.1.1:8080/ HTTPS_PROXY=https://USERNAME:PASSWORD@10.0.0.1:8080/ NO_PROXY=master.hostname.example.com, ~~~- However, this is not enough yet in the context of the CDK because of how OpenShift is being run inside the CDK because the openshift itself is started as a container, and the script that starts that container will not propagate these settings. This is a limitation that should be addressed via the existing Enhancement request [Bug 1313218- Support proxies](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1313218).- The workaround of this limitation while the enhancement is implemented is: after configuring openshift_option as described above, manually edit the script `/opt/adb/openshift/openshift` that takes care of starting openshift. You will see a function called `start_openshift` that executes a long `docker run` commandYou should add this parameter to that command invocation: ~~~--env-file /etc/sysconfig/openshift_option ~~~-The full updated function looks like this: ~~~ start_openshift() {docker run $1--name "openshift"--privileged--net=host--pid=host \-w ${ORIGIN_DIR} \-e "KUBECONFIG=${OPENSHIFT_DIR}/admin.kubeconfig" \--env-file /etc/sysconfig/openshift_option \-v /:/rootfs:ro \-v /var/run:/var/run:rw \-v /sys:/sys:ro \-v /var/lib/docker:/var/lib/docker:rw \-v ${ORIGIN_DIR}/openshift.local.volumes:${ORIGIN_DIR}/openshift.local.volumes:z \-v ${ORIGIN_DIR}/openshift.local.config:${ORIGIN_DIR}/openshift.local.config:z \-v ${ORIGIN_DIR}/openshift.local.etcd:${ORIGIN_DIR}/openshift.local.etcd:z \ $IMAGE start "${@:2}"} ~~~- Once this script is updated please restart openshift: ~~~ # systemctl restart openshift ~~~

title: Multiple Users Log In to Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3 Web Console
issue: - Can multiple users login at the same time to the web UI?- For example, user1 logs in first, then user2 logs in, but then user1 shows user2 projects. But if one logins through CLI different users can login at same time.- If I log into two sessions of the OpenShift web user interface, I only see the projects from one user
resolution: This behavior is intentional, not a bug. The web console is engineered to only allow one user to log in from a single browser. Using two different browsers on one machine allows multiple logins per workstation.

title: How can changes to the kubernetes scheduler be added OpenShift 3.
issue: - I see documentation on what can be configure but nothing on where to make the changes.- How can I modify how OpenShift 3 schedules pods to nodes.
resolution: Documentation on what can be configured with the Kubernetes Scheduler can be found in the [OpenShift 3 Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/admin_guide/scheduler.html)- There is already a scheduler policy a file located on the masters by default, located at ``/etc/origin/master/scheduler.json` To confirm the location of the scheduler policy file, look in the `master-config.yaml` file to see what is configured. ~~~ # grep schedulerConfigFile /etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml schedulerConfigFile: /etc/origin/master/scheduler.json ~~~ To change the scheduler configurations either edit the scheduler.json or create your own scheduler configuration file and update the `master-config.yaml` and edit `schedulerConfigFile` value with the new file location. Restart the mater services for the changes to take effect. ~~~ # systemctl restart atomic-openshift-master* ~~~

title: Issues Scaling Application With "Failed to Delete Containers" Message in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3.1
issue: - The deployer fails to deploy the application, because of failing to delete containers. ~~~ 12m 12m 1 {kubelet lpdospea00126.phx.aexp.com} implicitly required container POD Started Started with docker FailedSync Error syncing pod, skipping: failed to delete containers ([exit status 1]) ~~~- Pods stuck in `Error`, `Terminating`, or `DeadlineExceeded` state prevent scaling up of application ~~~ # oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE default-build-4-build 0/1 Error 0 3d default-deployment-5-qfjpl 1/1 Running 0 4d default-deployment-6-deploy 0/1 Error 0 3d default-node-sti-app-2-build 0/1 Completed 0 5h default-node-sti-app-3-build 0/1 Completed 0 2h default-node-sti-app-4-build 1/1 Running 0 1h default-node-sti-app-5-build 0/1 Completed 0 51m default-nodejs-1-deploy 0/1 Error 0 4d default-nodejs-2-deploy 0/1 DeadlineExceeded 0 5h default-nodejs-5-deploy 0/1 Error 0 1h default-nodejs-5-yt724 0/1 Terminating 0 1h default-nodejs-8-n4aj1 1/1 Running 0 49m ~~~- Failure to create pods due to `exceeding quota` error messages ~~~ 1h 1h 3 default-nodejs-5 ReplicationController FailedCreate {replication-controller} Error creating: Pod "default-nodejs-5-" is forbidden: [limited to 6 pods, unable to admit pod without exceeding quota for resource cpu: limited to 3 but require 3500m to succeed.] ~~~
resolution: In Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3.1, a few strategies can help alleviate the resource consumption issue.- Delete excess pods which are consuming a portion of the resource limits. Pods that are stuck in `Terminating` or `Failed` status can be force-deleted with the `--grace-period=0` option. ~~~ # oc delete pod--grace-period=0 ~~~- Modify the resource quotas in the Deployment Configuration to higher values. ~~~ # oc edit dc/... strategy: resources: limits: cpu: memory:... ~~~ NOTE: Over-committing memory can cause issues in some environments. For more information on quotas in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3.1, please view the [Developer Guide](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/dev_guide/compute_resources.html). The ability to quota time-bound vs long-running pods is included in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3.2. This allows greater flexibility with resource quotas and ensures deployment pods no longer count against the resource limit of the application. Build and deployer pods have an active deadline (meaning they are bound to complete in a specified time), and therefore they can now be charged under a time-bound quota. Long running apps that have a more permanent footprint can go under the long-running quota. More examples and information on quotas and the new quota types in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3.2 will soon be available in the [OpenShift Enterprise Dev Guide](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.2/dev_guide/compute_resources.html). This information can currently be found on [GitHub](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-docs/pull/2086).
root_cause: Setting resource limits on deployments can be used to prevent applications from consuming too many resources; however, in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3.1, deployment pods count against these limits, which can prevent them from being able to deploy another application pod if the limit is reached when the deployment pod runs.

title: Docker Registry Filling Up Storage in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise 3
issue: - `/var/lib/docker` is consuming large amounts of storage. Why is docker using `/var/lib/docker/container` and not the volume group/logical volume we have assigned to it?- We have set up docker to use a logical volume for storage as follows, yet it still uses `/var/lib/docker/` for storage ~~~ cat /etc/sysconfig/docker-storage DOCKER_STORAGE_OPTIONS=--storage-driver devicemapper--storage-opt dm.fs=xfs--storage-opt dm.thinpooldev=/dev/mapper/docker-docker--pool--storage-opt dm.use_deferred_removal=true ~~~ and ~~~ cat /etc/sysconfig/docker-storage-setup # Edit this file to override any configuration options specified in # /usr/lib/docker-storage-setup/docker-storage-setup. # # For more details refer to "man docker-storage-setup" VG=docker ~~~- When `/var/lib/docker` fills up, it fills up the entire root partition and makes the system inoperative.
resolution: Metadata is stored separately, in `/var/lib/docker`. Often, a large portion of storage is used by Docker logs. To remedy this, create a log rotation job that rotates the logs. ~~~ # cat /etc/logrotate.d/docker-logrotate /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*.log {rotate 7 daily compress create 0600 root root missingok notifempty} ~~~
root_cause: When setting up storage with `/etc/sysconfig/docker-storage`, and `/etc/sysconfig/docker-storage-setup`, this will result in the images and containers being saved on the logical volume or other storage setup indicated. However, Docker uses `/var/lib/docker/` for meta-data on the containers and images. For instance, container logs are stored in `/var/lib/docker/containers/*/*.log`.

title: Automatically Deploy Router and/or Registry During Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise Ansible Install
issue: - How do you automatically deploy the router or registry during the Advanced Installation method for Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise?- Designating or choosing a node in installation for router or registry using selectors, regions, or other labels- Automate the setup of the Docker Registry during the Ansible installation
resolution: The ansible hosts file can be configured, as per the [Advanced Installation](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/install_config/install/advanced_install.html) instructions, to automatically deploy the registry and router on a specific node or nodes. The default router and registry selector is `region=infra`. Therefore, a node provided with the label `region=infra` in the Ansible hosts file will cause the installer to deploy a router and registry on that node: ~~~ [nodes] node1.example.com openshift_node_labels="{'region': 'infra'}" ~~~- This example will result in a router and registry deployed on the `node1.example.com` node. Alternatively, customized label can be used to configure what node(s) the router and/or registry will be deployed on.- Add a router selector label to the `vars` section of the Ansible `hosts` file with a custom selector ~~~ [OSEv3:vars]... openshift_router_selector='purpose=router' ~~~- Add the matching selector label to the intended node ~~~ [nodes] node1.example.com openshift_node_labels="{'purpose': 'router'}" node2.example.com openshift_node_labels="{'region':'infra'}" ~~~- This example will result in the router being deployed on `node1.example.com` and the registry deployed on `node2.example.com`. Note: the installer will deploy a replica to every node with a matching label, such that there will be an equal number of replicas to nodes with the matching selector The installation documentation for the [Advanced Installation](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/install_config/install/advanced_install.html#configuring-host-variables) currently only contains information on using the "region=infra" label with the default router and registry labels. A documentation bug is under progress in [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1321673) with further information on [GitHub](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-docs/pull/1797). By default, the registry will only deploy if an existing NFS volume is specified for registry storage. A bug is under progress in [Bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1316868) to allow an empty directory as a default registry storage.

title: Red Hat Openshift Online - [ALERT] Proxy express has no server available
issue: - My servers are down and I am unable to bring them up: ~~~ [ALERT] 005/015432 (350193): proxy 'express' has no server available! [WARNING] 005/020435 (350193): Server express/local-gear is DOWN for maintenance. [WARNING] 005/020435 (472765): config: log format ignored for proxy 'stats' since it has no log address. [WARNING] 005/020435 (472765): config: log format ignored for proxy 'express' since it has no log address. [WARNING] 005/020435 (472765): Server express/local-gear is DOWN, reason: Layer7 wrong status, code: 404, info: "Not Found", check duration: 0ms. 0 active and 0 backup servers left. 0 sessions active, 0 requeued, 0 remaining in queue. [ALERT] 005/020435 (472765): proxy 'express' has no server available! [WARNING] 005/021114 (472765): Server express/local-gear is DOWN for maintenance. [WARNING] 005/021124 (472765): Server express/local-gear is UP (leaving maintenance). [WARNING] 005/021130 (472765): Server express/local-gear is DOWN, reason: Layer7 wrong status, code: 404, info: "Not Found", check duration: 4875ms. 0 active and 0 backup servers left. 0 sessions active, 0 requeued, 0 remaining in queue. [ALERT] 005/021130 (472765): proxy 'express' has no server available! ~~~- Cannot access or login to my high availability application- Gear is stuck down for maintenance
resolution: Ensure that the HAProxy is able to perform health checks on the application:- `ssh` into the main gear of the application. ~~~ $ rhc ssh [appname] ~~~- Update the `haproxy conf`: change the `httpchk GET` option from `/` to a valid location, such as an `index.html` or `index.jsp` file ~~~ $ cd ~/haproxy/conf $ vim haproxy.cfg... option httpchk GET /path/to/viable/resource... ~~~- Restart the `HAProxy` ~~~ $ rhc cartridge-restart--cartridge haproxy ~~~- Verify the status of your gears by going to http://-.rhcloud.com/haproxy-status
root_cause: Applications with scaling enabled utilize a High Availability Proxy (HAProxy) to perform health checks and other maintenance related to scaling. The health check URL identified in `haproxy.cfg` is contacted via the loopback IP on the gear. If the health check URL is inaccessible or otherwise non-valid (does not return a 200 status message on a curl over the loopback interface), the gear will fail the health check.

title: Issues when adding PVC with EFK Stack (ElasticSearch, FluentD, Kibana) in Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise
issue: - Errors when adding Persistent Volume Claim to the EFK stack.- Problem connecting to ElasticSearch- Storage issues with ElasticSearch ~~~ Kibana: Unknown error while connecting to Elasticsearch Error: Unknown error while connecting to Elasticsearch Error: No Living connections at sendReqWithConnection (https://kibana.example.com/index.js?_b=7562:85228:15) at next (https://kibana.example.com/index.js?_b=7562:83728:7) at https://kibana.example.com/index.js?_b=7562:52806:21 ~~~
resolution: When making changes to the EFK stack (particularly ElasticSearch and FluentD), each of these should be scaled down to 0 prior to making changes to configuration. Then they can be scaled back up, making sure to scale up FluentD shortly after scaling up ElasticSearch.- Scale down the deployments ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=0 dc/ dc/ ~~~- Make changes to the deployment configurations, like adding persistent volume claims.- Scale up ElasticSearch and FluentD ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=# dc/ $ oc scale--replicas=# dc/ ~~~

title: How to make the pv-recycler pod run on specific nodes for NFS PV's
issue: - Not all nodes in our environment have NFS access. So when OpenShift schedules a pv-recycler pod, it ends up on nodes which don't have any NFS access. This causes the recycle to fail. How can we modify the configuration to make the pv-recycler run in a particular region?- I want to limit the pv-recycler pod to specific nodes
resolution: ###IMPORTANT: This Will Only Work For Persistent Volumes Backed By NFS #### NOTE: As of [OpenShift Container Platform 3.6](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.6/architecture/additional_concepts/storage.html#recycling), the recyclerpod has been deprecated in favor of [dynamic provisioning](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.6/install_config/persistent_storage/dynamically_provisioning_pvs.html). This means that in versions 3.6, and moving forward, this will not be usable as the pod itself does not exist. First, add the `pv-recycler-pod-template-filepath-nfs` setting into the /etc/origin/master/master-config.yaml file: ~~~... kubernetesMasterConfig:... controllerArguments: ###This should likely already exist, find it before just making a new one pv-recycler-pod-template-filepath-nfs:- "/root/pv-recycle-template.json"... ~~~- The file and it's location do not really matter because the next step is to create that file, and as long as you are consistent the system will work. Next, create the file from the first step, i.e. `/root/pv-recycle-template.json` ###For OpenShift Enterprise Versions 3.1-3.2 and OpenShift Container Platform 3.3, please use this example, for versions 3.4+ please use the [second example](#34example): ~~~ # cat /root/pv-recycle-template.json {"apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "Pod", "metadata": {"name": "nfs-scrubber", "namespace":"default"}, "spec": {"nodeSelector": {"region": "myexample" ###NOTE:please replace this key:value pair with the node selector you have in mind}, "volumes": [{"name": "vol", "nfs": {}}], "containers": [{"name": "pv-recycler", "image": "registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ose-recycler", "command": ["/bin/sh"], "args": ["-c", "test-e /scrub && echo $(date) > /scrub/trash.txt && find /scrub-mindepth 1-maxdepth 1-delete && test-z \"$(ls-A /scrub)\" || exit 1"], "resources": {}, "volumeMounts": [{"name": "vol", "mountPath": "/scrub"}], "terminationMessagePath": "/dev/termination-log", "imagePullPolicy": "IfNotPresent"}], "restartPolicy": "Never", "terminationGracePeriodSeconds": 30, "activeDeadlineSeconds": 300, "securityContext": {}}} ~~~ ####OpenShift Container Platform version 3.4+ template example: {#34example}- the differences are the namespace the pod runs in has changed from "default" to "openshift-infra" and we have added the need for a serviceaccount (near the bottom of the template) ~~~ {"apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "Pod", "metadata": {"name": "nfs-scrubber", "namespace": "openshift-infra"}, "spec": {"nodeSelector": {"region": "myexample" ###NOTE:please replace this key:value pair with the node selector you have in mind}, "volumes": [{"name": "vol", "nfs": {}}], "containers": [{"name": "pv-recycler", "image": "registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ose-recycler", "command": ["/bin/sh"], "args": ["-c", "test-e /scrub && echo $(date) > /scrub/trash.txt && find /scrub-mindepth 1-maxdepth 1-delete && test-z \"$(ls-A /scrub)\" || exit 1"], "resources": {}, "volumeMounts": [{"name": "vol", "mountPath": "/scrub"}], "terminationMessagePath": "/dev/termination-log", "imagePullPolicy": "IfNotPresent"}], "restartPolicy": "Never", "terminationGracePeriodSeconds": 30, "activeDeadlineSeconds": 300, "serviceAccountName": "pv-recycler-controller"}} ~~~ As the note above indicates, you will need to change key:value pair under the nodeSelector. You should change it to match the labels you have set on your desired nodes. Finally, after you have created the file and modified the master config file, all you should need to do is restart your master service(s) and the change should take impact and the next PersistentVolume that needs to be recycled should work fine (from the standpoint that the recycler should be deployed to nodes with NFS access).

title: History of events in Red Hat Openshift 3
issue: - Is it possible to retrieve the full history of events for a given project in Openshift?- Why after a few days, the events tab inside a project is empty?
resolution: - Events are high-volume. Making them persistent is known to put a significant load on ETCD, and is not recommended. Events have a 2-hour lifespan by default. It is possible to adjust this in the `master-config.yaml` file settings: ~~~ kubernetesMasterConfig:... apiServerArguments: "event-ttl": ["3h"] ~~~- There is a [RFE](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1287512) for logging events, or having CFME pull event history every so often and performing roll-ups on the events.

title: Multicast support in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3
issue: - It is possible to communicate, via multicast, between OSE pods?- Is Multicast suppported on Openshift
resolution: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.5 introduces multicast support. Pods can now send or receive traffic with other pods subscribed to the same multicast group. Important, multicast is best used for low bandwidth coordination or service discovery and not a high-bandwidth solution. More information can be found in [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 3.5- Release Notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.5/release_notes/ocp_3_5_release_notes.html#ocp-35-networking) and [Managing Networking Guide](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.5/admin_guide/managing_networking.html#admin-guide-networking-multicast). To use multicast, the OpenShift SDN plugin should be ovs-multitenant or ovs-networkplugin. It cannot be used with ovs-subnet.

title: Occasionally pods fails to start and the message "SELinux: mount invalid.  Same superblock, different security settings for (dev dm-N, type xfs) is seen in the logs
issue: Occasionally pods fails to start and the message "SELinux: mount invalid. Same superblock, different security settings for (dev dm-N, type xfs) is seen in the logs. From the logs ~~~ Apr 06 14:49:45 localhost kernel: SELinux: mount invalid. Same superblock, different security settings for (dev dm-9, type xfs) Apr 06 14:49:45 localhost docker[3946]: time="2016-04-06T14:49:45.272036708+02:00" level=error msg="Error unmounting device ac58004eea05c383f6bd633f6822a182f17d073a0fe36bf4c87f522224a02c7d: UnmountDevice: device not-mounted id ac58004eea05c383f6bd633f6822a182f17d073a0fe36bf4c87f522224a02c7d" Apr 06 14:49:45 localhost docker[3946]: time="2016-04-06T14:49:45.272224632+02:00" level=error msg="HTTP Error" err="Cannot start container ac58004eea05c383f6bd633f6822a182f17d073a0fe36bf4c87f522224a02c7d: Error getting container ac58004eea05c383f6bd633f6822a182f17d073a0fe36bf4c87f522224a02c7d from driver devicemapper: Error mounting '/dev/mapper/docker-253:0-68067266-ac58004eea05c383f6bd633f6822a182f17d073a0fe36bf4c87f522224a02c7d' on '/var/lib/docker/devicemapper/mnt/ac58004eea05c383f6bd633f6822a182f17d073a0fe36bf4c87f522224a02c7d': invalid argument" statusCode=500 ~~~

title: How to use local Nexus mirror for EAP s2i in OpenShift
issue: - EAP s2i build downloading dependencies phase is slow- How to use local Nexus mirror for EAP s2i in OpenShift?
resolution: To create Nexus local mirror:- Create Nexus instance, expose it- **NOTE:** The `sonatype/nexus` container image is community image, not a Red Hat provided image. Using this image is at your own risk.- `oc new-app sonatype/nexus`- Or create it from yaml manifest with persistent volume example:- `oc expose service nexus`- Open nexus web UI- Login with `admin/admin123`- Go to Repositories tab, add, Proxy Repository, add a repo "redhat" with Red Hat Maven repository URL- If you have other repository, repeat this step and add it to Nexus- Go to Repositories tab, add, Repository Group, add a group repo (mirror repo) "main" with your required Maven repos For EAP s2i image you can add the following to your BuildConfig to enable the mirror: ~~~ spec: strategy: sourceStrategy: env:- name: MAVEN_MIRROR_URL value: http://$NEXUS_URL/content/groups/main/ ~~~

title: Recovering from deleting /var/lib/docker
issue: If you are using device mapper (instead of loopback), **/var/lib/docker*

contains metadata informing docker about the contents of the device mapper storage area. If you delete **/var/lib/docker**, that metadata is lost. In this case, docker detects that the thin pool has data, but docker is unable to make use of that information. The only solution is to delete the thin pool and recreate it so that both the thin pool and the metadata in **/var/lib/docker*
will be empty.
resolution: If **/var/lib/docker** is deleted and device mapper, rather than loopback storage, is being used, you must delete and recreate the thin pool in order for the docker service to be able to start up again.
root_cause: When the /var/lib/docker directory structure is deleted, when you try to restart the docker service without deleting the old thin pool, the following error appears: level=fatal msg="Error starting daemon: error initializing graphdriver: Unable to take ownership of thin-pool (dockerVG-docker--pool) that already has used data blocks"

title: Limitations for deploying OpenStack using the QuickStart Cloud Installer
issue: - Are there any limitations when deploying OpenStack using QCI- What are the limitations for deploying OpenStack
resolution: Deploying Red Hat OpenStack Platform using the QuickStart Cloud Installer introduce some limitations:- Isolating networks is not supported.- High availability is not supported.- OpenShift Enterprise is currently not supported on Red Hat OpenStack Platform.

title: OpenShift 3.2 and Docker 1.10
issue: - Will Docker 1.10 be certified / supported with OpenShift 3.2- Why is Docker 1.10 not supported with OpenShift 3.2
resolution: Docker 1.10 is supported / tested by Red Hat on OpenShift 3.2, as of the OpenShift 3.2.1 release. Please see the [Supported and Tested Configurations Matrix](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2176281) for more information, on this.- **Note**: It is recommended that customer running a version less than 3.2 of OpenShift add the following to their /etc/yum.conf files. ~~~ exclude= docker*1.10* ~~~- This will help avoid unintended updates to docker that may not be supported or tested with OpenShift version less than 3.2 version.- More information on the [supported / tested configuration](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2176281).)

title: Docker pull from private v2 registry fails with image not found
issue: Docker pull is not working, even though image exists in registry ~~~ # docker pull registry.example.com:5000/myrhel7 Using default tag: latest Trying to pull repository registry.example.com:5000/myrhel7... not found Error: image myrhel7:latest not found ~~~

docker pull fails with image not found, and docker daemon debug logs show the following error: ~~~ level=debug msg="Error trying v2 registry: Get http://registry.example.com:5000/v2/myrhel7/manifests/latest: no basic auth credentials" ~~~- [Using oreg_url in hosts doesn't work if private registry requires authentication](https://github.com/openshift/origin/issues/13918)
resolution: Authentication is configured on the registry, and `docker login` needs to be performed against the registry ~~~ # docker login-u user registry.example.redhat.com:5000 Password: Email: WARNING: login credentials saved in /root/.docker/config.json Login Succeeded # docker pull registry.example.com:5000/myrhel7 Using default tag: latest Trying to pull repository registry.example.com:5000/myrhel7... latest: Pulling from myrhel7 db4d6140b375: Pull complete Digest: sha256:bf54eba0767f4cfd65f37555899f1067e27fc5ed0f63513f37a8258f48e87eb3 Status: Downloaded newer image for registry.example.com:5000/myrhel7:latest ~~~ Also note that the a `docker login` will produce output which can be save in the host file ` /var/lib/openshift/.docker/config.json` and these will be picked up by a deployment (`deploymentConfig`). The below ansible script shows an example of creating for two registries. ~~~---- hosts: all gather_facts: no tasks:- name: create docker dir file: path: /var/lib/openshift/.docker state: directory- name: populate config.json copy: dest: /var/lib/openshift/.docker/config.json content: | {"auths": {"registry00.com:5000": {"auth": "token generated from manual login"}, "registry01.com:5000": {"auth": "token generated from manual login"}}} ~~~
root_cause: The registry configuration in /etc/docker-distribution/registry/config.yml had authentication enabled ~~~ version: 0.1 log: fields: service: registry storage: cache: layerinfo: inmemory filesystem: rootdirectory: /var/lib/registry http: addr::5000 auth: htpasswd: realm: example.com path: /path/to/htpasswd ~~~

title: OpenShift error: rhel-7-server-ose-3.1-rpms is not a valid repository ID
issue: - In OpenShift 3.1, the command `subscription-manager repos--enable="rhel-7-server-ose-3.1-rpms"` is failing- Error message reads `Error: rhel-7-server-ose-3.1-rpms is not a valid repository ID. Use--list option to see valid repositories.`- Acccess to certain repositories may need to be enabled via `subscription-manager'
resolution: List available subscriptions running: ~~~ subscription-manager list--available ~~~ Note the pool ID associated with an OpenShift subscription and run: ~~~ subscription-manager attach--pool= ~~~ Now running the following should work without error: ~~~ subscription-manager repos--enable="rhel-7-server-ose-3.1-rpms" ~~~

title: Pods fail to start when pulling an image from a private container registry
issue: - In OpenShift 3.1, pods fail to start because they are not able to pull the new image from the private container registry- The error message reads: ~~~ Failed to pull image / /:: image pull failed for / /:, this may be because there are no credentials on this request. details: (Error: image /: not found) ~~~
resolution: Private container registries typically secured and require authentication. The pods are failing to start because the secrets for the private container registry have not been configured. To pull a secured Docker-formatted container image that is not from OpenShift’s integrated registry, create a configuration secret and add it to the service account. If a `.dockercfg` file exists for the secured registry, a secret from that file can be created by running: ~~~ $ oc secrets new.dockercfg= ~~~ If a `$HOME/.docker/config.json` (for newer docker clients) file exists for the secured registry, a secret from that file can be created by running: ~~~ $ oc secrets new.dockerconfigjson= ~~~ If a `.dockercfg` file does not already exist, create a secret by running: ~~~ $ oc secrets new-dockercfg \--docker-server=--docker-username= \--docker-password=--docker-email= ~~~ To use a secret for pulling images for pods, add the secret to the service account. The name of the service account in this example should match the name of the service account the pod will use; default is the default service account: ~~~ $ oc secrets add serviceaccount/default secrets/--for=pull ~~~ To use a secret for pushing and pulling build images, the secret must be mountable inside of a pod. Accomplished by running: ~~~ $ oc secrets add serviceaccount/builder secrets/ ~~~ Reference: [Allowing Pods to Reference Images from Other Secured Registries](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/dev_guide/image_pull_secrets.html#allowing-pods-to-reference-images-from-other-secured-registries)

title: How to use degree symbol in RHEL6 ?
issue: Not able to use `degree` symbol in RHEL6
`Ctrl+Shift+u00b0` key combination is not working to add degree symbol in the system
resolution: * Degree symbol comes from locale `en_US.iso88591`, so need to set `en_US.iso88591` as default locale for the system. * Edit `/etc/sysconfig/i18n` as below to set `en_US.iso88591` as default locale. ~~~ [root@localhost]# cat /etc/sysconfig/i18n LANG="en_US.iso88591" SYSFONT="latarcyrheb-sun16" ~~~ * Please edit `/etc/sysconfig/i18n` if LANG parameter is not set to `en_US.iso88591`. * After making above changes restart the gdm. ~~~ [root@localhost]#pkill gdm-binary ~~~ * `Ctrl+Shift+u00b0` is key combination to use degree symbol. * Above changes are not required in RHEL7, key combination `Ctrl+Shift+u00b0` should provide the degree symbol.
root_cause: * Degree symbol is provided by locale `en_US.iso88591` and the default locale set is `en_US.UTF-8`.

title: Add variables to a file on several OpenShift nodes using Ansible
issue: - How to configure kubeletArguments via Ansible- We have several nodes to apply this change, is there a way to configure all nodes via Ansible?- I want to make the same change to all of my servers config files easily
resolution: The following command adds some of the [Garbage Collector](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/admin_guide/garbage_collection.html) variables into the /etc/node/node-config.yaml file and restarts the atomic-openshift-node service to let the new settings take effect. I have explained the command below. ~~~ ansible-m shell-a 'sed-i "$ a\kubeletArguments:" /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml;sed-i "$ a\ maximum-dead-containers-per-container:" /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml;sed-i "$ a\- '\'2\'' " /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml;sed-i "$ a\ maximum-dead-containers:" /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml;sed-i "$ a\- '\'25\'' " /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml; systemctl restart atomic-openshift-node' all ~~~ 1. The `ansible-m shell` portion of the command makes use of the shell module for Ansible. You can see the rest of the modules [here.](http://docs.ansible.com/ansible/modules_by_category.html) 2. The `-a` allows you to specify arguments for the module. In this case you are specifying the shell commands to run-- Using `sed`, you can then specify what to add, where to add it, and in what file ~~~ A sed-i "$ a\kubeletArguments:" /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml B sed-i "$ a\ maximum-dead-containers-per-container:" /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml C sed-i "$ a\- '\'2\'' " /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml D sed-i "$ a\ maximum-dead-containers:" /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml E sed-i "$ a\- '\'25\'' " /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml F systemctl restart atomic-openshift-node' ~~~ 2.A. This command edits the file in place and finds the last line of the file, and then adds `kubeletArguments:` after that last line inside the /etc/origin/node/node-config.yaml file. (for further details on sed, please refer to `man sed`). 2.B-E. These all do the same as A, except the "last line of the file" becomes the previous addition. 2.F. Is used to restart the atomic-openshift-node service

title: Does the Red Hat OpenShift subscription include CloudForms?
issue: - We have OpenShift subscription. Do we need to buy CloudForms subscription separately to support the OpenShift-related infrastructure?
resolution: - OpenShift customers receive the right to use CloudForms to manage OpenShift-related infrastructure and nodes for OpenShift-related tasks.- The OpenShift Broker Infrastructure SKU now provides a CloudForms entitlement along with it, giving customers access to download and use the CloudForms appliance, subject to the right to use agreement.- They should purchase addition OpenShift broker/master SKU for their CloudForms instance since they will need those to attach to the node they plan on deploying CloudForms.- The integration requires OpenShift 3.1 and CloudForms 4.0.

title: Pods hung in Pending after deploy
issue: - After deploying pods in OpenShift, some pods never recover from Pending status- Pods are showing as Pending in the OpenShift web console- Pods are showing as Pending in the OpenShift command-line interface (CLI) tool
resolution: Retry the last deployment, if it is in a failed state: ~~~ $ oc deploy--retry ~~~ If retry fails, cancel an in-progress deployment at any time: ~~~ $ oc deploy--cancel ~~~ To kick off a new deployment, if there is no pending deployment: ~~~ $ oc deploy--latest ~~~ To remove pods stuck in pending or terminating, see [How to delete pods stuck in pending or terminating](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2259041).
root_cause: This behavior may be associated with a [known issue with Kubernetes](https://github.com/openshift/origin/issues/4398)

title: How to extract the S2I scripts out of a Red Hat OpenShift Image
issue: - When creating a project, we want to create the ".sti/bin/assemble" script, that [overwrite's the original script](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/dev_guide/builds.html#override-builder-image-scripts) from the image. However, would like to base our script off that of the "original" image.- How can I get the content of the original script, be pulled from the image?- Can the our custom script be merged with the original script?
resolution: There are natural complexities, with merging two files, such as what file gets precipitance if there is a conflict or if you go with an includes method (an ordering has to be defined). The approach in [S2I](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/dev_guide/builds.html#override-builder-image-scripts) is the simplest way to solve a lot of these complexities. However it in order to overwrite the original file, based on what the current images provides, you need to first pull the [scripts](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/creating_images/s2i.html#s2i-scripts) from a running image, that you plan to use. ~~~ # oc new-application # oc rsync:/usr/local/s2i/assemble. ### Note the "." in this command is the "current" directory. ~~~

title: Using Redis as the Http Session store for JBoss servers
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - I am looking for a solution to enable session replication in the JBoss Cluster in our PaaS platform. In our current setup JGroups clustering (Infinispan) uses for session replication (the Red Hat JBoss EAP image default). I am looking for a solution to use Redis as the Http Session store for the web applications deployed in JBoss servers.
resolution: By default we only offer support for the provided EAP functionality and clustering through the "infinispan and jgroups" subystems. [Similar requests](http://infinispan.org/docs/8.1.x/user_guide/user_guide.html#_persistence) to this have been [made in the community](https://issues.jboss.org/browse/WFLY-1898) and were *rejected*, as infinispan provides the caching layer needed for clustering in JBoss. Because of this and our [support policy](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/production/soc) to **not** provide support for *Code development* or *System and network design*, this request would fall out side of the scope of support and as such we can provide little information or guidance on this other than to use the default clustering implementation provided with the images and EAP product. If you have issues with these technologies or tools, we can file issues and/or bugs to work to address your concerns, however we can *not* provide a supported suggestion or guidance to your current request.

title: Configuring CORS filter on the default Jetty Server on Fuse-6.1
issue: - We would like to know how you would configure the `CORS filters` on Fuse default Jetty server. There are certain REST services on Fuse that we want to be accessed over ajax on a web application.- The `@CrossOriginResourceSharing` annotation on our REST interfaces work if we shift our services to an embedded jetty configuration. However we want the REST services to run on the default jetty but when we do that the `@CrossOriginResourceSharing` annotation is not picked up and the ajax call fails saying `(Reason: CORS header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' missing)`.- The jetty documentation says that CORS configuration is done over web.xml. How does that relate to the default jetty on Fuse as we don't see any web.xml open for configuration. The only configuration we see is in `/etc/jetty.xml`.
resolution: - There is an `enableCORS` parameter that is available in camel-rest-dsl, [http://camel.apache.org/rest-dsl.html](http://camel.apache.org/rest-dsl.html), starting camel version 2.15. Hence, this is available in Fuse 6.2.1.- For the earlier versions, you will manually have to add CORS headers to the response. You can do this with the following code below, ~~~ ** * @author Viral Gohel * */ @Provider public class CORSFilter implements ContainerResponseFilter {/* * (non-Javadoc) * * @see javax.ws.rs.container.ContainerResponseFilter#filter(javax.ws.rs. * container.ContainerRequestContext, * javax.ws.rs.container.ContainerResponseContext) */ public void filter(ContainerRequestContext requestContext, ContainerResponseContext responseContext) throws IOException {responseContext.getHeaders().add("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"); responseContext.getHeaders().add("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "origin, content-type, accept, authorization"); responseContext.getHeaders().add("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", "true"); responseContext.getHeaders().add("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, HEAD"); responseContext.getHeaders().add("Access-Control-Max-Age", "1209600");}} ~~~- You can then register the above class in ` ` or if using camel-cxf transport, in ` `.- There is also a quickstart, `/jboss-fuse-6.1.0.redhat-379/quickstarts/secure-soap`, which has a class, `EnableCORSInterceptor.java`.

title: Listing image tags for Red Hat's Container Registry
issue: - How do I list all the tags for Red Hat Container Images on `registry.access.redhat.com`
resolution: - Currently `registry.access.redhat.com` accepts most v1 and v2 api calls. ***Registry v1 API*** To list information on an image's tags use the following: `https://registry.access.redhat.com/v1/repositories/(namespace)/(repository)/tags`- Example:- Curl: `# curl-s https://registry.access.redhat.com/v1/repositories/rhel7/tags`- Browser: `https://registry.access.redhat.com/v1/repositories/rhel7/tags` See documentation for [Registry API v1](https://docs.docker.com/v1.6/reference/api/registry_api/) for more information. ***Registry v2 API*** To list information on an image's tags use the following: `https://registry.access.redhat.com/v2/(namespace)/(repository)/tags/list`- Curl: `# curl-sL https://registry.access.redhat.com/v2/rhel7/tags/list`- Browser: `https://registry.access.redhat.com/v2/rhel7/tags/list` See documentation for [Registry API v2](https://github.com/docker/distribution/blob/release/2.4/docs/spec/api.md) for more information.
