title: How to verify OpenShift Container Platform has been deployed successfully
issue: - I have deployed an OpenShift environment. How can I validate this environment in order to:
verify my deployment confirms to Red Hat recommended configurations?

confirm my deployment has workarounds or solutions applied for known problems?- Is there a checklist that I can go through to verify whether this environment will hit any known problems in the future?- What are the best practices for configuring OpenShift services to avoid problems?- What are common problems I can avoid in an OpenShift environment?- Verify OpenShift Environment before starting Deployment- OpenShift Cluster limits- OpenShift v3 Scaling, Performance and Capacity Planning- Capacity planning for OpenShift- Best practices and recommendations for OpenShift planning
resolution: **Note:** This is not a complete list, but is intended to help verify that the OpenShift environment is correctly installed. Before starting with the installation, be sure to follow the [prerequisites](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#prerequisites-1) for the installation. ####OpenShift Enterprise Tested Integrations- Red Hat provides both production and development support for the tested integration's in the same major version family at or above the tested version according to your subscription agreement. Earlier versions of a tested integration in the same major version family are supported on a commercially reasonable basis. For more information please refer [OpenShift Enterprise Tested Integrations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2176281). ####OpenShift v3 Scaling, Performance and Capacity Planning- OpenShift is a platform-as-a-service (PaaS) product built on open source software including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Kubernetes, the docker container runtime, etcd and OpenvSwitch. From the HAproxy routing layer down through the kernel itself, there are opportunities to push the limits of scale and performance at each level in the product stack. Please refer [Best Practices and Recommendations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2191731). ####Before installation- A [base installation of Red Hat Enterprise Linux](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#system-requirements) (RHEL) 7.2 or later is required for master or node hosts with "Minimal" installation option.- Each host must be [registered using Red Hat Subscription Manager (RHSM)](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#host-preparation) and have an active OpenShift Enterprise subscription attached to access the required packages.Note: [OpenShift 3 rpm's is only available on CDN Red Hat Subscription Manager](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1488483). The hosts must have the below repo list: # yum repolist rhel-7-server-extras-rpms rhel-7-server-ose-3.1-rpms rhel-7-server-rpms- Required packages are installed: # yum install wget git net-tools bind-utils iptables-services bridge-utils bash-completion atomic-openshift-utils- Add the following option in `/etc/sysconfig/docker` file: OPTIONS='--selinux-enabled--insecure-registry 172.30.0.0/16'- Restart the docker service: # systemctl restart docker- Configuring [docker storage](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.1/install_config/install/prerequisites.html#configuring-docker-storage) and check the status of docker. # systemctl status docker ● docker.service- Docker Application Container Engine Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/docker.service; enabled; vendor preset: disabled) Drop-In: /usr/lib/systemd/system/docker.service.d └─docker-sdn-ovs.conf Active: active (running) since Wed 2015-11-25 17:38:35 IST; 1 day 17h ago Docs: http://docs.docker.com Main PID: 125076 (docker) CGroup: /system.slice/docker.service └─125076 /usr/bin/docker daemon--insecure-registry=172.30.0.0/16--selinux-enabled--storage-driver devicemapper--storage-opt dm.fs=xfs--storage-opt dm.thinpooldev=/dev/mapper/dock...- [ssh passwordless login](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#ensuring-host-access) between master and node hosts. The quick and advanced installation methods require a user that has access to all hosts.- DNS resolution of master and node hosts. This can be checked as below by running the below command on all hosts. ~~~ dig dig dig ~~~- One can also refer below article for example configuartion of DNS to work with Openshift v3: [How to configure DNS to work with Openshift v3](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2097731)- Enviroment requirements can be seen in the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#envirornment-requirements) where one need to make sure there are certain pods that needs to be opened between master and nodes under Section:2.2.3.2. Network Access(Required Ports)- One can then continue with either [Quick installation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#quick-installation) or [Advanced installation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#advanced-installation). ####After Installation####- One can check if the installation is done successfully by running the below command. In case it fails one can check ansible logs in `/tmp/ansible.log` to see what failed. ~~~ oc get nodes NAME LABELS STATUS AGE master.oselab.com kubernetes.io/hostname=10.65.4.z Ready,SchedulingDisabled 2d node1.oselab.com kubernetes.io/hostname=10.65.4.y Ready 2d node2.oselab.com kubernetes.io/hostname=10.65.4.x Ready 2d ~~~ ####Validating Master and node configuration#### Commands to validate master and node configuration files with OSE 3.1. ~~~ openshift ex validate master-config /path/to/master-config.yaml openshift ex validate node-config /path/to/node-config.yaml ~~~ ####Deploying a Red Hat Container Image Registry####- OpenShift can build docker-formatted images from source code, deploy them, and manage their lifecycle. To enable this, OpenShift provides an internal, integrated Red Hat Container Image Registry that can be deployed in your OpenShift environment to locally manage images. How to deploy registry with different options can be seen in the [Documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#deploy-registry). After successful deployment of registry you should be able to see the registry pod, service running as below: # oc get service NAME CLUSTER_IP EXTERNAL_IP PORT(S) SELECTOR AGE docker-registry 172.30.128.117 5000/TCP docker-registry=default 2d # oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE docker-registry-1-xrslo 1/1 Running 1 1d # oc get serviceAccount registry 3 2d- If it fails to deploy, then [further troubleshooting of the Internal Registry](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1616953) may be needed or run the following command: # openshift ex diagnostics-d ClusterRegistry ####Deploying a Router- The OpenShift router is the ingress point for all external traffic destined for services in your OpenShift installation. The oadm router command is provided with the administrator CLI to simplify the tasks of setting up routers in a new installation. A [service account for router has to be created]((https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#creating-the-router-service-account)) before installing the router. With OpenShift 3.1, it is created by default. Then continue with [deploying router](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.1/installation-and-configuration/#haproxy-router).- Once it successfully deployed, the router pod will show as running. In case it fails refer [link](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1542293#routing). # oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE router-1-cxjqs 1/1 Running 1 1d # oc get service NAME CLUSTER_IP EXTERNAL_IP PORT(S) SELECTOR AGE router 172.30.242.204 80/TCP router=router 2d ####Uninstall- For Quick installation: You can uninstall OpenShift using the installation utility by running: # atomic-openshift-installer uninstall- For Advanced installation: You can uninstall OpenShift by running the following Ansible playbook: # ansible-playbook /usr/share/ansible/openshift-ansible/playbooks/adhoc/uninstall.yml #### Working with HTTP Proxies Production environments can deny direct access to the Internet and instead have an HTTP or HTTPS proxy available. Configuring OpenShift to use these proxies can be as simple as setting standard environment variables in configuration or JSON files. To configure this one can refer [Documentaion](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/3.1/installation-and-configuration/chapter-12-working-with-http-proxies) ####Basic Troubleshooting- [Troubleshooting OpenShift Enterprise 3](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1542293)- [Common issues with OpenShift Enterprise 3](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1599603)- [How to prevent docker registry getting corrupt](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2203561)- [How to handle node overcommitment in OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2205821) ####Using Custom Images in OpenShift- Frequently, users want to use their own custom images but are unable to import to the OpenShift registry. Users need to perform extra steps to import the image to the OpenShift registry. Reference: [How to import an image from a local Red hat Container Image Registry into OpenShift registry](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2072843) ####Enable metrics for OpenShift- To collect the node, pod, and container metrics, it is required to run the OpenShift Metrics services inside your cluster. For more information on how to configure refer [link](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2137531)

title: OpenShift HA broker is slow during failover
issue: When a MongoDB replicaset member goes down, the API starts responding much slower. Is this normal or it can be fixed?
resolution: There can be slowness until a new mongo master is elected, after [30 seconds](https://docs.mongodb.org/v3.0/faq/replica-sets/#how-long-does-replica-set-failover-take) performance should return to normal. If this does not happen please open a support case with Red Hat Technical Support for a solution.
root_cause: In MongoDB just a single node can perform write requests and be the master. The [master heartbeat timeout](https://docs.mongodb.org/manual/core/replica-set-elections/) is 10 seconds. In a fail-over situation it can take [up to 30 seconds](https://docs.mongodb.org/v3.0/faq/replica-sets/#how-long-does-replica-set-failover-take) for elections to take place during which API performance will be affected. As the timeout is not configurable, it is not possible to change this behavior at the moment.

title: How to configure a persistent volume for the Integrated Docker Registry in OpenShift 3
issue: - How do I configure Integrated Docker Registry for production use in OpenShift Enterprise?
resolution: To add NFS a volume to your integrated Docker Registry for production follow these steps:- Create the exports in the [NFS Server](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-US/Red_Hat_Enterprise_Linux/7/html/Storage_Administration_Guide/nfs-serverconfig.html)- Create your Registry[2.5. Deploying a Docker Registry](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.0/openshift-enterprise-30-installation-and-configuration/chapter-2-installing) ~~~ # oadm registry--config=/etc/openshift/master/admin.kubeconfig--credentials=/etc/openshift/master/openshift-registry.kubeconfig--images='registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ose-${component}:${version}' ~~~- Create a persistent volume object to be used for you registry [Persistent Storage Using NFS](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.0/openshift-enterprise-30-administrator-guide/chapter-14-persistent-storage-using-nfs) ~~~ # oc create-f pv-registry.json # vim pv-registry.json {"apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "PersistentVolume", "metadata": {"name": "registry-volume"}, "spec": {"capacity": {"storage": "30Gi"}, "accessModes": ["ReadWriteMany"], "nfs": {"path": "/share/registry", "server": "172.17.0.2"}, "persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy": "Recycle"}} ~~~- Create a persistent volume claim in the default project to be bound to the Persistent Volume for use by your registry [Using Persistent Volumes](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en/openshift-enterprise/version-3.0/openshift-enterprise-30-developer-guide/chapter-15-using-persistent-volumes) ~~~ # oc create-f pvc-registry.json-n default ~~~ ~~~ # vim pvc-registry.json {"apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "PersistentVolumeClaim", "metadata": {"name": "registry-claim"}, "spec": {"volumeName": "registry-volume", "accessModes": ["ReadWriteMany"], "resources": {"requests": {"storage": "30Gi"}}}} ~~~- Make sure the Claim have bound to your Persistent Volume ~~~ # oc get pvc-n default NAME LABELS STATUS VOLUME AGE registry-claim map[] Bound registry-volume 1m ~~~- Add volume to registry ~~~ # oc set volume deploymentconfigs/docker-registry--add--overwrite--name=registry-storage--mount-path=/registry--type=persistentVolumeClaim--claim-name="registry-claim" ~~~- Test by pulling an image to your registry ~~~ # docker login-u-e-p # docker pull registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ruby-20-rhel7 # docker tag registry.access.redhat.com/openshift3/ruby-20-rhel7 /default/ruby-20-rhel7:latest # docker push /default/ruby-20-rhel7:latest ~~~

title: Deploy fails after changing deployment configuration
issue: After updating a deployment configuration, for example changing a environment variable, the new deployment fails with a message like this: ~~~ $ oc logs test-2-deploy I0901 11:11:11.123456 1 deployer.go:197] Deploying from demo/test-1 to demo/test-2 (replicas: 1) F0901 11:11:11.123987 1 deployer.go:64] couldn't assign source annotation to deployment demo/test-2: replicationControllers "test-2" cannot be updated: the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again ~~~ How can this be fixed?
resolution: Update to version 3.0.2 or newer where this issue is no longer reported. If it persists, please open a support case with Red Hat Technical Support

title: Is there a way in OpenShift to define NodeSelector for builds
issue: As far as I could see, there is no way to define a `NodeSelector` for builds in `BuildConfig`. We need the ability to specify on which nodes `STI` builds can run because of our network isolation.
Is there a way to define `NodeSelector` for builds
resolution: ###For 3.4.x###- Builds can be targeted to run on specific nodes by specifying labels in the nodeSelector field of a build configuration. The nodeSelector value is a set of key/value pairs that are matched to node labels when scheduling the build pod. ~~~ apiVersion: "v1" kind: "BuildConfig" metadata: name: "sample-build" spec: nodeSelector: key1: value1 key2: value2 ~~~- For more information refer [Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.4/dev_guide/builds/advanced_build_operations.html#dev-guide-assigning-builds-to-nodes) ###For Earlier release### * To obtain possible workaorund: ~~~ Suppose, I have labelled my nodes like as below: oc get nodes NAME LABELS STATUS AGE master.example.com kubernetes.io/hostname=master.example.com Ready,SchedulingDisabled 20d node1.example.com buildnode=test,kubernetes.io/hostname=node1.example.com Ready 20d node2.example.com deploy=demo,kubernetes.io/hostname=node2.example.com Ready 20d I then edit the scheduler file:/etc/origin/master/scheduler.json to instruct the build to use a specific label like as below: {"kind": "Policy", "apiVersion": "v1", "predicates": [{"name": "MatchNodeSelector"}, {"name": "PodFitsResources"}, {"name": "PodFitsPorts"}, {"name": "NoDiskConflict"}, {"name": "Region", "argument": {"serviceAffinity": {"labels": ["deploy"]}}}],"priorities": [{"name": "LeastRequestedPriority", "weight": 1}, {"name": "ServiceSpreadingPriority", "weight": 1}, {"name": "Zone", "weight": 2, "argument": {"serviceAntiAffinity": {"label": "zone"}}}, {"name": "BuildPrio", "weight": 100, "argument": {"labelPreference": {"label": "buildnode", "presence": true}}}]} You can see that I have added an additional buildprio to above file. Then restart the master service and check a new build and see if the build pod is getting created on the selected node. As of our "guidlines", every DeploymentConfig must have an label or NodeSelector, all deployments will run on the correct set of nodes. or you have to modify the predicates with the correct label where do you want your application to deploy. {"name": "Region", "argument": {"serviceAffinity": {"labels": ["deploy"]}}} ~~~

title: OpenShift Container Platform 3 channel is not available on Red Hat Satellite 5.
issue: OpenShift Container Platform 3.x does not appear in the channel list for RHEL-6/7 on Red Hat Satellite 5 server.
resolution: * Currently OpenShift Container Platform 3 repositories are only available through CDN Red Hat Subscription Manager and Red Hat Satellite 6. The same channel is not available on Red Hat Satellite-5 and is unlikely to be published for Red Hat Satellite 5.x in future. Please refer [article](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2099631) for more details. * As a workaround, use the Red Hat Satellite 6 content ISOs to create a custom OSE3 channel on Satellite 5.- Download all the `Base Satellite Content ISOs` for the Product (from Red Hat Customer Portal) (https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/250/ver=6.5/rhel---7/6.5.2.1/x86_64/content-isos)- Copy all of Satellite Content ISOs of product OSE3 on Satellite server to directory `/var/www/html/pub/`. ~~~ # mv sat-6-isos--rhel-7-server-ose-3_DOT_11-x86_64-2019-06-22T02.14-01.iso /var/www/html/pub/ # mv sat-6-isos--rhel-7-server-ose-3_DOT_11-x86_64-2019-06-22T02.14-02.iso /var/www/html/pub/ ~~~- Create a local directory that are shared through httpd on the Satellite. This example uses /var/www/html/pub/rhelosp7/. ~~~ # mkdir-p /var/www/html/pub/rhelosp7/ ~~~- Mount and recursively copy the contents of the first ISO to the local directory: ~~~ # mkdir /mnt/iso # mount-o loop /var/www/html/pub/first_iso /mnt/iso # cp-ruv /mnt/iso/* /var/www/html/pub/rhelosp7/ # umount /mnt/iso # rmdir /mnt/iso # 'find./rhelosp7/-name ‘*.rpm’ | sort > RPMs.txt' //To validate the integrity of RPM's. ~~~- Repeat the above step for each ISO until you have copied all the data from the Content ISOs into /var/www/html/pub/rhelosp7/.- Browse to content, example: http://your-satellite/pub/rhelosp7/content/dist/rhel/server/7/7Server/x86_64/ose/3.11/os/- Within Satellite WebUI: 1. Create custom repository and use URL to ISO from previous step: a. Channels > > Manage Software Channels > > Manage Repositories > > Create Repository b. Enter Label and URL (for example: http://localhost/pub/rhelosp7/content/dist/rhel/server/7/7Server/x86_64/ose/3.11/os/) c. Click “Create” **NOTE**: If there is any issues or not allowed to run http on Satellite server, as an alternative, `file:///` can be used. In that case, enter Label and URL as file:///var/www/html/pub/rhelosp7/content/dist/rhel/server/7/7Server/x86_64/ose/3.11/os/ 2. Create custom Channel: a. Manage Software Channels > > Create Channel > > fill in blanks, selecting appropriate base channel > > Create NOTE: In the case of a base-OS-like product (like RHEL OSP) the custom channel will be a base-channel so leave it 'none'. 3. Associate Repository (the link above) to Channel: a. Manage Software Channels > > Channel_Name > > Repositories > > Select repository and associate to channel 4. Synchronize the above created custom channel.- Once the above steps are completed, this custom channel can be added to the clients during registration and complete the OpenShift installation on client.

title: Adding LDAP authentication to Ansible playbook answer file
issue: - While following all the official documents for setting up an advance cluster and even simple cluster every time we run the oc installer or the Ansible playbook our LDAP settings files get wiped out of the `/etc/openshift/master/master-config.yaml` file. Is there a way to add the LDAP config to the answer file or a playbook config set?- How to set up LDAP authentication in the Ansible hosts file?
resolution: Add the following configuration inside */etc/ansible/hosts* file: ~~~ openshift_master_identity_providers=[{"name": "ldap_auth","challenge": "true","login": "true","kind": "LDAPPasswordIdentityProvider","attributes": {"id": ["dn"],"name": ["cn"], "preferredUsername": ["sAMAccountName"]},"insecure": "true", "bindDN": "CN=Administrator,CN=Users,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com","bindPassword": "redhat1@123","ca": "","url": "ldap://10.96.65.94:389/CN=Users,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com?sAMAccountName?sub"}] ~~~ Optionally, add: ~~~ openshift_master_ldap_ca_file= ~~~ Then run ansible-playbook again.

title: OpenShift installer fails on: No Package matching 'openshift' found available, installed or updated.
issue: OpenShift installation is failing on: No Package matching 'openshift' found available, installed or updated.
resolution: Ensure you have enabled the required repositories. For 3.0 ~~~ # subscription-manager repos--disable="*" # subscription-manager repos \--enable="rhel-7-server-rpms" \--enable="rhel-7-server-extras-rpms" \--enable="rhel-7-server-ose-3.0-rpms" ~~~ For 3.1 ~~~ # subscription-manager repos--disable="*" # subscription-manager repos \--enable="rhel-7-server-rpms" \--enable="rhel-7-server-extras-rpms" \--enable="rhel-7-server-ose-3.1-rpms" ~~~

title: Configuring OpenShift Container Platform 3 to authenticate against LDAP or Active Directory
issue: How to configure OpenShift Container Platform 3 to login with LDAP or Active Directory (AD) users?
resolution: This knowledge base solution is a re-hashing of information found in the [product documenation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/configuring_authentication.html#LDAPPasswordIdentityProvider).- Edit `/etc/openshift/master/master-config.yaml` to use these settings: ~~~ oauthConfig: assetPublicURL: https://master.corp.example.com:8443/console/ grantConfig: method: auto identityProviders:- name: ldap_auth challenge: true login: true provider: apiVersion: v1 kind: LDAPPasswordIdentityProvider attributes: id:- dn email:- mail name:- cn preferredUsername:- sAMAccountName bindDN: "Administrator@corp.example.com" bindPassword: "redhat" ca: my-ldap-ca-bundle.crt insecure: false url: "ldaps://ad.corp.example.com:636/OU=Users,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com?sAMAccountName?sub?(&(objectClass=person))" masterPublicURL: https://master.corp.example.com:8443 masterURL: https://master.corp.example.com:8443 ~~~ Make sure that the `sAMAccountName` is correctly set as the LDAP search is **Case Sensitive**.- Restart master services: ~~~ # master-restart api # master-restart controllers ~~~- For 3.9 or older releases: ~~~ # systemctl restart atomic-openshift-master* ~~~

title: Failed to resolve hostname from containers managed by OpenShift v3
issue: - When I tried to s2i build with internal gitserver, I got following error and failed to build. ~~~ E1006 03:21:45.329743 1 git.go:102] Clone failed: fatal: unable to access 'http://gitserver.example.com/foo/bar/testgit/': Failed connect to gitserver.example.com:80; Operation now in progresst I1006 03:21:45.329782 1 clone.go:35] Git clone failed: exit status 128 ~~~- I set up internal git repositories followed by [How to use internal git repositories with Openshift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1748853), and the setup is no problem.- Or when I tried to use external gitserver, it returns Connection timed out below. ~~~ E0823 08:59:07.653475 1 git.go:127] fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/foo/ruby-hello-world/': Failed connect to github.com:443; Connection timed out I0823 08:59:07.656487 1 clone.go:29] Git clone failed: exit status 128 ~~~- I started hitting this issue after update to v3.0.1.0 or later.
resolution: - Check your DNS setting regarding [environment-requirements](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.0/install_config/install/prerequisites.html#environment-requirements)- If your OpenShift host is `xxx.example.com`, then setup DNS as ~~~ *.clooudapps.example.com 192.168.133.10 ~~~- Do **NOT** set as ~~~ *.example.com 192.168.133.10 ~~~- Also, Do **NOT** add search path `clooudapps.example.com` in your `/etc/resolv.conf`. ~~~ search example.com clooudapps.example.com ~~~
root_cause: - Container managed by OpenShift/Kubernetes has `options ndots:5` in their `/etc/resolv.conf`.- It has been added after OpenShift v3.0.1.0(Kubernetes v1)- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10266- It will change the DNS resolution from host's behavior.- For example, in case your `/etc/resolv.conf` has following setting: ~~~ nameserver 192.168.133.10 search test.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local example.com options ndots:5 ~~~ and you lookup `$ curl access.redhat.com`, then it will lookup this order: ~~~ 1. access.redhat.com.test.svc.cluster.local 2. access.redhat.com.svc.cluster.local 3. access.redhat.com.cluster.local 4. access.redhat.com.example.com <-★ 5. access.redhat.com ~~~ and it will hit the wildcard DNS `*.example.com` as `access.redhat.com.example.com`.

title: The Cluster Monitoring Operator is stuck in Progressing state, triggering a ClusterOperatorDown alert.
issue: The Cluster Monitoring Operator is stuck in Progressing state, triggering a ClusterOperatorDown alert.
resolution: - Update the `cluster-monitoring-config` configmap in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace to ensure it references the correct key for the "username" in the "XYZ" secret: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: cluster-monitoring-config namespace: openshift-monitoring data: config.yaml: | prometheusK8s: remoteWrite:- url: "https://remote-write.endpoint" basicAuth: username: name: XYZ key: username password: name: XYZ key: password writeRelabelConfigs: rw-basic-auth: key: user <-------------- password: name: XYZ ~~~ OR- Update the "XYZ" secret in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace to ensure it references the correct key for the "user" in the `cluster-monitoring-config` configmap. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 data: password: MzEgYnl0ZXMgbG9uZw== username: MyBieXRlcyBsb25n <----------------- ~~~
root_cause: The key defined in the `cluster-monitoring-config` configmap does not match with the key defined in the "XYZ" secret, leading to the failure in creating the configuration.

title: How to forcefully delete provisioned clusters from ocm console?
issue: - Unable to delete clusters created from console.redhat.com- How to delete clusters from cli?
resolution: - The cluster can be removed using the `ocm cli` using the `best_effort=true` flag.- The command to initialize the deletion is as below: ~~~ $ ocm delete cluster-p best_effort=true 255urrtf5fpi40h1234596060390 ~~~ where, 255urrtf5fpi40h1234596060390 is the clusterid of the cluster.- The cluster id can be found by running: ~~~ $ ocm list clusters ~~~

title: AWS IPI Node Scaling Issue: Nodes Remain Provisioned Post-Cluster Upgrade
issue: - In AWS IPI, the nodes are not scaling up following the cluster upgrade, and the machines remain in a provisioned state.
resolution: **This solution should not be applied without first consulting with a Red Hat Support Engineer through a new support case.** 1. Verify the name of the secret utilized by the machineset: ~~~ $ oc get machinesets cluster01-compute-zone1 cluster01-compute-zone2 cluster01-compute-zone3-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml | grep-A1 "userDataSecret:" userDataSecret: name: compute-user-data-managed-- userDataSecret: name: compute-user-data-managed-- userDataSecret: name: compute-user-data-managed ~~~ 2. Create a new secret named compute-user-data-test based on compute-user-data-managed, updating the version to 3.2.0 and modifying the reference in the MachineSets: ~~~ $ oc extract-n openshift-machine-api secret/compute-user-data-managed--keys=userData--to=- {"ignition": {"config": {"merge": [{"source": "https://api-int.cluster01.example.com:22623/config/compute", "verification": {}}], "replace": {"verification": {}}}, "proxy": {}, "security": {"tls": {"certificateAuthorities": [{"source": "data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,", "verification": {}}]}}, "timeouts": {}, "version": "3.4.0"}, "kernelArguments": {}, "passwd": {}, "storage": {}, "systemd": {}} ~~~ 3. A new secret can be created based on the existing secret. After updating, it will appear identical but with the version changed to 3.2.0: ~~~ $ oc extract-n openshift-machine-api secret/compute-user-data-test--keys=userData--to=- {"ignition": {"config": {"merge": [{"source": "https://api-int.cluster01.example.com:22623/config/compute", "verification": {}}], "replace": {"verification": {}}}, "proxy": {}, "security": {"tls": {"certificateAuthorities": [{"source": "data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,", "verification": {}}]}}, "timeouts": {}, "version": "3.2.0"}, "kernelArguments": {}, "passwd": {}, "storage": {}, "systemd": {}} ~~~ 4. Update the reference in the MachineSets to utilize secret/compute-user-data-test instead of secret/compute-user-data-managed.
root_cause: - After cluster upgrade, ignition version changed to 3.4.0 from 3.2.0 because of which new machines are stuck in provisioned state.- The Machine Config Operator (MCO) generates a "$pool-user-data-managed" secret for each pool, including custom pools like compute. However:- Currently, no components within the system utilize this secret.- It is designed for future use when boot image updates are enabled, aligning the secret's version with the boot image version.- The secret is not intended for use by any cluster at this time, and the source of the machineset configuration is uncertain.- ** Booting directly into custom pools is unsupported; nodes must first boot as worker nodes before being moved to a custom pool. While this approach is not officially supported, it typically functions correctly. The worst-case scenario may involve a few extra reboots while the new custom node stabilizes. **

title: Insights operator is degraded with error "unable to build request to connect to Insights server" in OpenShift 4
issue: - Cluster Operator `insights` is in a degraded state with error like: ~~~ Unable to report: unable to build request to connect to Insights server: Post "https://console.redhat.com/api/ingress/v1/upload": Internal Server Error ~~~- The `insight` operator pod log shows errors like: ~~~ The operator has some internal errors: Unable to report: unable to build request to connect to Insights server: Post "https://cloud.redhat.com/api/ingress/v1/upload": Proxy Authentication Required ~~~
resolution: Validate the `proxy`, configuration: ~~~ $ oc get proxy cluster-o yaml [...] spec: httpProxy: http://1.0.0.0:8080 httpsProxy: http://1.0.0.0:8080 noProxy: xxxx trustedCA: name: 'xxxx' ~~~ Define the `noProxy` as per the necessary values. Define the `trustedCA` if the Proxy needs a certificate for connection. Check the connectivity from the Insights pod to the failing URL as explained in the "Diagnostic Steps" section. If the error shown in the message is "`Internal Server Error`", check the reply from `curl` to see if there is any issue with the Proxy, like the following, and in that case, check the Proxy: ~~~ [...] < X-Squid-Error: ERR_CANNOT_FORWARD 0 [...] curl: (56) Received HTTP code 500 from proxy after CONNECT ~~~ For additional information about the cluster-wide Proxy configuration, refer to the [configuring the cluster-wide proxy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/networking/enable-cluster-wide-proxy.html) and configure the `proxy` resource accordingly.
root_cause: Insights Cluster Operator is degraded when cannot communicate the reports to `console.redhat.com` (or `cloud.redhat.com` in older versions). The operator turns in the `Degraded` status after exceeding the threshold of 5 attempts.

title: How to perform Housekeeping on a rapidly growing NooBaa DB PVC 'db-noobaa-db-pg-0' without expanding it
issue: NooBaa DB PVC `db-noobaa-db-pg-0` is growing extensively; however, only housekeeping is required without expanding it.
resolution: Execute the following the commands to understand the size consumption by each schema in the NooBaa DB: ~~~ $ oc rsh noobaa-db-pg-0 $ psql nbcore; $ nbcore=# \d+ Schema | Name | Type | Owner | Size | Description--------+----------------------+----------+--------+------------+------------- public | accounts | table | noobaa | 96 kB | public | activitylogs | table | noobaa | 7883 MB | < <---- almost 8GB public | agent_configs | table | noobaa | 8192 bytes | public | alertslogs | table | noobaa | 48 kB | public | buckets | table | noobaa | 88 kB | public | bucketstats | table | noobaa | 64 kB | public | chunk_configs | table | noobaa | 48 kB | public | clusters | table | noobaa | 144 kB | public | datablocks | table | noobaa | 2734 MB | public | datachunks | table | noobaa | 4701 MB | public | endpointgroupreports | table | noobaa | 8512 kB | public | funcs | table | noobaa | 8192 bytes | public | iostats | table | noobaa | 144 kB | public | master_keys | table | noobaa | 48 kB | public | mdsequencesnative | sequence | noobaa | 8192 bytes | public | namespace_resources | table | noobaa | 8192 bytes | public | nodes | table | noobaa | 136 kB | public | objectmds | table | noobaa | 4707 MB | public | objectmultiparts | table | noobaa | 8192 bytes | public | objectparts | table | noobaa | 2543 MB | public | objectstats | table | noobaa | 2624 kB | public | pools | table | noobaa | 216 kB | public | replicationconfigs | table | noobaa | 8192 bytes | public | roles | table | noobaa | 48 kB | public | system_history | table | noobaa | 856 kB | public | systems | table | noobaa | 88 kB | public | tieringpolicies | table | noobaa | 48 kB | public | tiers | table | noobaa | 48 kB | public | usagereports | table | noobaa | 5544 kB | (29 rows) ~~~- To truncate table activitylogs: NOTE. Only this table that can be truncated safely, DO NOT truncate any other table, we could lose all access to the objects in noobaa buckets. ~~~ nbcore=# TRUNCATE activitylogs; TRUNCATE TABLE nbcore=# ~~~- Then, check if the activitylogs have been truncated.
root_cause: - The use of MultiCloud Gateway (MCG) for storing objects could lead to an increase in the NooBaa DB consumption as it stores the metadata- High size on activitylogs can be explained by the following [Bug 2264480- db-noobaa-db-pg-0 PVC continues to grow extensively, activitylogs already truncated need to either fix or workaround](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2264480)--> fixed in ODF 4.16: keep "activitylogs" table smaller "activity such as upload, delete are not being written to the DB to the activitylogs collection"

title: The S2I builds are failing with the latest  OpenJDK ubi8:1.19-1/ubi9:1.18-1 images Operation not permitted
issue: Failure with Operation not permitted as below in images OpenJDK 8, 11, 17 images ubi8:1.19-1/ubi9:1.18-1 Operation not permitted: ~~~ STEP 7/9: RUN /usr/local/s2i/assemble INFO S2I source build with plain binaries detected INFO Copying binaries from /tmp/src to /deployments..../example.jar rsync: failed to set times on "/deployments/.": Operation not permitted (1) agents/ rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors) (code 23) at main.c(1189) [sender=3.1.3] subprocess exited with status 23 subprocess exited with status 23 error building at STEP "RUN /usr/local/s2i/assemble": exit status 23 time="2024-02-28T18:34:45Z" level=error msg="exit status 23" ~~~
resolution: ### Alternatives: a- For S2I stand-alone toolkit: Add `--assemble-user 185` as additional argument in the S2I binary (s2i build...--as-dockerfile /path/Dockerfile.gen). Example: ~~~ name: generate resources: {} script: > s2i build $(workspaces.build-dir.path)/artifacts/ $(params.SOURCE_IMAGE) \--image-scripts-url image:///usr/local/s2i \--as-dockerfile /gen-source/Dockerfile.gen--assemble-user 185 ~~~ b- Adding USER 185 before the `RUN assemble` c- Using a specific dockerfile add the line `RUN chmod-R a+rwx /deployments`. Alternative A is preferred to avoid wider permissions on the `/deployments`, `Alternative C`. However, for Openshift buildconfig only `Alternative A` can be used given the buildConfig API does not have it, as `oc explain buildconfig.spec.*` shows. Finally, if a custom user is set in the building process, e.g. `USER 1001`, one alternative might be to set the permissions of that directory for that user specifically, for example: ~~~ $ chown-R 1001 /deployments ~~~
root_cause: The problem will occur on JDK8, 11, and 17 because they have the same scripts; it's in all the ubi8:1.19-1 images, and ubi9:1.18-1 images. And it will occur when doing s2i build with binaries copy (any S2I process), e.g. inside Openshift or with the s2i [stand-alone tool](https://github.com/openshift/source-to-image) using `--as-dockerfile` option and to mitigate the issue the UID has to be 185 when running assemble. The culprit is specifically, the rsync, which takes place during a binary-only s2i assemble, and attempts to modify the permissions on `/deployments` when copying artifacts. Regarding users:- User 185 is reserved for the JBoss EAP user and **OpenJDK container usage**. The OpenJDK user is called jboss.- User 1001 is the default value for the container and also the default value that s2i uses if it isn't set to use another value. For S2I toolkit, see the [openshift/source-to-image](https://github.com/openshift/source-to-image/blob/master/docs/cli.md) for details on the options for Source to Image, some options include: Option | Purpose----------|---------as-dockerfile | Output a Dockerfile to this path instead of building a new image--assemble-user | Specify the user to run assemble with--assemble-runtime-user | Specify the user to run assemble-runtime with Regarding BuildConfig in OCP 4, when OpenShift does a source-to-image build internally, it uses the same code as the s2i standalone tool, whereas OCP 4 does `--as-dockerfile` internally build by default. So the issue can happen on the stand-alone S2I tool or Openshift build, regardless, as long as it is copying a binary file. Finally, the S2I will run the [run.sh](https://github.com/jboss-container-images/openjdk/blob/d14ec7f363956b73684409c8b6bd9c766507013b/modules/s2i/bash/artifacts/usr/local/s2i/run#L20) script (together with assembly.sh), which will then add: ~~~ Starting the Java application... ~~~

title: etcd_object_counts metric only show OpenShift resources
issue: Reviewing the dashboard in `console-openshift-console.apps.[example.com]/monitoring/dashboards/grafana-dashboard-api-performance?apiserver=kube-apiserver`, it shows only OpenShift related resources in "etcd Object Count".
`etcd_object_counts` only reports OpenShift resources and is missing `kubernetes` core resources.
Starting with OCP 4.10, `etcd_object_counts` does no longer correctly report number of objects per resources.
resolution: Metric `etcd_object_counts` was deprecated, and `apiserver_storage_objects` should be used instead when attempting to query resources within etcd. The issue with the wrong metric used in the dashboard was tracked in [bug OCPBUGS-5873](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-5873) and fixed in OpenShift 4.13.0 by [errata RHSA-2023:1326](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:1326). Some `promql` query examples for using the `apiserver_storage_objects` metric:- Total number of resources in etcd (any of): ~~~ sum(resource:apiserver_storage_objects:max) sum(max(apiserver_storage_objects) by (resource)) ~~~- Show the top 15 resources (with regards to number of objects) in etcd (any of): ~~~ topk(15, resource:apiserver_storage_objects:max) topk(15, max(apiserver_storage_objects) by (resource)) ~~~

You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Metric `etcd_object_counts` was [replaced in Kubernetes 1.21](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#other-cleanup-or-flake-4), in which OpenShift 4.8 is based, and `apiserver_storage_objects`was promoted and marked as stable in [Kubernetes 1.21](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/100082).

title: RHOSO service unavailable after attempted password change
issue: Attempting to run a command results in HTTP error code 503 $ openstack volume service list (HTTP 503) command terminated with exit code 1: keystoneauth1.exceptions.http.Unauthorized: The request you have made requires authentication. (HTTP 401) (Request-ID: req-723ae722-4ce4-475d-866c-afaac2949720)
resolution: The recommended fix is to restore the previous password. If the password was overwritten using a command like ``` oc set data secret/osp-secret CinderPassword= ``` You can restore the service by setting the password back to the original: ``` oc set data secret/osp-secret CinderPassword= ``` If, however, you **do not** have a secure backup of the original password, using the following instructions to recover the service: 1. Delete the KeystoneService for the service: ``` oc delete KeystoneService/cinderv3--wait=false ``` 2. Remove the finalizers from the KeystoneService to allow CR deletion: ``` oc edit KeystoneService/cinderv3-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}'--type=merge ``` 3. Delete the KeystoneEndpoint for the given service: ``` oc delete KeystoneEndpoint/cinderv3--wait=false ``` 4. Remove the finalizers from the KeystoneEndpoint. ``` oc patch KeystoneEndpoint/cinderv3-p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}'--type=merge ``` The service operator re-creates the CRs and the Identity service (keystone) accepts the new password. NOTE: This is procedure is for recovery purposes and is not a Red Hat supported method for changing service passwords. A supported procedure is still under development.
root_cause: A service password is changed in `osp-secret`, for example, to rotate the password. The service operators adopt the new keystone user password, but the new password is not accepted by keystone.

title: How to identify CVE vulnerabilities in OpenShift Container Platform 3
issue: - How do we identify Common Vulnerability Exposures (CVEs) that may be impacting our OpenShift 3 Cluster.- We need to mitigate vulnerabilities, how do we determine whether our OpenShift 3 Cluster is impacted?
resolution: 1. Install the `openscap-scanner` RPM. # yum install openscap-scanner-y 2. Download the `openshift-3.11-including-unpatched.oval.xml.bz2` file. This is the CVE database that the `openscap-scanner` utility will reference when executed. # wget https://www.redhat.com/security/data/oval/v2/RHEL7/openshift-3.11-including-npatched.oval.xml.bz2 3. Extract the CVE database archive. # bunzip2 openshift-3.11-including-unpatched.oval.xml.bz2 4. Execute the `oscap` command and re-direct output into an output file. # oscap oval eval--results results.xml--report results.html openshift-3.11-including-unpatched.oval.xml > result_pass_fail.txt 5. View the results of the scan. The output file will contain a listing of known CVEs, and will identify whether or not the cluster is vulnerable to said CVEs, by appending a boolean value to each CVE. # cat result_pass_fail.txt.... Definition oval:com.redhat.cve:def:202232149: true Definition oval:com.redhat.cve:def:20223172: true Definition oval:com.redhat.cve:def:20223162: true Definition oval:com.redhat.cve:def:202231163: false Definition oval:com.redhat.cve:def:202230954: false Definition oval:com.redhat.cve:def:202230953: false.... Identify all listed CVEs with status **true**. These are the CVEs applicable to the Cluster 7. Refer to the [Red Hat CVE Database](https://access.redhat.com/security/security-updates/cve) and take the necessary remediation steps to secure your cluster where applicable.

title: WIP- How to use multiple redundant image mirrors for a disconnected OpenShift cluster
issue: How to provide redundancy in the image mirror configuration of a disconnected OpenShift cluster to protect against issues pulling images when one mirror repository goes down.
resolution: To get around the limitation of CatalogSources only allowing single URLs for the image manifests, a loadbalancer should be used as a frontend for the mirrors, providing both high availability and fallback if any of the backends go down.
root_cause: When configuring a disconnected cluster, mirror repositories are specified in an `ImageContentSourcePolicy` (ICSP), which has been deprecated since OCP 4.13, or `ImageDigestMirrorSet` (IDMS). Both allow for specifying one or more mirror repositories for each image source. This in turn is used by the cluster to generate a `/etc/containers/registries.conf` on each node that is used during image pulls and contains a mapping of the specified sources to the intended mirrors. One area that the multiple mirrors are not translated into is in the CatalogSource resources used to specify the Operator catalogues. These explicitly only allow specifying a URL to a single image.

title: ClusterAutoscaler is evicting DaemonSet Pods
issue: - The `ClusterAutoscaler` is causing the eviction of `pods` managed by `daemonsets`.
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-23000](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-23000) and delivered a fix in Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4.17.0 through errata [RHSA-2024:3718](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3718). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: The `cluster autoscaler` managed by the `cluster autoscaler operator`, evicts the `pods` residing on the node designated for draining during the scale-down operation. This includes `pods` owned by `daemonsets`. In certain situations, this behavior may lead to an incorrect termination of the application `pods`, potentially leading to a failed drain operation.

title: ELY01024: Filesystem-backed realm cannot create duplicate identity for a RHPAM user.
issue: Could not create realm for a user due to error ELY01024: Filesystem-backed realm cannot create duplicate identity for a user. ~~~ WARN KIE admin user "pamadmin" already exists in EAP, user will be updated if changes were made. pdated user 'pamadmin' to file '/opt/kie/data/configuration/application-users.properties' Updated user 'pamadmin' with groups kie-server,rest-all,admin,kiemgmt,Administrators,user to file '/opt/kie/data/configuration/application-roles.properties' INFO Migrating users to elytron kie-filesystem-realm /opt/kie/data/kie-fs-realm-users. WARNING: Could not create realm for user pamadmin due to error: ELY01024: Filesystem-backed realm cannot create duplicate identity for identity "pamadmin" WARNING: No name provided for filesystem-realm, using default filesystem-realm name for /opt/kie/data/configuration/application-users.properties. WARNING: No name provided for security-domain, using default security-domain name for /opt/kie/data/configuration/application-users.properties. ~~~
resolution: - The kie-server admin user name should be different than EAP admin name.- Open the KieApp instance in RH OCP admin console and select YAML tab.- Add the following configuration in the spec section: ~~~ spec: commonConfig: adminPassword: username adminUser: password ~~~
root_cause: The KIE admin user "pamadmin" already exists in EAP. Can not be assigned the same user name to the EAP user and the Kie admin user.

title: How to create a custom machineset containing required volumeszie and  instance type
issue: - How to add additional worker nodes with custom specifications?- Steps to create a new machineset with the required configuration?
resolution: - First, check the existing machinesets on the cluster. ~~~ $ oc get machinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2a 1 1 1 1 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2b 1 1 1 1 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2c 1 1 1 1 15d ~~~- Select the machineset as per the availability zone in which the new nodes need to be added and obtain its YAML definition. ~~~ $ oc get machinesets ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2a-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml > custom-worker-eu-west-2a ~~~- Delete the lines containing `creationTimestamp`, `generation`, `resourceVersion`, `selfLink`, `uid`. The `status` section also needs to be deleted which is present at the bottom along with `availableReplicas`, `fullyLabeledReplicas`, etc.- Modify the newly created file containing the configuration of existing machineset for these specific options only. ~~~... metadata: labels: machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-cluster: ocp-latest-v52gd name: custom-worker-eu-west-2a <----- Add the machineset name as per the requirement... spec: replicas: 1 <----- Specify the default number of replicas selector: matchLabels:... machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machineset: custom-worker-eu-west-2a <----- Same name specified for machineset template: metadata:... labels:... machine.openshift.io/cluster-api-machineset: custom-worker-eu-west-2a <----- Same name specified for machineset... spec: metadata:... providerSpec: value:...- ebs: iops: 0 volumeSize: 120 <----- Specify the volumeSize as per the requirement volumeType: gp2... instanceType: m4.large <----- Specify the EC2 instanceType as per the requirement ~~~- Create the machineset with help of the modified file. ~~~ $ oc create-f custom-worker-eu-west-2a machineset.machine.openshift.io/custom-worker-eu-west-2a created ~~~- The new machineset can be checked easily. ~~~ $ oc get machinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2a 1 1 1 1 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2b 1 1 1 1 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2c 1 1 1 1 15d custom-worker-eu-west-2a 1 1 1 1 6m4s ~~~- The new nodes take some time to get added to the cluster maybe around 8-10 minutes.- The status of the new machine can be checked with the following command. ~~~ $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE ocp-latest-v52gd-master-0 Running m4.xlarge eu-west-2 eu-west-2a 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-master-1 Running m4.xlarge eu-west-2 eu-west-2b 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-master-2 Running m4.xlarge eu-west-2 eu-west-2c 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2a-rv4d9 Running m4.large eu-west-2 eu-west-2a 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2b-bh6r7 Running m4.large eu-west-2 eu-west-2b 15d ocp-latest-v52gd-worker-eu-west-2c-52dlp Running m4.large eu-west-2 eu-west-2c 15d custom-worker-eu-west-2a-kwwzr Running m4.large eu-west-2 eu-west-2a 4m18s ~~~- Check the new node status. ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ip-10-0-129-26.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready master 15d v1.17.1 ip-10-0-138-212.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready worker 15d v1.17.1 ip-10-0-139-40.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready worker 4m28s v1.17.1 ip-10-0-145-37.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready worker 15d v1.17.1 ip-10-0-149-200.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready master 15d v1.17.1 ip-10-0-165-117.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready master 15d v1.17.1 ip-10-0-173-188.eu-west-2.compute.internal Ready worker 15d v1.17.1 ~~~- Similarly, the machinesets for other availability zones can be created.

title: How to configure backstage to use permanent storage?
issue: How to configure backstage to use permanent storage and reuse the PV each time it restarts? How to do it if we always use the configmap CR "app-config-rhdh" or the BackStage yaml?
resolution: To achieve this, that Backstage has to be deployed with persistent storage, where it can use a Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) to request storage. In the context of persistent storage and PV reuse, the process for configuring it in Red Hat Developer Hub is very similar to the standard Backstage setup in Kubernetes. Since it runs on OpenShift, follow OpenShift’s Persistent Volume (PV) and Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) management procedures. 1. Define the Persistent Volume (PV) and Persistent Volume Claim (PVC), which are managed outside the application configuration. * Persistent Volume (PV): ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata: name: developerhub-pv spec: capacity: storage: 10Gi accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain storageClassName: nfs nfs: path: /srv/nfs/developerhub server: ~~~ * Persistent Volume Claim (PVC): ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: name: developerhub-pvc spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 10Gi storageClassName: nfs ~~~ 2. The volumes or the persistent storage will not directly specify in the ConfigMap "app-config-rhdh" or Backstage configuration YAML. It will likely be configuring paths and environments to ensure Backstage uses the correct directory for storing data (e.g., database, logs, assets). An example of specifying paths within your "app-config.yaml" would be: # app-config.yaml ~~~ backend: database: client: pg connection: host: 'localhost' port: 5432 user: 'your_user' password: 'your_password' database: 'backstage' storage: path: /data/developerhub/storage # The path in the container where data is persisted ~~~ 3. Ensure that "/data/developerhub/storage" or similar is the directory mounted by the PVC in the container. Adjust this based on how the Backstage instance interacts with its storage (such as for SQLite, PostgreSQL, or other types of storage). If the configurations are being managed in Backstage’s main configuration YAML, the storage paths or database paths can also be defined there. In this example, the storage locations such as "/data/cache" or "/data/techdocs" should correspond to the mounted directories from the PVC. These directories will persist data across pod restarts since the PVC ensures the data persists even when the pod is redeployed. # app-config.yaml for Backstage ~~~ backend: database: client: pg connection: host: 'localhost' port: 5432 user: 'postgres' password: 'password' database: 'backstage' cache: store: memory connection: store: 'file' location: '/data/cache' techdocs: storageUrl: /data/techdocs # Example storage location for TechDocs ~~~ 4. While the application-level configurations are being managed via the ConfigMap or Backstage YAML, it has to ensure that the PVC is mounted correctly in the Deployment YAML (or equivalent). For example, in the Deployment YAML, ensure the PVC is correctly referenced: ~~~ apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: developerhub spec: replicas: 1 selector: matchLabels: app: developerhub template: metadata: labels: app: developerhub spec: containers:- name: developerhub image: registry.redhat.io/developerhub/developerhub:latest volumeMounts:- name: developerhub-storage mountPath: /data/developerhub # Mount point for persistent storage volumes:- name: developerhub-storage persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: developerhub-pvc ~~~

title: Jenkins master uses the Kind:route elements .spec.host to calculate JENKINS_URL which is used as callback url.
issue: - Jenkins `s2i` image doesn't work with subdomain routes- When Specifying a subdomain to create a route to Jenkins, the return URL from Jenkins is wrong (`null`)
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat Engineering and is tracked by [JKNS-382](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JKNS-382). #### Workaround Modify the file `/usr/libexec/s2i/run` in the Jenkins master `s2i` image as follows: ~~~ sed-i 's/.spec.host /.status.ingress[].host /g' /usr/libexec/s2i/run ~~~ As an example, one can use the following approach to create a patched image: * Copy the `/usr/libexec/s2i/run` script from a running Jenkins master `s2i` container, and modify it locally: ~~~ $ podman login registry.redhat.io $ podman run-d registry.redhat.io/ocp-tools-4/jenkins-rhel8:v4.15.0 $ podman ps CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES 3988ea071883 registry.redhat.io/ocp-tools-4/jenkins-rhel8:v4.15.0 16 seconds ago Up 16 seconds cranky_mclean $ podman cp cranky_mclean:/usr/libexec/s2i/run. $ sed-i 's/.spec.host /.status.ingress[].host /g'./run ~~~ * Build a new image by replacing the original `/usr/libexec/s2i/run` file with the locally modified script: ~~~ $ cat Containerfile FROM registry.redhat.io/ocp-tools-4/jenkins-rhel8:v4.15.0 COPY./run /usr/libexec/s2i/run $ podman build-t jenkins-rhel8:custom. STEP 1/2: FROM registry.redhat.io/ocp-tools-4/jenkins-rhel8:v4.15.0 STEP 2/2: COPY./run /usr/libexec/s2i/run--> Using cache 72fb38dd29c0f3030651f611b2cce6006f58fcbcf761a93e4abd58011771578c COMMIT jenkins-rhel8:custom--> 72fb38dd29c0 Successfully tagged localhost/jenkins-rhel8:custom 72fb38dd29c0f3030651f611b2cce6006f58fcbcf761a93e4abd58011771578c $ podman images REPOSITORY TAG IMAGE ID CREATED SIZE localhost/jenkins-rhel8 custom 72fb38dd29c0 3 minutes ago 1.67 GB registry.redhat.io/ocp-tools-4/jenkins-rhel8 v4.15.0 e7b1f7ce843f 2 weeks ago 1.67 GB ~~~ * Verify that the containers spawned with the newly built image contain the patched script: ~~~ $ podman run-d localhost/jenkins-rhel8:custom $ podman ps CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES d68ef55a9e95 localhost/jenkins-rhel8:custom 25 seconds ago Up 25 seconds heuristic_sanderson $ podman exec-it heuristic_sanderson /bin/bash bash-4.4$ cat /usr/libexec/s2i/run | grep ".spec.host" bash-4.4$ cat /usr/libexec/s2i/run | grep ".status.ingress" JENKINS_URL="$JENKINS_SCHEME$(oc get routes-o json | jq-c-r--arg JENKINS_SERVICE_NAME "$JENKINS_SERVICE_NAME" '.items[] | select (.spec.to.name == $JENKINS_SERVICE_NAME) |.status.ingress[].host ' | head-n 1)/" ~~~

title: After doing a hard reset on an OpenShift node, why is it taking so much time for the node to return to `Ready` state ?
issue: - crio high CPU load after worker node boot and kubelet does not start- crio initial start takes multiple hours on large cluster nodes after a node has been reseted
resolution: - when doing a hard reset, the Container Runtime used by OpenShift (crio) needs to perform a crash mitigation cleanup. This clean up can take time, and improvements are currently investigated by Red Hat.- the crash mitigation cleanup involves doing a recursive delete of all container overlays and all container images in /var/lib/containers- this recursive delete is known to be slow if containers have too many layers. [This blog post around good practices when creating container images](https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2016/02/24/10-things-to-avoid-in-docker-containers) recommends in point 4) to use four layers, and can be used as a general guideline- as all images will be deleted by the recursive delete, a high number of images might be redownloaded again by the worker node, and you might run into the registryPullQPS limit of the kubelet. This [knowledge base entry explains how to raise this limit](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4767061)- optionally [you can disable the crash mitigation](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6807281) but make sure your understand the caveats
root_cause: When an OpenShift node is forcefully reset (like pulling off the power plug), the crio Container Runtime does the following actions:- the crio-wipe service will notice that the crio service was not gracefully stopped- the crio-wipe service will initiate a crash mitigation. On RHOCP before 4.17, it basically calls `rm-rf /var/lib/containers`. This will delete all containers overlays and all container images. This it to prevent a situation where crio was in the middle of pulling an image, and was interrupted, leaving a corrupted container store. This is handled by the `shutdownWasUnclean()` function in `cri-o/wipe.go`. On [RHOCP starting from 4.17](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPSTRAT-1291) only images that has been corrupted because of sudden reboot will be wiped, not all images.- after this crash mitigation the crio service will clean up the CNI resources leftovers. This is handled by the `wipeIfAppropriate()` function in `cri-o/server.go`- finally the crio service will start, and the dependent kubelet service will follow- once the kubelet service is started, the node can post its status to the API server and the Node will marked as Ready

title: How to verify that the Custom build strategy is disabled in an RHOCP 4 cluster with default settings?
issue: As a cluster admin it is needed to verify that the custom build strategy is disabled in a RHOCP 4 cluster with default settings

As a cluster admin it is needed to apply the mitigations for [CVE-2024-7387](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2024-7387) and [CVE-2024-45496](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2024-45496) and it is needed to check which build strategies are currently enabled for users in a RHOCP 4 cluster
resolution: As a cluster admin, execute the following command: ~~~ $ oc get clusterrolebinding-o wide | grep build ~~~ The output in a cluster with standard settings should look like the following: ~~~ NAME ROLE AGE USERS GROUPS SERVICEACCOUNTS... system:build-strategy-docker-binding ClusterRole/system:build-strategy-docker 23d system:authenticated system:build-strategy-jenkinspipeline-binding ClusterRole/system:build-strategy-jenkinspipeline 23d system:authenticated system:build-strategy-source-binding ClusterRole/system:build-strategy-source 23d system:authenticated... ~~~ One should expect that, `system:authenticated` virtual group doesn't have a rolebinding for `ClusterRole/system:build-strategy-custom`. If such a rolebinding exists in the above output, then it is recommended to follow the steps in the official documentation [Securing builds by strategy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/cicd/builds/securing-builds-by-strategy.html). The example in the official documentation shows disabling the *docker* build strategy. One should modify the example to adapt it to the build strategy of interest.
root_cause: In all versions of OpenShift, the custom build strategy gives developers permission to run arbitrary commands in a privileged container. This is disabled by default, and the documentation section [Custom image builds with Buildah](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/cicd/builds/custom-builds-buildah.html) explicitly warns that this should only be enabled for highly trusted users (eg: cluster admins).

title: HCP ignition-server incorrect registry-overrides in RHOCP 4

title: View changes made from AlertRelabelConfig in RHOCP 4
issue: - Modifying core platform alerting rules, the changes do **NOT*
reflect on the web UI.
resolution: Changes are not reflected inside the web console as reported in the [documention](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/observability/monitoring/managing-alerts.html#managing-core-platform-alerting-rules_managing-alerts), but can be verified in alertmanager and prometheus pods. ### Verifying the change when the alert is firing Login to the CLI to use the command to observe changes: ``` oc-c alertmanager-n openshift-monitoring exec alertmanager-main-0-- amtool alert query-o json--alertmanager.url http://localhost:9093 alertname=Watchdog ``` ### Verifying the change when the alert is not firing ~~~ $ oc get secret-n openshift-monitoring alert-relabel-configs-o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' |base64-d ~~~ ~~~ $ echo-e $(oc-c prometheus-n openshift-monitoring exec prometheus-k8s-0-- curl-s http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/config |jq.data.yaml) |grep-2 ~~~
root_cause: Modify existing platform alerting rules by using an `AlertRelabelConfig` object, the modifications are not reflected in the Prometheus alerts API. Therefore, any dropped alerts_still_ appear in the RH OpenShift Container Platform web console even though they are no longer forwarded to Alertmanager. Additionally, any modifications to alerts, such as a changed severity label, do not appear in the web console.

title: OpenShift Agent Based Installer fails with "pull secret for new cluster is invalid"
issue: + When trying to deploy new RHOCP 4 cluster with Agent Based Installer the deployment fails and following error messages are returned: ~~~ failed to register cluster with assisted-service: AssistedServiceError ~~~ ~~~ Error reason: pull secret for new cluster is invalid: invalid pull secret: 'auth' for [image_registry_name] is not in 'user:password' format ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat Engineering, and was tracked in the following bugs: Target Minor Release | Bug | Fixed Version | Errata--- |--- 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-34400](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-34400)|**4.16.0**|[RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041) 4.15 | [OCPBUGS-34641](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-34641)|**4.15.18**|[RHSA-2024:3889](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3889) 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-35034](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-35034)|**4.14.30**|[RHSA-2024:3881](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3881) ### Workaround As a workaround, the password for the failing image registry can be changed to NOT contain the "`:`" (colon) character.
root_cause: The issue is the password for image registries encoded within the Pull Secret is containing "`:`" (colon) character.

title: Application routes suffer more unavailability than expected during OVN live migration if there are networkpolicies
issue: - During a [live migration from OpenShift SDN to OVN-Kubernetes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/networking/ovn_kubernetes_network_provider/migrate-from-openshift-sdn.html#nw-ovn-kubernetes-live-migration-about_migrate-from-openshift-sdn), application routes are facing more unavailability than expected.- The following conditions are met (otherwise, this solution doesn't apply)- The ingress controller used to expose the application route uses the `HostNetwork` endpoint publishing strategy.- The application allows the traffic from the ingress controller via a networkpolicy similar to the [allow-from-router](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/networking/network_security/network_policy/about-network-policy.html#nw-networkpolicy-allow-from-router_about-network-policy) or [allow-from-hostnetwork](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/networking/network_security/network_policy/about-network-policy.html#nw-networkpolicy-allow-from-hostnetwork_about-network-policy) documented ones
resolution: This issue has been reported under [OCPBUGS-42605](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42605) and is currently under investigation. #### First workaround Just temporarily remove all the networkpolicies of the application project before the migration and re-add them post-migration. #### Second workaround If deleting the networkpolicies is not an option, this workaround can be tried. **Before** the migration, you need to create temporary networkpolicies that will force OVN-Kubernetes to allow traffic from `tun0` and `ovn-k8s-mp0` interfaces. To do so, do as follows:- Label all the projects where you want to apply the workaround ~~~ oc label namespace... workaround-network-policy=workaround ~~~- Auto-generate a networkpolicy that allows the first and second IP of the hostsubnet, by using this big one-liner command: ~~~ oc get hostsubnet-o json | jq-r '.items[]|.subnet' | xargs-n1 bash-c 'ipcalc--no-decorate-S 32 $1|head-3 | tail-2'-- | jq--raw-input-s '.|split("\n")|map(select(.!=""))|map({"ipBlock":{"cidr":.}}) as $from|{"apiVersion":"networking.k8s.io/v1","kind":"NetworkPolicy","metadata":{"name":"workaround-network-policy","labels":{"workaround-network-policy":"workaround"}},"spec":{"policyTypes":["Ingress"],"ingress":[{"from":$from}]}}' > workaround-networkpolicy.json ~~~- Apply the networkpolicy to all the labeled projects: ~~~ for namespace in $(oc get ns-l workaround-network-policy-o name | sed s:namespace/::g); do oc apply-n ${namespace}-f workaround-networkpolicy.json; done ~~~ Then, you can do the migration. Once the migration is finished, you can delete the temporary networkpolicies. To do so:- Run ~~~ oc delete netpol-A-l workaround-network-policy=workaround ~~~
root_cause: During the live migration, there are nodes that are still using OpenShift SDN while others have already started using OVN-Kubernetes. Communication between them via VXLAN is possible thanks to the OVN-Kubernetes hybrid networking feature. The problem is that when OVN-Kubernetes renders the `ACL` and `Address_Set` resources that implement networkpolicies in the northbound database of OVN, they allow neither the IPs from the `tun0` interface of the nodes that are still using OpenShift SDN nor the IPs from the `ovn-k8s-mp0` interfaces of the nodes that are already migrated to OVN-Kubernetes. This ultimately blocks the traffic from the host network of those nodes to the pods inside the already migrated ones.

IN NS;; ANSWER SECTION: www.test.org. 30 IN CNAME www.test.org.cdn.cloudflare.net.;; AUTHORITY SECTION: cloudflare.net. 30 IN SOA ns1.cloudflare.net. dns.cloudflare.com. 23xxxx5 1xxxx xxxx xxx800 xxxx;; Query time: 167 msec;; SERVER: <$Master-IP> #53(<$Master-IP>);; WHEN: Thu Sep 05 16:21:51 UTC 2024;; MSG SIZE rcvd: 202 ~~~- If I were to perform these similar commands on a rhel 9, I wouldn't get a response back.- How can I either limit the message size or preferably the servers I am allowed to query the name server for such as it will only respond back if the server being queried.

One of challenges here is, if anyone wants to add a new node from different network, ACL will block it.- In UPI bare-metal cluster. root_cause: - Check if the cluster is IPI cluster, where coreDNS is running in `openshift-kni-infra` namespace. This is the reason you are able to hit/query port 53 on all the nodes.
