title: How to persistently mount secondary storage on a Openshift 4.x node for use with a OCV HostPathProvisioner.
issue: Secondary local storage was added to a OpenShift 4.x node and configured for use with a OCV HostPathProvisioner. After rebooting the node, the PVCs fail to mount and the virtual machines will not start.
resolution: - The local secondary storage must be created and mounted using a node Machine Config: ~~~ $ cat shift/configs/install/98-worker-hostpath.bu variant: openshift version: 4.12.0 metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 98-worker-hostpath storage: disks:- device: /dev/nvme0n1 <---- limits the rootfs to 128G and creates a 5th partition after it with the rest of the disk, ignore wipe_table: false partitions:- number: 4 label: root size_mib: 128000 resize: true- number: 5 label: hostpath size_mib: 0 filesystems:- device: /dev/disk/by-partlabel/hostpath path: /var/hostpath format: xfs mount_options: [defaults, prjquota] with_mount_unit: true wipe_filesystem: true ~~~ ~~~ $ cat shift/configs/hostpath.yaml apiVersion: hostpathprovisioner.kubevirt.io/v1beta1 kind: HostPathProvisioner metadata: name: hostpath-provisioner spec: imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent storagePools:- name: hostpath-nvme path: "/var/hostpath" workload: nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/os: linux--- apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata: name: hostpath-csi-nvme provisioner: kubevirt.io.hostpath-provisioner reclaimPolicy: Delete volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer parameters: storagePool: hostpath-nvme ~~~

title: Expose timeout options for leader election at the AMQ Broker Operator level in OpenShift
issue: - The AMQ Broker Operator is based on the operator-sdk that support leader election. A timeout on renew a lease == loosing the lease this lead to a restart of the AMQ Broker Operator pod. Exposing timeout options for leader election at the AMQ Broker Operator level will allow to avoid lot of restarts: spec: containers: args:--leader-lease-duration=60--leader-renew-deadline=40--leader-retry-period=5
resolution: This is an enhancement and it has been reported in the following JIRA: **[ENTMQBR-8120](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ENTMQBR-8120)**, and it will be resolved in the upcoming version of Red Hat AMQ Broker. To apply changes those changes to the AMQ Operator itself follow the below:- In case installing the Operator using the CLI Add the ARGS environment variable with the desired options to the manager deployment config, i.e. ~~~ env:- name: ARGS value: "--lease-duration=18--renew-deadline=12--retry-period=3" ~~~- Installing the Operator using OperatorHub Add the ARGS environment variable with the desired options to the subscription config, i.e. ~~~ config: env:- name: ARGS value: "--lease-duration=18--renew-deadline=12--retry-period=3" ~~~
root_cause: For Operators installed via the OLM's Subscription, edit it to pass the arguments to trigger the AMQ deployment. However, in case the AMQ Operator installed/deployed directly (without subscription) edit the deployment file.

title: OCP Microsoft Azure - SystemDLooping Update Risk
issue: - Red Hat has identified an update risk for clusters updating into OpenShift 4.13.46 on Microsoft Azure. Since these nodes are unable to reboot this stalls out the entire update process for OpenShift.- It is not recommended to update into OpenShift 4.13.46 on Microsoft Azure.
resolution: **IMPORTANT: For managed service, Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), refer [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7082093)**. #### Remediation steps for OpenShift Container Platform on Microsoft Azure that have updated to 4.13.46. **Note:** It is important to remove the created MachineConfigs once the cluster has been updated to a fixed version. Please see the final steps in this solution for details. 1. Create a local yaml file named `99-master-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml`. This will be a MachineConfig applied to master nodes. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master name: 99-master-azure-systemd-cycle-fix spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 systemd: units:- contents: | [Unit] Description=Machine Config Daemon Pull # Make sure it runs only on OSTree booted system ConditionPathExists=/run/ostree-booted # This "stamp file" is unlinked when we complete # machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service ConditionPathExists=/etc/ignition-machine-config-encapsulated.json # Run after crio-wipe so the pulled MCD image is protected against a corrupted storage from a forced shutdown Wants=crio-wipe.service NetworkManager-wait-online.service After=crio-wipe.service NetworkManager-wait-online.service NetworkManager.service [Service] Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=yes ExecStart=/bin/sh-c "while! /usr/bin/podman pull--authfile=/var/lib/kubelet/config.json 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:42c5c2aa93ed869f93601b8ce0b667f34fc75c4da492a46694c97f988dc2190e'; do sleep 1; done" [Install] RequiredBy=machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service enabled: true name: machine-config-daemon-pull.service- contents: | [Unit] Description=Machine Config Daemon Firstboot # Make sure it runs only on OSTree booted system ConditionPathExists=/run/ostree-booted # Removal of this file signals firstboot completion ConditionPathExists=/etc/ignition-machine-config-encapsulated.json After=machine-config-daemon-pull.service Before=kubelet-dependencies.target [Service] Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=yes # Disable existing repos (if any) so that OS extensions would use embedded RPMs only ExecStartPre=-/usr/bin/sh-c "sed-i 's/enabled=1/enabled=0/' /etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo" # Run this via podman because we want to use the nmstatectl binary in our container ExecStart=/usr/bin/podman run--rm--privileged--net=host-v /:/rootfs--entrypoint machine-config-daemon 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:42c5c2aa93ed869f93601b8ce0b667f34fc75c4da492a46694c97f988dc2190e' firstboot-complete-machineconfig--persist-nics ExecStart=/usr/bin/podman run--rm--privileged--pid=host--net=host-v /:/rootfs--entrypoint machine-config-daemon 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:42c5c2aa93ed869f93601b8ce0b667f34fc75c4da492a46694c97f988dc2190e' firstboot-complete-machineconfig [Install] RequiredBy=firstboot-osupdate.target enabled: true name: machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service ~~~ 2. Obtain the exact SHA digest for the ocp-v4.0-art-dev image for your OpenShift cluster ~~~ oc get mc 00-master-o json | jq-r '.spec.config.systemd.units[] | select(.name=="machine-config-daemon-pull.service") |.contents' | sed 's/\\n/\n/g' ~~~ 3. Update the image digest in the `99-master-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml` file to the one just obtained in the previous step. Note that there are three replacements to make. 4. Depending on initial cluster version, the final argument to machine-config-daemon-firstboot's first ExecStart statement might be `--maybe-persist-nics` or `--persist-nics`. If the initial cluster version is 4.13, change the argument to `--maybe-persist-nics`. 5. Apply the `99-master-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml` file using `oc apply`. 6. Create a local yaml file named `99-worker-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml`. This will be a MachineConfig applied to worker nodes. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-master-azure-systemd-cycle-fix spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 systemd: units:- contents: | [Unit] Description=Machine Config Daemon Pull # Make sure it runs only on OSTree booted system ConditionPathExists=/run/ostree-booted # This "stamp file" is unlinked when we complete # machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service ConditionPathExists=/etc/ignition-machine-config-encapsulated.json # Run after crio-wipe so the pulled MCD image is protected against a corrupted storage from a forced shutdown Wants=crio-wipe.service NetworkManager-wait-online.service After=crio-wipe.service NetworkManager-wait-online.service NetworkManager.service [Service] Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=yes ExecStart=/bin/sh-c "while! /usr/bin/podman pull--authfile=/var/lib/kubelet/config.json 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:42c5c2aa93ed869f93601b8ce0b667f34fc75c4da492a46694c97f988dc2190e'; do sleep 1; done" [Install] RequiredBy=machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service enabled: true name: machine-config-daemon-pull.service- contents: | [Unit] Description=Machine Config Daemon Firstboot # Make sure it runs only on OSTree booted system ConditionPathExists=/run/ostree-booted # Removal of this file signals firstboot completion ConditionPathExists=/etc/ignition-machine-config-encapsulated.json After=machine-config-daemon-pull.service Before=kubelet-dependencies.target [Service] Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=yes # Disable existing repos (if any) so that OS extensions would use embedded RPMs only ExecStartPre=-/usr/bin/sh-c "sed-i 's/enabled=1/enabled=0/' /etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo" # Run this via podman because we want to use the nmstatectl binary in our container ExecStart=/usr/bin/podman run--rm--privileged--net=host-v /:/rootfs--entrypoint machine-config-daemon 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:42c5c2aa93ed869f93601b8ce0b667f34fc75c4da492a46694c97f988dc2190e' firstboot-complete-machineconfig--persist-nics ExecStart=/usr/bin/podman run--rm--privileged--pid=host--net=host-v /:/rootfs--entrypoint machine-config-daemon 'quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:42c5c2aa93ed869f93601b8ce0b667f34fc75c4da492a46694c97f988dc2190e' firstboot-complete-machineconfig [Install] RequiredBy=firstboot-osupdate.target enabled: true name: machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service ~~~ 7. Obtain the exact SHA digest for the ocp-v4.0-art-dev image for your OpenShift cluster ~~~ oc get mc 00-worker-o json | jq-r '.spec.config.systemd.units[] | select(.name=="machine-config-daemon-pull.service") |.contents' | sed 's/\\n/\n/g' ~~~ 8. Update the image digest in the `99-worker-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml` file to the one just obtained in the previous step. Note that there are three replacements to make. 9. Depending on initial cluster version, the final argument to machine-config-daemon-firstboot's first ExecStart statement might be `--maybe-persist-nics` or `--persist-nics`. If the initial cluster version is 4.13, change the argument to `--maybe-persist-nics`. 10. Apply the `99-worker-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml` file using `oc apply`. 11. OpenShift will update the Ready nodes with these new Machine Configs. 12. For nodes that are in NotReady Status, the node's `machineconfiguration.openshift.io/desiredConfig` annotation must be manually updated. 13. Get the latest machine config for the master machine config pool. ~~~ $ oc get mc--sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | fgrep rendered-master | tail-n 1 | awk '{print $1}' rendered-master-2601c36688f03e2afff5da194c9ecf0a ~~~ 14. Run `oc edit node $NODENAME`, and set the annotation to `machineconfiguration.openshift.io/desiredConfig`: rendered-$ROLE-$HASH to the appropriate most recent rendered machine config returned from the previous command. 15. To get the master node back to Ready status `ssh` into to the master node on Azure and run the commands `systemctl start ovs-configuration.service` and `systemctl start kubelet.service`. 16. Get the latest machine config for the worker machine config pool. ~~~ $ oc get mc--sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | fgrep rendered-worker | tail-n 1 | awk '{print $1}' rendered-worker-2601c36688f03e2afff5da194c9ecf0a ~~~ 17. Run `oc edit node $NODENAME`, and set the annotation to `machineconfiguration.openshift.io/desiredConfig`: rendered-$ROLE-$HASH to the appropriate most recent rendered machine config returned from the previous command. 18. To get the worker node back to Ready status `ssh` into to the worker node on Azure and run the commands `systemctl start ovs-configuration.service` and `systemctl start kubelet.service`. 19. Verify the Machine Config pools have all nodes Ready and all nodes updated: ~~~ $ oc get mcp NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE master rendered-master-b6dfa2f98c8d937319249846b88689fb True False False 3 3 3 0 9h worker rendered-worker-2714b910525483c0358f5e384dd0b9c4 True False False 3 3 3 0 9h ~~~ 20. The cluster is now stable and ready to update. Update the cluster to one of the following versions; 4.13.48+, 4.14.35+, 4.15.28+, 4.16.8+. 21. Once the update is complete out of 4.13.46 remove the machine configs created in this article using the following commands: ~~~ oc delete-f./99-master-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml oc delete-f./99-worker-azure-systemd-cycle-fix.yaml ~~~
root_cause: In OpenShift 4.13.46 it was detected `systemd` dependency loop. Which causes `systemd` to delete some dependencies causing `kubelet` and `crio` to never start on the affected nodes. For more information:[OCPBUGS-33694](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-33694).

title: How to break the core user password of a single node in Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS
issue: - How do I reset a forgotten root password of an OpenShift node- If I forget the root password in RHCOS, how can I reset it?- How to reset a forgotten root password from the console in RHCOS?- How to break to the `ramfs` console using the `rd.break` argument?
resolution: **WARNING**: This procedure is for emergencies only and would allow restoring the password of a single node. Wherever possible, it is recommended to setup the `core` user password the usual way as per [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7010657). **This procedure may not be fully supported** ###### Break out to a shell using the `ramfs` breakpoint 1. Reboot the system. 2. Interrupt the boot loader countdown by pressing any key. 3. Move the cursor to the entry that needs to be booted. 4. Press `e` to edit the selected entry. 5. Move the cursor to the kernel command line (the line that starts with `linux`). It will look similar to the below output: ~~~ linux ($root)/ostree/rhcos-8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/vmlinuz-4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64 rhcos.root=crypt_rootfs random.trust_cpu=on console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200n8 rd.luks.options=discard ostree=/ostree/boot.0/rhcos/8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/0 ignition.platform.id=aws ~~~ 6. Append the `rd.break` argument to the end of the kernel command line. For example: ~~~ linux ($root)/ostree/rhcos-8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/vmlinuz-4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64 rhcos.root=crypt_rootfs random.trust_cpu=on console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200n8 rd.luks.options=discard ostree=/ostree/boot.0/rhcos/8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/0 ignition.platform.id=aws rd.break ~~~ 7. Press `Ctrl +x` to save the changes and reboot the system. 8. Once the boot process reaches the `ramdisk` breakpoint, a root shell will be presented, with the root file system of the RHCOS node mounted in read-only at `/sysroot`. ###### Reset the root password 9. Remount `/sysroot` as read-write: ~~~ switch_root:/# mount-o remount,rw /sysroot ~~~ 10. Switch root to `/sysroot` so that the Linux commands act on the right filesystem: ~~~ switch_root:/# chroot /sysroot ~~~ 11. Set a new root password: ~~~ sh-4.2# passwd core ~~~ 12. Relabel the shadow file: ~~~ sh-4.2# chcon-h system_u:object_r:shadow_t:s0 /etc/shadow ~~~ 13. Exit from chroot shell, and reboot: ~~~ # exit # reboot now ~~~ If the above process does not work using the `rd.break` parameter in the GRUB menu, another option is to do like below: ###### Alternative procedure 1. Follow steps 1 to 5 above. 2. Move the cursor to the kernel command line (the line that starts with `linux`). Remove the `console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200n8` options and add the `console=tty1 init=/bin/bash`, so it will look similar to the below output: ~~~ linux ($root)/ostree/rhcos-8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/vmlinuz-4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64 rhcos.root=crypt_rootfs random.trust_cpu=on rd.luks.options=discard ostree=/ostree/boot.0/rhcos/8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/0 ignition.platform.id=aws console=tty1 init=/bin/bash ~~~ 3. Press `Ctrl +x` to save the changes and reboot the system. 4. Once the boot finishes, a root shell will be presented, with the root file system of the RHCOS node mounted and the `bash` interpreter available. 5. Set a new password for the `core` user: ~~~ bash-4.2$ passwd core ~~~ 6. Restart the node: ~~~ bash-4.2$ reboot now ~~~ If the command above does not work, simply force a node reset using the available console. 7. Now redo the same thing as the steps 1 and 2 of this section, with the exception of changing the `console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200n8` options for the `console=tty1 enforcing=0` options, like below: ~~~ linux ($root)/ostree/rhcos-8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/vmlinuz-4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64 rhcos.root=crypt_rootfs random.trust_cpu=on rd.luks.options=discard ostree=/ostree/boot.0/rhcos/8788e016f1c002b53aed3f47bbfc2f191e6706085f0aa825fd533ff28a7f14b7/0 ignition.platform.id=aws console=tty1 enforcing=0 ~~~ 8. Follow steps 3 and 4 again. 9. Now log in as the `core` user with the password set previously. 10. With the `core` user logged in, change to the `root` user: ~~~ bash-4.2$ sudo-i ~~~ 12. Relabel the `/etc` directory: ~~~ bash-4.2# restorecon-RFvv /etc ~~~ 13. Set SELinux to `enforcing` mode again: ~~~ bash-4.2# setenforce 1 ~~~ 14. Restart the node: ~~~ bash-4.2# reboot now ~~~ If the command above does not work, simply force a node reset using the available console.

title: Why using MTV to migrate VMs from RHV-M to OpenShift Virtualization is causing the disk sizes to use fully allocated size?

resolution: - A workaround is to convert the disk to qcow2 at RHV before migration. This is only supported on RHV 4.4 SP-1.- Below curl command can be used to do the conversion: ~~~ # curl--insecure--request POST--header 'Version: 4'--header 'Accept: application/xml'--header 'Content-Type: application/xml'--user 'admin@internal:mypass'--data ' true cow ' https://manager-fqdn/ovirt-engine/api/disks/c4b63f3f-aced-4fac-9ea7-07229aa5b8b1/convert ~~~

title: [RHOCP4] Exclude specific projects / namespaces from default IngressController routers
issue: - Want to exclude all routes inside specific projects from being served by the default IngressControler routers- Router sharding in place for specific namespaces/routes using custom IngressController
resolution: For example, to exclude routes in the projects "test1" and "test2" from being served by the default IngressController, use the following `namespaceSelector` when configuring the default IngressController: ~~~ namespaceSelector: matchExpressions:- key: name operator: NotIn values:- test1- test2 ~~~ That will exclude namespaces "test1" and "test2" purely by name, instead of requiring additional specific labels on the namespaces which could use `matchLabels` as the `namespaceSelector`
root_cause: The "Traditional sharding example" documentation may be confusing regarding use of `matchExpressions` to match based on namespace metadata (name) instead of labels. [Traditional sharding example](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/networking/configuring_ingress_cluster_traffic/configuring-ingress-cluster-traffic-ingress-controller.html#nw-traditional-sharding_configuring-ingress-cluster-traffic-ingress-controller)

title: In AMQ Broker 7, how to add annotation on Route managed by the AMQ Broker Operator?
issue: In AMQ Broker 7, how to add annotation on Route managed by the AMQ Broker Operator? ~~~ oc annotate route broker-0-svc-rte haproxy.router.openshift.io/balance="roundrobin" oc annotate route broker-1-svc-rte haproxy.router.openshift.io/balance="roundrobin" oc annotate route broker-2-svc-rte haproxy.router.openshift.io/balance="roundrobin" ~~~ But once we update the routes, the broker operator revert the annotations back.
resolution: In 7.12.x, there is a new feature "resourceTemplates" for annotation for routes. In your ActiveMQArtemis_CR.yaml, apply the following: ~~~ spec: resourceTemplates:- annotations: haproxy.router.openshift.io/balance="roundrobin" selector: kind: Route ~~~ For more details: https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.12/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#proc-br-customize-operator-resources_broker-ocp

title: NodePort service is not accessible from all the nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: - Service of type NodePort is not accessible from the nodes except one node which is running the pod endpoint ~~~ $ curl-v telnet://ip-10-2-56-111.ap-south-1.compute.internal:32287
About to connect() to ip-10-2-56-111.ap-south-1.compute.internal port 32287 (#0)
Trying 10.2.56.111... $ curl-v telnet://ip-10-3-123-16.ap-south-1.compute.internal:32287
About to connect() to ip-10-3-123-16.ap-south-1.compute.internal port 32287 (#0)
Connected to ip-10-3-123-16.ap-south-1.compute.internal (10-3-123-16) port 32287 (#0) ~~~
resolution: - Delete all the existing network policies from the project: ~~~ # oc delete netpol allow-from-openshift-ingress-n test-project # oc delete netpol allow-from-openshift-monitoring-n test-project # oc delete netpol allow-same-namespace-n test-project ~~~
root_cause: - NetworkPolicy were not designed with a focus on `NodePort` and thus have some limitation when it comes to the same.- The NetworkPolicy is meant to be applied on the pod network and works based on pod/project labels and selectors.- To access the pod via its service NodePort, the request flow is like the below: ~~~ telnet(NodeIP and NodePort)------> Node network (nodePort)--------> Pod network. ~~~- The reason why accessing the NodePort via the node which is running the pod works is, somehow the network policy did not get enforced on the same node as the requests are getting answered by the node itself because the request traveled through switching/L2 network, not via SDN/L3 network.

title: Using KEDA (Custom Metrics Autoscaler) to create a simple autoscaling
issue: - You want to use [KEDA Operator](https://redhat.com/en/blog/custom-metrics-autoscaler-on-openshift) to create an autoscaling by querying an specific metric- The target metric in this example is_haproxy_backend_connections_total_- The metric should be accessible via the `route` of the `deployment`- You want to query the metric based on the `route` of the `deployment` to scale based on the number of requests.
resolution: The problem was as follows: 1. The ENV_KEDA_HTTP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_ was set, but empty on the `pod`, after setting this to 10000 (10s), the operator was already running 2. Issue with the `HPA`, because it tried to communicate between target `namespaces` and there were `NetPols`, resulting in these requests being blocked. Solution:- Set ENV_KEDA_HTTP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=10000_- Delete `NetPols` on KEDA `Namespace`
root_cause: - The following error is thrown when querying the metric: ``` Warning FailedGetExternalMetric 10m (x658 over 3h10m) horizontal-pod-autoscaler unable to get external metric ch-xyz-devl/s0-prometheus/&LabelSelector{MatchLabels:map[string]string{scaledobject.keda.sh/name: go-backend-keda,},MatchExpressions:[]Label SelectorRequirement{},}: unable to fetch metrics from external metrics API: the server is currently unable to handle the request (get s0-prometheus.external.metrics.k8s.io) ```

title: TLS server certificate using Common Name without SAN field no longer work
product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux for x86_64
issue: - TLS server certificate using Common Name without SAN field no longer work
resolution: Replace the TLS server certificate with a new TLS server certificate using SAN field. For Openshift follow the instructions in this solution to regenerate and replace the certificates: [Regenerating Cluster Certificates](https://access.redhat.com/articles/regenerating_cluster_certificates)
root_cause: RFC 2818, published in May 2000, deprecates the use of the Common Name (CN) field in HTTPS certificates for subject name verification. Instead, it recommends using the “Subject Alternative Name” extension (SAN) of the “dns name” type. See also RFC 6125 and RFC 9110. Modern software started to drop the CN field support when validating TLS certificates so the TLS server certificate without SAN field no longer works. See also [What you need to know about HTTPS Common Name deprecation in OpenShift 4.10](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/details-on-https-common-name-deprecation-in-openshift-4.10).

title: Additional `oc adm policy` subcommand for RBAC review
issue: - Is there an `oc adm policy` sub-command of similar nature to `who-can` that will list all bindings that grant a subject specific permissions?- If not, can this be requested via RFE?
resolution: - Such request had to be directed to upstream and propose changes to the AuthN/AuthZ stack there.- Recently upstream has added support for Structured Authentication [Beta in K8s 1.30](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3331-structured-authentication-configuration#implementation-history) which brings in new capabilities such as Multiple IDP support, Multiple Aud support.- Red Hat efforts are to align with upstream and we recommend these changes to be proposed there.- Red Hat focus is now to bring-in external OIDC OAuth server which enables customers to plug-in their own OAuth server and integrate it directly with OpenShift clusters similar to how they would do with [upstream K8s](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#openid-connect-tokens).- This would mean that the built-in OpenShift OAuth server is no longer available and that identities would be managed by external IDPs by direct OIDC access to K8s ApiServer [Ref. JIRA OCPSTRAT-306](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPSTRAT-306).

title: Pods with annotation "io.kubernetes.cri-o.LinkLogs" in "ContainerCreating" state
issue: - Pods with annotation `io.kubernetes.cri-o.LinkLogs`are stuck in `ContainerCreating` state presenting the following event: Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = invalid allowed_annotation: io.kubernetes.cri-o.LinkLogs`.
resolution: 1. Remove the `machineconfig` which enables the [Log linking](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/blob/main/pkg/annotations/annotations.go) to the worker nodes: $ oc delete machineconfig 2. Wait for the nodes rollout. The pods are expected to be scheduled with no issues.
root_cause: - This issue may occur if a `machineconfig` is applied to your cluster which enables the [Log linking](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/blob/main/pkg/annotations/annotations.go) in an OCP version (4.15+) which has this feature enabled by default.- The same may occur when upgrading clusters from OCP 4.14 to 4.15 with this `machineconfig` already in place.

title: How to import support-tools image without network connectivity?
issue: - Support tools image is needed for troubleshooting but there is no network connectivity, so it cannot be pulled.- [Sosreport](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3820762) is required from an RHOCP but it cannot be taken due to the lack of network connectivity.- [Network capture with tcpdump](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5074041) is required but the node has no network connectivity.
resolution: - Pull and save the right support tools image- For OCP 4.12 and lower, use RHEL8 one ~~~ $ podman pull registry.redhat.io/rhel8/support-tools:latest $ podman save podman pull registry.redhat.io/rhel8/support-tools:latest-o support-tools.tar ~~~- For OCP 4.13 and higher, use RHEL9 one ~~~ $ podman pull registry.redhat.io/rhel9/support-tools:latest $ podman save podman pull registry.redhat.io/rhel9/support-tools:latest-o support-tools.tar ~~~- Create an ISO image with the exported TAR ~~~ $ mkisofs-r-o support-tools.iso support-tools.tar ~~~- Attach the ISO to the node machine. The way to do so (or whether it is possible at all) depends on the infra where the cluster is deployed.- Mount the filesystem in the ISO image ~~~ $ mount /dev/sr0 /mnt ~~~ Note that you may need to replace `/dev/sr0` with another device name depending on your hardware and whether there are multiple optical discs attached, either virtual or real.- Load the image into the node podman storage ~~~ $ podman load-i /mnt/support-tools.tar ~~~ Now the support tools image is available for use in the node. You may need to replace the `toolbox` command with either of these ones:- For RHOCP 4.12 and lower: ~~~ $ podman container runlabel--replace run registry.redhat.io/rhel8/support-tools:latest ~~~- For RHOCP 4.13 and newer: ~~~ podman container runlabel--replace run registry.redhat.io/rhel9/support-tools:latest ~~~
root_cause: Many troubleshooting tools, including `sos` and `tcpdump` are available in the support-tools image, which can become a problem if there is no network availability in the RHOCP node (even not connectivity to a mirror registry). This solution provides quick and easy steps on how to create an ISO that allows easily importing the image.

title: EAP 7 deployment with Service Mesh
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Does EAP 7 deployment works with Service Mesh? How to troubleshot clustered EAP 7 deployed with OSSM?
resolution: Before troubleshooting verify if the PeerAuthentication is not set for strict- preventing the EAP cluster to form ### Troubleshooting EAP 7 deployment with OSSM: Get the pods and verify istio basic pod logs: ~~~ $ oc get pod NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE eap-app-1-8ccds 1/1 Running 0 169m eap-app-1-deploy 0/1 Completed 0 169m eap-app-1-flvf4 1/1 Running 0 16m eap-app-1-hg8bl 1/1 Running 0 11m eap-app-2-build 0/1 Completed 0 170m eap-app-build-artifacts-1-build 0/1 Completed 0 171m grafana-68446ccdb8-kfnlv 2/2 Running 0 14m istio-egressgateway-7bbddfcb4-wshpg 1/1 Running 0 14m istio-ingressgateway-c845d4c87-tnsqk 1/1 Running 0 14m istiod-basic-7c45f4459-82wbl 1/1 Running 0 14m <----- verify those logs jaeger-77b57f5b77-jkdbz 2/2 Running 0 13m kiali-f6748475d-jmww9 1/1 Running 0 11m prometheus-74c96988b-6xd8q 2/2 Running 0 14m ~~~ On the example above there are the following pods: Pod | Purpose--------- |--------- eap-app-1-something | app pod eap-app-build-artifacts-1-build | build pod grafana-something | grafana pod istio-egressgateway | egres gateway pod istio-ingressgateway | ingress gateway pod istiod-basic | istiod-basic jaeger | jaeger pod kiali | kiali pod prometheus | prometheus pod The name `basic` in the istio pod comes from the SMCP and the name `eap-app` comes from the `deploymentconfig` file of the application. The pod is called istiod, which manages and injects the envoy proxies inside the microservices pods- on this case the EAP app pods. Also note that istioD is the Pilot, Citadel, and Galley components combined as a pod. ### Get the service name: ~~~ $ oc get svc NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE eap-app ClusterIP 172.30.36.244 8080/TCP 172m eap-app-ping ClusterIP None 8888/TCP 172m ~~~ And after deploying OSSM below will show: ~~~ $ oc get svc NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE eap-app ClusterIP 172.30.17.179 8080/TCP 41m eap-app-ping ClusterIP None 8888/TCP 41m grafana ClusterIP 172.30.9.4 3000/TCP 7m53s istio-egressgateway ClusterIP 172.30.202.187 80/TCP,443/TCP 7m53s istio-ingressgateway ClusterIP 172.30.182.15 15021/TCP,80/TCP,443/TCP 7m53s istiod-basic ClusterIP 172.30.209.209 15010/TCP,15012/TCP,443/TCP,15014/TCP,8188/TCP 8m23s jaeger-agent ClusterIP None 5775/UDP,5778/TCP,6831/UDP,6832/UDP 7m51s jaeger-collector ClusterIP 172.30.233.158 9411/TCP,14250/TCP,14267/TCP,14268/TCP,4317/TCP,4318/TCP 7m50s jaeger-collector-headless ClusterIP None 9411/TCP,14250/TCP,14267/TCP,14268/TCP,4317/TCP,4318/TCP 7m51s jaeger-query ClusterIP 172.30.249.166 443/TCP,16685/TCP 7m51s kiali ClusterIP 172.30.253.41 20001/TCP,9090/TCP 6m53s prometheus ClusterIP 172.30.167.111 9090/TCP 8m10s zipkin ClusterIP 172.30.22.99 9411/TCP 7m53s ~~~ ### Get the service listed on istio's pod (istiod-basic): ~~~ $ oc logs istiod-basic-7c45f4459-82wbl | grep eap-app-ping 2022-12-09T02:25:32.758259Z info ads Full push, new service eap-galleon/eap-app-ping.eap-galleon.svc.cluster.local 2022-12-09T02:28:25.104031Z info ads Push debounce stable[36] 6 for config ServiceEntry/eap-galleon/eap-app-ping.eap-galleon.svc.cluster.local and 1 more configs: 101.04607ms since last change, 193.73896ms since last push, full=true 2022-12-09T02:28:37.048186Z info ads Push debounce stable[40] 3 for config ServiceEntry/eap-galleon/eap-app-ping.eap-galleon.svc.cluster.local and 1 more configs: 100.099319ms since last change, 100.340712ms since last push, full=true 2022-12-09T02:28:41.174113Z info ads Push debounce stable[43] 3 for config ServiceEntry/eap-galleon/eap-app-ping.eap-galleon.svc.cluster.local and 1 more configs: 100.370253ms since last change, 100.374713ms since last push, full=true 2022-12-09T02:28:57.773043Z info ads Push debounce stable[44] 3 for config ServiceEntry/eap-galleon/eap-app-ping.eap-galleon.svc.cluster.local and 1 more configs: 100.32519ms since last change, 104.659631ms since last push, full=true ~~~ The name `basic` in the istio pod comes from the SMCP: ~~~ oc get smcp NAME READY STATUS PROFILES VERSION AGE basic 9/9 ComponentsReady ["default"] 2.3.0 9m45s ~~~
root_cause: **At this point OSSM integration with EAP is not fully supported.** Service Mesh itself is a pattern, Istio is the implementation. The solution [EAP 7 clustering deployments boundaries in OCP cluster](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6988927) describes the DNS_PING troubleshooting and in regards to EAP 7's deployment requirement for the DNS_PING service- the service name is set in `standalone-openshift.xml`. The solution [EAP 7 image clustering in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6980435) describes all the details about clustering in EAP 7 image. OSSM works by adding a sidecar in the application pod and another one to control the deployment, on this side car are there to proxy the traffic, where istio sidecar is the so called `envoy`. It is there to proxy the traffic to the container. So when traffic goes out: container- sidecar--> outside cluster.

title: Missing Deployment and Failed Pods for ElasticSearch After RHOCP 4 Cluster Upgrade

title: Set the application.properties for the Spring Boot applications in the RHOCP
product: Red Hat support for Spring Boot
issue: - How to set the `application.properties` for the Spring Boot applications in the RHOCP.- How to place the externalized `application.properties` file for the Spring Boot applications in the RHOCP.
resolution: Although is possible to set/change the property file at runtime, this doesn't mean SpringBoot will honor the change without reload/restart. SpringBoot will read the configuration file (`application.properties`) located in `/deployments/config` at runtime at the starting process. Therefore creating a ConfigMap and setting it to that path will allow SpringBoot to read from a configmap created file. This is illustrated on the following steps: 1. Write a ConfigMap manifest that holds the `application.properties` data as given below: ~~~ cat < springboot_cm.yaml kind: ConfigMap apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: spring-boot-external-properties #-----> Configmap name namespace: #-----> Namespace name data: application.properties: > ##The application.properties data here <...> spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://${MYSQL_HOST:localhost}:3306/db_example spring.datasource.username=springuser spring.datasource.password=ThePassword spring.datasource.driver-class-name =com.mysql.jdbc.Driver <...> EOF ~~~ 2. Create a ConfigMap from the `springboot_cm.yaml` file created in the above step: ~~~ $ oc apply-f springboot_cm.yaml ~~~ 3. Mount the `spring-boot-external-properties` ConfigMap in the Spring Boot application deployment at the `/deployments/config` path as given below: ~~~ apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment <...> spec: <...> containers: <...> volumeMounts:- mountPath: /deployments/config name: app-config-volume #-----> Volume name mentioned in the "volumes:" section volumes:- name: app-config-volume #-----> Volume name configMap: name: spring-boot-external-properties... ~~~
root_cause: OCP platform allows the setting of a file (`application.properties`) in a volume loaded by the SpringBoot pod, however, it does not control if SrpingBoot will re-load that file.

title: [RHOCP] Ingress LoadBalancer Migration from AWS CLB to AWS NLB results in error: "ELB requires at least 8 free IP addresses in each subnet"
issue: - After migrating the default Ingress load balancer from AWS CLB to AWS NLB, the new AWS NLB is not getting created in the VPC.
resolution: - The NLB/CLB is controlled via flags on the `router-default` Service in `openshift-ingress` Namespace- Checking the `openshift-ingress` Namespace events (below), this is warning about too few IP addresses available in subnet ~~~ 1h19m Warning SyncLoadBalancerFailed service/router-default Error syncing load balancer: failed to ensure load balancer: error creating load balancer: "InvalidSubnet: Not enough IP space available in subnet-032a4f9e9cefe847b. ELB requires at least 8 free IP addresses in each subnet.\n\tstatus code: 400, request id: b720fd41-f15b-41f7-xyz-xyz" ~~~- Checking the AWS Console, there are NOT 8 IPs available in each of the Subnets- Remove some EgressIPs and the CLB from AWS to increase the subnet available IPs to at minimum 8- Delete the Openshift IngressOperator and AWS CloudControllerManager Pods.- The NLB should now be provisioned correctly in OpenShift- The OpenShift Console Web UI should now be accessible and the cluster should stabilize- It may take some time until the applications become ready
root_cause: - This error is propagated back to the `openshift-ingress` Namespace with events similar to the following: ~~~ 1h19m Warning SyncLoadBalancerFailed service/router-default Error syncing load balancer: failed to ensure load balancer: error creating load balancer: "InvalidSubnet: Not enough IP space available in subnet-032a4f9e9cefe847b. ELB requires at least 8 free IP addresses in each subnet.\n\tstatus code: 400, request id: b720fd41-f15b-41f7-xyz-xyz" ~~~

title: Kube-apiserver Restart Causes Unintended Container Restarts
issue: - Container kube-apiserver in various pods is being restarted, leading to other containers in the same pod being restarted as well. For instance, `manager` container in `kmm-operator-controller` pod, `manager` container in `lvms-operator` pod, `csi-provisioner` container in `topolvm-controller` pod, and `topolvm-controller` container in `topolvm-controller` pod have been reported to restart.
resolution: Review the **previous** logs of the containers for the `kmm-operator-controller`, `lvms-operator` and `topolvm-controller` PODs in their namespaces. Identify the instances where these containers failed to connect to the API during the leader election. Understand that in a SNO cluster, if the `kube-apiserver` container is killed, other containers may fail to connect to the API and restart. If you encounter this issue, consider running a cluster with multiple control-plane/master nodes to ensure high availability of the API server. Alternatively, you can contact the LVMS/KMM operator owners to request the addition of retries for the containers before they kill themselves during the election process.
root_cause: in a SNO cluster, if the `kube-apiserver` container is killed, other containers may fail to connect to the API and restart. So the restart of the kube-apiserver does not trigger directly the restart of the containers, but it's just a side effect.

resolution: 1. The first method is to update the field directly on the resource:- Edit the target user: ~~~ $ oc edit user ~~~- Change the field `fullName:` to the desired value- Save and quit 2. The second possibility (**test with an example user first as it can be destructive**) is to delete the User and this should be re-created upon the next login event.

title: AWS node with taint NodeWithImpairedVolumes
issue: Pods cannot be scheduled on a node with `Taints: NodeWithImpairedVolumes=true:NoSchedule` Suddenly the node was marked with `NodeWithImpairedVolumes` taint and no pod can be scheduled on it. **See below:*

~~~ # oc describe node node-0.example.com ~~~ Sample Output: ~~~ Name: node-0.example.com Roles: compute Labels: beta.kubernetes.io/arch=amd64 beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type=m5.xlarge beta.kubernetes.io/os=linux kubernetes.io/hostname=node-0.example.com node-role.kubernetes.io/compute=true Annotations: volumes.kubernetes.io/controller-managed-attach-detach=true Taints: NodeWithImpairedVolumes=true:NoSchedule... status: capacity: attachable-volumes-aws-ebs: "25" ~~~
resolution: Once the issue has been resolved and the node is able to attach the volumes, run the command below to remove the taint: ~~~ $ oc adm taint node NodeWithImpairedVolumes- ~~~ [Reclaiming Resources](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/persistent_storage/persistent_storage_nfs.html#nfs-reclaiming-resources)
root_cause: When OpenShift is running on AWS and an EBS volume is stuck in attaching state for more than 30min on a node, it will be marked as unschedulable with the following taint: ~~~ taints:- effect: NoSchedule key: NodeWithImpairedVolumes value: "true" ~~~ This is due to a function called applyUnSchedulableTaint. That function applies an unschedulable taint to a node after verifying if it has volumes getting stuck in attaching state.[1] No new pod will be scheduled on a node with the taint_NodeWithImpairedVolumes=true:NoSchedule_ but pods continues running if it is already running on the node when the taint is added. [1] [AWS Provider](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d9bb58fc49d3d4e6e816a45eb8c8ac3e146621e3/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws.go#L2146)

title: How to manually add or review proxy configuration on CoreOS Openshift node ?
issue: This solution has for purpose to list every services or environnent files that are involved in proxy configuration.
resolution: **List of CoreOS files and services**- EnvironmentFile=/etc/mco/proxy.envkubelet.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf- crio.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf- pivot.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf- rpm-ostreed.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf- nodeip-configuration.service- machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service- machine-config-daemon-pull.service **Adding manually a proxy configuration** 1. Login into the booting host via ssh as core and sudo to root with "sudo su-" 2. Create the file "/etc/mco/proxy.env" with following content ~~~ #Proxy environment variables will be populated in this file. Properly #url encoded passwords with special characters will use '% '. #Systemd requires that any % used in a password be represented as #%% in a unit file since % is a prefix for macros; this restriction does not #apply for environment files. Templates that need the proxy set should use #EnvironmentFile=/etc/mco/proxy.env'. HTTP_PROXY=http://gshs- HTTPS_PROXY=http://gshs- NO_PROXY=.cluster.local,.dis-gos.s ~~~ 3. Add the following entry ~~~ [Service] EnvironmentFile=/etc/mco/proxy.env ~~~ In the files: ~~~ /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf /etc/systemd/system/crio.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf /etc/systemd/system/pivot.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf /etc/systemd/system/rpm-ostreed.service.d/10-mco-default-env.conf ~~~ 4. Add the entry "EnvironmentFile=/etc/mco/proxy.env" directly after "[Service]" in the following files ~~~ /etc/systemd/system/nodeip-configuration.service /etc/systemd/system/machine-config-daemon-firstboot.service /etc/systemd/system/machine-config-daemon-pull.service ~~~ 5. Reboot the host

title: Version not found when using OSUS and caching proxy registry in RHOCP 4
issue: - OSUS does not recognize available udpates when using a caching proxy for `quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release`.- OpenShift Update Service is not building the graph with the desired image.- `version not found in the channel` when using OpenShift Update Service.
resolution: Remove any limitation in the registry proxy that can limit the `graph-builder` to identify all the available tags present in the remote registry (generally quay.io).
root_cause: The `graph-builder` executes the `release-scrape-dockerv2` plugin that scans the given repository to search all the available tags and then looks for the label `io.openshift.release` for identifying the available release images. If the registry proxy limits the returned list of the tags, the `graph-builder` will generate a limited graph.

title: Migration Toolkit for Application Multi-tenant or multiple Tackles per namespace in OpenShift 4
issue: - Is it recommended to have a single Tackle instance and have every team working on that same instance?- Can we possibly deploy a Tackle instance per OpenShift namespace, and would this be supported?- Multiple tackle CRs with RBAC
resolution: Currently, using RBAC with multiple tackles is a no-go givn MTA current implementation that relies on SSO, which handles only one namespace. Again, that's due to the underlying SSO component not allowing multiple authentication. The specific configuration to be used with MTA will be up to the user's Migration team's discretion given the requirements in terms of users and access. One alternative could be disabling the auth- i.e. removing SSO- which would work as an alternative for multiple namespaces.
root_cause: A change in that behavior would need a Request for Feature Enhancement, RFE.

title: ArgoCD not deleting resources in OpenShift 4
issue: Deleting an ArgoCD Application from the CLI did not result in deleting the underlying resources
resolution: ArgoCD Applications need to use the [finalizer](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/finalizers/) `resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io` to have ArgoCD perform a cascading deletion and remove the underlying resource. When deleting from the CLI using `oc delete` or similar, this will not be set. A user can apply `oc patch application/-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers": ["resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io"]}}'--type merge` to add the ArgoCD finalizers directly. When applied, the finalizers will appear like so on the Application: ~~~ $ oc get apps-n openshift-gitops https-gitops-tester-oyaml apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: Application metadata: finalizers:- resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io # <=== applied finalizers name: https-gitops-tester namespace: openshift-gitops... ~~~
root_cause: Argcd makes sure to remove all the resources it manages as long as the Application Custom Resource has the finalizer. In other words, if the finalizer is not set on the Application Custom Resource cr, ArgoCD won't delete all the specific application resources. See [this reference](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user-guide/app_deletion/#about-the-deletion-finalizer): > When deleting an Application with this finalizer, the Argo CD application controller will perform a cascading delete of the Application's resources.

title: All PostgreSQL Clients Exhausted noobaa-db-pg-0 - OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: NooBaa is designed to be resource-efficient and is included as a Multcloud Object Gateway object storage feature in ODF. Some customers may not need the functionality of object storage, or uses NooBaa infrequently. In this instance, NooBaa is not utilizing unneeded resources. However, in the event NooBaa/MCG is utilized more frequently, and used to it's max potential by users/workloads (clients), NooBaa is most likely going to need performance tuning. If NooBaa has not been tuned for performance yet, and it is heavily utilized, please see the [Performance tuning guide for Multicloud Object Gateway (NooBaa)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6719951) solution. Once the above solution has been reviewed, implemented, and the below error is shown in the NooBaa logs, it may be necessary to increase the `max_connections` in the `noobaa-postgres-config` configmap to allow more connections to the db. ~~~ error: sorry, too many clients already ~~~
resolution: 1. Increase the maximum number of db connections by running the following patch command. ~~~ $ oc patch noobaa-n openshift-storage noobaa--type='merge'-p '{"spec": {"dbConf": "max_connections '1200'\n"}}' ~~~ 2. Validate the patch command was successful. **NOTE:** There will be two numbers in the configmap. The default 600, and the new/updated value. The bottom value will be the new `max_connections`. ~~~ $ oc get noobaa-n openshift-storage noobaa-o yaml | grep-A1 dbConf $ oc get cm-n openshift-storage noobaa-postgres-config-o yaml | grep connect ~~~
root_cause: When experiencing endpoint timeouts, 504 gateway, etc. and NooBaa is showing `error: sorry, too many clients already`. It may be necessary to change the dbConf max_conections to a higher value than 600 clients.

title: ovs-configuration.service fails with  cp: cannot create regular file '/run/NetworkManager/system-connections/br-ex.nmconnection'
issue: - Unable to add `RHEL` worker nodes to the cluster.- `ovs-configuration.service` is failing on `RHEL` worker node with below error: ~~~ configure-ovs.sh[1541]: + exit 1 ovs-configuration.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE ~~~
resolution: - Move the below file or take backup. ~~~ $ mv /etc/dracut.conf.d/50-network-legacy.conf /tmp ~~~- Take a backup of current initramfs before rebuilding. ~~~ $ cp /boot/initramfs-$(uname-r).img /boot/initramfs-$(uname-r).bak.$(date +%m-%d-%H%M%S).img ~~~- Run below command to rebuild the initramfs of current booted kernel. ~~~ $ dracut-v-f ~~~- Check if `NetworkManager` binaries and libraries are now part of the initramfs. ~~~ $ lsinitrd | grep-i network network-manager <---- network kernel-network-modules drwxr-xr-x 3 root root 0 Jan 15 2024 usr/lib64/NetworkManager drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 0 Jan 15 2024 usr/lib64/NetworkManager/1.40.16-15.el8_9-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 49648 Jan 15 2024 usr/lib64/NetworkManager/1.40.16-15.el8_9/libnm-device-plugin-team.so-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 306560 Jan 15 2024 usr/lib64/NetworkManager/1.40.16-15.el8_9/libnm-settings-plugin-ifcfg-rh.so drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 0 Jan 15 2024 usr/lib/systemd/network-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 462 Jan 15 2024 usr/lib/systemd/network/99-default.link-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 505 Jun 22 2018 usr/lib/systemd/system/network-online.target-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 502 Jun 22 2018 usr/lib/systemd/system/network-pre.target-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 521 Jun 22 2018 usr/lib/systemd/system/network.target-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 3579408 Jan 15 2024 usr/sbin/NetworkManager ~~~
root_cause: - Ideally `/run/NetworkManager/system-connections` should get created at run time during early boot. As `network-manager` module was missing in initramfs it would not get created.- Script ` configure-ovs.sh` would copy `br-ex.nmconnection` connection file to `/run/NetworkManager/system-connections` but as this was missing, the script failed.- The module was not getting inserted due to presence of `network-legacy` in dracut configuration. Script `/usr/lib/dracut/modules.d/40network/module-setup.sh ` is responsible to add the module. If `network-legacy` is requested it will not add `network-manager` module.- Snippet of the script: ~~~ # called by dracut depends() {echo-n "kernel-network-modules " if! dracut_module_included "network-legacy" && [-x "/usr/libexec/nm-initrd-generator"]; then <---- logic echo "network-manager" else echo "network-legacy" <------------ this is true fi return 0} ~~~

title: Virtual Machine snapshot stuck in "Source not locked" state and times out with "deadline exceeded"
issue: Snapshots timeout, never progress from Source not locked state. ~~~ apiVersion: snapshot.kubevirt.io/v1alpha1 kind: VirtualMachineSnapshot... status: conditions:- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2024-09-18T18:13:48Z" reason: Source not locked <----------------- status: "False" type: Progressing- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2024-09-18T18:13:48Z" reason: Not ready status: "False" type: Ready- lastProbeTime: null lastTransitionTime: "2024-09-18T18:19:17Z" reason: snapshot deadline exceeded <------------ status: "True" type: Failure ~~~
resolution: You can workaround the issue by deleting the all failed snapshots, then making a trivial modification to the Virtual Machine yaml. 1. In the OCP console, open the VM under the "Virtualization" tab in the administrator view 2. Select VMs, and select the appropriate namespace 3. Select the VM having issues saving snapshots 4. In the snapshots list, delete all the failed snapshots 5. Go to the Yaml tab, then simply hit save. 6. Verify the VM yaml has a `spec.architecture` field You can also do this using the CLI by using `oc delete-n vmsnapshot ` on each failed snapshot, and then adding a random annotation to the virtual machine and deleting it. For example: `oc annotate-n vm forceUpdate=true` then remove it with `oc annotate-n vm forceUpdate-`.
root_cause: This bu was introduced with the addition multi-arch support. The controller thinks the VirtualMachine object can't be updated do to some overly strict validation checks, so it doesn't apply some necessary updates. When one tries to create a snapshot, it fails to add the finalizer because of some logic to prevent it from updating the object while a snapshot is in progress. The effect is that the snapshot ends up in a sort of deadlock. It eventually just times out. This is being corrected in issue [CNV-48769- Suspected potential race between adding finalizer and SnapshotInProgress](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-48769).

title: Upgrading to or installing a specific version of an operator fails with ResolutionFailed in RHOCP 4
issue: - An operator does not list available upgrades while an upgrade is publicly available.- Re-installing the same operator from scratch on the publicly available newer version does not succeed.
resolution: In case the `ResolutionFailed` error type (see also **Diagnostic Steps**) cannot be solved by [restarting the catalog-operator](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6777761) or [recreating the `Subscrition` and `CSV` resources.](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6603001) and there are "bundle unpacking" `Jobs` in the `openshift-marketplace` namespace (see also **Diagnostic Steps**), delete these jobs: **Note:**: *replace ` ` accordingly* ~~~ $ oc get job-n openshift-marketplace-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].value|contains (" ")) |.metadata.name'|xargs-n1 oc delete job-n openshift-marketplace ~~~ Then, restart both the `catalog-operator` and `olm-operator` pods: ~~~ $ oc delete pods-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager-l app=catalog-operator $ oc delete pods-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager-l app=olm-operator ~~~
root_cause: The OLM and the Catalog-Operator (CO) work together to install an Operator by listen to the Subscription resource. After the subscription is created, the CO inside the `openshift-marketplace` namespace will create a configmap, which creates a job. The job has ownership the configmap and both will have the same name, which is a hash and not a random number- that's why it can collide. The configmap will bring the CSV of the Operator to be installed and the CRD listed in a hash, below an example that can be used to read the CSV/CRD created via this configmap: Example: ~~~ $ oc get job NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE 67e966fb6b65855836ede5dad5080d78222bdd01091d14d17171e7f9db9be65 1/1 8s 34h <--------- $ oc get cm NAME DATA AGE.. 67e966fb6b65855836ede5dad5080d78222bdd01091d14d17171e7f9db9be65 6 34h <---------------------------- ~~~ The above shows the configmap and the job have the same name and that this specific operator installed has 1 CSV and 5 CRDs. To see the CSV and the CRD installed- open the configmap and it will be in binary: ~~~ $ oc get cm 67e966fb6b65855836ede5dad5080d78222bdd01091d14d17171e7f9db9be65-o yaml apiVersion: v1 binaryData: datagrid.clusterserviceversion.yaml: infinispan.org_backups.yaml: infinispan.org_batches.yaml: infinispan.org_caches.yaml: infinispan.org_infinispans.yaml: infinispan.org_restores.yaml ~~~ From the CRD details above, export to a file and do the following to read it: ~~~ 55386 base64-d crd.file 55387 base64-d crd.file > crd.b64 55388 base64-d crd.b64 55389 base64-d crd.b64 > crd.gz 55390 gunzip crd.gz 55391 ls-ltr 55392 cat crd ~~~ Finally, as explained in the solution [How can Operators be updated independently from each other?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6389681) install plans (IPs) will have all resources for a single OperatorGroup done in one install, and by default, all operators in a namespace are put into the same OperatorGroup (OG), in a 1:many for the operators on that namespace. This was the object of discussions on jira: [OCPBUGS-33348](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-33348).

The `keepalived-monitor` and the `haproxy` pods in the `openshift-vsphere-infra` namespace are printing as `INFO` logs that should be `DEBUG`
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in different bugs: For "logs of runtimecfg node-ip detection too verbose":- For OpenShift 4.16 bug [OCPBUGS-29919](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-29919) and delivered a fix in OpenShift 4.16.0 through errata [RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041)- For OpenShift 4.15 bug [OCPBUGS-32024](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-32024) and delivered a fix in OpenShift 4.15.11 through errata [RHSA-2024:2068](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:2068)- For OpenShift 4.14 bug [OCPBUGS-32524](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-32524) and delivered a fix in OpenShift 4.14.25 through errata [RHBA-2024:2789](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:2789) For "Logs of haproxy too verbose":- For OpenShift 4.16 bug [OCPBUGS-32028](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-32028) and delivered a fix in OpenShift 4.16.0 through errata [RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041)- For OpenShift 4.15 bug [OCPBUGS-32092](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-32092) and delivered a fix in OpenShift 4.15.28 through errata [RHSA-2024:3889](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3889)- For OpenShift 4.14 bug [OCPBUGS-35322](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-35322) and delivered a fix in OpenShift 4.14.38 throug errata [RHSA-2024:7184](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:7184) #### Workaround ##### Workaround 1. Collecting the logs, but reducing the log retention for this namespace If using Elasticsearch as Log Storage, it could be configured log retention per namespace as described in the article ["Configure log retention per namespace for OpenShift Elasticsearch log store"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7032734) for reducing the log retention time for the namespace `openshift-vsphere-infra`. If using Loki as Log Storage, it could configured as detailed in the documentation section ["Enabling stream-based retention with Loki"](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/observability/logging/log_storage/cluster-logging-loki.html#logging-loki-retention_cluster-logging-loki). ##### Workaround 2. Not collecting the logs This is detailed in the Documentation section ["Filtering logs by content"](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/observability/logging/performance_reliability/logging-content-filtering.html#logging-content-filter-drop-records_logging-content-filtering). An example is shared below: ``` apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogForwarder metadata: name: namespace: spec: filters:- drop:- test:- field:.kubernetes.namespace_name matches: openshift-vsphere-infra name: drop-vsphere-infra-logs type: drop pipelines:- filterRefs:- drop-vsphere-infra-logs inputRefs:- infrastructure- application name: exclude-vsphere-infra-logs outputRefs:- default ``` For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: The `keepalived-monitor` and the `haproxy` pods in the `openshift-vsphere-infra` namespace are printing as `INFO` logs that should be `DEBUG`.

title: How to Verify High Availability (HA) in OpenShift Virtualization using Console and CLI
issue: - Need to verify the high availability (HA) of their OpenShift Virtualization cluster to ensure that the control plane and critical components are resilient against node failures.- How can I verify if the cluster is Highly available?
resolution: 1. Using OpenShift Console: ~~~ Log in to the OpenShift Web Console Navigate to the “Administration” Section Select “Cluster Settings”, here you will find details about the cluster’s configuration. Look for settings or tab related to “Infrastructure” This will show the control plane topology, which indicates whether your control plane is in “HighlyAvailable” mode. ~~~ 2. Using the oc Command Line Tool ~~~ $ oc get infrastructure cluster-o jsonpath='{.status.controlPlaneTopology}' ~~~ The possible values for this field are:- HighlyAvailable: Indicates that the control plane is set up for high availability (multiple control plane nodes).- SingleReplica: Indicates that the control plane is not highly available (only a single control plane node). If the output shows HighlyAvailable, it means your OpenShift control plane is set up in an HA mode. If it shows SingleReplica, it indicates a non-HA setup.
root_cause: This is a standard verification process, not linked to a specific issue. However, verifying HA is crucial after initial setup, upgrades, or changes to the cluster configuration to ensure resilience and fault tolerance.

title: ImageContentSourcePolicy is not respected by CRIO while pulling images on a disconnected Red Hat Openshift Container Platform.
issue: - Despite having applied in the cluster an ImageContentSourcePolicy with a healthy mirror registry it is not getting respected and images cannot be pulled.- Pods are stuck in "ImagePullBackOff" state.
resolution: This article covers the situation where multiple mirror targets are defined inside the /etc/containers/registries.conf file of the node. In that case if the first target in the row is down and the second is healthy but not respected it would be needed to somehow make the first mirror target to be completely shut down or unreachable from network perspective. For the reason behind this please check Root Cause section.
root_cause: The logic in the code of the containers library that is being used from the pulling client "CRI-O" to pick the next mirror target upon pulling failure is not functioning as expected under specific circumstances. These circumstances include the case where the image is found in the mirror target but the blobs cannot be downloaded. This can happen in case there is a mirror registry deployed as container and has lost connectivity with its storage. In a specific case this issue was observed the error that was not considered as valid for the CRI-O service to pick the next available mirror target despite it was not able to pull the image was the below but might be other cases/errors as well that can result to the same situation. ~~~ parsing image configuration: fetching blob: received unexpected HTTP status: 502 Bad Gateway ~~~

title: How to locate stale resources when pod is terminated forcefully
issue: - When the pod is either stuck in `terminating` state or deleted with `--force` option, some stale resources are present on node.
resolution: - To remove any `stale` resources that are present on the node, first find the `podUID` and `containerID` of the terminated pod. If any volume is attached to the pod, then find the `volumeHandle` from the PersistentVolume.- To check if any stale `containers` are present on the node where the pod was previously configured, look for the `containerID` in the below directory. ~~~ $ ls-l /var/lib/container/storage/overlay-containers $ rm /var/lib/container/storage/overlay-containers/ ~~~- To check if any stale `pod` is present on the node, check for `podUID` in the below directory. ~~~ $ ls-l /var/lib/kubelet/pods $ rm /var/lib/kubelet/pods/ ~~~- To check if any stale `mounts` are present on the node, check for either `podUID` or `volumeHandle` in the below command. ~~~ $ mount | grep-i $ mount | grep-i $ umount ~~~
root_cause: - When a pod is `terminated` abruptly, the entire pod data is not cleared properly. Due to that some `resources` such as pod UID, containerIDs and stale mounts can be present on the `node` where terminated pod was scheduled.- Resources will still be present on the node even if the pod is `forcefully` deleted and scheduled on another node.

title: Resources Fail to be Garbage Collected
issue: Stale or deleted resources are not garbage collected. As a result, the number of resources will continue to grow. For example, pods that complete are never garbage collected.
resolution: 1. Find the log line in the `kube-controller-manager` containing `syncing garbage collector with updated resources from discovery`. 2. For each mentioned 'Resource', run `oc get resource-name`. If `oc` fails with `Internal error occurred: error resolving resource`, continue to the next step. 3. Run `oc edit crd resource-name` 4. If the resource features a `conversion` Webhook, confirm that the `service` mentioned by the Webhook exists. If it doesn't, the Webhook is a possible cause of the failing garbage collection. **NOTE**: A bash script [garbage_collector_check.sh](https://access.redhat.com/node/6761971/40/0/23133072) has been attached to this Solution to help automate the identification of Resources exhibiting the behavior described here. This script will use `oc` to search logs on your cluster and provide a list of resource names to be edited, this may take some time to run completely. A possible workaround is to delete the `conversion` portion of the CRD specification followed by deleting the CRD. The operator that installed the CRD may also need to be reinstalled.
root_cause: When there are failing webhooks, the garbage collector cannot discover the resource and instead of ignoring the pruned resources, it will stop garbage collecting altogether. Work is being done to address this issue. Progress can be followed here:- [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/WRKLDS-358](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/WRKLDS-358)- [https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105705](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105705)

title: Tuning MSS value in Haproxy Configuration
issue: Is there a way to tune `MSS` value in `Haproxy` Configuration?
resolution: No, there is no way to tune `MSS` value in `Haproxy` Configuration. `MSS` size totally depends on the value of the underlying `MTU` and it is generally 40 less than the set `MTU` i.e. if your `MTU` is 1500 then `MSS` is `MTU`-40 i.e. 1460

title: Bond Creation failed due to different NIC names using NNCP
issue: - `NNCP` is giving below error when trying to create `bond`: ~~~ $ oc get nnce-o yaml "error reconciling NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy on node node3 at desired state apply: \"\",\n failed to execute nmstatectl set--no-commit--timeout 480: 'exit status 1' '' 'Using 'set' is deprecated, use 'apply' instead... [2024-04-23T09:06:56Z INFO nmstate::iface] Include interface eno16495np0 to edit as its controller required so NmstateError: InvalidArgument: Controller interface bond1 is holding unknown port ens1f1np1 ~~~
resolution: - Change the label on the nodes having different interface names and run the nncp on that particular node. For example, let's say node02 and node03 have different interface names we can use the below command to label them and apply the nmstate to the nodes having the below label ~~~ # oc label node node02 node03 mylabel=myvalue ~~~- change the `NIC` name to the expected name through the udev method using the steps given in section 1.5 in the production [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html/configuring_and_managing_networking/consistent-network-interface-device-naming_configuring-and-managing-networking).
root_cause: - `NIC` name appears as an alternate name on the node system. As per the solution [article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6964829), the feature `AlternativeNamesPolicy` is added from `RHEL 8.5` and above version where it allows the feature to create alternate names for existing interfaces. It is a space-separated list of policies by which the interface's alternative names should be set. Each of the policies may fail, and all successful policies are used. The available policies are "database", "onboard", "slot", "path", and "mac". If the `kernel` does not support the alternative names, then this setting will be ignored.

title: Failed to deploy openstack dataplane - Podman Authentication Fails
issue: Using the `download-cache` service prevents Podman from pulling images for data plane deployment
resolution: Update to 18.0.1 (openstack operator version 1.0.2) to resolve/fix the above bug. Alternatively, with 1.0.2 (the updated containers) manually force/edit the CSV (ClusterServiceVersion) of the openstack-operator to make the version equal to the original, but with new containers (essentially pretending this is a green field deployment and not an update). This should also unblock the deployment and allow the Controlplane to reconcile. Then complete dataplane deployment. A third option would be to re-install the Controlplane with with 18.0.1 (1.0.2).
root_cause: The dataplane deployment is missing or has invalid podman credentials on the dataplane hosts. Specifically the logs for the pods/run-os-data-plane-deploy-openstack-data-plane- in the openstack namespace all show this error.

title: In OpenShift 4 an IngressController is degraded because the LoadBalancer service is pending
issue: The cluster upgrade is halted because of the error: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-ingress-operator logs ingress-operator-7b4fdfc769-pvfdg-c ingress-operator... 2024-10-04T18:33:24.206986862Z 2024-10-04T18:33:24.206Z ERROR operator.ingress_controller controller/controller.go:119 got retryable error; requeueing {"after": "1m0s", "error": "IngressController is degraded: LoadBalancerReady=False (LoadBalancerPending: The LoadBalancer service is pending)"} ~~~
resolution: In the service, add the annotation to configure the IP source: ~~~ annotations: metallb.universe.tf/address-pool: ip-addresspool-ingress-controllers ~~~
root_cause: The annotation to configure the source IP was missing.

title: How to configure kdump over remote target path (NFS) on Red Hat CoreOS
issue: - Unable to capture vmcore over NFS on Red Hat CoreOS, seeing below error on console: ~~~ mount /kdumproot bad option or mount.nfs Protocol not supported or Bad kdump network destination: xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx ~~~
resolution: - Mention the below parameters in `/etc/kdump.conf` to add necessary `nfs` modules and binaries to `kdump` initramfs. ~~~ extra_bins /sbin/mount.nfs extra_modules nfs nfsv3 nfs_layout_nfsv41_files blocklayoutdriver nfs_layout_flexfiles nfs_layout_nfsv41_files ~~~- Restart kdump service for cluster using SDN network. ~~~ $ systemctl restart kdump ~~~ **Note: For clusters using OVN network, a reboot is needed**
root_cause: - Necessary `nfs` kernel modules and system binaries supporting `nfs` mount functionality were not part of kdump initramfs which would cause the nfs mount to fail.- The `nfs` module is being omitted during the creation of kdump initramfs as `nfs` on root is not supported. This is done as a preventive measure on coreos. The below file plays a role while creating initramfs. ~~~ $ cat /lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/coreos-omits.conf # We don't support root on NFS, so we don't need it in the initramfs. It also # conflicts with /var mount support in ignition because NFS tries to mount stuff # title: Apply Custom Manifest for Hosted Control Planes in OpenShift
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - How to partition disks of bare metal hosted control plane (hypershift) nodes at cluster creation time.
resolution: This can be done as part of configuring a NodePool. After nodes are deployed using the discovery ISO and are part of an inventory, the hosted control plane is created and with it a NodePool. A machine config can be injected as a configmap in the hosted cluster's namespace. Example of a ConfigMap with an embedded MachineConfig that partitions the disk: ~~~ kind: ConfigMap apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: hcp-cluster-mcp namespace: clusters data: config: | apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 98-test-partition spec: config: ignition: version: 3.4.0 storage: disks:- device: /dev/sdb partitions:- label: test number: 1 sizeMiB: 1024 filesystems:- device: /dev/disk/by-partlabel/test format: xfs mountOptions:- defaults path: /test systemd: units:- contents: |- # Generated by Butane [Unit] Requires=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-test.service After=systemd-fsck@dev-disk-by\x2dpartlabel-test.service [Mount] Where=/test What=/dev/disk/by-partlabel/test Type=xfs Options=defaults [Install] RequiredBy=local-fs.target enabled: true name: test.mount ~~~ Then, configure the NodePool to use this config. The ConfigMap is expected to be created under the clusters namespace. The NodePool initially is scaled down to 0. NodePool example: ~~~ spec: arch: amd64 clusterName: hcp-cluster config:- name: hcp-cluster-mcp < < < management: autoRepair: false replace: rollingUpdate: maxSurge: 1 maxUnavailable: 0 strategy: RollingUpdate upgradeType: InPlace nodeDrainTimeout: 0s platform: type: Agent release: image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.15.17-x86_64 replicas: 2 < < < ~~~ Then when the NodePool is scaled up, it will begin the binding process. They will obtain their ignition config and begin installation.
root_cause: If the agent-install.yaml is edited to partition drives, the installation will fail as this cannot be modified after the install has begun.

title: Editing PersistentVolumes in Azure hosted storage fails with invalid credentials error, despite confirming accurate credentials
issue: - Attempts to expand, create, or otherwise change PersistentVolumes in a cluster with Azure backed storage fail.
resolution: - If the diagnostic **step 2** failed, validating the credential against the Azure portal. That means that the credentials set in the `kube-system/azure-credentials` secret needs to be updated. ``` # Archiving the current config: $ oc get secret-n kube-system azure-credentials-o yaml > azure-credentials.yaml # Editing the secret: $ oc edit secret-n kube-system azure-credentials ```- If the diagnostic **step 3** failed, validating that the configmap `openshift-config/cloud-provider-config` has the right config. That means that the configmap needs to be updated: ``` # Archiving the current config: $ oc get configmap-n openshift-config cloud-provider-config-o yaml > cloud-provider-config.yaml # Editing the configmap: $ oc edit configmap-n openshift-config cloud-provider-config ```
root_cause: The Azure cloud credentials may need to be stored in different places (secret and configMap) in the RHOCP configuration, and so they may need to be updated in all places when renewed.

title: Error performing deploy_step write_image: Command execution failed: Unable to stat device /dev/dm-0p2 after attempting to verify 3 times
issue: - After OSP 17.1 FFU, scaling out the the new nodes fails at ironic with: ~~~ ERROR ironic.conductor.utils [-] Agent returned error for deploy step {'step': 'write_image', 'priority': 80, 'argsinfo': None, 'interface': 'deploy'} on node xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx: Error performing deploy_step write_image: Command execution failed: Unable to stat device /dev/dm-0p2 after attempting to verify 3 times.. ~~~- Hardware is Cisco UCS-B200-M5 blades using no local disks and booting on multipathed devices- When compute host (or controller node or any other role) is booting, it's stuck on a single cursor (not blinking;)) and nothing happens. If you remove the console from the kernel argument at boot time by pressing "esc" or "shift", it might be on the emergency shell or hung.
resolution: - At the time of this writting, this issue was tracked through [RHBZ #2279328](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2279328). If you hit this issue or similar, please open a support case with us whilst refering to this article or BZ.- There is a workaround that you can apply to the overcloud image with the following script ran as root: ~~~ #make sure you have /tmp/overcloud-hardened-uefi-full.qcow2 guestmount-a /tmp/overcloud-hardened-uefi-full.qcow2-m /dev/vg/lv_root /mnt #create a simple multipath.conf so boot disk are under multipathd management cat < /mnt/etc/multipath.conf defaults {user_friendly_names yes find_multipaths yes max_fds 8192 polling_interval 5 queue_without_daemon no} EOF #add rd.multipath=default to default grub sed-i 's/no_timer_check/rd.multipath=default no_timer_check/' /mnt/etc/default/grub umount /mnt #actual workaround for non-booting hosts guestmount-a /tmp/overcloud-hardened-uefi-full.qcow2-m /dev/sda3 /mnt sed-i 's/mkfs_boot/mkfs_boot rd.multipath=default/g' /mnt/loader/entries/* umount /mnt # convert to raw (customer did, this is not necessary qemu-img convert-O raw /tmp/overcloud-hardened-uefi-full.qcow2 /tmp/overcloud-hardened-uefi-full.raw #copy the image to /home/stack/images cp /tmp/overcloud-hardened-uefi-full.* /home/stack/images # delete stale cache files in /var/lib/ironic find /var/lib/ironic-name \*.converted-exec rm-rf {} \; source /home/stack/stackrc # upload it to "glance" openstack overcloud image upload--update-existing--image-path /home/stack/images/ ~~~ *NOTE: The above script should work but wasn't tested*
root_cause: - Kernel arguments need to have `rd.multipath=default` in order to successfully boot from multipathed devices.
