title: The `metal3-baremetal-operator` pod fails to start in RHOCP4 due to kasten operator SCC conflict
issue: - The `metal3-baremetal-operator` pod in `CreateContainerConfigError` state with the below mentioned error: ~~~ message: 'container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root (pod: "metal3-baremetal-operator-fddxxx8-4xxqh_openshift-machine-api(530609fb-xxx-43d0-xx-2f6277xxx7)", container: metal3-baremetal-operator)' reason: CreateContainerConfigError hostIP: 172.x.x.70 phase: Pending ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [Bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-30919). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. ####Workaround 1. Make a copy of the `hostnetwork-v2` Security Context Constraint (SCC) with a custom name, such as `hostnetwork-v2-custom`. 2. Assign the newly created SCC to the service account by running the following command: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user hostnetwork-v2-custom system:serviceaccount:openshift-machine-api:cluster-baremetal-operator ~~~ 3. Edit the SCC to increase the priority value to `1`. 4. Restart the associated pod for the changes to take effect. **Note: If the issue still persists, Kindly reach out to the vendor.**
root_cause: After installing the Kasten backup operator from Veeam, the **metal3-baremetal-operator** pod fails to start because it requires root access. The Kasten applies its own Security Context Constraint (SCC) to the pod, which doesn't provide the necessary privileges. When attempting to change the **SCC to default**, it immediately reverts to Kasten's SCC.

title: Kafka mirror maker 2 fails with signature failed check
issue: We are trying to setup mirror maker between two kafka clusters and Kafka mirror maker 2 fails with signature failed check
resolution: - First, begin with the examples shipped is a good start. `amq-streams-2.7.0-ocp-install-examples/examples/mirror-maker/kafka-mirror-maker-2.yaml` & `amq-streams-2.7.0-ocp-install-examples/examples/mirror-maker/kafka-mirror-maker-2-tls.yaml` Do not need a fully fresh OCP, just need to create a new project. then create the kafka related resources. ~~~ oc new-project amqs oc create-f examples/mirror-maker/kafka-source.yaml oc create-f examples/mirror-maker/kafka-target.yaml oc create-f examples/mirror-maker/kafka-mirror-maker-2-tls.yaml ~~~- Second, in the sample `amq-streams-2.7.0-ocp-install-examples/examples/mirror-maker/kafka-mirror-maker-2-tls.yaml`: The key point for the certificate is the part, there are 2 certificates which are from the 2 clusters in same ocp project. ~~~- alias: "cluster-a" # Source cluster bootstrapServers: cluster-a-kafka-bootstrap:9093 tls: trustedCertificates:- secretName: cluster-a-cluster-ca-cert certificate: ca.crt- alias: "cluster-b" # Target cluster bootstrapServers: cluster-b-kafka-bootstrap:9093 tls: trustedCertificates:- secretName: cluster-b-cluster-ca-cert certificate: ca.crt ~~~ Need to setup 2 kafka yaml definitions in one ocp project. Or if using the kafka clusters in another project, then need to set the bootstrapservers in this format: `${kafkaClusterName}.${projectName}.svc` eg: `my-cluster-kafka-bootstrap.myproject.svc:9093`- Third, pls make sure the secrets of these 2 clusters exists in the MM2 namespace. If want to use custom certificate, Please follow the guide: [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.7/html/deploying_and_managing_streams_for_apache_kafka_on_openshift/security-str#security-using-your-own-certificates-str](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.7/html/deploying_and_managing_streams_for_apache_kafka_on_openshift/security-str#security-using-your-own-certificates-str)

title: The NO_PROXY parameter does not work in Red Hat Developer Hub
issue: OpenShift clusters are behind a corporate firewall and can't directly reach out to the Internet. In order to allow some plugins to reach out of the network the HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY environment variables has been set to use the Internet Proxies in the Backstage CRD and to keep all the internal calls functional. However the plugins that needed to reach out to the Internet worked fine, but all the calls internally started failing with 504 Gateway timeouts because they are not able to reach their destination since they were using the Internet proxies as well. Following there is the NO_PROXY parameter used in this configuration: ~~~ NO_PROXY='.cluster.local,.svc,10.3.131.0/24,10.56.0.0/14,127.0.0.1,172.29.0.0/16,api-int.ocp-hdc-sandbox-ext-1.paas.example.com,is.example.com,localhost,example.com,172.29.0.1,code.example.com' ~~~ When the Backstage Plugins tries to request the "https://code.example.com/...", it goes through the proxy and does not respect the NO_PROXY parameter. Backstage Plugins appear to be able to use the HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY ok, but do not seem to be working with NO_PROXY.
resolution: To avoid the queries to any subdomain **example.com** it should use **.example.com** (with the dot). **Note**: If the *https://code.example.com/...* did not work, maybe at some point there was an internal query to a different domain than *code.example.com* and it failed.
root_cause: The **NO_PROXY** variable is a comma-separated list of domains, IP addresses, or domain suffixes. Each entry defines a rule that matches hosts which should bypass the proxy:- Hostname or domain: To bypass the proxy for a specific domain, list the full domain (e.g., example.com).- IP address: To bypass the proxy for specific IP addresses, you can list them (e.g., 192.168.0.1).- Subnet: To bypass the proxy for a range of IPs, you can use CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.0.0/16).- Domain suffix: To bypass the proxy for all subdomains of a domain, prepend a dot (e.g.,.example.com). Example: NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,.example.com,192.168.1.0/24 The above configuration means that:- Requests to localhost and 127.0.0.1 will bypass the proxy.- Any subdomain of example.com (e.g., api.example.com, www.example.com) will bypass the proxy.- Any IP in the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet will also bypass the proxy. To avoid the queries to any subdomain "example.com" it should use ".example.com" (with the dot).

title: What version of HAProxy is used in the Ingress Controller of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?
issue: - What version of HAProxy is used in the Ingress Controller of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?
resolution: The following table depicts which HAProxy version is used by default on the ingress controller of each OpenShift version. | OpenShift version | HAProxy version | |-------------------|-----------------| | 4.10- 4.13 | 2.2 | | 4.14- 4.15 | 2.6 | | 4.16+ | 2.8 | Note that this table may need to be updated as new versions are released.
root_cause: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform uses HAProxy as the central element of its default ingress controller (also known as OpenShift Router). So it may become necessary to know which HAProxy version is in use, specially for troubleshooting scenarios.

title: Installing CLO v6 goes in pending state due to issue with CRD schema if cluster has LFME deployed in RHOL4
issue: - During the installation process of `ClusterLoggingOperator(CLO)` v6, the `CSV` of v6.0.0 goes into `pending` state, due to `CRD` Schema problem if the cluster has LogFileMetricExporter(LFME) instance deployed in the previous version i.e RHOL version 5.9 or lower. ~~~ error validating existing CRs against new CRD's schema for "logfilemetricexporters.logging.openshift.io": error validating custom resource against new schema for LogFileMetricExporter openshift-logging/instance: [[].status.conditions[0].message: Required value, [].status.conditions[0].reason: Required value] ~~~![Warning](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/screenshot_2024-09-29_at_12.49.05.png)- CSV for the CLO v6 goes in pending state. ~~~ $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE cluster-logging.v6.0.0 Red Hat OpenShift Logging 6.0.0 Pending ~~~
resolution: Follow the steps mentioned below to workaround the problem. 1. Take the `backup` of the existing LFME instance: ~~~ $ oc get lfme instance-o yaml-n openshift-logging > LFME.yaml ~~~ 2. `Delete` the `LFME` instance: ~~~ $ oc delete lfme instance-n openshift-logging ~~~ 3. `Uninstall` the CSV for CLO v6: ~~~ $ oc delete csv cluster-logging.v6.0.0-n openshift-logging ~~~ 4. Now `Install` CLO v6, `Operator--> Operator Hub--> Red Hat OpenShift Logging`. 5. Once the Operator installation is done, Recreate the LFME instance: ~~~ $ oc apply-f LFME.yaml ~~~
root_cause: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [Log-6201](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6201). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: Long execution time of the [POST] /server/containers/{containerId}/cases/instances/{caseId}/caseFile command
issue: - Long execution time of the `[POST] /server/containers/{containerId}/cases/instances/{caseId}/caseFile` REST API command;- Execution of the `POST /server/containers/{containerId}/cases/instances/{caseId}/caseFile` command takes 17-18 seconds and during that time the following two queries are executed more than 800 times for different process instance id: select processins0_.InstanceId as Instance1_31_0_, processins0_.lastModificationDate as lastModi2_31_0_, processins0_.lastReadDate as lastRead3_31_0_, processins0_.processId as processI4_31_0_, processins0_.processInstanceByteArray as processI5_31_0_, processins0_.startDate as startDat6_31_0_, processins0_.state as state7_31_0_, processins0_.OPTLOCK as OPTLOCK8_31_0_ from ProcessInstanceInfo processins0_ where processins0_.InstanceId=? and select contextmap0_.mappingId as mappingI1_8_, contextmap0_.CONTEXT_ID as CONTEXT_2_8_, contextmap0_.KSESSION_ID as KSESSION3_8_, contextmap0_.OWNER_ID as OWNER_ID4_8_, contextmap0_.OPTLOCK as OPTLOCK5_8_ from ContextMappingInfo contextmap0_ where contextmap0_.CONTEXT_ID=? and contextmap0_.OWNER_ID=?- The `handleScore` signal defined with the `default` scope in the case definition causes delay due to notifying all selected process instances and not only one:![handleScore](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/handlescore.png)
resolution: To change the default behaviour, change the scope of the `handleScore` from `default` to `process instance` since this signal is supposed to just trigger the subprocess for the case.
root_cause: That API ends up executing following command: [AddDataCaseFileInstanceCommand.java](https://github.com/kiegroup/jbpm/blob/main/jbpm-case-mgmt/jbpm-case-mgmt-impl/src/main/java/org/jbpm/casemgmt/impl/command/AddDataCaseFileInstanceCommand.java). When the following SQL is executed where `?` is replaced with `handleScore`: ~~~ select processins0_.InstanceId as col_0_0_ from ProcessInstanceInfo processins0_ inner join EventTypes eventtypes1_ on processins0_.InstanceId=eventtypes1_.InstanceId where eventtypes1_.element=? ~~~ as a result there are a lot of process instances registered to listen for this signal. This causes sending notifications to all registered process instances which as a consequence causes a delay. This is not a bug.

title: RHCS 6 - BLUESTORE_NO_PER_POOL_OMAP  OSD(s) reporting legacy (not per-pool) BlueStore omap usage stats
issue: - After upgrade from Red Hat Ceph Storage 5 to version 6, or from Red Hat Openshift Data Foundation 4.12 to version 4.13 the following errors are observed: ~~~ $ ceph health detail HEALTH_WARN 5 OSD(s) reporting legacy (not per-pool) BlueStore omap usage stats [WRN] BLUESTORE_NO_PER_POOL_OMAP: 5 OSD(s) reporting legacy (not per-pool) BlueStore omap usage stats osd.0 legacy (not per-pool) omap detected, suggest to run store repair to benefit from per-pool omap usage statistics osd.2 legacy (not per-pool) omap detected, suggest to run store repair to benefit from per-pool omap usage statistics osd.3 legacy (not per-pool) omap detected, suggest to run store repair to benefit from per-pool omap usage statistics osd.4 legacy (not per-pool) omap detected, suggest to run store repair to benefit from per-pool omap usage statistics osd.5 legacy (not per-pool) omap detected, suggest to run store repair to benefit from per-pool omap usage statistics ~~~- In the Red Hat Openshift Data Foundation 4.13 web console the following error is shown: ``` x OSD(s) reporting legacy (not per-pool) bluestore omap usage stats ```
resolution: **NOTE: The following procedure will NOT cause any data deletion** The "bluestore_fsck_quick_fix_on_mount=true" will trigger omap fix run to adjust to new version, the time it takes to finish depends on the size of the OMAP on the individual OSDs and its disk performance, if the OMAP size in GB it is recommended to also set noout flag in order to avoid OSDs to be set out after 600 seconds being in down state and trigger data rebalance. # For Red Hat Ceph Storage (RHCS) 6 1. Set the following value: ~~~ $ ceph osd set noout $ ceph config set osd bluestore_fsck_quick_fix_on_mount true ~~~ 2. Restart all OSDs- **Note: one node at a time and always wait for all PGs to be active+clean before restarting OSDs on another node** ~~~ $ ceph-s ~~~ 3. After restart of all OSDs, remove the configuration: ~~~ $ ceph config rm osd bluestore_fsck_quick_fix_on_mount $ ceph osd unset noout ~~~ # For Red Hat Openshift Data Foundation (RHODF) 4.13 1. Enable the Rook-Ceph Toolbox by following the article [Configuring the Rook-Ceph Toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891) and rsh connect to the Pod ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-storage rsh "$(oc get pods-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o name)" ~~~ 2. Once connected to the Rook-Ceph Toolbox Pod, set the following option: ~~~ $ ceph osd set noout $ ceph config set osd bluestore_fsck_quick_fix_on_mount true # This should be issued inside the Rook-Ceph Toolbox Pod ~~~ 3. Restart all OSDs by deleting their Pods. This will trigger a Pod restart- **Note: one Pod at a time and always wait for all PGs to be active+clean before restarting any other OSDs from any other Pod/Node** ~~~ $ oc delete pod/ $ oc-n openshift-storage rsh "$(oc get pods-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o name)" $ ceph-s # This should be issued inside the Rook-Ceph Toolbox Pod ~~~ 4. Once it is fixed for all OSDs, remove the config it via the Rook-Ceph Toolbox ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-storage rsh "$(oc get pods-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o name)" $ ceph config rm osd bluestore_fsck_quick_fix_on_mount # This should be issued inside the Rook-Ceph Toolbox Pod $ ceph osd unset noout ~~~
root_cause: One or more OSDs have volumes that were created prior to the Octopus release. In Octopus and later releases, BlueStore tracks omap space utilization by pool. If there are any BlueStore OSDs that do not have the new tracking enabled, the cluster will report an approximate value for per-pool omap usage based on the most recent deep scrub. The OSDs can be updated to track by pool by stopping each OSD, running a repair operation, and then restarting the OSD. Please check the [What are the Red Hat Ceph Storage releases and corresponding Ceph package versions?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2045583) article to track down Red Hat Container Storage vs Ceph Upstream versioning.

title: image pull failing with manifest unknown in disconnect environment
issue: - PODs are failing to pull the desired image from the disconnected mirror registry.
resolution: - Using skopeo to copy the image from the Public source into the Private Registry should allow the PODs to pull the image. 1. Setting the variable using the event message: ``` IMAGE_SHA256_VALUE= PUBLIC_URI= MIRROR_URI= ``` 2. Running Skopeo to copy the image: ``` skopeo copy--all docker://${PUBLIC_URI}@sha256:${IMAGE_SHA256_VALUE} docker://${MIRROR_URI} ```- If this error has been encountered during the installation process while bootstrapping the cluster, please ensure the OpenShift version mirrored to your mirror registry matches the `openshift-install` client version being used to install the cluster.
root_cause: - The error `unknown manifest` suggests the image being pulled is not present in the mirror registry. Hence, if the container image is not available in the disconnected mirror registry, the PODs cannot pull it.

title: Sample-app not getting BuildConfig when deployed from Web Console
issue: All sample apps deployed from the developer view of the Web Console fail with ImagePullBackOff
Sample apps deployed from Web Console do not generate a BuildConfig
root_cause: This issue is a bug existing in OpenShift 4.15-4.17 regarding the Web Console, and a fix has been merged in the (as of yet unreleased 4.18 [^1]). The fix for other versions is currently being backported to 4.17 [^2], at which point it will move to 4.16 and then 4.15. [^1]:https://github.com/openshift/console/pull/14222 [^2]:https://github.com/openshift/console/pull/14241 The bug causes sample apps created from the Web Console's Developer View to fail to create a BuildConfig. Without a BuildConfig, the sample project will not have its image built in the namespace, resulting in an ImagePullBackOff error that will not resolve.

title: Several pods in Pending status and kube-scheduler pod crashing due to runtime error: integer divide by zero in OpenShift 4
issue: There are several pods in `Pending` status with no clear reason.
The `kube-scheduler` Pods are repeatedly crashing with the error: ~~~ Observed a panic: "integer divide by zero" (runtime error: integer divide by zero) ~~~

The panic references the `findNodesThatFitPod` function: ~~~ panic({0x2031cc0, 0x38e93e0}) runtime/panic.go:884 +0x213 k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler.(*Scheduler).findNodesThatFitPod(0xc0008b1a70, {0x271a0f0, 0xc001ec09b0}, {0x273cbd0, 0xc0004e25a0}, 0x0?, 0xc002e91358) ~~~
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this issue, and it has being tracked in the following bugs: Target Minor Release | Bug | Fixed Version | Errata--- |--- 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-35551](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-35551)|**4.16.2**|[RHSA-2024:4316](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4316) 4.15 | [OCPBUGS-35552](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-35552)|**4.15.21**|[RHSA-2024:4321](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4321) 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-35553](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-35553)|**4.14.32**|[RHSA-2024:4329](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4329) The recommendation is to upgrade to a recent version that includes the fix. ###Troubleshooting There could be different reasons for the `kube-scheduler` to crash, and it is needed to check in a case basis to find the initial pods causing the issue. The issue will be resolved correcting the Pod causing the initial issue, that could be a faulty node selector, wrong node affinity,.... The Pod triggering the crash may be attempting to target a node no longer in the cluster, bearing the wrong label, etc. Due to the issue, the `kube-scheduler` could crash before it can log the affected Pod, so the admin must check all existing Pods and search for the affected one. Any selector that operates on node is affected, including `nodeAffinity` and `nodeSelector`. First of all, check if the pods causing the panic are logged in the `openshift-kube-scheduler` pods logs: ```sh $ oc get pods-n openshift-kube-scheduler-l "app=openshift-kube-scheduler" [...] $ oc logs-n openshift-kube-scheduler openshift-kube-scheduler--c kube-scheduler-p | grep-oP "(? <=pod=\").*?(?=\")" openshift-storage/rook-ceph-mon-e-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx openshift-storage/rook-ceph-mon-h-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxx ``` For the Pods listed in the above output, check the conditions. It is not needed than the `nodeAffinity` or `nodeSelector` is wrong, but for example that there are no enough nodes for scheduling several replicas of a Pod, like for example messages similar to: ~~~ $ oc get pod [pod_name]-n [namespace_name]-o yaml [...] message: '0/6 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn''t match Pod''s node affinity/selector, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master:}. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 6 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling..' [...] ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get pod [pod_name]-n [namespace_name]-o yaml [...] message: '0/6 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn''t find available persistent volumes to bind, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master:}. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 6 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling..' [...] ~~~ ####Additional troubleshooting If there are no pods names logged, to find all Pods currently pending scheduling which have `.status.conditions`, use the following command (requires `jq`): ```sh $ oc get pods-A-ojson | jq-r '.items[] | select((.status.phase == "Pending") and (.status|has("conditions"))) | {name:.metadata.name, namespace:.metadata.namespace, conditions:.status.conditions}, "-----------------------------------------"' ``` The Pods will show their names, namespaces, and the conditions. Also, to find all Pods currently pending scheduling with a `nodeAffinity` or `nodeSelector` selectors, use the following commands (requires `jq`): ```sh $ oc get pods-A-ojson | jq-r '.items[] | select((.spec.affinity|has("nodeAffinity")) and (.status.phase == "Pending")) | {name:.metadata.name, namespace:.metadata.namespace, affinity:.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity}, "-----------------------------------------"' ``` ```sh $ oc get pods-A-ojson | jq-r '.items[] | select((.spec | has("nodeSelector")) and (.status.phase == "Pending")) | {name:.metadata.name, namespace:.metadata.namespace, nodeSelector:.spec.nodeSelector}, "-----------------------------------------"' ``` The Pods will show their names, namespaces, and the selector. Try to check for any issues with the `nodeAffinity` or `nodeSelector`
root_cause: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* The panic in the `kube-scheduler` Pod is due to a regression bug, [documented upstream](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/124930). This bug causes an error in the `kube-scheduler` when it attempts to find a node to place a Pod on. Previously, if no node could be found, the `kube-scheduler` would log the error and continue. Due to this issue, the `kube-scheduler` crashes instead, resulting in this Pod and any others failing to be scheduled. This issue does not occur in OCP 4.13 and older, as the bug had not yet been introduced.

title: Pods are evicted from the node due to DiskPressure in RHOCP 4
issue: - Pods are being `evicted` from the node due to `DiskPressure`.- Garbage Collector processes are not enough to free the node consumption as container runtime is unable to reap `zombie processes` due to the `ptm2` buffer being full.
resolution: - Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-31317](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-31317) and delivered a fix in RHOCP version 4.16.0 through errata [RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/list?query=%20orderBy%20lastModifiedDate%20desc&p=1&size=10&searchType=basic) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.- For previous affected versions below mentioned workaround can be followed. **Workaround**- Efficiently `draining` and `rebooting` the node can help to `resolve` the issue. If that doesn't work, proceed with the `CRI-O cleanup` steps outlined in [How to clean CRI-O storage in Red Hat OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5350721)

title: How to exclude the istio-cni-node daemonset from a specific node
issue: - istio-cni-node daemonset pods are deploying every node when installing SMCP- Some nodes are not required to use servicemesh features- User wants to exclude istio-cni-node daemonset pod in specific nodes.
resolution: Set a node label to nodes that do not deploy istio-cni-node daemonset. ~~~ $oc label node [node_name] maistra.io/exclude-cni=true ~~~ Example ~~~ $oc label node worker-3.ocp.example.com maistra.io/exclude-cni=true $oc get pods-l k8s-app=istio-cni-node-v2-5-o wide // istio-cni-node is not running in worker-3 NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE READINESS GATES istio-cni-node-v2-5-4dlhm 1/1 Running 0 42m 10.128.0.68 master-2.ocp.example.com istio-cni-node-v2-5-dhwwv 1/1 Running 0 42m 10.128.6.125 worker-1.ocp.example.com istio-cni-node-v2-5-fssh5 1/1 Running 0 42m 10.128.8.166 worker-2.ocp.example.com istio-cni-node-v2-5-r6mdc 1/1 Running 0 42m 10.128.5.71 master-1.ocp.example.com istio-cni-node-v2-5-svjjd 1/1 Running 0 42m 10.128.3.171 master-3.ocp.example.com ~~~
root_cause: [OSSM-1698](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSSM-1698) istio-cni-node daemonset has nodeAffinity with labels since OSSM version 2.5 ~~~ $oc get daemonset/istio-cni-node-v2-5... spec: affinity: nodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms:- matchExpressions:- key: maistra.io/exclude-cni operator: NotIn values:- "true" ~~~

title: Syntax error when configuring TextFileCertificateLoginModule as a secret with ActiveMQArtemis CR
issue: I am following the documentation [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.12/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#proc-br-configuring-jaas-login-modules-for-authentication_broker-ocp](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.12/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#proc-br-configuring-jaas-login-modules-for-authentication_broker-ocp) to setup a custom login module for AMQ deployed to Openshift. I created a secret for "custom-jaas-config" with the login.config file as well as cert-users.properties and cert-roles.properties. I referenced the secret as an extraMount in our ActiveMQArtemis CR. But when I create the CR, I get a validation error: `InvalidExtraMount.Spec.DeploymentPlan.ExtraMounts.Secrets, content of login.config key in secret custom-jaas-config does not match supported jaas config file syntax ` I've tried a few variations of moving the TextFileCertificateLoginModule to its own security domain or as part of the activemq domain but still get that error message. Using just the default login module works. `oc create secret generic custom-jaas-config--from-file=./cert_based_auth/login.config--from-file=./cert_based_auth/cert-roles.properties--from-file=./cert_based_auth/cert-users.properties ` `oc create-f cert_based_auth/broker_activemqartemis_cr.yaml`
resolution: - Use the latest version AMQ broker Operator- Follow the guide: [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.12/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#proc-br-configuring-jaas-login-modules-for-authentication_broker-ocp](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.12/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#proc-br-configuring-jaas-login-modules-for-authentication_broker-ocp), use the 2 files `artemis-roles.properties` & `artemis-users.properties` in the example:[https://github.com/apache/activemq-artemis-examples/activemq-artemis-examples/examples/features/standard/ssl-enabled-dual-authentication/src/main/resources/activemq/server0/*](https://github.com/apache/activemq-artemis-examples/activemq-artemis-examples/examples/features/standard/ssl-enabled-dual-authentication/src/main/resources/activemq/server0/*), steps are as below: ~~~ oc create secret generic custom-jaas-config--from-file=./cert_based_auth/login.config--from-file=./cert_based_auth/cert-roles.properties--from-file=./cert_based_auth/cert-users.properties--from-file=./cert_based_auth/artemis-roles.properties--from-file=./cert_based_auth/artemis-users.properties ~~~ ~~~ oc create-f cert_based_auth/broker_activemqartemis_cr.yaml ~~~

title: RHOCP: Recreate the telemetry-remote-write secret
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: The `telemetry-remote-write` secret has been deleted manually and the operator does not recreate it.
resolution: 1. Ensure hosted control plane operator is installed and running 2. Check the logs of the hosted control plane operator 3. Restart the monitoring operators, using this command: ``` $ oc rollout restart deployment cluster-monitoring-operator-n openshift-monitoring $ oc rollout restart deployment prometheus-operator-n openshift-monitoring ```

title: How to configure multiple email addresses for email notifications in RHOCP 4
issue: - Is it possible to configure multiple email addresses in one receiver in Prometheus alertmanager?- How to add more than one email addresses into the alert notification configuration?
resolution: 1. Obtain the Alertmanager YAML configuration file: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-monitoring get secret alertmanager-main--template='{{index.data "alertmanager.yaml"}}' |base64-d > alertmanager.yaml ~~~ 2. Modify the `alertmanager.yaml` file configuring multiple email addresses separated by a comma (,) in the `to` field as showing below: receivers:- name: 'test_receiver' email_configs:- to: 'xxx@example.com,yyy@example.com' from: 'zzz@example.com' [...]- Alternatively is possible to modify the `alertmanager.yaml` file configuring multiple `to` fields in one `email_configs` as showing below: receivers:- name: 'test_receiver' email_configs:- to: 'xxx@example.com' from: 'zzz@example.com' [...]- to: 'yyy@example.com' from: 'zzz@example.com' [...] 3. Apply the new configuration: ~~~ oc-n openshift-monitoring create secret generic alertmanager-main--from-file=alertmanager.yaml--dry-run=client-o=yaml | oc-n openshift-monitoring replace secret--filename=- ~~~ Related documentation: [Configuring Alertmanager to send notifications](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/observability/monitoring/managing-alerts.html#configuring-alertmanager-to-send-notifications).

title: How to View Pod CPU & MEMORY Requests and Limits Across All Namespaces
issue: - What is the command to check CPU & MEMORY requests and limits for all pods across all namespaces in OpenShift.
resolution: - Below command can be used to check CPU requests and limit for all pods: ~~~ echo-e "NAMESPACE\tPOD NAME\tCPU REQUEST\tCPU LIMIT" && oc get pods--all-namespaces-o=jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}{"\t"}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.cpu}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[*].resources.limits.cpu}{"\n"}{end}' ~~~- Below command can be used to check MEMORY requests and limit for all pods: ~~~ echo-e "NAMESPACE\tPOD NAME\tMEMORY REQUESTS\tMEMORY LIMITS"; oc get pods--all-namespaces-o=jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}{"\t"}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.memory}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[*].resources.limits.memory}{"\n"}{end}' ~~~
root_cause: - High CPU resource requests across pods, leading to nodes appearing overutilized despite actual underutilization.

title: [RHACS] How to confirm the update date of "StackRox Scanner Vulnerability Definitions" via CLI ?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Is it possible to confirm the update date of `StackRox Scanner Vulnerability Definitions` using CLI?- Besides confirming via the Central web console (`Platform Configuration`-> `System Health`), the goal is to use the CLI.- Is there an option in the `roxctl` command to confirm this?
resolution: - To confirm the update date of `StackRox Scanner Vulnerability Definitions` using CLI, query the [`GetVulnDefinitionsInfo` API](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.5/rest_api/IntegrationHealthService.html#IntegrationHealthServiceGetVulnDefinitionsInfo). https:// /v1/integrationhealth/vulndefinitions?component=SCANNER- Querying the API endpoint will return a result similar to the following. {"lastUpdatedTimestamp": "2024-08-19T23:07:52.647646350Z"}
root_cause: - The `roxctl` command does not provide an option or feature to confirm the update date of `StackRox Scanner Vulnerability Definitions`.- For information on using the API, refer to [the API reference documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.5/rest_api/) or the API reference available in the Central console (https:// /main/apidocs).

title: [RHACS] Querying API fails with "error: credentials not found"
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - When querying the RHACS API endpoint, the following error occurs: $ curl-k https:// /v1/integrationhealth/vulndefinitions | jq. {"error": "credentials not found", "code": 16, "message": "credentials not found", "details": []}- Even though the OCP token was specified, the error still appears. $ curl-H "Authorization: Bearer $(oc whoami-t)"-k https:// /v1/integrationhealth/vulndefinitions | jq. {"error": "credentials not found: token-based: cannot extract identity: token validation failed", "code": 16, "message": "credentials not found: token-based: cannot extract identity: token validation failed", "details": []}- How can the credentials not found error be resolved?
resolution: - Follow the steps in [the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.5/configuration/configure-api-token.html#create-api-token_configure-api-token) to create the RHACS API token.- Use the API token when authenticating for queries to the API endpoint. $ export ROX_API_TOKEN= $ curl-H "Authorization: Bearer $ROX_API_TOKEN"-k https:// /v1/integrationhealth/vulndefinitions {"lastUpdatedTimestamp": "2024-08-19T23:07:52.647646350Z"}
root_cause: - The RHACS API endpoint requires authentication using an API token created in Central.

title: CSI Migration fails for PVs with missing vmdk suffix
issue: - During/Post the CSI migration (see: [KCS 7011683](https://access.redhat.com/node/7011683) for more details), volumes fail to mount. ~~~ Warning FailedAttachVolume #m (x# over ##m) attachdetach-controller AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "PV_NAME": rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to attach disk: "[DATASTORE] PATH/PATH" with node: "NODE_HASH" err ServerFaultCode: The object or item referred to could not be found. ~~~
resolution: We can workaround this issue by recreating the persistentvolume(PV) objects with vmdk suffix. Make sure existing PVs are Available/Released and not bound, since we will be deleting PV objects as part of the process.- **IMPORTANT**: We need to make sure that `[ReclaimPolicy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/storage/understanding-persistent-storage.html#reclaiming_understanding-persistent-storage)` of PV is set to **Retain**, by following [these docs](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/storage/understanding-persistent-storage.html#reclaim-policy_understanding-persistent-storage): ~~~ $ oc patch pv-p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}' ~~~- [Scale down](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/cli_reference/openshift_cli/developer-cli-commands.html#oc-scale) any pod that is using the PV. ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=0 ~~~- Delete corresponding PVC object.- Since `ReclaimPolicy`on PV is set to **Retain** this should not result in deletion of PV objects. ~~~ $ oc delete pvc/ ~~~- Take a backup of PV objects, by simply saving YAML of PV objects. ~~~ $ oc get pv-o yaml > pv_backup.yaml ~~~- Delete the PV objects ~~~ $ oc delete pv ~~~- Re-create PV object but by updating volumePath- Now we can re-create the PV object that were using same volumePath but this time with vmdk suffix. You can use YAML of PV objects you saved in step#2 as a reference. Be sure that `volumePath: 'PATH.vmdk'` has the **.vmdk** suffix. ~~~ $ vim pv_backup.yaml ### This is where you make the denoted edits above. $ oc create-f pv_backup.yaml ~~~
root_cause: Users who typically encounter this issue; have followed [these steps](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/storage/persistent_storage/persistent-storage-vsphere.html#vsphere-static-provisioning_persistent-storage-efs) to establish PV's in the cluster. It was discovered while debugging- [OCPBUGS-42321](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42321) that intree vSphere PVs for which vmdk suffix is missing fail during CSI migration. Usually for in-tree vSphere PVs, vmdk extension is expected in volumePath field: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata: name: manual-pv spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce capacity: storage: 4Gi persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain storageClassName: "" volumeMode: Filesystem vsphereVolume: fsType: ext4 volumePath: '[vsanDatastore] isos/hekumar-local' ~~~ If an admin forgot to specify the suffix (as in the example above), at PV creation, users migrating PV's will see CSI failures, not seen with the intree driver.

title: Repository Mirroring does not mirror image signatures.
issue: - When mirroring images using Repository Mirroring feature, only the container images are successfully mirrored, while the associated signature artifacts (signed by Cosign) are not included in the mirroring process.- This results in the mirrored images on the target instance appearing as unsigned, which raises concerns regarding security and compliance.
resolution: - A feature request has been raised to [Enable Repository Mirroring to Include Image Signature Artifacts](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-6402)- This focuses on implementing an option in Quay to allow mirroring of image signature artifacts, with an explicit toggle to enable or disable signature copying during Repository Mirroring.
root_cause: - Newer Skopeo versions store signatures locally in /var/lib/containers/sigstore/, but SELinux blocks skopeo from accessing it. This resulted in repository mirroring option failing. ``` Mirror of 5-41 failure to repository redis/redis-5-rhel7 Source 'docker:// registry.redhat.io/rhscl/redis-5-rhel7:5-41 ' failed to sync Getting image list signatures Copying 3 of 3 images in list Copying image sha256:bb1470a0f87e053026e2fefb2583594d3821aea4ecce858e3db70f8a5e8cb9b7 (1/3) Getting image source signatures Checking if image destination supports signatures Copying blob sha256:70d8ae8bb48eb4313de66e13b93ab02b1f12073961a32e6e5b957228ac52ca44 Copying blob sha256:608083cad0129a0f9240e5dcd4ceb087cc5ff025012277fc28bd77108e11a9bd Copying blob sha256:b77f42d650dc7d0d6fa21f8661f03957cfe70fcf92e48245d2a7cad7d795eb56 Copying blob sha256:a858833a9239708c0c07c8fdf95218065c0605e14950051b009f9ad263f43511 Copying config sha256:327ee2d8ff6817033d952540e054c419601dba151dff76c11b597cb89106d6f6 Writing manifest to image destination Storing signatures time="2021-06-15T14:16:09Z" level=fatal msg="Error writing signatures: mkdir /var/lib/containers/sigstore/redis: permission denied" ```- To address this, Quay introduced [--remove-signatures](https://github.com/quay/quay/pull/816), preventing signature copying during repo mirroring. This results in only images being mirrored, without signature artifacts.

title: How to extend login session duration for OpenShift user that the user token will never expire.
issue: We are doing some automation through script in the Openshift for that we need oc login command from CLI.
Oc login token is expiring in 24 hours so we need permanent oc login token.
Need oc login token from command line that will never expire.
resolution: Create and use a custom OAuthClient object in the cluster that generates a token which expires in 3 months: 1. Create the YAML file for the OAuthClient: ~~~ $ cat < oauthclient-cc-custom.yaml apiVersion: oauth.openshift.io/v1 grantMethod: auto kind: OAuthClient metadata: name: openshift-challenging-client-3m redirectURIs:- https://oauth-openshift.apps.example.com/oauth/token/implicit respondWithChallenges: true accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds: 0 EOF ~~~ *Make sure the redirectURI has the correct domain of the openshift-authentication route. Get the domain from: ~~~ $ oc get routes-n openshift-authentication ~~~ * The accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds is the login duration. In the example, 0= Infinite days (that will never expire). 2. Create the OAuthClient object in the cluster, as a cluster administrator: ~~~ $ oc create-f oauthclient-cc-custom.yaml oauthclient.oauth.openshift.io/openshift-challenging-client-3m created ~~~ 3. It's possible to request a token using this OAuthClient with the command: ~~~ $ curl 'https://oauth-openshift.apps.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=openshift-challenging-client-3m&response_type=token' \-u ": " \-skv-H "X-CSRF-Token: $(date +%s)" \--stderr- | grep-oP "access_token=\K[^&]*" ~~~ * This will get a token for this that expires never. Example output: BXCGIoMP7ju_q0M09cRp-1rkz-pd-QCJn-ucqnZUlwY; * Notice that the client_id specifies openshift-challenging-client-3m which is the name of the custom OAuthClient created in the previous step; * If grep is not used, the access token is within the Location header in the HTTP response. * If OpenShift is using an OpenID Identity Provider, the curl could return HTTP 401. Please see the workaround for this step later in this solution. 4. Use the provided token to login or access the API: ~~~ $ oc login--token Logged into "https://api.example.com:6443" as "testusername" using the token provided. ~~~ * To test the token duration, change the expiration to 60 seconds and test the API after a minute. Can also see in `oc explain oauthclients.oauth.openshift.io` ~~~ accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds AccessTokenMaxAgeSeconds overrides the default access token max age for tokens granted to this client. 0 means no expiration. ~~~

title: How to create a new machineset in ARO
issue: Need a new machine pool for an ARO cluster with the latest models and additional features.
Looking to deploy new worker machines in an ARO cluster using other instance classes with advanced features.
resolution: This guide outlines the steps to create a new MachineSet in Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) by listing the existing MachineSets, copying one of the current MachineSets, and customizing it based on specific requirements. For detailed information on creating MachineSets in Azure Red Hat OpenShift, please refer to the official documentation: [Creating MachineSets in Azure Red Hat OpenShift](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/machine_management/creating_machinesets/creating-machineset-azure.html). ### Prerequisites- Ensure access to the ARO cluster via oc command-line tool.- Sufficient permissions to list and modify MachineSets in the ARO OpenShift environment. 1. To begin, the current MachineSets in the ARO cluster should be listed. This step provides an overview of the MachineSets that are available for copying. ``` $ oc get machinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus1 1 1 1 1 18m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus2 1 1 1 1 18m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus3 1 1 1 1 18m ``` 2. Copy an Existing MachineSet Once the desired MachineSet is identified from the list, it will be copied for further editing. Use the following command to export the YAML configuration of the selected MachineSet: ``` $ oc get machineset-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml > new-machineset.yaml ``` Replace with the name of the MachineSet to be copied. The YAML content will be saved in a file named new-machineset.yaml. 3. Edit the MachineSet YAML After copying the MachineSet, the configuration must be adjusted to meet the specific requirements of the new MachineSet.- Open the new-machineset.yaml file in a text editor.- Modify the following fields: • `metadata.name`: Change the name to a unique value for the new MachineSet. • `spec.replicas`: Set the desired number of replicas (e.g., 2). • `spec.template.spec.providerSpec.value.vmSize`: Update the instance type to meet the specific requirements of your workload.- Save the changes. 4. Apply the New MachineSet Once the edits are complete, apply the new MachineSet to the cluster. Run the following command to create the new MachineSet: ``` $ oc apply-f new-machineset.yaml-n openshift-machine-api ``` This command will create the new MachineSet in the cluster. 5. Validate the New MachineSet and Resources After applying the new MachineSet, it is essential to perform several validation checks to ensure that the resources are set up correctly. It may take several minutes for the machines to be provisioned and reach the “Running” state. Run the following command to verify that the machines are being created and are in the expected state: ``` $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE example-aro-e4s-v5-worker-eastus1-45b22 Provisioned Standard_E4s_v5 eastus 1 63s example-aro-e4s-v5-worker-eastus1-fzsd5 Provisioned Standard_E4s_v5 eastus 1 63s mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus1-kfvl6 Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 1 3h33m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus2-gf6bg Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 2 3h33m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus3-sr97r Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 3 3h33m ``` **Check the status of the MachineSet:** Verify the status of the newly created MachineSet to ensure it is functioning correctly: ``` $ oc get machinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE example-aro-e4s-v5-worker-eastus1 2 2 14s mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus1 1 1 1 1 3h46m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus2 1 1 1 1 3h46m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus3 1 1 1 1 3h46m ``` After a few minutes: ``` $ oc get machinesets-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE example-aro-e4s-v5-worker-eastus1 2 2 2 2 10m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus1 1 1 1 1 4h3m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus2 1 1 1 1 4h3m mci-aro-1a2b3-worker-eastus3 1 1 1 1 4h3m ``` **Check the status of Nodes:** Confirm that the nodes associated with the new MachineSet are ready and operational: ``` $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION example-aro-e4s-v5-worker-eastus1-45b22 Ready worker 1m26s v1.26.14+03ee898 example-aro-e4s-v5-worker-eastus1-fzsd5 Ready worker 1m21s v1.26.14+03ee898 ``` By following the steps detailed in this document, users can effectively create and configure a new MachineSet in Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) to meet their specific workload requirements. It is crucial to monitor the status of the machines and confirm their operational readiness before proceeding with any deployments.

title: OpenShift 4 upgrade stuck with Machine Config Operator degraded
issue: - OpenShift 4.12 upgrade stuck with the Machine Config Operator (MCO) degraded due to mismatched osImageURL target.- The common workaround from [KCS Solution 5598401](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5598401) is not helping, and we have lost SSH access to the node after attempting to force the config.- When trying to log in as core user with password, the core home directory was missing which was preventing a switch to root user.
resolution: This is a [relatively recently discovered ostree issue](https://github.com/ostreedev/ostree/pull/2874/commits/de6fddc6adee09a93901243dc7074090828a1912) that can generally only be triggered on filesystems that allocate > 32 bit inodes, which include large XFS filesystems (> 2-3TB). We are tracking the RHEL backport fix via [BZ 2224081O](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2224081) and OpenShift 4.14 via [this JIRA OCPBUGS-16771](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-16771). For OCP 4.12, the fixed ostree was released in [OCP 4.12.30](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:4671). For OCP 4.13, the fix was released in [OCP 4.13.10](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:4731). ## WORKAROUND: In general, a pattern we recommend for large disks is to provision a separate /var filesystem. Please refer to an example of this [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/install_config/installing-customizing.html#installation-special-config-raid_installing-customizing). This pattern will work around this bug. However, if the upgrade has started and gets hung, it is not supported to re-partition the disks via the [MCO document](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/master/docs/FAQ.md#q-can-i-use-the-mco-to-re-partition-or-re-install). It would be a manual process for existing nodes or re-provisioning nodes. If this is one option for the customer, they can use a split /var filesystem per [our documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/installing_bare_metal/installing-restricted-networks-bare-metal.html#installation-user-infra-machines-advanced_disk_installing-restricted-networks-bare-metal). This is a generally recommended best practices and will guarantee to avoid this bug without any code changes in any supported OCP release. The idea is to split off a larger portion of the disk for /var, leaving the root partition smaller at around 100GB, for example. This is separate from having /var/lib/containers a different partition.
root_cause: - This ostree bug started at OCP 4.12 about inode (a unique file identifier) numbers which for XFS (64 bits) tend to follow disk size due to the change introduced in the container flow.- In such instances, multiple files were assigned the same inode, making the deployment unusable. A root cause analysis was performed, running the process under gdb, which revealed a lossy conversion from guint64 to guint32. This 32 bit truncation resulted in an incorrect internal cache when synthesizing filesystem trees (locally to a machine) which could result in arbitrary files being swapped. Further note that because inode allocations are individual to a filesystem, different machines could see different results.- We believe the issue only occurs on filesystems that allocate > 32 bit inodes, including large XFS filesystems > 2-3TB. We don't verify the deployment roots today which makes this problem much less visible. We have the ongoing composefs work to fix this part.- The problem is not directly related to the disk size. It is triggered by > 32 bit inodes. It is more about the allocation pattern for file identifiers, as distinct from the amount of storage those files occupy. The default RHEL (and RHCOS) filesystem is XFS. It happens to be today (at least up to RHEL9) that XFS will generally only use > 32 bit inodes when a sufficient number of allocation groups (a function of disk size) are used.

title: failed to fetch Agent Installer ISO: failed to load asset "Install Config": failed to create install config: failed to upconvert install config: unable to find object
issue: **Scenario A: When using a predefined or existing install-config.yaml**- Running the *openshift-install agent create image

title: Can AMQ Streams user and topic operators watch more than one namespace?
product: Red Hat OpenShift Streams for Apache Kafka
issue: According to the [AMQ Streams documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_amq/7.2/html/using_amq_streams_on_openshift_container_platform/assembly-operators-str#deploying-cluster-operator-kubernetes-to-watch-multiple-namespacesdeploying-co), AMQ Streams cluster operator supports watching multiple namespaces. Can the topic and user operator do the same?
resolution: The AMQ Streams Cluster Operator is in charge of deploying a Kafka cluster alongside a Zookeeper ensemble. As part of the AMQ Streams cluster, it can also deploy the topic and user operator which provides operator-style for managing new topics and users via KafkaTopic custom resources. Unfortunately, AMQ Streams topic operator and user operator do not support multiple namespaces: They need to be redeployed in each namespace to manage topic and user creation and configuration. There are no plans shortly about supporting user or topic operators in more than one namespace. This would probably be supported on a later release, but there is not an estimated or fixed release date for this

title: Baremetal Host Discovery Failed Due to Missing Managed Host IP in noProxy Configuration on ACM
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - When using the agent-based installation method for a baremetal host in ACM (Advanced Cluster Management), users may encounter issues where the baremetal host installation fails or experiences connectivity issues such as a node discovery failure.- Host discovery is stuck in the provisioning state on ACM.
resolution: As per the [Network Configuration documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.11/html/clusters/cluster_mce_overview#cluster-lifecycle-RBAC:~:text=for%20more%20information.-,Note,-%3A%20Registration%20Agent), the managed cluster's Registration Agent and Work Agent do not support proxy settings. These agents communicate with the API server on the hub cluster using an mTLS connection, which cannot pass through a proxy. In a proxy environment, it is important to configure the noProxy list in ACM to include the managed host's IP address. This ensures that communication between the managed cluster and the hub cluster bypasses the proxy, preventing connectivity issues. Alternatively, allow internal connections through the existing proxy server. To resolve the issue: 1. Identify the managed host's IP address. 2. Add this IP to the noProxy list in the ACM hub cluster configuration. 3. Add an IP of hub cluster to the noProxy list in the managed cluster
root_cause: - Note: Registration Agent and Work Agent on the managed cluster do not support proxy settings because they communicate with apiserver on the hub cluster by establishing an mTLS connection, which cannot pass through the proxy.

title: Temporarily Set Core User Password on Hosted Control Planes Nodes
issue: - Is it possible to set a password for the core user in a hosted control planes node?- Is it possible to access a hosted control plane node without using an ssh key or `oc debug node`?
resolution: ___ *The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and support procedures (Production Support- Red Hat Customer Portal)). The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the Operating System unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. The intent of this article is to provide information to accomplish the system's needs. Use of the information in this article at the user's own risk.*___ It is possible to set a core user password similar to the method mentioned in the [Official Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/post_installation_configuration/machine-configuration-tasks.html#core-user-password_post-install-machine-configuration-tasks). The only difference is specific to how the machine-configuration is implemented. The following provides the method for implementing a password for the **core** user on a Hosted Control Planes nodepool. **Note**: The following procedure has only been tested on Container Native Virtualization platform. **Important**: Upon changes to the nodepool object, new nodes will be rolled out and the prior nodes will be deleted.___ Create a hashed password to use for the user **core**. ~~~ $ openssl passwd-6 Password: Verifying- Password: ~~~ Create a machine-config that specifies the user core and the password as copied from the hash value above. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: set-core-user-password spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 passwd: users:- name: core passwordHash: ~~~ Per the [Hosted Control Planes Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/hosted_control_planes/hcp-machine-config.html), add the above machine-config to a configmap, and save the file as hcp-core-cm.yaml. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: core-user namespace: clusters data: config: | apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: set-core-user-password spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 passwd: users:- name: core passwordHash: ~~~ From the management cluster, create the configmap. ~~~ $ oc create-f hcp-core-cm.yaml ~~~ Edit the nodepool object. ~~~ $ oc edit nodepool--namespace clusters ~~~ Within the nodepool object, add the name of the configmap. ~~~ apiVersion: hypershift.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: NodePool metadata: #... name: nodepool-1 namespace: clusters #... spec: config:- name: core-user #... ~~~ Once the nodepool object has been modified, new nodes will be rolled out. When the new nodes are started up, access the serial console within the Virtualization graphical interface. Login as the **core** user and input the password that was hashed in the first step.___ To remove the **core** user password, edit the nodepool object again, and remove the `spec.config` field. ~~~ apiVersion: hypershift.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: NodePool metadata: #... name: nodepool-1 namespace: clusters #... spec: config: <-- remove- name: core-user <-- remove #... ~~~ After removing the `spec.config` field in the nodepool object, new nodes will be rolled out again.

title: Camel pod with multiple thousands routes can not finish start due to health check
product: Red Hat build of Apache Camel for Spring Boot
issue: Camel pod with multiple thousands routes can not finish start due to health check. ~~~ 2024-09-17T05:32:55.382Z WARN 1--- [XNIO-1 task-2] a.h.r.CamelReadinessStateHealthIndicator: Probe in group 'camel', with id 'consumer:xxxxx' failed with message 'Consumer has not yet polled route: xxxxx' ~~~
resolution: From OpenShift side, you can adjust the start timing by "initialDelaySeconds" option. [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/applications/application-health.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/applications/application-health.html) Camel also has some options for the health check too. [https://camel.apache.org/components/4.4.x/others/main.html#_camel_health_check_configurations](https://camel.apache.org/components/4.4.x/others/main.html#_camel_health_check_configurations) "camel.health.initialState" Option: ~~~ The initial state of health-checks (readiness). There are the following states: UP, DOWN, UNKNOWN. By default, the state is DOWN, is regarded as being pessimistic/careful. This means that the overall health checks may report as DOWN during startup and then only if everything is up and running flip to being UP. Setting the initial state to UP, is regarded as being optimistic. This means that the overall health checks may report as UP during startup and then if a consumer or other service is in fact un-healthy, then the health-checks can flip being DOWN. Setting the state to UNKNOWN means that some health-check would be reported in unknown state, especially during early bootstrap where a consumer may not be fully initialized or validated a connection to a remote system. This option allows to pre-configure the state for different modes. ~~~ "camel.health.excludePattern" Option: ~~~ Pattern to exclude health checks from being invoked by Camel when checking health. Multiple patterns can be separated by comma. ~~~ There are some samples about how to use the fileter. ~~~ https://camel.apache.org/manual/health-check.html#_excluding_health_checks ~~~ Multiple thousands routes may stress a system. For example by using a shared thread pool, the multiple thousands routes can reuse JVM threads. Also there would be some space for refactoring to reduce the number of routes. Please consider to use our Red Hat consulting service for refactoring and optimization.

resolution: Please limit the length of the JSON entry attribute less than Integer. MAX_VALUE /2.
root_cause: When executing the unmarshal() method, camel-jsonb internally invokes org.eclipse.parsson.JsonTokenizer.fillBuf() method. And the method uses java.util.Arrays.copyOf(char[], int). parsson-1.1.0/org/eclipse/parsson/JsonTokenizer.java ~~~ private int fillBuf() throws IOException {if (storeEnd!= 0) {int storeLen = storeEnd-storeBegin; if (storeLen > 0) {// there is some store data if (storeLen == buf.length) {// buffer is full, double the capacity char[] doubleBuf = Arrays.copyOf(buf, 2 * buf.length); // This part bufferPool.recycle(buf); buf = doubleBuf;} else {// Left shift all the stored data to make space System.arraycopy(buf, storeBegin, buf, 0, storeLen); storeEnd = storeLen; storeBegin = 0; bufferOffset += readBegin-storeEnd;}} else {storeBegin = storeEnd = 0; bufferOffset += readBegin;}} else {bufferOffset += readBegin;} // Fill the rest of the buf return reader.read(buf, storeEnd, buf.length-storeEnd);} ~~~ "2*buf.length" is passed to the 2nd argument as "int", but the value was more than Integer.MAX_VALUE then the value flipped o the negative value which causes java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException.

title: Backup Upload Failure to Hitachi HTC S3 Storage via OADP [RHOCP4]
issue: - Velero is reporting `error putting object` errors with status code 409 while putting `velero-backup.json`.
resolution: - Enable `versioning` on Hitachi HCP bucket used as `BackupStorageLocation`
root_cause: The `velero-backup.json` file contains the metadata, configuration, and status information for a Velero backup operation. Since this file is updated multiple times during the backup process, the storage backend where it's saved should support overwriting the file as it changes.

title: Will OpenShift Virtualization `vms` experience outage if `ip`, `sub` and `csv` are deleted?
issue: - Will `VirtualMachines` experience outage or go down if OpenShift Virtualization (OCV) `InstallPlan`, `Subscription` and `ClusterServiceVersion` are deleted?- Removing these resources is part of the steps listed on [KCS 6923501- Operator InstallPlanMissing](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6923501)
resolution: In OCV, the `crds` that manage `vm` workloads are separate from the Operator's `sub` and `csv` objects. Therefore:- Deleting the `sub` will stop OCV from receiving automatic updates;- Deleting the `csv` removes the current operator version from the cluster **and** will impact the operator's ability to manage (create, update etc) `vms`;- However, deleting either one **should not** affect running `vms`. In any case, it is important to consider the following:- Back up your data before **any** major changes, especially in Production/critical environments;- Execute any steps in a Test environment **beforehand** so you can familiarize yourself with the required steps and the expected results.

title: Not able to configurable the `globalMaxSnapshotsPerBlockVolume` in 4.16

title: ACM Managed Cluster AlertManager Still Tries to Send Alerts to Old Hub After Re-import
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - In the scenario where a Managed Cluster needs to be imported into a new Hub Cluster after a catastrophic failure of the original Hub.- When following [the steps documented](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.10/html/clusters/cluster_mce_overview#removing-a-cluster-from-management-in-special-cases) to clean up the Managed Cluster prior to importing it into the new Hub Cluster.- After import into the new Hub Cluster, the Managed Cluster still attempts to send Alerts to the AlertManager of the old Hub Cluster.
resolution: - Prior to the import into the new Hub Cluster, as an addition to the [documented Managed Cluster clean-up steps](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.10/html/clusters/cluster_mce_overview#removing-a-cluster-from-management-in-special-cases).- From the detached Managed Cluster, delete deployments `endpoint-observability-operator` and `metrics-collector-deployment`- Remove the `open-cluster-management-addon-observability` namespace.- Edit the configmap `cluster-monitoring-config` in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace and manually remove the stanza that looks like this: ~~~ additionalAlertmanagerConfigs:- apiVersion: v2 bearerToken: key: token name: observability-alertmanager-accessor pathPrefix: / scheme: https staticConfigs:- alertmanager-open-cluster-management-observability.apps.xxxx tlsConfig: ca: key: service-ca.crt name: hub-alertmanager-router-ca insecureSkipVerify: false externalLabels: managed_cluster: xxxx ~~~- Proceed with importing the Managed Cluster into the new Hub Cluster.
root_cause: - In the scenario where a Hub Cluster goes down and the Managed Cluster is not able to execute a regular detachment, the finalizers in the `endpoint-observability-operator` pod are unable to complete.- These finalizers are responsible for rectifying the modifications made by Advanced Cluster Management Observability to the `cluster-monitoring-config` of the Managed Cluster, including the addition of additional AlertManager configurations.- In this scenario the Managed Cluster maintains the old `cluster-monitoring-config` when being imported into the new Hub Cluster, causing the issue with Alerts being sent to the old Hub Cluster's AlertManager.

title: AMQ Broker on OpenShift - Changes in the Artemis Broker definition are not taking effect
issue: - Applying a modification in the Artemis definition, the broker pods are not being terminated and re-scheduled, manual intervention is required.- Regardless of the custom configuration defined in the Artemis definition, the pod does not show it.
resolution: If no `ERROR` or `WARN` traces exist in the operator log, probably one `secret` in the Broker definition lacks the `ownerReferences` field. 1. Review each `secret` in the problematic namespace. 2. Locate and delete the `secret` that lacks the field `ownerReferences`. 3. Restart the operator manager by deleting its pod. Red Hat investigated this issue in the bug report [ENTMQBR-9411](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ENTMQBR-9411) and delivered a fix in AMQ 7.12.3.OPR.1.GA. If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: This particular problem describes the workaround when there are no traces of this issue in the operator or the Artemis broker log when changes on the Broker definition are being done.

title: Failed to delete BFD Profile
issue: - Cannot delete a BFD profile
resolution: - Modify the BGPPeer that is using the BFD Profile by deleting the relative entry to the BFD Profile you want to delete: ~~~ oc edit BGPPeer bgp-peer.... spec: bfdProfile: bfd-profile <------------- delete this line myASN: 7777 peerASN: 7675 peerAddress: 192.168.123.203 peerPort: 179.... ~~~ Or, if the custom resource bgppeers.metallb.io is not needed any more, delete it. ~~~ oc delete bgppeers.metallb.io bgp-peer ~~~- Delete the bfdProfile: ~~~ oc delete bfdProfile bfd-profile-n metallb-system bfdprofile.metallb.io "bfd-profile" deleted ~~~
root_cause: It is not possible to delete a bfdProfile if there is a BGPPeer using it.

issue: - Getting hostPath errors when spinning up a pod ~~~ $ oc logs docker-registry-1-deploy--> Scaling docker-registry-1 to 1--> FailedCreate: docker-registry-1 Error creating: pods "docker-registry-1-" is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constraint: [spec.containers[0].securityContext.privileged: Invalid value: true: Privileged containers are not allowed spec.containers[0].securityContext.volumes[0]: Invalid value: "hostPath": hostPath volumes are not allowed to be used] error: couldn't scale docker-registry-1 to 1: timed out waiting for "docker-registry-1" to be synced ~~~- 500 error when pushing to docker-registry using hostPath or hostMount ~~~ # docker push 172.30.86.174:5000/example/test-image The push refers to a repository [172.30.86.174:5000/example/test-image] aabae48a5fa8: Retrying in 1 second d4d87debc120: Retrying in 1 second f1c7cb70e415: Retrying in 1 second 65956f7f583a: Retrying in 1 second 6f31e408653c: Retrying in 1 second 457598cf1733: Waiting 3291ee6ef6e0: Waiting 8d4d1ab5ff74: Waiting received unexpected HTTP status: 500 Internal Server Error ~~~

title: Unable to run Virtual Machine on a New Compute Node in an OpenShift cluster
issue: - Add a new compute node to an OpenShift cluster.- Clone a Virtual Machine and use node selector to select the compute node.- The VM gets stuck with `ErrorUnschedulable` (or later starting state) after start.
resolution: - Make sure the new node is configured with NTP so that its time is synced to the cluster.- Ensure the backing storage is allowed to be mounted.
root_cause: - Time between new node and cluster was not synced.- New node could not mount volumes.

title: Unable to deploy UIPlugin in RHOCP4
issue: - Unable to deploy the `UIPlugin` in RHOCP4.- During the deployment of the `UIPlugin`, the following error message is displayed: ~~~ $ oc create-f UIPlugin.yaml Error from server (NotFound): error when creating "UIPlugin.yaml": the server could not find the requested resource (post uiplugins.observability.openshift.io) ~~~ ~~~ cat < < EOF |oc create-f- apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: UIPlugin metadata: name: logging spec: type: Logging logging: lokiStack: name: logging-loki EOF Error from server (NotFound): error when creating "STDIN": the server could not find the requested resource (post uiplugins.observability.openshift.io) ~~~
resolution: - Prior to deploying the `UIPlugin`, it is essential to install the `Cluster Observability Operator` in the cluster.- Please [Install Cluster Observability Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/cluster_observability_operator/installing-the-cluster-observability-operator.html?extIdCarryOver=true&sc_cid=701f2000001OH6kAAG) first, and then proceed to deploy the `UIPlugin`. For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003)
root_cause: The `UIPlugin` serves as a console plugin for observability. Therefore, if the `Cluster Observability Operator` is not installed in the cluster, the `UIPlugin` will not be deployed.

title: Cannot open /etc/target dmesg error when RHOCP upgraded.

resolution: These messages are harmless and can be ignored.
root_cause: - When `target_core_mod` module was initialized, `DB_ROOT_DEFAULT` path was not able to open.- The `target_core_mod` loaded in RHOCP version 4.16 but not in 4.14.

title: How to configure fluentd to merge the logs to a JSON payload document in OCP 4
issue: - How to configure fluentd to inspect each logs and then determine if it's format is `JSON` and merge it into `JSON` payload documents.- How to enable OpenShift 4 to process container logs generated in `JSON` format in the same way as it was in OpenShift 3?
resolution: > **Important:** *Parsing of log files in `JSON` format is not yet officially supported in OpenShift 4. Following this procedure will put the 'Cluster Logging Operator' or the whole OpenShift cluster into **unsupported** state. Please, read the linked documentation for more details.* #### Unsupported procedure- Set the 'Cluster Logging Operator' or the whole OpenShift cluster into `unmanaged` state. See [support policy for `unmanaged` Operators](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/logging/config/cluster-logging-maintenance-support.html#unmanaged-operators_cluster-logging-unsupported).- Enable the feature by performing the following: ~~~ $ oc set env ds/fluentd MERGE_JSON_LOG=true ~~~ #### Potential risks that are involved in enablement of this feature- There are possibilities that Elasticsearch will reject the documents due to inconsistent type mapping and it will lead to log loss.- Buffer storage leak caused by rejected message cycling. ####Supported way- The feature to enable `JSON` logging has been merged with Logging 5.1 which is available from RHOCP 4.7. Follow [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/logging/cluster-logging-enabling-json-logging.html) to enable `JSON` logging on RHOCP. If you face any issues while enabling `JSON` logging on RHOCP 4.7, please open a [support case with Red Hat](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport).
root_cause: Parsing `JSON` format is not yet supported by the default `fluentd` configuration till RHOCP 4.6.

title: vsphere-problem-detector does not use cluster proxy configuration in OCP 4
issue: - The `vsphere-problem-detector` `pod` does not use the cluster `proxy` settings.- After configuring the cluster `proxy` the `vsphere-problem-detector` `pod` fails to connect to vSphere.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-28879](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-28879). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: The `vsphere-problem-detector` `pod` does not set up the general cluster proxy configuration in the pod. As the `proxy` configuration is not in place, the `vsphere-problem-detector` fails to validate the vSphere configurations.

title: When Image registry Using Custom Azure Storage Account in Different Resource Group Image registry operator Degrade and Upgrade Blocked
issue: - Upgrading an OpenShift cluster from version 4.14 to 4.15 stuck when the image registry is configured to use a custom Azure storage account located in a different resource group.- The upgrade process becomes stuck due to misconfiguration errors of Azure storage credentials by the image registry operator.- The image registry operator reports errors similar to: ``` NodeCADaemonProgressing: The daemon set node-ca is deployed Progressing: Unable to apply resources: unable to sync storage configuration: client misconfigured, missing 'TenantID', 'ClientID', 'ClientSecret', 'FederatedTokenFile', 'Creds', 'SubscriptionID' option(s) ```- After deleting the image-registry-private-configuration-user secret, a new error appears: ``` NodeCADaemonProgressing: The daemon set node-ca is deployed Progressing: Unable to apply resources: unable to sync storage configuration: failed to get keys for the storage account: storage.AccountsClient#ListKeys: Failure responding to request: StatusCode=404-- Original Error: autorest/azure: Service returned an error. Status=404 Code="ResourceNotFound" Message="The Resource 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/ ' under resource group ' ' was not found." ```
resolution: > **Note:** This is a temporary workaround. Red Hat is actively working on a permanent fix. ### Modify the `installer-cloud-credentials` Secret 1. **Backup the Existing Secret:** ```bash oc get secret installer-cloud-credentials-n openshift-image-registry-o yaml > installer-cloud-credentials-backup.yaml ``` 2. **Retrieve the Name of the Custom Resource Group:** Identify the resource group where your custom Azure storage account resides (e.g., `custom-storage-rg`). 3. **Encode the Resource Group Name in Base64:** ```bash echo-n 'custom-storage-rg' | base64 ``` The output will be a base64-encoded string (e.g., `Y3VzdG9tLXN0b3JhZ2Utcmc=`). 4. **Modify the Secret:**- Edit the `installer-cloud-credentials` secret: ```bash oc edit secret installer-cloud-credentials-n openshift-image-registry ```- Locate the `data.azure_resourcegroup` field and replace its value with the base64-encoded string from the previous step. ```yaml data: azure_resourcegroup: Y3VzdG9tLXN0b3JhZ2Utcmc= # Updated value # Other keys remain unchanged ``` 5. **Save and Exit the Editor** 6. **Backup and Delete the `image-registry-private-configuration-user` Secret (if present and image registry operator still Degraded):**- Review the status of the `image-registry` Cluster Operator. If notice the errors below, it would be advisable to create a backup and then remove the `image-registry-private-configuration-user` secret. ```bash Progressing: Unable to apply resources: unable to sync storage configuration: client misconfigured, missing 'TenantID', 'ClientID', 'ClientSecret', 'FederatedTokenFile', 'Creds', 'SubscriptionID' option(s) ``` ```bash oc get secret image-registry-private-configuration-user-n openshift-image-registry-o yaml > image-registry-private-configuration-user-backup.yaml oc delete secret image-registry-private-configuration-user-n openshift-image-registry ``` 7. **Verify the Image Registry Operator Status:** ```bash oc get clusteroperator image-registry ``` Ensure the operator reports `Available=True`, `Progressing=False`, and `Degraded=False`. 8. **Proceed with the Upgrade:** Initiate the upgrade to OpenShift 4.15.x using the standard upgrade process. > **Note: Rotate Service Principal Credentials** Rotating the service principal credentials **will reset the `installer-cloud-credentials` secret**, including the `azure_resourcegroup` key, back to the default resource group value. **As a result, the workaround will need to be reapplied after the rotation.** **Temporary Workaround:** The provided resolution is a temporary fix. The manual modification may need to be reapplied after future upgrades. **Permanent Fix:** Red Hat Engineering is working on a permanent solution to address this issue in a future release. **Monitoring Progress:** Refer to [OCPBUGS-42514](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42514) for updates on the permanent fix.
root_cause: The image registry operator expects the storage account to reside in the same resource group as the cluster's default resource group. When a custom storage account in a different resource group is specified, the operator misconfigures the Azure storage credentials, leading to failures in accessing the storage account during the upgrade.

title: Set ARO Node Resource Alert: CPU/Memory Utilization Exceeds 80%
issue: - Is it possible to set alert on nodes in ARO when it consumes CPU/Memory over 80%.
resolution: - In ARO, adding rules to the default cluster monitoring instance is unsupported.- An alternative approach is to create:- `UserWorkloadMonitoring` in ARO. [document](https://cloud.redhat.com/experts/aro/user-workload-monitoring/)- Alerting Rules for `user-defined projects`. [document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/observability/monitoring/managing-alerts.html#about-creating-alerting-rules-for-user-defined-projects_managing-alerts)
