title: etcd_network_peer_round trip increase after upgrading RHOCP 4
issue: - After upgrading the cluster an increase (nearly doubling) of the `etcd_network_peer_round_trip_time_seconds_bucket` metric is observed.
root_cause: The observation is a result of quantile calculation. The distribution of samples has shifted to the right, but for the top 1%, the results are influenced by the defined buckets. No impact on the cluster's performance is experienced.

title: Deployment failed with error : " cannot set `allowPrivilegeEscalation` to false and `privileged` to true"
issue: - Pod keeps on failing and show below mentioned events: ~~~ cannot set `allowPrivilegeEscalation` to false and `privileged` to true ~~~
resolution: - Edit the deployment or statefulset which is creating this pod, in this case pod was being created with the use of statefulset: ~~~ $ oc edit statefulset/platform-fts securityContext: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false capabilities: drop:- ALL privileged: true----------> change this value to false, because allowPrivilegeEscalation is also set to false runAsGroup: 1000 ~~~- Both values `allowPrivilegeEscalation` & `privileged` should be same either `true` or `false`. **NOTE: Setting privileged: true and allowPrivilegeEscalation: true in a container security context can introduce significant security risks because they grant the container extended privileges on the host system.**
root_cause: - The key issue lies in the conflict between two specific fields within the securityContext of the container: 1. `allowPrivilegeEscalation` is set to `false`. This field, when set to false, prevents the container from gaining more privileges than its parent process. It ensures that even if the container attempts to escalate privileges (e.g., through a setuid binary), it will not be allowed to do so. 2. `privileged` is set to `true`. This field, when set to true, allows the container to run in privileged mode, giving it extended privileges on the host machine (e.g., access to all host devices, the ability to manipulate kernel modules, etc.).- OpenShift does not allow both of these to be set at the same time for security reasons. If the container is running in privileged mode, it inherently escalates privileges, which conflicts with the allowPrivilegeEscalation: false setting.

title: AWS Placement support in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: We need support for [AWS Placement groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-groups.html) on AWS Outpost to achieve the required availability of the OpenShift platform.
resolution: * Starting with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform [4.14](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes.html#ocp-4-14-mapi-aws-placement-groups), it becomes possible to configure a `MachineSet` to deploy `Machines` within an existing AWS placement group. * For more information on how to configure `placementGroupName` usage in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 and later, review [Assigning machines to placement groups for Elastic Fabric Adapter instances by using machine sets](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/machine_management/creating_machinesets/creating-machineset-aws.html#machineset-aws-existing-placement-group_creating-machineset-aws). * Starting with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform [4.17](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/release_notes/ocp-4-17-release-notes.html#ocp-4-17-enhancements-aws-mapi-placement_release-notes), it becomes possible to configure `placementGroupPartition` field for `MachineSet` on Amazon Web Services (AWS). With this feature, it's possible to specify a partition number within an existing placement group, enabling precise instance allocation and improved fault tolerance. * For more information on how to configure `placementGroupPartition`, refer to [Assigning machines to placement groups for Elastic Fabric Adapter instances by using machine sets](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/machine_management/creating_machinesets/creating-machineset-aws.html#machineset-aws-existing-placement-group_creating-machineset-aws).

title: High Utilization on control plane nodes after upgrading Pipelines Operator in RHOCP 4
issue: - The state of the `tektonaddon` switches between `True` and `False` multiple times in a minute: $ oc get tektonaddons.operator.tekton.dev addon-w NAME VERSION READY REASON addon 1.11.1 False Installer set not ready: versioned cluster tasks not yet ready: TektonAddon/custom-versionedclustertask: installer set not ready, will retry: Install failed with message: Operation cannot be fulfilled on clusterroles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "tekton-clustertasks-view": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again addon 1.11.1 True- High load on control plane nodes post upgrading `Pipeline operator` from 1.10 to 1.11 version.- High load on control plane nodes when running `Pipeline operator` 1.13 version.
resolution: - Delete older `tektoninstallerset` execute below command: **NOTE: Do not delete the newest `tektoninstallerset`** $ oc delete tektoninstallerset-n openshift-pipelines

title: cluster_autoscaler_max_nodes_count metric query reports value from MachineAutoscaler instead of ClusterAutoscaler in RHOCP4
issue: - The metric query for `cluster_autoscaler_max_nodes_count` currently reports values sourced from the `MachineAutoscaler` rather than the intended `ClusterAutoscaler`.- The `cluster_autoscaler_max_nodes_count` metric query incorrectly reports values from the `MachineAutoscaler` instead of the `ClusterAutoscaler`.
resolution: - It is an expected change and has been implemented in the RHOCP 4.13 release.- For additional information, please refer to the [Pull Request 5362](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/pull/5362).
root_cause: - Please find below the [code](https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes-autoscaler/blob/master/cluster-autoscaler/core/static_autoscaler.go#L363-L367) for the production of this metric. ~~~ if a.MaxNodesTotal > 0 {metrics.UpdateMaxNodesCount(integer.IntMin(a.MaxNodesTotal, maxNodesCount))} else {metrics.UpdateMaxNodesCount(maxNodesCount)} ~~~- If `maxNodesTotal` field is specified in the `ClusterAutoscaler` record, then the metric will reflect the lesser value between the specified `maxNodesTotal` and the total sum of maximum nodes from all associated `MachineAutoscaler` records.- If `maxNodesTotal` field is not specified, then the metric will consistently display the total sum of maximum nodes from all the `MachineAutoscaler` records. For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).

title: Create persistent volumes in specific AWS availability zone using the EBS CSI driver
issue: - `EBS volumes` must be placed in the same AWS `availability zone` as the `instance` associated with the `OpenShift node` where `application workloads` run.
resolution: Creating a dedicated `storage class` for a specific `availability zone` ``` apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass allowedTopologies:- matchLabelExpressions:- key: topology.ebs.csi.aws.com/zone values:- metadata:... parameters: provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com... ```
root_cause: By default, volumes are generally round-robin created across all active zones where the OpenShift cluster has a node running. [Amazon EBS volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volumes.html) only could be attached to a single `instance` that must be placed on the same `availability zone` that the `volume`. ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. title: Incremental volume backup restore with OADP
issue: - I have tried to restore a previous restic PVC backup but the content did not get restored, although, no errors were reported in velero.- Want to restore a single PV from a restic backup done with OADP. Is this possible?- I would like to restore just one PV out of many. I am not interested in restoring any resource or namespace configuration at all.
resolution: OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) does **not support** the restore of existing files, incremental restore. You must delete the volume to be completely restored with the contents of the backup taken previously. For restic, you also need a Pod to mount the volume during the restore flow.
root_cause: By default, velero doesn't restore objects that already exist. For example if you are restoring 10 secrets from backup and 8 exist but you had accidentally deleted 2, then only those two are restored. You can modify the **existingResourcePolicy** spec in the Restore CR, although this setting only applies to the Kubernetes resource data such as its spec. In case of PVCs for example, data in the PV is not restored or overwritten in any way. Restic relies on the pod restore flow, if the pod exists in the target namespace/project, then the PodVolumeRestore (PVR) CR and related restic actions will not happen. This is due to the velero/restic implementation: 1) A pod must be mounting the volume in order for the restic pod to have access to it. 2) velero inserts an initcontainer into the pod on restore as part of the velero/restic/pod interaction. As a result, the best way to ensure that restic restores happen would be by deleting the pod beforehand. For a volumesnapshotter or CSI restore, the pod is unnecessary, although in that case the PVC would need to be deleted before restore happens, since incremental snapshot/CSI restore is not supported.

title: How to start multiple toolbox containers in OCP 4
issue: - How to start multiple toolbox containers?- When I run 2 toolboxes on the same node, one operation is reflected in the other toolbox.
resolution: Change the container name from `toolbox-root` to something else in the /root/.toolboxrc file using the `TOOLBOX_NAME` ~~~ sh-5.1# cat /root/.toolboxrc TOOLBOX_NAME=toolbox-01 ~~~
root_cause: The toolbox command executes a bidirectional bash shell on the `toolbox-root` container if one already exists. Therefore, if the `toolbox-root` container is already running, it wil be needed to start a container with a different name.

title: NMState does not delete edited routes
issue: - There appears to be a bug in NMState:- When editing the route in a NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy, NMState does not delete (or update) the old version of the route but creates an additional route to the Networkmanager instead, so two conflicting routes are part of the Network Manager configuration.
resolution: - To remove a route, state: absent needs to be specified. So for example: ~~~ routes: config:- destination: 10.10.10.10/32 metric: 451 next-hop-address: 10.123.0.64 next-hop-interface: eno2.100 table-id: 254 state: absent ~~~ Removal of the route from the policy doesn't remove the route. Removal of the policy itself is always a no-op.

title: Prometheus pods remain in CrashLoopBackOff
issue: Prometheus pods cannot start and remains in `CrashLoopBackOff`.
Pod logs show the error `"Opening storage failed open /prometheus/01HGTDKP8IYT1ELLOA8BYUYKAQ/meta.json: no such file or directory"`.
Prometheus pods are running out of memory.
resolution: NFS or any other storage solution which is not a Block storage is not supported.
root_cause: If cluster monitoring is using NFS or any other storage technology which is not a block storage, data corruptions to the time series database can happen. OpenShift monitoring supports only Block storage as documented for [OpenShift 3](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/prometheus_cluster_monitoring.html#persistent-storage) and [OpenShift 4](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/monitoring/configuring-the-monitoring-stack.html#persistent-storage-prerequisites_configuring-the-monitoring-stack).

title: Prometheus error where segments are not sequential in RHOCP 4
issue: Prometheus pod is in `crashLoopBackOff` with an error indicating that segments are not sequential: ``` $ oc logs-c prometheus-n |grep-i "segments are not sequential" 2024-10-14T07:12:16.582897967Z ts=2024-10-14T07:12:16.582Z caller=main.go:1119 level=error err="opening storage failed: get segment range: segments are not sequential" ```
resolution: Enter in the Prometheus pod in `crashLoopBackOff` and move to a different directory the `/prometheus/wal` folder. With the removal of the `/prometheus/wal` last minutes or hours of metrics that not given time to persist to the chunks will lose, but metrics for the same service should be available in the other Prometheus pod. ``` $ oc debug pod/-n $ mkdir /prometheus/temp $ mv /prometheus/wal /prometheus/temp ``` Restart the Prometheus pod: ``` $ oc delete pod-n ``` Verify that the Prometheus pod is started: ``` $ oc-n openshift-monitoring get pods-l app.kubernetes.io/component=prometheus-n ``` Not present the error: `segments are not sequential": ``` $ oc logs-c prometheus-n |grep-i "segments are not sequential" ``` Verify not other errors are present as other files could be corrupted: ``` $ oc logs-c prometheus-n-f ``` **NOTE**: Remember to delete the `/prometheus/temp` directory if it's not required for a posterior analysis
root_cause: This error is produced by a filesystem corruption and this could be caused for several reasons, some of them are:- Using NFS that it's not POSIX Compliance. This is not supported by Red Hat, more details in [Optimizing storage](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/scalability_and_performance/optimization/optimizing-storage.html) documentation- An event that leads to a filesystem corruption

title: ACM Thanos Store Shard PVs near full usage
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - Thanos Store Shard PVs usage near to 100%- Checking Grafana dashboards historical data are missing
resolution: - Expand the PV associated to the Thanos Compactor by editing the MulticlusterObservability object. For example, to expand the PV to 150GiB run the following command: ``` $ oc patch multiclusterobservability/observability--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"storageConfig":{"compactStorageSize": "150Gi"}}}' ```- ACM should delete and recreate the observability-thanos-compact statefulset: ``` $ oc logs multicluster-observability-operator-df9df9795-jl4zf-n open-cluster-management... 2024-10-15T14:17:31.409Z INFO controller_multiclustermonitoring Update storage size for PVC {"pvc": "data-observability-thanos-compact-0"} 2024-10-15T14:17:31.418Z INFO controller_multiclustermonitoring Successfully delete sts due to storage size changed {"sts": "observability-thanos-compact"}... ``` **Note:** If the observability-thanos-compact statefulset is not automatically recreated by ACM, it is possible to manually trigger the reconcile activity by deleting the observability-observatorium-operator pod: ``` $ oc delete pod observability-observatorium-operator-9ddd58785-gts5l-n open-cluster-management-observability ```- Monitor the following two PROMQL: ``` acm_thanos_compact_halted sum(acm_thanos_compact_todo_compactions) by (group) ```- The query `acm_thanos_compact_halted` should display 0, it means that the compactor is working.- The query `sum(acm_thanos_compact_todo_compactions) by (group)` should slowly decrease to 0, it can requires few days or few weeks.
root_cause: - Thanos Compactor is not working because it has been halted.- Thanos uses the Prometheus TSDB to store data. TSDB uses blocks, where each block by default represent 2 hours of time and it need an index. The index contains all the label names and values present in the block.- The Store Gateway shards need to download all the indexes to know where the data is when queries are submitted. This operation is not very efficient for storing large amounts of data, because most of the time the label names and values are repeated a lot in a stable cluster.- The Compactor exists to concatenate the blocks into longer time ranges, this operation includes merging the blocks indexes. For this reason a broken Compactor can impact the Store Gateways shards so negatively.

title: Missing upgradeable annotation cloudcredential.openshift.io/upgradeable-to on cloudcredential.operator.openshift.io/cluster object needs updating before upgrade
issue: - RHOCP Clusters on AWS with manually maintained credentials, the message `Upgradeable annotation cloudcredential.openshift.io/upgradeable-to on cloudcredential.operator.openshift.io/cluster object needs updating before upgrade` is shown for the cloud-credential cluster operator, for both CLI and Web Console: ~~~ $ oc get co cloud-credential-o yaml ======Output-trimmed====== message: Upgradeable annotation cloudcredential.openshift.io/upgradeable-to on cloudcredential.operator.openshift.io/cluster object needs updating before upgrade. See Manually Creating IAM documentation for instructions on preparing a cluster for upgrade. reason: MissingUpgradeableAnnotation status: 'False' type: Upgradeable ======Output-trimmed====== ~~~- In the case of EUS-EUS upgrade (eg 4.14-4.16 when available) does this process need to be completed twice? Once for 4.14-4.15 and then again from 4.15-4.16?
resolution: **NOTE:** This solution applies to `RHOCP` clusters only. For ROSA/OSD clusters check this [solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970039).- To solve this issue, you must create new credentials for the release image that you are upgrading to.- Follow the steps mentioned in the documentation section [Upgrading clusters with manually maintained credentials](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/updating/preparing_for_updates/preparing-manual-creds-update.html). One must review the required permissions for existing credentials and accommodate any new permissions requirements in the new release for those components.- The [Manually creating IAM](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/installing/installing_aws/manually-creating-iam.html) section of the installation content for your cloud provider explains how to obtain and use the credentials required for your cloud.- In the case of EUS to EUS upgrade (eg 4.14-4.16), It is required to perform these steps for each version i.e for 4.15 and 4.16 respectively.- When all of the secrets are correct for the new release, indicate that the cluster is ready to upgrade and an error message will be gone: ~~~ $ oc edit cloudcredential cluster ~~~ Text to add: ~~~ metadata: annotations: cloudcredential.openshift.io/upgradeable-to: ~~~ Where is the version that you are upgrading to, in the format x.y.z. For example, use 4.16.2 for OpenShift Container Platform 4.16.2. It may take several minutes after adding the annotation for the upgradeable status to change.
root_cause: - The Cloud Credential Operator (CCO) Upgradable status for a cluster with manually maintained credentials is `False` by default.- For minor releases, for example, from 4.9 to 4.10, this status prevents you from upgrading until you have addressed any updated permissions and annotated the CloudCredential resource to indicate that the permissions are updated as needed for the next version. This annotation changes the Upgradable status to True.- For z-stream releases, for example, from 4.10.0 to 4.10.1, no permissions are added or changed, so the upgrade is not blocked.

title: How to extend login session duration for OpenShift user that the user token will never expire.
issue: We are doing some automation through script in the Openshift for that we need oc login command from CLI.
oc login token is expiring in 24 hours so we need permanent oc login token.
Need oc login token from command line that will never expire.
resolution: Create and use a custom OAuthClient object in the cluster that generates a token which never expires: 1. Create the YAML file for the `OAuthClient:` ~~~ $ cat < oauthclient-cc-custom.yaml apiVersion: oauth.openshift.io/v1 grantMethod: auto kind: OAuthClient metadata: name: openshift-challenging-client-3m redirectURIs:- https://oauth-openshift.apps.example.com/oauth/token/implicit respondWithChallenges: true accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds: 0 EOF ~~~ *Make sure the `redirectURI` has the correct domain of the `openshift-authentication` route. Get the domain from: ~~~ $ oc get routes-n openshift-authentication ~~~ * The `accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds` is the login duration. In the example, it is integer (0) which denotes Infinite days (that will never expire). 2. Create the `OAuthClient` object in the cluster, as a cluster administrator: ~~~ $ oc create-f oauthclient-cc-custom.yaml oauthclient.oauth.openshift.io/openshift-challenging-client-3m created ~~~ 3. It's possible to request a token using this `OAuthClient` with the command: ~~~ $ curl 'https://oauth-openshift.apps.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=openshift-challenging-client-3m&response_type=token' \-u ": " \-skv-H "X-CSRF-Token: $(date +%s)" \--stderr- | grep-oP "access_token=\K[^&]*" ~~~ * This will get a token for this ` ` that expires never. Example output: `BXCGIoMP7ju_q0M09cRp-1rkz-pd-QCJn-ucqnZUlwY;` * Notice that the `client_id` specifies `openshift-challenging-client-3m` which is the name of the custom `OAuthClient `created in the previous step; * If `grep` is not used, the access token is within the `Location` header in the HTTP response. * If OpenShift is using an OpenID Identity Provider, the curl could return HTTP 401. Please see the workaround for this step later in this solution. 4. Use the provided token to login or access the API: ~~~ $ oc login--token Logged into "https://api.example.com:6443" as "testusername" using the token provided. ~~~ * To test the token duration, change the expiration to 60 seconds and test the API after a minute. The default duration for all users could also be changed according to the documentation: [Configuring the internal OAuth server’s token duration.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/authentication/configuring-internal-oauth.html) ### Workaround when using OpenID Identity Provider When using an OpenID Identity Provider, it's not possible to get the OpenShift token using the curl and username/password because the OpenID server generates another token that is used to generate the OpenShift token instead of the password. Because OpenID configuration changes depending on the case, there's a workaround for generating the OpenShift token. 1. Login with the specific user that needs to change the expire time in the Web Console; 2. Get the token for this user by clicking in the upper right corner username, and then Copy Login. Copy the Token. 3. In the command line, logged-in as the cluster administrator, export this token: ~~~ $ oc get oauthaccesstoken-o yaml--export > token.yaml ~~~ 4. Edit token.yaml and change attribute expiresIn to 0 (which means infinite days). 5. Recreate the token: ~~~ $ oc delete oauthaccesstoken $ oc create-f token.yaml ~~~ 6. Notice that the token should get the unlimited days expiration time: ~~~ $ oc get oauthaccesstoken ~~~ 7. You can login using the token: ~~~ $ oc login--token ~~~ 8. As this token will never expire, please take care to not leak it. If you need to revoke the token, just delete with: ~~~ $ oc delete oauthaccesstoken ~~~

title: Pod failing load balancer healthcheck but shows healthy and running.
issue: - In `OCP` cluster with `Citrix` configured. The `ingress load balancer` (`Netscaler`) stopped receiving TCP health check responses from multiple pods.
resolution: - Restarting the `CIC (Citrix Ingress Controller)` pods will cause the outdated configuration to be updated and fixes the issue.
root_cause: - Failover of `ARO Netscaler`, leading to running an outdated configuration on primary instance due to synchronization failure.

title: `oc mirror init` & `oc mirror list` is taking time/hanging for about 3 to 4 minutes to respond.
issue: - To setup a mirror while initialising `imageset-config.yaml` with the help of below command `$ oc mirror init--registry example.com/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata > imageset-config.yaml` is taking almost 3-4 minutes and then throwing output is this expected behavior?
resolution: - This is an `expected behavior`.- Below RFE's are raised in order to mitigate the same: [RFE-4460:Speed up oc-mirror plugin commands](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4460) [RFE-4461:Improve oc-mirror plugin User Experience](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4461)
root_cause: - While using oc mirror, it has to validate the user against `registry.redhat.io`, then download the index to a temp directory, find and inspect the manifests, then untar the relevant layers and finally apply the specific filtering to dump the results, hence it takes some time.

title: Editing a secret with any multibyte characters in the web console can cause the secret value to be corrupted
issue: - When using non-English characters expressed in multibyte characters such as Japanese, Chinese, and French as secret characters in the web console- The secret, which has any multibyte characters base64-encoded as its value, is displayed as a corrupted text in the web console- If the secret is saved in this state, the corrupted text will be encoded, and the secret will become the wrong content
resolution: - This issue has already been fixed in 4.15.0 and later ([OCPBUGS-19426](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-19426))- For 4.14, 4.14.38 has been fixed ([OCPBUGS-39389](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-39389))- For the not-fixed version, the CLI command `oc edit secret ` or `oc set data secret ` can be used to edit the secret instead of the web console
root_cause: - This issue was handled in [OCPBUGS-19426](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-19426) (4.15.0) and [OCPBUGS-39389](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-39389) (4.14.z)

title: Does Red Hat Loki Operator support using custom Lokistack deployments in user namespaces?
issue: - Does the Red Hat Loki Operator support using custom Lokistack deployments in user namespaces?
resolution: Although it is technically possible, the Red Hat support range for the Loki Operator is currently limited for two products only:- OpenShift Logging (running by default on the `openshift-logging` namespace)- OpenShift Network Obervability (running on the `netobserv` namespace) For other purposes, Red Hat encourage to use the Community Loki Operator or open an RFE to evaluate the use case. In general, customers may benefit from custom LokiStack deployments at the community level, but such deployments are not part of the Red Hat products.

title: OVS service reports 'remote_ip' and 'local_ip' has to be of the same address family on Red Hat Openshift Container Platform v4
issue: - Node Primary IP is set to Ipv6 instead of Ipv4- OVS service reports the below error: ~~~ 'remote_ip' and 'local_ip' has to be of the same address family ~~~- CSRs are generated after each reboot and does not get approved automatically- Some oc CLI command fail like (oc logs, oc exec, oc rsh)
resolution: To workaround this issue one can follow our [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/support/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-network-issues.html#overriding-default-node-ip-selection-logic_troubleshooting-network-issues) to force the selection of an IPv4 family on the primary node interface using the NODEIP_HINT variable.
root_cause: It is not 100% sure why this happens but it was observed on v4.16 cluster with OVN-Kubernetes CNI plugin where on the bridge of the primary interface **br-ex** there were configured both IPv4 and IPv6 families. We suspect that this is caused because of a slower DHCP lease for the IPv4 IP that resulted to the nodeip-configuration service to find only the Ipv6 IP assigned during the node booting process. So despite that the code logic is implemented in a way to prefer IPv4 IP the service found only 1 IP at the time it was run and it was of Ipv6 Family resulting on not having both Families to choose from. This will set as primary IP the IPv6 one for all services in the node that depend on it and as a result kubelet will generate a new Server Certificate to cover this new IPv6 under SAN section. A CSR will get generated but it won't be approved cause the **openshift-cluster-machine-approver** pods will complain that the SANs between the previous and new Certificate are different. ~~~ csr_check.go:198] Could not use current serving cert for renewal: CSR Subject Alternate Name values do not match current certificate csr_check.go:199] Current SAN Values: [], CSR SAN Values: []--- Trimmed Output--- controller.go:329] "Reconciler error" err="could not reconcile CSR: could not authorize CSR: exhausted all authorization methods: [CSR Subject Alternate Name values do not match current certificate, Unable to find machine for node]" controller="certificatesigningrequest" controllerGroup="certificates.k8s.io" controllerKind="CertificateSigningRequest" CertificateSigningRequest="csr-xxxxx" namespace="" name="csr-xxxxx" reconcileID="XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" ~~~ This will cause issues when API will try to access logs or containers on this node making the (oc logs, oc rsh, oc exec) commands to fail.

title: galera cluster is not formed and maradb-operator continuously restarted.
issue: - galera cluster is not formed and maradb-operator continuously restarted. The issue happens some time later after deploying control plane.
resolution: - This issue is being tracked at [OSPRH-8862](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSPRH-8862).- Workaround- Delete all galera pod by the following command. ~~~ $ oc--namespace openstack delete pod openstack-cell1-galera{0,1,2} ~~~- You can follow the live update of the status by ~~~ $ oc get-o json galera openstack-cell1 | jq 'del(.status.conditions,.status.hash) |.status' ~~~
root_cause: The liveness probe did not parse non-Primary condition out of the mysql CLI command. Consequently, the liveness did not fail whe a galera node was disconnected from the primary partition and the galera pod could not restart automatically, leading to long delays before restart or sometimes full cluster disruption.

title: Remove CPU limits from Service Mesh istio-proxy container
issue: - Is there a way to modify `CPU limits` for `istio-proxy` containers injected by the `Service Mesh Operator`?
resolution: - There is no way to remove `CPU limit` for `istio-proxy` container. If the `CPU limit` is removed it will always take the default value.- However, `service mesh control plane` can be modified as per the [document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/service_mesh/v2x/ossm-reference-smcp.html#:~:text=Example%20ServiceMeshControlPlane%20resource). ~~~ apiVersion: maistra.io/v2 kind: ServiceMeshControlPlane metadata: name: basic spec: version: v2.4 proxy: runtime: container: resources: requests: cpu: 100m memory: 128Mi limits: cpu: 500m < < < < < memory: 128Mi ~~~

title: Openshift 3.x - How to add a custom bundle CA certificate for the OpenShift Container Platform web console
issue: - How to specify a custom CA bundle certificate to the web console.
resolution: **Consider the scenario below:** When the cluster has a custom CA bundle certificate, the chaining process is similar to: `Root CA-> Intermediate CA-> custom certificate` In order to specify a custom CA bundle certificate, a new file would need to be created from both Root CA + Intermediate CA in the *following strict order*: `Root CA + Intermediate CA`. ~~~ $ cat rootCA.crt intermediateCA.crt > custom-ca.crt` ~~~ *** Then you can follow procedure explained on [How to add custom certificates for Openshift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3110541) and make sure you add a *cafile* option within *openshift_master_named_certificates* option in the ansible inventory file pointing to the file created earlier, e.g: ~~~ openshift_master_named_certificates=[{"certfile": "/etc/origin/master/custom.crt", "keyfile": "/etc/origin/master/custom.key", "names": ["example.net"], "cafile": "/etc/origin/master/custom-ca.crt"}] ~~~ **Note**: Please bear in mind that in order to customize your web console certificates, the namedCertificates section should only be configured for the host name associated with the **masterPublicURL**, **assetConfig.publicURL**, and **oauthConfig.assetPublicURL** settings. Using a custom serving certificate for the host name associated with the masterURL will result in TLS errors as infrastructure components will attempt to contact the master API using the internal masterURL host. For 3.9+ please check the documentation as web console is running as an application in pod.

title: [OpenShift Virtualisation] Machine Config Operator (MCP) is in a degraded state
issue: - The MCP was stuck and not rolling out due to non-migratable VirtualMachines (VMs) running on the node, preventing the node drain process.- Below messages can be seen in the `Machine-Config-Controller` POD: ~~~ error when evicting pods/"virt_POD_name"-n "namespace_name" (will retry after 5s): admission webhook "virt-launcher-eviction-interceptor.kubevirt.io" denied the request: VMI vmi_name is configured with an eviction strategy but is not live-migratable ~~~- It was found that these VMs had a ReadWriteOnce volume attached, making them non-live-migratable, which led to the issue.
resolution: - Stopping the VMs allowed the MCP to roll out successfully: ~~~ # virtctl stop ~~~- Once the MCP is rolled out successfully on all the nodes, start the VirtualMachine again: ~~~ # virtctl start ~~~
root_cause: - The VM has ReadWriteOnce volume attached and these are not ready for live migration. In this scenario, it is recommended to stop the VMs on that node and then start the node drain.

title: Is it possible to inherit labels to pods from namespace in RHOCP 4?
issue: - Is it possible to inherit labels to resources from namespace?- To sort resources deployed in specific namespaces, it is required to add defined labels to each resources manually. Is it possible to do it without manual intervention?
resolution: - Resources cannot inherit labels from namespace.- To avoid manual label addition to each resources, create [`admission webhook`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/).

title: Multiple co degraded after master node replacement in RHOCP 4
issue: - Observed multiple CO degraded after node replacement.- During master node replacement, older master node came up caused CO degrade issue. ~~~ authentication 4.14.17 False True True 39h APIServicesAvailable: "oauth.openshift.io.v1" is not ready: an attempt failed with statusCode = 503, err = the server is currently unable to handle the request... kube-apiserver 4.14.17 True True True 593d TargetConfigControllerDegraded: "serviceaccount/localhost-recovery-client": Internal error occurred: no matching key was found for the provided AES transformer kube-controller-manager 4.14.17 True False True 593d TargetConfigControllerDegraded: "serviceaccount/localhost-recovery-client": Internal error occurred: no matching key was found for the provided AES transformer kube-scheduler 4.14.17 True False True 593d TargetConfigControllerDegraded: "serviceaccount/localhost-recovery-client": Internal error occurred: no matching key was found for the provided AES transformer ~~~
resolution: - Make sure to follow [node replacement procees](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/backup_and_restore/control_plane_backup_and_restore/replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member.html#restore-replace-stopped-etcd-member_replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member) without skipping any step- Make sure old master node is not part of etcd member list. ~~~ $ ETCD=$(oc get pods-n openshift-etcd-l app=etcd--field-selector="status.phase==Running"-o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") $ oc exec-n openshift-etcd $ETCD-c etcdctl-- etcdctl member list-w table ~~~- Old master node should be shut down after node replacement.
root_cause: - If old master node is still part of etcd member list or is not shutdown poperly then etcd tries to connect to older node causes cluster to degrade.

title: FailedCreate: pods "test" is forbidden: [maximum memory  usage per Pod is xMi.]' in RHOCP4
issue: - Pod creation failed with below error: ~~~ message: ' deployment / has a replica failure FailedCreate: pods " is forbidden: [maximum cpu usage per Pod is m. No limit is specified, maximum memory usage per Pod is Mi. No limit is specified]' ~~~
resolution: - Verify `LimitRange` created in namespace. ~~~ $ oc get LimitRange-o yaml-n ~~~- Check resource request/limit set for deployment. Make sure it qualifies all restriction set with [`LimitRange`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/nodes/clusters/nodes-cluster-limit-ranges.html)
root_cause: - When resource request/limit are not correctly set as per restriction set with `LimitRange`, then pod creation fails.

title: Communication failure on vlan provider network when using bonds on compute nodes
issue: Instances using a vlan provider network cannot reach other addresses on the same network segment.
resolution: The corresponding vlan/s should be trunked on the bond interface on the switch, not the individual interfaces. ~~~ HOST(config)# interface port-channel HOST(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan ~~~
root_cause: The corresponding vlan/s are allowed on the individual ports on the switch, not on the bond interfaces as it should be.

title: Quay Operator upgrade failed with  Internal error occurred: admission plugin "ValidatingAdmissionWebhook"
issue: - Quay upgrade from 3.10.x to 3.12.x failed with below error ~~~ error creating object: Internal error occurred: admission plugin "ValidatingAdmissionWebhook" failed to complete validation in 13s ~~~
resolution: - Deleted quay-operator ClusterRole and- Restarted quay-operator pod

title: VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRDegraded: VMwareVSphereControllerDegraded: POST "/sdk": 503 Service Unavailable
issue: - Storage Operator degraded- Cluster operator shows below status ~~~ storage 4.13.29 True False True 16h VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRDegraded: VMwareVSphereControllerDegraded: POST "/sdk": 503 Service Unavailable ~~~
resolution: - Ensure that the vSphere API endpoint is accessible from the OpenShift nodes. ~~~ $ curl-kvv https:// /sdk ~~~- If connectivity is enabled and issue occurs all of a sudden, restart the csi driver pods and check. ~~~ $ oc delete pod-l app=csi-vsphere-controller ~~~
root_cause: - If issue is reported during the deployment phase, check the connectivity to vsphere API and folder permissions in VMWare.- If issue occurs abruptly then connectivity might be interrupted with the vsphere API, and if csi driver pod restart fix it then contact vendor to find the root cause as the csi driver is provided by VMware.

title: failed to authorize: failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status: 401 Unauthorized, while running oc-mirror
issue: - 401 Unauthorized- Server message: unauthorized: while running oc-mirror.- Getting Unauthorized while running oc-mirror command as root user.- Even after successful login to registry.redhat.io getting 401 Unauthorized after executing oc-mirror command. ~~~ [root@~]# podman login registry.redhat.io Username: user_id Password: password Login Succeeded! [root@~]# oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 level=info msg=trying next host error=failed to authorize: failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status: 401 Unauthorized host=registry.redhat.io error: failed to list operators, please check catalog name- registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12: render reference "registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12": error resolving name: failed to authorize: failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status: 401 Unauthorized ~~~
resolution: - Store the credential in `~/.docker/config.json`. Below steps can be followed. 1. First login using `podman` command. ~~~ [root@~]# podman login registry.redhat.io-u-p ~~~ 2. Make sure credentials are stored in below path ~~~ [root@~]# cat /run/containers/0/auth.json ~~~ 3. Create `.docker` directory in `root's` home directory and redirect the output to `~/.docker/config.json` ~~~ [root@~]# mkdir ~/.docker [root@~]# cat /run/containers/0/auth.json > ~/.docker/config.json ~~~ OR- Make sure that your [Red Hat OpenShift Pull Secret](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/install/pull-secret) and any other needed registry credentials are populated in `~/.docker/config.json`
root_cause: - oc-mirror currently retrieves [registry credentials](https://github.com/openshift/oc-mirror/blob/main/docs/usage.md#authentication) from ~/.docker/config.json or ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json. Since root user doesn't have `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json` path to store the credentials `oc-mirror` unable to find run-time credentials for `root` user.

title: Machine stuck in Provisioning status when machine is power off
issue: - Sometimes machine is powered off and in "Provisioning" phase, it will trigger a new machine creation, and report error "failed to Create machine: The name 'machine-name' already exists"
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and it is fixed a part of [bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-1735) in RHOCP 4.17 version.- Here is the link to [errata](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3718) and RHOCP 4.17 [release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/release_notes/ocp-4-17-release-notes.html)- Also, the work is being done to get this fix backported to RHOCP 4.16 [z-stream](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-43433)
root_cause: - machine controller failed to save the task ID of an instance template clone operation. This caused the machine to go into the `Provisioning` state and to power off.

title: How to simulate the resulting network configuration for a set of network kernel parameters
issue: - I need to know what exact NetworManager configurations would result from a set of kernel network parameters
resolution: Run: ~~~ /usr/libexec/nm-initrd-generator-s... ~~~ Where `... ` are the kernel parmeters to test (it is possible to just copy-paste the entire kernel command line, because unrelated or unrecognized parameters are ignored). The command above generates an output with the networkmanager connections (in keyfile format) and networkmanager configuration that would be applied to a dracut environment started with those kernel parameters.
root_cause: In Dracut (the initramfs environment used in RHEL and RHCOS), networking kernel parameters documented in `man dracut.cmdline` are read and parsed by `nm-initrd-generator`. From them, it creates some NetworkManager connections and configurations in the Dracut environment that are then used to setup the networking in this environment. Besides, Red Hat CoreOS also uses these parameters to generate the networking configuration of new nodes while being installed in some ways. As it is interesting in both cases to debug which exact result will happen from a given set of kernel parameters, `nm-initrd-generator` includes the `-s` option, to just dump the results to stdout so they can be inspected.

title: Changing the log level of the router on RHSI on OCP
issue: - How to change the log level of the router component of RHSI deployed on OCP via Operator?
resolution: When initializing a RHSI site by CLI, the logging level of the router can be set using the `router-logging` parameter. ~~~ $ skupper init--router-logging trace ~~~ The same result can be achieved by creating the skupper-site configmap adding the `router-logging` key value. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: skupper-site data: router-logging: trace ~~~ To change the log level of the router after the site has been initialized, edit the log section of the`skupper-internal` ConfigMap, then restart the router pod. ~~~ ["log", {"module": "DEFAULT", "enable": "trace+"}] ~~~

title: Upgrading RHSI operator to the latest version via OCP web console
issue: - How to upgrade RHSI operator via console to the latest version?
resolution: From RHSI operator release 1.8.1, it is possible to upgrade the operator to the latest version directly via console, without re-installing the operator. To achieve this follow the steps below:- Navigate in the web console to the Installed Operators page;- If a new version is available the status of the RHSI operator shows the `Upgrade available` link, [image=[src="images/screenshot_from_2024-10-08_14-57-19.png", alt="RHSI installed operators", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%",]]- Review and approve the operator upgrade install plan

title: Loki ingester fails to get token ranges
issue: When deploying the network observability operator a loki stack is deployed too, and it can happen that the loki-ingester faces a problem with stale entry of the ingester pods.
resolution: Replace XXX.XX.XX.XX in the below commands with the IP of distributor pods. ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging debug--image=registry.redhat.io/ubi8:latest deployment/logging-loki-distributor $ curl-k--cert /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.crt--key /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.key https://XXX.XX.XX.XX:3100/ring-H "Accept: application/json" ~~~ Sample output should look like ~~~ {"shards":[{"id":"logging-loki-ingester-0","state":"ACTIVE",[...]},{"id":"logging-loki-ingester-1","state":"UNHEALTHY",[...]} ~~~ If cluster has proxy then use below command ~~~ $ curl-k--cert /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.crt--key /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.key--noproxy "XXX.XX.XX.XX" https://XXX.XX.XX.XX:3100/ring-H "Accept: application/json" ~~~ Once we have which ingester is unhealthy delete the ingester entry using below steps ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging debug--image=registry.redhat.io/ubi8:latest deployment/logging-loki-distributor $ curl-k--cert /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.crt--key /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.key https://XXX.XX.XX.XX:3100/ring-X POST--data-raw 'forget=logging-loki-ingester-1' ## using logging-loki-ingester-1 as example using the name of the pod which is unhealthy in your case. ~~~ If cluster has proxy then use below command ~~~ $ curl-k--cert /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.crt--key /var/run/tls/http/server/tls.key--noproxy https://XXX.XX.XX.XX:3100/ring-X POST--data-raw 'forget=logging-loki-ingester-1' ## using logging-loki-ingester-1 as example using the name of the pod which is unhealthy. ~~~ Delete ingester pods ~~~ $ oc delete pods-l app.kubernetes.io/component=ingester-n openshift-logging ~~~

title: Upgrade to a version lower than 4.16 is blocked due to weak SHA1 signature algorithm
issue: Upgrade is blocked due to the error: ~~~- lastTransitionTime: "2024-10-17T07:52:49Z" message: 'Cluster operator ingress should not be upgraded between minor versions: Some ingresscontrollers are not upgradeable: ingresscontroller "default" is not upgradeable: OperandsNotUpgradeable: One or more managed resources are not upgradeable: certificate in secret openshift-ingress/router-certs-default-v4 has weak SHA1 signature algorithm: SHA1-RSA (see https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes.html#ocp-4-16-sha-haproxy-support-removed_release-notes for more details)' reason: IngressControllersNotUpgradeable status: "False" type: Upgradeable ~~~
resolution: The message above is misleading. It is true that upgrades to 4.16 will be blocked if SHA1 certificates are in use by Ingress. Refer to the the solution [Upgrade to RHOCP 4.16 is blocked due to weak SHA1 signature algorithm](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7089632) for more details. However, between.z versions of 4.15 the above message is just a warning and it does not block any upgrade. If the upgrade is blocked, ignore the above message and search for other reasons.
root_cause: If not upgrading to 4.16, the message is just a warning. It does not block the upgrade.

title: MCP Nodes count is incorrect
issue: - Nodes are missing from the MCP even if the nodeSelector in the MCP matches the node- The MCP count is incorrect, having extra or missing Nodes- Node belong to multiple MCPs ``` can't get pool for node " ": node belongs to X custom roles, cannot proceed with this Node ```- Multiple custom MCPs have similar NodeSelectors leading the MCO to ignore them.
resolution: ##### Node label(s) updated not reflected in the MCP In case the MCP machine number is not updated yet, please allow at least **30 min**, or restart the **machine-config-controller** POD: ~~~ oc delete pod-n openshift-machine-config-operator-l "k8s-app"="machine-config-controller" ~~~ ##### Node assigned to too many custom MCPs In the case of a node assigned to multiple custom MCP roles, please review your MCP **nodeSelectors** and Nodes **roles** and remove any conflicts with in the node's labels definition: ``` $ oc get mcp-o json | jq-r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name) | \(.spec.nodeSelector.matchLabels)"' | column-s'|'-t $ oc get nodes-o json | jq-r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name) | \(.metadata.labels | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("node-role.kubernetes.io")) |.key)"' | column-s '|'-t ``` Based on the example from the Diagnostic section, and knowing that the worker-2 should actually apply the **logging** MCP, the role **infra** can be unlabeled from the node. To remove a label, simply use the following command using only the label key followed by a minus '-' sign: ``` $ oc label node worker-2 node-role.kubernetes.io/infra- node/worker-2 unlabeled ``` ##### Multiple MCPs using the same nodeSelector match In the case of multiple custom MCP roles are trying to use the same *nodeSelector* match, so the MCO does not know where the node should belong to. Please review the MCP node selectors and adjust it: ``` $ oc get mcp-o json | jq-r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name) | \(.spec.nodeSelector.matchLabels)"' | column-s'|'-t ``` And edit the MCP to replace the incorrect *nodeSelector* match ``` oc edit mcp ```
root_cause: The Machine Config Pools (MCP) node allocations are managed by the machine-config-controller pod, part of the Machine Config Operator (MCO) The POD is reviewing the current configuration every 30 min, and when some nodes have some labels added. It can take some time for a modification to be applied in the `oc get mcp` output. Another cause of missing nodes in MCPs is when a node has multiple custom roles, and those roles are matching different custom MCPs. From a MCO perspective, a node can belong to one (or zero) generic MCP (worker or master) AND/OR only ONE custom MCP. In this case the node will use the custom MCP to deploy the related MCP config. And lastly, if multiple custom MCPs are refeering to the same *nodeSelector* match, any nodes matching this *nodeSelector* will be excluded from the MCPs by the MCO. So if a node is managed by multiple custom MCPs, the MCO does not know which custom MCP is the desired one, and it will exclude the node from any MCP (including the default ones)

title: Deny assignment error when trying to delete Azure disk
issue: When trying to delete an Azure volume that is or has been associated with an ARO cluster, the following error is observed: ~~~ Failed to delete disk ' '. Error: The client ' ' with object id ' ' has permission to perform action 'Microsoft.Compute/disks/delete' on scope ' '; however, the access is denied because of the deny assignment with name ' ' and Id ' ' at scope ' '. ~~~
resolution: _**WARNING**_: *The steps described here **will result in data loss** of the disk being deleted. Before continuing, make a **backup** of any important data. Also, double-double-check your **disk ID**!* ### If both the PV and PVC have been deleted 1. Clone an existing PV object (eg, 'oc get pv example-o yaml > example.yaml') 2. If the PVC doesn't exist, create a dummy PVC (it doesn't have to contain legitimate information; it is just a placeholder so the following steps work) 3. Change the *azurediskid* in the new PV yaml to match *the disk that you wish to delete* 4. In the new PV yaml, change the PVC binding info to match the newly-created PVC 5. Also in the new PV yaml, change the *reclaimpolicy* to "Delete" 6. Create a new PV object from the above edited PV yaml (eg, 'oc create-f example.yaml') 7. Verify the above steps worked (eg, 'oc get pv example.yaml-n namespace-o yaml') 8. Once satisfied that the above steps have been successful, delete the *PVC* (not the PV) to trigger the reclaim policy set in the PV ### If either the PV or PVC has been deleted Make a backup of either the PV or PVC, as appropriate to your situation, before continuing. Follow the relevant steps from above. For example, if only the PVC has been deleted, verify the PV disk ID and reclaim policy as above and then follow from step *2*, skipping step *6*. ### If the PV and PVC have *not* been deleted Make a backup of both PV and PVC before continuing. Using the above steps, verify that the PV has the correct Azure disk ID and that the PV reclaim policy is set to "Delete" and that the PV references the expected PVC. If all of this is valid, delete the PVC.
root_cause: **Disclaimer:** *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* OpenShift (and ARO) will automatically delete a volume that is associated with a PV object that is configured with a reclaim policy of 'Delete' *when the associated PVC is deleted*. The PV and associated volume will then also be deleted (unless the volume is locked or in use by some host). [This is the normal OpenShift/ARO process when processing a volume's *Delete* reclaim policy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/storage/understanding-persistent-storage.html) and works under most circumstances. There are occasions when something might go wrong-- for example, if the PV was not originally configured with a reclaim policy to delete and the PV and PVC were deleted. This will leave an "orphaned" disk that cannot be deleted from the Azure management console due to an ARO *deny assignment*. These deny assignments are created by the Azure Red Hat OpenShift resource provider which contains Azure Red Hat OpenShift cluster components, including virtual machines, network security groups, and load balancers. Azure Red Hat OpenShift cluster components located within this resource group are **not** modifiable by customers. **Cluster configuration against disks such as the steps given in the "Resolution" section must therefore be performed via interactions with the OpenShift API using the OpenShift web console or OpenShift CLI.** By following the steps in the "Resolution" section of this article, OpenShift will spot that the PVC for the PV with "Delete" reclaim policy is has been deleted and follow the normal Reclaim Policy. Provided the reclaim policy is set to "Delete" this process should delete the underlying Azure Disk and the PV. Note that in order to delete a disk, the volume would have to be *not in use* by any host and *not mounted nor attached*. Please see the [Azure Red Hat OpenShift service definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/openshift-service-definitions#azure-resource-architecture) page for more information about ARO architecture.

title: Incorrect MTU size in the network prevents TLS traffic in RHOCP 4
issue: - Is possible to access the Web Console from some networks but not from others.- A TCP connection can be established with the HAProxy but there is no TLS handshake.- Server Hello not reaching back the client preventing the OpenShift IngressVIP to work as expected.- HTTPS connectivity not working between hosts after TCP connection is established.- Noobaa is timing out to find the object from it's datastore.- Testing an HTTPS connection with curl the connection reach timeout after the `Client hello`: $ curl-kvs https://10.0.0.1
ALPN, offering h2
ALPN, offering http/1.1
CAfile: /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt
TLSv1.0 (OUT), TLS header, Certificate Status (22):
TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):- Curl command returns error: `curl: (35) schannel: failed to receive handshake, SSL/TLS connection failed`.
resolution: This is issue is external to OpenShift, all the devices between the client and the OpenShift cluster must have a correct MTU size to allow what is configured on the hosts.
root_cause: Client and server when establishing a TCP connection agree on a maximum segment size (MSS) based on their local MTU size, so if in the network path there is one or more devices with an MTU size lower than the server and the client when the full size is used the TLS packets are dropped because they have the Don't Fragment flag enabled.

title: How to search Red Hat OpenStack containers details

RHOSP 17 uses RHEL 8 only when it's doing FFU from RHOSP 16. rhosp-rhel8/openstack-nova-api-container > > > RHOSP 16 rhosp-rhel8/openstack-nova-api-container > > > for intermediate state of upgrade from RHOSP 16 to 17 rhosp-rhel9/openstack-nova-api-container > > > RHOSP 17 rhoso-operators/nova-rhel9-operator > > > RHOSO 18 OpenStack Operators rhoso/openstack-nova-api-rhel9 > > > RHOSO 18 OpenStack Container images [image=[src="images/screenshot_of_catalog.png", alt="The screenshot of container details on catalog", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%",]] 2. title: Failure to download base ISO with openshift-install agent create image
issue: - `openshift-install agent create image` fails to download the base ISO.- Attempting to install a disconnected cluster using the `Agent-based installer`. A mirror registry was set up in the disconnected environment, and necessary images were mirrored for installation.- To use the `openshift-install agent wait-for`, the `openshift-install` was installed on a machine that can communicate with the API server of the disconnected cluster.- When executing the `openshift-install agent create image` on that machine, it fails with an error and cannot generate the base ISO. ERROR failed to write asset (Agent Installer ISO) to disk: cannot generate ISO image due to configuration errors FATAL failed to fetch Agent Installer ISO: failed to fetch dependency of "Agent Installer ISO": failed to fetch dependency of "Agent Installer Artifacts": failed to generate asset "BaseIso Image": failed to get base ISO image: failed to download base ISO image https://rhcos.mirror.openshift.com/art/storage/prod/streams/4.15-9.2/builds/415.92.202402130021-0/x86_64/rhcos-415.92.202402130021-0-live.x86_64.iso: Get "https://rhcos.mirror.openshift.com/art/storage/prod/streams/4.15-9.2/builds/415.92.202402130021-0/x86_64/rhcos-415.92.202402130021-0-live.x86_64.iso": dial tcp: lookup rhcos.mirror.openshift.com: i/o timeout
resolution: - Use the `openshift-install` same version that the mirrored release image in the mirror registry.- Use the `openshift-install` extracted from the mirror registry with the following command. $ oc adm release extract-a ${LOCAL_SECRET_JSON}--command=openshift-install "${LOCAL_REGISTRY}/${LOCAL_REPOSITORY}:${OCP_RELEASE}"
root_cause: - The `openshift-install agent create image` fetches an ISO file from the `release image` specified in `openshift-install`. If it points to a mirror registry, the ISO will download from there.- If `openshift-install` is installed from an internet service like `cloud.redhat.com`, it points to the `release images` on `quay.io`. However, it fetches the ISO from the mirror registry based on the `ImageDigestSource (imageContentSource)` in `install-config.yaml`.- Using a version of `openshift-install` that does not match the release images in the mirror registry prevents downloading the ISO from there.- If unable to download the ISO from the mirror registry, it attempts to download from `rhcos.mirror.openshift.com`, which fails in a disconnected environment.

title: How to create a Prometheus Alert that only fires on week days in RHOCP4
issue: - How can alerts be configured not to send notifications at weekends- How can alerts be configured to only send notifications at certain times of the day- How can alerts be configured not to send notications outside of work hours
resolution: In this example a user defined alert will be configured against the user workload prometheus instance. That alert will be configured to fire continuously. Once that is setup, configuration will be added to Alertmanager inorder to define a "weekend" First confirm that user workload monitoring is enabled ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-monitoring edit configmap cluster-monitoring-config apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: cluster-monitoring-config namespace: openshift-monitoring data: config.yaml: | enableUserWorkload: true ~~~ Next deploy a sample application, configured to create an alert that is always firing: ~~~ cat < < EOF | oc create-f- apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: ns1--- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: labels: app: prometheus-example-app name: prometheus-example-app namespace: ns1 spec: replicas: 1 selector: matchLabels: app: prometheus-example-app template: metadata: labels: app: prometheus-example-app spec: containers:- image: ghcr.io/rhobs/prometheus-example-app:0.4.1 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: prometheus-example-app--- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: labels: app: prometheus-example-app name: prometheus-example-app namespace: ns1 spec: ports:- port: 8080 protocol: TCP targetPort: 8080 name: web selector: app: prometheus-example-app type: ClusterIP--- apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: ServiceMonitor metadata: labels: k8s-app: prometheus-example-monitor name: prometheus-example-monitor namespace: ns1 spec: endpoints:- interval: 30s port: web scheme: http selector: matchLabels: app: prometheus-example-app--- apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: example-alert namespace: ns1 spec: groups:- name: example rules:- alert: VersionAlert for: 1m expr: version{job="prometheus-example-app"} > 0 labels: severity: warning EOF ~~~ Add configuration to Alertmanager Extract the Alertmanager secret: ~~~ oc-n openshift-monitoring get secret alertmanager-main--template='{{index.data "alertmanager.yaml"}}' | base64--decode ~~~ Edit the configuration: ~~~ "global": "resolve_timeout": "5m" time_intervals:- name: weekends time_intervals:- weekdays: [saturday, sunday] location: Europe/London "inhibit_rules":- "equal":- "namespace"- "alertname" "source_matchers":- "severity = critical" "target_matchers":- "severity =~ warning|info"- "equal":- "namespace"- "alertname" "source_matchers":- "severity = warning" "target_matchers":- "severity = info"- "equal":- "namespace" "source_matchers":- "alertname = InfoInhibitor" "target_matchers":- "severity = info" "receivers":- "name": "Default"- "name": "Watchdog"- "name": "Critical"- "name": "null"- "name": "ns1" webhook_configs:- url: "http://alertmanager-webhook-signal-webhook.apps.examplec.redhat.com/api/v3/alertmanager" send_resolved: true "route": "group_by":- "namespace" "group_interval": "5m" "group_wait": "30s" "receiver": "Default" "repeat_interval": "12h" "routes":- "matchers":- "alertname = Watchdog" "receiver": "Watchdog"- "matchers":- "alertname = InfoInhibitor" "receiver": "null"- "matchers":- "severity = critical" "receiver": "Critical"- "matchers":- "namespace = ns1" "receiver": "ns1" mute_time_intervals:- weekends ~~~ Write the configuration: ~~~ oc-n openshift-monitoring create secret generic alertmanager-main--from-file=alertmanager.yaml--dry-run=client-o=yaml | oc-n openshift-monitoring replace secret--filename=- ~~~

title: Prometheus crashing with err="TSDB not ready" in RHOCP4
issue: - Promethus pods are reporting 5 of 6 containers are ready- Errors seen in the logs for "TSDB not ready"
resolution: Check that supported (storage)[https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/storage/] is being used for Prometheus. Please note that following: ~~~ CAUTION: Non-POSIX compliant filesystems are not supported for Prometheus' local storage as unrecoverable corruptions may happen. NFS filesystems (including AWS's EFS) are not supported. NFS could be POSIX-compliant, but most implementations are not. It is strongly recommended to use a local filesystem for reliability. ~~~
root_cause: The error for "TSDB not ready" can be seen in the Prometheus (codebase)[https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/v0.54.1/tsdb/db.go#L65] along with an accompanying comment: ~~~ // ErrNotReady is returned if the underlying storage is not ready yet. var ErrNotReady = errors.New("TSDB not ready") ~~~

title: The authentication operator can't honor OAuth configuration due to an `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` error
issue: - The authentication operator fails to honor `OAuth` OpenID Connect configuration due to an `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` error.- The following error is streamed into the `openshift-authentication-operator` pod logs: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-authentication-operator logs $(oc-n openshift-authentication-operator get pods-l app=authentication-operator-o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name--no-headers) [...] E1125 15:31:27.093873 1 oauth.go:69] failed to honor IDP v1.IdentityProvider{Name:"sso", MappingMethod:"claim", IdentityProviderConfig:v1.IdentityProviderConfig{Type:"OpenID", BasicAuth:(*v1.BasicAuthIdentityProvider)(nil), GitHub:(*v1.GitHubIdentityProvider)(nil), GitLab:(*v1.GitLabIdentityProvider)(nil), Google:(*v1.GoogleIdentityProvider)(nil), HTPasswd:(*v1.HTPasswdIdentityProvider)(nil), Keystone:(*v1.KeystoneIdentityProvider)(nil), LDAP:(*v1.LDAPIdentityProvider)(nil), OpenID:(*v1.OpenIDIdentityProvider)(0xc010181ef0), RequestHeader:(*v1.RequestHeaderIdentityProvider)(nil)}}: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority I1125 15:31:28.369400 1 status_controller.go:165] clusteroperator/authentication diff {"status":{"conditions":[{"lastTransitionTime":"2019-11-20T10:17:18Z","message":"IdentityProviderConfigDegraded: failed to apply IDP sso config: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority","reason":"AsExpected","status":"False","type":"Degraded"},{"lastTransitionTime":"2019-11-22T11:41:09Z","reason":"AsExpected","status":"False","type":"Progressing"},{"lastTransitionTime":"2019-10-26T16:15:59Z","reason":"AsExpected","status":"True","type":"Available"},{"lastTransitionTime":"2019-10-26T13:30:53Z","reason":"AsExpected","status":"True","type":"Upgradeable"}]}} ~~~
resolution: - Define the Red Hat Single Sign-On Certificate Authority (CA) `ConfigMap` as noted in [this documentation reference](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.2/authentication/identity_providers/configuring-oidc-identity-provider.html#identity-provider-creating-configmap_configuring-oidc-identity-provider).- Reference the CA `ConfigMap` though the `.spec.identityProviders.openID.ca` [OpenID Connect identity provider resource definition](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.2/authentication/identity_providers/configuring-oidc-identity-provider.html#identity-provider-oidc-CR_configuring-oidc-identity-provider).- Ensure the CA matches the CA for the endpoint server- Use `openssl x509-in-noout-subject-issuer` to check the CA file- Use `echo | openssl s_client-connect-showcerts` to check the certificate presented by the server- Compare the Subject and Issuer for both `x509` and `s_client` output. They should match.--- **NOTE:** when Red Hat Single Sign-On instance is deployed on the OpenShift cluster itself, the ingress router Certificate Authority (CA) can be extracted with the following command: ` $ oc extract secrets/router-ca-n openshift-ingress-operator `
root_cause: - As part of the Red Hat Single Sign-On`IdentityProvider` configuration, the Certificate Authority (CA) bundle is to be included in the `OpenID Connect` provider configuration.

title: Messages about stale NFS file handle in Prometheus logs on OpenShift 4
issue: - There are "`stale NFS file handle`" messages in Prometheus logs: ~~~ write to WAL: log samples: write /prometheus/wal/00000011: stale NFS file handle ~~~- Message about filesystem not supported when Prometheus pod is starting: ~~~ This filesystem is not supported and may lead to data corruption and data loss. Please carefully read https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/storage/ to learn more about supported filesystems ~~~
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Prometheus does **not support** file systems that are **non-POSIX** compliant, and in general NFS implementations are non-POSIX compliant. As per the [upstream Prometheus documentation for the storage](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/storage/): > **CAUTION:** Non-POSIX compliant filesystems are not supported for Prometheus' local storage as unrecoverable corruptions may happen. NFS filesystems (including AWS's EFS) are not supported. NFS could be POSIX-compliant, but most implementations are not. It is strongly recommended to use a local filesystem for reliability. Refer to [is NFS supported for OpenShift cluster internal components in Production?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3428661) for additional information about NFS support for different OpenShift internal components. For the specific "`stale NFS file handle`" error messages, please refer to [what causes stale NFS file handle?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2674) for different possible reasons for the stale NFS file handle.

title: How to turn on CIFS debugging?
issue: - How can `CIFS` debugging be turned on?- How can the `CIFS` debug level be increased?- A `CIFS` mount requires more verbose log output to assist troubleshooting efforts.
resolution: ### For all versions of RHEL- Load the cifs kernel module if it hasn't been, already: ~~~ # modprobe cifs ~~~- Enable `CIFS` debugging with the following: (Replace 7 with a number 1-9 for log level, with 9 being most verbose.) ~~~ # echo 7 > /proc/fs/cifs/cifsFYI ~~~- **Enable this only if the support engineer has specifically asked for this**. It's possible to enable additional tracing, but this will add a lot of messages: ~~~ # echo 1 > /proc/fs/cifs/traceSMB ~~~ ### For RHEL < 7.3- Note: Syslog is used in RHEL 5 and older(/etc/syslog.conf). RHEL 6 and newer will utilize rsyslog(/etc/rsyslog.conf).- Ensure the system logging will collect `debug` level messages. These are higher than `info` level messages. The default entry for `rsyslog` in `/etc/rsyslog.conf` will not capture this additional information: ~~~ *.info;mail.none;authpriv.none;cron.none /var/log/messages ~~~- For `rsyslog` (`/etc/rsyslog.conf`) or `syslog` (`/etc/syslog.conf`) add "kern.*" or "*.debug" (the messages are typically `kern.debug`) to the existing logs for `/var/log/messages` or create a new log file. For example: ~~~ kern.*;*.info;mail.none;authpriv.none;cron.none /var/log/messages *.debug /var/log/cifs-log ~~~- Restart the `syslog` or `rsyslog` service after the configuration change: ~~~ # service rsyslog restart # service syslog restart OR # systemctl restart rsyslog.service ~~~- **After sufficient debug data is collected**, return the debug levels to normal, to prevent generating an excessive amount of logs: ~~~ # echo 0 > /proc/fs/cifs/cifsFYI # echo 0 > /proc/fs/cifs/traceSMB ~~~- You may also wish to remove the `rsyslog` or `syslog` entries previously added, and then restart the service after the configuration change (as done previously). ### For RHEL > = 7.4 (kernel version > = 3.10.0-693.5.2.el7) & RHEL 8 and above. **Note**: For enabling dynamic debugging, secure boot must be disabled first. There was a change in kernel how CIFS debug work. If the server is using a RHEL 7.3 kernel older than `3.10.0-514.35.1.el7` or a RHEL 7.4 kernel older than `kernel-3.10.0-693.5.2.el7`, then the kernel needs to be upgraded as per [this document](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5446081). From the kernel version 3.10.0-693.5.2.el7 or newer, an extra step is required to enable the debug logs:- Enable dynamic debugging for the cifs module: ~~~ # echo "module cifs +p" > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control ~~~- When debugging is complete, disable the debug log, in addition to the `cifsFYI` file, disable also the dynamic logging: ~~~ # echo "module cifs-p" > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control ~~~

title: openstack-baremetal-operator-controller crashed with SIGSEGV when BMH uses PreprovisioningNetworkDataName.
issue: - openstack-baremetal-operator-controller crashed with SIGSEGV when BMH uses `PreprovisioningNetworkDataName`.
resolution: A workaround for this issue is to use cloud-init format networkData in `spec.nodes..networkData` and use `fixedIP` for ctlplane network of nodes in `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` CR. For example: ~~~ spec: nodes:: networkData: name: namespace: networks:- name: ctlplane subnetName: subnet1 fixedIP: ~~~ **NOTE** `PreprovisioningNetworkDataName` is provided in nmstate format, cloud-init which runs on RHEL9.4 OS for EDPM nodes doesn't understand nmstate format. 1. Create a new secret which contains the cloud-init based config normally like [upstream git](https://github.com/openstack-k8s-operators/openstack-baremetal-operator/blob/main/templates/openstackbaremetalset/cloudinit/networkdata). ~~~ kind: Secret apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: openstack-compute-up-cloudinit-networkdata-osp-compute namespace: openstack type: Opaque stringData: networkData:| links:- name: enp1s0 id: enp1s0 type: vif networks:- link: enp1s0 id: enp1s0 type: ipv4 ip_address: 192.168.122.100 netmask: "255.255.255.0" routes:- network: 0.0.0.0 netmask: 0.0.0.0 gateway: 192.168.122.1 services:- type: dns-nameserver address: 192.168.122.80 search: ctlplane.example.com ~~~ 2. Assign the networkData with the name of the secret and namespace. Also use the same `fixedIP` for ctlplane network. ~~~ spec: nodes:: networkData: name: openstack-compute-up-cloudinit-networkdata-osp-compute namespace: openstack networks:- name: ctlplane subnetName: subnet1 fixedIP: 192.168.122.100 ~~~- This issue is being addressed at [OSPRH-10411](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSPRH-10411)
root_cause: - Bug in code that dereferences a nil pointer when setting `networkData` in `OpenStackBaremetalSet` status.

issue: - During the cutover phase of a storage class conversion with MTC, all application workloads (such as `Deployments`, `Stateful Sets`, etc.) are scaled down for the target namespace, even if they are not linked to the `PersistentVolumeClaims` being migrated.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [MIG-1661](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MIG-1661). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: How to debug DevWorkspace going down due to inactivity while there is activity?

This is causing loss of ongoing work done by the developers on the workspace.
resolution: 1. Start a Devspace (or use an existing one) Note: Assuming the Namespace `admin-devspaces` from here $ oc get route-n admin-devspaces NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD devspaces devspaces.apps.ocp4.example.com / che-gateway 8080 edge/Redirect None 2. Verify the environment variable `SECONDS_OF_DW_INACTIVITY_BEFORE_IDLING` inside the shell of the pod sh-4.4$ env | grep SECONDS_OF_DW_INACTIVITY_BEFORE_IDLING SECONDS_OF_DW_INACTIVITY_BEFORE_IDLING=600 4. Check that this setting is consistent with the settings in the `checluster` $ oc get checluster devspaces-o yaml | grep secondsOfInactivityBeforeIdling secondsOfInactivityBeforeIdling: 600 5. Log into the DevWorkspace pod $ oc get pods-n admin-devspaces NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE workspacexxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxc-xxxx 2/2 Running 0 4m44s $ oc-n admin-devspaces-c tools rsh workspacexxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxc-xxxx 7. [GIN-debug] POST /activity/tick--> main.main.func6 (3 handlers)... [GIN] 2024/08/27- 06:58:58 | 204 | 4.98µs | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/activity/tick" [GIN] 2024/08/27- 06:59:58 | 204 | 3.134µs | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/activity/tick" [GIN] 2024/08/27- 07:00:58 | 204 | 4.377µs | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/activity/tick" 9. title: RHOCP: Unable to apply 4.xx.xx: a required extension is not available to update
issue: Cluster extension is missing and updates are blocked

Possible error messages:- Cluster version operator reports: ~~~ Unable to apply 4.xx.xx: a required extension is not available to update ~~~- The logs in `apiserver` pods shows: ~~~ failed to get resource type: no matches for kind "Build" in version "config.openshift.io/v1" ~~~
resolution: * To fix the issue, restart the cluster version operator pod. To so, run the following command: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-cluster-version delete pod-l k8s-app=cluster-version-operator ~~~ * After executing this command, allow 15 minutes for the operators to reconcile. During that time, it is possible to monitor the activity through the logs of: 1. the `apiserver` pods (present inside the Namespace `openshift-apiserver`). 2. the new `cluster-version-operator` pod (in the Namespace `openshift-cluster-version`). If the issue persists, please [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
