title: RHOCP: conditional overwrite of file using Machine Configuration for specific nodes
issue: How to overwrite a file provided by `MachineConfig` only for some specific nodes.
resolution: To achieve a conditional node configuration in OpenShift: 1. Create a `MachineConfig` (mc) with a specific role label (edge-worker in our example). ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: edge-worker name: 99-worker-test spec: config: ignition: version: 2.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:,test-99 filesystem: root mode: 0644 path: /etc/testmcp ~~~ 2. Create a new `MachineConfigPool` (mcp) that match both the existing `MachineConfig` worker role configuration and a new one. To do that, match 2 roles(label) in the "machineConfigSelector" section of the Manifest, also this new `MachineConfigPool` must only apply to the new node role types, so configure the "nodeSelector" section accordingly. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfigPool metadata: labels: pools.operator.machineconfiguration.openshift.io/edge-worker: '' name: edge-worker spec: machineConfigSelector: matchExpressions:- key: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role operator: In values:- worker- edge-worker nodeSelector: matchLabels: worker-type: edge paused: false ~~~ 4. Verify that the new `MachineConfigPool` is getting both files from worker and edge-worker (check the spec/configuration list of files) ~~~ $ oc describe mcp/edge-worker ~~~ 5. if everything looks correct, add the label to the desired node, this will apply the new configuration. ~~~ $ oc label node/my-remote-edge-worker worker-type=edge ~~~
root_cause: * `MachineConfiguration` provide files precedence, the `MachineConfigs` are read in order from 00* to 99*. In a case of a same file in multiple `MachineConfig` Manifest, the last one(99*) wins. Concretely, the content of the file that appears in a 99* `MachineConfig` Manifest will replace the same file that appeared in a 51* `MachineConfig` Manifest for example.

title: RHOCP: List and enable console plugin via CLI
issue: How to list and enable console plugins from OpenShift operators without overwriting the existing configuration of plugins using CLI?
resolution: * To list available `consoleplugin`, run the following command: ``` $ oc get consoleplugin NAME AGE forklift-console-plugin 26h gitops-plugin 26h kubevirt-plugin 26h monitoring-plugin 26h odf-console 26h pipelines-console-plugin 64m ``` * To list active `consoleplugin` run: ``` $ oc get console.operator-ojsonpath='{.items[].spec.plugins}' | jq ["monitoring-plugin", "kubevirt-plugin", "monitoring-plugin", "odf-console"] ``` * It is also possible to list active console plugins using the web console via: `Administration`-> `Cluster Settings`-> `Configuration`-> `Console`-> `Console plugins`. * To enable a plugin via CLI (e.g. the `pipelines-console-plugin`), use the following: ``` $ oc patch console.operator cluster--type='json'-p='[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/plugins/-", "value": "pipelines-console-plugin"}]' console.operator.openshift.io/cluster patched $ oc get console.operator-ojsonpath='{.items[].spec.plugins}' | jq ["monitoring-plugin", "kubevirt-plugin", "monitoring-plugin", "odf-console", "pipelines-console-plugin"] ``` After enabling the console plugin 1. wait for the `Web console update is available` window to appear at the top right of the OpenShift Web Console [image=[src="images/webconsole_update.png", alt="webconsole message", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%"]] 2. click on "Refresh web console" link on this window.

issue: - `ovnkube-master` POD stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` after upgrading cluster to 4.13.- `ovnkube-master` POD restarting continuously with below panic: ~~~ panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [recovered] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x8 pc=0x1a80fa5] goroutine 102 [running]: k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.HandleCrash({0x0, 0x0, 0x30?}) /go/src/github.com/openshift/ovn-kubernetes/go-controller/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:56 +0xd7 panic({0x1ceffe0, 0x32652a0}) /usr/lib/golang/src/runtime/panic.go:884 +0x212 github.com/ovn-org/ovn-kubernetes/go-controller/pkg/ovn.(*DefaultNetworkController).syncNetworkPolicies(0xc000c33680, {0xc001a26ce0, 0x2, 0x42a927?}) /go/src/github.com/openshift/ovn-kubernetes/go-controller/pkg/ovn/policy.go:351 +0xd65 ~~~- ovnkube-master PODs are going into `CrashLoopBackOff` due to presence of ACL with priority 1013 and without a name. ~~~ $ oc rsh-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-c northd $(oc get po-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-owide | grep ovnkube-master| grep $(oc get lease-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ovn-kubernetes-master-o template--template={{.spec.holderIdentity}})| awk '{print $1}') ovn-nbctl--no-leader list acl |grep-A 2-B 10 1013_uuid: 14934bbb-0d23-4963-96ce-338be3c203f8 action: allow direction: from-lport external_ids: {default-deny-policy-type=Egress} label: 0 log: false match: "inport == @clusterRtrPortGroup && (ip4.mcast || mldv1 || mldv2 || (ip6.dst[120..127] == 0xff && ip6.dst[116] == 1))" meter: [] name: [] options: {apply-after-lb="true"} priority: 1013 severity: [] tier: 0--_uuid: 3d73790e-690c-4332-9c54-d729f23ec3a9 action: allow direction: to-lport external_ids: {} label: 0 log: false match: "outport == @clusterRtrPortGroup && (ip4.mcast || mldv1 || mldv2 || (ip6.dst[120..127] == 0xff && ip6.dst[116] == 1))" meter: [] name: [] options: {} priority: 1013 severity: [] tier: 0 ~~~
resolution: **Workaround:**- Delete `ACL` with with priority `1013`. ~~~ $ oc rsh-c northd-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes $(oc get po-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-owide | grep ovnkube-master| grep $(oc get lease-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ovn-kubernetes-master-o template--template={{.spec.holderIdentity}})| awk '{print $1}') ovn-nbctl--no-leader acl-del clusterRtrPortGroup to-lport 1013 "outport == @clusterRtrPortGroup && (ip4.mcast || mldv1 || mldv2 || (ip6.dst[120..127] == 0xff && ip6.dst[116] == 1))" $ oc rsh-c northd-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes $(oc get po-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-owide | grep ovnkube-master| grep $(oc get lease-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ovn-kubernetes-master-o template--template={{.spec.holderIdentity}})| awk '{print $1}') ovn-nbctl--no-leader acl-del clusterRtrPortGroup from-lport 1013 "inport == @clusterRtrPortGroup && (ip4.mcast || mldv1 || mldv2 || (ip6.dst[120..127] == 0xff && ip6.dst[116] == 1))" ~~~- Restart `ovnkube-master` leader POD.- Make sure there are no ACL with `1013` priority in Northbound database: ~~~ $ oc rsh-c northd-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes $(oc get po-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-owide | grep ovnkube-master| grep $(oc get lease-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ovn-kubernetes-master-o template--template={{.spec.holderIdentity}})| awk '{print $1}') ovn-nbctl--no-leader acl-list clusterRtrPortGroup ~~~
root_cause: - ACL with `1013` priority used to be created in Openshift version till `4.9` to implement `allow multicast policies`. Later the priority was changed to `1012` but previously created ACLs were not removed. Those stale ACLs are causing the panic in Openshift version 4.13. This issue is being tracked in [OCPBUGS-21668](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-21668)

title: Disabling the VNC Console in the Overview Tab
issue: - In the `Virtualization-> Virtual Machines-> Overview` section, the **VNC console*
cannot be disabled. This can lead to accidental mouse movements or unintended command inputs being sent to the VM console.
resolution: - In the `Virtual Machines Overview Tab`, the **VNC console** is designed as an active element.- Currently, there are limitations for non-admin users who have view-only permissions.- However, there is no existing implementation that allows admin users to disable the VNC console in the current version.- A request has been opened to address this limitation in the future, which can be tracked at the [RFE "Disable or make read-only the VNC console in Overview in Virtualization"](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-49440)

Currently, it has a limitation for non-admin users who have been assigned view-only permission, as outlined in the [implementation](https://github.com/kubevirt-ui/kubevirt-plugin/pull/959) const isVMRunning = vmi?.status?.phase === vmiStatuses.Running; const [canConnectConsole] = useAccessReview({resource: 'virtualmachineinstances/vnc', group: 'subresources.kubevirt.io', namespace: vmi?.metadata?.namespace, name: vmi?.metadata?.name, verb: 'get',});

title: Volumesnapshot created by OADP getting deleted by OpenShift GitOps during backup process
issue: OpenShift GitOps/`ArgoCD` may reconcile/prune `VolumeSnapshot` resources during the backup procedure, causing the backup to fail. This is related to the fact that `PersistentVolumes`, managed by `ArgoCD` have a label applied to identify them as being managed by `ArgoCD`. This label is inherited by `VolumeSnapshot` for restore purpose but is causing `ArgoCD` to prune it during the backup procedure because it's not expected to be there. That way, backups are not working respectively failing unexpected.

OADP backup failing because of snapshot creation is failing respectively the snapshot created has gone missing and reporting the below error. [...] sourceNamespace: namespace-1 sourcePVC: pvc-source-1 status: completionTimestamp: '2024-05-23T11:59:28Z' message: >- error to expose snapshot: error wait volume snapshot ready: error to get volumesnapshot namespace-1/velero-pvc-source-1-x4294: volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io "velero-pvc-source-1-x4294" not found [...]
resolution: **Disclaimer**:_Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ Red Hat is aware about this condition and is looking to improve troubleshooting and detection of the conditon via [OADP-4736](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OADP-4736). To raise questions or obtain further information, contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport). ### Workaround Applying [`.spec.resourceTrackingMethod`](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user-guide/resource_tracking/#choosing-a-tracking-method) set to `annotation+label` in the offending `ArgoCD` custom resource as shown below, will work-around the issue, respectively prevent the removal of the `VolumeSnapshot` by `ArgoCD` and therefore OpenShift GitOps. apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1beta1 kind: ArgoCD metadata: name: example-argocd labels: example: repo spec: resourceTrackingMethod: annotation+label repo: replicas: 1 server: replicas: 1 route: enabled: true path: / tls: insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect termination: passthrough wildcardPolicy: None
root_cause: * OADP is cloning `label` data associated with `PersistentVolumeClaims` and `PersistentVolumes` into the `VolumeSnapshot` created when running a backup with [Data Mover](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/installing/about-oadp-1-3-data-mover.html) enabled to have required `metadata` available in case a [restore](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/backing_up_and_restoring/restoring-applications.html#oadp-creating-restore-cr_restoring-applications) based on `labels` is requested. * When managing `PersistentVolumeClaims` or `PersistentVolumes` using OpenShift GitOps, associated labels are being applied so OpenShift GitOps can track the resources and [prune](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/auto_sync/#automatic-pruning) not defined resource in case `prune: true` is set in the `ArgoCD` custom resource. * The above situation will create a conflict, because OADP will clone the OpenShift GitOps `label` to the `VolumeSnapshot` resouce. This resource though is not defined in the OpenShift GitOps source, causing OpenShift GitOps to prune the `VolumeSnapshot` when [`prune: true`](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/auto_sync/#automatic-pruning) is set in the `ArgoCD` custom resource. This in turn will cause the backup job started by OADP to fail, as the required `VolumeSnapshot` went missing, but would be required to take the necessary backup for the requested `PersistentVolumes`.

title: Red Hat Quay Security scanner not working with error "disallowed by policy"
issue: Red Hat Quay Security scanner cannot scan images and report vulnerability scores in disconnected environments.
Clair logs showing errors containing: ~~~ dial tcp:: address tcp4!: ","message":"error during scan" ~~~
resolution: * Remove or set the `airgap` configuration form the clair config bundle to false ~~~ indexer: airgap: false ~~~ * **Note** only RFC1918 (IPv4) and RFC4193 (IPv6) IP blocks are considered private * 10/8 * 172.16/12 * 192.168/16 * fc00::/7
root_cause: * Golang's module function `net.ParseIP().IsLocal()` only recognizes RFC1918 and RFC4193 addresses as private * does not recognize RFC3330 IP blocks as private IP addresses

title: Migrating from one namespace to another
issue: You must make sure that all of your existing deployments of AAP services (controller, hub, EDA) are deployed to the same, single namespace before upgrading to Ansible Automation Platform Operator on OpenShift Container Platform version 2.5.
resolution: To migrate your services from one namespace to another, perform the following steps: 1. Create a separate namespace on the Openshift cluster using the Openshift Console UI: a. Log in to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. b. Navigate to **Administration** → **Namespaces**. [image=[src="images/rhocp-ui-namespaces.png", title="The Namespaces window of the Red Hat OpenShift console page with Create Namespace button emphasized.", alt="The Namespaces window of the Red Hat OpenShift console page with Create Namespace button emphasized.", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="Namespaces window of the Red Hat OpenShift console",]] c. Click **Create Namespace**. The namespace is named `aap` by default when you installed the AAP Operator from OperatorHub, so provide a unique name to avoid conflict, if needed. 2. Recreate the `secret_key/db_encryption_fields_secret` and `postgres_configuration_secret` k8s secrets in the new namespace for all the components being migrated (AutomationController, AutomationHub, EDA, AnsibleAutomationPlatform). See [Creating a secret key secret](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ansible_automation_platform/2.4/html-single/deploying_the_red_hat_ansible_automation_platform_operator_on_openshift_container_platform/index#create-secret-key-secret_aap-migration) for more detail. 3. Create a new AnsibleAutomationPlatform custom resource in the new central namespace, specifying the secret key and `old_postgres_configuration_secret` secret for each component on the spec in the `controller`, `hub`, and `eda` sections. See [Create AnsibleAutomationPlatform custom resource](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ansible_automation_platform/2.5/html-single/installing_on_openshift_container_platform/index#con-operator-custom-resources_operator-install-planning) for more detail. 4. After creating the AnsibleAutomationPlatform custom resource, the operator will automatically create new AutomationController and AutomationHub custom resources, which will migrate the database from the old deployment in the previous namespace and use the secret key specified. **Note** The old deployment in the previous namespace should be kept running until the new deployment is complete.

title: Scaling nodepool fails to add worker nodes to the hosted cluster
issue: - Re-installing the worker nodes stuck because the nodes are unable to start when scaling up `nodepool`.
resolution: - This is a current behavior of assisted service. Even for disconnected cluster, the pull secret must contain auth of `registry.redhat.io`.- There are two solutions available to resolve this issue, as shown below: 1. Add credentials for `registry.redhat.io` to the pull secret in addition to credentials for internal mirror registry. 2. Add the `registry.redhat.io` to list of registries to ignore authentication.- Edit `AgentServiceConfig` CR and append the following spec field to it: ~~~ apiVersion: agent-install.openshift.io/v1beta1 kind: AgentServiceConfig metadata: name: agent spec: unauthenticatedRegistries:- registry.redhat.io ~~~ Note: Red Hat is aware that the documentation needs to be amended with this pull-secret requirement for assisted service. We are tracking this via a documentation [Jira](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSDOCS-12373). **Note: Adding `registry.redhat.io` pull secret in option 1 may cause insight operator to be in degraded state.**
root_cause: Even for the disconnected cluster, the pull secret must contain auth for `registry.redhat.io`. It is required since assisted service cannot determine if the local or `registry.redhat.io` registry will be used while validating the pull secret.

title: OADP scheduled backups doesn't sync on cluster if owner reference does not exist [RHOCP4]
issue: - Scheduled backups are not syncing or reconciling on another cluster.
resolution: You can workaround this issue by setting `useOwnerReferencesInBackup: false` in your `Schedule` to avoid the owner reference from the `schedule` on the `backup`. Find below an example: ~~~ $ oc edit schedule-n openshift_adp apiVersion: velero.io/v1 kind: Schedule metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/instance: openshift-adp name: example-schedule namespace: openshift-adp spec: schedule: 0 22 * * * skipImmediately: false useOwnerReferencesInBackup: false template: defaultVolumesToFsBackup: false storageLocation: default hooks: {} ttl: 720h0m0s ~~~
root_cause: If a backup was created on the source cluster using a `Schedule` with the parameter `.spec.useOwnerReferencesInBackup: true`, Velero expects the same `Schedule` to exist on the target (or secondary) cluster. If that `Schedule` is missing on the target cluster, Velero will skip syncing that backup on the secondary cluster.

title: 3scale 2.11 operator deployed in OCP 4.12 is in CrashLoopBackOff status and "PodDisruptionBudget" API missing message (workaround)
issue: After upgrading our Openshift cluster to version 4.12, we are trying to upgrade our 3scale instance from version 2.11 to version 2.13, but it still remains at the old version. There is an error in the `threescale-operator-controller-manager` pod of the 3scale Operator: ~~~ {"level":"error","ts":1691134791.155926,"logger":"setup","msg":"problem running manager","error":"no matches for kind \"PodDisruptionBudget\" in version \"policy/v1beta1\"","stacktrace":"github.com/go-logr/zapr.(*zapLogger).Errornt/remote-source/deps/gomod/pkg/mod/github.com/go-logr/zapr@v0.1.1/zapr.go:128nmain.mainnt/remote-source/app/main.go:318nruntime.mainnt/opt/rh/go-toolset-1.13/root/usr/lib/go-toolset-1.13-golang/src/runtime/proc.go:203"} ~~~
resolution: A permanent solution to this bug is being worked on in Jira [THREESCALE-10010](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-10010). This is a workaround that must be followed only when the solution described in [this article](https://access.redhat.com/node/7028293) can not be followed. If this workaround does not work in your environment, the next step would be to restore the backup on a fresh install of 3scale on an OpenShift 4.10 and follow the normal upgrade path. This workaround make the 3scale Operator 2.13 to install 3scale 2.12 in OpenShift 4.12. It is **VERY** important to complete the upgrade to version 2.13, because version 2.12 is not supported by Red Hat in OpenShift 4.12. To do this, first need to edit the APIManager YAML to specify the version 2.12 container images to use, remove the installed 3scale Operator version 2.11, install 3scale Operator version 2.13 (it will upgrade using the referenced 2.12 images), and after upgrading, remove references to the container images (this will make the operator to use the default values) to allow the operator to upgrade to version 2.13. There's two very important points to take care on this workaround: 1. **Never** remove the APIManager CRD. The APIManager is what keeps the 3scale workload installed. If you remove the APImanager CRD, all 3scale will be removed. 2. Do **NOT** uninstall the 3scale Operator 2.13 before editing the APIManager CRD and add the container images references. **WARNING**: It is **strongly** recommended to open a [Proactive case](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5387111) before trying this workaround. **WARNING**: If a problem occurs during the upgrade, it may corrupt the installation and this will cause product downtime while the upgrade is done using the traditional method on an OpenShift 4.10. This article has two methods: 1. Using the [CLI](#cli) (Command Line Interface) 2. Using the [OpenShift Web UI](#webui) ## Using the Command Line Interface {#cli} The commands assume that the current namespace is the 3scale installation that needs to be fixed. These are the steps to do this operation: 1. Make a complete backup of the 2.11 installation following the [2.11 Backing up system databases](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore#backup-procedures) documentation; 2. Edit the APIManager CRD to add 3scale 2.12 image references: $ oc edit apimanager The following parameters need to be merged into the APIManager CRD: spec: apicast: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/apicast-gateway-rhel8@sha256:dec57677b53180ef5b89338cb1d43fc727299cbef781c95da87e0cf10092395d backend: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/backend-rhel8@sha256:8697cedba82c700efed14a3ec1fa2aa9e990da9fb75857278e3f036844c0f005 redisImage: registry.redhat.io/rhscl/redis-5-rhel7@sha256:52ffb5bf944593c290c2de52db5117044e58633385dcbe70679ea69ff0c5ff01 system: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/system-rhel7@sha256:e55e769a21030b3aa268a714138dd7fdb2ab348515c917f72362431bc46d2cf5 redisImage: registry.redhat.io/rhscl/redis-5-rhel7@sha256:52ffb5bf944593c290c2de52db5117044e58633385dcbe70679ea69ff0c5ff01 memcachedImage: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/memcached-rhel7@sha256:08264cf3271b477562fa13b5e0190bf634c49d581e1cef59f5119c0bc88657f4 database: mysql: image: registry.redhat.io/rhel8/mysql-80@sha256:e2c4296aa3854c474a1cf1131f2f43cd19a1340bef510c180261a175bd58d58d zync: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/zync-rhel8@sha256:390cf1a4991bb5c62f18a0cf053d4e9a943d993c5f8ceddf1a1cf8d5bb34abc1 postgreSQLImage: registry.redhat.io/rhscl/postgresql-10-rhel7@sha256:74a95fba3fb7edd8f6e439d5488bc954e6bae7b66ce82be3e33b3195ac42a58e **NOTE**: The operator will not apply the modifications because the `threescale-operator-controller-manager` pod is in `CrashLoopBackOff` status and will be applied immediately when we reinstall the operator later. 3. Remove the installed operator: $ oc delete subscription $(oc get subscriptions-l operators.coreos.com/3scale-operator.3scale-o template--template '{{range.items}}{{.metadata.name}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}') subscription.operators.coreos.com "3scale-operator" deleted $ oc delete clusterserviceversions $(oc get clusterserviceversions-l operators.coreos.com/3scale-operator.3scale-o template--template '{{range.items}}{{.metadata.name}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}') clusterserviceversion.operators.coreos.com "3scale-operator.v0.8.4-0.1655690146.p" deleted 4. Reinstall the 3scale Operator version 2.13: $ (echo "apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1" echo "kind: Subscription" echo "metadata:" echo " name: 3scale" echo " namespace: 3scale" echo "spec:" echo " channel: threescale-2.13" echo " name: 3scale-operator" echo " source: redhat-operators" echo " sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace") | oc apply-f- subscription.operators.coreos.com/3scale created **NOTE**: This subscription installs the Operator into the `3scale` namespace. Change the `metadata_ →_namespace` if necessary. At this time, the 3scale Operator will start upgrading 3scale to version 2.12. 5. Wait for the upgrade process, test the 3scale instance and if everything is fine make a new complete backup of the 2.12 following the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates#backup-procedures). At this point the operator will show version 2.13, but the installed version will be 2.12. Check the correct version in the 3scale Administration Interface footer. 6. Edit the APIManager CRD again, using the same process used in step 2, and remove all `image`, `redisImage`, `memcachedImage` and `postgreSQLImage` entries added earlier. After saving the changes, the 3scale Operator will start upgrading 3scale to version 2.13. 7. Wait for the upgrade process, test the 3scale instance and if everything is fine make a new complete backup of the 2.13 following the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore#backup-procedures). After these steps, 3scale 2.13 will be running on OpenShift 4.12. To check, see the version at the 3scale Administration Interface footer. ## Using the OpenShift Web UI {#webui} These are the steps to do this operation: 1. Make a complete backup of the 2.11 installation following the [2.11 Backing up system databases](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore#backup-procedures) documentation; 2. Edit the APIManager CRD to add 3scale 2.12 image references. From the `Administrator` perspective, navigate to `Operators > Installed Operators > Red Hat Integration- 3scale > APIManager` and select the `Edit APIManager` option from the three dots to the right of the operator row. [image=[src="images/step2_3.png", alt="Editing APIManager", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] Parameters need to be added to the APIManager CRD, and below is the structure with x64_64 (AMD64) architecture image references for 3scale version 2.12. If the system uses another architecture (such as PPC64le or S390X), change the image references to the correct one. Use the [Red Hat Ecosystem Catalog](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/3scale-amp2/apicast-gateway-rhel8/5df398c85a13466876712703?container-tabs=gti&architecture=amd64&tag=1.21.2-3&push_date=1678365542000) to find references. The following parameters need to be merged into the APIManager CRD: spec: apicast: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/apicast-gateway-rhel8@sha256:dec57677b53180ef5b89338cb1d43fc727299cbef781c95da87e0cf10092395d backend: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/backend-rhel8@sha256:8697cedba82c700efed14a3ec1fa2aa9e990da9fb75857278e3f036844c0f005 redisImage: registry.redhat.io/rhscl/redis-5-rhel7@sha256:52ffb5bf944593c290c2de52db5117044e58633385dcbe70679ea69ff0c5ff01 system: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/system-rhel7@sha256:e55e769a21030b3aa268a714138dd7fdb2ab348515c917f72362431bc46d2cf5 redisImage: registry.redhat.io/rhscl/redis-5-rhel7@sha256:52ffb5bf944593c290c2de52db5117044e58633385dcbe70679ea69ff0c5ff01 memcachedImage: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/memcached-rhel7@sha256:08264cf3271b477562fa13b5e0190bf634c49d581e1cef59f5119c0bc88657f4 database: mysql: image: registry.redhat.io/rhel8/mysql-80@sha256:e2c4296aa3854c474a1cf1131f2f43cd19a1340bef510c180261a175bd58d58d zync: image: registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/zync-rhel8@sha256:390cf1a4991bb5c62f18a0cf053d4e9a943d993c5f8ceddf1a1cf8d5bb34abc1 postgreSQLImage: registry.redhat.io/rhscl/postgresql-10-rhel7@sha256:74a95fba3fb7edd8f6e439d5488bc954e6bae7b66ce82be3e33b3195ac42a58e **NOTE**: The operator will not apply the modifications because the `threescale-operator-controller-manager` pod is in `CrashLoopBackOff` status and will be applied immediately when we reinstall the operator later. 3. Remove the installed operator. From the `Administrator` perspective, navigate to `Operators > Installed Operators` and select `Uninstall Operator` option from the three dots to the right of the `Red Hat Integration- 3scale` operator row. [image=[src="images/step3_4.png", alt="Confirm the uninstall of 3scale Operator", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] Confirm removal by clicking `Uninstall`. [image=[src="images/step3-2.png", alt="Confirm the uninstall of 3scale Operator", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] **NOTE**: If the 3scale Operator was removed before editing the APIManager CRD, it will only be possible to edit in the CLI. Also, never install 3scale Operator version 2.13 before editing the APIManager CRD first, otherwise the operator will try to upgrade 3scale to version 2.13, skipping version 2.12! 4. Reinstall the 3scale Operator version 2.13. From the `Administrator` perspective, navigating to `Operators > OperatorHub`, search for `3scale` and select `Red Hat Integration- 3scale`. [image=[src="images/step4_2.png", alt="Searching for 3scale Operator", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] Click the "_Install_" button. [image=[src="images/step4-2.png", alt="Confirm the operator install", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] Make sure the `Update channel` is `threescale-2.13`, under `Installation mode` select `A specific namespace on the cluster`, select the namespace under `Installed Namespace` and click the `Install` button. [image=[src="images/step4-3.png", alt="Configuring 3scale Operator install", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] After the installation is complete, this message will be displayed: [image=[src="images/step4-4.png", alt="3scale Operator ready", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", lightbox="true"]] At this time, the 3scale Operator will start upgrading 3scale to version 2.12. 5. Wait for the upgrade process, test the 3scale instance and if everything is fine make a new complete backup of the 2.12 following the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore-using-templates#backup-procedures). At this point the operator will show version 2.13, but the installed version will be 2.12. Check the correct version in the 3scale Administration Interface footer. 6. Edit the APIManager CRD again, using the same process used in step 2, and remove all `image`, `redisImage`, `memcachedImage` and `postgreSQLImage` entries added earlier. After saving the changes, the 3scale Operator will start upgrading 3scale to version 2.13. 7. Wait for the upgrade process, test the 3scale instance and if everything is fine make a new complete backup of the 2.13 following the [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.13/html/operating_3scale/threescale-backup-restore#backup-procedures). After these steps, 3scale 2.13 will be running on OpenShift 4.12. To check, see the version at the 3scale Administration Interface footer.
root_cause: Only 3scale version 2.13 is compatible with OCP 4.12 due to the deprecated `PodDisruptionBudget` API. The `PodDisruptionBudget.v1beta1.policy` API is required by 3scale Operator version 2.11 and 2.12. Due to this limitation and the fact that 3scale cannot skip any version while upgrading, it is impossible to recover from this status and upgrade to version 2.13 using the traditional upgrade instructions. Check the 3scale Supported Configurations for reference:- [3scale 2.11 supported configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6961867)- [3scale 2.12 supported configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6982425)- [3scale 2.13 supported configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2798521) Check [Preparing to upgrade to OpenShift Container Platform 4.12](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6955381) for further information about the deprecated APIs.

title: Configuring a custom domain for applications in OpenShift 4
issue: - Support a custom domain with an additional certificate in OpenShift 4.- Can be the default domain for the applications be modified post installation?- Automatically create new routes with a custom domain, not with default.
resolution: Starting with OpenShift 4.7, it is possible to [configure an alternative cluster domain using the `appsDomain` option of the Ingress](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/networking/ingress-operator.html#nw-ingress-configuring-application-domain_configuring-ingress). ####Additional related information [Is it possible to update the Openshift Ingress domain?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5749041) [How to change the domain name of OpenShift 4 cluster post installation?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4853401) [Configure the custom ingress certificate with FQDNs in subjectAltName instead of wild-card subdomain](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5532581) [Configure Internal/External Ingress Controller sharding on an existing OpenShift 4 cluster](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4981211)

title: Throttling request took messages reported when running oc commands on OCP 4
issue: `Throttling request took...` messages are seen when running `oc get-A pod` in some of our large OpenShift 4- Cluster: ~~~ I0101 00:00:01.832226 3137411 request.go:621] Throttling request took 1.236534125s, request: GET:https://api.my-cluster.example.com:6443/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1?timeout=32s ~~~
resolution: This issue was tracked in [BZ 1906332](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1906332), and fixed in OCP 4.6.16 via [errata RHSA-2021:0308](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2021:0308). Please upgrade to OCP 4.6.16 or later (including the `oc` client) to prevent this issue from happening.
root_cause: The `oc` client caches a list of resources from the API server, which matches more or less the list of Custom Resource Definitions available from the API server. It is possible to inspect this cache in `${HOME}/.kube/cache/discovery/${API_END_POINT}`. Entries in this cache directory are refreshed when they're 10 minutes old. To build this cache, `oc` queries each apigroup end point to get a list of Resources Definitions for that apigroup. When the cluster has a large number of operators installed, this implies a large number of endpoints to query, and such a large number of request to the API server that the client will throttle itself when doing API discovery, to avoid overloading the API server.

title: Are there any Red Hat Fuse 7 images that we could use with podman ?

title: Too far behind messages when log forwarding to Loki in RHOCP 4
issue: Rejected messages in the collector when log forwarding to Loki with the error `entry too far behind`: ``` openshift-logging/logging-loki-ingester-1[loki-ingester]: level=warn ts=2023-10-04T09:17:18.665393472Z caller=grpc_logging.go:43 method=/logproto.Pusher/Push duration=2.273379ms err="rpc error: code = Code(400) desc = entry with timestamp 2023-10-04 07:36:24.87037 +0000 UTC ignored, reason: 'entry too far behind, oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2023-10-04T08:17:16Z' for stream: {fluentd_thread=\"flush_thread_1\", kubernetes_host=\"woker-1.example.com\", log_type=\"audit\"},\nuser 'audit', total ignored: 1 out of 122" msg=gRPC ```
resolution: In the **Root Cause** section is listed several possible root causes and depending on it, the action for solving the problem will be different. In case that the possible **Root Cause** is not one of the listed, then, it could be needed to review how the log line being rejected is, by default, the log line being rejected with the error `too far behind` is not visible in the collector logs. For being able to see it:- For fluentd, [change the `LOG LEVEL`](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4661421) to debug- For Vector, it's possible to use `vector tap--inputs-of `, where ` ` is the ID of the sink observed with the command `vector top` needed to run inside a `vector` pod
root_cause: The error `Too far behind` happens when the timestamp of the log send to Loki has a difference of time bigger that the stablished in the variable `max_chunk_age`. In older version of the Red Hat OpenShift LokiStack was set the `max_chunk_age` to 1 hour. In the latest versions, it's of 2 hours as visible in the Loki configuration: ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging get cm logging-loki-config-o json|jq-r '.data."config.yaml"' |grep max_chunk_age max_chunk_age: 2h ``` ##### Why does it exist a delay bigger than the `max_chunk_age` time? This problem could be caused for different reasons as it could be a big delay between when the log is read by the collector and sent/ingested to Loki. Then, aspects to be reviewed:- The collector has enough cpu/memory for being able to deliver the logs at the same pace that reading them. Review collector metrics of cpu/memory- Not [alerts](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/logging/logging_alerts/default-logging-alerts.html) for the collector- The timeclock of the nodes are not configured in a different timezone or the time diverges in hours: ``` $ for node in $(oc get nodes-o name); do echo-e "### $node ###"; oc debug $node-- chroot /host date 2> /dev/null; done ```

title: The AWS load balancer is failing to select the appropriate subnets
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - The `AWS load balancer` selects incorrect subnets when creating `custom ingress controllers`.
resolution: 1. Create a backup of the service linked to the `custom ingress controller`: Eg.: ~~~ $ oc get svc-o yaml-n openshift-ingress > svc_bkp.yaml ~~~ 2. Add the bellow `annotation` in the svc_bkp.yaml file: ~~~ service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-subnets: subnet-,subnet-,subnet- ~~~ Eg.: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: annotations: traffic-policy.network.alpha.openshift.io/local-with-fallback: "" service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-subnets: creationTimestamp: "2024-10-21T13:14:33Z" ~~~ 3. Scale down to 0 the `ingress-operator` pod: ~~~ $ oc scale deployment ingress-operator--replicas=0-n openshift-ingress-operator ~~~ 4. Delete the svc created by the `custom ingress`: ~~~ $ oc delete svc-n openshift-ingress ~~~ 5. Recreate the svc with the 'aws-load-balancer-subnets' annotation: ~~~ $ oc create-f svc_bkp.yaml ~~~ 6. Scale up the `ingress-operator pod`: ~~~ $ oc scale deployment ingress-operator--replicas=1-n openshift-ingress-operator ~~~ 7. Verify in the AWS console if the correct subnets were selected by the Load balancer.
root_cause: - The default behavior is to auto-discover the subnets [Subnet Discovery](https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/aws-load-balancer-controller/v2.1/deploy/subnet_discovery/)

title: CIS controller throwing errors in kube-system project in RHOCP 4
issue: - CIS controller throwing the following error in the `kube-system` project: ~~~ 1017 14:12:58.161209 1 reflector.go:138] github.com/F5Networks/service_account/pkg/appmanager/appManager.go:1217: Failed to watch *v1.Node: failed to list *v1.Node: nodes is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:kube-system:service_account" cannot list resource "nodes" in API group "" at the cluster scope ~~~

title: Enable logging Transaction/JCA on RH-SSO running on Openshift
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - Temporarily set logging levels on a running POD
resolution: 1. Open a shell to the pod ~~~ $ oc rsh pod-name ~~~ 2. Add the logging level with jboss-cli.sh ~~~ $ /opt/eap/bin/jboss-cli.sh-c ~~~ e.g: ~~~ > /subsystem=logging/logger=org.jboss.jca:add(level=TRACE) > /subsystem=logging/logger=org.jboss.as.connector:add(level=TRACE) > /subsystem=logging/logger=com.arjuna:write-attribute(name=level,value=TRACE) ~~~ 2.1) If you need to restart, do: ~~~ > reload ~~~ 3. Once you have tested what needs to be logged, download the log. ~~~ $ oc logs pod-name ~~~ 4. Do step 2 again to disable the logging, for example: ~~~ > /subsystem=logging/logger=org.jboss.jca:remove() > /subsystem=logging/logger=org.jboss.as.connector:remove() > /subsystem=logging/logger=com.arjuna:write-attribute(name=level,value=INFO) ~~~

title: Red Hat AMQ Broker - Cropped fields values checking messages in the broker
issue: - Looking for the payload of each message in the admin console, some messages have the following body: ~~~ "text":" <?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>
resolution: By default, all property values are being cropped until 255 characters, to avoid this limitation, please follow the next steps: 1. Edit the Red Hat AMQ Broker operator, adding the next `addressSetting` configuration: ~~~ spec: addressSettings: addressSetting:- match: "#" managementMessageAttributeSizeLimit:-1 ~~~ 2. Save the changes and wait until pods are being rescheduled. 3. Review the properties contents, now these will look as follow: ~~~ <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> DUMMY.APP COMP123 USER01 2024-10-11 12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012 2024-10-11T12:00:00.000Z 9876543210 5000.00 USD DUMMY.PRODUCT ~~~
root_cause: Starting from Red Hat AMQ Broker 7.10, there is a [property](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.12/html/configuring_amq_broker/ref-br-broker-properties_configuring) named `managementMessageAttributeSizeLimit`that handles the maximum number of characters being displayed under the administration console, if this value is-1, there is no limit.

title: Deployment is failing with "Invalid value: xx: must be in the ranges" in RHOCP4
issue: - Deployment is failing with below error: ~~~ message: 'pods "podname-xxx-" is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constraint: [pod.metadata.annotations[container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/podname]: Forbidden: seccomp may not be set, provider "trident-controller": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider restricted-v2:.containers[0].runAsUser: Invalid value:: must be in the ranges: [,],.... ~~~- Unable to schedule the pod.
resolution: **Workaround 1**- Create a new custom service account in the same project where deployment is created: ~~~ $ oc create serviceaccount-n ~~~- Add the custom service account name in the deployment to run the pod: ~~~ $ oc edit deployment serviceAccount: serviceAccountName: ~~~- Assign `anyuid` SCC to the serviceaccount that is running the pod: ~~~ $ oc project $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid-z ~~~ If this doesn't help to resolve the issue. Refer **Workaround 2**- Remove the below lines present under securityContext: ~~~ runAsUser: runAsGroup: runAsNonRoot: true ~~~- Remove the below two lines from the deployment: ~~~ seccompProfile: type: RuntimeDefault ~~~- Once the above lines are removed, again add the below lines under `securityContext`: ~~~ runAsUser: runAsGroup: runAsNonRoot: true ~~~
root_cause: - Such issues can occur if the fsGroup value does not fall in the supplemental-groups or uid-range set on the project.

title: Unable to add nodes after OpenShift SDN to OVN migration if the node is built before migration
issue: - I am unable to add new nodes after OpenShift SDN to OVN migration if the node is built before migration
resolution: - Ensure the nodes you add into the cluster are built after migration to allow the node to fetch the latest configurations from Machine Config Servers.
root_cause: - The MCO will always try to boot new nodes on the latest MachineConfig. If the nodes are booted before migration, they will be unable to join the cluster due to a mismatch of networking causing the kubelet to never become ready.

title: StorageClassName not updated on statfulset applications after running storage class conversion with MTC [RHOCP4]
issue: - `StorageClassName` remains unchanged in `StatefulSet` deployments after performing storage class conversion using Migration Toolkit for Containers (MTC)- After migrating to a new `StorageClass` using the Migration Toolkit for Containers (MTC), `PersistentVolumes` for new replicas of a `StatefulSet` application are still created under the old `StorageClass`.
resolution: A possible workaround is to manually edit each `StatefulSet` after applying the storage class conversion through MTC, ensuring that new replicas scale up using the new (migrated) `StorageClass`. For example: ~~~ $ oc edit statefulset-n-o yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: StatefulSet metadata: creationTimestamp: "2024-10-23T07:55:18Z" generation: 1 labels: app: ubi-minimal name: ubi-minimal namespace: papagayo resourceVersion: "39776731" uid: 53151199-3691-40f5-a9c0-2dac3ba04313 spec: persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy: whenDeleted: Retain whenScaled: Retain podManagementPolicy: OrderedReady replicas: 1 revisionHistoryLimit: 10 selector: matchLabels: app: ubi-minimal serviceName: ubi-minimal template: metadata: creationTimestamp: null labels: app: ubi-minimal spec: containers:- command:- /bin/bash--c- sleep infinity image: registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi-minimal:latest imagePullPolicy: Always name: ubi-minimal resources: {} terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log terminationMessagePolicy: File volumeMounts:- mountPath: /mnt/data1 name: volume1- mountPath: /mnt/data2 name: volume2 dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst restartPolicy: Always schedulerName: default-scheduler securityContext: {} terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 updateStrategy: rollingUpdate: partition: 0 type: RollingUpdate volumeClaimTemplates:- apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: creationTimestamp: null name: volume1 spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 1Gi storageClassName: thin-csi-sc2 #---> Replace with the migrated `StorageClass` name volumeMode: Filesystem status: phase: Pending- apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: creationTimestamp: null name: volume2 spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 2Gi storageClassName: thin-csi-sc2 #---> Replace by the migrated `StorageClass` volumeMode: Filesystem status: phase: Pending ~~~
root_cause: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [MIG-1660](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MIG-1660). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: Local Storage Operator fails releasing large volumes in RHOCP4
issue: - Large capacity `PersistentVolume` provisioned through LSO, under a `StorageClass` with `reclaimPolicy` set to `Delete` is stuck on `Released` status.
resolution: **Fix Provided in New Release:** Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-22250](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-22250). and delivered a fix in OpenShift Container Platform 4.15.0 through errata [RHSA-2023:7197](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7197). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: During the clean-up phase of the volume, the `Local Storage Operator` creates a temporary `ext2 filesystem` before wiping the data. Since `ext2 filesystems` are limited to 2,147,483,647 blocks, this operation fails when the device exceeds this limitation, preventing volume from being reused.

title: Segregating OpenShift Data Foundation from the Default Network: What Traffic Uses the Reserved Network Interface?
issue: There are three ways to segregate OpenShift Data Foundation from OpenShift default network, What Traffic Uses the Reserved Network Interface?- Reserve a network interface on the host for the public network of OpenShift Data Foundation- Reserve a network interface on the host for OpenShift Data Foundation’s cluster network- Reserve two network interfaces on the host for OpenShift Data Foundation: one for the public network and one for the cluster network
resolution: 1. Reserve a network interface on the host for the public network of OpenShift Data Foundation ~~~- Pod-to-storage and internal storage replication traffic coexist on a network that is isolated from pod-to-pod network traffic.- Application pods have access to the maximum public network storage bandwidth when the OpenShift Data Foundation cluster is healthy.- When the OpenShift Data Foundation cluster is recovering from failure, the application pods will have reduced bandwidth due to ongoing replication and rebalancing traffic. ~~~ 2. Reserve a network interface on the host for OpenShift Data Foundation’s cluster network ~~~- Pod-to-pod and pod-to-storage traffic both continue to use OpenShift’s default network.- Pod-to-storage bandwidth is less affected by the health of the OpenShift Data Foundation cluster.- Pod-to-pod and pod-to-storage OpenShift Data Foundation traffic might contend for network bandwidth in busy OpenShift clusters.- The storage internal network often has an overabundance of bandwidth that is unused, reserved for use during failures. ~~~ 3. Reserve two network interfaces on the host for OpenShift Data Foundation: one for the public network and one for the cluster network ~~~- Pod-to-pod, pod-to-storage, and storage internal traffic are all isolated, and none of the traffic types will contend for resources. Service level agreements for all traffic types are more able to be ensured.- During healthy runtime, more network bandwidth is reserved but unused across all three networks. ~~~

title: Service-CA pod in ContainerConfigError having runAsNonRoot in RHOCP 4
issue: - service-ca pod is in `ContainerConfigError` and its securityContexts contain the runAsNonRoot configuration set to true and it is showing the error `Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root`- openshift-service-ca operator has the message `Progressing: service-ca does not have available replicas`
resolution: 1. run the following command to edit the clusterrolebinding related to the `anyuid` SCC: ``` $ oc edit clusterrolebinding system:openshift:scc:anyuid ``` and delete the following lines from the `subjects` section: ```- apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Group name: system:serviceaccounts:kube-system ``` 2. run the following command to restart the service-ca deployment. ``` $ oc rollout restart deployment service-ca ```
root_cause: This happens when the standard configuration for the `anyuid` SCC is changed by adding the group system:serviceaccounts:kube-system to it. This deviates from the standard configuration of the cluster and it is not supported by Red Hat. When this group has such permissions, the user `system:serviceaccount:kube-system:replicaset-controller` will set `anyuid` SCC instead of`restricted-v2` because the first has higher priority, when assigning it to the service-ca pod.

title: 3scale 2.12 operator deployed in OCP 4.12 is in CrashLoopBackOff status and "PodDisruptionBudget" API missing message (workaround)
issue: Before upgrading 3scale to 2.13 version, the OCP cluster was upgraded to 4.12. The operator pod logs shows an error and 3scale cannot be upgraded to 2.13.
resolution: **Prerequisites** * Upgrade the external database from PosrgreSQL 10 to PostgreSQL 13. 3scale 2.12 is supported with both versions. * See [supported configurations table](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7010149) and [upgrade guide for 3scale 2.12](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html/migrating_3scale/upgrade-operator#upgrading-with-external-system-database-postgresql10-and-postgresql13). * If external Redis database is used, please follow the steps documented in [Removing unused MessageBus](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.12/html-single/migrating_3scale/index#removing-unused-messagebus-variables-operator). **Steps to upgrade 3scale 2.12 to 2.13** * Take a backup of the current 3scale 2.12 environment. * Remove the current 3scale 2.12 operator: navigate to *Operators > Installed Operators* and select *Uninstall Operator* option from the three dots menu on the right of the *Red Hat Integration- 3scale operator* row. * It is safe to remove the Operator. The operator reconciles and performs the changes in 3scale for you. If it is scaled down or uninstalled, the operator is not able to perform any changes. On the contrary, do NOT remove the APIManager CR or any other object, if you remove the APIManager CR you'll remove 3scale entirely. * Reinstall the 3scale Operator version 2.13. From the Administrator perspective, navigating to *Operators > OperatorHub*, search for *3scale* and select *Red Hat Integration- 3scale*. * Click the *Install* button. * Make sure the *Update channel* is `threescale-2.13`, under Installation mode. DO NOT install the 2.14 channel. * Select a specific namespace on the cluster, select the namespace under *Installed Namespace* and click the Install button. * Wait for the upgrade process, and once finished, test that everything is working as expected. * The admin portal at the bottom right corner should show 2.13 version. * The developer portal works as expected. * API requests are working correctly and the analytics are shown as expected.
root_cause: OCP 4.12 only supports 3scale 2.13.1 and above. The `PodDisruptionBudget.v1beta1.policy` API is required by 3scale operator version 2.12. Due to this limitation and the fact that 3scale cannot skip any version while upgrading, it is not possible to upgrade to version 2.13 using the traditional upgrade instructions.

title: How to download the pull secret from Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console using a REST API call?
issue: - How to download the pull secret from using a REST API call?- How to automate the download of the pull secret needed for OpenShift 4 installs?- Trying to get the pull secret via REST API call using user and password is not working with error "`Client not allowed for direct access grants`".
resolution: The api for is at. The pull secret endpoint is `POST /api/accounts_mgmt/v1/access_token`. It is needed to authenticate using a Bearer token, which can be obtained from the second section at. This link details using a long lived access token, which is obtained there too. ~~~ $ export BEARER=$(curl \--silent \--data-urlencode "grant_type=refresh_token" \--data-urlencode "client_id=cloud-services" \--data-urlencode "refresh_token=${OFFLINE_ACCESS_TOKEN}" \ https://sso.redhat.com/auth/realms/redhat-external/protocol/openid-connect/token | \ jq-r.access_token) $ curl-X POST https://api.openshift.com/api/accounts_mgmt/v1/access_token--header "Content-Type:application/json"--header "Authorization: Bearer $BEARER" | jq {"auths": {"cloud.openshift.com": {"auth": " ", "email": " "}, "quay.io": {"auth": " ", "email": " "}, "registry.connect.redhat.com": {"auth": " ", "email": " "}, "registry.redhat.io": {"auth": " ", "email": " "}}} ~~~
root_cause: The api for is at. The pull secret endpoint is `POST /api/accounts_mgmt/v1/access_token`.

title: BareMetalHost is failing to boot with message ignition: invalid config version (couldn't parse)
issue: While adding a BareMetalHost to a cluster, the node completes the introspection phase but fails during the boot phase with errors like the following (shown in the node console): ~~~ Ignition has failed. Please ensure your config is valid. Note that only Ignition spec v3.0.0+ configs are accepted. Displaying logs from failed units: ignition-fetch-offline.service Oct 09 12:28:45 ignition[1933]: no config URL provided Oct 09 12:28:45 ignition[1933]: reading system config file "/usr/lib/ignition/user.ign" Oct 09 12:28:45 ignition[1933]: parsing config with SHA512: aaabbbcccdddeeefffggghhh Oct 09 12:28:45 ignition[1933]: failed to fetch config: invalid config version (couldn't parse) Oct 09 12:28:45 ignition[1933]: failed to acquire config: invalid config version (couldn't parse) Oct 09 12:28:45 ignition[1933]: Ignition failed: invalid config version (couldn't parse) Oct 09 12:28:45 systemd[1]: ignition-fetch-offline.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE Oct 09 12:28:45 systemd[1]: ignition-fetch-offline.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'. Oct 09 12:28:45 systemd[1]: Failed to start Ignition (fetch-offline). Oct 09 12:28:45 systemd[1]: ignition-fetch-offline.service: Triggering OnFailure= dependencies. ~~~

While creating a BMH resource for a new node to be added to the bare metal cluster, the node completes pxe boot (one can see on console that ignition was applied with hostname and IP details) then reboots the server automatically and the next boot stops with errors about failed to start Ignition.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat Engineering and is tracked by bug: [OCPBUGS-43546](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-43546). #### Workaround Update the `spec.online` parameter as `false` in BareMetalHost CR and recreate it: ~~~ $ oc get bmh-n openshift-machine-api-o yaml > bmh.yaml $ sed-i-e 's/online: true/online: false/g' bmh.yaml $ oc delete bmh-n openshift-machine-api $ oc create-f bmh.yaml ~~~
root_cause: When adding a BMH with: ~~~ spec: online: true customDeploy: method: install_coreos ~~~ after inspection the BMO will provision the node in ironic, but the node is being created without any userdata/ignition data. As a consequence the `IPA ironic_coreos_install` then goes ahead to create ignition from scratch. But the created ignition is invalid and the node fails to boot after it is provisioned.

title: Housekeeping of /sysroot on Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - Services are failing to start due to an error `no space left` on the node.- Unable to debug to the node due to no space on the `/sysroot`.- How to remove the unwanted `images`,`logs/tmp` files from `/sysroot`?- How to clear space from `/sysroot` or subfolders of `/sysroot` filesystem from RHCOS node?
resolution: It is currently not supported to increase `/sysroot` in RHCOS, and the supported approach is to re-create the node with bigger disk. An internal RFE was already raised with engineering for supporting it: RFE-998. ###Workaround- By default `/syroot` is mounted in RO (read-only) mode. ~~~ $ mount | grep /sysroot /dev/vda4 on /sysroot type xfs (ro,relatime,seclabel,attr2,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=32k,prjquota) ~~~- Remount `/sysroot` in RW (read-write) mode. ~~~ $ mount-o remount,rw /sysroot ~~~- Delete the unwanted files inside `/sysroot`. ~~~ $ rm-rf ~~~- Reboot the node gracefully to again mount `/sysroot` in RO mode using the [official documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-rebooting.html).
root_cause: To find out which directory is contributing to the large usage of `/sysroot`, please check the Diagnostic Steps for an example. It is commonly seen that some processes are still holding deleted files though the files have been removed. In such cases, the [df still shows a high usage percentage of the filesystem](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2316).

title: Ports in NO_PROXY Configuration Supported for IPv6 Addresses in OpenShift (4.x versions before 4.16)
issue: - Is it possible to add `ports` only in `NO_PROXY`?- The current OpenShift documentation does not mention that ports can be included in the `NO_PROXY` environment variable for `IPv6` addresses.- Users may be unaware that adding ports to `NO_PROXY` is a valid option for `IPv6`.
resolution: - For OpenShift 4.x versions before 4.16, **ports** can be specified in the `NO_PROXY` environment variable, but **only for IPv6 addresses**. For example: ~~~ spec: httpProxy: http://[2012:xxxx:xxxx::8884]:8081 httpsProxy: http://[2012:xxxx:xxxx::8884]:8081 noProxy: cluster.domain.com,9999,6385,443 <==== ~~~ **NOTE:** If dealing with `IPv4` traffic, using ports in `NO_PROXY` is not supported. For `IPv4`, consider using CIDR ranges or domain names to manage proxy exceptions.

title: Child devfile is not inheriting starterProjects from Parent devfile
issue: When opening a new workspace using a child `devfile`, the `starterProjects` defined in the parent `devfile` are not available in the child workspace.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering, see [CRW-7531](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CRW-7531 "https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CRW-7531"). As a workaround, consider modifying the parent Devfile's `starterProjects` to be `projects`.
root_cause: This issue is caused by a conflict with the Che Dashboard and DevWorkspace Operator:- Che Dashboard will automatically inject an implicit project to the `devworkspace` when the `devfile` hosted on git, even if the `devfile` does not contain any projects. This implicit project contains the `devfile`'s source repository.- DevWorkspace Operator will prioritize `projects` over `starterProjects` when setting `$PROJECT_SOURCE` by design. You can find more details on the [upstream issue](https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/issues/23065#issuecomment-2417255184 "https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/issues/23065#issuecomment-2417255184")

title: Deploy  OpenShift cluster on Nutanix with multiple subnet
issue: - Can worker nodes be deployed across multiple subnets?- Can masters and workers be deployed in different subnets?
resolution: - Currently, only one subnet per Prism Element in an OpenShift Container Platform cluster is supported.- Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE-5358](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-5358). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: Blocking the network traffic between the host network and a pod or group of pods inhibits the functioning of the latter
issue: Let's say that the host network of a cluster is, for example, 10.0.0.0/24 and the following NetworkPolicy is created: ~~~ kind: NetworkPolicy apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: egress-block-host-ips namespace: test spec: podSelector: {} egress:- to:- ipBlock: cidr: 0.0.0.0/0 except:- 10.0.0.0/24 policyTypes:- Egress ~~~ Which would be the consequences of that?
resolution: **That configuration must not be performed because it will prevent the pods from communicating with the API**: ~~~ $ oc rsh sh-4.2$ curl-kvv https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local * About to connect() to kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local port 443 (#0) * Trying 172.30.0.1... ^C ~~~
root_cause: The traffic between application pods and the OpenShift API goes through the host network.

title: Connections between host-network and normal pods failing after creating NetworkPolicy
issue: - The `host-network` pods can't connect to normal pods running on a different node when the `allow-same-namespace` or `deny-by-default` NetworkPolicy is created while the pods are in the same namespace.- The issue resolves only after creating `allow-from-hostnetwork` NetworkPolicy which allows ingress traffic from the namespace with the label `policy-group.network.openshift.io/host-network`.
resolution: - When the pod runs with the `HostNetwork` set to true, the pods will be on the host network, and so their traffic will not be recognized as coming from any specific namespace.- Due to this, the connections coming from the `host-network` pod fail.- In OpenShift SDN, for somewhat accidental historical reasons, traffic coming from any non-pod source is treated as though it came from the namespace `default`. Thus, it's possible to allow traffic from `host-network` pod by adding a label to `default` and then allowing traffic based on that label. (This will also allow traffic from any other host-network pod, or node process.) However, this approach does not work with any other network plugin.- In theory, with other plugins, if you knew the pod network CIDR, you could create a policy saying "allow from anywhere (that can route to the pod network) except the pod network", which is essentially equivalent to "allow from default" in OpenShift SDN. eg: ~~~ ipBlock: cidr: 0.0.0.0/0 except:- 10.128.0.0/14 ~~~- This is not ideal, because it requires you to know the pod network CIDR, but even given that, it would not actually work with many network plugins anyway. Eg, in ovn-kubernetes, when a node or a host-network pod sends traffic to a pod-network pod, the source IP is not the node's "primary" node IP but rather the IP associated with the ovn-k8s-mp0 interface, which is inside the pod network CIDR (eg, it would be 10.128.6.2 on the node that has the 10.128.6.0/23 subnet). It would be possible to create a policy allowing specifically the relevant source node IP of each node, but such a policy would need to be updated any time nodes were added or removed from the cluster.- To allow connections between `host-network` and `pod-network` pods when the `allow-same-namespace` or `deny-by-default` network policies exist, the following NetworkPolicy can be created as per the documentation [Using the allow-from-hostnetwork network policy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/networking/network_policy/about-network-policy.html#nw-networkpolicy-allow-from-hostnetwork_about-network-policy). ~~~ apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: allow-from-hostnetwork spec: ingress:- from:- namespaceSelector: matchLabels: policy-group.network.openshift.io/host-network: "" podSelector: {} policyTypes:- Ingress ~~~- For more information, please refer to [allow-from-router-networkpolicy.md](https://github.com/openshift/enhancements/blob/master/enhancements/network/allow-from-router-networkpolicy.md).
root_cause: - When the pod runs with the `HostNetwork` set to true, the pods will be on the host network, and so their traffic will not be recognized as coming from any specific namespace.

title: Using "ansible-builder" to create an Execution Environment  with the "redhat.openshift" collection as a requirement fails
issue: - When building an Execution Environment using `ansible-builder` which includes the `redhat.openshift` collection, the build process fails with the following error message: ~~~ $ ansible-builder build-f execution-environment.yml-v 3 [...] + /usr/bin/microdnf install-y--nodocs--setopt install_weak_deps=0 openshift-clients Downloading metadata... [...] Downloading metadata... error: No package matches 'openshift-clients' Error: building at STEP "RUN /output/scripts/assemble": while running runtime: exit status 1 ~~~
resolution: **For Customers Using subscription-manager**- This issue can be resolved by passing additional options to the package manager via the environment variable `PKGMGR_OPTS` in the Execution Environment definition file- By default the environment variable `PKGMGR_OPTS` contains the following value: ~~~--nodocs--setopt=install_weak_deps=0 ~~~- The build succeeds when explicitly enabling the Red Hat OpenShift repository by overriding the environment variable `PKGMGR_OPTS` in the Execution Environment definition file: ~~~--- version: 3 [...] additional_build_steps: prepend_builder:- ENV PKGMGR_OPTS="--nodocs--setopt=install_weak_deps=0--setopt=rhocp-4.12-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms.enabled=true" prepend_final:- ENV PKGMGR_OPTS="--nodocs--setopt=install_weak_deps=0--setopt=rhocp-4.12-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms.enabled=true" ~~~- The environment variable `PKGMGR_OPTS` has to be overridden in the `prepend_builder` and `prepend_final` build stages, as these stages are responsible for installing package dependencies **For Customers using Red Hat Update Infrastructure (RHUI) Repositories**- Because the `rhocp-*` repositories are not available in the RHUI repositories, customers building execution environment images in cloud provider environments will need to obtain the `openshift-clients` [RPM package from the Red Hat Customer Portal](https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/290/ver=4.12/rhel---8/4.12.28/x86_64/packages) manually and then install it by adding the following lines to their `execution-environment.yaml` file: ~~~--- version: 3 [...] additional_build_files:- src: openshift-clients-4.12.0-202307200611.p0.g49844f7.assembly.stream.el8.x86_64.rpm dest: rpms [...] additional_build_steps: prepend_base:- COPY_build/rpms/*.rpm /tmp/openshift-clients.rpm- RUN $PKGMGR install bash-completion- RUN rpm-ivh /tmp/openshift-clients.rpm [...] ~~~
root_cause: - The package `openshift-clients` is a dependency of the `redhat.openshift` collection and thus needs to be installable during the build process- By default, only the Universal Base Image (UBI) repositories and the Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) BaseOS and AppStream repositories are enabled; however, these repositories do not provide the `openshift-clients` package

title: How to restore ceph-monitor quorum in Openshift Container Storage?
issue: `rook-ceph-operator` logs report of mon quorum issues even though OCS have 3 mon pods Running. ~~~ 53280:2021-03-18 10:56:43.090829 W | op-mon: failed to check mon health. failed to get mon quorum status: mon quorum status failed: exit status 1 53324:2021-03-18 10:57:43.200023 W | op-mon: failed to check mon health. failed to get mon quorum status: mon quorum status failed: exit status 1 ~~~
`ceph-monitor` quorum is lost with 2 of 3 monitors being lost. How to restore it back?
resolution: * Verify the the mon_status and quorum_status from all the mon pods. ~~~ $ oc rsh # ceph daemon /var/run/ceph/*.asok quorum_status # ceph daemon /var/run/ceph/*.asok mon_status ~~~ This would show an additional mon 'm' in the quorum. We could see [e,i,l,m] in quorum_status and mon_status. ~~~ {"rank": 3, "name": "m", "public_addrs": {"addrvec": [{"type": "v2", "addr": "172.30.39.184:3300", "nonce": 0}, ~~~ *'m' in above is taken an as example. The id may change.* * This additional mon has to be removed from the monmap. **Follow the below Action Plan for removal.** *Kindly note the below steps is a workaround to bring back the mon quorum. Please work with Red Hat Support to determine the root cause.* * First, stop the `rook-ceph-operator` so it will not try to failover the mons while we are modifying the monmap. ~~~ # oc-n openshift-storage scale deployment rook-ceph-operator--replicas=0 ~~~ * Take a backup of the current `rook-ceph-mon-e` deployment, which happens to be Running and the oldest one. ~~~ # oc-n openshift-storage get deployment rook-ceph-mon-e-o yaml > rook-ceph-mon-e-deployment.yaml ~~~ * Open the file and copy the command and args from the mon container (see containers list). This is needed for the `monmap` commands. ~~~ [...] containers:- args:---fsid=c7f51534-d8a4-4d0e-8f85-2853d91242c6---keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring---log-to-stderr=true---err-to-stderr=true---mon-cluster-log-to-stderr=true- '--log-stderr-prefix=debug '---default-log-to-file=false---default-mon-cluster-log-to-file=false---mon-host=$(ROOK_CEPH_MON_HOST)---mon-initial-members=$(ROOK_CEPH_MON_INITIAL_MEMBERS)---id=e---setuser=ceph---setgroup=ceph---foreground---public-addr=172.30.198.157---setuser-match-path=/var/lib/ceph/mon/ceph-e/store.db---public-bind-addr=$(ROOK_POD_IP) command:- ceph-mon [...] ~~~ * Cleanup the copied command and args fields to form a pastable command. ~~~ $ ceph-mon \--fsid=c7f51534-d8a4-4d0e-8f85-2853d91242c6 \--keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring \--log-to-stderr=true \--err-to-stderr=true \--mon-cluster-log-to-stderr=true \--log-stderr-prefix=debug \--default-log-to-file=false \--default-mon-cluster-log-to-file=false \--mon-host=$ROOK_CEPH_MON_HOST \--mon-initial-members=$ROOK_CEPH_MON_INITIAL_MEMBERS \--id=e \--setuser=ceph \--setgroup=ceph \--foreground \--public-addr=172.30.198.157 \--setuser-match-path=/var/lib/ceph/mon/ceph-e/store.db \--public-bind-addr=$ROOK_POD_IP (be sure to remove the single quotes around the--log-stderr-prefix flag and the parenthesis around the variables being passed ROOK_CEPH_MON_HOST, ROOK_CEPH_MON_INITIAL_MEMBERS and ROOK_POD_IP) ~~~ * Patch the `rook-ceph-mon-e` Deployment to run a sleep instead of the ceph-mon command: ~~~ # oc-n openshift-storage patch deployment rook-ceph-mon-e-p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name": "mon", "command": ["sleep", "infinity"], "args": []}]}}}}' ~~~ * Also set 'initialDelaySeconds: 2000' so that pod doesn't restart again while perform the activity. ~~~ # oc edit deployment rook-ceph-mon-e initialDelaySeconds: 2000 ~~~ * Perform the below steps on the `mon-e` pod. ~~~-> Connect to the `rook-ceph-mon-e` pod. # oc rsh rook-ceph-mon-e--> set a few simple variables # cluster_namespace=rook-ceph # good_mon_id=e # monmap_path=/tmp/monmap-> extract the monmap to a file, by pasting the ceph-mon command from the mon deployment (Step iv) and adding the `--extract-monmap=${monmap_path}` flag to it. # ceph-mon \--fsid=c7f51534-d8a4-4d0e-8f85-2853d91242c6 \--keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring \--log-to-stderr=true \--err-to-stderr=true \--mon-cluster-log-to-stderr=true \--log-stderr-prefix=debug \--default-log-to-file=false \--default-mon-cluster-log-to-file=false \--mon-host=$ROOK_CEPH_MON_HOST \--mon-initial-members=$ROOK_CEPH_MON_INITIAL_MEMBERS \--id=e \--setuser=ceph \--setgroup=ceph \--foreground \--public-addr=172.30.198.157 \--setuser-match-path=/var/lib/ceph/mon/ceph-e/store.db \--public-bind-addr=$ROOK_POD_IP \--extract-monmap=${monmap_path}-> Review the contents of monmap. # monmaptool--print /tmp/monmap-> Take a backup of current monmap. # cp /tmp/monmap /tmp/monmap.current-> Remove the mon "m" from the monmap. # monmaptool /tmp/monmap.current--rm m-> Inject the monmap back to the monitor. Add the "--inject-monmap" flag to the ceph-mon command from Step iv. # ceph-mon \--fsid=c7f51534-d8a4-4d0e-8f85-2853d91242c6 \--keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring \--log-to-stderr=true \--err-to-stderr=true \--mon-cluster-log-to-stderr=true \--log-stderr-prefix=debug \--default-log-to-file=false \--default-mon-cluster-log-to-file=false \--mon-host=$ROOK_CEPH_MON_HOST \--mon-initial-members=$ROOK_CEPH_MON_INITIAL_MEMBERS \--id=e \--setuser=ceph \--setgroup=ceph \--foreground \--public-addr=172.30.198.157 \--setuser-match-path=/var/lib/ceph/mon/ceph-e/store.db \--public-bind-addr=$ROOK_POD_IP \--inject-monmap=/tmp/monmap.current We should be seeing 3 Running mon ids in the monmap now. You may verify the monmap again by extracting to a different path and printing it. ~~~ * Patch the `rook-ceph-mon-e` deployment to run the "mon" command again. Replace the `sleep` command with the args and command present earlier as in Step 3. of action plan. Also revert initialDelaySeconds to 10 in the deployment. `initialDelaySeconds: 10` ~~~ $ oc edit deployment rook-ceph-mon-e ~~~ * Scale up the `rook-ceph-operator` deployment. ~~~ # oc-n openshift-storage scale deployment rook-ceph-operator--replicas=1 ~~~ * Verify all pods are Running. ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage ~~~
root_cause: * Please work with [Red Hat Support Team](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new) to find the root cause of this issue in your environment.

title: Change log format of CRI-O to JSON in OCP
issue: How can the container log format for containers running in `CRI-O` be changed to `JSON`?
How to change the log format that `CRI-O` uses to `JSON`.
resolution: * With OpenShift Logging 5.1, [JSON logging can be enabled](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/logging/cluster-logging-enabling-json-logging.html). You can configure the Log Forwarding API to parse JSON strings into a structured object. * Currently, it is not possible to change the container log format of CRI-O itself from `text` to `json`. > **Note:** at this moment, only the daemon log format can be changed from `text` to `json` with the `--log-format` option, but not the container log format. * Red Hat is aware of this issue and is tracking the resolution in an internal Request-for-Enhancement (RFE). If you encounter this issue in your environment, please open a new Support Case in the [Red Hat Customer Portal](https://access.redhat.com) referring to this Solution.
root_cause: The default log format for `CRI-O` is `text`.

title: How to run commands not available in RH UBI Micro inside Loki pods in RHOCP 4
issue: The `curl` command is not anymore present inside Loki, but it's needed for running some commands as for removing unhealthy members
Loki was moved from using image base RH UBI to RH UBI Micro, then, some commands as curl are not anymore available for debugging and troubleshooting purposes
How to execute `curl` inside loki pods.

Trying to run curl inside a Loki pod returns the error `executable file not found`: ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging rsh deployment/logging-loki-distributor curl ERRO[0000] exec failed: unable to start container process: exec: "curl": executable file not found in $PATH command terminated with exit code 255 ```
resolution: Use `oc debug` indicating an UBI image to be used. An example in case that needed to run a command inside the Loki Distributor where it's used the UBI 8: ``` /// Example for the distributor $ oc-n openshift-logging debug--image=registry.redhat.io/ubi8:latest deployment/logging-loki-distributor Starting pod/logging-loki-distributor-debug-9qxcv... Pod IP: 10.131.3.241 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.4$ curl curl: try 'curl--help' or 'curl--manual' for more information /// Example for an ingester that's an statefulset $ oc-n openshift-logging debug--image=registry.redhat.io/ubi8:latest logging-loki-ingester-0 ``` It's possible to see that all the variables are defined in the Loki debug pod defined: ``` sh-4.4$ env LOGGING_LOKI_INGESTER_HTTP_PORT_3100_TCP=tcp://172.30.225.115:3100 LOGGING_LOKI_DISTRIBUTOR_HTTP_PORT_3100_TCP_ADDR=172.30.176.205 COLLECTOR_PORT_24231_TCP_ADDR=172.30.57.108 COLLECTOR_SERVICE_PORT_METRICS=24231 LOGGING_LOKI_QUERY_FRONTEND_HTTP_SERVICE_PORT=3100 LOGFILESMETRICEXPORTER_PORT=tcp://172.30.204.112:2112 COLLECTOR_SERVICE_PORT=24231--- OUTPUT OMMITED--- ``` **NOTE**: Other interesting articles- ["Using nsenter to troubleshoot containers"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1611883)- ["How to do test inside a pod network namespace with the same DNS settings"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7067298)
root_cause: Starting in the RHOL versions listed below, the Base Image for Loki were changed from RH UBI to RH UBI Micro, then commands as curl won't be available in the Loki pods: * 5.6.19 * 5.7.14 * 5.8.7 * 5.9.2 The reason for this change is related to reduce the size of the images and at the same time, to reduce the exposition a security bugs related to packages not needed by Loki.

title: Node placement using virtctl
issue: With `virtctl migrate`, is it possible to specify which node my VM will migrate to?
Similarly, with `virtctl start `, can I choose which node the VM will start on?
resolution: * Configure affinity or tolerance rules, more information can be found [here](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/virt/virtual_machines/advanced_vm_management/virt-specifying-nodes-for-vms.html) * A workaround would be to cordon nodes where you do not want the VM to start (or migrate) to, initiate a start/migrate, then uncordon the nodes again.
