title: How an unshared CacheStore behave in a RHDG clustered environment?
issue: - What is loaded if a clustered with a underlying file-store is started- I see stale entries on some nodes in a replicated cache- How do I shutdown and restart a clusterd cache with unshared Cache Stores
resolution: Local stores, like file based stores must not be shared, like SingleFileStore, LevelDbStore, RocksDbStore. Other types might use different underlying persistence and might be configured as `shared=false`. In case of `preload=true` the cache loads the persistent store for every node but will only use it if this node is the primary owner. This will take time and the instance is not available during that time, also it might load stale entries which is useless. Preload=false prevent to waste time for reading the data from the persistence. If the cache is clustered, like distributed or replicated, and there are more nodes in the cluster the unshared persistence will cause problems if not handled correctly. Until version 7 there is no automatism to solve such scenario. #### cluster (aka graceful) shutdown- RHDG 7+ If a clustered cache should completely restarted it depends on the cache how it can be handled. With RHDG 7+ the cluster can be stopped gracefully see [Cluster Shutdown chapter](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/7.2/html-single/administration_and_configuration_guide/index#cluster_shutdown_and_restart "RHDG 7.2 Cluster Shutdown and Restart") All cluster nodes will stop client access and rebalancing, persist the local data and will go down immediately. The restart can be done in any order but all nodes which are active during "shutdown cluster" are mandatory to get back to a healthy state! Nodes which are not part of the cluster before are not able to start. Currently there is an issue if the starting cluster is accessed by clients. In case of `get` requests not all entries might be available. In case of `put` requests the update might be lost after all nodes are up and running as it will change the state-transfer state. This could end up in partial inconsistence. This is tracked by [JDG-3967](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JDG-3967 "Cluster in a confusing state after restarted from graceful shutdown- no hint for waiting on complete restarted") and will be fixed by RHDG 8.4+. #### Individual shutdown of nodes- In case of replicated caches the nodes can be go down in any order and the last one should hold the master-data. This node need to be started first and all other should start with a empty store to prevent from stale entries. Note that the last remaining node is still acepting incomming requests. To start with an empty store it is possible to set `purge=true`or remove the caches DAT files from the servers `data`directory.- In case of distributed caches the nodes need to be shutdowned one-by-one and the next node shutdown needs to be delayed until the rehashing is completed to not loose data. Finally the last node will have the complete cache persistent and this node need to be started first. **Warning** this is why we don't recommend this approach, a cluster should use the `shutdown cluster` command available with CLI and REST to handle a complete cluster shutdown. **Note** A local, file based store can be used if the data can be retrieved by another persistence or calculation to increase the speed. If the amount of data is huge or a reliable persistence is needed you should consider to use a different cache store approach. **Hint** This will apply to an environment which is managed individual, if managed by OpenShift Operator it will behave different.
root_cause: A cache with a local store, like file-store or any other with `shared=false`, will load the entries from the store first. Depend on the type it will be read to store the key's in memory (FileStore) first. If preload=true the values are loaded from the store, in case of a SingleFileStore this will be a second, random access to the file. After this is completed and the node joined the cluster, the state-transfer is used to update the local cache from the running cluster with changed and new entries. Because of this the stale entries are available on this instance only as they are not pushed to other nodes! Also in case of a full cluster restart the first started node is responsible for the new cluster state and ONLY the entities stored here are use for rebalancing, this will cause inconsistency within the cluster after restart if the shutdown and start order is wrong!

title: Troubleshooting Azure Red Hat OpenShift  4.14.z / 4.13.40: Cluster Installs and provisioning new machines fail
issue: *Update as of October 25, 2024

This issue is now fixed for installations and upgrades. Upgrades along Z-streams without admin acks are considered safe for clusters with special network routing.- Clusters installations at 4.14.z or 4.13.40 fails with `InternalServerError`:- Private cluster with User Defined Routing (UDR) specified and the subnet route tables lacks an Internet route for `arosvc.azurecr.io`- When a Virtual Appliance / Firewall is used that blocks outbound Internet traffic for `arosvc.azurecr.io`- Clusters upgraded to 4.14.z / 4.13.40 fail to provision new machines:- When UDR is specified and the subnet route tables lack an Internet route for `arosvc.azurecr.io`- When a Virtual Appliance / Firewall is used that blocks outbound Internet traffic for `arosvc.azurecr.io`
resolution: #### Cluster Install: *September 5, 2024 Update:*- As of September 5, 2024 all new cluster installs have had this issue patched. Customers can create a new cluster without any additional steps. #### Upgraded cluster: *October 25th, 2024 Update:* The fleet wide maintenance is complete and no new edge blocks will be created. Customers can upgrade clusters currently on all 4.12.z streams to 4.13 and beyond along the unblocked edges.The safe edges are: 4.13.51, 4.13.52, 4.14.38, and 4.14.39. Previously:- Add an Internet route for `arosvc.azurecr.io` or add an Internet route for `0.0.0.0/0` by following the Azure documentation:- [Azure/Manage route table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/manage-route-table)- [Azure/Virtual Network- UDR overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-networks-udr-overview)
root_cause: When a new 4.14.z / 4.13.40 machine (master or worker) is provisioned one of the first steps in the boot sequence is for the `machine-config-daemon-pull` service to pull images from the ARO Azure Container Registry (ACR) at `arosvc.azurecr.io:443`. In the situation where the machine provisioning is dependent on the RP Gateway Service the ACR image pull will fail with a timeout and the new machine will not provision. This occurs when the network policy does not allow Internet-bound traffic to the ARO Azure Container Registry. This is due to the ARO gateway proxy not being active early enough in the machine boot sequence. The `machine-config-daemon-pull` service attempts to pull an image before the ARO-provisioned `dnsmasq` service starts. The `dnsmasq` service enables the machine to resolve the ACR to the private link IP of the RP Gateway service and in turn pull the image and correctly provision the machine.

title: How to fix UpgradeConfigSyncFailureOver4HrSRE alert

title: How to mirror the boot source container images of RHEL locally to be consumed by OpenShift Virtualization?
issue: The RHEL8 and RHEL9 images are not updating after disconnecting the cluster from the network ~~~ Internal error occurred: registry.redhat.io/rhel9/rhel-guest-image:latest: Get \"https://registry.redhat.io/v2/\": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers) ~~~
The CDIDataImportCronOutdated alert is firing on a disconnected cluster
Configured ImageContentSourcePolicy but the issue persists.
resolution: * Configure ImageTagMirrorSet (ITMS) and ImageDigestMirrorSet (IDMS) to redirect the pulls for these images to the local registry. Both are needed, as some pulls are by digest and some are by tag (i.e. RHEL8 and 9 use an ImageStream). ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageTagMirrorSet metadata: name: itms-generic-0 spec: imageTagMirrors:- mirrors:- registry.example.internal/rhel8 source: registry.redhat.io/rhel8- mirrors:- registry.example.internal/rhel9 source: registry.redhat.io/rhel9--- apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageDigestMirrorSet metadata: name: idms-operator-0 spec: imageDigestMirrors:- mirrors:- registry.example.internal/rhel8 source: registry.redhat.io/rhel8- mirrors:- registry.example.internal/rhel9 source: registry.redhat.io/rhel9 ~~~
root_cause: * Some of these images are pulled by tag (ImageStream of RHEL8 and RHEL9), so an ImageContentSourcePolicy does not redirect them, as it only redirects pulls by digest. So both ImageTagMirrorSet and ImageDigestMirrorSet are needed instead of the older (deprecated) ImageContentSourcePolicy.

title: Some virtual machines that used to work are invalid with RHEL 9 and newer hypervisors
product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux for x86_64
issue: - Virtual machines based on the pc-i440fx-rhel7.0.0 machine type will not run as Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) version 9 and newer guests. RHEL 9 supports the pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0 machine type.- RHEL 10 introduces a new pc-i440fx-rhel10.0.0 machine type and removes support for all other i440fx machine types.- Future RHEL versions might not support **any*

i440fx machine type.- Virtual machines with SPICE consoles and/or QXL video drivers also will not run as RHEL 9 and newer guests.- [Bugzilla 2172676](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2172676) tracks official documentation improvements.
resolution: - For virtual machine configurations that RHEL 9 and newer no longer supports, perform the virtual equivalent of pulling the hard drive from an old computer and connecting it to a new computer.- Rename or remove the old virtual machine. **Important: Make sure to preserve the virtual disk image.**- Provision a new virtual machine based on the q35 chip-set and supported console with the same name as the old virtual machine.- Attach the preserved virtual disk image to the new virtual machine.- Boot the new virtual machine and make appropriate adjustments for new virtual hardware from inside the new virtual machine.- With RHEL 9, instead of provisioning a new virtual machine, it may be possible to edit a pc-i440fx-rhel7.0.0 virtual machine to change its machine type to pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0, change its console from SPICE to VNC, and remove now-obsolete references to the QXL video driver.- If successful, the edited virtual machine should work for the RHEL 9 lifecycle.- But pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0 virtual machines will not run with RHEL 10 and future RHEL versions.- The procedure will be tedious, prone to errors, and only delays the inevitable.- For RHEL 10, it may be possible to similarly edit a virtual machine to change its machine type to pc-i440fx-rhel10.0.0.- Future-proof new virtual machines by provisioning them to emulate the q35 chip-set with VNC consoles.
root_cause: - Intel first released the i440fx chip-set in 1996. It offered PCI bus support. Virtual machines have emulated that chip-set since the dawn of x86 virtualization.- Intel released the q35 chip-set in 2007, with support for the faster and more functional PCIe bus. Virtual machines soon offered a choice between emulating the i440fx or q35 chip-sets.- To support virtual machines, RHEL 7 bundled a KVM version named qemu-kvm-1.5.3. This supported an i440fx machine type named pc-i440fx-rhel7.0.0.- RHV and Openstack versions based on RHEL 7 used a more advanced KVM version named qemu-kvm-rhev. This supported an i440fx machine type named pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0.- By 2022, modern operating systems supported q35 and the PCIe bus. Support for i440fx and the now-obsolete PCI bus continues to decline.- As physical machine architectures evolve, virtual machine architectures evolve with them. RHEL 9 and newer defaults to q35 based virtual machines.- RHEL 9 removed support for virtual machines with the pc-i440fx-rhel7.0.0 machine type. They will not run as RHEL 9 guests.- RHEL 9 still supports pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0 machine types.- RHEL 10 removes pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0 and adds pc-i440fx-rhel10.0.0.- A future RHEL version will remove support for **all** i440fx machine types.- Openstack 17 and 18, based on RHEL 9, deprecates all i440fx support. But i440fx-rhel7.6.0 will still work with RHEL 9 compute nodes. RHEL 10 compute nodes may also support i440fx-rhel10.0.0. A future version will remove all i440fx support. See [bugzilla 1946898.](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1946898)- Openshift Virtualization does not support any version of the i440fx machine type, but may offer a method to create or import i440fx virtual machines. Contact Red Hat Product Management for more.- RHEL 9 also removed virtual machine support for SPICE consoles and QXL video drivers.- Virtualization environments based on RHEL depend on RHEL support constraints. For future virtual machine support details, see the [Release Notes for the appropriate future RHEL version.](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/)

title: Degraded performance due to tx dropped packets on bond device
issue: - Last week we migrated the services from a OpenShift cluster running Vmware with NSX to a new cluster as Bare-Metal. The application config is the same and the network ingress is also the same, using ingress controllers for HTTP, terminated as NodePort. The clients is communicating over a Layer 4 Load Balancer (F5 BigIP). In the application we see from 4x to 10x higher latency on components. And it looks like we have a lot of out-of-order tcp packages and tx dropped packets.
resolution: - Use ethtool to disable `rx-gro-hw` on all of the bonding devices. e.g: ~~~ # ethtool-K ens3f0np0 rx-gro-hw off # ethtool-K ens3f0np1 rx-gro-hw off ~~~ To make persistent see: [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2127401](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2127401)
root_cause: - This tracked was down to the ethtool offloading option `rx-gro-hw` on the bnxt_en NICs: ~~~ This requests that the NIC enables Hardware GRO (generic receive offload). Hardware GRO is basically the exact reverse of TSO, and is generally stricter than Hardware LRO. A packet stream merged by Hardware GRO must be re-segmentable by GSO or TSO back to the exact original packet stream. Hardware GRO is dependent on RXCSUM since every packet successfully merged by hardware must also have the checksum verified by hardware. ~~~- Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 is missing some upstream commits that facilitate ` rx-gro-hw ` that exist in upstream. Red Hat are working to to determine which commit fixed this.

title: Error when upgrading the cluster: "ImagePullBackOff: error creating read-write layer with ID * no such file or directory"
issue: While upgrading a cluster, a node fails to pull images. Its Machine Config Daemon pod shows an error like the following: ~~~ error creating read-write layer with ID "4372a0c382584d7752da058c5267d1d652d727585457a71c5ef3d4d17a951719": Stat /var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/27abd31f77c1e21b8897140edb61d1e52d48a3cd287c03796dbecb54684871d3: no such file or directory ~~~ Due to the latter, the upgrade job becomes blocked. The problem can happen on several nodes in a row.
resolution: - The issue happens due to a problem in CRI-O image layer handling, which is documented in bug [OCPBUGS-16874](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-16874).- Upgrade to OCP 4.13, or OCP 4.12.45 or later to avoid this issue. Note that if you have experienced this issue, you must perform the below steps to wipe all CRI-O storage to clear the condition regardless of whether the node was successfully upgraded; it must be wiped at least once to clear the condition.- If a cluster is affected, the following workaround can be applied to solve the problem:- Drain the node ~~~ $ oc adm drain--ignore-daemonsets--delete-emptydir-data ${NODE} ~~~- In the node affected, run the following commands as root: ~~~ $ systemctl disable kubelet $ systemctl disable crio $ reboot ~~~- After the reboot, execute the following commands also as root user: ~~~ $ rm-rf /var/lib/containers/* $ crio wipe-f $ systemctl enable--now crio $ systemctl enable--now kubelet ~~~- Uncordon the node ~~~ $ oc adm uncordon $NODE ~~~
root_cause: - An issue regarding how container storage handles layers was fixed and merged into CRI-O as of OCP 4.12.45.- As CRI-O utilizes a shared container storage package, the fixes can be seen in the `containers/storage` package which were then imported into CRI-O as of OCP 4.12.45 or later.- https://github.com/containers/storage/pull/1138- https://github.com/containers/storage/pull/1407- Prior to these versions, layer handling could potentially be mishandled, causing errors when reading or accessing container image layer directories.

title: Difference between default system-reserved and reservedSystemCPU in RHOCP4
issue: - What is the difference between default system-reserved CPU configuration by OCP automatically and reservedSystem CPU configuration by kubeletconfig using Performance addon opearator?- Which one is the correct CPU configuration for worker node of OCP cluster between system-reserved and reservedSystemCPU?
resolution: - Till Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.11, install [PAO](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/scalability_and_performance/cnf-performance-addon-operator-for-low-latency-nodes.html#installing-the-performance-addon-operator_cnf-master) in performance-addon-operator namespace from OperatorHub. Performance Addon Operator(PAO) provides the ability to enable advanced node performance tuning on a set of nodes.- Starting with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.11, OpenShift Container Platform uses the Node Tuning Operator instead of PAO to implement automatic tuning to achieve low latency performance for OpenShift Container Platform applications, so there is no need to install `Performance Addon Operator` (PAO).- [Create](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/scalability_and_performance/cnf-create-performance-profiles.html) a PerformanceProfile as below: ~~~ $ vi performance-profile.yaml apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v2 kind: PerformanceProfile... spec: cpu: isolated: 2-3 reserved: 0-1 globallyDisableIrqLoadBalancing: true... ~~~- After creating above PerformanceProfile, Below can be seen from node description: ~~~ $ oc describe node... Capacity: cpu: 4 ephemeral-storage: 41407468Ki hugepages-1Gi: 0 hugepages-2Mi: 0 memory: 8151808Ki pods: 250 Allocatable: cpu: 2 ephemeral-storage: 41407468Ki hugepages-1Gi: 0 hugepages-2Mi: 0 memory: 7025408Ki pods: 250... ~~~- Below can be verified from the worker node where changes are applied: ~~~ $ ssh worker-0.example.com $ ps-ef |grep reserved root 1673 1 8 04:04? 00:00:55 kubelet--config=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf--bootstrap- kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig--kubeconfig=/var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig--container-runtime=remote--container-runtime-endpoint=/var/run/crio/crio.sock--runtime-cgroups=/system.slice/crio.service--node-labels=node-role.kubernetes.io/worker,node.openshift.io/os_id=rhcos--node-ip=10.10.92.130--minimum-container-ttl-duration=6m0s--volume-plugin-dir=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet-plugins/volume/exec--cloud-provider=--pod-infra-container-image=quay.io/openshift-release- dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:2c5dfd9e71d5feea4473d65499c4e96721071af446debf6d28d2c3067c46b62c--system-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=500Mi--v=2 ~~~- Now create a custom [kubeletconfig](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-managing.html) specifying resources as below: ~~~ $ vi custom-kubeletconfig.yaml... spec: machineConfigPoolSelector: matchLabels: custom-kubelet: enabled kubeletConfig: systemReserved: cpu: 1000m memory: 1Gi... ~~~- After applying above resource, Node description changes as below: ~~~ $ oc describe node worker-0.example.com... Capacity: cpu: 4 ephemeral-storage: 41407468Ki hugepages-1Gi: 0 hugepages-2Mi: 0 memory: 8151816Ki pods: 250 Allocatable: cpu: 3 ephemeral-storage: 38161122446 hugepages-1Gi: 0 hugepages-2Mi: 0 memory: 7000840Ki pods: 250... ~~~- This can also be verified from login into worker node and checking as below: ~~~ $ ps-ef |grep reserved root 1640 1 6 04:33? 00:00:15 kubelet--config=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf--bootstrap-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig--kubeconfig=/var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig--container-runtime=remote--container-runtime-endpoint=/var/run/crio/crio.sock--runtime-cgroups=/system.slice/crio.service--node-labels=node-role.kubernetes.io/worker,node.openshift.io/os_id=rhcos--node-ip=10.10.92.130--minimum-container-ttl-duration=6m0s--volume-plugin-dir=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet-plugins/volume/exec--cloud-provider=--pod-infra-container-image=quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:2c5dfd9e71d5feea4473d65499c4e96721071af446debf6d28d2c3067c46b62c--system-reserved=cpu=1000m,memory=1Gi--v=2 ~~~- As observed changes from```--system-reserved=cpu=500m``` to ```--system-reserved=cpu=1000m``` and reservedSystemCPUs is not in action anymore. Conclusion: The reservedSystemCPUs option specifies the CPU list reserved for the host level system threads and kubernetes related threads and any CPUs specifically reserved using the reservedSystemCPU parameter are not available for allocation using kube-reserved or system-reserved.
root_cause: - **systemreserved:** This setting is used in default by OpenShift Container Platform to automatically configure optimal CPUs for kubelet/crio related to OCP cluster node.- **reservedSystemCPU**: This is used to explicitly select CPU cores for Openshift specific workloads [Ex. Pods, Containers, Applications, Infra Containers etc.] PerformanceProfiles using Performance addon operator is used to configure these setting for different workload in OCP cluster.

title: Conflicting titles for compliance rules: ip-whitelist & rate-limit
issue: The compliance operator includes two rules: **ocp4-route-ip-whitelist*
and **ocp4-routes-rate-limit**. It is observed that both have same title: `Ensure that all Routes has rate limit enabled`. This title is misleading in the compliance scan report.
resolution: - This was a known Bug [CMP-2485](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CMP-2485), and has been resolved in `Compliance Operator v1.6.0`.- Below are the updated titles of these compliance rules: ~~~ $ oc get rules.compliance.openshift.io ocp4-routes-rate-limit-oyaml | grep title title: Ensure that all Routes has rate limit enabled ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get rules.compliance.openshift.io ocp4-route-ip-whitelist-oyaml | grep title title: Ensure that all Routes has IP whitelist annotation ~~~

title: The token value and oauthaccesstoken name doesn't match
issue: Requested the token from https://oauth-openshift.apps. /oauth/token/request
The token value and oauthaccesstoken name doesn't match
There is no matched oauthaccesstoken by running `oc get oauthaccesstoken`
resolution: * This is expected behaivor. The token firstly is encrypted by golang SHA256 and then hashed by golang base64 library. * To convert the token to `oauthaccesstoken`, ``` $ echo-n IATOnLp0Zl4YGm0uJxMF3cb3nWcM_rKtgHpjCginUwQ | openssl dgst-sha256-binary | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr-d '=' cLsXrCZSuHALJ3s3uqZA1sYqXBC5AikiJYERk9MWX7k ```

title: The udev rules fails to rename the interfaces `systemd-udevd[...]: could not rename interface '2' from 'ens192' to 'ens224': File exists`
issue: - Losing the custom network interface name after rebooting- The udev rules fails to rename the interfaces- systemd-udevd[...]: could not rename interface '2' from 'ens192' to 'ens224': File exists
resolution: In the example below, we assume that the administrator wants to rename 2 interfaces based on their PCI path. ### Solution 1- ensure the udev rules are embedded in the initramfs image Ensure that the udev rules have to be embedded in the initramfs, otherwise the renaming may not happen if the device is used or got renamed already.- Check that the rule is present in the `/etc/udev/rules.d/` directory ```bash # cat /etc/udev/rules.d/70-persistent-net.rules SUBSYSTEM=="net",ACTION=="add",KERNEL=="eth*",SUBSYSTEMS=="pci",KERNELS=="0000:0b:00.0",NAME="ens224" SUBSYSTEM=="net",ACTION=="add",KERNEL=="eth*",SUBSYSTEMS=="pci",KERNELS=="0000:13:00.0",NAME="ens192" ```- Create a `.conf` file in `/etc/dracut.conf.d/` to include the rule in the initramfs disk ```bash # cat /etc/dracut.conf.d/custom_net.conf install_items+=" /etc/udev/rules.d/70-persistent-net.rules " ```- Regenerate the initramfs image ```bash # dracut--regenerate-all-fv ```- Confirm the file is present in the initramfs image ``` # lsinitrd | grep-E '70-per'-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 204 Sep 20 2021 etc/udev/rules.d/70-persistent-net.rules ``` ### Solution 2 (recommended)- use the "systemd.link" functionality Use a different method than *udev* rules. Use the `systemd.link(5)` method to rename the interfaces: ```bash # man systemd.link | grep-E ' Example 3'-A9 Example 3. /etc/systemd/network/10-internet.link This example assigns the fixed name "internet0" to the interface with the device path "pci-0000:00:1a.0-*": [Match] Path=pci-0000:00:1a.0-* [Link] Name=internet0 ```- Remove the udev rules if present ```bash # rm /etc/udev/rules.d/70-persistent-net.rules ```- Create a directory `network` in `/etc/systemd/` ```bash # mkdir /etc/systemd/network ```- Create the files `.link` for each interface to be renamed ```bash # cat > /etc/systemd/network/01-ens224.link < < EOF [Match] Path=pci-0000:0b:00.0 [Link] Name=ens224 EOF ``` ```bash # cat > /etc/systemd/network/01-ens192.link < < EOF [Match] Path=pci-0000:13:00.0 [Link] Name=ens192 EOF ```- Regenerate the initramfs image ```bash # dracut--regenerate-all-fv ```- Confirm the files are embedded in the initramfs image ``` # lsinitrd | grep-E '01-ens'-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 50 Sep 20 2021 etc/systemd/network/01-ens192.link-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 50 Sep 20 2021 etc/systemd/network/01-ens224.link ```
root_cause: Ensure that the udev rules have to be embedded in the initramfs, otherwise the renaming may not happen if the device is used or got renamed already. The error message `systemd-udevd[984]: could not rename interface '2' from 'ens192' to 'ens224': File exists` suggests that systemd and udev are unable to handle naming collisions. In this specific case, the system cannot rename `ens192` to `ens224` if another existing interface already bears the same name. Indeed, the interface had already been renamed during the initialization stage. Please see also the following articles:- [How to assign a specific network interface name in RHEL 7, 8, 9](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1301563)- [NICs have the wrong MAC address and "systemd-udevd: error changing net interface name ethX to ethY: File exists" error is seen in the logs](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1422203)

title: Security alerts on Vector generating checkpoints.json file in /var/lib/vector/ directory
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - As part of `Vector` `daemontset` deployment a file named `checkpoints.json` under `/var/lib/vector/` directory was created. Security scanners generating security alerts because of this file.- The file has `data_dir` configurations as: ~~~ name: datadir mountPath: /var/lib/vector/lgim-pe-logging/vector ~~~
resolution: - The `/var/lib/vector/` is default directory for `Vector (data_dir parameter)` and it is perfectly normal to have `Vector` write files into this particular location. Security alerts regarding `Vector` generating `checkpoints.json` file can be ignored.
root_cause: - When using `Vector` on `OpenShift` clusters. The `data_dir` global configuration parameter is responsible for the directory used for persisting `Vector` state, such as `on-disk buffers`, `file checkpoints`, and more. `Vector` project need write permissions to this directory and `/var/lib/vector` is the default directory in use.

title: Can raw_message be enabled in vector.toml in RHOCP 4?
issue: _**Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._

Can [raw_message](https://vector.dev/docs/reference/configuration/sinks/loki/#encoding.codec) be enabled in the `vector.toml` in the Red Hat Logging solution to reduce size of logs and overall storage consumption? ~~~ [sinks.default_loki_apps.encoding] codec = "raw_message" ~~~
resolution: Below is the reduced metadata (compared to default) that was observed when raw_message was enabled in `vector.toml` via the unsupported method for testing. [image=[src="images/2024-08-05_raw_message.png", title="Raw_message_enabled_unsupported ", alt="Raw_message_enabled_unsupported ", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="Raw_message_enabled_unsupported ", lightbox="true"]] As editing `vector.toml` is not supported by Red Hat, to reduce the overall size of log entry below filtering can be done: ~~~ # oc edit clf-n openshift-logging ``` spec: filters:- name: test-filter prune: notIn:-.log_type-.message- @timestamp type: prune pipelines:- filterRefs:- test-filter inputRefs:- infrastructure- application name: app-pipeline outputRefs:- default ``` ~~~ Below is the reduced metadata after adding the above filter: [image=[src="images/2024-08-05_test-filter_setup.png", title="Test_filter_added_via_supported_method ", alt="Test_filter_added_via_supported_method ", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="Test_filter_added_via_supported_method ", lightbox="true"]] **Observation** If the log store is the Red Hat Managed Log store, the "OpenShift Console > Observe > Logs" could not show any log. See article "[Log filter doesn't work if the labelKeys referenced doesn't exist in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7101353)" for all the details.
root_cause: The `raw_data` option for Vector is not exposed in the API to be modified and any manual modification to the `vector.toml` will be overwrite by the Red Hat OpenShift Logging operator if the Custom Resource (CR) is in `Managed` status.

title: Missing Jolokia agent in UBI8 OpenJDK 17 and UBI9 images
issue: Jolokia is absent in ubi8/openjdk-17 (also missing in runtime)- however it was present on former OpenJDK versions.
Missing `jmx-export` in openjdk ubi9 images.
resolution: This is not a mistake. The Jolokia agent was removed from ubi8/openjdk 17 and ubi9. ### Alternatives Alternatives can be add the RPM, or add copy the agent to the image. One can make a new container image based on the openjdk one. For rhel 8 user can get the jolokia package from ubi, for rhel 9 get it from upstream or some such. Version | Method--------- |--------- RHEL 8 | user can get the jolokia package from ubi RHEL 9 | user can get straight from the project upstream (Jolokia project) Example: If it's rhel8 then there's an RPM user could install: `jolokia-jvm-agent-1.6.2-3.el8.noarch`. ### For EAP image For EAP 7 Jolokia is deprecated [Deprecated in Red Hat Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) 7](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6978412). For alternatives: the EAP Management API can already be accessed via http and EAP 7.4 has `jboss-cli.sh [--output-json` in case the json is required. See solution [How to have the JBoss CLI output JSON and How to get the params needed to use the JBoss Management API via HTTP in JBoss EAP 7.2](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3486201) for more information. ### For generic (unsupported) use: Download the agent jar from the following upstream main landing page and configure the agent for HTTP, OpenTelemetry, or Combined mode: [https://prometheus.github.io/jmx_exporter/1.1.0/java-agent/](https://prometheus.github.io/jmx_exporter/1.1.0/java-agent/)
root_cause: Jolokia is an json-> jmx bridge client. Initially, the UBI8 OpenJDK containers shipped by default with two Java agents: Jolokia and Prometheus. These were included originally to support integrating metrics gathering in OpenShift. However, over time the approach for metrics and logging in OpenShift has evolved, and many of our customers did not require this functionality, and instead wanted the containers to be as lean as possible. For this reason, we no longer include either agent in the images.

title: How to make the secondary interface as a default network in OpenShift Virtualization VM?
issue: - The OpenShift Virtual Machine, which has two network interfaces consisting of a default pod interface and an additional bridge interface, cannot be reached from other networks in the environment.- The virtual machine can ping the bridge network gateway and is accessible from the servers within that network but not from any other network.- External traffic from the VM is routed through pod network instead of OVN secondary network. How to mark OVN secondary network as default route?
resolution: - Follow the procedure below to mark the secondary network as the default route while retaining traffic to the internal OCP network:- Find the cluster network address of the cluster: ~~~ # oc get network cluster-o yaml |yq '.spec.clusterNetwork,.spec.serviceNetwork'- cidr: 10.128.0.0/14 hostPrefix: 23- 172.30.0.0/16 ~~~- Remove the "pod networking" interface from the default routing configuration. Configure manual route for the pod network and OVN "join" network to forward those packets via gateway 10.0.2.1 ~~~ # nmcli con mod ipv4.never-default yes # nmcli con mod +ipv4.routes "10.128.0.0/14 10.0.2.1 90,100.64.0.0/16 10.0.2.1 90,172.30.0.0/16 10.0.2.1 90" # nmcli con up ~~~- Also, increase the priority for DNS server on pod network if both DHCP servers provide DNS servers: ~~~ # nmcli con mod 'System eth0' +ipv4.dns-priority 50 # nmcli con up ~~~
root_cause: - Refer RHEL doc, [How NetworkManager manages multiple default gateways](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html-single/configuring_and_managing_networking/index#con_how-networkmanager-manages-multiple-default-gateways_managing-the-default-gateway-setting) that explains how NetworkManager behaves when there are multiple default gateways configured.- When both offers a default gateway, the VM will have both the networks marked as default routes, but the pod network will have higher priority and will be used to route the external traffic because of the lower metric value. ~~~ default via 10.0.2.1 dev eth0 proto dhcp src 10.0.2.2 metric 100 <== pod network default via 192.168.0.1 dev eth1 proto static metric 101 <== bridge network 10.0.2.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 10.0.2.2 metric 100 192.168.0.0/24 dev eth1 proto kernel scope link src 192.168.0.13 metric 101 ~~~

title: How to increase the resource limit values for the ArgoCD application controller pod?
issue: - The ArgoCD application controller pod were killed by OOM- The ArgoCD application controller pod were in CrashLoopBackOff state due to OOM
resolution: Increase the resource gitops controller memory limits values under the controller section by executing the below patch command: ~~~ $ oc patch argocd openshift-gitops-n openshift-gitops--type json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/controller/resources/limits/memory", "value": "4Gi"}]' ~~~
root_cause: The default gitops controller resource limit of 2Gi is not enough to start the ArgoCD application controller pod. In order to initialize the pod, the gitops controller resouce limit values should be increased accordingly.

title: SRIOV-CNI failed to set vf X vlan configuration
issue: SRIOV-CNI failed to set VF vlan. The new workload that uses SR-IOV VF will fail with the following error ``` 2m48s Warning FailedCreatePodSandBox pod/sriovpod1 (combined from similar events): Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create pod network sandbox k8s_sriovpod1_test-topo-aware_86da0a19-db8d-4470-94c0-8a86008070c4_0(96b7b3a9ef1d2750412cc85d63b132320e297cedd011b220530150ac20a4a81b): error adding pod test-topo-aware_sriovpod1 to CNI network "multus-cni-network": plugin type="multus-shim" name="multus-cni-network" failed (add): CmdAdd (shim): CNI request failed with status 400: 'ContainerID:"96b7b3a9ef1d2750412cc85d63b132320e297cedd011b220530150ac20a4a81b" Netns:"/var/run/netns/17560f8d-f199-415c-af59-9df3f8ed48fc" IfName:"eth0" Args:"IgnoreUnknown=1;K8S_POD_NAMESPACE=test-topo-aware;K8S_POD_NAME=sriovpod1;K8S_POD_INFRA_CONTAINER_ID=96b7b3a9ef1d2750412cc85d63b132320e297cedd011b220530150ac20a4a81b;K8S_POD_UID=86da0a19-db8d-4470-94c0-8a86008070c4" Path:"" ERRORED: error configuring pod [test-topo-aware/sriovpod1] networking: [test-topo-aware/sriovpod1/86da0a19-db8d-4470-94c0-8a86008070c4:sriov-intel]: error adding container to network "sriov-intel": SRIOV-CNI failed to configure VF "failed to set vf 18 vlan configuration- id 100, qos 0 and proto 802.1q: invalid argument"... ```
Without setting the vlan in `net-attach-def`, there is no error

title: Troubleshooting OpenShift Container Platform 4.x: OpenShift-GitOps
issue: This article is for troubleshooting OpenShift Container Platform 4.x OpenShift GitOps only.
resolution: 1. OpenShift GitOps operator is released and maintained closely bound to the support lifecycle of the underlying OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) cluster. Support and Compatability matrix is available [here](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift_operators) 2. If Community version of the Argo CD Operator is already installed in cluster, then remove the Argo CD Community Operator before you install the Red Hat OpenShift GitOps Operator as it may cause conflicts. 2. It is not recommended to create multiple argocd instances in same namespace. This will make conflicts as mentioned [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6790471). 3. `openshift-gitops` argocd instance is the default instance that comes with the operator. Customers can either make use of this instance to create/manage cluster wide resources. Or create a new cluster-scoped argocd instance in another namespace. 4. It is not advised to create another Argo CD instance in `openshift-gitops` namespace after disabling the default instance.- As the name of the namespace implies, it's an OpenShift internal namespace and is usually `restricted`.- So, to create a new cluster scoped instance, create it in a **separate** namespace other than `openshift-gitops` namespace and use `ARGOCD_CLUSTER_CONFIG_NAMESPACES` environment variable in `subscription` object to make it cluster scoped. The process is mentioned [here](https://docs.openshift.com/gitops/1.10/declarative_clusterconfig/configuring-an-openshift-cluster-by-deploying-an-application-with-cluster-configurations.html#using-argo-cd-instance-to-manage-cluster-scoped-resourcesconfiguring-an-openshift-cluster-by-deploying-an-application-with-cluster-configurations). ~~~ apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: openshift-gitops-operator namespace: openshift-operators #... spec: config: env:- name: ARGOCD_CLUSTER_CONFIG_NAMESPACES <------ value: openshift-gitops, ~~~- It is not possible to directly modify argocd configmaps, deployments, etc as like in upstream argocd as OpenShift GitOps reverts that changes to default. To make any such changes, argocd custom resource needs to be modified as mentioned [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970884) **OpenShift GitOps FAQ** 5. How to Add a Local User in OpenShift GitOps?- The steps are documented in [KCS 1](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7027020) and [KCS 2](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6637881) 6. Is it necessary to keep the default argocd instance(openshift-gitops) that gets created with the operator?- This depends on customer's requirements. The argocd instance running in `openshift-gitops` namespace is cluster scoped instance. One benefit of using this instance as it comes with the operator itself, we can [move the workloads to infra nodes](https://docs.openshift.com/gitops/1.10/gitops_workloads_infranodes/run-gitops-control-plane-workload-on-infra-nodes.html) to prevent additional billing cost against subscription counts. Any other Argo CD instances installed to user namespaces are not eligible to run on infrastructure nodes. To disable the default argocd instance, use the `DISABLE_DEFAULT_ARGOCD_INSTANCE ENV` variable in subscription object.- If disabling the default instance, then customer needs to create a separate cluster-scoped argocd instance in-order to manage cluster scoped resources if any: ~~~ apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: openshift-gitops-operator namespace: openshift-operators #... spec: config: env:- name: DISABLE_DEFAULT_ARGOCD_INSTANCE <--- value: 'true'- name: ARGOCD_CLUSTER_CONFIG_NAMESPACES <--- value: ~~~ 7. Do customers need to install a separate ArgoCD instance for every namespace?- This also depends on customer's requirements. This usually comes in play if the Admins want to restrict the Application team or any other users to create/manage cluster scoped resources. By default, any new argocd instance has permissions to manage resources only in the namespace where it is deployed. Please refer our [Official Documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/gitops/1.10/argocd_instance/setting-up-argocd-instance.html) for more information. 8. How to migrate from Argo CD Community Operator to Openshift GitOps Operator?- The migration guide is available [here](https://github.com/redhat-developer/gitops-operator/blob/master/docs/Migration_Guide.md). However, we strongly recommend customers to test the procedure first in Test environment and take necessary backups as needed. *Disclaimer: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products, or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*

title: Wrong hostname node after agent based installation in RHOCP 4
issue: - The hostname of one of the node is wrong.- The hostname of one of the node is wrong irrespective of correctly install-config.yml and agent-config.yml.
resolution: Verify the `macAddress` information is correct in the `agent-config.yaml` file used for the installation.
root_cause: Agent based installation uses the mac-address of the nodes to identify their hostnames. It produces the script `/usr/local/bin/set-hostname.sh` and the directory `/etc/assisted/hostnames` containing the hostnames of all the nodes taken from the `agent-config.yaml` in the iso image. If there is any mis-match with the mac-address the script `/usr/local/bin/set-hostname.sh` is not able to understand which hostname to configure.

title: renewing the central-db certificate
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: The customer's **4.1.2*
Central pod was in *CrashLoopBackOff

with the logs showing the error message of ``` Migrator: 2024/08/05 16:12:47.429286 log.go:18: Info: Migrator failed: failed to scan clones: failed to connect to `host=central-db.stackrox.svc user=postgres database=postgres`: failed to write startup message (tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2024-08-05T16:12:47Z is after 2024-08-03T21:57:02Z) ``` The customer had installed and upgraded the product via Helm.
resolution: 1- First find the name of the Helm installation (assuming the namespace is stackrox). ``` ❯ helm-n stackrox list NAME NAMESPACE REVISION UPDATED STATUS CHART APP VERSION stackrox-central-services stackrox 1 2024-08-12 17:30:05.682098 +0200 CEST deployed stackrox-central-services-400.1.2 4.1.2 ``` From here on we assume that the name of Helm installation is `stackrox-central-services`, in the namespace `stackrox`, version `400.1.2`. 2- Run the following: ``` # get root ca caKey=$(kubectl-n stackrox get secret central-tls-o go-template='{{index.data "ca-key.pem"}}' | base64--decode) caPem=$(kubectl-n stackrox get secret central-tls-o go-template='{{index.data "ca.pem"}}' | base64--decode) # create root certificates value file yq e-n ".ca.cert = \"${caPem}\" |.ca.key = \"${caKey}\"" > extracted_private_values.yaml helm template-n stackrox stackrox-central-services rhacs/central-services--version 400.1.2 \--set central.db.serviceTLS.generate=true \--set central.persistence.none=true \-f extracted_private_values.yaml > newly_generated.yaml # extract the secret from `newly_generated.yaml`, either manually or with: awk '/# Source: stackrox-central-services\/templates\/01-central-05-db-tls-secret.yaml/,/^---/' newly_generated.yaml > central-db-tls-secret.yaml # apply the secret to the cluster kubectl apply-f central-db-tls-secret.yaml # finally restart the central-db deployment: kubectl-n stackrox scale deployment central-db--replicas=0 kubectl-n stackrox scale deployment central-db--replicas=1 ```

title: Users unable to access the system via SSH due to insufficient entropy
issue: - The server is running, but `SSH` connection attempts are **hanging*

due to insufficient entropy: ~~~ SSH Client: # ping-c2 test.example.com PING test.example.com (10.0.0.34) 56(84) bytes of data. 64 bytes from 10.0.0.34: icmp_seq=1 ttl=60 time=50.2 ms 64 bytes from 10.0.0.34: icmp_seq=2 ttl=60 time=58.6 ms--- test.example.com ping statistics--- 2 packets transmitted, 2 received, 0% packet loss, time 1001ms rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 50.176/54.403/58.631/4.227 ms # ssh 10.0.0.34-v OpenSSH_9.0p1, OpenSSL 3.0.9 30 May 2023 debug1: Reading configuration data /etc/ssh/ssh_config debug1: Reading configuration data /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/50-redhat.conf debug1: Reading configuration data /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/openssh.config.. debug1: Connection established. debug1: Local version string SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.0 (connection hangs) SSH Server: # for i in `pidof sshd`; do egrep "Name|^Pid" /proc/$i/status; cat /proc/$i/stack; done Name: sshd Pid: 30133 [<0>]_random_read.part.30+0x314/0x390 [<0>] do_syscall_64+0x5b/0x1a0 [<0>] entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x66/0xcb ~~~
resolution: - Enable and start the `rngd` service: ~~~ # systemctl enable rngd.service--now ~~~- Check the status of the `rngd` service: ~~~ # systemctl status rngd.service ~~~ *Note:* If the `rngd` service fails to start, then try the method suggested in the article: [7050211](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7050211 "")
root_cause: - The SSH connection hung due to insufficient entropy and the inactive `rngd` service. The SSH process was waiting for more entropy to generate secure keys but couldn't continue because the entropy level was too low. Moreover, SSH was configured to use a strong random number generator, which requires a higher amount of entropy.

title: How to create custom Jboss Image with Oracle JDK
issue: - How to create custom Jboss Image with Oracle JDK in Openshift.
resolution: Red Hat only supports the images it provides/builds/ships, so the resulting image will NOT be supported. Red Hat does not support docker as well. One can set alternatives in the Dockerfile which will work but one would need to add and set them separately, and also set both java and javac. The alternatives command will only work as root and the default user in our jboss images is 185. Below is an example that can be used (note: the oracle java version is slightly different) ~~~ FROM jboss-eap-6/eap64-openshift:1.2 ADD jdk-8u65-linux-x64.tar.gz /usr/lib/jvm/ USER root RUN /usr/sbin/alternatives--install "/usr/bin/java" java "/usr/lib/jvm/jdk1.8.0_65/bin/java" 1 RUN /usr/sbin/alternatives--set "java" "/usr/lib/jvm/jdk1.8.0_65/bin/java" RUN /usr/sbin/alternatives--install "/usr/bin/javac" javac "/usr/lib/jvm/jdk1.8.0_65/bin/javac" 1 RUN /usr/sbin/alternatives--set "javac" "/usr/lib/jvm/jdk1.8.0_65/bin/javac" ENV JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jdk1.8.0_65" \ JAVA_VENDOR="Oracle" \ JAVA_VERSION="1.8.0" USER 185 ~~~ Build the image: ~~~ docker build-t jboss. ~~~ Check the java version after docker run: ~~~ docker run-i-t jboss:latest java-version Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS:-Duser.home=/home/jboss-Duser.name=jboss java version "1.8.0_65" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_65-b17) Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.65-b01, mixed mode) ~~~

title: How are JBoss Products supported when used in container images?
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - What level of support can I expect when creating my own container images with JBoss products?- Which container formats and runtimes are supported for JBoss products?- Can I use existing Container images to build our own images?
resolution: Red Hat provides customers with JBoss Middleware products as containerized images specifically for use with OpenShift Container Platform. Red Hat JBoss Middleware for OpenShift containerized images are designed, built and tested to enable developers a stable and supported path to quick-start building and deploying applications. These container images are supplied with usage documentation and supported on various OpenShift Container Platform versions, as noted on their respective release notes. Customers may have a requirement to create and maintain their own container images that include JBoss Middleware products. Red Hat treats custom-built images as 'custom software' and will not provide support for the resulting images themselves, but rather the JBoss Middleware products included as part of the images, as long as the images are built using components that comply with the [Supported Configuration Page](https://access.redhat.com/support/configurations/jboss), in coordination with [Red Hat's Container Support Policy](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2726611). Taking into consideration that such custom images have not been delivered as part of a product release by Red Hat, customers should be aware that they may be asked to reproduce an issue outside of a containerized context to receive the necessary level support for JBoss Middleware components. This practice applies to custom image usage on or off the OpenShift Container Platform. ### **FAQ:** **Q1:** Am I supported running the Red Hat JBoss Middleware for OpenShift containerized images provided by Red Hat in a container environment other than OpenShift? **A1:** No. The container images Red Hat ships as part of the product ‘Red Hat JBoss Middleware for OpenShift’ are only tested and supported for running on OpenShift, such as JBoss EAP 7/8. **Q2:** Am I supported running JBoss Middleware products in runC, Docker, rkt, or other container engines? **A2:** All Red Hat JBoss Middleware for OpenShift products in active development provide containerized images designed for and tested with OpenShift 3 and 4. Red Hat does not provide JBoss Middleware for OpenShift containers to run on any other container platforms. Customers are free to create and maintain their own containers for JBoss Middleware products for other container engines, but Red Hat can only provide [commercially reasonable support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/710953) for those environments. **Q3:** If I have created a custom container image and have an issue, am I required to reproduce this outside of a container environment? **A3:** Red Hat provides full support to the Openshift images it builds and ships via the official registry, not necessarily custom images. Therefore given a problem that also happens with the official images, it is not necessarily required as part of the troubleshooting process. However, it could be useful in some scenarios to test nonetheless, so it will be a case by cases, depending on the customization.--- ## Related Articles For further information and policies about JBoss Middleware Containers, please see the following articles: **[JBoss Middleware Container Support FAQ](https://access.redhat.com/node/3052431)** **[Support of Red Hat Middleware products and components on Red Hat OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5115291)** **[Support for Red Hat JBoss Middleware Containers](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1495513)** **[Support Guidelines for Red Hat Middleware Products Deployed in 3rd-party Environments](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4292501)**---

title: How to allow pods to reference images across projects?
issue: - How to allow pods to reference images across projects?
resolution: `**Procedure:**`- To allow `pods` in project-a to reference `images` in project-b, bind a `service account` in project-a to the `system:image-puller` role in project-b: ~~~ $ oc policy add-role-to-user \ system:image-puller system:serviceaccount:project-a:default \--namespace=project-b ~~~- After adding that `role`, the `pods` in project-a that reference the `default service account` are able to pull `images` from project-b.- To allow access for any `service account` in project-a, use the group: ~~~ $ oc policy add-role-to-group \ system:image-puller system:serviceaccounts:project-a \--namespace=project-b ~~~- This procedure should be repeated for all the `namespaces`, as configuring global `secrets` referencing `images` across all namespaces is not possible.
root_cause: - When using the `internal registry`, to allow `pods` in project-a to reference `images` in project-b, a `service account` in project-a must be bound to the system:image-puller role in project-b.

title: What does it mean non common channels at the Operator Update Information Checker ?
issue: - What does it mean "non common channel" at the result of the checker?- You can see the "Show non common channels" at the below image.![checker_results](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/checker_noncommon.png)
resolution: - "non common channels" means that the channels are existing only for the specified OCP version index, not existing another ones.- For example, if the "stable-4.17" channel of an operator is existing only as of OCPv4.17 index, but the channel did not exist in the OCPv4.16 index. Then the "stable-4.17" channel will be evaluated as "non common channels" at the update information checker results.
root_cause: - [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Operator Update Information Checker](https://access.redhat.com/labs/ocpouic/) shows us the results based on [audit-tool index eus](https://github.com/operator-framework/audit/tree/main) command results.- The command creates a report of possible upgrade paths (bundle versions, channels) from one OCP EUS version to another.

resolution: **Create `ContainerRuntimeConfig(ctrcfg)` to patch the maximum PIDs in order to avoid the exhaustion limit.**- Create a `ctrcfg`in the Openshift nodes: **Note:** you must specify a label under matchLabels (custom-crio in this example) ~~~ pid-limits.yaml: apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: ContainerRuntimeConfig metadata: name: set-pids-limit spec: machineConfigPoolSelector: matchLabels: custom-crio: pid-limit-modified containerRuntimeConfig: pidsLimit: 2048 ~~~- Add the label to the `machineconfigpool` desired to be patched: ~~~ $ oc label machineconfigpool worker custom-crio=pid-limit-modified ~~~- Apply the `ctrcfg` in the cluster: ~~~ $ oc create-f pid-limits.yaml ~~~- Check the objects created: ~~~ $ oc get ctrcfg NAME AGE set-pids-limit 2m ~~~- Ensure new `machineconfigs` created correctly and applied on the nodes: ~~~ $ oc get machineconfigs NAME GENERATEDBYCONTROLLER IGNITIONVERSION AGE 99-worker-containerrunetime-managed asdf5f32273b24sdns7f235nss043532 3.1.0 1m ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get mcp NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE worker rendered-worker-test True False False 3 3 3 0 5m ~~~ **OR**, **Modify the exiting `ContainerRuntimeConfig(ctrcfg)` file to increase the PIDs limit**- Check `ContainerRuntimeConfig` object on the cluster. ~~~ $ oc get ContainerRuntimeConfig NAME AGE set-pids-limit 2m ~~~- Check the associated `machineconfig` object: ~~~ $ oc get mc |grep-i container ~~~- Modify the `pidsLimit` in `ContainerRuntimeConfig` object. ~~~ $ oc edit ContainerRuntimeConfig set-pids-limit: spec: containerRuntimeConfig: pidsLimit: 4096 <--------------- Change this value to desire one ~~~- Ensure that changes rollout on all the nodes. ~~~ $ oc get mcp NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE worker rendered-worker-xxxx True False False 3 3 3 0 23d ~~~ **Verify `pids_limit` on nodes after following any of the above section:** ~~~ $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host # crio-status config | grep pids_limit ~~~ **Note**: Setting the PIDs limit in the `ContainerRuntimeConfig` is expected to be deprecated from OpenShift 4.11 onward. If PIDs limits are required, it is recommended to use the `podPidsLimit` field in the `KubeletConfig` CR instead. To update the `podPidsLimit` using `KubeletConfig` follow KCS [How to change the value of pids_limit in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5366631)
root_cause: - CRI-O default `PID` limit is `1024` but may need to be increased on heavily trafficked nodes/clusters. ~~~ # crio--help | grep pids--pids-limit value Maximum number of processes allowed in a container (default: 1024) ~~~

title: Deleting elasticsearch CR errors when not installed Elasticsearch Operator in RHOCP4
issue: When only installed the ClusterLogging Operator (CLO) for log forwarding the logs to external outputs, the CLO operator returns continually the error log: ~~~ $ oc logs $(oc get pod-l name=cluster-logging-operator-o name) |grep "Failure deleting elasticsearch elasticsearch CR" |head-1 {"_ts":"2023-03-13T09:13:10.794416893Z","_level":"0","_component":"cluster-logging-operator","_message":"Error removing component","_error":{"msg":"Failure deleting elasticsearch elasticsearch CR for \"instance\": no matches for kind \"Elasticsearch\" in version \"logging.openshift.io/v1\""}} ~~~
When only installed the CLO since not needed the Elasticsearch Operator (EO), the CLO pod is throwing the error `"Failure deleting elasticsearch elasticsearch CR"`
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [LOG-3763](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-3763) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.6.4 through errata [RHBA-2023:1311](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:1311). If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. ####Workaround For the command below, take into consideration that it could be needed to change the version `release-5.6` for adapting to the RHOL version impacted with this issue: ~~~ $ oc create-f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openshift/elasticsearch-operator/release-5.6/bundle/manifests/logging.openshift.io_elasticsearches.yaml ~~~ **NOTE** Once the fix is available, the `Elasticsearch CR` can be removed in case not needed: ~~~ $ oc delete CustomResourceDefinition elasticsearches.logging.openshift.io ~~~
root_cause: The CLO has coded a dependency with the EO that shouldn't exist as it's supported to have only installed the CLO for log forwarding the logs to a non-Red Hat Managed Log Store: Elasticsearch.

title: How to modify etcd logLevel verbosity in OpenShift 4?
issue: - How to modify the etcd logs verbositiy in RHOCP 4?- How to modify etcd `logLevel` in OpenShift 4?
resolution: It is possible to configure the verbosity of the etcd components via the `etcd` operator resource, setting the `spec.logLevel` field, and the `spec.operatorLogLevel` field for the verbosity of the operator itself (replace the `${LOGLEVEL}` with the desired log level). > **Note:** setting the verbosity to a higher value will create more logs, so it is recommended to restore the values to `Normal` after the required logs were collected. Commands to configure the log verbosity for etcd: ~~~ $ oc patch etcd.operator/cluster--type=json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/logLevel", "value": "${LOGLEVEL}"}]' ~~~ ~~~ $ oc patch etcd.operator/cluster--type=json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/operatorLogLevel", "value": "${LOGLEVEL}"}]' ~~~ Valid log level values are `Normal`, `Debug`, `Trace` and `TraceAll`. Default value is `Normal`. > **Important:** Note that changing the `loglevel` will restart the etcd Pods in a rolling fashion. Changing the `operatorLogLevel` should not restart any component.
root_cause: In OpenShift 4, the etcd is managed by an operator, so in order to change its log level, it is necessary to modify the correct fields in the `etcd` operator resource.

title: OpenShift Data Foundation odf-console plugin doesn't work as expected on OpenShift
issue: - `Openshift Data Foundation odf-console` plugin doesn't work as expected, and can't create `Storage System` via console
resolution: 1. Make the pod networking for the `OpenShift Data Foundation` project global: ~~~ $ oc adm pod-network make-projects-global openshift-storage ~~~ 2. Check the `netnamespace` is global, `NETID` is set to 0: ~~~ $ oc describe netnamespace openshift-storage Name: openshift-storage Created: 46 minutes ago Labels: Name: openshift-storage ID: 0 Egress IPs: ~~~
root_cause: - When `Openshift SDN` is installed as `openshift-ovs-multitenant`, the `openshift-console` and `openshift-console` namespaces don't communicate with each other by default, this configuration needs to be set. The `OpenShift` console pod in the `openshift-console` namespace needs to connect to the `OpenShift Data Foundation odf-console` in the `openshift-storage` namespace. It is documented in the [Troubleshooting section](https://docs.redhat.com/pt-br/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.16/html-single/troubleshooting_openshift_data_foundation/index#accessing-odf-console-with-ovs-multitenant-plugin-by-manually-enabling-global-pod-networking_rhodf)

title: Unable to snapshot Virtual Machine with SentinelOne: "Source locked and operation in progress"
issue: Snapshots of Virtual Machines get stuck in "Source locked and operation in progress" state and then fail with "Deadline exceeeded"
resolution: Red Hat engineering is aware of the issue that will be fixed in a future release of `qemu-guest-agent`. Please open a support case to have updates on this. As a workaround, set the SELinux boolean below inside the VMs: # setsebool-P virt_qemu_ga_read_nonsecurity_files 1
root_cause: * A bind mount at `/opt/sentinelone/rpm_mount` with an SELinux context of `rpm_var_lib_t` prevents `qemu-guest-agent` from freezing it.

title: SRIOV-CNI failed to configure vlan on pod after updating SRIOV to 4.16
issue: When trying to configure a pod or vlan via SRIOV or a network attachment definition the pod creations fails with the following error. ~~~ The Pod can not be created with the error "SRIOV-CNI failed to configure VF "failed to set vf xx vlan configuration- id xxx, qos 0 and proto 802.1q: invalid argument"..." ~~~
