title: Is it possible to apply Multus static ipam to multiple Pod replicas in OpenShift?
issue: - Is it possible to apply Multus static ipam to multiple Pod replicas in OpenShift?
resolution: No it's not possible to apply the static ipam to multiple Pod replicas as replicas have identical configuration. The static IPs needs to be unique, different configuration between pods. In most cases, DHCP is best option to implement persistent static IP address assignment as the IP address assignment rules can be configured in the DHCP service side.

title: Unable to shut down all the nodes in OpenShift 4 cluster
issue: - Following the steps of [the document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/backup_and_restore/graceful-cluster-shutdown.html), I tried to shut down all of the nodes, but some nodes did not shut down. ``` $ for node in $(oc get nodes-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do oc debug node/${node}-- chroot /host shutdown-h 1; done ```- My cluster has infra nodes
resolution: - If your cluster has infra nodes, the debug Pod must be started according to this [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4976641).- Another consideration is that if the master nodes are retrieved before other nodes with `oc get node` and it takes longer to shut down, the apiserver may stop first, preventing the debug Pod from starting. In such an environment, it is necessary to adjust commands to shut down the non-master nodes first, then the master nodes. ``` $ for node in $(oc get nodes--selector='!node-role.kubernetes.io/master'-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' && echo ' ' && oc get nodes--selector='node-role.kubernetes.io/master'-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); \ do oc debug node/${node}--to-namespace dummy \-- chroot /host shutdown-h 1; \ done ```
root_cause: Some clusters require special consideration for the shut down commands described in the documentation.

title: The forklift-controller pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state.
issue: - After Migration Toolkit for Virtualization Operator upgrade to mtv-operator.v2.3.4, the `forklift-controller` pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state.- The `forklift-controller` pod is in CrashLoopBackOff due to OOMKill.
resolution: - Add the `controller_container_limits_memory` parameter to overcome this issue as documented at [link](https://github.com/kubev2v/forklift-operator/blob/4c8ec07c6cebb89afc3c6f17c94b424dc71ac34c/roles/forkliftcontroller/defaults/main.yml#L26 "link") into forkliftcontrollers (FC) CR configuration spec as shown below: ~~~ oc edit forkliftcontrollers.forklift.konveyor.io forklift-controller spec: controller_container_limits_memory: 2Gi ~~~
root_cause: - This was happening due to the pod requesting more memory than it is specified in the resource definition.

title: How to Implement Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (RHACS) on OpenShift Infrastructure Nodes
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - When deploying RHACS Central components on infrastructure nodes, the central-db pod fails to start with the following error: Warning FailedMount 16s (x6 over 31s) kubelet MountVolume.NewMounter initialization failed for volume "stackrox-db-pv": path "/var/lib/stackrox-db" does not exist
resolution: - Identify all the Infrastructure Nodes- Verify the Infra nodes are properly labeled: ~~~ $ oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/infra= ~~~- Verify the Infra node taints are properly labeled: ~~~ $ oc get nodes-o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TAINTS:.spec.taints ~~~- Create the required directory with proper permissions on all infrastructure nodes. The required directory path `/var/lib/stackrox-db` is not present on all infrastructure nodes where the pod might be scheduled. ~~~ for node in $(oc get nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/infra=-o name); do echo "Creating directory on $node" oc debug $node-- chroot /host mkdir-p /var/lib/stackrox-db oc debug $node-- chroot /host chown 1000:1000 /var/lib/stackrox-db oc debug $node-- chroot /host chmod 755 /var/lib/stackrox-db done ~~~- Create the Namespace: $ oc create namespace stackrox- Install RHACS Operator using the following official [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.6/installing/installing_ocp/install-central-ocp.html#install-central-using-operator)- Create the Storage Configuration:- Create Persistent Volume: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata: name: stackrox-db-pv spec: capacity: storage: 100Gi accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd local: path: /var/lib/stackrox-db nodeAffinity: required: nodeSelectorTerms:- matchExpressions:- key: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra operator: Exists ~~~- Create Persistent Volume Claim: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: name: central-db namespace: stackrox spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 100Gi storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ~~~- Deploy Central with Infra Node Configuration: ~~~ apiVersion: platform.stackrox.io/v1alpha1 kind: Central metadata: name: stackrox-central-services namespace: stackrox spec: central: persistence: persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: central-db nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: "" tolerations:- key: "node-role.kubernetes.io/infra" operator: "Exists" effect: "NoSchedule" scanner: nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: "" tolerations:- key: "node-role.kubernetes.io/infra" operator: "Exists" effect: "NoSchedule" ~~~
root_cause: - The central-db pod requires a specific directory path on the host node for persistent storage.- When deploying on infrastructure nodes with node selectors, the pod can be scheduled on any infrastructure node.- If the required directory is not present on the scheduled node, the volume mount fails.

title: Operator is not upgrading even after new version of Operator available in OperatorHub in RHOCP 4
issue: - Operator is not upgrading even after new version of operator available in `OperatorHub`.- Operator is not getting upgraded and latest version is showing uninstall option in `OperatorHub`.
resolution: - Try to mirror the Operator Images again using `oc-mirror` with `minVersion: `. ~~~- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.10 packages:- name: example-operator channels:- name: stable minVersion: 'Current-installed=version' ~~~
root_cause: - `skipRange` is the key which allows upgrade from operator's previous version to the latest version. The previous version is getting replaced because there is a `skipRange` for anything above for example `1.0.0` with `1.8.0`. In that case the update takes place even if it doesn't have an explicit replace for previous versions.

title: OpenShift/libreswan “F” Image Grades
issue: The releases of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) 4.14.43, 4.14.44, 4.15.42, 4.16.27, 4.16.28, 4.16.29, 4.17.9, 4.17.10 and 4.17.11 include container images `openshift4/ose-ovn-kubernetes` or `openshift4/ose-ovn-kubernetes-rhel9` rated “F” by the Red Hat "Clair" grading service.
resolution: Analysis revealed multiple contributing factors for the grade, but ultimately that the images are not impacted by any Critical or Important vulnerabilities (see Root Cause "section" below for more details). In order to address functional issues, `libreswan` was downgraded from either a RHEL 9.4 or 9.2 build to a RHEL 9.0 build which has had all CVE fixes from 9.2 and 9.4 backported. If your CVE scanner does not merge CVE data from RHEL 9.0, 9.2, and 9.4 it may identify the package `libreswan-4.6-3.el9_0.3` as vulnerable to multiple CVE. We are working to update CVE metadata in OpenShift Container Platform content to accurately reflect as soon as possible.
root_cause: The “F” grade was caused by two factors: 1. The `libreswan-4.6-3.el9_0.3` build was installed from a content set missing from the build inputs 1. The `libreswan-4.6-3.el9_0.3` build was released in [RHSA-2024:10594](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:10594) (RHEL 9.0.0), which does not include [CVE-2023-2295](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2023-2295) in its list of fixed flaws—that one was fixed by [RHSA-2023:3148](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3148) (RHEL 9.2.0) with a version number higher than `libreswan-4.6-3.el9_0.3` (`libreswan-4.9-4.el9_2`). [CVE-2023-2295](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2023-2295) per the errata text is due to [CVE-2023-30570](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2023-30570), and indicates that it’s only present in 9.2 (and 8.8) versions of `libreswan`.

title: OpenShift 4.14 IPSEC handling errors at cluster density exceeding 120 nodes
issue: - Cluster traffic degradation and a consistent failure rate of traffic calls between pods using IPSEC- Intermittent timeouts between pods on neighboring nodes, but pods on the same node experience no traffic interruptions- Traffic loss is observed from pods calling other pods via service, and throughput to applications is degraded by some percentage greater than zero.
resolution: - Currently this behavior is being tracked in priority bug: [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42952](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42952) This issue has been resolved in version **4.14.43** and incorporates the bug above as well as this additional OVS change outlined in bug: [https://issues.redhat.com//browse/OCPBUGS-44784](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/OCPBUGS-44784). [See errata](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:11031) ~~~ $ oc adm release info 4.14.43--image-for ovn-kubernetes quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:25e289236542301ef05e529a68c7b074b3f9cee85a4d3d1391f6993b54ad4649 ~~~ # Workaround:- The below steps outline a workaround for this problem that is expected to alleviate issues until an upgrade to the cluster can be completed. **NOTE: The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and support procedures.** The intent of this article is to provide information for diagnostics, debugging and non-production tasking that may bypass current restrictions or supported handling on OpenShift. Please note that these steps should only be taken with involvement from Red Hat and are not supported as a long-term solution. They are intended as an immediate stabilization method only while waiting for z-stream release to be made available to alleviate the behavioral issue within the IPSEC containers: 1. Start by patching the clusterversion to set the CNO to unmanaged in order to allow for modifications to networking components: ~~~ $ oc patch clusterversion version--type json-p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/overrides","value":[{"kind":"Deployment","group":"apps","name":"network-operator","namespace":"openshift-network-operator","unmanaged":true}]}]' ~~~ 2. Scale down the CNO (Cluster Network Operator) to allow for changes to be made on the ipsec-containerized pods. ~~~ oc-n openshift-network-operator scale deployment network-operator--replicas=0 ~~~ 3. Back up the yaml configuration for your ipsec-containerized pod deployment: ~~~ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get daemonset/ovn-ipsec-containerized-o yaml > ovn-ipsec-containerized-daemonset.yaml.bak ~~~ 4. Edit the daemonset and make the following changes to the yaml to modify the image + change the init script: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes edit daemonset/ovn-ipsec-containerized #- CURRENT IMAGE (4.14): image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:d3a1671bb47e281c6e06d8bafdea8556164ea3453194dc9eaa59b03f6228e1f5 #- CHANGE TO 4.12: image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:b61654dd4506756abe5bf05cf21c9091f4b4b7f088feb2bec6a7278dab81a6fa #init script change: ``` /usr/libexec/platform-python /usr/share/openvswitch/scripts/ovs-monitor-ipsec \--pidfile=/var/run/openvswitch/ovs-monitor-ipsec.pid--ike-daemon=libreswan--no-restart-ike-daemon \--ipsec-d /var/lib/ipsec/nss \ ## <--remove this line--log-file--monitor unix:/var/run/openvswitch/db.sock ``` #becomes: ``` /usr/libexec/platform-python /usr/share/openvswitch/scripts/ovs-monitor-ipsec \--pidfile=/var/run/openvswitch/ovs-monitor-ipsec.pid--ike-daemon=libreswan--no-restart-ike-daemon \--log-file--monitor unix:/var/run/openvswitch/db.sock ``` ~~~ 5. After the above changes to the image + the init script are completed, save + quit the file and allow the daemonset pods to roll out- this may take a few minutes to complete: ~~~ #check status of daemonset: $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get ds #check status of pods not in ready: $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get pod | grep ipsec-containerized | grep-v "Ready|Completed" ~~~ 6. `Ipsec-Containerized` Pods should all return to READY status and traffic should begin to normalize. Test Traffic flows and observe IPSEC connection counts on pods as outlined below in the Diagnostics section. 7. DO NOT SCALE UP THE CNO. Until updating to a z-stream release, the CNO will need to remain disabled or else the change will be reverted. Upgrades can still be completed as normal in the interim, but networking components are not managed, meaning deletion of objects that the operator would usually put back (like deployments/daemonsets/ingresscontrollers) will not occur automatically. If making changes to any of these objects, take explicit yaml backups before making changes. 8. **NOTE: ONLY PERFORM THIS STEP WHEN A BUG FIX IS AVAILABLE:** When the bug is fixed and the z-stream release is made available, upgrade the cluster to the release version, then re-enable the CNO by removing the unmanaged patch update and allowing the CNO to rescale to 1: ~~~ $ oc patch clusterversion version--type json-p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/overrides","value":[{"kind":"Deployment","group":"apps","name":"network-operator","namespace":"openshift-network-operator","unmanaged":true}]}]' ~~~- You may also test the 4.14.43 image proactively by reverting the init script change above to ensure the line `--ipsec-d /var/lib/ipsec/nss` is present in the daemonset init script section as outlined, then updating the image to point at the new 4.14.43 image build and allowing the ipsec-containerized pods to rollout: ~~~ $ oc adm release info 4.14.43--image-for ovn-kubernetes quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:25e289236542301ef05e529a68c7b074b3f9cee85a4d3d1391f6993b54ad4649 ~~~ # Validating Changes:- Check the yaml of the daemonset for ipsec containerized to confirm that the image was updated successfully and that the yaml removed the `--ipsec-d /var/lib/ipsec/nss` line from the start script.- Run the following command on a few different ipsec-containerized pods to confirm the status of the SA connections and wait for them to stabilize. If you see any connections listed as `half-open()` we need more time for the pod to finish linking with peer nodes (this can take upwards of 30m). ~~~ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh pod/${ipsec-containerized-podname} ipsec status |grep "IKE SAs" #output of a cluster still stabilizing (needs more time): sh-4.4# ipsec status |grep "IKE SAs" 000 IKE SAs: total(250), half-open(110), open(0), authenticated(140), anonymous(0) # +2m later: 000 IKE SAs: total(364), half-open(95), open(0), authenticated(269), anonymous(0) #output of a node that has finished stabilizing/ready (we want 0 in half-open). sh-4.4# ipsec status |grep "IKE SAs" 000 IKE SAs: total(250), half-open(0), open(0), authenticated(250), anonymous(0) ~~~ # Adding Nodes while in the above workaround state:- Due to the fact that when a node is added to the cluster, a CSR (certificate signing request) is generated for each node the CNO typically will approve these for each node object automatically. However, with the CNO down, it cannot do so. Additionally, each IPSEC-Containerized pod on a new host will generate a new CSR agreement for each other node in the cluster, leading to a high number of csr creations that need to be manually approved.- When adding nodes in this state you should add one node at a time, and ensure all CSRs are approved + the node is READY before moving to the next host. You can use the following command to approve all pending CSRS, and it is expected you will need to run this a few times before new CSRS stop getting generated. ~~~ $ oc get csr-o go-template='{{range.items}}{{if not.status}}{{.metadata.name}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}{{end}}' | xargs--no-run-if-empty oc adm certificate approve ~~~- If you intend to scale your cluster up past 500 nodes, please open a case with Red Hat Support to discuss.
root_cause: - There is a bug in the way Libreswan 4.9 is implemented on OpenShift at scale that was not present in the previous version of Libreswan 4.6 for RHEL8 hosts. When IPSEC for OpenShift 4.14 (based on RHEL9) was implemented, Libreswan 4.9 was added and the behavioral issue was created.- When IPSEC is deployed on 4.14, it relies on a containerized implementation of libreswan and Pluto to establish handshakes between peers, and maintains a constantly updated configuration file on each pod, labeling peers and certificates to be loaded for cross-talk between nodes.- A handling issue within Libreswan 4.9 prevents maintaining connections and SA connection link details for nodes after a certain threshold of node scale is reached and the connections begin to degrade. It is believed (at time of writing) that the ovn-monitor-ipsec script that fires a connection-establish request to the IPSEC libreswan implementation is not re-checking that all connections are established after the map is created, and subsequently when connections fail they are not rebuilt.- ovs-monitor-ipsec sends a request to libreswan by launching `ipsec auto--start`, but this command hangs indefinitely on certain connections. ovs-monitor-ipsec waits forever for ipsec auto to complete, so it can't proceed and can't establish any other connections that are not configured yet.- Restarting the node may alleviate issues temporarily but the target nodes that are impacted may change as maps are recreated and subsequently degrade.

title: The OTEL collectors dropping trace packets with the error "grpc: received message after decompression larger than max" in RHOCP
issue: The `OTEL` `collectors` in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) are dropping trace packets with the error "grpc: received message after decompression larger than max"
resolution: - Check the `OpenTelemetry` (OTEL) `Collector` configuration to ensure the `send_batch_size` setting is configured under the batch processor. This setting determines the minimum batch size before the data is sent to the downstream system. ~~~ $ oc get OpenTelemetryCollector-n processors: batch: send_batch_size: 10000 timeout: 10s ~~~- Lowering the `send_batch_size` helps reduce the payload size of each batch. This prevents excessive data from being sent in a single batch, which can lead to issues such as exceeding the allowed size limits- Configure the `send_batch_max_size` to be slightly larger than `send_batch_size`, This allows the system to handle bursts of trace data effectively while maintaining control over batch size limits. ~~~ $ oc edit OpenTelemetryCollector-n processors: batch: send_batch_size: 3000 send_batch_max_size: 4000 ~~~ **Note: These values are based on the cluster's payload characteristics and may vary depending on the system's capacity and trace size distribution.**
root_cause: The root cause is that the trace message exceeded the maximum allowed size, and reducing the batch size will prevent the payload from exceeding this limit. The settings for batch size are discussed in the upstream [documentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/processor/batchprocessor/README.md).

title: What container runtimes and container managment tools are supported in Red Hat Enterprise Linux?
issue: What container runtimes and container managment tools are supported in Red Hat Enterprise Linux?
resolution: The following table describes the supportability status of each technology in a standalone context in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. Technology | Function | RHEL7 | RHEL8------- |----- |----- |----- podman | Container Engine | Yes | Yes docker | Container Engine | Yes / Partial | No dockerd | Daemon | Yes | No runc | Runtime | Yes | Yes systemd-nspawn | Runtime | No | No libvirt-lxc | Runtime | Deprecated | No CRI-O | Container Runtime Interface | No | No containerd | Container Runtime Interface | No | No rkt | Runtime | No | No ## Podman `podman` was [introduced](https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2018/08/29/intro-to-podman/) in [RHEL-7.6](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/7.6_release_notes/chap-red_hat_enterprise_linux-7.6_release_notes-overview#idm140112685792176) and [RHEL-8.0](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8-beta/html-single/8.0_beta_release_notes/index#notable_changes_to_containers). `podman` complements [Buildah](https://www.projectatomic.io/blog/2017/06/introducing-buildah/) and [Skopeo](https://www.projectatomic.io/blog/2016/07/working-with-containers-image-made-easy/) by offering an experience similar to the `docker` command line by allowing users to run standalone (non-orchestrated) containers. Podman doesn’t require a daemon to run containers and pods. Since RHEL 8, `podman` replaces `docker` as the default CLI to interact with containers. ## Docker `docker` CLI and `dockerd` daemon are fully supported by Red Hat as of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7. Docker CLI has been replaced with `podman` in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and `podman` doesn't require any daemon like `dockerd`. For `docker-compose`, `docker-machine` or `docker swarm` check [How is the docker container runtime supported in RHEL 7?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1408853) article. ## runc `runc` runtime is required by `podman` and `dockerd` to run containers. `runc` on direct usage, without `podman` is also supported. ## systemd-nspawn `systemd-nspawn` is not supported. ## libvirt-lxc `libvirt-lxc` packages are [deprecated](https://access.redhat.com/articles/1365153) since Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.1. ## CRI-O `CRI-O` is a Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface that is supported for [Red Hat OpenShift](https://www.openshift.com/) and is not intended to be used as standalone solution under Red Hat Enterprise Linux. ## containerd `containerd` is a Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface that is supported for [Red Hat OpenShift](https://www.openshift.com/) and is not intended to be used as standalone solution under Red Hat Enterprise Linux. ## rkt `rkt` runtime has never been part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and thus never has been supported. ## Red Hat Container Support Policy For further information on Red Hat's support policy on containers, check [Red Hat Container Support Policy](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2726611) article.

title: One of the worker nodes went into NotReady state right after the installation of Aquasec
issue: - After installing Aquasec, one of the worker nodes went into__NotReady__ and required a full reboot to get back to normal state. Does aqua-agent-xxxx pod affect kubelet and kill all other running pods on the node?
resolution: - Aquasec intercepts CRI-O socket and also affects CRI-O to kubelet traffic. If Aquasec pod scheduled on the node crashes by any reason, then this also means that CRI-O cannot carry on its work. Thus a full kernel restart is needed for a full clean up.
root_cause: - Aquasec intercepts CRI-O socket and causes kubelet to CRI-O traffic to restrict which images can be used, etc. If Aquasec crashes, this socket intercept is not cleaned up and thus kubelet looses its ability to start containers as it can no longer talk to the CRI-O socket. This is like a man-in-the-middle tool that is no longer relaying the messages and kubelet cannot get restarted. To restart, kubelet needs to be able to talk to CRI-O which is essentially now intercepted by Aquasec.- Security tools like Aquasec use the linux function patching syscalls to intercept certain cgroup/syscalls. When the security application is sigkilled without a chance to remove its hooks, a bunch of syscalls start to not work. As CRI-O is intercepted by Aquasec, it cannot create container. Thus, a full kernel restart is needed to clean up the mess.

title: Erratic time issues on VMware based RHEL guests running ntpd/chronyd
issue: Erratic time issues on VMware based RHEL/RHCOS guests running ntpd/chronyd
Why is time on my RHEL guests under VMware behaving erratically?
Why is time on my RHEL guest under VMware skipping randomly?
How can I check if VMware time sync is disabled?

VMware has a functionality to enable time synchronization from the host system to VMs. This is typically undesirable and not recommended as it can interfere with ntpd/chronyd. What are the steps to ensure this functionality is disabled?
We have some virtual machines (running on VMware ESXi hosts) having problem with time synchronization by using ntpd/chronyd. How do we fix it?
VMWare recommends keeping one-off time synchronization enabled. Should we keep it enabled/disabled if ntpd/chronyd is running?

In Openshift nodes running on top of VMWare, the `NodeClockNotSynchronising` alert is firing after performing VMotion on clusters configured with [NTP/chrony](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/installing/install_config/installing-customizing.html#installation-special-config-chrony_installing-customizing).
resolution: If the VMware based RHEL guests are experiencing erratic time issues our suggestion to troubleshoot the problem is to disable the two types of VMware time synchronization (*periodic* and *one-off time sync*) to isolate the issue and use only a single time synchronization program (chronyd is preferred). ### Disabling periodic time synchronization Periodic time synchronization can be checked by using the command `vmware-toolbox-cmd timesync status` and disabled in one of three ways: * Run the command `vmware-toolbox-cmd timesync disable` from the guest * Deselect "Time synchronization between the virtual machine and the host operating system" in the VMware Tools toolbox GUI of the guest operating system. * Select or by add the line `tools.syncTime = "0"` to the.vmx file ### Disabling one-off time synchronization The following options need to be added to the.vmx file for each system: ~~~ time.synchronize.continue = "FALSE" time.synchronize.restore = "FALSE" time.synchronize.resume.disk = "FALSE" time.synchronize.shrink = "FALSE" time.synchronize.tools.startup = "FALSE" time.synchronize.tools.enable = "FALSE" time.synchronize.resume.host = "FALSE" ~~~ For more details, please contact the vendor.
root_cause: VMware has two types of time synchronization: **Periodic time synchronization** Only a single time synchronization program should be disciplining the time of an operating system. Therefore, when using NTP in the guest, you must ensure that VMware Tools periodic time synchronization is disabled (the default setting for VMware virtual machines). **One-off time synchronization** Certain virtual machine life-cycle events can cause guest clock to become incorrect (typically lag behind real wall clock time). VMware Tools recognizes the lag, and synchronizes guest operating system time to that of the host. This capability is turned on by default. Time is re-synchronized when you migrate the virtual machine using vMotion, take a snapshot, restore to a snapshot, shrink the virtual disk, resume a virtual machine after being suspended, or restart the tools service in the virtual machine (including rebooting the virtual machine). IMPORTANT: Since one-off time synchronization relies on the time in the host operating system as a reference, it is important that host system time is kept accurate using time synchronization software according to best practices for that host. NOTE: When a VM is migrated from one host to another and one-off sync is enabled, the VM will change the system clock according to the time from the new host. It's possible to see messages like "Time has been changed" or "Forward time jump detected". In order to avoid time jumps that may cause problems to the applications, it's recommended to disable one-off time sync and use only chronyd, which will adjust the system clock gradually without clock jumps. For more information, see: ["Migrating virtual machine may cause guest operating system clock to fall behind real time"](https://kb.vmware.com/s/article/2108828) *Disclaimer: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. title: The noProxy configuration is missing in Prometheus after configuring remote-write in OpenShift 4
issue: - Unable to send `metrics` to `remote-write` endpoint after upgrading RHOCP cluster to 4.16+ version.- `Promtheus-k8s` pods stream below logs indefinitely: ~~~ $ oc logs-c prometheus prometheus-k8s-1-n openshift-monitoring... 2024-08-06T14:56:36.607159251Z ts=2024-08-06T14:56:36.607Z caller=dedupe.go:112 component=remote level=error remote_name=8dee62 url=http://example-prometheus.test.svc.cluster.local:9090/api/v1/receive msg="non-recoverable error" count=9 exemplarCount=0 err="server returned HTTP status 403 Forbidden: " 2024-08-06T14:56:36.607239708Z ts=2024-08-06T14:56:36.607Z caller=dedupe.go:112 component=remote level=error remote_name=8dee62 url=http://example-prometheus.test.svc.cluster.local:9090/api/v1/receive msg="non-recoverab ~~~
resolution: This is a known issue tracked in [OCPBUGS-38289](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-38289), and has been already resolved in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 and newer releases: Target Minor Release | Bug | Fixed Version | Errata--- |--- 4.17 | [OCPBUGS-39029](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-39029)|**4.17.0**|[RHSA-2024:3718](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3718) 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-39170](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-39170)|**4.16.11**|[RHBA-2024:6401](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:6401) 4.15 | [OCPBUGS-39172](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-39172)|**4.15.31**|[RHSA-2024:6409](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:6409) 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-39176](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-39176)|**4.14.36**|[RHSA-2024:6406](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:6406)
root_cause: Starting with OpenShift 4.16, the `proxyURL` field (inherited from cluster proxy custom resource) gets injected in the `prometheus` `k8s` custom resource, but the `noProxy` is not injected because of which the remote-write endpoint which is in `noProxy` region is not able to receive metrics because of connectivity problems.

title: Cluster Autoscaler Not Enforcing Minimum Replica Count in MachineSets without Unschedulable Pods
issue: - In an OpenShift cluster, the Machine AutoScaler (MA) minimum replica setting is configured for each MachineSet. However, the Cluster Autoscaler does not maintain the expected minimum node count across MachineSets unless there are unschedulable pods. As a result, the cluster may have fewer worker nodes than specified by the Machine AutoScaler’s minimum replicas setting, despite sufficient resources.
resolution: - This behavior is due to the Cluster Autoscaler's default logic, which only triggers scaling when there are unschedulable pods. A Request for Enhancement [RFE-6528](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-6528) has been submitted to add a--enforce-node-group-min-size flag to the Cluster Autoscaler. When implemented, this feature will ensure that the autoscaler maintains the minimum node count configured in the Machine AutoScaler, even if there are no unschedulable pods.
root_cause: - The Cluster Autoscaler does not currently enforce a strict minimum node count on MachineSets. The autoscaler scales up only in response to unschedulable pods, regardless of the Machine AutoScaler’s configured minimum replica count. This design can result in discrepancies where the actual worker node count is below the expected minimum.

title: EgressIP fails to migrate to the correct node after deleting the machine
issue: - EgressIP fails to add on the replaced node.- The `cloud-network-config-controller-xxxxxx-xxxxx` Pod throws the below message. I0503 08:15:17.202909 1 cloudprivateipconfig_controller.go:189] CloudPrivateIPConfig: "X.X.X.X" will be deleted from node: "ip-X-X-X-X.region.compute.internal" E0503 08:15:17.202940 1 controller.go:165] error syncing 'X.X.X.X': node "ip-X-X-X-X.region.compute.internal" not found, requeuing in cloud-private-ip-config workqueue
resolution: This problem was resolved in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.13.1 via [RHSA-2023:3304](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3304) and Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.12.21 via [RHBA-2023:3546](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:3546). Please update to the aforementioned version of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 (or later version) to prevent the issue from happening. ### Workaround- List `CloudPrivateIPConfig` objects. ~~~ oc get cloudprivateipconfigs ~~~- Remove the one that is assigned to the non-existing Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node. ~~~ oc delete cloudprivateipconfigs X.X.X.X ~~~
root_cause: The `EgressIP` assigned to a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node that is being deleted by the `Machine-API` was not properly released and thus stuck on the no longer available Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4- Node.

title: OpenShift is triggering a warning about ingress-canary pods
issue: The OpenShift console is triggering the following warning: N Pods of DaemonSet openshift-ingress-canary/ingress-canary are running where they are not supposed to run.
resolution: Manually deleting the pods running on the tainted nodes will solve the issue
root_cause: Taints with `NoSchedule` effect are evaluated only at scheduling time, running pods on the tainted nodes are not evicted, thus needs to be manually removed.

title: RHOCP 4 initContainer in CrashLoopBackOff on pod with Service Mesh sidecar injected
issue: - Pod with istio-proxy sidecar injected fails to initialize due to failed `initContainer`, when `initContainer` needs to communicate with some service on a different project.- Pod with istio-proxy sidecar injected fails to initialize due to failed `initContainer`, when `initContainer` needs to communicate with a service in or outside the 'Mesh' via its `FQDN`.- The `initContainer` in a Service Mesh pod is not able to resolve or connect to any service: ~~~ Could not resolve host: kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local Closing connection 0 ~~~- The `initContainer` starts before the sidecar so the `NetworkPolicies` are blocking any egress traffic from mesh.
resolution: Permanent solution is introduced with ServiceMesh 2.6 and requires OpenShift 4.16 at minimum, as reported in the [Service Mesh 2.6 Release Notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/service_mesh/service-mesh-2-x#istio-1-20-support-ossm-2-6-0_ossm-release-notes). 1. Enable the Native sidecar in the ServiceMeshControlPlane, for example: ~~~ oc-n istio-system patch smcp basic--type=merge--patch '{"spec":{"runtime":{"components":{"pilot":{"container":{"env":{"ENABLE_NATIVE_SIDECARS":"true"}}}}}}}' ~~~ 2. Restart the application pods. ### Workarounds {#workaround} 1. Use the `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundPorts` or `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundIPRanges` annotations with the pod to allow the traffic. [See the example with `excludeOutboundPorts`](#example-excludeport).- **Note**: this workaround is not valid for DNS traffic. 2. Execute the `initContainer` as user `1337`. [See the example with `runAsUser: 1337`](#example-1337).- **Note:** this option must be used with care and only as a last resort in case of no possibility to use IP addresses, since the pod will run with more privileges. ### Example with `excludeOutboundPorts` {#example-excludeport} If some deployment, that is injecting 'istio-proxy' sidecar, has an `initContainer` that needs to run before the application container which needs, for any reason, to run some tasks prior by establishing a connection to some other service in the same project or another project, there are some details that need to be in consideration to avoid the initContainer to fail and with that the pod failing to initialize. In the example below we will go through some of these considerations before running some deployment. This example runs a simple Django with Postgresql web application, where an `initContainer` was configured on the Django `deploymentConfig` which needs to get a valid response from a 'TCP' server service running on another project. ~~~~ $ oc get all,ep-n django-project NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE pod/django-psql-persistent-8-rbkj4 2/2 Running 0 94m pod/postgresql-2-7kfnm 2/2 Running 0 126m NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE service/django-psql-persistent ClusterIP 172.32.112.108 8080/TCP 5h12m service/postgresql ClusterIP 172.32.136.38 5432/TCP 5h12m NAME REVISION DESIRED CURRENT TRIGGERED BY deploymentconfig.apps.openshift.io/django-psql-persistent 10 1 0 config,image(django-psql-persistent:latest) deploymentconfig.apps.openshift.io/postgresql 2 1 1 config,image(postgresql:12-el8) NAME TYPE FROM LATEST buildconfig.build.openshift.io/django-psql-persistent Source Git 1 NAME TYPE FROM STATUS STARTED DURATION build.build.openshift.io/django-psql-persistent-1 Source Git@064993e Complete 5 hours ago 6m18s NAME ENDPOINTS AGE endpoints/django-psql-persistent 10.132.0.146:8080 5h12m endpoints/postgresql 10.135.0.174:5432 5h12m $ oc get dc/django-psql-persistent-o yaml spec: replicas: 1 revisionHistoryLimit: 10 selector: name: django-psql-persistent strategy: activeDeadlineSeconds: 21600 recreateParams: timeoutSeconds: 600 resources: {} type: Recreate template: metadata: annotations: sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true" traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundPorts: "9000" creationTimestamp: null labels: name: django-psql-persistent name: django-psql-persistent spec: containers:- env: image: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/test-istio/django-psql-persistent@sha256:0f90bc03677c364ceed6d4ed71d0664f22a954a47fe4b35cab90f348d5fb4acd imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: django-psql-persistent ports:- containerPort: 8080 protocol: TCP terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log terminationMessagePolicy: File dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst initContainers:- command:- /bin/bash--c- | set-euo pipefail CONNECTION=$(echo "world" | nc tcp-echo.approve-init-containers.svc.cluster.local 9000) if [[${CONNECTION} == "hello world"]]; then echo "Connection succeeded, continue with the deployment" exit 0 else echo "Connection failed. Stop and review what is wrong" exit 1 fi image: registry.redhat.io/rhel7/rhel-tools imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: check-approval <----> ~~~~ The 'TCP' service is a simple 'tcp-echo' server that receives and responds to connections via 'TCP' by sending "hello + the client side request". ~~~~ $ oc get all,ep-n approve-init-containers NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE pod/tcp-echo-567c9458b8-z86qs 2/2 Running 0 174m NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE service/tcp-echo ClusterIP 172.32.248.178 9000/TCP,9001/TCP 8h NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE deployment.apps/tcp-echo 1/1 1 1 8h NAME ENDPOINTS AGE endpoints/tcp-echo 10.132.0.131:9001,10.132.0.131:9000 8h ~~~~ In order to have this working there are some special extra settings needed: ~~~~ template: metadata: annotations: sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true" traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundPorts: "9000"--> this annotation must be present excluding the outbound port used by the `initContainer` to avoid traffic loss. In this case port 9000 which is the port of the tcp-echo service. initContainers:- command:- /bin/bash--c- | set-euo pipefail CONNECTION=$(echo "world" | nc 172.32.248.178 9000)--> the connection made by the `initContainer` must go to the service ClusterIP and not the service hostname if [[${CONNECTION} == "hello world"]]; then echo "Connection succeeded, continue with the deployment" exit 0 else echo "Connection failed. Stop and review what is wrong" exit 1 fi ~~~~ With this when the pod is schedule the `initContainer` will start and finish its task and then the pod will initialize starting the application and 'istio-proxy' containers: ~~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE django-psql-persistent-12-pn8f4 2/2 Running 1 (84s ago) 2m6s postgresql-2-9dttg 2/2 Running 0 2m1s $ oc logs-c check-approval django-psql-persistent-12-pn8f4 Connection succeeded, continue with the deployment ~~~~ And from the 'tcp-echo' server the connection can also be seen: ~~~~ $ oc logs-c tcp-echo tcp-echo-567c9458b8-sck4k listening on [::]:9002, prefix: hello listening on [::]:9000, prefix: hello listening on [::]:9001, prefix: hello request: world response: hello world $ oc logs-c istio-proxy tcp-echo-567c9458b8-sck4k [2022-01-19T20:52:09.370Z] "---" 0--- "-" 6 12 36- "-" "-" "-" "-" "127.0.0.1:9000" inbound|9000|| 127.0.0.1:60570 10.132.0.102:9000 10.132.0.103:52380-- ~~~~ If `initContainer` is failing because of DNS errors accessing the service `hostname` the current workaround is to make sure containers use the service `ClusterIP` as the example on the script above. ### Example with `runAsUser: 1337` {#example-1337} In cases where is not possible at all to use an IP address the solution is to add the `istio-proxy` UID in addition to the annotation- `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundPorts: `- in order for the `istio-cni` to not have any interference in the `initContainer` network connections. For this to work the pod must run with either `nonroot` or `anyuid` `scc`: ~~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user nonroot-z ~~~~ Then add the user "1337" to the `initContainer` section: ~~~~ template: metadata: annotations: sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true" traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundPorts: "9000" [...] spec: containers: [...] initContainers:- command:- /bin/bash--c- | set-euo pipefail CONNECTION=$(echo "world" | nc tcp-echo-server.mycloud.example.com 9000) if [[${CONNECTION} == "hello world"]]; then echo "Connection succeeded, continue with the deployment" exit 0 else echo "Connection failed. Stop and review what is wrong" exit 1 fi image: registry.redhat.io/rhel7/rhel-tools imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: check-approval securityContext: runAsUser: 1337--> add the securityContext.runAsUser to the container ~~~~ Once the pod starts, the `initContainer` will start with user 1337 and bypass all the `istio-cni` settings used for the `istio-proxy` sidecar.
root_cause: **Disclaimer:** *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*- The Red Hat Openshift Service Mesh uses Istio CNI which is used to configure the network of the `envoyProxy`, including its iptables rules to capture applications traffic.- This plugin is also used to connect to the OCP cluster network including Multus CNI.- As stated by the [upstream Istio](https://istio.io/v1.9/docs/setup/additional-setup/cni/#compatibility-with-application-init-containers) this might create issues with `initContainers` since the pod will not start until the `initContainer` finishes. Because the pod will not start, the `istio-proxy` will also wait to start, but the Istio CNI initializes all the network for the `envoyProxy` to take over as soon as the pod is scheduled and the Istio control plane receives information that a new `istio-proxy` will be injected, causing possible network connectivity failures on the `initContainer`.

title: Adding a host using Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) in Host Inventory fails to boot with the boot NIC
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - We are creating an OCP cluster using RHACM and trying to add a node to host inventory using BMC form. But the node is not booting with the NIC and is stuck during the boot.
resolution: - When adding a host to the inventory using the Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) form, ensure the correct BMC address format is used.- BMC address formats for Dell iDRAC: Protocol | Address Format-------------------- |---------------------------------------------- iDRAC virtual media | `idrac-virtualmedia:// /redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1` Redfish network boot | `redfish:// /redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1`- BMC address formats for HPE iLO: Protocol | Address Format-------------------- |---------------------------------------------- Redfish virtual media | `redfish-virtualmedia:// /redfish/v1/Systems/1` Redfish network boot | `redfish:// /redfish/v1/Systems/1`

title: JBoss RPM vs Zip(jar) distribution/installation Method
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - Is it better to install JBoss with yum [RPM] or with a zip package?- What are the differences between the two distributions?- Is it possible to use two RPM installation's on one machine.- How to build an RPM containing JBoss EAP6
resolution: The directory structure of your JBoss instance is really the only physical difference between the two distributions but the conventions/reasons and support of each differ greatly. One of these different in philosophy is with Horizontal and Vertical provisioning. The RPM distribution only accounts for Horizontal provisioning (in EAP 5 and earlier) and while EAP 6 accounts for both, but only supports Vertical provisioning with Domain Mode. Because of these differences in philosophy, it is necessary to evaluate each option and choose the distribution that best meets your requirements. The following questions will help guide you in your decision: * Do you need to install a specific version of JBoss? * Are you looking for automatic Security updates? * Do you have a need or will you ever have a need for vertical scaling? * Do you need a supported `init` script?
root_cause: Each distribution (RPM vs [Zip | Binary]) has its pros and cons and it is at your discretion to determine what distribution the most appropriate. **Each distribution** has features that it supports and does **not** support, it is important to check with Red Hat's product documentation and Red Hat support for all of the details on what feature is and what is not supported. Below are list features for each distribution to guide on the decision: ## RPM * Only runs on RPM based Linux distributions and only supported on **Red Hat Enterprise Linux**. * Installed in common directories across the OS, consistent with the standard Linux file system layout. It requires a good understanding of the standard Linux file system layout. * Standard installation and OS integration makes it easy to have a multipurpose system managed by a single sysadmin (e.g. logs, shared libraries, etc. in central locations). * Only one RPM install of EAP on a system is tested and supported, so this affects your ability to provision systems (instances). * Designed for installing one major version of JBoss per system and running the latest release (e.g. the latest version of EAP7 or EAP8). * See what the [challenges of installing as specific version of JBoss with RPM](https://access.redhat.com/knowledge/solutions/68614) are and how this minimizes the benefits of an RPM install. * Can run a single standalone EAP instance, or a single host/domain controller (EAP 6+). * Vertical provisioning (running multiple EAP instances on a single system) possible with EAP6+ running Domain mode * Requires `root` access for management. * Installed as a service, and an `init` script is provided and supported. > **NOTE**: It is not recommended to be subscribed to multiple JBoss EAP repositories at the same time. ## Zip / Binary * Platform neutral. * Install is self-contained to the unzipped directory. * No standard installs, or OS integration means sysadmins cannot look in common locations for issues or logs. * Easy to install more than one JBoss version per system, even different versions across major releases. * Does not require `root` access for management, making it a good choice for developers and shops where server and application admins are separate. * Vertical provisioning (running multiple instances on a single system, including multiple host/domain controllers) supported.

title: Nooba Operator pod show's account not found error
issue: The Nooba Operator pod logs show the folowing error: ~~~ level=warning msg="⏳ Temporary Error: cannot read admin account info, error: account not found 493da838ef8327b683" sys=openshift-storage/noobaa ~~~
resolution: Please submit a case with Red Hat if you encounter this error.
root_cause: There are many reasons why the Noobaa Operator could be throwing this error. The most common is that the noobaa-db PVC has been recreated. If this is the case, noobaa may need to be rebuilt, or a restoration of the Noobaa-db PVC may need to take place. Please submit a case with Red Hat if this is the case.

title: The expected minimal permissions to access tenancy port of thanos-querier service do not work in clusters upgraded from OCP 4.14
issue: The expected minimal permissions to access tenancy port of thanos-querier service do not work in clusters upgraded from OCP 4.14
resolution: As per [OCPBUGS-17035](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-17035) The minimal permissions required to access the tenancy port on the thanos-querier service in the openshift-monitoring namespace were not functioning as expected. The expected permissions for accessing the tenancy port were like below But this gave `Forbidden` error: ~~~ rules:- verbs:- get apiGroups:- metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 resources:- pods // Output sh-4.4$ curl-k-H "Authorization:Bearer ${TOKEN}" 'https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc:9092/api/v1/query?query=up&namespace=ocp5' Forbidden (user=system:serviceaccount:ocp5:monitoring-view, verb=get, resource=pods, subresource=) ~~~ Instead below was needed for successful GET requests to the tenancy port. ~~~ rules:- verbs:- get- create apiGroups:- '' resources:- pods // Output sh-4.4$ curl-k-H "Authorization:Bearer ${TOKEN}" 'https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc:9092/api/v1/query?query=up&namespace=ocp5' {"status":"success","data":{"resultType":"vector","result":[{"metric":{"__name__":"up","endpoint":"web","instance":"10.128.3.171:8080","job":"prometheus-example-app","namespace":"ocp5","pod":"prometheus-example-app-6884c645b9-jhsw4","prometheus":"openshift-user-workload-monitoring/user-workload","service":"prometheus-example-app"},"value":[1731942812.121,"1"]}]}} ~~~ This Bug was fixed in RHOCP 4.15 and [OBSDOCS-1555](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDOCS-1555) is created to add it in RHOCP 4.15 release notes._NOTE: The Bug [OCPBUGS-17035](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-17035) was marked private while it was created hence it was not included in Release Notes earlier._ However, it was observed that `apiGroups:- metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` Role worked as expected in newly created 4.15 clusters and showed successful output for queries but clusters upgraded from 4.14 to 4.15 or later versions still gave `Forbidden` error. Bug [OCPBUGS-45895](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-45895) is created to fix this issue. **Workarround** Recreating secret: ~~~ # oc delete secret thanos-querier-kube-rbac-proxy-n openshift-monitoring ~~~
root_cause: Secret thanos-querier-kube-rbac-proxy is not updated after the upgrade from 4.14 to 4.15.

title: Apply terminationGracePeriodSeconds field for WMCO pods
issue: - In RHOCP for `windows` workload, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` feature is not applicable.
resolution: - An RFE [`RFE-6791`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-6791) has been raised to implement `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` feature in RHOCP for WMCO workload.
root_cause: - The `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` attribute of a pod or pod template controls the graceful `termination` period (default 30 seconds). With basic pod workload, this feature works fine but with `windows` pods, even after applying `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` field, pods will be delete immediately. This `feature` has recently seen progress upstream with a [`KEP`](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-windows/4802-windows-node-shutdown/README.md#design-details) for Windows Node shutdown behavior, the implementation is still in development and is not yet available in RHOCP.

title: RHOSO data plane deployment fails with error `This system is not yet registered`
issue: - During the deployment of RHOSO Data Plane deployment fails as nodes fails to subscribe to CDN ~~~ "stderr": ["Network error: Name or service not known (error code-2)", "This system is not yet registered. Try 'subscription-manager register--help' for more information." ~~~
resolution: - Pass the `pool-id` in `openstackdataplane` CR ~~~ edpm_bootstrap_command: | subscription-manager register--username {{subscription_manager_username}}--password {{subscription_manager_password}} subscription-manager attach--pool= subscription-manager release--set=9.4 subscription-manager repos--disable=* subscription-manager repos--enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-baseos-eus-rpms--enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-appstream-eus-rpms--enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-highavailability-eus-rpms--enable=fast-datapath-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms--enable=rhoso-18.0-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms--enable=rhceph-7-tools-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms ~~~
root_cause: - Missing Pool Details will lead to this issue as `subscription-manager` won't be able to attach the repos

title: Pods are struck in ContainerCreating state due to multiple mounts being in hung state
issue: - Application pods are stuck in `ContainerCreating` state due to `NFS` mount issues, ~~~ 4m Warning FailedMount pod/ <> Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[task-pv-logs], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition ~~~- Multiple `stale` mounts are present on the nfs `client` from the affected NFS server, which were `lazy` unmounted.
resolution: - To resolve this issue, from `NFS client` side, [`reboot`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-rebooting.html#nodes-nodes-rebooting-gracefully_nodes-nodes-rebooting) the node gracefully to wipe out all `lazy unmonuts` completely. To resolve it from NFS server side, restart the NFS service.

title: ClusterServiceVersions blocking cluster upgrade: openshift-storage/odf-operator:v4.y is incompatible with OpenShift minor versions greater than 4.(y+1)
issue: - There is a warning message displayed against the operator-lifecycle-manager from the RHOCP UI saying as seen in the screenshot below: [image=[src="images/warning_message_ocpui.png", alt="warning_message_ocpui", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="Warning message seen from OCP UI",]]- co/operator-lifecycle-manager reports `IncompatibleOperatorsInstalled` in its status with the below message: ``` $ oc get co/operator-lifecycle-manager-o json | jq-r.status.conditions[]- lastTransitionTime: "2024-07-09T07:13:23Z" message: 'ClusterServiceVersions blocking cluster upgrade: openshift-storage/odf-operator.v4.12.14-rhodf is incompatible with OpenShift minor versions greater than 4.13' reason: IncompatibleOperatorsInstalled status: "False" type: Upgradeable ```
resolution: - Update the RHODF operator to match the minor version of RHOCP. The warning message will go away once both RHODF and RHOCP are on same minor versions.
root_cause: - The warning message seen is triggered when a RHOCP cluster is on one minor version ahead of the RHODF. For example:- RHOCP is running v4.12.z, and RHODF is running v4.11.z- RHOCP is running v4.13.z, and RHODF is running v4.12.z.- This helps avoid a minor version gap of n+2 or more between RHOCP and RHODF.- This helps to limit incompatibility issues between RHOCP and RHODF that can surface if a cluster has a minor version difference of n+2 or more.

title: Kube-controller-manager unable to acquire leader lease in RHOCP 4
issue: - No new pods are scheduled after they are manually deleted or scaled out.- Pending `CSRs` can be seen and they multiply. If they are approved, they are not issued.- Nodes show `Ready` state even when they should be `NotReady` (Node `CSR` pending approval).- Pods and replicas are not in sync. Multiple replicas for the same pod can be seen even though replicas are set to 1.- `kube-controller-manager` pods are flapping in `CrashLoopBackOff` state.- The error seen in the `kube-controller-manager` pod logs is: ~~~ 2023-05-10T11:00:23.515837859Z W0510 11:00:23.515763 1 transport.go:313] Unable to cancel request for *app.rejectIfNotReadyHeaderRT 2023-05-10T11:00:23.515915858Z E0510 11:00:23.515880 1 leaderelection.go:330] error retrieving resource lock kube-system/kube-controller-manager: Get "https://api-int.ocp4.example.com:6443/api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/configmaps/kube-controller-manager?timeout=5s": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers) 2023-05-10T11:00:34.240450285Z E0510 11:00:34.240383 1 leaderelection.go:330] error retrieving resource lock kube-system/kube-controller-manager: Get "https://api-int.ocp4.example.com:6443/api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/configmaps/kube-controller-manager?timeout=5s": context deadline exceeded ~~~
resolution: Fix the root cause of the delay in the underlying environment. The reasons include, but are not limited to:- Slow external DNS server configured in the control plane nodes.- Slow network.- Overloaded Hypervisors.- High API call counts by Service Accounts in system projects, make sure there are no ServiceAccount that belong to application or any monitoring solution created in any of the default `OpenShift` namespaces.
root_cause: `kube-controller-manager` waits 5 seconds (6 in recent versions) to complete the `configmap` read operation, and this timeout doesn't tolerate delays.

title: [RHOCP 4] Assisted Installer: Error Defining Bond via Form View - 'nmstate Generate Configuration Failed'
issue: - During the cluster installation process using the `Assisted Installer (AI)`, an error occurs when attempting to define a `bond` in the `FORM` view under `Step 2: Static network configurations`, specifically during the `Host specific configurations` phase.- Error observed while defining `bond` configurations: ~~~ 1 error occurred:

failed to validate network yaml for host 0, nmstate GenerateConfiguration failed, error: failed when generating the configuration {"dns-resolver":{"config":{"server":["xx.xx.xx.xx"]}},"interfaces":[{"link-aggregation":{"mode":"802.3ad","options":{"miimon":"100"},"port":["eth0","eth1"]},"name":"bond0","state":"up","type":"bond"}],"routes":{"config":[{"destination":"0.0.0.0/0","next-hop-address":"xx.xx.xx.xx","next-hop-interface":"bond0","table-id":254}]}} with rc: 1, err_msg: The next hop interface of desired Route 'destination: 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop-interface: bond0 next-hop-address: xx.xx.xx.xx table-id: 254' has been marked as IPv4 disabled, err_kind: InvalidArgument ~~~- Unable to define `bond` using `FORM` view
resolution: - The issue has been identified as a bug in RHOCP and is being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under [MGMT-19611](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MGMT-19611)- To work around the issue, use the `YAML` view for the time being until the bug is resolved.

title: Support Splunk as an output in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to forward OpenShift 4 logs to Splunk.- Does the Cluster Log Forwarder natively support Splunk?
resolution: Starting with RHOL 5.6 version, Splunk is supported using Vector as a collector according to [LOG-2913](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-2913). This is noted in the [Release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/logging/cluster-logging-release-notes.html#openshift-logging-5-6-enhancements_cluster-logging-release-notes-v5x). The documentation for this feature is already in the Red Hat Openshift Logging for RHOL 5: [Forwarding logs to Splunk](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/log_collection_forwarding/configuring-log-forwarding.html#logging-forward-splunk_configuring-log-forwarding).
root_cause: Starting with RHOL 5.6 version, the `ClusterLogForwarder` natively support Splunk as a log destination endpoint using Vector.

title: Adding SSH keys for core user post-install creates .ssh folder owned by root
issue: - If a cluster is installed without SSH keys and those are added post-install as per [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3868301), `/home/core/.ssh` is owned by root and SSH doesn't work.
resolution: This is a known issue, which is already fixed in the following versions:- 4.12.0+ as per [BZ#2107113](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2107113).- 4.11.3+ as per [OCPBUGS-509](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-509)- 4.10.31+ as per [OCPBUGS-642](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-642) The workaround is to just chown the folder to `core` user: ~~~ oc debug node/${NODE}-- chroot /host chown-R core. /home/core/.ssh Starting pod/example-worker-1examplenet-debug... To use host binaries, run `chroot /host` Removing debug pod... ~~~ Where `${NODE}` has to be replaced with the name of the node.
root_cause: Machine config daemon (component of Machine Config Operator in charge of applying configuration changes to nodes) runs as root and just creates the `/home/core/.ssh` folder as needed, but it doesnt set the right `core` user to it. This, in turn, makes SSH unusable. This problem doesn't reproduce if the cluster was installed with SSH keys or for nodes created after having configured the SSH keys, because in both cases, the files are created by ignition (not Machine Config Daemon) and ignition doesn't have this problem.

title: Logs are not visible in the Observe > Logs dashboard within the RHOCP Web Console due to dns error in RHOCP4
issue: - All the pods are up and running in `openshift-logging` namespace; however, the Logs dashboard displays `No datapoint found`.- Unable to see logs under `Observe > Logs` dashboard in OpenShift Webconsole.- `Vector` pods are continuously streaming following warning message: ~~~ YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.XXXXXZ WARN sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=output_default_lokistack_infrastructure component_type=loki}: vector::internal_events::http_client: HTTP error. error=error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known error_type="request_failed" stage="processing" internal_log_rate_limit=true ~~~
resolution: Kindly ensure that the name specified in the `ClusterLogForwarder` observability Custom Resource under `spec.outputs.lokiStack.target.name` aligns with the name of the corresponding `LokiStack` instance.- Step 1: Check `LokiStack` Custom Resource name: ~~~ $ oc get lokistack-n openshift-logging NAME AGE logging-loki 28h < <==== ~~~- Step 2: Use the same name in `ClusterLogForwarder` observability Custom Resource: ~~~ $ oc edit obsclf instance-n openshift-logging-o yaml--- spec: managementState: Managed outputs:- lokiStack: authentication: token: from: serviceAccount target: name: logging-loki < <==== This name should be same a LokiStack Custom Resource name namespace: openshift-logging---- ~~~ If a similar issue occurs in the `Red Hat OpenShift Logging version 5`, then please refer to [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6988840) for further assistance.
root_cause: The key `clusterlogforwarder.spec.outputs.lokiStack.target.name` must have the same value that the LokiStack resource name. **Other root causes** The DNS error in the collector pods when log forwarding to the Red Hat Managed Loki can also be produced by other root causes- The error was observed in the collector pods before the Loki pods were created- The `.spec.output[].lokiStack.target.namespace` is not set. See the article "[CLO doesn't set default value for `.spec.output[].lokiStack.target.namespace` when namespace is not set in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7102843)" for more details.

title: [RHOCP 4] Failed to Provision Physical Server on xFusion: Missing Boot Attribute in Redfish Manager API
issue: - Over 100+ `Baremetal` worker nodes need to be added to the cluster, and `BMO` is being used to `provision` the physical servers. However, the process fails with the following error when the server is defined as `/redfish/v1/Systems/1`. ~~~ Normal Registered 2m52s metal3-baremetal-controller Registered new host Normal BMCAccessValidated 2m42s metal3-baremetal-controller Verified access to BMC Normal InspectionStarted 2m42s metal3-baremetal-controller Hardware inspection started Normal ProfileSet 2m42s metal3-baremetal-controller Hardware profile set: unknown Normal InspectionError 2m32s metal3-baremetal-controller Failed to inspect hardware. Reason: unable to start inspection: No suitable virtual media device found ~~~- Explored the resources under the `Redfish API` and identified the `virtual media` under `/redfish/v1/Managers/1`. Attempted to provision the server by pointing to this `endpoint`, but encountered the following error: ~~~ Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal Registered 139m metal3-baremetal-controller Registered new host Normal RegistrationError 139m metal3-baremetal-controller Failed to get power state for node. Error: The attribute Boot is missing from the resource /redfish/v1/Managers/1 Normal RegistrationError 137m metal3-baremetal-controller Failed to get power state for node. Error: The attribute Boot is missing from the resource /redfish/v1/Managers/1 ~~~
resolution: - The recommended resolution is to update the `baremetal` machine's firmware to determine if newer versions have proper `Virtual Media` support implemented.- Verify with the `hardware vendor` if the server hardware in use supports the `Redfish API`.
root_cause: - The `VirtualMedia` version [1.0.2](https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/VirtualMedia.v1_0_2.json) is quite old and lacks the necessary functionality to support virtual media via `Ironic`.- The captured response from the output of the `Redfish endpoints` for `VirtualMedia` does not include the required `Actions`, such as [InsertMedia and EjectMedia](https://docs.openstack.org/ironic/latest/admin/drivers/redfish/OpenStackIronicProfile.v1_1_0.html#virtualmedia), which are essential for `Ironic` to function properly.

title: Prune user and identity based on last login in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to prune `users` and `identities` that have not `logged` in for a while?
resolution: - Currently, the RHOCP feature for automatically pruning users and their respective identities has not been tested yet.- Manually prune `inactive` `users` and `identities` using the following steps:- Retrieve `users` and their `identities`:- ~~~ $ oc get users ~~~- Filter `inactive` users:-- Identify `users` who have not logged in for a specified `duration` (e.g., 6 months, 1 year, etc.). Refer to this solution to [`check user login history in OpenShift`](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5357001).- Delete `inactive` users and identities:-- Remove the `filtered` users along with their corresponding `identities` from the system using following commands:- ~~~ $ oc delete user $ oc delete identity ~~~

title: Image Signature Pull Fails for OpenShift Images Due to Redirect to catalog.redhat.com
issue: - I am running a cluster with Cluster-Wide Proxy configured and internet traffic is routed through a firewall to reach `registry.redhat.io`- The error occurs when attempting to read the image signature from `catalog.redhat.com`, which results in failed image pulls- Image signature verification for OpenShift related images fails with the following error when pulling images: ``` $ podman pull--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-aws-efs-csi-driver-container-rhel8@sha256:aa6ec0d89349022d8872ed9488a9b3e11cfea26fecf96e06789ffcbc02d592f2 Trying to pull registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-aws-efs-csi-driver-container-rhel8@sha256:aa6ec0d89349022d8872ed9488a9b3e11cfea26fecf96e06789ffcbc02d592f2... Getting image source signatures WARN[0001] Failed, retrying in 1s... (1/3). Error: copying system image from manifest list: reading signatures: Get "https://catalog.redhat.com/api/containers/v1/signatures/reference/openshift4/ose-aws-efs-csi-driver-container-rhel8@sha256=d1f2546d6718914d39a76696ad4d10a452bac884127403414554411167f1aba3/signature-1": read tcp 10.245.247.65:39872-> 23.212.250.13:443: read: connection reset by peer ```
resolution: As a temporary workaround please add `catalog.redhat.com` to the firewall allowlist for any RHOCP VLANs in your environment. This will allow image signature requests to complete successfully. Once the action has been done you can check and confirm it works by: ``` $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host # curl-vvvL https://catalog.redhat.com ``` In order to track any upcoming permanent solution, please open up a case with the Red Hat Support Portal and explicitly indicate this KCS into the case.
root_cause: - The image signature verification process incorrectly redirects requests from `registry.redhat.io` to `catalog.redhat.com`, which is not documented as a required endpoint in the official [Red Hat OpenShift Documentation- Configuring your firewall chapter](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/installation_configuration/configuring-firewall#configuring-firewall_configuring-firewall).- This behavior is caused by a misconfiguration on the Red Hat Registry Proxy, which unintentionally redirects image signature verification requests to catalog.redhat.com instead of `access.redhat.com`- Customers are not expected to explicitly allow access to `catalog.redhat.com` for pulling images from `registry.redhat.io`

title: AMQ Streams: how can I control route names created by the operator?
product: Red Hat OpenShift Streams for Apache Kafka
issue: How can I control the route hostnames for AMQ Streams listeners? I need to specify hostnames for use with an external load balancer.
resolution: This is one use case for a [cluster-ip](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.8/html/deploying_and_managing_streams_for_apache_kafka_on_openshift/deploy-client-access-str#configuration-points-listeners-str) listener type and configuring advertised hosts. For example: ~~~- name: mytls port: 9094 type: cluster-ip tls: true configuration: brokerCertChainAndKey: secretName: mycert certificate: cert key: key brokers:- broker: 0 advertisedHost: mybroker0-myproject.apps.apps-crc.testing advertisedPort: 443- broker: 1 advertisedHost: mybroker1-myproject.apps.apps-crc.testing advertisedPort: 443- broker: 2 advertisedHost: mybroker2-myproject.apps.apps-crc.testing advertisedPort: 443 ~~~ Openshift routes can be created that point to the corresponding bootsrap service and broker cluster-ip services. For example: ~~~ apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1 kind: Route metadata: name: my-kafka-mytls-bootstrap namespace: myproject spec: host: my-kafka-mytls-bootstrap-myproject.apps-crc.testing port: targetPort: 9094 tls: termination: passthrough insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: None to: kind: Service name: my-kafka-mytls-bootstrap weight: 100 wildcardPolicy: None--- kind: Route apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: mybroker0 spec: host: mybroker0-myproject.apps-crc.testing to: kind: Service name: my-kafka-mytls-0 port: targetPort: 9094 tls: termination: passthrough insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: None wildcardPolicy: None... ~~~ When a client connects via a bootstrap server, the server will return the list of brokers in the above configuration (the advertised hosts/ports). The client will then use that list of hostnames for communication with the cluster.

title: Failed to get VolumeID from volumeMigrationService for volumePath
issue: After an OCP cluster is upgraded to a version where CSI migration of in-tree vSphere volumes is automatically enabled, volumes fail to attach with error: ~~~ rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to get VolumeID from volumeMigrationService for volumePath: "[] kubevols/.vmdk ~~~ Upon further inspection, following logs can be observed in the CSI driver pods: ~~~ 30T18:42:43.774562897Z","caller":"migration/migration.go:525","msg":"failed to register volume \".... error: ServerFaultCode: A specified parameter was not correct: dsDiskUrl","TraceId":"375e6e5f-da57-4d30-b20e-f0cdc3b8dfff"} ~~~
resolution: In order to avoid attach/detach issues on vSphere platform, once CSI migration is enabled- customers are recommended to specify full path to Datacenter and Datastore in cloud-config. Full path to Datacenter and Datastore can be obtained by logging into vCenter UI. Full path to Datacenter and Datastore can be specified by editing- cloud-provider-config in openshift-config namespace: ~~~ data: config: | [Global] secret-name = "vsphere-creds" secret-namespace = "kube-system" insecure-flag = "1" [Workspace] server = "vcenter.foobar.com" datacenter = "/folder/dc-name" default-datastore = "/folder/dc-name/datastore/ds-name" folder = "/folder/dc-name/vm/cluster-name" [VirtualCenter "vcenter.foobar.com"] datacenters = "/folder/dc-name" ~~~
root_cause: The root cause of this problem is, when an in-tree vSphere volume is migrated to CSI, on vSphere platform the volume *must* be registered as an FCD. The in-tree vSphere driver was a bit flexible in how the Datacenter path was specified, but when the volume gets converted to FCD, then the full path to the Datacenter must be used.

title: How to monitor JBoss EAP 7 in OpenShift monitoring
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Customer wish to monitor JBoss EAP related metrics in openshift monitoring, How to do that?
resolution: Metrics should come by default on template deployment in port 9990. Follow the steps below to- Import Jboss templates for more information and customization: ~~~ oc new-project eapdemo oc_project="$(oc project-q)" for resource in \ eap74-basic-s2i.json do oc-n "$oc_project" create-f \ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jboss-container-images/jboss-eap-openshift-templates/eap74/templates/${resource} done ~~~ Install jboss for test with `-e AB_PROMETHEUS_ENABLE=true` `-e JAVA_OPTS_APPEND=-Dwildfly.statistics-enabled=true` need to be added for jmx-exporter java agent that exposes Prometheus format metrics: ~~~ oc new-app--template=eap74-basic-s2i \-p IMAGE_STREAM_NAMESPACE=openshift \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_URL="https://github.com/jboss-developer/jboss-eap-quickstarts" \-p SOURCE_REPOSITORY_REF=openshift \-p CONTEXT_DIR=kitchensink \-e AB_PROMETHEUS_ENABLE=true \-e JAVA_OPTS_APPEND=-Dwildfly.statistics-enabled=true ~~~ Setup metrics related service ~~~ oc apply-f- < < EOF apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: labels: app: monitor_sample name: eap-app-metrics namespace: "$oc_project" spec: selector: deploymentConfig: eap-app ports:- name: metrics port: 9799 protocol: TCP targetPort: 9799 EOF ~~~ Make sure `enableUserWorkload: true` ~~~ oc-n openshift-monitoring edit configmap cluster-monitoring-config apiVersion: v1 data: config.yaml: | enableUserWorkload: true ~~~ Setup ServiceMonitor, as detailed on the solution [EAP 8 and 7 container image jmx-exporter agent](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7024587): ~~~ oc apply-f- < < EOF apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: ServiceMonitor metadata: name: monitor namespace: "$oc_project" spec: endpoints:- port: metrics selector: matchLabels: app: monitor_sample EOF ~~~ Check in the web UI openshift-> Observe-> Metrics Example: jboss_undertow_active_sessions [How to monitor HTTP Sessions to count / view the number of active HTTP sessions in JBoss EAP](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/22091) ### Updated on October 10, 2023 For JBoss EAP 7.3 and EAP 7, see the solution [How to enable Prometheus and statistics in EAP for OpenShift?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4152921) and for more details on the prometheus agent and test see solution [EAP 7 image jmx-exporter agent](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7024587). As explained above, in JBoss EAP 7.3 and 7.4 for OpenShift, `:9990/metrics` is exported by default via metrics subsystem. `AB_PROMETHEUS_ENABLE=true` is no longer needed to export metrics in Prometheus format. `AB_PROMETHEUS_ENABLE=true` is still available for backward compatibility in JBoss EAP 7.4 images. It is recommended the metric subsystem instead of `AB_PROMETHEUS_ENABLE=true` because metrics exporting by Prometheus JMX exporter exposes only some of the subsystem metrics listed in `/opt/jboss/container/prometheus/etc/jmx-exporter-config.yaml` on JBoss EAP container images as below. It does not contain `jboss_io_busy_task_thread_count` one of the key metrics of JBoss EAP (for more details about [BusyWorkerThreadCount](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2433971)): ~~~ whitelistObjectNames:- "jboss.as:deployment=*,subsystem=ejb3,*"- "jboss.as:deployment=*,subsystem=undertow"- "jboss.as:deployment=*,subsystem=undertow,servlet=*"- "jboss.as:deployment=*,subdeployment=*,subsystem=ejb3,*"- "jboss.as:deployment=*,subdeployment=*,subsystem=undertow"- "jboss.as:deployment=*,subdeployment=*,subsystem=undertow,servlet=*"- "jboss.as:subsystem=datasources,data-source=*,statistics=jdbc"- "jboss.as:subsystem=datasources,data-source=*,statistics=pool"- "jboss.as:subsystem=datasources,xa-data-source=*,statistics=jdbc"- "jboss.as:subsystem=datasources,xa-data-source=*,statistics=pool"- "jboss.as:subsystem=messaging-activemq,server=*,jms-queue=*"- "jboss.as:subsystem=messaging-activemq,server=*,jms-topic=*"- "jboss.as:subsystem=transactions"- "jboss.as:subsystem=undertow,server=*,http-listener=*" ~~~ In order to collect metrics exported by the metrics subsystem, the port needs to be changed from `9797` to `9990` in Service. The rest of the steps are the same as above. ``` oc apply-f- < < EOF apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: labels: app: monitor_sample name: eap-app-metrics namespace: "$oc_project" spec: selector: deploymentConfig: eap-app ports:- name: metrics port: 9990 protocol: TCP targetPort: 9990 EOF ```
