title: CLO doesn't set default value for `.spec.outputs[].lokiStack.target.namespace` when namespace is not set in RHOCP 4
issue: After configuring the clusterLogForwarder to log forward to the Red Hat Managed Loki, not logs are visible in the OpenShift Console and the collectors have a dns error to resolve the Loki IP address: ``` 2025-01-13T10:15:01.107136Z WARN sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=output_default_lokistack_infrastructure component_type=loki}: vector::internal_events::http_client: HTTP error. error=error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known error_type="request_failed" stage="processing" internal_log_rate_limit=true 2025-01-13T10:15:01.107264Z WARN sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=output_default_lokistack_infrastructure component_type=loki}: vector::sinks::util::retries: Retrying after error. error=Failed to make HTTP(S) request: Failed to make HTTP(S) request: error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known internal_log_rate_limit=true 2025-01-13T10:15:01.166864Z WARN sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=output_default_lokistack_infrastructure component_type=loki}: vector::internal_events::http_client: Internal log [HTTP error.] is being suppressed to avoid flooding. ```

It's observed a DNS error in the collector pods resolving the Red Hat Managed Loki, but it's not matching the article ["Logs are not visible in the Observe > Logs dashboard within the RHOCP Web Console due to dns error in RHOCP4"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7091175) as the `.spec.outputs[].lokiStack.target.name` matches the name of the LokiStack resource.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [LOG-6573](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6573). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. #### Workaround Set the `clusterlogforwarder.spec.outputs[].lokiStack.target.namespace` to the namespace where LokiStack resource is. In the example below, the `openshift-logging` namespace will be set. Edit the `clusterLogForwarder resource`, in this example called "collector" defined in the `openshift-logging` namespace ``` $ oc edit clusterLogForwarder-n openshift-logging ``` And add to the Red Hat Managed Loki output the key `clusterLogForwarder.spec.outputs[].lokiStack.target.namespace: opennshift-logging` as follows: ```--- OUTPUT OMITTED--- outputs:- name: default-lokistack type: lokiStack lokiStack: target: name: logging-loki namespace: openshift-logging <--- add this line--- OUTPUT OMITTED--- ```
root_cause: The Cluster Logging Operator doesn't set the `clusterlogforwarder.spec.outputs[].lokiStack.target.namespace` to `openshift-logging` as documented in the `clusterLogForwarder` CRD if it's unset: ``` $ oc explain clusterlogforwarder.spec.outputs.lokiStack.target.namespace GROUP: observability.openshift.io KIND: ClusterLogForwarder VERSION: v1 FIELD: namespace DESCRIPTION: Namespace of the in-cluster LokiStack resource. If unset, this defaults to "openshift-logging". ``` **Other root causes** The DNS error in the collector pods when log forwarding to the Red Hat Managed Loki can also be produced by other root causes- The error was observed in the collector pods before the Loki pods were created- The `.spec.outputs[].lokiStack.target.name` doesn't match the name of the LokiStack resource. See the article ["Logs are not visible in the Observe > Logs dashboard within the RHOCP Web Console due to dns error in RHOCP4"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7091175) for more details.

title: RHOCP 4.14 upgrade is stuck during ODF pod scheduling stage
issue: - During upgrade from OpenShift 4.12 to OpenShift 4.14.37 on AWS cloud provider rollout go in stuck during Ceph OSD pod scheduling on new nodes.
resolution: - To address the behaviour above pointed it is possible to use this upgrade path- **WARNING: cluster must be health and have OpenShift and ODF in version 4.12.x** 1. get openshift-storage nodes $ oc get node-l cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal Ready worker 22h v1.25.11+1485cc9 ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal Ready worker 22h v1.25.11+1485cc9 ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal Ready worker 22h v1.25.11+1485cc9 2. set environment var `NODE` according one node to change export NODE=ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal 3. label `NODE` with node name $ oc label node ${NODE} kubernetes.io/hostname=${NODE}--overwrite node/ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal labeled 4. get "mon" deployment on `NODE` $ oc get po-n openshift-storage-o wide | grep ${NODE} | grep-oP 'rook-ceph-mon-[a-z]*' rook-ceph-mon-a 5. patch "mon" deployment with new nodeSelector $ oc patch deploy rook-ceph-mon-a-n openshift-storage-p "{\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"spec\":{\"nodeSelector\":{\"kubernetes.io/hostname\":\"${NODE}\"}}}}}"--type merge deployment.apps/rook-ceph-mon-a patched 6. check that "mon" is Running as expected $ oc get po-n openshift-storage-o wide | grep rook-ceph-mon-a rook-ceph-mon-a-59567cbb7d-crhpx 2/2 Running 0 32s XX-XX-XX-XXX ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal 7. get all OSDs deployment Running on `NODE` $ oc get po-n openshift-storage-o wide | grep ${NODE} | grep-oP 'rook-ceph-osd-[0-9]*' rook-ceph-osd-0 8. delete all OSDs deployment Running on `NODE` $ oc delete deploy rook-ceph-osd-0-n openshift-storage deployment.apps "rook-ceph-osd-0" deleted 9. check that all OSDs pod on `NODE` are Running as expected $ oc get po-n openshift-storage-o wide | grep rook-ceph-osd-0 rook-ceph-osd-0-77f8cc7c59-67zh2 2/2 Running 0 3m15s XX-XX-XX-XXX ip-XX-XX-XX-XXX.eu-central-1.compute.internal 10. before going forward to next node check ceph health status NAMESPACE=openshift-storage;ROOK_POD=$(oc-n ${NAMESPACE} get pod-l app=rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}');oc exec-it ${ROOK_POD}-n ${NAMESPACE}-- ceph-s--cluster=${NAMESPACE}--conf=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/${NAMESPACE}.config--keyring=/var/lib/rook/${NAMESPACE}/client.admin.keyring cluster: id: b64b1293-bae8-408b-9b3f-83bedbc1d5a5 health: HEALTH_OK services: mon: 3 daemons, quorum a,b,c (age 11m) mgr: a(active, since 93m) mds: 1/1 daemons up, 1 hot standby osd: 3 osds: 3 up (since 5m), 3 in (since 22h) data: volumes: 1/1 healthy pools: 4 pools, 193 pgs objects: 3.55k objects, 11 GiB usage: 30 GiB used, 6.0 TiB / 6 TiB avail pgs: 193 active+clean io: client: 853 B/s rd, 299 KiB/s wr, 1 op/s rd, 11 op/s wr- **WARNING: all OSDs must be up and all placement group (pgs) must be active+clean**- repeat steps 2 to 10 by setting the variable `NODE` to the next openshift-storage node and being careful to select the corresponding MON and OSD running on that node. 1. annotate every MCH to paused $ oc get machinehealthcheck-n openshift-machine-api--no-headers | awk '{print $1}' | xargs-I MHC oc-n openshift-machine-api annotate mhc MHC cluster.x-k8s.io/paused=""--overwrite 2. set worker MachineConfigPool to.spec.paused=true 3. set channel to eus-4.14 4. upgrade OCP from 4.12.30 to 4.13.50 5. upgrade ODF to 4.13 6. upgrade OCP from 4.13.50 to 4.14.37 7. upgrade ODF to 4.14 8. remove paused annotation on every MCH $ oc get machinehealthcheck-n openshift-machine-api--no-headers | awk '{print $1}' | xargs-I MHC oc-n openshift-machine-api annotate mhc MHC cluster.x-k8s.io/paused-""--overwrite 9. set worker MachineConfigPool to.spec.paused=false 10. wait until all worker nodes are upgraded to CoreOS/rhel9.2
root_cause: - The issue is caused by the change occurring in CoreOS/Cluster Operators between version 4.13 and 4.14 in conjunction with OSD portability set to false.- Before the upgrade:- the nodes have the label *"kubernetes.io/hostname"* set according to the DHCP option set- the node names is a generic *"ip.region.compute.internal"*- After the upgrade to 4.14, and reboot to CoreOS 4.14/rhel9.2:- the label has been overwritten to the node name => *"kubernetes.io/hostname: ip.region.compute.internal"*- Furthermore following configurations of the *storagecluster cr* lead to have *nodeSelector* on both the *mon* and *osd* component (osd portability to false):- *nodeSelector* on the *mon* component is being added by the following configuration of the *storagecluster cr*: ~~~ spec: monDataDirHostPath: /var/lib/rook ~~~- *nodeSelector* on the *osd* component is being added by the following configuration of the *storagecluster cr*: ~~~ spec: storageDeviceSets:- config: {} portable: false ~~~

title: How to create user, identity and map user and identity in LDAP authentication for 'mappingMethod' as 'lookup' inside the OAuth manifest
issue: - LDAP users and identity inside the Red Hat OCP cluster will not be created automatically when 'mappingMethod' as 'lookup' inside the OAuth manifest- How to prevent users that are not part of certain LDAP groups from authenticating and logging in- Administrator wants to create user object and grant permission to user object before the actual LDAP user logins
resolution: ####What is 'mappingMethod' as 'lookup' inside the OAuth manifest?- Looks up an existing identity, user identity mapping, and user, but does not automatically provision users or identities- This allows cluster administrators to set up identities and users manually, or using an external process- Using this method requires you to manually provision users ####Create User- Creating a user with username as 'myuser' ~~~ $ oc create user myuser ~~~ ####Base64 encode that LDAP user- To create a user Identity in the next step, We need a base64 encoded LDAP string for the user- The following step depends on how you set `ldap.attributes.id`. If you set `ldap.attributes.id` to `dn`, then you need to encode the whole dn like this: ~~~ # Change 'uid', 'cn' and 'dc' values as per your LDAP config $ echo-n "uid=myuser,cn=users,cn=department,dc=ocp4,dc=example,dc=com" | base64 ==> dWlkPW15dXNlcixjbj11c2Vycyxjbj1kZXBhcnRtZW50LGRjPW9jcDQsZGM9ZXhhbXBsZSxkYz1jb20= ~~~- Remove last 'K' or '=' or '==' if you get it and make sure it's in one line. This is because the [code](https://github.com/openshift/oauth-server/blob/release-4.12/vendor/github.com/openshift/library-go/pkg/security/ldaputil/attribute.go#L43) will use `base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString` to encode the string and the padding character will be removed. To ensure the encoded string will work you could refer to the golang program in Diagnostic Steps.- The final string will look something like this 'dWlkPW15dXNlcixjbj11c2Vycyxjbj1kZXBhcnRtZW50LGRjPW9jcDQsZGM9ZXhhbXBsZSxkYz1jb20'- If you set ldap.attributes.id to a specified attribute, like sAMAccount in AD, then you only need to encode the sAMAccount- To confirm how you set ldap.attributes.id, you could verify this by checking ``` $ oc get oauth cluster-o yaml ``` ####Create the Identity- Creating the identity for LDAP identity provider by considering we have LDAP Identity working with the name 'ldapauth'. This name could be verified by running `oc get oauth cluster-o yaml`- Replace 'ldapauth' and base64 encoded values with your encoded ldap.attributes.id. In the following example, it is assumed that you set dn as the ldap.attributes.id, and your LDAP provider name is ldapauth. ~~~ $ oc create identity ldapauth:dWlkPW15dXNlcixjbj11c2Vycyxjbj1kZXBhcnRtZW50LGRjPW9jcDQsZGM9ZXhhbXBsZSxkYz1jb20 ~~~ ####User and identity Mapping- After the creation of user and identity, map both by using the user and identity mapping.- In the following example, it is assumed that you set dn as the ldap.attributes.id, and your LDAP provider name is ldapauth. ~~~ $ oc create useridentitymapping ldapauth:dWlkPW15dXNlcixjbj11c2Vycyxjbj1kZXBhcnRtZW50LGRjPW9jcDQsZGM9ZXhhbXBsZSxkYz1jb20 myuser ~~~

title: oc-mirror fails to mirror the images with error : 'invalid data: tag byte does not have MSB set'
issue: - While trying to mirror the images using `oc-mirror` utility, the mapping process fails with the following message:- ~~~ error: the config map openshift-config-managed/release-verification has an invalid key "verifier-public-key-redhat" that must be a GPG public key: openpgp: invalid data: tag byte does not have MSB set: openpgp: invalid data: tag byte does not have MSB set ~~~- The process fails for both [Partially connected mirroring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/disconnected/mirroring/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#mirroring-image-set-partial) as well as [Fully Disconnected mirroring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/disconnected/mirroring/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#mirroring-image-set-full)
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and for the resolution, the following bug was reported as per https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-43386- As a temporary workaround, make sure that the server on which mirror-registry is running doesn't have `FIPS` enabled.- If it is enabled, `Disabling FIPS` on the mirror server will solve the issue.

title: OpenShift 4.x router-default pod deployment failure: backend-http check failed: healthz
issue: - Router default pods in constant crash-loop back-off- Router default pods reporting the following error message: ~~~ I0401 12:04:27.349490 1 healthz.go:257] backend-http check failed: healthz [-]backend-http failed: backend reported failure I0401 12:04:28.354411 1 healthz.go:257] backend-http check failed: healthz [-]backend-http failed: backend reported failure I0401 12:04:29.349149 1 healthz.go:257] backend-http check failed: healthz [-]backend-http failed: backend reported failure ~~~
resolution: - Ensure that your pods are able to bind to port 80, 443 on the host.- Ensure that `localhost` resolves correctly.- Check that you do not have any security policies, antivirus, firewall rulesets that would otherwise prevent a container from binding to port:80 on the node.- We need to see (in a healthy deployment) that not only is port:80 in `LISTEN` state; but there are multiple health probes from localhost querying the socket in TIME_WAIT. ~~~ sh-4.4# netstat-antpu | grep:80 tcp 0 0 0.0.0.0:80 0.0.0.0:* LISTEN 1808790/haproxy tcp 0 0 127.0.0.1:80 127.0.0.1:33808 TIME_WAIT- tcp 0 0 127.0.0.1:80 127.0.0.1:56560 TIME_WAIT- tcp 0 0 127.0.0.1:80 127.0.0.1:42432 TIME_WAIT- ~~~
root_cause: - Router pods must be able to complete a health check on local port `80` in order to succeed a healthcheck.- This error message originates here: [see code snippet at github](https://github.com/openshift/router/blob/3065f6583f3925328fbdbfe95e3bc7bb7a084d33/pkg/router/metrics/health.go#L42)- HAProxy healthz probe is curling the following: ~~~ httpURL:= env("ROUTER_METRICS_READY_HTTP_URL", fmt.Sprintf("http://%s:%s/_______internal_router_healthz", "localhost", env("ROUTER_SERVICE_HTTP_PORT", "80"))) ~~~- Essentially; the pod must be able to resolve a `200` at the following curl location for the above to succeed: ~~~ curl http://localhost:80/_______internal_router_healthz ~~~- This has been observed previously on a cluster with RHEL nodes running an antivirus service that was preventing a process from binding to the socket at port 80, leading to a continuous health probe failure. Disabling said antivirus was sufficient to mitigate the issue.- This has also been observed previously on a cluster where twistlock service was getting OOM killed on infra nodes; and preventing the router pods from deploying successfully. See this KCS:[https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7001710](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7001710)- This issue can ALSO be caused by a configuration error with your `proxy` settings. Ensure that your NOPROXY variable entry includes the `subnet range for your nodes` and your `upstream loadbalancer` (if applicable); so that your nodes can talk to one another without routing through your proxy platform.- This issue also happened on a node in which the file `/etc/hosts` was manually edited to remove the line: ~~~ 127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6 ~~~

title: Why do I see "Unstable" when checking a broker on the  Streams for Apache Kafka Console
issue: - When checking the broker's list on the Streams for Apache Kafka Console, they appear as "Unstable", even when they are working ok- Also, I see "0/0" in the Overview page

This is one of the required prerequisites. title: HTTP2 connections load balancing in Openshift
issue: - We need guidance related with load balancing of long lived connection. HTTP/2 is one of the long lived connection protocol. Default HAProxy looks like load balance the traffic at first connection open request receive, if new connection open request receive then load balance it. But with a long lived connections, connection open one time and communication continue on it. How I can load-balance this traffic?- One more example related with our load balance question.- Imagine that there are 3 backend pod running http2 server and 1 client pod. If the client send http2 request it will be established with one of the server pod for example backend_pod 1. Because of connection established between client1 and backend_pod1 all request between client and backed_pod1 established over this connection. But during all request, backend_pod2 and backend_pod3 will not take any request.
resolution: - This seems to be a expected behaviour if the connection is long running and not closed(terminated) via client.- This is because, HTTP/2 allows multiple requests (streams) to be sent over the same connection. A single long-lived connection may monopolize one backend server, defeating the purpose of round-robin.- Better way is to Connection Drain and Redistribution: Some systems can enforce connection closure after a timeout or request limit. This forces clients to reconnect, allowing the load balancer to distribute new connections round-robin.

title: How to enable Datasource Statistics in EAP for OpenShift?
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: How to enable or disable Datasource Statistics in EAP for OpenShift?
resolution: The following method can be used to enable data source statistics: EAP version | Alternative----------|------- EAP 7 | JAVA_OPTS_APPEND=-Dwildfly.datasources.statistics-enabled=true EAP 8 | SERVER_ARGS=-Dwildfly.datasources.statistics-enabled=true `Datasource Statistics` are enabled via `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` environment variable in EAP 7.4 by adding the systems property `-Dwildfly.datasources.statistics-enabled`. This configuration can be done through the `oc` command to edit the deployment or direct YAML change on the deployment file. To `Enable` `Datasource statistics`, run the `oc` command below: ~~~ $ oc set env dc/$DC_NAME JAVA_OPTS_APPEND=-Dwildfly.datasources.statistics-enabled=true ~~~ To add environment variable through `YAML` in `Deployment config`, use the string below: ~~~- name: JAVA_OPTS_APPEND value: '-Dwildfly.datasources.statistics-enabled=true' ~~~ After applying the configuration, can see the changes below: ~~~ sh-4.4$ /opt/eap/bin/jboss-cli.sh--connect-c "/subsystem=datasources/data-source=postgresnonxa_postgres-DS1/statistics=pool:read-attribute(name=statistics-enabled)" {"outcome" => "success", "result" => true} sh-4.4$ sh-4.4$ /opt/eap/bin/jboss-cli.sh--connect-c "/subsystem=datasources/data-source=postgresnonxa_postgres-DS1/statistics=jdbc:read-attribute(name=statistics-enabled)" {"outcome" => "success", "result" => true} sh-4.4$ ~~~ **Note**: To disable the `Datasource Statistics`, it is necessary to change value `true` to `false`
root_cause: This setting only works if the configuration file, standalone-openshift.xml, has the property substitution as below example: ~~~...... /subsystem=datasources/data-source=PostgreSQLDS:read-attribute(name=statistics-enabled) {"outcome" => "success", "result" => expression "${wildfly.datasources.statistics-enabled:${wildfly.statistics-ena bled:false}}" <---------------------}...... [standalone@localhost:9990 /] /subsystem=datasources/data-source=PostgreSQLDS:read-attribute(name=statistics-enabled, resolve-expressions=true) {"outcome" => "success", "result" => "true" <---------------------} ~~~

title: How to Use OpenSSL to Check Secret Certificate Information in OpenShift
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - My certificate in Openshift Secret seems expired, how can I check?
resolution: In OpenShift, Certificates usually stored as secrets. It's possible to use `openssl` combined with `oc` commands to inspect the content of these certificates directly from the command line.- **View Certificate Details**: To view the details of a certificate stored in a secret: ```bash oc get secret [SECRET_NAME]-o jsonpath='{.data.[CERT_KEY]}' | base64--decode | openssl x509-inform PEM-text-noout- ``` Replace `[SECRET_NAME]` with the name of your secret and `[CERT_KEY]` with the key under which the certificate is stored, escaping the ".", e.g., `ca\.crt`.- **Check Certificate Expiry Date**: To view the expiry date of a certificate: ```bash oc get secret [SECRET_NAME]-o jsonpath='{.data.[CERT_KEY]}' | base64--decode | openssl x509-inform PEM-noout-enddate- ```- **Verify Certificate's Signature**: If you have the root certificate or the certificate of the issuer, you can verify the signature of the certificate in the secret: ```bash oc get secret [SECRET_NAME]-o jsonpath='{.data.[CERT_KEY]}' | base64--decode | openssl x509-inform PEM-noout-verify-CAfile /path/to/root_or_issuer.crt- ```- **Check Private Key Information**: If you have a private key stored in a secret and want to inspect its details: ```bash oc get secret [SECRET_NAME]-o jsonpath='{.data.[KEY_NAME]}' | base64--decode | openssl rsa-inform PEM-text-noout- ``` Replace `[KEY_NAME]` with the key under which the private key is stored, escaping the ".", e.g., `tls\.key`.- **Check if Certificate and Private Key Match**: Sometimes, you might want to ensure that a certificate and private key in a secret match: ```bash oc get secret [SECRET_NAME]-o jsonpath='{.data.[CERT_KEY]}' | base64--decode > cert.pem oc get secret [SECRET_NAME]-o jsonpath='{.data.[KEY_NAME]}' | base64--decode > key.pem openssl x509-noout-modulus-in cert.pem | openssl md5 openssl rsa-noout-modulus-in key.pem | openssl md5 ``` The MD5 hashes produced by the last two commands should match if the certificate and private key are a pair.

title: Kubelet configuration on Hosted Control Planes
issue: When doing customizations to kubelet on a standalone OCP cluster, a kubeletconfig CR (https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/rest_api/machine_apis/kubeletconfig-machineconfiguration-openshift-io-v1.html) is used, which creates a machineconfig CR containing the default kubelet configuration merged with the defined changes, and machine config operator applies the changes. However when doing the same on an HCP cluster there is no kubeletconfig CR to be used and the only way to change the configuration is to create the machineconfig configmap manually and reference it in the cluster nodepool, i.e. merge the default configuration with the requested changes. This works rather well, but has one problem = upgrades. When the default configuration changes while upgrading to a new OCP version, the change is overriden by the machineconfig. As such the solution can't be hardly called future proof. As such similar solution to the standalone functionality should exists for HCP clusters.

title: How to disable automatic boot source download and clean up the images in OpenShift Virtualization?
issue: - I disable the automatic boot source images to save space on the system- When I delete the PVCs, they recreate
resolution: ### Disable the automatic boot source images:- **Via CLI**: patch the HCO resource: ~~~ $ oc patch hyperconverged kubevirt-hyperconverged-n openshift-cnv--type json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/featureGates/enableCommonBootImageImport", "value": false}]' ~~~- **Via UI**: go to `Virtualization`-> `Overview`-> `Settings`-> `General settings`-> `Automatic images download`-> switch off the button ### Clean up the images:- **Via CLI**:- Delete the `DataVolumes` in `openshift-virtualization-os-images` namespace (and/or `VolumeSnapshots` for some storage types) that are managed by the `DataImportCron`- Note: If a DataVolume owns a PVC, and you just delete the PVC without deleting the DataVolume- the PVC will be recreated (a new import will start) ~~~ $ oc delete dv,VolumeSnapshot-n openshift-virtualization-os-images--selector=cdi.kubevirt.io/dataImportCron ~~~- **Via UI**:- Go to `Storage`-> `PersistentVolumeClaims` and delete the `PVCs` in `openshift-virtualization-os-images` namespace- Note: When we delete a `PVC` in UI, it deletes the `DV` under the hood- Go to `Storage`-> `VolumeSnapshots` and delete the `VolumeSnapshots` in `openshift-virtualization-os-images` namespace if they are present (relevant only for some storage types)

title: PrometheusRule To Get Alerts For Too Many Deployments in Namespace in RHOCP4
issue: - Monitor namespaces with a high number of Deployments through alerts.- High Deployment count may indicate resource management or application configuration issues.- Lack of alerts could lead to unnoticed excessive Deployments.- Unmonitored Deployments can result in performance degradation or resource exhaustion.
resolution: 1. Create a PrometheusRule YAML file (`prom-rule.yaml`) with the following content: ``` apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: deployment-alerts namespace: openshift-monitoring spec: groups:- name: kubernetes-deployment-alerts rules:- alert: TooManyDeploymentsInNamespace annotations: description: The current number of Deployment in namespace {{$labels.namespace}} is {{$value}}. summary: There are more than 50 Deployment in namespace {{$labels.namespace}}. expr: count(kube_deployment_status_replicas) by (namespace) > 50 labels: severity: critical ``` 2. Apply the PrometheusRule configuration to the cluster: ``` $ oc apply-f prom-rule.yaml ``` 3. Confirm the PrometheusRule is successfully applied and active: ``` $ oc get prometheusrule-n openshift-monitoring ``` 4. Ensure the rule is loaded into the Prometheus instance by checking the alerts: ``` $ oc exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-- curl-s http://localhost:9090/api/v1/rules | jq. ```
root_cause: - A high number of Deployments in a namespace can indicate:- Excessive workload deployments- Orphaned Deployments- Misconfigured applications- Monitoring and alerting on this condition helps:- Ensure timely remediation- Prevent potential resource exhaustion or performance degradation- There is a defined limit for every object to maintain good etcd health, as outlined here: [Object Maximums in OpenShift](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/scalability_and_performance/planning-your-environment-according-to-object-maximums.html)

title: Completing the Migration Toolkit for Containers operator installation
issue: - After installing the Migration Toolkit for Containers operator, it does not appear to be running properly- Only the Migration and ADP controller pods are running after installing the Migration Toolkit for Containers operator.
resolution: Create an instance of the `MigrationController` resource in the namespace where the Migration Toolkit for Containers operator was installed. This can be done from the web console by locating the Migration Toolkit for Containers Operator and from the `Details` tab, locating the `MigrationController` card under the `Provided APIs` section and clicking `Create instance`. This will trigger the deployment of the remaining pods that make up the running operator.
root_cause: After the Migration Toolkit for Containers operator has been installed for the first time, a `MigrationController` resource needs to be created to complete the deployment of the operator.

title: Where is DG Operator 8.4.10?
issue: - Where is DG Operator 8.4.10?- Where is DG Operator 8.4.10 when installing from the OLM console/operator hub?- Why DG Operator 8.4.9 skips 8.4.10 and goes to 8.4.11?- How can I upgrade from 8.4.9 to 8.4.11 given 8.4.10 is missing?
resolution: This is an innocuous label issue on version/index 8.4.9, which makes it bring 8.4.10 CSV. Therefore Operator 8.4.10 was skipped to avoid propagating this issue. Otherwise, the version difference would be always present, meaning one index would always bring the next CSV. Given it is innocuous it won't make any impact on the DG Operator installation/upgrade whatsoever. Example below installs Inded 8.4.9 which is equivalent to the CSV 8.4.10: ~~~ $ cat subscription.yaml apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: labels: operators.coreos.com/datagrid.openshift-operators: "" name: datagrid namespace: openshift-operators spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Manual name: datagrid source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 $ oc apply-f subscription.yaml subscription.operators.coreos.com/datagrid created $ oc get csv No resources found in openshift-operators namespace. $ oc get csv No resources found in openshift-operators namespace. $ oc get ip NAME CSV APPROVAL APPROVED install-hqtk9 datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 Manual false <------------- $ oc edit ip install-hqtk9 installplan.operators.coreos.com/install-hqtk9 edited $ oc get ip NAME CSV APPROVAL APPROVED install-hqtk9 datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 Manual true <-------------- $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 Data Grid 8.4.9 datagrid-operator.v8.4.8 Installing <--- Subscription Index version 8.4.9 brings CSV datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 ~~~ Upgrade example: ~~~ $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 Data Grid 8.4.9 datagrid-operator.v8.4.8 Replacing <- Index 8.4.9 CSV 8.4.10 datagrid-operator.v8.4.11 Data Grid 8.4.11 datagrid-operator.v8.4.10 Installing <- Index 8.4.1 CSV 8.4.11 ~~~
root_cause: This is an innocuous label issue on the index 8.4.9 that was skipped so it brings mistakenly 8.4.10 CSV. Given it is innocuous it won't make any impact on the DG Operator installation/upgrade whatsoever. Version | CSV----------|------- DG 8.4.8 | DG 8.4.8 CSV DG 8.4.9 | DG 8.4.10 CSV- mistake that brings 8.4.10 as CSV rather than 9- | DG 8.4.10 CSV- this is already installed on index 8.4.9 DG 8.4.11 | DG 8.4.11 CSV DG 8.4.12 | DG 8.4.12 CSV

title: System with IMSM raid5 array gets hung during shutdown
issue: - System with IMSM raid5 array gets hung during shutdown.- We updated the systemd rpm to `239-58.el8_6.7` version as suggested in [KCS solution 6970749](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970749), but the same issue still persists. There were following call traces logged on console during shutdown hang: dracut Warning: Killing all remaining processes XFS (dm-0): Unmounting Filesystem dracut Warning: Unmounted /oldroot. dracut: Disassembling device-mapper devices md: md120: resync interrupted. INFO: task reboot:7986 blocked for more than 120 seconds. Not tainted 4.18.0-372.9.1.el8.x86_64 #1 "echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/hung_task_timeout_secs" disables this message. task:reboot state stack: 0 pid: 7986 ppid: 1 flags:0x00004080 Call Trace:__schedule+0x2d1/0x830 schedule+0x35/0xa0 raid5_quiesce+0x12b/0x2d0 [raid456]? finish_wait+0x80/0x80__md_stop_writes+0x68/0x110 md_notify_reboot+0x51/0xf0 notifier_call_chain+0x47/0x70 blocking_notifier_call_chain+0x3e/0x60 kernel_restart_prepare+0x19/0x40 kernel_restart+0xe/0x30__do_sys_reboot+0x1d2/0x210?__fput+0xd0/0x250? syscall_trace_enter+0x1fb/0x2c0?__audit_syscall_exit+0x249/0x2a0 do_syscall_64+0x5b/0x1a0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x65/0xca RIP: 0033:0x7f00c1c344b7
resolution: - Red Hat engineering team is aware of this issue and it is being tracked in Jira RHEL-37209. **Note:** Above Jira ticket is marked as private, so customers could not access the same. Please get in touch with your Red Hat support representative for more information, current status of this Jira.- For now, this issue could be work-around by adding `mdraid` and `mdmon` to initramfs image. This would allow `mdmon` process to be available till the very end of shutdown sequence, even after switchroot: 1. Take the backup of current initial ram disk image: $ cp-av /boot/initramfs-$(uname-r).img /boot/initramfs-$(uname-r).bak1 $ ls-l /boot/initramfs-$(uname-r).img* 2. Rebuild the initial ram disk image including mdraid module in it: $ dracut-f-v-a mdraid 3. Reboot the system with above initial ram disk image.
root_cause: - The IMSM raid array requires `mdmon` process to handle the active stripes in the array. But during shutdown sequence, the mdmon process can get terminated before it could handle all the active stripes in IMSM raid array. In the absence of any `mdmon` process, the stop operation on IMSM raid array would get stalled indefinitely, this would result in shutdown hang.

title: OCP4: Keepalived/ip-failover for secondary VIPs and migrating to OVN-kubernetes
issue: - Migration to OVN-kubernetes is completed on OpenShift 4, but the secondary ingressVIP created manually for keepalive/ip-failover handling for sharded router pods is failing to accept traffic/not routable- Routes managed by secondary router-shard pods are not reachable after migration to OVN- Curling to the router pods directly allows traffic to flow to backends on sharded router pods, implying that the ingress VIP address configured manually for these secondary router deployments is failing.
resolution: - When migrating to OVN-kubernetes, a major functional change of the way networking is handled within CoreOS nodes is that the primary interface of the host is migrated to a managed network device named: `br-ex`. This interface claims the MAC address and primary IP of the default network device on the host, and is used for all inbound and outbound traffic to the node after migration.- If you have configured a secondary ip-failover deployment [as per our documentation](https://gss--c.vf.force.com/apex/Case_View?caseUpdatePageSize=200&sbstr=03956486#:~:text=https%3A//docs.openshift.com/container%2Dplatform/4.15/networking/configuring%2Dipfailover.html%23nw%2Dipfailover%2Dconfiguration_configuring%2Dipfailover), This deployment needs to be updated to point to the new interface `br-ex` instead of the default iface that was used when it was configured (ens192) for example.- Updating the deployment as highlighted below, will immediately allow the secondary VIP address to be hosted on a node and begin accepting traffic once again: ~~~- env:- name: OPENSHIFT_HA_CONFIG_NAME value: ipfailover- name: OPENSHIFT_HA_VIRTUAL_IPS value: xx.xx.xx.xx- name: OPENSHIFT_HA_VIP_GROUPS value: "10"- name: OPENSHIFT_HA_NETWORK_INTERFACE value: ens192 ##----------------------> CHANGE TO: `br-ex`- name: OPENSHIFT_HA_MONITOR_PORT value: "80" ~~~
root_cause: - The ipfailover process binds a primary IP address to an available network interface on the target hosts scoped to allow this configuration.- When OVN-kubernetes is deployed, a managed process called [ovs-configuration.service](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/master/templates/common/_base/units/ovs-configuration.service.yaml) is fired, calling the script: [/usr/local/bin/configure-ovs.sh OVNKubernetes](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/master/templates/common/_base/files/configure-ovs-network.yaml) to provision the network on the host.- If the OPENSHIFT_HA_NETWORK_INTERFACE variable is still set to the previous default interface on the host node--> bond0, ens3, ens192, etc, it will fail to route traffic appopriately. It must be informed of the configuration change and reference the new primary iface on the host: `br-ex` to utilize routing tables properly and redirect traffic to pods appropriately.

title: How to configure collector pods in OpenShift Logging 5
issue: How to define resources for collector pods?
How to define tolerations for collector pods?
How to define node selector for collector pods?
Not able to configure resource, node selector, limits, and requests in the collector configuration.
Since Vector or Fluentd is a part of RHOL, the collector pods may need to adjust their configuration.
resolution: > **Note:** for OpenShift Logging 6, refer to [configure Tolerations, NodeSelector & Resources for collector pods in OpenShift Logging 6](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7089916). Edit the `ClusterLogging` custom resource (CR) instance in `openshift-logging` project to configure the collector `resources` following the structure as in the example below: ~~~ $ oc edit ClusterLogging instance-n openshift-logging apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogging [...] spec: collection: resources: limits: cpu: memory: requests: cpu: memory: [...] ~~~ Edit the `ClusterLogging` CR instance in `openshift-logging` project to configure the collector `tolerations` following the structure as in the example below: ~~~ $ oc edit ClusterLogging instance-n openshift-logging apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogging [...] spec: collection: tolerations:- key: operator: Exists [...] ~~~ Edit the `ClusterLogging` CR instance in `openshift-logging` project to configure the collector `nodeSelector` following the structure as in the example below in which `nodeSelector` for `infra` nodes is configured: ~~~ $ oc edit ClusterLogging instance-n openshift-logging apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogging [...] spec: collection: nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: "" [...] ~~~
root_cause: The information about collector pods configuration is already in the documentation in [configuring resources and scheduling for logging collectors](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/scheduling_resources/logging-taints-tolerations.html#log-collector-resources-scheduling_logging-taints-tolerations) and [using tolerations to control log collector pod placement](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/scheduling_resources/logging-taints-tolerations.html#cluster-logging-collector-tolerations_logging-taints-tolerations).

title: Resources, tolerations and nodeSelector for the collector are missing in OpenShift Logging 5
issue: The custom definition for the `resources`, `nodeSelector` and `tolerations` for the collectors are missing after upgrading to RHOL 5.7.
The custom definition for the `resources`, `nodeSelector` and `tolerations` for the collectors are not present in the collector pods running.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in:- For RHOL 5.7 in bug [LOG-4185](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4185) fixed in RHOL 5.7.2 through ERRATA [RHSA-2023:3495](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3495)- For RHOL 5.6 in bug [LOG-4201](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4201) won't be backported. For RHOL 5.7 versions that include the fix, and newer RHOL 5 versions, refer to [how to configure collector pods in OpenShift Logging 5](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6999814) for the configuration. For RHOL 6, refer to [configure Tolerations, NodeSelector & Resources for collector pods in OpenShift Logging 6](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7089916) instead. ### Workarounds for versions that does not include the fix #### Workaround 1 Delete `.spec.collection.type`, this was introduced automatically in bug [LOG-4086](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4086) or in the workaround for [LOG-3049](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-3049). For doing it: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging patch clusterlogging/instance--type json-p '[{"op":"remove","path": "/spec/collection/type"}]' ~~~ Review that `.spec.collection.type` is not more present: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging get clusterlogging/instance-o jsonpath='{.spec.collection.type}' ~~~ Review the collector daemonset has now the `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.resources`, `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.tolerations` and `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.nodeSelector` defined: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging get clusterlogging/instance... $ oc get ds collector-n openshift-logging-o yaml... resources: limits: memory: 500Mi requests: cpu: 200m memory: 500Mi... tolerations:- effect: NoSchedule key: node-role.kubernetes.io/master operator: Exists- effect: NoSchedule key: node.kubernetes.io/disk-pressure operator: Exists- effect: NoSchedule key: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker-hp operator: Exists... ~~~ The collector pods should be restarted automatically by the ClusterLogging operator being applied the values in case defined for `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.resources`, `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.tolerations` and/or `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.nodeSelector` #### Workaround 2 Move all the definitions of the collector from `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.resources`, `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.tolerations` and/or `spec.collection.logs.fluentd.nodeSelector` as it's defined in the article [How to define the collector in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6999814)
root_cause: A fix prior to this change to remove defaulting of the `collection.type` resulted in the operator no longer honouring the deprecated spec for resource, nodeSelector, and tolerations. This modifies the operator behaviour to always prefer "collection.logs" spec over those of "collection". Note this varies from previous behaviour that allowed using both the preferred fields and deprecated fields but would ignore the deprecated fields when "collection.type" is populated.

title: Received  "unauthorized: authentication required" when the internal Image Registry is configured as Image Registry Source in OpenShift 4
issue: - After modifying the object `image.config.openshift.io/cluster`, adding `image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000` inside `{.spec.registrySources.containerRuntimeSearchRegistries[]}`, pulling an image from the internal registry results in "`unauthorized: authentication required`".- When the internal Image Registry is configured as a Registry Source, image pull fails with "`unauthorized: authentication required`" error messages.
resolution: > **Important notes:** > > 1. Apply this solution **only** if `image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000` is an element of the array `.spec.registrySources.containerRuntimeSearchRegistries`. Refer to the Diagnostic Steps section for additional information. > 2. The procedure listed below attaches a token to the `serviceaccount` that is not updated when regenerated. It is a procedure that changes the security posture of the cluster because it overrides the global pull secret to allow all namespaces to pull images. > 3. For more information on managing images, please refer to [the documented image management procedure](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/4.11/html/images/managing-images#using-image-pull-secrets). To solve the issue is needed to update the pull secret with the username and password used to access the registry; for that purpose in the following commands a service account `image-puller` is created (with the `system:image-puller` cluster role associated) and its username and token will be referenced inside the pull secret to authenticate the registry: ~~~ $ oc debug node/$(oc get node | grep master | head-1 | awk '{print $1}') [...] sh-4.4# chroot /host sh-4.4# oc login-u kubeadmin-p https://api..:6443 sh-4.4# oc create sa image-puller-n openshift-config sh-4.4# oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user system:image-puller-z image-puller-n openshift-config sh-4.4# TOKEN=$(oc create token image-puller-n openshift-config) sh-4.4# oc get secret pull-secret-n openshift-config-o json | jq '.data.".dockerconfigjson"'-r | base64-d > /tmp/pull-secret sh-4.4# oc registry login--registry=image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000--auth-basic=image-puller:${TOKEN}--to=/tmp/pull-secret sh-4.4# oc set data secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--from-file=.dockerconfigjson=/tmp/pull-secret sh-4.4# exit sh-4.4# exit ~~~
root_cause: If the internal Image Registry is added as a Registry Source, it is needed to add the credentials to the pull secret.

title: Unable to build EAP image on OpenShift with S2I and custom Galleon feature pack
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - Trying to build an EAP image on OpenShift using S2I and a custom Galleon feature pack fails with an error like the following: ``` [INFO] Resolving feature-packs [INFO]------------------------------------------------------------------------ [INFO] BUILD FAILURE [INFO]------------------------------------------------------------------------... [ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.jboss.eap.plugins:eap-maven-plugin:1.0.1.Final-redhat-00008:package (provisioning-layers) on project layers-provisioning: Provisioning failed: Can not resolve latest Maven artifact (no stream found):::zip:-> [Help 1] org.apache.maven.lifecycle.LifecycleExecutionException: Failed to execute goal org.jboss.eap.plugins:eap-maven-plugin:1.0.1.Final-redhat-00008:package (provisioning-layers jaxrs-server,postgresql-datasource,postgresql-driver,web-clustering) on project layers-provisioning: Provisioning failed... ``` The `buildconfig` uses the following Galleon environment variables: ``` GALLEON_PROVISION_CHANNELS="org.jboss.eap.channels:eap-8.0" GALLEON_PROVISION_FEATURE_PACKS="org.jboss.eap:wildfly-ee-galleon-pack,org.jboss.eap.cloud:eap-cloud-galleon-pack,:: " GALLEON_PROVISION_LAYERS="jaxrs-server, " ``` The issue also occurs when the `eap-maven-plugin` is configured similar to the above environment variables.
resolution: See the main solution [JBoss EAP 7 thin image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6960786) for details on galleon and [JBoss EAP 7 Galleon provisioning via provisioning.xml or eap-maven-plugin](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970360) for eap-maven-plugin options. In the_pom.xml_ for the_custom Galleon feature pack_, double-check the configuration of the `wildfly-galleon-maven-plugin` plugin and ensure that `wildfly-channel-resolution-mode` option is *not* specified. ``` org.wildfly.galleon-plugins wildfly-galleon-maven-plugin 6.4.9.Final-redhat-00001 eap-datasources-galleon-pack-build build-user-feature-pack compile REQUIRED_FP_ONLY true false ``` The `wildfly-channel-resolution-mode` tells Galleon how to resolve the feature pack when a channel is specified. If set to anything other than the default `NOT_REQUIRED`, Galleon will attempt to resolve the custom feature pack using the specified channel, i.e. those specified in `$GALLEON_PROVISION_CHANNELS`. Since the custom feature pack does not exist in the channel, the above error is returned. See the [wildfly-galleon-maven-plugin documentation](https://docs.wildfly.org/galleon-plugins/#wildflyChannelResolutionMode) for more info.
root_cause: For more information about using custom feature packs as well as links to a demo example, see [Chapter 8. Capability trimming in JBoss EAP for OpenShift](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/8.0/html/using_jboss_eap_on_openshift_container_platform/assembly_capability-trimming-in-jboss-eap-for-openshift_default#proc_preparing-the-maven-project_assembly_capability-trimming-in-jboss-eap-for-openshift) in the [Using JBoss EAP on OpenShift Container Platform](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/8.0/html/using_jboss_eap_on_openshift_container_platform/index) guide.

title: Will Red Hat release JBoss Web Server 6 Service Pack 4 (6.0.4) in archive format?
issue: - JBoss Web Server 6.0.4 is available only in rpm package. Will Jboss Web Server 6.0.4 be available in zip/archive format?
resolution: - There will not be a zip/archive update for JBoss Web Server 6.0.4.

title: Export OpenShift Container Platform Logs from Kibana or Elasticsearch
issue: - How to export logs from Kibana dashboard.- How to programmatically access logs from Elasticsearch based on a specific search in Kibana dashboard.
resolution: **Unsupported Procedure**: The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and supported procedures. The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the Operating System unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. The intent of this article is to provide information to accomplish the system's needs.- Currently it is not possible to collect logs from a specific search via Kibana's Web Console. However, if we look under the hood, Kibana queries Elasticsearch to obtain the log data for visualization, hence It is possible to copy the same query and use it with Elasticsearch directly.- In a nutshell we need three things: 1. Query Payload from Kibana 1. Access to Elasticsearch API 1. `jq` for processing JSON data Query Payload from Kibana ====================- Browse to the Kibana dashboard and in the "Discover" tab setup filters as required.- Once the filters are setup, open the developer tools from the browser and go the "Network" tab.- Clear all existing entries in the Network tab by clicking on the clear button.- While keeping the developer tools open, go to the Kibana dashboard and refresh the dashboard by clicking on the search icon at the top right of the dashboard.- Once the dashboard refreshes and the data loads, you should see a `_msearch` request in the Network tab of developer tool's. You can also set filter in the Network tab to "_msearch" to easily locate the request.- Click on the "_msearch" request to expand it and locate the request payload. In Chrome its at the end of the "Header" tab. In Firefox it is under the "Params" tab.- Copy the the complete request payload. It should be two lines. Adding new lines or beautifying it will break the API call. Note: If your Kibana dashboard timeline spans across multiple days, you will see multiple "_mseasrch" requests. These are the same queries for each dated Elasticsearch index. You can pick any one and later add the dated indexes in the `"index":[]` array located in the first line of payload copied. Access to Elasticsearch API =======================- There are many ways to access the Elasticsearch API for example, via the pod IP address, service URL/IP or by exposing the service etc. But for the sake of simplicity in this article we will access the Elasticsearch API directly from one of the Elasticsearch pods.- Log in to the OpenShift logging project where Elasticsearch pods are running and rsh into one of the pods. For example: $ oc project openshift-logging Already on project "openshift-logging" on server "https://ocp311.local:8443". $ oc get pods--selector 'component in (elasticsearch, es)' NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE logging-es-data-master-8tcn3gj9-6-84j5n 2/2 Running 0 10h logging-es-data-master-k664i0oo-6-n5lvd 2/2 Running 0 10h logging-es-data-master-wcaix6sd-6-xx2jh 2/2 Running 0 10h $ oc rsh logging-es-data-master-8tcn3gj9-6-84j5n Defaulting container name to elasticsearch. Use 'oc describe pod/logging-es-data-master-8tcn3gj9-6-84j5n-n openshift-logging' to see all of the containers in this pod. sh-4.2$- Elasticsearch API can then be securely acessed via curl like this: sh-4.2$ curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca https://localhost:9200/_cat/health?v epoch timestamp cluster status node.total node.data shards pri active_shards_percent 1574268876 16:54:36 logging-es green 3 3 225 225 100.0%- Create a new file (e.g, `vi /tmp/payload`) and paste the request payload copied from the previous section.- Call the Elasticsearch's multisearch API endpoint with this payload like this: curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'--data-binary "@/tmp/payload" https://localhost:9200/_msearch You should see raw json out put as the output of this command.- For a step by step procedure for extracting **audit logs** see the solution: [How to retrieve audit logs from Elasticsearch in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6979438). `jq` for processing JSON data ==============================- In the previous section we queried Elasticsearch with the payload we copied from Kibana, however the data was raw and not human readable. Now we will use `jq` to process and filter the data. If installing `jq` via RPM is not an option you can get the compiled binary directly from the github: curl-Lo jq https://github.com/stedolan/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64 chmod +x jq- Now we can pass the raw json output to jq and get human readable output, for example: curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'--data-binary "@/tmp/payload" https://localhost:9200/_msearch |./jq- By default Elasticsearch returns a lot of query metadata along with actual log data. To narrow down specifically on the log data you can use jq filtering, for example: curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'--data-binary "@/tmp/payload" https://localhost:9200/_msearch |./jq ".responses[].hits.hits[]._source"- Even the log data has a lot of fields. We can further narrow down, for example to only see the "message": curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'--data-binary "@/tmp/payload" https://localhost:9200/_msearch |./jq ".responses[].hits.hits[]._source.message"- We can even also combine multiple fields, for example: curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'--data-binary "@/tmp/payload" https://localhost:9200/_msearch |./jq-r ".responses[].hits.hits[]._source | [.kubernetes.pod_name,.level,.message]"- This can then be exported directly to CSV using jq: curl-s--key /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-key--cert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-cert--cacert /etc/elasticsearch/secret/admin-ca-H 'Content-Type: application/json'--data-binary "@/tmp/payload" https://localhost:9200/_msearch |./jq-r ".responses[].hits.hits[]._source | [.kubernetes.pod_name,.level,.message] | @csv" > export.csv

title: How to grant permission to create Ray clusters and distributed workloads in RHOAI
issue: Users cannot create Ray clusters or distributed workloads in namespaces where they have `admin` or `edit` permissions.
resolution: To grant the appropriate permissions, create a ClusterRole for the resources created by the KubeRay Operator and CodeFlare Operator, and specify the `admin` and `edit` aggregation labels. Note that the KubeRay Operator and CodeFlare Operator are included in the Red Hat OpenShift AI product, and should not be installed separately. Complete the following steps as a user with `cluster-admin` permissions: 1. Create a file named `dw-roles.yaml` with the following content: ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: kuberay-edit-role labels: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/aggregate-to-edit: "true" rbac.authorization.k8s.io/aggregate-to-admin: "true" rules:- apiGroups:- ray.io resources:- rayjobs- rayclusters- rayservices verbs:- create- delete- get- list- patch- update- watch- apiGroups:- workload.codeflare.dev resources:- appwrappers verbs:- create- delete- get- list- patch- update- watch ~~~ 2. Run the YAML file: ~~~ oc apply-f dw-roles.yaml ~~~ Users with `admin` or `edit` privileges in the namespace associated with their data science project can now create Ray clusters and distributed workloads. This fix changes the permissions for all namespaces in the OpenShift cluster; therefore, you apply this fix only once.
root_cause: Red Hat OpenShift AI does not provide an access role for the resources created by the KubeRay Operator and CodeFlare Operator.

title: Collector pod is failing to mount a secret with error secret "collector" not found
issue: - Collector pod in Pending state with below error: ~~~ 12s Warning FailedMount pod/collector-bpd65 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "collector": secret "collector" not found ~~~
resolution: [Uninstall](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/cluster-logging-uninstall.html#uninstall-es-operator_cluster-logging-uninstall) the Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator and [install](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/cluster-logging-deploying.html) as documented where:- the **Installation Mode** is **All namespaces on the cluster**- and the **Installed Namespace** is **openshift-operators-redhat** Another option in case that not desired to use the Red Hat Log Store Elasticsearch is to create or modify the [`clusterLogForwarder`](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/log_collection_forwarding/configuring-log-forwarding.html) resource to log forward the logs to the not **default** log store.
root_cause: If the `clusterLogging` resource is configured with the `spec.logStore.type: elasticsearch` to log forward to it and 1. The Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator is not installed or not installed as documented with:- the **Installation Mode** is **All namespaces on the cluster**- and the **Installed Namespace** is **openshift-operators-redhat** 2. Or any problem existed during the Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator that avoids the deployment of the Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator and creation of the Elasticsearch pods in the `openshift-logging` namespace In any of the both cases, the Red Hat Cluster Logging Operator shouldn't be able to create the **collector** secret needed by the collector pods.

title: After updating Jenkins pod container image in OpenShift, it has stopped working
issue: After updating the Jenkins container image version provided by Red Hat, Jenkins is not working as expected.
After updating the OpenShift cluster, the Jenkins pod is not starting up.
Builds are failing after the Jenkins version update.
Jenkins agent pods are not being created after the Jenkins update.
The Pipelines and jobs are not showing up at the Jenkins dashboard.
resolution: Many different reasons could cause this. A Jenkins downgrade should never be performed in a Jenkins instance.
root_cause: There are many possible root causes for this kind of issue, some of the most common are: * Plugin incompatibilities. * Plugin unsatisfied dependencies. * Jenkins incompatibility with installed plugins. When a Jenkins plugin is not capable of being loaded because of an incompatibility or unsatisfied dependencies (either not loaded or not installed) there are many possible consequences in the Jenkins instance: * Jobs not showing up at the Jenkins Dashboard. * Jobs cannot be executed. * Jenkins does not startup. The impact depends on the affected plugin, whether it adds new features or it is a GUI plugin.

title: Change replication policy for cluster logging on OpenShift 4
issue: - Is it possible to change the shard replication policy in the `clusterLogging` custom resource (CR) post cluster installation for log the store Elasticsearch?- The `clusterLogging` CR has been configured with `ZeroRedundancy` replication policy with installation with `nodeCount` to be 1. Could post-installation be changed the Elasticsearch replication policy?- Is it supported to change the `redundancyPolicy` several times for the same cluster?
resolution: The Elasticsearch `replicationPolicy` can always be modifie post Elasticsearch deployment. Review the documentation section "[Configuring replication policy for the log store](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/log_storage/logging-config-es-store.html#cluster-logging-elasticsearch-ha_logging-config-es-store] for the replication policy supported and how to change them. Let's consider the notes in the documentation about the performance and availability of the data depending on the `redundancyPolicy` chosen. Before changing the `replicationPolicy`, it should be verified that:- the Elasticsearch cluster is in **green status**- the `clusterLogging` and the `elasticsearch` custom resources (CR) are in `managementState: Managed` for the operator take into consideration the changes- the Elasticsearch nodeCount is enough for the `redundancyPolicy` set, if the `redundancyPolicy` is different to **ZeroRedundancy**, then, the number of Elasticsearch nodes should be greater than 1, the recommended is having at least 3 Elasticsearch nodes. #### Complete steps for changing the `redundancyPolicy` from **SingleRedundancy** to **FullRedundancy**. 1. Verify the current `redundancyPolicy` where it's set in this example to **SingleRedundancy** ``` $ oc get clusterLogging instance-o jsonpath='{.spec.logStore.elasticsearch.redundancyPolicy}'-n openshift-logging SingleRedundancy ``` 2. Verify that the `clusterLogging` and the `elasticsearch` CR are in `managementState: Managed` ``` $ oc get clusterlogging instance-n openshift-logging-o jsonpath='{.spec.managementState}' Managed $ oc get elasticsearch elasticsearch-n openshift-logging-o jsonpath='{.spec.managementState}' Managed ``` 3. Verify the number of nodes is greater than 1: ``` $ oc get clusterlogging instance-n openshift-logging-o jsonpath='{.spec.logStore.elasticsearch.nodeCount}' 3 ``` 4. Verify that the Elasticsearch cluster is in **green** status: ``` $ es_pod=$(oc get pods-l component=elasticsearch-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'-n openshift-logging) $ oc-n openshift-logging rsh $es_pod health Defaulted container "elasticsearch" out of: elasticsearch, proxy Thu Jan 16 16:12:56 UTC 2025 epoch timestamp cluster status node.total node.data shards pri relo init unassign pending_tasks max_task_wait_time active_shards_percent 1737043976 16:12:56 elasticsearch green 3 3 16 8 0 0 0 0- 100.0% ``` 5. Verify the number of replicas (**rep** column) in the output. As in this case, it's **SingleRedundancy**, it should exist 1 replica per primary indice. ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging rsh $es_pod indices Defaulted container "elasticsearch" out of: elasticsearch, proxy Thu Jan 16 16:14:32 UTC 2025 health status index uuid pri rep docs.count docs.deleted store.size pri.store.size green open.kibana_1 kLmCekfVSk2_pOhffWkN1g 1 1 0 0 0 0 green open.security zQVqBb3wQJCUsp20JFgP2g 1 1 6 1 0 0 green open app-000001 oNPUu-iPTlCp398JV4elHA 3 1 15129 0 21 10 green open infra-000001 4LncLLzYSG2Wcx2i1KqEnQ 3 1 4529469 0 5512 2783 ``` 6. Change the `redundancyPolicy`. In the example below, it will be changed to **FullRedundancy**: ``` $ $ oc-n openshift-logging patch clusterlogging/instance--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"logStore":{"elasticsearch":{"redundancyPolicy":"FullRedundancy"}}}}' clusterlogging.logging.openshift.io/instance patched ``` 7. Review that the number of replicas per primary indice (**rep** column) has increased to be `(Number of nodes)- 1` as the [Configuring replication policy for the log store](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/log_storage/logging-config-es-store.html#cluster-logging-elasticsearch-ha_logging-config-es-store) indicates. In this example the number of nodes is 3, then, it will have 2 replicas. ``` $ oc-n openshift-logging rsh $es_pod indices|egrep "infra|app|audit|^health" health status index uuid pri rep docs.count docs.deleted store.size pri.store.size Defaulted container "elasticsearch" out of: elasticsearch, proxy green open app-000001 oNPUu-iPTlCp398JV4elHA 3 2 15191 0 37 14 green open infra-000001 4LncLLzYSG2Wcx2i1KqEnQ 3 2 4551404 0 8308 2800 ``` Once it's changed the `redundancyPolicy`, depending on the number of indices and the size of them, the time may vary on getting all the replicas available for all the indices when increasing the number of replicas as it needs to transfer the data to the Elasticsearch nodes.

title: OpenShift GitOps: failed to load open api schema while syncing cluster cache
issue: - The ArgoCD is not able to connect to default/remote cluster and throwing below error: Failed to load live state: failed to get cluster info for "https://kubernetes.default.svc": error synchronizing cache state: failed to load open api schema while syncing cluster cache: error getting openapi resources: the server is currently unable to handle the request- In `openshift-kube-apiserver` pod getting below error: 2024-11-13T19:03:37.422521016Z E1113 19:03:37.422390 19 handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/route.openshift.io/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/routes/{name}/status
resolution: Remove the `routes.route.openshift.io` CustomResourceDefinition[CRD]: $ oc delete crd routes.route.openshift.io
root_cause: - By default, `Route` has no CRD and there was one CRD with name `Route` present on cluster which caused this issue.
