title: Tuning the Undertow Thread Pool in JBoss EAP 7.x and 8.x
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: How to tune Undertow thread pool in JBoss EAP 7
I'm curious how many connector threads we have for https by default?
How do I configure the max servlet threads
How does request queuing work in JBoss EAP 7 when under heavy load
resolution: * To set the value for `task-max-threads` in JBoss CLI, for example `128` ***Standalone Mode*** [standalone@localhost:9990 /] /subsystem=io/worker=default/:write-attribute(name=task-max-threads,value=128) {"outcome" => "success", "response-headers" => {"operation-requires-reload" => true, "process-state" => "reload-required"}} [standalone@localhost:9990 /]:reload {"outcome" => "success", "result" => undefined} ***Domain Mode*** you need to specify `/profile= /` to suite your environment. The following is for example with `default` profile. [domain@localhost:9990 /] /profile=default/subsystem=io/worker=default/:write-attribute(name=task-max-threads,value=128) {"outcome" => "success", "result" => undefined, "server-groups" => undefined} ***JBoss EAP for OpenShift*** It can be configured by [mounting a custom script in ConfigMap](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.3/html/getting_started_with_jboss_eap_for_openshift_container_platform/reference_information#custom_scripts). The custom script function is available in `jboss-eap-7/eap72-openshift:1.2` or later. $ cat extensions/postconfigure.sh #!/bin/sh echo "Executing postconfigure.sh" $JBOSS_HOME/bin/jboss-cli.sh--file=$JBOSS_HOME/extensions/extensions.cli $ cat extensions/extensions.cli embed-server--std-out=echo--server-config=standalone-openshift.xml batch /subsystem=io/worker=default:write-attribute(name=task-max-threads,value=10) run-batch quit $ oc create configmap jboss-cli--from-file=postconfigure.sh=extensions/postconfigure.sh--from-file=extensions.cli=extensions/extensions.cli $ oc set volume dc/eap-app--add--name=jboss-cli-m /opt/eap/extensions-t configmap--configmap-name=jboss-cli--default-mode='0755' * To set it directly in `standalone.xml` or `domain xml`, add the `task-max-threads` parameter to the io subsystem's default worker, for example: * To avoid performance issues related to thread pool exhaustion `task-max-threads` should always be greater than the expected maximum concurrent request count. Note that certain application designs (like using asynchronous servlets or invoking EJBs residing on the same container) may lead to consuming more than one task thread per request so in these cases `task-max-threads` need to be adjusted accordingly. ***Note*** The task thread pool uses an unbounded queue which cannot be adjusted. If limiting request queuing is required, the request limit filter can be configured with a desired queue size as per [How to configure max concurrent requests limit for specific application in JBoss EAP 7](/solutions/2961121). ***Note:*** There is a known issue per [I/O threads experience increased CPU usage for https-listener when task worker thread pool is exhausted in JBoss EAP 7](/solutions/7031598) allowing for increased CPU if all task threads are in use. As written in the knowledge, you can try either of the following as a workaround:- [How to configure max concurrent requests limit for specific application in EAP 7](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2961121): With this configuration, you can tune in a manner to avoid this possibility by setting a request-limit filter to the desired number of concurrent requests and setting task-max-threads to a value greater than that.- [How to specify a custom task worker thread pool for the specific application in JBoss EAP 7](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6998221): With this configuration, you can separate worker thread pool for each thread pool.
root_cause: * JBoss EAP 7 uses Undertow as the default web container, In Undertow by default all listener will use the default worker which is provided by the IO subsystem. This worker instance manages the listeners (AJP/HTTP/HTTPS) IO threads. * The IO Threads are responsible to handle incoming requests. The IO subsystem worker will provide the following options to tune it further. /subsystem=io/worker=default/:read-resource(recursive=false) {"outcome" => "success", "result" => {"io-threads" => undefined, "stack-size" => 0L, "task-keepalive" => 60, "task-max-threads" => undefined}} Where, * `io-threads`: Specify the number of I/O threads to create for the worker. If not specified, a default will be chosen, which is calculated by `cpuCount * 2` * `stack-size`: The `stack size (in bytes)` to attempt to use for worker threads. * `task-keepalive`: Specify the number of milliseconds to keep non-core task threads alive. However, this setting does not become effective because there's no setting for core size of task threads and core size is always same to max size. * `task-max-threads`: Specify the maximum number of threads for the worker task thread pool. If not specified, default value used which is calculated by formula `cpuCount * 16`

title: Is Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4 compliant with FIPS?
product: Red Hat build of Apache Camel for Spring Boot
Red Hat build of Apache Camel for Quarkus
issue: Is Camel 4 compliant with FIPS?
Has Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4 been FIPS certified (validated) by NIST?
Can Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4 be run on FIPS enabled OpenJDK / RHEL?
resolution: **Important:** No version of Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4.x is FIPS validated! Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4.x has not undergone official FIPS certification (validation) and does not aim to do so. It did not complete the NIST CMVP process to receive a certificate from NIST. Red Hat build of Apache Camel is not fully designed for FIPS because some Camel components may register security providers that are not FIPS validated, like bouncycastle. However, Red Hat supports running **Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4.x** on FIPS enabled OpenJDK / RHEL / OpenShift. We have validated that running Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4.x on a FIPS enabled OpenJDK /RHEL / OpenShift does not break any Camel component nor the Camel runtime. Camel functions the same way as when running on a non-FIPS enabled and supported JDK. See the Red Hat build of Apache Camel [supported configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7037134) page for the specific Java versions supported. For more details on Red Hat Enterprise Linux and its cryptographic modules see [Compliance activities and government standards](https://access.redhat.com/articles/compliance_activities_and_gov_standards#fips-140-2-and-fips-140-3-2) ## Camel Components designed for FIPS All supported Camel components (except those listed below) and the Camel core runtime are designed for FIPS. That means they can be configured to use FIPS validated cryptographic modules. **Note:** Natively compiled Camel Quarkus applications are **not** designed for FIPS. Quarkus does currently not support running native applications on FIPS enabled RHEL. The [supported](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_apache_camel/4.4/html/red_hat_build_of_apache_camel_for_quarkus_reference/ref_reference#ref_supported-cxf-modules) modules of CXF for Quarkus and Spring Boot are also designed for FIPS from our Camel 4.8 release onwards. More specifically WS-Security in CXF can be configured to only use FIPS validated cryptography. See the [release notes](https://docs.quarkiverse.io/quarkus-cxf/dev/release-notes/3.8.1.html#_running_on_systems_with_fips_assertions_enabled). ## Camel Components not designed for FIPS The list of Camel components below may register and use security providers and cryptographic modules that are not FIPS validated. Whoever, these components won't break the application when being run in a FIPS enabled environment, they will function correctly.- `camel-ftp`- `camel-kafka`- ONLY IF used for SASL/SCRAM auth- `camel-smb`- `camel-ssh` Starting from Camel 4.8 `camel-cxf-soap` and `camel-crypto` are now also designed for FIPS, i.e. they use FIPS validated cryptographic modules.

title: Assisted installer returns an error when a new host is discovered: "No elegible disks were found"

title: Microsoft Entra ID group claims combine unexpectedly in OpenShift 4
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: What is the correct endpoint to configure Microsoft Entra ID (formerly known as Azure Active Directory) as an OIDC in OpenShift 4?
Adding users using Entra ID configured as an OIDC create malformed group entries in OCP 4.

When configuring Entra ID with the [OpenID Connect group claim attribute](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/authentication/identity_providers/configuring-oidc-identity-provider.html#identity-provider-oidc-CR_configuring-oidc-identity-provider) in the `OAuth` `CustomResourceDefinition` (`CRD`) all groups provided by the claim are unexpectedly combined together, instead of being added to multiple individual groups. This issue creates groups that appear like this: ~~~ kind: Group apiVersion: user.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: >- ["xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx","yyyyyyyy-yyyy-yyyy-yyyy-yyyyyyyyyyyy","zzzzzzzz-zzzz-zzzz-zzzz-zzzzzzzzzzzz"] uid: b3ed0b40-ffd3-5r0c-fcas-3b780aa40b3f resourceVersion: '1234' creationTimestamp: '2022-07-27T18:20:48Z' annotations: oauth.openshift.io/generated: 'true' oauth.openshift.io/idp.Entra: synced users:- example@example.com ~~~
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Ensure that the `issuer` URL specified in the `OAuth` `CustomResourceDefinition` (CRD) for the `openID` field is set to the Microsoft Entra ID v2.0 endpoint. The v2.0 endpoint format is: ~~~ https://login.microsoftonline.com/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/v2.0 ~~~ Where `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` is the Microsoft Entra ID application's tenant ID.
root_cause: The Microsoft Entra ID v1.0 endpoint concatenates groups together in the response provided to OpenShift. The Microsoft Entra ID v2.0 endpoint does not do this.

title: JBoss EAP 8 custom MicroProfile Health probe
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How to create a JBoss EAP 7/8 custom MicroProfile Health probe?- How to customize a MicroProfile Health probe?
resolution: On the `pom.xml` use the following dependencies in the dependencyManagement: ~~~ org.jboss.bom jboss-eap-ee-with-tools 8.0.0.GA-redhat-00009 pom import org.jboss.bom jboss-eap-xp-microprofile 5.0.0.GA-redhat-00009 pom import ~~~ With the following dependency: ~~~ org.eclipse.microprofile.health microprofile-health-api provided ~~~ Combined with the feature pack: `org.jboss.eap.xp:wildfly-galleon-pack`- not EAP 8's `org.jboss.eap:wildfly-ee-galleon-pack`. The code will have a simple Maven project structure: ~~~ ├── src │ ├── main │ │ ├── java │ │ │ └── org │ │ │ └── wildfly │ │ │ └── quickstarts │ │ │ └── microprofile │ │ │ └── health │ │ │ ├── DatabaseConnectionHealthCheck.java │ │ │ ├── DataHealthCheck.java │ │ │ ├── JaxRsApplication.java │ │ │ ├── RootResource.java │ │ │ └── SimpleHealthCheck.java ~~~ Example of Health Check using the `@Liveness` endpoint: ~~~ import org.eclipse.microprofile.health.HealthCheck; import org.eclipse.microprofile.health.HealthCheckResponse; import org.eclipse.microprofile.health.Liveness; import jakarta.enterprise.context.ApplicationScoped; @Liveness @ApplicationScoped public class SimpleHealthCheck implements HealthCheck {@Override public HealthCheckResponse call() {return HealthCheckResponse.named("Simple health check").up().build();}} ~~~
root_cause: To use MicroProfile Health, one must use EAP XP 5 feature pack (`org.jboss.eap.xp:wildfly-galleon-pack`) instead of the EAP 8 feature pack (`org.jboss.eap:wildfly-ee-galleon-pack`). Using both feature packs usually results in the custom health probe being ingnored.

title: How to install SAP JCo and SAP IDoc libraries for camel-sap-starter into the Java runtime on OCP
product: Red Hat build of Apache Camel for Spring Boot
issue: The official document says user needs to install SAP JCo and SAP IDoc libraries into the Java runtime on OCP [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_apache_camel/4.8/html/red_hat_build_of_apache_camel_for_spring_boot_reference/csb-camel-sap-component-starter#sap_jco_and_sap_idoc_libraries](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_apache_camel/4.8/html/red_hat_build_of_apache_camel_for_spring_boot_reference/csb-camel-sap-component-starter#sap_jco_and_sap_idoc_libraries) What's the official instruction to install SAP JCo and SAP IDoc libraries into the Java runtime on OCP?
resolution: Since required instructions are different between "running on OCP" and "running on local", we recommend to create 2 maven profiles, "openshift" and "local". [Instructions] 1: Prepare the sap libraries in the ${Project}/lib directory. 2: Define dependencies in the pom.xml. 3: Define spring-boot-maven-plugin. 4: Define openshift-maven-plugin. 5: Define properties. **[1: Install artifacts into the local maven repository]** Under the ${project}/lib directory, store required sap libraries. **[2: Define dependencies in the pom.xml]** Define dependencies. ~~~ com.sap.conn.jco sapjco3 ${sapjco3-version} system ${basedir}/lib/sapjco3.jar com.sap.conn.idoc sapidoc3 ${sapidoc3-version} system ${basedir}/lib/sapidoc3.jar ~~~ **[3: Define spring-boot-maven-plugin]** For "local" profile: ~~~ org.springframework.boot spring-boot-maven-plugin ${spring.boot-version} repackage ${basedir}/lib ~~~ For "openshift" profile: ~~~ org.springframework.boot spring-boot-maven-plugin ${spring.boot-version} repackage ZIP com.sap.conn.jco,com.sap.conn.idoc ~~~ **[4: Define openshift-maven-plugin]** ~~~ org.eclipse.jkube openshift-maven-plugin 1.16.2.redhat-00013 ${project.build.finalName} ${project.build.finalName} ${jkube.generator.from} /deployments lib lib data-Dloader.path=/deployments/data resource build apply ~~~ **[5: Define properties]** Define openshift-maven-plugin for "openshift" profile: ~~~ 8080 ~~~ If you want openshift-maven-plugin to use "Deployemnt" instead of "DeploygmentConfig", there are 2 extra steps. **[6:Add "jkube.build.switchToDeployment" property in the pom.xml]** ~~~ true 8080 ~~~ **[7: Define "filename" in the "openshift" profile]** ~~~ openshift ${project.artifactId} install ~~~ If you want to switch application.properties between "openshift" and "local" profiles, there are 2 extra steps. **[8:Create application-openshift.properties and application-local.properties files under the same directory with application.properties]** application-openshift.properties will be used by "Openshift" profile. application-local.propertie will be used by "local" profile. **[9: Modify application.properties]** The content will be 1 line. ~~~ spring.profiles.active=@spring.profiles.active@ ~~~
root_cause: [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CSB-6304](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CSB-6304)

title: RHACS 4.5 Network Policy Generator UI Remains in "Loading" State When Generating Network Policies

title: Why are OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines using 4K disks getting paused intermittently?
issue: - OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines using 4K disks are getting paused intermittently.- Issue is observed on virtual machines using Portworx storage.
resolution: - The bug has been fixed in OpenShift Virtualization 4.16, and the fix was backported to OpenShift Virtualization 4.14.10 and 4.12.15. Update to one of these versions to resolve the issue.
root_cause: - Due to QEMU [bug 2174676](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2174676#c5), if a guest is using a sector size of 512 and O_DIRECT I/O (the default in OpenShift Virtualization) on a 4K-sectored host disk, this bug manifests when application performs heavy i/o with extremely long I/O vectors that is not aligned to 4k.- Portworx volume which was used for creating images for VMs are having 4k block size: ~~~ % cat sys/block/px*/queue/physical_block_size 4096 4096 4096 4096 4096 4096 4096 % cat sys/block/px*/queue/logical_block_size 4096 4096 4096 4096 4096 4096 4096 ~~~

title: config-controller fails to become ready
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: config-controller fails to become ready: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://100.145.2.235:8081/readyz": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

Error in config-controller log: 2025-01-22T06:47:50.931358123Z pkg/client: 2025/01/24 06:57:50.931258 client.go:217: Error: Failed to exchange token: rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = ID token is invalid: failed to verify signature: fetching keys oidc: get keys failed Get "https://some.api.server:6443/openid/v1/jwks": dial tcp 1.2.3.4:6443: i/o timeoutFailed to initialize client. Will continue to retry...
resolution: If the [policy as code feature](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.6/operating/manage_security_policies/custom-security-policies.html#policy-as-code-about_custom-security-policies) is not used, it can be [disabled](https://docs.openshift.com/acs/4.6/operating/manage_security_policies/custom-security-policies.html#policy-as-code-disable_custom-security-policies). If the policy as code feature need to be enabled, then Central needs to be able to connect to the configured Kubernetes API server, e.g. some.api.server:6443 in the above issue statement. There is possibly a network policy configured to disallow access from Central to the Kubernetes API server.
root_cause: Central needs to connect to the Kubernetes API server in order to perform [OIDC discovery](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/service-accounts/#authenticating-credentials) so that it can authenticate the service account token issued to the config-controller pod. This is required for Central to trust API calls made by the config-controller.

title: Is it possible to upgrade Ansible Automation Platform 2.4 RPM based installation to Containerized Ansible Automation Platform 2.5?
issue: - Is it possible to upgrade AAP 2.4 RPM based installation to Containerized AAP 2.5?- Is it possible to upgrade Ansible Automation Platform 2.4 RPM based installation to Containerized Ansible Automation Platform 2.5?- How to upgrade AAP to Containerized AAP 2.5?
resolution: Red Hat does not support a method to migrate from RPM to Containerised or Openshift Deployments at this time. Migration options are being investigated as potential future offerings. ### Plans for Deployment Migrations #### Summary The RPM installer will continue to be maintained for RHEL 8 and RHEL 9. To receive support for your upgrade steps, the same installation method must be used for AAP 2.5 as AAP 2.4. Performing upgrades (between AAP versions) and migrations (between deployment types) outside of supported procedures from Red Hat cannot be supported by Red Hat at this time, however it will not invalidate future support of AAP for non-upgrade and migration issues. #### Details Automated migrations as part Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) upgrades or installation are not currently supported. Red Hat is currently considering options that would provide the capability to migrate from one installation model to another. If this capability is delivered, then a migration between installation types will likely require that deployments are on the same version of AAP when migrating. An RPM installer deployment would need to be on the latest AAP version before it could be converted to a different installer type. An upgrade-and-migrate model, such as moving AAP 2.4 installed via the RPM installer to AAP 2.5 containerized installer at the same time, would not be supported. **There is no timeline for such capability as Red Hat is still assessing the viability of this process.** If your organization would like to move from one deployment model to another today, then the effort will require a separate deployment of a new Ansible Automation Platform environment, and then a manual or configuration-as-code driven migration model may be used. ### Ansible Automation Platform Support on RHEL Ansible Automation Platform 2.5 is currently supported on RHEL 8 and RHEL 9 and will support RHEL 10 when it is released. There are currently two models that an organization may install Ansible Automation Platform on RHEL 8 or 9, an [RPM installation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ansible_automation_platform/2.5/html/rpm_installation/index) or a [containerized installation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ansible_automation_platform/2.5/html/containerized_installation/index). In October 2024, Red Hat issued a deprecation notice and plans to remove the RPM installer for RHEL 10 support and later. Support for the RPM installer for RHEL 8 and 9 will remain for the [support lifecycle](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/ansible-automation-platform) of the AAP versions that support those versions of RHEL. **All new deployments of Ansible Automation Platform are recommended to use either containerized on operator installation methods.** When RHEL 10 is launched, Ansible Automation Platform will only be installable through the *RHEL installer*[^1] on RHEL 10. The installation support matrix is below. | RHEL Version | AAP Installation Options | |----- |----- | | 8 | RPM & Containerized | | 9 | RPM & Containerized | | 10 | RHEL installer | RPM installer support will remain on RHEL 8 and RHEL 9 through the remainder of the [Ansible Automation Platform product lifecycle(s)](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/ansible-automation-platform) where the RHEL versions are supported in an actively supported AAP version. Future product enhancements and features will be introduced in the RHEL installation model. [^1]: Beginning with RHEL 10, the containerized installer will be referred to as the RHEL installer.

title: How to retrieve logs from a failed bootstrap in Agent-based Installer ?
issue: - How to retrieve logs from a failed bootstrap in the Agent-based Installer?- How to get bootstrap logs from the assisted-service API?
resolution: When the cluster installation fails, follow these steps:- SSH into the rendezvous node. $ ssh core@- Retrieve the cluster ID. $ curl-sS http://localhost:8090/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters | jq-r '.[].id'- Download the logs from the assisted-service using the retrieved cluster ID. $ curl-sS http://localhost:8090/api/assisted-install/v2/clusters/ /logs--output abi-logs.tar
root_cause: - When an installation using the Agent-based Installer fails, the usual method is to collect the `agent-gather` logs. Refer to [the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/installing/installing_with_agent_based_installer/installing-with-agent-based-installer.html#installing-ocp-agent-gather-log_installing-with-agent-based-installer) or [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7016487) for this process.- In the Agent-based Installer, the rendezvous node is set as the bootstrap node. The other two master nodes fetch the IgnitionConfig from the bootstrap node to start. Once the master nodes complete their setup, the rendezvous host reboots and becomes the third master node, fetching the IgnitionConfig from the other two master nodes.- If an issue occurs during the bootstrap phase and the other two master nodes do not become ready, the installation fails. The `openshift-install agent wait-for bootstrap-complete` command will time out.- The direct cause of bootstrap failure might not always be included in the agent-gather logs.- By retrieving logs from the assisted-service API, it is possible to gather more detailed bootstrap logs, which can assist in troubleshooting.

title: error: config GVK not recognized: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha1, Kind=ImageSetConfiguration
issue: When download the latest `oc-mirror` tool to mirror the images using below sample command, it populates below error: ~~~ $./oc-mirror--config=/root/mirror-registry/imageset.yaml docker://quay.example.com:8443/oc-mirror--dest-skip-tls--dry-run error: config GVK not recognized: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha1, Kind=ImageSetConfiguration ~~~
resolution: Update `apiVersion` in the `ImageSetConfiguration` YAML file:- For `oc-mirror plugin v2`: ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1 ~~~- For `oc-mirror 4.11` and newer: ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 ~~~
root_cause: Starting from OpenShift 4.11, the `oc-mirror` tool schema API version has been updated to `v1apha2` and the old schema is no longer supported. See OpenShift 4.11 [Creating the image set configuration](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#oc-mirror-creating-image-set-config_installing-mirroring-disconnected) for detail. It may also need to adjust the image set configuration accordingly. A similar change is with `oc-mirror plugin v2` that uses `mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1`.

title: How to add multiple additional networks for a pod?
issue: - Facing issues while adding multiple types of Network-Attachment-Definition.
resolution: - Take a backup of your current network.operator before proceeding. ~~~ $ oc get networks.operator.openshift.io cluster-o yaml &> network.operator ~~~- To create an additional network in your cluster, complete the following steps: Edit the CNO CR by running the following command: ~~~ $ oc edit networks.operator.openshift.io cluster ~~~- Modify the network.operator CR by adding the configuration for the additional network, as in the following example CR. The following YAML configures a bridge and a macvlan CNI plug-in: ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: Network metadata: name: cluster spec: additionalNetworks:- name: test-bridgenetwork-1 namespace: test-1 type: Raw rawCNIConfig: '{"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "name": "test-bridgenetwork-1", "type": "bridge", "ipam": {"type": "static", "addresses": [{"address": "192.168.x.x/y"}]}}'- name: test-macvlannetwork-2 namespace: test-1 type: SimpleMacvlan simpleMacvlanConfig: ipamConfig: staticIPAMConfig: addresses:- address: 192.168.x.x/y type: static clusterNetwork: ~~~- Save your changes and quit the text editor to commit your changes.- Optional: Confirm that the CNO created the NetworkAttachmentDefinition CR by running the following command. There might be a delay before the CNO creates the CR. ~~~ $ oc get network-attachment-definitions-n ~~~ Example output ~~~ NAME AGE test-bridgenetwork-1 10m test-macvlannetwork-2 10m ~~~- To attach a pod to the additional network created, refer the [documentation.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/networking/multiple_networks/secondary_networks/attaching-pod.html)

title: Create a pipeline run in OpenShift AI without using the web UI
issue: As an OpenShift AI user, I want to interact with the Data Science Pipeline API to trigger Pipeline Runs without the use of the web UI.
resolution: The kubeflow API is documented [here](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/reference/api/kubeflow-pipeline-api-spec/) The ds-pipeline-dspa route is exposed by default and can be used to interact with the pipeline server. ``` dspa_route=$(oc get route-n foo ds-pipeline-dspa-o go-template={{.spec.host}}) curl-s-k-H "Authorization: Bearer $(oc whoami--show-token)" https://$(dspa_route)/apis/v2beta1/runs\?namespace=foo ``` Sample JSON payload to trigger a run ``` #cat pipeline_run.json {"experiment_id": "7c24a9b0-f14f-42ba-b147-e10b006737ab", "display_name": "launched_by_API", "pipeline_version_reference": {"pipeline_id": "8d47ecdf-5dc5-4fda-bf1c-4004013c9d55", "pipeline_version_id": "69d61303-4ac0-4cd5-b9a2-d2a8782bdcc4"}} curl-X POST-k-H "Authorization: Bearer $(oc whoami--show-token)"-H 'accept: application/json' https://$(dspa_route)/apis/v2beta1/runs-d @pipeline_run.json ``` You can also interact with the API using the [kfp client](https://kubeflow-pipelines.readthedocs.io/en/sdk-2.11.0/source/client.html) Here is an example using this client: ``` import subprocess import uuid from kfp.client import Client namespace = "dspa" dspa = "sample" def terminal(cmd): proc = subprocess.run(cmd.split(), stdout=subprocess.PIPE) out = str(proc.stdout, encoding='utf-8') return out.strip() dspa_host = terminal(f"oc get routes-n {namespace} ds-pipeline-{dspa}--template={{{{.spec.host}}}}") route = f"https://{dspa_host}" token = terminal("oc whoami--show-token") client = Client(host=route, verify_ssl=False, existing_token=token) num_of_runs = 20 from perf import my_pipeline for i in range(num_of_runs): run_name = f"{dspa_host}-{i}-{uuid.uuid4()}" client.create_run_from_pipeline_func(pipeline_func=my_pipeline, run_name=f"{dspa_host}-{i}-{run_name}") ```

title: Pod data-dir-etcd is failing with ImagePullBackOff in OpenShift 4
issue: What are the `data-dir-etcd` pods failing in OpenShift 4 cluster?

There are `data-dir-etcd` pods failing with `ErrImagePull` and `ImagePullBackOff` in OpenShift 4 with messages like the following ones: ~~~ Failed to pull image "etcd:3.5.10-0": reading manifest 3.5.10-0 in docker.io/library/etcd: requested access to the resource is denied ~~~
resolution: The `data-dir-etcd` pods are generated by Commvault backup. From the error message, the issue is related to missing permissions accessing the image in `docker.io/library/etcd`, or due to non-existent registry and/or namespace: ~~~ Failed to pull image "etcd:3.5.10-0": reading manifest 3.5.10-0 in docker.io/library/etcd: requested access to the resource is denied ~~~ For being able to pull images from secured registries, it is needed to configure the credentials into the pull secret. Refer to [allowing pods to reference images from other secured registries](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/openshift_images/managing_images/using-image-pull-secrets.html#images-allow-pods-to-reference-images-from-secure-registries_using-image-pull-secrets) for additional information. If the image or even the registry namespace do not exists, it will be needed to configure an existing image (including the registry and namespace name). > **Note:** Commvault is a [third party tool](https://access.redhat.com/third-party-software-support) not provided or supported by Red Hat. In case of additional issues with it, please contact Commvault provider.
root_cause: The `data-dir-etcd` pods are not generated by OpenShift components, but by Commvault backup. Commvault is a [third party tool](https://access.redhat.com/third-party-software-support) not provided or supported by Red Hat. In case of additional issues with it, please contact Commvault provider.

title: Automate syncing RHOCP's etcd-db backups to Cloud Storage.
issue: - Presently in OCP, initial manual job creation is necessary to configure automatic backups syncing process with common cloud storage platforms like S3 buckets, as highlighted in this [KCS Article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970359).- Setup may encounter challenges due to potential typographical errors or cloud-specific complexities.- The process involves syncing backups with cloud storage, but initially it relies on manual intervention, which could lead to errors or complications.
resolution: **Description:**- In order to get this done in a streamlined method, a new feature request has been proposed to get this optional functionality to enable automated etcd database sync-up with common cloud buckets. **Objectives:**- It is expected to receive a preconfigured function or capability that includes:- On GUI there should be an option to provide cloud credentials, zone, and bucket path upon activation of the feature.- Adjusting the duration of the synchronization process.- Utilizing these provided values (ID, keys, Zone, Path) as variables.- Integration of a topology view within the GUI would greatly enhance the experience.- Enabling this feature would initiate the synchronization of the etcd database with the designated cloud storage.- This feature should be optional.- Should display alerts in case of failure and informative logs should be present on Prometheus. **Notion:**- This should be an optional Feature that can be managed by CLI and GUI ``` +------------------------+ | - Input Credentials | | - Cloud Zone | | - Bucket Path | | | | (Option in GUI to | | provide credentials,| | zone, and path | | (Like RHACM)) | +------------------------+ | v +------------------------+ | Duration Request | | - Define Sync Process | | Duration | | | | (Set duration for | | synchronization) | +------------------------+ | v +------------------------+ | Topology View | | Integration | | | | (Integration of | | topology view in | | GUI) | +------------------------+ | | v +------------------------+ | Optional Feature | | Activation (Yes/No) | | | | (Choice to activate | | synchronization | | feature that could | | be a radio button) | +------------------------+ | | | | v | +------------------------+ | Synchronization | | Initiation | | | | (Start syncing | | etcd db with cloud | | storage) | +------------------------+ | | | | v | +------------------------+ | Failure Alerts | | & Logging | | | | (Display alerts on | | failure, logs on | | Prometheus) | +------------------------+ | | v v +------------------------+ | End | +------------------------+ ```- For the inclusion of additional functionalities, please submit a ticket for further discussion and implementation.

title: Byteman inside EAP 8 Openshift images injection
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How to inject EAP 8 image with Byteman at build time- How to instrument EAP 8 image with Byteman at runtime
resolution: Although it would be possible to do an injection at build time, via Docekrfiel (or container file) an injection via runtime is possible and similar to the steps provided on [What are the options to use a custom runtime JBoss EAP 7 configurations in OCP](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6969444) for `postconfigure.sh`. For Build solution besides injecting byteman's jar and its rules you will need to set the env variable, either overwrite `JAVA_OPTS` or set `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` to enable the runtime injection, given the fact that merely being there doesn't make the jar injected, it is necessary to add in the Java path. ### Runtime injection The runtime process is similar to the one in [Enable a Byteman script for JBoss EAP or RH-SSO in OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3103211). ~~~ ### configmap 1 $ oc create configmap byteman-jar--from-file=byteman.jar ### configmap 2 $ oc create configmap byteman-config--from-file=byteman.btm ### volume 1 $ oc set volume dc/eap-app--add--name=byteman-jar-m /opt/tmp/bytemanjar-t configmap--configmap-name=byteman-jar--default-mode='0777'--overwrite ### volume 2 $ oc set volume dc/eap-app--add--name=byteman-config-m /opt/tmp/bytemanconfig-t configmap--configmap-name=byteman-config--default-mode='0777'--overwrite ### env variable $ oc set env dc/eap-app JAVA_OPTS_APPEND="-javaagent:/opt/tmp/bytemanjar/byteman.jar=script:/opt/tmp/bytemanconfig/byteman.btm,sys:/opt/tmp/bytemanjar/byteman.jar" ~~~
root_cause: This solution describes the implementation of Byteman for OCP in EAP 7/8, for other products in OCP 4, the process might change because they might rely on Custom Resouces, such as DG Operator, see [Setting up byteman script in RHDG 8 image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6890151), which relies on the Infinispan Custom Resource spec `container.extraJvmOpts` to be set.

title: coreos-installer fails to write ignition and images to the disk
issue: - The RHCOS nodes being used to install a cluster in a UPI environment fail to write ignition and images to disk via the `coreos-installer install` command line.- The ignition files can be manually fetched from the node and have a valid certificate as well.- The `coreos-installer install` command fails while fetching images and gets redirected to `builds.coreos.fedoraproject.org`.
resolution: - Please ensure the path of the installation disk being provided is correct and is not of the live iso attached to the node.- Also ensure the additional parameter `disk.EnableUUID=TRUE` is provided while setting up the VM in `VMware` environment.
root_cause: - The issue is observed due to the path of the installation disk being incorrect.- The `coreos-installer` expects a valid path of the disk being used to install. This path should not be of the `rhcos live iso` or any other iso. The path of the disk can be found under `/dev/disk/`

title: oc-mirror only mirrors the latest version
issue: - I mirrored the Operator with oc-mirror, but only the latest version (e.g. `4.16.5`) was mirrored- I specified `v4.16.0` and `v4.16.1` for the min/max versions ~~~ mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.16 full: false packages:- name: kubevirt-hyperconverged channels:- name: stable minVersion: v4.16.0 maxVersion: v4.16.1 ~~~- What happens when specifying the wrong versions in imageset-config.yaml?
resolution: Correct the Operator's min/max versions to the appropriate values. It is easy to make a mistake, but here `4.16.0` and `4.16.1` are valid version specifications. ~~~ mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.16 full: false packages:- name: kubevirt-hyperconverged channels:- name: stable minVersion: 4.16.0 maxVersion: 4.16.1 ~~~
root_cause: This is the expected behavior. oc-mirror must first download the operator-index, then process it by untarring the layers and inspecting the operator config json file for the given operator. It can't make a decision about the min/max versions until it has executed the steps. Therefore, oc-mirror will ignore the wrong versions and continue making a best effort to filter on the specified parameters.

title: Openshift local storage operator still showing up in CLI even after it was uninstalled
issue: - Openshift Local Storage Operator still showing up in CLI even after it was removed following [document](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/storage/persistent_storage/persistent_storage_local/persistent-storage-local.html#local-storage-uninstall_persistent-storage-local).

title: Decipher etcd objects in AES-CBC
issue: The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and support procedures. The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the Operating System unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. The intent of this article is to provide information to accomplish the system's needs. Use of the information in this article at the user's own risk. The goal of this solution is to help you decipher encoded Etcd objects in AES-CBC.
resolution: To extract an object from etcd, use the following command inside the etcd container to set up the environment variables (often found in /etc/etcd/etcd.conf) and retrieve the base64-encoded etcd object using etcdctl (a Secret in this example): ~~~ # source /etc/etcd/etcd.conf # export ETCDCTL_API=3 # etcdctl--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert $ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS get /kubernetes.io/secrets/test/my-secret--write-out=json {"header":{"cluster_id":1535328224928523406,"member_id":10396734553733729853,"revision":30198,"raft_term":3},"kvs":[{"key":"L2t1YmVybmV0ZXMuaW8vc2VjcmV0cy9zaW1vbi1wcm9qZWN0L215LXNlY3JldA==","create_revision":28525,"mod_revision":28525,"version":1,"value":"azhzOmVuYzphZXNjYmM6djE6c2ltb246lvj7pYRT71cyo+aqLPjJ2kuvAOI4FghpUG5n405KRZOLnDU3EAw55jxDt+qAJPFArX7Jmp8wppRgdk7NE+3XiOCGnQBQWGkJX1irZ31DxotG4CfrxH4pJ0Agnmzw/e+bJAJGPO84SMFjrhInd14iseyErrfrG5s/dy0tEyDUtQMrVGMLkztYoELfBARK8+PP3H52oJmlM1rvU6jV09dbcQ=="}],"count":1} ~~~ Retrieve the base64-encoded encryption key ("secret") from the EncryptionConfig (OpenShift stores it in /etc/origin/master/encryption-config.yaml or /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-pod- /secrets/encryption-config/encryption-config) from your Control Plane Nodes: ~~~ # cat /etc/origin/master/encryption-config.yaml kind: EncryptionConfig apiVersion: v1 resources:- resources:- secrets- configmaps providers:- aescbc: keys:- name: "test" secret: 1vTaJ76Pak2oXFu5k0muTN7Uo+VZWsV9caFjz/Pc3x4=- identity: {} ~~~ Using the value from the first step and the secret from the second step, you can then use the program in this repository to decrypt the object: ~~~ $./k8s-etcd-decryptor Tool to decrypt AES-CBC-encrypted objects from etcd Enter base64-encoded etcd value: azhzOmVuYzphZXNjYmM6djE6c2ltb246lvj7pYRT71cyo+aqLPjJ2kuvAOI4FghpUG5n405KRZOLnDU3EAw55jxDt+qAJPFArX7Jmp8wppRgdk7NE+3XiOCGnQBQWGkJX1irZ31DxotG4CfrxH4pJ0Agnmzw/e+bJAJGPO84SMFjrhInd14iseyErrfrG5s/dy0tEyDUtQMrVGMLkztYoELfBARK8+PP3H52oJmlM1rvU6jV09dbcQ== Enter base64-encoded encryption key from EncryptionConfig: 1vTaJ76Pak2oXFu5k0muTN7Uo+VZWsV9caFjz/Pc3x4= k8s ~~~ ~~~ v1Secretv T test"*$6567b48b-9f45-11ea-8fb6-fa163e827b272z mysupersecretOpaque" ~~~ This will print the the object (a Secret in this case) data as a string, which is not very nice but works well for most use-cases.

title: Fix the missing VM boot sources after changing the default storage class
issue: - I changed my default storage class, and my VM boot sources are missing
resolution: This issue is fixed in [OpenShift Virtualization 4.18 and later](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-51249). ### Clean up the images: Deleting the current boot sources will trigger a new import process that will solve the current issue.- **Via CLI**:- Delete the `DataVolumes` in `openshift-virtualization-os-images` namespace (and/or `VolumeSnapshots` for some storage types) that are managed by the `DataImportCron`- Note: If a DataVolume owns a PVC, and you just delete the PVC without deleting the DataVolume- the PVC will be recreated (a new import will start) ~~~ $ oc delete dv,VolumeSnapshot-n openshift-virtualization-os-images--selector=cdi.kubevirt.io/dataImportCron ~~~- **Via UI**:- Go to `Storage`-> `PersistentVolumeClaims` and delete the `PVCs` in `openshift-virtualization-os-images` namespace- Note: When we delete a `PVC` in UI, it deletes the `DV` under the hood- Go to `Storage`-> `VolumeSnapshots` and delete the `VolumeSnapshots` in `openshift-virtualization-os-images` namespace if they are present (relevant only for some storage types)

title: What is the default serialize-image-pulls configuration value?
issue: - If is not included the_serialize-image-pulls_ arguments in the node config, what is the default value will be considered for the cluster?
resolution: The default value for_SerializeImagePulls_ is `False` in OpenShift 3 and 4: $ cat /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf | grep-i pull "serializeImagePulls": false,
root_cause: - There are two different documentations, one from OpenShift and one from Kubernetes, that document different default values for the same parameter.- According to the [OpenShift 3 documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/install_config/master_node_configuration.html#master-node-configuration-parallel-image-pulls-with-docker), **false** is the default value for_SerializeImagePulls_: kubeletArguments: serialize-image-pulls: "false"- According to the [Kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kubelet-config.v1beta1/#:~:text=serializeImagePulls%0Abool,details.%20Default%3A%20true), the default for_SerializeImagePulls_ is **true**: SerializeImagePulls: true,

title: IBU upgrade fails with image pull issues for multiarch images
issue: - The `IBU` upgrade for `SNO` fails with image pull failure for `multiarch` images.- Components try to pull images which don't match the release info on the cluster.
resolution: - The issue was investigated and identified as a bug under [OCPBUGS-42703](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42703).- The fix has been released in OpenShift Container Platform 4.14.38 `IBU` extras update and Lifecycle Agent Operator 4.14.2.
root_cause: This happens when OCP payload (from `quay.io/opnshift-release-dev`) uses the same version of the image as the day2 operators e.g., lvms and ptp, from `registry.redhat.io/openshift4`). OCP pods refer to the actual `x86_64` image. Operators refer to the `multiarch` manifest list. Hence the sha from quay.io gets mirrored as part of OCP and all sha values for the image from from `registry.redhat.io` get mirrored with the `ImageSetConfiguration` for operators. The other sha values from `quay.io` doesn't get mirrored. It's included only by multi-arch OCP releases.

title: Unable to create Machines with error Invalid client secret provided in OpenShift 4 running on Azure
issue:
- Not able to create new `Machines` in OpenShift 4 cluster installed in Azure.- Errors like the following one are shown in the `machine-controller` and other components requiring access to Azure: ~~~ Invalid client secret provided. Ensure the secret being sent in the request is the client secret value, not the client secret ID, for a secret added to app '[random-id]' ~~~- New `Machine` is stuck in failed state with below error: ~~~ CreateError: failed to reconcile machine "address.domain-url"s: failed to create nic example-nic for machine example-machine-name unable to create VM network interface: failed to obtain instance type information for VMSize 'Standard_name' from Azure: failed to refresh resource sku cache: could not list resource skus: azure.BearerAuthorizer#WithAuthorization: Failed to refresh the Token for request to https://cloud-platform-url: StatusCode=401-- Original Error: adal: Refresh request failed. Status Code = '401'. Response body: {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"ID: Invalid client secret provided. Ensure the secret being sent in the request is the client secret value, not the client secret ID, for a secret added to app 'random-id'.
Trace ID: ID
Correlation ID: Random-ID
Timestamp: Y-M-H HH:MM:SSZ","error_codes":[7000215],"timestamp":"2Y-M-H HH:MM:SSZ"," ~~~
resolution: Check the `secret` `azure-credentials` in `kube-system` `namespace`. Refer to [how to update client secret in azure cloud credentials](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6242011) for additional information. If even after updating the `secret`, new `Machines` are still getting failed with same error, then scale down and scale up the `deployment/machine-api-operator`: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-machine-api scale deployment/machine-api-operator--replicas=0 $ oc-n openshift-machine-api scale deployment/machine-api-operator--replicas=1 ~~~
root_cause: The credentials in the `secret` expired, and even when it has been updated, due to the way Openshift manages pod instances, it is necessary to restart every pod that was using that `secret`. The `secrets` are stored in the pods as environment variables, so the value will not change until the pods are restarted.

title: Group synchronization limitations when using Azure Active Directory (AAD) with OpenShift 4 OpenID authentication
issue: - When configuring Azure Active Directory as an OpenID identity provider in OpenShift, users with more than 200 group memberships experience incomplete group synchronization.- AAD limits token group claims to 200 groups- For users exceeding this limit, AAD provides a Graph API endpoint instead of direct group lists- OpenShift's current OAuth implementation cannot process this API endpoint reference
resolution: - Current Workarounds- Implement Group Sync Operator ~~~ apiVersion: redhatcop.redhat.io/v1alpha1 kind: GroupSync metadata: name: azure-groupsync spec: providers:- name: azure azure: credentialsSecret: name: azure-credentials namespace: group-sync-operator ~~~ Note: Group Sync Operator is community supported but effectively handles Azure Graph API queries- Configure AAD Group Claims to filter groups in Azure Enterprise Application settings and limit token scope to essential OpenShift access groups.- Configure group claims in OAuth configuration ~~~ spec: identityProviders:- name: Azure mappingMethod: claim type: OpenID openID: claims: groups:- groups ~~~- Feature Development Status- Current [RFE Status](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4118): Aggregated and Distributed Claims support- Status: Deferred for upcoming BYO External OAuth implementation- Target: OpenShift 4.19+- Implementation of BYO (Bring Your Own) External OAuth- Will provide direct Azure AD integration- Eliminates token translation complexity- Tracking: OCPSTRAT-306
root_cause: - Azure AD implements distributed claims through Graph API when group memberships exceed token size limits (> 200 groups). The current OpenShift OAuth implementation expects direct group claims in the token and cannot process these API endpoint references.

title: Machine Config Operator stuck in progressing state due to PDB restrictions
issue: - The nodes can't drain due to PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) restrictions.- This leads to the upgrade process getting stuck and causing degradation in the Machine Config Operator (MCO): ~~~ $ oc get co NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE authentication 4.14.27 True False False 2y... machine-config 4.13.42 False True False 2y... ~~~
resolution: 1. Pause the involved worker MCP to prevent any potential issues: ~~~ $ oc get mcp worker $ oc patch mcp-p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'--type=merge ~~~ 2. Drain the Node Ignoring PDB Constraints: use the drain command with the option "--disable-eviction": **Note: "--disable-eviction" is used to force drain to use delete, even if eviction is supported. This will bypass checking PodDisruptionBudgets, use it with caution.** ~~~ $ oc adm drain--ignore-daemonsets--delete-emptydir-data--force--disable-eviction ~~~ 3. Unpause the worker MCP. Unpause to resume the upgrade after the degraded state is fixed: ~~~ $ oc patch mcp-p '{"spec":{"paused":false}}'--type=merge ~~~ 4. Check machine-config-daemon or machine-config-controller pod logs to see any errors. 5. Monitor if nodes are getting upgraded. If the issue is not fixed after following above steps, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: Some pods prevented the node from draining, causing the upgrade to get stuck and resulting in degradation of the Machine Config Operator (MCO).

title: Red Hat Quay builders fail with error: Name or service not known on RHOCP 4
issue: Quay builders fail with `Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno-2] Name or service not known` error: 2025-01-20T17:02:50.973994964Z builder stdout | 2025-01-20 17:02:50,973 [294827] [WARNING] [buildman.manager.ephemeral] Failed to get worker count from executors: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='https', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /api.example.com:6443/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/example/jobs?labelSelector=build%2Ctime%2Cmanager%2Cquay-sha (Caused by NewConnectionError(': Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno-2] Name or service not known'))
resolution: Edit Quay `Config Bundle Secret` and make sure that `K8S_API_SERVER` key inside `config.yaml` contains just the hostname and port for the API Server of the OpenShift Container Platform. For example: ~~~ $ oc get secret-n-o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' | base64-d | grep K8S_API_SERVER K8S_API_SERVER: api.example.com:6443 ~~~
root_cause: The key `K8S_API_SERVER`inside the Quay configuration file should contain only the hostname and port of the API Server of the OpenShift Container Platform cluster where Builds will take place, as specified in the [product documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_quay/3/html-single/configure_red_hat_quay/index#config-fields-build-manager).

title: unknown field "spec.dns.spec.platform" message is being spammed in OpenShift Container Platform 4.
issue: The machine-config-operator pod is spamming these logs: ~~~ W0811 13:55:54.303613 1 warnings.go:70] unknown field "spec.dns.spec.platform" ~~~

Power off the VM: ~~~ govc vm.power-off /DC/vm/folder/test-cluster1-mdcsn-worker-static-jf76h Powering off VirtualMachine:vm-13421... OK ~~~ 3. Apply the configuration: ~~~ $ govc vm.change-vm " "-e "guestinfo.afterburn.initrd.network-kargs=${IPCFG}" ~~~ 5. Power back ON the VM: ~~~ $ govc vm.power-on /DC/vm/folder/test-cluster1-mdcsn-worker-static-jf76h Powering on VirtualMachine:vm-13421... OK ~~~

title: RHOCP 4 Operator pods blocking the unmount of CSI volumes
issue: - Mounts not removed due to OpenShift processes still accessing mounpoint.- CSI volumes cannot be mounted with errors `mpatha: map in use` and `mpatha: can't flush`.- Multipath is not able to flush unmouted volumes because kept busy by ovnkube.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in the following bugs: **Node Tuning Operator** RHOCP Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-14946](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-14946) | **4.14.0** | [RHSA-2023:5006](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:5006) 4.13 | [OCPBUGS-15738](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-15738) | **4.13.5** | [RHSA-2023:4091](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:4091) **OVNKubernetes and Multus** RHOCP Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 4.17 | [OCPBUGS-30950](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-30950) | **4.17.1** | [RHSA-2024:7922](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:7922) 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-36594](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-36594) | **4.16.19** | [RHSA-2024:8415](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:8415) 4.15 | [OCPBUGS-42753](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42753) | **4.15.40** | [RHSA-2024:10839](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:10839) 4.14 | [OCPBUGS-42754](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42754) | **4.14.45** | [RHSA-2025:0364](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:0364) ### Workaround for ovnkube-node and multus Modify the daemonsets to add the `HostToContainer` propagation: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-multus patch daemonset multus--type='json'-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/volumeMounts/10", "value": {"name": "host-var-lib-kubelet", "mountPath": "/var/lib/kubelet", "mountPropagation": "HostToContainer",}}]' ~~~ ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes patch daemonset ovnkube-node--type='json'-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/7/volumeMounts/1", "value": {"name": "host-kubelet", "mountPath": "/var/lib/kubelet", "mountPropagation": "HostToContainer", "readOnly": true}}]' ~~~ ### Workaround for tuned- this resolution applies for the tuned pod created by the `node-tuning` ClusterOperator, and should only be used **after suggestion from a Red Hat Support Associate**. Please note that this is a temporary solution as an upgrade of the operator will remove the mitigation, [as long as this operator is not put into unmanaged mode](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6243031)- verify the current mount propagation for the `host` volumeMount for the tuned pods ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator-l openshift-app=tuned-o json | jq '.items[0].spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[] | select(.name=="host")' ~~~- this should return no special configured mountPropagation, which means the default will be used. If the command above does not return this exact output, stop here and contact Red Hat support. ~~~ {"mountPath": "/host", "name": "host"} ~~~- patch the tuned daemon set, so that the pod template of the daemonset uses the `HostToContainer` mount propagation. ~~~ $ oc patch daemonset tuned-n openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator--type=json-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/volumeMounts/-1", "value": {"name": "host", "mountPath": "/host", "mountPropagation": "HostToContainer"}}]' ~~~- verify that the pods have now the `HostToContainer` mount propagation. ~~~ $ oc get ds-n openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator tuned-o json | jq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[-1]' ~~~ ~~~ {"mountPath": "/host", "mountPropagation": "HostToContainer", "name": "host"} ~~~ Now from that point on, the tuned pods should **never** prevent the unmounting of a CSI volume.
root_cause: When a container mounts the directory `/var/lib/kubelet` without the `mountPropagation: HostToContainer` is not aware if there is any PersistentVolume mounted by other pods.

title: "504 Gateway Timeout" During NooBaa Bucket Operations - OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: Listing or uploading files from S3 bucket always fails with a `504 (Gateway Time-out)`. Sometimes mid-way through an operation. For example, a backup operator with many files. Additionlly, this issue can be present if the db is not set to the correct Collate which is `C`. If the db is not set to Collate `C` you may also see greater consumption on the `db-noobaa-db-pg-0` PVC.
resolution: 1. In the vast majority of 504 Gateway timeout issues related to NooBaa bucket operations, the symptom is generally due to insufficient CPU resources on the `noobaa-core-0` and `noobaa-db-pg-0` pods. The default resources configured on the NooBaa stack are usually not sufficient if NooBaa is going to be utilized in a moderate-to-heavy use case. Please see the [Performance tuning guide for Multicloud Object Gateway (NooBaa)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6719951) article to increase resources. **NOTE:** To confirm resource utilization of not only the noobaa-db-pg-0 and noobaa-core-0 resources, but also any other NooBaa resource that may be in question (operator, endpoint, backingstore pods (pv-pool)), navigate to the OCP console-> Workloads-> Pods-> pod name (ensure correct namespace is selected)-> select the pod-> click "Metrics" tab-> click on graph (memory/CPU)-> select a timeframe in the top/left dropdown (1d, 1w, etc.). 2. In the event the resources are sufficient, please review, confirm, and execute the steps in the [Change the Multi-Cloud Object Gateway Database's Collation Locale to C](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7031666) solution if the db is **NOT** set to Collate `C`.
root_cause: * This is a known postgres collation [bug](https://github.com/noobaa/noobaa-core/issues/5476)

title: Nodes with multiple network interfaces on vSphere show taint "node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized" in RHOCP4.
issue: - Scaling up RHOCP nodes with multiple network interfaces results not linked to the machine object.- Scaling nodes with multiple NICs can create `vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-node-XXXX` PODs in a `CrashLoopBackOff` state.- After upgrading to RHOCP 4.14 on the vSphere environment the scaling of nodes with multiple interfaces stopped to fully work.- Newly provisioned Nodes after RHOCP upgrade to version 4.14, does not have the Provider ID ~~~ $ oc get nodes-o json | jq '.items[]|[.metadata.name,.spec.providerID]' ["ocpnode-43210-master-0", "vsphere://4200xxxx-2xxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"] ["ocpnode-43210-worker-0", null] ["ocpnode-43210-worker-1", null] ["ocpnode-43210-master-3", "vsphere://4200xxxx-2xxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"] ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-25472](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-25472). In the `Infrastructure` object, configure the ["internal" and "external"](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/rest_api/config_apis/infrastructure-config-openshift-io-v1.html#spec-platformspec-vsphere-nodenetworking) `nodeNetworking` fields to the CIDRs used by the networking interfaces: ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: Infrastructure metadata: name: cluster spec: cloudConfig: key: config name: cloud-provider-config platformSpec: type: VSphere vsphere: failureDomains:- name: generated-failure-domain [..] nodeNetworking: external: networkSubnetCidr:- 192.168.xx.xx/24 internal: networkSubnetCidr:- 10.140.xx.xx/25 [..] ~~~
root_cause: The Cloud Controller Manager may fall back to legacy code if the above configuration is not in place, leading to the wrong IPs being selected.

title: UnmanagedRoutes alerts firing in RHOCP4
issue: - `Routes` owned by an `Ingress` are no longer `managed`.- The `UnmanagedRoutes` alert is firing for a specific `Route` in the cluster
resolution: * Verify that the `ingressClassName` field in the `Ingress` object is set to the name of the `IngressClass` that is creating the Routes (typically `openshift-default`): ~~~ $ oc patch ingress/--type=merge--patch '{"spec":{"ingressClassName":"openshift-default"}}' ~~~ * Red Hat is aware of an issue that this alert is not resolving even when the `ingressClassName` is set: [OCPBUGS-13181](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-13181). Red Hat is aware of this issue and is tracking the resolution in the Bug. Should you encounter this issue in your environment, please open a new Support Case in the [Red Hat Customer Portal](https://access.redhat.com) referring to this Solution.
root_cause: * If the wrong or no `ingressClassName` is specified, then OpenShift stops managing the `ingress`, and any `routes` that were previously generated for the `ingress` become `unmanaged`.

title: Installation of local mirror-registry fails with error  Permission denied (publickey)
issue: - Installation of the local mirror-registry as a root user fails with the following "Permission denied (publickey)" error: ``` fatal: [root@]: UNREACHABLE! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to connect to the host via ssh: Warning: Permanently added ‘ ’ (RSA) to the list of known hosts.\r\n: Permission denied (publickey).” “Unreachable”: true} ```
resolution: - Add the line `AllowUsers root` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`: ``` # vi /etc/ssh/sshd_config... AllowUsers root <--- Add this line ```- Restart the sshd.service: ``` # systemctl restart sshd ```
root_cause: - The root user was not allowed in the sshd_config, hence SSH access for root was implicitly denied.

title: Latency Profiles not applied on custom MCPs on Openshift 4
issue: - After applying the Latency Profile only default `worker` Machine Config Pool updated the `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` and the rest parameters controlled by the profile inside Kubelet configuration file.- Nodes under a custom Machine Config Pool are not getting the `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` value or the rest parameters changed in the Kubelet configuration file.
resolution: This is the expected behavior, as the worker latency profile `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` value and the rest parameters are not meant to be applied in other Machine Config Pools except the default `worker` one. The same is not mentioned in the documentation and there is an open bug [OCPBUGS-31917](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-31917) for adding a note for this to be clarified. Also, [RFE-5416](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-5416) has been created to enable worker latency profiles support on non default `worker` Machine Config Pools.
root_cause: By design the worker latency profiles are not meant to be applied in other Machine Config Pools except the default `worker` one.

title: Random Ports open to 0.0.0.0/0 in ROSA deployment
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - `Security group` inbound rules were configured to allow traffic from `0.0.0.0/0` for random ports (for example: 30444 and 30841).- This is usually a security concern raised when `vulnerability scanners` report these ports due to unrestricted access on `ROSA`.
resolution: - The `NodePort` creation is expected behaviour by design in `ROSA` clusters and not a security flow.- The issue with the `0.0.0.0/0` inbound rule on `worker node` security groups is tracked under [RFE-4812](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4812).
root_cause: - During the deployment of the `ROSA` cluster, `NodePort` services are created, which opened the ports.- These ports are used to forward traffic from standard ports `80 (HTTP)` and `443 (HTTPS)` to the `OpenShift` router via the `LoadBalancer` service.

title: External IP stuck at pending state when creating Internal Load Balancer

title: Pods in CrashLoop while OIDC endpoint is Unavailable
issue: - 3scale API Management pods in crashloopbackoff after new startup.- OIDC issuer endpoints were unavailable during startup.- After sometime, pods come back up and running.
resolution: Accorging to [APIcast fails to boot if one of the OIDC issuers does not respond](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-8006), if an OIDC endpoint is unreachable during the pod's startup, APIcast hangs long enough for the default liveness and readiness probes to kill the pod. In case any of the OIDC endpoints configured in APIcast is not reachable for some time, that would result in APIcast being killed repeatedly by OpenShift. After a while it is possible to see that APIcast times out and the configuration is loaded successfully. Therefore, if OIDC's outage is planned, then configuring the liveness and readiness probes time properly, would avoid this behavior. Also check: [APIcast hanging on boot, gets killed by OpenShift probes](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6956747).
root_cause: Starting up 3scale API Management pod while OIDC Issuer in unavailable.

title: User OAuth tokens in OpenShift 4
issue: - How to change / delete the user token for connecting to an OpenShift 4 cluster?- User token is not changed after deleting the `useroauthaccesstoken` related object.- Command `oc whoami--show-token` and command `oc get UserOAuthAccessToken` shows different token.- When doing an `oc logout`, the token from the OpenShift web console used is no longer valid, even if the expiration was not yet passed.- Invalid token error after using `oc logout` command: ~~~ error: The token provided is invalid or expired. ~~~
resolution: The command `oc whoami--show-token` (1) shows different token than the command `oc get useroauthaccesstokens` (2), because storing unhashed tokens is unsafe. The first command (1) displays the *local* token, whereas the second one (2) shows the tokens in the cluster. First command (1) is executed locally, and so removing the token remotely by running `oc delete useroauthaccesstoken ` will have no effect to the local token. On the other hand, when generating a token from the OpenShift web console to login into the cluster with `oc` CLI, a `useroauthaccesstoken` resource is created, in addition to the token shown in the web console (that will be the token stored locally when using it to login into the cluster). Using `oc logout` invalidates the OAuth token (removing the associated `useroauthaccesstoken`) and deletes the locally stored token from the `KubeConfig`. Creating a new token from the web console or using `user`/`password` will be needed to login into the cluster again. > **Note:** the `oc logout` command only invalidates the OAuth token for the active session. For deleting all the user-owned OAuth tokens, it is needed to delete all of them from the cluster as explained in [deleting user-owned OAuth access tokens](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/authentication/managing-oauth-access-tokens.html#oauth-delete-tokens_managing-oauth-access-tokens).
root_cause: The token shown with `oc whoami--show-token` (1) and the tokens shown with `oc get useroauthaccesstokens` (2) have different names, as the one shown by command (1) is the token stored locally in the `KubeConfig`, and the ones shown by (2) are the tokens in the cluster. When generating a token using the "`Copy login command`" from the top right dropdown on the OpenShift web console, the token shown (that will be used with the `oc login` command) is the token that will be stored locally, and a `useroauthaccesstoken` is also created in the cluster. Deleting the `useroauthaccesstoken` in the cluster doesn't delete the local token in the `KubeConfig`, but invalidate that token to be able to login into the cluster. Using the command `oc logout` will remove the `useroauthaccesstoken` associated to the current login, and also the local token, so creating a new one will be required.
