title: Getting "You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials)" error message on a Single Node OpenShift after certificates expire
issue: - After having an SNO turned off for more than 90 days and turning it back on, the self-signed certificates are all expired.- When trying to renew the certificates following the steps of the knowledge article [5953441](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5953441), the following error message is shown: ``` # export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/node-kubeconfigs/lb-int.kubeconfig # oc get csr-o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve [...] error: You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials) ```
resolution: 1. Copy the SNO `kubeconfig`: ``` # cp /etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/configmaps/control-plane-node-kubeconfig/kubeconfig /tmp/kubeconfig ``` 2. Update the certificate values in the copied `kubeconfig` using `vi /tmp/kubeconfig` and use the following values:- `certificate-authority: /etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/configmaps/trusted-ca-bundle/ca-bundle.crt`- `client-certificate: /etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/control-plane-node-admin-client-cert-key/tls.crt`- `client-key: /etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/control-plane-node-admin-client-cert-key/tls.key` 3. Set the `KUBECONFIG` environment variable to the new temporary `kubeconfig` file: ``` # export KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kubeconfig ``` 4. Now approve the pending certificates: ``` # oc get csr-o name--insecure-skip-tls-verify | xargs oc adm certificate approve--insecure-skip-tls-verify ``` Only after doing this, it will be possible to use the `/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/node-kubeconfigs/lb-int.kubeconfig` file again with the `KUBECONFIG` environment variable.
root_cause: The `/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/node-kubeconfigs/lb-int.kubeconfig` is typically used for nodes to communicate with the API server via the internal load balancer (`lb-int`). The associated user credentials in this `kubeconfig` are likely bound to a node-specific role, such as:- `system:node: `- `system:node-bootstrapper` These roles do not have permissions to approve CSRs, as approval typically requires an elevated role like `system:admin`. The `/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/configmaps/control-plane-node-kubeconfig/kubeconfig` file is usually linked to a higher-privileged account, likely with `cluster-admin` or similar roles, allowing it to approve CSRs. Since the API server itself uses this `kubeconfig`, it has elevated permissions necessary to manage CSRs.

title: Customize UID/GID in JWS image in OCP 4
issue: How to to run JWS as different UID/GID with image, e.g. FROM registry.redhat.io/jboss-webserver-5/jws57-openjdk11-openshift-rhel8:5.7.1?
resolution: OCP has three default Service Accounts: builder, default, deployer. And about either default SCC (e.g. anyuid, privileged, restricted-v2) If deployment doesn't set the service account, so then pod get the default SA and the SCC used will be restricted(-v2), for security reasons. On the JWS image the UID is set for 185, but during the execution OCP the uid and gip are set at much higher than the image itself. For details on association (role and role binding) see the solution [Verify ServiceAccount (SA) and SecurityContextContraints (SCC) in Openshift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7105695). ### Possible Customizations #### Customize SA To customize the SA in the deployment yaml (instead of using the default): ~~~ $ oc get deployment jws-custom-o yaml | grep serviceAccount serviceAccount: default serviceAccountName: default ~~~ ^ default SA are: deployer, default, builder #### Customize SA/SCC To customize the SCC used on a deployment/sts/dc: create a new SA and then assigning a different SCC (in the list of SCC available): 1- First create SA associated with any uid ~~~ $ oc create sa sa-with-anyuid <--- create a SA ~~~ 2- Second associate the SA with the SCC anyuid ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid-z sa-with-anyuid <--- set the SA created () to anyuid ~~~ 3- Set the SA above to the Deployment/DeploymentConfig: ~~~ $ oc patch dc eap-app--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccount":"sa-with-anyuid"}}}}' deploymentconfig.apps.openshift.io/eap-app patched ### Verify: $ get deployment-o yaml | grep serviceAccount serviceAccountName: sa-with-anyuid serviceAccount: sa-with-anyuid ~~~ #### Customize uid/gid To customize the uid/gid on the user inside the container, user might need to change the USER on the containerfile, given that JWS image the UID is set for 185 but during the execution OCP it runs at a higher level. So even setting as runAsUser at the container spec not overwrite the image default user id, so need to be set at image level: First create an image with user 2000 (which overwrites the USER 185): ~~~ FROM registry.redhat.io/jboss-webserver-5/jws57-openjdk11-openshift-rhel8:5.7.1 USER root RUN useradd-u 2000-s /bin/sh-m nfsjboss USER 2000 CMD ["/opt/jws-5.7/tomcat/bin/launch.sh"] ~~~ Second create an SA with anyuid and set on the deployment yaml (see one step above). #### Creating a new SCC Given the anyuid scc already there, most of the times user just need to create an SA and sets this SCC. However, for some specific cases it might be useful to create a new SCC: ~~~ ### define the new scc $ cat scc_admin.yaml kind: SecurityContextConstraints apiVersion: v1 # <--- this was later updated for apiVersion: security.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: scc-admin allowPrivilegedContainer: true runAsUser: type: RunAsAny seLinuxContext: type: RunAsAny fsGroup: type: RunAsAny supplementalGroups: type: RunAsAny users:- my-admin-user groups:- my-admin-group ### create the scc: $ oc create-f scc_admin.yaml securitycontextconstraints "scc-admin" created ~~~ With this new SCC user can associate to a SA and to the deployment yaml.
root_cause: By default, the SCC used by the default SA will be `restricted-v2`, and this is to avoid a security reasons. The deployment needs to point to the SA and then the SA is attached to the SCC, which sets the ranges user id can be. ~~~ deployment--> pod (--> creates/owns) deployment <--> SA <-> SCC (<--> means: associated to) ~~~ Where: Kubernetes Resource | Purpose--------- |--------- deployment | sets the pod yaml properties on template Service account |set the service account properties SCC | Security context constraints- set the constraints (it is attached to the SA) So the process is: User defines the deployment yaml and the deployment yaml's pod template defines the pod yaml. Below deployment yaml has default serviceAccount: ~~~ serviceAccountName: default serviceAccount: default ~~~ Below deployment has default sa-with-anyuid (which is associated with the anyuid scc): ~~~ ### Create SA called sa-with-anyuid $ oc create sa sa-with-anyuid ### Associate the scc anyuid with the sa sa-with-anyuid $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid-z sa-with-anyuid... serviceAccountName: sa-with-anyuid serviceAccount: sa-with-anyuid ~~~ Purpose | Command----------|------- To add | oc adm policy add-scc-to-user SCC-z SA (attention `to`) To remove | oc adm policy remove-scc-from-user SCC-z SA (attention `from`) On the JWS image the UID is set for 185. But during the execution OCP the uid and gip are set at much higher than the image itself: When running within an OpenShift environment, which assigns a higher, random UID to the user. And depending on the range user wants, the user must create a new service account and then attach to the SCC `anyuid`- so then the pod can have any gid/uid. Given the range is beyond the namespaces allowed range (which user fetch via `$oc describe project jws-test | grep sa.scc`). See below: ### Default user/uid/gid: Example below shows the uid used is 1000690000: ~~~ $ oc get pod-o jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{@.metadata.name}{" runAsUser: "}{@.spec.containers[*].securityContext.runAsUser}{" fsGroup: "}{@.spec.securityContext.fsGroup}{" seLinuxOptions: "}{@.spec.securityContext.seLinuxOptions.level}{"\n"}{end}' jws-wsch-app-1-build runAsUser: fsGroup: seLinuxOptions: jws-wsch-app-b9f96895-4vgdm runAsUser: 1000680000 fsGroup: 1000680000 seLinuxOptions: s0:c26,c15... $ whoami; id jboss uid=1000680000(jboss) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000680000 <-------------- uid is 1000680000... $ head /proc/1/status Name: java Umask: 0027 State: S (sleeping) Tgid: 1 Ngid: 0 Pid: 1 PPid: 0 TracerPid: 0 Uid: 1000680000 1000680000 1000680000 1000680000 Gid: 0 0 0 0 ~~~ ### Example (example below sets uid 2000) Create an image with user 2000: FROM registry.redhat.io/jboss-webserver-5/jws57-openjdk11-openshift-rhel8:5.7.1 USER root RUN useradd-u 2000-s /bin/sh-m nfsjboss USER 2000 CMD ["/opt/jws-5.7/tomcat/bin/launch.sh"] Custom image with USER 2000 Deployed on https://quay.io/repository/fdemeloj1/jws57 Create an SA called sa-with-anyuid- assign anyuid: $ oc create sa sa-with-anyuid $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid-z sa-with-anyuid Created an deployment yaml [deployment yaml] and set sa sa-with-anyuid: $ oc get deployment jws-custom-o yaml | grep sa-with-anyuid serviceAccount: sa-with-anyuid serviceAccountName: sa-with-anyuid Results: deployment and then get the uid and user: $ oc get pod NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE jws-custom-5f7bcb9d8c-l6sz4 1/1 Running 0 28s <---- running ### ### $ oc rsh jws-custom-5f7bcb9d8c-l6sz4 <------ confirm the uid and user: sh-4.4$ whoami; id nfsjboss uid=2000(nfsjboss) gid=2000(nfsjboss) groups=2000(nfsjboss) <---------- nfsjboss and uid 2000 To automate the process above, user can create a custom helm chart or custom cli commands. [deployment yaml- complete spec] ~~~ spec: replicas: 1 selector: matchLabels: deployment: jws-wsch-custom template: metadata: creationTimestamp: null labels: deployment: jws-wsch-custom annotations: openshift.io/generated-by: OpenShiftNewApp spec: containers:- name: jws-wsch-custom image: 'quay.io/fdemeloj1/jws57:latest' <-------------------- image ports:- containerPort: 8080 protocol: TCP- containerPort: 8443 protocol: TCP- containerPort: 8778 protocol: TCP resources: {} terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log terminationMessagePolicy: File imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent securityContext: runAsUser: 2000 <------------------------------------------ runAsUser* restartPolicy: Always terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst serviceAccountName: sa-with-anyuid <----------------------------- SA serviceAccount: sa-with-anyuid <----------------------------- SA securityContext: {} schedulerName: default-scheduler strategy: type: RollingUpdate rollingUpdate: maxUnavailable: 25% maxSurge: 25% revisionHistoryLimit: 10 progressDeadlineSeconds: 600 ~~~ [Results: test with default image and runAsUser 0] ~~~ $ oc get pod-o jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{@.metadata.name}{" runAsUser: "}{@.spec.containers[*].securityContext.runAsUser}{" fsGroup: "}{@.spec.securityContext.fsGroup}{" seLinuxOptions: "}{@.spec.securityContext.seLinuxOptions.level}{"\n"}{end}' jws-wsch-app-1-build runAsUser: fsGroup: seLinuxOptions: jws-wsch-app-9fbf8f7c9-wkl7l runAsUser: fsGroup: seLinuxOptions: s0:c26,c15... $ oc rsh jws-wsch-app-9fbf8f7c9-wkl7l sh-4.4$ whoami; id jboss uid=185(jboss) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),185(jboss) <-------------- uid comes from the containerfile... ~~~

title: RHACS: Keeping the violations intact even after deployments/or components deleted
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - When a deployment is deleted from the cluster, and a violation related to that deployment is triggered, the alert displays the following error: ~~~ There was an error fetching the deployment details. This deployment may no longer exist. Deployment with id 'xyz' does not exist: not found ~~~- A violation is not associated with metadata or context at the time of detection is not very useful as it is not traceable.
resolution: - RHACS save some of the basic metadata about a deployment that triggers a violation in the violation record, for some technical and UX reasons.- If the user needs all the information about the deleted deployment, one can reference the deployment object itself in Kubernetes to give them that detailed view.- Once that deployment is no longer deployed, that extra information is not available, and only the basic information stored in the violation itself remains. (The violation itself will also be deleted at the end of its retention period.)- The 'Keeping the violations intact even after deployments/or components deleted' feature is requested to be added into the RHACS.- This is a known feature request reported and Red Hat Engineering team is looking into it.- To get more details on it open a [Support Ticket](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true).

title: Running sosreport invokes a kernel crash upon looking up /proc/[pid_of_sosreport]/fd/[fd_num]
resolution: + [Enabling SLUB debugging](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5577011) as a next action item for further diagnostic would be a reasonable and worthwhile approach at this stage.
root_cause: + Please note, sosreport itself is neither a kernel bug nor an underlying cause here. + A use-after-free on a struct dentry (i.e., an object in the dentry slab cache) can potentially lead to corruption in the dentry hash table when a freed dentry remains linked in the hash table. + In such cases, the stale hash table entry contains a dangling pointer to freed memory, which can lead to an issue like this.

title: Taint a node before adding it in the cluster in RHOCP4
issue: - `Restricting workloads` on a `new node` until fully configured using `taints`
resolution: To ensure that user applications do not run on a `newly added node` by applying `taints`, follow these steps:- Approve the `First CSR` (Node Recognition in Cluster)- After installing CoreOS and rebooting the server, the node generates a Certificate Signing Request (CSR). List pending CSRs using: ~~~ $ oc get csr ~~~- Approve the `first CSR` to allow the node to join the cluster, Replace with the actual CSR name from the previous command output: ~~~ $ oc adm certificate approve ~~~- Add a `Taint` to the Node- Once the `first CSR` is approved, the node will be recognised but not yet in the Ready state. Apply a `taint` to prevent user applications from scheduling on it: ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes key=value:NoSchedule ~~~ * Replace with the node’s hostname. * Modify key=value as per the `tainting` requirement. * `NoSchedule` ensures that no new workloads get scheduled on this node unless `tolerated`.- Approve the `Second CSR` (Move Node to Ready State)- A `second CSR` will be generated, which must be approved to bring the node to a Ready state. List pending CSRs again: ~~~ $ oc get csr ~~~- Approve the `second CSR`: ~~~ $ oc adm certificate approve ~~~- Verify Node Status- Check if the node is in a Ready state and confirm the applied `taint`: ~~~ $ oc get nodes $ oc describe node | grep Taints ~~~- If the `taint` appears correctly, user applications will not be scheduled on this node unless explicitly `tolerated`.

title: How to run ingress controller pods run only on master nodes in OpenShift
issue: - Is it possible to run ingress pods on master nodes?
resolution: - To ensure that IngressController pods run only on master nodes, use nodeSelector and tolerations in the IngressController configuration:- Edit the IngressController object: ~~~ oc edit ingresscontroller default-n openshift-ingress-operator ~~~- Modify the nodePlacement section to include nodeSelector and tolerations: ~~~ spec: nodePlacement: nodeSelector: matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/master: "" tolerations:- effect: NoSchedule key: node-role.kubernetes.io/master operator: Exists ~~~- Restart the Ingress pods to apply the changes: ~~~ oc get pods-n openshift-ingress-o wide ~~~- If using F5 Load Balancer: ~~~ Update the F5 endpoints to point to the master nodes instead of worker nodes. ~~~- If using Keepalived: ~~~ No changes are needed; Keepalived will automatically adjust the routing. ~~~
root_cause: - By default, OpenShift schedules cluster-operator pods across available worker and master nodes.

title: Machine-Config Cluster operator degraded due to error "unexpected on-disk state validating against rendered-master-XXX: expected target osImageURL "quay.io...@XXX " have "quay.io...@XXX...possible root cause: error: Child process exited with code 1

resolution: - Go into affected `node`: ~~~ oc debug node/[node_name] [...] sh-4.4# chroot /host bash ~~~- Validate `ostree-finalize-staged` service logs and identify what is causing the `semodule` failure: ~~~ journalctl-b-1-u ostree-finalize-staged.service Feb 15 17:58:42.625784 ostree[42138]: Copying /etc changes: 24 modified, 0 removed, 2775 added Feb 15 17:58:43.004599 ostree[42148]: The--rebuild-if-modules-changed option is deprecated. Use--refresh instead. Feb 15 17:58:43.560841 ostree[42148]: libsemanage.semanage_direct_get_module_info: Unable to open glusterd-backup.tar.gz module lang ext file at /etc/selinux/targeted/tmp/modules/100/glusterd-backup.tar.gz/lang_ext. (Not a directory).=========> '_This is causing that semodule failes._' Feb 15 17:58:43.560841 ostree[42148]: semodule: Failed! Feb 15 17:58:43.561572 ostree[42138]: error: Child process exited with code 1 Feb 15 17:58:43.563194 systemd[1]: ostree-finalize-staged.service: Control process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE ~~~- Go into described path and move mentioned file into another path **Example** ~~~ mv /etc/selinux/targeted/tmp/modules/100/glusterd-backup.tar.gz /tmp ~~~- Execute next commands: ~~~ semodule-r gremlin-ocp4 rpm-ostree cleanup-p semodule-R ~~~

Add config to horizon httpd by edit openstackcontrolplanes. This config to redirect to KeyCloak logout page when user click logout on OpenStack Dashboard. # oc edit openstackcontrolplanes.core.openstack.org openstack-control-plane ~~~ apiVersion: core.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackControlPlane... spec:... horizon: template: defaultConfigOverwrite: httpd.conf: |... Header always add Set-Cookie "sessionid=; path=/; expires=25 Dec 1991 12:00:00 UTC" Header always add Set-Cookie "login_domain=; path=/; expires=25 Dec 1991 12:00:00 UTC" Header always add Set-Cookie "login_region=; path=/; expires=25 Dec 1991 12:00:00 UTC" Redirect 302 https://keycloak.localdomain/realms/AmigoIDP/protocol/openid-connect/logout/?client_id=openstack&post_logout_redirect_uri=https://keystone-public-openstack.localdomain/v3/auth/OS-FEDERATION/logout ~~~

title: Master Node is not creating pods due to error "Unable to create token for CNI kubeconfig error=serviceaccounts "calico-cni-plugin" is forbidden"
issue: - calico-node `install-cni` init container shows next error: ~~~ 2025-01-07 09:01:25.052 [ERROR][1] cni-installer/token_watch.go 108: Unable to create token for CNI kubeconfig error=serviceaccounts "calico-cni-plugin" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:calico-system:calico-node" cannot create resource "serviceaccounts/token" in API group "" in the namespace "calico-system" 2025-01-07 09:01:25.052 [FATAL][1] cni-installer/install.go 493: Unable to create token for CNI kubeconfig error=serviceaccounts "calico-cni-plugin" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:calico-system:calico-node" cannot create resource "serviceaccounts/token" in API group "" in the namespace "calico-system" ~~~- cluster operator `kube-apiserver` is degraded due to next error: ~~~ clusteroperator/kube-apiserver is degraded because InstallerPodContainerWaitingDegraded: Pod " " on node " " container "installer" is waiting since 2025-01-03 17:36:58 +0000 UTC because ContainerCreating InstallerPodNetworkingDegraded: Pod " " on node " " observed degraded networking: (combined from similar events): Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create pod network sandbox k8s_installer-203-domine_openshift-kube-apiserver_1f11f11-22c2-4444-88c8-dc283570fb02_0(394dad79510dc1929dfe9096096e55ab58f4ac81c348931ebcb5f85fc22b73b9): error adding pod openshift-kube-apiserver_installer-203-master2 to CNI network "multus-cni-network": plugin type="multus" name="multus-cni-network" failed (add): [openshift-kube-apiserver/installer-203-domine/1f11f11-22c2-4444-88c8-dc283570fb02:k8s-pod-network]: error adding container to network "k8s-pod-network": error creating calico client: stat /var/run/multus/cni/net.d/calico-kubeconfig: no such file or directory ~~~
resolution: Calico is a third party CNI plug-in, and while it is a certified CNI plug-in as per [documentation](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5436171), the support for it should be provided by **Tigera** and not by Red Hat. The referenced issue is in the upstream Calico repository, so they need to check with Tigera about that issue.
root_cause: Root cause is related with the CNI Calico configuration. We can not support further on this matter, especially since **Calico is not supported or provided by Red Hat.**

title: Resetting superuser password for Quay through the database
issue: - Pulls from the registry start to fail with the `Invalid username or password` error message and then subsequently Quay starts returning `429 Too many requests` on pulls and login attempts.
resolution: ### OpenShift/VM deployments of Quay 1. Generate a new user password for the affected user:- OpenShift deployment: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n quay-namespace $ oc exec-it quay-pod-name-- python3-c 'import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.hashpw(b"REAL-PASSWORD-HERE", bcrypt.gensalt(12)).decode("utf-8"))' $2b$12$d8W84Z50fNWzf4mL6WWmn.kPFj4dfOnQSnsraghETC8V0RIEBk9Lu ~~~- VM deployment: ~~~ $ podman exec-it quay-container-name python3-c 'import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.hashpw(b"REAL-PASSWORD-HERE", bcrypt.gensalt(12)).decode("utf-8"))' $2b$12$d8W84Z50fNWzf4mL6WWmn.kPFj4dfOnQSnsraghETC8V0RIEBk9Lu ~~~ 2. Execute a PostgreSQL shell inside Quay's database:- For operator managed Quay database: ~~~ $ oc exec-it quay-database-pod-name-- psql postgres=# \l # <--- to list databases postgres=# \c "quay-database-name" quay-database-name=# UPDATE "user" SET password_hash = 'HASH_FROM_STEP_1' WHERE username = 'your_username'; UPDATE 1 quay-database-name=# UPDATE "user" SET invalid_login_attempts = 0 WHERE username = 'your_username'; UPDATE 1 quay-database-name=# \q ~~~- VM deployments and non-managed databases: a. Install the `psql` tool which is available in the `postgresql` package ([package description](https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/postgresql/16.8-1.module+el9.5.0+22865+f9400010/x86_64/fd431d51/package)): ~~~ # yum install postgresql ~~~ b. Connect to the database by executing: ~~~ # psql-d quay-database-name-h quay-db-host-p port-U quay-db-name-W Enter password: ~~~ c. Execute the following queries: ~~~ quay-database-name=# UPDATE "user" SET password_hash = 'HASH_FROM_STEP_1' WHERE username = 'your_username'; UPDATE 1 quay-database-name=# UPDATE "user" SET invalid_login_attempts = 0 WHERE username = 'your_username'; UPDATE 1 quay-database-name=# \q ~~~ ### OpenShift Mirror Registry 1. Generate a new user password for the affected user: ~~~ $ podman exec-it quay-app python3-c 'import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.hashpw(b"REAL-PASSWORD-HERE", bcrypt.gensalt(12)).decode("utf-8"))' $2b$12$d8W84Z50fNWzf4mL6WWmn.kPFj4dfOnQSnsraghETC8V0RIEBk9Lu ~~~ 2. OMR stores all Quay information in a SQLite3 database which is usually stored as a Podman volume. You can check the volume name by inspecting the unit file. Assuming that OMR is installed under `root` user: ~~~ # cat /etc/systemd/system/quay-app.service | grep-i sqlite-v sqlite-storage-volume:/sqlite \ ~~~ 3. Shut down Quay by running: ~~~ # systemctl stop quay-app.service ~~~ The app must be completely shut down and `podman ps` should not show it as a running container. 4. Run the `ubi9` container on the node with the following command: ~~~ # podman run--rm-it-v sqlite-storage:/sqlite-storage:Z registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest ~~~ Install the `sqlite` utility inside the container ([package info](https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/sqlite/3.46.1-3.el10/x86_64/fd431d51/package)), we need it to connect to the SQLite database: ~~~ # yum install-y sqlite ~~~ Connect to the database and execute the following queries: ~~~ # sqlite3 /sqlite-storage/quay_sqlite.db sqlite> UPDATE user SET password_hash = 'HASH_FROM_STEP_1' WHERE username = 'your_username'; sqlite> UPDATE user SET invalid_login_attempts = 0 WHERE username = 'your_username'; sqlite>.quit # exit ~~~ 5. Restart Quay container by executing: ~~~ # systemctl start quay-app.service ~~~
root_cause: - Quay stores user information (such as username and e-mail address) in its own database. If internal auth is set to `Database`, it also stores a `bcrypt` hash of the user's password in the `password_hash` field.- On each login attempt, whether it's through the UI or through the Docker v2 API by `podman/crio`, the authentication endpoint checks the password validity against the hash stored in the database.- If a wrong password is given too many times, Quay will start throwing a `429 Too many requests to registry` HTTP code and will start exponentially increasing the cooldown time for the affected user. This number can grow very large very quickly if the wrong password is used in a pipeline for instance.- Super users can change passwords for normal users via the "super user control panel", but this cannot be done for other super users. So a direct change in the database is necessary.- Once passwords are reset using this procedure, the password is immediately active.- Note that this procedure **only** works if `AUTHENTICATION_TYPE: Database` is set in Quay's `config.yaml` file. If you're using `LDAP` or `OIDC` as the internal auth type, passwords cannot be changed using this procedure since user auth management is offloaded to the federated login service. However, the number of failed login attempts can still be reset as that is always stored in Quay's database.- We would **highly recommend not** using real user credentials in any pipelines that talk to the registry. Robot accounts are much better suited for automations, since their tokens never change (unless they are regenerated manually).

title: Send ArgoCD notifications to Teams
issue: How can we send ArgoCD notifications to Teams?
resolution: 1. Enable notifications with an ArgoCD instance: ~~~ $ oc patch argocd openshift-gitops-n openshift-gitops--type merge--patch '{"spec": {"notifications": {"enabled": true}}}' ~~~ 2. Edit the the `NotificationsConfiguration` CR to add the Teams service: ~~~ $ oc edit notificationsconfiguration default-notifications-configuration-n data: service.teams: | recipientUrls: channelName: $channel-teams-url ~~~ For more details about editing the `NotificationsConfiguration` CR please check the [official documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_gitops/1.13/html/argo_cd_instance/argo-cd-cr-component-properties#notifications-configuration-custom-resource-properties_argo-cd-cr-component-properties "https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_gitops/1.13/html/argo_cd_instance/argo-cd-cr-component-properties#notifications-configuration-custom-resource-properties_argo-cd-cr-component-properties") 3. Modify the `argocd-notifications-secret` CR: ~~~ kind: Secret apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: argocd-notifications-secret namespace: openshift-gitops data: channel-teams-url: ~~~ 4. Create subscription for your Teams integration by editing the app yaml: ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: Application metadata: annotations: notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-sync-succeeded.teams: channelName ~~~
root_cause: This is based on the [upstream documentation.](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/notifications/services/teams/ "https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/notifications/services/teams/")

title: Pods does not remove attached `NETNS` when deleted forcefully
issue: - When the pod is forcefully deleted, pod does not remove attached `NetworkNamespace (NETNS)`.- After pod is deleted, how to identify unused `NETNS` and remove them from `Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS (RHCOS)` node?
resolution: - Create a script `netns_script.sh` as below: ``` #!/bin/bash set-e # ========= Configuration ========= NETNS_DIR="/var/run/netns" DRY_RUN=false # ========= Parse Arguments ========= if [["$1" == "--dry-run"]]; then DRY_RUN=true echo "[DRY-RUN MODE] No netns will be deleted." fi # ========= Check for root privilege ========= if [["$(id-u)"-ne 0]]; then echo "ERROR: This script must be run as root." > &2 exit 1 fi # ========= Check if netns directory exists ========= if [[!-d "$NETNS_DIR"]]; then echo "No netns directory found at $NETNS_DIR" exit 0 fi # ========= Step 1: Collect all existing netns IDs ========= echo "[INFO] Collecting netns files from: $NETNS_DIR" all_netns_ids=$(ls "$NETNS_DIR") # ========= Step 2: Collect in-use netns from running sandboxes ========= # This part uses crictl to inspect each running pod (sandbox), # and extracts the network namespace path in use echo "[INFO] Collecting used netns from running sandboxes..." used_netns_ids=$(crictl pods-q | while read-r sandbox_id; do crictl inspectp "$sandbox_id" 2> /dev/null | \ jq-r '.info.runtimeSpec.linux.namespaces[]? | select(.type=="network") |.path' | \ grep "$NETNS_DIR" | xargs-n1 basename done | sort-u) # ========= Step 3: Compare and clean ========= echo "" echo "[INFO] Comparing netns on disk vs in-use..." orphan_count=0 for netns in $all_netns_ids; do # If the netns ID is not found in the list of in-use namespaces if! echo "$used_netns_ids" | grep-q "^$netns$"; then echo "Orphan netns found: $netns" if [["$DRY_RUN" == false]]; then ip netns delete "$netns" && echo "Deleted $netns" || echo "Failed to delete $netns" else echo "Dry-run: Skipping deletion of $netns" fi ((orphan_count++)) fi done # ========= Summary ========= echo "" echo "[INFO] Cleanup complete. Total orphan netns found: $orphan_count" ```- Make the script `netns_script.sh` executable on the node using the command below. ``` $ sudo chmod u+x netns_script.sh ```- Try passing `--dry-run` to safely check unused `NETNS` present on the `RHCOS` node. ``` $ sudo./netns_script.sh--dry-run [DRY-RUN MODE] No netns will be deleted. [INFO] Collecting netns files from: /var/run/netns [INFO] Collecting used netns from running sandboxes... [INFO] Comparing netns on disk vs in-use... [INFO] Cleanup complete. Total orphan netns found: 0 ```- If the above returns `Total orphan netns found:` greater than `0`, then execute the same command without the argument `--dry-run` to delete the unused `NETNS` on `RHCOS` node.
root_cause: ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*- If the application pods are deleted forcefully, using `--force` argument, then the pod is deleted quickly, bypassing any normal closure and finalizer processes, ignoring cleanup steps. ``` $ oc delete pod--force pod " " force deleted ```- The result is an unassigned `NETNS` still left on the `RHCOS` node, which can cause issues when new pods are scaled.- The following is also mentioned in the upstream `Kubernetes` [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubectl/generated/kubectl_delete/), mentioning what happens when a pod is forcefully deleted. ``` IMPORTANT: Force deleting pods does not wait for confirmation that the pod's processes have been terminated, which can leave those processes running until the node detects the deletion and completes graceful deletion. If your processes use shared storage or talk to a remote API and depend on the name of the pod to identify themselves, force deleting those pods may result in multiple processes running on different machines using the same identification which may lead to data corruption or inconsistency. Only force delete pods when you are sure the pod is terminated, or if your application can tolerate multiple copies of the same pod running at once. Also, if you force delete pods, the scheduler may place new pods on those nodes before the node has released those resources and causing those pods to be evicted immediately. ```

title: Why Quay did not free up storage/quota after tags were deleted
issue: - Quay did not free up storage/quota after tags were deleted
resolution: Quota and storage space won't be free up unless all images that contain the layer are deleted and garbage collection will remove the layers after the expiration period.
root_cause: Manifest layer may be used by another tag, as a Manifest can have multiple tags

title: Job fails with "Failed to JSON parse a line from worker stream ... Line with invalid JSON data: b''
issue: AAP jobs are failing frequently with error `Job reaped due to instance shutdown`.
Jobs are failing intermittently with the error: ``` Failed to JSON parse a line from worker stream. Error: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) Line with invalid JSON data: b'' ```
resolution: There is no workaround or fix available for every environment. The cause of the error message is environment-specific and will require checking logs from multiple components to find the root cause. Various logs to check, and workarounds that have resolved the issue, are available below. Find the platform and environment that corresponds to your Ansible Automation Platform configuration below. ### Platform Independent Below are a some workarounds that have worked on different installations. Each Ansible Automation Platform is unique, so more than one workaround may need to be applied. It's possible that the workarounds listed below may not resolve the issue. Evaluate the suggestions below and make a determination if any might fit your environment. 1. Ensure the script running (if any) is not sending a lot of output to stdout. 2. Check for any transient network latency 3. Set the `RECEPTOR_KUBE_SUPPORT_RECONNECT` to `enabled`. ### On-premise Virtual Machine Collect a sosreport from all controller nodes experiencing the issue and attach it to the support case. Check if `fapolicy` is enabled and make sure it's not preventing executables from running. ### OpenShift or Kubernetes platform Generate a must-gather archive and attach it to the support case. If a pod or container is exiting due to `OOMKill`, increase the request and limits on the controller/receptor pods ### Postgreql-related issues On some systems, editing the Postgresql keep-alive settings have resolved the problem. In order to resolve such issue follow below steps: 1. Make a backup from `/etc/tower/conf.d/postgres.py` on all control/hybrid nodes. 2. Add the following keepalive settings as per the following example: ``` 'OPTIONS': {'sslmode': 'prefer', 'sslrootcert': '/xxx/xxx/xxx/xxx/xxxxx.crt', 'keepalives': 1, 'keepalives_count': 5, 'keepalives_idle': 5, 'keepalives_interval': 5}, ``` 3. Stop and start the services with the following commands: ``` # automation-controller-service stop # automation-controller-service start ```

title: Example usage of the OpenShift Alertmanager REST API
issue: How can alerts be read from the Alertmanager instance in the User Workload Monitoring in OpenShift Container Platform?
How can `curl` be used to interact with the Alertmanager instance in OpenShift Container Platform?
resolution: * When using User Workload Monitoring in OpenShift Container Platform, Alertmanager can be enabled as part of User Workload Monitoring so that customer can create their own alerts, alerting rules and Alertmanager configuration. This Alertmanager instance can then be accessed by developers and users with the respective roles that Red Hat provides in OpenShift Container Platform: [Granting users permissions for monitoring for user-defined projects](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/monitoring/configuring-user-workload-monitoring/preparing-to-configure-the-monitoring-stack-uwm.html#granting-users-permission-to-monitor-user-defined-projects_preparing-to-configure-the-monitoring-stack-uwm) * For example, when you provide access to the `monitoring-edit` ClusterRole to a certain ServiceAccount, you can then use the ServiceAccount token to talk to the Alertmanager API via the tenant-restricted API via port 9092: ~~~ $ curl-k-H"Authorization: Bearer $(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)" https://alertmanager-user-workload.openshift-user-workload-monitoring.svc:9092/api/v2/alerts?namespace=example-project [] ~~~ Note that the URL parameter `namespace=` needs to be specified to access the tenant-restricted API. * Using the broader `monitoring-alertmanager-api-writer` or `monitoring-alertmanager-api-reader` roles allows users access to all alerts in the Alertmanager instance. The following example shows usage of the REST API via the non-tenant-aware API (port 9095): ~~~ $ curl-v-k-H"Authorization: Bearer $(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)"-H "Content-Type: application/json"-d '[{"labels":{"alertname":"test-alert","namespace":"example-project"}}]' https://alertmanager-user-workload.openshift-user-workload-monitoring.svc:9095/api/v2/alerts [..] < HTTP/1.1 200 OK ~~~ * The available API endpoints (with a description and necessary roles / ports) are documented in the following documentation section: [openshift-user-workload-monitoring/alertmanager-user-workload](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/monitoring/accessing-metrics/accessing-monitoring-apis-by-using-the-cli.html#openshift-user-workload-monitoringalertmanager-user-workload)

title: Storage CO is degraded due to VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRDegraded in RHOCP 4
issue: - The storage CO is degraded with the below error: ~~~ $ oc get co storage NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE storage 4.12.34 True False True 50s VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRDegraded: VMwareVSphereControllerDegraded: error logging into vcenter: ServerFaultCode: Cannot complete login due to an incorrect user name or password. ~~~
resolution: Workaround 1 ==================- Confirm if the Vcenter credentials are correct: ~~~ $ export GOVC_URL="https:// " $ export GOVC_USERNAME=" " $ export GOVC_PASSWORD=" " $ export GOVC_INSECURE=true $ govc ls ~~~- If that is successful, update the `kube-system` secret with the correct username and password, like below: ~~~ $ echo-n $GOVC_PASSWORD | base64 $ oc get secret vsphere-creds-o yaml-n kube-system > creds_backup.yaml $ cp creds_backup.yaml vsphere-creds.yaml $ vi vsphere-creds.yaml apiVersion: v1 data: YOURVCENTERADDRESS.password: YOURVCENTERPASSWORD_ENCODED** YOURVCENTERADDRESS.username: YOURVCENTERUSERVNAME_ENCODED** kind: Secret metadata: annotations: cloudcredential.openshift.io/mode: passthrough name: vsphere-creds namespace: kube-system type: Opaque ~~~ Workaround 2 ==================- Upgrade the VMware virtual hardware version to 15 or later of all the RHOCP nodes that have been reported to have a lower VMware virtual hardware version than 15.- Delete the `clustercsidriver` object to re-evaluate the checks: ~~~ $ oc delete clustercsidriver csi.vsphere.vmware.com ~~~

title: Error when adding restartPolicy for non-init containers
issue: Pods are throwing error if restartPolicy is incorrectly set.
resolution: Remove the `spec.containers.restartPolicy` field from the non-init container definition to resolve the error.
root_cause: The `spec.containers.restartPolicy` field only works with init containers and not for non-init containers. More details about the field can be read using below command: ~~~ $ oc explain pod.spec.containers.restartPolicy ~~~

title: Dynamic system-reserved creates memory reservation with 2 decimal places
issue: When using Dynamic system-reserved `SYSTEM_RESERVED_MEMORY` can be set as a figure with 2 decimal places- which is not supported by Kubernetes and causes the incorrect unit of measurement to be used by the node.
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-355](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-355) and delivered a fix in RHOCP 4.12.0 through errata [RHSA-2022:7398](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:7398). If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. #### Workaround Set manually the [recommended CPU and memory values reserved for the system](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5843241)
root_cause: Limits and requests for memory are measured in bytes. They can be expressed as a plain integer or as a fixed-point number using one of the following quantity suffixes: ~~~ E, P, T, G, M, k. ~~~ It can also use the power-of-two equivalents: ~~~ Ei, Pi, Ti, Gi, Mi, Ki. ~~~ Please pay attention to the case of the suffixes. A request for 200m of memory, is actually a request for 0.2 bytes. Someone who requests 200m probably meant to ask for 200 mebibytes (200Mi) or 200 megabytes (200M).

title: NooBaa System Phase is "Configuring" After Upgrade - The parsed AWS region is invalid: \"\" - OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: NooBaa/Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) fails to determine AWS region. This issue has been seen in ODF upgrades, or node name changes to a different region that no longer has the region in the node name. As a result, NooBaa is unable to parse, reconcile, and determine the proper region which can result in a `Configuring`, `Connecting`, or `Rejected` Phase. ~~~ time="2024-11-04T21:36:13Z" level=error msg="Got error from util.GetAWSRegion(). will use arnPrefix=\"arn:aws:s3:::\". error=The parsed AWS region is invalid: \"\"" sys=openshift-storage/noobaa ~~~
resolution: 1. Take a backup of the backingstore and credentials request that are having issues: **Example:** **Annotate the Resource Names:** ~~~ $ oc get credentialsrequest-n openshift-storage NAME AGE noobaa-aws-cloud-creds 130m $ oc get backingstore-n openshift-storage NAME TYPE PHASE AGE noobaa-default-backing-store aws-s3 Ready 140m ~~~ **Backup Using Annotated Resource Names from Previous Outputs:** ~~~ $ oc get credentialsrequest-n openshift-storage noobaa-aws-cloud-creds-o yaml > noobaa-aws-cloud-creds.yaml $ oc get backingstore-n openshift-storage noobaa-default-backing-store-o yaml > noobaa-default-backing-store.yaml ~~~ 2. Validate the region is set correctly with `$ oc get backingstore-n openshift-storage-o yaml | grep-i region`. If the region is not set correctly, edit the backingstore and change the region to reflect the region of the VPC/ODF Worker Instances: ~~~ $ oc edit backingstore-n openshift-storage noobaa-default-backing-store spec: awsS3: region: us-east-1 <---------------------- secret: name: noobaa-aws-cloud-creds-secret <---- CredentialsRequest namespace: openshift-storage ~~~ 3. Edit the `CredentialsRequest` and ensure the region is now reflected in the name: ~~~ $ oc edit credentialsrequest-n openshift-storage ~~~ **Example Output:** ~~~ spec: providerSpec: apiVersion: cloudcredential.openshift.io/v1 kind: AWSProviderSpec statementEntries:- action:- s3:* effect: Allow resource: arn:aws:s3:::nb.1733246637036.apps. <--------- action:- s3:* effect: Allow resource: arn:aws:s3:::nb.1733246637036.apps. /* <------ action:- s3:ListAllMyBuckets effect: Allow resource: '*' ~~~ **Change To:** **Note:** This will most likely need to be changed to the region that was previously in the node name. ~~~ spec: providerSpec: apiVersion: cloudcredential.openshift.io/v1 kind: AWSProviderSpec statementEntries:- action:- s3:* effect: Allow resource: arn:aws-us-east:s3:::nb.1733246637036.apps. <--------- action:- s3:* effect: Allow resource: arn:aws-us-east:s3:::nb.1733246637036.apps. /* <------ action:- s3:ListAllMyBuckets effect: Allow resource: '*' ~~~ 4. Once configs have been saved, restart the NooBaa pods in accordance with section [12.1. Restoring the Multicloud Object Gateway](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.17/html/troubleshooting_openshift_data_foundation/restoring-the-monitor-pods-in-openshift-data-foundation_rhodf#restoring_the_multicloud_object_gateway) of the Troubleshooting Product Documentation.
root_cause: This should mainly occur when there was a node name change and the previous/current node name reflected an AWS region name. Later, when node names/regions change the Noobaa operator fails to parse the region out of the node name and hits a conflict, shown in the NooBaa code and git issue below: [Line 1126- Subject to Change](https://github.com/noobaa/noobaa-operator/blob/master/pkg/util/util.go) ~~~ // GetAWSRegion parses the region from a node's name func GetAWSRegion() (string, error) {// parse the node name to get AWS region according to this: // https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_pv/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-dns.html#vpc-dns-hostnames // The list of regions can be found here: // https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html ~~~ The issue can be shown here as well: [noobaa-operator v2.0.2 crash in OCS testing](https://github.com/noobaa/noobaa-operator/issues/90) This is a bug fix, and the issue has been fixed in the following versions:- `ODF v4.16.9`- `ODF v4.17.6`- `ODF v4.18.0`

title: How do I configure fence_kdump for compute nodes in a Red Hat OpenStack Services on Openshift 18.x cluster
issue: - How do I configure fence_kdump for compute nodes in a Red Hat OpenStack on Openshift 18.x cluster
resolution: NOTE: Beacause of the limitations of kexec-tools fence_kdump may not work if your network is configured to use ovs bonds and/or ovs bridges for the interface that should be used to set the kdump notifications. We recommend using plain interfaces, vlan interfaces and linux bonds where appropriate. 1. Ensure that the kdump service is properly configured on all nodes and is started. The Kdump Helper web application can assist in configuring kdump. ~~~ # systemctl is-active kdump active ~~~ 2. Ensure that the fence_kdump fence agent is installed on all compute nodes. ~~~ # dnf install fence-agents-kdump ~~~ 3. Ensure the InstanceHA service is deployed with a network-attachment-definition so the pod is able to communicate directly with the computes, like over a vlan o similar, for example using the internalapi: ~~~ $ cat ihatests/iha.yaml apiVersion: instanceha.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: InstanceHa metadata: name: instanceha-0 spec: caBundleSecretName: combined-ca-bundle networkAttachments: ['internalapi']" ~~~ 4. Retrieve the ip address of the instanceha pod, either by 'oc describe ' or a command like: ~~~ $ oc get instanceha-o json |jq-r '.items[0].status.networkAttachments["openstack/internalapi"][0]' ~~~ 5. Ensure the kdump.conf config file contains the proper options for kdump to send messages over the network. Assuming 172.16.0.178 is the IP of the InstanceHA pod retrieved at step 4: ~~~ # echo "fence_kdump_nodes 172.16.0.178 > > /etc/kdump.conf # echo 'fence_kdump_args-p 7410-f auto-c 0-i 5' > > /etc/kdump.conf ~~~ 6. Regenerate the initrd image by restarting the kdump service: ~~~ # systemctl restart kdump ~~~ 7. Test the configuration by crashing one of the nodes using the command below. ~~~ # echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger ~~~ 8. On the crashed node, you may see the kdump progress on a graphical or serial console. On the instanceha pod logs you should see in the logs that fence_kdump received messages: ~~~ $ oc logs

title: How to downgrade OpenShift Logging 5.4 to 5.3?
issue: - How to downgrade OpenShift Logging 5.4 to 5.3?
resolution: The downgrade needs the following steps. 1. Backup and remove existing CRs, ClusterLogging and ClusterLogForwarder resources ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging get clusterlogging-o yaml > clusterlogging.yaml $ oc-n openshift-logging get clusterlogforwarder-o yaml > clusterlogforwarder.yaml $ oc-n openshift-logging delete $(oc-n openshift-logging get clusterlogging,clusterlogforwarder-o name) ~~~ 2. Confirm if the all non-operator pods terminated in the openshift-logging project ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging get pod ~~~ 3. Uninstall ClusterLogging and Elasticsearch operators In Web Console, Operators-> Installed operators-> All projects-> Click 3 dot menu icon of the target operator-> Uninstall 4. Re-install ClusterLogging and Elasticsearch operators Make sure to select stable-5.3 channel. 5. Restore CRs ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging create-f clusterlogging.yaml $ oc-n openshift-logging create-f clusterlogforwarder.yaml ~~~ ### Notes- ClusterLogging downgrade needs all CRs deleted for consistency.- The persistent volumes and PVCs for Elasticsearch are kept between the reinstall. There is no data loss expected.- Changing the channel in the subscription resource won't perform downgrade as it only support upgrades. We need to delete CRs and re-install the operator to perform the downgrade.

title: Missing Logs in /var/crash Post Kdump Setup in RHOCP4
issue: - Logs absent in /var/crash following Kdump setup.- Logs still missing despite deliberately triggering node NotReady to access logs using `echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger`.
resolution: - Here is an example for the workaround in which the kdump data will be transferred to the bastion host with the help of secure shell (SSH): # Prerequisites: On Bastion node:- Place the butane binary on the bastion node: ``` $ sudo curl-Lo /usr/bin/butane https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/butane/latest/butane && sudo chmod +x /usr/bin/butane ```- Check the hostname: ``` $ hostname bastion.cluster.domain.com ```- Check the user name: ``` $ whoami core ```- Create a directory with correct access to collect the kdump logs: ``` $ sudo mkdir /mnt/kdump_data && sudo chown core.core /mnt/kdump_data-R ```- Create a pair of keys to use with kdumps while coping data from the node to location `/mnt/kdump_data`. ``` $ ssh-keygen-m PEM-t rsa-b 4096-f ~/.ssh/id_kdump Generating public/private rsa key pair. Enter passphrase (empty for no passphrase): Enter same passphrase again: Your identification has been saved in /home/quickcluster/.ssh/id_kdump. Your public key has been saved in /home/quickcluster/.ssh/id_kdump.pub. The key fingerprint is: SHA256:FkkbY29PdcD7UpbFE0tPLaWye+K6gn/wzHYIp2j3uXQ quickcluster@upi-0.shrocp4upi414sdn.lab.upshift.rdu2.redhat.com The key's randomart image is: +---[RSA 4096]----+ | =.o**| | o *.+=*| | + o o.+=| | o o o..o| | S o + | |.o....| | o O..E.. | | + +.B+.o | |. o.=*=. | +----[SHA256]-----+ ```- Add public keys to the `authorized_keys` and and give the correct permissions: ``` $ cat ~/.ssh/id_kdump.pub > > ~/.ssh/authorized_keys $ chmod 0600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys ```- Create a butane file that will be used to create MachineConfig manifest file: ``` $ cat kdump.bu variant: openshift version: 4.14.0 # Set the correct version metadata: name: 99-worker-kdump labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker # To configure it for worker nodes. openshift: kernel_arguments:- crashkernel=512M storage: files:- path: /root/.ssh/id_rsa # User root has the permissions to deal with kdump mode: 0600 overwrite: true contents: inline: |-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- ADD_THE_PRIVATE_KEYS_HERE_FROM ~/.ssh/id_kdump # Internal content of private key.-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY------ path: /root/.ssh/config # Create this entry to silent the known host warning. mode: 0644 overwrite: true contents: inline: | Host bastion.cluster.domain.com # Add the correct hostname here StrictHostKeyChecking no- path: /etc/kdump.conf mode: 0644 overwrite: true contents: inline: | extra_bins /usr/bin/rsync core_collector makedumpfile-l--message-level 31-d 31-F ssh core@bastion.cluster.domain.com # Add the correct user name and hostname here sshkey /root/.ssh/id_rsa path /mnt/kdump_data- path: /etc/sysconfig/kdump mode: 0644 overwrite: true contents: inline: | KDUMP_COMMANDLINE_REMOVE="hugepages hugepagesz slub_debug quiet log_buf_len swiotlb" KDUMP_COMMANDLINE_APPEND="irqpoll nr_cpus=1 reset_devices cgroup_disable=memory mce=off numa=off udev.children-max=2 panic=10 rootflags=nofail acpi_no_memhotplug transparent_hugepage=never nokaslr novmcoredd hest_disable" KEXEC_ARGS="-s" KDUMP_IMG="vmlinuz"- path: /etc/sysctl.d/99-sysrq.conf mode: 0644 contents: inline: | kernel.sysrq = 1 systemd: units:- name: kdump.service enabled: true ```- Export a yaml file from the butane file: ``` $ butane kdump.bu-o kdump.yaml ```- Apply the MachineConfig manifest file to enable the kdump: ``` $ oc apply-f kdump.yaml machineconfig.machineconfiguration.openshift.io/99-worker-kdump created ``` # Testing:- Access any worker node: ``` $ oc debug node/worker01.xxxxxx.com Starting pod/worker01.xxxxxx.com-debug-8pgt8... To use host binaries, run chroot /host Pod IP: 10.0.128.4 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.4# chroot /host sh-5.1# echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger Removing debug pod... ```- Once that done check the collected content under /mnt/kdump_data on the bastion host: ``` # ls /mnt/kdump_data 127.0.0.1-2022-07-01-05:25:25 # ls /var/crash/127.0.0.1-2022-07-01-05\:25\:25/ vmcore vmcore-dmesg.txt ```
root_cause: - Post configuring the kdumps in the RHCOS node any file in the `/var/crash` not visible. ``` $ oc debug node/worker01.xxxxxx.com Starting pod/worker01.xxxxxx.com-debug-8pgt8... To use host binaries, run chroot /host Pod IP: 10.0.128.4 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.4# chroot /host sh-5.1# ls /var/crash/ sh-5.1# ```- Transitioning from version 4.6 to 6.12 might present a problem.- This issue arises because version 4.6 featured Luks encryption, which was removed in version 4.12.

issue: - After updating the RHACS Operator to the release 4.7.0, the local Scanner pods from the Secured Cluster are not able to start. ~~~ $ oc get pods-l app=scanner-n NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE scanner-xxxxxxxxx-yyyyy 0/1 Init:0/1 1 15m scanner-xxxxxxxxx-zzzzz 0/1 Init:0/1 1 15m scanner-xxxxxxxxx-wwwww 0/1 Init:0/1 1 15m ~~~- The issue is narrowed down to the Scanner pod **init-tls-certs*

Init Container not being able to start. ~~~ $ oc get events-n | grep BackOff 13m Warning BackOff pod/scanner-7b959496f-62ftk Back-off restarting failed container init-tls-certs in pod scanner-7b959496f-62ftk_stackrox(00791ff2-e16c-4086-a98a-e0dc04220c9d) 10m Warning BackOff pod/scanner-7b959496f-7fpb7 Back-off restarting failed container init-tls-certs in pod scanner-7b959496f-7fpb7_stackrox(564748be-dd53-41a2-a7e2-acf7a2f312ad) 14m Warning BackOff pod/scanner-7b959496f-s7bw8 Back-off restarting failed container init-tls-certs in pod scanner-7b959496f-s7bw8_stackrox(5ab01326-34ee-426b-a878-9533672675af) [supportshell-1.sush-001.prod.us-west-2.aws.redhat.com] [00:54:28+0000] ~~~
resolution: There are two different paths to resolve this issue, and they are listed in their recommended order below: 1- Upgrade to the RHACS 4.7.1 patch release which resolves this issue. 2- Update Central. Per the [Support Policy](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7045053), Red Hat does not recommend upgrading Secured Clusters ahead of Central.
root_cause: - This is a bug and a fix should be provided in the RHACS 4.7.1 release and a ticket is already opened and available at https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ROX-28591.- It occurs because the Scanner deployment file is referencing two non-existent keys (scanner-cert.pem and scanner-key.pem) from the secret scanner-tls, and therefore the Init Container init-tls-certs is able to find just the key named ca.pem.- Also, for this to happen the Central must be v4.5.z or older.

title: Is it possible to set `cpu_mode=custom` and `cpu_models=SapphireRapids` with Intel SapphireRapids on RHEL9?
issue: - Is it possible to set `cpu_mode=custom` and `cpu_models=SapphireRapids` with Intel SapphireRapids on RHEL9.4?- With Intel Xeon Gold 6421N Processor, `virsh domcapabilities` returns `usable=no` for SapphireRapids in custom mode.
resolution: - Some Xeon CPUs in SapphireRapids family doesn't support AMX. Due to that qemu doesn't allow to assign SapphireRapids when mode is custom.- There is a way to use custom profile for SapphireRapids, please refer to [When `cpu_mode=custom` and `cpu_models=SapphireRapids` assigned in nova, nova-compute cannot start.](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7098732)
root_cause: - Even thought the same class, Xeon Gold, there seems to be several CPU configuration. Some CPU lacks an feature, AMX. Due to that, qemu reports the feature doesn't exist in the CPU then 'SapphireRapids' model cannot be assigned as custom mode.

title: ROSA HCP Cluster upgrade causes worker node recreation and requiring Manual re-registration of targets in the AWS NLB target group.
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - After ROSA HCP cluster upgrade from version 4.15.18 to 4.15.43 all the worker nodes from machine pool have been recreated on AWS Console.- Recreation of worker node pool affected all the client application workloads running in our cluster, as all the worker machines recreated NLB's targets went into unhealthy state, and Manual re-registration of targets in the AWS NLB target group was performed to restore connectivity.- Is it an expected behaviors of worker machine node pool recreation and Manual re-registration of targets in the AWS NLB target group in ROSA HCP cluster during cluster update?
resolution: - [ROSA HCP upgrade](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html/upgrading/rosa-hcp-upgrading#rosa-upgrade-options_rosa-hcp-upgrading) mechanism follow the Rolling upgrade mechanism for hosted control plane and nodes in a machine pool.- Manually registering the AWS NLB target group after an upgrade is not expected behavior.- In ROSA HCP AWS-provided profiles are managed policies and cannot be edited by Customer/users.- Check if there can be extra security group `arn:aws:ec2:xx-xxxxxxx-x:xxxxxxxxxxxx:security-group/sg-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` attached with the VPC Endpoint manually.
root_cause: - ROSA HCP can only modify cloud resources that are tagged with `red-hat-managed=true` due to AWS managed IAM Policies.- It is expected that, the ROSA HCP is unable to update the VPC Endpoints while the customer-managed security group is attached to VPC endpoints.

title: oc-mirror plugin fails with catalog is invalid and 401 unauthorized error when it hangs for few minutes in RHOCP 4
issue: - Mirroring images for a disconnected environment using `oc-mirror` plugin gets hung and then getting failed.- Even though the registry credentials are good as per [`oc-mirror` in a disconnected environment fails with a "`HTTP 401 Unauthorized`" error](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6994367), mirroring is getting failed.- Usually the error occurs in between the mirroring while it is not able to get an image in a specified time limit.- The mirror fails with the following messages: ~~~ The rendered catalog is invalid. ~~~ ~~~ error: error rendering new refs: render reference "registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12": error resolving name: pulling from host registry.redhat.io failed with status code [manifests v4.12]: 401 Unauthorized ~~~
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this issue, and it has been fixed for RHOCP 4.14. via [OCPBUGS-20137](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/OCPBUGS-20137) by [errata RHSA-2023:5006](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:5006). If facing similar "`401 unauthorized`" issues in newer releases, please refer to [oc-mirror command is failing to execute with `401 unauthorized` error](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7089622).
root_cause: When several catalogs are mirrored, `oc-mirror` will loop catalogs and perform, for each, a rendering (with `operator-registry`'s `action.Render`) followed by `mirrorMappings` for the contents of that catalog. Using a single `operator-registry` for all catalogs means that the second time the registry will be used, it is going to start working with a expired token potentially.

title: Create ETCD ca, peer, server certificates in Openshift 3.11 manually.
issue: - Playbook is failing to renew etcd CA and etcd certs.- How I can manually create etcd CA and etcd certs?
resolution: - Create custom openssl.cnf files for CA.- Create the custom openssl.cnf {peer/server}.crt and master-etcd-client.crt **for each nodes as these contains hostname and IP of each etcd node**. ### etcd-server-peer-openssl.cnf: For peer and server certificate ~~~ [req] distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name x509_extensions = etcd_v3_ca_server # The extensions to add to the self signed cert [req_distinguished_name] [etcd_v3_ca_server] authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid,issuer:always basicConstraints = critical,CA:FALSE extendedKeyUsage = serverAuth,clientAuth keyUsage = digitalSignature,keyEncipherment subjectKeyIdentifier = hash subjectAltName = @alt_names [alt_names] DNS.1 = IP.1 = ~~~ ### client-openssl.cnf: For peer and server certificate ~~~ [req] distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name x509_extensions = etcd_v3_ca_server # The extensions to add to the self signed cert [req_distinguished_name] [etcd_v3_ca_server] authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid,issuer:always basicConstraints = critical,CA:FALSE extendedKeyUsage = clientAuth keyUsage = digitalSignature,keyEncipherment subjectKeyIdentifier = hash subjectAltName = @alt_names [alt_names] DNS.1 = IP.1 = ~~~ ### ca-openssl.cnf: For peer and server certificate ~~~ [req] distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name x509_extensions = v3_ca # The extensions to add to the self signed cert [req_distinguished_name] [v3_ca] authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid,issuer basicConstraints = critical,CA:TRUE,pathlen:0 keyUsage = critical,digitalSignature,keyEncipherment,keyCertSign subjectKeyIdentifier = hash ~~~ ### Lets generate the Etcd CA certificate.- Create the Etcd CA certificate. ~~~ # openssl req-newkey rsa:4096-keyout ca.key-new-out ca.crt-x509-config ca-openssl.cnf-nodes-days 1825-subj /CN=etcd-signer@$(date +%s) ~~~- Verify created etcd CA. ~~~ openssl x509-in ca.crt-noout-text ~~~- Place the ca.key and ca.crt file in the following location on all the etcd nodes. Prior to this step, please take a backup of /etc/etcd/ and /etc/origin dir on all the etcd nodes. ~~~ /etc/etcd/ca.crt /etc/etcd/ca.key /etc/etcd/ca/ca.key ~~~ ### Lets generate the peer and server certificate.- Create peer and server keys: ~~~ # openssl genrsa-out peer.key 2048 # openssl genrsa-out server.key 2048 ~~~- Generate CSR. Create {peer, server}.csr ~~~ # openssl req-new-key peer.key-out peer.csr-config etcd-server-peer-openssl.cnf-subj /CN= # openssl req-new-key server.key-out server.csr-config etcd-server-peer-openssl.cnf-subj /CN= ~~~- Create {peer, server}.crt file. ~~~ # openssl x509-req-in server.csr-CA /etc/etcd/ca.crt-CAkey /etc/etcd/ca/ca.key-CAcreateserial-out server.crt-days 1825-sha256-extensions etcd_v3_ca_server-extfile etcd-server-peer-openssl.cnf # openssl x509-req-in peer.csr-CA /etc/etcd/ca.crt-CAkey /etc/etcd/ca/ca.key-CAcreateserial-out peer.crt-days 1825-sha256-extensions etcd_v3_ca_server-extfile etcd-server-peer-openssl.cnf ~~~- Place the {peer,server}.key and {peer,server}.crt file in following location on all the etcd nodes. Prior to this step, please take a backup of /etc/etcd/ and /etc/origin dir on all the etcd nodes. ~~~ /etc/etcd/peer.crt /etc/etcd/peer.key /etc/etcd/server.crt /etc/etcd/server.key ~~~ ### Lets generate the master.etcd-client certificate.- Create the `master.etcd-client.crt` from `master.etcd-client.csr` using client-openssl.cnf which is present in `/etc/origin/master/`. ~~~ # openssl x509-req-in /etc/origin/master/master.etcd-client.csr-CA /etc/etcd/ca.crt-CAkey /etc/etcd/ca/ca.key-CAcreateserial-out master.etcd-client.crt-days 1825-sha256-extensions etcd_v3_ca_server-extfile client-openssl.cnf ~~~- Ensure the `master.etcd-client.crt` and `master.etcd-client.key` files are in the `/etc/origin/master/` folder; also ensure a copy of the new etcd CA is in the `/etc/origin/master/` folder and is named `master.etcd-ca.crt`.- Restart api, controllers, and etcd.

title: The '.evictionPressureTransitionPeriod' setting in 'KubeletConfig' is not applying '0s' for container garbage collection in RHOCP 4
issue: Unable to configure kubeletconfigs for container GC(Garbage Collection) with a `.evictionPressureTransitionPeriod` value of `0s`.

The '.evictionPressureTransitionPeriod' setting is configured to '0s' as per the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-garbage-collection.html#nodes-nodes-garbage-collection-configuring_nodes-nodes-configuring), but the value on the node changes to `5m0s`, indicating that the `0s` configuration does not get applied. However, when configured to `1s`, the value is correctly applied and reflects in the node configurations as expected.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in bug [OCPBUGS-48047](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-48047). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with `Red Hat Support`.
root_cause: - The issue arises because, in Kubernetes, the `evictionPressureTransitionPeriod` setting specifies how long the kubelet should wait before initiating eviction pressure after a condition like memory or disk pressure is triggered.- On setting `evictionPressureTransitionPeriod` to `0s`, Kubernetes might interpret this as an invalid configuration since `0s` could potentially imply "no waiting time", which doesn't align with how eviction processes are supposed to work. Kubernetes, instead, likely reverts to the default value `(5m0s)` to maintain a stable operational behavior.

title: Worker `NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy`  is in progressing state for some nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: - The `nmstate-handler` pod on some nodes is stuck, blocking updates from being processed correctly.
resolution: To resolve the issue, restart the affected `nmstate-handler` pods. This will help in processing the pending updates: ~~~ $ oc delete pod nmstate-handler-xxxx-n openshift-nmstate ~~~
root_cause: The `nmstate-handler` pod is stuck and unable to process updates, causing the status in the NodeNetworkConfigurationEnactment (NNCE) and NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy (NNCP) to remain blank or unchanged. This results in a delay in status updates and prevents nodes from transitioning out of the 'Progressing' state.

title: Unable to delete specific hugepages entries from '/proc/cmdline' in RHOCP 4
issue: - Missing tuned profile prevents kernel argument changes from applying to `sysctl` settings, causing configuration mismatch.- Restarting the tuned pod does not remove hugepages kernel parameters after deleting the profile.
resolution: - From the node which is affected, run the below command which removes the `hugepages=260` kernel boot parameter from the system's boot configuration using `rpm-ostree`: ~~~ $ rpm-ostree kargs--delete="hugepages=260" ~~~- A reboot is needed because kernel boot parameters are applied during the system's boot process: ~~~ $ systemctl reboot ~~~ **NOTE:**The arguments can be verified using **"$ rpm-ostree kargs"** and a pending ostree change is identified through **"$ rpm-ostree status-vvv"**.
root_cause: - The issue arises because no tuned profile exists with the same settings or machine configuration. While a render is created based on the machine configuration, tuned generates a machine configuration only for applying or removing kernel arguments.- However, `sysctl` settings are applied through the tuned pod rather than a machine configuration. Therefore, deleting or restarting the tuned pod has no impact on these settings.

title: Newly added worker node remains `NotReady` due to missing `k8s.ovn.org/node-chassis-id` annotation and MTU  configuration in RHOCP 4
issue: - New node is in `NotReady` state due to below mentioned error: ~~~ adding or updating remote node chassis worker01.local failed, err- failed to create or update chassis to remote for remote node worker01.local, error: failed to parse node chassis-id for node- worker01.local, error: suppressed error logged: k8s.ovn.org/node-chassis-id annotation not found for node worker01.local, error parsing annotation for node worker01.local: could not find "k8s.ovn.org/node-subnets" annotation] ~~~
resolution: - First, manually configure the MTU for the connection on the node: ~~~ $ nmcli con mod ethernet.mtu ~~~- Bounce the interface: ~~~ $ nmcli con down; nmcli con up ~~~- Restart the crio service on the node to redeploy pods with the new MTU: ~~~ $ systemctl restart crio ~~~- After rebooting the node, cluster becomes normal: ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master01.local Ready control-plane,master 2y53d v1.27.14+7852426 master02.local Ready control-plane,master 611d v1.27.14+7852426 master03.local Ready control-plane,master 611d v1.27.14+7852426 worker01.local Ready worker 45h v1.27.14+7852426 ~~~
root_cause: The root cause of the `NodeNotReady `status is due to the mismatch between the `MTU` of the newly added worker node and the MTU of the existing cluster, and is verified by the logs in the `ovnkube-controller` container.

title: How to add clusters to ArgoCD using Openshift-GitOps - RHOCP4
issue: - How to add clusters to ArgoCD using Openshift-GitOps- Getting error while creating cluster secret: ~~~ error msg="could not unmarshal cluster secret " ~~~- Getting `Permission Denied` Error while creating applications after adding the cluster.
resolution: A sample scenario: **Cluster 1**- Openshift-gitops installed here. **Cluster 2**- External Cluster that needs to be added to argocd deployed in cluster 1. 1. Login to Cluster 2(External Cluster) as a cluster admin user:- Create a new project: ~~~ $ oc new-project ~~~- Create a Service Account: ~~~ $ oc create sa ~~~- Provide cluster-admin privilege to the new service account: [*] ~~~ $ oc create clusterrolebinding--clusterrole=cluster-admin--serviceaccount= ~~~- Generate a token for that Service account ~~~ $ oc create token--duration=$((*24))h--> Save the token ~~~ *`Note`: Starting from 4.11 onwards, there are some changes in SA token generation, please refer [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7025261) for creating long lived tokens.* 2. Login to cluster 1 where openshift-gitops is installed and create a secret with above contents(indentations should be correct) Sample secret yaml--> vi cluster2-secret.yaml ~~~ apiVersion: v1 stringData: <----- config: | {"bearerToken": " ", "tlsClientConfig": {"insecure": true}} name:---> Name of cluster server: https://api.:6443---> API URL of cluster 2 kind: Secret metadata: labels: argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster name:---> Secret name namespace: openshift-gitops type: Opaque ~~~- *`Note`: Refer [Upstream Doc](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/declarative-setup/#clusters) for cluster secret samples.* 3. Apply the secret ~~~ $ oc apply-f.yaml ~~~ 4. Login to argocd and check the cluster status:- Go to Argocd UI--> Settings--> Cluster 5. Now try to create an Application- *`Note`: Red hat's multi cluster story is meant to be handled via ACM. But this is an another supported way if customers want to add OCP clusters under GitOps without using the ACM operator.*
root_cause: 1. If getting error msg="could not unmarshal cluster secret ":- There is no need to convert the secret data to base64 in OCP clusters as like mentioned in the [Upstream Doc](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/declarative-setup/#clusters). OCP will do that automatically when the secret is applied. 2. If getting `Permission Denied` Error while creating application after adding the cluster:- Check if the newly created service account does have the `cluster-admin` privilege in external cluster [*] `Disclaimer`: **Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. title: High response times when querying Loki series having cluster-reader clusterrole and namespace access granted in RHOL
issue: As a platform developer with cluster-reader Role in OpenShift Container Platform, when querying the Loki series takes up to 23 seconds when using Loki via Explore or Grafana dashboard with Loki functionality.

As an user granted cluster-reader clusterrole and namespace access to the Loki logs, when it's queried the Loki series, the time is high. The same behaviour is not observed when querying the application logs ~~~ $ time logcli-o raw--tls-skip-verify--bearer-token="$(oc whoami-t)"--addr "https://${lokiroute}/api/logs/v1/application" series--analyze-labels--retries=2--since=6h '{log_type="application"}' [...] Total Streams: 251 Unique Labels: 10 Label Name Unique Values Found In Streams k8s_pod_name 251 251 kubernetes_pod_name 251 251 k8s_namespace_name 202 251 kubernetes_namespace_name 202 251 kubernetes_host 3 251 k8s_node_name 3 251 kubernetes_container_name 1 251 openshift_log_type 1 251 log_type 1 251 k8s_container_name 1 251 real 0m53.729s user 0m0.117s sys 0m0.031s ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [LOG-6912](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6912). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. #### Workaround As it's given cluster-reader access to the user, this has access to all the logs in the cluster using "oc logs", then, granting also cluster-wide access to be able to see all the logs resolve this. For doing it: ~~~ // Remove the rolebinding to the application logs $ oc adm policy remove-role-from-user-n // Assign cluster-wide access to the application logs $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-logging-application-view ~~~
root_cause: The root cause is being analyzed by Red Hat engineering in Bug [LOG-6912](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6912).

title: (OCP4): DNS failures after upstream nameserver GSLB feature enabled
issue: - After enabling GSLB (Global Server Load Balancing) on upstream nameservers used by OpenShift, observed multiple failures in looking up critical domain addresses and resolving queries within OpenShift.- Within Oauth container, observed the following failure in looking up the domain address of LDAP server (leading to login failures): ~~~ 2025-03-31T13:34:35.774860279Z E0331 13:34:35.774817 1 login.go:176] Error authenticating " " with provider "ldap": LDAP Result Code 200 "Network Error": dial tcp: lookup on 172.30.0.10:53: read udp:46576-> 172.30.0.10:53: i/o timeout ~~~- coredns pods in openshift-dns are indicating upwards of 6s on multiple calls upstream: ~~~ 2025-03-31T15:08:48.919642050Z [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2. AAAA: read udp:58925->:53: i/o timeout 2025-03-31T15:08:49.652017873Z [INFO] 10.129.6.50:56101- 32890 "A IN. udp 69 false 1232"-- 0 6.003739349s 2025-03-31T15:08:49.652017873Z [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2. A: read udp:46268->:53: i/o timeout 2025-03-31T15:08:49.656132090Z [INFO] 10.129.6.50:56011- 12104 "AAAA IN. udp 69 false 1232"-- 0 6.00794457s 2025-03-31T15:08:49.656157672Z [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2. AAAA: read udp:32945->:53: i/o timeout ~~~
resolution: - It was observed that the GSLB configuration was not set properly on the upstream nameservers, and as a result, DNS server was not replying properly to queries performed by DIG (but was responding properly to CURL and NSLOOKUP), because the libraries used were different:- It is important to ensure that both `gslb` AND `guardian option: blast` services are enabled to ensure caching features work as expected, which should resolve the transport error.- In the particular case where this issue was observed, `GSLB` was enabled, but `BLAST` was set to `0` (disabled) and lead to a traffic flow handling discrepancy.
root_cause: - In this particular circumstance, the DNS resolution issue was due to the specific configuration: dnsblast/gslb engine started Guardian option blast=0- After setting both options below, the DNS server replied correctly to the DNS queries perform via dig command: blast=1 gslb=1 When `blast=0` There is an issue with how nameservers can respond to queries made by the following DIG versions which may impact specific versions of OpenShift using these builds: ~~~ 1. dig version 9.18 = DNS answer failure (used by client auth within oauth containers on 4.16 for domain resolution). 2. dig version 9.16 = DNS answer OK 3. nslookup = DNS answer OK 4. curl = DNS answer OK ~~~

title: Enabling xt_u32 in Openshift Container Platform 4
issue: Module xt_u32 is not available out of the box on rhcos nodes and can't be used in a pod definition such as the following one: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: centos-pod labels: name: centos-pod spec: containers:- name: centos-pod command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"] args: ["yum install-y iptables && sleep inf"] image: centos:latest securityContext: capabilities: add: ["NET_ADMIN"] ~~~
resolution: Create the following machineconfig so that xt_u32 module is not blacklisted and enabled at boot time, adapting the label to match the target nodes and wait for it to be applied: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: load-xt-u32-module spec: config: ignition: version: 2.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,xt_u32 filesystem: root mode: 420 path: /etc/modules-load.d/xt-u32-load.conf ~~~ After that, launching the pod sample above will work as expected, which can be confirmed with a sample iptables rule run within it such as the following one: ~~~ iptables-t filter-A INPUT-i eth0-m u32--u32 '6 & 0xFF = 1 && 4 & 0x3FFF = 0 && 0 > > 22 & 0x3C @ 0 > > 24 = 8'-j DROP ~~~
root_cause: xt_u32 is an iptables filtering kernel module. The module was removed from RHEL8 and brought back to life because important CNFs might relay upon it.
