An unauthenticated attacker could remotely crash the slapd process by sending a specially crafted request, causing a Denial of Service.", "Metadata": null, "Severity": "Unknown"}]}]}}} ~~~

title: Editing Image Content Source Policy (ICSP) mid-upgrade in a Disconnected OpenShift cluster
issue: During an OpenShift Container Platform upgrade, it was found out that the mirror image registry URL specified in the Image Content Source Policy (ICSP) was recently changed, but the updated settings had **not*
yet been deployed onto the nodes prior to initiating upgrade. This would cause the nodes to search for the OCP images at an incorrect mirror registry URL causing the upgrade to be stuck.
resolution: Since this issue specifically targets a change in URL for the mirror registry **mid-upgrade** in a disconnected cluster, it is vital to let the upgrade progress to complete, since the upgrade will try and pull newer version images. #### WORKAROUND As in this scenario, the upgrade has progressed, the nodes have to be able to pull newer version images. This can be achieved by editing the entries in `/etc/containers/registries.conf` manually on nodes and restarting `crio` service. IMPORTANT- this will NOT restart the node itself. ``` oc debug node/ chroot /host vi /etc/containers/registries.conf [edit- correct the mirror registry hostname/port and save changes] systemctl restart crio systemctl status crio ``` This will only propel the upgrade to the final stage (machine-config) and won't rollout RHCOS due to the "on-disk validation mismatch". The upgrade should continue, but during the upgrade of final stage (machine-config CO) `oc get co` will show: ``` machine-config: Unable to apply 4.12.60: error during syncRequireMachineConfigPools: [timed out waiting for condition, error pool master is not ready, retrying. status: (pool degraded: true total: 3, ready 0, updated: 0 unavailable 2)] ``` At this stage, revert back the changes made in the nodes ``` oc debug node/ chroot /host vi /etc/containers/registries.conf [edit- revert to original config and save changes] systemctl restart crio systemctl status crio ``` This should allow the upgrade to complete.
root_cause: An offline OpenShift cluster is experiencing an upgrade failure due to a changed mirror registry specification in the Image Content Source Policy (ICSP) for the registry. This KCS tackles the scenario when the upgrade has already started *before* the right mirror registry settings were specified, and aims to complete the upgrade so the nodes can pull new images for the upgrade to complete.

title: Nginx receive http2 directive is deprecated warning.
issue: - Nginx 'Listen … http2 directive is deprecated' Warnings received on restart.--- [warn] 1#1: the "user" directive makes sense only if the master process runs with super-user privileges, ignored in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:4- The old format found in the nginx.conf and which is depreciated. nginx: [warn] the "user" directive makes sense only if the master process runs with super-user privileges, ignored in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:4 [warn] 1#1: the "listen... http2" directive is deprecated, use the "http2" directive instead in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:37---
resolution: - Add the new format in the nginx.conf for http2 directive.--- server {listen 00.00.0.0:443 ssl; http2 on;---- This issue reported as a [bug](https://github.com/hestiacp/hestiacp/issues/3684)
root_cause: - The old format found in the nginx.conf and which is depreciated.--- server {listen 00.00.0.0:443 ssl http2;---

title: ArgoCD JWT stays valid after logging out
issue: - After logging out of ArgoCD, the JWT provided stays valid.- ArgoCD JWT can still be used for APIs after logout.
resolution: - The JWT is provided by the Dex Identity Server deployed with the Red Hat OpenShift GitOps Operator and there is no supported configuration to invalidate such token at logout.
root_cause: - Tipically, JWT are reusable and are only invalidated at expiration.- If an explicit revocation is needed, it is to be handled by the SSO provider (in this case the Dex Identity Server), as stated by the ArgoCD [upstream documentation](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/operator-manual/security/#authentication). title: The plugins download fails while building custom Jenkins image through S2I in RHOCP
issue: - The plugin download fails while creating a [customized Jenkins image through S2I](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/jenkins/images-other-jenkins#images-other-jenkins-customize-s2i_images-other-jenkins).- The builder pod's logs shows the build failure while downloading the plugin/s. ~~~ Failed to download plugin: antisamy-markup-formatter or antisamy-markup-formatter-plugin Failed to install plugins. error: build error: building at STEP "RUN /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble": while running runtime: exit status 1 ~~~- While trying to manually download the Jenkins plugin using curl, the request fails with error *`SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL`*. ~~~ # curl-O-L-v https://updates.jenkins.io/download/plugins/antisamy-markup-formatter/159.v25b_c67cd35fb_/antisamy-markup-formatter.hpi... curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to mirror.bom.albony.in:443 ~~~
resolution: - The official [Jenkins mirrors status page](https://get.jenkins.io/index.html?mirrorstats) has the list of the mirror hosts available for Jenkins downloads.- Whitelist the mirrors in the Web Proxy / Firewall and thereafter try to trigger the build.
root_cause: - When Jenkins download a plugin the request gets redirected to the nearest mirror, hence any network devices like Web Proxy / Firewall which intercepts all the traffic between the source and the destination (updates.jenkins.io), it is likely that the plugin's mirror url is not allowed/whitelisted for connection.- An article on the community Jenkins forum explains such cases of [plugin installation failures](https://community.jenkins.io/t/failed-to-install-plugins-in-jenkins/12412/3).

title: Cannot validate certificate because it doesn't contain any IP SANs
issue: - The following error message is shown in differents components when accessing to a service/host secured by a certificated, including OpenShift installation and components: ~~~ cannot validate certificate for [IP] because it doesn't contain any IP SANs ~~~
resolution: Change the IP with the `hostname` for accessing the service/host, or create a new certificate including the IP as Subject Alternative Name (SAN).
root_cause: An IP is configured for accessing to a service/host, but the certificate provided doesn't contain the IP as Subject Alternative Name (SAN).

title: Guaranteed pod fails to run with error `cpuset.cpus`: Device or resource busy
issue: - Guaranteed pod fails to run on cgroupv1 with crun as container runtime ~~~ Warning Failed 2s (x4 over 26s) kubelet Error: container create failed: write file `cpuset.cpus`: Device or resource busy ~~~
resolution: - Issue has been resolved in OpenShift version 4.18.6.- A fix was proposed through [PR #1693 in the crun repository](https://github.com/containers/crun/pull/1693)- The issue was tracked under [OCPBUGS-52357](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-52357)
root_cause: - The root cause of this issue is a known bug in the affected OpenShift version, where the system fails to properly enforce cgroup configurations due to inconsistencies in the cgroup hierarchy management.

title: Upgrading to OpenShift GitOps 1.16: Pod 'openshift-gitops-redis-ha-server-1' failing to start with SCC violation
issue: Pod 'openshift-gitops-application-controller' is experiencing frequent restarts due to Out of Memory (OOM) errors
Pod 'openshift-gitops-redis-ha-server-#' failing to start due to security context constraint (SCC) errors
resolution: Delete the `redis-ha-server` StatefulSet, triggering a rollout of a new StatefulSet.
root_cause: This is a known issue ([GITOPS-6670](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-6670)) in OpenShift GitOps 1.16.0 that causes the `redis-ha-server` StatefulSet to set the container's user to UID and GID 1000. This would violate the SecurityContextConstraints assigned to controller, `restricted-v2`, which prevents the Pods from being created. Deleting the controller causes it to be recreated without the static UID/GID assignment. This known issue is included in the release notes for [OpenShift GitOps 1.16.0](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_gitops/1.16/html/release_notes/gitops-release-notes#known-issues-1-16-0_gitops-release-notes).

title: Persistentvolumeclaims is forbidden: exceeded quota
issue: - Unable to create Persistent Volume- Upon attempting to create a PVC, I receive this error: ~~~ persistentvolumeclaims "example" is forbidden: exceeded quota: my-volume-quota, requested: requests.storage=50Gi, used: requests.storage=66660Mi, limited: requests.storage=100Gi ~~~
resolution: There are two possible solutions:- Deleting existing volume claims should allow more space in the quota- Expanding the quota would allow new PVC creation NOTE:- A PVC in any state (Bound, Pending, Terminating, etc.) will consume quota in a particular namespace.- If you are unable to delete a PVC, it may be stuck in a terminating state due to a pvc-protection finalizer in place. For resolving this situation, please refer to this KCS: [Unable to delete PVCs with finalizer "kubernetes.io/pvc-protection"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4670181). Following this and forcing PVC may lead to a volume remaining on the backend storage system. After clearing the finalizer and deleting the PVC in OpenShift, check that the backend storage volume is deleted properly.
root_cause: - The total persistent volume space would exceed the quota in place in the cluster

How to build and deploy a custom devfile registry?

title: Kube-apiserver high CPU/Memory consumption unexpectedly causing API calls to fail with "etcdserver: request timed out" on Openshift 4
issue: - Kube-apiserver pods consuming unusual high CPU/Memory resources.- Cluster functionality and performance is degraded.- Cluster operators are flapping to a degraded state.
resolution: This solution covers only the scenario of OpenShift GitOps controller pod making an excessive usage of the cluster API. The workaround in this case is to restart the Gitops controller pod by deleting it, and will require to review the GitOps configuration to check if the current configuration is the cause of the high impact in the `kube-apiserver`: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-gitops | grep controller-0 openshift-gitops-application-controller-0 1/1 Running 0 $ oc delete pod [openshift-gitops-application-controller-pod_name]-n openshift-gitops ~~~ For `kube-apiserver` high CPU/Memory usage when not using OpenShift GitOps, please refer to [the kube-apiserver pods are consuming high memory and CPU in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6983882).
root_cause: The OpenShift GitOps controller pod is making an excessive usage of the cluster API impacting in a great way cluster stability and etcd performance. This is because depending the use it might cause a storm of API requests to the `kube-apiserver` pods that the pods and etcd might not be able to manage in a timely manner. This will result to API to degrade and affect all cluster functionalities based on the API level.

title: Nodes entered into NotReady state after enabling feature sets in RHOCP 4.
issue: - Nodes are in NotReady state.- Some OVN pods are in CrashLoopBackOff state.
resolution: The Cluster Version Operator (CVO) is responsible for installing the necessary CRDs when the TechPreviewNoUpgrade feature set is enabled—either on an existing cluster or during cluster creation. Make sure the CVO is enabled and running healthy. ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion ~~~
root_cause: According to the documentation, enabling_featureSet: TechPreviewNoUpgrade_ activates a set of APIs, including the_dnsNameResolver_ API. However, since the_FeatureGate_ CR is unable to enable the_dnsNameResolver_ API, the OVN pods are entering a CrashLoopBackOff state, which is subsequently causing the nodes to be in a_NotReady_ state.

title: When WriteRequestBodies is enabled for apiserver, what verbs does the audit log entry show for  users  added and removed from a group?
issue: - With__WriteRequestBodies__ enabled for apiserver, audit logs captured for `$ oc adm groups add-users` come up with `"verb": "update"` but audit logs for `$ oc adm groups remove-users` doesn't come up with `"verb": "delete"` entry.- What verbs does the audit log entry show for users added and removed from a group when the apiserver is configured with__WriteRequestBodies__ or__AllRequestBodies__?
resolution: Both adding users to a group as well as deleting an existing user from a group are recorded as `"verb": "update"` event in audit logs.

Requirement is to identify namespaces without manually checking each one.

Search for the user and view the rolebindings. ~~~ Note the namespace associated with each rolebinding. **Using the CLI:** Use the following command to list rolebindings across all namespaces, filtering for a specific user: ~~~ oc get rolebindings-A-o wide | grep ~~~

title: How to prevent a machine config update during an MCP (MachineConfigPool) rollout?
issue: - User applies an incorrect machine configuration however, wants to revert the incorrect changes immediately.
resolution: If not already done, quickly pause the mcp rollout so as to stop the progression of the newly detected changes to more nodes. 1. Pause the MCP as mentioned in our document [Pause MachineConfigPool using oc](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/updating_clusters/performing-a-cluster-update#updating-control-plane-only-update-cli_control-plane-only-update). ~~~ $ oc patch mcp--type='merge'-p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}' ~~~ By setting "paused" to 'true' in the MCP’s spec will pause the ongoing rollout and prevent further updates from being applied. Note: "mcp mcp-name" specifies the MachineConfigPool you want to modify. Replace with the actual name of your MCP (for example, master or worker). Rollback the applied changes to the MachineConfig, for example in case of an image registry, you will need to do the following: 2. Edit the image config and remove the incorrect lines. ~~~ oc edit image.config.openshift.io cluster registrySources: insecureRegistries:- repository1- repository2 ~~~ The Machine Config Operator (MCO) watches for changes to the image.config.openshift.io/cluster custom resource (CR) related to registries. When changes are detected, the MCO triggers the creation and application of new machine configurations across all the nodes. 3. title: Continuous ETCD Growth in RHOCP 4.16

title: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Additional outbound URLs to allow at firewall and proxy level.
issue: - What URLs require access for a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster?- Which URLs must be permitted through the OCP HTTP proxy?- Are there additional domain considerations or subdomains necessary for access to Red Hat or third-party services (e.g., registries, specific pull images)?
resolution: For Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4, refer to [Configuring your firewall](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/installing/install_config/configuring-firewall.html) section in addition to this article. Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform depends on several registries, including the Red Hat registry, which provides the basic pod images, registry image and router image. Below is the list of the recommended URLs to be allowed on firewall or proxy: Registries: ~~~- registry.access.redhat.com (provides pod, registry, router, s2i, jboss and etc images)- registry.redhat.io- registry.connect.redhat.com (provides third-party images)- quay.io- *.quay.io- storage.googleapis.com/openshift-release- sso.redhat.com- docker.io (images not in Red Hat's registry)- docker.com- hub.docker.com- index.docker.io ~~~ > **Note:** It is possible to use `cdn.quay.io` and `cdn0[1-6].quay.io` instead of `*.quay.io`. Depending on the firewall it could be needed to add the following ones to be able to download image blobs: ~~~- oso-rhc4tp-docker-registry.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com (CNAME)- s3-us-west-2-r-w.amazonaws.com- s3-us-east-1-r-w.amazonaws.com- *.us-east-1.amazonaws.com- *.akamaiedge.net- *.akamaitechnologies.com- *.cloudflare.net ~~~ The outbound depends also on the languages and frameworks used for the applications deployed in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. Source code repositories (allow the ones that apply): ~~~- github.com- gitlab.com- Internal git repository hostnames ~~~ Language/framework related resources (allow the ones that apply): ~~~ *.maven.org *.apache.org *.npmjs.com *.openshift.io *.openshift.org *.docker.io *.docker.org *.rubygems.org *.cpan.org *.githubusercontent.com *.githubapp.com *.cloudfront.net *.fabric8.io *.codehaus.org *.sonatype.org *.jboss.org *.jenkins-ci.org *.jenkins.io *.bintray.com *.spring.io *.eclipse.org *.fusesource.com *.eclipse.org *.quay.io ~~~ For OpenShift 3, when registering RHEL hosts with subscription manager, it needs to access the subscription url [1] and has to have access the Red Hat repos `atomic-openshift-*` and `docker-*`. OpenShift could be installed without connection to internet, but pod, registry and router images must be available in custom registry or available on hosts. [1] [How to access Red Hat Subscription Manager (RHSM) through a firewall or proxy](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/65300) [2] [Public CIDR Lists for Red Hat (IP Addresses for cdn.redhat.com)](https://access.redhat.com/articles/1525183)
root_cause: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform depends on the Red Hat registry, which provides the basic pod images, registry image and router image. The outbound depends also on the languages and frameworks used for the applications deployed in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform.

title: Pods in ContainerCreating with FailedMount events using Dell Unity CSI driver in OpenShift 4
issue: - Pods are not able to start due to Volume failing mount, and the following events are shown for the pod: ~~~ Warning FailedMount 35m kubelet MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "csiunity-xxxxxxxxxx": kubernetes.io/csi: attacher.MountDevice failed to create newCsiDriverClient: driver name csi-unity.dellemc.com not found in the list of registered CSI drivers Warning FailedMount 35m kubelet MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "csiunity-xxxxxxxxxx": rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc = runid=1111 Unable to login to Unity. Error: rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = Authentication failed. Unable to login to Unity. Verify username and password. ~~~
resolution: The Dell EMC Unity CSI driver is not provided by Red Hat, and not supported by Red Hat Support as explained in the "Root Cause" section. If the error shown by the events shows "`Authentication failed. Unable to login to Unity. Verify username and password`", it usually means that the credentials in the `unity-creds` `secret`, usually in the `unity` namespace, are missing or wrong. For additional information or other issues with the Dell EMC Unity CSI driver, please contact the driver vendor support.
root_cause: The Dell EMC Unity CSI driver is not listed in the [CSI drivers supported by OpenShift Container Platform](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/storage/using-container-storage-interface-csi#csi-driver-daemonset_persistent-storage-csi), so it is not provided by Red Hat, and not supported by Red Hat Support. As explained in [overview of CSI volume snapshots](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/storage/using-container-storage-interface-csi#persistent-storage-csi-snapshots): > *OpenShift Container Platform only ships with select CSI drivers. For CSI drivers that are not provided by an OpenShift Container Platform Driver Operator, it is recommended to use the CSI drivers provided by [community or storage vendors](https://kubernetes-csi.github.io/docs/drivers.html). Follow the installation instructions furnished **by the CSI driver provider**.*

title: Is It possible to access a pod in NotReady state via service, route, or dns in RHOCP4
issue: - Cannot access a pod via Service, Route, or Headless Service DNS when the pod is in a NotReady state in RHOCP.
resolution: - When a `pod` fails its readiness check, it is marked as `NotReady` in RHOCP. This means the `pod` is still running, but it's not ready to handle any traffic. As a result, the pod is removed from the list of active `endpoints` for `services`, and it becomes inaccessible through `routes, ingress controllers, or services`.- The `readiness probe` is used to decide if a pod is ready to serve requests. Until the probe passes again, the pod won’t receive any traffic—even though it's technically still running.- In the case of a `headless service`, the behavior is slightly different. While headless services can show the IPs of all pods, they exclude NotReady pods from DNS lookups. So, if a pod is NotReady, its IP won’t appear in the DNS records, and clients using DNS won't be able to connect to it.
root_cause: The `readinessProbe` in a pod spec defines whether the pod is ready to serve requests. If the probe fails, the pod is unavailable for traffic routing purposes, effectively isolating it from `services`, `routes`, and `DNS` resolution via `headless services` until the probe passes again: $ oc describe pod Readiness: exec [cat /tmp/healthy] delay=5s timeout=1s period=10s #success=1 #failure=3 Conditions: Type Status Initialized True Ready False ContainersReady False PodScheduled True Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal Scheduled default-scheduler Successfully assigned test-probes/readiness-demo to worker-node Normal Pulled kubelet Container image "registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi" already present on machine Normal Created kubelet Created container web Normal Started kubelet Started container web Warning Unhealthy kubelet Readiness probe failed: cat: /tmp/healthy: No such file or directory

Set `label` and `taint` in nodes. ~~~ $ oc label node NAMENODE1 NAMENODE2 ansible_job=executejob $ oc adm taint nodes NAMENODE1 NAMENODE2 executejob=AutomationController:NoSchedule ~~~ 2. Access the `Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform` > `Automation Controller` > `Infrastructure` > `Instace Groups` > `default` > Click on `Edit Container Group` > Check box: `Customize pod spec`. An example `Customize pod spec` configuration below: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: namespace: aap labels: ansible_job: '' spec: nodeSelector: ansible_job: executejob serviceAccountName: default automountServiceAccountToken: false tolerations:- key: executejob value: AutomationController effect: NoSchedule operator: Equal affinity: podAntiAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:- weight: 100 podAffinityTerm: labelSelector: matchExpressions:- key: executejob operator: Exists topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname containers:- image: >- registry.redhat.io/ansible-automation-platform-25/ee-supported-rhel8@sha256:cf8ca1db577399b78778e222439d6d14bbebd5dd0e475a976c1db8dcabacbe94 name: worker args:- ansible-runner- worker- '--private-data-dir=/runner' resources: requests: cpu: 250m memory: 100Mi ~~~

issue: ICE driver could cause a deadlock when requiring the rtnl_mutex and taking the lock rtnl_lock producing errors like: ~~~ PID: 23803 TASK: ff30511065bd8000 CPU: 1 COMMAND: "kworker/1:52" #0 [ff765c67e9b9bd40]__schedule at ffffffff84b2ca2b #1 [ff765c67e9b9bda8] schedule_rtmutex at ffffffff8413c750 #2 [ff765c67e9b9bdb8] rt_mutex_slowlock_block.constprop.0 at ffffffff84b30723 #3 [ff765c67e9b9bdf0] rt_mutex_slowlock.constprop.0 at ffffffff84b31a76 #4 [ff765c67e9b9be88] linkwatch_event at ffffffff848f469a #5 [ff765c67e9b9be90] process_one_work at ffffffff8411be92 #6 [ff765c67e9b9bed8] worker_thread at ffffffff8411c110 #7 [ff765c67e9b9bf18] kthread at ffffffff84123d73 #8 [ff765c67e9b9bf50] ret_from_fork at ffffffff84002e0f ~~~
resolution: Update the system to a recent version: * OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 * Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.3 The fix for this deadlock required rebasing the 9.3.z ice driver closer to upstream. As such, it's not feasible to bring the patch into RHEL 8 based kernels, or 9.0 through 9.2.z kernels. As a result, it's recommended to use RHEL 9.3 or higher to avoid the issue, or upgrade OCP to 4.16 or higher.
root_cause: The deadlock can occur in the ice driver when using systems with the RHEL 8.x.z kernel, or the 9.2.z kernel or earlier.

title: NetApp ONTAP cinder-based block storage driver : Key Features and Known Limitations in RHOSP/RHOSO
issue: NetApp ONTAP Cinder driver is unable to extend an attached volume for NFS protocol
resolution: **Compatibility of NetApp ONTAP Cinder Driver On Red Hat Openstack Platform (RHOSP/RHOSO)**- NetApp ONTAP Cinder Driver has been tested and validated on RHOSP/RHOSO.- It is a storage solution from NetApp that supports most Cinder functions, such as volume and snapshot creation, deletion, etc.- It supports both iSCSI and NFS protocols.- It also supports backup, consistency groups, and multi-attach volume creation, update, and deletion. However, there is one limitation for the NFS protocol: **extending an attached volume**. Customers will not be able to extend a volume attached to an instance. Instead, they will need to detach the volume, extend it, and then reattach it. **Note:** The limitation regarding the extension of attached volumes is being addressed [upstream](https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/cinder/+/820578). It is expected to be included in a future version of its plugin for newer RHOSP versions and can be back-ported. **Supportability**- Support for the NetApp ONTAP cinder driver will be provided by NetApp, specified by Red Hat's support policy for third-party software.- For details on policy, refer to the article [How does Red Hat Global Support Services handle third-party software, drivers, and/or uncertified hardware/hypervisors](https://access.redhat.com/site/articles/1067)

title: How do I map a RHEL CVE fix to RHCOS and RHOCP?
product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux for x86_64
issue: - What is the process of mapping a RHEL CVE to the respective RHCOS / RHOCP version?- I see a CVE for a package in RHEL. How do I know if it is fixed in RHCOS/RHOCP?
resolution: A CVE page of a RHEL package may not list Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) as impacted. However, RHOCP may still be impacted indirectly by the CVE, if the impacted package is used by `RHCOS` or `RHOCP`. Follow the process below to identify where is the fix in the `RHEL` package and then which `RHCOS`/`RHOCP` version contains the fixed package. **1. Get the fixed RPM version**- Consider [CVE: 2022-0778](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-0778). In this CVE, a flaw has been found in the **openssl** package.- The `openssl` package is a part of **RHEL** and only an indirect part of `RHOCP`. Hence in the affected products we may `NOT see RHOCP` listed.- However, since RHOCP is based on `RHCOS` which is based on RHEL, indirectly, RHOCP too is affected by this vulnerability.- In such cases, the fix is always shipped via `RHEL security advisories` and not `RHOCP advisories`.- Take an example of OCP 4.8 for this CVE. How can we know which version of OCP 4.8 will have the fixed `openssl` package?- First of all, map the specific version of RHEL with the version of RHCOS / RHOCP in picture (in this case 4.8) using the knowledge base [#6907891](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6907891).- From the above knowledge base article, it is clear that RHOCP 4.8 is based on RHEL 8.4. Now, let's see what is the version of the fixed rpm in RHEL 8.4.- Checking again the [openssl CVE page](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2022-0778), the errata for RHEL 8.4 is shipped via: [RHSA-2022:1071](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:1071) and the fixed `openssl` package is: `openssl-1.1.1g-16.el8_4.x86_64`. **2. What is the RHOCP minor version that contains the fixed package** This section is based on the commands in KCS [Obtaining package list for RHEL CoreOS or specific image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5787001). We will take the commands to find out which RHCOS image in RHOCP 4.8 contains the fixed `openssl` package.- As RHOCP cluster admin, check current RHOCP cluster version by running command: ~~~ # oc version | grep-i server Server Version: 4.8.35 ~~~- This means that this is OpenShift 4.8 stream and **4.8.35** release.- Obtain the image sha256 digest for the `machine-os-content` container image where are stored details about corresponding RHCOS release: ~~~ # oc adm release info 4.8.35 | grep machine-os-content machine-os-content sha256:8e3f03baa3a1f15cf2f1e45d75c0f124f05ce2e1f1fc2a90535b888bf7bf1412** ~~~- As RHOCP cluster admin, use cluster pull secret to check bundled RPM packages in OpenShift RHCOS cluster nodes by running following command.- Either SSH or debug any of the RHOCP node and check the installed `openssl` RPM package in the corresponding to OCP 4.8.35 RHCOS release based on the obtained in the above step sha digest. ~~~ # podman run--rm--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json-it--entrypoint /bin/cat quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:8e3f03baa3a1f15cf2f1e45d75c0f124f05ce2e1f1fc2a90535b888bf7bf1412 /pkglist.txt | grep openssl ~~~- In the output there will be a list of RPM packages related to openssl in the OCP 4.8.35 RHCOS. On that list there will be: **`openssl-1:1.1.1g-15.el8_3.x86_64`**.- You may compare this version to the checked RHEL patched version (from earlier steps) and confirm if the installed openssl package is vulnerable or not. In this example in OpenShift 4.8.35 there is still a vulnerable openssl package (`openssl-1:1.1.1g-15.el8_3.x86_64` when the patched version is `openssl-1.1.1g-16.el8_4.x86_64`).- To check the newer OpenShift releases for 4.8 stream and find version with the fixed `openssl` package, you may repeat the above steps and verify other OpenShift release, like **4.8.36**: ~~~ # oc adm release info 4.8.36 | grep machine-os-content # podman run--rm--authfile.dockerconfigjson-it--entrypoint /bin/cat quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:a768dca45d8eabd3495d8454c231a4e167cb1bf1372b7c387718efef781f814e /pkglist.txt | grep openssl ~~~- In the output if you see **`openssl-1.1.1g-16.el8_4.x86_64`**, this means that RHCOS used in OpenShift 4.8.36 already contains a patched version of the openssl package. However, it is possible that this version of OpenShift would not contain the fixed package, and it will be required to repeat the process to check additional later versions.- Above method will provide a complete list of packages. One single package can also be checked using: ~~~ # rpm-qa | grep-i # rpm-qa | grep-i openssl ~~~- For a list of all OpenShift releases and information, you might want to check the OpenShift documentation, in the Release Notes section, like for OpenShift 4.8 stream it would be: [RHBA-2022:0872- OpenShift Container Platform 4.8.35 bug fix and security update](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/release_notes/ocp-4-8-release-notes.html#ocp-4-8-35).

title: S2I Build failing with error: /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble: No such file or directory
issue: - S2I Build failing with error: STEP 7: RUN /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble /bin/sh: /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble: No such file or directory"
resolution: ### Workaround Use path `/usr/local/s2i` instead of `/usr/libexec/s2i/assemble`
root_cause: - With OpenJDK17+, on RHEL8, 9, and 10 images s2i scripts are in a path `/usr/local/s2i` which differs from s2i standard path `/usr/libexec/s2i/assemble`.- It's a known issue and it is being tracked on Jira tickets [RHEL 9](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OPENJDK-2805 "RHEL 9"),

title: Keepalived pods crashes and fail to start on worker node (Ingress VIP)
issue: - `Keepalived` pods crash and fail to start on the worker node having `Ingress VIP`. The expectation is that the `keepalived` pod, labeled by `app=kni-infra-vrrp` should start. This affects everyone using Red Hat OpenShift v4.13 together with `Ingress VIP` and a potential bug in the `nodeip-configuration service` in Red Hat OpenShift v4.13.
resolution: - For the fix, the `nodeip-configuration service` template needs to be extended to consider the `Ingress VIPs` as well and the development team is working on the fix.- The issue was identified as a bug in Red Hat OpenShift v4.13 and was being tracked by the Red Hat Engineering team under OCPBUGS-18771. The root cause has been determined, and the fix is included in v4.13.22 ([RHSA-2023:6846](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:6846)) for OpenShift 4.13 ([OCPBUGS-22205](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-22205)) and from v4.14.0 ([RHSA-2023:5006](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:5006)) onwards for OpenShift 4.14 ([OCPBUGS-20025](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-20025)).
root_cause: - There are 2 problems in Red Hat OpenShift v4.13 currently:- The `regexp` expression will not match and the `chroot` command will fail because of missing `ldd libraries` inside the container. This has been fixed on Red Hat OpenShift v4.14, but not on Red Hat OpenShift v4.13.- The `nodeip-configuration service` creates the `/run/nodeip-configuration/remote-worker` file based on `onPremPlatformAPIServerInternalIPs(apiVIP)` and ignores the `onPremPlatformIngressIPs (ingressVIP)` as can be seen in the [source code](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/release-4.13/templates/common/on-prem/units/nodeip-configuration.service.yaml#L38). ~~~ node-ip \ set \--platform {{.Infra.Status.PlatformStatus.Type}} \ {{if not (isOpenShiftManagedDefaultLB.)-}}--user-managed-lb \ {{end-}} {{if or (eq.IPFamilies "IPv6") (eq.IPFamilies "DualStackIPv6Primary")-}}--prefer-ipv6 \ {{end-}}--retry-on-failure \ {{range onPremPlatformAPIServerInternalIPs.}}{{.}} {{end}}; \ do \ sleep 5; \ done" ~~~- The `keepalived` process will not start because the `remote-worker` file exists and consequently the liveness probes will fail because the `keepalived` process does not exist.

title: "No Alert Found" issue after clicking 'View Details' in RHOCP Web Console
issue: - `No Alert Found` issue after clicking `View Details` in RHOCP4 Web Console.- A similar issue in `Openshift Container Platform` version 4.14 is described in [KCS: 7108017](https://access.redhat.com/node/7108017).
resolution: This issue was reported to Red Hat Engineering and it can be tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-51117](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-51117) and delivered a fix in RHOCP 4.17.23 through errata [RHSA-2025:3297](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:3297). If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. **Workaround:** Clicking on "View Details" for an alert in `Status` will redirect to the link like below: ~~~ https://console-openshift-console.apps.xxxxxx.xxxx.xxx.xx.redhat.com/monitoring/alerts/xxxx?namespace=openshift-operators-redhat&prometheus=openshift-monitoring%2Fk8s&severity=warning&alertname=ElasticsearchOperatorRemovalWarning&version=5.8.17 ~~~ Removing parameter **"prometheus=openshift-monitoring%2Fk8s&"** from the above URL will redirect to the correct alert: ~~~ https://console-openshift-console.apps.xxxxxx.xxxx.xxx.xx.redhat.com/monitoring/alerts/xxxx?namespace=openshift-operators-redhat&severity=warning&alertname=ElasticsearchOperatorRemovalWarning&version=5.8.17 ~~~
root_cause: A code migration operation failed to process external labels correctly on the *Alert detail* page on the *Administrator perspective* of the web console. These external labels are required to prevent silenced alert notifications from getting added to notification bell icon. Because the *Alert detail* page did not handle external labels correctly, the notification bell provided links to these *Alert detail* pages that generated a `no matching alerts found` message when you clicked on a link.

title: Is xfs filesystem supported when using "volumeMode: Filesystem" for RBD storage class ?
issue: Is xfs filesystem supported when using "volumeMode: Filesystem" for RBD storage class?
resolution: * Currently xfs filesystem is NOT supported when using "volumeMode: Filesystem" for RBD storage class, the default supported fstype for RBD storage class is ext4: ~~~ $ oc get sc ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-oyaml...... parameters:...... csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype: ext4...... ~~~ * RFE bug [RHSTOR-6107](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHSTOR-6107) is created to track this feature.

title: "No Alert Found" issue after clicking 'View Details' in RHOCP Web Console
issue: - "No Alert Found" issue after clicking 'View Details' in RHOCP Web Console.- Similar issue in `Openshift Container Platform` version 4.17 is described in [KCS: 7107170](https://access.redhat.com/node/7107170)
resolution: - This issue was reported to Red Hat Engineering and it can be tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-51118](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-51118). **Workaround:**- Clicking on "View Details" for an alert in Status will redirect to the link like below: ~~~ https://console-openshift-console.apps.xxxxxx.xxxx.xxx.xx.redhat.com/monitoring/alerts/xxxx?namespace=openshift-operators-redhat&severity=warning&alertname=ElasticsearchOperatorRemovalWarning&version=5.8.17 ~~~- Adding parameter **"prometheus=openshift-monitoring%2Fk8s&"** to the above URL will redirect to the correct alert: ~~~ https://console-openshift-console.apps.xxxxxx.xxxx.xxx.xx.redhat.com/monitoring/alerts/xxxx?namespace=openshift-operators-redhat&prometheus=openshift-monitoring%2Fk8s&severity=warning&alertname=ElasticsearchOperatorRemovalWarning&version=5.8.17 ~~~ [image=[src="images/screenshot_from_2025-02-20_20-41-54.png", alt="Add parameter "prometheus=openshift-monitoring%2Fk8s&" to the redirect URL", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", caption="Add parameter "prometheus=openshift-monitoring%2Fk8s&" to the redirect URL", lightbox="true"]]
root_cause: A code migration operation failed to process external labels correctly on the *Home > Overview > Status* pane on the *Administrator perspective* of the web console. These external labels are required to prevent silenced alert notifications from getting added to *Status* pane. title: Persistent storage for OpenShift using a static Ceph RBD
issue: I want to use a static Ceph Rados Block Device (RBD) as persistent storage for my OpenShift cluster. How do I do this?
resolution: 1. Any client that connects to the Ceph cluster should have the same `ceph-comon` package as that of the Ceph cluster. Ensure `ceph-common` package on the OpenShift cluster, matches the version of the Ceph cluster. Failure to do so, can cause a feature mismatch when communicating to the Ceph cluster. If they do not match, then you may need to `# yum update ceph-common`. 2. Create the Ceph pool on the Ceph cluster: # ceph osd pool create 2.1. Example: # ceph osd pool create openshift 128 3. Create the OpenShift client user on the Ceph cluster with proper privileges and a `keyring`: # ceph auth get-or-create mon 'allow r' osd 'allow rwx pool= '-o /etc/ceph/.keyring 3.1. Example: # ceph auth get-or-create client.openshift mon 'allow r' osd 'allow rwx pool=openshift'-o /etc/ceph/openshift.keyring 4. On the Ceph Cluster create the `rbd` image with layering the desired size: # rbd create /-s--image-feature=layering 4.1. Example: # rbd create openshift/ceph-image-test-s 2048--image-feature=layering 5. On the Ceph cluster gather the client information, and convert it to a `base64` key. This output will be needed to insert into the `secret.yml` on the OpenShift cluster for this step. Note that either the `client.admin` or the newly create `client.openshift` can be used. For the rest of this document we will use the `client.openshift` key for the lowest level of privileges. Example: # ceph auth list....... client.admin key: AQAa/KtacWl3GxAAG90+vdWtTdx7l6Grg0zpZQ== caps: [mds] allow caps: [mon] allow * caps: [osd] allow *....... client.openshift key: AQAVX7Fa5vWbGRAAkorZCZKHUDO95XZA6E0B/g== caps: [mon] allow r caps: [osd] allow rwx pool=openshift # echo AQAVX7Fa5vWbGRAAkorZCZKHUDO95XZA6E0B/g== | base64 QVFBVlg3RmE1dldiR1JBQWtvclpDWktIVURPOTVYWkE2RTBCL2c9PQo= 6. On the OpenShift Master node create the secret definition and insert the `base64`. Example: # vi ceph-secret-test.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: ceph-secret-test data: key: QVFBVlg3RmE1dldiR1JBQWtvclpDWktIVURPOTVYWkE2RTBCL2c9PQo= # oc create-f ceph-secret-test.yaml # oc get secret ceph-secret-test NAME TYPE DATA AGE ceph-secret-test Opaque 1 1h 7. On OpenShift master node create the Persistent Volume updating the necessary information. Example: # vi ceph-pv-test.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata: name: ceph-pv-test spec: capacity: storage: 2Gi accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce rbd: monitors:- 192.168.122.133:6789 pool: openshift image: ceph-image-test user: openshift secretRef: name: ceph-secret-test fsType: ext4 readOnly: false persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain # oc create-f ceph-pv-test.yaml # oc get pv NAME LABELS CAPACITY ACCESSMODES STATUS CLAIM REASON AGE ceph-pv-test 2147483648 RWO Available 2s * Note that in the `ceph-pv-test.yaml` example above, that the user is `user: openshift` and not `user: client.openshift` as Ceph will imply the "client" when viewing this and could cause authorization issues. 8. Create the Persistent Volume Claim. Example: # vi ceph-claim-test.yaml kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: ceph-claim-test spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 2Gi # oc create-f ceph-claim-test.yaml # oc get pvc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESSMODES STORAGECLASS AGE ceph-claim-test Bound ceph-pv-test 2Gi RWO 5m 9. Create the pod ensuring the `name:` metadata, containers, and volumes sections are updated to match the appropriate names. Example: # vi ceph-pod-test.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: ceph-pod-test spec: containers:- name: ceph-busybox image: busybox command: ["sleep", "60000"] volumeMounts:- name: ceph-vol-test mountPath: /usr/share/busybox readOnly: false volumes:- name: ceph-vol-test persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: ceph-claim-test # oc create-f ceph-pod-test.yaml # oc get pod NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE ceph-pod-test 1/1 Running 1 5m docker-registry-1-mkrp6 1/1 Running 0 1d registry-console-1-h499l 1/1 Running 0 1d router-1-srr79 1/1 Running 0 1d * Note that the transition from creating container status to the running status can sometimes take several minutes to complete as the container has to be created and mounted. * Now that the pod is in a running status, login into the node where your RBD image is mapped and run the following commands to check the RBD image is mounted properly: # rbd showmapped id pool image snap device 0 openshift ceph-image-test /dev/rbd0 # df-h | grep ceph /dev/rbd0 1998672 6144 1871288 1% /var/lib/origin/openshift.local.volumes/plugins/kubernetes.io/rbd/rbd/openshift-image-ceph-image-test
root_cause: * For further information on this, please refer to your version of the OpenShift [Installation and Configuration Guide](https://docs.openshift.com/enterprise/3.0/install_config/install/quick_install.html). * Note that this article was created to provide supplementary information from the Ceph perspective on this process that may not be provided from the OpenShift side. * For information on creating dynamic Ceph RBD's to use as storage for OpenShift, please refer to [Ceph- Storage for OpenShift using dynamic Ceph RBDs](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3480331)

title: Diagnosing etcdGRPCRequestsSlow alert in OpenShift 4
issue: Why is `etcdGRPCRequestsSlow` alert firing in OCP 4?
How to detect potential issues when the `etcdGRPCRequestsSlow` alert shows?
How to understand `etcdGRPCRequestsSlow`?
resolution: This is usually the result of etcd slow disk (in some cases due to fragmented state, and defragmenting it could mitigate the issue) or CPU contention. Network issues are also possible. Starting with OpenShift 4.9, the `etcd` operator automatically defragments the etcd database, but in some cases, it could be still needed to manually compact and defragment it. Refer to [how to compact and defrag etcd to decrease database size in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5564771) for additional information about etcd compaction and defragmentation. Refer also to [backend performance requirements for OpenShift etcd](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4770281) for etcd requirements, and to the "Diagnostic Steps" section for additional troubleshooting.
root_cause: This alert fires when the 99th percentile of etcd `gRPC` requests are too slow. When requests are too slow, they can lead to various scenarios like leader election failure, slow reads and writes, and overall cluster instability. This is usually the result of etcd slow disk (in some cases due to fragmented state) or CPU contention. Network issues are also possible. Refer to the "Diagnostic Steps" section for additional troubleshooting. Alert expression that fires the alert is: ~~~ alert: etcdGRPCRequestsSlow annotations: description: 'etcd cluster "{{$labels.job}}": 99th percentile of gRPC requests is {{$value}}s on etcd instance {{$labels.instance}} for {{$labels.grpc_method}} method.' summary: etcd grpc requests are slow expr: | histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(grpc_server_handling_seconds_bucket{job=~".*etcd.*", grpc_method!="Defragment", grpc_type="unary"}[5m])) without(grpc_type)) > 0.15 for: 10m labels: severity: critical ~~~

title: Does RHOCP4 OADP operator support WORM storage ?
issue: - Is the Write Once Read Many (WORM) storage technology supported by the OADP operator?
resolution: The Write Once Read Many (WORM) storage technology isn't natively supported by Velero/OADP.
root_cause: **Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. WORM storage naturally contradicts with how Velero/OADP operator is supposed to work. After uploading a `backup` to the storage bucket, Velero will need to modify the metadata in object storage (e.g. marking the state of the `backup`) and that won't be possible if some kind of immutability is configured on the object storage provider (e.g. AWS S3 Object Lock). For more details, check [the Velero docs](https://velero.io/docs/v1.15/backup-reference/#:~:text=Cannot%20support%20backup%20data%20immutability).
