title: How to use the File System Backup (FSB) in OADP for NFS PVC (RWX) in RHOCP4 ?
issue: - OADP Backup error `volume doesn't have the expected volume type. Expected VolumeType: block. Queried VolumeType: FILE` found in `backup` logs.- Not able to create `Backup` for an NFS PVC (RWX mode) using the OADP operator.
resolution: To backup NFS PVCs, make sure to set the `defaultVolumesToFsBackup` to `true` in the `Backup` CR as below: ~~~ apiVersion: velero.io/v1 kind: Backup metadata: name: labels: velero.io/storage-location: default namespace: openshift-adp spec: defaultVolumesToFsBackup: true ~~~
root_cause: NFS PersistentVolumes (PV) backup can be only taken by the File System Backup (FSB) method. For other types of PVs, one can use either the VolumeSnapshot or the FSB methods. More details in [Backing up applications with FSB](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/backup_and_restore/oadp-application-backup-and-restore#oadp-backing-up-applications-restic-doc).

title: Logs are not visible in Openshift Console in RHOCP4
issue: - Logs are not getting stored in `Log Store Loki`- Is it supported to configure the `bucketname` with a path as ` / ` for Loki?- Not able to see logs stored in Loki and the only error observed is in the Loki Ingester pods: ~~~ level=warn caller=grpc_logging.go:76 method=/logproto.Querier/GetChunkIDs duration=1.957822ms msg=gRPC err="rpc error: code = Code(499) desc = The request was cancelled by the client." ~~~
resolution: 1. Get the LokiStack secret name where set the parameters to the object storage: ``` $ secret=$(oc get lokistack logging-loki-n openshift-logging-o jsonpath='{.spec.storage.secret.name}') ``` 2. Extract the secret content: ``` $ mkdir secret && cd secret $ oc extract secret/$secret-n openshift-logging ``` 3. Modify the content of the file `bucketnames` for being ` ` and not ` / `. 4. Delete the secret ~~~ $ oc delete secret $secret-n openshift-logging ~~~ 5. Recreate secret. Note that depending on the object storage used, the parameters could be different, more details in the "[Loki Object storage](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html-single/logging/index#logging-loki-storage_installing-log-storage) documentation": ~~~ $ oc create secret generic $secret--from-file=bucketnames=./bucketnames--from-file=endpoint=./endpoint--from-file=access_key_id=./access_key_id--from-file=access_key_secret=./access_key_secret--from-literal=region=./region ~~~
root_cause: The secret set in `lokistack.spec.storage.secret.name` doesn't support to set a path inside the ` `. The `bucketnames` must be only the ` ` and not ` / `

title: Live Migration fails with operation failed: guest CPU doesn't match specification: missing features: waitpkg
issue: - Live Migration of VM failing with `operation failed: guest CPU doesn't match specification: missing features: waitpkg`- After upgrade from OCP-V v4.15.8 to v4.16.5, live migrations are failing repeatedly.
resolution: - The issue is being tracked in [CNV-55362](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-55362) for OCP-V and in [RHEL-84868](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-83143) for KVM- Currently the only work around is to stop and start a VM. After doing so the VM will migrate successfully.- If you wish to stop the Live Migrations until a time you can shut down the VMs, in OCP-V you can do the following: 1. Turn off all workload update methods by running the following command: `$oc patch hco kubevirt-hyperconverged-n openshift-cnv--type json-p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/workloadUpdateStrategy/workloadUpdateMethods", "value":[]}]'` 2. Delete each `vmim` objects in the namespace: `$oc delete vmim kubevirt-workload-update-XXXXX` 3. Eventually set this back to LiveMigrate with: `$oc patch hco kubevirt-hyperconverged-n openshift-cnv--type json-p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/workloadUpdateStrategy/workloadUpdateMethods", "value":[LiveMigrate]}]'`
root_cause: - A workload update is needed when OCP-V is updated. A live migration of a VM is needed to pick up the new changes. This is not a requirement right away, but should be done eventually (or a stop/start of the VM). This is failing with `operation failed: guest CPU doesn't match specification: missing features: waitpkg`. [CNV-55362](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-55362) has been opened with engineering to resolve this.

title: Container fails with error message MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume - no space left on device in OpenShift
issue: - A pod is unable to start and throws an error message indicating there is no space left on the device, upon checking the node where the pod is scheduled, there are available disk space.- The following message can be seen in the namespace events: ~~~ (combined from similar events): MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kube-api-access-tmxx5": write /var/lib/kubelet/pods/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/volumes/kubernetes.io~projected/kube-api-access-xxxxx/xxxxx-xxxx-xxxx/file.ext: no space left on device ~~~
resolution: Change the pod configuration to use the correct suffix in resource limits and requests. **Example:** ~~~ resources: limits: memory: 300Mi requests: memory: 50Mi ~~~
root_cause: Memory limits and requests require using the adequate quantity suffixes: E, P, T, G, M, k. You can also use the power-of-two equivalents: Ei, Pi, Ti, Gi, Mi, Ki.

title: How to migrate already-applied ICSPs to IDMSs without rebooting the nodes.
issue: - ImageContentSourcePolicy(ICSP) was deprecated on OpenShift 4.13- Migrate from ICSP to IDMS and delete the existing ICSPs without rebooting the nodes.
resolution: 1. Export ICSP configuration to a YAML file. ``` # oc get imagecontentsourcepolicies.operator.openshift.io image-policy-0-o yaml > image-policy-0.yaml ``` 2. Migrate from ICSP to IDMS. ``` # oc adm migrate icsp /icsp/image-policy-0.yaml--dest-dir /idsm/ ``` 3. Check the content of the IDMS file converted from ICSP. ``` # cat /idsm/imagedigestmirrorset_image-policy-0.xxxx.yaml apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageDigestMirrorSet metadata: generation: 1 name: image-policy-0 resourceVersion: "1119" uid: 3719580b-43c6-4062-b769-7a1823f578a4 spec: imageDigestMirrors:- mirrors:- harbor.ocp4.example.com/ocp41430/openshift4 source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release ``` 4. Create the IDMS configuration for the OCP cluster. ``` # oc create-f /idsm/imagedigestmirrorset_image-policy-0.xxxx.yaml imagedigestmirrorset.config.openshift.io/image-policy-0 created ``` 5. A new render will be created by the machine config, but the nodes will not be rebooted. ``` # oc get mc.... rendered-master-7a61452eed4adc584b9b32ba28fd4715 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 10s.... rendered-worker-c7a4c70c1a16a6f342b583d18a29489c 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 10s # oc get mcp NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE master rendered-master-f136b2209357453120f2b23987882ce8 False True False 3 1 1 0 21d worker rendered-worker-3936e95080d18f2286cfc0d116ba939a False True False 3 1 1 0 21d # oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master-0.ocp4upgrade.example.com Ready control-plane,master 21d v1.27.16+03a907c master-1.ocp4upgrade.example.com Ready control-plane,master 21d v1.27.16+03a907c master-2.ocp4upgrade.example.com Ready control-plane,master 21d v1.27.16+03a907c worker-0.ocp4upgrade.example.com Ready worker 21d v1.27.16+03a907c worker-1.ocp4upgrade.example.com Ready worker 21d v1.27.16+03a907c worker-2.ocp4upgrade.example.com Ready worker 21d v1.27.16+03a907c ``` 6. Once the IDMS is created, the mirror config will be added to the registry.conf file, as shown below. ``` # cat /etc/containers/registries.conf unqualified-search-registries = ["registry.access.redhat.com", "docker.io"] short-name-mode = "" [[registry]] prefix = "" location = "quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release" [[registry.mirror]] location = "harbor.ocp4.example.com/ocp41230/openshift4" pull-from-mirror = "digest-only" [[registry]] prefix = "" location = "quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev" [[registry.mirror]] location = "harbor.ocp4.example.com/ocp41230/openshift4" pull-from-mirror = "digest-only" ``` 7. Now, remove the old ICSP resource. No new MC render will be created, and no reboot will happen. ``` # oc delete imagecontentsourcepolicies.operator.openshift.io image-policy-0 # oc get mc |grep rendered rendered-master-0163f7dc69ea4cc351e836a4a89a98db 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 19d rendered-master-243d0e520a233953e661af7d71113b77 e54335a3855fc53597e883ba98b548add39a8938 3.2.0 20d rendered-master-4ed52635e406224f17700fd3d2e2f148 e54335a3855fc53597e883ba98b548add39a8938 3.2.0 21d rendered-master-7a61452eed4adc584b9b32ba28fd4715 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 65m rendered-master-f136b2209357453120f2b23987882ce8 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 19d rendered-master-fd311cca2bb6c9a332708eda815ceb28 39e3612071458fb2d876b9b8fb0d3517bcb1c7cc 3.2.0 20d rendered-worker-029adafe24f1b022405a1a6f57d8117c 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 19d rendered-worker-064a1326f9713c56a999cf7769f066bf e54335a3855fc53597e883ba98b548add39a8938 3.2.0 20d rendered-worker-3936e95080d18f2286cfc0d116ba939a 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 5d3h rendered-worker-565c0f042da1f0132ef08ef256829b7a 39e3612071458fb2d876b9b8fb0d3517bcb1c7cc 3.2.0 20d rendered-worker-8fd650a5ead78a8396ce2075c6c51a91 e54335a3855fc53597e883ba98b548add39a8938 3.2.0 21d rendered-worker-ba04de0de3e815f2f9e82bc48dd9d949 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 5d21h rendered-worker-bfdc6d208eac64967208f43823bc6f2e 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 19d rendered-worker-c7a4c70c1a16a6f342b583d18a29489c 4f8b6f2a0e1a8ec475e5ef1dd8effd9306804518 3.4.0 65m # oc get mcp NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE master rendered-master-7a61452eed4adc584b9b32ba28fd4715 True False False 3 3 3 0 21d worker rendered-worker-c7a4c70c1a16a6f342b583d18a29489c True False False 3 3 3 0 21d ```

title: How to access OVN DB content in RHOSO18
issue: - How to access OVN DB content in RHOSO18?
resolution: - There are two ways to access OVN DB. 1. Access OVN-NB, OVN-SB pod and run ovn-nbctl, ovn-sbctl on each pord. For OVN-NB ~~~ $ oc get pod |grep nb ovsdbserver-nb-0 1/1 Running 0 6d6h ovsdbserver-nb-1 1/1 Running 0 6d6h ovsdbserver-nb-2 1/1 Running 0 6d6h $ oc rsh pod/ovsdbserver-nb-0 sh-5.1$ alias ovn-nbctl="/usr/bin/ovn-nbctl--no-leader-only" sh-5.1$ ovn-nbctl--no-leader-only list Port_uuid: c0d4d04d-6be8-45bc-8977-4a2effeae729 acls: [77750695-5da3-467a-ba70-6ee4f723636a, 77d0a2f7-115a-4352-868e-3c31a409870b] external_ids: {} name: neutron_pg_drop ports: [] ~~~ For OVN-SB ~~~ $ oc get pod |grep sb ovsdbserver-sb-0 1/1 Running 0 6d6h ovsdbserver-sb-1 1/1 Running 0 6d6h ovsdbserver-sb-2 1/1 Running 0 6d6h $ oc rsh pod/ovsdbserver-sb-0 sh-5.1$ alias ovn-sbctl="/usr/bin/ovn-sbctl--no-leader-only" sh-5.1$ ovn-sbctl list sb_global_uuid: 7a334daf-a1b0-4d0e-bdeb-4aecd656673a connections: [77dc2833-e841-45c9-b713-5af25acf0222] external_ids: {} ipsec: false nb_cfg: 0 options: {arp_ns_explicit_output="true", fdb_removal_limit="0", ignore_lsp_down="false", mac_binding_removal_limit="0", mac_prefix="82:e6:f2", max_tunid="16711680", northd_internal_version="24.03.4-20.33.0-72.6", svc_monitor_mac="d6:89:b0:40:73:43"} ssl: dd12a73f-aca6-41bf-ade8-f1b27ef1ad66 ~~~ 2. Connect OVN-NB and OVN-SB from ovn-northd Pod ~~~ $ oc get pods |grep northd ovn-northd-6cd8c5bf4c-wqxxf 1/1 Running 0 6d6h ~~~ Retrieve required certificates for the connection then create aliases. ~~~ sh-5.1$ ps auxwww USER PID %CPU %MEM VSZ RSS TTY STAT START TIME COMMAND 1000750+ 1 0.0 0.0 169632 13176? Ssl Nov14 1:01 /usr/bin/ovn-northd-vfile:off-vconsole:info--n-threads=1--ovnnb-db=ssl:ovsdbserver-nb-0.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6641,ssl:ovsdbserver-nb-1.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6641,ssl:ovsdbserver-nb-2.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6641--ovnsb-db=ssl:ovsdbserver-sb-0.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6642,ssl:ovsdbserver-sb-1.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6642,ssl:ovsdbserver-sb-2.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6642--certificate=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ovndb.crt--private-key=/etc/pki/tls/private/ovndb.key--ca-cert=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ovndbca.crt 1000750+ 1751883 0.8 0.0 7372 3968 pts/0 Ss 08:38 0:00 /bin/sh 1000750+ 1751907 0.0 0.0 10064 3456 pts/0 R+ 08:38 0:00 ps auxwww Based on the example output above, create alias sh-5.1$ alias ovn-nbctl="/usr/bin/ovn-nbctl--certificate=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ovndb.crt--private-key=/etc/pki/tls/private/ovndb.key--ca-cert=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ovndbca.crt--no-leader-only--db=ssl:ovsdbserver-nb-0.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6641" sh-5.1$ alias ovn-sbctl="/usr/bin/ovn-sbctl--certificate=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ovndb.crt--private-key=/etc/pki/tls/private/ovndb.key--ca-cert=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ovndbca.crt--no-leader-only--db=ssl:ovsdbserver-sb-0.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6642" sh-5.1$ ovn-nbctl list port_uuid: c0d4d04d-6be8-45bc-8977-4a2effeae729 acls: [77750695-5da3-467a-ba70-6ee4f723636a, 77d0a2f7-115a-4352-868e-3c31a409870b] external_ids: {} name: neutron_pg_drop ports: [] sh-5.1$ ovn-sbctl list sb_global_uuid: 7a334daf-a1b0-4d0e-bdeb-4aecd656673a connections: [77dc2833-e841-45c9-b713-5af25acf0222] external_ids: {} ipsec: false nb_cfg: 0 options: {arp_ns_explicit_output="true", fdb_removal_limit="0", ignore_lsp_down="false", mac_binding_removal_limit="0", mac_prefix="82:e6:f2", max_tunid="16711680", northd_internal_version="24.03.4-20.33.0-72.6", svc_monitor_mac="d6:89:b0:40:73:43"} ssl: dd12a73f-aca6-41bf-ade8-f1b27ef1ad66 ~~~ If the connection is not TLS, you don't need to check certificate. The alias will be ~~~ sh-5.1$ alias ovn-nbctl="/usr/bin/ovn-nbctl--no-leader-only--db=tcp:ovsdbserver-nb-0.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6641" sh-5.1$ alias ovn-sbctl="/usr/bin/ovn-sbctl--no-leader-only--db=tcp:ovsdbserver-sb-0.openstack.svc.cluster.local:6642" ~~~

title: Mirror-registry stuck at  Set facts for existing postgres secrets only if they are a string and not a jinja2 variable in the config.yaml
issue: - We have started upgrading the mirror registry to 2.0.5. During the upgrade migration, the session got closed and unable to proceed even after it was rerun.- Mirror-registry binary uses ansible playbooks and upgrade is stuck at a particular TASK ``` TASK [mirror_appliance: Set facts for existing postgres secrets only if they are a string and not a jinja2 variable in the config.yaml.] **

fatal: [root@hostname.com]: FAILED! => {"msg": "The task includes an option with an undefined variable. The error was: list object has no element 2. list object has no element 2

The error appears to be in '/runner/project/roles/mirror_appliance/tasks/upgrade-config-vars.yaml': line 24, column 3, but may
be elsewhere in the file depending on the exact syntax problem.

The offending line appears to be:


- name: Set facts for existing postgres secrets only if they are a string and not a jinja2 variable in the config.yaml.
 ^ here
"} PLAY RECAP ******************************************************************************************************************
root@hostname.com: ok=18 changed=3 unreachable=0 failed=1 skipped=6 rescued=0 ignored=0 ERRO[2025-04-02 17:15:06] An error occurred: exit status 2 ```- Postgres to Sqlite migration is stuck
resolution: - Set the DB_URI in quay-config.yaml file to the following format only: ``` DB_URI: "postgres://username:password@hostname:5432/database" ```
root_cause: From the [code](https://github.com/quay/mirror-registry/blob/0f749334a945abccdf1b57ddbe6335f6083591bb/ansible-runner/context/app/project/roles/mirror_appliance/tasks/upgrade-config-vars.yaml#L24), the [2]task failing does the following:- Extract the PostgreSQL database password from DB_URI only if following conditions are met:- Postgres container exists/running.- DATABASE_SECRET_KEY is a string (not a Jinja2 variable or undefined).- DB_URI is also a valid string [2] ```- name: Set facts for existing postgres secrets only if they are a string and not a jinja2 variable in the config.yaml. ansible.builtin.set_fact: PGDB_PASSWORD: "{{quay_config_file['DB_URI'].split('@')[0].split(':')[2]}}" when: postgres_container_status.stdout!= "" and quay_config_file['DATABASE_SECRET_KEY'] is string and quay_config_file['DB_URI'] is string ```- The DB_URI string was in below format: ``` DB_URI: sqlite:////sqlite/quay_sqlite.db ```

title: Provide options for RHEL 8 compatible OC CLI to be downloaded from WEB UI
issue: - Provide options for `RHEL 8` compatible `OC CLI` to be downloaded from `OCP WEB UI`- Downloading `OC CLI` from `OCP WEB UI` has options only for `RHEL 9` and requires `glibc 2.32` or above.
resolution: - This feature enhancement request to provide option to download `OC CLI` from `OCP Web UI` has been submitted to `Red Hat` and can be tracked under [RFE-7292](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7292).- For more information [open a new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).

title: Alerting rules "CollectorHighErrorRate" and "CollectorVeryHighErrorRate" not created after deploying collector pods in logging version 6
issue: Alerting rules "CollectorHighErrorRate" and "CollectorVeryHighErrorRate" not created after deploying `collector` pods deployed using `OBSCLF` in `RHOL version 6`.
resolution: - The alerts "CollectorHighErrorRate" and "CollectorVeryHighErrorRate" have been intentionally removed from the product, with the possibility of being reintroduced in the future.- The issue could be traced under [LOG-3432](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-3432).- For more information [open a new support case with Red Hat](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).

title: Too many process running on a node
issue: - Too many `process` running on a `node`.- What is the `maximum number` of `process` that could run on a `node`?
resolution: - The `maximum number` of `process` that can be run on a `node` depends on the resources allocated to the `node`.- Use below command to check `maximum numbe`r of `process` that can be run at a time on any particular `node`: ~~~ $ oc debug # cat /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max ~~~

title: Universal Developer Image is using old oc-client binary
issue: - With Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces- `Universal Developer Image`, the `oc client` binary version 4.12.0 (openshift-clients-4.12.0) is being used.
resolution: - A bug [`CRW-7272`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CRW-7272) has been raised for the issue and it's resolved in `Dev Spaces` version 3.19.- The `UDI9` image is using `oc client` binary version 4.17.

title: CredentialsRequest CR for mounting secrets from AWS Secrets Manager is failing
issue: - While creating `CredentialsRequest` CR for mounting `secrets` from `AWS Secrets Manager`, CR is failing with the below error, ~~~ CredentialsRequest aws-provider-test was failing- aws-provider status: conditions:- lastProbeTime: '2025-03-06T17:31:03Z' lastTransitionTime: '2025-03-06T17:31:03Z' message: 'failed to grant creds: error syncing creds in mint-mode: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:iam:: is not authorized to perform: iam:ListAccessKeys on resource: user because no identity-based policy allows the iam:ListAccessKeys action, status code: 403' reason: CredentialsProvisionFailure status: 'True' type: CredentialsProvisionFailure ~~~
resolution: - While configuring cloud configure operator utility to use with AWS, in AWS console few permissions are required, which are listed in [`documentation`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html-single/installing_on_aws/index#cco-ccoctl-configuring_installing-aws-customizations). In the `documentation`, one iam permission is missing which is `iam:ListAccessKeys`.- Make sure while creating `AWS account` for using `coctl` utility add `iam:ListAccessKeys` as well in required `iam` permissions.- A Documentation bug [`OCPBUGS-54410`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-54410) has been raised to add the information in the [`documentation`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html-single/installing_on_aws/index#cco-ccoctl-configuring_installing-aws-customizations) as well and engineering team is working on it, In case of any issues open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/) with the Red Hat support team.

title: ODF:  All Ceph-MON Pods crashing at the same time everyday.
issue: All Ceph-MON Pods crashing at the same time everyday.
Monitor pods are restarting
resolution: To resolve the issue with the Ceph MON Pods crashing every day, either uninstall `Twistlock-Defender` altogether, or use KCS Article [7001710](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7001710) to resolve the `Twistlock Defender` OOM issue.
root_cause: There is a known issue where `Twistlock-Defender` Pods are being OOM-killed (Out of Memory), which leads to Ceph MON Pods Crashing. It may be at the same time every day

title: How to solve oc rsync fails due to no space on the disk in /tmp storage
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - oc rsync fails due to no space on the disk in /tmp storage
resolution: - Setting TMPDIR before run rsync can help to modify cache path ~~~ export TMPDIR="folder were data should be cached" oc rsync pod:source_path target_path ~~~
root_cause: - When running oc rsync there will be cache exist default on /tmp

title: HCP cluster upgrade pending due to waiting on ingress
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - HCP cluster upgrade pending due to waiting on ingress
resolution: - Make sure the secret defined in ingress controller exists in openshift-ingress namespace, which can help to solve the issue. ~~~ $ oc get ingresscontroller/xxxxxxx-n openshift-ingress-operator-o yaml spec: clientTLS: clientCA: name: "" clientCertificatePolicy: "" defaultCertificate: name: ~~~
root_cause: - The Ingress controller related secret not exist

title: How do I identify high CPU utilization by Java threads on Linux/Solaris
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Java application using a large percentage of CPU
Java application server (JBoss EAP, Tomcat) high CPU utilization
CPU resource data is needed to diagnose high CPU usage
Need to identify a java thread utilizing large CPU resources
There is an elevated CPU consume in the processors of our virtual server where we could not evidence using TOP command
resolution: This article covers identifying CPU usage by Java applications on Linux or Solaris. As such, it covers just one part of diagnosing situations where there is unexplained high CPU utilization. High CPU usage is more generally addressed in [Java application high CPU.](/knowledge/node/24830) It is also possible to do the same on Openshift. See also the article [How to identify high CPU utilization by Java threads on OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5865191). ## 1. Collect thread-level CPU usage and thread dumps The first step is capturing Java thread dumps along with thread-level CPU usage information. Java thread dump can be captured by using `kill-3 ` (sending `SIGQUIT` signal to java process) that will output a java thread dump to the standard output of the Java process, or by using the `jstack` command which will capture java thread dump to the standard output of the `jstack` command. And the thread-level CPU usage information can be captured by `top` command with `-H` option like `top-b-n 1-H-p `. When the CPU spike happens, you can run the script appropriate for the architecture contained in the attached archive ([high_cpu_linux.tar.gz](/knowledge/sites/default/files/attachments/high_cpu_linux.tar_1.gz) or [high_cpu_solaris.tar.gz](/knowledge/sites/default/files/attachments/high_cpu_solaris.tar_1.gz)) passing in the Java process ID as an argument. The archive contains both scripts with the SIGQUIT version and the jstack version to capture Java thread dumps. Archive Summary high_cpu_linux.tar.gz |-- high_cpu_linux.sh # Using SIGQUIT to generate thread dumps |-- high_cpu_linux_jstack.sh # using jstack and SIGQUIT to generate thread dumps high_cpu_solaris.tar.gz |-- high_cpu_solaris.sh # Using SIGQUIT to generate thread dumps: |-- high_cpu_solaris_jstack.sh # Using jstack and SIGQUIT to generate thread dumps: The scripts will capture a series of 6 thread dumps along with CPU by light weight thread, spaced 20 seconds apart (the time interval can be adjusted if necessary). The CPU information will be captured in a file called `high-cpu.out` in the directory where the script is run, and thread dumps will be sent to stdout. If using the jstack version of the script, thread dumps will also be captured in `high-cpu-tdump.out`. If a non-jstack version is being used and the Java application is started with a service script that logs console output, the thread dumps will be in the console log. Otherwise, redirect stdout to a file on startup. See [How do I generate a Java thread dump on Linux/Unix?](/knowledge/node/18178) for a discussion on redirecting stdout to a file. Or aside from the script and having to manually determine the process id, a simple way to capture these data points for any running java processes is a line line command like the following: ~~~ $ for y in {1..20}; do echo $y > &2; for pid in $(ps-C java--noheader-o pid); do jstack-l $pid > > jstack-$pid.out; top-b-n 1-H-p $pid > > high-cpu-$pid.out; done; top-b-n 1-H > > high-cpu.out; sleep 10; done ~~~ Be sure to test the script or command before the issue happens to ensure it runs properly in the target environment. This is especially important when using the jstack version of the script as jstack may or may not work depending on what version of the JDK is being used or what version of the jstack tool is being used. Note that the jstack version should only be used with JDK 6+ as jstack from JDK 5 will not produce the same desired thread dump data. **Note:** * Usage instructions are included in each.sh script * If running JBoss EAP or one of the other JBoss enterprise products as a service, and are unable to find the generated thread dump see [Unable to generate thread dump using jstack or kill-3 command](/knowledge/node/69440) * Make sure to execute the `jstack` command from the same user as the java process when using `high_cpu_linux_jstack.sh` and `high_cpu_solaris_jstack.sh`. Please see [this article](https://access.redhat.com/site/solutions/317143) for more details. * Example while targeting a specific $USER and $JAVA_PID: ~~~ su-p-s /bin/sh $USER-c "./high_cpu_linux_jstack.sh $JAVA_PID" ~~~ ## 2. Identify thread consuming high CPU usage From the `high-cpu.out` file, it's possible to identify process ID's for java threads utilizing a large percentage of the CPU. For example, output such as the attached example [top command output "high-cpu-linux.out"](/knowledge/sites/default/files/attachments/high-cpu-linux.out_7.zip) shows CPU being used by three Java threads: PID USER PR NI VIRT RES SHR S %CPU %MEM TIME+ COMMAND 4382 root 25 0 1284m 480m 80m R 39.5 23.7 13:00.64 java 6657 root 25 0 1284m 480m 80m R 39.5 23.7 7:23.10 java 16322 root 25 0 1284m 480m 80m R 19.8 23.7 57:51.77 java And the same PID (4382) are consistently using significant CPU across the six snapshots in the attached example. Then, let's follow-up on thread with PID 4382 from Java thread dump. Using the [Thread Dump Analyzer](https://github.com/irockel/tda) (TDA) tool, one can load the thread dumps that were gathered with the high CPU data. Click on the Native-ID column in the upper right pane to sort by native thread ID and cross reference the light weight thread IDs from the top output to see the threads consuming high CPU. The screen shot below shows the stack track for thread ID 4382, identifying the code being executed by the thread:![](/knowledge/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/images/tda_3.png "") Since JDK 21, the process ID of the thread is captured as the same decimal format value as Native ID `nid=...` in Java thread dump. (This has been implemented since JDK18+ by the enhancement [JDK-8268425](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8268425)). ~~~ "default task-1" #215 [3177477] prio=5 os_prio=0 cpu=12.16ms elapsed=7.92s tid=0x000055f3d01034e0 nid=3177477 waiting on condition [0x00007fbbf55fc000] ^^^^^^^^^^^ ~~~ Until JDK 17, the process ID of the thread is captured as hexadecimal format value as Native ID `nid=0x...` in Java thread dump. For example: ~~~ "default task-123" #265 prio=5 os_prio=0 tid=0x0000563d65418000 nid=0x111e runnable [0x00007f0fb38ff000] ^^^^^^^^^^ ~~~ You can convert between hexadecimal value and decimal value by the `printf` command: ~~~ # convert from hexadecimal_value (0x....) to decimal value: $ printf "%d" # convert from decimal value to hexadecimal_value (0x....): $ printf "%x" # if you want to prepend "0x" to the output result: $ printf "0x%x" ~~~ For example: ~~~ $ printf "%d" 0x111e 4382 $ printf "%x" 4382 111e $ printf "0x%x" 4382 0x111e ~~~ ## 3. Shell script to run The shell script to run is *high_cpu_linux_jstack.sh* This script is taking 6 snapshots each 20s (total duration 2mn). Output files:- high-cpu.out- high-cpu-tdump.out Command line ~~~ Usage: sh./high_cpu_linux_jstack.sh ~~~ ~~~ #!/bin/sh # # Takes the JBoss PID as an argument. # # Captures cpu by light weight thread and thread dumps a specified number of # times and INTERVAL. Thread dumps are retrieved using jstack and are placed in # high-cpu-tdump.out # # Usage: sh./high_cpu_linux_jstack.sh # # Change Log: # * 2011-05-02 19:00 #- Added date output to high-cpu.out for log correlation #- Added-p argument to top to limit high-cpu.out to # # # Number of times to collect data. LOOP=6 # Interval in seconds between data points. INTERVAL=20 for ((i=1; i <= $LOOP; i++)) do_now=$(date) echo "${_now}" > > high-cpu.out top-b-n 1-H-p $1 > > high-cpu.out echo "${_now}" > > high-cpu-tdump.out jstack-l $1 > > high-cpu-tdump.out echo "thread dump #" $i if [$i-lt $LOOP]; then echo "Sleeping..." sleep $INTERVAL fi done ~~~

title: Image Build failed with version `GLIBC_2.33' not found (required by dotnet)
issue: - Image Build failed with error message `version `GLIBC_2.33' not found (required by dotnet)`.- While building image using openshift-pipelines with buildah task, `buildah bud` command failed with below error message: dotnet: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.33' not found (required by dotnet) dotnet: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found (required by dotnet)- After using updated Buildah version `v1.39.0` image started facing issue.
resolution: Use Buildah image with version `v1.39.4`
root_cause: - Bug in Buildah version `v1.39.0`, platform version and binary versions are mismatch like RHEL9 binary fails in RHEL8 and vice versa.

title: openstackclient env configuration in OpenStackControlPlane CR for environment variables does not work.
issue: - openstackclient env configuration in OpenStackControlPlane CR for environment variables does not work.
resolution: - The commit to implement env option to inject environment variable is implemented from RHOSO18.0.6. This means the user who use the earlier releases than RHOSO18.0.6 cannot use the interface. If you use those versions, you need to set required environment variable for openstack command needs to be set manually.

title: Is it possible to completely remove the Disabled Insights Operator status from OpenShift Webconsole ?
issue: - After disabling Insights Operator following [Opting out of remote health reporting](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/support/remote-health-monitoring-with-connected-clusters#opting-out-remote-health-reporting) doc, a yellow highlight/alert icon is seen for Insights[Disabled] from OpenShift Webconsole--> Administrator => Overview => Status. Is it possible to completely remove this?- Insights [Disabled] status needs to be removed altogether as this creates a confusion when any team member who is able to view the status as they can think something is wrong in the cluster and panic.- There is no point having a yellow Warning icon for Insights[Disabled] status in an air-gapped cluster.
resolution: Currently, there is no such functionality. RFE [RHIN-1863](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHIN-1863) is raised for this. For further information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: Enable ethtool collector for OpenShift Monitoring Node Exporter in RHOCP4
issue: - The `ethtool` `collector` in `Node Exporter` is included in RHOCP4 but is disabled by default.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE-7342](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7342). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: As per the [Official Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/monitoring/config-map-reference-for-the-cluster-monitoring-operator#nodeexportercollectorconfig), the `ethtool` `collector` is not listed in `NodeExporterCollectorConfig` resource settings.

title: ArgoCD: spec.controller.extraCommandArgs and  spec.server.extraCommandArgs are no longer accepting multiple entries of same flag with same or different value
issue: - ArgoCD, `spec.controller.extraCommandArgs` and `spec.server.extraCommandArgs` are no longer accepting multiple entries of same flag with same or different value.- When adding flags to `Controller` and `Server` pod via ArgoCD `spec.controller.extraCommandArgs` and `spec.server.extraCommandArgs` it is not reflecting all added entries into pod: #Config kind: ArgoCD [...] spec: controller: extraCommandArgs:---metrics-application-labels- application.argoproj.io/template-version---metrics-application-labels- application.argoproj.io/chart-version #Pod_Yaml containers:- command:- argocd-application-controller [...]---metrics-application-labels <------- Flag added only once- application.argoproj.io/chart-version <------- with bottom value from extraCommandArgs list- ArgoCD failed to add all `spec.controller.extraCommandArgs` and `spec.server.extraCommandArgs` flags after OpenShift GitOps Upgrade.
resolution: The `spec.controller.extraCommandArgs` and `spec.server.extraCommandArgs` will not add entry, if one of the commands is already part of the server/controller pod commands with same or different value.
root_cause: - This has been introduced to fix this bug [GITOPS-5200](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-5200 "GITOPS-5200") issue.- Earlier, While adding extraCommandArgs field in ArgoCD CR, if an existing flag is added, not only that flag was ignored, but the other arguments added with it which were not part of the deployment already will also be ignored.- With this fix, any added flag entires will be compared with pod entries and only one of the duplicate entries will be considered and rest of the duplicate entries will be ignored.

title: How to enable HA support for Argo Rollout Controller in Openshift GitOps - RHOCP4
issue: How to enable HA support for Argo Rollout Controller in Openshift GitOps?
resolution: - From [Openshift GitOps v1.15.0](https://docs.openshift.com/gitops/1.15/release_notes/gitops-release-notes-1-15.html#new-features-1-15-0_gitops-release-notes) onwards, high availability (HA) support is introduced in Argo Rollout controller.- Add `.spec.ha` field to the RolloutManager CR as below: ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: RolloutManager name: namespace: openshift-gitops spec: <---- ha: enabled: true ~~~- When enabling high availability, the GitOps Operator automatically sets the number of replicas to 2, the leader election is activated, and default anti-affinity rules are applied to ensure redundancy and reliability ~~~ oc get pods | grep-i argo-rollout argo-rollouts-7776c8cc55-fd2vp 1/1 Running 0 11m argo-rollouts-7776c8cc55-l6j4h 1/1 Running 0 12m ~~~

title: Unable to connect Kiali with TempoStack in RHOCP 4
issue: - Is it possible to integrate Kiali with TempoStack?- How to integrate Kiali with TempoStack?- Unable to integrate Kiali with multitenant TempoStack.
resolution: Config **spec.external_services.tracing** in `Kiali` custom resource should be configured as per below example: ~~~ spec: external_services: tracing: auth: insecure_skip_verify: true type: bearer use_kiali_token: true enabled: true in_cluster_url: 'https://-gateway..svc.cluster.local:8080/api/traces/v1/ ' namespace_selector: true provider: jaeger query_timeout: 30 url: 'https://-gateway..apps. /api/traces/v1/ /search' use_grpc: false ~~~- Replace **tempostack-name** with the name of TempoStack custom resource.- Replace **namespace** with the name of namespace in which TempoStack is created.- Replace **tenant-name** with the name of tenant which is configured in TempoStack custom resource.
root_cause: There can multiple root causes for the problem but below are most common ones:- Misconfigured in_cluster_url in Kiali config. The URL should contain **api/traces/v1/ ** as path.- spec.external_services.tracing.provider in Kiali config should be configured to use jaeger.

title: /run filesystem has no inodes or space available in RHOCP 4

title: OVNKubernetesNodeOVSOverflowKernel alert is firing on cluster with OVN-Kubernetes and Broadcom NICs
issue: There is an `OVNKubernetesNodeOVSOverflowKernel` alert firing on an OpenShift Container Platform cluster that is running OVN-Kubernetes and has Broadcom NICs.
Users are reporting that there are connectivity problems on some OpenShift Container Platform Nodes after migrating the cluster to OVN-Kubernetes.
resolution: There are multiple possible root causes for this issue, this Solution concerns the specific root cause when using Broadcom NICs. Please see the following article for more generic information about this alarm: [Troubleshooting the OVNKubernetesNodeOVSOverflowKernel alarm](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7115263) * Red Hat is aware of this issue concerning Broadcom NICs and is tracking the resolution in the following Bugs: [FDP-900](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/FDP-900), [RHEL-78363](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-78363) * A possible workaround is to temporarily disable `rx-gro-hw` on all interfaces on the affected OpenShift Container Platform Node: ~~~ $ ethtool-K rx-gro-hw off ~~~ Note that this will only temporarily disable the `rx-gro-hw` feature until the Node is rebooted and will only work for certain Broadcom NICs. This can be used to verify that the workaround works as expected. To persist the workaround, the following NetworkManager dispatcher script can be used: ~~~ $ cat script #!/bin/bash # Bug https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-73725 # Solution https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7107374 driver=$(nmcli-t-m tabular-f general.driver dev show "${DEVICE_IFACE}") if [["$2" == "up" && "${driver}" == "bnxt_en" &&-f /usr/sbin/ethtool]]; then logger-s "99-solution-7107374-workaround-rx-gro-hw-off triggered by ${2} on device ${DEVICE_IFACE}." /usr/sbin/ethtool-K ${DEVICE_IFACE} rx-gro-hw off fi ~~~ * To apply this workaround via persistent NetworkManager dispatcher script, apply the following `MachineConfig` to your cluster: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-solution-7107374-workaround-rx-gro-hw-off spec: config: ignition: config: {} security: tls: {} timeouts: {} version: 3.1.0 networkd: {} passwd: {} storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64, mode: 484 overwrite: true path: /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-solution-7107374-workaround-rx-gro-hw-off osImageURL: "" ~~~ Note that the label might need to be adjusted based on your Machine Config Pool selectors. Also note that applying an additional `MachineConfig` will lead to the selected Nodes being restarted.
root_cause: * The Broadcom networking driver or NIC is setting the wrong GSO (GRO) metadata which is causing a packet drop.

title: OpenShift Compliance Operator returns "Error from server (NotFound)" when attempting  to get a ComplianceRemediation object
issue: A compliance scan by the OpenShift Compliance Operator occassionally generates ComplianceCheckResult objects without creating associated ComplianceRemediation objects. For example, after running a compliance scan a ComplianceCheckResult object is created for a particular compliance rule: ~~~ $ oc get-n openshift-compliance compliancecheckresult NAME STATUS SEVERITY FAIL unknown ~~~ However, attempting to view the associated ComplianceRemediation object results in `Error from server (NotFound)`: ~~~ $ oc get-n openshift-compliance complianceremediation-o yaml Error from server (NotFound): complianceremediations.compliance.openshift.io " " not found ~~~
resolution: This is expected behavior for a ComplianceCheckResult that doesn't include the `compliance.openshift.io/automated-remediation` label.
root_cause: As stated in the compliance operator documentation, not all ComplianceCheckResult objects will create an associated ComplianceRemediation object. Only those results than can be automatically remediated will create the remediation object. If a ComplianceCheckResult is able to create a remediation object, it will contain the `compliance.openshift.io/automated-remediation` label. ComplianceCheckResults that aren't able to create remediation objects will not contain the `compliance.openshift.io/automated-remediation` label.

title: RHACM GUI does not show the Upgrade available option for local-cluster or managed cluster
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: RHACM GUI does not show the `Upgrade available` option on Hub cluster for local-cluster or managed cluster.
Cluster shows the next available option whereas the RHACM UI does not reflect.
resolution: * Delete the `ClusterCurator` of local-cluster or managed cluster from local-cluster or managed cluster namespace which is not reflecting on the RHACM UI. ~~~ Backup the configuration file: $ oc get ClusterCurator local-cluster-n local-cluster-o yaml > local-cluster_curator.yaml Delete the ClusterCurator: $ oc delete ClusterCurator local-cluster-n local-cluster ~~~ * Take a note if it has any Ansible automations defined in the spec of the `ClusterCurator`. If it does, you will need to re-apply the Automation template that set these up to the local-cluster or managed cluster.
root_cause: * The `ClusterCurator` job has stuck from a previous update and blocking a new one which fails to reflect on the RHACM UI for local-cluster or managed cluster.

title: EAP7/8 Bootable jar building
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - Bootable jar example- Bootable jar
resolution: ### Example Bootable jar `pom.xml`: ~~~ <?xml version="1.0"?> 4.0.0 test bootable-eap 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT war UTF-8 21 8.0.5.GA-redhat-00001 5.0.0.GA-redhat-00009 org.jboss.bom jboss-eap-ee ${jboss-eap-ee} pom import org.jboss.bom jboss-eap-xp-microprofile ${version.jboss.eap.xp} pom import org.slf4j slf4j-api provided jakarta.ejb jakarta.ejb-api provided jakarta.jms jakarta.jms-api provided jakarta.enterprise jakarta.enterprise.cdi-api provided jakarta.annotation jakarta.annotation-api provided jakarta.ws.rs jakarta.ws.rs-api provided org.eclipse.microprofile.health microprofile-health-api provided org.eclipse.microprofile.config microprofile-config-api provided bootable-jms-test org.apache.maven.plugins maven-war-plugin 3.4.0 false org.wildfly.plugins wildfly-jar-maven-plugin 9.0.1.Final-redhat-00010 org.jboss.eap.channels eap-8.0 org.jboss.eap.channels eap-xp-5.0 org.jboss.eap.xp:wildfly-galleon-pack se.uhr.nya.jboss jboss.eap.galleon 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT--> true jaxrs-server ejb microprofile-config microprofile-health microprofile-openapi microprofile-config microprofile-metrics datasources db2-driver--> embedded-activemq deployment-scanner extra-content true package redhat-ga Redhat GA https://maven.repository.redhat.com/ga/ redhat-ga Redhat GA https://maven.repository.redhat.com/ga/ ~~~ **References** * [[1] JBoss EAP 8 Maintenance Schedule][EAP8]- lists EAP 8 Update Channel Manifest Versions * [[2] JBoss EAP XP Maintenance Schedule][XP]- lists EAP XP Update Channel Manifest Versions [EAP8]: https://access.redhat.com/articles/7039745 "JBoss EAP 8 Maintenance Schedule" [XP]: https://access.redhat.com/articles/7105100 "JBoss EAP XP Maintenance Schedule"
root_cause: In the `pom.xml` above two main sections require detail: ### Bootable jar plugin version differences: Red Hat `wildfly-jar-maven-plugin`: ~~~ org.wildfly.plugins wildfly-jar-maven-plugin 9.0.1.Final-redhat-00011 ~~~ Community `wildfly-jar-maven-plugin`: ~~~ org.wildfly.plugins wildfly-jar-maven-plugin 12.0.0.Beta1 ~~~ We recommend the customer to use the latest in 9.x plugin. ### pluginRepositories vs repositories pluginRepositories: ~~~ redhat-ga Redhat GA https://maven.repository.redhat.com/ga/ ~~~ Repositories: ~~~ redhat-ga Redhat GA https://maven.repository.redhat.com/ga/ ~~~ Those settings above are not the same and serve different purposes:- Parent artifact dependencies are solved with `repository`- The plugin dependencies will be solved with `pluginRepository`. Note if the `./m2/settings.xml` has these repository setting, there is no reason to set them on the `pom.xml`.

title: OCP 4 Node upgrade fails with Operation not permitted error while cleaning old deployments
issue: - The worker node fails to upgrade and the corresponding machine-config-daemon pod logs show below error: ~~~ error: Cleaning deployments: Removing ostree/deploy/rhcos/deploy/ef91954348b1901dc79819991ddde8bffc718241fb23fa31a0798d337fa330ea.0: unlinkat(resolv.conf): Operation not permitted ~~~
resolution: - Make sure there are no file attributes such as immutable (i) set inside older RHCOS ostree deployments present in the directory `/ostree/deploy/rhcos/deploy/`.- Access the affected node using ssh or 'oc debug node/ ' ~~~ $lsattr /ostree/deploy/rhcos/deploy/ /etc/resolv.conf----i--------------- /ostree/deploy/rhcos/deploy/ /etc/resolv.conf ^ immutable attribute ~~~- The /sysroot is mounted as read-only, which means you cannot remove the immutable attribute using chattr. To remove, /sysroot needs to be remounted as read-write. ~~~ $mount-o remount,rw /sysroot ~~~- Run the following command to remove the attribute. ~~~ $chattr-i /ostree/deploy/rhcos/deploy/ /etc/resolv.conf ~~~- Find the correct machine-config-daemon pod for the affected node, then check its logs and monitor the upgrade process. ~~~ $oc-n openshift-machine-config-operator get pods-o wide $oc-n openshift-machine-config-operator logs machine-config-daemon-xxxx-c machine-config-daemon-f ~~~
root_cause: - There was an immutable file attribute set to the `/etc/resolv.conf' file inside the older RHCOS ostree deployment which was not letting the MCD to remove this older deployment in order to free up some space for the new ostree deployment during the upgrade. ~~~ # lsattr /ostree/deploy/rhcos/deploy/855dbb83e02cb2f2b627082f678936ee5c9a3b21e0eb3ac7667787102d13e316.0/etc/resolv.conf----i--------------- 855dbb83e02cb2f2b627082f678936ee5c9a3b21e0eb3ac7667787102d13e316.0/etc/resolv.conf ~~~

title: What are the negative performance impact  caused by enabling  routingViaHost?
issue: - When RHOCP nodes are configured with multiple interfaces i.e. primary interface for cluster traffic and secondary for storage traffic for connecting to external storage. In such cases the kernel routing table should be used and hence `routingViaHost` parameter should be `enabled`.- Is there any performance impact when using OVN-Kubernetes in `local gateway` mode i.e. enabling `routingViaHost` parameter?- What is the use of OpenvSwitch(OVS) hw-offload?
resolution: - OVS HW offload is supported when the NIC has dedicated hardware that can do some of the OVS tasks, so that it does not happen in the CPU. More details can be referred in the following [documentation](https://github.com/openshift/ovn-kubernetes/blob/master/docs/features/hardware-offload/ovs-kernel.md)- Refer to the list of [NICS](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/networking/hardware_networks/configuring-hardware-offloading.html#supported_devices_configuring-hardware-offloading) supporting hardware offloading.- Prerequisites for hardware offloading can be referred from the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/networking/hardware_networks/configuring-hardware-offloading.html#configuring-hardware-offloading-prerequisites) which mentions shared gateway should be used for OVN-Kubernetes.- If SR-IOV is not used, there is no use of OVS hw-offload.- Apart from ovs hardware offloading, routingviahost has impact on traffic flow, i.e. pod to external communication will have different traffic flows for local and shared gateway mode.- Shared gateway means `everything happens in OVS`. More concretely, packets leaving to external systems would go from the pod network namespace through `br-int`, then `br-ex` and it only leaves OVS once injected on the outgoing interface.- Local gateway means packets leave OVS earlier because it goes through `host network namespace`. In this case, packets go through `br-int` to the `ovn-k8s-mp0` interface in the host network and then, from the host network, they are sent to external systems.

title: Routes are automatically recreated after deleting them in OpenShift 4
issue: - After deleting a `route` from a `namespace` in OpenShift 4, it is automatically recreated with no known reason.- Why some `routes` are being automatically recreated after deletion in OpenShift 4?
resolution: Check if the `route` has `ownerReferences`, and check what owns the `route`: ~~~ $ oc get route [route_name]-n [namespace_name] [...] ownerReferences:- apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 controller: true kind: Ingress name: [ingress_resource_name] [...] ~~~ If the `ownerReferences` is an `ingress.networking.k8s.io` resource, it will be needed to remove that resource if the route is not really needed. Refer to [Creating a route through an Ingress object](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/networking/configuring-routes#nw-ingress-creating-a-route-via-an-ingress_route-configuration) for additional information about the `Ingress` resource.
root_cause: The `ingress.networking.k8s.io` manages the `route`, and if the `route` is deleted, the `ingress` will recreate it.

title: How to disable ArgoCD out of sync alerts ?
issue: - How to disable ArgoCD out of sync alerts?
resolution: To disable the alerting rule, try editing the prometheusrule 'gitops-operator-argocd-alerts' in the namespace of the argocd instance For example: $ oc edit prometheusrule-n openshift-gitops Change the line that looks like below: expr: argocd_app_info{namespace="openshift-gitops",sync_status="OutOfSync"} > 0 set it to be > 1 [RFE-6981](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-6981) is raised for an autonomous solution on this.

title: Ghost pod in list of jgroups clustering in Openshift 4
issue: - There is a pod being listed on the jgroups channel that doesn't exist anymore- Pod that was already deleted still listed as jgroups members- No physical address for unknown pod uid
resolution: Usually, a jgroups member being listed still, it means the JVM still working, therefore the container still running. ### Scenario 1- DNS still has the IP record Given the fact the DNS only keeps IPs record, not the JVM in fact running, so then DNS would just gives it a list of potential cluster members. If nothing was running on those IP:port then there wouldn't be any issue. This scenario therefore the pod IPs would be given but no member would_de facto_ join the cluster. ### Scenario 2- container is running but kubelet does not know about it In case of a misconfigured scenario, where the kubelet is not aware of the container still running so then there could be alternatives such as:- Draining the OCP Node: `$ oc drain node/NODE_NAME`- Removing the container from the ETCD list, similar to [Serverless Operator's pingsource Custom Resource is orphaned](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7100194)- Restarting the OCP Node ### Scenario 3- pods are in another namespace In case pods are in a separated namespace but misconfigured in terms of jgroups, so then jgroups would allow them to join the cluster. The jgroup's service would need to be directly wrong/misconfigured to allow that. Jgroups would still allow any member to join, no restriction is placed for joining a cluster, by default. However, jgropus can be set with AUTH, via OCP image's variable for configuring AUTH, see the solution [EAP 7 image clustering in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6980435).
root_cause: Usually, a jgroups member being listed still, it means the JVM still working, therefore the container still running.

title: Unable to add CD-ROM or Disk to existing VM from URL
issue: Option to add disk/cd-rom from URL is missing after upgrading to OpenShift Virtualization 4.17 or later
resolution: * Manually create a DataVolume from URL and once it is Ready attach it to the VM as an existing Volume: ~~~ apiVersion: cdi.kubevirt.io/v1beta1 kind: DataVolume metadata: name: my-iso namespace: my-namespace spec: source: http: url: http://webserver.example.com/iso/my-iso.iso storage: resources: requests: storage: 15Gi ~~~
root_cause: * The option to add new disk to existing VM from URL was removed from version 4.17. This is because any typo or problem with downloading the disk would make the VirtualMachine get stuck in Provisioning state requiring manual intervention to fix, which can cause extended downtime.
