title: Ceph MGR Log contains `[errno 39] RBD image has snapshots (error deleting image from trash)`
issue: - MGR logs contain `[errno 39] RBD image has snapshots (error deleting image from trash)`- Images moved to trash are not deleted.
resolution: 1. Identify the pools and images from the log output. In ODF deployments with internal ceph you would see this in the logs for the MGR pod or in ODF mustgathers. For pure ceph or external ceph you can use the journal logs of the active MGR. > ⓘ For the following command the `jq` package needs to be installed. # sudo journalctl--no-pager | grep-Eo '\{.*image_id": "([^"]*)".*\[errno 39\][^}]*\}' | jq-r '[.message, "Pool:" +.refs.pool_name, "ImageID:" +.refs.image_id,.retry_messge] | @tsv' | column-t-s $'\t' | sort-u Removing image pool1/7e1eb6d196b648 from trash Pool:pool1 ImageID:7e1eb6d196b648 Removing image pool1/c421ae66f83239 from trash Pool:pool1 ImageID:c421ae66f83239 Removing image pool2/511cbd97ee63a2 from trash Pool:pool2 ImageID:511cbd97ee63a2 Removing image pool2/58e14b89ae7146 from trash Pool:pool2 ImageID:58e14b89ae7146 Removing image pool2/a0f08b42595027 from trash Pool:pool2 ImageID:a0f08b42595027 Removing image pool3/8ada6916a40ab3 from trash Pool:pool3 ImageID:8ada6916a40ab3 Removing image pool3/8ada6921fa305e from trash Pool:pool3 ImageID:8ada6921fa305e Removing image pool4/9259ecbb50e003 from trash Pool:pool4 ImageID:2485e9757eab4 List the images from the trash for the pool. # sudo rbd trash ls--pool pool4--long ID NAME SOURCE DELETED_AT STATUS PARENT 2485e9757eab4 test USER Thu Dec 14 07:08:04 2023 expired at Thu Dec 14 07:08:04 2023 1. Get the image information from the image id. # sudo rbd info--pool pool4--image-id 2485e9757eab4 rbd image 'test': size 10 GiB in 2560 objects order 22 (4 MiB objects) snapshot_count: 1 id: 2485e9757eab4 block_name_prefix: rbd_data.2485e9757eab4 format: 2 features: layering, exclusive-lock, object-map, fast-diff, deep-flatten op_features: flags: create_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 05:43:51 2023 access_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 05:43:51 2023 modify_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 05:43:51 2023 1. List the snapshots for the image. # sudo rbd snap ls--pool pool4--image-id 2485e9757eab4 SNAPID NAME SIZE PROTECTED TIMESTAMP 4 test-snapshot 10 GiB yes Thu Dec 14 05:45:21 2023 If the snapshots are unprotected, you could remove them now: # sudo rbd snap rm--pool pool4--image-id 2485e9757eab4--snap test-snapshot Removing snap: 100% complete...done. After removing the snapshots you can then remove the image from the trash: # sudo rbd trash remove--pool pool4--image-id 2485e9757eab4 In the case above however, the snapshot is protected, so needs to be unprotect first. # sudo rbd snap unprotect--pool pool4--image-id 2485e9757eab4--snap test-snapshot 2023-12-14T07:29:54.231-0500 7fbffd34f640-1 librbd::SnapshotUnprotectRequest: cannot unprotect: at least 1 child(ren) [1a60296fa3437] in pool 'test-images' 2023-12-14T07:29:54.231-0500 7fbffd34f640-1 librbd::SnapshotUnprotectRequest: encountered error: (16) Device or resource busy You see the above error message if you can not unprotect it because it still has children (clones) associated. 1. List any clones for the image. To be able to list the children for the image, we have to restore it from the trash first. # sudo rbd trash restore--pool test-images--image-id 2485e9757eab4 Once it is restored, we can check the children (clones) of the image. # sudo rbd children--pool pool4--image test pool4/test-clone Looking at the clone, we see it has the image named `test` as parent set: # sudo rbd info--pool pool4--image test-clone rbd image 'test-clone2': size 10 GiB in 2560 objects order 22 (4 MiB objects) snapshot_count: 0 id: 208f75780dd8f block_name_prefix: rbd_data.208f75780dd8f format: 2 features: layering, exclusive-lock, object-map, fast-diff, deep-flatten op_features: flags: create_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 07:40:07 2023 access_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 07:40:07 2023 modify_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 07:40:07 2023 parent: test-images/test@test-snapshot overlap: 10 GiB 1. Flatten the clone. > ⚠ If the RBD clone image is consumed by multiple VMs or if the RBD image is used in high IO scenarios flattening the clone should be considered done during a Maintenace Window with the VMs stopped to not have possible IO pauses while the data is copied from the snapshot to the clone, see also [KCS 6983532](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6983532) for reference. # sudo rbd flatten--pool test-images--image test-clone Image flatten: 100% complete...done. After flattening the image has now no parent associated: # sudo rbd info--pool test-images--image test-clone rbd image 'test-clone': size 10 GiB in 2560 objects order 22 (4 MiB objects) snapshot_count: 0 id: 1a60296fa3437 block_name_prefix: rbd_data.1a60296fa3437 format: 2 features: layering, exclusive-lock, object-map, fast-diff, deep-flatten op_features: flags: create_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 05:46:52 2023 access_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 05:46:52 2023 modify_timestamp: Thu Dec 14 05:46:52 2023 1. Remove the snapshot. # sudo rbd snap unprotect--pool pool4--snap test-snapshot--image-id 2485e9757eab4 # sudo rbd snap remove--pool pool4--snap test-snapshot--image-id 2485e9757eab4 Removing snap: 100% complete...done. 1. Finally remove the image. # sudo rbd remove--pool pool4 test Removing image: 100% complete...done.
root_cause: - An RBD image with snapshots can not be deleted until the snapshot is removed.- An RBD image with a clone needs the clone to be flattened first, then the snapshot and the image can be removed.

title: Legacy clients fail to create SSL/TLS connections after upgrading to OCP 4.16
issue: - After upgrading a `FIPS`-enabled OCP cluster to 4.16, clients are unable to create secure (SSL/TLS) connections and fail with: ~~~ SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure ~~~
resolution: For more details on `openssl` client requirements for FIPS-140-3 compliant nodes, see the [relevant KB article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7018256). Note that the RHOCP ingress (HAProxy) pods come with its own set of `crypto-policies` files so updating the node's policies does not affect the ingress pod. To workaround the problem, a service type of `nodePort` can be used to bypass the HAProxy and forward traffic directly to the application pods.
root_cause: RHOCP 4.16 [uses Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9.4 packages](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes.html#ocp-4-16-rhcos_release-notes). making nodes compliant with FIPS-140-3. As a result, the `Extended Master Secret` is mandatory on TLSv1.2 connections.

title: Restart of the ovnkube-node pod results into crashloopbackoff state
issue: - Restart of the `ovnkube-node` pod results into `crashloopbackoff` state.- Additional network config should not cause `ovnkube-node` pod in `crashloopbackoff` state.
resolution: - Deleting the `NetworkAttachmentDefinition` shown in error logs of the failing container `ovnkube-controller` and restarting the respective `ovnkube-node` pod fixes the issue.- To improve the behavior so that operations like upgrade of Openshift Cluster doesn't get affected due to a config error in the NAD(`NetworkAttachmentDefinition`), the issue is also reported as a bug [OCPBUGS-53219](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-53219) towards engineering.
root_cause: The issue is observed when using `ovn-k8s-cni-overlay` for additional pod networking and when there are multiple NAD(`NetworkAttachmentDefinition`) with different configuration pointing to same `network` where `network` is the "name" under spec.config of the `NetworkAttachmentDefinition` resource.

title: Ingress, Authentication and Console Cluster Operators are degraded in AWS SNO Private cluster
issue: - `Ingress`, `Authentication` and `Console` Cluster Operators are in `Degraded` state.- The issue occurs when installing the Cluster as `Single Node` Openshift cluster in `Private` Subnet.
resolution: Using `Classic` Loadbalancer instead of `Network` Loadbalancer on AWS for publishing the `IngressController` in the Openshift Cluster fixes the issue. Example: $ cat clb.yaml apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: IngressController metadata: creationTimestamp: null name: default namespace: openshift-ingress-operator spec: endpointPublishingStrategy: loadBalancer: dnsManagementPolicy: Managed providerParameters: aws: classicLoadBalancer: connectionIdleTimeout: 0s type: Classic type: AWS scope: Internal type: LoadBalancerService $ oc replace--force--wait-f clb.yaml ingresscontroller.operator.openshift.io "default" deleted ingresscontroller.operator.openshift.io/default replaced
root_cause: - NLB(`Network` Loadbalancer) in AWS doesn't support `hairpinning` of requests. When the targets are registered by instance ID, the source IP addresses of clients are preserved. When connection to the NLB from the backend is tried, a loopback is created and this is not allowed by the NLB as the `source` and `destination` address is the same and the connection times out.- If an instance is a client of an internal load balancer that is registered by instance ID, the connection succeeds only if the request is routed to a `different instance`.- Considering above two points, If the cluster is of type `SNO`(Single Node Openshift Cluster) and NLB loadbalancer has scope: `Internal` the issue being faced is expected. ~~~ $ oc get ingresscontroller default-n openshift-ingress-operator-o yaml|grep-A8 endpointPublishingStrategy endpointPublishingStrategy: loadBalancer: dnsManagementPolicy: Managed providerParameters: aws: type: NLB type: AWS scope: Internal type: LoadBalancerService ~~~

title: Unknown DNS  Zone Transfer Requests from Red Hat Openshift Cluster
issue: - The client's `security` team has identified some `Zone Transfer` requests that are originating from the `OpenShift Nodes`.- The requests are originating from the `Openshift Nodes` and being directed to `upstream` DNS servers. This behavior happens randomly and doesn't show a particular pattern.
resolution: - Collect `tcpdump` from the Openshift Node sending the DNS `Zone Transfer` request to the `upstream` DNS. Below command can be used for same: ~~~ $ oc get nodes $ oc debug-t node/${NODE_NAME} $ FILENAME="/host/var/tmp/${HOSTNAME}$(date +%d%m_%Y-%H_%M_%S-%Z).pcap" $ tcpdump-nni any port 53 or 5353-W 10-C 100-w ${FILENAME} where,-C captured file size in MB-W Used in conjunction with the-C option, this will limit the number of files created to the specified number and begin overwriting files from the beginning, thus creating a ’rotating’ buffer. In addition, it will name the files with enough leading 0s to support the maximum number of files allowing them to sort correctly. ~~~- In the pcap collected, Look for `zone transfer` request(`dns.qry.type == 252`).- Analyzing the same, The device can be identified which sends the `Zone Transfer` request to `Openshift Node` and then the same request gets forwarded to the `upstream` DNS server.

title: Unable to see observability metrics for local-cluster in RHACM
issue: - Unable to see observability metrics for local-cluster in RHACM
resolution: Redeploy observability bysetting multicluster-observability to false in MCH, remove the open-cluster-management-observability namespace and re-enable MCH multicluster-observability. The details of the step are located in the observability documentation under "removing observability" and "enabling observability service". Removing the namespace is necessary to re-enable observability; the content of the thanos storage should not be affected.
root_cause: the hub-info-secret is missing and the other error prevents reconciliation of it from being possible.

title: In OpenShift, after a power outage, multiple cluster nodes appear as `NotReady`
issue: - The environment suffered a power outage. On power recovery multiple cluster nodes are marked as `NotReady`.
resolution: - Perform a full power cycle of all the VMs. A reboot may not work:- Power off the VM.- Start the VM.- Use a rolling method when powering cycle multiple VMs, i.e., one at a time, and wait for the node to be `Ready` before moving to the next.- When performing the power cycle of multiple VMs, use the order:- Control plane nodes.- Storage nodes.- Infra nodes.- All the other nodes.- If the cluster is partially working: 1. Take note of the VMs marked as `Ready`. 2. Start the procedure with the `NotReady` VMs. 3. When all the VMs are `Ready`, to be thorough, repeat the procedure with the VMs that were `Ready` in point 1.- If after a power cycle a node does not recover, the VM may have been corrupted by the abrupt power outage. Replace the cluster node.
root_cause: The root cause in unknown at this time, pointing to the underlying layers of the infrastructure.

title: Performance addons operator advanced configuration
issue: Advanced configuration instructions dedicated to field and performance teams for applying advanced tuning settings which are not the default latency sensitive workloads portfolio performance addons operator provides.
resolution: ### Advanced Configuration This is an advanced guide for changing low level performance configuration on a cluster to hotfix an issue or test impact. Instructions for editing (add/remove/change) kernel arguments, sysfs, proc parameters and are described in this section. ### Default tuning Default tuning applied with the [openshift-performance](https://github.com/openshift-kni/performance-addon-operators/blob/master/build/assets/tuned/openshift-node-performance) base profile, it is the base for creating a Tuned CR that would be detected by [cluster node tuning operator](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-node-tuning-operator) and finally be executed by [tuned](https://github.com/redhat-performance/tuned). ### Additional kernel arguments When creating a [performance profile CR](https://github.com/openshift-kni/performance-addon-operators/blob/master/config/samples/performance_v2_performanceprofile.yaml), a default set of kernel arguments are created from the [openshift-performance](https://github.com/openshift-kni/performance-addon-operators/blob/master/build/assets/tuned/openshift-node-performance) base profile in addition to tuned generated argument and can include for example: ~~~ nohz=on rcu_nocbs= tuned.non_isolcpus= intel_pstate=disable nosoftlockup tsc=nowatchdog intel_iommu=on iommu=pt systemd.cpu_affinity= isolcpus= default_hugepagesz= hugepagesz= hugepages= ~~~ **Note**: isolcpus is added only when [balanceIsolated](https://github.com/openshift-kni/performance-addon-operators/blob/master/docs/performance_profile.md#cpu) is disabled. Additional kernel arguments could be added in the performance profile CR using the `additionalKernelArgs` field: ~~~ apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v1 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: example-performanceprofile spec: additionalKernelArgs:- "nmi_watchdog=0"- "audit=0"- "mce=off"- "processor.max_cstate=1"- "idle=poll"- "intel_idle.max_cstate=0"... ~~~ **Note**: These arguments will be added on top of the default arguments mentioned above. Editing these additional arguments could be done when editing the CR. **Note**: This should be used for simple additions, for more complex operations see the following custom tunings section. ### Additional Kubelet Arguments To avoid `KubeletConfig` custom resource limitation, we introduced the experimental kubelet config snippet annotation `kubeletconfig.experimental`. It gives you a way to configure an additional set of kubelet parameters on top of the `KubeletConfig` custom resource generated by the performance-addon-operator. But take into account that it is the experimental feature, and we do not have any validations for the kubelet config snippet that you will provide under the annotation, so please make sure to set only parameters specified under the [v1beta1 specification](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kubelet-config.v1beta1/). Also, by default, the performance-addon-operator will override: 1. CPU manager policy 2. CPU manager reconcile period 3. Topology manager policy 4. Reserved CPUs 5. Memory manager policy Please avoid specifying them and use the relevant API to configure these parameters. To update the KubeletConfig CR, you should pass the `KubeletConfig` v1beta1 snippet in the json format, for example: ~~~ apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v2 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: unsafe-sysctl-performanceprofile annotations: kubeletconfig.experimental: | {"allowedUnsafeSysctls":["net.core.somaxconn"]} spec:... ~~~ ### Custom tuning To perform hotfixes on top of the tuned [openshift-performance](https://github.com/openshift-kni/performance-addon-operators/blob/master/build/assets/tuned/openshift-node-performance) base profile, a tuned custom profile (A child profile) will be used to apply the desired changes. This profile will inherit the base tuned profile and override its fields where needed. For complete details about customizing tuned see: [Customizing Tuned profiles](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/monitoring_and_managing_system_status_and_performance/customizing-tuned-profiles_monitoring-and-managing-system-status-and-performance). #### Getting the current deployed tuned profile In order to apply changes we will need to get the name of the deployed tuned profile that was generated by the performance addon operator: ~~~ #oc describe performanceprofile | grep Tuned Tuned: / ~~~ Any tuned profile created for custom tuning **will need to inherit** from this tuned profile: `include= ` The custom Tuned CR should be under the same tuned namespace: ~~~ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name:... namespace: ~~~ For example: ~~~ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: configuration-hotfixes namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=... # override performance addons generated tuned profile include=openshift-node-performance-manual recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: "worker-cnf" priority: 19 profile: configuration-hotfixes ~~~ **Important:** The Tuned CR created for custom configuration must take precedence over the existing one. To do so- its priority under the [recommend](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-node-tuning-operator#recommended-profiles) section must be a lower number than the existing tuned CR (lower number = higher priority). ### Example use case #1 #### Initial performance profile ~~~ performance_profile.yaml apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v1 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: manual spec: additionalKernelArgs:- "nmi_watchdog=0"- "audit=0"- "mce=off"- "processor.max_cstate=1"- "idle=poll"- "intel_idle.max_cstate=0" cpu: isolated: "1-3" reserved: "0" hugepages: defaultHugepagesSize: "1G" pages:- size: "1G" count: 1 node: 0 realTimeKernel: enabled: true numa: topologyPolicy: "single-numa-node" nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker-cnf: "" ~~~ Example of the kernel arguments generated after initial profile deployment: ~~~ sh-4.2# cat /proc/cmdline BOOT_IMAGE=(hd0,gpt1)/ostree/rhcos-35750ad692eb3cc24529d0bc23857ad3cc29340d39912b43e3a40d255f05f740/vmlinuz-4.18.0-147.8.1.rt24.101.el8_1.x86_64 rhcos.root=crypt_rootfs console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200n8 rd.luks.options=discard ostree=/ostree/boot.1/rhcos/35750ad692eb3cc24529d0bc23857ad3cc29340d39912b43e3a40d255f05f740/0 ignition.platform.id=gcp skew_tick=1 nmi_watchdog=0 audit=0 mce=off processor.max_cstate=1 `**idle=poll**` intel_idle.max_cstate=0 nohz=on rcu_nocbs=1-3 tuned.non_isolcpus=00000001 intel_pstate=disable nosoftlockup default_hugepagesz=1G tsc=nowatchdog intel_iommu=on iommu=pt systemd.cpu_affinity=0 ~~~ **Note**: check /proc/cmdline on the nodes to get the current kernel arguments list. ##### Removing kernel argument ~~~ oc create-f- < <_EOF_ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: configuration-hotfixes namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Configuration changes profile inherited from performance created tuned include=openshift-node-performance-manual [bootloader] cmdline_removeKernelArgs=-idle=poll name: openshift-configuration-hotfixes recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: "worker-cnf" priority: 19 profile: openshift-configuration-hotfixes_EOF_ ~~~ The kernel argument is now removed: ~~~ sh-4.2# cat /proc/cmdline | grep "idle=poll" sh-4.2# ~~~ ### Example use case #2 #### Initial performance profile ~~~ performance_profile.yaml apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v2 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: PerformanceProfile spec: additionalKernelArgs:- "intel_pstate=passive" cpu: reserved: 0,56,28,84 isolated: 1-27,29-55,57-83,85-111 machineConfigPoolSelector: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/master: "" workloadHints: highPowerConsumption: false realTime: true perPodPowerManagement: false realTimeKernel: enabled: false ~~~ Example of the kernel arguments generated after initial profile deployment: ~~~ sh-4.2# cat /proc/cmdline BOOT_IMAGE=(hd1,gpt3)/ostree/rhcos-b5628a9a54e131c37c605e9ccd23096a45739da417b0f3be4318a0e330b339d4/vmlinuz-5.14.0-284.86.1.el9_2.x86_64 ignition.platform.id=metal ostree=/ostree/boot.0/rhcos/b5628a9a54e131c37c605e9ccd23096a45739da417b0f3be4318a0e330b339d4/0 root=UUID=2bccb2df-9539-4375-a1b6-92c76e0e8687 rw rootflags=prjquota boot=UUID=9b942f8c-0165-4858-ad6f-f69f3516faf8 skew_tick=1 tsc=reliable rcupdate.rcu_normal_after_boot=1 nohz=on rcu_nocbs=1-27,29-55,57-83,85-111 tuned.non_isolcpus=00100000,01000000,10000001 systemd.cpu_affinity=0,56,28,84 intel_iommu=on iommu=pt isolcpus=managed_irq,1-27,29-55,57-83,85-111 nohz_full=1-27,29-55,57-83,85-111 tsc=reliable nosoftlockup nmi_watchdog=0 mce=off skew_tick=1 rcutree.kthread_prio=11 intel_pstate=passive intel_pstate=disable systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0 systemd.legacy_systemd_cgroup_controller=1 ~~~ **Note**: check /proc/cmdline on the nodes to get the current kernel arguments list.The **nohz_full** kernel argument is set by default in Openshift 4.14 when PerformanceProfile workloadHints includes **realTime: true**. ##### Removing **nohz_full** kernel argument ~~~ oc create-f- < <_EOF_ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: configuration-hotfixes namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Configuration changes profile inherited from performance created tuned include=openshift-node-performance-manual [bootloader] cmdline_remove_nohzfull=-nohz_full=${isolated_cores} name: openshift-configuration-hotfixes recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: "worker-cnf" priority: 19 profile: openshift-configuration-hotfixes_EOF_ ~~~ The kernel argument is now removed: ~~~ sh-4.2# cat /proc/cmdline | grep "nohz_full" sh-4.2# ~~~ ### Changing sysctl values ~~~ sh-4.2# sysctl-n kernel.hung_task_timeout_secs 600 sh-4.2# sysctl-n kernel.nmi_watchdog 0 sh-4.2# sysctl-n kernel.sched_rt_runtime_us-1 ~~~ ~~~ oc create-f- < <_EOF_ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: configuration-hotfixes namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Configuration changes profile inherited from performance created tuned include=openshift-node-performance-manual [sysctl] kernel.hung_task_timeout_secs = 700 # change value from 600 to 700 kernel.nmi_watchdog= # set empty value kernel.sched_rt_runtime_us=- # try removal name: openshift-configuration-hotfixes recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: "worker-cnf" priority: 19 profile: openshift-configuration-hotfixes_EOF_ ~~~ Verification: ~~~ sh-4.2# sysctl-n kernel.hung_task_timeout_secs 700 sh-4.2# sysctl-n kernel.nmi_watchdog 0 sh-4.2# sysctl-n kernel.sched_rt_runtime_us 950000 ~~~ ## RPS settings The default RPS settings for a performance profile are to set the RPS mask as the reserved CPUs, on the host level for all network devices excluding virtual(veth) devices and physical devices(pci) and on the container level for all virtual network devices(veth). ### RPS and workload hints (Openshift 4.12 and above) When the realtime workload hint is explicitly disabled there is no need for any RPS settings to be applied since it is relevant only for the realtime use case. The following will result in no RPS settings applied on the cluster at all: ~~~ performance_profile.yaml apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v2 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: example-performanceprofile spec: workloadHints: realTime: false ~~~ In special cases where there is a need to explicitly specify the realtime workload hint as false but keep the RPS settings, an override annotation `performance.openshift.io/enable-rps` could be added to the performance profile that will keep the default RPS settings: ~~~ performance_profile.yaml apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v2 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: example-performanceprofile annotations: performance.openshift.io/enable-rps: "true" spec: workloadHints: realTime: false ~~~ ### Enable RPS on physical devices annotation (Openshift 4.11 and above) In case there is a need to set RPS mask for physical(pci) devices as well on the host side an override annotation `performance.openshift.io/enable-physical-dev-rps` to the default RPS settings could be added to the performance profile: ~~~ performance_profile.yaml apiVersion: performance.openshift.io/v2 kind: PerformanceProfile metadata: name: example-performanceprofile annotations: performance.openshift.io/enable-physical-dev-rps: "true" ~~~ **Note**: `performance.openshift.io/enable-physical-dev-rps` annotation can be applied only when realtime workload hint is NOT explicitly set to false unless `performance.openshift.io/enable-rps` is set to true.
root_cause: The Performance Operator optimizes OpenShift clusters for applications sensitive to CPU and network latency. The operator consumes a PerformanceProfile CRD that offers high level options for applying various performance tunings to cluster node. These tunings are based on an underlying tuned profile that holds default configurations that are best suited for sensitive low latency workloads but there are **cases where extensible functionality is needed**. The target audience for this advanced solution are field and performance teams that test alternative settings before having to implement them.

title: vSphere node is unable to find UUID during agent based cluster installation in RHOCP4
issue: - Node is not able to get a UUID inside the cluster but the UUID has been allotted to the VM in the vSphere during agent based installation.
resolution: - Remove the `uninitialized` `NoSchedule` taint: ~~~ $ oc adm taint node node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized=true:NoSchedule- ~~~- Add the label `beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type: ` to the respective node as below: ~~~ $ oc label node beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type: ~~~- Add the `providerID` in the nodes that is present on the VM running on vSphere: ~~~ $ oc edit node ~~~

title: Is It Possible to Install the AWS EFS CSI Driver Operator on Non-AWS Clusters in RHOCP 4?
issue: - Can not Install the AWS EFS CSI Driver Operator on Non-AWS Clusters
resolution: The AWS EFS CSI Driver Operator requires the cluster to be deployed with AWS cloud provider integration enabled.

title: ArgoCD unable to connect with public repo
issue: ArgoCD is unable to connect to a public repository
resolution: Check that the required parameters are configured properly while connecting to the public repository from the ArgoCD UI:- The repository URL should be correct. For testing, one of the example apps from the [ArgoCD Example Apps](https://github.com/argoproj/argocd-example-apps) repo can be used.- Select and add the correct Kubernetes/configured clustered url. For example, the default URL for the local cluster is `kubernetes.default.svc`.- The credentials are not mandatory for adding to the public repository.
root_cause: Invalid parameter configuration will lead to ArgoCD failing to connect the requisite repositories to synchronize deployed applications.

title: OCP4: Migration from SDN to OVN is stalled, Operators degraded, API services unavailable
issue: - During your migration from SDN to OVN-kubernetes, you may experience an outage if proceeding with the [offline migration method outlined in the documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/networking/ovn-kubernetes-network-plugin#nw-ovn-kubernetes-migration_migrate-from-openshift-sdn) and after applying the last patch in step 10 (or similar): ~~~ oc patch Network.config.openshift.io cluster \--type='merge'--patch '{"spec": {"networkType": "OVNKubernetes"}}' ~~~- Cluster may be degraded, with API unavailable: `oc` commands delayed or unavailable- Nodes may be in NOTREADY state- Cluster console may be unavailable- Cluster Operators may be in various states of degraded
resolution: - After step 6 in the docs, all nodes will set an updated machine-configuration state. All nodes must undergo a reboot after this step, and after redeploying multus [as outlined in the documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/networking/ovn-kubernetes-network-plugin#:~:text=%20to%20complete%20changing%20the%20network%20plugin%2C%20reboot%20each%20node%20in%20your%20cluster.%20you%20can%20reboot%20the%20nodes%20in%20your%20cluster%20with%20either%20of%20the%20following%20approaches%3A%20). This reboot step is not optional, and the cluster will remain degraded until completed. ~~~ To complete changing the network plugin, reboot each node in your cluster. You can reboot the nodes in your cluster with either of the following approaches: NOTE: Cluster Operators will not work correctly before you reboot the nodes. ~~~- Check the below Diagnostics steps outlined below to validate that you have reached this `split-tunnel` state, then reboot all nodes in the cluster manually to allow the platform to stabilize. Issues with operators, ETCD quorum, console, authentication will all be cleared after nodes restart successfully into OVN-kubernetes.
root_cause: - During the offline migration, After patching the nodes to the OVNkubernetes network type and rolling out the multus pods, the cluster will immediately degrade until all nodes are restarted.- All nodes are in a half-way split-tunneled state where they are now expecting new traffic requests to arrive via the geneve_sys_6081 tunnel interface between peers. Traffic flow will be interrupted, as we are holding on to both SDN and OVN traffic configuration states.- In order to recover, a reboot into the latest machine-configuration template is required, which will clear SDN tunnel states, and deploy ovnkubernetes network configurations properly.- Failing to restart the nodes (due to Pod Disruption Budgets, script failures, or errors in executing the required reboot step), will result in the cluster remaining in a degraded state until this is completed.- ETCD quorum loss is possible/expected during this timeframe- and you should proceed to restart in order to allow the cluster to restore services.

title: Error "failed to unmarshal status response" when upgrading ODF on IBM Z Platforms
issue: ODF upgrade on IBM Z results in CephCluster CR with the message ```failed to unmarshal status response: json``` ``` $ oc get cephcluster-o yaml | grep message-A2 message: 'failed to unmarshal status response: json: cannot unmarshal number 10997917846272475136 into Go struct field.fsmap.by_rank.gid of type int' severity: Urgent health: HEALTH_ERR ```

title: RHACM search-collector in open-cluster-management namespace getting Warnings in events
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: The `open-cluster-management` namespace has Events indicating the warning "FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret"
Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (`search-pull-secret`); attempting to pull the image may not succeed
resolution: The issue is known and tracked in [ACM-15056](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-15056), which is resolved in errata for the ACM operator: [RHSA-2024:11381](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:11381) for v2.11.4, and [RHSA-2025:0851](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:0851) for v2.12.2. Upgrading to either of these will resolve this issue. Without upgrading, the issue may be resolved by manually creating the missing Secret: ~~~ $ DOCKER_CONFIG_JSON=`oc extract secret/pull-secret-n openshift-config--to=-` oc create secret generic search-pull-secret \-n open-cluster-management \--from-literal=.dockerconfigjson="$DOCKER_CONFIG_JSON" \--type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson ~~~
root_cause: The issue is due to installing Search via OperatorHub, which has since resolved in ACM via [ACM-15056](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-15056). When installed this way, the installation will look for the non-existant Secret `search-pull-secret`. It has no effects in the cluster outside of issuing an Event warning the user of the missing Secret.

title: Install and Execute the GNU Debugger (GDB) to Analyze CephFS Volume Operations OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: In some instances, such as further research when hitting a bug it may be necessary to deploy a tool such as the GNU Debugger (GDB) to analyze CephFS Volume Operations. This will allow for a more verbose outlook of volume operations to be analyzed. For example, this particular solution was used to understand why a CephFS PV clone was failing, and the information provided to Engineering. **Related Articles:*

[Ceph MDS Troubleshooting- Gather All of the Necessary Logs/Data- OpenShift Data Foundations](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7031034) [Ceph Data Capture Scripts in Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation (RHODF)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7041409)
resolution: 1. Install the `rook-ceph-tools` pod by following the [Configuring the Rook-Ceph Toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891) solution. 2. Capture the active MDS: ~~~ $ oc exec-n openshift-storage deployment/rook-ceph-tools-- ceph fs status ~~~ 3. Annotate the node name the active MDS is scheduled on. This will be the node where the data will be if the clone process restarts the pod (the pod may or may not restart). ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage-o wide | grep mds ~~~ 4. From the output of step 2, rsh into the active mds pod and install gStack (gdb) tool: ~~~ $ oc rsh-n openshift-storage $ microdnf install gdb-y ~~~ 5. While still inside the active mds pod, start the gstack collection script: ~~~ gstack_dir="/var/log/ceph/gstack_dir";mkdir-p ${gstack_dir};COUNTER=0; while [$COUNTER-lt 3600]; do gstack `pidof ceph-mds` > > ${gstack_dir}/gstack.`hostname-s`.$(date +%F_%H-%M-%S).log; let COUNTER=COUNTER+60; sleep 60; done /var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/log ~~~ **Note: The command above will begin collecting data. Leave that terminal window open and perform the next steps in a separate terminal window.** 6. Perform the CephFS operation that was previously failing (e.g. pv clone), which fails and causes active MDS to become degraded, crash (respawn/unresponsive), etc. **NOTE:** Kindly note down the time at which the operation was executed and specify if time is local or UTC/Zulu. 7. Wait for 25 minutes after active mds changes to standby mds. You can see this by running one of the following commands: ~~~ $ oc exec-n openshift-storage deployment/rook-ceph-tools-- ceph mds stat $ oc exec-n openshift-storage deployment/rook-ceph-tools-- ceph fs status ~~~ 8. Stop the gstack command with `ctrl+c` in the original CLI terminal window, which was started in step [5]. The data will be located in the `/var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/log/gstack_dir` from the node the earlier active mds pod was scheduled on shown in step [3]. 9. Debug/SSH into each storage node and provide a compressed tarball of the `var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/log` along with `/var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/crash` directories from all storage nodes as well. **Example:** ~~~ $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host $ tar czvf /tmp/-logs.tar.gz /var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/log $ tar czvf /tmp/-crash-dir.tar.gz /var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/crash ~~~ 9. Collect ODF must-gather and provide it to the support case along with data collected in step [9].

title: NVIDIA Cuda Validator Pod Crashes
issue: When using the NVIDIA GPU Operator on OpenShift 4.16.32 with a Grace Hopper node where a performance profile has also been applied to the system the nvidia-cuda-validator pod may go into a crashloop state.
resolution: The solution to the issue is to apply an additional patch for tuned to remove iommu.passthrough which is not support on Grace Hopper and enable the stalld service. The patch below will provide those requirements when applied to the system. ~~~ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: performance-patch namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Configuration changes profile inherited from performance created tuned include=openshift-node-performance-openshift-node-performance-profile [bootloader] cmdline_iommu_arm=-iommu.passthrough=1 [service] service.stalld=start,enable name: performance-patch recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master priority: 19 profile: performance-patch ~~~ Once the performance-patch is applied and the system reboots the nvidia-cuda-validator should go to a completed state: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n nvidia-gpu-operator NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE gpu-feature-discovery-mn8j9 1/1 Running 0 21h gpu-operator-64fbfb7fd8-vld5r 1/1 Running 1 2d18h nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset-4htpl 1/1 Running 0 21h nvidia-cuda-validator-69fq4 0/1 Completed 5 (2m19s ago) 5m12s nvidia-dcgm-2d2h6 1/1 Running 0 21h nvidia-dcgm-exporter-sqk4v 1/1 Running 2 (21h ago) 21h nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset-dxv96 1/1 Running 0 21h nvidia-driver-daemonset-416.94.202501220853-0-zg5j2 3/3 Running 0 21h nvidia-mig-manager-kgnqt 1/1 Running 0 21h nvidia-node-status-exporter-492xn 1/1 Running 0 21h nvidia-operator-validator-7gsq5 1/1 Running 193 (5m54s ago) 21h ~~~

title: Operator index image gets CrashLoop with "cache requires rebuild: cache reports digest as xxx, but computed digest is yyy" in OpenShift
issue: - Operator index image gets CrashLoop with `cache requires rebuild: cache reports digest as \"xxx\", but computed digest is \"yyy\"` in OpenShift ~~~ oc logs-f redhat-operator-index-t7svb time="2023-04-20T05:24:15Z" level=fatal msg="cache requires rebuild: cache reports digest as \"xxx\", but computed digest is \"yyy\"" ~~~
resolution: * If the cluster is connected to Internet and the index image is pulled from Red Hat registry.redhat.io, please open a support case to Red Hat. * If the cluster is disconnected to Internet and you used the `oc-mirror` to sync the images and build the index image, please make sure the latest oc-mirror tool is used. * If the cluster is disconnected to Internet and you are using the latest `oc-mirror`, then please make sure the index image in your own registry is not corrupted. To quickly verify this, the user could consider to simply compare the size of the index image on another connected server by pulling the corresponding index image. Normally if you see the index image size is smaller in your own registry, it means the index image in your own registry is corrupted and needs to be synced again.
root_cause: * index image has a pre injected digest value when the image is built to make sure the cache is consistent after the image is pulled. * In index Pod there is an `initContainer` which is responsible to copy the cache content from the image to the emptyDir volume. * As the `container` of the index Pod, when the `opm` container starts, the `opm` will calculate the cache digest which has been copied to the emptyDir. If the computed digest doesn't match the value that has been injected during the build, then the `opm` will report the error `cache requires rebuild: cache reports digest as \"xxx\", but computed digest is \"yyy\"` * For oc-mirror bugs have been fixed to improve cache build issue. Here are the links and versions in details: 4.13- [OCPBUGS-12257 Catalogs rebuilt by oc-mirror are in crashloop: cache is invalid](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-12257). 4.14- [OCPBUGS-12236 Catalogs rebuilt by oc-mirror are in crashloop: cache is invalid](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-12236). 4.16- [OCPBUGS-38035 A better fix has been merged for cache requires rebuild: cache reports digest as](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-38035).

title: How to access noVNC Web Console for VMs in OpenShift Virtualization?
issue: Unable to access VM web console using a separate URL in OpenShift Virtualization.
Desire to configure web console access similar to noVNC in OpenStack or Red Hat Virtualization.
How to configure noVNC console for VMs in Openshift Virtualization?
resolution: * Create a NodePort service in desired namespace: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: virtvnc namespace: my-project--- kind: ClusterRoleBinding apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: virtvnc subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: virtvnc namespace: my-project roleRef: kind: ClusterRole name: virtvnc apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io--- kind: ClusterRole apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: virtvnc rules:- apiGroups:- subresources.kubevirt.io resources:- virtualmachineinstances/console- virtualmachineinstances/vnc verbs:- get- apiGroups:- kubevirt.io resources:- virtualmachines- virtualmachineinstances- virtualmachineinstancepresets- virtualmachineinstancereplicasets- virtualmachineinstancemigrations verbs:- get- list- watch--- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: labels: app: virtvnc name: virtvnc namespace: my-project spec: ports:- port: 8001 protocol: TCP targetPort: 8001 selector: app: virtvnc type: NodePort--- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: virtvnc namespace: my-project spec: replicas: 1 selector: matchLabels: app: virtvnc template: metadata: labels: app: virtvnc spec: serviceAccountName: virtvnc nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/master: '' tolerations:- key: "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" operator: "Equal" value: "" effect: "NoSchedule" containers:- name: virtvnc image: quay.io/samblade/virtvnc:v0.1 livenessProbe: httpGet: port: 8001 path: / scheme: HTTP failureThreshold: 30 initialDelaySeconds: 30 periodSeconds: 10 successThreshold: 1 timeoutSeconds: 5 ~~~ * Apply the configuration: ~~~ $ oc apply-f virtVNC.yaml ~~~ * Get node port of virtvnc service ~~~ $ oc get svc-n my-project virtvnc ~~~ * Now visit following url in browser ~~~ http://NODEIP:NODEPORT/ ~~~ * If you want manager virtual machines in other namespace, you can specify namespace using query param namespace like following: ~~~ http://NODEIP:NODEPORT/?namespace=my-project ~~~

title: [MTV] Failed to migrate VMs configured with LUKS/vmdk in Openshift Virtualization.
issue: Migration process has been unsuccessful due to guest conversion running virt-v2v with an error: ~~~ commandrvf: cryptsetup luksUUID /dev/sdaX libguestfs: trace: v2v: luks_uuid = "1axxxxcc-xxxx-4aeb-xxxx-3cxx86xxxxf3" getline: Inappropriate ioctl for device virt-v2v: could not read key from user libguestfs: trace: v2v: close ~~~

title: Upgrading OpenShift Cluster (s390x) from 4.12.69 to Latest Stable Version
issue: To upgrade an OpenShift cluster (architecture: s390x) running version 4.12.69 cannot upgrade directly to a standard 4.13 release via the stable channel. The standard upgrade command `# oc adm upgrade` shows no available updates because the upgrade graph for s390x from 4.12.69 does not include a typical upgrade path to 4.13 via the stable channel.
resolution: For s390x clusters running 4.12.69, there is no upgrade path to a 4.13 release on the stable channel because:- Upgrades from 4.12.69 on s390x can only move to 4.13 via a forced upgrade using the last available 4.13.z build for s390x, which is 4.13.53.- To proceed with upgrading (with the intent to eventually move to 4.14), perform the following steps: 1. Set the Upgrade Channel to 4.14: ``` # oc adm upgrade channel stable-4.14 ``` Verify the current upgrade channe to confirm the channel is set to stable-4.14: ``` # oc adm upgrade ``` 2. Identify the Release Image for 4.13.53-s390x: Retrieve the explicit pull specification from the 4.13.53-s390x release using: ``` # oc adm release info quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.13.53-s390x | grep Pull ``` *Example output:* ``` Pull From: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@sha256:8f75e7c8e75ed81d2e6115720035307824886430fde6beb003dd0666e5f49348 ``` Note the output pull spec, ``` quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@sha256:8f75e7c8e75ed81d2e6115720035307824886430fde6beb003dd0666e5f49348 ``` 3. Force the Upgrade to the explicit 4.13.53-s390x release: Use the upgrade command with the digest-based pull spec: ``` # oc adm upgrade--allow-explicit-upgrade--to-image quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@sha256:8f75e7c8e75ed81d2e6115720035307824886430fde6beb003dd0666e5f49348 ``` This will upgrade your cluster to 4.13.53 (the last available 4.13.z build for s390x), thereby placing the cluster on a path that will support future upgrades (e.g., to 4.14). 4. Monitor the upgrade progress: ``` # oc get clusterversion ``` to verify the cluster version transitions to 4.13.53 successfully. 5. Once on 4.13.53, change the upgrade channel to stable-4.15 (or another desired channel) to enable the normal upgrade path to later versions: ``` # oc adm upgrade channel stable-4.14 ``` then proceed with any further upgrades using the standard procedure.
root_cause: The standard upgrade graph for s390x does not include a 4.13 stable release (apart from the forced path via 4.13.53) because:- The EUS releases for 4.12 are available for s390x. There are no s390x builds of the standard 4.13 versions, as the stable-4.13 release was produced only for x86_64.- Subsequent stable-4.13 releases were produced only for amd64, and due to an inadvertent build process, an additional 4.12.z was shipped for all architectures after the last 4.13 all-arch release. An accidental inclusion of a 4.12 build for s390x beyond 4.12.68 means clusters on 4.12.69 have no valid automatic upgrade path.- As a result, s390x clusters above 4.12.69 are effectively “stranded” unless an explicit upgrade to 4.13.53 is performed. The upgrade graph for s390x does not include further releases until a forced explicit upgrade is performed.- The forced upgrade to 4.13.53-s390x is a temporary workaround; once on 4.13.53, future upgrades (to 4.14 and later) will follow the standard upgrade process since they are based on RHEL9 and available across all architectures.- Consideration may be given in the future to validate a 4.13.53.1 build that could seamlessly integrate into the upgrade graph for s390x, but this would require additional validation.

issue: - Folders created by `Loki` are not removed from `S3` after they get empty.- Empty folders are seen in `S3` used by `Lokistack`.
resolution: > DISCLAIMERS > *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*- `LokiStack` is not responsible for managing or deleting empty folders in `S3`, regardless of the [retention settings](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7053212) defined in the [LokiStack CRD instance](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/logging/log-storage-4#cluster-logging-loki).- Different `S3-compatible` storage providers like [AWS S3, GCP, AZURE etc](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/logging/log-storage-4#logging-loki-storage_installing-log-storage) have different policies on handling empty folders.- Example: In [AWS S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-folders.html) folder disappears automatically when all objects inside are deleted.- If empty folders are observed in the `S3 bucket` used by `Loki`, it's recommended to consult with the `S3 provider` to explore available methods for automatically removing them.

title: How to enable HAProxy ingress router access log in Openshift 4
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Is it possible to enable HAProxy access logs in the ingress router in Openshift 4?- How to workaround ingress access logging for Openshift prior to 4.5?
resolution: > **Note:** For OSD and ROSA, refer to [Customize the ingresscontroller in OSD and ROSA](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6750161). Starting with OpenShift 4.5, enabling the ingress access logs is available as per explained in [Ingress Controller enhancements](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.5/release_notes/ocp-4-5-release-notes.html#ocp-4-5-ingress-enhancements). Refer to current documentation for [Configuring Ingress access logging](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/networking/networking-operators#nw-configure-ingress-access-logging_configuring-ingress). When configuring the `Syslog` destination (with the `.spec.logging.access.destination.type` and `.spec.logging.access.destination.syslog` fields), the `syslog` destination `port` must be `UDP`. Refer also to [Gathering HAProxy Ingress Access Logs and how to analyze them](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7063425) for additional information. > **Note:** while it is currently possible to customize the HTTP log format (via the `spec.logging.access.httpLogFormat` field), the HTTP**S** log format cannot be changed, and [RFE-3811](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3811) was created for requesting it to be customizable.

title: How to schedule all the pods of a specific namspace to designated worker nodes in RHOCP4.
issue: - How to schedule all the pods of a specific namespace to designated `workers nodes` in RHOCP4?- Restricting pod scheduling of a specific namespace to a designated `worker nodes` in RHOCP4?- How to designate the `worker nodes` to a specific namespace in RHOCP4?
resolution: **Follow below steps to designated the worker nodes to a specific namespace in RHOCP4.** 1. Create a `taint` on the designated `worker nodes` to ensure that only `pods` with the corresponding `toleration` can be scheduled on them. ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes = NoSchedule ~~~ **Example:** ~~~ $ oc adm taint nodes worker-2.example.com dedicated=app:NoSchedule ~~~ 2. Assign a unique `label` to each designated `worker node`. ~~~ $ oc label nodes/ = ~~~ 3. Assign a `node-selector` `label` to the desired `project` to control `pod` scheduling. ~~~ $ oc annotate ns openshift.io/node-selector=" = " ~~~ 4. Update the `Deployment` configuration by modifying `spec.template.spec.tolerations` to include the below `taint` `toleration` to the `pod`. ``` spec: tolerations: # <--- Add this toleration- key: # <--- Add this toleration value: # <--- Add this toleration operator: Equal # <--- Add this toleration effect: NoSchedule # <--- Add this toleration ``` 5. Ensure that all the `pods` are scheduled and running on designated `worker node`. ~~~ $ oc get pods-o wide-n NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE NODE NOMINATED NODE hello-app-2x2x8 1/1 Running 0 81s worker-2.example.com hello-app-42csw 1/1 Running 0 81s worker-2.example.com hello-app-64g6t 1/1 Running 0 80s worker-2.example.com hello-app-8bkgd 1/1 Running 0 80s worker-2.example.com hello-app-9695p 1/1 Running 0 80s worker-2.example.com hello-app-9wng8 1/1 Running 0 80s worker-2.example.com ~~~ If needed to add multiple `nodes`, repeat steps 1 and 2 for each `worker node` that needs to be added.

title: How to perform backup and restore of ETCD on single node RHOCP4 cluster.
issue: - How to perform backup and restore of ETCD on Single Node RHOCP4 cluster.
resolution: **Prerequisites:**- SSH access to a single node.- Before taking backup of etcd ensure RHOCP cluster is in healthy state. **ETCD Backup Procedure:** To create a backup of the `etcd database` on a single-node RHOCP 4 cluster, follow the steps below: 1. Use the `oc debug` command to enter the `debug` shell for the single node ~~~ $ oc debug node/ ~~~ 2. Run the `etcd-snapshot-backup.sh` backup script and pass in the location to save the `etcd` snapshot to. ~~~ $ sudo /usr/local/bin/etcd-snapshot-backup.sh./assets/backup/snapshot.db ~~~ In this example, the snapshot is saved to `./assets/backup/snapshot.db` on the single node. **ETCD Restore Procedure:** To restore the `etcd` data from a previously taken backup, follow these steps: 1. Access the single node directly using SSH as `oc debug` `pod` will disconnect during the process. ~~~ $ ssh @ ~~~ 2. Run the RHOCP cluster `cluster-restore.sh` restore script with the backup path. ~~~ $ sudo-E /usr/local/bin/cluster-restore.sh /home/core/assets/backup ~~~ 3. Restart the `kubelet` service to bring new changes into effect. ~~~ $ sudo systemctl restart kubelet.service ~~~ Wait approximately 5 minutes to allow the node and RHOCP services to come back online. **Note:**- Ensure the backup directory has sufficient space and is accessible for long-term storage.- The restore process will overwrite the existing etcd state, so it should be performed with caution and only when necessary.- Back up your cluster’s etcd data regularly and store in a secure location ideally outside the OpenShift Container Platform environment. Do not take an etcd backup before the first certificate rotation completes, which occurs 24 hours after installation, otherwise the backup will contain expired certificates. It is also recommended to take etcd backups during non-peak usage hours, as it is a blocking action.- For more details check the official Red Hat Document [Backup and restore](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.1/html/backup_and_restore/index)

title: Configure an alert to trigger when a pod restarts within a specific namespace in Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO)
issue: - Setup alerts which is triggered when pods are getting frequently restarted in one or many projects so that you can check critical production cluster pods.- Set up an alert for dns pod restarts
resolution: - As per the [ARO Support Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/support-policies-v4), Don't remove or modify the default cluster Alertmanager svc, default receiver, or any default alerting rules, except to add other receivers to notify external systems.- However adding new rule to the default cluster Alertmanager.- Create Alert-rule as below: ~~~ apiVersion: monitoring.openshift.io/v1 kind: AlertingRule metadata: name: example namespace: openshift-monitoring spec: groups:- name: example-rules rules:- alert: ExampleAlert for: 1m expr: vector(1) labels: severity: warning annotations: message: This is an example alert. ~~~- To check pod restart in openshift-dns namespace use below expression: ~~~ increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="openshift-dns", pod=~"dns-default-.*"}[5m]) > 0 ~~~ Explanation:- kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total- The Prometheus metric for the number of restarts for a container in a pod.- namespace="openshift-dns"- Filter the metric by the target namespace (openshift-dns).- pod=~"openshift-dns-default-.*"- Use regular expressions to match pod names starting with openshift-dns- default- followed by any character(s) (.* means 0 or more of any character).- Increase- Calculate the increase in restarts for pods.

DEBUG: ErrorXML: Resource: '/obc-test-noobaa-bd45a66d-045d-4cf1-a8aa-2c6644648924/file1' DEBUG: ErrorXML: RequestId: 'kvuo3ac5-28ielj-d8s' WARNING: Upload failed: /file1 (500 (InternalError): We encountered an internal error. Please try again.) WARNING: Waiting 3 sec... ~~~ **ISSUE 2:*

In ODF 4.10.6, after a backup and restore operation of noobaa DB, we can see a similar error on the noobaa-endpoint pod logs: ~~~ 2022-11-07T22:51:09.731150489Z Nov-7 22:51:09.730 [Endpoint/12] [ERROR] core.util.postgres_client:: updateOneWithClient failed {system: 6335cd3ed98f8500293a0830, bucket: 6336d4827d328300283c9ba3, content_type: 'binary/octet-stream'} {'$set': {last_write: 1667861469712, system: 6335cd3ed98f8500293a0830, bucket: 6336d4827d328300283c9ba3, content_type: 'binary/octet-stream'}, '$inc': {writes: 67779, reads: 0}} UPDATE bucketstats SET data = jsonb_set(jsonb_set(jsonb_set(jsonb_set(jsonb_set(jsonb_set(data,'{content_type}','"binary/octet-stream"'),'{bucket}','"6336d4827d328300283c9ba3"'),'{system}','"6335cd3ed98f8500293a0830"'),'{last_write}','1667861469712'::jsonb),'{reads}',to_jsonb(COALESCE(Cast(data-> > 'reads' as numeric),0)+0)),'{writes}',to_jsonb(COALESCE(Cast(data-> > 'writes' as numeric),0)+67779)) WHERE (data-> > 'system'='6335cd3ed98f8500293a0830' and data-> > 'bucket'='6336d4827d328300283c9ba3' and data-> > 'content_type'='binary/octet-stream') RETURNING_id, data AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]:_id must be unique. found 2 rows with_id=undefined in table bucketstats ~~~ Somehow the restore caused duplicate id sequences found in bucketstats tables.
resolution: Please, contact with RedHat Support and open a case to address this issue. We will need to connect to the Noobaa database and may need to delete some duplicate entries. **ISSUE 2** was analyzed in [Bug 2141035- [GSS] ODF 4.10 noobaa db restore: endpoint AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]:_id must be unique. found 2 rows with_id=undefined in table bucketstats](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2141035) and fixed in ODF 4.12 and in previous ODF versions via the following bugs: [Bug 2142337](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2142337) Fixed In Version ODF 4.11.3 [Bug 2142338](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2142338) Fixed In Version ODF 4.10.8
root_cause: - We found on the internal Postgress database used by Noobaa (located on pod `noobaa-db-pg-0`) that the were duplicate entries on two tables, `mdsequences` and `bucketstats`- This issue happened because of a race condition in noobaa code. When a user pushed data to the bucket, Noobaa created two entries in `bucketstats` with the same bucket id, system id, and content_type, and these duplicates entries still remain. This issue was [fixed](https://github.com/noobaa/noobaa-core/pull/7091) in ODF 4.13 (Noobaa 5.13.0). However, the fix does not remove the duplicate rows; it only addresses the race condition. As a result, newly created buckets (after the fix) will no longer trigger the race condition, preventing duplicate rows in bucketstats.

title: RHOCP 4 nodes have incorrect interface name showing as eth0
issue: - Network interfaces showing up as `eth0` with inconsistent altnames.- `systemd-udevd[972]: ens0f0np0: Failed to rename network interface 2 from 'eth0' to 'ens0f0np0': File exists`
resolution: Use `MachineConfig` to add the kernel argument `net.naming-scheme=v250` in order to force to use the naming scheme implemented before RHEL 9: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: name: 05-net-naming-scheme spec: kernelArguments:- net.naming-scheme=v250 ~~~ **Note**: applying the above MachineConfig will trigger a reboot of the nodes in the related MachineConfigPool.
root_cause: RHEL 9, in use from OpenShift 4.13, introduced slot-based names for PCI multifunction devices. This issue of conflic names may happens if these devices are not children of the same PCI bridge, e.g. there are multiple PCI bridges in the same slot. With [Bug RHEL-44630](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-44630) was introduced a new optional scheme available from RHEL 9.5, and can be added as kernel argument like `net.naming-scheme=rhel-9.5`.

title: Pod fails to start after Red Hat OpenShift GitOps operator upgrade in RHOCP4
issue: - Pods are failing with SCC error after upgrading Red Hat OpenShift GitOps operator to version 1.16.0.- Pod failing with error: ~~~ pods "argocd-redis-ha-server-x" is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constraint: [provider "anyuid": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider restricted-v2:.spec.securityContext.fsGroup: Invalid value: []int64{1000}: 1000 is not an allowed group, provider restricted-v2:.initContainers[0].runAsUser: Invalid value: 1000: must be in the ranges: [1000820000, 1000829999], provider restricted-v2:.containers[0].runAsUser: Invalid value: 1000: must be in the ranges: [1000820000, 1000829999], provider restricted-v2:.containers[1].runAsUser: Invalid value: 1000: must be in the ranges: [1000820000, 1000829999], provider "restricted": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "nonroot-v2": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "nonroot": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount... ~~~- ArgoCD pods are failing.
resolution: - Check the `ownerReferences` in `redis-ha-server` statefulset yaml: ~~~ $ oc get statefulset redis-ha-server-n argocd ~~~- Confirm if the stateful resource is created by ArgoCD ~~~ ownerReferences:- apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1beta1 blockOwnerDeletion: true controller: true kind: ArgoCD name: argocd ~~~- Take statefulset yaml backup: ~~~ $ oc get statefulset argocd-redis-ha-server-o yaml > backup-sfs-argocd ~~~- Delete the statefulset: ~~~ $ oc delete statefulset argocd-redis-ha-server ~~~- ArgoCD will recreate this statefulset, check if it is created: ~~~ $ oc get statefulset ~~~
root_cause: - There is a known BUG [GITOPS-6670](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-6670) that assigns a lower SecurityContextConstraints (SCC) to Redis service account in Red Hat OpenShift GitOps operator v1.16 after upgrading from v1.15 to v1.16.- Refer to the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_gitops/1.16/html/release_notes/gitops-release-notes#known-issues-1-16-0_gitops-release-notes) for more details.

title: How to configure the HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) scale up/down policy in RHOCP
issue: - How to configure the HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) scale up/down policy in RHOCP.- The HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) is not working as expected.
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* The OpenShift allows the configuration of scaling policies for the HPA to fine-tune its scale-up and scale-down behavior. These policies can be defined within the `behavior` field of the HPA object. **Define the `behavior` Field in the HPA YAML:** Within the HPA specification (`spec`), add or modify the `behavior` field. This field allows the definition of separate policies for scaling up (`scaleUp`) and scaling down (`scaleDown`). The `behavior` field structure is as follows: ```yaml spec:... behavior: scaleUp: policies:- type: Percent value: periodSeconds:- type: Pods value: periodSeconds: selectPolicy: stabilizationWindowSeconds: scaleDown: policies:- type: Percent value: periodSeconds:- type: Pods value: periodSeconds: selectPolicy: stabilizationWindowSeconds:... ``` **Explanation of Parameters:** * **`policies`:** A list of scaling policies to apply during a scale-up or scale-down event. Multiple policies can be defined. * **`type`:** The type of scaling policy. Available options are: * **`Percent`:** Specifies the maximum allowed percentage increase/decrease of replicas during the `periodSeconds`. * **`Pods`:** Specifies the maximum allowed absolute increase/decrease in the number of replicas during the `periodSeconds`. * **`value`:** The integer value associated with the `type` (e.g., the percentage or the number of pods). * **`periodSeconds`:** The duration in seconds over which the policy is considered. * **`selectPolicy`:** Determines how multiple policies within `scaleUp` or `scaleDown` are chosen. Available options are: * **`Min`:** Selects the policy that allows the smallest change in the number of replicas. * **`Max`:** Selects the policy that allows the largest change in the number of replicas. * **`Disabled`:** Disables scaling in that direction (either `scaleUp` or `scaleDown`). * **`Ordered`:** Applies the policies in the order they are defined in the `policies` list until the desired number of replicas is reached. Only the first policy that allows a change is applied in each scaling interval. * **`stabilizationWindowSeconds`:** (Optional, but highly recommended for scaleDown) Specifies the number of seconds for which past recommendations should be considered while scaling up or scaling down. * The value must be greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to 3600 (one hour). * If not set, it uses the default values:- For scale up: 0 (i.e. no stabilization is done).- For scale down: 300 (i.e. the stabilization window is 300 seconds long). **Example Configurations:** * **Slow Scale Up:** To allow a maximum of 10% increase every 5 minutes, configure: ```yaml spec:... behavior: scaleUp: policies:- type: Percent value: 10 periodSeconds: 300 selectPolicy: Max... ``` * **Gradual Scale Down:** To allow a maximum decrease of 2 pods every 2 minutes, configure: ```yaml spec:... behavior: scaleDown: policies:- type: Pods value: 2 periodSeconds: 120 selectPolicy: Max... ``` * **Combined Scale Up Policy (Apply the most restrictive):** To allow either a 5% increase every minute or a maximum of 1 pod increase every minute, whichever is smaller, configure: ```yaml spec:... behavior: scaleUp: policies:- type: Percent value: 5 periodSeconds: 60- type: Pods value: 1 periodSeconds: 60 selectPolicy: Min... ``` **Additional Considerations:** * **Metric Stability:** Ensure that the metrics the HPA is based on are stable and not prone to rapid fluctuations. Unstable metrics can lead to frequent and potentially unnecessary scaling events, even with configured policies. * **Testing:** Thoroughly test the HPA scaling policies in a non-production environment to ensure they behave as expected under different load conditions. * **Check the [desired replicas calculation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/#algorithm-details) algorithm**. By configuring the `behavior` field in the HPA object, more control can be gained over how the application scales in response to changes in resource utilization, leading to more stable and predictable resource management in the OpenShift cluster.

title: How to run an entitled build on an OCP 4 cluster?

resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Starting in OCP 4.9 (as a Tech Preview), and in OCP 4.10, it's possible to use [Simple Content Access (SCA)](https://access.redhat.com/articles/simple-content-access) for entitled builds. Please, refer to [How to Build Images with RHEL Subscriptions on OpenShift](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/how-to-build-images-with-rhel-subscriptions-on-openshift) and [Importing simple content access certificates with Insights Operator](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/support/remote_health_monitoring/insights-operator-simple-access.html) for additional information. > **Note:** The Simple Content Access (SCA) is not available for OSD/ROSA/ARO clusters. For those clusters, use the below workaround for OCP 4.9. ####Workaround for OCP 4.9 and previous versions The detailed steps to use entitled builds is covered in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 documentation: [Using Red Hat subscriptions in builds](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.6/builds/running-entitled-builds.html) (for specific version of OCP steps, it's possible to select the version from drop down menu and refer the documented steps). Additional info:- The `{ID}.pem` and `{ID}-key.pem` files referenced in the "Adding subscription entitlements as a build secret" section can be found in a subscribed RHEL machine, in directory `/etc/pki/entitlement`.- The `etc-pki-entitlement`, `rhsm-conf` and `rhsm-ca` referenced in the "Docker builds using Subscription Manager" section can be found in a subscribed RHEL machine, respectively in `/etc/pki/entitlement`, `/etc/rhsm/rhsm.conf` and `/etc/rhsm/ca/`. > **Note:** Refer to [NVIDIA gpu-operator Fails to Build Kernel](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5820151) which is written and published for dedicated steps for `nvidia gpu-operator` failing to build `kernel` using entitled builds.
root_cause: Red Hat uses the Subscription Model to allow customers to download Red Hat tested and certified Enterprise Software. This way customers are supplied with the latest patches, bug fixes, updates and upgrades.

title: Increase the default timeout of the terminal in the console in RHOCP4
issue: - How to increase default timeout of terminal in web console in RHOCP 4.- The pod or node terminal auto-closed after 15 min by default with below message. ~~~ the terminal connection has closed. ~~~
resolution: - Adding annotation to the default route won't be fruitful because that will be overridden by the Console Operator. But if a custom route is manually created that isn't managed by the Operator, we can fix it.- Red Hat reviewed the feature request in [RFE-6168](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-6168) and delivered a fix in 4.16.3 to create custom ingress. Using that feature a custom route can be created.- Please follow the below steps to achieve the same: 1. Edit the ingress and add the below lines under the spec section. ~~~ $ oc edit consoles.operator.openshift.io cluster [...] spec: ingress: consoleURL: https://your-custom-console.apps.url.com [...] ~~~ 2. Create a custom route similar to default console url, set the `timeout` and `tunnelTimeout` value as required: ~~~ apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1 kind: Route metadata: annotations: haproxy.router.openshift.io/timeout: 1h haproxy.router.openshift.io/tunnelTimeout: 8h labels: app: console name: console-custom namespace: openshift-console spec: host: port: targetPort: https tls: insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect termination: reencrypt to: kind: Service name: console weight: 100 wildcardPolicy: None ~~~ 3. Create the route using below command: ~~~ $ oc create-f custom-console.yaml ~~~
root_cause: This is an expected behaviour of the default route and is imposed by the router.

title: NFD Operator fails to upgrade from 4.14 with error "updated validation is too restrictive" in RHOCP 4

title: Ceph/ODF/OSP:  Ceph RBD Client error "kernel: rbd: rbdX: encountered watch error: -107" in kernel logs and/or dmesg.
issue: - App pods running mounting ceph-rbd PVs are left in CreateContainerError, Terminating, CrashLoopBackOff- In the kernel logs (dmesg-T) of the OCP node hosting the App Pods we can find errors like: ~~~ 2025-02-25T11:44:06.181157+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd3: encountered watch error:-107 2025-02-25T11:45:07.828163+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd3: failed to unwatch:-110 2025-02-25T11:45:07.828311+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd4: encountered watch error:-107 2025-02-25T11:46:09.268158+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd4: failed to unwatch:-110 2025-02-25T11:46:09.268298+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd2: encountered watch error:-107 2025-02-25T11:47:10.708159+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd2: failed to unwatch:-110 2025-02-25T11:47:10.708327+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd5: encountered watch error:-107 2025-02-25T11:48:12.149156+0000 kernel: rbd: rbd5: failed to unwatch:-110 ~~~- What does the message `rbd: rbdX: encountered watch error:-107` mean?
resolution: - Determine the network issue.- Network Saturation?- High speed drives in the Ceph can saturate the network.- Actual issue with the network?- Firewall or DNS issue?- OpenShift Environments- Scale Application Deployments down and up to restore service.- In some cases it requires a Cordon, Drain, and Reboot to resolve stale mounts- OpenStack- Virtual Machines may pause due to I/O errors.- Virtual Machines may need to be restarted.- Capture `dmesg-T` and `journalctl` if possible
root_cause: The issue is a transient network problem which affected the RBD devices at the time. From the Ceph code, the `watch error:-107` is defined as ~~~ #define ENOTCONN 107 /* Transport endpoint is not connected */ ~~~ "drivers/block/rbd.c" (where the error message originates) ~~~ 3885 static void rbd_watch_errcb(void *arg, u64 cookie, int err) 3886 {3887 struct rbd_device *rbd_dev = arg; 3888 3889 rbd_warn(rbd_dev, "encountered watch error: %d", err); 3890 3891 down_write(&rbd_dev-> lock_rwsem); 3892 rbd_set_owner_cid(rbd_dev, &rbd_empty_cid); 3893 up_write(&rbd_dev-> lock_rwsem); 3894 3895 mutex_lock(&rbd_dev-> watch_mutex); 3896 if (rbd_dev-> watch_state == RBD_WATCH_STATE_REGISTERED) {3897__rbd_unregister_watch(rbd_dev); 3898 rbd_dev-> watch_state = RBD_WATCH_STATE_ERROR; 3899 3900 queue_delayed_work(rbd_dev-> task_wq, &rbd_dev-> watch_dwork, 0); 3901} 3902 mutex_unlock(&rbd_dev-> watch_mutex); 3903} ~~~

title: Pod outgoing connections using EgressIPs are timing out in a Cisco ACI switching environment when nodes are rebooted
issue: - EgressIP traffic is interrupted when EgressIP switches nodes- When doing a cluster upgrade, outgoing traffic going through EgressIP is interrupted- EgressIP issues with Cisco ACI- Connections to a service running outside the cluster are failing when started from the pod running the EgressIP, but are successful when started from the node itself.
resolution: - Verify if the switches handling the link layer traffic on the worker nodes does not have a mechanism to limit Gratuitous ARP messages- Such mechanisms can have a variety of names depending on the switch vendor, for instance with Cisco ACI this is called `Rogue EP Control`.- In the switch software, relax or disable the limiting requirement in regards to Gratuitous ARP messages.- In a specific environment, that `Rogue EP Control` configuration was relaxed so that an endpoint is declared "rogue" only if it is learned over different interfaces 10 times within 60 seconds, and this was enough to solve the outgoing EgressIP issues. Exact values will depend on the number of EgressIPs assigned to each nodes, so you should test in your own environment.- The Cisco ACI environment mentioned here refers to the software running on the switches connected to OpenShift Bare Metal nodes, it is *not* the [Cisco ACI CNI Plugin](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/container-stacks/detail/5ec54ea38b6f188e53644c5a).
root_cause: Disclaimer: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.- When an EgressIP moves to a new node, the new node on which the EgressIP is assigned sends a gratuitous ARP message on the link layer- The aim of this gratuitous ARP message, is to notify hosts on the same link layer to update their link layer address tables (ARP cache)- When large OCP nodes are restarted, a large number of EgressIPs are reassigned to other nodes. It can also happen than an EgressIP moves between a serie of nodes, as the worker nodes of the `worker` MachineConfigPool are rebooted one after the other.- Some switches have a built in mechanism to protect the link layer against abusive Gratuitous ARP messages, as this could come from a misconfiguration of the host. Sometimes the feature is called `ARP Flood Protection`. For Cisco ACI this feature is called `Rogue EP control`, see the ['Rogue EP control' section in the ACI white paper](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/solutions/collateral/data-center-virtualization/application-centric-infrastructure/white-paper-c11-739989.pdf)
