The external configuration is deprecated and will be removed in the future. Please use the template section instead to configure additional environment variables or volumes. WARN StatusUtils:131- Reconciliation #620(timer) KafkaConnect(my-project/my-connect-cluster): In resource KafkaConnect(my-project/my-connect-cluster) in API version kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 the object externalConfiguration at path spec.externalConfiguration has been deprecated. This object has been replaced with KafkaConnectTemplate. WARN StatusUtils:106- Reconciliation #620(timer) KafkaConnect(my-project/my-connect-cluster): In resource KafkaConnect(my-project/my-connect-cluster) in API version kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 the volumes property at path spec.externalConfiguration.volumes has been deprecated. The external configuration volumes are deprecated and will be removed in the future. Please use the additional volumes and volume mounts in pod and container templates instead to mount additional secrets or config maps. ### apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 kind: KafkaConnect... spec:... externalConfiguration: env:- name: MY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE valueFrom: configMapKeyRef: name: my-config-map key: my-key volumes:- name: my-credentials secret: secretName: my-credentials--- kind: ConfigMap apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: my-config-map data: my-key: "my-key-value"--- apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: my-credentials type: Opaque data: key1: aG9nZTI=--- ~~~
resolution: To resolve the warning message you need to replace spec.externalConfiguration with template.connectContainer.env, template.pod.volumes or template.connectContainer.volumeMounts [1][2]. ~~~ apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 kind: KafkaConnect... spec:... template: pod: volumes:- name: my-credentials secret: secretName: my-credentials connectContainer: volumeMounts:- mountPath: /mnt/my-credentials # please change here, you can set any path. name: my-credentials env:- name: MY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE valueFrom: configMapKeyRef: name: my-config-map key: my-key--- kind: ConfigMap apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: my-config-map data: my-key: "my-key-value"--- apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: my-credentials type: Opaque data: key1: aG9nZTI=--- ~~~ [1] Streams for Apache Kafka API Reference > Chapter 93. ExternalConfiguration schema reference https://docs.redhat.com/ja/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.9/html-single/streams_for_apache_kafka_api_reference/index#type-ExternalConfiguration-reference ~~~ The type ExternalConfiguration has been deprecated. Please use KafkaConnectTemplate instead. ~~~ [2] Release Notes for Streams for Apache Kafka 2.9 on OpenShift > Chapter 9. Deprecated features https://docs.redhat.com/ja/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.9/html-single/release_notes_for_streams_for_apache_kafka_2.9_on_openshift/index#deprecated-features-str ~~~ ExternalConfiguration.env: Replaced by template.connectContainer.env ExternalConfiguration.volumes: Replaced by template.pod.volumes and template.connectContainer.volumeMounts ~~~

title: How to Check Previous Ansible Automation Platform Operator Versions and Installation Dates in OpenShift
issue: - The OpenShift Console only shows the current AAP operator version and the date when it was installed. How can we find the exact older AAP operator versions and their installation dates?
resolution: - Use the following oc command to find the older AAP operator versions installed in a particular namespace: ~~~ $oc get installplan-n aap | more install-94gjn aap-operator.v2.4.0-0.1720482179 Manual true install-fkgnj aap-operator.v2.4.0-0.1711590540 Manual true install-llr64 aap-operator.v2.4.0-0.1717558474 Manual true install-ngkln aap-operator.v2.4.0-0.1718152210 Manual true ~~~- The above command shows the current and all the previous operator versions installed in the "aap" namespace. Please change the namespace name as per your environment.- To get the exact date when the particular operator version was installed, use the following command: ~~~ $ oc get installplan install-fkgnj-o json | jq-r.metadata.creationTimestamp 2024-04-02T20:59:48Z ~~~ **Note**: Replace the install plan name with the one in your AAP deployment.
root_cause: - There is no easy way to determine the previously installed AAP operators versions using the OpenShift console. Please use the oc command line tool to get the exact information.

title: OpenTelemetryCollector Trace Export failed with unknown tenant error in Multi-Tenant RHOCP 4 cluster
issue: - How to resolve `InvalidArgument: unknown tenant` Error in `OpenTelemetryCollector` pod logs.- `OpenTelemetryCollector` Trace Export failed with `InvalidArgument: unknown tenant` error in Multi-Tenant cluster.
resolution: To resolve the issue, ensure that the `OpenTelemetryCollector` exporters field includes the correct `tenantName` (X-Scope-OrgID) when sending data.- Identify the correct `tenantName` from the `TempoStack` CR (Custom Resource): ~~~ $ oc get TempoStack-n-o yaml ~~~- Update the `spec.config.exporters.otlp/dev.headers.X-Scope-OrgID` field in the `OpenTelemetryCollector` CR with the appropriate `tenantName`. ~~~ $ oc edit OpenTelemetryCollector-n... spec: mode: deployment serviceAccount: otel-collector config: | extensions: bearertokenauth: filename: "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token" exporters: otlp/dev: endpoint: tempo-simplest-gateway.tempo.svc.cluster.local:8090 tls: insecure: false ca_file: "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/service-ca.crt" auth: authenticator: bearertokenauth headers: X-Scope-OrgID: " " < <======= otlphttp/dev: endpoint: https://tempo-simplest-gateway.chainsaw-multitenancy.svc.cluster.local:8080/api/traces/v1/ tls: insecure: false ca_file: "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/service-ca.crt" auth: authenticator: bearertokenauth headers: X-Scope-OrgID: " " < <=======... ~~~ For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).
root_cause: `OpenTelemetryCollector` attempted to send traces to `TempoStack` `tenant` but the `tenant` mentioned in the exporters field was invalid.

title: Backup shows VolumeSnapshot warnings during execution in OADP
issue: When running backups with OADP 1.4.X, the backup completes successfully but displays warning messages related to VolumeSnapshot creation failures. The warnings indicate that the snapshot controller was unable to update the VolumeSnapshotContent object due to concurrent modifications. ~~~ Velero: message: /VolumeSnapshot has a temporary error Failed to create snapshot: error updating status for volume snapshot content snapcontent-3ded3cba-XXXXXXXXXXX: snapshot controller failed to update snapcontent-3ded3cba-XXXXXXXXXXXXX on API server: Operation cannot be fulfilled on volumesnapshotcontents.snapshot.storage.k8s.io "snapcontent-3ded3cba-XXXXXXXXXXXXX": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again. Snapshot controller will retry later. ~~~ In some cases, the warning escalates into an error, causing the backup to `fail`. ~~~ Velero: message: /Failed to create snapshot: error updating status for volume snapshot content snapcontent-XXXXXXXXXXXXX: snapshot controller failed to update snapcontent-0adc6db5-XXXXXXXXXXXXXX on API server: Operation cannot be fulfilled on volumesnapshotcontents.snapshot.storage.k8s.io "snapcontent-0adc6db5-XXXXXXXXXXXX": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again, plugin: velero.io/csi-volumesnapshot-backup ~~~
resolution: - If the backup completes successfully despite the warnings the warnings can be `safely ignored`.- If the backup fails with snapshot errors `Re-run` the backup.- The issue is transient, and retrying the backup typically resolves it.- If the issue persists frequently then create a `manual snapshot` to verify that the CSI driver and snapshot controller are functioning properly.
root_cause: The issue occurs due to a known limitation in the Kubernetes external snapshot controller, which can occasionally fail to update the VolumeSnapshotContent object due to API server contention. OADP 1.4 includes improvements to safely ignore these warnings, but the issue can still occur intermittently due to the underlying snapshot controller behavior, which is outside the control of the OADP team.

title: OADP backup fails for kopia.blobcfg with AWS KMS encryption and S3 bucket policy
issue: When using OpenShift API for Data Protection for offline backups with an AWS S3 bucket encrypted with KMS encountered a failure during the backup process. Although most files were successfully uploaded, the backup failed specifically for the kopia.blobcfg file, with the following error. ~~~ error to create backup repo: error to create repo with storage: error to initialize repository: unable to write blobcfg blob: PutBlob() failed for "kopia.blobcfg": unable to complete PutBlob(kopia.blobcfg) despite 10 retries: User: XXXXXXXXXX42748994 is not authorized to perform: s3:PutObject on resource: "arn:aws:s3:XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXkopia.blobcfg" with an explicit deny in a resource-based policy. ~~~
root_cause: The backup fails for the kopia.blobcfg file due to Kopia's built-in in-transit encryption, which encrypts the file before upload, making it unrecognizable as KMS-encrypted data.

title: OADP backup fails with volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io not found error on VMware vSAN storage in OpenShift
issue: When running a backup using the OADP operator in OpenShift with persistent storage on VMware vSAN, the backup job fails with the following error. ~~~ Errors: Velero: name: /stress-XXXXXXXXX message: /Error backing up item error: /error executing custom action (groupResource=volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io, namespace=XXXXXX, name=velero-XXXXXXXX-925ds): rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to get volumesnapshot stress/velero-XXXXXXX-925ds: volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io "velero-XXXXXXXXX" not found ~~~
resolution: Ensure that the VolumeSnapshotClass is correctly configured for the VMware vSAN storage. If missing, create a VolumeSnapshotClass. ~~~ $ oc get volumesnapshotclass $ oc describe volumesnapshotclass ~~~ Manually create a VolumeSnapshot to confirm if the CSI driver is functioning.
root_cause: The backup process fails because VolumeSnapshotContent is not created, which prevents the backup from locating the snapshot.

title: RHOCP Cluster Update stuck in the machine-config-daemon roll-out
issue: - The machine-config-daemon operator is in crashloopback.- The machine-config-operator is complaining about an issue like this: ``` Error performing safety controllerconfig sync: Our version (v4.16.0-202501281935.p0.g9e721f0.assembly.stream.el9-dirty) differs from controllerconfig (v4.16.0-202407101706.p0.gd70a17f.assembly.stream.el9-dirty), can't do 'safety' controllerconfig sync until controller is updated ```
resolution: The issue is currently under investigation by the Engineering team in the Jira BUG [OCPBUGS-54926](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-54926) Please collect SOSREPORT of the nodes impacted by the crashlooping **machine-config-daemon** PODs, and rise a ticket to the support team. ### Workaround As a workaround, a reboot of the impacted node(s) may help the machine-config-daemon to start and so to allow the roll-out of the POD to continue.
root_cause: Once the **machine-config-operator** has been updated, it triggers the roll-out of the **machine-config-daemon** PODs on the nodes, before updating the **machine-config-controller**. If the **machine-config-daemon** roll-out is stuck, this is blocking the rest of the update.

title: VMware IPI installation with static IPs create NM "Wired Connection" connection without associated interface in OCP4
issue: - Adding a secondary interface to a node does not work.- The secondary interface result configured with the same primary interface configuration.- Rebooting the node with a new interfaces the node become unreachable.- Primary IP get duplicated in the secondary interface.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [OCPBUGS-54961](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-54961). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. ### Workaround: 1. Add the main interface to the default `Wired Connection`: ~~~ $ nmcli con modify "Wired Connection" connection.interface-name ens192 ~~~ 2. If the secondary interface has been already installed remove it from the VM, and re-create it after have execute step **1**.
root_cause: Under investigation.

title: Unable to run podman or buildah in devspaces workspace after upgrading operator from 3.17 version
issue: - Unable to run podman or buildah commands inside devspaces workspace and getting below mentioned error: ``` failed to setup From and Build flags: failed to get default container config: path "/home/user/.config" exists and it is not owned by the current user ```
resolution: Starting with OpenShift DevSpaces Operator version 3.18, it is no longer necessary to create a [ConfigMap](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_dev_spaces/3.17/html-single/administration_guide/index#enabling-fuse-for-all-workspaces) to mount the `storage.conf ` file for all user workspaces. Therefore, the fuse-overlay ConfigMap can be safely removed from the namespace where the CheCluster instance is deployed. ``` $ oc delete cm fuse-overlay-n ```
root_cause: - From OpenShift DevSpaces Operator version 3.18 onwards, the Universal Developer Image (UDI) already contains the necessary configuration by default. However, if custom image is being used, configure the script manually as Podman 5.x require `/home/user/.config` folder to be owned by the current user.- For detailed information on enabling Fuse for all workspaces, please refer to the [official documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_dev_spaces/3.19/html-single/administration_guide/index#enabling-fuse-for-all-workspaces).

title: oc-mirror fails with "Instructed to preserve digests" when mirroring images for RHOCP 4
issue: - `oc-mirror` fails to mirror an image to a private registry and fails with: ~~~ Manifest list must be converted to type "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json" to be written to destination, but we cannot modify it: "Instructed to preserve digests ~~~
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this problem and has [RHBZ#53455](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-53455) open for this.
root_cause: The `oc-mirror` tool [forcefully preserves digests](https://github.com/openshift/oc-mirror/blob/cebda881256083837127077bf467fd882d6c8582/v2/internal/pkg/batch/concurrent_worker.go#L54) to ensure an operator installed in disconnected mode is able to retrieve its related image (which is commonly digest-based). However if the private registry [does not support](https://github.com/containers/image/blob/d3b241257363a7ed9b114df9d9e9ab26641ffb62/copy/manifest.go#L217) the original manifest type, `oc-mirror` [errors out](https://github.com/containers/image/blob/d3b241257363a7ed9b114df9d9e9ab26641ffb62/copy/multiple.go#L218-L226).

title: Unable to create new ARO cluster getting an "Error: Insufficient privileges to complete the operation."
issue: - Getting an error: Insufficient privileges to complete the operation. While running command `az aro create....`- Trying to create ARO Private cluster using Service principal owner role, All other resources in Azure are created with same SP just the ARO that is failing.
resolution: Login into [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com/#home): 1. Go to App Registration 2. Select the `Service Principal` that using or if doesn´t have any `Service Principal` create a new one 3. Go to API Permissions 4. Click Add a permission 5. Go to Microsoft Graph-> Delegated permissions and check for Application 6. Expand Application > select Application.ReadWrite.All and in the end click Add permission 7. Need to Grant admin consent for Microsoft 8. Try to create again ARO cluster.
root_cause: - The Service Principals used to run az aro create must have below permissions: 1. User Access Administrator (As Owner should have this permission) 2. Directory reader ("Directory.Read.All") to read applications and pull SPs.

title: Reinstall Cluster Monitoring Operator on RHOCP 4
issue: - Accidentally deleted the `openshift-monitoring` project on RHOCP 4 cluster which has the pods running for the default monitoring stack.- How to reinstall the default monitoring stack on RHOCP 4?
resolution: - In the case of OCP v4.x, CVO is responsible for recreating the `openshift-monitoring` namespace in the event of deletion. But if in case the `openshift-monitoring` namespace is not cleaned completely may be due to any finalizer issue then namespace re-creation will fail.- If the `openshift-user-workload-monitoring` namespace is present in the cluster, remove it too and restart the marketplace operator (delete the `operator-marketplace-xyz` pod in the `openshift-marketplace` namespace).- Delete the monitoring Cluster Operator using the command: ~~~ $ oc delete co monitoring ~~~ The Operator and its associated resources will be automatically recreated in the openshift-monitoring namespace.

title: Ability to configure HW RAID for ZTP install from RHACM

resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this request, and a [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-5666) is already in place to track this request.- As a workaround, User can add RAID disk as normal disk using `rootDeviceHints` [parameter](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html-single/postinstallation_configuration/index#the-baremetalhost-spec) to `baremetalhost` [configuration](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.12/html/clusters/cluster_mce_overview#auto-add-host-steps-cli).- Currently, HW RAID configuration is only supported for BM IPI based installation.

Desire to track metrics for ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT sockets

title: Migrate a CephFS PVC to a CephRBD (CephBlockPool) PVC - OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: In some instances, it may be necessary to migrate PVCs using the `cephfs` storageclass to `ceph-rbd`. There are certain scenarios where this could be true, but the highlighted scenario for this solution will be [OCS / ODF Database Workloads Must Not Use CephFS PVs/PVCs (RDBMSs, NoSQL, PostgreSQL, Mongo DBs, etc.)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7003415). This particular issue is not specific to Ceph. Database workloads should be stored on block storage as shown in the OpenShift Container Platform Docuemtation as well:_"Databases: Databases (RDBMSs, NoSQL DBs, etc.) tend to perform best with dedicated block storage,"_ not a shared filesystem. [OCP v4.18- Other specific application storage recommendations](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/postinstallation_configuration/post-install-storage-configuration#other-specific-application-storage-recommendations)
resolution: **WARNING: It is recommended to take a form of backup of the PVC prior to executing this (OADP, snapshot, etc.).** **Note:** The MariaDB application will be used for example purposes. Substitute `mariadb` deployment name with the application to match your environment. Additionally, practicing this process in a sandbox/test cluster before execution may prove to be useful as well. 1. Gather information about the current CephFS volume mount: ~~~ $ oc set volume deployment-n mariadb mariadb pvc/mariadb-storage (allocated 50GiB) as mariadb-storage mounted at /var/lib/mysql <------------------------------------- VOLUME MOUNT/DATA LOCATION ~~~ 2. Scale down the application associated with the CephFS PVC. ~~~ $ oc scale deployment-n mariadb--replicas=0 ~~~ 3. Create a migration application that will be used to attach and copy data between the old and new volumes. ~~~ $ oc create deployment-n migrate--image=registry.access.redhat.com/rhel7/rhel-tools-- tail-f /dev/null ~~~ 4. Mount the old volume (volume to be migrated), to the new `migrate` deployment: ~~~ $ oc set volume deployment/migrate-n--add-t pvc--name=mariadb-old--claim-name=mariadb-storage--mount-path=/mariadb_old ~~~ 5. After the `migrate` pod becomes `Running` again from step 4, create a new `ceph-rbd` PVC and attach it to the `migrate` deployment: ~~~ $ oc set volume deployment/migrate-n--add-t pvc--claim-class ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd--name=mariadb-rbd-storage--claim-name=mariadb-rbd-storage--mount-path=/mariadb_new--claim-mode=ReadWriteOnce--claim-size=50Gi ~~~ 6. After the `migrate` pod becomes `Running` again from step 5, rsh into the new `migrate` pod: ~~~ $ oc rsh-n migrate- ~~~ 7. rsync the data between the old and new volumes: ~~~ $ rsync-avxHAX--progress /mariadb_old/* /mariadb_new ~~~ 8. When the data has transferred, exit the pod and scale down the migrate deployment: ~~~ $ exit $ oc scale deployment-n migrate--replicas=0 ~~~ 9. Allow the migrate pod to terminate and release the volumes, then edit the `mariadb` deployment, and update the `claimName` with the new PVC name. ~~~ $ oc edit deployment-n mariadb volumes:- name: mariadb-storage persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: mariadb-storage <--- Modify this to the new PVC name e.g. mariadb-rbd-storage ~~~ 10. Scale up the mariadb deployment: ~~~ $ oc scale deployment-n mariadb--replicas=1 ~~~

title: NVIDIA DGX H-series systems do not support virtualization in RHEL or Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: Unable to enable or start QEMU-KVM virtualization features on RHEL 8 or RHEL 9 installations on NVIDIA DGX H-series systems after adjusting BIOS settings enabling Intel VT-x or VT-D virtualization features. Unable to enable OpenShift Virtualization features on Red Hat OpenShift versions v4.11 and up on NVIDIA DGX H-series systems after adjusting BIOS settings enabling Intel VT-x or VT-D virtualization features.
resolution: There is no resolution for this issue. Intel VT-x and VT-D virtualization features cannot be enabled on these platforms, per the platform vendor. KVM virtualization, therefore, is unavailable.
root_cause: Intel VT-x and VT-D CPU virtualization features are disabled by the vendor on NVIDIA DGX H-series systems. There are settings in the system BIOS to allow enabling Intel VT-x and VT-D technologies; however, those settings do not have any effect- CPU virtualization features via KVM remain unavailable even when they are set to 'enabled' in the BIOS.

title: Node Tuning Operator does not set disk option read_ahead_kb for external devices
issue: - `read_ahead_kb` is not configured as expected by Node Tuning Operator- Default value of 4096 is not set- Custom value configured in a custom `Tuned` profile is not set- The issue relevant for external devices after it is removed and added back- No error messages observed in tuned pod's log nor in the operator's log
resolution: - This issue was resolved in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.14. Please update to version 4.14 or later to resolve the issue
root_cause: - `tuned` is using `python3-pyudev` library- `python3-pyudev` library needs access to `/run/udev/control` to work correctly- Until OCP version 4.14 `Tuned` pods did not have access to `/run/udev/control`- Without access to `/run/udev/control` `Tuned` was missing `hotplug` events, causing the tuned profiles not to be applied to the device

title: Windows virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization are intermittently going down with BSOD
issue: - Windows virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization are intermittently going down with BSOD. At the time of the problem, high read and write latency were reported for the backend disks used by the virtual machines.
resolution: - Work with the storage vendor to understand the root cause of storage latency at the time of the problem.
root_cause: - For the affected virtual machines, the Windows (BSOD) reported a bug check code of 0x1A, with parameter 1 set to either 0x3F or 0x41793. The following events were logged in the Windows Event Viewer: ~~~ The computer has rebooted from a bugcheck. The bugcheck was: 0x0000001a (0x000000000000003f, 0x000000000003dff0, 0x000000001cab720b, 0x00000000d93305a5). A dump was saved in: C:\windows\Minidump\ 01.dmp. Report Id: 232d8ee0-eda5-4697-a3ab-c811b030e705. ~~~ ~~~ The computer has rebooted from a bugcheck. The bugcheck was: 0x0000001a (0x0000000000041793, Oxfffff68054027c80, 0x0000000000000001, 0x0000000000000000). A dump was saved in: C:\CrashDumps\MEMORY.DMP. Report Id: 032425-16484-01. ~~~- The Windows coredump analysis indicated that the issue is because of performance bottlenecks in the storage stack, with multiple threads observed waiting on pending I/O requests.- The backend disks used by the VM reported high read and write latency at the time of problem as per the stats from the Prometheus dump.

title: Java Pod OOME Killer after migration from OCP 3.9 to OCP 3.11
issue: After migration from OCP 3.9 to OCP 3.11 the application is not starting with `OOME Killer`.
resolution: Usually the OOME-Killer acts when there is not enough memory on the pod for the process to function properly. See solution [How to change JVM memory options using Red Hat JBoss EAP image for Openshift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2682021) for more information on the flags and tuning suggestion. For Java memory consumption details in a container see [Java's memory consumption inside a Openshift 4 container](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7107764) and for Java tuning suggestions, see solution [Java Tuning on OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5495931).

title: NNCP settings are not applied to the additional node (Kubernetes NMState Operator)
issue: - After applying a `NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy`(NNCP), newly added nodes do not get the expected DNS or network configuration.
resolution: Wait for the node to become Ready, then confirm the `nmstate-handler` Pod is running.
root_cause: - The nmstate (`NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy`) applies network configurations via a DaemonSet that runs `nmstate-handler` Pods on each node. These handler Pods only function on nodes that are Ready. If the new node is not fully initialized (Ready) or if the `nmstate-handler` Pod has not started on that node, NNCP updates will not be applied yet.- Right after a new node is provisioned, `/etc/resolv.conf` or other network settings are typically derived from cloud metadata, DHCP, or the underlying platform. The `NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy` does not override these settings until the DaemonSet Pod is running on the node.

title: Is it possible to change the bonding interface configured in agent-config.yaml after cluster installation?
issue: - The bonding interface was configured in `agent-config.yaml`, and the cluster was installed by using the Agent-based Installer.- Is it supported to change the bonding settings after the cluster installation?
resolution: - No. It is not supported changing the bonding settings using `NMState` after cluster installation.- If it is necessary to change the bonding settings, the cluster must be reinstalled.
root_cause: - NMState does not support changing the primary NIC. If the bonding interface configured in `agent-config.yaml` works as the primary NIC of the node, changing it after cluster installation is not supported.

title: Dev Spaces: How to change size of /dev/shm?

title: How to modify the Image/cluster custom resource in a Hosted Cluster in Hosted Control Plane?
issue: - Editing the `Image/cluster` custom resource in a Hosted Cluster in Hosted Control Plane results in an error.- How to modify the `Image/cluster` custom resource in a Hosted Cluster in Hosted Control Plane?
resolution: - To modify parameters of the `Image/cluster` custom resource, configure them in `.spec.configuration.image` of the `HostedCluster` custom resource.- Information about `.spec.configuration.image` is available through the `oc explain` command. $ oc explain HostedCluster.spec.configuration.image GROUP: hypershift.openshift.io KIND: HostedCluster VERSION: v1beta1 FIELD: image DESCRIPTION: Image governs policies related to imagestream imports and runtime configuration for external registries. It allows cluster admins to configure which registries OpenShift is allowed to import images from, extra CA trust bundles for external registries, and policies to block or allow registry hostnames. When exposing OpenShift's image registry to the public, this also lets cluster admins specify the external hostname. Changing this value will trigger a rollout for all existing NodePools in the cluster. FIELDS: additionalTrustedCA additionalTrustedCA is a reference to a ConfigMap containing additional CAs that should be trusted during imagestream import, pod image pull, build image pull, and imageregistry pullthrough. The namespace for this config map is openshift-config. allowedRegistriesForImport <[]Object> allowedRegistriesForImport limits the container image registries that normal users may import images from. Set this list to the registries that you trust to contain valid Docker images and that you want applications to be able to import from. Users with permission to create Images or ImageStreamMappings via the API are not affected by this policy- typically only administrators or system integrations will have those permissions. externalRegistryHostnames <[]string> externalRegistryHostnames provides the hostnames for the default external image registry. The external hostname should be set only when the image registry is exposed externally. The first value is used in 'publicDockerImageRepository' field in ImageStreams. The value must be in "hostname[:port]" format. registrySources registrySources contains configuration that determines how the container runtime should treat individual registries when accessing images for builds+pods. (e.g. whether or not to allow insecure access). It does not contain configuration for the internal cluster registry.
root_cause: - In a Hosted Control Plane environment, the configuration of a Hosted Cluster is managed through the `HostedCluster` custom resource. Editing `Image/cluster` is not allowed.

title: oc-mirror v2 is failing with context deadline exceeded error while downloading to disk  in RHOCP 4
issue: - oc-mirror v2 is failing with an error ``mirroring image docker://registry.redhat.io/ (Operator bundles: [operator-version]- Operators: [operator]) error: copying image 4/4 from manifest list: writing blob: Patch "http://localhost:55000/v2/ ": context deadline exceeded error while downloading to disk.``
resolution: Change the default image download timeout from 10m to something higher depends on the internet bandwidth using the parameter ``--image-timeout`` ~~~ # oc-mirror--config imageset-config-1.yaml file:///--v2--image-timeout 30m--> value in minutes ~~~
root_cause: The ``oc-mirror`` has a default image download timeout set to 10 minutes. If an image takes longer than that to download, then the particular image download will be failed.

title: OpenShift Cluster Upgrade breaks the cluster when upgrading ≤4.12 to 4.13+ with FIPS enabled or custom MachineConfigs are used.
issue: - The `OpenShift Upgrade` fails with `node`in ` NotReady,SchedulingDisabled` status while doing upgrade from ≤ 4.12 to 4.13+ while `FIPS` enabled or custom `MachineConfig` are used for services like `OpenSSL` or `OpenSSH`. ~~~ # oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master0.ocp.example.com NotReady,SchedulingDisabled master 574d v1.26.14+03ee898 master1.ocp.example.com Ready master 574d v1.26.14+03ee898 master2.ocp.example.com Ready master 574d v1.26.14+03ee898 ~~~- The `kubelet` service fails to start on `NotReady` node with error `FIPS mode is enabled, but the required OpenSSL backend is unavailable` as, ~~~ Apr 15 07:20:15 master0.ocp.example.com kubenswrapper[2692]: FIPS mode is enabled, but the required OpenSSL backend is unavailable Apr 15 07:20:15 master0.ocp.example.com systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE Apr 15 07:20:15 master0.ocp.example.com systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'exit-code' ~~~- The `sshd` service fails to start with error `Bad configuration option: CRYPTO_POLICY` as, ~~~ master0.ocp.example.com systemd[1]: Stopped OpenSSH server daemon. master0.ocp.example.com systemd[1]: Starting OpenSSH server daemon... master0.ocp.example.com sshd[397714]: master0.ocp.example.com sshd[401448]: /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config: line 1: Bad configuration option: CRYPTO_POLICY master0.ocp.example.com sshd[401448]: /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config: terminating, 1 bad configuration options master0.ocp.example.com systemd[1]: sshd.service: Main proces ~~~
resolution: - OpenShift Container Platform 4.13 is based on Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9.2. RHEL 9.2 has not yet been submitted for FIPS validation as per General FAQ for OpenShift and FIPS compliance the details can be checked at Compliance Activities and Government Standards for the particular package validations.- The upgrade shouldn't be initiated with FIPS enabled clusters at or below 4.12 to 4.13 or above releases at the moment.- In case of customized `MachineConfig` used then a validation shall be done on test cluster at targeted version of `Upgrade` to ensure the configs supplied are supported according to the major release configuration. After fixing/removing the customized `MachineConfig`, the following commands may help to move `sshd` service back to normal state: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ # chroot /host # ls-l /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends # cat /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config # update-crypto-policies # ls-l /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends # cat /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config ~~~
root_cause: - The Upgrade was initiated on unsupported version for FIPS where the OpenSSL configs were not compatible resulting failure. Also the [release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.13/html/release_notes/ocp-4-13-release-notes#ocp-4-13-about-this-release) for 4.13 release do mention that validation is yet to be obtained and would be available in later minor release though there isn't a timeframe available.- There are some custom `MachineConfigs` used for managing the security configurations instead of `compliance operator` for components like `OpenSSL`, `OpenSSH` or `Kernel space configuration` which are applicable for system wide configs.- There are some fundamental changes in `OpenSSH` configuration starting with `Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9` and the existing customized `MachineConfigs` written according to `Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8` aren't compatible with it.

title: What is the command to get pod version on RH-SSO?
issue: - Need information about the output of a program trying to log on in a keycloak pod.
resolution: 1) Using project `-project`. 2) Command to get pods: ~~~ oc get pods ~~~ 3) Get the result which is the version value: ~~~ oc rsh-c "keycloak"-n $name_pod /bin/bash-c "env | grep PRODUCT_VERSION" | awk-F'=' '{printf "Version SSO: %-8s\n", $2}' ~~~ * The output now is: `Version de SSO1: 7.6.4.GA`

title: Error creating a ClusterInstance after upgrading Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management from v2.12 to v2.13
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: After upgrading from Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management v2.12 to v2.13, attempting to create a ClusterInstance results in the following error: ~~~ Error from server (InternalError): error when creating ".": Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "clusterinstances.siteconfig.open-cluster-management.io": failed to call webhook: Post "https://webhook-clusterinstances-siteconfig-open-cluster-management-io.open-cluster-management.svc:443/validate-siteconfig-open-cluster-management-io-v1alpha1-clusterinstance?timeout=10s": no endpoints available for service "webhook-clusterinstances-siteconfig-open-cluster-management-io" ~~~
resolution: Delete the siteconfig-controller-manager deployment in the open-cluster-management project: ~~~ $ oc delete-n open-cluster-management deployment/siteconfig-controller-manager ~~~ The deployment should be re-created by the MultiClusterHub operator within a few seconds: ~~~ $ oc get-n open-cluster-management deployment/siteconfig-controller-manager NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE siteconfig-controller-manager 1/1 1 1 16s ~~~
root_cause: The labels for the siteconfig-controller-manager deployment changed between Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management v2.12 and v2.13. The ClusterInstance webhook service was introduced in v2.13 and uses the new labels to discover the endpoints. After updating to v2.13, the old labels of the deployment do not get updated since it is an immutable field, causing the discovery of the service's endpoints to fail. Deleting the deployment allows the operator to re-create the deployment with the updated labels.

title: Pipeline Builds fail on Multi-arch cluster
issue: - Builds fail not being able to execute build processes- The build log prints an error about a mismatch in the expected architecture
resolution: For any S2I builder images being used, re-pull the images using the "PreserveOriginal" import-mode, for example ~~~ oc import-image ruby:2.7-ubi8--confirm--import-mode="PreserveOriginal"-n openshift imagestream.image.openshift.io/ruby imported oc import-image java:latest--confirm--import-mode="PreserveOriginal"-n openshift imagestream.image.openshift.io/java imported ~~~
root_cause: By default, the OpenShift installer only pulls the builder images that match the current architecture. For a multi-arch cluster, the other architectures need to be pulled for the S2I builds to succeed on worker nodes with a different architecture. Take a look at [Building multi-architecture container images on OpenShift Container Platform clusters](https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2024/08/27/building-multi-architecture-container-images-openshift-container-platform?source=sso) for a more detailed explanation. Also note, if you don't have a "ClusterPodPlacementConfig" or a misconfigured one, you can have similar problems because the cluster won't properly schedule pods based on the architecture. For more information see [Creating the ClusterPodPlacementConfig](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/postinstallation_configuration/configuring-multi-architecture-compute-machines-on-an-openshift-cluster#multi-architecture-creating-podplacement-config_multiarch-tuning-operator)

title: JBoss EAP S2I build template options
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: What are JBoss EAP S2I build template options? What are JBoss EAP S2I build config options? What are JBoss EAP S2I Galleon config options?
resolution: Environment variable | Purpose | Example value--------- |--------- |--------- APPLICATION_IMAGE | Application name | any name EAP_IMAGE | EAP image | jboss-eap-xp1-openjdk11-openshift:1.0 \ 2 EAP_RUNTIME_IMAGE | Runtime image | jboss-eap-xp1-openjdk11-runtime-openshift:1.0 EAP_IMAGESTREAM_NAMESPACE | set Image Stream namespace | $(oc project-q) SOURCE_REPOSITORY_URL | Github repo dir | https://github.com/jboss-developer/jboss-eap-quickstarts.git SOURCE_REPOSITORY_REF | Github branch or tag | xp-1.0.x CONTEXT_DIR| Context directory | microprofile-config GALLEON_PROVISION_LAYERS | Galleon Layers | jaxrs-server,web-clustering,sso GALLEON_PROVISION_FEATURE_PACKS | Feature packs | any feature packs GALLEON_MAVEN_ARGS | Set the Maven Arguments | `ENV GALLEON_MAVEN_ARGS="-X-e-Dverbose-DcreateChecksum=true"` MAVEN_ARGS/MAVEN_ARGS_APPEND | Set Maven settings and Maven arguments for build | MAVEN_ARGS_APPEND value: '-Dcom.redhat.xpaas.repo.jbossorg
root_cause: As explained the main solution [EAP 7 thin image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6960786), if one uses `provisioning.xml` file one cannot set any `GALLEON_PROVISION_*` environment variables, because the environment variables take precedence and the `provisioning.xml` will be ignored. The options are either or:- Set any Galleon-related environment- Or set the file `galleon/provisioning.xml`to provision the server S2I artifacts can include several artifacts, for additional generic deployments that provide the necessary configuration infrastructure required for the deployment, one can use `CUSTOM_INSTALL_DIRECTORIES` variable, as detailed on [JBoss EAP 7.4 Configuring EAP Openshift Image- S2I Artifacts](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.4/html/getting_started_with_jboss_eap_for_openshift_container_platform/configuring_eap_openshift_image#S2I-Artifacts). In OCP, via S2I build via templates, as explained on [Customizing EAP 7 Template buildconfig deployment in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7011706) and [Troubleshooting EAP 7 local BuildConfig in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7031934) there will be two build configs: `eap-app` and `eap-app-build-artifacts`. The build `eap-app-build-artifacts` will provision EAP and use the `GALLEON_PROVISION_*` environment variables to build the EAP. When Galleon is used the following logs show on the build pod: ~~~ [INFO]------------- < org.jboss.galleon.s2i:layers-provisioning >-------------- [INFO] Building Provision a set of Galleon layers from s2i feature-pack 1.0.0.Final [INFO]--------------------------------[pom]--------------------------------- [INFO] [INFO]--- galleon-maven-plugin:4.2.9.Final:provision (wildfly-provisioning-layers jaxrs-server,postgresql-driver,postgresql-datasource) @ layers-provisioning--- [INFO] Downloading from central: https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/jboss/eap/eap-datasources-galleon-pack/7.4.0.GA-redhat-00003/eap-datasources-galleon-pack-7.4.0.GA-redhat-00003.zip [INFO] Downloading from redhat-ga-repository: https://maven.repository.redhat.com/ga/org/jboss/eap/eap-datasources-galleon-pack/7.4.0.GA-redhat-00003/eap-datasources-galleon-pack-7.4.0.GA-redhat-00003.zip [INFO] Downloaded from redhat-ga-repository: https://maven.repository.redhat.com/ga/org/jboss/eap/eap-datasources-galleon-pack/7.4.0.GA-redhat-00003/eap-datasources-galleon-pack-7.4.0.GA-redhat-00003.zip (16 kB at 57 kB/s) [INFO] Downloading from central: https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.2.5/postgresql-42.2.5.jar [INFO] Downloaded from central: https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.2.5/postgresql-42.2.5.jar (826 kB at 5.8 MB/s) ~~~

issue: Migrating Virtual Machine from vSphere fails if it has NVMe Disks
resolution: * Until a fix is avalable there is no workaround to migrate NVMe disks at the moment, please reconfigure the VM without NVMe Disks, ensure it boots and works fine and then try again.

title: Pods fail with "CreateContainerError" error and "executable file not found in $PATH" is found in pod's log in OCP 4
issue: - Pods are unable to start and stays in a `CreateContainerError` status: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-logging collector-58cpc 0/1 CreateContainerError 0 3m collector-5c8qj 1/1 Running 0 8d ~~~- This issue could be affecting one or more images.
resolution: The workaround is to delete all the images from `/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay` directories and reboot. The steps for accomplishing this are:- Drain the node with the problematic images: ~~~ $ oc adm drain master1.example.com--ignore-daemonsets--delete-local-data--force--grace-period=1 ~~~- SSH to the node, disable `crio` and `kubelet` services and reboot: ~~~ $ systemctl disable crio; systemctl disable kubelet; reboot ~~~- Once the node has restarted ssh to it again and delete storage overlay directories from the node, and after this, enable and start crio and kubelet services. As root user execute: ~~~ $ rm-rf /var/lib/containers/storage/overlay* $ systemctl enable crio; systemctl enable kubelet Created symlink /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/crio.service → /usr/lib/systemd/system/crio.service. Created symlink /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/kubelet.service → /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service. $ systemctl start crio; systemctl start kubelet ~~~- Wait for some minutes and check whether the containers are `Running` again by using the below command: ~~~ $ crictl ps ~~~
root_cause: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in BUG [OCPBUGS-55055](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-55055?filter=-2). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: Upgrade from 3scale 2.13 to 2.14 does not happen
issue: In a disconnected environment, according to [the document](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.14/html/migrating_red_hat_3scale_api_management/upgrade-operator#upgrading-operator-installation ""), the channel of the subscription was changed from `threescale-2.13` to `threescale-2.14`, but nothing happens. All of pods including operator are still running with version 2.13 images healthy and installPlan is not created for version 2.14.
resolution: Delete the failed job and corresponding configmap in `openshift-marketplace` namespace, e.g. ~~~ oc delete cm-n openshift-marketplace oc delete job-n openshift-marketplace ~~~ and then set the channel to `threescale-2.14` again (if it's not set yet.).
root_cause: Bundle unpacking job for 3scale operator failed because corresponding configmap was empty by any reason (This might be due to temporary image pull failure.) e.g. ~~~ $ oc get cm-n openshift-marketplace NAME DATA AGE... 4b08bfb52e37df6474cfcc7a7a1113a3dee543ab855baaeb5936c123456789 0 1h < < < empty... ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get job-n openshift-marketplace NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE... 4b08bfb52e37df6474cfcc7a7a1113a3dee543ab855baaeb5936c123456789 0/1 3h20m 1h < < < this did not complete... ~~~

root_cause: * [DFBUGS-1335](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/DFBUGS-1335) is created to track the issue

title: Modify kernel parameters in OpenShift 4 using Node Tuning Operator
issue: - How to modify an existing kernel parameter in OpenShift 4 nodes using sysctl?- How to configure `tuned` custom resource to modify kernel parameters?- How to modify `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` and `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` in RHCOS?
resolution: - `node-tuning` cluster operator can be used to modify kernel parameters. Following `Tuned` custom resource should be created in `openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator` project in order to modify couple of default kernel parameters. Label(tuned.spec.recommended.[match].[label]) in tuned custom resource should be added carefully while implementing. Following custom resource is modified such that the changes to default value of `net.core.somaxconn` and `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` will take place in both master and worker nodes. If kernel parameters should be changed in worker nodes only then add `node-role.kubernetes.io/worker` label only. apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Set net.core.somaxconn and net.ipv4.tcp_rmem to recommended values include=openshift-node [sysctl] net.core.somaxconn = 4096---> Format should be. = net.ipv4.tcp_rmem = 4096 87380 16777216---> Format should be. = name: openshift-sysctl recommend:- match:- label: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker- label: node-role.kubernetes.io/master priority: 20 profile: openshift-sysctl- For the parameters `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`, `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` it is required to set the filed `operand.tunedConfig.reapply_sysctl` as `false`, for example: apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] include=openshift-node [sysctl] fs.inotify.max_user_watches=1048576 name: inotify-max-user-watches recommend:- profile: inotify-max-user-watches priority: 30 operand: tunedConfig: reapply_sysctl: false match:- label: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker- To rollback aforementioned kernel parameters to default value, the tuned custom resource needs to be deleted only. ~~~ $ oc delete tuned-n openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator ~~~
root_cause: There are two major ways to set kernel parameters in OpenShift.- Using Tuned Operator as this page describes.- Using `/etc/sysctl.conf` file or `/etc/sysctl.d/xxx` files. Some of these files exist on OpenShift by default and they set some parameters such as `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` and `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` These files can be created by creating MachineConfig resources according [How to update kernel parameter with custom machine config to worker nodes?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6973071). The `reapply_sysctl` parameter is used to configure which one takes precedence using when the same kernel parameters are set on both:- If `reapply_sysctl` is set to `false`, Tuned Operator setting takes precedence.- If `reapply_sysctl` is set to `true`, `/etc/sysctl*` files takes precedence. (Default) `/etc/sysctl*` files have some default settings even if `/etc/sysctl*` files are not created explicitly, and by default, after tuned profiles are applied `/etc/sysctl*` is reloaded. Therefore, when the Tuned Operator way is used, if tunable parameters are defined also in the `/etc/sysctl*` files, it is required to specify `reapply_sysctl: false` in the Tuned resource to prevent `/etc/sysctl*` files from overwriting them. Red Hat is at work for improving TuneD Operator documentation via [documentation bug OCPBUGS-25477](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-25477).

title: Modifying scrape intervals in Openshift Prometheus
issue: - Can the `scrape interval` be modified in `Openshift` `Prometheus`?- How to change the default `scrape interval` for the `openshift-monitoring` `Prometheus`?- Methods to modify the default `scrape interval` for the `openshift-user-workload-monitoring` `Prometheus`.
resolution: - The `scrape interval` can be configured for a specific `ServiceMonitor` as described below:- [Configuring parameter `Interval`: If empty, Prometheus uses the global scrape interval.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/rest_api/monitoring_apis/podmonitor-monitoring-coreos-com-v1.html#:~:text=by%20the%20target.-,interval,-string)- [Specifying how a service is monitored by Cluster Observability Operator.](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/observability/cluster_observability_operator/configuring-the-cluster-observability-operator-to-monitor-a-service.html#specifying-how-a-service-is-monitored-by-cluster-observability-operator_configuring_the_cluster_observability_operator_to_monitor_a_service)- Modifying the `global scrape interval` is outside the scope of Red Hat support, as it requires setting the `Monitoring Operator` to `unmanaged` mode. This approach is not recommended, as it may lead to potential performance issues within the cluster. Refer below for more details:- [Ability to modify Prometheus scrape interval without setting CMO to unmanaged.](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-449)- The ability to configure `scrape profiles`, which allow setting a common `scrape interval` for multiple `ServiceMonitor` resources, is being tracked under[OBSDA-211](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-211).- For more information open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).

title: Possibility to configure the scrape_interval within the OpenShift Monitoring stack for a group of ServiceMonitor /PodMonitor resources.
issue: Ability to customise the `scrape_interval` in the `OpenShift Monitoring stack` for a defined set of `ServiceMonitor`/`PodMonitor` resources.
resolution: - Configuring the same `scrape_interval` for `multiple ServiceMonitor`/`PodMonitor` resources is possible by using `scrape profiles`.- The feature request to implement `scrape profiles` has been reported to Red Hat engineering and it is being tracked in under [MON-3808](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MON-3808).- This feature is available as a technology preview starting with `OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) 4.13`. For additional context and development updates, refer to [OBSDA-211](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-211).- For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).

title: Project openshift-cnv stuck in "Terminating"
issue: - While trying to uninstall the OpenShift Virtualization from a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform, the `openshift-cnv` project got stuck in a "Terminating" state: ~~~ $ oc get project openshift-cnv NAME DISPLAY NAME STATUS openshift-cnv Terminating ~~~- A few objects are still pending: ~~~ $ oc get all-n openshift-cnv [...] kubevirt.kubevirt.io/kubevirt-kubevirt-hyperconverged 17h Deployed ~~~- Trying to delete or edit the mentioned objects results in the following error: ~~~ $ oc edit kubevirt.kubevirt.io/kubevirt-kubevirt-hyperconverged error: kubevirts.kubevirt.io "kubevirt-kubevirt-hyperconverged" could not be patched: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "kubevirt-update-validator.kubevirt.io": failed to call webhook: Post "https://kubevirt-operator-webhook.openshift-cnv.svc:443/kubevirt-validate-update?timeout=10s": service "kubevirt-operator-webhook" not found You can run `oc replace-f /tmp/oc-edit-1463650549.yaml` to try this update again. ~~~
resolution: - First of all, try to remove any pending `apiservices` objects pending in the `openshift-cnv` project.- Delete the `validatingwebhookconfigurations` object related to the RHOCPV operator: ~~~ $ oc delete validatingwebhookconfigurations virt-operator-validator validatingwebhookconfiguration.admissionregistration.k8s.io "virt-operator-validator" deleted ~~~- Now remove any finalizer attribute and field on every object pending in the `openshift-cnv`project and try to remove them again.- If needed, try to delete again the project: ~~~ $ oc delete project openshift-cnv--force--grace-period=0 ~~~
root_cause: - The issue is caused by the `HyperConverged` object not being deleted before uninstalling the operator as explained in our [Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/virtualization/installing#uninstalling-virt-web-console_uninstalling-virt).- To avoid this issue, the documentation linked above should be strictly followed and the mentioned objects removed in the correct order.

title: Communication between different nodes is degraded in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform using OVN-k

resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in [OCPBUGS-41551](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-41551) and delivered a fix in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.16.17 through errata [RHSA-2024:7944](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:7944). title: Gitopsify alertmanager silences declaratively using YAML files in RHOCP4
issue: - Gitopsify alertmanager silences declaratively using YAML files.- How to silence specific alerts automatically through GitOps in openshift.

title: Collector configmap not generated when same input used twice for the same output in RHOL 6
issue: When the same input is set as `inputRefs` twice for the same output, the configmap containing the Vector configuration is not generated
All the `inputConditions`, `outputConditions` and `pipelineConditions` show `reason: ValidationSuccess and status: True`, but the collector configmap is not generated

The `clusterLogForwarder` custom resource (CR) shows in the `status.conditions` that not `Ready` caused by a `ValidationFailure`, but it doesn't indicate the validation failing ~~~- lastTransitionTime: "2025-02-24T18:04:27Z" message: one or more of inputs, outputs, pipelines, filters have a validation failure reason: ValidationFailure status: "False" type: observability.openshift.io/Valid- lastTransitionTime: "2025-02-24T18:04:27Z" message: "" reason: ValidationFailure status: "False" type: Ready ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [LOG-6758](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6758) and delivered a fix in RHOL 6.2.1 through errata [RHBA-2025:3908](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:3908) If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution #### Workaround Remove the `inputRef` being used twice for the same `outputRef` in the pipeline as it could cause at the same time the logs being duplicated in the destination.
root_cause: The collector verify a ClusterLogForwarder with multiple inputs to a LokiStack output as invalid due to incorrect, internal processing logic.

title: After upgrade to 2.19, failed to inference with RBAC error message
issue: The InferenceService was previously operating without authentication integration for KServe using Authorino, and the Authorino operator was not installed. However, following an upgrade to Red Hat OpenShift AI version 2.19, inference requests began failing with the following error: ``` RBAC:accessdenied ``` This behavior was unexpected given the previous configuration. How can inference functionality be restored under the new environment?
resolution: This issue is a known bug in Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) version 2.19 related to Authorino integration. As a result, the behavior described above is expected under this version. To temporarily resolve the issue in RHOAI 2.19, the following steps are required:- Install the Authorino Operator from tech-preview channel.- Restart the rhods-operator deployment. ``` oc rollout restart deploy/rhods-operator-n redhat-ods-operator ```- Restart the odh-model-controller deployment. ``` oc rollout restart deploy/odh-model-controller-n redhat-ods-applications ``` This issue has been addressed and resolved in RHOAI version 2.20. After upgrading to version 2.20, the following steps should be taken to restore normal functionality:- Remove Authorino CR- Remove Authorino operator- Remove any Authorino-related CRDs that were installed as a workaround.- Restart both the odh-model-controller and kserve deployments.
root_cause: The detail information can be found here:- https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHOAIENG-24142- https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHOAIENG-20356

title: Effect of unavailability of vCenter API on OCP cluster during the vCenter upgrade/restart.
issue: - Considerations/Best practices from OpenShift perspective during the vCenter upgrade/restart.
resolution: - The vSphere Problem Detector Operator checks clusters that are deployed on vSphere. In case vSphere is unavailable during the upgrade/restart, it will send alerts of loss of connectivity. To know more about vSphere Problem Detector Operator, check this [**Document**](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/installing/installing_vsphere/using-vsphere-problem-detector-operator.html)- The cluster's autoscaling capabilities and the volumes provisioned with dynamic provisioning will be impacted, as there will be no connectivity between the cluster and vCenter due to vCenter unavailability during the vCenter upgrade.- Although the cluster will be up and running, any feature that requires vsphere integration, such as above, will not work if the vCenter is down.
root_cause: - There is a need to upgrade/restart vCenter.

title: Liquibase checksum errors when upgrading RH-SSO Operator
issue: - The Operator is throwing the following exception during the upgrade process from RH-SSO 7.6.0 to 7.6.2 (or later): ~~~ Caused by: liquibase.exception.ValidationFailedException: Validation Failed: 1 changesets check sum META-INF/jpa-changelog-14.0.0.xml::14.0.0-KEYCLOAK-18286-supported-dbs::keycloak was: 8:c0f6eaac1f3be773ffe54cb5b8482b70 but is now: 8:f43dfba07ba249d5d932dc489fd2b886 ~~~- Upgrade process is blocked due to failing pods at startup.
resolution: Apply the following **workaround**, by setting the checksums of affected changesets to `NULL` in the `databasechangelog` table **before migrating**: ~~~ UPDATE databasechangelog set md5sum = NULL WHERE id = '14.0.0-KEYCLOAK-18286-supported-dbs'; UPDATE databasechangelog set md5sum = NULL WHERE id = '14.0.0-KEYCLOAK-18286-unsupported-dbs'; ~~~ Liquibase will automatically re-calculate the missing checksums and update the table, preserving changes already made.
root_cause: The root cause of the problem was identified as a [change](https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase/pull/2767) in Liquibase behavior in version 4.10.0, which caused EnterpriseDB to be recognized as a separate database type from PostgreSQL. This led to checksum validation issues when upgrading from RH-SSO 7.6.0 to 7.6.2 (or later), as the changesets targeted for PostgreSQL were no longer applied to EnterpriseDB.

title: changes in EgressRouter CR does not reflect in the EgressRouter pod.
issue: - Changes or modification or any update in EgressRouter CR does not reflect in the EgressRouter pod.- Getting `connection refused` error when connecting to the EgressRouter on few destinationIP or Port combinations.
resolution: - This is a known issue and [OCPBUGS-55141](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-55141 "OCPBUGS-55141") is reported to address this issue.- **Workaround**:- Upon making any changes in the EgressRouter CR, ensure that the EgressRouter pod is restarted so that the updated configurations from the CR is reflected. ~~~ $ oc delete pod ~~~
root_cause: - Currently, if any changes or modifications are done in the EgressRouter CR it is not reflected in the EgressRouter pod.- Ideally, upon any changes in the EgressRouter CR, the EgressRouter pod should be automatically restarted.

title: Adding certificates to the RH-SSO truststore on OpenShift
issue: - When RH-SSO is deployed on OpenShift, it is not possible to access to RH-SSO truststore to add external certificates (e.g. LDAP certificates).
resolution: ### Create the truststore Create a new keystore using the command `keytool`: ~~~ keytool-import-file-alias-keystore truststore.jks ~~~ Verify the keystore: ~~~ keytool-list-v-keystore truststore.jks-storepass changeit ~~~ ### Add the truststore SPI To add the truststore SPI to the JBoss EAP configuration, which is disabled by default in the RH-SSO OpenShift image, the following options can be considered: #### Add the truststore configuration via custom image- Edit the standalone configuration (`standalone-openshift.xml`) and create a `Containerfile` (or `Dockerfile`) step to copy it into the custom RH-SSO image. ~~~ ~~~ #### Add the truststore configuration via CLI script- Incorporate a JBoss extension CLI script (e.g., `sso.cli`) to enable the truststore SPI during startup. ~~~ /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=truststore/:add /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=truststore/provider=file/:add(enabled=true) /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=truststore/provider=file/:map-put(name=properties,key=file,value=/opt/eap/keystores/truststore.jks) /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=truststore/provider=file/:map-put(name=properties,key=password,value=changeit) /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=truststore/provider=file/:map-put(name=properties,key=hostname-verification-policy,value=ANY) /subsystem=keycloak-server/spi=truststore/provider=file/:map-put(name=properties,key=disabled,value=false) ~~~ Detailed KCS instructions on how to add custom CLI scripts can be found [here](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6170972). ### Create the secret Create the secret from keystore JKS file: ~~~ oc create secret generic sso-truststore-secret--from-file=truststore.jks ~~~ ### Mount the secret to the deployment Edit the deployment configurations as follows: ~~~ spec: containers: volumeMounts: # name must match the volume name below- name: truststore mountPath: /opt/eap/keystores readOnly: true volumes:- name: truststore secret: secretName: sso-truststore-secret ~~~

title: Modifying NetConfig failed with a message similar to 'error: netconfigs.network.openstack.org "openstacknetconfig" is invalid'
issue: - Tried to modify `NetConfig` but it failed with a message similar to the below. ``` error: netconfigs.network.openstack.org "openstacknetconfig" is invalid A copy of your changes has been stored to "/tmp/oc-edit-61234158.yaml" error: Edit cancelled, no valid changes were saved. ```- Is there any way to modify the `NetConfig` after the dataplane nodes have already been deployed?
resolution: **Note** If the interface configurations on the Worker nodes needs to be modified by NNCP as well, the below steps would not be a solution. In this case, fresh install is recommended as some other resource like `net-attach-def` and `L2Advertisement` could need to be modefied as well as NNCP. 1. Add a detached annotation to all of `BareMetalHost` resources ``` $ oc annotate BareMetalHost/ 'baremetalhost.metal3.io/detached=true'-n openstack ``` 2. Delete all of `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` resources ``` oc delete OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet/openstack-data-plane-n openstack ``` 3. Modify the `NetConfig` ``` oc edit NetConfig/-n openstack ``` or ``` oc apply-f-n openstack ``` 4. Re-create all of `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` with [Pre-provisioning method](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html/deploying_red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/assembly_creating-the-data-plane#proc_creating-an-OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet-CR-with-preprovisioned-nodes_dataplane) instead of the Unprovisioning method.- Please make sure especially following points:- Update `preProvisioned: false` to `preProvisioned: true`- Remove `baremetalSetTemplate` section- Remove `userData`, `networkData`, `bmhLabelSelector` for each dataplane node under the `nodes` section The re-created `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` will be stay in the below status but the dataplane nodes which have already deployed are working fine so nothing to do here. ``` # oc get OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet-n openstack NAME STATUS MESSAGE openstack-data-plane False NodeSet setup ready, waiting for Deployment... ``` **NOTE**: please avoid to remove the metal3 annotation. If you removed the annotation, the baremetal hosts could be shutdown or provisioning unexpectedly.
root_cause: - The `IPSet` CR will be created immediately after the `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` CR was created.- And `IPSet` and `NetConfig` are dependencies.- Therefore, if the `NetConfig` is needed to be edited, the `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` needs to be deleted first.- However, if `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet` was deleted, the `BareMetalHost` resources will be in `deprovisioning` immediately and then these will be powered off.- So `BareMetalHost` resources need to be detached from Metal3 before deleting `OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet`.

title: FailedValidation error with Resource Modifiers changing the storage class in an OADP restore
issue: - Restore fails- Unable to change the storage class with a configmap- Error in restore job log: ~~~ Phase: FailedValidation Validation errors: Error in parsing resource modifiers provided in configmap openshift-adp/change-storage-class-config: failed to decode yaml data into resource modifiers, err: error unmarshaling JSON: while decoding JSON: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type resourcemodifiers.ResourceModifiers ~~~
resolution: This happens if the configmap is referenced as a resource modifier in the yaml or the velero cli. Simply remove it. For example: Change ~~~ velero restore create restore-example-ns-1--from-backup schedule-backup-every8hrs-2025xxxxxxx--include-namespaces example-ns--resource-modifier-configmap change-storage-class-config ~~~ to ~~~ velero restore create restore-example-ns-1--from-backup schedule-backup-every8hrs-2025xxxxxxx--include-namespaces example-ns ~~~
root_cause: The [documentation describes creating a configmap to replace the storage class](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/oadp-application-backup-and-restore#storage-class-mapping-oadp_oadp-advanced-topics), but it doesn't mention changing the way the restore process is run, or adding any resource modifiers, so it's unclear how that configmap is applied. The resource process just picks it up based on the labels in the configmap and the backup should be run as it would be without it.

title: Pipeline error: /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble: No such file or directory
issue: The pipeline is failing and the pipeline log shows an error when using the s2i-java task. ~~~ STEP 7/8: RUN /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble /bin/sh: /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble: No such file or directory subprocess exited with status 127 subprocess exited with status 127 Error: building at STEP "RUN /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble": exit status 127 ~~~
resolution: - This is a known issue: [task-s2i-java Issue#363](https://github.com/openshift-pipelines/tektoncd-catalog/issues/363)- As a workaround modify the pipeline and add the following lines under 'build' task: ~~~...- name: build params:- name: IMAGE_SCRIPTS_URL <---------- ADD THIS LINE value: image:///usr/local/s2i <---------- ADD THIS LINE... ~~~
root_cause: - This exit code(status 127) is a part of the system's way of communicating that a particular command it tried to execute could not be found. Here the command `RUN /usr/libexec/s2i/assemble` was unable to execute due to the script file not being present in the specified location `/usr/libexec/s2i/`.- In all the latest OpenJDK Builder images the s2i `IMAGE_SCRIPTS` are available in this directory `image:///usr/local/s2i`. However the default value of `IMAGE_SCRIPTS_URL` in task-s2i-java: [task-s2i-java.yaml](https://github.com/openshift-pipelines/tektoncd-catalog/blob/46920d551b551a5fd86db78e7977b04abd46c015/tasks/task-s2i-java/0.6.0/task-s2i-java.yaml#L47) is `image:///usr/libexec/s2i`. This is the reason why the pipeline was failing with the error above.
