title: Unable to install and run the Red Hat OpenShift GitOps operator
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Cluster is unable to install the Red Hat OpenShift GitOps operator after removing an old release of ArgoCD which was installed from the upstream project (community). The below warning is presented: Error Loading: request to convert CR from an invalid group/version: argoproj.io/v1beta1
resolution: **Disclaimer:** *Please notice this process includes installation of community operators. These are Operators which have not been vetted or verified by Red Hat. Community Operators should be used with caution because their stability is unknown. Red Hat provides no support for community Operators.* 1. Using the OperatorHub, install the ArgoCD community operator (latest)[^1], which comes with both v1beta1 and v1alpha1 versions:![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/screenshot_from_2024-01-12_16-51-20.png) 2. Validate the operator comes with both versions installed. It can be verified by checking the operator yaml file on the Openshift Console or via the command below: $ oc get crd argocds.argoproj.io-o yaml | grep "conversionReviewVersions"-A2 conversionReviewVersions:- v1alpha1- v1beta1 3. After completely installed and validated, remove the ArgoCd community operator; 4. Install the Red Hat OpenShift GitOps operator:![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/screenshot_from_2024-01-12_17-04-27.png) [^1]: At the time of writing, the latest release was Argo CD 0.8.0- provided by Argo CD Community
root_cause: The `Custom Resource Definition (CRD)` provided with the OpenShift GitOps Operator does not provide a conversion strategy between the APIs `v1beta1` and `v1alpha1` as the GitOps Operator only comes with the `v1alpha1` and the particular upstream ArgoCD version with `v1beta1`. As both operators use the same name `argocds.argoproj.io`, when attempting to install the GitOps Operator, the `KubeAPIServer` identifies the existing `argocds.argoproj.io/v1beta1` `custom resources (CRs)` and no defined conversion strategy, which makes the process to stop showing the warning message presented above. Even after uninstalling the upstream ArgoCD version and deleting the `argocds.argoproj.io/v1beta1` CRD, the error still persists. Since the operator has been uninstalled and the CRD removed, it stops our ability to remove remaining ArgoCD objects from ETCD using the APIServer.

title: jgroups in EAP/DG 8 thread dumps on the server logs
issue: - In DG 8 why there are thread dumps on the server logs?- Automatic thread dumps created in DG 8 server logs- jgroups triggering thread dumps on the server logs in EAP
resolution: In DG 8, when the thread pool has been filled 10k times a thread dump will be logged ~ thread dump (dumped once, until thread_dump is reset) ~ so this explains why it appears on the server.log: ~~~ 2022-10-15 12:46:14,895 FATAL (Connection.Receiver [127.0.0.0:7600- 127.0.0.0:7600:port]-15,cluster-1182) [org.jgroups.protocols.TCP] cluster-1182: thread pool is full (max=200, active=200); thread dump (dumped once, until thread_dump is reset): <------------ here "main" #1 prio=0 tid=0x1 nid=NA waiting java.lang.Thread.State: WAITING at java.base@11.0.10/jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe.park(Native Method)- parking to wait for <0x3553cd> (a java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture$Signaller) at java.base@11.0.10/java.util.concurrent.locks.LockSupport.park(LockSupport.java:194) at java.base@11.0.10/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture$Signaller.block(CompletableFuture.java:1796) at java.base@11.0.10/java.util.concurrent.ForkJoinPool.managedBlock(ForkJoinPool.java:3128) at java.base@11.0.10/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.waitingGet(CompletableFuture.java:1823) at java.base@11.0.10/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.get(CompletableFuture.java:1998) at org.infinispan.server.Bootstrap.runInternal(Bootstrap.java:165) at org.infinispan.server.tool.Main.run(Main.java:98) at org.infinispan.server.Bootstrap.main(Bootstrap.java:50) at java.base@11.0.10/jdk.internal.reflect.NativeMethodAccessorImpl.invoke0(Native Method) at java.base@11.0.10/jdk.internal.reflect.NativeMethodAccessorImpl.invoke(NativeMethodAccessorImpl.java:62) at java.base@11.0.10/jdk.internal.reflect.DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl.invoke(DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl.java:43) at java.base@11.0.10/java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(Method.java:566) at app//org.infinispan.server.loader.Loader.run(Loader.java:106) at app//org.infinispan.server.loader.Loader.main(Loader.java:51) ~~~
root_cause: The thread pool is full and after 10k hits of full threads, an automatic thread dump will be generated. This mean if there is **one message on the server log** the threads got full 10k times. This comes from the default configuration- server on `$RHDG_HOME/lib/infinispan-core-13.0.10.Final-redhat-00001.jar/default-config/default-jgroups-tcp.xml` ~~~ ~~~ The same happens on EAP 7/8, given this is a jgroups feature. The only difference is the specific threshold for that to happen.

title: Externalizing 3scale API Management databases
issue: - Is it possible to configure 3scale to use external databases instead of the default internal ones?- Is it supported to use external instances of MySQL/Oracle, Redis and PostgreSQL?- Is it possible to use an external Oracle database for system-database?- Is there an official reference in the 3scale API management documentation on how to proceed with such external database setup?
resolution: 3scale API Management comes with some embedded/internal databases that can be summarized as follows:- system-database (MySQL)- system-redis (Redis)- backend-redis (Redis)- zync-database (PostgreSQL) By default, 3scale API Management uses the built-in databases. However, 3scale API Management supports the `externalization` of these built-in databases which means to stop using them and instead use new databases provisioned within the same Openshift cluster or in a separate infrastructure. When databases from a 3scale API Management deployment are externalized, that means to provide isolation from the application and resilience against service disruptions at the database level. The resilience to service disruptions depends on the service level agreements (SLAs) provided by the infrastructure or platform provider where the new provisioned databases are hosted. In other words, when integrating 3scale API Management with external databases, any backup routines, updates or troubleshooting are the responsibility of the owners of such external components. For more details (configurations required) on externalizing databases, check the associated [3scale official documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#getting-apimanager-admin-master-portal-credentials). When installing 3scale API Management, there some alternatives for the databases:- system-database supports externalization to MySQL, PostgreSQL or Oracle.- system-redis and backend-redis only supports externalization to Redis (with a separate Redis instance for each one).- zync-database only externalization to PostgreSQL. The specific database versions that 3scale API Management has been tested and hence, are supported regarding a particular 3scale API Management version can be consulted in the [supported configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2798521). The following 3scale API Management official documentation links can be consulted for configuring such database integrations with the different providers supported:- [Backend Redis secret setup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html-single/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/index#backend-redis-secret)- [System Redis secret setup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html-single/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/index#system-redis-secret)- [System database secret setup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html-single/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/index#system-database-secret)- [Zync database secret setup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html-single/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/index#zync-database-secret) Additionally, the following links to official documentation may also result useful:- [External Redis database configuration for high availability support in 3scale API Management](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/external-redis-database-configuration-for-high-availability-support-in-threescale)- [Configuring an external MySQL database](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/configure-external-mysql-database)- [Using Oracle as the system database](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#installing-threescale-with-operator-oracle-system-database)- [Using PostgreSQL as system database](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.15/html/installing_red_hat_3scale_api_management/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#postgresql_installation)

title: Can't scrape OVN-Kubernetes metrics using Openshift network-tools image and/or need a dedicated way to collect metrics for scripting
issue: - The `openshift/network-tools` official image is not collecting any data when gathering metrics from OpenShift OVN-Kubernetes
resolution: **OCP 4.12 and 4.13** On OCP clusters with version 4.12.z ad 4.13.z there is an option to gather metrics from only one of the `ovnkube-master` and `ovnkube-node` pods, by checking which master nodes is the leader. To run this option do: ~~~~ $ export OVNK-MASTERNODE=$(oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get lease ovn-kubernetes-master-o jsonpath='{.spec.holderIdentity}') $ export OVNK-MASTERPOD=$(oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get pods--field-selector spec.nodeName=${OVNK-MASTERNODE}-l app=ovnkube-master-o=jsonpath='{.items..metadata.name}') $ export OVNK-NODEPOD=$(oc get pods-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes--field-selector spec.nodeName=${OVNK-MASTERNODE}-l app=ovnkube-node-o=jsonpath='{.items..metadata.name}') $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-master $OVNK-MASTERPOD curl-sS http://localhost:29102/metrics > ovnk-master_metrics.txt $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-node $OVNK-NODEPOD curl-sS http://localhost:29105/metrics > ovnk-node_metrics.txt $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-node $OVNK-NODEPOD curl-sS http://localhost:29103/metrics > node-cni_metrics.txt ~~~~ To gather all `ovnkube-node` pods metrics from all nodes, then something like this can be done: ~~~~ $ for OVNK-NODEPOD in $(oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get pods-l app=ovnkube-node-o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name--no-headers); \ do echo "Gathering OVN metrics for pod $OVNK-NODEPOD" > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 1; \ echo "--------------------------------------------------" > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 1; \ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-node $OVNK-NODEPOD curl-sS http://localhost:29105/metrics > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 2; \ echo "--------------------------------------------------" > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 1; \ do echo "Gathering CNI node metrics for pod $OVNK-NODEPOD" > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 1; \ echo "--------------------------------------------------" > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 1; \ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-node $OVNK-NODEPOD curl-sS http://localhost:29103/metrics > > ovn-node_${OVNK-NODEPOD}_metrics.txt; sleep 2; \ done ~~~~ **OCP 4.14 and above** With OCP 4.14 OVN-Kubernetes architecture changed from centralized databases running on masters to a decentralized architecture with each node having its own databases and control. Therefore the metrics can either be collected all on one or set of nodes, when needed or metrics need to be collected from all `ovnkube-node` pods. To do so two similar options like the ones above can be used as follow: ~~~~ $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-controller curl-sS http://localhost:29103/metrics $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-controller curl-sS http://localhost:29105/metrics ~~~~ And for the `ovnkube-control-planes` there is one endpoint to gather its metrics. Start by checking the current leader: ~~~~ $ oc get leases $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-cluster-manager curl-sS http://localhost:29108/metrics ~~~~ All of these can be configured on a script in the similar way as mentioned in the `4.12+` examples. For the new OVN masters, something like this can be done to automtically check the leader: ~~~~ OVNLEADER=$(oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes get lease ovn-kubernetes-master-o custom-columns=HOLDER:.spec.holderIdentity--no-headers) oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rsh-Tc ovnkube-cluster-manager "$OVNLEADER" curl-sS http://localhost:29108/metrics ~~~~

title: How to create a custom route in keycloak
issue: Keycloak operator by default creates a `passthrough` route but we need to customize it or create another type of route.
resolution: Keycloak operator by default creates a `passthrough` route, this creation can be disabled setting `.spec.ingress.enabled: false` on `Keycloak CR`: ~~~ apiVersion: k8s.keycloak.org/v2alpha1 kind: Keycloak metadata: name: keycloak1 spec: instances: 1 db: vendor: postgres host: postgres-db-w usernameSecret: name: keycloak-db-secret key: username passwordSecret: name: keycloak-db-secret key: password http: tlsSecret: tls-secret-wildcard hostname: hostname: ingress: enabled: false ~~~ After disabling the automatic creation, the route can be [created manually](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/networking/configuring-routes#configuring-default-certificate).
root_cause: Keycloak operator by default creates a `passthrough` route.

title: Elasticsearch Operator  pod is in CreateContainerConfigError state  in RHOCP 4
issue: - `Elasticsearch-operator` pod stuck in `CreateContainerConfigError` with the below error in the `spec.conditions` section of the Elasticsearch Operator's Cluster Service Version (CSV): ~~~ message: 'installing: waiting for deployment elasticsearch-operator to become ready: deployment "elasticsearch-operator" waiting for 1 outdated replica(s) to be terminated' ~~~
resolution: - The Security Context Constraints (SCC) applied to the `Elasticsearch Operator` pod must be checked and modified to ensure proper configuration.- Remove `system:authenticated` group from the `anyuid` SCC: ~~~ $ oc adm policy remove-scc-from-group anyuid system:authenticated ~~~- Restart the pod after making necessary changes: ~~~ $ oc delete pod elasticsearch-operator-xxx-n openshift-operators-redhat ~~~
root_cause: - The `anyuid` SCC is currently assigned to the `system:authenticated` group, which is not the default setting. This allows any authenticated user to run pods with any UID, which can create security risks.- To reduce this risk and follow security best practices, the `system:authenticated` group should be removed from the `anyuid` SCC. This way, only trusted groups, like `system:cluster-admins` (and possibly `system:masters`), can use this SCC.

title: Multiple namespaces stuck in terminating state in RHOCP 4
issue: - Multiple namespaces are stuck in `Terminating` state, preventing their deletion. Manual deletion and automated scripts did not help in deleting those namespaces.
resolution: - Identify and remove the orphaned API services: ~~~ $ oc delete apiservice ~~~- Verify that the namespaces are not longer stuck in `Terminating` state: ~~~ $ oc get project | grep-i Terminating ~~~
root_cause: The issue is caused by noise maker `API service` dependencies that remains after an incomplete uninstallation of an operator. These noise maker API services prevent proper namespace termination.

title: Configuring multiple identity providers with the same user in OAuth in RHOCP 4
issue: - Need to transition from a single `Identity Management (IDM) server` to a cluster of `IDM servers` to improve availability and scalability.- When attempting to configure multiple `IDM servers` as `identityProviders` in `OAuth`, errors may occur.
resolution: - Before migrating to the new `IDM servers`, ensure that any existing `user identities` in OpenShift that were mapped to the old `IDM server` are removed.- Update the `OAuth` configuration to include multiple `identityProviders`. Use the `mappingMethod: add` to prevent conflicts: ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: OAuth metadata: name: cluster spec: identityProviders:- name: my_identity_provider mappingMethod: claim #### here type: HTPasswd htpasswd: fileData: name: htpass-secret ~~~- Please refer [Identity provider parameters](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.18/authentication/understanding-identity-provider.html#identity-provider-par[…]ing-identity-provider) to get more details about `identityProvider` parameters.
root_cause: The primary cause of issues when configuring multiple `IDM servers` is the conflict arising from `identical user` and `group identities` across the servers. When multiple `identityProviders` are configured with the same set of users, OpenShift may encounter errors during authentication due to the replication of identities.

title: Unable to delete pod from console in RHOCP 4
issue: - Pods cannot be deleted from the `console`, resulting in the following error message: ~~~ "Unexpected token ' <', "
resolution: Review and modify the `firewall` settings to allow the `HTTP DELETE` method. Once the `firewall` configuration has been updated, try deleting a pod from the `console`.
root_cause: The issue is caused by a `firewall` configuration that blocks the `HTTP DELETE` method. This restriction prevents the console from processing `delete` requests successfully.

title: How to inject custom configurations for OpenShift Agent Based installer
issue: - How to configure additional customizations for `clusterOperators`, like for example change the default `OVN-Kubernetes` internal networks, the same it can be done for other installation types.- Using examples on how to customize cluster objects prior to installation, used on other installation docs, like for example [here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/installing_on_bare_metal/user-provisioned-infrastructure#modifying-nwoperator-config-startup_installing-bare-metal-network-customizations), doesn't work and agent based installation documentation only mentions that `machineConfigs` are the only ones that can be configured.

In that regard start by creating this directory under the main installation directory: ~~~~ $ mkdir openshift ~~~~ In this directory create the files with the additional configurations needed. For example to change some of the OVN-Kubernetes internal networks and enable IPsec create the following file: ~~~~ $ cat openshift/cluster-network-03-config.yml apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: Network metadata: name: cluster spec: defaultNetwork: ovnKubernetesConfig: ipsecConfig: mode: Full ipv4: internalTransitSwitchSubnet: 100.72.0.0/20 internalJoinSubnet: 100.72.16.0/20 ~~~~ With the file created, follow the rest of the documented procedure to create the `image` or the `pxe-files` for the cluster installation. title: Disabling RoCE On Nvdia Mellanox Cards
issue: If an end user or some user application used UDP port 4791, which is outside of operator control, Mellanox NIC will capture user traffic which conflicts with RoCEv2 as it is enabled by default.
resolution: ### Disabling RoCE Feature ~~~ [root@localhost ~]# mstconfig-d 4b:00.0 set ROCE_CONTROL=ROCE_DISABLE Device #1:---------- Device type: ConnectX6DX Name: MCX623432AN-ADA_Ax Description: ConnectX-6 Dx EN adapter card; 25GbE for OCP 3.0; with host management; Dual-port SFP28; PCIe 3.0/4.0 x16 Device: 4b:00.0 Configurations: Next Boot New ROCE_CONTROL ROCE_ENABLE(2) ROCE_DISABLE(1) Apply new Configuration? (y/n) [n]: y Applying... Done!-I- Please reboot machine to load new configurations. ~~~ ### Resetting The Card **NOTE:** This will cause a service interruption. ~~~ root@localhost ~]# mstfwreset reset-d 4b:00.0-y-l 4 Requested reset level for device, 4b:00.0: 4: Warm Reboot Continue with reset?[y/N] y-I- Sending Reset Command To Fw-Done-I- Sending reboot command to machine-Done ~~~ #### Validating ~~~ [root@localhost ~]# mstconfig-d 4b:00.0 q | grep-i roce ROCE_NEXT_PROTOCOL 254 ROCE_CC_LEGACY_DCQCN True(1) ROCE_CC_PRIO_MASK_P1 255 ROCE_CC_PRIO_MASK_P2 255 ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_P1 0 ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_MODE_P1 DEVICE_DEFAULT(0) ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_P2 0 ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_MODE_P2 DEVICE_DEFAULT(0) ROCE_CONTROL ROCE_DISABLE(1) ~~~
root_cause: By default the setting is enabled: ~~~ [root@localhost ~]# mstconfig-d 4b:00.0 q | head-8 Device #1:---------- Device type: ConnectX6DX Name: MCX623432AN-ADA_Ax Description: ConnectX-6 Dx EN adapter card; 25GbE for OCP 3.0; with host management; Dual-port SFP28; PCIe 3.0/4.0 x16 Device: 4b:00.0 [root@localhost ~]# mstconfig-d 4b:00.0 q | grep-i roce ROCE_NEXT_PROTOCOL 254 ROCE_CC_LEGACY_DCQCN True(1) ROCE_CC_PRIO_MASK_P1 255 ROCE_CC_PRIO_MASK_P2 255 ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_P1 0 ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_MODE_P1 DEVICE_DEFAULT(0) ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_P2 0 ROCE_RTT_RESP_DSCP_MODE_P2 DEVICE_DEFAULT(0) ROCE_CONTROL ROCE_ENABLE(2) ~~~

title: Automating OpenShift cluster subscriptions with the ocm tool
issue: When a new connected OpenShift cluster is deployed and is registered in the [Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/cluster-list), it’s assigned a 60-day evaluation subscription, regardless of the availability of valid OpenShift subscriptions in the account. The subscription type can be updated as described in the solution article [“How to attach subscriptions to OpenShift 4 clusters?”](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6262561), however it’s a manual process done through the Cloud Console and doesn’t provide an automated way to attach valid subscriptions to clusters.
resolution: The ocm CLI tool can be used to automate the process of assigning valid subscriptions to connected OpenShift clusters. The ocm tool connects to the Red Hat OpenShift Cluster Manager (OCM) API and can assign Standard or Premium subscriptions to OpenShift clusters, provided they are available in the user’s account. This article describes how to subscribe OpenShift cluster using a CLI tool, which could then be easily automated by adding CLI commands to a script (and running as a cron job) or by using automated tools such as Ansible or Terraform. Please note that only the cluster owner OR organization administrator can update a cluster's subscription properties, so verify before proceeding. #### Download ocm tool Download the ocm tool from `https://github.com/openshift-online/ocm-cli/releases`, and place it in your bastion node as `/usr/local/bin/ocm`. Be sure to set execute permissions with `chmod +x /usr/local/bin/ocm`. #### Login to the OpenShift Cluster Manager Login using the token obtained from `https://console.redhat.com/openshift/token/show`: ~~~ ocm login--token=" " ~~~ #### Get the cluster’s OCM ID We need to get the cluster’s ID in OCM, which is different from the cluster’s UUID. When searching for a cluster, there are several variables to use to find the correct cluster. The variables include: | Variable | Description | |--------------|-------------| | CLUSTER_UUID | Cluster ID. Extract with `oc get clusterversion version-o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterID}{"\n"}'` | | CONSOLE_URL | The URL of the console dashboard. Extract with `oc get route console-n openshift-console` and prepend with `https://` | | DISPLAY_NAME | Cluster’s display name in OCM. If not set, it defaults to the cluster’s UUID | Set environment variable values as needed, depending on the search parameter: ~~~ CLUSTER_UUID=1e15df02-6be6-4dac-b0c9-2ab1a7418bd9 CONSOLE_URL=”https://console-openshift-console.apps.lab.example.com” DISPLAY_NAME=”lab demo” ~~~ In the examples below, the return value is stored in the variable `$CID` for ease of use. * Example 1: Extract the OCM Cluster ID using the cluster’s UUID. This is the recommended way to search for a cluster entry, as the UUID is unique: ~~~ CID=`ocm get subs-p search="external_cluster_id='${CLUSTER_UUID}'" | jq-r '.items[].href'` echo $CID # Optional, just to confirm it returned a valid value /api/accounts_mgmt/v1/subscriptions/2v6JPdWrEoCsvlq3ws3CLzYInOs ~~~ * Example 2: Extract the OCM Cluster ID using the console URL. This may return several entries if the cluster with the same DNS entries has been deployed more than once. `The status=’Active’` is optional, although needed here as all other cluster entries with the same console URL are assumed to be `Inactive`: ~~~ CID=`ocm get subs-p search="status ='Active' and console_url='${CONSOLE_URL}'" | jq-r '.items[].href'` echo $CID # Optional, just to confirm it returned a valid value /api/accounts_mgmt/v1/subscriptions/2v6JPdWrEoCsvlq3ws3CLzYInOs ~~~ * Example 3: Extract the OCM Cluster ID using the cluster’s display name in OCM. This is not the best way to search for a cluster, as cluster display names are not unique and we may get more than one value. Here, we match any cluster that contains the given display name (doesn't have to be an exact match): ~~~ CID=`ocm get subs-p search="status ='Active' and display_name like '%${DISPLAY_NAME}%'" | jq-r '.items[].href'` echo $CID # Optional, just to confirm it returned a valid value /api/accounts_mgmt/v1/subscriptions/2v6JPdWrEoCsvlq3ws3CLzYInOs ~~~ #### Update the cluster’s subscription type Now that we have the cluster’s OCM ID, we can update the subscription type using the following variables: | Variable | Values | |----------------|----------| | SUPPORT_LEVEL | * Self-Support * Standard * Premium | | USAGE | * Development/Test * Production * Disaster Recovery | | SERVICE_LEVEL | * L1-L3 | * Example 1: Update the cluster’s subscription type to Standard, usage to “Development/Test” and service level to “L1-L3”: ~~~ echo '{"support_level":"Standard", "usage":"Development/Test", "service_level":"L1-L3"}' | ocm patch $CID ~~~ * Example 2: Update the cluster’s subscription type to Premium (assuming that Premium subscriptions are already allocated in the Red Hat account). Set the usage to “Production” and service level to “L1-L3”: ~~~ echo '{"support_level":"Premium", "usage":"Production", "service_level":"L1-L3"}' | ocm patch $CID ~~~ If the update is successful, the cluster's updated properties will be displayed in the console in JSON format. If an incorrect value is attempted, in this case `support_level=”Ultra-Premium”` (a non-existent value), an error such as this will be displayed: ~~~ echo '{"support_level":"Ultra-Premium", "usage":"Production", "service_level":"L1-L3"}' | ocm patch $CID {"code":"ACCT-MGMT-8", "href":"/api/accounts_mgmt/v1/errors/8", "id":"8", "kind":"Error", "operation_id":"874db2e4-8629-4b80-8bef-472ab36bfa30", "reason":"Invalid support_level: 'Ultra-Premium'"} ~~~ When done, log out from OCM: ~~~ ocm logout ~~~
root_cause: When a new connected OpenShift cluster is deployed and is registered in the [Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/cluster-list), it is assigned a 60-day evaluation subscription by default.

title: Network Operator Degraded: Error while updating operator configuration: could not apply (k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1, Kind=NetworkAttachmentDefinition)
issue: - Network operator is degraded with below mentioned error: ~~~ network 4.10.31 True True True 2y167d Error while updating operator configuration: could not apply (k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1, Kind=NetworkAttachmentDefinition) oldproject/myoldcni; Namespace error for networkattachment definition, consider possible solutions: (1) Edit config files to include existing namespace (2) Create non-existent namespace (3) Delete erroneous network-attachment-definition: could not apply (k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1, Kind=NetworkAttachmentDefinition) oldproject/myoldcni: ApplyObject of (k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1, Kind=NetworkAttachmentDefinition) oldproject/myoldcni was unsuccessful: namespaces "oldproject" not found ~~~- Openshift cluster is impacted as network and authentication operators are degraded.
resolution: - There is likely an additional network configured on the network.operator.openshift.io that points to a project that has been removed. ~~~ # oc get network.operator.openshift.io cluster-o yaml apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: Network metadata: name: cluster spec: additionalNetworks:- name: myoldcni namespace: oldproject rawCNIConfig: |- {...} type: Raw ~~~- If there is a network configured that isnt used or pointing to a nonexistent project remove it. If network is needed modify the config correctly following [Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/networking/multiple-network) ~~~ # oc edit network.operator.openshift.io cluster ~~~- A restart of the network operator might be needed after the fix to remove the operator from a degraded state. ~~~ oc delete pod-n openshift-network-operator-l name=network-operator ~~~
root_cause: - The root cause of the issue is that the Network Operator is encountering an error due to a missing namespace (oldproject). When attempting to update the operator configuration, it fails because it cannot create the specified NetworkAttachmentDefinition (myoldcni).- The additionalNetworks configured for the network.operator.openshift.io is likely referencing the oldproject namespace, which does not exist or is misspelled. As a result, the operator cannot apply the configuration as a NetworkAttachmentDefinition.

title: How to set Proxy environment variables in OpenShift Pipelines?
issue: How to set Proxy environment variables in OpenShift Pipelines?
resolution: Set proxy environment variables in task parameters like below, set values default or pass through Pipeline: kind: Task metadata: name: [...] spec: params:- default: "" description: | HTTP proxy server (non-TLS requests). name: HTTP_PROXY type: string- default: "" description: | HTTPS proxy server (TLS requests). name: HTTPS_PROXY type: string- default: "" description: | Opt out of proxying HTTP/HTTPS requests. name: NO_PROXY type: string [...] stepTemplate: env:- name: PARAMS_HTTP_PROXY value: $(params.HTTP_PROXY)- name: PARAMS_HTTPS_PROXY value: $(params.HTTPS_PROXY)- name: PARAMS_NO_PROXY value: $(params.NO_PROXY)- OR, Update `Operator` pod with proxy environment variables to run Tekton controllers, Webhook and also TaskRun pods with proxy configuration. Any taskRun pod under `openshift-pipeliens` will not use proxy environment variables by default. To use this in OpenShift Pipelines Operator need to update openshift-pipelines operator Subscription like below: apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: openshift-pipelines-operator-rh namespace: openshift-operators spec: config: env:- name: HTTP_PROXY value:- name: HTTPS_PROXY value:- name: NO_PROXY value:

title: Cluster upgrade blocked due to cluster operators monitoring and service-ca are degraded.
issue: - Error like below is observed on `monitoring` and `service-ca` cluster operators. **Operator: 'monitoring'*

~~~ Issue: Not available Reason: UpdatingConsolePluginComponentsFailed Message: reconciling Console Plugin Deployment failed: updating Deployment object failed: waiting for DeploymentRollout of openshift-monitoring/monitoring- plugin: context deadline exceeded LastTransition: 2024-11-29T12:38:40Z ~~~ **Operator: 'service-ca'*
~~~ Issue: Progressing Reason:_ManagedDeploymentsAvailable Message: Progressing: Progressing: service-ca does not have available replicas LastTransition: 2024-11-28T12:31:57Z ~~~
resolution: - Revoke the permissions from the group system:authenticated ~~~ oc adm policy remove-scc-from-group anyuid system:authenticated ~~~
root_cause: It is not supported to have **anyuid or any other SCC assigned directly to the "system:authenticated" group**, due to the fact it breaks internal components (like service-ca pod).

title: RHOAM data backups
issue: What RHOAM data is Red Hat backing up?
How often does Red Hat back up?
resolution: Red Hat is backing up all the databases that RHOAM requires. This includes: * 3scale system database * RHSSO x2 database * 3scale system Redis * 3scale backend Redis * Rate limiting Redis Red Hat doesn't back up the data stored in S3. The data is the customer developer portal data. Red Hat backups them every day at roughly 3AM UTC. Backups may also be performed by SRE on a demand basis.

title: How to specify platform.vsphere.failureDomains.topology.template in vSphere IPI OCP 4 cluster
issue: - As an administrator, I want to specify a pre-updated Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS (RHCOS) template/VM in install config- How to specify `platform.vsphere.failureDomains.topology.template` in vSphere IPI OCP 4 cluster
resolution: The `platform.vsphere.failureDomains.topology.template` field is usually in the following format: `/ /vm/ / ` You can check the path of the vm or template recursively with the following `govc` command: ``` $ govc ls /*/vm/* ```
root_cause: This parameter is mentioned in the [manual](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes#ocp-4-14-vsphere-pre-existing-template), but can not find how to specify it

title: OCP 4 IPI Installation on vsphere fails as the control plane node stuck in NotReady state
issue: - The OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) 4.x Installer-Provisioned Infrastructure (IPI) installation on vSphere fails as the control plane node is stuck in the NotReady state.
resolution: - This issue often occurs when OCP nodes cannot resolve or access the vCenter server using its hostname. Proper hostname resolution is critical for communication between OCP nodes and the vCenter server during installation- Ensure that all OCP nodes can resolve the vCenter hostname correctly. Use the following command on each node to verify: ~~~ # nslookup ~~~- Confirm that all OCP nodes can communicate with the vCenter server using its hostname. You can verify this using the ping command: ~~~ # ping ~~~- If the nodes cannot reach the vCenter server, troubleshoot network connectivity or firewall configurations to ensure proper communication.
root_cause: - The error log in the CCM pod: ~~~ E0313 13:18:36.140118 1 connection.go:67] Failed to create govmomi client. err: Post "https://vcenter.example.com:443/sdk": dial tcp: lookup vcenter.example.com: no such host E0313 13:18:36.140128 1 connectionmanager.go:147] Cannot connect to vCenter with err: Post "https://vcenter.example.com:443/sdk": dial tcp: lookup vcenter.example.com: no such ~~~

title: How to attach a secondary disk to the OCP node to save the kernel core dump
issue: - Sometimes, you may need to configure an OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) node to save kernel core dumps to a dedicated secondary disk.
resolution: - Create a script named find-secondary-device that identifies and formats the secondary disk. Replace with the appropriate device type for your setup (e.g., /dev/sd* or /dev/vd*). ~~~ #!/bin/bash set-uo pipefail for device in; do /usr/sbin/blkid "${device}" &> /dev/null if [$? == 2]; then echo "secondary device found ${device}" echo "creating filesystem for vmcore mount" mkfs.xfs-L vmcore-mount-f "${device}" &> /dev/null udevadm settle touch /etc/mnt-vmcore-mount exit fi done echo "Couldn't find secondary block device!" > &2 exit 77 ~~~- Encode the find-secondary-device script into a Base64 format. Replace with the actual content of the script: ~~~ # echo | base64-w0 ~~~- Create a MachineConfig file named mc.second.disk.mnt.vmcore.yaml. Replace with the Base64-encoded string from the previous step. ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 98-mnt-vmcore spec: config: ignition: version: 3.4.0 storage: files:- path: /etc/find-secondary-device mode: 0755 contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64, systemd: units:- name: find-secondary-device.service enabled: true contents: | [Unit] Description=Find secondary device DefaultDependencies=false After=systemd-udev-settle.service Before=local-fs-pre.target ConditionPathExists=!/etc/mnt-vmcore-mount [Service] RemainAfterExit=yes ExecStart=/etc/find-secondary-device RestartForceExitStatus=77 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target- name: mnt-vmcore.mount enabled: true contents: | [Unit] Description=Mount /mnt/vmcore Before=local-fs.target [Mount] What=/dev/disk/by-label/vmcore-mount Where=/mnt/vmcore Type=xfs TimeoutSec=120s [Install] RequiredBy=local-fs.target- name: restorecon-mnt-vmcore.service enabled: true contents: | [Unit] Description=Restore recursive SELinux security contexts DefaultDependencies=no After=mnt-vmcore.mount Before=kdump.service [Service] Type=oneshot RemainAfterExit=yes ExecStart=/sbin/restorecon-R /mnt/vmcore/ TimeoutSec=0 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target graphical.target ~~~- Apply the MachineConfig and check if the secondary disk is successfully mounted: ~~~ # oc create-f mc.second.disk.mnt.vmcore.yaml # mount | grep /mnt/vmcore ~~~- Update the /etc/kdump.conf file to set /mnt/vmcore as the directory for saving kernel core dumps. ~~~ path /mnt/vmcore ~~~- Restart the kdump service to apply the changes: ~~~ # systemctl restart kdump.service ~~~- Additional Note: Ensure that the secondary disk has sufficient storage capacity to accommodate kernel core dumps.

title: How to disable vSphere Problem Detector Operator health check errors in OpenShift
issue: - The vSphere Problem Detector Operator feature could trigger alerts that degrade the Storage Operator or other components when there is a lack of connectivity or the credentials are incorrect.- In some cases, this kind of behavior is intended by customers due to internal security policies.- The `VSphereOpenshiftClusterHealthFail` alert has been triggered and the vSphere Problem Detector logs show some or all of the messages below: ~~~ vsphere_check.go:236] CheckAccountPermissions failed: missing privileges for vcenter: Cns.Searchable, InventoryService.Tagging.AttachTag, InventoryService.Tagging.CreateCategory, InventoryService.Tagging.CreateTag, InventoryService.Tagging.DeleteCategory, InventoryService.Tagging.DeleteTag, InventoryService.Tagging.EditCategory, InventoryService.Tagging.EditTag, Sessions.ValidateSession, StorageProfile.Update, StorageProfile.View vsphere_check.go:236] CheckDefaultDatastore failed: defaultDatastore "datastoreName" in vSphere configuration: missing privileges for datastore datastoreName: Datastore.AllocateSpace, Datastore.Browse ~~~
resolution: - Starting from OpenShift 4.14 it is allowed opting-out from receiving vSphere Problem Detector alerts via a ConfigMap. The following ConfigMap example disable the alerts. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: vsphere-problem-detector namespace: openshift-cluster-storage-operator data: config.yaml: | alertsDisabled: true ~~~ **Note:** The `vsphere-problem-detector` pod will still keep collecting issues via logs and metrics, which can be useful to detect other problems.

title: Pipeline PVC is in pending status with error: no persistent volumes available for this claim and no storage class is set
issue: - After a successful update of the Pipelines operator, PVCs created by a `PipelineRun` remain in Pending status. ~~~ NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS VOLUMEATTRIBUTESCLASS AGE pvc-3230947924 Pending 22h ~~~- The events on the namespace where the `PipelineRun` is executed show a `FailedBinding` message. ~~~ LAST SEEN TYPE REASON OBJECT MESSAGE 3m29s Normal FailedBinding persistentvolumeclaim/pvc-3230947924 no persistent volumes available for this claim and no storage class is set ~~~- The `volumeClaimTemplate` in the `PipelineRun` spec shows the `storageClassName` value empty. ~~~ spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 1Gi storageClassName: "" volumeMode: Filesystem status: {} ~~~
resolution: - Reinstall the Pipelines Operator without removing the associated resources.- If the issue persists, [a full reinstall removing associated resources is required](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_pipelines/1.15/html-single/installing_and_configuring/index#installing-pipelines). Make sure of taking a backup of the pipelines resources before proceeding with this.

title: vsphere-plugin~Synchronization failed due to missing privileges for datastore
issue: - After changing the existent datastore to a new one, the cluster shows the alert `vsphere-plugin~Synchronization failed`.- The `vsphere-problem-detector-operator` log reports there are missing privileges for the old datastore. ~~~ 2025-02-13T22:10:59.284952686Z I0213 22:10:59.283985 1 datastore.go:125] CheckStorageClasses: thin-csi: storage policy openshift-storage-policy-xxxx-yyyy: missing privileges for datastore ds:///vmfs/volumes/aaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd/: Datastore.AllocateSpace, Datastore.Browse, Datastore.FileManagement 2025-02-13T23:11:29.218497391Z I0213 23:11:29.218375 1 event.go:364] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"Deployment", Namespace:"openshift-cluster-storage-operator", Name:"vsphere-problem-detector-operator", APIVersion:"apps/v1", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'FailedVSphereCheckStorageClasses' StorageClass thin-csi: storage policy openshift-storage-policy-xxxx-yyyy: missing privileges for datastore ds:///vmfs/volumes/aaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd/: Datastore.AllocateSpace, Datastore.Browse, Datastore.FileManagement ~~~
resolution: 1. Check the `openshift-storage-policy` shown in the error message to see if the old datastore is still included in the tags. 2. On vSphere, click on menu `Policies and Profiles`, then click on `VM Storage Policies`. An `Edit` option should appear, after clicking that option you should see the `Tags` and `Rules` assigned to the `Storage Policy`. 3. Remove the tag for the old datastore from the storage policy.
root_cause: - The `StorageClass` in the cluster have an associated `Storage Policy` that contains rules and tags to determine which datastores should use. When the datastore configuration is changed on the `cloud-provider-config` `ConfigMap` that information is not passed to the `StorageClass`.

title: Red Hat build of Keycloak Operator with an EDGE route
issue: - How to set up Red Hat build of Keycloak Operator with an EDGE route?
resolution: Edit the KeycloakCR by configuring httpEnabled option: ~~~ apiVersion: k8s.keycloak.org/v2alpha1 kind: Keycloak... spec:... hostname: hostname: my-sso-hostname.example.com http: httpEnabled: true proxy: headers: xforwarded ~~~ Create the edge route: ~~~ apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1 kind: Route... spec: host: my-sso-hostname.example.com port: targetPort: http tls: insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect termination: edge to: kind: Service name: example-kc-service weight: 100 wildcardPolicy: None ~~~

title: OpenShift container stuck in ContainerCreating with error "multipath device not found when it is expected" using NetApp Trident and multipath
issue: - The dynamic provisioning fails and the containers could not start with `FailedMount` errors.- Kubelet reports the errors shown below: ~~~ type="Warning" reason="FailedMount" message="MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume \"pvc-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxx\": rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to stage volume: multipath device not found when it is expected" ~~~
resolution: - A temporary workaround is to drain and reboot the affected node. That will clear all the failed multipaths.- The bug fix should be on NetApp trident after version 22.
root_cause: - NetApp trident up to version 22.10 has a bug in its self healing feature which causes it to discover every LUN on the initiator even if that device isn't being used on a node.

title: How to check ServiceAccount token expiry in RHOCP4
issue: - How to check when a ServiceAccount token will expire?- How to save the ServiceAccount token expiry date/time?
resolution: - Use the following steps to create a service account, generate a token with a defined expiry, and decode it to check the expiration timestamp- 1. Create a service account: ~~~ $ oc create sa ~~~ 2. Generate a token and save it: ~~~ TOKEN-SA-NAME=$($ oc create token--duration=60m-n) ~~~ 3. Check the expiry of this token: ~~~ $ echo $TOKEN-SA-NAME | cut-d "."-f2 | base64--decode | jq ~~~ 4. Copy the exp value from the above command output. 5. Check the date/time of expiry: ~~~ # date-d @ ~~~- Ensure the exp timestamp is in the future compared to the current system time to confirm validity.

title: Pipeline Server Internal MariaDB Will Not Deploy with InnoDB Error
issue: When configuring a PipelineServer in a Red Hat OpenShift AI Data Science Project using the `Use default database stored on your cluster` option, the MariaDB Pod will not start properly and displays an InnoDB error. The Pod logs may look something like this: ``` => sourcing 20-validate-variables.sh... => sourcing 25-validate-replication-variables.sh... => sourcing 30-base-config.sh...---> 17:16:44 Processing basic MySQL configuration files... => sourcing 60-replication-config.sh... => sourcing 70-s2i-config.sh...---> 17:16:44 Processing additional arbitrary MySQL configuration provided by s2i... => sourcing 40-paas.cnf... => sourcing 50-my-tuning.cnf...---> 17:16:44 Initializing database...---> 17:16:44 Running mysql_install_db... 2025-04-17 17:16:44 0 [ERROR] InnoDB: Corrupted page [page id: space=0, page number=0] of datafile './ibdata1' could not be found in the doublewrite buffer. 2025-04-17 17:16:44 0 [ERROR] InnoDB: Plugin initialization aborted with error Data structure corruption 2025-04-17 17:16:45 0 [ERROR] Plugin 'InnoDB' init function returned error. 2025-04-17 17:16:45 0 [ERROR] Plugin 'InnoDB' registration as a STORAGE ENGINE failed. 2025-04-17 17:16:45 0 [ERROR] Unknown/unsupported storage engine: InnoDB 2025-04-17 17:16:45 0 [ERROR] Aborting ```

title: OpenShift Assisted Installation fails with 'connection refused' for slow-installing nodes
issue: An OpenShift Container Platform installation using the Assisted Installer (agent-based) fails for one or more nodes.
During the installation, a node with slower hardware (e.g., HDD storage) takes a long time to write the Red Hat CoreOS (RHCOS) image to disk.

Before the slow node can complete its installation and check in, the bootstrap node (which runs the `assisted-service`) finishes its own tasks and reboots to transition into its final role as a control plane node.

When the bootstrap node reboots, the `assisted-service` API becomes unavailable. The slow-installing node, still trying to communicate, begins to log `connection refused` errors: ```text May 12 05:58:22 worker-1.example.com next_step_runne[6121]: time="12-05-2025 05:58:22" level=error msg="Step processing failed, will try again in 509.800243ms: could not query next steps: Get \"http://[assisted-service-ip]:8090/api/assisted-install/v2/infra-envs/[infra-env-uuid]/hosts/[host-uuid]/instructions?timestamp=[timestamp]\": dial tcp [assisted-service-ip]:8090: connect: connection refused" file="step_processor.go:300" ```
Eventually, the slow node's installation attempt fails, and it may revert to a "pending registration" or similar state.
resolution: The solution is to investigate and correct the underlying infrastructure issue that is causing poor disk write performance or slow image download speeds. The Assisted Installer is not designed to compensate for hardware or network infrastructure that does not meet the performance requirements for a stable OpenShift cluster. * **Check Local Disk Write Speed:** The most common cause is the write performance of the node's local disk. Use the `dd` test in the **Diagnostic Steps** below to measure this. Ensure the nodes have enterprise-grade SSDs rather than HDDs. * **Check Image Source Performance:** Ensure that the web server or other source hosting the Red Hat CoreOS (RHCOS) image is reachable from the nodes and providing adequate download speeds. Network latency or a slow source server can delay the initial step of fetching the image before it is written to disk. * **Investigate Virtualization Layer:** If using virtual machines, examine the underlying datastore (SAN, vSAN, NAS) and hypervisor configuration for performance bottlenecks, high latency, or misconfigurations that could affect either disk I/O or network throughput. * **Review Server and RAID Configuration:** On bare metal nodes, inspect the server's BIOS/UEFI settings and the disk controller (RAID) configuration to ensure they are optimized for performance. Check for faulty hardware, such as failing disks, cables, or controllers.
root_cause: * The direct cause is that the node's disk I/O performance is insufficient to complete the RHCOS image write within the time limit expected by the Assisted Installer. * The agent-based installation process has internal timeouts that assume a baseline of adequate hardware performance. * When a node's installation is significantly delayed by slow disk writes, the overall process can time out. In a bootstrap-in-place scenario, the bootstrap node may proceed to reboot into its final control plane role, terminating the `assisted-service` and causing any remaining nodes that are still installing to fail.

title: OpenShift Data Foundation  fresh deployment with external mode - noobaa-db-pg-0 pod always pending
issue: - Fresh deployment with OpenShift Data Foundation in external mode- Only the "noobaa-db-pg-0" pod is in pending mode.
resolution: - First, review the docs on how to deploy for external mode, refer to [deployment guide](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.15/html-single/deploying_openshift_data_foundation_in_external_mode/index)- Make sure all operators are installed. Please verify all the operators via [Verify that the following pods are in running state](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.15/html/deploying_openshift_data_foundation_in_external_mode/deploy-openshift-data-foundation-using-red-hat-ceph-storage#verifying_the_state_of_the_pods)- Make sure the versions match between external ceph all use Python3 commands, refer to [python3 ceph-external-cluster-details-exporter.py](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.15/html/deploying_openshift_data_foundation_in_external_mode/deploy-openshift-data-foundation-using-red-hat-ceph-storage) (*Important: Use python instead of python3 if the Red Hat Ceph Storage 4.x cluster is deployed on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.x (RHEL 7.x) cluster*)- Cross-check if there are any networking/DNS/default namespace mismatch issues. ~~~ cat /etc/resolv.conf nslookup ~~~- Review whether cephcluster is connected or not, and whether storagecluster is ready or not. ~~~ ping ~~~ Refer to [cephcluster](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.15/html/deploying_openshift_data_foundation_in_external_mode/deploy-openshift-data-foundation-using-red-hat-ceph-storage#verifying_that_ceph_cluster_is_connected) and [storagecluster](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.15/html/deploying_openshift_data_foundation_in_external_mode/deploy-openshift-data-foundation-using-red-hat-ceph-storage#verifying_that_storage_cluster_is_ready)- expected outputs are: ~~~ cephcluster: $ oc get cephcluster-n openshift-storage NAME DATADIRHOSTPATH MONCOUNT AGE PHASE MESSAGE HEALTH EXTERNAL ocs-external-storagecluster-cephcluster 30m Connected Cluster connected successfully HEALTH_OK true storagecluster: $ oc get storagecluster-n openshift-storage NAME AGE PHASE EXTERNAL CREATED AT VERSION ocs-external-storagecluster 30m Ready true 2021-11-17T09:09:52Z 4.15.0 ~~~- Make sure there is no OOM killed or resource issues from Nodes, and make sure no tainted issues either. ~~~ oc get events-A | grep OOMKILL ~~~- Jumping into the CSI pods, run curl noobaa-mgmt to eliminate issues with networking ~~~ oc get pod-n openshift-storage | grep csi openshift-storage csi-cephfsplugin-xxx 2/2 Running 9 78d openshift-storage csi-rbdplugin-xxx 3/3 Running 11 78d oc rsh csi-cephfsplugin-xx-n openshift-storage curl ~~~- Review the external Ceph healthy status and especially review the OSD/Mon and Public networks, make sure all OSDs are able to talk to the monitors.- In the external Ceph review. ~~~ #ceph-s #ceph health detail ~~~
root_cause: - There may be issues with the external Ceph cluster itself, even though the `CephCluster` ODF object shows ODF is connected successfully.- Also, verify the public network connects to ensure the OSDs and MONs on the external Ceph cluster are connected.- Although from cephcluster it seems all connected, the public network has to make sure all are connected between all OSDs and Monitors. Some customers have newly deployed OSDs but not fully connected to the monitors.

title: "Error: OCI runtime error: crun: cgroups in hybrid mode not supported, drop all controllers from cgroupv2"
issue: - Nodes are in `NotReady` state after reboot.- `crio` and `podman` are unable to start containers, fails with below error: ~~~ "Error: OCI runtime error: crun: cgroups in hybrid mode not supported, drop all controllers from cgroupv2" ~~~
resolution: - The cgroup version can be set cluster wide using the below configuration. In the spec section of the configuration file, add or modify the `cgroupMode` field: ~~~ $ oc edit nodes.config.openshift.io cluster spec: cgroupMode: v2 <--- Mention either v2 or v1 as per need. ~~~ Save the changes and wait for the nodes to reboot. The Machine Config Operator (MCO) will apply the new configuration to all nodes in the cluster, which will involve a rolling reboot. ###### To rescue a node which has both the `cgroup` modes enabled, perform the below steps: 1. Reboot the node and interrupt the boot loader countdown by pressing any key. 2. Move the cursor to the entry that needs to be booted and press `e` to edit the selected entry. 3. Move the cursor to the kernel command line (the line that starts with `linux`) and remove the `systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0` entry or the argument which is causing the conflict. Make sure the same mode set is same as the cluster wide `cgroupMode`. 4. Press `Ctrl +x` to save the changes and reboot the system. 5. Once `kubelet` and `crio` are up, force the desired render on the node. If the issues persist or unexpected behavior occurs, submit a new [Technical Support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true)
root_cause: - Starting with OpenShift 4.14, cgroupv2 is the default for new installations. `cgroupv1 ` and `cgroupv2` cannot be enabled simultaneously on a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster.

title: Volume size of clairpostgres pvc cannot be overridden
issue: - Volume size of the clairpostgres pvc cannot be overridden via `clairpostgres` component in the quayregistry CR
resolution: - VolumeSize `overrides` feature for clair postgres pvc can be used via clair component not via clair-postgres component. Set volumesize in the Quay registry CR: ~~~ $ oc edit quayregistry-n- kind: clair managed: true overrides: volumeSize: 100Gi ~~~- Wait for the operator to reconcile and pods to be up and running, check the pvc size and notice the default pvc size 50Gi has changed to 100Gi. ~~~ $ oc get pvc-n NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS VOLUMEATTRIBUTESCLASS AGE example-registry-clair-postgres-13 Bound pvc-3af3c6d1-9d81-4342-ac71-b4b5f88fedeb 100Gi RWO gp3-csi 19m example-registry-quay-postgres-13 Bound pvc-ef085eb5-8031-4283-a996-b068b9c9775e 50Gi RWO gp3-csi 19m ~~~- Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [PROJQUAY-4301](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-4301) and delivered a fix in Quay operator v3.13. If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: VolumeSize `overrides` is not supported for clair-postgres component until version 3.12.x of Quay Operator based deployment.

title: Web Terminal operator discloses proxy detail in RHOCP 4
issue: - When the web terminal is accessed, environmental variables show proxy details such as credentials.- Proxy credentials are visible while using Web Terminal.
resolution: - This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in internal Bug. For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. **Workaround**- If it is required to remove the proxy env variables for normal users, it can be achieved by disabling the proxy env propagation globally by creating this resource as follows: ~~~ $ cat > devworkspace.yaml < < EOF apiVersion: controller.devfile.io/v1alpha1 kind: DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig metadata: name: devworkspace-operator-config namespace: config: routing: proxyConfig: httpProxy: "" httpsProxy: "" noProxy: "" EOF $ oc create-f devworkspace.yaml ~~~ This will result in the proxy env variables being unavailable for all web terminals.- If it is needed to have the environment vars just for admins, please try adding a secret in the `openshift-terminal` namespace: ~~~ $ cat > my-secret.yaml < < EOF apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: my-secret namespace: openshift-terminal labels: controller.devfile.io/mount-to-devworkspace: 'true' controller.devfile.io/watch-secret: 'true' annotations: controller.devfile.io/mount-as: 'env' stringData: no_proxy: https_proxy: EOF $ oc create-f my-secret.yaml ~~~ This will mount the data as environment variables to the web terminals started by admins in the `openshift-terminal` namespace

title: How to check and confirm whether the garbage collection is working or not in RHOCP 4?
issue: - How to check the values set up for garbage collection in OCP?- After customizing the garbage collection on RHOCP nodes, how to verify if the custom settings are applied?
resolution: - This [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-garbage-collection.html) can be referred to customize the built-in garbage collection.- Verify the default settings with the below command: ~~~ $ oc get--raw /api/v1/nodes/$NODE/proxy/configz | jq-r '.kubeletconfig | with_entries(select(.key | contains("GC"))) ' {"imageMinimumGCAge": "2m0s", "imageGCHighThresholdPercent": 85, "imageGCLowThresholdPercent": 80} ~~~- Check the below sample yaml file to customize garbage collection: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: KubeletConfig metadata: name: worker-kubeconfig spec: machineConfigPoolSelector: matchLabels: custom-kubelet: small-pods kubeletConfig: evictionSoft: memory.available: "500Mi" nodefs.available: "10%" nodefs.inodesFree: "5%" imagefs.available: "15%" imagefs.inodesFree: "10%" evictionSoftGracePeriod: memory.available: "1m30s" nodefs.available: "1m30s" nodefs.inodesFree: "1m30s" imagefs.available: "1m30s" imagefs.inodesFree: "1m30s" evictionHard: memory.available: "200Mi" nodefs.available: "5%" nodefs.inodesFree: "4%" imagefs.available: "10%" imagefs.inodesFree: "5%" evictionPressureTransitionPeriod: 0s imageMinimumGCAge: 5m imageGCHighThresholdPercent: 30 <---- Change value here as per the requirement imageGCLowThresholdPercent: 25 <---- Change value here as per the requirement ~~~- Create the object: ~~~ $ oc create-f.yaml ~~~- After applying the mc the value set up can be checked in the kubelet.conf of each node: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host # cat /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf ~~~- Check that the garbage collection is running with the customized thresholds set by looking at the journalctl logs of the `kubelet`: ~~~ Jul 01 06:28:25 worker-0.akash4.xx.xx.xx.com hyperkube[1446]: I0701 06:28:25.174179 1446 image_gc_manager.go:305] [imageGCManager]: Disk usage on image filesystem is at 31% which is over the high threshold (30%). Trying to free 2250769408 bytes down to the low threshold (25%). Jul 01 06:28:25 worker-0.akash4.xx.xx.xx.redhat.com hyperkube[1446]: I0701 06:28:25.192412 1446 image_gc_manager.go:376] [imageGCManager]: Removing image "16d409e28813fd38f926258d70eb7611f19acdef07c927f82e6077f9f1c59649" to free 255819633 bytes Jul 01 06:28:25 worker-0.akash4.xx.xx.xx.redhat.com hyperkube[1446]: I0701 06:28:25.194096 1446 image_gc_manager.go:376] [imageGCManager]: Removing image "229dbdee63b061c21623adb8ae30dad4ad25ddf8f48b3ffca0509a95bf9b0d13" to free 309609321 bytes Jul 01 06:28:25 worker-0.akash4.xx.xx.xx.redhat.com hyperkube[1446]: I0701 06:28:25.194982 1446 image_gc_manager.go:376] [imageGCManager]: Removing image "83f1d60a9c2d4dd141cc379620ad1b4fdc59d1555ccf0a064996fc102931c9f2" to free 297758628 bytes Jul 01 06:28:25 worker-0.akash4.xx.xx.xx.redhat.com hyperkube[1446]: I0701 06:28:25.286380 1446 image_gc_manager.go:376] [imageGCManager]: Removing image "32ec6737584b438a8b7e6b594fba19599f464a722b18e461cfdb3359f5877b6b" to free 262075930 bytes Jul 01 07:33:37 worker-0.akash4.lab.xx.xx.xx.com hyperkube[1446]: I0701 07:33:37.614014 1446 image_gc_manager.go:376] [imageGCManager]: Removing image "d93101477816e4d259c0296060f9aae2338ac98f3ee8d4b73a9e07c708cf45e6" to free 369426034 bytes ~~~

title: Crio split logs into multiple lines stored at /var/log/containers/*.log
issue: - On CoreOS host logs are stored at /var/log/containers/*.log and these logs are sent to Splunk. Crio splits these logs into multiple lines.- Logs from build pod gets split into multiple lines by crio. Is there a way to merge it and get just one log line? ~~~ [...] 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957601404+00:00 stdout P [INFO] DM:: TEST:: Messagi 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957613838+00:00 stdout P ng:: Pa 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957623665+00:00 stdout P yloa 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957633327+00:00 stdout P d DM- 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957643860+00:00 stdout P ES.. 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957653967+00:00 stdout P...... SUCC 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957663734+00:00 stdout P ESS 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957673538+00:00 stdout P [0 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957683290+00:00 stdout P.471 2020-10-05T04:38:15.957693080+00:00 stdout F s] ~~~
resolution: - Crio uses the CRI log format and writes to the log file as it keeps reading chunks from the process. The log file written by Crio is processed by kubectl logs to display the original log. Whenever the line splits there is a P annotation in the log. And the line will have a F whenever we see a new line emitted by the container process.- If a container writes 'some text1 text2 text3\n'. It could end up in the raw unprocessed log files as: ~~~ P some tex1 P text2 F text3 ~~~ Or ~~~ F some text1 text2 text3 ~~~ Or ~~~ P some text1 text2 F text3 ~~~- Over here `P` indicates the line is partial, and `F` indicates that it is the final part of the line. The line splits could happen anywhere, but after processing by `kubectl log` (or other log consumers) the original log line can be reproduced back to `some text1 text2 text3\n` looking at `P` and `F` annotations.

title: OpenShift GitOps: Using `argocd_app_sync_total` Metric fails to Notify Sync Failed Applications correctly
issue: - Using `argocd_app_sync_total` Metric fails to Notify Sync Failed Applications correctly.- Using `argocd_app_sync_total` Metric Alerts are firing continuously even when the Application is in Synced and Healthy State: apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: argocd-app-sync namespace: openshift-gitops spec: groups:- name: ArgoCD rules:- alert: ArgoAppSyncFailed annotations: summary: '''{{$labels.name}}'' Application has sync phase as ''{{$labels.phase}}''' expr: argocd_app_sync_total{phase!="Succeeded",dest_server="https://kubernetes.default.svc"} == 1 for: 1m labels: severity: warning
resolution: Use `argocd_app_info` like below in PrometheusRule: apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: argocd-app-sync namespace: openshift-gitops spec: groups:- name: ArgoCD rules:- alert: ArgoAppSyncFailed annotations: summary: '''{{$labels.name}}'' Application has sync phase as ''{{$labels.phase}}''' expr: max(argocd_app_info{sync_status!="Synced"}) by (name, namespace) == 1 for: 1m labels: severity: warning
root_cause: - The `argocd_app_sync_total` Metric is a `counter` type metric which is not good/suitable for Application state checks.- Counter Metric keeps on increasing it's value for matching expression and because of that alert doesn't go away even after state of Application gets in Synced and Healthy state as counter will always be `1` till the time Application Sync fails again and counter increase to `2`.

title: OCP 4: Storage degradation may lead to API instability
issue: - Web console and oc/kubectl commands time out against one or more clusters.- API-server pods log repeated messages similar to: ~~~ patch_genericapiserver.go:204] Request to "/api/v1/namespaces/openshift-etcd/pods/etcd-example.local" (source IP X.X.X.X:50454, user agent "cluster-etcd-operator/v0.0.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/$Format") before server is ready, possibly a sign for a broken load balancer setup. ~~~- etcdctl member health on master nodes reports unhealthy or long write latencies (> 1 s).- Load balancer may mark all API targets DOWN.
resolution: - Verify storage health on the platform that hosts etcd disks (vSAN, Ceph, SAN, RAID controller).- Look for `rebuild`, `reduced availability`, or `resync` indicators.- Allow rebuild or resync operations to complete until storage returns to a healthy state.- Confirm etcd write latency < 200 ms and that etcd etcdctl member health returns healthy. A healthy cluster may include timestamps of greater than 200ms, but consistent repeated reports of over 1s can be a sign of a larger performance problem that will impact API performance and cluster health ~~~ for i in $(oc get pod-n openshift-etcd | grep-Ev 'NAME|prune|guard' | awk {'print $1'}); do echo $i; oc-n openshift-etcd logs $i-c etcd | grep "took too long" | awk-F ',' {'print $2,$5'} | tail-n 10; done ~~~- Prevent recurrence by:- Placing etcd data on a dedicated disk that does not rebuild across nodes. RAID can be considered fast enough for etcd, but during a rebuild from a parity based RAID storage host, Disk IO is severely degraded and may lead to performance instability on master nodes which require much faster performance. etcd cannot withstand disk repair procedures.- Monitoring storage health and latency with alerts that page the on-call team.
root_cause: - When shared storage enters a degraded or rebuild state, parity RAID (e.g., RAID-5/6) or distributed erasure coding dramatically increases write latency. etcd cannot commit within its deadline, causing the Kubernetes API server to fail readiness checks. The load balancer then refuses connections, making cluster consoles unreachable even though worker traffic may remain unaffected.- Raid storage can be considered fast enough for ETCD, but during a rebuild process from a degraded storage host, disk i/o is severely degraded and leads to performance instability on master nodes that require much faster performance. (Etcd cannot operate properly on a disk that is being reconstructed)

title: NMState changes are not getting reflected on the RHOCP node
issue: - NMState changes are not getting reflected on the RHOCP node.- NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy (NNCP) was successfully configured via a YAML manifest, but the expected network changes are not being applied to the node.
resolution: - Take SSH of the affected node and switch the user to root. ~~~ $ ssh core@ $ sudo-i ~~~- Restart the `on-prem-resolv-prepender.service` service to sync the DNS and NetworkManager of the node. ~~~ $ systemctl restart on-prem-resolv-prepender.service ~~~- Check if the service has restarted successfully. ~~~ $ systemctl status on-prem-resolv-prepender.service $ journalctl-u on-prem-resolv-prepender.service--no-pager ~~~- Verify if the changes are reflected on the node. ~~~ $ cat /var/run/NetworkManager/resolv.conf # Generated by NetworkManager search example.com nameserver X.X.X.X nameserver Y.Y.Y.Y ~~~ ~~~ $ cat /etc/resolv.conf # Generated by NetworkManager search example.com nameserver X.X.X.X nameserver Y.Y.Y.Y ~~~
root_cause: - The `on-prem-resolv-prepender.service` is a custom system service that modifies DNS settings, likely by appending or prioritizing on-premises DNS servers in the resolver configuration.- Usually, after configuring a NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy (NNCP) CR, the `on-prem-resolv-prepender.service` service is expected to restart automatically on the desired nodes. However, in some cases it does not restart as expected, preventing NMState network changes from taking effect.

title: How to use HTTPS endpoints for Ignition in RHOCP 4
issue: Does `coreos-installer` support HTTPS endpoints for the `ignition_url` parameter during the installation of the RHOCP 4?

Using `coreos-installer` without `--insecure-ignition` gives the following error: ~~~ $ coreos-installer install-I https://xyz.example.com/path/to/ignition.ign--copy-network error: failed to fetch ignition config: error sending request for url (https://xyz.example.com/path/to/ignition.ign): error trying to connect: tls handshake failure ~~~
resolution: The `coreos-installer` now supports HTTPS endpoints for the `ignition_url` parameter, a functionality that has been available since OpenShift 4.6. To fix the `TLS handshake failure` error during the UPI installation using `coreos-installer`, follow these steps on **each node**: 1. Fetch the certificate from HTTPS url: ~~~ $ openssl s_client-connect:-showcerts /dev/null | openssl x509-outform PEM > certficate.pem ~~~ 2. Copy the above generated certificate `certificate.pem` file into `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/` directory on the node and update the CA trust list: ~~~ $ cp certificate.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ $ update-ca-trust ~~~ 3. Add an entry in the `/etc/hosts` file on all nodes to resolve the web server’s hostname to the correct IP address (If network DNS does not resolve the web server url): ~~~ $ xyz.example.com ~~~ 4. Once the node network settings have been configured, run the `coreos-installer`, which will validate the SSL certificate and initiate the installation process. ~~~ $ coreos-installer install-I https://xyz.example.com/path/to/ignition.ign--copy-network ~~~
root_cause: The [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GRPA-2058) was raised regarding the HTTPS endpoint functionality for coreos-installer which was closed and the RFE was merged since OCP version 4.6.

title: Quay.io login error e-mail address is already associated with an existing Quay account
issue: Trying to login, but a warning message `Red Hat login error` with the following text. ~~~ "The e-mail address `user@example.com` is already associated with an existing Quay account. Please log in with your username and password and associate your Red Hat account to use it in the future." ~~~
resolution: The error message could be rectified through the implementation of the following steps: 1. Please go to [https://recovery.quay.io/signin](https://recovery.quay.io/signin) 2. Sign in with a existing Quay.io email address and password. 3. Once in, open account settings, click on "External logins" on the left side, and then on the "Attach to Red Hat" link. 4. Go to [quay.io/signin](https://quay.io/signin) and enter a Red Hat Customer Portal credentials and it should be set, Red Hat SSO button should work now. > **Note:** If needed try to Detach, open account settings, click on "External logins" on the left side, and then on the "Detach Account" and reattach when in recovery mode.
root_cause: All accounts in Quay must have unique e-mail addresses and usernames. The issue here is that there exists a user under e-mail in Quay's db. Logging in with a user with the same e-mail address will not work because users are not connected via a special table in Quay's db and Quay will perceive logging in via that button as though a new user is coming in. Quay will then check if the e-mail address is unique and will find that it is not and will error out.

title: Data Grid Operator 8.4.x and 8.5.x spec.version feature
resolution: ### Using multiple versions of Data Grid (not Data Grid Operator versions) Starting on DG Operator 8.4.x (channel 8.4.x) a feature to use more than one DG cluster version in the same DG Operator version. This tackles the problem of having only one DG Operator version in the whole cluster, given the CRDs are saved on the etcd global cluster section. This limitation [still exist](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6956600). The user can have a single Data Grid Operator installation that supports multiple versions of Data Grid. For doing so use `spec.version` field in your Infinispan CR to upgrade between supported versions. Supported Data Grid versions by each Data Grid Operator version are listed in the Release Notes for Data Grid Operator:- 8.4.x:- 8.5.x: Note that Data Grid Operator versions do not always directly correspond to Data Grid versions because the release schedule is different.
