Message: admission webhook "vinfinispan.kb.io" denied the request: Infinispan.infinispan.org "dgtest" is invalid: spec.version: Invalid value: "8.5.0-1": unknown version: 8.5.0-1. Received status: Status(apiVersion=v1, code=422, details=StatusDetails(causes=[StatusCause(field=spec.version, message=Invalid value: "8.5.0-1": unknown version: 8.5.0-1, reason=FieldValueInvalid, additionalProperties={})], group=infinispan.org, kind=Infinispan, name=dgtest, retryAfterSeconds=null, uid=null, additionalProperties={}), kind=Status, message=admission webhook "vinfinispan.kb.io" denied the request: Infinispan.infinispan.org "dgtest" is invalid: spec.version: Invalid value: "8.5.0-1": unknown version: 8.5.0-1, metadata=ListMeta(_continue=null, remainingItemCount=null, resourceVersion=null, selfLink=null, additionalProperties={}), reason=Invalid, status=Failure, additionalProperties={}). ~~~
root_cause: The `spec.image` is a mandatory field on the Infinispan Custom resource that sets the image on the DG pods to be used. The fact it is mandatory means if the user creates a custom resource without spec, the Operator will fill the `spec.version` with a certain value. On this case can be 8.3.1 (in case of a upgrade or custom image) or 8.4.2-latest. Not just that but the `spec.version` will overwrite the image that user sets on the custom resource and using a custom image won't be possible.

title: How to remove Alert PrometheusTSDBCompactionsFailing due to the disk for Prometheus becoming full
issue: - Alert PrometheusTSDBCompactionsFailing 1. What is the alert about? 2. Will this impact our services?- Before this, we had the same alert with error message in logs (no space left in device) and we decide to extend /prometheus disk.- After extend the disk we still got this alert but with different message in logs: ~~~ (err="WAL truncation in Compact: create checkpoint: read segments: corruption in segment /prometheus/wal/000xxxxx at 12xxxxxx: unexpected full record") ~~~- Relates to Prometheus using permanent storage not ephemeral storage
resolution: It looks like there's an issue with Prometheus due to the disk for Prometheus becoming full. As this is just for monitoring, the pod can be safely deleted and then re-provisioned. This won't be of impact to the other pods in the cluster; this just involves the monitoring in `openshift-monitoring` namespace. If `user workload monitoring` is targeted, only the `prometheus-user-workload-X` pods in the `openshift-user-workload-monitoring` namespace will be affected. Once it's fixed, all should return back to normal. 1. Get the pods running (should be 2) ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0 prometheus-k8s-1 ```- If using `user workload monitoring`, check it with the following command (should be 2) ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring prometheus-user-workload-0 prometheus-user-workload-1 ``` 2. Scale the replicas down from 2 to 0 to remove the Prometheus pods and their data ``` $ oc patch prometheuses-n openshift-monitoring k8s--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"replicas":0}}' ```- If using `user workload monitoring`, set the replicas in the `user-workload` custom resource from 2 to 0 ``` $ oc patch prometheuses-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring user-workload--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"replicas":0}}' ``` 3. Validate no pods output; once none return, go to step 4 ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0 prometheus-k8s-1 ```- If using `user workload monitoring`, check it with the following command ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring prometheus-user-workload-0 prometheus-user-workload-1 ``` 4. Scale back up to 2 replicas ``` $ oc patch prometheuses-n openshift-monitoring k8s--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"replicas":2}}' ```- If using `user workload monitoring`, set the replicas field in the `user-workload` custom resource back to 2 ``` $ oc patch prometheuses-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring user-workload--type=merge--patch='{"spec":{"replicas":2}}' ``` 5. Confirm 2 pods have come back ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0 prometheus-k8s-1 ```- If using `user workload monitoring`, confirm it with the following command ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-user-workload-monitoring prometheus-user-workload-0 prometheus-user-workload-1 ```
root_cause: Both 'prometheus-k8s' pods ran out of space and became corrupt. The pods were redeployed and the issue was resolved. The reason for the WAL corruption was due to the disk becoming full (no space left in device). When it got full, the WAL got corrupted so extending the disk wasn't going to fix the WAL. They just needed to delete the WAL. By scaling the prometheus-k8s pods down to 0, we're deleting them and their data (WAL) and then scaling back up to 2 replicas to basically rebuild them.

title: Decouple trusted CA configmap creation from RBAC resource creation in TektonConfig
issue: - Is it possible to manage the auto generation of CA bundle configmap and other RBAC resources by OpenShift Pipelines operator separately?- How can we edit TektonConfig to manage CA bundle configmaps and RBAC resources created by OpenShift Pipelines operator?
resolution: - Currently the `createRbacResource` flag in TektonConfig, disables/enables the creation of both RBAC resources and trusted CA configmaps together.- A [feature request](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SRVKP-7716) is created with the Red Hat Engineering to remove this tight coupling to be able to manage the configmaps and RBAC resources separately. If this feature is required, please [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: Apicurio Registry 3.x Operator Fails to Start with TimeoutException and Thread blocked WARNs
product: Red Hat build of Apicurio Registry
issue: - Apicurio Registry 3.x operator fails to start correctly.- The operator pod exhibits TimeoutException and Thread blocked warnings in its logs.
resolution: Increase the resource limits and requests for the Apicurio Registry 3 operator pod. Example resource configuration for the operator's YAML: ``` resources: limits: cpu: 1 memory: 2Gi requests: cpu: 1 memory: 2Gi ```
root_cause: In some environments, the operator requires more resources than its default configuration provides to communicate effectively with the OpenShift API and deserialize dependent resources.

title: Operator Subscriptions not visible and gives warning on OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: - When attempting to list `Operator Lifecycle Manager` (OLM) `Subscriptions` using the `oc command-line tool` with the short name sub fails or produces unexpected results as below: ~~~ $ oc get sub-A Warning: short name "sub" could also match lower priority resource subscriptions.operators.coreos.com No resources found. ~~~- A Pipeline job fails to run due to missing subscriptions. ~~~ Error message: 'Error from server (Forbidden): subscriptions.messaging.knative.dev is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:group-sync-operator:wait-install-job" cannot list resource "subscriptions" in API group "messaging.knative.dev" at the cluster scope'. ~~~
resolution: - To avoid ambiguity, do not use the `sub` short name. Instead, use the unambiguous short name `subs` or the full resource name `subscriptions.operators.coreos.com` in all scripts and manual commands.
root_cause: - The issue is caused by a short name collision between two or more different resources on the cluster. 1. The `Operator Lifecycle Manager` (OLM) provides the `subscriptions.operators.coreos.com` resource, which uses the short names `sub` and `subs`. 2. The OpenShift Serverless Operator, when installed, introduces the `subscriptions.messaging.knative.dev` `Custom Resource Definition (CRD)`, which also uses the short name `sub.`

title: OpenShift automatic etcd defragmentation detection cycle
issue: How to check automatic `etcd` defragmentation detection cycle and triggering conditions?
resolution: - [By default](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/release-4.19/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go), the defrag controller checks if a defragmentation is needed every 11 minutes (the 10 minutes of [compaction interval](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/release-4.19/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L34) plus [1 additional minute](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/release-4.19/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L78)).- It [checks](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/release-4.19/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L304) whether `[(DbSize- DbSizeInUse) / DbSize]` is greater than `maxFragmentedPercentage`, which is [hardcoded as 45%](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/release-4.19/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L31), and `DbSize` is greater than `minDefragBytes`, which is [hardcoded as 100MB](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/main/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L29). If both these conditions are met, defrag is triggered.

title: How to install a cluster using "ImageDigestMirrorSet" in the install-config.yaml on Red Hat Openshift Container Platform 4
issue: Creating disconnected clusters in latest versions are still getting created using "ImageContentSourcePolicy" CR instead on the "ImageDigestMirrorSet".
resolution: The user needs to replace in the install-config.yaml the "imageContentSources" with the "imageDigestSources" like below: **From this:** ~~~ imageContentSources:- source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release mirrors:- registry.example:5000/ocp-release- source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev mirrors:- registry.example:5000/ocp-v4.0-art-dev ~~~ **To this:** ~~~ imageDigestSources:- source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release mirrors:- registry.example:5000/ocp-release- source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev mirrors:- registry.example:5000/ocp-v4.0-art-dev ~~~
root_cause: This is not mentioned in our documentation and for the same a [bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSDOCS-4982#) is opened to be fixed.

title: "CsvAbnormalFailedOver30Min" Alert Triggered After Upgrading to OpenShift 4.15 in RHOCP4
issue: - Getting an alert for `CsvAbnormalOver30Min` after upgrading to 4.15.
resolution: - To resolve this issue, Kindly follow the below steps- Kindly remove the CSV which are stuck in Replacing state using below command. ~~~ $ oc delete csv < csv_name > ~~~- And restart the `catalog-operator` and `olm-operator` pods from `openshift-operators-lifecycle-manager` namespace. ~~~ $ oc delete pod catalog-operator-xxx-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager $ oc delete pod olm-operator-xxx-n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager ~~~
root_cause: - The `CsvAbnormalFailedOver30Min` alert fires when a ClusterServiceVersion of any operator remains in a Failed state for more than 30 minutes.

title: ACM/Openshift console displaying BMH's status as 'Powering on'.

BMH state of the nodes remains in "Powering on" state, even after deployment of spoke cluster.

title: "Permission Denied" on ODF CephFS RWX Volumes with Custom SCCs
issue: - Pods in a multi-replica deployment using a ReadWriteMany (RWX) PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) on ODF CephFS are unable to access the shared volume concurrently.- Typically, only one pod (often the last one to start) can access the volume mount, while all other pods receive Permission denied errors.
resolution: **Workaround**- Update the `PersistentVolume (PV)` object associated with the problematic PVC and add the `kernelMountOptions`:- As a first step, back up all the PVC, PVs, and Ceph data affected by this procedure. Although these steps only manipulate OCP API objects in the API server/etcd, it's a best practice to keep this information safe. The available methods for taking this backup are outside this document's scope. For further reference, please review [KCS article 5456281- OpenShift APIs for Data Protection (OADP) FAQ](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5456281).- Create a copy of the PersistentVolume: ~~~ $ oc get pv-o yaml > pv-backup.yaml ~~~- Edit the PV and change the field: ~~~ $ oc edit pv persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Delete <-- Modify from Delete to Retain ~~~- Verify the `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy` is correctly set to `Retain`. This step prevents OCP from deleting the underlying Ceph volume in case something unexpected occurs: ~~~ $ oc get pv NAME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES RECLAIM POLICY STATUS CLAIM STORAGECLASS VOLUMEATTRIBUTESCLASS REASON AGE pvc-1a205b41-6628-4aac-b142-646a49ffd469 2Gi RWO Retain Bound [REDACTED] ocs-storagecluster-cephfs 1y ~~~- Edit the file `pv-backup.yaml` taken and add the following `kernelMountOptions` line in the volumeattributes section to force a generic SELinux context that all pods can access: ~~~ $ vim pv-backup.yaml volumeAttributes: clusterID: openshift-storage fsName: ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem + kernelMountOptions: context="system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0" storage.kubernetes.io/csiProvisionerIdentity: 1632867397636-8081-openshift-storage.cephfs.csi.ceph.com subvolumeName: csi-vol-9ff22e37-27c8-11ec-9f29-0a580a81020a volumeHandle: 0001-0011-openshift-storage-0000000000000001-9ff22e37-27c8-11ec-9f29-0a580a81020a ~~~- Delete the existing PV: ~~~ $ oc delete pv ~~~- This deletion process might get stuck in the Terminating status. If so, edit the PV once more and remove the finalizers section: ~~~ $ oc edit pv finalizers:- kubernetes.io/pv-protection <---remove this line in the pv yaml. ~~~- At this point, the PVC bound to the deleted PV will result in Lost status, i.e., status.phase: Lost. This is expected and doesn't impact the running IO to ODF/OCS: any pod already mounting the affected PV will keep the usual read and write access. Any new pods trying to mount this PV will be in ContainerCreating status until the procedure is finished. After that, they'll run normally.- Recreate the PV with the modifications done: ~~~ $ oc create-f pv-backup.yaml ~~~- Remove annotation `pv.kubernetes.io/bind-completed` from the PVC (not the PV!) This tells OCP to rebind the PV and PVC and resolve the lost phase. ~~~ $ oc patch-n $PVCNAMESPACE pvc $PVCNAME--type json '-p=[{"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/annotations/pv.kubernetes.io/bind-completed"}]' ~~~
root_cause: - The `ODF CephFS CSI` driver is working as expected.- When a pod mounts the volume, the entire shared directory is relabeled with the unique `Multi-Category Security (MCS)` label of that specific pod's container process (e.g., s0:c25,c26). When another pod with a different MCS label (e.g., s0:c27,c28) attempted to mount the same volume, the volume was relabeled with another set of unique `Multi-Category Security (MCS)` labels. The last pod to successfully mount the volume "won," effectively locking out all others. This behavior violates the `ReadWriteMany` contract, which requires simultaneous access for multiple pods.- The workaround forces a generic, shared SELinux context (`container_file_t:s0`) on the mount, which does not contain specific MCS categories, making it accessible to any container process.

title: Master node machine in Failed Phase in OCP 4
issue: After moving out the VM from VSphere folder the machine entered into Failed phase and can not reconcile. ~~~ $ oc get machine NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE ocp47-machine-master-2 Failed 26h $ oc get machine-o yaml Status: Addresses:... Error Message: Can't find created instance. ~~~- Logs from`machine-api-controllers` ~~~ nodelink_controller.go:425] Finding machine from node "node-master-2" by ProviderID nodelink_controller.go:441] Found machine "node-master-2" for node "node-master-2" with providerID "vsphere:// " controller.go:168] thor-fzdb6-master-2: reconciling Machine controller.go:265] thor-fzdb6-master-2: machine has gone "Failed" phase. It won't reconcile ~~~
resolution: To resolve this issue, it is required to replace the failed master node. [Documentation- Replace etcd member](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.15/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#restore-replace-stopped-etcd-member_replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member)
root_cause: The reason a machine enters the `Failed` phase is that because the provider associated with it cannot be found. (In the cloud this is assumed to be because the corresponding VM has been deleted). As per [Bugzilla #1962195](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1962195#c6), once a machine gets into `Failed` phase, the controller can not reconcile it again.

title: ODF: rook-ceph-osd-prepare Pods Continue to Deploy in a "Pending" state after the Desired Ceph OSD State has been Attained
issue: In some instances, ODF users may notice `rook-ceph-osd-prepare` pods appearing in their `$ oc get pods-n openshift-storage` output. These prepare pods are associated with OSD prepare jobs `$ oc get jobs-n openshift-storage`. Usually, these jobs will be in a `Completed` state and can be cleared out when the user deletes the jobs. However, there may be instances when these pods/jobs are in a `Pending` status indefinitely, or more deployed than expected. If in `Pending`, these pods/jobs will also have a `Pending` PVC associated with them as well. The function of the prepare pod/job is to deploy a Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) to bind with a Persistent Volume (PV). However, in the event there are no PVs to bind with (Local Storage), that job/PVC will remain in a `Pending` state. A common way this occurs is that a user utilizes the "Add Capacity" function too many times, which increases the count in the `storagecluster.yaml` and in most cases won't match the amount of `Available` PVs. ~~~ $ oc get pods,jobs-n openshift-storage|grep prepare pod/rook-ceph-osd-prepare-36569fd6d3212d7a37d3e5b465185e9c-4jq4d 0/1 Pending 0 3m51s pod/rook-ceph-osd-prepare-840b1b664511e2febad3e19225298a3e-d4nc8 0/1 Pending 0 3m51s job.batch/rook-ceph-osd-prepare-36569fd6d3212d7a37d3e5b465185e9c 0/1 3m51s 3m51s job.batch/rook-ceph-osd-prepare-840b1b664511e2febad3e19225298a3e 0/1 3m51s 3m51s $ oc get pvc-n openshift-storage | grep-i pending NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE ocs-deviceset-ocs-storagecluster-1-data-4l2b4w Pending ocs-storagecluster ocs-deviceset-ocs-storagecluster-2-data-4f2967 Pending ocs-storagecluster ~~~
resolution: The most common cause of `Pending` prepare jobs/pods is usually a disparity between the `storageDeviceSet` `count` in the `storagecluster.yaml` and OSDs in the Ceph tree. If applicable, the following actions can be taken: 1. Check the `storagecluster.yaml`. Ensure the `count` and `replica` correlate with the desired OSDs in the ceph tree. To run Ceph commands, please see the [Configuring the Rook-Ceph Toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891). **NOTE:** Navigate to the `storageDeviceSets` spec in the storagecluster.yaml and multiply ~~~ count x replica = total number of OSDs. ~~~ The above is what Rook references to determine how many OSDs to deploy in the Ceph cluster. See some examples below. **failureDomain Rack/Zone:** ~~~ $ oc get storagecluster-n openshift-storage-o yaml storageDeviceSets:- config: {} count: 2 <------------------------ Two OSDs for each rack/zone storage: 100Gi storageClassName: localblock volumeMode: Block replica: 3 <---------- 3 racks/zones. Multiply replica x count for a total of 6 OSDs in the Ceph tree. ~~~ **failureDomain Host:** ~~~ $ oc get storagecluster-n openshift-storage-o yaml storageDeviceSets:- config: {} count: 6 <------------------------ A total of 6 OSDs in the Ceph Tree storage: 100Gi storageClassName: localblock volumeMode: Block replica: 1 <-------- Disburse x1 OSD per host when count is increased. Multiply by count, 6 OSDs in the Ceph tree. ~~~ **Example of Ceph tree using failureDomain: rack:** ~~~ $ ceph osd tree ID CLASS WEIGHT TYPE NAME STATUS REWEIGHT PRI-AFF-1 24.00000 root default-8 4.00000 rack rack0-7 4.00000 host host1 0 ssd 4.00000 osd.0 up 1.00000 1.00000 3 ssd 4.00000 osd.3 up 1.00000 1.00000-12 4.00000 rack rack1-11 4.00000 host host2 2 ssd 4.00000 osd.2 up 1.00000 1.00000 4 ssd 4.00000 osd.4 up 1.00000 1.00000-4 4.00000 rack rack2-3 4.00000 host host 3 1 ssd 4.00000 osd.1 up 1.00000 1.00000 5 ssd 4.00000 osd.5 up 1.00000 1.00000 ~~~ 2. If the desired count is the Ceph tree correlates with what is in the `storagecluster.yaml`, it may be necessary to delete the `rook-ceph-osd-prepare` jobs and any `Pending` PVCs associated with the jobs and monitor to see if the jobs return. **Note:** Deleting the jobs will clear pods/jobs. However, if the pods/PVCs were in a "Pending" status, the PVCs will still remain and need to be deleted manually. ~~~ $ oc delete jobs-n openshift-storage--all $ oc get pvc-n openshift-storage | grep-i pending NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE ocs-deviceset-ocs-storagecluster-1-data-4l2b4w Pending ocs-storagecluster ocs-deviceset-ocs-storagecluster-2-data-4f2967 Pending ocs-storagecluster $ oc delete pvc-n openshift-storage ocs-deviceset-ocs-storagecluster-1-data-4l2b4w $ oc delete pvc-n openshift-storage ocs-deviceset-ocs-storagecluster-2-data-4f2967 ~~~ 3. Once the above has been accomplished, monitor to confirm that the prepare jobs no longer deploy. If the prepare jobs/pods continue to deploy, there is likely an indexing issue with the PVCs and the `rook-ceph-operator` is confused and will attempt to fill a void. Please open a case with Red Hat Support. Most likely, some OSDs will need to be redeployed in a safe/slow/monitored process. For more context regarding the indexing issue, see the "Root Cause" section.
root_cause: `rook-ceph-osd-prepare` jobs get created whenever there is a disparity between the count/replica in the `storagecluster.yaml` and what's in the Ceph OSD tree. This generally happens when the `Add Capacity` feature is used with no `Available` PV or if the `Add Capacity` feature was overused on accident when attempting to expand the cluster (adding more OSDs). However, if `rook-ceph-osd-prepare` jobs continue to deploy when more OSDs are not desired, there can be multiple reasons why this occurs. Those issues consist of the following: 1. A recent storagecluster change by editing the `count` or `replica` for the `storageDeviceSets`. **NOTE: Changing `replica` is not recommended without ODF Support involvement.** 2. Continuing to select the `Add Capacity` option in the OCP Console. This increments the `count` in the storagecluster.yaml each time. 3. Bad indexing. **More Context on the Indexing Issue:** Each PVC has an indexing naming scheme associated with it. This scheme is entirely dictated by the failureDomain. a. For `failureDomain: host`, all PVCs will have a `0-data` naming scheme in the name. For example: ~~~ NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-0pj26j Bound local-pv-8d566d1c 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-0h7mbw Bound local-pv-cd3e4650 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-0sdsqj Bound local-pv-3c646fd8 256Gi RWO localblock ~~~ b. For `failureDomain: rack/zone`, all PVCs will have an equal amount of `0-data`, `1-data`, `2-data`, etc., and this correlates with the `replica` in the `storagecluster.yaml`. For example, a `storagecluster.yaml` with `count: 1` and `replica: 3` in the `storageDeviceSet` spec, PVCs will have the following naming scheme: ~~~ NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-0pj26j Bound local-pv-8d566d1c 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-1-data-0h7mbw Bound local-pv-cd3e4650 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-2-data-0sdsqj Bound local-pv-3c646fd8 256Gi RWO localblock ~~~ If expanded to `count: 2` and `replica: 3`, notice the pattern: ~~~ NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-0pj26j Bound local-pv-8d566d1c 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-1-data-0h7mbw Bound local-pv-cd3e4650 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-2-data-0sdsqj Bound local-pv-3c646fd8 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-we694u Bound local-pv-8d566d1c 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-1-data-9hj81n Bound local-pv-cd3e4650 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-2-data-2vlks8 Bound local-pv-3c646fd8 256Gi RWO localblock ~~~ Looking above, we can see there is an equal amount of `0-data`, `1-data`, and `2-data` PVCs. No more prepare jobs will execute unexpectedly. The last example shows that a storagecluster.yaml consisting `count: 1` and `replica: 4`, the PVCs will appear as follows, and so on: ~~~ NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS ocs-deviceset-localblock-0-data-0pj26j Bound local-pv-8d566d1c 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-1-data-0h7mbw Bound local-pv-cd3e4650 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-2-data-0sdsqj Bound local-pv-3c646fd8 256Gi RWO localblock ocs-deviceset-localblock-3-data-2gio4l Bound local-pv-3c646fd8 256Gi RWO localblock ~~~

title: Why does image pull fails from quay mirror registry using skopeo command with --all switch ?
issue: - Image pull failing from quay mirror registry due to missing tags
resolution: - The **sha value** is not needed at the destination.to copy container images from one container registry to another. Hence, the correct command syntax would be like: $ skopeo copy--all docker://{source_registry}@sha256:eb951af6132643b224d10a1f4dd193964187b61b10aaaefdd012fcde15533043 docker://{destinamtion_registry}- For example: $ skopeo copy--all docker://registry.redhat.io/devworkspace/devworkspace-rhel8-operator@sha256:eb951af6132643b224d10a1f4dd193964187b61b10aaaefdd012fcde15533043 docker://bastion.mgmt.infyitapps.local:8443/catalog-image/devworkspace-devworkspace-rhel8-operator
root_cause: - There is no need to specify the sha value at the destination.

title: Why does users with only lowercase able to match with LDAP configuration in quay ?
issue: - Unexpected behavior with LDAP authentication
resolution: - This is an expected behavior since LDAP is case insensitive and one must define the rule accordingly from the LDAP end and Quay has nothing to do as it already adds an extra security to the functionality.
root_cause: - Red Hat Quay performs case-sensitive matching for LDAP usernames by default. If LDAP authentication is configured without normalization (e.g., no forced lowercase conversion), Quay will attempt to match the exact username as entered.

title: How to Remove an Unwanted Ceph Monitor (rook-ceph-mon) from ODF
issue: There may be instances where there are issues with the rook-ceph-mon pod resource. Quorum on the backend (Ceph) may not be attained. An example of this is when more than one host exists, the rook-ceph-operator will always attempt to maintain High Availability (HA). This means that when a rook-ceph-mon pod is down for an extended period of time, the rook-ceph-operator will create a new rook-ceph-mon deployment. However, in the event the previous rook-ceph-mon was not removed, there may be an issue where there are four rook-ceph-mon deployments on the frontend (ODF), and three monitor daemons on the backend (Ceph), resulting in degraded quorum.
resolution: # WARNING: DO NOT attempt this solution if you DO NOT have AT LEAST two healthy Ceph monitors in Ceph: **Example:** ~~~ $ ceph-s health: HEALTH_WARN 1/3 mons down, quorum a,b <---- need AT LEAST 2 healthy mons in quorum THAT WILL NOT BE the mon removed. services: mon: 3 daemons, quorum a,b (age 1.14231s), out of quorum: c <--- only one mon out of quorum. ~~~ **Prerequisite:** Use the [Configuring the Rook-Ceph Toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891) solution to enable the functionality of running Ceph commands. Assuming there are only three rook-ceph-mon daemons in the Ceph cluster, and actions were not taken to increase the monitor count manually, below is the proposed solution. 1. Identify the disparity between what is reported in Ceph and what OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) has on the front end. a. Check the pods/deployments: ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage | grep mon $ oc get deployment-n openshift-storage ``` The example output below indicates there is an extra mon deployment (rook-ceph-mon-f): ``` rook-ceph-mon-b 1/1 1 1 138d rook-ceph-mon-d 1/1 1 1 138d rook-ceph-mon-e 1/1 1 1 20d rook-ceph-mon-f 0/1 1 0 23m ``` b. Using the rook-ceph-tools pod validate the output matches the running mons: ``` $ oc exec-n openshift-storage deployment/rook-ceph-tools-- ceph-s ``` The example output that shows the three mons are in quorum and the unwanted mon (f) is out of quorum: ``` health: HEALTH_WARN 1/4 mons down, quorum b,d,e services: Monday: 4 daemons, quorum b,d,e (age 84m), out of quorum: f <----- ``` 2. Validate that the `$ ceph-s` output above matches the monitor resources listed in the `rook-ceph-mon-endpoints` configmap and perform a backup on that resource. ``` $ oc get cm rook-ceph-mon-endpoints-o yaml-n openshift-storage > rook-ceph-mon-endpoints.yaml $ cat rook-ceph-mon-endpoints.yaml ``` Example output validates that mons "b,d,e" should be the only monitors in Ceph.: ``` csi-cluster-config-json: '[{"clusterID":"openshift-storage","monitors": data: b=xxx,d=xxxx,e=xxxxxx <----- ``` 3. As a precaution, backup the unwanted rook-ceph-mon deployment: ``` $ oc get deployment-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-mon-f-o yaml > rook-ceph-mon-f.yaml ``` 4. Delete the extra rook-ceph-mon deployment: ``` $ oc delete deployment-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-mon-f ``` 5. After ~5 minutes, validate the deployment is removed from openshift and Ceph: ``` $ oc get deployment-n openshift-storage $ oc exec-n openshift-storage deployment/rook-ceph-tools-- ceph-s ``` 6. In the event `$ ceph-s` still reflects the unwanted monnitor the following command can be used to remove the monitor: ``` $ oc exec-n openshift-storage deployment/rook-ceph-tools-- ceph mon remove f ```
root_cause: Rook reconciled a rook-ceph-monitor daemon that was down for a period of time and scaled up more mons than defined by the cephcluster resource.

title: Setting Env variables in JWS and JBoss EAP Operator in Openshift 4
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - Setting Env variables in JWS Operator in Openshift 4- Setting Env variables in JBoss EAP Operator in Openshift 4- Setting Env variables in Data Grid Operator in Openshift 4
resolution: In JWS and EAP Operator the user sets the env variables not directly via statefulset but via the custom resource (CR) spec.env. And that's a general rule the user should not touch the intermediary deployment resources such as statefulsets, because that will be overwritten by the operator via the custom resource. That would be the case for EAP 8 helm chart deployment for example, where the user interfaces via sts (statefulset resource). The solution [How to modify JVM options (JAVA_OPTS) for JBoss EAP in Openshift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1535353) and the solution [How to change JVM memory options using Openshift images with Java?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2682021) tackle this problem but not for Operator deployment. And the solution [Using JAVA_MAX_MEM_RATIO on container JBoss EAP 7 image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6180301) handles specifically `JAVA_INITIAL_MEM_RATIO` and `JAVA_MAX_MEM_RATIO` environment variables. ### Respective Custom resource For Middleware Operators the spec.containers section must be applied on the respective custom resource: Operator | Custom Resource----------|------- EAP Operator | WildFlyServer CR JWS Operator | WebServer CR SSO Operator | Keycloack CR Data Grid Operator | Infinispan CR ### Example ~~~ Example for env setting: $ oc get wildflyserver NAME REPLICAS AGE example-env 1 84m...... $ oc get wildflyserver-o yaml apiVersion: v1 items:- apiVersion: wildfly.org/v1alpha1 kind: WildFlyServer metadata: name: example-env spec: applicationImage: registry.redhat.io/... env:- name: JAVA_OPTS_APPEND value: '"-XX:MinHeapFreeRatio=11"'... $ oc get sts example-o yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: StatefulSet... ownerReferences:- apiVersion: wildfly.org/v1alpha1 kind: WildFlyServer name: example-env ~~~

title: Can I customize the Dockerfile from EAP 8 images for running in OCP 4?
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - Can I customize the Dockerfile from EAP 8 images for running in OCP 4?- Customizing the EAP 8 images on Openshift 4
resolution: EAP container images are currently only supported on Openshift, as-is. This means the user cannot customizing the Dockerfile without losing the support for EAP container image. That's because the container image is built and tested fully as-is and then shipped to the official container registry. In case required, EAP images can be trimmed using Galleon features on EAP 8 and EAP 7. On this matter for details see the following solutions: Issue | Solution--------- |--------- JBoss EAP 7 thin image- missing jars | [JBoss EAP 7 thin image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6960786) Deploy applications with EAP 7 Operator | [How to deploy an application in JBoss EAP 7 in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6959339) Custom module in EAP 7 | [Creating a custom module in EAP 7's OCP image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6964154) Custom configuration in EAP 7| [What are the options to use a custom runtime EAP configurations](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6969444) EAP 7 trimming using Galleon | [After installing EAP openshift trimmed with Galleon cannot find openshift-launch.sh](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6959339) EAP 7 Operator service creation | [JBoss EAP 7 Operator creates LoadBalancer service](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6649471) Template (S2I options) | [JBoss EAP S2I build template options](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6969842) Usage of `provisioning.xml` | [JBoss EAP 7 Galleon using provisioning.xml](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6970360) `CONFIG_IS_FINAL` Flag setting | [EAP 7/8 CONFIG_IS_FINAL on Galleon Build for image building](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7100775) PROVISIONING_MAVEN_PLUGIN_VERSION for EAP 8 | [How to set Maven Plugin Version in Galleon build EAP 8](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7083500) Discusses `MAVEN_OPTS`, `MAVEN_ARGS` amd `MAVEN_ARGS_APPEND` flags | [Using Maven parameters on Buildconfig in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7032621)
root_cause: The trimming of the EAP should be done via Galleon only, so the user is not recommended to chop (remove) the jars/dependencies inside EAP directly. Most trivial customizations do not invalidate supportability, but hard ones (changing jars, changing OpenJDK, changing critical env variables) do make it unsupported. EAP container is a layered product, so you have the UBI layer, which has their CVEs, the OpenJDK ones, which have their CVEs, and the EAP layer.

title: Storage CO Degraded due to incorrect username in vsphere-creds
issue: Storage CO was degraded. The status is as below: ``` status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: " " message: |- VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRProgressing: VMwareVSphereDriverControllerServiceControllerProgressing: Waiting for Deployment to deploy pods VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRProgressing: VMwareVSphereDriverNodeServiceControllerProgressing: Waiting for DaemonSet to deploy node pods reason: VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCR_VMwareVSphereDriverControllerServiceController_Deploying::VMwareVSphereDriverNodeServiceController_Deploying status: "True" type: Progressing- lastTransitionTime: " " message: 'VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCRAvailable: VMwareVSphereDriverControllerServiceControllerAvailable: Waiting for Deployment' reason: VSphereCSIDriverOperatorCR_VMwareVSphereDriverControllerServiceController_Deploying status: "False" type: Available ```
resolution: - Modify `secret/vsphere-creds` in `ns/kube-system` by updating username `user1` to the correct Frequently Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) `user1@ `- After this, all `vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-controller-*` pods start Running- If incase, `vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-node-*` pods are still waiting from prior CrashLoopBackOff, then delete these pods. Once recycled, `vmware-vsphere-csi-driver-node-*` pods too get into Running state.

title: Accessing private ROSA HCP API server cross account via additional allowed principal
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: Not able to access private ROSA HCP API server after setup additional allowed principal
resolution: **account A** is where the **ROSA HCP cluster** is installed. **account B** is where the **client EC2** is created to access private ROSA HCP API. 1. In EC2 account B, create IAM policy. ~~~ {"Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{"Sid": "VisualEditor0", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["vpce:*", "ec2:CreateVpcEndpointServiceConfiguration", "ec2:CreateVpcEndpoint", "ec2:CreateVpcEndpointConnectionNotification"], "Resource": "*"}]} ~~~ ~~~ IAM_POLICY_ARN=$(aws iam create-policy \--policy-name ROSAHcpVPCEndpointPolicy \--policy-document file://vpce-policy.json \--query 'Policy.Arn' \--output text) ~~~ 2. In EC2 account B, create IAM role and attach policy: ~~~ IAMUSER_ARN=$(aws sts get-caller-identity--query "Arn"--output text) ~~~ ~~~ cat > trust-policy.json < [profile myprofile] role_arn = # e.g., arn:aws:iam::[]:role/ROSAHcpVPCEndpointRole source_profile = default region = ~~~ 4. In ROSA HCP account A, register IAM role with ROSA cluster: ~~~ CLUSTER_NAME=$(rosa list clusters-o json | jq '.[0].name' | sed 's/"//g') IAM_ROLE_ARN= # e.g., arn:aws:iam::[]:role/ROSAHcpVPCEndpointRole rosa edit cluster-c $CLUSTER_NAME--additional-allowed-principals $IAM_ROLE_ARN ~~~ 5. In ROSA HCP account A, get VPC endpoint service name for ROSA HCP control plane access: ~~~ aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints \--query "VpcEndpoints[*].[VpcEndpointId, ServiceName]" \--output table example: com.amazonaws.vpce.ap-northeast-1.vpce-svc-00d2aa09630561234 ~~~ 6. title: ACS UI became intermittently unavailable and AD authentication briefly failed
issue: - User updated the certificate for ACS. Then the ACS UI became intermittently unavailable and AD authentication briefly failed.- ACS UI Unavailability ("cannot read properties of null").
resolution: Restart the `central StackRox` pods to forces these pods to re-read their configuration from scratch, including the updated certificate from the secret.

title: Why HorizontalPodAutoscaler is not working as expected
issue: - HorizontalPodAutoscaler is not working as expected even after the target is reached.
resolution: - The HorizontalPodAutoscaler controller operates on the ratio between desired metric value and current metric value: ~~~ desiredReplicas = ceil[currentReplicas * (currentMetricValue / desiredMetricValue)] ~~~- For example, if the current metric value is 200m, and the desired value is 100m, the number of replicas will be doubled, since `200.0 / 100.0 == 2.0`. If the current value is instead 50m, you'll halve the number of replicas, since `50.0 / 100.0 == 0.5`. The control plane skips any scaling action if the ratio is sufficiently close to 1.0 (within a globally-configurable tolerance, 0.1 by default).- When a `targetAverageValue` or `targetAverageUtilization` is specified, the `currentMetricValue` is computed by taking the average of the given metric across all Pods in the HorizontalPodAutoscaler's scale target.- The HPA has a tolerance of `0.1` when considering the ratio of the current metric value to the desired metric value. This feature is present in order to prevent flapping (where a pod is added and removed repeatedly) when a metric goes up and down near the target value. This means that there are values which, while above the target value, will not cause scaling to happen because they are within the tolerance.- HPA considers these values "close enough" to the target value, and does not perform scaling.

title: RHACS cannot scan JAR file with bash script
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Some container images have JAR files which start with a bash script. RHACS cannot identify these nor detect vulnerabilities affecting them.
resolution: - Upgrade to RHACS 4.8.0
root_cause: - JAR files are just ZIP files, ACS scanner checks the JAR's header to ensure it's a valid ZIP before reading the entire file. There was a [BUG in Claircore](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CLAIRDEV-156), as Scanner V4 was not able to check a JAR file that starts with a bash script: ~~~ $ head sso-rh.jar #!/bin/bash # #._________ # /\\ /___'_____(_)______ \ \ \ \ # (()\___ | '_ | '_| | '_ \/_` | \ \ \ \ # \\/___)| |_)| | | | | || (_| |)))) # ' |____|.__|_| |_|_| |_\__, | / / / / # =========|_|==============|___/=/_/_/_/ #:: Spring Boot Startup Script:: ~~~

title: Not able to securely login to the cluster

title: How to distribute pod replicas across multiple nodes to use local disks in OpenShift 4?
issue: - The application, such as a distributed database, requires each pod replica to run on a different node to use that node's local storage.- When using `Deployment`, all pod replicas are scheduled on the same node.- How can pods be distributed across multiple nodes, with each pod using its own local `PersistentVolume`(PV)?
resolution: **Disclaimer:**_Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ To ensure each pod is scheduled on a different node and uses that node's local storage, you must use `StatefulSet` instead of `Deployment`. When using `StatefulSet` with the Local Storage Operator, it creates a unique `PersistentVolumeClaim`(PVC) for each pod replica. This setup ensures that each pod is tied to a specific local `PersistentVolume`(PV) on a node. Here is an example snippet of a `StatefulSet`. `spec.volumeClaimTemplates` section defines how to create a PVC for each pod replica. ~~~ apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: StatefulSet metadata: name: my-stateful-app spec: #...snip... # This template creates a unique PVC for each Pod replica volumeClaimTemplates:- metadata: name: my-local-storage spec: accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"] storageClassName: "local-sc" # Specify the StorageClass for local storage resources: requests: storage: 1Gi ~~~ For details, refer to the official Kubernetes documentation: [StatefulSets | Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/)
root_cause: A `StatefulSet` is designed for stateful applications. It provides stable storage for each pod. When used with a topology-aware storage like the Local Storage Operator, it uses the Kubernetes scheduler's awareness of storage locality to correctly place pods on the nodes where their data resides.

title: How to inject a custom CLI script as a ConfigMap in OpenShift for EAP/RH-SSO ?
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How to update/modify existing DataSource Connection Pool Parameters in RHSSO running on OpenShift Using Custom CLI Scripts?- How to inject a custom CLI script as a ConfigMap in OpenShift for EAP/RH-SSO?
resolution: - To dynamically apply DataSource connection pool configurations, use a custom CLI script injected via a ConfigMap. This approach modifies the RHSSO/ EAP server configuration during deployment. 1. Prepare CLI Script (extensions.cli) Create a script to update the DataSource configuration: ~~~ embed-server--std-out=echo--server-config=standalone-openshift.xml batch /subsystem=datasources/data-source=:write-attribute(name=min-pool-size,value=5) /subsystem=datasources/data-source=:write-attribute(name=max-pool-size,value=20) /subsystem=datasources/data-source=:write-attribute(name=valid-connection-checker-class-name,value=org.jboss.jca.adapters.jdbc.extensions.mysql.MySQLValidConnectionChecker) /subsystem=datasources/data-source=:write-attribute(name=validate-on-match,value=true) /subsystem=datasources/data-source=:write-attribute(name=exception-sorter-class-name,value=org.jboss.jca.adapters.jdbc.extensions.mysql.MySQLExceptionSorter) run-batch quit ~~~ Replace with the actual DataSource name (e.g., KeycloakDS). 2. Create a Post-Configuration Script (postconfigure.sh)- This script executes the CLI commands during deployment: ~~~ #!/bin/sh echo "Executing postconfigure.sh" $JBOSS_HOME/bin/jboss-cli.sh--file=$JBOSS_HOME/extensions/extensions.cli ~~~ 3. Create a ConfigMap in OpenShift- Bundle the scripts into a ConfigMap: ~~~ oc create configmap jboss-cli--from-file=postconfigure.sh=extensions/postconfigure.sh--from-file=extensions.cli=extensions/extensions.cli ~~~ 4. Mount the ConfigMap into the DeploymentConfig- Attach the ConfigMap as a volume to the SSO pod: ~~~ oc set volume DeploymentConfig/--add--name=jboss-cli-m /opt/eap/extensions-t configmap--configmap-name=jboss-cli--default-mode='0755' ~~~ Replace with the actual RHSSO deployment name. **Notes:** Execute the following steps to update the pods to use the new image that includes the updated CLI file. To rebuild and apply updates to your application in the rhsso-76 namespace, follow these steps: Get the Build Configuration (BC) name: ~~~ oc get bc-n rhsso-76 ~~~ Start a new build using the updated CLI files: ~~~ oc start-build sso76--from-dir=.--follow-n rhsso-76 ~~~ Restart the application pods to apply the new build: ~~~ oc rollout restart dc/-n rhsso-76 ~~~ Replace with the actual name of your DeploymentConfig. Ensure that the updated CLI script is correctly copied into the build context used for the image. To verify that the changes have been successfully applied at runtime after the pod starts, execute the following: ~~~ oc rsh /opt/eap/bin/jboss-cli.sh--connect /subsystem=datasources/data-source=KeycloakDS:read-resource ~~~ This command will display the current datasource configuration, including any updated validation settings. Alternatively, you can check the standalone-openshift.xml file to confirm whether the new datasource configuration has been added.

title: Procedure to update the OSP Director Operator itself from 17.1.3/4 to 17.1.6
issue: - Need for a procedure to update the OSP Director Operator itself- The documentation in [Performing a minor update of the RHOSP overcloud with director Operator](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_platform/17.1/html/deploying_an_overcloud_in_a_red_hat_openshift_container_platform_cluster_with_director_operator/assembly_performing-a-minor-update-of-the-rhosp-overcloud-with-director-operator) instructs to use a static `CatalogSource` to install the OpenStack Director Operator. However, that means the automatic update won't happen unless the repository pointed in `spec.image` is manually updated.
resolution: #### Manual intervention The explicitly supported and recommended method for upgrading the OpenStack Director Operator is to delete and then recreate the associated OLM resources. This process is outlined as follows:- The existing `CatalogSource`, `Subscription`, and `ClusterServiceVersion` CRs linked to the OpenStack Director Operator must be deleted.- Following the deletion, new `CatalogSource` and `Subscription` CRs must be created, ensuring they point to the desired newer version of the operator.- This method will result in the operators being removed and then recreated as their new version, while the **operands** (the resources managed by the operator) will remain untouched.
root_cause: Automatic updates typically don't occur for the OpenStack Director Operator because:- The current official installation documentation instructs users to use a static `CatalogSource` that points to a specific index, often in a personal Quay repository where specific images are pushed statically.- That means the automatic update will not happen unless the repository pointed to in `spec.image` is manually updated.- There is currently no `registry.redhat.io` index image available to tie the operator and bundle images together for automated updates.

product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: Unable to execute oc commands from bastion host in ROSA environment.
Encountered `dial tcp: lookup- no such host`error during ROSA cluster login process.
Error message: `dial tcp: lookup api.xxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.p1.openshiftapps.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host`.
DNS resolution for `api.xxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.p1.openshiftapps.com` is failing.
resolution: The bastion host must be configured to use an appropriate DNS resolver that can resolve private domain names associated with the ROSA cluster. This can be achieved by updating the DNS settings to use the internal VPC resolver. For example: ~~~ sudo vi /etc/resolv.conf nameserver 10.87.163.2 ~~~ **Note**- The IP `10.87.163.2` is the AWS VPC’s internal DNS resolver, typically assigned as the `.2` address in each subnet, and is used to resolve private DNS names within the VPC, including those for PrivateLink-enabled ROSA clusters. This ensures that DNS queries for the private cluster (e.g., *.openshiftapps.com) are correctly resolved via the VPC's internal DNS service.
root_cause: The issue indicates that the DNS lookup for the OpenShift API endpoint is failing. The DNS resolver being used—Google's public DNS (8.8.8.8)—is unable to resolve the domain name to an IP address. In a *ROSA cluster configured with **PrivateLink**, the DNS zone is not expected to be publicly resolvable*. The output shows that Google's DNS servers are being used to attempt a connection to the cluster, which is failing as expected in this setup.

title: RHOCP 4 Reports Overcommit Based on Limits Without Application Load
issue: A "CPU overcommit" issue is observed in the OCP console. The cluster reports a CPU utilization issue even when there is no application load.
resolution: * Perform Risk Assessment Evaluate if the potential for resource contention poses a real-world risk. If applications rarely or never reach their defined resource limits simultaneously, the overcommit warning may be acceptable and require no further action. This is a business and operational decision based on application performance requirements and risk tolerance. * Adjust Pod CPU Limits Review and lower the CPU limits on deployed pods to more accurately reflect their typical resource consumption. This will reduce the calculated overcommit ratio and resolve the warning. * Increase Node Capacity If high CPU limits are required and the potential for resource contention is a concern, increase the cluster's capacity by adding more worker nodes or using nodes with more CPU resources.
root_cause: In RHOCP a limit is the maximum amount of a resource, like CPU or memory, that a container is allowed to use on a node. It is crucial to understand that this defined limit is different from the container's actual, real-time resource consumption which fluctuates based on the application's workload. The "CPU overcommit" warning appears when the sum of the CPU limits of all pods on a node exceeds the node's total CPU capacity. This is an alert about potential risk and does not mean the node is currently overloaded. The issue would only materialize if all containers simultaneously attempted to use their maximum allowed CPU limit, which is often not the case in real-world scenarios.

title: Pods stuck in pending state due to terminating pods on the nominated node in RHOCP4
issue: - Pods are not getting scheduled on respective node because of the following error: ~~~ Warning FailedScheduling 91s default-scheduler 0/6 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient memory. preemption: not eligible due to a terminating pod on the nominated node.. ~~~
resolution: - Verify if there are any pods stuck in terminating state using following command: ~~~ $ oc get pods-A | grep-i terminating ~~~- Delete the pods forcefully as shown below: ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n--grace-period=0--force ~~~- Restart the affected pods: ~~~ $ oc delete pods ~~~
root_cause: In OpenShift, the Kubernetes scheduler avoids scheduling a pod to a node where a terminating pod is still using the required resources, even if the node technically has enough allocatable resources once the terminating pod is gone. This behavior is by design to prevent resource overcommitment.

title: Ceph OSDs Crashing "osd_op_tp thread 0x7f3d47b32640' had suicide timed out after 150.000000000s"
issue: High latency in RocksDB transactions due to OMAPs not being compacted in the database. This results in the OSDs crashing. ~~~ 2024-12-04T19:15:26.466+0000 7f3d47b32640 1 heartbeat_map reset_timeout 'OSD::osd_op_tp thread 0x7f3d47b32640' had suicide timed out after 150.000000000s NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE rook-ceph-osd-8-676774779d-rfsx5 2/2 Running 519 5d rook-ceph-osd-3-55c4d84b5d-d4bfc 2/2 Running 488 5d rook-ceph-osd-0-84694bd764-4fp52 2/2 Running 473 5d rook-ceph-osd-11-7f6d4b6645-q624g 2/2 Running 456 5d rook-ceph-osd-12-5d44f4678d-q4qq9 2/2 Running 537 5d rook-ceph-osd-13-859df6cdcc-w7v7h 2/2 Running 537 5d ~~~ ~~~ health: HEALTH_WARN 1 osds down Degraded data redundancy: 506465/10815969 objects degraded (4.683%), 148 pgs degraded, 108 pgs undersized 903 daemons have recently crashed services: mon: 3 daemons, quorum b,c,d (age 3h) mgr: a(active, since 2d) mds: 1/1 daemons up, 1 hot standby osd: 26 osds: 25 up (since 32s), 26 in (since 15h); 52 remapped pgs rgw: 1 daemon active (1 hosts, 1 zones) data: volumes: 1/1 healthy pools: 12 pools, 665 pgs objects: 3.61M objects, 9.0 TiB usage: 27 TiB used, 72 TiB / 99 TiB avail pgs: 506465/10815969 objects degraded (4.683%) 503 active+clean 73 active+undersized+degraded 50 active+recovery_wait+undersized+degraded+remapped 23 active+recovery_wait+degraded 12 active+undersized 2 active+recovery_wait 2 active+recovering+undersized+degraded+remapped io: client: 274 MiB/s rd, 1.4 GiB/s wr, 6.89k op/s rd, 799 op/s wr recovery: 114 MiB/s, 39 objects/s ~~~
resolution: The solution is to stabilize the OSDs and then compact the BlueStore area of the OSD.- Stabilize the OSDs- Use the [Configuring the Rook-Ceph Toolbox in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.x](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891) solution to enable the functionality of running Ceph commands.- Change "`osd_op_tp`" timeout to 1200.- This will prevent the OSD from restarting.- Compact the BlueStore area of the OSD.- Ensure the ODSs are not restarting (flapping) before moving on.- The compaction is done offline.- The longer the OSD stays down, the more on point this solution.- When done with all OSDs- remove all settings. 1.) [Ceph CLI] Change "`osd_op_thread_suicide_timeout`" from 150 to 1200: ~~~ $ ceph config set osd osd_op_thread_suicide_timeout 1200 Trust- but verify $ ceph config dump | grep osd osd basic log_to_file true osd advanced osd_op_thread_suicide_timeout 1200 ~~~ Once this change is made, the OSD should stop crashing (flapping). Use "`ceph-s`" and "`ceph osd df tree`" to determine the OSDs are stable. 2.) [Ceph CLI] If stable, enable Compaction On Start for one of the problem OSDs. Let's use osd.2 as an example. ~~~ $ ceph config set osd.2 osd_compact_on_start true $ ceph config dump | grep osd Trust- but verify osd basic log_to_file true osd advanced osd_op_thread_suicide_timeout 1200 osd.2 advanced osd_compact_on_start true ~~~ 3.) [Ceph CLI] Set these flag [1] so that Recovery and Backfill do not occur while the OSD is down ~~~ $ ceph osd set nobackfill; ceph osd set norebalance; ceph osd set noout nobackfill is set norebalance is set noout is set $ ceph-s cluster: id: 68da6934-b884-11ef-9f18-fa163e5cef64 health: HEALTH_WARN noout,nobackfill,norebalance flag(s) set [1] [truncated] ~~~ 4.) [OpenShift CLI] Delete the OSD Pod. Again, our example is osd.2 ~~~ $ oc project openshift-storage $ oc get pod | grep osd-2 rook-ceph-osd-2-84c87b6597-bhqld 2/2 Running 0 37d $ oc delete pod rook-ceph-osd-2-84c87b6597-bhqld pod "rook-ceph-osd-2-84c87b6597-bhqld" deleted ~~~ 5.) [Ceph CLI] Use "`ceph osd df tree`" to monitor how long the OSD remains in the down [2] state: ~~~ $ ceph osd df tree ID CLASS WEIGHT REWEIGHT SIZE RAW USE DATA OMAP META AVAIL %USE VAR PGS STATUS TYPE NAME-1 0.11755- 120 GiB 2.5 GiB 116 MiB 22 KiB 2.4 GiB 117 GiB 2.10 1.00- root default-9 0.01959- 20 GiB 399 MiB 19 MiB 4 KiB 380 MiB 20 GiB 1.95 0.93- host edon-1 4 hdd 0.00980 1.00000 10 GiB 84 MiB 9.5 MiB 2 KiB 75 MiB 9.9 GiB 0.82 0.39 166 down osd.2 [2] 7 hdd 0.00980 1.00000 10 GiB 315 MiB 9.5 MiB 2 KiB 305 MiB 9.7 GiB 3.07 1.47 140 up osd.3-5 0.01959- 20 GiB 409 MiB 19 MiB 4 KiB 389 MiB 20 GiB 2.00 0.95- host edon-2 3 hdd 0.00980 1.00000 10 GiB 106 MiB 10 MiB 3 KiB 96 MiB 9.9 GiB 1.04 0.50 151 up osd.1 9 hdd 0.00980 1.00000 10 GiB 302 MiB 9.5 MiB 1 KiB 293 MiB 9.7 GiB 2.95 1.41 148 up osd.5-11 0.01959- 20 GiB 421 MiB 19 MiB 4 KiB 402 MiB 20 GiB 2.06 0.98- host edon-3 0 hdd 0.00980 1.00000 10 GiB 97 MiB 9.6 MiB 3 KiB 88 MiB 9.9 GiB 0.95 0.45 156 up osd.0 [3] 6 hdd 0.00980 1.00000 10 GiB 324 MiB 9.5 MiB 1 KiB 314 MiB 9.7 GiB 3.16 1.51 153 up osd.4 [3] ~~~ The longer the OSD stays down, the more on point this solution is for the situation. 6.) [Ceph CLI] Once osd.2 comes back up, remove the osd.2 parameter and move on to all OSDs in a failure domain [3]. ~~~ $ ceph config rm osd.2 osd_compact_on_start $ ceph config set osd.0 osd_compact_on_start true $ ceph config set osd.4 osd_compact_on_start true Trust- but verify $ ceph config dump | grep osd osd basic log_to_file true osd advanced osd_op_thread_suicide_timeout 1200 osd.0 advanced osd_compact_on_start true osd.4 advanced osd_compact_on_start true ~~~ 7.) [OpenShift CLI] Delete the OSD Pods in a given failure domain [3]. Our examples are osd.0 and osd.4 ~~~ $ oc project openshift-storage $ oc get pod | egrep "osd-0|osd-4" rook-ceph-osd-0-6bcd9c89c7-46v5n 2/2 Running 0 23d rook-ceph-osd-4-5d9777fc8c-zzzgd 2/2 Running 0 37d $ oc delete pod rook-ceph-osd-0-6bcd9c89c7-46v5n pod "rook-ceph-osd-0-6bcd9c89c7-46v5n" deleted $ oc delete pod rook-ceph-osd-4-5d9777fc8c-zzzgd pod "rook-ceph-osd-4-5d9777fc8c-zzzgd" deleted ~~~ 8.) [Ceph CLI] Monitor the OSDs and remove the "`osd_compact_on_start`" parameters. Repeat this process until all OSDs are done Once all OSD are done, remove this setting and all flags ~~~ $ ceph config rm osd osd_op_thread_suicide_timeout $ ceph config rm osd.{number} osd_compact_on_start $ ceph config rm osd.{number} osd_compact_on_start Trust- but verify $ ceph config dump | grep osd osd basic log_to_file true $ ceph osd unset nobackfill; ceph osd unset norebalance; ceph osd unset noout nobackfill is unset norebalance is unset noout is unset $ ceph crash archive-all $ ceph-s cluster: id: 68da6934-b884-11ef-9f18-fa163e5cef64 health: OK [truncated] ~~~ For additional assistance with this issue contact Red Hat Ceph Support.

title: Considerations Before Manually Editing IPPools and Overlapping IP Reservations in Whereabouts
issue: - Is it recommended to manually edit/delete `overlappingrangeipreservations` and `ippools.whereabouts.cni.cncf.io` resources?- What are the potential issues or system instabilities that could arise from manually `editing` or `deleting` these `IP address allocation` resources?- IP addresses assigned via `secondary network attachments` (i.e., using Multus) are not reflected in `OverlappingRangeIPReservations` or `IPPools`.- The same IP address is being assigned to two different pods, as seen in both `OverlappingRangeIPReservations` and `IPPools`.
resolution: - No, it is not recommended to manually `delete` or `modify` `IPPools` and `OverlappingRangeIPReservations` managed by Whereabouts.- While the currently running pod may not be affected immediately, a new pod could be assigned the same IP address, leading to an `IP conflict`.- IP address allocation is handled automatically by the `Whereabouts IPAM` plugin during pod creation.- If any discrepancies or mismatches are observed in IP assignment, please raise a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support for further investigation.

title: Controlling UDN/CUDN Resource Allocation on Specific Cluster Nodes
issue: - Applying a UDN (User Define Network) /CUDN (Cluster User Defined Network) configuration currently results in the creation of network components and the application of annotations from that configuration to all nodes.- Currently, network flows and annotations are applied to all available nodes within the cluster.- Is it possible to limit the nodes on which application projects are created?- Master/Infrastructure nodes typically do not handle application workloads in most clusters. Therefore, there is no need to create additional annotations, switches, or routers within their OVN-IC (Open Virtual Network- Interconnect). Furthermore, this configuration generates Open vSwitch (OVS) flows on these nodes that remain unused if application workloads are not scheduled to run there.- Is it possible to limit the host subnet and overhead configuration to selected nodes within the UDN?
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-57530](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-57530). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: How to configure custom ingress certificate in MicroShift
issue: - How to configure custom ingress certificate in MicroShift?- After restart of MicroShift systemd service, the ingress controller / router is reverted back to use the default certificate.- How to change the Ingress certificate so it persists after MicroShift restart?
resolution: ### Note The issue only affects version lower or equal to 4.18 version of Red Hat built of MicroShift. From version 4.19 a new feature was introduced to configure the certificates through the config.yaml. Please see the docs below.- [7.1. Configuring custom certificate authorities](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_microshift/4.19/html/configuring/configuring-microshift-authentication-and-security#microshift-custom-ca) ### Workaround **NOTE** Run the commands as `root` or add `sudo` before the commands. #### Prepare Certificates 1. Add the CA for the ingress into the RHEL trust store. ~~~ # cp-v ca.crt /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ ~~~ 2. Update the local trust store. ~~~ # update-ca-trust ~~~ 3. Add the CA to the Ingress Certificate, so the CA is served with the Ingress Cert. ~~~ # cat tls.crt ca.crt > > tls.pem ~~~ #### Configure Ingress 1. Create a directory in `/etc/microshift/manifests.d/` ~~~ # mkdir-v /etc/microshift/manifests.d/custom-ingress-cert ~~~ 2. Copy the certificate and the key files to the directory. ~~~ # cp-v tls.{pem,key} /etc/microshift/manifests.d/custom-ingress-cert/ ~~~ 3. Create a deploy for router as follows. ~~~ # cat < /etc/microshift/manifests.d/custom-ingress-cert/router-default-deployment.yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: router-default namespace: openshift-ingress spec: template: spec: volumes:- name: "default-certificate" secret: secretName: custom-ingress-cert defaultMode: 420 EOF ~~~ 4. Create a kustomize file. ~~~ # cat < /etc/microshift/manifests.d/custom-ingress-cert/kustomization.yaml apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: Kustomization resources:- router-default-deployment.yaml secretGenerator:- name: custom-ingress-cert namespace: openshift-ingress options: disableNameSuffixHash: true files:- tls.crt=tls.pem- tls.key=tls.key EOF ~~~ 5. Restart the MicroShift systemd service ~~~ # systemctl restart microshift ~~~ 6. Check if the Ingress Certificate was configured. ~~~ # oc get deployment router-default-n openshift-ingress-ojsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.volumes[0]}' | jq {"name": "default-certificate", "secret": {"defaultMode": 420, "secretName": "custom-ingress-cert"}} ~~~ 7. Check the microshift logs ~~~ # journalctl-u microshift--since "1 day ago" | grep-A6 "Applying.*custom-ingress-cert" ~~~
root_cause: The issue only affects version lower or equal to 4.18 version of Red Hat built of MicroShift. From version 4.19 a new feature was introduced to configure the certificates through the config.yaml. Please see the docs below.- [7.1. Configuring custom certificate authorities](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_microshift/4.19/html/configuring/configuring-microshift-authentication-and-security#microshift-custom-ca)

title: After upgrading Service Mesh Control Plane to 2.6, headless services begin to fail
issue: After we upgraded our OpenShift Service Mesh Control Plane to 2.6. Applications (with istio sidecar injected) that rely on a headless service to operate start to fail.
resolution: You need to explicitly specify the protocol you're headless service is using in the Service CRD for envoy proxy to route traffic properly in Service Mesh ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: nginx labels: app: nginx spec: ports:- port: 80 name: tcp-web # Explicitly defining an tcp port clusterIP: None # Creates a Headless Service selector: app: nginx ~~~
root_cause: - Istio 2.5. Envoy proxy is based on version 1.18.7- Istio 2.6 is based on version 1.20.8 Please see how istio handles headless service traffic [here.](https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/traffic-management/traffic-routing/#headless-services) and other common isses [here.](https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/common-problems/network-issues/#503-error-while-accessing-headless-services)

title: How to configure Apicurio Registry deployment using PodTemplate in version 3?
product: Red Hat build of Apicurio Registry
issue: How to configure Apicurio Registry deployment using PodTemplate in version 3? There is documentation in [V2](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_apicurio_registry/2.6/html/installing_and_deploying_apicurio_registry_on_openshift/managing-the-registry#pod-spec) but there is none in V3. I encountered the following error: ``` Caused by: io.fabric8.kubernetes.client.KubernetesClientException: Failure executing: POST at: https://172.30.0.1:443/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/XXXX/deployments. Message: Deployment.apps "simple-app-deployment" is invalid: [spec.template.spec.containers[0].name: Required value, spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value]. Received status: Status(apiVersion=v1, code=422, details=StatusDetails(causes=[StatusCause(field=spec.template.spec.containers[0].name, message=Required value, reason=FieldValueRequired, additionalProperties={}), StatusCause(field=spec.template.spec.containers[0].image, message=Required value, reason=FieldValueRequired, additionalProperties={})], group=apps, kind=Deployment, name=simple-app-deployment, retryAfterSeconds=null, uid=null, additionalProperties={}), kind=Status, message=Deployment.apps "simple-app-deployment" is invalid: [spec.template.spec.containers[0].name: Required value, spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value], metadata=ListMeta(_continue=null, remainingItemCount=null, resourceVersion=null, selfLink=null, additionalProperties={}), reason=Invalid, status=Failure, additionalProperties={}). ```
resolution: 1. Unlike V2, use podTemplateSpec in V3 instead. 2. In the CR's "container.name" you must either use "apicurio-registry-app" or "apicurio-registry-ui" to specify which pod you want to apply the podTemplateSpec. Please see the [Example](https://github.com/Apicurio/apicurio-registry/blob/main/operator/controller/src/test/resources/k8s/examples/podtemplatespec/podtemplatespec.apicurioregistry3.yaml)

title: Login using ssh not working after RHOCP 4.13 upgrade
issue: - After upgrading from OpenShift 4.12 to 4.13 it was not possible to ssh into the nodes.- Accessing a node using SSH failing with the follwoing message after openshift upgrade: ~~~ $ ssh-i sshkey core@10.0.0.1 core@10.0.0.1: Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic). ~~~
resolution: There are different reasons that could lead to this same issue after upgrading to OpenShift 4.13:- If the file `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` was customized, ensure that the following line is present at the beginning of the file, or better, add the customization to a new file within `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/` and revert the customization in file `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`: ~~~ Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf ~~~- If the issue appeared after applying compliance remediations, it has been reported to Red Hat Engineering and it has been tracked in [bug OCPBUGS-18331](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-18331), and already fixed in OpenShift Compliance operator by [errata RHBA-2024:1830](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:1830).- A **workaround** for older versions of the operator is to create an additional `MachineConfig` resource to overwrite the `sshd` configuration generated by the OpenShift Compliance operator to add the following line:- Check [How to add Include statement in the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7071828) ~~~ Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf ~~~ > **Note:** The created `MachineConfig` should be removed after upgrading to a version of the operator that includes the fix.- If the `sshd` configuration is not intentionally altered and is correct, make sure the issue is not caused by the use of a **RSA** key as explained in the solution [Failing ssh access to nodes using RSA key after RHOCP 4 upgrade](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7051873). ###Recommendation for preparing the upgrade from 4.12 to 4.13+ If the `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` file was already modified, before upgrading the 4.12 cluster:- Create an additional `MachineConfig` resource populating the mandatory directory and include file- Create the `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d` directory ~~~ $ mkdir /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d ~~~- Create one file by touching an empty `*.conf` to be found by glob ~~~ $ touch /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/empty_include.conf ~~~
root_cause: In OpenShift 4.13 the location for ssh keys changed, as reported by the [release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/release_notes/ocp-4-13-release-notes.html#ocp-4-13-rhcos-ssh-key-location). By default the following `sshd` configuration is present for retrieving users keys starting with that version: ~~~ AuthorizedKeysCommand /usr/libexec/ssh-key-dir %u ~~~ In OpenShift 4.12 the `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d` directory is absent. Applying the steps above will lead to Segmentation fault when connecting to the ssh service. An emtpy `.conf` is mandatory as the Segementation fault would still occure without.
