title: SSL handshaking error while contacting upstream
issue: - Querying the service returns 504 and APIcast logs show: ~~~ 2020/11/26 16:08:17 [crit] 26#26: *10211 SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:141A318A:SSL routines:tls_process_ske_dhe:dh key too small) while SSL handshaking to upstream...." ~~~
resolution: **Disclaimer**: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. It is possible to configure [`proxy_ssl_ciphers` NGINX directive](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html#proxy_ssl_ciphers) to control the cipher selection during the TLS handshake. Using `'DEFAULT:!DH'` will ensure the API backend does not use any ciphers with DH keys in the TLS handshake. The `crypto policy` is left unchanged at "DEFAULT". Details on configuration:- Create a `ciphers.conf` file with the following line ~~~ proxy_ssl_ciphers 'DEFAULT:!DH'; ~~~- Mount the `ciphers.conf` file as a custom configuration into `APIcast` container **Podman (or docker)** ~~~ sudo podman run--name apicast--rm--volume <> /ciphers.conf:/opt/app-root/http.d/ciphers.conf-p 8080:8080-e THREESCALE_PORTAL_ENDPOINT=https://{access-token}@ registry.redhat.io/3scale-amp2/apicast-gateway-rhel8:3scale2.9 ~~~ **OpenShift** ~~~ oc create configmap apicast-config--from-file=ciphers.conf oc set volume dc/{apicast-staging}--add--name=apicast-config--mount-path=/opt/app-root/http.d/ciphers.conf--sub-path=ciphers.conf--source='{"configMap":{"name":"apicast-config"}}' ~~~ 　 　 NOTE: For 3scale 2.15 or later, replace "dc" with "deployment" in the above command.- Query the Service again to check its behavior
root_cause: Since versions 3.8, APIcast are based on RHEL 8 image. RHEL 8 includes [stronger crypto defaults and deprecation of weak crypto algorithms](https://access.redhat.com/articles/3642912) using different crypto policies- DEFAULT, LEGACY, FUTURE, FIPS. Ciphersuites with Diffie Helman parameters that are accepted for each level are different:- DEFAULT- at least 2048 bits long.- LEGACY- at least 1023 bits long.- FUTURE- at least 3072- FIPS- at least 2048 bits long. The crypto policy of RHEL 8 image in `APIcast container` version [3.8](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5305511), [3.9](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2798521) is DEFAULT. This policy level requires DH parameters to be at least 2048 bits long. An `API backend` with DH parameters less than 2048 bit results in the error.

title: How to restart Red Hat 3scale On-premises deployed with Operator in OCP 4.x
issue: - It is not possible to restart 3scale when it is deployed via the 3scale operator.
resolution: Although there is no specific reason why the entire 3scale instance must be restarted, below is the procedure to gracefully reduce all components in order so as not to cause a possible loss of synchronization between the system and databases or in case of scheduled activities: **Note**: In version 2.15, there is known issue with below steps due to system-app-pre/system-app-post jobs which have been introduced. Please refer to [the knowledge](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7122101) for more detail. ### Stop Red Hat 3scale On-premises 1. Set replicas to 0 for the configurable components in the APIManager CRD. There are 2 methods to do this: a. Edit the APIManager CRD yaml: ~~~ spec: imageStreamTagImportInsecure: false resourceRequirementsEnabled: true system: appSpec: replicas: 0 sidekiqSpec: replicas: 0 sphinxSpec: {} appLabel: 3scale-api-management zync: appSpec: replicas: 0 queSpec: replicas: 0 backend: cronSpec: replicas: 0 listenerSpec: replicas: 0 workerSpec: replicas: 0 tenantName: 3scale apicast: managementAPI: status openSSLVerify: false productionSpec: replicas: 0 registryURL: 'http://apicast-staging:8090/policies' responseCodes: true stagingSpec: replicas: 0 wildcardDomain: ~~~ b. Patch the APIManager CRD with the following commands: * Export the following variables: `CRD_NAME= `. For example in the 3scale documentation the APIManager name is "example-apimanager". `ORIG_SPEC=$(oc get APIManager ${CRD_NAME}-o json|jq ".spec")` to save the current values for scaling up. `SCALE_SPEC=$(oc get APIManager ${CRD_NAME}-o json|jq ".spec"|sed s/'"replicas": 1'/'"replicas": 0'/g)` to scale the replicas from 1 to 0. * Then use the patch command: `oc patch APIManager ${CRD_NAME}--type merge-p "{\"spec\": ${SCALE_SPEC}}"`. 1. Scale down the databases. Since it is not possible to configure the number of replicas for the databases in the APIManager CRD (it's not possible to have more than 1 replica) the databases must be scaled down manually: ~~~ oc scale dc/system-sphinx--replicas=0 oc scale dc/backend-redis--replicas=0 oc scale dc/system-memcache--replicas=0 oc scale dc/system-mysql--replicas=0 oc scale dc/system-redis--replicas=0 oc scale dc/zync-database--replicas=0 ~~~ ###Start Red Hat 3scale On-premises 1. Scale up back the databases to 1 replica: ~~~ oc scale dc/backend-redis--replicas=1 oc scale dc/system-memcache--replicas=1 oc scale dc/system-mysql--replicas=1 oc scale dc/system-redis--replicas=1 oc scale dc/zync-database--replicas=1 oc scale dc/system-sphinx--replicas=1 ~~~ 1. Scale up back to one replica (or the amount configured) in the APImanager CRD. The same can be done by the 2 methods described above: a. Edit the APIManager CRD yaml: ~~~ spec: imageStreamTagImportInsecure: false resourceRequirementsEnabled: true system: appSpec: replicas: 1 sidekiqSpec: replicas: 1 sphinxSpec: {} appLabel: 3scale-api-management zync: appSpec: replicas: 1 queSpec: replicas: 1 backend: cronSpec: replicas: 1 listenerSpec: replicas: 1 workerSpec: replicas: 1 tenantName: 3scale apicast: managementAPI: status openSSLVerify: false productionSpec: replicas: 1 registryURL: 'http://apicast-staging:8090/policies' responseCodes: true stagingSpec: replicas: 1 wildcardDomain: ~~~ b. Patch the APIManager CRD with the following command using the variables exported before: `oc patch APIManager ${CRD_NAME}--type merge-p "{\"spec\": ${ORIG_SPEC}}"`.
root_cause: The APIManager CRD defines the amount of replicas per component except for the databases, because the databases must not be set to more than 1 replica. When scaling down is manually performed the operator scales back to the defined number of replicas in the APIManager CRD. Scaling should be performed through APIManager CRD.

title: Can hostPath be used to store logs  locally on OpenShift cluster nodes?
issue: - Can hostPath be used to store logs locally on cluster nodes?- While implementing Cloud-native network function(CNF) solution, is the cluster supported if `hostPath` storage is used to store CNF logs locally on the nodes?
resolution: - It is not recommended to use hostPath to store network element data locally. As mentioned in [RHOCP official docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html/storage/configuring-persistent-storage#persistent-storage-using-hostpath):_In a production cluster, you would not use hostPath. Instead, a cluster administrator would provision a network resource, such as a GCE Persistent Disk volume, an NFS share, or an Amazon EBS volume. Network resources support the use of storage classes to set up dynamic provisioning._- It is also recommended to use [OpenShift Logging](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/latest/html-single/about_openshift_logging/index) to consolidate and [forward logs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/latest/html-single/configuring_logging/index#configuring-log-forwarding) to an external aggregator. This can help achieve comprehensive log aggregation and convenient monitoring.

title: How to add a machine pool to a single AZ for a Multi-AZ ROSA cluster
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - In Multi-AZ ROSA cluster, can we add a machine pool to a single AZ using "rosa create machinepool" command?- I cannot specify a number of machine pool replicas that is not a multiple of 3. Is there an alternative? ~~~ E: Multi AZ clusters require that the replicas be a multiple of 3 ~~~
resolution: - Using **--availability-zone** option, we can select availability zone to create a single AZ machine pool for a multi-AZ cluster. ~~~ $ rosa list machinepools--cluster test-rosa ID AUTOSCALING REPLICAS INSTANCE TYPE LABELS TAINTS AVAILABILITY ZONES SUBNETS SPOT INSTANCES DISK SIZE SG IDs worker No 3 m5.xlarge us-east-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1c No 300 GiB $ rosa create machinepool--cluster=test-rosa--name=test-node-01--replicas=1--availability-zone=us-east-1a ~~~
root_cause: - By default, if you add a machine pool to an existing Multi-AZ cluster, the new machine pool is automatically created in all of the zones, so that the number of replicas are must be a multiple of 3. So the rosa command provides the ability to create a machinepool in a single zone with the "--availability-zone" option.

title: Hosted Control Plane proxy parameter specified using GUI is getting ignored
issue: - The proxy values specified during the hosted control plane deployment via the RHACM UI are being ignored.
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and is being tracked under [bug](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-43784).- This issue is already fixed RHACM 2.12 version which uses MCE 2.7.0- As a workaround, user can use update `hostedcluster` CR to specify proxy details. ~~~ ``` apiVersion: hypershift.openshift.io/v1beta1 kind: HostedCluster spec: configuration: proxy: httpProxy: 'http://proxy.example.com:3128' httpsProxy: 'http://proxy.example.com:3128' noProxy: '10.0.0.0/8' ``` hostedcluster.spec.configuration.proxy. ~~~
root_cause: - The hosted cluster creation UI needs to be fixed to add the proxy configurations correctly in the HostedCluster's spec

title: Deleting protected service account is not allowed
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Service account created in `default` namespace cannot subsequently be deleted- Cluster role binding created in `kube-system` namespace cannot subsequently be deleted- When attempting to delete resources in protected namespaces, errors similar to the following may be presented: ~~~ Error from server (Deleting protected service account under namespace default is not allowed): admission webhook "serviceaccount-validation.managed.openshift.io" denied the request: Deleting protected service account under namespace default is not allowed ~~~
resolution: - Use the below command to delete the Service account. ~~~ $ oc delete sa-n--as backplane-cluster-admin ~~~- If the above command dose not work please open a Support Case at the [Red Hat Customer Portal](https://access.redhat.com) including the action and the error message in the issue description.
root_cause: - Admission webhooks prevent certain resources in protected namespaces from being deleted, even when creation of resources in some protected namespaces is permitted. These affected namespaces include:- `openshift-*`- `kube-*`- `default`

title: Installation of OCP on top of SR-IOV fails to find Virtual Function(VF).
issue: During OpenShift Container Platform installation using Assisted Installer, the following error occurs when trying to use the SR-IOV, nmstate could not handle VF's created, resulting into cluster installation being stuck.
Creating the network bond on top of VF's(Virtual Function) created from PF's(Physical Function) is not working as VF's are not getting discovered.
resolution: The issue is currently being addressed with [NMT-1682](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/NMT-1682). And for the assisted installer, it is being worked on in [MGMT-20617](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MGMT-20617).
root_cause: OCP with cluster network on SR-IOV installations fail because nmstate tries to configure newly-declared VFs before the kernel finishes creating their device names, aborting cluster deployment with “VF interface name not found.” It is the race condition between PF re-apply and VF readiness.

title: Virtual Machine with Database workload has high iowait and load averages
issue: Migrated a Virtual Machine from vSphere to OpenShift Virtualization, the VM now has considerable higher load averages.
Database running in KVM has high load average and disk iowait
resolution: * Change the guest caching to "write through", so that the Guest does not need to send the flushes, which are then automatically added by qemu-kvm after each write. * This can be accomplished by 2 equivalent ways: * Option 1: set the Guest disk cache to "none" in the hypervisor and "write through" in the Guest OS. * RHEL KVM * Hypervisor: configure the Guest XML with cache="none" for the relevant disks ~~~... ~~~ * Guest OS: set each relevant disk to "write through" ~~~ # virtio-blk echo 'write through' > /sys/block/vdX/cache_type # virtio-scsi echo "write through" > /sys/class/scsi_disk/0:0:0:0/cache_type ~~~ * OpenShift Virtualization * Hypervisor: no changes needed, "none" is the default * Guest OS: set each relevant disk to "write through" ~~~ # virtio-blk echo 'write through' > /sys/block/vdX/cache_type # virtio-scsi echo "write through" > /sys/class/scsi_disk/0:0:0:0/cache_type ~~~ * Option 2: set the Guest disk cache to "directsync" * RHEL KVM * Hypervisor: configure the Guest XML with cache="directsync" for the relevant disks ~~~... ~~~ * Guest OS: no changes needed, cache_type inside the guest should be reported as "write through" ~~~ $ cat > /sys/block/vdX/cache_type write through ~~~ * OpenShift Virtualization * This cache mode is not available yet, use Option 1. * To make the Guest side changes persistent, an udev rule can be used: ~~~ $ cat /etc/udev/rules.d/50-virtioblk-cache.rules # virtio-blk cache ACTION=="add|change", KERNEL=="vd[a-z]*", ATTR{cache_type}="write through" # virtio-scsi cache ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="scsi_disk", ATTR{cache_type}:="write through" ~~~
root_cause: * The Guest OS kernel is doing extra work and generating contention by sending flushes down the virtual storage device, as the device is reported with "writeback" cache. * Setting cache="none" in the Guest definition disables the page cache, but it may still hit other caches so it is seen as writeback from the Guest, therefore it sends flushes. * Setting the hypervisor side caching between "none" and "directsync" affects the following settings: Mode | cache.writeback | cache.direct--------- |--------- |--------- none |- | disk image opened with O_DIRECT directsync | add fsync() each write request from guest | disk image opened with O_DIRECT * Setting the Guest OS cache_type setting for the virtio-blk device makes: Guest cache_type | qemu-kvm will | Guest OS will--------- |--------- |--------- write through | add fsync() each write request from guest |- write back |- | send flushes * With the suggested settings, the flushes/fsync() are moved from Guest OS to the Hypervisor, reducing the load on the Guest OS and improving efficiency for certain specific workloads.

title: ClusterLogForwarder is not sending full audit logs to external rsyslog
issue: - Enabled `ClusterLogForwarder` to send audit logs to external rsyslog log aggregator, but full audit logs are not appearing.- Checking the OpenShift audit logs on the node using `oc node-logs`, full log entries are shown.- The output send from the `ClusterLogForwarder`, only the following is shown: ~~~ fluentd: type=ANOM_PROMISCUOUS msg=audit(xxxxxxxxxx.989:205): dev=vethxxxxxxxx prom=0 old_prom=256 auid=4xxxxxxx5 uid=800 gid=801 ses=4xxxxxxx 5AUID="unset" UID="openvswitch" GID="xxxxxfs" ~~~- The collector is not forwarding the logs to external `rsyslog` server when `RFC5424` is used with `ClusterLogForwarder` custom resource.- The `payloadKey` syslog parameter is configured to `message` to capture audit messages.
resolution: Most of the audit data is being dropped because of the `payloadKey` config: payloadKey: message Remove the `payloadKey` entry to allow the full log to arrive. The OpenShift Logging operator will redeploy the collector pods with the new configuration.
root_cause: As per the [syslog parameters documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/log_collection_forwarding/configuring-log-forwarding.html#cluster-logging-collector-log-forward-examples-syslog-parms): ~~~ Configuring the `payloadKey` parameter prevents other parameters from being forwarded to the syslog. ~~~ Looking at the logs in Kibana from a default deployment, other parts of the log actually show significantly more information than the `message` field. For instance, the `annotations.authorization.k8s.io/reason` key shows: ~~~ RBAC: allowed by ClusterRoleBinding "system:openshift:operator:kube-controller-manager-operator" of ClusterRole "cluster-admin" to ServiceAccount "kube-controller-manager-operator/openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator" ~~~

title: Pods with NetApp Trident iSCSI volume stuck in "ContainerCreating" and "no devices present yet"
issue: A Pod that is using a `PersistentVolume` provided by the NetApp Trident CSI driver is failing to start with the following error message being shown: ~~~ 1h10m Warning FailedMount pod/alertmanager-main-0 MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "pvc-a9508fe2-72d6-4dc2-9e9f-9a4f334917ea": rpc error: code = Internal desc = rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to stage volume: no devices present yet ~~~

The `trident-node-linux-` Pods in the Trident namespace show error messages like this: ~~~ 2025-07-07T07:34:52.025514973Z time="2025-07-07T07:34:52Z" level=error msg="Could not find iSCSI device: no devices present yet" logLayer=csi_frontend requestID=13632312-cb25-4c60-9006-ec3b222efe1f requestSource=CSI workflow="node_server=stage" 2025-07-07T07:34:54.030689498Z time="2025-07-07T07:34:54Z" level=warning msg="Could not find any devices " logLayer=csi_frontend requestID=13632312-cb25-4c60-9006-ec3b222efe1f requestSource=CSI workflow="node_server=stage" ~~~
resolution: * Ensure that the `nodePrep` for iSCSI is enabled in the Trident configuration: ~~~ apiVersion: trident.netapp.io/v1 kind: TridentOrchestrator metadata: name: trident [..] spec: [..] nodePrep:- iscsi [..] ~~~ This will ensure that on the OpenShift Container Platform Node, the necessary services and configuration is in place before Pods are scheduled on the Node.
root_cause: * The `iscsid` and the `multipathd` systemd units on the OpenShift Container Platform Node are not running.

title: How to define environment variables for custom image of Red Hat build of Keycloak?
issue: - Deployments do not respect environment variables set into `Keycloak` resource definition when using `Red Hat build of Keycloak`custom images.- How to change `Red Hat build of Keycloak` environment variables, like relational database transaction timeouts, while using custom images.
resolution: When building `Red Hat build of Keycloak` custom images, for example to use different `JDBC drivers` that are already bundled into base images, like when using `Microsoft MS-SQL` as relational back-end database, environment variables must be set into container file definition. For example, if user need to customize values of any of `KC_*` or `QUARKUS_*` environment variables, those must be set at container file definition, like example below for `Microsoft MS-SQL` driver inclusion to the custom image: ~~~ FROM registry.redhat.io/rhbk/keycloak-rhel9:26.0-1747828910 ADD--chown=keycloak:keycloak--chmod=644 https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/microsoft/sqlserver/mssql-jdbc/12.8.1.jre11/mssql-jdbc-12.8.1.jre11.jar /opt/keycloak/providers/mssql-jdbc.jar ENV KC_HEALTH_ENABLED=true ENV KC_METRICS_ENABLED=true ENV QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT=1300 ENV QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_JDBC_MAX_LIFETIME=60000 ENV QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_JDBC_ACQUISITION_TIMEOUT=30 ~~~
root_cause: Environment variables are not correctly set when user define them at `Keycloak` custom resource definition while using `Red Hat build of Keycloak` custom images.

title: PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit warning alerts on any namespace with running VMs
issue: - If a namespace has a running VM, the warning alert `PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit` fires with the message: ~~~ The pod disruption budget is preventing further disruption to pods because it is at the minimum allowed level. ~~~
resolution: - The issue is fixed in OpenShift Virtualization 4.17.7 where a silence rule will be created by default to silence the PDB alert of VMs.- Because of [CNV-55759](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-55759), the upgraded cluster might still have invalid rule in `negative form(!~)`, use the following command to confirm: ~~~ # oc exec alertmanager-main-0-n openshift-monitoring-- amtool silence--alertmanager.url http://localhost:9093 ec86e733-4e94-45aa-a477-105feeba735d alertname="PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit" poddisruptionbudget!~"kubevirt-disruption-budget-.*" 3000-01-01 00:00:00 UTC hyperconverged-cluster-operator Silence KubeVirt PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit alerts ~~~ If it is present, this rule in "negative form" needs to be manually removed to facilitate the creation of the new rule: ~~~ # oc rsh-n openshift-monitoring alertmanager-main-0 for i in `amtool silence--alertmanager.url http://localhost:9093 |grep 'alertname="PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit"' |awk '{print $1}'`;do amtool silence expire--alertmanager.url http://localhost:9093 $i;done ~~~- For previous versions, as a workaround, create a new rule to silence `kubevirt-disruption-budget` pdb by running the following command: ~~~ # oc-n openshift-monitoring exec-ti alertmanager-main-0-c alertmanager-- amtool silence add alertname=PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit poddisruptionbudget=~kubevirt-disruption-budget-.*--alertmanager.url=http://localhost:9093--duration="5000d"--comment="kubevirt pdb" ~~~ Refer [Silencing alerts](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html-single/monitoring/index#silencing-alerts_managing-alerts)
root_cause: The issue is known and mentioned in the OpenShift Virtualization [release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.15/html/virtualization/release-notes#virt-4-15-known-issues): The Pod Disruption Budget (PDB) is created for virtual machines with live migrate eviction strategy to prevent the eviction of virt-launcher pods during a node drain. These PDBs are created with `minAvailable: 1`. When the VMs are not migrating, only a single virt-launcher pod will be available. This triggers the alert `PodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit` which is fired when the healthy pod is equal to `minAvailable`. The alert is false and a silence rule is created by default in OpenShift Virtualization 4.17 as per ([CNV-33834](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-33834)).

title: OpenShift NetApp CSI (Trident) using iSCSI loss of Multipath paths during ONTAP Upgrade
issue: During a NetApp ONTAP rolling upgrade or a takeover/giveback event while running OpenShift, can result in multipath paths not recovering during the giveback. The next NetApp controller to upgrade can result in no viable paths to the storage LUNs.
resolution: Before performing an ONTAP upgrade on the NetApp Storage Arrays, ensure the NetApp Trident self-healing function is disabled. This will be fixed in a future release of the NetApp CSI driver. More details at: [Trident iSCSI paths do not recover after ONTAP Upgrade](https://kb.netapp.com/Cloud/Astra/Trident/Trident_iSCSI_paths_do_not_recover_after_ONTAP_Upgrade) [How to disable Trident iscsi self healing feature](https://kb.netapp.com/Cloud/Astra/Trident/How_to_disable_Trident_iscsi_self_healing_feature) Disclaimer: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.
root_cause: The Trident CSI driver does not recover all paths during a takeover/giveback event if self-healing is enabled.

title: Multiple secrets are creating only while deploying the application from OpenShift console
issue: - While creating application using template from OpenShift console, multiple secrets are creating and not deleting after application is removed.
resolution: - The application deployed by OpenShift console using a template, generates ` TemplateInstance` CR which is used to deploy application.- `TemplateInstance` contains information about the application which are encoded in the secret and are being used to create the application. These parameters works as environment variable in the template.- The correct way to delete secrets and other application related objects automatically, is by deleting `TemplateInstance` CR, Once the templateInstance is deleted, all the respective object including secrets will be deleted. Make sure to be cautious while deleting TemplateInstance CR.- To clean up application objects,use the below command, ~~~ $ oc delete templateinstance-n ~~~

title: vsphere cloud credentials not syncing correctly on GUI

title: OCP 4.x: 20-40 s page stalls (503) after scaling a Route’s pods
issue: - After an application Deployment is scaled down (pods deleted) and scaled back up, a client that refreshes the web page within ~1 minute experiences 20 s (sometimes two consecutive 20 s) stalls before the page loads.- Browser Developer Tools show the initial request blocked for ~20 s → HTTP 503- Router logs show `sC--` or `SD` and 15s+ timings `0/15015/-1/-1/20017` in access logs. This would need to be enabled by following this documentation [4.8.9.5. Configuring Ingress access logging](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/networking/networking-operators#nw-configure-ingress-access-logging_configuring-ingress)- New connections from a different client succeed immediately
resolution: - Upgrade to OCP 4.18.4 or later. These versions include the `idleConnectionTerminationPolicy` field.- Edit the default IngressController (namespace openshift-ingress-operator): ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: IngressController metadata: name: default spec: idleConnectionTerminationPolicy: Immediate ~~~- Enabling this option `Immediate`; forces HAProxy to close idle client connections on every reload, eliminating stale-endpoint retries as documented in [Chapter 15. IngressController](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/operator_apis/ingresscontroller-operator-openshift-io-v1#specification-14)- (Optional) shorten reload delay if pod churn is low: ~~~ spec: tuningOptions: reloadInterval: 2s # default 5s ~~~- Reduces the 4-5 s gap in which the second pod deletion can reintroduce stale IPs.- Caution: In high-churn clusters a shorter interval increases router CPU/memory.
root_cause: - [Initially tracked in this Jira](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-56141)- This issue is caused by connections that are in "ESTABLISHED" state connecting a client via the loadbalancer to the router pod that were talking to a pod that is no longer present. When a pod is deleted, a new HAProxy pid is created to handle new inbound connections with the new pod IP's that took the place of the (now deleted) older pods. However, Existing sessions are still connected to the PREVIOUS pid that does not know about the change yet. This pid handles the new GET on the same session, and times out looking for the pod IP that used to exist according to it's local haproxy.config file. A new client session on a new port would go immediately to the new haproxy process, and route properly. Older sessions get routed through the same previous handler process which is reaped late.- The new option in 4.18.4+ is added to address this behavior: `ingresscontroller.spec.idleConnectionTerminationPolicy` which reaps connections immediately when the server pod is removed. This is documented in `explain` as below: ~~~ oc explain ingresscontroller.spec.idleConnectionTerminationPolicy--- KIND: IngressController VERSION: operator.openshift.io/v1 FIELD: idleConnectionTerminationPolicy DESCRIPTION: idleConnectionTerminationPolicy maps directly to HAProxy's idle-close-on-response option and controls whether HAProxy keeps idle frontend connections open during a soft stop (router reload). Allowed values for this field are "Immediate" and "Deferred". The default value is "Deferred". When set to "Immediate", idle connections are closed immediately during router reloads. This ensures immediate propagation of route changes but may impact clients sensitive to connection resets. When set to "Deferred", HAProxy will maintain idle connections during a soft reload instead of closing them immediately. These connections remain open until any of the following occurs:- A new request is received on the connection, in which case HAProxy handles it in the old process and closes the connection after sending the response.- HAProxy's `timeout http-keep-alive` duration expires (300 seconds in OpenShift's configuration, not configurable).- The client's keep-alive timeout expires, causing the client to close the connection. ~~~- HAProxy keeps the client connection open and retries the dead endpoint three times (default 5 s connectTimeout) before returning 503 (~15–20 s).- Browsers that reuse the same TCP port may hit this 20s timeout twice when two router pods serviced the original page load, producing the observed 40 s stall.

title: Openshift LightSpeed postgres pod is in crashloopbackoff with ERROR: tuple already updated by self
issue: The Openshift LightSpeed PostgreSQL pod is terminated causing the database process in the pod to be unable to shut down in an orderly fashion. This most leaves unwanted artifacts behind putting the pod into an infinite crashloopbackoff during automatic recovery. The following error is seen in the logs of the Quay/Clair PostgreSQL pod: ~~~~ 2025-07-07 08:05:00.112 UTC [40] ERROR: tuple already updated by self ~~~~
resolution: To fix the current state of the database follow below steps: 1. Find the name of the ols postgres pod that is in the crash loop. ~~~~ # oc project Using project "openshift-lightspeed" on server "https://api.mycluster.example.com:6443". # oc get pods | grep postgres lightspeed-postgres-server-6975cb957d-5wwdp 1/1 Running 1 (101s ago) 107s ~~~~ 2. Start an "oc debug" session with the pod. ~~~~ # oc debug pod/lightspeed-postgres-server-6975cb957d-5wwdp Starting pod/lightspeed-postgres-server-6975cb957d-5wwdp-debug... Pod IP: X.Y.2.30 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-5.1$ ~~~~ 3. Scale down the Lightspeed Operator and then the Lightspeed postgres pods. ~~~~ # oc scale deployment/lightspeed-operator-controller-manager--replicas=0 deployment.apps/lightspeed-operator-controller-manager scaled # oc scale deployment/lightspeed-postgres-server--replicas=0 deployment.apps/lightspeed-postgres-server scaled ~~~~ 4. From the command line of the debug session execute run-postgresql. The run-postgresql is a custom script used to start and configure a PostgreSQL database instance inside a container. As part of the start-up process, this script will create the necessary files, including /var/lib/pgsql/openshift-custom-postgresql.conf and /var/lib/pgsql/passwd which are used by command pg_ctl stop to control authenticated graceful shutdown. ~~~~ # oc exec-it lightspeed-postgres-server-6975cb957d-5wwdp-debug-- /bin/bash bash-5.1$ run-postgresql ~~~~ 5. Execute the below command to cleanly shutdown Postgres. ~~~~ bash-5.1$ pg_ctl stop-D /var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata waiting for server to shut down....2025-07-07 17:34:38.995 UTC [32] LOG: received fast shutdown request 2025-07-07 17:34:38.997 UTC [32] LOG: aborting any active transactions 2025-07-07 17:34:38.999 UTC [32] LOG: background worker "logical replication launcher" (PID 38) exited with exit code 1 2025-07-07 17:34:39.000 UTC [33] LOG: shutting down 2025-07-07 17:34:39.002 UTC [33] LOG: checkpoint starting: shutdown immediate 2025-07-07 17:34:39.011 UTC [33] LOG: checkpoint complete: wrote 3 buffers (0.0%); 0 WAL file(s) added, 0 removed, 0 recycled; write=0.001 s, sync=0.003 s, total=0.012 s; sync files=2, longest=0.002 s, average=0.002 s; distance=0 kB, estimate=0 kB; lsn=0/14EBA68, redo lsn=0/14EBA68 2025-07-07 17:34:39.027 UTC [32] LOG: database system is shut down done server stopped ~~~~ 6. Execute below command to start Postgres. The output should wait there indefinitely (no errors). Press the enter key a couple of times to get back to the cmd prompt. Once it appears ~~~~ bash-5.1$ pg_ctl start-D /var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata waiting for server to start....2025-07-07 17:34:48.101 UTC [49] LOG: starting PostgreSQL 16.8 on x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (GCC) 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-5), 64-bit 2025-07-07 17:34:48.101 UTC [49] LOG: listening on IPv4 address "0.0.0.0", port 5432 2025-07-07 17:34:48.101 UTC [49] LOG: listening on IPv6 address "::", port 5432 2025-07-07 17:34:48.104 UTC [49] LOG: listening on Unix socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432" 2025-07-07 17:34:48.108 UTC [49] LOG: listening on Unix socket "/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432" 2025-07-07 17:34:48.111 UTC [52] LOG: database system was shut down at 2025-07-07 17:34:39 UTC 2025-07-07 17:34:48.116 UTC [49] LOG: database system is ready to accept connections done server started bash-5.1$ ~~~~ 7. Execute the below command again and wait for Postgres to stop. The series of steps will ensure a clean shutdown and restart. Exit the debug session ~~~~ bash-5.1$ pg_ctl stop-D /var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata waiting for server to shut down....2025-07-07 17:35:08.066 UTC [49] LOG: received fast shutdown request 2025-07-07 17:35:08.068 UTC [49] LOG: aborting any active transactions 2025-07-07 17:35:08.070 UTC [49] LOG: background worker "logical replication launcher" (PID 55) exited with exit code 1 2025-07-07 17:35:08.070 UTC [50] LOG: shutting down 2025-07-07 17:35:08.072 UTC [50] LOG: checkpoint starting: shutdown immediate 2025-07-07 17:35:08.081 UTC [50] LOG: checkpoint complete: wrote 3 buffers (0.0%); 0 WAL file(s) added, 0 removed, 0 recycled; write=0.001 s, sync=0.003 s, total=0.011 s; sync files=2, longest=0.002 s, average=0.002 s; distance=0 kB, estimate=0 kB; lsn=0/14EBB18, redo lsn=0/14EBB18 2025-07-07 17:35:08.098 UTC [49] LOG: database system is shut down done server stopped bash-5.1$ exit ~~~~ 8. Scale up the Lightspeed postgres and then the Lightspeed Operator pods. ~~~~ # oc scale deployment/lightspeed-postgres-server--replicas=1 deployment.apps/lightspeed-postgres-server scaled # oc scale deployment/lightspeed-operator-controller-manager--replicas=1 deployment.apps/lightspeed-operator-controller-manager scaled ~~~~

title: How to provision storage in static provisioning from OpenShift console
issue: - How to provision persistent storage using NFS from OpenShift console.
resolution: - To configure persistent volume statically, follow the below steps, 1. Create an object definition for the PV, ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata: name: pv0001 spec: capacity: storage: 5Gi accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce nfs: path: server: persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain ~~~ 2. Create a persistent volume claim (PVC) that binds to the PV, ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: name: nfs-claim1 spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 5Gi volumeName: pv0001 storageClassName: "" ~~~ 3. Now to use the persistent volume in openshift workload, Go to Workloads-> Deployments-> Add Storage.![Add Storage](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/screenshot_2025-07-08_at_1.46.19_am.png) 4. Then select the PVC that was created and add the mount path.![Add Storage](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/screenshot_2025-07-08_at_1.50.44_am.png)

title: In RHEL 9.3 or later, "irqbalance: Cannot change IRQ 76 affinity: Input/output error "
issue: `irqbalance` outputs error messages such as following. ``` Jan 29 10:24:07 rhel9 /usr/sbin/irqbalance[854]: Cannot change IRQ 0 affinity: Input/output error Jan 29 10:24:07 rhel9 /usr/sbin/irqbalance[854]: /usr/sbin/irqbalance[1041]: IRQ 0 affinity is now unmanaged ```
resolution: * Please confirm whether this issue affects your system environment. If so, kindly review the following Knowledge Base article and update irqbalance to the latest available version:- [After update openshift from 4.14 to 4.16, irqbalance report: Cannot change IRQ xxxx affinity: No space left on device](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7103050).
root_cause: * Since irqbalance-1.9.2-3.el9, the error starts to print which is an expected behaviour. * `irqbalance` has improved error handling; failures in affinity changes, which are just ignored in old versions, will recorded in logs. * This issue is discussed in BZ[2227536 – irqbalance: Cannot change IRQ 76 affinity: Input/output error](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2227536) ``` Thanks for reporting the issue. However I think it is expected due to upstream patch: 9a1fd29a82c97 ("activate_mapping: report error reason") and eee7917ef52726 ("activate_mapping: only blacklist irq if error is considered permanent"). In short words, if a IRQ number failed to set affinity due to!(ENOSPC && EAGAIN && EBUSY && EINVAL && ERANGE && ENOMEM) error, it will be kicked out of schedule list in case of re-set affinity next time, and at the same time throw out a error message to report the failing details. Previous version of irqbalance will just fail with no error report, so users don't know if a irq number is affinity set successfully or not, this bug is addressed in bz2184735, and the patches I mentioned previously is meant to fix this bz. ```

title: Updating the Default SSL Certificate for a Custom Domain Route in Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO)
issue: - How can I update the default SSL certificate for a custom domain used in external Routes.- How to automate the TLS certificate management for a custom domain used with OpenShift Routes.- what would be the most effective and recommended approach to achieve this?- Is it necessary to trigger a rolling update? After certificate secret generated by cert-manager, when cert-manager renews the certificate.
resolution: - Install [cert manager operator](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/security_and_compliance/cert-manager-operator-for-red-hat-openshift#cert-manager-about_cert-manager-operator-about) and configure it to use Let’s Encrypt on [ARO](https://cloud.redhat.com/experts/aro/cert-manager/).- Note: If you install cert-manager with version 1.16.0, It fails with RBAC values. There is a workaround mentioned in the [Article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7122938) for the [BUG](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-56758).- Create a new secret instead of updating the existing one, because changes to the contents of a secret are automatically propagated by the kubelet to mounted volumes, and do not trigger a rolling update of the pods. ~~~ $ oc create secret tls--cert=--key=-n openshift-ingress ~~~- Update the Ingress Controller configuration with the newly created secret ~~~ $ oc patch ingresscontroller.operator--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"defaultCertificate": {"name": " "}}}'-n openshift-ingress-operator ~~~- Once the secret generated by cert-manager and when cert-manager renews the certificate in the future, there is no need to trigger a rolling update. The operator will automatically roll out the updated certificate.

title: openshift-marketplace pods not Running due to missing image pull secrets - FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret
issue: - Pods in `openshift-marketplace` namespace are not Running due to the operator catalogs image pull (dockercfg) secrets missing ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-marketplace get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE certified-operators-frz5g 0/1 Running 0 1m community-operators-rtpll 1/1 Running 2 75d marketplace-operator-7dc58b684b-xjjfx 1/1 Running 2 121d redhat-marketplace-v9tzg 0/1 Init:3/8 0 1m redhat-operators-hl5wr 0/1 Init:3/8 0 1m ~~~- Events in `openshift-marketplace` namespace are showing *Warning
`FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret`
resolution: - Disable all default Catalog Sources: ~~~ $ oc patch OperatorHub cluster--type json-p '[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/disableAllDefaultSources", "value": true}]' ~~~- Enable the internal image registry (`managementState: Managed`) with 1 replica using ephemeral (`emptyDir`) storage: ~~~ $ oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io cluster--type json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/replicas", "value": 1}]' $ oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io cluster--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"storage":{"emptyDir":{}}}}' $ oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io cluster--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"managementState":"Managed"}}' ~~~- Re-enable all default Catalog Sources so the related image pull Secrets are automatically recreated: ~~~ $ oc patch OperatorHub cluster--type json-p '[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/disableAllDefaultSources", "value": false}]' ~~~
root_cause: [Legacy service account API token secrets are no longer generated for each service account](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes#ocp-4-16-notable-technical-changes_release-notes) ~~~ Before OpenShift Container Platform 4.16, when the integrated OpenShift image registry was enabled, a legacy service account API token secret was generated for every service account in the cluster. Starting with OpenShift Container Platform 4.16, when the integrated OpenShift image registry is enabled, the legacy service account API token secret is no longer generated for each service account. Additionally, when the integrated OpenShift image registry is enabled, the image pull secret generated for every service account no longer uses a legacy service account API token. Instead, the image pull secret now uses a bound service account token that is automatically refreshed before it expires. ~~~ For more information, see [Automatically generated image pull secrets](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html-single/nodes/#auto-generated-sa-token-secrets_nodes-pods-secrets)

title: Hosted cluster creation on agent platform with proxy fails due to API connectivity issues
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - While creating hosted cluster on agent platform using a proxy, the installation fails abruptly after the worker nodes are added to the hosted cluster.- The hosted cluster is stuck in `partial` state with worker nodes of the hosted cluster ready. Majority of the operators either fail to setup or are stuck in progressing state.- The pods in `openshift-dns` and `openshift-multus` are stuck in `ContainerCreating` state with tls secrets not being found. ~~~ 97m Warning FailedMount pod/dns-default-bmdpw MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "metrics-tls": secret "dns-default-metrics-tls" not found ~~~- The pod `service-ca-operator-xxx` in the namespace `openshift-service-ca-operator` is in `CrashLoopBackOff` state with API connectivity issues. ~~~ 2025-07-02T05:45:56.834935002Z F0702 05:45:56.834813 1 cmd.go:182] failed checking apiserver connectivity: Get "https://172.32.0.1:443/apis/coordination.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/openshift-service-ca-operator/leases/service-ca-operator-lock": context deadline exceeded ~~~
resolution: - The kubernetes endpoint `172.20.0.1` has to be added in the `noProxy` section. Setting `kubernetes` in no proxy will also add the kubernetes endpoint in `noProxy`.
root_cause: - Hosted clusters use a local proxy in every compute node to communicate with the control plane. This local proxy listens on IP address `172.20.0.1` and forwards traffic to API server.- When an external proxy is being used the local proxy needs to use external proxy to send traffic outside. Hence, the external proxy should have the IP address `172.20.0.1` added in the `noProxy` section. The [document](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html-single/hosted_control_planes/index#hcp-proxy-api_hcp-networking) can be referred for more details.

title: Error: namespace object is not managed in ArgoCD synchronization
issue: ArgoCD is returning the following error during the synchronization of an application: ~~~ ComparisonError: Namespace "XXXX" for Service "XXXXX" is not managed. ~~~
resolution: There are two options to grant permissions to ArgoCD to manage different namespaces. First option[^0] applyes roles and rolebindings and it is referenced in another solution[^1]. This solutions adds more flexibility as the resources and verbs that are granted can be defined. Second option[^2] is applied by labelling the target namespace, and grants all permissions. ***OPTION 1*** It is needed to create a `Role` and a `RoleBinding` to give privileges to the new ArgoCD instance. This way, ArgoCD will be able to create resources in a different namespace. The `role.yaml` should be similar to the one below, but it can be configured with different verbs depending on the user case: ~~~ $ cat < < EOF > > role.yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: namespace: rules:- apiGroups:- "*" resources:- "*" verbs:- Get- List- Watch- Patch EOF ~~~ ~~~ $ oc create-f role.yaml ~~~ The `RoleBinding` should be similar to the following: ~~~ $ cat < < EOF > > rolebinding.yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: namespace: roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Role name: subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: namespace: EOF ~~~ ~~~ $ oc create-f rolebinding.yaml ~~~ After creating the `Role` and `RoleBindig`, the sync process should finish successfully. ***OPTION 2*** To grant access to ArgoCD to manage resources in a namespace, label the namespace with the label "Argo CD.argoproj.io/managed-by" and set the value of the namespace that needs to by managed: ~~~ $ cat < < EOF > > rolebinding.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: nstest // new namespace to be managed by an existing Argo CD instance labels: argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by: openshift-gitops // namespace where Argo CD is deployed EOF ~~~ After adding the label, apply the change to the namespace: ~~~ $ oc apply-f nstest.yaml ~~~ After doing this, ArgoCD should be able to synchronize resources in that namespace. [^0]: https://github.com/redhat-developer/gitops-operator/blob/master/docs/OpenShift%20GitOps%20Usage%20Guide.md#deploy-resources-to-a-different-namespace-with-custom-role [^1]: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5875661 [^2]: https://github.com/redhat-developer/gitops-operator/blob/master/docs/OpenShift%20GitOps%20Usage%20Guide.md#deploy-resources-to-a-different-namespace
root_cause: Due a security fix in GitOps **1.1.2** it's needed to add more privileges to new instances to be able to manage objects in a namespace different from the one in which the instance is installed.

title: Labels are missing on worker nodes after upgrading NFD operator
issue: - cpu model labels are missing on worker nodes.- `system-os_release.OSTREE_VERSION` labels are missing on worker nodes.- `nfd-gc` pod is in CrashLoopBackOff: ~~~ Warning Failed pod/nfd-gc-599d9464b4-mtwbj Error: container create failed: time="2025-05-02T12:15:31Z" level=error msg="runc create failed: unable to start container process: exec: \"nfd-gc\": executable file not found in $PATH" ~~~
resolution: - Unset the `spec.operand.image` parameter `nodefeaturediscovery` configuation, so the pods will take the default image provided by the operator Or set the image as per the operator version. ~~~ $ oc get nodefeaturediscovery-n openshift-nfd-o yaml | grep-i image operand: image: registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ ~~~- Starting from Red Hat OpenShift container platform 4.18, the `NFD CR` no longer needs to contain the image field, and the operator itself will determine the correct image for the operand and will update masters/workers pods as needed.
root_cause: The `spec.operand.image` parameter was set in `nodefeaturediscovery` configuration which pointed out to an outdated image of nfd operator. Older operator images will not have new fixes and features, due to this new feature labels will not get applied. It can also cause issues such as `CrashLoopBackOff` if the image is not compatible with the latest cluster version. ~~~ operand: image: registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-node-feature-discovery:v4.7.0 ~~~

title: Allow management of CAs independently from full certificate chains in GitOps
issue: - Managing multiple clusters requires updating the full certificate chain in GitOps whenever any certificate changes. With multiple clusters, this causes frequent, time-consuming maintenance. Allowing independent management of certificate authorities (CAs) would simplify updates and reduce overhead.
resolution: - Currently, when updating trusted certificates across multiple clusters, it is required to update the entire certificate chain whenever any certificate within the chain changes.- Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE-7809](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7809). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.- This feature request proposes the ability to add or update only the certificate signers (Certificate Authorities, or CAs) within the trusted CA configuration, rather than having to replace the full certificate chain each time. This would streamline certificate management and reduce operational overhead, particularly in environments with numerous clusters.

title: Permission denied when ed25519 keys are used for Red Hat CoreOS nodes
issue: - We are using `ed25519` keys during an OpenShift installation and generating keys using: ~~~ $ ssh-keygen-t ed25519-N ''-f ~~~- The `bootstrap.ign` includes the public key but once the node finishes booting up, there is a permission denied message while accessing the node: ~~~ ssh core@x.x.x.x core@x.x.x.x: Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic). ~~~
resolution: - To use `ed25519` keys in the cluster installation, disable `FIPS` in the `install-config.yaml`.- A documentation enhancement is filed to include a note for this issue: [Bug-1962414](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1962414).- Refer to the solution [SSH/SSHD failing in FIPS mode due to unsupported encryption key](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3643252) for more details.
root_cause: - The only supported key types for `FIPS` are the following: ~~~ ecdsa | rsa ~~~- Because `ed25519` key types are not supported with `FIPS` enabled nodes, the user was not able to `ssh` to the OpenShift nodes.

title: Is it safe changing default SCC like adding anyuid SCC to system:authenticated group in OpenShift?
issue: - Is it safe changing default SCC by `oc adm policy add-scc-to-group anyuid system:authenticated` in OpenShift?
resolution: Do not change the SCC for the `system:authenticated` virtual group which includes all internal system service accounts. In sort, modifying the default SCCs is not safe and can cause several issues in the cluster. Some examples:- [The service-ca cluster operator stuck in progressing state and monitoring operator is degraded due to SCC modifications](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5875621).- [Operator `service-ca` is blocking cluster upgrade in RHOCP 4: service-ca does not have available replicas](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6820151). Red Hat recommends creating custom SCCs only for the required scope and not changing the default SCCs for these virtual groups.
root_cause: Modifying the default SCCs is a cluster-wide breaking change. All pods get different SCC when redeployed (not immediately, this makes the issue worse), and will get into issues like UID mismatch permission denied issue when using `ReadWriteMany` persistent volumes. Also makes some `CreateContainerConfigError` pods. Even using `system:authenticated:oauth` virtual group (in other words, normal users) may break other users deployments. Refer to [why editing reserved OpenShift SCCs could severely impact OCP functionality](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7080694) for additional information.

title: Issues when creating an image larger than 1GB using horizon UI

resolution: Following the solution [The portal Marketplace.redhat.com is not longer avaliable since April 1st 2025](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7121317), in the Openshift Marketplace there will be a catalog source pod for each catalog source set and there is a `opm cli` command interface for the Operator SDK. title: Increase the verbosity or log level of the Console
issue: - How can the log level verbosity of the Openshift Console be increased?- Can the verbosity of the Openshift Console be changed?- How to troubleshoot authentication issues and increase openshift-authentication pods loglevel to Debug in Openshift Container Platform 4?
resolution: There are 2 ways to set the `logLevel`/`Verbosity` for the console PODs. You can either:- Set the `logLevel` in the console.operator config._**This is the preferred method**._- Unmanage the `console` deployment and set the `verbosity` to the desired value._**IMPORTANT NOTE**: Reverting the debug log level is important to avoid exposure of sensitive logs._ ### Configure the Console Operator The console operator accepts 5 different value for the `logLevel`: | logLevel | matching Verbosity level | |---|---| | "" | none | | "Normal" | 2 | | "Debug" | 4 | | "Trace" | 6 | | "TraceAll" | 10 | #### How to check the current logLevel- Checking the `logLevel` in the console operator: ``` $ oc get consoles.operator.openshift.io cluster-o json | jq-r.spec.logLevel ```- Checking the `verbosity` in the console deployment: ``` $ oc get deployment console-n openshift-console-o json | jq-r '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].command' ``` Check the value of the `-v` option in the command. The absence of `-v` option will suggest that the `logLevel` was set to "" #### Set the desired `logLevel` in the console operator ``` $ LOGLEVEL= $ oc patch consoles.operator.openshift.io cluster--type=json-p "[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/logLevel\",\"value\":\"${LOGLEVEL}\"}]" ``` #### Revert the `logLevel` to the default value in the console operator ``` $ LOGLEVEL=$(oc get crd consoles.operator.openshift.io-o json | jq-r '.spec.versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties.logLevel.default') $ oc patch consoles.operator.openshift.io cluster--type=json-p "[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/logLevel\",\"value\":\"${LOGLEVEL}\"}]" ``` ### Unmanage the **console-operator** and increase the log level in the console deployment to a specific value_**Disclaimer:** Please note that the sample code within this article is provided for customer benefit, but, is not supported by Red Hat. Customers can use it "as it is" or by customizing it appropriately. Red Hat does not support custom code. Please refer to the Scope of coverage (What Red Hat supports) for further details._ In order to increase the log level of the Console POD(s) to a specific verbosity (from 0 to 10), the `console-operator` will be set to unmanaged, this should be a temporary solution, and this should be reverted once the logs have been collected. 1. Set the console-operator Deployment unmanaged ~~~ oc patch clusterversion version--type merge-p '{"spec":{"overrides":[{"kind":"Deployment","group":"apps","name":"console-operator","namespace":"openshift-console-operator","unmanaged":true}]}}' ~~~ 2. Scale down the console-operator deployment ~~~ oc scale deployment/console-operator-n openshift-console-operator--replicas=0 ~~~ 3. Increase the log verbose in the deployment/console ~~~ # Edit the deployment/console oc edit deployment/console-n openshift-console # Replace in the command section the-v=2 (default) by-v=8- command:- /opt/bridge/bin/bridge---public-dir=/opt/bridge/static---config=/var/console-config/console-config.yaml---service-ca-file=/var/service-ca/service-ca.crt---v=2 # <= Replace the 2 by 8 ~~~ 4. Confirm that the command option was successfully edited ~~~ oc get deployment console-n openshift-console-o json | jq-r '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].command' ~~~ 5. Reduce the number of POD to 1 to consolidate all messages in 1 POD log (_Optional_) ~~~ oc scale deployment/console-n openshift-console--replicas=1 ~~~ 6. Review the logs from the POD (_Optional_) ~~~ oc logs-n openshift-console-c console--tail=10-f ~~~ 7. Collecting the logs for sharing them with the support (_Optional_) ~~~ oc adm inspect co/console ~~~ Collect the inspect folder in a tar file and append it to your Support case. #### Revert the changes, and set back the deployment to be managed As soon as the logs have been reviewed and/or collected the changes should be reverted. Setting the the **console-operator** to be managed back by the clusterversion will revert all changes. ~~~ oc patch clusterversion version--type json-p '[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/overrides"}]' ~~~
root_cause: In some case, it may be helpful to review advance logs from the console. The **console** deployment is managed by the **console-operator** POD.

title: How to replace the pull secret in OpenShift hosted control planes (HCP)
issue: - How to replace the pull secret in OpenShift hosted control plane (HCP) clusters.- Need to change the pull secret of a hosted control plane (HCP) cluster.
resolution: The solution [how to change the global pull secret in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4902871) provides generic information for updating/changing the pull secret in OpenShift 4 clusters. For HCP clusters, refer to the above solution to change the pull secret for the ***hosting** cluster* (the *management cluster*), and if the pull secret needs to be changed in a ***hosted** cluster*, continue reading this solution. ###Testing a pull secret before changing it in the cluster Before updating the pull secret in the cluster, please test if the new pull secret is valid and working: ~~~ $ podman pull--authfile /path/to/downloaded/pull-secret registry.redhat.io/ubi8/ubi:latest ~~~ ###Replacing the pull secret for a hosted HCP cluster `clusters` is the namespace from the host cluster used in this example. Change it accordingly with the namespace where the `HostedCluster` Custom Resource (CR) for which the pull request is going to be changed is deployed.- Create a new `secret` using updated pull secret data like below: ~~~ $ oc create secret generic--from-file=.dockerconfigjson=./pull-secret.txt--type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson-n clusters ~~~- Update the `HostedCluster` Custom Resource (CR) `.spec.pullSecret.name` with newly created `secret`: ~~~ $ oc edit hostedclusters.hypershift.openshift.io-n clusters ~~~- Verify the `secret` is correctly added to `HostedCluster` CR: ~~~ $ oc get hostedclusters.hypershift.openshift.io-o json-n clusters | jq.spec.pullSecret.name " " ~~~- Verify the respective ``NodePool`` is started updating with new pull secret change: ~~~ $ oc get nodepools.hypershift.openshift.io-n clusters NAME CLUSTER DESIRED NODES CURRENT NODES AUTOSCALING AUTOREPAIR VERSION UPDATINGVERSION UPDATINGCONFIG MESSAGE-ap-south-1a 2 2 False False 4.18.12 False True ~~~
root_cause: To update the pull secret of a hosted HCP cluster, changes needs to be done in the `hostedclusters` resource from the host cluster.

title: How to Use the OpenShift Internal Image Registry as a Pull-Through Cache
issue: - How to configure the OpenShift internal image registry to act as a pull-through cache using `ImageStreams`.
resolution: The OpenShift internal image registry supports pull-through caching by default when external images are referenced through `ImageStreams`. This capability enables automatic caching of remote images inside the cluster registry on first use, enhancing speed and resilience to upstream registry outages. **1. Create an ImageStream Referencing an External Image** An ImageStream can reference an image from an external registry such as Docker Hub, Quay, or Red Hat registry: ~~~ apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: hello # <---CHANGE ME namespace: test # <---CHANGE ME spec: tags:- from: kind: DockerImage name: quay.io/podman/hello name: latest ~~~ Apply the file: ~~~ $ oc apply-f imagestream.yaml ~~~ **2. Use the Internal Registry to Pull the Image** The external image is stored and served by the OpenShift internal registry. Applications or other workloads can now reference the image through the internal registry route or directly through the ImageStream tag. *For example:* Pull using the internal/external route of the registry(The same URL can be used in the Openshift deployment): ~~~ $ podman pull--tls-verify=false ${INTERNAL_REGISTRY}/ /: ~~~ A Deployment can use: ~~~... spec: containers:- name: image: INTERNAL_REGISTRY_URL/ /:... ~~~ The `ImageStreamtag` way: ~~~ $ oc new-app /:...-> Creating resources... deployment.apps "hello" created--> Success Run 'oc status' to view your app.... ~~~ **3. Verify Caching Behavior** Check that the image is available internally: ~~~ $ oc get is-n NAME IMAGE REPOSITORY TAGS UPDATED hello image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/test/hello latest 15 minutes ago ~~~ The internal registry will serve future requests using the cached image, reducing latency and avoiding repeated downloads from the external registry.

title: Authentication Cluster Operator is Degraded and Pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff state.
issue: - Authentication operator is degraded because `OAuthServerDeploymentDegraded: 1 of 3 requested instances are unavailable` for `oauth-openshift.openshift-authentication` (crashlooping container is waiting in `oauth-openshift-1234xxx` pod)- `oauth` pod is in `CrashLoopBackOff` state, failing with below error message: ~~~ 2025-06-12T13:38:59.943631541Z F0612 13:38:59.943541 1 cmd.go:56] failed to load SNI cert and key: tls: failed to find PEM block with type ending in "PRIVATE KEY" in key input after skipping PEM blocks of the following types: [CERTIFICATE CERTIFICATE] ~~~
resolution: Make sure that the secret that is being referenced on the `ingresscontroller default` object exist on the namespace `openshift-ingress` and contains a correct certificate as defined in the prerequisite for [Replacing the default ingress certificate](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/security_and_compliance/configuring-certificates#replacing-default-ingress_replacing-default-ingress)
root_cause: The secret that was referenced on the `ingresscontroller default` did not had a certificate and keys in the valid format. This secret is internally used by the `openshift-config-managed` and `openshift-authentication` namespaces, which populates the certificate contents on secret `v4-0-config-system-router-certs`. The workflow on how this certificate is populated on the cluster is explained in official docs, check the [custom certificate flow](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/security_and_compliance/certificate-types-and-descriptions#workflow) If the secret of the `custom-ingress` certificate is not valid, the `authentication-operator` is not able to redeploy the `oauth` pod with the new revisions, which in-turns making the authentication cluster degraded with the `OAuthServerDeploymentDegraded`.

title: Node port range overlapping with Ephemeral port range causing issue with MetalLB service
issue: - After increasing the `node port` range it is overlapping with the `ip_local_port_range`.- MetalLB LoadBalancer service is not reachable as the node port assigned to the service is not listening.
resolution: Change the `ip_local_port_range` kernel parameter so that it does not overlap with `node-port range` with either `machine config` or `tuned`. The documentations [tuned](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/scalability_and_performance/using-node-tuning-operator.html) and [machine config](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/machine_configuration/index.html#about-machine-config-operator_machine-config-overview) can be referred to for more details.
root_cause: - The `node port` range was overlapping with `ip_local_port_range`and document bug [OCPBUGS-45077](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-45077) has been registered to improve the documentation.

title: Nodepool creation in a separate agent namespace fails to scale nodes
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - While creating a new nodepool from cli in a separate agent namespace than the current one fails to scale nodes in the hosted cluster.- The nodepool fails to scale nodes with following error. ~~~ message: | 1 of 1 machines are not ready Machine nodepool-hcp-2-c95kf: NoSuitableAgents observedGeneration: 1 ~~~
resolution: - Update the field `agentNamespace` from the hosted cluster CR and replace the existing namespace to the new namespace where the `agent` and respective `InfraEnv` is present. The following command can be used to patch the hosted cluster CR. ~~~ $ oc patch hc/-n hcp--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"platform":{"agent":{"agentNamespace":" "}}}}' ~~~- This patch would not have any effect on the existing nodepools and nodes.
root_cause: - The nodepool creation in a new agent namespace fails to scale nodes as the nodepool CR created is looking for a new agent in the existing `agentNamespace` instead of new `agentNamespace`.- This is because hosted clusters in agent platform support a single namespace.- If the existing `agentNamespace` does not have agent, the nodepool fails to scale the nodes.

title: How to disable the public/private network access to OSdisk of nodes in ARO or self managed OCP on Azure
issue: - Whether it is possible to disable the public and or private network access mode to OSdisks of the cluster nodes hosted on ARO or self-managed?- Is there any downtime required for this? Can this be achieved as day 1 operation i.e at the time installation?- Organization's security auditor's are asking to disable the public and private access to OSdisks of the nodes of OCP.- Is there any plan to have this as a day 1 operation in future release?
resolution: - Openshift installer by default use 'public access from all networks' access mode to the OSdisks of the cluster nodes.- Openshift doesn't bother about the disk being publically available OR should have any private access to any of the networks.- [RFE-5132](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-5132) is raised to perform this in Day-1 i.e. at the time of installation. This would take time, as on date this needs to be implemented in upstream first.- Follow the below procedure to change the disk access for cluster at Day-2, Downtime is not required. ~~~ Login to azure console--> > > Locate your resource group of the cluster---> > > click on the OSdisk---> > > Settings-> > > Networking--> > > Change the disk mode to 'Disable public and private access` ~~~
root_cause: - Openshift doesn't bother about the disk being publically available OR should have any private access to some networks.

title: Error generating must-gather: No available strategies to copy
issue: - During must-gather collection, log messages like the following ones are shown: ~~~ gather output not downloaded: No available strategies to copy ~~~ ~~~ error: unable to download output from pod must-gather-XXXXX: No available strategies to copy ~~~ ~~~ Error running must-gather collection: unable to download output from pod must-gather-XXXXX: No available strategies to copy. ~~~ ~~~ WARNING: rsync command not found in path. Please use your package manager to install it. WARNING: cannot use tar: tar not available in container ~~~- Running must-gather collection in Windows fails with the following message: ~~~ WARNING: rsync command not found in path. Download cwRsync for Windows and add it to your PATH. ~~~
resolution: 1. Install the `rsync` and/or `tar` tool on local system running the `oc adm must-gather` command. The packages on Red Hat Enterprise Linux are `rsync` and `tar`: ~~~ $ sudo yum install rsync tar ~~~ **Note:** for Windows machines, as explained in the [copying files to and from containers documenation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/nodes/containers/nodes-containers-copying-files.html#nodes-containers-copying-files-procedure_nodes-containers-copying-files), the `cwRsync` client should be installed and added to the `PATH`. 2. Run the must-gather command to collect data: ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather ~~~
root_cause: The warning log is produced by the lack of the `rsync` and/or `tar` binary in the local machine where the `oc adm must-gather` command runs. It does not prevent the collection of the data, but the pulling of the data from the must-gather container. More information about the execution and outcomes of `oc adm must-gather` can be found in the article [must-gather copy strategies](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7075924).

title: How to downgrade The MetalLB operator in RHOCP4 ?
issue: - MetalLB version X.Y.Z has a certain bug. Until a backport is released, How to downgrade to a previous version?- Is it possible to downgrade the MetalLB operator?
resolution: OpenShift doesn't natively support operator downgrade, however, there is a downgrade workaround. **Note**: This workaround assumes the MetalLB operator is configured with the `IPAddressPool` CRD. Previous MetalLB versions (4.10 downward) use `AddressPool ` instead and the workaround is still valid for this case. ### Workaround To downgrade the MetalLB operator, these steps must be followed: backup the operator configurations, uninstall the operator, re-install the older version, and re-apply the operator configurations. 1. Backup the MetalLB configurations 1. Get and save all MetalLB CRDs: ~~~ $ oc get MetalLB,IPAddressPool,BGPPeer,BFDProfile,L2Advertisement,BGPAdvertisement-A ~~~ 2. Backup each CRD instance individually: ~~~ $ oc get-o yaml >.yaml For example: $ oc get MetalLB metallb-n metallb-system-o yaml > metallb-MetalLB.yaml ~~~ 2. Uninstall the MetalLB operator Either use the OpenShift CLI or Web console. See [Deleting Operators from a cluster](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html-single/operators/index#olm-deleting-operators-from-a-cluster). 3. Install the older MetalLB version using the CLI Make sure the only specified version of the operator is installed by setting the `startingCSV` and `installPlanApproval` as below while creating the `Subscription` CR: ~~~ apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: metallb-operator-sub namespace: metallb-system spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Manual <-- It has to be "Manual" to prevent automatic operator update. name: metallb-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace startingCSV: metallb-operator.v4.y.z-1 <-- The previous working version of MetalLB operator. ~~~ Make sure to approve the `InstallPlan` to start the installation. For more details, check the [Installing from OperatorHub using the CLI](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html/networking/networking-operators#nw-metallb-installing-operator-cli_metallb-operator-install). 4. Re-apply the MetalLB operator configurations Reconfigure the operator using the backup files. For more details, check [Configuring MetalLB](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html/networking/load-balancing-with-metallb).
root_cause: OpenShift doesn't natively support operator downgrade.

title: DNF crashes with "platform-python: /builddir/build/BUILD/libdnf-0.63.0/libdnf/dnf-sack.cpp:781: gboolean load_yum_repo(DnfSack*, HyRepo, GError**): Assertion `fp_primary' failed" error
issue: - When updating a system with *yum
or *dnf

or trying to install any specific packages, the operation fails, and the following error message is displayed: ~~~ platform-python: /builddir/build/BUILD/libdnf-0.63.0/libdnf/dnf-sack.cpp:781: gboolean load_yum_repo(DnfSack*, HyRepo, GError**): Assertion `fp_primary' failed ~~~
resolution: * Refer to the **Diagnostic Steps** and **Root Cause** sections of this article to understand more about this problem. * If the problem is happening on a **Red Hat Satellite or Capsule 6.11- 6.15** system, then **[upgrade](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2146501)** the setup to **Red Hat Satellite \ Capsule 6.16** or later. This will install the `libsolv` package, which contains the fix without causing any operational impact. * If the problem is observed on a **RHEL 8** system, then perform the following steps i.e. ~~~ # subscription-manager repos--disable=* # subscription-manager repos--enable rhel-8-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms--enable rhel-8-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms--enable satellite-client-6-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms # dnf module disable satellite:el8 # dnf clean all && dnf repoinfo # dnf list--showduplicates libsolv # dnf downgrade libsolv ~~~ **NOTE:** The installed package version is expected to be `libsolv-0.7.20-6.el8`. * In either of the situations, if an **upgrade of the product** or **downgrade of the package** is not possible. Then- Either disable the repository that has the zst compressed metadata.- or else re-create the repository with a supported compression method, e.g., **bzip2** or **gzip**, or **xz**. * Reach out to the [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support) in case any further assistance or clarification is required.
root_cause: - The issue has been reported to the Red Hat Engineering team and is being tracked via [SAT-26026- dnf crashes in assertion because Sat's libsolv lacks ZST support](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SAT-26026) JIRA.- It is only expected to happen when dnf is trying to read and work with a repository metadata having **zst** type compression. Example: ``` total 16-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 3605 May 20 20:54 54242efa319f23112832c95d88e0d68a82e6823a85c059ce2c1bd48df7fa8d1e-filelists.xml.zst-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1108 May 20 20:54 badb63245b7b989e1f90d0e7abbb9909a431ee4be7c34f63a054227d33b45c7c-primary.xml.zst-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 248 May 20 20:54 f1459da5fe6b6e217138a611e956cb034ffee80dfec93c3780276fa8c9a8a1e3-other.xml.zst-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1553 May 20 20:54 repomd.xml ```- The **libsolv** package shipped with **Red Hat Satellite 6.11- 6.15**, lacks the support for **zst compression type**, and hence, if the package is installed from the repositories related to any of those satellite versions, dnf errors out and aborts the operation.- The same has been fixed with the **libsolv** package and its related dependencies shipped with **Red Hat Satellite 6.16** and later. The libsolv package shipped via the `rhel-8-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms` repository also has the same support available.

title: ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd": rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to create rbd image: rbd: ret=-22, Invalid argument
issue: While installing Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) or Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage using Red Hat Ceph Storage (RHCS) in external mode an erasure-coded pool was setup as the default data pool during the Ceph cluster creation. `Noobaa` will use `RBD` which by default does not work with erasure-code pools.- erasure-coded pools by default do not support omap. To work for `RBD` or `CephFS` an additional parameter must be set (see resolution). When trying to create the PVC for `Noobaa` it would hang in the pending state, with the following errors: ~~~ E0123 15:48:01.294750 1 utils.go:210] ID: 19 Req-ID: pvc-5bc7c09d-0216-4946-85d7-0dfb5f27b3a0 GRPC error: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = failed to fetch monitor list using clusterID (openshift-test): missing configuration for cluster ID "openshift-test" E0123 15:48:03.760918 1 utils.go:210] ID: 21 Req-ID: pvc-5bc7c09d-0216-4946-85d7-0dfb5f27b3a0 GRPC error: rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to create rbd image: rbd: ret=-22, Invalid argument E0123 15:48:01.295455 1 controller.go:957] error syncing claim "5bc7c09d-0216-4946-85d7-0dfb5f27b3a0": failed to provision volume with StorageClass "ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd": rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = failed to fetch monitor list using clusterID (openshift-test): missing configuration for cluster ID "openshift-test" I0123 15:48:01.295558 1 event.go:298] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"PersistentVolumeClaim", Namespace:"openshift-test", Name:"db-noobaa-db-pg-3", UID:"5bc7c09d-0216-4946-85d7-0dfb5f27b3a0", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"466828", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'ProvisioningFailed' failed to provision volume with StorageClass "ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd": rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = failed to fetch monitor list using clusterID (openshift-test): missing configuration for cluster ID "openshift-test" E0123 15:48:03.761653 1 controller.go:957] error syncing claim "5bc7c09d-0216-4946-85d7-0dfb5f27b3a0": failed to provision volume with StorageClass "ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd": rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to create rbd image: rbd: ret=-22, Invalid argument ~~~
resolution: - By default, erasure-coded pools work only with operations that perform full object writes and appends (for example, RGW) [Rados Operations with erasure-code](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/storage-ceph/8.1.0?topic=overview-erasure-coding-overwrites).- The erasure-coded pools will not work with `RDB` or `CephFS` unless the pool for `Noobaa` is set to `allow_ec_overwrites true`: ~~~ $ ceph osd pool set ERASURE_CODED_POOL_NAME allow_ec_overwrites true ~~~- If you are still having problems, we recommend opening a support case with Red Hat for assistance.
root_cause: The pools were created as erasure-coded which are not by default used with `Noobaa`:- By default, Ceph pools are created with the type `replicated`.- By contrast, erasure-coded pools use a method of data protection that is different from replication [Erasure code pools overview](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/storage-ceph/8.1.0?topic=strategies-erasure-code-pools-overview).

title: RHACS scrolling issue when assigning roles to auth provider
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: The RHACS UI fails to scroll through all available roles when adding rules to an auth provider configuration. This prevents the ability to effectively create and modify auth providers in environments with a large number of roles.![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/acs_auth_provider_scrolling_roles.png)
resolution: - This issue was identified as a bug and resolved by the Red Hat Engineering team under [ROX-27116](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ROX-27116) for RHACS versions 4.6+.
root_cause: - A default maxHeight value is missing from the wrapper around PatterFly's component which prevents scrolling of long lists. This was corrected in the upstream Stackrox project via [PR 15286](https://github.com/stackrox/stackrox/pull/15287).
