doesn't support DPO or FUA ~~~
resolution: From HPE Alletra 5000/6000 documentation under the [Limitations](https://scod.hpedev.io/csi_driver/container_storage_provider/hpe_alletra_6000/index.html#:~:text=When%20using%20an%20FC%20only%20array%20and%20provisioning%20RWX%20block%20volumes%2C%20the%20%22multi_initiator%22%20attribute%20won%27t%20get%20set%20properly%20on%20the%20volume.%20The%20workaround%20is%20to%20run%20group%20%2D%2Dedit%20%2D%2Discsi_enabled%20yes%20on%20the%20Array%20OS%20CLI) section: Consult the compatibility and support table for supported array OS versions. CSI and CSP specific limitations are listed below.- Striped volumes on grouped arrays are not supported by the CSI driver.- The CSP is not capable of provisioning or importing volumes protected by Peer Persistence.- When using an FC only array and provisioning RWX block volumes, the "multi_initiator" attribute won't get set properly on the volume. The workaround is to run group--edit--iscsi_enabled yes on the Array OS CLI. iSCSI does not work and is not supported on routed data networks. The REST API traffic may be routed and is supported. **Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. **Note for Windows VMs:**- Once the storage has been created with "single-initiator", it will change back from "multi-initiator" (after setting) on the migration. The migration will fail as described.- The only workaround so far is to re-create the VM with new storage after setting the Alletra Storage array to "multi-initiator".
root_cause: By default, HPE Alletra 5000/6000 (Nimble) Storage Array uses "single-initiator". This does not work with OpenShift-Virtualization VM migration from one hypervisor to another. All the storage must have the "multi-initiator" attribute set. When "single-initiator" mode is enabled on an Alletra array (or NimbleOS-based arrays like Alletra 5000/6000), it forces the array to restrict each host (initiator) to its own dedicated access paths. When the sharing is detected (for a brief time the LUNs will be served to both hypervisors), the Alletra will off-line the Volumes (LUNs).

title: Machine API controller does not use new vCenter credentials
issue: - vCenter events show failed login attempts after credentials change, that can lead to account lockout.- After following the solution "[Modifying the vSphere configuration in RHOCP4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4618011)", the `machine-api-controller` continues showing `401: Unauthorized` error.- After changing the password following the documentation steps in "[Rotating cloud provider credentials manually](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/postinstallation_configuration/changing-cloud-credentials-configuration#manually-rotating-cloud-creds_changing-cloud-credentials-configuration)", the `machine-api-controller` pod will not update and reconcile the new credentials automatically. ``` "master-node" error: master-node: reconciler failed to Update machine: failed to reconcile tags: POST https://VCENTER-URL/rest/com/vmware/cis/session: 401 Unauthorized ```
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug: [OCPBUGS-58399](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-58399) #### Workaround Restart the `machine-api-controller` pod: $ oc delete pod-n openshift-machine-api-l k8s-app=controller For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: Machine API controller is not restarted automatically after the password change to use the new credentials.

title: How to install LokiStack Using OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) 4.16+ using Ceph's RADOS Gateway (RGW)
issue: - Cannot install Lokistack **Related Articles:*

[Install Ceph's RADOS Gateway (RGW) in an OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) Environment if not Already Configured](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7127851) [How to install LokiStack Using OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) 4.16+ Using NooBaa Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7002870) [Configure Lifecycle Policies on Noobaa/RGW buckets](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7114687)
resolution: **Starting from no Red Hat Cluster Logging installed** 1. Using OperatorHub install the following operators:- Red Hat OpenShift Logging (at minimum v6.1 (do not configure))- Loki Operator (at minimum v6.1 (do not configure)- Cluster Observability Operator 2. Once the above operators are successfully installed, run the following commands: ~~~ $ oc label namespace openshift-logging openshift.io/cluster-monitoring="true" $ oc label namespace openshift-operators-redhat openshift.io/cluster-monitoring="true" $ oc label namespace openshift-cluster-observability-operator openshift.io/cluster-monitoring="true" ~~~ 3. Create an ObjectBucketClaim in openshift-logging namespace: **NOTE: Please make sure the storageclassName, and other values in this document apply to your specific naming scheme. Failure to do so could result in a failed deployment** ~~~ apiVersion: objectbucket.io/v1alpha1 kind: ObjectBucketClaim metadata: finalizers:- objectbucket.io/finalizer name: loki-bucket-odf namespace: openshift-logging spec: generateBucketName: loki-bucket-odf objectBucketName: obc-openshift-lokistack-bucket-odf storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw ~~~ 4. Get bucket properties from the associated ConfigMap: ~~~ BUCKET_HOST=$(oc get-n openshift-logging configmap loki-bucket-odf-o jsonpath='{.data.BUCKET_HOST}') BUCKET_NAME=$(oc get-n openshift-logging configmap loki-bucket-odf-o jsonpath='{.data.BUCKET_NAME}') BUCKET_PORT=$(oc get-n openshift-logging configmap loki-bucket-odf-o jsonpath='{.data.BUCKET_PORT}') ~~~ 5. Get bucket access key from the associated Secret: ~~~ ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(oc get-n openshift-logging secret loki-bucket-odf-o jsonpath='{.data.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}' | base64-d) SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(oc get-n openshift-logging secret loki-bucket-odf-o jsonpath='{.data.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}' | base64-d) ~~~ 6. Before creating the secret, we must validate what port RGW is using. If using `443`, we'll need to use `https`. If using `80`, we'll need to use `http`. ~~~ echo $BUCKET_PORT ~~~ or ~~~ $ oc get svc-n openshift-storage | grep rgw ~~~ 7. Create an Object Storage secret with keys as follows: ##Select One: **For http port 80:** ~~~ oc create-n openshift-logging secret generic lokistack-dev-odf \--from-literal=access_key_id="${ACCESS_KEY_ID}" \--from-literal=access_key_secret="${SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}" \--from-literal=bucketnames="${BUCKET_NAME}" \--from-literal=endpoint="http://${BUCKET_HOST}:${BUCKET_PORT}" ~~~ **For https port 443:** ~~~ oc create-n openshift-logging secret generic lokistack-dev-odf \--from-literal=access_key_id="${ACCESS_KEY_ID}" \--from-literal=access_key_secret="${SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}" \--from-literal=bucketnames="${BUCKET_NAME}" \--from-literal=endpoint="https://${BUCKET_HOST}:${BUCKET_PORT}" ~~~ Where lokistack-dev-odf is the secret name, the values for ACCESS_KEY_ID, SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, BUCKET_NAME, BUCKET_HOST and BUCKET_PORT are taken from your ObjectBucketClaim's accompanying secret and ConfigMap. 8. Create a LokiStack instance (Select your size based on available resources) **Sizes from smallest to largest:** `1x.pico`, `1x.extra-small`, `1x.small`, `1x.medium` ~~~ apiVersion: loki.grafana.com/v1 kind: LokiStack metadata: name: lokistack namespace: openshift-logging spec: limits: global: retention: days: 7 # <------ number of days to keep logs size: 1x.pico storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd storage: schemas:- effectiveDate: "2024-04-02" version: v13 secret: name: lokistack-dev-odf type: s3 tls: caName: openshift-service-ca.crt caKey: service-ca.crt tenants: mode: openshift-logging ~~~ **NOTE:** The storageClassName here needs to be a class that can create PVC's for the pods, not the S3 storage for LokiStack. The caName refers to the openshift-service-ca.crt ConfigMap in openshift-logging Namespace as ODF uses OCP Service CA. The PVC's listed below were created using the storageClassName provided. ~~~ storage-lokistack-compactor-0 Bound pvc-6c72a3d4-8a40-4749-96ad-bd2cc28046c6 10 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd storage-lokistack-index-gateway-0 Bound pvc-9b478000-6c6a-4579-9e2d-8841d3d911d0 50 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd storage-lokistack-index-gateway-1 Bound pvc-6d824ff3-7dfb-43b1-b04a-97827a0fac55 50 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd storage-lokistack-ingester-0 Bound pvc-fba4624b-22f0-4d1e-afc1-713c7058327f 10 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd storage-lokistack-ingester-1 Bound pvc-0d076883-b5b2-4ac7-9b5e-76e6b84a0a2e 10 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd storage-lokistack-ingester-2 Bound pvc-89d673a4-6929-46fe-8c73-656271672636 10Gi- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd wal-lokistack-ingester-0 Bound pvc-803d0ddc-4294-4cea-a100-c1ad0f3e17e2 150 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd wal-lokistack-ingester-1 Bound pvc-78d87c25-5362-469b-abd7-d8cfa4715dd9 150 GiB- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd wal-lokistack-ingester-2 Bound pvc-47a06190-0a25-40ce-991f-fffb37fd1156 150Gi- ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ~~~ 9. Validate pods are running: ~~~ $ oc get po NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cluster-logging-operator-75d6949fcf-gm5ln 1/1 Running 0 4m30s lokistack-compactor-0 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-distributor-6bf78f9d6f-7dgjv 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-distributor-6bf78f9d6f-v6vlw 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-gateway-64bc9779-mgt5z 2/2 Running 0 172m lokistack-gateway-64bc9779-w5vzg 2/2 Running 0 172m lokistack-index-gateway-0 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-index-gateway-1 1/1 Running 0 171m lokistack-ingester-0 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-ingester-1 1/1 Running 0 171m lokistack-ingester-2 1/1 Running 0 169m lokistack-querier-587f8d564b-t7sf8 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-querier-587f8d564b-tghb9 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-query-frontend-774bbf984-97ldl 1/1 Running 0 172m lokistack-query-frontend-774bbf984-z7d6h 1/1 Running 0 172m ~~~ 10. Create serviceaccount, and assign the necessary permissions to the service account for the collector to be able to collect and forward logs: a. Create serviceaccount: ~~~ $ oc create sa logging-collector-n openshift-logging ~~~ b. Copy/Paste contents into the command line terminal interface: ~~~ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user logging-collector-logs-writer-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user collect-application-logs-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user collect-infrastructure-logs-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user collect-audit-logs-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging ~~~ 11. Create a `ClusterLogForwarder` CR: ~~~ apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogForwarder metadata: name: instance namespace: openshift-logging spec: serviceAccount: name: logging-collector outputs:- name: lokistack-out type: lokiStack lokiStack: target: name: lokistack namespace: openshift-logging authentication: token: from: serviceAccount tls: ca: key: service-ca.crt configMapName: openshift-service-ca.crt pipelines:- name: infra-app-logs inputRefs:- infrastructure #- application <-------- Uncomment if wanted #- audit <-------------- Uncomment if wanted outputRefs:- lokistack-out ~~~ 12. Validate that additional pods are now in place: ~~~ instance-56pls 1/1 Running 0 2m22s instance-6kprg 1/1 Running 0 2m21s instance-g4xcg 1/1 Running 0 2m22s instance-pflnp 1/1 Running 0 2m22s instance-rvfnn 1/1 Running 0 2m22s instance-zttnj 1/1 Running 0 2m21s ~~~ 13. For Logging Observability, perform the following: a. Install the Cluster Observability Operator, be sure to check the box to enable cluster monitoring before installing. b. Once the operator has successfully installed, create the UIPlugin: ~~~ apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: UIPlugin metadata: name: logging spec: type: Logging logging: lokiStack: name: lokistack # <---- name should match lokistack name ~~~

title: EAP 8 Runtime vs Builder image  container images tools in OpenShift
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How does EAP 8 images builder vs runtime compare- Is there any major difference on the EAP 8 images?
resolution: Regarding the fundamental difference between runtime and builder images, see the solution [What is the difference between Builder and Runtime images in Red Hat Container Catalog?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6971476). However, in terms of base image: EAP 8 runtime is built against the minimal ubi 8 image so it won't have some tools, such as tar, which is used to copy files from the container. Example: ~~~ sh-4.4$ ps sh: ps: command not found sh-4.4$ aux sh: aux: command not found sh-4.4$ top sh: top: command not found sh-4.4$ grep Usage: grep [OPTION]... PATTERN [FILE]... Try 'grep--help' for more information. ~~~ That's given: ~~~ ## START target image jboss-eap-8/eap8-openjdk17-runtime-openshift-rhel8:1.0.1.GA ## \ FROM registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal <----------- ~~~ EAP 7 was based on just ubi images, on EAP 8 runtime got reduced size, in relation to difference of images:- EAP 7 runtime image doesn't have- starting the EAP 7 runtime image will result in- EAP 7 builder image does have the full server
root_cause: EAP 8 runtime comes with ubi-minimal. Not ubi (main) base image, this has implications on the tools one can use it. The EAP 8 builder image does not contain a server, whereas the EAP 7 builder image contains a server. The runtime image doesn't contain an EAP 7 server. See the solution [Empty /opt/eap (/opt/server) directory in EAP 8 runtime image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7003492) for more details on EAP builder image vs runtime image. EAP 8.1 Images will bring a few of those tools, such as tar.

title: In OCP, high CPU usage observed in the CPU cores for sending and receiving packets
issue: A dedicated core is used to send and receive network packets where the rest of the cores are responsible for consuming the data. High CPU usage observed in the CPU cores for sending and receiving packets, more than 90%. This has become the main bottleneck for the application as the cores which consume the data are quite idle.
Pod in OCP environment is consuming higher CPU utilisation due to IO performance of Worker/Socket threads.
Perf data shows high cpu usage in **ep_poll, napi_busy_loop or mlx5e_napi_poll*
system calls.
resolution: * To reduce the CPU usage, try to disable the net.core.busy_poll and net.core.busy_read. The following is an example to disable the busy poll mechanism through tuned CR. ``` apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: extra-sysctl namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Configuration changes profile inherited from performance created tuned include=openshift-node-performance-worker-performance-profile [sysctl] net.core.busy_poll = 0 net.core.busy_read = 0 name: openshift-extra-sysctl recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: "worker" priority: 19 profile: openshift-extra-sysctl ```
root_cause: * `performanceProfile` will automatically involve network-latency tuned profiles where the busy poll will be enabled. By enabling the busy poll the latency could be reduced but more CPU and memory resources will be used. If the application is not too sensitive to the latency but the high CPU has become the bottleneck, the busy poll needs to be considered to be disabled in this scenario. * For what is busy poll and its mechanism, please refer to this [KCS article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6481941 "")

title: Unable to create inference service using RedHat Openshift AI
issue: - Unable to create inference service using Openshift AI- failed to find kserve-container in ServingRuntime containers- java.io.IOException: Unable to create directory /home/model-server/tmp/models
resolution: - The `Serving models` chapter indicates models should be placed in storage as pre-packaged artifacts (for example,.mar archives), or declared through file manifests. The TorchServe runtime usage examples always reference.mar, never raw.pth data- Red Hat’s RHOAI 2.x docs with TorchServe and their runtime configurations (e.g., supportedModelFormats: pytorch) implicitly require it.- The only explicit.mar examples are found in TorchServe’s own [documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/serve/use_cases.html "pytorch")- To use PyTorch models via TorchServe in RHOAI, it needs TorchServe’s.mar packaging.- sample InferenceService YAML ``` apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1" kind: "InferenceService" metadata: name: "torchserve" namespace: xxx-poc spec: predictor: serviceAccountName: s3-service-account model: modelFormat: name: pytorch-mar version: "0" name: "" runtime: xxx-yyy-pytorch-server storageUri: s3://xxx-s3storage-bucket/xxx_data/test1 resources: {} env:- name: TS_CONFIG_FILE value: /mnt/models/config.properties containers:- name: kserve-container volumeMounts:- name: model-tmp-dir mountPath: /home/model-server/tmp subPath: tmp volumes:- name: model-tmp-dir emptyDir: {} ```- containers.name: kserve-container: This must match the container name expected by the KServe controller.- volumeMounts: Mounts a writable emptyDir to /home/model-server/tmp, where TorchServe tries to unzip.mar files.- volumes: Defines the emptyDir volume used for temporary storage.- Correct permissions on /home/model-server/tmp- Runs as a user that can write to it (e.g., USER 1001)

title: How to upgrade Red Hat Quay Registry

title: Optimising Pod Scheduling and Performance in OpenShift with Resource Requests and Limits
issue: Pods without properly defined resource requests and limits can cause intermittent application issues and node instability by:- Overcommitment of cluster resources.- Critical application workloads being starved by less important Pods.- Pods being killed (OOM) or throttled, resulting in performance issues.
resolution: ### Understanding OpenShift CPU and Memory Requests and Limits When running applications on OpenShift, it’s critical to control how your Pods use cluster resources. CPU and memory are the primary resources to manage. Properly setting resource `requests` and `limits` helps you:- Ensure critical workloads always get the resources they need.- Prevent noisy neighbours from consuming all available resources.- Control scheduling and avoid unexpected performance issues. ### What Are Requests and Limits? #### Requests A `request` is the minimum amount of a resource (CPU or memory) that OpenShift guarantees for a container.- The OpenShift scheduler uses requests to decide where to place Pods.- If a Node doesn’t have enough free resources to satisfy the requests of all containers in the Pod, the Pod won’t be scheduled and will stay in Pending. Example: ``` resources: requests: cpu: 200m memory: 256Mi ``` This means the Pod will only be scheduled on a Node with at least 200 millicores of CPU and 256Mi of memory available. #### Limits A `limit` is the maximum amount of CPU or memory that a container is allowed to use.- If a container tries to use more memory than its limit, it is killed with an OOM (Out of Memory) error.- If it tries to use more CPU, it’s throttled. Example: ``` resources: limits: cpu: 500m memory: 512Mi ``` #### CPU Particularities- CPU is compressible: If a Pod exceeds its CPU request, it can use more CPU up to its limit, but may be throttled if it goes above the limit.- Measured in cores: 1 core = 1000 millicores (m). You can request fractions (e.g., 500m = 0.5 core).- Minimum: 1m (millicore).- Multi-core nodes: Nodes can have more than one core; requesting more than 1 core is allowed. #### Memory Particularities- Memory is non-compressible: If a Pod exceeds its memory limit, it will be killed (OOM).- Measured in bytes: Use units like Gi, Mi, Ti for binary (e.g., 500Mi, 4Gi).- Warning: Do not use lowercase `m` for memory (represents millibytes, which is extremely small).- Common units: E, P, T, G, M, k (Exabyte, Petabyte, Terabyte, Gigabyte, Megabyte, kilobyte); binary units: Ei, Pi, Ti, Gi, Mi, Ki. ### How Requests and Limits Impact Your Pods #### Scheduling- The scheduler looks at `requests` only. It never uses `limits`- If the total pod request is more than the available resource on the node, the pod will not be scheuled on the node.- If no nodes can forfill the resource request then the pod remains in a pending state. Ensureing nodes are not over utilised.- If the no requests are set or set too low the pod will be scheduled, but pods will be throttled or OOMKilled depending on the overutilised resource type. #### Runtime behaviour- **CPU** is compressible. If you exceed your `request`, your container will continue to run but may be throttled above the `limit`.- **Memory** is not compressible. If you exceed the memory `limit`, your container is killed with an OOM error.--- ### Summary- Add more nodes, to provide more available resources to the cluster.- Revise your current workloads to free some resources on the cluster.- Use `requests` to ensure critical workloads always have guaranteed resources.- Be cautious with `limits`, they prevent overuse but can lead to throttling (CPU) or OOM kills (memory).- For predictable performance, set `requests` equal to limits (this gives your Pod the **Guaranteed QoS class**).- Monitor usage and adjust based on actual needs.---

title: Unexpected rolling over indices in RHOCP 4
issue: New empty indices (audit, app, infra) are created without fulfilling the [index management cronjob roll-over conditions](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/logging/config/cluster-logging-log-store.html#cluster-logging-elasticsearch-retention_cluster-logging-store). ~~~ $ oc exec-n openshift-logging-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- es_util--query=_cat/indices?v health status index uuid pri rep docs.count docs.deleted store.size pri.store.size green open app-000001 5oA5aoOzQuuTZod6AyP6cw 1 0 119 0 216.3kb 216.3kb green open.security PP8U8rGTTV-H4IJUsltsmg 1 0 6 0 33.2kb 33.2kb green open infra-000001 mdiyyrYCQUmCuUWF4f_MCA 1 0 0 0 261b 261b green open.kibana_1 m1LJ3pWFQxeW56bhdCCzGQ 1 0 0 0 261b 261b green open app-000002 r1qc1skYSPGlP-noNiPjqA 1 0 0 0 261b 261b--> new empty index green open audit-000002 EbUGAFv5TMKqRhu2GY8C-Q 1 0 0 0 261b 261b--> new empty index green open infra-000002 JBvjHyTkSse0C9alXEsmgA 1 0 0 0 261b 261b--> new empty index green open audit-000001 TENxomASTPWZT3-UCbhsTg 1 0 0 0 261b 261b ~~~
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [LOG-4452](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4452) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.8.1 through errata [RHSA-2023:7720](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:7720). If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: The issue happens after changing the way that the maximum age of the indices is calculated for rollover after introducing `rollover.MaxAge` parameter in indexManagement policies. `RetentionParameter` is the age at which indices should be deleted and `rollover.maxAge` corresponds to the age at which indices will rollover. Since ClusterLogging Custom Resource instance does not define an age for rollover, it calculates it as a percentage of the deletion age. Cluster Logging Operator API only let's define the `retentionParameter`, then it calculates the rollover age as a percentage of the deletion age (5% to be exact 0.05*$RetentionParameter).

title: Collector pods have no requests and limits in OCP 4
issue: Collector pods consume excessive memory causing scheduling failures of critical components.
Collector pods have no limits and requests defined, even when they are not defined.
resolution: Edit ClusterLogging custom resource (CR) instance in `openshift-logging` project deleting `resources: {}` in order to obtain default requests and limits values. If RHOL Operator is configured as `Managed` state, collector pods should be restarted automatically applying the new configuration: ~~~ $ oc patch ClusterLogging instance--type json-p '[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/collection/logs/fluentd/resources"}]' ~~~ Check default resources have been configured in fluentd pods: ~~~ $ oc get pod-o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="fluentd")].resources}' {"limits":{"memory":"736Mi"},"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"736Mi"}} ~~~
root_cause: When the parameter `/spec/collection/logs/fluentd/resources` is defined like `resources: {}` in the ClusterLogging custom resource (CR) instance, then, the RHOL Operator interprets that the user is defining the `requests` and `limits` values, consequently, it doesn´t set the default.

title: Collector pods keep restarting after install or upgrade in RHOCP 4
issue: Doing a fresh install or after upgrading RHOL to 5.5 version, the collector pods keep restarting.
resolution: [Bug LOG-3049](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-3049) was opened for addressing the issue in RHOL 5.5 and the fix was released in ERRATA [RHSA-2022:7434](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2022:7434) available in RHOL 5.5.4.
root_cause: In RHOL 5.5, when updating the status of the ClusterLogging instance a global variable for the update call is re-used which causes the server-side version to get written back into that variable. This causes the global variable to not have a valid collector configuration and thus the ClusterLogging Operator removes the collector.

title: JSON logs are not parsed for the default Elasticsearch in RHOCP 4
issue: Application logs with a JSON structure are not parsed.
After adding `parse: json` field in the ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance, the JSON logs are not parsed.
resolution: Define `structuredTypeKey` parameter inside `outputDefaults` field in the CLF instance. The structure should be similar to the line below: ~~~ spec outputDefaults: elasticsearch: structuredTypeKey: pipelines:- inputRefs:- application outputRefs: default parse: json ~~~ Documentation Bug [RHDEVDOCS-4790](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHDEVDOCS-4790) to update the documentation.
root_cause: Even if the `parse: json` field is added, the `structuredTypeKey` parameter is required in the CLF instance.

title: How to temporarily disable the Collector component in RHACS
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Kernel crash by Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes Collector EPBF
resolution: 1. Find your RHACS SecuredCluster name ~~~ # oc get securedcluster NAME AGE stackrox-secured-cluster-services 49m ~~~ 2. Modify the `collection` field in the RHACS Securedcluster resource from `CORE_BPF` to `NoCollection` ~~~ # oc edit securedcluster stackrox-secured-cluster-services apiVersion: platform.stackrox.io/v1alpha1 kind: SecuredCluster... spec: admissionControl:..... perNode: collector: collection: NoCollection 《====== here forceCollection: false imageFlavor: Regular taintToleration: TolerateTaints ~~~ + Please note that if CORE_BPF is disabled, all related features `network activity` and `process executions` will be unavailable, e.g. you will no longer be able to view application flows in the RHACS console. + **You will lose the network graph, running processes and process listening on ports.** + **Any policies that rely on processes running or port being listened on or network activity will also not work, but all other policies are fine.** + **Scanning of images, deployments, compliance, vulnerabilities are all handled by other processes will not be affected.** + **We strongly recommend upgrading to OCP and RHACS to latest version and re-enabling CORE_BPF as soon as possible.**
root_cause: Due to a kernel panic caused by RHACS, and as referenced in the following Knowledge Base articles:- [The kernel crashes due to a false MCE triggered due to an exception trapped in copy_from_kernel_nofault() where pagefault_disable() is in effect](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7107976)- [Kernel panics at copy_from_kernel_nofault() due to page fault.](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7081287) Temporarily disabled the RHACS Collector component to avoid further kernel crashes on affected nodes.

issue: After creating a ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance to send the logs to Kafka, the message below appears in the collector logs: ~~~ emit transaction failed: error_class=ArgumentError error="comparison of Fluent::Plugin::Buffer::Metadata with Fluent::Plugin::Buffer::Metadata failed" ~~~

title: Vector supports Elasticsearch in RHOCP 4
issue: Does Vector support internal Elasticsearch?
Is only Elasticsearch as a third party supported by Vector?
resolution: Vector can be used if logs are sent to internal Elasticsearch or external Elasticsearch, therefore Vector solution supports both configurations (default and third-party Elasticsearch). The documentation issue is currently being tracked by the Red Hat team under the Bug [RHDEVDOCS-4855](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHDEVDOCS-4855). **Workaround** Add vector as a collection type to the ClusterLogging custom resource (CR): ~~~ apiVersion: "logging.openshift.io/v1" kind: "ClusterLogging" metadata: name: "instance" namespace: "openshift-logging" annotations: logging.openshift.io/preview-vector-collector: enabled spec: collection: logs: type: "vector" vector: {} ~~~ Define the default output in the ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance to send the logs to the internal Elasticsearch: ~~~ apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogForwarder metadata: name: instance namespace: openshift-logging spec: pipelines:- inputRefs:- application- infrastructure outputRefs:- default ~~~
root_cause: The [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/logging/cluster-logging-release-notes.html#cluster-logging-about-vector) says that Vector supports an external Elasticsearch but there is no reference to the internal Elasticsearch (default).

title: Configuring ulimit for applications running on Openshift Pods
issue: - How to configure `ulimit` for the application running on Openshift Pods?
resolution: - `Ulimit` configuration only applies to the `pam_limits` module. The pam_limits(`pam_limits.so`) PAM module sets limits on the system resources that can be obtained in a user-session.- `Ulimit` configuration in the `/etc/security/limits.conf` file and `*.conf` files in the `/etc/security/limits.d` directory only apply to the `user's login shell` and the applications that are launched by the user from the `login shell`.- Resource allocation to `Openshift` containers/pods are generally managed by the `Cgroups` through `systemd`, `cri-o` and `kubelet`.- Consult the product documentation regarding [Limiting resource allocation to Pods](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/nodes/clusters/nodes-cluster-resource-configure.html).- Consult the solution article regarding [Setting default ulimits on CRI-O Using machine config](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6243491)- Consult the solution article regarding [How to change the value of pids_limit in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5366631)- Consult the solution article regarding [Changing the maximum number of process IDs per pod for ROSA](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7033551)

title: JSON logs are not parsed for the external Elasticsearch in RHOCP 4
issue: Application logs with a JSON structure are not sent.
After adding `parse: json` field in the ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance, the JSON logs are not sent.

After creating a `ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance` with the external Elasticsearch output and JSON enabled, the message below appears in the instance: ~~~ $ oc get clf instance-o yaml [...] status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: "2023-04-03T08:41:15Z" message: 'validation failed: structuredTypeKey or structuredTypeName must be defined for Elasticsearch output named "elasticsearch-test" when JSON parsing is enabled on pipeline "my-app" that references it' reason: Invalid status: "False" type: Ready [...] ~~~
resolution: Define `structuredTypeKey` or `structuredTypeName` parameter inside the outputs field in the CLF instance. The structure should be similar to the lines below: ~~~ [...] spec: outputs:- name: elasticsearch-test type: "elasticsearch" url: http://example.com:9200 elasticsearch: structuredTypeKey: structuredTypeName: [...] ~~~
root_cause: Bug [RHDEVDOCS-4549](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHDEVDOCS-4549) for documentation was created to update how to configure the external Elasticsearch when `parse: json` parameter is added.

title: How to configure custom routes for OpenStack services
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - I'd like to configure the custom server certificate and intermediate CA certificate for openstack servces. How do I do that?
resolution: - In RHOSO18, the public endpoint is served by Route in OpenShift. Some services has an interface to customize their using route resource. For example, nova-vncproxy endpoint route configuration can be customized with the following configuration. ~~~ cellOverride: cell1: noVNCProxy: route: spec: host: tls: caCertificate: |------BEGIN CERTIFICATE----------END CERTIFICATE----------BEGIN CERTIFICATE----------END CERTIFICATE----- certificate: |------BEGIN CERTIFICATE----------END CERTIFICATE----- key: |------BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----------END PRIVATE KEY----- ~~~ In Route, certificate field only accepts a single server certificate. If you want to assign intermediate CA certificate, you need to add it into caCertificate field in order of intermediate CA certificate then CA certificate.

title: TLS configuration issue for multiple Kafka brokers in RHOCP 4
issue: After creating a ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance to send the logs to multiple Kafka brokers using TLS, the message below appears in the collector logs: ~~~ rdkafka::client: librdkafka: Global error: BrokerTransportFailure (Local: Broker transport failure): kafkacluster1:9092/bootstrap: Disconnected while requesting ApiVersion: might be caused by incorrect security.protocol configuration (connecting to a SSL listener?) or broker version is < 0.10 (see api.version.request) (after 2ms in state APIVERSION_QUERY, 1 identical error(s) suppressed) ~~~
TLS configuration is not fully added for Vector pods when using multiple Kafka brokers.
resolution: Bug report [LOG-4009](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4009) and delivered a fix in RHOL 5.7.2 through errata [RHSA-2023:3495](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3495). RHOL Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 5.8 | [LOG-4009](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4009) | 5.8.0 | [RHBA-2023:6139](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:6139) 5.7 | [LOG-4163](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4163) | 5.7.2 | [RHSA-2023:3495](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:3495) If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: Can audit logs be stored in the default Loki in RHOCP 4?
issue: Send audit logs to the default Loki.
Default Loki stores audit logs.
resolution: By default, audit logs are not stored in the internal Logging stack. Using Loki as the internal logging store will allow enabling this option in the Cluster Log Forwarder (CLF) instance. The documentation issue is currently being tracked by the Red Hat team under the Bug [OBSDOCS-280](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDOCS-280). **Procedure** Add Loki as the log store to the ClusterLogging custom resource (CR): ~~~ apiVersion: "logging.openshift.io/v1" kind: "ClusterLogging" metadata: name: "instance" namespace: "openshift-logging" spec: [...] logStore: type: lokistack lokistack: name: logging-loki [...] ~~~ Define the default output in the ClusterLogForwarder (CLF) instance and audit as an input to send also the audit logs to the default Loki: ~~~ apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogForwarder metadata: name: instance namespace: openshift-logging spec: pipelines:- inputRefs:- application- infrastructure- audit outputRefs:- default ~~~
root_cause: The [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/logging/config/cluster-logging-log-store.html#cluster-logging-elasticsearch-audit_cluster-logging-store) says that audit logs could be stored in the internal Elasticsearch but there is no reference to the internal Loki(default).

root_cause: A potential conflict might arise between output names and inputRefs names in the ClusterLogForwarder if they have the same name. With this update, a prefix `OUTPUT_` will be added to labels conflicting with pipeline names. This adjustment ensures the uniqueness and distinction of output labels from pipeline names.

title: Why mon pods fail to start due to unable to mount PVC in OCS 4.x ?
issue: - When snapshots was taken for OCS VMs on vmware environment, during OCS upgrade mon pods fails to start.- ceph-mon pod reporting `AttachVolume.Attach` failure for PVC ~~~ Warning FailedMount 8m33s (x20 over 4h22m) kubelet, rhocs4.redhat.com Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[ceph-daemon-data], unattached volumes=[rook-ceph-log rook-ceph-crash ceph-daemon-data default-token-lxfxr rook-config-override rook-ceph-mons-keyring]: timed out waiting for the condition Warning FailedMount 3m37s (x24 over 4h6m) kubelet, rhocs4.redhat.com Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[ceph-daemon-data], unattached volumes=[ceph-daemon-data default-token-lxfxr rook-config-override rook-ceph-mons-keyring rook-ceph-log rook-ceph-crash]: timed out waiting for the condition Warning FailedAttachVolume 69s (x68 over 152m) attachdetach-controller AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-111111111-2222-3333-4444-555555666666": Failed to add disk 'scsi1:2'. ~~~
resolution: - Remove snapshots associated with OCS VMs from vmware environment and restart VMs.- If there is no snapshot, check the datastore health. If the datastore is not healthy and have problem, this issue can arise. So fix the datastore issue if there is any.

title: On NooBaa account creation the NooBaa Operator is crashing
issue: Creating a NooBaaAccount will lead to the `noobaa-operator-*` pod in the `openshift-storage` namespace to go into `CrashLoopBackOff` state
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [DFBUGS-90](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/DFBUGS-90) and delivered a fix in OpenShift Data Foundation 4.18 through errata [RHSA-2025:2652](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:2652). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. For prior versions of OpenShift Data Foundation 4.18, the following workaround exists: * Set the field `force_md5_etag` to `false` in the NooBaaAccount CR: ~~~ apiVersion: noobaa.io/v1alpha1 kind: NooBaaAccount metadata: name: namespace: openshift-storage spec: allow_bucket_creation: true default_resource: force_md5_etag: false // set this flag in the spec of account ~~~
root_cause: The NooBaa Operator prior to OpenShift Data Foundation version 4.18 requires that the field `force_md5_etag` is set, the NooBaaAccount CRD however defines it as optional. This makes it possible to create NooBaaAccount CRs without the field the Operator expects to exist.

title: Updates started from the RHACM hub fail while updates started directly on the cluster pass
issue: - Updates started from the RHACM hub fail while updates started directly on the cluster pass- Updates started from the RHACM hub fail with a post-hook error
resolution: To be able to apply this update from the hub you need to annotate the cluster with ~~~ annotations: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/upgrade-allow-not-recommended-versions: 'true' ~~~ This is required for the `ClusterCurrator` to be able to update a spoke cluster when the targeted version is not listed in the `availableUpdates`.
root_cause: If a version is only in the `conditionalUpdates` it will not be considered for checks by the `ClusterCurrator`. The version needs to be listed under `availableUpdates` to be able to update from the hub without the annotation.

title: What are the options to use a custom runtime JBoss EAP 7 configurations in OCP
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: How to customize a standalone-openshift.xml How to add the UFC protocol on the jgroups stack on EAP image?
resolution: Options to customize **standalone-openshift.xml** (and its behavior): Option | Pro | Con | Runtime--------- |--------- |--------- |--------- Change JVM property via DC's via `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` | easy to set | can only change JVM properties | Can be done in runtime (restart of the pod will be done) changes via config map: actions.cli and postconfigure.sh | very simple: just need the cli command | Red Hat is maintaining the standalone-configuration and the user has to updates/adds only what they want to add to the default configuration | Can be done in runtime overwrite standalone-openshift in /standalone/config | one and done (apply on the custom image) | In that case, the default standalone-openshift.xml is not used and it is up to the user to keep its custom configuration in sync with default configuration (in addition to their own changes) | no, another image must be provisioned S2I build were EAP_HOME/standalone/configuration- create a file standalone-openshift.xml | One and done (apply on the custom image) | Need to do a [S2I process and deployment](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.4/html/getting_started_with_jboss_eap_for_openshift_container_platform/configuring_eap_openshift_image#eap_s2i_process) | no, another image must be provisioned Using LOGGER_CATEGORIES- described on [EAP 7 logging mechanism and customization in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6988040)| Can be used at runtime, no need for postconfig.sh/actions.cli | Need to be set at deployment (dc or deployment) level | Can be used at runtime:yes, e.g. oc set env dc/eap-app LOGGER_CATEGORIES=org.jgroups.protocols.DNS_PING:TRACE- **requires pod restart** ## **Example 1: Adding a property via JAVA_OPTS_APPEND** For example, adding a certain JVM property that can be done via `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND`: ~~~ ### set the environment variable JAVA_OPTS_APPEND $ oc set env dc/eap-app JAVA_OPTS_APPEND=-Dflag=example ### get the environment variable: $ oc get dc/eap-app-o yaml | grep-A2 JAVA_OPTS_APPEND- name: JAVA_OPTS_APPEND value:-Dflag=example ~~~ ## **Example 2: Adding UFC protocol on the default EAP image** ### Via config-map (actions.cli + postconfigure.sh): $ cat actions.cli ~~~ embed-server--std-out=echo--admin-only--server-config=standalone-openshift.xml /subsystem=jgroups/stack=tcp/protocol=UFC:add(add-index=10) stop-embedded-server ~~~ $ cat postconfigure.sh ~~~ $JBOSS_HOME/bin/jboss-cli.sh--file=$JBOSS_HOME/extensions/actions.cli ~~~ Do the following to create the config-map: ~~~ oc create configmap jboss-cli--from-file=postconfigure.sh=postconfigure.sh--from-file=actions.cli=actions.cli oc set volume dc/eap-app--add--name=jboss-cli-m /opt/eap/extensions-t configmap--configmap-name=jboss-cli--default-mode='0777'--overwrite ~~~ There are two commands above: The first creates the configmap called jboss-cli; And the second one just sets the volume in the deployment. The second command does not complain about a cm that is **not there.** Given the files: `actions.cli` and `postconfigure.sh` above, this can be set in a Dockerfile and an image provisioned from it, this is described on [Running JBoss CLI commands on extended JBoss EAP 7 OpenShift Image](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3911211).
root_cause: This article describes runtime alternatives, for build time see the solution [What are the options to execute CLI commands at build time in JBoss EAP 7 in OCP images](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7096710) that provides alternatives for executing CLI commands at build time, such as replace the default `standalone-openshift.xml` file inside `/opt/eap/standalone/configuration` also can be used to declare environment variables via docker set `ENV EXAMPLE=/opt/eap/`. **Note:** as described on the solution [Customizing standalone-openshift.xml](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3250791), currently EAP images are not supported on podman/docker.

title: Investigating 'write-only' or 'modify-only' RBAC permissions for resources on OpenShift Container Platform
issue: How can an administrator grant a user permissions to modify a resource (e.g., scale a MachineSet) without also granting them full read (get) access to the entire manifest, which may contain sensitive data?
resolution: For standard use of oc commands, it is not possible to separate modification (patch) permissions from read (get) permissions. As a result, to allow modification of a resource, it is also necessary to grant get permission, which allows read access to its contents. A technical workaround using oc apply--server-side exists, but it is not recommended due to operational risks (see Root Cause for details).
root_cause: Standard oc commands like oc patch and oc scale are designed with a read-modify-write pattern. They must first get the resource from the API server to read its current state before applying a modification. This implicit requirement for the get verb is why a role with only patch permission fails. **Verification** This conclusion was based on the following tests. 1. Setup An RBAC Role was created and assigned to a user, granting only list and patch permissions to test modification-only access. ~~~ rules:- verbs:- list- patch apiGroups:- machine.openshift.io resources:- machinesets ~~~ 2. Test oc patch Command (fail) An attempt to modify the resource using oc patch failed, confirming its dependency on the get verb. ~~~ $ oc patch machineset--patch '{"spec":{"replicas":2}}'-n openshift-machine-api Error from server (Forbidden): machinesets.machine.openshift.io " " is forbidden: User "user1" cannot get resource "machinesets" in API group "machine.openshift.io"... ~~~ 3. Test oc apply--server-side Command (success) A workaround using oc apply with a partial manifest and forceful server-side options successfully modified the resource.- patch.yaml content: ~~~ apiVersion: machine.openshift.io/v1beta1 kind: MachineSet metadata: name: namespace: openshift-machine-api spec: replicas: 2 ~~~- Command: ~~~ $ oc apply-f patch.yaml--server-side--force-conflicts machineset.machine.openshift.io/ serverside-applied ~~~ This method is a forceful change, so extreme caution is required for the configuration. Please test it thoroughly before applying it in a production environment.

" err="found duplicate series for the match group {device="sdX"} on the left hand-side of the operation: [{__name__="ceph_disk_occupation", ceph_daemon="osd.X", container="mgr", device="sdX", device_ids="sdX=XXXXX", devices="sdX", endpoint="http-metrics", job="rook-ceph-mgr", managedBy="ocs", namespace="openshift-storage", pod="rook-ceph-mgr-X-XXXXX", service="rook-ceph-mgr"}, {__name__="ceph_disk_occupation", ceph_daemon="osd.X", container="mgr", device="sdX", device_ids="sdX=XXXXX", devices="sdX", endpoint="http-metrics", job="rook-ceph-mgr", managedBy="ocs", namespace="openshift-storage", pod="rook-ceph-mgr-X-XXXXX", service="rook-ceph-mgr"}];many-to-many matching not allowed: matching labels must be unique on one side" ~~~
The alert `PrometheusRuleFailures` is triggered for the rule_group `/etc/prometheus/rules/prometheus-k8s-rulefiles-0/openshift-storage-prometheus-ceph-v16-rules-XXXXX.yaml`.

Either of the Prometheus rules `prometheus-ceph-v14-rules` or `prometheus-ceph-v16-rules` exist along with `prometheus-ceph-rules`. ~~~ $ oc get prometheusrules-n openshift-storage NAME AGE noobaa-prometheus-rules 1y ocs-prometheus-rules 3y prometheus-ceph-rules 2y prometheus-ceph-v14-rules 3y prometheus-ceph-v16-rules 2y ~~~

title: How to update route configuration manually for zync generated routes in 3scale
issue: - We would like to add the custom metadata annotations to the zync generated route.- It is not possible to persist the changes due to zync overriding them.- How can I achieve this?
resolution: In order to configure manually a route:- Take a note of the Public Base URL and make a backup of the APIcast route in OpenShift for the specific Product.- Go to the admin portal, change in *Integration > Settings > DEPLOYMENT* the deployment type from *APIcast 3scale managed* to *APIcast self-managed*.- Update the Staging and Production public base URL with the desired route if you wish to change the URLs. Then click *Update Product* button at the end of the page and promote the changes.- There are 2 options available:- Create a route manually in OpenShift in the 3scale namespace with the desired Public Base URLs pointing to the Service *apicast-staging | production*. So, even though the *Settings* in the 3scale admin portal are configured with a *self-managed APIcast*, the `apicast-staging` and `apicast-production` gateways deployed within 3scale can still be used.- Deploy a Self-Managed APIcast with the APIcast Operator if for some reason a separate gateway is needed for this use case. Then the route should be created in the self-managed APIcast namespace if it's deployed in another project.
root_cause: When 3scale is deployed, by default `apicast-staging` and `apicast-production` gateways are *3scale managed*. This is configured under *Integration > Settings > DEPLOYMENT*. In this case *zync* generates automatically the routes and are not configurable. Any changes will be reverted by zync.

title: Collect logs from application pods using a custom path
issue: - How to collect logs from custom path?- Is it possible to collect logs from custom path application pods?
resolution: - Using `Red Hat OpenShift Logging`:- It is technically possible to achieve this using Red Hat OpenShift Logging, however, it requires setting the logging component’s management state to Unmanaged, which is unsupported by Red Hat. For more details and customization options, refer to the upstream [Vector documentation](https://vector.dev/docs/reference/configuration/#:~:text=The%20following%20is%20an%20example%20of%20a%20popular%20Vector%20configuration%20that%20ingests%20logs%20from%20a%20file).- Using `Red Hat build of OpenTelemetery`:- This is done by configuring the filelog receiver in OpenTelemetry Collector and exporting via the OTLP exporter.- Refer [Filelog Receiver OTLP](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/red_hat_build_of_opentelemetry/configuring-the-collector#filelog-receiver_otel-collector-receivers).

title: Metrics dashboard shows "No Data Point Found" for application namespace
issue: - Metrics dashboard shows "No Data Point Found" for application namespace- The target reporting down with "help text is not a valid utf8 string".
resolution: This has to be fixed from application side by disabling the problematic metric(s) that include non-UTF-8 encoded help text.
root_cause: - Prometheus expects all metric metadata (including help text) to be valid UTF-8. If even one metric violates this, the entire scrape fails, and no metrics are collected from that target.

title: Improve OpenShift 4 cluster upgrade time when using multiple MachineSets
issue: - All worker nodes are in the same `MachineConfigPool` called `worker` and it is not possible to select how many nodes per `MachineSet` will be rebooted simultaneously during the upgrade when using more than one `MachineSet` for worker nodes.- How to decrease upgrade time on Openshift 4 clusters when using multiple `MachineSet`?
resolution: **NOTE**: To configure one `MachineConfigPool` per `MachineSet`, it is needed to create a `label` on `MachineSet` to be used on `Node`. In this example, the label is `env`. 1. List all cluster `Nodes` and verify that the label is defined on `worker` nodes: ~~~ oc get nodes-L env NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ENV ipi-2ckhw-dev-2jcvv Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-dev-9plfh Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-dev-h422p Ready worker 12h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-dev-ldgjk Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-dev-s698c Ready worker 12h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-dev-whmr2 Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-dev-ws4k6 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d dev ipi-2ckhw-infra-cfsss Ready infra 24h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-infra-mwbzd Ready infra 24h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-infra-sxsx6 Ready infra 24h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-master-0 Ready master 26h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-master-1 Ready master 26h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-master-2 Ready master 26h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-prd-49ht4 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d prd ipi-2ckhw-prd-9fvvz Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d prd ipi-2ckhw-prd-bgrc2 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d prd ipi-2ckhw-prd-gvdct Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d prd ipi-2ckhw-prd-rk8j4 Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d prd ipi-2ckhw-qa-7b95d Ready worker 12h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ipi-2ckhw-qa-cddg5 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ipi-2ckhw-qa-ct2gn Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ipi-2ckhw-qa-lc4wt Ready worker 18h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ipi-2ckhw-qa-n5k9h Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ipi-2ckhw-qa-scwkh Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ipi-2ckhw-qa-xrcdx Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d qa ~~~ 2. Check all `MachineSet` configured on cluster: ~~~ oc get machineset-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE ipi-2ckhw-dev 7 7 7 7 22h ipi-2ckhw-infra 3 3 3 3 24h ipi-2ckhw-prd 5 5 5 5 22h ipi-2ckhw-qa 7 7 7 7 22h ~~~ 3. Check all `MachineConfigPool` before creating new ones: ~~~ oc get machineconfigpool NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE infra rendered-infra-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 3 3 3 0 21h master rendered-master-173032e0ecdef0a4147d80dff86a5af9 True False False 3 3 3 0 23h worker rendered-worker-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 19 19 19 0 18h ~~~ 4. Create an `yaml` file based on `MachineConfigPool` `worker`: ~~~ oc get machineconfigpool worker-o yaml > /tmp/mcp-worker.yaml ~~~ 5. For each `MachineSet`, edit the `/tmp/mcp-worker.yaml` file and change the name and `nodeSelector` values. After this change, apply it: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfigPool metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/mco-built-in: "" pools.operator.machineconfiguration.openshift.io/worker: "" name: worker <------ change the name spec: configuration: name: rendered-worker-d96e77a6f25bb0a3304a412da6d37192 source:- apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig name: 00-worker- apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig name: 01-worker-container-runtime- apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig name: 01-worker-kubelet- apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig name: 99-worker-generated-registries- apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig name: 99-worker-ssh machineConfigSelector: matchLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker nodeSelector: matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: "" <----- change 'node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ""' to label env: paused: false ~~~ **WARNING**: After applying the `/tmp/mcp-worker.yaml` file, all nodes with the label defined on `nodeSelector` will be rebooted. ~~~ oc apply-f /tmp/mcp-worker.yaml machineconfigpool.machineconfiguration.openshift.io/prd ~~~ 7. Wait for several minutes until all nodes are rebooted and list the `MachineConfigPools`: ~~~ oc get machineconfigpool NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED MACHINECOUNT READYMACHINECOUNT UPDATEDMACHINECOUNT DEGRADEDMACHINECOUNT AGE dev rendered-dev-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 7 7 7 0 21h infra rendered-infra-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 3 3 3 0 24h master rendered-master-173032e0ecdef0a4147d80dff86a5af9 True False False 3 3 3 0 26h prd rendered-prd-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 5 5 5 0 22h qa rendered-qa-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 7 7 7 0 21h worker rendered-worker-2701f95ff4a61b9d6442d362669a8436 True False False 0 0 0 0 21h ~~~ 8. Patch the `MachineConfigPool`: During the cluster upgrade process the `Machine Config Operator` will reboot the nodes to apply the Operating System configs. By default, only one node per `MachineConfigPool` is rebooted and to change this default value is necessary to configure the parameter `maxUnavailable` on `MachineConfigPool`. For any `MachineConfigPool` that may reboot more than one node during the cluster upgrade execute the patch to change the `maxUnavailable` to the desired value. In this example `MachineConfigOperator` can reboot two nodes simultaneously for the `MachineConfigOperator` `prd`, three nodes for the `MachineConfigOperator` `qa` and three nodes for the `MachineConfigOperator` `dev`. ~~~ oc patch machineconfigpool prd--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"maxUnavailable": 2}}' ~~~ ~~~ oc patch machineconfigpool qa--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"maxUnavailable": 3}}' ~~~ ~~~ oc patch machineconfigpool dev--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"maxUnavailable": 3}}' ~~~ 9. Start the [Openshift Cluster Upgrade](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4606811): **NOTE**: Wait for several minutes until all `Operators` are upgraded to the new release. Check the nodes when the `Machine Config Operator` starts the reboot of the `worker` node's to verify that the reboot is being executed as following the configuration defined in `maxUnavailable` on `MachineConfigPool` ~~~ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ipi-2ckhw-dev-2jcvv Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-dev-9plfh Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-dev-h422p Ready worker 12h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-dev-ldgjk Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-dev-s698c Ready worker 12h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-dev-whmr2 Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-dev-ws4k6 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-infra-cfsss Ready infra 24h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-infra-mwbzd Ready,SchedulingDisabled infra 24h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-infra-sxsx6 Ready infra 24h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-master-0 Ready master 26h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-master-1 Ready,SchedulingDisabled master 26h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-master-2 Ready master 26h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-prd-49ht4 Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-prd-9fvvz Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-prd-bgrc2 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-prd-gvdct Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-prd-rk8j4 Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-7b95d Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 12h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-cddg5 Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-ct2gn Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-lc4wt Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 18h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-n5k9h Ready worker 22h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-scwkh Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ipi-2ckhw-qa-xrcdx Ready worker 21h v1.19.0+4c3480d ~~~
root_cause: All `worker` machines are in the same `MachineConfigPool` called `worker` and it is not possible to configure how many nodes will be rebooted per `MachineSet ` when upgrading a cluster.

title: oc logs/debug/rsh gives x509: certificate signed by unknown authority error
issue: - Accessing logs/shell of a pod fails with x509: certificate signed by unknown authority- After recovery of master from VM Snapshot
resolution: - Force deployment of `kube-apiserver` pods: ~~~ $ oc patch kubeapiserver/cluster--type merge-p "{\"spec\":{\"forceRedeploymentReason\":\"Forcing new revision with random number $RANDOM to make message unique\"}}" ~~~- Force deployment of `kube-controller` manager: ~~~ $ oc patch kubecontrollermanager cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date--rfc-3339=ns)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~- Force deployment of `kube-scheduler` pod: ~~~ $ oc patch kubescheduler cluster-p='{"spec": {"forceRedeploymentReason": "recovery-'"$(date--rfc-3339=ns)"'"}}'--type=merge ~~~
root_cause: - `kube-controller-manager` Pods are running with some older revision where other masters have `kube-controller-manager` Pods running with a newer revision. This happens due to the recovery of master from the VM Snapshot. The resources were on some revision at the time of snapshot- This older revision had different kubelet CSR signer CA than the current one used in the cluster and eventually kubelet certificates are signed by different CA- Either recover all masters using the snapshot or perform above procedure to have same CA certificates- Above procedure makes this revision same on all master nodes by forcing new deployment on all masters

title: Users session disconnected from VNC when new users connect to the same instance
issue: - While working on a virtual machine using the built-in VNC console in Openshift, end-users are being disconnected from their session when other users establish a VNC connection to the same virtual machine.- While working on a virtual machine using the built-in VNC console in Openshift and using another TAB to view details or configuration of the virtual machine, the session will refresh making it difficult for users to perform activities.
resolution: This issue is being tracked by the engineering teams in:- [CNV-64791- VNC Multi connection](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-64791)- [CNV-60117- Regular VNC console disconnect, due to competing request between the VNC thumbnail, and a full screen VNC view.](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-60117)

title: CustomResourceDefinition "securitypolicies.config.stackrox.io" in namespace "" exists and cannot be imported into the current release
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: When upgrading ACS to 4.8.0 via Helm, I get the following error: Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: Unable to continue with install: CustomResourceDefinition "securitypolicies.config.stackrox.io" in namespace "" exists and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata; annotation validation error: key "meta.helm.sh/release-name" must equal "my-release-name": current value is "stackrox-central-services"; annotation validation error: key "meta.helm.sh/release-namespace" must equal "my-namespace": current value is "stackrox"
resolution: To avoid upgrade failure, Helm users need to apply the following changes to the CRD prior to upgrade: # Change the following values if needed: namespace=stackrox release=stackrox-central-services kubectl annotate crd/securitypolicies.config.stackrox.io meta.helm.sh/release-name=$release kubectl annotate crd/securitypolicies.config.stackrox.io meta.helm.sh/release-namespace=$namespace kubectl label crd/securitypolicies.config.stackrox.io app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm The above values will need to be updated to match your release name (i.e. "stackrox-central-services") or namespace (i.e. "stackrox") in case you had used different ones.
root_cause: The way custom resource definitions (CRDs) are being delivered in the ACS Helm chart is changing in 4.8.0. This requires previously-installed CRDs to be updated to look like they are part of the pre-existing Helm chart installation for Central.

title: Vertical Pod Autoscaler RequestsOnly Admission Webhook Warning in RHOCP4
issue: - While specifying any parameters under `resourcePolicy` on a VPA object, getting the following Admission Webhook Warning. ~~~ VerticalPodAutoscaler amq-broker-controller-manager violates policy 299- "unknown field \"Â resourcePolicy\"", 299- "unknown field \"Â Â Â- containerName\"", 299- "unknown field \"Â Â Â containerPolicies\"", 299- "unknown field \"Â Â Â Â Â controlledResources\"", 299- "unknown field \"Â Â Â Â Â controlledValues\" ~~~- Unable to implement VPA feature.- Parameters under `resourcePolicy` on a VPA object yaml. ~~~ apiVersion: autoscaling.k8s.io/v1 kind: VerticalPodAutoscaler metadata: name: vpa-ami-example namespace: automated-underwriting-dev spec: targetRef: apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment name: ami-example updatePolicy: updateMode: "Off" resourcePolicy: containerPolicies:- containerName: "*" controlledResources: ["cpu", "memory"] controlledValues: "RequestsOnly" ~~~
resolution: - To resolve this issue, You need to sanitize the YAML to remove these characters. Here's how. ~~~ apiVersion: autoscaling.k8s.io/v1 kind: VerticalPodAutoscaler metadata: name: vpa-ami-example namespace: automated-underwriting-dev spec: targetRef: apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment name: ami-example updatePolicy: updateMode: "Off" resourcePolicy: containerPolicies:- containerName: "*" controlledResources: ["cpu", "memory"] controlledValues: RequestsOnly ~~~
root_cause: - The character `Â` is likely a non-breaking space `(Unicode U+00A0)` or a similar special character.- This can happen when YAML content is copied from rich text sources like MS Word, Outlook, or websites, or when it's pasted using tools or terminals that change how spaces are handled.

For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.- #####Workaround:- Create a NetworkPolicy as below. ~~~ kind: NetworkPolicy apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 metadata: annotations: internal.config.kubernetes.io/previousKinds: NetworkPolicy internal.config.kubernetes.io/previousNames: test internal.config.kubernetes.io/previousNamespaces: redhat-ods-applications name: notebook-np namespace: redhat-ods-applications labels: app.kubernetes.io/part-of: networkpolicy app.opendatahub.io/networkpolicy: 'true' spec: podSelector: {} ingress:- ports:- protocol: TCP port: 8443- protocol: TCP port: 8080- protocol: TCP port: 8081- protocol: TCP port: 5432- protocol: TCP port: 8082- protocol: TCP port: 8099- protocol: TCP port: 8181- protocol: TCP port: 9443 policyTypes:- Ingress ~~~

title: RHACS false negative Java scan results
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: False negative Java scan results. Known common cases include Spring and Tomcat JARs.
resolution: **Note that this resolution will configure Scanner V4 Indexer to access data from the public Maven Search API, it will not work in disconnected environments (will be addressed in a future release). This is the only process in Scanner V4 that does_not_ communicate directly with Central (outside of pulling images from registries).** By default, this is the Maven Search API URL: `https://search.maven.org/solrsearch/select`._If using delegated scanning, these changes must be applied to the Scanner V4 Indexer deployment in every Secured Cluster as well as Central Services._ Upgrade to RHACS 4.8 or newer and ensure the Scanner V4 Indexer deployment has the following environment variable set: ``` ROX_SCANNER_V4_MAVEN_SEARCH="true" ``` If scan results have already been indexed with the false negative(s), reindexing will need to be enabled. This should be on by default. To be absolutely sure that is the case, set the following environment variable for the Scanner V4 Indexer deployment: ``` ROX_SCANNER_V4_REINDEX="true" ``` If a proxy or different Maven Search API URL is required, set the following environment variable for the Scanner V4 Indexer container: ``` ROX_SCANNER_V4_MAVEN_SEARCH_URL=" " ```
root_cause: Scanner V4's Java scanner searches for specific metadata in JAR (read: any kind of JVM archive) when it's indexing all the components in a container image. There are instances where the metadata for the components isn't accurate enough to match vulnerability data with the components properly. In particular, OSV defines the name of a Java package as `groupId:artifactId`. If either of these is incorrect or missing, Scanner won’t be able to match the Java package with any relevant vulnerabilities, causing false negatives.

title: Changing standalone-openshift.xml in EAP 7 container in OCP 4's buildconfig
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How to change standalone-openshift.xml in EAP 7 container in OCP 4's buildconfig?- Changing standalone-openshift.xml via OCP 4's buildconfig
resolution: It is possible to inject a standalone-openshift.xml via the BuildConfig, which will be injected in the build process and it result in a EAP pod with the custom standalone configuration. 1. Create a configmap with the custom standalone-openshift.xml ~~~ $ cat standalone-openshift.xml... $ oc create configmap standaloneconfig--from-file=standalone-openshift.xml ~~~ 2. Create a buildconfig with the details: ~~~ spec: failedBuildsHistoryLimit: 5 nodeSelector: null output: to: kind: ImageStreamTag name: eap-standalone:latest postCommit: {} resources: {} runPolicy: Serial source: configMaps:- configMap: name: standaloneconfig dockerfile: |- FROM eap74-openjdk17-openshift-rhel8:7.4.12-10 USER root COPY standalone-openshift.xml /opt/eap/standalone/configuration/standalone-openshift.xml CMD $JBOSS_HOME/bin/openshift-launch.sh type: Dockerfile strategy: dockerStrategy: from: kind: ImageStreamTag name: jboss-eap74-openjdk11-openshift:7.4.0 namespace: openshift type: Docker successfulBuildsHistoryLimit: 5 status: lastVersion: 1 ~~~
root_cause: User can change configurations at [runtime](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6969444) and [build time](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7096710). The standalone-openshift.xml, give its importance, is better to be changed at build time.
