title: How to configure the Prometheus Alert for EphemeralStorageLimitexceeds over 80 % ?
issue: - How to create custom alert when pods are going into evicted state due to [ephemeral storage](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/storage/understanding-ephemeral-storage.html) full?- Configure the alert when pods [ephemeral storage](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/storage/understanding-ephemeral-storage.html) exceeds the limit of 80%.
resolution: **Step 1:** Enable [user workload monitoring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.10/monitoring/enabling-monitoring-for-user-defined-projects.html#enabling-monitoring-for-user-defined-projects_enabling-monitoring-for-user-defined-projects). **Step 2:** Create a YAML file for alerting rules. In this example, it is called Ephemeral-storage-alert-rule.yaml. Add an alerting rule configuration to the YAML file. For example: ~~~ apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: ephemeralstoragealert namespace: < <-----Namespace in which you want to apply the rule spec: groups:- name: EphemeralStorageAlert rules:- alert: EphemeralStorageAlert annotations: description: "EphemeralStorage usage is above 80%\n VALUE = {{$value}}\n LABELS = {{$labels}}" summary: EphemeralStorage usage above 80 percent expr: sum by(pod) (pod:container_fs_usage_bytes:sum{container="",namespace=" ",pod!=""}) > 80 for: 2m labels: severity: warning ~~~ **Step 3:** Apply the configuration file to the cluster. ~~~ $ oc apply-f Ephemeral-storage-alert-rule.yaml prometheusrule.monitoring.coreos.com/ephemeralstoragealert created ~~~

title: Failed to install/update Helm chart \"istiod\": unrecoverable helm release status pending-rollback
issue: - Red Hat Service Mesh Operator pod in CrashLoopBackOff with error: ``` ERROR ctrlr.istiocni Reconciler error {"IstioCNI": "default", "reconcileID": "xxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx", "error": "failed to install/update Helm chart \"cni\": unrecoverable helm release status pending-rollback"} ```
resolution: - List Helm releases in the namespace: ``` $ helm list-n istio-system ``` This displays details such as release name, namespace, revision, status, chart, and app version.- Check the revision history for the `default-istiod` release: ``` $ helm history default-istiod-n istio-system ``` This shows each revision, when it was updated, its status, and a description (e.g., upgrade complete).- Rollback the `default-istiod` release to a specific revision (for example, revision 13): ``` $ helm rollback default-istiod 13-n istio-system ``` This command reverts the release to the specified revision, applying the configuration and resources from that point in history.- Helm stores release information as Kubernetes secrets. To list these secrets in the `istio-system` namespace: ``` $ oc-n istio-system get secret-l owner=helm ``` This will display secrets like `sh.helm.release.v1.default-istiod.v12` and `sh.helm.release.v1.default-istiod.v13`, which represent the state of each release revision.- Remove secrets associated with obsolete or superseded revisions (for example, revision 12): ``` $ oc-n istio-system delete secret sh.helm.release.v1.default-istiod.v12 ``` **Note:** 1. Always verify which revision you want to rollback to using `helm history` before running the rollback. 2. Deleting Helm secrets should be done with caution. Only remove secrets for revisions you are certain are no longer needed.

title: NVIDIA GPU operator daemonSet pod stuck in Init:ContainerCreating state in RHOCP4
issue: - The pods of the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` consistently remain stuck in the `Init:ContainerCreating` phase with multiple `restarts`: ~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE nvidia-driver-daemonset-xxxx 0/2 Init:CrashLoopBackOff 6 15m ~~~
resolution: - The [issue](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/nvidia-kernel-module-refuses-to-unload-no-matter-what/256803) originates from the [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/en-in/) side, where kernel modules fail to unload properly.- However, a workaround from the OpenShift side is to `drain` and `uncordon` the affected node as shown below: ~~~ $ oc adm drain node/ $ oc adm uncordon node/ ~~~ **Note** The link provided is not from official Red Hat documentation, but rather from the NVIDIA vendor's community site.For any further queries, it is recommended to follow up with [NVIDIA support](https://www.nvidia.com/en-in/).
root_cause: `NVIDIA kernel modules failing` to unload or reinitialize properly during driver installation. This prevents the `nvidia-driver-daemonset` pods from completing their init phase, causing them to get stuck in the `Init:ContainerCreating` state with repeated `restarts`.

title: nvidia-driver-daemonset pod fails to install RHEL packages
issue: On Red Hat OpenShift 4.10 or later with the NVIDIA GPU operator, a driver pod (*nvidia-driver-daemonset-...*) is in *CrashLoopBack
state. Logs of the *nvidia-driver-ctr

container inside the pod indicate a failure to install a RHEL package, for any reason. Among common reasons are:- no valid entitlement is installed- an RPM repository is inaccessible- a required RPM package cannot be found The failures are accompanied by warnings about a broken driver toolkit (DTK) image in the logs. Entitled driver builds are not supported on recent versions of OpenShift, and exist only as a fallback for older OpenShift versions. The user must focus on debugging the broken DTK image.
resolution: First, on a node where the driver build is failing, the actual OSTREE_VERSION needs to be found out: ~~~ oc debug node/${NODE}-- chroot /host bash-c "grep OSTREE_VERSION /etc/os-release" ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ export NODE=... $ oc debug node/${NODE}-- chroot /host bash-c "grep OSTREE_VERSION /etc/os-release" Starting pod/...-debug... To use host binaries, run `chroot /host` OSTREE_VERSION='9.6.20250530-0' Removing debug pod... ~~~ Next, the value of *feature.node.kubernetes.io/system-os_release.OSTREE_VERSION* label on the node resource needs to be checked for correctness. It must match the actual OSTREE_VERSION. ~~~ oc get node ${NODE}-o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.feature\.node\.kubernetes\.io/system-os_release\.OSTREE_VERSION}' ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ oc get node ${NODE}-o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.feature\.node\.kubernetes\.io/system-os_release\.OSTREE_VERSION}' 9.6.20250530-0 ~~~ If the values **do not match**, the Node Feature Discovery (NFD) is not working correctly, and the user should proceed to troubleshooting NFD:- Verifying that there is a *nfd-worker* pod running on the node: ~~~ oc get pod-n openshift-nfd-l=app=nfd-worker--field-selector spec.nodeName=${NODE} ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ oc get pod-n openshift-nfd-l=app=nfd-worker--field-selector spec.nodeName=${NODE} NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE nfd-worker-lxvg9 1/1 Running 0 20m ~~~- Checking the status of *NodeFeatureDiscovery* resource: ~~~ oc describe NodeFeatureDiscovery-n openshift-nfd nfd-instance ~~~ or ~~~ oc get NodeFeatureDiscovery-n openshift-nfd nfd-instance-o jsonpath='{.status}' | jq ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ oc get NodeFeatureDiscovery-n openshift-nfd nfd-instance-o jsonpath='{.status}' | jq {"conditions": [{"lastTransitionTime": "2025-07-09T10:56:49Z", "message": "", "reason": "AllInstanceComponentsAreDeployedSuccessfuly", "status": "True", "type": "Available"}, {"lastTransitionTime": "2025-07-09T10:56:49Z", "message": "", "reason": "CanBeUpgraded", "status": "True", "type": "Upgradeable"}, {"lastTransitionTime": "2025-07-09T10:56:49Z", "message": "", "reason": "ConditionNotBeingMetCurrently", "status": "False", "type": "Progressing"}, {"lastTransitionTime": "2025-07-09T10:56:49Z", "message": "", "reason": "ConditionNotBeingMetCurrently", "status": "False", "type": "Degraded"}]} ~~~- [Node Feature Discovery](https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/node-feature-discovery/) documentation and general OpenShift documentation should be referred to for further troubleshooting. If the values of OSTREE_VERSION **match**, the DTK image stream must be made to contain a healthy image with the same tag. ~~~ oc get is/driver-toolkit-n openshift-o jsonpath="{.status.tags[?(@.tag==\"${OSTREE_VERSION}\")]}" | jq ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ OSTREE_VERSION=9.6.20250530-0 $ oc get is/driver-toolkit-n openshift-o jsonpath="{.status.tags[?(@.tag==\"${OSTREE_VERSION}\")]}" | jq {"items": [{"created": "2025-06-17T11:03:22Z", "dockerImageReference": "quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:fe0322730440f1cbe6fffaaa8cac131b56574bec8abe3ec5b462e17557fecb32", "generation": 2, "image": "sha256:fe0322730440f1cbe6fffaaa8cac131b56574bec8abe3ec5b462e17557fecb32"}], "tag": "9.6.20250530-0"} ~~~ In a **disconnected environment**, the image might need to be mirrored manually. The DTK image that corresponds to an OpenShift version can be found by running the following command: ~~~ oc adm release info quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:${OCP_VERSION}-${ARCH}--image-for=driver-toolkit ~~~ Example: ~~~ $ oc adm release info quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.18.16-x86_64--image-for=driver-toolkit quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:7d0234b52e232a849c2081aaa8be60c44a4ac3929b6156b1fcfbbc104f7a5881 ~~~
root_cause: During a new installation, or after a cluster upgrade, NVIDIA GPU drivers must be rebuild on each node with a NVIDIA GPU. The build process uses the OpenShift Driver Toolkit (DTK) to access the required packages (such as kernel headers)- instead of installing them from an RPM repository. The GPU operator looks at the *feature.node.kubernetes.io/system-os_release.OSTREE_VERSION* NFD label to find the right DTK image in the DTK image stream, when constructing a driver pod spec. If the DTK image does not match the OSTree (and kernel) version running on the node, or is not available- the build will fall back to using an entitlement to install the packages, and eventually fail.

title: A single noobaa bucket's account credentials can list all noobaa buckets' name
issue: A single noobaa bucket's account credentials can list all noobaa buckets' name, is it expected behavior?
resolution: * It's expected behavior that a single noobaa bucket's account credentials can list all noobaa buckets' name.
root_cause: * For previous ODF version, like odfv4.14, a single noobaa bucket's account credentials can only list it's own bucket and can't list other noobaa buckets' name, it's a noncompliant behaviour with AWS::S3 inside MCG, which was removed to make compliant with AWS::S3 in ODFv4.16. The ability to control if a certain bucket name would return need to be implemented via IAM policy which is not released yet. RFE bug [RHSTOR-7353](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHSTOR-7353) is created to track this IAM policy feature.

title: RHOSO Volume/Image Creation Failing
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Following the successful deployment of Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift 18.0, users are consistently unable to create new images and volumes.
resolution: - To deploy the Image service, you must set the number of replicas for the service and configure the back end for the service. For information about the recommended replicas for the Image service and how to configure a back end for the service, see [Configuring the Image service (glance)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html/configuring_persistent_storage/assembly_glance-configuring-glance_image) in Configuring persistent storage. If you do not deploy the Image service, you cannot upload images to the cloud or start an instance. ~~~ glance: apiOverrides: default: route: {} template: databaseInstance: openstack storage: storageRequest: 10G secret: osp-secret keystoneEndpoint: default glanceAPIs: default: replicas: 3 # Configured for proper service deployment override: service: internal: metadata: annotations: metallb.universe.tf/address-pool: internalapi metallb.universe.tf/allow-shared-ip: internalapi metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs: 172.17.0.80 spec: type: LoadBalancer networkAttachments:- storage ~~~
root_cause: - The root cause of the inability to create images and volumes after Red Hat OpenStack Platform on OpenShift (RHOSO) deployment was identified as an incomplete or misconfigured Image service (Glance) deployment. For the Image service to function correctly and enable image uploads and volume creation, it is crucial to explicitly define its replica count and configure its storage backend. ~~~ glance: apiOverrides: default: route: {} template: databaseInstance: openstack storage: storageRequest: 10G secret: osp-secret keystoneEndpoint: default glanceAPIs: default: replicas: 0 # Configure back end; set to 3 when deploying service override: service: internal: metadata: annotations: metallb.universe.tf/address-pool: internalapi metallb.universe.tf/allow-shared-ip: internalapi metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs: 172.17.0.80 spec: type: LoadBalancer networkAttachments:- storage ~~~

title: Vmin Shift Instability issue on Intel® Core™ 13th and 14th Gen desktop processor
issue: Unexplained kernel panic occurs on Intel® Core™ 13th and 14th Gen desktop processor.
resolution: * Please contact Hardware vendor to update microcode with new version `0x12f` or later.- https://community.intel.com/t5/Processors/Intel-Core-13th-and-14th-Gen-Vmin-Shift-Instabilty-Update-New/m-p/1686948 * Previously it was supposed to be resolved with `0x12b`.- https://community.intel.com/t5/Processors/Intel-Core-13th-and-14th-Gen-Desktop-Instability-Root-Cause/m-p/1633442
root_cause: * ~~~ Vmin Shift Instability Root Cause Intel® has localized the Vmin Shift Instability issue to a clock tree circuit within the IA core which is particularly vulnerable to reliability aging under elevated voltage and temperature. Intel has observed these conditions can lead to a duty cycle shift of the clocks and observed system instability. Intel® has identified four (4) operating scenarios that can lead to Vmin shift in affected processors: Motherboard power delivery settings exceeding Intel power guidance. a. Mitigation: Intel® Default Settings recommendations for Intel® Core™ 13th and 14th Gen desktop processors. eTVB Microcode algorithm which was allowing Intel® Core™ 13th and 14th Gen i9 desktop processors to operate at higher performance states even at high temperatures. a. Mitigation: microcode 0x125 (June 2024) addresses eTVB algorithm issue. Microcode SVID algorithm requesting high voltages at a frequency and duration which can cause Vmin shift. a. Mitigation: microcode 0x129 (August 2024) addresses high voltages requested by the processor. Microcode and BIOS code requesting elevated core voltages which can cause Vmin shift especially during periods of idle and/or light activity. a. Mitigation: Intel® is releasing microcode 0x12B, which encompasses 0x125 and 0x129 microcode updates, and addresses elevated voltage requests by the processor during idle and/or light activity periods. ~~~ Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. title: Direct Upgrade from OpenShift Pipelines Operator 1.15.x to 1.17.x Fails Due to Missing olm.skipRange in RHOCP 4
issue: - Attempting to directly upgrade from `openshift-pipelines-operator-rh` version `1.15.x to 1.17.x` fails due to a missing olm.skipRange in the operator's metadata.- The upgrade path is not available because the `olm.skipRange` does not define a direct upgrade from 1.15.x to 1.17.x.
resolution: - Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [SRVKP-7156](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SRVKP-7156) and delivered a fix through errata [RHBA-2025:8778](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:8778). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.- **WorkAround:** Manually upgrade the operator in the following order:- 1.15.1 → 1.15.2- 1.15.2 → 1.16.3- 1.16.3 → 1.17.1
root_cause: - The `olm.skipRange` for version `1.15.x` is missing, which prevents the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) from identifying a valid upgrade path to version 1.16.x or 1.17.x.- The `olm.skipRange` for 1.16.x should include `'> =1.15.0 <1.16.x'` to allow a seamless upgrade from 1.15.x to 1.16.x.

title: Tuned operator is in degarded state : "Profiles with bootcmdline conflict" error
issue: - Node Tuning Operator got degraded when creating a PerformanceProfile with `Profiles with bootcmdline conflict` error message.- Cluster operator `node-tuning` is degraded with below error: ~~~ Operator: 'node-tuning' Issue: Degraded Reason: ProfileConflict Message: 3/11 Profiles with bootcmdline conflict ~~~
resolution: - When using `MachineConfigPools`, it's best to group nodes with the same hardware into the same pool. This avoids conflicts with `TuneD`, which applies kernel tuning based on hardware. If different hardware types share one MCP, `TuneD` may apply the wrong settings, leading to performance issues or instability.- Best practice:- Label nodes by hardware type.- Create a separate MCP for each hardware type using a node selector.- Apply custom `MachineConfigs` or `TuneD` profiles per pool. This ensures correct tuning and consistent performance.
root_cause: - When nodes with differing hardware profiles (e.g., CPU architecture, core count, NUMA topology) are assigned to the same MCP, the `Tuned` operator — which optimizes performance settings based on node characteristics — calculates a single, shared set of kernel tuning parameters for the entire pool. Since these settings are derived from hardware assumptions, nodes with incompatible configurations may receive suboptimal or conflicting kernel parameters.

title: Failed to create pod with  privileges in the RHOCP namespace
issue: - Pod creation fails with the below error, when trying to create a pod in the namespace where `PSA mode(enforce)` and `profile(restricted)` is already applied. ~~~ Error from server (Forbidden): error when creating "pod-xxx.yaml": pods "yyy" is forbidden: violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": privileged (container "zzz" must not set securityContext.privileged=true), allowPrivilegeEscalation!= false (container "zzz" must set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false), unrestricted capabilities (containee "zzz" must set securityContext.capabilities.drop=["ALL"]), runAsNonRoot!= true (pod or container "zzz" must set securityContext.runAsNonRoot=true), runAsUser=0 (container "zzz" must not set runAsUser=0), seccompProfile (pod or container "zzz" must set securityContext.seccompProfile.type to "RuntimeDefault" or "Localhost") ~~~
resolution: - This error usually occurs when the `security context` privileges used in pod's deployment yaml are inadmissible because of the `PSA mode`(such as enforce) and `profile`(such as restricted) applied to the respective namespace.- The complete list of policies which can be use with security context privileges are mentioned in the upstream kubernetes [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/) as per the pod security standards.- Also refer the [RHOCP documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/authentication/understanding-and-managing-pod-security-admission.html) to understand more about pod security admission(PSA).
root_cause: - Pods that do not comply with the [pod security admission](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/authentication/understanding-and-managing-pod-security-admission.html) defined globally or at the namespace level are not admitted to the cluster and cannot run.

title: OpenShift installation fails to detect iSCSI boot disk as eligible target on OCI
issue: - During OpenShift installation on a host configured to boot from an iSCSI-attached volume, the installer fails to detect the disk as a valid installation target. The process is halted with the error: ~~~ No eligible disks were found. Please check specific disks to see why they are not eligible. ~~~- This error halted the process, as the system failed to recognize the attached disk as a valid option for cluster installation.
resolution: - iSCSI boot volume support is available starting from OpenShift 4.15; earlier versions do not support it.- To enable iSCSI boot support, OpenShift 4.15 or later must be installed.
root_cause: - The host inventory reveals that the system has only one available disk, which is an iSCSI boot volume.- In OpenShift versions below OCP 4.15, iSCSI boot volumes are not supported for installation.- As a result, the Assisted Installer fails to recognize the iSCSI disk as an eligible installation target, leading to the error: "No eligible disks were found."

title: crio-wipe failed to clean storage directory /var/lib/containers/storage on boot
issue: - `crio-wipe` service failed to clean storage directory `/var/lib/containers/storage` on boot- `ocp-tuned-one-shot.service` fails after reboot. ~~~ May 02 11:31:00 testworker crio[1221737]: time="2025-05-02 11:31:00.013568771Z" level=info msg="Checking whether cri-o should wipe containers: open /var/run/crio/version> May 02 11:31:00 testworker crio[1221737]: time="2025-05-02 11:31:00.013630886Z" level=info msg="File /var/lib/crio/clean.shutdown not found. Wiping storage directory /va> May 02 11:31:01 testworker crio[1221737]: time="2025-05-02 11:31:01.497148834Z" level=fatal msg="failed to remove storage directory: unlinkat /var/lib/containers/storage> May 02 11:31:01 testworker systemd[1]: crio-wipe.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE ~~~
resolution: This issue has been fixed in `Red Hat Openshift Container Platform (RHOCP) 4.19` and above. ### Workaround 1. Disable the `ocp-tuned-one-shot.service`: ``` # systemctl disable ocp-tuned-one-shot.service ``` 2. Set correct permissions on container storage directory: ``` # chmod 755 /var/lib/containers/storage ``` 3. Reboot the system: ``` # systemctl reboot ``` 4. Ensure that the `crio-wipe` service has completed successfully after reboot. ``` # systemctl status crio-wipe.service ``` 5. Once `crio-wipe` has completed, manually start the `ocp-tuned-one-shot` service: ``` # systemctl start ocp-tuned-one-shot.service ``` 6. Verify if the `kubelet` service starts automatically else start it manually. ``` # systemctl start kubelet ```
root_cause: - The node was not shut down properly, leading to the triggering of the `crio-wipe` service during reboot. The `crio-wipe` service attempted to continuously wipe `/var/lib/containers/storage`.- Simultaneously, `ocp-tuned-one-shot.service` attempted to run a podman command, which required writing to the same storage path. This resulted in a conflict, as crio-wipe was clearing the storage while podman was trying to access it, leading to a failure in `ocp-tuned-one-shot.service`, which in turn blocked kubelet from starting.

title: How to modify the pod eviction and reschedule timeout in OpenShift 4?
issue: - How long does it take to evict the Pods from a failing node in OpenShift 4?- Why Pod failover takes about 6 minutes when a node got down?- Is it possible to modify the Pod eviction and reschedule timeout in OpenShift 4?- Can the `node-monitor-grace-period` and `pod-eviction-timeout` parameters be modified?- What is the expected behavior of Pods in case of VM failure/crash?- How much time it will take to mark the node as `NotReady` state in case of VM failure?
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* It is possible to configure the `tolerationSeconds` for the Pod `tolerations` as explained in [understanding evicting Pods by condition (taint-based evictions)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/nodes/controlling-pod-placement-onto-nodes-scheduling#nodes-scheduler-taints-tolerations-about-taintBasedEvictions_nodes-scheduler-taints-tolerations).- `tolerationSeconds` can be modified for a particular `deployment` if Pods have to be forced to re-schedule on the next available worker node.- Terminated Pods on the failed worker node will be wiped out immediately when the node is back to the `Ready` state. Also, starting with OpenShift 4.11, it is possible to use worker latency profiles, that allows to control the reaction of the cluster to latency issues without needing to determine the best values manually. Refer to [Improving cluster stability in high latency environments using worker latency profiles](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/scalability_and_performance/scaling-worker-latency-profiles) for additional information. ####Pod eviction and reschedule timeout when using RWO volumes When using RWO volumes, they are not automatically detached from the node when a non-graceful node shutdown happens. To allow the pods using RWO volumes to be properly evicted and rescheduled, the volumes needs to be detached. There are two options for working with that:- Manually taint the node(s) with `node.kubernetes.io/out-of-service=nodeshutdown:NoExecute` (it is important to ensure the node is fully shut down to avoid filesystem corruption. Refer to [detach volumes after non-graceful node shutdown](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/storage/ephemeral-storage-csi-vol-detach-non-graceful-shutdown) for additional information.- Use the [Self Node Remediation (SNR)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/workload_availability_for_red_hat_openshift/25.3/html/remediation_fencing_and_maintenance/self-node-remediation-operator-remediate-nodes), which as explained in the documentation: "*This remediation strategy minimizes downtime for stateful applications and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) volumes, and restores compute capacity if transient failures occur*". ###OpenShift 4.10 and previous releases In previous OpenShift 4 releases, it is possible to use the `node-status-update-frequency` and `node-status-report-frequency` for remote worker nodes, which are only supported on bare metal clusters with user-provisioned infrastructure. The `node-status-update-frequency` parameter works with the `node-monitor-grace-period` and `pod-eviction-timeout` parameters, but those parameters cannot be manually modified. Refer to [Using remote worker nodes at the network edge](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/nodes/edge/nodes-edge-remote-workers.html) and the section [Remote worker node strategies](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.8/nodes/edge/nodes-edge-remote-workers.html#nodes-edge-remote-workers-strategies_nodes-edge-remote-workers) for additional information. > **Note:** The remote worker nodes are only supported on bare metal clusters with user-provisioned infrastructure. > **Note:** the `pod-eviction-timeout` parameter is no longer available starting with OpenShift 4.14. This change is due to its removal in Kubernetes 1.27 [Kubernetes Removals and Major Changes in v1.27](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/03/17/upcoming-changes-in-kubernetes-v1-27/#removal-of-pod-eviction-timeout-command-line-argument), which serves as the base for OpenShift 4.14. As a result, the parameter cannot be used or configured in OpenShift 4.14 and later versions. ####**Unsupported** workaround for previous releases > ***Disclaimer:** The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and supported procedures. The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the whole OpenShift cluster unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. The intent of this article is to provide information to accomplish the system's needs. Use of the information in this article at the user's own risk.* It is possible to use the `unsupportedConfigOverrides`, but note that it's an unsupported feature. Please check unsupportedConfigOverrides in OpenShift Container Platform 4 for details on `unsupportedConfigOverrides`. The Pod reschedule timeout is determined by `kube-controller-manager` arguments `pod-eviction-timeout` and `node-monitor-grace-period`. In OpenShift 4, some of the `kube-controller-manager` arguments are not supported to change. Technically, the `kube-controller-manager` arguments can be configured by editing `kubecontrollermanagers/cluster` resources: ~~~ $ oc edit kubecontrollermanagers cluster-n openshift-config spec: unsupportedConfigOverrides: extendedArguments: node-monitor-grace-period:- 20s pod-eviction-timeout:- 3m ~~~
root_cause: The `node-monitor-grace-period` parameter specifies how long OpenShift Container Platform waits after a node is marked "Unhealthy" if the controller manager does not receive the node heartbeat. Workloads on the node continue to run after this time. If the worker node rejoins the cluster after `node-monitor-grace-period` expires, pods continue to run. New pods can be scheduled to that node. The default `node-monitor-grace-period` interval is 40 seconds. When a Node becomes unreachable (or the `kubelet` stops reporting its status), it will be tainted with `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable`. By default, Pods tolerate this taint for 5 minutes. Thus it will take by default 5m 40s for a Pod created by a ReplicaSet to be rescheduled to another node. Refer to [taint based evictions upstream documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/#taint-based-evictions) for additional information.

title: Keycloak pod got restarted without any reason in RHOCP
issue: - The production `keycloak` pod got restarted without any reason.- The `Keycloak` pod service was unavailable for some time due to a pod restart.
resolution: Change the operators `Update Approval` setting from `Automatic` to `Manual` to avoid automatic operator updates. The path to change the `Update Approval` is given below in the RHOCP console. ~~~ Operator--> Installed Operator--> Operator name--> Subscription--> Update Approval--> Manual ~~~
root_cause: Red Hat Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) can be configured to automatically upgrade operators when new versions are available in the selected channel. This happens when the Update approval strategy is set to Automatic.

title: Application deployment or statefulset are failing in RHOCP4 with error: UID is not an allowed group, provider "restricted": Forbidden: not usable by user
issue: - Attempting to deploy an application using a particular UID leads to the following error: ~~~ create Pod "XXX" is failed error: pods "XXX" is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constraint: [provider "anyuid": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider restricted-v2:.spec.securityContext.fsGroup: Invalid value: []int64{xxxxxxxx}: xxxxxxxx is not an allowed group, provider "restricted": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "nonroot-v2": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "nonroot": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "machine-api-termination-handler": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "hostnetwork-v2": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "xxx-scc": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "XXXXX": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount, provider "privileged": Forbidden: not usable by user or serviceaccount] ~~~
resolution: - Check the `supplementalGroups` or `uid-range` parameter in the `projects` YAML: ~~~ $ oc get ns/-o yaml openshift.io/sa.scc.supplemental-groups: 1001290000/10000 openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range: 1001290000/10000 ~~~- Replace the `runAsGroup` and `fsGroup` parameter from `deployment/statefulset` under `securityContext` with `supplementalGroups` **Note:** `supplementalGroups` values must be in range of project `supplemental-group` so adding +1 to the `supplemental-group` from `project` yaml. ~~~ runAsNonRoot: true runAsUser: 1001290001---> supplementalGroups: [1001290001] runAsNonRoot: true fsGroup: 1001290001---> supplementalGroups: [1001290001] ~~~
root_cause: When a `project` or `namespace` is created in RHOCP, it is automatically assigned a `supplementalGroup` and a `uidRange`. If the `runAsUser` or `fsGroup` values specified in a `Deployment` or `StatefulSet` fall outside the assigned `supplementalGroups` or `uidRange` of the `project` or `namespace`, the `deployment` may fail due to security policy restrictions.

title: Enabling the MultiClusterObservability Service is failing in RHACM 2
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - Pods not creating in `multicluster-observability-operator` namespace after Enabling the `MultiClusterObservability` in RHACM.- MultiClusterObservability does not shows any `status` after applying the `multiclusterobservabilities` custom resource YAML file named `multiclusterobservability_cr.yaml` on the hub cluster.- The `multicluster-observability-operator` pods are repeatedly throwing the following error: `\"observability\" is invalid:: Internal error: resource name may not be empty.`
resolution: - Add correct details of object storage config in `thanos-object-storage` secret to avoid this issue: For `Amazon S3 or S3 compatible`, secret might resemble the following file: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: thanos-object-storage namespace: open-cluster-management-observability type: Opaque stringData: thanos.yaml: | type: s3 config: bucket: YOUR_S3_BUCKET endpoint: YOUR_S3_ENDPOINT 1 insecure: true access_key: YOUR_ACCESS_KEY secret_key: YOUR_SECRET_KEY ~~~ For other cloud providers with stable object stores please refer [Create a secret for your object storage for your cloud provider](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.13/html-single/observability/index#prerequisites-observability:~:text=Create%20a%20secret%20for%20your%20object%20storage%20for%20your%20cloud%20provider.%20Your%20secret%20must%20contain%20the%20credentials%20to%20your%20storage%20solution.%20For%20example%2C%20run%20the%20following%20command%3A)
root_cause: - If no `storageConfig.storageClass` field is defined in MultiClusterObservability custom resource, object stores default StorageClass will be populated in the storageConfig section of `MultiClusterObservability`. For example for `Amazon Web Services S3 (AWS S3)` default storageClass will be `gp2`.

title: Authentication error caused by restored users and identities
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: Unable to authenticate to the Openshift cluster using an Identity Provider and after restoring users with a backup/restore tool or any other method.
resolution: Delete the users and identities that were restored by the backup tool using the commands: * `oc delete user ` * `oc delete identity ` And login again with the same user using the corresponding Identity Provider.
root_cause: The labels: `velero.io/backup-name: backup-name` and/or `velero.io/restore-name: restore-name` in this case, (there could be other labels related to other back up tools or other methods of creating users) indicate that the User and Identity objects were restored by a backup tool, and these resources were not freshly created by the OpenShift OAuth workflow, for this reason, the original `useridentitymapping` can't be found on the cluster, and OAuth needs to establish a new `useridentitymapping`. **Note:** It is not necessary to back-up/restore users and identities, as these resources will be automatically created at login time if they don't exist, also these resources are created by the OAuth workflow.

title: Red Hat Data Grid SCC and SA details in Openshift 4

title: Is it possible to install Red Hat Service Mesh 3.x alongside existing Service Mesh 2.x in same cluster?
issue: - Is it possible to install Service Mesh 3 along side Service Mesh 2.x?
resolution: - Running Service Mesh 2.x and 3.x simultaneously on the same cluster is not supported, except during the migration process. During this transitional phase, both operators may briefly coexist to facilitate the migration of workloads from Service Mesh 2 to Service Mesh 3. Outside of this specific use case, concurrent operation of both versions is not supported.- Supporting both Service Mesh 2.x and 3.x operators on the same cluster over an extended period is not recommended due to several potential risks and limitations:- Upgrading the 2.6 operator while 3.0 is already installed may unintentionally overwrite Istio CRDs. This scenario has not been tested.- When adding new workloads, it's essential to correctly apply the annotation maistra.io/ignore-namespace: "true"—a requirement that no longer applies once the 2.6 operator is removed.- Creating or modifying 2.6 workloads in a mixed-operator environment has not been thoroughly validated.- Ongoing changes in upstream APIs during this period may introduce compatibility issues. For these reasons, running both operators should be limited strictly to the migration phase.

title: How to Install smartmontools and nvme-cli to view SMART logs and Error logs of Storage Devices in OpenShift Container Platform v4.x
issue: Enabling device analysis tools in CoreOS on an OpenShift node requires additional effort which will be outlined in this solution.
resolution: **Prerequisite:** Capture the device name and host of the affected disk: **Example Using OpenShift Data Foundation Storage Devices:** ~~~ $ oc describe pod-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-osd-- | grep ClaimName ~~~- Match the `ClaimName` with the associated Persistent Volume (PV). `$ oc get pv-n openshift-storage | grep `- Capture device name and hostname: `$ oc get pv-n openshift-storage-o yaml | egrep 'device-name|hostname'` # Procedure: 1. Debug into the storage node hosting the device using a custom image: **Note:** An image can be prepared in advance with the correct tools installed ~~~ oc debug--image=quay.io/fedora/fedora node/ dnf install-y smartmontools nvme-cli lsblk ~~~ 2. Capture the device name(s) ~~~ lsblk ls-l /host/dev/disk/by-id ~~~ **Note:** For LSO configurations it may be necessary to view the contents of the `/host/mnt/local-storage/ /` directory, followed by the output of `$ ls /host/dev/disk/by-id-l` 3. Run the following commands in addition to any additional commands the Red Hat Support Engineer requests: ~~~ smartctl--all /dev/ smartctl--all /host/dev/disk/by-id/ <...> nvme smart-log /dev/ nvme error-log /dev/ ~~~ **NOTE:** You may receive an `ERRO[0000] container not running` message at the end of the output, this can be ignored. The output that precedes that message is valid.
root_cause: When it's determined a hardware failure or performance degradation is at play it may be necessary to gather the outputs outlined in this solution in addition to any additional outputs RH Support deems necessary.

title: How to enable Cockpit debug logging
issue: How can I enable debug logging in Cockpit?
resolution:
You can enable debug logging by following these steps: In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7: ~~~~ # mkdir-p /etc/systemd/system/cockpit.service.d # printf '[Service]
Environment=G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=cockpit-ws,cockpit-bridge
User=root
Group=
' > /etc/systemd/system/cockpit.service.d/debug.conf # systemctl daemon-reload # systemctl restart cockpit ~~~~ In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9: ~~~~ # cp /lib/systemd/system/cockpit-wsinstance-https@.service /etc/systemd/system # sed-i 's/\[Service\]/\[Service\]
Environment=G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=cockpit-ws,cockpit-bridge/' /etc/systemd/system/cockpit-wsinstance-https@.service # systemctl daemon-reload # systemctl restart cockpit ~~~~ **Note:** To enable debugging for all cockpit components change `G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=cockpit-ws,cockpit-bridge` to `G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=all` To view debug logging, run: ~~~~ # journalctl-g cockpit ~~~~ To disable debug logging, run: ~~~~ # rm /etc/systemd/system/cockpit.service.d/debug.conf # systemctl daemon-reload # systemctl restart cockpit ~~~~ Additional details can be found in upstream Cockpit documentation:

title: ACS update to 4.8.0 is blocked due to migration 211 failed in RHOCP4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Advanced Cluster Security operator update to version 4.8.0 is stuck on database migration.- `unable to alter table network_flows_v2: unable to update column updatedat: unexpected EOF` error during ACS update.- Database migration from 209 to 211 is blocking the update to ACS 4.8.0.
resolution: 1. Check the minimum resources required to run Central DB in [ACS documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.8/html/installing/acs-default-requirements#default-requirements-central-services-central_acs-default-requirements). 2. Increase the memory limits of `central-db` by setting `spec.central.db.resources.limits` parameter in `Central` resource: ~~~ $ oc-n edit Central [...] spec: central: db: resources: limits: cpu: "1" memory: 2Gi <-- INCREASE THIS VALUE ~~~ Note that migration may takes some time to finish.
root_cause: The `UPDATE network_flows_v2` in migration 211 is an expensive query and if the resources assigned to `central-db` pod are not sufficient, the underlying operating system sends a signal 9 to kill the Postgres process, stopping the query and therefore the update to ACS 4.8.0.

title: Not set permissions to system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s for scrapping the `openshift-update-service` namespace resources
issue: After installing the OpenShift Update Service operator are visible errors in the Prometheus pods indicating that the user `system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s` has not permissions to list the pods: ~~~ ts=2025-02-24T11:25:18.124Z caller=klog.go:108 level=warn component=k8s_client_runtime func=Warningf msg="github.com/prometheus/prometheus/discovery/kubernetes/kubernetes.go:556: failed to list *v1.Pod: pods is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"openshift-update-service\"" ts=2025-02-24T11:25:18.124Z caller=klog.go:116 level=error component=k8s_client_runtime func=ErrorDepth msg="github.com/prometheus/prometheus/discovery/kubernetes/kubernetes.go:556: Failed to watch *v1.Pod: failed to list *v1.Pod: pods is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"openshift-update-service\"" ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-51196](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-51196). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. #### Workaround Create a role using the yaml: ~~~ $ cat role.yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-update-service rules:- apiGroups:- "" resources:- services- endpoints- pods verbs:- get- list- watch $ oc create-f role.yaml ~~~ Create the RoleBinding for allowing to the serviceAccount prometheus-k8s scrape the metrics from the resources in the namespace "openshift-update-service" using the yaml: ~~~ $ cat rolebinding.yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-update-service roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Role name: prometheus-k8s subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-monitoring $ oc create-f rolebinding.yaml ~~~
root_cause: The OpenShift Update Service has not set the needed permissions by default for the `system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s` user being able to scrape the resources for getting the metrics in the namespace `openshift-update-service`.

title: How can Operators be updated independently from each other?
issue: - InstallPlans are referencing more than one operator. The InstallPlans for an operator should be distinct from other operators.- While using different operators in `openshift-operators` namespace. The different subscriptions are deployed with either automatic or manual `approvalMode`. It's expected that the install plans of an operator are distinct from other operators. But, InstallPlans are referencing more than one operator and an InstallPlan contains all operators that could be updated. If one of the operators have `approvalMode` Manual rest of the operators will not update though they have been subscribed with Automatic mode.- Updating an operator in the `openshift-operators` namespace triggers an update of all Operators in the namespace.- When an operator is configured with an automatic `approvalMode`, the OpenShift GUI displays the `Update approval` status as ` Automatic Functioning as manual`.- We have several operators installed in our cluster and currently have the subscription for each operator set to "manual" approval to ensure upgrades are planned and appropriately tested/validated. However, when I go to approve the single operator I want to upgrade, OpenShift creates an install plan for `ALL POSSIBLE` operators that can be upgraded and asks me to approve upgrades for all. Is it not possible to upgrade a single operator through OLM?- How do I upgrade just a single operator at a time in OpenShift?
resolution: - Install Plans are referenced by more than one Operator and this is the current intended behavior. In the future, this will change due to an API re-design of OLM which will operate at the cluster-scope. The way to avoid this with today's API is by installing the operators into separate namespaces.- As of now OLM can handle the Operators independently, but there are manual steps needed. As a workaround, create a new OperatorGroup object, subscribe a namespace to the Operator in AllNamespaces mode, the namespace needs to be different than `openshift-operators`. Full workaround description is [found in the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.9/operators/admin/olm-adding-operators-to-cluster.html#olm-installing-operator-from-operatorhub-using-cli_olm-adding-operators-to-a-cluster).- There was an open feature request [OLM-2151](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OLM-2151) regarding changing this default behavior. From RHOCP 4.14 version, we have launched Operator Lifecycle Manager [OLM](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes.html#ocp-4-14-olm) v1.0 which will be in the Technical Preview for now. This will give improved insight into catalog content, administrators can specify target versions for installation and updates. This grants administrators more control over the target version of Operator updates.
root_cause: - This behavior is currently expected, due to the namespaced API design and dependency resolution of OLM. Current API design and dependency resolution causes all Operators in a namespace, related by dependencies or not, to be treated as one big set to install / upgrade and fail / succeed altogether.- The OLM UI defaults all global operators into the same namespace (`openshift-operators`), that causes this side effect.

title: Applications with a Failed condition fail to appear in argocd_app_condition metric in the argocd controller pod
issue: - When utilizing the OpenShift GitOps operator to record application metrics, the Argo CD controller pod fails to retrieve the `argocd_app_condition` metric for applications in a `Failed` condition, even when `Failed` is specified as a condition in the `.spec.controller.extraCommandArgs` field.- The following configuration provides an example for the ArgoCD controller pod configuration: ~~~ spec: controller: extraCommandArgs:---metrics-application-conditions- SyncFailed,SyncError,Failed,OrphanedResourceWarning prometheus: enabled: true ~~~- The following application status provides an example for the application `Failed` condition: ~~~ status: conditions:- type: Failed status: 'True' ~~~
resolution: - There is no solution or workaround for this issue.- There is an ongoing [RFE-7872 (Request For Enhancement)](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-7252 "") that is adding `Failed` as a condition in the backend code of the `.spec.controller.extraCommandArgs` field.
root_cause: - This is an expected behavior, as the condition `Failed` is not included in the backend code of the list of conditions under the field `.spec.controller.extraCommandArgs`.

title: Lint validation errors on the YAML formatted API object file in RHOCP4
issue: - There is automation in place that is managing the namespace and objects, and when new object VMs are added, the yamls are dumped and pushed to git and are setup in automation tool to maintain the objects, and before they can be used, they are all linted and fail on indication. Following errors /warnings occurs, $ oc get VM-o yaml > vm-resource-output.yaml $ ansible-lint vm-resource-output.yaml.. yaml[indentation]: Wrong indentation: expected 6 but found 4 test.yaml:20 yaml[indentation]: Wrong indentation: expected 6 but found 4 test.yaml:35
resolution: - The best practice is to use a command-line tool like `yq` to automatically reformat the file. This ensures consistency easier than manual editing.- Runing `ansible-lint` on the new vm-resource-output.yaml file should pass without any indentation errors. $ oc get vm examplevm-oyaml | yq > vm-resource-output.yaml $ ansible-lint vm-resource-output.yaml 1:1 warning missing document start "---" (document-start)
root_cause: - Kubernetes YAML output `oc get-o yaml` uses valid but compact indentation usually 2 or 4 spaces.- The ansible-lint expects strict YAML style, usually 2-space indentation per level, and proper alignment for readability and structure. Hence, the error is simply a result of conflicting formatting standards.

title: Custom systemd unit makes RHOCP 4 node to not complete the boot
issue: - After adding a custom systemd unit some services like `ovsdb-server.service` and `console-login-helper-messages-gensnippet-ssh-keys.service` fail to start. The journald logs show the following error messages: ~~~ gensnippet_ssh_keys[1392]: mktemp: failed to create file via template '/run/console-login-helper-messages/console-login-helper-messages.XXXXXXXXXX.tmp': No such file or directory gensnippet_ssh_keys[1393]: /usr/lib/console-login-helper-messages/libutil.sh: line 37:: No such file or directory systemd[1]: console-login-helper-messages-gensnippet-ssh-keys.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE [..] chown[1407]: /usr/bin/chown: cannot access '/run/openvswitch': No such file or directory [..] nostalgic_satoshi[1585]: time="2025-07-14T07:15:39Z" level=info msg="Failed to read ip from file /run/nodeip-configuration/primary-ip" error="open /run/nodeip-configuration/primary-ip: no such file or directory" ~~~- After creating a custom systemd unit with a MachineConfig that starts before `multipathd.service` the OpenShift Container Platform Node does not complete the boot.- After adding a custom systemd unit, the Node fails to boot and shows the following error message: ~~~ level=info msg="Failed to read ip from file /run/nodeip-configuration/primary-ip" error="open /run/nodeip-configuration/primary-ip: no such file or directory" level=error msg="Failed to find a suitable node IP" ~~~- After creating a custom systemd unit the node remains `NotReady` and trying to access it returns: ~~~ "System is booting up. Unprivileged users are not permitted to log in yet. Please come back later. For technical details, see pam_nologin(8)." ~~~
resolution: * Include `DefaultDependencies=no` and `Conflicts=shutdown.target` in the configuration of a custom systemd unit that needs to be executed at the early stages, for example: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-custom-unit spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 systemd: units:- contents: | [Unit] Description=Custom unit name Before=multipathd.service DefaultDependencies=no Conflicts=shutdown.target [Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=/bin/true RemainAfterExit=yes [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target enabled: true name: custom-unit.service- enabled: true name: multipathd.service ~~~
root_cause: - Custom services are triggered after `local-fs.target` is reached, if the `Before=` option mentions a unit that starts before `local-fs.target` a cycle is created leading to systemd randomly removing jobs at boot.- Custom systemd services that need to be started at the early stages must have the `DefaultDependencies=no` and `Conflicts=shutdown.target` configurations.

title: Turbostat tool not showing exclusive or isolated CPU core info in RHEL 9
issue: - Unable to get all `CPU info` using `turbostat` Linux performance monitoring tool.- The `turbostat` tool give `cpu
not effective` for few CPUs.
resolution: - Use `sysfs interface` to get the `CPU info` for all the cores: ~~~ $ grep-r. /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy*/scaling_cur_freq ~~~ This will show the current `frequency of each CPU`, even if they are isolated e.g.: ~~~ $ grep-r. /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy*/scaling_cur_freq /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy0/scaling_cur_freq:800000 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy1/scaling_cur_freq:800317 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy2/scaling_cur_freq:800000 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy3/scaling_cur_freq:800001 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy4/scaling_cur_freq:800000 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy5/scaling_cur_freq:800000 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy6/scaling_cur_freq:800000 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy7/scaling_cur_freq:800000 ~~~
root_cause: This behavior is intentional and due to an `upstream kernel tools` update which handles `cgroup v2 cpu` limitation:- In `cgroup v2`, CPUs marked as isolated (via cpuset.cpus.partition) are excluded from tasks like performance monitoring to prevent unintentional task migration.- Before `upstream kernel tools` update `turbostat` displays the CPU information for all eight processors 0-7. ~~~ $ turbostat-s CPU,Busy%,Bzy_MHz-q-n 1 CPU Busy% Bzy_MHz- 3.54 802 0 0.23 804 1 0.08 817 2 7.91 801 3 0.10 815 4 19.67 801 5 0.05 831 6 0.18 806 7 0.06 981 ~~~- After isolation, `turbostat` no longer provides information on the isolated cpus: ~~~ /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.effective:0-7 cd /sys/fs/cgroup echo +cpuset > cgroup.subtree_control cd isolated echo 4-7 > cpuset.cpus echo isolated > cpuset.cpus.partition /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.effective:0-3 /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.isolated:4-7 ~~~ ~~~ $ turbostat-s CPU,Busy%,Bzy_MHz-q-n 1 cpu4 not effective < < < < < < < < <------- Isolated CPU cpu5 not effective < < < < < < < < <------- Isolated CPU cpu6 not effective < < < < < < < < <------- Isolated CPU cpu7 not effective < < < < < < < < <------- Isolated CPU CPU Busy% Bzy_MHz- 2.25 801 0 0.17 804 1 0.12 811 2 8.64 801 3 0.05 901 ~~~

title: Can an Azure Disk PV be mounted by multiple pods simultaneously in an ARO cluster?
issue: - What is the pod assignment limit for Azure Disk based PVs in ARO?- Can Azure Disk Persistent Volumes be assigned to multiple pods in an Azure Red Hat OpenShift cluster?- Is there a limit to the number of pods that can access a single Azure Disk PV?- Are there restrictions related to node or Availability Zone (AZ) placement with respect to Azure Disk based PV?
resolution: 1. Azure Disk Persistent Volumes in ARO are backed by block storage and support the `ReadWriteOnce (RWO)` access mode. This mode allows a volume to be attached to **a single node** only. 2. Multiple pods running on the same node can access the volume concurrently. Therefore, the number of pods that can use the PV depends on the number of pods that can be scheduled on the node to which the disk is attached. 3. *Azure Disk PVs are specific to the Availability Zone* in which they were provisioned. They can only be attached to nodes within the same zone. Cross-zone or multi-node attachment is not supported with `ReadWriteOnce`. **Note**- Azure imposes [a limit on the number of data disks that can be attached to a single virtual machine](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/openshift-service-definitions#block-storage-rwo), depending on the VM size used for worker nodes. It is recommended to review the VM specs to ensure disk limits are not exceeded.
root_cause: The access mode of Azure Disk (ReadWriteOnce) restricts the volume to a single node, regardless of the number of pods.

title: Image pull fails with "unknown blob" error for ImageStreams using a pull-through cache with an external registry in OpenShift Container Platform 4.
issue: An ImagePullBackoff error is observed for pods consuming an ImageStream that references an external container registry with referencePolicy: type: Local. The OpenShift Container Platform registry logs show err.detail="unknown blob" and Background mirroring failed. This issue often occurs when the external registry (e.g., Artifactory) provides inconsistent HTTP responses, specifically returning HTTP 200 OK to a HEAD request but HTTP 404 Not Found to a subsequent GET request for a non-existent image layer (blob).
resolution: The fundamental issue lies with the external registry's non-compliance with the container registry specification. It is required to reconfigure the external registry to return a consistent HTTP 404 Not Found for both HEAD and GET requests against non-existent blobs. Engage the vendor of the registry software for remediation.- Optional Temporary Workaround: Recreating the ImageStream object often resolves the immediate pull failure. This action can repopulate the OpenShift registry's cache with currently valid image layers, allowing pods to start. Creating a new ImageStream that references the same upstream image can also have the effect of caching the necessary blobs, which may resolve the issue for the original, failing ImageStream. ~~~ # (Optional) Save the definition of the old ImageStream oc get is-o yaml > imagestream_backup.yaml # Delete the problematic ImageStream oc delete is # Re-create the ImageStream from its definition or CI/CD process oc create-f imagestream_backup.yaml ~~~ To reduce the likelihood of referencing stale or deleted blobs from the external registry, it is recommended to periodically prune historical image data from the ImageStream status. ~~~ # Prune images, keeping the last 5 revisions for each tag oc adm prune images--keep-tag-revisions=5--confirm ~~~
root_cause: The behavior of oc tag creating a spec.tags.from.kind of ImageStreamImage is expected for permanent tags and is not the root cause. The failure is a direct result of a logical conflict between the OpenShift Image Registry's pull-through cache implementation and the behavior of the external registry. The flow confirmed from engineering is the following: ~~~ Pull Request Initiated: A client (cri-o on a compute node) requests to pull an image tag from the OpenShift Image Registry, for instance, image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/my-project/my-app:release. Pull-Through Cache (referencePolicy: Local): The release tag in the ImageStream is configured to pull from an external registry. The OpenShift registry acts as a proxy and cache. It first checks its local storage for the required image manifest and layer blobs. Blob Existence Check (The Failure Point): If a required blob is not in its local cache, the OpenShift registry attempts to fetch it from the external source. As per the Docker V2 API specification, it first sends a HEAD request to the external registry to verify the existence and size of the blob. Non-Compliant External Registry Response: The external registry receives the HEAD request for a blob that has been deleted or never existed. Instead of returning the expected HTTP 404 Not Found response, it incorrectly returns HTTP 200 OK. Conflicting Signals: The OpenShift registry receives the HTTP 200 OK and assumes the blob exists. It proceeds by sending a GET request to download the blob's content. The external registry, upon receiving the GET request, now correctly responds with HTTP 404 Not Found. Internal State Corruption: The OpenShift registry enters a failed state. It was told the blob exists (HEAD-> 200) but was then unable to retrieve it (GET-> 404). This inconsistency leads to the logged error Background mirroring failed: error committing to storage: unknown blob. Client Error: The registry returns an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error to the pulling client (cri-o). The pod enters ImagePullBackoff because it cannot fetch the layer. ~~~

title: ARO egress lockdown conflicts with Entra ID Conditional Access due to dynamic egress IPs
issue: When Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) clusters are configured with **egress lockdown**, traffic destined for the public Microsoft Entra ID endpoint is routed through the ARO management infrastructure via a private link. This traffic then egresses to the internet from a **pool of dynamic IP addresses*
managed by the ARO service, which frequently change, especially with new ARO releases.
This dynamic nature of egress IPs creates a conflict for customers who use **Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access policies*

to restrict access to Entra ID applications from known and trusted IP addresses. Since the ARO egress IPs are not static or published, it becomes impossible to create reliable and future-proof Conditional Access policies.

This forces customers into undesirable choices: either weakening their security posture by disabling IP-based Conditional Access or engaging in manual, and error-prone tracking and updating of IPs, which can lead to unexpected outages.
resolution: Currently, there is no direct resolution within the customer's control to provide a static or allow-listed IP range for ARO egress traffic when using egress lockdown with Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access. This is an upstream design limitation that requires collaboration with Microsoft Azure. Until a solution is found, customers may need to consider alternative authentication methods or accept the limitations imposed by the dynamic egress IPs. Workarounds like using local accounts or exploring managed identities for applications, although potentially more complex to manage at scale for individual developers, might be necessary depending on the security requirements and use case.
root_cause: The root cause of this issue lies in the dynamic and unpredictable nature of the public egress IP addresses used by the ARO management infrastructure when an ARO cluster has egress lockdown enabled and traffic is routed to the public Microsoft Entra ID endpoint. Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access policies, on the other hand, rely on the ability to define and restrict access from known, static IP ranges. The mismatch between ARO's dynamic egress IPs and Entra ID's static IP requirement for Conditional Access policies prevents customers from effectively securing their authentication traffic.

title: Ceph status in HEALTH_ERR: all pools are full
issue: - Ceph status shows `HEALTH_ERR` and all pools currently full: ~~~ sh-5.1$ ceph-s cluster: id: [...] health: HEALTH_ERR 1 backfillfull osd(s) 1 full osd(s) 1 nearfull osd(s) 12 pool(s) full ~~~- Even after deleting the more impactful `PersistentVolume` objects, the `HEALTH_ERR` statut remains even though the pools are not at capacity anymore: ~~~--- POOLS--- POOL ID PGS STORED OBJECTS USED %USED MAX AVAIL ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool 1 128 530 GiB 142.79k 1.6 TiB 100.00 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.otp 2 8 0 B 0 0 B 0 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.buckets.non-ec 3 8 0 B 0 0 B 0 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.control 4 8 0 B 8 0 B 0 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.log 5 8 3.3 MiB 348 12 MiB 100.00 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.meta 6 8 5.9 KiB 26 240 KiB 100.00 0 B.rgw.root 7 8 5.4 KiB 17 192 KiB 100.00 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.buckets.index 8 8 31 MiB 44 93 MiB 100.00 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-metadata 9 32 331 MiB 147.12k 992 MiB 100.00 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore.rgw.buckets.data 10 32 22 GiB 171.61k 68 GiB 100.00 0 B ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-data0 11 32 31 GiB 621.84k 97 GiB 100.00 0 B.mgr 12 1 5.8 MiB 3 17 MiB 100.00 0 B ~~~
resolution: - After assuring that some space has been freed (pods, PersistentVolumeClaim objects, and PersistentVolume objects have been deleted), it is helpful to rebalance the OSDs on Ceph: ~~~ # ceph osd crush reweight osd.0 1 # ceph osd crush reweight osd.1 1 [...] # ceph osd crush reweight osd.8 1 ~~~- Now, you will need to set a coherent ratio by following the related [solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6387181).- Sometimes, you might also want to trim some space to delete pending data in your disks: `$ for i in $(oc get node-l node-role.kubernetes.io/worker-o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do oc debug node/${i}-- chroot /host fstrim-av; done`

title: ovnkube-node pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state because of bad certificate
issue: - Observed `ovnkube-node` pod is `CrashLoopBackOff` state. ~~~ NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE ovnkube-control-plane-7464bcfXXX-dhxxx 2/2 Running 0 69d ovnkube-control-plane-7464bcfXXX-jtxxx 2/2 Running 0 69d ovnkube-control-plane-7464bcfXXX-s2xxx 2/2 Running 0 69d ovnkube-node-2gxxx 7/8 CrashLoopBackOff 190 (2m57s ago) 15h ovnkube-node-bcxxx 8/8 Running 8 69d ~~~- On restarting problematic ovnkube-node-xxxxx pod issue still persists
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-36195](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-36195) and delivered a fix in 4.17.0 through errata [RHEA-2024:3718](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:3718). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. ###Workaround to fix this issue:- Log in to problematic `ovnkube-node-xxxxx` pod and navigate to path `/etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs/`- Remove the file which is linked with `ovnkube-client-current.pem` with below commands ~~~ $ oc rsh ovnkube-node-2gxxx sh-5.1# cd /etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs/ sh-5.1# ls-lrth | tail-3-rw-------. 1 root root 1.2K Feb 20 14:00 ovnkube-client-2024-02-20-14-00-23.pem lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root 66 Feb 22 05:08 ovnkube-client-current.pem-> /etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs/ovnkube-client-2024-02-22-05-08-30.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 0 Feb 22 05:10 ovnkube-client-2024-02-22-05-08-30.pem sh-5.1# rm-rf /etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs/*- If unable to remote to pod, ssh to node and remove the cert data # ssh core@ # sudo rm-rf /var/lib/ovn-ic/etc/ovnkube-node-certs/*- Restart the problematic ovnkube-node-xxxxx pod and it will come to running state with new certificate. # oc delete-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ovnkube-node-xxxxx- Double check CSR is created and approved, if not approved manually approve the CSR. # oc get csr # oc get csr-o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve ~~~
root_cause: The certificate `ovnkube-client-current.pem` was `blank` hence causing `ovnkube-node` pod to fail.

title: LDAP Result Code 52: "Unavailable": Error initializing SSL/TLS when setting up an OAuth LDAP IdP
issue: The below message is thrown when trying to login to OpenShift using a set OAuth LDAP IdP: ~~~ 2025-05-30T17:54:37.364002232Z E0530 17:54:37.363876 1 login.go:176] Error authenticating " " with provider " ": LDAP Result Code 52 "Unavailable": 00000000: LdapErr: DSID-0C09169C, comment: Error initializing SSL/TLS, data 0, v4f7c ~~~
resolution: * If willing to use `ldaps://`, create a config map containing the LDAP server CA in the `openshift-config` namespace: ~~~ oc create configmap ca-config-map--from-file=ca.crt=/path/to/ca-n openshift-config ~~~ * Then patch it to your IdP configuration: ~~~ oc patch oauth cluster--type=json-p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/identityProviders/ /ldap/ca/name", "value": "ca-config-map"}]'-n openshift-config ~~~ Replace ` ` (from 0 on) by the correct index of your IdP if there is more than one configured in the `OAuth` resource definition. * If willing to use a non-secured conenction (`ldap://`), make sure that the `.spec.identityProviders[].ldap.insecure` field is set to "true" and that the `.spec.identityProviders[].ldap.url` is using `ldap://`, and not `ldaps://`.
root_cause: This happens when not specifying the `.spec.identityProviders[].ldap.ca.name` field with the name of a valid config map containing the LDAP server CA for secured LDAP (`ldaps://`). Sometimes the `.spec.identityProviders[].ldap.url` field may even be set with `ldap://`, but if the `.spec.identityProviders[].ldap.insecure` field is set to "false", the connection will default to `ldaps://` and if the `.spec.identityProviders[].ldap.ca.name` field is empty, the `LDAP Result Code 52 "Unavailable": 00000000: LdapErr: DSID-0C09169C, comment: Error initializing SSL/TLS` will be thrown and the user login won't be possible.

title: JBoss EAP KUBE_PING clustering in OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - How to configure JBoss EAP clustering in OpenShift?
resolution: See main solution [EAP 7 image clustering in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6980435) for details on clustering explanation, EAP template deployment, EAP 7 Operator, `DNS_PING` vs `KUBE_PING`. JBoss EAP image is configured to use `KUBE_PING` which uses Kubernetes API to discover clustering members. To enable clustering, we need to allow JBoss EAP service account access to the Kubernetes API. It's recommended that always starts from templates like `eap70-basic-s2i`. Do not directly use images such as `registry.access.redhat.com/jboss-eap-7/eap70-openshift` or imagestreams like `jboss-eap70-openshift`. The reason is that the `KUBE_PING` needs various environment variables and named container port definition in DeploymentConfig to form a cluster. They are pre-configured in these templates along with some other useful things such as livenessProbe and readinessProbe. If you use image directly, the required configuration is missing so you need additional lengthy manual configurations and copy them from the templates. This is unnecessary effort. **Required Items** 1. A headless service with the correct pods labels. 2. A port named `ping` must be defined. The Red Hat templates default this port to 8888. 3. The service account needs permissions to view the default namespace and current namespace. 4. The variables `OPENSHIFT_KUBE_PING_NAMESPACE`, `JGROUPS_PING_PROTOCOL=kubernetes.KUBE_PING`, `OPENSHIFT_KUBE_PING_LABELS` must be set according. They are `deploymentconfig`- for deploymentConfig deployment, or WildflyServer CR for EAP 7 Operator. Using template, to allow JBoss EAP service account access to Kubernetes API, you need to add `view` role to the service account, in this example `default`. ~~~ $ oc project YOUR_PROJECT $ oc policy add-role-to-user view system:serviceaccount:$(oc project-q):eap-service-account $ oc policy add-role-to-user view system:serviceaccount:$(oc project-q):default ~~~ Then create a JBoss EAP app with templates like `eap70-basic-s2i`, scale up to 2 replicas. ~~~ $ oc new-app eap70-basic-s2i $ oc scale dc eap-app--replicas=2 ~~~ In `oc logs` we can see 2 pods formed a cluster in the following lines: ~~~ $ oc logs eap-app-1-8l9fw | grep 'new cluster view' 01:22:43,070 INFO [org.infinispan.remoting.transport.jgroups.JGroupsTransport] (MSC service thread 1-4) ISPN000094: Received new cluster view for channel web: [eap-app-1-dlt3p|1] (2) [eap-app-1-dlt3p, eap-app-1-8l9fw] 01:22:43,081 INFO [org.infinispan.remoting.transport.jgroups.JGroupsTransport] (MSC service thread 1-2) ISPN000094: Received new cluster view for channel ejb: [eap-app-1-dlt3p|1] (2) [eap-app-1-dlt3p, eap-app-1-8l9fw] 01:22:43,081 INFO [org.infinispan.remoting.transport.jgroups.JGroupsTransport] (MSC service thread 1-3) ISPN000094: Received new cluster view for channel server: [eap-app-1-dlt3p|1] (2) [eap-app-1-dlt3p, eap-app-1-8l9fw] 01:22:43,084 INFO [org.infinispan.remoting.transport.jgroups.JGroupsTransport] (MSC service thread 1-5) ISPN000094: Received new cluster view for channel hibernate: [eap-app-1-dlt3p|1] (2) [eap-app-1-dlt3p, eap-app-1-8l9fw] ~~~ [EAP 7 Guide Openshift Clustering](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_middleware_for_openshift/3/html-single/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform_for_openshift/#clustering)
root_cause: See main solution [EAP 7 image clustering in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6980435) for details on clustering explanation, EAP template deployment, EAP 7 Operator, `DNS_PING` vs `KUBE_PING`.

title: How to configure NodeTuning in OCP 4.x
issue: - Node tuning using Node Tuning operator in OCP 4.x
resolution: - First label the node to apply the desired tuning profile: ~~~ # oc label node node1.example.com node-role.kubernetes.io/ingress-node-label= ~~~- Create a custom tuning profile (Custom Resource- CR) as below: ~~~ # vi custom-ingress-tuned.yaml apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: ingress namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=A custom OpenShift ingress profile include=openshift-control-plane [sysctl] net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535" net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 name: openshift-ingress recommend:- match:- label: "node-role.kubernetes.io/ingress-node-label" priority: 10 profile: openshift-ingress ~~~- Apply this CR: ~~~ # oc create-f custom-ingress-tuned.yaml ~~~- Now check the node has got the desired changes or not? ~~~ # oc debug node/node1.example.com Starting pod/node1.example.com-debug... To use host binaries, run `chroot /host` Pod IP: 10.1.1.1 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.2# chroot /host sh-4.4# sysctl-a | grep-E "tcp_tw_reus|ip_local_port_range" net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 1024 65535 <------- applied net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1 sh-4.4# ~~~ [Using the Node Tuning Operator](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/scalability_and_performance/using-node-tuning-operator)

title: ManagedCluster becomes unknown after major Openshift upgrade
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: ManagedCluster in Unknown state after major Openshift upgrade
resolution: 1. On the hub cluster, delete and receate the import secret: ``` oc-n $manageclustername delete secret $manageclustername-import ``` 2. On the hub cluster, once the secret is re-created, export the `import.yaml` file: ``` oc-n $manageclustername get secret $manageclustername-import-o jsonpath='{.data.import\.yaml}' | base64-d > import.yaml ``` 3. On the managed cluster, update the klusterlet manifests manually by applying the `import.yaml` file: ``` oc apply-f import.yaml ``` 4. On the managed cluster, recreate the klusterlet pods:: ``` oc get-n open-cluster-management-agent-o name | xargs oc delete ```
root_cause: * [Openshift no longer generates serviceaccount token secret as of 4.16](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/authentication_and_authorization/using-service-accounts#auto-generated-sa-token-secrets_using-service-accounts)

title: OpenShift Pipelines `Overview` and `Pipelines` menu items appears blank
issue: - In Openshift Webconsole the Overview and Pipelines menu items appear blank.- The OpenShift Pipelines Console Plugin does not work correctly from Pipelines Operator Version 1.18.x which has `results-api` enabled by default.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [SRVKP-7859](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SRVKP-7859). For more information, please open a new support case with Red Hat Support. #### Workaround 1. Delete the `tekton-results-tls secret` from the openshift-pipelines project: $ oc delete secret tekton-results-tls-n openshift-pipelines 2. Wait for sometime to get the secret regenerated. 3. If secret is taking longer time to regenerate, restart the pod `service-ca` pod from `openshift-service-ca` project: $ oc delete pod-n openshift-service-ca 4. After the `tekton-results-tls secret`is regenerated restart the `tekton-results-api-xxxx` pod.
