title: RHOCP node get deleted from cluster due to platform outage
issue: - Node gets removed from RHOCP cluster after outage at platform level.- Node is not showing up in cluster post network outage: ~~~ NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION worker1.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready egress 16d v1.27.10+28ed2d7 worker2.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready egress 16d v1.27.10+28ed2d7 worker3.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready infra 16d v1.27.10+28ed2d7 worker4.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready infra 16d v1.27.10+28ed2d7 master1.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready control-plane,master 1y v1.27.10+28ed2d7 master2.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready control-plane,master 1y v1.27.10+28ed2d7 worker5.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready worker 16d v1.27.10+28ed2d7 worker6.ocp2.chn.example.com Ready worker 16d v1.27.10+28ed2d7 ~~~ In above output `master3` is missing from cluster.
resolution: - Red Hat is adding enhancement in RHOCP for unintended node removal from cluster, currently under review in RFE [RFE-6882](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-6882). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. **Workaround**- Reboot the impacted node from platform end which will bring it back in cluster.
root_cause: The issue happens due to the behavior of the node lifecycle controller. When a node is not able to be found by the cloud controller manager and it is determined to be removed from the infrastructure by the cloud provider, then the node is removed from the cluster.

title: [AMQ Broker] How to remove messages from a queue after set time
issue: - How to remove/delete/drop the messages directly from the queue after some set time to live (expiration) without messages going to an expiry queue?
resolution: - To have messages dropped instead of going to a configured Expiry queue, there must be an empty `Expiry Address` element configured for the applicable address setting. **On OpenShift (Artemis CR)**- Put your `expiryDelay` and an empty `expiryAddress` to address where you want to drop the messages (instead of expiry). Below example shows removal of messages for *all* addresses after 1 minute (60,000 milliseconds). ~~~ spec: addressSettings: addressSetting:- match: '#' expiryDelay: 60000 expiryAddress: '' ~~~ **On premise**- Put an empty element ` ` to the ` `. Removing the element completely will not work if there is default settings of expiry queue in broker.xml (as usually is in ` `). Below example shows removal of messages for *TEST* address after 1 minute (60,000 milliseconds). ~~~ 60000 ~~~
root_cause: - The settings under ` ` establish a default set of configuration which is applied to any created queue or topic.- Therefore, if there is ` ExpiryQueue ` defined in ` ` (as it is in default broker.xml), the messages from address *without* any` ` element will use this default setting (and expired messages will not drop from the queue without ` ` element).- This also applies to OpenShift, where expiry address is [automatically created](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_amq_broker/7.13/html-single/deploying_amq_broker_on_openshift/index#con-br-how-operator-generates-address-settings-configuration_broker-ocp) during the broker pod startup.

title: While testing kdump on RHCOS node, nodes falls in to emergeny shell on reboot.
issue: - After crashing the node manually to test kdump, node fails to boot.- Node fails to boot with error `Couldn't find specified OSTree root`:![alt text](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/images/panic_0.png)
resolution: To rescue the node from boot failure, follow the below solution: [RHCOS nodes are failing to boot with an error "Couldn't find specified OSTree root" in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7128024) Before crashing the node manually to test kdump, please perform the below steps: 1. Check current deployments and ensure only one deployment exists: ```bash rpm-ostree status-vvv ``` 2. Clean older deployments manually: ```bash rpm-ostree cleanup-r ``` If it says `Deployments unchanged`, there are no deployments to be removed. 3. If the above command fails due a transaction already in progress, wait for it to complete. The pid of the of the process can be found via below command. ```bash ps aux | grep rpm-ostree ```
root_cause: - After booting into a new deployment (`boot.0)`, the `machine-config-daemon` pod runs `rpm-ostree cleanup-r` to remove the old rollback deployment `(boot.1)`. If the node is crashed or rebooted while this cleanup is in progress, the `bootloader` may not be updated correctly. As a result, GRUB may try to boot from a now-missing `boot.1`, causing boot failure.

title: How to forward OpenShift Container Platform Logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - How to configure `OpenShift Container Platform` to forward cluster logs (application, infrastructure, audit) to `Amazon CloudWatch Logs` for centralized storage and analysis.
resolution: To forward `OpenShift Logs` to `Amazon CloudWatch Logs`, the following steps are required: 1. Install `AWS CLI` (if not already present) on `bastion` or `management machine`. Refer to the [official AWS CLI installation documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html). 2. Prepare `AWS Credentials` and environment variables. Create environment variables on the `bastion` host with `AWS Credentials` and desired configuration. These credentials need IAM permissions to interact with `CloudWatch Logs` (e.g., `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents` or `logs:DescribeLogStreams`). ~~~ # Replace placeholder values with the actual AWS credentials and configuration export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=ACCESS_KEY_ID_PROVIDED_BY_AWS export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_PROVIDED_BY_AWS # export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=SESSION_TOKEN # If using temporary credentials export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 # <= Replace with desired AWS region export LOG_GROUP_NAME=openshift-cluster-logs # <= Choose a name for CloudWatch Log Group ~~~ **Note:** Ensure the `AWS CLI` is configured to use these credentials. 3. Create an `Amazon CloudWatch Log Group`. This group will receive the logs from `OpenShift Logging Operator`: ~~~ aws logs create-log-group--log-group-name ${LOG_GROUP_NAME}--region ${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION} ~~~ 4. Follow the `OpenShift Logging Operator` documentation for installing the [OpenShift Logging Operator](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/logging/cluster-logging-deploying). **(Ensure tho install the version 6.x of the `OpenShift Logging Operator`)** and It is not necessary to create an `OpenShift Logging instance` for this procedure. 5. Validate the `configmap` and `services` exists in the `openshift-logging` `namespace`: ~~~ oc get service,configmap-n openshift-logging NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE service/cluster-logging-operator-metrics ClusterIP 172.30.212.95 8686/TCP 20s NAME DATA AGE configmap/kube-root-ca.crt 1 37s configmap/openshift-service-ca.crt 1 37s ~~~ 6. Create the `secret` for `AWS Credentials` in `OpenShift`. The `ClusterLogForwarder` instance will use these credentials to authenticate with AWS: ~~~ oc create secret generic aws-cloudwatch-credentials-n openshift-logging \--from-literal=aws_access_key_id=${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID} \--from-literal=aws_secret_access_key=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY} ~~~ **Note:** If the `OpenShift cluster` is running on AWS and configured with IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA), might use an IAM role associated with the `logcollector` service account instead of creating a secret with access keys. This KCS assumes access key authentication for broader applicability. 7. Create the `ServiceAccount` on `OpenShift cluster` and include the needed `ClusterRoleBindings` for log forwarding: ~~~ oc create sa log-collector-n openshift-logging oc create clusterrolebinding collect-app-logs-for-log-collector--clusterrole=collect-application-logs--serviceaccount=openshift-logging:log-collector oc create clusterrolebinding collect-infra-logs-for-log-collector--clusterrole=collect-infrastructure-logs--serviceaccount=openshift-logging:log-collector ~~~ 8. Create the `ClusterLogForwarder` Custom Resource at `OpenShift cluster`: ~~~ cat < ` with one from the output above) and look for some data ouput: ~~~ aws logs get-log-events--log-group-name ${LOG_GROUP_NAME} \--log-stream-name--region ${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION}--limit 5 ~~~ 12. Query Logs from Amazon CloudWatch Logs via AWS CLI. To get a quick sample of logs: ~~~ aws logs filter-log-events--log-group-name ${LOG_GROUP_NAME} \--region ${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION}--limit 1--output json {"events": [{"logStreamName": "localhost.journal.system", "timestamp": 1748822137863, "message": "{\"@timestamp\":\"2025-06-01T23:55:37.863272Z\",\"TID\":\"378\",\"_RUNTIME_SCOPE\":\"initrd\",\"_SYSTEMD_INVOCATION_ID\":\"1a2c3c4d5e6f7g8hadeq135fe234fde321s\",\"hostname\":\"localhost\",\"level\":\"info\",\"log_source\":\"node\",\"log_type\":\"infrastructure\",\"message\":\"Creating group 'nobody' with GID 65534.\",\"openshift\":{\"cluster_id\":\"123456789-abcd-1234-abcd-123456789012\",\"sequence\":123456789012345678901},\"stream_name\":\"localhost.journal.system\",\"systemd\":{\"t\":{\"BOOT_ID\":\"1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i6r4de123521asde\",\"CAP_EFFECTIVE\":\"1ffffffffff\",\"COMM\":\"systemd-sysuser\",\"GID\":\"0\",\"MACHINE_ID\":\"abcde3224fds42v56thnr431sdcbf545m\",\"PID\":\"378\",\"SELINUX_CONTEXT\":\"kernel\",\"SYSTEMD_CGROUP\":\"/system.slice/systemd-sysusers.service\",\"SYSTEMD_INVOCATION_ID\":\"1q2w3e4r5t6y7u8i9oasqrew123bgfd362\",\"SYSTEMD_SLICE\":\"system.slice\",\"SYSTEMD_UNIT\":\"systemd-sysusers.service\",\"TRANSPORT\":\"journal\",\"UID\":\"0\"},\"u\":{\"CODE_FILE\":\"src/sysusers/sysusers.c\",\"CODE_FUNCTION\":\"add_group\",\"CODE_LINE\":\"1344\",\"SYSLOG_FACILITY\":\"3\",\"SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER\":\"systemd-sysusers\"}},\"time\":\"2025-06-01T23:55:37+00:00\"}", "ingestionTime": 12345825981438, "eventId": "330230354320323567307682723455543223947654769949876567200"}], "searchedLogStreams": [], "nextToken": " > "} ~~~ This will return the latest log event from any stream in the log group. It is possible to use CloudWatch Logs Insights via the AWS Console for more complex queries. At this point, `OpenShift` log forwarding to `Amazon CloudWatch Logs` should be properly configured and operational. Logs from the `OpenShift cluster` will be sent to the specified `CloudWatch Log Group` in the configured AWS region.

title: Does Red Hat provide or support the cri-o container engine for Red Hat Enterprise Linux outside of an OpenShift installation?
issue: - Does Red Hat provide independent `cri-o` engine `rpm` for Red Hat Enterprise Linux through Base or AppStream channels?- Does Red Hat support `cri-o` outside of an OpenShift Container Platform environment?
resolution: - Red Hat doesn't ship independent `cri-o` runtime Engine `rpm` package through any Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 related repositories except for the ones below.- `rhocp-4.1-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms`- `rhocp-4.2-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms`- `rhocp-4.3-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms`- `rhocp-4.4-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms`- `rhocp-4.5-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms`- The software channels above are available only when one has Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x Subscriptions. Direct/independent versions of the `cri-o` runtime engine are not shipped with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x.- Red Hat does not support `cri-o` outside of OpenShift Container Platform; `cri-o` must be part of an OpenShift Container Platform cluster in order to receive support.

title: Running RHSI 1.x and RHSI 2.x networks on the same OpenShift cluster
issue: Is it possible to run RHSI 1.x and RHSI 2.x networks side-by-side?
resolution: Yes, it is possible to run both concurrently, as the CRDs changed between versions and are not overlapping. To run both concurrently, cluster-wide operators are installed in separate namespaces for each version, for example: The skupper v1 operator is installed in the `skupper-operator-v1` namespace: ~~~ $ cat yaml/subscription-skupper-operator-v1.yaml apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: skupper-og namespace: skupper-operator-v1 spec: upgradeStrategy: Default--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: labels: operators.coreos.com/skupper-operator.skupper-operator-1: "" name: skupper-operator-v1 namespace: skupper-operator-v1 spec: channel: stable-1.9 installPlanApproval: Automatic name: skupper-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~ The skupper v2 operator is installed in the `skupper-operator-v2` namespace: ~~~ $ cat yaml/subscription-skupper-operator-v2.yaml apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: skupper-og namespace: skupper-operator-v2 spec: upgradeStrategy: Default--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: labels: operators.coreos.com/skupper-operator.skupper-operator-2: '' name: skupper-operator-v2 namespace: skupper-operator-v2 spec: channel: stable-2 installPlanApproval: Automatic name: skupper-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~ After both operators are running, it is possible to run skupper v1 sites and skupper v2 sites in separate namespaces. This is a supported configuration.

title: Downloading Virt-IO Driver for Windows 2022 in OpenShift Container Platform 4.18

Need to download the virt-io driver for adding to PXE boot image
Seeking a link to download the Windows 2022 virt-io driver for OpenShift Container Platform

title: NVIDIA gpu-operator driver daemonsets are terminated when the NodeFeatureDiscovery operator includes PCI device IDs in node labels
issue: The NVIDIA gpu-operator relies on the Node Feature Discovery (NFD) operator to apply the default node label `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true` to OpenShift worker nodes that contain NVIDIA hardware (PCI Vendor ID `10de`). If an administrator modifies the `NodeFeatureDiscovery` custom resource to include the PCI Device ID in the default `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci--.present=true` node label, it will automatically terminate an existing NVIDIA gpu-operator driver rollout and set all “nvidia.com/gpu” node resources to zero. ~~~ apiVersion: nfd.openshift.io/v1 kind: NodeFeatureDiscovery metadata: name: openshift-nfd namespace: openshift-nfd spec: workerConfig: configData: | core: sleepInterval: 60s sources: pci: deviceClassWhitelist:- "0200"- "03"- "12" deviceLabelFields:- "vendor"- "device" # <----This blocks OR terminates the NVIDIA driver daemonset rollout ~~~
resolution: If a cluster administrator needs to include the PCI Vendor ID and PCI Device ID in the default NFD node labels applied to worker nodes, they need to create a `NodeFeatureRule` specifically for discovering worker nodes containing NVIDIA hardware. ~~~ apiVersion: nfd.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: NodeFeatureRule metadata: name: nvidia-gpu-operator-nfdrule namespace: openshift-nfd spec: rules:- name: nvidia-gpu labels: feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present: "true" matchAny:- matchFeatures:- feature: pci.device matchExpressions: vendor: {op: In, value: ["10de"]} ~~~
root_cause: The NVIDIA gpu-operator relies on the Node Feature Discovery operator to apply the `feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-10de.present=true` node label to all worker nodes containing NVIDIA hardware. By default, the `NodeFeatureDiscovery` resource will create this label automatically but the cluster administrator can modify the label format for purposes outside of enablement of NVIDIA hardware which breaks the NVIDIA hardware enablement workflow.

title: [RHOCP 4]  How to Enable mTLS on Service Mesh 3 ?
issue: This article addresses how to enable mutual TLS (mTLS) on Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh (RHOSSM) version 3 in different scopes:
Enabling mTLS on specific projects (namespaces).
Enabling mTLS on all projects (mesh-wide).
resolution: #### **1. Enabling mTLS on Specific Projects** To enable mTLS for a particular project, apply the following `PeerAuthentication` resource in the target namespace: ``` apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1 kind: PeerAuthentication metadata: name: default namespace: spec: mtls: mode: STRICT ``` If **auto mTLS is disabled**, and `PeerAuthentication` is set to `STRICT`, one should also create a `DestinationRule` to enforce mTLS for all destination hosts within the namespace: ``` apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1 kind: DestinationRule metadata: name: enable-mtls namespace: spec: host: "*..svc.cluster.local" trafficPolicy: tls: mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL ```--- #### **2. Enabling mTLS Mesh-Wide** To enforce mTLS across the entire service mesh, apply the following `PeerAuthentication` resource in the `istio-system` namespace: ``` apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1 kind: PeerAuthentication metadata: name: default namespace: istio-system # namespace where the `istiod` or the `controlPlane` is deployed spec: mtls: mode: STRICT ``` Additionally, to prevent communication issues with services that do not have sidecars (like the Kubernetes API server), you must disable mTLS for those specific hosts by applying a `DestinationRule` like the one below: ``` apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1 kind: DestinationRule metadata: name: api-server namespace: istio-system # namespace where the `istiod` or the `controlPlane` is deployed spec: host: kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local trafficPolicy: tls: mode: DISABLE ``` *Note: Similar `DestinationRule` configurations should be applied for other non-sidecar services as needed.*

title: [RHOCP 4] Is it possible to disable metrics exposed at `:15090/stats/prometheus` on Istio Proxy Sidecar?
issue: Can we completely disable the metrics exposed at the endpoint `localhost:15090/stats/prometheus` on the Istio sidecar proxy (`istio-proxy`)?
This endpoint is used by Prometheus to scrape Envoy-specific metrics. Some users may want to restrict or eliminate access to this due to some reasons.
resolution: Currently, it is not possible to completely disable the `/stats/prometheus` endpoint exposed by the Envoy proxy (used by the Istio sidecar) through standard Istio configuration alone. However, the following points provide an explanation of what is and is not configurable. 1. `enablePrometheusMerge: false` Does Not Disable the Endpoint Configuration Example: ``` meshConfig: enablePrometheusMerge: false ``` **Explanation:** * This setting disables the merging of application-level metrics (those based on `prometheus.io` annotations) with Envoy metrics. * It does not remove or disable the `/stats/prometheus` endpoint itself. * Envoy will continue to expose its internal metrics at `http://localhost:15090/stats/prometheus`. 2. Disabling Istio Metrics Collection Using the Telemetry API One can prevent Istio from collecting and exporting metrics to Prometheus using a `Telemetry` custom resource: Configuration Example: ```yaml apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1alpha1 kind: Telemetry metadata: name: mesh-default namespace: istio-system spec: metrics:- overrides:- disabled: true providers:- name: prometheus ``` **Explanation:** * This configuration disables Istio-generated metrics from being collected or exposed to Prometheus. * However, Envoy metrics will still be available at the `/stats/prometheus` endpoint. * This endpoint is part of Envoy's internal metrics system and cannot be disabled via Istio config alone. * Disabling metrics collection in this way may break observability tools like `Kiali`, which rely on these metrics to visualize service traffic and topology.--- Summary * The `/stats/prometheus` endpoint is hardcoded into Envoy and cannot be disabled through Istio’s configuration. * One can disable Istio’s Prometheus integration using the `Telemetry` API, but this does not remove the endpoint or prevent Envoy from exposing metrics. * Tools like `Kiali` depend on this endpoint, so disabling it (if manually done at the Envoy level) may have side effects on observability.

title: How to configure log levels for Red Hat Connectivity Link pods
issue: How to configure log levels for RHCL pods?
resolution: ### authorino configure `spec.logLevel` of `Authorino` CR under `authorino-operator`. The log levels range `error`, `info`, `debug`. **Note**: `debug` log messages **may include sensitive information** like access tokens and API keys, and those are not redacted. ~~~ apiVersion: operator.authorino.kuadrant.io/v1beta1 kind: Authorino metadata: name: authorino... spec: logLevel: debug logMode: production ~~~ ### limitador configure `spec.verbosity` of `Limitador` CR under `limitador-operator`. The log levels range from 1 (lowest) to 4 (highest). ~~~ apiVersion: limitador.kuadrant.io/v1alpha1 kind: Limitador metadata: name: limitador... spec: verbosity: 3 ~~~ ### kuadrant-operator-controller-manager configure `LOG_LEVEL` environment variable under `spec.config.env` of `rhcl-operator` Subscription: ~~~ apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: rhcl-operator... spec: config: env:- name: LOG_LEVEL value: debug ~~~ ### limitador-operator-controller-manager configure `LOG_LEVEL` environment variable under `spec.config.env` of `limitador-operator-stable-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace` Subscription: ~~~ apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: limitador-operator-stable-redhat-operators-openshift-marketplace... spec: config: env:- name: LOG_LEVEL value: debug ~~~

title: [RHOCP 4] Helm repo mirroring failure when using `--v2` option
issue: - When running `oc-mirror` with the `--v2` option, the Helm repository mirroring fails with error `Docker references containing both a tag and a digest`.- Example command and error output: ```./oc-mirror--config=./helmimageset.yaml file:///opt/testnginx/--v2 ``` ``` 1 / 1 () [=====================================================================================================================================================================================================] 100 % () xxxxxx:v1.12.1@sha256:xxxxxxxxx cache 2025/04/11 11:25:01 [INFO]: === Results === 2025/04/11 11:25:01 [INFO]: ✗ 0 / 1 helm images mirrored: Some helm images failed to be mirrored- please check the logs 2025/04/11 11:25:01 [ERROR]: [Worker] error mirroring image regixxx.xxx.io/ingress-xxxx/xxxx:v1.12.1@sha256:d2fbc4xxxx1506e998765e86cxxxx9c34eed5b error: invalid source name docker://xxxx.xxxx.io/ingress-xxxx/xxxxx:v1.12.1@sha256:d2fbxxxxxxxx: Docker references with both a tag and digest are currently not supported 2025/04/11 11:25:01 [INFO]: Preparing the tarball archive... 2025/04/11 11:25:01 [INFO]: mirror time: 17.856017384s 2025/04/11 11:25:01 [WARN]: [Worker] some errors occurred during the mirroring. ```
resolution: * This issue is a known bug in `oc-mirror` when used with the `--v2` option. * The engineering team is aware of the problem and tracking it under [OCPBUGS-54891](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-54891). * The fix is included starting from OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) version **4.19** and has been backported to **4.18**.

title: ACS central pod reports error: "x509: negative serial number" in RHOCP4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Status of StackRox Scanner Vulnerability Definitions is "out of date".- Central pod is unable to connect to `definitions.stackrox.io` due to `negative serial number` error.- A custom certificate is not accepted with error `tls: failed to parse certificate from server: x509: negative serial number`.- How to trust a certificate with negative serial number?
resolution: There are several workarounds to this issue. In order of recommendation: 1. Substitute the custom certificate with a valid one. 2. Set the `GODEBUG` environment variable. 3. Exclude problematic addresses from ACS proxy. ### Substitute the custom certificate with a valid one Substitute the certificate returned by your proxy with a certificate with a non-negative serial number. This could also have positive effects on other applications that strictly follow the [RFC5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280#section-4.1.2.2). ### Set the GODEBUG environment variable Set `x509negativeserial=1` in the `GODEBUG` environment variable both for `Central` and `SecuredCluster` CR following this procedure: 1. Edit `Central` CR and set the `GODEBUG` variable in `spec.customize.envVars`: ~~~ $ oc-n stackrox edit Central [...] spec: customize: envVars:- name: GODEBUG <-- ADD THIS LINE value: x509negativeserial=1 <-- ADD THIS LINE ~~~ 2. Edit `SecuredCluster` CR and set the variable in `spec.customize.envVars`: ~~~ $ oc-n stackrox edit SecuredCluster [...] spec: customize: envVars:- name: GODEBUG <-- ADD THIS LINE value: x509negativeserial=1 <-- ADD THIS LINE ~~~ ### Exclude problematic addresses from ACS proxy Put `definitions.stackrox.io` (plus all other addresses affected by this issue) in `NO_PROXY`/`excludes` parameter in [ACS proxy configuration](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.7/html-single/configuring/index#configure-proxy).
root_cause: The issue is caused by custom certificates with negative serial number. [RFC5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280#section-4.1.2.2) requires serialNumber to be a non-negative integer. Several applications tolerate certificates with negative serial number, so it's possible that the same certificate works with other applications. Regarding ACS, the problem started with version 4.7. The reason is that in 4.7 Go bumped from 1.22 to 1.23 and in the latter [negative serial number are no longer tolerated](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/x509#ParseCertificate). Issue [ROX-28891](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ROX-28891) has been raised in order to consider whether the old behavior should be restored.

title: Migrating ODF from ovn-kubernetes to Multus
issue: OCP4.14 brought GA support to use ODF with Multus, customers who were reluctant to activate Multus with ODF are now interested in adopting this feature. The process of moving ODF to use Multus is a one way street, once we move from vanilla network (ovn-k8s) to Multus we can’t revert to ovn-k8s. To move back to ovn-k8s the whole ODF storage cluster needs to be deleted and re-deployed which will incur total loss of data.
resolution: 1. Verify that the multus verification tool test passes successfully. For connected environments, use [KCS #7050249](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7050249) For disconnected environments, use [KCS #7071159](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7071159) 2. Backup critical applications using OADP Operator or any other solution available. 3. Make sure you raise a preventive case before carrying out this procedure with [Red Hat support](https://access.redhat.com/support/). 4. Check the health of the storage cluster. Do Not proceed if the storage cluster is unhealthy. Make sure the ceph toolbox is running. For OCP = < 4.14 ~~~ oc patch OCSInitialization ocsinit-n openshift-storage--type json--patch '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/enableCephTools", "value": true}]' ~~~ For OCP > = 4.15 ~~~ oc patch storagecluster ocs-storagecluster-n openshift-storage--type json--patch '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/enableCephTools", "value": true}]' ~~~ Login to the rook ceph toolbox pod to check the storage cluster health. ~~~ oc rsh $(oc get pods-l app=rook-ceph-tools-oname) ~~~ Check the health of the CEPH cluster. ~~~ sh-5.1$ ceph-s cluster: id: 1201f801-a58c-400d-b405-eb630101cbd0 health: HEALTH_OK services: mon: 3 daemons, quorum a,b,c (age 2d) mgr: a(active, since 2d) mds: 1/1 daemons up, 1 hot standby osd: 6 osds: 6 up (since 2d), 6 in (since 2d) rgw: 1 daemon active (1 hosts, 1 zones) data: volumes: 1/1 healthy pools: 12 pools, 169 pgs objects: 938 objects, 893 MiB usage: 3.2 GiB used, 21 TiB / 21 TiB avail pgs: 169 active+clean io: client: 938 B/s rd, 4.2 KiB/s wr, 1 op/s rd, 0 op/s wr sh-5.1$ ~~~ Check to see if all OSDs are correctly detected by CEPH and are up. ~~~ sh-5.1$ ceph osd tree ID CLASS WEIGHT TYPE NAME STATUS REWEIGHT PRI-AFF-1 20.95560 root default-5 6.98520 host master1-cwl-site1-npss-bos2-lab 1 ssd 3.49260 osd.1 up 1.00000 1.00000 3 ssd 3.49260 osd.3 up 1.00000 1.00000-7 6.98520 host master2-cwl-site1-npss-bos2-lab 2 ssd 3.49260 osd.2 up 1.00000 1.00000 5 ssd 3.49260 osd.5 up 1.00000 1.00000-3 6.98520 host master3-cwl-site1-npss-bos2-lab 0 ssd 3.49260 osd.0 up 1.00000 1.00000 4 ssd 3.49260 osd.4 up 1.00000 1.00000 sh-5.1$ ~~~ At this stage, the storage cluster's pods are only attached to the default "cluster network" i.e. ovn-k8s network. ~~~ $ oc get network cluster-ojsonpath='{.spec.clusterNetwork}{"\n"}' | jq-r [{"cidr": "10.128.0.0/14", "hostPrefix": 23}, {"cidr": "1001:1::/48", "hostPrefix": 64}] ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get pods-l app=rook-ceph-osd-ocustom-columns=Name:.metadata.name,Networks:.status.podIPs[*] Name Networks rook-ceph-osd-0-744b8c9b6c-mgjsr map[ip:10.129.0.55],map[ip:1001:1:0:2::37] rook-ceph-osd-1-ff97895d-gqrcm map[ip:10.128.0.73],map[ip:1001:1:0:1::49] rook-ceph-osd-2-6bc9986f99-q5fdg map[ip:10.129.0.56],map[ip:1001:1:0:2::38] rook-ceph-osd-3-7c77c4c77c-fx9f4 map[ip:10.131.0.104],map[ip:1001:1:0:4::68] rook-ceph-osd-4-645f8bd76c-6zpf9 map[ip:10.128.0.74],map[ip:1001:1:0:1::4a] rook-ceph-osd-5-74c7b49598-fdzgv map[ip:10.131.0.115],map[ip:1001:1:0:4::73] $ ~~~ 5. Provision a new test project, let’s call it test-odf. ~~~ oc new-project test-odf ~~~ Get the default secret associated with this namespace ~~~ oc get secret-n test-odf | grep default-token | awk '{print $1}' ~~~ In this new project, spin up a new pod using the following manifest. ~~~ kind: Pod apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: test-pod namespace: test-odf annotations: openshift.io/scc: anyuid spec: restartPolicy: Always serviceAccountName: default priority: 0 schedulerName: default-scheduler enableServiceLinks: true terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority nodeName: worker1.cwl-site1.npss.bos2.lab <--- Change to one of the worker nodes. securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: 's0:c26,c0' containers:- resources: {} terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log name: test-pod securityContext: capabilities: drop:- MKNOD imagePullPolicy: Always volumeMounts:- name: pvc-testfile mountPath: /mnt- name: default-token-98crd ← Change to the default secret readOnly: true mountPath: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount terminationMessagePolicy: File image: quay1.apps.mgmt1.npss.bos2.lab/ocp/ocp4/ubi8/ubi:latest <--- In case of disconnected deployment, if it is a connected deployment use registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi:latest args:- /bin/sh- '-c'- | while true; do echo "Bart Bucks are not legal tender." > > /mnt/messages; sleep20; done serviceAccount: default volumes:- name: pvc-testfile persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: pvc-testfile- name: default-token-98crd ← Change to the default secret secret: secretName: default-token-98crd <--- Change to the default secret defaultMode: 420 dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst ~~~ Prepare a manifest for the PVC to be consumed by the pod ~~~ kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: pvc-testfile namespace: test-odf annotations: pv.kubernetes.io/bind-completed: 'yes' pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller: 'yes' volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com volume.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com finalizers:- kubernetes.io/pvc-protection spec: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 1Gi storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd volumeMode: Filesystem ~~~ Deploy the manifests ~~~ oc apply-f pvc-test.yml-f test-pod.yml ~~~ Make sure the pod is Running, this pod will be using the default ovn-k8s network ~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE test-pod 1/1 Running 0 28s $ oc get pvc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE pvc-testfile Bound pvc-10a15360-722b-4dc2-8bdb-7e86cd635624 1Gi RWO ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd 3m2s $ ~~~ connect to the test pod ~~~ $ oc exec-it test-pod-- /bin/bash [root@test-pod /]# ~~~ Write a file under /mnt directory, this file will be used to make sure there is no data corruption after migration ~~~ [root@test-pod /]# cd /mnt [root@test-pod mnt]# ls-lth total 351M-rw-r--r--. 1 root 1001120000 350M May 26 13:19 testfile drwxrws---. 2 root 1001120000 16K May 26 13:19 lost+found [root@test-pod mnt]# echo "I hope I don't get corrupted" > message [root@test-pod mnt]# ls-lth total 351M-rw-r--r--. 1 root 1001120000 30 May 26 13:22 message-rw-r--r--. 1 root 1001120000 350M May 26 13:19 testfile drwxrws---. 2 root 1001120000 16K May 26 13:19 lost+found [root@test-pod mnt]# cat message I hope I don't get corrupted [root@test-pod mnt]# ~~~ 6. Provision two networks: odf-cluster that will be used to replicate storage traffic among the storage nodes and odf-public that will be used by the workloads to mount their PVCs. These two networks should be layer-2/ Non-routable networks. 7. Verify that the two networks (odf-public & odf-cluster) are layer-2 networks. In this example, we are using the following networks: odf_public: bond1.63 10.0.63.0/24 odf_cluster: bond1.64 10.0.64.0/24 8. To verify these two networks are layer-2 (no routing involved based on IP addresses) we will provision two test pods that will use both of these networks, however, we will force the pods to use IP addresses outside of the CIDR provisioned on the network side, this is enough to guarantee the networks are created as layer-2 Provision a test-nameSpace (test-odf), skip this step if already created in step (5). ~~~ oc new-project test-odf ~~~ Provision a new Node Network Configuration Policy (NNCP) for the worker nodes that will connect workloads to the ODF using odf-public network. ~~~ apiVersion: nmstate.io/v1 kind: NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy metadata: name: odf-policy #namespace: spec: nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: '' desiredState: interfaces:- name: bond1.63 type: vlan state: absent mtu: 8950 vlan: base-iface: bond1 id: 63 ipv4: enabled: false ipv6: enabled: false ~~~ Provision a new Node Network Configuration Policy (NNCP) for the storage nodes that will connect ODF pods to both (odf-public) & (odf-cluster). In this example, the master nodes are used for storage as well. ~~~ apiVersion: nmstate.io/v1 kind: NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy metadata: name: odf-policy #namespace: spec: nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/master: ‘’ desiredState: interfaces:- name: bond1.63 type: vlan state: absent mtu: 8950 vlan: base-iface: bond1 id: 63 ipv4: enabled: false ipv6: enabled: false- name: bond1.64 type: vlan state: up mtu: 8950 vlan: base-iface: bond1 id: 64 ipv4: enabled: false ipv6: enabled: false ~~~ Provision a net-attach-def in the test-odf nameSpace but using fake IP addresses to confirm Layer-2 configuration on the switches. ~~~ $ cat odf-fake-nad-public.yaml apiVersion: "k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1" kind: NetworkAttachmentDefinition metadata: name: odf-public namespace: test-odf spec: config: '{"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "type": "macvlan", "master": "bond1.63", "mode": "bridge", "ipam": {"type": "whereabouts", "range": "192.168.20.0/24"}}' ~~~ ~~~ $ cat odf-fake-nad-cluster.yaml apiVersion: "k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1" kind: NetworkAttachmentDefinition metadata: name: odf-cluster namespace: test-odf spec: config: '{"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "type": "macvlan", "master": "bond1.64", "mode": "bridge", "ipam": {"type": "whereabouts", "range": "192.168.10.0/24"}}' $ ~~~ ~~~ oc apply-f odf-fake-nad-cluster.yaml-f odf-fake-nad-public.yaml ~~~ Get the default secret associated with this namespace ~~~ oc get secret-n test-odf | grep default-token | awk '{print $1}' ~~~ Create the first test pod ~~~ $ cat pod-net-1.yml kind: Pod apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: pod-net-1 namespace: test-odf annotations: openshift.io/scc: anyuid k8s.v1.cni.cncf.io/networks: '[{"name":"odf-public","namespace":"test-odf"},{"name":"odf-cluster","namespace":"test-odf"}]' <--- Needed annotation for the Pod to get assigned to needed secondary networks spec: restartPolicy: Always serviceAccountName: default priority: 0 schedulerName: default-scheduler enableServiceLinks: true terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority nodeName: worker1.cwl-site1.npss.bos2.lab <-- Replace by one of the worker nodes securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: 's0:c26,c0' containers:- resources: {} terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log name: test-pod securityContext: capabilities: drop:- MKNOD imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent volumeMounts:- name: default-token-gfbls <--- Use default secret in the nameSpace readOnly: true mountPath: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount terminationMessagePolicy: File image: quay1.apps.mgmt1.npss.bos2.lab/ocp/ocp4/rhel8/support-tools:latest <--- In case of disconnected deployment, if it is a connected deployment use registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi:latest args:- /bin/sh- '-c'- | while true; do echo "Bart Bucks are not legal tender." > > /mnt/messages; sleep20; done serviceAccount: default volumes:- name: default-token-gfbls <--- Use default secret in the nameSpace secret: secretName: default-token-gfbls <--- Use default secret in the nameSpace defaultMode: 420 dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst $ ~~~ Create the second test-pod (pod-net-2) ~~~ $ cat pod-net-2.yml kind: Pod apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: pod-net-2 namespace: test-odf annotations: openshift.io/scc: anyuid k8s.v1.cni.cncf.io/networks: '[{"name":"odf-public","namespace":"test-odf"},{"name":"odf-cluster","namespace":"test-odf"}]' <--- Needed annotation for the Pod to get assigned to needed secondary networks spec: restartPolicy: Always serviceAccountName: default priority: 0 schedulerName: default-scheduler enableServiceLinks: true terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority nodeName: worker2.cwl-site1.npss.bos2.lab <-- Replace by one of the worker nodes, preferably another worker other than the one used to run test-pod-1 securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: 's0:c26,c0' containers:- resources: {} terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log name: test-pod securityContext: capabilities: drop:- MKNOD imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent volumeMounts:- name: default-token-gfbls <--- Use default secret in the nameSpace readOnly: true mountPath: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount terminationMessagePolicy: File image: /bin/sh- '-c'- | while true; do echo "Bart Bucks are not legal tender." > > /mnt/messages; sleep20; done serviceAccount: default volumes:- name: default-token-gfbls <--- Use default secret in the nameSpace secret: secretName: default-token-gfbls <--- Use default secret in the nameSpace defaultMode: 420 dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst ~~~ Apply both manifests to provision pods (pod-net-1) & (pod-net-2) in the (test-odf) nameSpace ~~~ oc apply-f pod-net-1.yml-f pod-net-2.yml ~~~ Make sure that both test pods are running ~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE pod-net-1 1/1 Running 0 4m57s pod-net-2 1/1 Running 0 3m2s $ ~~~ Remote shell to the first test pod/test-pod-1 ~~~ [cwl@bastion ~]$ oc exec-it pod-net-1-- /bin/bash [root@pod-net-1 /]# ~~~ Find the IP address assigned to each test pod using below format ~~~ $ oc get overlappingrangeipreservations.whereabouts.cni.cncf.io-n openshift-multus-ocustom-columns=Name:.metadata.name,IPaddress:.spec.podref | grep test 192.168.10.1 test-odf/pod-net-1 192.168.10.2 test-odf/pod-net-2 192.168.20.1 test-odf/pod-net-1 192.168.20.2 test-odf/pod-net-2 $ ~~~ Curl the IP address of pod-net-2 from pod-net-1, the ping test should be successful ~~~ [root@pod-net-1 /]# ping 192.168.10.2 PING 192.168.10.2 (192.168.10.2) 56(84) bytes of data. 64 bytes from 192.168.10.2: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=0.273 ms 64 bytes from 192.168.10.2: [root@pod-net-2 /]# ~~~ 9. Delete the test pods (pod-net-1 & pod-net-2). ~~~ $ oc get pods NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE pod-net-1 1/1 Running 0 16m pod-net-2 1/1 Running 0 14m $ oc delete pod pod-net-{1,2} pod "pod-net-1" deleted pod "pod-net-2" deleted ~~~ 10. Move to the openshift-storage namespace and save a copy of the StorageCluster object to your local machine. ~~~ oc project openshift-storage ~~~ ~~~ oc get StorageCluster-oyaml > storage-cluster-backup.yml ~~~ 11. Provision both (odf-cluster) and (odf-public) network attachment definitions in the openshift-storage nameSpace. ~~~ $ cat odf-nad-cluster.yaml apiVersion: "k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1" kind: NetworkAttachmentDefinition metadata: name: odf-cluster namespace: openshift-storage spec: config: '{"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "type": "macvlan", "master": "bond1.64", "mode": "bridge", "ipam": {"type": "whereabouts", "range": "10.0.64.0/24"}}' $ ~~~ ~~~ $ cat odf-nad-public.yaml apiVersion: "k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1" kind: NetworkAttachmentDefinition metadata: name: odf-public namespace: openshift-storage spec: config: '{"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "type": "macvlan", "master": "bond1.63", "mode": "bridge", "ipam": {"type": "whereabouts", "range": "10.0.63.0/24"}}' $ ~~~ ~~~ oc apply-f odf-nad-public.yaml-f odf-nad-cluster.yaml ~~~ 12. Edit the StorageCluster Object by adding the following lines under the network part. ~~~ network: connections: encryption: {} multiClusterService: {} provider: multus selectors: cluster: openshift-storage/odf-cluster public: openshift-storage/odf-public ~~~ 13. All the pods in the openshift-storage nameSpace will start rebooting one after the other. 14. Observe the progress of the storage cluster migration. ~~~ oc get event-w--sort-by.metadata.creationTimestamp-n openshift-storage ~~~~ On a separate window, run the watch command. ~~~ watch-n0.2 "oc get pods-n openshift-storage" ~~~ 15. title: Pod stuck in "Init:CreateContainerError" state with message "no such file or directory"
issue: - Application workload pod stuck in `Init:CreateContainerError`.- It is possible to see the following error in the pod manifest: ~~~ state: waiting: message: 'relabel failed /var/lib/kubelet/pods/[...]/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/oneagent-bin/mount: readdirent /var/lib/kubelet/pods/[...]/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/oneagent-bin/mount: no such file or directory' reason: CreateContainerError ~~~
resolution: - Check if the Dynatrace CSI is currently being used by checking the pod manifest. It should look like the following snippet: ~~~ volumes:...- csi: driver: csi.oneagent.dynatrace.com readOnly: false volumeAttributes: dynakube: dynakube mode: app retryTimeout: 10m0s name: oneagent-bin ~~~- Check in the namespace where Dynatrace is deployed the logs of the `dynatrace-oneagent-csi-driver-...` pods to find the mount call. The log message should look like this: ~~~ 2025-07-10T23:22:35.509026461Z {"level":"info","ts":"2025-07-10T23:22:35.508Z","logger":"csi-driver","msg":"publishing volume","csiMode":"app","target":"/var/lib/kubelet/pods/[...]/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/oneagent-bin/mount","fstype":"","readonly":false,"volumeID":"csi-[...]","attributes":{"csi.storage.k8s.io/ephemeral":"true","csi.storage.k8s.io/pod.name":" ","csi.storage.k8s.io/pod.namespace":" ","csi.storage.k8s.io/pod.uid":" ","csi.storage.k8s.io/serviceAccount.name":" ","dynakube":"dynakube","mode":"app","retryTimeout":"10m0s"},"mountflags":[]} ~~~- The above is proof that the cause for the issue should be investigated on the Dynatrace side as this is something related to their CSI.

title: Error generating deleteSetImageConfiguration manifest by using oc-mirror v2 in RHOCP 4
issue: - Encountering an issue creating the delete file manifest using oc-mirror v2.- While running `oc-mirror` command to generate `delete manifest` its throwing below error: ~~~ [ERROR]: collection error: collect catalog "registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.16": reading manifest v4.16 in localhost:55000/redhat/redhat-operator-index: manifest unknown ~~~
resolution: For clearing cache use `--cache-dir` parameter while running `oc-mirror` for generating delete manifest: ~~~ $ oc-mirror delete--v2--config=.yaml--workspace file://///--cache-dir--generate docker:// ~~~
root_cause: This was caused due to issue in cache `localhost:55000/redhat/redhat-operator-index: manifest unknown`.

title: Users from LDAP group unable to create ArgoCD resources in OpenShift GitOps with error 'invalid RBAC policy'
issue: Users belonging to an LDAP group cannot create resources using ArgoCD.
Despite correct group membership, actions were denied for users in the CN=RHACM_Admin,... LDAP group.
The error message observed in logs indicate: `invalid RBAC policy: g, CN=...,..., role:my-role`
resolution: 1. In an environment with authentication managed by OpenShift OAuth with Dex as identity provider and RBAC configured via ArgoCD CR (`argocd-rbac-cm` ConfigMap) ensure the RBAC policy in the ArgoCD resource references the LDAP groups using double quotes: `oc edit argocd-n openshift-gitops` 2. If necessary update the RBAC policy field to include the correct LDAP group in quotes ```yaml spec: rbac: policy: | g, system:cluster-admins, role:admin g, cluster-admins, role:admin g, "CN=LDAP_Admin_Group,OU=GitOps_Groups,OU=Departments,OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com", role:admin scopes: '[groups]' ```
root_cause: Generally in YAML format a string does not need double quotes, except when special characters are present, such as `=` in LDAP Distinguished Names (DNs),

title: Unable to Sync ACM Managed Clusters in ArgoCD due to Certificate Failure: failed to verify certificate: x509
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - After upgrading to RHACM 2.13.2 and Openshift GitOps 1.16.0, some ArgoCD applications have an unknown sync status and ApplicationSet CRs are missing.
resolution: - The Red Hat Engineering Team has released a hotfix errata for this issue at [https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:4435](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:4435) (RHACM 2.13.2)- If you are able to upgrade your ACM, upgrade to version 2.13.3 or newer one, which contain the fix. In other cases, follow instruction to install hotfix.- To apply the hotfixed image to a running ACM environment you need to manually substitute in its values into the Advanced Cluster Management CSV object within the `open-cluster-management` namespace.- Edit the Advanced Cluster Management CSV ~~~ oc edit csv advanced-cluster-management.v2.13.2-n open-cluster-management ~~~- Locate instances of the multicloud-integrations image and replace it with the hotfixed image taken from the Errata notice- For example, on x86_64: ~~~- image: registry.redhat.io/rhacm2/multicloud-integrations-rhel9@sha256:fea090059b37ec98ffe4e56ab27155a5341bef75ba75a3e9e7060aa61c75e650 name: multicloud_integration ~~~ and ~~~- name: OPERAND_IMAGE_MULTICLOUD_INTEGRATIONS value: registry.redhat.io/rhacm2/multicloud-integrations-rhel9@sha256:fea090059b37ec98ffe4e56ab27155a5341bef75ba75a3e9e7060aa61c75e650 ~~~ Should be edited to ~~~- image: registry.redhat.io/rhacm2/multicloud-integrations-rhel9@sha256:9f269ad2b2b97bf4c5a5ae7b39876ac49b4ce306bbe981946a595a21316dac53 name: multicloud_integration ~~~ and ~~~- name: OPERAND_IMAGE_MULTICLOUD_INTEGRATIONS value: registry.redhat.io/rhacm2/multicloud-integrations-rhel9@sha256:9f269ad2b2b97bf4c5a5ae7b39876ac49b4ce306bbe981946a595a21316dac53 ~~~- Following the change in the CSV you should see the `multiclusterhub-operator` pods within project `open-cluster-management` restart and begin propagating the new image across ACM. This process can take 5-10 minutes to complete.- To avoid the removal of ApplicationSet objects in the future when ArgoCD cluster secrets become invalid you may set the `applicationsSync: create-update` parameter as shown in the example below. ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: ApplicationSet metadata: name: bgdk-app-set namespace: openshift-gitops spec: syncPolicy: applicationsSync: create-update- clusterDecisionResource: configMapRef: acm-placement labelSelector: matchLabels: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/placement: all-openshift-clusters ~~~
root_cause: The issue is due to failed certificate verification for managed clusters, specifically "tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority".

title: The Jenkins Pipelines  have disappeared from the Jenkins Dashboard in OpenShift 4
issue: After updating OpenShift, the Jenkins jobs are missing.
All Jenkins Pipelines were deleted.
Jenkins dashboard is not showing any of the jobs.
The Jenkins Pipelines and their logs were lost.
resolution: Check the `Diagnostic Steps` section to confirm the jobs status and reach out to Red Hat support confirming whether the Jenkins jobs were deleted from the filesystem or are just not showing in the Jenkins dashboard.
root_cause: This issue can be caused by some Jenkins plugin not being properly started. Some common root causes for Jenkins plugins not being loaded are: * Unsatisfied plugin dependencies. * Jenkins version not being compatible with the installed plugins.

title: Kopia failed to take backup of volume provisioned via HPE CSI Driver
issue: - Kopia backup with OADP failed with error when backend storage is provided by HPE. ``` level=error msg="Async fs backup data path failed" dataupload= error="Failed to run kopia backup: unable to get local block device entry: resolveSymlink: lstat /dev/dm-16: no such file or directory" logSource="/remote-source/velero/app/pkg/controller/data_upload_controller.go:414" ```
resolution: - This has been identified as a know [issue](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OADP-5028) due to default configuration/working of third party CSI storage provider.- Check with CSI driver vendor if their CSI driver can be configured to create block volume device files under `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` instead of any other path such as `/dev`.
root_cause: - The cause of the failure seems to be in the location in which the configured HPE CSI driver is placing the block device files for the block volumes. The key difference is that the RH provided CSI driver is creating the device files under `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` on the node (and symlinking them to the entry in `/var/lib/kubelet/pods`) while the Third party CSI driver (in this case HPE) is creating the device files under `/dev` on the node (and again symlinking them to the entry in `/var/lib/kubelet/pods`).- Note that the OADP/Velero node agent runs a privileged pod using mount propagation to access volumes mounted by other pods on the same node. The volumeDevices entries for block volumes (and volumes entries for filesystem volumes) under `/var/lib/kubelet/pods` are mounted in the node agent pod under `/host_pods`. In addition, the velero configuration also mounts the contents of `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` from the node using the same path in the pod.- Backup with RH provided CSI works fine for OADP, since the backup process in the node agent pod is able to follow the symlink from `/host_pods` to `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` and access the device file. However, in the HPE CSI driver case, when the backup process on the node agent encounters the symlink to `/var/dm-??`, the result is a not found error, since the CSI-driver-created device files under `/dev` are not exported to the node agent pod container.

title: Secret name cloud-credentials is missing data for key aws
issue: - OADP `BackupStorageLocation` Phase `Unknown` due to secret missing.
resolution: Create/Verify confirm if secret named `cloud-credentials` present. For example if using aws refer[official documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/oadp-application-backup-and-restore#oadp-creating-default-secret_installing-oadp-aws) ``` Create a credentials-velero file: $ cat < < EOF >./credentials-velero [default] aws_access_key_id= aws_secret_access_key= EOF ``` ``` oc create secret generic cloud-credentials-n openshift-adp--from-file cloud=credentials-velero ```
root_cause: Secret named `cloud-credentials` was missing from namespace `openshift-adp`.

title: How to reach services on different clusters in OpenShift Service Mesh 3
issue: In a [multi-primary multi-network mesh topology](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_mesh/3.0/html/installing/ossm-multi-cluster-topologies#ossm-installing-multi-primary-multi-network-mesh_ossm-multi-cluster-topologies) on two OpenShift Container Platform clusters `c1` and `c2`, DNS resolution of Kubernetes services across clusters only works in certain scenarios (described below). #### Scenario 1 Assume a pod `app1` and service `svc1` in namespace `ns1` on cluster `c1`, as well as a pod `app2` and service `svc2` in namespace `ns2` on cluster `c2`. Pod `app1` now wants to communicate with pod `app2` via service `svc2`. The following drawing attempts to illustrate the situation: ``` ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ Cluster c1 │ │ Cluster c2 │ │ ┌──────────────────┐ │ │ ┌──────────────────┐ │ │ │ Namespace ns1 │ │ │ │ Namespace ns2 │ │ │ │ ┌──────────┐ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Pod app1 │ │ │ │ │ │ Pod app2 │ │ │ │ │ └──────────┘ │ │ │ │ └──────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Service svc1 │ │ │ │ │ │ Service svc2 │ │ │ │ │ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ │ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ └──────────────────┘ │ │ └──────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────┘ ``` In this scenario, pod `app1` is not able to communicate with service `svc2` due to failing DNS resolution. Executing the following `curl` command inside pod `app1` fails with the following error message: ``` $ curl-v http://svc2.ns2.svc.cluster.local:8080/
Could not resolve host: svc2.ns2.svc.cluster.local

shutting down connection #0 curl: (6) Could not resolve host: svc2.ns2.svc.cluster.local ``` #### Scenario 2 For the second scenario, assume the same setup as in the first scenario with the addition of service `svc2` in namespace `ns2` on cluster `c1`, as follows: ``` ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ Cluster c1 │ │ Cluster c2 │ │ ┌──────────────────┐ │ │ ┌──────────────────┐ │ │ │ Namespace ns1 │ │ │ │ Namespace ns2 │ │ │ │ ┌──────────┐ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Pod app1 │ │ │ │ │ │ Pod app2 │ │ │ │ │ └──────────┘ │ │ │ │ └──────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Service svc1 │ │ │ │ │ │ Service svc2 │ │ │ │ │ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ │ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ └──────────────────┘ │ │ └──────────────────┘ │ │ ┌──────────────────┐ │ └──────────────────────┘ │ │ Namespace ns2 │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Service svc2 │ │ │ │ │ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ └──────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────┘ ``` In this case, pod `app1` can successfully communicate with pod `app2` via service `svc2`. Is there a way to make Kubernetes services that are part of the same mesh accessible without all namespaces and services having to exist on both clusters at the same time?
resolution: Enable DNS proxying on the applicable service meshes by adding the following definition to the Istio custom resources in question: ``` apiVersion: sailoperator.io/v1 kind: Istio metadata: name:... spec: values: meshConfig: defaultConfig: proxyMetadata: ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE: 'true' ```
root_cause: In contrast to OpenShift Service Mesh 2, DNS proxying is no longer enabled by default in OpenShift Service Mesh 3. This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [OSSM-9894](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSSM-9894). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

interface: timed out waiting for OVS port binding (ovn-installed) for 02:a1:3b:00:00:70 []... ~~~
resolution: There is no recommended workaround nor fix as of yet, but this issue is currently being investigated in [OCPBUGS-61823](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-61823). Breaking a long list of CIDRs into multiple policies doesn't totally eradicate the issue as the effect appears to be cumulative. Simply removing the MNP doesn't remdiate the issue for new pods coming to a Ready status: it is also necessary to restart the openshift-ovn-kubernetes/ovnkube-node (OKN) pod on the affected node (eg, where there are pods pending w the CNI error).
root_cause: The usage of EXCEPT in the IPBLOCK stanza can cause issues for clusterNetworks due to the number of OpenFlows created for a large array of CIDRs listed: this is a scaling issue for component. For the smaller lists that do work, it has been noted that the time needed to process the policy increases when CIDRs are added to an existing list. OVN engineering notes that single massive except policies are considered an anti-pattern because of the number of OpenFlow rules generated. The process of OVN generating and processing these rules takes too long, leading to a timeout. When this condition is active, all clusterNetworking can be effected as all requests to add ports to the CNI will be impacted even when the MNP at issue is for a secondary network.

title: Enable debugging for OpenStack services in Red Hat OpenStack Platform 12 to 14
issue: - How to enable debugging for OpenStack services in Red Hat OpenStack Platform 12 to 14- How to enable debug logging in RHOSP 12- How to enable debug logging in RHOSP 13- How to enable debug logging in RHOSP 14
resolution: > **Note:** For Red Hat OpenStack Platform versions from 7 to 11, please refer to [Enable debugging for OpenStack services in Red Hat OpenStack Platform 7 to 11](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1391343). > **Note:** For Red Hat OpenStack Platform versions from 15 to 17, please refer [Enable debugging for OpenStack services in Red Hat OpenStack Platform 15, 16 and 17](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6016081). > **Note:** For Red Hat Openstack Services on OpenShift 18, please refer [Enable debugging for OpenStack services in Red Hat Openstack Services on Openshift 18](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7109382). > **Note:** Debug logging by default creates large amounts of data in `/var/log` on any node where it is enabled. Debug logging should only be enabled for short durations of time and only with sufficient amount of disk space. Should Red Hat support ask for debug logging to be switched on, it should be switched off as soon as troubleshooting is over and a support ticket was closed. If Red Hat support needs debug logging for a specific service on a specific node, they will explicitly request where and for which service this setting should be enabled. ## Apply changes temporarily This method of enabling debug logging is not persistent, a re-deployment of the overcloud will revert changes back to their defaults. ### Nova #### Enable debug logging ##### Controllers ##### Set `debug` to `true` in the `nova.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/nova/etc/nova/nova.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ For OSP 13 also set: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/nova_placement/etc/nova/nova.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Nova` related containers For OSP 13: ~~~ docker ps | awk '/nova_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ ##### Computes ##### For the compute nodes set: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/nova_libvirt/etc/nova/nova.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Nova` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/nova_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ #### Disable debug logging ##### Controllers ##### Set `debug` to `true` in the `nova.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/nova/etc/nova/nova.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ For OSP 13 and later also set ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/nova_placement/etc/nova/nova.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Nova` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/nova_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ ##### Computes ##### For the compute nodes set: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/nova_libvirt/etc/nova/nova.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Nova` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/nova_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ ### Cinder #### Enable debug logging ##### OSP 12 Set `debug` to `true` in the `/etc/cinder/cinder.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /etc/cinder/cinder.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Cinder` related services ~~~ systemctl restart 'openstack-cinder-*' ~~~ ##### OSP 13 to 14 Manipulate the settings in `/var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/cinder/etc/cinder/cinder.conf`: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/cinder/etc/cinder/cinder.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Then, restart the cinder containers: ~~~ docker ps | awk '/cinder_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ Or for cinder volume in particular, one can restart the pacemaker resource: ~~~ pcs resource restart openstack-cinder-volume ~~~ #### Disable debug logging ##### OSP 12 Set `debug` to `false` in the `/etc/cinder/cinder.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /etc/cinder/cinder.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Cinder` related services ~~~ systemctl restart 'openstack-cinder-*' ~~~ ##### OSP 13 to 14 Manipulate the settings in `/var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/cinder/etc/cinder/cinder.conf`: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/cinder/etc/cinder/cinder.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Then, restart the cinder containers: ~~~ docker ps | awk '/cinder_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ Or for cinder volume in particular, one can restart the pacemaker resource: ~~~ pcs resource restart openstack-cinder-volume ~~~ ### Keystone #### Enable debug logging Set `debug` to `true` in the `keystone.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/keystone/etc/keystone/keystone.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the` Keystone` container ~~~ docker restart keystone ~~~ #### Disable debug logging Set `debug` to `false` in the `keystone.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/keystone/etc/keystone/keystone.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the` Keystone` container ~~~ docker restart keystone ~~~ ### Neutron #### Enable debug logging ##### OSP 12 Set `debug` to `true` in the `/etc/neutron/neutron.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /etc/neutron/neutron.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Neutron` related services. ~~~ systemctl restart 'neutron-*' ~~~ ##### OSP 13 to 14 Set `debug` to `true` in the `/etc/neutron/neutron.conf` configuration file: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/neutron.conf DEFAULT debug true crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/l3_agent.ini DEFAULT debug true crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/metadata_agent.ini DEFAULT debug true crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/dhcp_agent.ini DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Neutron` related services: ~~~ docker ps | awk '/neutron_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ #### Disable debug logging ##### OSP 12 Set `debug` to `false` in the `/etc/neutron/neutron.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /etc/neutron/neutron.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Neutron` related services. **This will cause a momentary loss in network connectivity to your instances** ~~~ systemctl restart 'neutron-*' ~~~ ##### OSP 13 to 14 Set `debug` to `false` in the `/etc/neutron/neutron.conf` configuration file: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/neutron.conf DEFAULT debug false crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/l3_agent.ini DEFAULT debug false crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/metadata_agent.ini DEFAULT debug false crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/neutron/etc/neutron/dhcp_agent.ini DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Neutron` related services: ~~~ docker ps | awk '/neutron_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ ### Octavia #### Enable debug logging ##### OSP 13 to 14 Set `debug` to `true` in the `octavia.conf` configuration file on the controller nodes: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/octavia/etc/octavia/octavia.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Octavia` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/octavia/ {print $NF}' | xargs docker restart ~~~ #### Disable debug logging Set `debug` to `false` in the `octavia.conf` configuration file on the controller nodes: ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/octavia/etc/octavia/octavia.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Octavia` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/octavia/ {print $NF}' | xargs docker restart ~~~ ###OVN See [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4270652](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4270652) for instructions about how to enable debug logging with OVN in Red Hat OpenStack Platform 13. ###Glance #### Enable debug logging Set `debug` to `true` in the `glance-api.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/glance_api/etc/glance/glance-api.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `glance_api` container ~~~ docker restart glance_api ~~~ #### Disable debug logging Set `debug` to `false` in the `glance-api.conf` configuration file ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/glance_api/etc/glance/glance-api.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `glance_api` container ~~~ docker restart glance_api ~~~ ### Heat #### Enable debug logging Set `debug` to `true` in the `heat.conf` configuration files ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/heat/etc/heat/heat.conf DEFAULT debug true crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/heat_api/etc/heat/heat.conf DEFAULT debug true crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/heat_api_cfn/etc/heat/heat.conf DEFAULT debug true ~~~ Restart the `Heat` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/heat_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ #### Disable debug logging Set `debug` to `false` in the `heat.conf` configuration files ~~~ crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/heat/etc/heat/heat.conf DEFAULT debug false crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/heat_api/etc/heat/heat.conf DEFAULT debug false crudini--set /var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/heat_api_cfn/etc/heat/heat.conf DEFAULT debug false ~~~ Restart the `Heat` related containers ~~~ docker ps | awk '/heat_/ {print $NF}' | xargs-I {} docker restart {} ~~~ ### Horizon #### Enable debug logging Set `debug` to `True` in the `/var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/horizon/etc/openstack-dashboard/local_settings` configuration file ~~~ DEBUG = True ~~~ Also change the handlers to DEBUG level ~~~ 'handlers': {... 'file': {'level': 'DEBUG', <=== 'horizon': {'handlers': ['console'], <=== 'level': 'DEBUG', 'openstack_dashboard': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'DEBUG', <=== 'novaclient': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'DEBUG', <=== 'cinderclient': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'DEBUG', <=== # repeat for each component that needs to be debugged ~~~ Restart the `httpd` related service ~~~ docker restart horizon ~~~ #### Disable debug logging Set `debug` to `True` in the `/var/lib/config-data/puppet-generated/horizon/etc/openstack-dashboard/local_settings` configuration file ~~~ DEBUG = False ~~~ Revert the handlers back to INFO ~~~ 'handlers': {... 'file': {'level': 'INFO', <=== 'horizon': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'INFO', 'openstack_dashboard': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'INFO', <=== 'novaclient': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'INFO', <=== 'cinderclient': {'handlers': ['file'], <=== 'level': 'INFO', <=== # repeat for each component that needs to be debugged ~~~ Restart the `httpd` related service ~~~ docker restart horizon ~~~ ### Other services For other services please refer to your specific Openstack Red Hat manual.
root_cause: > **Note:** This same method can be used for any other OpenStack service as well. However other core services will be found on the controller node.

title: Support Self-Managed OIDC JWKs in ccoctl for GCP Workload Identity Federation.
issue: - When deploying OpenShift 4.18 on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with Workload Identity Federation (WIF), the command: ~~~ ccoctl gcp create-workload-identity-provider ~~~- Creates a public Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket to host the OIDC discovery document and JWKs.- The bucket requires allUsers:objectViewer permissions, which is often blocked by default GCP organization policies.- This creates a security concern in environments that prohibit public access.- However, GCP now supports self-managed OIDC JWKs with the--jwk-json-path flag, allowing direct upload of JWKs without requiring a public bucket.
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this feature request and is being currently reviewed. If this feature is required, open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

issue: - Currently, there is no option to run existing tailored profiles defined in the Compliance Operator directly from RHACS.- Tailored profiles in the Compliance Operator currently support:- Customizing reports by silencing or suspending specific rules within a profile.- Combining checks from multiple profiles into a single tailored profile.- Extending profiles by overriding or modifying selected checks.- Currently, RHACS does not provide functionality to directly execute predefined tailored profiles, which limits reusing existing compliance configurations.
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this feature request and is being currently reviewed. If this feature is required, open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
