title: Skopeo fails to copy images from the external registry to the internal registry
issue: - Copying images from an external registry to an internal registry using Skopeo fails due to authentication errors.- Copy with either of the options--dest-creds and--dest-authfile result in the same authentication failure.- ```msg="invalid token: Unauthorized"```- ```Error uploading signature, status 401, &http.Response{Status:\"401 Unauthorized\", StatusCode:401,...."}```
resolution: 1. Make sure "system:image-builder" and "system:image-signer" roles are assigned to the service account. ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user system:image-builder-z-n $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user system:image-signer-z-n ~~~ 2. Use```--dest-registry-token``` flag to perform skopeo copy. ~~~ $ OC_TOKEN=$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token | tr-d '\n') $ skopeo copy--debug--dest-registry-token "${OC_TOKEN}"--dest-tls-verify=false "docker://${src}" "$tgt" ~~~
root_cause: Skopeo is trying to authenticate against OpenShift’s internal registry using a token that is invalid, missing, or lacks the necessary permissions. In this case, it lacks the role permissions (image-builder and image-signer) as specified in Resolution section.

title: Inconsistent memory unit display between GitHub YAML manifests and OpenShift cluster
issue: When defining VM memory values in GitHub YAML manifests using Gi units (e.g., 4.5Gi), ArgoCD syncs the configuration to OpenShift as specified. However, OpenShift converts and displays the value in Mi (e.g., 4608Mi). Similarly, if memory is defined using Mi units (e.g., 8192Mi) in the manifest, OpenShift may display it in Gi (e.g., 8Gi) after synchronization via ArgoCD.
resolution: Although there is no direct command to force ```oc``` to consistently display values in a specific unit, you can use straightforward commands to manually convert the output as needed. For example, to view the memory request for a pod in GiB, you can extract the value using jq and then perform the necessary conversion. ``` $ oc get pod-n default-l kubevirt.io=virt-launcher-o json \ | jq-r '.items[0].spec.containers[0].resources.requests.memory' 2294Mi ``` This might return 2294Mi. To convert this to GiB, you can pipe the output to a simple script using sed and awk: ``` $ oc get pod-n default-l kubevirt.io=virt-launcher-o json \ | jq-r '.items[0].spec.containers[0].resources.requests.memory' \ | sed 's/Mi//' \ | awk '{printf "%.2fGi\n",$1/1024}' 2.24Gi ```
root_cause: The behavior you're observing is based on how Kubernetes—the underlying platform for OpenShift—handles resource values. When a memory request is defined in a manifest (e.g., 2Gi or 1024Mi), Kubernetes stores it internally as a raw number of bytes, without retaining the original unit specified. When resources are viewed through the OpenShift web console or via commands such as `oc get pod`, the system converts the stored byte value into a human-readable format. It selects a unit (such as Mi, Gi, or Ki) that best represents the value for readability. As a result, a request defined as 2Gi may be displayed as 2048Mi—the underlying value remains the same, but the unit used for display may differ.

title: Why does the OpenShift Installer fail to create a cluster on AWS when using SSO credentials?
issue: - Why does `OpenShift` cluster installation on `AWS` fail with `UnauthorizedOperation` when using `SSO`?- How to use `AWS SSO` credentials with the `OpenShift Installer` to create a cluster?- Why is `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG` required for the `OpenShift Installer` to use `AWS SSO` credentials?- Why does running `openshift-install create cluster` with `AWS SSO` credentials configured via `aws configure sso` fail with an `UnauthorizedOperation` error?- Why does the `OpenShift Installer` use the `EC2` instance `IAM` role instead of `AWS SSO` credentials? Though the installer detects the `SSOProvider` credentials, it reverts to using the `EC2` instance’s `IAM` role, which does not have sufficient permissions to create the required `AWS` infrastructure.
resolution: - To use `AWS SSO credentials` with the `OpenShift Installer`, enable the `shared config` functionality in `AWS SDK v1` by setting: ~~~ export AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG=true ~~~ This requirement is documented in [AWS SDK for Go v1 – Sessions with Shared Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/v1/developer-guide/sessions.html#sessions-with-shared-config) and further explained in the [AWS blog on SSO support in AWS SDK for Go](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/developer/aws-sso-support-in-the-aws-sdk-for-go/) (refer the v1 example).- This forces the installer and `CAPA` to load and use credentials from the shared `~/.aws/config` file, including `SSO` profiles.- Rerun `openshift-install create cluster` command. The installation should complete successfully.
root_cause: - The issue is caused by a limitation in `AWS SDK v1`, used by both the `OpenShift Installer` and the `cluster-api-provider-aws (CAPA)` component.- `AWS CLI` automatically uses credentials cached by `aws configure sso` from `~/.aws/sso/cache`.- `AWS SDK v1` does not load shared configuration files by default.- As a result, the installer detects the `SSOProvider credentials`, but `CAPA` cannot access them. The credential provider chain then falls back to the `EC2` instance’s `IAM` role, which may lack permissions to create `VPCs` and other infrastructure resources required for cluster installation.

title: Degraded ODF Storage in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x due to Ceph Health Warnings
issue: - Ceph health shows warning state due to the following errors.- ```FAILED Result: hostbyte=DID_OK driverbyte=DRIVER_OK cmd_age=0s```- ```HEALTH_ERR 1 scrub errors; Too many repaired reads on 1 OSDs; Possible data damage: 1 pg inconsistent```
resolution: Check with hardware vendor for any underlying hardware issues, and replace defective hardware. Workaround: Ceph health warning can be silenced by “archiving” the crash (perhaps after being examined by an administrator) so that it does not generate this warning: To clear health warning, archive the old crash by following the step below. ~~~ $ ceph crash archive ~~~ Once the above step is performed, please verify the Ceph cluster status and verify if the health warning has been cleared after archiving the crash. ~~~ $ ceph-s ~~~ This would show the Ceph status as Ok.
root_cause: The presence of one or more of the following symptoms suggests potential hardware problems and can degrade the Ceph status. 1. Sense Key indicates that the kernel is able to send the I/O to the underlying disk and the storage is responding back with ```Defect list not found``` 2. I/O errors reported when attempting to access disk sectors. 3. The Ceph cluster has entered a HEALTH_ERR state, indicating health issues. It includes scrub errors like an excessive number of repaired reads on an OSD, and a possibly inconsistent Placement Group (PG), which may result in data integrity risks.

title: Why does 'oc adm release extract' fail with 'unexpected EOF' when downloading OpenShift installer binaries ?
issue: - What causes `oc adm release extract` to fail with `unexpected EOF` when downloading `openshift-baremetal-install`?- Why do large `OpenShift binaries` fail to download with `oc adm release extract`?- How to fix `unexpected EOF` errors when extracting `openshift-baremetal-install` using `oc adm release extract`, even though other files `extract` successfully and basic `network connectivity` appears stable?
resolution: - `Extract` on a stable network and copy the `binary` on a different system with a stable network, run: ~~~ oc adm release extract \--registry-config \--command=openshift-baremetal-install \--command-os=linux \--to /tmp/ocp-installer \ quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@sha256: ~~~- `Copy` the `binary` back to the `original system`: ~~~ scp /tmp/ocp-installer/openshift-baremetal-install user@failing-system:/path/to/destination/ ~~~- Verify the `binary`: ~~~ openshift-baremetal-install version ~~~
root_cause: - The `unexpected EOF` error occurs due to an incomplete or interrupted transfer of the large `openshift-baremetal-install` binary. Common contributors include:- Transient `network instability` (bursty or slow connections).- `Firewalls`, `proxies`, or `NAT` devices terminating long-lived connections.- The `oc adm release extract` command is more sensitive to interruptions than tools like `podman`, and lacks `robust retry handling`.

title: Why do APIRequestCount objects show zero request counts after OpenShift upgrade to 4.18 or later?
issue: - Why, after upgrading to `OCP 4.18` or later, `oc get apirequestcounts` shows zero request counts for all `APIs(REQUESTSINLASTHOUR and REQUESTSINLAST24H)`, even though workloads are actively using the cluster?- Why are `APIRequestCount` metrics empty in `OpenShift 4.18+` despite active workloads?- Why does `oc get apirequestcounts` return only zero values after an `OpenShift` upgrade?
resolution: - This is `expected behavior` and a design change introduced in `OpenShift 4.18`.- Zero values in `apirequestcount` objects for non-deprecated `APIs` are normal from `4.18` onward.- Update `monitoring/alerts` accordingly. `Stale` objects with zeros may be safely deleted or ignored.
root_cause: - The behavior of `apirequestcount` objects was changed starting with `OpenShift 4.18`:- Before `4.18` `(OCP 4.17 and older)`: `apirequestcount` objects were created for all `API` resources, regardless of `deprecation` status.- From `4.18` onward: `apirequestcount` objects are created only for `API` resources that are `deprecated` and have a defined removal version.- Impact on `upgraded` clusters `(4.17 → 4.18+)`: Old `apirequestcount` objects `remain`, but they stop updating. Their request counts drop to zero; only deprecated `APIs` with removal schedules continue to be `tracked`.

title: Migration fails while creating registried on source and target cluster
issue: - While migrating namespaces between clusters, the migration fails while creating registries in the source and target cluster.- Mig migrations has following errors suggesting labels of a registry deployment are immutable. ~~~ 'Deployment.apps "registry-4f436435-1cb5-4625-8851-9d21e2394dd7-qmf9b" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: v1.LabelSelector{MatchLabels:map[string]string{"app":"registry-4f436435-1cb5-4625-8851-9d21e2394dd7-5ttwm", "app.kubernetes.io/part-of":"openshift-migration", "deployment":"registry-4f436435-1cb5-4625-8851-9d21e2394dd7-5ttwm", "migmigration":"29b716e6-5db5-4f0a-99c5-bc64621dde8a", "migplan":"4f436435-1cb5-4625-8851-9d21e2394dd7", "migration.openshift.io/migration-registry":"True"}, MatchExpressions:[]v1.LabelSelectorRequirement(nil)}: field is immutable' ~~~
resolution: To resolve the issue, you will have to manually delete the deployment in the source and destination cluster to unblock the migration. ~~~ oc delete deployment-l migration.openshift.io/migration-registry-n openshift-migration ~~~
root_cause: - This generally happens when a older registry deployment of a successful / failed migrations is detected and has not been cleaned up automatically after migration.- The registry deployment detected by the latest mig migration refers to an registry deployment of an older mig migration uid and not the latest mig migration.

title: OpenShift reports SELinux-related conflicts when creating Pods
issue: SELinux related events observed when starting a Pod: ~~~ `SELinuxLabel ‘XXX’ conflicts with pod YYY that uses the same volume as this pod with SELinuxLabel ‘ZZZ’. If both pods land on the same node, only one of them may access the volume.` ~~~ ~~~ `SELinuxLabel ‘XXX’ conflicts with another pod that uses the same volume as this pod with a different SELinuxLabel. If both pods land on the same node, only one of them may access the volume.` ~~~ ~~~ `SELinuxChangePolicy ‘XXX’ conflicts with another pod that uses the same volume as this pod with a different SELinuxChangePolicy. If both pods land on the same node, only one of them may access the volume.` ~~~
resolution: Each event must be validated separately:- **Event: `SELinuxLabel ‘XXX’ conflicts with pod YYY that uses the same volume as this pod with SELinuxLabel ‘ZZZ’`.** Considerations: * Understand the nature of the conflict. This event indicates that the Pod associated with this event is using the same volume as Pod *`YYY`*, and they have different SELinux labels (XXX and ZZZ). This may be permissible currently, but in a future OCP release, when the SELinuxMount feature gate graduates to General Available (GA), all Pods concurrently accessing the same volume will need to have identical SELinux labels. At this point, nothing is broken, and all Pods exhibiting these events will start. This is merely preparation for a breaking change. The future OCP release will prevent cluster upgrades until all such conflicts are resolved, ensuring that an upgrade does not break existing applications. * Check SELinux labels used by the Pods reported in the event. These can be set either at the Pod level, in *`spec.securityContext.seLinuxOptions`*, or within the individual containers, in *`spec.containers[*].securityContext.seLinuxOptions`*. * An empty *`seLinuxOptions`* in unprivileged Pods means that the container runtime (CRI-O) will assign a random SELinux label to the Pod upon startup. CRI-O will then always recursively relabel all files on the Pod volumes to this unique value. Consequently, no other Pod can access the Pod’s volumes, except for privileged Pods. * Privileged containers always start with *`spc_t`* SELinux label, regardless of their SELinux label specified in Pod’s *`spec`*. Privileged containers can access any file on the host or in any other container, especially with any SELinux label. **You have 2 options to resolve this issue**: * **Option 1**: Set SELinux labels on all these Pods to the same value. Typically, by editing the owners of the Pods, such as StatefulSets or Deployments. When all Pods use the same SELinux label and the default SELinuxChangePolicy, OCP will mount the volume in constant time with the `-o context=XXX` mount option in the future OCP release and thus the Pods will start faster. * **Option 2:** Set `SELinuxChangePolicy` to `Recursive` in all conflicting Pods. This is useful when it’s impossible or undesirable to set the same SELinux labels on these Pods. For example, when a privileged Pod (running with `spc_t` label) and unprivileged Pod (running with some `cXX,cYY:s0` label) want to share data on a volume. * Using `seLinuxChangePolicy: Recursive` opts-out the Pod from SELinuxMount feature and the container runtime will keep relabeling the Pod volumes recursively. It also disables the event \+ related metrics, even when multiple Pods use the same volume with different SELinux labels. * With the privileged \+ unprivileged Pod example above, the privileged pod starts with label `spc_t` and the container runtime won’t relabel any files on the volume. When the un-privileged one starts, the container runtime will relabel all files to the Pod’s SELinux label. As a result, both Pods can access the files on the volume. But both must set their `seLinuxChangePolicy` to `Recursive`, because the mount option can’t be used. * You can set the default `seLinuxChangePolicy` at the namespace level by setting the namespace label `storage.openshift.io/selinux-change-policy` to `Recursive`. Note that it will affect only newly started Pods in the namespace: ``` $ oc label namespace storage.openshift.io/selinux-change-policy=Recursive ``` As a concrete example, consider these two Deployments, each with a single replica: 1. Deployment `myapp`, using volume `myclaim`, running with `restricted` SCC. Due to the `restricted` SCC, the Pods of this Deployment inherit their SELinux label from its namespace, say `level: s0:c27,c19`: ``` $ oc get pod myapp-545f9bb5d9-hswnp--o yaml... spec: securityContext: seLinuxOptions: level: s0:c27,c19... volumes:- name: vol persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: myclaim ``` 2. Deployment `my-privileged-app`, running a privileged container, with no explicit SELinux label and using the same PVC: ``` $ oc get pod my-privileged-app-7c79944f6-x69r9--o yaml spec: containers:- name: scanner securityContext: privileged: true... volumes:- name: vol persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: myclaim ``` While both Pods can run on OCP 4.20 and access the volume, it will not be possible when the SELinuxMount feature gate is promoted to GA. To warn users about it, OCP sends events to both of them when it detects such a conflict: ``` $ oc describe pod myapp-545f9bb5d9-hswnp... Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal SELinuxLabelConflict 45s selinux_warning SELinuxLabel ":::s0:c27,c19" conflicts with pod my-privileged-app-7c79944f6-x69r9 that uses the same volume as this pod with SELinuxLabel "". If both pods land on the same node, only one of them may access the volume. $ oc describe pod my-privileged-app-7c79944f6-x69r9... Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal SELinuxLabelConflict 45s selinux_warning SELinuxLabel "" conflicts with pod myapp-545f9bb5d9-hswnp that uses the same volume as this pod with SELinuxLabel ":::s0:c27,c19". If both pods land on the same node, only one of them may access the volume. ``` Since the user needs both Pods as they are, one unprivileged, with a SELinux label inherited from the SCC and one privileged, the user can decide to set `seLinuxChangePolicy` in both Deployments to ensure the volume is always relabelled recursively and to silence the event: ``` $ oc patch deployment myapp-p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"securityContext": {"seLinuxChangePolicy": "Recursive"}}}}}' $ oc patch deployment my-privileged-app-p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"securityContext": {"seLinuxChangePolicy": "Recursive"}}}}}' ``` Alternatively, the user can choose to default to `Recursive` policy in the whole namespace. This will affect only newly started Pods: ``` $ oc label namespace myapp "storage.openshift.io/selinux-change-policy=Recursive" ```------- **Event: `“SELinuxLabel ‘XXX’ conflicts with another pod that uses the same volume as this pod with a different SELinuxLabel.”`** This is just a variant of the previous event when the conflicting Pods are in different namespaces. OCP won’t reveal the name of the Pods, as it would allow unprivileged users to peek into other namespace Pod names. To find the exact names of the conflicting Pods, use the metric described below in Diagnostic steps. Only users with elevated privileges, such as the cluster administrator, can see the metrics.------- **Event: `“SELinuxChangePolicy ‘XXX’ conflicts with another pod that uses the same volume as this pod with a different SELinuxChangePolicy.”`** All Pods that concurrently access the same volume need to have the same *`seLinuxChangePolicy`*. * Check the `spec.securityContext.seLinuxChangePolicy` of all Pods reported in the event and make sure it’s the same. * You can set the default `seLinuxChangePolicy` at the namespace level, by setting the namespace label `storage.openshift.io/selinux-change-policy` to `Recursive`. Note that it will affect only newly started Pods in the namespace.
root_cause: Currently, the Pod SELinux label may be applied using the mount option *`-o context= `* for PersistentVolumes with *`spec.accessMode: [ReadWriteOncePod]`*. This applies the SELinux label to Pod volume in a constant time, regardless of the amount of files on the volume. For all other PVs `accessMode`, the SELinux label is applied recursively to all files on the volume, which can take a significant amount of time for volumes with many files. We plan to apply the SELinux label using the mount option to all PersistentVolumes in a future OCP release. Since a volume can be mounted with only a single such option, all Pods that concurrently access the volume will have to use the same SELinux label. In addition, the label must be known when starting the first Pod that uses the volume. OCP expects that such a change will be fine for the vast majority of applications.\` OCP reports any possible breakage with the events described above and offers cluster or application administrators to opt out from the new behavior and use the same recursive relabeling as in the previous OCP releases.

title: Cluster upgrade stuck with failed to update OS to quay.io in RHOCP4
issue: Cluster upgrade stuck with the `worker` MachineConfigPool (MCP) reporting the below error: ~~~ Reason: Status: True Type: Updating Last Transition Time: 2025-07-13T15:23:49Z Message: Node is reporting: "failed to update OS to quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:ad2174094abfb7182f223f9651d9929899a7ed5ceacf3c4eaad5c89eae687f39: error running rpm-ostree rebase--experimental ostree-unverified-registry:quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:ad2174094abfb7182f223f9651d9929899a7ed5ceacf3c4eaad5c89eae687f39: \x1b[0m\x1b[31merror: \x1b[0mImporting: proxy failure: remote error: read tcp 10.XX.XX.XX:38778-> 10.YY.YY.YY:8080: read: connection reset by peer and client error: Layer sha256:a233fe07bac5afca6f5bfaaec7e60bca65dfc8cd5495f2e6c9b9e177558916bc: unexpected end of file\n: exit status 1" Reason: 1 nodes are reporting degraded status on sync Status: True Type: NodeDegraded ~~~
resolution: Troubleshoot the issue with the default `proxy`, and confirm that the image is successfully getting pulled by following the last step from the `Diagnostic Steps` section: ~~~ # podman pull quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json Copying config 41cdef9e4d done Writing manifest to image destination Storing signatures 41cdef9e4dda189ba50e8aa56cb9c723c7c1af1e2feea22f88af43933b1eedbf ~~~
root_cause: The `proxy` has `SSL/TLS inspection` enabled, which interferes with the secure image pull from `Quay.io`, resulting in TLS handshake and blob download failures.

title: oc-mirror v2 fails with context deadline exceeded when mirroring large images to a local registry in RHOCP 4
issue: When using the `oc-mirror` plugin v2 to mirror OpenShift images, the process may fail for certain large images with errors similar to: error mirroring image docker://registry.redhat.io/rhelai1/instructlab-nvidia-rhel9@sha256:... error: copying image 1/2 from manifest list: writing blob: Patch "http://localhost:55000/v2/ /blobs/uploads/?_state=...": context deadline exceeded error mirroring image docker://registry.redhat.io/rhoai/odh-operator-bundle@sha256:aa94b4b3c494eb103665a289008c718467206ef9614f2ef3c872bb106771eb3b error: skipping operator bundle docker://registry.redhat.io/rhoai/odh-operator-bundle@sha256:aa94b4b3c494eb103665a289008c718467206ef9614f2ef3c872bb106771eb3b because one of its related images failed to mirror
resolution: - Tune the execution parameters of `oc-mirror v2` to increase timeouts and retries during the disk-to-mirror stage.- Red Hat recommends always using the **mirror-to-disk → disk-to-mirror** workflow with v2. ~~~ oc-mirror--config=imageset.yaml file:///--v2 \--image-timeout 2h \--parallel-images=10 \--parallel-layers=10 \--retry-delay=10s \--retry-times=5 ~~~ **Parameter explanation:**- `--image-timeout 2h` → allows up to 2 hours per image instead of default 10 minutes.- `--parallel-images=10` and `--parallel-layers=10` → manage concurrency for images/layers.- `--retry-times=5` and `--retry-delay=10s` → improve resiliency against transient upload For further technical detail, please refer to the official Red Hat documentation on mirroring in disconnected environments: [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/disconnected_environments/mirroring-in-disconnected-environments](URL "TITLE")
root_cause: The default behavior of `oc-mirror v2` has a default image download timeout set to 10 minutes per image and fixed concurrency. When mirroring images with very large layers, the local registry may not complete `PATCH` uploads within the default timeout. This results in a `context deadline exceeded` error from the client side, even though the source image is valid and accessible. Contributing factors may include:- Slow or remote storage backend for the registry (e.g., NFS/S3).- Reverse proxy in front of the registry with short timeouts (NGINX, HAProxy).- Large multi-GB image layers processed concurrently with insufficient retries.

title: Is it possible to migrate the Network of RHOCP from NCP to OVN-k?
issue: - Is it possible to migrate the Network of a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform from the VMWare NSX Container Plugin (NCP) to OVN-k?- Is the above migration supported by Red Hat?
resolution: - There is no supported way to migrate an RHOCP cluster from NCP to OVN-k.- It will be needed to install a fresh new cluster using OVN-k.
root_cause: - While Red Hat supports RHOCP clusters using NCP, please note that **NCP is a third-party solution**.- Support for the NCP component itself must be obtained directly from the vendor.

title: Alertmanager and Prometheus pods provided by COO failing to start when using resourcequota in RHOCP 4
issue: - Alertmanager and Prometheus pods failing to start when using `resourcequota` in the namespace: ~~~ create Pod alertmanager-example-monitoring-stack-0 in StatefulSet alertmanager-example-monitoring-stack failed error: pods "alertmanager-example-monitoring-stack-0" is forbidden: failed quota: namespace-quota: must specify limits.cpu for: alertmanager; limits.memory for: alertmanager; requests.cpu for: alertmanager create Pod prometheus-example-monitoring-stack-0 in StatefulSet prometheus-example-monitoring-stack failed error: pods "prometheus-example-monitoring-stack-0" is forbidden: failed quota: namespace-quota: must specify limits.cpu for: thanos-sidecar; limits.memory for: thanos-sidecar; requests.cpu for: thanos-sidecar; requests.memory for: thanos-sidecar ~~~
resolution: - Edit the `alertmanager.monitoring.rhobs` object to add the resource requests and limits under `.spec.resources`: ~~~ $ oc edit alertmanager.monitoring.rhobs-n--- spec: resources: limits: cpu: 250m memory: 1Gi requests: cpu: 100m memory: 512Mi--- ~~~- Edit the `prometheus.monitoring.rhobs` object to add the resource requests and limits under `.spec.thanos.resources`: ~~~ $ oc edit prometheus.monitoring.rhobs-n--- spec: thanos: resources: limits: cpu: 250m memory: 1Gi requests: cpu: 100m memory: 512Mi--- ~~~- A bug [COO-1063](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/COO-1063) has been opened to fix the missing default resource requests and limits on `Alertmanager` and `thanos` component in `Prometheus`.
root_cause: Missing resource requests and limits on workloads when `resourcequota` is used in the namespace.

title: After upgrading cluster from 4.14 to 4.15 getting errors as could not get ARP entries when using Calico as Network CNI
issue: - After updating OCP cluster from 4.14 to 4.15, getting the following error messages: ~~~ log:ts=2025-09-02T11:57:23.437Z caller=collector.go:169 level=error msg="collector failed" name=arp duration_seconds=0.001082927 err="could not get ARP entries: rtnetlink NeighMessage has a wrong attribute data length" ~~~
resolution: - As per [KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/652593), which is for the RTNETLINK issue, it is mentioned that the maximum length supported for a network interface name is 15 characters.- As per [upstream details](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/issues/2849) The "rtnetlink NeighMessage has a wrong attribute data length" error comes from the [package](https://github.com/jsimonetti/rtnetlink) that the collector uses to fetch the ARP cache via rtnetlink.- This is Patched in [1.8.0 node-exporter for prometheus](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/releases/tag/v1.8.0) and this got added in [4.16.0](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/MON-3847)- Upgrade your platform to 4.16.0 or later to alleviate this problem.
root_cause: - The "rtnetlink NeighMessage has a wrong attribute data length" error comes from the [package](https://github.com/jsimonetti/rtnetlink) that the collector uses to fetch the ARP cache via rtnetlink. ~~~ errInvalidNeighMessageAttr is returned when neigh attributes are malformed. errInvalidNeighMessageAttr = errors.New("rtnetlink NeighMessage has a wrong attribute data length") ~~~

title: Hosted Control Planes stuck in ValidReleaseImage because of Container Image rewrite failure

github.com/openshift/hypershift/hypershift-operator/controllers/hostedcluster.(*HostedClusterReconciler).Reconcile
	/hypershift/hypershift-operator/controllers/hostedcluster/hostedcluster_controller.go:343

Reconciling or Updates of `HostedCluster` resource is failing, when the `ImageDigestMirrorSet` does contain the actual upstream Image Registry URL as part of the repository definition like `registry.example.org/quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev`.
resolution: * This problem is being investigated by Red Hat via [OCPBUGS-62426](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-62426). Please contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact) to obtain for more inforemation or raise questions. * The problem is the `ImageDigestMirrorSet` configruation as shown below, that does contain the upstream Image Registry URL as part of the repository path that is causing the rewrite logic to match and therefore trigger additional, non required rewrites. title: CIFS/SMB share doesn't automatically reconnects upon server IP change
issue: CIFS/SMB shares mounted and referenced by DNS hostname get hanged and never reconnect if the server IP change, even if the the hostname points to a valid server ip with the correct share.
resolution: Issue is being worked on [this issue](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-59146) under Openshift umbrella, but the fix is backported from [this issue](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-105106) in RHEL
root_cause: The key is marked as permanent (e.g. no expiration), which should explain why the CIFS client isn't getting the new IP address as the key never gets revalidated. It still can be deleted/invalidated, but since dns_query() is being called by the client with @invalidate = false, it will end up getting the old and cached value. The affected kernel versions are missing important upstream commits that fixes this issue.

title: OSD(s) Fails on Devices Previously Used by LVMOperator
issue: When attempting to provision an OSD on a device previously managed by the LVM Operator, issues occur:- The OSD prepare pod fails to complete.- The prepare pod succeeds and the OSD is provisioned, but the newly created OSD pod enters a CrashLoopBackOff (CLBO) state.
resolution: 1. Delete the LVMCluster Ensure no `LVMCluster` is still managing the device(s) ``` # Verify and delete the LVMCluster oc get lvmcluster-n oc delete lvmcluster-n ``` 2. Clean LVM metadata from the node(s) SSH or debug into the worker node that holds the device(s) and run the following commands. In this example, the device is `/dev/nvme1n1`. ``` # Forcefully wipe the LVM labels from the physical volume lvm pvremove-ff /dev/nvme1n1 # Remove the device from LVM's device list lvmdevices--deldev /dev/nvme1n1 # Verify that the device is longer referenced in system.devices cat /etc/lvm/devices/system.devices ``` 3. Zap the device to prepare the device for use in ODF This procedure is detailed in Red Hat KCS article [7115651](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7115651). ``` Syntax: /usr/bin/podman run--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json--rm-ti--privileged--device--entrypoint ceph-bluestore-tool zap-device--dev--yes-i-really-really-mean-it Example: /usr/bin/podman run--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json--rm-ti--privileged--device /dev/nvme1n1--entrypoint ceph-bluestore-tool registry.redhat.io/odf4/rook-ceph-rhel9-operator@sha256:60623084100a785f7eaf4bd3a4f87de4982daa37e30849bdb0b8304d3d1b7cd5 zap-device--dev /dev/nvme1n1--yes-i-really-really-mean-it ``` If OpenShift Data Foundation is still unable to provision an OSD after applying the workaround, open a Red Hat Support case with the OpenShift Data Foundation to review.
root_cause: When an `LVMCluster` is deleted, the LVM Operator may not automatically wipe the underlying LVM metadata from the devices. This stale metadata corrupts the device from ODF's perspective, causing the OSD provisioner or the OSD itself to fail.

title: How to install the OpenShift Client Tools
issue: - I am getting started with Red Hat OpenShift and see references to "RHC Client Tools" for controlling my applications. Where can I get the tools and how do I install them?
resolution: ### OpenShift Client Tools Reference Guide The [OpenShift Client Tools Reference Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/openshift_container_platform/3.6/html/cli_reference/) is the place to start for this question, as the OpenShift client tools make it easy to create and deploy applications, manage domains, control access to your OpenShift applications, and give you complete control of your cloud environment. The subsequent sections provide instructions on how to install the client tools on supported operating systems. ### Download Client Tools To download the Client Tools, [click here](https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/290). ### Installing OpenShift Documentation To read more about installing Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) more generally, the latest [OpenShift Container Platform product documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/) can be found here. ### Public Content Red Hat OpenShift publishes a wealth of images, client binaries (both openshift-install, oc and odo) and other content to [mirror.openshift.com](miror.openshift.com). ### Images OpenShift ships images from [quay.io](quay.io) and we mirror these images to the [Red Hat Container Catalog](https://access.redhat.com/containers/).

title: Option to disable writing K8s events in Openshift Gitops ArgoCD
issue: - ArgoCD events are filling ETCD
resolution: - Starting with OpenShift GitOps 1.16.0, you can now disable the creation of k8s events by the ArgoCD controller. This feature was introduced to address [RFE-5602](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-5602).- To disable the events, you need to add the `ARGOCD_ENABLE_K8S_EVENT` environment variable to your ArgoCD custom resource.- Run the following command to edit the ArgoCD CR: $ oc edit argocd-n- In the spec.controller.env section, add environment variable. If the env section doesn't exist, create it. spec: controller: env:- name: "ARGOCD_ENABLE_K8S_EVENT" value: "none"- After you save this change, the ArgoCD controller pod will restart with the new configuration and will no longer generate k8s events for resource synchronization and health status changes.

title: Compute node unable to apply latest Machine Configuration Pool due to issues running rpm-ostree
issue: - A compute node is stuck trying to deploy the latest MCP config with the following error message: ~~~ failed to update OS to quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:cacaa2faf72f25dc690fdf8429b55ea4f91ce37e62c27c63e1a06323de7163ae: error running rpm-ostree rebase--experimental /run/mco-machine-os-content/os-content-805611229/srv/repo:ff2687741404a2ac05f03e0f2b63670d39a154b82ba61935c62de27e25513011--custom-origin-url pivot://quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:cacaa2faf72f25dc690fdf8429b55ea4f91ce37e62c27c63e1a06323de7163ae--custom-origin-description Managed by machine-config-operator: error: Timeout was reached\n: exit status 1 ~~~
resolution: After connecting to the faulty compute node (_in this example `worker-1`_) #### Set some Variables 1. Set the variable RPMOSTREE_CMD based on the content extracted in the step 2 from the Diagnostic Section. ~~~ $ RPMOSTREE_CMD="rpm-ostree rebase--experimental /run/mco-machine-os-content/os-content-805611229/srv/repo:ff2687741404a2ac05f03e0f2b63670d39a154b82ba61935c62de27e25513011--custom-origin-url pivot://quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:cacaa2faf72f25dc690fdf8429b55ea4f91ce37e62c27c63e1a06323de7163ae--custom-origin-description Manual_trigger" ~~~ 2. Set additional variables ~~~ $ MCO_FOLDER_CONTENT="/$(echo ${RPMOSTREE_CMD} | cut-d'/'-f2-4)" $ osImageUrl="$(echo ${RPMOSTREE_CMD} | awk '{print $6}' | cut-d'/'-f3-)" ~~~ Please verify that the variables are set with the desired values ~~~ $ echo ${MCO_FOLDER_CONTENT} $ echo ${osImageUrl} ~~~_As part of this example the value are:_ ~~~ $ echo ${MCO_FOLDER_CONTENT} /run/mco-machine-os-content/os-content-805611229 $ echo ${osImageUrl} quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:cacaa2faf72f25dc690fdf8429b55ea4f91ce37e62c27c63e1a06323de7163ae ~~~ #### Build the new content and apply it ~~~ $ sudo mkdir-p ${MCO_FOLDER_CONTENT} $ sudo nice-- ionice-c 3 oc image extract--path /:${MCO_FOLDER_CONTENT}--registry-config /var/lib/kubelet/config.json ${osImageUrl} $ sudo ls-l ${MCO_FOLDER_CONTENT} $ sudo ${RPMOSTREE_CMD} ~~~ once the `rpm-ostree` command will be applied, the node should reboot automatically within the next 5 minutes.
root_cause: In some case, the `rpm-ostree` command failed to create the osImage folder for the new osVersion. In this case a manual intervention may be required.

title: Multiple namespaces stuck in terminating state after SDN to OVN migration in RHOCP 4
issue: Following the CNI migration from SDN to OVN, multiple namespaces, including the debug namespaces, are stuck in `Terminating` state, even after their finalizers have been removed.
resolution: - Uninstall and re-install the `OpenShift Virtualization Operator` to remove stale or broken API groups and CRDs, by following the [Official Red Hat documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/virtualization/installing#uninstalling-virt).- Re-check the affected namespaces and if this issue still occurs in your environment, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution: ~~~ $ oc get projects | grep-iv active ~~~
root_cause: The discovery failure happens due to stale `GroupVersion` discovery for `subresources.kubevirt.io/v1` and `subresources.kubevirt.io/v1alpha3` resources. This means the API definitions for `OpenShift Virtualization` are corrupted or outdated. As the system cannot properly identify and interact with all the resources associated with these stale APIs, it cannot complete the cleanup of objects within the namespaces leaving them stuck in the `Terminating` state.

title: After RHOCP upgrade to v4.16 iptables-alerter pods are stuck in CreateContainerError state
issue: After RHOCP cluster upgrade, `network` operator stuck in progressing state.

iptables-alerter pods in the `openshift-network-operator` namespace are stuck in a `CreateContainerError` state with below error, ~~~ $ oc get pod-o yaml-n openshift-network-operator- image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:dec071164a68d135905f27e593b42be7ac14002c938fb08613c59c629c6c4f80 imageID: "" lastState: terminated: exitCode: 137 finishedAt: null message: The container could not be located when the pod was deleted. The container used to be Running reason: ContainerStatusUnknown <======= startedAt: null name: iptables-alerter ready: false restartCount: 1 started: false state: waiting: message: context deadline exceeded <======= reason: CreateContainerError <======= ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [`OCPBUGS-57501`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-57501). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. ## Workaround There are two available `workarounds`, and either can be implemented.- First: Run the following command to `disable` the `iptables-alerter` pods: ~~~ $ oc create configmap-n openshift-network-operator iptables-alerter-config--from-literal enabled=false ~~~ **Note:** This is a `temporary` workaround and `disabling` these pods will not impact cluster performance.- Second: `Migrate` from RHOCP SDN to OVN-Kubernetes by following this [`documentation`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/networking/ovn-kubernetes-network-plugin#migrate-from-openshift-sdn). **Note:** The `permanent` resolution is to `migrate` from RHOCP SDN to OVN-Kubernetes, which is the default network plugin in RHOCP post v4.16.

title: Not able to install older version of AAP operator via the web console in RHOCP4

issue: How to Set a `Non-Default` DNS View in External `DNS` Operator Infoblox?

External DNS Operator for Infoblox in RHOCP always tries to create DNS records in the default DNS view, which results in error, ~~~ time="xxxx-xx-xx:xx" level=error msg="Failed to create TXT record named 'xxxxx-xxx-xxx-xxxx' to 'xxxxx-xxx-xxx-xxxx,external-dns/resource=service/xxxx-xxx-xx' for DNS zone 'xxx-xxx-xxx': WAPI request error: 400('400 Bad Request')

" ~~~
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in RFE [`RFE-4642`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4642). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: Granting delete permission does not result in deletion of other objects within IPI installation on vSphere
issue: The documentation does not explicitly mention that the `Delete` permission will not affect any existing `non-RHOCP` resources during cluster installation.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [`OCPBUGS-51270`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-51270). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. **Note:-** Granting the `Delete` permission during `RHOCP IPI` installation on vSphere does not result in the deletion of any existing resources outside those created by the `installer`. This behavior has `no impact` on the broader production environment.
root_cause: The [`Official documentation`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/installing_on_vmware_vsphere/installer-provisioned-infrastructure#installation-vsphere-infrastructure_ipi-vsphere-installation-reqs) does not clearly state that the `RHOCP installer` only deletes its own resources. The missing information caused confusion about the possible risks to other production environment objects when `Delete permissions` are given.

title: Admission webhook warning is triggering in the node terminal for RHOCP 4 web console
issue: While accessing the node terminal from `RHOCP console` the below `warning` message observed: [image=[src="images/screenshot_from_2024-10-11_14-56-34.jpg", alt="Warning Message", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center",]] ~~~ pod master-0-debug violates policy 299- "metadata.name: this is used in the Pod's hostname, which can result in surprising behavior; a DNS label is recommended: [must not contain dots]" ~~~

Possible additional error messages might include: ~~~ "Warning: metadata.name: this is used in the Pod's hostname, which can result in surprising behavior; a DNS label is recommended: [must be no more than 63 characters]" ~~~
resolution: * Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [`OCPBUGS-52418`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-52418) and delivered a fix in `RHOCP v4.16.38` through errata [`RHSA-2025:3301`](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:3301). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. **Note:-** This is just a `warning` message, it will not have any impact on the cluster. * In some cases, this can prevent the creation of a debug shell and block administrative tasking. A `workaround` is to create a yaml file of the desired debug pod, then modify the yaml config to resolve the error and apply the required change (or rename the pod name to be smaller than a character limit, etc): ~~~ $ oc debug node/--output=yaml > debug-pod.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: annotations: ## <-- can add new labels or annotations debug.openshift.io/source-container: container-00 debug.openshift.io/source-resource: /v1, Resource=nodes/sunbro3-xfrmd-worker-eastus1-sntbp name: default-worker-1-debug ## <-- can be renamed namespace: default ## <-- can target a different namespace spec: containers:- command:- /bin/sh env:- name: TMOUT value: "900" image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:a39635594b2996a7782f6adc389a89e2dc1f983fe3f3a5c4ae3cded51557ebae name: container-00 resources: {} securityContext: privileged: true runAsUser: 0 stdin: true stdinOnce: true tty: true volumeMounts:- mountPath: /host name: host hostNetwork: true hostPID: true nodeName: worker-1 restartPolicy: Never volumes:- hostPath: path: / type: Directory name: host ~~~ * Make your changes to the `yaml` configuration and create the pod, then `rsh` into the newly created `privileged` container to achieve the same result as `oc debug node/ `: ~~~ $ oc create-f debug-pod-yaml $ oc rsh debug-pod-1a #can run chroot /host to get to host Network if needed, or just run expected tools at debug pod layer as usual like tcpdump, etc. We're in a debug node pod shell here at this state. tcpdump can be run without escalating to chroot. ~~~
root_cause: Admission controller lockout caused by missing required configuration in the default debug shell creation fails to be built. This can be fixed with an `upgrade`, or `bypass` with a manual debug pod creation from yaml file.

title: To retrieve back last 'n' number of unused machineconfigs in RHOCP4

title: Existence of   Expired Certificates in RHOCP4
issue: - Presence of the `EXPIRED` certificates in the cluster. There is `NO PENDING` csr in the cluster.- Nodes with incorrect IP configuration causes certificate invalidation.- Changing IP addresses results in expired certificates for associated pod resources.- Multiple expired certificates identified in the cluster.
resolution: - It is an expected behavior. As OpenShift Container Platform will not use the unused certificates that are expired.- The presently utilized certificates should be updated.- Delete the old certificates from the cluster. ~~~ $ oc delete csr ~~~
root_cause: The old certificates were not able to get pruned automatically. Therefore, the expired certificates are present. Yet those certificates will not be used by the cluster anymore as they have expired.

title: IPI Private cluster installation on Azure failed due to static IP not in range of subnet in RHOCP4
issue: Deploying an `Azure IPI` RHOCP cluster in a `disconnected environment` is failing with the following error: ~~~ time="xxxx-xx-xxx" level=fatal msg="failed to fetch Cluster: failed to fetch dependency of \"Cluster\": failed to generate asset \"Cluster API Manifests\": failed to generate Azure manifests: failed to get azure ip availability: network.VirtualNetworksClient#CheckIPAddressAvailability: Failure responding to request: StatusCode=400-- Original Error: autorest/azure: Service returned an error. Status=400 Code=\"PrivateIPAddressNotInAnySubnet\" Message=\"Private static IP address xx.x.x.xxx does not belong to the range of any subnet in the virtual network /subscriptions/ /resourceGroups/ /providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/ \" Details=[]" ~~~
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [`OCPBUGS-43724`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-43724) and delivered a fix in `RHOCP v4.19` through errata [`RHBA-2025:3775`](https://errata.engineering.redhat.com/advisory/148001). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. The fix has been backported to the following releases: | **RHOCP version** | **Jira issue** | **Bugfixed release** | **Errata** | |-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------| | 4.17 | [`OCPBUGS-55224`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-55224) | 4.17.27 | [`RHSA-2025:4204`](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:4204) | | 4.18 | [`OCPBUGS-54947`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-54947) | 4.18.11 | [`RHSA-2025:4211`](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:4211) |
root_cause: The issue is a `bug` in RHOCP where the installer attempts to use a `static IP address` that falls outside of the `configured subnets` in the Azure virtual network. This has been identified as a regression as the same configuration works in older version of RHOCP.

title: Risks of Manually Applying sysctl Parameters on OpenShift Nodes
issue: - In a production OpenShift Container Platform environment, there is a requirement to apply **custom kernel performance tuning parameters*

(e.g., `net.core.*`, `net.ipv4.tcp_*`) to a subset of worker nodes to support a high-performance application. The proposed method is to apply these changes directly on the Red Hat CoreOS (RHCOS) nodes using the `sysctl-w` command. What are the risks associated with this manual approach and provides the supported, safe alternative?
resolution: The correct, supported, and safe method for applying runtime-tunable kernel parameters is to use the **Node Tuning Operator**. This ensures the configuration is **declarative, persistent** across reboots.- **Label the Target Nodes:** Apply a unique label to the nodes you wish to tune. This allows for precise targeting.- **Create and apply a Tuned Custom Resource (CR):** Define a new, high-priority Tuned profile that contains the desired sysctl settings and targets only the nodes with the new label. The Node Tuning Operator will now automatically and safely apply these settings to the two labeled nodes without a reboot.
root_cause: Manually applying `sysctl` changes on production OpenShift nodes is unsupported and introduces risks, with the worst-case scenario being a **hard-to-diagnose production outage after the next node reboot.**- **The Problem on Reboot:** The manual changes are not permanent. Because of this, the next time a node reboots for any reason (like a cluster upgrade, maintenance, or a crash), it will revert to its original, untuned kernel settings. Your high-performance application will then be scheduled onto this untuned node, likely causing it to fail or perform poorly, which could lead to an outage.- **Inconsistent Nodes:** By modifying only two nodes, you create servers that are configured differently from the rest of the cluster. This makes troubleshooting a nightmare, as any future issue could be caused by either the application or the undocumented, manual changes made only on that specific node. This adds significant time and confusion to every investigation.- **Resource Contention:** The aggressive new settings increase kernel memory usage for network buffers. Under high load, this can starve other critical node processes like the `kubelet` or `crio`, leading to node instability and pod evictions. The correct and safe method is to use the **`Tuned` Operator**, which applies these changes declaratively, makes them persistent, and allows you to target specific nodes without creating an unsupported configuration.

title: Is it possible to use `CronJobTimeZone` for a CronJob in OpenShift 4.12?
issue: - Set a particular timezone to a CronJob in OpenShift- How to use `CronJobTimeZone` in OpenShift
resolution: **Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content. `CronJob.spec.timeZone` is introduced from OpenShift Container Platform 4.12 which is based on Kubernetes 1.25.- OpenShift Container Platform 4.12 which is based on Kubernetes 1.25: `CronJobTimeZone` feature gate, which is a [Beta](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/#feature-stages) feature gate, is introduced and it's enabled by default- OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 which is based on Kubernetes 1.27: `CronJobTimeZone` is GA. In a CronJob you can set the `.spec.timeZone` to the name of a valid time zone. For example, setting `.spec.timeZone: "Etc/UTC"` instructs Kubernetes to interpret the schedule relative to Coordinated Universal Time. The `.spec.schedule` cron schedule syntax: ~~~ # ┌───────────── minute (0- 59) # │ ┌───────────── hour (0- 23) # │ │ ┌───────────── day of the month (1- 31) # │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1- 12) # │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of the week (0- 6) (Sunday to Saturday; # │ │ │ │ │ 7 is also Sunday on some systems) # │ │ │ │ │ OR sun, mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat # │ │ │ │ │ # * * * * * ~~~ Example of CronJob using`CronJobTimeZone`: ~~~ apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: CronJob metadata: name: hello spec: timeZone: "Europe/Madrid" schedule: "52 13 * * *" jobTemplate: spec: template: spec: containers:- name: hello image: busybox:1.28 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent command:- /bin/sh--c- date; echo Hello from the CronJob securityContext: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false runAsNonRoot: true seccompProfile: type: RuntimeDefault capabilities: drop:- ALL restartPolicy: OnFailure ~~~ There is more information about`CronJobTimeZone` usage in the official kubernetes documentation: [https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs/#time-zones](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs/#time-zones)

title: Is it supported to use Azure snapshots for backing up or restoring ARO cluster nodes?
issue: - Is it possible to take an Azure-level snapshot of cluster instances and use them to overwrite the cluster instances later?- Would this approach be supported or recommended? What are the risks, limitations, or potential issues with this method?
resolution: It is not supported to use Azure-level snapshots to restore nodes in an Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) cluster. For supported backup and restore methods:- Applications: Use OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) or save the application-related YAML manifests. In case of an issue, applications can be restored using these YAML files or OADP. **Note:**- Azure-level snapshots of cluster nodes are not a supported recovery mechanism because ARO clusters are managed, and node replacements are handled by the platform itself.- To protect applications and workloads, always rely on OADP or configuration exports (YAML files).- For cluster-level recovery scenarios, the recommended approach is to redeploy applications rather than restoring VM snapshots.

title: What timezone does CronJob use in OpenShift?
issue: - What timezone does CronJob use in OpenShift?
resolution: In OpenShift 3, CronJobs are executed based on a timezone of the master hosts. In OpenShift 4, CronJobs uses UTC. Since OpenShift Container Platform 4.9 is based on Kubernetes 1.22 it’s possible to configure `CRON_TZ` for a CronJob as explained in [this article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6447931). Starting from OpenShift Container Platform 4.12 which is based on Kubernetes 1.25 it’s possible to use the `CronJobTimeZone` [feature gate](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs/#time-zones) as explained in [this article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6995558).
root_cause: CronJob refers to the timezone of the `kube-controller-manager` process. In OpenShift 3, `kube-controller-manager` runs just as a process, and its timezone is the same as the master hosts. In OpenShift 4, `kube-controller-manager` runs as a static pod and its timezone is UTC. The pod's timezone is independent of the host, and the timezone changed by [Configuration of a custom timezone for RHCOS nodes](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5487331) is not reflected in the `kube-controller-manager` pod. Changing the timezone of `kube-controller-manager` pod is not supported. The timezone of CronJob needs to be changed by the methods described in the above resolutions.

title: must-gather service accounts (ClusterAdmin) and projects are not being deleted in OpenShift 4
issue: When running the must-gather tool, a `ServiceAccount` with the `ClusterAdmin` role and a project are automatically created. These temporary objects do not get deleted when the must-gather is aborted and (being a `ClusterAdmin`) could pop up in security scans, audits and penetration tests causing them to fail.
The namespace that is created by the `oc adm must-gather` command with the name of `must-gather-xxxxx` still exists in the cluster. Is this safe to remove it?
resolution: Check for `ClusterRoleBinding` using `ServiceAccounts` with `ClusterAdmin`: ~~~ oc get clusterrolebindings-o json | jq-r '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name == "cluster-admin")|select(.subjects[0].name=="default") |.subjects[] | select(.kind == "User" or.kind == "Group" or.kind == "ServiceAccount") |.kind + ": " +.name +":" +.namespace' ~~~ Or: ~~~ $ oc get clusterrolebindings | grep must-gather ~~~ If there is any `ClusterRoleBinding` called `must-gather-xxxxx`, it is possible to delete it: ~~~ $ oc delete clusterrolebinding [must-gather-xxxxx] ~~~ > **Note:** DO NOT delete any of the other `ClusterRoleBindings` or `ServiceAccounts`, as it can break the cluster. Starting with OpenShift 4.17, via [OCPBUGS-31848](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/OCPBUGS-31848), when the must-gather namespace is deleted, the `ClusterRoleBinding` is automatically deleted. For removing the projects: ~~~ $ oc get projects | grep must-gather $ oc delete project [must-gather-xxxxx] ~~~
root_cause: When using the must-gather tool, a `ServiceAccount` and `project` are created to run it. The account has the `ClusterAdmin` role assigned but does not get deleted when the must-gather is aborted. The `must-gather-xxxxx` namespace is a temporary namespace that is only created to start the pod that collects all the logs for the must-gather command. Since it has no other purpose, it can be safely deleted.

title: TLS Certificate Validation Failure Between API Server and Metallb Webhook Service
issue: - TLS certificate validation errors between the API server and the metallb-operator-webhook-server-service. Specifically, the API server is unable to verify the webhook's certificate and logs the following error: ~~~ failed to connect to webhook "addresspools.metallb.io" via service "metallb-operator-webhook-server-service.metallb-system.svc:443": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~- The webhook certificate is self-signed by OLM, and the Certificate Authority (CA) used by the webhook service does not match the trusted CA configured within the cluster. **Note**: The proxy CAs are not only for external consumption, they are also applied for internal consumption. However, for the situation described here, it should not be necessary to add anything to the proxy CA config, as the CA of the webhook should already be configured such that it matches the webhook one.
resolution: - If the deprecated CRD (addresspools.metallb.io) is unused, it should be removed to prevent webhook validation errors:- Confirm if the deprecated CRD is still present or in use: ~~~ $ oc get addresspools.metallb.io-A-o yaml ~~~- Example output when unused: ~~~ Warning: metallb.io v1beta1 AddressPool is deprecated, consider using IPAddressPool apiVersion: v1 items: [] kind: List ~~~- Backup and delete the CRD: ~~~ $ oc get crd addresspools.metallb.io-o yaml > addresspools.metallb.io.back.yaml $ oc delete crd addresspools.metallb.io ~~~
root_cause: - The error is triggered by a deprecated addresspools.metallb.io CRD webhook.- The CA bundle used in the webhook configuration does not match the certificate presented by the webhook service.- Although the certificates in the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and the MetalLB pods appear valid, the webhook references a deprecated CRD (addresspools.metallb.io) that is no longer in active use.- Since the CRD is deprecated, its webhook CA bundle remains stale, causing the API server to fail certificate validation.

title: Router pods are not automatically restarted after updating Ingress Controller resource
issue: Router pods related to an `IngressController` resource are not automatically restarted after udpating the spoken resource.
The Ingress operator should automatically restart the router pods related to an `IngressController` resource when an update is detected in its definition.
resolution: * If the faulty field detected in the diagnostic steps is not the one you are updating, restarting the router pods will have them getting the new `defaultCertificate` (in this case). But the existence of a faulty field, can result in things breaking or not working as expected. * So, make the correction on the `IngressController` resource and the router pods should restart automatically.
root_cause: * Previous wrong configuration on other fields rather than the one that was being updated blocked the router pods of rolling out.

title: Add k8s_observer extension to Red Hat OpenTelemetry Collector for dynamic workload discovery in RHOCP 4
issue: - Currently, the `Red Hat OpenTelemetry` `Collector` build does not include the `k8s_observer` extension. As a result, customers cannot dynamically discover and manage `Kubernetes workloads` for `observability` purposes. This limitation makes it difficult to collect `telemetry` from common applications (such as Apache HTTP Server) that do not natively support `OpenTelemetry`, leaving gaps in `observability` coverage on `OpenShift` clusters.
resolution: - To address this challenge, the [upstream](https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2025/otel-collector-k8s-discovery) `OpenTelemetry` community has introduced the `k8s_observer` extension, which enables `dynamic discovery` of `Kubernetes` `workloads`. This capability simplifies the management of `telemetry` and logs for `non-OTEL` applications by automatically detecting and handling relevant components deployed on `OpenShift`.- Incorporating this enhancement would significantly improve the ability to collect and manage `observability` data across a broader range of `workloads` in `OpenShift`, particularly those that do not offer native OTEL support.- Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [TRACING-5531](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/TRACING-5531). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: The `Red Hat build of the OpenTelemetry` `Collector` gathers `observability` data from both applications and the `OpenShift` cluster. While this setup works effectively for workloads that natively support `OpenTelemetry`, several widely used applications (such as Apache HTTP Server) lack built-in `OTEL` `instrumentation`, creating gaps in `observability`.

title: Make Thanos Query gRPC port configurable for cross cluster chaining in RHOCP4
issue: - The `Thanos Query` instance deployed by the `Cluster Monitoring Operator (CMO)` currently binds its `gRPC port` to `localhost`. This restricts access to local connections only and prevents external` Thanos Query `instances from connecting for `federated` queries.
resolution: - A global view of `metrics` is needed by `aggregating` data from multiple `OpenShift` clusters into a centralized `observability` stack. Enabling the `Cluster Monitoring Operator (CMO)` managed `Thanos Query` to connect with external `Thanos Query` instances would allow `federated` queries across clusters, enhancing `observability`, simplifying operations, and improving cross-cluster troubleshooting. Without this capability, `multi-cluster metrics` aggregation cannot be achieved natively.- Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE-8009](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-8009). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: By default, `Cluster Monitoring Operator (CMO)` configures the `Thanos Query` `gRPC` port to listen only on `127.0.0.1`. This design limits connectivity to the local pod and does not allow chaining with Thanos Query instances deployed outside the cluster.

title: How to configure to use the ja_JP.SJIS for Japanese locale
issue: - How do I configure to use the ja_JP.SJIS for Japanese locale?- How about JIS2004?
resolution: **Note:** In different versions of Red Hat Enterprise Linux(RHEL), below is the default locale. And if the customer change locale from default to SJIS, we will not support the customer when there are problems in RHEL. Refer to [What is the character code of the locale that Red Hat supports?](/node/38948). Version | Support Locale------- |--- RHEL2.1 | EUC RHEL3 | EUC RHEL4 | UTF-8 RHEL5 | UTF-8 RHEL6 | UTF-8 RHEL7 | UTF-8 RHEL8 | UTF-8 RHEL9 | UTF-8 RHEL10 | UTF-8 1. **In case of RHEL8, RHEL9 and RHEL10**, install `glibc-locale-source` package: ~~~ # yum install glibc-locale-source ~~~ 2. Create a character map of the locale using the following command: ~~~ # localedef-f SHIFT_JIS-i ja_JP ja_JP.SJIS character map `SHIFT_JIS'' is not ASCII compatible, locale not ISO compliant A warning message will be displayed due to non-ASCII compatability. The /usr/lib/locale/locale-archive file will be updated regardless of the warning message. ~~~ **Note:** In RHEL7 or earlier, add `--no-archive` option to preserve the custom locale accross updates. For more details, please refer to [How to preserve custom locales across glibc-* updates?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1335353) 3. Run the following command to set the SJIS environment. ~~~ # LANG=ja_JP.SJIS ~~~ 4. To apply the added locale system-wide after a reboot: (RHEL7 and later) Set the LANG variable using the command `localectl set-locale` ~~~ # localectl set-locale LANG=ja_JP.SJIS ~~~ (Prior to RHEL7) Modify the file `/etc/sysconfig/i18n` to add `ja_JP.SJIS` ~~~ LANG=ja_JP.SJIS SUPPORTED=en_US.UTF-8:en_US:en:ja_JP.eucJP:ja_JP:ja:ja_JP.SJIS:ja SYSFONT=lat0-sun16 SYSFONTACM=8859-15 ~~~

title: OpenShift cluster destroy fails with Swift container deletion error in RHOCP 4
issue: - When running `openshift-install destroy cluster` command, the cluster destruction process fails with errors similar to the following: ``` ERROR Deleting container "int-prod-image-registry" failed: Delete "https://cloud-storage.com/swift/v1/...": EOF ```
resolution: - Manually clean up leftover Swift objects from OpenStack related to the OpenShift cluster and retry the cluster destruction: ``` $./openshift-install destroy cluster--dir--log-level info ``` After the stale Swift objects are cleaned, the destroy cluster process completes successfully.
root_cause: The installer was unable to delete Swift objects associated with the OpenShift cluster. This typically occurs when: The Swift backend is under heavy load, Or The registry container objects remain in a bad state, causing **503/504 errors** during deletion.

title: AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume xyz timed out waiting for external-attacher of smb.csi.k8s.io CSI driver to attach volume  xyz-cifs-volume
issue: Creation of a pod that attempts to mount CIFS volumes fails due to: ``` AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume xyz timed out waiting for external-attacher of smb.csi.k8s.io CSI driver to attach volume xyz-cifs-volume ```
resolution: - [Install CIFS/SMB CSI Driver](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html-single/storage/index#persistent-storage-csi-olm-operator-install_persistent-storage-csi-smb-cifs) and ensure that `ClusterCSIDriver` instance is created. This also creates Deployment/smb-csi-driver-controller as well as Daemonset/smb-csi-driver-node. ``` $ oc get csidriver | grep-E 'smb.csi|NAME' NAME ATTACHREQUIRED PODINFOONMOUNT STORAGECAPACITY TOKENREQUESTS REQUIRESREPUBLISH MODES AGE smb.csi.k8s.io false true false false Persistent 6m11s $ oc get deployment | grep 'sbm-csi' smb-csi-driver-controller 2/2 2 2 7m1s smb-csi-driver-operator 1/1 1 1 9m29s $ oc get ds | grep 'smb-csi' smb-csi-driver-node 6 6 6 6 6 kubernetes.io/os=linux 8m27s $ oc get pods-n openshift-cluster-csi-drivers | grep 'smb-csi' smb-csi-driver-controller-7fcdc56b58-btm57 5/5 Running 0 6m40s smb-csi-driver-controller-7fcdc56b58-k2qnh 5/5 Running 0 6m40s smb-csi-driver-node-55ppv 3/3 Running 0 6m43s smb-csi-driver-node-9l8bf 3/3 Running 0 6m43s smb-csi-driver-node-gj275 3/3 Running 0 110s smb-csi-driver-node-lbqh2 3/3 Running 0 6m43s smb-csi-driver-node-nlbpr 3/3 Running 0 6m43s smb-csi-driver-node-t7p2k 3/3 Running 0 6m43s smb-csi-driver-operator-7f54d4bd7b-hzjxp 1/1 Running 0 9m8s ```- Fix `volumeHandle` value for pvc/xyz using the correct format `{smb-server-address}#{sub-dir-name}#{share-name}`. Check [Static provisioning](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html-single/storage/index#persistent-storage-csi-smb-cifs-provision-static_persistent-storage-csi-smb-cifs) for more details.
