title: Elasticsearch Operator stuck in Pending state with duplicate ClusterServiceVersion in RHOCP 4
issue: - `Elasticsearch` Operator stuck in `Pending` state with `Duplicate ClusterServiceVersion` ~~~ NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102042059.p0 OpenShift Elasticsearch Operator 4.6.0-202102042059.p0 elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202101300140.p0 Pending elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102130420.p0 OpenShift Elasticsearch Operator 4.6.0-202102130420.p0 elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102042059.p0 Pending ~~~- Operator logs shows the below error: ~~~ time="2021-02-25T15:49:30Z" level=info msg="couldn't ensure RBAC in target namespaces" csv=elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102042059.p0 error="no owned roles found" id=9C4bG namespace=openshift-operators-redhat phase=Pending E0225 15:49:30.619645 1 queueinformer_operator.go:290] sync {"update" "openshift-operators-redhat/elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102042059.p0"} failed: no owned roles found time="2021-02-25T15:49:31Z" level=info msg="requirements were not met" csv=elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102042059.p0 id=JjOA/ namespace=openshift-operators-redhat phase=Pending time="2021-02-25T15:49:31Z" level=info msg="couldn't ensure RBAC in target namespaces" csv=elasticsearch-operator.4.6.0-202102042059.p0 error="no owned roles found" id=dhqug namespace=openshift-operators-redhat phase=Pending ~~~
resolution: When an operator `is installed` a list of resources is created associated with that CSV. And on the `operator upgrade process` new of those resources will be created again. But at the end of the upgrade those resources need to be deleted, to clean the previous ones. The absence of one of the resources with the CSV leads the Operator to be on **Pending status**. On this instance, the OLM was having issues deleting exactly the resources associated with `4.6.0-202102042059` to resolve that scenario it was enough to:- Try to `delete` one of the operators stuck in the `Pending` state. This will make the other operator take over the resources and help the OLM to clean the resources there that are on `Running` state.- Verify the resources listed already on the operator installed namespace. In case of misbehaved upgrade, the OLM might not be able to delete the resources there (including the CSV) by itself and a re-installation may be required. However, if you still face the issue, please raise a support ticket with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: The absence of one of the CSV associated resources makes the CSV to go into `Pending` status. This message indicates that the `RBAC` assigned to the service account does not match the requirements specified by `CSV` (cluster service version). In other words, while creating an operator one defines `CSV` which defines the requirements for creating the custom resource. Then, when the operator creates the resource it checks if the user service account fulfills these requirements. A certain CSV is associated with the respective created resources because it is the owner of that resource: ~~~ $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE amqstreams.v2.8.0-0-0.1738265624.p Streams for Apache Kafka 2.8.0-0+0.1738265624.p amqstreams.v2.7.0-0 Succeeded $ oc get role amqstreams.v2.8.0-0-0.17-1NsWxaWRw72R0qoWhpd8qUByNzXbV61pn006ql-o yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: labels: olm.managed: "true" olm.owner: amqstreams.v2.8.0-0-0.1738265624.p <---------------------------------------------------- olm.owner.kind: ClusterServiceVersion <---------------------------------------------------- olm.owner.namespace: openshift-operators olm.permissions.hash: 9UgePkV26ZKNqJfGG6xBl52gk5PriKCIm55z1v operators.coreos.com/amq-streams.openshift-operators: "" name: amqstreams.v2.8.0-0-0.17-1NsWxaWRw72R0qoWhpd8qUByNzXbV61pn006ql <---------------------------------------- namespace: openshift-operators ownerReferences:- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 blockOwnerDeletion: false controller: false kind: ClusterServiceVersion name: amqstreams.v2.8.0-0-0.1738265624.p <-------------------------------------------------------------------- uid: ec734c58-ad93-41d5-b281-2b638c08cb71 ~~~ In case the subscription is present, the `Installed Operator` section options will report the option `Uninstall Operator`. Otherwise, if the Subscription is not present, and only the CSV is present, the option will be `Remove CSV`.

title: IDMS operators sync report triggering unintended pod restarts in RHOCP
issue: - Unintended pod restarts occur after `IDMS operators` sync report is triggered.- `IDMS` configuration was already applied prior to the upgrade however `index` syncing showing in process which causes the pod restart.
resolution: - As per [Understanding image registry repository mirroring](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/images/image-configuration#images-configuration-registry-mirror-configuring_image-configuration) after the object is created, the `Machine Config Operator (MCO)` `drains` the nodes for `ImageTagMirrorSet` objects only. The MCO does not drain the nodes for `ImageDigestMirrorSet` and `ImageContentSourcePolicy` objects.- So, `IDMS` doesn't `drain` the nodes but `ITMS` does.

title: Error: Option '--offline' is unknown, try 'nmcli -help' while adding RHEL worker node to OpenShift Container Platform 4.16
issue: Unable to join RHEL 8.6 server to OpenShift 4.16 cluster.

During the process of running the playbook the script `configure-ovs.sh` encounters an error as, ~~~ configure-ovs.sh[19143]: + nmcli--offline c mod conn.interface br-ex connection.multi-connect '' connection.autoconnect no connection.master d2e19c53-262b-4646-8df2-854546edddd2 connection.slave-type ovs-port ovs-interface.type internal 802-3-ethernet.mtu 1500 802-3-ethernet.cloned-mac-address ipv4.route-metric 48 ipv6.route-metric 48 configure-ovs.sh[19471]: Error: Option '--offline' is unknown, try 'nmcli-help'. configure-ovs.sh[19143]: ++ handle_exit configure-ovs.sh[19143]: ++ e=2 ~~~
resolution: - The OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 release supports addition of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8 and above as node.- The workaround with updating the `Network-Manager` package release equivalent to 8.8 release works but would be not be a supported procedure.
root_cause: - The Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 release usage a `NetworkManager` package at a lower version failing to run commands with latest options required `ovs-configuration`.

title: Elasticsearch Operator logs shows "index_not_found_exception"
issue: - Elasticsearch Operator logs shows "index_not_found_exception" as below: ``` 2024-05-05T19:35:14.488479888Z {"_ts":"2024-05-05T19:35:14.48833459Z","_level":"0","_component":"elasticsearch-operator_controllers_Elasticsearch","_message":"Failed to initialize first index alias for mapping","_error":{"cluster":"elasticsearch","msg":"failed to update aliases","namespace":"openshift-logging","response_body":{"error":{"index":"app-000001","index_uuid":"_na_","reason":"no such index","resource.id":"app-000001","resource.type":"index_or_alias","root_cause":[{"index":"app-000001","index_uuid":"_na_","reason":"no such index","resource.id":"app-000001","resource.type":"index_or_alias","type":"index_not_found_exception"}],"type":"index_not_found_exception"},"status":404},"response_error":null,"response_status":404},"cluster":"elasticsearch","handler":"indexmanagement","mapping":"app","name":"app","namespace":"openshift-logging"} ```
resolution: **Note**: replace ` ` by `app`, `infra` or `audit` 1. Manually roll over a new index for the index type depend on `Elasticsearch Operator` pod logs, using the following commands. Replace ` ` by `app`, `infra` or `audit` ~~~ $ oc project openshift-logging $ es_pod=$(oc get pod-l component=elasticsearch-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') $ oc rsh $es_pod sh-5.1$ es_util--query=-000001-XPUT ~~~ 2. Create the alias to the indice and open it for writes. ~~~ sh-5.1$ es_util--query=_aliases-XPOST-d '{"actions":[{"add":{"index":"-000001","alias":"app-write","is_write_index":true}}]}' ~~~
root_cause: The Red Hat Elasticsearch was not able to create the alias to the indice `app-write`, `infra-write` or `audit-write` or it was deleted by error.

title: ODF deployment fails to deploy OSDs due to unclean disks - How to properly erase a disk which was an ODF / Ceph OSD.
issue: - ODF deployment fails to deploy OSDs due to unclean disks.- How to properly erase a disk which was an ODF / Ceph OSD.- OSD is not cleaning properly while re-deploying the OSD.
resolution: - There are 2 methods to clean/wipe disks to be used for ODF OSDs.- Method 1 is intended for OCP / ODF clusters running 4.16 or higher.- Method 2 is intended for OCP / ODF clusters running 4.15 or lower.- Method 2 is also intended as a fall back if method 1 fails.--- ###Method 1 ⓘ You can clean a device for use in ODF by running the **`ceph-bluestore-tool`** from the Rook Ceph Operator container image. 1. Identify the Rook Ceph Operator Image. Identify the image of the running **`rook-ceph-operator`** deployment: ``` Syntax: # oc get deploy-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[].image}' Example: # oc get deploy-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-operator-o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[].image}' registry.redhat.io/odf4/rook-ceph-rhel9-operator@sha256:60623084100a785f7eaf4bd3a4f87de4982daa37e30849bdb0b8304d3d1b7cd5 ``` 2. Cleaning the device. On the node, use `podman` to run the `ceph-bluestore-tool` utilizing the operator's image to wipe the device: ``` Syntax: # /usr/bin/podman run--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json--rm-ti--privileged--device--entrypoint ceph-bluestore-tool zap-device--dev--yes-i-really-really-mean-it Examples: # /usr/bin/podman run--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json--rm-ti--privileged--device /dev/sdc--entrypoint ceph-bluestore-tool registry.redhat.io/odf4/rook-ceph-rhel9-operator@sha256:60623084100a785f7eaf4bd3a4f87de4982daa37e30849bdb0b8304d3d1b7cd5 zap-device--dev /dev/sdc--yes-i-really-really-mean-it # /usr/bin/podman run--authfile /var/lib/kubelet/config.json--rm-ti--privileged--device /dev/nvme1n1--entrypoint ceph-bluestore-tool registry.redhat.io/odf4/rook-ceph-rhel9-operator@sha256:60623084100a785f7eaf4bd3a4f87de4982daa37e30849bdb0b8304d3d1b7cd5 zap-device--dev /dev/nvme1n1--yes-i-really-really-mean-it ``` * Replace **` `** with the path to the target disk (e.g., `/dev/nvme1n1`). * Replace **` `** with the image you found in step 1.--- ###Method 2 ⓘ This procedure is specific to Downstream ODF (Rook) which uses CoreOS as the Platform Operating System. ``` DISK="/dev/sdX" DISK="/dev/nvme1n1" # Wipe the partition table off the disk to a fresh, usable state. wipefs-fa $DISK # Wipe certain areas of the disk to remove Ceph Metadata which may be present. for gb in 0 1 10 100 1000; do dd if=/dev/zero of="$DISK" bs=1K count=200 oflag=direct,dsync seek=$((gb * 1024**2)); done # This might not be supported on all devices. blkdiscard $DISK ```---- In OpenShift environment, the [solutions 7114870](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7114870) can be used as a **workaround** where a `MachineConfig` configures a script to run during the first node boot to clean the Ceph bluestore metadata from all disks.- In order to cleanup `ceph bluestore metadata` by `ODF Operator` from `OSD` disks before deploying the cluster, a new feature is requested and being tracked as part of [ODFRFE-19](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ODFRFE-19).
root_cause: - As per the [PR 55374](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/55374), ceph copies bdev label to 4 potential replica places on device: 0(original), 1GB, 10GB, 100GB, 1000GB. If all replicas do not match the label, osd refuses to start.

title: Application metrics not scrapped by user workload monitoring. Targets shown as dropped.
issue: After creating a `ServiceMonitor` for an application, user workload monitoring is not scrapping the application metrics yet.
resolution: Confirm that the port in the `ServiceMonitor` resource definition is matching the port name of the service. The output of these two commands should match: ~~~ oc get servicemonitor prometheus-example-monitor-n ns1-o jsonpath="{.spec.endpoints[].port}" oc get svc-n ns1 prometheus-example-app-o jsonpath="{.spec.ports[].name}" ~~~
root_cause: The port at `ServiceMonitor` level is not matching the port name at `Service` level.

title: Elasticsearch PVCs not recreated automatically in RHOCP 4
issue: Elasticsearch pods' Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) fail to get created.
PVC recreation for two specific Elasticsearch pods is affected.

After deleting Elasticsearch PVC, they do not get recreated and the Elasticsearch pods are in `STATUS: Pending`: ~~~ elasticsearch-cd-ia7c6vhd-1-5f76f9b6f8-8gw5d 0/2 Pending 0 4d elasticsearch-cd-ia7c6vhd-2-7b7886f6fc-h4hdw 0/2 Pending 0 4d ~~~
resolution: Review the reconciling error in the Red Hat Elasticsearch pod logs and fix it. After this, the Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator should continue the reconciliation and recreate the PVC to be used by the Elasticsearch pods. In the use case from the **Diagnostic steps** section in the present Red Hat Knowledge Article, it's required to delete the Elasticsearch Custom Resource created in an end-user namespace. ~~~ // List the Elasticsearch CR $ cr=$(oc get elasticsearch-n) // Take a backup of the Elasticsearch CR $ oc get $cr-o yaml-n > elasticsearch_cr.yaml // Delete the Elasticsearch CR $ oc delete $cr-n ~~~
root_cause: If the Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator returns an error reconciling a resource, it will not reconcile the rest of the resources. It needs to be fixed the error. In the use case from the **Diagnostic steps** section, it was created an Elasticsearch Custom Resource (CR) in an end-user namespace. The Red Hat Elasticsearch Operator can not be used for other purposes that the documented in the Red Hat OpenShift Documentation and with the conditions established.

title: OVN address set is missing IPs of new added nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: - Ingress controller not working after creating new node and NetworkPolicy.- IngressController traffic is dropped due to the NeworkPolicy that should allow it.- The OVN address set for the host-network is not correct.- OVN-IC fails to synchronize join switch IP and management port IP details to NBDB for new nodes.- Application returning 503 after creating new nodes for the ingress controller.
resolution: Fixed in the following releases: RHOCP Release | Private Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 4.16 | OCPBUGS-28724 | **4.16.0** | [RHSA-2024:0041](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0041) 4.15 | OCPBUGS-29599 | **4.15.2** | [RHSA-2024:1210](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:1210) 4.14 | OCPBUGS-29606 | **4.14.18** | [RHSA-2024:1458](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:1458) ### Workaround {#workaround} Restart the ovnkube pods (**Note:** this action may cause temporary outage of the ClusterNetwork): ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-l app=ovnkube-node ~~~ In case a simple restart of the pods is not sufficient is required to [rebuild the OVN database](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6963671#rebuild_ovn_on_ocp_4_14_later) on the specific nodes where the IPs are missing.
root_cause: - When a new node is added the new related IPs are not added to the North Bound databases.- If a `NetworkPolicy` for allowing ingress controller traffic is used may not have correct information.

title: Enabling the Domains Tab in Horizon for Red Hat Openstack Services on Openshift 18.0
issue: A new keystone domain has been created but there is no option to select which one to use when logging into Horizon
Selecting a domain is required during Horizon login in older environments, but this behavior is not observed in RHOSO 18.
resolution: * Add `OPENSTACK_KEYSTONE_MULTIDOMAIN_SUPPORT = True` to horizon's customServiceConfig in the OpenStackControlPlane CR file like below: ~~~... horizon: apiOverride: {} enabled: true template: customServiceConfig: | SESSION_TIMEOUT = 3600 OPENSTACK_KEYSTONE_MULTIDOMAIN_SUPPORT = True OPENSTACK_KEYSTONE_DEFAULT_DOMAIN = 'Default' extraMounts: [] memcachedInstance: memcached override: {} preserveJobs: false replicas: 1 resources: {} secret: "" tls: {}... ~~~
root_cause: * Horizon's multidomain support is disabled by default and needs to be enabled when multiple domains are in use

title: Setting MachineSet onHostMaintenance to Migrate is not supported in OpenShift Container Platform 4 on Google Cloud Platform
issue: Unable to configure MachineSet `onHostMaintenance` to `Migrate` in OpenShift Container Platform 4.
Experience disruptions when encountering multiple worker reboots due to infrastructure maintenance on GCP due to `onHostMaintenance` set to `Terminate`.
When deploying OpenShift on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), setting `onHostMaintenance: Migrate` for MachineSets is blocked by a webhook unless specific conditions are met.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this limitation and is actively tracking it under [OCPBUGS-613950](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-61395). Currently, this behavior is `intentional` and documented [here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/machine_management/managing-compute-machines-with-the-machine-api#machineset-gcp-confidential-vm_creating-machineset-gcp).- OpenShift does not support configuring `onHostMaintenance: Migrate` for GCP instances. This is considered as a [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-8263), rather than a bug. `Backporting` to `4.16` in the OpenShift API, MAPG, and all components, it would be a considerable amount of work hence fixing it in a `future release` of OpenShift is more reasonable.
root_cause: OpenShift uses validating `webhooks` in the GCP `Cluster API Provider` (cluster-api-provider-gcp) to restrict `invalid` or `unsupported configurations` on MachineSets. GCP imposes certain limitations on the use of `onHostMaintenance: Migrate`, particularly when used with Confidential VMs or unsupported machine types.

title: Request to enable Centralized ImageContentSourcePolicy management across Hosted Clusters in RHOCP 4
issue: - Configuring `ImageContentSourcePolicy` individually for each `Hosted Cluster` in `disconnected` environments is inefficient, error-prone, and difficult to scale.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE-7925](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7925). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: The existing design of `Hosted Clusters` requires that `ImageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP)` configurations be applied individually to each cluster `manifest`. As the number of `Hosted Control Planes` increases, this `decentralized` approach becomes inefficient and error-prone. `Administrators` must manually replicate changes, such as adding new `operators` or updating` image sources`, across all clusters. This lack of a `centralized` configuration mechanism leads to higher operational overhead, increased risk of inconsistencies, and challenges in maintaining large-scale, `disconnected` `OpenShift deployments`.

title: Use insecureSkipVerify true with not SSL/TLS connection stops the collectors in RHOCP 4
issue: When it's configured in the `clusterLogForwarder` `insecureSkipVerify: true` when using http instead of https, it stops the collectors
When the `clusterlogforwarder` is defined using not SSL/TLS and at the same time defined `insecureSkipVerify: true`, not collector pods
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report: RHOL Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 5.8 | [LOG-4893](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4893) | 5.8.3 | [RHSA-2024:0728](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:0728) If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. #### WORKAROUND It's not expected to use `insecureSkipVerify: true` when using a not TLS/SSL connection, then, it could be two escenarios: ##### 1. The url of the endpoint is a not TLS/SSL Connection Then, remove `spec.outputs..tls.insecureSkipVerify` editing the `clusterlogforwarder`: ``` $ oc edit clusterlogforwarder instance-n openshift-logging ``` Changing from: ``` spec: outputs:- name: splunk tls: insecureSkipVerify: true type: splunk url: http://splunk:8088 ``` To: ``` spec: outputs:- name: splunk type: splunk url: http://splunk:8088 ``` ##### 2. The url of the endpoint should be a TLS/SSL Connection Change the url of the `output` for using a TLS/SSL Connection. In this example, change http for being https as follows: ``` $ oc edit clusterlogforwarder instance-o yaml... spec: outputs:- name: splunk tls: insecureSkipVerify: true type: splunk url: https://splunk:8088 <--- changed to be https ``` **NOTE**: it's not recommended to use `spec.outputs..tls.insecureSkipVerify: true` in productive environments. As the CA is always public, it could be get as follow: ``` $ server= $ port= $ echo | openssl s_client-connect ${server}:${port}-servername ${server} | openssl x509-out ca.pem ``` This generated a file called `ca.pem` containing the CA. With it, it's possible to create the secret as indicated in the Documentation Section: ["Creating a Secret"](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/logging/log_collection_forwarding/configuring-log-forwarding.html#creating-a-secret).
root_cause: When configuration used an insecure (HTTP) URL while specifying TLS option `insecureSkipVerify` lead to the Cluster Logging Operator to create an invalid configuration for the collector.

title: OpenShift upgrade fails to complete with non-responsive node in the cluster
issue: When upgrading OpenShift Container Platform to a new release, the upgrade stalls on a node which is marked `NotReady` and does not proceed past this point.
resolution: * Troubleshoot the `NotReady` node. If the node is completely unresponsive and unrecoverable, delete the node from the cluster as follows: ~~~ oc delete node nodeName ~~~ Then, the upgrade will proceed as normal.
root_cause: * The OpenShift upgrade process runs serially on each node in a cluster and will stall out if a node is unreachable by the machine config service.

title: Is it possible to use OpenShift API for Data Protection(OADP) without object storage?
issue: - How to use `OpenShift API for Data Protection(OADP)` operator without S3 compatible object storage?
resolution: - `OpenShift API for Data Protection(OADP)` operator can't be used without object storage as the backup location is required to be S3 compatible object storage.- `OpenShift Data Foundation(ODF)` or any other S3 compatible object storage needs to be set up as backup location in the `DataProtectionApplication` CR.
root_cause: - Object storage is a must for backup location to set up `OADP` operator which is also mentioned in the [OADP operator installation documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html-single/backup_and_restore/index#about-installing-oadp).

title: Pruning of images fails with an invalid character error in RHOCP 4
issue: - Pruning of images fails with an error like below. ~~~ imagestream /: failed to delete layer link sha256:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: invalid character '\x1f' looking for beginning of value ~~~
resolution: - Check for objects that may be referencing non existent `ImageStreams`.- `BuildConfigs` could be the usual suspects that may be referencing non existent `ImageStreams`. Deleting such `BuildConfigs` will resolve the issue.
root_cause: - Objects like `BuildConfigs` referencing non existent `ImageStreams`.

title: Pod deployment fails with 'unsafe sysctl "kernel.sem" is not allowed' in RHOCP 4
issue: - Applying below for `semaphore` settings in a container fails. ~~~ securityContext: sysctls:- name: kernel.sem value: 250 32000 32 192 ~~~- Below error is shown when creating the pod. ~~~ Error creating: pods " " is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constraint: [pod.spec.securityContext.sysctls[0]: Forbidden: unsafe sysctl "kernel.sem" is not allowed] ~~~
resolution: - OpenShift Container Platform doesn't have unsafe `sysctls` enabled by default.- Enable the unsafe `sysctls` manually by applying a `kubeletConfig` on a `machineConfigPool` by referring to [the documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/nodes/working-with-containers#nodes-containers-sysctls-unsafe_nodes-containers-using).
root_cause: - The setting is getting rejected as it's considered unsafe `sysctl`.

title: Operator status is unknown with 'no operators found in channel' messages in catalog operator logs
issue: **Issue-1**- Operator status is `unknown` and the operator upgrade status is `unknown failure`.- Getting below messages in the catalog operator logs. ~~~ YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.xxxxxxxxZ xxxxx 14:43:40.547245 1 event.go:282] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"Namespace", Namespace:"", Name:"openshift-operators", UID:"xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"xxxx", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'ResolutionFailed' constraints not satisfiable: no operators found in channel of package in the catalog referenced by subscription, subscription exists ~~~ **Issue-2**- Operator is stuck in installation phase and the install plan is not getting created.- The operator's subscription describe output shows *`ResolutionFailed`
in the *`Status.Conditions`
section with an error message- *`constraints not satisfiable: no operators found in channel..`
for any existing affected operator/s in the namespace. **Note:*
The affected operator is the one which is shown in the *`ResolutionFailed`

error, NOT the one which is not getting installed. ~~~- message: 'constraints not satisfiable: no operators found in channel stable of package elasticsearch-operator in the catalog referenced by subscription elasticsearch-operator, subscription elasticsearch-operator exists' reason: ConstraintsNotSatisfiable status: "True" type: ResolutionFailed ~~~
resolution: **Issue-1**- Update the subscription channel and upgrade the operator as per the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/operators/administrator-tasks#olm-changing-update-channel_olm-upgrading-operators "Changing the update channel for an operator"). **Issue-2**- Modify the subscription of the affected operator populated in the *`ResolutionFailed`* error and update the correct catalog source in which the affected operator exist. ~~~ $ oc edit subscription elasticsearch-operator apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription....... spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Manual name: elasticsearch-operator source: my-operator-index--> Update the catalog source in which the operator exist sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~
root_cause: **Issue-1**- Operators were not upgraded before and the operator update channel being used in the subscription is not available post Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform upgrade. **Issue-2**- If more than one operators are installed in a namespace and if any of the existing operator/s is having issues related to subscription, install-plan or CSV, the installation of any new operator or upgrade of another existing operator will not be progressed until the issue with the affected operator is fixed.

title: How to configure additionalTrustedCA for multiple image registries in RHOCP 4?
issue: - How to configure `additionalTrustedCA` for multiple image registries in `image.config.openshift.io/cluster` custom resource?- How to update the existing registry configmap with an additional CA for a new registry?- Pulling container images from a new image registry failed with this error: ~~~ tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~
resolution: - Create a `configmap` yaml configuration file like below to store each registry's certificate in it as per the [doc](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/images/image-configuration-classic#images-configuration-cas_image-configuration "Configuring additional trust stores for image registry access"). ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: my-registry-ca data: registry.example.com: |-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE----- registry-with-port.example.com..5000: |-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...-----END CERTIFICATE----- ~~~- Create the `configmap`. ~~~ $ oc create-f-n openshift-config ~~~- If you already have an existing `configmap` for one of the registries, take a yaml backup of it and edit the `configmap` to include the certificates for the other registries. ~~~ $ oc get cm-o yaml-n openshift-config > orginal-cm-backup.yaml $ oc edit cm-n openshift-config //Add the additional certs in the configmap as per the format shown in the above example. ~~~- Edit the `image.config.openshift.io/cluster` custom resource to mention the `configmap` name to be trusted under `additionalTrustedCA`. ~~~ spec: additionalTrustedCA: name: ~~~- A new machine config update is rolled out and the certificates are updated in each node for each registry under /etc/docker/certs.d directory. ~~~ $ ls-l /etc/docker/certs.d/ ~~~

title: Kube Scheduler operator is degraded in OpenShift Container Platform 4
issue: - The `kube-scheduler` operator is degraded with below error message. ~~~ Message: StaticPodsDegraded: pod/openshift-kube-scheduler- container "kube-scheduler" is waiting: CrashLoopBackOff: back-off 5m0s restarting failed container=kube-scheduler pod=openshift-kube-scheduler-_openshift-kube-scheduler(xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx) ~~~- The cluster `scheduler` object is modified to have a spec section similar to below but the `kube-scheduler` operator is degraded after some time. ~~~ spec: defaultNodeSelector: type=worker mastersSchedulable: false policy: name: scheduler-policy ~~~
resolution: - Validate that there is no policy configmap created in `openshift-config` namespace with the name mentioned in the cluster `scheduler` object for example `scheduler-policy`. ~~~ $ oc get cm-n openshift-config ~~~- If the config map doesn't exist in `openshift-config` namespace, remove the the config map name `scheduler-policy` from the name under policy section of the cluster scheduler object and keep it empty with ''. ~~~ $ oc edit scheduler cluster---output omitted--- spec: defaultNodeSelector: type=worker mastersSchedulable: false policy: name: scheduler-policy <--- Remove this scheduler-policy and keep empty with '' ~~~- The scheduler policy feature is deprecated. Use scheduler profiles if needed as per the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html-single/nodes/index#nodes-scheduler-profiles "Scheduling pods using a scheduler profile").
root_cause: Config map for custom `scheduler policy` was misconfigured for the cluster `scheduler` object.

title: Applying new KubeletConfig doesn't work when a KubeletConfig exists created by Compliance Operator
issue: - Creating a new `KubeletConfig` not working when there is already a `KubeletConfig` applied which was created by Compliance Operator.- How to apply a `KubeletConfig` on top of an existing one?
resolution: - Instead of creating another `KubeletConfig` for a setting in `kubeletConfig` section, update the already existing one which was created by `Compliance Operator`.- Make sure that any parameter you want to set in the `kubeletConfig` section of an existing `KubeletConfig`is not already set by `Compliance Operator`. Updating any such parameter will be overwritten by the operator.
root_cause: Only one `kubeletConfig` section in a `KubeletConfig` object takes effect for a particular MCP. Hence, when there is already an existing `kubeletConfig` section in an existing `KubeletConfig` for an MCP, creating another one won't work.

title: oc-mirror removes operator images from mirror registry that are not referenced in the channel anymore
issue: - Images get pruned from the private registry if the images don't exist in the catalog anymore when performing mirroring with `oc-mirror`.- How to prevent `oc-mirror` from removing images from mirror registry?
resolution: - This was reported in the bug [OCPBUGS-863](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-863).- There is a new flag now `--skip-pruning` that was released with oc-mirror 4.12.11. This flag can be used to avoid pruning of images in the mirror registry by `oc-mirror`.
root_cause: `oc-mirror` is designed to prune any images from the target mirror registry that were excluded from the image set configuration since the previous execution. When the images don't exist in the catalog anymore, they are considered excluded and get pruned from the mirror registry.

title: OpenShift GitOps has permission issues even in managed namespaces
issue: - Trying to create an `ArgoCD` project is failing with permission denied errors even after setting the label `argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by: ` on the namespace to be managed by `ArgoCD`.- Labeling namesapces with `ArgoCD` label is not creating the required roles and rolebindings in the namespace.
resolution: - This issues can arise due to using both `.spec.dex` and `.spec.sso.dex` in the `ArgoCD` instance.- Make sure to remove the `.spec.dex` section from the `ArgoCD` instance and use only `.spec.sso.dex`.- As mentioned in the [doc](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/cicd/gitops/configuring-sso-on-argo-cd-using-dex.html), the `.spec.dex` option is now deprecated and will be removed in the 1.9 release of `GitOps`.
root_cause: Using both `.spec.dex` and `.spec.sso.dex` in the `ArgoCD` instance is not supported.

title: Installing operators in multiple namespaces in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to install operators in some specific namespaces only instead of all namespaces?- Is it possible to install operators in 2 or more namespaces?
resolution: - It is possible to install operators in specific namespaces from the CLI.- Create a new namespace where the operator `subscription` will be created. ~~~ $ oc new-project ~~~- Create an `OperatorGroup` in the namespace created in previous step which lists desired namespaces in `targetNamespaces` like below. ~~~ kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: namespace: spec: targetNamespaces:- namespace1 //List appropriate namespaces for installing the operators- namesapce2- namespace3 ~~~- The `targetNamespaces` section can be left blank if the operator needs to be installed in all namespaces. **Note** that one namespace should have only one `OperatorGroup`. Avoid using openshift-operators namespace for this purpose as it has an `OperatorGroup` by default and many operators use this namespace by default when installed via GUI Console.- Then, from the namespace where the `OperatorGroup` is created, use a `subscription` like below to install the operator. Below example uses quay operator. Use appropriate operator in it's place. Use `Automatic` or `Manual` `installPlanApproval` as needed. ~~~ kind: Subscription metadata: name: quay-operator //Use appropriate operator name namespace: spec: channel: stable-3.8 //Use appropriate channel as per the operator installPlanApproval: Manual //Use Automatic or Manual as needed name: quay-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~- A new `installplan` will be created. Approve the `installplan` if using `Manual` `installPlanApproval`. Operator installation will start. If using `Automatic` `installPlanApproval`, the installation will start automatically. ~~~ $ oc get ip-n $ oc patch installplan-n--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"approved":true}}' ~~~
root_cause: Operator installation in multiple specific namespaces is allowed only from CLI.

title: Operator installation fails with 'error validating existing CRs against new CRD's schema'
issue: - Error like below is observed when installing an operator. ~~~ error validating existing CRs against new CRD's schema for "servicemeshcontrolplanes.maistra.io": error listing resources in GroupVersionResource schema.GroupVersionResource{Group:"maistra.io", Version:"v1", Resource:"servicemeshcontrolplanes"}: conversion webhook for maistra.io/v2, Kind=ServiceMeshControlPlane failed: Post "https://maistra-admission-controller.openshift-operators.svc:443/convert-smcp?timeout=30s": no endpoints available for service "maistra-admission-controller" ~~~
resolution: - Edit the `CRD` mentioned in the error to make the conversion strategy `None` instead of `Webhook`. ~~~ $ oc edit crd servicemeshcontrolplanes.maistra.io----------output truncated----------- spec: conversion: strategy: Webhook //Change Webhook to None webhook: //Remove these lines below strategy clientConfig: caBundle: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX service: name: maistra-admission-controller namespace: openshift-operators path: /convert-smcp port: 443 conversionReviewVersions:- v1beta1 ~~~ It should look like below. ~~~ spec: conversion: strategy: None ~~~- Uninstall the operator. Make sure that the `subscription` and `CSV` are removed. ~~~ $ oc get sub,csv-n openshift-operators ~~~- Install the operator again from `OperatorHub`.- See the [KCS 6992396](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6992396) if similar issue is observed for `Red Hat OpenShift Dev Spaces` operator.
root_cause: `OLM` does not allow a `CSV` to "adopt/update" an existing `CRD` if it would invalidate existing `CRs` on cluster.

title: The image-registry ClusterOperator is in Progressing state with 'invalid control character in URL' message in RHOCP 4
issue: - Below message is seen for the `image-registry` clusteroperator and it remains in `Progressing` state. ~~~ Progressing: Unable to apply resources: unable to sync storage configuration: failed to get SPT from client credentials: parse " \n": net/url: invalid control character in URL NodeCADaemonProgressing: The daemon set node-ca is deployed ~~~
resolution: - Validate the `azure-credentials` secret in the `kube-system` namespace.- Decode the values of each parameter in the secret and figure out if any of them is encoded twice or having an incorrect value along with a new line character. ~~~ echo " " | base64-d ~~~- Correct the value of the parameter which is encoded twice in the secret or has incorrect value.- The `image-registry` CO will be able to reconcile and the message will go away.
root_cause: - At least one of the parameter values in the `azure-credentials` secret is encoded twice and/or having a wrong value.

title: Operator upgrade not available even after changing channel in a disconnected RHOCP 4 cluster
issue: - Operator is not showing upgrade available on the console even after changing the channel to a newer one.
resolution: - Some operators can't directly upgrade to the latest version.- Check the [Operator Update Information Checker](https://access.redhat.com/labs/ocpouic/) to understand what version of a Red Hat provided operator is the latest in a channel for a respective version of catalog.- Use below commands to see the details for `Certified` operators or any other catalog. They can be used for Red Hat operators as well. ~~~ $ oc mirror list operators--catalog= //To list the available operators in the catalog $ oc mirror list operators--catalog=--package= //To see channels available for an operator $ oc mirror list operators--catalog=--package=--channel= //To see the versions available in a channel ~~~- Mirror the latest version of the operator in each channel by mentioning both `minVersion` and `maxVersion` in the imageset-config file as per the [oc-mirror doc](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#oc-mirror-image-set-examples_installing-mirroring-disconnected).- Once the latest versions in each channel is mirrored and the `catalogsource` pod is restarted with the latest index image, the operator will be able to show upgrade available in the console.
root_cause: - If the latest version of an operator in a channel doesn't show up in the packagemanifests as a CSV and the `skipRange` doesn't include the versions between the CSVs mentioned in the packagemanifests of the 2 successive channels, that means the latest version in the older channel was not mirrored.- Since the operator can't skip versions outside the `skipRange`, it doesn't show upgrade available in the console even after changing the channel to newer one.

title: Certified operator not available to install in latest RHOCP version
issue: - Some operators from the `certified-operators-index` are not available to install after upgrading the cluster to latest version.- Same operators are available in older versions of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform.
resolution: - Create a new `CatalogSource` yaml file by using the older index image and a different name. ~~~ apiVersion: "operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1" kind: "CatalogSource" metadata: name: "certified-operators-test" //Using a different name than the default catalogsource namespace: "openshift-marketplace" spec: sourceType: grpc image: registry.redhat.io/redhat/certified-operator-index:v4.12 //Using older index image than the latest displayName: "Certified Operators" publisher: "Red Hat" updateStrategy: registryPoll: interval: 10m ~~~- Apply the `CatalogSource` yaml file on the cluster. ~~~ $ oc apply-f ~~~- The desired operators should be available in the `OperaotrHub` on console to install from the newly created `CatalogSource`.- Many duplicate instances of operators will be visible in the `OperaotrHub`. Install only those operators from the new `CatalogSource` that are not available in the latest index image. Rest of the operators can be installed from the already existing default `certified-operators` `CatalogSource` with the latest index image.- **Caution**: It is recommended to check the compatibility of operators available in older index images with the latest version of OpenShift. Contact the publisher of the certified operator to understand if it is safe to install the operator from an older version of catalog.
root_cause: - Certified operators are published by Red Hat partners as and when they complete development and testing. In some cases, this procedure may take time and the latest catalog version may not have the operator published by the partner at all.

title: Scaling a machineset fails with node throwing 'error creating file "/sysroot/etc/chrony.conf"'
issue: - `Machine` gets stuck in `Provisioned` state when scaling a `machineset` and the console of the `machine` shows an error like below. ~~~ ignition[1270]:}CRITICAL: Ignition failed: failed to create files: failed to create files: error creating /sysroot/etc/chrony.conf: error creating file "/sysroot/etc/chrony.conf": A file exists there already and overwrite is false ~~~
resolution: Add `overwrite: true` in the `machineconfig` used for [configuring chrony service](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/installation_configuration/installing-customizing#installation-special-config-chrony_installing-customizing "Configuring chrony time service") in the cluster nodes. This helps overwrite the existing file and create a new configuration.
root_cause: The `machine-config` operator can't overwrite the existing config file if `overwrite: true` is not mentioned in the `machineconfig`.

title: Pod throws the error 'failed to watch file ..."": no space left on device' in RHOCP 4
issue: - Getting the error `'failed to watch file *file_name*..."": no space left on device'` when trying to launch pods.- Same error appears when trying to check logs of some pods.
resolution: - Increase the value of the sysctl `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` by applying a `tuned` like below. The default value is 65536. The following `tuned` will be applied to worker nodes. ~~~ apiVersion: tuned.openshift.io/v1 kind: Tuned metadata: name: openshift-node-custom namespace: openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator spec: profile:- data: | [main] summary=Custom OpenShift node profile with an additional kernel parameter [sysctl] fs.inotify.max_user_watches=163840 name: openshift-node-custom recommend:- machineConfigLabels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: "worker" priority: 20 profile: openshift-node-custom operand: tunedConfig: reapply_sysctl: false debug: false ~~~- Verify that the new value has been applied by running below on a worker node. ~~~ # sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches ~~~ **Note**: The value in the `tuned` may need to be set even higher depending on application requirement or if it doesn't work with the mentioned value.
root_cause: The processes on the node where the pod is scheduled or running are watching many files and the total value is exceeding the default maximum of 65536 of sysctl `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`.

title: Cluster Autoscaler fails to remove nodes with 'pod with local storage present' messages in RHOCP 4
issue: - `ClusterAutoscaler` is not able to remove nodes even through the resource utilization criteria is met.- Errors like below are seen in the `ClusterAutoscaler` pod logs. ~~~ node cannot be removed: pod with local storage present: ~~~
resolution: - `ClusterAutoscaler` can't remove the nodes which have pods running with local storage.- The [ClusterAutoscaler Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/machine_management/applying-autoscaling) can be referred to understand the conditions under which the nodes are not scaled down.- `emptyDir` is considered local storage as it stores data directly on the nodes.- If it's okay to evict the pods in the errors, annotation like below should be applied on the deployment/statefulset/daemonset. ~~~ "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict-local-volumes": "volume-1,volume-2,.." ~~~- If it's okay to evict any pods with local storage, `skipNodesWithLocalStorage: false` option can be added in the `ClusterAutoscaler` under `spec`.
root_cause: `ClusterAutoscaler` doesn't evict the pods having local storage by default.

title: Slowness observed inside containers in a specific namespace in RHOCP 4
issue: - Commands run slower inside containers in a specific namespace.- Builds running slow in a namespace but relatively faster in other namespaces.
resolution: - Use `enableServiceLinks: false` in the deployment under pod spec to disable inheriting service environemnt variables. This will help with faster command excecution and better speed for builds.
root_cause: - By default all the service environment variables from a namespace are inherited in the pods.- If the environment variable count is way too high, it can cause slowness.

title: Baremetal nodes are shutdown in a minute after powering on in RHOCP 4
issue: - Baremetal nodes get powered off in a minute when trying to power them on from BMC/console.- The baremetal nodes were shutdown earlier and don't start later on.- Login from one of the master nodes can be seen on the logs of the BMC/console.
resolution: Power on the node from the cluster by changing the value of `online` to `true` in the spec of the `BareMetalHost`. ~~~ $ oc patch bmh-n openshift-machine-api--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"online":true}}' ~~~
root_cause: Power management is enabled for the `BareMetalHost` to manage its power state from the cluster.

title: Pod randomly gets thread_siblings from different cores in RHOCP 4
issue: - Sometimes `thread_siblings` from different cores get assigned to pods.- `PerformanceProfile` is already applied with `isolated` and `reserved` CPUs set still same core `thread_siblings` are not assigned.
resolution: Check if `full-pcpus-only` is disabled as per [the solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6991798 "How to disable full-pcpus-only option in performance profile?"). It will need to be enabled. **Caution**: Be careful when enabling it as it has implications. For example, guaranteed containers with just a single cpu will not be able to start. Asses why the setting was disabled before taking a decision to enable it.
root_cause: It is required to have `cpuManagerPolicyOptions` to be `full-pcpus-only` for the pods to get `thead_siblings` from the same CPU core.

title: Operator is not visible in the OperatorHub after creating a file-based custom catalog in RHOCP4
issue: - Operator is not visible in the `OperatorHub` after creating a custom catalog as per [the documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/operators/administrator-tasks#olm-creating-fb-catalog-image_olm-managing-custom-catalogs "Creating a file-based catalog image").- The `olm.csv.metadata` property doesn't get added to the `index.yaml` with `opm render` comand.
resolution: - Download and use the latest version of `opm` from the [official repository](https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/) for the respective Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform version.- Make sure that the `olm.csv.metadata` property gets added to the `index.yaml` file with `opm render` command with the latest version of `opm`.
root_cause: - Older versions of `opm` didn't have the functionality to add the `olm.csv.metadata` property.- Console requires this property to be able to identify `packagemanifests` of operators and henceforth populate them in the `OperatorHub`.

title: Baremetal node registration via RHACM fails for HPE servers with ILO5 having FIPS mode enabled in RHOCP4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - Baremetal node registration via RHACM fails with below error for HPE hardware with FIPS mode enabled. ~~~ XXs Normal RegistrationError baremetalhost/ Failed to get power state for node. Error: Redfish connection failed for node: Unable to connect to http:// /redfish/v1/. Error: HTTPSConnectionPool(host=' ', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /redfish/v1/ (Caused by SSLError(SSLError(1, '[SSL] unsupported (_ssl.c:1129)'))) ~~~
resolution: Upgrade the `ILO5` firmware to 3.00 version or higher.
root_cause: The `ILO5` firmware version is old and doesn't support TLS 1.3 or TLS 1.2 EMS which is a requiremnt for connecting to `ironic` from the `BMC` in `FIPS` mode.

title: CRI-O is using higher memory than recommended system-reserved value in RHOCP 4
issue: - CRI-O service has high memory utilization.- Regularly receiving `SystemMemoryExceedsReservation` alerts.- Memory utilization by CRI-O service is higher than [recommended system-reserved value](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5843241).

title: 'manifest invalid' error appears when mirroring images to docker registry with oc-mirror
issue: Errors like below appear when mirroring images to `docker registry` with `oc-mirror`. ~~~ error: unable to push manifest to:5000/cp4mcm-orchestrator-operator-bundle:2.3.32: manifest invalid: manifest invalid ~~~
resolution: Use the `docker registry` image version 2.8 or higher. The issue is not reproduced in newer versions.

title: Tuned profile for node is degraded with "No such file or directory: 'grub2-editenv'" after cluster shutdown and power on
issue: - `Tuned profile` for node is degraded with error like below after cluster shutdown and power on. ~~~ YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS ERROR tuned.utils.commands: Executing 'grub2-editenv- set tuned_params= tuned_initrd=' error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'grub2-editenv' ~~~
resolution: This was identified as a bug [OCPBUGS-38526](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-38526) and the fix has been released in OCP version 4.16.9.

title: SNO deployment fails at day-2 operation for operators
issue: - SNO installation fails with an error like below during day-2 operation for operators. ~~~ STDERR: Error from server (InternalError): error when creating "/mnt/vol/ /lvms-lvm-cluster.yaml": Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "vlvmcluster.kb.io": failed to call webhook: Post "https://lvms-operator-service.openshift-storage.svc:443/validate-lvm-topolvm-io-v1alpha1-lvmcluster?timeout=10s": service "lvms-operator-service" not found ~~~
resolution: A bug was identified under [OCPBUGS-45080](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-45080) and the fix has been released in OCP 4.14.43.

title: node-tuning operator degraded due to 'bootcmdline conflict' messages in RHOCP4
issue: - Node Tuning Operator is degraded with errors like below in the operator pod: ~~~ I0617 14:20:48.887790 1 status.go:313] 1/4 Profiles with bootcmdline conflict I0617 14:20:48.892294 1 status.go:313] 1/4 Profiles with bootcmdline conflict E0617 14:20:48.893980 1 controller.go:786] not all 3 Nodes in MCP master agree on bootcmdline: skew_tick=1 tsc=reliable rcupdate.rcu_normal_after_boot=1 nohz=on rcu_nocbs=8-79 tuned.non_isolcpus=000000ff systemd.cpu_affinity=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 intel_iommu=on iommu=pt isolcpus=managed_irq,8-79 default_hugepagesz=1G hugepagesz=1G hugepages=0 hugepagesz=2M hugepages=0 intel_pstate=disable I0617 14:20:48.895594 1 status.go:313] 3/4 Profiles with bootcmdline conflict I0617 14:20:48.904388 1 status.go:313] 2/4 Profiles with bootcmdline conflict ~~~
resolution: - A bug [OCPBUGS-56442](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-56442) was reported for this issue.- It was fixed in the tuned version `tuned-2.25.1-1.6.20250507gitf828dcf7.el9fdp.noarch`.- The fixed tuned version was included in `RHOCP` versions 4.18.17, 4.17.33 and 4.16.42.
root_cause: This was a bug with the tuned verison `tuned-2.25.1-1.4.20250507gitf828dcf7.el9fdp.noarch`.

title: Baremetal EC2 machine instance gets removed before becoming a node in RHOCP 4
issue: - When adding a baremetal EC2 instance in RHOCP 4 cluster on AWS, the machine gets removed before the node is added to the cluster.
resolution: - Set the `.spec.maxNodeProvisionTime` to `30m` or higher in the `ClusterAutoscaler`. The node should get added after waiting a bit more than 15 minutes. ~~~ $ oc edit clusterautoscaler default-n openshift-mahcine-api------------------- spec: maxNodeProvisionTime: 30m ~~~- See the spec reference for the `ClusterAutoscaler` in the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html-single/autoscale_apis/index#spec).
root_cause: - The `ClusterAutoscaler` waits for 15 minutes for a new node to become ready and get registered with the cluster.- Adding baremetal nodes may take a little bit more than 15 minutes. If the machine instance has not become a node within 15 minutes, the `ClusterAutoscaler` removes it as per design.

title: LDAP superuser not able to create organizations
issue: - When user who is both a superuser and a restricted user in LDAP, they cannot create organisations.
resolution: The Red Hat engineering department is aware of this issue and is currently working on a fix. The ongoing discussions for this issue and the current progress can be reviewed in the following ticket: [PROJQUAY-9352](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-9352). The current workaround is to explicitly adding the usernames to the **SUPER_USERS** field in the Quay config, which allow the user to create organisations. For more information or to register your interest in this feature, please open a case with Red Hat Technical Support.
root_cause: When user who is both a superuser and a restricted user, LDAP Search prioritizes restricted user over superuser and comes back with Unauthorized on trying to create an organization

title: How to change the password of the user using HTPASSWD?
issue: - How to change the user password using the **HTPASSWD**?
resolution: Please follow the below steps to change the password of the user:- Extract the HTPASSWD secret: ~~~ # oc extract secret/HTPASSWD_SECRET_NAME--to--n openshift-config > htpasswd ~~~_**NOTE:**_ The file `htpasswd` will be created which will contain all the user names and passwords.- To change the password of an existing user, use the below **htpasswd** command: ~~~ # htpasswd htpasswd USER_NAME ~~~_**NOTE:**_ The command will prompt for a new password for the user and modify the entry in the specified `htpasswd` file.- Replace secret with a new one, which is based on the `htpasswd` file, on which the password of the user is updated: ~~~ # oc create secret generic--from-file=--dry-run=client-o yaml-n openshift-config | oc replace-n openshift-config-f- ~~~- Try login to the user with the new password: ~~~ # oc login-u-p ~~~

title: ClusterMonitoringOperator in Degraded State Due to Expired TLS Certificate in Console Plugin Webhook in RHOCP 4
issue: - Receiving `ClusterMonitoringOperatorReconciliationErrors` in OpenShift Cluster.- `ClusterMonitoringOperator` `Degraded` due to Expired Console Operator `Webhook` Certificate.- `ClusterMonitoringOperator` reports a `Degraded` state with the reason `UpdatingConsolePluginComponentsFailed`. ~~~ message: 'reconciling Console Plugin failed: retrieving ConsolePlugin object failed: conversion webhook for console.openshift.io/v1alpha1, Kind=ConsolePlugin failed: Post "https://webhook.openshift-console-operator.svc:9443/crdconvert?timeout=30s": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2025-09-05T12:58:49Z is after 2025-09-01T20:51:13Z' reason: UpdatingConsolePluginComponentsFailed status: "True" type: Degraded ~~~
resolution: To resolve this issue, force the `openshift-console-operator` to regenerate its expired serving certificate. This can be done by deleting the secret that stores the certificate. The operator will create a new secret with a valid certificate. 1. Identify the `webhook` related secret from `openshift-console-operator` namespace and take a backup: For this example, the `webhook` secret name is `"webhook-serving-cert"`: ~~~ $ oc get secret-n openshift-console-operator $ oc get secret webhook-serving-cert-n openshift-console-operator-o yaml > webhook-serving-cert.bkp ~~~ 2. Delete the identified secret: ~~~ $ oc delete secret webhook-serving-cert-n openshift-console-operator ~~~ 3. Delete the `Console Operator` and `Cluster Monitoring Operator` Pods to trigger a restart: ~~~ $ oc delete pod console-operator-XXXXXXXXXX-XXXXX-n openshift-console-operator $ oc delete pod cluster-monitoring-operator-XXXXXXXXXX-XXXXX-n openshift-monitoring ~~~ This typically forces the operator to regenerate the `webhook` certificates. 4. After the pods restart, check that the `webhook` TLS certificate has been reissued: ~~~ $ oc get secret-n openshift-console-operator ~~~ 5. After a few minutes, check the status of the `Monitoring` and `Console` cluster operators: ~~~ $ oc get clusteroperator monitoring console ~~~ The operators should no longer be in a `degraded` state. The status should show `AVAILABLE=True`, `PROGRESSING=False`, and `DEGRADED=False`. For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).
root_cause: This issue occurred because the `TLS serving certificate` used by this `webhook` service (webhook.openshift-console-operator.svc) has expired. So the API server cannot establish a trusted TLS connection to the `webhook`, the ConsolePlugin reconciliation fails. This failure blocks the `ClusterMonitoringOperator's` reconciliation loop, causing it to report a `degraded` status.

title: OCP 4 installation failed to create client for cachedClientParams with key nutanix-cloud-controller-manager in Nutanix
issue: During deploying OpenShift on Nutanix, the Nutanix `Cloud Controller Manager` (CCM) / `Cloud Credential Operator` (CCO) is unable to communicate with Prism Central.

Log message errors in cloud-controller pods shows: ~~~ E1004 19:11:50.245433 1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:156] error checking if node ocp-8xxx-master-1 exists: failed to create client for cachedClientParams with key nutanix-cloud-controller-manager: Get "https://mynuta.example.com:9440/api/nutanix/v3/users/me": dial tcp xx.xx.xx.xx:9440: i/o timeout ~~~
Master nodes are still in `NotReady` during installation.
resolution: The issue is caused by the Nutanix `Cloud Controller Manager` (CCM) failing to create a client due to a network timeout while attempting to connect to the `Prism Central API endpoint` (https://prism-host:9440). This prevents it from retrieving instance metadata, leading to master nodes remaining in `NotReady` state and `CCO/CCM` pod failures. * Ensure the Control plane nodes must be able to reach `Prism Central` and `Prism Element` on port 9440 for the installation to succeed. * If you use a `firewall`, you have met these prerequisites:- Confirmed that port `9440` is accessible. * Make sure the DNS firewall rule are allowed from OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) nodes from resolving the Nutanix Prism Central hostname.
root_cause: The Nutanix `Cloud Controller Manager` is trying to communicate with `Prism Central` over port **9440** and is failing due to a network timeout. This prevents it from retrieving instance metadata, which is needed for correct node management — thus keeping masters in a NotReady state. The DNS resolution failure blocked by the `firewall` prevents the Nutanix Cloud Controller Manager (CCM) from reaching the `Prism Central API endpoint` (https://prism-host:9440), which in turn caused failures in retrieving instance metadata and left master nodes in a NotReady state.

title: Password authentication failed for user postgres
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: After re-installing Central with an operator, the RHACS logs show an error message of ~~~ Timed out trying to open database: failed to connect to `host=central-db.rhacs-operator.svc user=postgres database=postgres`: failed SASL auth (FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01)) ~~~ Errors related to possible changes in secrets in the central cluster: ~~~ Info: checking if the database "central_active" exists Info: Could not check for central database: failed to connect to `user=postgres database=postgres`::5432 (central-db.stackrox.svc): failed SASL auth: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01) ~~~
resolution: The steps to reconcile the PostgreSQL database in the central cluster using the new password created by the operator. In the case of a central cluster installed on OCP, verify the central-db-password secret from the OCP web console: Workloads--> Secrets--> Change the project to stackrox--> find the central-db-password secret--> at the lower part of the section named Data, copy the password, and save it. That will be the password you will use in step 5. 1. Uninstall the Operator to prevent it from reconciling ACS and reverting the changes we’re making. 2. Scale down the central-db deployment 3. Create a pod in the RHACS namespace with the following contents (adapt the namespace to your needs): ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: central-db-maintenance namespace: stackrox spec: containers:- name: postgres-maintenance image: postgres:15 # Use 13 for ACS 4.7 or older command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep infinity"] securityContext: runAsUser: 70 fsGroup: 70 volumeMounts:- name: db-data mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data securityContext: fsGroup: 70 serviceAccount: central-db serviceAccountName: central-db volumes:- name: db-data persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: central-db ~~~ 4. Open a terminal inside the newly created maintenance pod: ~~~ $ oc exec-it central-db-maintenance-n stackrox-- /bin/bash ~~~ 5. Inside the terminal: ~~~ chmod 0700 /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata sed-i.bak "s/^\(local\s*all\s*all\s*\).*$/\1trust/" /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata/pg_hba.conf pg_ctl start-D /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata psql-U postgres ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD ` `; ~~~ Instead of ALTER USER, you can also use this more secure alternative to change the password in psql (without logging the password in the log file): ~~~ =# \password Enter new password for user "postgres": ~~~ 6. Delete the central-db-maintenance pod 7. Reinstall the Operator 8. Wait and verify that Central now starts
root_cause: The lifecycle of the central-db password does not match that of the central-db PVC. The operator intentionally does *not* delete Central's PVC when Central is deleted, to prevent data loss. However, operator *does* delete the central-db password secret. During the initial installation, the *original* secret is initialized as the database password and saved in the PVC, but upon reinstallation, Central attempts to use the *new* secret, which does not match. This issue is tracked in [ROX-13947](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ROX-13947).

title: Support to connect to multiple DevWorkspaces via gateway
issue: - Is it possible for users to connect to multiple DevWorkspaces simultaneously?
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [CRW-5773](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CRW-5773). If this feature is required, [open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: - The root cause of this limitation is the Dev Spaces Gateway plugin using a hardcoded local port for port forwarding.- The plugin uses the same local port (5990) to establish the secure connection/tunnel for every DevWorkspace. When a user is already connected to one workspace, that local port is in use. Any subsequent attempt to connect to a second workspace immediately fails due to the port conflict.

title: OpenShift Single Node Cluster Installation Failing at 87% with `CRIO-conmon-0111a0ed` and `libcrun` Container Restarts and `503 Service Unavailable` Error
issue: SNO cluster installation fails during the finalization stage, timing out at 87% completion.
OpenShift cluster displays `RouteHealthDegraded: route not yet available` error and Operator console status: Failed
The installation log shows an `503 Service Unavailable` error when the cluster attempts to access its own routes (e.g., console route).

In the host's iLO console, containers named `CRIO-conmon-0111a0ed` and `libcrun` are observed to be continuously restarting, indicating a low-level container runtime issue, but masking the primary failure.
resolution: Manually create the missing DNS entries and ensuring the SNO node can successfully resolve its own routes. 1. **Ensure all Mandatory DNS Records are Created**:- The **API record** `api.. ` must be created and point to the SNO node's IP address.- The **Wildcard Application record** `*.apps.. ` must be created and point to the SNO node's IP address. 2. **Verify DNS Records**: Confirm that the SNO node can successfully resolve these records using `dig` or `nslookup` after the DNS changes are propagated. 3. **Trigger Retest/Reboot**: Once the external DNS records are confirmed to be functioning correctly, the installation will typically resume and complete after a brief waiting period, or after a reboot of the SNO host.
root_cause: The installation failure is caused due to **missing or incorrect mandatory DNS prerequisites** for the cluster. The SNO host is unable to resolve its own application routes because the required wildcard DNS record is missing from the external DNS server. This prevents internal components (like the `console` operator) from communicating correctly, leading directly to the `RouteHealthDegraded` status and the `503 Service Unavailable` errors. The required wildcard DNS record `*.apps.. ` is not available or does not resolve to the SNO node's IP address.

title: OpenShift SNO Installation Fails Due to ETCD Certificate Mismatch on Multiple Network Interfaces
issue: The SNO cluster installation fails or experiences degraded control plane health because a core component attempts to connect to an etcd member using an incorrect IP address (**10.0.0.y**). The etcd server presents a Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate that is only valid for its intended IP address (**10.0.0.x**). The connection attempt fails with a certificate verification error: ``` transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is valid for 10.0.0.x, 127.0.0.1,::1, not 10.0.0.y ``` The OpenShift installer or a cluster component is incorrectly using a secondary or unintended network interface IP for etcd communication.
resolution: **Explicitly disable or deconfigure all secondary network interfaces** during the SNO installation process to ensure only the intended primary IP (**10.0.0.x**) is active for cluster communication. This must be done by providing a **Static Network Configuration** file in YAML format when generating the installation ISO. 1. **Define Static Network Configuration (YAML):** Create a YAML file that explicitly configures the primary interface while setting the state of all other unnecessary interfaces to **`down`**. ```--- interfaces: # 1. PRIMARY INTERFACE (REQUIRED): Use the intended etcd IP (10.0.0.x)- name: enp1s0 type: ethernet state: up ipv4: address:- ip: 10.0.0.x prefix-length: 24 enabled: true # 2. SECONDARY INTERFACE (MUST BE DISABLED): Set state to 'down'- name: enp7s0 type: ethernet state: down ipv4: enabled: false # 3. OTHER INTERFACES (MUST BE DISABLED): Set state to 'down'- name: enp8s0 type: ethernet state: down ipv4: enabled: false ``` Replace the interface names (`enp1s0`, `enp7s0`, `enp8s0`, etc.) and IP addresses with values appropriate for your setup. All interfaces that should not participate in cluster communication must have `state: down` and `ipv4: enabled: false`. 2. **Regenerate and Re-install:** Use this static network configuration YAML when generating the SNO installation media (ISO). Reinstall the SNO cluster using the newly configured image. This ensures the etcd certificate is validated correctly against the single active IP, allowing the cluster to complete the installation successfully.
root_cause: The **presence of multiple active network interfaces** on the SNO host, with one interface receiving an IP address (`10.0.0.112`) that is not included in the TLS certificate generated for the `etcd` endpoint. OpenShift generates etcd certificates only for the **primary IP address** of the SNO node, which should be the only active network endpoint used for cluster communication. When a secondary, active interface exists, cluster components or etcd itself bind to and attempt to connect via this uncertified IP, leading to a handshake failure and preventing the control plane from establishing a quorum.
