title: How to remove Propagated UserTags from machineset to create new ones without old tags in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform on AWS?
issue: It is not possible to remove the "machineset" tag that is implemented at the time of cluster installation. Even after removing the "machineset" tag, old user tags still appear on newly created machines. New nodes come up with the incorrect old tag.
resolution: 1. Remove the old tag from `subresource status infrastructure cluster`: ~~~ $ oc edit--subresource status infrastructure cluster... platform: AWS platformStatus: aws: region: us-east-2 resourceTags:- key: CoreOS_Exception value: "true"- key: OldKey #remove it value: "oldvalue" #remove it type: AWS ~~~ 2. Remove the old tag from `machineset`: ~~~ $ oc edit machineset-n openshift-machine-api... tags:- name: kubernetes.io/cluster/default-tags-745d7 value: owned- name: CoreOS_Exception value: "true"- key: OldKey #remove it value: "oldvalue" #remove it... ~~~ 3. Remove the old tag from the `router-default` service, there are two ways to remove it:- Delete the `router-default` service in the `openshift-ingress` namespace, it will be create new load balancer in AWS without old tag and without `aws-load-balancer-additional-resource-tags` annotation tag in service, this is the recommended approach, because the operator will manage the creation of a new service with updated tags: ~~~ $ oc delete svc router-default-n openshift-ingress ~~~- Or edit the `router-default` service, removing the annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-additional-resource-tags: = `: ~~~ $ oc edit svc router-default-n openshift-ingress kind: Service metadata: annotations: service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-additional-resource-tags: CoreOS_Exception=true, = #remove it service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-healthy-threshold: "2"... ~~~ **Warning** These steps work with `controlplanemachineset`. However, after removing the old tags, the `controlplanemachineset` will recycle the control planes. Any AWS service that is not recreated will remain with the old tag, if the desire is remove it, it should be removed manually in AWS. There is a [KCS to list the tags in AWS resources associated with RHOCP](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3932551).
root_cause: The propagated user tags used to configure the RHOCP `Installer Provisioned Infrastructure(IPI)` cluster on AWS in the `install-config.yaml` file store information in the `infrastructure cluster`, keeping the desired state configured during installation. The `machineset`, `controlplanemachineset`, and `ingress` resources reconcile for the tags.

title: How to Reduce Log Volume in Loki by Dropping Debug and Trace Logs
issue: - Exclude Debug and Trace Logs in OpenShift Loki Logging.- How to Stop vector from collecting Debug and Trace logs in OpenShift
resolution: To Reduce Log Volume in Loki by dropping debug and trace Logs the recommended approach is to use a drop filter in the ClusterLogForwarder. This filter removes unwanted log levels before they are sent to Loki. Here’s a basic example of how to configure the filter: ~~~ filters:- name: drop-debug-trace type: drop drop:- test:- field:.level matches: 'debug'- test:- field:.level matches: 'trace' ~~~ This configuration tells the system to drop logs where the.level is debug or trace, so only more important logs like info, warn, and error are kept. For more details you can refer [Configuring content filters to drop unwanted log records](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.15/html/logging/performance-and-reliability-tuning#logging-input-spec-filteringl).
root_cause: In openshift logging, by default, all log levels are captured. This can lead to unnecessary log ingestion, especially in production environments where only higher-severity logs are typically required. Filtering is implemented by dropping logs based on matching patterns, rather than selecting levels to include.

title: How to Backup a Specific Persistent Volume using OADP in OpenShift
issue: - How to take backup of specific persistent volumes using OADP in openshift namespace?
resolution: - The most precise way to select a specific PVC for backup is by applying a unique label to the PVC and using the `labelSelector` in your [Backup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/backup_and_restore/oadp-application-backup-and-restore#oadp-creating-backup-cr-doc:~:text=Create%20a%20Backup%20CR%2C%20as%20in%20the%20following%20example%3A) resource. ~~~ $ oc label pvc app= $ oc label pvc app= ~~~- Create a backup using a label selector: ~~~ apiVersion: velero.io/v1 kind: Backup metadata: name: labels: velero.io/storage-location: default namespace: openshift-adp spec: hooks: {} includedNamespaces:- includedResources: [] excludedResources: [] storageLocation: ttl: 720h0m0s labelSelector: matchLabels: app: <----- ~~~- List the contents of the backup to ensure that PVC was included: ~~~ $ velero backup describe-n openshift-adp ~~~

title: Pods are running with `anyuid` SCC
issue: - All the OCP cluster pods are running with `anyuid` SCC.- Prometheus, or other application pods are not running and failing with `Permission denied` error. ~~~ level=error ts=ts=yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.2234xx36Z caller=query_logger.go:85 component=activeQueryTracker msg="Error opening query log file" file=/prometheus/queries.active err="open /prometheus/queries.active: permission denied" yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.2234xx36Z panic: Unable to create mmap-ed active query log ~~~
resolution: - **OPTION #1** Remove/delete the `system:openshift:scc:anyuid` ClusterRoleBinding if exists. ~~~ Check if `system:openshift:scc:anyuid` ClusterRoleBinding is present: $ oc get clusterrolebindings | grep-i anyuid Delete the ClusterRoleBinding: $ oc delete clusterrolebindings system:openshift:scc:anyuid ~~~- **OPTION #2** Edit the `system:openshift:scc:anyuid` ClusterRoleBinding; if it contains a service account binding for an affected application then remove that service account binding. ~~~ $ oc edit clusterrolebinding system:openshift:scc:anyuid... subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount # <----- REMOVE BINDING FOR AFFECTED APP SERVICE ACCOUNT name: broken-app-service-account namespace: broken-app-namespace ~~~
root_cause: - After removing the `system:authenticated` group from the `anyuid` SCC, the `system:openshift:scc:anyuid` ClusterRoleBinding still exists in the cluster and caused the issue.

title: Is the CVE-2025-5187 impacting my RHOCP cluster?
issue: - Security scan on my RHOCP cluster is raising a concern about the **CVE-2025-5187**
resolution: The Issue has been raised in the Kubernetes community (Reference: [CVE-2025-5187: Nodes can delete themselves by adding an OwnerReference](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133471)) for the following version:- kube-apiserver: <= v1.31.11- kube-apiserver: <= v1.32.7- kube-apiserver: <= v1.33.3 And has been fixed in versions:- kube-apiserver > = **v1.31.12**- kube-apiserver > = **v1.32.8**- kube-apiserver > = **v1.33.4** As described in the KCS solution [What release of Kubernetes is Red Hat Openshift based on](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7107417), RHOCP **4.18.z** and **4.19.z** are respectively based on Kubernetes v1.31 and v1.32. The issue is fixed from those releases: | Minor Version| kubelet Version | Associate Releases | |---|---|---| | 4.18 | 1.31.12 | 4.18.24 | 4.19 | 1.32.8 | 4.19.12 All previous releases from those minor versions should be considered affected by this bug (exception of 4.19.10 which was based on 1.32.8, before being rolled-back to 1.32.7 in 4.19.11) *Disclaimer: Note that the link provided above points to a web site not owned or controlled by Red Hat. Use information present here at your own discretion.*
root_cause: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where node users can delete their corresponding node object by patching themselves with an OwnerReference to a cluster-scoped resource. If the OwnerReference resource does not exist or is subsequently deleted, the given node object will be deleted via garbage collection. By default, node users are authorized for create and patch requests but not delete requests against their node object. Since the NodeRestriction admission controller does not prevent patching OwnerReferences, a compromised node could leverage this vulnerability to delete and then recreate its node object. This would permit the node object to be recreated with modified taints or labels which are normally rejected by this plugin. Modifying taints or labels on a node could allow an attacker to control which pods are running on the compromised node.

title: Data Corruption when attaching a DataVolume or PVC to multiple VMs in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: Data Corruption after inadvertently attaching the same disk to multiple VMs
DataVolume in OpenShift Virtualization is attached to multiple VMs, causing data corruption due to concurrent updates.
Attaching one DataVolume to multiple VMs is technically possible but can lead to data corruption.
resolution: * Avoid attaching the same disk to multiple VMs, unless it is really intended to be used as a shared disk. * An issue is raised to improve the product and add extra protection around these situations to detect unitended multiple attaches: [CNV-70323- Guardrails around attaching same disk to multiple VMs are missing.](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-70323)
root_cause: * Usually, each Virtual Machine has its own unique disks, not shared with any other VMs. In specific circumstances, Disk may be shared between many VMs (vm.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks.shareable), but these are special disks usually with clustered filesystems that support multiple mounting, or coordinate the mounting only on a single VM at a time. * While OpenShift Virtualization allows setting the disk as shareable, it doesn't prevent multiple VMs with the same disk and without this property set from starting up simultaneously.

title: Uninstall Red Hat build of Cryostat Operator using CLI
issue: - How do I uninstall Red Hat build of Cryostat Operator?
resolution: The following example assumes that Red Hat build of Cryostat Operator is installed in `cryostat-operator` namespace. 1. Remove the labels `cryostat.io/name` and `cryostat.io/namespace`, which are used to attach the Cryostat agent, from the Deployment monitored by Cryostat. This operation will trigger a restart of the Pods: ~~~ $ oc get deployment app-n app apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata:... spec:... template: metadata:... labels: deployment: app cryostat.io/name: "cryostat-sample" < < <=== cryostat.io/namespace: "cryostat" < < <=== spec: $ oc patch deployment app-n app--type='json'-p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/metadata/labels/cryostat.io~1name"},{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/metadata/labels/cryostat.io~1namespace"}]' ~~~ 2. Delete `kind: cryostat` custom resources: ~~~ $ oc get cryostat--all-namespaces NAMESPACE NAME APPLICATION URL TARGET NAMESPACES STORAGE SECRET DATABASE SECRET cryostat cryostat-sample https://cryostat-sample-cryostat.apps.nagetsum-ocp416.apac.aws.cee.support ["app"] cryostat-sample-storage cryostat-sample-db $ oc delete cryostat cryostat-sample-n cryostat ~~~ 3. Delete subscription and csv from `cryostat-operator` namespace: ~~~ $ oc get subscription--all-namespaces NAMESPACE NAME PACKAGE SOURCE CHANNEL cert-manager-operator openshift-cert-manager-operator openshift-cert-manager-operator redhat-operators stable-v1 cryostat-operator cryostat-operator cryostat-operator redhat-operators stable $ oc delete subscription cryostat-operator-n cryostat-operator $ oc get csv NAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE cert-manager-operator.v1.17.0 cert-manager Operator for Red Hat OpenShift 1.17.0 cert-manager-operator.v1.16.1 Succeeded cryostat-operator.v4.0.3 Red Hat build of Cryostat 4.0.3 cryostat-operator.v4.0.2-4 Succeeded $ oc delete csv cryostat-operator.v4.0.3 ~~~ 4. Optional: If the Cryostat Operator is installed in a namespace other than `openshift-operators`, and that namespace is dedicated solely to the Cryostat Operator, delete the OperatorGroup and the Project. If the Cryostat Operator is installed in `openshift-operators` namespace, do **NOT** perform this step. ~~~ $ oc get operatorgroup-n cryostat-operator NAME AGE cryostat-operator-pqtwv 17h $ oc delete operatorgroup cryostat-operator-pqtwv-n cryostat-operator $ oc delete project cryostat-operator ~~~ 5. Delete cluster-level resources created by the Cryostat Operator: ~~~ $ oc delete CustomResourceDefinition cryostats.operator.cryostat.io $ oc delete operator cryostat-operator.cryostat-operator ~~~ 6. If one also want to uninstall `cert-manager` Operator, which is a dependency of the Cryostat Operator, follow the steps described in document [9.13. Uninstalling the cert-manager Operator for Red Hat OpenShift](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/security_and_compliance/cert-manager-operator-for-red-hat-openshift#cert-manager-operator-uninstall). There is a known issue [OCPBUGS-44742 cert-manager crd hangs on an uninstall](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-44742) when uninstall `cert-manager` Operator.

title: Once the cumulative number of Cryostat targets reaches 26 Pods, any Pods launched afterward are no longer displayed in the Topology view.
issue: When 26 or more Pods are started at once, or when 25 Pods are running and then one Pod is scaled down and scaled up again, the newly started Pods with the Cryostat agent attached are not detected and does not appear in the Topology view. ~~~ $ oc scale deployment/app--replicas=26-n app ~~~ or ~~~ $ oc scale deployment/app--replicas=25-n app $ oc scale deployment/app--replicas=24-n app $ oc scale deployment/app--replicas=25-n app ~~~ At this time, the following error can be seen in the logs of the Cryostat Pod: `ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "discoverynode_pkey"`. ~~~ $ oc logs-c cryostat-sample cryostat-sample-99fc47f8f-j79kt... 2025-09-18 05:10:28,543 WARN [org.hib.eng.jdb.spi.SqlExceptionHelper] (executor-thread-27) SQL Error: 0, SQLState: 23505 2025-09-18 05:10:28,544 ERROR [org.hib.eng.jdb.spi.SqlExceptionHelper] (executor-thread-27) ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "discoverynode_pkey" Detail: Key (id)=(8) already exists. 2025-09-18 05:10:28,552 WARN [io.cry.ExceptionMappers] (executor-thread-27) org.hibernate.exception.ConstraintViolationException: could not execute statement [ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "discoverynode_pkey" Detail: Key (id)=(8) already exists.] [insert into DiscoveryNode (labels,name,nodeType,parentNode,id) values (?,?,?,?,?)] ~~~
resolution: This is caused by a known issue in Cryostat and has been fixed in Red Hat build of Cryostat 4.0.3. Unfortunately, no workaround is available. The fix [#1057](https://github.com/cryostatio/cryostat/pull/1057) has already been merged in the upstream project.

title: Is it supported to change the subnet mask/IP information of the nodes post deployment in RHOCP4.x?
issue: - Is it supported to change the `subnet mask`/`IP` information of the nodes post deployment in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x?
resolution: - **Changing the IP address or Subnet Mask of a node is not supported (without redeploying the node), this is applicable for the primary interface which is used for cluster communication.**- It is recommended to decide network topology prior to cluster deployment. Making any changes post deployment may hamper the behavior of `OpenShift-SDN` or `OpenShift-OVN-Kubernetes` causing complete cluster breakdown.- In the case where a full network change is necessary (to neighboring subnets for example), it is recommended to initiate a new cluster installation with the network changes.- Secondary interface changes are still possible casewise, hence open a new Red Hat ticket to know recommendation for the possible extent of change.

title: Creating a full backup in RHDG 8.2+
issue: What is the process of creating a backup in zip in DG 8? How to confirm the creation of the backup zip?
resolution: Putting data inside: ~~~ [user-2089@cluster//containers/default/caches/___script_cache]> put 1 abcd [user-2089@cluster//containers/default/caches/___script_cache]> get 1 abcd ~~~ ### **Backup Creation:** For Backup creation see [here](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.2/html/data_grid_command_line_interface/backup): ~~~ ### backup creation [fdemeloj-2089@cluster//containers/default/caches/___script_cache]> backup create Creating backup 'Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425'... ### backup listing [fdemeloj-2089@cluster//containers/default/caches/___script_cache]> backup ls ["Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425"]... ### export as zip file: [fdemeloj-2089@cluster//containers/default/caches/___script_cache]> backup get Red\ Hat\ Data\ Grid-20220511115425 Downloading backup Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425 Downloaded file 'Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425.zip' <----... ### export as zip listing [fdemeloj-2089@cluster//containers/default/caches/___script_cache]> backup ls ["Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425"]... ### see the zip file on $RHDG root path: [fdemeloj@fdemeloj redhat-datagrid-8.3.0-server]$ ls bin boot Copyright.txt docs lib README.adoc Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425.zip server static version.txt... To see the zip data... ~~~ ### **Backup Inspection:** ~~~ [fdemeloj@fdemeloj redhat-datagrid-8.3.0-server]$ unzip-l Red\ Hat\ Data\ Grid-20220511121300.zip Archive: Red Hat Data Grid-20220511121300.zip Length Date Time Name... 354 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/container.properties 0 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/counters/counters.dat 517 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.SCATTERED_SYNC.xml 384 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.LOCAL.xml 445 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.INVALIDATION_SYNC.xml 483 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.REPL_SYNC.xml 462 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.REPL_ASYNC.xml 424 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.INVALIDATION_ASYNC.xml 464 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.DIST_ASYNC.xml 485 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/org.infinispan.DIST_SYNC.xml 671 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/templates/example.PROTOBUF_DIST.xml 2726 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/global.xml 1 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/tasks/abcd <--- data 1 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/tasks/abc <--- data 4 05-11-2022 12:13 containers/default/tasks/1 <--- data 100 05-11-2022 12:13 manifest.properties... 7521 16 files ~~~ Important during the creation of the backup: ~~~ 2022-05-11 11:54:25,956 INFO (non-blocking-thread--p2-t16) [org.infinispan.server.core.backup.BackupManagerImpl] ISPN005043: Starting backup 'Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425' 2022-05-11 11:54:26,113 INFO (non-blocking-thread--p2-t15) [org.infinispan.server.core.backup.BackupManagerImpl] ISPN005044: Backup file created 'Red Hat Data Grid-20220511115425.zip' ~~~ ### Restore After the file backup is created one can restore it in another cluster by the `backup restore` command: ~~~ backup restore /path/data/red_hat_data_grid.zip ~~~ There might or might not be a `null` message after the operation, but it does not mean the restore failed. ### Process on OCP 4 As described on [DG Operator- Backup & Restore](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.2/guide/9721c7a2-584b-4974-bbee-791283fd9242), on the DG Operator create a new CR Batch, the process will create a pod (with default 1 cpu and 1Gi memory) that is not a "standard" node. It has zero-capacity=true, so no state transfer occurs when it joins the cluster. Then a storage (PVC) will be created and a pod to run this process. The pod will do the process (create the backup)- the backup.zip is created on a PVC named after the Backup CR: ~~~ apiVersion: infinispan.org/v2alpha1 kind: Backup metadata: name: an-example-backup namespace: a-namespace spec: cluster: a-cluster container: cpu: 1000m extraJvmOpts: '-Djava.property=me' memory: 1Gi ~~~ Another option to create a backup and apply it as a restore is to connect the [cli inside](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6971393) in the pod and do it manually: `./bin/cli.sh-c-`; backup created; `backup restore /opt/infinispan/server/data/red_hat_data_grid-example.zip`. For manual generation inside a pod, the backup will be located inside: `/opt/infinispan/server/data/backups`. Example: ~~~ sh-5.1$ cd /opt/infinispan/server/data/backups sh-5.1$ ls 'Red Hat Data Grid-20251007065013' ~~~
root_cause: Backup and restore command were implemented DG 8.2.x. Also one could use REST request to get some data from DG 8, but downloading by http is not implemented. [DG 8- 2.1.12. Retrieving Data By Keys](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.3/html/data_grid_rest_api/index) ~~~ GET /rest/v2/caches/{cacheName}/{cacheKey} ~~~

title: oc explain does not provide information on OpenShift Pipelines (Tekton) resources
issue: - Executing `oc explain` on api-resources of the group `tekton.dev` does not provide any information. For example querying for `tasks.tekton.dev.spec` results in an error: ~~~ $ oc explain tasks.tekton.dev.spec *Output
GROUP: tekton.dev KIND: Task VERSION: v1 error: field "spec" does not exist ~~~
resolution: - This issue has been fixed in OpenShift Pipelines version 1.19, details can be found in the [release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_pipelines/1.19/html/release_notes/op-release-notes#pac-new-features-1-19_op-release-notes).
root_cause: - The `CustomResourceDefinitions` for the group `tekton.dev` are missing schema descriptions and therefore do not provide the required information for the `oc explain` command.

title: mirror registry fails to start due to missing podman secret for quay-redis.service
issue: We are not able to access the mirror registry: Oct 06 15:45:53 mirror-registry.example.com podman[633919]: Error: running container create option: no secret with name or id "redis_pass": no such secret Oct 06 15:45:53 mirror-registry.example.com podman[633919]: 2025-10-06 15:45:53.774249844 +0530 IST m=+0.016089865 image pull 98e8e93480964fcefedcc65a9c29ab9e23eb055cd0973c3764fbbb2abe290c1e registry.redhat.io/rhel8/redis-6:1-190 Oct 06 15:45:53 mirror-registry.example.com systemd[1]: quay-redis.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=125/n/a
resolution: Recreate the missing Podman secret using the same Redis password found in the Quay `config.yaml`. The password is located at the `USER_EVENTS_REDIS.password` path in the YAML file: ~~~ # yq-r '.USER_EVENTS_REDIS.password' /path/to/quayroot/config.yaml | tr-d '\n' | podman secret create redis_pass- ~~~
root_cause: The `redis_pass` podman secret required by `quay-redis.service` is missing from the mirror registry host.

title: OpenShift Virtualization Engine VM in OpenShift ServiceMesh cannot connect to any resources
issue: trying to connect to any resource inside a VM inside OpenShift ServiceMesh(OSSM) fails with ~~~ curl https://www.google.com-Ik ~~~
example output ~~~ curl: (16) OpenSSL SSL_write: error:80000020:system library::Broken pipe, errno 32 ~~~
resolution: * Red Hat is aware of this issue and is working on enhancing a future version of Red Hat OpenShift ServiceMesh. * apply the annotation `istio.io/reroute-virtual-interfaces` by executing following command ~~~ oc patch vm--type=merge-p \ '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"istio.io/reroute-virtual-interfaces": "k6t-eth0"}}}}}' ~~~
root_cause: * Istio upstream deprecation of the annotation `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/kubevirtInterfaces` * missing annotation of `istio.io/reroute-virtual-interfaces` creates nft rules that do not capture and rewrite traffic accordingly

title: OpenShift Virtualization Engine VM in OpenShift ServiceMesh cannot resolve a names through DNS
issue: trying to resolve to any resource inside a VM running inside OpenShift ServiceMesh(OSSM) fails with ~~~ curl: (6) Could not resolve host: www.google.com ~~~
resolution: * Red Hat is aware of this issue and is working on enhancing a future version of Red Hat OpenShift ServiceMesh. * apply the `proxy.istio.io/config` annotation to the VM by executing following command ~~~ oc patch vm--type=merge-p \ '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"proxy.istio.io/config": "proxyMetadata: \n ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE: \"false\""}}}}}' ~~~ * stop the VM by executing following command ~~~ oc patch vm--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"runStrategy":"Halted"}}' # deprecated stopping of the VM through running attribute # oc patch vm--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"running":false}}' ~~~ * start the VM by executing following command ~~~ oc patch vm--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"runStrategy":"RerunOnFailure"}}' # deprecated starting of the VM through running attribute # oc patch vm--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"running":true}}' ~~~

title: Logging/Collection dashboards shows No datapoints found for Produced Logs in RHOCP4
issue: - Logging/Collection dashboards shows `No datapoints found` for "Produced Logs" in Logging: [image=[src="images/5.8_before_reinstall.png", alt="No datapoints found for 'Produced Logs'", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", caption="No datapoints found for 'Produced Logs'", lightbox="true"]]
resolution: - To enable monitoring for the "openshift-logging" namespace, apply the label "openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true"": ~~~ $ oc label namespace openshift-logging openshift.io/cluster-monitoring=true ~~~- Starting from RHOL version 5.8, `LogFileMetricsExport` needs to be enabled to collect container related metrics. ####Creating a `LogFileMetricExporter` instance- A `LogFileMetricExporter` instance can be created using the `yaml` below as an example. Copy the content in a file and create the instance using command `oc create-f `, adapting in case that needed the `nodeSelector` and `tolerations`: ~~~ apiVersion: logging.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: LogFileMetricExporter metadata: name: instance namespace: openshift-logging spec: nodeSelector: {} resources: limits: cpu: 500m memory: 256Mi requests: cpu: 200m memory: 128Mi tolerations: [] ~~~- Above command will create new `logfilesmetricexporter` pods in `openshift-logging` namespace. Check that a `logfilesmetricexporter` pod is running in parallel in the same node that a collector pod is running: ~~~ $ oc get pods-l app.kubernetes.io/component=logfilesmetricexporter-n openshift-logging NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE logfilesmetricexporter-xxxxx 1/1 Running 0 40m logfilesmetricexporter-yyyyy 1/1 Running 0 40m [...] ~~~- After few minutes, the metrics data should be visible in Dashboard: [image=[src="images/upgrade_5.8.png", alt="After creating logmetricexporter metrics are visible", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", caption="After creating logmetricexporter metrics are visible", lightbox="true"]]
root_cause: The `logfilemetricexporter` is no longer deployed with the collector deployment by default. To get the produced metrics, it has to be deployed explicitly as per the procedure mention in the Resolution section.

title: Configure Lifecycle Policies on S3 buckets
issue: - How to configure a Lifecycle Policy for a Noobaa bucket- How to configure a Lifecycle Policy for an RGW bucket
resolution: 1) Create a bucket-lifecycle file called "lifecycle.json" with the following: NOTE: change the 'Days' ({n}) to match how long you want to keep files in the bucket for 1 days means noobaa/rgw will purge ALL objects older than a day. ~~~ {"Rules": [{"Expiration": {"Days": {n}}, "ID": "data-expire-withoutprefix", "Filter": {"Prefix": ""}, "Status": "Enabled"}]} ~~~ 2) Gather the secret key, access key, and endpoint URL from the proper secrets (oc get secrets) in your cluster. 3) Create an alias for the s3 cmd to keep track of the secret and access keys: ~~~ alias s3api-120='AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID= AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY= aws s3api--no-verify-ssl--endpoint-url ' ~~~ 4) Apply the lifecycle policy to the bucket: ~~~ s3api-120 put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration--bucket--lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle.json ~~~ 5) Double check the policy was applied: ~~~ s3api-120 get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration--bucket {"Rules": [{"Expiration": {"Days": 1}, "ID": "data-expire-withoutprefix", "Filter": {"Prefix": ""}, "Status": "Enabled"}]} ~~~

title: Receiving KubeletTooManyPods alert
issue: - How to verify if the alert `KubeletTooManyPods` is true?- A node is allowed to schedule `250` pods on it. The number of pods running on the node are `less` than 250.- Still the alert-manager is throwing `KubeletTooManyPods` alert.
resolution: - Consider that the affected node is allowed to schedule 250 pods on it.- Check the total number of `running` pods on the node: ~~~ $ oc get pods-A-o wide | grep | grep 'Running' | wc-l ~~~- If the output is `greater` than 250, then the alert received is true.- In order to resolve this, there are two options:- [Modify maximum number of pods per node](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-managing-max-pods.html)- [Distribute the load across workers nodes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/nodes/scheduling/nodes-scheduler-about.html)- However, if the output of the command is `less` than 250, then the alert received is false.- The issue was filed as a bug: [BZ-1846805](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1846805) and has been fixed in the ERRATA: [RHBA-2020:4196- Bug Fix Advisory](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2020:4196).- The query `kubelet_running_pod_count` used in the alert `KubeletTooManyPods` also takes `Completed` pods into consideration. ~~~- alert: KubeletTooManyPods annotations: message: Kubelet '{{$labels.node}}' is running at {{$value | humanizePercentage}} of its Pod capacity. expr: | max(max(kubelet_running_pod_count{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics"}) by(instance) * on(instance) group_left(node) kubelet_node_name{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics"}) by(node) / max(kube_node_status_capacity_pods{job="kube-state-metrics"}) by(node) > 0.95 for: 15m labels: severity: warning ~~~- To verify this, check the total number of running as well as completed pods on the node: ~~~ $ oc get pods-A-o wide | grep | grep 'Running|Completed' | wc-l ~~~- The output should be `greater` than 250.- The alert received should `not` cause any `problem` as Completed pods `do not consume` any resources.- The node will still schedule pods on it.- The only work-around for this is to `silence` the alert:- [Silencing alerts](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.4/monitoring/cluster_monitoring/managing-cluster-alerts.html#monitoring-silencing-alerts_managing-alerts)
root_cause: - There is a problem in the design at Kubernetes/Kubelet level. Kubelet is reporting number of running pods with `kubelet_running_pod_count` which includes `Completed` pods.- Kubernetes upstream issue: [kubelet_running_pod_count includes completed pods](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92180) `Disclaimer`: Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. title: Restarting ovnkube-node pod also restarts the multus pod
issue: - Restarting the `ovnkube-node` pod also restarts the `multus` pod running on the same node.- Multus pod remains in a `CrashLoopBackOff` state until the `ovnkube-node` pod on the same node either in `CrashLoopBackOff` state or is not in a `Running` state.
resolution: This is `expected behavior` because, during a `restart`, the `readinessindicatorfile` will be `recreated`. Once the `ovnkube-node` pod restarts, it `generates` a new file on the node.
root_cause: The Configuration file inside the `multus` pod specifies the `readinessindicatorfile` as follows: ~~~ $ oc rsh pod/multus-r5gbw sh-4.4# cat /etc/cni/net.d/multus.d/daemon-config.json|grep readinessindicatorfile "readinessindicatorfile": "/host/run/multus/cni/net.d/10-ovn-kubernetes.conf", sh-4.4# ~~~

title: Workaround for model deployment failure when using hardware profiles
issue: Model deployments that use hardware profiles fail because the Red Hat OpenShift AI Operator does not inject the `tolerations`, `nodeSelector`, or `identifiers` from the hardware profile into the underlying `InferenceService` when manually creating `InferenceService` resources. As a result, the model deployment pods cannot be scheduled to suitable nodes and the deployment fails to enter a ready state. Workbenches that use the same hardware profile deploy successfully.
resolution: To resolve this issue, run the following script to manually inject the `tolerations`, `nodeSelector`, and `identifiers` from the hardware profile into the underlying `InferenceService`. Replace the HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAME, HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAMESPACE, ISVC_NAME, and ISVC_NAMESPACE values for your environment. ~~~ #!/bin/bash # This script manually injects a HardwareProfile nodeSelector, tolerations, and identifiers into an InferenceService at the correct path. set-e HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAME=" " HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAMESPACE=" " ISVC_NAME=" " ISVC_NAMESPACE=" " # Extract nodeSelector from HardwareProfile NODE_SELECTOR=$(oc get hardwareprofiles.infrastructure.opendatahub.io "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAME}"-n "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAMESPACE}" \-o jsonpath='{.spec.scheduling.node.nodeSelector}') # Extract tolerations from HardwareProfile TOLERATIONS=$(oc get hardwareprofiles.infrastructure.opendatahub.io "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAME}"-n "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAMESPACE}" \-o jsonpath='{.spec.scheduling.node.tolerations}') # Extract identifiers (resources) from HardwareProfile IDENTIFIERS=$(oc get hardwareprofiles.infrastructure.opendatahub.io "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAME}"-n "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAMESPACE}" \-o jsonpath='{.spec.identifiers}') # Build the patch JSON for nodeSelector if [-n "${NODE_SELECTOR}"] && ["${NODE_SELECTOR}"!= "{}"]; then oc patch inferenceservice "${ISVC_NAME}"-n "${ISVC_NAMESPACE}"--type=merge-p "{\"spec\":{\"predictor\":{\"nodeSelector\":${NODE_SELECTOR}}}}" fi # Build the patch JSON for tolerations if [-n "${TOLERATIONS}"] && ["${TOLERATIONS}"!= "null"]; then oc patch inferenceservice "${ISVC_NAME}"-n "${ISVC_NAMESPACE}"--type=merge-p "{\"spec\":{\"predictor\":{\"tolerations\":${TOLERATIONS}}}}" fi # Build the patch JSON for resources (from identifiers) if [-n "${IDENTIFIERS}"] && ["${IDENTIFIERS}"!= "null"]; then # Parse identifiers and build resources object RESOURCES=$(oc get hardwareprofiles.infrastructure.opendatahub.io "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAME}"-n "${HARDWARE_PROFILE_NAMESPACE}"-o jsonpath='{range.spec.identifiers[*]}{.identifier}{"\t"}{.defaultCount}{"\n"}{end}') # Build a proper resources patch from identifiers cat > /tmp/resources-patch.json < > /tmp/resources-patch.json # Remove trailing comma and close JSON sed-i '$ s/,$//' /tmp/resources-patch.json cat > > /tmp/resources-patch.json < > /tmp/resources-patch.json # Remove trailing comma and close JSON sed-i '$ s/,$//' /tmp/resources-patch.json cat > > /tmp/resources-patch.json <
root_cause: The Red Hat OpenShift AI Operator does not inject the `tolerations`, `nodeSelector`, or `identifiers` from the hardware profile into the underlying `InferenceService` when manually creating `InferenceService` resources.

title: Is RHEL 9 package mode supported as a worker node for RHOCP 4?
issue: - Is it possible to use a RHEL 9 package mode worker node with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP)?
resolution: - RHEL 9 package mode nodes are not supported as a worker nodes for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP).- RHEL 8 package mode can be used as worker nodes, however, note that RHEL machines are deprecated in OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 and will be removed in a future release.- In 4.18 and up, off and on-cluster layering are available and fully supported. This functionality allows you to customize the RHCOS nodes as needed. See https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/machine_configuration/mco-coreos-layering

title: [RHACS] Is it possible to change the expiration date of the init-bundle certificate?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - The certificate included in the `init-bundle` secret, which allows `SecuredCluster` components to communicate with `Central`, has an expiration period of `one year`.- Is there a supported feature or procedure to modify this expiration period?
resolution: - No. There is no supported feature or procedure to change the expiration date of the certificate included in the `init-bundle` secret.
root_cause: - To update the expiration date of the `init-bundle` certificate, the secret in the namespace where `SecuredCluster` is deployed must be deleted. A new `init-bundle` should then be downloaded and applied.- For details, refer to [the documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/latest/html/configuring/reissue-internal-certificates#reissue-internal-certificates-secured-clusters_reissue-internal-certificates).

title: [RHACS] Is it possible to change the expiration date of Central's CA certificate?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - According to [the documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.8/html/configuring/reissue-internal-certificates#reissue-internal-certificates-central_reissue-internal-certificates), the expiration date of Central's CA certificate is set to 5 years and is not automatically updated.- Is it possible to change the expiration date of Central's CA certificate?
resolution: - No. There is no feature or supported procedure to change the expiration date of the CA certificate.
root_cause: - If the expiration date of Central's CA certificate needs to be changed, it must be done manually. For details, refer to the KCS.

title: How to create ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding after accidental deletion of Quay Operator's subscription
issue: Quay Operator Subscription was accidentally deleted.
Unable to access Quay instances due to missing permissions.

Error message: 'quayregistries.quay.redhat.com "quay" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:openshift-operators:quay-operator" cannot get resource "quayregistries" in API group "quay.redhat.com" in the namespace "quay-project-name"'
resolution: Here is the yaml file to restore ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. 1. Create a yaml file clusterRoleRestore.yaml ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: quay-operator-permissions rules:- apiGroups:- quay.redhat.com resources:- quayregistries- quayregistries/status verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- apps resources:- deployments verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- "" resources:- pods- services- secrets- configmaps- serviceaccounts- persistentvolumeclaims- events verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- "" resources:- namespaces verbs:- get- watch- list- update- patch- apiGroups:- rbac.authorization.k8s.io resources:- roles- rolebindings verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- route.openshift.io resources:- routes- routes/custom-host verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- autoscaling resources:- horizontalpodautoscalers verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- objectbucket.io resources:- objectbucketclaims verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- monitoring.coreos.com resources:- prometheusrules- servicemonitors verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- batch resources:- jobs verbs:- '*'- apiGroups:- "" resources:- namespaces verbs:- get- list- watch--- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: name: quay-operator-permissions-binding subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: quay-operator namespace: openshift-operators roleRef: kind: ClusterRole name: quay-operator-permissions apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io ~~~ 2. Now apply the clusterRole ~~~ #apply-f clusterRoleRestore.yaml ~~~ 3. Check the newly created clusterRole and clusterRoleBinding ~~~ #omc get clusterrole #omc get clusterrolebindings ~~~ 4. Scale down and scale up Quay deployments and check Quay pod's status.
root_cause: - ClusterRoleBinding was missing hence quay operator's service account lost cluster-wide permissions

title: Multi-part Image Push Failure to S3 with Unknown Error in Red Hay Quay
issue: Failure to push multi-part images from Quay to S3 storage
Error message: '{"code":"BLOB_UPLOAD_UNKNOWN","detail":{},"message":"blob upload unknown to registry"}]'
resolution: After adding this feature server_side_assembly: false, the issue was fixed. ~~~ DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default:- RadosGWStorage- access_key: abcdekey bucket_name: quay hostname: storage-host-name is_secure: false port: 9000 secret_key: abcdepass storage_path: /datastorage/registry server_side_assembly: false <----- this was added DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_DEFAULT_LOCATIONS: ["default"] DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_PREFERENCE:- default FEATURE_PROXY_STORAGE: true ~~~
root_cause: The default server-side assembly of blob chunk did not work.

title: Quay Instance Generating Abnormal LDAP Traffic with Non-Existent User Queries
issue: Quay instance is generating abnormal traffic on LDAP servers.
LDAP queries are being made for accounts not present on LDAP.
resolution: The issue is being followed by this Jira ticket [Quay calls LDAP on robot account login](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-90060)

title: How to reduce the Persistent Volume Claim(PVC) size of Virtual Machines in Openshift Virtualization ?
issue: - Is it possible to reduce the disk size of a Virtual Machine in OpenShift Virtualization?
resolution: The shrinking of PVC is not supported by Red Hat and it is mentioned in the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html-single/virtualization/index#virt-expanding-vm-disks). Workaround:- Create a new PVC with the desired size and migrate the data from the existing PVC to the newly created one and follow the [article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5794841) for migrating data.
root_cause: - Openshift does not support shrinking of Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) due to data integrity and to prevent data loss.

title: How to fix the quay clair application pods which are continuously restarting due to Out of Memory (OOM) issue ?
issue: - The quay clair app pods are restarting and failing with exit code 137.
resolution: The below are the solutions to fix the issue- Increase the memory limit of pod: This ensures that the pod has enough resources allocated to it to avoid being terminated by the OOM killer.- Increase the memory of the node: If increasing the memory limit of the pod does not resolve the issue then we need to [increase the memory resources on the node](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3048681) where the pods are scheduled. This prevents memory starvation at the node level.
root_cause: The exit code 137 indicates that the pod was killed by a SIGKILL signal and this happens when a process managed by cgroups is forcibly terminated due to memory constraints. The below are the reasons as shown below- The memory usage of the pod exceeded its configured memory limit.- The memory of the node is exhausted and the pod was terminated to free up resources.

title: oc-mirror is mirroring all versions of the ansible-automation-platform-operator regardless of the value specified in minVersion/maxVersion in RHOCP 4
issue: - `oc-mirror` is not honouring the `minVersion` and `maxVersion` set for `ansible-automation-platform-operator` operator and instead mirroring images related to all the versions.- `oc-mirror` is mirroring all versions of the `ansible-automation-platform-operator` regardless of the value specified in `minVersion/maxVersion`.
resolution: - At present, there is no option to filter for a specific range of the `ansible-automation-platform-operator` until the bug [OCPBUGS-61104](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-61104) is fixed.- As a workaround, either proceed with all versions as it currently behaves when `minVersion/maxVersion` are set or use the channel without any `minVersion/maxVersion` set, it will help to mirror only latest version available in the specified channel, example shown below: ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1 kind: ImageSetConfiguration mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.18 packages:- name: ansible-automation-platform-operator defaultChannel: stable-2.5 channels:- name: stable-2.5--------> it will help to mirror the latest version available in the channel ~~~
root_cause: This has been identified as a bug as mentioned in [OCPBUGS-61104](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-61104).

title: buildah fails with masking non-directory in mount namespace: permission denied
issue: When running buildah on OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 cluster, `useradd` or `groupadd` commands fail with the following error message: ~~~ error running subprocess: masking non-directory "/var/tmp/buildah1757143299/mnt/rootfs/proc/interrupts" in mount namespace: permission denied ~~~
The observed error only occurs using buildah image `1.40.0`, using image tag `1.39.3` works
resolution: * **Fix Provided in New Release:** Red Hat investigated this issue in bug reports [RHEL-92000](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-92000) and [RHEL-100030](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-100030) and delivered a fix in OpenShift Container Platform 4.16.47 / 4.17.40 / 4.18.24 through errata [RHBA-2025:9456](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:9456). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. * As a workaround, there are two possible options: * Use buildah image tag `1.39.3` * Or add buildah parameter `--security-opt=unmask=/proc/interrupts`

title: aws-cloud-controller-manager failure after OpenShift 4.19 upgrade
issue: After upgrading from OpenShift Container Platform 4.18.z to 4.19.6, the `aws-cloud-controller-manager` pods no longer start and show the following error message: ``` MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "config-accm": configmap "cloud-conf" not found ```
resolution: **Fix Provided in New Release:** Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [OCPBUGS-60950](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-60950) and delivered a fix in OpenShift Container Platform 4.19.10 through errata [RHBA-2025:14823](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:14823). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: Earlier releases of OpenShift Container Platform, such as 4.16, did not create the `cloud-conf` config map which the OpenShift Container Platform 4.19 release expects to exist.

title: What to check if custom CA has been leaked from OpenShift Container Platform 4 cluster.
issue: The cluster’s custom Certificate Authority (CA) private key was exposed, allowing potential attackers to issue trusted certificates. This compromises authentication and TLS trust across OpenShift components. Immediate CA rotation and certificate reissuance are required to restore cluster integrity.
resolution: If the CA's private key was leaked, it's a serious security incident. If only the public CA certificate is leaked (i.e no private key), impact is minimal. What an attacker can do if the private key is leaked:- Mint valid TLS server certs and impersonate API server, etcd, ingress, webhooks — enabling MITM.- Sign client certificates to authenticate as users/components (kubelets, controllers) and get cluster access.- Forge mTLS for service-to-service traffic if you rely on that CA.- Bypass TLS-based controls and issue trusted certs for internal services. Rotate the CA is a must as per [procedure](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/security_and_compliance/configuring-certificates#updating-ca-bundle). Create a new CA and reissue all server + client certs (API server, kubelets, etcd, ingress, webhooks, kubeconfigs). Additionally it is recommended to:- Revoke and replace kubeconfigs and short-lived credentials.- Inspect audit logs for suspicious activity and isolate affected nodes.- Tighten RBAC and network policies while you recover.

title: TLS Certificate Auto-Renewal causes Prometheus pods to restart in  RHOCP 4
issue: - Prometheus pods `(prometheus-k8s-0, prometheus-k8s-1)` in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace were observed to restart unexpectedly. Upon investigation, the restarts coincided with the auto-renewal of the TLS secret` (prometheus-k8s-tls)` used by the `Prometheus` instances.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [OBSDOCS-2495](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDOCS-2495). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: - As per [Official Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/security_and_compliance/certificate-types-and-descriptions#expiration-10) monitoring components use service CA certificates to secure their traffic. These certificates are system-managed and automatically rotated if they reside in the openshift-monitoring or openshift-logging namespaces. Each certificate is valid for two years and is automatically replaced upon service CA rotation, which occurs every 13 months.- This is expected platform behavior. `Secrets` are recreated and updated as part of the certificate lifecycle, causing short-lived pod restarts `(Prometheus)`, which automatically recover. No manual intervention is needed unless pods fail to recover.

title: What Server Signature Algorithm are used in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?
issue: - What are the Server Signature Algorithm in use with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?- Is the rsa_pkcs1_sha224 of TLS 1.2. being used in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform?- Is there any configuration option for Server Signature Algorithms in RHOCP Ingress/ HAProxy?
resolution: ####Server Signature Algorithm in use with Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform- The TLS artefacts in use for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform can be found from which contains all the certificate information in.- As can be seen it contains the information on all certificate types generated by OpenShift in the `CertMetadata`. The `SignatureAlgorithm` is logged as well.- OpenShift only generates certificates with SHA256-RSA or ECDSA-SHA256 signatures for 4.12, 4.14 and later releases.- To further improve certificate strength SHA-1 certificates are no longer supported for use with HAProxy since Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 and will be rejected as can be seen in [4.16 release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes.html)- The primary security requirement is met because the Server Certificate itself is signed with SHA-256 (or ECDSA-SHA256), not SHA-224. This is a core function of Red Hat OpenShift Container platform. The pen test is reporting an available protocol capability, not a deployed signature.- The same holds true if custom certificates are used for API/Ingress certificates. Customers need to verify the Server Certificate signing to be SHA-256 or higher to not be exposed to this issue. ####Special notes on Server Signature Algorithm rsa_pkcs1_sha224- Regarding the Signature Algorithm `rsa_pkcs1_sha224` usage in TLS 1.2 protocol, signature algorithms used for key exchange are specified via the list of supported cipher suites.- At this time they can not be configured separately in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform.- HAProxy has added a configuration named [`ssl-default-bind-client-sigalgs`](https://www.haproxy.com/documentation/haproxy-configuration-manual/2-7r1/#ssl-default-bind-client-sigalgs). As of RHOCP 4.16 Red Hat is shipping HAProxy version 2.8 which does ship this configuration option. But it is currently not possible to configure this in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. An [RFE-4958](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4958) has been raised to address this and is being reviewed.- But as stated above OpenShift only generates certificates with SHA256-RSA or ECDSA-SHA256 signatures. Regardless of the client's request, only certificates with these two types of signatures are provided.-

title: Role.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller" is invalid: rules[407].nonResourceURLs: Invalid value: []string{"/metrics"}: namespaced rules cannot apply to non-resource URLs
issue: - OpenShift GitOps failed to install default ArgoCD instance in `openshift-gitops` namespace with below error in operator pod logs: Role.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller" is invalid: rules[407].nonResourceURLs: Invalid value: []string{"/metrics"}: namespaced rules cannot apply to non-resource URLs
resolution: ### Workaround Update the `openshift-gitops-operator` Subscription with environment variable `CONTROLLER_CLUSTER_ROLE` and value as custom-role-name which is manually created, Subscription will be present at default operator namespace which is `openshift-gitops-operator`. If operator installed in any other project then check in that project: apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: openshift-gitops-operator namespace: openshift-gitops-operator spec: config: env:- name: CONTROLLER_CLUSTER_ROLE value:
root_cause: - The `admin` ClusterRole doesn't have "Non-Resource URLs" configurations in a standard installation.- The `admin` clusterrole is appended to the "openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller" role.

title: Ceph Services (OSDs) seemingly binding to cluster_network instead of public_network
issue: - Slow operations or failed operations on RBD volumes in Open Stack or Openshift.- `socket closed` errors seen in dmesg on client nodes, the IP is an IP from the `cluster_network` instead of the `public_network`.- The osdmap from the MON shows some OSDs with the wrong network in the public IP. See Diagnostic section for details.
resolution: With RHCS 6.1z1 (see Artifacts table [1] and [2]) we got the ability to configure the `public_network` on the global level by supplying a `ceph.conf` file. In a new [BZ 2314438](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2314438) [3] we are now changing that the `public_network` is set to `global` level by default, and that it can be overriden by a `ceph.conf` file if necessary. However Clusters upgraded from earlier versions might still experience this issue. Check the ceph configuration database how the `public_network` is defined. If it is set on the `mon` level then add the `public_network` to the `global` level instead and remove it afterwards from the `mon` level: ``` $ sudo ceph config dump | grep public_network mon advanced public_network 10.0.88.0/21 ``` Add to the `global` level and remove from the `mon` level: ``` $ sudo ceph config set global public_network 10.0.88.0/21 $ sudo ceph config rm mon public_network ``` Confirm it is now set correctly: ``` $ sudo ceph config dump | grep `public_network` global advanced public_network 10.0.88.0/21 ``` **Artifacts:** | Product/Version | BZ/Tracker | Errata | Fixed Version | Comment | |-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|---------------------| | RHCS 8 [3] | [BZ 2314438](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2314438) | [RHBA-2024:10216](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:10216) | 8.0 | Made global default | | RHCS 7.1 | [BZ 2314606](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2314606) | [RHBA-2025:1770](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:1770) | 7.1z3 | " | | RHCS 6.1 | [BZ 2314604](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2314604) | N/A | N/A | " | | RHCS 6.1 [1] | [BZ 2156919](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2156919) | [RHBA-2023:4473](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2023:4473) [2] | 6.1z1 | Made configurable |
root_cause: We found that this issue did show up mostly in high osd node count scenarios. After reviewing data it seems the OSDs bind to the correct IPs locally, but the OSDMap shows the IP the OSD binds to for the `cluster_network` for both, the cluster ip and the public ip. This is a situation very difficult to reproduce. We had the opportunity twice to view the OSDs and to check which IPs they have bound to internally. In both circumstances, the OSDs bound the IP on the network interface the cluster network was configured to, and the public IP was bound to `0.0.0.0`. After the `public_network` is set on the global level however the OSDs upon restart are binding to the IP on the network interface the public network is configured to, instead of `0.0.0.0`. Both scenarios will technically work fine (binding to `0.0.0.0` which means to all configured local IPv4 IPs instead of binding to an actual IP). The issue seems to be the MON for some reason not updating the OSDMON map correctly and showing the wrong IP address for the public IP, but to confirm the actual issue having a reliable reproducer is necessary. Please contact Red Hat Support if you have a reliable way to reproduce this issue.

title: Allowing Users to Create NooBaa Object Bucket Claims without Having the "cluster-admin" Role - Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG)
issue: There may be instances where Cluster Admins will want to grant the ability for users to create Object Buckets/Object Bucket Claims in their respective namespace using the Admin role, but not having the Cluster Admin role. This solution will cover this process. **Prerequisite:*

Follow the respective OCP documentation to create users and assign the respective role (admin) ot the user in the desired namespace. [How to create new users in OpenShift with htpasswd and OAuth](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/openshift-htpasswd-oauth) [Chapter 9. Using RBAC to define and apply permissions](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/authentication_and_authorization/using-rbac) **NOTE:*

The user will need admin access to both the `openshift-storage` namespace as well as the namespace where the desired bucket creation will occur. This is because the NooBaa API calls go through the `noobaa-operator` that is in the `openshift-storage` namespace. Additionally, if using the NooBaa CLI, those commands must be executed in the `openshift-storage` namespace. **Optional (If Wanting to Use the NooBaa CLI):*

[2.2. Accessing the Multicloud Object Gateway from the MCG command-line interface](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.19/html/managing_hybrid_and_multicloud_resources/accessing-the-multicloud-object-gateway-with-your-applications_rhodf#accessing-the-Multicloud-object-gateway-from-the-mcg-command-line-interface_rhodf)
resolution: **Ensure you're logged in as a "cluster-admin" role and the prerequisites and the NOTE have been followed in the "Issue" section of this solution prior to executing the steps below.** 1. After the user has been created, assign the appropriate admin roles in the `openshift-storage` namespace along with the desired namespace that they will be creating OBCs in. ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user admin-n $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user admin-n openshift-storage ~~~ 2. Edit the namespace in the `obc-creator-role.yaml` file below and save the file: ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: obc-creator-role namespace: rules:- apiGroups: ["objectbucket.io"] resources: ["objectbucketclaims"] verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "watch", "delete"] ~~~ 3. Create a role to allow OBC creation: ~~~ $ oc create-f obc-create-role.yaml ~~~ 4. Assign the role to the user: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user obc-creator-role-n ~~~ 5. Logout as `cluster-admin` user and login as the user. **Note:** If a new user was just added, it may take ~10 minutes for `OAth` to update. 6. At this point, the user can perform the following: a. Login to the OCP UI and create OBCs Storage-> Object Storage-> Object Bucket Claims-> Project (Dropdown)-> "Create Object Bucket Claim". b. Or use the CLI, creating an `obc.yaml`: ~~~ apiVersion: objectbucket.io/v1alpha1 kind: ObjectBucketClaim metadata: name: namespace: spec: bucketName: storageClassName: openshift-storage.noobaa.io additionalConfig: bucketclass: ~~~ c. Create the OBC: ~~~ $ oc create-f obc.yaml ~~~ 7. **(Optional Step)** If the NooBaa CLI was configured, below is an example using the NooBaa CLI: ~~~ $ oc project openshift-storage $ noobaa obc create--app-namespace= ~~~ **Note:** If using a different backingstore other than the `noobaa-default-backing-store`, a bucketclass needs to be configured for that backingstore. Once configured, the `--bucketclass ` flag must be used in the `$ noobaa obc create` command to point to that backingstore. If wanting the default `noobaa-default-backing-store` and `noobaa-default-bucket-class`, the command in step 7 will work fine as-is.

title: Is there a list of Certified Hardware for Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS?
issue: What hardware is certified to run Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS?
Is there a list of Certified Hardware for Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS?
resolution: * Server hardware that is certified to run Red Hat Enterprise Linux is also certified to run Openshift Container Platform and as part of that this includes Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS. * There is no separate hardware certification list for Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS. RHEL CoreOS is an edition of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and inherits the Hardware Certification from the Red Hat Enterprise Linux. * All RHEL certified servers are supported running either RHEL or RHEL CoreOS equally. Note: RHEL CoreOS is only supported as a component of OpenShift Container Platform. * The list of hardware certified to run Red Hat Enterprise Linux can be found in the [Red Hat Ecosystem Catalog](https://catalog.redhat.com/).

title: Windows Virtual Machine fails to boot on Sapphire Rapids CPUs
issue: Windows Virtual Machines will not boot after being migrated from VMware
Windows Virtual Machines will BSOD if set with more than 1 core
Windows Virtual Machines will BSOD if using Sapphire Rapids, host-model or host-passthrough CPUs.
Windows Virtual Machines stop booting when enabling WSL/Hyper-V/VBS
resolution: * Red Hat has found the issue is not present in the latest versions of Windows updates released after January 2025. * In Windows 2022, it appears solved by [KB5049983](https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/topic/january-14-2025-kb5049983-os-build-20348-3091-789bf923-7777-419d-9c3a-23f7c814930f). * As a workaround, set the Virtual Machine with a lower CPU model.
root_cause: * This is documented in the RHEL 9.6 [release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html/9.6_release_notes/known-issues#known-issues-virtualization) under *Windows VM running on Sapphire Rapids CPU with hypervisor launch type set to auto might fail to boot when restarted*, but it not specific to RHEL 9.6. * Issue is was tracked in [RHEL-67699](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-67699). * Only Windows Guests using nested virtualization are affected.

title: How to disable cloud-init network configuration?
issue: How to prevent `cloud-init` from configuring the network?
Network is configured by other means, how to prevent `cloud-init` from touching network?
The VM is not coming with the IP address specified with `cloud-init`, why?
resolution: * In the instance `/etc/cloud/cloud.cfg` file, disable network: ~~~ network: config: disabled ~~~ * If you are trying to assign an IP via cloud-init and it's not working, ensure the above lines are removed from `/etc/cloud/cloud.cfg`.
root_cause: Cloud-init network config can be disabled if required. More information in upstream documentation [here](https://cloudinit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/network-config.html).

title: How to grant  permission to  an user  to list all the project in the cluster along with project admin access to a specific project in RHOCP 4
issue: - Grant Permission to an user to list the `projects/namespaces` in the cluster (i.e user can only get o/p of `oc get projects` command) and should have project admin access for a specific `project/namespace`.
resolution: - Create a custom `ClusterRole` for listing all the `namespace/project` in cluster as below: ~~~ $ vi custom_CR.yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: <---------- This is name can be changed rules:- apiGroups:- ""- project.openshift.io resources:- namespaces- projects verbs:- get ~~~- Create the `ClusterRole` and assign this role to user: ~~~ $ oc create-f custom_CR.yaml $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user ~~~- Assign `admin` role to the user for a desired project: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-role-to-user admin-n ~~~
root_cause: The requirement has two different types of roles, i.e `ClusterRole` (for listing project) and `admin` role for a project,so the above procedure in the resolution will be helpful.

title: Users/Groups with cluster-reader role are unable to view the monitoring dashboards after cluster upgrade in RHOCP 4
issue: - Users with `cluster-reader` role are unable to view the Monitoring dashboards, Alert and Cluster utilization after upgrade to 4.16.- Users/Groups with `cluster-reader` role assigned is getting `forbidden` error while viewing the monitoring dashboard.
resolution: - This is an expected behavior from RHOCP 4.16+- **Workaround:**- provide `cluster-monitoring-view` role to the affected users/groups: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-monitoring-view ~~~ ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-group cluster-monitoring-view ~~~
root_cause: - As per `bug` [OCPBUGS-30294](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-30294)`cluster-reader` role worked fine in previous `RHOCP` releases because the access limitations were not fine grained enough and thus it was allowing access with the the `cluster-reader` role.- Later `RHOCP` releases will no longer allow the `cluster-reader` role to access the metrics.

title: Prometheus ServiceAccount missing permissions to monitor services in OpenShift native namespaces in RHOCP 4
issue: - Unable to monitor service in OpenShift native namespaces.- Logs from pod `prometheus-k8s-0` shows permissions error when monitoring services on OpenShift native namespaces. ~~~ $ oc logs-c prometheus prometheus-k8s-0-n openshift-monitoring | grep "cannot list resource" <...> User "system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s" cannot list resource "services" in API group "\" in the namespace "openshift-xxxxx" <...> ~~~
resolution: Promtheus-k8s pods running in openshift-monitoring project scrape metrics of namespaces which has the label `openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true"`. This label is reserved only for the namespaces with core OpenShift Container Platform components and Red Hat certified components. This label `openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true"` should not be applied on user-defined namespaces as per [support considerations](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html-single/monitoring/index#maintenance-and-support-for-monitoring:~:text=Adding%20the%20openshift.io/cluster%2Dmonitoring%3A%20%22true%22%20label%20to%20namespaces.%20This%20label%20is%20reserved%20only%20for%20the%20namespaces%20with%20core%20OpenShift%20Container%20Platform%20components%20and%20Red%C2%A0Hat%20certified%20components.). If it is applied on user-defined namespace, then it can trigger [this problem](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7024333). If any OpenShift native namespace is missing the expected `roles` or `rolebindings`, please open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat. These resources are expected to be present by default and their absence could be due to a bug in the relevant component. **Workaround**- Make sure a `Role` exists granting the correct permissions in the namespace `openshift-xxxxx`: ~~~ $ cat role.yaml-- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: prometheus-k8s namespace: rules:- apiGroups:- "" resources:- services- endpoints- pods verbs:- get- list- watch ~~~- Make sure the `RoleBinding` exists binding the previously created role to the ServiceAccount `system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s` in the namespace `openshift-xxxxx`: ~~~ $ cat rolebinding.yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: prometheus-k8s namespace: roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Role name: prometheus-k8s subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: prometheus-k8s namespace: openshift-monitoring ~~~- Run the following commands and check the output to validate the `Role` and `RoleBinding`: ~~~ $ oc get role,rolebinding-n < | egrep "NAME|prometheus" NAME CREATED AT role.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/prometheus-k8s 2023-06-30T20:44:45Z NAME ROLE AGE rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/prometheus-k8s Role/prometheus-k8s 15m $ oc get svc-n--as=system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE httpd ClusterIP 172.30.184.120 8080/TCP,8443/TCP 20m nginx ClusterIP None 80/TCP 18h ~~~
root_cause: - The `Role` resource granting privileges to monitor the namespace `openshift-xxxxx`is missing or deleted by mistake.- The `RoleBinding`resource assigned to the `Role` of the ServiceAccount `system:serviceaccount:openshift-monitoring:prometheus-k8s` is missing or deleted by mistake.

title: How to query Prometheus API from the command line?
issue: - Need to access Prometheus API from the command line.
resolution: - Create a prometheus service account token. ~~~ $ export TOKEN=$(oc-n openshift-monitoring create token prometheus-k8s) ~~~- Get the hostname from the Prometheus route: ~~~ $ export PROMETHEUS_HOST=$(oc-n openshift-monitoring get route prometheus-k8s-o json | jq-r '.spec.host') ~~~- Query the Prometheus API (in this example, we use a simple query=up). ~~~ $ curl-X GET-k "https://$PROMETHEUS_HOST/api/v1/query?query=up"-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"... {"metric": {"__name__": "up", "endpoint": "https", "instance": "10.0.130.143:6443", "job": "apiserver", "namespace": "default", "service": "kubernetes"}, "value": [1580986794.817, "1"]},... ~~~- For a more complex query, this could be used: ~~~ $ curl-G-k "https://$PROMETHEUS_HOST/api/v1/query"-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"--data-urlencode 'query= ' ~~~ To get details on firing alerts from the Prometheus API instead of just metrics, see the command examples in the following article. [How to get fired alerts on OpenShift using cli or script?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4250221)

title: Public load balancer automatically recreated by cluster in Private installation.
issue: - In private IPI cluster on Azure, public loadbalancer is getting created automatically and have public IPs attached causing security issues.- Even if you delete the public loadbalancer, it will be created again after some time.
resolution: - For this particular cluster, the user should be able to annotate the service (nooba-mgmt) to prevent it from creating the public load balancer. [Here is the link](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#internal-load-balancer) for reference.- We have an RFE to solve this issue automatically with services, but until then it will be necessary to annotate such services. [RFE for reference](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-2816)
root_cause: - It is observed that the public loadbalancer is getting created by nooba-mgmt.
