title: Elasticsearch has Yellow Status as replicas are Unassigned in RHOCP 4
issue: Elasticsearch alert fires continuously ElasticsearchClusterNotHealthy- Cluster elasticsearch health status has been YELLOW for at least 20m. Some shard replicas are not allocated.
After switching OSSM to integrate with user-workload monitoring, the Elasticsearch turns YELLOW as replicas for indices are `UNASSIGNED`.

Elasticsearch indices are in YELLOW as indices replicas are `UNASSIGNED` and when reviewed the Elasticsearch allocation policy is observed the message: ~~~ "replica allocations are forbidden due to cluster setting [cluster.routing.allocation.enable=primaries]"} ~~~
resolution: Modify the `cluster.routing.allocation.enable` from `primaries` to `all`. Replace in the command ` ` by `istio-system` if the Elasticsearch is used with OSSM or `openshift-logging` if used for Red Hat OpenShift Logging: ~~~ $ es_pod=$(oc get pods-l component=elasticsearch-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'-n) $ oc exec-n-c elasticsearch $es_pod-- es_util "--query=_cluster/settings?pretty"-X PUT-d '{"persistent": {"cluster.routing.allocation.enable":"all"}}' ~~~
root_cause: The Elasticsearch pods have allocation set to primary but also are configured to store a replica, see diagnostic steps, so it can't allocate replicas of the data to other pods. This causes Elasticsearch to have a yellow status since it's able to function with the primary data storage, but isn't able to meet its configuration settings with regard to replication of data. For more information about resolving Elasticsearch status errors, see the documentation [Elasticsearch Cluster Health is Yellow](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/observability/logging/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-logging-alerts.html#elasticsearch-cluster-health-is-yellow) The instructions for integrating OSSM with the OCP user workload monitoring can be found at [OSSM Integrating with User Workload Monitoring Observability](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/service_mesh/v2x/ossm-observability.html#ossm-integrating-with-user-workload-monitoring_observability)

title: How to restrict the user login from OpenID Connect (OIDC) in RHOCP.
issue: - All the OpenID Connect users are able to login in the cluster.- How to restrict the user authentication.
resolution: - Restrict the user authentication as per the below two methods. ~~~ 1. Change the OpenShift mappingMethod to lookup: This prevents OpenShift from automatically creating a user account for every person who can log in via your OpenID provider. Only users with a pre-existing user object in OpenShift will be allowed to log in. ~~~- [How to create user, identity and map user and identity in OIDC authentication for 'mappingMethod' as 'lookup'](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7072510). ~~~ 2. OIDC providers offer features to limit which users or groups can receive a token for a specific application. In your Azure AD app registration, you can configure the application to require user assignment. This means that only users and groups explicitly assigned to the application in Azure AD will be able to get a token and authenticate with OpenShift. This is the most effective method for controlling which groups of users can login. ~~~- Refer the article from Red Hat [Add or remove user/group from Azure AD application for OpenShift OpenID authentication](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3335101).- Microsoft documentation for more detailed information: [Manage users and groups assignment to an application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal?pivots=portal).
root_cause: - This is the default behaviour when the cluster is configured with OpenID Connect it uses the mappingMethod as claim, this means it creates a new user object if it doesn't exist based on claim data.

title: Unable to logout users when multiple OIDC Identity Provider is configured in OCP
issue: - Configured multiple RH-SSO realm in our Openshift cluster for users to login, and for user logout we have configured [logoutRedirect](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/web_console/configuring-web-console.html) in `console.config.openshift.io` which allows users from 1 specific realm to logout.- How can we configure Openshift cluster, to logout users from more than 1 RH-SSO realm?- Configured multiple OIDC Identity Provider in Openshift cluster and how to configure multiple logout URL to logout users logged In from different Identity Providers.
resolution: - Please open a support case in case you are looking to include this feature- to logout users logging in from different OIDC Identity Provider. Please note the request for enhancement will be subject to [RFE process](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/73513).- This feature request is submitted to Engineering team and its being track under internal RH jira [Unable to logout users when multiple OIDC Identity Provider is configured in OCP](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7917)
root_cause: - Currently it is not possible to configure multiple logout endpoint(each for each realm or different OIDC Identity Provider). Currently as of now there is no plan to improve this behavior.- The Openshift webconsole is not aware of which Identity Provider the user is logged In with, hence it won't be able to forward logout request to a specific logout URL.

title: Guide for VMware datastore migration of OpenShift Infrastructure
issue: - Migrate the storage used by the virtual machines (corresponding to OpenShift nodes) to a new datastore.- Migrate the PersistentVolumes used by application workloads and operators to a new datastore.
resolution: This article serves as a foundational guide for migrating the storage from the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform infrastructure (nodes and CSI-driver) installed over VMware, to a new datastore. It provides an overview of the general process and links to more specific articles that cover detailed steps and considerations. Whether you're planning a simple migration or dealing with more complex scenarios, this guide will help you navigate the transition efficiently by directing you to the resources that best suit your needs. ### Step 1: Migrate the virtual machine storage In this step, the goal is to migrate the disk where the root filesystem is mounted on each virtual machine used as an Openshift node to a new datastore. Since Storage vMotion is not supported for this, it will be necessary to rebuild the Openshift nodes:- For `IPI` installations or UPI installations running with `MachineSets` follow [Migrating Virtual Machines with the Machine API](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6718991) in order to recreate the Openshift nodes on the new datastore.- For `UPI` installations without `MachineSets` it will be required to recreate the Openshift nodes following the below procedure depending on the node type.- Compute Nodes: [Adding more compute machines to a cluster in vSphere](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/installing/installing_vsphere/upi/installing-vsphere.html#machine-vsphere-machines_installing-vsphere)- Control plane: [How to replace unhealthy master nodes in UPI on OpenShift 4.x?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6387841) ### Step 2: Migrate your application workload data: #### Option 1: Migrating CNS volumes on vmware (for clusters running on 4.19 or later) Red Hat OpenShift clusters **on version 4.19 or later** now support a new method for migrating CNS volumes between vSphere datastores. For more inforamtion, please consult the [product documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html-single/storage/index#persistent-storage-csi-vsphere-migrating-cns-vols-between-datastores_persistent-storage-csi-vsphere) and confirm you meet all requirements and understand any limitations. #### Option 2: Data migration using a new StorageClass With this option, the storage of the application workloads will be migrated to a new `StorageClass` configured under a new datastore. 1. Creating a new `StorageClass` that consumes the new datastore from a new `StoragePolicy` at vmware side [vSphere storage policy](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/storage/container_storage_interface/persistent-storage-csi-vsphere.html#persistent-storage-csi-vsphere-stor-policy_persistent-storage-csi-vsphere). Is recommended to keep the same settings as the original `StorageClass`, like `volumeBindingMode`, `allowVolumeExpansion`, `reclaimPolicy` etc. 2. Migrate your application workloads to the `StorageClass` created on the above step using one of the below-listed methods:- Perform a storageclass conversion using MTC (Migration toolkit for containers) operator [Converting storage classes in the MTC web console](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/migration_toolkit_for_containers/advanced-migration-options-mtc.html#migration-converting-storage-classes_advanced-migration-options-mtc)- Manually perform PV migration using the following procedure: [How to migrate data between PVs in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5794841)- Backup and Restore your workloads to a new storageclass with [OpenShift API for Data Protection OADP](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/oadp-intro.html) [Mapping storage classes with OADP](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/backup_and_restore/application_backup_and_restore/oadp-advanced-topics.html#storage-class-mapping-oadp_oadp-advanced-topics) 3. Migrating data for specific operators. Persistent storage for some operators cannot be migrated using the procedure described above, as these operators manage storage on their own. For these operators, please refer to their specific procedures for migrating data:- Openshift Data Foundation [How to migrate OSD's from one VMWare vSphere datastore to another, in an OCS (ODF) 4.X cluster?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5897101)- Logging: [Migrate ElasticSearch PersistentVolumeClaim to a new StorageClass in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7025818)- Monitoring: [Migrate prometheus data to larger persistent volume](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6958231)- Image registry operator: [How to migrate an Image Registry Operator PV in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6893321)- Red Hat AMQ Streams: [In AMQ Streams how to switch the Kafka log (PV) storage class when PV does not support VolumeSnapshots?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7076218)- AMQ broker: [[AMQ] How to migrate data between PV for AMQ7 Broker on OpenShift?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5354651)- Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes [[ACM] How to migrate data from an existing pv of a "search-redisgraph" pod to a new pv?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6380471)- For more information about other [Red Hat operators](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4807821), please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: Storage VMotion is not currently supported as is described in product documentation [Using OpenShift Container Platform with vMotion](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/installing/installing_vsphere/ipi/ipi-vsphere-installation-reqs.html).

title: During adoption, nova-compute fails to connect to nova services.
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - During adoption, nova-compute fails to connect to nova services.
resolution: - Ensure all compute hosts have the OpenStack services running in the control plane added to the `no_proxy` setting on the compute hosts if a proxy is used. This allows them to reach the OpenStack services in the OpenShift control plane after adoption.
root_cause: - proxy configuration prevent nova services to reach the endpoint.

title: Quay reports an invalid namespace name when logging in with Azure OIDC
issue: - When a login attempt is tried via OIDC hooked to Azure Entra Id, Quay sometimes displays the following message: ~~~ AAD login error Invalid namespace f0asxv...: Namespace must match expression ^([a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*)$ ~~~
resolution: - user information endpoint must be disabled for OIDC login to work properly. ## OpenShift deployments 1. Find the init config bundle that the Quay instance was deployed from: ~~~ oc get quayregistry name-of-registry-o yaml-n quay-namespace | grep-i configbundle ~~~ 2. Open the OpenShift console and find the secret from step 1 under `Workloads-> Secrets`. Click on it and then click on `Actions-> Edit secret` on the right side. 3. Under the `config.yaml` key find the OIDC Entra configuration and paste the following: ~~~ ENTRA_LOGIN_CONFIG:... OIDC_DISABLE_USER_ENDPOINT: true # <-- add this line ~~~ 4. Save the new secret and wait for the operator to reconcile the deployment. ## VM deployments 1. Shut down all Quay containers. 2. Edit the `config.yaml` file on each of the nodes and under the Entra OIDC configuration add the following config option: ~~~ ENTRA_LOGIN_CONFIG:... OIDC_DISABLE_USER_ENDPOINT: true # <-- add this line ~~~ 3. Save the new `config.yaml` file on each of the nodes and restart Quay.
root_cause: - OIDC providers contain a specific user information endpoint that user information is read from. This endpoint should in theory contain the same information as the login endpoint.- Communication between Quay and the OIDC provider is done via JSON web tokens which encode all permissions and user information needed for Quay to create a new user or log in an existing user. The first JWT is provided by the login endpoint, the user endpoint is then read to provide additional user information if needed.- Quay's OIDC configuration usually contain the `PREFERRED_USERNAME_CLAIM_NAME` configuration which tells Quay what key from the user info JWT to interpret as the username for the new user.- If the field defined under `PREFERRED_USERNAME_CLAIM_NAME` is not found, Quay will default to the `sub` field for username information.- If this `sub` field is not parsable through the username regex (defined [here](https://github.com/quay/quay/blob/8de588929e550bf21542b51dd15f9e8bba49e6ff/util/validation.py#L17)), an invalid namespace error will be raised.- For Entra Id specifically, data returned by the user information endpoint might **not** contain the same data as the data returned by the login endpoint, so even if login endpoint contains the field defined by `PREFERRED_USERNAME_CLAIM_NAME` is present, it might **not** be present in the user information endpoint. In that case, Quay will fall back to the `sub` field of the JWT which is the same in both JWTs.- To resolve this issue, setting `OIDC_DISABLE_USER_ENDPOINT: true` is needed, as it tells Quay to use data provided by the login endpoint as the source of truth for all users.

title: Can we create a second DataScienceCluster in same Openshift AI installation?
issue: - Can we create a second DataScienceCluster in same Openshift AI installation?
resolution: In Red Hat Openshift AI 2.22.x or later relase 2.23.x, 2.24.0 **Only**_one_ instance of **DataScienceCluster** object is **allowed** per OCP cluster. You will get following **error** if you try to create it. ~~~ Danger alert:Error Fix the following errors: admission webhook "datasciencecluster-validator.opendatahub.io" denied the request: Only one instance of DataScienceCluster object is allowed ~~~ Basically, When the operator is installed successfully in the cluster, a user can create a DataScienceCluster CR to enable RHOAI components. At a given time, RHOAI supports **only one** instance of the **DataScienceCluster** CR, which can be **updated** to get **custom** list of components.

title: The Deny Ingress Network Policy is not working on OpenShift 4.x
issue: - The `NetworkPolicy` to [Deny all Ingress traffic](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/networking/network-policy#about-network-policy:~:text=The%20following%20example%20NetworkPolicy%20objects%20demonstrate%20supporting%20different%20scenarios%3A) to a specific namespace is not working, and application is still accessible via the ingress routers.
resolution: - To overcome this issue, make sure that the application pods are running on different nodes than the nodes hosting the Ingress router pods.- If the OpenShift cluster is using infrastructure nodes, it is recommended, if possible, to follow this [article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5034771#:~:text=Moving%20Components%20to%20the%20Infrastructure%20Nodes) to configure the `IngressController` to move the Ingress router pods to the Infrastructure Nodes.
root_cause: Some architectures use `HostNetwork` as default `endpointPublishingStrategy` on the ingress controller. This means that ingress controllers are in the host network. On the other hand, Kubernetes mandates that all the pods must be reachable from the host network of the same node, irrespective of the `NetworkPolicy` rules (so that probes made by the kubelet can always reach the pods). As a result, if the ingress controller pods are placed in the same nodes than the application pods, the ingress controller pods (in the host network) will be able to reach the application pods on the same node even if you try to avoide that with a `NetworkPolicy`. So the only way to avoid this situation is to ensure that no ingress controller is placed in the same node than an application pod, so that nodes are different and `NetworkPolicy` rules are always applied.

title: Clarifying Red Hat AI Inference Server Version Mapping to Red Hat OpenShift AI Releases
issue: Customers and internal teams have raised questions about which version of Red Hat AI Inference Server (RHAIIS) is officially included or supported in each Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) release. While both products evolve independently, without a clear mapping table, users may find it difficult to understand compatibility and support boundaries.
resolution: The table below provides the definitive mapping between **upstream vLLM versions**, **Red Hat AI Inference Server (RHAIIS) releases**, and their corresponding **RHOAI versions**: | vLLM Version | RHAIIS Version | RHOAI Version | |--------------|----------------|---------------| | v0.10.1.1 | 3.2.2 | 2.25 | | v0.10.0 | 3.2.1 | 2.24 | | v0.9.2 | 3.2.0 | 2.23 | ### Key Points- **Version Independence** RHAIIS and RHOAI follow separate release cycles and are versioned independently.- **Compatibility** Each RHOAI release includes a specific RHAIIS version that has been tested and validated for compatibility.- **Support Scope** Within RHOAI, only RHAIIS versions officially bundled with the release are supported.- **Upgrade Path** To ensure compatibility and supportability, RHAIIS should be upgraded only through RHOAI version updates, rather than independently.
root_cause: RHOAI documentation does not explicitly list which **RHAIIS** (and indirectly **vLLM**) version is included in each release. This gap creates confusion for customers and support engineers when validating compatibility.- For reference, please see the official life cycle documentation of the related products: [Red Hat OpenShift AI Self-Managed Life Cycle](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/rhoai-sm/lifecycle) [Red Hat OpenShift AI Cloud Service Life Cycle](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/rhoai-cs/lifecycle) [Red Hat AI Inference Server Life Cycle](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/rhaiis)

title: How do I automatically generate fencing secret for RHOSO18 instanceha from a osp17.1 cluster that I want to adopt?
issue: - I want to automatically translate fencing configuration from osp17 to rhoso18- How do I convert stonith from osp17 to rhoso18
resolution: Please note that the following script is provided as is and it is not supported by Red Hat.- copy the following script to one of the controllers: ~~~ import xmltodict import subprocess import json import yaml # create temporary cib.xml file to read from with open('/tmp/cib.xml', 'w') as f: subprocess.run(["pcs", "cluster", "cib"], stdout=f) f.close() with open('/tmp/cib.xml', 'r') as f: xml = f.read() o = xmltodict.parse(xml) f.close() nodes = o["cib"]["configuration"]["nodes"] resources = o["cib"]["configuration"]["resources"] # load from hieradata with open('/etc/puppet/hieradata/service_configs.json', 'r') as x: hiera_json = json.load(x) x.close() devices = hiera_json["tripleo::fencing::config"]["devices"] # computes have a single dict of attributes and not a list like other resources, so we can filter the other nodes computes = [i["@id"] for i in nodes["node"] if (isinstance(i["instance_attributes"]["nvpair"], dict) and i["instance_attributes"]["nvpair"]["@name"] == "compute-instanceha-role")] stonith = [i["instance_attributes"]["nvpair"] for i in resources["primitive"] if i["@class"] == "stonith"] s = {} header = """--- apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: fencing-secret stringData: fencing.yaml: | FencingConfig:""" print(header) for i in stonith: j = [g for g in i if g["@name"] == "pcmk_host_list"] for j in j: mac = j["@id"].replace('-instance_attributes-pcmk_host_list', '').split('-')[2] host = j["@value"] if host in computes: s[host] = mac for i in devices: if mac in i["host_mac"].replace(':', ''): print(" %s:" % host) if 'ipmilan' in i["agent"]: print(' agent: ipmilan') print(' ipaddr: ' + i["params"]["ipaddr"]) print(' ipport: ' + i["params"]["ipport"]) else: print(' agent: redfish') if ':' in i["params"]["ipaddr"]: print(' ipaddr: ' + i["params"]["ipaddr"].split(':')[0]) print(' ipport: ' + i["params"]["ipaddr"].split(':')[1]) print(' tls: \'true\'') else: print(' ipaddr: ' + i["params"]["ipaddr"]) print(' login: ' + i["params"]["login"]) print(' passwd: ' + i["params"]["passwd"]) try: if i["params"]["systems_uri"]: print(' uuid: ' + i["params"]["systems_uri"].split('/')[4]) except: pass # remove temporary cib file subprocess.run(["rm", "-rf", "/tmp/cib.xml"]) ~~~- run as follows: ~~~ [root@controller-0 ~]# dnf install python3-pip [root@controller-0 ~]# python3-m venv fencing-venv [root@controller-0 ~]# source fencing-venv/bin/activate (fencing-venv) [root@controller-0 ~]# pip install xmltodict pyyaml (fencing-venv) [root@controller-0 ~]# python3 script.py > fencing-secret.yaml (fencing-venv) [root@controller-0 ~]# cat fencing-secret.yaml ~~~- delete the virtualenv when done: ~~~ [root@controller-0 ~]# rm-rf fencing-venv ~~~

title: ROSA upgrade fails with "Forbidden access to update resource"
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - When using ROSA cli to perform a cluster upgrade, it fails with the following error: ``` [user@ip-XX-XX-XXX-XXX ~]$./rosa version 1.2.15 Your ROSA CLI is up to date. [user@ip-XX-XX-XXX-XXX ~]$./rosa upgrade cluster-c xX-XxxxXXxx-Xx? Version: 4.11.27? IAM Roles/Policies upgrade mode: auto I: Ensuring account and operator role policies for cluster 'xXxxxxXxxxxxxxXxxxxxXX' are compatible with upgrade. I: Account roles/policies for cluster 'xXxxxxXxxxxxxxXxxxxxXX' are already up-to-date. I: Operator roles/policies associated with the cluster 'xXxxxxXxxxxxxxXxxxxxXX' are already up-to-date. I: Account and operator roles for cluster 'xXxxxxxX' are compatible with upgrade? Are you sure you want to upgrade cluster to version '4.11.27'? Yes E: failed to check for missing gate agreements upgrade for cluster 'dl-xXxxxxxX-1d': Forbidden access to update resource 'xXxxxxXxxxxxxxXxxxxxXX' ```
resolution: - In order to upgrade the cluster, it is required to get the token of the cluster owner from the [OpenShift Cluster Manager Console](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/token/rosa). The steps below shows how to retrieve it: 1. Go to a terminal and run the `rosa login` command: ``` $ rosa login ``` 2. It will prompt you to open a web browser and go to: ``` https://console.redhat.com/openshift/token/rosa ``` 3. If you are asked to log in, please do so. 4. Click on the "Load token" button. 5. Then, copy the token and paste it back into the CLI prompt and press enter. Alternatively, you can just copy the full `rosa login--token=abc####` command and paste that into the terminal, for example: ``` rosa login--token=" XXXXXXXxxxXXXXXXXxxxXXXXxxXXXxxxXXXXxxXXXxxXXXxxxxXXXxxxXX" ```
root_cause: - The upgrade of the cluster can only be carried out by either the cluster owner or the user who installed it. Even if other users possess cluster-admin privileges, they will encounter this problem.

title: Renaming a secured cluster name in RHACS
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - How to rename RHACS secure clusters once it is installed and in a running state.
resolution: - As per the design guidelines, renaming of secured clusters is not supported in RHACS after it is installed. It is needed to recreate the cluster with the correct cluster name.- If in case cluster name is renamed, Below error messages will show in cluster's custom resource: ~~~ message: >- SecuredCluster instance was initially created with clusterName "ocpxxx", but current value is "ocpxxx-prod". Renaming clusters is not supported- you need to delete this object, and then recreate one with the correct cluster name. reason: ReconcileError ~~~- Also, from the RHACS operator pod, below error will be available: ~~~ {"level":"error","ts":"2024-01-22T03:15:12Z","msg":"Reconciler error","controller":"securedcluster-controller","object":{"name":"stackrox-secured-cluster-services","namespace":"stackrox"},"namespace":"stackrox","name":"stackrox-secured-cluster-services","reconcileID":"xxxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxx","error":"SecuredCluster instance was initially created with clusterName \"ocpxxx\", but current value is \"ocpxxx-prod\". Renaming clusters is not supported- you need to delete this object, and then recreate one with the correct cluster name." ~~~
root_cause: - Renaming secured clusters is not supported in RHACS.

title: How to use S3 API in Swift
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: Needs instructions to use S3 API in RHOSP/RHOSO
resolution: The S3 API in Swift is enabled by default. Please follow the below steps to access the Swift using AWS CLI. 1. Generate a ec2 credential ~~~ (overcloud) [stack@director ~]$ openstack ec2 credentials create +------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Field | Value | +------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | access | 89827701ac304d028e5ab5d6d8a6a58f | | links | {'self': 'https://overcloud.rhosp.example.com:13000/v3/users/547b543ccaa1499584277a029e9fa8b3/credentials/OS- | | | EC2/89827701ac304d028e5ab5d6d8a6a58f'} | | project_id | 5077962707064c3f91d47c6a8aa81bf1 | | secret | fd8f91d3614d49b08b00d2e0a35acf7e | | trust_id | None | | user_id | 547b543ccaa1499584277a029e9fa8b3 | +------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ ~~~ 2. Configure a profile to access Swift using AWS CLI ~~~ (overcloud) [stack@director ~]$ aws configure--profile=swift AWS Access Key ID [None]: 89827701ac304d028e5ab5d6d8a6a58f AWS Secret Access Key [None]: fd8f91d3614d49b08b00d2e0a35acf7e Default region name [None]: [Enter] Default output format [None]: [Enter] ~~~ 3. Confirm the public endpoint of Swift ~~~ (overcloud) [stack@director ~]$ openstack endpoint list--service swift--interface public +----------------------------------+-----------+--------------+--------------+---------+-----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+ | ID | Region | Service Name | Service Type | Enabled | Interface | URL | +----------------------------------+-----------+--------------+--------------+---------+-----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+ | 9b9761a99f3248d6bd3f56e1cdcb2c50 | regionOne | swift | object-store | True | public | https://overcloud.rhosp.example.com:13808/v1/AUTH_%(tenant_id)s | +----------------------------------+-----------+--------------+--------------+---------+-----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+ ~~~ 4. Create an alias to point to the FQDN of Swift public endpoint ~~~ (overcloud) [stack@director ~]$ alias aws="aws--endpoint-url=https://overcloud.rhosp.example.com:13808" ~~~ 5. List owned backets ~~~ (overcloud) [stack@director ~]$ aws--profile=swift s3api list-buckets ~~~

title: Unknown output appears in the oc adm top nodes command for newly added nodes in RHOCP 4.
issue: Recently added worker nodes in the existing cluster, which are on a new subnet, are in a Ready state. However, the oc adm top nodes command returns 'unknown' output for each of these nodes: ~~~ $ oc adm top nodes node1 808m 5% 9625Mi 31% node2 948m 6% 10679Mi 34% node3 835m 5% 10111Mi 32% node4 node5 node6 ~~~
resolution: Ensure that port 9100 is allowed through the firewall to enable successful communication between newly added nodes and Prometheus. This port is required for Prometheus to scrape metrics from the node exporter running on each node.
root_cause: Port 9100, used by the Node Exporter, was blocked by the firewall. As a result, Prometheus was unable to scrape metrics from the newly added nodes, leading to unknown data.

title: Why are there so many IPv6 addresses on RHOCP4 nodes?
issue: - On Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x nodes, there are multiple active `ipv6` addresses. The output below is processed in order to remove confidential information, so just co-relate it. ~~~ $ cat ip_addr 1: lo inet 127.0.0.1/8 scope host lo\ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 1: lo inet6::1/128 scope host \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 4: ovn-k8s-mp0 inet 10.10.0.2/23 brd 10.10.1.255 scope global ovn-k8s-mp0\ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 4: ovn-k8s-mp0 inet6 fe80::aaaa:bbbb:cccc:ddee/64 scope link \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 5: genev_sys_6081 inet6 fe80::bbbb:cccc:dddd:eeee/64 scope link \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 7: br-ex inet 192.0.2.10/24 brd 192.0.2.255 scope global noprefixroute br-ex\ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 7: br-ex inet 192.0.2.11/29 brd 192.0.2.15 scope global br-ex\ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 8: 04953xxxxxxxxxx inet6 fe80::cccc:dddd:eeee:ffff/64 scope link \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 9: c446xxxxxxxxxx inet6 fe80::dddd:eeee:ffff:0001/64 scope link \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 11: 677xxxxxxxxxx inet6 fe80::eeee:ffff:0001:0002/64 scope link \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever... 123456: 55bcxxxxxxxxxx inet6 fe80::0012:0013:0014:0015/64 scope link \ valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever ~~~- Is it expected? What's the purpose of these `IPv6` addresses?
resolution: - In the `ip a` output, the first two, i.e. `lo` are for internal routing to check `tcp` and `tcp6` networking.- The `ovn-k8s-mp0` has both `ipv4` and `ipv6` addresses. These IPs are defining the node's Pod network IP address on the `OVNKubernetes` bridge. It purely utilized for communicating with Pods and other nodes via the overlay network over `OVNKubernetes`. This is internal again.- Out of these IP addresses, the `br-ex` IP address is the external Node IP as follows. This `ip` is routable and used for deployment of the node too.- The rest `inet6` i.e. `ipv6` addresses are ephemeral IP addresses, most probably for the pods residing on top of the node which would show removed once the node is restarted. These IPs are purely internal too for communication purposes and are automatically assigned by `kernel` to every active interface and are only valid for that specific communication channel.- It's [NOT recommended to disable IPv6](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5513111 "Disable IPv6 address in OpenShift 4") on the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform4.x Cluster as it breaks many networking components.

title: ovsdbserver-XXX pods failed to startup with CreateContainerError status
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: ovsdbserver-XXX pods failed to startup with CreateContainerError status

title: How to setup bonded VLAN interface on Red Hat CoreOS node using dracut parameters?
issue: - How to setup `bonded VLAN` interface on Red Hat CoreOS node using `dracut` parameters?
resolution: - While booting the Red Hat CoreOS 4.18 `ISO`media, press `tab`to edit the `rhcos boot command-line` and append the information below in the `linux`line. ~~~ setparams ‘RHEL CoreOS (Live)’ linux /images/pxeboot/vmlinuz rw coreos.liveiso=rhcos-418.94.202501221327-0 ignition.firstboot ignition.platform.id=metal bond=bond0:ens193,ens194:mode=active-backup,miimon=100 ip=192.168.0.100::192.168.0.254:255.255.255.0::bond0.101:none vlan=bond0.101:bond0 initrd /images/pxeboot/initrd.img /images/ignition.img ~~~- The above example considers the parameters below.- `bond` device name is marked as `bond0`- The networking devices being part of `bond0`are `ens192`and `ens193`- The mode is `active-backup` with option `miimon` value of 100.- The Networking details are taken for example as `IP`, `netmask` and `gateway`.- The `vlanid`is considered 101- Any values above needs to get replaced as per the requirements. The syntax is as follows. ~~~ bond=:,:mode=, ip:[]:::::{dhcp|dhcp6|auto6|on|any|none|off} vlan=.: ~~~- Once appended, press `Ctrl+x`to accept the newly modified command line and then boot.- To confirm the device configuration, execute the commands below once the user prompt appears. ~~~ # ip a # nmcli con show # nmcli dev status ~~~- To make use of this network configuration, don't forget to use `--copy-network` option alongside `coreos-installer`command as follows. ~~~ # coreos-installer install —-copy-network —ignition-url=http://example_server/ignition/worker.ign /dev/sda —insecure-ignition —insecure ~~~- This will install the node and upon reboots (as part of installation and configuration), the `node` will become `ready` with `Bonded VLAN` interface as per configuration.

title: How to remove OpenShift cluster from Subscription Management
issue: - How to remove an OpenShift cluster from Subscription Management- After archiving a cluster, it automatically gets unarchived and reappears in the active cluster list.
resolution: - An OpenShift Container Platform cluster can be archived to remove it from **OpenShift Cluster Manager** ([OCM](https://console.redhat.com/openshift)). Archiving a cluster removes it from **subscription management** and from the cluster list in OpenShift Cluster Manager.- For detailed steps to archive a cluster, refer below document:- [2.3.1. Removing an OpenShift Container Platform cluster from OpenShift Cluster Manager](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_cluster_manager/1-latest/html-single/managing_clusters/index#archiving-cluster_assembly_cluster-lifecycle)- If telemetry is still enabled on the cluster, cluster will automatically unarchive itself whenever new telemetry data is received. To prevent this, it is required to **disable telemetry** service as well.- For detailed steps to disable or opt-out of remote health reporting, refer below documents:- [4.3.3. Consequences of disabling remote health reporting](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/support/remote-health-monitoring-with-connected-clusters#telemetry-consequences-of-disabling-telemetry_remote-health-reporting)- [4.3.4. Disabling remote health reporting](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/support/remote-health-monitoring-with-connected-clusters#insights-operator-new-pull-secret_remote-health-reporting)
root_cause: - If telemetry service is enabled on the cluster even after cluster is archived, it will continue to send telemetry data for the cluster. Hence, cluster will automatically get unarchived whenever new data is received.

title: One of the galera pod is in Ready:False without reconcil
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: Some services seems not able to connect to galera DB.
Some compute node are currently down.
resolution: * Restart the galera pods: ~~~ $ oc delete pods-l app=galera ~~~
root_cause: * Currently the issue is investigate in [OSPRH-20280](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSPRH-20280) * Based on the status openstack-galera-x-describe: ~~~ State: Running Started: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 10:10:16 +0000 [...] Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Warning Unhealthy 2m13s (x2490 over 6h8m) kubelet Readiness probe failed: wsrep_local_state_comment (Donor/Desynced) differs from Synced ~~~ * and galera-x logs: ~~~ 2025-09-23 10:12:13 2 [Note] WSREP: ================================================ View: id: 843d4cfc-9865-11f0-8652-3e96913b6316:7 status: primary protocol_version: 4 capabilities: MULTI-MASTER, CERTIFICATION, PARALLEL_APPLYING, REPLAY, ISOLATION, PAUSE, CAUSAL_READ, INCREMENTAL_WS, UNORDERED, PREORDERED, STREAMING, NBO final: no own_index: 2 members(3): 0:, openstack-galera-0 1:, openstack-galera-1 2:, openstack-galera-2 ================================================= 2025-09-23_10_12_13 mysql_wsrep_notify.sh called with args:--status joined--uuid--primary yes--index 2--members... 2025-09-23 10:12:13 2 [Note] WSREP: Lowest cert index boundary for CC from group: 2 2025-09-23 10:12:13 2 [Note] WSREP: Min available from gcache for CC from group: 1 2025-09-23 10:12:14 0 [Note] WSREP: Member 0.0 (openstack-galera-0) requested state transfer from '*any*'. Selected 1.0 (openstack-galera-1)(SYNCED) as donor. 2025-09-23 10:12:15 0 [Note] WSREP: 1.0 (openstack-galera-1): State transfer to 0.0 (openstack-galera-0) complete. 2025-09-23 10:12:15 0 [Note] WSREP: Member 1.0 (openstack-galera-1) synced with group. 2025-09-23 10:12:16 0 [Note] WSREP: (...) turning message relay requesting off 2025-09-23 10:12:16 0 [Note] WSREP: 0.0 (openstack-galera-0): State transfer from 1.0 (openstack-galera-1) complete. 2025-09-23 10:12:16 0 [Note] WSREP: Member 0.0 (openstack-galera-0) synced with group. 2025-09-23 10:16:30 29 [Warning] Aborted connection 29 to db: 'nova_cell0' user: 'nova_cell0..' host: '10.0.0.122' (Got an error reading communication packets) ~~~ the openstack-galera-2 pod was in a Ready: False state primarily because its readiness probe was failing. * The underlying reason for the readiness probe failure was that the Galera cluster was reporting the node's state as Donor/Desynced rather than Synced. title: How to list the number of objects and size in etcd on OpenShift?
issue: We observe performance issues with etcd and would like to know what kind of objects are stored in etcd.
How can objects in etcd can be listed in OpenShift?
What is a normal amount of objects in etcd for OpenShift clusters?
How the size of any kind of objects in etcd can be checked?
resolution:
> ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* Check the number of objects and their size in the etcd database, when they were created, and the namespaces in which they are with the following commands: > **NOTE:** the following commands use `oc exec` with an etcd pod to get the results. When it is not possible to use `oc` commands but an etcd pod is running, it is possible to use `crictl exec-ti $(crictl ps--label "io.kubernetes.container.name=etcdctl"-q)` within a control plane node instead, adding the commands from the `sh-c` (included) till the end of the command. * To check the **size** and **number** of occurrences of each kind of object in the etcd database with the following commands (command `numfmt` is included in `coreutils` package): ~~~ $ export ETCD_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-etcd-l app=etcd--field-selector="status.phase==Running"-o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") $ oc exec-n openshift-etcd-c etcdctl ${ETCD_POD_NAME}-- sh-c 'etcdctl get /--prefix--keys-only | grep-oE "^/[a-z|.]+/[a-z|.|8]*" | sort | uniq-c | sort-rn | while read KEY; do printf "$KEY	" && etcdctl get ${KEY##*}--prefix--print-value-only | wc-c | numfmt--to=iec; done | sort-k3-hr | column-t' 419 /kubernetes.io/operators.coreos.com 24M 1172 /kubernetes.io/secrets 19M 446 /kubernetes.io/configmaps 11M 5171 /kubernetes.io/events 6.1M [...] ~~~ This command will retrieve all keys from the etcd database, including the number of occurrences and the size by object type, **ordered by size**. Size `0` is **shown if the command** for specific key **fails**, but it does not mean the real size is `0`. > **Note:** for OpenShift Container Platform 3.11, execute the above `etcdctl` command with `etcdctl3` on the OpenShift Container Platform Master Nodes as `root`. * To check the **size** of some objects **by namespace** in the etcd database, use the following commands: ~~~ $ export ETCD_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-etcd-l app=etcd--field-selector="status.phase==Running"-o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") $ oc exec-n openshift-etcd-c etcdctl ${ETCD_POD_NAME}-- sh-c 'etcdctl get /--prefix--keys-only | grep-oE-e "^/kubernetes.io/secrets/[-a-z|.0-9]*/"-e "^/kubernetes.io/configmaps/[-a-z|.0-9]*/"-e "^/kubernetes.io/events/[-a-z|.0-9]*/" | sort-u | while read KEY; do printf "$KEY	" && etcdctl get ${KEY##*}--prefix--print-value-only | wc-c | numfmt--to=iec; done | sort-k2-hr' | head-50 | awk-F'/' 'BEGIN{print "NAMESPACE TYPE SIZE"}{print $4" "$3" "$5}'| column-t ~~~ In the above example, the bigger `secrets`, `configmaps` and `events` per namespace are shown. Additional objects can be added with an additional `-e "^/kubernetes.io/[object_name]/[-a-z|.0-9]*/"` (replacing the `[object_name]`). To check size of individual objects, refer to [how to review the size of the largest `secrets` and `configmaps` in etcd on OpenShift?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7132598). > **Note:** for OpenShift Container Platform 3.11, execute the above `etcdctl` command with `etcdctl3` on the OpenShift Container Platform Master Nodes as `root`. * To check only the **number** of occurrences for each kind of object in the etcd database, use the following commands: ~~~ $ export ETCD_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-etcd-l app=etcd--field-selector="status.phase==Running"-o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") $ oc exec-n openshift-etcd ${ETCD_POD_NAME}-- sh-c "etcdctl get /--prefix--keys-only | sed '/^$/d' | cut-d/-f3 | sort | uniq-c | sort-rn" 5171 events 1172 secrets 446 configmaps 318 serviceaccounts 295 rolebindings [...] ~~~ This command will retrieve all keys from the etcd database and list how many objects there are by object type. > **Note:** for OpenShift Container Platform 3.11, execute the above `etcdctl` command with `etcdctl3` on the OpenShift Container Platform Master Nodes as `root`. * To check when specific objects were created (by month, and more detailed by day and by hour): ~~~ $ export OBJECT=[name_of_the_object_to_check] #### by month $ oc get ${OBJECT}-A-o jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{.metadata.creationTimestamp}{"
"}{end}' | grep-oE "[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}" | sort | uniq-c 1035 2024-11 [...] #### by day $ oc get ${OBJECT}-A-o jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{.metadata.creationTimestamp}{"
"}{end}' | grep-oE "[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}" | sort | uniq-c 613 2024-11-17 81 2024-11-18 [...] #### by hour $ oc get ${OBJECT}-A-o jsonpath='{range.items[*]}{.metadata.creationTimestamp}{"
"}{end}' | grep-oE "[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}" | sort | uniq-c 39 2024-11-17T06 394 2024-11-17T07 [...] ~~~ * Check the specific responsible namespace(s) for specific objects with the following commands (change the `[name_of_the_object_to_check]` with the bigger object(s) from the output of the above commands): ~~~ $ export OBJECT=[name_of_the_object_to_check] $ for NS in $(oc get ns--no-headers-o custom-columns=NAME:metadata.name); do echo-e "$(oc get ${OBJECT}-n ${NS}--no-headers | wc-l)	${OBJECT} in ${NS}"; done | sort-nr [...] 673 secrets in argo-test 171 secrets in openshift-kube-apiserver 110 secrets in kube-system 87 secrets in openshift-monitoring [...] ~~~- The metric `kube-state-metrics` is quite complete, and can be used for PromQL to query the count of most objects. Examples in the [`kube-state-metrics` upstream documentation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/38e2fa6e5318a872f1afba37d34e601ea680140c/docs/metrics). > **Note:** The amount of objects may vary between clusters depending on the usage, and the cluster version. The output can be interesting to see if there are object types with too many objects (for example millions of `events`) and if most of them are in specific `namespaces`.
root_cause: It is possible to query the etcd database with command `etcdctl` from the etcd `pods` to retrieve the number and size of objects.

title: How to check if etcd needs defragmentation in OpenShift?
issue: - How to check if etcd needs defragmentation.- How much fragmentation is acceptable or unacceptable for etcd cluster?
resolution: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* According to [how to defrag etcd to decrease DB size in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5564771), user should defrag etcd when the `dbSize` and the `dbSizeInUse` differ in more than 40-50%. On the other hand, the automatic etcd defragmentation in OpenShift 4 is done when the difference is more than 45%, according to the [defragcontroller.go](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-etcd-operator/blob/fd67e610d5b01b8326a10bb92286877130dc1451/pkg/operator/defragcontroller/defragcontroller.go#L31) source code: ~~~ maxFragmentedPercentage float64 = 45 [...] func isEndpointBackendFragmented(member *etcdserverpb.Member, endpointStatus *clientv3.StatusResponse) bool {if endpointStatus == nil {klog.Errorf("endpoint status validation failed: %v", endpointStatus) return false} fragmentedPercentage:= checkFragmentationPercentage(endpointStatus.DbSize, endpointStatus.DbSizeInUse) if fragmentedPercentage > 0.00 {klog.Infof("etcd member %q backend store fragmented: %.2f %%, dbSize: %d", member.Name, fragmentedPercentage, endpointStatus.DbSize)} return fragmentedPercentage > = maxFragmentedPercentage && endpointStatus.DbSize > = minDefragBytes} [...] func checkFragmentationPercentage(ondisk, inuse int64) float64 {diff:= float64(ondisk- inuse) fragmentedPercentage:= (diff / float64(ondisk)) * 100 return math.Round(fragmentedPercentage*100) / 100} ~~~ #### Check if the etcd needs manual defragmentation * To check if the etcd needs manual defragmentation, it is possible to get the `dbSize` and `dbSizeInUse` by: ~~~ $ export ETCD_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-etcd-l app=etcd--field-selector="status.phase==Running"-o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") $ oc exec ${ETCD_POD_NAME}-c etcd-n openshift-etcd-- etcdctl endpoint status--cluster-w json | jq ~~~ * It is also possible to use `jq` to calculate the the fragment percentage: ~~~ $ export ETCD_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-etcd-l app=etcd--field-selector="status.phase==Running"-o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}") $ oc exec $ETCD_POD_NAME-c etcd-n openshift-etcd-- etcdctl endpoint status--cluster-w json | jq '.[].Status|"dbSize: " + (.dbSize|tostring) + ", dbSizeInUse: " + (.dbSizeInUse|tostring) + ", (dbSize-dbSizeInUse)/dbSize => " + ((.dbSize-.dbSizeInUse)/.dbSize*100|tostring)+"%"' ~~~ If `[(dbSize- dbSizeInUse) / dbSize]` % > 45%, it should be considered to perform etcd defragmentation. Then, refer to [how to compact and defrag etcd to decrease database size in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5564771) or [how to defrag etcd to decrease DB size in Red Hat OpenShift 3](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3259921).
root_cause: The documentation of OpenShift Container Platform does not provide a clear standard on when should perform etcd defragmentation.

title: How to defrag etcd to decrease DB size in Red Hat OpenShift 3?
issue: - `etcd` DB is large, how can one defrag `etcd`?- Following error message can be seen from etcd pods: ~~~ etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded ~~~- The master API fails to start after hitting this issue.
resolution: ### For OpenShift 4 Check solution [how to defrag etcd in OpenShift to decrease DB size in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5564771). ### For OpenShift 3.11- Maintenance should be done monthly or bi-monthly to ensure `etcd` health.- When encountering the above message, the `etcd` cluster may enter maintenance mode. The first step is to try pruning objects to free up storage used by `etcd`.- If that doesn't work, `compacting/defragmenting` etcd may help to free additional space.- Before doing anything, ensure you take a [snapshot(backup) of the etcd data](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/3.11/day_two_guide/environment_backup.html#etcd-backup_environment-backup).- To take a snapshot/backup, run the following on your `etcd` host: # Backup ETCD Configuration $ mkdir-p /etc/etcd/etcd-config-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ $ cp-R /etc/etcd/ /etc/etcd/etcd-config-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ # Backup ETCD Data $ etcdctl3 snapshot save /var/lib/etcd/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)-backup.db # Confirm backup $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl3--write-out=table snapshot status /var/lib/etcd/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d)-backup.db- Gather endpoint status and source/set variables: # source /etc/etcd/etcd.conf # export ETCDCTL_API=3 # ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS=`etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_LISTEN_CLIENT_URLS--write-out=fields member list | awk '/ClientURL/{printf "%s%s",sep,$3; sep=","}'` # etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS--write-out=table endpoint status- Compact `etcd` using the same `rev` value for all members. # rev=$(etcdctl3 endpoint status--write-out="json" | egrep-o '"revision":[0-9]*' | egrep-o '[0-9]*'-m1) # etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--endpoints=$ETCD_ALL_ENDPOINTS compact $rev- Then run the `defrag` command once for each `etcd` member.- This command should be run against each member individually, setting one member at a time using the `--endpoints` argument; also set the flag `--command-timeout=30s`.- It is preferred to run the command against the leader last.- If a timeout occurs, increase the `--command-timeout` value until the command succeeds.- Replace `$MEMBER_IP` with the `etcd` IP # MEMBER_IP= # etcdctl3--cert=$ETCD_PEER_CERT_FILE--key=$ETCD_PEER_KEY_FILE--cacert=$ETCD_TRUSTED_CA_FILE--command-timeout=30s--endpoints=https://$MEMBER_IP:2379 defrag # etcdctl3 alarm disarm
root_cause: > ***Disclaimer:** Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* The OpenShift installation Ansible playbook(3.7-3.11) sets "[ETCD_QUOTA_BACKEND_BYTE](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-ansible/blob/release-3.7/roles/etcd/templates/etcd.conf.j2#L48)" to [4294967296(4G)](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-ansible/blob/release-3.7/roles/etcd/defaults/main.yaml#L97) by default. If one of the `etcd` members exceeds the quota, all cluster members will enter maintenance mode and only accept key reads and deletes. Setting [etcd space quota](https://github.com/coreos/etcd/blob/master/Documentation/op-guide/maintenance.md#space-quota) allows for better performance. Without it, `etcd` may suffer from poor performance when key-spaces grow excessively large, or storage is depleted. If your cluster contains a large number of objects or you create/delete a large number of objects, you should consider increasing this value and/or compacting and de-fragmenting the database periodically.

title: Quay repository mirroring fails with `408 Request Time-out` error.
issue: - Quay repository mirroring fails with `408 Request Time-out` error.- Image pull fails with `Error: parsing image configuration: fetching blob: StatusCode: 408, 408 Request Time-out`
resolution: - Update the network configuration to allow stable, uninterrupted connections to the remote registry. After this, rerun the mirroring process.

resolution: Red Hat has deprecated the legacy Fuse 7 Console in favor of the Hawtio console, which is the officially supported web-based management interface going forward. title: Very slow POD to POD throughput via vxlan when the Hypervisor has bnx2x_en NIC(s)
issue: - On our OCP cluster, communication between pods running on different worker nodes is extremely slow. The cluster is installed on 25 GB Ethernet, yet inter pod communication has throughput only in 8-9 Mbit range.
resolution: Update the device firmware. * `BCM5741x` firmware `224.1.102.0b` or later (Nov 2022) * `BCM5750x` is awaiting ETA from Broadcom ### Workaround Disable the GRO hardware offloading feature on hypervisor, using command: ethtool-K rx-gro-hw off
root_cause: There is an issue with GRO hardware offloading (`rx-gro-hw`) on some `bnxt_en` NICs which causes degraded VXLAN performance. VXLAN GRO packets are dropped at the tap interface to VM due to the `vxlan` module not being loaded, but VXLAN offload being enabled by default in the NIC firmware. To mitigate this, Broadcom have released a fix for BCM5741x devices in firmware version `224.1.102.0b`. This fix disables VXLAN and Geneve tunnel offload by default, and enables them dynamically only upon request from driver. This avoids the need to explicitly disable hardware GRO offloading with `ethtool`. Note: For a multi-port/multi-function device, if the ports/functions are not in the same kernel space (which is not a typical scenario), the firmware workaround might not be effective. In those situations, it might be necessary to explicitly enable/disable hardware GRO offloading manually.

title: RHCL Policy shows "Accepted (Not Enforced)" and is waiting for Gateway to sync
issue: A RHCL policy, such as an AuthPolicy, has a status condition where Enforced is False with the message: `waiting for the following components to sync: [Gateway (...)]`.
resolution: There are two options to resolve this issue. #### Option 1 If the native OpenShift Gateway API (openshift-default) is to be used, the Red Hat Connectivity Link operator must be explicitly configured to manage gateways of this class. This is done by editing the Subscription resource for Connectivity Link and adding the `ISTIO_GATEWAY_CONTROLLER_NAMES` environment variable. apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription... spec: config: env:- name: ISTIO_GATEWAY_CONTROLLER_NAMES value: openshift.io/gateway-controller/v1... Refer to [Release Notes for Connectivity Link 1.1](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_connectivity_link/1.1/html-single/release_notes_for_connectivity_link_1.1/index) for more details. #### Option 2 When the intention is to use Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh (OSSM) to provide the gateway, the Gateway resource must specify the istio GatewayClass. apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Gateway metadata:.... spec: gatewayClassName: istio....

title: AgentClusterInstall failing due to reference to incorrect mirror-registry in RHACM
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - During the deployment of an OCP cluster using RHACM 2.11, observed below error in `AgentClusterInstall` for mirror-registry i.e `registry-2` whereas `registry-1` is referenced in `AgentServiceConfig`. ~~~ message: 'The Spec could not be synced due to an input error: pull secret for new cluster is invalid: pull secret must contain auth for " registry-2"' ~~~
resolution: - Check if there is any `ClusterImageSet ` with same version but different registry exists. ~~~ $ oc get clusterimageset ~~~- If yes, delete duplicate `ClusterImageSet` which is not referenced in `AgentClusterInstall` ~~~ $ oc delete clusterimageset ~~~- Restart `assisted-service` pod ~~~ $ oc get pod-n multicluster-engine-l app=assisted-service $ oc delete pod-n multicluster-engine ~~~
root_cause: - `Assisted-service` tries to cache all `ClusterImageSets`. During cluster deployment, it doesn't match it by `ClusterImageSet ` name, rather it just passes in the architecture and version. Then assisted tries to find a matching image from the cache.- Due to cache, wrong registry selected instead of one which is configured. Restarting `assisted-service` pod helps to refresh cache.

title: How to remove a worker node from Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 UPI?
issue: - How to remove a `worker` node from an `UPI` installation of `Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4`?- Documentation explains only how to scale down a `MachineSet` but a `baremetal` or any other `UPI` installed cluster lacks of `MachineSets`.- How to recover a `worker` node that has been deleted?
resolution: **NOTE: If you are running ODF on worker nodes, removing the worker nodes where ODF pods run can cause data loss. Please do not remove nodes in such a situation. Scaling down ODF cluster is not supported. If you want to remove worker nodes where ODF is running, please file a support case.** When you delete a node using the CLI, the node object is deleted in `Kubernetes`, but the `pods` that exist on the node are not deleted. Any bare `pods` not backed by a replication controller become inaccessible to `OpenShift Container Platform`. `Pods` backed by replication controllers are rescheduled to other available `nodes`. You must delete local manifest `pods`.- To delete the node from the `UPI` installation, the node must be firstly drained and then marked `unschedulable` prior to [deleting](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-working.html) it: ~~~ $ oc adm cordon $ oc adm drain--force--delete-local-data--ignore-daemonsets ~~~- Ensure also that there are no current `jobs/cronjobs` being ran or scheduled in this specific node as the draining does not take it into consideration.- For Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.7+, utilize the option `--delete-emptydir-data` in case `--delete-local-data` doesn't work. The `--delete-local-data` option is deprecated in favor of `--delete-emptydir-data`. ~~~ $ oc get node-o yaml > backupnode.yaml ~~~- To delete the node, run the command below. ~~~ $ oc delete node ~~~- Although the node object is now deleted from the cluster, it can still rejoin the cluster after `reboot` or if the `kubelet` service is restarted. To permanently delete the node and all its data, you must decommission the node once it is in `shutdown` mode.- **Apply this step only if node deletion is confirmed, since this step is going to non-revertible.** If the `node` is a Virtual machine, simply mark it `poweroff` and then `delete` it from `hypervisor` console and if's a physical `baremetal` machine, first `shred` it's disk as follows and then power if off. Shredding the disk will remove all data on top of the disk. ~~~ # nohup shred-n 25-f-z /dev/[HDD] ~~~ **This command will overwrite all data on `/dev/[HDD]` repeatedly, in order to make it harder for even very expensive hardware probing to recover the data. Command line parameter-z will overwrite this device with zeros at the end of cycle to re-write data 25 times (it can be overridden with-n [number]). One should consider running this command from RescueCD.** **If the node needs to be rejoined back to the cluster:**- Once the node is deleted from `OCP` Software Layer, it can be ready for a power-off activity, or if it is needed to rejoin the cluster, it could be possible to either restart the `kubelet` or create the `yaml` back: ~~~ $ oc create-f backupnode.yaml ~~~- In order to get the `node` back, it can also be back by restarting `kubelet` and `approve` any `node CSR` if generated. ~~~ $ systemctl restart kubelet ~~~

title: Azure Load Balancer Health Probe is showing several nodes Down in ARO
issue: - Why are the Health Probes failing on Azure Load Balancer in ARO?- Several nodes are down in Health Probes in ARO
resolution: It is an expected behavior because the ingress pods are not running on all cluster nodes so in consequence they don't have the ports that the load balancer check opened and therefore it doesn´t mean the other nodes are not working properly. More information about the Azure Load Balancer health probes can be found in:- [curling Azure loadbalancer health probes fails & changing health probe config fails](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6781561)- [How to Check Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) Load Balancer Health Probe Status and Filter by Specific Port](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7013900)
root_cause: The Azure Load Balancer points to every node of the cluster, but only the nodes with an ingress controller pod running are considered healthy from their perspective, as they are the only ones where the traffic is going to be routed.

title: Multus pods logging: [error] failed to find the primary CNI plugin
issue: - While trying to deploy new pods, the following error fires: ~~~ error adding pod to CNI network "multus-cni-network": plugin type="multus-shim" name="multus-cni-network" failed (add): CmdAdd (shim): failed to send CNI request: Post "http://dummy/cni": dial unix /run/multus/socket/multus.sock: connect: no such file or directory ~~~- The multus pods are continuously restarting with the following error: ~~~ [error] failed to find the primary CNI plugin: failed to find the cluster master CNI plugin: could not find a plugin configuration in /host/run/multus/cni/net.d [error] failed to create the configuration manager for the primary CNI plugin: failed to find the cluster master CNI plugin: could not find a plugin configuration in /host/run/multus/cni/net.d ~~~
resolution: 1. Restart the `nsx-node` pods in the `nsx-system` namespace: ~~~ $ oc rollout restart daemonset/nsx-node-agent-n nsx-system ~~~ 2. Restart the `multus` pods in the `openshift-multus` namespace: ~~~ $ oc rollout restart daemonset/multus-n openshift-multus ~~~ 3. After restarting multus, some nodes might get stuck in a `NotReady` status. If that's the case, just reboot the node.
root_cause: The issue might happen after a sudden shutdown or restart of the cluster. NCP should be able to create a config file called `.conflist` for each node under the `/host/run/multus/cni/net.d/` path. It should be a JSON containing the CNI to be executed in order to attach the network to nodes and pods. At the time of the issue, no file can be find under the path and that's why multus cannot find a CNI to use for new pods.

title: Set log level for 3scale APIcast on Operator via the `logLevel` field
issue: - How do you increase the log level on APIcast?
resolution: ####List of available APICast log level options Following is the list of log levels available in APIcast. Default level is **warn**.- debug- info- notice- warn- error- crit- alert- emerg ####Follow the steps based on the APICast deployment **3scale managed APICast**, manged by the [APIManager instance](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/installing_3scale/install-threescale-on-openshift-guide#deploying-apimanager-custom-resource) (only available starting with **3scale 2.11**, for older versions please refer to [this solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3652951) instead). One of the following approaches can be used.- Using command line Get the list of the apimanagers Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) in the current OpenShift Project: ~~~ $ oc get apimanagers ~~~ Get the current value of logLevel. This can be used to revert back to the original value. Setting logLevel in CRD is optional. The current value is null if logLevel is not set in the CRD, otherwise it is the value set in the CRD. ~~~ $ oc get apimanagers-o jsonpath='{.spec.apicast.stagingSpec.logLevel}' $ oc get apimanagers-o jsonpath='{.spec.apicast.productionSpec.logLevel}' ~~~ Patch the CRDs (replace with the name of the correct apimanager CRD) ~~~ $ oc patch apimanagers-p '{"spec":{"apicast":{"stagingSpec":{"logLevel":"debug"}}}}'--type=merge $ oc patch apimanagers-p '{"spec":{"apicast":{"productionSpec":{"logLevel":"debug"}}}}'--type=merge ~~~- Using Web Console Update the APIMananger Custom Resource Definition(CRD) with the *logLevel: debug* entry as follows. ~~~ spec: apicast: stagingSpec: logLevel: debug productionSpec: logLevel: debug ~~~ **NOTE**: Regardless of the approach used, wait for APIcast pods to roll out their respective configuration changes before performing any calls to APIcast in order for them to be logged verbosely. **APICast self-managed** deployed via the [operator](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_3scale_api_management/2.11/html/installing_3scale/installing-apicast#installing-the-apicast-operator)- Add the_logLevel: debug_ entry under the APIcast CRD specification as follows ~~~ spec: adminPortalCredentialsRef: name: 3scaleportal logLevel: debug ~~~

title: rpm-ostree rebase command fails with error "is rejected by policy" upgrading to OpenShift 4.19
issue: - Unable to upgrade to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.19.12, `rpm-ostree` command fails with below error: ~~~ Node test is reporting: "failed to update OS from local storage: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:02695f992e254ea004e2846a7bd0b2fa7d00298192e86244650a32d8b0583886: error running rpm-ostree rebase--experimental ostree-unverified-image:containers-storage:quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:02695f992e254ea004e2846a7bd0b2fa7d00298192e86244650a32d8b0583886: error: Creating importer: failed to invoke method OpenImage: failed to invoke method OpenImage: Running image containers-storage:[overlay@/var/lib/containers/storage+/run/containers/storage:overlay.skip_mount_home=true]quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:02695f992e254ea004e2846a7bd0b2fa7d00298192e86244650a32d8b0583886@e0bccfc882dbadb1be0cdf1eee16fd59e43f41d4c44eef740e56ca165ca9fd6a is rejected by policy.\n: exit status 1"' ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat Engineering via [OCPBUGS-62510](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-62510), and it is currently fixed in OpenShift 4.19.16 via [OCPBUGS-62788](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-62788) by [errata RHBA-2025:17662](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:17662). ### Workaround 1- To resume the cluster upgrade process follow the below steps:- Fetch the `target image digest` using the below command: ~~~ IMAGE=$(oc get cronjobs-n openshift-machine-config-operator machine-config-nodes-crd-cleanup-o jsonpath='{.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[*].image}') ~~~- Fetch the node that is stuck due to the error: ~~~ NODE=$(oc get mcp master-o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="NodeDegraded")].message}' | sed 's/^Node \([^]*\).*/\1/') ~~~- Remove the image from the node using the below command: ~~~ oc debug node/${NODE}-- chroot /host crictl rmi ${IMAGE} 2> &1 | grep-q "no such image"; do echo "Retrying in 5 seconds..."; sleep 5; done && echo "Success" ~~~ **IF THE ABOVE WORKAROUND FAILS:** ### Workaround 2 Remove the new osImageURL image if it exists on the node, this way the machine-config-daemon will retry the upgrade with the older method `rpm-ostree rebase--experimental ostree-unverified-registry: `. Run the below command to check if the image exists and remove it. ~~~ # podman images-q--filter reference= # podman rmi-f ~~~ Or Create the below config under root's home directory as skopeo first checks for policy.json under home directory before falling back to `/etc/containers/policy.json`. Once the upgrade is complete, please remove this file. ~~~ # cat.config/containers/policy.json {"default": [{"type": "reject"}], "transports": {"containers-storage": {"": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}]}}} ~~~
root_cause: Due to a recent change in the machine-config handling of the rpm-ostree rebase command, when the image exists locally, the system attempts to use the new ostree-unverified-image:containers-storage syntax. However, because Openshift cluster’s image configuration sets, the default container policy at following directory path `/etc/containers/policy.json` to "reject", this causes the rebase attempt to fail, as rpm-ostree uses skopeo command in the background, and skopeo first checks for policy.json under root's home directory before falling back to `/etc/containers/policy.json`. The new upgrade behavior has been introduced by [OCPBUGS-33248](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/OCPBUGS-33248).

title: How to append JVM options to JWS for OpenShift
issue: - How to append JVM options to JWS for OpenShift- The setting environment variable `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` does not work on JWS for OpenShift.
resolution: It's possible to add the environment variable `CATALINA_OPTS_APPEND` to a pod or DeploymentConfig like below: ~~~ oc set env dc/ CATALINA_OPTS_APPEND="-XX:+HeapDumpOnOufOfMemoryError-XX:HeapDumpPath=/ " ~~~ Setting `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` doesn't work has been filed as a known issue [CLOUD-2899[JWS] JAVA_OPTS_APPEND not working](https://issues.jboss.org/browse/CLOUD-2899). `GC_CONTAINER_OPTIONS` should be used to change GC algorithm from the default parallel collector to something else per [CLOUD-2941](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CLOUD-2941) ~~~ oc set env dc/ GC_CONTAINER_OPTIONS="-XX:+UseG1GC" ~~~
root_cause: The JWS container does not have the `JAVA_OPTS` and `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` flags, so the following need to be used: JWS environment variable | Equivalent in OpenJDK image-------------|----------- `CATALINA_OPTS` | Equivalent of `JAVA_OPTS` `CATALINA_OPTS_APPEND` | Equivalent of `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` `GC_CONTAINER_OPTIONS` | Same as OpenJDK's `GC_CONTAINER_OPTIONS`

title: OpenShift 4 installation support on Intel VROC RAID Configuration
issue: - Is Intel® VROC RAID is supported during the installation process?- Can OpenShift be installed on Intel® Virtual RAID on CPU (VROC) configurations, during the installation process (Day 0), as documentation suggested it was supported as a Day 2 operation?
resolution: Intel® VROC RAID configurations are supported during installation starting from OpenShift 4.16 as per the release notes: [support for RAID storage using Intel® Virtual RAID on CPU (VROC)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes#ocp-4-16-raid-intel-vroc_release-notes). Refer to [configuring an Intel® Virtual RAID on CPU (VROC) data volume](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/installation_configuration/installing-customizing#installation-special-config-raid-intel-vroc_installing-customizing) for the procedure to configure an Intel® VROC-enabled RAID1 ensuring that the RAID is properly set up before installation. This procedure is only valid for UPI installations. The [RFE-7613](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7613) was created to request the support for IPI installations.
root_cause: Prior to OCP 4.16, support for Intel® VROC was in Technology Preview. With the release of 4.16, it became Generally Available (GA), thus supported for installation: [support for RAID storage using Intel® Virtual RAID on CPU (VROC)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes#ocp-4-16-raid-intel-vroc_release-notes).

title: Is NGINX container aware?
issue: - Is NGINX container aware?
resolution: It is not container aware: so NGINX will use the limits from the Openshift HOST for `worker_processes` calculations. Example: If deploying in a host with four CPUs it will generate the 4 `worker_process`: ~~~ sh-4.4$ ps-aux USER PID %CPU %MEM VSZ RSS TTY STAT START TIME COMMAND 1000860+ 1 0.0 0.1 44084 9472? Ss 15:15 0:00 nginx: master process nginx-g daemon off; 1000860+ 7 0.0 0.0 44528 3704? S 15:15 0:00 nginx: worker process 1000860+ 8 0.0 0.0 44528 3704? S 15:15 0:00 nginx: worker process 1000860+ 9 0.0 0.0 44528 3704? S 15:15 0:00 nginx: worker process 1000860+ 10 0.0 0.0 44528 3704? S 15:15 0:00 nginx: worker process ~~~
root_cause: The [NGINX blog post documentation](https://blog.nginx.org/blog/performance-tuning-tips-tricks) on the matter is ambiguous, therefore unclear, given the following: > However, when NGINX Plus is running in a containerized environment such as Docker, a system admin might chose to assign fewer cores to the container that are available on the **host machine**. In this case, NGINX Plus detects the number available on the **host**, and rotates workers among the cores that are actually available within that container. In that case, reduce the number of workers by setting worker_processes to the number of cores available in the container. Above could be understand that NGINX is **NOT container-aware** and simulates container awareness by detecting the cgroup limitation and using those cores as below: 1. nginx is started in a container with a CPU limitation 2. nginx detects x number of processors from the Openshift host 3. nginx detects y number of allowed CPU cores allocated through cgroup in the container 4. nginx uses y CPUs to assign workers accordingly However, it is not clear what is this rotation process detailed. Also, it is seems counter-intuitive the need to reduce the number of workers yourself, which to me indicates it is indeed not container aware. ### Consequences Corollary to the discussion above, it is the association between the container memory and container CPUs for container deployments in Openshift 4:- For the memory: the container will still be OOMKill in case it crosses its cgroups limits. Any instrumentation, such as Dynatrace, may add on the footprint.- For the CPU: the CPUs container impacts (although not as a authoritative/final limit) on the `worker_processes`. This can be tune in a case-by-case basis.

title: SRIOV NIC drivers can allocate up to 500MB of memory for ring buffers per PF
issue: - ice driver consumes 15GB of memory with below call trace when VFs are created.- Every time we create 1 VF on a NIC port, memory usage increases by approximately 500 MB.- Removing the VF brings back the memory to normal. So we suspect its not a memory leak, but unexpected use of 500MB for each VF which seems not reasonable. It should be a maximum of 40MB.
resolution: - If possible only set the VFs MTU to 9000 and leave the PF as 1500.- Otherwise consider decreasing the number of NIC queues with e.g: `ethtool-L combined 8`, also if possible reduce the number of RX descriptors with e.g: `ethtool-G rx 512` for PFs.
root_cause: - This issue is triggered when the VF is provisioned. OpenShift is one common environment where this configuration is triggered, but the issue is not limited to the OpenShift environment.- This is expected because the SRIOV operator assigns VFs to multiple PFs and increases the PF MTU to 9000 at the same time. The bulk of the memory increase is due to the MTU 9000 setting on the PF which requires 6x the memory of the default 1500 MTU. The SRIOV operator sets the MTU to 9000 on a PF and then assigns a VF. It uses multiple PFs in the process and by setting the MTU to 9000 increases the memory dramatically considering 2048 descriptors of 9000 bytes are added for each of the 64 NIC queues per PF.
