title: Does OpenShift GitOps provide any compatibility features for using Argo Workflows and Argo Events ?
issue: - Are there any features in OpenShift GitOps that support Argo Workflows and Argo Events?- Does OpenShift GitOps offer any native support or integration for Argo Workflows and Argo Events?
resolution: **Argo Workflows and Argo Events** cannot be directly managed through the ArgoCD Operator (or OpenShift GitOps Operator) available on *OperatorHub*. **Instead:**- Deploy Argo Workflows and Argo Events manually using Helm charts or manifests.- Manage them declaratively using OpenShift GitOps (Argo CD) for synchronization and lifecycle management.- If Red Hat–certified Operator-based automation is required, consider the following supported alternatives:- OpenShift Pipelines (Tekton) for workflow orchestration- Ansible Automation Platform Operator, which includes Event‑Driven Ansible (EDA) for event automation These operators are available on *OperatorHub* and supported by Red Hat, *providing automatic CRD creation, namespace isolation, and RBAC management.*
root_cause: - **Argo Workflows and Argo Events** are community CNCF projects and have no native integration with the ArgoCD Operator. The ArgoCD Operator is designed only to handle Argo CD instances and associated GitOps CRDs. This leads to confusion when users expect the operator to manage all Argo components within OpenShift.

title: Changing the TimeZone of the Logs when forwarding the Logs to a LogStore in RHOCP4
issue: - Is it possible to change the `TimeZone` of a log before sending/forwarding it to a `LogStore`?
resolution: As of writing the article, converting the `TimeZone` of the log when sending it to a `LogStore` is not possible. However, a request to make this feature available in the RHOL has been made to the Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in RFE [OBSDA-1322](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-1322). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. **Note: Even if the TimeZone of the node or pod is changed even then the logs will still be forwarded to LogStore in default `TimeZone` which is `UTC`.**
root_cause: Currently there is no possibility to change the TimeZone of a log to a custom value, This feature will allow users to forward the logs to an endpoint with logs getting shipped to the endpoint in a custom TimeZone.

title: Monitoring Operator Degraded Due to Alertmanager Pod Pending from Volume Node Affinity Conflict
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: The monitoring Cluster Operator is in a Degraded state with the error: ~~~ UpdatingAlertmanagerFailed: waiting for Alertmanager openshift-monitoring/main: context deadline exceeded. ~~~ One of the Alertmanager pods remains in **Pending*
state and cannot be scheduled.
resolution: To resolve the issue, ensure that the Alertmanager pod can be scheduled on a node that satisfies **both pod anti-affinity rules and PV node affinity constraints.** Choose one of the following options: **1. Add an additional worker node in eu-west-3a zone**- This allows the second Alertmanager pod to attach its Persistent Volume while still honoring the required pod anti-affinity (Alertmanager replicas must run on different nodes). **2. Migrate one of the Alertmanager Persistent Volumes to eu-west-3b zone**- Recreate the PV in eu-west-3b and rebind it to the corresponding PVC.- This enables scheduling across zones while preserving anti-affinity rules. **Note:** Pod anti-affinity rules must not be modified, as Alertmanager replicas are required to run on separate nodes for high availability. Once a valid node–volume placement is available, the pending Alertmanager pod will schedule successfully and the monitoring operator will recover.
root_cause: The Alertmanager pod (alertmanager-main-1) could not be scheduled due to a **Persistent Volume node affinity conflict**.- Both Alertmanager PVs are restricted to eu-west-3a via EBS CSI node affinity.- The cluster has only **one worker node** in eu-west-3a, which is already occupied by the other Alertmanager pod (alertmanager-main-0).- Pod anti-affinity rules prevent Alertmanager replicas from running on the same node.- As a result, no eligible node satisfies both:- Pod anti-affinity requirements- PV zone affinity requirements This causes the pod to remain in **Pending** state and the monitoring operator to report a degraded condition.

title: CDI DataVolume upload fails with Pending status on RHOCP 4
issue: - Uploading an ISO file or creating a `DataVolume` results in the process hanging in a `Pending` state.- The `PersistentVolumeClaim` (`PVC`) associated with the `DataVolume` remains in `Pending` status despite being created.- The upload process eventually times out with the error: `Data Volume failed to initiate upload`.
resolution: To resolve the issue, the `DataVolume` or `PersistentVolumeClaim` must be configured to use an access mode compatible with the underlying `StorageClass` and Volume Mode. 1. Get the `DataVolume` and `PVC` yaml in the file. ~~~ $ oc get dv-o yaml > dataVolume.yaml $ oc get pvc-o yaml > pvc.yaml ~~~ 2. Change the `accessMode` in the `dataVolume` YAML Configuration. ~~~ $ vi dataVolume.yaml apiVersion: cdi.kubevirt.io/v1beta1 kind: DataVolume metadata: name: first-boot-volume spec: source: upload: {} pvc: accessModes:- ReadWriteOnce # Ensure this is ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 10Gi storageClassName: powerstore volumeMode: Block ~~~ 3. Apply the new `DataVolume` YAML configuration. ~~~ $ oc apply-f dataVolume.yaml datavolume.cdi.kubevirt.io/first-boot-volume created ~~~ 4. Verify that the `PersistentVolumeClaim` binds immediately and the status becomes Bound. ~~~ $ oc get pvc NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE first-boot-volume Bound pvc-12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab 10Gi RWO powerstore 2m ~~~ 5. Start the upload using `virtctl` (if not using the web console). ~~~ $ virtctl image-upload dv--image-path=--no-create Example: $ virtctl image-upload dv first-boot-volume--image-path=/home/user/isos/rhel-installer.iso--no-create Uploading data to https://cdi-uploadproxy-openshift-cdi.apps.cluster.example.com 10.00 GiB / 10.00 GiB [===================================================================================================] 100.00% 1m30s ~~~

title: HCP NodePool creation is failing with a NoSuitableAgents error in RHOCP 4
issue: - When creating or scaling a `NodePool`, the process fails or gets stuck with the `NoSuitableAgents` status.- During the creation or scaling of the `NodePool`, the `capi-provider` pod reports the error `role.rbac.authorization.k8s.io capi-provider-role not found`.
resolution: Create the missing `capi-provider-role` in the namespace where the `Agents` reside (Only role needs to be created). ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: annotations: metaclusterinstall.openshift.io/sync-wave: "1" name: capi-provider-role namespace: rules:- apiGroups:- agent-install.openshift.io resources:- agents verbs:- '*' ~~~
root_cause: When a `HostedCluster` is created via the command line `hcp` client, the client creates a `Role` in the cluster namespace that allows access to agents in that namespace. When creating a `HostedCluster` without the client, that role must be manually created.

title: How to run Ansible hook on Windows VM while migrating it using Migration Toolkit for Virtualization(MTV)?
issue: Getting following error while trying to use `windows.win_shell` in Ansible hook: ~~~ ERROR! couldn't resolve module/action 'ansible.windows.win_shell'. This often indicates a misspelling, missing collection, or incorrect module path. The error appears to be in '/tmp/hook/playbook.yml': line 7, column 7, but may be elsewhere in the file depending on the exact syntax problem. ~~~
resolution: The default hook-runner image provided by MTV does not include the necessary Ansible Windows collections. To run Windows-specific modules, a custom hook-runner image including the `ansible.windows` collection is required. 1. Create a Dockerfile using the default hook-runner as a base and installing the required collection: ~~~ FROM quay.io/konveyor/hook-runner:latest USER root RUN ansible-galaxy collection install ansible.windows USER 65534:65534 ~~~ 2. Build the image using podman and push it to a registry accessible by the OpenShift cluster: ~~~ podman build-t / /custom-windows-hook-runner:latest. podman push / /custom-windows-hook-runner:latest ~~~ Use this image as a pre-hook image. Following is an example playbook: ~~~- name: Main hosts: localhost tasks:- name: Load Plan include_vars: file: plan.yml name: plan- name: Load Workload include_vars: file: workload.yml name: workload- add_host: name: "{{workload.vm.ipaddress}}" ansible_user: Administrator groups: vms ansible_user: user ansible_password: pass ansible_connection: winrm ansible_port: 5985 ansible_winrm_transport: basic # Play 2 put the custom scripts here- hosts: vms tasks:- name: your custom scripts here................ ~~~
root_cause: The standard `quay.io/konveyor/hook-runner` image is a minimal Ansible environment that does not pre-install the ansible.windows collection. So the playbooks utilizing modules like win_shell fail because the underlying Ansible runtime cannot locate the module definitions.

title: OpenShift Console Plugins Fail to Load After Upgrade from 4.19.2 to 4.19.3 in RHOCP4
issue: - After upgrading OpenShift Container Platform from `4.19.2 to 4.19.3`, multiple OpenShift Console UI features are no longer accessible. The Networking and Virtualization tabs are missing from the OpenShift web console, and several console plugins fail to load.- The OpenShift Console reports degraded **console plugins**, and errors such as the following are observed in the console pod logs: ~~~ E0717 10:40:00 handlers.go:164] failed to send GET request for "pipelines-console-plugin": Get "https://pipelines-console-plugin.openshift-pipelines.svc.cluster:8443/plugin-manifest.json": dial tcp 10.0.1.x:8443: connect: connection refused E0717 10:40:15 handlers.go:164] failed to send GET request for "odf-console" plugin: Get "https://odf-console-service.openshift-storage.svc.cluster:9001/compatibility/plugin-manifest.json": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is valid for machine-config-daemon.openshift-machine-config-operator.svc, not odf-console-service.openshift-storage.svc.cluster.local E0717 10:40:15 handlers.go:164] failed to send GET request for "kubevirt-plugin": Get "https://kubevirt-console-plugin-service.openshift-cnv.svc.cluster:9443/plugin-manifest.json": dial tcp 10.0.x.x:9443: connect: connection refused ~~~
resolution: - To resolve the issue remove the degraded console plugins from the `console.operator` configuration. **Step 1: Identify degraded console plugins** ~~~ $ oc get consoleplugins.console.openshift.io ~~~ *Example output*: ~~~ forklift-console-plugin kubevirt-plugin monitoring-plugin networking-console-plugin nmstate-console-plugin odf-console pipelines-console-plugin ~~~ **Step 2: Back up the affected console plugins** Before making any changes, back up the plugin configurations: ~~~ $ oc get consoleplugins.console.openshift.io-o yaml >.yaml ~~~ Repeat this step for all degraded plugins. **Step 3: Edit the console operator configuration** Edit the `console.operator` resource: ~~~ $ oc edit console.operator ~~~ Remove the degraded plugins from the `spec.plugins` list. For example: ~~~ plugins:- forklift-console-plugin--------> ** delete this entry **- kubevirt-plugin--------> ** delete this entry **- monitoring-plugin- networking-console-plugin- nmstate-console-plugin--------> ** delete this entry **- odf-console--------> ** delete this entry ** ~~~
root_cause: - During the upgrade from OpenShift `4.19.2 to 4.19.3`, several console plugins failed to reconcile correctly with the updated OpenShift Console API. As a result, the console attempted to load plugins that were either unreachable or incompatible, leading to `connection errors and TLS validation failures`.- These degraded plugins blocked the OpenShift Console from rendering associated UI components, causing multiple menu items and features to disappear.

[/usr/src/nvidia-580.65.06/kernel-open/Kbuild:290: preempt_rt_sanity_check] Error 1 make[2]: **
Waiting for unfinished jobs.... make[1]: **

[Makefile:138: modules] Error 2 ++ make-s-j SYSSRC=/lib/modules/5.14.0-427.87.1.el9_4.x86_64+rt/build clean ~~~

title: error: x509 certificate signed by unknown authority when logging in OpenShift 4 after replacing API certificate
issue: - API certificate has been replaced and now `oc login`fails with the next error: ~~~ $ oc login https://api.cluster.domain.tld:6443 error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~- Below command also throws same x509: certificate error: ~~~ $ oc get clusteroperator authentication ~~~- Adding the CA in the command line doesn't help: ~~~ $ oc login--certificate-authority=ca-cert.pem https://api.cluster.domain.tld:6443 error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~
resolution: - Replace the default Ingress certificate as detailed in [the documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/security/certificates/replacing-default-ingress-certificate.html) with one signed by a trusted CA OR- Add the CA which signed the default Ingress certificate as trusted in the system where the login is run. For more details, see [this article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4505101).
root_cause: - During a login operation two different hosts are reached: API and Authentication, therefore as they use different certificates both of them must be properly validated- The parameter `--certificate-authority` is only used to validate the API connections, so the Authentication URL must be validated using the CA bundle in the system.

title: How to Configure an HTTPS Gateway in OpenShift Service Mesh

title: Systemd units without content cannot be enabled via machine-config.
issue: - Machine-config does not allow enabling an existing systemd unit unless the unit’s content is explicitly specified, preventing management of pre-installed units.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this issue and is currently working on it. The issue is tacked under below JIRA: [Unable to enable systemd service on OCP 4.20](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-70259)
root_cause: As the affected machine-config did not have any content section in the unit, enabling the service has been skipped. This comes via below machine-config code, which would ignore such services. ~~~ # less pkg/daemon/update.go:: if u.Enabled!= nil {// Only when a unit has contents should we attempt to enable or disable it. <----- // See: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-56648 if unitHasContent(u) {if *u.Enabled {enabledUnits = append(enabledUnits, u.Name)} else {disabledUnits = append(disabledUnits, u.Name)}} else {action:= "disable" if *u.Enabled {action = "enable"} klog.Infof("Could not %s unit %q, because it has no contents, skipping", action, u.Name) <-- ~~~ This change was introduced to fix bug: [layered image update loops on failure to find systemd unit files, MCP degraded](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-56648) Below is the commit which has caused this behavior: ~~~ commit 702dd8b295b052efb698405bec78288f01f58f4b Date: Wed May 28 11:07:21 2025-0400 fixes systemd unit creation for empty units If a MachineConfig is applied with empty systemd unit contents, the MCD will degrade because it skips writing the file in that particular situation. For parity with the CoreOS Ignition implementation, we should not attempt to enable or disable any systemd units where the unit file does not have any contents. ~~~

title: Unable to set the IPv6 IP Ranges within the 'endpointPublishingStrategy.loadBalancer.allowedSourceRanges' field of the custom IngressController
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Unable to set an `IPv6` IP ranges in the `endpointPublishingStrategy.loadBalancer.allowedSourceRanges` field of the custom ingress controller.- The `IPv6` IP ranges cannot be applied to AWS Security groups.
resolution: The IPFamilies is a list of IP families (e.g. IPv4, IPv6) assigned to this service. This field is usually assigned automatically based on cluster configuration and the ipFamilyPolicy field. If this field is specified manually, the requested family is available in the cluster, and ipFamilyPolicy allows it, it will be used; otherwise creation of the service will fail. This field is conditionally mutable: it allows for adding or removing a secondary IP family, but it does not allow changing the primary IP family of the Service. Valid values are **IPv4** and **IPv6**. This field only applies to Services of types ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer, and does apply to headless services. This field will be wiped when updating a Service to type ExternalName. This field may hold a maximum of two entries (dual-stack families, in either order). These families must correspond to the values of the clusterIPs field, if specified. Both clusterIPs and ipFamilies are governed by the ipFamilyPolicy field. To enable a `dual stack` that supports `IPv6` IP ranges, you need to adjust the `Service spec` in the custom ingress controller. Please check this [Service spec Network APIs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/network_apis/service-v1#spec-19) for more information.

title: OADP backup stuck in 'Failed' state with error StatusCode: 504, api error GatewayTimeout: Gateway Timeout
issue: - The backup process stuck in `Failed` state due to the `error: 504, api error GatewayTimeout: Gateway Timeout` ~~~ rpc error: code = Unknown desc = error putting object velero/backups/xxxx-xxx-xxxx-xxxxxx/velero-backup.json: operation error S3: PutObject, exceeded maximum number of attempts, 3, https response error StatusCode: 504, RequestID:, HostID:, api error GatewayTimeout: Gateway Timeout ~~~- Velero logs showed an error:`Error checking repository for stale locks` ~~~ 2025-12-18T16:36:32.936718852Z time="2025-12-18T16:36:32Z" level=error msg="Error checking repository for stale locks" backupRepo=openshift-adp/xxx-velero-restic-xxxx error="error running command=restic unlock--repo=s3:https://s3-openshift-storage.apps.xxx.xxxx/velero-bucket-xxxxxx/velero/restic/xxxxxx--password-file=/tmp/credentials/openshift-adp/velero-repo-credentials-xxxxx--cache-dir=/scratch/.cache/restic--insecure-tls=true, stdout=, stderr=Fatal: config or key xxxxxxxxx ~~~
resolution: If you are using `Restic` for backups, switch to `Kopia` to resolve the `stale lock` errors identified in the logs. After switching, retry the backup and restore operation. While **OADP 1.3 and later** versions support both `Kopia` and `Restic` for application backups, Kopia is required when using the built-in Data Mover. In **OADP version 1.2 and earlier**, `Restic` is the only supported option. For more information, please refer to the documentation: [Backing up applications with File System Backup: Kopia or Restic](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html-single/backup_and_restore/index#oadp-backing-up-applications-restic-doc) on how to configure the File System backup and [About Kopia]("https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html-single/backup_and_restore/index#oadp-about-kopia") to learn more about how to use Kopia.

title: How to Use a Service Account to modify ROSA Machine Pools via OpenShift API (api.openshift.com)
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Unable to modify a ROSA cluster machine pool using OpenShift API (api.openshift.com)- When doing a `PATCH` using a Service account, an error message occur: ~~~ {"kind":"Error","id":"422","href":"/api/clusters_mgmt/v1/errors/422","code":"CLUSTERS-MGMT-422","reason":"Specified account is invalid","operation_id":"xxxxxx-5e2f-4921-a936-xxxxxx"} ~~~
resolution: Please follow the steps on how to modify the machine pool using OpenShift API (api.openshift.com): 1. From the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, Go to Cluster > Access Control > Add the OCM Roles and Access as Machine pool Editor or Cluster Editor. 2. Go to Machine pools tab > Click on Add the Machine pool. 3. From the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, Click the settings icon (⚙) and click Service Accounts > Click Create service account > Enter a Service account name and a Short description and click Create > Copy and Save the Client ID and Client Secret 4. Add the Service Account in the User Groups. In this case, make sure to add the OCM Machine pool editor. **NOTE:** Adding roles **take an hour** to sync up in the RBAC 5. After an hour, Paste the following information on a terminal, replacing the CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET variables ~~~ export HOST='https://sso.redhat.com' CLIENT_ID=' ' CLIENT_SECRET=' ' SCOPES='openid api.iam.service_accounts' ~~~ 6. Get a token for the service account with ~~~ curl "${HOST}/auth/realms/redhat-external/protocol/openid-connect/token" \--data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \--data-urlencode "client_id=${CLIENT_ID}" \--data-urlencode "client_secret=${CLIENT_SECRET}" \--data-urlencode "scope=${SCOPES}" ~~~ 7. Send a request to an application that supports service accounts: ~~~ curl--header "Authorization:Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"--location "https://console.redhat.com/api/rbac/v1/access/?application=inventory" ~~~ 8. The response should be empty, or unprivileged depending on the app. Try adding the service account to an RBAC group, and adding roles to that group. [User Access Groups](https://console.redhat.com/iam/user-access/groups?per_page=50&page=1) 9. Copy the Access token, paste and Authorize it in the URL: [https://api.openshift.com/api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/] (https://api.openshift.com/api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/) 10. **Testing the GET Request**: Execute the `GET` request to the following endpoint:`/api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/{cluster_id}/machine_pools/` by entering your `cluster_id` in the appropriate field. A **200 OK** response code confirms that the service account credentials are functioning correctly. 11. **Modifying the Machine Pool**: Perform a `PATCH` request to the following endpoint: `PATCH /api/clusters_mgmt/v1/clusters/{cluster_id}/machine_pools/{machine_pool_id}` In the `Request Body`, include the following `JSON` to update the replica count below. A **200 OK** response indicates that the machine pool has been successfully updated. ~~~ {"replicas": 2 <--- Set this to your desired number of replicas} ~~~ For more information, please refer to the following documentation: [Transition of Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console APIs from basic authentication to token-based authentication via service accounts](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7036194) [Creating and Managing a Service Account](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_hybrid_cloud_console/1-latest/html/creating_and_managing_service_accounts/proc-ciam-svc-acct-overview-creating-service-acct) [Using service accounts with services](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_hybrid_cloud_console/1-latest/html/creating_and_managing_service_accounts/ref-ciam-svc-acct-api-creating-service-acct#:~:text=Chapter%C2%A03.-,Using%20service%20accounts%20with%20services,-The%20following%20information)

title: Machine Config Operator stuck due to invalid machineconfignodes CRD in RHOCP 4
issue: - While upgrading an RHOCP cluster sequentially from `4.16.47 → 4.17.45 → 4.18.30 → 4.19.21`, the upgrade is halted due to CRD corruption.- The `Machine Config Operator (MCO)` does not progress, and the cluster upgrade is halted with an error indicating an `invalid value` in `machineconfignodes.machineconfiguration.openshift.io` CustomResourceDefinition.- On listing the `Cluster version` it shows the below error: ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion-o yaml Message: Could not update customresourcedefinition "machineconfignodes.machineconfiguration.openshift.io" (785 of 924): the object is invalid, possibly due to local cluster configuration Reason: UpdatePayloadResourceInvalid Status: True Type: Failing Last Transition Time: 202x-0x-01T0x:2x:xxx Message: Unable to apply 4.19.21: some cluster configuration is invalid Reason: UpdatePayloadResourceInvalid: CustomResourceDefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io \"machineconfignodes.machineconfiguration.openshift.io\" is invalid: status.storedVersions[0]: Invalid value: \"v1alpha1\": must appear in spec.versions" logger="UnhandledError" ~~~
resolution: 1. Take a backup of the affected `CustomResourceDefinition`: ~~~ $ oc get crd machineconfignodes.machineconfiguration.openshift.io-o yaml > machineconfignodes-crd-backup.yaml ~~~ 2. Delete the `invalid CustomResourceDefinition`: ~~~ $ oc delete crd machineconfignodes.machineconfiguration.openshift.io ~~~ 3. Restart the `Cluster Version Operator pod` to force reconciliation: ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n openshift-cluster-version-l k8s-app=cluster-version-operator ~~~ 4. Restart the `Machine Config Controller` & `Machine Config Operator` pods: ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n openshift-machine-config-operator-l k8s-app=machine-config-controller $ oc delete pod-n openshift-machine-config-operator-l k8s-app=machine-config-operator ~~~
root_cause: - The upgrade was blocked due to an invalid `storedVersions` entry (`v1alpha1`) present in the status of the `machineconfignodes.machineconfiguration.openshift.io` CustomResourceDefinition.- This version was no longer listed under `spec.versions`, causing `schema validation` to fail during the `4.19 upgrade payload application`.

title: Operator Installation Stuck in Pending State Due to Unmet CSV Requirements and Non-Established CRDs
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: An Operator installed via OLM remains in a Pending state with RequirementsNotMet. The ClusterServiceVersion (CSV) does not progress because one or more required components (such as CRDs or service accounts) are missing or not fully established. As a result, OLM cannot complete the operator installation and the operator does not become functional. (Example observed with External Secrets Operator where the CSV external-secrets-operator.v0.11.0 remained Pending.) NOTE: This issue was observed with Community version ESO however, the behavior is not operator specific and this KCS can be referred for other operators.
resolution: 1. Identify CSV requirements that are not satisfied (CRDs, service accounts, RBAC, etc.). 2. For CRDs that are Present but not Established, manually (re)create the CRDs from the operator’s official release artifacts or source repository corresponding to the target version.- Example (External Secrets Operator v0.11.0): ~~~ kubectl apply-k https://github.com/external-secrets/external-secrets/config/crds/bases? ~~~ 3. Verify that all required CRDs reach the **Established=True** condition. 4. Confirm that required service accounts and related RBAC objects are created. 5. Once all requirements are satisfied, OLM automatically reconciles the CSV and transitions it to Succeeded, allowing the operator to function normally.
root_cause: The operator CSV remained in Pending state because OLM detected unmet requirements. Although the CRDs were present, several of them were not fully established due to naming conflicts `(NamesAccepted=True but Established=False)`. Additionally, dependent resources (such as the controller service account) were not created because OLM halts installation until all CSV requirements are satisfied. This left the operator in a deadlock where retries and CSV re-creation did not resolve the underlying dependency issues.

title: How adjust this group_wait and group_interval parameters based on the severity of alerts?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - We want to adjust group_wait as 1 minute group_interval as 10 minutes for critical alerts, group_wait as 5 minutes group_interval as 60 minutes for warning alerts, group_wait as 60 minutes group_interval as 6 hours for info alerts separately.
resolution: In alertmanager config route-> routes you can set a custom group_interval, group_wait per matcher to a receiver. For example, similar configuration with repeat_interval: ~~~ global: http_config: tls_config: insecure_skip_verify: true resolve_timeout: 15m smtp_require_tls: false smtp_from: '01-central-alertmanager@myhost.com' smtp_smarthost: 'smtp.myhost.com:25' route: group_wait: 120s group_interval: 20m repeat_interval: 24h group_by: ['severity', 'cluster1'] receiver: default routes:- matchers:- severity = warning- alertname!~ "(?i)alertmy.*|caas.*|cpet.*|cog.*"- namespace =~ "openshift-.*|myvector|kyverno|external-secrets|kube-.*|default|openshift|^$" repeat_interval: 12h receiver: warning- matchers:- severity = warning- alertname =~ "(?i)alertmy.*"- namespace =~ "openshift-.*|myvector|kyverno|external-secrets|kube-.*|default|openshift|^$" repeat_interval: 12h receiver: warning-example- matchers:- severity = critical- alertname!~ "(?i)alertmy.*|caas.*|cpet.*|cog.*"- namespace =~ "openshift-.*|myvector|kyverno|external-secrets|kube-.*|default|openshift|^$" repeat_interval: 4h receiver: critical- matchers:- severity = critical- alertname =~ "(?i)alertmy.*"- namespace =~ "openshift-.*|myvector|kyverno|external-secrets|kube-.*|default|openshift|^$" repeat_interval: 4h receiver: critical-example- matchers:- alertname = "DeadMansSwitch" repeat_interval: 5m receiver: deadmansswitch receivers:- name: default- name: deadmansswitch- name: warning slack_configs:- api_url: 'https://chatops.myhost.com/hooks/xxxj5xxxhimbbxucbb'- name: warning-example webhook_configs:- url: 'http://pys03.myhost.com/probe/webhook/prometheus' slack_configs:- api_url: 'https://chatops.myhost.com/hooks/xxxj5xxxhimbbxucbb' email_configs:- to: 'admin@myhost.com'- name: critical-example webhook_configs:- url: 'http://pys03.myhost.com/probe/webhook/prometheus' email_configs:- to: 'admin@myhost.com' slack_configs:- api_url: 'https://chatops.myhost.com/hooks/aaywazzopXXX5XXXX'- name: critical slack_configs:- api_url: 'https://chatops.myhost.com/hooks/aaywazzopXXX5XXXX' ~~~

title: Unable to Assign Cluster-Admin Role to IDP User During Cluster Creation Automation Using ocm CLI
issue: When automating identity provider (IDP) creation for a newly created OpenShift Dedicated (OSD) cluster using the ocm CLI, assigning **cluster-admin*
privileges to the user fails if attempted within a single command. The ocm create idp command **does not support*
`group` assignment flags, resulting in errors and preventing automated admin access configuration.
resolution: To successfully assign administrative privileges using the ocm CLI, perform the operation in **two separate steps**: **1. Create the Identity Provider:** ~~~ ocm create idp--type htpasswd--cluster ~~~ **2. Create the User and Assign the Admin Group:** ~~~ ocm create user--cluster=--group=cluster-admins ~~~ This approach ensures the IDP is fully registered before attempting to associate users with administrative groups. **Note: For non-CCS clusters, cluster-admin access is restricted by default. Temporary cluster-admin access must be requested through a Red Hat support case. This solution applies only when the cluster type permits admin access (e.g., CCS clusters).**
root_cause: The `ocm create idp` command does not support assigning groups or roles (such as `cluster-admins`) at creation time. Attempting to pass unsupported flags like `--group` in a single command results in an error (`unknown flag:--group`). As a result, role assignment must be performed as a separate step after the IDP is created.

title: Image pull from OpenShift Mirror registry fails with 504 Gateway Timeout
issue: - Pods in OpenShift are giving imagepullbackoff error- Image pull from mirror registry fails with 504 gateway timeout
resolution: The **Workaround** is to increase the worker count to 2 or 4 as per need and do not perform any mirroring or pushes to mirror registry, when the worker count is more than 1. 1. Edit the /etc/systemd/system/quay-app.service file to contain WORKER_COUNT=4 ~~~-e WORKER_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED_MINIMUM=1 \-e WORKER_COUNT=4 \ > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > change to 4 registry.redhat.io/quay/quay-rhel8:v3.12.10 registry ~~~ 2. Reload the daemon ~~~ $ systemctl daemon-reload $ systemctl restart quay-app.service ~~~ 3. Reset the worker count back to 1 once image pull succeeds. If you require higher concurrency, scalability, and performance, and want to use a centralized mirror registry for multiple OCP clusters, consider deploying a full **Red Hat Quay** instance with **PostgreSQL** as the backend database.
root_cause: - With Mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift 2.0, worker count is explicitly set to 1 as sqlite database is being used.- Refer [KCS- OMR Uses Only One Worker Due to SQLite Database Limitation](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7133214) for more information.

title: AAP on OpenShift deployment fails because PVC storageClass cannot be modified — “spec is immutable after creation”
issue: Automation Hub deployment (or redeployment) on OpenShift fails when attempting to change the storageClass of an already created PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC). The Ansible Operator reports failure while patching the PVC.
resolution: **Scenario 1: Fresh Deployment (No Data to Preserve)** If this is a new deployment and data retention is not required, you can safely delete the existing PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC). The operator will automatically recreate it using the updated StorageClass. Run: ~~~ oc delete pvc-n ~~~ After removing the PVC, re-run the deployment or allow the operator to reconcile and recreate the PVC with the correct StorageClass. **Scenario 2: Production Environment (Data Must Be Preserved)** For production environments, the PVC cannot be modified directly because the StorageClass field is immutable for bound claims. Instead, you must migrate the data to a new PVC configured with the desired StorageClass. For guidance on safely backing up, cloning, and migrating PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) in OpenShift environments, refer to the following Red Hat blog: [How to backup, clone, and migrate Persistent Volume Claims on OpenShift](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/how-to-backup-clone-and-migrate-persistent-volume-claims-on-openshift)
root_cause: As per Openshift Design, it does not allow modifying certain PVC fields after creation, including: storageClass access modes volume binding In this case, the operator attempts to update the existing PVC to a new storageClass, but the PVC is already bound, making the spec immutable.

title: PVC Space Consumption is very high During VM Snapshot Operations in OpenShift Virtualization when Huwai CSI driver is used
issue: - VM snapshot operation results in high PVC space consumption- Is Huwai CSI driver supported in openshift Virualization?- Why PVC consumtion is high even after increasing the storage(PV) for the virtual machines snapshot operations?
resolution: - Huawei’s CSI driver implements snapshots using a copy-on-write (CoW) model with reserved snapshot space configured at the StorageClass (SC) level. If no dedicated reserved snapshot space is configured, the driver borrows from the same pool as the PVC, making it appear as if the PVC itself is consuming space.- During an online snapshot, every new write requires old data to be preserved in snapshot storage (CoW mechanism). Since Huawei CSI reserves snapshot delta space inside the same storage pool, the PVC’s apparent consumption grows to cover these deltas.- This is not an OpenShift Virtualization limitation but a Huawei CSI driver behavior.so Its required to raise a case with Huwawei vendor.
root_cause: - OCP correctly creates VolumeSnapshot + VolumeSnapshotContent, but the backend storage driver decides how data is stored/restored/managed.- Red Hat’s scope is limited to confirming correct CSI orchestration from the OpenShift side. Further analysis and resolution require direct engagement with Huawei support to validate driver-specific snapshot space handling and restore behavior.

title: RHBK 24 container doesn't adjust heap memory based on allocated container memory. It uses fixed -Xmx=512m
issue: RHBK 24 server guide states following: > The Red Hat build of Keycloak container, instead of specifying hardcoded values for the initial and maximum heap size, uses relative values to the total memory of a container. This behavior is achieved by JVM options-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70, and-XX:InitialRAMPercentage=50. > > [Red Hat build of Keycloak Server Guide](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_keycloak/24.0/html/server_guide/containers-#containers-specifying-different-memory-settings) but actually, the JVM is started with following options in RHBK 24 container: ~~~ cat /proc/1/cmdline java-Dkc.config.built=true-XX:MetaspaceSize=96M-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=256m-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8-Dsun.stdout.encoding=UTF-8-Dsun.err.encoding=UTF-8-Dstdout.encoding=UTF-8-Dstderr.encoding=UTF-8-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError-Djava.security.egd=file:/dev/urandom-XX:+UseParallelGC-XX:GCTimeRatio=4-XX:AdaptiveSizePolicyWeight=90-XX:FlightRecorderOptions=stackdepth=512-XX:MinHeapFreeRatio=10-XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio=20-Xms64m-Xmx512m--add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED--add-opens=java.base/java.util.concurrent=ALL-UNNAMED--add-opens=java.base/java.security=ALL-UNNAMED-Dkc.home.dir=/opt/keycloak/bin/..-Djboss.server.config.dir=/opt/keycloak/bin/../conf-Djava.util.logging.manager=org.jboss.logmanager.LogManager-Dpicocli.disable.closures=true-Dquarkus-log-max-startup-records=10000-Djgroups.dns.query=rhbk24-discovery.rhbk24-cp/opt/keycloak/bin/../lib/quarkus-run.jario.quarkus.bootstrap.runner.QuarkusEntryPoint--verbosestart ~~~ This doesn't have `MaxRAMPercentage` option but have `-Xmx512m`. The tracking JIRA ticket: [RHBK-2547](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHBK-2547)
resolution: The issue arises because the RHBK 24 container image does not include the `KC_RUN_IN_CONTAINER` environment variable. Adding environment variable `KC_RUN_IN_CONTAINER="true"` can be a workaround. In OpenShift environment, you can add the environment variable by adding following to your Keycloak custom resource. ``` spec:... unsupported: podTemplate: spec: containers:- env:- name: KC_RUN_IN_CONTAINER value: 'true' ``` As RHBK 26.x is not affected, upgrading to RHBK 26 can be a resolution too.
root_cause: The `MaxRAMPercentage` option was added to `kc.sh` script in RHBK 24 [PR details](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/26661/files#diff-28d941fe33e0f8217892e8096ba7152ba9ade67e3b2c3f0ce31a333d90cc339d). If the `$KC_RUN_IN_CONTAINER` environment variable switch is true, the script is used therefore `MaxRAMPercentage` option is added. Otherwise, `-Xmx512m` option is used regardless.

title: Pod SR-IOV network interface interface shows DOWN or NO-CARRIER after node reboot
issue: After a node reboots, the Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV) Virtual Function (VF) interfaces within a Pod disappear
The top Bonded interfaces of the disappearing VFs display a `NO-CARRIER` state and `DOWN`

Example output from `ip link` inside the Pod: ``` 3: bond1: mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state DOWN group default qlen 1000 link/ether xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff inet 172.15.xx.xx/24 brd 172.15.xx.xx scope global eth1 valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever 4: bond2: mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state DOWN group default qlen 1000 link/ether xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff inet 172.15.xx.xx/24 brd 172.15.xx.xx scope global eth2 valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever ```

Logs from `sriov-network-config-daemon` indicate the failure to locate the interface: ``` 2025-12-01T11:32:38.316709441Z INFO sriov/sriov.go:495 VFIsReady() {"device": "0000:xx:xx.x"} 2025-12-01T11:32:39.317543758Z ERROR wait/wait.go:109 VFIsReady(): invalid index number {"device": "0000:xx:xx.x", "error": "failed to get interface name"} 2025-12-01T11:32:40.317323902Z ERROR wait/wait.go:109 VFIsReady(): invalid index number {"device": "0000:xx:xx.x", "error": "failed to get interface name"} 2025-12-01T11:32:48.317654613Z ERROR sriov/sriov.go:587 configSriovVFDevices(): VF link is not ready {"address": "0000:xx:xx.x", "error": "timed out waiting for the condition"} 2025-12-01T11:32:48.317668303Z INFO sriov/sriov.go:498 RebindVfToDefaultDriver() {"vf": "0000:xx:xx.x"} 2025-12-01T11:32:48.317674953Z LEVEL(-2) kernel/kernel.go:200 Unbind(): unbind device driver for device {"device": "0000:xx:xx.x"} ```
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in OCPBUGS-66342. For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support
root_cause: The issue is caused by a race condition between the OpenShift scheduler and the `sriov-network-config-daemon` `externallyManaged: true` mode during node initialization: 1. When a node reboots successfully, the external entity such as `nmstate` succesfully configures VFs for this node 2. Then the node becomes `Ready`, the scheduler immediately assigns VNF Pods to it. 3. The Pods start successfully with the initially available VFs. 4. Simultaneously, the `sriov-network-config-daemon` begins configuring VFs one by one, which involves unbinding and rebinding the VF drivers. 5. If a VF has already been assigned to a running Pod, the driver rebind process causes that VF to disappear from the Pod's namespace. 6. The VF is not automatically re-added to the Pod; it remains missing until the Pod is deleted and recreated.

title: OIDC Authentication intermittent loss of group membership after login
issue: An OpenShift user intermittently loses group membership after a successful login via OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) CLI. While the OpenID Connect (OIDC) claims in the `oauth-server` logs show the correct group membership, the `oc get groups` command does not list the user in the expected group.
Example login attempt where User_A a member of Group_A: ``` $ oc login https://api.example.com:6443 \-u User_A \-p password \--insecure-skip-tls-verify ```
The user is missing from the group output: ``` $ oc get groups | grep-C1 Group_A Group_B User_B, User_C Group_A User_D, User_E, User_F Group_C User_G, User_H ```

The `oauth-server` logs confirm the OIDC provider is sending the correct group claim: ``` I1208 08:02:10.158503 1 openid.go:195] openid claims: map[string]interface {}{"acr":"1", "at_hash":"...", "aud":"openshift-client", "auth_time":0, "azp":"openshift-client", "email_verified":false, "exp":1.76518123e+09, "groups":[]interface {}{"Group_A", "Group_X"}, "iat":1.76518093e+09, "iss":"https://keycloak.example.com/auth/realms/openshift", "preferred_username":"User_A", "sub":"629608cd-3018-465e-85ba-e9fc99162d95", "typ":"ID"} ```
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in OCPBUGS-63228. For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/new) with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: The issue is caused by a stale cache. When a user is removed from a group, the API updates, but the cache may fail to update. When the user logs in again, the OIDC provider sends the group membership, but because the stale cache believes the user is already in that group, it does not trigger the necessary update to the API.

title: sriov-network-operator-webhook TLS certificates do not automatically reload after secret update
issue: The `sriov-network-operator-webhook` and `resource-inject-webhook` do not reload TLS certificates when the underlying secret is updated.
This issue doesn't happen in officially released Sriov Network Operator but custom or upstream Sriov Network Operator
Logs show that only the `tls.key` file events are captured, while the certificate event is missed.

The following log pattern is observed: ``` 2025-09-23T02:16:21.815555751Z INFO sriov-network-operator-webhook runtime/asm_amd64.s:1693 start server 2025-09-23T02:17:27.526848339Z INFO sriov-network-operator-webhook cobra@v1.8.0/command.go:987 watcher event {"event": "CHMOD "/etc/tls/tls.key""} 2025-09-23T02:17:27.526951762Z INFO sriov-network-operator-webhook cobra@v1.8.0/command.go:987 modified file {"name": "/etc/tls/tls.key"} 2025-09-23T02:17:27.526991595Z INFO sriov-network-operator-webhook cobra@v1.8.0/command.go:987 watcher event {"event": "REMOVE "/etc/tls/tls.key""} 2025-09-23T02:17:27.526999249Z INFO sriov-network-operator-webhook cobra@v1.8.0/command.go:987 modified file {"name": "/etc/tls/tls.key"} ```
resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report `OCPBUGS-62089` and delivered a fix in **OpenShift Container Platform 4.21** and later versions. **Note:** This fix will not be backported to versions 4.18 or 4.20 because the issue is not reproducible using the default configurations deployed by the SR-IOV Network Operator. The problem typically manifests in custom configurations (e.g., specific `ServiceAccount`, `Service`, or `DaemonSet` setups) that differ from the standard operator deployment. **Workaround:** If this issue is encountered in custom `sriov-network-operator-webhook`, manually restart the webhook pods to force them to load the new certificates. ``` $ oc delete pod-n openshift-sriov-network-operator-l app=sriov-network-operator-webhook ```
root_cause: The issue is caused by a race condition between the `kubelet` volume update and the webhook's fsnotify library. This is triggered by specific `SecurityContextConstraints` (SCC) associated with the ServiceAccount. When a `fsGroup` is present in the pod's `securityContext` (often due to the operator-webhook ClusterRole being active), it changes how the `kubelet` updates volumes, preventing the file watcher from correctly detecting and reloading the updated certificate files.

title: model-registry-operator-controller-manager pod - CrashLoopBackOff with OOMKilled (exit code 137)
issue: The `DataScienceCluster` resource indicates that some components are not ready, specifically the `modelregistry`.
The `model-registry-operator-controller-manager` pod fails to start and enters a `CrashLoopBackOff` state.

Checking the pod status returns details similar to the following: ``` model-registry-operator-controller-manager-6746b9f5cf-tz22x 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 2124 (2m9s ago) 5d16h 10.5.xx.xx node.example.com ```
resolution: To resolve this issue, trigger a reconciliation for the deployment to apply the correct memory limits. * Run the following command to add the management annotation to the deployment: ``` $ oc annotate deployment model-registry-operator-controller-manager-n redhat-ods-applications opendatahub.io/managed='true'--overwrite ``` * Wait for the deployment to perform a rollout. * Verify that the new pods are running and no longer failing due to `OOMKilled` errors.
root_cause: The `model-registry-operator-controller-manager` pod is configured with an insufficient memory limit (128Mi) during the upgrade process. This issue is tracked internally as `RHOAIENG-29729`. The operator requires higher memory limits in version 2.23 and later to function correctly.

title: numa-aware-scheduler - High Availability support with multiple replicas
issue: The `numa-aware-scheduler` previously only supported a **single replica**, which created the following limitations:
Inability to guarantee **high availability (HA)*
for the scheduler.
Lack of **fast switching*
or failover capabilities when the node hosting the scheduler instance becomes abnormal or experiences an exception.
resolution: Red Hat reviewed the feature request in `RFE-6552` and delivered a fix in `OpenShift Container Platform 4.20` to support **multiple replicas** for the NUMA-aware scheduler. This allows the scheduler to maintain operations and switch rapidly if a node failure occurs. 1. Upgrade the environment to **OpenShift Container Platform 4.20** or later. 2. Configure the `numa-aware-scheduler` to utilize multiple replicas through the NUMA Resources Operator. 3. For detailed implementation steps, refer to the official documentation on [Managing HA NROP NUMA-aware](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/scalability_and_performance/cnf-numa-aware-scheduling#cnf-managing-ha-nrop_numa-aware). **Important:** Managing high availability for this component is currently a **Technology Preview** feature. Technology Preview features are not supported with Red Hat production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete. Red Hat does not recommend using them in production environments. These features provide early access to upcoming product functionality, enabling testing and feedback during the development process.

title: Residual overlapping IP reservations prevent IP allocation after node power cycles
issue: When using Whereabouts IPAM with overlapping ranges enabled, several issues occur regarding IP address reclamation and allocation:
After a node is powered down or restarted, `overlappingrangeipreservations` resources remain in the cluster, which prevents those IP addresses from being reallocated to new pods.

Attempts to reclaim leaked overlapping addresses fail with rate limiter timeout errors in the whereabouts logs: ``` 2024-05-19Txx:xx:xx+08:00 [error] failed to remove cluster wide IP-192.186.xx.101: client rate limiter Wait returned an error: rate: Wait(n=1) would exceed context deadline ```

Pod deployment fails with a networking configuration error indicating the storage engine cannot allocate an IP within the specified range: ``` ERRORED: error configuring pod [/] networking: [/ /:]: error adding container to network " ": error at storage engine: Could not allocate IP in range: ip: 10.225.xx.173 /- 10.225.xx.174 / range: 10.225.xx.0/24 / excludeRanges: [] ```
resolution: **Disclaimer:** *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* If the environment does not strictly require overlapping IP ranges, disable this feature to prevent the creation and retention of `OverlappingRangeIPReservation` objects. 1. Identify the affected `NetworkAttachmentDefinition`. 2. Edit the `spec.config` to set `enable_overlapping_ranges` to `false` within the `ipam` configuration block. 3. Refer to the [Whereabouts documentation](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/whereabouts?tab=readme-ov-file#overlapping-ranges) for further configuration details. Example configuration: ``` spec: config: '{"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "name": "whereaboutsnetwork", "type": "macvlan", "master": "ens7", "mode": "bridge", "ipam": {"type": "whereabouts", "range": "10.225.xx.0/24", "enable_overlapping_ranges": false}}' ```
root_cause: The whereabouts reconciliation logic hits a client-side rate limiter when attempting to delete a high volume of leaked IP reservations, causing the process to exceed the context deadline. Furthermore, node power events can lead to orphaned overlappingrangeipreservations objects that are not automatically cleaned up, resulting in IP exhaustion within the defined range.

title: How to redirect the cache directory for oc-mirror v2
issue: How can the default cache directory (typically located in `$HOME/.cache`) used by `oc-mirror` v2 be redirected to a specific custom directory?
Is the specified cache directory automatically deleted after the image synchronization is complete?
resolution: To redirect the cache directory used by `oc-mirror` v2 to a specific location, use the `--cache-dir` command-line argument. 1. Execute the `oc-mirror` command with the `--cache-dir` flag followed by the desired path: ~~~bash $ oc-mirror v2--cache-dir /path/to/custom/directory... ~~~ 2. **Cleanup:** The cache directory specified by `--cache-dir` is **not** automatically deleted after the synchronization process completes. If the cache data is no longer required, it must be removed manually.

title: Error "Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON" when installing SR-IOV Network Operator via Web Console
issue: The installation of the SR-IOV Network Operator fails with a JSON syntax error popup when attempting to deploy it using the OpenShift Web Console.
resolution: To resolve this issue, install the SR-IOV Network Operator using the Command Line Interface (CLI) instead of the Web Console. 1. Create a YAML file (e.g., `sriov-install.yaml`) with the following `Namespace`, `OperatorGroup`, and `Subscription` definitions: ~~~yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-sriov-network-operator annotations: workload.openshift.io/allowed: management--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: sriov-network-operators namespace: openshift-sriov-network-operator spec: targetNamespaces:- openshift-sriov-network-operator--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: sriov-network-operator-subscription namespace: openshift-sriov-network-operator spec: channel: stable name: sriov-network-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ~~~ 2. Apply the configuration using the `oc` command: ~~~bash $ oc apply-f sriov-install.yaml ~~~ 3. Verify the installation is successful: ~~~bash $ oc get csv-n openshift-sriov-network-operator NAME DISPLAY VERSION PHASE sriov-network-operator.v4.20.0-202510211040 SR-IOV Network Operator 4.20.0-202510211040 Succeeded $ oc get pod-n openshift-sriov-network-operator ~~~
root_cause: A software defect causes the OpenShift Web Console to fail when parsing the JSON properties associated with specific versions of the SR-IOV Network Operator during installation. ## Diagnostic Steps 1. Attempt to install the SR-IOV Network Operator via the OpenShift Web Console. 2. Observe the following error message displayed in a popup: ~~~text Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 285 (line 13 column 5) ~~~

title: Non-English Windows VM does not have VirtIO Ethernet Adapter after migration
issue: After Windows VM MTV migration the VirtIO Ethernet Adapter is not available and the following error is shown in Device Manager: ~~~ The class configuration for this device is still being set up by Windows. (Code 56) ~~~ This only occurs on non-English (i.e.: German) Windows Client version; updating the driver completes successfully but the device remains in a Code 56 state and adapter is not visible.
resolution: * This issue is related to Windows 'PCI Label Id' and affects only Client Windows versions (10,11) as Server versions have a fix (Windows Server 2016 KB5046612, Windows Server 2019 KB5046615, Windows Server 2022 KB5046616). * For RHEL KVM and OpenShift Virtualization, Red Hat is currently backporting fixes to both RHEL 9.4.z and RHEL 9.6.z that can help to workaround this Guest problem when unpatched. This is currently being tracked in [Private RHEL-133299](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-133299) and fix is expected to be available in one of the next releases.
root_cause: On non-English Windows systems, locale-specific behavior can interfere with the configuration of the VirtIO network driver after migration

title: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3 dashboard link returns "Application is not available"
issue: When clicking the Red Hat OpenShift AI link, the browser displays an "Application is not available" error.
resolution: * On baremetal clusters, the Gateway API requires an external load balancer to function correctly. 1. Install a LoadBalancer controller, such as **MetalLB**, to manage and fulfill `LoadBalancer` type service requests. 2. Identify the external IP address assigned to the `data-science-gateway` service. 3. Update the DNS resolution for the Red Hat OpenShift AI URL to point to the assigned LoadBalancer IP address. * If you don't want to install metallLB, another workaround is to create a passthrough `route` and patch the `LoadBalancer` service to make dashboard URL accessible to the `Gateway` Pod. For further details, refer to the Red Hat [Knowledgebase article](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7133770).
root_cause: **Red Hat OpenShift AI 3** utilizes the **Gateway API** for ingress rather than the traditional HAProxy-based ingress controllers used in previous versions. The gateway creates a service of type `LoadBalancer`. In baremetal environments, this service remains in a `Pending` state because there is no default provider to assign an external IP address. Consequently, the gateway remains unprogrammed and the application link fails to resolve.

title: Getting error Unchecked throwable in manageConnectionReconnected() in kie-server log file
issue: - When we submit the task in process instance for our workflow in business central we are getting the `Unchecked throwable in manageConnectionReconnected()` error the kie-server logs;- Using external MySQL XA data source with RHPAM 7.13.5, getting `java.sql.SQLSyntaxErrorException: (conn=4700414) XAER_INVAL: Invalid arguments (or unsupported command)` error.
resolution: Use ` false ` for the RHPAM XA datasouce, To configure this in the RHPAM on OCP follow below steps. 1. Create a actions.cli file with following contents. Change the DATASOURCE-NAME with the MySQL datasource. ``` embed-server--std-out=echo--server-config=standalone-openshift.xml /subsystem=datasources/xa-data-source=:write-attribute(name=same-rm-override,value=false) quit ``` 2. Create a postconfigure.sh to launch run the CLI script via jboss-cli ``` #!/bin/bash # This script is run automatically via the 'postconfigure_extensions' function defined in /opt/eap/bin/launch/configure_extensions.sh # This must be run after environment variables are used to inject content into the standalone-openshift.xml $JBOSS_HOME/bin/jboss-cli.sh--file=/opt/eap/extensions/actions.cli ``` 3. Create a config map using both of this file in the namespace where this can be accessed by the kie-server deployment. ``` oc create configmap eap-scripts--from-file actions.cli=actions.cli--from-file postconfigure.sh=postconfigure.sh ``` 4. Attach this to files as Volume mount at '/opt/eap/extensions' in server configuration of kieconfigs-7.13.5 configmap. the mount configuration will look as follows. ``` volumeMounts:- name: eap-scripts mountPath: "/opt/eap/extensions"... volumes:- name: eap-scripts configMap: name: eap-scripts defaultMode: 0777 items:- key: "actions.cli" value: "actions.cli"- key: "postconfigure.sh" value: "postconfigure.sh" ```
root_cause: - There were changes related to Transaction Handling in EJBTimerScheduler class ([JBPM-10209](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JBPM-10209)) Those changes rely on the usage of CMT and REQUIRES_NEW- There possibility is that the driver is now reporting the two connections as the “same RM,” which leads Narayana to attempt a JOIN-style XA start. MySQL does not support XA START... JOIN, and that can result in XAER_INVAL. The behavior may have changed due to the SSL connection properties.- To resolve this the follow workaround of using ` false ` as it prevents JOIN from being used.

title: How to configure tolerations on collector DaemonSet for Logging 6 in RHOCP 4
issue: - `Logging 6.3` [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.3/html/scheduling_resources/scheduling-logging-resources#cluster-logging-collector-tolerations_scheduling-logging-resources) for configuring `tolerations` to control log collector pod placement references the deprecated `ClusterLogging(CL)` resource.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Documentation Bug [`OSDOCS-17734`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSDOCS-17734). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. ###Workaround:- `Tolerations` can be added to the `collector` DaemonSet by editing the `ClusterLogForwarder(CLF)` resource. 1. Edit the `ClusterLogForwarder(CLF)` and add `tolerations` under `spec.collector.tolerations`: ~~~ $ oc edit clf-n openshift-logging apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterLogForwarder metadata: creationTimestamp: "2025-12-30T13:11:52Z" generation: 1 name: collector namespace: openshift-logging resourceVersion: "63588" uid: 5660f720-624a-4110-9093-a4520665a4ee spec: collector: tolerations:- effect: NoExecute key: collector operator: Exists tolerationSeconds: 6000 managementState: Managed ~~~ 2. Verify that the `tolerations` are applied: ~~~ $ oc get clf-o yaml-n openshift-logging $ oc get ds-o yaml-n openshift-logging ~~~
root_cause: - The Logging [`6.3`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.3/html/scheduling_resources/scheduling-logging-resources#cluster-logging-collector-tolerations_scheduling-logging-resources) and [`6.4`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/scheduling_resources/scheduling-logging-resources#cluster-logging-collector-tolerations_scheduling-logging-resources) documentation references the `ClusterLogging(CL)` resource, which has been deprecated.- `ClusterLogForwarder(CLF)` is now the supported method for configuring `tolerations` on `collector` DaemonSet.

title: Authorino pod does not have istio-proxy container cause HTTP 403 error while accessing the model external route
issue: - Authorino pod does not have `istio-proxy` container **cause*
`HTTP 403 error` while accessing the model external route.

title: Which OpenShift versions have which container runtime as default?
issue: Which OpenShift versions have which container runtime as default?
resolution: * OpenShift Container Platform clusters installed with versions up until 4.17 have RunC as the default container runtime. * For newer OpenShift Container Platform 4.18 and later installations, the default container runtime has changed to Crun. * It is important to note that OpenShift clusters installed before version 4.18 have not automatically changed their default container runtime as part of an upgrade to 4.18 or later. This is assuming you have not already overwritten the default runtime in the `ContainerRuntimeConfig` CR. See the relevant documentation: [Red Hat Documentation- 1.3.17.1. crun is now the default container runtime](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/release_notes/ocp-4-18-release-notes#ocp-release-notes-nodes-crun-default_release-notes)

title: How to run 3scale must-gather in a disconnected environment
issue: How to run 3scale must-gather in a disconnected environment?

Followed [Fetching 3scale project logs in must-gather in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6115421) but got this error. In addition, the gathered files did not contain 3scale project information. Error running must-gather collection: gather did not start for pod must-gather-98dns: unable to pull image: ImagePullBackOff: Back-off pulling image "quay.io/3scale/must-gather" Falling back to `oc adm inspect clusteroperators.v1.config.openshift.io` to collect basic cluster information.
resolution: ### Prerequisites Mirror 3scale's must-gather image to a local registry. For overall instructions on mirroring, refer to [Disconnected installation mirroring](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html-single/disconnected_environments/index#installing-mirroring-disconnected-about). 1. Add `- name: quay.io/3scale/must-gather` under `additioanImages` in `ImageSetConfiguration` CR. Refer to [Creating the image set configuration](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/disconnected_environments/mirroring-in-disconnected-environments#oc-mirror-building-image-set-config-v2_about-installing-oc-mirror-v2) about `ImageSetConfiguration`. additionalImages:- name: quay.io/3scale/must-gather 2. Mirror images as described in [Mirroring an image set to a mirror registry](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/disconnected_environments/mirroring-in-disconnected-environments#mirroring-image-set) ### Execution Once the above images are mirrored, the must-gather can be run using the following command: ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--image=$LOCAL_REGISTRY/3scale/must-gather ~~~ When running the above command, replace the image in the `--image` parameter with the mirrored must-gather image.

title: How to adjust gitops-plugin and cluster resource limits

resolution: - This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [RFE](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-7787). For more information, please open a new support case with Red Hat Support.- As per recent release of OpenShift GitOps operator v 1.19 it is possible to configure resource requests and limits for the cluster and GitOps plugin components through the GitOpsService.

title: StorageCluster CR is not creating after installing RHODF v4.20 in disconnected environment
issue: - After `RHODF` installation, `StorageCluster` CR is not configuring due to below error, ~~~ constraints not satisfiable: bundle odf-dependencies.v4.20.2-rhodf requires an operator with package: odf-external-snapshotter-operator and with version in range: 4.20.2-rhodf, subscription odf-dependencies exists, subscription odf-dependencies requires cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20/openshift-marketplace/stable-4.20/odf-dependencies.v4.20.2-rhodf ~~~
resolution: Add `odf-external-snapshotter-operator` package in `ImageSetConfiguration` CR and then mirror the operator bundle. ~~~ $ oc edit imagesetconfiguration-oyaml kind: ImageSetConfiguration apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v2alpha1 mirror: platform: channels:- name: stable-4.20 minVersion: 4.20.5 maxVersion: 4.20.5 graph: true operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.20 packages:- name: odf-external-snapshotter-operator <---- Add this package in existing operator bundle ~~~
root_cause: - Starting with `RHODF v4.20`, `odf-external-snapshotter-operator` package is added in the `operator bundle` which is required for RHODF installation and configuration.- To know more about what all `packages` are needed for RHODF installation and deployment, do check out the [`documentation`](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.20/html-single/planning_your_deployment/index#disconnected-environment_rhodf).

title: Service Mesh Operator upgrade fails with "error finding unpacked bundle configmap" due to missing bundle images or stale InstallPlans
issue: An Operator upgrade (e.g., Service Mesh 2.4.5 to 2.6) fails or hangs.
Encountering an error while upgrading servicemesh operator
Receiving the following error message: ~~~ error finding unpacked bundle configmap for ref {ConfigMap 6edf1b23d485319501c69ce6f10f68a52ff545bf6a621b4bb6b79d7d8d9cd6a} ~~~
Error message: `configmap "6edf1b23d485319501c69ce6f10f68a52ff545bf6a621b4bb6b79d7d8d9cd6a" not found`
An Operator upgrade (e.g., Service Mesh 2.4.5 to 2.6) fails or hangs.
The `InstallPlan` status reports **Failed*
or contains the following error message in the status block: ```log error finding unpacked bundle configmap for ref {ConfigMap...}: configmap " " not found ```
You may observe multiple `InstallPlans` for the same operator, some of which are unapproved.
Deleting the `InstallPlan` does not immediately resolve the issue, or the new `InstallPlan` fails with the same error.
resolution: This error occurs when OLM tries to read the Operator bundle metadata but cannot locate the `ConfigMap` that should contain it. This is typically caused by one of two scenarios: 1. **Missing Images:** The bundle unpacking job failed because the image is missing from the private registry. 2. **Stale InstallPlans:** The ConfigMap was garbage-collected while the InstallPlan was pending approval. Follow these steps to diagnose and resolve the issue. ##### 1. Check for Failed Bundle Unpack Jobs (Most Likely in Disconnected Clusters) OLM spins up a temporary Job to "unpack" the operator bundle image into a ConfigMap. If this job fails, the ConfigMap is never created. 1. Check for pods in the `openshift-marketplace` namespace (or the operator's namespace) that are failing to start: ```bash oc get pods-n openshift-marketplace | grep-v Running ``` 2. Look for pods with status `ImagePullBackOff` or `ErrImagePull`. 3. Describe the failing pod to identify the image it is trying to pull: ```bash oc describe pod-n openshift-marketplace ``` 4. **Fix:** If the image is missing, you must mirror the required operator bundle image to your private registry using `skopeo` or the `oc adm catalog mirror` command. ```bash skopeo copy docker://registry.redhat.io/ docker:// / ``` ##### 2. Clean Up Stale OLM Resources If the images are present, or after you have mirrored the missing images, you must reset the OLM state to force a retry. 1. **Delete failed or unapproved InstallPlans:** Identify the InstallPlans for the affected operator and delete them. OLM will regenerate them automatically. ```bash oc get ip-n oc delete ip-n ``` 2. **Restart the CatalogSource Pods:** Restarting the CatalogSource forces OLM to refresh the registry catalog and generate a new, valid InstallPlan. ~~~ # Identify the catalog source pods oc get pods-n openshift-marketplace-l olm.catalogSource=redhat-operators # Delete the pods to restart them oc delete pods-n openshift-marketplace-l olm.catalogSource=redhat-operators ~~~ *Note: If you are using a custom catalog source (e.g., for Service Mesh), target that specific pod.* 3. **Approve the New InstallPlan:** Once the CatalogSource pod is running, a new `InstallPlan` should appear. ```bash oc get ip-n ``` If it is set to Manual approval, approve it to proceed with the upgrade.
root_cause: * **Scenario A: Missing Image:** In disconnected environments, if the operator bundle image referenced by the index is not present in the internal registry, the OLM "unpack" job fails with an Image Pull error. Consequently, the ConfigMap containing the bundle data is never created, leading the InstallPlan to report "configmap not found." * **Scenario B: Stale Plan:** Unpacked bundle ConfigMaps are temporary. If an `InstallPlan` sits in a `Manual` approval state for too long, the system may garbage collect the referenced ConfigMap. When the administrator finally attempts to approve or view the plan, the reference is invalid.

title: How to mirror only a specific version of an operator using oc-mirror plugin
issue: - How to mirror only a specific version of an operator from a channel.- How to mirror only few operator versions from a channel.- How to mirror only latest version of an operator from default channel.- How to mirror latest version of an operator from all the available channel.- How to mirror an operator till a particular version from a channel.- How to mirror an operator from a specific version to latest version from a channel.
resolution: - How to mirror only a specific version of an operator from a channel. ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL::8443/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 packages:- name: quay-operator channels:- name: stable-3.9 minVersion: 3.9.0 maxVersion: 3.9.0 ~~~- How to mirror only few operator versions from a channel (below `ImageSetConfiguration` will help to mirror all the intermediate version including `minVersion` and `maxVersion`). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL::8443/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 packages:- name: quay-operator channels:- name: stable-3.9 minVersion: 3.9.1 maxVersion: 3.9.4 ~~~- How to mirror only latest version of an operator from default channel (Find out the default channel using any of the method described in the "Diagnostic Steps" and mention only default channel name). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL::8443/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 packages:- name: quay-operator channels:- name: stable-x ~~~- How to mirror latest version of an operator from all the available channel (if no channel specified latest version from all the channels will be mirrored). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL::8443/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 packages:- name: quay-operator ~~~- How to mirror an operator till a particular version from a channel (if `maxVersion` set alone, then all the available versions till the `maxVersion` will be mirrored). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL::8443/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 packages:- name: quay-operator channels:- name: stable-3.9 maxVersion: 3.9.4 ~~~- How to mirror an operator from a specific version to latest version from a channel (if `minVersion` set alone, then all the available versions from the `minVersion` to latest version will be mirrored). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL::8443/mirror/oc-mirror-metadata skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.12 packages:- name: quay-operator channels:- name: stable-3.9 minVersion: 3.9.1 ~~~
root_cause: The tool `oc-mirror` provides a feature to fetch the images via the `ImageSetConfiguration` that provides a list of operators to be mirrored from the index container image (called catalog above). The user can use `minVersion` and `maxVersion` to prune/customize the packages manifests that come from the catalog (container image) available for the mirroring process.

title: MachineConfigPool is degraded with "parsing Ignition config spec v3 failed with error: config is not valid.. duplicate entry defined" error
issue: - One or more MachineConfigPools (MCP) are in a `DEGRADED` state.- Cluster upgrades cannot proceed.- The cluster cannot apply patches or updates while the MCP is degraded.- New configuration changes are not applying to nodes.- Rendering controller is stuck processing the invalid configuration.- The MCP status displays a `RenderDegraded` error indicating a duplicate entry definition in the Ignition config.- The `machine-config-controller` logs or the status of the `MachineConfigPool` resource show an error similar to the following: ``` Failed to render configuration for pool worker: could not generate rendered MachineConfig: parsing Ignition config spec v3 failed with error: config is not valid Report: error at $.storage.files.3, line 1 col 842: duplicate entry defined ```
resolution: Identify the MachineConfig containing the duplicate file definition, edit or recreate it to remove the duplication, and allow the Machine Config Operator to re-render the configuration. 1. **Identify the problematic MachineConfig** List all MachineConfigs and sort by age to find recently applied configurations that likely triggered the issue: ```bash oc get mc--sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp ``` 2. **Inspect the MachineConfig** Check the YAML of the suspect MachineConfig (e.g., `75-rhcos4-moderate-worker-chrony-service`) to confirm duplicate entries. Look for multiple entries in `spec.config.storage.files` pointing to the same `path`. Example of an invalid config: ```yaml spec: config: storage: files:- path: /etc/chrony.conf <-- First definition contents:...- path: /etc/chrony.conf <-- Duplicate definition causing the error contents:... ``` 3. **Correct the MachineConfig** Delete MachineConfig object and recreate them, or edit them if they are not generated. * **Edit the MachineConfig (if editable)** ```bash oc edit mc ``` 4. Remove the duplicate section from the `storage.files` list so that `/etc/chrony.conf` (or the affected file) is defined only once. Save and exit. **If editing is not possible**, update the source yaml to remove the duplicate and re-apply, or delete the bad object: ```bash oc delete mc ``` 5. **Verify MCP Recovery** Once the duplicate entry is removed, the Machine Config Operator will attempt to re-render the MachineConfigPool. Monitor the status of the pools: ```bash oc get mcp ``` The `DEGRADED` state should switch to `False`, and `UPDATING` may switch to `True` as the new valid configuration is rolled out.
root_cause: The issue is caused by a MachineConfig object that violates the Ignition spec v3 validation rules. Ignition spec v3 does not allow defining the same file path multiple times within a single source unit. A specific `MachineConfig` object applied to the cluster contains invalid data structure within the spec.config.storage.files section. There are duplicate entries defined for the same file path (e.g., `/etc/chrony.conf` is defined twice within the same YAML object). Defining the same file path (e.g., `/etc/chrony.conf`) multiple times within the same Ignition configuration is not allowed. When the Machine Config Controller attempts to render (merge/combine) this invalid configuration and all fragments into a final ignition file, `rendered-worker- ` MachineConfig, the internal validator fails, causing the rendering process to abort and marking the pool as `RenderDegraded`.
