title: Configuring EgressFirewall for API connectivity in Hosted Control Plane clusters
issue: - In standard OpenShift Container Platform 4 clusters, the EgressFirewall can be configured as described below; however, this approach cannot be used in Hosted Control Plane (HCP) environments because the control plane runs as pods. ~~~ spec: egress:- ports:- port: 6443 protocol: TCP to: nodeSelector: matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/master: '' ~~~
resolution: - In a standalone OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) 4 cluster, the endpoints for the `kubernetes` Service in the `default` namespace always point to the control plane (master) node IP addresses.- However, in a Hosted Control Plane (HCP) cluster, the endpoint for the same service consistently points to `172.20.0.1` by design.- This IP address is assigned to the `lo` (loopback) interface on all HCP nodes.- An `EgressFirewall` can be configured to explicitly allow egress traffic to `172.20.0.1` in order to enable connectivity to the Kubernetes API service. ~~~ apiVersion: k8s.ovn.org/v1 kind: EgressFirewall metadata: name: default namespace: spec: egress:- to: cidrSelector: 172.20.0.1/32 type: Allow- to: cidrSelector: 0.0.0.0/0 type: Deny ~~~
root_cause: - In a Hosted Control Plane (HCP) cluster, the endpoint for `kubernetes` Service in the `default` namespace always points to the `172.20.0.1` IP address by design.- For communication with the control plane, hosted control planes uses a local proxy in every compute node that listens on IP address 172.20.0.1 and forwards traffic to the API server as per the documentation [Compute nodes that need to access the API server](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/hosted_control_planes/networking-for-hosted-control-planes#hcp-proxy-api_hcp-networking).

title: Unable to create domain mapping for serverless application
issue: - Unable to create domain mapping for serverless application.- Unable to consume third party certificate which was created as a secret in the application namespace.
resolution: - To manually label a custom TLS secret with a placeholder UID for use in a Knative DomainMapping, add the label `networking.internal.knative.dev/certificate-uid` with any unique string value. ~~~ $ oc label secret secrent-name networking.internal.knative.dev/certificate-uid="xxx-tls-secret"-n app-namespace ~~~
root_cause: - The secret has to be labelled manually for use in a Knative DomainMapping if the custom certificates are consumed from the secret.

title: The RHOCP must-gather fails with Unauthorized error when accessTokenInactivityTimeout is exceeded
issue: - The `oc adm must-gather` fails with `Unauthorized` error when accessTokenInactivityTimeout is exceeded.
resolution: This is a known limitation in the current `must-gather` client implementation. A Request for Enhancement (RFE) has been filed to implement a "keep-alive" mechanism or token refresh logic to ensure the session remains valid during long-running diagnostic operations. Review the following RFE for status and details:- [RFE-8595](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-8595) **- The must-gather should maintain session activity to prevent accessTokenInactivityTimeout failures** ### Workaround To collect `must-gather` data without failure, the `accessTokenInactivityTimeout` must be temporarily increased to a value longer than the expected must-gather runtime. 1. Edit the OAuth configuration: ~~~ $ oc edit oauth cluster ~~~ 2. Adjust the `accessTokenInactivityTimeout` field (e.g., increase from `300s` to `1800s` or temporarily remove it). 3. Run `$ oc adm must-gather`. 4. Revert the changes to the OAuth configuration to restore compliance settings.
root_cause: The `oc adm must-gather` lacks a mechanism to keep the session alive during long operations.

title: OVS configuration failed to start after reboot in RHOCP4

Sep 08 12:45:34 ocp4.example.com configure-ovs.sh[9472]: ++ handle_exit ~~~

It is being tracked in the following bugs: RHOCP Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 4.19 | [OCPBUGS-41489](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-41489) | **4.19.0** | [RHSA-2024:11038](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:11038) 4.18 | [OCPBUGS-48341](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-48341) | **4.18.3** | [RHBA-2025:2229](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:2229) 4.17 | [OCPBUGS-52257](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-52257) | **-** |- 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-52310](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-52310) | **4.16.38** | [RHSA-2025:3301](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:3301) ### Workaround {#workaround} Delete the `ovs-if-br-ex` interface and restart the `ovs-configuration.service`: ~~~ $ ssh core@node-name $ sudo nmcli connection delete ovs-if-br-ex $ sudo systemctl restart ovs-configuration.service ~~~

title: Windows VM IP Address and Guest Agent Status Missing After Migration of VM from RHV to OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - After migrating a Windows VM to OpenShift Virtualization from RHV, the Web Console displays "Guest agent is required" and the IP address is missing.
resolution: - Remove the oVirt Guest Agent- Install the [qemu-guest Agent](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html-single/virtualization/index#installing-qemu-guest-agent-on-windows-vm_virt-installing-qemu-guest-agent)- Verify service is running ~~~ net start | findstr "QEMU" ~~~
root_cause: - The VM is using the legacy oVirt Guest Agent from the source environment (RHV). Modern OpenShift Virtualization requires the QEMU Guest Agent to report networking and status details. The old agent is not compatible with the new platform. Note: Ideally, the guest agent should have been updated in the source RHV environment prior to migration. As of RHV 4.3, the ovirt-guest-agent is deprecated in favor of the qemu-guest-agent. For more details, see [RHV Deprecated Features](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_virtualization/4.3/html/release_notes/deprecated_features_rhv).

title: Can a repository name in Red Hat Quay contain slashes ("/") ?
issue: - When using repository names with '/' inside (i.e. "example/mydebian"), operations like pull and push work seamlessly, while mail notification are not sent.- Can a repository name in Red Hat Quay contain slashes ("/")?
resolution: - Red Hat has acknowledged the [issue](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-7538) and is planning to release the fix in- Red Hat Quay 3.15.3- Red Hat Quay 3.16.x- Related [PR](https://github.com/quay/quay/pull/3778) has been merged and the fix will be available in the versions stated above.
root_cause: The issue arises from the [repository_tag_reference](https://github.com/quay/quay/blob/3c8ed17b171b9923f35e9b9b8ff30dd00baa1f95/util/jinjautil.py#L49) function, where_repository_path.split("/")_ is expecting exactly two parts (namespace and repository), but it fails when the_repository_path contains_ more than two segments due to slashes.

title: RHOCP 4 core components related pods are running on worker nodes
issue: - Core component `pods` such as `kube-apiserver` or `kube-scheduler`, are running on `nodes` labeled as `worker nodes` in `RHOCP 4`.- `Static pod` manifests are found residing in the `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` directory on `nodes` where they are not intended to run.- `oc get pods-o wide` shows `control plane` components assigned to `worker node IP` addresses.
resolution: To resolve this issue, the `static pod` manifest must be removed from the affected `worker node` to stop the `kubelet` from managing the unwanted services. 1. Access the affected `worker node` using `debug`. ~~~ $ oc debug node/ # chroot /host ~~~ 2. Move the identified `static pod` manifest to a backup location outside of the `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` directory. ~~~ $ sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ /tmp/.backup ~~~ **Note:** Moving the file out of this directory causes the `kubelet` to immediately terminate the associated `pod`. 3. Confirm the termination of the `pod` from a terminal with cluster-admin access. ~~~ $ oc get po-n-o wide NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE openshift-kube-scheduler-master01 3/3 Running 0 27d openshift-kube-scheduler-master02 3/3 Running 0 27d openshift-kube-scheduler-master03 3/3 Running 0 27d ~~~ Ensure the `pod` corresponding to the affected `worker node` is no longer listed.
root_cause: There are two primary scenarios that lead to this behavior: 1. **Node Repurposing:** An existing `master node` was repurposed or re-added to the cluster as a `worker node` without performing a clean re-installation of the Operating System or wiping the `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` directory. Residual configuration files from its previous role as a `control-plane node` remain active. 2. **Manual Intervention:** A `static pod` manifest was manually or accidentally copied into the `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` directory of a worker node. The kubelet on the worker node is designed to run any valid manifest found in that specific directory.

title: Provisioning a new baremetal node in a hosted cluster gets stuck in Joined stage
issue: We are trying to build a new Hosted Cluster but one of the nodes will not join the nodepool.
resolution: This issue is under investigation and being tracked in Bug [OCPBUGS-68355](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-68355). For more information, please open a new support case with Red Hat Support.
root_cause: From the [upstream bug report](https://github.com/openshift/assisted-service/pull/8622) we can read: ~~~ During Day-2 worker node installation, hosts get stuck in `Joined` stage and timing out after 60 minutes, even though the node was healthy and ready in the cluster. The `tryApproveDay2CSRs` function used either/or logic for CSR approval:- If node is nil: try client CSR approval only- If node exists: try serving CSR approval only This created a race condition on fast-booting hardware. When a node appeared in the cluster before the controller could approve the client CSR, the function permanently switched to serving-only mode. The client CSR was never processed, and areCSRsHandled() returned false forever because it requires both client and serving CSRs to be tracked. ~~~

title: Not able to query logs older than some hours and the logs are not deleted from the object storage in RHOCP 4
issue: - Logs not visible for more than few hours in the Observe > Logs in `OCP` console irrespective of the configured retention for `Loki`- Logs are not visible as per retention period set for `Loki` `Object Storage`.- `Loki` is able to write the logs to `Object Storage` bucket but not able to query them.- How to define endpoint in the secret for `Loki` `Object Storage` bucket?- Loki logs are not purged, but it's set Loki retention in the configuration- `Loki Compactor` does not delete the objects from the object storage and it throws the error: ~~~ 2024-08-21T04:51:00.635778080Z level=error ts=2024-08-21T04:51:00.544702159Z caller=cached_client.go:189 msg="failed to build table names cache" err="NoSuchKey: The specified key does not exist.\n\tstatus code: 404, request id:, host id: " ~~~
resolution: 1. Verify that the account used for accessing to the object storage has the needed permissions. Read the Red Hat Knowledge Article ["What object storage is supported and the permissions needed for Loki in RHOCP 4?"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7075815) 2. Modify the `Loki` `Object Storage` secret's for the `endpoint` not contain the bucket name as a suffix. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: loki-object-secret namespace: openshift-logging stringData:...... bucketnames: lokibucketname endpoint: ~~~ For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).
root_cause: The `Loki Object Storage` secret's endpoint should not contain the bucket name as a suffix. When the `bucketname` is added to the `endpoint`, Loki is able to write to the object storage, but the queries will fail and if the Loki Compactor is not able to list the `keys`, it won't be able to delete the objects from the Object Storage.

title: Resolving Orphaned CSV and Subscription Resolution Failures for AMQ Broker Operator on OpenShift
issue: - Resolving Orphaned CSV and Subscription Resolution Failures for AMQ Broker Operator on Open Shift- AMQ Broker Operator Subscription Fails with `ConstraintsNotSatisfiable` After ROSA Minor Upgrade- AMQ Broker Operator Subscription in ResolutionFailed State After Open Shift Minor Version Upgrade- we upgraded the ROSA stage cluster from `4.17.40` to `4.18.30`, and we noticed on all amq namespace that they're all don't have any subscription and upon checking the yaml, there's an error like this ``` constraints not satisfiable: @existing/amq-dev//amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1-0.1747217191.p, redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.0-opr-1, redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.3-opr-1-0.1741884937.p, redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1-0.1747217191.p and redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.5-opr-1-0.1764078330.p provide ActiveMQArtemis (broker.amq.io/v2alpha5), clusterserviceversion amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1-0.1747217191.p exists and is not referenced by a subscription, subscription amq-broker-rhel8 exists, subscription amq-broker-rhel8 requires at least one of redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.5-opr-1-0.1764078330.p, redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1-0.1747217191.p, redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.3-opr-1-0.1741884937.p or redhat-operators/openshift-marketplace/7.12.x/amq-broker-operator.v7.12.0-opr-1 ```
resolution: - `ResolutionFailed: ConstraintsNotSatisfiable` OLM is explicitly stating that `amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1` already exists but is not referenced by any Subscription. This is the exact failure mode described in the OLM troubleshooting guide.- currentCSV: amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1-0.1747217191.p The Subscription is attempting to resolve to a packaged bundle (.p) from the catalog, while a non-packaged CSV with the same operator version already exists in the namespace.- when a CSV exists without being owned by a Subscription, OLM will not be able to satisfy constraints and the Subscription will remain in ResolutionFailed.- Leave the Subscription exactly as is (no `startingCSV`).- Delete the orphaned CSV only: ``` oc delete csv amq-broker-operator.v7.12.4-opr-1-n ```- Allow OLM to resolve a new InstallPlan.- Manually approve the InstallPlan if required.- Verify if One CSV exists `subscription.status.installedCSV` matches that CSV and CSV phase is `Succeeded`
root_cause: - After the ROSA minor upgrade, Operator Lifecycle Manager enforced stricter dependency resolution and detected an existing AMQ Broker operator CSV that was not associated with its Subscription.- This orphaned CSV caused OLM to fail constraint resolution (ConstraintsNotSatisfiable), preventing the Subscription from reconciling until the CSV was removed.

title: 100% of the alertmanager-metrics/alertmanager-metrics targets in Namespace NS open-cluster-management-observability namespace have been unreachable for more than 15 minutes.
issue: - Alert received for open-cluster-management-observability `100% of the alertmanager-metrics/alertmanager-metrics targets in Namespace NS open-cluster-management-observability namespace have been unreachable for more than 15 minutes.`
resolution: ####Solution 1:####- Delete the configmap in the namespace open-cluster-management-observability. It should automatically be re-created afterwards. ~~~ $ oc get configmap alertmanager-clientca-metric-n open-cluster-management-observability-o yaml > alertmanager-clientca-metric-bkp.yaml $ oc delete configmap alertmanager-clientca-metric-n open-cluster-management-observability ~~~- Restart the alertmanager pods in the open-cluster-management-observability namespace: ~~~ $ oc delete pod-l app=multicluster-observability-alertmanager-n open-cluster-management-observability ~~~ ####Solution 2:####- Edit the servicemonitor and add the line `bearerTokenFile: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token` as below: ~~~ $ oc-n open-cluster-management-observability edit servicemonitor alertmanager apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: ServiceMonitor metadata: name: alertmanager namespace: open-cluster-management-observability spec: endpoints:- bearerTokenFile: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token <--- add this line interval: 30s port: metrics scheme: https tlsConfig: caFile: /etc/prometheus/configmaps/serving-certs-ca-bundle/service-ca.crt certFile: /etc/prometheus/secrets/metrics-client-certs/tls.crt keyFile: /etc/prometheus/secrets/metrics-client-certs/tls.key serverName: alertmanager-metrics.open-cluster-management-observability.svc selector: matchLabels: app: multicluster-observability-alertmanager-metrics ~~~
root_cause: - This is a known issue tracked in Jira [ACM-20743](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-20743), and currently, the Red Hat engineering team is working on it.- The certificate information in this resource `oc get configmap alertmanager-clientca-metric-n open-cluster-management-observability` is outdated after a cert rotation. It should match the content from `oc get configmap extension-apiserver-authentication-n kube-system`.

title: Quay pods crashloop due to Could not connect to storage error when ODF/NooBaa backend is full
issue: Quay pods fail to start and enter a `CrashLoopBackOff` state with the following error in logs: ~~~ DistributedStorage | Could not connect to storage local_us. Error: Get "https://s3.openshift-storage.svc.cluster.local/quay-datastore- /?location=": context deadline exceeded ~~~
resolution: 1. Free up space in the ODF cluster to bring pool usage below nearfull_ratio (85%) threshold:- Delete unused data or buckets from NooBaa S3.- Remove stale or orphaned image layers from Quay.- Clean up temporary test repositories if safe to remove. 2. Temporarily increase available storage space by:- Adding or expanding OSD disks.- Temporarily increasing the object storage capacity until permanent expansion. 3. Restart affected Quay pods once sufficient space is available. The pods should recreate and connect to storage successfully.
root_cause: - The Quay application failed to establish a connection to its object storage (NooBaa S3) because the ODF storage backend reached its full or nearfull state.

title: HTTP OPTIONS Method Reported as Vulnerability on Quay HTTPS Endpoint (False Positive)
issue: - The scanner flagged that the HTTP OPTIONS method is enabled on port 8443, reporting it as a security risk.
resolution: - No configuration changes are required.- The reported vulnerability is a false positive from the vulnerability scanner.- The OPTIONS method should not be disabled in Quay.- The 400 error when accessing via HTTP is expected behavior and confirms HTTPS enforcement.- Red Hat does not recommend modifying Quay’s internal NGINX configuration to disable OPTIONS, as this would impact functionality.- A related internal issue is already tracked here: [PROJQUAY-8200](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-8200 "PROJQUAY-8200")
root_cause: - The HTTP OPTIONS response is generated by Quay’s embedded NGINX layer and is part of normal API behavior.- The OPTIONS method:- Does not expose sensitive data- Only returns supported HTTP methods for a given endpoint- Is required for browser-based API interactions and CORS preflight checks- Disabling the OPTIONS method would break normal Quay functionality, including:- Web UI behavior- Browser-based API calls- Registry operations

title: Serving models with custom vllm-cpu runtime in OpenShift AI
issue: - I need to test my LLMs using CPU in my OpenShift AI environment- Is it possible to serve my Model in OpenShift AI using CPU only?- Is there vLLM CPU ServingRuntime for KServe available in RHOAI to deploy small model using CPU only?
resolution: **NOTE:** **This procedure involves a custom-built vLLM runtime** [**and it goes beyond the support coverage**](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7127194) **1. Create the custom runtime:**- In the RHOAI Dashboard, navigate in the left panel to Settings > Runtimes. Then,- Click "Add serving runtime" button.- In the editor, create a custom `ServingRuntime` referencing a valid vllm-cpu image built for this custom runtime. Here is an example for the custom vLLM `v.0.11.2` built image (the recommendation here is to build your own image and push it to your preferred repository): ~~~ apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: ServingRuntime metadata: annotations: opendatahub.io/recommended-accelerators: "" opendatahub.io/runtime-version: v0.11.2 openshift.io/display-name: vLLM custom CPU ServingRuntime for KServe opendatahub.io/apiProtocol: REST labels: opendatahub.io/dashboard: "true" name: vllm-cpu-custom-runtime spec: annotations: prometheus.io/path: /metrics prometheus.io/port: "8080" containers:- args:---port=8080---model=/mnt/models---served-model-name={{.Name}} command:- python--m- vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server env:- name: HF_HOME value: /tmp/hf_home- name: VLLM_CACHE_ROOT value: /tmp/cache image: quay.io/abarbosa/vllm-cpu:0.11.2 ## Here must be set the custom image path name: kserve-container ports:- containerPort: 8080 protocol: TCP multiModel: false supportedModelFormats:- autoSelect: true name: vLLM ~~~- Click the "Create" button. **2. Create a DataScience project and deploy the model.**- Create the DataScience project in the OpenShift AI Dashboard- Create the connection with the `URI` path where the LLM is located. For example: ~~~ oci://quay.io/rh-aiservices-bu/tinyllama:1.0 ~~~- Serve the model select `vLLM custom CPU ServingRuntime for KServe` as `Serving Runtime` and `Accelerator=None`._**The serving process will take some minutes while pulling the images.**_ **3. Test the served model.** ~~~ curl-X POST " /v1/chat/completions"-H "Content-Type: application/json"--data '{"model": "tinyllama", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}'--insecure ~~~ Expected output: ~~~ {"id":"chatcmpl-97f3dc8a37345948","object":"chat.completion","created":1764685941,"model":"tinyllama","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"The capital of France is Paris.",...} ~~~
root_cause: vLLM CPU runtime for x86_64/aarch64 is not provided for OpenShift AI. With CPU runtime, users will notice the model takes longer to load and could respond more slowly compared to GPU runtimes.

title: NVIDIA GPU driver 580.105.08 compatibility issue with RHOAI 2.25.0 and 3.0
issue: - CUDA 13.0 Driver Compatibility Issues When Deploying Models with vLLM NVIDIA GPU ServingRuntime for KServe- Error observed: ~~~ (EngineCore_DP0 pid=96) RuntimeError: Unexpected error from cudaGetDeviceCount(). Did you run some cuda functions before calling NumCudaDevices() that might have already set an error? Error 803: system has unsupported display driver / cuda driver combination ~~~
resolution: - The Red Hat OpenShift AI `2.25.0` is based on `vLLM v0.10.1.1` that was built with `CUDA 12.8`. Hence it is **not** compatible with CUDA 13.- Also, The Red Hat OpenShift AI `3.0` is based on `vLLM v0.11.0` that was built with `CUDA 12.8`. Hence it is **not** compatible with CUDA 13. Refer to [Red Hat OpenShift AI: Supported Configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/rhoai-supported-configs). However, you can apply below **workaround** to avoid this issue:- Disable the automatic upgrade of the NVIDIA GPU Operator.- **WebUI:** Disable the automatic upgrade of the NVIDIA GPU Operator. Path to NVIDIA GPU Operator. ~~~ Openshift Dashboard-> Operators-> Installed Operators-> NVIDIA GPU Operator-> Subscription-> Update approval-> Select "Manual"-> Save ~~~- **CLI:** To disable automatic Operator upgrades in OpenShift by updating the "Update approval". ~~~ # oc edit subscription-n ~~~ Locate the `spec.installPlanApproval` field and change its value from `Automatic` to `Manual`.- Downgrade the GPU driver version via the NVIDIA GPU Operator for the compatibility issue. Update/Create ClusterPolicy.CR: ~~~ You should expand the Driver section in ClusterPolicy and configure the following fields: version: 570.195.03 (or another supported version) image: driver (or another supported image) repository: nvcr.io/nvidia (or another supported repository) Example:.. driver: repository: nvcr.io/nvidia version: 580.95.05 image: driver ~~~ ## Workaround for RHOAI Create a custom ServingRuntime referencing [**RHAIIS 3.2.5 image or upper**](https://catalog.redhat.com/en/software/containers/rhaiis/vllm-cuda-rhel9/6825c6b827e18fe3162148a9). Here is an example: ~~~ apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: ServingRuntime metadata: annotations: opendatahub.io/recommended-accelerators: '["nvidia.com/gpu"]' opendatahub.io/runtime-version: v0.11.2 openshift.io/display-name: vLLM NVIDIA GPU custom RHAIIS ServingRuntime for KServe opendatahub.io/apiProtocol: REST labels: opendatahub.io/dashboard: "true" name: vllm-cuda-runtime-custom-rhaiis spec: annotations: opendatahub.io/kserve-runtime: vllm prometheus.io/path: /metrics prometheus.io/port: "8080" containers:- args:---port=8080---model=/mnt/models---served-model-name={{.Name}} command:- python--m- vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server env:- name: HF_HOME value: /tmp/hf_home image: registry.redhat.io/rhaiis/vllm-cuda-rhel9@sha256:094db84a1da5e8a575d0c9eade114fa30f4a2061064a338e3e032f3578f8082a ## Here must be set the custom image path name: kserve-container ports:- containerPort: 8080 protocol: TCP multiModel: false supportedModelFormats:- autoSelect: true name: vLLM ~~~ The full procedure to set the custom runtime is the same as the one described for [Serving models with custom vllm-cpu runtime in OpenShift AI](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7134585), but referencing a valid RHAIIS image in the YAML configuration, as the above-described. **NOTE:** **This procedure involves a custom-built vLLM runtime** [**and it goes beyond the support coverage**](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7127194)
root_cause: * Driver compatibility issue when using the RHAIIS image version 3.2.2 and above with NVIDIA GPU driver version 580.105.08 and CUDA 12.x during model deployment. * This issue arises from a conflict between the host and the container-provided binary, leading to a compatibility mismatch that prevents successful model deployment. * Specifically, the problem is caused by the cuda-compat package, which provides a CUDA binary that is preferred over the host driver library. * In the vLLM container, the `cuda-compat` package via dynamic linker run time bindings is adding `libcuda.so.1` link to file `/usr/local/cuda/compat/libcuda.so.1` causing the error: ~~~ # ldconfig-p | grep libcuda.so.1 libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/local/cuda/compat/libcuda.so.1 libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /lib64/libcuda.so.1 ~~~ * This occurs due to forward compatibility behavior (i.e., a newer CUDA runtime with an older driver), causing the container’s compat library to be loaded instead of the host driver.

title: Configlistener not coming up after DG Operator upgrade

title: Labeling OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) nodes as infra nodes
issue: How to separate application and storage workloads and avoid double use of OCP and ODF subscriptions for nodes that are used exclusively for storage services.
resolution: * Label the ODF nodes to add the infra label and annotate the odf namespace with a default node selector: ~~~ oc label nodes node-role.kubernetes.io/infra='' oc label nodes node-role.kubernetes.io=infra oc annotate namespace openshift-storage openshift.io/node-selector= ~~~ Delete the CSI pods in `Pending` state so new pods will get scheduled: ~~~ oc delete pod-l app=csi-cephfsplugin-n openshift-storage oc delete pod-l app=csi-rbdplugin-n openshift-storage ~~~ Please note that some of the CSI plugin pods will continue running on worker nodes. The CSI plugin pods need to run on every node where storage needs to be provisioned. Other pods like `rook-ceph-tools` may also run on worker nodes.- To have dedicated storage nodes, where other pods are prevented from being scheduled on the same infra nodes, add a taint: ~~~ oc adm taint nodes-l node-role.kubernetes.io/infra node.ocs.openshift.io/storage=true:NoSchedule ~~~- If multiple unique nodes are labeled as part of `infra` (storage, worker, router, etc.), all these nodes should belong to a single Machine Config Pool (MCP) named `infra`, else this error may appear during updates: ~~~ can't get pool for node "infra-node-1": node infra-node-1 belongs to 2 custom roles, cannot proceed with this Node ~~~- For more information on configuring infrastructure nodes, refer to the solutions article [Infrastructure Nodes in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5034771).- Note that, infrastructure nodes for ODF and OCP can be shared if the nodes have enough compute resources. However, only infrastructure related pods are allowed to be run on infrastructure nodes.

title: How to resize a worker node in ARO
issue: - How can I adjust the Azure VM sizes for worker nodes in an ARO cluster?- Can I modify the disk sizes for ARO worker nodes?
resolution: **NOTE**: For ARO, **only** the worker nodes(machinesets) can be resized/modified, not control plane nodes. The steps are documented on OpenShift documentation:- [Creating a compute machine set on Azure](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/machine_management/creating_machinesets/creating-machineset-azure.html).- [Modifying a compute machine set on Azure](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html/machine_management/modifying-machineset) Example on how to change VM and disk sizes for worker nodes: 1. List the cluster nodes: ``` $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE mci-aro-dzfqp-master-0 Running Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 1 156m mci-aro-dzfqp-master-1 Running Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 2 156m mci-aro-dzfqp-master-2 Running Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 3 156m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-ssxmp Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 1 63m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2-llkmt Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 2 151m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3-vxvcd Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 3 151m ``` The current worker nodes are of type `Standard_D4s_v3`, which we will change to `Standard_D8s_v3` in this exercise. 2. List the machineSets: ``` $ oc get machineset-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1 1 1 1 1 160m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2 1 1 1 1 160m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3 1 1 1 1 160m ``` You need to modify each machineset, since each machineset is located in an availability zone. 3. Modify the machineSet: ~~~ $ oc edit machineset/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-n openshift-machine-api ~~~ ~~~ osDisk: diskSettings: {} diskSizeGB: 128 vmSize: Standard_D4s_v3 ~~~ The original disk size of `128` will be increased to `256`, and the vmSize parameter will be changed from `Standard_D4s_v3` to `Standard_D8s_v3`. After changing the machinset configuration, you will receive the following message: ~~~ machineset.machine.openshift.io/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1 edited ~~~ The next step is to cordon each node, remembering that this procedure must be done for each one. ~~~ $ oc adm cordon mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-ssxmp ~~~ Checking the nodes: ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-ssxmp Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 80m v1.26.14+03ee898 mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2-llkmt Ready worker 165m v1.26.14+03ee898 mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3-vxvcd Ready worker 165m v1.26.14+03ee898 ~~~ The next step is to drain the node. ~~~ $ oc adm drain mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-ssxmp--delete-emptydir-data--ignore-daemonsets ~~~ ~~~ node/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-ssxmp already cordoned ~~~ ~~~ Warning: ignoring DaemonSet-managed Pods: openshift-azure-logging/mdsd-xfmf9, openshift-cluster-csi-drivers/azure-disk-csi-driver-node-wtzbt, openshift-cluster-csi-drivers/azure-file-csi-driver-node-xpzkc, openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator/tuned-6f9xd, openshift-dns/dns-default-svfz5, openshift-dns/node-resolver-n69bv, openshift-image-registry/node-ca-46t5k, openshift-ingress-canary/ingress-canary-hwphv, openshift-machine-config-operator/machine-config-daemon-p86vt, openshift-monitoring/node-exporter-zr2vs, openshift-multus/multus-additional-cni-plugins-bzpb4, openshift-multus/multus-vwxvr, openshift-multus/network-metrics-daemon-chkzc, openshift-network-diagnostics/network-check-target-h6z8v, openshift-ovn-kubernetes/ovnkube-node-fstbb node/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-ssxmp drained ~~~ Once the node has been drained, you can proceed to scale down the replicas of the machineset to 0 so that the changes are applied to the machineset. ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=0 machineset mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-n openshift-machine-api machineset.machine.openshift.io/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1 scaled ~~~ Validating the machineset: ~~~ $ oc get machineset-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1 0 0 4h36m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2 1 1 1 1 4h36m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3 1 1 1 1 4h36m ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2-llkmt Ready worker 4h24m v1.26.14+03ee898 mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3-vxvcd Ready worker 4h24m v1.26.14+03ee898 ~~~ You can see that there are only 2 worker nodes in the `Ready` state. 4. Scale up the machineset ~~~ $ oc scale--replicas=1 machineset mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-n openshift-machine-api machineset.machine.openshift.io/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1 scaled ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get machineset-n openshift-machine-api NAME DESIRED CURRENT READY AVAILABLE AGE mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1 1 1 4h39m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2 1 1 1 1 4h39m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3 1 1 1 1 4h39m ~~~ The new node has been provisioned with the updated type: `Standard_D8s_v3` ~~~ $ oc get machines-n openshift-machine-api NAME PHASE TYPE REGION ZONE AGE mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-cj47z Provisioned Standard_D8s_v3 eastus 1 33s < < <=== mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2-llkmt Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 2 4h34m mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3-vxvcd Running Standard_D4s_v3 eastus 3 4h34m ~~~ 5. Validating the new node Finally, the new node has been provisioned and is in a `Ready` state. ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-cj47z Ready worker 115s v1.26.14+03ee898 mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus2-llkmt Ready worker 4h32m v1.26.14+03ee898 mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus3-vxvcd Ready worker 4h32m v1.26.14+03ee898 ~~~ To verify that the node was provisioned with the specified disk size in the machineset, you can debug the node and check the disk size using the command. `df-h`. ~~~ $ oc debug node/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-cj47z ~~~ ~~~ $ oc debug node/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-cj47z Temporary namespace openshift-debug-h85rb is created for debugging node... Starting pod/mci-aro-dzfqp-worker-eastus1-cj47z-debug-jf8f5... To use host binaries, run `chroot /host` Pod IP: 10.0.2.6 If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter. sh-4.4# ~~~ ~~~ sh-4.4# $ chroot /host sh-5.1# $ df-h Filesystem Size Used Avail Use% Mounted on /dev/sdb4 256G 9.9G 246G 4% / < <=== Disk with new Size tmpfs 4.0M 0 4.0M 0% /sys/fs/cgroup devtmpfs 4.0M 0 4.0M 0% /dev tmpfs 16G 0 16G 0% /dev/shm tmpfs 6.3G 60M 6.3G 1% /run ~~~

title: systemd-network-generator: Failed to parse kernel command line: Invalid argument
issue: - `systemd-network-generator` service fails during boot with below error: ~~~ May 15 18:28:11 testnode systemd-network-generator[1236]: Failed to parse kernel command line: Invalid argument ~~~
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this issue and is currently working on it. The `systemd-network-generator` service failure should not cause any impact. ### Workaround: Remove the network parameters from kernel command line which will allow the service to run. ~~~ # rpm-ostree kargs--delete="ip=enp68s0:dhcp,dhcp6" # systemctl reboot ~~~
root_cause: `systemd-network-generator` lacks support for `ip=NIC:dhcp,dhcp6`, this is being worked actively upstream. Below are the upstream issues for the same: [systemd-network-generator support for ip=NIC:dhcp,dhcp6](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/27944) [network-generator: split out udev pieces from systemd-network-generator](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/27945)

title: Several components fail with "tls: failed to parse certificate from server: x509: negative serial number" error in RHOCP4
issue: - OpenShift update fails with `Unable to retrieve available updates: Get "https://api.openshift.com/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph?arch=amd64&channel=stable-4.20&version=4.20.3": tls: failed to parse certificate from server: x509: negative serial number` error.- A custom certificate is not accepted with error `tls: failed to parse certificate from server: x509: negative serial number`.- How to trust a certificate with negative serial number?
resolution: Either:- Substitute custom proxy certificate with a valid one (i.e. with a non-negative serial number).- Put `.openshift.com` (plus all other addresses affected by this issue) in `noProxy` configuration of [cluster-wide proxy](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/configuring_network_settings/enable-cluster-wide-proxy). This solution may not work if proxy is the only way to reach internet. ### With Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security If this issue is related to RHACS, please follow this dedicated solution: [ACS central pod reports error: "x509: negative serial number" in RHOCP4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7115185). ### With oc-mirror plugin If this issue is related to oc-mirror plugin, please follow this dedicated solution: [oc-mirror plugin fails with " tls: failed to parse certificate from server: x509: negative serial number" in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7128537).
root_cause: The issue is caused by custom certificates with negative serial number. [RFC5280](https://access.redhat.com/bounce/?externalURL=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.rfc-editor.org%2Frfc%2Frfc5280%23section-4.1.2.2) requires serialNumber to be a non-negative integer. The reason why this wasn't an issue in previous OCP versions is that OCP components was based on Go version 1.22 or earlier, but from Go 1.23 certificates with negative serial number are no longer tolerated. Issue [OCPBUGS-71197](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-71197) has been opened to further investigate the issue and possible workarounds.

title: Live storage migration fails if VM has "tpm enabled: false" in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - Live storage migration hangs in the "Running" state and fails to create a VMIM object.- The VM status reports a RestartRequired condition with the message: a non-live-updatable field was changed in the template spec.- The VM is configured with tpm: {enabled: false}.
resolution: To unblock the migration, apply the following workaround to revert the configuration drift and clear the restart condition. 1. Patch the VM specification to explicitly set "TPM" to disabled again: ~~~ # oc patch vm--type=merge-p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"domain":{"devices":{"tpm":{"enabled":false}}}}}}}' ~~~ 2. Identify the index of the RestartRequired condition in the VM status. ~~~ # oc get vm-o yaml |yq '.status.conditions' ~~~ 3. Remove the RestartRequired condition from the status using the index identified in the previous step. ~~~ # oc patch vm--subresource status--type=json-p '[{"op": "remove", "path": "/status/conditions/4"}]' ~~~ Once the condition is removed and the spec is corrected, the storage migration should proceed automatically.
root_cause: - During the storage class migration process, if the VM was configured with `tpm: {enabled: false}`, the update process incorrectly resets this field to an empty value (`tpm: {}`). This change is detected by the virt-controller as a modification to a non-live-updatable field, which triggers the `RestartRequired` condition on the VM. Because the VM is marked as requiring a restart, the controller refuses to initiate the live migration (VMIM), causing the process to hang.- The bug is tracked in [CNV-75813](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-75813).

title: Machine config controller reporting node is not in a pool in RHOCP 4
issue: `Machine config controller` reporting: ~~~ all nodes must be in a pool if managed by the MCO. Node worker.example.com is not in a pool ~~~
resolution: For fixing the issue, two different approaches can be followed. #### Approach 1: Change the `node-role.kubernetes.io` value from the node Assign a `node-role.kubernetes.io` value that matches one of the available Machine Config Pool (MCP). For instance, for assigning the node to the `worker` MCP: ~~~ $ oc label node/ node-role.kubernetes.io/worker= ~~~ #### Approach 2: create a MCP where the `.spec.nodeSelector` matches the `node-role.kubernetes.io` from the node that has not assigned a MCP Read the Red Hat Knowledge Article "[Managing Custom Machine Config Pool in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5688941)" for creating the MCP.
root_cause: The node is not assigned to any Machine Config Pool (MCP) as the `node-role.kubernetes.io` label in the node is not matching any of the values in `.spec.nodeSelector` from the Machine Config Pool (MCP).

title: Can Service Mesh logs be migrated between ARO clusters?
issue: - Is it possible to access service mesh logs from a decommissioned ARO cluster?- Supportability of migrating service mesh logs to a new ARO cluster.
resolution: Service Mesh logs **cannot be migrated automatically** to a new ARO cluster. Service Mesh logs can be viewed in a new cluster only if one of the following conditions was met prior to cluster replacement:- Logs were forwarded to an external logging system (for example, external Elasticsearch, Splunk, Azure Monitor, or externally hosted Loki).- The logging backend data (such as Elasticsearch indices or Loki object storage) was backed up and restored. Without external log storage or backups, historical Service Mesh logs from the previous cluster are not recoverable.
root_cause: Service Mesh components (Envoy sidecars and Istio control plane) write logs to standard output. These logs are collected and stored by the OpenShift Logging stack running within the cluster. Deletion or replacement of the cluster results in the permanent loss of logs unless external log retention mechanisms are configured.

title: OpenShift 4 Ingress Operator is Degraded with Reason IngressDegraded or IngressUnavailable
issue: - The `ingress` Operator is Degraded with Reason `IngressControllersDegraded`.- Ingress Cluster Operator degraded with the following message: ~~~ $ oc get co ingress NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE ingress 4.19.14 False True True 18m The "default" ingress controller reports Available=False: IngressControllerUnavailable: One or more status conditions indicate unavailable: DeploymentAvailable=False (DeploymentUnavailable: The deployment has Available status condition set to False (reason: MinimumReplicasUnavailable) with message: Deployment does not have minimum availability.) ~~~
resolution: 1. Add additional compute nodes. 2. If no compute nodes exist, it is also possible to edit the scheduler to allow control plane nodes to run ingress. See below URL for details [Configuring control plane nodes as schedulable](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/nodes/working-with-nodes#nodes-nodes-working-master-schedulable_nodes-nodes-managing)
root_cause: The router pods require two schedulable nodes, typically `compute` nodes. The message indicates there are not enough nodes available for the router deployment (2 router pods) to be deployed on unique compute nodes.

title: The collector pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff in RHACS 4.8.4 in RHOCP4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes

title: Vector pods are consuming very high memory.
issue: - `Vector` pods are consuming very high memory causing pressure on nodes.
resolution: - Set limit in `Cluster Logging instance` for `collector` where type is `Vector`. ~~~ spec: collection: type: vector resources: requests: cpu: 50m memory: 250Mi limits: cpu: 1 memory: 1Gi ~~~- Even after adding the above if the issue persists, then please open a [support ticket with Red Hat](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).

title: Support for Software RAID Configuration during Assisted Installer and Agent-based Installer Workflows
issue: Is Software RAID configuration supported when installing OpenShift Container Platform using the Assisted Installer or Agent-based Installer?
resolution: Yes, and no. [Software RAID is supported during installation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/installation_configuration/installing-customizing#installation-special-config-raid_installing-customizing) for external storage via the Assisted Installer and Agent-based Installer Although official documentation for Software RAID often highlights the use of the `openshift-install` binary (typically associated with IPI and UPI), both the Assisted Installer and Agent-based Installer allow users to provide custom manifests. To implement Software RAID in these environments, you must include a custom `MachineConfig` manifest that defines the RAID arrays and file systems during the installation process.- **For Assisted Installer:** Upload the `MachineConfig` YAML file in the "Custom manifests" step of the wizard.- **For Agent-based Installer:** Include the `MachineConfig` YAML file within the `manifests` directory before generating the ISO image. **NOTE: OpenShift Container Platform does NOT support software RAIDs on the installation drive.** The documentation distinguishes between generic Software RAID (which you configure yourself for data) and Boot Mirroring (which the installer manages). Unsupported: You cannot use mdadm or the installation config to create custom RAID levels (like RAID 0, 5, 6, or 10) for the operating system drive. You also cannot install OpenShift onto a drive that you have manually pre-formatted with mdadm. This is what the [warning note in our documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/installation_configuration/installing-customizing#installation-special-config-raid_installing-customizing) refers to. Supported: OpenShift does support RAID 1 Mirroring for the boot drive, but only if configured through the specific boot_device mirroring parameters in the installation configuration (Butane/Ignition).
root_cause: The standard installation documentation mentions downloading the installation program on an installation node, which implies a focus on IPI or UPI workflows. However, the underlying mechanism for Software RAID is handled by Ignition via `MachineConfig`, which is a feature supported across all RHCOS-based installation methods, including AI and ABI.

title: ppc64le system using GPFS panics due to a reference to a freed or corrupted ovl_inode
issue: On a node using GPFS storage, running an `lsof` command may cause the system to panic: ``` sh-5.1# chroot /host sh-5.1# lsof | grep inotify | wc-l The terminal connection has closed. Danger alert: The debug pod failed. The container could not be located when the pod was terminated ```
resolution: Please partner with the vendor of GPFS to review the situation and check if there may be an available update to address a similar known issue.
root_cause: The panic occurs when the `lsof` command tries to dereference an invalid value that should have been valid kernel space address for a `dentry` structure. The invalid address comes from the `__upperdentry` pointer of an `ovl_inode` structure that was previously freed, so this type of issue is a use-after-free. The inode associated with the `ovl_inode` is related to a gpfs super block that no longer shows up in the mount list. The IBM Storage Scale Container Native (CNSA) development team confirmed that there was an issue with CNSA leading to kernel panics that had been fixed in their latest images.

title: Why link flapping is observed for Intel ice E810-C NICs ?

title: Getting Unauthorized: Authentication Required When Trying to Push Into External Exposed Image Registry
issue: ~~~ [root@localhost ~]# docker login-u example-p somepassword registry.apps.example.com Login Succeeded [root@localhost ~]# [root@localhost ~]# docker push registry.apps.example.com/openshift/test 22j4zia2lk2nm: Pushing [==================================================>] 8.192 kB... a23gfzs1c363a: Waiting unauthorized: authentication required ~~~- Pushing into exposed registry in a separate cluster fails
resolution: - Ensure that the route is set to Passthrough, not Edge or Reencrypt termination. Passthrough is currently the only type of route supported for exposing the secure registry.- You might need to add the cert to the registry-certs secret

title: Node Tuning Cluster Operator is in Degraded state in OpenShift Hosted control planes (HCP)
issue: - Tuned pods failing with `CreateContainerError` are causing the Node Tuning Cluster Operator to stuck in Degraded state. ~~~ NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE node-tuning 4.16.45 False True True 16d ~~~
resolution: Delete the TuneD DaemonSet so that the Operator recreates it. If it is up to date (running version 4.16.45), the recreated DaemonSet will no longer have reference to `/var/lib/tuned/bin/run`: ~~~ $ oc delete ds tuned-n openshift-cluster-node-tuning-operator ~~~
root_cause: - The file `/var/lib/tuned/bin/run` was not included in any official 4.16.z release; it was removed during the 4.16 development cycle before 4.16.0.- This indicates that the referenced DaemonSet is incorrect or outdated.

title: Unable to Access ARO Console and Applications After Proxy Change
issue: Could not access the ARO Management Console or applications. Timeouts occurred when accessing any ARO-hosted service. CLI access remained functional Cause: Proxy was changed from IP → hostname, but the hostname could not be resolved. Nodes could not apply the invalid proxy setting, causing external connectivity failures.
resolution: 1. Let the currently rebooting node complete its reboot. 2. Reverted proxy configuration back to the working IP address. 3. Rebooted all remaining Infra and Worker nodes to apply the corrected proxy settings. Outcome: Access to the ARO Console and applications restored after nodes applied the corrected proxy settings.
root_cause: The cluster became inaccessible because the proxy was changed to an unresolvable hostname, causing nodes to lose external connectivity after reboot and preventing the ARO Console and applications from loading.

title: Limiting WildcardPolicy Usage to Specific Namespaces
issue: Customer wants to enable wildcardPolicy: Subdomain on a custom IngressController but restrict its use to only certain namespaces. Cause Wildcard behavior on an IngressController is cluster-wide. OpenShift has no native feature to allow wildcard routes only in selected namespaces. To enforce this requirement, a custom policy must be added externally.
resolution: - The Admission Webhook framework (validating/mutating) is fully supported on OCP/OSD.- Custom webhook logic created by the customer is not supported by Red Hat, but it is allowed.- A custom Validating Admission Webhook can be used to check all new or updated Routes and allow wildcardPolicy: Subdomain only in approved namespaces. Recommendation:- Implement a custom validating webhook to enforce namespace restrictions.- Test webhook behavior before applying it cluster-wide.
root_cause: Wildcard configuration is applied cluster-wide in OpenShift, so it cannot be restricted to specific namespaces without implementing a custom admission webhook.

title: pam_systemd(crond:session): Failed to create session: Maximum number of sessions (8192) reached, refusing further sessions.
issue: - Received below error in `/var/log/secure` ~~~ May 21 03:15:01 testdomain.com crond[241599]: pam_systemd(crond:session): Failed to create session: Maximum number of sessions (8192) reached, refusing further sessions. ~~~
resolution: In usual case, having `SessionsMax=8192` in `/etc/systemd/logind.conf` is sufficient, hitting the limit mostly indicates you are hitting a bug. Update *systemd* to at least version `systemd-239-82.el8_10.8` as per errata [RHBA-2025:19556](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:19556). ### Workaround in case *systemd* cannot be updated (not recommended at all) Restart *systemd-logind* periodically, e.g. when encountering 100 or more dead sessions not being automatically deleted. The following script, running as a *cron*, may be used to perform this task: ~~~ #!/bin/bash # # Script detecting user sessions still registered by systemd-logind but that do not exist anymore # KCS https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7016011 # # Author: Renaud Métrich # Maintainer: Flos Qi Guo cg_version=1 numberofleaks=0 while [["$#"-gt 0]]; do case $1 in--cg) cg_version="$2"; shift;; *) echo "Unknown parameter: $1"; exit 1;; esac shift done echo "## Checking for session leaks using Cgroup v$cg_version logic..." for f in $(ls-1 /run/systemd/sessions | grep-v ".ref"); do echo "## Checking session $f.." file=/run/systemd/sessions/$f [-e "$file.ref"] && echo " * Still in use" && continue uid=$(grep-oP "UID=\K(.*)" "$file") scope=$(grep-oP "SCOPE=\K(.*)" "$file") if ["$cg_version"-eq "1"]; then cg_path="/sys/fs/cgroup/systemd/user.slice/user-$uid.slice/$scope" elif ["$cg_version"-eq "2"]; then cg_path="/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-$uid.slice/$scope" else echo "Error: Unsupported cgroup version: $cg_version" exit 1 fi if [-d "$cg_path"]; then if [-f "$cg_path/cgroup.procs"]; then strings "$cg_path/cgroup.procs" fi continue fi numberofleaks=$((numberofleaks + 1)) done if ["$numberofleaks"-ne 0]; then echo "## Detection complete: $numberofleaks leak(s) found." else echo "## Detection complete: No leaks found." exit 0 fi if ["$numberofleaks"-ge 100]; then echo "## Restarting systemd-logind because more than 100 sessions are leaking" systemctl restart systemd-logind fi exit 1 ~~~
root_cause: Up to *systemd-239-78* excluded, a [Upstream fix](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/25483/commits/3022916b4d2483452c3ddbbac9ee7c4372b1cb46) was missing. With recent *systemd*, there was still an issue, caused by *systemd* sometimes disconnecting from the bus, which causes *systemd* to lose track that *systemd-logind* is interested in receiving notifications about session closure. This issue was tracked by Private JIRA [RHEL-75081- systemd doesn't notify logind of session removal, causing a session leak on logind side](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-75081) and is now resolved with [RHBA-2025:19556](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:19556).

title: Failed to migrate VM from VMware to OpenShift Virtualization with error: "filesystem was mounted read-only".
issue: During migration of a virtual machine from VMWare to OpenShift Virtualization, the virt-v2v conversion process fails with the following error message: ~~~ virt-v2v: error: filesystem was mounted read-only, even though we asked for it to be mounted read-write. This usually means that the filesystem was not cleanly unmounted. Possible causes include trying to convert a guest which is running, or using Windows Hibernation or Fast Restart. ~~~
resolution: * Ensure the source Windows VM is properly shut down with Fast Startup disabled and that the filesystem is in a clean state. * Disable Windows Fast Startup: * On the source Windows VM, open Control Panel-> Hardware and Sound-> Power Options-> Choose what the power buttons do. * Under Shutdown settings, uncheck the box for Turn on fast startup (recommended). * Click Save changes. * Verify Filesystem Health * Log in to the source Windows VM and perform a check of the NTFS filesystem, often by running chkdsk from an elevated Command Prompt or relying on Windows' internal error checking mechanisms upon a standard reboot. * Perform a full, clean shutdown of the source virtual machine from within the guest OS. * If Fast Startup was already disabled or if the issue persists: * Keep the VM running at source side and do the migration again after archiving and deleting the old migration plans. (allow MTV to shutdown the VM).
root_cause: Fast Startup leaves the system in a state similar to hibernation, writing system files to the disk and locking the filesystem, which is why the migration tools interpret it as being "not cleanly unmounted."

title: Logs with detectMultilineException option enabled not properly parsed in RHOCP 4
issue: Logs are being printed with a multiline format for certain services.
Each line in the log is treated as a separate line in Loki and it causes difficulties in searching and identifying logs.
When log forwarder sends multiline exception, log is forwarded in multiple single lines
Remap support for the reduce transform (multi-line logs)
Certain Java stack traces appear split line-by-line in Loki instead of a single aggregated event.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of a request for being able to create custom remap in the collector for being able to parse application multi-line logs as a single log line, currently under review in RFE [OBSDA-762](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-762). If this feature is required, open a support case on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: The feature `multi-line exception` assembles multi-lines **exception stack trace** generated by the languages described in the [Red Hat OpenShift Logging Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/logging/log-collection-and-forwarding#logging-multiline-except_configuring-log-forwarding), not multi line logs generated by the application. For example in case of Java language: * Multiline aggregation is based on strict pattern matching for Java exceptions. * Stack traces are aggregated only while the log lines match a recognized Java exception pattern * If a non-Java line appears within the stack trace (for example, URLs such as https://docs.oracle.com/error-help/db/ora-12541/), the filter exits the Java exception state * When the filter exits the Java exception state, subsequent `at...` lines and chained exceptions are ingested as separate log events in Loki Read the Red Hat Knowledge Article "[How detectMultilineErrors or detectMultilineException works in Logging stack with RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7013395)" for understanding better how the `detectMultilineException` feature works.

issue: - LokiStack pods `Compactor`, `Index-Gateway` and `Ingester` fails to start due to `Permission Denied` error. ~~~ $ oc get pods | grep-i Crash logging-loki-compactor-0 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 7 LokiStack is trying to write the data to the PVC.- Compactor pod ~~~ $ oc logs logging-loki-compactor-0 2026-01-05T17:50:00.298519742+05:30 init compactor: mkdir /tmp/loki/compactor: permission denied oc logs logging-loki-ingester-0 2026-01-05T17:50:19.192949799+05:30 mkdir /tmp/loki/tsdb-index: permission denied 2026-01-05T17:50:19.192949799+05:30 error initialising module: store /opt/app-root/src/loki/vendor/github.com/grafana/dskit/modules/modules.go:138 2026-01-05T17:50:19.192949799+05:30 github.com/grafana/dskit/modules.(*Manager).InitModuleServices ~~~
resolution: - A straight forward solution would be to create a new `StorageClass` with the `fsType: ext4` added to the New StorageClass and recreating the Lokistack with updated `StorageClass`. If creating a new `StorageClass` is not possible, Please follow the steps below. **Note: Please involve respective Storage Vendor before performing the steps as this might cause issue to existing workload in the cluster.**- Step 1: Take the Backup of the StorageClass which is being used. ~~~ $ oc get storageclass-o yaml > sc-ext4.yaml ~~~- Step 2: Edit the yaml. **Below is just a sample yaml, might differ from cluster to cluster, the only thing needed to be done is to add ` fsType: ext4 ` part in the `StorageClass`.** ~~~ apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata: name: provisioner: csi.trident.netapp.io parameters: backendType: #### depending on setup fsType: ext4 # Add the fsType parameter allowVolumeExpansion: true reclaimPolicy: Delete # or Retain volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer # or Immediate ~~~- Step 3: Delete the existing storage class. **This is important step which is why Storage Vendor confirmation is necessary.** ~~~ $ oc delete storageclass ~~~- Step 4: Recreate the `StorageClass` with updated `fsType`. ~~~ $ oc create-f sc-ext4.yaml ~~~- Once the above steps are done, `Delete` the existing `LokiStack` as well as `Delete` the `PVC` and `PV` that are created with `LokiStack` and then recreate the `LokiStack`.
root_cause: When a PersistentVolume (PV) or PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is created for block storage the fsType field tells Kubernetes what `filesystem` to format the volume with before mounting it. If fsType is not specified Kubernetes will go ahead and format the filesystem with and provide the permission which is same as `root` filesystem of the node leading to the permission denied error.

resolution: - The broker certificate is self-signed with only a CN (CN=amq-broker) and no Subject Alternative Name (SAN). Java 17+ enforces strict hostname validation against SANs. The AMQP/MQTT client connects using Open Shift Route hostnames, which do not match the CN. Browsers for console routes work because HTTP clients can bypass trust errors, but AMQP clients strictly enforce TLS validation.- Generate broker certificate with SAN,Create a configuration file broker_cert_ext.cnf including all AMQP/MQTT route hostnames: ``` [alt_names] DNS.1 = xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-amqp-0-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprodc.zzz.in DNS.2 = xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-amqp-1-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprodc.zzz.in ```- Generate the keystore with SAN: ``` keytool-genkeypair-alias broker-keyalg RSA-keysize 2048 \-keystore broker.ks-storepass changeit-keypass changeit \-validity 3650 \-dname "CN=xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-amqp-0-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprod.yyy.in, OU=AMQ, O=xxx, L=India, ST=XX, C=IN" \-ext SAN=dns:xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-amqp-0-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprod.yyy.in,dns:xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-amqp-1-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprod.yyy.in,dns:xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-mqtt-0-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprod.yyy.in,dns:xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-mqtt-1-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprod.yyy.in ```- Export broker certificate and import into client truststore: ``` keytool-exportcert-alias broker-keystore broker.ks-storepass changeit-file broker_cert.crt keytool-importcert-alias broker-file broker_cert.crt-keystore client.ts-storepass changeit-noprompt ```- Update Open Shift secret: ``` oc create secret generic xxx-amq-broker-tls \--from-file=broker.ks--from-file=broker.ts--from-file=client.ts \--from-literal=keyStorePassword=changeit--from-literal=trustStorePassword=changeit \-n xxx-amq-broker--dry-run=client-o yaml | oc apply-f- ```- Restart broker pods: ``` oc rollout restart statefulset xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-n xxx-amq-broker ```- Verify certificate and trust, Check certificate SAN and trust chain in one step: ``` openssl s_client-connect xxx-amq-broker-non-prod-amqp-0-svc-yyy-xxx-amq-broker.apps.ocpnonprod.yyy.in:443-showcerts ```- Also, inspect broker certificate: ``` keytool-list-v-keystore broker.ks-storepass changeit-alias broke ```- Use AMQP route, not console route. TLS passthrough route must be used.
root_cause: The AMQArtemis Broker was configured with a self-signed TLS certificate that contained only a Common Name and no Subject Alternative Name entries. Modern TLS clients (Java 11+, Go, OpenSSL-based clients) validate hostnames strictly against SAN and ignore the CN field. Since clients connected using OpenShift Route hostnames that were not present in the certificate SAN, TLS hostname verification failed. This resulted in PKIX path building and SSL handshake errors during client connections.

title: Requisites of migration of VM in Nutanix in OpenShift Container Platform 4.
issue: VM migration in Nutanix OpenShift Container Platform 4 is supported only under strict conditions.
resolution: Migration of OpenShift worker and control plane VMs is supported only between Nutanix clusters managed by the same Prism Central (PC):- Cluster-to-cluster migration across different Prism Central instances is not supported- Both source and destination Nutanix clusters must be registered under the same PC- VM migration relies on Prism Central–level inventory, networking, and storage consistency If clusters belong to different PCs, the operation is considered a new cluster deployment, not a migration. The following parameters must remain identical before, during, and after migration. Any change here may result in cluster instability, node failure, or full rebuild requirements.- Node and cluster identity- Node IP addresses- Node hostnames- Node domain- OpenShift cluster domain name These values are embedded in the following and can not be changed in kubelet configuration, etcd member definitionn and TLS certificates. Networking and access must remain the same:- API DNS record (api.)- Ingress DNS record (*.apps.)- External load balancer IP- Pod CIDR, Service CIDR, Machine CIDR- Same storage classes and container storage interface configuration as persistent volumes must remain accessible from the destination cluster nodes.

title: Sending Alert notifications to Microsoft Teams with msteamsv2_configs in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to send alert notification to Microsoft Teams?- How to configure alert notifications to be sent to Microsoft Teams with `msteamsv2_configs`?
resolution:
Define the Microsoft Teams receiver in the ``receivers`` section of the ``Alertmanager`` configuration like below: To change the ``Alertmanager`` configuration from the CLI: 1. Print the currently active ``Alertmanager`` configuration into file ``alertmanager.yaml``: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-monitoring get secret alertmanager-main--template='{{index.data "alertmanager.yaml"}}' | base64--decode > alertmanager.yaml ~~~ 2. Edit the configuration in ``alertmanager.yaml`` so that there is a defined ``Microsoft Teams receiver`` with ``msteams_configs`` field like below: ~~~ route: group_wait: 30s group_interval: 5m repeat_interval: 12h receiver: msteams-webhook routes:- match: alertname: Watchdog repeat_interval: 5m receiver: watchdog receivers:- name: msteams-webhook msteamsv2_configs:- webhook_url:- name: watchdog ~~~ 3. Apply the new configuration in the file: ~~~ oc-n openshift-monitoring create secret generic alertmanager-main--from-file=alertmanager.yaml--dry-run=client-o=yaml | oc-n openshift-monitoring replace secret--filename=- ~~~ 4. Restart the Alert Manager: ~~~ oc restart statefulset alertmanager ~~~ 5. Test that the configuration has been properly set up: ~~~ $ oc port-forward-p 9093:9093 $ curl http://localhost:9093/api/v2/status | jq.config... {"original":...- receiver:...- name: msteamsv2-webhook
 msteamsv2_configs:
- send_resolved: true
 http_config:
 follow_redirects: true
 enable_http2: true
 proxy_from_environment: true
 webhook_url: 
 "} ~~~
root_cause: The `msteamsv2_configs` setting is a built-in Alertmanager config type that formats alerts in the Adaptive Cards format supported by Microsoft Teams. This config replaces the older `msteams_configs` and supports richer payloads and better Teams compatibility.

title: Enable debug loglevel for openshift-authentication pods in OpenShift Container Platform 4 Cluster
issue: - How to troubleshoot authentication issues and increase openshift-authentication pods `loglevel` to `Debug` in Openshift Container Platform 4?
resolution: > **NOTE**: this solution focuses on changing log verbosity of the `openshift-authentication` pods. For updating the log verbosity of the `openshift-authentication-operator`, please refer to [this Knowledge Base solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4371671) **If you want to configure log verbosity for HCP oauth deployment then please refer to this [this Knowledge Base solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7131672)** The authentication operator accepts 5 different values for the `logLevel` of the authentication PODs: | logLevel | matching Verbosity level | |---|---| | "" | none | | "Normal" | 2 | | "Debug" | 4 | | "Trace" | 6 | | "TraceAll" | 10 | In order to enable 'Debug' level logs for the openshift-authentication pods to troubleshoot issues, the following steps can be followed: 1. Check status of pods in openshift-authentication namespace ~~~ $ oc get pod-n openshift-authentication ~~~ 2. Check logs of pod in openshift-authentication namespace ~~~ $ oc logs-n openshift-authentication ~~~ 3. Increase of debug logs for the POD in the authentication operator ~~~ $ LOGLEVEL= $ oc patch authentications.operator.openshift.io cluster--type=json-p "[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/logLevel\",\"value\":\"${LOGLEVEL}\"}]" ~~~ 4. Check for the logs from the pod in ‘openshift-authentication’ namespace again after the pods get restarted to reflect the new change. ~~~ $ oc get authentications.operator.openshift.io cluster-o json | jq-r.spec.logLevel $ oc logs-n openshift-authentication ~~~ 5. Once the debugging is done, the operator config should be restored with the default value for the `logLevel` field. ~~~ $ LOGLEVEL=$(oc get crd authentications.operator.openshift.io-o json | jq-r '.spec.versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties.logLevel.default') $ oc patch authentications.operator.openshift.io cluster--type=json-p "[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/logLevel\",\"value\":\"${LOGLEVEL}\"}]" ~~~ **IMPORTANT NOTE**: Reverting the debug log level is important to avoid exposure of sensitive logs.

resolution: Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report: RHOL Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata--- |--- 6.0 | [LOG-6759](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6759) | 6.0.6 | [RHSA-2025:3132](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:3132) 6.1 | [LOG-6585](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-6585) | 6.1.2 | [RHBA-2025:1229](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:1229) If this issue still occurs in the environment after updating, open a support case in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. #### Workaround Review the `outputs` defined in the `clusterLogForwarder` custom resource not used in the `pipelines` and:- or remove the not used output- or use the output in the pipeline for log forwarding logs to it
