title: Machine stuck in Provisioned state due to MachineHealthCheck timeouts during scale‑up  in RHOCP 4
issue: When scaling a `MachineSet` in `OpenShift`, newly created machines remained in `Provisioned state` and the corresponding `nodes` did not join the `cluster`, even though the `virtual machines` were running in `Azure`.
resolution: - Update the `MachineHealthCheck` configuration to allow more tolerance during `node` startup: ~~~ $ oc edit machinehealthcheck-n openshift-machine-api apiVersion: v1 items: apiVersion: machine.openshift.io/v1beta1 kind: MachineHealthCheck metadata: name: namespace: openshift-machine-api spec: maxUnhealthy: "40%"----> # changed to 50% nodeStartupTimeout: "10m"-----> # changed to 30m ~~~- After updating the `MachineHealthCheck` and scale up the `MachineSet` again and check if `machines` are successfully created.
root_cause: - The `MachineHealthCheck` thresholds were too restrictive during the `MachineSet` scale-up operation.- During scale-up:- New `Azure nodes` required more than 10 minutes to fully initialize and become `Ready`- Before completing startup, `nodes` were marked `unhealthy` due to the low `nodeStartupTimeout`- With `maxUnhealthy` set to `40%`, the cluster quickly reached or exceeded the allowed `unhealthy` `node` limit- Once the limit was reached, `OpenShift` remediation logic either:- `Deleted` the `machines` prematurely, or- `Paused remediation`- As a result, `machines` transitioned from `Running` to `Deleting` state and remained stuck in `Provisioned state`.- This behavior is expected and serves as a safety mechanism to prevent excessive `node` replacement, but it interfered with scale-up due to longer `node` startup times in `Azure`.

title: How to Disable NVMe multipath devices on RHCOS?
issue: - How to Disable NVMe multipath devices on RHCOS?- Disabling NVMe multipath devices on RHCOS nodes. ~~~ $ ls-lrt /dev/disk/by-id total 0 nvme-eui.123456790123456789_0->../../nvme0n1 nvme-ABCDEFGHIJKL.CDGETFT1234_1->../../nvme0n1 nvme-ABDEFGHIJKL_FGRDHTHK12345->../../nvme0n1 ~~~
resolution: - Administrative privileges to the OpenShift cluster are needed.- Before making any changes, verify that all the nodes in the cluster are in a healthy state to avoid potential issues after making changes: ~~~ $ oc get nodes $ oc get co ~~~- Create a MachineConfig to specify the kernel argument for disabling `NVMe multipath.` ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 05-worker-kernelarg-disable-nvme-multipath spec: kernelArguments:- nvme_core.multipath=N ~~~- Apply the configuration by creating the new MachineConfig using the following command: ~~~ $ oc create-f 05-worker-kernelarg-disable-nvme-multipath.yaml ~~~- Verify that the new MachineConfig was successfully added: ~~~ $ oc get mc ~~~- Once changes are applied, nodes automatically reboot to apply the new configuration.- After the nodes have rebooted, access the node and verify whether the kernel argument has been applied by running the following commands: ~~~ $ oc debug no/ # chroot /host # cat /sys/module/nvme_core/parameters/multipath ~~~- If the output is `N,` this confirms that NVMe multipath has been disabled.- If the output is `Y,` multipath is still enabled.
root_cause: NVMe multipath can create duplicate disk ID entries for NVMe disks, leading to conflicts and confusion in disk management. This issue occurs when multiple paths to the same NVMe device are recognized, causing the system to treat the same disk as separate devices. Disabling multipath resolves this by ensuring only one path is used, eliminating duplicate entries and improving system stability.

title: Data Grid 8 Operators coexistence in a same Openshift cluster
issue: - Can one have two DG 8 Operators in the same cluster?- Can user have two DG 8 in the same cluster?
resolution: It is not supported to have multiple versions of the DG Operator in the same OCP cluster The coexistence of **different** DG versions in the **same cluster** could sometimes work, but it's **not** a supported use case in general: since CRDs are common to the whole OCP cluster, old versions can conflict with new definitions. The component that sets the scope of the DG Operator is the [OperatorGroups](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6962683) (aka `OG`), which is set as follows:- in case it brings no `.spec` details, it will be cluster-wide- in case it brings target namespace in the `.spec` details, it will be namespace bounded Therefore, **Intersecting OperatorGroups** issue is caused by multiple operators installed, targeting same namespaces (or wrong configured `OperatorGroups`). Given the above:- For cluster-wide installations the installation is done in `openshift-operators`- because it has a `OG` with no target namespace- For namespace specific the operator namespace's installation is set on the subscription and the target namespace is set on `Operator Groups`, which are objects that connect between the operator namespace and the target namespace, which is the namespace the operator will listen to APIs creations (cluster, cache). ### Using multiple versions of Data Grid Operand (not Data Grid Operator versions- but Operand) Starting on [DG Operator 8.4](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.4/html/data_grid_operator_8.4_release_notes/rhdg-operator-releases#rhdg-operator-84GA_rhdg-operator-releases), the user can have a single Data Grid Operator installation that supports multiple versions of Data Grid, which we call Operands. For doing so use `spec.version` field in your Infinispan CR to upgrade between supported versions. Example:- Data Grid Operator version 8.4 supports the following Data Grid versions (for DG Operator 8.4.1.csv): Data Grid OPERATOR version | OPERAND versions--------- |--------- DG 8.4.14 | (...) 8.4.7-1 DG 8.4.8 | 8.3.1-1, 8.4.0-1, 8.4.0-2, 8.4.1-1, 8.4.1-2, 8.4.1-3, 8.4.2-1, 8.4.3-1, 8.4.3-2, 8.4.4-1 DG 8.4.1 | 8.3.1-1, 8.4.0-1, 8.4.0-2 DG 8.3 | 8.3.1-1 For more details on the **DG Operator <-> DG Operand (DG server)** association, see the solution [Association between DG Operator and DG Server version/DG Operands](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7036542). ### FAQ **Q1. Can I have multiple DG Operator versions in the same OCP cluster?** A1. No. That's not supported because they will certainly collide given CRD are cluster wide. **Q2. Can I have multiple DG versions in the same OCP cluster?** A2. Starting on DG 8.4 Operator, it can (with limitations) support different versions of clusters: DG 8.3.1 and DG 8.4.0 in the same DG Operator. **Q3. User has Dg Operator 8.4.1 and deployed a Infinispan CR with version 8.4.0, can it be downgraded?** A3. Downgrade is not allowed.
root_cause: Operators can be installed namespace bounded (one Operator listening to one namespace) or cluster-wide (one operator for all the OCP cluster). Having multiple operators of the same DG Operator version is possible given a namespace bounded operator- which is set by OperatorGroup's target namespaces. However, when the upgrade is done in one, it must be done for all- to avoid CRDs conflicts. Meaning DG Operator upgrade in one namespace means to do upgrade for all the namespaces- sequentially. Given one operator with specific namespace (let's say A) and another cluster wide (same version), they are incompatible and you cannot install both- at the same time. The following messages can be seeing: ~~~ Danger alert:Installation Failed Failed: intersecting operatorgroups provide the same apis ~~~ And the namespace in question is A because there would be two DG 8 Operators managing the same namespace A. Otherwise, manually installing it, even though the install plan will be approved but the message (on the Install Plan) will have `message: more than one operator group(s) are managing this namespace count=2.` For migration step, see solution [How to migrate from DG 8.1/8.2 to DG 8.3 in DG 8 Operator](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6958429).

title: Windows Guest migrated from VMware shows high CPU utilization
issue: Windows Guest has High CPU usage, not responding well
Even when idle CPU usage in the Guest is very high
High CPU usage in the OCP node
Windows Guest migrated from VMware has high CPU utilization when running in OpenShift.
Intel CPUs.
resolution: * Enabling VBS causes a performance overhead due to the nested virtualization. Using HVCI (memory integrity) also causes a performance hit. If these are not required please consider disabling them for best performance. * If VBS and/or HVCI are required, enable the EVMCS hyper-v enlightenment in the Virtual Machine spec: ~~~ apiVersion: kubevirt.io/v1 kind: VirtualMachine spec: template: spec: domain: features: hyperv: evmcs: {} <--- add to the list ~~~ * Further hyper-v enlightenments are needed to alleviate the performance impact (such as Direct TLB Flush) but they are not available yet in OpenShift Virtualization (see Root Cause section). NOTE: adding this to a Virtual Machine that does not run any hypervisor itself should not cause any harm. So it can be added to standard user templates and boot sources if needed.
root_cause: * Lack of EVMCS enlightenment makes nested virtualization required by VBS sub-optimal as it triggers too many exists on the L0 host when accessing VMCS. * Improvements to automatically enable this are being tracked in [CNV-69067- Sub-optimal performance of Windows with VBS enabled due to lack of EVMCS](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-69067). * On top of enabling EVMCS, further performance improvements are available via enabling Direct and Extended TLB Flushes enlightenments. These are not currently available in the VM configuration, and are being tracked in [CNV-69327- Missing knob to control hv-tlbflush-direct and hv-tlbflush-extended](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-69327). Once these are available, enable them as well. For alternate ways of enabling these (for testing only), please contact Red Hat Support.

title: TargetDown alert for GitOps operator metrics after upgrade
issue: - After upgrading the OpenShift GitOps Operator to 1.17.3, a TargetDown alert is triggered in the OpenShift console for the `openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service`: ``` 100% of the openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service/openshift-gitops-operator-metrics-service targets in openshift-gitops-operator namespace have been unreachable for more than 15 minute...) ```
resolution: - After upgrade from 1.17.2 version, the TargetDown alert is triggered because the metrics endpoint returns 403 forbidden response.- Red Hat investigated this issue in bug [GITOPS-8591](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/GITOPS-8591) and delivered a fix in GitOps versions 1.19.1, 1.18.3, and 1.17.4. If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, open [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) in the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.- As a workaround, below mentioned clusterrole and clusterrolebinding can be created to get the access for `/metrics` endpoint: ``` apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: gitops-operator-metrics-reader rules:- nonResourceURLs:- /metrics verbs:- get... apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: name: metrics-reader-binding roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: gitops-operator-metrics-reader subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: openshift-gitops-operator-controller-manager namespace: openshift-gitops-operator ```
root_cause: The 403 error indicates an authorization failure. One identified scenario is that the required RBAC permissions are missing for accessing the `/metrics` endpoint. As a result, Prometheus is unable to scrape metrics successfully, leading to the TargetDown alert.

The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products, or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* #### Using [ApplicationSet](https://argocd-applicationset.readthedocs.io/en/stable/#introduction-to-applicationset-controller) Controller/CRD to achieve this.- The ApplicationSet controller is made up of multiple Generators. As of this writing, there are seven [Generators](https://argocd-applicationset.readthedocs.io/en/stable/Generators/#generators:~:text=Developer%20Guide-,Generators,-%C2%B6).- Three of the most commonly used Generators are List, Cluster, and Git generator. Each Generator tackles different scenarios and use-cases.- An example of ApplicationSet using **List** generator would look like this: ~~~ apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: ApplicationSet metadata: name: guestbook spec: generators:- list: elements:- cluster: dev url: https://api.dev.xyz.cloud.com:6443- cluster: prod url: https://api.prod.xyz.cloud.com:6443 template: metadata: name: '{{cluster}}-guestbook' spec: project: default source: repoURL: https://github.com/argoproj/applicationset.git targetRevision: HEAD path: examples/list-generator/guestbook/{{cluster}} destination: server: '{{url}}' namespace: guestbook ~~~- For more examples, review [Getting Started with ApplicationSets](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/getting-started-with-applicationsets) Blog post and [Argo CD documentation](https://argocd-applicationset.readthedocs.io/en/stable/Generators/).- Enabling `ApplicationSets` for the target instance is required if an instance other than the default `openshift-gitops` is being utilized. ~~~ spec: applicationSet: resources: limits: cpu: "2" memory: 1Gi requests: cpu: 250m memory: 512Mi ~~~
root_cause: ApplicationSets interact with Argo CD by creating, updating, managing, and deleting Argo CD Applications.

title: Finding and removing  orphaned RBD images in ODF and OCS 4.x
issue: - Orphaned RBD images occupy the space even after the PVC and PV has been deleted- When checking the number of existing images within Ceph on ODF, sometimes we see a mismatch between the number of RBD images versus the number of existing PVs/PVCs on OCP, where the number of RBD images is higher than the number of created and active PVs/PVCs, evidencing these images are orphaned somehow. So how might one delete these orphaned images not linked to any PV/PVC?
resolution: ---------------------------------- #### Important- *Please investigate how did cluster reached the current state before attempting to delete any orphaned volumes. The volume delete flow in ODF should prevent any orphaned volumes. A Bugzilla should be filed for further investigation if required.*- *Please perform the orphan removal with extreme caution; wrongly deleting any RBD image that is in use will result in unrecoverable data loss*- *Please open an RH support case to get technical guidance before you perform this on a production cluster*---------------------------------- The resolution involves finding the RBD volumes and removing them from the cluster manually. **Pre-requisite**: Configure the `ceph toolbox` pod as documented [here](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4628891); this will help us to run all the relevant ceph commands 1. Check the available number of images in RBD for the specific pool, keep a note of the number of images- For this article, the default ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool pool is used. List the images in this pool using `#rbd ls` command. You may redirect the output to a file. ``` $ oc exec-n openshift-storage $(oc get pod-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o name)-- rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool ls |tee /tmp/all_rbd_images.txt ``` 2. List the number of volumes/PV in OpenShift; you may redirect it to a file. If you have more than one storageclass for RBD volumes then please check available volumes for all RBD storage classes. ``` $ oc get pv-o 'custom-columns=IMAGENAME:.spec.csi.volumeAttributes.imageName' | grep-v none | grep-v IMAGENAME |tee /tmp/all_pvs.txt ``` 3. Compare both files using comm. This output will tell you rbd images that are uniq to all_rbd_images.txt that do not exist in sort all_pvs.txt ``` $ comm-23 <(/usr/bin/sort all_rbd_images.txt) <(/usr/bin/sort all_pvs.txt) > /tmp/rbd_images_with_no_PV.txt ``` 4. Some of these rbd images can be snapshots that can be associated to a VolumeSnapshotContent (VSC). We must not delete an rbd image associated to a VolumeSnapshotContent. So we need to exclude these from above list rbd_images_with_no_PV.txt--> create a subset called: rbd_images_with_no_PV_and_no_VSC.txt Example to manually identify rbd images associated to a VSC ~~~ csi-snap-0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21 has no PV associated, but is related to this VSC: snapcontent-3af20138-a416-4bd4-a2d9-c913f7e59918 true 32212254720 Delete openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass rhel8-cd97caf10611 openshift-virtualization-os-images 15d % oc get volumesnapshotcontent-o yaml|grep 0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21 snapshotHandle: 0001-0011-openshift-storage-000000000000000b-0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21 % oc get volumesnapshotcontent-o yaml|grep 0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21-B30|grep "name: snapcontent" name: snapcontent-a6f2a49c-0926-45dd-80f9-3f00afd6f494 ~~~ Creation of the new list: ~~~ % cut-d "-"-f3,4,5,6,7 rbd_images_with_no_PV.txt > ID_rbd_images_with_no_PV.txt % for ID in $(cat ID_rbd_images_with_no_PV.txt); do echo "Checking image: $ID" snap_output=$(oc get volumesnapshotcontent-o yaml|grep $ID) if [-z "$snap_output"]; then echo "$ID" > > ID_rbd_images_with_no_PV_and_no_VSC.txt fi done % for ID in $(cat ID_rbd_images_with_no_PV_and_no_VSC.txt); do grep $ID rbd_images_with_no_PV.txt; done > rbd_images_with_no_PV_and_no_VSC.txt ~~~ 5. From above list we need to find if these are parent of a child:- An rbd with a child must not be deleted.- A child is a clone from a snapshot.- Data of that child is dependent on the parent, which means parent cannot be deleted. NOTE. To make the child independent, we would need to flatten the clone (the child), but this is not required here. The "rbd children" command will display children of an image or its snapshot, see [Listing Children of a Snapshot](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/rbd/rbd-snapshot/#listing-children-of-a-snapshot) If it reports nothing, that means it not a parent. ~~~ sh-5.1$ rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool children csi-vol-062ec147-ced7-4cf0-b259-38787b6ea347 ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool/csi-vol-61a7319b-09f2-45ba-95ca-62e1c7258910-temp < < <-- children ~~~ To identify orphaned images, we use 'rbd children' command on each of the rbd_images_with_no_PV_and_no_VSC.txt as an additional check. If no children exist, we deem it orphaned: ~~~ % for image in $(cat rbd_images_with_no_PV_and_no_VSC.txt); do echo "Checking image: $image" children_output=$(oc exec-n openshift-storage $(oc get pod-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o name)-- rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool children $image) if [-z "$children_output"]; then echo "$image" > > rbd_images_with_no_PV_no_VSC_and_no_children.txt fi done ~~~ 6. You can also map the persistent volumes in RBD storageclass to Ceph RBD images by following the steps [here](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4718301) 7. Once you have the list of RBD orphan volumes (rbd_images_with_no_PV_no_VSC_and_no_children.txt), confirm that the volume is not in use from the Ceph side. There should be no watchers for the volume (ie: 'Watchers: none') ~~~ $ for i in $(cat /tmp/rbd_images_with_no_PV_no_VSC_and_no_children.txt);do echo $i; rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool status $i;done Watchers: watcher=10.129.2.1:0/1849604752 client.4740 cookie=18446462598732840961 <--- There are active watchers for this volume and may be in use by an application. ~~~ NOTE. You can see how much data each rbd image contains with command below: ~~~ sh-5.1$ rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool du NAME PROVISIONED USED csi-snap-0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21@csi-snap-0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21 30 GiB 0 B csi-snap-0ee7cc43-8ec2-42bd-af10-807b3dcddc21 30 GiB 0 B csi-vol-062ec147-ced7-4cf0-b259-38787b6ea347 30 GiB 0 B csi-vol-062ec147-ced7-4cf0-b259-38787b6ea347-temp 30 GiB 3.9 GiB csi-vol-126aa626-b1ee-4d53-8793-2e7d75f755cb 120 GiB 0 B csi-vol-17875e43-9f3d-4660-aee2-28238885a247 30 GiB 1.1 GiB ~~~ 8. If there are active watchers then you will need to trace the IP and client application. Oftentimes, these active watcher entries are stale, but it will prevent RBD volumes from being deleted with error "rbd: error: image still has watchers". Please refer this KCS article [`Ceph- rbd image cannot be deleted with "rbd: error: image still has watchers"`](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5834801) to know how to unmap and clear the watcher list to proceed with deletion 9. In ODF environment, you have to run the 'showmapped' command from the csi-rbdplugin pod where the PV is attached to: ``` Example: $ oc rsh-n openshift-storage-c csi-rbdplugin pod/csi-rbdplugin- $ rbd showmapped id pool namespace image snap device 0 ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool csi-vol-09477143-85e0-4c2f-bed1-f236d39aa9f3- /dev/rbd0 ``` + If you are not able to figure out on which worker node the image is mapped and mounted, then you may have to do this from all the rbdplugin pods You can use a bash script like: ``` $ for rbdpluginpods in $(oc get pod-l app=csi-rbdplugin-o name); do echo $rbdpluginpods; oc exec-it $rbdpluginpods-c csi-rbdplugin rbd showmapped; done ``` + This will list all the mapped RBD images from all the worker nodes. Identify in which csi-rbdplugin the orphaned RBD image is mapped, then get inside the corresponding csi-rbdplugin pod and run ``` $ oc rsh-n openshift-storage-c csi-rbdplugin pod/csi-rbdplugin- $ rbd unmap-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool ``` 10. Remove the orphaned RBD volumes ``` $ rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool rm csi-vol-e097a3e7-1098-11ec-ae7f-0a580a83002e $ rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool rm csi-vol-062ec147-ced7-4cf0-b259-38787b6ea347-temp ``` NOTE. We may fail to delete a ceph-rbd image (that comes from a VSC) with this error: ``` sh-5.1$ rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool rm csi-snap-9d50d946-c910-42c5-8481-cac963aebcc7 Removing image: 0% complete...failed. rbd: image has snapshots- these must be deleted with 'rbd snap purge' before the image can be removed. sh-5.1$ ``` In this case, we need to purge the snapshot, and then delete the image: ``` rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool snap purge csi-snap-9d50d946-c910-42c5-8481-cac963aebcc7 rbd-p ocs-storagecluster-cephblockpool rm csi-snap-9d50d946-c910-42c5-8481-cac963aebcc7 ```
root_cause: - The volume delete flow in ODF should prevent any orphaned volumes. But in some corner cases, we have seen the presence of orphaned RBD volumes in the cluster. Some scenarios include: + Manual deletion of PV before the PVC. + PVC `reclaimpolicy` is set to `retain` instead of `delete`. This will prevent the underlying RBD image from being deleted.- When the volumesnapshotclass "ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass" has configured the DELETIONPOLICY to Retain, the volumesnapshotcontents (VSC) will have the deletionPolicy set to Retain. In that case, when the VSC is deleted the underlying ceph-rbd image "csi-snap" is not deleted, neither the associated snapshot of the csi-snap image.

title: Unable to mount volumes using LVM Storage in RHOCP 4
issue: - LVM storage is unable to provision volume: ~~~ $ oc get events-n default 4h27m Normal Provisioning persistentvolumeclaim/prime-6c164f59-b241-42cd-8a58-1890934d234e External provisioner is provisioning volume for claim "default/prime-6c164f59-b241-42cd-8a58-1890934d234e" 4h35m Warning ProvisioningFailed persistentvolumeclaim/prime-6c164f59-b241-42cd-8a58-1890934d234e failed to provision volume with StorageClas ~~~
resolution: - Update the `lvmcluster/lvmcluster` object using the disk UUID, like below: ~~~ $ oc edit lvmcluster/lvmcluster-n openshift-storage spec: storage: deviceClasses:- name: vg1 fstype: xfs deviceSelector: paths:- /dev/disk/by-path/- /dev/disk/by-path/ thinPoolConfig: name: thin-pool-1 sizePercent: 90 overprovisionRatio: 10 ~~~- The disks UUID can be obtained from the SNO node using the below command: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ $ sudo blkid /dev/sdb $ sudo blkid /dev/sdc ~~~
root_cause: - The disk device names may get renamed after the SNO node reboot, better would be to use the disk UUID which remains persistent.- An [OCPBUG-35943](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-35943) raised with engineering to dynamically figure out the additional disks on the node and use the device paths/disk UUID for LVM storage.

title: Is the use of LVM for a non-root disk supported in RHCOS?
issue: - Does `LVM` creation over an additional non-root disk in RHCOS supported with the `immutable` nature of RHCOS??
resolution: - Creating `LVM` over an additional `non-root` local disks is possible and supported with RHCOS.- It does not affect immutable nature of RHCOS since `LVM signature` resides over the particular disk and it will be consistent across reboot and version upgrades.
root_cause: - In general there are two things which are required for successful configuration and utilization of LVM over RHCOS.- `LVM signature` and `metadata` over the Disk.- Once configured the `LVM signature` and `metadata` will be residing on that particular disk and it will always be intact unless the disk itself gets corrupted.- Even if the disk is detached from the original host and attached to any other RHCOS or RHEL system, still complete LVM structure with underlying data will be accessible in the new system.- Only `manual deletion` and `LVM signature or metadata corruption` can affect LVM structure and the data over the disk.- `LVM` and `Devicemapper` packages and Binaries.- These packages and binaries enable RHCOS to read the on disk LVM metadata and even if the cluster and RHCOS is updated the still those packages and binaries will always be there.

title: How to remove Public IP on OpenShift Ingress Load Balancer for Existing ARO Clusters
issue: A customer wants to disable or remove the public IP address associated with the OpenShift ingress/router load balancer on an existing Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) cluster. The cluster was created as:- A **private*
ARO cluster- **Pre-UDR*
(User Defined Routing) configuration- Ingress/router load balancer still has a public IP attached The customer wants the API and ingress endpoints to be fully private.
resolution: There is no supported method to remove or disable the public IP address from the Azure Load Balancer used by the OpenShift ingress/router on an existing pre-UDR ARO cluster. To have fully private API and ingress endpoints (no public IP exposure), the cluster must be **redeployed with User Defined Routing (UDR) enabled** at creation time. Refer the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-create-private-cluster-4x#create-a-private-cluster-without-a-public-ip-address) for creating a private cluster without a public IP address. **NOTE:** Modifying the Azure Load Balancer directly to remove the public IP is unsupported and may lead to cluster instability.
root_cause: In pre-UDR ARO clusters, the public IP attached to the Azure Load Balancer is **required for outbound internet access (egress)**. While it is possible to add NAT Gateways and update subnet route tables to use those NAT Gateways for egress, the public IP on the Azure Load Balancer remains mandatory in pre-UDR architectures and **cannot be removed in a supported manner**. Only clusters created with UDR enabled from day one support fully private API and ingress endpoints without a public IP.

title: Is it possible to change api-vip and ingress-vip by keeping same domain name post cluster installation in RHOCP 4.x?
issue: - Can api & ingress vip be changed post OCP cluster installation?- It is required to change the IPs of api & ingress vip due to the external LB change. The domain name will be the same. Is it possible to achieve this task?- For OpenShift clusters installed using `platform: openstack`, can the API and Ingress external floating IPs be changed post-installation while keeping the same domain names?
resolution: **OCP clusters provision via UPI (or similarly, the agent-based installer with platform type none)**- Yes, it is supported to change the external Load Balancer VIPs (for API and Ingress) after the cluster has been installed, provided that the domain names remain unchanged. These VIPs are managed at the external load balancer level, and any changes must be coordinated with the infrastructure or networking team. This includes updating backend mappings, DNS records, and ensuring correct routing.- Any issues related to the external load balancer configuration need to be addressed by the responsible infrastructure or networking team, as they fall outside the scope of OpenShift support **OCP clusters provision via IPI (or similarly, the agent-based installer with platform type baremetal or vsphere)**- It is not supported to modify the API and Ingress VIPs after cluster installation when using the IPI (Installer-Provisioned Infrastructure) approach. The following enhancement request was raised but has been rejected:[RFE-2085- Ability to change `apiVIP` and `ingressVIP` on a deployed cluster](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-2085)- As per the current OpenShift design, modifying `apiVIP` and `ingressVIP` post-installation in IPI-based clusters is not supported and cannot be changed. **OCP clusters provisioned on OpenStack (platform: openstack)**- For OpenShift clusters installed using the OpenStack IPI installer (`platform: openstack`), the platform configuration is considered immutable after installation. Modifying the API and Ingress VIPs post-installation is not a tested or formally supported workflow.- However, in OpenStack deployments, the floating IPs associated with the API and Ingress endpoints function as external NAT mappings at the OpenStack infrastructure layer. OpenShift itself continues to bind to the internal API and Ingress VIPs, which remain unchanged.- In practice, reassociating new floating IPs to the existing API and Ingress VIP ports may work, provided:- The internal VIPs are unchanged- Traffic continues to reach the same VIP ports- External DNS records are updated to point to the new floating IPs- This approach is outside the scope of OpenShift support and depends entirely on correct OpenStack (Neutron / Load Balancer) configuration. The OpenStack infrastructure team must handle any issues related to the creation, association, or routing of floating IPs.- It is strongly recommended to validate this change on a test or non-production cluster first, ensuring API access, console access, and application routes function as expected before applying similar changes in production.

title: CUDA 13.0 Driver Compatibility Issues When Deploying Models with RHAIIS (vLLM)
issue: - Cuda Version: 13.0 driver compatibility issue when trying to deploy any model using `vLLM`.- In `RHAIIS 3.2.4`, vLLM based LLM inference failed with error. ~~~ $ podman run--rm-it--device nvidia.com/gpu=all--security-opt=label=disable--shm-size=4g-p 8000:8000--userns=keep-id:uid=1001--env "HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0"--env=VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1--env=VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG-v./rhaiis-cache:/opt/app-root/src/.cache:Z registry.redhat.io/rhaiis/vllm-cuda-rhel9:3.2.4--model RedHatAI/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8.. (EngineCore_DP0 pid=96) torch._C._cuda_init() (EngineCore_DP0 pid=96) RuntimeError: Unexpected error from cudaGetDeviceCount(). Did you run some cuda functions before calling NumCudaDevices() that might have already set an error? Error 803: system has unsupported display driver / cuda driver combination ~~~
resolution: - This issue is fixed in latest [RHAIIS 3.2.5](https://catalog.redhat.com/en/software/containers/rhaiis/vllm-cuda-rhel9/6825c6b827e18fe3162148a9?image=6940265a4fae4079031da944#overview)- `RHAIIS 3.2.1` is not impacted but the version after that has been impacted.- The image `http://registry.redhat.io/rhaiis/vllm-cuda-rhel9:latest` works perfectly.- Product impact status: | Build | vLLM | CUDA driver | Is RHAIIS starting? | RHOAI with RHAIIS CUDA impacted | |--------------|----------|-------------|----------------------|---------------------------------| | RHAIIS 3.2.1 | 0.10.0 | 580.105.08 | ✅ |- | | RHAIIS 3.2.2 | 0.10.1.1 | 580.105.08 | ❌ | 2.25 | | RHAIIS 3.2.3 | 0.11.0 | 580.105.08 | ❌ | 3.0 | | RHAIIS 3.2.4 | 0.11.0 | 580.105.08 | ❌ |- | | RHAIIS 3.2.5 | 0.11.2 | 590.44.01 | ✅ |- | ##**Workaround** 1. In Openshift AI, following work around steps provided in link [NVIDIA GPU driver 580.105.08 compatibility issue with RHOAI 2.25.0 and 3.0](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7134740) 2. In RHEL (RHAIIS), downgrade the NVIDIA GPU Driver. ~~~ # dnf downgrade nvidia-driver nvidia-driver-cuda ~~~
root_cause: * Driver compatibility issue when using the RHAIIS image version 3.2.2 and above with NVIDIA GPU driver version 580.105.08 and CUDA 12.x during model deployment. * This issue arises from a conflict between the host and the container-provided binary, leading to a compatibility mismatch that prevents successful model deployment. * Specifically, the problem is caused by the cuda-compat package, which provides a CUDA binary that is preferred over the host driver library. * In the vLLM container, the `cuda-compat` package via dynamic linker run time bindings is adding `libcuda.so.1` link to file `/usr/local/cuda/compat/libcuda.so.1` causing the error: ~~~ # ldconfig-p | grep libcuda.so.1 libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/local/cuda/compat/libcuda.so.1 libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /lib64/libcuda.so.1 ~~~ * This occurs due to forward compatibility behavior (i.e., a newer CUDA runtime with an older driver), causing the container’s compat library to be loaded instead of the host driver. **Note:** Any RHOAI images built on top of this RHAIIS image will be impacted by the same issue.

NVIDIA and Red Hat can initiate the collaboration with TSANet. **FAQ** **1. As an OpenShift customer, how can I get NVAIE license?** The following links are ways to obtain to NVAIE license:- [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-ozgjkov6vq3l6?sr=0-1&ref_=beagle&applicationId=AWSMPContessa)- [GCP](https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/nvidia/nvidia-ai-enterprise-vmi?project=nvidia-ngc-public&pli=1)- [Azure](https://azuremarketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/marketplace/apps/nvidia.nvidia-ai-enterprise?tab=Overview)- [NVAIE customers can bring their own licenses on the cloud](https://docs.nvidia.com/ai-enterprise/deployment-guide-cloud/0.1.0/aws-overview.html) **2. As an OpenShift customer, must I subscribe to NVAIE support to use OpenShift on VMware vSphere Virtual Machines?** In the context of using NVIDIA GPUs with OpenShift on VMware vSphere, it's important to understand the nuances of NVIDIA GPU Operator support and licensing. This article aims to clarify when and why an NVAIE (NVIDIA AI Enterprise) license is required and the implications for Red Hat customers seeking support. For OpenShift deployments on VMware vSphere, the NVIDIA GPU Operator allows you to utilize PCIe Passthrough, enabling GPU resources for your workloads. However, it's essential to be aware that this configuration falls under the category of "Community supported." This means that while it is technically feasible, it may not receive the same level of support and troubleshooting capabilities as a licensed solution. While you can employ PCIe Passthrough, it is highly recommended to obtain this license for multiple reasons, including NVIDIA GPU operator support, NVIDIA CUDA driver build failures, assistance with NVIDIA device plugin bugs, DCGM exporter problems, etc. In order to receive NVIDIA Enterprise Support, NVAIE (NVIDIA AI Enterprise) or vGPU entitlement must be in place and purchased. For Red Hat customers using OpenShift on VMware vSphere, it's important to understand that Red Hat's support capabilities are closely tied to NVIDIA's NVAIE licensing. Red Hat can engage with NVIDIA support on behalf of a customer only when the customer has purchased an NVAIE license. In summary, while PCIe Passthrough can be used without an NVAIE license in OpenShift on VMware vSphere, the decision to purchase an NVAIE license should be based on the level of support and assistance required. To ensure access to NVIDIA's support resources and to enable Red Hat's support team to collaborate effectively with NVIDIA, customers are encouraged to order an NVAIE license when working with NVIDIA GPU operator and related technologies. This approach ensures a smoother and more efficient resolution of GPU-related issues and ensures the best possible support for your OpenShift deployment. **3. As an OpenShift customer, NVIDIA A100X Driver Support** The [NVIDIA A100X](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/gtcf21/converged-accelerator/pdf/datasheet.pdf) is a converged accelerator card consisting of a Bluefield 2 DPU and an A100 GPU. When the A100X is deployed as two discrete cards (GPU, NIC) then the RHEL supported driver, MLX5, is used for the NIC and NVIDIA provides the GPU drivers. Divers are available [here](https://network.nvidia.com/products/infiniband-drivers/linux/mlnx_ofed/).

title: Jaeger Deprecation and Removal in OpenShift
issue: When installing the Red Hat OpenShift Distributed Tracing Platform or OpenShift Service Mesh, there is a warning on OpenShift web console regarding the deprecation of Jaeger.
resolution: Starting with the Red Hat Openshift distributed tracing platform 3.0, Jaeger and OpenShift Elasticsearch Operator are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Red Hat will provide bug fixes and support for these features during the current release lifecycle, but these features will no longer receive enhancements and will be removed. As an alternative to Red Hat OpenShift Distributed Tracing Platform (Jaeger), it is recommended to use [Red Hat OpenShift Distributed Tracing Platform (Tempo)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html-single/distributed_tracing/index) instead, together wit the [Red Hat build of OpenTelemetry](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html-single/red_hat_build_of_opentelemetry/index). > **Notes about Tempo storage** > > * Tempo requires **object storage** to store tracing data, and supports all major cloud object storage types. Refer to the [object storage setup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html-single/distributed_tracing/index#distr-tracing-tempo-object-storage-setup_distr-tracing-tempo-installing) documentation for additional information. > * Tempo also provides a [TempoMonolithic instance](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html-single/distributed_tracing/index#installing-a-tempomonolithic-instance_distr-tracing-tempo-installing) which can serve as a great replacement for "*Jaeger all-in-one*", providing the ability to store traces in-memory or disk (not intended for production environments). More information can be found in this [Blog post](https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2024/08/14/introducing-tempo-monolithic-mode). #### Jaeger usage with Service Mesh The Distributed Tracing is an optional component of OpenShift Service Mesh. Refer to [understanding distributed tracing](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/service_mesh/service-mesh-2-x#understanding-distributed-tracing) in the Service Mesh documentation for additional information. Note that since the Jaeger and Elasticsearch operators are supported as part of OpenShift Distributed Tracing, they may reach end of life before OpenShift Service Mesh 3.0, and is no longer the default since version 2.6 as explained in [Red Hat OpenShift Distributed Tracing Platform (Jaeger) default setting change](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/service_mesh/service-mesh-2-x#jaeger-default-setting-change-ossm-2-6-0_ossm-release-notes). It will be required to migrate off of Jaeger and Elasticsearch before upgrading to OpenShift Service Mesh 3.0.
root_cause: The Jaeger operator, supported by Red Hat OpenShift was deprecated in December 2023 with the release of the Red Hat Openshift distributed tracing platform 3.0 and [General Availability of the Red Hat build of OpenTelemetry](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/red-hat-build-opentelemetry-reaches-general-availability). It is expected that Jaeger Operator is be **removed** from the OpenShift Operator Catalog in **November 2025**. The Observability team will continue providing support for critical CVEs, but users are highly encouraged to change to the new `Tempo` and `OpenTelemetry` stack as soon as possible. Refer to [OpenShift Operator Life Cycles](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/openshift_operators) for additional information.

title: Monitoring  Cluster Operator Degraded With Error "UpdatingMetricsServer: reconciling MetricsServer Deployment failed"
issue: During the upgrade, it was identified that the `monitoring` cluster operator entered into a `degraded` state with an error: ~~~ $ oc describe co monitoring message: 'UpdatingMetricsServer: reconciling MetricsServer Deployment failed: updating Deployment object failed: waiting for DeploymentRollout of openshift-monitoring/metrics-server: context deadline exceeded' reason: UpdatingMetricsServerFailed status: 'True' ~~~
resolution: Before making any changes, back up the existing cluster monitoring configuration: ~~~ $ oc get cm cluster-monitoring-config-n openshift-monitoring-o yaml > cluster-monitoring-config-bkp.yaml ~~~ Next, update the cluster-monitoring-config ConfigMap by replacing the existing `K8sPrometheusAdapter` configuration with the metricsServer configuration. ~~~ $ oc edit cm cluster-monitoring-config-n openshift-monitoring metricsServer: nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: '' tolerations:- key: "node.ocs.openshift.io/storage" operator: "Equal" value: "true" effect: "NoSchedule" ~~~
root_cause: As the Prometheus Adapter is [deprecated from 4.16](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes.html#ocp-4-16-monitoring-metrics-server-to-access-metrics-api-ga), It's replaced by the [Metrics Server component](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.16/observability/monitoring/config-map-reference-for-the-cluster-monitoring-operator.html#metricsserverconfig).

title: ManagedCluster becomes unknown after upgrading MCE
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: ManagedCluster becomes unknown after upgrading MCE
resolution: 1. Check the current generation of the klusterlet ManifestWork. Run the following command on the hub cluster: ``` oc-n get manifestwork-klusterlet-o jsonpath='{.metadata.generation}' ``` Assume the current generation is M. 2. Delete the secrets in the cluster namespace on the hub: First delete the secret containing the bootstrap token that has the legacy-token-invalid-since label (its name begins with-bootstrap-sa-token-). Then delete the-import secret. 3. Verify the klusterlet ManifestWork has been refreshed. After a new bootstrap token is generated automatically, check the new generation: ``` oc-n get manifestwork-klusterlet-o jsonpath='{.metadata.generation}' ``` The new generation (N) should be greater than M. 4. Wait for the updated ManifestWork to be applied. Run the following and make sure the output becomes Generation: N, Applied: True: ``` oc-n get manifestwork-klusterlet \-o jsonpath="{range.status.conditions[?(@.type=='Applied')]}{'Generation: '}{.observedGeneration}{', Applied: '}{.status}{'\n'}{end}" ``` Note: Try these steps on one managed cluster first. If the cluster remains in the Available state for the next 10 minutes, it should be safe to proceed with other clusters. ``` oc get managedcluster-o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="ManagedClusterConditionAvailable")].status}' ```
root_cause: * MCE does not handle cases where the [token is expired](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-27180), only if the token was deleted

title: InitContainer does not run for DaemonSet pod after node reboot in OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - A DaemonSet pod's initContainer fails to execute following a node reboot.- The pod uptime (Age) is observed to be longer than the actual uptime of the node it is running on.- Application containers within the DaemonSet pod may fail or behave incorrectly because the prerequisite tasks in the initContainer were skipped.- The pod status remains Running even though the node was recently restarted.
resolution: To ensure initContainers always run after a node reboot, the pod must be transitioned to a new lifecycle. Use one of the following methods: Method 1: Delete the Stale Pod--- Manually deleting the pod will force the DaemonSet controller to create a new pod object, which guarantees the execution of initContainers. Identify the stale pod: `oc get pods-o wide` Delete the pod: `oc delete pod-n ` Method 2: Implement a Readiness Probe--- Adding a readinessProbe to the main application container can help the cluster detect when a pod is not actually "Ready" after a reboot, although this may not always trigger an initContainer re-run without a full pod restart. For more information on readinessProbes, see: [Understanding health checks- OpenShift Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/building_applications/application-health#application-health-about_application-health)
root_cause: This behavior occurs because DaemonSet pods have default tolerations for node.kubernetes.io/not-ready and node.kubernetes.io/unreachable. When a node reboots: The API server maintains the pod's state as "Running" because the pod is not evicted. If the kubelet restarts and finds the pod record in the API server marked as Initialized: True, it may attempt to start the application containers directly, skipping the initContainers. The discrepancy in "uptime" occurs because the startTime in the pod metadata reflects the original creation time from before the reboot.

title: Can I define maintenance windows for scheduled updates in OpenShift Container Platform?
issue: - Is there a way to define a maintenance window in OpenShift for scheduling cluster or operator updates?- Can I schedule an update to start at a specific date and time automatically?- Does OCP have a native "Maintenance Window" object for self-managed clusters?- We need to restrict update operations to specific hours to comply with company policies.
resolution: Currently, self-managed OpenShift Container Platform does not have a native "Maintenance Window" feature or a built-in scheduler to trigger cluster-wide updates at a specific future time. Red Hat is tracking this requirement through a Request for Enhancement (RFE). See the Root Cause section for more details. As a Workaround Administrators can control the timing of update applications using the following methods: ### 1. Manual Initiation The most common practice is to trigger the update manually during a planned maintenance window via the Web Console or the CLI. Start the update: oc adm upgrade--to= The Cluster Version Operator (CVO) will begin the process immediately. *Note that once approved, the CVO managed updates will run until complete; it is not possible to stop a CVO operator upgrade once started. However, the node updates and reboots can be managed. For that, see item 2 below* ### 2. Pausing Machine Config Pools (MCP) To prevent nodes from rebooting or applying new configurations until a specific window, you can "pause" the MCPs. This allows the update to download and the Control Plane to update, but stalls the worker node rollout. 1. Pause the pool: `oc patch mcp/worker--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'` 2. Perform the cluster update. The nodes will stay at the old version while the pool is paused. 3. Unpause during the maintenance window: `oc patch mcp/worker--type merge--patch '{"spec":{"paused":false}}'` ### 3. Operator Maintenance Windows For operators managed by the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), you can switch the Approval strategy to Manual. 1. Edit the Subscription for the operator. 2. Set spec.installPlanApproval to Manual. 3. During your maintenance window, manually approve the generated InstallPlan. *Note that once approved, the update will run until complete; it is not possible to stop a OLM operator upgrade once started*
root_cause: OpenShift Container Platform currently follows an "immediate execution" model for updates once they are initiated. The ability to define a native maintenance window schedule is a known feature request. If you're interested in finding out more, or would like to request this, please raise a case with Red Hat Support and reference the following Request for Enhancement (RFE): [OCPSTRAT-1695](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPSTRAT-1695)

title: Releasing Disk Space in OpenShift Mirror registry/Quay
issue: - using oc-mirror with updated imageset removes the images:tag but disk space isn't released- manually cleaning up images in mirror registry via the Quay UI when using `--skip-prune` with oc-mirror does not free up disk space.
resolution: * For existing organisations, modify the `Timemachine setting to "few seconds"` from the drop down available in organization settings for a particular organization. Delete the tags or a repo using Quay UI, and within sometime the disk space is released. * To Globally set the Timemachine setting to "few seconds"(0s) or 1m or any certain period so it's applied to new organizations created later on(Optional): **NOTE**: The procedure to modify config.yaml described here assumes that Mirror registry has been installed under root user. If Mirror registry has been installed as the particular user(rootless), the location of the unit file is under `/home/user_name/.config/systemd/user` and most likely the location of the config files will differ from what is written here. However, all other steps will remain the same. 1) Shut down the mirror registry instance ~~~ # systemctl stop quay-app.service ~~~ 2) config.yaml for mirror registry resides in the directory that bind mounts to `/quay-registry/conf/stack` directory inside the container. The location on the disk can be read from Quay's SystemD unit file: ~~~ # cat /etc/systemd/system/quay-app.service | grep-i conf-v /path/to/quay-install/quay-config:/quay-registry/conf/stack:Z \ ~~~ 3) Modify the config.yaml under path `/path/to/quay-install/quay-config` with below to remove the tag within 1m after deleting it from UI: ~~~ DEFAULT_TAG_EXPIRATION: 1m <---- modified from 2w to 1m TAG_EXPIRATION_OPTIONS:- 0s- 1m <---- add 1m- 1d- 1w- 2w- 4w ~~~ This sets the default expiration (Timemachine setting) globally to 1m and this is auto applied to newly created organizations. 4) Restart mirror registry by running: ~~~ # systemctl start quay-app.service ~~~ The service should start momentarily and one can track the startup process by running `journalctl-u quay-app.service-f`. After 60-90 seconds, mirror registry should be available.
root_cause: Due to the default Timemachine setting of 2 weeks, the tags deleted aren't garbage collected until 2 weeks and will be available for restoration in the tag history for 2 weeks. The Quay documentation explains the [Garbage Collection](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_quay/3.8/html-single/manage_red_hat_quay/index#garbage-collection-practice), which also details how images are stored in the backend.

title: Cluster update is completed, but one or more Cluster Operators have failed to be updated
issue: - The cluster was successfully updated, but one or more Cluster Operators (COs) are still in the previous version. ``` $ oc get clusterversion NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING SINCE STATUS version 4.16.45 True False 26m Cluster version is 4.16.45 oc get clusterversion version-o json | jq-r '.status.history[0]' {"completionTime": "2026-01-08T16:29:03Z", "image": "quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release@sha256:6d097cefdcc369ba328e25fdfbfcdeaabcecad38be4b3c12a99f2222f384a31c", "startedTime": "2026-01-08T15:28:00Z", "state": "Completed", < < < < The update is completed "verified": false, "version": "4.16.45"} $ oc get co | grep-Ev 4.16.45 NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE node-tuning 4.12.60 True False False 329d < < < < This CO is still in a previous version. ```
resolution: - If the `baselineCapabilitySet` is set to **None**, ensure that all installed capabilities are included in the `additionalEnabledCapabilities`. If any are missing, use the `oc edit clusterversion version` to add them in the `.spec.capabilities.additionalEnabledCapabilities` list.- If the `baselineCapabilitySet` is set to a **specific version** please refer to the Documentation [Cluster capabilities](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html/installation_overview/cluster-capabilities#enabling-cluster-capabilities_cluster-capabilities) to review the profile and adjust as require, or add the missing Capabilities in the `additionalEnabledCapabilities` list.
root_cause: When setting the `baselineCapabilitySet` to `None` the cluster will not use any specific profile, and only manage the capabilities that are listed in the `additionalEnabledCapabilities` list. If during the cluster installation, one of the capability was installed but removed from the `additionalEnabledCapabilities` list this capability is no longer manager by the cluster. Similar behavior will occurs if the `baselineCapabilitySet` is modified to different profile overtime.

title: Does removing the cluster wide proxy cause node reboot in OCP 4?
issue: - Need to understand the impact of removing / modifying the cluster-wide proxy configuration in OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) 4. Specifically:- Will this trigger a reboot of cluster nodes?- Can the rollout of changes be controlled to minimize application impact?
resolution: - Removing or modifying the cluster-wide Proxy object generates a new MachineConfig.- The Machine Config Operator (MCO) applies the new MachineConfig by draining and rebooting nodes in the affected MachineConfigPools (MCPs).- Node reboots will occur as part of this rollout. By default, the MCO handles it sequentially (one node at a time).- Options to minimize impact: 1. Pause/unpause MCPs: You can pause the MCP before removing the proxy to prevent immediate rollout, and unpause later when ready. 2. Use multiple MCPs: Group worker nodes into different MCPs (for example, based on workloads or availability zones). This allows you to pause/unpause pools independently, controlling the order and timing of node reboots. 3. Tuning the MCP `spec.maxUnavailable` setting controls how many nodes in a pool can reboot simultaneously.
root_cause: - The proxy configuration is rendered into the node’s MachineConfig (e.g., CRI-O environment, registries.conf). Any change to the proxy object modifies the rendered MachineConfig, which requires a node reboot to apply.

title: Argo CD status.operationState.syncResult is inconsistent for ClusterInstance resources during GitOps deployments
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: Automation scripts relying on status.operationState.syncResult[] in Argo CD Applications fail to detect the creation of ClusterInstance resources or incorrectly detect stale "Pruned" resources. This behavior is primarily observed during parallel redeployments of Single Node OpenShift (SNO) clusters using Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (RHACM). Symptoms:- A ClusterInstance is successfully created in the cluster, but it does not appear in the syncResult array of the Argo CD Application status.- The syncResult continues to show "Pruned" entries for resources that were deleted in previous commits.- Automation scripts checking for resource existence via syncResult exit with errors, despite the underlying deployment progressing correctly.
resolution: The field status.operationState.syncResult[] is a historical record of actions attempted during a specific sync operation; it is not a real-time authoritative view of the resources existing in the cluster. To resolve this in automation and deployment workflows, implement the following changes: 1. **Use Authoritative Fields**: Modify automation scripts to validate resource existence using.status.resources[] within the Argo CD Application or by querying the API directly via oc get clusterinstance-n. 2. **Adjust Prune Propagation**: If stale prune entries are causing timing issues, change the Application's PrunePropagationPolicy to foreground. This ensures Argo CD does not consider the sync complete until the resource (including finalizers) is fully removed from the API server. 3. **Implement Fallback Logic**: If using status.resources[] fails to return the expected result immediately, implement a retry loop that queries the ClusterInstance CR directly, as the SiteConfig controller may still be processing the request asynchronously.
root_cause: The inconsistency is caused by a shift in resource ownership and reporting between the legacy SiteConfig (v1) and the new ClusterInstance (v2) workflows:- **Asynchronous Orchestration**: In the ClusterInstance workflow, Argo CD only manages the top-level ClusterInstance Custom Resource (CR). The actual provisioning of sub-resources (InfraEnv, BareMetalHost, etc.) is handled asynchronously by the SiteConfig controller.- **Sync Reporting Semantics**: status.operationState.syncResult reflects only the actions (Create, Sync, Prune) performed during the transition from the previous state to the current state. If a resource was not modified during a particular sync, it may not appear in this specific array.- **Prune Background Policy**: By default, many applications use PrunePropagationPolicy=background. Argo CD marks a resource as "Pruned" as soon as the delete request is issued. It does not wait for the controller to finish cleanup, leading to a discrepancy between the Argo CD status and the actual cluster state.

title: Network Interface Not Automatically Activated After Migrating RHEL 9 VM from VMware to OCP
issue: After migration of RHEL 9 virtual machine from VMware to OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) the VM’s network interface is not automatically activated, and requires manual intervention to bring up the network.
resolution: To address this issue, follow the below two methods Option #1: Updating NetworkManager configuration to match the network interfaces Option #2: Updating network interfaces to match the NetworkManager configuration For more detail configuration, please refer to the following link. [Red Hat Blog](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/openshift-virtualization-networking-for-vsphere-migration)
root_cause: Red Hat OpenShift handles networking in a different way, by using a dedicated pod network for microservices, with software-defined load balancers (called services) in front of the applications. These services are available within the cluster and can be exposed by a route with a DNS name to other applications and users outside the OpenShift cluster. One of the benefits of this method is that the specific network configuration of any particular microservice, such as its IP address, becomes irrelevant. The OpenShift cluster and service manages those relationships. However, traditional virtual machines do not necessarily fit into the OpenShift way of doing things, certainly not when the priority is to lift and shift the workloads from VMware to OpenShift Virtualization. Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the underlying Linux kernel use a variety of different rules to name a network interface card (NIC). For example, a RHEL 9 server running on VMware may have a network adapter using the VMXNET driver that udev calls ens192, as in this example: ~~~ # ip link 1: lo: mtu 65536 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/loopback 00:00:00:00:00:00 brd 00:00:00:00:00:00 2: ensXXX: mtu 1400 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/ether 00:50:56:af:23:16 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff ~~~ But after using a tool such as the Migration Toolkit for Virtualization to move to OpenShift Virtualization, the same server might use the VirtIO driver and boot with a network adapter name called enpYYY, as in this example: ~~~ # ip link 1: lo: mtu 65536 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/loopback 00:00:00:00:00:00 brd 00:00:00:00:00:00 2: enpYYY: mtu 1400 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/ether 00:50:56:af:23:16 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff ~~~ If you do nothing to prepare for the migration, then your migrated virtual machine has no access to the network because it's unable to find the network adapter it was initially using. This means the virtual machine administrator must log in to the console of every migrated virtual machine and manually change its network configuration.

title: SR-IOV VF MAC Address resets to 00:00:00:00:00:00 post reboot
issue: - Wy are `SR-IOV` `VF`s (Virtual Functions) failing to initialise as expected after a reboot with their `MAC` address visible as below? ~~~ ip link show vf 0 link/ether 00:00:00:00:00:00 ~~~- The `SR-IOV` application pods cannot communicate using the attached `VF`s.
resolution: ***Unsupported Procedure**: The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and supported procedures. The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the Operating System unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. This article intends to provide information to accomplish the system's needs.*- Preloading the `iavf` driver during the early boot sequence in the `initramfs` stage using kernel argument `rd.driver.pre` resolves this timing issue. This ensures the driver is ready as soon as the hardware is available.- Deploy [Node Tuning Operator](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/scalability_and_performance/using-node-tuning-operator#about-node-tuning-operator_node-tuning-operator "Chapter 10. Using the Node Tuning Operator") and create a `PerformanceProfile` with the below kernel argument added under `spec.additionalKernelArgs` to make the configuration persistent. ~~~ spec: additionalKernelArgs:- "rd.driver.pre=iavf" ~~~ #### Workaround **WARNING**: This is an unsupported method. This approach should only be considered after verifying the logs mentioned in `Diagnostic Steps` and the `PerformanceProfile` cannot be considered.- [Add the `rd.driver.pre=iavf` kernel argument to RHOCP node](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6891971 "How to add or remove kernel argument from RHCOS node in RHOCP 4") using below command. ~~~ # rpm-ostree kargs--append='rd.driver.pre=iavf' ~~~
root_cause: - The issue is caused by a race condition where the `iavf` driver is loaded too late in the `RHEL CoreOS` boot process to properly coordinate with the Physical Function (PF).- With some Intel NIC/adapters it has been observed that during the `RHEL CoreOS` boot the Intel `ice` driver initializes the `PF`, but the `iavf` driver may not load in time to initialize the `VF` to receive the `MAC` address assignment before the `SR-IOV Network Operator` and later the application pod attempts to bind the VF.- By the time application pod starts, the VF remains in an uninitialized state with a zeroed `MAC` address.

title: Can a RHOCP 4 cluster be restored using VMware snapshots?
issue: - Master and worker node VMware backup files are available. Can these backup files be used to restore the RHOCP cluster to the previous healthy state?
resolution: - Restoring a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) 4 cluster or node from Virtual Machine snapshots or backups is not supported.- For the supported backup and recovery procedures, please refer to the [Backing up and restoring etcd guide](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/backup_and_restore/index).
root_cause: While technically possible if all VMs are perfectly synchronized at the exact same moment, restoring from snapshots is unreliable for distributed systems. * Etcd Consistency: The etcd key-value store requires strict data consistency. VM restorations frequently lead to database corruption or "split-brain" issues where nodes diverge. * Volume Integrity: Application data on Persistent Volumes may not match the memory state of the restored VMs, leading to filesystem corruption. * SDN/IPAM State Mismatch: OpenShift SDN plugins rely on etcd for IP Address Management (IPAM). Restoring to a previous state desynchronizes the IPAM database from the actual running workloads. This causes the SDN to assign duplicate IP addresses to new pods (IPs that are physically still in use but "forgotten" by the restored database), resulting in IP conflicts and severe network instability. Because of these risks, environments restored via this method are considered unvalidated and outside the scope of support.

title: Forbidden error when listing namespaces in RHOCP 4
issue: - A permissions error occurs when attempting to list `namespaces` in an OpenShift cluster. ~~~ Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces is forbidden: User "example-user" cannot list resource "namespaces" in API group "" at the cluster scope ~~~
resolution: - To allow listing `namespaces` at the cluster scope, create a `ClusterRole` and `ClusterRoleBinding` with the minimum required permissions. This requires an account with elevated privileges, such as `cluster-admin`. #### Example 1: Grant permissions to a user. To grant permissions to a `user`, proceed with the following steps: 1. Create a `ClusterRole` that grants `namespace` access: ~~~ $ oc create clusterrole namespace-access--verb=get,list,watch--resource=namespaces ~~~ 2. Binding the `ClusterRole` to a specific `user` grants the associated permissions to that `user` account: ~~~ $ oc create clusterrolebinding namespace-access-binding--clusterrole=namespace-access--user= ~~~ #### Example 2: Grant permissions to a group. To grant permissions to a `group`, proceed with the following steps: 1. Create a `ClusterRole` that grants `namespace` access: ~~~ $ oc create clusterrole namespace-access--verb=get,list,watch--resource=namespaces ~~~ 2. Binding the `ClusterRole` to a `group` grants the associated permissions to all members of that `group`: ~~~ $ oc create clusterrolebinding namespace-access-binding--clusterrole=namespace-access--group= ~~~
root_cause: By default, listing all `namespaces` is restricted to `cluster-admin` `roles`. Consequently, it is necessary to create and bind a specific `role` to provide the required permissions.

title: Red Hat Quay 3 undetectable 500 Errors on Main Page.

Health endpoint returns 200 and indicates all services are operational even during error occurrences. ~~~ gunicorn-web stdout | conn =_connect(dsn, connection_factory=connection_factory, **kwasync) gunicorn-web stdout | peewee.OperationalError: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for roles with the SUPERUSER attribute ~~~

title: Cluster upgrade stuck with the useUnsupportedUnsafeNonHANonProductionUnstableEtcd error in RHOCP
issue: - OpenShift Upgrade stuck with the error: ~~~ clusteroperator/etcd is not upgradeable because UnsupportedConfigOverridesUpgradeable: setting: [useUnsupportedUnsafeNonHANonProductionUnstableEtcd] ~~~
resolution: The next steps will not trigger: * an etcd pod restart * not new rendered machine config (MC) will be created for the control-plane/masters, then, the nodes will not be restarted 1. Ensure that `unsupportedConfigOverrides` contains only the relevant override for this issue (useUnsupportedUnsafeNonHANonProductionUnstableEtcd) ~~~ $ oc get etcd/cluster-o jsonpath='{.spec.unsupportedConfigOverrides}' {"useUnsupportedUnsafeNonHANonProductionUnstableEtcd":true} ~~~ 2. If `useUnsupportedUnsafeNonHANonProductionUnstableEtcd` is the only override in place, then the entire `unsupportedConfigOverrides` section can be removed from etcd operator: ~~~ $ oc patch etcd/cluster--type json-p '[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/unsupportedConfigOverrides"}]' ~~~
root_cause: Using the `unsupportedConfigOverrides` section to modify the configuration of an Operator is unsupported and might block cluster updates. You must remove this setting before you can update your cluster. All the details in the Red Hat Knowledge Documentation: "[Updating clusters](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html-single/updating_clusters/index#prerequisites)"

title: etcd member in CrashLoopBackOff state with message: "wal: max entry size limit exceeded"
issue: - etcd member goes into `CrashLoopBackOff` state.- etcd operator turns into `Degraded` state with message: `wal: max entry size limit exceeded`.
resolution: This is a known issue which has been worked by Engineering in bug [OCPBUGS-5458](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-5458), and fixed in the following releases: Target Minor Release | Bug | Fixed Version | Errata--- |--- 4.13 | [OCPBUGS-5458](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-5458)|**4.13.0**|[RHSA-2023:1326](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:1326) 4.12 | [OCPBUGS-5761](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-5761)|**4.12.1**|[RHSA-2023:0449](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0449) 4.11 | [OCPBUGS-5876](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-5876)|**4.11.26**|[RHSA-2023:0565](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0565) 4.10 | [OCPBUGS-5950](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-5950)|**4.10.51**|[RHSA-2023:0561](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0561) 4.9 | [OCPBUGS-6516](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-6516)|**4.9.56**|[RHSA-2023:0778](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2023:0778) ### Workarounds Any operation that rotates the etcd WAL should help to mitigate the issue: * Trigger a new snapshot on the failed member. This can be achieved by running the `/usr/local/bin/cluster-backup.sh` script. Refer to the [backing up etcd data](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.10/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#backing-up-etcd-data_backup-etcd) documentation for additional information. ~~~ sh-4.4# /usr/local/bin/cluster-backup.sh /home/core/assets/backup ~~~ * Compact the etcd to latest revision as it is explained in [how to compact and defrag etcd to decrease database size in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5564771). > **Note:** if the etcd pods is not automatically restored after some time, try restarting the failing etcd pod after following any of the above procedures. * Restore the failing etcd member from a snapshot as explained in [restoring to a previous cluster state](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.10/html-single/backup_and_restore/index#dr-restoring-cluster-state) (note that a recent etcd backup is required for this). If none of the above workarounds work, then the recommended step would be to [replace the unhealthy etcd member](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.10/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member). Note that there was a bug in older versions listed in [etcd restore process failed to recreate the master `secrets`](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6992693), please review it carefully before following the replace procedure.
