title: How to Rebuild NooBaa in Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) 4.x?
issue: The db-noobaa-db-0 PVC was deleted, due to which Backingstores went into NotReady state. How can I get noobaa working?
Installation of openshift-storage/noobaa-default-backing-store fails with an AUTH error stating "account not found".
When OCS Operator is stuck at "Installing State" while Object Storage resources are not detected.
When the Noobaa management endpoint is accessible but no configuration is found (Noobaa Web GUI indicates the need to create a user as the system is not ready).

When the OCS operator is running 0/1 pods. ~~~ time="2021-03-18T08:42:07Z" level=warning msg="RPC: GetConnection creating connection to wss://noobaa-mgmt.openshift-storage.svc.cluster.local:443/rpc/ 0xc00059acd0" time="2021-03-18T08:42:07Z" level=info msg="RPC: Connecting websocket (0xc00059acd0) ReconnectDelay:0s}" time="2021-03-18T08:42:07Z" level=info msg="RPC: Connected websocket (0xc00059acd0) ReconnectDelay:0s}" time="2021-03-18T08:42:07Z" level=error msg="⚠️ RPC: system.read_system() Response Error: Code=UNAUTHORIZED Message=account not found 5e96a72c498f080030a76337" ~~~
resolution: **WARNING:** The solution below involves the **deletion and recreation** of **ALL** of noobaa resources, which means **ALL data inside noobaa buckets will be lost**. Doing this means **ALL** Noobaa resources will be gone. Please reach out Red Hat Technical Support (sbr-ocs) team for a review of cluster before applying the changes outlined in this KCS. # Steps for ODF versions 4.11+ 1. Patch and Deletion Commands: ``` $ oc patch-n openshift-storage noobaa noobaa--type='merge'-p '{"spec":{"cleanupPolicy":{"allowNoobaaDeletion":true}}}' ``` 2. Delete NooBaa/Multcloud Gateway (MCG): ``` $ oc delete-n openshift-storage noobaas.noobaa.io--all ``` If there are existing buckets the above step will hang. If the command hangs, please do the following **in a separate terminal window** ~~~ $ oc patch-n openshift-storage noobaas/noobaa--type=merge-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":null}}' ~~~ 3. After waiting some time for the termination/re-creation of all NooBaa resources validate the new age of all MCG resources with the following command: ``` oc get pv,deployment,pods,sts-n openshift-storage|grep noobaa ``` **Note**: The above steps won't delete any custom backingstore, custom bucketclass, custom noobaa storageclass, obc, ob. You need to delete them manually: 4. Delete existing OBC, that should delete the associated OB and secret. Then recreate new OBC with the same name as before (in the same namespaces as before), that will create a new OB, noobaa bucket and new secret with new AWS credentials. Thew new values will need to be configured on the applications that were using noobaa buckets. Example with only one OBC "test-todelete" on namespace "openshift-storage" ``` % oc get obc-A NAMESPACE NAME STORAGE-CLASS PHASE AGE openshift-storage test-todelete openshift-storage.noobaa.io Bound 81s % oc get secret test-todelete-n openshift-storage NAME TYPE DATA AGE test-todelete Opaque 2 116s % oc get ob NAME STORAGE-CLASS CLAIM-NAMESPACE CLAIM-NAME RECLAIM-POLICY PHASE AGE obc-openshift-storage-test-todelete openshift-storage.noobaa.io Delete Bound 2m22s % oc-n openshift-storage delete obc test-todelete objectbucketclaim.objectbucket.io "test-todelete" deleted % After that we can see that these resources are gone: % oc get obc-A No resources found % oc get ob No resources found % oc get secret test-todelete-n openshift-storage Error from server (NotFound): secrets "test-todelete" not found ``` ## For OCS/ODF versions 4.10 and below: **Follow the below steps to safely recreate noobaa system in OCS/ODF versions 4.10 and below**: * For ODF version 4.9+, scale down the odf-operator-controller-manager, ocs operator, and noobaa-operator: ~~~ $ oc scale deployment odf-operator-controller-manager ocs-operator noobaa-operator--replicas=0 ~~~ * Delete the noobaa deployments\statefulsets. ** NOTE: For OCS 4.7.x+ the statefulset is called 'noobaa-db-pg' ~~~ $ oc delete deployments.apps noobaa-endpoint $ oc delete statefulsets.apps noobaa-db noobaa-core ~~~ * Delete the PVC db-noobaa-db-0 ** NOTE: For OCS 4.7.x+ the PVC is called 'db-noobaa-db-pg-0' ~~~ $ oc delete pvc db-noobaa-db-0 ~~~ * Delete the backingstores and bucket-class. ~~~ $ oc delete bucketclasses.noobaa.io,backingstores.noobaa.io--all NOTE: You might need to remove finalizers for the two resources in order for the deletion to complete. Run the following patch commands if this is true: $ oc patch backingstore/noobaa-default-backing-store-n openshift-storage--type=merge-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":null}}' $ oc patch bucketclass/noobaa-default-bucket-class-n openshift-storage--type=merge-p '{"metadata": {"finalizers":null}}' ~~~ * Delete the noobaa secrets. Note: If an external KMS is being used, we can skip the removal of the "noobaa-root-master-key" By default, the NooBaa master root secret is stored in the k8s secret named 'noobaa-root-master-key'. However, if an external KMS is defined in the NooBaa system CR, the master root key will instead be stored in the specified backend, and the 'noobaa-root-master-key' secret will not be created by the operator. ~~~ $ oc delete secrets noobaa-admin noobaa-endpoints noobaa-operator noobaa-server noobaa-root-master-key ~~~ * Restart ocs-operator by setting the replicas back to 1. ~~~ $ oc scale deployment ocs-operator--replicas=1 ~~~ * For ODF version 4.9+, scale up the odf-operator-controller-manager operator as an additional step: ~~~ $ oc scale deployment odf-operator-controller-manager--replicas=1 ~~~ * Restart noobaa-operator by setting the replicas back to 1. ~~~ $ oc scale deployment noobaa-operator--replicas=1 ~~~ The operator should start a fresh install of noobaa system. * Monitor the pods in openshift-storage for noobaa pods to be Running. Also check for the status of backingstore/bucketclass. ~~~ $ oc get pods,backingstore,bucketclass-n openshift-storage-o wide ~~~ Both should be in Ready status. **Note**: In case the rebuilding of noobaa is stuck or not progressing try to delete the **noobaa** Custom resource while deleting the other resources. ~~~ $ oc delete noobaa noobaa ~~~
root_cause: * The noobaa DB holds all of noobaa's metadata- system configurations, authentication info, buckets info, and objects metadata. Deleting the PV would mean losing the entire data, and only a rebuild can bring noobaa to Ready status. * The "Code=UNAUTHORIZED Message=account not found" messages are seen due to account information missing from the noobaa-db.

title: ImageSetConfiguration for oc-mirror v2
issue: How to find available operators using plugin `oc-mirror` version 2.
How to configure ImageSetConfiguration to mirror operators with `oc-mirror' version 2.
resolution: [Get operator information](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/how-oc-mirror-will-help-you-reduce-container-management-complexity). ~~~ a. Login OperatorHub catalogs $ podman login registry.redhat.io b. Find the available catalogs for the target version. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalogs--version=4.11 Available OpenShift OperatorHub catalogs: OpenShift 4.11: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11 registry.redhat.io/redhat/certified-operator-index:v4.11 registry.redhat.io/redhat/community-operator-index:v4.11 registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-marketplace-index:v4.11 c. Find the available packages within the selected catalog. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11 > package.out $ cat package.out NAME DISPLAY NAME DEFAULT CHANNEL 3scale-operator Red Hat Integration- 3scale- Managed Application Services threescale-mas [···] d. Find channels for the selected package. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11--package=cluster-logging NAME DISPLAY NAME DEFAULT CHANNEL cluster-logging Red Hat OpenShift Logging stable PACKAGE CHANNEL HEAD cluster-logging stable cluster-logging.5.5.5 cluster-logging stable-5.3 cluster-logging.5.3.9 cluster-logging stable-5.4 cluster-logging.5.4.9 cluster-logging stable-5.5 cluster-logging.5.5.5 or $ for i in cluster-logging elasticsearch-operator; do oc-mirror list operators-- catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11--package=$i; done e. Find package versions within the selected channel. $ oc-mirror list operators--catalog=registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11-- package=elasticsearch-operator--channel=stable-5.5 VERSIONS 5.5.5 ~~~ 4. [Configuring credentials](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#installation-adding-registry-pull-secret_installing-mirroring-disconnected) that allow images to be mirrored. ~~~ a. Download pull-secret(https://console.redhat.com/openshift/install/pull-secret). b. Add local Image Registry credentials to the pull-secret. $ MIRROR_REGISTRY=docker.registry.example.net:5000 $ podman login ${MIRROR_REGISTRY} $ podman login--authfile /root/pull-secret ${MIRROR_REGISTRY} c. Save the file either as ~/.docker/config.json or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json. $ cat /root/pull-secret | jq. > ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json $ cat ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json {"auths": {"cloud.openshift.com": {"auth": "xxxxxx...", "email": "you@example.com"}, "docker.registry.example.net:5000": {"auth": "xxxxxx" [···] ~~~ 5. Creating the [imageset configuration](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#oc-mirror-imageset-config-params_installing-mirroring-disconnected). **Note:** When running the `oc-mirror` plugin again, images gets [pruned](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#oc-mirror-updating-registry-about_installing-mirroring-disconnected) automatically from the target mirror registry if they are no longer included in the latest `imageset` that was generated and mirrored. ~~~ $ cat > imageset-config.yaml < < EOF apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL: ${MIRROR_REGISTRY}/mirror/metadata # <-- Do not delete or modify metadata generated by the oc-mirror plugin, use the same storage backend every time run the oc-mirror plugin for the same mirror registry. skipTLS: false mirror: operators:- catalog: registry.redhat.io/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11 # <-- Set the Operator catalog packages:- name: cluster-logging # <-- Operator name channels: # <-- Specify channel and version- name: stable # <-- Default Channel- name: stable-5.5 # <-- Target Channel- If the expected Channel is different from the Default Channel, need to set the Target Channel after setting the Default Channel minVersion: '5.5.5' # <-- If the first field of the set value is a number, need to add ' '. maxVersion: '5.5.5'- name: elasticsearch-operator channels:- name: stable- name: stable-5.5 minVersion: '5.5.5' maxVersion: '5.5.5'- name: cincinnati-operator channels:- name: v1 minVersion: v5.0.0 maxVersion: v5.0.0- name: kubernetes-nmstate-operator channels:- name: stable- name: '4.11' minVersion: '4.11.0-202212070335' maxVersion: '4.11.0-202212070335' EOF ~~~ 6. [Mirroring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#mirroring-image-set-partial) an imageset to a mirror registry. ~~~ $ oc mirror--config=./imageset-config.yaml \ docker://${MIRROR_REGISTRY}--dest-skip-tls ··· info: Mirroring completed in 1m57.76s (40.22MB/s) Rendering catalog image "docker.registry.example.net:5000/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.11" with file-based catalog Writing image mapping to oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047/mapping.txt Writing CatalogSource manifests to oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047 Writing ICSP manifests to oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047 # <-- This path is used in subsequent steps to create icsp and catalogsource ~~~ 7. Create `imageContentSourcePolicy` and `catalogsource`. ~~~ $ ls oc-mirror-workspace/results-1670920047 catalogSource-redhat-operator-index.yaml charts imageContentSourcePolicy.yaml mapping.txt release-signatures $ oc create-f imageContentSourcePolicy.yaml imagecontentsourcepolicy.operator.openshift.io/operator-0 created $ oc create-f catalogSource-redhat-operator-index.yaml catalogsource.operators.coreos.com/redhat-operator-index create ~~~ 8. Verify that the operator download is complete. ~~~ $ oc get catalogsource-n openshift-marketplace NAME DISPLAY TYPE PUBLISHER AGE redhat-operator-index grpc 13s $ oc get packagemanifest-n openshift-marketplace NAME CATALOG AGE cluster-logging 33s cincinnati-operator 33s elasticsearch-operator 33s kubernetes-nmstate-operator 33s ~~~ * If it is a completely disconnected environment, `storageConfig.local.path` needs to be set instead of `storageConfig.registry.imageURL` to [mirror the imageset to disk with the metadata, then mirror the imageset file on disk to a mirror](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.11/installing/disconnected_install/installing-mirroring-disconnected.html#mirroring-image-set-full). ~~~ apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: registry: imageURL: ${MIRROR_REGISTRY}/mirror/metadata ***Change it to*** apiVersion: mirror.openshift.io/v1alpha2 kind: ImageSetConfiguration storageConfig: local: path: /home/user/metadata ~~~ **Note:** Do not delete or modify metadata generated by the `oc-mirror` plugin, use the same storage backend every time run the `oc-mirror` plugin for the same mirror registry.

title: Pod restarts with OOMKilled post migration of application to OpenShift 4.16
issue: - The application is down due to pod restart post migration of application to OpenShift 4.16 or higher with `OOMKilled` messages: ~~~ kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason test-project https-main kube-state-metrics single-api-platform testing openshift-monitoring/k8s OOMKilled kube-state-metrics xxx None ~~~
resolution: Increase the pod memory `limits` as per real application usage.
root_cause: Starting with OpenShift 4.14, [Linux Control Groups version 2 is now default for new installations](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes#ocp-4-14-nodes-cgroupv2-default), and starting with OpenShift 4.16 [Linux Control Groups version 1 is now deprecated](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/release_notes/ocp-4-16-release-notes#ocp-4-14-nodes-cgroupv1-deprecated_release-notes) and the default mode is cgroup v2 for new deployments. As the cgroups v1 interface differs from cgroups v2 (e.g.: cgroupsv1: `memory.limit_in_bytes` VS cgroupsv2: `memory.max`), there could be differences in the memory used, specially if the `limit` was too tight adjusted before.

title: OpenShift 4 node with cgroup out of memory and oom-kill errors
issue: OpenShift 4 node is going to `NotReady` state and is getting unresponsive.
There are "`Memory cgroup out of memory`" and "`oom-kill`" messages in the node.
resolution: Increasing the memory resource limit for the failing pod(s) is required. Check the Diagnostic Steps section for identifying the affected pods.
root_cause: Memory `cgroup` OOM messages for containers reaching the configured `limit`. When this occurs, other processes from the pod could become *uninterruptible sleep processes* (`D` state processes).

title: Failure to Connect to EDPM Nodes using SSH Keys in RHOSO

Delete the osdpd. 3. Create a new key pair and secret. 4. Provision the nodes again. 5. Deploy dataplane again.

title: How to Export/Import Placement Group (PG) Data and/or Examine the State of an Object Storage Daemon (OSD) using the Ceph ObjectStore Tool in OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) v4.x
issue: - How to export/import PGs from OSD disk?- How to import PGs to OSD daemon to recover `Incomplete` PGs? **CAUTION: These steps typically involve the Engineering team via bug case/Jira and have provided approval to accomplish the process.**
resolution: 1. Backup the OSD deployment: ```$ oc get deployment-n openshift-storage rook-ceph-osd--o yaml > rook-ceph-osd-.yaml``` 2. Patch the deployment with a sleep loop. This will allow the OSD to come 1/2 to start an OSD in maintenance mode. **WARNING: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO EXPORT/IMPORT PGs WHEN THE OSD IS RUNNING 2/2 AND IS UP/IN Ceph.** $ oc-n openshift-storage patch deployment rook-ceph-osd--p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name": "osd", "command": ["sleep", "infinity"], "args": []}]}}}}' # Export: 3. Wait for the OSD pod to restart and come to a `1/2` `Ready` state: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage ~~~ 4. Login to the pod to access OSD data directory mount path: ~~~ $ oc rsh-n openshift-storage sh-4.4# df-h ~~~ **Example Output:** ~~~ $ oc rsh rook-ceph-osd-2-56d76cf697-b4zb8 sh-4.4# df-h Filesystem Size Used Avail Use% Mounted on overlay 120G 9.5G 111G 8% / tmpfs 64M 0 64M 0% /dev tmpfs 32G 0 32G 0% /sys/fs/cgroup shm 64M 0 64M 0% /dev/shm tmpfs 32G 49M 32G 1% /run/udev /dev/mapper/coreos-luks-root-nocrypt 120G 9.5G 111G 8% /etc/ceph tmpfs 32G 24K 32G 1% /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph-2 tmpfs 32G 28K 32G 1% /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount ~~~ 5. List the PGs from object store: ~~~ sh-4.4# ceph-objectstore-tool--data-path /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph---op list-pgs ~~~ **Example Output:** ~~~ e.g sh-4.4# ceph-objectstore-tool--data-path /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph-2--op list-pgs 3.f 3.d 3.b 3.a ~~~ 6. Export PG from object store **WARNING: Ensure there is enough space on the node the OSD is scheduled on to hold the contents of the PG.** sh-4.4# mkdir /var/lib/rook/pg.dir/ sh-4.4# ceph-objectstore-tool--data-path /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph---op export--pgid--file /var/lib/rook/pg.dir/pg..data **Example Output:** sh-4.4# ceph-objectstore-tool--data-path /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph-2--op export--pgid 2.17--file /var/lib/rook/pg.2.17.data Exporting 2.17 info 2.17(empty local-lis/les=37/38 n=0 ec=13/13 lis/c 37/37 les/c/f 38/38/0 37/37/37) Export successful 7. Once exporting of PG(s) is accomplished, exit the pod and copy the PG data from the pod onto the host: a. Find the container: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host $ crictl ps-a|grep rook-ceph-osd- ~~~ **Example Output shows "9f03a5b2490ef" as the container ID:** ~~~ 9f03a5b2490ef 8106dd8b53492eb402671c9818f1ce3e336e69a9f1e56226aa242afb87ba7a6f 23 minutes ago Running osd 0 1a018e28c1884 rook-ceph-osd-2-6cb959c4b8-bddkf ~~~ b. Find where the `rook-data` host path is mounted: ~~~ $ crictl inspect 9f03a5b2490ef|grep-e 'hostPath' | grep-e 'rook-data' "hostPath": "/var/lib/kubelet/pods/30f8df5e-da54-47b8-8e28-3a78b6c78eb1/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/rook-data", ~~~ c. Copy the directory from the pod to the `/var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/` directory on the node: ~~~ $ cp-r /var/lib/kubelet/pods/30f8df5e-da54-47b8-8e28-3a78b6c78eb1/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/rook-data/pg-dir/ /var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/ ~~~ **Note:** The `/var/lib/rook/openshift-storage/pg-dir/` contents can now be used to import PGs on another OSD on the host, or copied outside of the host to import to a redeployed OSD. 8. Exit maintenance mode by exiting the pod and navigating to the directory of the OSD deployment yaml, and executing the following: `$ oc apply-n openshift-storage-f rook-ceph-osd-.yaml--force` # Import 9. Ensure the OSD is in maintenance mode by following steps 1-2. 10. Import the PG to the OSD: **Syntax:** ~~~ $ ceph-objectstore-tool--data-path /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph---op import--pgid--file / /pg..data ~~~ 11. Once complete, remove the OSD from maintenance mode, step [8].
root_cause: This typically happens in a bug scenario or when a user is running an unsupported pool that isn't size 3, min_size 2, where the OSD has failed, but it still has weight, and PGs can be accessed.

title: Snapshot creation from Instance attached volume always failed in RHOSO18
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Snapshot creation from Instance attached volume always failed in RHOSO18. OpenStack CLI returns the following errors. The output is taken with--debug option to CLI. ~~~ Since microversion 3.66 of the Block Storage API, the 'force' option is invalid for this request. For backward compatibility, however, when the 'force' flag is passed with a value evaluating to True, it is silently ignored. Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/cinderclient/v3/volume_snapshots.py", line 163, in create raise ValueError() ValueError During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/cliff/app.py", line 410, in run_subcommand result = cmd.run(parsed_args) File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/osc_lib/command/command.py", line 39, in run return super(Command, self).run(parsed_args) File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/cliff/display.py", line 117, in run column_names, data = self.take_action(parsed_args) File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/openstackclient/volume/v2/volume_snapshot.py", line 131, in take_action snapshot = volume_client.volume_snapshots.create(File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/cinderclient/api_versions.py", line 421, in substitution return method.func(obj, *args, **kwargs) File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/cinderclient/v3/volume_snapshots.py", line 165, in create raise ValueError(MV_3_66_FORCE_FLAG_ERROR) ValueError: Since microversion 3.66 of the Block Storage API, the 'force' option is invalid for this request. For backward compatibility, however, when the 'force' flag is passed with a value evaluating to True, it is silently ignored. clean_up CreateVolumeSnapshot: Since microversion 3.66 of the Block Storage API, the 'force' option is invalid for this request. For backward compatibility, however, when the 'force' flag is passed with a value evaluating to True, it is silently ignored. END return value: 1 ~~~
resolution: - To avoid the issue, force option needs to be added to snapshot creation command if the volume is in-use status as older release required.- This issue is being discussed at [OSPRH-25297](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSPRH-25297).
root_cause: - From Cinder API 3.66 microversion or later, snapshot creation for instance attached volume(i.e. in-use status volume) doesn't require force option. However, current openstackclient implementation always passes force option and its default is false. Due to that, CInder returns an error to the request.

title: Display user's last login date and time in OpenShift Web Console
issue: - Is it possible to show the user's last login date and time upon login in the OpenShift Web UI?- Is there a login banner on the Web UI that shows the user's last login date and time for security reasons?
resolution: The Red Hat engineering department reviewed this request in [RFE-1847](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1847), and it has been rejected.
root_cause: This type of auditing needs to be done on the IdP (Identity Provider) side, as OpenShift is not part of the authentication path and does not have visibility into login events. Except for the `htpasswd` provider, all user authentication is handled externally to OpenShift.

title: kube-apiserver ClusterRoleBinding is automatically assigned to kube-apiserver user in RHOCP 4
issue: When a `kube-apiserver` `user` is created, the user is automatically added as a subject to the existing `kube-apiserver` `ClusterRoleBinding`, granting `get` and `create` permissions on `node/proxy` resources cluster-wide.![Warning](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/attachments/screenshot_from_2026-01-08_12-18-13.png)
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [`OCPBUGS-70298`](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-70298). For more information, please open a [`new support case`](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. ###Workaround: Remove the `kube-apiserver` `user` from the `kube-apiserver` `ClusterRoleBinding` using the OpenShift web console by deleting only the `ClusterRoleBinding` `subject`. Do not delete the `ClusterRoleBinding` itself. This removes the user entry from the binding and prevents the unintended permissions from being applied.![Warning](https://access.redhat.com/sites/default/files/attachments/screenshot_from_2026-01-08_13-25-22_0.png) **Note:** Do not delete the `system:kube-apiserver` entry, which is required for the cluster to function correctly. Only remove the `kube-apiserver` user entry.
root_cause: OpenShift creates the `kube-apiserver` `ClusterRoleBinding` for internal use by `system:kube-apiserver`. When a `kube-apiserver` user is created, the user is automatically added as a `subject` to the existing ClusterRoleBinding.

title: Is there support for cloud‑init or Cloudbase‑Init for Windows guests in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - Support for cloud‑init and Cloudbase‑Init for Windows guests in OpenShift Virtualization.
resolution: - `cloud‑init` does not work at all for Windows virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization Windows guests do not consume `cloud‑init` data sources.- `Cloudbase‑Init` is a Windows equivalent of cloud‑init, but it is not supported by Red Hat for use with Windows virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization.- If you choose to use `Cloudbase‑Init`, you should work directly with the `Cloudbase‑Init` vendor or community for guidance and troubleshooting.
root_cause: - The cloud‑init mechanisms (cloudInitConfigDrive and cloudInitNoCloud) included in OpenShift Virtualization are designed and validated for Linux guest workloads only.- Windows operating systems do not interpret Linux `cloud‑init` userdata. While `Cloudbase‑Init` exists to provide similar functionality on Windows, it is a third‑party implementation and is not covered by Red Hat’s support or product certification.

title: Is switching between Openshift 4 update channels supported?
issue: Is it supported to switch between `eus` (Extended User Support) and `stable` channels?
Switch between `stable` and `fast` to get updates sooner is supported?
Is the `candidate` channel supported for upgrades?
resolution: It is possible to switch from `stable-4.y` to `eus-4.y` as soon as it is available, or back again until the release has gone to into EUS status. Switching from `stable-4.y` to `fast-4.y` is also allowed if, for example, a required bugfix was released. The `fast` channels are fully supported as explained in the OpenShift documentation linked in the *Root Cause* section. Switching back to `stable` afterward is also allowed, but note that if the version upgraded to via `fast-4.y` is not yet available in the `stable-4.y+1`, it could require some time to get that `stable-4.y+1` channel available for switching (when the version upgraded to is available in that channel). > **Note:** downgrading an OpenShift cluster is **not tested or supported** as explained in [is it possible to downgrade a version in OpenShift Container Platform 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4777861). While switching to `candidate-4.y` is also available, upgrades onto the `candidate` channel are **not supported**, so it is not recommended for production and in some cases it could be required to reinstall the cluster as it is explained in the documentation for [candidate-4.y channel](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/updating_clusters/understanding-openshift-updates-1#candidate-version-channel_understanding-update-channels-releases).
root_cause: Switching channels is always possible, and at no point will the upgrade path normally allow to upgrade to an unsupported version or via and untested path (with the exception of the `candidate-4.y` channel, which is not supported). Tested upgrade paths are shown in the [Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Update Graph tool](https://access.redhat.com/labs/ocpupgradegraph/update_path). If the latest version on the new channel is earlier than the current version of the cluster, updates will simply not be shown as available and it will be needed to wait till new versions are available for upgrading to. > **Note:** once a minor version has gone from fully supported to EUS (only for EUS versions), then there will be updates on the `eus` channel that are not available on the `stable` channel. For more information refer to: * [Understanding update channels and releases](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/updating_clusters/understanding-openshift-updates-1#understanding-update-channels-releases). * [`eus-4.y` channel](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/updating_clusters/understanding-openshift-updates-1#eus-4y-channel_understanding-update-channels-releases). * [Choosing the correct channel for your cluster](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/updating_clusters/understanding-openshift-updates-1#fast-stable-channel-strategies_understanding-update-channels-releases). * [Switching between channels](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/updating_clusters/understanding-openshift-updates-1#switching-between-channels_understanding-update-channels-releases).

title: Hotplugged network interface name changes after VM restart in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - A hotplugged network interface is renamed by the guest OS after the Virtual Machine (VM) is restarted (e.g., changing from enp10s0 to enp5s0).- Network connectivity is lost because of the configuration references the old interface name.
resolution: This behaviour is a known limitation in OpenShift Virtualization 4.18 and 4.19, where the number of PCI slots reserved for hotplugging depends on the number of existing interfaces (calculated as 4 minus the number of existing interfaces). If a VM starts with 4 or more interfaces, no slots are reserved for hotplugging, causing new interfaces to receive temporary high-numbered PCI addresses which is changed to lower addresses upon reboot. This limitation is documented in VirtIO limitations: [Hot plugging network interfaces](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/virtualization/networking#virtio-limitations_virt-hot-plugging-network-interfaces) This issue is resolved in OpenShift Virtualization 4.20, and in this version, the controller logic reserves a fixed block of 6 PCI slots for hotplugged interfaces, regardless of how many interfaces are present at boot time.
root_cause: The issue is at the dynamic PCI slot reservation algorithm used in OpenShift Virtualization 4.19 and earlier. OpenShift Virtualization calculates the number of reserved hotplug slots during the VM startup using the formula (4- current_interface_count). When a VM boots with four or more interfaces, the result is zero, meaning no buffer slots are reserved between the network interfaces and other peripheral controllers. Typically, the virtio-scsi controller occupies the very next slot (e.g., 0x05) immediately after the fourth NIC. When a user subsequently hotplugs a fifth interface, it cannot occupy slot 0x05 because it is already in use, so the libvirtd assigns a higher available slot (e.g., 0x0a), leading the guest OS to name the device enp10s0. However, upon rebooting the VM, it assigns network interfaces sequential slots (0x01 through 0x05) and shifts the virtio-scsi controller PCI address. Because the fifth interface's PCI bus address changes from 0x0a to 0x05 during this re-evaluation, the guest OS's "Consistent Network Device Naming scheme" renames the interface to enp5s0, invalidating any configuration tied to the original name.

title: Is it supported a S3 subpath in LokiStack in RHOCP 4?

resolution: The parameters supported in the Loki Object storage for the different object storage backends are documented in the Red Hat Documentation section [Loki object storage](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/configuring_logging/configuring-lokistack-storage#logging-loki-storage_configuring-the-log-store). The `subpath` parameter is not one of them. It's not supported.

title: CreateContainerError with requests timing out in CRI-O due to system load in OpenShift 4
issue: - Pods stuck in `ContainerCreating` or failing with `CreateContainerError` errors.- Pod deployments failing with messages like the following one: ~~~ Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Kubelet may be retrying requests that are timing out in CRI-O due to system load: error reserving pod name k8s_[pod_name]_[namespace_name]_xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx_xx: name is reserved ~~~- Events shows messages like the following one: ~~~ Error: kubelet may be retrying requests that are timing out in CRI-O due to system load. Currently at stage container volume configuration: context deadline exceeded: error reserving ctr name k8s_[pod_name]_[namespace_name]_xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx_xx for id xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: name is reserved ~~~- The `kubelet` logs on the node affected shows messages like the following one: ~~~ pod_workers.go:1298] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="failed to \"StartContainer\" for \"[deployment_name]\" with CreateContainerError: \"kubelet may be retrying requests that are timing out in CRI-O due to system load. Currently at stage container volume configuration: context deadline exceeded: error reserving ctr name k8s_[pod_name]_[namespace_name]_xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx_xx for id xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: name is reserved\"" pod="[namespace_name]/[pod_name]" podUID="xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx" ~~~- Draining and restarting the Nodes with the symptoms isn't solving the issue.
resolution: There is unlikely to be any universal resolution for this error, because this error is a catch-all notification from the Kubelet, which is saying "*the pod or container creation process is taking longer than I expect*". There are several reasons this can pop up, and several bugs that have been already fixed throughout the OpenShift 4 cycle. Bug [OCPBUGS-1263](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-1263) was created to improve the behavior of CRI-O's handling of these cases, providing additional information about the cause of the issue. Based on that, in recent OpenShift releases CRI-O will report the stage of resource creation. For example, if the Kubelet re-requests the container to be created, and CRI-O is currently relabeling the volume, CRI-O will also report `Currently at stage container volume configuration` in the error message. Below is an attempt to summarize some cases this has happened, most of them already fixed in currently supported OpenShift versions:- Bug [BZ #1987112](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1987112) is an issue that is **still present**. Basically, if a pod has volume with lots of files attached, and the plugin that manages that volume tells CRI-O to recursively SELinux relabel the directory, then container creation time can stall.- This issue is the likeliest scenario that causes "`error reserving ctr name`", and in newer releases it usually also reports "`Currently at stage container volume configuration`" in the error message.- There are two possible workarounds described in [pods using Persistent Volumes with high file counts fail to start or take an excessive amount of time in OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6221251). **Note:** in few cases, the same error message could be caused by the issue described in [error reserving ctr name <...>: name is reserved messages on OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6976004).- Bug [BZ #1785399](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1785399) is the originally reported bug and was already fixed.- In the past, the only remediation was to remove all of the containers and try again. However, this only made matters worse.- The fix linked in the bug (along with a couple of subsequent ones) changed CRI-O's behavior in these cases to *save* the created resource (pod or container) and return it to the Kubelet when the creation finally finished. This way, with enough time (assuming it's not a symptom of hardware that's incapable of handling the workloads), the error will go away and pods will be running.- Bug [BZ #1924741](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1924741) was from a crash in OpenShift SDN and was already fixed.- If the networking plugin is not up, then non `HostNetwork` pods cannot be created. **Note:** while this specific bug has been fixed, issues with the network plugin are the likeliest cause of `error reserving pod name` errors.- Bug [BZ #2082344](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2082344) was a bug in CRI-O's dbus library, wherein the creation of the `conmon` `cgroup` stalled in `dbus` and a thread was leaked, and was already fixed.- Bug [BZ #2106264](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2106264) was an instance where the aforementioned CRI-O optimization caused a static pod to get stuck and never be created, and was already fixed. #### Workarounds If "`Currently at stage container volume configuration`" is also shown in the error message, refer to [pods using Persistent Volumes with high file counts fail to start or take an excessive amount of time in OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6221251). While this issue is rarely a fault of CRI-O, in some cases [rebooting the affected node gracefully](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6089061) could help. Specially for those cases, but also if the CPUs/memory of the nodes is high, it is highly recommended to properly configure the system resource reservations as explained in [which amount of CPU and memory are recommended to reserve for the system in OpenShift 4 nodes](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5843241).
root_cause: This error has many different causes. It is mostly saying there is a bottleneck on the node where CRI-O is taking longer than expected, and it is rarely been the fault of CRI-O: Kubelet makes requests to CRI-O to create pods and containers (henceforth called resources). When CRI-O takes longer than the Kubelet expects, the Kubelet re-requests that resource. However, since CRI-O has reserved the name for that resource, and is currently working on creating it, it reports an error containing the phrase "`name is reserved`".

title: Deleting stale/failed jobs in openshift-marketplace namespace in RHOCP 4
issue: - Is it safe to delete the failed/stale `jobs` in `openshift-marketplace`?
resolution: Delete the `failed/stale` `jobs` using below command: ~~~ $ for job in $(oc get jobs-n openshift-marketplace--no-headers | awk '$2=="Complete" || $2=="Failed" {print $1}'); do oc delete job "$job"-n openshift-marketplace done ~~~
root_cause: - The `jobs` in `openshift-marketplace` are usually created by the `Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM)` to perform tasks like, Unpacking `operator` bundles, Installing or upgrading an `operator`, Running post-install or cleanup steps.- Once the `job` completes successfully, it typically becomes `stale` (i.e., finished) and is usually left around.

title: List all the repositories on all organizations and search for specific layer in an image in Quay via API
issue: - List all the repositories on all Organization via API calls to `/api/v1/find/repositories` to list repositories, but this does not return all the repos, just the ones the current user owns (even though that user is a superuser).- Search specific layer inside container image inside Quay via API call to `api/v1/repository/ / /tag/`.
resolution: Currently, there is no direct method to retrieve the size of repositories. However, this can be achieved by combining multiple API calls.- List all organization: ~~~ $ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/superuser/organizations/" | jq ~~~- List all repositories inside the organization ~~~ $ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/repository?namespace= " | jq ~~~- List all tags inside a repository ~~~ $ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/repository/ / /tag/" | jq ~~~ Sample scripts are provided to demonstrate how these API calls can be combined to achieve certain outcomes: > **Important Note:** The scripts provided are for reference only and are not officially supported by Red Hat. Although shared as a courtesy, Red Hat does not offer troubleshooting, maintenance, or guarantees for custom scripts. Usage should include proper validation within the environment. #### List all repositories on all organizations- Example script: ~~~ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET https:// /api/v1/superuser/organizations/ | jq-r '.organizations[].name' | xargs-I {} sh-c ' org="{}" echo "Fetching repositories for organization: $org" curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/repository?namespace=$org" | \ jq-r ".repositories[].name" | while read repo; do echo "Fetching images for repository: $repo in organization: $org" curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/repository/$org/$repo/tag/" | \ jq echo "----------------------------------" done ' ~~~- Outcome example: ~~~ Fetching repositories for organization: devops Fetching images for repository: archlinux in organization: devops {"tags": [{"name": "latest", "reversion": false, "start_ts": 1741360479, "manifest_digest": "sha256:5dfcf86c5b995c59282a4c952d66c72b770291d28a43fce5c8faa627c9d0fa9e", "is_manifest_list": false, "size": 164853558, "last_modified": "Fri, 07 Mar 2025 15:14:39-0000"}], "page": 1, "has_additional": false} ~~~ #### List specific image layer to identify which images contain it- Example script: ~~~ TARGET_LAYER="sha256:5c224e52fb7cdf4c1e972ec2798099d2c60e3fca2ab0684f91c6f9e3d0fc06f7"; \ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET https:// /api/v1/superuser/organizations/ | \ jq-r '.organizations[].name' | while read-r org; do \ echo "Fetching repositories for organization: $org"; \ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/repository?namespace=$org" | \ jq-r ".repositories[].name" | while read-r repo; do \ echo "Fetching images for repository: $repo in organization: $org"; \ curl-s-H "Authorization: Bearer "-X GET "https:// /api/v1/repository/$org/$repo/tag/" | \ jq-r '.tags[].name' | while read-r tag; do \ echo "Inspecting image: $repo:$tag"; \ skopeo inspect docker:// /$org/$repo:$tag | \ jq-r--arg TARGET_LAYER "$TARGET_LAYER" '.Layers[] | select(. == $TARGET_LAYER)' && \ echo "Match found in $repo:$tag"; \ echo "----------------------------------"; \ done; \ done; \ done ~~~- Outcome example: ~~~ Fetching repositories for organization: devops Fetching images for repository: archlinux in organization: devops Fetching repositories for organization: devops Fetching images for repository: archlinux in organization: devops Inspecting image: archlinux:latest sha256:5c224e52fb7cdf4c1e972ec2798099d2c60e3fca2ab0684f91c6f9e3d0fc06f7 Match found in archlinux:latest---------------------------------- Fetching images for repository: ubuntu in organization: devops Inspecting image: ubuntu:latest Match found in ubuntu:latest---------------------------------- ~~~
root_cause: Currently, there is no direct method to retrieve the size of repositories. However, this can be achieved by combining multiple API calls.

title: How to configure OpenShift Logging with external MinIO object storage in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - What is the recommended approach to integrate OpenShift Logging with an external MinIO instance as an object storage backend?- How to configure OpenShift Logging to store logs in an external MinIO object store?
resolution: This procedure assumes that a MinIO instance is already installed and configured externally to the OpenShift cluster. ### 1. Install the Red Hat OpenShift Logging Operator **Via Web Console:** 1. Access the OpenShift Web Console as a cluster administrator 2. Navigate to **Operators** → **OperatorHub** 3. Search for "Red Hat OpenShift Logging" 4. Click on the operator and then click **Install** 5. On the installation page, configure:- **Update Channel**: stable or stable-6.x- **Installation Mode**: A specific namespace on the cluster- **Installed Namespace**: openshift-logging- **Enable operator recommended cluster monitoring on this namespace**: Check this option (sets the openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true" label)- **Update approval**:- **Automatic**: Allows Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) to automatically update the Operator when a new version is available- **Manual**: Requires a user with appropriate credentials to approve the Operator update (recommended for production environments to control updates) 6. Click **Install** and wait for completion **Via CLI:** ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-logging--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: openshift-logging namespace: openshift-logging spec: targetNamespaces:- openshift-logging--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: cluster-logging namespace: openshift-logging spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Manual name: cluster-logging source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ``` Apply with: `$ oc apply-f logging-operator.yaml` ### 2. Install the Loki Operator **Via Web Console:** 1. In OperatorHub, search for "Loki Operator" 2. Select the operator provided by Red Hat 3. Click **Install** 4. Configure:- **Update Channel**: stable or stable-6.x- **Installation Mode**: All namespaces on the cluster- **Installed Namespace**: openshift-operators-redhat- **Enable operator recommended cluster monitoring on this namespace**: Check this option- **Update approval**:- **Automatic**: Allows Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) to automatically update the Operator when a new version is available- **Manual**: Requires a user with appropriate credentials to approve the Operator update (recommended for production environments to control updates) 5. Click **Install** and wait for completion **Via CLI:** ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-operators-redhat--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: openshift-operators-redhat namespace: openshift-operators-redhat spec: {}--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: loki-operator namespace: openshift-operators-redhat spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Manual name: loki-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ``` Apply with: `$ oc apply-f loki-operator.yaml` ### 3. Install the Cluster Observability Operator (COO) The Cluster Observability Operator is required to manage Observability UI Plugins, including the Logging UI plugin. **Via Web Console:** 1. Navigate to Operators → OperatorHub 2. Search for Cluster Observability Operator 3. Select Cluster Observability Operator (Red Hat) 4. Click **Install** 5. Configure:- **Installation Mode**: All namespaces- **Installed Namespace**: openshift-observability-operator- **Channel**: stable- **Update approval**: Manual- Click **Install** and wait for completion **Via CLI:** ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-observability-operator--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: observability-operator-group namespace: openshift-observability-operator spec: {}--- apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: cluster-observability-operator namespace: openshift-observability-operator spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Manual name: cluster-observability-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ``` Apply with: `$ oc apply-f openshift-observability-operator.yaml` ### 4. Create the S3 Secret for the External MinIO Backend Create a Secret in the `openshift-logging` namespace containing the MinIO connection details: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: namespace: openshift-logging type: Opaque stringData: access_key_id: " " access_key_secret: " " bucketnames: " " endpoint: "http://:9000" forcepathstyle: "true" ``` **Required fields:**- ` `: Name of the secret- ` `: MinIO user Access Key- ` `: MinIO user Secret Key- ` `: Name of the bucket created in MinIO- ` `: IP address or hostname of the MinIO server Apply with: `$ oc apply-f SECRET_NAME.yaml` **Important note:** Ensure the bucket already exists in MinIO and that the bucket policy allows the necessary actions (Put, Get, List, Delete). ### 5. Create the LokiStack Resource The LokiStack configures Loki to use MinIO storage. Create the following custom resource: ```yaml apiVersion: loki.grafana.com/v1 kind: LokiStack metadata: name: namespace: openshift-logging spec: managementState: Managed limits: global: retention: days: 15 # Set the value as per requirement size: 1x.small storage: schemas:- version: v13 effectiveDate: "-- " secret: name: type: s3 storageClassName: tenants: mode: openshift-logging ``` **Field configuration:**- `name`: Name of the LokiStack- `size`: Deployment size. Production-supported options:- `1x.extra-small`: For test/development environments- `1x.small`: For small clusters- `1x.medium`: For medium to large clusters- Additionally, `1x.pico` is supported starting with logging 6.1.- **Note:** `1x.demo` is for demonstrations only and should not be used in production- `effectiveDate`: Set the date two months ago.- `secret.name`: Name of the Secret created in the previous step- `secret.type`: Always `s3` for MinIO- `storageClassName`: StorageClass available in the cluster for Loki PVCs Apply with: `$ oc apply-f lokistack.yaml` Check status: `$ oc get lokistack-n openshift-logging` ### 6. Grant required permissions to the `logging-collector` ServiceAccount The ClusterLogForwarder uses the logging-collector ServiceAccount, which requires explicit RBAC permissions to collect logs. ### Create the ServiceAccount ``` oc create serviceaccount logging-collector-n openshift-logging ``` ### Grant cluster roles ``` oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user logging-collector-logs-writer-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging ``` ``` oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user collect-application-logs-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging ``` ``` oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user collect-infrastructure-logs-z logging-collector-n openshift-logging ``` ### 7. Create the ClusterLogForwarder Resource The ClusterLogForwarder defines how logs are collected and forwarded. This resource configures:- **Inputs**: Which logs to collect (application, infrastructure, audit)- **Outputs**: Where to send the logs (Loki gateway)- **Pipelines**: Connection between inputs and outputs ```yaml kind: ClusterLogForwarder apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1 metadata: name: instance namespace: openshift-logging spec: serviceAccount: name: logging-collector outputs:- lokiStack: authentication: token: from: serviceAccount target: name: namespace: openshift-logging name: lokistack-out tls: ca: configMapName: openshift-service-ca.crt key: service-ca.crt type: lokiStack pipelines:- inputRefs:- application- infrastructure name: infra-app-logs outputRefs:- lokistack-out ``` **Component explanation:**- **outputs**: Defines the log destination- `name`: Output identifier- `type`: `lokiStack` to use the LokiStack- `lokiStack.target.name`: Name of the LokiStack created in the previous step- `tls.ca` Configures the OpenShift Service CA certificate for secure TLS communication.- **pipelines**: Connects logs to destinations- `inputRefs`: Types of logs to collect:- `application`: Application/container logs- `infrastructure`: OpenShift component logs- `outputRefs`: Reference to the output defined above Apply with: `$ oc apply-f clusterlogforwarder.yaml` ### 8: Enable Observe → Logs (Logging UIPlugin) The Observe → Logs view is not enabled automatically by the console operator. It is enabled exclusively by creating a UIPlugin resource managed by the Cluster Observability Operator. The UIPlugin resource is a cluster-scoped Custom Resource and must be created through the Cluster Observability Operator. Where to create the UIPlugin in the OpenShift Web Console. In the OpenShift Web Console, the UIPlugin can be created from the operator details page: 1. Navigate to Operators → Installed Operators 2. Select `Cluster Observability Operator` 3. Click the `UIPlugin` tab **Create the UIPlugin:** ``` apiVersion: observability.openshift.io/v1alpha1 kind: UIPlugin metadata: name: logging spec: type: Logging logging: lokiStack: name: logsLimit: 50 timeout: 30s schema: viaq ``` **Field explanation:** `type`: Logging: identifies the logging UI plugin `lokiStack.name`: references the previously created LokiStack `logsLimit`: maximum number of log entries per query `timeout`: query timeout `schema`: otel ### 9. Verification After applying all configurations, verify the status: ``` $ oc get pods-n openshift-logging ``` Example output: ``` NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cluster-logging-operator-fb7f7cf69-8jsbq 1/1 Running 0 98m instance-222js 2/2 Running 0 18m instance-g9ddv 2/2 Running 0 18m instance-hfqq8 2/2 Running 0 18m instance-sphwg 2/2 Running 0 18m instance-vv7zn 2/2 Running 0 18m instance-wk5zz 2/2 Running 0 18m logging-loki-compactor-0 1/1 Running 0 42m logging-loki-distributor-7d7688bcb9-dvcj8 1/1 Running 0 42m logging-loki-gateway-5f6c75f879-bl7k9 2/2 Running 0 42m logging-loki-gateway-5f6c75f879-xhq98 2/2 Running 0 42m logging-loki-index-gateway-0 1/1 Running 0 42m logging-loki-ingester-0 1/1 Running 0 42m logging-loki-querier-6b7b56bccc-2v9q4 1/1 Running 0 42m logging-loki-query-frontend-84fb57c578-gq2f7 1/1 Running 0 42m ``` Logs should start being sent to MinIO through Loki. You can verify in MinIO that objects are being created in the configured bucket.

title: Is it possible to use multiple subnets for clusterNetwork and serviceNetwork CIDRs in OCP 4?
issue: - Can there be multiple subnets for `clusterNetwork` and `serviceNetwork` in OCP 4?- Does OpenShift 4 support changing `clusterNetwork` and `serviceNetwork` CIDR after installation?
resolution: - The `clusterNetwork` and the `serviceNetwork` can not be modified after cluster installation as explained in [Is it possible to expand clusterNetwork and serviceNetwork in OpenShift 4?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4769921).- Multiple subnets can be mentioned only for `clusterNetwork` at the time of installation, refer to the "Diagnostic Steps" section for additional information.
root_cause: Only the `clusterNetwork` can take multiple `CIDR` and `hostprefix` entries at the time of cluster installation provided that each `CIDR` entry should not overlap with the other.

title: Image pull from the internal registry is failing in RHOCP 4
issue: - A pod fails with `ImagePullBackOff` when the `deployment` is configured with the internal `ImageStream` URL. ~~~ Back-off pulling image "image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/example-namespace/example-imagestream:stable" ~~~- The `image-registry` `pod` logs show the following error: ~~~ level=error msg="response completed with error" err.code=unknown err.detail="unexpected end of JSON input" err.message="unknown error" ~~~
resolution: - Refresh the `ImageStream` metadata: ~~~ $ oc import-image-n ~~~ #### Example: Update the 'example-imagestream' `ImageStream` metadata for the stable `tag` located in the 'example-namespace' `namespace`: ~~~ $ oc import-image example-imagestream:stable-n example-namespace ~~~
root_cause: Due to corruption in the `ImageStream` metadata, the `image` was not pushed to the internal registry.

title: Is it possible to resize memory and cpu resources in OpenShift Container Platform without restart?
issue: Is there any solution that would allow to add memory/cpu to OpenShift Container Platform nodes, without draining and/or powering them off? Is there any way to avoid kubelet restart while adding memory/cpu resources in the cluster?
resolution: No, it is not possible to be avoided as per current design, however, there is upstream Kubernetes enhancement to determine the changes in compute capacity of the node without restarting as per following: [KEP-3953: Node Resource Hot Plug](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3953) and [respective PR.](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3955).
root_cause: There is an Incremental Implementation expectation as the project is currently prioritizing "hotplug" (adding resources) over "hotunplug" (removing resources) to manage complexity.- Current Infrastructure Limitations: The cAdvisor cache is presently updated only during cluster initialization. It is unaware of any runtime changes to compute capacity (CPU/memory shrinkage).- The Re-admission Requirement: "hotunplug" would require the Kubelet to perform a "re-admission" of all running pods to ensure they still fit within the reduced capacity, a process described as technically "hard" and avoided for the initial phase.- Proposed "Error Mode" for Downsizing: * If a resource reduction is detected, the Kubelet could mark the node as NotReady. ~~~ This serves as a "kill switch" to prevent the cluster from scheduling tasks on a node with mismatched resource reporting. State Management: * A proposal exists to track the "last valid state" in the internal cache. If a "hotunplug" event occurs, the Kubelet would compare the new machine info against this cached value to detect the discrepancy. Recovery Logic: The node would likely return to a Ready state only if the resources are increased back to the last known valid state. ~~~ There is concern that supporting resource additions but not removals defies user expectations and creates an inconsistent experience. If the Kubelet doesn't react to resource removal, it creates a dangerous "false reality" where the cluster thinks capacity exists that is no longer physically available. Removing resources without Kubelet awareness is highly likely to cause Out-of-Memory (OOM) events and general application failures.

title: Pagination support in the Application List endpoint
issue: When calling the 3scale `Application List` endpoint, the returned results are not paginated. Can the call be made to return a paginated response?
resolution: If paginated responses are desired, the `Application List (all services)` endpoint can be called. This endpoint supports pagination and filtering by service using the `service_id` parameter.
root_cause: The `Application List` endpoint does not support pagination. Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in RFE [THREESCALE-12098](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-12098). If this feature is required, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: How to override the cluster-wide default node selector in RHOCP 4?
issue: - Pod stuck in pending state with below error: ~~~ pod=" / " err="0/x nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/x nodes are available: x Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.. ~~~- `KubeDaemonSetRolloutStuck` Alert Triggered ~~~ prometheus=openshift-monitoring/k8s severity=warning alertname=KubeDaemonSetRolloutStuck container=kube-rbac-proxy-main daemonset=ingress-canary endpoint=https-main job=kube-state-metrics namespace= service=kube-state-metrics ~~~
resolution: - Add `Namespace` Annotation to Bypass `defaultNodeSelector` ~~~ $ oc annotate ns openshift.io/node-selector='' ~~~- Verify Pods are Scheduled: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n | grep-i Pending ~~~- Restart the `pending` pods after adding annotation: ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n ~~~
root_cause: - Pod scheduling failure occurs when the pod’s `nodeSelector` or `affinity` does not match the cluster’s `defaultNodeSelector`. The `OpenShift scheduler` combines the pod’s node selection criteria with the `defaultNodeSelector`.- If no nodes satisfy both the pod's `nodeSelector` and the `scheduler's defaultNodeSelector`, the pod remains in Pending.- This can affect `DaemonSets`, `Deployments`, `StatefulSets`, or any pod-based workload.

title: Creating a Windows VMs compliant to AWS EC2 Windows License Included
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - I want to create a Windows VM compliant with Windows License Included (LI)
resolution: If you plan to run Windows VMs on OpenShift hosts (AMD64 bare metal EC2 instances) with enabled [AWS Windows License Included](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html/cluster_administration/managing-compute-nodes-using-machine-pools#creating_a_machine_pools_cli_win_li_rosa-managing-worker-nodes) you need to create the Windows VMs in a license-compliant manner by utilizing `d1` preferences. For details about preparing a host in a ROSA cluster, see this article: [https://access.redhat.com/articles/7136295](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7136295).. about Windows License-Included hosts. You can create a compliant VM from a list of available bootable volumes.- In the web console, navigate to **Virtualization-> Catalog**.- The **InstanceTypes** tab opens by default.- Create a new Windows boot source by click **Add volume** to upload a new volume or to use an existing persistent volume claim (PVC), a volume snapshot, or a `containerDisk` volume.- In the **Volume metadata** section, ensure to select a preference with a name starting with `windows` and followed by your Windows version, e.g., `windows.11.virtio`.- Click **Save**.- Select a suitable bootable volume from the list. If the list is truncated, click the **Show all** button to display the entire list.- The bootable volume table contains the previously uploaded boot source.- Select a suitable `InstanceType` from the `d1` family.- Click in `User provided` tab.- Select an `InstanceType` starting with the `d1` name suitable for your VM, e.g., `d1.2xmedium` for a Windows 11 VM.- Optional: If you are creating a Windows VM, you can mount a Windows driver disk:- Click the **Customize VirtualMachine** button.- On the **VirtualMachine** details page, click **Storage**.- Select the **Mount Windows drivers** disk checkbox.- Optional: Click **View YAML & CLI** to view the YAML file. Click **CLI** to view the commands for OpenShift Virtualization `virtctl` CLI. You can also download or copy either the YAML file contents or the CLI commands.- Click **Create VirtualMachine**. After the VM is created, you can monitor the status on the **VirtualMachine details** page. In a cluster with enabled [AWS Windows License Included](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html/cluster_administration/managing-compute-nodes-using-machine-pools#creating_a_machine_pools_cli_win_li_rosa-managing-worker-nodes), only VMs utilizing InstanceType from the `d1` family are expected to run. Windows VMs created from templates or utilizing other InstanceTypes are expected to be unable to start. Windows VMs must enable the `dedicatedCpuPlacement` attribute. This attribute is enabled by default if the IntanceTypes having a name starting with `d1` is used.

title: Users cannot login to Openshift 4 with error "Login failed (401 Unauthorized)" while a control plane node is failing
issue: - When a control plane node went down login into the cluster is not possible with `Login failed (401 Unauthorized)`.- There are `oauth` Pods in `Pending` status.- `x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid` errors shown in the `openshift-oauth-apiserver` Pods logs.
resolution: It is needed to unblock the revision rollout of the authentication Pod that is stuck due to the control plane node being in `NotReady` state. The current situation looks like this: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-authentication-owide NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE oauth-openshift-8f66c8b57-j8p6m 1/1 Running 1 78d oauth-openshift-8f66c8b57-mcsdg 1/1 Running 1 78d oauth-openshift-8f66c8b57-sjchh 1/1 Running 0 78d oauth-openshift-d694495cb-9z65h 0/1 Pending 0 59m <---------- Here ~~~ As it can be seen, the Pod stuck in `Pending` state has a different hash "d694495cb" indicating that this is from a different `replicaSet` for updated `deployment`. This to be fixed needs either to bring the control plane node Up again OR force the rollout to complete. If the control plane node is not possible to be brought up due to serious problem or hardware failure it might be need to workaround this issue to provide relief and let user be able to use the cluster. #### Workaround To be able to force the rollout it is needed to do the following steps: 1. Set the `authentication` operator to "`Unmanaged`" state for being able to edit the `oauth-openshift` `deployment`: ~~~ $ oc patch authentication.operator cluster--type=merge-p '{"spec": {"managementState": "Unmanaged"}}' ~~~ 2. Set the `deployment` rolling update strategy `maxUnavailable` value from 1 to 2: ~~~ $ oc patch deployment oauth-openshift-n openshift-authentication--type=merge-p '{"spec": {"strategy": {"rollingUpdate": {"maxUnavailable": 2}}}}' ~~~ Now the Pods under `openshift-authentication` namespace should start to rollout and there will be 2 running replicas from the new revision and one will be stuck in `Pending` due to the control plane that is down. Wait until this process finishes that should take a couple of minutes. 3. When 2 replicas of the new revision are already running, then set the `authentication` operator back to "`Managed`" with the below command: ~~~ $ oc patch authentication.operator cluster--type=merge-p '{"spec": {"managementState": "Managed"}}' ~~~ The `deployment` will revert `maxUnavailable` back to 1 automatically as soon as the operator gets to the "`Managed`" state so no need to do anything else but please check if was done or not to be sure: ~~~ $ oc get deployment oauth-openshift-n openshift-authentication-o yaml ~~~
root_cause: The cluster system processes are maintaining a lot of things to keep the cluster healthy. One of these things are the certificates that have an expiration date and need to be rotated regularly. This process requires pods to get rolled out to get updated with the new certificates and this is a part of the maintenance process and normal. If a control plane node goes into `NotReady` state for whatever reason and stay there for many days will cause this issue cause at some point a rollout will need to be done and it will get stuck. The rollout cannot proceed if the deployment Rollout strategy is set with `maxUnavailable = 1`.

title: How to build a custom  RHBK image  ?
issue: How to build a custom RHBK image?
resolution: ## 1. Overview The goal of this article is to present how to perform and to use a custom RHBK image build locally. ## 2. Building a custom image ### 2.1 Updating keycloak.conf In the example used, we are going to update the log level used in the container image. By default log level is set to INFO. It is possible to adjust the log level by setting it to `TRACE` in the file `keycloak.conf`. file *conf/keycloak.conf* ~~~ # Hostname for the Keycloak server. #hostname=myhostname log-level=org.keycloak:TRACE ~~~ ### 2.2 Preparing a Dockerfile You need to prepare a `Dockerfile` file *Dockerfile* ~~~ FROM registry.redhat.io/rhbk/keycloak-rhel9:22-8 as builder COPY./keycloak.conf /opt/keycloak/conf # Enable health and metrics support ENV KC_HEALTH_ENABLED=true ENV KC_METRICS_ENABLED=true WORKDIR /opt/keycloak RUN /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh build RUN keytool-genkeypair-storepass password-storetype PKCS12-keyalg RSA-keysize 2048-dname "CN=server"-alias server-ext "SAN:c=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"-keystore conf/server.keystore RUN /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh build FROM registry.redhat.io/rhbk/keycloak-rhel9:22-8 COPY--from=builder /opt/keycloak/ /opt/keycloak/ ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh"] ~~~ For more information all the different `Dockerfile` usage, see RHBK documentation at [3.1. Creating a customized and optimized container image](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_build_of_keycloak/22.0/html/server_guide/containers-#containers-creating-a-customized-and-optimized-container-image) ### 2.3 Building a custom image using podman To build a RHBK custom image, use the `podman` command tool. ~~~ $ podman build.-t localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 ~~~ ~~~ [1/2] STEP 1/8: FROM registry.redhat.io/rhbk/keycloak-rhel9:22-8 AS builder [1/2] STEP 2/8: COPY./keycloak.conf /opt/keycloak/conf...... [2/2] STEP 3/3: ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh"] [2/2] COMMIT localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0--> 8c5cfe0f4ced Successfully tagged localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 8c5cfe0f4ced7640d3fca26ba2c64abb0f34f1dbbd66a5d6639064b53af40856 [orivat@orivat docker_0202_1]$ podman push localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 quay.io/rhn_support_orivat/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 Getting image source signatures Copying blob e418572c6ebe done Copying blob 62f60fa9d14c skipped: already exists Copying blob f72461870632 skipped: already exists Copying config 8c5cfe0f4c done IWriting manifest to image destination ~~~ ### 2.4 Listing local images using podman tool Run the command *podman images* to display the local images from podman repository. ~~~ $ podman images REPOSITORY TAG IMAGE ID CREATED SIZE localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug 5.0 8c5cfe0f4ced 2 hours ago 612 MB registry.redhat.io/rhbk/keycloak-rhel9 22-8 7b5add1a98f0 9 days ago 446 MB ~~~ ### 2.4 Verifying the content of the custom RHBK image build It is also possible to verify if the image has been build correct For this, you will need to use podman to start a RHBK container. **Running podman as container:** ~~~ $ podman run--name mykeycloak-debug localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 start--hostname-strict=false ~~~ **Listing active container** You can use the command *podmand ps* to list active containers. ~~~ $ podman ps CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES 53a52315693c localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 start--hostname-... 33 seconds ago Up 33 seconds mykeycloak-debug ~~~ **Connecting using bash to the active container** The command *podman exec* allows you to connect to the target contaiber and run bash command inside. ~~~ podman exec-it mykeycloak-debug /bin/bash bash-5.1$ ~~~ Like this, you can verify that the `keycloak.conf` file has been updated correctly. ~~~ bash-5.1$ cd /opt/keycloak/conf bash-5.1$ cat keycloak.conf #hostname=myhostname log-level=org.keycloak:TRACE ~~~ ## 3. Pushing RHBK image to quay.io ### 3.Login to quay You fist need to log to quay.io ~~~ podman quay.io login-u-p ~~~ ### 3.2 New repository Create a new repository. You can can do it using the Quay UI, using the *Create New Repository* command. It will create a new repository at URL: *quay.io/<username>/mykeycloak-debug* Make also this new *Quay.io* repository **public**. ### 3.3 Pushing local image You can now push your local image image to quay, using the *podman* command. ~~~ $ podman push localhost/keycloak/mykeycloak-debug:5.0 quay.io/ /mykeycloak-debug:5.0 Getting image source signatures Copying blob 6eeab094aa10 done Copying blob ee0b43bf2a20 done Copying blob ddbaea2d0909 done Copying config dc076384a2 done Writing manifest to image destination ~~~ ## 4. Using the custom RHBK image build You can now use your new custom RHBK image by using the image: *quay.io/<username>/mykeycloak-debug:5.0* ## 5. Additional pointers For build in Openshift directly, the same process can be done via `BuildConfig` using Dockerfile as `strategy.type.Docker`, similarly to [Troubleshooting EAP 7 local BuildConfig in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7031934). This bypasses quay (pull and get phases) given the result image will be in the Openshift container platform. See the solution [How to deploy a new custom image for RHBK operator?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7053142), specifically for deploying the custom image.

title: Patching RHDH Operator image in Openshift 4
issue: How to patch the RHDH Operator image in Openshift 4 via Operator and Helm chart?
resolution: This process is rarely used in production and used only for when patching is necessary ### RHDH Operator The user can switch the RHDH's image directly editing the [CSV resource](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7108078) `spec.template.spec.containers[0].image, full example below: ~~~ ############# ### Get the rhdh csv: ############# $ OPERATOR_NAMESPACE=rhdh-operator $ CSV=$(oc-n $OPERATOR_NAMESPACE get csv-o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') #################### ### Make sure the CSV is the RHDH one- in the example above it is the first item, but it may not be: ##################### $ oc-n $OPERATOR_NAMESPACE patch csv "$CSV" \--type='json' \-p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/install/spec/deployments/0/spec/template/spec/containers/0/image", "value": "quay.io/rhdh-community/operator:0.7.4-hotfix-rhdhsupp-290"}]'... clusterserviceversion.operators.coreos.com/rhdh-operator.v1.8.2 patched ~~~ Result: It is also useful to set the `Upgrade Approval` to Manual to avoid the upgrading automatically starting and overwriting the image present: ~~~ OPERATOR_NAMESPACE=rhdh-operator SUBSCRIPTION=rhdh oc-n $OPERATOR_NAMESPACE patch subscription $SUBSCRIPTION \--type merge \-p '{"spec": {"installPlanApproval": "Manual"}}' ~~~ ### RHDH Helm Charts Helm chart deployment, the user only need to update the respective RHDH Operator deployment resource (statefulset or deployment) and no need to update the Subscription or CSV, given they are not used.
root_cause: The process can be done to replace the RHDH Operator image directly.

title: Is it possible to replace a control plane node in a bare metal cluster installed with Agent-based Installer?
issue: - One of the control plane nodes is no longer working — either because it became NotReady, or due to physical hardware failure. The node is not recognized by the cluster anymore, and we want to replace it to restore full functionality.- There is a relevant document, [6.2.4. Replacing the unhealthy etcd member](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#replacing-the-unhealthy-etcd-member). However, this procedure seems to assume an IPI or UPI environment, and may not work for a bare metal cluster installed using the Agent-based Installer (ABI), especially in environments without Baseboard Management Controller(BMC).- Is there any officially supported method for this case?
resolution: Starting from **OpenShift version 4.19**, it is supported to [Replacing a failed bare-metal control plane node without BMC credentials](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/nodes/working-with-nodes#replacing-control-plane-node).

title: How to add new ETCD member to cluster after control plane node replacement in agent-based, disconnected, baremetal environment
issue: There is no documented procedure for replacing a Control Plane node in a bare metal cluster built with the Agent-Based Installer(ABI).
Inability to recover control plane node requires a complete rebuild of the cluster versus just a partial recovery of replacing the unhealthy node.

Following [4.18 guidance](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#restore-replace-stopped-baremetal-etcd-member_replacing-unhealthy-etcd-member) for replacing a failed etcd member on-prem, does not work as expected due to the lack of BMC configuration.
resolution: For **OpenShift version 4.19 and newer**, it is supported to [Replacing a failed bare-metal control plane node without BMC credentials](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/nodes/working-with-nodes#replacing-control-plane-node). ### Control Plane Node Replacement on Agent-Based Installed Cluster without DHCP and BMC credentials #### Table of Contents * [Introduction](#intro) * [Prerequisites](#prereq) * [Procedure](#procedure) * [Verify and remove the unhealthy member](#ocp_step_1) * [Turn off etcd quorum guard](#ocp_step_2) * [Remove the old secrets for the etcd member that was removed](#ocp_step_3) * [Ensure that the BareMetal Operator is available](#ocp_step_5) * [Remove the affected BareMetalHost](#ocp_step_6) * [Obtain the machine for the affected node](#ocp_step_4) * [Delete the machine of the unhealthy member](#ocp_step_7) * [Verify that the machine was deleted](#ocp_step_8) * [Verify that the nodes has been deleted](#ocp_step_9) * [Wait for Cluster Operators](#ocp_step_9a) * [Create the new BareMetalHost](#ocp_step_10) * [Create New ControlPlane Node](#ocp_step_11) * [Link Node, BareMetalHost, and Machine](#bmh_link_host) * [Add The New Etcd Member](#new_etcd) * [Force Etcd redeployment](#clp_step_5) * [Turn the quorum guard back on](#clp_step_6) * [Wait for the Cluster Operators](#wait_cl_ops) * [References](#refer) ### Introduction {#intro} The following procedure describes replacing an OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) ControlPlane node that has failed and is powered off. This procedure assumes that the ControlPlane was originally deployed using the Agent Installation procedure without providing BMC credentials in the agent config yaml. For clarity, the installation the OCP cluster required that each node booted the generated Agent Installer ISO thru BMC (iLO or iDRAC) attached virtual media, network boot, or temporarily attached drives (e.g., USB thumb drive). ### Prerequisites {#prereq} * You have identified the unhealthy bare metal etcd member. * You have verified that either the machine is not running or the node is not ready. * You have access to the cluster as a user with the cluster-admin role. * You have taken an [etcd backup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#backup-etcd). * Downloads: * [`coreos-installer` CLI](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/downloads#tool-coreos-installer) * Red Hat CoreOS live iso > **NOTE:** an [etcd backup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/control-plane-backup-and-restore#backup-etcd) before performing this procedure is required, so that the cluster can be restored if any issues are encountered. For this type of installation there will be no `machineset` for the control plane. Run the following command to look for machine sets: ~~~ $ oc get machinesets,controlplanemachinesets-n openshift-machine-api ~~~ > **IMPORTANT NOTE:** there should only be one or more `machinesets` for the workers. If `controlplanemachinesets` exists for the control plane, do not use the following procedure. ### Procedure {#procedure} #### Verify and remove the unhealthy member [\[ocp\]](#ocp) {#ocp_step_1} 1. Choose an etcd pod that is not on the affected node using the following command: oc-n openshift-etcd get pods-l k8s-app=etcd-o wide 2. Connect to the running etcd container, passing in the name of a pod that is not on the failed node: oc rsh-n openshift-etcd etcd- (1) (1): replace `etcd- ` with the name of an etcd pod associated with one of the healthy nodes. 3.
