title: Restoring an OpenShift cluster after migration
issue: OpenShift nodes have been migrated between environments. All networking remains the same.
resolution: We will need to create a new bootstrap kubeconfig using a valid token. Replacing the kubeconfig on the node, will allow the bootstrap process to re-join the node back to the cluster. ~~~ export BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=$(oc create token node-bootstrapper-n openshift-machine-config-operator--duration=4h) //check how the token looks like, it should start with "eyJ..." echo $BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN ~~~ ~~~ export KUBECONFIG_NAME=bootstrap.kubeconfig export API_SERVER=$(oc whoami--show-server) export CA_DATA=$(oc get configmap-n openshift-config-managed kube-root-ca.crt-o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}') oc config set-cluster my-cluster \--server=$API_SERVER \--certificate-authority= <(echo "$CA_DATA") \--embed-certs=true \--kubeconfig=$KUBECONFIG_NAME oc config set-credentials node-bootstrapper \--token=$BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN \--kubeconfig=$KUBECONFIG_NAME oc config set-context default-context \--cluster=my-cluster \--user=node-bootstrapper \--kubeconfig=$KUBECONFIG_NAME oc config use-context default-context--kubeconfig=$KUBECONFIG_NAME ~~~ copy the file to /tmp/bootstrap.kubeconfig on the node ~~~ sudo systemctl stop kubelet sudo rm /var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig sudo rm /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-client-current.pem sudo cp /tmp/bootstrap.kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig sudo systemctl start kubelet ~~~ After the kubelet is running again, certificate signing requests should be created from the bootstrap process. These need to be approved with: ~~~ oc get csr-o go-template='{{range.items}}{{if not.status}}{{.metadata.name}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}{{end}}' | xargs oc adm certificate approve ~~~ **note: It is recommended to always keep a backup of all the deleted or overwritten files**
root_cause: The node got disconnected from the cluster due to certificate expiring. For the same reason, bootstrap also could not re-add the node back to the cluster.

title: Missing controlplanemachineset resource in IPI RHOCP 4 cluster
issue: - When trying to adjust the resource sizes for the control plane, the responsible custom resource `controlplanemachineset` is not present in the OpenShift cluster.
resolution: Starting with OpenShift 4.12, control plane machine sets were introduced to provide management capabilities for the control plane machines. Refer to [getting started with control plane machine sets](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/machine_management/managing-control-plane-machines#cpmso-getting-started) for additional information. The supportability of the `ControlPlaneMachineSets` depends on the OpenShift version and the cloud provider. Refer to [supported cloud providers](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/machine_management/managing-control-plane-machines#cpmso-platform-matrix_cpmso-getting-started) for the supportability matrix for OpenShift 4.12, and change the documentation version for different OpenShift versions. For some OpenShift and cloud provider combinations, while the `ControlPlaneMachineSets` are supported, it is needed to manually create them or manually activate them (as shown in the table linked above). Refer to the respective documentation version for additional information about creating `ControlPlaneMachineSets` resources, for OpenShift 4.12 it is in [creating a control plane machine set custom resource](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/machine_management/managing-control-plane-machines#cpmso-creating-cr_cpmso-getting-started). For specific examples: * OpenShift 4.12 IPI installed on Azure: refer to [Creating `controlplanemachineset` in OpenShift 4.12 clusters in Azure](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7060794). * OpenShift 4 IPI installed on vSphere: refer to [Creating `controlplanemachineset` in OpenShift 4 clusters in vSphere](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7063111).
root_cause: Starting with OpenShift 4.12, [control plane machine sets](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/release_notes/ocp-4-12-release-notes#ocp-4-12-mapi-control-plane-machine-sets_release-notes) were introduced to provide management capabilities for the control plane machines. They are similar to what compute machine sets provide for compute machines. For some OpenShift and cloud provider combinations, while the `ControlPlaneMachineSets` are supported, it is needed to manually create them or manually activate them.

title: HCP control plane components do not restart automatically when certificates are renewed in RHOCP 4
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - The HCP cluster unexpectedly stopped working and trying to login to the OCP console is returning the error: ~~~ {"error":"server_error","error_description":"The authorization server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.","state":"00000000000000a"} ~~~- HCP control plane components are reporting `Unauthorized` in their logs.- HCP certificates are rotate but the control-plane components are not using them.
resolution: Restart all the pods in the hosted control-plane namespace in the management cluster. Issue permanently fixed with bug [OCPBUGS-50014](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-50014) from **MulticlusterEngine 2.9** (released with RHACM 2.14).
root_cause: After rotating the control plane certificates the hosted cluster controller does not execute the restart of the pods.

title: OIDC IDP missing from the HCP Web Console in RHOCP 4
issue: - Multiple Identity Providers (e.g., LDAP and OIDC) are configured in the `HostedCluster` Customresource, only one provider (typically LDAP) is visible on the login screen of the Web Console.- The `oauth-openshift` pods in the `hosted control plane` namespace (on the management cluster) are missing the volume mounts for the OIDC CA bundle (e.g., idp-cm-0-ca).
resolution: **Permanent Fix** Upgrade to a version containing the fix for [OCPBUGS-61101](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-61101) 4.17.39 or later. The fix ensures the reconciler starts with the system-trust-bundle before adding customer-provided certificates. **Workaround** Apply an annotation to the `HostedCluster` CustomResource to bypass the operator's internal validation and force the IDP configuration into the OAuth server: ~~~ $ oc annotate hc/-n clusters \ idpoverrides.hypershift.openshift.io/ ='{"urls":{"authorize":" ","token":" ","userInfo":" "},"claims":{"id":["sub"],"preferredUsername":["preferred_username"],"name":["name"],"email":["email"]},"challenge":false}' ~~~ *Note*: Replace ` ` and `URLs` with your specific provider details. This annotation should be removed after upgrading to a fixed version.
root_cause: The HyperShift `control-plane-operator (CPO)` reconciler contains a logic error in how it constructs TLS trust bundles. Instead of inheriting the standard system root CA bundle and appending customer-provided certificates, the reconciler initializes the HTTP client's trust store from an empty state. Consequently, the operator fails to verify public Identity Provider (IDP) certificates—such as those for `login.microsoftonline.com`, because the required public Root CAs are excluded from the constructed bundle, resulting in `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority errors`.

title: The metrics-server pod fails to establish connection towards kube-apiserver
issue: - OpenShift metrics endpoints are showing as `Down`.- The `TargetDown` and `KubeletDown` alerts are displayed.
resolution: 1. Scale up `cluster-monitoring-operator` to `replicas=1`: $ oc scale deployment/cluster-monitoring-operator--replicas=1-n openshift-monitoring 2. Verify that the `cluster-monitoring-operator` pod is running: $ oc get pods-l app=cluster-monitoring-operator-n openshift-monitoring NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cluster-monitoring-operator-6585d87cd5-g69gq 1/1 Running 0 24h 3. Wait several minutes for the `metrics-server` deployment to be reconciled by the operator. $ oc get pods-l app.kubernetes.io/name=metrics-server-n openshift-monitoring NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE metrics-server-8d6bbd79c-k9hsz 1/1 Running 0 3d14h metrics-server-8d6bbd79c-p2mkl 1/1 Running 0 3d14h 4. Then, check the creation timestamp of the secret: $ NEW_SECRET_NAME=$(oc get deploy/metrics-server-o json | jq-r '.spec.template.spec.volumes[] | select(.name=="client-ca-bundle") |.secret.secretName') $ oc get secret "${NEW_SECRET_NAME}"-n openshift-monitoring-o json | jq-r '.metadata.creationTimestamp' 2025-12-15T13:58:34Z
root_cause: - The `cluster-monitoring-operator` was accidentally scaled down to `replicas=0`, stopping monitoring reconciliation.- As a result, required certificate and configuration updates for monitoring components (including `metrics-server`) were not applied, causing communication failures with the `kube-apiserver`.

title: The ovnkube-node fails to start on a new worker node
issue: - Pods fail to schedule on the node newly created because the `network` ClusterOperator is not available on it. "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="network is not ready: container runtime network not ready: NetworkReady=false reason:NetworkPluginNotReady message:Network plugin returns error: no CNI configuration file in /etc/kubernetes/cni/net.d/. Has your network provider started?" pod="openshift-multus/multus-xxxxx" podUID="4d340bce-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-1d3b6f6733e0"
resolution: **Disclaimer**: *Do not add, modify, or delete entries in the OVN-Kubernetes databases without explicit approval from Red Hat Support.* 1. Delete the `k8s.ovn.org/node-chassis-id` annotation: $ NODE_NAME=" " $ oc annotate node ${NODE_NAME} k8s.ovn-org/node-chassis-id- 2. Verify the `ovnkube-xxxxx` pod for the node is running: $ oc get pods-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes | grep "${NODE_NAME}" NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE READINESS GATES ovnkube-node-xxxxx 8/8 Running 0 1m xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx worker1 3. Ensure that the `chassis name` in OVN Southbound DB matches the value of the `k8s.ovn.org/node-chassis-id` annotation: $ oc get node "${NODE_NAME}"-o json | jq-r '.metadata.annotations["k8s.ovn.org/node-chassis-id"]' c5b243aa-85ce-46c1-aa89-bce639533ceb $ OVN_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-o wide--no-headers | grep "${NODE_NAME}" | awk {'print $1'}) $ oc rsh "${OVN_POD_NAME}" ovn-sbctl--columns=hostname,name list chassis | grep-A2 "${NODE_NAME}" hostname: worker1 name: "c5b243aa-85ce-46c1-aa89-bce639533ceb" 4. Verify the node is in the `Ready` state and the `network` ClusterOperator state: $ oc get node "${NODE_NAME}" NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION worker1 Ready app,worker 4d20h v1.31.11 $ oc get co network NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE network 4.18.22 True False False 25d 5. Allow time for workloads to reschedule and for OVN-Kubernetes to complete reconciliation using the newly generated chassis ID.
root_cause: - The worker node was rebuilt multiple times, resetting its local OVN state.- The `k8s.ovn.org/node-chassis-id` annotation no longer matches entry in the OVN Southbound DB.- Consequently, the mismatch prevented OVN-Kubernetes from attaching the node, causing `ovnkube-node` restarting indefinitely.

title: The ovnkube-node fails to convert ovnkube-client-current.pem certificate
issue: - Node reports a `NotReady` condition.- Pods are stuck in `ContainerCreating` or `Pending` because the network is unreachable.
resolution: 1. Define the required variables: $ NODE_NAME=" " $ OVN_POD_NAME=$(oc get pods-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-o wide--no-headers | grep "${NODE_NAME}" | awk {'print $1'}) 2. Remove the current `ovnkube-client-current.pem` symbolic link: $ oc rsh "${OVN_POD_NAME}"-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes rm-f /etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs/ovnkube-client-current.pem 3. Wait for the `ovnkube-node-xxxxx` pod to restart: $ oc get pods-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes-o wide | grep "${NODE_NAME}" NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE ovnkube-node-xxxxx 8/8 Running 0 17h xx.xx.x.xx 4. Verify the `/etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs` directory to ensure the new `ovnkube-client-current.pem` points to a valid PEM file: $ oc rsh "${OVN_POD_NAME}"-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ls-l /etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 1 10:30 ovnkube-client-2026-01-01-10-30-15.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 2 06:02 ovnkube-client-2026-01-02-06-02-29.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 3 03:21 ovnkube-client-2026-01-03-03-21-01.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 4 00:48 ovnkube-client-2026-01-04-00-48-40.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 4 21:26 ovnkube-client-2026-01-04-21-26-11.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 5 17:24 ovnkube-client-2026-01-05-17-24-15.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 0 Jan 6 14:42 ovnkube-client-2026-01-06-14-42-45.pem-rw-------. 1 root root 1155 Jan 6 16:06 ovnkube-client-2026-01-06-16-06-52.pem <=== New PEM lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root 66 Jan 6 16:06 ovnkube-client-current.pem-> /etc/ovn/ovnkube-node-certs/ovnkube-client-2026-01-06-16-06-52.pem
root_cause: - The `ovnkube-node-xxxxx` pod cannot start because it fails to load the node certificate.- The `ovnkube-client-current.pem` symbolic link points to a certificate file that is empty.- The empty `.pem` file prevents the certificate manager from converting it into a valid cert/key pair.- As a result, the node’s OVN pod initialization is blocked, causing networking issues for pods on that node.

title: Third-party CNI in OSD, ROSA, and ARO
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - Can I install third-party Container Network Interface (CNI) like Calico or Cilium in OSD, ROSA, and ARO?- I found [KCS:5436171](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5436171), will it apply to OSD, ROSA, and ARO?
resolution: In managed OpenShift environments—Red Hat OpenShift Dedicated (OSD), Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA), and Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO)—the default Container Network Interfaces (CNIs) are:- **OVN-Kubernetes**: Default for clusters running OpenShift version 4.11 and above.- **OpenShift-SDN**: Default for clusters running OpenShift version 4.10 and below. By default, third-party CNIs like Calico or Cilium are not supported in these managed services. However, for ROSA with Hosted Control Planes (HCP), there is an option to deploy a cluster **without a CNI plugin**, allowing you to install a third-party CNI of your choice post-deployment. It's important to note that if you choose to use your own CNI for ROSA with HCP clusters, it is strongly recommended that you obtain commercial support from the plugin vendor before creating your clusters. Red Hat support cannot assist with CNI-related issues such as pod-to-pod traffic for customers who choose to use their own CNI plugin. For detailed guidance on creating a ROSA with HCP cluster without a CNI plugin, refer to the official Red Hat documentation. [0] [0] [ROSA with HCP clusters without a CNI plugin](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html/install_clusters/rosa-hcp-cluster-no-cni)

title: Is it supported to scale up control plane / etcd node replicas in OpenShift 4?
issue: - Is it possible to scale master / etcd nodes to more than 3 in OpenShift 4?- How to configure more than 3 master nodes in OCP 4
resolution: It is important to know that scaling etcd **does not improve performance**. When scaling to 5 members the quorum has to pass traffic to all the members and wait for consensus from more members before committing a change. This introduces latency to etcd, which in turn increases latency for the API server and cluster operators. > **Note:** for easier management of control plane nodes in IPI installed clusters, like replacing failing one, it is possible to use the control plane machine sets (CPMS) described in [is it possible to define `machinesets` for control plane nodes in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5238591). ### Support for more than 3 control plane nodes Starting with OpenShift 4.17, for clusters installed on a bare metal platform, it is possible to [scale a cluster to 4 or 5 nodes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/release_notes/ocp-4-17-release-notes#ocp-4-17-etcd-4-5-nodes_release-notes) as a post-installation task. The etcd Operator scales accordingly to account for the additional node. For more information, refer to [node scaling for etcd](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/scalability_and_performance/recommended-performance-and-scalability-practices-2#etcd-node-scaling_recommended-etcd-practices). Starting with OpenShift 4.18, it is possible to [configure 4 and 5 node control planes with the Agent-based Installer](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/release_notes/ocp-4-18-release-notes#ocp-release-notes-agent-5-node-control-plane_release-notes). Refer to the [optional configuration parameters](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/installing_an_on-premise_cluster_with_the_agent-based_installer/installation-config-parameters-agent#installation-configuration-parameters-optional_installation-config-parameters-agent) for the supported number of `replicas` for the `controlPlane` parameter. > **Note:** as explained in [node scaling for etcd](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/etcd/ensuring-reliable-etcd-performance-and-scalability#etcd-node-scaling_etcd-performance), and only applicable to the above mentioned versions, scaling a cluster to 4 or 5 control plane nodes is available **only** on **bare metal** platforms. In addition to that, it is also explained that *while adding control plane nodes can increase reliability and availability, it can decrease throughput and increase latency, **affecting performance***. In OpenShift 4.16 and older releases, the above is **not supported** and exactly three control plane nodes (so, etcd nodes) must be used for all production deployments. Refer to the [control plane architecture](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/architecture/control-plane) in the official documentation for additional information about the control plane.
root_cause: With the redesign of OpenShift 4 and performance improvements of components that make up OpenShift 4, it is no longer necessary to run with more than (>) 3 control plane nodes. Scaling etcd **does not improve performance**. Also, adding more master nodes increases complexity of the system, increases maintenance costs and does not increase the redundancy by a big margin. Additionally, having more etcd nodes has a larger impact on the networking system, since one needs to distribute the etcd database across more nodes. etcd works with a quorum consensus algorithm called `RAFT`.

title: What are the smallest OpenShift 4 cluster deployments supported
issue: - Can OpenShift 4 run as an appliance (in a small form factor)?- Can OpenShift 4 run in an edge (not in a data center/cloud) situation?- Can a development cluster be run (for 1-5 members)?- What is the smallest OpenShift 4 Deployment that can be created?
resolution: For regular OpenShift 4 clusters with High Availability (HA) for the control plane and the workloads, the minimum cluster requires **three control plane** machines and at least **two compute** machines as explained in [required machines for cluster installation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/installing_on_any_platform/installing-platform-agnostic#installation-machine-requirements_installing-platform-agnostic). Additional installation methods using less machines than the regular installation were introduced, like three-node clusters and Single Node OpenShift (SNO). ### Three-node clusters This topology for OpenShift Container Platform cluster is a smaller and more resource efficient, as it consists of only three control plane machines, which also act as compute machines. > **Note:** the **hardware requirements** for the control plane nodes in three-node clusters is higher than the requirements for control plane nodes when they are not schedulable, as in that installation topology those nodes also run custom workloads. #### Three-node clusters support- Starting with OpenShift 4.5, three-node compact clusters using the agnostic installation workflow (platform `none`) are supported on either physical or virtual hardware: [three-node bare metal deployments](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.5/html/release_notes/ocp-4-5-release-notes#ocp-4-5-three-node-bare-metal-deployments).- Starting with OpenShift 4.13, the [three-node cluster support](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.13/html/release_notes/ocp-4-13-release-notes#ocp-4-13-installation-and-upgrade-three-node_release-notes) was extended to Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and VMware vSphere.- Starting with OpenShift 4.14, the [three-node cluster support](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes#ocp-4-14-nutanix-three-node) was extended to Nutanix.- Starting with OpenShift 4.17, the [three-node cluster support](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/release_notes/ocp-4-17-release-notes#installation-and-update-shiftstack-compact_release-notes) was extended to Red Hat OpenStack Platform (RHOSP). The deployment process for agnostic installation is covered in the product documentation: [configuring a three-node cluster](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/installing_on_any_platform/installing-platform-agnostic#installation-three-node-cluster_installing-platform-agnostic). Check for separate documents for specific cloud provider. > **Note:** if adding compute nodes to three-node clusters, it is generally **recommended** to unset the control plane nodes as schedulable (at least 2 compute nodes are required for that) to avoid the additional load in the control plane nodes caused by custom workloads to impact the cluster performance. Refer to [how to remove worker role from control plane in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4564851) for additional information. #### Three-node compact hub cluster with Hosted Control Planes (HCP) Starting with OpenShift 4.17, it is supported to have a compact three-node bare metal cluster as a hosting for HCP clusters. For additional information and recommendations, refer to [Compact Hub Clusters with Hosted Control Planes](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7109585) and also [shared infrastructure between hosted and standalone control planes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/hosted_control_planes/preparing-to-deploy-hosted-control-planes#hcp-shared-infra_hcp-sizing-guidance) for additional information. ### Two-node clusters A two-node OpenShift cluster is a compact, cost-effective topology with a reduced hardware footprint. Refer to the documentation for the use case of each topology:- Starting with OpenShift 4.20, a two-node OpenShift cluster with an additional arbiter node feature (which requires lower resources than a standard control plane node) has been promoted to Generally Available as described in [configuring a local arbiter node](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/release_notes/ocp-4-20-release-notes#ocp-4-20-edge-computing-arbiter-node_release-notes). This was introduced as a [Technology Preview feature](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview) in OpenShift 4.19 [configuring a local arbiter node (Technology Preview) for two-node OpenShift cluster](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/release_notes/ocp-4-19-release-notes#ocp-4-19-edge-computing-arbiter-node_release-notes).- Starting with OpenShift 4.20, a [Technology Preview feature](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview) for [two-node OpenShift cluster with fencing](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/release_notes/ocp-4-20-release-notes#ocp-4-20-edge-computing-two-node-fencing_release-notes) has been introduced, which is still not Generally Available. ### Single Node OpenShift (SNO) Starting with OpenShift 4.9, Single Node OpenShift (SNO) is also supported. > **Note:** Review the [OpenShift 4.9 release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.9/html/release_notes/ocp-4-9-release-notes), which outline some of the limitations for installing OpenShift Container Platform on a single node. Refer to the product documentation about [installing on a single node](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html-single/installing_on_a_single_node/index) for additional information.
root_cause: For regular OpenShift 4 clusters with High Availability (HA) for the control plane and the workloads, the minimum cluster requires **three control plane** machines and at least **two compute** machines. Additional smaller topologies has been introduced in different OpenShift releases.

title: How to configure Loki Object Storage CA certificate in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to configure the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate for the `ObjectStorage` endpoint in the `LokiStack`?- After installing the Network Observability Operator using the SSL/TLS protocol, an error with the CA trust certificate occurs while Loki Operator attempts to save data on a S3 bucket using a customized certificate.- Errors while flushing to the `ObjectStorage` backend: ~~~ msg="failed to flush" err="failed to flush chunks: store put chunk: RequestError: send request failed\ncaused by: Put \"https://objectstorage.example.com:1234/loki-storage/backend\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ~~~ ~~~ msg="failed to flush" err="failed to flush chunks: store put chunk: RequestError: send request failed\ncaused by: Put \"https://objectstorage.example.com:1234/loki-storage/backend\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate relies on legacy Common Name field, use SANs instead ~~~- Error message in the `LokiStack` status: ~~~ message: 'Invalid object storage CA configmap contents: key not present or data empty: service-ca.crt' ~~~
resolution: #### When using S3 Compatible object storage or S3 object storage with custom certificate 1. Create a `ConfigMap` containing the CA certificate necessary to connect to the Object Storage endpoint: ~~~ # oc create cm loki-s3-ca-n--from-file=service-ca.crt=./.pem ~~~ 2. Modify the `LokiStack` resource to add the `spec.storage.tls.caName` field referencing the name of the `ConfigMap` previously created, for example: ~~~ # oc patch lokistack/-n--type merge-p '{"spec":{"storage":{"tls":{"caName":"loki-s3-ca"}}}}' ~~~ #### When using ODF Object storage in the same OpenShift that the Loki pods For OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF), if it uses the OCP Service CA, so it is not necessary to create an extra `ConfigMap`, the `openshift-service-ca.crt` `ConfigMap` existing in all the namespaces when created can be used and configured for providing the OpenShift CA: ``` $ oc patch lokistack/-n--type merge-p '{"spec":{"storage":{"tls":{"caName":"openshift-service-ca.crt","caKey":"service-ca.crt"}}}}' ``` When using noobaa `ObjectStorage` backend, refer to [how to configure Lokistack with noobaa `ObjectStorage` backend?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7046579) > **IMPORTANT NOTES** > >- the `caKey` where the `Key` is the data key of a Configmap containing a CA certificate. It needs to be in the same namespace as the LokiStack custom resource. If empty, it defaults to `service-ca.crt` >- The certificate needs to have the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) set as explained in [Error x509: certificate relies on legacy Common Name field, use SANs instead in Openshift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6886271). >- For OpenStack Swift storage, this procedure does not work at the moment of writing this article. For OpenStack Swift object backend storage, read the article [How to configure tls for accessing to OpenStack Swift object storage in Loki in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7040935). >- For Azure object storage this procedure does not work at the moment of writing this article as not implemented. Review RFE ["Support to configure.spec.storage.tls for Azure storage in Loki"](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-836).
root_cause: The Loki ingester, querier or compactor are not able to trust the certificate provided by the Object Storage endpoint.

title: UBI 8 OpenJDK 17 JAVA_OPTS overwrites JAVA_OPTS_APPEND
issue: - UBI OpenJDK ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1 image `JAVA_OPTS` overwrite `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND`- UBI OpenJDK ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1 image image ignores `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` ~~~ oc new-app--context-dir=getting-started--name=quickstart--image-stream=test/openjdk-17:1.17-2~https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts.git#3.2--build-env='JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx1024M'--build-env='JAVA_OPTS_APPEND=-Dbox=fox' ~~~- UBI OpenJDK ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1 breaks backward with previous versions on `JAVA_OPTS` environment variable, which differs from ubi8/openjdk-17 behavior
resolution: Starting on `ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1` the `JAVA_OPTS` overwrites other JVM flags- and that is expected. So for most use cases: use `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` it should have the same intended behavior. Changes that were introduced in `ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1`:- Before the image `ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1` the behavior was: user could use `JAVA_OPTS` in combination to `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND`- **behavior: combine them both**.- After `ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1`, the behavior is: usage of `JAVA_OPTS` replaces other JVM flags- **behavior: java_opts replaces java_opts_append**. Finally, in case of deployment of builds, be sure the images are the same on different pods, via `ImageID/shaID` verification on the pod yaml. Quarkus had a similar issue, where `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` was not being used, which is now fixed in Quarkus 3.5.0.CR1+, [Quarkus PR 35983](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/35983).
root_cause: The changes introduced on `ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1` restore `JAVA_OPTS` to its original behavior, which was broken inadvertently on previous images (ubi8 images). And this aligns the behavior with the ubi9 images. The intent behind the two variables is:- customer-provided JAVA_OPTS **overrides** all our options generation- customer-provided JAVA_OPTS_APPEND **adds** to our options generation. The main recommendation is to switch to `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` for appending, i.e. the user should be using `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` for most use cases except advanced replacement. Image | Behavior----------|------- ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1 (before) | JAVA_OPTS: adds, and JAVA_OPTS_APPEND: adds ubi8/openjdk-17:1.15-1 (after) | JAVA_OPTS: overrides, and JAVA_OPTS_APPEND: adds ubi9/images | JAVA_OPTS: overrides, and JAVA_OPTS_APPEND: adds

title: Applying performanceProfile will reboot every node
issue: Applying performanceProfile will reboot every node, which is even not included in the nodeSelector of the performanceProfile
Every node includes control plane nodes and infra nodes
This behavior is not observed in OCP 4.12 or 4.13
resolution: * This behavior is expected as stated in the [release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/release_notes/ocp-4-14-release-notes.html "") * In OpenShift Container Platform 4.14, all nodes use Linux control group version 2 (cgroup v2) for internal resource management in alignment with the default RHEL 9 configuration. However, if you apply a performance profile in your cluster, the low-latency tuning features associated with the performance profile do not support cgroup v2. * As a result, if you apply a performance profile, all nodes in the cluster reboot to switch back to the cgroup v1 configuration. This reboot includes control plane nodes and worker nodes that were not targeted by the performance profile. * To revert all nodes in the cluster to the cgroups v2 configuration, you must edit the Node resource. For more information, see Configuring Linux cgroup v2. You cannot revert the cluster to the cgroups v2 configuration by removing the last performance profile. (OCPBUGS-16976)"

title: Red Hat OpenShift Support for VMware Cloud Foundation 9 (VCF9) and vSphere Foundation 9 (VVF9)
issue: New installations of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) 4.18+ are now supported on VMware Cloud Foundation 9 (VCF9) and VMware vSphere Foundation 9 (VVF9).
resolution: The engineering team, in collaboration with Broadcom, has been working to integrate Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (RHOCP) clusters with VMware Cloud Foundation 9 (VCF9), and they have recently announced supported for VCF9 and VVF9 in this [blog post](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/ga-support-red-hat-openshift-vmware-vsphere-foundation-9-and-vmware-cloud-foundation-9).
root_cause: Broadcom is advising customers to migrate from vSphere 8 to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 (VCF9). Full support is necessary to enable the deployment, management, and upgrading of RHOCP clusters on VCF9, ensuring customers can use VCF’s latest features while receiving full support and feature parity from Red Hat.

title: clair-postgres pvc is full
issue: - clair pods are in crashloopbackoff and pod logs show PVC is full. ~~~ sfit-registry-clair-app-6cf647c65-l24br 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1594 (4m25s ago) 5d15h sfit-registry-clair-app-6ff4844c45-dkqs4 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 1594 (4m46s ago) 5d16h sfit-registry-clair-postgres-5dcd6c4899-w7cxr 0/1 Running 1099 (5m11s ago) 3d23h ~~~ ~~~ $ oc logs dr-clair-postgres waiting for server to start....2023-12-13 03:40:37.875 GMT [23] FATAL: could not write lock file "postmaster.pid": No space left on device stopped waiting pg_ctl: could not start server Examine the log output. ~~~
resolution: **1.** Clear rows from a table without removing the table structure. `uo_vuln` table contains information about update operations on Clair's database. And it's safe to truncate it. ~~~ $ oc get pods | grep clair $ oc rsh clair-pod-name sh-4.4$ psql \clairdb-name psql (10.21) Type "help" for help. clairdb-name-# TRUNCATE TABLE uo_vuln; ~~~ **2.** Clair regularly updates its own CVE database in search for new definitions. The update frequency is defined by the [.matcher.period](https://quay.github.io/clair/reference/config.html#matcherperiod) value in Clair's config.yaml file. If this value does not exist, Clair should use the default value which is 6 hours. The higher the count the less frequently it will update vuln database [.matcher.update_retention](https://quay.github.io/clair/reference/config.html#matcherupdate_retention) holds the number of updates in the database and garbage collects the rest. On new versions of Clair, the default value (if this field doesn't exist in Clair's config.yaml file) is 2. Setting it to 1 will decrease the growth of this table ~~~... matcher: update_retention: 1 period: 12h... ~~~ **3.** Increase the size of the pv/pvc. The volume size of the clairpostgres component cannot be overridden. This is a known issue and will be fixed in a future version of Red Hat Quay [(PROJQUAY-4301)](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/PROJQUAY-4301) **4.** Redeploy clair as when clairdb is full pod goes into crashloopbackoff. When Clair database is dropped, the information related to already indexed images also gets dropped. To get the security reports back for those images, Quay must send them to Clair once again to be re-indexed. This can be a very lengthy procedure if there are many images stored in the registry. Clair will always recreate the database schema and will populate it with CVE data automatically if it's connected to the internet. But security reports will not be available until the indexing process is completed. ~~~- Add sleep command to clair container through the clair deployment as follows? $ oc edit deployment... spec: containers: command: ["/bin/sh"] args: ["-c", "while true; do echo hello; sleep 10;done"]- Once done restart clair postgres pod $ oc delete pod pod-name- Downscale Quay operator to 0 pods. $ oc scale--replicas=0 deployment quay-operator.v3.8.x-n- Execute psql shell inside Clair's database $ oc exec-it-- psql- List databases to see what user was used to create the db. \l+- Drop current clair datbase drop database;- Create new Clair database with the same user as owner as the previous db had. e.g Name | Owner | Encoding | Collate |-----------+-------+----------+------------- clair | clair | UTF8 | en_US.utf8 | create database clair owner clair- Connect to the new database and create extension "uuid-ossp" on the database. \c clair;- create extension uuid-ossp CREATE EXTENSION "uuid-ossp";- scale Quay operator back to 1 pod. It will reconcile the whole deployment. ~~~

title: OpenShift 4 Authentication - failed to load SNI cert and key - Cluster API server unavailable after API certificate update
issue: - After updating the API and Ingress certificates, the API and Console became unavailable.- OpenShift oAuth API server cannot connect to etcd.- Authentication pods stuck in `CrashLoopBackoff` state and shows a message like the following ones: ~~~ failed to load SNI cert and key: tls: found a certificate rather than a key in the PEM for the private key ~~~ ~~~ failed to load SNI cert and key: tls: failed to find any PEM data in certificate input ~~~ ~~~ failed to load SNI cert and key: tls: failed to find PEM block with type ending in "PRIVATE KEY" in key input after skipping PEM blocks of the following types: [CERTIFICATE CERTIFICATE CERTIFICATE] ~~~
resolution:
The issue is causing in incorrect formatting of the newly added certificate. Create the certificate with the correct format:- Make sure that the cert file contains all the certificates in the chain, starting with the host certificate, then any intermediate (if any) certificate, ending with the certificate authority's certificate. Refer to [how to check the order of certificates for certificate chain](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6109821) for additional information. For example: ~~~ $ cat ingress.crt intermediateCA{1..n}.crt CA.crt > ingress.pem ~~~- Ensure that the file `ingress.pem` has a new empty line after the last "`------ END CERTIFICATE------`". This is also important for the ingress operator. If not present, the certificate file and key could be considered as only one file, and the process of certificate replacement fails. It is possible to verify it with running following command: ~~~ $ od-c ingress.pem | tail-n 4 0004420 4 L q q r c D R g h G f M 0 A = 0004440 = 
----- E N D C E R T I 0004460 F I C A T E----- 
 0004473 ~~~ Make sure that at the end of the certificate is new line `
`. When there is a new line after the last certificate, re-create the secret from that fixed file and the key and deploy the ingress cert as mentioned in the official documentation [Replacing the default ingress certificate](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/security/certificates/replacing-default-ingress-certificate.html).
root_cause: There is incorrect formatting in the Ingress certificate. For other issues caused by incomplete certificate chain, refer to [RouterCertsDegraded with x509 certificate signed by unknown authority in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4542531).

title: How to Create Automated ETCD Backup in OpenShift 4.x
issue: - Automate ETCD backup
resolution: - **STEP 1: Create a Namespace** Specific namespaces must be created for running ETCD backup pods. `$ oc new-project ocp-etcd-backup`- **STEP 2: Create Service Account** You must create a service account in the namespace dedicated to backup ETCD. This service account will be responsible for performing backup commands for the master nodes: ~~~ kind: ServiceAccount apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: openshift-backup namespace: ocp-etcd-backup labels: app: openshift-backup ~~~ `$ oc apply-f sa-etcd-bkp.yml`- **STEP 3: Create Cluster Role** You must create a Cluster Role with specific permissions for running the backup. This Cluster Role has specific permissions to specific resources and verbs, such as:- Resource: Nodes- Verbs: Get, List- Resource: pods and pods/log- Verbs: Get, List, Create, Delete, and Watch ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: cluster-etcd-backup rules:- apiGroups: [""] resources:- "nodes" verbs: ["get", "list"]- apiGroups: [""] resources:- "pods"- "pods/log" verbs: ["get", "list", "create", "delete", "watch"] ~~~ `$ oc apply-f cluster-role-etcd-bkp.yml`- **STEP 4: Create Cluster Role Binding** After creating the Service Account and Cluster Role, you need to create the link between the two resources: ~~~ kind: ClusterRoleBinding apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 metadata: name: openshift-backup labels: app: openshift-backup subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: openshift-backup namespace: ocp-etcd-backup roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: cluster-etcd-backup ~~~ `$ oc apply-f cluster-role-binding-etcd-bkp.yml`- **STEP 5: Add Special Privileges to Service Account** You will need to set special privileges to the service account running the directory creation commands and backup execution of ETCD (The aforementioned commands are executed with sudo, so you will need the service account to have special privileges): ``` apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: name: system:openshift:scc:privileged roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: system:openshift:scc:privileged subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: openshift-backup namespace: ocp-etcd-backup ``` `$ oc apply-f scc.yaml`- **STEP 6: Create a CronJob** Create CronJob similar to the below example. This cronjob will be run at 23:56 everyday, do the backup and remove all the previous backups. ~~~ kind: CronJob apiVersion: batch/v1 metadata: name: openshift-backup namespace: ocp-etcd-backup labels: app: openshift-backup spec: schedule: "56 23 * * *" concurrencyPolicy: Forbid successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 5 failedJobsHistoryLimit: 5 jobTemplate: metadata: labels: app: openshift-backup spec: backoffLimit: 0 template: metadata: labels: app: openshift-backup spec: containers:- name: backup image: "registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-cli" command:- "/bin/bash"- "-c"- oc get no-l node-role.kubernetes.io/master--no-headers-o name | xargs-I {}-- oc debug {}-- bash-c 'chroot /host sudo-E /usr/local/bin/cluster-backup.sh /home/core/backup/ && chroot /host sudo-E find /home/core/backup/-type f-mmin +"1"-delete' restartPolicy: "Never" terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 activeDeadlineSeconds: 500 dnsPolicy: "ClusterFirst" serviceAccountName: "openshift-backup" serviceAccount: "openshift-backup" ~~~ `$ oc apply-f cronjob-etcd-bkp.yml`- **STEP 7: Test validation** `$ oc create job backup--from=cronjob/openshift-backup` `$ oc get pods-n ocp-etcd-backup` ~~~ NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE backup-29bnd 1/1 Running 0 41s ci-ln-xxxxxx-12345-abcdef-master-1-debug 0/1 Completed 0 15s ~~~ `$ oc get job-n ocp-etcd-backup` ~~~ NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE backup 1/1 57s 100s ~~~ `$ oc get cronjob-n ocp-etcd-backup` ~~~ NAME SCHEDULE SUSPEND ACTIVE LAST SCHEDULE AGE openshift-backup 56 23 * * * False 0 2m5s ~~~ **NOTE:** During the execution of CronJob, the automatically created pods will debug on nodes for backup execution. Review [OCP Disaster Recovery Part 1- How to Create Automated ETCD Backup in OpenShift 4.x](https://cloud.redhat.com/blog/ocp-disaster-recovery-part-1-how-to-create-automated-etcd-backup-in-openshift-4.x) for further reading.

title: Troubleshooting Syntax Errors in the SiteConfig Generator
issue: After making changes to the SiteConfig configuration GitOps/ArgoCD sync fails and a generic error is returned similar to: `Failed to load target state: failed to generate manifest for source 1 of 1: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = kustomize build /site/siteconfig--enable-alpha-plugins failed exit status 1: Error: MalformedYAMLError: yaml: line 2: did not find expected key`
resolution: * For a more detailed error message we will need to run the full repository against the SiteConfig kustomize plugin directly via the following steps. 1. * Manually refresh and resync the failing Application from ArgoCD. This should cause the latest state of the repository to become available within the GitOps repo-server pod on the Hub or Provisioning Cluster. 2. * Locate and access the GitOps repo-server pod on the Cluster. Your command will look similar to `oc rsh-n openshift-gitops openshift-gitops-repo-server-68cbfdc74c-6p2f3` 3. * Navigate to the temp argocd-repo directory `cd /tmp/_argocd-repo/` and modify permissions to allow access `chmod u+r.` 4. * Locate the directory that contains the copy of the GitOps repo from within `_argocd-repo` and modify its permissions. Command will look similar to `chmod u+rwx 58723d48-d0c7-4d6b-a0a7-cf54bac52fbe/` 5. * Navigate next to the specific directory where the SiteConfig resource is located. For this example we will use `ztp-deploy/site-config.yaml` 6. * Execute the following command to run the SiteConfig resource against the SiteConfig kustomize plugin directly `/.config/kustomize/plugin/ran.openshift.io/v1/siteconfig/SiteConfig ztp-deploy/site-config.yaml` 7. * The output here should return specific syntax errors if there are any, if no errors are returned and the issue persists please reach out to Red Hat Global Support Services for further assistance.

title: How to auto-prune of images in Red Hat Quay Registry
issue: - Prune images by the number of tags- Prune image tags by creation date
resolution: - Red Hat Quay administrators can set up auto-pruning policies on namespaces (both users and organization). This feature allows for image tags to be automatically deleted within a namespace based on specified criteria, which allows Red Hat Quay organization owners to stay below the storage quota by automatically pruning content. Currently, two policies have been added: **Prune images by the number of tags:** For this policy, when the actual number of tags exceeds the desired number of tags, the oldest tags are deleted by their creation date until the desired number of tags is achieved. **Prune image tags by creation date:** For this policy, any tags with a creation date older than the given time span, for example, 10 days, are deleted. For details, follow this Red Hay Quay doc [Red Hat Quay namespace auto-pruning overview](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_quay/3.17/html-single/manage_red_hat_quay/index#red-hat-quay-namespace-auto-pruning-overview)

title: Procedure to migrate RHACS to a new storage class in an operator-based without losing secured cluster access
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: - Steps to be performed to migrate Advanced RHACS to new storageclass in an `operator-based` install.- Restore back up should retain all the cluster connected which are shown in the cluster list.
resolution: Steps to be performed to migrate RHACS to a new storageclass in an operator-based install are mentioned below:- [Backup](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.10/html/backup_and_restore/backing-up-acs#backup-deployment-config-operator_backing-up-acs)` central-tls` secret, central custom resource, and `central-htpasswd`.- Create a database [backup](https://docs.redhat.com/it/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.8/html/troubleshooting_central/backing-up-central-database-by-using-the-roxctl-cli#on-demand-backups-roxctl-api_backing-up-central-database-by-using-the-roxctl-cli) of Central using `roxctl`.- [Uninstall](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.10/html/installing/uninstall-acs) the old Central instance.- Restore `central-tls` and `central-htpasswd` secret in the new namespace. ``` $ oc apply-f central-tls.json $ oc apply-f central-htpasswd.json ```- Install the new Central instance from the backup created in step 1. Edit `Central` YAML to use the new VMware datastore's storage class name. You must specify the new class under the `central.db.persistence.persistentVolumeClaim` section. ``` Example configuration: spec: central: db: isEnabled: Default persistence: persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: central-db size: 100Gi storageClassName: $ oc apply-f central-cr.yaml ``` Note: Ensure you do not change the value of `isEnabled` from `Default` to `Enabled`.- [Restore](https://docs.redhat.com/it/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_security_for_kubernetes/4.10/html/troubleshooting_central/restoring-central-database-by-using-the-roxctl-cli#:~:text=Chapter%C2%A02.-,Restoring%20Central%20database%20by%20using%20the%20roxctl%20CLI,-You%20can%20use) the Central database backup using the `roxctl` command. The `central-tls secret `includes the certificates for authenticating with Secured clusters and signing API tokens. Backing up and restoring the `central-tls` secret will ensure that all secured clusters will be connected to central after backup and restore.

title: node-exporter netclass collector fails with "operation not supported" when OVN/OVS interface has the highest ifindex on OpenShift Container Platfor
issue: The node-exporter pod in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace logs repeated errors: ``` level=error msg="collector failed" name=netclass duration_seconds=0.000894048 err="could not get link modes: netlink receive: operation not supported" ``` As a result, network-related monitoring metrics such as `node_network_up`, `node_network_info`, and other `node_network_*` metrics are missing for the affected nodes. These nodes do not appear in the Prometheus/web console metrics, causing monitoring gaps. The issue occurs on some nodes but not others, even though the VM configurations appear identical.
resolution: ### Workaround 1: Disable Netlink for the netclass collector Modify the `cluster-monitoring-config` ConfigMap to disable the netlink-based collector: ```bash oc edit cm cluster-monitoring-config-n openshift-monitoring ``` Set the configuration as follows: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 data: config.yaml: | enableUserWorkload: true nodeExporter: collectors: netclass: enabled: true useNetlink: false ``` Reference: [Config Map Reference for the Cluster Monitoring Operator- NodeExporterCollectorNetClassConfig](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/monitoring_stack_for_red_hat_openshift/4.16/html/config_map_reference_for_the_cluster_monitoring_operator/config-map-reference-for-the-cluster-monitoring-operator#nodeexportercollectornetclassconfig) Verify by checking that the node-exporter pods no longer log "collector failed" errors: ```bash oc logs-n openshift-monitoring-c node-exporter | grep "collector failed" ``` ### Workaround 2: Restart a pod on the affected node to refresh ifindex ordering Restart a pod in the `openshift-network-diagnostics` namespace on the affected node. This creates a new OVN interface with an ifindex higher than the unsupported interface (e.g., `genev_sys_6081`), preventing the failure: ```bash oc delete pod-n openshift-network-diagnostics ``` Verify by confirming that the node-exporter error logs stop and the missing `node_network_*` metrics reappear: ```bash curl-s http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep 'node_network_info' ``` ### Workaround 3: Reboot the affected node Rebooting the node resets all interface ifindex values to their default ordering, ensuring that the unsupported interfaces (e.g., `genev_sys_6081`) no longer have the highest ifindex. ### Permanent fix: Upgrade to OpenShift Container Platform 4.18 The node-exporter version shipped in OpenShift Container Platform 4.18 handles `LinkModes()` failures for unsupported interfaces gracefully. Even when an unsupported interface has the highest ifindex, the netclass collector does not fail. Upgrading to 4.18 permanently resolves this issue.
root_cause: This issue involves two contributing factors: ### 1. node-exporter netclass collector defect (OCP 4.16)** The node-exporter netclass collector uses a netlink-based ethtool library (`github.com/mdlayher/ethtool`) to perform a bulk `LinkModes()` dump (using `NLM_F_DUMP`) across all network interfaces. The kernel processes interfaces in ifindex order. When the **last** interface in the ifindex sequence is one that does not support ethtool link mode queries (such as `genev_sys_6081`, `ovs-system`, `ovn-k8s-mp0`, `br-int`, or `br-ex`), the kernel returns "operation not supported" as the final response, and the ethtool library treats this as a fatal error for the entire bulk operation. This causes the entire netclass collector to fail, resulting in all `node_network_*` metrics being missing for that node. Any interface that does not support ethtool `LinkModes()` can trigger this issue if it happens to have the highest ifindex on the node. ### 2. OVN rebuild causes genev_sys_6081 to be recreated with a high ifindex** When all OVN databases are rebuilt simultaneously (e.g., during EgressIP troubleshooting or OVN recovery operations), all geneve tunnels on each node are torn down at the same moment. OVS detects that no geneve tunnels exist and determines that the `genev_sys_6081` interface is no longer needed, so it deletes the interface. Once the OVN databases are restored and tunnels are re-established, OVS recreates `genev_sys_6081`, but the newly created interface is assigned a new, higher ifindex (e.g., 49 instead of the original 5). On nodes where no pod is subsequently scheduled or restarted after the rebuild, no new OVN veth interface is created with a higher ifindex, leaving `genev_sys_6081` as the last interface in the ifindex sequence and triggering the netclass collector failure described above.

title: EgressIP Failover Dynamics: Normal Behavior and the Impact of Graceful Shutdowns/Reboots
issue: In a default configuration where `egressIPReachabilityTotalTimeout` is set to 5 seconds, the `ovnkube-cluster-manager` actively monitors node health. During a service disruption or a node reboot, the `EgressIP` must migrate to a healthy node to maintain traffic continuity. This failover process involves health-probe monitoring and `Gratuitous ARP (GARP)` announcements, which can result in temporary "dual MAC" observations on the network.
resolution: ##Scenario 1: ovnkube-node Pod Restart When the `ovnkube-node` pod restarts on the host currently assigned the `EgressIP`, the `gRPC` health check on port `9107` fails, causing the `ovnkube-cluster-manager` to receive a `context deadline exceeded` error. Once the 5 second timeout threshold is reached, the manager flags the node as unreachable and triggers an immediate rebalancing. The `EgressIP` is then reassigned to a healthy "egress-assignable" node, and the cluster manager updates the `EgressIP` object status to reflect the new assignment. ##Scenario 2: Graceful Node Shutdown/Reboot During a graceful shutdown/reboot, the following sequence occurs:- **Detection**: Within the *5 second interval*, the health probe receives a *connection timeout*. The `ovnkube-cluster-manager` immediately reassigns the `EgressIP` to a new node.- **Transition & GARP**: The newly assigned node `broadcasts` a `Gratuitous ARP (GARP)` announcement to update the local network with its `MAC address`. Simultaneously, the `ovnkube-cluster-manager` and `ovnkube-node` pod on new node ensures the necessary `SNAT (Source Network Address Translation)` entries are created in the `OVN Northbound Database (OVN NBDB)` for the newly assigned node, ensuring the data path is correctly programmed for outbound traffic.- **Dual MAC Observation**: If an `arping` is executed simultaneously during the failover process, **two distinct MAC addresses** may respond for a single `EgressIP`. This overlapping state typically persists for several seconds. This `"dual MAC"` condition remains active until the networking services on the source node become inactive or enter a `"dead" state` during the shutdown sequence done by `systemd`. Once the original node’s services are fully terminated and the network interface is brought *down*, the legacy `MAC address` stops responding to `ARP` requests. Red Hat engineers are aware of this bug, see [EgressIP inconsistent MAC addresses during RHOCP 4 node reboot](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140923) for more details.- **Network Impact**: As long as the physical network switches are configured to *learn and update* `arp tables` based on `GARP announcements`, traffic will successfully route through the new node *without issue*. #### **Note: This behavior is not a regression of the issue mentioned in [KCS- egressIP GARP sent by incorrect node after reboot in RHCOP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7088619) and [OCPBUGS-63155](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-63155).**
root_cause: The failover mechanism is driven by the interaction between the OVN-K health-check client and the node's local services.- **Proactive Monitoring**: The `ovnkube-cluster-manager` uses a `gRPC` based "heartbeat" to verify the `egress data path`. When this *heartbeat fails* (due to pod restarts or service stops), it triggers the `EgressIP` controller's rebalancing logic.- **Service Termination Latency**: During a node reboot, the `ovnkube-node` pod is terminated, causing the health checks performed by the `ovnkube-cluster-manager` to fail. Consequently, the manager migrates the `EgressIP` to a healthy node. Because the `ovnkube-node pod` is no longer *active* during this transition, it cannot perform the removal of the `EgressIP` from the `local bridge interface (br-ex)`.- **ARP Race Condition**: The `EgressIP` is only fully removed once the network interface state is set to `"down"` as part of the standard operating system reboot workflow. Therefore, it is **expected** to observe multiple `MAC addresses` responding for a single `EgressIP` during the interval between the `ovnkube-cluster-manager` reassignment and the moment the primary `bridge interface (br-ex)`, on the original node, is physically brought down.

title: KRaft migration in Streams for Apache Kafka
issue: - Is KRaft officially supported in Streams for Apache Kafka 2.8/2.9?- Is it considered safe and stable for production deployments in 2.8/2.9?- Are there any known limitations for using KRaft mode under Red Hat's support policy for versions 2.8/2.9?
resolution: - For **OpenShift** deployments, KRaft mode is officially supported and considered production ready(i.e. generally available) since [version 2.8](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.8/html-single/release_notes_for_streams_for_apache_kafka_2.8_on_openshift/index#kraft_support_moves_to_ga).- Documentation for KRaft migration for OpenShift deployments [is available here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.8/html-single/deploying_and_managing_streams_for_apache_kafka_on_openshift/index#proc-deploy-migrate-kraft-str).- For **RHEL** deployments, it is still a [technology preview](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.8/html-single/release_notes_for_streams_for_apache_kafka_2.8_on_rhel/index#kraft_mode) in version 2.8. It is generally available in version 2.9.- **Limitations:** In version 2.8 scaling of KRaft controller-only nodes up or down is not supported: [RHEL](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.8/html-single/release_notes_for_streams_for_apache_kafka_2.8_on_rhel/index#kraft_mode), [OpenShift](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.8/html-single/release_notes_for_streams_for_apache_kafka_2.8_on_openshift/index#kraft_support_moves_to_ga).

title: Live Migrating Virtual Machines leaves many virt-launcher pods in Completed state
issue: Many virt-launcher pods in Completed state exist in the cluster
Live Migration of Virtual Machine does not delete source node virt-launcher pod, which remains in Completed state.
RWO vTPM Persistent Volume Claims (PVC) remain in `Terminating` state
resolution: * An RFE to improve this has been raised, see [CNV-36218- RFE- Cleanup old live migration source virt-launcher pods](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-36218). * These pods do not pose any harm * If desired they can be manually deleted or some automatic cleanup as explained in [How to use the cronjob for deleting all the pods with 'Completed' status in OpenShift Container Platform 4?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6934861) or using a policy can be setup as well.
root_cause: * This is expected. While the VirtualMachineMigrationInstance objects are garbage collected and only the last 5 are kept, the virt-launcher pods are not garbage collected. * The completed virt-launcher pods will all be deleted when the Virtual Machine is stopped (VMI object deletion). * Due to standard PVC `finalizers` a vTPM volume with `RWO` mode will remain in `Terminating` state as long as the completed pod exists.
