title: Unable to install cert-manager operator in OpenShift Cluster
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: While installing the cert-manager Operator getting an error: ~~~ Installing Operator RequirementsNotMet: one or more requirements couldn't be found The Operator is being installed. This may take a few minutes. View installed Operators in Namespace cert-manager-operator ~~~
resolution: - Deleting all the unsupported CRDs and keep only the supported v1 version.- Reinstall the stable version of the cert-manager operator.
root_cause: - Due to multiple CRDs present in the cluster (v1, v1beta1, v1alpha2, v1alpha3 etc.) from the operator’s perspective, Supported only the v1 version.

title: How to configure Kiali in Service Mesh 3 to use Prometheus User Workload Monitoring
issue: Need to set up Kiali to pull the metrics from User Workload Monitoring
resolution: The cluster should have already deployed Service Mesh 3, and User Workload Monitoring Configured. Deploy Kiali with the following configuration. This configuration assumes that Service Mesh 3 is installed in the `namespace` "istio-system", and that the monitoring stack is deployed in the `namespace` "openshift-monitoring" ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: name: kiali-monitoring-rbac roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: cluster-monitoring-view subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: kiali-service-account namespace: istio-system--- kind: Kiali apiVersion: kiali.io/v1alpha1 metadata: name: kiali namespace: istio-system spec: version: default istio_namespace: istio-system deployment: logger: log_level: debug view_only_mode: false external_services: prometheus: auth: type: bearer use_kiali_token: true thanos_proxy: enabled: true url: https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9091 ~~~ In the `namespace` where the application is deployed, create the following `ServiceMonitor`. This will create a `target` in Prometheus, and Kiali will be able to fetch the metrics from that target. ~~~ apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: ServiceMonitor metadata: name: servicemonitor-application spec: selector: matchExpressions:- key: istio-prometheus-ignore operator: DoesNotExist endpoints:- interval: 30s path: /stats/prometheus relabelings:- action: keep regex: istio-proxy sourceLabels:-__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_name- action: keep sourceLabels:-__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotationpresent_prometheus_io_scrape- action: replace regex: (\d+);(([A-Fa-f0-9]{1,4}::?){1,7}[A-Fa-f0-9]{1,4}) replacement: '[$2]:$1' sourceLabels:-__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_port-__meta_kubernetes_pod_ip targetLabel:__address__- action: replace regex: (\d+);((([0-9]+?)(\.|$)){4}) replacement: $2:$1 sourceLabels:-__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_port-__meta_kubernetes_pod_ip targetLabel:__address__- action: labeldrop regex:__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_(.+)- action: replace sourceLabels:-__meta_kubernetes_namespace targetLabel: namespace- action: replace sourceLabels:-__meta_kubernetes_pod_name targetLabel: pod_name ~~~ After a couple of minutes, if there is traffic to/from the application, the Kiali console will start showing the traffic.
root_cause: Kiali is not deployed by default in Service Mesh 3, and by default it does not pull the metrics from the monitoring stack.

title: Ansible Automation Platform Operator upgrade gets stuck with "manifest unknown" error
issue: - The upgrade to the latest version of the Ansible Automation Platform Operator on RHOCP gets stuck while trying to pull the specific `ose-kube-rbac-proxy` needed by the operator with the following error: ~~~ Failed to pull image "registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-kube-rbac-proxy@sha256:514e9e03f1d96046ff819798e54aa5672621c15805d61fb6137283f83f57a1e3": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = reading manifest sha256:514e9e03f1d96046ff819798e54aa5672621c15805d61fb6137283f83f57a1e3 in registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-kube-rbac-proxy: manifest unknown ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering and the team is working on a solution. For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support. Two possible workarounds are available: 1. Reapply the CSV manifest from the old version of the operator (ie: for the namespace-scoped operator, the one before `v2.4.0+0.1725256739` should be `v2.4.0+0.1720482179`) giving up for now the latest updates. 2. Edit the current CSV manifest and replace the ose-kube-rbac-proxy digest reference to a newer one. Right now, the latest available is `9674694d47bf0056d6ff9ab3c9f8d0849399ac66c74c98b63bc8fa68c8aaec58`.

title: ODF Regional DR failed to add rbd-mirror peer token for pool "ocs-storagecluster- cephblockpool". : signal: interrupt
issue: failed to add rbd-mirror peer token for pool "ocs-storagecluster- cephblockpool".: signal: interrupt
resolution: This indicates a communication issue between the 2 managed ODF clusters. The communication takes place via IPsec tunnel with submariner. First check the ACM / HUB managed cluster set and ensure the submariner add-on is showing all green check marks. Next check for firewall rules that may be blocking the required ports listed here. [ODF Regional DR ports that need to be unblocked by firewall rules](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7056550) This can be verified by running curl-kv with: < port number > from a node or pod from one managed cluster to another. Once all ports are open re check to see if the issue still persists. You can also restart the mirror pods on ODF for both managed clusters. ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-storage | grep mirror ~~~ If you are still experiencing issues with connectivity with the same error. > failed to add rbd-mirror peer token for pool "ocs-storagecluster- cephblockpool".: signal: interrupt The next step would be to install subctl and check the following: ~~~ $ curl-Ls https://get.submariner.io | VERSION=latest bash export PATH=$PATH:~/.local/bin echo export PATH=\$PATH:~/.local/bin > > ~/.profile $ subctl show connections ~~~ AND this may help resolve: [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.13/html/troubleshooting/troubleshooting#resolving-submariner-data-plane](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.13/html/troubleshooting/troubleshooting#resolving-submariner-data-plane) ~~~ Example verify command: oc logim via api link oc login via api link export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config kubectl config get-contexts subctl verify--verbose--only connectivity--context default/api-cos5-vmw-openshift-eu:6443/kube:admin--tocontext default/api-cos6-vmw-openshift-eu:6443/kube:admin--image-override submariner-nettest=quay.io/submariner/nettest:devel--packet-size 200 ~~~
root_cause: Connectivity failure between 2 ACM managed ODF clusters.

title: Red Hat OpenShift 4 cluster fails to recover after long shutdown
issue: OpenShift cluster is unreachable after an extended shutdown.
The following control plane components are unavailable and have its internal certificates expired: `kube-apiserver`, `kube-scheduler`, and `kube-controller-manager`, while `etcd` is healthy.
Not able to login into cluster via oc login due to certificate expired.
resolution: **Reinstall the cluster** as it is not supported to keep an OpenShift cluster powered off for more than **90 days** from version 4.18, before this version a cluster can stay powered off for no more than 30 days. See [Hibernating a cluster for up to 90 days](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/release_notes/ocp-4-18-release-notes#ocp-4-18-hibernating_release-notes). ### Workaround {#workaround} **Warning:** This workaround is not guaranteed to recover the cluster. Index: [1. Prerequisite](#prereq) [2. Renew the client tokens, if needed](#token) [3. Manually rotate the API certificates](#apicerts) [4. Renew the Kube-controller-manager and Kube-scheduler client certificates](#kcm-client) [5. Update the client-ca certificate](#client-ca) [6. Renew the kubelet certificate on control-plane nodes](#kubelet) #### 1. Prerequisite {#prereq} Cluster is accessible with the `localhost-recovery.kubeconfig`: 1a. Access one of the control-plane nodes using SSH: ~~~ $ ssh-i core@ ~~~ 1b. Export the `KUBECONFIG` variable with the `localhost-recovery.kubeconfig`: ~~~ $ export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/node-kubeconfigs/localhost-recovery.kubeconfig ~~~ 1c. Confirm it is possible to interact with the API by running any `oc` command like: ~~~ $ oc get nodes ~~~ #### 2. Renew the client tokens, if needed {#token} 2a. Open the container logs to see if they can connect to the API: ~~~ $ crictl logs $(crictl ps--name kube-apiserver-cert-regeneration-controller-q) $ crictl logs $(crictl ps--name kube-apiserver-cert-syncer-q) $ crictl logs $(crictl ps--name kube-controller-manager-cert-syncer-q) $ crictl logs $(crictl ps--name kube-scheduler-cert-syncer-q) ~~~ 2b. If they are failing reporting errors like `"Unauthorized` execute the following to renew the client tokens: Get the location of the current tokens: ~~~ $ KAStoken=$(crictl inspect $(crictl ps--name kube-apiserver-cert-syncer-q) |jq-r '.status.mounts[]|select(.containerPath=="/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources").hostPath')/secrets/localhost-recovery-client-token/token $ KCMtoken=$(crictl inspect $(crictl ps--name kube-controller-manager-cert-syncer-q) |jq-r '.status.mounts[]|select(.containerPath=="/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources").hostPath')/secrets/localhost-recovery-client-token/token $ KStoken=$(crictl inspect $(crictl ps--name kube-scheduler-cert-syncer-q) |jq-r '.status.mounts[]|select(.containerPath=="/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources").hostPath')/secrets/localhost-recovery-client-token/token ~~~ Take a backup of the tokens: ~~~ $ cp-p ${KAStoken} ${KAStoken}_bck $ cp-p ${KCMtoken} ${KCMtoken}_bck $ cp-p ${KStoken} ${KStoken}_bck ~~~ Create new tokens: ~~~ $ oc create token localhost-recovery-client-n openshift-kube-apiserver--duration=50000h > ${KAStoken} $ oc create token localhost-recovery-client-n openshift-kube-controller-manager--duration=50000h > ${KCMtoken} $ oc create token localhost-recovery-client-n openshift-kube-scheduler--duration=50000h > ${KStoken} ~~~ Test the new tokens: ~~~ $ curl-sk-H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat $KAStoken)"-XGET https://localhost:6443/api/v1/nodes/ |head $ curl-sk-H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat $KCMtoken)"-XGET https://localhost:6443/api/v1/nodes/ |head $ curl-sk-H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat $KStoken)"-XGET https://localhost:6443/api/v1/nodes/ |head ~~~ 2c. Copy the same tokens in the other control-plane nodes. #### 3. Manually rotate the API certificates {#apicerts} ~~~ $ oc adm ocp-certificates regenerate-leaf-n openshift-kube-apiserver secret external-loadbalancer-serving-certkey internal-loadbalancer-serving-certkey ~~~ **Note:** this command adds the annotation `auth.openshift.io/certificate-not-after: force-regeneration` in the secrets, container `kube-apiserver-cert-regeneration-controller` rotate them and container `kube-apiserver-cert-syncer` writes them in the nodes in `/etc/kubernetes/static-pod-resources/kube-apiserver-certs/secrets/`. **Note 2:** See [Regenerating Openshift Cluster Certificates due to FIPS misconfiguration](https://access.redhat.com/articles/regenerating_cluster_certificates) for more details if needed. #### 4. Renew the Kube-controller-manager and Kube-scheduler client certificates {#kcm-client} Verify the client certificates are automatically renewed and synced from `openshift-config-managed` namespace: ~~~ $ oc get secret kube-scheduler-client-cert-key-n openshift-config-managed-o yaml $ oc get secret kube-scheduler-client-cert-key-n openshift-kube-scheduler-o yaml ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get secret-n openshift-config-managed secrets kube-controller-manager-client-cert-key-o yaml $ oc get secret kube-controller-manager-client-cert-key-n openshift-kube-controller-manager-o yaml ~~~ If not double-check point 2. #### 5. Update the client-ca certificate {#client-ca} Ensure that content of secret `openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator/csr-signer` is present in the configmap `openshift-kube-apiserver/client-ca`: ~~~ $ csrcert=$(oc get secret-n openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator csr-signer-o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' |base64-d) $ oc get configmap-n openshift-kube-apiserver client-ca-o yaml |grep-o-- "${csrcert}" ~~~ If not included include it by running: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-kube-apiserver get cm/client-ca-o jsonpath='{.data.ca\-bundle\.crt}' > /var/tmp/client-ca_ca-bundle.crt $ oc-n openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator get secret/csr-signer-o json | jq-r '.data["tls.crt"]|@base64d' > > /var/tmp/client-ca_ca-bundle.crt $ oc create configmap client-ca-n openshift-kube-apiserver--from-file=ca-bundle.crt=/var/tmp/client-ca_ca-bundle.crt--dry-run=client-o yaml |oc apply-f- ~~~ #### 6. Renew the kubelet certificate on control-plane nodes {#kubelet} See [How to recover from all nodes' certificate expiry in OpenShift Container Platform 4?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6992388).
root_cause: The cluster was powered off longer than supported and many certificates and tokens have expired. How internal components work:- Container `kube-apiserver-cert-regeneration-controller` recreate the certificates if `auth.openshift.io/certificate-not-after: force-regeneration` annotation is present.- Container `kube-apiserver-cert-syncer` writes the certificates from API to the control-plane nodes.- Containers `kube-controller-manager-cert-syncer` and `kube-scheduler-cert-syncer` sync the certificates from `openshift-config-managed` to their namespaces.- Kubelet uses `/etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig` only if `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig` is missing or not working.- Content of secret `openshift-kube-controller-manager-operator/csr-signer` must be into the configmap `openshift-kube-apiserver/client-ca` to trust kubelet client certificates.

title: Red Hat Developer Hub Orchestrator plugin ignores external dataIndexService and forces local SonataFlow deployment
issue: - We are reporting an issue following the upgrade of Red Hat Developer Hub (RHDH) and the Orchestrator plugins to version 1.8.2.- Despite having a functional Orchestrator infrastructure managed by the OpenShift Serverless Logic Operator in a separate namespace (sonataflow-infra), the new version of the RHDH Orchestrator plugin appears to ignore the external dataIndexService configuration. This results in 404 errors and an unwanted attempt by the RHDH Operator to provision a local SonataFlow instance.- The RHDH Operator automatically attempts to deploy SonataFlow pods (DataIndex, JobService) in the rhdh namespace. These pods fail to start (CrashLoopBackOff) because they require a local database (backstage-psql-secret-rhdh and backstage-psql-rhdh) which does not exist in our environment. Manually creating the missing Secret/Service temporarily restores functionality, but the RHDH Operator deletes them during the next reconciliation cycle and the dataIndexService URL provided in the pluginConfig is ignored by the system.
resolution: To disable creating default objects users need to disable creating dependencies like this: ~~~- package: "@redhat/backstage-plugin-orchestrator-backend-dynamic@1.8.2" disabled: false dependencies: [{}] ~~~ However, `dependencies: [{}]` does not remove any previously created objects, so the objects created by `sonataflow.yaml` have to be removed manually. Make sure to remove all references to the RHDH namespace for the Orchestrator plugin.

title: How to collect cluster Prometheus metrics in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
issue: How to collect cluster Prometheus metrics in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform.
How to provide specific time range from a Prometheus DB.
resolution: ### Complete collection {#complete} * One option to capture cluster prometheus metrics is with the following script. Once the capture of data is complete, please share this data with Red Hat Technical Support via a support case. ~~~ cat < <'EOF' > prometheus-metrics.sh #!/usr/bin/env bash function queue() {local TARGET="${1}" shift local LIVE LIVE="$(jobs | wc-l)" while [["${LIVE}"-ge 45]]; do sleep 1 LIVE="$(jobs | wc-l)" done echo "${@}" if [[-n "${FILTER:-}"]]; then "${@}" | "${FILTER}" > "${TARGET}" & else "${@}" > "${TARGET}" & fi} ARTIFACT_DIR=$PWD mkdir-p $ARTIFACT_DIR/metrics echo "Snapshotting prometheus (may take 15s)..." queue ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/metrics/prometheus.tar.gz oc--insecure-skip-tls-verify exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-- tar cvzf--C /prometheus. FILTER=gzip queue ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/metrics/prometheus-target-metadata.json.gz oc--insecure-skip-tls-verify exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-- /bin/bash-c "curl-G http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets/metadata--data-urlencode 'match_target={instance!=\"\"}'" wait EOF bash prometheus-metrics.sh ~~~ **The script above may not work completely, as the generated tar file might fail to extract because the script copies files while Prometheus is actively working on them. Using the collection method below might be a better option.** ### Partial collection {#partial} * If a specific time range from your Prometheus database needs to be selected, use the following commands to list the Block ULID, copy the directories, and then compress the folders. 1. Get the list of time block chunks you wish to review: ~~~ $ oc exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-- promtool tsdb list-r /prometheus BLOCK ULID MIN TIME MAX TIME DURATION NUM SAMPLES NUM CHUNKS NUM SERIES SIZE 01GGQV2KWQ7DX0RAHWZZFPCNTM 2022-10-31 17:17:39 +0000 UTC 2022-10-31 18:00:00 +0000 UTC 42m20.389s 15306022 215664 215457 46MiB747KiB476B 01GGRRZ7B4VMK4PGENCKC642FK 2022-10-31 18:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 133853179 1122268 195484 161MiB1016KiB281B 01GGSDJDEDKAVW84H85123N5DW 2022-11-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-01 06:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 135702215 1140143 199963 166MiB899KiB888B 01GGT25KJ6HQ0SK622J57PNZ4M 2022-11-01 06:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-01 12:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 135950916 1147756 230258 190MiB936KiB527B 01GGTPRRYWQXTNE8C4D3KD40WF 2022-11-01 12:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-01 18:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 135618858 1169963 224173 178MiB160KiB467B 01GGVBBYM6R3MV21Q84KCAAMMH 2022-11-01 18:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-02 00:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 139185809 1165518 201794 172MiB206KiB895B 01GGVZZ4CDD2FN548AZ5QWHYSF 2022-11-02 00:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-02 06:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 139566486 1171364 204422 169MiB81KiB250B 01GGWMJBTHJEH4VQBC2361RTEH 2022-11-02 06:00:00 +0000 UTC 2022-11-02 12:00:00 +0000 UTC 5h59m59.811s 140284758 1175662 203168 172MiB559KiB886B ~~~ 2. From the previous output, update the below script (or execute the lines sequentially) to pull the blocks and chunk data for analysis (you must set the values for "blocks" to match your output first). ~~~ #!/bin/bash ## IMPORTANT: set the block UUIDs to be copied first in a space-delimited list (depends upon your output above) blocks="01GGQV2KWQ7DX0RAHWZZFPCNTM 01GGRRZ7B4VMK4PGENCKC642FK" CAPTUREDIR=./data mkdir-p $CAPTUREDIR for i in $(echo $blocks); do mkdir-p $CAPTUREDIR/$i/chunks; done for i in $(echo $blocks); do for file in index meta.json tombstones; do oc exec-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0-c prometheus-- cat /prometheus/$i/$file > $CAPTUREDIR/$i/$file; done; done for i in $(echo $blocks); do oc cp-n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0:/prometheus/$i-c prometheus $CAPTUREDIR/$i; done oc cp-n openshift-monitoring-c prometheus prometheus-k8s-0:chunks_head $CAPTUREDIR/chunks_head #Note capturing Wal segment may report "file changed as we read it"- we can ignore this error oc cp-n openshift-monitoring-c prometheus prometheus-k8s-0:wal $CAPTUREDIR/wal oc cp-n openshift-monitoring-c prometheus prometheus-k8s-0:queries.active $CAPTUREDIR/queries.active tar-zcvf prometheus-db.tar.gz ${CAPTUREDIR} ~~~ We should see in the output of these directories the following files: ~~~ ~/Downloads/data tree. ├── 01K94F3NNVR4YG19FB8E1YDZ7K # chunk directory for specific time selection │ ├── chunks │ │ └── 000001 │ ├── index │ ├── meta.json │ └── tombstones ├── 01K94NZZ6M1194YNR4KBFCFF27 │ ├── chunks │ │ ├── 000001 │ │ └── 000002 │ ├── index │ ├── meta.json │ └── tombstones ├── chunks_head ├── queries.active └── wal └── 00000000 ~~~ Ensure that we aren't missing the `index`, `meta.json` or `tombstones` file for a given `chunk directory`- without these the chunk cannot be parsed, and you may need to go back to pull these files explicitly out of the pod. `chunks_head` and `queries.active` and `wal` is also required to parse the chunk blocks. ### Cluster Observability Operator {#COO} In the case of needing to collect a Prometheus dump from the Cluster Observability Operator, use the following commands: The Cluster Observability Operator Prometheus instance pods do not contain the `tar` binary ~~~ $ datadir=./data $ mkdir-p $datadir ## set the block ULIDs to be copied: $ blocks="01J0T747YMVTQHT5AK122TD9K8 01J0T08GPMBY81J1SHHRYSS0GF 01J0SSCSEKP4RRR5MK9DQ9S103" $ for i in $(echo $blocks); do mkdir-p $datadir/$i/chunks; done $ for i in $(echo $blocks); do for file in index meta.json tombstones; do oc exec-n $NAMESPACE prometheus-coo-monitoring-stack-0-c prometheus-- cat /prometheus/$i/$file > $datadir/$i/$file; done; done $ for i in $(echo $blocks); do oc exec-n $NAMESPACE prometheus-coo-monitoring-stack-0-c prometheus-- cat /prometheus/$i/chunks/000001 > $datadir/$i/chunks/000001; done $ tar zcvf prometheus-db.tar.gz ${datadir} ~~~ ### Opening Prometheus data for offline review with podman {#review} This can be accomplished using podman and a simple launch script: $ cat prometheus_viewer.sh ~~~ #!/bin/bash #prometheus launcher #provided as-is with no warranty for use in troubleshooting or analysis of prometheus data bundles. # #script assumes you have podman installed, firefox is available, and that you can call the file ~/Downloads/data. #script also assumes you have a pull-secret available to reference to acquire the correct runtime image. # #Running this script will prompt you first to confirm you have completed the requisite step of un-compressing #the tarball of the promql output into your downloads directory, and then will prompt for the exact clusterversion #after which it will kick-start a container and open a web browser session to the locally running prometheus instance. ##-----Script start-----## echo "this script assumes you have already expanded a tarball of the prometheus-db.tar.gz file to the directory: ~/Downloads/data" echo "press return to continue or ctrl + c to abort and do that first" read emptyvar1 #ensure we match the same version of promql from openshift that was used to generate the data echo "insert clusterversion for the bundle you are reviewing" read OCP_VERSION IMG="$(oc adm release info--image-for=prometheus ${OCP_VERSION})" #load pull-secret (can be obtained from https://console.redhat.com/openshift/downloads)" PULL_SECRET= ### Retrieve the image URL and run the container (here using `-ti` option to run it in foreground mode) ### The script below will assume that our data directory is in ~/Downloads and load $PWD/data after going there. ### You may need to adjust where the data directory is, and where the script takes you to execute below if different. ### Script will also try to launch firefox, change this to chrome or edge or your preferred browser executable ### Or just open your webrowser at that page. #navigate to ~/Downloads so we can reference $PWD/data cd ~/Downloads/ #open firefox so the page is available and load the container as a session in this shell in the foreground. echo "launching firefox in a new window and starting the container below- press ctrl+c to stop the process and remove the container when finished" firefox http://localhost:9090/ & podman run--rm--authfile=${PULL_SECRET}-it-u $(id-u):$(id-g)-p 9090:9090-v $PWD/data:/data:U,Z $IMG--storage.tsdb.path=/data--storage.tsdb.retention.time=999d--config.file=/dev/null ~~~ NOTE: Script requires a [pull secret](https://console.redhat.com/openshift/downloads)- edit the script above to include the path to this file locally on your machine before execution. **Usage:** 1. copy this script to your local machine that where `podman` and a local browser like `firefox` is available and un-compress the prometheus tarball in the path: `~/Downloads` (should result in the folder: `~/Downloads/data` being created) 2. Modify the script to include a path to the local pull-secret file where the script can reference it 3. Modify the script to select a different browser if not using firefox or to point to where the expanded `data` folder is. 4. Execute the script, pressing return to acknowledge the first message, then insert the exact clusterversion (4.18.24 for example) to pull that image version. 5. Open your browser to http://localhost:9090 (if it does not automatically launch and wait for the container to finish setup- you may need to refresh the page once or twice before it will populate). 6. Query for a wide time-range (7d or so) and search for a very generic query like the following in graph view: `sum(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="true"}==1)` #number of ready nodes in the cluster. 7. highlight the block where you see data in the graph to see the specific time segments you exported which will adjust your range to this timeframe only and then run the queries you want with the correctly scoped view.

title: [RHOSO 18] - Customize EDPM LVM Partition Sizes
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - How to change the default disk layout of unprovisioned EDPM nodes in RHOSO 18
resolution: - Modify the [OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet CR template](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html/deploying_red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/assembly_creating-the-data-plane#ref_OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet-CR-properties_dataplane)- Example: ~~~ nodeTemplate:... ansible:... ansibleVars: growvols_args: > /=30GB /tmp=10GB /home=10GB /var/log=50GB /var/log/audit=5GB /var=90% ~~~ Default configuration: ~~~ growvols_args: type: str default: > /=8GB /tmp=1GB /var/log=10GB /var/log/audit=2GB /home=1GB /var=100% ~~~ Additional Reference: [https://openstack-k8s-operators.github.io/edpm-ansible/roles/role-edpm_growvols.html](https://openstack-k8s-operators.github.io/edpm-ansible/roles/role-edpm_growvols.html)

title: [RHOSO 18] - Control Plane Hot Fix Example - cinder-volume
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Apply hotfix RPMs to Openstack Control Plane Pod(s)
resolution: - See [this KCS](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7133487) for Data Plane hot fix.- *Important*: By default the image registry operator is installed but image storage may not be configured. Configure image registry storage as outlined [here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/registry/setting-up-and-configuring-the-registry#installation-registry-storage-config_configuring-registry-storage-baremetal). If Storage is not configured builds will fail with the following error: ~~~ Error from server (BadRequest): build cinder-hotfix-1 failed: InvalidOutputReference: Output image could not be resolved. ~~~ **Example Walk-through of Applying Hot Fix to Cinder Volume Container**- Get current State of cinder-volume: ~~~ $ oc get pods-l service=cinder-l component=cinder-volume NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cinder-volume-ceph-0 2/2 Running 0 8m9s ~~~- Show current container images: ~~~ $ oc get pod/cinder-volume-ceph-0-o json| jq-r '.spec.containers.[]|"\(.name) \(.image)"' cinder-volume registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-cinder-volume-rhel9@sha256:c1f7aeeae675ddef99acd5ad224cd7425b90f26940b5bd7692dda3c011d1c405 probe registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-cinder-volume-rhel9@sha256:c1f7aeeae675ddef99acd5ad224cd7425b90f26940b5bd7692dda3c011d1c405 ~~~- Here "registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-cinder-volume-rhel9@sha256:c1f7aeeae675ddef99acd5ad224cd7425b90f26940b5bd7692dda3c011d1c405" is the container image to patch- Verify container user and quit ~~~ $ oc rsh-c cinder-volume cinder-volume-ceph-0 whoami cinder $ exit ~~~- If this user is not 'root' then we need to switch to root and back to container user in Dockerfile as shown in the example below.- Setup Hot Fix environment ~~~ mkdir hotfix ~~~- Copy all hotfix RPMs into hotfix/ dir ~~~ $ ls hotfix/ openstack-cinder-22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch.rpm python3-cinder-22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch.rpm python3-cinder-common-22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch.rpm ~~~- Create Dockerfile in hotfix/ dir, use container image as discovered above. Set USER as outlined to switch between root and cinder. ~~~ $ cat hotfix/Dockerfile FROM registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-cinder-volume-rhel9@sha256:c1f7aeeae675ddef99acd5ad224cd7425b90f26940b5bd7692dda3c011d1c405 USER root COPY *.rpm /tmp/ RUN dnf update-y--nobest /tmp/*.rpm RUN dnf clean all RUN rm-f /tmp/*.rpm USER cinder ~~~- Create hotfix.yaml that defines the imagestream and buildconfig: ~~~ $ cat hotfix.yaml apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: cinder-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: lookupPolicy: local: true--- apiVersion: build.openshift.io/v1 kind: BuildConfig metadata: name: cinder-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: output: to: kind: ImageStreamTag name: cinder-hotfix:latest source: type: Binary strategy: type: Docker triggers:- type: ConfigChange ~~~- Apply hotfix.yaml to create build environment: ~~~ $ oc apply-f hotfix.yaml imagestream.image.openshift.io/cinder-hotfix created buildconfig.build.openshift.io/cinder-hotfix created ~~~- Start binary build to use local RPMs and Dockerfile: ~~~ $ oc start-build cinder-hotfix--from-dir=hotfix/--follow Uploading directory "hotfix" as binary input for the build... Uploading finished build.build.openshift.io/cinder-hotfix-3 started Receiving source from STDIN as archive... [...] Upgraded: openstack-cinder-1:22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch python3-cinder-1:22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch python3-cinder-common-1:22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch Complete! [...] Copying config sha256:c06ecf9723690ff89498375cd01aba2c19ed6a9baa5a90c12611e144f1a36a99 Writing manifest to image destination Successfully pushed image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openstack/cinder-hotfix@sha256:8979d859629edecfae7e33e48ae4bee3bd0ae933515e4680288161 422b713ba8 Push successful ~~~- Update the openstackversion CR to use hotfix image ~~~ $ cat openstackversionpatch.yaml spec: customContainerImages: cinderVolumeImages: ceph: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openstack/cinder-hotfix@sha256:8979d859629edecfae7e33e48ae4bee3bd0ae933515e4680288161422b713ba8 $ oc patch openstackversion openstack-control-plane--type=merge--patch-file openstackversionpatch.yaml openstackversion.core.openstack.org/openstack-control-plane patched ~~~- Verify pod is running hot fix image ~~~ $ oc get pods-l service=cinder-l component=cinder-volume NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE cinder-volume-ceph-0 2/2 Running 0 30s $ oc get pod/cinder-volume-ceph-0-o json| jq-r '.spec.containers.[]|"\(.name) \(.image)"' cinder-volume image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openstack/cinder-hotfix@sha256:8979d859629edecfae7e33e48ae4bee3bd0ae933515e4680288161422b713ba8 probe image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openstack/cinder-hotfix@sha256:8979d859629edecfae7e33e48ae4bee3bd0ae933515e4680288161422b713ba8 $ oc rsh-c cinder-volume cinder-volume-ceph-0 rpm-qa |grep cinder python3-cinderclient-9.3.0-18.0.20240620163745.f7a612e.el9ost.noarch python3-cinder-common-22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch python3-cinder-22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch openstack-cinder-22.3.1-18.0.20251015144659.ae2d250.el9osttrunk.noarch ~~~- To remove hotfix container from openstackversion CR and return to default image: ~~~ oc patch openstackversion openstack-control-plane--type=json-p='[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/customContainerImages/cinderVolumeImages"}]' ~~~

title: [RHOSO 18] - Data Plane Hot Fix Example - nova_compute
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Apply Hot Fix RPMs to Openstack Data Plane Container(s)
resolution: - The Data Plane hot fix procedure is similar to the Control Plane [procedure](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7133065); however, accessing the OCP image-registry from external systems requires several additional configurations. **Pre-requisites** 1. Ensure image-registry operator is configured.- *Important*: By default the image registry operator is installed but image storage may not be configured. Configure image registry storage as outlined [here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/registry/setting-up-and-configuring-the-registry#installation-registry-storage-config_configuring-registry-storage-baremetal). If storage is not configured builds will fail with the following error: ~~~ Error from server (BadRequest): build nova-hotfix-1 failed: InvalidOutputReference: Output image could not be resolved. ~~~ 2. Enable external network access via a service "route" to the registry.- Check if the image-registry is available via an OCP "route": ~~~ $ oc get route-n openshift-image-registry NAME HOST/PORT PATH SERVICES PORT TERMINATION WILDCARD default-route default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab image-registry reencrypt None ~~~- If this route is not present, create it: ~~~ $ oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io/cluster--patch '{"spec":{"defaultRoute":true}}'--type=merge ~~~- Get the route hostname ~~~ $ REG_HOST=$(oc get route-n openshift-image-registry default-route-o json |jq-r.spec.host); echo $REG_HOST ~~~ 3. Create CA Trust on the EDPM nodes for the image-registry CA.- By default the SSL certificate will be signed by an internal ingress controller CA. To verify this: ~~~ $ openssl s_client-connect ${REG_HOST}:443 2> /dev/null cacerts.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: cacerts namespace: openstack type: Opaque data: ingressCa: $CACERT EOF $ cat cacerts.yaml $ oc apply-f cacerts.yaml ~~~- Edit the Openstack Control Plane CR and add a tls spec if not present. ~~~ $ oc get oscp NAME STATUS MESSAGE openstack-control-plane True Setup complete ~~~ ~~~ oc edit oscp/openstack-control-plane ~~~- Add the following tls spec: ~~~ spec: tls: podLevel: enabled: true caBundleSecretName: cacerts ~~~ 4. Create a service account with access to the image-registry.- Create a 'hotfix' service account ~~~ $ oc create serviceaccount hotfix-n openstack serviceaccount/hotfix created ~~~- Get 'hotfix' service account name: ~~~ $ HOTFIX_USER=$(oc get sa hotfix-n openstack-o json |jq-r '."imagePullSecrets".[]."name"'); echo $HOTFIX_USER hotfix-dockercfg-cj9dx ~~~- Create 30 day token ~~~ $ HOTFIX_TOKEN=$(oc create token--duration=2592000s hotfix-n openstack); echo $HOTFIX_TOKEN ~~~- Note: to get token for existing hotfix serviceaccount: ~~~ $ oc get secret $(oc get sa hotfix-n openstack-o json |jq-r '."imagePullSecrets".[]."name"')-o json| jq-r '.data.".dockercfg"'|base64-d |jq-r ".\"${REG_HOST}\".\"auth\""|base64-d|awk-F\: '{print $2}' ~~~- Delete and re-create the redhat-registry secret to include the hotfix registry credentials- Get the current redhat-registry secret: ~~~ $ oc get secret redhat-registry-o json |jq-r.data.edpm_container_registry_logins|base64-d|jq-r. {"registry.redhat.io": {" ": " "}} $ RH_REG_USER= $ RH_REG_PASS= ~~~ ~~~ $ oc delete secret redhat-registry ~~~ ~~~ $ oc create secret generic redhat-registry--from-literal edpm_container_registry_logins="{\"registry.redhat.io\": {\"${RH_REG_USER}\": \"${RH_REG_PASS}\"}, \"${REG_HOST}\": {\"${HOTFIX_USER}\": \"${HOTFIX_TOKEN}\"}}" ~~~- Verify the secret looks proper with credentials for both registries: ~~~ $ oc get secret redhat-registry-o json |jq-r.data.edpm_container_registry_logins|base64-d|jq-r. ~~~ 5. Setup DNS for image registry.- Depending on the DNS configuration EDPM nodes may not be able to resolve the image registry's name.- Verify on an EDPM node: ~~~ [root@compute18-node2 ~]# ping default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab ping: default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab: Name or service not known ~~~- If this fails like shown above an entry can be added for the dnsmasq pod(s):- Example (update the name and IP appropriate for your OCP deployment): ~~~ $ cat hotfixDns.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: labels: dnsmasqhosts: dnsdata namespace: openstack name: default-route-openshift-image-registry data: default-route-openshift-image-registry: | 10.28.1.21 default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab ~~~ ~~~ $ oc apply-f hotfixDns.yaml configmap/default-route-openshift-image-registry configured ~~~- Confirm: ~~~ [root@compute18-node2 ~]# ping-c1 default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab PING default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab (10.28.1.21) 56(84) bytes of data. 64 bytes from default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab (10.28.1.21): icmp_seq=1 ttl=62 time=3.11 ms ~~~ **Example Walk-through of Applying Hot Fix to Nova Compute Container**- On an EDPM node, get the current image to be patched: ~~~ [cloud-admin@compute18-node2 ~]$ sudo podman inspect nova_compute |grep-i ImageName "ImageName": "registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-nova-compute-rhel9@sha256:2239cd01182cbc2c6f491fb3bb2e4f9a2957c98ceb71ac16e45736fda91f4be7", ~~~- Here: "registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-nova-compute-rhel9@sha256:2239cd01182cbc2c6f491fb3bb2e4f9a2957c98ceb71ac16e45736fda91f4be7" is the container image to patch- Verify container user: ~~~ [cloud-admin@compute18-node2 ~]$ sudo podman exec-ti nova_compute whoami nova ~~~- If this user is not 'root' then we need to switch to root and back to container user in Dockerfile as shown in the example below.- Setup hot fix environment on OCP client machine: ~~~ mkdir hotfix ~~~- Copy all hot fix RPMs into hotfix/ dir ~~~ $ ls hotfix/ python3-nova-27.5.2-18.0.20250815124721.c1c6d67.el9ost.noarch openstack-nova-common-27.5.2-18.0.20250815124721.c1c6d67.el9ost.noarch openstack-nova-compute-27.5.2-18.0.20250815124721.c1c6d67.el9ost.noarch ~~~- Create Dockerfile in hotfix/ dir, use container image as discovered above. Set USER as outlined to switch between root and nova. ~~~ $ cat hotfix/Dockerfile FROM registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-nova-compute-rhel9@sha256:2239cd01182cbc2c6f491fb3bb2e4f9a2957c98ceb71ac16e45736fda91f4be7 USER root COPY *.rpm /tmp/ RUN dnf update-y--nobest /tmp/*.rpm RUN dnf clean all RUN rm-f /tmp/*.rpm USER nova ~~~- Create hotfix.yaml that defines the imagestream and buildconfig: ~~~ $ cat hotfix.yaml apiVersion: image.openshift.io/v1 kind: ImageStream metadata: name: nova-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: lookupPolicy: local: true--- apiVersion: build.openshift.io/v1 kind: BuildConfig metadata: name: nova-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: output: to: kind: ImageStreamTag name: nova-hotfix:latest source: type: Binary strategy: type: Docker triggers:- type: ConfigChange ~~~- Apply hotfix.yaml to create build environment: ~~~ $ oc apply-f hotfix.yaml imagestream.image.openshift.io/nova-hotfix created buildconfig.build.openshift.io/nova-hotfix created ~~~- Start binary build to use local RPMs and Dockerfile: ~~~ $ oc start-build nova-hotfix--from-dir=hotfix/--follow Uploading directory "hotfix" as binary input for the build... Uploading finished build.build.openshift.io/nova-hotfix-3 started Receiving source from STDIN as archive... [...] Upgraded: python3-nova-27.5.2-18.0.20250815124721.c1c6d67.el9ost.noarch openstack-nova-common-27.5.2-18.0.20250815124721.c1c6d67.el9ost.noarch openstack-nova-compute-27.5.2-18.0.20250815124721.c1c6d67.el9ost.noarch Complete! [...] Writing manifest to image destination Successfully pushed image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openstack/nova-hotfix@sha256:705c653d9951250907970c7295997e213af2e8b18322aaed2b93a5c6e481c160 Push successful ~~~ ~~~ $ oc get imagestream NAME IMAGE REPOSITORY TAGS UPDATED nova-hotfix default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab/openstack/nova-hotfix latest 3 minutes ago ~~~ The hotfix image is: "default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab/openstack/nova-hotfix:latest"- Get Container Image Parameter from openstackversion CR: ~~~ $ oc get openstackversion/openstack-control-plane-o json |grep registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-nova-compute-rhel9@sha256:2239cd01182cbc2c6f491fb3bb2e4f9a2957c98ceb71ac16e45736fda91f4be7 "novaComputeImage": "registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-nova-compute-rhel9@sha256:2239cd01182cbc2c6f491fb3bb2e4f9a2957c98ceb71ac16e45736fda91f4be7", ~~~- The Container image parameter to modify is: "novaComputeImage"- Patch the openstackversion CR to use the hot fix image: ~~~ $ cat openstackversionpatch.yaml spec: customContainerImages: novaComputeImage: default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab/openstack/nova-hotfix:latest $ oc patch openstackversion openstack-control-plane--type=merge--patch-file openstackversionpatch.yaml openstackversion.core.openstack.org/openstack-control-plane patched ~~~- To work-around a known issue, create data plane deployment that only runs the bootstrap service initially to update the CA data first. ~~~ $ cat dataplane-deploy_hotfix.yaml apiVersion: dataplane.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment metadata: name: data-plane-deploy-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: nodeSets:- openstack-data-plane servicesOverride:- bootstrap ~~~--OR- to limit to a specific node: ~~~ $ cat dataplane-deploy_hotfix.yaml apiVersion: dataplane.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment metadata: name: data-plane-deploy-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: nodeSets:- openstack-data-plane servicesOverride:- bootstrap ansibleLimit: compute18-node2 ~~~- Start the data plane deployment: ~~~ $ oc apply-f dataplane-deploy_hotfix.yaml openstackdataplanedeployment.dataplane.openstack.org/data-plane-deploy-hotfix created ~~~- Wait for data plane deployment to complete: ~~~ $ oc get osdpd/data-plane-deploy-hotfix NAME NODESETS STATUS MESSAGE data-plane-deploy-hotfix ["openstack-data-plane"] True Setup complete ~~~- Delete this data plane deployment: ~~~ $ oc delete osdpd/data-plane-deploy-hotfix ~~~- Then run another full data plane deployment: ~~~ $ cat dataplane-deploy_hotfix.yaml apiVersion: dataplane.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment metadata: name: data-plane-deploy-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: nodeSets:- openstack-data-plane ~~~--OR- to limit to a specific node: ~~~ $ cat dataplane-deploy_hotfix.yaml apiVersion: dataplane.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment metadata: name: data-plane-deploy-hotfix namespace: openstack spec: nodeSets:- openstack-data-plane ansibleLimit: compute18-node2 ~~~- Wait for data plane deployment to complete and verify hot fix container on edpm node: ~~~ [cloud-admin@compute18-node2 ~]$ sudo podman ps |grep nova_compute f2f365e16a97 default-route-openshift-image-registry.apps.rhoso.lab/openstack/nova-hotfix:latest kolla_start 21 hours ago Up 21 hours nova_compute ~~~- To remove hotfix container from openstackversion CR and return to default image: ~~~ oc patch openstackversion openstack-control-plane--type=json-p='[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/customContainerImages/novaComputeImage"}]' ~~~- Once the hotfix container is no longer required and removed from openstackcontrolplane CR, the 'hotfix' user in the redhat-registry secret should be removed as the expired token will cause future data plane deployment failures.- Get current config: ~~~ $ oc get secret redhat-registry-o json |jq-r.data.edpm_container_registry_logins|base64-d|jq-r. $ RH_REG_USER= $ RH_REG_PASS= ~~~ ~~~ $ oc delete secret redhat-registry ~~~ ~~~ oc create secret generic redhat-registry--from-literal edpm_container_registry_logins="{\"registry.redhat.io\": {\"${RH_REG_USER}\": \"${RH_REG_PASS}\"}}" ~~~

title: MicroShift GitOps Application Remains in Unknown State Due to Missing argocd-secret.server.secretkey
issue: The issue was fixed with the version [Red Hat OpenShift GitOps and MicroShift Gitops version 1.19.2](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2026:4581). When running the test application `pet-clinic` using the Gitops on Microshift, it fails due to missing 'server.secretkey' in argocd-secret. The `application` shows statsu `Unknown`. ~~~ $ oc get application-n openshift-gitops NAME SYNC STATUS HEALTH STATUS spring-petclinic Unknown Unknown ~~~
resolution: The issue is tracked in the bug in Root Cause. Before the fix, please check the workaround below.- Generate a random key and save it as variable. ~~~ $ GENERATED_SERVERKEY=$(openssl rand 32 | base64 | base64-w 0) ~~~- Patch the secret with the random key. ~~~ $ oc patch secret argocd-secret-n openshift-gitops-p "{\"data\":{\"server.secretkey\":\"$GENERATED_SERVERKEY\"}}" ~~~- Restart the Gitops application controller. ~~~ $ oc scale statefulset-n openshift-gitops argocd-application-controller--replicas=0 $ oc scale statefulset-n openshift-gitops argocd-application-controller--replicas=1 ~~~- Check the state of the application. ~~~ $ oc get application-n openshift-gitops NAME SYNC STATUS HEALTH STATUS spring-petclinic Synced Healthy ~~~

title: Clarification on Availability Zone–Aligned Subnets and Multi-Subnet Support in Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO)

resolution: - ARO is initially deployed with one worker subnet.- You cannot pin subnets to Availability Zones (AZs) during installation.- After deployment, you can:- Create additional subnets (one per AZ)- Use MachineSets to assign worker nodes to a specific AZ and subnet- This allows a multi-subnet, AZ-aligned architecture within the same cluster.

issue: How can the Red Hat build of OpenTelemetry be configured to receive data from HAProxy?
resolution: Integration of HAproxy with the Red Hat build of OpenTelemetry is not supported by Red Hat.

title: Node exporter netclass collector fails with "could not get link modes: netlink receive: operation not supported"
issue: The node-exporter pod in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace logs repeated errors: ``` level=error msg="collector failed" name=netclass duration_seconds=0.000894048 err="could not get link modes: netlink receive: operation not supported" ``` As a result, network-related monitoring metrics such as `node_network_up`, `node_network_info`, and other `node_network_*` metrics are missing for the affected nodes. These nodes do not appear in the Prometheus/web console metrics, causing monitoring gaps. The issue occurs on some nodes but not others, even though the VM configurations appear identical.
resolution: ### Workaround 1: Disable Netlink for the netclass collector Modify the `cluster-monitoring-config` ConfigMap to disable the netlink-based collector: ```bash oc edit cm cluster-monitoring-config-n openshift-monitoring ``` Set the configuration as follows: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 data: config.yaml: | enableUserWorkload: true nodeExporter: collectors: netclass: enabled: true useNetlink: false ``` Reference: [Config Map Reference for the Cluster Monitoring Operator- NodeExporterCollectorNetClassConfig](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/monitoring_stack_for_red_hat_openshift/4.16/html/config_map_reference_for_the_cluster_monitoring_operator/config-map-reference-for-the-cluster-monitoring-operator#nodeexportercollectornetclassconfig) Verify by checking that the node-exporter pods no longer log "collector failed" errors: ```bash oc logs-n openshift-monitoring-c node-exporter | grep "collector failed" ``` ### Workaround 2: Restart a pod on the affected node to refresh ifindex ordering Restart a pod in the `openshift-network-diagnostics` namespace on the affected node. This creates a new OVN interface with an ifindex higher than the unsupported interface (e.g., `genev_sys_6081`), preventing the failure: ```bash oc delete pod-n openshift-network-diagnostics ``` Verify by confirming that the node-exporter error logs stop and the missing `node_network_*` metrics reappear: ```bash curl-s http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep 'node_network_info' ``` ### Workaround 3: Reboot the affected node Rebooting the node resets all interface ifindex values to their default ordering, ensuring that the unsupported interfaces (e.g., `genev_sys_6081`) no longer have the highest ifindex. ### Permanent fix: Upgrade to OpenShift Container Platform 4.18 The node-exporter version shipped in OpenShift Container Platform 4.18 handles `LinkModes()` failures for unsupported interfaces gracefully. Even when an unsupported interface has the highest ifindex, the netclass collector does not fail. Upgrading to 4.18 permanently resolves this issue.
root_cause: This issue involves two contributing factors: **1. node-exporter netclass collector defect (OCP 4.16)** The node-exporter netclass collector uses a netlink-based ethtool library (`github.com/mdlayher/ethtool`) to perform a bulk `LinkModes()` dump (using `NLM_F_DUMP`) across all network interfaces. The kernel processes interfaces in ifindex order. When the **last** interface in the ifindex sequence is one that does not support ethtool link mode queries (such as `genev_sys_6081`, `ovs-system`, `ovn-k8s-mp0`, `br-int`, or `br-ex`), the kernel returns "operation not supported" as the final response, and the ethtool library treats this as a fatal error for the entire bulk operation. This causes the entire netclass collector to fail, resulting in all `node_network_*` metrics being missing for that node. Any interface that does not support ethtool `LinkModes()` can trigger this issue if it happens to have the highest ifindex on the node. **2. OVN rebuild causes genev_sys_6081 to be recreated with a high ifindex** When all OVN databases are rebuilt simultaneously (e.g., during EgressIP troubleshooting or OVN recovery operations), all geneve tunnels on each node are torn down at the same moment. OVS detects that no geneve tunnels exist and determines that the `genev_sys_6081` interface is no longer needed, so it deletes the interface. Once the OVN databases are restored and tunnels are re-established, OVS recreates `genev_sys_6081`, but the newly created interface is assigned a new, higher ifindex (e.g., 49 instead of the original 5). On nodes where no pod is subsequently scheduled or restarted after the rebuild, no new OVN veth interface is created with a higher ifindex, leaving `genev_sys_6081` as the last interface in the ifindex sequence and triggering the netclass collector failure described above.

title: Does Red Hat Connectivity Link support disconnected (air-gapped) clusters?

title: Support for UDN Layer 3 Network Topology in OpenShift Virtualization Virtual Machines
issue: - Virtual machines in OpenShift Virtualization fail to attach to the NetworkAttachmentDefinition (NAD) automatically created by a Layer 3 UserDefinedNetwork (UDN).- While creating a VirtualMachine, the OpenShift console displays the error: **VirtualMachine creation is not supported due to incompatible UserDefinedNetwork configuration.**- The issue occurs specifically when attempting to use a Layer 3 UDN-backed network with OpenShift Virtualization workloads, preventing successful VM provisioning with the desired network attachment.
resolution: - Layer 3 UserDefinedNetwork (UDN) is not supported with OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines due to its IP address allocation model, which differs from the networking requirements of VM workloads.- In a Layer 3 UDN configuration, a CIDR is defined along with a `hostSubnet` parameter, resulting in node-specific subnet allocation (similar to pod networking using `hostPrefix`). Each node is assigned a unique, non-overlapping subnet from the overall CIDR range.- Because of this per-node subnet allocation, IP addresses are tied to the node where the workload is running, and the same IP address cannot exist across multiple nodes within the Layer 3 UDN.- OpenShift Virtualization requires the ability for a virtual machine to retain its IP address during Live Migration between nodes. This requirement cannot be satisfied with Layer 3 UDN due to its non-overlapping, node-scoped IP allocation design.- As a result, Live Migration is not feasible with Layer 3 UDN-backed networks, leading to incompatibility with OpenShift Virtualization VMs.- To support VM mobility and consistent networking, only Layer 2 UDN is supported, as it allows the same IP address to be maintained across nodes within the cluster.

title: Keystone returns HTTP 500 "Internal Server Error" when querying LDAP users with `ldaps://` and `use_tls = True`
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Running `openstack user list--domain ` returns `Internal Server Error (HTTP 500)`.- The Keystone domain config uses `url = ldaps://...` together with `use_tls = True`.- The Red Hat documentation example (Configuring security services, Chapter 5) shows `ldaps://` with `use_tls = True`, but this combination is not supported by the Keystone code.
resolution: 1. In the `keystone..conf` within the `keystone-domains` Secret, set `use_tls = False` when using `ldaps://`. The `ldaps://` protocol handles SSL/TLS automatically without needing `use_tls = True`: ```ini [ldap] url = ldaps://ldap.example.com use_tls = False tls_cacertfile = /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-ca.pem tls_req_cert = demand ``` 2. Alternatively, use `ldap://` with `use_tls = True` for StartTLS mode (port 389): ```ini [ldap] url = ldap://ldap.example.com use_tls = True tls_cacertfile = /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-ca.pem tls_req_cert = demand ``` 3. Re-apply the Secret and wait for the Keystone pods to restart: ``` $ oc apply-f keystone-domains.yaml $ oc-n openstack get pods-l service=keystone-w ``` 4. Verify LDAP users are visible: ``` $ openstack user list--domain ```
root_cause: 1. **`ldaps://` and `use_tls = True` are two different TLS mechanisms that cannot be combined:**- **`ldaps://`** (port 636): the connection is SSL/TLS encrypted from the start, like HTTPS.- **`use_tls = True`** (port 389): starts a plain connection, then upgrades to encrypted via the StartTLS command. 2. **The upstream Keystone source code explicitly rejects this combination.** In `keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py` (line 599): ```python if use_tls and using_ldaps: raise AssertionError(_('Invalid TLS / LDAPS combination')) ``` Source references:- RHOSO 18 (2023.1): [common.py#L599](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/branch/unmaintained/2023.1/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L599)- RHOSP 17 (Wallaby): [common.py#L599](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/tag/wallaby-eol/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L599) 3. **`ldaps://` does not need `use_tls = True` to enable certificate verification.** The code checks `if use_tls or using_ldaps:` (line 603), so `ldaps://` automatically enters the TLS config path: ```python if use_tls or using_ldaps: if tls_cacertfile: ldap.set_option(ldap.OPT_X_TLS_CACERTFILE, tls_cacertfile) ``` Source references:- RHOSO 18 (2023.1): [common.py#L603](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/branch/unmaintained/2023.1/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L603)- RHOSP 17 (Wallaby): [common.py#L603](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/tag/wallaby-eol/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L603) 4. **Valid combinations summary:** ``` ldaps:// + use_tls = False ✅ Works (SSL mode, port 636) ldap:// + use_tls = True ✅ Works (StartTLS mode, port 389) ldaps:// + use_tls = True ❌ Fails: "Invalid TLS / LDAPS combination" ``` **Key point: `ldaps://` must be used with `use_tls = False`. `ldaps://` + `use_tls = True` is NOT a valid combination.**

title: CollectorNodeDown alert triggered in OpenShift Logging
issue: - `CollectorNodeDown` alert triggered in OpenShift Logging
resolution: When the `limits.cpu` is hit, the faster way of removing the alert is increasing the `limits.cpu` to the collectors. Follow the Red Hat Documentation "[Configure log collector CPU and memory limits](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/configuring_logging/cluster-logging-collector#cluster-logging-collector-limits_cluster-logging-collector)" for Logging v6 to increase the `limits.cpu`. Further actions could be to identify the load or loads generating too many logs with the steps in the Red Hat Article "[Troubleshooting the Vector collector in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7089751#toomanylogs)" and decide if: 1. Review if it was required and possible to reduce the verbosity of the load contacting with the responsible of that service 2. Set a rate limit in the collectors for those load too verbose. The option is `obsclf.spec.inputs..tuning.rateLimitPerContainer` 3. Filtering out the logs from those namespaces too verbose. The filtering itself could help to increase the cpu usage, then, it requires evaluation for each situation and measure the impact of it. Read the "[Configuring log forwarding](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/configuring_logging/configuring-log-forwarding)" documentation to know about the different strategies to filter out the logs.
root_cause: The prometheus cannot scrape the collector metrics with the metrics scrape timeout 10s. The collector is actually down, or having performance issues where the collector cpu hits the `limits.cpu` set. The collector pod could have a high cpu usage caused by a high number of logs that required to read and log forward and features as `filtering` or [detecting multi-line exception dectection](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/configuring_logging/configuring-log-forwarding#enabling-multi-line-exception-detection_configuring-log-forwarding) will also contribute to increase the cpu usage.

title: Horizon dashboard does not reflect updated quota usage after shelving instances
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - After an Instance is shelved, the free resources are not getting reflected on the Horizon Dashboard and remains the same
resolution: - For `RHOSP` environment:- Create a custom environment file. You can apply this using `ExtraConfig` to ensure it is configured across all nodes, or limit it to specific roles like `ControllerExtraConfig` and `ComputeExtraConfig` parameter_defaults: ExtraConfig: nova::config::nova_config: quota/count_usage_from_placement: value: True- For `RHOSO` environment- Update the `Nova` configuration via the `OpenStackControlPlane` CR: spec: nova: template: apiServiceTemplate: customServiceConfig: | [quota] count_usage_from_placement = True- Apply the changes: $ oc apply-f
root_cause: With the setting `False`, `Nova` calculates quota usage from its internal database instead of `Placement`. In scenarios such as shelve offload, the resources are released in `Placement` immediately, however `Nova`’s internal usage tables are not updated in real time. As a result, `Horizon` may continue to display stale resource usage even though the compute resources have already been freed.

title: Not able to see as normal user logs from deleted namespaces in Loki in RHOCP 4
issue: An OpenShift user, not cluster admin, is not able to see the logs from deleted namespaces.
How is it possible that an OpenShift user that was project admin of a deleted namespace can continue viewing the logs from the containers running inside this namespace?
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in RFE [OBSDA-881](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-881). If this feature is required, open a support case on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. **Note**: There is a Bug [OCPBUGS-56368](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-56368) in place to allow users to search for the logs of a pods that has been deleted.
root_cause: The Red Hat Logging Storage is integrated with the OpenShift Authentication, then, when an user desires to query logs from pods running in a namespace, it's done a call the API to verify if the user has access or not to check the logs. When the namespace is deleted, then, the answer to the query returns that the user has not access to that namespace deleted, finishing in the OpenShift user not being able to see the logs.

title: How to migrate AMQ streams on openshift to KRaft ?
issue: How to migrate AMQ streams on openshift to KRaft?
resolution: - Before migrating to KRaft, first check if clusters are using node pools. If not then migrate amq streams cluster to node pools:-- To migrate cluster to use node pools, follow below steps:- 1. Create a new KafkaNodePool resource. [Under operator-> installed operator-> Kafka Node Pool-> Create KafkaNodePool] a. Name the resource kafka. b. Point a strimzi.io/cluster label to your existing Kafka resource. c. Set the replica count and storage configuration to match your current Kafka cluster. d. Set the roles to broker. e. Click on create 2. Now Enable support for node pools in the Kafka resource using the strimzi.io/node-pools: enabled annotation as below:- a. Click on created Kafka node pool-> YAML and add annotations strimzi.io/node-pools: enabled ~~~ name: my-cluster annotations: strimzi.io/node-pools: enabled ~~~ b. Save the changes 3. Please refer [here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.9/html-single/deploying_and_managing_streams_for_apache_kafka_on_openshift/index#proc-migrating-clusters-node-pools-str)- To migrate KRaft mode (if your clusters are using node pools):- 1. For the Kafka cluster, create a node pool with a controller role (Under operator-> installed operator-> Kafka Node Pool-> Create KafkaNodePool-> Set role as "Controller") ~~~ apiVersion: kafka.strimzi.io/v1beta2 kind: KafkaNodePool metadata: name: controller labels: strimzi.io/cluster: my-cluster spec: replicas: 3 roles:- controller.... ~~~ 2. Now enable KRaft migration in the Kafka resource by setting the strimzi.io/kraft annotation to migration: a. Click on created Kafka node pool-> YAML and add annotations strimzi.io/kraft: migration ~~~ name: my-cluster namespace: my-project annotations: strimzi.io/kraft: migration ~~~ b. Save the changes 3. Please refer [here](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_streams_for_apache_kafka/2.9/html-single/deploying_and_managing_streams_for_apache_kafka_on_openshift/index#proc-deploy-migrate-kraft-str)

title: Keystone LDAP query fails with `OSError: tls_cacertfile not found or is not a file`
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Running `openstack user list--domain ` returns `Internal Server Error (HTTP 500)`.- The Keystone log shows `OSError: tls_cacertfile not found or is not a file`.- The LDAP domain config has `tls_cacertfile` set, but the path does not match the actual file location inside the Keystone container.
resolution: 1. **Identify the correct certificate mount path inside the Keystone container.** The path depends on how the CA certificate was mounted (Secret, ConfigMap, etc.). Check the pod/container description for volume mounts: RHOSO 18: ``` $ oc describe pod/-n openstack | grep-B 1 "ldap\|ca\|cert\|ssl" /etc/keystone/ssl/certs from keystone-ldap-ca (ro) ``` RHOSP 17 (on a controller node): ``` $ sudo podman inspect keystone--format '{{json.Mounts}}' | python3-m json.tool | grep-i "ldap\|ca\|cert\|ssl" ``` 2. **List the actual files at the mount path** to confirm the file name: RHOSO 18: ``` $ oc-n openstack rsh ls-la /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1234 Apr 1 08:26 ldap-root-ca.pem ``` RHOSP 17 (on a controller node): ``` $ sudo podman exec keystone ls-la /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ ``` 3. **Update `tls_cacertfile` in the domain config to use the correct path.** For example, if the certificate is mounted at `/etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem`: ```ini [ldap] tls_cacertfile = /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem ``` **Note: use `=` as the delimiter, not `:`.** The OpenStack INI config standard format uses `=` (per upstream [Keystone documentation](https://docs.openstack.org/keystone/latest/admin/configuration.html)). Using `:` may cause unexpected parsing: ```ini # Wrong tls_cacertfile: /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem # Correct tls_cacertfile = /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem ``` 4. Re-apply the config and verify: RHOSO 18: ``` $ oc apply-f keystone-domains.yaml ``` RHOSP 17 (on a controller node): ``` $ sudo pcs resource restart galera-bundle ``` Then test: ``` $ openstack user list--domain ```
root_cause: 1. **Keystone checks that `tls_cacertfile` exists before connecting to LDAP.** In `keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py` (line 614-617), the code uses `os.path.isfile()` to verify the file path. If the file does not exist, it raises an `IOError` which results in HTTP 500: ```python if tls_cacertfile: if not os.path.isfile(tls_cacertfile): raise IOError(_("tls_cacertfile %s not found " "or is not a file") % tls_cacertfile) ldap.set_option(ldap.OPT_X_TLS_CACERTFILE, tls_cacertfile) ``` Source references:- RHOSO 18 (2023.1): [common.py#L614](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/branch/unmaintained/2023.1/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L614)- RHOSP 17 (Wallaby): [common.py#L614](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/tag/wallaby-eol/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L614) 2. **Common causes for path mismatch:**- **Using the host path instead of the container path.** The CA certificate file exists on the host (e.g. `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ca.crt.pem`), but Keystone runs inside a container where a different mount path is used (e.g. `/etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem`).- **File name mismatch.** The ConfigMap or Secret was created with `--from-file=ldap-root-ca.pem`, but the config references a different file name like `ca.crt.pem`.- **Using `:` instead of `=` as INI delimiter.** While Python's configparser accepts `:`, the upstream Keystone [documentation](https://docs.openstack.org/keystone/latest/admin/configuration.html) uses `=` as the standard format. Using `:` may cause confusion especially when the value itself contains `:` (e.g. in URL values like `ldap://host:389`).

title: Keepalived VIP flips frequent due to health check timeouts
issue: - The Ingress VIP of the cluster switches between the nodes frequently. ``` $ oc logs keepalived-xxx-node01.example.com-n openshift-kni-infra Fri Feb 20 04:49:41 2026: Track script chk_ingress is already running, expect idle- skipping run Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: Track script chk_ingress_ready is being timed out, expect idle- skipping run Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: Track script chk_ingress is being timed out, expect idle- skipping run Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: VRRP_Script(chk_ingress_ready) failed (due to signal 15) Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: (node01.example.com_INGRESS_0) Changing effective priority from 80 to 70 Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: VRRP_Script(chk_ingress) failed (due to signal 15) Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: (node01.example.com_INGRESS_0) Entering FAULT STATE Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: (node01.example.com_INGRESS_0) sent 0 priority Fri Feb 20 04:49:42 2026: (node01.example.com_INGRESS_0) removing VIPs. ```- This results in extended periods of unavailability of the Ingress routers.- Cluster Operators, such as the 'authentication' Cluster Operator, can experience status flips between 'ready' and 'notReady'.
resolution: - Change the server workload profile from 'Standard' or 'Balanced' to 'Performance' or 'Virtualization Optimized Performance Profile', or the equivalent high-performance setting for your specific hardware vendor- Ensure that OS-level power management settings, such as 'ENERGY_PERF_BIAS_CFG', are explicitly set to 'Performance' to prevent the CPU from entering deep sleep states that delay small task execution.- Apply these performance-oriented settings across all nodes hosting Ingress or keepalived workloads to ensure consistent health check behavior.- Confirm that keepalived logs no longer report `VRRP_Script(chk_ingress) failed (due to signal 15)` timeout errors after applying the changes.
root_cause: - The keepalived service uses a 'vrrp_script' to check the routers health with a 0.9 second timeout. ``` vrrp_script chk_ingress_ready {script "/usr/bin/timeout 0.9 /usr/bin/curl-o /dev/null-Lfs http://localhost:1936/healthz/ready" interval 1 weight 10 rise 3 fall 2} vrrp_script chk_ingress {script "/usr/bin/timeout 0.9 /usr/bin/curl-o /dev/null-Lfs http://localhost:1936/healthz" interval 1 rise 3 fall 2} ```- On servers with 'Balanced' power profiles, the CPU may not ramp up from lower power states quickly enough to complete the curl request within 0.9 seconds.- This latency triggers a false failure, causing keepalived to enter a FAULT state and move the VIP to another node.

title: The Network Observer metrics endpoint is not reachable
issue: - The metrics endpoint of the Network Observer is not reachable from outside the container.
resolution: Change the Network Observer `listen address` from `127.0.0.1:8080` to `0.0.0.0:8080`, which will expose the Network Observer service (including its metrics endpoint) to other pods in the cluster, for example using `extraArgs` to override the listen address: ~~~ $oc edit networkobservers.observability.skupper.io [...] extraArgs:--listen=0.0.0.0:8080 [...] ~~~ After applying this change, the container spec shows: ~~~ spec: containers:- args:--listen=127.0.0.1:8080--prometheus-api=http://127.0.0.1:9090--router-endpoint=amqps://skupper-router-local--router-tls-ca=/etc/messaging/ca.crt--router-tls-cert=/etc/messaging/tls.crt--router-tls-key=/etc/messaging/tls.key--listen=0.0.0.0:8080 ~~~ **Note:** While this approach works as a workaround, it creates duplicate `-listen` arguments. A [JIRA](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SKUPPER-2952) ticket has been opened to address this properly.
root_cause: The Network Observer binds to localhost only: `127.0.0.1:8080`.

title: RHBK Admin Console Stuck with "Loading the Admin UI" Message
issue: - The Administration Console gets stuck with a message "Loading the Admin UI."- Browser's Developer Tools shows that a request to `/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/login-status-iframe.html/init?client_id=security-admin-console&origin= ` fails with a 403 error.- RHBK is running behind a reverse proxy(i.e. OpenShift Route), which terminates TLS.
resolution: In case you are using an old browser version, please upgrade it to the latest version. RHBK is tested with latest version of the browsers. If outdated version is used, you may face JavaScript error from the Admin Console, which can be checked from the console of the browser's developer tools. When running RHBK server behind a reverse proxy, you need to specify `proxy-headers=xforwarded` option or `proxy-headers=forwarded` option. When a reverse proxy relays information using `X-Forwarded-*` headers, please use the `xforwarded` option. When it relays the information using a `Forwarded` header, please use the `forwarded` option. If deploying RHBK using RHBK Operator, you can specify the option in `spec.proxy.headers` as follows: ``` apiVersion: k8s.keycloak.org/v2alpha1 kind: Keycloak metadata:... spec:... proxy: headers: xforwarded # double check your reverse proxy sets and overwrites the X-Forwarded-* headers ```

title: [RHOSO 18] Re-provisioned EDPM Node does not show up in `openstack hypervisor list`
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - A Nova Compute hypervisor node was [removed](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html/maintaining_the_red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift_deployment/assembly_scaling-data-plane-nodes#proc_removing-a-Compute-node-from-the-data-plane_scaling) and re-provisioned but now does not show up in `openstack hypervisor list` output.
resolution: - Delete nova_compute service, purge stale entries from placement, then re-discover the node:- On EDPM compute- stop nova_compute: ~~~ sudo systemctl stop edpm_nova_compute ~~~- Delete nova_compute service and purge stale entries from placement service: ~~~ oc rsh openstackclient openstack compute service list--service nova-compute |grep oc rsh openstacklient openstack compute service delete oc rsh nova-cell0-conductor-0 nova-manage placement audit--delete--verbose ~~~- Start nova_compute on EDPM node: ~~~ sudo systemctl start edpm_nova_compute ~~~- Rediscover the EDPM node: ~~~ oc rsh nova-cell0-conductor-0 nova-manage cell_v2 discover_hosts--verbose--by-service ~~~- Verify: ~~~ oc rsh openstackclient openstack hypervisor list ~~~

title: [RHOSO 18] - Configure NIC bonding for ControlPlane OVN Gateway
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - How to configure NIC bonding for ControlPlane OVN Gateway in RHOSO.- **Important*
This feature is only available with RHOSO version 18.0.15 or later. ~~~ oc get openstack version ~~~
resolution: - Below is an example entry for ovnController service in OpenstackControlPlane CR to enable bonding: ~~~ oc edit oscp/openstack-control-plane ~~~ ~~~ ovn: template: ovnController: bondConfiguration: bond_ovngw: links:- enp14s0- enp13s0 mtu: 1500 mode: active-backup nicMappings: datacentre: bond_ovngw ~~~- Note: The NICs used for OVN Gateway bonding must be dedicated for this and should not be configured for other OCP/OSP services.- If the NICs have been setup in a bond via the OCP NNCP config, Below is an example to remove the bond and prepare them for the ovnController services: ~~~ apiVersion: nmstate.io/v1 kind: NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy metadata: name: nncp-remove-bond0-all spec: desiredState: interfaces:- name: bond0 # delete bond0 type: bond state: absent- description: Configuring enp13s0 ipv4: enabled: false ipv6: enabled: false mtu: 1500 name: enp13s0 state: up type: ethernet- description: Configuring enp14s0 ipv4: enabled: false ipv6: enabled: false mtu: 1500 name: enp14s0 state: up type: ethernet nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: "" ~~~

title: [RHOSO] - Increase Ansible Verbosity for Openstack Data Plane Deployments

title: [RHOSO] - Admin User Can't Migrate or Evacuate VMs with Encrypted Volumes
issue: - VM Migration, Evacuation, Unshelving operations fail with the following error: ~~~ Key manager error: Forbidden: Secret payload retrieval attempt not allowed- please review your user/project privileges ~~~
resolution: - The following custom policy will work-around this issue (support exception required)- Modify the OpenStackControlPlane CR: ~~~ spec:... barbican:... template: barbicanAPI: customServiceConfig: | [oslo_policy] policy_file=/etc/barbican/barbican.conf.d/policy.yaml defaultConfigOverwrite: policy.yaml: | "secret:decrypt": "role:admin or rule:secret_project_admin or (rule:secret_project_member and rule:secret_owner) or (rule:secret_project_member and rule:secret_is_not_private) or rule:secret_acl_read" ~~~
root_cause: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSPRH-21959
