title: How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.18 and Below
issue: In some instances, generally coming from a standalone Multicloud Object Storage (MCG) deployment to a full ODF Ceph Internal/External cluster, it may be desired to migrate the database storageclass to an ODF Ceph storageclass. This solution will cover those steps. **Related Articles:*

[Migrating From Standalone Multicloud Gateway (MCG/NooBaa) to ODF/Ceph Full Deployment (Deployed Using StorageCluster)- OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7055285) **WARNING: IF STEPS ARE NOT FOLLOWED EXACTLY IN THIS SOLUTION, IT MAY CAUSE COMPLETE NOOBAA DATA LOSS.**
resolution: 1. Patch the `storagecluster.yaml`, and change the `dbStorageClass` parameter to the desired storageclass: ~~~ $ oc patch storagecluster ocs-storagecluster-n openshift-storage--type='merge'-p '{"spec":{"multiCloudGateway":{"dbStorageClassName":" "}}}' ~~~ 2. Validate this change has been pushed to the `noobaa.yaml`: ~~~ $ oc get noobaa-n openshift-storage noobaa-o yaml | grep dbStorageClass ~~~ 3. Stop writing to the database: ~~~ oc-n openshift-storage scale deployment noobaa-operator noobaa-endpoint--replicas 0 oc-n openshift-storage scale statefulsets.apps noobaa-core--replicas 0 ~~~ 4. Perform a one-time backup by following the steps in the backup solution, AND ENSURE THE `dump.sql` FILE IS COPIED OUTSIDE OF THE POD. **NOTE: Do not scale up NooBaa services once the backup is complete; leave the services down. The only pod that should be running is the database pod.** [Perform a One-Time Backup of the noobaa-db-pg-0 Database for the Mulitcloud Object Gateway (NooBaa) for ODF v4.18 and Below](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7117672) 5. With ONLY the database pod running, delete the PVC, and delete the `noobaa-db-pg` statefulset: **WARNING: All NooBaa DB data will be lost at this point. The only way to recover is to use the database dump, WHICH NEEDS TO BE COPIED OUTSIDE OF THE POD, as all pod data will be lost. Secondly, the db dump must be valid. If the database dump verification step was not followed in the backup article, and the database dump is bad, only a NooBaa rebuild that accepts complete data loss in NooBaa will be able to recover and bring NooBaa back to a Ready phase.** ~~~ $ oc delete pvc-n openshift-storage db-noobaa-db-pg-0 ~~~ **Note:** The Finalizer will hold up the deletion of the PVC. Once the delete command has been issued, type `ctrl + c` in order to have your command line back and issue the statefulset deletion command, which will release the finalizer. ~~~ $ oc delete sts-n openshift-storage noobaa-db-pg ~~~ 6. Scale up JUST the noobaa-operator, which will recreate the `noobaa-db-pg` statefulset and `db-noobaa-db-pg-0` PVC with the newly applied storageclass: ~~~ $ oc scale deployment-n openshift-storage noobaa-operator--replicas=1 ~~~ 7. The `dump.sql` file is no longer in the pod; copy it into the pod: ~~~ $ oc cp-n openshift-storage dump.sql noobaa-db-pg-0:/var/lib/pgsql/data/ ~~~ 8. Restore from backup: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-storage rsh noobaa-db-pg-0 $ psql-U postgres < /$HOME/data/dump.sql $ echo $? $ exit ~~~ 9. Scale up the remaining NooBaa services: ~~~ oc-n openshift-storage scale deployment noobaa-endpoint--replicas 1 oc-n openshift-storage scale statefulsets.apps noobaa-core--replicas 1 ~~~ 10. The noobaa-operator, noobaa-endpoint, noobaa-core-0, and noobaa-db-pg-0 pods should all be running. Validate that NooBaa and the backingstore(s) are all in `Ready` phase (may take ~5 minutes): ~~~ $ oc get noobaa-n openshift-storage $ oc get backingstore-A ~~~

title: Error while provisioning a PVC from a specific VolumeSnapshot - error getting handle for DataSource Type VolumeSnapshot by Name testsnapshot: error getting snapshot xxxxx from api server: volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io
issue: csi-provisioner container generating old snapshot logs
ProvisioningFailed warnings indicating volume provisioning issues
Persistent logging of error messages related to storage class provisioning failures
Unclear reason for recurring provisioning failures and old log generation in OpenShift Data Foundation csi-provisioner container
resolution: 1. Wait for the volumesnapshot you are using as data source for a PVC to be in Ready state 2. Once the volumesnapshot is in Ready state, the PVC stuck in Pending state will need to be deleted: ~~~ # oc delete pvc-n namespace ~~~ 3. Now try to provision the PVC by using the volumesnapshot as the datasource. 4. In the `csi-provisioner` pod, you will now see: ~~~ I0122 20:33:26.893249 1 event.go:389] "Event occurred" object="openshift-storage/new-pvc-from-snapshot" fieldPath="" kind="PersistentVolumeClaim" apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="Provisioning" message="External provisioner is provisioning volume for claim \"openshift-storage/new-pvc-from-snapshot\"" I0122 20:33:30.861709 1 event.go:389] "Event occurred" object="openshift-storage/new-pvc-from-snapshot" fieldPath="" kind="PersistentVolumeClaim" apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="ProvisioningSucceeded" message="Successfully provisioned volume pvc-eaf7896b-e7c3-4e38-960f-4f097021b4ce" ~~~
root_cause: 1. Sometimes the volumesnapshot takes time to come into `Ready` state. 2. At this time if a PVC is provisioned using the specific volumesnapshot, it will give an error of- `error getting handle for DataSource Type VolumeSnapshot by Name testsnapshot: error getting snapshot testsnapshot from api server: volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io \"testsnapshot\" not found" `

title: How to Enable Trace Logging Verbosity in Network Manager on Openshift
issue: - In order to diagnose and resolve problems related to `NetworkManager`, enabling trace logging verbosity is of great help to understand what `NetworkManager` is doing. It is advisable to adjust the log level verbosity according to the specific issue that needs to be investigated.- If you need to report a bug, just enable `domains=ALL:TRACE` to collect all trace information to further investigation.
resolution: It is possible to reconfigure logging at runtime by using the command `nmcli general logging level "TRACE" domains "ALL"`. However, it is often preferable to obtain a complete log from the beginning, particularly when debugging an issue. It is recommended to activate debug logging in `NetworkManager.conf` or adding configuration files in `/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d` directory (modify the default behavior of `NetworkManager` without modifying the main configuration file directly) and restart the service. To enable trace logging verbosity level in `NetworkManager` on Openshift for `worker` nodes, follow these steps:- Create a `MachineConfig` to modify the log settings to enable trace logging verbosity ~~~ $ cat < nm-trace-logging.yaml apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-nm-trace-logging spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,W2xvZ2dpbmddCmRvbWFpbnM9QUxMOlRSQUNFCg== mode: 0644 overwrite: true path: /etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/99-nm-trace-logging.conf EOF ~~~- Verify the new `NetworkManager` configuration file contents `/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/99-nm-trace-logging.conf` to be deployed ~~~ $ cat nm-trace-logging.yaml | awk-F'base64,' '{print $2}' | base64-d [logging] domains=ALL:TRACE ~~~- Apply the new `MachineConfig` `99-nm-trace-logging` to enable trace logging verbosity ~~~ $ oc apply-f nm-trace-logging.yaml ~~~ Once the `MachineConfig` is created, the Openshift `MachineConfig Operator (MCO)` will drain/restart the Openshift worker nodes and `NetworkManager` service will apply the new settings. ~~~ $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master-0 Ready master 133m v1.23.12+8a6bfe4 master-1 Ready master 133m v1.23.12+8a6bfe4 master-2 Ready master 133m v1.23.12+8a6bfe4 worker-0 Ready worker 115m v1.23.12+8a6bfe4 worker-1 Ready worker 113m v1.23.12+8a6bfe4 worker-2 Ready,SchedulingDisabled worker 115m v1.23.12+8a6bfe4 < < draining/restarting worker ~~~- Verify the `MachineConfig` resource `99-nm-trace-logging ` is created and the `MachineConfig` is applying changes (UPDATING=True) ~~~ $ oc get machineconfig | grep 99-nm-trace-logging 99-nm-trace-logging $ oc get machineconfigpool worker NAME CONFIG UPDATED UPDATING DEGRADED... worker rendered-worker-72016d37e7b7b1dac230ad0b2e18ee98 True True False... ~~~ In this case, `worker` nodes will be restarted one by one if the [MaxUnavailable](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4669561) is set to 1.- Once the changes han been applied and the `MachineConfigPool` updating status is `false`, verify that logging verbosity level has been changed on a `worker` node. ~~~ $ oc debug node/worker-2 sh-4.4# chroot /host bash [root@worker-2 /]# cat /etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/99-nm-trace-logging.conf [logging] domains=ALL:TRACE $ journalctl-u NetworkManager-b...-- Logs begin at Thu 2023-04-06 11:11:57 UTC, end at Thu 2023-04-06 11:53:04 UTC.-- Apr 06 11:50:20 localhost systemd[1]: Starting Network Manager... Apr 06 11:50:20 localhost NetworkManager[1345]: [1680781820.1921] CONFIG: Apr 06 11:50:20 localhost NetworkManager[1345]: [1680781820.1921] CONFIG: [logging] Apr 06 11:50:20 localhost NetworkManager[1345]: [1680781820.1921] CONFIG: domains=ALL:TRACE... ~~~ Documentation references:- [Introduction to NetworkManager Debugging](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/configuring_and_managing_networking/introduction-to-networkmanager-debugging_configuring-and-managing-networking)- man 5 NetworkManager.conf- [NetworkManager TRACE logging](http://blog.nemebean.com/content/networkmanager-trace-logging)

title: ODF-Noobaa: How to Migrate NooBaa Buckets to a New Backingstore?
issue: - How to retire the existing backingstore and migrate the buckets to the new backingstore? **NOTE:*

Due to a known issue with ODF 4.13/4.14, this procedure only works with BucketClasses that do not contain any Object Buckets. If Object Buckets do exist for the given Bucket Classes, it fails. **Red Hat engineering team is working to backport the fix [Bug 2279280](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2279280)**
resolution: 1. Add new backingstore to the cluster. [Creating a new backingstore](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.12/html-single/managing_hybrid_and_multicloud_resources/index#creating-a-new-backing-store_rhodf) 2. Once the backingstore is in **READY** state, modify the appropriate bucketclass to add additional tiers under backingstores and change the placement policy to mirror. Modify the bucketclass spec as below: ``` spec: placementPolicy: tiers:- backingStores:- noobaa-default-backing-store #### Old Backingsotre- test-back #### New Backingstore placement: Mirror #### placement Policy ``` 3. Wait for data to be copied to the new backing store. **Note:** It will be up to the user to best determine if the data has been mirrored over before decommissioning the old backingstore. Best practices as as follows: a. On S3 buckets that back the backingstore (non-pv-pools). Install the NooBaa CLI and execute the following: ~~~ $ noobaa bucket status ~~~ b. For pv-pool, the best way to check is to analyze the PVC utilization on both backingstore PVCs. c. If the number of objects in the s3 bucket from the `$ noobaa bucket status` output, or the PVC size, aligns with the backingstore being mirrored completely, stop IO to NooBaa on the **application-side** by scaling down the application (e.g., Loki, Quay, etc.). Decommission the old backingstore by re-editing the bucketclass, changing the `placement` back to `Spread`, and removing the old backingstore.

title: Migrating the PV-Pool Backingstore Storageclass to Ceph RBD after Standalone Multicloud Gateway (MCG/NooBaa) to Full OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment
issue: In some instances, it may be desirable to change the storageclass of a pv-pool backingstore, generally after a migration from Standalone MCG, to Full Internal ODF Deployment, which this solution will cover. **NOTE:*

This solution will cover a generic source pv-pool, to a destination pv-pool backingstore migration. However, in the event the PV-pool is the `noobaa-default-backing-store`, review the respective Troubleshooting Product Documentation that correlates with the version of ODF, as the backing store may need to be overridden. For example: [3.2. Overriding the default backing store ODF v4.21](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.14/html/managing_hybrid_and_multicloud_resources/adding-storage-resources-for-hybrid-or-multicloud_rhodf#overriding-the-default-backing-store_rhodf) **Related Articles:*

[Migrating From Standalone Multicloud Gateway (MCG/NooBaa) to ODF/Ceph Full Deployment (Deployed Using StorageCluster)- OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7055285) [How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.18 and Below](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140944) [How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.19+](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140980)
resolution: 1. Create a new PV-pool backingstore (destination) by going to the OCP Console UI-> Storage-> Object Storage- Backing Store, and create it by setting the Provider to "PVC" and selecting the desired storage class in the dropdown. Additionally, calculate the required space and adjust the "Number of Volumes" and "Volume Size" specs accordingly. 2. The old pv-pool (source), will have a bucketclass associated with it. Edit the bucketclass and add the new backingstore created in step 1, and set the bucketclass `placement` to `Mirror`. Mirror the bucket between two backingstores (source/destination), and decommission the old backingstore as shown in the [How to migrate noobaa buckets to a new backingstore?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7009908) solution. 3. Once the old backingstore is removed from the previous bucketclass, allow for a monitoring timeframe to ensure the bucket is still healthy before deleting the old backingstore.

title: Unable to Use Ceph Commands in Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) in the rook-ceph-tools or rook-ceph-operator Pods "Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "validate-exec.devworkspace-controller.svc": failed to call webhook"
issue: The DevWorkspace Controller in Openshift can sometimes block the use of Ceph commands, either in the rook-ceph-tools pod or the rook-ceph-operator pod, firing an `Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "validate-exec.devworkspace-controller.svc"` error. The [Not able to open a Remote Shell to any Containers in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6971276) solution generally resolves this issue. However, there are instances where a customer does not want to delete the devworkspace. This solution will serve in lieu of deleting the `mutatingwebhookconfigurations controller.devfile.io` and `validatingwebhookconfigurations controller.devfile.io` CRs.
resolution: 1. Find the node hosting the rook-ceph-tools pod (see NODE column): ~~~ $ oc get pod-n openshift-storage-l app=rook-ceph-tools-o wide ~~~ 2. Debug into the desired node: ~~~ $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host ~~~ 3. Identify the rook-ceph-tools pod on the node: ~~~ $ crictl ps | grep tools ~~~ 4. Enter the rook-ceph-tools container: ~~~ $ crictl exec-it sh ~~~ 5. Run ceph commands, for example: ~~~ $ ceph status $ ceph health detail $ ceph healthcheck history ls $ ceph osd df tree ~~~
root_cause: This error is related to a webhook that was presumably installed by the web terminal operator, which relies on devworkspace.

title: Cluster Loadbalancer is unable to associate with suitable subnets
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - After the cluster creation the `Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS ROSA with HCP` cluster web console is not accessible due to a degraded console cluster operator.
resolution: - For the `subnet auto discovery` to work the subnet tagging needs to be present according to the documentation [Installing an AWS Load Balancer Operator](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html/networking_operators/aws-load-balancer#aws-load-balancer-operator-installation_aws-load-balancer-operator)- Proper subnet will be selected by the`LB` if it has the tag `"kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb"` for the internal `LB`- Remove tags `kubernetes.io/cluster/*` from all subnets and recreate the cluster
root_cause: - A `kubernetes.io/cluster/*` tag is also defined on AWS side that is not the cluster name, which causes the `subnet auto discovery` to associate a wrong subnet

title: Image pull fails with unauthorized to access repository in OpenShift 4
issue: After configuring the image pull secret as described in [Updating the global cluster pull secret](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.7/openshift_images/managing_images/using-image-pull-secrets.html#images-update-global-pull-secret_using-image-pull-secrets), access to the repository becomes unauthorized. Error message: ``` Error: ImagePullBackOff " ". Access repository:, action: pull: unauthorized to access repository: ```
How to test a pull secret for a Red Hat image registry?
resolution: Update the pull secret with the correct credentials. If the credentials are correct but the issue persists, it could be needed to [request pull-secret rotation](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6992996).
root_cause: When adding or updating the pull secret, a typo was made in the credentials. This was automatically stored in the `config.json` file.

title: OpenStack operations fails due to "The broker has blocked the connection: connection blocked, see broker logs" error
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - OpenStack operations such as instance creation fails with the following error: ERROR oslo.messaging._drivers.impl_rabbit [...] The broker has blocked the connection: connection blocked, see broker logs
resolution: 1. Restarting the RabbitMQ pods. By restarting the RabbitMQ pods, memory will be released, $ oc rollout restart statefulset/rabbitmq-server $ oc rollout restart statefulset/rabbitmq-cell1-server 2. Ensure that the memory limit warning message is no longer shown $ oc logs pod/rabbitmq-server-X $ oc logs pod/rabbitmq-cell1-server-X 3. If the issue still occurs even after restarting RabbitMQ, increase `resources.limits.memory` of RabbitMQ pods. $ oc edit openstackcontrolplane: rabbitmq:: resources: limits: cpu: '2' memory: 10Gi <==== For example, increase from 2Gi to 10Gi requests: cpu: '1' memory: 2Gi:
root_cause: RabbitMQ has its memory limitation setting, which is set to `0.4` by default. ~~~ $ oc rsh rabbitmq-server-0 rabbitmqctl environment | grep vm_memory_high_watermark {vm_memory_high_watermark,0.4}, ~~~ The default `resources.limits.memory` of RabbitMQ pods is `2Gi`: ~~~ $ oc get openstackcontrolplane-o yaml: rabbitmq:: resources: limits: cpu: '2' memory: 2Gi <========== requests: cpu: '1' memory: 2Gi: ~~~ Therefore, the memory limitation will be `2Gi` * `0.4` = `0.8Gi`. As there are some overheads, the actual memory limitation will be `0.6872 gb`. This issue occurs when RabbitMQ uses much memory than `0.6872 gb`. ~~~ sh-5.1$ rabbitmqctl status | grep-A 3 Memory Memory Total memory used: 0.2152 gb Calculation strategy: rss Memory high watermark setting: 0.4 of available memory, computed to: 0.6872 gb <===== the memory limitation is 0.6872 gb reserved_unallocated: 0.055 gb (25.58 %) code: 0.0354 gb (16.43 %) ~~~

title: Instance is not getting the correct IPv6 address
issue: - The IPv6 address on Horizon differs from the IPv6 on the instance- IPv6 instance is not able to ping the gateway.- Instance is not getting the correct IPv6 address
resolution: If instance is connected to IPv4 networks or `--config-drive True` is present, cloud-init configures proper IPv6 setting automatically. If the instance is only connected to IPv6 networks, `--config-drive True` option is recommended because metadata proxy server is not supported on IPv6 network. In this case, please ensure that the instance has cloud-init. If SLAAC or DHCPv6 is expected to work, there are several important points to obtain correct IP address via SLAAC or DHCPv6 on Red Hat OpenStack Platform environments:- **A router which sends Router Advertisement packets must be connected to the Neutron network** The router can be Neutron router or an external physical router.- If Neutron router is connected and it is supposed to send Router Advertisement packets, please ensure that `ipv6_ra_mode` of the subnet has proper setting.- If an external router is connected and it is supposed to send Router Advertisement packets, please ensure that the external router has correct Router Advertisement setting (A/M/O flag settings), which matches `ipv6_address_mode` of the subnet. And `ipv6_ra_mode` of the subnet should be unset to avoid Neutron routers from sending duplicated Router Advertisement packets.- **Instances must be configured to use both Router Advertisement and DHCPv6** If the instance is using NetworkManager, `ipv6.method` must be `auto`: ~~~ # nmcli c mod ipv6.method auto ~~~ Common mis-configuration is that `ipv6.method` is set to `dhcp`. `dhcp` won't work well because it will exchange DHCPv6 packets but doesn't exchange Router Advertisement packets.- **Instances must be configured to use EUI64 to generate its link local IPv6 address** If the instance is using NetworkManager, `ipv6.ipv6.addr-gen-mode` must be `eui64` (or `default-or-eui64`), must not be `stable-privacy` or something like that: ~~~ # nmcli c mod ipv6.addr-gen-mode eui64 ~~~ If Neutron port security is enabled (it's enabled by default), Neutron drops packets with a link-local IPv6 address which is not generated by EUI64. In this case, DHCPv6 packet sent by the instance will be dropped and expected IPv6 address won't be configured well. The following setting can be added to images: ~~~ IPV6.ADDR-GEN-MODE="eui64" ~~~ **Note:** If `dhcpv6-stateful` is used, `ip addr show` shows `/128` prefix, but it is expected. Please refer to [IPv6 addresses obtained by stateful DHCPv6 shows /128 prefix](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7109120) Please refer to Red Hat OpenStack Platform documents describing IPv6 configuration as well:- Red Hat OpenStack Platform 17.1: [Project networking with IPv6](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_platform/17.1/html/configuring_red_hat_openstack_platform_networking/proj-network-ipv6_rhosp-network)

title: The data plane nodes are not mapped to the compute cell1

Found 2 cell mappings. Skipping cell0 since it does not contain hosts. Getting computes from cell 'cell1': c9v3f5b6-5a48-4fe9-ad0b-5df47daf05f6 Found 0 unmapped computes in cell: c9v3f5b6-5a48-4fe9-ad0b-5df47daf05f6- From the messages log under var the compute node for nova services perspective is not able to connect to rabbitmq. Mar 17 10:52:29 milan-compute-1 nova_compute[91470]: 2025-03-17 10:52:29.685 2 ERROR oslo.messaging._drivers.impl_rabbit [None req-4b68c6fa-a09b-4baa-9e36-c34293e9257c------] Connection failed: [Errno-2] No address found (retrying in 31.0 seconds): socket.gaierror: [Errno-2] No address found#033[00m or Mar 17 10:52:29 milan-compute-1 nova_compute[91470]: 2025-03-17 10:52:29.685 2 ERROR oslo.messaging._drivers.impl_rabbit [None req-4b68c6fa-a09b-4baa-9e36-c34293e9257c------] Connection failed: [Errno-3] Lookup timed out (retrying in 31.0 seconds): socket.gaierror: [Errno-3] Lookup timed out#033[00m
resolution: Usually the transport URL is configured to reach rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc on port 5671, So on compute node you should be able to:- resolve rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc into an IP address on the EDPM node: # dnf install bind-utils (if dig command is not avaialble) # dig rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc- rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc should be reachable # arping rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc- you can telnet rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc on port 5671 # telnet rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc 5671 If the previous one doesn't work you can:- check if you can reach the ocp worker nodes from the compute node, to see if the general network is ok # ping- if that works, best to check if the metallb l2advertisement config has the correct interface of the ocp worker node and `nodeSelector` settings on `oc get l2advertisement-n metallb-system` # oc get l2advertisement-n metallb-system NAME IPADDRESSPOOLS IPADDRESSPOOL SELECTORS INTERFACES ctlplane ["ctlplane"] ["enp2s0"] internalapi ["internalapi"] ["internalapi"] storage ["storage"] ["storage"] storagemgmt ["storagemgmt"] ["storagemgmt"] tenant ["tenant"] ["tenant"] # oc get l2advertisement-n metallb-system ctlplane-o yaml: spec: interfaces:- enp2s0 ipAddressPools:- ctlplane nodeSelectors:- matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ""- Just as general check could have also sense check if you can reach the internal API of keystone for example, like you can curl the keystone-api metallb vip on the internalapi network- also good to validate is step 9 of [attaching service pods to the isolated networks_preparing_networks guide](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html-single/deploying_red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/index#proc_attaching-service-pods-to-the-isolated-networks_preparing_networks)
root_cause: - All containers running on the dataplane nodes need to resolve the domain names for RHOSO components like, `rabbitmq-cell1.openstack.svc`, `keystone-internal.openstack.svc` with the dnsmasq pods running on the control plane. For example: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openstack | grep dns dnsmasq-dns-6589b455c-mljcm 1/1 Running 0 49m dnsmasq-dns-6589b455c-tj6m8 1/1 Running 0 50m ~~~- The IP address of the dnsmasq pods is defined in the OpenStackControlPlane CR like below: ~~~ apiVersion: core.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackControlPlane metadata: name: openstack-control-plane namespace: openstack [...] dns: template: options:- key: server values:- 172.16.0.1 override: service: metadata: annotations: metallb.universe.tf/address-pool: ctlplane metallb.universe.tf/allow-shared-ip: ctlplane metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs: 192.168.122.80 <=============================== spec: type: LoadBalancer replicas: 2 ~~~ So basically, the dataplane nodes should use only the above IP address of the dnsmasq pods instead of your own DNS server outside of the RHOSO/RHOCP env. Because the domain name entries for RHOSO components are managed by the dnsmasq pods.

title: BMH stuck in `Provisioning` due to RedfishError: Failed to set `Boot Mode` to UEFI
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: Installation of bare metal clusters using IPI method, fails due to Bare Metal Host[BMH] stuck in provisioning status.
Node addition in Bare Metal IPI fails due to issue with BMH stuck in providioning state.
resolution: Before installation, set each node’s firmware boot mode to UEFI via OOB (iLO/CIMC) and explicitly configure bootMode: UEFI in the installation configuration. 1. Before starting the cluster installation, access the Out-of-Band management interface (e.g., HP iLO or Cisco CIMC) for each node. 2. Manually set the BIOS/Firmware boot mode to **UEFI** on each physical machine. 3. In the installation configuration files (such as the `install-config.yaml` or relevant Bare Metal Operator resources), explicitly set the `bootMode` parameter to `UEFI`. * **Note** Do not leave this parameter blank or set it to `Legacy` for hardware that implements `BootMode` as read-only.
root_cause: Certain hardware vendors (including HP iLO 5 and Cisco CIMC) implement the Redfish `BootSourceOverrideMode` attribute as read-only. When the OpenShift installer or the Bare Metal Operator attempts to programmatically change the boot mode via a Redfish `PATCH` request, the BMC returns an `HTTP 400 UnsupportedOperation` error, causing the hardware inspection process to hang or fail.

title: RHOSO Galera cluster fails to recover after ungraceful shutdown with all pods stuck at `Waiting for gcomm URI to be configured for this POD`
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - After all OCP nodes experienced an ungraceful shutdown (e.g. power outage), all Galera pods are `0/1 Running` and not recovering automatically.- Galera pods are stuck at: ``` Waiting for gcomm URI to be configured for this POD ```- All `grastate.dat` show: ``` # GALERA saved state version: 2.1 uuid: 0802d61f-1bbc-11f1-97c6-c37fc0888c63 seqno:-1 safe_to_bootstrap: 0 ```- **May also occur:*
All OpenStack services depending on Galera (Keystone, Cinder, Glance, etc.) enter `CrashLoopBackOff` due to database unavailability. Dashboard returns 504 and CLI returns 502.- **May also occur:*
Some Galera pods show `Pending` with `volume node affinity conflict` if OCP nodes have not fully recovered.
resolution: **Important:** The mariadb-operator is designed to auto-detect this situation and perform bootstrap automatically. Before manually intervening, first check whether the operator is already handling the recovery (step 1-3). Manual bootstrap (step 4-6) is **only needed if the operator has not auto-pushed `gcomm_uri` after 10+ minutes**. 1. Confirm all OCP nodes are `Ready` and all Galera pods have passed the init stage (must be `0/1 Running`, NOT `Init:CrashLoopBackOff`): ``` $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master0 Ready control-plane,master 30d v1.27.6+b49f9d1 master1 Ready control-plane,master 30d v1.27.6+b49f9d1 master2 Ready control-plane,master 30d v1.27.6+b49f9d1 $ oc get pods-n openstack | grep galera openstack-galera-0 0/1 Running 0 10m openstack-galera-1 0/1 Running 0 10m openstack-galera-2 0/1 Running 0 10m ``` If pods are in `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` instead of `Running`, the init container is failing — the operator cannot proceed until pods reach `Running` state. See [RHOSO Galera pods stuck in Init:CrashLoopBackOff with SSL certificate errors after OCP node restart](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140998). 2. Check the mariadb-operator log to determine if the operator is auto-recovering or stuck: ``` $ oc logs-n openstack-operators-l app.kubernetes.io/name=mariadb-operator--tail=100 | grep-E "Controllers.galera" ``` **Output A — Operator is auto-recovering (no manual intervention needed, wait 2-3 minutes):** ``` 2026-04-03T04:38:46Z Controllers.galera Pod openstack-galera-0 running, retrieve seqno 2026-04-03T04:38:47Z Controllers.galera Attributes retrieved for openstack-galera-0 "Seqno": "410606", "SafeToBootstrap": false 2026-04-03T04:38:48Z Controllers.galera Attributes retrieved for openstack-galera-1 "Seqno": "410606", "SafeToBootstrap": false 2026-04-03T04:38:49Z Controllers.galera Attributes retrieved for openstack-galera-2 "Seqno": "410606", "SafeToBootstrap": false 2026-04-03T04:38:49Z Controllers.galera Pushing gcomm URI to bootstrap "pod": "openstack-galera-2" 2026-04-03T04:38:53Z Controllers.galera Pushing gcomm URI to joiner "pod": "openstack-galera-0" 2026-04-03T04:38:53Z Controllers.galera Pushing gcomm URI to joiner "pod": "openstack-galera-1" ``` If you see `Pushing gcomm URI to bootstrap`, the operator has already selected a bootstrap node and is auto-recovering. **Skip to step 6** to verify the cluster. **Output B — Operator is stuck (manual bootstrap needed after 10+ minutes):** ``` 2026-04-03T04:37:48Z Controllers.galera Requeuing until all replicas are available 2026-04-03T04:37:51Z Controllers.galera Requeuing until all replicas are available 2026-04-03T04:37:54Z Controllers.galera Requeuing until all replicas are available (repeats without any "retrieve seqno" or "Pushing gcomm" lines for 10+ minutes) ``` If only `Requeuing until all replicas are available` is shown without progressing to `retrieve seqno` for 10+ minutes, **proceed with manual bootstrap (step 3-5)**. 3. Check the `grastate.dat` on each Galera pod to find **the highest `seqno`**. Note that `grastate.dat` may show `seqno:-1` — the operator recovers the real seqno from InnoDB redo log internally. You can also run `galera_recovery` manually: ``` $ for i in 0 1 2; do echo "--- galera-$i---" oc exec-n openstack openstack-galera-$i-c galera-- cat /var/lib/mysql/grastate.dat 2> &1 done ``` When all nodes show `seqno:-1`, run `galera_recovery` on each pod to determine the real seqno: ``` $ for i in 0 1 2; do echo "--- galera-$i---" oc exec-n openstack openstack-galera-$i-c galera-- galera_recovery 2> &1 | grep "Recovered position" done ``` Select the node with **the highest recovered seqno** for bootstrap. 4. Trigger manual bootstrap on **the node with the highest seqno**. First confirm which pod is on which OCP node: ``` $ oc get pod-n openstack-o wide | grep galera openstack-galera-0 0/1 Running 0 37m 10.128.26.23 worker20.ocp.example.com openstack-galera-1 0/1 Running 0 37m 10.128.40.28 worker18.ocp.example.com openstack-galera-2 0/1 Running 0 37m 10.128.38.50 worker19.ocp.example.com ``` Then write `gcomm://` to the selected pod (assuming `galera-2` has the highest seqno): ``` $ oc exec-n openstack openstack-galera-2-c galera-- bash-c 'echo "gcomm://" > /var/lib/mysql/gcomm_uri' ``` 5. Repeat the same for `cell1-galera` if applicable: ``` $ for i in 0 1 2; do echo "--- cell1-galera-$i---" oc exec-n openstack openstack-cell1-galera-$i-c galera-- cat /var/lib/mysql/grastate.dat 2> &1 done # Bootstrap on the node with the highest seqno: $ oc exec-n openstack openstack-cell1-galera--c galera-- bash-c 'echo "gcomm://" > /var/lib/mysql/gcomm_uri' ``` 6. Wait for Galera to form a cluster (typically 1-2 minutes), then verify: ``` $ oc get pods-n openstack | grep galera openstack-galera-0 1/1 Running 0 5m openstack-galera-1 1/1 Running 0 5m openstack-galera-2 1/1 Running 0 5m openstack-cell1-galera-0 1/1 Running 0 5m openstack-cell1-galera-1 1/1 Running 0 5m openstack-cell1-galera-2 1/1 Running 0 5m ``` 7. If any Galera pod is in `Pending` with `volume node affinity conflict`, wait for the bound node to become `Ready`: ``` $ oc describe pod openstack-galera--n openstack | grep-A3 Events Events: Warning FailedScheduling 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:}, 2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict. ``` The pod will be automatically scheduled once the node recovers. 8. After Galera is fully recovered, delete remaining `CrashLoopBackOff` service pods to accelerate recovery: ``` $ oc get pods-n openstack--no-headers | grep CrashLoopBackOff | awk '{print $1}' | xargs-I {} oc delete pod {}-n openstack ```
root_cause: **After an OCP cluster restart, all Galera pods enter `Waiting for gcomm URI to be configured for this POD` as a normal intermediate state.** The mariadb-operator is designed to detect this state, recover the real seqno from the InnoDB redo log via `detect_last_commit.sh`, select a bootstrap node, and push `gcomm://` to complete the recovery automatically. **Under normal conditions, the operator completes this auto-bootstrap within 1-2 minutes after all pods reach `0/1 Running` state.** **The Galera cluster remains stuck at `Waiting for gcomm URI` only when the mariadb-operator is unable to complete this auto-bootstrap process.** The following conditions prevent the operator from progressing: 1. **Galera pods have not reached `Running` state** — e.g. stuck in `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` due to [SSL certificate errors on compact clusters](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140998), or stuck in `Pending` due to `volume node affinity conflict`. The operator can only retrieve seqno from pods in `Running` state. 2. **The mariadb-operator itself is unavailable or in an error state** — unable to reconcile the Galera CR. If all pods are in `0/1 Running` and the operator log shows `Requeuing until all replicas are available` without progressing to `retrieve seqno` for 10+ minutes, manual bootstrap is required as described in the Resolution. To prevent service disruption during planned maintenance, follow the [official RHOSO shutdown procedure](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html/maintaining_the_red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift_deployment/assembly_shutting-down-and-starting-up-rhoso-nodes) which ensures a proper shutdown order (instances → data plane → RHOCP cluster).

title: Keystone returns HTTP 500 with `tls_cacertfile not found or is not a file` when querying LDAP users
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Running `openstack user list--domain ` returns `Internal Server Error (HTTP 500)`.- The Keystone log shows `OSError: tls_cacertfile not found or is not a file`.- The LDAP domain config has `tls_cacertfile` set, but the path does not match the actual file location inside the Keystone container.
resolution: 1. **Identify the correct certificate mount path inside the Keystone container.** The path depends on how the CA certificate was mounted (Secret, ConfigMap, etc.). Check the pod/container description for volume mounts: RHOSO 18: ``` $ oc describe pod/-n openstack | grep-B 1 "ldap\|ca\|cert\|ssl" /etc/keystone/ssl/certs from keystone-ldap-ca (ro) ``` RHOSP 17 (on a controller node): ``` $ sudo podman inspect keystone--format '{{json.Mounts}}' | python3-m json.tool | grep-i "ldap\|ca\|cert\|ssl" ``` 2. **List the actual files at the mount path** to confirm the file name: RHOSO 18: ``` $ oc-n openstack rsh ls-la /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1234 Apr 1 08:26 ldap-root-ca.pem ``` RHOSP 17 (on a controller node): ``` $ sudo podman exec keystone ls-la /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ ``` 3. **Update `tls_cacertfile` in the domain config to use the correct path.** For example, if the certificate is mounted at `/etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem`: ```ini [ldap] tls_cacertfile = /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem ``` **Note: use `=` as the delimiter, not `:`.** The OpenStack INI config standard format uses `=` (per upstream [Keystone documentation](https://docs.openstack.org/keystone/latest/admin/configuration.html)). Using `:` may cause unexpected parsing: ```ini # Wrong tls_cacertfile: /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem # Correct tls_cacertfile = /etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem ``` 4. Re-apply the config and verify: RHOSO 18: ``` $ oc apply-f keystone-domains.yaml ``` RHOSP 17 (on a controller node): ``` $ sudo pcs resource restart galera-bundle ``` Then test: ``` $ openstack user list--domain ```
root_cause: 1. **Keystone checks that `tls_cacertfile` exists before connecting to LDAP.** In `keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py` (line 614-617), the code uses `os.path.isfile()` to verify the file path. If the file does not exist, it raises an `IOError` which results in HTTP 500: ```python if tls_cacertfile: if not os.path.isfile(tls_cacertfile): raise IOError(_("tls_cacertfile %s not found " "or is not a file") % tls_cacertfile) ldap.set_option(ldap.OPT_X_TLS_CACERTFILE, tls_cacertfile) ``` Source references:- RHOSO 18 (2023.1): [common.py#L614](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/branch/unmaintained/2023.1/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L614)- RHOSP 17 (Wallaby): [common.py#L614](https://opendev.org/openstack/keystone/src/tag/wallaby-eol/keystone/identity/backends/ldap/common.py#L614) 2. **Common causes for path mismatch:**- **Using the host path instead of the container path.** The CA certificate file exists on the host (e.g. `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ca.crt.pem`), but Keystone runs inside a container where a different mount path is used (e.g. `/etc/keystone/ssl/certs/ldap-root-ca.pem`).- **File name mismatch.** The ConfigMap or Secret was created with `--from-file=ldap-root-ca.pem`, but the config references a different file name like `ca.crt.pem`.- **Using `:` instead of `=` as INI delimiter.** While Python's configparser accepts `:`, the upstream Keystone [documentation](https://docs.openstack.org/keystone/latest/admin/configuration.html) uses `=` as the standard format. Using `:` may cause confusion especially when the value itself contains `:` (e.g. in URL values like `ldap://host:389`)

Err: +password is missing","TraceId":"784aa8fd-9190-40a1-ad94-33259ee39924", ~~~

title: How do I recover from lost or invalid Galera cluster root credentials in Red Hat OpenStack Services on Openshift
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: As an operator I need to recover service for a Galera cluster that has invalid root credentials, which prevents it from running.
resolution: Resetting the database root credentials for a specific Galera CR in use in the Openstack control plane can be achieved by following the steps below. 1. Identify the Galera resource to recover In the OCP namespace that hosts the Openstack control plane (e.g. `openstack`), look for the Galera resource that requires password recovery: ``` $ NAMESPACE=openstack $ oc get galera NAME READY MESSAGE openstack Unknown Setup started openstack-cell1 True Setup complete ``` Then store the name of the target resource in an environment variable for the next steps. ``` $ export GALERA_CR=openstack ``` 2. Create a new secret to replace the existing Galera root credentials Prepare a new secret that will hold the new database root password. Keep the name of this new secret in an environment variable for the next steps. ``` $ SECRET=${GALERA_CR}-new-root-credentials $ cat < ${SECRET}.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: ${SECRET} type: Opaque stringData: DatabasePassword: "mynewrootpassword" EOT ``` And create this secret resource in the OCP cluster, in the same namespace as the Galera CR to recover. ``` $ oc-n $NAMESPACE apply-f $SECRET.yaml ``` NOTE: Make sure that the name of this secret is unique. If another Galera CR is to be recovered on the same control plane, make sure to create a new secret with a different name. 3. Identify the MariaDBAccount CR associated to the Galera CR to restore. Starting RHOSO 18.0.17 (FR5), the Galera CR has an associated MariaDBAccount CR to hold information about the root credentials. This CR will be updated to reference the new secret created before hand. Store the name of the MariaDBAccount CR in an environment variable for the following steps. ``` $ DBACCOUNT_CR=$(oc get-o name mariadbaccount-l "dbName=${GALERA_CR}") $ echo ${DBACCOUNT_CR} mariadbaccount.mariadb.openstack.org/openstack-mariadb-root ``` 4. Update the MariaDBAccount CR to reference the new credentials The MariaDBAccount CR holds two references to root credentials: the CR's spec holds a reference for the new root password, while the CR's status holds a reference to the current root password, that can be used to connect to mysql to update credentials. First, save the name of the secret currently used by the MariaDBAccount CR. ``` $ OLD_SECRET=$(oc-n $NAMESPACE get $DBACCOUNT_CR-o json | jq-r.spec.secret) $ echo $OLD_SECRET openstack-mariadb-root-db-secret ``` Then, update the MariaDBAccount's spec to point to the new secret that holds the new root credentials. ``` $ oc-n $NAMESPACE patch $DBACCOUNT_CR--type merge-p '{"spec": {"secret": "'${SECRET}'"}}' ``` In this scenario, the Galera CR is not operational due to the current root credentials being invalid. So as an additional step, update the MariaDBAccount's status to point to the new secret as well. ``` $ oc-n $NAMESPACE patch $DBACCOUNT_CR--subresource=status--type merge-p '{"status": {"currentSecret": "'${SECRET}'"}}' ``` Verify that the two references to the new secret have been updated correctly ``` $ oc-n $NAMESPACE describe $DBACCOUNT_CR | grep-i secret Secret: openstack-new-root-credentials Current Secret: openstack-new-root-credentials ``` 5. Force the Galera CR to restart and update the root credentials Now that the new root credentials are set up, delete the existing pods of the Galera CR to be recovered. ``` $ PODS=$(oc get pods-l "galera/name=${GALERA_CR}"-o name) $ echo $PODS pod/openstack-galera-0 pod/openstack-galera-1 pod/openstack-galera-2 $ echo $PODS | xargs-r oc-n $NAMESPACE delete pod "openstack-galera-0" deleted from openstack namespace pod "openstack-galera-1" deleted from openstack namespace pod "openstack-galera-2" deleted from openstack namespace ``` The pods will get automatically recreated. On restart restart, the startup script running in the pod's init container will notice that new root credentials are available, and it will automatically update the mysql database. This will allow each pod to restart correctly, reform a Galera cluster, and restore database service for this Galera CR. 6. Optional: remove the secret that holds the old credentials If the old secret is no longer in use, you can delete it. Before you do that, since the secret was not released by the mariadb-operator itself, you need to manually remove the finalizer set for the MariaDBAccount before being able to delete it. ``` $ oc-n $NAMESPACE get secret $OLD_SECRET-o json | jq 'del(.metadata.finalizers[] | select(. == "openstack.org/m ariadbaccount"))' | oc-n $NAMESPACE apply-f- ```

title: How to backup and restore RHOSO Galera database PVCs using CSI VolumeSnapshot
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - Need to backup RHOSO Galera (MariaDB) database PVCs before performing maintenance operations such as deleting pods, scaling down replicas, or cluster upgrades.- Need to restore Galera database from backup after data loss (e.g. accidental PVC deletion).
resolution: ## Backup: Creating VolumeSnapshots 1. Confirm all Galera pods are `1/1 Running` and the cluster is healthy before creating snapshots: ``` $ oc get pods-n openstack | grep galera openstack-galera-0 1/1 Running 0 107m openstack-galera-1 1/1 Running 0 107m openstack-galera-2 1/1 Running 0 107m ``` 2. Identify the VolumeSnapshotClass for your storage backend: ``` $ oc get volumesnapshotclass NAME DRIVER DELETIONPOLICY AGE lvms-vg1 topolvm.io Delete 2d20h ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com Delete 2d5h ``` Use **the VolumeSnapshotClass that matches your Galera PVC's StorageClass driver**. For LVMS, use `lvms-vg1`. For ODF/Ceph RBD, use `ocs-storagecluster-rbdplugin-snapclass`. 3. Check the current PVC sizes. **For LVMS (topolvm), the PVC capacity must match the actual LV size on disk, otherwise the snapshot will fail with `requested size is smaller than source logical volume`.** If the PVC was originally created by the operator with a default size, you may need to expand it first: ``` $ oc get pvc-n openstack | grep mysql-db-openstack-galera mysql-db-openstack-galera-0 Bound pvc-xxx 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-galera-1 Bound pvc-xxx 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-galera-2 Bound pvc-xxx 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d ``` If PVC capacity is not a round GB value (e.g. `4882816Ki` instead of `5Gi` or `6Gi`), expand the PVCs to the next round GB to avoid the LVMS size mismatch: ``` $ for i in 0 1 2; do oc patch pvc mysql-db-openstack-galera-$i-n openstack \--type merge-p '{"spec":{"resources":{"requests":{"storage":"6Gi"}}}}' done persistentvolumeclaim/mysql-db-openstack-galera-0 patched persistentvolumeclaim/mysql-db-openstack-galera-1 patched persistentvolumeclaim/mysql-db-openstack-galera-2 patched ``` Wait for the resize to complete: ``` $ oc get pvc-n openstack | grep mysql-db-openstack-galera mysql-db-openstack-galera-0 Bound pvc-xxx 6Gi RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-galera-1 Bound pvc-xxx 6Gi RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-galera-2 Bound pvc-xxx 6Gi RWO lvms-vg1 2d ``` 4. Create VolumeSnapshots for all Galera PVCs: ``` $ for i in 0 1 2; do cat <
root_cause: **This KCS is a procedural guide, not a problem resolution.** CSI VolumeSnapshot provides a point-in-time, storage-level snapshot of Galera PVCs. Since Galera is a synchronous multi-master replication cluster, all 3 nodes hold identical data — taking a snapshot of any single node's PVC is sufficient to restore the entire dataset. However, snapshotting all 3 PVCs ensures consistency regardless of which node the operator selects for bootstrap during restore. **LVMS (topolvm) specific limitation:** When the Galera PVC was originally provisioned, the actual LV size on disk may be slightly larger than the PVC capacity reported by Kubernetes (due to LVM thin provisioning metadata overhead). This causes `VolumeSnapshot` creation to fail with `requested size is smaller than source logical volume`. Expanding the PVC to the next round GB value before creating the snapshot resolves this mismatch. **LVMS snapshot node affinity:** LVMS snapshots can only be restored on the same node as the source logical volume. For separated architectures where Galera pods run on specific worker nodes, ensure those nodes are available during restore. # Diagnostic Steps 1. If VolumeSnapshot creation fails, check the snapshot status: ``` $ oc describe volumesnapshot galera-snapshot-0-n openstack | grep-A5 "Status:" Status: Error: Message: Failed to check and update snapshot content: failed to take snapshot of the volume: "rpc error: code = OutOfRange desc = requested size 5000003584 is smaller than source logical volume: 5003804672" Ready To Use: false ``` This error indicates the PVC capacity does not match the actual LV size. Expand the PVC (Resolution step 3) and retry. 2. If restored PVCs remain `Pending` after scaling Galera back to 3, check the PVC events: ``` $ oc describe pvc mysql-db-openstack-galera-0-n openstack | grep-A5 Events: ``` For LVMS with `WaitForFirstConsumer`, PVCs will remain `Pending` until a pod is scheduled — this is normal. 3. If Galera pods fail to start after restore, check the galera container log: ``` $ oc logs-n openstack openstack-galera-0-c galera--tail=20 ```

title: RHOSO Galera pods stuck in `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` with `SSL error: Unable to get certificate from '/etc/pki/tls/certs/galera.crt'` after OCP node restart
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - After OCP nodes restart (graceful or ungraceful shutdown), all Galera pods are stuck in `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` and not recovering.- The init container (`mysql-bootstrap`) logs show: ``` SSL error: Unable to get certificate from '/etc/pki/tls/certs/galera.crt' [ERROR] Failed to setup SSL [ERROR] SSL error: Unable to get certificate [ERROR] Aborting ```- **May also occur:*

Pod events show `FailedMount` errors for TLS cert volumes during early startup: ``` Warning FailedMount MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "galera-tls-certs": object "openstack"/"cert-galera-openstack-svc" not registered ```- **May also occur:*
All OpenStack services depending on Galera (Keystone, Cinder, Glance, etc.) enter `CrashLoopBackOff` due to database unavailability. Dashboard returns 504 and CLI returns 502.
resolution: 1. Confirm all OCP nodes are `Ready`: ``` $ oc get nodes NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION master0 Ready control-plane,master,worker 2d20h v1.31.14 master1 Ready control-plane,master,worker 2d21h v1.31.14 master2 Ready control-plane,master,worker 2d21h v1.31.14 ``` If any node is `NotReady`, wait for it to recover or investigate the node issue first. 2. Confirm the TLS Secret is available in the openstack namespace: ``` $ oc get secret-n openstack | grep cert-galera cert-galera-openstack-svc kubernetes.io/tls 3 2d cert-galera-openstack-cell1-svc kubernetes.io/tls 3 2d ``` If the Secret exists, the SSL error is transient — the init container started before OCP had fully recovered the Secret mounts. 3. Check the current Galera pod status and confirm they are in `Init:CrashLoopBackOff`: ``` $ oc get pods-n openstack | grep galera openstack-galera-0 0/1 Init:CrashLoopBackOff 7 (102s ago) 44m openstack-galera-1 0/1 Init:CrashLoopBackOff 7 (97s ago) 44m openstack-galera-2 0/1 Init:CrashLoopBackOff 7 (107s ago) 44m ``` 4. Before deleting any pod, **ensure the associated PVC is in `Bound` state and consider [backing up the PVC data using CSI VolumeSnapshot](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7141000). If you are unsure, please contact Red Hat Support for remote assistance.** ``` $ oc get pvc-n openstack | grep mysql-db mysql-db-openstack-galera-0 Bound pvc-a44b1b88 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-galera-1 Bound pvc-f059e76e 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-galera-2 Bound pvc-2e273a24 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-cell1-galera-0 Bound pvc-a4bd233c 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-cell1-galera-1 Bound pvc-46588aa0 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d mysql-db-openstack-cell1-galera-2 Bound pvc-3c106831 4882816Ki RWO lvms-vg1 2d ``` All PVCs must show `Bound`. 5. After confirming all PVCs are `Bound`, delete the affected Galera pods to trigger recreation: ``` $ for i in 0 1 2; do oc delete pod openstack-galera-$i openstack-cell1-galera-$i-n openstack--grace-period=0--force done ``` 6. Wait for Galera pods to recreate and verify they reach `1/1 Running` (typically 2-3 minutes): ``` $ oc get pods-n openstack | grep galera openstack-galera-0 1/1 Running 0 3m openstack-galera-1 1/1 Running 0 3m openstack-galera-2 1/1 Running 0 3m openstack-cell1-galera-0 1/1 Running 0 3m openstack-cell1-galera-1 1/1 Running 0 3m openstack-cell1-galera-2 1/1 Running 0 3m ``` 7. Verify Galera cluster is fully formed: ``` $ oc exec-n openstack openstack-galera-0-c galera-- bash-c \ 'source /var/lib/operator-scripts/mysql_root_auth.sh && mysql-u root-e "SHOW STATUS LIKE '\''wsrep_cluster_size'\'';"' Variable_name Value wsrep_cluster_size 3 ``` 8. After Galera is fully recovered, delete remaining `CrashLoopBackOff` service pods to accelerate recovery: ``` $ oc get pods-n openstack--no-headers | grep CrashLoopBackOff | awk '{print $1}' | xargs-I {} oc delete pod {}-n openstack ```
root_cause: **The Galera init container (`mysql-bootstrap`) starts MariaDB in `--skip-grant-tables` mode to reset the root password. This process requires the TLS certificate at `/etc/pki/tls/certs/galera.crt`, which is mounted from the Kubernetes Secret `cert-galera-openstack-svc`.** After an OCP node restart, the kubelet may schedule and start the pod before all volume mounts (including Secrets and CSI volumes) are fully ready. When the init container attempts to start MariaDB with an incomplete or missing TLS certificate, it fails with `SSL error: Unable to get certificate` and aborts. **This issue primarily affects compact clusters** (control-plane + worker on the same nodes). On a compact cluster, after a full restart, etcd, API server, CSI drivers, and Secret controller all restart on the same nodes simultaneously. The kubelet begins scheduling pods before all controllers are fully ready, causing the TLS Secret to be unavailable when the init container runs. On **separated architectures** (dedicated master + dedicated worker nodes), the master nodes recover the control-plane first (including Secret controller and CSI drivers), so by the time workers begin scheduling Galera pods, the Secrets are already propagated — the init container does not encounter SSL errors. The init container then enters `CrashLoopBackOff` with increasing backoff intervals (10s, 20s, 40s,..., up to 5 minutes). This prevents the main `galera` container from starting, which in turn prevents the mariadb-operator from retrieving the `seqno` and performing auto-bootstrap. All OpenStack services then cascade-fail because they depend on Galera as the database backend. Deleting the pods and allowing them to be recreated resolves the issue because by that time OCP has fully recovered all Secrets and CSI volumes, so the init container can successfully mount the TLS certificate.

title: Is APIcast pod terminated gracefully
issue: Is it possible to configure APIcast to shutdown after returned responses for all requests on OpenShift?
resolution: An RFE to add this graceful shutdown behavior to the product has been opened in [THREESCALE-6454](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-6454)　and it has been implemented in 3scale 2.16.0.　As of version 2.16.0, the `preStop` configuration specified in the Deployment below is deprecated and no longer required. As a workaround, 3scale administrators can configure `preStop` directive like below: ~~~ lifecycle: preStop: exec: command:- /bin/sh- '-c'- /opt/app-root/src/bin/apicast-s quit-p /tmp/lua_*/nginx.pid && sleep 10 ~~~ This can be applied to both of:- `DeploymentConfig` managed by 3scale operator version 2.13/2.14- `Deployment` managed by APIcast operator(self-managed apicast) or 3scale operator version 2.15 or later Generally, the value of sleep (10s) provided in this KCS is enough for most use case, but if the backend require longer time to process the request then sleep value will need to be adjusted.- Sleep value should be larger then the longest time take to finish a request.- Sleep value should be smaller then the value of [terminationGracePeriodSeconds](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/building_applications/deployments#deployments-graceful-termination_route-based-deployment-strategies).- After the graceful termination period expires, a process that has not exited is sent the KILL signal, which immediately ends the process. The terminationGracePeriodSeconds attribute of a pod or pod template controls the graceful termination period (default 30 seconds) and can be customized per application as necessary.- With above configuration, `FailedPreStopHook` warning with the message `"PreStopHook failed"` may happen in OCP event log when terminating apicast pod. This is due to that the container process(nginx) terminates by graceful shutdown request while executing preStop hook and this can be safely ignored when it could terminate gracefully.
root_cause: APIcast stops handling requests immediately. A client can retry the request which will then be routed to another running APIcast pod. OpenShift sends `SIGTERM` to processes in a container when a node is evacuated, then APIcast stop handling requests immediately. Even if multiple APIcast pods are deployed, the evacuating APIcast returns 502 Bad Gateway. On the other hand, Nginx will shutdown gracefully if it receives `QUIT` signal, or 'nginx-s quit' command.

title: Supportability for ImageContentSourcePolicy resource to use tags in OpenShift 4
issue: Can the `ImageContentSourcePolicy` resource use tags instead of image digests for images?
How to use community operators with tags?
How to mirror image registries in disconnected environments to refer image tags instead of digests?
How to configure `mirror-by-digest-only` option to allow the ICSP to use tags?
How to configure `mirror-by-digest-only = false` to allow the use of image tags in disconnected environments?
How to change `pull-from-mirror = "digest-only"` in the `/etc/containers/registries.conf`?
resolution: Starting from RHOCP 4.13, it is possible to use `ImageTagMirrorSet` (ITMS) object to pull mirrored images using tags, see [RHOCP 4.13 release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/release_notes/ocp-4-13-release-notes.html#ocp-4-13-icsp).- **Attention:** before RHOCP 4.15, `ImageTagMirrorSet` (ITMS) are not compatible with `ImageContentSourcePolicy` (ICSP), [RHOCP 4.15 release notes](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.15/release_notes/ocp-4-15-release-notes.html#ocp-4-15-nodes-icsp-idms-compatibility), and is required to convert the ICSP into `ImageDigestMirrorSet` (IDMS) first. For details see: [Converting ImageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP) files for image registry repository mirroring](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/post_installation_configuration/preparing-for-users.html#images-configuration-registry-mirror-convert_post-install-preparing-for-users). ### Workaround before RHOCP 4.13 {#workaround} > **Important:** there is a security risk if using this workaround, as pulling images from mirror registries without the digest specifications could lead to returning different image version from different registry if the image tag mapping is out of sync. Refer to [Image SHA Digests vs. Image Tags](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4975041) for more information. 1. If the mirror was already created in the `ImageContentSourcePolicy`, remove the one that needs the `mirror-by-digest-only = false` option from there. 2. Create a `my_registry.conf` configuration file, specifying the source and mirror registry and set the `mirror-by-digest-only = false` option (change the image location accordingly): [[registry]] prefix = "" location = "[original_image_or_registry_namespace_location]" mirror-by-digest-only = false [[registry.mirror]] location = "[mirrored_image_or_registry_namespace_location]" 3. Encode the file content to the `base64` format: $ base64-w0 my_registry.conf 4. Create a `worker-mirror-by-digest-registries.yaml` file that can be applied to the MCO to [change the cluster configuration](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator#applying-configuration-changes-to-the-cluster). Copy the `base64` text to the `source` field (changing the `[base64_code]` in the example), and set the `/etc/containers/registries.conf.d` to the `path` field: apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-worker-mirror-by-digest-registries spec: config: ignition: version: 3.1.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,[base64_code] filesystem: root mode: 420 path: /etc/containers/registries.conf.d/99-worker-mirror-by-digest-registries.conf > **Important:** it's needed to create a separate `machineconfig` for each node role. 5. Create the `worker-mirror-by-digest-registries.yaml` `machineconfig`: $ oc apply-f worker-mirror-by-digest-registries.yaml 6. Allow the MCO time to rollout the changes to all the nodes, and check that the file `99-mirror-by-digest-registries.conf` is created and it has the desired configuration: $ oc debug node/[node_name]-- cat /host/etc/containers/registries.conf.d/99-mirror-by-digest-registries.conf 7. And check that `podman` is able to use that configuration: $ oc debug node/[node_name]-- chroot /host bash-c 'podman info' [...] registries: [original_image_or_registry_namespace_location]: Blocked: false Insecure: false Location: [original_image_or_registry_namespace_location] MirrorByDigestOnly: false Mirrors:- Insecure: false Location: [mirrored_image_or_registry_namespace_location] Prefix: [original_image_or_registry_namespace_location] [...]
root_cause: - `ImageContentSourcePolicy` configure the `/etc/containers/registries.conf` for pulling mirrored images only by using digest.- In RHOCP 4.13 new CRDs where introduced for allowing mirroring images using tags.- For more information regarding why image SHA ID is used instead of image tags, please refer to [Image SHA Digests vs. Image Tags](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4975041).
