title: Private Automation Hub database migration fails with 'Incompatible versions detected (ansible >= 0.23.0 needed)' during AAP operator upgrade
issue: - When upgrading or installing Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) Operator, the installation fails during the run-migrations step with the following error: ~~~ RuntimeError: Incompatible versions detected (ansible > = 0.23.0 needed):- 'ansible'='0.21.7' with api server 'prod-infra-aap-hub-api-xxx-xxx'- 'ansible'='0.21.7' with api server 'prod-infra-aap-hub-api-xxx-xxx' ~~~ Please shutdown or upgrade the outdated components before you continue the migration. stream closed EOF for ansible-automation-platform/prod-infra-aap-hub-api-xxx-xxx(run-migrations)
resolution: Delete all hub-related deployments to break the deadlock. The operator will automatically recreate them, and the migration will succeed with no old components blocking it. 1. Delete the hub deployments (adjust names to match your environment): ``` oc delete deployment-n ``` For example: ``` oc delete deployment prod-pah-api prod-pah-content prod-pah-worker prod-pah-redis-n 000001-aap-hub ``` Do not delete Keycloak, RHSSO, or database deployments. 2. Wait for all hub pods to fully terminate: ``` oc get pods-n-w ``` 3. After all hub pods are terminated, wait at least 5 minutes for the old component registrations to expire from the Pulp database. The `API_APP_TTL`, `CONTENT_APP_TTL`, and `WORKER_TTL` settings control this expiration (default is 5 minutes). Alternatively, if you have database access, you can manually clear the stale registrations: ``` oc exec-it-c database-n-- psql-U-d-c "DELETE FROM core_apiappstatus;" ``` 4. The operator will detect the missing deployments and recreate them on its next reconciliation cycle. Monitor the API pod logs to confirm the migration completes: ``` oc logs-f deployment/-n ``` Look for the migration output ending with no errors, followed by gunicorn starting successfully. 5. Verify the fix: ``` oc get pods-n ``` All hub pods should be Running and Ready. The PAH web UI should load without errors, and EE image pulls should succeed. Note: If the migration fails a second time at `ansible.0059_collectionversion_unique_sha256` with an error about NULL sha256 values (rather than incompatible versions), this is a separate issue. Check for NULL values in the `ansible_collectionversion` table and populate them before retrying. For AAP 2.5 environments, upgrading to operator version 2.5.20250924 or later includes a permanent fix that prevents this deadlock from occurring.
root_cause: This is caused by a race condition during operator-managed rolling updates (Jira AAP-49016). When the operator pushes a new hub image, Kubernetes uses the RollingUpdate strategy, which keeps old pods running until new pods pass readiness checks. However, the new pods cannot pass readiness because the database migration fails. The migration fails because old pods are still registered in the Pulp `core_apiappstatus` table with outdated plugin versions. This creates a deadlock:- Old pods heartbeat to the database, keeping their outdated version registrations alive- The migration requires all registered components to be at the new version- New pods wait for the migration to complete before starting- The migration cannot complete because old pods are still registered On AAP 2.4, an additional defect in the API pod entrypoint script (missing `set-e`) causes gunicorn to start despite the migration failure, resulting in 500 errors from schema mismatches rather than a clean crash. A permanent fix was delivered in AAP operator version 2.5.20250924, which scales down old hub deployments before running migrations. AAP 2.4 operator releases do not include this fix.

title: Unable to reach a pod on its UserDefinedNetwork IP using BGP advertisement over isolated VRF in RHOCP
issue: - When using an isolated `VRF` to advertise a `UserDefinedNetwork` ("UDN") over `BGP`, the session is established but traffic from outside the cluster does not reach a pod's `UDN` IP.
resolution: Enable [Global IpForwarding](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/networking_operators/cluster-network-operator#nw-cno-enable-ip-forwarding_cluster-network-operator) to allow non-Kubernetes/OpenShift related traffic to be forwarded across unmanaged (*non OVN-managed*) interfaces.
root_cause: To establish the `BGP` session over an isolated (`UDN`-specific) `VRF`, it must be attached to an interface configured (ip / route) to reach the BGP peer. Once the `BGP` sesison is established, `UDN` traffic is routed over that interface. Neither the interface or its attachment to the `UDN` `VRF` is OVN-managed, and by default (see **Resolution**), non-Kubernetes/OpenShift traffic is not forwarded to *unmanaged* interfaces.

title: VMs migrated with MTV between OpenShift clusters fails to boot because of corrupted destination disks
issue: Virtual Machines (VMs) migrated between OpenShift clusters using MTV fail to boot in the destination cluster. The destination disks are found to contain raw POSIX tar archive data instead of a bootable operating system. ~~~ # oc exec-n virt-launcher--- dd if=/dev/vol-0 bs=1M count=1 > vol-0.out # file vol-0.out vol-0.out: POSIX tar archive (GNU) ~~~ The disks are located in filesystem PVCs
resolution: This issue is a known bug tracked in [CNV-82196](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNV-82196) where the disk is exported as a compressed archive but imported without extraction. Workaround is to manually add the kubevirt content-type annotation to the source PVCs before initiating the migration. ~~~ # oc annotate pvc-n cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.contentType=kubevirt ~~~ After applying the annotation, restart the migration plan. The VM should boot successfully in the destination cluster.
root_cause: When a source VM disk is located on a filesystem-based PVC (such as NFS) and is missing the `cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.contentType: kubevirt` annotation, the OpenShift Virtualization export server defaults to exposing the disk as a disk.tar.gz file. During the migration, the Containerized Data Importer (CDI) on the destination cluster downloads this stream. However, if the PVC lacks a DataVolume owner or the specific content-type annotation, CDI may dump the raw tar data directly onto the destination block device without extracting the actual disk image. This results in the destination disk being a tar file containing the VM's data, which is not bootable.

title: Log Forwarding to External LokiStack Fails with HTTP 302 Error in RHOCP 4
issue: - Log Forwarding to `External LokiStack` Fails with `HTTP 302` response.- `External LokiStack` Log Forwarding Interrupted with request_failed Error.- Collector pod logs show authentication-related failures similar to the following: ~~~ YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.XXXXXXXXZ YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.XXXXXXXXZ ERROR sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=output_loki_infra component_type=loki}: vector_common::internal_event::service: Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted. error=Some(ServerError {code: 302}) request_id=40572 error_type="request_failed" stage="sending" internal_log_rate_limit=true ~~~
resolution: To resolve this issue, configure proper authentication between the clusters:- Create a `ServiceAccount` on `External LokiStack` Cluster: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging create sa logger-external ~~~- Grant Required Permissions: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user logging-collector-logs-writer-z logger-external ~~~- Create a `ServiceAccount` Token `Secret`: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: logger-external-token namespace: openshift-logging annotations: kubernetes.io/service-account.name: logger-external type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token ~~~- Get a token value: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging get secret logger-external-token-o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64-d ~~~- Create a `secret` in the source cluster: ~~~ $ oc-n openshift-logging create secret generic remote-loki-token--from-literal=token= ~~~- Update the `ClusterLogForwarder` with new `secret`: ~~~ outputs:- loki: authentication: token: from: secret secretName: remote-loki-token #new secret name key: token url: https:// /api/logs/v1/infrastructure name: loki-infra tls: ca: key: ca-bundle.crt secretName: type: loki ~~~- After executing the above action plan, verify that logs are successfully ingested into the `External LokiStack`. For more information, please open a [new support case with Red Hat Support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1242003).
root_cause: This issue occurs due to authentication misconfiguration between the vector collector log forwarder and the `External LokiStack`.

title: Red Hat OpenJDK  vs AdoptJDK vs IBM Semeru
issue: - What is the difference between Red Hat OpenJDK vs AdoptOpenJDK?- What is the difference between Red Hat's OpenJDK vs IBM's Semeru?
resolution: OpenJDK is an open source project with several companies, head by Oracle. Red Hat has the leadership on some releases, see [OpenJDK Life Cycle and Support Policy](https://access.redhat.com/articles/1299013). Red Hat also contributes to GraalVM (together with other actors) and heads Mandrel project, as a downstream of GraalVM (meaning a fork of the project maintained by Red Hat). In a nutshell, Mandrel can be described as a distribution of a regular OpenJDK with a specially packaged GraalVM native image, especially for Quarkus, which is supported as RHBQ (Red Hat Build of Quarkus). Red Hat's Mandrel (and Red Hat's Mandrel images) explicitly does not support Polyglot, it only supports Java with Mandrel and Quarkus. There are no plans to change this, i.e., to support Polyglot in Mandrel. ### Eclipse Adoptium Temurin (formerly AdoptOpenJDK) Adoptium Temurin (formerly AdoptOpenJDK) builds are prebuilt OpenJDK binaries maintained by the community under the Eclipse Foundation. The Red Hat and Adoptium Temurin builds are nearly identical. In fact, the Temurin build is created by many of the same Red Hat engineers who also create the Red Hat build. Notable differences: * The Temurin build includes a few crypto algorithms that do not conform to the Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) security policy (e.g. `secp256k1`). * The Temurin rpm install does not properly set the SELinux context. See [How to integrate Eclipse Temurin java with SELinux policy](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7106343). **Red Hat support for Temurin:** Red Hat supports Temurin, and any entitlement that provides support for the RH build of OpenJDK starting on August 2022 also provides support for the Temurin builds. However, for Red Hat only support Red Hat build of OpenJDK (and Temurin) for RHEL 8.x as explained on [Is OpenJDK 17 supported on RHEL7?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6971906) Technically, Eclipse Adoptium/AdoptOpenJDK is very similar to Oracle's OpenJDK distribution- i.e. in that it is free, and it is a build produced by compiling the sources from the hg.openjdk.java.net OpenJDK source repository. Red Hat OpenJDK has different features, such as Shenandoah GC, see doc [OracleJDK vs OpenJK](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2489791) However, AdoptOpenJDK is not on the list for support in some of our products, as JBoss EAP, thus not technically supported. In other words, some products from Red Hat **do not support Correto/AdoptJDK/Temurin as valid JVM**, for instance:- [EAP 7](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2026253): EAP 7.x currently does not but EAP 8 supports Adoptium- [RHPAM](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6065021);- [Data Grid 8](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4933551); AdoptOpenJDK produced binaries with OpenJ9, however since their move to the Eclipse Foundation under the new name, Adoptium, which is no longer legally allowed. Meaning they cannot provide AdoptOpenJDK's with OpenJ9. Therefore, see supported configurations of each product to validate the JVM and keep the support. ### Temurin Eclipse Temurin is the name of the OpenJDK distribution from Adoptium. ### Semeru Considering the shift on Adoptium described above, IBM developed its Semeru Runtimes, which basically wraps the class libraries from OpenJDK, along with the Eclipse OpenJ9 Java Virtual Machine. ### Summary table Distribution | Details | Notable differences------------|-----------|---------- Temurin | Eclipse Temurin is the name builds produced by the Eclipse Adoptium Working Group | crypto algorithms and SELinux context Semeru | IBM developed its Semeru Runtimes, which basically wraps the class libraries from OpenJDK, along with the Eclipse OpenJ9 Java Virtual Machine | Semeru's jcmd doesn't have VM.info (use jcmd $PID Dump.java) and takes 50% of container as heap size (RH takes 80% currently)

title: ACM Thanos compact pod continuously restart due to gorutine error.
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - ACM Thanos pod continuously restart due to `gorutine` error.- ACM Thanos compact pod continuously restart due to `pthread` creation failed error.
resolution: Add `max_conns_per_host` to `100` in thanos-object-storage secret: 1> Extract `thanos-object-storage` secret in a file (take a back up too if needed): ~~~ oc get secret thanos-object-storage-o jsonpath='{.data.thanos\.yaml}' | base64-d > thanos-object-storage.yaml ~~~ 2> Adding `max_conns_per_host` to `100` ~~~ type: s3 config: bucket: XX endpoint: s3-openshift-storage.apps.xx:443 insecure: false access_key: xx secret_key: xx/xx+xx http_config: max_conns_per_host: 100 # < < ==================== ADD THIS tls_config: ca_file: /etc/mco-bucket-for-thanos-tls/certs/ca.crt insecure_skip_verify: false ~~~ 3> Recreate secret: ~~~ oc create secret generic thanos-object-storage \--from-file=thanos.yaml=thanos-object-storage.yaml \--dry-run=client-o yaml | oc apply-f- ~~~
root_cause: The root cause was resource exhaustion triggered by an unlimited connection pool during high-intensity compaction cycles. In Go-based applications like Thanos, a missing `max_conns_per_host` parameter defaults to 0, which the runtime interprets as unlimited. This allowed the Compactor to attempt thousands of concurrent TLS handshakes simultaneously, creating a "handshake storm" of [runnable] goroutines. Manually setting the limit to `100` introduced critical backpressure, forcing the pod to reuse existing connections and preventing the Go scheduler from drowning in new connection overhead.

title: Migrating From Standalone Multicloud Gateway (MCG/NooBaa) to ODF/Ceph Full Deployment (Deployed Using StorageCluster) - OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)
issue: In the event a standalone MCG wants to migrate to a Full ODF Internal deployment, this solution will cover the process. **KNOWN ISSUE:*

All steps work correctly; however, there is a cosmetic issue: JUST the OCP Console UI Storage-> Data Foundation splash page shows "2 Storage Systems" despite only 1 storage system showing in the CLI and in the YAML post-migration (See below). ~~~ $ oc get storagesystem-n openshift-storage NAME STORAGE-SYSTEM-KIND STORAGE-SYSTEM-NAME ocs-storagecluster-storagesystem storagecluster.ocs.openshift.io/v1 ocs-storagecluster ~~~ **Only One Storage System Post Migration but OCP Console Shows 2:*

[image=[src="images/2_storage_systems.jpg", title="2 Storage Systems when there should be 1", alt="2 Storage Systems when there should be 1", size="LG- Large", data-cp-size="100%", data-cp-align="center", caption="2 Storage Systems when there should be 1", lightbox="true"]]
resolution: **WARNING: If this solution is not followed exactly and the noobaa-db database is compromised/lost, access to previous buckets will no longer be possible. A backup process is provided in this KCS.** # Prerequisite: * Ensure you're on a storagecluster.yaml deployed MCG. a. If the following output shows the storagecluster.yaml is populated with the following, proceed to the resolution. ~~~ $ oc get storagecluster-n openshift-storage-o yaml multiCloudGateway: dbStorageClassName: reconcileStrategy: standalone ~~~ b. `If the storagecluster.yaml` is empty or there is no `storagecluster.yaml`, execute the steps in the [Migrating from a Quay Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to an ODF StorageCluster ODF MCG- NooBaa](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7135274) solution before proceeding to the solution. # Resolution: The information below has been derived from the [Install Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation (previously known as OpenShift Container Storage) 4.X in internal-attached mode using command line interface](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5692201#create-cluster-11) solution. Refer to this solution or the official ODF product documentation for any additional configuration. 1. Take a backup of the `storagecluster.yaml` ~~~ $ oc get storagecluster-n openshift-storage-o yaml > storagecluster.yaml ~~~ 2. Prepare your nodes to be ODF storage nodes by adding the `openshift-storage` label: ~~~ $ oc label node cluster.ocs.openshift.io/openshift-storage='' ~~~ 3. Backup the NooBaa database using the respective solution correlating with the ODF version: [Perform a One-Time Backup of the noobaa-db-pg-0 Database for the Mulitcloud Object Gateway (NooBaa) for ODF v4.18 and Below](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7117672) [Perform a One-Time Backup of the Database for the Multicloud Object Gateway (NooBaa) in ODF v4.19+](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7127658) 4. If using Local storage, ensure devices are ready for consumption and in `Available` status. Refer back to the [Local Storage](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5692201#auto-discovering-devices-and-creating-persistent-volumes-7) section in the solution for configurations: ~~~ NAME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES RECLAIM POLICY STATUS CLAIM STORAGECLASS local-pv-59cdc4b9 100Gi RWO Delete Available <---- localblock local-pv-63304da2 100Gi RWO Delete Available <---- localblock local-pv-71fc8115 100Gi RWO Delete Available <---- localblock local-pv-90f5b88d 100Gi RWO Delete Available <---- localblock local-pv-d1d0e89e 100Gi RWO Delete Available <---- localblock local-pv-e169362c 100Gi RWO Delete Available <---- localblock ~~~ 5. Create an ODF storagecluster by adding the following to the storagecluster.yaml: **Note:** count x replica = total number of OSDs, but is determined by topology such as `failureDomain` (e.g. host, rack, zone, etc). See the [OSD Topology](https://rook.io/docs/rook/v1.12/CRDs/Cluster/ceph-cluster-crd/#osd-topology) documentation for clarification. The example below shows a deployment in `failureDomain: rack` or `failureDomain: zone`. Save and exit the storagecluster. Rook should begin building the cluster. Please allow plenty of time to complete successfully. **IMPORTANT:** At this point, the `noobaa-db-pg-(pod-name)` and/or if any PV-Pool (PVC-backed Backingstore) exists, they'll still be on the OLD storageclass. **If this is acceptable, you can stop here.** If wanting to migrate the default `ceph-rbd` storageclass review the respective solutions below: [How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.18 and Below](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140944) [How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.19+](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140980) [Migrating the PV-Pool Backingstore Storageclass to Ceph RBD after Standalone Multicloud Gateway (MCG/NooBaa) to Full OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140981) [ODF-Noobaa: How to Migrate NooBaa Buckets to a New Backingstore?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7009908)

title: Migrating data between PVs using the DataVolume CR
issue: - How do I manually migrate data between PVs using a DataVolume?- Persistent volume (PV) is getting full.- Need to migrate old PV data to different storage class.
resolution: 1. Gracefully shut down the VM (disks must be unlocked to clone). You can do this via the OCP web UI or using the below command: ~~~ $ virtctl stop ~~~ 2. Find the attached PVC you want to migrate in the VMs volumes field: ~~~ $ oc get vm-ojson|jq '.spec.template.spec.volumes' ~~~ 3. Create the DataVolume Clone YAML and apply the yaml: ~~~ $ vim datavolume-clone.yaml apiVersion: cdi.kubevirt.io/v1beta1 kind: DataVolume metadata: name: $NEW_PVC namespace: $NAMESPACE spec: source: pvc: namespace: $NAMESPACE name: $OLD_PVC storage: storageClassName: $TARGET_SC resources: requests: storage: $PVC_SIZE $ oc apply-f datavolume-clone.yaml ~~~ 4. Edit the VM to point to the new disk (claimName). The change will be under '.spec.template.spec.volumes': ~~~ $ oc edit vm volumes:- name: datavolume-disk persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: new-storage-pvc # Your new PVC name goes here ~~~ 5. Start the VM back up. You can do this via the OCP web UI or using the below command: ~~~ $ virtctl start ~~~
root_cause: For more complicated scenarios where multiple volumes need to be migrated or where volume data must be moved across clusters, Red Hat recommends using OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) or the Migration Toolkit for Containers (MTC).* *For more details on using OADP, please see:*- *[OADP documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/backup_and_restore/oadp-application-backup-and-restore#oadp-introduction)*- *[OpenShift APIs for Data Protection (OADP) FAQ](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5456281)* *For more details on using the MTC, please see:*- *[MTC documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/migration_toolkit_for_containers/about-mtc#about-mtc)*

title: How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.19+
issue: In some instances, generally coming from a standalone Multicloud Object Storage (MCG) deployment to a full ODF Ceph Internal/External cluster, it may be desired to migrate the database storageclass to an ODF Ceph storageclass. This solution will cover those steps. **NOTE:*

With the new Highly Available (HA) CNPG NooBaa Database introduced in ODF v4.19+. The steps in this solution are much safer/less complex than those in ODF v4.18. In this solution, there is no need to stop IO/writing to the database. **Related Articles:*

[Migrating From Standalone Multicloud Gateway (MCG/NooBaa) to ODF/Ceph Full Deployment (Deployed Using StorageCluster)- OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7055285) [How to Migrate the db-noobaa-db-pg- StorageClass to Ceph RBD after Migrating from Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to Full Openshift Data Foundation (ODF) Internal Deployment v4.18 and Below](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140944) **WARNING: IF STEPS ARE NOT FOLLOWED EXACTLY IN THIS SOLUTION, IT MAY CAUSE COMPLETE NOOBAA DATA LOSS.**
resolution: **Note:** The example below will show a CNPG Cluster with `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1` as Primary, and `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-2` as Secondary. These numbers change based on whether the database was failed over. Other clusters may have different`noobaa-db-pg-cluster-X` naming. Simply take the concepts below, and change the naming as needed. 1. Patch the `storagecluster.yaml`, and change the `dbStorageClass` parameter to the `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storageclass. Validate the storageclass name is correct with `$ oc get sc`: ~~~ $ oc patch storagecluster ocs-storagecluster-n openshift-storage--type='merge'-p '{"spec":{"multiCloudGateway":{"dbStorageClassName":"ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd"}}}' ~~~ 2. Validate this change has been pushed to the `noobaa.yaml`: ~~~ $ oc get noobaa-n openshift-storage noobaa-o yaml | grep dbStorageClass ~~~ 3. Backup the database IAW: [Perform a One-Time Backup of the Database for the Multicloud Object Gateway (NooBaa) in ODF v4.19+](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7127658) solution. 4. Once the database is backed up, capture the current/Primary database: **Syntax:** ~~~ $ oc get clusters.postgresql.cnpg.noobaa.io noobaa-db-pg-cluster-n openshift-storage ~~~ **Example output shows noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 as Primary:** ~~~ NAME AGE INSTANCES READY STATUS PRIMARY noobaa-db-pg-cluster 57m 2 2 Cluster in healthy state noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 ~~~ 5. Using the output from step 4, failover the **SECONDARY ONLY**, and allow for a `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3` database to be created and mounted on a PVC with the `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storageclass. **Example, failing over the Secondary noobaa-db-pg-cluster-2, the PVC MUST be delete first:** ~~~ $ oc delete pvc-n openshift-storage noobaa-db-pg-cluster-2 $ oc delete pod-n openshift-storage noobaa-db-pg-cluster-2 ~~~ 6. Allow `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3` to come in, import, and join. This process can be monitored with `$ watch oc get pods-n openshift-storage`. Once joined, capture the output of the CNPG cluster and confirm there are 2 healthy instances, and one of those instances is on the `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storageclass: ~~~ $ oc get clusters.postgresql.cnpg.noobaa.io noobaa-db-pg-cluster-n openshift-storage NAME AGE INSTANCES READY STATUS PRIMARY noobaa-db-pg-cluster 57m 2 <- 2 <- Cluster in healthy state noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 $ oc get pvc-n openshift-storage NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 Bound pvc-f221b541-xx 50Gi RWOP gp3-csi noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3 Bound pvc-8f74c954-xx 50Gi RWOP ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ~~~ 7. Once it's confirmed there are 2 healthy instances in step 6, and the new database is on the `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storageclass, delete the `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1` **pod**. This will allow for failover and make `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1` Secondary and `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3` Primary. **Do not force delete the pod,** allow plenty of time for the CNPG cluster to ensure `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3` is ready for Primary and for the transition to take place. ~~~ $ oc delete pod-n openshift-storage noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 ~~~ 8. Confirm `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3` is now Primary, then allow ~30 minutes to elapse before failing over `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1` PVC/Pod to allow for `noobaa-db-pg-cluster-4` to come in with the new `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storageclass. ~~~ $ oc get clusters.postgresql.cnpg.noobaa.io noobaa-db-pg-cluster-n openshift-storage NAME AGE INSTANCES READY STATUS PRIMARY noobaa-db-pg-cluster 90m 2 2 Cluster in healthy state noobaa-db-pg-cluster-3 $ oc delete pvc-n openshift-storage noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 $ oc delete pod-n openshift-storage noobaa-db-pg-cluster-1 ~~~

title: Live migration fails via UI for VirtualMachines with names 48 characters or longer in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - Attempting to initiate a Live Migration for a VirtualMachine from the OpenShift Web Console fails to trigger- This issue specifically occurs for VirtualMachines with names that are 48 characters or longer- Initiating the live migration for the exact same VirtualMachine via the command line using `virtctl migrate` completes successfully- Checking the VirtualMachineInstance (VMI) events reveals `FailedUpdate` warnings from the virtualmachine-controller, stating that the PodDisruptionBudget label exceeds the 63-character limit: ~~~ > oc describe vmi... Events: Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal SuccessfulCreate 61m disruptionbudget-controller Created PodDisruptionBudget Normal SuccessfulCreate 61m virtualmachine-controller Created virtual machine pod virt-launcher- Normal Created 61m virt-handler VirtualMachineInstance defined. Normal Started 61m virt-handler VirtualMachineInstance started. Warning FailedUpdate 59m (x15 over 60m) virtualmachine-controller Error expanding the PodDisruptionBudget: PodDisruptionBudget.policy " " is invalid: metadata.labels: Invalid value: "-migration- ": must be no more than 63 characters ~~~
resolution: - This issue is resolved in OpenShift Virtualization 4.20 and later. To permanently resolve this issue, plan an upgrade to a version where the fix is included- If upgrading the cluster is not immediately possible, you can bypass the UI-specific suffix limitation by triggering the live migration via the CLI 1. Log in to your OpenShift cluster using the oc CLI. 2. Ensure you have the virtctl client installed and configured. 3. Initiate the live migration using the following command: ~~~ > virtctl migrate-n ~~~
root_cause: - When migrating via the OpenShift Web Console, a `-migration- ` suffix is appended to the VMI name to generate a label for the PodDisruptionBudget. If the base VMI name is 48 characters or longer, the resulting string exceeds the strict 63-character limit for Kubernetes metadata labels, causing the operation to fail

title: Provide the ability to explicitly specify the VolumeSnapshotClass when creating a VirtualMachine snapshot in OCV4
issue: - In OpenShift Virtualization, VirtualMachine snapshot creation automatically relies on the snapshotClass configured in the StorageProfile associated with the StorageClass used by the VM disks.- In environments where:- Multiple StorageClasses exist- Multiple VolumeSnapshotClasses are configured- VMs use different Storage backends there is no mechanism to explicitly choose which VolumeSnapshotClass should be used when creating a VM snapshot.- Instead, the system implicitly selects the snapshot class defined in the StorageProfile, which can lead to incorrect snapshot class usage.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNV-81835). If this feature is required, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: OpenShift Logging console shows identical-timestamp logs out of order
issue: - In the OpenShift Logging console (`Observe-> Logs`), log entries that share the exact same timestamp are displayed in an inconsistent order that does not match the original pod log stream sequence.- The default sort view is `Date (timestamp)` with the latest entries shown at the top.- When multiple log entries carry identical timestamps — such as lines from a multi-line Java stack trace — no stable secondary sort key is applied, causing the entries to appear shuffled.- This behavior leads customers to believe that log collection or storage itself is broken, when in fact LokiStack has ingested and stored the records correctly.- The issue is reproducible regardless of whether `detectMultilineException` is enabled or disabled.- Example: the following order is observed in the console for entries sharing the same timestamp: ``` 1774248119668626272: "" 1774248119668701252: "" 1774248119668510686: "a multiline" 1774248119668798054: "log" 1774248119668168035: "2026-03-23T06:41:58.562Z INFO 1---..." ```- Expected order (matching LokiStack API response, latest entry first): ``` 1774248119668798054: "log" 1774248119668701252: "" 1774248119668626272: "" 1774248119668510686: "a multiline" 1774248119668168035: "2026-03-23T06:41:58.562Z INFO 1---..." ```
resolution: - Red Hat is aware of this issue and is working to improve log ordering behavior in a future release.
root_cause: - The OpenShift Logging console `Observe-> Logs` view sorts log entries by `Date (timestamp)` only, without applying a stable secondary ordering key when multiple entries share the same timestamp.- As a result, the display order for same-timestamp entries is non-deterministic and does not reflect the original pod log stream sequence or the LokiStack API response.- This is a display-layer limitation in the console. LokiStack ingestion and storage of the log records are not affected.

title: Observability Add-on intermittently stuck in Progressing state in RHACM 2.13
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: The `observability-controller` add-on on a managed cluster intermittently gets stuck in the `Progressing` state in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes (RHACM) 2.13.x
The add-on does not transition to `Available` despite metrics being forwarded successfully from the managed cluster

Checking the `ManagedClusterAddOn` status on the Hub cluster shows `Progressing` with reason `UpdateSuccessful`: ```json {"lastTransitionTime": "...", "message": "observability-controller add-on is progressing.", "reason": "UpdateSuccessful", "status": "True", "type": "Progressing"} ```
Meanwhile, on the managed cluster the `endpoint-observability-operator` logs confirm the add-on reports `Available` with reason `ForwardSuccessful`
resolution: This issue is tracked in Jira: [ACM-29923](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ACM-29923). A fix is being developed by the Engineering team. Update to the RHACM version containing the fix once available. **Workaround:** Restart the `endpoint-observability-operator` pod on the affected managed cluster: ``` oc delete pod-l name=endpoint-observability-operator-n open-cluster-management-addon-observability ``` If the issue persists after deleting the operator pod, also delete the `metrics-collector-deployment` pod: ``` oc delete pod-l component=metrics-collector-n open-cluster-management-addon-observability ``` After restarting, collect ACM must-gather from both the Hub and managed clusters to verify the status has transitioned to `Available`.
root_cause: The `status_controller` in the `multicluster-observability-operator` on the Hub cluster caches the `MetricsCollector` condition. When both `Progressing: True` and `Available: True` are present simultaneously, a conflict in the reconcile logic prevents the `MetricCollector` status from being updated, causing the add-on to remain stuck in `Progressing`.

title: Migrating from a Quay Standalone Multicloud Object Gateway (MCG) to an ODF StorageCluster-Managed MCG - NooBaa
issue: It has been previously shown in the [Quay Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_quay/3.7/html/deploy_red_hat_quay_on_openshift_with_the_quay_operator/operator-preconfigure#create_a_standalone_object_gateway) to deploy a NooBaa MCG stack using a NooBaa CR yaml instead of a storagecluster.yaml or going through the ODF UI to create the standalone MCG. If this configuration is discovered and can be easily identified with an empty storagecluster.yaml in the `openshift-storage` namespace, it will be required to migrate this configuration before the upgrade to ODF v4.19. **RELATED ARTICLES:*
[Standalone MCG Deployed via Quay Documentation Fails ODF v4.19 Upgrade](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7134589)

Run the following command and note that the same PVC storageclass **MUST** match the storageclass when creating the StorageCluster CR: **Example shows** `gp3-csi` storageclass: ~~~ $ oc get pvc-n openshift-storage | grep noobaa NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE db-noobaa-db-pg-0 Bound pvc-00d96c61-4bf5-4302-a5c4-739a493bbd3f 50Gi RWO gp3-csi 2m22s ~~~ 3. Apply the `storagecluster.yaml`: ~~~ $ oc apply-f storagecluster.yaml ~~~ 4. The pods will take some time to restart. Once all NooBaa pods are running, validate that the following two outputs reflect a phase `Ready`: ~~~ $ oc get noobaa-n openshift-storage $ oc get backingstore-A ~~~ **NOTE:** If on v4.19, this will take time as the new Cluster HA resource will begin copying the PVC from the `db-noobaa-db-pg-0` PVC to the two new PVCs for the primary/secondary db.

title: AJP File Read/Inclusion in Apache Tomcat (CVE-2020-1938) and Undertow (CVE-2020-1745)
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: [CVE-2020-1938](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2020-1938) is a file read/inclusion using the AJP connector in **Apache Tomcat**. The AJP protocol is enabled by default, with the AJP connector listening in TCP port `8009` and bond to IP address `0.0.0.0`. A remote, unauthenticated/untrusted attacker could exploit this AJP configuration to read web application files from a server exposing the AJP port to untrusted clients. In instances where a poorly configured server allows file uploads, an attacker could upload malicious JavaServer Pages (JSP) code within a variety of file types to gain remote code execution (RCE).
[CVE-2020-1745](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2020-1745) is a file read/inclusion using the AJP connector in **Undertow*
and very similar to CVE-2020-1938.
resolution: This is a configuration issue with AJP protocol in Tomcat/Undertow. AJP is a highly trusted protocol and should never be exposed to untrusted clients. It is insecure (clear text transmission) and assumes that your network is safe. The preventive measures should be taken by using the configuration that will not allow AJP to be exposed. In order of preference, one of the following mitigations should be applied: * Disable AJP altogether in Tomcat, and instead use HTTP or HTTPS for incoming proxy connections. HTTP and HTTPS do not contain the same trust issues as AJP. * Protect the AJP connection with a secret, as well as carefully reviewing network binding and firewall configuration to ensure incoming connections are only allowed from trusted hosts. * Use only network binding and firewall configuration to ensure incoming connections are only allowed from trusted hosts. The first option, disabling AJP, is the most secure and robust recommended solution. Protecting AJP with a secret may be less disruptive, but requires using either `mod_jk` or a version of `httpd` that supports the `secret` parameter. This parameter is supported by current versions of `httpd` in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 and 8, but the version included in Red Hat Software Collections do not support this parameter, so another mitigation strategy must be employed. Configuration showing how to disable AJP and how to protect it with a secret is shown below, for various Red Hat products. ### JWS (Tomcat) * If your site is **not** using the AJP Connector, disable it by commenting it out from the ` /conf/server.xml` file as: ~~~ ~~~ * If AJP connector is required and cannot be commented/deactivated, then we recommend to set a secret password for the AJP conduit- Only requests from workers with the same secret keyword will be accepted. At the Tomcat side, edit `conf/server.xml`: ~~~ ~~~ Note that `YOUR_AJP_SECRET` must be changed to a value that is highly secure and cannot be easily guessed. ### JWS (Tomcat) OpenShift container images * [JWS OpenShift container images](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/search?q=jboss%20web%20server&p=1) do not expose AJP connector port 8009 by default. Hence they are not affected by this vulnerability. ### JBoss EAP 5.2 (JBossWeb 2.1.x) * If your site is **not** using the AJP Connector, disable it by commenting it out from the ` /server/$PROFILE/deploy/jbossweb.sar/server.xml` file as: ~~~--> ~~~ * If AJP connector is required and cannot be commented/deactivated, then we recommend to set a secret password for the AJP conduit- Only requests from workers with the same secret keyword will be accepted. At the EAP 5.2 side, edit ` /server/$PROFILE/deploy/jbossweb.sar/server.xml`: ~~~ ~~~ Note that `YOUR_AJP_SECRET` must be changed to a value that is highly secure and cannot be easily guessed. ### JBoss EAP 6.4 (JBossWeb 7.x) The AJP connector is enabled by default only in [`standalone-full-ha.xml`, `standalone-ha.xml` and `full-ha`, `ha` profiles in `domain.xml`](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/6.4/html-single/administration_and_configuration_guide/index#sect-Configuration_Files). AJP connector can be secured as follows: * In JBoss EAP 6.4 Update 23+ or after applying the One off Patch to EAP 6.4 Update 22, the vulnerability is fixed and custom AJP request attributes are blocked by default. If using custom AJP and request attributes, see [How to allow custom AJP request attributes after applying the CVE-2020-1938 AJP File Read/Inclusion Vulnerability fix in JBoss EAP 6.4 Update 23+ or with the Security Patch applied to top of Update 22](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4950971), as they will not be allowed by default after the CVE fix. * If you do not use AJP, you can disable the AJP port configuration in your `standalone-*.xml` and/or `domain.xml` file by setting `enabled="false"` as shown below or comment out the whole ` ` clause: ~~~ ~~~ * If AJP connector is a requirement and cannot be commented or deactivated, then, it is recommended to add credential to AJP connector by configuring the following system property. See also [this knowledge article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/372563) about adding system properties: ~~~ ~~~ Note that `YOUR_AJP_SECRET` must be changed to a value that is highly secure and cannot be easily guessed. ### JBoss EAP 7 (Undertow) The AJP connector is enabled by default only in [`standalone-full-ha.xml`, `standalone-ha.xml`](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.3.beta/html-single/configuration_guide/index#standalone_server_configuration_files) and [`full-ha`, `ha` profiles in `domain.xml`](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_jboss_enterprise_application_platform/7.3.beta/html-single/configuration_guide/index#managed_domain_configuration_files). AJP connector can be secured as follows: * In EAP 7.2.8+ / EAP 7.3.1+ (or after applying the One off Patch to EAP 7.2.7 / EAP 7.3.0), the vulnerability is fixed and custom AJP request attributes are blocked by default. If using custom AJP and request attributes, see [How to allow AJP request attributes after applying the CVE-2020-1745 AJP File Read/Inclusion Vulnerability fix in JBoss EAP 7.2 Update 8+](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4900931) as they will not be allowed by default after the CVE fix. * If you do not use AJP, you can disable the AJP port configuration in your `standalone-*.xml` and/or `domain.xml` file by setting `enabled="false"` as shown below or comment out the whole ` ` clause: ~~~ ~~~ **Important**: notice that `mod_cluster` uses AJP by default as a conduit. You need to configure `mod_cluster` to use HTTP or HTTPS instead of AJP before disabling the AJP connector. * If AJP connector is a requirement and cannot be commented or deactivated, configure the following configuration inside undertow subsystem to check secure request attribute on AJP request.......... response-code(403)"/> The above configuration can be added by the following two command in JBoss-CLI[^1]: ~~~ /subsystem=undertow/configuration=filter/expression-filter=secret-checker:add(expression="not equals(%{r,secret}, 'YOUR_AJP_SECRET')-> response-code(403)") /subsystem=undertow/server=default-server/host=default-host/filter-ref=secret-checker:add(predicate="equals(%p,8009)") ~~~ Note that `YOUR_AJP_SECRET` must be changed to a value that is highly secure and cannot be easily guessed. If the above configuration is not possible, then consider binding AJP port to the loopback interface, or having a firewall that only allows access from trusted hosts would considerably reduce the attack surface to local, or trusted users. #### Note: If one has custom AJP attributes, then one needs to configure them to allow them after the CVE-2020-1745 fix and the [solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4900931) explains how to do so.--- ### Apache httpd (httpd in JBCS or RHEL) When the above "secret" setting is configured on Tomcat/JBoss side, the same secret value (`YOUR_AJP_SECRET` in the above example) will be required to be configured on the front-end proxy (mod_proxy_ajp or mod_jk). `httpd` in Red Hat Software Collections (RHSCL) does not support the `secret` parameter. In this case we recommend using HTTP or HTTPS and disabling AJP in Tomcat as shown above. #### mod_proxy (mod_proxy_ajp / mod_proxy_balancer using ajp) * The `secret` property is supported since the following versions: JBCS httpd 2.4.37; RHEL 7 httpd-2.4.6-67[^2]; RHEL 8 httpd-2.4.6-62. * For [`mod_proxy_ajp`](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/en/mod/mod_proxy_ajp.html), the `secret` property can be added to `ProxyPass` setting. * For [`mod_proxy_balancer`](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/en/mod/mod_proxy_balancer.html), the `secret` property can be added to each `BalancerMember` setting. * For example, add `secret=YOUR_AJP_SECRET` in your configuration (e.g. ` /conf/httpd.conf` or ` /conf.d/proxy_ajp.conf`) like the following: * `mod_proxy_ajp`: ~~~ ProxyPass /example/ ajp://localhost:8009/example/ secret=YOUR_AJP_SECRET ~~~ * `mod_proxy_balancer`: ~~~ BalancerMember ajp://node1:8009 route=node1 secret=YOUR_AJP_SECRET BalancerMember ajp://node2:8009 route=node2 secret=YOUR_AJP_SECRET ProxyPass /example/ balancer://mycluster/example/ stickysession=JSESSIONID|jsessionid ~~~ #### mod_jk * [`mod_jk`](https://tomcat.apache.org/connectors-doc/reference/workers.html)- `secret` can be specified to a worker or a load balancer in `workers.properties`. If you set a secret on a load balancer, all its members will inherit this secret. This `secret` property support was added in mod_jk 1.2.12 onwards. * For example, add the following in your `workers.properties`: ~~~ worker..secret=YOUR_AJP_SECRET ~~~ Ensure that WORKER_NAME must be replaced with the appropriate name. #### mod_cluster- `mod_cluster` does not support the`secret` property [^3] in JBCS httpd 2.4.37 SP1 or earlier. With JBCS httpd 2.4.37 SP2 (and later), you can set the `AJPsecret` directive in your httpd mod_cluster config to match your AJP connector secret. Note that the `AJPsecret` directive must be set globally outside the `VirtualHost` tags/section.- If mod_cluster is required with earlier versions, you need to change your configuration to use `http` or `https` instead of `ajp` because you can not connect without a correct secret value when `secret` is configured on the AJP connector in Tomcat/JBoss side.--- ### Tomcat on RHEL * Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 makes Tomcat available in the `pki-deps` module. This module is only intended for use to support the Dogtag Certificate System as shipped in the `pki-core` module, and not for hosting custom or third-party applications. In this configuration, Tomcat is only available locally and therefore remote attacks are not considered possible. As a result, the severity is Moderate. * Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 and 6 are affected. Please follow the CVE page for further updates. * Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 is in the [Extended Life Phase](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/errata) of the Support and Maintenance Life Cycle. As this vulnerability is rated Moderate, it is not in support scope for Extended Life Phase, and no updates are planned to be released for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5. The Mitigation strategies described above should be used. * Red Hat Software Collections are not affected. The binary RPMs produced from the `rh-java-common-tomcat` source RPM do not contain the Apache Coyote code which is affected by this vulnerability unless it is manually recompiled. A future update may fix the code. * Red Hat Satellite 6 makes use of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7's tomcat. Satellite versions 6.5 and older enable AJP. Users of these versions should install RHSA-2020:0855 to get the fixed version of the tomcat component.--- ### Spring Boot with Embedded Tomcat If we have a Spring boot application with an embedded Tomcat we need to define a bean that handle the embedded application container creation. This bean must make a connector using AJP to connect Apache to Tomcat. We can define this in a @Configuration annotated class as follows: ~~~ @Configuration public class TomcatConfig {@Bean public TomcatServletWebServerFactory servletContainer() {TomcatServletWebServerFactory tomcat = new TomcatServletWebServerFactory(); Connector ajpConnector = new Connector("org.apache.coyote.ajp.AjpNioProtocol"); AjpNioProtocol protocol= (AjpNioProtocol)ajpConnector.getProtocolHandler(); protocol.setSecret("myapjsecret"); ajpConnector.setPort(9090); ajpConnector.setSecure(true); tomcat.addAdditionalTomcatConnectors(ajpConnector); return tomcat;}} ~~~ Restart the app and you should see messages that Tomcat is now listening on both port 8080 and 9090. ~~~ [restartedMain] org.apache.coyote.ajp.AjpNioProtocol: Initializing ProtocolHandler ["ajp-nio-127.0.0.1-9090"] [restartedMain] org.apache.coyote.ajp.AjpNioProtocol: Starting ProtocolHandler ["ajp-nio-127.0.0.1-9090"] ~~~--- For further updates please follow up on [CVE-2020-1938](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2020-1938) and [CVE-2020-1745](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2020-1745) pages. [^1]: [How to connect JBoss EAP 7 to JBoss EAP 6 through CLI or vice versa?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3113731) [^2]: [BZ1397241 – Backport Apache Bug 53098- mod_proxy_ajp: patch to set worker secret passed to tomcat](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1397241) [^3]: [mod_cluster Documentation- Migration from mod_jk](https://docs.modcluster.io/#migration-from-modjk)
root_cause: This vulnerability leverages a AJP protocol functionality to get access to files at the server side and it is not a code failure. The AJP protocol, if used, must be properly isolated with proper firewall rules and secret keys to accept only valid content.

title: High repository load caused by frequent graph builds in openshift
issue: The graph builder component of the OpenShift Update Service (cincinnati-operator) executes at a fixed 5-minute interval, leading to increased connection requests and load on disconnected registries (e.g., Artifactory).
Pod logs consistently show graph update trigger events occurring at 5-minute intervals.
There is no supported configuration to modify the update interval, and any attempt to scale the deployment to zero replicas is automatically reconciled by the operator.
resolution: * There is no configurable parameter in the UpdateService CR to modify the graph update interval. Additionally, scaling replicas to zero is not supported, as the operator continuously reconciles and restores the desired state. * To reduce load on the container registry, the recommended workaround is to remove the UpdateService when it is not required for cluster upgrades. Workaround Steps: * Take a backup of the existing UpdateService Custom Resource configuration: ~~~ $ oc get updateservice-n openshift-update-service-o yaml > updateservice-backup.yaml ~~~ * Delete the UpdateService Custom Resource to halt the constant polling: ~~~ $ oc delete-f updateservice-backup.yaml ~~~ * When disconnected upgrades are needed again in the future, restore the service by reapplying the backed-up YAML configuration: ~~~ $ oc apply-f updateservice-backup.yaml ~~~
root_cause: * The 5-minute (300s) polling interval is hardcoded in the graph builder binary and is not exposed via the UpdateService CR, so it cannot be modified. * The operator enforces the desired state, automatically reverting any manual scaling changes, which results in continuous registry polling.

title: After rebooting an EDPM node, chony makes source servers offline.
product: Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift
issue: - After rebooting an EDPM node, chony makes source servers offline.
resolution: - Disable dispatcher script in NetworkManager. ~~~ # ln-f-s /dev/null /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/20-chrony-onoffline ~~~- This command should be added to `edpm_bootstrap_command` option in OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet CR for greenfield deployment.- For existing deployments, add the command to `edpm_bootstrap_command` option then define and run a new OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment CR.(Please note that the name of the CR and nodeSets name should be updated along with your deployments.) ~~~ apiVersion: dataplane.openstack.org/v1beta1 kind: OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment metadata: name:- example namespace: openstackode spec: nodeSets:- openstack-edpm servicesOverride:- bootstrap ~~~
root_cause: The NetworkManager executes the chrony dispatcher script during interface reconfiguration, stop or start operations. However, if you configure certain interfaces or routes outside of NetworkManager, you can encounter the following situation: 1. The dispatcher script might run when no route to the NTP servers exists, causing the NTP servers to switch to the offline state. 2. If you establish the route later, the script does not run again by default, and the NTP servers remain in the offline state. This is written at [11.3.4. Disabling a chrony dispatcher script](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html/configuring_basic_system_settings/configuring-time-synchronization_configuring-basic-system-settings#proc_disabling-a-chrony-dispatcher-script_using-chrony).

title: GPUOperatorNodeDeploymentFailed alert after enabling Dynamic Accelerator Slicer in OpenShift Container Platform
issue: - The GPUOperatorNodeDeploymentFailed alert fires a false positive when the device plugin is intentionally disabled in the ClusterPolicy `(spec.devicePlugin.enabled: false)`.
root_cause: - The customer disabled the device plugin in the GPU Operator ClusterPolicy (`devicePlugin.enabled: false`), as required when using DAS for MIG-based GPU partitioning. The `nvidia-node-status-exporter` continues to monitor `gpu_operator_node_device_plugin_devices_total`, which correctly reports 0 (since the device plugin is not running). This triggers the `GPUOperatorNodeDeploymentFailed` alert — a false positive because the device plugin is intentionally disabled.- A jira[OCPBUGS-66079](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-66079) was raised internallay with engineering team.- We confirmed this is not a DAS/Instaslice-operator issue. DAS requires MIG to be enabled as a prerequisite but has no control over the GPU Operator's alerting or device plugin metrics. The false positive is entirely within the NVIDIA GPU Operator — the nodeStatusExporter does not check whether devicePlugin.enabled is set to false before firing the alert. An upstream issue [2237](https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator/issues/2237) is raised with NVDIA/gpu-operator for the alert to be suppressed when devicePlugin.enabled: false in the ClusterPolicy.- Customer should follow up directly with NVIDIA for tracking and resolution, as the GPU Operator is not provided or supported by Red Hat. ## Workaround Interim workaround is to [silence the alert via OCP monitoring](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/monitoring/managing-alerts).

title: OpenShift Virtualization CNV Stuck Upgrade to 2.5.3
issue: The status of the ClusterServiceVersion kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator reaches phase `Installing`, but does not proceed any further.
resolution: Permanent resolution being tracked in the following bugzilla:- [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1909975](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1909975) ### Workaround If the upgrade is currently stuck, the operator may do the following steps to help it through. The following actions will not impact current workloads (will not restart the VMIs or impact their networking) and the operator will recreate the objects automatically. 1. Backup the templates for safety (and if the issue persists attach to case) ~~~ oc get KubevirtCommonTemplatesBundle-n openshift common-templates-kubevirt-hyperconverged-o yaml > KubevirtCommonTemplatesBundle.yaml oc get CDI cdi-kubevirt-hyperconverged-o yaml > CDI.yaml ~~~ 2. Proceed with the first object deletion ~~~ oc delete CDI cdi-kubevirt-hyperconverged ~~~ 3. Wait for the operator to have recreated the resource The following command will show the current status: ~~~ oc get apiservices v1beta1.upload.cdi.kubevirt.io-o yaml ~~~ The successful output status should be like the following: ~~~ status: conditions:- lastTransitionTime: "2021-03-21T17:48:21Z" message: all checks passed reason: Passed status: "True" type: Available ~~~ 4. Final deletion step ~~~ oc delete KubevirtCommonTemplatesBundle-n openshift common-templates-kubevirt-hyperconverged ~~~ Once these steps are executed the upgrade should progress anew. If this is not the case, please attach a new cnv specific must-gather report.- [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/virt/logging_events_monitoring/virt-collecting-virt-data.html](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/latest/virt/logging_events_monitoring/virt-collecting-virt-data.html)
root_cause: The root cause as to why the endpoint is missing during the upgrade process is still being determined in the [bugzilla](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1909975).

title: Machines are stuck in the provisioned state due to SNAT port exhaustion in ARO
issue: - Failed to scale up machinesets in ARO.- Machines are stuck in the provisioned state in ARO with the message `SpecifiedAllocatedOutboundPortsForOutboundRuleExceedsTotalNumberOfAvailablePorts`.- Nodes are not able to join the cluster due to SNAT port exhaustion in ARO
resolution: - Update the number of managed IPs on the public load balancer per the [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-multiple-ips#update-the-number-of-ip-addresses-on-existing-clusters). ~~~ $ az aro update--resource-group aroResourceGroup--name aroCluster--load-balancer-managed-outbound-ip-count 4 ~~~- The above procedure is harmless and will not result in node reboots or pod restarts.
root_cause: - Azure Red Hat OpenShift public clusters are created with a public load balancer that's used for outbound connectivity from inside the cluster.- By default, one public IP address is configured on that public load balancer, and that limits the maximum node count of your cluster to 62.- To be able to scale your cluster to the maximum supported number of 250 nodes, you need to assign multiple additional public IP addresses to the load balancer.

title: KubeletConfig updates not being applied to Hosted Control Plane NodePools in RHOCP 4
issue: Updates to a KubeletConfig ConfigMap in a Hosted Control Plane (HCP) NodePool do not progress to the nodes, and the NodePool status reports a `failed to generate payload` error due to an out-of-date machine-config-server ConfigMap.
resolution: * Identify the custom API server configuration in the `HostedCluster` custom resource (CR). * Remove the conflicting custom serving certificate configuration using the following command: ~~~ $ oc patch hostedcluster-n--type json-p='[{"op":"remove", "path":"/spec/configuration/apiServer/servingCerts"}]' ~~~ * Verify that the API server pods in the hosted cluster control plane namespace (e.g., `- `) restart automatically. * Confirm that the nodes are drained and restarted, allowing the new machine-config payload to be applied successfully.
root_cause: The `HostedCluster` configuration contained an invalid custom serving certificate for the API server. The custom DNS names added to the certificate `Subject Alternative Names (SANs)` conflicted with the default internal Kubernetes API server SANs. This invalid configuration prevented the `machine-config-server` from successfully generating new Ignition payloads, causing the NodePool update process to stall.

title: Unexpected ListAndWatch error: failed to list operator: service operator not found; reinitializing in RHOCP4
issue: - The `kube-apiserver` logs are being spammed with errors indicating it cannot resolve the service for some operators `CRD's` conversion `webhook`. ~~~ $ oc logs kube-apiserver-node-n openshift-kube-apiserver-c kube-apiserver | tail-n1 cacher (tenants.minio.min.io): unexpected ListAndWatch error: failed to list minio.min.io/v1, Kind=Tenant: conversion webhook for minio.min.io/v2, Kind=Tenant failed: Post "https://operator.minio-operator.svc:4222/webhook/v1/crd-conversion?timeout=30s": service "operator" not found; reinitializing... ~~~
resolution: - If the `operator` is no longer used that is logging error then take `backup` and [`remove the Leftover Resources`](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6762071) such as **CRDs, Roles, RoleBindings, ServiceAccounts etc**
root_cause: - Operator being in a `faulty state` (e.g., not running, service misconfigured) or `completely absent` from the cluster.- The immediate impact is a `high volume of error` logs from the `kube-apiserver`, which can obscure other issues and potentially impact performance.

title: Allow to use insecure or skip tls for datavolume in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - Needs to use a self-signed certificate for the Red Hat Satellite HTTPS endpoint in the `dataVolumeTemplates` HTTP source configuration in order to download the RHEL ISO image.- Allow to use `insecure` or `skip tls` for `datavolume` in OpenShift Virtualization.
resolution: Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in [RFE](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNV-81049). If this feature is required, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: OpenShift Versions dropdown is greyed out in a connected cluster while creating host inventory in ACM.
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - When creating a new infrastructure environment, the OpenShift Versions dropdown is blank.- Error when host inventory is created with OpenShift version greyed out: ~~~ Failing infrastructure environment Failed to create image No OS image for Openshift version 4.18 and architecture x86_64 The requested OS image for version (4.18) and CPU architecture (x86_64) isn't specified in OS images list ~~~
resolution: 1. Add the `osImages` spec in the `agentserviceconfig` custom resource as follows: ~~~ oc edit agentserviceconfig agent osImages:- cpuArchitecture: x86_64 openshiftVersion: '4.17' url: 'https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/dependencies/rhcos/4.17/4.17.42/rhcos-4.17.42-x86_64-live.x86_64.iso' version: 417.94.202507291008-0- cpuArchitecture: x86_64 openshiftVersion: '4.18' url: 'https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/dependencies/rhcos/4.18/4.18.30/rhcos-4.18.30-x86_64-live.x86_64.iso' version: 418.94.202511191518-0- cpuArchitecture: x86_64 openshiftVersion: '4.19' url: 'https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/dependencies/rhcos/4.19/4.19.23/rhcos-4.19.23-x86_64-live-iso.x86_64.iso' version: 9.6.20260112-0- cpuArchitecture: x86_64 openshiftVersion: '4.20' url: 'https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/dependencies/rhcos/4.20/4.20.13/rhcos-4.20.13-x86_64-live-iso.x86_64.iso' version: 9.6.20260112-0 ~~~ 2. After this, the assisted-service and assisted-image-service will restart, and the OpenShift Versions dropdown will show the option to select OCP versions in the host inventory as well as in the cluster creation UI. 3. If the `clusterimagesets` are not available for the mentioned OCP versions, then create them using the following: apiVersion: hive.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterImageSet metadata: name: img4.17.42-x86-64-appsub spec: releaseImage: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.17.42-x86_64--- apiVersion: hive.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterImageSet metadata: name: img4.18.30-x86-64-appsub spec: releaseImage: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.18.30-x86_64--- apiVersion: hive.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterImageSet metadata: name: img4.19.23-x86-64-appsub spec: releaseImage: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.19.23-x86_64--- apiVersion: hive.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterImageSet metadata: name: img4.20.13-x86-64-appsub spec: releaseImage: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.20.13-x86_64
root_cause: - The UI relies on two distinct configurations being present and correctly formatted: the `ClusterImageSet` and the `osImages` defined in the AgentServiceConfig.- The discovery ISO and release image requirements were not satisfied, which was stopping the UI to successfully populate the OpenShift version dropdown.
