title: Networking conflict with docker0 interface
issue: - User with client IPs (eg 172.17.12x.y) can not access the Openshift GUI since the docker0 interface is using random addresses from the range 172.17.0.0/16.- I thought the docker0 interface is not used anymore by OpenShift from version 3.1 on. Can we disable it?
resolution: Change the docker network CIDR to fix the network address conflict issue.- During installation[1] ~~~ openshift_docker_options="--log-driver=journald--bip 10.17.0.1/16" ~~~ or- Editing docker.json or /etc/sysconfig/docker and add ~~~ OPTIONS='--selinux-enabled--log-driver=journald--bip 10.17.0.1/16' ~~~ Do not disable docker network, it's used within Dockerfile build (Docker build strategy) for outgoing communication. [1][Configuring Cluster Variables](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/3.9/html/installation_and_configuration/installing-a-cluster#configuring-cluster-variables)

title: ODF: Recurring "Network Partitions Detected" Warnings in Stretch Clusters
issue: - The ODF cluster intermittently reports HEALTH_WARN with the message MON_NETSPLIT: X network partitions detected. This occurs repeatedly even when standard networking tools (ping, nc) show no connectivity issues between nodes Key Observations:- Intermittent Nature: The warning often clears after restarting Monitor pods or switching the election strategy to classic, but reappears within minutes when returned to the required connectivity strategy.- Clock Skew Symptoms: The cluster may also report clock skew warnings (MON_CLOCK_SKEW), which are often a symptom of network latency delaying monitor messages rather than actual system clock drift.
resolution: 1. Identify the Broken Communication Link Run the connection scores dump on the current leader (often mon.a or mon.f) to identify which specific monitors cannot communicate: ~~~ export NAMESPACE=openshift-storage # Identify the leader pod first, then run: oc exec-n $NAMESPACE-c mon-- ceph daemon mon. connection scores dump ~~~ Look for peer_score: 0 and peer_alive: false in the JSON output to pinpoint the problematic nodes. 2. Check for Underlying Hardware or OVN Issues- Check Node Stability: Investigate the node kernel logs (dmesg) for I/O errors or disk instability (e.g., "no unique device id"), as a frozen storage process can prevent the Monitor from responding to network probes.- Restart OVN Pods: If networking is suspected, restart the OVN-Kubernetes pods on the affected nodes to clear stale flows. 3. Temporary Mitigation: If the cluster remains operational and the warnings are confirmed as false positives due to the bug, the warning can be muted persistently: ~~~ ceph health mute MON_NETSPLIT--sticky ~~~ Note: Suppressing the warning should only be done as a temporary measure while awaiting the official fix in an upcoming ODF/Ceph release.
root_cause: - Primary Cause: A bug in the Ceph messaging layer protocol related to how reconnection is handled after the net split detection feature was implemented.- We have the jira [DFBUGS-5890](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/DFBUGS-5890) opened for this issue.

title: Error message "metadata.annotations: Too long: must have at most 262144" when restoring Automation Controller Backup
issue: - Ansible Automation Controller Restore fails with the following error message: ``` Secret \\\\\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\\\\\" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: must have at most 262144 ```
resolution: - Secret needs to be removed from the Backup following these steps: ``` Create a file pod-with-pvc.yml: apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: my-pod-with-pvc spec: containers:- name: my-container image: registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi:latest # Using Red Hat UBI as an example command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"] # Just keeping the pod alive for testing volumeMounts:- mountPath: "/mnt/data" # This is where the PVC appears inside the container name: my-storage-vol volumes:- name: my-storage-vol persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: Create a pod: oc apply-f pod-with-pvc.yml Exec to pod: oc exec-it my-pod-with-pvc-- bash Edit secret: cd /mnt/data/ / vi secrets.yaml ```
root_cause: - If the secret is not removed fully ahead of the Restore, it exists twice in the Restore, causing it to exceed the size limit.

title: How to retain the same Ansible Automation Platform URL during backup and restore on OpenShift Container Platform?
issue: - Why is the original route_host not retained after restoring AAP from a PVC backup?- What causes the AAP route to change to the default-.apps... value during restore?- Is this expected behavior when performing an AAP restore on OpenShift?- How can the original AAP URL be preserved during the restore process?- What steps are required to ensure the restored AAP instance uses the same route as before backup?- Why does the restored environment not reflect the previously configured route settings?
resolution: - Use the `route_host` option to retain the same URL when restoring an Ansible Automation Platform backup. ~~~ spec_overrides: route_host: myaap2.ansible.com ~~~ ~~~ $oc get crd ansibleautomationplatformrestores.aap.ansible.com-o yaml spec_overrides: description: Overrides to apply to the restored AnsibleAutomationPlatform spec. This allows you to modify specific fields from the backup, such as storage classes, postgres configuration secrets, resource requirements, or other deployment settings. properties:.. route_host: description: Override the route host type: string ~~~ ~~~ Example: apiVersion: aap.ansible.com/v1alpha1 kind: AnsibleAutomationPlatformRestore metadata: name: aap-202603240106 namespace: aapprod spec: deployment_name: aap backup_source: PVC backup_pvc: aap-backup-claim backup_dir: '/backups/aap-openshift-backup-2026-03-24-00:15:01' spec_overrides: route_host: myaap2.ansible.com ~~~

title: Is it possible to migrate an OpenShift 4 cluster running on one vCenter to another?
issue: - Is cross vCenter migration supported for OpenShift clusters?- Can two vCenters running OpenShift workloads be merged?- Can we redeploy the vCenter with the OpenShift cluster untouched?
resolution: - No, it is not a supported approach to migrate OCP clusters running workload among different vCenters.- It is always suggested to set up a new cluster and migrate the workload.- This is also true when redeploying the vCenter. Regarding support for vCenter replacement, there is an [RFE-3983](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-3983), but it has not been implemented at the moment.
root_cause: - Core Kubernetes relies on the UUID of VMs being stable. It uses this to match Node objects to virtual machines.- If at any point it cannot find the VM that matches a Node, it considers it to have been removed on the infrastructure side and deletes the Node object from the cluster.- By moving the VM from one vCenter to another, this will cause the Kube Controller Manager's Node controller to observe the VM as missing, and it will delete the Node.- We also have questions about the UUIDs of VMs when they are transferred between vCenters. If these change during this process, this will add further confusion to the situation.- The Machine API controllers have several paths that will lead to the Machine entering a Failed state.- If a Machine enters a Failed state, this is considered terminal, and we no longer reconcile the Machine. **Scenarios that might cause a VM to go Failed:**- The Machine's Node has been removed from the cluster- The VM has been removed on the cloud provider side **If a VM is moved from one vCenter to another, either of the above scenarios could be caught by the Machine controller, causing the Machines to enter a Failed state.**- Based on the above, given that the Kubernetes Controller Manager and Machine API controllers are typically only configured to talk to one vCenter at any one time, it is impossible for them to track the VMs as they are moved between two vCenters. It appears to these controllers like the VMs have been deleted, and as such, it causes these terminal side effects within the cluster.

title: Cannot migrate Openshift Virtualization VM between worker nodes with different CPU type
issue: When trying to migrate VM's between worker nodes with different CPU types, I get the following error: ~~~ Migration cannot proceed since no node is suitable to run the required CPU model ~~~
VM may be using `host-model` CPU type
resolution: * The cpu-model.node.kubevirt.io is what CPU models natively supported by the node during scheduling of the VM. * The cpu-model-migration.node.kubevirt.io are what CPU models are supported during migration of the VM. * Check to see what CPU model (cpu-model.node.kubevirt.io) are supported on all worker nodes: ~~~ oc get nodes-o yaml-l node-role.kubernetes.io/worker= |grep 'cpu-model.node.kubevirt.io' |sort |uniq-c ~~~ * Set the [defaultCPUModel](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.21/html/virtualization/managing-vms#virt-configuring-default-cpu-model) to the latest common CPU model matching to all nodes. * NOTE: Changing the `defaultCPUModel` will require a restart of the Virtual Machines to take effect. * Also setting the `defaultCPUModel` to a CPU model that **doesn't exist** in the cpu-model.node.kubevirt.io but **exists** in cpu-model-migration.node.kubevirt.io, it may result in VM not able to start/schedule.
root_cause: VM's cannot live migrate to a worker node if they do not have the CPU capability for which the VM is running.

title: Can Red Hat provide optimal MaxRAMPercentage or related flags for SpringBoot or Java applications
product: Red Hat support for Spring Boot
issue: - Can Red Hat provide optimal `MaxRAMPercentage` or related flags?- Can Red Hat provide optimal `MaxRAMPercentage`?- Does increasing `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage` gives the application more space?
resolution: No. Red Hat cannot provide the optimal value for heap percentage or off-heap for SpringBoot or Java applications given the fact those are custom applications, i.e. Red Hat does not have the application's source. The main recommendation is for the DevOps Team of the application to benchmark it directly with workload for optimal configurations. Similar to other JVM flags- like GC collector- Red Hat cannot know the optimal values for the `MaxRAMPercentage` of the application, since Red Hat does not have access to its source code. If the current `MaxRAMPercentage` is inadequate (too small for heap, or too large for off-heap) so then it is recommended benchmarking for the optimal value. Note that if keeping the container on at the same size, and increase the heap percentage, so then the off-heap percentage is naturally being reduced. Red Hat recommends therefore keep the same ratio and just increase the container size, which will lead to a natural heap increase (as long as Java container awareness is used, which is available in recent Red Hat OpenJDK images).
root_cause: The increase of `MaxRAMPercentage` value does not give an application more space directly. It does however, this gives heap more space, by reducing off-heap space directly (a trade-off). This type of tuning won't necessarily matter for performance stats as long as the GC is not the cause of the latency or no OOMException is being triggered.- When using a Red Hat build of OpenJDK- without `run-java.sh` as start up- the application can will use `25%` of the container as heap max limit (`MaxRAMPercentage` = `25%`), which is the default upstream.- When using a Red Hat build of OpenJDK- with `run-java.sh` as start up- the application can will use `80%` of the container as heap max limit (`MaxRAMPercentage` = `80%`). The default `ENTRYPOINT` for Red Hat build of OpenJDK images is using `run-java.sh`, which sets at `80%`- that is an specific optimization with Red Hat's build (the `run-java.sh` script). If they are not using `80%`/`50%` they are using a custom ratio, so the recommendation is just to increase the container size, because the heap will increase accordingly.

title: How to control node parallel updates in OpenShift 4
issue: Is there a way to control Node updates in OCP 4?
Is it possible to set the `maxUnavailable` node in OpenShift 4 to `0` and wait until having approval, and then set this to `1`? Would that work?
Is it possible to continue upgrading other nodes in the cluster, if one node cannot be drained?
resolution: Is it possible to control the upgrade of nodes in different ways. #### Custom Machine Config Pools It is possible to configure custom Machine Config Pools for compute nodes with different subsets of compute nodes to allow several nodes to be updated at the same time. Unless a MCP is paused (explained below), nodes from different MCPs will be upgraded in parallel. Please refer to [managing custom Machine Config Pool in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5688941) for configuring custom MCPs. #### Maximum number of unavailable nodes per Machine Config Pool The MCPs also has a functionality to control the amount of nodes that can be taken offline at a given time within the same `MachineConfigPool`, the `maxUnavailable` field: * By default this field is set to `1`, meaning only one node per `MachineConfigPool` can be unavailable. * It is not possible to set `maxUnavailable` to `0` for stopping updates (it will default back to `1`). * A value larger than `1` will mean **multiple** nodes going **unavailable** during the update, which **may affect** the workload stress on the remaining nodes. The rest of the available nodes needs to be able to **manage all the load** and all the pods to avoid additional issues due to lack of nodes/resources during upgrades. To change `maxUnavailable` in any given `MachineConfigPool`, execute the `oc patch` command as shown below: ~~~ $ oc patch--type merge machineconfigpool/-p '{"spec":{"maxUnavailable":}}' ~~~ > **IMPORTANT NOTE:** the `maxUnavailable` should **never** be changed for the **control plane nodes** (the `master` MCP), as changing it from the default `1` could cause all the control plane nodes to got stuck as explained in [all master nodes are `SchedulingDisabled` and `maxUnavailable` configured to more than `1` in the `master` MachineConfigPool in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7051674). #### Pausing Machine Config Pools Since `maxUnavailable` is primarily meant to specify the percentage or constant number of nodes that can be updating at any given time, there is additional functionality available to prevent a `MachineConfigPool` from being updated: in `MachineConfigPool`, `paused` can be set to either `true` or `false`. If set to `true`, changes to this `MachineConfigPool` should be stopped. This includes generating new `desiredMachineConfig` and update of node part of that `MachineConfigPool`. To set `paused` to either `false` or `true` in a specific `MachineConfigPool` use the below procedure: ~~~ $ oc patch--type merge machineconfigpool/-p '{"spec":{"paused":}}' ~~~ > **Important:** if the `spec.paused` field is not restored to `false`, or the `spec.maxUnavailable` set to a value greater than `0`, the nodes will not be rebooted by configuration changes in the cluster like certificates renewal, and it can cause that the cluster may not work if the old certificates expire. Refer to [disable autoreboot when the certificates of kube-apiserver-to-kubelet-signer will be rotated at around the 80 percent of that one year](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5484051) for additional information. Related to the node upgrades, there is a RFE to add the ability to [continue with nodes upgrade if a node cannot be drained](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-1489).
root_cause: It is possible to control node update behavior with one or several `MachineConfigPools`, the `maxUnavailable` field, and the `paused` field. Refer to the [performing a canary rollout update](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/updating_clusters/performing-a-cluster-update#update-using-custom-machine-config-pools) documentation for additional information.

title: Migrate ARO Container Runtime from runc to crun
issue: In OpenShift 4.18, `crun` became the default container runtime for new installations. However, for stability reasons, clusters upgraded from 4.17 to 4.18 (or higher) are automatically pinned to the older `runc` runtime via two system-generated MachineConfigs:
`00-override-master-generated-crio-default-container-runtime`
`00-override-worker-generated-crio-default-container-runtime` Previously, ARO customers were restricted from modifying these system-level configs, preventing the transition to `crun`.
resolution: **Migration from `runc` to `crun` is now fully supported for ARO clusters.** This support applies to both **public** and **private** ARO cluster configurations. If your cluster is updated from OpenShift Container Platform 4.17, you can migrate to the crun container runtime by deleting the `00-override-worker-generated-crio-default-container-runtime` and `00-override-master-generated-crio-default-container-runtime` MachineConfig objects. See the documentation [Configuring the container runtime](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.21/html/machine_configuration/machine-configs-custom#config-container-runtime_machine-configs-custom) for details.
root_cause: To prevent breaking changes during a major version upgrade, the Machine Config Operator (MCO) generates "override" configs to maintain the existing runtime (`runc`). While these were previously locked in managed environments to prevent reconciliation loops, ARO SRE and Engineering have validated the path for customers to safely delete these overrides.

title: 'kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes' and  'kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes' metrics  is not visible on  web-console in RHOCP 4 .
issue: - Unable to view `kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes ` and `kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes` metrics from web-console.- PV and PVC usage metrics
resolution: - Starting with OpenShift Container Platform 4.3, the `kubelet` does extract this information from the respective CSI driver and exposes it accordingly.- These metrics is expected to be exposed by CSI drivers so that Prometheus can collect it.- If using `CSI driver`, make sure that it is being used the official Red Hat as documented in- [Using Container Storage Interface (CSI)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/storage/using-container-storage-interface-csi#persistent-storage-csi-drivers-supported_persistent-storage-csi.html).- If a `third-party` `CSI driver` is being used, the availability of these Prometheus metrics must be verified with the vendor, as they are responsible for exposing them.

title: When an OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment CR is defined, download-cache pods are failed status in disconnected installation
issue: - When an OpenStackDataPlaneDeployment CR is defined, download-cache pods are failed status in disconnected installation- To identify the issue, run `podman--log-level=debug pull registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-ovn-controller-rhel9@sha256:6c7827dbe25c168d28250f197d5ea6f3f60cfbab4c974267ec5ea0f8d631c3f5` on EDPM node then the debug log contains the following error. ~~~ DEBU[0000] Error pulling candidate registry.redhat.io/rhoso/openstack-ovn-controller-rhel9@sha256:6c7827dbe25c168d28250f197d5ea6f3f60cfbab4c974267ec5ea0f8d631c3f5: copying system image from manifest list: Source image rejected: A signature was required, but no signature exists Error: copying system image from manifest list: Source image rejected: A signature was required, but no signature exists ~~~
resolution: - Current workaround is modifying `/etc/containers/policy.json` to make "registry.redhat.io" entry to accept insecure images. ~~~ {"default": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}], "transports": {"docker": {"registry.access.redhat.com": [{"type": "signedBy", "keyType": "GPGKeys", "keyPaths": ["/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-release", "/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-beta"]}], "registry.redhat.io": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}]}, "docker-daemon": {"": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}]}}} ~~~- The issue is being tracked at [OSPRH-28352](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OSPRH-28352)
root_cause: - oc-mirror v2 plugin mirrors the signatures from oc mirror v2 4.19+. But they are not verified in OCP4.18. However, EDPM nodes has the default /etc/containers/policy.json which tries to verify the signature. This default configuration causes the error.

title: How to update client secret in azure cloud credentials
issue: - Azure Service Principal has expired or is about to expire, and needs to be rotated.- Client secret expired presenting the following error: ~~~ Status Code = '401'. Response body: {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"AADSTS7000222: The provided client secret keys are expired. Visit the Azure Portal to create new keys for your app, or consider using certificate credentials for added security. ~~~
resolution: **Disclaimer**: *Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* **NOTE:** For Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), please follow the Microsoft [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-service-principal-credential-rotation) or refer to this [article](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6999617).- Client secrets are generally stored in the `azure-credentials` secret within the `kube-system` project in base64 encode. If the Client secret got expired or new secret needs to be updated, please follow the below procedure: 1. Take backup of the `azure-credentials` secret: ~~~ $ oc get secret azure-credentials-n kube-system-o yaml > azurebackup.yaml ~~~ 2. Convert the new secret to base64 format: ~~~ $ echo-n " " | base64-i ~~~ 3. Copy the base64 encoded value and update the same in the `azure-credentials`: ~~~ $ oc edit secret azure-credentials-n kube-system... data: azure_client_id: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX azure_client_secret: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX azure_region: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX azure_resource_prefix: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX azure_resourcegroup: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX azure_subscription_id: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX azure_tenant_id: XXXXXXXXXXXXXX ~~~ 4. Save and exit the file.
root_cause: - Whenever the Client secret got rotated as per organization policy, it also needs to be updated in OpenShift, otherwise it will misbehave as OpenShift will not be able to communicate with Azure.

title: Web Console should allow direct CPU and Memory editing for MTV-migrated VMs without InstanceTypes in OpenShift Virtualization
issue: - `CPU` and `memory` cannot be edited from the OpenShift `Web Console` for virtual machines `migrated` using `MTV` when `no InstanceType` is configured.
resolution: - This behavior is a `user interface limitation`. Virtual machines migrated using `MTV` define `CPU` and `memory` directly in the VirtualMachine specification, but the OpenShift `Web Console` assumes `InstanceType-based` management and does not expose editable CPU and memory fields.- `CPU` and `memory` can be modified using supported YAML/API workflows.- Edit the VirtualMachine resource directly: ~~~ $ oc edit vm-n ~~~- Update `CPU configuration`: ~~~ spec: template: spec: domain: cpu: cores: 4 sockets: 1 threads: 1 ~~~- Update `memory configuration`: ~~~ spec: template: spec: domain: memory: guest: 8Gi ~~~- Apply the changes and verify: ~~~ $ oc get vm-n-o yaml | grep-A5 domain ~~~- Red Hat is aware of this `feature request`, currently under review in [CNV-75799](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNV-75799). If this feature is required, [open a new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/) with on the Red Hat Customer Portal.
root_cause: - Virtual machines migrated from `Red Hat Virtualization` using MTV are created as standalone VirtualMachine objects without `InstanceType` references.- The OpenShift `Web Console` currently assumes `InstanceType-based` configuration and `hides direct CPU and memory` fields even when the VirtualMachine defines resources explicitly in the spec.

title: How to override default node IP selection logic for secondary interfaces on HCP nodes in RHOCP 4
issue: Adding a default route with a lower metric to a secondary interface on Hosted Control Plane (HCP) nodes causes cluster disruption after a reboot because the default node IP selection logic incorrectly selects the secondary interface IP as the primary.
resolution: - To allow egress traffic through a secondary interface while ensuring the original primary node IP remains stable across reboots, follow these steps:- Validate if a static route is already configured for the secondary interface. ~~~ $ oc debug no/-- chroot /host ip route show ~~~- If the routes are not present, the required static route can be added using the Kubernetes NMState Operator as described in the [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/networking/k8s_nmstate/k8s-nmstate-updating-node-network-config).- Create a `ConfigMap` in the management cluster (under the `clusters` namespace) to deploy a `MachineConfig` that explicitly defines the correct primary node IP address.- This `MachineConfig` must create the `/etc/default/nodeip-configuration` file to provide a "hint" to the kubelet, preventing it from switching to the secondary interface IP after a reboot.- Example configuration structure: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: node-ip-config namespace: clusters data: config: | apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 99-nodeip-hint-worker spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64, mode: 0644 overwrite: true path: /etc/default/nodeip-configuration ~~~
root_cause: * By default, the OpenShift IP selection logic follows the interface with the lowest metric default route. If a secondary interface is configured with a lower metric gateway to handle egress traffic, the node may attempt to use that secondary IP as its primary internal cluster IP after a reboot, leading to network inconsistency and cluster failure.

title: Alert ClusterMonitoringOperatorDeprecatedConfig is firing in ROSA.
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - The alert `ClusterMonitoringOperatorDeprecatedConfig` is firing after upgrading the ROSA cluster to the OpenShift version 4.16+.- The configuration field k8sPrometheusAdapter in openshift-monitoring/cluster-monitoring-config was deprecated in 4.16 and has no effect.
resolution: - Since Q1 2026 the Cluster Monitoring Operator can be configured by cluster admins as announced in the [release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/4/html-single/whats_new/index#rosa-q1-2026_rosa-whats-new).- Please follow the instructions in this [solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7076965).
root_cause: - The configuration field "k8sPrometheusAdapter" in cluster-monitoring-config has been deprecated since 4.16.- Starting RHOCP 4.16, a new metric `cluster_monitoring_operator_deprecated_config_in_use` is exposed to identify if any deprecated config is in use for the cluster monitoring operator. If any deprecated config is found to be in use for the cluster monitoring operator, then an alert `ClusterMonitoringOperatorDeprecatedConfig` will be triggered.

title: Dynatrace Reports 5MB Disk Path at 100% Utilization on OpenShift RHCOS Nodes
issue: - `Dynatrace` continuously `reports disk utilization alerts` on certain OpenShift nodes.
resolution: - The `~5MB filesystem` mounted on `/` is a `ComposeFS immutable root filesystem` and showing `100% usage` is expected behavior. This `filesystem` is not a writable disk and does not indicate `disk exhaustion`.- No remediation is required on the OpenShift cluster. Configure the monitoring tool to `ignore ComposeFS mounts`.- Recommended monitoring filter:- Ignore `filesystem` type `overlay`- Ignore `filesystem` type `composefs`- Alert only on `xfs or ext4` block devices
root_cause: - The `ComposeFS` root filesystem:- Is `immutable` by design- `Always` appears `100% full`- Does `not` store application data- Does `not grow` or consume node storage- Is part of `RHCOS` image layering

title: Is it supported to migrate VMs from AMD to Intel in RHOCP
issue: - `Kernel panic` after VM migrated from `AMD to Intel`
resolution: - `Live migration` across `heterogeneous CPU` vendors is `not supported`. The source and destination nodes must expose `compatible CPU vendor` and feature sets.- The node inventory shows a `mixture` of `AMD and Intel CPU models`: ~~~ $ oc get nodes-o yaml | grep-i host-model-cpu.node ~~~- This `limitation` applies to Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization and is consistent with other virtualization platforms. The behavior is tracked in [CNV-71957](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNV-71957).- Recommended supported approaches:- Use worker nodes with a `single CPU vendor`.- Group nodes into `CPU-homogeneous pools`.- Schedule virtual machines using `nodeSelector or nodeAffinity`.- Perform `live migration` only within `compatible CPU pools`.
root_cause: - In `heterogeneous` clusters with `Intel and AMD processors`, no common `CPU` baseline exists. During `live migration`, the destination node cannot satisfy the required `CPU` features, resulting in `migration failure`.

title: Switching container runtime to crun on clusters upgraded to 4.17 + in RHOCP4
issue: - With the update of a cluster to v4.17 two MachineConfig are generated to overrride the default crun to runc- Is deleting generated MachineConfig objects sufficient to switch the container runtime to crun on clusters upgraded from versions prior to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.17?
resolution: - `Deleting` the generated `MachineConfig` objects is `not supported`. The recommended and supported method is to use a `ContainerRuntimeConfig`, which generates a `higher-priority MachineConfig` that `overrides` the runtime to `crun`.- Create a `ContainerRuntimeConfig` to set the `default` runtime to `crun`: ~~~ cat <-- chroot /host cat /etc/crio/crio.conf.d/01-ctrcfg-defaultRuntime ~~~ Expected output: ~~~ [crio.runtime] default_runtime = "crun" ~~~
root_cause: - Clusters installed on versions `prior` to `4.17` defaulted to `runc`.- During upgrade to `4.17 and later`, the `Machine Config Operator` generates `override MachineConfigs` (prefix 00-) to preserve the existing runtime.- When a `ContainerRuntimeConfig` is applied:- A new `MachineConfig` with `prefix 99-` is generated.- `MachineConfig` ordering determines precedence.- The higher-priority `MachineConfig` overrides the default runtime to` crun`.

title: StatusCode=400 -- Original Error: Code="BadRequest" Message="The selected VM size 'Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4' cannot boot Hypervisor Generation '1'.
issue: - In the `image` session for the `machineset` YAMLconfiguration: ~~~ image: offer: aro4 publisher: azureopenshift resourceID: '' sku: aro_410 version: 410.84.20220125 ~~~- Error in Azure side: ~~~ failure sending request for machine myworkernode: cannot create vm: compute.VirtualMachinesClient#CreateOrUpdate: Failure sending request: StatusCode=400-- Original Error: Code="BadRequest" Message="The selected VM size 'Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4' cannot boot Hypervisor Generation '1'. ~~~
resolution: *Official documentation on how to setup Gen 2 SKU is publised at [learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/openshift/howto-gpu-workloads#ensure-the-correct-sku-is-set).* Depending on the image used for the machine set, the value for `image.sku` and `image.version` must be set accordingly. Example:- If using `Standard_NC4as_T4_v3`, it is supported both versions, as mentioned at [Feature support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/gpu-accelerated/ncast4v3-series?tabs=sizebasic#feature-support). So no change is required.- If using `Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4`, only **Generation 2 VM** is [supported](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/gpu-accelerated/nca100v4-series?tabs=sizebasic#feature-support). In the case of `Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4`, the `image.sku` value must follow the equivalent `v2` version of the cluster's original `image.sku` For this example, the value will be `v410-v2`. This can be found using below command: ~~~ az vm image list--architecture x64-o table--all--offer aro4--publisher azureopenshift ~~~- BEFORE ~~~ image: offer: aro4 publisher: azureopenshift resourceID: '' sku: aro_410 version: 410.84.20220125 ~~~- AFTER ~~~ image: offer: aro4 publisher: azureopenshift resourceID: '' sku: v410-v2 version: 410.84.20220125 ~~~--- **NOTE**: It is not supported to use a different `sku` **Y** version from the original one on cluster creation. Eg. Inspect the control plane machines, `oc get machine $mastermachinename-o jsonpath='{.spec.providerSpec.value.image.sku}{"\n"}'`, and if is `aro_44`, it should be used `44-v2` not later ones like `v410-v2`.
root_cause: If the cluster was created with the base SKU `aro_410`. Azure reports that it cannot make the `Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4` because this SKU requires a v2 hypervisor-compatible image. This is documented on Microsoft documentation for Virtual Machines, sessions: [v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/generation-2#generation-2-vm-sizes) and [VM type: nc-a100-v4-series](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/nc-a100-v4-series).

title: After upgrading to OpenShift 4.20 and above the web console looks unstable logging out users several times

title: EgressIP inconsistent MAC addresses during RHOCP 4 node reboot
issue: EgressIP failover blocked after reboot or crash of infra node
EgressIP Dual MAC GARP blocked by security solutions like Cisco ACI
Mac Flapping Observed for EgressIP when nodes being rebooted
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [Bug OCPBUGS-77068](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77068).
root_cause: During graceful shutdown ovnkube-controller does not remove the EgressIP from the br-ex interface, causing the OpenShift node to reply ARP requests even if the OVN CNI is not running if there is any client sending broadcast ARP requests for the EgressIP. This bug is different from private bug OCPBUGS-77015, where after the reboot of the node Gratuitous ARP are seen coming from the previous EgressIP node. This is also different from: [egressIP GARP sent by incorrect node after reboot in RHCOP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7088619).

title: IdM webui not allowing logins due wrong SELinux contex
issue: IDM server is not allowing logins from the webui. But log in via SSH works.
resolution: 1. Try restoring the default context. ~~~ # restorecon-Rv /var/lib/ipa/gssproxy/ ~~~ 2. If the restorecon above doesn't report any context changes, apply log suggestion using the correct tag (ipa_http_keytab_t) that belongs to the Apache keytab in IdM. ~~~ # semanage fcontext-a-t ipa_http_keytab_t '/var/lib/ipa/gssproxy/http.keytab' # restorecon-v /var/lib/ipa/gssproxy/http.keytab ~~~ 3. Restart the services below: ~~~ # systemctl restart gssproxy # systemctl restart httpd ~~~ 4. Reactivate SELinux and test. ~~~ # setenforce 1 ~~~ Go to the WebUI and retest the log in.
root_cause: Incorrect SELinux context on /var/lib/ipa/gssproxy/http.keytab.

title: Nodes stuck in NotReady state during upgrade with wait-for-br-ex-up service not completing in RHOCP 4
issue: - During a cluster upgrade in Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4 (RHOCP 4), one or more nodes transition to a `NotReady` state and fail to recover to Ready.- The kubelet fails to start because the `wait-for-br-ex-up` job does not complete successfully and remains in a running state. ~~~ $ systemctl list-jobs JOB UNIT TYPE STATE 337 systemd-update-utmp-runlevel.service start waiting 180 graphical.target start waiting 328 wait-for-br-ex-up.service start running ## <--- blocker 316 crio.service start waiting 181 multi-user.target start waiting 327 node-valid-hostname.service start waiting 317 kubelet-dependencies.target start waiting 340 afterburn-checkin.service start waiting 342 afterburn-firstboot-checkin.service start waiting 315 kubelet.service start waiting ~~~
resolution: Available Workaround:- Stop the service: `systemctl stop wait-for-br-ex-up.service`- This will bypass the stall condition on the host and allow the process flow to continue, allowing Kubelet/Crio to start up successfully.- The script for `/etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/30-resolv-prepender` can be updated via machine-config to use the [expected version](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/release-4.14/templates/common/on-prem/files/NetworkManager-resolv-prepender.yaml). (This should not stay permanently as this script should be replaced by a subsequent update once the bug is resolved/backported successfully- This KCS will be updated with release versions once available). It can be used to progress through upgrades correctly between versions 4.14--> 4.19- Script- [base64 encoded from 4.14 release](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/release-4.14/templates/common/on-prem/files/NetworkManager-resolv-prepender.yaml): ~~~  ~~~ ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: creationTimestamp: null labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: master name: 99-master-30-resolv-prepender-override spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage: files:- path: /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/30-resolv-prepender contents: source: data:;base64, filesystem: root mode: 0755 ~~~
root_cause: - This behavior is being tracked under bug [OCPBUGS-78958](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-78958). To know more about the supportability and current status, open a [support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/open-case?caseCreate=true) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.- See this related bug: [OCPBUGS-49436](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-49436).- A change was made in 4.14 to modify the boot scripts for resolv-prepender and the wait-for-br-ex-up service as a locking mechanism to control boot time. However, the required script that places the unlock-keyfile for this service: `/etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/30-resolv-prepender` was not successfully updated. NEW installations acquire this file during install time as a manifest, but subsequently this file is not modified/checked by machine-configuration template. As a result- clusters that were installed prior to 4.14 and upgraded to the latest z-stream of 4.14+ can encounter this bug.- A backport was released to correct the behavior on 4.19+ but was not backported to 4.14, 4.15, 4.16, 4.17, 4.18 and so step-through upgrades from clusters on 4.13 or earlier can hit this repeatedly until reaching current releases.- The machine-config solution above should be removed after a patch fix from Red Hat is released to avoid conflicting stale script initializations with desired upstream config handlers once available.

title: Evaluating ACS Replacement with Gatekeeper, Compliance Operator, and Qualys: Red Hat Guidance
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
issue: Customers evaluating Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (RHACS) may consider replacing or supplementing it with a combination of:- Kubernetes Gatekeeper + Validating Admission Policies (VAP)- OpenShift Compliance Operator- Third-party container scanning tools (e.g., Qualys) Questions typically include:- Can these tools replace RHACS admission control, compliance, and runtime security?- What functional gaps exist compared to RHACS?- Is this approach supported or recommended by Red Hat?
resolution: While these tools provide overlapping capabilities, they are not direct replacements for RHACS. They serve different purposes and are best viewed as complementary. 1. Admission Control (Gatekeeper + VAP vs RHACS) Gatekeeper and VAP focus on validating Kubernetes configurations at deployment time (e.g., enforcing labels, security contexts, and policies). However, RHACS provides additional capabilities:- Inline image scanning during deployment- Ability to block deployments based on vulnerabilities (e.g., critical CVEs)- Coverage across build, deploy, and runtime phases As a result, Gatekeeper/VAP cannot fully replace RHACS admission control functionality.--- 2. Compliance (Compliance Operator vs RHACS) The OpenShift Compliance Operator focuses on:- Node and platform-level compliance (e.g., CIS benchmarks, PCI profiles) RHACS focuses on:- Workload and container image compliance Additionally:- RHACS avoids automatic remediation to prevent unintended impact to applications- Compliance Operator is designed for infrastructure-level remediation workflows These tools are complementary and address different layers of compliance.--- 3. Overall Architecture Considerations Replacing RHACS with a combination of tools (Gatekeeper + Compliance Operator + external scanning) may introduce:- Gaps in runtime security and threat detection- Lack of network visibility and runtime enforcement- Increased operational complexity and tool sprawl- Potential alert fatigue across multiple systems Red Hat provides a unified solution through OpenShift Platform Plus, which includes:- RHACS (security)- RHACM (cluster management)- Quay (registry)- ODF Essentials (storage) This integrated approach reduces fragmentation and provides end-to-end coverage.
root_cause: There is no direct one-to-one replacement for RHACS using a combination of Gatekeeper, Compliance Operator, and third-party tools. Each tool addresses a specific layer (admission control, infrastructure compliance, or scanning), while RHACS provides unified security coverage across build, deploy, and runtime.

title: Minimum supported OpenShift Container Platform version for Azure Standard DSv6 VM family vCPUs Deployment
issue: Planning to deploy a cluster on Azure using the **Installer-Provisioned Infrastructure (IPI)*
method to use the **Standard DSv6 Family*
of virtual machines but are having trouble pinning down which OpenShift version officially supports these instances.
Determining compatible OpenShift Container Platform version for Azure Standard DSv6 Family vCPUs during IPI deployment.
Most of the documentation you've found points to Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), which isn't the path you're looking to take.
Seeking version information excluding Azure-specific solutions like ARO.
Lack of documentation on OpenShift Container Platform version compatibility with Azure Standard DSv6 Family vCPUs for IPI deployment.
Need for guidance on minimum supported OpenShift Container Platform version for specified Azure VM family.

resolution: To use the Azure Standard DSv6 instance types for an OpenShift IPI deployment, you need to be on at least **OpenShift Container Platform 4.17**. These specific machine types were added to the "tested and supported" list starting with that release. title: LokiStack per stream rate limited in RHOCP 4
issue: - `Loki` Internal log is being `stream rate limited`.- Alert `X% of records have resulted in an error by `openshift-logging/collector-xxx` `collector` component" is active`- How to minimize the effort to continuously tune the `ingestion per stream rate limit` when forwarding logs to `Loki`.- Automatically control the "per-stream ingestion rate" in `Loki`.- Loki Ingester pods are throwing error message as: ``` level=warn ts=2024-08-07T15:38:10.37249059Z caller=grpc_logging.go:57 method=/logproto.Pusher/Push duration=749.707µs err="rpc error: code = Code(429) desc = entry with timestamp 2024-08-07 15:38:10.26457417 +0000 UTC ignored, reason: 'Per stream rate limit exceeded (limit: 5MB/sec) while attempting to ingest for stream '{kubernetes_container_name=\" \", kubernetes_host=\" \", kubernetes_namespace_name=\" \", kubernetes_pod_name=\" \", log_type=\" \"}' totaling 4305B, consider splitting a stream via additional labels or contact your Loki administrator to see if the limit can be increased' ```
resolution: The issue can partially be addressed by automatically controlling the "per-stream ingestion rate" using the stream sharding mechanism. This mechanism dynamically adjusts the ingestion rate for each stream, ensuring optimal performance and minimizing `per stream rate limit` issues. Red Hat reviewed the feature request in [LOG-4551](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-4551) and delivered a fix in 5.9.0 through ERRATA [RHBA-2024:1591](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2024:1591). ### Other actions #### Reduce the number of logs produced by the container Review in the Loki logs the stream hitting the per stream rate limit and check if the logs are valid and the container is not in verbose/DEBUG mode or the application is not working and that's the reason for generating so many logs #### Reduce the size of the logs Review the tenant visible in the logs hitting the per-stream Rate Limit and try to apply filters for reducing the size of the logs log forwarded applying:- API audit [filters](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/observability/logging/log_collection_forwarding/configuring-log-forwarding.html#logging-audit-filtering_configuring-log-forwarding) if collecting the audit logs- [Filtering logs by content](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/observability/logging/performance_reliability/logging-content-filtering.html)- [Filtering logs by metadata](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/observability/logging/performance_reliability/logging-input-spec-filtering.html) #### Adjust per-stream ingestion rate [Manually adjust per stream ingestion rates](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7060001) not exceeding the maximum values recommended of `perStreamRateLimit: 5` and `perStreamRateLimitBurst: 20`. These numbers are expressed in MB. **NOTE**: the `ingestionRate` attribute should have a bigger value than `perStreamRateLimit` **Note:** In the article ["How to define per_stream_rate_limit parameter in LokiStack CRD?"](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7060001) is explained the default values as Red Hat delivers the Loki stack and the maximum recommended values that shouldn't be exceeded. #### Increase the number of LokiStack ingesters See the Red Hat Knowledge Base article "[Log is missing during 1 node down when using LokiStack in RHOCP4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7050447)".
root_cause: **Disclaimer**:_Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content._ If the per-stream ingestion rate limit is reached, those events will be retried to be delivered as described in the "[Retry policy](https://vector.dev/docs/reference/configuration/sinks/loki/#retry-policy)". ### What's an stream? An stream is a set of unique labels sent with the stream. In RHOL 5, some of the labels by default are: `kubernetes_host`, `kubernetes_namespace_name`, `kubernetes_pod_name`, `log_type` and `kubernetes_container_name`. Speaking about a pods, if it's observed the per-stream rate limit when defined `perStreamRateLimit: 3`, this means that a single container is producing 3MB per second of logs. Doing some calculations, if the container was producing 3MB/second of logs during all the day, a single container would produce: `3MB/s * 60 second has a minute * 60 minutes has an hour * 24 hours has a day = 259200MB day = 259.200GB day`

title: How to investigate VM Pause to due to I/O Error in OpenShift Virtualization?
issue: VM has paused due to I/O error, but need more information.
resolution: Every time the Virtual Machine requests a disk read or write on its virtual Disk, the request is received by the emulator (QEMU), which executes system calls such as read(), write() and io_submit() on the hypervisor against the storage file/device backing the Virtual Machine disk. After the syscall is complete it returns the result to the Virtual Machine. By default, the Virtual Machine is Paused if QEMU receives an I/O error from the host OS when issuing those syscalls. While usually not advisable, this can be changed to pass the error to the Guest OS to handle. Normally it is better to Pause the VM to protect its disk integrity. ~~~ # oc explain vm.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks.errorPolicy GROUP: kubevirt.io KIND: VirtualMachine VERSION: v1 FIELD: errorPolicy DESCRIPTION: If specified, it can change the default error policy (stop) for the disk ~~~ To investigate further why the IOError occurs, one must use strace on the qemu-kvm binary on the Host, to see the read(), write(), ioctl() or io_submit() syscall that is returning error and investigate what exactly was sent in the syscall and what error code it returned. A reproducer is needed, and here are the steps. 1\. Start the VM (start it in Paused mode if the error occurs very early in boot) 2\. Identify what node the VM is running 3\. SSH to that node. If you don't have SSH access, you can use `oc debug node` instead: ~~~ $ ssh core@node.example.com or $ oc debug node/ $ chroot /host ~~~ 4\. Enter the toolbox ~~~ [core@node ~]$ sudo su [root@node core]# toolbox ~~~ 5\. Find the PID of the qemu-kvm process of the respective Virtual Machine that is used as reproducer ~~~ # pgrep-a-f /usr/libexec/qemu-kvm | cut-d ','-f1 65149 /usr/libexec/qemu-kvm-name guest=default_rhel-8 ~~~ 6\. Start strace against the PID of the qemu-kvm process ~~~ $ strace-fvttTyy-s 256-e pread64,pwrite64,ioctl,io_submit,sendmsg-o-p ~~~ 7\. Reproduce the Pause issue 8\. Stop strace (CTRL+C) and look at the strace output to identify the error in mode details, for example, this would be a EINVAL returned due to a problematic discard, causing QEMU to Pause the guest due to the error policy stop being set. ~~~ 37072 23:01:31.642885 ioctl(22, BLKDISCARD, [0, 512]) =-1 EINVAL (Invalid argument) <0.000011> ~~~ 9\. Match the timestamps of the strace with the Pause event on the Guest and virt-launcher logs to confirm. 10\. Investigate why the storage is returning an IO error for the syscall. It may be a problem from the storage side handling the call, or the request sent by QEMU is invalid for some reason. IMPORTANT: if no clear error is found in the strace, consider switching the VM to `aio=threads` and repeat the process again, this will make it stop using io_submit() (used by aio=native, which is default). This will make the strace more readable with standard reads and writes. ~~~ # oc explain vm.spec.template.spec.domain.devices.disks.io GROUP: kubevirt.io KIND: VirtualMachine VERSION: v1 FIELD: io DESCRIPTION: IO specifies which QEMU disk IO mode should be used. Supported values are: native, default, threads. ~~~

title: Unable to run BERT using vLLM 'There is no module or parameter named 'final_logits_bias' in BartForConditionalGeneration'
issue: - Unable to run BERT model using vLLM 'There is no module or parameter named 'final_logits_bias' in BartForConditionalGeneration'
resolution: - `RHAIIS 3.2.2` and earlier are built on the vLLM v0 codebase, which natively supports BART models.- BART-related fixes for the v0 codebase are newly included in 3.2.2. We plan to include the BART plugin starting from 3.3.1 and 3.4A1+. In summary, you can run BART types of model in `RHAIIS 3.2.2`, but you can't run the same in `RHAIIS 3.3`. We have a plan to include new plugin for BART model starting from 3.3.1 and 3.4A1+. [For details refer to KCS article 7138695](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7138695)

title: OpenShift installation OpenStack failing with ansible version ansible core 2.14.2
issue: - OpenShift installation over OpenStack by using Ansible has failed with the following error. ~~~ Looks like module next_nth_usable was not found [cloud-user@bastion-dev-pok install-playbooks-ocp4.18]$ ansible-doc-t filter next_nth_usable [WARNING]: Collection ansible.netcommon does not support Ansible version 2.14.2 [WARNING]: Collection ansible.utils does not support Ansible version 2.14.2 [WARNING]: next_nth_usable was not found ~~~
resolution: - As per OCP documentation, need to follow [Ansible playbooks dependencies](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/installing_on_openstack/installing-openstack-user#installation-osp-downloading-modules_installing-openstack-user), and enable these repos. ~~~ sudo subscription-manager repos \--enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms \--enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms \--enable=openstack-17.1-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms ~~~- The next step is to install the modules with the below command. ~~~ $ sudo dnf install ansible-collection-ansible-netcommon \ ansible-collection-community-general \ ansible-collections-openstack \ python3-netaddr \ python3-openstackclient \ python3-openstacksdk \ python3-pip ~~~- After running the command, the output looks like. ~~~ $ sudo subscription-manager repos--disable=* Updating Subscription Management repositories. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 for x86_64- AppStream (RPMs) 33 MB/s | 79 MB 00:02 Red Hat OpenStack Platform 17.1 for RHEL 9 x86_64 (RPMs) 4.8 MB/s | 3.5 MB 00:00 Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 for x86_64- BaseOS (RPMs) 57 MB/s | 95 MB 00:01 Dependencies resolved. ~~~

title: During the Openshift upgrade image-registry CO is stuck in the progressing state.
issue: - During the OCP upgrade, it failed with the following error ($ oc get co image-registry-o yaml) ~~~ message: Progressing: Unable to apply resources: unable to sync storage configuration: RequestError: send request failed.Progressing: caused by: Head "https://s3-openshift- storage.apps.xx./image-registry-bucket-abcd-": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority NodeCADaemonProgressing: The daemon set node-ca is deployed reason: Error status: "True" type: Progressing ~~~
resolution: - Please refer to the doc [Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation integration with storage](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html-single/registry/index#registry-configuring-registry-storage-rhodf-nooba_configuring-registry-storage-rhodf)- The image-registry-private-configuration-user secret provides credentials needed for storage access and management. It overrides the default credentials used by the Operator if default credentials were found.- For S3 on AWS storage, the secret is expected to contain two keys: ~~~ REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_ACCESSKEY REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_SECRETKEY ~~~- Create an OpenShift Container Platform secret that contains the required keys. ~~~ $ oc create secret generic image-registry-private-configuration-user--from-literal=REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_ACCESSKEY=myaccesskey--from-literal=REGISTRY_STORAGE_S3_SECRETKEY=mysecretkey--namespace openshift-image-registry ~~~- After that added the access keys from the image-registry-bucket to the image-registry-private-configuration-user secret.
root_cause: The lack of permissions caused this issue.

title: openshift-marketplace namespace pods are in CrashLoopBackOff  state.
issue: - The `openshift-marketplace` namespace pods are in a `CrashLoopBackOff` state.- The operators are not visible in `OperatorHub` in the web console.
resolution: - For those using the `Dynatrace OneAgent` operator, you can try the following workarounds:- Remove the `Dynatrace agent` and operator.- Alternatively, disable the following features in the `Dynatrace` settings dashboard:- Automatically monitor processes.- Automatically inject real user monitoring JavaScript tag in the **`Process Group`**.- Exclude all namespaces starting with "openshift" from their monitoring.- This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [OCPBUGS-72597](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-72597). To raise questions or obtain more information, contact [Red Hat Technical Support](https://access.redhat.com/support/contact/technicalSupport).
root_cause: Performance issues are linked to the deprecated `Dynatrace OneAgent Operator` for OpenShift Container Platform 4. For more details, see [Is Dynatrace OneAgent supported in RHEL / RHOCP?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6016311)

title: [Master] Configuring Access Logs in Red Hat Middleware Products
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: - How to enable friendly access log times in JBoss EAP?- How to enable friendly access log times in Apache HTTPD?- How to enable friendly access log times in Apache Tomcat?- How to enable friendly access log times in NGINX?
resolution: The default access log timing in Apache HTTPD, Tomcat, and JBoss EAP are in milliseconds and are not conducive to quickly identifying high access times, or for easily tracing through the flow of a request from HTTPD to EAP using `mod_jk`, for example. One approach that has worked well in modifying the default configuration is to add a Time Taken string to the log pattern followed by the request time in seconds and milliseconds. As well as other information such as cookies, request headers, process ID, thread ID, etc. Each server has different configuration and arguments to do it and here is the list with solutions for each server and its version: * [EAP 4 and EAP 5](#EAP4_5) * [EAP 6](#EAP6) * [EAP 7 and EAP 8](#EAP7_8) * [Apache HTTPD](#Apache) * [Apache Tomcat](#Tomcat) * [NGINX](#NGINX) ####For EAP 4.x / 5.x # {#EAP4_5}- [How to enable access logging for JBoss EAP 4 or 5?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4398611) ####For EAP 6.x # {#EAP6}- [How to enable access logging for JBoss EAP 6](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/185383) ####For EAP 7.x / 8.x # {#EAP7_8}- [How to enable access logging for JBoss EAP 7/8?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2423311) ####For Apache HTTPD # {#Apache}- [How to customize the access log in Apache HTTPD?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4398631)- [How to log which node handled a request from httpd?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/1235863) ####For NGINX # {#NGINX}- [Tuning access log in NGINX](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7025193)- [How to customize the access log in NGINX?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3641722) ####For Apache Tomcat # {#Tomcat}- [How to enable access log in Apache Tomcat?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4398651)- [How to enable access log in JWS for OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5325191)

title: OVN pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state  and node becomes NotReady
issue: - `OVNKube-node` pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state and node becomes `NotReady`.- Unable to access the web console.- Intermittent issue while accessing the cluster through `OC CLI`.- The `ovnkube-node` pod does not come up on that node: ``` failed to run ovnkube: failed to start node network controller: failed to start default node network controller: error waiting for node readiness: gateway init failed to start watching services: watchResource for resource *factory.serviceForGateway. Failed addHandlerFunc: context deadline exceeded ```- Restarting the OVN pod didn't fix the issue.
resolution: - Analyze the ovnkube-controller pod logs and recreate the namespace that was deleted. ``` $ oc new-project ```- Refer to the below `Diagnostic Steps` on how to find the deleted namespace.- Clean up the leftover resources before deleting any namespaces.
root_cause: - The namespace was deleted without cleaning up the leftover resources, causing the OVN pods to reconcile in an indefinite loop during pod restart.- If there is a service dependency, deleting the namespace won't delete the service automatically.

title: How to check the detailed rule list for cluster-admin role in RHOCP
issue: - Users would like to know the detailed list of '*' rules held by the cluster-admin role.
resolution: ~~~- apiGroups: ["*"] $oc api-versions // List of all API versions supported by the cluster- resources: ["*"] $oc api-resources // List of all API resources supported by the cluster- verbs: ["*"] // RestAPI verb get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete- nonResourceURLs ["*"] //List of full path URLs provided by the API $oc get--raw / ~~~
root_cause: ~~~ $ oc get clusterrole cluster-admin-o yaml apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: annotations: rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate: "true" labels: kubernetes.io/bootstrapping: rbac-defaults name: cluster-admin rules:- apiGroups:- '*' resources:- '*' verbs:- '*'- nonResourceURLs:- '*' verbs:- '*' ~~~

title: Can we remove the Subscription.apps.open-cluster-management.io CRD from the ACM environment?
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - The " Subscription.apps.open-cluster-management.io" CRD gets created after installing ACM. It is already deprecated; can we remove it? It's causing confusion and errors while running the OC command: `oc get sub`?
resolution: 1. While the `Subscription.apps.open-cluster-management.io` API (used for RHACM's older application lifecycle management) was officially deprecated starting in RHACM 2.13 in favor of OpenShift GitOps (Argo CD), you should not manually delete the CRD. 2. The deprecation period for this feature has been extended for five releases before it will be permanently removed from the product. Because the MultiClusterHub operator actively manages the application lifecycle components, manually deleting the CRD is an unsupported action. Doing so will likely cause the RHACM operator to continuously attempt to recreate it or place your RHACM installation into a degraded state. 3. To safely avoid this conflict and query the correct resource without modifying operator-managed CRDs, you should use the fully qualified resource name when running your commands: ~~~ OLM subscriptions: subscriptions.operators.coreos.com ACM application subscriptions: subscriptions.apps.open-cluster-management.io ~~~

title: Not able to update the imageSetRef in the agentclusterinstall after the cluster was upgraded to next major version.
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - When editing agentclusterinstall it throws this error when changing the imageSetRef from 4.14.38 to 4.16.39: ~~~ error: agentclusterinstalls.extensions.hive.openshift.io "ocp4-rsc1" could not be patched: admission webhook "agentclusterinstallvalidators.admission.agentinstall.openshift.io" denied the request: Attempted to change AgentClusterInstall.ImageSetRef which is immutable ~~~
resolution: ####Workaround 1. You can update the imageSetRef in AgentClusterInstall as follows:- Backup the agentclusterinstallvalidators and agentclusterinstallmutators validating webhook: ~~~ $ oc get validatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io agentclusterinstallvalidators.admission.agentinstall.openshift.io-o yaml > agentclusterinstallvalidators.yaml $ oc get mutatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io agentclusterinstallmutators.admission.agentinstall.openshift.io-o yaml > agentclusterinstallmutators.yaml ~~~- Delete them: ~~~ $ oc delete validatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io agentclusterinstallvalidators.admission.agentinstall.openshift.io $ oc delete mutatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io agentclusterinstallmutators.admission.agentinstall.openshift.io ~~~ Technically, they should come back up, since the operator is managing these resources.- Sync the siteConfig for ocp4-xyz with a `clusterImageSetNameRef` referenced to the 4.16.39 image. This should update the `imageSetRef` name in the AgentClusterInstall with the 4.16.39 version. ~~~ In siteconfig: clusterImageSetNameRef: "img4.16.39-x86-64-appsub" ~~~ 2. The cluster's infraEnv will not update with 4.16.39 iso. This is an expected behaviour. The OCP version selected at the time of the infraenv creation will continue to exist, and it cannot be upgraded to a newer version. If you want a newer version, then you will need to create a new infraenv. But this version is only used for discovery. Once the hosts are discovered and the cluster is created, the clusterimageset OCP version that you select will be used to install the cluster.
root_cause: - The AgentClusterInstall resource is still referencing the old 4.14.38 ClusterImageSet, even though the cluster has been upgraded to 4.16.39. This mismatch causes the ACM to fail when trying to sync the cluster's specifications.- RFE to make the `AgentClusterInstall.spec.imageSetRef` field mutable is tracked in internal Jira MGMT-21334.

title: RHOSO: full /runner/artifacts folder may block EDPM provisioning

title: OLM Fails to create InstallPlan for latest ODF Operator version in RHOCP 4

InstallPlan for latest OpenShift Data Foundation version is not recreated.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [Bug OCPBUGS-82532](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-82532). ### Workaround {#workaround} 1. title: Converting ephemeral hotplug volumes to be persistent in a VM
issue: The `HotplugVolumes` feature gate is currently deprecated and is being replaced by `DeclarativeHotplugVolumes`. The new declarative API does not support the use of ephemeral hotplug volumes, or volumes that are hotplugged to a `VirtualMachineInstance` but do not persist in the owner `VirtualMachine` definition. Because of this incompatibility, when you switch from `HotplugVolumes` to `DeclarativeHotplugVolumes`, any and all ephemeral hotplug volumes will be unplugged. In order to avoid this unexpected behavior, it is recommended to convert any existing ephemeral volumes to become persistent in the VM spec.
resolution: If your cluster contains any running VMs that have ephemeral hotplug volumes, you will receive a new `VirtualMachineInstanceHasEphemeralHotplugVolume` alert for each impacted VM. Each alert will contain the VMI name as well as the ephemeral volume. To manually find each VMI that contains an ephemeral hotplug volume, run this command which will return a list of entries with format `[vm-name, namespace]` ~~~ $ oc get vmis-A-o json | jq-r '.items[].metadata | select(.annotations | has("kubevirt.io/ephemeral-hotplug-volumes")) | [.name,.namespace] | @tsv' ~~~ Now for each impacted VMI, find the volumes that need to be patched by running the following, substituting ` ` and ` `: ~~~ $ oc get vmis-n-o json | jq-r '.metadata.annotations."kubevirt.io/ephemeral-hotplug-volumes"' ~~~ Finally, to convert the ephemeral volumes to be persistent, run the following virtctl command, substituting ` ` and ` `: ~~~ $ virtctl addvolume--volume-name= ~~~ NOTE: `virtctl addvolume` and `removevolume` has been updated and always persist volumes in both the VM and VMI spec without the need of providing the now deprecated `--perist` flag. This measure was taken to prevent any creation of any new ephemeral hotplugs.
