title: How to extract audit log events matching a specific creation timestamp for a openshift resource in RHOCP 4
issue: - A specific cluster resource was created, patched, or updated at an unexpected time.- The identity of the user or process that triggered a manual resource change needs to be audited.- A method is required to query the `must-gather` audit logs to find API events matching a specific resource's creation timestamp.
resolution: **Prerequisites:**- Generate a cluster must-gather specifically targeting the audit logs. ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather-- /usr/bin/gather_audit_logs ~~~ Follow the steps below to find the specific audit log events:- Discover the creation timestamp of the target resource (e.g., a ReplicationController or DeploymentConfig) by checking its YAML definition: ~~~ $ oc get-o yaml | grep "creationTimestamp" ~~~- Navigate into the extracted must-gather directory and locate the API server audit logs path: ~~~ $ cd / / /audit_logs/openshift-apiserver/ ~~~- Search the audit logs for the specific resource name to find the create, patch, or update events, utilizing zgrep and jq for readable formatting: ~~~ $ zgrep-i " " * | grep-E "update|patch|create" | awk-F "gz:" '{$1=""; $3=""; print $2}' | jq-r '., "========================================================================================"' ~~~- Review the generated JSON output. Compare the requestReceivedTimestamp field in the log event with the creationTimestamp obtained in the first step.- Inspect the user.username and user.groups fields within the matching JSON block to identify the account responsible for the action.

title: How to enable FIPS in a working OCP installation?
issue: - Enable FIPS in a working OCP installation
resolution: - OpenShift Container Platform components are written in Go and built with Red Hat's Golang compiler. When you enable FIPS mode for your cluster, all OpenShift Container Platform components that require cryptographic signing call the RHEL and RHCOS cryptographic libraries.- OpenShift Container Platform requires the use of a FIPS-capable installation binary (`openshift-install-fips`) to install a cluster in [FIPS mode](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/installation_overview/installing-fips#installation-about-fips-components_installing-fips).

title: Developer Hub Operator upgrade from 1.8.2 to 1.9.2 is stuck at pending
issue: - RHDH operator upgrade from 1.8.2-> 1.9.2 leads to pending status- Red Hat Developer Hub Operator- old version is stuck with replacing state and new one with pending state with error: `risk of data loss updating 'backstages.rhdh.redhat.com': new CRD removes version v1alpha1 that is listed as a stored version on the existing CRD`
resolution: This caused by the Backstage CRD collision (not Backstage CR colliding), details below: The Backstage 1.7.4 CRD has `v1alpha1` as one stored of the versions, but the RHDH's Backstage 1.9.2 CRD does not have `v1alpha1`, only `v1alpha3` and `v1alpha4`. Note that a Backstage Custom Resource (CR) is created having `v1alpha3` as `apiversion`. Even deleting the Backstage instance (CR) once the error happens, still upgrade is stuck, given the problem is at the CRD level (CRD is installed by the OLM, from the Operator bundle). Backstage version | Backstage CRD-------------------|------------- RHDH v 1.7.4 | storedVersions: v1alpha1 and v1alpha3 RHDH v 1.9.2 | storedVersions: v1alpha3 and v1alpha4 (version v1alpha1 was removed) It's a known issue and product team is working on the fix [RHDHBUGS-2922](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHBUGS-2922). ### Workaround The following workaround is applicable- and shall be followed in this order: 1. Backup Backstage Custom Resource (CRs) (oc get backstage-o yaml > backup.yaml) and back up any config maps or secrets created and last step reinstall latest version operator and CR using back up 2. Delete the Backstage Custom Resource (CRs) 3. Uninstall the RHDH Operator via Subscription and CSV removal 4. Delete the Backstage Custom Resource Definition (CRD)- last step 5. Reinstall latest version RHDH Operator and Backstage CR from the backup (first step)
root_cause: Deleting the Operator will not remove the CRD. The simplest workaround is to remove the Backstage CR and the respective Backstage CRD, this means an clean slate this implies the Backstage Operand will be deleted. Given a collision, the OLM cannot impose a new CRD (because is breaks the current Backstage CR collides) the RHDH Operator won't necessarily remove by itself, given the deprecated field. The OLM, given the Backstage CRD has changed will block the upgrade with the message: ~~~ 'risk of data loss updating 'backstages.rhdh.redhat.com': new CRD removes version v1alpha1 that is listed as a stored version on the existing CRD' ~~~ Removal of the **Backstage Custom Resource** is a requirement to avoid having an Backstage without the respective CRD, given it could lead to an orphan scenario (when the Backstage CR is decoupled without Backstage CRD). If the CR is decoupled from CRD, so only advanced manipulation like [etcd removal](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7100194)/[dummy CRD](https://access.redhat.com/articles/7108149) creation to remove it. See the following table for understanding: Component | Details/Purpose | Manipulation-------|-------|------- Backstage CR | User created file | `$ oc get backstage` Backstage CRD | OLM installed it from the Backstage bundle | `$ oc get crd backstages.rhdh.redhat.com`

title: How to remove devices and deviceClasses from LVMS Operator in RHOCP 4
issue: - How to safely remove a single disk device from a `deviceClass` in RHOCP 4?- How to remove a complete `deviceClass` from an `LVMCluster`?- Removing storage devices that are no longer needed or were added accidentally, without requiring the complete removal of the `LVMCluster`.
resolution: - Previously, removing a device or deviceClass was a cumbersome procedure requiring the complete removal of the LVMCluster.- Now new feature in RHOCP v4.21 will allows targeted day-2 removal operations, provided the underlying data and associated storage resources are safely evacuated first.- This can be track in the [OCPSTRAT-1698](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPSTRAT-1698) RFE request.- Soon this feature will be available in the RHOCP v4.21 release.

title: How to run pods in linux user namespaces in OpenShift 4.20
issue: - Share steps to run pods in user namespaces without the need to edit project annotations.
resolution: - As highlighted in reported [JIRA Issue](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77039), the steps shared in the documentation to run pods in user namespaces, require editing the UID and GID range annotations on the OpenShift project and thus lead to multiple issues/risks.- To mitigate the problems posed when editing the OpenShift project annotations, the below steps must be followed to create the workload using `restricted-v3` SCC. 1. Create a new OpenShift project: ~~~ $ oc new-project project-name ~~~ 2. Assign `restricted-v3` SCC to `default` Service Account in the namespace `project-name`: ~~~ $ oc adm policy add-scc-to-user restricted-v3-z default-n ~~~ 3. Create a workload/pod definition that complies with `restricted-v3` SCC and has the field `hostUsers: false` configured: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: userns-pod annotations: openshift.io/required-scc: restricted-v3 spec: securityContext: runAsNonRoot: true seccompProfile: type: RuntimeDefault hostUsers: false containers:- name: userns-container image: registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9 command: ["sleep", "1000"] securityContext: runAsUser: 1000 runAsGroup: 1000 runAsNonRoot: true procMount: Unmasked ~~~ 4. Check the user ID in container user namespace: ~~~ $ oc rsh userns-pod sh-5.1$ id uid=1000(1000) gid=1000(1000) groups=1000(1000) sh-5.1$ lsns-t user NS TYPE NPROCS PID USER COMMAND 4026534241 user 3 1 1000 /usr/bin/coreutils--coreutils-prog-shebang=sleep /usr/bin/sleep 1000 sh-5.1$ ~~~ 5. Check the UID used on the node, where the pod is running: ~~~ sh-5.1# chroot /host sh-5.1# lsns-t user NS TYPE NPROCS PID USER COMMAND 4026534241 user 1 3415717 4029678568 /usr/bin/coreutils--coreutils-prog-shebang=sleep /usr/bin/sleep 1000 ~~~

title: Pod unable to communicate on specific VLAN due to double VLAN tagging with bridge and NAD
issue: VMs / Pods are unable to communicate with endpoints on a specific VLAN, while connectivity to other VLANs works as expected.
resolution: Remove VLAN configuration from the `NetworkAttachmentDefinition` (NAD) when VLAN tagging is already handled at the host level. ####Example ~~~ {"cniVersion": "0.3.1", "name": "example-network", "type": "bridge", "bridge": "br0", "ipam": {}, "macspoofchk": true, "preserveDefaultVlan": false} ~~~
root_cause: The issue occurs because VLAN tagging is applied at both the host level (via a VLAN sub-interface such as bond-1.vlanX) and the CNI level (via the NAD using "vlan": X), resulting in unintended double tagging (nested VLAN headers), which leads to packet drops.

title: OpenShift GitOps namespace admin privilege escalation vulnerability
issue: OpenShift GitOps operator allows namespace admins to escalate privileges in the cluster.
Namespace admins can have privileged access to the cluster resources when specifying `sourceNamespaces` in namespace scoped ArgoCD custom resource.
resolution: - The issue, identified as important [vulnerability](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2025-13888) has been fixed in GitOps operator versions [1.16.5](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:23207), [1.17.3](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:23206), [1.18.2](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:23203) and [1.18.3](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:1017) respectively. The fix ensures that cross-namespace permissions are not granted when an Argo CD instance requesting `sourceNamespaces` is namespace-scoped.- Post upgrade to the fix versions, run the [audit script](https://github.com/redhat-developer/gitops-operator/tree/master/scripts/audit-namespace-roles) to verify the valid cross-namespace access and take action if the role and rolebindings are not needed/intentional.
root_cause: The [Applications in any namespace](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_gitops/1.18/html/argo_cd_applications/managing-apps-in-non-control-plane-namespaces) and [Applicationset in any namespace](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_gitops/1.18/html/argo_cd_application_sets/managing-app-sets-in-non-control-plane-namespaces) feature in GitOps requires updating the namespaces in `spec.sourceNamespaces` field of cluster scoped ArgoCD CR, which creates the required roles and rolebindings in the target namespace giving access to the service accounts specific to the ArgoCD instance. As this feature, before the fix, has been working with the namespace scoped ArgoCD instances as well, this allowed, namespace admins to specify any namespace as `sourceNamespaces` in the ArgoCD instance, eventually allowing them to escalate privileges to the cluster.

title: Tekton Pipeline fails with initContainer failure
issue: - Observing random failures with exit code 255 for initContainers causing tekton pipelines to fail.
resolution: The issue is identofied as a CRI-O bug for fast exiting initContainers tracked in upstream bugs [1](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/issues/9840) and [2](https://github.com/tektoncd/pipeline/issues/9654) **Workaround** Currently the workaround is to add `retries` to tasks in a Pipeline, to restart the failing tasks: ~~~ tasks:- name: git-clone retries: 2 <--------------------------- taskRef: name: git-clone ~~~

title: How to Migrate From OSSM 2 to OSSM 3
issue: - How to perform `migration` from `OSSM 2` to `OSSM 3` in **MultiTenant*
mode.
resolution: - This solution follows the **MultiTenant** Upgrade strategy, which is the recommended approach for safely migrating workloads with minimal traffic disruption.- Step 1: Premigration Checklist: 1. If you are not running OpenShift Service Mesh (`OSSM`) 2.6.14, you must update before you can continue. For more information, see [Upgrading Service Mesh.](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/service_mesh/service-mesh-2-x#upgrading-ossm) 2. If you have automated updates configured in the OpenShift Container Platform web console, change them to Manual. 3. Keep the modification and traffic less while `migration` will be perform as the request traffic will be disturbed. **Note:** If you need to add a new workload namespace during the `migration`, it must be managed by the OpenShift Service Mesh 3 control plane and labeled with maistra.io/ignorenamespace: "true". 4. The Kiali Operator provided by Red Hat is running the latest version. 5. Installed the OpenShift Service Mesh Operator 3. To install the OpenShift Service Mesh 3 Operator, see: [Installing OpenShift Service Mesh](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_mesh/3.0/html-single/installing/#installing-openshift-service-mesh). 6. Disable add-ons like Prometheus, grafana and kiali in Service Mesh Control Plane (`SMCP`). 7. [Migrate to gateway injection](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.17/html/service_mesh/service-mesh-2-x#ossm-gateway-migration). 8. Disable network policy management, please refer to below patch command: ~~~ $ oc get smcp-n-o json | jq-r '.spec.security.manageNetworkPolicy' ~~~- Step 2: Performing `migration` in **MultiTenant** mode: 1. In the installed `OSSM 3`, create `IstioCNI` respource. 2. Install the `istioctl` binary tool. 3. Identify the current `IstioRevision` for your `OSSM 3` control plane, refer to below command: ~~~ $ oc get istios ~~~ 4. Copy the revision as `istio.io/rev` label and update injection labels on the dataplane namespace to append all new pods in the namespace connect to `OSSM 3`, refer to below commad: ~~~ $ oc label ns istio.io/rev= maistra.io/ignore-namespace="true"-- overwrite=true ~~~ 5. Restart the application pods one by one, refer to below command: ~~~ $ oc rollout restart deployments-n ~~~ 6. Recreate necessary network policies in the new `OSSM 3` control plane namespace.- Step 3: `Migration` verification: 1. Check if all the workload pods are running or not: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n ~~~ 2. Verify if any pod is refers to `OSSM 2`: ~~~ $ istioctl ps--istioNamespace--revision basic ~~~ 3. Check the application connectivity with its peer pods. 4. Remove `OSSM 2` operator from OpenShift Console.

title: AlertRelabelConfig modifications not seen in OpenShift Web Console (Observe > Alerting)
issue: - The [AlertRelabelConfig](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/monitoring_stack_for_red_hat_openshift/4.21/html-single/managing_alerts/index#modifying-core-platform-alerting-rules_managing-alerts-as-an-administrator) modifications are not seen in OpenShift Web Console (Observe > Alerting)
resolution: Issue [OBSDA-1382](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OBSDA-1382) is opened to explore this option as Feature Request. **Workaround** Current workaround for this is to create new alerting rules with custom prefixes to track the same alert which needed to be modified._Example: For ThanosRuleHighRuleEvaluationWarnings rule, change severity from warning. As below will not refect in Observe > UI_ ~~~ apiVersion: monitoring.openshift.io/v1 kind: AlertRelabelConfig metadata: name: thanosrulehighruleevaluationwarnings namespace: openshift-monitoring spec: configs:- action: Replace regex: ThanosRuleHighRuleEvaluationWarnings;info replacement: warning sourceLabels:- alertname- severity targetLabel: severity ~~~_Users can created below_ ~~~ apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1 kind: PrometheusRule metadata: name: custom-thanos-rule-evaluation-warnings namespace: openshift-user-workload-monitoring spec: groups:- name: custom-thanos-rules rules:- alert: ThanosRuleHighRuleEvaluationWarnings_Warning annotations: description: "Thanos Rule {{$labels.instance}} in {{$labels.namespace}} has high number of evaluation warnings." summary: "Thanos Rule has high number of evaluation warnings." expr: | sum by (namespace, job, instance) (rate(thanos_rule_evaluation_with_warnings_total{job="thanos-ruler"}[5m])) > 0 for: 15m labels: severity: warning ~~~ But it will surely create a lot of noise if such modification is needed for many platform alerts. Hence, RFE [OBSDA-1382](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OBSDA-1382) opened so that changes will be visible in Observe > Alerting directly, it will help users function better.
root_cause: **AlertRelabelConfig modifications not seen in OpenShift Web Console (Observe > Alerting)**- The OpenShift Web Console (under Observe > Alerting) displays alerts by querying the Prometheus API directly, rather than the Alertmanager API.- Because the OpenShift console retrieves its data from Prometheus to show alert states, it reflects this original state. **AlertRelabelConfig modifications visible on Alert receivers.**- AlertRelabelConfig modifies the outbound payload: An AlertRelabelConfig intercepts the alert and dynamically modifies the labels right before sending it to Alertmanager, but it does not actually modify the underlying alerting rule inside Prometheus.- Alertmanager handles the notifications: Alertmanager is only responsible for receiving that modified payload, deduplicating it, and routing the notification to external channels like email or Slack. Because notifications and receivers have no influence on the alert state stored in Prometheus, the OpenShift Web Console will always display the original alert. User receivers show the updated warning severity because they are downstream from Alertmanager, which receives the payload after the AlertRelabelConfig has applied its changes.

title: OpenTelemetry Collector logs "Instrument description conflict" for JVM memory metrics in RHOCP4
issue: - When configuring the OpenTelemetry Operator to send metrics to Prometheus in OpenShift, the OTel Collector logs an Instrument description conflict for the jvm_memory_used_bytes metric.- The collector receives the same metric from two different sources with conflicting description strings ("Measure of memory used." vs. "The amount of used memory"), resulting in log noise similar to the following: 2025-10-30T13:07:56.669Z info prometheusexporter@v0.135.0/collector.go:517 Instrument description conflict, using existing {"resource": {"service.instance.id": "2x1b46f5-x6df-4a13-8c26-f4ee151780b5", "service.name": "otelcol", "service.version": "0.135.0"}, "otelcol.component.id": "prometheus", "otelcol.component.kind": "exporter", "otelcol.signal": "metrics", "instrument": "jvm_memory_used_bytes", "existing": "The amount of used memory", "dropped": "Measure of memory used."}
resolution: - This issue was tracked in the Red Hat issue tracker [Opentelemetry instrument description conflict for jvmmemoryused](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/TRACING-5835).- The log errors are purely cosmetic as the metrics are still successfully exported to Prometheus, just with one description prioritized over the other. However, to eliminate the duplication and log noise, choose one of the following solutions based on your application's needs: **Option 1:** Disable Micrometer Instrumentation in OTel- Disable Micrometer instrumentation `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_MICROMETER_ENABLED=false` or simply remove the override; this is the simplest fix if the Micrometer-bridged metrics aren't specifically needed, since the agent already provides equivalent JVM metrics out of the box. **Option 2:** Disable OTel Agent Runtime Telemetry- If you want to keep the Micrometer bridge active for your application specific metrics but want Micrometer to handle the JVM metrics exclusively, disable the OTel agent's built-in runtime telemetry: Update your Instrumentation CR to include the following environment variables: env:- name: OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_MICROMETER_ENABLED value: "true"- name: OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_ENABLED value: "false" **Option 3:** Disable JVM Metrics at the Application Level (Spring Boot)- If you prefer to let the OTel Java agent be the sole source of JVM metrics while keeping the Micrometer bridge active for other custom app metrics, exclude the overlapping JVM meters within the Spring Boot application itself: Add the following property to your Spring Boot application's application.properties or application.yaml: Properties management.metrics.enable.jvm=false **Option 4:** Tolerate the Log Noise- If Micrometer bridging is required and modifying the application or instrumentation configuration is not feasible, you can safely ignore these logs. The description conflicts on JVM metrics are harmless, though they cannot currently be suppressed from the Prometheus exporter.

title: How to obtain ROSA cluster audit logs
product: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS
issue: - How to obtain cluster audit logs for a Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) cluster- What audit log data does Red Hat collect for ROSA clusters, and what are the limitations?- How can all audit events that Red Hat does not capture be accessed?- How can full access to cluster audit log events be obtained more than twice a year?
resolution: > **Important: Options 2 and 3 are restricted** > Red Hat collects a filtered subset of audit events and imposes strict limits on support-based log requests. Options 2 and 3 can only provide this filtered, limited dataset and are subject to eligibility criteria. Option 1 is the only path that gives the cluster owner full, ongoing, and unfiltered access to audit log data. ### 1. Configure self-service audit log forwarding (recommended) Configuring a customer-controlled log forwarding destination is the recommended option for customers who require ongoing, comprehensive, or compliance-driven audit log access. Unlike Options 2 and 3, this approach gives the cluster owner complete control over:- **Event coverage** — all Kubernetes API server events, without Red Hat filtering- **Retention** — set according to the customer's own compliance requirements- **Access frequency** — no request limits, time-window restrictions, or Red Hat involvement Refer to the ROSA documentation and the following article for setup instructions:- [Configuring audit log forwarding in ROSA](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7002219) **NOTE:** The `oc adm node-logs` method can also be used to retrieve audit logs directly from the cluster's control plane nodes by anyone with cluster-admin permissions, including the customer. Logs include all API server events without filtering. The available time window varies by cluster type:- **ROSA Classic** — approximately the last 2–3 weeks depending on cluster activity- **ROSA HCP** — the available window is significantly shorter; customers should test whether it meets their security or operational requirements before relying on this method > **NOTE** > If a request does not meet the criteria for Option 2 or Option 3, Option 1 (self-service log forwarding) is the only available path for obtaining audit log data. ### 2. Request audit logs through a support case (troubleshooting and support use only) For customers who need a targeted set of audit logs to assist with a specific troubleshooting or support investigation, logs can be requested through a support case. Red Hat access to audit log data for this purpose is limited; this option is not suitable for ongoing compliance monitoring, large-volume requests, or anything beyond a focused investigation. To ensure the request can be fulfilled efficiently, the following information is required: 1. Open a support case with the subject line: `Audit Log Request — ` 2. Provide the following details in the case description:- **Cluster ID** — the OpenShift cluster ID- **Time window** — start date and end date (maximum **6 weeks**). Red Hat retains audit logs for up to 12 months.- **Event filter** — a specific description of the events needed, for example:- Events matching a specific `user.username` or `system:serviceaccount` pattern- `create`, `update`, `delete`, or `patch` verbs on a specific resource type- Events scoped to a specific resource type (e.g. `secrets`, `rolebindings`, `configmaps`)- **Reason** — the compliance or security purpose for the request- **GPG public key and fingerprint** — required for secure delivery of the logs 3. Audit logs contain sensitive information and will be delivered **GPG-encrypted**. Provide a GPG public key and fingerprint in the support case before logs can be shared. For instructions on generating a GPG key pair and decrypting files received from Red Hat, see: [How to generate a GPG key and decrypt sensitive files received from Red Hat support](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7140183) #### Limitations Audit log information provided through a support case is subject to the following limitations:- Audit information is provided solely to assist with security investigations and compliance reviews.- Requests are limited to **2 per year** per cluster.- Requests are limited to a maximum window of **6 weeks** per request.- Red Hat collects a filtered subset of events — not all auditable events are captured. Customers requiring full audit coverage must configure their own log forwarding. Customers who require more than this option provides should refer to Option 1. ### 3. Request escalation for confirmed security incidents For confirmed security incidents — such as an active breach investigation or forensic analysis — where larger volumes of logs are required or the customer's security team has specific, targeted forensic requirements that exceed the limits of Option 2, a support case can be raised. Red Hat will assess the request and escalate internally to the appropriate security team, who have broader access to audit log infrastructure and are better equipped to handle high-volume or forensic log retrieval. To request an escalation: 1. Open a support case and clearly indicate the request relates to an active security incident. 2. Provide a description of the security event and the specific log data required. 3. Red Hat will assess the request and coordinate the escalation internally. > **NOTE** > This path is for genuine security incidents only. Requests that do not meet this threshold will be directed to Option 1 or Option 2 as appropriate.
root_cause: ROSA does not forward audit logs to a customer-controlled destination by default. Customers who need ongoing or historical access to audit log data must either configure their own log forwarding destination or, where eligibility criteria are met, request logs through Red Hat support. Red Hat collects audit logs via a Splunk forwarder integrated with the managed monitoring stack. This applies to clusters with unrestricted egress to the Splunk ingest endpoint. Audit logs are retained for up to 12 months. The subset of events collected is filtered at ingest to focus on compliance-sensitive operations. This is not a full audit trail of all Kubernetes API server events.

title: OCP cluster upgrade completed but the upgrade is not reconciling and stuck at (0% complete)
issue: Openshift cluster upgrade completed but the STATUS is not reconcilling.

cluster-version pod stuck with `Unsupported value: "OperatorLifecycleManagerV1"`and showing errors: ~~~ cvo.go:636] Error handling openshift-cluster-version/version: ClusterVersion.config.openshift.io "version" is invalid: [capabilities.enabledCapabilities[12]: Unsupported value: "OperatorLifecycleManagerV1": supported values: "openshift-samples", "baremetal", "marketplace", "Console", "Insights", "Storage", "CSISnapshot", "NodeTuning", "MachineAPI", "Build", "DeploymentConfig", "ImageRegistry", "OperatorLifecycleManager", "CloudCredential", "Ingress", "CloudControllerManager",: Invalid value: "null": some validation rules were not checked because the object was invalid; correct the existing errors to complete validation] ~~~
resolution: OCP upgrade is not reconcilling due to errors in`cluster-version` pod. This is due to `clusterversion` CR has wrong capabilities enabled. Take backup of clusterversion CR. ~~~ $ oc get clusterversion-o yaml &> /tmp/clusterversion.yaml $ cp /tmp/clusterversion.yaml /tmp/clusterversion.bkup.yaml ~~~ There is "capabilities.enabledCapabilities[12]: Unsupported value: "OperatorLifecycleManagerV1"". Edit "/tmp/clusterversion.yaml" and remove "OperatorLifecycleManagerV1" in the YAML file. Also, remove "generation and resourceVersion" as below. ~~~ apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1 kind: ClusterVersion metadata: creationTimestamp: "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" generation: 28 < < < < < < < < < < < < < Remove name: version resourceVersion: "2976053627" < < < < < < < < < < < < < Remove ~~~ Replace the "clusterversion yaml" and restarted the cvo pod. ~~~ $ oc replace--subresource status-f clusterversion.yaml $ oc delete pod-l k8s-app=cluster-version-operator-n openshift-cluster-version ~~~

In case those images are not present in the registry, to ensure the digest is preserved exactly as the installer expects it, use the `oc image mirror` command (which preserves the manifest structure and digest by default) rather than pushing to a tag: ~~~ oc image mirror registry.redhat.io/multicluster-engine/assisted-installer-rhel9@sha256:7c13a7ea99227ddabff2f70859cb3398adad7f30185aa19913f74a89dc74f573 ocp-private-registry-quay.apps.hub01.example.com/platform/multicluster-engine/assisted-installer-rhel9--keep-manifest-list=true ~~~ 5. Do the same for the controller image; the installer will immediately need the `controller` image once the `assisted-installer-rhel9` container succeeds. Make sure you mirror it the exact same way to preserve its digest. ~~~ oc image mirror registry.redhat.io/multicluster-engine/assisted-installer-controller-rhel9@sha256:1bc18afa7846d3732f44e22308c11edcb70557119005ec2b8b2671925e87c5d5 ocp-private-registry-quay.apps.hub01.example.com/platform/multicluster-engine/assisted-installer-controller-rhel9--keep-manifest-list=true ~~~
root_cause: - The `assisted-installer-rhel9@sha256:7c13a7ea99227ddabff2f70859cb3398adad7f30185aa19913f74a89dc74f573` image was not available in the local registry.- The required assisted-installer images were not mirrored in the private registry.

title: OSSM 3: How to Change Service type to NodePort while Deploying Gateway using Kubernetes Gateway API in ambient mode
issue: - How to change the service to NodePort from LoadBalancer while deploying the Gateway Object using Kubernetes Gateway API in ambient mode.- Is it possible to change service type at the time of Gateway Creation using Kubernetes Gateway API.
resolution: - By default, a Deployment and Service of type `LoadBalancer` is created automatically when the Gateway object is created. To change the service type to `NodePort`, add the below annotation to the deployment: ~~~ networking.istio.io/service-type=NodePort ~~~- If the Gateway object is already created, use the `oc annotate` command to change the service type to `NodePort`. ~~~ oc-n annotate gateway networking.istio.io/service-type=NodePort ~~~
root_cause: - When the Gateway object is created, a Deployment and Service of type `LoadBalancer` is created automatically. An annotation can be applied to change the service type from `LoadBalancer` to any other service type.

title: How to start/enable USBGuard service using MachineConfig in RHOCP 4.20?
issue: How to start/enable USBGuard service using MachineConfig in RHOCP 4.20?
resolution: * Enable usbguard extension with below yaml: ~~~ # cat 80-extensions.yaml apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 80-worker-extensions spec: config: ignition: version: 3.5.0 extensions:- usbguard ~~~ * Then start the usbguard service with below yaml: ~~~ # cat 80-worker-usbguard-complete.yaml apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker name: 80-worker-usbguard-complete spec: config: ignition: version: 3.5.0 storage: files:- contents: source: 'data:,RuleFile=/etc/usbguard/rules.conf%0APresentDevicePolicy=apply-policy%0AIPCAllowedGroups=wheel%0A' mode: 384 overwrite: true path: /etc/usbguard/usbguard-daemon.conf- contents: source: 'data:,allow%20with-interface%20all-of%20%7B%2003%3A*%3A*%20%7D%0A' mode: 384 overwrite: false path: /etc/usbguard/rules.conf systemd: units:- contents: | [Unit] Description=USBGuard daemon After=network.target [Service] PIDFile=/run/usbguard.pid # Reset ExecStart to clear the RPM default ExecStart= # Start in foreground (-f) with persistent policy (-P) ExecStart=/usr/sbin/usbguard-daemon-f-P-c /etc/usbguard/usbguard-daemon.conf # Force Type to simple so systemd doesn't wait for a fork Type=forking Restart=on-failure [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target enabled: true name: usbguard.service ~~~ * Then apply the created yaml files to enable the usbgurd extension and start the service: ~~~ # oc apply-f 80-extensions.yaml // to enable the extension # oc apply-f 80-worker-usbguard-complete.yaml // to start the service. ~~~

title: NotReady node with high load and many D state processes in OpenShift 4
issue: - There is a node in `NotReady` status with very high load and many processes in `D` state.- The load average shown for the node is very high, while there are no processes using excessive CPU.
resolution: Follow the Diagnostic Steps section to find the cause of many processes in `D` status. There is additional information about processes in `D` state in [what is "`D`" state (or `dstate`, `d-state`)?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/59989) If the cause is the `rpc_wait_bit_killable`, it typically means the processes are waiting on a response from a NFS server, and checking if there is any issue with the NFS will be required. For processes in `D` state caused by NFS, please refer to the workaround below. For other causes shown in the `ps-elfL` `WCHAN` column, please open a [new Support Case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new) for troubleshooting. ### Workaround for processes in `D` state caused by NFS To clear NFS blocked processes that have not automatically recovered, the system will need to be rebooted as explained in [is there a way to kill a process in the 'Z' or 'D' state without a reboot?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/2972) > *If operations do not complete due to a hardware or software fault (for example network connectivity problems) it may not be possible to eliminate all processes in `D` state without rebooting.* Processes stuck in `D` status due to NFS can be caused by the recovery behavior of the NFS client after an NFS request times out. From the `man nfs`: ~~~ soft / hard Determines the recovery behavior of the NFS client after an NFS request times out. If neither option is specified (or if the hard option is specified), NFS requests are retried indefinitely. If the soft option is specified, then the NFS client fails an NFS request after retrans retransmissions have been sent, causing the NFS client to return an error to the calling application. NB: A so-called "soft" timeout **can cause silent data corruption** in certain cases. As such, use the soft option only when client responsiveness is more important than data integrity. Using NFS over TCP or increasing the value of the retrans option may mitigate some of the risks of using the soft option. ~~~ For configuring NFS mount options, refer to [how to edit mount options for pods that are backed by NFS `PersistentVolumes` in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7034542).
root_cause: If there are many processes in `D` status due to `rpc_wait_bit_killable`, it typically means the processes are waiting on a response from a NFS server. When a NFS client is waiting on the server and doesn't receive a response, the processes will go into `D` state. The load average calculation includes blocked processes, so the load average will be very high and similar to the number of blocked processes.

2026-04-07T07:24:24.378188421Z ^[[0;31mfatal: [localhost]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to apply object: b'{\"kind\":\"Status\",\"apiVersion\":\"v1\",\"metadata\": {},\"status\":\"Failure\",\"message\":\"StatefulSet.apps \\\\\"aah-dev-postgres-15\\\\\" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than \\'replicas\\', \\'ordinals\\', \\'template\\', \\'updateStrategy\\', \\'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy\\' and \\'minReadySeconds\\' are forbidden\",\"reason\":\"Invalid\",\"details\":{\"name\":\"aah-dev-postgres-15\",\"group\":\"apps\",\"kind\":\"StatefulSet\",\"causes\":[{\"reason\":\"FieldValueForbidden\",\"message\":\"Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than \\'replicas\\', \\'ordinals\\', \\'template\\', \\'updateStrategy\\', \\'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy\\' and \\'minReadySeconds\\' are forbidden\",\"field\":\"spec\"}]},\"code\":422}\\n'", "reason": "Unprocessable Entity"}^[[0m 2026-04-07T07:24:24.378188421Z ~~~

title: GitLab Operator installation and upgrade in Openshift 4
issue: - What's Red Hat support for GitLab in Openshift 4?- GitLab Operator installatoin details in Openshift 4?
resolution: The OLM installation relies on indexes and bundles that come from the package manifest and that are provided by the respective product. However, if the bundle is not available, the OLM cannot upgrade and the Operator has not marked it as available on that version. PackageManifest is expected to mention what the upgrade path is and the versions available to it. Therefore, if GitLab explicitly excludes 1.3.3+ on 4.16+ or otherwise, it will not be available in the install and/or upgrade. Checking the Gitlab operator repository source code, I could see it is not the OLM that has a broken path, but GitLab's manipulating the build seem to skip/skip range the upgrade path- see below. Below defines `spec.replaces` and `spec.skips` in its bundle's CSV, which affects the update graph that OLM produces, and Red Hat cannot know the versions they are setting- this is done at build time: ~~~ set_upgrade_path() {local csv_files=$(grep-l 'kind: ClusterServiceVersion' "${BUNDLE_DIR}"/manifests/*.yaml) for csv in $csv_files; do if [-n "${OLM_SKIP_VERSION}"]; then ${YQ} eval-i ".spec.skips=[\"${OLM_PACKAGE_NAME}.v${OLM_SKIP_VERSION}\"]" $csv fi if [-n "${PREVIOUS_OPERATOR_VERSION}"]; then ${YQ} eval-i ".spec.replaces=\"${OLM_PACKAGE_NAME}.v${PREVIOUS_OPERATOR_VERSION}\"" $csv fi done} ~~~ Providing the indexes/manifest falls within the GitLab Operator purview/support. In other words, the bundle isn't available, operator has not marked it as available on that version the OLM cannot build the upgrade path. Although the OLM builds the upgrade path, the versions must be provided in the package manifest to be built upon. link from one to another? they have to show a path from what is currently available to the latest. If that's present, then OLM just isn't generating the installplan. if it isn't, then they're blocked on current version, full-stop.
root_cause: GitLab Operator is provided by GitLab, which is a 3rd party vendor, in the list of Certified and Community Operators. Regarding limitations, Gitlab has some limitations/restrictions [Docs GitLab Openshift](https://docs.gitlab.com/operator/installation/?tab=OpenShift) shows clearly OCP 4.16 is not supported. Therefore, the OLM is not to be blamed for this. This is also shown by [GitLab Runner Operator- 203](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gl-openshift/gitlab-runner-operator/-/issues/203). In this type of issues, one option would be to remove the Operator and install the new version Operator, leaving the Operand as is. The only potential difference could be the Gitlab Custom Resource's `spec.version`. However, a full due diligence must be done regardless, but on our side the Operand seem to have worked nominally. Note I saw this warning in the package manifest: ~~~ **Installation using OLM is considered experimental.** GitLab does not support any issues related to instances deployed using OLM. For more information on potential issues with OLM, see [issue 241](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cloud-native/gitlab-operator/-/issues/241). The GitLab operator is responsible for managing the full lifecycle of GitLab instances in your Kubernetes or Openshift container platforms. ~~~ Finally this can be useful [Docs GitLab Operator installation- OLM details](https://docs.gitlab.com/operator/installation/?tab=OLM) where OCP 4.16 is not supported, so we think that's done on purpose.

title: Dynamic provisioning for NFS volumes in OpenShift
issue: - Does OpenShift dynamic provisioning support for plain NFS servers?- Does Red Hat support dynamic provisioning of PVs using NFS exports from a RHEL server?- Is there any CSI driver supported for NFS dynamic PV provisioning?

title: Configure mount options for pods that are backed by PersistentVolumes (NFS or other volume types) in OpenShift 4?
issue: Is it possible to configure mount options for volumes in OpenShift 4?
How to configure NFS mount options for pods backed by NFS PV?
When creating a pod backed by NFS Persistent Volume, default mount options are set. How to edit these NFS mount options?
resolution: It is not possible to configure required mount options (for NFS or other volume types) directly in the pods, but they can be specified while creating a `PersistentVolume` by using the PV attribute `spec.mountOptions`, or using the `mountOptions` field from `StorageClasses` for dynamically provisioned PVs. > **Note:** currently, [dynamic provisioning NFS volumes is not supported in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3353451). Refer to the *Diagnostic Steps* section for examples for manually creating `PersistentVolumes` backed by NFS with customized mount options (like `nfsvers` and `soft`).

Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.* It is possible to configure mount options (for NFS or other volume types) directly in the `PersistentVolumes` via the `spec.mountOptions` field, or in the `mountOptions` field from `StorageClasses` for dynamically provisioned `PersistentVolumes`. > **Note:** currently, [dynamic provisioning NFS volumes is not supported in OpenShift 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3353451). Refer to the upstream Kubernetes documentation about the `PersistentVolumes` types supporting [mount options](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#mount-options), and to the `StorageClasses` [mount options](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes/#mount-options).

title: Failed to configure NFS for the internal image-registry storage in OpenShift
issue: When attempting to utilize an NFS share for image-registry storage, the PVC created by the image registry operator fails with an error such as: ~~~ Failed to provision volume with StorageClass "thin": invalid AccessModes [ReadWriteMany]: only AccessModes [ReadWriteOnce] are supported ~~~
resolution: Based on the information in [is NFS supported for OpenShift cluster internal components in Production](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3428661), while it is supported to use NFS V4 as the storage provider, there are known issues and **it is not recommended** to use NFS as the storage provider for the internal image registry in OpenShift. ### Workaround To work around the `invalid AccessMode` issue, even if it is not recommended to use NFS as the storage provider for the internal image registry, the following procedure can be followed: 1. Delete the PV and PVC ~~~ timeout 2 oc delete pv pv-name timeout 2 oc delete pvc image-registry-storage-n openshift-image-registry ~~~ 2. Delete image-registry pods ~~~ oc get pods-n openshift-image-registry # for each pod with a name beginning with image-registry-, run: timeout 2 oc delete pod image-registry-some-random-numbers-n openshift-image-registry ~~~ 3. Create a new storage class which does not have a configured access mode. ~~~ oc create-f- < 4. Disable the "thin" storage class as the default storageclass ~~~ oc patch storageclass thin-p '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class": "false"}}}' ~~~ 5. Enable the "non-dynamic" storage class as the default storageclass ~~~ oc patch storageclass non-dynamic-p '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class": "true"}}}' ~~~ 6. Create a new PV which references the new storage class. ~~~ oc create-f- < 7. Create a new image-registry PVC which references the custom storage class. ~~~ oc create-f- <
root_cause: On a vSphere cluster, the default storage class is `thin` which has an access mode of `ReadWriteOnly`. The PVC created by the image registry does not define a storage class and as a result, the default storage class is used. The image registry PVC is configured to have an access mode of `ReadWriteMany`.

title: Is there any way to reduce the size of must-gathers from OpenShift 4?
issue: - In some clusters, usually with a big number of nodes, must-gathers can reach very large sizes (next to 100 GiB in some cases). This implies that creating, uploading, and uncompressing them can take a very long time and that has a significant impact on Red Hat's capacity to provide support promptly.
resolution: A request for enhancement [RFE-4568](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RFE-4568) was submitted concerning this topic and it has been accepted. Due to the above mentioned RFE, starting with OpenShift 4.16 `oc` binary and must-gather images, it was introduced as a [Technology Preview teature](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview) the ability to allow filtering the logs collected by must-gather using `since` and `since-time` options for the must-gather sub-command. That feature is GA starting with OpenShift 4.17 as per the release notes: [new flags added for must-gather command](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.17/release_notes/ocp-4-17-release-notes.html#ocp-4-17-must-gather-new-flags_release-notes). ###Using the new options to filter the logs Example of usage of the new options in OpenShift 4.16 (as a [Technology Preview teature](https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview)) and in OpenShift 4.17 and newer releases as GA: ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--since=24h ~~~ ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather--since-time=$(date-d '-24 hours' +%Y-%m-%dT%T.%9N%:z) ~~~ > **Note:** for being able to use those options, the cluster and the `oc` binary needs to be 4.16 or newer. ###Workaround for 4.15 and older releases For Red Hat Openshift Container Platform versions 4.15 and earlier, the following command is applicable: ~~~ $ oc adm must-gather-- "sed-i 's#oc adm inspect#oc adm inspect--since=24h#g' /usr/bin/*gather*; /usr/bin/gather" ~~~ It alters how the `oc adm inspect` command operates within the must-gather procedure. More precisely, it employs the `sed` command to locate occurrences of `oc adm inspect` within the different `gather*` scripts in `/usr/bin/` (utilized internally by `oc adm must-gather`), substituting them with `oc adm inspect--since=24h`. The addition of `--since=24h` restricts the inspection to data from the previous 24 hours (change the `--since=24h` with the desired time). This adjusted command essentially compiles diagnostic data while focusing solely on information pertinent to the preceding 24 hours. This capability proves valuable for scrutinizing recent issues or events within the cluster.
root_cause: In some clusters, the main reason for this problem is the rotated logs of the pods hosted in some OpenShift projects like `openshift-sdn`. However, the reason why a must-gather becomes too large does not have to be the same in all cases. If other root causes are found, feel free to report them to [Red Hat Support](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/support).

title: LDAP and LDAPS server integration with RHDG 8.4 in OCP 4
issue: - How to set up LDAP server integration with RHDG 8.4- How to set up LDAPS server integration with RHDG 8.4
resolution: Starting on DG Operand 8.4.2+ (Operand `spec.version` > 8.4.1-1) users can configure LDAP in a straightforward manner- see an example on [How to set LDAP configuration on Data Grid deployed in Openshift 4 via Helm Charts and Operator](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7125399): 1. Set up LDAP server and service (on OCP 4) 2. Write the ConfigMap with the adequate LDAP settings 3. Configure RHDG to Use LDAP's Realm (using `spec.configMapName` field of the Infinispan CR) 4. Confirm authentication: ~~~ 21:08:45,127 DEBUG (main) [org.wildfly.security] [javax.naming.ldap.InitialLdapContext@61533ae] successfully created. Connection established to LDAP server <----- ~~~ ### ConfigMap example: ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: $cluster-name namespace: $cluster-namespace data: infinispan-config.xml: > binaryData: {} immutable: false ~~~ Note:- The security tag is below the server and infinispan tags;- Currently, you cannot use the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) protocol with the DIGEST or SCRAM authentication mechanisms, because these mechanisms require access to specific hashed passwords. **Attention:** For LDAPS in OCP see the solution [LDAP and LDAPS server integration with RHDG 8.4 in OCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7034290), in that case, attention: Route type | Comment----------|--------- `Edge` Route | is required because the request arrives as non-encrypted for DataGrid `Passthrough` Route | can be used as long as DG's SSL via server-identities is done. ### Optional steps- LDAPS (up to the user's discretion to set LDAP or LDAPS): 1. Obtain the LDAP Server's SSL/TLS Certificate: 2. Import the LDAP Server's Certificate into RHDG's pods via `spec.security.endpointEncryption.clientCertSecretName` on the Infinispan CR. 3. **If the user wants to client cert auth on the Infinispan clients:** The clientCertSecretName can be set with strategies: Validate or Authenticate. Otherwise, it can be set for `None` and the certs in `clientCertSecretName` can/should still be added to the truststore. Strategy | Requires | Purpose----------|-------|------- None |- |- Validate | Requires a trust store that contains any part of the certificate chain for the signing authority, typically the root CA certificate | More light restrictions Authenticate | Requires a trust store that contains all public client certificates in addition to the root CA certificate | More strict restrictions ### FAQ **Q1. How can the Infinispan server be configured to trust the certificates of the LDAP server** A1. Via `spec.security.endpointEncryption.clientCertSecretName`. **Q2. why clientSecretName instead of certSecretName?** A2. Because LDAP cert are certificates that the Infinispan server trusts, not the ones that it provides. [certSecretName](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7017543) is about what the DG server provides. **Q3. What was the issue with DG 8.4.2.previous for LDAP?** A3. DG 8.4.2.previous had an issue with the LDAP default configuration which would be always overwritten. This was fixed on DG Operator 8.4.2- see [Release notes](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.4/html-single/data_grid_operator_8.4_release_notes/index), which fixes [JDG-5756](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JDG-5756). The user must configure the Operand via `spec.version > = 8.4.1-1` otherwise [JDG-5756](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JDG-5756) will still be an issue. **Q3. What Jira DG 8.5 fixed for LDAP** A4. DG 8.5 provides the fix for [JDG-7077](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JDG-7077) for Data Grid 8.5.x., which allows ldap-realm element to be configured with a client-ssl-context and to the realm configurationto be used for TLS connections. **Q5 After setting up LDAP, only Edge route works, why?** A5. The below SSL configuration is required for passthrough Route usage, without it only Edge will work because the request arrives as non-encrypted for DataGrid: ~~~ ~~~
root_cause: See [DG Operator 8.4 Guide](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.4/html/data_grid_operator_guide/client-certificates#providing-client-certificates_client-certificates) for providing client certificates. ### Workflow for LDAPS The DG client certifies with the DG server, which in turn certifies with the LDAP server. When there is LDAPS: 1. DG validates its connection(s) with the LDAPS server using the cert stored in its truststore via `clientCertSecretName`. 2. If `spec.encryption.clientCert`!= None: DG clients certs are also validated against certs that are provided via `clientCertSecretName` Note about `clientCert` creation: from a DG perspective, it doesn't matter which entity creates the secret as long as it contains the LDAP certs and is in the same namespace as the Infinispan Custom Resource. ### DG 8.4 limitation DG 8.4's LDAP realm does not apply SSL context. Although the server schema states that the `ldap-realm` element can be configured with `client-ssl-context` for TLS connections, unfortunately, the configuration parser does not apply the configuration to the realm. This was worked on [JDG-7077](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/JDG-7077) for Data Grid 8.5.x. ### Edge vs Passthrough Route for LDAP The LDAP configuration by default does not come with SSL, which means it will be unencrypted. The user needs to set the `ssl` tag (stanza) in the configuration to work nominally, otherwise only Edge Route will work, reason: because Edge route is un-encrypted from Ingress to DG pods.

title: Kuadrant "RBAC: access denied" on requests to Gateway in disconnected environments
issue: Inference and chat completion requests fail in disconnected or restricted environments. The Gateway attempts to fetch the WASM authentication module image from public Red Hat registries (`registry.access.redhat.com`). It does not automatically respect cluster-wide `ImageDigestMirrorSet` configurations and lacks the necessary credentials to pull from the local mirror registry. ```bash $ oc logs-n openshift-ingress openshift-ai-inference-openshift-ai-inference-5fdc976c4c-wfmpk-f #... 2026-04-10T18:02:10.161014Z info wasm fetching image rhcl-1/wasm-shim-rhel9 from registry registry.access.redhat.com with tag sha256:22c87cc5fa70cf8f10588687145a7e32551a5f3734d5fc81e72b9a4aab550db6 2026-04-10T18:02:40.161112Z error wasm error in converting the wasm config to local: cannot fetch Wasm module oci://registry.access.redhat.com/rhcl-1/wasm-shim-rhel9@sha256:22c87cc5fa70cf8f10588687145a7e32551a5f3734d5fc81e72b9a4aab550db6: could not fetch Wasm OCI image: could not fetch manifest: Get "https://registry.access.redhat.com/v2/": context deadline exceeded. applying deny RBAC filter [2026-04-10T18:03:00.165Z] "GET /llm-conformance-test/single-gpu/health HTTP/1.1" 403- rbac_access_denied_matched_policy[none]- "-" 0 19 0- "10.128.2.2" "Go-http-client/1.1" "73d6a41e-8e7f-4f48-a061-e3e2bdb1994c" "openshift-ai-inference-route-openshift-ingress.apps. " "-" outbound|8000||single-gpu-kserve-workload-svc.llm-conformance-test.svc.cluster.local- 10.128.3.174:443 10.128.2.2:48602 openshift-ai-inference-route-openshift-ingress.apps. llm-conformance-test.single-gpu-kserve-route.2 #... ```
resolution: To enable disconnected logic, you must configure the Kuadrant Operator `Subscription` and provision the required secrets. Follow these steps: 1. Override the WASM Image (`RELATED_IMAGE_WASMSHIM`) Patch the Kuadrant Operator Subscription (in the `kuadrant-system` namespace) to include the `RELATED_IMAGE_WASMSHIM` environment variable.- Set the value to the full path of the WASM module in your local mirror registry (for example, `: /...`).- **Note: You can find your local mirror registry by listing the `ImageDigestMirrorSet` resources and locating the one with `source: registry.access.redhat.com/rhcl-1`.** 2. Provision the Pull Secret Create a Kubernetes Secret named exactly `wasm-plugin-pull-secret` in the Gateway namespace (for example, `openshift-ingress`) with the local mirror registry image pull secret. 3. Enable Pull Secret Auto-Injection (`PROTECTED_REGISTRY`) By default, the Kuadrant operator removes unsupported fields like `imagePullSecrets` from `WasmPlugin`. To prevent this, use the protected registry feature by adding the `PROTECTED_REGISTRY` environment variable to the same Operator Subscription.- Set the value to the hostname of your local mirror registry.- When the operator detects a WASM URL matching this registry, it automatically injects the required image pull secret into the WasmPlugin. Here is an example of the patched Subscription containing both required environment variables: ```yaml apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: labels: operators.coreos.com/rhcl-operator.kuadrant-system: "" name: rhcl-operator namespace: kuadrant-system spec: channel: stable config: env:- name: RELATED_IMAGE_WASMSHIM # example:: /rhcl-1/wasm-shim-rhel9@sha256:22c87cc5fa70cf8f10588687145a7e32551a5f3734d5fc81e72b9a4aab550db6 value:: /rhcl-1/ @- name: PROTECTED_REGISTRY value:: installPlanApproval: Automatic name: rhcl-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace ``` 4. Bypass TLS for Internal Registries (If Applicable) If your local mirror registry uses self-signed certificates, update the Gateway `ConfigMap` to trust the insecure registry. Add the `WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES` environment variable to the container configuration. Set the value to the hostname of your local mirror registry. ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name:-config namespace: openshift-ingress data: #... deployment: | spec: template: spec: containers:- name: istio-proxy env:- name: WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES value: ``` ```yaml apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Gateway metadata: name: namespace: openshift-ingress spec: #... infrastructure: parametersRef: group: "" kind: ConfigMap name:-config ```
root_cause: ``` error in converting the wasm config to local: cannot fetch Wasm module oci://registry.access.redhat.com/rhcl-1/wasm-shim-rhel9@sha256:22c87cc5fa70cf8f10588687145a7e32551a5f3734d5fc81e72b9a4aab550db6: could not fetch Wasm OCI image: could not fetch manifest: Get "https://registry.access.redhat.com/v2/": context deadline exceeded. applying deny RBAC filter ```

title: DG 8 Cross-site approaches and limitations in and out of OCP
issue: - What is the limitations on manual and automatic approaches for cross-site in DG 8?- Using DG 8 cross-site automatic approach without authentication in OCP
resolution: There are two approaches for cross-site setting: automatic using NodePort|LoadBalancer, or manual via LoadBalancer. Those approaches are not interchangeable and are designed for a specific environment/setting and therefore should not to be mixed as well. For details on manual vs automatic URL see, [Setting up Cross site replication locations url when using the nodeport/loadbalancer/routes in DG 8 OCP](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/6961656). ### Limitations on automatic cross-site setting The automatic approach is based on Operators discovery in each datacenter. It can be configured following the steps described on [Data Grid 8.2- Setting up cross-site replication](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_data_grid/8.2/guide/7836d92e-e546-4972-a378-7178c53d4a32#_a1c72f43-1770-4ce5-9170-cd6a7754a83a), including NodePort and the authentication/role assign with: ~~~ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-reader-z-n ~~~ And as consequence the Infinispan CR, will be similar to the below line, since you are using `NodePort` as type and expose: ~~~ expose: type: NodePort spec.service.sites.local.expose.nodePort ~~~ Note that NodePort is the port expose method for bare-metal environment. For cloud environment, it depends on LoadBalancer technology enabled by the cloud provider, as the table below: Environment | Exposed Supported Method--------- |--------- bare-metal OCP | expose NodePort* Cloud environment | expose LoadBalancer *LoadBalancer **will not** work on-premise, except MetalLB, which is third party. ### Limitations on manual cross-site setting The manual xsite was designed to enable xsite with clusters outside OCP, and must be done with exposing LoadBalancer. Although it could be possible be used inside of it, it is not a supported scenario. The Infinispan CR will be as follows: ~~~ expose: type: LoadBalancer... spec.service.sites.local.expose.port ~~~

title: RHOSO 18 Distributed Zones: Networking Requirements - BGP for Control/Data Plane
issue: Uncertainty regarding networking requirements for [RHOSO 18 distributed zones](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openstack_services_on_openshift/18.0/html/deploying_a_rhoso_environment_with_distributed_zones/assembly_creating-a-rhoso-environment-distributed-zones)
Query on necessity of dynamic routing with BGP for both control and data planes in RHOSO 18 distributed zones
resolution: To be supported, an environment with distributed zones needs to use dynamic routing (BGP). Any other solution need to be evaluated as support exception or RFE. It's possible to distribute both control or/and data planes.
root_cause: * Transition from L2 stretch to routed L3 design between AZs desired * Inquiry about supported designs using BGP solely for control plane, without dynamic routing for data plane

title: CVE-2026-0871 – Understanding User Profile (Preview Feature) and Impact on Unmanaged Attributes in RHBK 22
issue: According to CVE-2026-0871 advisory released on the Red Hat Customer Portal, 'An administrator with manage-users permission can modify unmanaged user attributes in Keycloak, even when the "Only administrators can view" setting is enabled.
resolution: 1. Feature Enablement (User Profile): To enable the functionality associated with the CVE, start RHBK with: ~~~./kc.sh start--features=preview ~~~ 1.1. This exposes the User Profile configuration in the Admin Console: ~~~ Realm Settings > User Profile ~~~ 2. Attribute Configuration: Once enabled, administrators can:- Define managed attributes Configure permissions:- Who can view- Who can edit e.g:- View: admin- Edit: (empty or restricted) This configuration corresponds to “Admin View Only” 3. When the CVE Applies The vulnerability is only relevant if:- The User Profile feature is enabled- Attributes are configured with restricted edit permissions- An administrator has “manage users” permission
root_cause: The behavior described in CVE-2026-0871 is related to the User Profile feature, which enables: Managed user attributes Fine-grained attribute permissions (view/edit) Configurations such as “Admin View Only” In RHBK 22, this functionality is part of a Technology Preview feature and is not enabled by default. By default: Keycloak uses unmanaged attributes (free-form attributes under Users → Attributes) These do not support fine-grained permission controls

title: How to configure an external load balancer in front of IPI based cluster installation
issue: - How to configure an `external load balancer` in front of IPI based cluster installation?- Is it possible to deploy an `external load balancer` in IPI based baremetal cluster?
resolution: - As mentioned in official [documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/latest/html-single/installing_on_bare_metal/index#installation-load-balancing-user-infra-example_installing-bare-metal), it is possible to deploy an `external load balancer` in Layer-4 mode for the `IPI` baremetal cluster where traffic coming to the cluster will be load balanced between master nodes and worker nodes on respective ports i.e.`6443` for `master nodes` and `80,443 and 1936` for `worker nodes`.- To configure an `external load balancer` in `IPI` baremetal cluster, follow the steps mentioned below:- At first, leave the already-configured `API VIP` and `Ingress VIP` as it is, as it cannot be removed from the `IPI` cluster.- Update the upstream DNS records to point the `API.. ` and `*.apps.. ` ingress URLs to the `external load balancer's` IP address.- In `external load balancer` configuration file, forward the traffic coming for `port 6443` to `master nodes` IP address or hostname and traffic coming for `port 80,443` to `worker nodes` IP address or hostname. Refer to the [documentation](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.14/installing/installing_bare_metal/installing-bare-metal-network-customizations.html#installation-load-balancing-user-infra_installing-bare-metal-network-customizations) where the Haproxy configuration is given to configure the loadBalancer. ~~~ listen api-server-6443 bind *:6443 mode tcp option httpchk GET /readyz HTTP/1.0 option log-health-checks balance roundrobin server bootstrap bootstrap.ocp4.example.com:6443 verify none check check-ssl inter 10s fall 2 rise 3 backup server master0 master0.ocp4.example.com:6443 weight 1 verify none check check-ssl inter 10s fall 2 rise 3 server master1 master1.ocp4.example.com:6443 weight 1 verify none check check-ssl inter 10s fall 2 rise 3 server master2 master2.ocp4.example.com:6443 weight 1 verify none check check-ssl inter 10s fall 2 rise 3 listen machine-config-server-22623 bind *:22623 mode tcp server bootstrap bootstrap.ocp4.example.com:22623 check inter 1s backup server master0 master0.ocp4.example.com:22623 check inter 1s server master1 master1.ocp4.example.com:22623 check inter 1s server master2 master2.ocp4.example.com:22623 check inter 1s listen ingress-router-443 bind *:443 mode tcp balance source server worker0 worker0.ocp4.example.com:443 check inter 1s server worker1 worker1.ocp4.example.com:443 check inter 1s listen ingress-router-80 bind *:80 mode tcp balance source server worker0 worker0.ocp4.example.com:80 check inter 1s server worker1 worker1.ocp4.example.com:80 check inter 1s ~~~- `API VIP` and `Ingress VIP` will be bypassed by this method and will not be needed for communication.- Either `API VIP` and `Ingress VIP` or both can be configured in `external load balancer` to load balance the request. Configuring only the Ingress Controller service is a common configuration option.
root_cause: - In `IPI` based baremetal installed OpenShift cluster, `load balancing` between the `master nodes` and `worker node` does not happen due to `API/Ingress VIP`, as `API VIP` and `Ingress VIP` gets attached to one `master node` and one `worker node` at a time. And due to this, all request coming for port `6443` or `80,443` is handled by the node where `API VIP` and `Ingress VIP` is attached. Therefore, for `load balancing` the request between all master and worker node, `external load balancer` can be deployed.

title: Quay Registry Crashing due to Database Index Corrupted
issue: The Quay pod log shows that every time a manifest is pushed (`PUT /v2/latitude2/gangwaymobilemiddleware/manifests/0.0.6-device`), Quay attempts to write an audit entry to the database via `LogEntry3.create`. The operation fails, errors observed:
peewee.InternalError: right sibling's left-link doesn't match

psycopg2.errors.IndexCorrupted: right sibling's left-link doesn't match Because Quay cannot write to its audit logs, the entire request fails with a `500 Internal Server Error`, preventing any image promotion or synchronisation.
resolution: Run the `REINDEX` command on the Quay PostgreSQL database. ~~~ $ oc rsh pod/example-registry-quay-database-6fd99cd974-v4l7j postgres=# \c example-registry-quay-database; example-registry-quay-database=# REINDEX INDEX logentry3_performer_id_datetime; ~~~
root_cause: When an image is pushed, Quay tries to write a Log Entry. This will fail with a 500 error when the PostgreSQL index `logentry3_performer_id_datetime` is physically corrupt.

title: Resolving Multi-Attach Error: Volume Already Exclusively Attached to One Node in RHOCP
issue: - Encounter a `Multi-Attach error` that prevents a PV from being attached to more than one node. This error is a result of the PV being exclusively attached to one node and is attempting to attach to another node simultaneously. ~~~ $ oc get events............ Type Reason Age From Message------------------------- Normal Scheduled XXXX default-scheduler Successfully assigned XXXX Warning FailedAttachVolume XXXX attachdetach-controller Multi-Attach error for volume "XXXX" Volume is already exclusively attached to one node and can't be attached to another............. ~~~- If PV is supplied from Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation (RHODF) or Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage (RHOCS), please follow this KCS [https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7000129](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7000129)
resolution: - To resolve the `Multi-Attach` error and allow successful scheduling of pods, follow these steps: ~~~ Identify the Affected PV: $ oc describe pv ~~~- Determine which node is holding the PV. Find this information in the PV's status section of the describe output. ~~~ Name: my-persistent-volume Labels: Annotations: Finalizers: [kubernetes.io/pv-protection] StorageClass: my-storage-class Status: Bound Claim: my-persistent-claim-1/my-namespace Reclaim Policy: Retain Access Modes: RWO (ReadWriteOnce) VolumeMode: Filesystem Capacity: 10Gi Node Affinity: Message: Source: Type: HostPath (bare host directory) Path: /my/host/path HostPathType: DirectoryOrCreate Events: ~~~- `Remove` inappropriate attachments. If the PV is `mistakenly` attached to the `wrong` node or has `lingering` attachments, the attachment can be `identified and removed` using the steps mentioned in the [solution](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4651451).- Check for pod `affinity/anti-affinity`` rules review pod definitions for any node [affinity or anti-affinity](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.12/nodes/scheduling/nodes-scheduler-node-affinity.html) rules that might be affecting the pod scheduling. These rules can force pods to specific nodes and may contribute to Multi-Attach errors.
root_cause: The PV in question is already `bound and attached` to a `specific` node, and attempting to attach it to another node concurrently. This can occur due to misconfigurations, manual interference, or other unexpected issues in the cluster.

title: Is it supported to delete the default virtualization templates in Openshift Virtualization?
issue: It is not possible to delete or edit the default virtualization templates that get installed with the OpenShift Virtualization Operator.
Is there any option to delete these default templates, or edit template to point to custom images, or hide the existing default templates so they are not presented as an option in the console.
resolution: * The template are available in the openshift namespace so customized templates can be removed but Red Hat supplied templates cannot be removed. Refer [11.5. Deleting virtual machine templates](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.13/html/virtualization/virtual-machine-templates#virt-deleting-vm-template) * As a workaround, one can change the templates project to a "private" project that is not shared with the end users.
root_cause: * The possibility is in discussion with the engineering team in jira: [Option to delete default template in Openshift Virtualization](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CNV-56584)

title: RHCOS installation via PXE reboots repeatedly and returns to the PXE menu
issue: - When installing Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS (RHCOS) via PXE, the server reboots and returns to the PXE boot menu in an infinite loop.- The installed OS does not start after the installation process finished.- Console logs show SELinux "denied" messages before the server reboots. e.g., ~~~ avc: denied {create} for pid=1561 comm="mkdir" name="mdadm.conf.d" scontext=system_u:system_r:coreos_installer_t:s0 tcontext=system_u:object_r:mdadm_conf_t:s0 tclass=dir permissive=1 ~~~
resolution: Change the BIOS/UEFI boot order settings on the physical server.- Set the local hard disk (where RHCOS is installed) to a higher priority than the PXE network interface.- Once the installation is complete, the server must boot from the local disk instead of starting the PXE installer again.
root_cause: The installation finishes successfully, but the server starts the PXE process again because the network boot has a higher priority in the BIOS/UEFI settings. **NOTE:** The SELinux "denied" messages in the logs are running in "permissive" mode (permissive=1). This means the messages are recorded, but they do not stop the installation.

title: NFD pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff and Error due to operand image version mismatch after OpenShift 4.19 upgrade
issue: nfd-master and nfd-worker pods fail to start after upgrading to OpenShift Container Platform 4.19.
Nfd pods are stuck in `Error` and `CrashLoopBackOff` states.
Nfd components continue to run with an outdated operand image that does not match the upgraded cluster version.
The nfd Operator does not automatically update the operand image during or after the upgrade.
resolution: To resolve the issue related to the Node Feature Discovery custom resource using an incorrect or outdated operand image, follow the steps below: 1. Export the existing NFD Custom Resource: ~~~ $ oc get nodefeaturediscovery-n openshift-nfd-o yaml > nfd-cr.yaml ~~~ 2. Delete the current NFD CR ~~~ $ oc delete nodefeaturediscovery-n openshift-nfd ~~~ 3. Edit the exported YAML Open the `nfd-cr.yaml` file and perform the following changes:- Remove the entire `status` section.- Clean up Kubernetes-generated `metadata` fields (`resourceVersion`,`uid,creationTimestamp`,`generation`,`managedFields` (if present))- Remove the `image` field under `spec.operand` ~~~ spec: enableTaints: false instance: "" operand: image: registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-node-feature-discovery-rhel9@sha256:d85281ce1f44d9d97dc7ef225074b94472b9bae1053f1d2c897a7543a38d9507 servicePort: 12000 prunerOnDelete: false ~~~ **Note**: Starting from OpenShift 4.19, the NFD Operator automatically determines and injects the correct operand image. Manually specifying the `spec.operand.image` field can lead to version mismatches and upgrade issues. 4. Reapply the updated CR ~~~ $ oc apply-f nfd-cr.yaml ~~~ 5. Ensure that the NFD components are deployed successfully: ~~~ $ oc get pods-n openshift-nfd $ oc get nodefeaturediscovery-n openshift-nfd ~~~
root_cause: * In OpenShift versions 4.12 through 4.18, the `spec.operand.image` field in the Node Feature Discovery (NFD) Custom Resource (CR) was mandatory and required an explicit image reference. * When NFD was installed via Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), this field was automatically populated with the correct operand image. However, during cluster or operator upgrades, the existing NFD CR was not automatically updated with the new image corresponding to the upgraded version. * The NFD CR continued to reference an outdated operand image. * The Operator did not override this value because it was explicitly defined in the CR. * This led to a version mismatch between the operator and operand components. This behavior caused issues such as: * Inconsistent or failed upgrades * Potential pod failures or degraded states * Manual intervention required to update the image Although this behavior was corrected starting in OpenShift 4.19 (where `spec.operand.image` is optional and automatically managed by the operator if not specified), clusters upgraded from earlier versions may still retain the stale, user-defined image field, leading to continued issues unless manually remediated.

title: How to disable self-provisioning for authenticated users in RHOCP 4
issue: - The `self-provisioners` ClusterRoleBinding is automatically reconciled and restored by the API server after manual deletion or subject modification.
resolution: 1. Disable automatic reconciliation for the `self-provisioners` ClusterRoleBinding by setting the `autoupdate` annotation to `false`: ~~~ $ oc annotate clusterrolebinding self-provisioners rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate=false--overwrite ~~~ 2. Remove the subjects from the binding to disable the self-provisioning capability for authenticated users: ~~~ $ oc patch clusterrolebinding self-provisioners--type=merge-p '{"subjects":[]}' ~~~ **Note:** After disabling the self-provisioner role binding, users will no longer be able to create projects/namespaces independently. Administrators must manually assign the `self-provisioner` ClusterRole to specific users or groups whenever project creation permissions are required.
root_cause: The OpenShift API server periodically reconciles default RBAC objects to maintain the platform's bootstrap configuration. This process is governed by the `rbac.authorization.kubernetes.io/autoupdate` annotation, which is set to `true` by default for the `self-provisioners` binding.

title: How to create token using service account for Observability API
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - How to create `token` using service account to query `metrics` using the Observability API.
resolution: To create the token using `ServiceAccount`, use the below steps. **Step 1: Create the ServiceAccount** ~~~ $ oc create serviceaccount metrics-reader-n open-cluster-management-observability ~~~ **Step 2: Grant Permissions to the `ServiceAccount`** The `rbac-query-proxy` requires the ServiceAccount to have permissions to `get` and `list` namespaces. Create a `ClusterRole` that grants this specific right, and a `ClusterRoleBinding` to attach it to new ServiceAccount. Follow the below `rbac.yaml` file as an example. ~~~ apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: name: rbac-query-proxy-accessor rules:- apiGroups: [""] resources: ["namespaces"] verbs: ["get", "list"]--- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: name: rbac-query-proxy-accessor-binding roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: ClusterRole name: rbac-query-proxy-accessor subjects:- kind: ServiceAccount name: metrics-reader namespace: open-cluster-management-observability ~~~ Apply the file to `hub` cluster. ~~~ $ oc apply-f sa-metrics-rbac.yaml ~~~ **Step 3: Generate the ServiceAccount Token** ~~~ $ oc create token metrics-reader-n open-cluster-management-observability--duration=24h ~~~ **Note:-** To create a `long-lived` secret token for `legacy applications`, if an external application requires a `permanent` token, create a `secret` annotated to manually hold the ServiceAccount token. Create the Secret using below yaml. ~~~ apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token metadata: name: metrics-reader-token namespace: open-cluster-management-observability annotations: kubernetes.io/service-account.name: "metrics-reader" ~~~ Apply the secret. ~~~ oc apply-f ~~~ **Step 4: Extract the generated token** ~~~ export TOKEN=$(oc get secret metrics-reader-token-n open-cluster-management-observability-o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64-d) ~~~
root_cause: While querying metrics through the RHOCP `rbac-query-proxy` route with the `Observability` external API, OAuth access token is needed. The token must be associated with a user or service account, which has permission to get namespaces.
