title: Kube API Server insecure port 6080 on OpenShift 4
issue: > ***Disclaimer:*

Links contained herein to external website(s) are provided for convenience only. Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.
What is the purpose of Kube API Server insecure port `6080` in OpenShift 4 clusters?
How to remediate Kube API Server insecure port flag against API Server on OpenShift Container Platform?
How to remediate [Kubernetes STIG- V-242386- Kube API Server insecure port](https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/kubernetes/2025-05-16/finding/V-242388) finding on OpenShift Container Platform?
Received the following flag while running Kubernetes CIS benchmarks against OpenShift Container Platform 4: ~~~ 1.2.18 Ensure that the--insecure-port argument is set to 0 ~~~
resolution: No configuration change is required to remediate the Kubernetes CIS benchmark flag for the Kube API Server: * The OpenShift `kube-apiserver` only listens and securely serves via port `6443`. * The `kube-apiserver-insecure-readyz` container listens on port `6080`, but does not expose anything other than the `/readyz` (health check). The health check is exposed via `insecure-port` flag because some load balancers do not support `https`.
root_cause: The OpenShift `kube-apiserver` is served over `https` with authentication and authorization; the secure API endpoint is bound to `0.0.0.0:6443` by default. By default the `insecure-port` argument is set to `0` for OpenShift versions older than 4.10: ~~~ $ oc get configmap config-n openshift-kube-apiserver-ojson | jq-r '.data["config.yaml"]' | jq '.apiServerArguments["insecure-port"]' ["0"] ~~~ For OpenShift versions newer than 4.10, the `insecure-port` itself has been removed. So the OpenShift `kube-apiserver` does not have the option to listen to insecure port. The `kube-apiserver-insecure-readyz` container listens on port `6080` and does not expose anything other than the `/readyz` (health check), because some load balancers do not support `https`: ~~~ $ oc get pod kube-apiserver-[pod_name]-n openshift-kube-apiserver-o yaml [...]- args:---insecure-port=6080---delegate-url=https://localhost:6443/readyz command:- cluster-kube-apiserver-operator- insecure-readyz image: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev@sha256:64ba53b7a043a40ccad89bd65a063b49be371c5e60b7e0a8a0e50e6791ddc598 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: kube-apiserver-insecure-readyz ports:- containerPort: 6080 hostPort: 6080 protocol: TCP resources: requests: cpu: 5m memory: 50Mi securityContext: readOnlyRootFilesystem: true terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log terminationMessagePolicy: FallbackToLogsOnError [...] ~~~

However, the default `backup-restore-enabled` policy is triggering an `oadp-channel-validation` violation with the following description. ~~~ The version of the redhat-oadp-operator operator installed in the open-cluster-management-backup namespace is lower than the supported version set by the backup and restore operator Helm chart. ~~~

title: Assisted-installer cluster installation times out in OCM after one hour.
issue: An assisted cluster installation initiated through the Red Hat `OpenShift Cluster Manager (OCM)` console times out on the assisted installation page, even if the background process eventually succeeds.
resolution: - This is as per the design. This behavior occurs because the OpenShift Cluster Manager has a hard-coded `1-hour` timeout for the assisted installation page. If the installation fails to complete within this window (e.g., due to limited network bandwidth), the UI will report a failure.- To resolve this issue, use one of the following methods: **Method 1: Request a Soft Limit Adjustment** If your organization consistently requires more than one hour for cluster installations, you can request an increase to this limit. 1. [Open a support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new) with Red Hat Support. 2. Request that a "soft limit" for cluster installation be applied to your specific Organization ID. **Method 2: Manual Completion (Workaround)** If the installation is successful in the background despite the UI timeout, you can complete the process manually: 1. Manually reboot the nodes if they have not done so already. 2. Manually approve any pending Certificate Signing Requests (CSRs) to allow the nodes to join the cluster. 3. If necessary, scale down the machine sets to the required number of replicas.
root_cause: The OpenShift Cluster Manager assisted installation web interface has a hard-coded timeout limit of one hour. In environments with slow network bandwidth, the installation may exceed this limit, causing the OCM console to display a "Failed" status even if the backend process continues.

title: OpenShift Marketplace is blank and pods in ImagePullBackOff status
issue: - How to resolve ImagePullBackOff in openshift-marketplace namespace?- How to fix blank OpenShift Marketplace page in web console?- How to update registry credentials for the openshift-marketplace namespace?
resolution: **Step 1:** Create new `secret` with proper credentials: ~~~ oc create secret docker-registry redhat-registry-pullsecret \--docker-server=registry.redhat.io \--docker-username=' ' \--docker-password=' ' \--docker-email=' ' \-n openshift-marketplace ~~~ **Step 2: ** Patch the `service account` **marketplace-operator**: ~~~ oc patch serviceaccount marketplace-operator \-n openshift-marketplace \-p '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"redhat-registry-pullsecret"}]}' ~~~
root_cause: The **Operator Lifecycle Manager** (OLM) and the **Marketplace Operator** rely on `CatalogSources` to populate the OperatorHub. These catalogs (Red Hat, Certified, etc.) are pulled as container images from `registry.redhat.io`. The issue occurs when: 1. The credentials in the `openshift-marketplace` namespace are missing, expired, or invalid. 2. The `marketplace-operator` ServiceAccount is not correctly linked to a valid pull secret for the Red Hat registry. 3. The cluster-wide global pull secret is not inherited by the marketplace namespace, preventing the `index-image` from being downloaded.

title: OpenShift Cluster Monitoring degraded on hosted cluster when MultiCluster Observability Addon is enabled
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: After installing with or importing an OpenShift cluster into Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 2.15.0, monitoring on the hosted cluster is in degraded state: ``` $ oc get clusteroperator monitoring NAME VERSION AVAILABLE PROGRESSING DEGRADED SINCE MESSAGE monitoring 4.18.27 False True True 6d19h UpdatingPrometheus: Prometheus "openshift-monitoring/k8s": NoPodReady: shard 0: pod prometheus-k8s-0: containers with incomplete status: [init-config-reloader]... ``` Looking at the Prometheus pods in namespace `openshift-monitoring`, both pods are stuck at the `Init` step: ``` $ oc--namespace openshift-monitoring get pods--selector prometheus=k8s prometheus-k8s-0 0/6 Init:0/1 0 2m27s prometheus-k8s-1 0/6 Init:0/1 0 2m24s ``` Events in the `openshift-monitoring` namespace show failed secret mounts: ``` $ oc--namespace openshift-monitoring get events LAST SEEN TYPE REASON OBJECT MESSAGE 57m Warning FailedMount pod/prometheus-k8s-0 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "secret-hub-alertmanager-router-ca": secret "hub-alertmanager-router-ca" not found 53m Warning FailedMount pod/prometheus-k8s-0 MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "secret-observability-alertmanager-accessor": secret "observability-alertmanager-accessor" not found ``` However, secrets containing `hub-alertmanager-router-ca` and `observability-alertmanager-accessor` exist: ``` $ oc--namespace openshift-monitoring get secrets | grep hub-alertmanager-router-ca hub-alertmanager-router-ca-xyz123 Opaque 1 6d $ oc--namespace openshift-monitoring get secrets | grep observability-alertmanager-accessor observability-alertmanager-accessor-xyz123 Opaque 1 6d ```
resolution: **Fix Provided in New Release:** Red Hat investigated this issue in bug report [ACM-27722](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ACM-27722) and delivered a fix in RHACM 2.15.1 through errata [RHBA-2026:1074](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2026:1074). If this issue still occurs in your environment after updating, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution. If this issue occurs but the MultiCluster Observability Addon is not enabled, refer to [KCS 7026005](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7026005).
root_cause: As part of changes for the ACM multicluster global hub feature, the generation of alertmanager secret names was changed. This led to incorrectly referenced secret names in the `additionalAlertManagerConfigs` stanza in ConfigMap `cluster-monitoring-config`.

title: The observability-controller ManagedClusterAddOn for local-cluster is stuck in "Progressing" due to "mimical" version
product: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
issue: - The observability-controller ManagedClusterAddOn for local-cluster is stuck in "Progressing" due to "mimical" version.- On ACM 2.15.1 with OCP 4.19.23 as the hub cluster, the observability-controller ManagedClusterAddOn for local-cluster is permanently stuck in Progressing: True / Available: Unknown. All other clusters (managed spokes) are healthy. Metrics are confirmed flowing.
resolution: - Wrong namespace lookup: MCO looks for the ManagedClusterAddon in namespace open-cluster-management-observability instead of local-cluster when processing the hub cluster.- The openshiftVersion: "mimical": MCO resolves OCP 4.19's internal codename "mimical" for local-cluster (reading from ClusterVersion internally) rather than the version string "4.19.23" from the ManagedCluster label. Spoke clusters correctly show openshiftVersion: "4.19.23" and "4.20.14". This version codename appears to trigger the wrong namespace lookup code path in the hub self-management logic.- Bug [ACM-31062](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ACM-31062) is raised to check this issue further.For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) with Red Hat Support.

title: OpenShift Serverless Metrics Endpoints are Unsecured and Accessible from Any Pod
issue: - The `ServiceMonitors` `knative-operator-metrics`, `knative-openshift-metrics-3` and `knative-openshift-ingress-metrics` expose all metrics details without authorization and without traffic encryption (plain `HTTP`)- Any `pod` with general network access within the cluster can retrieve all cluster-wide metrics exposed by these targets.
resolution: - This behavior is currently expected and is a known architectural trade-off to enable integration with OpenShift's monitoring system.- There is no immediate plan to enforce `mTLS` on these endpoints until the underlying `User Workload Monitoring` component fully supports secure metrics scraping. A [request for enhancement](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OBSDA-200) is being tracked to incorporate security measures for these endpoints in a future release. ### Workaround A workaround based on `NetworkPolicies` may be implemented to secure the targets from [other pods and namespaces in the cluster in a multi-tenant environment](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/networking/network-security#nw-networkpolicy-deny-all-multi-network-policy_creating-network-policy): 1. As cluster administrator, in the `openshift-serverless` namespace, create a deny-by-default `NetworkPolicy`. ~~~ oc project openshift-serverless # create deny-by-default NetworkPolicy cat <
root_cause: - The metrics endpoints for the mentioned Knative services are intentionally left unsecured (using `HTTP` rather than `HTTPS`/`TLS`) to comply with the requirements for the built-in OpenShift `User Workload Monitoring` (UWM) component.- Currently, the UWM architecture does not natively support scraping metrics from endpoints secured using mutual `TLS` (`mTLS`) or other authentication mechanisms, necessitating the unsecured configuration for proper monitoring integration.

title: egressIP GARP sent by incorrect node after reboot in RHCOP 4
issue: - After migrating the openshift CNI from OpenShiftSDN to OVNKubernetes Trident cannot connect to the storage using the egressip.- Neighbors in the network have the incorrect ARP record for the egressIP when the assigned node is rebooted.- Gratuitous ARP requests are sent by the incorrect node for egressIP.
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in: | RHOCP Release | Bug | Fixed version | Errata | |---------|---------|---------|---------| | 4.21 | [OCPBUGS-42303](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-42303) | **4.21.1** | [RHSA-2026:2129](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:2129) | | 4.20 | [OCPBUGS-62273](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-62273) | **4.20.1** | [RHSA-2025:19003](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:19003) | | 4.19 | [OCPBUGS-62670](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-62670) | **4.19.18** | [RHBA-2025:19301](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:19301) | | 4.18 | [OCPBUGS-62671](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-62671) | **4.18.27** | [RHSA-2025:19047](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2025:19047) | | 4.17 | [OCPBUGS-63154](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-63154) | **4.17.44** | [RHBA-2025:21225](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:21225) | | 4.16 | [OCPBUGS-63155](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-63155) | **4.16.53** | [RHBA-2025:21825](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2025:21825) | ### Workaround 1 {#workaround} 1. Identify the assigned node: ~~~ $ oc get egressip NAME EGRESSIPS ASSIGNED NODE ASSIGNED EGRESSIPS egressips-prod 10.0.0.1 worker0.example.com 10.0.0.1 ~~~ 2. Restart the `ovn-controller` container on the identified node: ~~~ $ oc debug node/worker0.example.com-q-- chroot /host bash-c 'crictl stop $(crictl ps--name ovn-controller-q)' ~~~ ### Workaround 2 {#workaround2} Create a `MachineConfig` that delete the OVN database at every node restart to avoid `ovn-controller` starts with stale data, this workaround does not work when the issue is caused by `ovnkube-node` pod restart: ~~~ apiVersion: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/v1 kind: MachineConfig metadata: labels: machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: name: 90-bug-ocpbugs-42303-mitigation spec: config: ignition: version: 3.2.0 storage: files:- contents: source: data:,%23%21%2Fbin%2Fbash%0A%0Arm%20-f%20%2Fvar%2Flib%2Fovn-ic%2Fetc%2Fovn%2A.db mode: 493 overwrite: true path: /usr/local/bin/refresh-ovndb.sh systemd: units:- contents: | [Unit] # This service was created to workaround the bug OCPBUGS-42303 # The objective is deleting the ovndb before the ovs-configuration.service # Once the ovndbs are removed, the ovn-controller is going to create a new one Requires=ovs-configuration.service Before=ovs-configuration.service [Service] # Need oneshot to delay kubelet Type=oneshot ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/refresh-ovndb.sh StandardOutput=journal+console StandardError=journal+console [Install] RequiredBy=ovs-configuration.service enabled: true name: workaround-ocpbugs42303.service ~~~ ### Workaround 3 {#workaround3}- To prevent Gratuitous ARP (GARP) announcements caused by frequent restarts of the ovnkube-node pod, consider applying the following workaround.- Increase the value of `reachabilityTotalTimeoutSeconds` by modifying the networks.operator configuration, as shown below. For more details, refer to the [official documentation.](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/networking/ovn-kubernetes-network-plugin#nw-egress-ips-config-object_configuring-egress-ips-ovn) ~~~ apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1 kind: Network metadata: name: cluster spec: clusterNetwork:- cidr: 10.128.0.0/14 hostPrefix: 23 defaultNetwork: ovnKubernetesConfig: egressIPConfig: reachabilityTotalTimeoutSeconds: 45 ## <---- tunable gatewayConfig: routingViaHost: false genevePort: 6081 ~~~- This changes the `configMap` that holds the `OVN-K` configuration started by the `ovnkube` services. The containers automatically get the changes and reload to start the new configuration. This can be confirmed by running the following commands: ~~~ $ oc get configmap ovnkube-config-o yaml-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes | grep egressip-reachability-total-timeout $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes exec-c ovnkube-controller-- cat /run/ovnkube-config/ovnkube.conf $ oc-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes exec-c ovnkube-cluster-manager-- cat /run/ovnkube-config/ovnkube.conf ~~~- Optionally, if for some reason after a while the changes are not seen in the container or the new timeout value is not being respected, do a rolling restart the `ovnkube-control-plane` and `ovnkube-node` pod by running the command below: ~~~ $ oc rollout restart daemonset ovnkube-node-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes $ oc rollout restart deployment ovnkube-control-plane-n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ~~~- The value for `reachabilityTotalTimeoutSeconds` accepts integer values from 0 to 60. A value of 0 disables the reachability check of the egressIP node. Values of 1 to 60 correspond to the duration in seconds between probes sending the reachability check for the node.- Modifying this value ensures that the egress IP does not move to another egress-assignable node if the pod restarts and comes back within the specified timeout (e.g., 45 seconds in the example above).- If the pod takes longer than the configured timeout to restart, the egress IP will be reassigned to another eligible node. **Note**: The value `45` is used here as an example and can be tuned based on environment. The ideal value may vary depending on the platform's CPU and memory load, as these affect the pod restart time. In test environments, a 45-second timeout has proven effective.
root_cause: After a node assigned to an egressIP reboot the `ovn-controller` container may start before `ovnkube-controller`, causing the `ovn-controller` to start with the incorrect OVN SouthBound DB configuration because `ovnkube-controller` still has not updated the OVN DB. The `ovn-controller` container generally sends 5 Gratuitous ARP requests for announcing the egressIP and when it starts it looks at the OVN SouthBound database information to send them. This issue is particularly problematic when in the infrastructure network is enabled a mechanisms for caching the ARP records based on the broadcast GARP requests, for example Arista networks. In other scenario this issue does not cause any disruption.

title: Support for Java 9 / Java 10 / Java 11 with JBoss EAP
product: Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform
issue: Is there any roadmap for Java 9 / 10 support with JBoss EAP?
JBoss EAP support for Oracle JDK 1.9.0_x
JBoss EAP support for Oracle JDK 1.9
We would like to know if JDK 9 would be supported?
Support for Java 10 in JBoss EAP

The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*--- Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) 7.2 was tested in JDK 11, see [Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) 7 Supported Configurations](https://access.redhat.com/articles/2026253) for details. When JBoss EAP 7.2 was released, the maintenance stream has shifted to EAP 7.2 and there will be no more cumulative patch updates for [7.1](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3824062) and [7.0](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3377221) and thus there are no plans to certify these. There are no plans to certify EAP 6.4 on new JDK's as EAP 6.4 is end of life (EOL) June 2019 [Red Hat JBoss Middleware Product Update and Support Policy](https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/jboss_notes#p_eap) Oracle JDK 9 and JDK 10 had a 6 month lifecycle and is End of Life (EOL) in March 2018 / September 2018 [1], therefore there are no plans to certify JBoss EAP on JDK 9 / JDK 10 which is EOL. Oracle JDK 8 is ending public updates on January 2019 [1], JDK 11 the long term support release is expected to be released in September 2018. As per [OpenJDK Life Cycle and Support Policy [2]](https://access.redhat.com/articles/1299013), support for **OpenJDK 8** will end in June 2023. See also [[3] Is OpenJDK supported on Windows](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3116731) **Related Solutions** [[1] Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap](http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/java/eol-135779.html) [[2] OpenJDK Life Cycle and Support Policy](https://access.redhat.com/articles/1299013) [[3] Is OpenJDK supported on Windows?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3116731)

title: The autoscale feature in the OpenTelemetryCollector fails to scale the collector deployment despite high resource utiliization
issue: - When using the autoscale feature for the `OpenTelemetryCollector` in deployment mode, the `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` (HPA) that gets created fails to scale the `collector` deployment when the resource utilization exceeds the target utilization.- The `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` (HPA) status desired replica value increases, but the actual `collector` replica count remains unchanged.
resolution: - Upgrade the to `Red Hat Build of OpenTelemetry` 3.8 which is available in operator `version 0.140.0-1`- A workaround to overcome this issue can be implemented by removing the `minReplicas` setting from `.spec.autoscale` in the `OpenTelemetryCollector` custom resource (CR).

Red Hat has not reviewed the links and is not responsible for the content or its availability. The inclusion of any link to an external website does not imply endorsement by Red Hat of the website or their entities, products or services. You agree that Red Hat is not responsible or liable for any loss or expenses that may result due to your use of (or reliance on) the external site or content.*- This is a [known defect](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/issues/4400) in the operator for versions up to `0.135.0-1`.- This bug causes the HPA to incorrectly retrieve the `minReplicas` setting instead of the `.spec.replicas` parameter that the HPA modifies.- A fix for this issue has been incorporated upstream in `0.140.0-1`, and is available with `Red Hat Build of OpenTelemetry` 3.8

title: Defining retention for logs in LokiStack on RHOCP 4
issue: - As per [enabling stream-based retention with Loki](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/logging/log-storage#logging-loki-retention_cluster-logging-loki), it is recommended to define `retention` period under `spec.limits.global.retention` for global retention and `spec.limits.tenants.[tenant_name].retention` for tenant based retention (`application`, `infrastructure`, `audit`). How does this prune data from the object storage bucket?- Is there any other alternative way to set `retention` for logs storage in object storage bucket?- We would like assistance deleting old logs stored in Loki
resolution: If there is no retention set on S3 bucket or within the [`LokiStack` CR](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/configuring_logging/configuring-lokistack-storage#logging-loki-retention_configuring-the-log-store), then the objects are never deleted from the backend object storage. ### Log retention recommendation It is **recommended** to set retention on the object storage provider side for deletion of the objects as it is more efficient in terms of costs: computational and money. The reason is that pruning the objects is a cost free task provided by the storage provider. When it is set in the Loki side:- The Compactor runs at every `compactor.compaction-interval` and the objects are marked firstly for deletion and later deleted asynchronously. This creates a scenario of sweeper lag which means there could be logs beyond the mention retention time.- The API calls for getting the chunks and performing deletions could incur costs in Cloud Environments. > **Important note:** when setting retention on the object storage provider, the `retention` specification is **not required** on the `LokiStack` definition. ### Configuring log retention in Loki If for any reason it is not desired to configure the log retention in the S3 bucket as recommended, it is possible to configure log retention in Loki. #### Set retention by time The `spec.limits.global.retention` and `spec.limits.tenants.[tenant_name].retention` are meant to be used for `individual` (pod level) or group of `workload` (namespace level) where stream corresponds to the workload. For setting "globally" and/or "by tenant" log retention, see ["Enabling stream-based retention with Loki"](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_logging/6.4/html/configuring_logging/configuring-lokistack-storage#logging-loki-retention_configuring-the-log-store). Here is an example to configure in Loki a global log retention of 7 days: ~~~ $ oc edit LokiStack logging-loki-n openshift-logging--- OUTPUT OMMITED--- spec: limits: global: retention: days: 7---> Set the value as per requirement. managementState: Managed--- OUTPUT OMMITED--- ~~~ #### Set retention by threshold and/or size Refer to [implement threshold and/or size based retention for Loki in RHOCP 4](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7073886). ### Use cases #### Use case 1: All the logs have the same retention time If all the logs have the same retention time, the recommendation is to set the lifecycle in the object storage side and don't set any configuration in Loki #### Use case 2: Global retention and some specific tenants or stream have shorter retention time 1. Set the longest retention time in the object storage side as "Global policy" 2. Set for those streams requiring to be maintained shorter that the "Global policy" in the LokiStack Custom Resource (CR). Don't set "spec.limits.global.retention.days" in the Lokistack CR as it's already set in the object storage side as "Global policy". ### Considerations when using NooBaa as object storage backend See the article [how to configure Lifecycle policy on noobaa bucket](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7058004). > **Note:** there is a known bug in older versions [Bug 2279964- [GSS][ODF 4.12.7] noobaa bucket lifecycle policy does not delete all objects](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2279964) that explains that although object storage global retention is configured in noobaa, not all objects are deleted and causes storage bucket size to grow as objects are not being purged. This is fixed with this [errata](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4591) starting in ODF 4.16. In older versions, the only effective option is to set retention on Loki side.
root_cause: It is **recommended** to set retention on the object storage provider side for deletion of the objects as it is more efficient in terms of costs.

title: Image signatures missing after mirroring images using oc-mirror plugin v2
issue: Unable to see images signatures generated in ` /working-dir/cluster-resources/` after mirroring images.

Why image signatures are not getting generated after [mirroring images for a disconnected installation by using the `oc-mirror` plugin v2](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/disconnected_environments/about-installing-oc-mirror-v2).
resolution: In `oc-mirror` plugin v2, adding flag `--remove-signatures=false` while mirroring images is required to also mirror the image signatures. For the command to run with the above flag, it is required that all the images have signatures. In some cases, for third-party operators, there could be images with missing signatures as described in [missing image signatures while mirroring certified operators from `registry.connect.redhat.com`](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7130655).
root_cause: In `oc-mirror` plugin v2, it is needed to add a flag `--remove-signatures=false` while mirroring images to also mirror the image signatures. Refer to [enabling signature mirroring for oc-mirror plugin v2](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/disconnected_environments/about-installing-oc-mirror-v2#oc-mirror-signature-mirroring-procedure_about-installing-oc-mirror-v2) for additional information.

title: OpenShift Upgrade Fails with internal server error and stuck Terminating namespaces due to Authentication Operator `managementState` being set to `Removed`
issue: During an upgrade from OpenShift 4.14 to 4.15 (and eventually 4.16), the cluster becomes unstable, the web console becomes inaccessible and throws 503 internal server errors. The `kube-apiserver` pods enter a `CrashLoopBackOff`, and essential namespaces like `openshift-authentication` and `openshift-oauth-apiserver` are stuck in a `Terminating` state. Even if these namespaces are deleted, they are immediately recreated and then terminated again in an endless loop.
The `openshift-authentication` and `openshift-oauth-apiserver` namespaces are stuck in a Terminating state.
These namespaces are being recreated and immediately transitioning back into the `Terminating` state in a loop.
`kube-apiserver` pods enter a `CrashLoopBackOff`.
Upgrade progress stalls (e.g., "754 of 881 done").
resolution: To break the termination loop and restore the cluster to a healthy state, the Authentication operator must be moved back to the `Managed` state. 1. Edit the Operator State: Modify the Authentication operator configuration to ensure it is actively managing its resources: ``` oc edit authentication.operator.openshift.io cluster ``` 2. Update the Configuration Spec: Locate the `managementState` field and change it from `Removed` to `Managed`: ``` spec: managementState: Managed ``` 3. Monitor the Recovery: Wait about 5 to 10 minutes. Once the state is changed, the operator will stop trying to delete the namespaces. The `kube-apiserver` should find the necessary OAuth metadata, its pods should move to `Running`, and the upgrade will proceed.
root_cause: The cluster entered this state because the Authentication operator's `managementState` was set to `Removed`. Although the Authentication operator does not support the `Removed` state, setting it this way triggers a logic conflict: * The **Workload Controller** attempts to delete the operand `openshift-authentication` and `openshift-oauth-apiserver` namespaces because the state is `Removed`. * Simultaneously, the **Static Resource Controller** immediately tries to recreate these namespaces because they are defined as required in the operator assets. The Static Resource Controller sees these as required and recreates them. * This creates a race condition (create/terminatei loop) that deletes the `oauth-metadata` ConfigMap file during the process, causing `kube-apiserver` to crash and fail to start because it cannot find the mandatory metadata file and blocking the overall cluster upgrade. The issue is a library logic bug where a `workload.go` controller in `library-go` forcefully deletes namespaces when `managementState` is `Removed`, even if the operator doesn't support that state. This is tracked under CNTRLPLANE-782.

title: Missing image signatures while mirroring certified operators from registry.connect.redhat.com
issue: - Getting errors while mirroring third party operators from the Red Hat certified operator index ``` operator@sha256:813915784f144314a8cd70784ba5c073d137934d422f49c970e2ee668a7a90a9 (Operator bundles: [vault-secrets-operator.v0.10.0]- Operators: [vault-secrets-operator]) error: reading signatures: reading manifest sha256-813915784f144314a8cd70784ba5c073d137934d422f49c970e2ee668a7a90a9.sig in registry.connect.redhat.com/hashicorp/vault-secrets-operator: name unknown: Image not found ```- These errors are not allowing the `oc-mirror` command to complete successfully ``` oc-mirror-c isc.yaml--workspace file:///apps/ocp/oc-mirror/mirror docker://internal-registry.example.com/platform--v2 authfile auth.json--dest-tls-verify=false--remove-signatures=false--cache-dir /tmp/mirrorcache/--parallel-images 20--parallel-layers 20--log-level debug ```
resolution: As the signature is missing in operators provided in `registry.connect.redhat.com`, and that registry is for third-party products, the sustainable solution is to reach out to the respective third-party vendor and request the signatures to be provided during the release process. #### Workaround There are two possible workarounds:- Remove the offending entries from the `ImageSetConfiguration` file.- Run the `oc-mirror` command without `--remove-signatures=false` (or with `--remove-signatures`).
root_cause: The `--remove-signatures=false` parameter causes the `oc-mirror` to fail on images that are not packaged with a signature object, hence this is not a bug in `oc-mirror` but missing signature in the image. The `registry.connect.redhat.com` registry is populated by third-party vendors as explained in [Red Hat Container Registry Authentication](https://access.redhat.com/articles/RegistryAuthentication). Also, as explained in the [mirroring and verifying image signatures in oc-mirror plugin v2](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.21/html/disconnected_environments/about-installing-oc-mirror-v2#oc-mirror-signature-mirroring_about-installing-oc-mirror-v2) documentation: > *Because the certified, marketplace, and community catalogs contain third-party content, Red Hat does not ensure the availability or validity of their signatures. In such cases, you must disable signature mirroring.*

title: How to change the job execution path on a single Execution Node without modifying the job execution path setting in Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform?
issue: - Default for job execution path is `/tmp` and this directory is mounted with `noexec`- Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform is running in an OpenShift / Kubernetes environment
resolution: *The following information has been provided by Red Hat, but is outside the scope of the posted Service Level Agreements and supported procedures. The information is provided as-is and any configuration settings or installed applications made from the information in this article could make the Operating System unsupported by Red Hat Global Support Services. The intent of this article is to provide information to accomplish the system's needs.* *Red Hat is aware of this feature request, currently under review in RFE [AAPRFE-2464](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/AAPRFE-2464). If this feature is required, open a support case on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.* This KCS assumes the directory will be `/awxjobs` and the user running the jobs is `awx`; names are arbitrary. Make sure that job execution path directory will live on a partition that is not mounted with `noexec`.- Create a directory that will be used for job executions ~~~ mkdir-p /awxjobs && chown awx:awx /awxjobs ~~~- Add the following to `/etc/tmpfiles.d/aap_receptor.conf` ~~~ R! /awxjobs/storage-run-* ~~~- Modify the `receptor.service` file ~~~ systemctl edit receptor.service ~~~- Add the following contents in the opening space in the output ~~~ [Service] User=awx Group=awx BindPaths=/awxjobs:/tmp:rbind ~~~- Reload systemd and restart receptor ~~~ systemctl daemon-reload ~~~ ~~~ systemctl restart receptor.service ~~~
root_cause: At the moment, Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform doesn't allow for changing the job execution path for individual execution nodes or instance groups. The setting `Settings-> Automation Execution-> Job-> Job Execution Path` applies to the entire system. This can be a problem when working in an environment where Ansible Automation Platform runs in OpenShift / Kubernetes and the Execution Nodes are not.

title: DevSpaces container in container usage and requirement
issue: Red Hat DevSpaces Operator container in container requirements
resolution: It comes to if the user wants any rootless user to work with containers it will fail, only the root user at this point can run a container because the root user can still create the namespaces needed which were listed. See more details on [Dev Spaces 3.x- Administration Guide](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_dev_spaces/3.27/html/administration_guide/assembly_configuring-workspaces-globally_administration_guide#proc_enabling-container-run-capabilities_administration_guide).
root_cause: ### FAQ **Q1. Is there a security concern here? If not, can we provide documentation saying there is no security concern?** A1. Not any more concern than running as the root user in general, at this point *only* root can run containers. **Q2. We are running nested container in DevSpaces (want to have option to run podman compose inside devspaces). With the nested container feature enabled, will we be able to turn off namespace root?** A2: Per discussions, it is a strict requirement unless user run the workspaces as privileged containers(i.e. as the root user) **Q3. Are there any option in Dev Spaces' Che cluster level to disable namespace root?** A3. There are settings like `spec:components:cheServer:extraProperties:CHE_INFRASTRUCTURE_KUBERNETES_CLUSTER__ROLE__TYPE: "none"`, which prevents Dev Spaces from requesting or using ClusterRoles. It will only be able to manage resources within the namespaces it is explicitly granted access to. **Q4. Given the above, if the user disables it, what will be impact to devspaces functioning?** A4. It likely will not function unless configured to run privileged **Q5. Are there option to disable it in che cluster with no impact to current functioning?** A5. Unlikely to have off-the shelf option for this specific use case without major impact.

title: 'Session is not authenticated' error during MTV Storage Offload
issue: `disconnect host request failed with status 401: {"errors":[{"message":"Invalid session.","location_context":{"resource_type":"remote-arrays","name":"example","id":null}}]}`
`ServerFaultCode: The session is not authenticated.`
resolution: Issue is being investigated in [MTV-4935](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MTV-4935)

title: NooBaa DB pod noobaa-db-pg-0 enters CrashLoopBackOff with wrong ownership
issue: NooBaa DB pod `noobaa-db-pg-0` enters `CrashLoopBackOff` with the following error.
FATAL: data directory "/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata" has wrong ownership
resolution: ### Option 1- Change the ownership of the directory `/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata` with the desired username. 1. Start a debug session on the affected pod: ~~~ oc debug pod/noobaa-db-pg-0-n openshift-storage ~~~ 2. Check the ownership of the PostgreSQL data directory: ~~~ ls-ld /var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata ~~~ 3. Update the ownership to match the PostgreSQL user used by the container: ~~~ chown-R postgres:postgres /var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata ~~~ 4. Exit the debug session: ~~~ exit ~~~ 5. Restart the pod to verify the issue is resolved: ~~~ oc delete pod noobaa-db-pg-0-n openshift-storage ~~~ ### Option 2- If the directory ownership is correct but does not match the user configured in the Secret, update the Secret so the username matches the directory owner. 1. Check the current user configured in the Secret: ~~~ oc get secret noobaa-db-n openshift-storage-o jsonpath='{.data.user}' | base64-d ~~~ 2. Update the Secret: ~~~ oc edit secret noobaa-db-n openshift-storage ~~~ 3. Modify the user field so it matches the owner of `/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata`, and ensure values in the `data` field are base64-encoded, or use the `stringData` field with plain text ~~~ BASE64USERNAME=$(echo " " | base64) oc patch secret-n openshift-storage--type merge-p "{\"data\":{\"user\":\"${BASE64USERNAME}\"}}" ~~~ 4. Restart the pod to apply the change: ~~~ oc delete pod noobaa-db-pg-0-n openshift-storage ~~~
root_cause: The ownership of the directory `/var/lib/pgsql/data/userdata` does not match with the user data in the Secret resource.

title: df -h command hangs on nodes due to unresponsive NFS volumes
issue: - `df-h` command getting stuck while accessing specific NFS volumes in OpenShift Container Platform 4.16- `newfstatat` system call hanging on NFS directory paths within kubelet pod volumes- Strace output showing `newfstatat` stuck on various NFS merged directory paths under `/var/lib/kubelet/pods` and `/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay` directories
resolution: - Try umount this NFS manually- Also NFS could cause cluster-wide impact when unstable. If possible, use alternative options such like ODF(Ceph), csi-based storage, EBS/EFS (on AWS), Azure Disk/Files, that will provide better sustainability.
root_cause: When the pod got moved from this node, Kubernetes correctly triggered the volume cleanup process and kubelet attempted to unmount the NFS volume on the original node. However, the unmount operation depends on the Linux kernel successfully communicating with the NFS server. At that time, the NFS mount was in a blocked I/O state (for example due to NFS server or network unresponsiveness), causing the unmount system call to hang in the kernel. Because this operation cannot be interrupted, kubelet was unable to complete the unmount even though the pod had already been removed or relocated. As a result, the stale NFS mount remained on the node until the storage connectivity recovered or the mount was manually cleaned up.

title: Windows stops with MEMORY MANAGEMENT code on low latency storage
issue: Windows Virtual Machines BSOD with "MEMORY MANAGEMENT" code (0x1A).
There is no storage latency present at the time, its not [Windows stops with MEMORY MANAGEMENT code](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7132512).
Increasing or decreating the IoTimeoutValue makes no difference.
resolution: * Please upgrade the Guest drivers to virtio-win-1.9.53-0.el9_6 or later. This was fixed by [RHBA-2026:2280](https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2026:2280). * As a workaround, in In RHEL KVM, disable multiqueue in the domain XML by adding queues='1' to each virtio-blk disk: ~~~ [...] ~~~
root_cause: * This is was investigated in [RHEL-141510"MEMORY MANAGEMENT" BSOD with no storage delay and only on virtio-blk](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-141510). * There is a problem affecting virtio-blk with Multiqueue, causing the BSOD. * Similar problems exists on virtio-scsi, but its more rare.

title: Windows stops with MEMORY MANAGEMENT code
issue: Microsoft Windows running on OpenShift Virtualization has random BSODs with these codes:
0x1A- MEMORY MANAGEMENT (most common)
0x7A- KERNEL DATA INPAGE ERROR
0x50- PAGE FAULT IN NONPAGED AREA
0xEF- CRTCL PROCESS DIED
resolution: * Ensure the storage is not producing excessive IO delays.- Verify storage configuration with your storage vendor.- On the server, check for any storage errors:- For Filesystem based storage a general start of diagnosing this can be reviewed here: [Gathering data and logs to troubleshoot NFS issues](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4330981)- For Block baed storage a general start of diagnosing this can be reviewed here: [Troubleshooting performance issue in RHEL](https://access.redhat.com/articles/6965124)- If no storage delays are found, it could be a known driver bug with similar symptoms, see [Windows stops with MEMORY MANAGEMENT code on low latency storage](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7136486). * Ensure the Virtual Machine is configured with adequate RAM memory size for its workload, to avoid excessive use of pagefile. * As a workaround while storage delays are investigated, a higher timeout can be set on virtio-blk (when using VirtIO interface) and/or virtio-scsi (when using SCSI interface). In the Windows registry, set these below to REG_DWORD value higher than the default (60s), such as 120 (for 120s). But note this will prevent the BSODs as long as the delays are lower than this timeout, but may the storage issue may still be present and cause other delays and performance issues. The system may also take more time to recover from I/O issues. Storage delays should still be investigated. ~~~ HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\viostor\Parameters\IoTimeoutValue HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\vioscsi\Parameters\IoTimeoutValue ~~~
root_cause: * These stop codes usually relate to a slowdown in storage (60s or more by default), causing delayed IO during paging operations which trigger a Windows BSOD. * This was investigated in [RHEL-115745- Multiple BSODs on Windows virtual machines probably related to the storage backend](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-115745). * The CRC error (ReportPageHashError) is due to an issue with transfer length of the virtio driver during a reset (which happens on the I/O timeout of 60s from the Guest side). This is fixed in virtio-win-1.9.49-0.el9_6.iso. But this only changes the BSOD code from `MEMORY MANAGEMENT` to `CRTCL PROCESS DIED` to more appropriately reflect the situation. The main issue caused by slower storage or stuck IO remains and still ultimately causes the BSOD.

title: Deploying kubevirt-csi-infra-default on UPI OpenShift Virtualization 4.20 Clusters
issue: Deploying `kubevirt-csi-infra-default` on UPI cluster with OpenShift Virtualization
Replicating storage configuration from hypershift `kubevirt-csi-infra-default`
Lack of clear procedure or documentation for the desired deployment on specified OpenShift Container Platform version (4.20)
Inability to find relevant guides or steps for configuring storage class similar to hypershift on UPI clusters running OpenShift Virtualization
Seeking guidance on adapting the storage class configuration from hypershift to the existing UPI cluster setup on OpenShift with ODF
resolution: * As of today `15th April 2026` and current RHOCP 4.21, the deployment of `kubevirt-csi` in UPI clusters **is not supported**. * The suggested approach/workaround is to use Hypershift/HCP clusters instead of UPI.
root_cause: * UPI are in essence clusters with **no platform integration** while using `kubevirt-csi` is a platform integration feature meant for/supported on Hypershift only.

title: Scheduled VMs Unable to Connect to VNC Console on Specific Nodes
issue: - VNC console experiencing continuous buffering without error messages.
resolution: - Ensure UDP port 6081 is open on both the host firewall and any third-party firewall configured on the affected node. [Red Hat OpenShift Documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/installation_configuration/configuring-firewall#network-flow-matrix-bm_configuring-firewall)
root_cause: - OVN-Kubernetes uses GENEVE tunnels over UDP port 6081 to encapsulate and transport pod network traffic between nodes.

title: Admin Portal page returns 504 - Gateway Timeout after loading for a long time
issue: - When performing an action on the Admin Portal UI, the page takes a long time to load and eventually returns a `504- Gateway Timeout` status message.
resolution: The resolution varies depending on the root cause. See the `Root Cause` and `Diagnostic Steps` sections.- The application takes longer than the route timeout value to complete the request- Set a higher value for the timeout of the route that points to the `system-provider` service in OpenShift ~~~ $ oc get route | grep system-provider $ oc edit route ~~~ Replace: ` ` with the proper value obtained from the first command. Create the annotations: tag inside metadata or add the value below in case it already exists as in the following example for 120 seconds: ~~~ metadata: annotations: haproxy.router.openshift.io/timeout: 120s ~~~- A worker process or a pod is terminated, for example because of Out Of Memory errors- Set a higher value for the memory limit of the `system-provider` container in the `system-app` Deployment Configuration ~~~ $ oc edit dc/system-app ~~~ Increase the value of memory limits for the `system-provider` container and save the Deployment Configuration. This should trigger the pod to redeploy.- Database (MySQL) storage is full- Free up disk space or increase the Persistent Volume (PV) capacity for the `system-mysql` pod.- After resolving the storage issue, ensure the `system-provider` processes can communicate with the database normally.
root_cause: There are multiple possible root causes:- The application takes longer than the route timeout value to complete the request- The default route timeout in OpenShift is 30 seconds. If the Application takes longer to complete its task, OpenShift will return the `504- Gateway Timeout` status message once the timeout expires.- A worker process or a pod is terminated, for example because of Out Of Memory errors- In this situation even a longer timeout on the OpenShift route wouldn't help: the pod or the process was terminated and won't be able to complete its task. It's possible to understand if this is the case by analyzing the `system-provider` container's logs as described in the `Diagnostic Steps`- Database storage exhaustion- If the `system-mysql` storage is full, database queries from `system-provider` will hang or fail to complete. This causes the Ruby worker process to wait until it exceeds the internal `UNICORN_TIMEOUT` (default 40s), at which point the process is killed (SIGKILL), leading to a `504` error.

title: False Alert – CsvAbnormalFailedOver2Min in RHOCP4
issue: - Getting false alert `CsvAbnormalFailedOver2Min` in RHOCP4.
resolution: - This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in [Bug](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-66421). For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.

title: Node unable to boot with mpath disks having `root` label
issue: CoreOS node drops to emergency shell following errors mounting /sysroot
Node fails to boot with `root` disk
resolution: The node needs to either: A) Have its disks adjusted such that the `root` disk (where /sysroot exists) is the only disk with the `root` label B) Have its kernel parameters adjusted such that the `root` disk is specified by id or UUID The latter can be done on the correctly booted node using: ```sh $ rpm-ostree kargs--delete root--append root='UUID= ' ``` This will remove the original `root` key and add a new one bearing the specified UUID.
root_cause: When the `root` disk is identified via label instead of id or UUID, it can trigger a race condition that may resolve the wrong disk as the root disk, causing a failed boot if /sysroot doesn't exist on the wrongly selected device. The node's kernel parameters shoud be adjusted such that `root` is specified more specifically, i.e. removing the label from other disks, or specifying it by id or UUID.

title: OpenShift image garbage collector deletes all unused images instead of stopping at imageGCLowThresholdPercent?
issue: After the disk usage hits the `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` (e.g., 85%) and the garbage collector starts, will it stop deleting images once it reaches the `imageGCLowThresholdPercent` (e.g., 80%)?
resolution: The `image garbage collector` attempts to delete images until the `imageGCLowThresholdPercent` is reached, however the garbage collection **still continues** even if `imageGCLowThresholdPercent` if reached.- After hitting `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` The garbage collector only deletes unused images those not associated with any running or paused containers.- If unused images are still present after reaching the `imageGCLowThresholdPercent`, the collector will continue to delete them until all reclaimable (unused) images are removed.- This can result in disk usage dropping significantly below the low threshold (for example, to 33%), as the collector prioritises removing all available unused images rather than stopping precisely at the 80% mark.
root_cause: The image garbage collector will not stop precisely at the `imageGCLowThresholdPercent` if additional unused images are present, it will prune all unreferenced images once the `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` is triggered.

title: Logging Operator does not restart collectors when changed the CA in ".spec.outputs[].tls.ca.configMapName"
issue: The configmap `openshift-service-ca.crt` was updated
Configmap containing the CA to connect to Loki was updated, but the collectors were not restarted automatically failing to deliver the logs

After a change in the CA used by the collector to connect to Loki, the collectors started suddenly to fail to deliver the logs to Loki with the error: ~~~ 2026-03-01T18:59:34.312536227Z 2026-03-01T18:59:34.312487Z WARN sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=output_lokistack_audit component_type=loki}: vector::internal_events::http_client: HTTP error. error=error trying to connect: error:0A000086:SSL routines:tls_post_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed:ssl/statem/statem_clnt.c:1889:: self-signed certificate in certificate chain error_type="request_failed" stage="processing" internal_log_rate_limit=true ~~~
resolution: This issue has been reported to Red Hat engineering. It is being tracked in Bug [LOG-8631- "Logging Operator does not restart collectors when changed the CA in ".spec.outputs[].tls.ca.configMapName"](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/LOG-8631). #### Workaround 1. Restart the collector pods: ~~~ $ cr="collector" ### Modify if the clusterLogForwarder Custom Resource (CR) has a different name $ ns="openshift-logging" ### Modify if the clusterLogForwarder CR is running in a different namespace $ oc delete pods-l app.kubernetes.io/instance=${cr}-n ${ns} ~~~ 2. Restart the logfilesmetricexporter pods: ~~~ $ oc delete pods-l app.kubernetes.io/component=logfilesmetricexporter-n ${ns} ~~~ For more information, please open a [new support case](https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/new/) on the Red Hat Customer Portal referring to this solution.
root_cause: When a CA certificate stored in a ConfigMap (referenced via.spec.outputs[].tls.ca.configMapName) is updated, collector pods are not restarted to pick up the new certificate. The root cause is that only Secrets were included in the pod template hash annotation mechanism. ConfigMaps were fetched and mounted but their content was not hashed, so changes went undetected.

title: IBM Storage Fusion Hub Operator installation fails with CSV stuck in Pending due to operator pods in CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKilled) in RHOCP4
issue: - Installation of the IBM Storage Fusion operator fails. The `ClusterServiceVersion` (CSV) remains in a `Pending` state and does not progress to Succeeded.- Operator pods associated with the installation enter a `CrashLoopBackOff` state.
resolution: To resolve this issue, Increase memory requests and limits for affected operator pods by editing the CSV.- Edit the CSV: ~~~ $ oc edit csv isf-operator.v2.11.0-n ibm-spectrum-fusion-ns ~~~- Update resource configurations: #####[isf-application-operator-controller-manager] ~~~- label: control-plane: isf-application-controller-manager name: isf-application-operator-controller-manager name: manager ports:- containerPort: 9443 name: webhook-server protocol: TCP readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /readyz port: 8081 initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 10 resources: limits: cpu: 100m memory: 500Mi------> 1000Mi requests: cpu: 100m memory: 100Mi-------> 200Mi ~~~ #####[isf-cns-operator-controller-manager] ~~~- label: app.kubernetes.io/version: v2.7.0 control-plane: isf-cns-operator-controller-manager name: isf-cns-operator-controller-manager name: manager ports:- containerPort: 8082 name: scale-metrics protocol: TCP- containerPort: 9443 name: webhook-server protocol: TCP readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /readyz port: 8081 initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 10 resources: limits: cpu: 500m memory: 1000Mi---------> 2000Mi requests: cpu: 100m ephemeral-storage: 2Mi memory: 200Mi----------> 400Mi ~~~ #####[isf-ui-operator-controller-manager] ~~~- label: control-plane: isf-ui-operator name: isf-ui-operator-controller-manager name: manager readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /readyz port: 8081 initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 10 resources: limits: cpu: 400m memory: 800Mi----------> 1600Mi requests: cpu: 200m memory: 200Mi----------> 400Mi ~~~- Save the changes. ####Note: Please increase the resource limits for the pods that are in a `CrashLoopBackOff` state due to `OOMKilled` errors.
root_cause: - The operator controller pods are being `OOMKilled` (Out Of Memory) due to `insufficient memory` limits defined in the operator CSV.- This results in:- Container termination with `exit code 137`- Pods entering `CrashLoopBackOff`- CSV failing to reconcile and remaining in `Pending` state

title: Mounting separate disk for OpenShift 4 etcd
issue: - How to mount a separate disk for `etcd` on OpenShift control plane nodes.- How to mount a separate disk for `/var/lib/etcd` on OpenShift master nodes.- Due to bad etcd disk performance, a separate disk for `etcd` is needed.- Following the recommendations in [etcd backend performance requirements for OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4770281), it is needed to configure a separate disk for `etcd` in our installed cluster.- There is a way to separate `/var/lib/containers` to a different disk: [Mounting separate disk for OpenShift 4 container storage](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4952011). Is it possible to do the same with `/var/lib/etcd`?- Bad etcd performance.
resolution: Starting with OpenShift 4.6, it is possible to configure an additional disk for etcd during the installation, following the documentation: [Disk partitioning](https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/installing/installing_bare_metal/installing-bare-metal.html#installation-user-infra-machines-advanced_vardisk_installing-bare-metal). In recent versions of OpenShift 4, it is possible to move etcd to a different disk following the documentation:- [Moving etcd to a different disk in OpenShift 4.11](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.11/html/scalability_and_performance/recommended-host-practices#move-etcd-different-disk_recommended-host-practices).- [Moving etcd to a different disk in OpenShift 4.12 to 4.18](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.12/html/scalability_and_performance/recommended-performance-and-scalability-practices-2#move-etcd-different-disk_recommended-etcd-practices) (change the version accordingly).- [Moving etcd to a different disk in OpenShift 4.19](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/etcd/performance-considerations-for-etcd#move-etcd-different-disk_etcd-performance).- [Moving etcd to a different disk in OpenShift 4.20+](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/etcd/ensuring-reliable-etcd-performance-and-scalability#move-etcd-different-disk_etcd-performance). > **IMPORTANT NOTE:** it is not supported to move etcd to a different disk following the documentation when using control plane machine sets (CPMS). There is an internal RFE-479 to add the ability to configure a separate disk in IPI installations, and also RFE-5214 for creating additional data disk using `MachineSet` in Azure, but still not implemented.
root_cause: Some of the most common issues with etcd are caused by slow storage. Separating the `/var/lib/etcd` to a different and faster disk could help resolving those issues. For additional information about the etcd requirements, please review [etcd backend performance requirements for OpenShift](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4770281). While this process can be used to mount additional disks to a RHEL CoreOS node, support is limited to no more than one additional disk/partition. Please see [Understanding OpenShift File System Monitoring (eviction conditions)](https://access.redhat.com/articles/4766521) for more information.

title: Worker node fails to fetch Ignition config with "dial tcp: lookup api-int... connection refused" during RHCOS boot
issue: - During RHCOS boot, Ignition fails to fetch the worker (or master) config from the Machine Config Server (MCS) endpoint on port 22623. The console shows repeated errors: ~~~ ignition[860]: GET error: Get "https://api-int..:22623/config/worker": dial tcp: lookup api-int..: connection refused A start job is running for Ignition (fetch) (Xs / no limit) ~~~- The node retries indefinitely but never succeeds.
resolution: 1. Identify what DNS server the node is using. For static configurations, check the nmconnection keyfile or kernel arguments. For DHCP, check the DHCP lease being offered on that subnet. 2. From a working host on the same network segment as the new node, verify the DNS server is reachable and resolving the api-int record: ~~~ dig @ api-int.. ~~~ If this returns "connection refused" or times out, the problem is confirmed on the DNS server side. 3. Fix the DNS server or update the node's DNS configuration to point to a working DNS server that resolves api-int.\.\ to the correct API VIP. 4. Confirm the required DNS records exist on the target DNS server: ~~~ dig @ api-int.. dig @ api.. dig @ *.apps.. ~~~ 5. Confirm network connectivity from the node's subnet to the API VIP on ports 22623 (MCS) and 6443 (API). 6. Reboot the node once DNS is corrected. Ignition will retry and proceed once it can resolve and reach the MCS endpoint.
root_cause: - The "connection refused" on the DNS lookup means the node's network interface is up and it can route packets to the configured DNS server IP, but the DNS server is actively refusing the connection on port 53. This typically happens when:- The DNS server IP configured on the node (via DHCP, nmconnection keyfile, or kernel arguments) is incorrect or points to a host that is not running a DNS service.- The DNS server is down or its DNS service (named, dnsmasq, unbound, etc.) is not running.- A firewall on the DNS server or in the network path is blocking UDP/TCP port 53.- The node is on a different VLAN or subnet from the intended DNS server and the traffic is being rejected at a network boundary.- This is distinct from the "network is unreachable" error covered in solution 6960854, where the node's network interface itself fails to come up in time due to carrier timeout.

title: Assisted Installer fails with Input/Output and SquashFS errors when using iDRAC Virtual Media in RHOCP
issue: During the installation of a `Single Node OpenShift (SNO)` or a `multi-node` cluster via the Assisted Installer on Bare Metal, the node fails to become "Ready." Error logs seen in journalctl- ~~~ Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain kernel: SQUASHFS error: Unable to read fragment cache entry [98f53e7] Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain kernel: SQUASHFS error: Unable to read page, block 98f53e7, size a0a3 Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain kernel: SQUASHFS error: Unable to read fragment cache entry [98f53e7] Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain kernel: SQUASHFS error: Unable to read page, block 98f53e7, size a0a3 Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain kernel: SQUASHFS error: Unable to read fragment cache entry [98f53e7] Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain kernel: SQUASHFS error: Unable to read page, block 98f53e7, size a0a3 Mar 25 11:09:55 localhost.localdomain podman[4103833]: Error: copying system image from manifest list: Source image rejected: None of the signatures were accepted, reasons: Invalid crypto engine; Invalid crypto engine; ~~~
resolution: - To eliminate routing bottlenecks during deployment, host the `ISO` payload within the same Layer 2 broadcast domain or `VLAN` as the target `iDRAC` interface.- Maintain a high-stability connection, any network latency or drops will interrupt the virtual media mount.- If a stable network mount is not possible, use a `CD-ROM` or an bootable `USB` to boot the machine.
root_cause: The Input/output error and `SQUASHFS` errors indicate that the operating system cannot read data from the boot media. When using `iDRAC Virtual Media` over a high-latency or unstable network, the connection to the `ISO` is frequently interrupted. Because the RHCOS live environment runs partially from the compressed `SquashFS` image on that media, any interruption results in corrupted file reads, causing services (like Podman and the Assisted Agent) to crash.

title: RHOAI: During LLM Model deployment external model route option is greyed out for normal user added as contributor to a project.
issue: RHOAI: During LLM Model deployment external model route option below is greyed out for normal user added as contributor to a project. ~~~ Make deployed models available through an external route ~~~
resolution: 1. This is expected behavior. 2. External route enabled option is controlled based on `rolebinding`. 3. There are 2 `rolebindings` for normal users in a project in RHOAI dashboard. ~~~ $ oc get rolebindings NAME ROLE AGE admin ClusterRole/admin 59m dashboard-permissions-dnrnpl ClusterRole/admin 25m dashboard-permissions-viwl0e ClusterRole/edit 31m openshift-pipelines-edit ClusterRole/edit 59m pipelines-scc-rolebinding ClusterRole/pipelines-scc-clusterrole 59m system:deployers ClusterRole/system:deployer 59m system:image-builders ClusterRole/system:image-builder 59m system:image-pullers ClusterRole/system:image-puller 59m ~~~ * Rolebinding `dashboard-permissions-dnrnpl` is to manage `ClusterRole/admin`. * Rolebinding `dashboard-permissions-viwl0e` is to manage `ClusterRole/edit` for `contributor` role. 4. Exact content of `admin` `rolebinding`. ~~~ $ oc describe rolebinding dashboard-permissions-dnrnpl Name: dashboard-permissions-dnrnpl Labels: opendatahub.io/dashboard=true opendatahub.io/project-sharing=true Annotations: Role: Kind: ClusterRole Name: admin Subjects: Kind Name Namespace----------------- User user1 ~~~ **Note:** User `user1` is part of `admin` `ClusterRole` hence options `Make deployed models available through an external route` and `Require token authentication` is enabled. 5. Exact content of `contributor` `rolebinding`. ~~~ $ oc describe rolebinding dashboard-permissions-viwl0e Name: dashboard-permissions-dnrnpl Labels: opendatahub.io/dashboard=true opendatahub.io/project-sharing=true Annotations: Role: Kind: ClusterRole Name: edit Subjects: Kind Name Namespace----------------- User user2 ~~~ **Note:** User `user2` is part of `contributor` `ClusterRole` hence options `Make deployed models available through an external route` and `Require token authentication` is disabled. 6. Normal user should to be part of `admin` role in project using following path. ~~~ RHOAI Dashboard-> Login as `admin` user-> Data Science Projects->-> Permissions-> Users->-> Select 3 dots at the end-> Edit-> Select `Admin` under permission section-> Click on `Check Mark Button`. ~~~

title: OCP node installation fails due to interface not configured
issue: - During the OCP node installation, the node cannot fetch the ignition file showing errors related to connection from the node to nameserver: ~~~- [***] A start job is running for Ignition (fetch) (50s / no limit)[63.252650] ignition[1125]: GET error: Get "https://api-int.sandbox.tb.cp.internal.example.com:22623/config/worker": dial tcp: lookup api-int.example.com on 10.0.0.19:53: read udp 172.0.0.32:48590-> 10.0.0.19:53: i/o timeout ~~~ ~~~ [296.837213] ignition[1104]: GET error: Get "https://api-int.example.com:22623/config/worker": dial tcp: lookup api-int.example.com on 10.0.0.19:53: dial udp 10.0.0.19:53: connect: network is unreachable ~~~
resolution: - Boot adding *rd.net.timeout.carrier* kernel argument with a value bigger than 6, for instance 15 seconds.- As final solution, a [patch](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/-/merge_requests/1239) to Network manager has been submitted to increase the rd.net.timeout.carrier default value from 6 seconds to 15 seconds.
root_cause: - NetworkManager has a built-in timeout of 6 seconds to wait for the carrier in the interfaces.- In some cases it may be not enough with 6 seconds, so the NetworkManager quits without finishing the interfaces configuration (bond, vlan, IP config) properly.

title: Change Quay superuser password via WebUI
issue: - Not possible to login to Quay WebUI- Forgotten quayadmin password- User is not able to login receiving message "Invalid Username or Password"
resolution: ### Red Hat Quay installation with the Quay Operator 1. Identify the Quay Config Bundle Secret- Open the Red Hat OpenShift Cluster WebUI- On the left side panel find the Installed Operators tab- Select the Quay Operator- Click on the Quay Registry tab- Select the Quay Registry on the Name Column- Click on the secret on the Config Bundle Secret section 2. Edit the Quay Config Bundle Secret- On the right upper corner you will find a dropdown action menu, click and select *Edit Secret*- On the new window opened set `tempuser` user on superuser scope- Under quay configuration file `config.yaml` removing the `quayadmin` user and adding the `tempuser` under the `SUPER_USERS` feature: ~~~ SUPER_USERS:- tempuser ~~~- Click on the Save button on the left down corner to save the changes- Wait until the new quay-app pod starts- Verify if the new pod is up and running ~~~ $ oc get po-l quay-component=quay-app NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE quay-enterprise-registry-quay-app-bf798c55d-q67zp 1/1 Running 0 118s <==== new pod with few second lifetime ~~~ 3. On the Red Hat Quay WebUI click on "Create Account" and fill the Create new account form: e.g. ~~~ Username: tempuser E-mail address: tempuser@example.com Password: tempuserpass ~~~ 4. Login with the new user (`tempuser`) 5. Change the `quayadmin` password via *Super User Admin Panel* After login, on the top right corner, click on the username icon- Select *Super User Admin Panel*- Select the tab *User*- Select the user (in this example `quayadmin`)- Select the gear icon on the right side of the selected user- Click on *Change Password* option- Type the new password- Logout from Quay WebUI 6. Login to Quay WebUI using the `quayadmin` and type the new password. ### Red Hat Quay standalone installation 1. Set `tempuser` user on superuser scope Edit the quay configuration file `config.yaml` removing the `quayadmin` user and adding the `tempuser` under the `SUPER_USERS` feature: ~~~ SUPER_USERS:- tempuser ~~~ 2. Restart the quay container ~~~ $ podman restart ~~~ 3. On the Red Hat Quay WebUI click on "Create Account" and fill the Create new account form: e.g. ~~~ Username: tempuser E-mail address: tempuser@example.com Password: tempuserpass ~~~ 4. Login with the new user (`tempuser`) 5. Change the `quayadmin` password via *Super User Admin Panel* After login, on the top right corner, click on the username icon- Select *Super User Admin Panel*- Select the tab *User*- Select the user (in this example `quayadmin`)- Select the gear icon on the right side of the selected user- Click on *Change Password* option- Type the new password- Logout from Quay WebUI 6. Login to Quay WebUI using the `quayadmin` and type the new password. ### OpenShift Mirror Registry (OMR) On OpenShift Mirror Registry the default values during the deployment are: `username = init` On the `config.yaml` file the `admin` user is already set under the `SUPER_USERS` feature: ~~~ SUPER_USERS:- admin ~~~ 1. On the Red Hat Quay WebUI click on "Create Account" and fill the Create new account form: e.g. ~~~ Username: admin E-mail address: admin@example.com Password: adminpass ~~~ 2. Login with the new user (`admin`) 3. Change the `init` password via *Super User Admin Panel* After login, on the top right corner, click on the username icon- Select *Super User Admin Panel*- Select the tab *User*- Select the user (in this example `init`)- Select the gear icon on the right side of the selected user- Click on *Change Password* option- Type the new password- Logout from Quay WebUI 4. Login to Quay WebUI using the `admin` and type the new password.
root_cause: The password attempted for the user with `SUPER USER` right could be incorrect or forgotten.

title: Intermittent TCP Connection Failures in OpenShift Windows Pods Due to TCP/IP Stack Limits
issue: - Applications running in Windows pods on OpenShift Container Platform experience intermittent TCP connection failures, often manifesting as connection timeouts or an inability to establish new connections. This can be particularly prevalent when connecting to external databases or services, and may be linked to TCP port exhaustion or aggressive handling of `TIME_WAIT` connections within the Windows host's networking stack.
resolution: - To mitigate intermittent TCP connection failures, adjust the Windows TCP/IP registry settings on affected Windows worker nodes. These changes reduce the `TIME_WAIT` duration, expand the ephemeral port range, and increase the maximum number of TCP connections. **Steps:** 1. **Access the Windows Node:** Connect to the affected Windows worker node using administrative privileges (e.g., via RDP or an administrative PowerShell session). 2. **Apply Registry Changes (PowerShell):** Execute the following PowerShell commands. These commands modify the TCP/IP parameters in the Windows Registry. ```powershell # Reduce TIME_WAIT duration from 120s (default) to 30s New-ItemProperty-Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters" `-Name TcpTimedWaitDelay-PropertyType DWORD-Value 30-Force # Expand ephemeral port range from ~5000 to 65534 New-ItemProperty-Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters" `-Name MaxUserPort-PropertyType DWORD-Value 65534-Force # Increase max TCP connections New-ItemProperty-Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters" `-Name TcpNumConnections-PropertyType DWORD-Value 16777214-Force ``` 3. **Restart the Computer:** For these registry changes to take effect, the Windows node must be restarted. ```powershell Restart-Computer-Force ``` 4. **Verify Registry Changes (Post-Reboot):** After the restart, re-access the Windows node and verify that the registry values were set correctly: ```powershell Get-ItemProperty-Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters" | ` Select-Object TcpTimedWaitDelay, MaxUserPort, TcpNumConnections ``` Expected output: ``` TcpTimedWaitDelay: 30 MaxUserPort: 65534 TcpNumConnections: 16777214 ``` 5. **Verify Runtime TCP Stack Configuration:** Confirm that the TCP stack is actively using the new dynamic port range: ```powershell netsh int ipv4 show dynamicport tcp ``` Look for the "Start Port" and "Number of Ports" values to reflect the expanded range.
root_cause: - Default Windows TCP/IP stack parameters for `TcpTimedWaitDelay`, `MaxUserPort`, and `TcpNumConnections` can be too restrictive for high-concurrency workloads typical in OpenShift environments. This can lead to: * `TIME_WAIT` state connections lingering too long, consuming available ports. * Insufficient ephemeral ports available for new outgoing connections. * A limit on the total number of TCP connections the system can handle.
